Present application filed by the applicant­ Mohammad Idrish Ali, under section 156(3) of The Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, for the offence punishable under section 366A, 375, 376 of Indian Penal Code with POSCO Act. 2. The applicant has contended that accused used to follow complainant's daughter Viz. Ms. Nagma while she was her way to school. He further contended that the commission of serious cognizable an offences by the accused upon minor, and since no action has been taken by the police authorities on the complaint. 3. On perusal of the application and documents placed on record, heard the argument of learned advocate for the complainant and perusal of act. The POSCO Act is also triable by the Special Court. Section 28 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act (POCSO). Section 28 (1) – For the purposes of providing a speedy trial, the State Government shall in consultation with the Chief Justice of the High Court, by notification in the Official Gazette, designate for each district, a Court of Session to be a Special Court to try the offences under the Act. Provided that if a Court of Session is notified as a children's court under the Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005 or a Special Court designated for similar purposes under any other law for the time being in force, then such Court shall be deemed to be a Special Court under this section. 4. I have gone through the aforesaid provision of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, this court has no jurisdiction to take cognizance in the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act (POCSO). Therefore, I proceed to pass the following final order. ORDER Application is rejected Sd/- Vasai ( I.J.Thakare) Dt. 26.03.2018 III Judicial Magistrate, F.C., Vasai

Judgment Pocso Spl. Case No.05/2017. CNR NO.MHTH23­000103­2017. Received on : 17/01/2017 Registered on : 17/01/2017 Decided on : 16/08/2018 Duration : 01 07 01 D M Y IN THE COURT OF THE ADDITIONAL SESSIONS JUDGE­2,VASAI. ( Presided over by Rahul R. Bhosale ) Pocso Spl.Case No. 5 of 2017. CNR NO.MHTH23­000103­2017 Ex.No. 25. The State of Maharashtra .... Complainant. (through Virar Police Station) versus Kashinath Krushna Bhoir, … Accused. Age 51 years, Resident of Krushna Niwas Building, ground floor, Patil Alley, Hanuman Temple, Dongarpada, Virar (W) Native Place – village Karbude, Dist. Ratnagiri. Learned Advocates : Mrs. Hiwarale A.P.P. for State. Mrs. Sharda Patil for accused. JUDGMENT (Delivered on this 16th day of August, 2018. ) 1] Accused is facing trial for offences punishable under sections 452 & 354 of Indian Penal Code 1860 (IPC)and S.8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (POCSO Act). /2 / Judgment POCSO Spl. Case No.05/2017. CNR NO.MHTH23­000103­2017. 2] Brief facts of the prosecution case are as under: The informant, due to his ill­health, did not attend his duty on 18/7/2016 . At around 5.00 p.m. he went for chit­chatting with adjacent resident and his wife went for bringing back their younger son from school while his daughter – the Child was alone present in the house. Accused visited to the house and inquired to the Child regarding whereabout of other family members. He then caught hold on the hand of Child and touched her breast with mal intention. The Child raised alarms to which the informant's brother with his wife responded and came there. Meanwhile, the adjacent residents nabbed the accused who was also beaten with fist blows and kicks by the informant and his brother when they approached there. Said incident was then reported by the informant to the Virar Police station. 3] After investigation, the charge­sheet was filed in this court against the accused. A charge for offences punishable under sections 452,354 of I.P.C. and S.8 of POCSO Act was framed against accused, to which he denied and claimed to be tried. The prosecution has examined ABC (Child) (P.W.No.1) at Ext. 07, XYZ ­ Father of Child (P.W.No.2) at Ext.08, Devdhar (P.W.No.3) at Ext.12 and I.O Balu (P.W.No.4) at Ext.15. The prosecution has thereafter, filed the pursis at Ext..23 for closing the evidence. The statement of accused has been recorded u/s. 313 of Cr.P.C.at Ext.24. Accused has raised the defence of total denial and false implication and has not examined any defence witnesses. 4] On the basis of the material on record, the points arise for my determination are answered for the reasons as under ­ /3 / Judgment POCSO Spl. Case No.05/2017. CNR NO.MHTH23­000103­2017. Points Findings 1. Whether the prosecution has proved that the ..Proved victim was Child on the day of incident as provided under POCSO Act ? 2. Whether prosecution has proved that accused ..Proved. committed house trespass by entering into the house of informant and committed assault on Child? 3. Whether prosecution has proved that accused ..Proved used criminal force against Child, outraged her modesty and committed sexual assault on her ? 4. What is the order ? ..As per final order. REASONS 5] Point no.1 ­ The offence under S.7 r/w S.8 of POCSO Act has been alleged against the accused. In view of the scope and object of that Act, let us first scrutinize as per its S.2(d) that the victim was whether below age of 18 years at the time of the incident, termed as a 'Child'. The prosecution has materially relied on the document at Ext.25 which is the birth certificate issued by the Government local authority. It is admissible in evidence under S.74 & 79 of the Indian Evidence Act 1872 r/w S.17 of the Registration of Birth and Deaths Act 1969. It discloses the birth date of Child is 14/4/2005. The informant­the father of Child, has corroborated that date of birth in his testimony at Ext.08. Accused has not challenged that date of birth. Thus the prosecution has succeeded to prove the Child's birth date is 14/4/2005. The alleged incident in respect of the Child was allegedly held on 18/07/2016. It concludes that the /4 / Judgment POCSO Spl. Case No.05/2017. CNR NO.MHTH23­000103­2017. Child was round 11 years 3 months and 4 days older when the alleged incident was held. Thus, the present victim is covered by the term ‘Child ’ therefore, the provisions of POCSO Act are applicable to the present set of facts. I therefore, answer the point no.1 in the affirmative. 6] Point Nos. 2 & 3: Accused is facing material charge under S.7 r/w 8 of the POCSO Act. S.7 for ready reference reads as : Section 7 : Sexual Assault ­ Whoever, with sexual intent touches the vagina, penis, anus or breast of the child or makes the child touch the vagina, penis anus or breast of such person or any other person, or does any other act with sexual intent which involves physical contact without penetration is said to commit sexual assault. This provision is to be read with presumptions under Ss.29 & 30 of the POCSO Act as under : Section 29 : Presumption as to certain offenes – Where a person is prosecuted for committing or abetting or attempting to commit any offence under Sections 3,5,7 and Section 9 of this Act, the Special Court shall presume, that such person has committed the offence, unless the contrary is proved. Section 30 : Presumption of culpable mental state – (1) In any prosecution for any offence under this Act which requires a culpable mental state on the part of the accused, the Special Court shall presume the existence of such mental state but it shall be a defence for the accused to prove the fact that he had no such mental state with respect to the act charged as an offence in that prosecution. /5 / Judgment POCSO Spl. Case No.05/2017. CNR NO.MHTH23­000103­2017. (2) For the purposes of this section, a fact is said to be proved only when the Special Court believes it to exist beyond reasonable doubt and not merely when its existence is established by a preponderance of probability. 7] Honourable Apex Court in the case of State of Bihar Vs. Rajbatar Prasad, (2017) 1 SCC Cri. 678, has held that, any offence involving statutory presumption of guilt, the general presumption of innocence of accused is not applicable where accused is prosecuted under Ss.3,5,7,8 and 9 of the POSCO Act 2012. For attracting the presumptions under Ss.29 & 30 of the POCSO Act, the prosecution has to prove firstly the act of accused in the light of cogent evidence and then the presumptions would be made applicable and thereafter the chance of rebuttal is to be given to the accused for coming to the conclusion of commission of the offence alleged as per the provisions under the POCSO Act. 8] Thus in the aforesaid statutory frame ­ work the prosecution case and evidence are to be scrutinized. The victim – Child aged around 11 years at the time of incident has materially deposed at Ext.7 that on 18/7/2016 at around 5.30 to 6.00 p.m. after taking bath at her house she was taking the food for eating when no other family members was present. She further deposes that accused entered the house, caught hold on her hand, touched her breast and was saying her to come into the bed­ room therefore, she shouted loudly to call her uncle and aunt residing nearby who responded her. She lastly deposes that the accused was apprehended by her uncle. In her cross­examination nothing is found for disbelieving the Child except the only material suggestions of false implication put to her that as her father was dignitary of the housing /6 / Judgment POCSO Spl. Case No.05/2017. CNR NO.MHTH23­000103­2017. society in arrears of accused and accused had business rivalry with her uncle out of the common real estate business. Both of these suggestions have been denied by the Child. 9] Child's uncle (P.W.3)who rushed immediately to the spot in response to the alarms of the Child at the time of incident, has deposed at Ext. No.12 about the immediate events held after the incident took place. He deposes that when he rushed to the house of Child, he saw the accused was coming out of the house hence he caught hold on him and asked the reason of shouting to the Child who stated him the incident as held. In his cross­examination the suggestion on behalf of accused is put about the accused was conducting business as a real estate agent which he has denied. However, even no further suggestion was put to him about same business was also conducted by him and he had business rivalry with accused, as suggested to the Child in her cross­examination. The reason about not putting such defence to this direct witness is not explained by accused which concludes falsity in the defence. Therefore, the only material defence about business rivalry in between him and the accused caused to file the present prosecution against the accused is not found reliable. Thus, Child's uncle (P.W.3) supports the Child by deposing the natural events held after the incident making evidence of Child reliable. 10] In the argument, Advocate Mrs. Sharda Patil for the accused has tried to bring on record another sort of dispute held about payment of erection of pendol by accused into the housing society of Child for celebrating Republic Day on 26th January. The accused further raises the defence that as the relative of Child was dignitary of housing society hence, to evade such arrears the accused is roped in the crime. But apparently accused is found not sure even about who was then such /7 / Judgment POCSO Spl. Case No.05/2017. CNR NO.MHTH23­000103­2017. dignitary either the father of Child or the uncle of the Child, who was liable to make payment to the accused. Such suggestion was put to both of them by accused in cross­examination of both wherein the Child's father has denied. But Child's uncle admitted in his cross­examination that he was the chairman of the housing society when accused raised the pendol. However, surprisingly again in cross­examination, the accused has even not put further the suggestions that the accused at any time demanded such remuneration or the housing society was in arrears of such remuneration to the accused. Therefore, that defence is also not found reliable to attract any doubt to the evidence led by Child (P.W.No.1) supported by her uncle (P.W.No.3). 11] Child's father (P.W.No.2) is also examined by the prosecution at Ext. 08, who at the time of incident had gone to meet his friends nearby while within one hour thereafter his son came there calling him immediately to the house. He further deposes that his brother and his wife found out side of his house holding the accused and the Child was crying who told him the incident. He further deposes that he slapped the accused in the fit of anger and lastly lodged the report of incident at Ext. . 09 to the police station. In cross­examination again the accused put the suggestions about business rivalry in between his brother and accused compelled him to file that report. Some questions in detail about those transactions are also put to him by the accused in the cross­examination which he has denied. But question remains as why the accused did not put such questions to the direct witness on it i.e. the uncle of Child (P.W.No.3). Thus, the said defence is not found reliable which otherwise is not made the version of Child's father (P.W.No.2) as unreliable. /8 / Judgment POCSO Spl. Case No.05/2017. CNR NO.MHTH23­000103­2017. 12] The prosecution has lastly examined I.O Balu (P.W.No.4) at Ext. No.15 in support of ocular testimonies of the witnesses. He proves the regular course of conducting investigation by preparing the spot panchanama at Ext. No.11 etc. In his cross­examination the stress has been put by the accused unnecessarily on the authenticity of VCD recorded of the Child's statement before the police. The prosecution has not relied upon the VCD which is in fact at the most the statement under S. 161 of Cr.P.C having no evidentary value even if prosecution relies upon that. Therefore, the defence even if is considered as acceptable then also it will not falsify the investigation carried out by I.O Balu (P.W.No.4) resulting into filing of charge­sheet against the accused. No other defence is found reliable to disbelieve the prosecution evidence. 13] The prosecution has thus succeeded to prove that accused entered the house of Child, touched her breast by gripping her hand. The deposition of Child that the accused asking her to come into the bed­room thereafter would prove his sexual intent as required to attract S. 7 of the POCSO Act for committing the sexual assault on Child. Thus, the prosecution has succeeded to prove that the accused committed sexual assault on the Child as provided under S. 7 of the POCSO Act. This act of accused also attracts S. 442 of IPC defining house trespass. It in turn in the light of above evidence, proves house trespass with intent to assault on the Child attracting S.452 of the IPC. Thus prosecution has also proved offence under S. 452 of IPC committed by the accused. 14] Section 354 of IPC 1860 is also charged against the accused regarding the said incident. For ready reference it reads as : S.354 – Assault or criminal force to woman with intent to outrage her modesty – Whoever assaults or uses criminal /9 / Judgment POCSO Spl. Case No.05/2017. CNR NO.MHTH23­000103­2017. force to any woman, intending to outrage or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby outrage her modesty, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall note less than one year but which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine. The required ‘assault’ as defined under S. 351 of IPC and ‘criminal force’ under S. 350 of IPC to the Child here intending to outrage her modesty, are proved as the prosecution has brought on record that the accused caught hold on the hand of the Child without the consent of the Child. It certainly outraged her modesty when the Child raised alarm for protecting herself. In the result the prosecution has succeeded to prove the charge under S. 354 of IPC as evident earlier. 15] The decision of Honourable Apex Court (2017) 1 SCC Cri. 678 (supra) is applicable to the present set of facts. As per Ss. 29 and 30 of the POCSO Act 2012, statutory presumptions are applicable to the present prosecution case about accused committed the offence for which he had culpable mental state. The accused as per Ss.29 and 30 of the POCSO Act has not disproved those statutory presumptions as provided in the decision of Honourable Apex Court (Supra) hence prosecution has succeeded to prove that the accused is to be sentenced under S. 8 of the POCSO Act. 16] It concludes that the prosecution has succeeded to prove the guilt of accused beyond reasonable doubts. I accordingly answer point nos.2 and 3 in the affirmative. 17] Point No. 4 : As the prosecution has succeeded to prove the offences / 10 / Judgment POCSO Spl. Case No.05/2017. CNR NO.MHTH23­000103­2017. levelled against the accused hence accused is to be sentenced under S. 8 of POCSO Act and under Ss. 452,354 of IPC 1860. I pause here to afford the chance of hearing to the accused on the point of sentencing as required under S.235 (2) of Cr.P.C 1973. 18] Advocate Sharda Patil has argued that the accused is a sole bread winner of his family and no criminal antecedent is found against him hence she prays to take lenient view. APP Mrs.Hiwarale has countered it by submitting that such act of accused spoiled the mental state of Child as a human being hence she submits further to sentence the accused severely. On this backdrop, I do not find any lenient view should be taken into the matter as the accused aged 52 years committed sexual assault and outraged modesty of Child aged around 11 years. It has certainly caused physical and materially the mental trauma on the Child. Such kind of offences see a rampant growth recently which are to be dealt with iron hand not only for deterring the accused but also for preventing the social elements in involving such kind of offences. 19] I pass the sentence to the accused under S. 8 of POCSO Act and under Ss. 452, 354 of IPC 1860. The secretary DLSA, Thane be informed to arrange for paying compensation to the Child. Accordingly, I pass the order as under : ORDER 1] The accused Kashinath Krushna Bhoir is convicted under Section 235(2) of Cr.P.C 1973 for the offences punishable : (i) Under S.452 of IPC 1860 and sentence to undergo R.I for a term of 3 years and to pay fine of / 11 / Judgment POCSO Spl. Case No.05/2017. CNR NO.MHTH23­000103­2017. Rs.5000/­ (Rupees Five Thousand Only); in default of payment of fine, accused shall undergo further the S.I for three months. (ii) Under S.354 of IPC 1860 and sentence to undergo R.I for a term of 3 years and to pay fine of Rs.5000/­ (Rupees Five Thousand Only); in default of payment of fine, accused shall undergo further the S.I for three months. (iii) Under S.8 of POCSO Act and sentence to undergo R.I for a term of 3 years and to pay fine of Rs.15,000/­ (Rupees Fifteen Thousand Only); in default of payment of fine, accused shall undergo further the S.I for three months. 2] His bail bonds stand cancelled. 3] The sentences shall run concurrently. 4] The copy of judgment be given to the accused free of cost. 5] The copy of judgment be sent to The Collector, Palghar under S.365 of Cr.P.C. 1973. sd/­xxx Vasai ( Rahul R. Bhosale ) Date : 16/08/2018. Additional Sessions Judge­2, Vasai.

Case No. 5/2018 Judgment (CNR :MHTH23­000128­2018) Presented on : 23.01.2018 Registered on : 23.01.2018 Decided on : 19.11.2018 Duration : 0 years 09 months 26 days IN THE COURT OF THE ADDITIONAL SESSIONS JUDGE­1, VASAI, AT VASAI, DISTRICT PALGHAR [Presided over by M. P. Divate] 05 of 2018 (CNR : MHTH23­000128­2018) Exhibit No.25 The State of Maharashtra .. Complainant (through Virar police station Crime No. I­399/2017) .. 2 .. Pocso Spl. Case No. 5/2018 Judgment (CNR :MHTH23­000128­2018) versus Umesh Chimanlal Thakkar, .. Accused Age 48 years, Resident of A/101, Shyam Sarita C.H.S., Virat Nagar, Virar (W), Tal. Vasai. Offences punishable under section 354­A of Indian Penal Code and Section 8 of POCSO Act. …................................................................................... Appearance ­ Mrs. Khandagale, A.P.P. for the State Mrs. Darshana Tripathi, Advocate for the accused JUDGMENT (Delivered on this 19th day of November, 2018.) 1. The accused stands trial for the offence punishable under section 354­A of Indian Penal Code and Section 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act (in short 'POCSO Act' ). 2. Prosecution's case, in brief, is as under ­ .. 3 .. Pocso Spl. Case No. 5/2018 Judgment (CNR :MHTH23­000128­2018) That on 16.7.2017 at 3.00 p.m. accused called victim girl at his computer class. Accused displayed obscene/pornographic film on computer to the victim girl. Accused sat victim girl on his lap and pressed her breasts and outraged her modesty. Police completed the investigation and filed charge­sheet against the accused. 3. Charges under Section 354­A of Indian Penal Code and Section 8 of Pocso Act were framed against accused at Exh.2. Contents of the charge were read over to accused and explained to him in Hindi. He has not pleaded guilty and claimed to be tried. His defence is that of total denial. 4. Prosecution has examined P.W.No.1 ­ mother of victim girl at Exh.13, P.W.No.2 ­ victim child girl at Exh.16 and P.W.No.3 ­ investigation officer Sachin Ingole at Exh.20. 5. After going through the evidence of prosecution witnesses and police papers, following points arise for my determination. I have recorded my findings against each of them for the reasons given below. Points 1} Whether prosecution has proved that on 16.7.2017 between 3.00 and 5.00 p.m., at Virat Nagar, Virar (West) accused has outraged the modesty of victim child girl / committed sexual assault on victim child girl ? .. 4 .. Pocso Spl. Case No. 5/2018 Judgment (CNR :MHTH23­000128­2018) 2} What order and sentence if any ? Findings 1} In Negative 2} Accused is acquitted. See the order below. :REASONS: As regards to point no.1 ­ 6. P.W.No.1 ­ complainant is mother of victim child girl. She has deposed that victim was learning in 10th standard. Victim was minor child. This fact has not been disputed by the accused. Complainant further deposed that on the day of incident at about 4.00 p.m. she was present at her job. Victim telephoned her. She came back. She noticed that the victim was ill and was having fever. Brother's wife namely Sunita was present at home. Victim was under tension. Complainant was under misconception that something is happened with victim in a class. She went at police station. She has filed complaint against the accused. Complainant has admitted her signature on complaint Exh.14 and FIR Exh.15. She has denied the facts contended in complaint. Complainant has specifically deposed that no alleged incident had taken place as contended in complaint and FIR. Complainant has not supported the case of prosecution. .. 5 .. Pocso Spl. Case No. 5/2018 Judgment (CNR :MHTH23­000128­2018) 7. P.W.No.2 ­ victim girl deposed that at the time of filing case she was learning in 8th standard. She was attending the computer class run by the accused. Her mother was doing work with the brother of accused. She completed two months training of computer. Accused was giving computer training to her free of cost. On 16.7.2017 she attended computer class. On that day her brother was not accompanied with her. She came back at home. Mother had taken her at police station. Mother had some misunderstanding. Mother was under tension. Accused did not misbehave with her. Accused did not outrage her modesty. 8. Complainant and victim girl have not supported the case of prosecution. Both they were declared hostile. A.P.P. has invited the attention of complainant on facts contended in portion marked P­1 recorded in complaint. A.P.P. invited the attention of victim on facts contended in portion marked P­2 which came to be recorded in her previous police statement. A.P.P. confronted these witnesses with their earlier statements. A.P.P. failed to elicit material facts through their cross­examination. I hold that the evidence of complainant and victim is not fully consistent and corroborative with the story of prosecution. Complainant and victim have deposed different set of facts before police officer at the time of filing complaint. They have deposed different set of facts before this court. Complainant and victim disclosed that .. 6 .. Pocso Spl. Case No. 5/2018 Judgment (CNR :MHTH23­000128­2018) complainant was under misunderstanding, therefore she has filed complaint at police station. I hold that the evidence of complainant and victim is self­contradictory and it creates doubt about their integrity. The evidence of Investigation Officer P.W.3 Sachin Ingole is formal in nature. I conclude that the evidence on record is not sufficient to bring accused to the home of guilt beyond all reasonable doubt. I have answered Point No.1 in negative. As regards to point no.2 ­ 9. In view of my finding on point No.1, I hold that the evidence on record is not sufficient to bring accused to the home of guilt beyond all reasonable doubt. I proceed to pass following order :­ ORDER 1} Accused Umesh Chimanlal Thakkar is acquitted under section 235(1) of Cr.P.C. of charge for offence punishable under section 354­A of Indian Penal Code and section 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 2} Bail bonds of accused stand cancelled and sureties are discharged. .. 7 .. Pocso Spl. Case No. 5/2018 Judgment (CNR :MHTH23­000128­2018) 3} In view of mandate laid down in section 437A of Cr.P.C., accused is directed to execute P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­. He shall undertake to appear before appellate court on receipt of notice of appeal. Date : 19.11.2018 ( M. P. Divate ) Additional Sessions Judge­1, Vasai.

1 Spl.Case No.1/15 Presented on­ :08­01­2015 Registered on­ :08­01­2015 Decided on­ :20­12­2016 Duration­ :1Y­11M­12D IN THE COURT OF SESSION JUDGE, VASAI. (Presided over by N.R.Pradhan,Addl.S.J.) Special Case NO. 01/2015. Exh The State. (Through Manikpur Police Stn.) ­­­­­­­Complainant. V/s. Sayyad Shabbir Shekh, Age 50 years, R/at Anandnagar Zopadpatti, Vasai (W), Tal.Vasai (E), Dist.Palghar. –­­­­­­ Accused. Offences punishable u/s.376(2)(i)(f)& (n), 323 & 506 of the Indian Penal Code and Sec.4,6 & 8 of Prevention of Child Sexual Offences Act. Appearances­ A.P.P. Smt.Moholkar for the State. Adv. Smt.Sharda Patil for the accused (appointed through legal aid). JUDGMENT (Delivered on 20­12­2016 ) The accused is facing trial for the offences punishable u/s.376(2)(i)(n)(f), 323 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code (hereinafter referred to as IPC) and under Sec.4,6 2 Spl.Case No.1/15 and 8 of Prevention of Child Sexual Offences Act (hereinafter referred to as POCSO Act). The case of prosecution can be epitomized is as under :­ 2] A 15 years old unfortunate girl lodged report against her father on 16­11­2014 before Manikpur Police Station about rape. Victim was residing along with accused and her brother at Mata Ramabai Nagar,Vasai. Since the childhood, her mother did not reside along with them. Her mother was residing along with another man at Ratlam (Madhya Pradesh). At the relevant time, victim was taking education in 6th Std. 3] She has made allegations against her father that since last one year during night time her father used to tie her hands, lags and mouth and forcefully used to commit intercourse with her. The last episode took place on 14­11­ 2014. She had narrated about the sexual harassment of her father to the neighbouring women. However, they did not help her. Then she narrated about the sexual harassment to one Sunita Bablu Chavhan. She helped her and took her before one member of Mahila Dakshata Samiti and then she lodged report against her father. 4] On the basis of said report, Manikpur police registered crime No.296/14 against the accused. Investigation was handed over to PSI Ashwini Chandrakant Patil. She prepared spot panchanama and seized clothes and one bed sheet under said panchanama. She also seized clothes of accused under seizure panchanama. She sent victim and 3 Spl.Case No.1/15 accused for medical examination. She recorded statement of witnesses. She also collected birth date certificate of victim. She sent clothes and other samples to Forensic Laboratory. After completion of investigation, she filed charge­sheet against accused. 5] I have framed charge at Exh.9 against the accused. Charge was read over and explained to accused. He pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. The defence of the accused raised u/s.313 of Cr.P.C. is that Bablu Chavhan who is husband of Sunita Chavhan had demanding house of accused, therefore there was quarrel between accused and Bablu Chavhan. Therefore, false case is filed against accused. 6] Following points arise for my consideration,to which I have recorded my findings against them for the reasons to follow­ POINTS FINDINGS 1] Whether prosecution proves that one year prior to 4­11­2014 at at Mata Ramabai Zopadpatti, Anand Nagar accused being father of victim aged about 15 years committed rape on her repeatedly and thereby committed an offence punishable In the affirmative. u/s.376(2)(1)(n) & (f) of I.P.C.and punishable u/s.6 & 8 of POCSO Act ? 2] Whether prosecution proves that on the above said period, date, time and place, accused voluntarily caused hurt to victim by assaulting her when she used to resist at the time of In the affirmative. committing rape by accused on her and thereby committed an offence 4 Spl.Case No.1/15 punishable u/s.323 of I.P.C.? 3] Whether prosecution proves that on the above said period, date, time and place accused committed criminal intimidation by threatening to victim with injury to her person In the affirmative. to kill if she will disclose about the incident to anybody and thereby committed offence punishable u/s.506 of I.P.C.? 4] What order ? Accused convicted as per final order. 7] Heard ld. A.P.P.Smt.Moholkar and ld. Adv.Smt. Sharda Patil for the accused. 8] In order to prove its case, prosecution has examined PW1 Gita Ravindra Ayre at Exh.15, PW2 Shain Sayyad Saha at Exh.17, PW3 Dr.Anjali Janardan Pimpale at Exh.20,PW4 Ramsagar Ramgyan Yadav at Exh.26,PW5 Nilesh Sureshs Gharat at Exh.28,PW6 Dr.Rani Vikas Badlani at Exh.32 ,PW7 IO PSI Ashwini Chandrakant Patil and PW8 Balvita Thomas Silvera. REASONS Points No.1 to 3 :­ All these points are interlinked each other and hence they are discussed simultaneously. 9] Ld.A.P.P.has forcefully submitted that the victim is totally supporting to the case of prosecution. She submitted 5 Spl.Case No.1/15 that no doubt there are some admissions given by the victim, however, the medical evidence is totally supporting to the case of prosecution and as per the medical evidence, victim was repeatedly undergone sexual intercourse. She submitted that version of victim has to be believed. She submitted that the defence put­forth by the accused is not probable and acceptable. Hence, according to her, prosecution has proved charges beyond reasonable doubt. 10] On the other hand, ld. Advocate for the accused has forcefully submitted that the version of victim is not at all believable. She submitted that the victim admitted in her cross examination that Bablu Chavhan who is husband of Sunita was demanding house of her father. She also admitted that Bablu Chavhan was threatening her father. She further admitted that Sunita Chavhan asked her to speak against her father. Therefore, she submitted that the version of victim is not acceptable. 11] It is also contention of ld. Advocate for the accused that the accused is not capable to perform sexual intercourse. She submitted that the investigating officer has deliberately used habitual panch. The ld. Advocate for the accused submitted that at the instance of Sunita Chavhan and Bablu Chavhan, false complaint is filed against the accused. It is contention of ld. Advocate for the accused that the prosecution has failed to prove the charges beyond reasonable doubt. 12] The first question is whether the prosecution has proved the age of victim. To prove the age of victim, the 6 Spl.Case No.1/15 prosecution has examined Balvita Thomas Silhera (PW8 Exh.46). She deposed that since 1998 she was working as Teacher in Zilla Parishad School. Their school received letter from Manikpur Police Station demanding school leaving certificate of victim. She submitted that school leaving certificate is issued by their school, which is at Exh.47. This witness brought general register No.1 She produced the certified copy of the page of general register No.1 at Exh.48. As per school record, birth date of victim is 1­6­2004. The ld. Advocate for the accused has taken elaborate cross examination of this witness. However, nothing has come on record to disbelieve the version of this witness. 13] Dr.Anjali Janardan Pimpale (PW3 Exh.20) also deposed that after radiological examination and as per the report of Radiologist, the age of victim was between 14 to 15 years. Therefore, the prosecution has proved that at the time of incident victim was 15 years old. 14] In this case, the important witness is victim, (PW2 Exh.17). She deposed that in the year 2014 she was residing at Mata Ramabai Slum area Vasai along with her father and younger brother. That since her childhood, her mother has not been residing along with them. Since one year from the date of filing of complaint her father used to threaten her and used to remove her clothes and used to tie her hands and used to do dirty things almost daily. Her father used to tie mouth from cloth whenever he used to do such dirty things with her. Her father used to point out knife on the neck of her younger brother and threatened her that if she disclosed said act then 7 Spl.Case No.1/15 he will kill his younger brother. Her father used to remove her clothes and forcefully used to do bad thing. Her father used to remove his clothes and her clothes and he used to give some pill. Her father used to press her breast and used to kiss her. Her father used to sleep on her and at that time both were in naked condition. Thereafter, her father used to rape on her. She further deposed that her father had done this bad thing for one year. Then she disclosed about it to Sunita Chavhan who reside near her house. Then Sunita Chavan had taken her to Mahila Mandal and then She was taken to Manikpur police station where she lodged complaint. She admitted the contents of complaint and her signature on complaint. The complaint is at Exh.18. It is pertinent to note here that court has recorded the demeanor of the victim i.e. at the time of giving material evidence, she was crying and tremendous pressure to disclose or deposed about the bad act of her father. 15] The ld. Advocate for the accused has submitted before me that the victim has made improvement in her statement. She submitted that the contents like giving pills, pressing breast and taking pills and pointing out knife are missing from the complaint. Therefore, she submitted that the version of victim can not be accepted. 16] I have minutely scrutinized the evidence of victim from all the angles. I am of the definite view that the deposition of victim is truthful. She might have made some improvement that does not cause any embellishment of serious nature of her evidence. 8 Spl.Case No.1/15 17] The ld. Advocate for the accused has forcefully submitted before me that victim has admitted that Ramabai Nagar is slum area and her father is owner of said house. She admitted that Bablu Chavhan who is husband of Sunit Chavhan is head of slum area. She further admitted that if someone refused to give house then Bablu Chavhan used to file complaint against him. She further admitted that Bablu Chavhan wants house of her father. Her father used to tell her not to go in the house of Bablu Chavhan. She further admitted that residents of Ramabai slum area used to frighten from Sunita Chavhan and Bablu Chavhan. She admitted that Bablu Chavhan used to threaten her father that if her father has not vacant house then he will file false complaint against him. She further admitted that Sunita Chavhan asked her not to reside in her house and asked to reside along with her for few days in her house. It is on record that victim has admitted in her cross examination that before filing complaint she was residing in the house of Sunita Chavhan for 3 to 4 days. Thus, according to ld. Advocate for the accused these admissions are sufficient to come to the conclusion that Bablu Chavhan and Sunita Chavhan told victim to falsely depose against accused. 18] No doubt, the victim has given some admissions. However, we have to appreciate entire evidence of the victim. The victim admitted that Sunita Chavhan told her to depose against her father. However, at the similar time victim voluntarily deposed that she gave reply to Sunita Chavhan that she will speak truth and accordingly she is deposed. She specifically deposed that bad things happened against her and therefore she is speaking about the said bad things. When the 9 Spl.Case No.1/15 defence counsel asked victim suggestive question that she is deposing falsely at the instance of Sunita Chavhan. At that time victim started crying. Therefore, this court feel it necessary to put court question to the victim in absence of ld. A.P.P. and ld. advocate for accused. Hence, court put question to victim whether her father has done wrong and bad things with you? The victim answered that her father has done wrong with her and it is correct. Then court put question whether she has any pressure for deposing against her father? She answered in negative. This piece of evidence clearly shows that the victim was speaking the truth. The victim was deposing against her father who maintained her and therefore naturally she was in some mental pressure. However, nowhere she denied about the sexual act done by her father. Therefore, I found the evidence of victim is full of confidence and trustworthy. 19] The evidence of victim is corroborated and supported by the medical evidence. Dr.Anjali Janardan Pimpale (PW3 Exh.20) deposed that at the relevant time she was working in Civil Hospital, Thane as Eye Surgeon. On 7­11­ 2014 she was working as a Casualty Medical Officer in Civil Hospital Thane. On that day, their hospital received letter from Manikpur Police Station for medical examination of victim. The said letter is at Exh.21. Accordingly, on 7­11­2014 this witness examined victim. She obtained consent of victim for internal examination. The consent is at Exh.22. On that day, at about 3 p.m. she examined victim. Victim had given history of forcibly sexual intercourse during night hours repeatedly since one year by administering sedative before 10 Spl.Case No.1/15 each episode at home by her father and last episode took place on 1­11­2014. As per radiological examination age of victim was between 14 to 15 years. The radiological report is annexed with the medical paper. The final opinion of Doctor is that victim was repeatedly undergone sexual intercourse and her opinion is based on vaginal examination of the said patient. The vaginal opening of the said patient was broad therefore she has given opinion. The entire medical papers are at Exh.23. 20] The ld. Advocate for the accused has elaborately taken cross examination of Dr.Pimpale (PW3), however nothing has come on record to disbelieve her version. The medical evidence corroborates with the version of victim. 21] The ld. Advocate for the accused has submitted that the accused is too old and is handicapped and therefore he is not capable for performing sexual intercourse. The prosecution has examined Dr.Rani Badlani (PW6 Exh.32). She deposed that on 7­11­2014 she was working as Medical Officer in Sir D.M.Petit Hospital Vasai. On that day, hospital received letter from Manikpur Police Station for the medical examination of accused for the potentiality test of accused. Said letter is at Exh.33. Accordingly, Manikpur police brought accused in the hospital for examination. She had examined the accused who was 50 years old. After examined the accused, she has given opinion that accused was capable for performing sexual intercourse. The Medical Officer has collected blood sample, semen sample, pubic hair and nail clipping sample of the accused and sealed and handed over to the police. The 11 Spl.Case No.1/15 medical report of the accused is at Exh.34. It is specifically mentioned therein that the accused is capable to do sexual intercourse. 22] Ld. Advocate for the accused has taken elaborate cross examination of Dr.Rani Bhadlani, however nothing has come on record to disbelieve her version. Therefore, the defence taken by the accused that he is not capable to do sexual intercourse cannot be acceptable. Accused's leg may be fracture but that does not mean that he cannot do sexual intercourse. The prosecution has proved that the accused is capable for performing sexual intercourse. 23] The prosecution has examined Gita Ravindra Ayre (PW1). She deposed that on 6­11­2014 Sunita Chavhan called her at about 6 p.m. at Ramabai Nagar slum area for urgent work. Accordingly, Sunita Chavhan told her that father of victim is sexually harassing her. Then before her victim narrated entire episode and then she took victim to Manikpur police station. There statement of victim was recorded before her. This witness is also cross examined at length, however nothing has come on record to disbelieve her version. 24] The prosecution has proved the spot panchanama and recovery of clothes through the evidence of panch witness Ramsagar Ramgyan Yadav (PW4 Exh.26) and Nilesh Suresh Gharat (PW5 Exh.27) and through IO Ashwini Chandrakant Patil (PW7). These all witnesses cross examined at length. However, nothing has come on record to disbelieve their version. No doubt, the panch witness (PW5) admitted that he 12 Spl.Case No.1/15 has acted as panch in more than 200 cases. He also admitted that for some time he put the signatures on prepared panchanama. However, this admission is not sufficient to entirely throw out the prosecution case, which is otherwise established beyond reasonable doubt. 25] Ld. Advocate for the accused has forcefully submitted that since one year from lodging of FIR, if the accused was doing sexual assault repeatedly then what prevent victim to lodge complaint earlier. Therefore, she submitted that the delay of one year is fatal. Therefore, the prosecution case is not believable. 26] As I have earlier mentioned that accused is father of victim, who forcefully done sexual intercourse repeatedly with her. Naturally tendency of the child is that they hesitate to speak against their parents. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, I am of the view that prosecution has explained the delay and therefore in this case delay of one year is not fatal to the case of prosecution. 27] The accused is facing trial for the offence punishable u/s.6 i.e. aggravated sexual assault. Admittedly the accused is father of victim and victim was in her custody and care. The incident took place in the house. Therefore, the ingredients of aggravate penetrative sexual assault mentioned in sec.5 of POCSO Act are attracted. As per sec. 29 of POCSO Act, there is presumption as to the certain offence and sec.5 is included in it. Sec.29 of POCSO Act provides presumption in favour of prosecution that special court shall presume that 13 Spl.Case No.1/15 accused has committed or abated or attempt to commit the offence as the case may be unless contrary is proved. The defence of the accused is that Bablu Chavhan wants to take his house and therefore with the help of victim he filed false complaint against him. However, one cannot accept that daughter can file false complaint against her father about sexual harassment and assault at the instance of others. Therefore, in this particular case, the presumption is not rebutted by the accused and the defence of the accused is not probable and acceptable. 28] The conspectus of the aforesaid discussion is that through the evidence of victim (PW2) and medical evidence prosecution has proved beyond reasonable doubt that the accused who is father of victim has repeatedly committed sexual intercourse against the will of victim within the meaning of Sec.376 (2)(f) & (n) of I.P.C. The prosecution also proved that accused has committed offence of aggravated penetrative sexual assault within the meaning of sec.5 punishable u/s.6 & 8 of POCSO Act. The prosecution has also proved that the accused committed offence punishable Sec.323 & 506 of I.P.C. Therefore, I hold accused guilty for the offence punishable u/s.376(2)(i)(f)& (n)of I.P.C. punishable u/s.6 of POCSO Act under Sec.323 & 506 of I.P.C. Therefore, I answer points No.1 to 3 in affirmative. 29] I take pause here to hear the accused and ld.A.P.P.on the point of sentence. Vasai. (N.R.Pradhan.) Date:20­12­2016 Additional Sessions Judge, Vasai. 14 Spl.Case No.1/15 30] I heard accused, his advocate and Ld. A.P.P. on the point of sentence. 31] The accused submitted that he is handicapped and has not committed any offence. He submitted that false case filed against him. He submitted that he lost his house. Ld. Advocate for the accused submitted that minimum punishment be ordered to him. 32] On the other hand, ld.A.P.P.has submitted that the accused has committed rape on his daughter and therefore maximum punishment be awarded to him. 33] Maximum punishment as prescribed for the aggravated penetrative sexual assault u/s.6 of POCSO Act is life imprisonment and as per Sec.376(2)(i)(n)of I.P.C., maximum punishment is life imprisonment, which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person's natural life. As per Sec.42 of POCSO Act, offender found guilty of such offence shall be punished under this Act or Indian Penal Code as provided punishment which is greater in degree. As per sec. 376(2)(i)(n)of I.P.C., maximum punishment is life imprisonment, and life imprisonment shall mean for the remainder of that person's natural life and therefore, severe punishment is prescribed in sec.376(2)(i)(n) of I.P.C. Though the accused is held guilty for the offence punishable u/s. 8 of POCSO Act but as the accused is held guilty for major offence therefore it is not necessary to punish the accused for lesser offence. Therefore, I direct accused to suffer sentence 15 Spl.Case No.1/15 u/s.376(2)(i)(n) of I.P.C. and u/s.323 & 506 of I.P.C. 34] It is on record that the victim was residing along with accused. The prosecution has proved that the accused repeatedly for one year committed rape on his daughter. The accused has committed heinous crime and even did not spare her daughter for the satisfaction of his lust. The father is most respected and reliable person of every daughter. But the accused has broken her confidence and has taken disadvantage of helpless minor victim, who was in his care and custody to satisfy his lust. Therefore, I am of the view that this is a fit case to award maximum punishment as prescribed in sec.376 (2)(i) (n) of I.P.C. 35] After considering submissions of both the sides and considering the facts and circumstances of the case, I am of the view that following sentence is just and proper to meet the ends of justice. Hence, I pass the following order. ORDER 1] Accused Sayyad Shabbir Shekh is hereby convicted u/s.235(2) of Cr.P.C.for the offence punishable u/s.376(2)(i)(n) of I.P.C. and sentenced him to suffer life imprisonment and to pay fine of Rs.10,000/­(Rs.Ten thousand only)and in default to suffer Rigorous Imprisonment for three months. 2] The accused is further convicted u/s.235(2) of Cr.P.C.for the offence punishable u/s.323 of I.P.C. and sentenced him to suffer rigorous imprisonment for six months and to pay fine of Rs.500/­(Rs.Five hundred only) and in default to suffer Rigorous Imprisonment 16 Spl.Case No.1/15 for 15 days. 3] The accused is further convicted u/s.235(2) of Cr.P.C.for the offence punishable u/s.506 of I.P.C. and sentenced him to suffer rigorous imprisonment for six months and to pay fine of Rs.500/­(Rs.Five hundred only) and in default to suffer Rigorous Imprisonment for 15 days. 3] The substantive sentence shall run concurrently. 4] The accused is entitled to get set off u/s.428 of Cr.P.C.for the period already undergone in the jail. 5] Muddemal property seized in this crime, being worthless be destroyed, after appeal period is over. 6] Copy of this judgment be given to the accused at free of costs. Vasai. (N.R.Pradhan.) Date:20­12­2016 Additional Sessions Judge, Vasai. 17 Spl.Case No.1/15 IN THE COURT OF SESSION JUDGE, VASAI. (Presided over by N.R.Pradhan,Addl.S.J.) Special Case NO. 01/2015. ..1.. Spl.C.No.13/2015(J) Presented on­ : 5/2/2015 Registered on­ : 5/2/2015 Decided on­ : 17/3/2018 Duration­ : 3­Y 1­M 12­D IN THE COURT OF ADDL. SESSIONS JUDGE, VASAI. (Presided over by N.R.Pradhan,Addl.S.J.) Special Case No.13/2015 CIS No.2300013/2015 Exh.54 The State. (Through Nallasopara Police Stn. C.R.No.I­766/2014 ) ­­­­­­­Complainant. V/s. Baban Sapan Vishwas, Age 23 yrs., R/at­ D­104, Chandresh Riddhi Apt., Sankeshwar Nagar, Achole Rd. Nalasopara –­­­­­­ Accused. Offences punishable U/S.376 & 506 of the Indian Penal Code, Sec.4 & 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and Under Sec. 67, 67(a) of Information Technology Act. Appearances­ A.P.P. Shri. J.R.Patil for the State. Adv. Shri. Uday Patil for the accused. JUDGMENT (Delivered on this 17th day of March, 2018) The accused is facing trial for the offences punishable U/Sec. 376 & 506 of the Indian Penal Code (hereinafter referred to as IPC), Sec.4 & 12 of Protection of ..2.. Spl.C.No.13/2015(J) Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter referred to as POCSO Act) and Under Sec. 67 & 67(a) of Information Technology Act (hereinafter referred to as IT Act). Case of prosecution in short is, as under :­ 2] On 10/12/2014, prosecutrix has lodged complaint against accused. She informed that at the relevant time she was 16 years old and taking education in 9 th std. Accused has Chinese shop in the housing society of prosecutrix. Prosecutrix got acquainted with accused Baban prior to six months and they became friend. She used to talk with accused Baban through the mobile phone of her friend. 3] In the month of October, 2014 accused had taken the prosecutrix to his room which was situated at Sankheshwar nagar, Chandresh Riddhi Society. Then again after 5 to 6 days accused called prosecutrix in the said room. Prosecutrix went in said room. At that time friend of accused was not present in the room. The prosecutrix has made allegations against accused that he assured her that he will marry with her and forcefully maintained sexual intercourse with her. At that time prosecutrix was requesting accused not to do said act, however, inspite of it accused committed sexual intercourse with her. Then, accused told her that he has made video shooting and if she stop calling him through the mobile phone of her friend, then he will viral the said video shooting in internet. On the basis of said threat, again after one or two weeks accused maintained sexual intercourse with her against her will. Again on 1/12/2014, accused called her in the room and forcefully maintained sexual intercourse with her on same ..3.. Spl.C.No.13/2015(J) threat. On 7/12/2014, when the father of prosecutrix had gone to Baroda, on mobile phone she informed him that accused forcefully maintaining sexual relations with her under the threat that he will viral said video shooting in social media. Then on 9/12/2014 with the help of one Deputy Mayor, she filed complaint against accused. 4] On the basis of said information, crime No.I­ 766/2014 lodged against the accused for the above offences. Investigation was handed over to API Landage. Clothes of accused were seized before two panchas on 11/12/2014. On 12/12/2014 accused made memorandum of statement and on the basis of it, mobile phone of accused was seized under panchanama. Again on 12/12/2014 accused made memorandum of statement and on the basis of it, IO seized one bed sheet from the room of accused under panchnama before two pachas. On the same day, he seized clothes of prosecutrix under seizure panchnama before two panchas. He recorded statements of witnesses and after completion of investigation, filed charge sheet against accused. 5] I have framed charge at Exh.10 against the accused. Charge was read over and explained to accused. He pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. The defence of the accused emerges from the statement U/Sec.313 of Cr.P.C. is of total denial. 6] Heard Ld. A.P.P. J.R.Patil for the State and Adv. Shri. Uday Patil for the accused. ..4.. Spl.C.No.13/2015(J) 7] In order to prove its case, prosecution has examined in all 5 witnesses viz Dr. Piyushi Ashutosh Sharma (PW­1) Exh.20, prosecutrix (PW­2) exh.29, Devendra Saudagar Yadav (PW­3) exh.32, Investigating officer API Dilip Dattatraya Landage (PW­4) Exh.33, PSI, Annapurna Shamrao Mhaske (PW­5) Exh.53. 8] Prosecution has relied on documentary evidence i.e., consent form Exh.22, medical examination report Exh.23, FIR Exh.34, bonafide certificate of prosecutrix Exh.35, seizure panchnama Exh.36, office copy of muddemal receipt Exh.37, seizure panchnama of CD Exh.38, office copy of muddemal receipt Exh.39, arrest form of accused Exh.40, personal search and seizure panchnama of clothes of accused Exh.41, muddemal receipt Exh.42, memorandum of statement of accused Exh.43, seizure panchnama of bedsheet Ex.44, muddemal receipt Exh.45, memorandum of statement of accused Exh.46, seizure panchnama of mobile phone of accused Exh.47, office copy of muddemal receipt Exh.48, office copies of two letters Exh.49 & 50, portion marked “A” of complaint Exh.54 and portion marked “B” of complaint Exh.55 and closed its evidence by filing purshis at Exh.53. 9] Following points arise for my consideration,to which I have recorded my findings against them for the reasons to follow­ NO. POINTS FINDINGS 1] Whether prosecution proves that at the time of incident, prosecutrix was minor ? .. Yes ..5.. Spl.C.No.13/2015(J) 2] Whether prosecution proves that in between October. 2014 to 1/12/2014 accused committed rape on minor prosecutrix and thereby committed an offence punishable under Sec. 376 of IPC and under Sec. 4 of POCSO Act ? .. No. 3] Whether prosecution proves that on above mentioned period accused committed aggravated sexual assault on minor prosecutrix and threatened her that he will forward video clip on internet and thereby committed an offence punishable U/Sec.12 of POCSO & under Sec. 67 (4) & 67(a) of Information Technology Act ? .. No. 4] Whether prosecution proves that on the above mentioned period accused committed criminal intimidation to prosecutrix and thereby committed an offence punishable under Sec. 506 of IPC ? .. No. 5] What order ? Accused acquitted. REASONS As to Point No.1:­ 10] It is a case of prosecution that at the relevant time prosecutrix was minor. To prove this aspect prosecution placed reliance on the evidence of prosecutrix (PW­1) exh.11. She deposed that her birth date is 12/12/1999. Prosecution has produced bonafide certificate at Exh. 35. It explicits from the bonafide certificate that said certificate has been issued by Pancham English High School and Junior College, Achole road, Nallasopara road. As per said certificate birth date of prosecutrix is 1/12/1998. Father of prosecutrix (PW­3) deposed that birth date of prosecutrix is 1/12/1998. from the above evidence prosecution has proved that at the relevant ..6.. Spl.C.No.13/2015(J) time prosecutrix was minor. Hence, I answered point No.1 in affirmative. As to point Nos. 2 to 4: 11] At the outset it, has to be mention here that prosecutrix (PW­1) is not supporting to the case of prosecution. She deposed that in the year 2004 she developed love affair with accused. She further deposed that except that there was no relationship between her and accused. Prosecutrix has denied that accused committed forcible intercourse with her at any point of time. She also denied that accused committed forceful intercourse with her on the ground that if she refused, he will viral video shooting in social media. She admitted that she filed complaint. However, she denied portion marked “A” and “B” of her complaint. 12] Devendra Saudagar Yadav (PW­3) Exh.32 is the father of prosecutrix. He deposed that in the year 2014, prosecutrix was 16 yrs. old. He deposed that Chinese restaurant under the name and style Tufan Chinese Center was in one of shop of his residential building. On 7/12/2014, when he was at Baroda for his work, at that time during night time he received phone call of his daughter. She informed him that her friend Baban committed rape on her by giving threat. She also told him that accused has taken her video clip. Then on next day he reached Mumbai and talk to prosecutrix. She told him that accused called her to see his rented room and then after some days he called her in his room. At that time accused told her that he will marry with her and then he committed rape on her in said room. Prosecutrix further told him that accused told her that he has taken video clip and if ..7.. Spl.C.No.13/2015(J) she refused to come, then he will viral said video shooting in social media. Then he met with Deputy Mayor and with his help he filed complaint against accused. 13] Evidence of Devendra Yadav (PW­2) exh.32 is hearse evidence. As I have mentioned that prosecutrix has not supported the case of prosecution hence, evidence of this witness being hearse evidence, is not helpful to the case of prosecution. 14] Dr. Piyushi Sharma (PW­1) exh.20 deposed that she examined prosecutrix and she has given history of sexual assault for 4 to 5 times. She found hymen was ruptured with old tear. In cross­examination she admitted that hymen ruptured can be happened due to sport and dance activities. 15] Dilip Dattatraya Landage (PW­4) Exh.34 is the investigating officer. His evidence is formal in nature. Annapurna Shamrao Mhaske (PW­5) Exh.53 is the lady police officer who recorded statement of prosecutrix. However, I have repeatedly mentioned that prosecutrix is not supporting to the case of prosecution. She is the important witness, but unfortunately, she is not supporting to the case of prosecution. She is the only witness who can depose about the alleged sexual assault. However, as she is not supporting therefore, prosecution has failed to prove the charges levelled against accused. Hence, I answered point Nos. 2 to 4 in the negative. In view of finding of above points accused deserves to be acquitted. In the result, I proceed to pass following order :­ ..8.. Spl.C.No.13/2015(J) ORDER 1] Accused Baban Sopan Vishwas is hereby acquitted U/Sec. 235(1) of Cr.P.C.for the offence punishable U/Sec. 376, 506 of the Indian Penal Code, Sec.4 & 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and Under Sec. 67, 67(a) of Information Technology Act. 2] Bail bond of accused stands cancelled and surety is discharged. 3] Muddemal articles No. 1 to 4 & 6 to 9 being worthless, be destroyed after appeal period is over. Muddemal property no.5 Samsung mobile phone be returned to accused after appeal period is over. ( N. R. Pradhan ) Vasai Special Judge, Dt.:­17/3/2018 under Protection of Children from CIS No.2300013/2015 Sexual Offences Act,2012, Vasai. Saa

P. Divate ) 12 of 2017 ( CNR : MHTH23-000185-2017 ) Exhibit No. 69 State of Maharashtra .. Complainant through Tulinj police station Crime no. I-600/2016 versus 1/ Ajay Bhiku Kharva, Age 25 years, Residence – Near church, Bhim Dongri, Nalasopara(E) 2/ Sushila Ajay Kharva, Age 24 years, Residence – Near church, Bhim Dongri, Nalasopara(E) .. Accused Smt. K.M.Khandagale, A.P.P. for the State. Smt. Varsha Birade, advocate for accused. .. 2 .. 12/2017 Judgment CNR : MHTH23-000185-2017 JUDGMENT (Delivered on this 26th day of March, 2018) 1] Accused number 1 stands trial for the offence punishable under section 342, 376 of Indian Penal Code and under section 4 of protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. 2] Accused number 2 stands trial for the offences punishable under section 342, 109, 114 of Indian Penal Code and under section 16 and 17 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. 3] Prosecution’s case, in brief, is as under: – Complainant victim child girl is 14 years old. She is residing at the given address in a complaint along with parents, 5 brothers and one sister. Her parents are doing the business of selling old clothes. Her parents use to left house at 9 AM and used to come back at 5 PM. Accused are the neighbours. Complainant did not have TV set. Complainant and her brother used to go at the house of accused to see TV programs. 4] On 28 October 2016 at about 5 PM complainant and her sister were present at home. She had friendly relations with accused who was residing in the same vicinity of her residence. On 17/09/2015 at around 7.30 p.m. the informant went for worshiping at Sarvajanik Ganesh Mandal in her area alongwith friends. They were chit­chatting surrounded by noisy situation when the accused made a phone call to the informant. She went to the silent place for talking to the accused but he came there who forciably dragged her to the first floor of the under construction building situated nearby. He caught hold the waist of the informant and hugged her. The informant tried to separate from him by pushing but he fell her on the heap of the bricks. The informant sustained scratches on her hand and leg. He again dragged her by pulling hairs. He threatened and hurled abuses to her. The friends of informant came to the spot after hearing the screaming of informant. She told them about that incident while they rescued her. On 18/9/2015 the accused threatened informant to kill if she exposed him. Therefore, the informant filed the report of that incident on 18/9/2015 to the Virar Police Station 3] After investigation, the charge­sheet was filed in this court against the accused. A charge for offences punishable under Ss. 354, 354(D), 323, 504 and 506 of IPC 1860 and under Ss.7, 8, 9(i) of the POCSO Act 2012 was framed against accused, to which he denied and .. 3 .. The prosecution has thereafter, filed the pursis Ext.14 for closing the evidence. As no incriminating substance is found against accused, hence his statement under S.313 of Cr.P.C is not recorded. 4] On the basis of the material on record, the points arise for my determination are answered for the reasons as under ­ Points Findings 1. Not proved. voluntarily caused hurt to victim girl on his hand and legs by pushing her on the ground ? 5. Whether prosecution has proved that accused .. Not proved. intentionally insulted victim girl by abusing and thereby gave provocation to the victim girl to break public peace ? 6. Whether prosecution has proved that accused .. Not proved. committed criminal intimidation by threatening the victim girl? .. 4 .. Judgment Spl. Case No.5/2016. CNR NO.MHTH23­000231­2016. 7. Whether prosecution has proved that accused .. Not proved. committed sexual assault on the victim girl by touching her waist ? 8. Whether prosecution has proved that accused .. Not proved. committed sexual assault on the victim girl ? 9. Whether prosecution has proved that accused .. Not proved. committed sexual assault causing grievous hurt­scratches on the hand and legs of the victim girl ? 10. What is the order ? .. As per final order. REASONS 5] Point Nos. 1 to 9 : The prosecution, to prove the accusation, has mainly examined the informant ­ Child at Ext.No.11 and her mother (P.W.No.2) at Ext. No.13. They both have not supported to the prosecution case. The informant deposes mainly about her family background and her prior acquaintance with the accused. She has specifically stated that her family members disliked the accused hence they refused her to get marry with him. While describing the incident, informant deposes that while she was talking with her friends including the accused, her mother came there and dragged her away. This much is the testimony of informant­Child. It does not disclose any incriminating material against the accused hence the questions like cross examination were permitted to the prosecution to be asked under S. 154 of the Indian Evidence Act 1872. But the prosecution therein also has not found any supporting evidence to its present case. .. 5 .. Judgment Spl. Case No.5/2016. CNR NO.MHTH23­000231­2016. 6] Informant­Child's mother (P.W.No.2) deposes at Ext. No.13 about in the relevant time the Child was taking education in Viva College while at the time of incident the Child went for participating in the celebration on the occasion of Ganpati festival. She further deposes that she disliked the talking of Child with accused there hence she brought Child back to the house. This evidence certainly neither supports to the prosecution nor reveals any incriminating material against the accused. The prosecution thereafter has presented the closure preacipe at Ext. No.14 and thus has not led any evidence further. 7] The available evidence on record discloses that the Child had friendly relations with the accused which was disliked by her family members. The obvious result of lodging police report in the instant situation is evident. The close relations of informant and accused do not give even any traces of incrimination as per the evidence of prosecution to attract the offences as charged under of Prevention of Child from Sexual offences Act ( POCSO Act). Shri.Chetan Patil for the accused JUDGMENT (Delivered on 21­01­2017) The accused is facing trial for the offences punishable u/s.354, 506 of the Indian Penal Code (hereinafter referred to as IPC) and under Sec.8, 9(1)(n) of Protection of 2 Spl.Case No.12/16 Children from Sexual Offences Act,2012 (hereinafter referred to as POCSO Act). The case of prosecution in short is as under :­ 2] Informant is the victim,who lodged report before Vasai Police Station on 28­1­2015. She informed that accused is her brother. In the month of November 2014 when she and accused went in Suruchi Baug area for collecting plastic garbage. At that time, in isolated place, the accued moved his hand from her body and pressed her chest and outraged her modesty. 3] Again on 10­1­2015 accused repeated said act when no one was present in the house and outraged her modesty. Her elder brother came on 14­10­2015 from his work, at that time the victim narrated her the incident and then they decided to lodge complaint and accordingly the complaint was lodged. 4] On the basis of said information, crime No.I­13/15 lodged against the accused for the above offences. Investigating officer prepared spot panchanama, recorded statement of witnesses and after completion of investigation, filed chargesheet against the accused. 5] My Ld. predecessor framed charge at Exh.4 against the accused. Charge was read over and explained to accused. He pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. The defence of the accused emerges from the statement u/s.313 of Cr.P.C. is of total denial. 3 Spl.Case No.12/16 6] Following points arise for my consideration,to which I have recorded my findings against them for the reasons to follow­ POINTS FINDINGS 1]Whether prosecution proves that in November 2014 and on 14­1­2015 at Malonde village,Suruchi Baug and in the residential premises of complainant, accused being the real brother of victim minor girl used criminal force to victim girl and moved his hands from her body In the negative. and pressed her chest and thereby outraged her modesty and thereby committed offence punishable u/s.354 of I.P.C.and Sec.8, 9(1)(n) of POCSO Act of sexual assault ? 2]Whether prosecution proves that on the above mentioned period, time and place accused committed criminal In the negative. intimidation by threatening to victim girl to kill the children of their elder brother if she will disclose the incident to anybody and thereby committed offence punishable u/s.506 of I.P.C.? 3] What order ? Accused acquitted. 7] Heard ld. A.P.P. Smt. Moholkar and ld. Adv.Shri. Chetan Patil for the accused. 8] In order to prove its case, prosecution has examined PW1 Radhika Kanti Waghari at Exh.12, PW2 Leelabai Kanti Waghari at Exh.13, PW3 I.O.Rajendra Balkrishna Varade at Exh.14. 4 Spl.Case No.12/16 REASONS As to Point No.1 & 2 :­ 9] At the outset, it has to be mentioned here that the victim and her mother are not supporting to the case of prosecution. The deposition of victim (PW1) is at Exh.12. She deposed that accused is her brother. Accused was working as a labour. She further stated that in the month of November 2014 she had not gone along with accused and accused had not done any wrong or illegal act with her. She admitted that she lodged complaint against accused on 28­1­2015. However, she denied that she stated the contents mentioned in portion mark A of her complaint. 10] Leelabai who is mother of victim (PW2 Exh.13) also not supporting to the case of prosecution. She deposed that victim is her daughter and accused is her son. She denied that her daughter told her that accused had done wrong act with her. She denied that she stated the contents of portion mark 'A' of her statement. 11] The prosecution has examined investigating Officer Rajendra Varade (PW3 Exh.14). He is the formal witness. The material witness i.e. victim and her mother are not supporting to the case of prosecution. Therefore, there is absolutely no evidence against accused. Therefore, prosecution has failed to prove the charges against accused. I, therefore answer points No.1 & 2 in negative. 5 Spl.Case No.12/16 12] In view of above discussion, accused deserves to be acquitted. It is pertinent to note here that though bail order was passed during the trial, accused could not furnish the surety because he is poor and therefore though bail order was passed he was in jail. Considering it, I am of the view that for the compliance as per Sec.437­A of Cr.P.C. it is necessary to release accused on his personal bond. I, therefore pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused Anil Kanti Waghari is hereby acquitted u/s.235(1) of Cr.P.C.for the offence punishable u/s.354,506 of I.P.C.and Sec.8,9(1)(n) of POCSO Act. 2] Accused is in jail. He be released forthwith,if not required any other offence. 3] He is directed to give personal bond of Rs.15,000/­ in compliance of section 437­A of Code of Criminal Procedure,1973. Vasai. I conclude that evidence of complainant/victim and her mother is not trustworthy and reliable. Their evidence is not sufficient to bring accused to the home of guilt beyond reasonable doubt. I have answered point no.1 and 2 in negative. As regards point no.3 ­ 13] In view of my findings to point no.1 and 2, I hold that evidence of prosecution witnesses is not sufficient to bring home guilt of accused beyond all reasonable doubt. I have answered point no.3 accordingly. I proceed to pass following order ­ ORDER 1} Accused Aslam Anwar Khan is acquitted under section 235(1) of Cr.P.C. of charge for offences punishable under section 376(2), 506 of Indian Penal Code and section 4 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 2} Accused be released from jail forthwith if not required in any other crime. 3} In view of mandate laid down in section 437A of Cr.P.C., accused is directed to execute P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­. He shall undertake to appear before appellate court on receipt of notice of appeal. Date : 29.11.2017 ( M. P. Divate ) Additional Sessions Judge­1, Vasai.

As to Points No.2 & 3 :­ These points are interlinked to each other,hence they are decided simultaneously. 10] Learned APP has submitted that the victim is merely 9 years old and she cannot falsely implicate any person. He submitted that the prosecution has proved the case beyond reasonable doubt against the accused through the evidence of PW­1 victim, PW­2 complainant, PW­3 Sampat Giri and through other witnesses. She deposed that on 23/11/2015 at about 8 p.m., she was playing near the school with her friend Sampat. At that time accused who also known as Babu came there and he told her that he ..7.. She narrated the incident to the police. She identified the accused before the Court. 12] In the cross­examination question was put to the victim that whether she knows the meaning of Chedchad ( NsMNkM ). She replied she did not know the meaning of Chedchad ( NsMNkM ). Learned advocate for the ..8.. Spl.C.No.16/16 (J) accused submitted that the word Chedchad ( NsMNkM ) is mentioned in the police statement of victim and if victim do not know the meaning of said word, then how said word find place in her police statement. Learned advocate for the accused also draw my attention towards the admission that the victim has admitted that when her statement was recorded at that time she was stating as per the say of lady police and her mother. Therefore, she submitted that the victim is tutored witness and her evidence cannot be believed. However, the victim is 11 years old when she was giving the deposition. One cannot take doubt on the version of victim only on the ground that she do not know the meaning of word Chedchad ( NsMNkM ). No doubt, victim has admitted that at the time of recording her police statement she was stating as per the lady police and her mother. However, she voluntarily stated before the Court that she was stating what was happened with her and therefore, the objection raised by the learned advocate for the accused are not sufficient to disbelieve the version of victim. 13] Learned advocate for the accused has submitted that the police recorded the statement of victim and at that time video shooting was done . Spl.C.No.16/16 (J) filed any application before the Court asking to verify the CD of statement before the Court. Secondly, the evidence of victim is very reliable, cogent and therefore, I am of the view that objection raised by the learned advocate for accused regarding video shooting of her police statement is not sufficient to discard the evidence of victim. 14] Another important witness is PW­3 Sampat Mahadev Giri. He is only 12 years old boy. At the time of incident he was taking education in 3 rd standard. On 23/11/2015 at about 8:30 p.m., he was playing with the victim near their house. Spl.C.No.16/16 (J) 19] The prosecution has examined spot panch Anil Balu Jadhav (PW­6 Exh.26). Sec. 10 is aggravated form of the Sec. 8 of POCSO Act and therefore, I held the accused guilty under Sec. 10 of POCSO. The prosecution has also proved that the accused committed offence punishable U/Sec.354 of I.P.C. There is evidence on record that accused committed criminal intimidation by threatening the victim ..15.. Spl.C.No.16/16 (J) not to disclose his act. Therefore, the prosecution has proved that the accused committed an offence punishable under Sec. 506 of IPC. Therefore, I hold accused guilty for the offence punishable u/s.10 of POCSO Act, under Sec.354, 363 & 506 of I.P.C. Therefore, I answer points No.2, 3 and 4 in affirmative. 25] I take pause here to hear the accused and ld.A.P.P.on the point of sentence. Vasai. (N.R.Pradhan.) A.P.P. on the point of sentence. 27] Accused submitted that false case is filed against him, therefore, he submitted that minimum punishment may be awarded. A.P.P. has submitted that considering the age of victim maximum punishment be awarded. ..16.. Spl.C.No.16/16 (J) 29] Minimum punishment as prescribed for the purpose of sexual assault U/Sec. 10 of POCSO Act is five years and as per Sec.354 maximum punishment is three years. Special Case No. 18/2016 Judgment 4] Charge under section 376(2) of Indian Penal Code and section 4 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act is framed against accused at Exhibit 8 and explained to him in Hindi. His defence is that of total denial. 5] After going through the evidence of prosecution witnesses and police papers on record, following points arise for my determination. Whether prosecution has proved that since July, 2015 onwards for three months, in room no.5 Coral Apartment, near Baba ground, Virar(W), accused has committed rape / penetrative sexual assault on victim­ girl age 17 years ? In the negative. 2. What order and sentence, if any ? Accused is acquitted. REASONS As regards point no.1 ­ 6] I have heard learned A.P.P. for the State and learned advocate for accused. A.P.P. submitted that unfortunately victim and her mother have not supported case of prosecution. However, evidence of medical officer P.W.1 Dr. Pallavi Saha, evidence of police station officer P.W.5 A.P.I. Rekha Londhe and investigation officer P.W.3 Nagnath Dhone, P.I., is fully consistent and corroborative with the story of prosecution. Victim narrated incident in detail to her. Victim narrated before police station officer that accused developed intimacy with victim. They were in love with each other. Accused promised her to marry and had forcible intercourse with her under such pretext. Complainant became pregnant. Prosecution has proved the facts narrated by the complainant and proved complaint Exhibit 43. A.P.P. submitted that investigation officer has completed investigation. He has collected samples of victim girl, accused and samples of aborted fetus and sent for DNA test. DNA test report is filed on record. It is crystal clear from DNA test report that victim and accused are biological parents of aborted fetus. All these circumstances have been established by the prosecution. 8] A.P.P. has invited my attention on section 29 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and submitted that presumption is available to presume that accused has committed an offence under section 3 of the Act. Learned A.P.P. has submitted that victim girl and her mother have purposely deposed false facts to save accused. However, report of DNA test is sufficient to prove that victim girl and accused are the biological parents of the aborted fetus. Victim was pregnant and was admitted in hospital for abortion. A.P.P. prayed to place reliance on the evidence of prosecution witnesses and to convict the accused. .. 5 .. Special Case No. 18/2016 Judgment 9] Advocate for accused submitted that evidence of victim and her mother is contradictory. Their evidence is not consistent and corroborative with the story of prosecution. Advocate has submitted that identity of the girl who was admitted in hospital of Dr. Pallavi Saha has not been proved beyond all reasonable doubt. Advocate submitted that another minor girl might have been admitted in said hospital for the purpose of abortion by her mother. There is possibility that said girl and woman might have disclosed name of the present victim and possibility of misrepresentation cannot be ruled out. There is possibility that blood sample of said another girl might have been collected under the name of present victim girl. Thus, prosecution fails to prove identity of the victim girl. 10] Advocate submitted that evidence of victim girl and her mother is not fully consistent and corroboration with the story of prosecution. Their evidence is self­contradictory. Victim never claimed that present applicant/accused has committed rape on her. In these circumstances, evidence of prosecution witnesses does not appear to be trustworthy and reliable and creates doubt. Prosecution fails to prove guilt of accused beyond all reasonable doubt.
