A.P.P. declared complainant hostile and cross­examined in length by putting suggestion. Witness has denied each and every suggestion. Witness has also denied facts which comes to be recorded in the complaint. A.P.P. confronted this witness. 16] Prosecution has examined P.W.4 lady A.P.I. Rekha Londhe. She deposed that she received letter Exhibit 11 from Mamta Nursing Home. Police station officer suggested her to go in hospital and to record statement of victim. She went in hospital. She noticed that the girl Seeta was admitted in hospital for the purpose of abortion. Said girl was below 18 years and unmarried. Mother was present thee. She inquired with victim and mother. Victim made allegation that present accused came at her house in absence of .. 8 .. Special Case No. 18/2016 Judgment parents, promised to marry and had forcible intercourse with her. Victim narrated incident in detail. She has recorded complaint Exh.43. She has obtained signature of complainant and her mother below the complaint. She has submitted complaint before the police station officer alongwith report Exhibit 46. 17] P.W.3 Nagnath Dhone, P.I., deposed that he received complaint Exhibit 43 and F.I.R. Exhibit 44 for investigation. He visited spot of incident in presence of panchas and prepared panchnama Exhibit 19. He issued letter to medical officer and requested to preserve aborted fetus for the purpose of DNA test. Medical officer preserved the aborted fetus in container and handed over to him. He prepared panchnama Exhibit 29. He issued letter Exhibit 43 and sent the container to F.S.L. Kalina. He issued letter to medical officer. He has collected kits of DNA from F.S.L. Kalina. He has collected blood sample of victim and accused for the purpose of DNA. He sent samples alongwith letter Exhibit 26 and 27. He has collected sample and sent it for DNA test alongwith letter Exhibit 32. He wrote letter Exhibit 33 to Virar police station and requested to collect samples of victim for DNA test. Girl was referred to J. J. hospital However, said hospital directed to collect samples from local doctor. I.O. have deposed that victim has produced clothes before him. He has attached clothes and prepared panchnama Exhibit 28. Witness further deposed that P.W.2 Lakhpatidevi has deposed before him the facts contended in portion marked P1 at Exhibit 34. He completed investigation and filed charge­ sheet against accused. 18] In the present case accused has not disputed the circumstance of spot inspection panchnama Exhibit 26, circumstance .. 9 .. Special Case No. 18/2016 Judgment of recovery of clothes of victim, circumstance of recovery of clothes of accused and C.A. report. These documents are not sufficient to prove the material fact that present accused has committed penetrative sexual assault on victim girl. 19] Evidence of victim is not fully consistent and corroborative with the story of prosecution. Victim girl claims that she never went in hospital for the purpose of abortion. She has not narrated any fact to police. She has not filed any complaint. Moreover, she has denied her signature on complaint. In these circumstances I find substance in the submission of advocate. 20] Now, material question arises before me is as to whether present victim was admitted in hospital at the time of abortion. It was required to the prosecution to prove identity of present victim. Victim was not shown to P.W.1 Dr. Pallavi Saha and police officer P.W.5 Rekha Londhe. Identity of victim has not been proved in the present case. This is one of the missing circumstances in the present case. In these circumstances I find that defence made out by accused appears to be just and probable. I conclude that evidence of victim and her mother is self­contradictory. In these circumstances evidence of other witnesses is not sufficient to establish complete chain of facts and circumstances of the present case as well as identity of the girl who was admitted in hospital for abortion. I discard evidence of medical officer, police officer and investigation officer. I hold that prosecution fails to establish guilt of accused beyond all reasonable doubt. I have answered point no.1 in negative. P. T. O. .. 10 .. Special Case No. 18/2016 Judgment As to point no.2 ­ 21] In view of my findings to point no.1, I hold that evidence of prosecution witnesses is not sufficient to bring home guilt of accused beyond all reasonable doubt. I have answered point no.2 accordingly. I proceed to pass following order ­ ORDER 1} Accused Dharmendra Shivmurat Gupta is acquitted under section 235(1) of Cr.P.C. of charge for offences punishable under section 376(2) of Indian Penal Code and section 4 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 2} Bail bonds of accused stand cancelled and sureties are discharged. 3} Muddemal articles, being worthless, be destroyed after expiry of appeal period. 4} In view of mandate laid down in section 437A of Cr.P.C., accused is directed to execute P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­. He shall undertake to appear before appellate court on receipt of notice of appeal. Date : 07.12.2017 ( M. P. Divate ) Additional Sessions Judge­1, Vasai.

Victim deposed that her birth date is 15/11/1999. Prosecution has examined father of victim Vijay Bhosale PW­2 (Exh.17). ..10.. Spl.C.No.30/15(J) CNR No. MHTH23­000692­2015 However, he has not deposed about the age of victim girl. He deposed that victim girl is educated upto 5th std. It is on record that victim girl was going to work alongwith her mother. That means it is not case that at the relevant time victim girl was taking education. 18] Prosecution is only relying on the evidence of school leaving certificate of victim which is at Exh.37. Except school leaving certificate, prosecution has not produced any other evidence showing that birth date of victim girl is 15/11/1999 as mentioned in school leaving certificate. On perusal of school leaving certificate, it explicits that “it is duplicate”. There is also reference that from Z.P. School Pelhar Pada victim girl has taken admission in said school. That means the school which issued school leaving certificate is not a school where first time victim girl has taken admission. Prosecution has not examined headmaster of said school to prove the said school leaving certificate. Now, the question is whether simply filing of school leaving certificate on record without examining headmaster of the school can be stated that the said school leaving certificate is provided. To solve this question it is profitable here to refer the Judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Alamelu & Anr. Vs. State represented by Inspector of Police, SCC (2011) 2 page 385, the Hon'ble Supreme Court was dealing the case in which the appellant accused was convicted by the Sessions Court and said court conviction was upheld by the Hon'ble High Court and convicted him under Section 366 and 376 of I.P.C. While dealing said appeal the Hon'ble Supreme Court has made ..11.. Spl.C.No.30/15(J) CNR No. MHTH23­000692­2015 observation regarding the age proof of victim in para No.39 & 40 as under:­ 39. Considering the manner in which the facts recorded in a document may be proved, this Court in the case of Birad Mal Singhvi Vs. Anand Purohit1, observed as follows:­ "The date of birth mentioned in the scholars' register has no evidentiary value unless the person who made the entry or who gave the date of birth is examined . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ......................................................................... Merely because the documents Exs. 8, 9, 10, 11, and 12 were proved, it does not mean that the contents of documents were also proved. Mere proof of the documents Exs. 8, 9, 10, 11 and 12 would not tantamount to proof of all the contents or the correctness of date of birth stated in the documents. Since the truth of the fact, namely, the date of birth of Hukmi Chand and Suraj Prakash Joshi was in issue, mere proof of the documents as produced by the aforesaid two witnesses does not furnish evidence of the truth of the facts or contents of the documents. The truth or otherwise of the facts in issue, namely, the date of birth of the two candidates as mentioned in the documents could be proved by admissible evidence i.e. by the evidence of those persons who could vouchsafe for the truth of the facts in issue. No evidence of any such kind was produced by the respondent to prove the truth of the facts, namely, the date of birth of Hukmi Chand and of Suraj Prakash Joshi. In the circumstances the dates of birth as mentioned in the aforesaid documents have no probative value and the dates of birth as mentioned therein could not be accepted." The same proposition of law is reiterated by this Court in the case of Narbada Devi Gupta Vs. Birendra Kumar Jaiswal 2, where this Court observed as follows:­ "The legal position is not in dispute that mere production and marking of a document as exhibit by the court cannot be held to be a due proof of its contents. Its execution has to be proved by admissible evidence, that is, by the "evidence of those persons who can vouchsafe for the truth of the facts in issue"." 40. In our opinion, the aforesaid burden of proof has not been discharged by the prosecution. The father says nothing about the transfer certificate in his evidence. The Headmaster has not been examined at all. Therefore, the entry in the transfer certificate can not be relied upon to definitely fix the age of the girl. ..12.. Spl.C.No.30/15(J) CNR No. MHTH23­000692­2015 19] From this observation, it is crystal clear that without examining headmaster the school leaving certificate cannot be said to prove. 20] Ld. A.P.P. forcefully submitted that Dr. Sana Amir Vali PW­6 (Exh.30) deposed that victim girl was sent for ossification test to orthopedist. She deposed that orthopedist sent report to her and as per said report age of patient was 15 to 17 years old. Therefore, according to Ld. A.P.P. from medical evidence also prosecution proved that at the relevant time prosecutrix was minor, therefore, there is no question of consent. 21] Admittedly, Dr. Sana Samir Vali PW­6 has not conducted ossification test of victim. The said test was conducted by orthopedist and report regarding ossification test is signed by orthopedist. Prosecution has not examined the doctor who conducted ossification test of victim and therefore, the report regarding ossification test is not duly proved by the prosecution and therefore, one cannot place reliance on said report. 22] Assuming that as per ossification test report, age of victim girl was in between 15 to 17 years old. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Alamelu & Anr. Vs. State represented by Inspector of Police, SCC (2011) 2 page 385 in para No. 41 observed as under:­ This margin of error in age has been judicially recognized by this Court in the case of Jaya Mala Vs. ..13.. Spl.C.No.30/15(J) CNR No. MHTH23­000692­2015 Home Secretary, Government of Jammu & Kashmir & Ors.3, In the aforesaid judgment, it is observed as follows:­ "......However, it is notorious and one can take judicial notice that the margin of error in age ascertained by radiological examination is two years on either side." 23] From this observation of the Hon'ble Supreme Court that the margin of error by radiological examination is two years on either side. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in above Judgment has further observed in para No. 42 as under: We are of the opinion, in the facts of this case, the age of the girl could not have been fixed on the basis of the transfer certificate. There was no reliable evidence to vouchsafe the correctness of the date of birth as recorded in the transfer certificate. The expert evidence does not rule out the possibility of the girl being a major. In our opinion, the prosecution has failed to prove that the girl was a minor, at the relevant date. 24] From this observation, it is crystal clear that unless and until headmaster of school is examined the school leaving certificate cannot be said to be proved. In this case, prosecution has not examined the headmaster of the school who issued school leaving certificate. Gurmit Singh & Ors. referred above ­ “In sexual offences delay in lodging of the FIR can be due to variety of reasons, particularly the reluctance of the prosecutrix or her family members to go to the police and complain about the incident which concerns the reputation of the prosecutrix and the honour of her family. It is only after giving it a cool thought that a complaint of sexual offence is generally lodged. Hence, even if there is some delay in lodging FIR in respect of offence of rape, if it is properly explained and the explanation is natural in the facts and circumstances of the case, such delay would not matter.” It was further observed in this authority that, “In the normal course of human conduct, an unmarried minor girl, would not like to give publicity to the traumatic experience she had undergone and would feel terribly embarrassed in relation to the incident to narrate it to others overpowered by a feeling of shame and her natural inclination would be to avoid talking about it to any one, lest the family name and honour is brought into controversy.” ..20.. Spl.C.No.31/15(J) 35] As per the Apex Court, the girl in a tradition bound non permissive society in India, would be extremely reluctant even to admit that any incident which is likely to reflect upon her chastity had occurred, being conscious of the danger of being ostracized by the society or being looked down by the society. 36] Therefore, the point to be stressed is that the delay in lodging the FIR in the case of sexual offences is not something to be looked into with suspicion but to be understood and appreciated, keeping in mind the social reality and the facts and circumstances of that particular case. That's why the Apex Court in the case of State of Punjab V. Ramdev Singh AIR 2004 SC 1290 while condoning the delay of around 17 days commented that ­ “Delay in lodging the FIR cannot be used as a ritualistic formula for doubting the prosecution case and discarding the same. Delay has the effect of putting the court on its guard to search if any explanation has been offered for the delay, and if offered, whether it is satisfactory or not. If the prosecution fails to satisfactorily explain the delay and there is possibility of embellishment in prosecution version on account of such delay, the same would be fatal to the prosecution. However, if the delay is explained to the satisfaction of the court, the same cannot, by itself, be a ground for disbelieving and discarding the entire prosecution version.” 37] It is also profitable here to refer the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in case of State of Punjab Vs. Gurmit Singh and other, AIR 1996 SC 1393. The Hon'ble Apex Court held that the delay in filing FIR for sexual offence, may not be even properly explained, but if found natural the accused cannot be given any benefit thereof. ..21.. Spl.C.No.31/15(J) 38] Herein the case therefore, one has to see whether the conduct of prosecutrix of not lodging the complaint immediately after the first incident was unnatural? whether the delay has resulted into embellishment in prosecution case? and whether the delay is properly and satisfactorily explained by the prosecution? 39] As observed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in AIR 2004 SC pg.no.1290 that the Court cannot look the fact of any sexual offence delay in FIR can be due to variety of reasons. 40] In this case, it is on record that initially prosecutrix was residing at Calcutta alongwith her parent. Then accused took her at Nallsopara. Prosecutrix has explained in her evidence that her father frequently used to threaten her and therefore, earlier she has not lodged complaint against her father. It is on record that she fled away from the house, then with the help of social worker she able to lodge complaint against her father. 41] Therefore, prosecution has satisfactorily explained the delay. The ground of delay in filing of FIR is not sufficient to disbelieve the entire case of prosecution which is otherwise trustworthy and reliable. 42] Ld. Advocate for the accused submitted that no injury marks were found on the person of prosecutrix and therefore, it creates serious doubt about the case of prosecution. It is profitable here to refer the judgment in ..22.. Spl.C.No.31/15(J) case of Gurucharan Singh Vs. State of Haryana AIR 1972 SC 2661, the Honourable Apex Court has held that­ “The absence of injury or mark of violence on the private part on the person of the prosecutrix is of no consequence when the prosecutrix is minor and would merely suggest want of violent resistance on the part of the prosecutrix. Further absence of violence or stiff resistance in the present case may as well suggest helpless, surrender to the inevitable due to sheer timidity. In any event, her consent would not take the case out of the definition of rape. ” 43] From the above observations, it is crystal clear that the Court cannot acquit the accused on the ground that no injury marks were found on the person of prosecutrix. 44] The evidence of prosecutrix found cogent, reliable and trustworthy. Her evidence is totally corroborated by the evidence of Dr. Nisha Nathu Thakare, (PW­3) Exh.23. 45] Conspectus of this discussion is that in this case, the sole testimony of prosecutrix itself is sufficient to clinch the guilt of accused. It is also supported by evidence of Dr. Nisha Thakare(PW­3) Exh.23 & evidence of social worker Dhanashree Yogesh Ghadage (PW­4) exh.26. In this case DNA report is very important and as per the DNA report the prosecutrix and accused are the biological parent of the baby. The argument advanced by counsel for accused that prosecution has not proved its case beyond reasonable doubt cannot hardly be accepted. ..23.. Spl.C.No.31/15(J) 46] Thus, after assessing the entire evidence on record in most dispassionate manner and also at the same time taking realistic and sensitive view which, this Court has come to an unmistakable conclusion that prosecution has succeeded in its case against the accused for the offence punishable under Sec. 376(2)(f)(h)(i)(m) & (n) of IPC and under Sec. 4, 5(i)(m)(n)(g) & (q) punishable U/Sec. 6 of POCSO Act. Therefore, I answered point Nos. 2 & 3 in the affirmative. 47] As I held the accused guilty for the offence punishable U/Sec. 376(2)(f)(h)(i)(m) & (n) of IPC and for the offence punishable U/Sec.4, 5(i)(m)(n)(g) & (q) punishable U/Sec. 6 of POCSO Act. Therefore, I take pause here to hear the accused and Ld.A.P.P.on the point of sentence. Vasai. (N.R.Pradhan.) Date:­21/2/2018 Special Judge, Under POCSO Act,Vasai 48] I heard accused, his advocate and Ld. A.P.P. on the point of sentence. 49] The accused submitted that he do not want to say anything about the punishment. Ld. Advocate for the accused submitted that it is his first offence, therefore, minimum punishment be awarded to him. 50] On the other hand, Ld.A.P.P. has submitted that the accused has committed heinous crime, therefore, maximum punishment be awarded to him. ..24.. Spl.C.No.31/15(J) 51] It is on record that the victim was residing alongwith accused. The prosecution has proved that the accused repeatedly committed rape on his daughter since the victim was 12 years old. Because of it two times she became pregnant. The accused has committed heinous crime and even did not spare his daughter for the satisfaction of his lust. The father is most respected and reliable person of every daughter. But to satisfy his lust, the accused has broken her confidence and has taken disadvantage of his helpless minor daughter. Therefore, I am of the view that this is a fit case to award maximum punishment. 52] Maximum punishment as prescribed for the penetrative sexual assault under Sec.4 & 6 of POCSO Act is life imprisonment and as per Sec.376(2)(f)(h)(i)(m) & (n)of I.P.C. maximum punishment is life imprisonment, which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person's natural life. As per Sec.42 of POCSO Act, offender found guilty of such offence shall be punished under this Act or Indian Penal Code as provided punishment which is greater in degree. As per Sec. 376(2)(f)(h)(i)(m) & (n)of I.P.C., maximum punishment is life imprisonment, and life imprisonment shall mean for the remainder of that persons natural life and therefore punishment prescribed in Sec.376(2)(f)(h)(i)(m) & (n) of I.P.C., is greater in degree. Therefore, I direct accused to suffer sentence U/ Sec.376(2) (f)(h)(i)(m) & (n) of I.P.C. ..25.. Spl.C.No.31/15(J) 53] After considering submissions of both the sides and considering the facts and circumstances of the case, I am of the view that following sentence is just and proper to meet the ends of justice. Hence, I proceed to pass the following order :­ ORDER 1] The accused Naim @ Mussa Taslim Shaikh is hereby convicted U/Sec. 235(2) of Cr.P.C. for the offence punishable U/S.376(2)(f)(h)(i)(m) & (n)of I.P.C. and he is sentenced to suffer life imprisonment and to pay fine of Rs.10,000/­(Rs. Ten thousand only) and in default to suffer Rigorous Imprisonment for three months. 2] The accused is entitled to get set off U/Sec. 428 of Cr.P.C.for the period already undergone in the jail. 3] Muddemal property seized in this crime, being worthless be destroyed after appeal period is over. 4] Copy of this judgment be given to the accused at free of costs. Sd/­ Vasai. (N.R.Pradhan) Date:­21/2/2018 Special Judge, CIS No.2300031/2015 Under POCSO Act, Saa Vasai

.. 1 .. Special Case No.50/2014 Judgment Presented on : 11.10.2014 Registered on : 11.10.2014 Decided on : 16.03.2016 Duration : 1 year 5 months 5 days In The Court of Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act), Vasai At Vasai (Presided over by S. J. Bharuka) Special Case No. 50 of 2014 Exhibit No. 29 The State of Maharashtra .. Complainant (through Nalasopara Police Station) versus Chandrakant Harishchandra Kadam .. Accused Age 29 years, Resident of room no.311, Sai Shraddha Apartment, in front of Rajiv Gandhi School, Nariyanagar, Moregaon, Nalasopara (E) Appearance ­ Smt. Moholkar, Special P.P. for State. Mrs. Sharada Patil, advocate for accused. JUDGMENT (Delivered on 16.03.2016.) .. 2 .. Special Case No.50/2014 Judgment The accused is charge­sheeted for offences punishable under section 354A, 506 of I.P.C. and section 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act (hereinafter in short referred to as ''P.O.C.S.O. Act''). 2] All the safeguards have been followed as per the directions of the Hon'ble High Court and Supreme Court and proceedings have been conducted In Camera. Keeping in view social object of preventing social victimisation of the victim­ child of sexual offence for which section 228A of I.P.C. has been enacted, I have chosen to describe her in the present judgment as 'victim'. 3] The prosecution case, in brief, is as under ­ i) Victim aged 15 years was staying with her mother and three sisters at room no.204, Shraddha Apartment, by the side of Rajiv Gandhi High School, Moregaon, Nalasopara. She was studying in 9th Std. in Moreshwar Vidyalay at Moregaon. Accused was staying in same building in room no.311 and victim was knowing him and he used to say 'bye' to her when she used to go school. ii ) On 21.06.2014 at about 8.00 p.m. victim and her younger sister Ayushi were watching TV in her house. At that time accused also came in their house and was watching TV with them. After some time when victim went inside kitchen, accused also went there following her and said to her that .. 3 .. Special Case No.50/2014 Judgment moles on her person were much pleasing and started having physical advances with her and embraced her and kissed her lips. Therefore, victim shouted and hearing her shouts, her younger sister Ayushi rushed to her and she also raised shouts and hearing their shouts, neighbouring persons gathered there and seeing all, accused fled away. Thereafter, victim went to Nalasopara Police Station and lodged report. 4] On the basis of F.I.R., C.R.No.I­359/2014 for offence punishable under section 354A, 506 of I.P.C. and section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act came to be registered. During investigation spot panchnama was drawn. Certificate showing date of birth of victim was obtained. Accused was arrested and arrest form was filled in. Statements of witnesses including the victim­girl were recorded and the proceeding of recording her statement was videographed. After completion of investigation, charge­sheet for offence punishable under section 354A, 506 of I.P.C. and section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act came to be submitted against the accused, to this Court, being Special Court under P.O.C.S.O. Act. 5] A charge for offence punishable under section 354A, 506 I.P.C. and section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act was framed against accused by my learned predecessor. Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. After examination of prosecution witnesses, statements of accused persons under .. 4 .. Special Case No.50/2014 Judgment section 313 of Cr.P.C. came to be recorded. The defence of accused is that of total denial and false implication. 6] On facts of the case, following points arise for my determination and my findings against them with reasons therefor are as under ­ Points Findings 1. Whether prosecution has proved that the victim­girl was minor at the time of incident ? Yes. 2. Whether prosecution has proved that on 21.06.2014 at about 8.00 p.m. in the dwelling house of victim, accused had physical contact and advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures, with victim girl by kissing and embracing her and thereby outraged her modesty ? Proved. 3. Whether prosecution has proved that during the course of same incident, accused committed sexual assault on the minor victim­girl by embracing her and kissing her lips with sexual intent ? Proved. 4. Whether prosecution has proved that during the course of same incident when the victim girl resisted, accused threatened her and abused her ? Not proved. 5. What order ? As per final order. .. 5 .. Special Case No.50/2014 Judgment REASONS 7] In order to establish allegations against the accused, the prosecution has examined following witnesses ­ P.W.1 victim­girl P.W.2 Priya Jitendra Aapkare P.W.3 P.I. Bajirao Kalantre, I.O. 8] The prosecution has relied upon following documentary evidence ­ Exh.13 Complaint Exh.14 Printed F.I.R. Exh.18 Spot panchnama Exh.19 Panchnama of videographing the recording of statement of victim Exh.21 Certificate of date of birth of victim Exh.25 Certificate of date of birth of victim 9] Learned A.P.P. Smt. Moholkar vehemently argued that the testimony of all the witnesses, so examined proves the guilt of the accused. She further submits that it is a settled principle of law that conviction can be based on the sole testimony of the victim of sexual assault without corroboration from any other evidence as the statement of the prosecutrix is more reliable than any other witness. She further submits that where the testimony of victim of sexual assault instills the confidence in court, the same can be relied for conviction of the accused. She further submits that first .. 6 .. Special Case No.50/2014 Judgment informant lodged F.I.R. immediately after the incidence and prosecution has proved all the charges levelled against the accused beyond reasonable doubt and hence, accused is liable to be convicted for the same. 10] Learned counsel for accused Mrs. Sharada Patil submits that testimony of prosecutrix P.W.1 is totally unreliable which is full of material contradictions, improvements and does not inspire confidence and creates doubt about her version. She further submits that accused has been falsely implicated by the prosecutrix as the relation between her and accused had strained. She further submits that when evidence of prosecutrix is found suffering from serious infirmities and inconsistent with other material facts, no reliance can be placed upon her evidence. She further submits that prosecution utterly failed to prove any of the alleged charges beyond reasonable doubt and hence, accused is entitled to be acquitted. 11] I have heard the rival contentions of the A.P.P. and counsel for accused and given thoughtful consideration to the arguments advanced by them and have also perused the evidence as well as the exhibited documents carefully. It is a case of sexual assault on minor girl and hence, I have taken as much care and caution as possible to evaluate and appreciate the evidence come on record. Bearing in mind .. 7 .. Special Case No.50/2014 Judgment submissions made by both the counsels and ingredients of alleged sections, now I proceed to discuss and appreciate the evidence led by the prosecution. As to Point no.1 ­ 12] To prove that the victim was minor at the relevant time, prosecution has produced on record certificate issued by Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai below Exh.21 and 25, It appears that earlier Exh.21 came to be filed on which there is one endorsement ''cancelled''. Hence, prosecution filed another birth date certificate of victim below Exh.25 and as per said certificate birth date of victim is 09.03.1999. It is pertinent to note that P.W.1 and her mother P.W.2 have also deposed the same date. There is no suggestion to any of witnesses that said date of birth is wrong. So considering documentary as well as oral evidence I come to the conclusion that victim was minor aged about 15 years at the time of alleged incidence and hence I answer point no.1 as 'proved'. As to point no.2 and 3 ­ 13] The moot point involved for consideration in the present matter is whether evidence adduced by prosecution, particularly testimony of victim P.W.1 is trustworthy, credible and worthy of reliance. To appreciate evidence of P.W.1 in .. 8 .. Special Case No.50/2014 Judgment proper perspective, it is necessary to consider the same alongwith testimony of P.W.2 simultaneously. 14] P.W.1 victim has deposed that she resides at Shraddha Apartment alongwith her mother and four sisters and accused resides in same building, who is known to her. She has further deposed that on 21.06.2014 her mother left home to attend her duty and she was present in the home alongwith her sisters. She has further deposed that her two sisters went to market to bring book and she alongwith her younger sister Ayushi was watching TV in the house. She has further deposed that accused came to her house and sat besides them, watching TV and when she went to the kitchen, accused followed her and kissed her lips after making physical advances. She has further deposed that she resisted the same act by pushing him and started shouting and Ayushi rushed there, who was frightened. She has further deposed that she informed the incidence to her mother and thereafter, went to the police station to lodge report. 15] In her cross­examination she has deposed that accused has two daughters, who used to come in her house and that when accused came to her house, he was under the influence of liquor. She denied the suggestion that accused just visited her house, watched TV and left her house and no such incidence was taken place as alleged. .. 9 .. Special Case No.50/2014 Judgment 16] P.W.2 Priya, who is mother of victim, has deposed that she is working as a security guard on shift basis and accused is resident of same building where she was residing. She has further deposed that on 21.06.2014 at about 8.45 p.m. she received call from her elder daughter Kajal who narrated the incidence to her. She has further deposed that when she returned home and inquired with the victim, she came to know that accused came to her house and committed sexual assault on victim. P.W.2 has deposed in the similar fashion like P.W.1 in respect of incidence. It was suggested to this witness also that accused was under the influence of liquor when he visited the house of victim. 17] After careful scrutiny of testimonies of above witnesses, it appears that there is consistency in their version, F.I.R. came to be lodged immediately after the incidence. On perusal of cross­examination of both the witnesses, it appears that it is suggested to both the witnesses that accused was present on the spot of incidence under the influence of liquor and he did nothing as alleged. So, by putting such suggestion defence admits presence of accused at the house of victim under the influence of liquor. In view of above­said evidence, presence of accused on the spot of incidence at the relevant time is proved by the prosecution and in view of the suggestions put up in cross­examination, practically accused admits that he was present there. .. 10 .. Special Case No.50/2014 Judgment 18] It is the defence of accused that he has been implicated in false case due to strained relations. It is pertinent to note that there is no suggestion to P.W.1 that due to strained relations between herself and accused, false case came to be filed. On the contrary, it was suggested to P.W.1 in cross­examination that daughters of accused used to come to her house. It was suggested to P.W.2 in respect of their strained relations, which she denied. So practically there is nothing on record which can indicate any motive for false implication of accused. If really relations between the parties had strained, then P.W.1 would not have allowed the accused to come to their house and watch TV with them or accused would not have gone to their house. It has come on record that father of victim is not residing with them and her mother is a working woman. No explanation has come on record from accused as to why he went to the house of victim in the absence of her mother and two sisters, that too under the influence of liquor. Suggestion put by the accused in cross­ examination reflects that there was cordial relation between accused and P.W.1. On the other hand, accused has taken defence that he has been implicated in false case. So it appears that contradictory stand has been taken by the accused. Hence, defence put forth by the accused that he was implicated in false case, does not appear to be probable and acceptable. .. 11 .. Special Case No.50/2014 Judgment 19] It is interesting to note that in the statement made by the accused under section 313 of Cr.P.C. he stated that case of the prosecution was false. During the cross­ examination of P.W.1 it was suggested to her that accused was present at the relevant time in the house of P.W.1 but no incidence occurred, as alleged. On perusal of statement under section 313 of Cr.P.C. he answered question no.9 as follows ­ Q.09 It has further come in the evidence of P.W.1 that you came to the home of victim and sat watching TV, at that time she was washing rice. What you want to say ? Ans. It is false. So, it is expected that he should have answered to the above­ said question that he was present there but nothing has happened as alleged by the victim, but he simply denied the same and this shows that accused has just taken stand of total denial, which is contrary to his defence. 20] In the case of Om Prakash vs. State of U.P. ­ 2006 ALL MR (Cri) 2394 (S.C.) Hon'ble Apex Court has held that if prosecutrix did not have strong motive to falsely involved person charged, Court should ordinarily have no hesitation in accepting her evidence. Hon'ble Supreme Court has also observed that the Indian woman has tendency to conceal such offence because it involves her prestige as well as prestige of her family. Only in few cases the victim­girl or .. 12 .. Special Case No.50/2014 Judgment the family members has courage to go before the police station and lodge a case. 21] In the present case suggestion given on behalf of defence that victim has falsely implicated the accused does not appeal for the reasons mentioned above. There is no reason come on record to show that a school­going tender­ age girl will falsely implicate the accused after scatting her own prestige and honour and would suffer pain and agony of being subjected to such an offence. 22] Learned advocate for accused submits that prosecution failed to examine any other independent witnesses to prove the alleged incidence. It is pertinent to note that as per the case of prosecution only P.W.1 was present in the kitchen when accused followed her there and kissed her lips and embraced her. It has come on record that other two sisters of victim had gone to market and only younger sister Ayushi was present alongwith victim in the house. So practically no purpose would have been served by examining any other witness as they are not the eye witnesses to the alleged incidence. If substantive evidence of witnesses who are examined, repose confidence, then non­examination of other independent witnesses cannot be treated as fatal to the case of prosecution. .. 13 .. Special Case No.50/2014 Judgment 23] It is pertinent to note that in order to take advantage of circumstances of failure to examine independent witnesses, reasonable opportunity must always be given to the investigation officer as to why such witnesses were not questioned, and same is not happened in the present case. It may not be lost sight of situation that presence of witnesses on the spot is one thing and anybody coming forward to give statement to the police is another thing. Moreover, it is not mandatory on the part of prosecution to examine each and every witness available to them. So I do not find any substance in the submission advanced by learned counsel for accused that prosecution failed to examine any other independent witness. 24] It is the case of accused that he was under the influence of liquor. It appears that though accused denied the alleged incidence, in the alternative, he wants to take advantage of section 85 of I.P.C. As per section 85 of I.P.C. if act is done under intoxication, it is not an offence when the thing which intoxicated him was administered to him without his knowledge or against his will. In the case in hand accused has not brought anything on record to show that he was compelled to take alcohol and someone administered him alcohol without his knowledge. So, he cannot take advantage of section 85 of I.P.C. Nothing has come on record from the side of defence to rebut presumptions under P.O.C.S.O. Act. .. 14 .. Special Case No.50/2014 Judgment 25] Defence counsel brought on record some omissions and contradictions. It is settled that minor omissions and contradictions are bound to happen and each omission is not fatal to the case of prosecution. In the present case omissions and contradictions are of very minor nature which are not fatal in nature and same are not helpful to the defence in any way to prove innocence of accused. 26] It is well settled law that to hold an accused guilty for commission of an offence of sexual assault/harassment, the solitary evidence of victim is sufficient, provided the same inspires confidence and appears to be absolutely trustworthy, unblemished and should be of sterling quality. When evidence of P.W.1 and 2 is evaluated in the light of settled principles of law, it appears that their deposition is natural and consistent, which inspire confidence and both witnesses appears to be trustworthy. In the case in hand judicial conscience of this Court has been satisfied after considering the case in totality, as discussed above. 27] Moreover, in view of section 29 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, when a person is prosecuted for committing any offence under section 3, 5, 7 and 9 of the Act, the special Court shall presume that the accused has committed the offence, unless the contrary is proved. Likewise, in view of section 30(1) of .. 15 .. Special Case No.50/2014 Judgment P.O.C.S.O. Act ''in any prosecution for any offence under this Act which requires a culpable mental state on the part of the accused, the Special Court shall presume the existence of such mental state but it shall be a defence for the accused to prove the fact that he had no such mental state with respect to the act charged as an offence in that prosecution''. 28] In the present case prosecution has discharged its burden by examining P.W.1. Nothing has come on record though she was cross­examined at length, her version on the core spectrum of the crime has remained intact while all other attendant materials matched the said version in material particulars which has enabled this Court for holding the accused guilty of the charge. Thus, accused is liable to be held guilty for offence under section 354A of I.P.C. and section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. Therefore, point no.2 and 3 are answered as 'proved'. As to point no. 4 ­ 29] The prosecution has not brought on record any such evidence about any threat causing alarm given to the victim by the accused, which is a necessary ingredient of the offence for the offence punishable under section 506 of I.P.C. Consequently, the prosecution has failed to prove the charge for the said offence and hence, accused is liable to be acquitted under said charge and hence, I answer point no.4 as 'not proved'. .. 16 .. Special Case No.50/2014 Judgment 30] In view of all above discussion and in the facts and circumstances of this case, I hold the accused guilty for offences punishable under section 354A of Indian Penal Code and section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. Accused is made aware that he is held guilty for offences punishable under section 354A of Indian Penal Code and section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and he can submit on the point of sentence. Hence, I take a pause to hear the accused on the point of sentence. Vasai, ( S. J. Bharuka ) Date : 16.03.2016 Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act) Vasai. Resumed. 31] Counsel for accused submitted that family of accused is depending upon him. It is his first offence and prayed for awarding minimum punishment. 32] Spl.P.P. submitted that offence is of serious nature involving a tender­aged girl. Accused committed the offence in the house of victim when no elderly person was present in the house of victim and prayed for imposing maximum punishment as provided in the Act. 33] It is settled principle of law that it is the duty of the Court while awarding sentence to ensure justice to both the parties and therefore, undue leniency in awarding sentence needs to be avoided as it does not have the .. 17 .. Special Case No.50/2014 Judgment necessary effect of being deterrent for the accused and does not re­assure the society that the offender has been properly dealt with. 34] The sexual offences against the children are on the rise at alarming proportion. Before enactment of P.O.C.S.O. Act sexual offences against children were not adequately addressed and hence, this new Act has been introduced. The object of this Act is that offenders should be given adequate penalties which should act as effective deterrence. Present offence is against minor girl which comes under the head of moral turpitude. Hence, accused is not entitled for any benefit under Probation of Offenders act. But keeping in view the age of accused and clear past record, he deserves some leniency in awarding sentence. 35] It is pertinent to note that Section 42 of P.O.C.S.O. Act provides that ''Where an act or omission constitutes an offence punishable under this Act and also under sections 166A, 354A, 354B, 354C, 354D, 370, 370A, 375, 376, 376A, 376C, 376D, 376E or section 509 of I.P.C., then, notwithstanding anything contained in any law for the time being in force, the offender found guilty of such offence shall be liable to punishment under this Act or under the Indian Penal Code as provides for punishment which is greater in degree''. .. 18 .. Special Case No.50/2014 Judgment 36] In this respect offence under section 354A(1)(i) of I.P.C. provides for punishment of rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both; whereas section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act provides for punishment of imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than three years but which may extend to five years, and also fine. In view of above­ mentioned legal position, the accused is liable for punishment under section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act only. In the result, I pass following order ­ ORDER 1) Accused Chandrakant Harishchandra Kadam is convicted under section 235(2) of Cr.P.C. for offences punishable under section 354(1)(i) of I.P.C. and section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. 2) Accused is sentenced to undergo R.I. for a term of three years and to pay fine of Rs.1,000/­ ; in default of payment of fine, he shall undergo further S.I. for 15 days, for offence punishable under section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. 3) In view of section 42 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, no separate sentence is awarded for offence punishable under section 354(1)(i) of Indian Penal Code. .. 19 .. Special Case No.50/2014 Judgment 4) Accused is entitled for set off as per section 428 of Cr.P.C. against substantive sentence, for the period he has already undergone during the investigation, inquiry or trial of this case. 5) Accused is acquitted of the charge for offence punishable under section 506 of Indian Penal Code. 6) Bail bonds of accused stand forfeited and sureties are discharged. 7) Muddemal property shown in the charge­ sheet i.e. cassette containing video­recording of the statement of victim­girl shall be destroyed after expiry of appeal period. Vasai ( S. J. Bharuka ) Date : 16.03.2016 Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act), Vasai

Sec. 4 & Sec. 5(1) r/w. Sec. 6 Of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter referred to as POCSO Act). The case of prosecution in short is as under :­ 2] Informant Smt. Laxmi Shankar Mourya, who is mother of victim lodged report before Nallasopara Police Station on 11/12/2014. She informed that victim was 17 years old and she was taking education in 11th std. Victim was also going to coaching classes. 3] On 3/12/2014 as usual victim had gone to her tuition on 9 a.m. and returned on 10 a.m. Then at about 12:30 p.m. victim had gone to her College and informant dropped her near the corner of College and had gone to Hospital. Usually victim used to come to house from College at about 6:15 p.m. However, on 3/12/2014 till 6:30 p.m. victim had not returned to her house. Therefore, informant had been to College ..3.. SPL.C.No.32/2015(J) of victim. Her College was closed. Then she had taken search of victim in nearby vicinity. However, she could not trace out victim. Then on 4/12/2014 she lodged missing complaint in Nallasopara Police Station bearing No. 83/2014. 4] Later on she came to know that on same day and time accused who was residing in front of building of victim also missing and therefore, she suspected that accused might have kidnapped her daughter and fled away. Therefore, she lodged this complaint. 5] On the basis of said information, crime No.I­774/2014 registered against the accused for the above offence. During investigation, it was revealed the accused kidnapped victim and took her to Faridabad. Therefore, the accused and victim were apprehended from Faridabad and brought to Nallasopra police station. There the statement of victim was recorded. As per statement of victim accused maintained sexual relations with her. As victim was minor therefore, IO added relevant Section of IPC and POCSO Act. He recorded statement of witnesses and after completion of investigation, filed chargesheet against the accused. ..4.. SPL.C.No.32/2015(J) 6] My Ld. predecessor framed charge at Exh.7 against the accused. Charge was read over and explained to accused. He pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. The defence of the accused emerges from the statement Under Sec.313 of Cr.P.C. is that total denial. 7] Following points arise for my consideration,to which I have recorded my findings against them for the reasons to follow ­ NO. POINTS FINDINGS 1] Whether the prosecution has proved that on 3/12/2014 victim .. No. was minor? 2] Whether the prosecution has proved that on 3/12/2014 at about 12:30 noon, when minor victim girl had gone to Kapol College, Nallasopara (E) the accused kidnapped her from lawful guardianship of her parents and committed an offence punishable under Sec. 363 of IPC ? .. No. 3] Whether prosecution has proved that after kidnapping said minor girl, during the period from 3/12/2014 to 24/3/2015 at Rameshwar Aptt., Pach Amba, Nallasopara (E), at Swaroop nagar, Delhi and Faridabad had forcible sexual intercourse with said minor girl and committed an offence ..5.. SPL.C.No.32/2015(J) punishable under Sec. 376 of IPC ? .. No. 4] Whether prosecution has proved that on the given date, time and place committed aggravated penetrative sexual assault on said minor girl by doing forcible sexual intercourse with her more than once and committed offences under Sec. 3 r/w. Sec. 4 & Sec. 5(1) r/w. Sec. 6 of POCSO Act ? .. No. 5] What order ? Accused acquitted. 8] Heard ld. A.P.P. Smt. Khandagale and Ld. Adv. Smt. Sharda Patil for the accused. 9] In order to prove its case, prosecution has examined in all PW­1 victim at Exh.14, PW­2 API & IO Dilip Dattatraya Landage at Exh.21, PW­3 Shankar Khunkhun Mourya at Exh.31 & PW­4 PSI Shankar Hanumant Jadhav, at Exh.35. Prosecution has relied on office copy of letter dt.25/3/2015 Exh.22, arrest panchanama Ex.23 seizure panchnama Exh.24, letter dt.25/3/2015 Exh.25, panchnamas of seizure of clothes of victim and accused at exh.26 & 27, muddemal receipts Exh.28 & 29, office copy of letter sent to CA, Kalina Exh.30 and complaint Exh.36. Prosecution has closed its evidence by filing purshis at Exh.33. ..6.. SPL.C.No.32/2015(J) REASONS As to Point No.1 to 3 :­ 10] At the outset, it has to be mention here that victim PW­1 (Exh.14) has not supported to the case of prosecution. She deposed that in the year 2014 she on her own accord left the house of her parent and went alongwith accused to Delhi and then to Faridabad and there they performed marriage. The learned APP has asked leading question to the victim. She denied that accused kidnapped her under the pretext of marriage and took her to Delhi. She also denied that accused maintained sexual relations with her without her consent at Delhi. She denied that at the relevant time she was below 18 years. She admitted that she performed marriage with the accused and both of them are cohabiting. She denied that she deposing falsely to save the accused. 11] The prosecution has examined father of victim (PW­3) at Exh.31. He deposed that victim is his daughter. In the year 2014 she was 17 years old and taking education in Kapol Junior College. She used to go to College daily at about 12:30 p.m., and used to return at about 6:30 p.m. On 3/12/2014 his wife informed him that victim had not returned to house ..7.. SPL.C.No.32/2015(J) till 8 p.m. Therefore, she lodged missing report in Nallasopara police station. On next day he came to know that accused who was residing in front of the building of victim is also missing. Therefore, his wife lodged complaint against the accused that he kidnapped victim. After three months police brought accused and victim and police handed over victim to him. On enquiry victim informed him that she and accused were resided at Delhi and performed marriage and maintained sexual relations. 12] The victim has categorically denied that at the relevant time she was below 18 years old. The IO has not filed original School Leaving Certificate alongwith chargesheet. The prosecution has not proved the school leaving Certificate as the original School leaving certificate is not produced on record. Neither victim(PW­1) nor her father (PW­3) deposed the birth date of victim. No cogent and reliable document is produced by the police regarding the age of victim on record. Therefore, prosecution failed to prove that at the relevant time victim was below 18 years. 13] The evidence of investigating officer Dilip Dattatraya Landage (PW­2) is formal in nature. ..8.. SPL.C.No.32/2015(J) Similarly the evidence of PW­4 is formal in nature. In this case, victim has admitted that she on her own accord left the house of her parent and went alongwith accused to Delhi and then to Faridabad and there they performed marriage and maintained sexual relations. The prosecution failed to prove that at the relevant time victim was below 18 years old. Victim admitted that she on her own accord left the house and she maintained sexual intercourse with accused as per her will and wish. The accused married with the victim and both of them are happily cohabiting. The prosecution has failed to examine complainant. Father of victim filed an application at Exh.32 and informed the Court that his wife is ill and therefore, she is not in a position to come and depose before the Court and hence, the complainant is not examined. 14] Considering the above evidence on record, I come to the conclusion that the prosecution has failed to prove the charges levelled against the accused. Accordingly, I answered the point Nos. 1 to 3 in the negative. In view of above findings accused deserves to be acquitted. I, therefore pass following order :­ ..9.. J. Bharuka) Special Case No. 42/2014 Exhibit No. State of Maharashtra, (through Valiv police station C.R.No.I-256/2014) ... Complainant versus Nitesh Mahadev Rakshe, … Accused Age 21 years, Resident of Vakipada, Naigaon (E), Taluka Vasai Appearance - Smt. U.P.Moholkar, learned A.P.P. for State. Mr. Santosh Khale, learned advocate for accused. JUDGMENT (Delivered on 20.02.2017) 1. Accused is charge-sheeted for offences punishable under section 376 of the Indian Penal Code and section 4, 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act (hereinafter in short ''P.O.C.S.O. Act''). .. 2 .. Special Case No.42/2014 Judgment 2. All the safeguards have been followed as per the directions of the Hon'ble High Court and Supreme Court and proceedings have been conducted In Camera. Keeping in view social object of preventing social victimisation of the victim of sexual offence for which section 228A of I.P.C. has been enacted, I have chosen to describe her in the present judgment as 'victim'. 3. The prosecution case, in brief, is as under - i} Victim is the minor daughter of the first informant. They were staying at Vakipada, Naigaon (E). Accused was also staying in front of their house and both families were knowing each other and were on visiting terms. ii} It is further case of prosecution that on 30.05.2014 victim was suffering from stomachache and was crying. Therefore, first informant inquired with her. At that time victim disclosed to her that on 18.04.2014 at about 11.30 p.m. accused had called her in his house and had committed forceful sexual intercourse with her and had warned her of dire consequences. It is further alleged that after said instance, accused had twice called victim at the house of his sister in night time and had committed rape on her. After knowing these facts, first informant lodged F.I.R. to Valiv police station. 4. On the basis of her F.I.R., offences punishable under section 376 of the Indian Penal Code and section 4, 6 of P.O.C.S.O. Act came to be registered vide C.R.No.I-256/2014 at Valiv Police Station. During investigation spot panchnama was prepared, hand-sketch of spot was drawn and its photographs were taken. Accused was arrested under panchnama. Clothes of victim and accused were seized under separate panchnama and .. 3 .. Special Case No.42/2014 Judgment both were referred for medical examination and their certificates were obtained. Accused voluntarily disclosed to produce his clothes which he had worn at the time of offence and then said clothes came to be seized under panchnama. Birth certificate showing date of birth of victim-girl was obtained. Statements of witnesses including victim were recorded. It was revealed that accused committed penetrative sexual assault on victim and at the relevant time she was minor, therefore, charge-sheet came to be filed against the accused for offences punishable under section 376 of the Indian Penal Code and section 4, 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act before this Court, it being Designated Court to try offence under P.O.C.S.O. Act. 5. A charge for offences punishable under section 376 of the Indian Penal Code and section 4, 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act was framed against the accused by my learned predecessor as per Exhibit 13 and its contents were read over and explained to him in vernacular. Accused denied the charges and claimed to be tried. After examination of prosecution witnesses, statement of the accused under section 313 of Cr.P.C. came to be recorded. Accused took defence of total denial and false implication. 6. I heard the learned A.P.P. and the learned counsel for the accused. Considering the facts of the prosecution case and submissions of both side, following points arise for my determination and I have recorded findings thereon for the reasons recorded below - POINTS FINDINGS 1 ) Does prosecution prove that at the time of her kidnapping and sexual assault, the victim-girl was 'child' as per the definition prescribed under P.O.C.S.O. Act ? Proved. .. 4 .. Special Case No.42/2014 Judgment 2 ) Does prosecution prove that on 18.04.2014 at 11.30 p.m. in his house, on 28.05.2014 at about 12.00 midnight and also between 18.04.2014 and 28.05.2014, in the house of his sister, accused committed forceful sexual intercourse with the victim-girl against her will, Not proved. without her consent ? 3 ) Does prosecution prove that on the given dates, time and place, accused committed penetrative sexual assault on victim-girl by doing forceful sexual intercourse with her against her will without her consent ? Not proved. 4 ) Does prosecution prove that on the given date, time and place accused committed sexual assault on the victim having physical contact and advances with her, which were involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overture? Not proved. 5 ) What order ? Accused is acquitted. REASONS 7. In order to establish its case, prosecution has examined in all eight witnesses - P.W.1 Victim-girl P.W.2 Sangita Bhalchandra Vartak P.W.3 Dr. Rashmi Prasannan P.W.4 Meena Ramesh Kene P.W.5 Rani Laxman Puri, A.P.I. 8. The documentary evidence relied upon by the prosecution is as under - Exhibit 36 Complaint Exhibit 40 Spot panchnama Exhibit 41 Hand-sketch of the spot. Exhibit 44 Panchnama of seizure of clothes of victim-girl .. 5 .. Special Case No.42/2014 Judgment Exhibit 45 Memorandum statement of accused Exhibit 46 Panchnama of seizure of clothes of accused Exhibit 31 Medical certificate of victim Exhibit 21 Birth certificate of victim Exh.51 & 52 Reports of chemical analysis 9. Learned A.P.P. argued that the testimony of all the witnesses proves the guilt of the accused. A.P.P. further submits that it is a settled principle of law that conviction can be based on the sole testimony of the victim of sexual assault without corroboration from any other evidence and in the present matter all the witnesses supported the case of prosecution. The statement of the victim is more reliable than any other witness. Where the testimony of victim of sexual assault instills the confidence in court, the same can be relied for conviction of the accused. A.P.P. further submits that prosecution has proved all the charges levelled against the accused beyond reasonable doubt and hence, accused is liable to be convicted for the same. 10. Learned counsel for accused Mr. Khale submits that testimony of victim P.W.1 and 4 is totally unreliable and does not inspire confidence and creates doubt about their version. He further submits that medical evidence does not corroborate the version of the victim as accused has been falsely implicated by P.W.1 and 4. He further submits that when evidence of victim is found suffering from serious infirmities and inconsistent with other material facts, no reliance can be placed upon her evidence. He further submits that prosecution utterly failed to prove any of the alleged charges beyond reasonable doubt and hence, accused is entitled to be acquitted. .. 6 .. Special Case No.42/2014 Judgment 11. I have heard the rival contentions of the A.P.P. and counsel for accused and given thoughtful consideration to the arguments advanced by them and have also perused the evidence as well as the exhibited documents carefully. It is a case of rape and hence, I have taken as much care as possible to evaluate and appreciate the evidence come on record. Bearing in mind submissions made by both the counsels and ingredients of alleged sections, now I proceed to discuss and appreciate the evidence led by the prosecution. 12. The accused is facing charge of committing sexual assault on the victim who was minor at the relevant time. In this regard, birth certificate issued by Gram Panchayat of Chandrapada, Taluka Vasai, is proved by P.W.1 in her evidence and as per the said certificate, her date of birth is 15.01.1998. It further appears that school leaving certificate is proved by P.W.2 Sangita Vartak who is head mistress in Zilha Parishad school, Vakipada, and as per said certificate also, date of birth of the victim is 15.01.1998. On perusal of evidence of Dr. Rashmi Prasannan it appears that as per radiological test age of victim is between 16 to 17 years at the time of examination of victim on 23.06.2014 and she proved age certificate which is marked as Exhibit 32. Considering all the documents on record and evidence of P.W.1, 2 and 3 that she was aged below 17 years and she was 'child' as defined in the Act. Hence, I answer point no.1 as 'proved'. 13] Now, the moot point involved for consideration in the present matter is whether evidence adduced by prosecution particularly testimony of victim P.W.1 and 4 is trustworthy, credible and worthy of reliance, in order to prove the allegation .. 7 .. Special Case No.42/2014 Judgment of repeated instances of rape by the accused. 14] On perusal of evidence of P.W.1 victim it appears that she has stated that accused committed forceful sexual intercourse initially 18.04.2014 and later on on 28.05.2014. It further appears that victim was well acquainted with accused. It further appears that accused promised to marry with victim but broke the said promise, hence, belated F.I.R. came to be filed on 20.06.2014. 15] On perusal of evidence of mother of victim, P.W.4 Meena Kene, it appears that she has admitted in cross- examination that once accused called victim at 11.30 p.m. and on another occasion, at 12.00 midnight and she did not ask victim not to go in such odd hours in night. She has further admitted that till lodging of F.I.R., victim did not make any grievance to her against accused. She has further admitted that once victim had consumed phenyl and on another occasion, she had also caused injury to herself by blade and this witness could not tell whether victim committed such act due to broken relationship with her earlier boyfriend. She further admits that accused was to marry on 22.06.2014 with another girl and due to her complaint dated 20.06.2014 he could not perform marriage. She further admits that victim has marks of lucoderma on her person. She further admits that it was her desire that accused should marry with victim. 16] After considering evidence of P.W.1 and 4 together, it appears that there was love affair between victim and accused and mother of accused was having support for the same, victim and her mother was having desire that accused should marry .. 8 .. Special Case No.42/2014 Judgment with victim, victim was suffering from lucoderma, accused was going to marry with another girl and hence, belated F.I.R. came to be filed on 20.06.2014 and no plausible explanation has come on record for such belated F.I.R. If really there had been forceful sexual intercourse as alleged, then victim would have informed the said fact to her mother. Admittedly, P.W.4 came to know about the sexual assault from victim and she has not witnessed any instance of sexual assault. So here considering the facts and circumstances in the present case, the delay to lodge F.I.R. after two months of first sexual assault itself is fatal to the case of prosecution. Strong desire of victim and P.W.4 that accused should marry with victim and when accused refused to marry with victim, lodging belated F.I.R., that too, just before two days of proposed marriage of accused, speaks in volume and shows that possibility of false implication cannot be ruled out. Hence, evidence of P.W.1 and 4 does not inspire confidence and it is not worth credible to rely upon. 17] On perusal of medical certificate of victim-girl at Exhibit 31 it appears that at the time of her examination no injury was found on body and no evidence of force / restraint or penetrative assault was found. It is opined therein that evidence of sexual intercourse/assault cannot be ruled out however final opinion is kept pending till receipt of F.S.L. report. P.W.3 Dr.Rashmi Prasannan has stated that on perusal of said reports it is not possible to give any opinion whether sexual intercourse had taken place or not. Reports of chemical analysis at Exhibit 51 and 52 give negative finding about detection of blood or semen on the clothes of accused and victim and on the nail clipping, pubic hair, vaginal, cervical and vulval swab and blood sample of victim. So evidence of doctor and the findings of .. 9 .. Special Case No.42/2014 Judgment chemical analysis are not helpful for the prosecution to prove the fact that victim was sexually assaulted. In this backdrop evidence of P.W.1 again creates doubt whether any sexual assault was really taken place as alleged. 18] P.W.5 is investigation officer who has deposed in her evidence about the investigation carried out by herself. She proved the spot panchnama Exhibit 40, hand-sketch map of the spot Exhibit 41, arrest panchnama Exhibit 43, clothes' seizure panchnama of victim Exhibit 44, memorandum statement given by accused Exhibit 45, clothes' seizure panchnama of accused Exhibit 46. 19] Learned A.P.P. submits that in rape cases victim is not an accomplice to the crime and her evidence cannot be tested with suspicion and she placed reliance in case of State of T.N. vs. Ravi alias Nehru – 2006 ALL MR (Cri) 2356 (S.C.) There is no dispute about the legal proposition observed in above-said case but considering factual matrix of the case, it is not helpful to the prosecution. 20] Learned A.P.P. submits that if victim did not have strong motive to falsely involve person charged, Court should ordinarily have no hesitation in accepting her evidence and she placed her reliance in the case of Om Prakash vs. State of U.P. - 2006 ALL MR (Cri) 2394 (S.C.) I have gone through said judgment and it appears that in the said matter victim was adult, married who was full of understanding and accused was caught red-handed and there was one eye witness. In the present case there is delay of two months in lodging F.I.R. Moreover, motive has also come on record for the false .. 10 .. Special Case No.42/2014 Judgment implication of accused as he refused to marry with victim and he was going to marry with another girl and admittedly there is no eye witness in the present case. Hence, the ratio laid down in the case cited supra is not applicable here in the given facts and circumstances. 21] Learned A.P.P. has also submitted that there was no bodily injury on the person of victim, was no ground to reject the case of prosecution and sole statement of victim can be made the basis for conviction of accused and it may not be even necessary to have a corroboration from other sources and placed reliance in the case of State of Maharashtra vs. Suresh Shankar Jadhav – 2009(3) Mh.L.J. (Cri) 22. In the said case victim was 12 years old and she was found in the custody of accused and her version was also corroborated by the deposition of her brother and report of F.S.L. In the said matter doctor has not supported the case of prosecution and hence Hon'ble High Court has observed that sole statement of victim can be made the basis for conviction of accused and it may not be even necessary to have a corroboration from other sources. In the present case conduct and evidence of victim itself is not cogent and trustworthy and is not corroborated by any other witness and medical evidence. Moreover, in the said judgment Hon'ble Court further observed that statement of victim satisfies the judicial conscience, then there is no need of corroboration from any other source. In the case in hand judicial conscience of this Court has not been satisfied after considering the case in totality as discussed above. So the judgments cited by the learned A.P.P. are not helpful to the prosecution considering the facts and circumstances of the .. 11 .. Special Case No.42/2014 Judgment present case. 22] Learned A.P.P. further submits that though there is delay of two months in lodging the F.I.R., considering age and relation of victim it is not fatal to the case of prosecution and she placed her reliance in the case of Bhiku Tukaram Jadhav vs. State of Maharashtra – 2012 CRI.L.J. 1129 In the said case accused sexually assaulted his minor daughter repeatedly who was 12 years old and victim disclosed said fact when she became pregnant. In the present matter accused did not use to reside with victim and there is no close relation between them. Moreover, her parents and other family members were available, whom she could have disclosed said incidence and she was 16 to 17 years old at the relevant time. So facts are different than the case cited supra and hence same is not helpful to the prosecution. It is settled principle of law that in criminal cases question of precedent particularly relating to appreciation of evidence is really of no consequences and each case has to be considered in the background of factual scenario. 23] On the contrary, in case of Rai Sandeep alias Deepu Vs. State - (2012) 8 SCC 21, it has been held that - ''In our considered opinion, the ‘sterling witness’ should be of a very high quality and caliber whose version should, therefore, be unassailable. The Court considering the version of such witness should be in a position to accept it for its face value without any hesitation ''. In the said judgment Hon'ble Court further observed that ''To be more precise, the version of the said witness on the core spectrum of the crime should remain intact while all other attendant materials, namely, oral, documentary and material .. 12 .. Special Case No.42/2014 Judgment objects should match the said version in material particulars in order to enable the Court trying the offence to rely on the core version to sieve the other supporting materials for holding the offender guilty of the charge alleged.'' 24] In case of Pratap Mishra vs. State of Orissa – (1977) 3 SCC 41 it has been held that where the oral evidence of the victim is not supported by the medical evidence, it is dangerous to punish the accused for rape solely on the basis of her oral evidence. 25] In case of Mahesh Balkrishna Dandane vs. State of Maharashtra reported in [2014]0 Supreme (Mah) 40072 it has been observed by the Hon'ble High Court that every breach of promise to marry cannot be said to be either a cheating or rape. A couple in love with each other may be having sexual relationship and realize that they are not compatible and sometimes love between the parties is lost and their relationship dries gradually, then earlier physical contacts cannot be said as rape. 26] There is no doubt that rape causes great distress and humiliation to the victim of rape but at the same time false allegation of committing a rape also causes humiliation and damage to the accused. An accused has also rights which are to be protected and the possibility of false implication has to be ruled out. The Supreme Court in Radhu vs. State of Madhya Pradesh – 2007 Cr.L.J. 4704 had in this context noted as follows - ''The courts should, at the same time, bear in mind that false charges of rape are not uncommon. There have also .. 13 .. Special Case No.42/2014 Judgment been rare instances where a person has persuaded a gullible or obedient daughter to make a false charge of a rape either to take revenge or extort money or to get rid of financial liability. Whether there was rape or not would depend ultimately on the facts and circumstances of each case. 27] In case of Abbas Ahmed Choudhary Vs. State of Assam - (2010) 12 SCC 115, the Hon’ble Supreme Court has held that ''We are conscious of the fact that in a matter of rape, the statement of the victim must be given primary consideration, but, at the same time, the broad principle that the prosecution has to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt applies equally to a case of rape and there can be no presumption that a victim would always tell the entire story truthfully. 28] Keeping in mind the above cited judgments, the testimony of victim has to be consistent and natural in line with the case of the prosecution and free from infirmities which inspire confidence in the Court. It cannot be presumed that the statement of the victim is always true or without any embellishment. When evidence of P.W.1 is evaluated in the light of case cited supra, it appears that her deposition does not inspire confidence and creates a doubt about her version which appears to be neither natural nor probable for the reasons discussed above. The version of the victim has not been corroborated by medical evidence and has not disclosed the true genesis of the crime. It would not be out of place to mention here that today there is a public outrage and a hue and cry is being raised everywhere that Courts are not convicting the rape accused. .. 14 .. Special Case No.42/2014 Judgment However, no man, accused of rape, can be convicted if the witnesses do not support the prosecution case or give quality evidence, as happened in the present case, which is already discussed above. It should not be ignored that the Court has to confine itself to the ambit of law and contents of the file as well as the testimonies of the witnesses and is not to be swayed by emotions or reporting in the media. 29] In the present case, non-credible evidence of P.W.1 and 4, delay in lodging F.I.R. and non-supporting medical evidence, made the foundation of prosecution case shaky and unbelievable. After considering all the evidence on record, I come to the conclusion that there is no cogent and reliable evidence has come on record to prove guilt of accused beyond reasonable doubt. Prosecution has failed to prove the charges levelled against accused. Therefore, I answer point no.2 to 4 as 'not proved'. In the result accused is entitled to be acquitted. Hence, I proceed to pass following order - ORDER Accused Nitesh Mahadev Rakshe is acquitted as per section 235(1) of Cr.P.C. of charge for offences punishable under section 376 of Indian Penal Code and section 4, 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 2) His bail bonds stand cancelled and sureties are discharged. 3) In compliance of provisions of section 437A of Cr.P.C. accused shall furnish P. B. of Rs.15,000/-. 4) Muddemal clothes and quilt, being worthless, be destroyed after expiry of appeal period. Date : 20.02.2017 ( S. J. Bharuka ) Additional Sessions Judge-1, Vasai

Case No. 51/2017 Judgment CNR : MHTH23­000732­2017 Accused stands trial for the offence punishable under section 363, 376 of Indian Penal Code and sec. 4, 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act ( in short P.O.C.S.O.
