1 Spl.Case No.34/15 Presented on­ :07­07­2015 Registered on­ :07­07­2015 Decided on­ :07­11­2016 Duration­ :1Y­4M­0D IN THE COURT OF SESSION JUDGE, VASAI. (Presided over by N.R.Pradhan,Addl.S.J.) Special Case NO. 34/2015. Exh The State. (Through Waliv Police Stn.) ­­­­­­­Complainant. V/s. Lala @ Mousam Azamali Khan, Age 18 years, R/at Lavdeep Bldg.,Room No.401, F Wing,Navjivan, Tal.Vasai (E), Dist.Palghar. –­­­­­­ Accused. Offences punishable u/s.354, 323 of the Indian Penal Code and Sec.8 & 10 of Prevention of Child Sexual Offences Act. Appearances­ A.P.P. Smt.Moholkar for the State. Adv. Shri Ketan Barot for the accused (appointed through legal aid). JUDGMENT (Delivered on 07­11­2016 ) The accused is facing trial for the offences punishable u/s.354, 323 of the Indian Penal Code (hereinafter referred to as IPC) and under Sec.8 and 10 of Prevention of 2 Spl.Case No.34/15 Child Sexual Offences Act (hereinafter referred to as POCSO Act). The case of prosecution in short is as under :­ 2] Informant lodged report before Waliv police station on 7­04­2015. Informant is mother of victim. At the relevant time, victim was 12 years old and she was taking education in 7th Std. in Ambassador School at Waliv, Vasai (E). 3] On 7­04­2015 annual examination of victim was going on and therefore the school timing was from 7 a.m. to 10 a.m. On that day, after completion of examination, victim was returning to her house with her friend Noorsabha Aktar Chaudhary at about 10.15 a.m. When they reached at Dhumal Nagar,near Rajjak Steel shop, at this juncture, accused who was also residing in said society where victim residing, suddenly came behind her and he caught hold victim and gave fist blow on her head and moved his hand from her chest. Due to said act, victim was frightened. She managed to escape from the clinches of accused. Then she had been to her house and informed about the incident to her mother. Then her mother lodged complaint against accused. 4] On the basis of above report, police registered crime No.I­122/15 against accused. Investigation was handed over to PSI Smt. Shinde. She conducted spot panchanama and recorded statement of witnesses. After completion of investigation, she filed chargesheet against accused. 5] I have framed charge at Exh.5 against the accused. 3 Spl.Case No.34/15 Charge was read over and explained to accused. He pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. The defence of the accused raised u/s.313 of Cr.P.C. is that of total denial and that the brother of victim was responsible for the accident, in which accused sustained injury. He has taken treatment in KEM hospital and spent huge amount towards medical expenses. Initially, victim's family admitted to pay the medical charges, however later on they refused to pay the said charges. Accused was about to lodge complaint against the brother of victim, therefore just to give counter blast, this false complaint is filed. The accused has produced medical bills on record. 6] Following points arise for my consideration,to which I have recorded my findings against them for the reasons to follow­ POINTS FINDINGS 1] Whether prosecution proves that at the time of commission of offence victim In the affirmative. was minor ? 2] Whether prosecution proves that on 7­04­2015 at about 10.30 a.m. at Dhumal Nagar, Vasai (E),accused caught hold victim from her behind and assaulted her with fist blow on her head and moved his hand from her chest and thereby committed an offence punishable In the affirmative. u/s.354 of I.P.C. and under sec.8 of POCSO Act ? 3]Whether the prosecution further proves that at the time of incident victim was below 12 years old and therefore the accused has committed aggravated sexual assault on 4 Spl.Case No.34/15 victim and thereby committed offence punishable u/s.10 of POCSO Act ? In the negative. 4] Whether prosecution proves that on above date, time and place accused voluntarily caused hurt to victim by giving fist blow on her head and thereby committed an offence punishable u/s.323 of I.P.C. ? In the affirmative. 3] What order ? Accused convicted as per final order. 7] Heard ld. A.P.P.Smt.Moholkar and ld. Adv.Shri Ketan Barot for the accused. 8] In order to prove its case, prosecution has examined PW1 Aasma Halim Chaudhary at Exh.20, PW2 Sayna Mohamadali Chaudhary at Exh.21, PW3 Noorsabha Chaudhary Akhtarali at Exh.25, PW4 PSI Kalyani Satish Shinde. REASONS As to Point No.1 :­ 9] It is contention of the prosecution that at the time of incident victim was minor. To prove this aspect, prosecution has examined victim (PW1) at Exh.20 and her mother Shayna Mohamd Ali Chaudhary (PW2) at Exh.21. Both of them deposed that date of birth of victim is 9­08­2002. Prosecution has produced verified copy of birth date certificate issued by Municipal Corporation of Greater Bombay at Exh.30. As per said birth date certificate, the date of birth of victim is 9­08­ 5 Spl.Case No.34/15 2002. The defence has not seriously challenged the age of victim. The prosecution has proved that at the time of incident victim was minor. Therefore, I answer point No.1 in affirmative. As to Points No.2 to 4 :­ These points are interlinked to each other,hence they are decided simultaneously. 10] The deposition of victim is at Exh.20. She deposed that on 7­04­2015 after finishing her paper, she was returning to her house from the school at about 10 to 10.15 a.m. At that time, accused came there and he had given blow of fist on her head and then he moved his hand from her chest and went away. She further deposed that said incident took place in front of Rajjak Steel shop, Dhumal Nagar. She stated that at the time of incident, her friend Noorsabha and Ruksar were with her. Then she had been to her house and informed immediately to her mother. She specifically deposed that when accused gave fist blow on her head and moved his hand from chest, at that time she felt ashame and bad. Thereafter, she and her mother immediately had been to the police station and lodged complaint against the accused. 11] The version of victim is supported by evidence of Noorsabha Chaudhary Akhtarali (PW3 Exh.25). She deposed that on 7­04­2015 her school timing was from 7 to 10 a.m. as their final examination was going on. On that day, after finishing her paper, she along with victim and her sister were 6 Spl.Case No.34/15 returning to home at about 10 a.m. When they reached near Rajjak Steel shop, Dhumal Nagar, at this juncture, accused Lala came there and he caught hold victim and gave fist blow on the head of victim and then pressed the chest of victim. Then victim managed to escape from the clinches of the accused and she had been to her house. Then she narrated the incident to her mother. This witness identified the accused before the court. 12] The prosecution has examined mother of victim Shayna Mohamadali Chaudhary (PW2 Exh.21). She also deposed that on 7­04­2015 examination of victim was going on and therefore her school timing was from 7 a.m. to 10 a.m. She further deposed that when victim was returning from school , at that time accused came and gave blow of fist on the head of victim and he moved his hand from the chest of victim. Then victim came to their house and at that time she was crying and frightened. Then victim informed the above incident to her. Therefore, she immediately lodged complaint against accused. The complaint is at Exh.28. She identified her signature and contents of the complaint. 13] It is defence of the accused that brother of victim was responsible for the motor bike accident in which the accused sustained serious injury and he spent huge amount towards medical expenses. Initially the victim's family agreed to pay medical expenses. However, later on they refused to pay medical expenses to the accused. Therefore, there were serious dispute between accused and victim's family. Therefore, it is contention of accused that this false complaint 7 Spl.Case No.34/15 is filed against him just to counter blast said dispute. 14] No doubt, Shayna Mohamad Ali Chaudhary (PW2) admitted in her cross examination that accused was admitted in KEM hospital for taking treatment. However, victim as well as her mother straightway denied the suggestion given by ld. Advocate for the accused that the brother of victim was responsible for the accident and accused was about to lodge complaint against him and therefore, just to counter blast it, this false complaint is filed against accused. 15] After going through the entire evidence minutely, I come to the conclusion that the prosecution has examined independent witness i.e. Noorsabha Chaudhary Akhtarali (PW3 Exh.25). No doubt she also admitted that she is relative of victim. However, only on that ground one cannot discard her entire evidence. 16] Ld. Advocate for the accused has argued before me that the prosecution has not examined independent witness. He submitted that incident took place on busy road at about 10.15 a.m. He submitted that there are number of shops near the spot of incident. Therefore, according to ld. Advocate for the accused,non examination of independent witness creates serious doubt about the case of prosecution. 17] It is on record that the incident took place in the morning on busy road. However, the incident took place in few minutes and therefore, I am of the view that non examination of shop keepers and other persons does not 8 Spl.Case No.34/15 create serious doubt about the case of prosecution. 18] Ld. Advocate for accused further submitted that victim along with complainant had been to Waliv police station at about 1.30 p.m. and both of them remained in Waliv Police Station till 3.00 p.m. Therefore, he raised question how spot panchanama was conducted in between 2.00 p.m. to 2.30 p.m. and how the complainant shown spot of incident in between 2.00 p.m. to 2.30 p.m. Therefore, according to the ld. Advocate for the accused, the version of PW2 is not believable and acceptable. 19] In spot panchanama, it is mentioned therein that complainant shown the spot of incident. The complainant (PW2) admitted in her cross examination that she reached Waliv Police station, on that day at about 12.00 in noon and remained present there till 3.00 p.m. However, one cannot mathematically calculate the exact timing and only on this minor contradiction, one can not discard the entire evidence of complainant Sayna Mohamad Ali Chaudhary and throw out the entire case of prosecution, which is believable and acceptable. 20] Ld. Advocate for the accused has raised objection that there is no medical certificate on record to show that victim was examined by the Medical Officer and therefore, he submitted that the incident of assault is not proved. It is case of prosecution that the accused gave fist blow on the head of victim. As per Sec.319 of I.P.C. hurt means, whoever causes bodily pain,disease or infirmity to any person is said to cause 9 Spl.Case No.34/15 hurt. Giving fist blow on the head definitely cause bodily pain. Therefore, the medical certificate is not necessary. Hence, this objection of ld. Advocate for the accused cannot be accepted. 21] Charge is also framed u/s.10 of POCSO Act. It is case of prosecution that at the relevant time, the victim was below 12 years and therefore Sec.9(m) of POCSO Act is attracted. The prosecution has proved that date of birth of victim is 16­08­2002 and incident took place on 7­04­2015. Therefore, if we calculate the age of victim, then it reveals that at the time of incident she was more than 12 years. Hence, at the time of incident, victim was more than 12 years old and therefore in this case Sec.9(m) of POCSO Act is not attracted. Therefore prosecution failed to prove that accused is guilty for the offence of aggravated sexual assault within the meaning of Sec.9(m) punishable under Sec.10 of POCSO Act. Hence, I answer point No.3 in negative. 22] The conspectus of the aforesaid discussion is that through the evidence of victim (PW1), independent witness Noorsabha Chaudhary (PW3 Exh.25) and PW2 Sayna Mohamad Ali Chaudhary, prosecution has proved beyond reasonable doubt that the accused sexually assaulted victim within the meaning of Sec.7 of POCSO Act and thereby committed an offence punishable u/s. 8 of POCSO Act. The prosecution has also proved that the accused committed offence punishable u/s.354 of I.P.C. and Sec.323 of I.P.C. Therefore, I hold accused guilty for the offence punishable u/s.8 of POCSO Act, under Sec.354 & 323 of I.P.C. Therefore, I answer points No.2 and 4 in affirmative. 10 Spl.Case No.34/15 23] I take pause here to hear the accused and ld.A.P.P.on the point of sentence. Vasai. (N.R.Pradhan.) Date:07­11­2016 Additional Sessions Judge, Vasai. 24] I heard accused, his advocate and Ld. A.P.P. on the point of sentence. 25] The accused submitted that minimum punishment be ordered to him. The Ld. advocate for accused also submitted that minimum punishment be awarded. On the other hand, ld.A.P.P.has submitted that maximum punishment be awarded. 26] Minimum punishment as prescribed for the purpose of sexual assault u/s.8 of POCSO Act is three years and as per Sec.354(A) maximum punishment is three years. As per Sec.42 of POCSO Act, offender found guilty of such offence shall be punished under this Act or Indian Penal Code as provided punishment which is greater in degree. As per sec. 8 of POCSO Act, minimum punishment is three years, which is greater in degree. Therefore, I direct accused to suffer sentence u/s.8 of POCSO Act and u/s.323 of I.P.C. 27] After considering submissions of both the sides and considering the the facts and circumstances of the case, I am of the view that following sentence is just and proper to meet the ends of justice. Hence I pass the following order. 11 Spl.Case No.34/15 ORDER 1] Accused Lala @ Mausam Azamali Khan is hereby convicted u/s.235(2) of Cr.P.C.for the offence punishable u/s.8 of POCSO Act and sentenced him to suffer rigorous imprisonment for three years and to pay fine of Rs.5,000/­(Rs.Five thousand only) and in default to suffer Rigorous Imprisonment for three months. 2] The accused is further convicted u/s.235(2) of Cr.P.C.for the offence punishable u/s.323 of I.P.C. and sentenced him to suffer rigorous imprisonment for six months and to pay fine of Rs.500/­(Rs.Five hundred only) and in default to suffer Rigorous Imprisonment for 15 days. 3] The substantive sentence shall run concurrently. 4] The accused is entitled to get set off u/s.428 of Cr.P.C.for the period already undergone in the jail. 5] Copy of this judgment be given to the accused at free of costs. On perusal of her evidence it appears that from the alleged subsequent conduct of the accused that he was returning alone from the place of incidence and when she noticed swelling on the private part of victim-girl, she suspected accused that he was the wrong doer. Special Case No.54/2014 Judgment about the alleged sexual assault on her. Therefore, the evidence of her mother P.W.1 needs to be scrutinized minutely and cautiously. 12] In the beginning of cross-examination itself she has stated that at the time of incidence the victim-girl was not grown-up enough to talk and used to speak only words like mummy, pappa and uncle. Though P.W.1 has stated in examination-in-chief that the victim-girl showed her finger towards private part and if really there had been swelling and reddishness on the private part of the victim-girl, no mother would have waited till 11.00 a.m. of next day, when, as per prosecution case, P.W.1 and her husband had taken the victim- girl to Government hospital at Parol for medical examination and treatment. Moreover, if there had been fingering by accused, then victim-girl must have pain at the private part due to fingering and the victim-girl could not play in the courtyard, as stated by the first informant P.W.1. There is time gap of about 14 to 15 hours between time when first informant noticed the injury sustained to the victim-girl and the time when the victim- girl was taken for medical treatment. This creates doubt about the happening of incidence itself. 13] As per prosecution case, one boy by name Vivek told the first informant P.W.1 that accused had taken the victim-girl towards lonely place near bunglaow of Baba. It appears that statement of said boy has been recorded during the investigation and he was a boy of 15 years at the relevant time. Said boy is the only witness so far the 'last seen theory' of prosecution on the point of accused taking the victim-girl towards lonely place. Moreover, when accused was returning .. 8 .. Special Case No.54/2014 Judgment towards his house, P.W.1 asked her as to where the victim-girl is and he replied that he had given her to Nageshri and Arati. These two children were also important witnesses, so far the aspect of custody of the victim-girl with the accused just after the alleged incidence, is concerned. Surprisingly none of these three children namely Vivek, Nageshri and Arati has been examined by the prosecution. In absence of direct of evidence of these three witnesses, the evidence of P.W.1 does not find any sort of corroboration on the aspect that the accused had taken the victim-girl towards lonely place and he had freed the victim- girl from his custody and given her to two other children. It is alleged that sexual assault occurred on 27.09.2014 whereas F.I.R. came to be lodged on 04.10.2014 and no plausible explanation has come on record for such delay. Hence, considering all the facts and circumstances evidence of P.W.1 does not inspire confidence and it is not helpful to connect the accused with the allegation of sexual assault on the victim-girl. 14] P.W.2 Uddhav Rathod is a panch witness on the point of spot panchnama as well as seizure of clothes of victim-girl and accused. This witness has not supported the prosecution case and in spite of being cross-examined by the A.P.P., nothing helpful to the prosecution could be brought on record. 15] P.W.3 lady P.S.I. Annapurna Mhaske is the investigation officer and she has stated about the different steps taken in investigation of this crime including preparation of spot panchnama, arrest of accused under panchnama, seizure of clothes of accused and victim and referring both of them for medical examination and forwarding the seized muddemal and samples for chemical analysis. .. 9 .. P.W.3 has stated about preparation of panchnama of spot of incidence, nothing was found there which can be helpful to the prosecution to prove the guilt of accused. 17] It appears that prosecution has not adduced on record oral evidence of medical expert to support the allegation of sexual assault. Special Case No.54/2014 Judgment 19] During cross-examination of P.W.1 and in reply to the question put to him during statement under section 313 of Cr.P.C. the accused has put forth defence of false implication, which appears to be probable one after considering facts and circumstances of the case. 20] In case of Pratap Mishra vs. State of Orissa – (1977) 3 SCC 41 it has been held that where the oral evidence of the victim is not supported by the medical evidence, it is dangerous to punish the accused for rape solely on the basis of her oral evidence. 21] There is no doubt that rape causes great distress and humiliation to the victim of rape but at the same time false allegation of committing a rape also causes humiliation and damage to the accused. An accused has also rights which are to be protected and the possibility of false implication has to be ruled out. The Supreme Court in Radhu vs. State of Madhya Pradesh – 2007 Cr.L.J. 4704 had in this context noted as follows - ''The courts should, at the same time, bear in mind that false charges of rape are not uncommon. There have also been rare instances where a person has persuaded a gullible or obedient daughter to make a false charge of a rape either to take revenge or extort money or to get rid of financial liability. Whether there was rape or not would depend ultimately on the facts and circumstances of each case. 22] In case of Abbas Ahmed Choudhary Vs. State of Assam - (2010) 12 SCC 115, the Hon’ble Supreme Court has held that ''We are conscious of the fact that in a matter of rape, .. 11 .. Special Case No.54/2014 Judgment the statement of the victim must be given primary consideration, but, at the same time, the broad principle that the prosecution has to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt applies equally to a case of rape and there can be no presumption that a victim would always tell the entire story truthfully. 23] Keeping in mind the above cited judgments, the testimony of first informant (P.W.1) has to be consistent and natural in line with the case of the prosecution and free from infirmities which inspire confidence in the Court. It cannot be presumed that the statement of the first informant (P.W.1) is always true or without any embellishment. The version of the first informant has not been corroborated by medical evidence and has not disclosed the true genesis of the crime. 24] In the present case, evidence of P.W.1, delay in lodging F.I.R., non-examination of material witnesses and non- supporting medical evidence, made the foundation of prosecution case shaky and unbelievable. Suspicion, however, strong it may be, cannot take place of proof. The friend of deceased Shejal (PW­3) has admitted that there was love affair between deceased and accused and they were good friends. Making friendship with minor girl is not an offence. To attract Section 11 & 12 of POCSO an intention of accused must be bad. In this case, accused was having friendship with minor girl and i.e., not an offence. Absolutely there is no evidence against the accused that he was sexually harassing deceased within a meaning of Se. ..15.. Spl.C.No.37/15(J) 11 & 12 of POCSO Act. In absence of cogent and reliable evidence, the prosecution has miserably failed to prove the charges punishable under Sec. 12 of POCSO Act against the accused. I, therefore answer point No.3 in negative. 27] In view of above discussion, accused deserves to be acquitted. I, therefore pass following order :­ ORDER 1] Accused Salman Subhanali Ansari is hereby acquitted U/Sec. 235(1) of Cr.P.C.for the offence punishable U/Sec. 306 of the Indian Penal Code, Under Sec. 3(1) Xii of S.C.& S.T.(Prev.of Atro.)Act 1989 and under Sec. 12 of POCSO Act. 2] Seized muddemal, if any be destroyed after appeal period is over. 3] He is directed to give PR bond of Rs.15,000/­ with S.B. of like amount in compliance of Section 437­A of Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973. Vasai. (N.R.Pradhan.) Date:­29/9/2017 Addl Sessions Judge, Vasai. Saa

1 Spl.Case No.36/15 Presented on­ : 30­07­2015 Registered on­ : 30­07­2015 Decided on­ : 05­11­2016 Duration­ :1Y­3M­5D IN THE COURT OF SESSION JUDGE, VASAI. (Presided over by N.R.Pradhan,Addl.S.J.) Special Case NO. 36/2015. Exh The State. (Through Tulinj Police Stn.) ­­­­­­­Complainant. V/s. Rakesh Dipnath Khatri, Age 34 years, R/at Sai Shradha Chawl, Paach Amba,Achole road, Nalasopara (E), Tal.Vasai.Dist.Palghar. –­­­­­­ Accused. Offences punishable u/s.354(A)(i) of the Indian Penal Code and Sec.8,9(m) (n),11(i)punishable u/s.12 of Prevention of Child Sexual Offences Act. Appearances­ A.P.P. Smt.Moholkar for the State. Adv. Smt.Anjali Patil for the accused. JUDGMENT (Delivered on 05­11­2016 ) The accused is facing trial for the offences punishable u/s.354(A)(i) of the Indian Penal Code (hereinafter referred to as IPC)and under Sec.8,9(m)(n),11(i) 2 Spl.Case No.36/15 of Prevention of Child Sexual Offences Act (hereinafter referred to as POCSO Act). The case of prosecution in short is as under :­ 2] Informant is the mother of victim. She lodged information on 7­3­2015 before Tulinj Police Station. The accused is the step father of victim. 3] In the year 1999 informant married with Subhash Lakhankar. From their wedlock, she begotten victim. At the relevant time, victim was 12 years old and she was taking education in 6th Std. On 7­3­2015 as usual informant had been to her work at Borivali. On that day, victim had not gone to her school. In the afternoon, she was playing outside the house. At about 1.00 p.m. accused called victim for lunch. When victim was washing her hand and leg at that time accused came from behind and he lifted her and put his hand into her nicker and touched her private part and then he took kiss of the lips of victim. The victim pushed the accused and went towards her neighbour. She was very frightened. She asked mobile phone of her neighbour, however there was no balance therefore she obtained Rs.10/­ from the neighbour. Then she made phone call to her mother i.e. informant and informed all the incident. Mother advised her to sit in the house of neighbour. The informant came at about 4 p.m. to her house and then she again asked victim what happened. At that time victim told all the incident to her and then informant lodged complaint against the accused. 4] On the basis of said information, crime No.I­9/15 registered against the accused. Investigation was handed over 3 Spl.Case No.36/15 to police officer. The investigating officer recorded statement of witnesses, collected medical examination paper of victim and accused. After completion of investigation filed charge­ sheet against accused. 5] I have framed charge at Exh.5 against the accused. Charge was read over and explained to accused. He pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. The defence of the accused raised u/s.313 of Cr.P.C. is that of total denial. 6] Following points arise for my consideration,to which I have recorded my findings against them for the reasons to follow­ POINTS FINDINGS 1] Whether prosecution proves that at the time of commission of offence victim In the affirmative. was minor ? 2] Whether prosecution proves that accused being step father of victim took disadvantage and on or about 7­3­2015 at about 1 p.m. with sexual intention lifted victim and putting his hand into her nicker and touched her vagina and also kissed her and uttered word “Tu Khup Barik Zali In the affirmative. Ahes Kahi Khates Ki Nahi” and thereby outraged her modesty and thereby committed an offence punishable u/s.354(A)(i)of I.P.C.and Sec.10 & 12 of POCSO Act ? 3] What order ? Accused convicted as per final order. 7] Heard ld. A.P.P.Smt.Moholkar and ld. Adv.Smt. Anjali Patil for accused. 4 Spl.Case No.36/15 8] In order to prove its case, prosecution has examined PW1 Jagruti Subhash Lakhankar at Exh.12, PW2 Rashmi Rakesh Khatri at Exh.13, PW3 Gauri Prakash Bhoir, PW4 Anup Rakesh Singh at Exh.21,PW5 Dr.Nitu Rakesh Singh at Exh.25 & PW6 API Smt.Rekha Dattatray Londhe at Exh.30. REASONS Point No.1 :­ 9] It is contention of the prosecution that date of birth of victim is 9­12­2002. To prove this aspect, prosecution has examined mother of the victim Rashmi Rakesh Khatri (PW2 Exh.13). The prosecution has produced verified copy of the birth date certificate issued by Municipal Corporation,Greater Mumbai at Exh.16. The defence has not seriously challenged the age of the victim. The prosecution has proved birth date through birth date certificate and oral evidence of Rashmi Khatri (PW2). The incident took place on 7­03­2015. Therefore at the time of incident, victim was minor. I, therefore, answer point No.1 in affirmative. Point No.2 :­ 10] It is an admitted fact that the accused is step father of victim. Prosecution has examined victim as PW1 Exh.12. She deposed that her step father was not doing any job. At the relevant time, her mother was working as domestic servant. On the day of incident i.e. 7­03­2015 she had not gone to school. She was playing with other children behind her house. At that time her father called her for lunch. When she was washing her hand and leg at this juncture her father came from behind and lifted her and then asked her whether she is eating 5 Spl.Case No.36/15 or not as her weight is less and she became slim. Then her father put his hand into her nicker and touched her vagina and also took kiss of her lips. Therefore, she pushed her father and went to the house of her neighbour. From her neighbour, she had taken Rs.10/­ and then she made phone call from PCO to her mother. Her mother came at about 4 p.m. Then she again narrated the incident to her mother. She has specifically deposed that when her father had done said act, at that time she felt shy and bad. 11] Rashmi Rakesh Khatri (PW2), who is mother of victim is totally supporting to the version of victim. She deposed that on the day of incident i.e. 7­03­2015 as usual she had been to her work. On that day, victim had not gone to school. At about 1.00 p.m. victim had called her and at that time she was frightened. Victim informed her that her father lifted her and put his hand into her nicker and touched her vagina and also took kiss of her lips. As the victim was frightened therefore she told her to sit in the house of neighbour. From whom she obtained money to call her. Then she made phone call to her husband and inquired him about the incident. At that time, accused admitted that he committed said act. Then this witness returned to her house at about 4 p.m. She noticed that victim was frightened. Then she again asked what happened, at that time victim told her the entire incident. Then she immediately lodged complaint against the accused. She admitted her signature and contents of complaint, which is at Exh.14. 12] In cross examination, victim (PW1) and her mother Rashmi (PW2) have admitted that accused used to 6 Spl.Case No.36/15 prepare food for victim and her younger brother and in the evening he used to prepare food for entire family. They further admitted that victim used to call Pankaj Nayak as Papa and her father was opposing to call Pankaj Nayak as Papa. They further admitted that on that ground there were frequent quarrels between accused and Rashmi (PW2). They also admitted that room was purchased in the name of Rashmi (PW2) and an amount of Rs.4,90,000 was paid by Jitendra Khatri. However, these admissions are not at all sufficient to disbelieve the version of victim and her mother. 13] The independent witness Gauri Prakash Bhoir (PW3) has not totally supported case of prosecution but her evidence is important to prove subsequent circumstances. Gauri Bhoir (PW3 Exh,19) deposed that on 7­3­2015 she was present in her house. On that day, approximately at about 1 p.m. daughter of Khatri came to her house. At that time she was crying and she asked mobile of the witness to call her mother. This witness told her that she has not having enough balance. Then this witness asked her why she is crying, at that time she has given some reply, however this witness was not in position to recollect said reply. Then this witness handed over Rs.10/­ to her to call her mother. This witness declared hostile to the extent that on that day victim told this witness that her father touched her vagina and kissed her. This witness is cross examined at length. Through this witness, the prosecution proved that on the day of incident at about 1 p.m. victim had been to the house of this witness and at that time she was crying and she had taken Rs.10/­ from this witness to call her mother. 7 Spl.Case No.36/15 14] Ld. Advocate for the accused raised objection that her father was preparing food and taking care of his daughter. Then where is the question of doing such act. At the time of incident, the accused was not doing any job and he was remained in his house. Therefore only on the ground that he was preparing food to his family, one cannot entirely discard the case of prosecution and therefore this objection of ld. Advocate for the accused cannot be accepted. 15] Ld. Advocate for the accused has taken objection that victim admitted that on the day of incident she was playing along with her friends, however the investigating officer has not recorded statement of these children and therefore according to ld. Advocate for the accused, it creates serious doubt about the case of prosecution. It is also contention of ld. Advocate for the accused that there are 40 houses in said chawl. Therefore, according to ld. Advocate for the accused, it was necessary on the part of investigating officer to record statement of other independent witnesses. Ld. Advocate for the accused further submitted that investigating officer has not recorded statement of PCO owner. Therefore, according to ld. Advocate for the accused benefit of doubt should be given to accused. 16] The incident took place inside the house. The prosecution has examined one independent witness i.e. PW3 Gauri Prakash Bhoir, therefore I am of the view that only on the ground of non recording statement of children with whom victim was playing and non recording statement of neighbour is not a ground to disbelieve the case of prosecution. 8 Spl.Case No.36/15 17] Ld. Advocate for the accused submitted that Gauri Prakash Bhoir (PW3) has not deposed about the incident. Therefore, according to him, as the incident had not taken place therefore she is not deposing about it. 18] As I have mentioned earlier that Gauri Prakash Bhoir (PW3) has specifically deposed that on the day of incident at about 1 p.m. victim had been to her house and at that time she was crying and she asked her mobile phone to call her mother. However,as there was no balance in mobile phone therefore she had given Rs.10/­ to victim to call her mother. Therefore, only on the ground that she has not deposed that victim had informed her about incident,one cannot entirely throw out the prosecution case. 19] Prosecution has examined Dr.Nitu Singh (PW5 Exh.30). She deposed that on 10­03­2015 at about 1.45 p.m. she examined victim. She further deposed that victim had given history of vaginal touch by her father Rakesh on 07­03­ 2015 at about 1.30 p.m. 20] Prosecution has examined investigating officer Smt.Rekha Londhe (PW6 Exh.30). She admitted that she has not recorded statement of children with whom victim was playing outside the house when accused called her. She also admitted that she has not recorded statement of PCO booth proprietor. However, as I have already mentioned that the evidence of victim and her mother is cogent, reliable and trustworthy. As per Sec.29 of POCSO Act, when a person is prosecuted for committing or abetting or attempting to commit any offence u/s.3,5,7 & 9 of this Act, the Special court shall 9 Spl.Case No.36/15 presume that such a person shall commit or abet or attempt to commit offence as the case may be unless the contrary is proved. In this case, the accused has not given any satisfactorily reason why his wife lodged false complaint against him. In cross examination, question was put to Rashmi (PW2) that during the pendency of this case she had been to jail along with her son to meet accused, at that time she has given answer in affirmative. Admittedly, from the wedding lock of accused and Rashmi Khatri, they have one son. Then question remains the lady who took her son to meet accused can file false complaint against him. This aspect is sufficient to come to the conclusion that the version of victim and her mother (PW2) is trustworthy. 21] The next objection raised by the ld. Advocate for the accused is that section 9(m) of POCSO Act is not attracted, because the victim is more than 12 years old at the time of incident. The date of birth of victim is 9­12­2002 and the incident took place on 7­3­2015. Therefore at the time of incident, the victim was more than 12 years However Sec. 9(n) of the said Act is totally applicable to the facts and circumstances of this case. Admittedly, the accused is step father of victim and he sexually assaulted victim within the meaning of sec.7 of the said Act. Therefore, in this particular case, sec.9 is applicable. Therefore, presumption u/s.29 of the said Act is applicable and as I have mentioned earlier that the accused has not put­forth any ground to rebut the presumption. So far as sec. 11 of the said Act is concerned, i.e. sexual harassment, I am of the view that the accused lifted victim with bad intention and took her kiss of lips. Therefore prosecution has proved that the accused sexually harassed 10 Spl.Case No.36/15 victim within the meaning of sec.11 of POCSO Act. 22] The conspectus on the aforesaid discussion is that through the evidence of victim, Rashmi PW2 and Gauri (PW3), prosecution has proved beyond reasonable doubt that at the time of incident, victim was minor and she was in care and custody of her step father i.e. accused and the accused took disadvantage of it and put his hand into the nick of victim and touched her vagina and took kiss of her lips. Therefore, prosecution has proved beyond reasonable doubt that accused has committed offence of aggravated sexual assault within the meaning of sec. 9 and sexual harassment within the meaning of sec. 11 of POCSO Act, punishable u/s.10 & 12 of said Act. Therefore, I held accused guilty for the offences punishable u/s.354(A) of I.P.C.and sec. 10 & 12 of POCSO Act. I, therefore, answer point No. 2 in the affirmative. 23] I take pause here to hear the accused and ld.A.P.P.on the point of sentence. Vasai. (N.R.Pradhan.) Date:05­11­2016 Additional Sessions Judge, Vasai. 24] I heard accused and Ld. A.P.P. on the point of sentence. 25] The accused submitted that minimum punishment be awarded to him. On the other hand, Ld. A.P.P. submitted that maximum punishment be awarded to him. 11 Spl.Case No.36/15 26] The ld. Advocate for accused absent when lastly called today at 3.20 p.m. 27] Minimum punishment as prescribed for the purpose of aggravated sexual assault u/s.10 of POCSO Act is five years and maximum punishment for sexual harassment prescribed u/s.12 of POCSO Act is three years and as per Sec.354(A) of I.P.C., maximum punishment is three years. As per Sec.42 of POCSO Act, offender found guilty of such offence shall be punished under this Act or Indian Penal Code as provided punishment which is greater in degree. As per sec. 10 of POCSO Act, minimum punishment is five years, which is greater in degree. Therefore, I direct accused to suffer sentence u/s.10 & 12 of POCSO Act. 28] After considering submissions of both the sides and considering the the facts and circumstances of the case, I am of the view that following sentence is just and proper to meet the ends of justice. Hence I pass the following order. ORDER 1] Accused Rakesh Dipnath Khatri is hereby convicted u/s.235(2) of Cr.P.C.for the offence punishable u/s.10 of POCSO ACt and sentenced him to suffer rigorous imprisonment for five years and to pay fine of Rs.5,000/­(Rs.Five thousand only) and in default to suffer Rigorous Imprisonment for three months. 2] The accused is further convicted u/s.235(2) of Cr.P.C.for the offence punishable u/s.12 of POCSO Act and sentenced him to suffer rigorous imprisonment for two years and to pay fine of Rs.2,000/­(Rs.Two thousand only) and in default to suffer Rigorous Imprisonment for two months. 12 Spl.Case No.36/15 3] The substantive sentence shall run concurrently. 4] The accused is entitled to get set off u/s.428 of Cr.P.C.for the period already undergone in the jail. 5] Copy of this judgment be given to the accused at free of costs. 1 Presented on­ : 11­08­2015 Registered on­ : 11­08­2015 Decided on­ : 10­05­2016 Duration­ :0Y­8 M­29D IN THE COURT OF SESSION JUDGE, VASAI. (Presided over by N.R.Pradhan,Addl.S.J.) SESSION CASE NO. 40/2015. Exh. No. The State. (Through Waliv Police Stn.) ­­­­­­­Complainant. V/s. Salman @ Salamuddin Nijamuddin Shah, Age 23 years, R/at Kuvarapada Sativali,Vasai (E), Tal.Vasai. Ori.R/at Gram Chitora, Tal.Maujubi, Dist.Banaras (U.P.) –­­­­­­ Accused. Offences punishable u/s. 376(2)(n), 417 of the Indian Penal Code and sec.4(1), 8 of POCSO Act. Appearances­ A.P.P. Smt.Moholkar for the State. Adv. Smt.Sadhana Dhuri for the accused. JUDGMENT (Delivered on 10­05­2016 ) The accused is facing trial for the offences punishable u/s. 376(2), 417 of the Indian Penal Code (hereinafter referred to as IPC) and u/s.4(1),8 of Prevention of Child Sexual Offence Act (Hereinafter referred to as POCSO 2 Act). The case of prosecution in short is as under :­ 2] The informant Roshanbanu Mushtaq Shaikh lodged report before Waliv Police Station on 19­5­2015. She informed that at the relevant time she was residing along with her family at Sativali, Vasai. Her elder daughter was 16½ years old. She was working in New Natraj Co. Sativali. 3] On 9­05­2015 it was holiday of her daughter and therefore she was present in her house. At that time, her daughter complained that she is suffering from abdomen pain and her menstrual period is missed. Therefore, the informant had been to the dispensary for check up of her daughter. The local doctor advised her to conduct sonography. Accordingly, sonography was conducted on 18­5­2015 and in said sonography it was revealed that her daughter was three months pregnant. 4] Then she inquired with her daughter, at that time she told that since last one and half year she knows accused, who was working in her company and she developed friendly relation with him. She further told that accused asked her to get marry without the permission of parents. She refused to do so. In the month of March 2014 when nobody was present in company premises at that time, the accused committed forcible intercourse with victim and the accused told victim that he will marry her and therefore, she should not disclose about it to anybody. Then time to time accused committed sexual intercourse with victim on said pretext. The victim told 3 informant that she is pregnant from accused. Then on 19­5­ 2015 the complainant had been to the house of accused and she met with accused and his father and requested them that accused should marry victim. The father of accused told that accused is already married and therefore it is not possible to marry with victim. Thus, it is allegation of the complainant that the accused is already married and he gave false promise to marry victim and established sexual intercourse with her when she was minor and when she became three months pregnant, accused refused to marry with her. 5] On the basis of said information, crime No.I­ 196/15 was registered against the accused. Investigation was handed over to PSI Smt. S.S.Jagtap. She prepared spot panchanama. Recorded the statement of witnesses. Medical examination of victim and accused was conducted and the relevant papers were collected. After completion of investigation,she filed charge­sheet against accused. 6] I have framed charge at Exh.9 against the accused. Charge was read over and explained to accused. He pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. The defence of the accused raised u/s.313 of Cr.P.C. is that he performed Nikah with victim and thereafter they have maintained relation and therefore he falsely implicated in this case. 7] Following points arise for my consideration,to which I have recorded my findings against them for the reasons to follow­ POINTS FINDINGS 1] Whether prosecution proves that since No. 4 March 2014 to 12­4­2015 the accused committed rape on minor victim,aged about 16 years and thereby committed offence punishable u/s.376(2) of I.P.C.sec.4­(1) of POCSO Act ? 2] Whether it further proves that on the No. above mentioned period the accused with sexual intention touched the body of minor victim girl which involves physical contact without penetration and thereby committed an offence punishable u/s.8 of POCSO Act ? 3] Whether it further proves that on the No. above mention period the accused cheated victim girl by inducing her giving false promise to marry with her, committed rape on her from time to time and due to which the victim became pregnant and then accused denied to marry with her and thereby committed offence punishable u/s.417 of IPC? 4] What order ? Accused acquitted. 8] Heard ld. A.P.P.Smt.Moholkar and ld. Adv.Smt. Sadhana Dhuri for accused. 9] In order to prove its case, prosecution has examined PW1 Hinabano Mushtaq Shaikh at Exh.14, PW2 complainant Roshanbau Mushtaq Shaikh at Exh.15, PW3 PSI Smt. Swati Shrirang Jagtap at Exh.22, PW4 Dr.Pavan Ramdasji Sabale at Exh.37, PW5 Smt. Usha Surendra Gupta at Exh.39 and filed evidence close pursis at Exh.42. The accused has also examined DW1 Anvar Husain Khan at Exh.45. REASONS Points No.1 to 3 :­ 5 All the points are interlinked to each other, hence they are discussed simultaneously. 10] The learned A.P.P.has submitted before me that at the time of incident, victim was minor and therefore the defence taken by the accused that with her consent he maintained sexual relation with victim cannot be accepted, because minor cannot give consent. She submitted that Head Mistress of the school of victim is examined by the prosecution and as per school leaving certificate, birth date of victim is 9­ 11­1997 and therefore she submitted that at the time of incident victim was minor. She submitted that the defence has not proved that accused performed Nikah with victim. She submitted that it has come on record that the accused is already married and therefore she submitted that though the victim and complainant are not supporting to the case of prosecution, but as the prosecution has proved the portion mark of the statement of victim and complainant through investigating officer, therefore the prosecution has proved the case against accused. 11] At the outset, it has to be mentioned here that the complainant and victim are not supporting to the case of prosecution. Victim (PW1) deposed that she and accused were working in Natraj Co. and they developed love affair. Then accused performed marriage with her in Mumbai. They both have not informed about their marriage to their parents. She further deposed that after marriage she was residing along with accused at Mumbai and there for five times she has made sexual intercourse with accused. The ld.A.P.P.has declared her 6 hostile and taken cross examination at length. However, she maintained the stand that she performed marriage with accused and thereafter, she maintained sexual relation with accused. In cross examination of ld. Advocate for the accused, she admitted that she performed marriage with accused and she categorically admitted that accused had not committed forcible sexual intercourse with her and against her will. 12] The complainant Roshanbi Shaikh (PW2 Exh.15) is also not supporting to the case of prosecution. She denied that at the time of recording her complaint, she informed police that accused committed sexual intercourse with her daughter on the pretext of marriage. In cross examination, she admitted that accused performed marriage with her daughter. 13] In this case, neither victim nor her mother i.e. complainant is supporting to the case of prosecution. Therefore, there is absolutely no use to discuss the medical evidence on record. The prosecution has examined Head Mistress ,however the record shows that the victim was on the verge of attending majority. The victim was working in the company. The defence has examined Anvar Husain Khan who is one of the witness of Nikahnama. He deposed that he is friend of father of victim. Victim came to him and shown her willingness to marry with accused and requested him to remain as witness as she does not want to inform her parents. As the victim was working in factory, therefore this witness believed that the victim is more than 18 years old. Then he took them to Mankhurd before one Kazi and said Kazi performed Nikah of accused and victim. Nikahnama is produced on record. The translated copy of Nikahnama is marked Exh.48. The affidavit 7 of translator Bilal Hasrat is also filed on record. 14] From the evidence, it reflects that now neither victim nor complainant has any complaint or grievance against accused and therefore under these circumstances, if I accept the argument of ld. A.P.P. that the victim was minor and therefore she cannot give consent and as the accused is already married therefore accused should be punished. Then,it will amount to punish the accused without the complaint of victim or original complainant. The victim is married with accused and if accused is convicted and sent in jail, then definitely both of them will suffer. Therefore, from the social point of view also, the argument advanced by the ld. A.P.P. cannot be accepted. 15] The ld. Advocate for the accused placed reliance on the order passed by the Hon'ble Division Bench of Bombay High Court in case of Raju Bhupat Soni Cri.Application No.102 of 2016 dated 9 Feb.2016. In that case, the victim was minor and section of perfection of child from sexual offence Act were applied. The Hon'ble Division Bench has quashed the FIR against the accused on the ground that the matter is amicable settled between victim,complainant and accused. 16] Turning back to the present case, it reveals from the evidence that neither victim nor complainant has any grievance against the accused and therefore, prosecution has failed to prove the charges leveled against him. I, therefore answer points No.1 to 3 in the negative. As a result, the accused deserves to be acquitted. I, therefore pass the 8 following order. ORDER 1] The accused is hereby acquitted u/s.235(1) of the Criminal Procedure Code of the offences punishable u/s. 376(2), 417 of the Indian Penal Code and u/s.4(1),8 of Prevention of Child Sexual Offence Act. 2] The accused is in jail. He be released forthwith if not required in any other case. 3] The muddemal property i.e. clothes as per receipt Exh.29 being worthless, be destroyed, after appeal period is over. 4] The property No.3 i.e. Compact Disc is part of evidence and not muddemal therefore,no order regarding it is passed. 5] The accused shall furnish P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ each and surety bond in the like amount in compliance of Sec. 437­A of Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973. Sd/­ (N.R.Pradhan.) Vasai. Additional Sessions Judge, Date:10­05­2016 Vasai.

P. Divate, Additional Sessions Judge­1] 48 of 2015 (CNR : MHTH23­001099­2015) Exhibit No. 28 The State of Maharashtra .. Complainant (through Nalasopara police station Crime No.I­15/2015) versus Albert Domnic Gonsalves .. Accused Age 71 years, Residence – Runpalwadi, Agashi, Taluka Vasai JUDGMENT (Delivered on 20th day of January, 2018) .. 2 .. Special Case No. 48/2015 Judgment CNR : MHTH23­001099­2015 Accused stands trial for the offence punishable under section 452, 354 of Indian Penal Code and section 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act ( in short P.O.C.S.O. Act ). 2] Prosecution's case in brief is as under ­ That complainant Tiruma w/o Madhav Deka is mother of victim­girl. She is residing at given address alongwith husband, daughter, sons and son of sister. On 03.01.2015 she was at home. At about 3.00 p.m. she went at the first floor to visit one Sudhane. She was talking with neighbour in gallery. One person went out of building. She came back after 15 minutes. She rang bell. Daughter did not open the door. She had given call to daughter. Daughter opened the door. Daughter started weeping. She has calmed down her daughter and taken her in confidence. Daughter told her that, “when she went at the first floor, at that time her door bell was rung She opened the door. One uncle was standing in the door. He came inside the room. He inquired about Bharati auntie. She replied to uncle that Bharati went at the house of her parents. Uncle inquired with her about her name and name of school. Uncle touched her chest and pressed”. Daughter narrated her physical description of that person. Complainant came out of the building. She had inquired with watchman namely Talvalkar and Gavkar. Neighbour namely Sadashiv Kadam told complainant that said old person was inquiring about Bharati. Physical description of said old person and the description narrated by the complainant is similar. Complainant telephoned her neighbour Bharati and narrated description of said old person. Bharati replied that said old person .. 3 .. Special Case No. 48/2015 Judgment CNR : MHTH23­001099­2015 may be the present accused. However, they will get ascertained about it when she came back at home. On 04.01.2015 Bharati came at home. She telephoned accused and called him but could not have contact. On 05.01.2015 again she telephoned accused and called him at home. Accused came in building at 10.00 a.m. Bharati called complainant and her daughter and pointed out accused. Bharati inquired with victim as to whether said old person is the present accused. Victim was frightened. Victim told that accused is the same person. Accused disclosed his name as Albert Gonsalves, resident of Agashi. Complainant went at police station. She has filed complaint Exhibit 13. 3] Police completed investigation and filed charge­sheet against accused. 4] Charge under section 452 and 354 of Indian Penal Code and section 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act were framed at Exhibit 6. Contents of the charge were read over to accused and explained to him in vernacular. He did not plead guilty and claimed to be tried. His defence is that of total denial. 5] After going through the evidence of prosecution witnesses and police papers, following points arise for my determination. I have recorded my findings against each of them for the reasons given below. .. 4 .. Special Case No. 48/2015 Judgment CNR : MHTH23­001099­2015 Points ­ 1} Whether prosecution has proved that on 03.01.2015 at about 3.00 p.m. at building no.116, plot no.003, Leo Society, Evershine City, Nalasopara(E), accused has committed criminal house trespass having made preparation to commit cognizable offence ? 2} Whether prosecution has proved that on the same date, time and place, accused has outraged modesty of victim girl/committed sexual assault on her ? 3} What order and sentence, if any ? Findings ­ 1} In negative. 2} In negative. 3} Accused is acquitted. REASONS As regards point no.1 and 2 ­ 6] Accused has not disputed the circumstance of spot inspection panchnama Exhibit 15, sketch map Exhibit 23. Accused has not disputed the material fact that victim­child girl is minor child and school­going girl. Aforesaid admitted facts are not sufficient to connect accused with the present case. 7] Prosecution has examined complainant at Exhibit 12. She has deposed that at about 3.00 p.m. she went at first floor to visit Hema. She came back after 15 minutes. She rang the bell and had given call to daughter. Daughter opened the door. Daughter .. 5 .. Special Case No. 48/2015 Judgment CNR : MHTH23­001099­2015 started weeping and appears to be frightened. She inquired with daughter. Daughter told her that, “when she left house, one uncle came at home. Said uncle inquired with her about Bharati auntie, her name and her school. Said uncle touched her chest and pressed and went away”. Her daughter told that said person was age old and was wearing cap and specs. Said uncle was having white beard. She immediately went near the gate of the building. She inquired with watchman and one neighbour namely Sadashiv Kadam Kaka. Said Sadashiv Kadam told her that one age old person inquired with him about Bharati auntie. Said person was not found nearby the building. Complainant further deposed that she telephoned Bharati. Bharati is her neighbour. She inquired with Bharati about the person who visited her house. She has narrated description of that person to Bharati. Bharati told her that description narrated by complainant is matched with the parents of accused. Bharati has disclosed possibility that said person may be the present accused. On next day Bharati came back at home. She had discussion with Bharati. Bharati telephoned accused. On Monday accused came to visit Bharati. She was standing at the door alongwith victim­child girl. She had pointed out accused to the victim. Victim was frightened by looking at that person. Victim told her that accused is the same person who came at home on Saturday. Somebody telephoned police. She was frightened. Police came at their society. She went at police station. She filed complaint Exhibit 13. 8] Victim­child girl has deposed similar set of facts. .. 6 .. Special Case No. 48/2015 Judgment CNR : MHTH23­001099­2015 9] Accused cross­examined the complainant and victim­ child girl in a length. They have denied suggestions put to them while cross­examination. Complainant disclosed while cross­ examination that their society building is surrounded by compound and there is only one gate. Watchman is always present in the gate. Society has maintained register of visitors at the gate of the society. Bharati suspected that the accused may have visited her house. 10] Complainant further disclosed while cross­examination that her husband was not at home. She did not went at police station on 03.01.2015. Her husband came back at midnight. She narrated the incident to her husband. They went at police station on 05.01.2015 though Bharati came in their building. This witness is not having knowledge that her neighbour borrowed Rs.2 lacs from accused. It is transpired that Bharati is having wedlock with her husband. Bharati filed petition for divorce. Bharati was visiting court. 11] Prima facie it appears that alleged incident had taken place on 03.01.2015 at 3.00 p.m. Complainant did not go at police station on the same day or on next day. She explained that Bharati was not at home. On 04.01.2015 Bharati came at home. She narrated the incident to Bharati. Bharati had suspicion on accused. Facts and circumstances make it clear that complainant, victim­child girl and Bharati were not sure about the culprit but Bharati had suspicion on the accused. .. 7 .. Special Case No. 48/2015 Judgment CNR : MHTH23­001099­2015 12] Bharati appears to be material witness in the present case. Investigation officer did not record her statement. This is material omission on the part of I.O. A.P.P. filed application under section 311 of Evidence Act and prayed to issue summons to Bharati. Application comes to be allowed. Prosecution has examined Bharati at Exhibit 18. Bharati deposed that complainant and victim are her neighbours. On 03.01.2015 she went at Pune. At 4.30 p.m. she received telephone call from the complainant. Complainant told her that one unknown person came at her house in her absence and had outraged modesty of victim­child girl. Complainant narrated description of the person came at her home. Bharati suspected that said person may be accused. Bharati further deposed that on 04.01.2015 at 7.30 a.m. she came back at home. She had given call to accused but could not have contact. On next day she called accused at her home in order to get ascertained the culprit. On next day accused came near the building at 10.30 to 11.00 a.m. Victim­ child girl disclosed that accused is the same person. Members of society annoyed. Members of society assaulted accused. Accused confessed about guilt and apologized. Society members have applied black colour to the face of accused. Police were called. Police came at the spot. Accused was handed over to the police. Complainant went at police station alongwith victim. Police recorded her complaint. Bharati disclosed that she filed suit for divorce against her husband. She got acquainted with accused in court. She has denied suggestion that she owed Rs.2 lacs from accused and accused was importunating her for recovery of amount. Therefore, she has abetted complainant society members against .. 8 .. Special Case No. 48/2015 Judgment CNR : MHTH23­001099­2015 accused. It is transpired while cross­examination of Bharati that on 04.01.2015 she herself and Anita Rathod, Sanyukta Desai and Reeta Dubey had meeting at home of complainant. They have decided to call accused in the building. They have informed about the incident to secretary of society. All they had discussion together. Hansraj, Shrinivas, Kadam kaka and other 2 – 3 persons were present. Above material facts have been suppressed by complainant while filing complaint. Complainant also suppressed aforesaid material facts while deposing before this court. Anita Rathod, Sanyukta Desai, Reeta Dubey, watchmen namely Talvalkar and Gavkar and members of society namely Hansraj, Shrinivas, Kadam kaka and other 2 – 3 persons appears to be material witnesses in the present case. All they were waiting for arrival of accused on 05.01.2015. facts and circumstances indicate that Bharati was not sure about the culprit. However, she has suspected that accused might be the culprit in the present case. It was the duty of the complainant and aforesaid persons to immediately report the incident to police but they did not. 13] Facts and circumstances makes it clear that on 05.01.2015 at 10.30 a.m. members of society have assaulted accused and defaced her face by applying black colour and then handed over him to police. In the present case accused appears to be an aggrieved person. Prima facie it appears that police have not taken cognizance of the incident narrated by the accused. Prosecution fails to examine material witness to the incident. Thus, prosecution has withheld evidence of material witnesses. This fact is .. 9 .. Special Case No. 48/2015 Judgment CNR : MHTH23­001099­2015 sufficient to draw adverse inference against prosecution. 14] Facts and circumstances indicate that the I.O. did not record statement of material witnesses. Moreover, prosecution fails to examine material witness. Aforesaid material facts and circumstances have been suppressed by the complainant and Bharati while filing complaint. In this circumstance the defence made out by the accused appears to be just and proper. I hold that Bharati appears to be interested person and witness. Therefore, evidence of complainant and Bharati does not appear to be just, natural and trustworthy in absence of due corroboration from other material witness. I discard their evidence. I hold that the evidence of prosecution witnesses is not sufficient to bring accused to the home of guilt beyond all reasonable doubt. The evidence of I.O. appears to be formal in nature. I.O. has not investigated the case impartially. I hold that prosecution has miserably failed to prove the guilt of accused beyond all reasonable doubt. I have answered point no.1 and 2 in negative. As regards point no.3 ­ 15] In view of my finding to point no.1 and 2, I hold that prosecution has miserably failed to prove the guilt of accused beyond all reasonable doubt. Accused deserves to be acquitted. I proceed to pass following order ­ ORDER 1} Accused namely Albert Domnic Gonsalves is acquitted under section 235(1) of Cr.P.C. of charge for offences punishable .. 10 .. Special Case No. 48/2015 Judgment CNR : MHTH23­001099­2015 under section 452, 354 of Indian Penal Code and section 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 2} Bail bonds of accused stand cancelled. Sureties are discharged. 3} In view of mandate laid down in section 437A of Cr.P.C., accused is directed to execute P.R. bond of Rs.5,000/­. He shall undertake to appear before appellate court on receipt of notice of appeal. Date : 20.01.2018 ( M. P. Divate ) Additional Sessions Judge­1, Vasai.

The case of prosecution in short is as under :­ 2] Santosh Bhanubhai Makwana has lodged report on 18/7/2015 in Tulinj Police Station. Prosecutrix is the daughter of informant. He informed that at the relevant time he was residing alongwith his wife and 16 years old girl at Nallasopara. His daughter passed out 10 thstd. examination and after that she left the education. His elder daughter is married. 3] On 31/5/2015, his elder daughter Tejal came to his house and at that time she enquired whereabouts of the prosecutrix. He told that she went outside the house for taking imitation jewellery. At that time Tejal informed him that she had seen prosecutrix alongwith one boy on the motorcycle at Achole road. Then prosecutrix came in the house at about 3:30 p.m. He enquired with her where she was wandering with boy on motorcycle. Initially she refused to answer and then she admitted that she had been with said boy. Then he asked prosecutrix to call said boy. Then prosecutrix introduced him with said boy and told him that said boy is her friend. Name of said boy was Rakesh Mane. The informant given understanding to him not to follow prosecutrix. ..3.. Spl.C.51/15 (J) 4] On 1/6/2015, prosecutrix told informant and his wife that she is going outside for some work and left the house. However, till night she had not returned. Therefore, informant realised that said boy might have kidnapped prosecutrix. Therefore, he lodged missing report on 2/6/2015. 5] On 15/6/2015, informant received phone call of prosecutrix and she told that on next day she will come at home. Accordingly, on 16/6/2015 prosecutrix informed him that she is standing near PCO,near Nallasopara railway station. Accordingly informant took her to his house. Then prosecutrix informed that she has friendship with accused Rakesh Mane. In the month of February, 2015 he had taken her to Chirag Hotel, Kalam Beach and under the pretext that he will marry with her, maintained sexual intercourse with her. Then again on 1/6/2015 he called prosecutrix near Shivshakti Hotel and taken her to his cousin's house. He resided there for 4 to 5 days. During said period he took her at Kalam beach Chirag Hotel and committed sexual intercourse with her. Then he took one room near Dhaniv Talalo on rent and they were residing there till she returned to house and during said period accused maintained sexual intercourse with her. Therefore, the informant lodged complaint against accused. 6] On the basis of said information, crime No.I­ 212/2015 lodged against the accused for the above offences. Investigating officer prepared spot panchnama on 1/8/2015 before two panchas, recovered clothes after seizure panchnama on 18/6/2015 & 23/6/2015. He recorded statements of the witnesses. He sent accused and prosecutrix ..4.. Charge was read over and explained to accused. He pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. POINTS FINDINGS 1] Whether prosecution proves that at .. Yes. the time of incident prosecutrix was minor ? 2] Whether prosecution proves that since 1/6/2015 to 16/7/2015 accused kidnapped prosecutrix who was minor from the lawful custody of her guardian with intention to compel said minor girl to marry with her and thereby committed an offence .. No. punishable U/Sec. 363 & 366 of IPC ? 3] Whether prosecution proves that accused committed rape on minor prosecutrix and thereby committed an offence punishable under Sec. 376 of IPC and U/Section 4 of POCSO Act ? .. No. 4] Whether prosecution proves that accused with sexual intention touched the private part of minor prosecutrix and sexually harassed her and thereby committed offence punishable under Sec. 7 & 12 of POCSO Act ? .. No. 5] What order ? Accused acquitted. ..5.. Spl.C.51/15 (J) 9] Heard Ld. A.P.P. Smt. Khandagale and Ld. Adv. Smt. Sharda Patil for the accused. 10] In order to prove its case, prosecution has examined in all four witnesses viz prosecutrix (PW­1) at Exh.13, Santosh Bhanubhai Makwana (PW­2) at Exh.19, API Dilip Dattatraya Landage (PW­3) Exh.26 and IO API Smt. Rekha Dattatraya Londhe (PW­4) Exh.39. Prosecution has relied on complaint Exh.20, FIR Exh.27, seizure panchnama Exh.23, office copy of muddemal receipt Exh.28, office copy of muddemal report Exh.29, office copy of letter for medical examination to Dr. Babaaheb Am bdekar Hospital, Kandivali Exh.30, arrest form Exh.31, seizure panchnama of clothes of accused Exh.32, office copy of muddemal receipt Exh.33, panchnama of preparation of CD of video shooting of statement Exh.24, office copy of muddemal receipt Exh.34, spot panchnama Exh.21, another spot panchnama Exh.22, office copy of letter to MO Exh.36, office copy of letters to CA Exh.37 & 38. REASONS As to Point No.1 11] Prosecutrix PW­1 (exh.13) deposed that her birth date is 14/6/1999. Verified copy of birth certificate is at Exh.14. PW­2 Santosh Bhanubhai Makwana deposed that birth date of his daughter is 14/6/1999. From the oral as well as documentary evidence, prosecution has proved that in the year 2015, prosecutrix was minor. Hence, I answered point no.1 in affirmative. ..6.. Spl.C.51/15 (J) As to point Nos.2 to 4 12] At the outset it has to be mention here that prosecutrix PW­1 is not supporting to the case of prosecution. She denied that on 31/5/2015 accused threatened her father that he will kidnap his daughter and forcefully married with her. She denied that and on 1/6/2015 accused kidnapped her from the lawful custody of her parent. She denied the contents of portion marked A, B & C of her police statement. 13] It is on record that Santosh Bhanubhai Makwana PW­2 (exh.19) deposed that prosecutrix is his daughter. In the month of June, 2015 prosecutrix told him that she is going outside, however, later on she did not come back to home. CNR NO.MHTH23­001177­2016 Received on : 03/08/2016 Registered on : 03/08/2016 Decided on : 28/08/2018 Duration : 25 00 02 D M Y IN THE COURT OF THE ADDITIONAL SESSIONS JUDGE­2,VASAI. ( Presided over by Rahul R. Bhosale ) 47 of 2016. CNR No.MHTH23­001177­2016. Exhibit No. 40 The State of Maharashtra .... Complainant. (through Tulinj Police Station) versus Raju Tekbahadur Subedi …. Accused. Age 22 years, Resident of Jana Shakti Welfare Society, Gokulnagar, Bavshetpada, Nalasopara. Learned Advocates : Mr. Yogesh Rawool Spl.AP.P. for State. Mrs. Sharda Patil for accused. JUDGMENT (Delivered on this 28th day of August, 2018. ) 1] Accused is facing trial for offences punishable under S.4 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (POCSO Act and S. 376 of Indian Penal Code 1860 (IPC). .. 2 .. Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.47/2016. CNR NO.MHTH23­001177­2016 2] Brief facts of the prosecution case are as under: The Child was residing on the given address with her parents, elder brother and younger sisters while her father was working as a driver. Child left the school since last two years and stayed at the house. Their family friend­Tekbahadur was residing at Nallasopara hence his family and family of Child were having visiting terms. In the year 2015, Tekbahadur approached to the house of Child for arranging marriage of his son­accused with the Child. Accordingly, the marriage was arranged but as the Child was then aged 16 years hence her father told about performing the marriage after 1 year. Meanwhile the Child and accused were talking with each other on phone and they also used to go for outing. b) In October­2015 the accused took the Child to his house under the guise of outing. His parents were sleeping in their shopping block. Being alone in the house, the accused tried to maintain physical relations with the Child ignoring her protest and then he maintained physical relations forciably. Again in December 2015 accused took the Child to his house and maintained physical relations but he told her that he was not going to marry with her. In January 2016 however, the Child became pregnant. On 12/6/2016 the mother of the Child saw her pregnant tummy therefore, she inquired about it. The Child expressed about the physical relations maintained by the accused with her hence the Child was taken to Dr. Sameer where he diagnosed 5 months pregnancy of the Child. The Child thereafter alongwith her parents reported that incident to the Tulinj Police Station. 3] After conducting the investigation, the investigating officer filed charge­sheet against the accused in the Court. A charge for .. 3 .. Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.47/2016. CNR NO.MHTH23­001177­2016 offences punishable under S.4 of POCSO Act and S.376 of I.P.C. was framed and read over to the accused. He pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. The prosecution has examined : Gayatri (P.W.1) Ext.18, Legbahadur (P.W.2) Ext.19, Dr.Mangesh (P.W.3) Ext.21, I.O Sunil (P.W.4) Ext.29 and Mohan (P.W.5) at Ext.34. The prosecution has thereafter, filed the preacipe at Ext.37 for closing the evidence. The statement of accused has been recorded u/s. 313 of Cr.P.C at Ext.38. Accused has raised the defence of total denial. 4] On the basis of the material on record, the points arise for my determination are answered for the reasons as under ­ Points Findings 1. Whether the prosecution has proved that the .. Not Proved. victim was Child on the day of incident as provided under S.2(d) of POCSO Act ? 2. Whether the prosecution has proved that .. Not proved. accused committed penetrative sexual assault on Child? 3. Whether the prosecution has proved that .. Not proved. accused committed rape on Child ? 4. What is the order ? .. As per final order. REASONS 5] Point Nos. 1 to 3 : To prove the charge under S.4 of the POCSO Act, prosecution has relied upon the evidence of mother and father of the Child. The mother of child (P.W.No.1) as per her deposition at Ext.18 has supported .. 4 .. Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.47/2016. CNR NO.MHTH23­001177­2016 the prosecution case that the marriage of the Child was arranged with the accused but as the Child was minor hence it was not performed however, after the engagement, the Child and accused met frequently. She further deposes that the accused had maintained sexual intercourse with the Child on 2 to 3 occasions due to which she became pregnant. Lastly she deposes that the accused refused to marry with the Child. In the cross­ examination however she has admitted that accused has suggested to conduct the DNA test of infant born to Child but they refused. This admission of the witness creates doubt about the accused maintained physical relations with the Child resulted into giving birth to said infact by the Child. 6] The proper witness for removing these doubts would be the Child herself who could lead the direct evidence on these facts. But the prosecution has not examined the Child even after obtaining sufficient time. Basically the prosecution has not found whereabouts of the Child during the trial. In fact, the parents of the Child were also not found aware regarding whereabout of the Child because her mother has admitted in her cross­examination that her daughter married to another and now she has been residing in Nepal and she does not know the present address of the Child. 7] The father of Child (P.W.No.2) has deposed at Ext. 19 on the same line as per the deposition of mother of Child (P.W.No.1). He has also brought on record the fact about arranging the marriage of Child with the accused, which let their meeting with each other resulted into giving birth to the infant by the Child. This evidence however is certainly not the direct evidence which has to be given only by Child who is not been examined by the prosecution. The father of the Child (P.W.No.2) .. 5 .. Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.47/2016. CNR NO.MHTH23­001177­2016 also does not know the whereabout of the Child as he states that the Child left the house of Niranjan Pandit at Nepal where he kept her. Thus, as the Child does not come before the Court hence the prosecution cannot prove that the accused committed the offence of penetrative sexual assault on the Child as required to be proved under S. 3 r/w S.4 of the POCSO Act. 8] Dr. Mangesh (P.W.3) has deposed at Ext. 21 about potency of accused and also collected his blood and semen samples for C.A. On the backdrop of availability of such samples from the accused, the investigating officer would easily get verified the DNA profile with that of infant whom the Child gave birth to. Nothing is found on record that any successful attempt was done by the I.O – Sunil(P.W.4) as per his deposition at Ext.20. Even the said examination was done then also that would become circumstantial evidence which certainly requires the corroboration from the Child who here is not examined. Lastly, the prosecution has examined Mohan (P.W.No.5) at Ext.34 who was PSO who registered the FIR filed by the Child. Again the author of that FIR i.e. Child has not come before the Court hence his evidence as well as FIR at Ext. 35 will not prove independently the case of prosecution. 9] The prosecution has thus not succeeded to prove the charge framed against the accused. No specific age proof of the Child is brought on record so as to conclude that the provisions of POCSO Act would become applicable as the Child who has been covered under s. 2(b) of the POCSO Act.Thus the prosecution has also not proved materially that the Child was aged below 16 years at the time when the alleged incident was held. 10] As the prosecution is not succeeded to prove any penetrative .. 6 .. Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.47/2016. CNR NO.MHTH23­001177­2016 sexual assault therefore, the offence under S. 376 of IPC charged against the accused is also not proved by the prosecution. The prosecution has not proved even prima­facie case against accused relating to the charge therefore the presumptions under Ss. 29 and 39 of the POCSO Act are inapplicable to the present set of facts. The prosecution has thus not succeeded to prove all the charges leveled against the accused. I therefore, answer point nos. 1 to 3 in the negative. 11] Point No.4: The prosecution has not succeeded to prove the entire case against the accused hence he is to be acquitted under S. 235(1) of Cr.P.C 1973 therefore, I proceed to pass the following order. ORDER 1] Accused Raju Tekbahadur Subedi is acquitted as per section 235(1) of Cr.P.C. of the offences punishable under S.4 of POCSO Act,2012 and S. 376 of I.P.C. 1860. 2] His bail bonds stand cancelled. 3] Muddemal Property being worthless be destroyed after appeal period is over. 4] For compliance of provisions of section 437A of Cr.P.C., the accused shall execute bail bonds with sureties of Rs.15,000/­ and shall appear before the higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect of any appeal or revision, if filed against the judgment. sd/­xx Vasai ( Rahul R. Bhosale ) Date : 28/08/2018. Additional Sessions Judge­2, Vasai.
