Her statement was recorded under Section 164(5) of Cr.P.C., 1973 before the 4th Judicial Magistrate First Class, Vasai, wherein the child stated about putting a penis by the accused into her mouth. That statement also does not disclose that accused fingered her anus. I do not find the prosecution case reliable about the accused put his penis into the mouth of child which is not supported by the child in her deposition before the court. But at the same time I also do not find any ground to disbelieve the child that the accused fingered her anus merely because she had not stated same before the police. Because, her said statement attract Sec.59 r.w. Sec.60 of Evidence Act to attract probative value. There is no proof on record as well as no ground is placed by the accused to disbelieve the child on said statement on account of some sort of interest or she was tutored in that regard. Materially, there was no earlier relevance of the child's side with the accused, hence no any personal grudges or revenges play the role in the instant case. Thus, as there is no sufficient explanation on record for deliberately roping the accused in the instant crime, I do not find any ground to disbelieve the ocular testimony of the child before the court. It thus certainly also not the omission amounting to contradiction as the major part of child's statement is based upon her statement. 13] The child's friend – EFG (P.W.6), as per his deposition at Exh.No.24, after entering into the said flat by opening its door forcibly, he noticed post part of that incident. Hence, he ran away alongwith other friend and told about that incident to his mother. In this context, child's mother (P.W.2) deposes at Exh.No.9 that she was informed about the said ..12.. Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.81/2017 CNR No.MHTH23­001268­2017 incident by the neighbour – Nikhat to whom EFG's mother informed it. She repeats what the child has deposed before the court about the incident, wherein she specifically corroborates the fingering committed by the accused as deposed by the child apart from the fondling on her body committed by him. The child told same to her immediately after facing that incident. The immediate reaction of the mother in this situation would be to trace out the wrongdoer, which is found deposed by this witness attracting the reliability to her deposition. She thus, deposes further that she alongwith the child and her friends went to search the accused nearby the said building while the child pointed out the accused who was hesitantly going by his way, therefore she nabbed him with the help of the passers nearby and brought him to the police station. The prosecution has thus completed the chain of incidences in the event of crime as alleged, therefore I do not find any ground to disbelieve the prosecution case. 14] The accused has tried to raise doubt about the prosecution case regarding the fingering committed by the accused on the child in the light of the evidence of Dr.Nirali (P.W.4) at Exh.No.15. She had examined the child on the alleged incident of sexual assault only to give opinion that no such evidence was found and accordingly she has proved her opinion at Exh.No.16. The accused asked her in her cross­ examination that when a major person inserts his finger into the anus of a small child, then it would lead internal bruises, but that suggestion was denied by Dr. Nirali. She, however has admitted that the history of fingering was not told to her before examination of the child. That might be truth, however at the same time it is also to be taken into consideration that immediately within a day from the incident, the child was examined ..13.. Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.81/2017 CNR No.MHTH23­001268­2017 by Dr. Nirali (P.W.4). As evident earlier, the child was traumatized, therefore skipping the details of the incident while telling the same before her examination to unknown Dr. Nirali (P.W.4) by the child is infact a natural event. It is not expected that the child of such a tender age should dare to tell everything about what she faced during that incident. She was of such a small age that she was even not aware about the deliberations behind omission of those incriminating acts on her. 15] It is very unfortunate that in our civilized society where the child's rights are protected by our Constitution, but every now and then we come across to the unbelievable events faced by such delicate minds at so early rise of their life span. Such child would carry on the scars of such ghastly incident throughout its life and sometimes it would lose the natural bonding with the human­being of the opposite sex. It would not only disturb psychologically such child, but grab its basic right to lead the life of human­being. Thus, such cases are required to be handled with an iron hand so as not only to deter the culprit, but also to prevent the constituents of our so­called civilized society from repeating same acts in future. I therefore, do not find the lawful protest of accused to the fingering as proved by prosecution. 16] Section 3 of the POCSO Act provides the definition of sexual assault as : Section 3 : Penetrative sexual assault – A person is said to commit “penetrative sexual assault” if ­ (a) he penetrates his penis, to any extent, into the vagina, mouth, urethra or anus of a child or makes the child to do so with him or any other person; or ..14.. Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.81/2017 CNR No.MHTH23­001268­2017 (b) he inserts, to any extent, any object or a part of the body, not being the penis, into the vagina, the urethra or anus of the child or makes the child to do so with him or any other person; or (c) he manipulates any part of the body of the child so as to cause penetration into the vagina, urethra, anus or any part of body of the child or makes the child to do so with him or any other person; or (d) he applies his mouth to the penis, vagina, anus, urethra of the child or makes the child to do so to such person or any other person. The fingering committed by the accused is covered under clause (b) of Section 3 17] The prosecution has thus succeeded to prove that the accused fondled the body of child particularly touched inappropriately to her breast and the private part. It is also proved that the accused fingered the child. The investigation carried out by Subhash (PW7) as deposed at Ext.25 attracts the regularity in his allotted public duty revealing the presumption under section 114(e) of the Evidence Act. Those are the foundational aspects proved by the prosecution as per the decisions of Hon'ble Apex Court and Hon'ble Bombay High Court (supra). Hence in the light of those decisions, thus, the presumption under Section 29 of the POCSO Act will be made applicable to the prosecution case. The accused thus carries the burden now to rebut that presumption of his culpability. But as evident earlier, the accused has not even brought on record iota of doubt to the prosecution case. There is no convincible defence raisedfor ..15.. Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.81/2017 CNR No.MHTH23­001268­2017 even disbelieving any of the prosecution witnesses on any sound grounds. I also do not find anything on record to conclude that the child and other witnesses have deposed falsely to rope the accused in the instant crime. In the result the prosecution has proved that the accused committed crime under sections­376(2)(i) of IPC 1860 and U/s.3 of the POCSO Act. As the child was below 12 years of age when said penetrative sexual assault was committed, hence it attracts aggravated penetrative sexual assault as provided under section 5(m) of the POCSO Act. 18] The prosecution has thus succeeded to prove that the accused committed the offences under Ss. 3 and 5(m) punishable respectively under Ss.4 and 6 of POCSO Act 2012, and under Ss. 376(2)(i) of IPC 1860. However, before proceeding for sentencing the accused I will give the opportunity to him for making submission on the point of sentencing as required under S.235 (2) of Cr.P.C 1973. 19] Today, in presence of the accused, his counsel Yogesh Rawool has argued that the accused is old person suffering from severe bronchitis and he is the sole bread winner for his entire family therefore, he lastly submits to take a lenient view while sentencing the accused. In counter APP Mrs. Khandagale has submitted that the accused committed heinous and gruesome serious crime against a minor hence the maximum sentence may be inflicted. 20] As evident earlier, the accused committed aggravated penetrative sexual assault on the Child then aged around 12 years having no capacity of even thinking about maintaining the sexual relations. Due to such assault the accused caused not only the crime against the body of the Child but he also affected grossly to the emotional quotient of the ..16.. Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.81/2017 CNR No.MHTH23­001268­2017 Child making her parallised in the emotional bonding about the persons of opposite sex. The agony of a girl to face such heinous crime in her adolescent age would change entirely the pattern of her life. This offence is also committed against the society of which the element like the Child should be mentally and physically healthy and sound constituent. However, as the accused is old and ailing person upon whom his entire family is depending hence considering his role in the instant crime, those aspects should be taken into mind while coupling him with a punishment. 21] The accused is thus convicted for the offences under Ss. 3 and 5(m) punishable respectively under Ss.4 and 6 of POCSO Act 2012, and under Ss. 376(2)(i) of IPC 1860. The minimum sentence for the offences under S. 5(m) punishable under S.6 of the POCSO Act 2012 and under S.376(2)(i) of IPC 1860 is similar i.e. rigorous punishment for term which shall not be less than 10 years but which may extend to imprisonment for life and fine. S.42 of the POCSO Act 2012 provides the alternate punishment in this situation is to be passed which is greater in degree. As both of those punishments are similar hence I prefer to pass the sentence only for S. 5(m) punishable under S.6 of the POCSO Act 2012. The sentence of 10 years rigorous imprisonment alongwith fine of Rs.10,000/­(Rupees Ten Thousand only) is proportionate to the act of present accused. 22] Honourable Apex Court in the case of Ms. Era through Manjula Vs. Government of NCT of Delhi, Cri. Appeal No.12171219/2017, dated 21/07/2017 has held that in such kind of sentence the proper care is to be taken for neutralizing the impact upon the Child by providing various medical as well as psychological assistance. It is made possible only if the comprehensive compensation is granted. ..17.. Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.81/2017 CNR No.MHTH23­001268­2017 The cardinal principle in such cases is the re­formative and beneficial arrangement to be made for the victim of the sexual abuse. S.357­A of Cr.P.C 1973 r/w R.7 of POCSO Rules 2012, mandate such compensation is to be arranged by DLSA. Therefore, I answer point nos. 2 and 3 in the affirmative and pass the order as under : ORDER 1] The accused Mohammad Ismail Abu Baker Jan Mohammad Memon is convicted under Section 235(2) of Cr.P.C 1973 for the offence 5(m) and punished under section 6 of POCSO Act with rigorous imprisonment for a term of 10 years and to pay fine of Rs.10,000/­ (Rupees Ten Thousand Only); in default of payment of fine, accused shall undergo further the simple imprisonment for six months. 2] The benefit of set off under S.428 of Cr.P.C.1973 regarding the period of under trail imprisonment be given to the accused. 3] The Secretary, DSLA, Thane, shall arrange for making the payment of compensation to the Child as earlier as possible. 4] The muddemal property being worthless be destroyed after appeal period is over. 5] The copy of judgment be given to the accused free of cost. 6] The copy of judgment be sent to The Collector, Palghar for taking appropriate action under S.365 of Cr.P.C. 1973. sd/­xxx Vasai ( Rahul R. (Presided over by N.R.Pradhan,Addl.S.J.) Special Case No.38/2015 Exh The State. (Through Arnala Police Stn. C.R.No. I­74­2017) ….Complainant. V/s. Darshan Damodar Meher, Age 23 years, R/at Kumbharwada,Agashi,Virar (W) …. Accused. Offences punishable U/S.354(A)(i)of the Indian Penal Code and Sec.8 Of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Appearances­ A.P.P. Smt. Khandagale for the State. Adv. Shri.J.D.Gharat for the accused JUDGMENT (Delivered on this 7th day of November, 2017) Accused is facing trial for the offences punishable U/Sec. 354(A)(i)of the Indian Penal Code and ..2.. Spl.C.No.38/2015(J) Sec.8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act,2012 (hereinafter referred to as POCSO Act). Case of prosecution in short is as under :­ 2] Informant is father of victim lodged report against the accused on 9/5/2015. He informed that at the relevant time victim was 13 years old. In the month of April, 2015 he had been to the house of his father­in­law for attending the marriage alongwith his family at Agashi, Greenland building, room No.1. 3] On 8/5/2015 at about 10:30 p.m., all the family members were sitting for dinner. At that time wife of informant told victim to call her grand mother who was sitting in another house for taking dinner. The victim had been to her grand mother and gave her message and while she was returning, accused Darshan who was residing in same building caught hold her hand and forcibly dragged her behind the building and embarrassed her, kissed her and pressed her breast. Informant and his wife were waiting for her. However, she did not return till 10:45 p.m. Then victim told informant the incident that accused sexually assaulted her. 4] On the basis of said information, crime No.I­ 74/2015 registered against the accused for the above offences. Investigating was handed over to PSI Vijay ..3.. Spl.C.No.38/2015(J) Yadav. He prepared spot panchanama, recorded statement of victim and other witnesses. Arrested the accused and and after completion of investigation, filed chargersheet against the accused. 5] Charge is framed against the accused vide Exh.6. Charge was read over and explained to accused. He pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. The defence of the accused emerges from the statement U/Sec.313 of Cr.P.C. is of total denial. 6] Following points arise for my consideration,to which I have recorded my findings against them for the reasons to follow­ NO. POINTS FINDINGS 1] Whether prosecution proves that at the time of commission of offence .. In the victim was minor ? affirmative. 2] Whether prosecution proves that on 8/5/2015 at about 10:45 p.m., at Agashi Kumbharwada, behind Green land building, accused embrassed and kissed the victim and pressed her breast who was below 13 years old and thereby committed sexual assault and thereby committed offence punishable U/Sec.8 of POCSO Act .. In the & 354 of IPC ? negative. 3] What order ? Accused acquitted. ..4.. Spl.C.No.38/2015(J) REASONS 7] Heard ld. A.P.P. Smt. Khandagale and ld. Adv. Shri. J.D. Gharat for the accused. 8] In order to prove its case, prosecution has examined in all 5 witnesses viz PW­1 victim at Exh.13, PW­2 Vilas Mewalal Benbansi, father of victim and informant at Exh.20, PW­3 Smt.Sunita Vilas Benbansi, mother of the victim at Exh.23, PW­4 Anil Sopatram Gupta at Exh.25 and PW­5 IO P.I. Vijay Hari Yadav, at Exh.26 and closed its evidence by filing pushis at Exh.32. As to Point No.1 :­ 9] It is the case of the prosecution that at the time of incident victim was 13 years old. Prosecution has examined father and mother of victim. They deposed that birth date of victim is 29/9/2001. The accused has not seriously challenged the age of victim. On the contrary, the learned advocate for the accused has put question in cross­examination to father of victim ­PW­2 that at the time of incident age of his daughter was 13 years. From the evidence of father and mother of victim, the prosecution has proved that at the relevant time victim was minor. Therefore, I answered point No.1 in affirmative. ..5.. Spl.C.No.38/2015(J) As to Point No.2 :­ 9] Ld. APP has forcefully submitted before me that the victim in chief examination has stated that she has doubt that accused Darshan who was residing near the house of her maternal uncle has done bad thing with her. She submitted that in the last line of Chief examination the victim has categorically stated that she identify the person before the Court who has done bad act with her. Therefore, she submitted that the evidence of victim is sufficient to prove the charges levelled against the accused. She forcefully submitted that the parents of victim i.e., PW 2 & 3 deposed about the entire incidence before the Court, except the name of accused. She submitted that the portion marked A & B of their statements which are regarding to the name of accused proved through the evidence of investigating officer and he has categorically deposed that before him PW­2 & 3 stated the name of accused i.e., Darshan Meher and therefore, she submitted that their evidence is also corroborating to the version of victim. She submitted that the presumption under Sec. 29 of POCSO Act, is applicable to Sec. 7 of said Act and Section 8 is punishable Section of Section 7 of the said Act, therefore, presumption is applicable in this case. She submitted that the prosecution has proved the spot panchnama through the evidence of investigating officer. Lastly, she submitted that the prosecution has proved charges against the accused ..6.. Spl.C.No.38/2015(J) beyond reasonable doubt. 10] In this case, the victim is an important witness. Victim PW­1 has deposed that on 8/5/2015 at about 10:30 p.m., her mother asked her to call her grand mother who was in another house for taking the dinner. When she was going to call her grand mother at that time someone had caught hold her hand and forcibly took her behind the building. Said person embarrassed her, pressed her chest and kissed her. She asked said person to leave her otherwise she will shout. At that time her parents came there. Then she went to her house. She further deposed that one boy was residing near the house of her maternal uncle. His name is Darshan. She has doubt on him. She further deposed that she can identify the person, with whom she has doubt if shown to her. Then she identified the accused before the Court and stated that this is the person who has done bad act with her. 11] In cross­examination victim PW­1 admitted that at the time of incident there was darkness. She further admitted that due to darkness she had not properly seen the person who had done said bad act with her. She further admitted that immediately her parents came there and took her to the house of her maternal uncle. She admitted that she had taken the name of accused in police statement on the basis of doubt. She further admitted that when she was residing at Virar at that time accused ..7.. Spl.C.No.38/2015(J) frequently looking towards her. Therefore, she has taken his name. She further categorically admitted in cross­ examination that she had come to home, therefore, she did not know to whom her father caught hold. From the evidence of victim it explicits that she is not firmed on the point that the accused is the person who caught hold her and forcibly took her behind the building, embarrassed her, pressed her breast and kissed her. She only expressed doubt. No doubt, she has stated in the chief examination that accused is the person who had done bad act with her. However in cross­examination she has given vital admission that due to darkness she had not properly seen the person who had committed said bad act with her and therefore, evidence of victim is shaky, hence it is difficult to rely on her evidence. 12] In this case, the parent of victim are not supporting to the case of prosecution on material point. PW­2(Exh.22) is the father of victim has deposed that on 8/5/2015 at about 10:30 p.m., he was present at Virar. At that time his wife asked victim to call her grand mother who is sitting in another house for dinner. However she did not return and there was late. Thereafter he noticed that victim was coming shouting towards the house where he was sitting. Then he asked victim as to what happened. She told him that one boy had caught hold her hand. Therefore, he had been to see said spot but said boy was ..8.. Spl.C.No.38/2015(J) not there. He further deposed that victim told him that the said boy caught hold her hand and forcibly dragged her towards backside of the building. Then the said boy forcibly put his hand into her chest and kissed her. Then he took victim to police station and lodged complaint. He stated that he cannot read Marathi and police did not explain the contents of the complaint in Hindi. Only he has admitted his signature on complaint which is at Exh.21. He specifically denied that while lodging complaint he informed the police that accused Darshan Meher caught hold hand of victim, pressed her breast and kissed her. This witness declared hostile. He did not support the case of prosecution that he heard the shout of victim then he and his wife went to the spot and red handedly caught hold the said boy. He specifically denied that accused Darshan Meher was the boy to whom he caught hold. In cross­examination, this witness admitted that victim had not informed him the name of Accused Darsan Meher. He specifically admitted that the accused before the Court was not present at the time of incident. He specifically admitted that he had not informed name of accused while lodging complaint, as culprit. 13] Mother of victim PW­3(Exh.23) is also not supporting to the case of prosecution. She deposed that on 8/5/2015 in between 10 to 10:30 p.m., she had sent victim to call her grand mother for diner and after some ..9.. Spl.C.No.38/2015(J) time victim came and at that time she was crying and frightened. She further deposed that victim informed her that someone caught hold her hand and tried to drag her. However she specifically stated in chief examination that victim had not informed name of said person to her. She deposed that except that victim had not informed her any other thing. This witness has also cross­examined by the learned APP. She flatly denied that when victim shouted for help then she herself and her husband went under the Greenland building and at that time her husband red handedly caught hold accused Darshan Meher. 14] In this case evidence of victim is not firm. She only expressed doubt that accused is the person who committed bad thing with her. It is the case of prosecution that father of victim red handedly caught hold accused Darshan Mehre. However, on this point he is not supporting to the case of prosecution and flatly denied that he red handedly caught hold accused on the spot. The parent of victim are not supporting to the case of prosecution on material point i.e., accused is the person who embarrassed her, pressed her breast and kissed her. Learned Advocate for accused has placed reliance in case of Harchand Singh & Anr. Vs. State of Haryana AIR 1974, 394, the Honourable Supreme Court has observed that :­ ..10.. Spl.C.No.38/2015(J) “ The function of the Court in a Criminal Trial is to find whether the person arraigned before it is guilty of the offence with which he is charged. For this purpose, the Court scans the material on record to find whether there is any reliable and trust worthy evidence upon the basis of which it is possible to convict the accused and to hold that he is guilty of the offence with which he is charged. If in a case, the prosecution leads two wets of evidence, each one of which contradict and strikes at the other and shows it to be unreliable. The conviction cannot be sustained. From these observations, it is clear that the function of criminal trial is to find whether the person arraigned before it is guilty of the offence with which he is charged. In this case, the material witnesses i.e., victim PW­1, PW­2 and PW­3 deposed about the incident but the victim is not firm that the accused is the person who sexually assaulted her. The parent of victim are not supporting to the case of prosecution that the accused is the person who embarrassed victim, pressed her breast and kissed her. Learned APP has submitted that on the basis of question marks which are proved through the I.O, the Court can convict the accused, however substantial piece of evidence is oral evidence before the Court. The police statements are always corroborative piece of evidence. If substantial piece of evidence is not supporting to the case of prosecution, then only on the basis of police statement one cannot convict the accused. ..11.. Spl.C.No.38/2015(J) 15] The presumption under Sec. 29 is also not applicable in this case because initially burden is on the prosecution to prove the charges against the accused and then only presumption can be drawn. However, in this case the prosecution has failed to prove beyond reasonable doubt the charges levelled against the accused and therefore, Court cannot directly jump on the presumption under Sec. 29 of POCSO Act and only on the basis of said presumption Court cannot convict the accused. 16] The spot panch PW­4 Anil Gupta is not supporting to the case of prosecution. He deposed that he was called on 9/5/2015 by Agashi police and police asked him to put his signature on prepared panchnama. Accordingly he signed on it. 17] The evidence of IO P.I. Shri. Vijay Hari Yadav is formal in nature. The material witnesses are not supporting to the case of prosecution and only on the basis of evidence of I.O., one cannot convict the accused. 18] The conspectus of this discussion is that the evidence of victim PW­1 is not trustworthy and reliable. PW­2 who is father of victim and PW­3 is mother of victim are not supporting to the case of prosecution and they flatly denied that red handedly they had caught hold ..12.. Spl.C.No.38/2015(J) accused. The father of victim also denied that he informed the name of accused to the police as culprit. Therefore, the prosecution has failed to prove the charges levelled against the accused beyond reasonable doubt. Hence, I answered points No.1 in the affirmative & No. 2 in negative. In view of findings of point No.2 accused deserves to be acquitted. I, therefore pass following order :­ ORDER 1] Accused Darshan Damodar Meher is hereby acquitted U/Sec.235(1) of Cr.P.C.for the offence punishable U/Sec. 354(A)(i) of I.P.C. and Sec.8 of POCSO Act. 2] His bail bond stands cancelled. 3] He is directed to give PR bond of Rs.15,000/­ with S.B. of like amount in compliance of section 437­A of Code of Criminal Procedure,1973. Vasai. (N.R.Pradhan.) Date:­7/11/2017 Additional Sessions Judge, saa Vasai.

JUDGMENT ( Delivered on this 14th day of March, 2018 ) The accused is facing trial for the offences punishable U/Sec.354 of the Indian Penal Code (hereinafter referred to as IPC) and Sec.9(m) & 10 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act,2012 (hereinafter referred to as POCSO Act). ..2.. Spl.C.No.54/15(J) Case of prosecution in short is as under :­ 2] On 14/7/2015, informant Majida Khatun Sallauddin Khan lodged report before Valiv police station. She informed that prosecutrix is her daughter. At the relevant time prosecutrix was 8 years old. 3] On 13/7/2015, informant came from her work to her house at about 7:30 p.m. She was not feeling well and therefore, at about 8 p.m., she went to dispensary. At that time prosecutrix was alone in the house. Informant returned to the house of her elder daughter Guddy. At that time prosecutrix was in the house of Guddi and she was crying. The informant wait till the arrival of her son­ in­law and then she lodged complaint against accused. 4] On the basis of said information, crime No.I­ 290/2015 lodged against the accused for the above offences. ..3.. Spl.C.No.54/15(J) Investigation was handed over to PSI S.G.Langhi. He prepared spot panchnama on 15/7/2015 before two panchas. He arrested accused on 15/7/2015. Statement of prosecutrix was recorded before the member of Mahila Dakshata Samitee and video shooting of her statement was also carried out. He recorded statements of witnesses. After completion of investigation, filed charge­sheet against the accused. 5] My Ld. predecessor framed charge at Exh.6 against the accused. Charge was read over and explained to accused. He pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. The defence of the accused emerges from the statement U/Sec.313 of Cr.P.C. is that he was residing near the house of prosecutrix. Some boys used to come to the house of prosecutrix, therefore, he advised her that such behaviour is not proper. He also taken defence that there was quarrel between mother of prosecutrix and him on the ground of water. He submitted that the version of prosecutrix get corroboration from the evidence of her mother. Therefore, he submitted that prosecution has proved the charges beyond reasonable doubt and hence accused be convicted. 12] On the other hand, Ld. Advocate for accused has submitted that prosecution has failed to prove the charges against the accused beyond reasonable doubt. Ld. Advocate for the accused has raised number of objections, I will deal said objections at the relevant time. ..6.. Spl.C.No.54/15(J) 13] It being a case of sexual offence, this Court has to bear in mind certain principles of law, as crystallized from various pronouncements of the Apex Court and High Courts, which has settled the law as regards the appreciation of evidence of the prosecutrix in the cases of sexual assault. In the case of State of Punjab V. Gurmit Singh & Ors. AIR 1996 SC 1393 which is a landmark decision on this point, the Apex Court has laid down that­ “The testimony of the victim in sexual assault cases is vital and unless there are compelling reasons which necessitate looking for corroboration of her statement, the Court should find no difficulty to act on the testimony of victim of sexual assault alone to convict an accused where her testimony inspires confidence and is found to be reliable.” 14] In the backdrop of these legal principles, now I will analise the evidence of prosecutrix (PW­1) Exh.12. She deposed that when she was taking meal at that time uncle Rakesh Gupta came and knocked the door of her house. At that time her mother had gone to the hospital for taking medicine as she was ill. Then accused Rakesh asked her where is her mother. She told him that her mother is ill and she went to hospital for taking medicines. Then she washed her hands and sat in the house. At that time accused Rakesh tied her hands and legs. Then accused took his saliva on his finger and moved his finger from her private part. At this juncture her brother knocked the door from outside. Then she opened her hands ..7.. Spl.C.No.54/15(J) and legs with the help of her teeth and then opened the door. Accused hidden himself behind the door. Her brother entered into the house. Then accused left the said place. She deposed that she was frightened, therefore her brother asked her what happened. Then she narrated the incident to her brother and then both of them went to the house of her elder sister Guddy. 15] Ld. Advocate for the accused submitted that there are contradictions in the evidence of prosecutrix. No doubt, there are some minor contradictions and improvements made by this witness. In police statement there is only reference of applying saliva, however, there is no reference that accused took saliva on his finger. Ld. Advocate for the accused submitted that this is a vital improvement made by witness. Ld. Advocate for the accused further pointed out that there are contradictions in police statement and deposition of prosecutrix regarding when her mother came to the house of her elder sister Guddy, at that time she was crying. However said version not find place in her police statement. She further pointed out that prosecutrix has deposed that when her brother knocked the door accused hidden himself behind the door. But said contents are not finding place in her police statement. She further drawn my attention that prosecutrix has deposed that some neighboures gathered there and they enquired what happened. However, said contents are not finding in her police statement. She further drawn my attention that prosecutrix has deposed that one of the neighbour gave slap to accused. She further submitted that the prosecutrix has made improvement that then the neighbour took accused to the police station. Ld. Advocate for the accused submitted that ..8.. Spl.C.No.54/15(J) these are the vital improvements made by the prosecutrix and therefore, her evidence is not believable and acceptable. 16] It is profitable here to refer the landmark judgment of the Honourable Supreme Court in case of State of Punjab Vs. Gurmit Sigh and others AIR 1986 SC 1392. The Honourable Supreme Court held that in cases involving sexual harassment, molestation etc. the court is duty bound to deal with such cases with utmost sensitivity. Minor contradictions or insignificant discrepancies in the statement of a prosecutrix should not be a ground for throwing out an otherwise reliable prosecution case. 17] It is also profitable here to refer the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court cited ( Vijay @ Chinee Vs.State of Madhya Pradesh) supra. In para No.20 & 21,it is observed by the Supreme Court that­ 20. It is settled legal proposition that while appreciating the evidence of a witness, minor discrepancies on trivial matters, which do not affect the core of the prosecution case, may not prompt the Court to reject the evidence in its entirety. 21. In State of Rajasthan Vs. Om Prakash AIR 2007 SC 2257, while dealing with a similar issue, this Court held that "irrelevant details which do not in any way corrode the credibility of a witness cannot be levelled as omissions or contradictions." 18] Thus, in view of the above, the law on the point can be summarised to be that the evidence of the witnesses must be read as a whole and the cases are to be considered in totality of the circumstances and ..9.. Spl.C.No.54/15(J) while appreciating the evidence of a witness, minor discrepancies on trivial matters, which do not affect the core of the prosecution case, should not be taken into consideration as they cannot form grounds to reject the evidence as a whole. 19] In this case prosecutrix is 9 years old girl. She is not expected to give details of incident while recording her police statement. The contradictions pointed out by the Ld. Advocate for the accused are minor and not sufficient to discard the evidence of prosecutrix which is otherwise trustworthy, believable and acceptable. 20] Second important witness is mother of prosecutrix Majida Khan (PW­2) exh.14. She deposed that on 13/7/2015 as she was not feeling well she returned to her house from her work place at about 7 p.m. At that time her daughter i.e. prosecutrix was present in the house. She told prosecutrix to take meal and closed the door properly as she wanted to go to dispensary for taking medicines. Then she provided meal to prosecutrix and asked her that after taking meal she should go to the house of her elder sister Guddy. She further deposed that at that time her son went to the neighbour house for watching TV. She returned from dispensary and directly went to the house of her elder daughter. When she reached, she noticed that all were crying. Prosecutrix was sitting and she virtually looking frightened. She asked prosecutrix what happened. Prosecution started crying and she told her that when she was taking meal at that time Rakesh uncle came ..10.. Spl.C.No.54/15(J) there and knocked the door. Then Rakesh uncle asked about her mother. Then she replied that her mother went to dispensary and it requires some time to return to house. Then Rakesh sat on the bed. Then Rakesh tied her hands and legs and lay down her on the bed and asked her to take oath of her mother and Quran not to disclose about it. Prosecutrix further told her that then accused removed her underwear and applied his saliva to her private part. Meantime her brother came there and knocked the door. Then she opened the door. Accused hidden himself behind the door. When her brother entered into the house and then accused went away from the house. 21] Ld. Advocate for the accused drawn my attention that PW­2 has also made improvement in her deposition. She drawn my attention that in her complaint PW­2 has not stated that her son went to watch TV in the house of neighbour. She also submitted that the version, when her son knocked the door, accused hidden himself behind the door and not find place in the complaint (Exh.14). She submitted that these are the vital contradictions, which creates serious doubt about the case of prosecution. Again it has to be mention here that there are some minor contradictions. However, said minor contradictions are not sufficient to disbelieve the entire case of prosecution. I find the evidence of PW­2 is trustworthy and creditable. 22] Prosecution has examined panch Kamlakar Kanha Dalvi (PW­3) Exh.16. Similarly the spot panchnama is proved through the evidence of Sunil Dhnyaneshwar Langhi (PW­4) Exh.19, who is IO. Admittedly no incriminating article found and seized under said panchnama (exh.17). ..11.. Spl.C.No.54/15(J) 23] Now I will deal the objection raised by Ld Advocate for the accused. First objection raised by Ld. Advocate for accused is that incident took place on 13/7/2015 and FIR lodged on 14/7/2015. She submitted that there is delay in lodging FIR and therefore, it creates serious doubt about the case of prosecution. 24] It is true that the importance of prompt lodging of FIR cannot be minimized in any way as it gives assurance to the truthfulness of prosecution case. However, at the same time, it has to be remembered that every time delay in lodging of FIR does not become fatal to the prosecution case. Mere delay by itself is not at all a ground to discard the prosecution case. The Court has to see whether the delay in lodging of FIR is explained properly and satisfactorily by the prosecution, as held in umpteen number of authorities by the Apex Court and the High Courts. One of such authority is that of Amar Singh V. Balwinder Singh & Ors. (2003)2 Supreme Court Cases 518. In this authority, it was laid down that­ “Mere delay by itself is not enough to reject prosecution case unless there are clear indications of fabrication. Delay by itself is not a circumstance to doubt the prosecution case. At the most, it will call upon the court to subject the evidence to a closer scrutiny. However, unless there are indications of fabrication, the court cannot reject the prosecution version as given in the FIR and later substantiated by the evidence merely on the ground of delay. These are all matters of appreciation and much depends on the facts and circumstances of each case and for this a host of circumstances like the condition of the informant, the nature of offence, the circumstances in which the incident has taken place etc. have to be taken into consideration.” ..12.. Spl.C.No.54/15(J) In the words of the Apex Court observed that ­ “There is no mathematical formula by which a inference can be drawn either way, merely on account of delay in lodging the FIR.” 25] In Ravinder Kumar & Anr. V State of Punjab (2001) 7 S.C.C. 690 it is held that ­ “The attack on prosecution cases on the ground of delay in lodging FIR has almost bogged down as a stereotyped redundancy in criminal cases. It is a recurring feature in most of the criminal cases that there would be some delay in furnishing the first information to the police. It is to be noted that the law has not fixed any time for lodging the FIR Hence a delayed FIR is not illegal. Of course, a prompt and immediate lodging of the FIR is the ideal as that would give the prosecution a twin advantage. First is that it affords commencement of the investigation without any time lapse. Second is that it expels the opportunity for any possible concoction of a false version. Barring these two plus points for a promptly lodged FIR the demerits of the delayed FIR cannot operate as fatal to any prosecution case. Even a promptly lodged FIR is not an unreserved guarantee for the genuineness of the version incorporated therein. Hence, when there is a criticism on the ground that FIR in the case is delayed, the court has to look into the reason, why there was such a delay. There can be a variety of genuine causes for FIR lodgment to get delayed. Hence the stale demand made in the criminal courts to treat the FIR vitiated merely on the ground of delay in its lodgment cannot be approved as a legal corollary. In any case, where there is delay in making the FIR, the Court has to look into the causes for it and if such causes are not attributable to any effort to concoct a version, no consequence shall be attached to the mere delay in lodging the FIR” ..13.. Spl.C.No.54/15(J) 26] Especially in the cases of sexual offences, the law is more than well settled that, it is very common to come across the delay in lodging of the FIR. As observed by the Apex Court in the landmark decision of State of Punjab V. Gurmit Singh & Ors. referred above ­ “In sexual offences delay in lodging of the FIR can be due to variety of reasons, particularly the reluctance of the prosecutrix or her family members to go to the police and complain about the incident which concerns the reputation of the prosecutrix and the honour of her family. It is only after giving it a cool thought that a complaint of sexual offence is generally lodged. Hence, even if there is some delay in lodging FIR in respect of offence of rape, if it is properly explained and the explanation is natural in the facts and circumstances of the case, such delay would not matter.” It was further observed in this authority that, “In the normal course of human conduct, an unmarried minor girl, would not like to give publicity to the traumatic experience she had undergone and would feel terribly embarrassed in relation to the incident to narrate it to others overpowered by a feeling of shame and her natural inclination would be to avoid talking about it to any one, lest the family name and honour is brought into controversy.” 27] As per the Apex Court, the girl in a tradition bound non permissive society in India, would be extremely reluctant even to admit that any incident which is likely to reflect upon her chastity had occurred, being conscious of the danger of being ostracized by the society or being looked down by the society. ..14.. Spl.C.No.54/15(J) 28] Therefore, the point to be stressed is that the delay in lodging the FIR in the case of sexual offences is not something to be looked into with suspicion but to be understood and appreciated, keeping in mind the social reality and the facts and circumstances of that particular case. That's why the Apex Court in the case of State of Punjab V. Ramdev Singh AIR 2004 SC 1290 while condoning the delay of around 17 days commented that ­ “Delay in lodging the FIR cannot be used as a ritualistic formula for doubting the prosecution case and discarding the same. Delay has the effect of putting the court on its guard to search if any explanation has been offered for the delay, and if offered, whether it is satisfactory or not. If the prosecution fails to satisfactorily explain the delay and there is possibility of embellishment in prosecution version on account of such delay, the same would be fatal to the prosecution. However, if the delay is explained to the satisfaction of the court, the same cannot, by itself, be a ground for disbelieving and discarding the entire prosecution version.” 29] It is also profitable here to refer the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in case of State of Punjab Vs. Gurmit Singh and other, AIR 1996 SC 1393. The Hon'ble Apex Court held that the delay in filing FIR for sexual offence, may not be even properly explained, but if found natural the accused cannot be given any benefit thereof. 30] Herein the case therefore, one has to see whether the conduct of complainant of not lodging the complaint immediately after the incident was unnatural? whether the delay has resulted into embellishment in prosecution case? and ..15.. Spl.C.No.54/15(J) whether the delay is properly and satisfactorily explained by the prosecution? 31] It is on record that incident took place on 13/7/2015 and FIR was lodged on 14/7/2015. Complainant (PW­2) has deposed that when she came to know about the incident on 13/7/2015, she called her son­in­law who was on his work place. Her son­in­law arrived at about 9 p.m. Then she called her land owner. She narrated the entire incident to her landlord. Mobile number of accused was written on the door of his house. With the help of said number, landlord called accused on his mobile phone and then accused came there. Then they went to police station. However, they reached to Valiv police station at about 1 a.m., therefore, police asked her to come on next day and accordingly she again went to Valiv police station on 14/7/2015 and then police recorded FIR. 32] As observed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in AIR 2004 SC 1290 that the Court cannot overlook the fact that in sexual offence delay in lodging FIR can be due to variety of reason. In this case prosecution has properly explained the delay and therefore, the delay in lodging FIR in this case is not sufficient to discard the entire case of prosecution which is otherwise proved. 33] Ld. Advocate for the accused has raised objection that IO has not seized dupatta with the help of which accused allegedly tied the hands of victim. She submitted that this creates serious doubt about the case of prosecution. She also ..16.. Spl.C.No.54/15(J) submitted that IO has not recorded statement of member of Mahila Dakshata Samitee, before whom statement of prosecutrix was recorded and police officer who recorded her statement. Therefore she submitted that it creates serious doubt about the case of prosecution. 34] However, defective investigation or negligency of IO even if it is so, does not affect credibility of the evidence of prosecution witnesses. There are ample case laws on the said aspect like Dhanaj Singh alias Shera and Ors. V. State of Punjab, 2004 S.C.C.(Cri) 851 and C.Muniappan and Ors. V State of Tamilnadu (2010) 3 S.C.C. (Cri) 1402 wherein it is categorically held, “If primacy is given to such designed or negligent investigation, to the omissions or lapses by perfunctory investigation, the faith and confidence of the people would be shaken, not only in the law enforcing agency but also in the administration of justice as doing so would tantamount to playing into the hands of the Investigating Officer.” 35] Therefore, the alleged defects in the investigation which do not go to the root of the matter and do not affect the core of substratum of prosecution case have absolutely no impact on the outcome of the case. 36] Ld. Advocate for the accused has raised objection that complainant (PW­2) has not given consent for medical examination of prosecutrix. She submitted that if there was substance in her complaint, then she would not have refused for medical examination of prosecutrix and therefore, it creates ..17.. Spl.C.No.54/15(J) serious doubt about the case of prosecution. She further submitted that the defence of accused is that due to dispute, complainant filed false case and tutored her minor daughter, cannot be ruled out. 37] Admittedly, it is not a case that accused penetrated his finger in the private part of prosecutrix and therefore, refusal of medical examination of prosecutrix or not giving consent by her mother does not create doubt on the case of prosecution. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case, objection raised by the Ld. Advocate for accused is not sufficient to discard the entire case of prosecution on this ground. 38] Ld. Advocate for the accused raised objection that prosecution has not examined brother and sister of prosecutrix. She submitted that brother of prosecutrix was very important witness, however prosecution has not examined them and therefore, it creates serious doubt about the case of prosecution. 39] As observed by the Honourable Supreme court in number of cases that if the evidence of prosecution found reliable, trustworthy and cogent then, no corroboration is required and conviction can be solely based on the testimony of prosecutrix. Therefore, non examination of these two witnesses is not sufficient to throw the entire case of prosecution which is otherwise reliable and trustworthy. ..18.. Spl.C.No.54/15(J) 40] The conspectus of this discussion is that in this case sole testimony of prosecutrix itself is sufficient to clinch the guilt of accused. It also supported by the evidence of PW­2. The argument advanced by Ld. Advocate for the accused that prosecution has not proved its case beyond reasonable doubt cannot hardly be accepted. Alleged defects shown by Ld. Advocate for the accused merely not recovering dupatta are too minor in the broad conspectus of entire case of prosecution. 41] Thus, after assessing the entire evidence on record in most dispassionate manner and also at the same time taking realistic and sensitive view, this Court has come to the conclusion that prosecution has succeeded in its case against the accused for the offence punishable under Sec. 354 of IPC and under Sec. 9(m) & 10 of POCSO Act. Therefore, I answered point Nos. 2 & 3 in the affirmative. 42] As I held the accused guilty for the offence punishable U/Sec. 354 of IPC and for the offence punishable U/Sec. 10 of POCSO Act, therefore, I take pause here to hear the accused and Ld.A.P.P.on the point of sentence. Vasai. (N.R.Pradhan.) Date:­14/3/2018 Special Judge, Under POCSO Act,Vasai 43] I heard accused, his advocate and Ld. A.P.P. on the point of sentence. ..19.. Spl.C.No.54/15(J) 44] The accused submitted that he does not want to say about the quantum of punishment. Ld. Advocate for the accused submitted that the accused is young and newly married and his first child is in the womb. Therefore, she prayed that minimum punishment be awarded to him. 45] On the other hand, Ld.A.P.P. has submitted that the considering the act of accused maximum punishment be awarded to him. 46] As per Sec. 42 of POCSO Act, where an act or omission constitutes an offence punishable under this act and as U/Sec. 354 of IPC then, notwithstanding anything contained, in any law for the time being in force, the offender found guilty of such offence shall be liable to punishment under this Act or under the IPC, provides for punishment which is greater in degree. As per Sec. 354 of IPC maximum punishment is 5 years and as per Sec. 10 of POCSO Act, minimum punishment is 5 years which may extent to 7 years. Therefore, the punishment prescribed in Sec. 10 of POCSO Act is greater in degree. Therefore, I direct accused to suffer sentence U/ Sec. 10 of POCSO Act. 37] After considering submissions of both the sides and considering the facts and circumstances of the case, I am of the view that following sentence is just and proper to meet the ends of justice. Hence, I proceed to pass the following order :­ ..20.. She further deposed in cross­examination that Naik was staying in the night in the school and used to left school in morning as per his work. That means accused was not working in the school and he was nowhere concern with the work of school. 26] Evidence of I.O. Prakash Shantaram Lahane PW­6 (Exh.28) is formal in nature. As I have mentioned earlier that ..11.. Spl.C.No.52/2015(J) CNR No. MHTH23­001393­2015 he has not made panchanama of 3rd floor and classroom and therefore, the actual situation regarding it is not on record. He also not recorded the statement of other student of school. 27] Conspectus of this discussion is that the prosecution has failed to prove the charges against the accused beyond reasonable doubt. Hence, I answered point No. 2 in the negative. 28] In view of finding of point No.2 accused deserves to be acquitted. I, therefore pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused Karan Hanumant Naik is hereby acquitted U/Sec.235(1) of Cr.P.C.for the offence punishable U/Sec. 509 of I.P.C.and Sec. 12 of POCSO Act. 2] Bail bond of accused stands cancelled and his surety is discharged. 3] He is directed to give PR bond of Rs.15,000/­ with S.B. of like amount in compliance of Section 437­A of Code of Criminal Procedure,1973. Vasai. (N.R.Pradhan) Date:­05/05/2018 Special Judge, Under POCSO Act, Vasai.
