JUDGMENT (Delivered on this 29th day of January, 2019. ) 1] Accused is facing the trial for crime under Ss. 4,6,8 and 12 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act (POCSO Act) and Ss. 376(2)(i) & 451 of Indian Penal Code 1860 (IPC). / 2/ Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.54/2016 CNR No.MHTH23­001398­2016. 2] Brief facts of the prosecution case are as under : On 08/6/2016, the Child stayed in her house alone at around 2.30 pm. Watching the television programme. Her elder­brother was playing out of the house. The accused, earlier known to the Child, came into the house and bolted the door from inside. He said to the Child that he would show her a picture. He caught hold on her hand and brought behind the plywood partition in the room. He shut her mouth by pressing his hand and let her to lay on the ground. The accused removed her pant as well as stripped his pant also and rubbed her vagina. He inserted penis into the vagina of the Child and committed penetrative sexual assault. The Child was bleeding from vagina and suffering pains hence she raised alarms. Ritesh­playing out side of the room responded by opening the front door . Accused ran away. The Child told that incident when her mother returned from attending her job. Child's mother had a talk with her brother and then they filed report of the incident to the police station. 3] After investigation, the charge­sheet was filed in this court against the accused. A charge for offences punishable under sections 376(2)(i), 451 of IPC and S. 4, 6, 8 and 12 of POCSO Act was framed against accused, to which he has denied and claimed to be tried. The prosecution has examined : XYZ (Mother of Child) (P.W.1) Ext.18, ABC (Child) (P.W.2) Ext.20, Deepak (P.W.3) Ext.21, Bhavin (P.W.4) Ext. 26, I.O Ganesh (P.W.5) Ext. 28, Atikul (P.W.6) Ext.36, Ritesh (P.W.7) Ext.38, Dr.Umesh (P.W.8) Ext. 39 and Dr. Swapnil (P.W.9) Ext. 44. The prosecution has thereafter, filed the pursis Ext.47 for closing the evidence. The statement of accused has been recorded u/s. 313 of Cr.P.C. Ext.No.48. Accused has raised the defence of total denial and false implication and has not examined any defence witnesses. / 3/ Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.54/2016 CNR No.MHTH23­001398­2016. 4] On the basis of the material on record, the points arise for my determination are answered for the reasons as under ­ Points Findings 1. Whether the prosecution has proved that the .. Proved. victim was a 'Child' on the day of incident as provided under S.2(d)POCSO Act ? 2. Whether the prosecution has proved that .. Proved. accused committed rape on the Child by shutting her mouth ? 3. Whether the prosecution has proved that .. Proved. accused committed house trespass by entering in the room of informant used as a human dwelling in order to commit the offence of rape on the Child ? 4. Whether the prosecution has proved that .. Proved. accused committed penetrative sexual assault on the Child ? 5. Whether the prosecution has proved that .. Proved. accused committed aggravated penetrative sexual assault on the Child ? 6. Whether the prosecution has proved that .. Proved. accused committed sexual assault on the Child ? 7. Whether the prosecution has proved that .. Not Proved. accused committed sexual harassment on the Child ? 8. What is the order ? .. As per final order. / 4/ Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.54/2016 CNR No.MHTH23­001398­2016. REASONS 5] Point No. 1 : XYZ(P.W.1) ­ the mother of Child has deposed at Ext.17 the Child's birth date as 28/06/2010 while the incident was held on 08/6/2016. Therefore the Child would be aged around 06 years when the incident was held. The Child's age is not in much dispute. The provisions of POCSO Act will be applicable only in case if the prosecution proves that the victim is covered by Section 2(d) of the Act. It provides that, 'child means any person below the age of 18 years'. The child is examined by the prosecution at Ext. No.20, wherein she has deposed her age as of 08 years on the date of deposition recorded on 10/05/2018. This evidence corroborates her birth date as 28/06/2010 is reliable. In the cross­examinations of Child's mother and Child, nothing is found, to disbelieve the genuineness of said entire evidence. 6] Hon'ble Bombay High Court in the case of Ramprasad V/s. State of Maharashtra, 2018(3) RCR (Criminal) 656, lays the test for the age determination of the child. In this decision Hon'ble Bombay High Court has relied upon Rule 12(3) of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection) Rules, 2007, by placing reliance upon the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of State of M.P. V/s. Anoop Singh, (2015) 7 SCC 773, for determination of the age of the victim of rape. Before proceeding further, it is material to peruse said Rule 12(3) as follows : “.....12.3 : In every case concerning a child or juvenile in conflict with law, the age determination inquiry shall be conducted by the court or the Board, or as the case may be, the Committee by seeking evidence by obtaining (i) the matriculation or equivalent certificates, if / 5/ Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.54/2016 CNR No.MHTH23­001398­2016. available; and in the absence whereof; (ii) the date of birth certificate from the school (other than a play school) first attended; and in the absence of whereof; (iii) the birth certificate given by a corporation or a municipal authority or a panchayat; (b) and only in the absence of either (i), (ii) or (iii) of clause (a) above, the medical opinion will be sought from a duly constituted Medical Board, which will declare the age of the juvenile or child. In case exact assessment of the age cannot be done, the Court or the Board, or as the case may be, the Committee, for the reasons to be recorded by them may, if considered necessary, give benefit to the child or juvenile by considering his/her age on lower side within the margin of one year, and while passing orders in such case shall, after taking into consideration such evidence as may be available, or the medical opinion, as the case may be, record a finding in respect of his age and either of the evidence specified in any of the clauses (a) (i), (ii), (iii) or in the absence whereof, clause (b) shall be the conclusive proof of the age as regards such child or the juvenile in conflict with law......” 7] Hon'ble Bombay High Court has further observed that, by referring the aforesaid rule, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that the documents like matriculation or equivalent certificate, date of birth certificate from school first attended and birth certificate issued by local authority can be used for ascertaining the age of prosecutrix alongwith / 6/ Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.54/2016 CNR No.MHTH23­001398­2016. the medical examination reports. Therefore, Hon'ble Bombay High Court, by relying on that decision, has determined the age of the victim. 8] The ossification test was conducted, which has been proved by Dr.Swapnil (P.W.9) in his deposition at Exh.No.44 with his opinion about then age of the child was in between 6 to 7 years which is corroborated by the medical opinion report at Ext.No.46. This is a reliable evidence as per decision (supra) in absence of Child's birth certificate. This evidence also consolidates the birth date of the child is 28/06/2010. As the alleged incident was occurred on 08/06/2016, hence the child was exactly 05 years 11 months and 11 days old when that incident was held. Thus, the victim is covered by the definition of child under Section 2(d) of the POCSO Act, therefore provisions of said Act are applicable to the prosecution case, hence I answer Point No.1 in the Affirmative. 9] Point Nos. 2 to 7 : The prosecution has materially tried to prove penetrative sexual assault on the child and while advancing argument, A.P.P. Mrs.K.M.Khandagale has relied upon the presumptions under S. 29 & 30 of the POCSO Act for presuming that the accused in culpable mind committed the instant crime. In counter Adv. Mr. Digambar Desai for the accused has argued that the prosecution has to prove its case on the basis of the facts with the evidence beyond reasonable doubts. He further submits that though the act provides presumptions of culpability under Ss.29 and 30 of the POCSO Act yet the prosecution has to prove the guilt of accused beyond reasonable doubts in the light of admissible cogent evidence. Before proceeding further it is material to note that Advocate Digambar Desai was appointed as a counsel of accused from free legal aid panel under S.307 of Cr.P.C. 1973. He has taken immense labours and / 7/ Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.54/2016 CNR No.MHTH23­001398­2016. intelligently made all possible defences wittily as expected from the senior defence counsel hence his work as free legal aid panel member is appreciated. 10] To scrutinize that controversy about application of presumptions, accused ha relied upon the decision of Hon'ble Bombay in the case of Ramprasad Amdare Vs. State of Maharashtra, Cri.Appeal No.579/17, dated 27/06/2018. In this decision also the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Babu V./s. State of Kerala, (2010) 9 SCC 189, has been relied upon the basic statutory presumption as every accused is presumed to be innocent, which is a human right. Hon'ble Apex Court held further that, therefore, subject to the statutory exceptions, for which the nature of offence, its seriousness and gravity has to be taken into consideration & mere application of the presumption should not lead to any injustice or mistaken conviction. The various statutory presumptions for guilt of the accused would shift burden of proof of innocence on the accused. However, such presumption should be raised only when certain ‘ foundational facts ’ are established by the prosecution. In the light of this decision therefore, Hon'ble Bombay High Court has concluded that the presumption under Section 29 of the POCSO Act is not absolute and it is triggered only when the prosecution is able to prove 'the foundational facts' in the first place. It has further held that the evidence placed on record by the prosecution is to be examined to first come to the conclusion that ‘ the foundational facts ’ of the prosecution case have been established and thereafter only the accused can rebut the presumption either by discrediting the prosecution witnesses by effective cross­examination or by leading defence evidence. 11] Thus, to find out the ‘ foundational facts ’ to attract / 8/ Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.54/2016 CNR No.MHTH23­001398­2016. presumptions u/s.29 & 30 of the POCSO Act, in view of those decisions (supra), the evidence of the prosecution in the present case needs to be examined. The sole eyewitness­child­ABC(P.W.2) who is the victim of the crime, has deposed at Exh.No.20 that at the time of the incident she was watching the T.V. programme when Porva (accused) came there and told her about he would show her a picture inside and he bolted the door of the house from inside and took her at other side of the plywood­ partition in the house. She deposes further that he made her asleep on the floor by shutting her mouth with hands removed his as well as her pants and rubbed his hand on her urinating part and inserted his urinating part in her urinating part. The Child started crying in the Court when she has deposed the sexual abuse. She was pacified by APP. She deposed further that she raised alarms thereafter. Thus, Child supports the prosecution case. Earlier, I confirmed the capacity of the Child to answer the questions put to her by verifying she as a capable witness under S. 118 of Evidence Act 1872. She was found a competent witness. In her cross­examination also nothing is found adverse to her examination­in­chief except her admissions that the accused was a frequent visitor to her house and he was doing some trifle domestic works also such as fetching water for them. These admissions however nothing bring on record except the fact that the Child and accused were well acquainted with each other hence the Child allowed the accused inside of her house when she was alone. 12] Hon'ble Apex Court has set the law in the case of Madho Ram Vs. State of U.P., AIR 1973 SC 469, that the sole testimony of the prosecutrix can be relied as legal even if it is uncorroborated and conviction on such testimony was upheld. However, the prosecutrix in / 9/ Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.54/2016 CNR No.MHTH23­001398­2016. the present case is Child and the rule of appreciation of Child's evidence is laid by Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Baby Kandayanathil Vs. State of Kerala, AIR 1992 (4) SCC 225, that evidence of Child witness must find adequate corroboration before it is relied upon such rule is a particular wisdom than of law. However, it is not the law that if the witness is Child his evidence shall be rejected even if it is found reliable. The law is that evidence of a Child witness must be evaluated carefully and with greater circumspection because a Child is susceptible to be swayed by what others tell and Child witness is an easy prey to tutoring by others. It evidence of Child is not of a quality to place reliance, it is expected that the court to search for corroboration from some evidence which could give credence to the testimony of a Child witness. The combination of aforesaid rullings is to be applied to the Child's evidence. As evident earlier, the Child's evidence is not found doubtful in her cross­examination hence these rullings (supra) make her evidence admissible. However, let's scrutinize the corroboration from other evidence on record for better precaution. 13] Ritesh (P.W.7)­the adjacent resident of the Child, responded to the alarms Child raised when she felt pains after the accused committed penetrative sexual assault. He deposes at Ext. No.38 that at the time of the incident he was playing cricket alongwith other children adjacent to the house of Child when he heard her alarms as ' Bachao ­ ­ bachao ' (save, save). He ran towards the house of Child, inserted his hand through the hole on the front door and opened the inside hand­drop. He further deposes that after entering into the room he saw the crying Child was wearing her pair of pants standing near the place of cooking gas while one boy present in room attempted to hide himself but after he / 10 / Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.54/2016 CNR No.MHTH23­001398­2016. hurled abuses, that boy ran away. Lastly Ritesh (P.W.7) has identified the accused in the Court as said boy. 14] The cross examination of Ritesh (P.W.7) has not earned any disbelieveness to his evidence. He simply denied the suggestions about his interestedness on account of the cordial relation his maternal aunt had with the mother of the Child. He has denied further that he deposed as instructed by the mother of the Child. Advocate Desai has argued that the other boys playing with Ritesh(P.W.7) at that time are not seen on record as also approached to Child's house hence only response of Ritesh (P.W.7) to the call of Child is disbelieveable. In cross­examination, Ritesh (P.W.7) has admitted that he was playing with around 5 boys he however denied that those boys also rushed to spot of incident. But no ground is found to disbelieve him about his extending helping hand only on the ground that other boys had not reacted. No doubt, the minor omissions found such as the accused tried to hide in the room etc. which was not stated by him in his statement before the police yet they are so minor to affect his deposition. 15] Advocate Digambar Desai for the accused has firstly tried to bring on record that no hole was present on door of house of the Child but Ritesh (P.W.7) as well as spot pancha Deepak (P.W.3) have denied that defence when the door's photograph at Article ­A1 showed to them in their cross­examinations. That photograph­A1 shows clearly the presence of hole at middle portion on the door. Advocate Digambar Desai further submits that hole on the door of the Child's house was so small that none could pass through a hand for opening the inner hand­drop. The actual measurement of that hole is brought on record by the I.O Ganesh (P.W.5) in his deposition at Ext.No.28 in the light of the spot panchanama at Ext. / 11 / Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.54/2016 CNR No.MHTH23­001398­2016. No.22. It was a 5 x 5 cm hole on the door through which Ritesh (P.W.7) as deposed at Ext. No.38 had inserted from outside his hand to open the inner hand­drop. Ritesh (P.W.7) was aged 15 years when he deposed on 19/09/2018, hence he was aged around 12 years on the day of incident, 09/6/2014. Such a Child can easily insert his hand through the 5 x 5 cm hole on the door for opening the inner hand­drop. I therefore, do not find any sort of disbelieveness in the prosecution evidence. 16] That evidence is tried to be doubted in the light of cross­ examination of Deepak (P.W.3) who was a pancha on spot panchanama and he admits in cross­examination that said door did not bear a middle hand­drop from inside. Therefore, accused submits that it was impossible for Ritesh (P.W.7) to open the door from outside by inserting his hand through the hole which was present at middle portion. 17] This argument of accused is though found attractive yet it is not based upon the simple probability also. Because panch­Deepak (P.W.3) has answered immediately before said so called admission that he did not know whether that door bore the upper bolt from inside. Hence he was not aware of actual situations of the inside bolt and hand­drops on the said door therefore, he probably made said a stray admission. Moreover, earlier he has admitted in his cross­examination para no.7 that he is unable to state the exact distance between that inside hand­drop and said hole on that door. It consolidates that this pancha witness is not aware about inside hand­drop was present or not. 18] On the contrary, the Child has deposed that accused by entering into the house, had bolted it with inside hand­drop while Ritesh (P.W.7) deposes that he opened that hand­drop by inserting his hand / 12 / Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.54/2016 CNR No.MHTH23­001398­2016. through the hole on door from outside. This evidence is unrebutted and reliable which sufficiently conclude its genuineness. 19] As per the deposition of the Child, after bolting the door of house form inside the accused had taken her behind the plywood partition of the front room of her house under the pretext that he would show her a picture. This act of accused gives rise to culpable state of mind of the accused to commit the penetrative sexual assault. Ritesh (P.W.7) has deposed that when he entered in house by opening the front door, firstly the accused tried to hide himself in the room and further he deposes that the accused ran away from the house of the Child after he was confronted. Thus, the guilty mind and the intention of the accused in commission of the alleged offence is evident in the prosecution evidence. 20] The central line of defence, as per questions put in the cross­ examinations of those witnesses and argument advanced by Advocate Digambar Desai for accused, is about the illicit relationship in between Child's mother and a ' panipuri ' vendor were getting known to the accused who in­turn conveyed same to the father of the Child. Hence, the defence is taken that on said ground the accused has been roped into the crime by the mother of the Child. The Child has denied in her cross­ examination that said ' panipuri wala ' frequently visited her house as suggested by the accused. Ritesh (P.W.7) has also denied about he knew that 'panipuri wala ' who as per the defence of accused was always present in the vicinity of the house of the Child. Lastly, the accused asked various questions to the mother of Child (P.W.1) in her cross­examination about her such illicit relations. But by admitting only the fact that due to differences her husband reside at native place, she has not admitted any suggestion making the defence of accused reliable. Thus, said defence is / 13 / Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.54/2016 CNR No.MHTH23­001398­2016. not sustainable as even probability in it is not proved. It is also not evident the probability that the Child's mother is of such grossly hostile nature that she could expose her Child to the grave allegations of sexual assault only on the ground about alleged knowledge to the accused of her illicit relations. Lastly, the Child answered in this regard in her cross­ examination that she had not seen her father since long who was residing at native place. Hence defence of accused about accused informed the Child's mother's unchastity to her father is not found probable. 21] The prosecution has relied upon the evidence of Dr. Swapnil (P.W.9) who deposes at Ext.No.44 that upon examination of the Child he materially found the injuries on the genitals as : (i) hymen showed recent tear in 7 O'clock position not reaching upto margin and blood stains were present and, (ii) Fourchette was having recent tear in 7 O'clock position, margins were reddish, the length of tear was 0.5 cm. Dr. Swapnil (P.W.9) was the member of the medical panel formed with Dr. B.M. Kalel and Dr. Shriya Prabhu and that panel opined on the basis of Child's medical examination that evidence of recent forceful vaginal penetration sexual assault was found. This evidence is corroborated by the medical opinion report of the panel at Ext. no.46. 22] In his cross­examination Dr.Swapnil (P.W.9) has denied that the history was only told to him by the mother of the Child and he added afterwards the sentence as the blood was oozing from the vagina of the Child in the history. He has also denied that no blood particles were evident in vagina of the Child. Thus, in and all Dr. Swapnil (P.W.9) has undoubtedly proved about the Child was raped by a major person forcibly. He deposes that the injuries to the hymen and fourchette are so brutal / 14 / Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.54/2016 CNR No.MHTH23­001398­2016. that the fully grown male could easily inflict them in attempt to forcibly rape the under­aged minor Child. 23] The Child was bleeding from vagina during that penetrative sexual assault as deposed by the Child, supported by her mother and corroborated by the seizure of her blood stained apparels as per the seizure panchanama at Ext. 27. Bhavin (P.W.4) is the witness on seizure panchanama at Ext.27, who deposes at Ext.26 that, in his presence, the Child's mother handed over Child's white top with elastic pair of pants which were worn by the child at the time of incident. The seizure panchanama Ext.27 discloses seizure of white ‘ Salwar ’ but Bhavin (P.W.4) has deposed before the court as it was a while ‘ top ’. I.O. ­ Ganesh (P.W.5) deposes at Ext. No.28 that the said top was bearing blood stains while it was dirty also. He sent that Top with pant in sealed condition to the FSL. The C.A. report at Ext. 12/1 (alongwith Ext.12) reveals the ‘ Salwar ’ is in fact a ‘ Top ’. Hence, the seizure panchanama at Ext. 27 mistakenly mentions the ‘ Top ’ as ‘ Salwar ’. But this will not affect prosecution case, as it would be at the most a negligence of I.O. in mentioning name of apparel properly. As two independent pieces of evidence prove it was a ‘ Top ’ hence ‘ Salwar ’ as mentioned in seizure panchanama Ext.27 in description of seized apparels should be read as ‘ Top ’. The C.A. report at Ext. 12/1 discloses the Top bears a human blood stain but seizure pancha Bhavin (P.W.4) does not state about it. However, seizure panchanama Ext. 27 which he proves as prepared in his presence, reveals presence of blood stains on Top. Hence the conclusion will be the Child was bleeded from vagina made that Top blood stained. This conclusion supports evidence of prosecution which already reveals only pant of Child was removed by accused. Thus, this circumstantial / 15 / Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.54/2016 CNR No.MHTH23­001398­2016. evidence also corroborates the prosecution case to conclude that the Child was bleeding out of said gruesome rape by sustaining vaginal injuries. 24] Child was put a suggestion in her cross­examination that she had sustained vaginal injury due to felling on the stony surface which has been denied by her. The accused also cross­examined Dr. Swapnil (P.W.9) by putting the suggestion that the hymen and fourchette of the Child would have been ruptured due to self fingering and playing. Dr. Swapnil (P.W.9) has denied that suggestion. Thus, the only conclusion here is that the Child faced a brutal penetrative sexual assault from the accused as per occular testimony evidence earlier. 25] Dr. Umesh (P.W.8) who gave the potency certificate of the accused at Ext.No.41 has proved it in his deposition at Ext.39. He has opined that the accused was capable to do the sexual intercourse. In his cross­examination he has admitted that the potency of accused he opined by conducting secondary characteristics examination and not conducted any test for penial erection. However, it is not the defence of accused that he is not potent or suffering from any erectile deformity. Thus, the opinion of expert in medical field cannot be ruled out merely on he had not carried any particular potency test. Examination of secondary characteristic is a reliable examination for inferring potency in this situation. The accused, in this backdrop, has not brought on record anything to disbelieve that test. The Child has already deposed that the accused inserted his urinating part into her urinating part due to which she suffered immense pains. In the result, asper the evidence given by the prosecution on record, no other inference could be drawn except the penetrative sexual assault, as alleged, was committed by the accused on the Child. / 16 / Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.54/2016 CNR No.MHTH23­001398­2016. 26] There are some sort of minor omissions and improvements found in the evidence of material prosecution witnesses However, one material aspect is to be considered that at the time of incident the child and the circumstantial witness, Ritesh (P.W.7) were of tender aged persons. Such Child faced that unnatural frightening incident which certainly pressurized and disturbed her abundantly. It is evident that she was profusely crying. There was a natural impact on the child who faced said barbaric and beastly act of the accused. Therefore, it is not expected at all from such a child that she should depose before the court every minute detail of such incident, therefore some sort of discrepancies should be there which only rates such deposition as natural and not tutored one. 27] It is very unfortunate that in our civilized society where the child's rights are protected by our Constitution, but every now and then we come across to the unbelievable events faced by such delicate minds at so early rise of their life span. Such child would carry on the scars of such ghastly incident throughout its life and sometimes it would lose the natural bonding with the human­being of the opposite sex. It would not only disturb psychologically such child but rob its basic right to lead the normal life as human­being. Thus, such cases are required to be handled with an iron hand so as not only to deter the culprit but also to prevent the so­called errant constituents of civilized society from repeating such acts in future. I therefore, do not find the lawful protest of accused to the sexual abuse as proved by prosecution. 28] Section 3 of the POCSO Act provides the definition of penetrative sexual assault as : Section 3 : Penetrative sexual assault – A person is said to commit / 17 / Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.54/2016 CNR No.MHTH23­001398­2016. “penetrative sexual assault” if ­ (a) he penetrates his penis, to any extent, into the vagina, mouth, urethra or anus of a child or makes the child to do so with him or any other person; or (b) he inserts, to any extent, any object or a part of the body, not being the penis, into the vagina, the urethra or anus of the child or makes the child to do so with him or any other person; or (c) he manipulates any part of the body of the child so as to cause penetration into the vagina, urethra, anus or any part of body of the child or makes the child to do so with him or any other person; or (d) he applies his mouth to the penis, vagina, anus, urethra of the child or makes the child to do so to such person or any other person. The act committed by the accused is covered under clause (a) of Section 3(supra) as per protection case as evident. 29] The prosecution has thus succeeded to prove the accused fondled the body of child and committed penetrative sexual intercourse. Deepak (P.W.3), the witness in whose presence as per the case of prosecution, the disclosure statement was made by the accused at Ext.23 and in its persuation, the place of offending articles was discovered and accordingly the memorandum recovery panchanama at Ext.24 was prepared. This entire evidence reveals that the accused made disclosure statement about he would hand over his wearing apparels on the day of incident and accordingly he handed them over to the police from his / 18 / Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.54/2016 CNR No.MHTH23­001398­2016. residence at the work place. However, as per S.27 of the Evidence Act 1872, the fact discovered distinctly if relevant then only it would be admissible. As no other evidence is found on record to establish that the accused had worn recovered apparels at the time of incident. It is also not the prosecution case that those apparels of the accused bore any blood or semen stains to couple him with the incident. The CA report at Ext. 12(1) also does not disclose any such proof was detected except the accused's underwear bore semen stain. This aspect is natural even in case of male accused in such a sexually grown physical age. It would not couple him with penetrative sexual assault he committed on present Child. I therefore, also do not find relevant to consider Advocate Digambar Desai's argument that such preservation of apparels by accused is improbable on the ground that the culprit would dispose of the apparels if they were used in crime. Thus, the prosecution has not succeeded to prove discovery under S. 27 of Evidence Act 1872. However, not proving this circumstantial evidence will not affect to the prosecution case which is already proved in the light of cogent occular evidence. 30] The investigation carried out by Ganesh (PW.5) as deposed at Ext.28 attracts the regularity in his allotted public duty applying the presumption under section 114(e) of the Evidence Act. Advocate Digambar Desai has asked various questions to this witness in the cross­ examination about the mode and manner of videography of the Child's statement for doubting the truthness of the statement made by her. Ganesh (P.W.5) has answered about he does not remember about the events as suggested in the cross­examination. The said VCD of the Child's statement is produced on record but the prosecution has not relied upon it. The accused also has not confronted Ganesh (P.W.5) with the content / 19 / Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.54/2016 CNR No.MHTH23­001398­2016. of said VCD. Basically the videography of the Child's statement is to be conducted as per S.26(4) of the POCSO Act only as the additional requirement of recording of the statement under S. 161 of Cr.P.C.1973. That procedure thus is to be carried out only for additional security measures for effective investigation and the same is to be dealt with as per the procedure under S. 162 of Cr.P.C.1973. Thus, on the basis of any doubtful situation in the recording if at all is noticed then the procedure aforesaid is to be carried out for bringing that aspect on record. That apart, when the prosecution has not relied upon the videographed statement of the Child then the defence has no right to raise doubts to the Child's statement recorded byhe police in usual manner under S.161 of Cr.P.C.1973. Moreover, the Child in her occular testimony has deposed the reliable evidence about the incident hence the doubts tried to be raised by the accused are not sustainable. 31] The prosecution has succeeded to prove ‘ the foundational facts ’ as per the decisions of Hon'ble Apex Court and Hon'ble Bombay High Court (supra). Hence in the light of those decisions, thus, the presumption under Sections 29 & 30 of the POCSO Act will be made applicable to the prosecution case concluding culpability and involvement of accused in instant crime. The accused carries the burden now to rebut those presumptions of his culpability. But as evident earlier, the accused has not brought on record even iota of doubt to the prosecution case There is no convincible defence raised for even disbelieving any of the prosecution witnesses on any sound grounds. I also do not find anything on record to conclude that the child and other witnesses have deposed falsely to rope the accused in the instant crime. In fact no deleberations found with witnesses to rope the accused in the instant crime. The Child / 20 / Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.54/2016 CNR No.MHTH23­001398­2016. at such tender age in fact has brought on record the sexual assault she faced which is creditable in the sense to remove the weeds like accused from the Civilized Soceity. In the result the prosecution has proved that the accused committed crime U/s.3 of the POCSO Act which attracts the definition of rope under s. 375 (a) (sixth) of IPC 1860. As the child was below 12 years of age when said penetrative sexual assault was committed, hence it attracts aggravated penetrative sexual assault as provided under section 5(m) punishable u/s. 6 of the POCSO Act & S. 376(2)(i) of IPC 1860. The prosecution has also succeeded to prove the sexual assault on Child as defined under S. 7 punishable u/s.8 of the POCSO Act. Accused is found trespassed Child's house attracting S. 442 punishable u/s.451 of IPC. However, the prosecution has not succeeded to prove sexual harassment of the Child was committed by the accused as defined under S.11 punishable u/s.12 of the POCSO Act. Hence I answer point nos. 2 to 6 in the affirmative & point no.7 in the negative. 32] Point No. 8 : The prosecution has succeeded to prove that the accused committed the offences : u/Ss. 3, 5(m) and 7 punishable respectively under Ss.4, 6 and 8 of POCSO Act 2012, under S.375(a)(sixth) punishable u/s.376(2)(i) and u/s. 442 punishable u/s.451 of IPC 1860. But the prosecution has not succeeded to prove the offence u/s. 11 punishable under S.12 of the POCSO Act. However, before proceeding for sentencing the accused I will give the opportunity to him for making submission on the point of sentencing as required under S.235 (2) of Cr.P.C 1973. 33] Today, in presence of the accused, his counsel Mr. Digambar / 21 / Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.54/2016 CNR No.MHTH23­001398­2016. Desai has argued that the accused is of very young aged hence considering his future prospectives the lenient view may be taken while sentencing him. In counter APP Mrs. K.M.Khandagale has submitted that the accused committed heinous and gruesome serious crime against a minor hence the maximum sentence may be inflicted. 34] As evident earlier, the accused is found known to the Child who was frequently visiting her house and by taking disadvantge of the faith reposed by the Child, he indulged in her sexual abuse. Thus, the act committed by the accused discloses his gross inculpability. Due to such assaults the accused caused not only the crime against the body of the Child but he also affected grossly to the emotional quotient of the Child making her paralyzed in the emotional bonding with the persons of opposite sex. The agony of a girl to face such heinous crime in her early childhood would change entirely the pattern of her life. This offence is also committed against the society of which the element like the Child should be mentally and physically healthy and sound constituent. Therefore the proportionate sentence has to be passed. The young age of accused around 23 years is to be considered for passing proportionate sentence with due considerations about his gruesome acts. 35] The guilt of accused is proved punishable under S.376(2)(i) of IPC 1860 and under S.6 of the POCSO Act, both coupled with punishment for not less than 10 years alongwith fine. S.42 of the POCSO Act 2012 provides the alternate punishment in this situation is to be passed which is greater in degree. The prosecution has also succeeded to prove penetrative sexual assault as per S.3 punishable u/s.4 and sexual harassment as per S.7 punishable u/s.8 of POCSO Act however, those offences were committed in the chain reached to the more serious offence / 22 / Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.54/2016 CNR No.MHTH23­001398­2016. u/s.5(m) punishable u/s.6 of POCSO Act. I therefore prefer to pass sentence under S.6 of the POCSO Act for rigorous imprisonment of 20 years alongwith fine of Rs.15,000/­ (Rupees Fifteen Thousand Only). Further, the accused is sentenced u/s.451 of IPC for 2 years rigorous imprisonment and fine of Rs.1000/­ (Rupees One Thousand Only) ; u/s. of IPC 1860 for 1 years rigorous imprisonment and fine of Rs.1000/­ (Rupees One Thousand Only). However, prosecution has not succeeded to prove the sexual harassment of the Child as per S.11 punishable u/s.12 of POCSO Act hence, the accused is to be acquitted from that charge. 36] Honourable Apex Court in the case of Ms. Era through Manjula Vs. Government of NCT of Delhi, Cri. Appeal No.12171219/2017, dated 21/07/2017 has held that in such kind of sentence the proper care is to be taken for neutralizing the impact upon the Child by providing various medical as well as psychological assistance. It is made possible only if the comprehensive compensation is granted. The cardinal principle in such cases is the re­formative and beneficial arrangement to be made for the victim of the sexual abuse. S.357­A of Cr.P.C 1973 r/w R.7 of POCSO Rules 2012, mandate such compensation is to be arranged by DLSA. Hence, I pass the order as under : ORDER 1] The accused ­ Ansar Ahmed Fazlur Rehaman Ansari @ Pora is convicted under Section 235(2) of Cr.P.C 1973 for : (i) the offence under S.5(m) punishable u/s. 6 of the POCSO Act for rigorous imprisonment of 20 years alongwith fine of Rs.15,000/­ (Rupees Fifteen Thousand Only); in default of payment of fine, accused shall undergo further the simple imprisonment for six months. / 23 / Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.54/2016 CNR No.MHTH23­001398­2016. (ii) the offence under S. 442 punishable u/s. 451 of IPC 1860 for 2 years rigorous imprisonment and fine of Rs.1000/­ (Rupees One Thousand Only); in default of payment of fine, accused shall undergo further the simple imprisonment for one month. 2] All sentences shall run concurrently. 3] The benefit of set off under S.428 of Cr.P.C.1973 regarding the period of under trial imprisonment be given to the accused. 4] The Secretary, DSLA, Thane, shall arrange for making the payment of compensation to the Child as earlier as possible. 5] The muddemal property being worthless be destroyed after appeal period is over. 6] The copy of judgment be given to the accused free of cost. 7] The accused is acquitted under S.235(1) of Cr.P.C.1973 for the offence punishable under S. 12 of POCSO Act. 8] The copy of judgment be sent to The Collector, Palghar for taking appropriate action under S.365 of Cr.P.C. 1973. sd/­xx Vasai ( Rahul R. Bhosale ) Date : 29/01/2019. Additional Sessions Judge­2, Vasai.

Pravin Narayan Nimbalkar at Exh.20 .. 5 .. POCSO Spl. I have recorded my findings against each of them for the reasons given below. .. 6 .. POCSO Spl. Case No. 63/2015 CNR : MHTH23­001403­2015 Judgment Points 1. Whether prosecution has proved that since November­2014 to 26.6.2015, at Gangdpada, Dhainvbaug, Nalasopara (East), accused no.1 to 4, in furtherance of their common intention, have outraged modesty/committed sexual assault on victim girl time to time? 2. What order and sentence if any? Findings. 1. In negative. 2. In negative. 3. Accused are acquitted. See the order below. : REASONS : As regards to point number 1 and 2 : – 11] Learned A.P.P. for the State has submitted that admittedly the marriage of complainant was fixed with accused no.1. Admittedly complainant refused to marry with accused no.1. Complainant made allegation that the conduct of accused no.1 was not good. The evidence of complainant is fully consistent and corroborative with facts contended in complaint. .. 7 .. POCSO Spl. Case No. 63/2015 CNR : MHTH23­001403­2015 Judgment Complainant and her father P.W.2 Nafis Ansari have specifically deposed about the acts of accused no.1 to 4. The evidence of father P.W.2 Nafis Ansari is fully consistent and corroborative with the evidence of complainant. Their evidence is just, natural, trustworthy and reliable. Learned A.P.P. has submitted that the evidence of P.W.3 Rahat Alam Shaikh is sufficient to prove the circumstance of spot. The evidence of Investigation Officer P.W.4 Pravin Nimbalkar is fully consistent and corroborative. The evidence of prosecution's witnesses remained unshaken. Learned A.P.P. has prayed to place reliance on the evidence of prosecution's witnesses and to convict the accused. 12] Learned Advocate Smt. Kusum Pandey, who appeared for accused, has submitted that the marriage of complainant and accused no.1 was arranged marriage. Complainant was coming at the house of accused before marriage. Family members of accused have suggested complainant not to come at their house before marriage. Complainant was sending obscene message to accused no.1. Accused no.1 has displayed the said messages to the father of complainant. There was a quarrel between family of accused and complainant. Accused and his family members have refused to perform the marriage of accused no.1 with complainant. Accused are rich persons. Complainant and her family members are having grudge against accused because accused no.1 refused to marry with complainant. They have made false allegations and imaginary story. .. 8 .. POCSO Spl. Case No. 63/2015 CNR : MHTH23­001403­2015 Judgment 13] Learned Advocate Smt. Kusum Pandey for accused has submitted that complainant has not specifically mentioned the date, day and time of each incident took place with her. She has not specifically narrated the act of each accused with detailed material particulars including the place, day, date and time of incident. The evidence of complainant appears to be vague one. Learned Advocate for the accused has submitted that the evidence of P.W.2 Nafis Ansari is hearsay in nature. He had not seen any incident. Learned Advocate has submitted that admittedly complainant and accused are neighbours. Their houses are before each other. They are residing in densely populated area. Complainant has made allegations that each accused have outraged her modesty whenever she was going out of the house and coming back to the house. Learned Advocate has submitted that this fact indicates that the alleged incident had taken place before the house of complainant. Admittedly, complainant is residing with her parents. Admittedly complainant is residing with her parents. Admittedly witnesses and accused are residing in densely populated area. If accused have committed such offence near the house, then definitely other family members of complainant and neighbours would have seen the incident. Investigation Officer P.W.4 Pravin Nimbalkar has specifically deposed that he enquired with neighbours. Prosecution fails to examine the neighbours and the family members of victim girl who have actually witnessed the .. 9 .. POCSO Spl. Case No. 63/2015 CNR : MHTH23­001403­2015 Judgment alleged incident. Therefore, the sole testimony of complainant does not appear to be trustworthy and reliable one for want of due corroboration. 14] Learned Advocate has submitted that the evidence of complainant is not free from material omissions and contradictions. Complainant has deposed coloured version. Complainant has deposed exaggerated facts before the court. She has made improvements. It creates doubt about her integrity. Learned Advocate has submitted that the evidence of panch witness and investigation officer appears to be formal in nature. Learned Advocate has prayed to discard the evidence of prosecution's witnesses and to acquit the accused. 15] It is an admitted fact that complainant and accused are neighbours. It is an admitted fact that the houses of complainant and accused are before each other. It is an admitted fact that there is a road in between the houses of complainant and accused. It is an admitted fact that the school is nearer to the house of complainant. It is an admitted fact that complainant is residing with her parents and other family members. The facts and circumstances indicate that more than five members are residing in the house of complainant. It is an admitted fact that complainant and accused are residing in densely populated area. It is an admitted fact that complainant got married with Salman Ansari on 18.3.2015. It is an admitted fact that meeting was .. 10 .. POCSO Spl. Case No. 63/2015 CNR : MHTH23­001403­2015 Judgment arranged at the house of Shakilbhai for the settlement of dispute between families of complainant and accused which arose on account of breaking of marriage between complainant and accused no.1. The said dispute was settled. 16] Prosecution has examined complainant at Exh.14. Complainant and her parents have not engaged Advocate. They were explained about the availability of Legal Services. They have refused to accept Legal Services. I have verified complainant. Complainant was having sufficient power of understanding. She was having knowledge about the sanctity of oath. Oath was administered to her. Precaution was taken that accused and witness shall not see each other. Parents of complainant were allowed to sit in Court Hall to give moral support to her. 17] Complainant has deposed that in the month of November, 2014 accused no.1 Habin Khan started stalking her while going to school and returning back. Accused no.1 used to utter obscene words, “Ae Aati Kya Khandala. Wah Kya Item Hai”. Complainant has not disclosed specific date, place and time of each incident took place with her. The statements made by complainant against accused no.1 appear to be general and omnibus. 18] Complainant deposed that accused no.2 Taufik is .. 11 .. POCSO Spl. Case No. 63/2015 CNR : MHTH23­001403­2015 Judgment elder brother of accused no.1 Habib. Accused no.2 was always taunting and defaming her as her marriage was broken. Accused no.3 was always blowing whistle by looking at her while going outside the house and coming back. Accused no.3 was always playing obscene songs on mobile phone by looking at her. All accused have caused her harassment. 19] I have carefully considered the evidence of complainant. It has been alleged that accused no.1 to 4 have continuously caused harassment of complainant since November­ 2014 till 26.6.2015. Admittedly each incident had taken place nearer to the house of complainant. Had it been a fact, then definitely the family members of complainant and neighbours would have got an opportunity to see at least any one of the incident of harassment caused by accused to the complainant. It is very surprising that none of the neighbours or family members of complainant had seen a single instance of outraging modesty of complainant or causing harassment of complainant. This is unnatural circumstance. If alleged instances were taking place day­to­day, then definitely complainant in due natural course should have disclosed about it to her family members or at least to the female members of her family. Complainant is silent on this point. 20] I have carefully considered the evidence of complainant and facts contended in complaint (Exh.15). .. 12 .. POCSO Spl. Case No. 63/2015 CNR : MHTH23­001403­2015 Judgment Complainant has not specifically mentioned one of the particular incident took place with her. Complainant has not given the detailed material particulars of each incident took place with her. She has not disclosed particular date, time and place of any one of the incident took place with her. The allegations made by complainant appear to be general and omnibus. In these circumstances it is not just and proper to place reliance on evidence of complainant in absence of due corroboration from other material witnesses. 21] The evidence of complainant is not free from material omissions and contradictions. Material omissions came to be recorded in para No.6 of cross­examination of complainant. 22] I have carefully considered the evidence of P.W.2 Nafis Ansari. He is the father of complainant. He claimed that on 26.6.2015 he came back at home at 6.00 p.m. At that time complainant told him that accused no.1 to 4 have caused her harassment by stalking her and by taunting her in obscene words. Complainant told him that accused were blowing whistle by looking at her. Accused used to play obscene songs on mobile phone by looking at her. The evidence of P.W.2 Nafis Ansari appears to be general and omnibus. He has not specifically disclosed the overt act of each accused which complainant has disclosed to him. The nature of allegations made by this witness against accused are general and omnibus. The evidence of .. 13 .. POCSO Spl. Case No. 63/2015 CNR : MHTH23­001403­2015 Judgment complainant and P.W.2 Nafis Ansari does not appear to be just, natural, trustworthy and reliable. I discard their evidence. 23] The evidence of panch witness P.W.3 Rahat Alam Shaikh and Investigation Officer P.W.4 Pravin Nimbalkar appears to be formal in nature. The circumstance of inspection of spot is not sufficient to connect accused with the present crime. 24] I have carefully considered the material facts and circumstances of the present case. The evidence of complainant and her father does not disclose a single material particular incident of harassment caused by any one of the accused to the complainant. In these circumstances the conduct of complainant and her father does not appear to be just, natural and trustworthy. 25] Admittedly accused are rich persons. Admittedly accused no.1 refused to marry with complainant. Admittedly a meeting was held at the house of Shakilbhai for the settlement of dispute. Shakilbhai appears to be a material witness in the present case in order to prove the facts which were disclosed by complainant and her father at the time of incident. Prosecution did not examine Shakilbhai. Thus, prosecution has withheld the corroborative piece of evidence. This fact is sufficient to draw an adverse inference against the prosecution. In these circumstances the defence made out by accused appears to be .. 14 .. POCSO Spl. Case No. 63/2015 CNR : MHTH23­001403­2015 Judgment probable one. I hold that the evidence of prosecution's witnesses does not appear to be just, natural and trustworthy. The evidence of prosecution's witnesses is not sufficient to establish the complete chain of material facts and circumstances beyond all reasonable doubt. Accused have made out defence. The defence made out by accused appears to be probable one. Prosecution fails to prove the guilt of accused beyond all reasonable doubt. I have answered Point No.1 and 2 in Negative. As regards to point no.3 ­ 26] In view of my findings on point No.1 and 2, I hold that the evidence on record is not sufficient to bring accused to the home of guilt beyond all reasonable doubt. The defence made out by the accused appears to be probable one. Accused are entitled for benefits of doubt. I proceed to pass following order :­ ORDER 1} Accused Habib Shafik Khan, Taufik Shafik Khan, Rafik Shafik Khan and Nafis Shafik Khan are acquitted under section 235(1) of Cr.P.C. of charge for offence punishable under section 354, 506 r.w. 34 of Indian Penal Code and Section 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 2} Bail bonds of accused stand cancelled and sureties are discharged. .. 15 .. Therefore, though accused is held guilty for the offence punishable U/Sec. 4, he is punished U/Sec. 6 of the said Act, which is aggravated form of Sec. 4. As per Sec. 42 of POCSO Act, where an act or omission constitutes an offence punishable under this act and as U/Sec. 376 of IPC then, notwithstanding anything contained, in any law for the time being in force, the offender found guilty of such offence shall be liable to punishment under this Act or under the IPC, provides for punishment which is greater in degree. As per Sec. 376 of IPC minimum punishment is 7 years and as per Sec. 6 of POCSO Act, minimum punishment is 10 years. Therefore, the punishment prescribed in Sec. 6 of POCSO Act is greater in degree. Therefore, I direct accused to suffer sentence U/ Sec. 6 of POCSO Act. 37] Accused is 20 years old. The prosecutrix is the cousin of accused and he put his pennis into her mouth. After considering submissions of both the sides and considering the facts and circumstances of the case, I am of the view that following sentence is just and proper to meet the ends of justice. Hence, I proceed to pass the following order :­ ORDER 1] The accused Dineshkumar Kamlashankar Yadav, is hereby convicted U/Sec. 235(2) of Cr.P.C. for the offence punishable U/S. 6 of POCSO Act and he is sentenced to suffer 10 years Rigorous Imprisonment and ..15.. Spl.(Atro)C.No.69/15(J) to pay a fine of Rs.10,000/­(Rs. Ten thousand only) and in default to suffer Rigorous Imprisonment for six months. 2] The accused is entitled to get set off U/Sec. 428 of Cr.P.C.for the period already undergone in the jail. 3] Muddemal property, if any be destroyed after appeal period is over. 4] Copy of this judgment be given to the accused at free of costs. He should be kept under watch and supervision of the Probation Officer who would visit his house and record the statement of his wife and father in law every month and the Probation Officer should report the same to this court every month. He should keep the accused under his control and would make him realize how difficult for him to get out from the clutches of law. (S.R.Vadali.) Vasai. Extra Addl.Sessions Judge, Date: 16­01­2019 Vasai. 38] The accused is present in the court today. I have informed him that all the charges levelled against him to have been proved and he is going to be convicted . I have asked him as to what he has to say. He has not answered anything and just remained silent before this court. 39] Heard ld.A.P.P. Smt. Khandagale . She has stated that the accused has committed severe offence. He has committed rape on his own daughter and if he is allowed to go he may commit similar offence in future also. Now suddenly she cannot state that whatever she has stated was out of frustration. She being a house wife she does not work in any way. She is depending on the accused 25 Spl.Case No.68/16 for living. She has come out with a truth now in Exh.43 dated 12­9­18 and as the real problem with which she is frustrated. The question before her as how would she take care of her three daughters and a son if he is in jail? If he is in jail they will have to permanently reside at her father's house. She has stated in court that her brother also is not supporting her, so her life would become miserable. She will have to suffer for the fault committed by her husband. This court holds that in such a situation on humanitarian ground, this court consider that he should be given benefit of sec.4 of the Probation of the Offenders Act. 42] Ld.A.P.P. Smt.Khandagale vehemently opposed this court view that benefit of Probation of offenders Act should be given to accused. She has argued vehemently that it is such a serious case. It cannot be given benefit in which imprisonment for life is prescribed. This court has gone through legal position taking into consideration several circumstances of the case which involve not only the accused but entire family and her parental house also. In order to save them from total disaster this court feels humanitarian approach. This court holds that sec.6 of the POCSO Act is dealing with punishment for aggravated penetrative sexual assault which punishes accused with rigorous imprisonment term which was not less than 10 years but which may extend to imprisonment for life. He is also be liable to fine. This court has taken lenient view and granted R.I.for 10 years. I hold that evidence of prosecution's witnesses is not sufficient to inspire confidence. It is transpired while cross­examination that she got disputed compromised with accused/husband. I hold that prosecution's evidence is not sufficient to bring accused to the home of guilt. I have answered point no.1,2,3 in negative. I proceed to pass following order ­ ORDER 1} Accused Bharat Mithailal Gupta is acquitted under section 235(1) of Cr.P.C. of charge for offences punishable under section 354, 504 506 of Indian Penal Code and section 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 2} Bail bonds of accused stand cancelled. Sureties are discharged. 3} In view of mandate laid down in section 437A of Cr.P.C., accused is directed to execute P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­. He shall undertake to appear before appellate court on receipt of notice of appeal. Date : 08.02.2018 ( M. P. Divate ) Additional Sessions Judge­1, Vasai.
