Special Case No. 74/2016 Judgment Accused stands trial for the offence punishable under section 363, 376 of Indian Penal Code and section 4 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act ( in short P.O.C.S.O. Act ). 2] Prosecution's case in brief is as under ­ That complainant Vasanti Kini is residing with her husband and children. Victim­girl is her daughter. Victim­girl is 17 years old. She was learning in B.A. On 07.06.2016 victim left house under guise to go to college and did not return. Complainant attempted to contact at the mobile phone of victim and accused. Their mobile phones were switched off. Complainant suspected that accused kidnapped her daughter. She filed complaint Exhibit 31. 3] Victim­girl and accused appeared before police at Palghar police station on 05.70.2016. They have produced marriage certificate. Police have completed investigation and filed charge­sheet against accused. 4] Charge under section 363, 376 of Indian Penal Code and section 4 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act and explained to him in Marathi. He did not plead guilty and claimed to be tried. His defence is of total denial. 5] After going through the evidence of prosecution witnesses and police papers, following points arise for my determination. I have recorded my findings against each of them for the reasons given below. Points Findings 1. Whether prosecution has proved that on 07.06.2016 from Vasai, accused has kidnapped .. 3 .. Special Case No. 74/2016 Judgment victim­girl aged 17 yeas out of lawful In the guardianship of her parents ? negative. 2. Whether prosecution has proved that in between period from 07.06.2016 till 27.06.2016 at village Khetsarai in Uttar Pradesh State, accused has committed rape / penetrative In the sexual assault on victim­girl ? negative. 3. What order and sentence, if any ? Accused is acquitted. REASONS As regards point no.1 and 2­ 6] Heard learned A.P.P. and learned advocate for accused. Complainant P.W.2 Vasant Kini deposed that her daughter,victim­girl, is 17 years old. Her daughter went to college on 07.06.2016 and did not return back. She attempted to contact with daughter and accused but their mobile phones were switched off. She suspected that accused has kidnapped her daughter. She filed complaint Exhibit 31. Later on she came to know that on 04.07.2016 accused and victim got married. Accused sent her photograph of marriage on 05 th July, 2016. Accused and victim were present at police station Palghar. She was called there. Victim was referred for medical examination. 7] Prosecution has examined victim­girl p.W.1 at Exhibit 29. Victim deposed that her birth date is 27.06.1998. She is learning in F.Y.B.A. at Vasai. On 07.06.2016 she was going to the house of maternal uncle. Jayesh telephoned her brother and informed that she is roaming with accused. Brother telephoned her and suggested to go back to home. She was frightened. She told brother that she will not go at home. She went with accused at Goregaon and then to Khetsarai in Uttar Pradesh. She has further deposed that she is having love affairs with accused. Her parents were having knowledge about it. .. 4 .. Special Case No. 74/2016 Judgment Parents have opposed for her marriage with accused because accused belongs to other caste. She herself and accused have decided to marry. She did not complete age of 18 years on 07.06.2016. They have decided to marry after completion of age of 18 years. They decided to go to another place for twenty days and then come back to perform marriage. She got married with accused on 07.06.2016. Accused did not have intercourse with her before marriage. They went at police station Palghar on 05th July, 2016. She narrated above facts to police. 8] Evidence of complainant appears to be formal in nature. Evidence of complainant makes it clear that victim and accused were having love affairs. It is transpired from the evidence of complainant that she herself and her family members have strongly opposed love affairs of victim with accused. Brother assaulted victim on that count. Evidence of complainant makes it clear that victim has left house voluntarily. 9] It is crystal clear from evidence of victim­girl that she was 17 years 11 months 3 days' old on alleged day of incident. It is crystal clear from the evidence of victim­girl that on that day she was going at the house of maternal uncle. At that time she received telephone call from her brother. Brother suggested her to go back at home. She was frightened. She refused to go back at home. She has left the house. Evidence of complainant makes it clear that she was at the verge of attaining majority after 23 days of the incident. She has left the house of parents of her own accord. I do not find any element of kidnapping of victim by the accused. .. 5 .. Special Case No. 74/2016 Judgment 10] Victim has specifically deposed that she has not completed age of 18 years on the day of alleged incident. Therefore, she herself and accused have decided to marry after attaining majority. She has attained majority. She and accused got married on 04th July, 2016. Both they appeared before police on 05th July, 2016 at Palghar police station. Victim specifically deposed that accused did not have intercourse with her before marriage. Evidence of victim makes it clear that she got married with accused after attaining majority and then after she has consummated marriage with accused. This does not appear to be an offence under section 4 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and section 376 of I.P.C. 11] There is no dispute about the fact that birth date of victim is 27.06.1998. There is no dispute about the fact that victim has attained majority on 26.06.2016. 12] Accused has not disputed the circumstance of spot inspection and medical examination of victim. I have carefully considered evidence of victim and her mother. Prima facie it appears that victim was intending to marry with accused. Her parents have strongly opposed her. Victim has left house on her own accord. There is no sufficient evidence on record to prove guilt of accused beyond all the reasonable doubt. Prosecution miserably fails to establish the guilt of accused. I have answered point no.1 and 2 in the negative. As regards point no.3 ­ 13] In view of my findings to point no.1, I have taken into consideration the facts and circumstances of the present case. I hold that evidence on record is not sufficient to bring home guilt of accused .. 6 .. Special Case No. 74/2016 Judgment beyond all the reasonable doubt. I have answered point no.3 accordingly. I proceed to pass following order ­ ORDER Accused Arunkumar Rameshwar Prasad is acquitted under section 235(1) of Cr.P.C. of charge for offence punishable under section 363, 376 of Indian Penal Code and section 4 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. Bail bonds of accused are cancelled and sureties are discharged. In view of mandate laid down in section 437A of Cr.P.C., accused is directed to execute P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­. He shall undertake to appear before appellate court on receipt of notice of appeal. Date : 04.10.2017 ( M. P. Divate ) Additional Sessions Judge­1, Vasai.

/ 1 / Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.79/2016. CNR No.MHTH23­001806­2016. Received on : 25/11/2016 Registered on : 25/11/2016 Decided on : 23/01/2019 Duration : 29 01 02 D M Y IN THE COURT OF THE ADDITIONAL SESSIONS JUDGE­2, VASAI. ( Presided over by Rahul R. Bhosale ) POCSO Special Case No. 79 of 2016. CNR NO. MHTH23­001806­2017 Exhibit No. 61. The State of Maharashtra .... Complainant. (through Manikpur Police Station) versus Prem alias Mantu Dhirendra Dalpati .... Accused. Age 25 years, Resident of Vasai, Native Place­ Gram Dharampur, Pol. Stn. Bangaon, Dist­North 24 Paragana, West Bengal. Learned Advocates : Mr.J.P.Patil A.P.P. for State. Mr. Sharada Patil for accused. JUDGMENT (Delivered on this 23rd day of January , 2019. ) 1] Accused is facing trial for crime punishable under Section 6 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (POCSO Act) and sections – 323, 342,363, 376, 392, 504 and 506 of Indian Penal Code 1860 (IPC). / 2 / Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.79/2016. CNR No.MHTH23­001806­2016. 2] Brief facts of the prosecution case are as under: The child was 14.7 year old when that incident was held on 07/08/2016 at about 08:30p.m. She was residing with her parents and maternal aunt in a building. She went for purchasing file required for completing school project of her 10th standard academic year. After purchasing the file, she was on the way to return to her building, when the accused approached her. He asked her about her ability to read the name plates in English language of the flats situated in a nearby Jui Building as he told to find out a flat of his sister. He took her on the 3 rd floor of Jui Building and told her to stay at terrace of the building, because the drunken persons residing on that floor would harass her. The child went at Terrace, but its door was closed. As the child was reluctant to stay there, accused threatened her on the point of razor blade and he told her to remove the apparels by threatening her to kill. He kissed her cheek and touched in­properly all over the body. He later on, forcefully removed her jeans pant and knicker upto the knees and also stripped down his apparels and hugged her. He tried to insert his penis into her vagina, but as noise was heard from down stairs hence by taking her mobile, the accused left that spot. The frightened child hesitantly came down and told that incident to her mother who later on, filed report to the police. 3] After investigation, the charge­sheet was filed in this court against the accused. A charge for offences punishable under sections­ 323, 342,363, 376, 392, 504 and 506 of Indian Penal Code 1860 and S.4 of the POCSO Act, 2012 was framed against accused, to which he has denied and claimed to be tried. / 3 / Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.79/2016. CNR No.MHTH23­001806­2016. 4) The prosecution has examined ABC (Child) (P.W.1) Ext. No.9, Santosh (spot pancha) (P.W.2) Ext. No.10, Dr. Balaji (P.W.3) Ext. No.12, XYZ(mother) (P.W.4) Ext. No.17, Bindu (P.W.5) Ext. No.20, Sanket (Pancha) (P.W.6) Ext. No.22, Santosh(P.W.7) Ext. No. 24, Rahul (P.W.8) Ext. No.25, Jitendra (Pancha) (P.W.9) Ext. No.27, Sarjerao­(I.O.) (P.W.10) Ext. No.32, Anil (I.O.) (P.W.11) Ext. No.37 and Dr. Maruti (P.W.12) Ext. No.53. The prosecution has thereafter, filed pursis Ext.58 for closing evidence. The statement of accused has been recorded u/s. 313 of Cr. P.C. Ext. No.59. Accused has raised the defence of total denial and false implication and has not examined any defence witnesses. 5] On the basis of the material on record, the points arise for my determination are answered for the reasons as under ­ Points Findings 1. Whether the prosecution has proved that the .. Proved victim was a 'Child' on the day of incident as provided under S.2(d) of POCSO Act ? 2. Whether the prosecution has proved that the .. Proved accused kidnapped a minor victim girl from lawful guardianship of her parents ? 3. Whether the prosecution has proved that the .. Proved accused, after kidnapping the Child wrongfully confined her ? 4. Whether the prosecution has proved that .. Proved. accused committed rape/penetrative sexual assault on the Child ? 5. Whether the prosecution has proved that .. Proved accused committed robbery of mobile handset which was the property Child? / 4 / Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.79/2016. CNR No.MHTH23­001806­2016. 6. Whether the prosecution proves that accused .. Proved voluntarily caused hurt to the Child by slapping her ? 7. Whether the prosecution proves that accused .. Not Proved gave provocation to child girl with intention that such provocation would cause her to break public peace ? 8. Whether the prosecution proves that accused .. Proved committed criminal intimidation by threatening the child with intent to cause alarm ? 9. What is the order ? .. As per final order. REASONS 6] Point No.1 ­ Materially, the offence under S.5 punishable u/s.6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act 2012 (for short, POCSO Act) has been charged against the accused. Hence in view of the scope and object of that Act, let us first scrutinize that whether the victim was below age of 18 years, termed as a 'Child' as provided U/S.2(d) of POCSO Act. The document is produced at Ext. No.36 which is the verified true copy of the birth certificate of Child. It is admissible in evidence under Ss.74 & 79 of Evidence Act 1872 r/w S.17 of the Registration of Birth and Deaths Act 1969. It discloses the birth date of Child is 13/12/2001. The informant, the mother of Child has corroborated that date of birth in her testimony Ext.17 before the Court. Nothing is found to disbelieve that entire evidence. Thus the prosecution has succeeded to prove the Child's birth date is 13/12/2001 while the alleged sexual abuse of the Child was held on 07/8/2016. It concludes that the Child was exactly 11 / 5 / Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.79/2016. CNR No.MHTH23­001806­2016. years 7 months & 25 days old when the alleged incident was held. Thus, the present victim is covered by the term ' Child ' as per S.2(d) therefore, the provisions of POCSO Act are applicable to the present prosecution case. I therefore, answer the point no.1 in the affirmative. 7] Point No. 4 : The prosecution has materially tried to prove penetrative sexual assault on the child and while advancing argument, A.P.P. Mr. Jayprakash Patil has relied upon the presumption under S. 29 of the POCSO Act for presuming that the accused committed the instant crime. In counter Adv. Mrs. Sharda Patil for the accused has argued that firstly the prosecution has to prove the case beyond reasonable doubts. 8] Honourable Bombay High Court in the case of Ramprasad Vs. State of Maharashtra, 2018(3)RCR(criminal)656 has laid down the ruling for application of the statutory presumptions under Ss.29 & 30 of the POCSO Act. In that decision the judgment of Honourable Apex Court in the case of Babu V./s. State of Kerala, (2010) 9 SCC 189, has been relied upon for mode of application of the statutory presumption as every accused is presumed to be innocent, which is a human right. However, subject to the statutory exceptions, for which the nature of offence, its seriousness and gravity has to be taken into consideration. Mere application of the presumption should not lead to any injustice or mistaken conviction. The various statutory presumptions for guilt of the accused would shift burden of proof of innocence on the accused. However, Honourable Apex Court concludes such presumption should be raised only when certain 'foundational facts' are established by the prosecution. Therefore, Honourable Bombay High Court (supra) has concluded that the presumption under Section 29 of the POCSO Act is not / 6 / Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.79/2016. CNR No.MHTH23­001806­2016. absolute and it is triggered only when the prosecution is able to prove 'the foundational facts' in first place. It has further held that the evidence placed on record by the prosecution is to be examined to first come to the conclusion that the 'foundational facts' of the prosecution case have been established and thereafter only the accused can rebut the presumption either by discrediting the prosecution witnesses by effective cross­ examination or by leading defence evidence. 9] Before proceeding further to ascertain the ' foundational facts ' it is material to note the accusation found in the prosecution case is about the accused committed ‘ penetrative sexual assault ’ on the child which would attract the section­3 of the POCSO Act as under : Section­3 – Penetrative sexual assault ­ A person is said to commit “penetrative sexual assault” if : (a) he penetrates his penis, to any extent, into the vagina, mouth, urethra or anus of a child or makes the child to do so with him or any other person; or (b) he inserts, to any extent, any object or a part of the body, not being the penis, into the vagina, the urethra or anus of the child or makes the child to do so with him or any other person; or (c) he manipulates any part of the body of the child so as to cause penetration into the vagina, urethra, anus or any part of body of the child or makes the child to do so with him or any other persons; or (d) he applied his mouth to the penis, vagina, anus urethra of the child or makes the child to do so to such person or any other person. / 7 / Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.79/2016. CNR No.MHTH23­001806­2016. The evidence of prosecution is to be scrutinized in the light of this provision. 10] The sole eye witness is the child herself who faced that incident has deposed at Exh.9. By deposing her joint residence with her parents at the relevant time of incident, she further deposes that accused intercepted her way when she was returning to the house after purchasing a file from stationary shop at around 8.00 p.m. on 7/8/2016. Accused after confirming her ability to read English language, requested her to read the name plates of the flats situated in Jui Building to find out the house of his sister on third floor. She further deposes that after they approached 3rd floor of building the accused made action of ringing a door bell of one of the flats and told the child to go upstairs at terrace as many drunken persons who were residing there, would harass her. She further deposes that accused told her to wait upstairs while he would come alongwith the name plate and sister. But observing her reluctance, he threatened her on the point of razor blade. As per her further deposition, the door of terrace was closed, hence she was returning, but the accused told her to lay down. He also slapped her when she attempted to make contact with her father on her mobile phone, and by threatening to kill her, he compelled her to remove her jeans pant. She further deposes that accused forcibly stripped down her knicker when she resisted and by removing her pant partially, he penetrated his penis into her vagina. With this deposition, child supports the prosecution case for attracting the definition of penetrative sexual assault as provided under clause 'a' of section 3 of POCSO Act. 11] Her cross­examination was conducted materially on the defence of total denial by trying to bring on record some trifle omissions / 8 / Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.79/2016. CNR No.MHTH23­001806­2016. and improvements. However, the child has not admitted anything adverse to her deposition which makes the prosecution case reliable. The accused by taking disadvantage of vulnerable age of Child who would easily fell prey to the accused out of inbuilt enthusiasm at that age of the child and committed the said incriminating act. After relieving, the child immediately conveyed that incident to her mother­informant–XYZ (P.W.4). She has deposed at Exh.17 materially to support the incident immediately narrated to her by the child as she has deposed before the Court. It is material to note that though she was cross­examined by accused yet nothing is found either adverse to her deposition or any cooked up story against accused disclosing any sort of interestedness. This witness thus, supports the prosecution to reveal truth on the basis of natural events held immediately after the child faced that incident. 12] Informant–XYZ (P.W.4) has also brought on record that during the occurrence of that incident, the child made a phone call to her father, but she was unable to convey except crying under fear. The Child has also deposed that she tried to contact her father during that incident by making a phone call. Thus, the mother of Child deposes a truth. Her further statement about her husband tried to recall the child. But as deposed by the child earlier that her mobile phone was directed to be switched off by the accused caused her to keep aide that mobile phone hence the contact was not established. Thus, I do not find anything doubtful about the deposition of the child and her mother in support of the prosecution case. The prosecution has thus, succeeded to prove trust­ worthy case against accused. Nothing abnormal found in entire conduct of Child since inception of incident to conclude that she might have tutored. She deposes about partial insertion of penis into her vagina by / 9 / Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.79/2016. CNR No.MHTH23­001806­2016. accused which certainly attracts definition of penetrative sexual assault as per clause 'a' of S.3 of POCSO Act (Supra). 13] The Child thus deposes as rape surviver. As relied upon by prosecution the law relating to scrutiny of the rape surviver has been long back laid down by the Honourable Apex Court in the case of State of Punjab Vs. Gurmit Singh, AIR 1996 (SC) 1393. It has been held that a murderer destroys the physical body of the victim, a rapist degrades the very soul of the helpless female. The courts therefore, shoulder a great responsibility while trying accused on charges of rape. They must deal such cases with utmost sensitivity by examining broader probabilities of a case and not get swayed by minor contradictions or insignificant discrepancies in statement of victim. If evidence of prosecutrix inspires confidence, it must be relied upon without seeking corroboration of her statement in material particulars. The testimony of the prosecutrix must be appreciated in background of entire case and the trial court must be alive to its responsibility and be sensitive while dealing with cases involving sexual molestations. 14] The Child's sole deposition, as per decision (supra), if qualifies certain tests led down then it would be accepted as it is. This rulling is consistently followed in subsequent decisions by Honourable Apex Court as can be also evidence in case of Vijay Vs. State of M.P., 2010(8) SCC 191 as relied upon by APP. But Honourable Apex Court, in case of Baby Kandayanathil Vs. State of Kerala, AIR 1992 (4) SCC 225, has held that evidence of Child witness must find adequate corroboration before it is relied upon such rule is a particular wisdom than of law. However, it is not the law that if the witness is Child his evidence shall be rejected even if it is found reliable. The law is that evidence of a Child / 10 / Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.79/2016. CNR No.MHTH23­001806­2016. witness must be evaluated carefully and with greater circumspection because a Child is susceptible to be swayed by what others tell and Child witness is an easy prey to tutoring by others. It evidence of Child is not of a quality to place reliance, it is expected that the court to search for corroboration from some evidence which could give credence to the testimony of a Child witness. In the present case the Child is herself a rape surviver hence the laws led supra by Honourable Apex Court should be applied simultaneously to the Child's deposition. Hence, the corroborative evidence is also required to be scrutinized. 15] Dr. Balaji (P.W.3) has deposed to prove his medical examination certificate at Ext.14 revealing that accused was competent to maintain intercourse. Medical certificate­Ext.14 supports specifically that the accused was capable to do intercourse. His cross­examination is only of denials which has not attracted any doubt to his evidence. It concludes that accused was potent at the time of that incident. 16] Santosh (P.W.2) is the panch who has proved the spot panchnama at Exh.11 by his deposition at Ext.10. The situation of the spot as he has brought on record, the same has been deposed by the child. The passage in front of the terrace door reveals the panchanama is found sufficient to uphold the evidence of the child that she was compelled to lay down on the ground at the spot by the accused. That passage is situated at secluded place in the Jui Building which d given required privacy for commission of the alleged offence. 17] Bindu(P.W.5) is a social worker who as per her deposition at Ext.20, was present when the child narrated happening of that incident to / 11 / Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.79/2016. CNR No.MHTH23­001806­2016. the woman police officer at police station. Her cross­examination was conducted by doubting her such attendance, but it has not earned anything as her attendance is proved in the light of her signature she made while child reported that incident to the police. Thus, Bindu (PW­ 5) not only corroborates the presence of child and her mother while reporting that incident, but genuineness of the prosecution case which is carried out on record by the other witnesses also. 18] Sanket (P.W.6) is the witness on the accused's disclosure statement and memorandum panchnama respectively at Ext.23 and 24. He has proved the same in the light of his deposition at Ext.22 by stating specifically about the disclosure statement was made in his presence by the accused on 01/09/2016 when accused was in the police custody during the investigation. S.27 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 makes this statement of the accused as exception to his confession under sections 24 and 26 of the Evidence Act 1872. The accused thus stated police that he would show the shop from which he collected the offending weapon­the half part of razor blade. In the light of said disclosure statement , as per further deposition of Sanket (P.W.6), he alongwith the accused and police squad reached to the said shop as per the direction of accused himself. His said evidence reveals that said shop was a hair cutting saloon where the accused pointed out the box of used blades was kept. Therefore, said disclosure statement couples the chain of event held preceding to the occurrence of the incident. In his cross­examination again except all denials, no material is found to attract doubt. Thus, in view of Sec.27 of the Indian Evidence Act, the disclosure of the 'facts' made by the accused about his knowledge of situation of the said shop from which the collected offending weapon is established. It certainly / 12 / Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.79/2016. CNR No.MHTH23­001806­2016. couples him to the incident as per prosecution case as it has already proved by Child that the accused committed penetrative sexual assault under the point of razor blade . 19] It is also material to note that Pancha­Jitendra(P.W.9) has proved the another seizure panchnama at Exh.28 disclosing seizure of razor blade from the wallet in custody of accused when he was arrested in his presence. He has also identified it before the Court which is at article 'A'. His deposition at Exh.27 also reveals that apparels of accused were seized in his presence which he has identified as articles “B to D”. This entire evidence would attract reliability, to prosecution case concluding that the disclosure statement and seizure of the offending weapon is reliable. It concludes independently that the accused was equipped with razor at the time of said incident. This evidence certainly corroborates the case of the prosecution that the child was threatened by the accused on the point of the razor blade for surrendering her to his atrocities. The deposition of child has already revealed said case is true as by use of that razor blade the accused made succumbing the child to his whims. There is no other inference to be drawn except upholding the deposition of the child regarding the said incident is the reliable evidence. Because said threats under the point of offending weapon, Article ­A is sufficient naturally compelling the child at said age to surrender herself to atrocities of the accused. 20] Further Sanket (P.W.6) has also brought on record in the light of the memorandum panchnama at Exh.24 the disclosure statement made by the accused about the situation of the spot of incident near the terrace door of the Jui Building. But that disclosure of spot is not admissible under section 27 of Indian Evidence Act, 1972, because said spot was / 13 / Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.79/2016. CNR No.MHTH23­001806­2016. already brought to the notice of investigation machinery by the informant in her FIR at Exh.19 earlier by narrating the said spot in detail. The investigating officer Sarjerao (PW­10) has deposed at Exh.32 that he initiated the Course of investigation after going through the content of FIR which was handed over to him earlier. Therefore, said spot of incident was within the knowledge of I.O. when the accused made disclosure statement to him about that spot later on as per Exh.23 and 24. Thus, the fact of finding out the spot of incident only through accused as per said disclosure statement is not admissible. However, the child, her mother and pancha in the light of spot panchnama have brought on record the reliable evidence about the said spot of the incident, hence that deformity in the investigation will not stumbling the prosecution case. 21] Santosh(P.W.7) is the former employer of accused who as per evidence at Exh.24 brings forth the earlier engagement of the accused in similar nature of activities. He deposes that accused during his service with him harassed the girls from nearby housing society which was informed to him by the concerned persons, hence he removed the accused from services. He has identified the accused in the Court as his former employee. I do not find any ground to disbelieve him in the light of his cross examination which has not earned any adverse material except his unability to produce on record the proof of employment of accused with him. But it is not found in his entire cross­examination any probable ground that he is lying about such employment, therefore, his evidence is admissible. However, the previous bad character of accused is not relevant in criminal proceeding as per S. 54 of the Evidence Act 1872. In the result, Sanotsh (P.W.7) corroborates only the prosecution case to the extent of identifying the accused as a culprit. / 14 / Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.79/2016. CNR No.MHTH23­001806­2016. 22] Rahul (P.W.8), Anil (P.W.11) and Dr. Maruti(P.W.12) respectively at Ext. 25, 37 and 53 have conducted the allotted works during the investigation and nothing is found adverse in their respective cross­examinations. Rahul (P.W.8) is a technician who copied CCTV footage regarding the presence of accused in the vicinity of the incident through the pen­drive to DVD. But the prosecution has not proved that electronic evidence by applying a proper mode of proof, hence his evidence has no bearing on the prosecution case. Anil (P.W.11) was the member of a police squad formed for searching accused, which later on nabbed the accused. To that extent, he supports the prosecution case. Lastly, Dr. Maruti (P.W.12) deposes at Exh.53 about he attended the child which was referred to him for conducting the medical examination and he also collected samples for chemical analysis as per the requisition of the police. But in his cross­examination he has admitted that he had not conducted the examination of genital of the child as consent was not given. The medical papers at Exh 55 and 56 disclose that parents as well as the child refused to undergo such examination. This evidence will not affect prosecution case against the accused because the accused tried to partially insert his penis in the vagina of the child, but immediately thereafter he left the spot as he heard the noise at down­stairs in Jui building. This act would certainly not leave behind any signs or traces of forceful penetrative sexual assault which can be reflected in the medical examination of the genitals. However, that much act of the accused as evident earlier has attracted the definition of penetrative sexual assault under section­3(1) of POCSO Act. 23] Lastly, the prosecution has examined I.O.­Sarjerao (P.W.10) at Exh.32 who has proved the course of investigation ending into / 15 / Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.79/2016. CNR No.MHTH23­001806­2016. concluding the involvement of the accused as alleged in the prosecution case. He has supported the investigation which he carried out as per his deposition at Ext.32 attracting the presumption under section 114(e) of the Indian Evidence Act about regularity in that work as a public officer regarding duties entrusted upon him. Accused has taken defence in his statement under section­313 of Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 that as he was drunken and scuffled with the persons near the spot of incident, hence he was roped in the incident. But that defence is even not found acceptable also because neither the presence of such person is found in the prosecution evidence nor any of the prosecution witnesses admitted even the probability as per the said defence. In the result nothing is found to either disbelieve the Child as per decisions (supra) or witnesses. It concludes that the foundational facts found in the prosecution case attracting presumption under S.29 & 30 of POCSO Act which are not rebutted by accused. Therefore, the prosecution has succeeded to prove the incriminating acts of the accused under section 3(a) of the POCSO Act. The evidence discloses that the accused committed penetrative sexual assault on the Child using the deadly weapon like razor blade while the Child was below 12 years when she faced that sexual abuse. It attracts the provisions of aggravated penetrative sexual assault as per S.5(h)&(m) attracting the punishment under S.6 of the POCSO Act. That evidence also proves the offence of rape under S.375 (a)(6) attracting the punishment under S.376 (2)(i) of IPC 1860. Hence, I answer point No.4 in the Affirmative. 24] Point Nos. 2 and 3. The kidnapping, as alleged in the prosecution case, of the child by the accused is to be proved under section 361 of IPC, 1860 . It is / 16 / Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.79/2016. CNR No.MHTH23­001806­2016. evident that under the false cause, the accused by taking benefit of minority of the child firstly enticed and then compelled her to come at the spot. This act of the accused certainly attracts the definition of kidnapping u/s.361 of IPC, 1860 as accused enticed the minor to come at the spot which invites punishing S. 363 of IPC 1860. The prosecution evidence, particularly, the depositions of minor child and her mother reveals that the child was confined by the accused at the passage of terrace door of Jui building under the point of razor blade with threatening to kill. It is an offence of wrongful confinement under section 340 of IPC which attracts the punishment u/s.342 of IPC. Thus, I answer point no.2 and 3 in the affirmative. 25] Point Nos.5 to 8 : The accusations in the prosecution case about accused robbed mobile phone of child is sustainable. It is already evident that the child possessed the mobile phone during the occurrence of that incident. She tried to make contact with her father and again she was recalled during that time by her father which is convincingly brought on record in the light of evidence of child’s mother. Though, the purchase proof of that mobile phone of the child is not brought on record yet I do not find any ground to disbelieve the evidence of the child and her mother on the fact of possessing the said mobile phone by the child. Therefore accused's taking away that mobile phone by threatening to kill her attract the act of extortion resulting into robbery as defined section 390 of IPC, 1860 attracting the punishment under section 392 of IPC 1860. 26] The child was slapped repeatedly by the accused as evident from her deposition ­ Exh.9 is reliable evidence which attracts section 319 / 17 / Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.79/2016. CNR No.MHTH23­001806­2016. for concluding that the accused caused hurt to the child. It brings forth offence punishable under section 323 of IPC. The accused threatened to kill the Child under point of razor blade as evident from her deposition attracts definition of Criminal intimidation under S. 503 of IPC coupled with punishment under S. 504 of IPC. However, there is convincing proof in the prosecution evidence about commission of the crime by the accused under section 506 of IPC hence, prosecution has not succeeded to prove it. In the result I answer point nos.5 & 8 in the affirmative and point no.7 in the Negative. 27] Point No. 9 : The prosecution has thus succeeded to prove that the accused committed the offences : (i) u/s.359 punishable u/s. 363 of IPC 1860, (ii) u/s.340 punishable u/s. 342 of IPC 1860, (iii) u/s.375 (a) punishable u/s.376 (2)(i) of IPC 1860, (iv) u/s.5(h)&(m) punishable u/s. 6 of the POCSO Act 2012, (v) u/s. 390 punishable u/s. 392 of IPC 1860, (vi) u/s. 319 punishable u/s. 323 of IPC 1860, (vii) u/s. 503 punishable u/s. 506 of IPC 1860. But the prosecution has not succeeded to prove the guilt of accused punishable u/s.504 of IPC 1860. However, before proceeding for sentencing the accused I will give the opportunity to him for making submission on the point of sentencing as required under S.235 (2) of Cr.P.C 1973. 28] Today, in presence of the accused, his counsel Mrs. Sharda Patil has argued that the accused is the only earning member of the family upon whom the minor children are dependent hence, she lastly / 18 / Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.79/2016. CNR No.MHTH23­001806­2016. submits to take a lenient view while sentencing the accused. In counter APP Mr. Jayprakash Patil has submitted that the accused committed heinous and gruesome serious crime against a minor making his relationship with the Child immoral and unethical hence the maximum sentence may be inflicted. 29] As evident earlier, the accused is found involved in the crime which he pre­planned by considering all probable issues to be dealt with. Thus, the act committed by the accused not only discloses his gross inculpability but the hardened criminal activity is evident also. Due to such assaults the accused caused not only the crime against the body of the Child but he also affected grossly to the emotional quotient of the Child making her paralyzed in the emotional bonding with the persons of opposite sex. The agony of a girl to face such heinous crime in her adolescent age would change entirely the pattern of her life. This offence is also committed against the society of which the element like the Child should be mentally and physically healthy and sound constituent. Therefore the proportionate sentence has to be passed. 30] The guilt of accused is proved punishable under S.376(2)(i) of IPC 1860 and under S.6 of the POCSO Act, they both coupled with punishment for not less than 10 years alongwith fine. S.42 of the POCSO Act 2012 provides the alternate punishment in this situation is to be passed which is greater in degree. I therefore prefer to pass sentence under S.6 of the POCSO Act for rigorous imprisonment of 20 years alongwith fine of Rs.15,000/­ (Rupees Fifteen Thousand Only). It covers the offence u/s.3 punishable u/s.4 of POCSO Act committed in the continuing final offene. Hence I will not sentence the accused separately u/s.4 of POCSO Act. Further, the accused is sentenced u/s. 363 of IPC / 19 / Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.79/2016. CNR No.MHTH23­001806­2016. 1860 for 7 years rigorous imprisonment and fine of Rs.5000/­ (Rupees Five Thousand Only) ; u/s. 342 of IPC 1860 for 1 years rigorous imprisonment and fine of Rs.1000/­ (Rupees One Thousand Only) ; u/s. 392 of IPC 1860 for 5 years rigorous imprisonment and fine of Rs.1500/­ (Rupees One Thousand Five Hundred Only) ; u/s. 323 of IPC for 1 years rigorous imprisonment and fine of Rs.1000/­ (Rupees One Thousand Only) & u/s. 506 of IPC 1860 for 2 years rigorous imprisonment and fine of Rs.1500/­ (Rupees One Thousand Five Hundred Only) 31] Honourable Apex Court in the case of Ms. Era through Manjula Vs. Government of NCT of Delhi, Cri. Appeal No.12171219/2017, dated 21/07/2017 has held that in such kind of sentence the proper care is to be taken for neutralizing the impact upon the Child by providing various medical as well as psychological assistance. It is made possible only if the comprehensive compensation is granted. The cardinal principle in such cases is the re­formative and beneficial arrangement to be made for the victim of the sexual abuse. S.357­A of Cr.P.C 1973 r/w R.7 of POCSO Rules 2012, mandate such compensation is to be arranged by DLSA. Therefore, I answer point no. in the affirmative and pass the order as under : ORDER 1] The accused Prem alias Mantu Dhirendra Dalpati is convicted under Section 235(2) of Cr.P.C 1973 for : (i) the offence under S.5(h)&(m) punishable u/s. 6 of the POCSO Act for rigorous imprisonment of 20 years alongwith fine of Rs.15,000/­ (Rupees Fifteen Thousand Only); in default of payment of fine, accused shall undergo further the simple imprisonment for six months. (iii) the offence under S. 340 punishable u/s. 342 of IPC 1860 for 1 years rigorous imprisonment and fine of Rs.1000/­ (Rupees One Thousand Only); in default of payment of fine, accused shall undergo further the simple imprisonment for one month. Special Case No.81/2016 Judgment Presented on : 25.11.2016 Registered on : 25.11.2016 Decided on : 01.04.2017 Duration : 4 months 6 days In The Court of the Additional Sessions Judge-1, Vasai At Vasai (Presided over by S. J. Bharuka) Special Case No. 81 of 2016 Exhibit No. 25 The State of Maharashtra, (through Arnala police station C.R.No.I-6/2016) ... Complainant versus Karan Rama Thakre, Age 21 years, Occupation – labour work Residence – Dhobitalav Agashi, Virar (W), Taluka Vasai ... Accused Appearance - Smt. U.P.Moholkar, learned A.P.P. for State. Mr. Prashant Dalvi, learned advocate for accused. JUDGMENT (Delivered on 01.04.2017.) .. 2 .. Special Case No.81/2016 Judgment 1] Accused is charge-sheeted for offences punishable under section 376(2)(i)(n) of the Indian Penal Code and section 4, 6 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act (hereinafter in short ''P.O.C.S.O. Act''). 2] All the safeguards have been followed as per the directions of the Hon'ble High Court and Supreme Court and proceedings have been conducted In Camera. Keeping in view social object of preventing social victimisation of the victim of sexual offence for which section 228A of I.P.C. has been enacted, I have chosen to describe her as 'victim' in the present judgment . 3] The prosecution case in brief is that at the relevant time victim was staying at Dhobitalav, Agashi with her mother and brothers. She was studying in 9th standard at that time. Accused Karan was staying in her neighbourhood. Both were knowing each other and were having love affair. It is further case of prosecution that in year 2015 accused Karan assured victim that he would marry her and thereafter they underwent sexual intercourse more than once with each other. Thereafter, when her menarche was missed, her mother took her to corporation hospital where doctor found her to be pregnant of two months. Matter was reported to police. Police inquired with the victim in the hospital itself and recorded her complaint. 4] On the basis of said complaint, offences punishable under section 376 of I.P.C. and section 4, 6 of P.O.C.S.O. Act came to be registered vide C.R.No.I-6/2016 at Arnala Police Station. During investigation spot panchnama was prepared. Sketch of the spot was got prepared from Circle Officer. .. 3 .. Special Case No.81/2016 Judgment Accused was arrested under panchnama. Victim and accused were referred for medical examination. Statements of witnesses were recorded. School leaving certificate showing date of birth of victim was collected. After completion of investigation, since sufficient evidence was found against the accused, charge-sheet came to be filed against him for offences punishable under section 376 of I.P.C. and section 4, 6 of P.O.C.S.O. Act before this Court directly, being Designated Court to try offence under P.O.C.S.O. Act. 5] A charge for offences punishable under section 376(2)(i)(n) of I.P.C. and section 4, 6 of P.O.C.S.O. Act was framed against the accused as per Exhibit 7 and its contents were read over and explained to him in vernacular. Accused denied the charges and claimed to be tried. After examination of prosecution witnesses, no incriminating evidence was found against accused person. Hence, his statement under section 313 of Cr.P.C. was dispensed with. Accused put forth defence of total denial and false implication. 6] I heard the learned A.P.P. and the learned counsel for the accused. Considering the facts of the prosecution case and submissions of both side, following points arise for my determination and I have recorded findings thereon for the reasons recorded below - POINTS FINDINGS 1. Whether prosecution has proved that the victim-girl was 'child' as defined under P.O.C.S.O Act at the time of sexual assault ? No. 2. Whether prosecution has proved that since year 2015 till 12.01.2016 in her house at Agashi, Virar (W), accused committed rape on victim-girl aged about 15 years by doing .. 4 .. Special Case No.81/2016 Judgment forcible sexual intercourse with her more than once under false assurance of Not proved. marriage ? 3. Whether prosecution has proved that on the given date, time and place, accused committed penetrative sexual assault on the victim-girl by doing forceful sexual Not proved. intercourse with her ? 4. Whether prosecution has proved that on the given date, time and place, accused committed aggravated penetrative sexual assault on victim-girl by committing forceful sexual intercourse with her more Not proved. than once ? 5. What order ? Accused is acquitted. REASONS 7] In order to establish its case, prosecution has examined only three witnesses namely victim-girl (P.W.1), her mother Ladki Pachalkar (P.W.2) and I.O. P.S.I. Annapurna Shamrao Mhaske (P.W.3). 8] I have heard the rival contentions of the A.P.P. and counsel for accused and given thoughtful consideration to the arguments advanced by them and have also perused the evidence as well as the exhibited documents carefully. It is a case of rape and hence, I have taken as much care as possible to evaluate and appreciate the evidence come on record. Bearing in mind submissions made by both the counsels and ingredients of alleged sections, now I proceed to discuss and appreciate the evidence led by the prosecution. .. 5 .. Special Case No.81/2016 Judgment As to point no.1 - 9] Besides the penal act under Indian Penal Code, accused is facing charge of committing sexual assault on victim- girl more than once, who was allegedly 'child' as per P.O.C.S.O. Act at the relevant time. Therefore, the prosecution is bound to first establish that the victim-girl was 'child' aged below eighteen years as per P.O.C.S.O. Act. In this connection the prosecution has produced on record a certificate issued by the school in which victim-girl was studying. Said certificate shows that her date of birth is 15.03.2001. Though this certificate has not been proved by the prosecution by examining relevant witness, for just appreciation of the evidence, if properly calculated, the age of the victim at the time of sexual assault comes to 15 years. But, on the other hand, victim-girl P.W.1 and her mother P.W.2 have deposed that real date of birth of the victim is 21.05.1997, which is wrongly mentioned as 15.03.2001 in the school certificate and in the complaint at Exhibit 12. Therefore, in such circumstance on the basis of the date of birth stated by victim-girl and her mother i.e. 21.05.1997, she appears to be not aged below eighteen years at the time of sexual assault. Thus, the prosecution has failed to prove this issue and therefore, point no.1 is answered in the negative. As to point no.2 to 4 - 10] P.W.1 victim-girl has deposed in examination-in-chief that in year 2016 she was staying at Agashi alongwith her mother and accused was also living in same locality and they both were in love with each other. She has further deposed that accused assured her that he would marry her and then they both had sexual intercourse with each other and she has .. 6 .. Special Case No.81/2016 Judgment delivered a female child. At the same time P.W.1 has stated in cross-examination that she never had grievance against the accused and their physical relations before the marriage were consensual. She has further admitted that her complaint was not read over to her and therefore, she does not know its contents. She has further admitted that on 06.03.2016 accused has married to her and now both are living happy married life. 11] P.W.2 Ladki Pachalkar is mother of the victim-girl. She has also deposed in the same line like the victim-girl on the point of acquaintance and love affair between the victim-girl and the accused. In the cross-examination P.W.2 has stated that before the incidence in question victim-girl and accused were engaged by ceremony and subsequently they married to each other on 06.03.2016 and are living happy married life. She has further admitted that she did not have any complaint against the accused before the incidence and also does not have complaint against him now. 12] P.W.3 lady P.S.I. Annapurna Mhaske is the investigation officer and she has stated about the different steps taken in investigation of this crime including medical examination of victim, recording statements of witnesses and referring the samples for DNA analysis and filing of charge- sheet. The I.O. has also stated that accused and victim-girl have married to each other on 06.03.2016. 13] The gist of the oral evidence of victim-girl and her mother is that accused and victim were engaged by ceremony with each other and they kept physical relations by consent of each other and now accused has married with victim-girl and .. 7 .. Special Case No.81/2016 Judgment she has delivered a female child and they are leading happy married life. 14] It appears that this is not a case which has to be dealt with in a routine manner by applying the penal parameters. This case has base of consent for sex by each other and even going ahead, both have married to each other. Chief ingredients of offence of 'rape' are sexual intercourse 'against the will of woman' and 'without her consent'. Obviously and admittedly both the ingredients are absolutely absent in the present case. As per the version of P.W.1 and 2 victim was major at the time of alleged incidence. Hence, for want of fulfillment of these basic ingredients, the alleged misdeed at the hands of accused does not fall within the ambit of offence of 'penetrative sexual assault on child'. Moreover, it appears that both victim and accused are from Adivasi community and there is custom in their community to keep physical relationship without performing marriage and to perform marriage when both, bride and bridegroom, are minor. It is pertinent to note that on perusal of F.I.R. it appears that practically there is no grievance came to be made against the accused by the victim. 15] In this scenario there is no evidence on record to prove guilt of accused beyond reasonable doubt. Prosecution has utterly failed to prove the charges levelled against accused. Therefore, I answer point no.2 to 4 accordingly. In the result accused is entitled to be acquitted. Hence, I proceed to pass following order - ORDER Accused Karan Rama Thakre is acquitted as per section 235(1) of Cr.P.C. of charge for offences punishable under .. 8 .. Special Case No.81/2016 Judgment section 376(2)(i)(n) of the Indian Penal Code and section 4, 6 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 2) His bail bonds stand cancelled and sureties are discharged. 3) In compliance of provisions of section 437A of Cr.P.C. accused shall furnish P. B. of Rs.15,000/- [rupees fifteen thousand only]. 4) No muddemal property is shown in this case. Hence, no order regarding its disposal is passed. Date : 01.04.2017 ( S. J. Bharuka ) Additional Sessions Judge-1, Vasai

Complainant (through Tulinj police station C.R.No.I­619/2017) versus Rajendrakumar Hasmukhrai Mashru alias Vimal Thakkar, .. Accused Age 48 years, Residence – room no.302, Vasundhara building, Vijaynagar, Nalasopara(E) Native place – Anupam building, room no.301, Giriraj Society, in front of S.T.depot, Junagadh, Gujarat JUDGMENT (Delivered on 15th day of February, 2018) .. 2 .. Special Case No. 112/2017 Judgment CNR : MHTH23­001814­2017 Accused stands trial for the offence punishable under section 354, 509, 506 of Indian Penal Code and sec. 8, 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act ( in short P.O.C.S.O. Act ). 2] Prosecution's case in brief is as under ­ That victim is 14 years old. Accused is stepfather of the victim. Mother of victim­child girl remarried with accused. Accused and mother were suggesting victim to sleep in between them. Accused was purposely keeping his hand or leg on person of complainant. Complainant was under conception that this might have taken place due to oversight. On 24.10.2017 at 10.00 p.m. victim was sleeping in between father and mother. At about 11.30p.m. accused kept his leg on the person of complainant. Complainant strongly opposed accused. Accused raised hand to assault complainant. Accused abused complainant. He has purposely kept his hand at the chest of complainant and outraged her modesty. He abused and threatened complainant. He suggested complainant to sleep with him if she wants to have mobile. Complainant went at police station alongwith mother. She filed complaint Exhibit 16. 3] Police have taken cognizance and registered crime. Police have completed investigation and filed charge­sheet against accused. .. 3 .. Special Case No. 112/2017 Judgment CNR : MHTH23­001814­2017 4] Charge under section 354, 509, 506 of Indian Penal Code and section 8, 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act were framed at Exhibit 11. Contents of the charge were read over to accused and explained to him in vernacular. He did not plead guilty and claimed to be tried. His defence is that of total denial. 5] After going through the evidence of prosecution witnesses and police papers, following points arise for my determination. I have recorded my findings against each of them for the reasons given below. Points ­ 1} Whether prosecution has proved that on 24.10.2017 at about 12.00 to 12.30 p.m. at his residential house, accused has outraged modesty of victim girl/committed sexual assault on victim­child girl age 14 years ? 2} Whether prosecution has proved that accused intentionally insulted victim­child by abusing and thereby gave provocation to victim intending or knowing it to be likely that such provocation may cause her to break public peace ? 3} Whether prosecution has proved that on the same date, time and place, accused has committed criminal intimidation by threatening the complainant to kill with intention to use alarm ? 4} Whether prosecution has proved that accused has insulted modesty of the victim­child girl by uttering words ? 5} What order and sentence, if any ? .. 4 .. Special Case No. 112/2017 Judgment CNR : MHTH23­001814­2017 Findings ­ 1} In negative. 2} In negative. 3} In negative. 4} In negative. 5} Accused is acquitted. REASONS As regards point no.1 to 4 ­ 6] Accused has not disputed the spot of incident. Accused has not disputed age of victim­ch8ild girl. Admittedly, victim is minor. All these aspects are not sufficient to connect accused with present case. 7] P.W.1 Kamal Bhandwale is mother of victim­child girl. She deposed that victim is learning in 8th standard. She is 14 years old. She had quarrel with accused on account of petty reason. Accused used to have quarrel daily with her. Her daughter was annoyed. One day she went at police station and reported the incident. Her daughter told police about quarrel taken place between her and accused. Victim was referred to J. J. Hospital for medical examination. Medical officer did not examine victim and suggested to come on next day but she did not go. Victim said to her that accused used to trouble her. Accused is addicted of liquor. Daughter told her that accused used to scold in her absence. P.W.1 did not support case of prosecution. .. 5 .. Special Case No. 112/2017 Judgment CNR : MHTH23­001814­2017 8] Victim is examined at Exhibit 15. Child­friendly atmosphere was created. Precaution was taken that victim and accused shall not see each other. Victim deposed that she is learning in 8th standard. Her mother used to sell snacks ''dhokala''. Daily she used to study. Accused unnecessarily interfered and was giving unnecessary suggestions. She was having disturbance to her study. Accused was misguiding about method of study. She was preparing for examination on the day of incident. At about 1.00 p.m. accused started scolding her. She had disturbance to her study. She could study. Accused caused harassment. She felt that she could not able to complete her education. She narrated the incident to mother. She suggested mother to go at police station in order to file complaint. She narrated above incident to police. She requested police to convince her father. Victim did not support case of prosecution. 9] A.P.P. declared victim and her mother hostile and cross­examined in a length by putting material suggestions. Witnesses have denied each and every suggestion put to them. A.P.P. invited attention of P.W.1 on facts contended in portion marked P1 and confronted her. A.P.P. invited attention of victim on facts contended in portion marked P2 comes to be recorded in complaint Exh.16 and confronted her. 10] Investigation officer P.W.3 deposed that victim has deposed facts contended in portion marked P2 which is marked Exhibit 22. P.W.1 Kamla has deposed facts contended in 'P1' comes .. 6 .. Special Case No. 112/2017 Judgment CNR : MHTH23­001814­2017 to be marked Exhibit 21. It is crystal clear from the evidence of prosecution's witnesses that victim and her mother have deposed different set of facts before police officer and investigation officer. Witnesses have deposed different set of facts before this court. Evidence of victim and witnesses appears to be self­contradictory. I conclude that victim and her mother have filed complaint against accused with ulterior motive. Evidence of P.W.1 and 2 does not appears to be trustworthy and reliable. I hold that evidence of prosecution's witnesses is not sufficient to bring accused to the home of guilt. I have answered point no.1 to 4 in negative. I proceed to pass following order ­ ORDER 1} Accused Rajendrakumar Hasmukhrai Mashru alias Vimal Thakkar is acquitted under section 235(1) of Cr.P.C. of charge for offences punishable under section 354, 504 506 of Indian Penal Code and section 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 2} Bail bonds of accused stand cancelled. Sureties are discharged. 3} In view of mandate laid down in section 437A of Cr.P.C., accused is directed to execute P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­. He shall undertake to appear before appellate court on receipt of notice of appeal. Date : 15.02.2018 ( M. P. Divate ) Additional Sessions Judge­1, Vasai.

Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.113/2017 CNR No.MHTH23­001819­2017 Received on : 04/12/2017 Registered on : 04/12/2017 Decided on : 21/01/2019 Duration : 17 01 01 D M Y IN THE COURT OF THE ADDITIONAL SESSIONS JUDGE­2, VASAI ( Presided over by Rahul R. Bhosale ) POCSO Special Case No. 113 of 2017. CNR No.MHTH23­001819­2017 Exhibit No.50. The State of Maharashtra .... Complainant. (through Manikpur Police Station.) versus 1] Kisan Shamal Walendra .... Accused. Age 45 years, R/at : Chulanegaon, Khalatipada, Vasai (W), Tal.Vasai, Dist.Palghar. 2] Kavita @ Sushma Kisan Walendra Age 40 years, R/at : Chulanegaon, Khalatipada, Vasai (W), Tal.Vasai, Dist.Palghar. Learned Advocates : Mr.Jayprakash Patil A.P.P. for State. Ms. Sheetal Patil for accused No.1. Mrs. Anjali Patil for accused No.2. JUDGMENT (Delivered on this 21st day of January, 2019. ) 1] Accused are facing the trial for crime under Ss. 4,6,8 and 17 /2/ Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.113/2017 CNR No.MHTH23­001819­2017 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act (POCSO Act) and Ss. 376, 354 & 506 of Indian Penal Code 1860 (IPC). 2] Brief facts of the prosecution case are as under : a) The Child was residing with her mother­accused no.2 and stepfather – accused no.1 while her elder brother was engaged in the job at Mumbai. Child's mother and accused were working as sweeper. Earlier, when Child was studying in 4 th std, the accused no.1 was touching inappropriately to her breast, back, abdomen and other body parts which was disliked by her hence she was keeping distance from him. In the year 2014 the Child was studying in 7 th standard. Child's mother­ accused no.2 went to attend her job when Child and the accused no.1 alone stayed at the house. At around 2.00 p.m. accused no.1 came in close proximity of the Child & rubbed his hand on the body of the Child. The Child tried to protest him but he by shutting her mouth with his hand let her to lay on the floor. He removed her frock and other apparels by removing his apparels also . He slapped the Child when she tried to put aside him and later on he shut her mouth by threatening not to make any noise. He then inserted his urinating part into urinating part of Child to commit forcible rape on her. He thereafter, deliberately stayed in the house to prevent the Child from telling that incident to any one. Child's mother­accused no.2 returned at 5.00 p.m. to home, the Child told her that incident but she ignored by replying to deal the matter at her own.
