However, before proceeding for sentencing the accused I will give the opportunity to him for making submission on the point of sentencing as required under S.235 (2) of Cr.P.C 1973. 27] Today, in presence of the accused, his counsel Ms. Sheetal Patil has argued that the accused no.1 is the only earning member of the family upon whom the minor children are dependent hence, she lastly submits to take a lenient view while sentencing the accused. In counter APP Mr. Jayprakash Patil has submitted that the accused committed heinous and gruesome serious crime against a minor making his relationship with the Child immoral and unethical hence the maximum sentence may be inflicted. 28] As evident earlier, the accused no.1 being stepfather committed aggravated penetrative sexual assault on the Child having no capacity of even thinking about maintaining the sexual relations. Due to such assault the accused caused not only the crime against the body of the Child but he also affected grossly to the emotional quotient of the Child making her paralyzed in the emotional bonding with the persons of opposite sex. The agony of a girl to face such heinous crime in her adolescent age would change entirely the pattern of her life. This offence is also committed against the society of which the element like the Child should be mentally and physically healthy and sound constituent. At the same time it is required to be noted that the accused no.1 has two minor children. His contention about they are depending upon him for their / 22 / Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.113/2017 CNR No.MHTH23­001819­2017 survival is not acceptable as accused no.2 ­ the mother of those Children is also an earning member. But considering the age of accused no.1 and dependency of the Children on him emotionally, the proportionate sentence is to be passed. 29] The accused is thus convicted for the offences under Ss. 5(l)&(n) & 7 punishable respectively under Ss. 6 and 8 of POCSO Act 2012, and under Ss. 376(2)(f)&(n) & 506 of IPC 1860. The minimum sentence under Ss. 6 of the POCSO Act 2012 and under 376(2)(f)&(n) of IPC 1860 is similar i.e. rigorous punishment for term which shall not be less than 10 years but which may extend to imprisonment for life and fine. S.42 of the POCSO Act 2012 provides the alternate punishment in this situation is to be passed which is greater in degree. As both of those punishments are similar hence I prefer to pass the sentence only for the offence under S. 5(l)&(n) punishable under S. 6 of POCSO Act 2012. The sentence of 15 years rigorous imprisonment alongwith fine of Rs.15,000/­(Rupees Fifteen Thousand only) is proportionate to the act of present accused. I further pass the sentence for offence under S.7 punishable under S.8 of the POCSO Act 2012 for 3 years rigorous imprisonment alongwith fine of Rs.5000/­ (Rupee Five Thousand only). I lastly pass the sentence for offence under S.503 punishable under S. 506 of IPC 1860 for 1 year rigorous imprisonment. 30] Honourable Apex Court in the case of Ms. Era through Manjula Vs. Government of NCT of Delhi, Cri. Appeal No.12171219/2017, dated 21/07/2017 has held that in such kind of sentence the proper care is to be taken for neutralizing the impact upon the Child by providing various medical as well as psychological assistance. It is made possible only if the comprehensive compensation is granted. / 23 / Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.113/2017 CNR No.MHTH23­001819­2017 The cardinal principle in such cases is the re­formative and beneficial arrangement to be made for the victim of the sexual abuse. S.357­A of Cr.P.C 1973 r/w R.7 of POCSO Rules 2012, mandate such compensation is to be arranged by DLSA. Therefore, I answer point no.9 in the affirmative and pass the order as under : ORDER 1] The accused No.1­ Kisan Shamal Walendra is convicted under Section 235(2) of Cr.P.C 1973 for : (i) the offence under Ss. 5(l)&(n) punishable under S. 6 of POCSO Act 2012 with rigorous imprisonment for a term of 15 years and to pay fine of Rs.15,000/­ (Rupees Fifteen Thousand Only); in default of payment of fine, accused No.1 shall undergo further the simple imprisonment for six months. (ii) the offence under S.7 punishable under S.8 of the POCSO Act 2012 with rigorous imprisonment for a term of 3 years and to pay fine of Rs.5000/­ (Rupee Five Thousand only); in default of payment of fine, accused No.1 shall undergo further the simple imprisonment for three months. (iii) the offence under S.503 punishable under S. 506 of IPC 1860 with rigorous imprisonment for a term of 1 year. 2] All sentences shall run concurrently. 3] The benefit of set off under S.428 of Cr.P.C.1973 regarding the period of under trial imprisonment be given to the accused No.1. 4] The accused No.2 ­ Kavita @ Sushma Kisan Walendra is acquitted as per section 235(1) of Cr.P.C. for offences punishable under sections Ss. 376(2)(f)&(n), 354, 506 of I.P.C. 1860 and under sections 4,6,8,17 of POCSO Act 2012. 5] The Secretary, DSLA, Thane, shall arrange for making the / 24 / Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.113/2017 CNR No.MHTH23­001819­2017 payment of compensation to the Child as earlier as possible. 6] The muddemal property being worthless be destroyed after appeal period is over. 7] The copy of judgment be given to the accused no.1 free of cost. 8] The copy of judgment be sent to The Collector, Palghar for taking appropriate action under S.365 of Cr.P.C. 1973. sd/­xxx Vasai ( Rahul R. Bhosale ) Date : 21/01/2019. Additional Sessions Judge­2, Vasai.

Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.83/2016 CNR No.MHTH23­001829­2016 Received on : 02/12/2016. Registered on : 02/12/2016. Decided on : 23/01/2019. Duration : 21 01 02 D M Y IN THE COURT OF THE ADDITIONAL SESSIONS JUDGE­2, VASAI ( Presided over by Rahul R. Bhosale ) POCSO Special Case No. 83 of 2016. CNR No.MHTH23­001829­2016. Exhibit No.30. The State of Maharashtra .... Complainant. (through Manikpur Police Station.) versus Prem alias Mantu Dhirendra Dalpati .... Accused. Age 25 years, Resident of Vasai Native Place – Gram Dharampur,Pol.Stn. Bangaon, Dist. North 24 Paragana,West Bengal. Learned Advocates : Mrs.K.M.Khandagale A.P.P. for State. Mrs. Sharda Patil for accused. JUDGMENT (Delivered on this 23rd day of January, 2019. ) 1] Accused is facing the trial for crime under S. 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act (POCSO Act) and Ss.342, 354(A) & (D),323 & 506 of Indian Penal Code 1860 (IPC). 2] Brief facts of the prosecution case are as under : a) The Child was residing with her parents and sibling on the given / 2/ Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.83/2016 CNR No.MHTH23­001829­2016 address while learning in 8th standard. On 17/7/2016 at around 6.30 p.m. the Child went for patching up the punctured tyre of her bicycle in the nearby cycle shop. The shop keeper told her to collect the bicycle after 2 days hence she was returning to the home and reached near Jui Building at around 7.00 p.m. The accused called her from that building. He told the Child to help him to find out the occupant as he was unable to read the name plate in the English language. The Child replied him to get it read from any other persons as she was late to reach the house where her sister was waiting for her. But the accused requested her by folding hands that his such un­ability to read English language would cause his termination from service as a watchman of that building. b) They both went into the building where the Child by stopping near the occupants' name board asked the accused what was the name of that occupant. The accused replied that as that occupant came recently to reside hence his name was not included in that board and he requested her to come to the flats for reading the name plates. They went at third floor by visiting first and second floors also but the accused directed her towards the terrace of that building to which the Child protested. But the accused replied that she should read the English content on the lock of the terrace and all of sudden he pushed her towards the table placed in that passage. He shut her mouth with hand and caught hold on her neck by threatening for not to raised alarms. The Child was frightened. c) The accused kissed Child on the lips and waived his hand all over her body. He also rubbed her breast by inserting his hand inside of her T­ shirt. The accused asked the Child her name which she told falsely with false mobile number. The Child asked him that whether he did such acts with his mother and sister. The accused got angry and again kissed her. The Child pushed him while the accused was picking the handkerchief. / 3/ Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.83/2016 CNR No.MHTH23­001829­2016 The Child came down­stairs but the accused chased her by holding her T­ Shirt. The Child lastly came to the 2nd floor where she rang a door bell of one flat. The Child told that occupant to accompany her at down stair as she was harassed by accused. d) Thus, Child was relieved by that occupant. Her friends then escorted her to the vicinity of her residence where her mother met the Child. The Child narrated her that incident by crying. They both took search of the accused but he was not found. In the fear of disrepute the report of that incident was not filed immediately but they learned that similar incident was repeated in vicinity on 28/8/2016 in respect of another girl and the molester was apprehended by the police. Hence by gathering courage the FIR was filed to the police. 3] After investigation, the charge­sheet was filed in this court against the accused. A charge for offences punishable under sections 342, 354(A) & (D), 323, 506 of I.P.C. and S.8 of POCSO Act was framed against accused, to which he denied and claimed to be tried. The prosecution has examined : Deepak (P.W.1) Ext.6, XYZ (Mother of Child) (P.W.2) Ext.9, ABC (Child) (P.W.1) Ext.11, Panch­Mahesh (P.W.4) Ext. 12, Nipun(P.W.5) Ext.No.13 and I.O Anil (P.W.6) Ext.17. The prosecution has thereafter, filed the pursis Ext.28 for closing the evidence. The statement of accused has been recorded u/s. 313 of Cr.P.C. Ext.No.29. Accused has raised the defence of total denial and false implication and has not examined any defence witnesses. 4] On the basis of the material on record, the points arise for my determination are answered for the reasons as under ­ / 4/ Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.83/2016 CNR No.MHTH23­001829­2016 Points Findings 1. Whether the prosecution has proved that the .. Proved victim was a 'Child' on the day of incident as provided under S.2(d) of POCSO Act ? 2. Whether the prosecution has proved that the .. Proved accused wrongfully confined the Child ? 3. Whether the prosecution has proved that the .. Partly accused stalked the Child and committed sexual Proved. harassment? 4. Whether the prosecution has proved that .. Proved. accused voluntarily caused hurt to the Child ? 5. Whether the prosecution has proved that .. Proved accused committed criminal intimidation by threatening the Child with intent to cause alarm? 6. What is the order ? .. As per final order. REASONS 5] Point no.1 ­ Materially, the offence under S.7 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act 2012 (for short, POCSO Act) has been charged against the accused. Hence in view of the scope and object of that Act, let us first scrutinize that the whether victim was below age of 18 years, termed as a 'Child' as provided U/S.2(d) of POCSO Act. The document produced by prosecution at Ext. No.25 is the verified true copy of the birth certificate of Child. It is admissible in evidence under Ss.74 & 79 of Evidence Act 1872 r/w S.17 of the Registration of Birth and Deaths Act 1969. It discloses the birth date of Child is 09/12/2003. The informant­ the mother of Child has corroborated that date of birth in her testimony / 5/ Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.83/2016 CNR No.MHTH23­001829­2016 Ext.09 before the Court. Nothing is found to disbelieve that entire evidence. Thus the prosecution has succeeded to prove the Child's birth date is 09/12/2003 while the alleged molestation of the Child was held on 17/7/2016. It concludes that the Child was exactly 12 years 7 months and 08 days old when the alleged incident was held. Thus, the present victim is covered by the term ' Child ' as per S.2(d) therefore, the provisions of POCSO Act are applicable to the present prosecution case. I therefore, answer the point no.1 in the affirmative. 6] Point Nos. 2 & 3 : The prosecution has materially tried to prove sexual assault on the child and while advancing argument, A.P.P. Mrs.K.M. Khandagale has relied upon the presumption under S. 29 of the POCSO Act for presuming that the accused committed the instant crime. In counter Adv. Mrs. Sharda Patil for the accused has argued that firstly the prosecution has to prove the case beyond reasonable doubts. 7] Honourable Bombay High Court in the case of Ramprasad Vs. State of Maharashtra, 2018(3)RCR(criminal)656 has laid down the ruling for application of the statutory presumptions under Ss.29 & 30 of the POCSO Act. In that decision also the judgment of Honourable Apex Court in the case of Babu V./s. State of Kerala, (2010) 9 SCC 189, has been relied upon for mode of application of the statutory presumption as every accused is presumed to be innocent, which is a human right. However, subject to the statutory exceptions, for which the nature of offence, its seriousness and gravity has to be taken into consideration. Mere application of the presumption should not lead to any injustice or mistaken conviction. The various statutory presumptions for guilt of the / 6/ Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.83/2016 CNR No.MHTH23­001829­2016 accused would shift burden of proof of innocence on the accused. However, such presumption should be raised only when certain 'foundational facts' are established by the prosecution. Therefore, Honourable Bombay High Court has concluded that the presumption under Section 29 of the POCSO Act is not absolute and it is triggered only when the prosecution is able to prove 'the foundational facts' in the first place. It has further held that the evidence placed on record by the prosecution is to be examined to first come to the conclusion that the 'foundational facts' of the prosecution case have been established and thereafter only the accused can rebut the presumption either by discrediting the prosecution witnesses by effective cross­examination or by leading defence evidence. 8] Thus, to find out the 'foundational facts' to attract presumption u/s.29 of the POCSO Act, in view of those decisions. In the light of the law aforesaid, the evidence of the prosecution is to be scrutinized. The Child around 13 years of age at the time of that incident is the victim as well as sole eye­witness of the prosecution case. She deposes at Ext.11 that on 17/7/2016 as it was holiday i.e. Sunday. Hence she went to the cycle­shop for repairing punctured tyre of her bicycle­which was told to be collect after two days by the shop­keeper. On the way to return to the home she was called by the accused from compound of Jui building requesting her to read the name plate in English language. She firstly replied her inability as her sister was waiting at home but the accused insisted by saying her that his service as a watchman of that building would be terminated if the said occupant was not found out. The Child further deposes that the accused told her when they came in building near the occupants' name board that' said occupant was newly shifted / 7/ Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.83/2016 CNR No.MHTH23­001829­2016 hence his name was not projected on that board. He requested her to read the name plate of that flat. The accused thus, took the round of each floor of that three storied building and lastly they reached near the passage of terrace of that building. Nothing inappropriate and un­ natural is found in the evidence of the Child uptill now as with shere enthusiasm and with a childish feeling to extend the help to the person in difficulty, the Child innocently went with the accused in search of said occupant. 9] The Child further deposes that in the passage of terrace the accused gagged her mouth but the Child tried to protest him. Accused threatened her for not to shout, he kissed her and put his hand into her T­ shirt and molested her. The cross­examination of Child was taken materially on her omissions while stating the incident to the police as per deposition here that the accused requested the Child to read the name plate of one occupant who came recently to reside in that building. Her statement before the police discloses that the accused requested the Child to read the English name plate of the house of his sister where he had to visit. However, that omission is not brought on record by the accused by applying the legal recourse under S. 162 of Cr.P.C r/w S.145 of Indian Evidence Act 1872. That apart, the deposition of the Child before the Court, in this situation has a probative value than what she had omitted while making the statement before the police. 10] The Child thus deposes as rape surviver. As relied upon by prosecution the law relating to scrutiny of the rape surviver has been long back laid down by the Honourable Apex Court in the case of State of Punjab Vs. Gurmit Singh, AIR 1996 (SC) 1393. It has been held that / 8/ Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.83/2016 CNR No.MHTH23­001829­2016 a murderer destroys the physical body of the victim, a rapist degrades the very soul of the helpless female. The courts therefore, shoulder a great responsibility while trying accused on charges of rape. They must deal such cases with utmost sensitivity by examining broader probabilities of a case and not get swayed by minor contradictions or insignificant discrepancies in statement of victim. If evidence of prosecutrix inspires confidence, it must be relied upon without seeking corroboration of her statement in material particulars. The testimony of the prosecutrix must be appreciated in background of entire case and the trial court must be alive to its responsibility and be sensitive while dealing with cases involving sexual molestations. 11] The Child's sole deposition, as per decision (supra), if qualifies certain tests led down then it would be accepted as it is. This rulling is consistently followed in subsequent decisions by Honourable Apex Court as can be also evidence in case of Vijay Vs. State of M.P., 2010(8) SCC 191 as relied upon by APP. But Honourable Apex Court, in case of Baby Kandayanathil Vs. State of Kerala, AIR 1992 (4) SCC 225, has held that evidence of Child witness must find adequate corroboration before it is relied upon such rule is a particular wisdom than of law. However, it is not the law that if the witness is Child his evidence shall be rejected even if it is found reliable. The law is that evidence of a Child witness must be evaluated carefully and with greater circumspection because a Child is susceptible to be swayed by what others tell and Child witness is an easy prey to tutoring by others. It evidence of Child is not of a quality to place reliance, it is expected that the court to search for corroboration from some evidence which could give credence to the testimony of a Child witness. / 9/ Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.83/2016 CNR No.MHTH23­001829­2016 In the present case the Child is herself a rape surviver hence the laws led supra by Honourable Apex Court should be applied simultaneously to the Child's deposition. 12] The Child's deposition in the light of aforesaid ruling reveals the sexual assault accused committed on her is a truth. It is also material to note that the FIR of incident was filed by Child's mother to the police. She deposes at Ext.9 that after facing that incident the Child was returning and approached to Surya garden where she was present. After noticing her, as per further deposition of this witness, the Child ran towards her in crying, hugged her tightly and later on narrated the incident she faced. In her further deposition, the Child's mother deposes what Child told her the incident which Child has deposed here earlier. That was the Child's spontaneous and natural emotional errupt after facing that incident. Therefore mother's deposition corroborates the version of Child before the Court as nothing is found in her cross­examination to disbelieve her version. It does not reveal about what is shown as the statement of the Child before the police that the accused was in search of his sister at the time of said incident. I therefore, do not find anything doubtful in the deposition of Child about the manner of said incident. 13] The Child has alleged that the accused by gagging her mouth, hugged her, kissed her lips, waived his hand all over body and molester her by inserting his hand inside her T­shirt. This evidence is also corroborated by the Child's mother to whom the Child stated that incident immediately after facing it. Nothing is found to disbelieve that evidence as the line of cross­examination of both of the witnesses is not suggestive of any solid defence such as roping in of the accused deliberately etc. I / 10 / Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.83/2016 CNR No.MHTH23­001829­2016 also not find on record any material which could raise the probability that these witnesses have roped the accused in the crime. The natural enthusiasm and curiosity of the Child was taken disadvantage of by the accused for molesting her. That evidence attract the definition of Sexual Assault as per S.7 of the POCSO Act which for ready reference reads as under : Section 7 : Sexual Assault ­ Whoever, with sexual intent touches the vagina, penis, anus or breast of the child or makes the child touch the vagina, penis anus or breast of such person or any other person, or does any other act with sexual intent which involves physical contact without penetration is said to commit sexual assault. The evidence of Child thus proves the definition of Sexual Assault in prosecution case. 14] One material aspect, though is not raised by the accused yet for removal other doubt is to be considered, as the FIR of the incident was filed by the Child's mother on 29/8/2016 about the Sexual Assault faced by the Child from the accused on 17/7/2016. The delay of more than 42 days is tried to be explained in the FIR itself as the informant­mother did not find accused immediately after that incident in the search in the said vicinity and to prevent the Child's family to be disreputed, that incident was not immediately informed to the police. The FIR further discloses that on 28/8/2016 the Child's mother learned that similar incident as faced by the Child was repeated regarding another girl in that vicinity hence to prevent further repetition and for taking stern action regarding that incident, the FIR was filed on 29/8/2016. If these events are / 11 / Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.83/2016 CNR No.MHTH23­001829­2016 scrutinized one by one then the natural consistency of human behaviour is evident. Firstly, the Child's mother ignored to report immediately the molestation of the Child to police as she thought it would disrepute the family. But when similar incident was repeated regarding another girl in vicinity, her conscience topped up to prevent any further repetition, she approached to the police and filed the present FIR. Thus, I do not find any un­natural or any sort of attempt intentionally made for roping the accused in the instant crime caused delay to file the present FIR. It is not even the suggestion of the accused to the prosecution witnesses about any deliberation they made to file the FIR lately only on account of roping the accused in the instant crime. I therefore do not find the delay is fatal to the prosecution case. 15] The prosecution has examined Mahesh(P.W.4) who was the pancha on the spot panchanama which he has proved as per Ext.13. The spot of incident which the Child has deposed before the Court is proved by the said evidence as nothing disbelievable has been noticed in his cross­ examination conducted by the accused. 16] The prosecution has examined Deepak(P.W.1) who has proved in his deposition at Ext.6 the disclosure statement made by the accused at Ext. 7 and memorandum panchanama resulting from it at Ext.8. This entire evidence discloses that the accused made a disclosure statement to the investigation officer about the spot of incident when he was in his custody. Further evidence discloses that as per direction of the accused , the police squad including the present pancha approached to the said spot of incident. APP Mrs.K.M. Khandagale has submitted that said evidence is admissible so as to conclude the knowledge of the accused about spot of / 12 / Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.83/2016 CNR No.MHTH23­001829­2016 incident attached him to the offence he committed in view of S.27 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872. This argument is not acceptable simply on the ground that as per the disclosure statement at Ext.7 the accused disclosed his knowledge about spot of incident on 8/9/2016 to the investigation officer when he was in his custody. But the prosecution case on record reveals that spot panchanama at Ext.30 was carried out earlier by same investigation officer on 30/8/2016 by visiting to the spot of incident. Thus, the situation of the spot of incident was quite within knowledge of investigation officer on 30/8/2016 much earlier to the disclosure statement made by the accused on 8/9/2016 as per Ext.7. The fact which was known to the investigation officer earlier cannot become the discovery as per S.27 of the Indian Evidence Act 1872 as tried to be submitted by the APP in the light of disclosure statement of the accused at Ext.7. The said evidence is therefore not useful to the prosecution. However, as noticed earlier, the prosecution independently proved the spot of incident in the light of cogent evidence hence the failure of prosecution regarding discovery will not effect the prosecution case. 17] APP Mrs. K.M.Khandagale has argued that the accused being the habitual offender created fear in the mind of the residents in the vicinity of the spot of incident. The FIR at C.R.No.221/2016 was earlier filed against the present accused about penetrative sexual assault on the another Child. Therefore, as per submission of APP Mrs. K.M.Khandagale combing operation for apprehending the accused was started by he police machinery in that vicinity. Nipun (P.W.5) who participated in said operation as a reputed resident in that vicinity, supports the prosecution as per his deposition at Ext.15. He deposes that during search of accused with police squad, the accused was found in the vicinity who was nabbed / 13 / Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.83/2016 CNR No.MHTH23­001829­2016 in his presence. Nipun (P.W.5) has identified the accused in the court also. Thus, his evidence corroborates the prosecution case about the seriousness in commission of the crime as the accused was habitual offender. He was involved in the molestation and crime against minor girls who obviously had no physical capacity to defend as well as they were the soft targets and preys because the parents and family members are generally reluctant to take any action about atrocities faced by minor girls. However, the prosecution witnesses making exception to that general feeling, came forward against the accused to bring his atrocities in the light. 18] Anil (P.W.6), the Investigating Officer, has deposed at Ext.17 to support the investigation he carried out in the instant crime to conclude the accused as culprit in the light of cogent evidence,. His deposition carries presumption under S. 114(e) of Indian Evidence Act 1872 to attract the official regularly as nothing adverse is found in his cross­ examination. This evidence also corroborates the prosecution case to reach to the conclusion that accused is guilty of the alleged crime. 19] The prosecution has thus succeeded to prove the foundational facts against the accused as per the decisions of Honourable Apex court (supra). The prosecution thus attracts presumption under S. 29 and 30 of the POSCO Act which prove the culpability and involvement of the accused in the instant crime. The accused has not brought on record any probability to attract reasonable doubts to the prosecution. His material defence as also stated by accused in recording of statement under S. 313 of Cr.P.C that he was roped in the crime as he had drunken liquor hence he was roped in, is not found probable also. There is no any other reliable / 14 / Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.83/2016 CNR No.MHTH23­001829­2016 or probable defence raised by the accused. Thus, the prosecution has succeeded to prove sexual assault by accused on Child. The prosecution evidence also reveals that the accused by holding hand of Child and threatening her, confined her in the passage of 3 rd floor terrace of the Jui building. It attracts definition of ' wrongful confinement ' under S.340 coupled with punishment under s. 342 of IPC. The prosecution further proves that accused by fondling the Child, committed her sexual harassment as provided and punishable under S. 354­A of the IPC 1860. The prosecution however does not prove 'stalking' of Child as provided under S.354­D of IPC 1860 committed by the accused as nothing is found in prosecution evidence that the accused followed the child repeatedly. In the result I answer point no. 2 in the affirmative and 3 in the partly affirmative. 20] Point Nos. 4 and 5 : The Child, has not deposed at Ext. 11 about the accused had caused hurt to Child as defined under S. 319 of IPC to prove his guilt under S. 323 of IPC 1860. Further, the criminal intimidation as required as per its definition under S. 503 of IPC 1860 however is proved by the Child in her deposition as the accused threatened her by shutting her mouth ordering her to keep silence caused alarm to her. It attracts the offence punishable under S.506 of the Code. I therefore, answer point nos. 4 and 5 in the affirmative. 21] Point No. 6 : The prosecution has thus succeeded to prove that the accused committed the offences under S. 7 punishable under S. 8 of POCSO Act 2012, and under Ss. 354(A), 342, 323 & 506 of IPC 1860. However, / 15 / Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.83/2016 CNR No.MHTH23­001829­2016 before proceeding for sentencing the accused I will give the opportunity to him for making submission on the point of sentencing as required under S.235 (2) of Cr.P.C 1973. 22] Today, in presence of the accused, his counsel Mrs. Sharda Patil has argued that the accused is the only earning member of the family upon whom the minor children are dependent hence, she lastly submits to take a lenient view while sentencing the accused. In counter APP Mrs. K.M.Khandagale has submitted that the accused committed heinous and gruesome serious crime against a minor making his relationship with the Child immoral and unethical hence the maximum sentence may be inflicted. 23] As evident earlier, the accused is found involved in the crime which he pre­planned by considering all probable issues to be dealt with. It is also evident that he is convicted in Spl.C.No.79/2016 relating to the crime of sexual abuse of another Child. Thus, he is found a habitual offender. Due to such assaults the accused caused not only the crime against the body of the Child but he also affected grossly to the emotional quotient of the Child making her paralyzed in the emotional bonding with the persons of opposite sex. The agony of a girl to face such heinous crime in her adolescent age would change entirely the pattern of her life. This offence is also committed against the society of which the element like the Child should be mentally and physically healthy and sound constituent. His repeated such acts made him serial sexual abuser of the Children in vicinity terrorizing the residents in vicinity. Therefore the proportionate sentence has to be passed. / 16 / Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.83/2016 CNR No.MHTH23­001829­2016 24] The accused is thus convicted for the offences under Ss. 7 punishable under S. 8 of POCSO Act 2012, and under Ss. 354(A), 342, 323 & 506 of IPC 1860. The minimum sentence for the offences under 7 punishable under S.8 of the POCSO Act 2012 is 3 years while under 354(A) of IPC 1860 is of 1 year. S.42 of the POCSO Act 2012 provides the alternate punishment in this situation is to be passed which is greater in degree. Therefore, I pass the sentence only under S.8 of the POCSO Act for 5 years rigorous imprisonment alongwith fine of Rs.5,000/­ (Rupees Five Thousand only) which is proportionate to the act of present accused. I also pass the sentence under S. 342 of IPC 1860 for 1 year simple imprisonment with fine of Rs.500/­(Rupee Five Hundred Only); U/s. 323 of IPC 1860 for 1 year simple imprisonment with fine of Rs.500/­ (Rupee Five Hundred Only) and U/s. 506 of IPC 1860 for 2 years simple imprisonment with fine of Rs.1000/­. 25] Honourable Apex Court in the case of Ms. Era through Manjula Vs. Government of NCT of Delhi, Cri. Appeal No.12171219/2017, dated 21/07/2017 has held that in such kind of sentence the proper care is to be taken for neutralizing the impact upon the Child by providing various medical as well as psychological assistance. It is made possible only if the comprehensive compensation is granted. The cardinal principle in such cases is the re­formative and beneficial arrangement to be made for the victim of the sexual abuse. S.357­A of Cr.P.C 1973 r/w R.7 of POCSO Rules 2012, mandate such compensation is to be arranged by DLSA. Therefore, I answer point no. in the affirmative and pass the order as under : / 17 / Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.83/2016 CNR No.MHTH23­001829­2016 ORDER 1] The accused Prem alias Mantu Dhirendra Dalpati is convicted under Section 235(2) of Cr.P.C 1973 for : (i) the offence under S.7 punishable u/s.8 of the POCSO Act for 5 years rigorous imprisonment alongwith fine of Rs.5,000/­(Rupees Five Thousand only); in default of payment of fine, accused shall undergo further the simple imprisonment for four months. (ii) the offence u/s.340 punishable u/s. 342 of IPC 1860 for 1 year simple imprisonment with fine of Rs.500/­(Rupee Five Hundred Only); in default of payment of fine, accused shall undergo further the simple imprisonment for one month. (iii) the offence u/s.319 punishable u/s. 323 of IPC 1860 for 1 year simple imprisonment with fine of Rs.500/­ (Rupee Five Hundred Only); in default of payment of fine, accused shall undergo further the simple imprisonment for one month. (iv) the offence u/s. 503 punishable u/s. 506 of IPC 1860 for 2 years simple imprisonment with fine of Rs.1000/­ (Rupee One Thousand Only); in default of payment of fine, accused shall undergo further the simple imprisonment for one month. 2] All sentences shall run concurrently. 3] The benefit of set off under S.428 of Cr.P.C.1973 regarding the period of under trial imprisonment be given to the accused. 4] The Secretary, DSLA, Thane, shall arrange for making the payment of compensation to the Child as earlier as possible. 5] The muddemal property being worthless be destroyed after appeal period is over. / 18 / Judgment Pocso Spl.Case No.83/2016 CNR No.MHTH23­001829­2016 6] The copy of judgment be given to the accused free of cost. 7] The copy of judgment be sent to The Collector, Palghar for taking appropriate action under S.365 of Cr.P.C. 1973. Najmuddin Husnoddin Shaikh, Age – 27 years, R/at : Ek Lakh Maulavi Chawl, Behind Urdu High School, Chaudhary Mohalla, Kalyan. 2. Shaikh Azar Shaikh Hamid, Age – 27 years, R/at : Ek Lakh Maulavi Chawl, Behind Urdu High School, Chaudhary Mohalla, Kalyan. 3. Shaikh Karim Hussain Haji, Age – 20 years, R/at : Ek Lakh Maulavi Chawl, Behind Urdu High School, Chaudhary Mohalla, Kalyan. .. Accused Offence : U/Sec. 354(A) of the Indian Penal Code and under section 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. (2) Appearances: ==================================== Smt. R. R. Bhoir, A.P.P. for State Shri. V. P. Sonekar, Advocate for the accused ==================================== J U D G M E N T. ( Delivered in open court on 09th January, 2017 ) 1. These accused persons are prosecuted by the State through Bazarpeth police station, Kalyan for the above stated offences. Facts in nut shell are as follows: 2. Complainant Ayesha Irshad Kaskar and accused persons are residents of one and same area. The incident took place on 02/12/2013. At that time complainant Ayesha was studying in 9 th standard and she was 14 years old. It is her say that she was used to go to her school at 12.30 noon by walk. Since 8 months prior to the alleged incident these accused persons were giving trouble to the complainant by passing abusive remarks, by giving whistles to her etc. etc. On 02/12/2013 at about 12.00 noon when the complainant Ayesha was proceeding to her school, accused Azar and Karim Shaikh came from her backside. Accused Azar pulled her Dupatta. Accused Karim pulled her school bag. At that time accused Ajmuddin was standing nearby and he was laughing loudly. Complainant Ayesha shouted and thereafter all the accused persons ran away. After returning home in the evening complainant narrated this incident to (3) Spl. Case No. 01/2014 (J) her father and mother. When father, mother and brother of complainant had been to the house of these accused persons, they abused them and beat them by fists and kick blows. Thereafter complainant came to police station and lodged complaint against accused persons. Crime was registered as C.R. No.306/2013. Investigation was carried by one A.P.I. S.M. Ghotekar. Investigating officer recorded statements of mother, father and brothers of the complainant. Thereafter after completion of investigation he submitted chargesheet against these accused persons in the court. 3. Accused persons appeared before this court. Charge against them is framed at Exh.2. Charge was read over and explained to accused persons in Marathi language. Accused persons pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. Their defence is of total denial. 4. Prosecution was directed to adduce its evidence in support of its case. In response to that prosecution examined P.W. No.1 Ayesha Kaskar the complainant at Exh.4. Further prosecution examined P.W. No.2 Irshad Kaskar father of the complainant at Exh.5. Thereafter prosecution closed its evidence. 5. I have gone through the prosecution evidence on record. I have heard both learned advocates. 6. Following points arise for my consideration. My findings on those points are as follows for the reasons stated below. (4) POINTS FINDINGS 1) Does prosecution prove that on 02/12/2013 at about 12.00 hours on the way to school of complainant Ayesha, Kalyan West accused persons tried to make physical contact and advances involving unwelcome as well as made sexual coloured remarks towards minor victim and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 354(A) of the I.P.C.? No. 2) Does prosecution further prove that on the above­said date, time and place accused persons committed sexual harassment to the minor complainant and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 ? No. REASONS As to Points no. 1 and 2 :­ 7. Though prosecution tried its level best to prove the guilt of accused persons by examining the complainant and her father, it could not succeed. Complainant Ayesha and her father Irshad both turned hostile. About the alleged incident not a single word uttered by the complainant Ayesha or her father Irshad. In the entire deposition of P.W. No.1 and P.W. No. 2 absolutely no incriminating (5) Spl. Case No. 01/2014 (J) evidence against the accused persons. Nowhere Ayesha stated that these accused persons passed any abusive remarks or vulgar remarks against her or made any vulgar sign to her or whistle. Both witnesses of prosecution stated that there was quarrel between P.W. No.2 Irshad and the accused persons. On that count this complaint is filed. Though complainant Ayesha admitted her signature on the complaint, she has not supported the contents in the complaint. Thus, absolutely no evidence adduced on record by the prosecution to establish any of the guilt of any accused. 8. As there is no incriminating evidence against the accused persons, their statement under section 313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure stands dispensed with. 9. In these facts and circumstances there is no alternative for me except to answer both the points in negative. I answer the points accordingly and pass the following order. O R D E R 1) The accused No.1) Najmuddin Husnoddin Shaikh, 2) Shaikh Azar Shaikh Hamid and 3) Shaikh Karim Hussain Haji are hereby acquitted of the offence punishable under Section 354 (A) of the Indian Penal Code and under section 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2) Their bail bonds stands cancelled. They are set at (6) liberty. 3) Accused persons to furnish bail under section 437(A) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Kalyan ( D.S. Hatarote ) Date :­ 09/01/2017 Special Judge under the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences, Act, Kalyan.

.. 1 .. Spl. Case 5/2016 [Judgment] Presented on : 6/1/2016. Registered on : 6/1/2016 Decided on : 27/2/2017 Duration : 1Y. 1 M. 21 D. IN THE COURT OF SPECIAL JUDGE, KALYAN AT : KALYAN. (Presided over by : M.J.Mirza) SPECIAL CASE NO.5/2016 Exh. State of Maharashtra. Through : P.I., Central Police Station. ...Complainant. Vs. Aakash Pralhad Sonavane, Age : 22 years, Occ. Education, R/at : C­147, Shiv Colony, Near Anmol Apartment, Ulhasnagar­3 ….Accused. Appearance : Spl.P.P.Shri D.V. Bhangare for the State. Advocate Shri M.M. Punde for the accused. Offences : ­ Punishable under Section 354, 354­D & 509 of I.P.C. and Section 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. :JUDGMENT: (Delivered in open Court on 27/2/2017) 1. The accused Aakash Pralhad Sonavane is facing the trial for the offences punishable under Sections 354, 354­D & 509 of I.P.C. and Section 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, alleging that the accused outraged her modesty and .. 2 .. Spl. Case 5/2016 [Judgment] uttered the words intending to insult the victim and also committed sexual harassment. 2. The case of the prosecution, in short is as under : The informant/victim, aged 16 years, lodged the FIR on 8/8/2015 stating therein that she is residing with her parents and her two brothers at Ulhasnagar­2 since her birth. She was studying in 11th standard in Art faculty in R.K.T. College, Ulhasnagar. After S.S.C., she joined MS­CIT in Swati Classes at Ulhasnagar­3. She acquainted with the accused as he also joined MS­CIT in same classes. Her friend Varsha Shelar and Nandini Parmar also came in said class. The accused was the friend of her two friends due to which friendship was developed. Accused was also studying in R.K.T. college. Thereafter, the accused used to tease her and used to take her photographs and was demanding her cell number. She disclosed the said fact to her mother, her mother who told her not to go to the college. 3. On 7/8/2015, at 3.30 p.m. after the college hours she arrived at the college gate near Sapna Garden where the accused arrived there with his two friends and whistled and winkled his eyes. When she asked the reason to him, he caught hold her hand and started saying to have a photograph with him. Due to fear she went to her house. When her brother Ganesh asked her as to what had happened, then she disclosed the incident to him. Her brother Ganesh then went to ask the accused about the incident, however the accused and his friends assaulted him. Then she lodged the FIR. She has assigned the reason of belated FIR as she had frightened. .. 3 .. Spl. Case 5/2016 [Judgment] 4. PW­3 PSI Swapnil Sanjay Kedar of Central Police Station was on PSO duty from 9 a.m. to 9 pm., who recorded the FIR (Exh.14) lodged by the victim and then he registered the crime at C.R.No.I­376/2015 under Sec. 354 & 509 of IPC and Sec. 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 on 8/8/2015. The accused came to be arrested on 8/8/2015 under arrest form. 5. Further investigation was carried out by PSI Smt. Punam Dadasaheb Jadhav (PW.4) as the investigation was entrusted with her by Sr.P.I. She recorded the statements of the witnesses, however the victim refused to give her statement to be recorded under Sec. 164 of Cr.P.C. After completion of investigation, she filed the chargesheet in this Special Court. 6. Charge at Exh.6 was framed by me which was read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. The accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. His defence is of false involvement as per his statement recorded under Section 313 of Code of Criminal Procedure. Neither the accused stepped into the witness­box nor examined any defence witness. 7. Heard learned Spl. P.P. Shri D.V.Bhangare for the State and learned Advocate Shri M.M. Punde for the accused, at length. 8. The following points arise for my determination and my findings thereon are recorded against them for the reasons to follow:­ .. 4 .. Spl. Case 5/2016 [Judgment] Points Findings 1. Whether the prosecution proved that the victim was minor below 18 years ? .. Yes. 2. Whether the prosecution has proved that on 7/8/2015, at about 3.30 p.m. at the gate of the R.K.T. College, Ulhasnagar, the accused used criminal force to informant/minor victim, aged 16 years, intending to outrage her modesty, punishable .. Not proved. under Sec.354 of IPC ? 3 Whether the prosecution has proved that at the relevant time, the accused followed the informant/minor victim and attempted to contact her to foster personal interaction repeatedly despite a clear indication of disinterest by her, whistled and blinked his eyes, punishable under Sec.354­D of IPC ? .. Not proved. 4 Whether the prosecution has proved that at the relevant time, the accused intended to insult the modesty of the victim and uttered words by saying to the victim that she should snap a photograph with him and also whistled and wonk his eyes towards .. 5 .. Spl. Case 5/2016 [Judgment] her punishable under Sec.509 of I.P.C. ? .. Not proved. 5 Whether the prosecution has proved that at the relevant time, the accused committed sexual harassment upon a minor victim, by uttering her to have a photograph with him and also made gesture by his eyes wonk, punishable under Sec.12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 ? .. Not proved. 6 What order ? ….. Accused acquitted. : REASONS : 9. To substantiate the charge, prosecution has examined in all four witnesses, viz. PW.1 the minor victim at Exh.13 whose evidence was recorded in camera and in child friendly atmosphere. PW.2 Ganesh Mahadev Asawale (Exh.15), the brother of the victim. PW­3 PSI Swapnil Sanjay Kedar (Exh.17), who recorded the FIR (Exh.14) and registered the crime on 8/8/2015. The last witness is PW­4 IO PSI Smt. Punam Dadasaheb Jadhav, who recorded the statements of the parents and two brothers of the victim. The victim refused to give her statement before learned Magistrate to be recorded under Sec. 164 of Cr.P.C. After completion of investigation she filed the chargesheet. AS TO POINT NO. 1 : 10. The victim has brought on record in her testimony that her age as on 4/2/2017 when her evidence was recorded, her age .. 6 .. Spl. Case 5/2016 [Judgment] was 17 years, however, she has not stated her birth date. Even her brother PW.2 Ganesh Mahadev Asawale, has also not stated the birth date of the victim/informant nor the Investigating Officer collected any evidence or proof regarding the birth date of the victim to show that she was below 18 years of her age in view of Sec. 2(d) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. There is only evidence of the victim who has vaguely stated her age at 17 years while recording her evidence in her title clause. In absence of any such proof of age of the victim, I hold that she was minor below 18 years of age on the date of the incident i.e., 7/8/2015 as the defence has not seriously challenged her age. Hence, I answer the point No.1 in the affirmative. AS TO POINT NO.2 TO 4 :­ 11. The best witness is the victim to depose about the incident in absence of his brother (PW.2) Ganesh Mahadev Asawale to whom she had disclosed about the incident but he is not direct witness. The victim being minor and in view of Sec.37 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, the trial was conducted in camera under child ­ friendly atmosphere. The age of the victim was 17 years at the relevant time and hence, she was of the age of understanding, therefore an oath was administered to her considering her age and maturity of understanding. 12. A victim though tendered her evidence that in the year 2015 she was studying in 11th standard in Art faculty in R.K.T. College, Ulhasnagar in RKT college but she has denied that she had an acquaintance with the accused nor the alleged incident .. 7 .. Spl. Case 5/2016 [Judgment] tookplace on 7/8/2015 at 3:30 p.m. at the college gate nor the accused teased her or asked her to have a photograph with him nor he wonk his eyes towards her. She has admitted her signature on the FIR at Exh.14, but denied the contents therein portion marked A & B. 13. PW­2 Ganesh is the brother of the victim who has deposed somehow same as deposed by the victim. He has also denied any incident occurred with the victim which alleged to have been disclosed to him immediately after the incident and reaching at her home. PW­3 PSO PSI Shri.Kedar though proved portion marked A & B in the FIR(Exh.14) at Exh.18 & 19, however, the victim has denied the contents of her FIR in toto. He has tried to explain the delay in lodging the FIR by stating that the victim was frightened and hence she could not lodge FIR promptly. This fact has also been mentioned in the FIR Exh.14, however, the victim has denied the contents therein in toto. 14. The last witness is IO PSI, Smt. Punam Jadhav who has proved the portion marked A & B of the witness PW­2 Ganesh at Exh.21 & 22 but he has also denied the contents of his statement given by him. She has further brought on record that the victim did not co­operate in the investigation and she refused to give her statement under Sec. 164 of Cr.P.C. Though she has verified the attendance of the victim in the college on 7/8/2015 but the attendance was not compulsory and hence she did not produce any certificate to that effect alongwith the chargesheet. .. 8 .. Spl. Case 5/2016 [Judgment] 15. As the victim and her brother both have denied their version in toto, there is nothing on record to hold that the accused is guilty of any of the charges levelled against him. Further, though the learned APP cross examined these two witnesses with the permission of the Court after declaring them hostile but nothing fruitful come on record to believe their testimony from any angle. Absolutely there is nothing on record to hold that the accused used criminal force by holding the hand of the victim insisting to her to have a photograph with him and outraged her modesty nor he attempted to contact with the victim for personal interaction repeatedly and whistled and then wonk his eyes towards her and she was subjected to sexual harassment, etc. 16. Considering the circumstances under which the FIR of the victim came to be registered seems to be out of the friendship in between her and the accused. 17. Today teenagers are exposed to more sex related issues and lot of material is also available to them. 18. As the ingredients required to constitute the offence the knowledge plays important role than that of deliberate intention. The further requirement is that the person assaulted must a woman, that the accused must use criminal force on her and that the criminal force must have been used on that woman intending thereby to outrage her modesty as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Pramia Vs. State of Rajisthan [(2008) 4 Crimes 126 (S.C.)]. In view of settled position of law merely .. 9 .. Spl. Case 5/2016 [Judgment] because asking about the friendship by the accused to the victim will not fall within the purview of offence punishable under Sec. 354 of I.P.C. for want of further requirement such as criminal force on her and such force must have been used on her intending thereby to outrage her modesty. In order to constitute the offence under Sec. 354 of I.P.C. mere knowledge that the modesty of a woman is likely to be outraged is sufficient without any deliberate intention of having such outrage alone for its object. The essential ingredients of the offence are that the person assaulted must be a woman; that the accused must have used criminal force on her and that the criminal force must have been used on that woman intending thereby to outrage her modesty. Therefore, at any stage of imagination it cannot be said that the accused committed the offence punishable under Sec. 354 of I.P.C. 19. To attract the offence punishable under Sec.354­D it is necessary for the prosecution to prove that the accused followed or attempted to contact a woman to foster personal interaction repeatedly despite a clear indication of disinterest by such woman, however, proviso (iii) is an exception which speaks that 'in the particular circumstances such conduct was reasonable and justified'. There is no evidence on record to attract the offence punishable under Sec. 509 of IPC and the Sec. 12 of POCSO, 2012 to hold the accused guilty. Hence, I answer the point Nos.2 to 4 in the negative. .. 10 .. Spl. Case 5/2016 [Judgment] 20. Resultantly, I hold that the prosecution has utterly failed to prove the charges levelled against the accused by adducing cogent and reliable evidence and hence the accused deserves to be acquitted, and as such, I proceed to pass the following order : ORDER i) Accused Aakash Pralhad Sonavane is hereby acquitted vide Section 235(1) of Cr.P.C. of the offences punishable under Sections 354, 354­D & 509 of I.P.C. and Section 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. ii) His bail bonds stand cancelled. iii) The accused shall execute his P.R. of Rs.15,000/­ to appear before the Higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect of appeal filed against this judgment as per Sec. 437­A of Cr.P.C. iv) Such bail shall remain in force for six months from today. Kalyan. [M.J.Mirza] Dt.:­27/2/2017. Special Judge, Under Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, Kalyan.

:ORDER BELOW EXH.1 IN ANTI. BAIL APPLN. NO. 49/2017: 1. Read application and say of the prosecution. Perused documents. Heard both learned advocates. 2. This is an application for anticipatory bail under section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 3. Crime bearing No.I 03/2017 is registered against this accused Prakash Mane and other accused persons in Ambernath police station for the offence punishable under section 354, 34 of the Indian Penal Code and under section 3(1)(x) of the S.C. and S.T (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989. As this accused apprehend his arrest in that crime by Ambernath police, he has filed this application for anticipatory bail. 4. Allegation against this accused is that on 02/01/2017 brother of complainant Shivani Tak namely Kunal came on his motor cycle in front of the gate of their house. At that time one Sanju Mane came there. On account of previous quarrel he started abusing him. Exchange of words took place between them. At that time Atul Mane and his elder brother i.e. the present applicant came there. They started beating Kunal. Atul beat Kunal by iron pipe and this accused beat Kunal by hockey stick. Complainant went to intervene the quarrel. At that time accused Sanju pressed her breast and outraged her modesty. Accused Sanju also said that, “ Hkaxh yksx gS] ;g D;k dj ysaxs**- Thus, he humiliated the complainant in the public on account of her caste. And therefore, she lodged complainant against this accused and others and crime is registered. 5. In this application, it is the say of this applicant/accused that accused Sanju has filed complaint against 2 A.B.A. No.49/2017 Order Exh.1 complainant and her family members for the offence punishable under section 323, 452, 427, 147, 148, 149 of the I.P.C. and the crime is registered in Ambernath police station as C.R. No.02/2017. Thereafter to give counter blast to that complaint this false complaint is filed. This accused has committed no offence. Provisions of the S.C. and S.T. ( Prevention of Atrocities) Act 1989 are not applicable. They do not attract. Nothing is to be seized from this accused. Nothing is to be interrogated with him. This accused is doing service in reputed company. If he is arrested by police his reputation will me maligned. His prestige will be lowered down in the society. He is innocent and falsely roped in the offence. To use as a tactics this false complaint is filed. And therefore, he prayed that he be released on bail. 6. This application is strongly opposed by the prosecution. It is the contention of prosecution that hockey stick is to be recovered from this accused. Anticipatory bail cannot be granted to this accused in view of the provisions of the S.C. and S.T. (Prevention of Atrocities)Act, 1989. There is possibility of repeating the same offence by this accused. And therefore, prosecution prayed that application be rejected. 7. After going through the complaint, it appears that prima facie the provisions of S.C. and S.T. (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 are not attracted in the given facts and circumstances of the case. However, there is specific allegation in the complaint that this accused beat Kunal by Hockey stick. Definitely there is recovery from this accused. At least I.O. has to carry custodial interrogation with this accused in respect of that recovery. And for that purpose custody of this accused is 3 A.B.A. No.49/2017 Order Exh.1 must. Because unless the custody of this accused is given, the I.O. will be helpless to carry forward the further investigation. Whether the complaint is false or true will be decided at the time of decision. It is true that there are counter complaints against each other. At this stage there is no reason to say that one complaint is true and another complaint is false. Both complaints are to be investigated and the culprits are to be brought to the book. For that, ample opportunity of investigation is to be given to the I.O. And therefore, considering the fact that something is to be recovered from this accused as per allegation in the complaint, it is not just and proper to grant anticipatory bail to this accused. And hence, I pass the following order. : ORDER : 1. Application stands rejected. 2. The applicant Prakash Suresh Mane is directed to surrender before the I.O. immediately. 3. Copy of this order be sent to concerned police station for information. Date: 27/01/2017 ( D.S. Hatarote) Kalyan. Addl. Sessions Judge, Kalyan.

ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN CRI. ANTI. BAIL APPLN. NO. 52/2017 Manoj Aagare ...Applicant Vs State of Mah.
