No. I­305/2016 registered with Ulhasnagar Police Station punishable under Sections 452, 324, 323 r.w. 34 of IPC and Sections 7, 8 of POCSO Act. 2] It reveals from the allegations of the FIR that applicant Manoj along­with his brother Mukesh entered into the house of victim – girl and tried to outrage her modesty by touching her body part indecently. Said brothers have assaulted the parents of victim girl when they arrived on the spot on the cry raised by the victim girl. Hence this offence. 3] The applicant came with the case that, the complainant­family and the family of applicant are having cross terms and they developed long standing criminal enmity between them. On the day of incidence, the mother of the applicant sustained bodily injury as the member of the complainant – family gave dash to her by his vehicle. Thus, counter FIR came to be lodged while each other. It is stated that the complainant – family has tried to exaggerate the offence projecting the minor girl of the family in the alleged assault. Therefore, the applicant/accused is apprehending un necessary arrest in this concocted story. Hence prayed for pre­arrest relief. 2 4] This application is strongly opposed by the prosecution and the complainant – family being intervener. It is submitted that the minor girl studying in 10 th standard is the victim of this crime. She is assaulted by the applicant while behaving with her in indecent manner. If they are released or protected from arrest then there is every possibility of pressurising the victim girl and her family members. The photographs of the injured girl are produced to substantiate the apprehension, and prayed for rejection. 5] Heard both the sides and gone through the criminal complaints lodged by either of the parties against each other. It is tried to demonstrate by Ld. Counsel Smt. Sudha Joshi on behalf of applicant that the complainant­ family itself is having criminal background including the commission of heanious offence like PITTA. The minor girl studying in 10th standard is projected to gather sympathy and to exaggerate the alleged nature of crime. In such situation, if the applicant/accused is sent behind bar, it would cause injustice to him in such after thought implication. Infact, counter FIR filed by applicant/accused is regarding earlier incidence, but the applicant and his brother are being unnecessarily harassed on this false story. Hence, prayed for protection. 6] On the other hand, the Ld., APP Smt. Bhamre Patil assisted by Ld. Counsel S.R. Pillaye submitted that the photographs filed on record is enough prima facie evidence to 3 constitute the act attributed by applicant/accused along­with his brother. The applicant/accused – family is having criminal background if they are left scotfree then there is every possibility of tampering of evidence and pressurising the victim­complainant who is going to attend forthcoming S.S.C.Examination in this or next month. In such situation, the applicant may not be granted the relief of pre­arrest bail. 7] On going through the allegations of the FIR and counter FIR, supported with criminal background record of both the families, it appears that they are using criminal process of Law to play tit for tat. Both the families appears to be equally responsible for their continuous criminal enmity resulted into filing various prosecutions and N.C. Complaints against each other. In such scenerio, the nature of alleged offence is liable to be considered on the backdrop of the minor age of the victim­girl who is going to appear for forthcoming S.S.C.Examination. I do agree the nature of offences alleged in the FIR shows that there was quarrel between two families in which the minor girl sustained forehead injury in that assault. Moreover, it reveals from the allegations regarding outrage of modesty that complainant – family has tried to exaggerate the incidence. In such situation, considering the examination period of the victim girl, it would be proper if the applicant/accused is directed to keep himself away from his residential house which is neighbouring to the house of complainant till the S.S.C. Examination are over, then it would be justifiable to consider 4 the application for grant of anticipatory bail. It reveals from record that while granting interim relief, some conditions were imposed including attendance to the police station. The applicant has obeyed said conditions. In such situation, I am inclined to grant his application for anticipatory bail saddling condition to keep himself away from the complainant's vicinity till the S.S.C. Examination is over. With this conclusion, I proceed to pass the following order. : ORDER : 1] The application for grant of anticipatory bail is allowed as follows :­ a] In the event of arrest applicant/accused Manoj Aagare be released on bail on furnishing P.B. & S.B. of Rs.15,000/­. b] He is directed not to enter the vicnity of complainant's house i.e. Room No.27, Barrack No.424, near Mahakali Temple, in front of Bholenath Tower, Ulhasnagar­1, till S.S.C. Examination,2017 is over. He should co­operate with investigation agency and attend Ulhasnagar P.Stn. On every Wednesday and Sunday between 11.00 a.m. to 2.00 p.m. till the 15th April,2017. 3] Inform Concern P.Stn. accordingly. Kalyan [ S.P. Gogarkar ] Dt : 13/02/2017 Dist. Judge­4 & Addl. Sessions Judge, Kalyan

1 Spl. Case No.11/2014 [Judgment] Presented on : 20­1­2014. Registered on : 20­1­2014. Decided on : 6­12­2016. Duration : Y. M. D. 2 10 16 IN THE COURT OF SPECIAL JUDGE, KALYAN AT : KALYAN. (Presided over by : M.J.Mirza) SPECIAL CASE NO.11/2014. Exh. No. State of Maharashtra. Through : P.I. Kasara Police Station. … Complainant. Vs. Sunil Devidas Ubale, Age­21 years, Occ. Bhel business, R/at­ Room No.15, Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkarnagar, Kasara, Taluka­Shahapur, District­Thane. . .. Accused. Appearance : Spl.P.P.Shri D.V. Bhangare for the State. Advocate Shri K.B. Kakade for the accused. Offences : ­ Punishable under Section 354, 504 & 506 of the I.P.C. and Section 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. :JUDGMENT: (Delivered in open Court on 6/12/2016) 1. The accused Sunil Devidas Ubale is facing the trial for the offences punishable under Sections 354, 504 & 506 of I.P.C. and Section 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2 Spl. Case No.11/2014 [Judgment] 2012, alleging that the accused outraged the modesty of the minor victim aged 16 years by uttering filthy or abusing words with an intention that such word should be heard by her and also insulted and committed criminal intimidation by threatening her. 2. The case of the prosecution, in short runs as under : The victim, aged about 16 years is residing with her parents, sister and brother and his father is serving in PWD at Kasara. In the year 2012 she was studying in 11th standard at Hardi, in higher education school. She was knowing the accused, resident of Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Nagar, Kasara as he used to follow her while proceeding to her college. Initially, she was neglecting him but he was continuously following her and was attempting to meet her. Sometimes he used to say to love him and should keep love relations with him by holding her hand but she used to refuse him and therefore he used to abuse him. The accused is of gunda nature person, therefore she kept quite many times and then disclosed the incident to her parents who tried him to give understanding but invain. Because of the terror of the accused, she discontinued her college education. She did not lodge the FIR to avoid her defamation. 3. On 15/8/2013 at 10:30 a.m. she had gone to mobile shop to recharge her cell phone on the main road Kishor Mobile shop at Kasara. Her mobile was recharged. At that time the accused arrived there and asked her whose cell phone she recharged as she has no cell phone. By saying so he uttered obscene words and caught hold her hand and then started using filthy language due to which her modesty was outraged. He also abused and threatened her. Then she returned to her home and disclosed the incident to her parents and then approached to the police 3 Spl. Case No.11/2014 [Judgment] station to lodge the FIR. 4. PSO PN Shri. Vasave was on duty on 15.8.2013 at 5.17 p.m. who recorded the FIR (Exh.12) of the victim and registered the crime at C.R.No.I­62/2013 under Sec.354, 504 & 506 of IPC and Sec.12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 5. P.W.4 API Sunil Tanaji Bachhao was attached to Kasara police station as PSI who received the investigation as per the directions of his superior. He drew the spot panchanama (Exh.10) in the presence of victim, her mother and two panch witnesses. He recorded the statement of the witnesses. Then he collected the bonafide certificate of the victim and the accused from Z.P school, Kasara at Exh.22 and 23. On 15.8.2013 at 8:05 p.m. he arrested the accused under arrest panchanama (Exh.24). The birth date of the victim was 27.4.1994. After completion of investigation, he filed the chargesheet in this Special Court. 6. Charge at Exh.6 was framed by me against the accused, which was read over and explained to him in vernacular. The accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. His defence is of false involvement as per his statement recorded under Section 313 of Code of Criminal Procedure. Neither the accused stepped into the witness­box nor examined any defence witness. 7. Heard learned Spl. P.P. Shri D.V. Bhangare for the State and learned Advocate Shri. K. B. Kapare for the accused, at length. 8. The following points arise for my determination and my findings 4 Spl. Case No.11/2014 [Judgment] thereon are recorded against them for the reasons to follow:­ Points Findings 1. Whether the prosecution proved that the victim is minor aged 16 years ? .. Yes. 2. Whether the prosecution has proved that on 15.8.2013 at 10:30 a.m. on main road, Kasaragaon, in a mobile shop of Kishor Mobile Shop, used criminal force to minor victim girl, aged 16 years, intending to outrage her modesty, punishable under Sec.354 of the IPC ? .. Not proved. 3. Whether the prosecution has proved that at the relevant date, time and place the accused intentionally abused in filthy language and insulted the informant/victim girl intending or knowing that such insult would likely to cause breach of public peace, punishable .. Not proved. under Sec.504 of IPC? 4. Whether the prosecution has proved that at the relevant date, time and place the accused committed criminal intimidation by threatening victim girl with intent to cause alarm to her, punishable under .. Not proved. Sec.506 of IPC ? 5. Whether the prosecution has proved that 5 Spl. Case No.11/2014 [Judgment] at the relevant date, time and place, the accused used to repeatedly and constantly followed or watched or contacted the victim girl directly and uttered words with the intention that it would be heard by the victim and caused sexual harassment to her, punishable under Sec.12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, . . Not proved. 2012? 6. What order ? .. Accused acquitted. : REASONS : 9. To substantiate the charge, prosecution has examined in all four witnesses, viz. PW.1 Smt. Bharti Malhari Jadhav (Exh.9), the mother of the victim and P.W.2 the victim, Smt. Chitra Suresh Khandejhod (Exh.11) who was studying in 11th standard at Hardi College and lodged the FIR at Exh.12. P.W.3­Kishor Madhukar Choure (Exh.14) the mobile shop owner who runs the shop under the name and style as 'Shri Ganesh Mobile Shoppe' and he used to open the shop at 7.30 a.m. and closes at 9 p.m. In addition to recharge of mobile phones he also used to repair the mobile phones. The last witness P.W.4, I.O. API­Sunil Tanaji Bacchao (Exh.18) who carried out the investigation and arrested the accused. After registering the crime by PSO PN Shri. Vasave on the basis of the FIR lodged by the victim. As to point No. 1 : 10. The victim has brought on record in her testimony that on 15.8.2013 at 10.30 a.m. she had gone to recharge the cell phone in Kishor Mobile shop and at that time the accused arrived there and 6 Spl. Case No.11/2014 [Judgment] abused her. Neither the victim girl nor her mother PW1­Smt. Bharti brought on record the birth date of the victim. The FIR is also silent regarding the birth date of the victim. However, the IO has produced the bonafide certificate of the victim at Exh.22 as her birth date as 14.5.1997 issued by Head Master Z.P. School, Kasara, Taluka­Shahapur, Dist­Thane dated 10.10.2013. At the relevant time the victim was studying in 7th standard. 11. The alleged date of incident seems to have occurred on 15.8.2013 on the main road, Kasara. In view of the bonafide certificate of the victim at Exh.22 dated 10.10.2013 her birth date shown as 14.5.1997. Therefore, on the date of incident, the exact age of the victim was 15 years, 3 months & 1 day. Section 2(d) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 “child” means any person below the age of 18 years. Therefore, I hold that the victim was child within the meaning of Sec.2(d) of the Act at the time of alleged incident and was below 18 years of her age. Hence, I answer the point No.1, in the affirmative. As to point No.2 to 5 :­ 12. In order to constitute the offence under Sec. 354 of I.P.C. mere knowledge that the modesty of a woman is likely to be outraged is sufficient without any deliberate intention of having such outrage alone for its object. The essential ingredients of the offence are that the person assaulted must be a woman; that the accused must have used criminal force on her and that the criminal force must have been used on that woman intending thereby to outrage her modesty. 13. As the ingredients required to constitute the offence the 7 Spl. Case No.11/2014 [Judgment] knowledge plays important role than that of deliberate intention. The further requirement is that the person assaulted must a woman, that the accused must use criminal force on her and that the criminal force must have been used on that woman intending thereby to outrage her modesty as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Pramia Vs. State of Rajisthan [(2008) 4 Crimes 126 (S.C.)]. In view of settled position of law merely because asking about the friendship by the accused to the victim will not fall within the purview of offence punishable under Sec. 354 of I.P.C. for want of further requirement such as criminal force on her and such force must have been used on her intending thereby to outrage her modesty. Therefore, at any stage of imagination it cannot be said that the accused committed the offence punishable under Sec. 354 of I.P.C. 14. For the offence punishable under Sec.12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 the basic requirement is that of sexual harassment as enumerated one of the Acts mentioned in Sec.11 of the Act. An utterances of any word or makes any sound, gesture, exhibits any object etc. 15. For the purpose of the offence punishable under Sec.504 of I.P.C. intentional insult and giving provocation knowing it that it would cause him to break the public peace or to commit any offence. Further, criminal intimidation with threat to cause death or grievous hurt is required for the purpose of the offence punishable under Section 506 of I.P.C. Though the prosecution has examined the victim, who lodged the FIR at Exh.12, her mother Smt. Bharti Jadhav (PW.2) at Exh.9, however, both these witnesses have not supported the case of the prosecution by any means. The victim on the contrary has put­forth her 8 Spl. Case No.11/2014 [Judgment] case that she has compromised the matter with the accused who is residing in the same village. It appears that she is married having a daughter, therefore, she is not willing to proceed with the accused. 16. The witness Kishor Madhukar Chaure (PW.3) is the mobile shop owner and runs 'Ganesh Mobile Shopee' at Kasara but he has denied any incident occurred in his shop or any person had caught­hold the hand of any girl nor spoke any obscene language with her when the girl was in his shop. This witness knows the accused present before the Court as he is resident of Kasara. 17. The last witness is PW.4 I.O. Shri Sunil Tanaji Bacchao who carried out the investigation as usual and produced the bonafide certificate of the victim at Exh.22 and accused at Exh.23. He recorded the statements of the witnesses and arrested the accused under arrest form at Exh.24. The FIR of the victim was recorded by P.N. Shri Vasave and not by any lady staff, though as far as practically her statement was required to be recorded by a woman police officer not below the rank of sub­inspector as required under Sec.24 of the Act. 18. It is seen that the evidence of all the witnesses is not useful for the prosecution who never fulfills any of the essential ingredients of any of the offence levelled against the accused. None of them have brought any incriminating circumstances against the accused to hold him guilty for the offences. Under the circumstances, I hold that the prosecution has utterly failed to prove the charges levelled against them by adducing cogent, reliable and trustworthy evidence. Hence, I answer the point No.2 to 5, in the negative. 9 Spl. Case No.11/2014 [Judgment] 19. Resultantly, the accused deserves to be acquitted, and as such, I proceed to pass the following order : ORDER i) Accused Sunil Devidas Ubale is hereby acquitted vide Section 235(1) of Cr.P.C. of the offences punishable under Sections 354, 504 & 506 of IPC and Section 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. ii) His bail bonds stand cancelled. iii) The accused shall execute his P.R. of Rs.15,000/­ to appear before the Higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect of appeal filed against this judgment as per S. 437­A of Cr.P.C. iv) Such bail shall remain in force for six months from today. Kalyan, [M.J.Mirza] Dt.:­6/12/2016. Special Judge, Under Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, Kalyan.

1 Spl. Case 12/2014 [Judgment] Presented on : 20.1.2014. Registered on : 20.1.2014. Decided on : 9.3.2016. Duration : Y. M. D. 2. 1. 19. IN THE COURT OF SPECIAL JUDGE, KALYAN AT : KALYAN. [Presided over by : M.J.Mirza] SPECIAL CASE NO.12/2014. Exh. No. The State of Maharashtra. Through : P.I. Shahapur Police Station. ...Complainant. Vs. Prakash Gopinath Masane Age­33 Years, Occ. Driver, R/at­ Sapgaon, Belwadi, Tal. Shahapur, Dist.­ Thane. ….Accused. Appearance : Spl.P.P.Smt. J.S.Lohakare for the State. Advocate Shri K.B.Kakade for the accused. Offences : ­ Punishable under Section 354 of I.P.C. and Section 7 r/w 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. :JUDGMENT: (Delivered 9/3/2016, in the open Court) 1. The accused Prakash Gopinath Masane is facing the trial for the offences punishable under Section 354 of I.P.C. and Section 7 r/w 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2. The case of the prosecution, in short is as under : 2 Spl. Case 12/2014 [Judgment] That the victim aged 13 years is residing with her father, brother, younger sister and step mother Malti at Sapgaon. She is taking education. Her father ply auto­rickshaw. She studied in Z.P. School upto 6th standard and his brother Ajay is studying in 8th standard. Her younger sister is studying in 4th standard. 3. Her mother died before one year, therefore, her father performed second marriage with Malti. She used to go to school at 10 a.m. and return at 5 p.m. Her father plies auto­rickshaw from 9 a.m. to 9 p.m. Till arrival of her father they make wait and then take meal and went to bed. She alongwith brother Ajay and younger sister used to sleep in the first room, however, her parents in the second room. 4. In the first week of September, her step mother had gone to her maternal home, at 8 p.m. she took meal and were waiting for her father. At 9 p.m. her father arrived with autorickshaw but he did not take meal. They all slept in the first room and her father also slept with them. At 12 mid­night her father woke­up and he made her to wake­up and told her to make bed for him inside the room. Therefore, she made bed for him, however, he asked to sleep inside the room and hence, she slept with her father. Then her father started kissing her, moving his hand on her body and also pressed her breast. When she woke­up, he threatened her that she should not shout or else he will kill her. Due to fear she kept mum. Then her father by moving her hand on her person and started kissing her, she raised shouts suddenly and started crying. Even though her father did not leave her. Her brother who was sleeping in the first room woke up and told to her father that he should leave her and then her father left her. Her father threatened her and her brother not to disclose the incident to any one or else he would kill them. Due to fear they did 3 Spl. Case 12/2014 [Judgment] not approach to the police. At the time of Gatasthapana, Smt. Jijabai Baswant of village Kutghar, who is the maternal aunt of her mother had come to village Sapgaon to take her and her younger sister. Therefore, she alongwith her younger sister accompanied with her to Kutghar and then she disclosed the incident to her grandmother Jijabai about the incident of her father. Then she approached to Shahapur Police with her grandmother Jijabaid and lodged the FIR against her father (accused). 5. PSO, P.S.I. Shri Sandeep Patil of Shahapur Police Station recorded the FIR and registered the crime at C.R. No.I­218/2013, under Section 354 of I.P.C and Section 7 r/w 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Further investigation was entrusted to PW.2 P.I. Shri Vijay Sadashiv Patil, who was A.P.I. at that time and carried out the investigation. He drew the spot panchanama (Exh.11) and arrested the accused on the very day. He recorded the statements of the witnesses and after completion of investigation filed the chargesheet in this Court. 6. Charge vide Exh.5 was framed by me which was read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. The accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. His defence is of false involvement as per his statement recorded under Section 313 of Code of Criminal Procedure. Neither the accused stepped into the witness­box nor he adduced the evidence of any defence witness. 7. Heard learned Spl. P.P. Smt. J. S. Lohokare for the State and learned Advocate Shri K.B.Kakade for the accused, at length. 8. The following points arise for my determination and my findings 4 Spl. Case 12/2014 [Judgment] thereon are recorded against them for the reasons to follow:­ Points Findings 1. Whether the prosecution proved that the victim is minor aged 13 years ? .. Yes. 2. Whether prosecution has proved that in the first week of September, 2013, at Sapgaon, Belwadi, in the house of the informant/ victim, the accused used criminal force to minor victim , aged 13 years intending to .. Not proved. outrage her modesty, punishable under S.354 of I.P.C.? 3. Whether the prosecution has proved that at the relevant time, the accused committed sexual assault on the minor victim, aged 13 years, with sexual intent touched her breast involving physical contact without penetration, punishable under S. 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 ? .. Not proved. 4. What order ? ….. Accused acquitted. : REASONS : 9. To substantiate the charge, the prosecution has examined in all two witnesses, viz. PW.1 minor victim/informant at Exh.­9, who has proved her signature on the FIR (Exh.10) but denied the contents therein in toto. P.I. PW.2, Shri Vijay Sadashiv Patil, the I.O. at Exh.­12 who carried out the investigation as usual after arresting the accused and filed the chargesheet. The defence has admitted the spot panchanama at Exh.11. 5 Spl. Case 12/2014 [Judgment] As to point No.1 :­ 10. The trial of this case was taken in camera. On initial enquiry with the victim she gave rational answers and hence, an oath was administered to her. 11. She has deposed that her age is 15 years but she has not stated her birth date. The investigating officer has also not collected the proof of her birth date from the concerned school where the victim was studying. Therefore, in absence of such proof of age of the victim I have to believe and accept her age as 15 years as defence has not challenged her age in any manner. Therefore, I answer the point No.1 in the affirmative. As to point No.2 & 3 :­ 12. I have taken both these points together as they are interlinked and to avoid repetition. The case putforth by the prosecution is that the accused is the father of the victim who was residing with them and the step mother, brother and sister at Sapgaon and studied upto 7 th standard in Z.P. school at Sapgaon. It is seen that the accused performed the second marriage after the accidental death of his first wife, the natural mother of the victim. 13. According to her the incident occurred when she was studying in 7th standard but she is unable to tell the exact date and time. At the relevant time she alongwith her brother and sister were only present in the house as her step mother had gone to her maternal home. She has specifically stated that no such incident had occurred with her at any time. She assigned the reason of lodging the FIR was that she was willing to go to her grandmother's home but accused was not allowing 6 Spl. Case 12/2014 [Judgment] her. She identified her signature on her FIR (Exh.10) and denied the contents therein in toto. Though the Ld. A.P.P. has cross examined this witness at length but nothing fruitful has been brought on record establishing the nexus of the accused with the alleged incident of outraging her modesty and sexual assault. According to the victim the accused who is the father was addicted to liquor and he was arrested after the incident. The accused used to provide her maintenance including her grandmother Jijabai. She has no grievances against the accused as she has settled her grievances out of the Court. 14. The investigating officer PW.2 P.I. Shri Vijay Sadashiv Patil has carried out the investigation as usual and stated that a lady police officer was present in the police station when the FIR of the victim came to be recorded and then crime was registered. 15. Absolutely there is nothing on record to hold that the accused had outraged the modesty of the victim at any time or committed sexual assault with sexual intend by touching the part of the body of the victim. The purpose of lodging the FIR seems to be that the accused disallowed the victim to go to the house of her grandmother Jijabai. Thus, there is nothing on record to hold that the accused has committed the alleged offences levelled against him. Hence, I hold that the prosecution has miserably failed to prove the charges levelled against the accused by adducing cogent, reliable and trustworthy evidence. Hence, I answer the point Nos. 2 & 3 in the negative. 16. Resultantly, the accused deserves to be acquitted, and as such, I proceed to pass the following order : 7 Spl. Case 12/2014 [Judgment] ORDER i] Accused Prakash Gopinath Masane is hereby acquitted vide Sec. 235(1) of Cr.P.C. of the offences punishable under Sections 354 of I.P.C. & Section 7 r/w 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. ii] His bail bonds stand cancelled. iii] The accused shall execute his P.R. of Rs.15,000/­ to appear before the Higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect of appeal filed against this judgment as per S. 437­A of Cr.P.C. iv] Such bail shall remain in force for six months from today. Kalyan. [M.J.Mirza] Dt.:­9/3/2016. Special Judge, Under Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, Kalyan.

Received on : 27-01-2014. Registered on: 27-01-2014 Decided on : 17-11-2016. Duration: 02Y 10 M 21 D IN THE COURT OF THE ADDL. SESSIONS JUDGE -2 AT KALYAN ( Before : D.S. Hatarote, Additional Sessions Judge-2, Kalyan) Special Case No. 16/2014 Exh.No.__ The state of Maharashtra Through Kalyan Taluka Police Station, .. Prosecution VERSUS Gurunath Ram Mali, Age – 23 years, R/at : At/Post- Ghotsai, Taluka- Kalyan, District- Thane. .. Accused Offences : U/Sec. 452, 354, 323 of the Indian Penal Code and section 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Appearances: ==================================== Smt. Bhoir, A.P.P. for State Shri. I. M. Thakur, Advocate for the accused ==================================== (2) J U D G M E N T. ( Delivered in open court on 17th November 2016 ) 1. This accused is prosecuted by the State through Kalyan Taluka Police Station, for the offence punishable U/Sec. 452, 354, 323 of the Indian Penal Code and under section 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Prosecution case in short is as follows: 2. One Sayali Gaikwad was residing alongwith her parents and brother at Ghotsai, Taluka-Kalyan. Incident took place on 02/01/2014 at about 2.00 p.m. in the house of complainant Sayali at Ghotsai. At the alleged time of incident this Sayali was 16 years old and was taking education in the 9th standard. As usual at about 1.00 p.m. she returned home from her school. Her parents were in the house. At about 1.30 p.m. parents of complainant Sayali left the house for Titwala in order to prepare Adhar Card. Sayali alone was in the house. After taking meals she was cleaning the utensils in the kitchen. At that time accused Gurunath Mali forcibly entered in her house. Sayali asked him what he want. He put latch of the door from inside, with sexual intention he hugged Sayali, he removed her veil and put his hand on her chest. Accused put one hand on the mouth of Sayali. When Sayali tried to shout, he beat her by fists blows and stretched her hair. Meanwhile mother of complainant Sayali came and she knocked the door. At that time this accused gave threat to (3) Spl. Case No.16/2014 (J) complainant Sayali saying that if she disclose the incident to anybody he will kill her. Thereafter accused opened the latch and in presence of her mother ran way. Then parents of the complainant came in the house. Complainant stated the incident to them. Thereafter parents of Sayali came to police station Kalyan Taluka and lodged complaint. Crime was registered as C.R. No. I 06/2014 against this accused for the offence punishable under section 452, 354, 323, 506 of the I.P.C. and under section 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 3. Investigation was carried by one Jyoti Hibare, then P.S.I. On 02/01/2014 she recorded statements of 4 witnesses. She sent victim Sayali to medical alongwith Yadi. She prepared spot panchanama on next day. Then she prepared rough sketch of the spot of offence which is attached to the spot panchanama. She obtained bonafide certificate of the victim. On 03/01/2014 she recorded statements of other witnesses. On 04/01/2014 she arrested the accused and produced before the Magistrate. She obtained injury certificate of the victim. After completion of the investigation she submitted chargesheet against the accused in the court. 4. After committal of this case to the Sessions court, accused appeared. Charge against him is framed at Exh.10. Charge was read over and explained to him in Marathi language. He pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. His defence seems to be that there was love affair (4) between he himself and the victim. Even prior to incident 3-4 times he had been to the house of victim. On the day of incident victim herself gave phone call and informed this accused that she is alone in the house and asked him to come to her house. And therefore, he went there. However, parents of the victim returned much earlier before expected time. After opening the door parents of victim beat this accused as well as Sayali. The parents of the victim put pressure on the victim and forced her to lodge the complaint. This is the defence of the accused. 5. Prosecution was directed to prove its case. In response to that prosecution examined in all 5 witnesses in this case. P.W. No.1 is the victim at Exh.12. She deposed as per her complaint which is at Exh.13. She stated on oath that at the time of incident accused illegally entered in her house, closed the door from inside and put the latch. He hugged her. He removed her veil and put his hand on her chest. He put one hand on the mouth of victim so that she should not shout. Remaining incident also deposed by her as per the prosecution story. She specifically deposed that at the time of incident she was 16 years old. P.W. No.2 Vandana Gaikwad is mother of victim. She deposed that on the day of incident she and her husband had been to Titwala for preparing Adhar Card. Their daughter victim was alone in the house. Much time was not required in preparation of Adhar Card. And therefore, they immediately returned home. She further deposed that when she came in front of the door of her house, she heard (5) Spl. Case No.16/2014 (J) sound of weeping of victim. And therefore, she vicariously knocked the door. When doors were opened and the accused came out of the house, gave dash to her and ran away. She tried to catch the accused, but he succeeded to rescue. Thereafter she inquired with the victim and victim told the entire incident. P.W. No.3 Ramabai Gaikwad is alleged eye witness at Exh.17. She deposed that on the day of incident at about 2.30 p.m. she was in her courtyard. She heard commotion from the house of P.W. No.2 Vandana. And therefore, she went there. At that time P.W. No.2 Vandana told her that accused Gurunath Mali had been to her house in their absence and when their daughter was alone in the house. She further told this witness that as soon as door was opened accused ran away. P.W. No.4 Dr. Neeta Bhagwat is a medical officer who examined victim on 02/01/2014 and found some contusions on occipital region on left side and abrasion over left shoulder and right hand of the victim. She proved the injury certificate which is at Exh.19. P.W. No.5 Jyoti Hibare is the Investigating Officer. She narrated investigation and stated that as there was sufficient evidence against this accused she submitted chargesheet against this accused. 6. Statement of the accused under section 313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is recorded. This accused denied the incriminating facts put to him. However, during the answer of last question he stated that on the day of incident victim herself called him to her house. He and the (6) victim were talking to each other. At that time mother of victim came there. Victim became frightened. After opening the door parents of victim entered into the house. They beat him and victim Sayali. They bumped Sayali's head on wall. Due to force by the parents victim has filed false complaint. No evidence is adduced by the accused. 7. I have gone through oral and documentary evidence on record. I have heard both the learned advocates at length. 8. Following points arise for my consideration. My findings on those points are as follows for the reasons stated below. POINTS FINDINGS 1) Does prosecution prove that on 02/01/2014 at about 2.00 p.m. accused committed tresspass by entering into the house of complainant Sayali Gaikwad used as a human dwelling having prepared to commit sexual assault on complainant and thereby committed an offence punishable No. under section 452 of the I.P.C.? 2) Does prosecution further prove that on the above-said date, time and place this accused used criminal force against the complainant intending to outrage her modesty and thereby committed an offence punishable No. under section 354 of the I.P.C. (7) Spl. Case No.16/2014 (J) POINTS FINDINGS 3) Does prosecution further prove that on the above said date, time and place while outraging the modesty of complainant this accused beat her by fists blows and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 323 of the I.P.C.? No. 4) Does prosecution further prove that on the above said date, time and place accused committed sexual assault on complainant Sayali a minor girl aged about 16 years and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 ? Yes. REASONS As to Points no. 1 to 3:- 9. Before proceeding to discuss evidence on record, I would like to mention some admitted facts here. The fact that on the date of alleged incident victim was 16 years old is not much disputed. The fact that at the time of incident victim alone was in her house is also admitted fact. The fact that at the time of incident parents of victim had been to Titwala is not much disputed. From the number of suggestions given on behalf of the accused to the prosecution witnesses, it seems that presence of this accused in the house of victim or on the spot of offence at the time of incident is also admitted, rather not disputed at (8) all. Now, in the background of these admitted facts I proceed further. In order to avoid repetition of discussion, I would like to discuss all the 3 points together. 10. Victim P.W. No.1 deposed that on the date of incident she was 16 years old and was studying in 9 th standard. Her bonafide certificate is produced on record at Exh.23 which also prove the fact that victim was 16 years old on the day of incident. This piece of evidence regarding minority of complainant on record is not at all challenged on behalf of the accused during the cross examination of either the victim P.W. No.1 or her mother P.W. No.2 Vandana or the I.O. or the medical officer. And therefore, I took this fact as proved. 11. Now, it is the contention of prosecution that accused forcibly entered into the house of victim and committed house tresspass. He hugged victim, put his hand on her chest, removed her veil and committed offence of outraging modesty of the victim. It is also contention of prosecution that when victim tried to shout, this accused beat her by fists blows and committed the offence under section 323 of the I.P.C. Per contra, it is the contention of accused that victim was his friend. On the day of incident she made phone call to him and called him to the house. He and victim both were chit-chatting. At that time parents of victim came there. Due to sudden change in scenario victim frightened. Parents of victim beat him as well as the victim and forced her to lodge the false (9) Spl. Case No.16/2014 (J) complaint. 12. Evidence of P.W. No.3 Ramabai is completely hearsay. And therefore, that is of no use for the purpose of prosecution to prove any offence against the accused. 13. Evidence of P.W. No.4 Dr. Neeta Bhagwat is of general nature. She admitted in her cross examination that the injuries allegedly found on the person of victim are possible due to fall on wall or plain surface. Her admission in the cross examination that if the victim resisted the accused for about 5 to 10 minutes forcibly then multiple injuries on her person may be possible. No such multiple injuries are found on the person of victim. And therefore, the contention of victim that she resisted the accused from doing any illegal act seems to be after thought. P.W. No.5 Jyoti Hibare is the Investigating Officer. She proved spot panchanama which is admitted by the accused. She proved police Yadi for medical as well as medical certificate. 14. The evidence of P.W. No.2 Vandana is relevant only on the point of coming out the accused from her house when she knocked the door and running away by giving dash to her. 15. Now, from this evidence on record I have to see whether prosecution succeeded to prove all these three offences against the accused beyond all reasonable doubts. (10) After scrutiny of the evidence it is revealed to me that chain of evidence against this accused to prove all these offences is not completed. Important strings in the chain are missing. It is pertinent to note that till accused entering into the house of complainant, closing the door and putting latch of the door from inside, the complainant was silent. It is nowhere brought on record that she shouted for help or she raised hue and cry for help. What she deposed that she tried to shout but accused put his hand on her mouth. It means that she never shouted during the entire offence. Admittedly incident was going about 5 to 10 minutes as narrated by complainant Sayali herself. It is not case that throughout incident the hand of accused was on her mouth. There was ample time for this complainant to raise hue and cry, but she did not. It suggests that the entry of accused in the house of complainant and further acts were with the consent of the complainant Sayali. 16. The very important thing is that except Sayali no other was known that at that particular time the parents of Sayali had been to Titwala for their work and Sayali is alone in the house. Then how this accused came to know that Sayali is alone in the house and therefore he entered in the house? It is not possible that parents of Sayali might have been informed this accused that Sayali is alone. There is no evidence on record to show that when parents of Sayali left their house this accused was wandering in the nearby vicinity. And therefore, he came (11) Spl. Case No.16/2014 (J) to know that Sayali is alone. Then the only source of information regarding loneliness of Sayali in the house remains from Sayali herself. There is every possibility and probability that Sayali herself might have been contacted accused and informed that she is alone in the house. And therefore, the accused came to her house and further incident took place with her consent. This important missing chain in the evidence strengthen the defence of the accused that with the consent of Sayali he entered into her house as there were friendly relations between them. 17. Complainant Sayali stated that accused was not acquainted with her. This statement of Sayali is false. In her complaint she has specifically stated name of this accused. Even her mother Vandana also know the accused as he is resident of same vicinity. Dr. Neeta admitted that while stating history of the injuries victim told her that accused was her brother's friend. All these admissions and facts on record indicate that this complainant was well known the accused. However, she might have been concealing this fact under the pressure of her parents. The another inference from these facts and circumstances on record can be drawn that as Sayali was acquainted with this accused, she kept mum even though this accused closed the doors and put latch from inside. 18. The story put forth by the prosecution is seems not probable at all. Generally no unknown person will dare to enter into the unknown house and outrage the modesty (12) of a girl in that house. Even Sayali would not have kept mum or silent knowing that unknown person entered in her house and closed the doors. In these facts and circumstances, the defence put forth by the accused seems more probable and possible. As per contention of accused there were friendly relations or love affair between accused and Sayali. When parents of Sayali left the house she was alone in the house. It was her expectation that her parents will not return home for about 1 and half to 2 hours. This fact is admitted by Sayali in her cross examination. And therefore, probably she might have been called accused to the house. However, her parents returned home much earlier than expected by her. They spotted the complainant and accused in the house and door closed from inside. Obviously, the natural reaction of mother of Sayali that she became angry. They might have beaten the complainant as well as the accused. All these events seems probable and possible to great extent in the given facts and circumstances. And therefore, I accept the defence of the accused in this respect. 19. It is argued by the learned APP that even though there is the consent of minor Sayali, it is not the valid consent. And therefore, offence under section 354, 452 and 323 of the I.P.C. is proved. I am not in agreement with this submission. Under section 90 of the I.P.C. consent of a minor below the age of 12 years is not the valid consent. And therefore, the consent given by the minor of 16 years old, then that can be considered in I.P.C. as the valid (13) Spl. Case No.16/2014 (J) consent. 20. Thus, there is no concrete proof to prove that the accused has committed an offnece punishable under section 452, 354, 323 of the I.P.C. When there was consent of the complainant Sayali question of assaulting her or causing hurt to her by the accused does not arise at all. Considering the fact that with the consent of minor that is complainant Sayali 16 years old accused entered in her house and hugged her and did further acts, I answer all three points in negative. AS TO POINT NO.4 : 21. Accused is charged for the offence punishable under section 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. This is the special Act. If any person with sexual intent touches the vagina, penis, anus or breast of the child or makes the child touch the vagina, penis, anus or breast of such person or any other person, or does any other act with sexual intent which involves physical contact without penetration is said to commit sexual assault. Definition of child is given in the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (Henceforth referred to as the POCSO Act, 2012), in section 2(d) of the POCSO Act, 2012 which means the person below the age of 18 years. As per section 29 of the POCSO Act, 2012 there is presumption regarding certain offences. As per that section where a person is prosecuted for committing or abetting or attempting to commit any offence under section (14) 3, 5, 7 and 9 of the Act, the Special court shall presume, that such person has committed or abetted or attempted to commit the offence, as the case may be unless the contrary is proved. In the background of this legal provision, I proceed to consider the facts of this case and the alleged offence of the accused. 22. Admittedly, on the date of incident victim Sayali was 16 years old. Presence of this accused at the spot of offence at the time of incident is admitted. It is specifically deposed by the complainant Sayali that after entering into the house this accused closed the doors, put the latch. Then he hugged her, removed her veil, put his hand on her breast. Thus, from these acts of accused stated by the complainant or victim Sayali, it is crystal clear that with sexual intent this accused hugged her, removed her veil and put his hand on her breast. Thus, all the ingredients of the offence under section 7 punishable under section 8 of the POCSO Act, 2012 are fulfilled and proved. 23. Now, I consider the contention of learned advocate for accused. It is vehemently contended by the learned advocate for accused that all these acts were done with the consent of victim Sayali as she was in friendly relations or in love affair with this accused. It is pertinent to note that the evidence of Sayali regarding the hug by accused, removal of veil and putting his hand on her breast is nowhere specifically challenged or denied in the entire (15) Spl. Case No.16/2014 (J) cross examination of the victim Sayali. Rather the contention of accused is that all this was done with the consent of Sayali. And therefore, no offence is committed by the accused. 24. I am not in agreement with this submission of learned advocate for accused. Even though all these acts were done by the accused with the consent of victim Sayali and even though we accept the same as it is, that cannot exempt this accused from punishment. Because the POCSO Act, 2012 does not recognize any consented sexual intimacy. Sexual contact between the adolescent and adult are considered as illegal in POCSO Act, 2012. No exception has been granted in the Act to an act with the consent of minor. And therefore, even though the alleged act of sexual assault is done by this accused with the consent of the complainant Sayali who was 16 years old at that time, this also amounts to an offence. Because the very intention or purpose of the POCSO Act, 2012 is to protect every child below the age of 18 years from any sort of sexual assault or sexual offence either penetrative or non penetrative. No exception in the entire Act is given for the sexual act done with the minor with the consent of the minor. And hence, offence under section 8 of the POCSO Act, 2012 is duly established. Rather it is admitted by accused through the various suggestions given to the prosecution witnesses. And therefore, I hold that prosecution has succeeded to prove the offence under section 8 of the POCSO Act, 2012. Hence, I answer point (16) No.4 in affirmative. 25. Now I take pause to hear the accused and his advocate as well as the advocate for prosecution on the point of sentence. Kalyan ( D.S. Hatarote ) Date :- 17/11/2016 Additional Sessions Judge Kalyan. 26. At this stage I recorded further statement of accused under section 313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure on the point of sentence. He submitted that this is his first offence. He is the only earning member in his family. His mother and sister are dependent on him. He prayed leniency. I heard learned APP on the point of sentence. She prayed for maximum punishment. I heard learned advocate Shri. I.M. Thakur for accused on the point of sentence. He also prayed leniency and minimum punishment as this is the first offence of this accused. 27. It is true that the alleged act of sexual assault took place with the consent of victim Sayali. However, consent is of no use while considering the offence under Special Act POCSO, 2012. The offence punishable under section 8 of the POCSO Act, 2012 against this accused is duly proved. Maximum sentence provided for the offence is which may extend to 5 years. However, there is specific mention in section 8 of the POCSO Act, 2012 that punishment which shall not be less than 3 years. It is the Legislature mandate that minimum punishment should be (17) Spl. Case No.16/2014 (J) given to the accused. Considering all these facts and circumstances, I am of the opinion that following sentence will meet the ends of justice. 28. In conclusion, I pass the following order. ORDER : 1) The accused Gurunath Ram Mali is hereby convicted for the offence punishable under section 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for three years and to pay fine of Rs.2,000/- ( Rs. Two thousand only). In default to further undergo rigorous imprisonment for three months. 2) Accused Gurunath is hereby acquitted of the offence punishable under section 452, 354, 323 of Indian Penal Code. 3) Bail Bonds of this accused stands surrendered to the Government. 4) Accused is entitled to get set-off under section 428 of the Code of Criminal Procedure if he was detained in jail during trial. 5) Accused is hereby apprised that he is at liberty to prefer appeal against this judgment and conviction order before the Hon'ble Bombay High court. 6) Copy of this judgment and conviction order be supplied to this accused free of costs. Kalyan ( D.S. Hatarote ) Date :- 17/11/2016 Additional Sessions Judge Kalyan.

REASONS : 9] To substantiate the charge, the prosecution has examined only three witnesses viz. P.W.1­ minor victim girl (Exh.15), the informant, P.W.2­ Smt. Sunita Narayan Shrirao (Exh.16), the mother of the victim girl & P.W.3­ I.O., PSI­ Shri. Dattatray Arun Landge (Exh.19), who carried out the investigation as usual. 10] As to point No. 1: The prosecution did not bring on record anything showing that the victim was minor on the date of the missing report dtd. 29/3/2013 and FIR dtd. 7/5/2013. The victim who has studied up to 9th standard in Shriganesh Vidya Mandir, Sagaon, Dombivali. She has stated her birth date as 1/8/1996, however, no documentary proof is produced on record though the investigating officer testified that he obtained the school leaving certificate from the concerned school. Even on perusal of the entire charge sheet, there is no such proof. Even assuming the birth date stated by the victim as 1/8/1996, her age on the date of missing report 6 Spl. Case 17/2014 [Judg.] dtd. 29/3/2013 was 16 years, 7 months and 28 days and hence she was minor on the date of alleged incident. Therefore, I hold that she was minor on the date of the alleged incident. Hence, I answer the point No. 1, in the affirmative. 11] As to point No. 2 & 3: For the offence punishable under S. 363 of IPC, it is necessary for the prosecution to prove “taking'' or ''enticing'' away a minor under 16 years of age, if a male and under 18 years of age, if a female. Further, ''taking'' or ''enticing'' must be out of keeping of the lawful guardian of such minor and such ''taking'' or ''enticing'' must be without consent of such guardian. 12] Where the accused was charged with kidnapping a minor girl out of the guardianship of her parents for compelling her for marriage is an offence. In order to prove this charge, though the prosecution has examined P.W.1, the victim girl and the informant, P.W.2­Sunita, the mother of the victim girl, no where whispered that the accused kidnapped the victim from her lawful guardianship by inducing to marry with her. The victim girl has denied that accused No.1 before the Court is acquainted by her & she had love affair with him. This fact was knowing by the informant herself who had given an understanding to the victim. However, on 27/3/2013 at 12 noon the victim left the house on her own accord under the pretext to go to her friend and thereafter she did not turn up. After waiting for few days, the informant initially lodged the missing report on 29/3/2013 and after gathering some information, she lodged the FIR on 7/5/2013. The accused No.2 – Saroj is the mother of accused No.1 – Vicky. The allegation of the informant as per her supplementary statement 7 Spl. Case 17/2014 [Judg.] she instigated her son Vicky to kidnap the victim for the purpose of marriage. It is also alleged in the FIR that the accused No.1 – Vicky compelled the victim girl to marry with him. 13] The substantive evidence of the victim girl is not supporting any of the version of the prosecution. On the contrary, the victim girl has stated that she left her parents home on her own accord and married with the accused No.1 – Vicky before two years. Out of the wedlock she has a female child, born on 25/9/2013, aged 2 years and at present she is conceived. She has further deposed that she left her parents home voluntarily in order to accompany with accused No.1 – Vicky. She also performed marriage with the accused No.1­Vicky voluntarily. After the marriage she was visiting her parents home but they never objected her marriage. According to her, the said marriage was performed simply. She has no grievances against any of the accused No. 1 – Vicky, her husband and accused No.2­ Saroj, her mother­in­law. 14] The informant, P.W.2­ Sunita has deposed that though her daughter left her house on 27/3/2013 but she filed missing report on 29/3/2013 and then the FIR on 7/5/2013. She also admits that her daughter has married with accused No.1 ­Vicky and out of the wedlock she has a female child and now she is conceived for second child. Now her relations with the accused are cordial. The investigating officer has carried out the investigation but DNA test report has not been filed on record. 15] The victim and the informant, both these witnesses, have given go­bye to the statement and FIR – Exh. 18 by stating that they have not narrated any contents therein but put signature on the FIR Exh.18. 8 Spl. Case 17/2014 [Judg.] Though the Ld. APP has cross examined both the witnesses on material point, but nothing fruitful has brought on record to hold the accused guilty for the offences levelled against them. Hence, I answer the point Nos. 2 & 3 in the negative. As to point Nos. 4 & 5 : 16] For all these charges, the evidence of the victim girl is material. In the substantive evidence of the victim girl, she has put forth her case that she is married and she was not kidnapped from her lawful guardianship by any of the accused. Even the informant is also silent on these aspects. 17] For both these points the evidence of the victim girl is important who was able to depose about rape and penetrative sexual assault on her. In the substantive evidence of P.W.1, the victim girl, she has denied the alleged rape and penetrative sexual assault on her by the accused No.1­Vicky. On the contrary, she putforth her case that she married with accused No.1 and out of the wedlock she has a daughter aged two years and now she is conceived pregnancy. The investigating officer has not recorded her statement under S. 164 of Cr.P.C. 18] The victim was sent for her medical examination and medical certificate has been produced on record, however, the history recorded by the medical officer shows that she had consensual sex and was pregnant before marriage and on the date of examination she was found pregnant. This document has been admitted by the defence vide Exh.23. This history given by the victim gives go­bye to the case of the prosecution. Under the circumstances, there is nothing on record to hold the accused No.1­Vicky 9 Spl. Case 17/2014 [Judg.] guilty for both these points. Hence, I answer the point Nos. 4 & 5 in the negative. 19] Resultantly, the accused Nos. 1 & 2 deserve to be acquitted, and as such, I proceed to pass the following order : ORDER 1] Accused No. 1­ Vicky Balbir Lot & No.2-Smt. Saroj Balbir Lot are hereby acquitted under S. 235(1) of Cr.P.C. of the offences punishable under Section 363, 366, 376(1) r/w 34 of IPC & S. 3 r/w 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] The accused Nos. 1 & 2 are on bail. Their bail bonds stand cancelled. 3] No muddemal has been seized and produced, hence, no order is passed. 4] The accused shall execute their P.R. and S.B. of Rs.15,000/­each to appear before the Higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect of appeal filed against this judgment as per S. 437­A of Cr.P.C. 5] Such bail shall remain in force for six months from today. Kalyan, [M.J.Mirza] Dt.30/7/2015. Special Judge, vsi­p.c. Under Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 10 Spl. Case 17/2014 [Judg.] 11 Spl. Case 17/2014 [Judg.]

Accused For the offences punishable under Sections 376 (2) (n), 504 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 3 & 4 of Protection of the Children from Sexual Offences Act. ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ . 2 Spl. Case No.9/2015 (Judgment) Ld. APP Mrs. N.M.Kamathe for the State. Ld. Adv. Mr. S.D.Pagare for accused. : JUDGMENT : (Delivered on 19th July 2017). 1] Accused named­above is prosecuted for the offences punishable under Sections 376 (2) (n), 504 of the Indian Penal Code and under Sections 3 & 4 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] Case of prosecution in brief is that informant is the victim girl and she is aged about 17 years and her name is kept secret. Accused resides opposite to the house of informant and there was friendship between accused and informant. In the year 2009 while informant was studying in 9th standard accused expressed his desire that he loves her and that he would marry with her . In the month of April 2010 informant's one neighbour asked her as to whether she goes to the lodge. So informant inquired from accused as to what is the meaning of lodge. So accused took informant to his house while the mother and brother of accused were not present there and at that time accused told her that he loves her and he would marry with her and that he would explain to her the meaning of lodge and by saying so accused did sexual intercourse with her forcibly. Informant informed this fact to her neighbour Sanny Valmiki and Raju Valmiki but they told her that accused would marry with her. So, informant did not inform this fact to anybody. It is further the case of prosecution that thereafter on so many occasions accused took her to his house 3 Spl. Case No.9/2015 (Judgment) when nobody was present in the house of accused and accused did sexual intercourse with her. Thereafter in the year 2012 accused called informant in the house of Sanny Valmiki and accused told Sanny Valmiki that informant is his wife and that he would marry with her and thereafter accused did sexual intercourse with informant in the house of Sanny Valmiki and thereafter by giving promise of marriage accused did sexual intercourse with her from time to time. 3] It is further the case of prosecution that on 03.03.2014 at about 3.00 p.m. accused caused the informant to sit on the motorcycle which he had taken from his friend Rinku and accused took the informant by that motorcycle in Akshay Lodge at Titwala and accused by saying that he would soon marry with her and that she is his wife accused did sexual intercourse with her without her consent and that accused brought her to her house. Thereafter informant asked accused as to when he would marry with her then accused replied that her character is not good and that she was sleeping with so many people. In this way accused refused to marry with her. So, informant alongwith her mother came to police station and lodged complaint. On the report of informant crime No.143/2014 for the offences punishable under Sections 376 (2) (n), 504 of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 3 & 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offices Act, 2012 was registered by Ambernath Police Station. 4] In further statement of the informant it is mentioned that the incident of accused taking her to Akshay Lodge took place on 4 Spl. Case No.9/2015 (Judgment) 06.03.2014 instead of 03.03.2014. Police recorded statements of witnesses. Police obtained the xerox copy of the leaving certificate of the informant wherein her date of birth is mentioned as 24.05.1996. Police seized relevant page of the register of Akshay Lodge of the dated 06.03.2014 under panchnama in presence of panchas. Police drew panchnama of the place of incident in presence of panchas. After completion of investigation charge­ sheet was filed . 5] Charge at Exh.2 under Sections 376 (2) (n), 504 of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 3 & 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offcences Act, 2012 was framed against accused. Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 6] After recording evidence and hearing both the sides following points arise for my determination and I have noted my findings against each of them for the reason to follow: Sr.No. Points Findings 1. Whether it is proved by prosecution that accused committed rape on the minor victim girl i.e. informant .. Not proved. repeatedly ? 2. Whether it is proved by prosecution that accused intentionally insulted the informant (i.e. victim girl) and thereby gave provocation to her intending or knowing it to be likely 5 Spl. Case No.9/2015 (Judgment) that such provocation would cause her to break the public peace or to commit any other offence ? .. Not proved. 3. Whether it is proved by prosecution that accused from time to time repeatedly committed penetrative sexual assault on the informant (i.e. .. Not proved. victim girl ) ? 4. What offences, if any are proved .. No offence is proved against against accused ? accused. : REASONS : As to Point Nos.1 to 6 :­ 7] Perusal of the evidence of the informant (PW­1) shows that she knows accused as accused resides opposite to her house. Her evidence shows that accused did not do anything on her. Her evidence further shows that it did not happen that there was love affair between accused and her. Her evidence further shows that it did not happen that while she was minor from time to time accused kept sexual relation with her. It has come in her evidence that since quarrel took place with the mother of accused she went to police station to lodge the complaint. When she was shown complaint, she identified her signature but she deposed that its contents are not correct. She is cross­examined by the learned APP but nothing is brought on record to show that she supported the prosecution case. It can be said that informant has not 6 Spl. Case No.9/2015 (Judgment) supported the prosecution case. 8] Under the circumstances, prosecution has failed to prove its case. Accordingly, my answer to point Nos.1 to 3 is not proved and my answer to point No.4 is that no offence is proved against accused. Consequently, accused is entitled for acquittal. Hence, I pass following order:­ : ORDER : i. Accused viz. Shivraj Yallappa Kaibhavi is hereby acquitted of the offences punishable under Sections 376 (2) (n), 504 of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 3 and 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. ii. His bail bond stands cancelled and his surety is discharged. iii. Accused is required to execute bail bonds of Rs.15,000/­ with one surety in the like amount under Section 437­A of Cr.P.C. to appear before the Hon'ble Higher Courts or Appellate Courts as and when the Hon'ble Higher Courts or Appellate Courts issue notices in respect of any appeal or petition filed against this Judgment and such bail bonds shall be in force for six months. iv No property is produced or seized in this case. Hence no order with respect to muddemal property. Kalyan. (A.A.A.Shaikh) Date: 19.07.2017. Additional Sessions Judge, Kalyan.

1 ABA No. 187/2018 (Exh.1) CNR No. MHTH­06­000344­2018 ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN CRI. ANTI. BAIL APPLN. NO. 187/2018 CNR No. MHTH­06­000344­2018 1] The applicant/accused Sudhir Shantaram Patil has moved present application to enlarge him on anticipatory bail under Section 438 of Code of Criminal Procedure. 2] The applicant's case in brief is that, one Cr. No. I­ 309/2017 under secs. 376(g)(n), 506(2), 363 of IPC, under sec. 4 of POCSO and under sec. 5 of PITA Act is registered to Kalyan Taluka police station wherein one victim aged 17 years has lodged a report that after demise of her mother her father expelled her and she had taken shelter at the house of one Chhaya Arjun Naikade. After exhausting some days she was administered with some pills and thereafter she became seditious. Accordingly, some of the accused have raped her from time to time. She was continuously given those seditious pills and faced rape at the hands of other accused. Accordingly, on 23/12/2017 she had been with one of the Patil at one Lodge where that Patil has committed rape. Therefore, the matter was reported. 3] The contention of the applicant is that, the role of the applicant is nowhere attributed in the evidence. There is neither specific description of the applicant or detail name whereby the applicant could be identified. There is absolutely no evidence against the applicant. In fact, no CC TV footage of that Lodge has been recovered by the I.O.. The applicant is one of the reputed person in the society. He is doing job in Co­Op. Credit Society. If he is arrested, then his image would be lowered down in the society. 2 ABA No. 187/2018 (Exh.1) CNR No. MHTH­06­000344­2018 Hence, he urged for anticipatory bail. 4] Learned APP and I.O. have resisted their application by filing say at Exh.6. It is their contention that, other accused have been arrested. The accused are involved in the anti­social and heinous crime. They have committed rape from time to time. The victim was compelled to do prostitution business at the instance of one another woman. The accused has participated in that offence. There is every chance of tampering and abscondance of the applicant. Therefore, they urged to reject the application. 5] At first, it needs to be seen that, in spite of direction the I.O. remained absent. He has sent case diary to the learned APP but his absence from the proceeding so otherwise intention of him. 6] At the next turn, it is relevant to mention here that, on bare perusal of FIR it seems that, the victim has just quoted presence of one Patil who had committed rape. As pointed by the applicant's counsel there is no specification of Patil or full name mentioned there. Even it is not come on record that, the I.O. has dig out or searched the name of the accused who had committed said rape. There is no CC TV footage of the Lodge where the actual incident took place. The investigation itself is suspicious and only to score the case. In such situation I am of the considered view that, except the bare word Patil there is no iota of evidence against the applicant. Ultimately, the custodial interrogation of the applicant is not at all necessary. In view, the application deserves to be allowed. Consequently, I pass following order :­ 3 ABA No. 187/2018 (Exh.1) CNR No. MHTH­06­000344­2018 : ORDER : 1] Application below Exh. 3 in Cri. Anti. Bail Application No. 187/2018 filed by the applicant/accused Sudhir Shantaram Patil in Cr. No.I­309/2017 registered of Kalyan Taluka Police Station, is hereby allowed. 2] In the event of arrest, applicant/accused shall be released on bail on executing their P.R. and S.B. of Rs.25,000/­ (Twenty Five thousand only) with one or two sureties in the like amount on the condition that, he shall co­operate the Investigating Agency as and when required or called. 3] He shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any other persons acquainted with the facts of the accusation against him so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court to any other officer. 4] The applicant/accused is directed to attend concern police station on every Friday between 5.00 p.m. to 8.00 p.m. for one month only. 5] Breach of any of the conditions shall entail cancellation of bail. 6] Inform to the concerned Police Station, accordingly. ORDER BELOW EXH.1 IN CRI. ANTI.BAIL APPLN.NO.130/2017, Mayur Prakash Magare ..Applicant Vs The State of Mah. (Ulhasnagar P.Stn.) ..Opponent 1] This application is preferred by the applicant involved in Cr. No. I­35/2017 registered with Ulhasnagar Police Station punishable under sec. 354(A), 323, 504 and 506 of IPC r.w. Sec. 12 of POCSO Act to seek relief of pre­ arrest bail u/s. 438 of Cr.P.C. 2] It reveals from the allegations of the FIR that, the complainant­family and accused are residing in the same area and are well acquainted being neighbourers. On 26.01.2017, at about 9.30 p.m. the complainant Priya went to see her paternal aunt upto Bus Stand, Ulhasnagar. When she was coming back towards her house and reached near the house of Shivaji Yadav, the applicant/accused who was present there has dragged the victim­complainant towards him, saying as, “I love you”. When the victim resisted him, he gave slaps on her face and hit kicks on her stomach. The victim rescued herself and rushed to her house and narrated the incidence to her mother and then matter came to be reported with police. Hence this prosecution. 3] The applicant came with the case that, he is falsly implicated in the present case due to misunderstanding. In ..2.. fact, he is not inv0olved the alleged crime. Moreover, the victim girl is well acquainted with him and having cordial relations being neighbourer. The alleged prosecution is lodged on the behest of rival person and hence, prayed for pre­arrest relief in this false implicated case. 4] This application is opposed by the prosecution submitting that, the act alleged to be attributed by the accused is specifically reflected in the FIR. The name of the accused is shown as assillant of victim girl, if he is released on anticipatory bail. There is every likelyhood of tampering the complainant and her family. Hence, urged for rejection. 5] Heard Ld. Counsel Shri Tidke and gone through the documents relied by the applicant. It reveals from the record that the complainant along­with her mother went to police station to report the matter, but after coming from police station they realised that report is made due to some misunderstandings against the accused. Hence, the mother of the victim filed affidavit to that effect stating there in that, now she has no grievances against the applicant. The Ld. APP tried to resist the prayer submitting that, the affidavit prepared by the complainant appears to be pressurizing tactis used by the applciant. I have gone through the affidavit sworn by complainant Sapana the mother of the victim girl. It is pertinent to note that, both the families are residing adjacent to each other. Thus, alleged settlement between ..3.. neighbourers cannot be viewed suspiciously. In such situation, I am inclined to grant pre­arrest protection. Hence, following order.:­ : ORDER : 1] The application for grant of anticipatory bail is allowed as follows :­ a] In the event of arrest applicant/accused Mayur Magare be released on bail on furnishing P.B. & S.B. of Rs.15,000/­. 2] The applicant is directed to co­operate with investigation agency and attend Ulhasnagar P.Stn. on every Sunday at 11­00 to 2.00pm, till the end of May. 3] Inform Concern P.Stn. accordingly. Moreover, it is held that a false explanation or false plea taken by the accused cannot be used as an additional link in the chain of circumstantial evidence subject to satisfaction of three essential conditions viz. i) various links in the chain of evidence laid by the prosecution have been satisfactorily proved, ii) the said circumstance points the guilt of the accused with reasonable definiteness, and iii) the circumstances is in proximity to the time and Judg. Spl. Case 20/14 ...24... situation. 39] The last ruling is reported in MANU/SC/0313/2000, Joseph Kooveli Poulo V/s State of Kerala, wherein it is held that it is not that every discrepancy or contradiction that matters much in the matter of assessing the reliability or credibility of a witness or truthfulness of his version. Unless the discrepancies and contradictions are so material and substantial and that too are in respect of vitally relevant aspects of the facts deposed, the witness cannot be straight way condemned and their evidence discarded in its entirety. So far as the rulings cited above by the defence, there is no dispute regarding settled position of law. 40] It is settled position of law that if the testimony of the prosecutrix is found reliable and trustworthy, it can be accepted. Here in the case on hand, the minor victim aged about 16 years, 1 month and 28 days and the accused No.1 – Goraksha was knowing by her, believing his words accompanied with him as the accused disclosed her that she is going towards her class and would leave her there. Then he took her to Akshay Lodge/Hotel via Chinchpada road, Teenzadi road and Nalambi road. Then she was taken in a room under the pretext to take meal as he was hungry. Instead of taking meal, she bolted the door of room No. 204 from inside and committed rape on her though she told him that she never loves him and she is not of that age. It is clear from the testimony of the victim that the accused Goraksha committed penetrative sexual assault on her. The victim has also disclosed the incident to her mother immediately after reaching at her home. The version of the prosecutrix is trustworthy and reliable. The medical evidence to the extent that her hymen was torn but Judg. Spl. Case 20/14 ...25... no external injuries on her body or genital were found. The ruling relied by the prosecution as well as advocate for the original complainant on these points are squarely application to this case. Therefore, in absence of medical evidence of rape, it cannot be presumed that the accused Goraksha is innocent. Thus, it is proved by the prosecution that the accused No.1 – Goraksha has committed rape on the minor victim. Moreover, the consent of the prosecutrix is immaterial because of her minority of age. Even otherwise, there is presumption under S. 114­A of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 as to absence of consent of the prosecutrix. 41] The accused No.2 – Jagannath Subanna Shetty has been arrayed as an accused as he was found in Akshay Lodge from which the Lodge register was seized, but not produced before the Court. The spot of occurrence was Room No. 204 where the spot panchanama was drawn. The prosecution has not produced any documentary proof showing that he is either owner or Manager who facilitated the accused No.1 ­Goraksha and allotted the room. None of the witnesses have stated about his concern with the said lodge. Therefore, he is entitled to be acquitted. Hence, I answer the point Nos. 2 & 3 in the affirmative to the extent of accused No.1 Goraksha and in the negative so far as accused No.2 ­Jagannath is concerned. As to Point No. 3: 42] The prosecution has produced the caste certificate of father of victim viz. Yallappa Ramchandra Ghaste at Exh.29. The defence has admitted this caste certificate. It shows that the caste of the father of the victim is Mang ­46 which is recognized as Scheduled Caste issued by Sub Judg. Spl. Case 20/14 ...26... Divisional Officer, Ulhasnagar dtd. 22/12/2010. Though there is no report of caste scrutiny committee, but the fact remains that the victim is belonging to Scheduled Caste. It was necessary on the part of the prosecution to adduce evidence regarding the caste of the accused No.1 ­Goraksha but not produced. Hence, I answer the Point No. 4 in the negative. 43] Resultantly, in my view,the prosecution has proved the case against the accused No.1­ Goraksha Arjun Mahakal only and the prosecution has failed to establish any of the offence against the accused No.2 – Jagannath Subanna Shetty. At this stage, I take pause here to hear the accused No.1­Goraksha on the point of quantum of sentence. Kalyan. [M.J.Mirza] Dt.:4/3/2015. Addl. Sessions Judge, Kalyan. 44] I informed the accused No.1 – Goraksha that he is found guilty of offence punishable under S. 376 of IPC and he was asked to submit his say on the quantum of sentence. The accused No.1 – Goraksha Arjun Mahakal submitted that he do not want to make any submissions on the quantum of sentence. 45] The Ld. APP Sou. J.S.Lohokare for State submitted that the offence is serious one and anti social. The age of girl is below 18 years, therefore, she prayed to award maximum sentence. 46] On the other hand, the Ld. advocate Shri. D.S.Sawant for Judg. Spl. Case 20/14 ...27... accused No.1, submitted that the accused is Government servant and his aged mother is dependent on him. He is not habitual offender. Hence, he submitted that minimum sentence may be awarded. 47] As the offence of rape is concerned, it is against society and anti social one. The gravity of offence is serious because the minor girl has became victim of rape. It has come on record that the accused No.1 ­Goraksha by taking disadvantage of friendship with minor victim, she was taken to the Lodge, the place of occurrence under the pretext that he wanted to say something to her instead of taking her to Kirti Computer Class. Moreover, he took the victim in a room of Akshay Lodge, then he bolted the door of room from inside and then committed rape and penetrative sexual assault on the victim. Therefore, considering the mitigating circumstances, the following sentence would be just and proper. 48] The punishment prescribed for the offence punishable under S. 376 of IPC and S. 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 is not less than 7 years and fine. D. 2 ­ 5 ­ 3 IN THE COURT OF ADDL.SESSIONS JUDGE, KALYAN AT : KALYAN (Presided over by D.S.Ghumare) Session Case No.21/2014 Exh.No. The State of Maharashtra (Through Manpada Police Station) ....
