Smt.Bhopi, Ld.Adv. for the accused. ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ JUDGMENT (Delivered on 28th day of July, 2016) 1] The accused Vaibhav Vinayak Choudhary stands charged for the offenses punishable under Secs.363 and 376(1) of the Indian Penal Code besides Sec.4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act,2012. 2 S.C.NO.21/2014 Judgment 2] The prosecution’s case, in brief, is that the informant Smt.Deepali Ramesh Hegde resided at Rana Bhavan, room No.1, Bhopar, Deslepada, Dombivli alongwith her two daughters namely Rani, prosecutrix Rinkal and son Omkar. Her daughter prosecutrix Rinkal was aged 14 yrs and was studying in 8th standard in Shankeshwar Vidyalay, Sagaon. The informant Deepali along with her daughters Rani and prosecutrix Rinkal had been to the house of Rinkal's friend namely Sayli Surve for celebration of her birthday at about 8 pm on 7/11/2013. The informant Deepali and her elder daughter Rani were there for sometime and then they returned to their house, informing Sayli's father to drop daughter prosecutrix Rinkal to her house after celebration of birthday. The prosecution's case further proceeds to narrate that as prosecutrix Rinkal did not return home, the informant Deepali had been to the house of Sayli Surve at about 9 pm. There one girl told her that two boys had come there. They called prosecutrix Rinkal out side the house and took her towards Church of that locality. The said girl gave description of that two boys, from which the informant Deepali got assured that the said two boys must be the accused Vaibhav Choudhary and Shrikant Salunwala. Thereafter, the informant Deepali searched for her daughter prosecutrix Rinkal in the vicinity. She also looked­up for Vaibhav Choudhary and Shrikant Salunwala with help of their relatives. But as they were not found, the informant Deepali became sure that the accused Vaibhav Choudhary and Shrikant Salunwala had enticed away her daughter Rinkal. Therefore, she lodged report against them with Manpada Police Station. On the basis of her report a crime against the 3 S.C.NO.21/2014 Judgment accused for offences punishable under sections 363 & 376 of I.P.C. and Section 3 & 4 of the P.O.C.S.O.Act was registered vide C.R.No.I­ 508/2014. 3] The investigation of the crime was conducted by P.S.I. Shri.A.A.Patil (PW.5). During the course of investigation he learnt that the prosecutrix Rinkal was enticed away by the accused Vaibhav and they are at Gurhan Farm House situated at Talegaon of Murbad Tahasil. Therefore, they went to the said Farm House, where the accused Vaibhav was found along with the prosecutrix Rinkal. Thereupon, the investigation officer PW.5 arrested the accused Vaibhav and the other accused Yogesh Pawar, whose name was incorrectly stated as Shrikant Saloonwala. The investigating officer conducted the necessary panchanama of scene of offence. He also referred the accused Vaibhav as well as the prosecutrix Rinkal for the medical examination to K.D.M.C. Hospital. He recorded the statements of the witnesses and collected the birth certificate of the prosecutrix Rinkal issued by Greater Bombay Municipal Corporation. Ultimately, after completion of investigation, the investigating officer filed report under section 173 of the Code of Criminal Procedure in the court of Ld. Judicial Magistrate, First Class Kalyan, who after complying the provisions of Sections 207 of the Code of Criminal Procedure committed present case to the Court of Sessions under section 209 of Cr.PC. 4] The Charge Exh.5 was framed against the accused Vaibhav Choudhari for the offence punishable U/Secs. 363, 376(1) of I.P.C. and Sec.3 r.w. Sec.4 of the P.O.C.S.O.Act. The charge was read 4 S.C.NO.21/2014 Judgment over and explained to the accused Vaibhav. He pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. Upon completion of the prosecution evidence, the statement of accused Vibhav U/Sec. 313(1)(c) of Cr.P.C was recorded. The defence of the accused is that of total denial and false implication in the crime. 5] The following points arise for determination and my findings are noted against each thereon for the reasons states herein below : POINTS FINDINGS 1) Whether the prosecution proves that on 7/11/2013 at about 8.00 to 9.00 pm. at Desalepada,Dombivli (E) in front of house of witness Sayli Surve the accused Vaibhav Chodhary, had kidnapped Kum.Rinkal Ramesh Hegade aged 14 yrs. from lawful guardianship of her parents ? Proved. 2) Whether the prosecution proves that on 10/11/2013 at Burhan Farm House, Talegaon, Murbad the accused Vaibhav committed rape on Kum.Rinkal Ramesh Hegade,who was below the age of 16 at the time of incident ? Proved. 3) Whether the prosecution proves that on the abovesaid date, time and place the accused Vaibhav committed penetrative sexual assault on a minor girl Kum.Rinkal Ramesh Hegade, aged 14 years ? Proved. 4) What order ? As per final order. 5 S.C.NO.21/2014 Judgment :REASONS: 6] The prosecution in support of its case has examined in all five witnesses. They are the informant P.W.1­ Deepali Ramesh Hegade, prosecutrix P.W.2 Rinkal Ramesh Hegade, medical officer P.W.3­ Dr. Shweta Omprakash Gupta, prosecutrix Rinkal's friend P.W.4­ Sayli Chandrakant Surve and the investigating officer P.W.5­ Abasaheb Anandrao Patil. POINT NOS.1 to 3 : 7] All the points are dealt with simultaneously to avoid repetition of discussion of the evidence, which is common for them. 8] The informant P.W.1­ Deepali testified that on 7/11/2013 at about 8 pm her daughter prosecutrix PW.2 Rinkal had gone to the house of her friend PW.4 Sayli, who resided at Desalepada. It was PW.4 Sayli's birthday on that day and there was celebration. The prosecutrix PW.2 Rinkal did not return from the birthday celebration and so the informant PW.1 Deepali along with her elder daughter Rani went to the house of Sayli, where she was told by one girl that two boys took Rinkal along with them. She learnt that accused Vaibhav and his friend Shrikant had abducted her daughter Rinkal and despite of her search she was not found. Therefore, she lodged report against the accused. In her evidence F.I.R. Exh.13 was proved and exhibited. 9] P.W.2 prosecutrix Rinkal testified that she went to her friend Sayli Surve's house situated at Deslepada for her birthday 6 S.C.NO.21/2014 Judgment celebration at about 8 pm on 7/11/2013. The accused Vaibhav and one Yogesh came there. She accompanied them and reached a place behind the church of that locality. From that place accused Vaibhav's friend Yogesh went away, whereas they both went towards Dombivli Railway Station by walk. P.W.2 prosecutrix Rinkal deposed that at that time she told the accused that she would not return to her house as her mother and uncle would scold her and so she went along with the accused Vaibhav to C.S.T. Railway Station. She further deposed that then from C.S.T. they came to Thakurli Railway Station and from there went to Vaibhav's friend namely Shrikant's house, where they stayed over night. Then the prosecutrix Rinkal and accused Vaibhav went to Vaibhav's sister's house at Dombivli, where they halted for a day and from there they went to Murbad by bus. Then they went to one Farm House. P.W.2 prosecutrix Rinkal specifically deposed that at that Farm House, they stayed for night, where they had sexual relations. She also deposed that she and accused were having affair prior thereto. On the next day, police from Manpada Police Station came and took them to the Manpada Police Station. They got her medically examined by the doctor and thereafter her custody was handed over to her mother. 10] P.W.4­ Sayli has testified that Rinkal had been to her house for her birthday celebration on 7/11/2013 and after celebrating her birthday, Rinkal had gone along with her two boy friends. 11] It would be pertinent to note here that from the cross­ examination of prosecutrix Rinkal, it is clear that the accused Vaibhav had taken away prosecutrix Rinkal from the custody of her mother 7 S.C.NO.21/2014 Judgment informant P.W.1 Deepali. This fact stands established because the suggestion had been put that the accused Vaibhav had not forced the prosecutrix Rinkal to accompany him. Besides that a suggestion had also been put that the informant P.W.1 Deepali did not like friendship of the accused Vaibhav with the prosecutrix Rinkal. From this an inference can be clearly drawn that the accused Vaibhav had taken away the prosecutrix Rinkal to Murbad at a Farm House, where they had sexual relations with each other. 12] The said fact of sexual relationship by the accused Vaibhav with the prosecutrix Rinkal stands corroborated by medical evidence. The prosecutrix Rinkal was medically examined at K.D.M.C. Hospital on 12/11/2013 i.e. after one day of alleged incident of sexual intercourse. The medical officer PW.3 Dr.Shweta Ompraksh Gupta has testified that the prosecutrix Rinkal had given history of attempted sexual intercourse. She has also deposed that on medical examination she found that prosecutrix Rinkal's hymen had been ruptured and vagina admitted one finger. She also testified that on medical examination she found that there was possibility of sexual intercourse with her. In evidence of medical officer PW.3 Dr.Shweta Ompraksh Gupta the medical certificate Exh.16 was duly proved. Thus from P.W.3 Dr.Shweta Ompraksh Gupta's evidence corroborates the the proecution case that the accused had sexual intercourse with the prosecutrix Rinkal. 13] It would be material to note here that the evidence of investigating officer P.W.5­ A.P.I. Shri.A.A.Patil is relevant since he had found the accused Vaibhav and the prosecutrix Rinkal at the Farm House 8 S.C.NO.21/2014 Judgment at Murbad. His evidence corroborates the testimony of the prosecutrix Rinkal regarding the fact of taking away of her and then of sexual intercourse by the accused Vaibhav with her. 14] The prosecution has even placed on record the birth certificate issued by the Greater Bombay Municipal Corporation. It depicts the birth of prosecutrix Rinkal as 14 th Aug.,1999. The Ld.Adv.Smt.Bhopi for the accused submitted that the documentary evidence adduced by the prosecution about the age by production of certified copy of Birth Certificate Ex.22 issued by the Muncipal corporation, though exhibited, is of no value for the reason that the material effect of this document is that the same could not be said to proved without examining the officer from Municipal Corporation . She submitted that, it will not be appropriate to read the Birth certificate in evidence as same is not duly proved by the prosecution for it had not led best evidence available. She vehemently contented that the documentary evidence as to dates of birth in accordance with the record of the then Greater Bombay Municipal Corporation, the scrutiny of the contents of the said documents and the improbability as to the correctness thereof still remains. She contented that there is failure of proof as to preponderance of probabilities on the part of the prosecution and she wished to exclude the Birth certificate from consideration for having being not proved in strict sense. 15] Per contra Ld. Adv Sachin Kulkarni for the accused submitted that Section 35 of the Indian Evidence Act refers to the relevancy of entry in Public record made in the performance of duty. 9 S.C.NO.21/2014 Judgment Under Section 35, a register or official book maintained in terms of a statute or by a statutory authority in regular course of business would be a relevant fact. Therefore, the certified copy of the Birth Certificate could be relevant and considered for it does satisfy the requirements of Section 35 of the Indian Evidence Act. He contented that it is reliable evidence on record to show that the date of birth was recorded in the Muncipal register is thus relevant under section 35 and as such are vital pieces of evidence, which clinches the issue to prove the birth date of the prosecutrix PW.2 Rinkal as to be 14/8/1999. 16] Ld A.P.P. Sachin Kulkarni further made reference to the decision of their Lordships of Apex Court in case of in Birad Mal Singhvi vs. Anand Purohit [AIR 1988 SC 1796] , wherein it is held : "...To render a document admissible under Section 35, three conditions must be satisfied, firstly, entry that is relied on must be one in a public or other official book, register or record, secondly, it must be an entry stating a fact in issue or relevant fact, and thirdly, it must be made by a public servant in discharge of his official duty, or any other person in performance of a duty specially enjoined by law. " He contended that as the Birth Certificate Ex.22 fulfills all three condi­ tions it is admissible piece of evidence 17] Section 77 of the Evidence Act, provides for proof of documents by production of certified copies. It lays down that the certified copies may be produced in proof of the contents of the public 10 S.C.NO.21/2014 Judgment documents or parts of the public documents of which they purport to be copies. Therefore, the contention of Ld.Adv. Bhopi for the accused to disbelieve the contents of the certified copies mentioned above is an too fragile attempt to dislodge valid proof regarding factum of birth date of prosecutrix PW.2 as to be 14­8­1999. In fact Ld.Advocate Smt.Bhopi by the aforesaid argument desires to make the statutory presumption sterile by a process of convoluted logic. Her arguments disregards the provisions of section 79 of the Evidence Act which provides for the presumption as to genuineness of certified copies. It runs as under:— “The Court shall presume to be genuine every document purporting to be a certificate, certified copy or other document, which is by law declared to be admissible as evidence of any particular fact and which purports to be duly certified by any officer of the Central Government or of a State Government, or by any officer in the State of Jammu and Kashmir who is duly authorised thereto by the Central Government: Provided that such document is substantially in the form and purports to be executed in the manner directed by law in that behalf. The Court shall also presume that any officer by whom any such document purports to be signed or certified held, when he signed it, the official character which he claims in such paper.” 18] The Court has to start with such presumption. The genuine­ ness of the certified copies has been ascertained as per the procedure laid down under the provisions of Indian Evidence Act regarding proof of documents. Ld. A.P.P. Sachin Kulkarni for the State is quite correct in his submission that the genuineness of the birth certificates Ex.22 being certified copy of public record produced on record stands proved as that certified copy had the presumption of correctness as stated above. Thus 11 S.C.NO.21/2014 Judgment as the birth cerficate Ex.22 is public document and its secondary evidence is allowed, it has been exhibited and same is read in evidence. I do not have any doubt regarding genuineness of the birth certificate. Thus, the birth certificate is trust worthy evidence of the age of the prosecutrix Rinkal. Considering the said birth date, the prosecutrix Rinkal's age at the time of occurrence did not exceed 15 years. 19] Ld. Adv. Bhopi for the accused contented that the informant PW.1 Deepali in her FIR Exh.13 had stated that she and her elder daughter had accompanied the prosecutrix Rinkal to the house of her friend P.W.4 Sayli and after being there for some time returned to their home and later on again went to her P.W.4 Sayali's house as she did not come back till 9.00 pm. She contented this discrepancy itself shows that the evidence of prosecution witnesses is not reliable. Ld. Adv. Bhopi further submitted that there is no statement of any witness from Murbad, where at farm house the accused had committed rape on the prosecutrix Rinkal and so without corroboration to her evidence should not be relied upon at all. 20] The above contention on behalf of the accused have been controverted by Ld APP Sachin Kulkarni by placing reliance on the judgment of the Honble Apex Court in the matter of State of Himachal Pradesh v. Lekh Raj & anr. MANU/SC/0714/1999 : 1999 (4) Crimes 337 (S.C.), and submitting that when the testimony of the prosecutor is of such a nature that on the face of it the same discloses truthful version of the incident that might have been occurred and for that reason to be believed to be a truthful witness, corroboration of such a testimony in 12 S.C.NO.21/2014 Judgment each and every case cannot be considered as a matter of rule and cannot be invariably insisted upon, totally ignoring the facts of the particular case. According the learned Public Prosecutor, the testimony of the prosecutrix P.W.2 Rinkal clearly makes out the case put forth by the prosecution against the accused and brings out the necessary ingredients of section 376 of the Indian Penal Code and requires no corroboration, apart from the fact that the same has been, in fact, fully corroborated by the testimony of the doctor P.W. 3 ­Dr.Shweta Gupta as well as that of informant P.W. 1 Deepali. Ld. A.P.P. Shri.Kulkarni also drew my attention to the fact that the prosecutrix Rinkal after requiring her mother to move out of the court testified about the sexual relation the accused had with her when they were at a farmhouse at Murbad. 21] Ld. Adv. Sachin kulkarni to butress his above submission also placed his reliance on the decision of their Lordships of the Apex Court in the case of State of Maharashtra v. Chandraprakash Kewalchand Jain, MANU/SC/0122/1990 : 1990CriLJ889 , wherein it is held thus: "A prosecutrix of a sex offence cannot be put on a par with an accomplice. She is in fact a victim of the crime. The Evidence Act nowhere says that her evidence cannot be accepted unless it is corroborated in material particulars. She is undoubtedly a competent witness under section 118 and her evidence must receive the same weight as is attached to an injured in cases of physical violence. The same degree of care and caution must attach in the evaluation of her evidence as in the case of an injured complainant or witness and no more. What is necessary is that the Court must be alive to and conscious of the fact that it is dealing with the evidence of a person who is interested in the outcome of the charge levelled by her. If the Court keeps this in mind and feels satisfied that it can act on 13 S.C.NO.21/2014 Judgment the evidence of the prosecutrix, there is no rule of law or practice incorporated in the Evidence Act similar to Illustration (b) to section 114 which requires it to look for corroboration. If for some reason the Court is hesitant to place implicit reliance on the testimony of the prosecutrix it may look for evidence which may lend assurance to her testimony short of corroboration required in the case of an accomplice. The nature of evidence required to lend assurance to the testimony of the prosecutrix ;must necessarily depend on the facts and circumstances of each case. But if a prosecutrix is an adult and of full understanding the Court is entitled to base a conviction on her evidence unless the same is shown to be infirm and not trustworthy. If the totality of the circumstances appearing on the record of the case discussed that the prosecutrix does not have a strong motive to falsely involve the person charged, the Court should ordinarily have no hesitation in accepting her evidence." 22] In the present case in hand the prosecutrix Rinkal is of tender age not exceeding 15 at the time of offence and seems have had no motive to falsely involve the accused in crime. It would be apposite to state her that the courts while trying an accused on charges of rape must deal with such cases with utmost sensitivity. The courts should examine the broader probabilities of a case and not get swayed by minor contradictions or insignificant discrepancies in the statement of the prosecutrix Rinkal which are not of a fatal nature, to throw out an otherwise reliable prosecution case. In the present case in hand the evidence of the prosecutrix Rinkal inspires confidence and so same could be relied upon without seeking corroboration of her statement in material particulars alike witnesses from Murbad farmhouse where the rape was committed. Ld. APP Shri.Kulkarni is right in submitting that the relative of the accused worked at the Farmhouse at Murbad and certainly that witness, if could have been examined, would have turned hostile to the 14 S.C.NO.21/2014 Judgment prosecution. That apart there is reason for false implication of the accused in the present crime for making it difficult to place implicit reliance on the testimony of the Prosecutrix PW.2 Rinkal so as to look for evidence, which may lend assurance to her testimony, short of corroboration required in the case of an accomplice. 23] That apart, the fact is to be noted is that in a case of rape, no self­respecting woman would come forward in a Court just to make a humiliating statement against her honour such as is involved in the commission of rape on her. The inherent bashfulness of the females and the tendency to conceal outrage of sexual aggression are factors which could not overlook. More so in the case in hand since the prosecutrix Rinkal is of tender age and the accused had not specified any special reason for her to falsely implicate her in serious offence. Therefore, I do not find any compelling reasons which necessitate looking for corroboration of her statement. Needless to state here that I do not find any difficulty to act on the testimony of prosecutrix Rinkal alone to believe her testimony as it inspires confidence and same is reliable. Furthermore, the corroborative evidence is not an imperative component of judicial credence in every case of rape. Thus where the prosecutrix is believed to be truthful witness, in her deposition, then no further corroboration need be insisted upon, as corroboration is only a rule of prudence, as has been held by the Honble Apex Court in Lekh Raj's case (cited supra) relied upon by the learned APP Shri Kulkarni for the state. 15 S.C.NO.21/2014 Judgment 23] Next Ld.Advocate Smt.Bhopi for the accused submitted that the evidence on record clearly establishes that how the prosecutrix Rinkal herself accompanied the accused to various places in public transport and reached to Murbad, where they had sexual intercourse clearly proves that the same was consensual sex and not a rape at all. More so when admittedly the prosecutrix PW.2 Rinkal and the accused Vaibhav, were in love. She also submitted that considering the fact that the sexual relationship was with consent of each other, it can not be said that the accused Vaibhav had committed offence punishable under Section 376 of I.P.C. 24] As against this Ld. A.P.P. Shri.Kulkarni for the State submitted that in the present case the question of consent for sexual intercourse is out of question because the prosecutrix Rinkal was below the age of 18 years. He submitted that considering birth certificate Exh.22 it is clear that the age of the prosecutrix Rinkal on the date alleged offence is of 14 years and 4 months. He submitted that as the victim is not above 15 years consent becomes immaterial, in view of placentum sixthly of Section 375 of I.P.C, which defines rape. Thus, considering the factum of age of the prosecutrix Rinkal, the said consent even if is proved can not be said to be consent as intended by Section 375 of I.P.C. as the consent was of a girl, who is below the age of 16 years. 25] That being so, the contention of the Ld.Adv. Smt.Bhopi for the accused that the prosecutrix Rinkal had been willingly joined the 16 S.C.NO.21/2014 Judgment company of the accused and the accused had sexual intercourse with her with her consent. She rightly submitted that the fact that prosecutrix Rinkal had accompanied the accused Vaibhav in public transport like railway and bus to Murbad clearly established that she was consenting party. That apart there are no injuries on the person of prosecutrix Rinkal suffered or might have suffered in defending herself and from this also it can be said that she had consented to have sexual relations with the accused Vaibhav out of their love. Even if that is held to be proved, question of consent as has been rightly submitted by Ld.A.P.P. Shri.Kulkarni is immaterial, as the offence would fall within the clause sixthly of the definition of rape given in Sec.375 of I.P.C. Therefore, I hold that the prosecution has been able to prove that the accused had committed rape and penetrative sexual assault on the prosecutrix Rinkal after he had kidnapped Kum.Rinkal from lawful guardianship of her parents. Hence, point No.1 to 3 are answered in the affirmative. 26] This takes me to hear the accused on the point of sentence. Kalyan. (D. S. Ghumre) 28/7/2016 Addl. Sessions Judge, Kalyan 27] The accused has submitted that the lenient view may be taken for imposing the punishment. Considering his age and that his parents are dependant upon him. 28] Ld.Adv.Smt.Bhopi submitted that the accused did not have any criminal antecedent and he is the first time offender. She also 17 S.C.NO.21/2014 Judgment submitted that the offence of rape has been committed as a consequence of consent given out of love relationship between the accused Vaibhav and the prosecutrix PW.2 Rinkal. She also submitted that considering the age of the accused, it would not be proper to impose maximum punishment prescribed by the offence by law. She also submitted that the accused be imposed for punishment for the period he had already undergone in prison as a under trial prisoner. 29] As against this Ld.A.P.P. Shri. Kulkarni submitted that the offence is serious and deserves no leniency. More so, when the victim of the crime prosecutrix PW.2 Rinkal is hardly not more than 15 yrs. of age. He submitted that stringent punishment should be imposed upon the accused taking into account the fact that the crime of violence upon woman needs to be severely dealt with. He also submitted that protection of society and deterring the criminal is the avowed object of the law and for that purpose appropriate sentence needs to be imposed upon the accused of the heinous crimes of sexual violence. 30] I have considered the rival submissions of Ld.A.P.P. Shri.Kulkarni and Ld. Adv. Smt.Bhopi. Even though the Ld.A.P.P. has argued that maximum punishment should be imposed upon the accused contending that it is heinous crime of rape on a innocent helpless girl of tender age not more than 15 years, I do not find it justifiable to take stringent view to impose maximum punishment. This because there are following mitigating circumstances available on record, which justify minimum punishment prescribed by law : 18 S.C.NO.21/2014 Judgment i) First is that the accused and the prosecutrix PW.1 had only one sexual encounter as per the prosecution case. ii) Second is that the prosecutrix Rinkal herself had consented for sexual intercourse in all probabilities as both of them had traveled from Dombivali to C.S.T. , then again to Dombivli and then to Murbad in public transport like railway and bus and had stayed together voluntarily. iii) Third is that the accused Vaibhav and the prosecutrix Rinkal seems to be deeply in love as she herself had joined his company after birthday celebration at the house of her friend PW.4 Sayali. iv) Fourth is that the prosecutrix Rinkal has admitted in her cross­examination that the accused Vaibhav had not forced her to accompany him and in her examination­in­chief itself she has stated that as it was late to return back home, she told the accused Vaibhav that she would not return to her house and then accompanied him to C.S.T. railway station, from where they came to Thakurli where they stayed at his friend's house. v) Fifth is that in the testimony of prosecutrix Rinkal also she has not stated that accused Vaibhav by false promise of marriage or by force had sexual intercourse with her. But she has stated that when they stayed over night at the farm house at Murbad , they kept sexual relationship. vi) Sixth is that the accused Vaibhav as per police record was only 19 years of age at the time of incident and presently must be about 21 years age. 19 S.C.NO.21/2014 Judgment vii) Seventh is that the accused do not have any criminal antecedent and appears to be swayed away by lust at the time of offence. 31] Considering the above noted mitigating circumstances, it would not be appropriate to award maximum punishment to the accused. On the other hand, it would be appropriate to impose minimum punishment prescribed under law. Section 4 of the P.O.C.S.O. Act provides that punishment shall not be less than seven years, if the accused is found guilty for the offence of commission of penetrative sexual assault. So also Section 376 of I.P.C. provides punishment for rape shall not be less than seven years. Therefore, the accused Vaibhav deserves punishment of seven years for offence punishable under Section 4 of the P.O.C.S.O. Act and also punishment of seven years for offence punishable under Section 376 of I.P.C. Besides the above substantiative punishment the accused is also liable for the punishment of fine of Rs.2,000/­ for each of the offence. The guilt of the accused Vaibhav is also proved under Section 363 of I.P.C. and I deem fit to impose punishment of two years and fine of Rs.1,000/­ for the said offence. In facts and circumstances of the case the substantive sentence shall run concurrently. In the result, the following order is made : :ORDER: 1) Vide section 235 (2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the accused Vaibhav Vinayak Choudhari is convicted for the offence punishable under Section 363 of I.P.C. and is sentenced to suffer 20 S.C.NO.21/2014 Judgment Rigorous Imprisonment for the period of Two years and shall pay fine of Rs.1,000/­ in default of payment of fine to suffer Simple Imprisonment for the period of one month. 2) Vide section 235 (2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure the accused Vaibhav Vinayak Choudhari is convicted for the offence punishable under Section 376(1) of I.P.C. and is sentenced to suffer Rigorous Imprisonment for the period of Seven years and shall pay fine of Rs.2,000/­ in default of payment of fine to suffer Simple Imprisonment for the period of two months. 3) Vide section 235(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure the accused Vaibhav Vinayak Choudhari is convicted for the offence punishable under Section 3 r.w. Sec.4 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act,2012 and is sentenced to suffer Rigorous Imprisonment for the period of Seven years and shall pay fine of Rs.2,000/­ in default of payment of fine to suffer Simple Imprisonment for the period of two months. 4) All the abovesaid sentences shall run concurrently. 5) The accused is in jail since 11/11/2013 and the said period undergone by him shall be given as set off U/Sec.428 of Cr.P.C. Kalyan. ( D.S.Ghumre) Dt.28/7/2016 Addl.Sessions Judge,Kalyan.

1 A.B.A.No.177/2017 Order below Exh.3. ORDER BELOW EXH.3 IN ANTI.BAIL APPLN.NO. 177/2017 : This is an application U/Sec.439 of Cr.P.C. for bail filed by the applicant/accused Jeetu Ramprasad Jaiwat in C.R.No.I­ 32/2017 registered with Hill Line Police Station for the offence punishable U/Secs.341,363,354(d),504,506,509,323 of I.P.C. besides Secs. 8 & 12 of the P.O.C.S.O. Act. 2] The applicant has contended that he is permanent resident of Ulhasnagar , he is innocent and has been falsely roped in this crime, with a view to take political revenge from him. He has contended that the F.I.R. is delayed. He also contended that the provisions of POCSO Act are applied with intention to keep him behind the bars. He further contended that the victim's age might be 19 to 20 years and she is not a minor. He further contended that there is no possibility to tamper with the prosecution witnesses and he is ready and willing to abide all the conditions imposed upon him, if he released on bail. He has prayed for his release on bail on above stated grounds amongst others. 3] I have heard Ld.Adv. Shri.Rafiq Khan for the applicant/accused. I have perused the documents filed by him on record. 4] Ld.Adv. for the accused contended that the accused is innocent person and is falsely implicated in the crime due to his giving support to one Rupchand Pawar. He also contended that to refrained the accused from giving support to the said Rupchand Pawar this case has been lodged against him. He also contended that the accused does not have any criminal antecedent and would not tamper with any evidence if released on bail. He sought for release 2 A.B.A.No.177/2017 Order below Exh.3. of the accused in ad interim anticipatory bail. 5] From the F.I.R. it appears that the accused had kidnapped the minor girl when she was on her way to her work place and took her to the room situated in constructed building where he told her that he likes her and he has love for her. The F.I.R. also proceeds on to narrate that the accused had even assaulted her and outraged her modesty when she tried to run away. From the F.I.R. it also appears that the accused had threatened the informant Komal and her mother that if they would report the matter to police, he would see them. Considering this factual aspects I am of the opinion that it is not the case where one can say that custodial interrogation is not necessary. On the contrary, as the offence falls under the provisions of POCSO Act and the crime is against the minor girl, it will not be appropriate to exercise discretion to grant interim anticipatory bail to the accused. 6] Apart from above factual reasons of need for custodial interrogation of the accused , there are further more reasons due to which it can be said that it would not be proper and appropriate to exercise discretion to grant anticipatory bail to the accused. First reason is that the release of the applicant/accused on anticipatory bail would cause hindrance in investigation of the crime since the offence pertains to crime again minor girl. Second reason is that there is possibility of tampering of evidence if the accused is released on anticipatory bail as the applicant/accused as the victim is a girl. Third reason is that I do not find any reasons to believe that accusations do not made with the object of injuring or humiliating the 3 A.B.A.No.177/2017 Order below Exh.3. applicant/accused by having him so arrested. On the contrary, there is a very strong prima facie case against the accused. Fourth reason is that the nature and gravity of the accusations does not warrant anticipatory bail to the accused, since the accused appears to have kidnapped a minor girl and after taking her to secluded place had outraged her modesty and even beat her for not accepting his proposal. Fifth reason is for collecting evidence against the accused there is need of interrogation of the accused. This justify custodial interrogation of all the applicant/accused and even grant of anticipatory bail application would prejudice the investigation of crime.. Sixth reason is that there is strong prima facie case against the accused as regards to kidnapping and outraging the modesty of a minor girl who had no axe to grind against the accused. Seventh reason is that to know the modus operandi of the crime and to collect the evidence the custodial interrogation of the accused is quite necessary in view of allegations made in F.I.R. Particularly when, by no stretch of imagination it can be stated that the accusations have been made against the applicant/accused with object of humiliating him. No doubt the accused has stated in his application that he is falsely implicated as he is supporting a particular candidate in the Municipal Elections. This is nothing but a cock and bull story to raise ground for anticipatory bail in serious offence punishable under provisions of POCSO Act. Eighth reason is that there are circumstances in which the accused may provide information leading to discovery of material facts of the crime and the manner in which the crime is committed. 4 A.B.A.No.177/2017 Order below Exh.3. 7] For the above reasons, the custodial interrogation seems to be quite necessary for effective and proper investigation of crime, which pertains to the crime against a minor girl. 8] In such factual matrix it would be far fetch to say that the applicant/accused is falsely implicated in the crime and the first information report has been lodged at the behest of opposite candidate who had political rivalry against the present applicant/accused. 9] It would also be of some significance to mention that the power conferred by Section 438 is of an extraordinary character in the sense and that it is not ordinarily resorted to like the power conferred by Sections 437 and 439. The power to grant anticipatory bail has to be exercised with due care and circumspection. Very cogent and overwhelming circumstances are necessary for an order directing the pre­ arrest bail in serious offences, which, in my opinion, are missing in the instant case. Furthermore, nothing was brought to my notice from which it could be inferred that the accused are falsely implicated in the crime and that too solely out of political rivalry. 10] In the given facts and circumstances of the present case, there is no justification for granting ad interim bail to the accused. In the result the following order is made : :ORDER: 1. The application Exh.3 is hereby rejected. 2. Inform to the Hillline police station accordingly. Kalyan. (D.S.Ghumare) Dt.10/2/2017 Addl. Sessions Judge , Kalyan.

1 Spl. Case 23/2014 [Judgment] Presented on : 13.2.2014 Registered on : 13.2.2014 Decided on : 13.1.2017. Duration : Y. M. D. 2 10 13 IN THE COURT OF SPECIAL JUDGE, KALYAN AT : KALYAN. [Presided over by : M.J.Mirza] SPECIAL CASE NO.23/2014 Exh. No. 21 The State of Maharashtra. Through : P.I.Bazarpeth Police Station, Kalyan. … Complainant. Vs. Dinesh Shatrughna Dalvi Age : 28 years, Occ. Agriculture, R/at : Village Wadeghar, Sapad Road, Opposite RKV Brick Kiln, Own House, Kalyan (W), Dist. Thane. … Accused. Appearance : Spl.P.P.Shri D.V. Bhangre for the State. Advocate Shri P.H. Rathod for the accused. Offences : ­ Punishable under Section 354­D, 354 of I.P.C. & Section 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. :JUDGMENT: [Delivered 13/1/2017, in the open Court] 1. The accused Dinesh Shatrughna Dalvi is facing the trial for the offences punishable under Sections 354­D & 354 of I.P.C. and Section 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2 Spl. Case 23/2014 [Judgment] 2. The case of the prosecution, in short is as under : That the informant/victim, aged about 16 years, lodged the FIR on 23/1/2014 stating therein that she is residing since her birth with her parents at Kalyan (W). She was studying in VPM Thane College and was going to attend Pinacal Engineering Classes, Tilak Chowk, Kalyan. Since last two months one boy was following her while proceeding to the class situated at Tilak Chowk, Kalyan and was teasing her. Therefore, she had stopped to going Pinacal Class. 3. On 22/1/2014 at 2:30 p.m. she while returning from her college at Lal Chowky and was proceeding by foot to her house and reached near grave yard, the said boy came behind her and pulled her odhani and went away on his bike. She frightened. One rickshawala who was standing there disclosed the name of the said boy Dinesh Shatrughna Dalvi. Then she disclosed the said incident to her father who arrived at 8:30 p.m. from his job and then she approached to the Bazarpeth Police Station. 4. P.S.O. of Bazarpeth Police Station after recording the FIR, registered the crime No. I­20/2014 under Sec. 354 of IPC and Sec.12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Further investigation entrusted to W ASI P.W.4 Smt. Surekha Sadashiv Sakpal who then arrested the accused on 17/1/2014 under arrest panchanama (Exh.11). Then she recorded the statements of the parents of the victims. She collected copy of school leaving certificate (Article A) for the purpose of birth date of the victim as 25/10/1997. After completion of investigation, she 3 Spl. Case 23/2014 [Judgment] filed chargesheet in this Special Court. 5. Charge (Exh.7) was framed by me which was read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. The accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. His defence is of false involvement as per his statement recorded under Section 313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Neither the accused stepped into the witness­ box nor examined any witness in his defence. 6. Heard learned Spl. P.P. Shri D.V. Bhangare for the State and learned Advocate Shri P. H. Rathod for the accused, at length. 7. The following points arise for my determination and my findings thereon are recorded against them for the reasons to follow:­ Points Findings 1. Whether the prosecution proved that the victim is minor aged 16 years ? .. Yes. 2. Whether the prosecution has proved that on 22/1/2014, at Tilak Chowk near Pinacal Engineering Class, Kalyan (W), the accused followed the minor victim informant, aged 16 years and attempted to contact her to foster personally interaction repeatedly with her, despite clear indication of disinterest by her, 4 Spl. Case 23/2014 [Judgment] punishable under Sec. 354­D(i) of .. Not proved. IPC ? 3. Whether the prosecution has proved that on 22/1/2014 at 2:30 p.m. at grave yard, near Lal Chowky, Kalyan (W) the accused followed the minor victim and pulled her beil (odhani) and used criminal force to her intending to outrage her modesty, .. Not proved. punishable under Sec. 354 of IPC ? 4. Whether the prosecution has proved that at relevant time the accused committed sexual harassment upon the minor victim/informant, punishable under Sec. 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012? .. Not proved. 5. What order ? ... Accused acquitted. : REASONS : 8. To substantiate the charge, prosecution has examined in all four witnesses, viz. PW.1 minor victim girl at Exh.9 who lodged the FIR at Exh.10, however she has not supported the case of the prosecution on the reason that the contents in the FIR was dictated by her father, however her signature was obtained by the police. 5 Spl. Case 23/2014 [Judgment] PW.2 Ramdas Trimbak Binnar at Exh.13, the father of the victim who is not direct witness to the incident but it is his case that the victim disclosed him about the incident and prior to that he had warned the accused regarding the incident occurred in the year 2013. He has also stated the birth date of the victim as 25/10/1997 and her birth place was at Hivre, Taluka­Sinnar, Dist. Nashik. P.W.3 Sau Vimal Ramdas Binnar at Exh.14, the mother of the victim who has brought on record that the victim had disclosed her about one boy who was harassing her for which the victim lodged the FIR with Bazarpeth Police Station. The last witness is P.W.4 Smt. Surekha Sadashiv Sakpal at Exh.16 the I.O. who has carried out the investigation as usual after arresting the accused and recording the statements of the witnesses. She also collected photostat copy of school leaving certificate of the victim showing her birth date as 25/10/1997. As to point No. 1 : 9. The victim has failed to bring on record in her testimony that her birth date as 25/10/1997. On the date of recording of her evidence, she has narrated her age as 20 years. Her father and mother have disclosed the birth date of the victim as 25/10/1997. The investigating officer has collected the photostat copy of school leaving certificate produced at Article­A showing her birth date as 25/10/1997, however, it has not been exhibited on the reason of want of certified or original one. This date has not been challenged by the defence in any manner. The investigating officer has not produced any proof of birth date of the victim on record except the photostat copy of the school leaving certificate at Article­A. Under 6 Spl. Case 23/2014 [Judgment] the circumstances, I hold that the birth date of the minor victim girl is 25/10/1997. The date of incident was two months prior to 22/1/2014. Thus, age of the victim on the date of the incident was 16 years 2 months and 27 days. Hence, she was minor on the date of alleged incident. Therefore, I answer the point No.1, in the affirmative. As to point No.2 to 4 :­ 10. I have taken all these points together as they are interlinked and to avoid repetition. The victim has failed to bring any incident of outraging her modesty or the accused attempting to contact her repeatedly despite her clear intention of disinterest and alleged sexual harassment on her. 11. The parents of the victim namely Ramdas and Sau. Vimal had come to know about the incident from the victim but the victim did not state so. The father has brought on record that on 22/1/2014 when the victim was returning to her home at Kalyan from Polytechnic College, Thane and arrived at Lal Chowky Kalyan, at that time, the accused pulled her odhani. This fact came to know by him at 9 p.m. when the victim disclosed him. According to him, he had warned the accused in the year 2013 and therefore he identified the accused. 12. The mother has also brought on record that the victim had disclosed her disclosing that one boy was harassing her for which she lodged the FIR with Bazarpeth Police Station. She further disclosed her that said boy used to come on bike and pulled her 7 Spl. Case 23/2014 [Judgment] odhani. She has denied the incident occurred in the year 2014 by stating that she does not recollect. According to her, her victim daughter disclosed the incident to her husband. She also identified the accused as he has married with the victim. 13. Except the testimony of the parents of the victim, there is nothing on record to hold that the accused committed the offences charge against him. It appears that the accused has now married with the victim and this may be the reason for the victim who has not supported the prosecution in toto. The victim being minor and in view of Sec.37 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, the trial was conducted in camera under child ­ friendly atmosphere. However, she failed to bring required ingredients of the offences charged against the accused. 14. Under the circumstances, there is nothing on record to hold the accused is guilty for any of the offences levelled against the accused as none of the witnesses have supported the case of the prosecution in all respect. Hence, I hold that the prosecution has utterly failed to prove the charges levelled against the accused by adducing cogent and reliable evidence. Hence, I answer the point Nos. 2 to 4, in the negative. 15. Resultantly, the accused deserves to be acquitted, and as such, I proceed to pass the following order : ORDER i] Accused Dinesh Shatrughna Dalvi is hereby acquitted vide Sec. 235(1) of Cr.P.C. of the offences punishable under Sections 8 Spl. Case 23/2014 [Judgment] 354 & 354­D of IPC & Section 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. ii] The bail bonds of the accused stand cancelled. iii] The accused shall execute his P.R. of Rs.15,000/­ to appear before the Higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect of appeal filed against this judgment as per S. 437­A of Cr.P.C. iv] Such bail shall remain in force for six months from today. Kalyan. [M.J.Mirza] Dt.:­13/1/2017. Special Judge, Under Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, Kalyan.

1 Sessions Case No. 30/2014 (Judgment) ( CNR -MHTH06-000538-2014) Presented on : 27/02/2014 Registered on : 27/02/2014 Decided on : 11/01/2019 Duration Y-04 M-10 D-15 IN THE COURT OF DISTRICT JUDGE-4 & ADDITIONAL SESSIONS JUDGE, KALYAN, AT KALYAN (Presided over by S. R. Pahade) Session Case No. 30/2014 Exh.No. (CNR- MHTH06-000538-2014 ) The State of Maharashtra (Through Kolsewadi Police Station) ......... Prosecution V/s. Kishor Tukaram Gaikwad, Age- 28 yrs., R/at. : Anandwadi, Mahatma Phule Chowk, Kalyan East. .......... Accused Offence punishable under Sections 363 of The Indian Penal Code and under Section 12 of The Prevention of Children from Sexual Offence Act. ----------------------------------------------------------- Smt. R. R. Bhoir, Ld. A.P.P. for State. Shri. S.H. Omble, Ld. Adv. for accused JUDGMENT (Delivered on 11th Day of January, 2019) 1] The accused stand prosecuted for the offences punishable under Sections 363 of The Indian Penal Code and under Section 12 of The 2 Sessions Case No. 30/2014 (Judgment) ( CNR -MHTH06-000538-2014) Prevention of Children from Sexual Offence Act. 2] Prosecution case in brief may be stated as under :- The complainant Ratan Harijan Bhalerao lodged complaint on 24.1.2014 that, his brother-in-law and his wife are dead, hence, their daughter namely Suvarna resides with him since her childhood. Her age was 16 years. She stopped the education. On 19.1.2014 the complainant had completed night duty and was sleeping at his house. The family members went to the marriage at the house of neighborer Rambhau Oval. Suvarna was also present for marriage. After solemnization of marriage, all family members returned to their house, but Suvarna did not return. At 3.00 p.m. Yamunabai Gaikwad and her daughter-in-law Laxmibai came at the house of complainant and informed that, Kishor and Suvarna went towards Vithalwadi Railway Station. They asked them to come with them for search. Accordingly, they went, but they did not find Suvarna and Kishor. Therefore, the complaint lodged against Kishor Gaikwad. 3] On the basis of statement a crime for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366 of The Indian Penal Code and under Section 12 of The Prevention of Children from Sexual Offence Act was registered with Kolsewadi Police Station vide C.R.No.I- 34/2014. 4] The investigation of the crime was handed over to PSI Shri. Sultane. He recorded statement of witnesses, collected documents, sent victim to medical examination and obtained report of medical examination. Ultimately, after completion of investigation, the investigating officer forwarded charge sheet. 3 Sessions Case No. 30/2014 (Judgment) ( CNR -MHTH06-000538-2014) 5] The charge was framed by my Ld. Predecessor against the accused for the offences punishable Section 363 of The Indian Penal Code and under Section 12 of The Prevention of Children from Sexual Offence Act at Exh. 18. The contents of charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. He pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. As there is no incriminating evidence, the statement of the accused U/Sec. 313 of Cr. P. C. is dispensed with. 6] The following points arise for determination and my findings are noted against each thereon for the reasons states herein below : POINTS FINDINGS 1) Whether the prosecution proves that the accused on 19/01/2014 at about 3.00 p.m. In the negative. kidnapped daughter of complainant's deceased brother-in-law namely Suvarna, the minor girl of 17 years from the lawful custody of complainant and his without without their consent or permission as alleged ? 2] Whether the prosecution proves that the accused committed sexual harassment to the In the negative. minor girl Suvarna as alleged ? 2) What order ? As per final order. : REAS O NS : 7] The prosecution in support of its case has examined two witnesses Ratan Haribhau Bhalerao (PW 1) at Exh. 20 and Suvarna Kishor Gaikwad (PW-2) at Exh.24. The prosecution also relied upon documentary evidence i.e. FIR Exh.21 and Adhar Card, Pan Card, school leaving certificates at Exh.27 to 29. 4 Sessions Case No. 30/2014 (Judgment) ( CNR -MHTH06-000538-2014) POINT NO. 1 and 2 :- 8] As per prosecution it is alleged that accused committed offence under Sections 363 of The Indian Penal Code and under Section 12 of The Prevention of Children from Sexual Offence Act. In order to prove offence punishable under Section 363 of The Indian penal Code, the prosecution has to prove that, the accused kidnapped victim from the lawful guardianship and in order to prove Section 12 of POCSO the burden of prosecution to prove that the accused committed sexual harassment upon a child. Accordingly, the evidence adduced by the prosecution is necessary to be scrutinized. 9] Ratan Haribhau Bhalerao (PW 1) deposed that Suvarna is daughter of his brother-in-law. There was marriage at the house of their neighborer on 19.1.2014. Therefore, family members and Suvarna went to attend the marriage. After marriage Suvarna did not come back, therefore, they took search and thereafter lodged missing report. He denied that, accused Kishor Gaikwad kidnapped Suvarna. In his cross-examination taken by APP, he admitted his signature, but denied the contents of FIR. Thus, his testimony is not helpful to the prosecutions case. The material witness Suvarna who is victim examined by prosecution at Exh.24 deposed that, her marriage was solemnized on 24.1.2014 with accused Kishor and her date of birth is 4.3.1995. She further deposed that, she has one daughter. She further specifically deposed that, she is living peacefully with accused. As such, her testimony is also not helpful to the prosecutions case. 10] Considering the entire evidence and the fact that the complainant and victim have not supported the prosecution. There is no evidence to prove that, accused kidnapped victim without consent of her parents. Hence, I come to the conclusion that the prosecution has failed to prove the offence 5 Sessions Case No. 30/2014 (Judgment) ( CNR -MHTH06-000538-2014) against the accused. Therefore I answer point No. 1 and 2 in the negative and proceed to pass the following order : - ORDER 1) The accused Kishor Tukaram Gaikwad is hereby acquitted of the offence punishable under Secs. 363 of The Indian Penal Code and under Section 12 of The Prevention of Children from Sexual Offence Act vide Sec.235 (1) of the Cr. P. C. 2) The bail bonds of the accused stands cancelled. 3) Accused to furnish fresh P.R. and S.B. of Rs.15,000/- as per Sec.437(A) of Cr. P. Code. Date : 11/01/2019 (S. R. Pahade) Place : Kalyan District Judge - 4 & Addl. Sessions Judge, Kalyan
