Spl.C.NO.28/2014 (Judg.) 1 CNR No. MHTH06­000558­2014 Presented on : 24/02/2014 Registered on : 24/02/2014 Decided on : 25/05/2018 Duration : Y. M. D. 4 ­ 3 ­ 1 IN THE COURT OF ADDL.SESSIONS JUDGE, KALYAN AT : KALYAN (Presided over by D.S.Ghumare) Special Case No.28/2014 CNR No. MHTH06­000558­2014 Exh. No. The State of Maharashtra (Through Ulhasnagar Police Station) .... Prosecution V/s. Nabihussain @ Sheru Mohamed Rajjak Khan, Age­ 23 years, R/at: Behind Fire brigade office, Opp. AmanTalkies, Ulhasnagar­2. …. Accused. ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ Shri.Kulkarni Sachin ,Ld.APP. for State. Smt.Borse­Jadhav Ld.Adv. for the accused. ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ JUDGMENT (Delivered on 25th day of May, 2018) 1] The accused Nabihussain @ Sheru Mohamed Rajjak Khan stands charged for the offenses punishable under Secs.376 of the Indian Penal Code besides Sec.4, 5(j)(ii) r/w. Sec. 6 of the Protection of Spl.C.NO.28/2014 (Judg.) 2 CNR No. MHTH06­000558­2014 Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] The prosecution’s case, in brief, is that the informant P.W.1 Kharunissa has five daughters and two sons. The accused is husband of her eldest daughter Asmin and they both were residing in front of their house. When Asmin was pregnant, the informant P.W.1 Kharunissa's another minor daughter, the victim, used to go to the house of Asmin to help her in the household work. After some days, the informant P.W.1 Kharunissa felt that there was change in the victim, and therefore, she asked her about her wellbeing. The victim then told her that since last five months the accused used to commit rape upon her whenever her sister Asmin used to go out of the house. The victim further told the informant P.W.1 Kharunissa that when Asmin was admitted in the hospital, at that time also the accused committed rape upon her and he also threatened her not to disclose this to anybody otherwise he will beat her, and therefore, she did not disclose to anybody about committing rape upon her by the accused. Therefore, the informant P.W.1 Kharunisa lodged report against the accused with Ulhasnagar Police Station. On the basis of her report a crime against the accused for offences punishable under Sections Secs.376 of the Indian Penal Code besides Sec.4, 5(j)(ii) r/w. Sec. 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 was registered vide C.R.No.I­ 305/2013. 3] The investigation of the crime was conducted by P.S.I. Shri. M.J.Jagtap (PW.7). During the course of investigation he went to the spot and prepared spot panchanama (Exh.39). He also prepared sketch of the spot of incident (Exh.40). He seized clothes of the victim under Spl.C.NO.28/2014 (Judg.) 3 CNR No. MHTH06­000558­2014 seizure panchanama Exh.41. On 18/01/2013 he sent the victim girl for medical examination at Central Hospital, Ulhasnagar. He collected birth certificate of the victim girl from her school. He recorded statements of witnesses. The accused was in jail in another crime and therefore, he took custody of the accused by orders of the court. During his custody, accused gave memorandum to produce clothes which he wore at the time of incident. Accordingly, he prepared memorandum and seizure panchanama. He then got recorded the statement of victim girl from Child Welfare Committee, Thane. He then forwarded clothes of the victim girl, her blood sample, vagina swab, pubic hair, nail clippings and semen to the Chemical Analyser, Mumbai vide letters Exh.43 and 44. The Investigating officer also sent blood samples of accused and victim girl for DNA profile vide letter Exh.45. Ultimately, after completion of investigation, the investigating officer filed report under section 173 of the Code of Criminal Procedure in the court of Ld. Judicial Magistrate, First Class, Ulhasnagar, who after complying the provisions of Sections 207 of the Code of Criminal Procedure committed present case to the Court of Sessions under section 209 of Cr.P.C. 4] The Charge Exh.8 was framed against the accused for the offence punishable U/Secs. 376 of the Indian Penal Code besides Sec.4, 5(j)(ii) r/w. Sec. 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. The charge was read over and explained to the accused Nabihussain @ Sheru. He pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. Upon completion of the prosecution evidence, the statement of accused U/Sec. 313(1)(c) of Cr.P.C was recorded. The defence of the accused is that of total denial and false implication in the crime. Spl.C.NO.28/2014 (Judg.) 4 CNR No. MHTH06­000558­2014 5] The following points arise for determination and my findings are noted against each thereon for the reasons states herein below : POINTS FINDINGS 1) Whether the prosecution proves that from 5 months before 19/08/2013, the accused in his residential house situated behind fire brigade office,Room No.12,Ulhasnagar­1, committed rape on the victim girl, aged 12 years ? Proved. 2) Whether the prosecution proves that during the aforesaid date, time and place, the accused committed aggravated penetrative sexual assault on the minor victim by making her pregnant as a consequence of sexual assault ? Proved. 3) What order ? As per final order. :REASONS: 6] The prosecution in support of its case has examined in all seven witnesses. They are the informant P.W.1­ Kharunissa Salauddin Khan, P.W.2, the victim, Head Master of Municipal School P.W.3­ Rajendra Mulchand Sonavane, neighbour of the informant P.W.4 – Sheela Ashok Gupta, P.W.5­Nirmala Tayappa Koli, Medical officer P.W.6 Dr. Anjali Chaudhari and the investigating officer P.W.7­ Mahendra Jaiwantgirao Jagtap. POINT NOS. 1 & 2 : 7] Both the points are dealt with simultaneously to avoid Spl.C.NO.28/2014 (Judg.) 5 CNR No. MHTH06­000558­2014 repetition of discussion of the evidence, which is common for them. 8] The victim was medically examined by P.W.6 Dr. Anjali Chaudhary, Medical Officer. She has deposed that on 18/11/2013 when she was attached to Central Hospital, Ulhasnagar as a Medical officer, a female child, the victim, was brought to the hospital for medical examination at about 12.00 p.m. by WPC 2826. She further testified that the child victim gave history of sexual assault by known person about 9 to 10 months prior and the last sexual assault was stated to be 4 to 5 months back. She further testified that on examination, she found that her uterus was 26 weeks. The child victim was admitted in the hospital for gynecological examination. The medical certificate bears her signature and it is at Exh.37. She had also brought MLC register which depicts the entry corresponding to the entries made in the medical certificate. 9] The informant P.W.1­ Kharunissa Khan is mother of the victim. She testified that she resides at Ulhasnagara­1 along with her family. She is having five daughters and two sons. Her elder daughter Asmin was married with accused and she went to reside with him at Bhiwandi. The informant P.W.1 further testified that her second daughter Afrin used to go to the house of the accused to help Asmin after delivery of her child. However, she denied the incident of committing rape by the accused on her second daughter Afrin. She also denied that the accused committed rape on her minor daughter, the victim, and she became pregnant and delivered a child. She also denied that accused used to give threat to the victim that if she will disclose to any body Spl.C.NO.28/2014 (Judg.) 6 CNR No. MHTH06­000558­2014 about the said act, he will kill her. Thus, the informant P.W.1 Kharunissa, who is the star witness of the prosecution, had failed to support the prosecution case in its material particulars. Ld. A.P.P. has declared P.W.1 Kharunissa hostile and cross­examined her. During cross­examination, she denied the entire incident which she narrated while lodging the report. When she was confronted with her earlier statement wherein she incriminated the accused, she denied having made it. From the cross­examination of the informant P.W.1 Kharunissa, mother of minor victim, nothing material was elicited so as to incriminate the accused in the crime. 10] P.W.2, the victim, has testified that she has three sisters. Asma is her elder sister. Her age is 32 years. She deposed that the accused Shiru is her brother­in­law. He is married to her sister Asma. His house is near to her house. When her sister Asma was pregnant and when she had delivered a child, she used to go to her house to do the household work. When her sister used to go to the hospital, she used to be alone at the house of her sister Asma. When her sister was not at her house, the accused came there when she was alone. But she denied that at that time accused removed her clothes and had committed sexual intercourse against her wishes. She also denied that at that time accused had threatened that if she had disclosed about their sexual relations, then he would kill her. 11] Even though the victim had denied that the accused had raped her but she had volunteered in her testimony that she had sexual relations with him on her own accord. Spl.C.NO.28/2014 (Judg.) 7 CNR No. MHTH06­000558­2014 12] P.W.3­ Rajendra Mulchand Sonavane, the Head Master of the school, has testified that after admission of student to the school, entries are recorded about name, caste, date of birth, birth of place and other things in general register. The entries of date of leaving school is also made in this register. He has brought general register of their school. He further testified that in Municipal Corp. School No. 27 Afrin Salauddin Shaikh had taken admission in first standard of the school on 07/07/2010. She had left the school on 19/11/2013. As per general register, her date of birth is 01/01/2002. Her caste is Muslim. He has brought xerox copy of page No.42 of the said general register. The said copy is verified from the Superintendent of the Court and is also verified by the Presiding Officer from the original register which is marked as Exh.28. 13] Ld. Advocate for the accused Smt. Borse­jadhav has submitted that the informant P.W.1 Kharunissa, who is mother of the victim girl and the victim P.W.2 herself had not supported the prosecution case as they have deposed that the accused had not raped the victim. She also contended that at the most the sexual relationship was consensual one. But the fact remains that whether the accused had sexually assaulted the victim by having sexual intercourse with her. As far as this fact is considered, I find that it is established that the accused had committed sexual intercourse with the victim and same stands proved by following facts. [i] The victim herself had volunteered in her examination­in­ chief that she had sexual relation with the accused on her own accord. Further in cross­examination she has also stated that she had become Spl.C.NO.28/2014 (Judg.) 8 CNR No. MHTH06­000558­2014 pregnant from the accused and that she was loving him. This part of the evidence of the victim clearly establishes that the victim and the accused had sexual relations with each other from which she had become pregnant. [ii] Second is that P.W. Sheela and P.W.5 Nirmala had also testified that when they both were sitting in the house of Urmila, the informant P.W.1 Kharunissa asked them to accompany to police station and had told them that her son­in­law had made her daughter, the victim, pregnant. Their evidence is relevant under Sec. 6 of the Indian Evidence Act as it is so connected with the fact in issue of sexual assault upon the victim by the accused so as to form the part of same transaction and as such is relevant. It is pertinent to note here that they have no reason to depose against the accused as they are the independent witnesses. They deposed the fact what happened at that time. So, their evidence cannot be discarded on the material aspect of finding that the victim was pregnant. [iii] The most important witness i.e. Medical officer P.W.6 Dr. Anjali Chaudhary, who medically examined the victim, has testified that the victim herself gave history of sexual assault since last 9 to 10 months and the last sexual assault was 4 to 5 months back. She further testified that on gynecological examination, it is found that the uterus of the victim was 26 weeks which support the prosecution case. Thus, the sexual relationship between the victim and the accused stands corroborated and established by the evidence of Medical officer P.W.6. [iv] Similarly, the Investigating Officer P.W.7 Mahendra Jagtap has also testified about the medical examination of the victim from the Spl.C.NO.28/2014 (Judg.) 9 CNR No. MHTH06­000558­2014 Government hospital i.e. central Hospital, Ulhasnagar. He sent the blood sample of the victim and accused Shiru for DNA test. From his evidence, it is clear that the victim delivered a child and blood sample of child was also sent for DNA. He also testified that he had forwarded clothes of the victim girl, her blood sample, vagina swab, pubic hair, nail clippings and semen to the Chemical Analyser, Mumbai vide letters Exh.43 and 44. The Investigating officer also sent blood samples of accused and victim girl for DNA profile vide letter Exh.45. The victim girl had delivered a child on 04/02/2014. Thus, the prosecution story regarding sexual relation of the accused with the victim P.W.2 is fully corroborated by Investigating Officer P.W.7 Jagtap. 14] It would be pertinent to note here that in the cross­ examination, the victim has stated that she was having love affair with accused Shiru and she had consented him to have sexual relations with her. However, at the time of said incident, the victim was minor and the consent of minor is not a consent. To prove the age of the victim, the prosecution has examined the Head Master of the Municipal School in which the victim was studying. The Head master P.W.3 Rajendra Mulchand Sonavane has deposed that the victim had taken admission in first standard of the school on 07/07/2010 and she left the school on 19/11/2013. He further deposed that as per the general register of the school, the date of birth of the victim is 01/01/2002. To substantiate his contention, the Head Master of the school has brought original register of the school with him which depicts that the date of birth of the victim is 01/01/2002. The xerox copy of the said original register is produced on record by the P.W.3 Rajendra Sonavane, head master of the school. The Spl.C.NO.28/2014 (Judg.) 10 CNR No. MHTH06­000558­2014 same is verified from the superintendent of the court and also it is verified by the Presiding Officer and then it is marked as Exh.28. 15] The Ld.Adv.Smt. Borse­Jadhav for the accused submitted that in the said certificate name of the victim is not correctly written. Therefore, the documentary evidence adduced by the prosecution about the age by production of Birth Certificate and the verified extract of general register issued by the Municipal school, though exhibited, is of no value for the reason that the name of he victim varies since the victim's surname is 'Khan' and not 'Shaikh'. True there is change in surname but then considering the fact that the parents might have told their surname as 'Shaikh' instead of 'Khan' to the school authority while admitting the child in the school and so to my mind that does not make much difference. There was no reason for the investigating officer to collect false record about the birth date of the victim. 16] I find substance in the submission of Ld. A.P.P. Sachin Kulkarni for the State that Section 35 of the Indian Evidence Act refers to the relevancy of entry in Public record made in the performance of duty. Under Section 35, a register or official book maintained in terms of a statute or by a statutory authority in regular course of business would be a relevant fact. Therefore, the verified copy of the extract of general register of Municipal School could be relevant and considered for it does satisfy the requirements of Section 35 of the Indian Evidence Act. He contented that it is reliable evidence on record to show that the date of birth was recorded in the Municipal register is thus relevant under section 35 and as such are vital pieces of evidence, which clinches Spl.C.NO.28/2014 (Judg.) 11 CNR No. MHTH06­000558­2014 the issue to prove the birth date of the victim PW.2, the victim as to be 01/01/2002. 17] Ld A.P.P. Sachin Kulkarni further made reference to the decision of their Lordships of Apex Court in case of in Birad Mal Singhvi vs. Anand Purohit [AIR 1988 SC 1796] , wherein it is held : "...To render a document admissible under Section 35, three conditions must be satisfied, firstly, entry that is relied on must be one in a public or other official book, register or record, secondly, it must be an entry stating a fact in issue or relevant fact, and thirdly, it must be made by a public servant in discharge of his official duty, or any other person in performance of a duty specially enjoined by law. " He contended that as the extract of general register Ex.28 fulfills all three conditions it is admissible piece of evidence. 18] The Court has to start with such presumption. The genuine­ ness of the verified copies has been ascertained as per the procedure laid down under the provisions of Indian Evidence Act regarding proof of documents. Ld. A.P.P. Sachin Kulkarni for the State is quite correct in his submission that the genuineness of the extract of original general reg­ ister maintained by the Municipal School Authority Ex.28 being verified copy of public record produced on record stands proved as that document had the presumption of correctness as stated above. Thus as the extract of page from general register maintained by the Municipal School is public document and its secondary evidence is allowed, it has been ex­ Spl.C.NO.28/2014 (Judg.) 12 CNR No. MHTH06­000558­2014 hibited and same is read in evidence. I do not have any doubt regarding genuineness of this document. Thus, the extract of original general regis­ ter is trust worthy evidence regarding the age of the victim. Considering the said birth date, the age of the victim at the time of occurrence did not exceed 12 years. 19] In the present case in hand the victim is of tender age not exceeding 12 at the time of offence and seems have had no motive to falsely involve the accused in crime. It would be apposite to state here that the courts while trying an accused on charges of rape and offences against child must deal with such cases with utmost sensitivity. The courts should examine the broader probabilities of a case and not get swayed by minor contradictions or insignificant discrepancies in the statement of the victim and the documentary evidence, which are not of a fatal nature, to throw out an otherwise reliable prosecution case. 20] Next Ld. Advocate Smt. Borse­Jadhav for the accused submitted that the evidence on record clearly establishes that the victim P.W.2 herself in love with the accused and they had sexual intercourse clearly proves that the same was consensual sex and not a rape at all. More so when admittedly the victim has stated in her evidence that she was loving the accused Shiru. She also submitted that considering the fact that the sexual relationship was with consent of each other, it can not be said that the accused Nabihussain @ Shiru had committed offence punishable under Section 376 of I.P.C. and further committed aggravated penetrative sexual assault. Spl.C.NO.28/2014 (Judg.) 13 CNR No. MHTH06­000558­2014 21] As against this Ld. A.P.P. Shri.Kulkarni for the State submitted that in the present case the question of consent for sexual intercourse is out of question because the victim P.W.2 was below the age of 12 years. He submitted that considering the extract of general register Exh.28 maintained by the school, it is clear that the age of the on the date alleged offence is below 12 years old. He submitted that as the victim is not above 15 years, consent becomes immaterial, in view of placentum sixthly of Section 375 of I.P.C, which defines rape. Thus, considering the factum of age of the victim, the said consent even if is proved can not be said to be consent as intended by Section 375 of I.P.C. as the consent was of a girl, who is below the age of 16 years. 22] In the cases of sexual assault on children, it is the psychology of child to obey the orders of the rapists if she is his custodian, may be father, uncle, teacher or warden of the hostel. It is also seen that most of such children who are dependent on abusers abide by their orders. There are many reasons for children not disclosing the fact of sexual abuse to their relatives or friends. One of the reasons is that they are threatened. The other reason is that in many cases, they are dependent on the persons who had sexually abused them. It is also seen that there is threat from the abuser to the near and dear ones of the sexually abused child. In the present case, the victim is younger sister of the wife of the accused and so she must not have told about sexual assault to any one until she becomes pregnant. Therefore, the contention of the Ld. Adv. Smt. Borse­Jadhav for the accused that the victim had been willingly had sexual relationship with accused with her consent has no merits particularly when she was not of the age to give consent for Spl.C.NO.28/2014 (Judg.) 14 CNR No. MHTH06­000558­2014 sexual relationship. 23] Even if that is held to be proved, question of consent as has been rightly submitted by Ld.A.P.P. Shri.Kulkarni is immaterial, as the offence would fall within the clause sixthly of the definition of rape given in Sec.375 of I.P.C. Therefore, I hold that the prosecution has been able to prove that the accused had committed rape and aggravated penetrative sexual assault on the victim P.W.2 by making her pregnant by the sexual assault. Hence, point No.1 and 2 are answered in the affirmative. 24] This takes me to hear the accused on the point of sentence. Kalyan. (D. S. Ghumre) 25/05/2018 Addl. Sessions Judge, Kalyan 25] The accused has submitted that the lenient view may be taken for imposing the punishment. The accused has submitted that his mother and sister are dependents upon him besides his wife and children and so minimum punishment be imposed upon him. 26] Ld.Adv.Smt. Borse­Jadhav has submitted that the accused did not have any criminal antecedent and he is the first time offender. She also submitted that the offence of rape has been committed as a consequence of consent given out of love relationship between the accused and the victim PW.2. She also submitted that considering the age of the accused, it would not be proper to impose maximum Spl.C.NO.28/2014 (Judg.) 15 CNR No. MHTH06­000558­2014 punishment prescribed by the offence by law. She also submitted that the accused be imposed for punishment for the period he had already undergone in prison as a under trial prisoner as he has completed four years in the jail. 27] As against this Ld.A.P.P. Shri. Kulkarni submitted that the offence is serious and deserves no leniency. More so, when the victim of the crime PW.2 is hardly not more than 12 yrs. of age. He submitted that stringent punishment should be imposed upon the accused taking into account the fact that the crime of violence upon woman needs to be severely dealt with. He also submitted that protection of society and deterring the criminal is the avowed object of the law and for that purpose appropriate sentence needs to be imposed upon the accused of the heinous crimes of sexual violence. 28] I have considered the rival submissions of Ld.A.P.P. Shri.Kulkarni and Ld. Adv. Smt.Borse­Jadhav. Even though the Ld. A.P.P. has argued that maximum punishment should be imposed upon the accused contending that it is heinous crime of rape on a innocent helpless girl of tender age not more than 12 years. 31] Considering the rival submission of both parties and the facts and circumstances, it would not be appropriate to award maximum punishment to the accused. On the other hand, it would be appropriate to impose minimum punishment prescribed under law. Section 6 of the P.O.C.S.O. Act provides that punishment shall not be less than Ten years, if the accused is found guilty for the offence of commission of Spl.C.NO.28/2014 (Judg.) 16 CNR No. MHTH06­000558­2014 aggravated penetrative sexual assault. So also Section 376 (n) of I.P.C. provides punishment for rape shall not be less than ten years. Therefore, the accused Nasibulla @ Shiru deserves punishment of ten years for offence punishable under Section 6 of the P.O.C.S.O. Act and also punishment of ten years for offence punishable under Section 376 of I.P.C. Besides the above substantiative punishment the accused is also liable for the punishment of fine of Rs.5,000/­ for each of the offence. In facts and circumstances of the case the substantive sentence shall run concurrently. In the result, the following order is made : :ORDER: 1) Vide section 235 (2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the accused Nabihussain @ Shiru Moahmmed Rajjak Khan is convicted for the offence punishable under Section 376 of I.P.C. and is sentenced to suffer Rigorous Imprisonment for the period of Ten years and shall pay fine of Rs. 5,000/­ in default of payment of fine to suffer Simple Imprisonment for the period of three months. 3) Vide section 235(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure the accused Nabihussain @ Shiru Moahmmed Rajjak Khan is convicted under Sec. 5(j)(ii) for the offence punishable under Section 6 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act,2012 and is sentenced to suffer Rigorous Imprisonment for the period of Ten years and shall pay fine of Rs.5,000/­ in default of payment of fine to suffer Simple Imprisonment for the period of three months. Spl.C.NO.28/2014 (Judg.) 17 CNR No. MHTH06­000558­2014 4) All the abovesaid sentences shall run concurrently. 5) The accused is in jail since 02/12/2013 and the said period undergone by him shall be given as set off U/Sec.428 of Cr.P.C. 6) Muddemal property, if any, be destroyed after appeal period is over. Kalyan. ( D.S.Ghumre) Dt.25/05/2018 Addl.Sessions Judge,Kalyan. Spl.C.NO.28/2014 (Judg.) 18 CNR No. MHTH06­000558­2014

1 Spl.Case No.25/2015 Judgment Presented on : 27/02/2015 Registered on : 27/02/2015 Decided on : 22/09/2016 Duration : Y. M. D. 1 – 6 ­ 27 IN THE COURT OF ADDL.SESSIONS JUDGE, KALYAN (Presided over by D.S.Ghumare) Session Case No.25/2015 Exh.No.24 The State of Maharashtra (Through Bazarpeth Police Station) .... Prosecution V/s. Jayesh Ramrao More, Age­ 26 yrs., R/at: 503, Sudhanshu­Kiran Building, Opposite of Mohan Rigency, Kalyan (W), Dist. Thane. .... Accused ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ Shri.Kulkarni Ld.A.P.P.for State. Shri.M.M.Deshmukh, Ld.Adv.for accused. ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ JUDGMENT (Delivered on 22nd day of September , 2016) 1] The accused stands charged for the offence punishable under Sections 376 of the Indian Penal Code, and under Section 4 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offence Act. 2] The prosecution’s case is that the prosecutrix PW.3 Janhvi, aged 13 years, is the daughter of the informant P.W.1­ Hemlata Sunil Sonawane and PW.2 Sunil Sonawane. The family resided in Mohan 2 Spl.Case No.25/2015 Judgment Rijency, situated at Adharwadi, Kalyan(W). Husband of P.W.1 Hemlata , Sunil is police Head­Constable and is attached to Shahunagar Police Station, Brihan Mumbai. The F.I.R. further narrates that prosecutrix Janhavi was studying in 8th standard in Don Bosko School in the year 2014 and her age at that time was 13 years. The informant P.W.1 Hemlata was doing social work was required to stay out of house for long hours. As the informant P.W.1 Hemlata and her husband Sunil were not remaining in the house often for long time, they had given to prosecutrix Janhvi a mobile phone bearing No. 9594048184. At the relevant time, particularly from 11/11/2014 to 23/11/2014 the informant P.W.1 Hemlata used to frequently go to Lower Parel for getting medical treatment. The prosecution further case is that on 23/11/2014 at about 7.30 p.m. informant P.W.1 Hemlata had found one miss call on the mobile phone of prosecutrix Janhavi from phone bearing No.8976604090. She then made a call on that phone and learnt that the said call was made by accused Jayesh More, who told her that he is in love of her daughter PW.3 Janhvi and desired to marry her. Thereupon, the informant P.W.1 Hemlata asked Jayesh to meet her to discuss the affair. She had also informed about this telephone call to her husband PW.2 Sunil. Then they had asked daughter Janhavi after taking her in to confidence, whether she knows Jayesh More , upon which Janhavi told that she is in love with Jayesh More and they are going away to marry each other. Thereafter, the informant P.W.1 Hemlata went to the Janhavi's school Don Bosko and inquired about on going love­affair between Janhavi and the accused Jayesh, who told her that they are in love relationship since prior to 3 to 4 months and she had seen them roll together. 3 Spl.Case No.25/2015 Judgment The F.I.R. further proceeds to narrate that on 24/11/2014 when the informant P.W.1 Hemlata and her husband Sunil had asked Janhavi whether she had physical relationship with the accused, she had told them that accused Jayesh is a good boy and he is going to marry her and so she had kept physical relationship with him. Then they asked Janhavi the address of the accused Jayesh, and went to his house from where they took him to the Bazarpeth Police Station, where, the informant P.W.1 Hemlata lodged report Exh.17 in that regard with Bazarpeth Police Station. On the basis of the said report crime was registered against the accused Jayesh More vide C.R.No.I­ 293/14 for offences punishable U/Secs.376 of I.P.C. and U/Sec.4 of P.O.C.S.O. 3] The investigation of the crime was conducted by A.P.I.Narvade. He firstly sent the prosecutrix Janhavi for medical examination at Rukhminibai Hospital, Kalyan. The accused Jayesh More was arrested in connection with the crime on same day. He was also got medically examined from Rukhminibai Hospital,Kalyan. During the course of investigation, the panchanama of the scene of offence Exh.24, seizure panchanama of clothes of accused Jayesh Exh.25, seizure panchanama of clothes of prosecutrix PW.3 Janhavi Exh.26 were prepared in the presence of panch witnesses. He also sent the clothes of the accused Jayesh and prosecutrix Janhavi to F.S.L. Mumbai for its analysis. The investigation officer PW.4 A.P.I. R.S.Narvade recorded the supplementary statement of the informant P.W.1 Hemlata and statements of other witnesses. He also got recorded the statement of the prosecutrix PW.3 Janhavi U/Sec.164 of Cr.P.C. In due course, the investigation officer collected the medical examination report of the prosecutrix PW.3 4 Spl.Case No.25/2015 Judgment Janhvi and the accused Jayesh from the medical officer of the Rukhminibai Hospital,Kalyan. He then collected C.D.R. reports in respect of telephonic calls between the accused Jayesh and prosecutrix Janhavi from the Mobile Phone company. He had collected C.A. reports and produced the same on record. He also collected birth certificate of prosecutrix Janhavi as a age proof her minor­ship. Ultimately, after completion of the investigation, the investigation officer submitted final report under section 173 of Cr.P.C against the accused in the court of Ld. Judicial Magistrate, First Class Kalyan, who after complying the provisions of Sections 207 of the Code of Criminal Procedure committed present case to the Court of Sessions under section 209 of CrPC. 4] The Charge Exh.14 was framed against the accused for the offences punishable under section U/Secs.376 of I.P.C. & U/Sec. 4 of P.O.C.S.O.. The charge was read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. The accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. The statement of the accused U/Sec.313 of Cr.P.C. was recorded after examination of the witnesses of prosecution. The defence of the accused is that of total denial and false implication in the crime. 5] The following points arise for determination and my findings are given against each thereon for the reasons given thereunder. POINTS FINDINGS 1) Whether the prosecution proves that prior to 2 to 3 months of 24/11/2014 and on the same day at the house of prosecutrix Janhvi at Mohan Rijency, A/4/702, Adharwadi Jail Road, near Don Bosco School, Kalyan under 5 Spl.Case No.25/2015 Judgment the pretext of marriage committed rape on the prosecutrix minor girl Janhavi aged 13 yrs. ? No. 2) Whether the prosecution proves that the accused on the above said dates, time and place, committed penetrative sexual assault on the prosecutrix minor girl Janhavi, aged 13 years ? No. 3) What order ? As per final order. REASONS POINT NO.1 :­ 6] To bring home the guilt of the accused, the prosecution examined in all four witnesses. They are the informant PW.1 Hemlata Sunil Sonawane, PW.2 Sunil Vitthal Sonawane, PW.3 prosecutrix Jhanvi and Investigating Officer P.W. 4­ R.S.Narwade. 7] The informant P.W.1 Hemlata Sunil Sonawane has testified that she reside alongwith her husband Sunil Sonawane and daughter Janhavi reside at Mohan Rejency, situated at Adharwadi, Kalyan(W) since last 10 yrs. She has testified that she does social work while her husband Sunil is police Head­Constable attached to Shahunagar Police Station, Brihan Mumbai. She has testified that her daughter Janhavi aged 13 yrs. was studying in 8th standard in Don Bosko School in the year 2014. She has stated that as they both used to be outside the house often and so had given a mobile phone having No.9594048184 to their daughter Janhvi. She had also deposed that from 11/11/2014 to 23/11/2014 she had to go frequently to Lower Parel for getting medical 6 Spl.Case No.25/2015 Judgment treatment. She has further testified that on 23/11/2014 at about 7.30 pm, she had found one miss call from a phone bearing No. 8976604090. She then made a call on that mobile phone and inquired with the person on that phone, who told her name as to be Jayesh More. At that time she had told him to meet her to discuss the matter. 8] The informant PW.1 Hemlata further failed to support the prosecution case, as he denied that the accused Jayesh had told her that he is in love with her daughter PW.3 Janhavi and that he intends to marry with her. She has further denied that Janhavi told them that she is in love with accused Jayesh and they are going to marry. She also denied that she had gone to the Janhavi's school at Don Bosko and inquired with her friend Tanu Santosh Gedam about love relation between Janhavi and the accused Jayesh, whereupon Tanu told her that since prior to 3 to 4 months they both were love relation between Janhavi and Jayesh and both were seen moving together. 9] P.W.3­ Sunil Vitthal Sonawane also did not support the prosecution case. His testimony is on the same line as per the evidence of his wife informant P.W.1­Hemlata. He has only additionally stated about the age, education and school timings of his daughter. He has specifically denied that he was called at Bazarpeth Police Station on 25/11/2014 and that his statement was recorded as per his say. 10] The prosecution has examined P.W.2 Janhavi, who is victim of the crime. She has testified that Tanvi Gedam was her friend and she used to visit her house. But, then she has denied that in the year 2014 7 Spl.Case No.25/2015 Judgment said Tanvi had introduced her with the accused Jayesh More. She also denied that the accused Jayesh More used to come to the house of Tanvi and used to talk with her and that they were in each others Love . Thus , the informant P.W.1­ Hemlata and P.W.2 Janhavi and P.W.3 Sunil have not at all supported the prosecution case. 11] In such background of the testimony of the prosecution witnesses, it is rather unfortunate for the prosecution that prosecutrix PW.2 Jhanhvi, her mother­ the informant PW.1 Hemlata and her father P.W.3­ Sunil did not support the prosecution case. In their testimony, they all denied about the love and physical relationship between the prosecutrix P.W.2 Janhavi and accused Jayesh. They also denied that accused Jayesh used to come to their house and under the pretext of marriage he had kept physical relationship with prosecutrix P.W.2 Jhanvi. 12] Ld.A.P.P. Shri.Kulkarni declared P.W.1­Hemlata, prosecutrix P.W.2­Janhavi and P.W.3 Sunil as hostile witnesses and cross­examined them at length. When they are confronted with their earlier statement wherein they incriminated the accused they denied having made. The searching cross­examination of these witnesses by Ld.A.P.P. did not yield any benefit to the prosecution as nothing material was elicited there from incriminating against the accused. Thus, there is no evidence against the accused to substantiate the charge against him of commission of rape upon the prosecutrix P.W.2 Janhavi under the pretext of marriage, against her will. 8 Spl.Case No.25/2015 Judgment 13] Here it may be stated that no purpose would have been served by referring to the evidence of the I.O. P.W.4 A.P.I. R.S.Naravade as the material witnesses of the prosecution failed to support the prosecution case. He testified about all the details of the investigation carried out by him, but it not worth the name to substantiate the prosecution case against the accused as all other witnesses including the victim of crime. It would be pertinent to note here that even if the circumstantial evidence, which includes panchanama of the scene of offence Exh.24, genuineness of which is admitted under section 294 of Cr.P.C. and , CA reports Exh.28 (colly) is considered, still it would not have yield any benefit to the prosecution as there is no incriminating substantiative evidence against the accused. 14] For these reasons, I hold that the prosecution has miserably failed to bring home beyond reasonable doubt, the guilt of the accused for the offence punishable U/Sec.376 of I.P.C. and U/Sec.4 of P.O.C.S.O Act. Hence, point No.1 is answered in the negative. In the result, the following order is made : :ORDER: 1) The accused­ Jayesh Ramrao More is hereby acquitted of the offence punishable U/Secs.376 of the Indian Penal Code & U/Sec.4 of P.O.C.S.O. Act vide Section 235 (1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure Code. 2) The Accused is in jail and is ordered to be released forthwith, if not required in any other case. 9 Spl.Case No.25/2015 Judgment 3) The accused shall furnish P.B. and S.B. of Rs.15,000/­ (Rs.Fifteen Thousand only) within two weeks vide Sec. 437(A) of Code of Cr.P.C. for his appearance before the Hon’ble Appellate Court and it shall be in force for six months period. 4) The Muddemal property viz. Samsung mobile phone having IMEI No. 352384050865957 and other mobile of Nokia Company having IMEI No.89910391110013353204 be returned to the accused Jayesh More after the expiry of the period of appeal. The remaining muddemal property cloths etc. being worthless be disposed off after the period of appeal is over. Kalyan. ( D. S. Ghumare ) Dt. 22/9/2016. Addl. Session Judge, Kalyan

P.S.O. Murbad Police Station registered this offence vide Crime No. I ­ 135 /2015, on the report of complainant father Sharad Ambo Wagh. 2] The story of the prosecution in short is that, complaint family is resident of village Dangurle and their earning is from agricultural labour. The victim daughter Pama left her schooling education prior to three years of the incident, and thus, she used to remain at house. 3] On 11/10/2015, the complainant parents went to their labour work and returned back to home at about 6 p.m. They learnt from younger child Ravi that their daughter Pama left the house at 12 noon, but since then she did not return .. 3/­ .. 3 .. Atro. Special Case No. 31/2016 CNR NO. ­ MHTH060006592016 ( Judgment ) back. The complainant searched for her with neighbouring persons and close relatives, but in vain. Then, police report was made on 17/10/2015, on which crime No. I – 135/2015 came to be registered against unknown person. 4] P.S.O. Murbad Police Station, registered this offence vide Crime No. I – 135/2015, for the offence punishable under Section 363 of I.P.Code which was converted into Section 376 of I.P.Code. alongwith Section 3 punishable under Section 4 of POCSO Act. The accused was traced out during the course of investigation as he left the victim after committing forceful intercourse with him repeatedly for considerable period. He has committed said sexual assault on the pretext of marrying with her, but he was already married person. He left the victim and fled away. The victim has disclosed everything to her parents and then to the police. The accused has enticed her saying that he would reach the victim at the house of maternal aunt of the victim at village Khapari. However, instead of taking her to that village, he took her at village Kharid – Kinhavali and kept her at the house his relative Mangesh. He used to commit regular sexual intercourse with her saying that he is going to marry with her. .. 4/­ .. 4 .. Atro. Special Case No. 31/2016 CNR NO. ­ MHTH060006592016 ( Judgment ) 5] On the narration of the victim girl, accused came to be arrested and then the father of victim girl lodged the report. During further investigation, the victim and accused were sent for medical examination. Then, police visited the place at village Kharid where accused committed alleged sexual assault with her. Investigating Officer has seized the clothes from both and sent it to C.A. Kalina. The statements of concerned witnesses came to be recorded. On completion of necessary investigation, and after collecting medical evidence on record, the Investigating Officer has submitted charge­sheet before the Court. 6] Accused appeared before the Court in response to the committal order passed by the Ld. J.M.F.C. Court. Thus, my learned predecessor has framed charge against the accused Machhindra Wagh vide Exh.3 . It was read over and explained to him in vernacular. Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 7] The prosecution has examined only two witnesses i.e. P.W.1 complainant Sharad Wagh and the victim girl P.W.2 Pama Wagh. It is pertinent to note that the present matter is settled between the parties out of the Court and .. 5/­ .. 5 .. Atro. Special Case No. 31/2016 CNR NO. ­ MHTH060006592016 ( Judgment ) such pursis is produced on record vide Exh.11, and thus, the prosecution has closed its evidence vide Exh.12. The statement of accused under Section 313 Cr.P.C. came to be dispensed with as no incriminating evidence on record against him. The defence of the accused is of total denial. 8] Considering the evidence on record and defence of the accused, following points arose for my determination and my findings thereon, are as under for the reasons given below : POINTS FINDINGS 1] Does prosecution prove that, on 17/10/2015, between 12 noon to 7.25 p.m. the accused kidnapped the minor daughter of complainant Sharad from his lawful custody without his consent or permission, and thereby committed an offence punishable under Section 363 of I.P.Code ? .. Negative. 2] Does prosecution prove that, on the above date, place and period, the accused committed rape repeatedly on the victim minor girl Pama, and thereby committed an offence punishable under Section 376 of I.P.C. ? .. Negative. .. 6/­ .. 6 .. Atro. Special Case No. 31/2016 CNR NO. ­ MHTH060006592016 ( Judgment ) 3] Does prosecution prove that, on the above date, place and period, the accused committed penetrative sexual assault on the minor girl Padam, ageing about 14 years old, and thereby committed an offence under Section 3 punishable under Section 4 of POCSO Act ? .. Negative. 4] What order ? .. Accused is acquitted. :REASONS: POINT NOS. 1 TO 3 : 9] In the present case, the prosecution is placing reliance on the evidence of P.W.1 complainant Sharad and his victim daughter P.W.2 Pama to substantiate the offence of enticement of minor girl and for commission of penetrative sexual assault, and the rape repeatedly. I have already stated above that the victim girl is now married woman enjoying her matrimonial life happily with her husband by staying with her parents. Similarly, accused already got married and both the parties to maintain their future relations and individual life without any hindrance. They arrived at compromise and on that background, the complainant father and the victim girl have not deposed anything incriminating against the accused. .. 7/­ .. 7 .. Atro. Special Case No. 31/2016 CNR NO. ­ MHTH060006592016 ( Judgment ) 10] The charge levelled against the accused for the alleged commission of enticement of minor girl and for committing penetrative sexual assault, and thus, to substantiate said charge, the Investigating Officer has collected minor age proof of the victim girl from the concerned school. Moreover, the victim was medically examined to assert repeated sexual assault committed on her. Similarly, medical examination of the accused was conducted to prove his ability to perform sexual intercourse. No doubt, said technical scientific evidence including the C.A. Report is produced on record, but the ocular evidence is lacking as victim and her father turned hostile. The alleged act committed by the accused is not proved at all. Therefore, the other admitted evidence is of no use to connect the accused with the crime. In such situation, I have no alternative, but to answer point Nos. 1 to 3 in negative. POINT NO. 4 : 11 ] As I held above, the prosecution failed to prove the required ingredients of the offence, for want of adequate evidence. The star witnesses i.e. prosecutrix and her father have not supported the prosecution case. Hence, the accused can not be connected with the alleged crime. In the result, I .. 8/­ .. 8 .. Atro. Ramteke, Ld. APP for the State Shri M.M. Deshmukh, Ld. Adv. for the Accused ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ 2 Atro. Spl. Case No. 34/2016 [Judg.] JUDGMENT ( Delivered on this 3rd day of May, 2016 ) 1] Accused Yogesh Kashinath Donde, residence of Vashind (East) stands prosecuted for the alleged commission of enticing the minor girl of complainant Mrs. Manda Damu Donde from her guardian custody and committed repeated rape on the pretext of marriage at the house of relative of the accused as well as in the temporary shed of newly constructed building at Shilphata. Vashind Police registered this offence vide Crime No. I­29/2015 on the report of complainant Mrs. Manda Donde, the mother of the victim. 2] The story reflected from the prosecution case is that, the victim girl Poonam and the accused Yogesh are blood relatives. Accused Yogesh is cousin uncle of victim Poonam. Even then, they developed intimacy with each other, being inhabitant of adjoining houses. The mother of the victim noticed said relation between the victim and the accused and objected, it on the ground of blod relation, but, in vain. 3] The father of the victim is a driver by profession and mother is doing job as a maid servant in the hospital canteen. On the day of incident i.e. on 20.10.2015, when complainant came back from her work and was preparing food, her younger son Ravi told her that accused Yogesh visited the house in same evening at 7.30 p.m. He gave some 3 Atro. Spl. Case No. 34/2016 [Judg.] gestures and signals to Poonam and thereafter both of them fled away. The complainant mother guessed that accused Yogesh might have taken away the victim Poonam, hence, with the help of relatives they searched both of them in the nearby vicinity, but, they could not find them. On the other hand, the victim and accused took shelter at the house of elder brother of accused. They stayed there for a night. On next morning, accused performed marriage in the temple of Gaondevi by putting sindoor in the hairs of victim and thereafter they committed physical relations as husband and wife. Accused Yogesh took Poonam at Shilphata where he obtained labour job and the accommodation in the newly constructed building in shed type accommodation with other labours. Their physical relations continued for 8 to 10 days and then due to Diwali Vacation and as the construction work was stopped they were compelled to return back to Village Khardi at the house of their relative Tejabai. They took shelter there. Accused started working at mobile tower. Meanwhile, missing complaint came to be lodged and police traced out them at Village Khardi on 27.11.2015. The couple was brought to the police station, where the statement of victim came to be recorded, on which offence is registered and necessary investigation was carried out. 4] The Investigation Officer sent victim girl for medical examination along with accused. Both were examined to assert their capability of sexual intercourse. Then the clothes of the victim and accused were seized and 4 Atro. Spl. Case No. 34/2016 [Judg.] spot panchanamas were drawn where alleged physical relations were conducted by them. The statements of corresponding witneses came to be recorded and after receiving the medical evidence and completion of the investigation, the Investigation Officer has submitted charge­ sheet before the Court. 5] The accused appeared before the court in response to the committal order passed by learned J.M.F.C. I have framed charge against the accused vide Exh.2. It was read over and explained to him in vernacular. Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. It is pertinent to note that, during investigation, statement under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure came to be recorded in which the victim girl has disclosed her intention and the fact of their marriage. On this background, trial commenced. The Ld. Counsel Shri M.M. Deshmukh on behalf of accused submitted that the accused has performed marriage with the victim girl and now she has begotten one child out of their wedlock. On this background, the prosecution has examined complainant Mrs. Manda Damu Donde and her victim daughter Poonam to substantiate the charge along with the evidence of Investigation Officer. It is pertinent to note that, because of the said compromise, both the material witneses have not uttered single word incriminating against the accused, hence, the statement of accused under section 313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure stands dispensed with. The defence of the accused is of total denial and of false 5 Atro. Spl. Case No. 34/2016 [Judg.] implication. 6] Considering the evidence on record and defence of the accused, following points arose for my determination and my findings thereon are as under for the reasons given below :­ POINTS FINDINGS 1] Does prosecution prove that, on 20.10.2015 accused enticed minor girl from the custody of her parents with intention to commit offence No. with her and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 363 of the Indian Penal Code ? 2] Does prosecution prove that, on the above date, place and time, and thereafter up to 27.11.2015 accused committed repeated rape on the victim without her consent No. knowing that she is a minor and even then committed penetrative sexual assault and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 376 of the Indian Penal Code and under section 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 ? 3] What order ? Accused is acquitted. REASONS 7] POINT NOS.1 & 2 :­ To constitute the offence punishable under section 363 of IPC, the estimation of age and consistent documentary 6 Atro. Spl. Case No. 34/2016 [Judg.] proof to establish minor age of the victim is necessary to connect the accused with the said charge. Moreover, for convicting the accused for the alleged commission of rape, the physical intercourse against the will and wish of the victim is required to be proved and if the victim is minor, then the consent given by such victim has no concern. 8] Here, in present case, the age of the victim is shown around 17 years and 4 months i.e. below 18 years old. Surprisingly, corresponding documentary evidence is not proved with supporting evidence. It is pertinent to note that the victim and her complainant mother turned hostile. On this background, the prosecution evidence is closed after the deposition of Investigation Officer. No incriminating evidence is on record, hence, I have no alternative but to held that nothing is proved against the accused as alleged in the FIR. It is submitted by the Ld. Counsel on behalf of defence that the blood relation between victim and the accused caused the hurdle for their marriage, but, after physical relations, the relatives of both the sides calm down and settled the matter resulting into marriage of the said young couple. The witnesses including mother and the victim have admitted this fact during the course of cross­examinations. In other words, it can be said that there is no adequate evidence to connect the accused with the charge and hence, I have no alternative but to answer point nos. 1 and 2 in the negative. 7 Atro. Spl. Case No. 34/2016 [Judg.] 9] POINT NO. 3 :­ As I held, above charge levelled against accused is not proved with adequate evidence because of compromise outside the Court on the background of the marriage between the victim and the accused. In such situation, accused is liable tobe acquitted. In the result, I answer point no.3 accordingly and proceed to pass following order :­ ORDER 1] Accused Yogesh Kashinath Donde, aged 23 years, R/of Bhatsai Road, Near Kishan Mangal Karyalay, Vashind (East), Tal. Shahapur, District­Thane is hereby acquitted under section 235(1) of Cr.P.C. of the offence punishable under sections 363, 376 of Indian Penal Code and under section 4 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012. 2] Accused is under trial prisoner. He be set at liberty forthwith, if, not required in any other crime or offence. 3] The seized clothes of the victim and accused being worthless, be destroyed, after appeal period is over. 4] The accused is directed to furnish fresh P.B. of Rs.15,000/­ in compliance with the provisions of section 437(A) of Cr.P.C. 5] Judgment pronounced in open Court. Kalyan Dt. 03.05.2016 [ S.P. Gogarkar ] Dist. Judge­3 & Addl. Sessions Judge, Kalyan & Special Judge, Kalyan

ORDER BELOW EXH­3 IN ANTICIPATORY BAIL APPLICATION NO.350/2018. (CNR NO.MHTH06­000740­2018) 1] By this application filed under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. accused viz. Raghunath Ragho Harad has prayed for interim pre­arrest bail in connection with crime No.I­438/2018 under Section 354 (A), 506 of Indian Penal Code and under Sections 8 and 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 registered with Manpada Police Station. 2] I have perused application and heard learned advocate for the accused. 3] Case of prosecution in brief is that informant is the father of the victim girl. Name of the informant and the victim girl is kept secret. The victim girl is studying in Marathi medium school in six standard. Informant came to know that in that school misbehaviour with the girls student was going on. So informant after winning the confidence of the victim girl asked her about the same. At that time the victim girl informed the informant that for last one and half month their Hindi subject teacher i.e. present accused whenever comes for checking the notebook near their bench at that time he passes his hand over her back and chest which she does not like and that accused further threatened her not to inform that fact to anybody and therefore she did not inform this fact to anybody. The victim girl further informed to informant that accused misbehaved similarly with other girls of the class and she has also named three more girls with whom accused misbehaviour similarly. So informant lodged his report to police and aforesaid crime is registered. 4] It is submitted by learned advocate for accused that accused has 2 been in service since 1999 and he is having clean record . It is further argued that due to the reduction of students the procedure for declaring surplus teacher is going on in the school and that applicant is therefore targeted and this offence is registered in collusion with parents. It is further argued that in the said school in every class there is CCTV camera installed in working condition and if any such incident had occurred it would have been seen in CCTV footage. False complaint is registered. Accused has been suspended for 30 days by the letter dated 10.02.2018 by the head Master of the concerned school. It is therefore prayed that application may be allowed. 5] Considering the nature of the allegation and the fact that accused at the material time was teacher in the school and the victim girl is studying in six standard I am of the view that accused is not entitled to be released on interim pre­arrest bail. Hence, I pass following order :­ ORDER 1] Application is rejected. 2] As the application for interim pre­arrest bail Exh.3 is rejected the main application for anticipatory bail is also rejected. Kalyan (A.A.A.Shaikh) Dt.:­ 01.03.2018. Additional Sessions Judge, Kalyan.

Therefore, the informant was not knowing anything about the incident nor any kind of injury to the vagina of victim during her stay at Ulhasnagar in Diwali holidays. Case No.35/2014 The accused No.1 Anil is addicted to bad vices and used to give threats to her and her grandmother to kill them by throatling. Therefore, the victim has fear of accused No.1 Anil who used to come to the house under intoxication of liquor. He was also playing gambling. Therefore, the informant and the victim are disliking him in all respects. 49. PW.2 Suryakant Sahebrao Sabale (Exh.30) though acted as panch witness for spot panchanama (Exh.28) seems to have been stock witness of the police as he has acted as panch in various cases and also used to go to the police station whenever police called him as he is residing behind Hilline Police Station. This witness is unable to state description of the spot of occurrence. Therefore, his evidence is not helpful to the prosecution and nothing incriminating has been seized from the house of the informant including chaddar. 50. PW.4 Vinod Madhukar Tigote (Exh.41) acted as panch witness for arrest panchanama of both the accused and PW.5 Raju Ashok Devare (Exh.42) though acted as panch witness for seizure of clothes panchanama of the victim at Exh.43 but they both have not supported the case of the prosecution in any manner. Though the leading questions were put by the Ld. APP with the permission of the Court but nothing fruitful has been brought on record. 51. As regards to the medical witness PW.6 Dr. Mugdha Laxmanrao Jungari is concerned, she is specialist in Obstretrics & Gynecology and serving as Asst. Professor in J.J. Hospital who examined the victim on 28/12/013 brought by LPC Smt. Rahane for her medical examination. According to her the victim narrated the history of sexual 20 Judgment Spl. Case No.35/2014 assault by her father four times in last three months who was under the influence of liquor. However, this fact was denied by the victim herself that she had no talk with the said doctor but her grandmother narrated the incident to the doctor. 52. On her examination, she found no external injury, but on her local examination, her hymen was found torn. Minimal redness and tenderness was present. The tears were old and healed. The hymnal orifice admits one finger. After thorough history, physical examination, systemic examination findings are likely due to sexual assault however, final opinion reserved after chemical analysis report. As the sexual assault was old one, therefore, there may not be positive report from FSL. Accordingly, she issued the medical certificate at Exh.48. According to her, the secondary sexual characters were not developed, therefore, the age of the victim girl was 8 years. The victim was not attended the age of puberty. 53. She has reserved her opinion. Moreover, “Ps/Pv was not done as victim did not allow as of pain” are in different handwriting than the handwriting therein. The signature on Exh.48 though made by this witness but handwriting therein is not in her hand. 54. According to her, in medico legal case it is not for the Medical Officer to write in his/her own handwriting as there is residence assistant and lecturer used to remain present with the expert doctors who under the dictation of expert doctor used to write the findings. Though there was errasers but she had not initialled in 21 Judgment Spl. Case No.35/2014 column (10) of Exh.48. 55. The J.J. Hospital is totally computerized. She has not given her final opinion in Exh.48 for want of report from FSL. The investigating officer PW.7 though sent the seized muddemal property and sample collected by the Medical Officer to FSL on 7/1/2014 & 21/1/2014 respectively vide Exh.56 & 57 but no such analysis reports are produced on record nor it was shown to the doctor PW.6 Dr. Mugda Jungari so as to give her final report. She has admitted that an hymen can be torn due to horse riding and local injury. 56. The opinion of the expert is material which would help the Court to arrive at proper conclusion. But here in the case on hand no such opinion has been given except the medical examination of the victim showing that her hymen was torn. The reason thereof stated by her is that it may possible due to local injury or horse riding etc. 57. There is enmity in between the informant and the accused No.1 Anil on the various reasons and frequent quarrels used to take place. As I already held that the informant was loving the victim much more and hence, to avoid the quarrels the informant might have been tutored the victim and hence, there is no corroboration in the testimony of both these witnesses. Further more the victim has admitted that the informant was threatening the accused No.1 that she would send him in jail. Therefore, the possibility of tutoring the 22 Judgment Spl. Case No.35/2014 victim to arrest and keep the accused No.1 Anil in jail cannot be ruled out. 58. The informant and the victim both have improved their case in material particulars including on the point of the incident, disclosure of the incident by the victim and actual noticing the private part of the victim at Kedgaon school and not at Ulhasnagar residence of the victim, that too with interperson contradictions by putting different stories each of them, the benefit must go to the accused where there are two versions putforth by the prosecution witnesses. 59. As regards the accused No.2 Vitthal is concerned, there is nothing on record to connect him with the alleged charges except that he did acts like her (victim) father which is not sufficient to hold him guilty. He also tried to show enmity in between him and the accused on account of quarrel at the time of Navratra festival prior to the alleged incident by examining DW.1 Alim Ibrahim Pathan. According to him, there was no incident of withdrawal of the case by accepting Rs.500/­ in the police station had taken place. The evidence of this witness is not helpful to the defence of the accused No.2 Vitthal as nothing has been brought on record in view of the charges levelled against them. 60. Though the reports of C.A. are produced at Exh.22 to 25, however, except the blood group of the victim as 'O' in Exh.22 and blood group of accused No.2 Vitthal Natekar as 'A' in Exh.25, the 23 Judgment Spl. Case No.35/2014 result of other reports are negative. 61. Under the circumstances, there is nothing on record to hold that both the accused committed rape repeatedly on the victim and also committed penetrative sexual assault or sexual assault more than once or repeatedly on the victim aged 7 years. Hence, I answer the point Nos.2 to 6, in the negative. 62. Resultantly, both the accused deserves to be acquitted, and as such, I proceed to pass the following order :­ ORDER i) The accused No.1 Anil Bhima Pagare and accused No.2 Vitthal Arjun Natekar are hereby acquitted of the offences punishable under sections 376 (2) (f) of the Indian Penal Code, Section 4, 8, 9(l) & (n) r.w. Sec. 10 and 5(l)(m) & (n) r.w. Section 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, vide Sec. 235(1) of Cr.P.C. ii) Both the accused are in jail since the date of their arrest, therefore they shall be set at liberty forthwith, if not required in any other case or crime. iii) The seized muddemal property i.e. clothes of the minor victim which are lying in the police station, being worthless be destroyed after the period of appeal is over. iv) The accused shall execute their P.R. of Rs.15,000/­ each 24 Judgment Spl. Case No.35/2014 to appear before the Higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect of appeal filed against this judgment and order vide S. 437­A of Cr.P.C. v) Such bail shall remain in force for six months from today. 1 RBA No. 281/17 ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN R.B.A.NO.281/2017 This is an application for grant of anticipatory bail U/Sec.438 of Cr.P.C. filed by the applicant/accused Jitu Ramprasad Jajwat in C.R.No.I­32/2017 under Sec. 363, 376, 354(d), 504, 506 & 509 of I.P.C. besides Sec. 8 & 12 of POCSO Act registered with Hill Line Police Station. 2] The applicant/accused has contended that he is falsely implicated in this crime by the informant. The applicant/accused contended that the FIR is delayed by 8 hours and the delay is not explained. He also contended that the informant and the accused were well acquainted with each other and they were having affair. He also contended that the offences under provisions of POCSO Act are not attracted in the present case. He also contended that in FIR there are no allegation of rape and so offence under Sec. 376 also cannot be attracted. He has contended that there is no need of his custodial interrogation. He further contended that he is permanent resident of Ulhasnagar and there is no possibility of his absconding or tampering with the prosecution evidence. He further contended that if he is released on bail he would co­operate the investigating officer and his release on bail would not be prejudicial to the investigating machinery. On these amongst other grounds the applicant/accused has sought for his release on anticipatory bail. 3] The I.O. has resisted the application by filing his say Exh.5 contending that the victim is minor and offence is serious. He contended that the accused would abscond if released on bail as he is absconding 2 RBA No. 281/17 from the date of commission of offence. He also contended that the accused would tamper with the prosecution evidence if he released on bail. He also contended that accused would create hindrance to the investigation if he released on bail. On above grounds amongst others, I.O. wish to reject the application. 4] The Ld. Advocate for the accused failed to appear for hearing of the case for many dates. The Ld. APP moved application Exh. 15 to decide the application as same is pending since long and there is impediment in the investigation. Therefore, I had taken up the application for order without hearing the Ld. Advocate for the accused. 5] Upon hearing the Ld. APP, I find that it would not appropriate to exercise discretion to grant anticipatory bail to the accused for more than one reasons : First reason is that the previous anticipatory bail application bearing No. 177/2017 of the accused has been rejected by this court and there has been no change in circumstance which would enable the applicant accused to make this second bail application for anticipatory bail. Second reason is that the accused is clearly named in the FIR and his role has been stated in it. Third reason is that in the statement recorded before the Ld. Magistrate under Sec. 164 of Cr.P.C. it has been clearly stated that the accused had raped the victim by threatening her with knife. Fourth reason is that the nature and gravity of the accusations does not warrant anticipatory bail to the accused, since it does not appear 3 RBA No. 281/17 that the accusation have been made with object of injuring or humiliating the applicant/ accused by having him so arrested. Fifth reason is that the accusations against the accused are well founded and without custodial interrogation the crime would not be effectively investigated. Sixth reason is that the possibility of tampering with the prosecution evidence can not be ruled out because the offence pertains to rape on minor girl and is punishable with life imprisonment. Seventh reason is that there is need of custodial interrogation of the accused as the case pertains to rape on a minor girl. Eight reason is that , ordinarily, arrest is a part of the process of investigation intended to secure several purposes. The accused in present crime is of serious offence and the accused could have to be questioned in detail regarding various facets of motive, preparation, commission and aftermath of the crime and the connection of other persons, if any, in the crime. Ninth reason is that there are circumstances in which the accused may provide information leading to discovery of material facts of the crime and modus operandi of the crime. That is quite necessary for effective investigation of crime. Tenth reason is that in order to enable the investigation to proceed without hindrance and to protect witnesses and persons connected with the victim of the crime, to prevent his dis­ appearance to maintain law and order in the locality, the arrest of the accused is justified. 6] For these above quoted reasons, in the present crime, the arrest 4 RBA No. 281/17 seems to be inevitable part of the process of investigation. No doubt Ld advocate for the accused could have urge about the innocence and false implication of the accused in the crime. But, the legality of the proposed arrest cannot be gone into in an application under Section 438 of the Code. The role of the investigator is well­defined and the jurisdictional scope of interference by the Court in the process of investigation is limited. The Court ordinarily will not interfere with the investigation of a crime or with the arrest of accused in a cognizable offence. That being so, an interim order restraining arrest, if passed while dealing with an application under Section 438 of the Code will amount to interference in the investigation, which cannot, at any rate, be done considering the seriousness of allegation. Particularly, when from FIR it clearly appears that for effective and proper investigation of crime custodial interrogation is quite necessary. 7] Needless to state that the anticipatory bail is to be granted in exceptional circumstances and not as routine matters but for valid reasons. And in such legal paradigm, if the rival submissions and facts and circumstances discussed hereinabove are considered in proper perspective, I do not find that it would be justifiable to enlarge the accused on bail. 8] It has to be also noted that the offences complained of, being of serious nature, there is no justifiable ground to exercise description to grant anticipatory bail to the accused persons. Therefore, the accused is not entitled for anticipatory bail. 5 RBA No. 281/17 9] For the reasons stated here­in­above I hold that it is not a fit case to grant the anticipatory bail to the applicant/accused. Hence, the application of the applicant/accused for anticipatory bail deserves to be rejected. In the result, the following order is made : :ORDER: 1) The application is hereby rejected. 2) Inform to the concerned Police Station, accordingly. Kalyan. (D.S.Ghumare) Date ­26/07/2017 Addl. Sessions Judge , Kalyan.

Rakesh Haresh Garud (i.e. accused) as usual after doing the night duty used to come to sleep in her house in the afternoon time and on that day at about 12.15 p.m. after the school time was over informant came to her house from the school. She came to the house. At that time accused was already sleeping. She changed her uniform in the kitchen room and thereafter she came and sat on the bed. Since that time for the period of two months M.C. did not come to informant. So on 21.11.2016 her mother took her to the doctor and doctor gave some pills and asked her to come within a week. Thereafter, on 05.12.2016 Doctor conducted urine test of the informant and at that time it was disclosed that she was pregnant. So in order to be certain in respect of that conclusion Doctor advised for sonography test. So, the sonography test of the informant was conducted on 06.12.2016 and at that time it was disclosed that informant was carrying pregnancy of two months and 20 days. At that time Doctor asked her 4 Spl. Case No.29/2017 (Judgment) (CNR NO.MHTH06­000755­2017). as to who kept physical relation with her and at that time due to fear she had stated that her mother's sister's husband Harish Kalu Garud did forcible intercourse with her. In her further statement she has stated that on 20.09.2016 at about 12.15 p.m. while nobody was there in the house accused forcibly committed sexual intercourse with her and thereby made her pregnant and that she lodged complaint against accused. 4] Police conducted investigation and drew spot panchnama in presence of panchas. Police recorded statement of witnesses. Police obtained sonography report of the informant. Police collected the blood sample of the informant for DNA test. Blood sample of the informant and accused was also taken by the police for DNA test and chemical analysis. Police also took the blood sample of the foetus for the DNA test. After completion of investigation charge­sheet was filed against present accused. However, charge­sheet is not filed against Harish Kalu Garud as no evidence is found against him. 5] Charge against accused at Exh.5 under Section 376 (2) (i) of Indian Penal Code and under Sections 4, 6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 was framed against accused. Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 5 Spl. Case No.29/2017 (Judgment) (CNR NO.MHTH06­000755­2017). 6] After recording evidence and hearing both the sides, following points arise for my determination and I have noted my findings against each of them for the reason to follow:­ Points Findings 1. Whether it is proved by prosecution that accused committed rape on the informant .. Not proved. who was at that time under 16 years of age? 2. Whether it is proved by prosecution that accused committed penetrative sexual .. Not proved. assault on the informant ? 3. Whether it is proved by prosecution that accused committed aggravated .. Not proved. penetrative sexual assault on the informant ? 4. What offences, if any are .. No offence is proved against proved against accused ? accused. : REASONS : As to Point Nos.1 to 4 :­ 7] Perusal of the evidence of informant (PW­1) shows 6 Spl. Case No.29/2017 (Judgment) (CNR NO.MHTH06­000755­2017). that her father was in the habit of drinking liquor and he used to quarrel in the house and that therefore her mother used to send her to the house of her aunt viz. Surekha Garud who was residing with her family near her house. However, she has not supported the prosecution case though she has identified her signature on the complaint but she has denied its contents to be correct. She is cross­examined by the learned APP. She has denied the suggestion that her uncle gave her drowsy substance in the water and caused her to drink that water and did sexual intercourse with her against her consent. She has denied the contents of the complaint portion marked 'A'. She has also denied the suggestion that her cousin brother Rakesh (i.e. accused) after doing the work in the company used to come to her house in the noon time for sleeping. She has also denied the suggestion that on 20.09.2016 her cousin brother Rakeksh Garud came to her house in the noon time for sleeping and that at that time her school timing was from 7.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon. She has denied the entire portion marked 'A', 'B', 'C' and 'D' of her further statement. She is cross­ examined by learned advocate for accused and in that cross­examination she has admitted that there was dispute between her family and family of accused prior to lodging of this complaint. She has further deposed that on 06.12.2016 Surekha Garud quarreled with her parents. Therefore, she alongwith her mother in a fit of 7 Spl. Case No.29/2017 (Judgment) (CNR NO.MHTH06­000755­2017). anger went to police station to lodge complaint. At that time male police officer was there in the police station. At that time police only obtained her signature but the contents of the complaint was not read over to her.
