No. I­330/2014 ) ...Complainant Versus Sumit Suresh Shirke, Age : 25 years, Occ.: ­­­­ R/at : Charang Babanagar, Sai Colony, Ulhasnagar – 4. ...Accused Offences punishable under secs. 376, 506 of the Indian Penal Code & under secs. 3, 4, 5(L), 6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ 2 Spl. Case No. 31/2015 [ Judg. ] Shri S.H. Ramteke & Mrs. A.B. Patil­Bhamare Ld. APP For Complainant Shri K.M. Singh, Ld. Adv. For Accused ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ JUDGMENT ( Delivered on this 25th day of July, 2016 ) 1] Accused Sumit Suresh Shirke residence of Sai Colony, Ulhasnagar­4 is prosecuted for the alleged commission of rape on the minor victim girl ageing about 7 years on the pretext of playing game with her as a "Doctor, Doctor" and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 376 of the Indian Penal Code read with punishable under sections 4 and 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act for committing penetrative assault on the victim girl. He is also chargesheeted for giving threats to the victim girl causing alarm of fear in her mind by said criminal intimidation. Vithalwadi Police Station registered this offence vide Cr. No. I­330/2014 on the report of complainant mother Prajakta Kharat. 2] The story of the prosecution in short is that, accused Sumit Shirke resides at the house of his married sister Sumita Kochrekar and the complainant family resides in front of the residence of accused across the road. They are having visiting terms to each other as the daughter of Sumita Kochrekar i.e. Tavishi and the victim daughter of the 3 Spl. Case No. 31/2015 [ Judg. ] complainant are of same age. They used to play some times at the house of complainant and some times at the house of Sumita Kochrekar where accused is staying with the family of his sister. 3] It reveals from the allegations of the FIR that somewhere in the month of October, 2014 during the period of Diwali vacation on one Sunday said Sumita Kochrekar was not at home. Her husband has also gone out of the house and thus the accused Sumit Shirke, small girl Tavishi and her cousin child were in the house. Victim girl alongwith her younger brother also came there to play. The accused Sumit put on the T.V. and all the children were watching Cartoon channel. Taking advantage of this situation accused put on A.C. on full speed, he took the victim girl on cot, made her lie byside him and covered with bed­sheet. Then he removed the nicker of victim girl and also removed his clothes and then started penetrating his penis into the vagina of victim girl. She tried to resist the accused giving him blow on his chest but accused gagged her mouth and continued giving jerk, due to which the victim girl was sustaining pain in her private part and the abdomen. She rescued from the accused but he gave threat to throw her brother from the up­stair, if she would disclose the incidence to anybody. The victim girl was frightened, she could not disclose said incidence to her family members due to the fear of accused. 4 Spl. Case No. 31/2015 [ Judg. ] 4] The victim girl­R was sustaining pain and burning irritation in her vaginal part. Hence her mother took the victim girl to their family Doctor, who gave some medication. However said complaint was persistent. On one day i.e. on 8/12/2014 victim­R went to her school as usual but she came back after some period complaining vaginal irritation and burning sensation. The paternal aunt of the victim girl Shaila Kharat enquired with the girl the reason of her paining. Initially the girl was reluctant to disclose but then she narrated entire episode committed by the accused with her to the aunt Shaila in presence of her mother Prajakta. 5] On hearing the said narration said Shaila and Prajakta were shocked. They informed said fact to the husband of Prajakta and her husband's brother. They got annoyed and re­acted in the anger. They beat the accused alongwith the neighbourers and then victim was taken to the Vithalwadi Police Station where complainant mother Prajakta lodged report against the accused narrating entire incidence committed by him. 6] PSO Vithalwadi Police Station registered the offence accordingly vide Cr. No. I­330/2014 and the victim girl was sent for medical examination with the consent of her mother. During further investigation the Investigating Officer PSI Rajashree Shinde and PSI Baban Bhor have visited the house of accused and prepared spot panchanama. One bed­ sheet used in this crime came to be seized from the spot. 5 Spl. Case No. 31/2015 [ Judg. ] Moreover the clothes produced by the complainant mother of the victim girl were also seized and sent for Chemical Analysis. The I.O. has recorded statements of concerned witnesses. After receiving medical report and completion of investigation I.O. has submitted chargesheet before the court. 7] The accused appeared before the court in response to the committal order passed by learned J.M.F.C. Court. I have framed charge vide Exh.9. It was read over and explained to him in vernacular. Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. The prosecution has examined in all fifteen witnesses in support of its case. I have recorded statement of the accused under section 313 of Cr.P.C.. Defence of the accused is of total denial and of false implication. The accused has examined one defence witness to substantiate his stand. 8] Considering the evidence on record and defence of the accused following points arose for my determination and my findings thereon are as under for the reasons given below :­ POINTS FINDINGS 1]Does prosecution prove that, accused Sumit Shirke during the period of Diwali vacation 2014 on Sunday in noon time at his sister's house in Sai Colony, Yes. Ulhasnagar­4 committed rape on the victim girl ageing about 7 years old and thereby 6 Spl. Case No. 31/2015 [ Judg. ] POINTS FINDINGS committed offence punishable under section 376 of the Indian Penal Code ? 2] Does prosecution prove that, on the above date, place and time accused committed penetrative sexual assault on the victim girl ageing about 7 years Yes. and thereby committed offence punishable under section 4 and aggrivated penetrative sexual assault punishable under section 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 ? 3] Does prosecution prove that, on the above date, place and time the accused committed criminal intimidation by giving threats to the victim to cause Yes. alarm of fear in her mind punishable under section 506 of the Indian Penal Code ? 4] What order ? Accused is convicted. REASONS 9] The prosecution has placed reliance on the oral evidence of complainant mother (PW 1) Prajakta the maternal aunt of the victim, (PW 3) Shaila Kharat and the victim herself­R as (PW 2), the neighbouring witness (PW 5) Swati Sawant is examined to corrborate their version regarding the alleged incidence, (PW 4) Dr. Sandeep Khot, (PW 6) Dr. Mukund Wani and (PW 9) Dr. Hemantkumar 7 Spl. Case No. 31/2015 [ Judg. ] Khambait are examined before the court to prove the medical evidence brought on record regarding alleged commission of penetrative assault on the victim girl and the sexual capability of the accused. The evidence of Head Master Rajaram Dagade is examined to prove the child age of the victim, panch witness (PW 8) Lata Bhuigade, (PW 11) Hemant Poipkar and (PW 12) Chetan Sathelkar are examined to prove the investigation of prosecution regarding seizure of the clothes and to prove the spot. The police officers (PW 13) Police Nike Krishna Pandit, (PW 14) PSI Rajashree Shinde and (PW 15) PSI Baban Bhor have adduced their evidence to prove the investigation conducted by said Police Officers. 10] On the other hand the accused has examined his sister Sumita @ Vaishali Kochrekar to rebute the evidence of prosecution. I have to consider said evidence to see whether alleged offence is proved against the accused or he is falsely implicated as per his defence. 11] POINT NOS.1 AND 2 :­ The FIR Exh.19 proved by (PW 1) Prajakta Kharat discloses that her minor daughter ageing about 7 years old is the student of second standard learning in Ulhas Vidyalay, Ulhasnagar­4. The accused resides in front of their house alongwith his married sister family where the minor girl Tavishi of the same age also resides with them. The victim girl and said Tavishi are good friends. Both the families were having visiting terms to each other. Thus, the children i.e. 8 Spl. Case No. 31/2015 [ Judg. ] victim girl, her younger brother, said Tavishi and her cousin brother used to play together, some times at the house of complainant and some times at the house of Kochrekar where accused resides. 12] During Diwali vacation 2014 on Sunday the said children were playing in the house of Sumita Kockrekar alongwith the accused. Said Sumita was not at home. Her husband had also gone out of the house. Thus, accused and the children were in the room where they were watching Cartoon game on Television. Accused took advantage of the said situation. He took the victim girl on the cot with him and made her lie by covering her with the bed­sheet. On the pretext of playing game as "Doctor, Doctor" he removed the nicker of victim girl­R. Then he removed his own barmuda pant and nicker and then penetrated his penis in the vagina of victim girl. She tried to resist him but he gagged her mouth and continued giving jerks. He gave threats not to disclose said incidence to anybody otherwise he would throw her younger brother from up­stair. Thus, she could not disclose said fact to anybody. 13] To substantiate these wild allegations the prosecution is relying on the evidence of complainant Prajakta, maternal aunt Shaila and the victim­R herself. Nodoubt the evidence of complainant Prajakta and said Shaila is hearsay evidence. They have learnt the fact after more than 1 1/2 months' i.e. on 8/12/2014. However the 9 Spl. Case No. 31/2015 [ Judg. ] evidence of victim girl regarding the alleged incidence appears to be cogent and consistent. She has narrated the factual incidence in her own words saying as "The uncle of Tavishi i.e. Sumit entered his private part (Tyachi Su) in my vagina (Mazya Lagvichya Jaget Gatali). She further stated that, he has committed said act in the house of Tavishi. At that time her younger brother, Tavishi and her cousin were also present in the house but accused put bed­sheet on her person and committed said act giving threat to kill her and her younger brother. 14] The learned counsel Mr. Singh on behalf of accused submitted that, the evidence of Prajakta and Shaila being hearsay witnesses is having least evidential value. Moreover the child witness­R has admitted in her cross­ examination that before entering into the witness box she was present in the prosecutor's room and thus possibility of tutoring of child witness cannot be ruled out. 15] On the other hand, the then learned APP Mr. Ramteke submitted that, the victim girl was the witness of the POCSO case in which the atmost care of victim girl is to be taken. The evidence adduced by the said child witness is free from the shadow of doubt as she has narrated the entire incidence in her own words. Such trustworthy evidence of the victim girl cannot be brushed out only on the count that she was present in the prosecution room before entering into the witness box. 10 Spl. Case No. 31/2015 [ Judg. ] 16] On going through the evidence of the victim girl corroborated by the evidence of Prajakta and Shaila it reveals that, their evidence is consistent on point of the alleged act committed by the accused. The learned counsel Mr. Singh submitted that, said evidence of the victim is not supported by the medical evidence and therefore it does not inspire confidence in the mind of court to connect the accused with the alleged crime. To substantiate this submission the reliance is placed in the case of Arvind Datal ­ Vs ­ State of Maharashtra decided by Our Hon'ble Bombay High Court in Criminal Appeal No. 229/2010 in which the evidential value of the hearsay witness and the sole testimony of victim herself is discussed in the light of other corroborative evidence. Similar aspect is considered by Hon'ble High Court in the case of Manoharlal ­ Vs ­ State of M.P. in Criminal Appeal No. 1407/2013. 17] I do agree with the prepositions laid down in the cited case supra. However the facts and circumstances of the present case are altogether different. The victim girl­R is the close friend of Tavishi. It is whispered in the evidence that she tried to narrate the act of accused with Tavishi during the occurrence of incidence, on which Tavishi also disclosed that accused uncle has committed same act with her also. It apart that Tavishi is not examined before the court but it is sufficient to draw the inference of the attitude and the conduct of accused with the children. It is pertinent to note that, he has committed alleged act when the elder members 11 Spl. Case No. 31/2015 [ Judg. ] i.e. his sister Sumita and her husband were not at home and the children playing in the room were engaged in watching Cartoon show on T.V.. The intention of the accused to commit the act with victim girl can be gathered from the said circumstances in which he has committed the act. 18] The neighbouring witness (PW 5) Swati Sawant also corroborated the evidence of said family witnesses. She has also stated the alleged act committed by the accused learnt from the complainant mother. It is pertinent to note that in the case of rape or penetrative assault on the child, we cannot expect eye witness or the direct evidence. The victim is the only witness who can narrate the act of accused with the corroboration of other evidence. In this case also the victim girl­R has narrated entire story with her aunt in presence of her mother when she was enquired silently and when she could gather courage to disclose the thing and when her pains became unbearable for her. 19] Another facet of this case is the medical examination of victim and it's report. The learned defence counsel gave more emphasis to the medical report produced on record. No doubt, it is admitted position that, the hymen of the victim girl was intact and the concerned Medical Officer did not notice any visible or internal injury to the vaginal part of the victim girl. (PW 6) Dr. Wani merely stated that said girl patient was appearing ancious but no external injury was found on genital region or other portion of the 12 Spl. Case No. 31/2015 [ Judg. ] body. The learned defence counsel submitted that, the story exaggerated by the victim girl and her supporting family witnesses, if considered, in the light of medical evidence, then it becomes improbable and impossible. In such situation benefit is to be given to the accused. 20] On the other hand the learned APP submitted that the testimony of prosecutrix corroborated by FIR and other evidence is sufficient to prove the offence of rape. It is settled principle of law that slightest penetration is sufficient to make out an offence of rape. The reliance is placed in the case of Wahid Khan ­ Vs ­ State of M.P. decided on 1st December, 2009 by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Criminal Appeal No.1798/2008. In the present case the version of prosecutrix victim girl right from lodging the FIR till her examination by the concerned Medical Officer and till deposition before the court is absolutely consistent. It reveals from the history of the patient recorded by Dr. Wani that she has stated the name of accused and his particular act committed with her. Thus, the corroboration to the testimony of prosecutrix is not required as a rule of law when her evidence inspires confidence to connect the accused with the crime. 21] It is true the medical evidence is not suggesting the penetration act into the vaginal part but it cannot be inferred that there was no penetration. The absence of injuries and the intact hymen is not fatal to the prosecution case as it is held time and again that slightest penetration is 13 Spl. Case No. 31/2015 [ Judg. ] sufficient to constitute the offence of rape. This aspect is discussed in the case of Pooran Ram ­ Vs ­ State of Rajasthan decided by Hon'ble Rajasthan High Court in Criminal Appeal No. 543/1995 decided on 17th August, 2000. It is tried to demonstrate the discrepancies and infirmities in the evidence of prosecution witnesses. However stray admissions does not affect the cogent evidence of prosecutrix and her supporting family witnesses. Therefore said minor omissions brought on record by the defence cannot be said fatal or adverse against the prosecution case. 22] It is submitted that, alleged incidence took place somewhere in the month of October, 2014 and the police report came to be lodged on 8/12/2014 i.e. after the gap of 1 1/2 month which is not explained properly. On the contrary it reveals from the admissions given by the witnesses that the complainant family was not pleased due to arrogant and adamant attitude of the accused and to teach him lesson they all have cooked the story to implicate him in this false case. 23] It is submitted by the learned counsel Mr. Singh that accused was beaten at the hands of complainant family as well as neighbouring persons and he sustained some muffled injuries with abrasions and contusions. However the concerned I.O. did not take cognizance of his complaint. On the contrary he tried to hide this fact which is against the prosecution. It is true it is whispered on record that on hearing about the act committed by the accused the family 14 Spl. Case No. 31/2015 [ Judg. ] heads of the victim got annoyed. They alongwith neighbourers caughthold the accused and questioned him about his act and when accused failed to give proper explanation they reacted in anger by beating the accused while bringing him to the Polie Station. It is pertinent to note that, this fact is not hidden by the prosecution. It reveals from the arrest panchanama of the accused that he sustained certain injuries on his person while bringing to the Police Station. Minor contradiction is brought on record as to whether accused was brought by the public or the police officer Mr. Patil. It cannot be said fatal thing to the concrete story of the prosecution. The re­action of the public while beating the accused also appears natural conduct when the victim girl is a small child ageing about 7 years old. Therefore such discrepancies cannot be said as vital to the prosecution. 24] The complainant family came to know about the act of accused for the first time on 8/12/2014 and then immediately complainant mother lodged the report. Therefore the submission on point of unexplained delay holds no water. The evidence of family Doctor (PW 4) Sandeep Khot stated that victim girl­R was brought to his Clinic on 20/10/2014 with complaints of irritation in urinary track. This date of examination of victim girl shows the period of incidence during Diwali Vacation in the month of October, 2014. It is true the victim girl did not give real history to the said Doctor but as I stated above, she could gather courage for the first time on 8/12/2014 and then she narrated detail 15 Spl. Case No. 31/2015 [ Judg. ] incidence to her family members as well as to the concerned Medical Officer. Therefore the conduct of the victim girl if considered in view of her small age, appears to be natural. In such situation I have no hesitation to held that prosecution has proved alleged commission of rape and penetrative sexual assault on the child victim with cogent evidence. 25] The evidence of examined Police Officer clearly indicates their investigation on point of alleged commission of rape with the help of medical assistance. The clothes seized from the accused and from the person of victim girl were sent to C.A.. Nodoubt the C.A. report produced on record is not conclusive to opine the commission of forceful intercourse but the medical evidence is one of the piece of entire evidence. It is pertinent to note that, alleged incidence took place during Diwali vacation in the month of October, 2014 and said fact was disclosed for the first time on 8/12/2014 after the period of around two months' and thereafter investigation started. In such situation we cannot expect semen stains or presence of smegma on the clothes nor we expect some injury marks on the vaginal part of victim. Therefore the emphasis given by the defence with the help of medical evidence is not helpful to save the accused from the alleged crime. The cogent and consistent evidence adduced by the victim and her supporting witnesses cannot be disbelieved. 26] It is pertinent to note that, the family cannot prosecute the accused falsely on the stake of the character of 16 Spl. Case No. 31/2015 [ Judg. ] their daughter only to get rid of their displeasure against the accused. Therefore the defence adopted by the accused of false implication is not sustainable. The evidence adduced by the sister of accused as a defence witness is only in the form of denial of the act at the hands of accused. On the contrary in cross­examination the family relations between the parties and their earlier closeness is rightly brought on record by learned APP Mr. Ramteke. Considering all these aspects and cogent evidence on record I am of the confirm opinion that, accused has committed rape on the minor girl causing penetrative sexual assault on the victim ageing about 7 years old and thus I have no hesitation to answer point nos.1 and 2 in affirmative. 27] POINT NO. 3 :­ The accused is charged for causing criminal intimidation by way of threats to the life of victim and her brother and caused alarm of fear in the mind of victim which resulted into non­disclosure of the fact for the long period upto 1 1/2­2 months'. The witnesses examined before the court has stated specific evidence on point of the threats given by the accused and the re­action of the victim due to the said threats given by him. It is pertinent to note that, the point of criminal intimidation is not seriously shakened by the defence. The overall effect in lodging the FIR after the disclosure from victim on the discreet enquiry made by her maternal aunt clearly shows that, the victim was under the alarm of fear because of said criminal intimidation. Thus, the 17 Spl. Case No. 31/2015 [ Judg. ] offence of criminal intimidation is proved with cogent evidence. Hence I answer point no.3 in affirmative. 28] POINT NO. 4 :­ As I held above prosecution succeeded in proving the charge levelled against him with necessary ingredients to prove the guilt of accused. Hence he is liable to be convicted for the alleged commission of rape and for committing aggrievated penetrative sexual assault on the child victim ageing about 7 years old. Thus, accused is liable to be punished according to the law. However before passing the sentence of imprisonment it is my duty to hear the accused and defence on point of quantum of sentence. 29] Heard the accused Sumit Shirke and the learned counsel Mr. Singh on behalf of defence as well as learned APP Mrs. Patil­Bhamare on behalf of State. It is submitted by the accused that he is facing trial being under trial prisoner and he is in Jail since last 19­20 months'. He has undergone sufficient period for his act and thus lenient view may kindly be taken while awarding the sentence. 30] The learned counsel Mr. Singh submitted that, he is the only bread earner of his family. The responsibility of his mother is shouldered on him as his father is not staying with him. Thus, minimum sentence may kindly be passed. 18 Spl. Case No. 31/2015 [ Judg. ] 31] On the other hand learned APP Mrs. A.B. Patil­ Bhamare submitted that considering the nature of offence committed by the accused and to pass the message in the society for such offenders deterent punishment may be awarded. 32] On going through the record and proceeding it reveals that, the accused is a young person ageing about 25­ 26 years old. He was addicted with some bad vices because of his family background. His father alleged to have performed second marriage within short period from the death of his mother. Moreover his father performed third marriage immediately after the death of second wife. On such background the accused boy is nourished. His married sisters are staying away with their respective marital homes. The accused boy is abandoned without any control over him. In such situation I am inclined to consider his case with some sympathetic view considering his background. The punishment prescribed for these offences is upto life imprisonment that too till the end of life as per the amended provisions of section 376. However the maximum punishment if given to the accused, it will ruined his entire life. At the same time the heinous nature of offence committed by him cannot be overlooked and therefore the statute might have taken care of the quantum of such offences. The accused is charged with the offences of penetrative sexual assault as per section 3 and aggrievated penetrative sexual assault as per section 5 punishable under sections 4 and 6 respectively. 19 Spl. Case No. 31/2015 [ Judg. ] Minimum sentence of seven years imprisonment is prescribed for section 4 and minimum imprisonment sentence not less than ten years is prescribed by penal section 6 of POCSO. Thus, considering the heinous offence committed by the accused with the small child ageing about 7 years he is liable to be punished with minimum imprisonment of ten years with fine. With this conclusion I answer point no.4 accordingly and proceed to pass following order :­ ORDER 1] Accused Sumit Suresh Shirke, age 25 years R/of Sai Colony, Ulhasnagar­4 is hereby convicted under section 235(2) of Cr.P.C. for the offences punishable under section 376 of Indian Penal Code read with punishable sections 4 and 6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for the period of ten years with fine of Rs.5,000/­ in default to suffer simple imprisonment of three months'. 2] The accused is convicted under section 235(2) of Cr.P.C. for the offence punishable under section 506(b) of Indian Penal Code and sentenced to suffer one year rigorous imprisonment with fine of Rs.500/­ in default to suffer simple imprisonment for one month. 3] Both the sentences of imprisonment shall run concurrently. 4] The accused be given benefit of undergone period in Jail as per the provisions of section 428 of Cr.P.C.. Considering the conduct of material witnesses prosecution has closed the evidence and I have dispensed with statement of the accused under section 313 of Cr.P.C.. Defence of the accused is of total denial and of false implication. 7] Considering the evidence on record and defence of the accused, following points arose for my determination and my findings thereon are as under for the reasons given below :­ POINTS FINDINGS 1] Does prosecution prove that, on 11/1/2015 at about 4.45 p.m. in the room of Brilliant Coaching Classes, Ambernath, accused Firoj Khan committed carnal intercourse against the order of No. nature with a victim boy by sucking his penis and thereby committed offence punishable under section 377 of the Indian Penal Code ? 2] Does prosecution prove that, on the above date, place and time, accused Firoj Khan committed sexual assault on the victim boy ageing about 14 years 5 Atro Spl. C. No. 36/2015 [ Judg. ] POINTS FINDINGS and committed sexual offence against the protection of children punishable under sections 11 No. and 12 of the said Act ? 3] What order ? Accused is acquitted. REASONS 8] POINT NOS.1 AND 2 :­ The offence contemplated under section 377 is against the moral turpitude and it is liable to be viewed seriously when it is committed with the child ageing below 14 years old. The provisions of sections 11 and 12 of POCSO are also attracted in the present case as the act is committed on the minor child on the pretext of taking him to the tuition class. To substantiate these serious charges the prosecution has examined the victim boy himself alongwith his mother and maternal aunt to whom he has disclosed the alleged incidence. But surprisingingly all these three witnesses turned hostile and not even whispered anything against the accused. On this background I find no incriminating evidence on record. 9] It reveals from the allegations of the FIR that accused Firoj Khan is running his Tuition Class under the name and styled as “Brilliant Coaching Classes”. On the day of incidence when the tuition batch was over, he brought the victim boy Joy to his tuition class on the pretext of handing 6 Atro Spl. C. No. 36/2015 [ Judg. ] over him the note­book left by his cousin brother Pratik. The accused took the victim boy inside the tuition class, closed the door and then took out the penis of victim and started sucking it. After the completion of said unnatural act accused washed the penis and then requested the victim boy to come regularly for the same during the recess period. The victim boy was frightened and he disclosed the act of accused to his maternal aunt and the mother. Then report came to be lodged. 10] The allegations made in the FIR are certainly serious. The minor boy is victimised at the hands of accused. He intentionally took the boy in the tuition class to commit such unnatural act. To substantiate these allegations the evidence of victim himself is of vital important. But surprisingly he deposed nothing. On the contrary he tried to explain that there was quarrel amongst his friends and hence matter was reported to the police on his disclosure. The victim boy has stated altogether different story entirely hiding the alleged unnatural act committed by the accused. Moreover the evidence of the mother and the maternal aunt of the victim boy is also on the same footing. Thus, there is no incriminating evidence on record. Therefore it is difficult to held him guilty relying on bare words of the FIR. 11] It is true the admitted medical evidence suggests some swelling injuries to the private part of the victim boy, but the explanation of quarrel amongst friend circle is tried to 7 Atro Spl. C. No. 36/2015 [ Judg. ] demonstrate for the said injury. It is pertinent to note that victim and his family witnesses admitted in the cross­ examination that matter is compromised out of the court as they have decided to forgive the accused who is HIV positive patient in third degree condition. In such situation there is no evidence against accused to connect him with the alleged offence. Hence I answer point nos.1 and 2 in negative. 12] POINT NO. 3 :­ As I held above prosecution failed to prove necessary ingredients to prove the guilt of accused. Hence he is liable to be acquitted giving benefit of inadequate evidence to prove the charge. In the result I answer point no.3 accordingly and proceed to pass following order :­ ORDER 1] Accused Firoj Abdul Majid Khan, age 43 years R/of Fatima Manjil, Woolan Chawl, Ambernath (West), Taluka­Ambernath, District­Thane, is hereby acquitted under section 235(1) of Cr.P.C. of the offence punishable under section 377 of Indian Penal Code and under sections 11 and 12 of the Protectionof Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] Accused is in Jail, he be released forthwith if not required in any other case/crime. 3] The accused is directed to furnish fresh P.B. & S.B. of Rs.15,000/­. In compliance with the provisions of section 437(A) of Cr.P.C. to abide himself to appear before Appeallate Court in case of appeal is preferred by the prosecution. 8 Atro Spl. C. No. 36/2015 [ Judg. ] 4] Judgment pronounced in open Court. Kalyan Dt : 01/01/2016 [ S.P. Gogarkar ] Special Judge, Kalyan & Dist. Judge­3 & Addl. Sessions Judge, Kalyan

Received on : 09­04­2014. Registered on: 09­04­2014 Decided on : 22­02­2017 Duration: 02Y 10 M 13 D IN THE COURT OF THE ADDL. SESSIONS JUDGE ­2 AT KALYAN ( Before : D.S. Hatarote) Special (Atro) Case No. 42/2014 Exh.No._12 The state of Maharashtra Through Mahatma Phule Chowk Police Station, .. Prosecution VERSUS Suresh Lalmani Chavan, Age – 19 years, R/at : Saikrupa Nagar, Behind Walmiki School, Ambivali (W). .. Accused Offences : U/Sec. 452, 354 of the Indian Penal Code and under section 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual offences Act, 2012. Appearances: ================================= Smt. R. R. Bhoir, A.P.P. for State Shri. B.D. Palshetkar, Advocate for the accused ================================ 2 Spl.(Atro) Case No. 42/2014 Judgment J U D G M E N T. ( Delivered in open court on 22nd February, 2017 ) 1. This accused is prosecuted by the State through Mahatma Phule Chowk Police Station, for the offence punishable U/Sec. 452, 354 of the Indian Penal Code and under section 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Prosecution story in brief is as follows: 2. This accused and complainant Afsana Shaikh are residents of Sai Krupa Nagar, behind Walmik School, Ambivali. They are neighbours. Incident took place on 08/03/2014 in the house of complainant at 7.30 p.m. At that time complainant Afsana was alone in the house. At that time accused illegally entered in the house of complainant, hugged the complainant and started kissing her. Complainant was frightened. She tried to rescue herself from the clutches of accused. She shouted and protested. She get rescued herself and ran away out of the house towards the neighbour Priya Gulab Sawant. She went to the house of Priya and narrated the incident to her. Priya gave phone call to the mother of complainant Afsana and called her. Thereafter mother of complainant, complainant Afsana, Priya all came to Mahatma Phule Chowk police station and lodged the complaint. It is stated in the complaint that at the time of incident this complainant Afsana was 17 years old and she was taking education in 7th standard. On her complaint crime was 3 Spl.(Atro) Case No. 42/2014 Judgment registered as C.R. No.165/2014. 3. Investigation in said crime was carried by one S.V. Nigade, police Sub Inspector. He prepared spot panchanama on the next day. He recorded the statements of the witnesses. He arrested the accused. Thereafter, after completion of the investigation, he submitted chargesheet in the court. 4. This accused appeared before this court. Charge against him is framed at Exh.2. Charge was read over and explained to accused in Marathi language. Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. His defence is of total denial. He has not adduced any defence evidence. 5. Prosecution was directed to adduce its evidence. Accordingly, prosecution examined in all 5 witnesses in this case. P.W. No.1 Afsana Suleman Shaikh (Exh.4) is the complainant. She narrated the incident in detail and proved her complaint which is at Exh.5. P.W. No.2 Raju Taydi Patel (Exh.6) is panch witness on the spot panchanama. He supported the prosecution and proved the spot panchanama at Exh.7. P.W. No.3 Priya Gulab Sawant (Exh.7A) is independent witness. She stated that immediately after incident Afsana rushed to her and narrated the incident that accused hugged her and kissed her. P.W. No.4, Nanda Vanmali Patil (Exh.8) is Head mistress of Madhyamik Vidyalaya at village Atali. She 4 Spl.(Atro) Case No. 42/2014 Judgment deposed about the birth date of the complainant Afsana. She proved the bonafide certificate issued by the school which is at Exh.9. P.W. No.5 Sandip Nigade A.P.I. (Exh.10) is the I.O. He deposed about the investigation and about the submission of chargesheet. He deposed about the collection of bonafide certificate. Thereafter, prosecution closed the evidence. 6. All incriminating facts, circumstances and evidence put to accused during his statement under section 313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. From the answers given by the accused, it reveals that his defence is of total denial. As I have already stated he has not adduced any defence evidence. 7. I have gone through oral and documentary evidence of the prosecution on record. I have heard both learned advocates at length. 8. Following points arise for my consideration. My findings on those points are as follows for the reasons stated below. POINTS FINDINGS 1) Does prosecution prove that on 08/03/2014 at 7.30 p.m. in the house of complainant at Saikrupa Nagar, Ambivali West accused committed house tress­pass by entering into the house of complainant Afsana used as a human dwelling for sexually 5 Spl.(Atro) Case No. 42/2014 Judgment POINTS FINDINGS assaulting said complainant and thereby committed an offence Yes. punishable under section 452 of the I.P.C.? 2) Does prosecution further prove that on the above­said date, time and place accused made physical contact with complainant Afsana, took her kiss and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 354 Yes. of the I.P.C. 3) Does prosecution further prove that on the above said date, time and place accused committed sexual assault on complainant Afsana who is minor and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 8 of the Protection of Children from Yes. Sexual offences Act, 2012? REASONS As to Points no. 1 to 3:­ 9. In order to avoid repetition of discussion, I prefer to consider all these three points together. For the sake of logical conclusion it is also necessary to consider all these three points together. 6 Spl.(Atro) Case No. 42/2014 Judgment 10. It is admitted fact that complainant and the accused are neighbours. It is also fact that one independent witness Priya Sawant is also the neighbour of complainant and accused. Complainant, accused and Priya knows each other. 11. This accused is charged for the offence under section 7 punishable under section 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. First and prime contention for my consideration is that whether the complainant was child as per definition in section 2(d) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (henceforth referred to as the Act of 2012). In this respect, complainant deposed that the incident took place on 08/03/2014. At that time she was studying in 7 th standard in Walmiki Vidyalaya, Ambivali. Prosecution examined Principal of Walmiki Madhyamik Vidyalaya at Atali namely Nanda Vanmali Patil at Exh.8. She deposed about the birth date of the prosecutrix. She deposed that as per the school record date of birth of the prosecutrix is 01/01/1997. She deposed that while taking admission in the school in the primary school, date of birth is recorded. While issuing school leaving certificate, the primary school issued the same mentioning the date of birth of the prosecutrix. On the basis of same the admission register of prosecutrix in Madhyamik Vidyalaya is filled and prepared. She further deposed that her school has issued bonafide certificate which is at Exh.9 containing date of birth of prosecutrix as 7 Spl.(Atro) Case No. 42/2014 Judgment 01/01/1997. Sum and substance of her evidence is that date of birth of the prosecutrix is 01/01/1997. It means that prosecutrix was 17 years and 3 months old on the date of incident. She was a child as per definition mentioned in section 2(d) of the Act of 2012 as she was below 18 years. 12. At this stage, learned advocate for accused vehemently submitted before me that evidence pertaining to age of prosecturix is not reliable and acceptable. Bonafide certificate (Exh.9) cannot be treated as conclusive proof of the birth date of the prosecutrix. The school has original birth certificate but that is not produced. And therefore, the date of birth of prosecutrix as stated by P.W. No.4 Nanda Patil cannot be accepted. After thorough consideration of the submissions of both parties on this point, I found no substance in the submission of learned advocate for accused. It is pertinent to note that date of birth of the prosecutrix is recorded in her school record long back and before the incident. There was no reason for recording false date of birth when the prosecutrix took admission in the first standard of her school. At that time no one was expected such type of incident in future with the prosecutrix. The school authority has no reason to record false date of birth of the prosecutrix. On the contrary, the date of birth stated by P.W. No.4 Nanda is based on the school record which is there since the first standard of this prosecutrix. It is also brought on record through the cross examination of P.W. 8 Spl.(Atro) Case No. 42/2014 Judgment No.4 that date of birth is to be recorded on the basis of original birth certificate at the time of admission in the school. Thus, all the acts of recording the birth date mentioning the record in the school about the prosecutrix has done in due course of day to day business of the school. And therefore, there is strong presumption that date of birth stated by P.W. No.4 Nanda is based on true and original birth certificate which is with the school record. And therefore, there is no reason to disbelieve or discard the deposition of P.W. No.4 Nanda Patil on the point of date of birth of prosecutrix. It is worth to mention that no where it is suggested either to prosecutrix or to P.W.No.4 Nanda that on the date of alleged incident prosecutrix had completed her age of 18 years or she was not below the 18 years. Mere suggestions of denial of the age of prosecutrix are not sufficient enough to accept the contention of the learned advocate for accused. And therefore, I hold that on the date of alleged incident i.e. on 18/03/2014 the prosecutrix was below 18 years, a child as defined in section 2(d) of the Act of 2012. 13. Before proceeding further to discuss the evidence on record, I would like to reproduce section 29 of the Act of 2012 which runs as follows: “ Presumption as to certain offences –: where a person is prosecuted for committing or abetting or attempting to commit any offence under sections 3, 5, 7 and 9 of this Act, the Special Court shall presume, that such person has 9 Spl.(Atro) Case No. 42/2014 Judgment committed or abetted or attempted to commit the offence, as the case may be unless the contrary is proved (emphasis supplied). 14. In this case it is alleged that accused has committed offence under section 7 punishable under section 8 of the Act of 2012. And therefore, there is presumption that the accused has committed the offence unless the contrary is proved. Thus, to prove contrary is the burden on the accused. The legal presumption of committal of offence is in favour of the prosecution as per this section. 15. Prosecutrix is the sole witness of the incident. She deposed that incident took place at about 7.00 to 7.30 p.m. At that time she was in her house and she was studying. Door of her house was half opened. She further deposed that at that time accused entered in her house in drunken condition. He hugged her. He tried to push her to the earth to which she protested. Then he kissed her. Thereafter she raised hue and cry. She herself got rescued from the clutches of accused and rushed to the neighbour Priya Sawant. Now, considering this nature and alleged act of the accused it cannot be expected that there ought to have been any independent witness to the act of accused. It is also not expected that accused might have been done all these acts in presence of other persons. This act is naturally to be committed in isolation concealing from the eyes 10 Spl.(Atro) Case No. 42/2014 Judgment of others. And therefore, P.W. No.1 prosecutrix is the only eye witness to the offence. She has deposed all the acts of the accused in unambiguous words. This witness is cross examined at length on behalf of the accused. However, except the mere suggestions of denial which are flatly denied by the prosecutrix, there is nothing in the entire cross examination. The evidentiary value and credibility of the evidence of P.W. No.1 prosecutrix is not at all shattered by the cross examination of this witness prosecutrix. There is no reason to disbelieve or discard the evidence of P.W. No.1 prosecutrix. And therefore, I accept the evidence of prosecutrix as the truth. 16. There is independent corroboration to the evidence of P.W. No.1, the prosecutrix. P.W. No.3, Priya Sawant is admittedly the neighbour of prosecutrix as well as accused. P.W. No.1 prosecutrix deposed that after getting rescued from the clutches of accused she immediately rushed to her neighbour Priya and narrated the incident. This version of prosecutrix is duly corroborated by the deposition of P.W. No.3 Priya. Priya deposed that on the day of incident in the evening when she was in the house, prosecutrix came to her house hurriedly. She was frightened. She told this Priya that accused entered into her house, hugged her, tried to push her to the ground and tried to kiss her. Thus, the evidence of P.W. No.3 Priya is in full support of the deposition of P.W. No.1 prosecutrix. Thus, there is immediate narration of the incident 11 Spl.(Atro) Case No. 42/2014 Judgment by prosecutrix to Priya Sawant after the incident. There is no reason for prosecutrix to state false incident to Priya. Thus, the evidence of Priya is in full support of the prosecution as well as the prosecutrix. 17. Spot of offence is the house of complainant/prosecutrix. That is shown by the prosecutrix and the same is proved by P.W. No.2 Raju Patel. He proved the spot panchanama which is at Exh.7. Spot panchanama is mere panchanama and there is nothing incriminating in that panchanama against the accused. Nothing incriminating is expected from the spot panchanama. 18. P.W. No.5 is the Investigating officer. He stated about the investigation, spot panchanama, arrest of the accused as well as recording of the evidence. 19. P.W. No.1 prosecutrix and P.W. No.3 Priya are the two star witnesses in this case of the prosecution. Both these witnesses fully supported the prosecution. Both these witnesses are cross examined at length, but nothing is brought through their cross examination to discredit the evidentiary value of their version. There is immediate lodging of complaint by the prosecutrix. This fact is also brought on record through the mouth of P.W. No.1 prosecutrix and P.W. No.3 Priya. Priya P.W. No.3 after hearing the incident from the mouth of 12 Spl.(Atro) Case No. 42/2014 Judgment prosecutrix immediately gave call to the mother of prosecutrix, called her to the house. After coming to the house mother of prosecutrix alongwith Priya and prosecutrix went to police station and immediately lodged the complaint. All this conduct of Priya, complainant/prosecutrix and her mother is natural and no discrepancy found in the entire evidence of prosecution as well as in the natural conduct of the prosecution witnesses. 20. Thus, by cogent, corroborative and reliable evidence, prosecution established the fact that with intention to outrage the modesty of prosecutrix, accused entered into her house, hugged her against her will and kissed her and outraged her modesty. These facts are duly proved by the prosecution. 21. Now, the burden is on the accused to prove that no incident as alleged by the prosecution took place at any time and he has committed no offence. Said burden is on him as per section 29 of the Act of 2012 stated above. To prove the innocence or to rebut the prosecution evidence or to rebut the presumption available to prosecution under section 29 of the Act of 2012, absolutely no evidence is adduced on record by the accused. Even there are no suggestion to any prosecution witness as to why the witnesses impleaded this accused falsely in a false case. Mere suggestions which are denied by the witnesses are there in the cross examination of the prosecution witnesses. Why the prosecutrix and other witnesses falsely 13 Spl.(Atro) Case No. 42/2014 Judgment impleaded this accused in this case is nowhere explained, suggested to the prosecution witnesses during the entire cross examination. In fact, no defence is raised at all during the cross examination of the prosecution witnesses except giving mere suggestions of denial. It seems that accused has no defence at all to defend him or to discharge his burden under section 29 of the Act of 2012. 22. The poor attempt was made by learned advocate for accused at the time of final arguments that parents of prosecutrix were intending to purchase the room of this accused to which he refused. And therefore, parents of prosecutrix with the help of prosecutrix has filed this false complaint. This submission is put­forth only at the time of final arguments. This story of defence is neither suggested to any prosecution witness nor it was stated by accused during his statement under section 313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. And therefore, this argument has no meaning at all. 23. Thus, the guilt of accused for the offence under section 452, 354 of the I.P.C. as well as under section 8 of the Act of 2012 is duly proved by cogent and corroborative and un­ shattered evidence of prosecutrix and independent evidence of Priya Sawant. There is legal presumption in favour of commission of the offence by this accused under section 29 of the Act of 2012. Contrary to this presumption is not proved by 14 Spl.(Atro) Case No. 42/2014 Judgment the accused. And therefore, I answer all the three points in affirmative and hold the accused guilty for all the offences. Now, I take pause to hear the accused and his advocate as well as learned advocate for prosecution on the point of sentence. Kalyan ( D.S. Hatarote ) Date :­ 22/02/2017 Additional Sessions Judge Kalyan. 24. At this stage I have recorded further statement of accused under section 313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure on the point of sentence. He stated that he has been falsely implicated in a false case. He do not want to say anything about the sentence. I have heard learned advocate for accused Shri. S.U. Warpe on the point of sentence. He submitted that this is the first offence of this accused. He is young boy. He is the only earning member in his family. He prayed for leniency and also prayed that minimum sentence be awarded. Per contra, it is contended by learned APP Smt. Bhoir that maximum sentence be awarded as this is the offence involving moral turpitude. 25. I have considered the submissions of both sides carefully. Nature of offence under section 354 of the I.P.C. as well as the offence under section 7 of the Act of 2012 is similar in nature. And therefore, in my humble opinion instead of sentencing the accused for both offences separately justice will 15 Spl.(Atro) Case No. 42/2014 Judgment be done if accused is sentenced for both the offences jointly. 26. Considering the nature of offence, considering the young age of the accused, considering all other facts and circumstances, I think following sentence will meet the ends of justice. 27. In conclusion, I pass the following order. ORDER : 1) Accused Suresh Lalmani Chavan is hereby convicted for the offence punishable under section 452 of the Indian Penal Code and sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for one year and to pay fine of Rs.500/­ (Rs. Five hundred only). In default to suffer further rigorous imprisonment for one month. 2) Accused Suresh Lalmani Chavan is hereby convicted for the offence punishable under section 354 of the Indian Penal Code and under section 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for three years and to pay fine of Rs.1,000/­ ( Rs. One thousand only). In default to suffer further rigorous imprisonment for three months. 3) Bail Bonds of this accused stands surrendered to the Government. 16 Spl.(Atro) Case No. 42/2014 Judgment 4) All substantive sentences shall run concurrently. 5) Accused is entitled to get set­off under section 428 of the Code of Criminal Procedure if he was detained in jail during trial. 6) It is informed to the accused that he is at liberty to prefer appeal against this judgment and conviction order before the Hon'ble Bombay High court, Mumbai. 7) Copy of this judgment and conviction order be provided to this accused free of costs. Kalyan ( D.S. Hatarote ) Date :­ 22/02/2017 Additional Sessions Judge Kalyan.

R.G.Bhopi for the accused. Offences : ­ Punishable under Section 376, 375(d) r/w 376, 354 of I.P.C. and Section 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act,2012. :JUDGMENT: [Delivered 14/1/2016, in the open Court] 1] The accused Dilip Vishnu Jathar is facing the trial for the offences punishable under Sections 376, 375(d) r/w 376 & 354 of I.P.C. and Section 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2 Spl. Case 43/2014 [Judgment] 2] The case of the prosecution, in short is as under : The minor victim aged 15 years lodged FIR on 11/2/2014 with Kolsewadi Police Station stating therein that she is residing with her parents and studying in Xth standard. Her father (accused) is working in Badrakali Production drama company as light and sound operator. For the preparation of her X th examination she was present in the house. As there was stress on her eyes while studying she slept at 1.00 p.m. by taking chaddar on her person and had slept. At 1.30 p.m. somebody moved hand on her breast and private part. Such incident had also occurred before six months and when she was slept her clothes were found removed and her both the legs were made aside and by sleeping infront of her both leg sucked her private part. When she woke up she noticed her father who was looking at her eagerly. Then she gave jerk to him and worn her clothes and then started crying loudly as she was frightened. At that time, her father told her that she should not disclose the incident to her mother or else she would be driven out of the house permanently, therefore, she did not disclose the incident to her mother. The incident was happening repeatedly and then she went to the house of her friend Pooja and then she disclosed the incident. Then Pooja took her to Reshma and then went to Kolsewadi Police Station where she lodged the F.I.R. in the presence of her mother PW­2 Vaishali and L.P.C. Smt. Shette. She was sent to Rukminibai hospital for medical examination by the police. 3] In the meantime, A.P.I. Shri Pawar recorded the F.I.R. and registered the Crime at C.R.No.65/2014, under Section 376 & 354 of I.P.C. and section 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences, 2012. He drew the spot panchanama shown by the victim and arrested the accused on 11/2/2014 in view of arrest form. 3 Spl. Case 43/2014 [Judgment] 4] Further investigation was entrusted with PW.3 P.S.I. Smt. Vrushali Sagar Pawar who seized the clothes of the victim and accused under seizure panchanama at Exh.­20 & 21 respectively. He collected the medical reports of the victim vide Exh.­22 and recorded the statement of PW.2 Vaishali. She received the C.A. reports vide Exh.­24. After completion of the investigation she filed charge­sheet in this Special Court. 5] Charge Exh.13 was framed by me which was read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. The accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. His defence is of false involvement as per his statement recorded under Section 313 of Code of Criminal Procedure. Neither the accused stepped into the witness­box nor examined any defence witness. 6] Heard learned Spl.P.P. Smt. J. S. Lohokare for the State and learned Advocate Smt. R.G.Bhopi for the accused, at length. 7] The following points arise for my determination and my findings thereon are recorded against them for the reasons to follow:­ Points Findings 1] Whether the prosecution proved that the victim is minor aged 15 years ? .. Yes. 2] Whether prosecution has proved that six months prior to 10/2/2014, at 1.30 p.m. in room No.1, Chawl No.2 of Vidyavasini colony, Kalyan, the accused committed rape repeatedly on the minor victim girl? .. Not proved. 4 Spl. Case 43/2014 [Judgment] 3] Whether prosecution has proved that at the relevant time the accused sucked the vagina of minor victim girl by his tongue ? .. Not proved. 4] Whether the prosecution has proved that at the relevant time the accused used criminal force to the minor victim girl intending to outrage her modesty ? .. Not proved. 5] Whether the prosecution has proved that at the relevant time the accused committed sexual harassment upon the minor victim .. Not proved. girl ? 6] What order ? ….. Accused is acquitted. REASONS : 8] To substantiate the charge, prosecution has examined in all three witnesses, viz. the minor victim girl as PW­1 at Exh.­13, her mother PW.2 Smt. Vaishali Dilip Jathar at Exh.­18, and lastly, the investigating officer PW.3 Vrushali Sagar Pawar, P.S.I. at Exh.­26. The minor victim girl and her mother have not supported the case of prosecution in toto. The defence has admitted the medical examination report of the accused at Exh.­19, panchanama of seizure of the clothes of minor victim girl at Exh.­20, panchanama of seizure of clothes of accused at Exh.­21, medical examination report of the victim girl including collection of vaginal swab, pubic hair, nail clipping, blood sample of the victim at Exh.­22 and spot panchanama shown by the victim girl at Exh.­23 as genuineness thereof is not disputed. 5 Spl. Case 43/2014 [Judgment] As to point No. 1 : 9] The victim has stated in her testimony that her age as 17 years and studying in XII th standard when she tendered her evidence on 6/1/2016. The alleged incident is dated 10/2/2014 at 1.30 p.m. and six months prior to it. Her birth date as deposed by her is 11/9/1998. the prosecution has produced bonafide & character certificate issued by Prabhu Ram Vidya Mandir English High School, Prabhu Ram Nagar, Katemanevali, Kalyan (E), at Exh.­28 showing the birth date of victim at 11/9/1998. This being the public document it is exhibited. PW.2 Smt. Vaishali , the mother of the victim has also brought on record that the age of her victim daughter was 15 years at the time of alleged incident. Therefore, her age as on the date of the incident i.e. on 10/2/2014 comes to 15 years four months and 29 days. Hence, I hold that the victim was minor on the day of incident. Therefore, I answer point No.1, in the affirmative. As to point No.2 to 5 :­ 10] I have taken all these points together as they are interlinked and to discuss properly. The testimony of the victim PW.1 is material for all these points and she is the only witness who can depose about the actual incident involving her father in such serious offences. The trial was taken in camera. The victim deposes that when she was studying in IX th and X th standard at Prabhu Ram Vidyalaya, Kalyan, at that time she was staying with her parents at Vidyavasini colony, Vithalwadi, Kalyan. She is the only daughter to her parents. The accused who is the father is working as light and sound operator in Badrakali Production drama company, who used to go as per the scheduled program. Her mother Vaishali was working in three shifts in “Times of India” as receiptionist. The school timing of the victim was from 7.30 a.m. to 12.30 p.m. After the school timing she used to stay at her home. 6 Spl. Case 43/2014 [Judgment] 11] According to her when the alleged incident took place, at that time her parents were present in the house at 10.00 to 10.30 a.m. At that time, her father (accused) drove her out of the house on the reason that she was no studying, therefore, she went to the house of her friend Pooja who in turn took her to Reshma and then lodged the F.I.R. (Exh.17). She has not stated anything about the contents of the F.I.R. but admitted her signature at Exh.­17 and hence contents in the F.I.R. cannot be said to have been proved. Though the Ld. A.P.P. has cross examined the victim at length, but nothing could be brought on record. On the contrary she has stated that on 10/2/2014 at 1.00 p.m. she was present with her father (accused) in her house and her father was taking her studies. Her mother had gone for work. She was sent to Rukminibai Hospital for her medical examination. She has also produced her clothes worn at the time of incident before the police. After registering the crime she alongwith her mother started residing at the house of her grandmother (mother's mother) at Parel. The victim has not whispered anything about the charges levelled against the accused. 12] The mother of the victim PW.2 Smt. Vaishali Jathar has deposed somewhat similar as deposed by the victim. She has also not supported the case of the prosecution in all respects, except that when she was on duty, the Kolsewadi police called her at police station. According to her, her victim daughter disclosed nothing about the incident to her. She has also denied that the F.I.R. of the victim girl was recorded in her presence, but she admits that the F.I.R. bears signature of her daughter. 13] So far as medical evidence is concerned the defence has not disputed the report of medical evidence of minor victim girl and the 7 Spl. Case 43/2014 [Judgment] accused. The history of the victim girl recorded by medical officer of Rukminibai Hospital shows that the age of the victim as 15 years and alleged that her father had removed her clothes and suck her breast and private part. There was also history of sexual intercourse and similar incidents were repeated. The patient was brought by neighbour and friends. The sample of pubic hair, nail clipping, blood and vaginal swab was collected and sent to C.A. for analysis purpose. The C.A. certificate at Exh.­10 regarding nail clipping, semen, pubic hair and blood sample of the accused are negative reports. The C.A. report of sample of the victim shows negative except that her blood group is “O”. Therefore, the alleged rape etc. negatives the medical report coupled with C.A. report. 14] As regards the seizure of clothes of the victim and accused are concerned, neither semen nor blood were found, therefore, the defence has admitted both the panchanamas. 15] Under the circumstances, none of the ingredients of the offences are levelled against the accused are proved by the prosecution by adducing cogent, reliable and trustworthy evidence inspiring judicial confidence, hence, I answer the point Nos. 2 to 5, in the negative. 16] Resultantly, the accused deserves to be acquitted, and as such, I proceed to pass the following order : ORDER 1] Accused Dilip Vishnu Jathar, is hereby acquitted vide Sec. 235(1) of Cr.P.C. of the offences punishable under Sections 376, 375(d) r/w 376 & 354 of IPC and Section 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 8 Spl. Case 43/2014 [Judgment] 2] The accused is in jail. He be set at liberty forthwith, if not required in any other crime or case. 3] No muddemal has been seized or produced before the Court. If any muddemal is seized, it shall be destroyed being worthless after the period of appeal is over. 4] The accused shall execute his P.R. of Rs.15,000/­ to appear before the Higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect of appeal filed against this judgment as per S. 437­A of Cr.P.C. 5] Such bail shall remain in force for six months from today. Kalyan. [M.J.Mirza] Dt.:­14/1/2016. Special Judge, Under Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, Kalyan.

1 ABA 324/2016 Order below Exh.1. ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN A.B.A.NO.324/2016 : This is an application for grant of anticipatory bail U/Sec.438 of Cr.P.C. filed by the applicant/accused Sevak @ Harish Janardan Chavle. 2] The applicant has contended that he is falsely implicated in C.R.No.I­11/2016 registered with Murbad Police Station. The applicant contended that he had love affair with the informant Pratiksha and when this fact came into light , her relatives warned her not to meet the applicant/ accused. The applicant/accused was called by the informant Pratiksha at her school center on 3/3/2016 and when this fact came to the knowledge of her maternal uncle the present false complaint came to be filed against him. The applicant/accused contended that there is no need of custodial interrogation. There is delay of 2 days in lodging the report. He further contended that he is permanent resident of the village Talekhal and there is no possibility of his absconding or tampering with the prosecution evidence. The applicant further contended that he does not have any criminal antecedent. On these amongst other grounds the applicant/accused has sought for his release on anticipatory bail. 3] The investigating officer has resisted the application contending that the offence is serious and the applicant/accused has been named in the F.I.R. The I.O. has further contended that the investigation is pending and without custod of accused there would not be proper investigation of the crime. He further contended that the accused is absconding since the registration of the crime. Ultimately the I.O. sought for rejection of the application. 4] I have heard Ld.Adv.Punyarthi for the applicant. I have also 2 ABA 324/2016 Order below Exh.1. perused the documents filed alongwith it which includes the love letter purpotedly written by the informant Pratiksha. 5] Ld.Adv.Punyarthi for the applicant submitted that the applicant/ accused has been falsely implicated in the crime because the relatives of informant Pratiksha came to know about her love affair with applicant/ accused. He submitted that the accused had never outraged the modesty of the informant Pratiksha but is falsely involved in this crime at the pressure of the relatives of the informant Pratiksha. 6] As against this Ld.A.P.P. submitted that considering the fact that the offence under Sec.12 of POCSO Act is serious offence and there is need for custodial interrogation of the accused, it will not be appropriate to released the applicant/accused on bail. 7] I have given anxious consideration to the rival submissions. It is not justifiable to exercise discretion to grant anticipatory bail to the applicant/ accused for more than one reason: First reason is that the offece is under the provisions of POCSO Act and exact role of the applicant/accused has been assigned by her in the First Information Report. Second reason is that the informant Pratiksha is a minor girl studying in 10th std. and she would not make false allegation with object of injuring or humiliating the applicant/accused by arresting him. On the contrary, applicant/ accused himself states that he and the informant Pratiksha had love affair. Considering the fact that applicant/accused is more than of 26 yrs. and a quite matured adult, he ought not to have dared to fall in love at least with a minor girl of tender age not exceeding 16 yrs. 3 ABA 324/2016 Order below Exh.1. Third reason is that for free fair and full investigation I find that custodial interrogation of the applicant/accused is necessary. Fourth reason is that it can not be said to be that there is frivolity in prosecution and I find that there is element of genuineness of the prosecution. Fifth reason is that considering the societal interest discretion can not be exercised to grant the bail to the applicant as the offence committed by the applicant is against a school going girl and is punishable under the provisions of POCSO Act. 8] For the reasons stated hereinabove I hold that it is not a fit case to grant the anticipatory bail to the applicant/accused. Hence, the application of the applicant/accused deserves to be rejected. In the result, the following order is made : :ORDER: 1) The application Exh.1 for anticipatory bail of the applicant/ accused is hereby rejected. 2) Inform to the concerned Police Station, accordingly. Kalyan. (D.S.Ghumare) Dt.21/3/2016 Addl. Sessions Judge , Kalyan.

Order below Exh.1 in Anticipatory Bail Application No.477/2018. (CNR NO.MHTH06­001008­2018) 1] By this application filed under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. accused viz. Amitkumar Radhesham has prayed for anticipatory bail in connection with C.R.No.No.I­309/2017 under Sections 376(j) (n), 506(2), 363 of the Indian Penal Code, read with Section 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act and Section 5 of Prevention of Immoral Trafficking Act registered with Kalyan Taluka Police Station. 2] I have perused say of Investigating Officer submitted through learned APP and heard both the sides. 3] Case of prosecution in brief is that informant is the victim girl aged 17 years old. The name of the victim girl is kept secret. Informant lodged her report to police that her mother expired for about eight months before lodging of her report and that her step­mother used to assault her on one or other reason and when she made complaint to her father her father asked her to do any work to earn money. So from the third day of death of her mother she left her father's house and came to Titwala Railway Station. Thereafter accused Chaya Arjun Naikade took her to her house and in that house Chaya's sister's son Ajay Patarkar aged 20 to 22 years and one rickshaw­wala Harishchandra Gaikwad aged 50 years were also residing. On the third day of her residing with Chaya, Chaya forcibly caused her to consume liquor and rickshaw­wala viz. Chaya used to give her sleeping pills under the pretext that those pills were given by the doctor for her medical treatment. Because of the consumption of sleeping pills 2 ABA No.477/2018 (Or.Exh.1) (CNR NO.MHTH06­001008­2018) by the victim girl she used to remain in semi unconscious condition. Chaya took the disadvantage of this fact and within 20 to 25 days Chaya asked Ajay Patarkar to have physical relation with the victim girl and accordingly accused Ajay Patarkar had physical relation with her. So, in this way Harishchandra Gaikwad and Ajay Patarkar used to have physical relation with the victim girl for the period of five months. They further threatened that they would kill her if she inform this fact to anybody. For the last three months before lodging of her report, Chaya alongwith Harishchandra Gaikwad and Ajay Patarkar and the victim girl came to reside behind Sakharpak Building, Ambekar Room, Indira Nagar, Kalyan (W) and within 15 to 20 days again Chaya gave her sleeping pills. After consuming those sleeping pills the victim girl felt giddiness at that time Chaya called one person viz. Dadasheth in her house and asked that person to have physical relation with the victim girl and accordingly that person kept physical relation with her. Thereafter the M.C. of the victim girl was stopped and she was taken by Chaya to Dr. Poonam at Pune who gave certain pills to the victim girl. Thereafter after some days one person i.e. Waghe who was residing as the neighbour of Chaya in furtherance of common intention with Chaya and one person viz. Patil who was doing service in Bank brought the victim girl to Sony Lodge, Mharal, Taluka Kalyan and prior to that Chaya had given her pills for sleeping and Chaya had also forced her to consume Vimal Gutaka. After coming to Sony Lodge Chaya alongwith Waghe went away by keeping the victim girl in the company of Patil. There the person viz. Patil kept physical relation with the victim girl and brought her to the house of Chaya at 7.30 p.m. As the M.C. of the victim girl was stopped, Chaya took the victim girl to one more doctor at Fish Market Kalyan (W) who gave one injection to the victim girl and M.C. started coming to the victim girl. Thereafter on 24.12.2017 Chaya and Ajay Patarkar after consuming 3 ABA No.477/2018 (Or.Exh.1) (CNR NO.MHTH06­001008­2018) liquor assaulted the victim girl mercilessly and they started forcing her to consume liquor. So in a frightened condition she ran out of the house and she came below the Sakarpark building and stopped there. While she was crying there one resident of that building viz. Shobha inquired from the victim girl as to what happen to her and why she was crying ? So the victim girl told all the facts to Shobha. Shobha brought the victim girl to police station. On the report of the victim girl the aforesaid crime is registered. 4] It is argued by learned advocate for accused that there are total six accused in this C.R. Accused Chaya was running brothel. It is further argued that present accused is the manager of Sony Lodge. Name and role of present accused is not there in the FIR. It is further argued that accused No.5 i.e. Patil took the victim girl to Sony Lodge and did sexual intercourse with her. It is further argued that this is nothing but a conflict of two groups of prostitutes and therefore this false complaint is lodged against accused persons. Accused Nos.1 to 4 are in custody. It is therefore submitted that present accused may be granted anticipatory bail on the ground of parity. 5] However, learned APP has submitted that last incident of committing rape on the victim girl took place in Sony Lodge i.e. the hotel of accused.
