1 Judgment Spl. Case No.50/2014 Received on : 3/5/2014 Registered on : 3/5/2014 Decided on : 2/2/2017. Duration : 2 Y. 8 M. 29 D. IN THE COURT OF SPECIAL JUDGE, KALYAN AT : KALYAN (Under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012) (Presided over by : M.J.Mirza) SPECIAL CASE NO.50/2014. Exh.56 The State of Maharashtra. Through: P.I. Kolsewadi Police Station, Dombivli, District­Thane. … Complainant. Vs. Rakesh Matadip Varma, Age : 50 years, Occp.­ Labour, R/at.­ Neharu Nagar, Near New Building of Mangesh Gaikar, Vitthalwadi, Kalyan (E), District­Thane. … Accused. Appearance : Ld. Spl. A.P.P. Shri D.V.Bhangre for the State. Ld. Advocate Shri M.D. Suryavanshi for the accused. Offences : Punishable under section 376 of I.P.C. and Section 4 & 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. :JUDGMENT: (Delivered in the open Court, on 2/2/2017) 1. The accused Rakesh Matadip Varma is facing trial for the offences punishable under Section 376 of Indian Penal Code and Section 4 & 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 on 2 Judgment Spl. Case No.50/2014 the allegations that the accused raped and also committed aggravated penetrative sexual assault on the minor victim girl aged 12 years. 2. The case of the prosecution, may be summarised in brief, as under: The victim, aged 12 years lodged the FIR on 14/3/2014 stating therein that her mother and the accused are doing labour work. After the death of her natural father, the accused started residing with her mother. Her mother is also addicted to liquor. 3. Two months prior to the incident, she alongwith her mother and accused were sleeping in the house. At that time, her mother had consumed liquor. The accused was looking towards her. He removed the electric bulb and in the darkness he removed her clothes and committed sexual intercourse with her. She was attempting to raise shouts but her mouth was pressed by the accused and he threatened her. Till 11/3/2014, the accused was committing sexual intercourse with her. On 11/3/2014, she disclosed the incident to her mother but she did not say anything to the accused. On 13/3/2014, at 6 p.m. she alongwith her parents went to the house of her sister P.W.2 Chhaya at Kolivaligaon, Kalyan (W). Thereafter, her parents went to consume liquor. Then she disclosed the sexual assault committed by the accused on her to her sister Chhaya (P.W.2) who then took her to Bazarpeth Police Station and then she was taken to Kolsewadi Police Station where her FIR came to be recorded. 4. PSO API Shri Mahadev Krishna Naikwade of Kolsewadi Police Station recorded her FIR (Exh.21) on 14/3/2014 at 8.30 p.m. and 3 Judgment Spl. Case No.50/2014 registered the crime as C.R.No. I­118/2014 under Sec.376 of IPC and Sec.4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. He then drew the spot panchanama at Exh.30 in the presence of panchas and seized clothes on the person of accused on 15/3/2014 viz. saphari shirt, blue coloured full pant, blue coloured under pant and sandow baniyan under seizure panchanama (Exh.31) and sealed the clothes with wax. He arrested the accused on 15/3/2014. On 15/3/2014, he then handed over the investigation to WPSI Sou Hire. 5. WPSI Smt. Vrushali Karbhai Hire (P.W.9) carried out further investigation as the investigation was entrusted to him by API Shri Naikwade. She then sent the victim for medical examination and also to Civil Hospital, Thane for ascertaining her age. The accused was also sent for medical examination. She requested the medical officer to collect sample of blood, nail clippings, pubic hairs and semen of the accused. 6. She then seized the clothes of the victim, salwar and kurta produced by P.W.2 Chhaya, the sister of victim under seizure panchanama (Exh.32). She then sent the clothes of the victim and accused to FSL Kalina alongwith her covering letter (Exh.43). She then recorded the statements of the witnesses and collected document from the builder regarding construction of building which was in progress where the incident occurred. She also produced two letters sent to medical officer of Rukminibai Hospital for medical examination of accused and victim at Exh.44 & 45. After completion of investigation, she filed the chargesheet on 3/5/2014 before this Court. 7. Charge at Exh.15 was framed by me against the accused which 4 Judgment Spl. Case No.50/2014 was read over and explained to him in vernacular. The accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be innocent. His defence is of false involvement as per his statement recorded under Section 313 of Cr.P.C. and the suggestions put to the prosecution witnesses. The accused examined the defence witness D.W.1 Smt. Anusaya Hari Aade, the mother of the victim at Exh.50 but he did not step into the witness­box. 8. The learned Spl. A.P.P. by filing an application at Exh.51 dated 31/1/2017 prayed for framing of additional charge for the offence punishable under Sec.6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 as the victim in her FIR as well as in her substantiative evidence has brought on record that accused committed aggravated penetrative sexual assault on her more than once or repeatedly. Say to the said application filed by the accused through his Advocate and resisted the application, however, by passing order below Exh.13 dated 21/1/2017 the said application was allowed and additional charge at Exh.52 was framed which was read over and explained to the accused in vernacular, however he pleaded not guilty. The prosecution filed pursis at Exh.54 and accused filed pursis at Exh.55 informing the Court that no evidence is required to be adduced or cross­ examined any of the witness. 9. Heard learned Spl. APP Shri D.V.Bhangre for the State and learned Advocate Shri M.D. Suryavanshi for the accused, at length. 10. Following points arise for my determination and my findings alongwith reasons thereon, are as under :­ 5 Judgment Spl. Case No.50/2014 Points Findings 1 Whether the prosecution has proved that the age of the minor victim was below 18 years at the time of incident as alleged? ..... Yes. 2 Whether the prosecution has proved beyond realm of doubt that two months prior to the date of FIR i.e. 11/3/2014 at Neharu Nagar in new building of Mangesh Gaikar, Vitthalwadi, Kalyan (E), the accused committed rape on the minor victim aged 12 years, punishable under Sec.376 of I.P.C. ? …In the negative. 3 Whether the prosecution has proved beyond realm of doubt that the accused at the relevant time committed aggravated penetrative sexual assault on the minor victim aged 12 years repeatedly, punishable under Sec. 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 ? …In the negative. 4 What order ? … Accused acquitted. : REASONS : 11. To substantiate the charge, the prosecution has examined in all 9 witnesses viz. P.W.1 victim at Exh.20 who lodged the FIR at Exh.21 narrating the incident and brought on record that accused committed rape on her for 4­5 times. P.W.2 Smt. Chhaya Ashok Suryavanshi (Exh.25), the sister of the victim to whom the victim disclosed about sexual intercourse on her by the accused after repeating the incident of rape on her who then took the victim to Kolsewadi Police Station where 6 Judgment Spl. Case No.50/2014 victim lodged the FIR. P.W.3 Dr. Smt. Rajani Shamrao Halgarkar (Exh.27), MO Civil Hospital, Thane before whom the victim was brought by Kolsewadi police on 18/3/2014 for determination of her age and rape examination. She advised her for admission but she refused. Her x­ ray was taken by Radiologist for determination of her age. She prepared the case papers bearing MLC No.5222 at Exh.28. 12. P.W.4 Madhukar Baliram Bansode (Exh.29), the panch witness for spot panchanama (Exh.30) and also acted as panch witness for two seizure panchanamas of the clothes of the victim and accused at Exh.31 & 32 respectively but he has not supported the case of the prosecution. P.W.5 Dr. Neeta Prashant Bhagat (Exh.33), MO Gynecologist Rukminibai Hospital, Kalyan who examined the victim on 15/3/2014 after obtaining consent of Chhaya who is the sister of the victim and brought by WPN Smt. Pawar and recorded the history of sexual assault. Her hymen was not intact but no external injuries were found on her body and perineum and her findings were suggestive of sexual assault in view of distinsible vagina and tearing of hymen. She also collected blood sample, nail clipping, pubic hair and vaginal swab and handed over to WPN Smt. Pawar in sealed condition on 15/3/2014 at 11.45 p.m. She issued the medical certificate at Exh.34. P.W.6 Mahadev Krishna Naikwade (Exh.35), API who was on PSO duty on 14/3/2014 and recorded the FIR (Exh.21) of the victim and registered the crime and then drew the spot panchanama (Exh.30) and seized the clothes of the accused under seizure panchanama (Exh.31). P.W.7 PN Shri Swapnil Macchindra Gosavi (Exh.37), who carried the seized muddemal property on 21/3/2017 to CA Kalina in CR No. I­118/2014 and also muddemal properties in other crime to FSL Kalina alongwith 7 Judgment Spl. Case No.50/2014 covering letter and obtained an acknowledgement of the office of the C.A. P.W.8 Dr. Smt. Kalpana Sudhakar Vyavhare (Exh.39), the Radiologist Civil Hospital, Thane who opined the age of the victim on the basis of the x­ray taken by x­ray technician on 18/3/2014 and she opined the age of the victim in between 14­15 years and issued the age certificate of the victim on 21/3/2014 at Exh.40. The last witness is P.W.9 PSI Smt. Vrushali Karbhari Hire (Exh.42), the Investigating Officer who carried out the investigation since 15/3/2014 and had sent the victim for medical examination to Rukminibai Hospital and Civil Hospital, Thane for ascertaining her age. The accused was also sent for medical examination and collecting sample of blood, nail clipping, pubic hair and semen. She seized the clothes of the victim produced by her sister Smt. Chhaya under seizure panchanama (Exh.32). She sent the clothes of the victim and accused to FSL Kalina alongwith covering letter (Exh.43). She then recorded the statements of the witnesses, collected documents from the builder regarding under construction of building which was in progress where the incident had occurred. She also produced a letter requesting the medical officer to examine the victim and accused at Exh.44 & 45 but the statement of the victim under Sec.164 of Cr.P.C. was never recorded. 13. The defence has examined the witness D.W.1 Smt. Anusaya Hari Aade (Exh.50), the mother of the victim to support the defence of the accused (her husband) that he has been involved falsely in this case as the bride groom for the marriage of the victim was approved in U.P. As to point No.1 : 14. P.W.1 is the victim (Exh.20). She is an illiterate as she did not 8 Judgment Spl. Case No.50/2014 go to school at any time. Her evidence was recorded on oath in camera by creating child friendly atmosphere as she was knowing the sanctity of oath and given rational answers to the questions put to her. She has narrated entire incident involving the accused and also disclosed the incident to her sister Smt. Chhaya (P.W.2) who then took her to Kolsewadi Police Station where her FIR (Exh.21) came to be recorded and crime was registered at C.R. No. I­118/2014. 15. There is no document showing the birth date of the victim. She has stated her age as 12 years on the date of her deposition. P.W.2 Chhaya Ashok Suryavanshi is the real sister of the victim who has stated the age of the victim as 16 years being younger to her. She does not know whether the age of her elder brother is 28 years and elder sister 25 years. She has denied the suggestion put to her as her age was 17­18 years. 16. To ascertain the age of the victim, it is necessary for the prosecution to prove that she was child within the meaning of Sec.2(d) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Though the informant/victim lodged her FIR dated 14/3/2014 stating her age as 12 years and stated the same age when she deposed on 8/1/2016. Her sister P.W.2 Chhaya has stated the age of the victim as 16 years but without any proof. 17. The Investigating Officer P.W.9 Smt. Hire had sent the victim for her medical examination to Rukminibai Hospital, Kalyan and then to Civil Hospital, Thane for ascertaining her age. P.W.3 Dr. Smt. Rajani Shyamrao Halgarkar (Exh.27) was on CMO duty on 18/3/2014 9 Judgment Spl. Case No.50/2014 before whom the victim was produced by Kolsewadi police. The victim disclosed her age as 12 years. When she advised her for admission but victim refused. Then she advised her for x­ray to ascertain her age. Accordingly, the Radiologist took her x­ray and given his final opinion. This witness has prepared two case papers bearing MLC No.5222 produced at Exh.28. 18. The Radiologist P.W.8 Dr. Smt. Kalpana Sudhakar Vyavhare attached to Civil Hospital, Thane has brought on record that on 18/3/2014 the victim was produced by WPC Smt. Gunjal for ascertaining her age. Accordingly, the x­ray technician took the x­ray. She then examined x­ray and opined the age of the victim as 14­15 years and accordingly she issued the age certificate at Exh.40. The x­ray of elbow, wrist and illiac crest were taken. She stated that the age can be ascertained on the basis of dental test but it was not necessary to take x­ray of teeth for determination of age. She also stated that there is error of margin of 2 years on either side. 19. Except the ossification test there is no other age proof of the victim, however, P.W.8 Dr. Smt. Kalpana Vyavhare on the basis of the x­ ray taken by x­ray technician opined the age of the victim as 14­15 years with an error of margin of two years. Therefore, the age of the victim would be 17 years on the date of the incident. Therefore, she was child within the meaning of Sec.2(d) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Hence, I answer the point No.1, in the affirmative. 10 Judgment Spl. Case No.50/2014 As to point No.2 & 3 :­ 20. I have taken both these points together for proper and convenient discussion as both the points are inter­linked. 21. It is settled position of law that a slight penetration is sufficient to constitute the offence of rape or penetrative sexual assault as held by Their Lordships of the Apex Court in the case of Aman Kumar Vs. State of Haryana (2004 S.C.C. (Cri) 1266) wherein it is held that, “Penetration is the sine qua non for an offence of rape. In order to constitute penetration, there must be evidence clear and cogent to prove that some part of the virile member of the accused was within the labia of the pudendum of the woman, no matter how little. The depth of penetration is immaterial in an offence punishable under Section 376 of I.P.C. Even a slight penetration in the vulva is sufficient to constitute the offence of rape and rupture of the hymen is not necessary. Vulva penetration with or without violence is as much rape as vaginal penetration. The statute merely requires evidence of penetration, and this may occur with the hymen remaining intact. The actus reus is complete with penetration. Thus, to constitute the offence of rape, it is not necessary that there should be complete penetration of the penis with emission of semen and rupture of hymen. Partial penetration within the labia majora of the vulva or pudendum with or without emission of semen is sufficient to constitute the offence of rape as defined in the law.” 22. For the offence punishable either under Sec.4 or Sec.6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 same ingredients of Section 376 are required but only additional requirement is that the age of the victim must be below 18 years and there must be penetrative sexual assault (Sec.4) and aggravated penetrative sexual 11 Judgment Spl. Case No.50/2014 assault (Sec.6) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. 23. To prove this point of rape, penetrative sexual assault or aggravated sexual assault alleged to have been committed by the accused on the victim/informant, it is necessary to evaluate the evidence of the victim who is the star witness in this case. 24. Admittedly, after the death of the father of the victim the accused started residing with her mother and their relations are like husband and wife. The victim and her sister P.W.2 Chhaya were treating the accused as step father. The mother of the victim has a daughter born from the accused because of such relations with the accused. 25. P.W.2 Chhaya is the elder sister of the victim whose first marriage was performed but due to differences she deserted her husband. Thereafter, she is married with Ashok Gaikwad with whom she is presently residing and cohabiting. Because of the relation of the accused who started residing with the mother of the victim, two brothers of the victim started residing separately. The victim and her two brothers alongwith their mother and accused had occasioned to go to the native place of the accused at Madhepura, Post & Taluka­Baha, District­Agra U.P. where the accused had searched groom for the victim. Therefore, the accused used to take the victim and her mother to his native place at Madhepura and had also arranged finance for her marriage. When she was taken lastly to the native place of the accused, at that time there was talk took place about her marriage as the accused has seen and approved groom at his native place. The boy was poor and residing in rural area for which the victim ready to marry with a boy 12 Judgment Spl. Case No.50/2014 shown by the accused. 26. The victim was initially residing with her maternal uncle Bharat at Akola when she was 6­7 years old. Her mother's name is Anusaya (D.W.1) and name of her deceased father was Hari Aade who died before six years at Khadakpada as he was addicted to liquor. Till the death of her father she was residing with him alongwith her mother. She has two elder brothers and two elder sisters. Initially her brothers were staying with her at Kalyan, however, her elder sister P.W.2 Chhaya was married at that time. All her family members are labourers. 27. The victim was not knowing nor acquainted with the accused but her mother was knowing him as he was also doing labour work with her and her mother. She was treating the accused as her father and he was maintaining her and her mother. The accused started residing with the mother of the victim after the death of her father, therefore, her brothers started residing separately from her mother. Her sister Chhaya came to know that accused is residing with her mother after about one month. The accused was disliking her (victim) and her brothers. Her mother was addicted to liquor. According to the victim, the first incident was occurred before 2 years at 12 midnight, and at that time the accused had consumed liquor. In the midnight by switching off lights and pressing her mouth he committed forcible sexual intercourse with her. However, she resisted but the accused had tied her hands. When she tried to run away but the accused assaulted her. When she raised shouts, however the accused pressed her mouth. It is her case that 4­5 times the accused committed such sexual intercourse with her. Then she disclosed the incident to her mother but she did not pay any attention 13 Judgment Spl. Case No.50/2014 towards her. She then went to the house of her sister Chhaya and disclosed the incident to her. 28. Her sister chhaya (P.W.2) took her to Vitthalwadi Police Station where she (victim) narrated the incident to the police, recorded her FIR (Exh.21) and then obtained her thumb impression on it. However, she is unable to tell the contents of her FIR. 29. She had shown the place of incident to the police. She was also sent for medical examination where her x­ray was taken. She then produced her clothes before the police. Thereafter, she went to her native at Akola and started residing with her maternal uncle Bharat. 30. She has also putforth her case that after 4­5 days of the FIR, her mother had come to her work place and threatened to her life in the presence of her sister Chhaya. 31. The room where the victim, her mother and accused were residing was at Vitthalwadi and it was under construction in which they were temporarily residing. The said room like a shop having shutter to close. Adjoining to the said room many other labourers were residing. After 3­4 days of the incident, she had gone to the house of sister Chhaya who married with Ashok Gaikwad. Then her parents had come to take her back but she refused to accompany with them. 32. There was no resistance mentioned in the FIR or in the substantial evidence of the victim before the Court such as her hands were tied, she attempted to run away but accused assaulted her and 14 Judgment Spl. Case No.50/2014 when she raised shouts, at that time the accused had pressed her mouth. Moreover, an omission has brought on record that accused used to commit sexual intercourse with her forcibly, portion marked 'A'. The victim never disclosed the first incident as narrated by her to her sister Chhaya at any time till she went there during the period of two months. When she had gone to the house of Chhaya, her parents had come there and there was quarrel in between the accused and Ashok, the husband of Chhaya. 33. The natural conduct of the victim for non disclosing the incident immediately to anyone including her sister P.W.2 Chhaya is unnatural. She had an opportunity to disclose the incident to her neighbours residing nearby her room or to her sister or to her employer where she was working with labour with her mother. 34. Sou Chhaya Ashok Suryavanshi though married with one Chandu Patel initially but she deserted him and then married with Ashok Gaikwad before 15 years. According to her, her mother Anusaya (D.W.1) is addicted to liquor. Her father died before 15 years i.e. after six months of her marriage. Initially her mother and sister were residing at Golden Park hutment, Kalyan. This witness has knowing since her childhood as she was working with Jaya Patil builder where she was working as labour. 35. When she was residing at village Kolivali, at that time the victim, the mother and accused were residing at Kolshewadi in a room which was under construction. It is her case that after repeating the incident of rape on the victim she had come to her house in the evening 15 Judgment Spl. Case No.50/2014 time and disclosed that accused used to put off lights, undressed her and commits sexual intercourse on her. Then she immediately took the victim to Dudhnaka Policy Chowki who then sent to Kolshewadi Police Station where FIR (Exh.21) was recorded by police. The victim was sent to Rukminibai Hospital for medical examination and then to Civil Hospital, Thane. Thereafter, the victim went to Akola to reside with her maternal uncle. The victim had come to her house from Akola one month prior to her deposition. She had gone for labour work on the site, at that time her mother told her that she would give her Rs.10,000/­ and she should not depose anything against the accused. The victim has contradicted her version regarding offering of cash Rs.10,000/­, so that the victim should not depose against the accused. 36. For the purpose of rape and penetrative sexual assault, the prosecution has examined P.W.5 Dr. Neeta Bhagwat, MO Rukminibai Hospital stated that WPC Smt. Pawar of Kolshewadi Police Station had brought the victim on 15/3/2014 at 11.30 p.m. She recorded her history disclosed by the victim that her step father (Rakesh Varma­accused) was committing rape on her at her residence since last two months. The last sexual intercourse was not remembering her. Since last three days she was staying with her sister Chhaya. She has further brought on record that her menses was 8 days back as it was started 6 months back. 37. After obtaining the consent of Chhaya, she examined the victim. On her examination she found that her hymen was not intact but there was no evidence of fresh injury over hymen edges. There was no bleeding found from vagina. The vaginal opening was distinsible with one finger easily. Her finding were suggesting of sexual assault in view 16 Judgment Spl. Case No.50/2014 of distinsible vagina and tearing of hymen. She has collected the blood sample, nail clipping, pubic hair and vaginal swab which were sealed and labeled and then they handed to WPN Smt. Pawar on 15/3/2014 at 11.45 p.m. Accordingly, she issued the medical certificate at Exh.34. 38. This witness did not find any healed injury over private part of the victim. She has also stated that hymen ruptured is caused by passage of blood clots during menstruation and hymen can be torned by putting any foreign body in vagina and masturbation. She has made it clear that if there is possibility of two fingers admits easily then sexual intercourse probably occurred. She did not mention in medical certificate at Exh.34 about violent intercourse laceration of vaginal wall or posterior side and single posterior side and gait broad based and pain. She did not observe that soon after the assault the torn margin are sharp and red and bleed on touch. Even examined the victim after 3­4 days of the incident, the edges of laceration are congested and swollen the surroundings tissues are also swollen and tendered. In view of the opinion of this witness there was vaginal opening distinsible. Though her findings were suggesting of sexual assault in view of distinsible of vagina and tearing of hymen, but hymen can be caused by passage of blood clots during menstruation. She has clearly opined that if there is possibility of two fingers admit easily, then sexual intercourse probably occurs. This was not the position in this case and hence the possibility of hymen ruptured by the passage of blood clots during menstruation cannot be ruled out. Further, she did not observe that the torn margin are sharp and red and bleed on touch even examine the victim after 3­4 days of the incident and the edges of laceration were not found congested and swollen and the surrounding tissue were also not swollen. Therefore, the medical 17 Judgment Spl. Case No.50/2014 evidence is not supporting the case of the prosecution regarding the rape or penetrative sexual assault. 39. P.W.7 PN Swapnil Macchhindra Gosavi carried the seized muddemal property in C.R. No. I­118/2014 under Sec.376 of IPC to CA Kalina, Mumbai in different crime which were in all 6 parcels, 7 small bottles and 3 tubes, total 16 muddemal properties and handed over to the office of C.A. Kalina, Mumbai alongwith the covering letter. He obtained an acknowledgment of C.A. office on covering letter and handed over to P.W.9 Smt. Hire, IO. According to him, all the muddemal properties were in sealed condition but she did not state from whom he received the muddemal property. 40. The prosecution has produced C.A. reports at Exh.22, 23 and 24 wherein no blood or semen was detected on nail clipping and pubic hair of the victim vide Exh.22 nor the blood or semen nor vaginal fluid was detected on the pubic hair and nail clippings of the accused vide Exh.23, however, on safari half shirt of the accused and salwar of the victim human blood was found but blood group was inconclusive. 41. The learned advocate for the accused placed his reliance on the ruling reported in 2016 ALL MR (Cri) 126 (State of Maharashtra Vs. Arun Gopalrao Verulkar), wherein the testimony of the victim was disbelieved on the reason that the victim did not report any rape in the FIR lodged immediately by her but mentioned about the rape allegedly taken place 15 days prior to lodging the FIR but did not depose about it in the Court. The medical evidence does not lend to support to her assertion and entire story of alleged rape surfaces omission. Considering 18 Judgment Spl. Case No.50/2014 the event of quarrel between the accused and father prior to the incident on account of money transaction and fact of her alleged hiding and then coming out of the house of the accused, Their Lordship held that the testimony of the victim cannot be believed. In this case on hand, prior to lodging the FIR the quarrel had taken place in between the accused and Ashok Gaikwad, the husband of Chhaya as he was not allowing the victim to go with her mother and the accused who had come to fetch her back. Therefore, due to quarrel P.W.2 Chhaya must have aggrieved and hence she had taken the victim to the police station to lodge the FIR. 42. PSO P.W.6 API Madhav Krishna Naikwad had recorded the FIR of the victim at Exh.21 and drew the spot panchanama (Exh.30) and also seized the clothes on the person of the accused on 15/3/2014 under seizure panchanama (Exh.31) viz. Saphari shirt, blue full pant, underwear with red stains and sandow baniyan after arresting him. P.W.9 WPSI Smt. Vrushali Karbhari Hire carried out the investigation from 15/3/2014 and sent the victim to Civil Hospital for ascertaining her age. She had also sent the accused for his medical examination with request to collect the blood sample, nail clipping, public hair and semen. She also seized the clothes of the victim produced by P.W.2 Chhaya viz. Salwar and kurta. Then she sent the seized clothes of the victim and accused and samples to FSL, Kalina, Mumbai. She then recorded the statements of the witnesses including the contractor­cum­builder who was constructing the room where the alleged incident occurred. 43. P.W.4 Madhukar Bhosale is the panch witness for spot panchanama (Exh.30), seizure panchanama of the clothes of the victim and accused at Exh.31 & 32 but he has not supported the case of the 19 Judgment Spl. Case No.50/2014 prosecution in all respect. Even during the cross­examination by the Ld. A.P.P. with the permission of the Court nothing fruitful has brought on record. 44. The accused has examined the defence witness D.W.1 Smt. Anusaya Hari Aade, the mother of the victim on the point of the false involvement of the accused who had selected the groom from his native place U.P. but the victim was not ready and only with a view to pressurise the accused and avoid said groom she concocted her false story. 45. Admittedly, the accused was residing with D.W.1 Smt. Anusaya. This fact was disliking by the sons of Anusaya and hence they started residing separately from her. The conduct of this witness is also unnatural as she did not take any action when the victim and her mother had come to her house for the first time and victim disclosed her that accused was keeping physical relations with her. Thereafter, the victim alone had come after 8 days and then she had taken her to the police chowki immediately. It is not the case of this witness that the family members i.e. her victim's sister and brothers were hating the accused but on the contrary they were visiting the native place of the accused in U.P. 46. She has also admitted that the accused has searched the groom for the victim at his native place and there was talk about the marriage of the victim. The groom was residing in small village. 47. Though this witness had failed seriousness of the incident 20 Judgment Spl. Case No.50/2014 but she did not believe the words of the victim when she narrated about the incident. About the physical relations narrated by the victim has been brought on record as an omission. Thus, the victim who is aggrieved by her groom chosen by the accused and her mother at the native place of the accused in U.P. must be the reason behind filing such FIR, so that she need not go to U.P. after the marriage. Further, the first incident was not disclosed to anyone by the victim including her sister Chhaya. If really such incident could have been occurred, she should have approach to the police or at least could have disclose the incident to her near and close relatives including the neighbours but this has not happened. P.W.2 Chhaya also did not believe the words of the victim when she disclosed the alleged incident. It has come on record that after the first incident of alleged sexual intercourse the victim had come her house after eight days and then she was taken to the police chowki. After the incident, the victim had gone to her native place at Akola. She had come to the house of Chhaya one month before her deposition. When the victim had gone to labour work, her mother had offered Rs.10,000/­, so that she should not depose against the accused, however, the victim in her evidence has made out different story by stating that after 4­5 days of the lodging of her FIR her mother had come to her work place when the victim was working with Chhaya as labour work and threatened to her life. This itself shows some concoction in respect of imaginary facts including the alleged rape and penetrative sexual assault. The reason of involvement of the accused appears to be that of the groom selected by him at his native place but the victim was disliking. 48. Under the circumstances, I hold that the prosecution has 21 Judgment Spl. Case No.50/2014 failed to prove the charges the levelled against by adducing cogent, reliable and trustworthy evidence. Hence, I answer the points No.2 & 3, in the negative. 49. Resultantly, the accused deserves to be acquitted, and as such, I proceed to pass the following order : ORDER i] The accused Rakesh Matadip Varma is hereby acquitted vide Section 235(1) of Cr.P.C. of the offences punishable under Sec.376 of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 4 & 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offenes Act, 2012. ii] He is in Jail since 15/3/2014, hence, he shall be set at liberty forthwith if not required in any other crime or case. iii] The seized muddemal property i.e. safari shirt, blue coloured full pant, blue coloured under pant and sandow baniyan of the accused and one orange coloured half sleeves kurta and salwar of the victim which are not produced before this Court, however, it being worthless be destroyed after the period of appeal is over. iv] The accused shall execute his P.R. & S.B. of Rs.15,000/­ to appear before the Higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect of appeal filed against this Judgment as per Sec.437­A of Cr.P.C. v] Such bail shall remain in force for six months from today. Kalyan, (M.J.Mirza) Dt.2/2/2017. Special Judge, Under Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Kalyan.

1 Order below Ex.1 in Criminal Anticipatory Bail Application No.376/2016 Shri Kishor Tukaram Gaikwad ….. Applicant Vs. State of Maharashtra, (Through Kolsewadi Police Station) ….. Opponent 1/­ This is an application for anticipatory bail filed under section 438 of Cr.P.C. in C.R.No. I­41/2016 of Kolsewadi Police Station for the offence punishable under sections 363, 366­A, 376­A r/w.34 of IPC and under sections 4, 8 and 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2/­ The applicant/accused has contended that false case is filed against him. The arrested accused Anil Tukaram Gaikwad who had eloped with the victim girl is the elder brother of this applicant/accused. This applicant/accused has no concern with the alleged kidnapping and rape of the victim girl. The custodial interrogation of this applicant/accused is not necessary. He lastly prayed for allowing his application. 3/­ The Investigation Officer has resisted the application by filing his Say at Exh.7 wherein it is contended that the name of the applicant/accused is mentioned in the FIR. The offences are of serious nature and the investigation is going on. The Investigation Officer lastly prayed for rejecting the application. 4/­ Heard Ld. Advocate Shri A.N. Khandare for applicant/accused 2 and Ld. APP Shri Ramteke for the State. 5/­ After considering the rival submissions, now it is to be seen as to whether the custodial interrogation of the applicant/accused is necessary or what. After perusing the FIR which is lodged by the father of the victim girl it is seen that it is lodged against unknown person with an allegation that he has kidnapped his daughter aged 17 years. The Investigation Officer on previous date had produced statement of the victim girl for my perusal. After perusing said statement it is seen that the victim girl who was 17 years and 9 months old at the time of incident was having love affair with the main accused who is the elder brother of this applicant. Her statement further makes out that she performed marriage with the main accused in a temple at Titwala. Her statement no where makes out any sort of allegation against the present applicant. Her statement also does not say anything regarding this applicant helping the main accused for taking away the victim girl. The offence of rape is registered against the main accused who is elder brother of this applicant. Thus, considering the above facts, I am of the considered opinion that the custodial interrogation of this applicant is certainly not necessary and he is entitled to pre­arrest bail. Accordingly, I pass following order : ORDER 1] The application is allowed. 2] In the event of arrest of applicant/accused Kishor Tukaram Gaikwad in C.R.No. I­41/2016 of Kolsewadi Police Station for the offence punishable under sections 363, 366­A, 376­A r/w.34 of IPC and under sections 4, 8 and 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, he be released on his executing P.R. Bond of Rs. 3 15,000/­ (Rupees Fifteen Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount. 3] The applicant shall mark his presence in Kolsewadi Police Station on every Wednesday in between 11.00 a.m. to 1.00 p.m. till filing of charge­sheet and to co­operate police in investigation. 4] The applicant shall not try to come in contact with informant and other witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence or witnesses. 5] Inform concerned Police Station accordingly. Kalyan. (S.B. Gaidhani) 10/06/2016 Addl. Sessions Judge, Kalyan.

1 ABA 539/2018 Or. Exh.1 CNR NO. MHTH06­001122­2018 ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN A.B.A.NO. 539/2018 : CNR NO. MHTH06­001122­2018 This is an application for grant of anticipatory bail U/Sec. 438 of Cr.P.C. filed by the applicants/accused in C.R.No.I­91/2018 registered with Vitthalwadi Police Station for offence punishable U/Sec. 354, 323, 336, 337, 504 and 506 of I.P.C. 2] The applicants/accused have been required to move this application for anticipatory bail in sequel to FIR lodged by the informant Sau. Swati Chandrakant Kanade alleging that on 02/03/2018 at about 12.00 the informant's daughter had gone to take her clothes at the tailor shop. However, the said shop was closed, therefore, she was returning from there. When she reached at Jagat Kirana shop, the applicants/ accused came in Maruti car bearing No. MH­05­9294, pulled her hand and told her to sit in their said Maruti car and thus outraged her modesty. The applicants/accused also pelted stones and abused, threatened her. On the basis of said complaint, FIR had been registered against the said accused. 3] The applicants have contended that they are innocent and are falsely implicated in this case. They contended that the applicants have lodged N.C. reports bearing N.C.No. 494/2018 against the informant as the informant is in habit of lodging false report. They further contended that the cases under MOCCA and MPID are pending against the informant's son and nobody is helping the informant in releasing her son from the said cases, therefore, the informant is lodging 2 ABA 539/2018 Or. Exh.1 CNR NO. MHTH06­001122­2018 the reports against the boys to extract huge amount from the applicant/accused. They contended that the story in this crime is concocted one. They also contended that there is no prima­facie case against the applicants/accused. They further contended that they are ready to abide by the conditions imposed by this court. They also contended that there is no need of custodial interrogation and no possibility of tampering with prosecution witnesses, if he is released on bail. On the aforestated amongst others grounds, the applicants have sought for their release on anticipatory bail. 4] I.O. has resisted the bail application by filing his say contending that in furtherance of their common intention, the applicants/accused have committed this crime and the interrogation is yet to be conducted. He contended that the vehicle used while committing the crime is yet to be recovered from the applicants/accused. He further contended that if the applicants/accused are released on bail, there is possibility of committing similar offence. He also contended that there was previous dispute between applicants/accused and the informant and custody for that purpose is also necessary to find out the truth. The Investigating Officer contended that for detail interrogation, custody of the applicants/accused is necessary. 5] I have heard Ld.A.P.P. Shri. Kulkarni for the State and Ld. Adv. Smt. Bhopi for the applicants/accused. 6] Here itself I may state that there is no need of custodial interrogation as far as accused is concerned. This because the offences 3 ABA 539/2018 Or. Exh.1 CNR NO. MHTH06­001122­2018 pitted against are under Secs. 354, 323, 504, 506, 336, 337 of the I.P.C. and Sec. 12 of the POCSO Act and all these offences are punishable not more than three years imprisonment. Even except Sec. 354 of I.P.C. and Sec. 12 of POCSO Act, other offences are bailable. Therefore, considering the nature of the allegations made in the F.I.R. and in view of the decision of Their Lordships of Apex Court in the case of Arnesh Kumar /State of Bihar, in Cri.Appeal No.1277/2014, it would be appropriate to grant anticipatory bail to the applicants/ accused directing the police not to arrest them in the event of their arrest. 7] It appears that the applicants are permanent resident of the addresses given in the title clause of the application and there is no possibility of their fleeing away from justice. Furthermore, the possibility cannot be ruled out that the applicants/accused might have been implicated in this crime as no one is coming to help the informant to get release her son from jail following his imprisonment in serious offences. 8] It would be worthwhile to mention here that the contention of the Ld.Advocate for the applicant that there is no necessity for arrest of the applicants/accused as per the parameters laid down under Sec.41 of Cr.P.C. Therefore, considering the nature and gravity of the accusations, it will be appropriate to grant anticipatory bail to the applicants/ accused. 9] The I.O. has contended in his say that there was previous dispute between the applicants and informant. If this fact is considered, 4 ABA 539/2018 Or. Exh.1 CNR NO. MHTH06­001122­2018 then the possibility cannot be ruled out that the accusation have been made with object of humiliating the applicants/accused by having them arrested. Therefore, in the present case in hand, considering the rival submissions, it would be appropriate to grant anticipatory bail to the applicants/accused. 10] In this connection the Ld. Advocate for the applicants/ accused rightly placed his reliance on the decision in the case of Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre V/s. State of Maharashtra 2011 (1) SC cases 694, wherein it has been laid down that the court should be loath to reject the grant of anticipatory bail in as much as it impinges on the personal liberty of an individual. Meaning thereby, unless and until there is an imminent and a great imperative to have a custodial interrogation of an accused, the anticipatory bail does not deserve to be denied. However, for the ends of justice, it would be justifiable to direct the applicants to give attendance to the police station so as to enable the Investigating Officer to investigate the crime. 11] For these reasons, it is a fit case to exercise discretion to grant anticipatory bail to the accused, as it would not be appropriate to refuse anticipatory bail to the accused. In the result, the following order is made : :ORDER: i] The Vitthalwadi Police Station is directed that the applicants/accused in C.R.No.I­91/2018 registered with Vitthalwadi Police Station for offence punishable under Sec. 354, 323, 336, 337, 504 and 506 of I.P.C. and Sec. 12 of POCSO Act, 2012, in the event of their 5 ABA 539/2018 Or. Exh.1 CNR NO. MHTH06­001122­2018 arrest, they be released on bail on furnishing their P.B. and S.B. in sum of Rs.15,000/­ each by this order of anticipatory bail. ii] The applicants/accused shall attend Vitthalwadi police station on every Friday between 1,00 p.m. to 3.00 p.m. till filing of charge­sheet or two months period whichever is earlier. iii] They shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any other persons acquainted with the facts of the accusation against them so as to dissuade them from disclosing such facts to the Court to any other officer. iv] Breach of any of the conditions shall entail cancellation of bail. v] Inform to the concerned Police Station, accordingly. Kalyan. (D.S.Ghumare) Dt.11/04/2018 Addl. Sessions Judge, Kalyan.

Received on : 13­05­2014. Registered on: 13­05­2014 Decided on : 19­12­2016. Duration: 02Y 07 M 06 D IN THE COURT OF THE ADDL. SESSIONS JUDGE ­2 AT KALYAN (Presided over by D.S. Hatarote) Special Case No. 54/2014 Exh.No.__ The state of Maharashtra Through Shivajinagar Police Station Ambernath .. Prosecution VERSUS Bhim Pundalik Dhepe, Age – 22 years, R/at : Room No.1230, Bhim nagar, Kansai Road, Opposite Jalagram Glass House, Ambernath (E), Dist. Thane. .. Accused Offence : U/Sec. 354, 323 of the Indian Penal Code and under section 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. (2) Appearances: ================================= Smt. Bhoir, A.P.P. for State Shri. Deshmukh, Advocate for the accused ================================= J U D G M E N T. ( Delivered in open court on 19th December, 2016 ) 1. This accused is prosecuted by the State through police station Shivajinagar, Ambernath for the abovestated offences. Brief facts are as follows: 2. One Jyoti Yadav lodged complaint against this accused on 14/03/2014. In her complaint she alleged that on 14/03/2014 she had been to meet her friend Seema at Laxmi Nagar. Her friend Govind Sharma was also with her. She and her friend Govind were going to Seema by rickshaw at about 1.00 to 1.35 p.m. On the way she saw accused. Therefore, she stopped the rickshaw. She and Govind alighted from the rickshaw. They went to accused in front of Prabha Hospital. Accused asked this complainant who is the boy. She replied that he is her boy friend. At that time accused gave the slap to Govind. When complainant Jyoti asked accused why he slapped her friend, at that time accused caught her hand and stated that (3) Spl. Case No. 54/2014 (J) he loves her. Saying so he outraged her modesty by touching on her cheek and then accused went away. Therefore, complainant went to Shivajinagar police station, Ambernath East and lodged complaint. Crime was registered. Investigation was carried by one police sub inspector R. R. Kochrekar. He prepared spot panchanama on 15/03/2014. He recorded statement of Sunil Yadav, Ravindra Yadav, Seema Mandarai and others. After completion of investigation he submitted chargesheet in the court. 3. Charge against this accused is framed by this court at Exh.20. Charge was read over and explained to him in Marathi language. Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. His defence is of total denial. He has not adduced any defence evidence. 4. Prosecution was directed to adduce its evidence. In response to that prosecution examined complainant Jyoti Yadav Sherbahadur at Exh.22. Accused admitted spot panchanama. No further evidence is adduced by the prosecution. 5. I have gone through the oral and documentary evidence of prosecution. I have heard both the learned advocates at length. 6. Following points arise for my consideration. My (4) findings on those points are as follows for the reasons stated below. POINTS FINDINGS 1) Does prosecution prove that on 14/03/2014 at about 13.30 to 13.45 hours at Shivaji Chowk, in front of Prabha hospital, near Bus stop, Ambernath (E) accused used criminal force to complainant Jyoti Yadav intending to outrage her modesty and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 354 of the I.P.C.? No. 2) Does prosecution further prove that on the above­said date, time and place while outraging modesty of complainant Jyoti Yadav accused voluntarily caused hurt to complainant and her friend by slapping them and thereby committed an offence punishable U/Sec. 323 of the I.P.C.? No. 3) Does prosecution further prove that on the above said date, time and place accused committed sexual assault on complainant Jyoti Yadav who is minor aged about 17 years and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012? No. (5) Spl. Case No. 54/2014 (J) REASONS As to Points no. 1 to 3:­ 7. As I have already stated in order to establish the guilt of accused, prosecution examined single witness i.e. the complainant Jyoti Yadav. She deposed that nothing was happened with her. She flatly denied that accused outraged her modesty. She further denied that accused gave any slap to Govind. She denied that she shown the spot of offence. In her examination in chief she admitted that in the year 2014 she was 19 years old. Now, she is wife of the present accused. As now this complainant is married with this accused, it seems that she is not ready to depose anything against her husband. It is but natural. She cannot be compelled to depose against her husband. Her evidence is of no use for the prosecution to prove the guilt of accused. She deposed that at the time of alleged incident she was 19 years old. Therefore, alleged offence under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 neither attracts nor proved. Considering the fact that the complainant herself turned hostile, prosecution has rightly declined to examine any further witness. 8. As there is no incriminating evidence against this accused, his statement under section 313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure stands dispensed with. (6) 9. As absolutely no incriminating evidence against this accused in the evidence of prosecution, I have no hesitation to answer all the three points in negative. In conclusion, I pass the following order. O R D E R 1) The accused Bhim Pundalik Dhepe is hereby acquitted of the offence punishable under Section 354, 323 of the Indian Penal Code and under section 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2) His bail bonds stands cancelled. He is set at liberty. 3) Accused to furnish bail under section 437(A) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Kalyan ( D.S. Hatarote ) Date :­ 19/12/2016 Additional Sessions Judge Kalyan.

Case 59/2014 [Judg.] :JUDGMENT: [Pronounced in the open Court on 10.10.2015] 1] The accused Manohar Shridhar Mahanto is facing trial for the offences punishable under Sections 376, 377 & 504 of Indian Penal Code and Sections 4 & 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 . 2] The case of the prosecution, in short, can be summarized in brief, as under : That the victim, P.W.2, is minor aged 7 years. She is the daughter of the informant ­P.W.1 Sau. Chaya Raja Padyachi. The victim is residing with her parents, brother and sister at Village­Vadavali. The informant and her husband used to leave the house at 10 a.m. and returned at 10 p.m. During their absence, the victim girl used to stay with her elder sister and brother. In their absence, the neighbourers used to take care of them. 3] The birth date of the victim is 29­8­2004 who born on the day of Raksha­bandhan festival. On the day of the incident when the informant returned to home, at that time victim girl aged 7 years was sitting in the corner of the house and was in frighten condition. When she inquired with her she disclosed that at 6 to 6.30 p.m. when she was playing out of the house, at that time the accused Manohar Shridhar Mahanto called her in his house promising her to pay Rs.10/­. Then he removed her nicker and she was made to sleep. Then he put a cloth on her mouth and then rubbed his penis to her body and applied sticky substance. Then he put clothes of minor and threatened by saying that she should not disclose the incident to anyone or else he would take away her elder sister. By saying 3 Spl. Case 59/2014 [Judg.] so she was sent to her home. When the informant inspected her anus, she found that it was reddish and swelling. Then informant called her mother who also confirmed. Her neighbour had seen that the victim girl was taken by the accused but she did not give much attention as he used to play with small children. The people residing in the area when came to know about the incident, they assaulted the accused and handed over to the police. Then she lodged the FIR Exh.18. 4] Ambernath police registered the crime bearing C.R. No. I­94/2014 under Sections 376, 377 & 506 of IPC and Sections 7 & 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 . 5] Further investigation was entrusted to P.W.3 P.I. Shri Sunil Digmbar Ghuge who received FIR recorded by the PSO API, Shri Bhoir and arrest panchanama (Exh.26) of the accused. Then he drew the spot panchnama (Exh.19) and seized the clothes of the victim under seizure panchanama (Exh.20). On the basis of voluntary disclosure statement (Exh.27) made by the accused under Section 27 of the Evidence Act, he seized his clothes under seizure panchnama (Exh.28). He then sent the seized clothes of the victim and accused to FSL for analysis purpose along with his covering letter (Exh.31). He received C.A. report (Exh.10). The victim was sent for her statement to be recorded under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C. He collected her birth extract issued by the KDMC authority below Exh.32. After completion of investigation he filed charge­sheet in this Court. 6] I framed the charge at Exh.14 which was read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. The accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. His defence is of false involvement as per his statements recorded 4 Spl. Case 59/2014 [Judg.] under Section 313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The accused has not stepped into the witness box nor examined any witness in defence. 7] Heard learned APP Shri Y.M.Patil for the State and learned Advocate Shri M.A.Shivdas for the accused, at length. 8] The following points arise for my determination and my findings thereon are recorded by me against them for the reasons to follow:­ Points Findings 1 Whether prosecution proved that age of the prosecutrix was below 18 years on the date of incident ? .. In the affirmative. 2 Whether prosecution proved that the accused on 20­3­2014 at about 6.30 p.m. at Vadolgaon, near Papad Company, behind water tank, Ambernath (W) in his house committed rape on the minor victim girl aged 7 years (376) ? .. In the negative. 3 Whether prosecution proved that on the aforesaid date, time and place the accused had carnal intercourse against the order of nature with minor victim girl aged 7 years (377) ? .. In the negative. 4 Whether prosecution proved that on the aforesaid date, time and place the accused intentionally insulted and thereby gave provocation would cause the minor victim girl aged 7 years to break public peace (504)? .. In the negative. 5 Whether prosecution proved that on the 5 Spl. Case 59/2014 [Judg.] aforesaid date, time and place the accused committed penetrative sexual assault on the minor victim girl, aged 7 years, punishable under Section 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 ? .. In the negative. 6 Whether prosecution proved that on the aforesaid date, time and place the accused committed sexual assault on the minor victim girl, aged 7 years punishable under Section 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 ? .. In the negative. 7 What order ? .. Accused acquitted REASONS : As to point No. 1: 9] To substantiate the charge, the prosecution has examined only three witnesses viz. P.W.1 – Sau. Chaya Raja Padyachi, the informant and mother of the victim girl (Exh.17), P.W.2 ­ minor victim girl (Exh.24) and P.W.3 ­ I.O. P.I. Shri. Sunil Digambar Ghuge (Exh.25). The Investigating Officer has produced her birth extract at Exh. 32 issued by KDMC Authority showing the birth date of the victim girl as 29­8­2004. The date of incident is 20­3­2014. Therefore, her age on the date of incident is 9 Years, 6 months and 21 days. The victim girl has stated her age as 9 years and her mother, P.W.1, states that her age was 10 years. The birth extract is being public document within the meaning of Section 74 of the Evidence Act, hence, it can be exhibited and read in evidence. The learned advocate for the accused has also not challenged the birth certificate (Exh.32). Therefore, I hold that the victim was minor on the date of the alleged incident. Hence, I answer the point No. 1, in the 6 Spl. Case 59/2014 [Judg.] affirmative. As to points No. 2, 3 , 5 & 6: 10] To prove the offence under S. 376 of IPC, it is necessary for the prosecution to prove that penetration though slight or forcibly trying to penetrate and on such rubbing ejaculate himself to hold that it is certainly an attempt to commit rape under Section 376 r.w. 511 of IPC to record the conviction. 11] The victim girl is admittedly of 9 years therefore her consent has no relevancy. The oral testimony of the victim recorded by following the directions of the Hon'ble Apex Court, she states that she is studying in 5 th standard and her younger brother studying in 3rdstandard. Her school time is 12 pm. To 5 p.m. After returning from school she used to play with her younger brother. Her mother goes for work and used to return during night time. So far as the incident is concerned she has stated that the accused known as Bhaiyya had assaulted her on her back by his hands due to which she had fever but no sticky substance was applied on her person. She had disclosed the incident of assault by accused to her mother who then took her to the police station where the police inquired with her in the presence of her mother. She has specifically denied that her clothes were removed by the accused. She has not stated anything before the Medical Officer when she was medically examined. 12] The mother of the victim PW­1 Smt. Chaya was disclosed by the victim that she was assaulted by the accused when she returned at 10 p.m. from her work. On enquiry with the accused about beating the victim she was playing in front of the house of the accused. The victim also showed 7 Spl. Case 59/2014 [Judg.] the place where she was playing. When she had gone to make inquiry with the accused, at that time the accused was sleeping in a room. At that time, her husband was also with her. When she asked accused as to why he assaulted her victim daughter he replied that she was shouting in front of his house and hence he beat her. Then her husband and the neighbours assaulted accused Bhaiyya. One of her neighbour made phone call to the police and accordingly, police arrived. She has stated that in her FIR except the assault by the accused on her daughter she stated nothing. 13] Though the learned APP cross­examined PW­1 Smt. Chaya at length on the basis of her FIR at Exh.18 but she denied the portion mark 'A' in her statement. In her cross­examination by the defence she has made it clear that she lodged the FIR stating that accused assaulted her daughter. Both these witnesses were material but not supported the case of the prosecution except that the accused assaulted the victim girl. 14] The medical certificate below Exh.21 has been admitted by the defence wherein no injuries on the person of the victim girl were noticed by the Medical Officer including swelling or reddishness on anus. The defence has also admitted the spot panchnama (Exh.19) wherein nothing incriminating was seized. The clothes on the person of the victim girl were also seized under the seizure panchnama (Exh.20) having some stains which was sent to FSL for analysis. The C.A. report (Exh.22) show the towel and underwear of the accused at Exh.A­6 and Exh.B shows blood group of A of human origin and semen of human. However, neither blood or nor semen was detected on the clothes of the victim girl. Thus, there is no evidence connecting the accused with alleged offence. 8 Spl. Case 59/2014 [Judg.] 15] Furthermore, the statement of the victim was recorded at belated stage i.e. after one months and 10 days of the incident but no explanation was offered by the prosecution. Moreover, nothing has been brought on record regarding aggravated penetrative sexual assault and for sexual assault punishable under Sections 4 & 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences, Act, 2012 and also for unnatural offence punishable under Section 377 of IPC. Under the circumstances, no nexus has been established by the prosecution for the offence punishable under Section 376 or Section 377 of IPC. Hence, I answer the points No.2, 3, 5 & 6 in the negative. As to point No.4 16] For the purpose of intentionally insult to provoke the breach of the peace, it is for the prosecution to prove that the accused intentionally insulted and gave provocation intending or knowing it to be likely that such provocation will cause to break public peace or to commit any other offence. None of the requisite ingredients have been proved by the prosecution by adducing cogent, reliable and trustworthy evidence as none of the witnesses including Investigating Officer whispered anything about it . Hence, I answer point No.4, in the negative. 17] Resultantly, the accused deserves to be acquitted, and as such, I proceed to pass the following order :­ ORDER i] The accused Manohar Shridhar Mahanto is hereby acquitted vide Section 235(1) of Cr.P.C. of the offences punishable under Sections 376, 377 & 504 of IPC and Sections 4 & 8 of the Protection of Children from 9 Spl. Case 59/2014 [Judg.] Sexual Offences Act, 2012. ii] The accused Manohar Shridhar Mahanto is in jail since his date of arrest i.e. 21­3­2014, therefore, he be set at liberty forthwith, if not required in any other case or crime. iii] The seized muddemal property i.e. clothes of the accused and victim, being worthless be destroyed after the period of appeal is over. iv] The accused shall execute his P.R. of Rs.15,000/­ to appear before the Higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect of appeal filed against this judgment as per Section 437­A of Cr.P.C. Such bail shall remain in force for six months from today. Kalyan, [M.J.Mirza] Dt.10.10.2015. Special Judge, Under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 10 Spl. 1 Spl. Spl.Case 66/2014 [Judgment] Presented on : 2.6.2014. Registered on : 2.6.2014. Decided on : 20.7.2016. Duration : Y. M. D. 2. 1. 18. IN THE COURT OF SPECIAL JUDGE, KALYAN AT : KALYAN. (Presided over by : M.J.Mirza) SPECIAL CASE NO.66/2014 Exh. No. State of Maharashtra. Through : P.I., Tilaknagar Police Station. ...Complainant. Vs. Haresh Dhanaji Mhatre, Age­23 Years, Occ. Owner of Hukka Parlour, R/at­ Shantinagar, Desaigaon, Near Jakatnaka, Post Padale, Dist.­ Thane. ….Accused. Appearance : Spl.P.P.Shri D.V. Bhangare for the State. Advocate Shri V.P.Sonekar for the accused. Offences : ­ Punishable under Section 354 & 509 of I.P.C. and Section 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. :JUDGMENT: (Delivered in open Court on 20/7/2016) 1. The accused Haresh Dhanaji Mhatre is facing the trial for the offences punishable under Sections 354 & 509 of I.P.C. and Section 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, alleging that the accused outraged her modesty and uttered the words intending to insult the victim and also committed sexual harassment. 2. The case of the prosecution, in short is as under : 2 Spl. Spl.Case 66/2014 [Judgment] The informant/victim, aged 15 years, lodged the FIR on 28/10/2013 stating therein that she is residing with her parents at Desale pada, Dombivli(E). On 26/10/2013 at 10.45 a.m. she reached to her school at Pandurangwadi, at that time suddenly a boy on motorcycle reached near her and kept a cell phone in the self of her bag, however, she neglected as it was time for her examination and therefore, she went to the class room. There was exam of history and political science. After the examination was over she noticed a cell phone kept in the self of her bag which was of Corban make and was in good condition. After returning home she showed the said cell phone to her parents and cousin brother Prashant Vijay Parab. When it was started, E­mail I.D. and photograph of the accused was seen therein and the said boy had told her on 24/10/2013 and 25/10/2013 at 12 noon twicely who had come on the motorcycle near Jain Mandir, Dombivli (E) by saying that whether she would do friendship with him, however, she replied that she will not do friendship with him and then he left away. 3. On 26/10/2013 at 10.45 a.m. when she reached near Pandurang High School at Pandurangwadi, again the accused came to her on motorcycle and asked whether she would do friendship with him repeatedly and thereby outraged her modesty and also sexually harassed her. She also produced the Corban make cell phone A­2 Plus model before the police. 4. PSO of Tilaknagar Police Station registered the crime at C.R.No.II­24/2013 under Sec. 509 of IPC and Sec. 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 on 28/10/2013 at 12.30 p.m. The accused came to be arrested on 28/10/2013 under arrest panchanama (Exh.17). 5. Further investigation was carried out by PW.3 Vinod Shankar Bhoir as the investigation was entrusted with him by Sr.P.I. He then drew the spot panchanama at Exh.18 and recorded the statements of the witnesses. He also collected the birth extract of the victim girl from the office of KDMC. After completion of investigation, he filed the chargesheet in this Special Court. 3 Spl. Spl.Case 66/2014 [Judgment] 6. Charge Exh.7 was framed by me which was read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. The accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. His defence is of false involvement as per his statement recorded under Section 313 of Code of Criminal Procedure. Neither the accused stepped into the witness­box nor examined any defence witness. 7. Heard learned Spl. P.P. Shri D.V.Bhangare for the State and learned Advocate Shri V.P.Sonekar for the accused, at length. 8. The following points arise for my determination and my findings thereon are recorded against them for the reasons to follow:­ Points Findings 1. Whether the prosecution proved that the victim is minor aged 15 years ? .. Yes. 2. Whether the prosecution has proved that on 26/10/2013, at 10.45 a.m. near Pandurang Vidyalaya, Jain Mandir, Dombivli (E), the accused used criminal force for maintaining friendship to minor victim girl, aged 15 years, intending to outrage her modesty, .. Not proved. punishable under Sec.354 of IPC ? 3. Whether the prosecution has proved that at the relevant time the accused intending to insult the modesty of minor victim girl, uttered repeatedly “ek>s lkscr QzsaM'khi dj'khy dk” intending that the same 4 Spl. Spl.Case 66/2014 [Judgment] shall be heard by the minor victim, punishable under Sec.509 of I.P.C. ? .. Not proved. 4. Whether the prosecution has proved that at the relevant time the accused committed sexual harassment upon minor victim girl, punishable under Sec.12 of the Protection of Children .. Not proved. from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 ? 5. What order ? ….. Accused acquitted. : REASONS : 9. To substantiate the charge, prosecution has examined in all three witnesses, viz. PW.1 minor victim girl at Exh.13 whose evidence was recorded in camera and also knowing the accused before the date of incident as she was having friendship with the accused but she did not disclose her friendship with the accused to any one. PW.2 Dattaram Tukaram Parab (Exh.­15), the father of the victim who had seen the cell phone in the self of the bag of the victim and hence he deposited it with the police in the police station. Then the victim disclosed him that the accused had met her twicely and asked her whether she can make friendship with him. He was asked by one Jaywant Mali to withdraw the case as accused is his nephew. The last witness is PW.3 I.O., A.P.I. Shri Vinod Shankar Bhoir (Exh.16) who carried out the investigation as usual by arresting the accused and prepared spot panchanama and also recorded the statements of the witnesses. As to point No. 1 : 10. The victim has brought on record in her testimony that her birth date is 31/8/1999. On the date of her evidence, her age was 15 5 Spl. Spl.Case 66/2014 [Judgment] years. PW.2 Dattatray Parab, the father of the victim failed to state the birth date of the victim. The investigating officer has not produced any proof of birth date of the victim on record. Under the circumstances, the age of the victim comes as 14 years 1 month & 27 days. However, for want of the document showing the birth extract it is difficult to accept the birth date stated by the victim. The defence has not seriously challenged the birth date of the victim brought on record by her. Hence, I hold that the birth date of the minor victim girl is 31/8/1999, and hence, she was minor on the date of the alleged incident. Therefore, I answer the point No.1 in the affirmative. As to point No.2 :­ 11. The best witness is the victim to depose about the incident in absence of her father (PW.2) Dattaram Tukaram Parab who was not the direct witness to the incident. The victim being minor and in view of Sec.37 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, the trial was conducted in camera under child ­ friendly atmosphere. The age of the victim was 15 years at the relevant time and hence, she was of the age of understanding. An oath was administered to her considering the age and maturity. She has brought on record that her birth date is 31/8/1999. She has also deposed the date of incident as 26/10/2013 at 12.15 p.m. at Pandurangwadi which is on the way of her school. On that day her examination of History and Geography paper was scheduled and time thereof was 12.45 p.m. 12. She has also brought on record that she knows the accused before the incident. According to her the accused handed over his cell phone to her by putting in the self of her bag where she used to keep her water bag. Then she showed the said cell phone to her father after returning from her examination who then was making calls to the 6 Spl. Spl.Case 66/2014 [Judgment] accused but the accused was replying either 'Yes' or 'No'. Then she approached to the police alongwith her parents where her father lodged the FIR. Nothing had happened after handing over the cell phone by the accused in her bag. The accused was asking her whether she can make friendship with him by obstructing her way but she refused. She has proved the FIR at Exh.14. 13. In her testimony she has stated that one Jaywant Mali is the maternal uncle of the accused who is residing in her locality and having visiting terms to his parents. She was knowing the accused who is visiting to the house of Jaywant Mali. 14. About 2­3 months before lodging the FIR, she had talking terms with the accused. Her father after seeing the cell phone in her bag enquired with her and scolded her but she did not disclose that she has friendship with the accused. During the period of friendship of 2­3 months prior to the incident, the accused did not misbehave with her at any time. As her parents had scolded her because of the reason that the cell phone was found in her bag, due to which her health was affected adversely. 15. Her father was searching the accused with his police friend Shri Desale. Since 26/10/2013 to 28/10/2013 her father was repeatedly calling the accused to come and see him but he did not turn up, therefore, her father approached to the police. Due to fear the accused did not see her father as her father was knowing her friendship with him. Infact, it is her case that she made demand of cell phone to the accused and then he had given cell phone to her. According to her, her father lodged the FIR but infact the record reveals that she herself is the informant and crime came to be registered on the basis of her own FIR. 7 Spl. Spl.Case 66/2014 [Judgment] 16. PW.2 Dattaray Parab, the father of the victim has no personal knowledge about the utterance made by the accused to the victim that whether she had made friendship with him. Due to fear of the parents, the victim might have concocted the story that accused put his cell phone in the self of her bag but the fact remains that she had made demand of the cell phone to the accused who had handed over to her. The victim was frightened when police were making enquiry with him and victim daughter. Jaywant Mali is the family friend of this witness who had requested him to withdraw the case as the accused is his nephew. He has putforth his case that she came to know about the friendship of the accused and the victim daughter after lodging the FIR. Inspite of repeated calls made by him but due to fear the accused did not speak with him on phone. He also took guidance from his friend Shri Desale serving in police force. Though the FIR is shown to have been lodged by the victim, however, this witness has stated that he dictated the contents thereof and the police reduced into writing as per his say. Moreover, because of the friendship in between his daughter and accused he became angry and lodged the FIR. 17. The I.O. PW.3 Vinod Shankar Bhoir A.P.I. has produced the arrest panchanama (Exh.17) and spot panchanama (Exh.18) which are not seriously challenged by the defence as nothing incriminating has been seized. 18. In order to constitute the offence under Sec. 354 of I.P.C. mere knowledge that the modesty of a woman is likely to be outragen is sufficient without any deliberate intention of having such outrage alone for its object. The essential ingredients of the offence are that the person assaulted must be a woman; that the accused must have used criminal force on her and that the criminal force must have been 8 Spl. Spl.Case 66/2014 [Judgment] used on that woman intending thereby to outrage her modesty. 19. Considering the circumstances under which the FIR of the victim came to be registered seems to be out of the friendship in between her and the accused. She made demand of cell phone to the accused. When her father saw the cell phone in the bag of the victim, he enquired and then scolded her. 20. Today teenagers are exposed to more sex related issues and lot of material is also available to them. Because of their impressionable age, girls and boys both may tend to get provoked and there can be a curious and very compelling demand of the body to get into such kind of relationship. Behavioural pattern of teenagers as biologically whenever the child turns into puberty, the child starts understanding his or her sexual needs. The nature of response depends on the upbringing, peer pressure, how civilized the environment is etc. Therefore, some sects of the community have acknowledged this biological factor and therefore, the early age marriages are performed in some religions or communities. Taking into consideration this social and biological factors, the law makers have considered the age of 15 as a age of consent when the marriage is performed. 21. As the ingredients required to constitute the offence the knowledge plays important role than that of deliberate intention. The further requirement is that the person assaulted must a woman, that the accused must use criminal force on her and that the criminal force must have been used on that woman intending thereby to outrage her modesty as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Pramia Vs. State of Rajisthan [(2008) 4 Crimes 126 (S.C.)]. In view of settled 9 Spl. Spl.Case 66/2014 [Judgment] position of law merely because asking about the friendship by the accused to the victim will not fall within the purview of offence punishable under Sec. 354 of I.P.C. for want of further requirement such as criminal force on her and such force must have been used on her intending thereby to outrage her modesty. Therefore, at any stage of imagination it cannot be said that the accused committed the offence punishable under Sec. 354 of I.P.C. Hence, I answer the point No.2, in the negative. As to point Nos. 3 & 4 :­ 22. As both the points are interlinked with each other, hence I discuss both the points together to avoid repetition. For the purpose of offence punishable under Section 509 the requirements are that the accused must be intending to insult the modesty of any woman, utters any words, makes any sound or gesture, or exhibit any object, intending that such word or sound shall be heard or that such gesture or object shall be seen, by such woman or intrudes upon the privacy of such woman. Here in the case in hand what the accused utters the words to the victim is whether she can make friendship with him? In fact the victim and the accused had friendship for the period of 2­3 months prior to the date of the incident, and the teenagers are exposed to more sex related issues and lot of material is also available to them. Because of their impressionable age, girls and boys both may tend to get provoked and there can be a curious and very compelling demand of the body to get into such kind of relationship. The victim has stated that though she was having friendship with the accused for 2­3 months prior to the incident but the accused did not misbehave with her at any time. Moreover, because of previous acquaintance the accused might have freely asked to the victim whether she can made friendship with him which does not attract Section 509 of I.P.C. or Section 12 of the 10 Spl. Spl.Case 66/2014 [Judgment] Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 as Sec. 11 of the said Act gives the definition of 'Sexual harassment' which is one and the same and as requirement of the ingredients of the offence punishable under Sec. 509 of I.P.C. Such utterance by the accused do not attract either the offence punishable under Sec.509 of I.P.C. or Sec. 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Hence, I answer the point Nos. 3 & 4, in the negative. 23. Resultantly, the accused deserves to be acquitted, and as such, I proceed to pass the following order : ORDER i) Accused Haresh Dhanaji Mhatre is hereby acquitted vide Section 235(1) of Cr.P.C. of the offences punishable under Sections 354, 509 of I.P.C. & Section 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. ii) His bail bonds stand cancelled. iii) No muddemal i.e. cell phone has been produced before the Court. If any seized, it shall be returned to the accused after the period of appeal is over. iv) The accused shall execute his P.R. of Rs.15,000/­ to appear before the Higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect of appeal filed against this judgment as per S. 437­A of Cr.P.C. v) Such bail shall remain in force for six months from today. Kalyan. [M.J.Mirza] Dt.:­20/7/2016. Special Judge, Under Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, Kalyan.
