No. I­53/2016 registered with Badlapur Police Station punishable under secs. 354, 341, 323, 504, 506 r/w 34 of IPC alongwith sec. 8 of POCSO Act. 2] It reveals from the allegations of the FIR that, applicant Sayali, Aboli, Vidya Bhagwat, Aruna and victim girl Bhagyashree are college going friend circle group of the same college. Some rumour was whispered regarding the pregnancy of Sayali in that friend circle on which Sayali questioned Bhagyashree as to why she has spread up such false rumour of pregnancy in the college campous. There was hot talk on that point. It is alleged that, Bhagyashree was beaten by other girls with the help of their common friend Nikhil. Hence this prosecution on the allegation of beating the victim and outraging her modesty at the hands of Nikhil. 3] The applicants came with the case that they are not at fault nor they have any nexus with the alleged crime.The mother of victim exagarated the story as she is from police family. The applicants are being harrashed unnecessarily in this false prosecution. The Bhagyashree has taken disadvantage doing daughter of police. Except hot talk nothing was happened. Hence prayed for protection from unwanted arrest. 4] The application is opposed on the ground that the role attributed by each of the members of said group is specifically reflected in the FIR. After marriage accused no.2 started to reside at her matrimonial house at Ulhasnagar where the victim has lived there. The accused No.1 is father­in­law of Bhavika. Husband of accused no.2 Tushar Rao had got a job ...3/­ 3 Atro. Spl. Case No. 33/2017 [Judg.] at Dubai and he went there. The accused No.1 was keeping ill eye on the victim. On 26/11/2015 when the victim was alone in the kitchen at about 12.00 noon, the accused No.1 arrived there. He had hug and kissed her cheek and pressed her breasts. Its contents were read over and explained to the accused in their vernacular and accused pleaded not guilty ...4/­ 4 Atro. Spl. Case No. 33/2017 [Judg.] and claimed to be tried. Whether prosecution prove that, the accused No.1 from 26/11/2015 at 2.00 p.m. to 5/12/2015 at Khadakpada, Kalyan (West) within the Not proved. jurisdiction of Khadakpada police station, in furtherance of their common intention, used criminal force to complainant Miss. Jyoti Chunmul Vishwakarma, aged about 17 years, intending to outrage her modesty caught hold her, hug her, pressed her breasts and took kiss and the accused No.2 exploited to accused No.1 and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 354 read with 34 of the Indian Penal Code ? ...5/­ 5 Atro. Spl. Case No. 33/2017 [Judg.] 2. Whether prosecution prove that, the accused No.1 on the aforesaid date, time Not proved. and place, in furtherance of their common intention, committed sexual assault with complainant Miss Jyoti, by touching her with sexual intent and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 8 of the Protection of Child from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 ? 3. As there is no incriminating evidence against the accused and the matter was compounded, therefore the prosecution evidence was closed. 8] In consideration of the compromise and close relations of the parties, the PW­1 and PW­2 have not supported the prosecution case. ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN CRI. ANTI. BAIL APPLN. NO. 557/2017 Amol Bombe ...Applicant Vs State of Mah. ( Shahapur P.Stn. ) ...Opponent 1] This is the application under sec. 438 of Cr.P.C. for grant of anticipatory bail in Cr. No. I­174/2017 registered with Shahapur Police Station punishable under sec. 354 of IPC and Section 11 (4) of POCSO Act. 2] It reveals from the allegations of the FIR that, on the day of incidence i.e. on 7.4.2017, when the victim girl was present in college premises more particularly in the canteen area of the college and was talking with her other 3­4 friends, the applicant/accused who is the canteen owner of the said college, abruptly arrived there under influence of liquor and uttered abusive words asking her to let us have a drink and pulled her odni (long scarf) and thereby committed the offence of outrage of modesty. Hence this prosecution. 3] The applicant/accused came with the case that he is the student of Engineering College and studying in Mechanical Branch. The present prosecution is offshut product of canteen business rivalry of applicant/accused and the father of the victim. The victim's father was annoyed against the accused who got canteen contract against the victim's father. Since then he developed grudge against the 2 accused. Moreover, the father of the victim is having criminal antecedents and thus he tried to misuse the provisions of special statute to implicate the applicant/accused falsely. Infact, the applicant/accused now lost that contract due to said prosecution. His examination is forthcoming. If the applicant/accused is relieved from the tension of police arrest, he would be in a position to face his engineering examination. Hence prayed for grant of anticipatory bail. 4] The application is strongly opposed on the ground that the role attributed by applicant/accused is specifically mentioned in the FIR. Moreover, the applicant/accused is reluctant to disclose the names of his other co­accused associates. His cutodial interrogation is necessary to investigate the matter properly. Moreover, the victim­girl is apprehending threat being student appearing for examination. Hence prayed for rejection. 5] Heard both the sides and gone through the investigation papers and the documents produced on record. It reveals from the examination admission cards produced on record that the victim as well as applicant/accused are students taking education in different Institutions. It is true, no false prosecution would be launched at the stake of the character of young daughter. However, it cannot be accepted as universal truth. In some cases wise men who are well aware about the stringent provisions of Law may misuse the Law to make the accused scapegoat of their individual 3 grudge. In the present case, it reveals that the father of the victim was seriously annoyed against the applicant/accused who obtained canteen contract against his wish. Therefore, possibility of false implication cannot be decided definitely. Thus, considering the forthcoming exam. period, I am inclined to grant him anticipatory bail to relieve him from tension of arrest. It is pertinent to note the annual examination of the victim is now over and thus the apprehension of repetition of teasing on her way is remote. With this conclusion, I am inclined to grant pre­arrest bail on following conditions. : ORDER : 1] The application for grant of anticipatory bail is allowed as follows :­ a] In the event of arrest applicant/accused be released on bail on furnishing P.B. & S.B. of Rs.15,000/­. b] He is directed to co­operate with investigation agency and attend Shahapur P.Stn. on every Sunday between 11.00 a.m. to 2.00 p.m. till the end of June,2017. c] He should refrain from entering into judicial area of the victim till her evidence is over. 2] Inform Concern P.Stn. accordingly. Kalyan [ S.P. Gogarkar ] Dt : 12/05/2017 Dist. Judge­4 & Addl. Sessions Judge, Kalyan

1 ABA No. 570/2017 (Exh.1) ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN CRI. ANTI. BAIL APPLN. NO. 570/2017 1] Read application and say of the prosecution. Perused documents. Heard both the learned advocates at length. 2] This is anticipatory bail application under section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 3] Crime bearing No.I­3/2017 is registered against this accused and other accused persons for the offence punishable under secs. 323, 324 of IPC in Ambernath police station. As this accused apprehend his arrest by Ambernath police station he has filed this application for anticipatory bail. 4] Allegation against this accused that, on 2/1/2017 on account of previous quarrel again quarrel took place between brother of complainant namely Kunal and brother of this accused namely Sanju. Exchange of words took place. This accused and other accused persons who are brothers of main accused Sanju came there. They beat Kunal. Sanju beat Kunal by an iron pipe and this accused beat Kunal by hockey stick. When complainant tried to intervene accused Sanju pressed her breasts and outraged her modesty. Not only this but accused Sanju also abused complainant and her family members naming their caste in order to humiliate them in the 2 ABA No. 570/2017 (Exh.1) society. And therefore complainant Shivaji lodged complaint against this accused and other accused persons. 5] In this application it is the say of this accused that he has committed no offence. There is long standing strained relations between this accused and his family on one side and the complainant and her family on other side. On account of pipe line in front of their respective house the quarrel took place. House of accused as well as house of complainant are in front of each other. It is further say of this accused that on the day of incident complainant Shivani her brothers, her father and other family members beat accused Sanju and others by dangerous weapons and caused injuries. For that Sanju has lodged complaint against the complainant and other family members in the police station and that complaint is prior to the complaint of this complainant. Only in order to give go­bye to that complaint this false complaint is filed by the complainant. This accused has committed no offence. No overt act is given to this accused in the alleged complaint. Other accused persons are already released on bail by this court. This accused is permanent resident of Dubai Colony, Ambernath (West). He is ready to abide by any condition. He will not abscond. It is further say of this accused that, he is the only bread earner in his family. If this accused sent behind bar then he will loose his job and respect in society. He is doing service and he is reputed in the society. He prayed that he be released on anticipatory bail. 3 ABA No. 570/2017 (Exh.1) 6] This application is strongly opposed by prosecution. It is the say of prosecution that offence is of serious nature. If this accused released on bail, then there is possibility of another incident of similar nature. Because complainant and accused persons reside in front of each other. Investigation is incomplete. Custody of this accused is necessary. And therefore prosecution prayed that application be rejected. 7] After going through the complaint it is revealed to me that neither there is allegation against this accused that he committed any offence under POCSO Act nor he committed any offence under S.C. & S.T. Act. And therefore section 18 of the S.C. & S.T. Act does not come in picture at all. Admittedly long standing enmity is there between these two families. In these facts and circumstances I am of the considered view that this accused is definitely entitled to be enlarged on anticipatory bail. Hence I pass the following order :­ ORDER 1. AVP Atro.Spl.Case 54/16 .5/­ 5 Atro.Spl.Case No.54/2016 Judgment. 6] Prosecution was directed to adduce its evidence in support of its case. In response to that prosecution examined in all 12 witnesses in this case. P.W.1­ Smt.Mukta Pardhi (Exh.24) is the complainant. P.W.2­ Renuka Ramesh Pardhi (Exh.26) is the victim girl. (Exh.35) is the police constable who recorded complaint of complainant Mumta. She proved the complaint which is at Exh.36. P.W.5­ Smt.Gauri Virag Phatak (Exh.41) is social worker. She is one of the person before whom the victim girl narrated the entire incident and specifically stated that she conceived from accused Ganpat Hilam. P.W.7­ Dr.Anagha Sanjay Patil (Exh.46) is the medical practitioner who runs Sfurti Hospital at village Wangani. Complainant Mukta had taken the victim girl first time for medical examination to this Dr.Anangha Patil. This Dr.Anagha for first time declared the victim girl as pregnant. She deposed that on 12/1/2016 victim girl was brought to her by her mother AVP Atro.Spl.Case 54/16 .6/­ 6 Atro.Spl.Case No.54/2016 Judgment. i.e. complainant P.W.1 Mukta Pardhi. On her clinical examination she found that victim girl was pregnant of 4 months. She advised the mother of victim girl to go to Central Hospital, Ulhasnagar. Her mother refused to go there. Thereafter, she sent the victim girl to Mukta Balika Parivartan Kendra, Titwala. P.W.8­ Trupti Rajkumar Ambade (Exh.47) is the social worker who was attached to District Child Protection Unit, Thane in between 2013 to 2016. On 16/1/2016 her office received phone call from Jyoti Patkar from Mukta Balika Parivartan Kendra, Titwala. In her presence victim girl narrated the incident and told them that one Ganpat Hilam kept forcible relations with victim girl. She further deposed that at that time victim girl was 15 to 16 years old and she was pregnant. She further deposed that her mother told that she is going to lodge the complaint. Therefore, she also accompanied her mother to the police station and lodged the complaint. P.W.9­ Amit Mohan Dubla (Exh.51) is a carrier of samples to F.S.L. Mumbai. He deposed accordingly and proved the letters at Exh.52 & 53. He also deposed that on 22/1/2016 he carried sealed envelope having blood samples for D.N.A. from Kulgaon Police Station to F.S.L. Kalina, Mumbai with forwarding letter at Exh.53. P.W.10­ Dr. Tejaswini Gautam Gosavi (Exh. 54) is the radiologist. She deposed that on 29/1/2016 victim girl was AVP Atro.Spl.Case 54/16 .7/­ 7 Atro.Spl.Case No.54/2016 Judgment. brought to her for sonography. She conducted sonography. At that time age of victim girl was 17 years. She further stated that on her examination she found that victim girl was pregnant of 23 weeks and 6 days. Accordingly she submitted report. That report is at Exh.57. She proved it. P.W.11­ P.S.I. Laxman Tanku Bhoi (Exh.58) is the investigating officer. He narrated entire investigation in detail. He proved the complaint at Exh.36. He stated that at the time of complaint complainant had stated age of her girl as 16 years. On 17/01/2016 he arrested the accused. On 29/01/2016 he prepared spot panchanama. On 18/01/2016 he seized the clothes of accused. On 29/01/2016 he seized the clothes of victim girl. He sent all the clothes to F.S.L. Kalina, Mumbai vide letter at Exh.59. He got examined victim girl as well as accused. He obtained bonafide certificate of the victim girl from her school and thereafter he submitted chargesheet in the court. P.W.12 Dr.Archana Akhade, the medical officer of Central Hospital, Ulhasnagar is the doctor who examined the victim girl on 28/1/2016 clinically. On carrying ultrasound examination of the victim girl she found that victim girl was pregnant of 23 weeks and 6 days. She accordingly issued medico­legal examination report which is at Exh.63. 7] In this case accused admitted some documents. Amongst those documents panchanama of seizure of clothes of accused is at Exh.27, spot panchanama is at Exh.28, panchanama AVP Atro.Spl.Case 54/16 .8/­ 8 Atro.Spl.Case No.54/2016 Judgment. of seizure of clothes of victim girl is at Exh.29 8] Statement of the accused is recorded U/Sec.313 of Cr.P.C. All incriminating facts, circumstances and evidence were put to him and sought his explanation. From the answers given by accused during statement U/Sec.313 of Cr.P.C. it reveals that his defence is of total denial. The another defence of this accused seems that victim girl had married with one Rupesh. She conceived from Rupesh. He is not acquainted with complainant or the victim girl. She is major one on the date of alleged incident. He has not adducted any defence evidence. 9] I have gone through the oral as well as documentary evidence on record carefully. I have heard learned A.P.P. Shri.Bhangare for State and learned advocate Shri.Deshmukh at length. 10] Following points arise for my consideration. My findings on those points are as follows for the reasons stated below : Sr. Points Findings No 1. Does prosecution prove that on 16/1/2016 victim girl was minor In the affirmative. below age of 18 years? 2. Does prosecution further prove that on the 16/1/2016 at Kasgaon, Tal. Ambernath, Dist. Thane, in the forest AVP Atro.Spl.Case 54/16 .9/­ 9 Atro.Spl.Case No.54/2016 Judgment. area the accused committed rape on minor victim girl aged 16 years and thereby he has committed an offence In the affirmative. punishable U/Sec.376 of I.P.C. ? 3 Does prosecution further prove that on the abovesaid date, time and place the accused committed criminal intimidation by threatening minor victim girl aged 16 years with dire consequences with intent to cause alarm to her and that thereby he committed an offence punishable U/ Sec.506 of I.P.C. ? In the negative. 4 Does prosecution further prove that on the abovesaid date, time and place the accused committed penetrative sexual assault on the minor victim girl aged 16 years and thereby he has committed an offence punishable U/Sec.4 of the P.O.C.S.O. Act, 2012 ? In the affirmative. 5 Does prosecution further prove that on the abovesaid date, time and place the accused committed aggravated penetrative sexual assault, repeatedly on minor victim girl aged 16 years and thereby he has committed an offence U/Sec.6 of the P.O.C.S.O.Act, 2012 ? In the affirmative. : REASONS : 11] Except complainant Mukta and her daughter the victim girl all other prosecution witnesses fully supported the case of prosecution. P.W.1 Mukta and P.W Renuka do not support the AVP Atro.Spl.Case 54/16 .10/­ 10 Atro.Spl.Case No.54/2016 Judgment. prosecution. Prosecution declared them hostile and alleged that they are won by the accused. AS TO POINT NO.1 : 12] It is the case of prosecution that when pregnancy of victim girl was detected she was minor below the age of 18 years. Per contra, it is the contention of accused that she was major. To prove the contention of accused, accused adduced no evidence rather defence evidence. 13] To prove the age of victim girl on the date of incident prosecution mainly examined P.W.6 Sayli Sudhir Naik. She is teacher of Zillha Parishad School in which victim girl was taking education during the year 2011­2012. She deposed that in 2011­ 2012 victim girl was taking education in 7th standard. She further deposed that as per school record date of birth of the victim girl is 10th June 1999. She proved the bonafide certificate issued by school at Exh.44. Same date of birth of the victim girl is mentioned in that certificate. 14] P.W.8 Trupti Ambade deposed that on16/1/2016 she had interaction with victim girl at Mukta Bal Parivartan Kendra, Titwala. At that time victim girl told her age as 15 to 16 years. Most important evidence is of Dr.Tejaswini Gosavi, P.W.10. She is a radiologist. She carried sonography of the victim girl. She also stated that when she examined the victim girl, the victim girl was AVP Atro.Spl.Case 54/16 .11/­ 11 Atro.Spl.Case No.54/2016 Judgment. 17 years old and was pregnant of 23 weeks and 6 days. P.W.11 P.S.I. Laxman Bhoi, the investigating officer also stated that during his investigation he transpired that age of the victim girl is 16 years. P.W.12 Dr.Archana Akhade, the medical officer of Central Hospital, Ulhasnagar is the doctor who examined the victim girl on 28/1/2016. To this doctor victim girl told her date of birth as 10/6/1999. She deposed accordingly. Thus, evidence of P.W.12 Dr.Archana Akhade, P.W.6 Sayli Naik, the bonafide certificate at Exh.44, evidence of radiologist Dr.Tejaswini Gosavi, P.W.10 fully corroborates each other on the point of age of the victim girl, when she was first examined by Dr. Anagha Patil, P.W.7. Here it is pertinent to note that though the complainant denied the contents in the complaint, those contents are duly proved by P.W.4 Sunita Vaidya, L.P.C. Buckle No.1335 who recorded complaint of complainant on 13/1/2016. In the complaint victim girl is shown as minor. P.W.3 Shailaja Bhoir, L.P.C. Buckle No. 1410so deposed that on 16/1/2016 complainant had been to police station along with victim girl and at that time she told that victim girl is of 16 years and carrying pregnancy of 4 months. 15] Thus, it is crystal clear that the medical practitioner, the radiologist, the police officers as well as social workers who had talks to victim girl for one or other reason stated in an unambiguous words before this court that victim girl was then minor. These witnesses are cross­examined by the Ld.Advocate AVP Atro.Spl.Case 54/16 .12/­ 12 Atro.Spl.Case No.54/2016 Judgment. for accused. But nothing brought to discredit their evidence on the point of age of the victim girl on the date of incident or when her pregnancy was first detected. Thus, the cumulative effect of all this evidence on record is that the prosecution succeeded to prove the fact that on the date of incident or on the date of first intercourse of the victim girl she was minor below the age of 18 years. I have no hesitation to answer point No.1 in the affirmative. AS TO POINT NO.3 : 16] It is the contention of prosecution that accused committed offence of criminal intimidation by giving threats to victim girl saying that if she discloses of him keeping physical relations with her to anybody, then he will kill her. Thus by giving threats to kill the victim girl accused had committed criminal intimidation, the offence punishable U/Sec.506 of I.P.C. However, these are the mere allegations. To prove these allegations absolutely there is no evidence on record. In this respect P.W.2­ the victim girl Renuka is the most important witness. She has not uttered a single word against the accused especially regarding his giving threat to her. Therefore, for want of evidence I answer this point in negative. AS TO POINT NOS.2,4 & 5 : 17] In order to avoid repetition of discussion, I would like to consider all these points together. AVP Atro.Spl.Case 54/16 .13/­ 13 Atro.Spl.Case No.54/2016 Judgment. 18] Charge against this accused is framed U/Sec.376 of I.P.C. as well as U/Secs.4 & 6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offence Act, 2012. (henceforth referred to as POCSO Act). Before going to discuss the evidence on record, I would like to refer here one important provision in the P.O.C.S.O. Act i.e. Sec.29 of P.O.C.S.O Act which runs as :“Where a person is prosecuted for committing or abetting or attempting to commit any offence under Section 3,5,7 and 9 of the Act, the Special Court shall presume that such person has committed or abetted or attempted to commit the offence, as the case may be, unless the contrary is proved." 19] Thus, it is crystal clear from this section that in a case for the offence U/Secs.3,5,7 punishable U/Secs. 4,6 & 8 respectively the Special Court shall presume that the person has committed the offence , unless the contrary is proved. There is legal presumption against this accused that he has committed the offence as alleged by the prosecution unless he rebutted said presumption. Keeping in mind this important section as well as the presumption enunciated in this section, I proceed to discuss the evidence on record. 20] At the very outset, I would like to state that pregnancy of victim girl prior to 16/1/2016 is not at all specifically challenged or denied by the accused. No doubt, one or two stray AVP Atro.Spl.Case 54/16 .14/­ 14 Atro.Spl.Case No.54/2016 Judgment. suggestions were given to the medical officers or doctors that victim was not pregnant. But this can not be treated as serious challenge to the pregnancy of victim girl on 16/1/2016 or prior to that. Apart from this there is ample evidence on record. Medical evidence on record of the witness from medical field, from social workers from police persons is sufficient to prove the fact that on 16/1/2016 the victim girl was pregnant. In this respect the most important evidence is of Dr.Tejaswini Gosavi, P.W.10. She is a readiologist in Government hospital. She examined the victim girl on 29/1/2016 by conducting sonography of victim girl for the purpose of pregnancy. She further deposed on oath that she found victim girl was pregnant on that day of 23 weeks and 6 days. No reason to disbelieve or discard this evidence of P.W.10 Dr.Tejaswini Gosawi on the point of pregnancy of victim girl. She has been cross­examined at length, but nothing is brought on record through her cross­examination to disbelieve her or to discard her. 21] Not only the evidence of expert Dr.Tejaswini Gosavi, P.W.10 is on record regarding pregnancy of the victim girl, but other medical officers and medical practitioners Dr.Archana Akhade, P.W.12 and Dr.Anasha Patil, P.W.7 deposed that when the victim girl was brought to them in the month of January, 2016. On their examination they found victim girl was pregnant. Thus, pregnancy of the victim girl is duly established and proved. AVP Atro.Spl.Case 54/16 .15/­ 15 Atro.Spl.Case No.54/2016 Judgment. 22] Now, the only question before me that who is the biological father of the child of the victim girl. 23] As per the contention of prosecution victim girl conceived from accused as he has committed rape on her for 4­5 times by taking her to the jungle prior to the complaint. Per contra, it is the contention of the accused that victim girl is married with one Rupesh, she conceived from her husband. Even though the complainant Mukta and victim girl both turned hostile irrespective of their statements before police, there is ample evidence on record to show that victim girl got conceived from this accused and accused committed rape on her. In this case P.W.3 Shailaja Bhoir, L.P.C. stated that on 16/1/2016 complainant Mukta had been to the police station Kulgaon alongwith social workers Smt.Doiphode, Smt.Phatak, Smt.Shinde etc. She further deposed that Mukta met A.P.I. Shri.Pore and told him that her daughter is carrying pregnancy of 4 months from Ganpat Ika Hilam i.e. the accused. Not only this but she further stated that she alongwith one P.C.Phadtare went to Mukta Balikashram, Titwala. In her presence statement of the victim girl was recorded. At that time mother of victim girl was also present. In her presence victim girl stated that accused committed rape on her and due to that she conceived. Similarly P.W.4 Sunita Vidya, L.P.C. who recorded the F.I.R. stated that informant Mukta disclosed her that her victim daughter of 16 years age is carrying pregnancy. Accordingly she recorded the complaint. P.W.5­ AVP Atro.Spl.Case 54/16 .16/­ 16 Atro.Spl.Case No.54/2016 Judgment. Gauri Phatak, the social worker also stated in her deposition that she talked with the victim girl and victim girl disclosed her about her pregnancy, about her sexual intercourse with accused for 4­5 times. P.W.8 Trupti Ambade, the social worker then working with District Child Protection Unit, Thane also deposed that she talked with the victim girl personally. Victim girl stated to her that Ganpat Ika Hilam had kept forcible sexual relations with her against her will and from that she conceived. P.W.12 Dr.Archana Akhade stated that at the time of examination of the victim girl, victim girl stated her history of physical relationship with known person 3­4 times before 5 to 6 months against her will. All these witnesses are cross­examined by the Ld.Advocate for accused. However, except the suggestions of denial which are denied by the witnesses there is nothing in their cross­examination to discredit or disbelieve these witnesses. Sum and substance of the evidence of all the witnesses referred above is that in their presence and to them personally victim girl herself disclosed the fact of keeping sexual relations by accused with her for 3 to 4 times against her will. 24] It is pertinent to note that there is no enmity between these witnesses and accused person. Even these witnesses might not have known personally who is the accused. There is no reason for these witnesses to depose either against the accused or against the victim girl. Then why these witnesses should depose false ? No explanation is put forth in this respect on behalf of the accused AVP Atro.Spl.Case 54/16 .17/­ 17 Atro.Spl.Case No.54/2016 Judgment. person. Even there is no suggestions in their cross­examination that for this particular reason the witness or the witnesses are deposing false. Thus, absolutely there is no reason to disbelieve or discredit the evidence of these witnesses to whom the victim girl personally disclosed the fact that accused committed rape on her and from accused she got conceived. I accept the evidence of all above stated witnesses as it is genuine and true. 25] There is one more circumstance on record which supports the evidence of the above stated witnesses as well as the contention of prosecution i.e. most important scientific evidence of the D.N.A. test. It is deposed by P.W.11 Laxman Bhoi the investigating officer that he caused the blood samples of the accused, victim girl and her child to be taken for D.N.A. test purpose by calling D.N.A. kit from Kalina, Mumbai . He further deposed that he sent those samples for D.N.A. test to Kalina, Mumbai. This fact is also deposed by P.W.9 Amit Dubla. This fact is further strengthened by the chemical analysis report at Exh.15,19,21,22,23. As per examination report at Exh.21, the blood sample of accused Ganpat was sent to the F.S.L. , Kalina, Mumbai for examination. While giving results of this analysis it is specifically mentioned that "For DNA profiling results refer F.S.L.M.L.Case No.DNA­2284/16". Similarly chemical analysis report at Exh.23 proved the fact that blood sample of Renuka the victim girl was sent for DNA test. In this examination report while giving the results of analysis it is specifically mentioned that "For AVP Atro.Spl.Case 54/16 .18/­ 18 Atro.Spl.Case No.54/2016 Judgment. DNA profiling results refer F.S.L.M.L.Case No.DNA­2284/16". As per chemical analysis report Exh.22 the blood sample of baby of Renuka was sent for DNA. This is proved. DNA analysis report is mentioned in the examination report at Exh.22. The report of DNA test says that "Ganpat Ika Hilam and Renuka Ramesh Pardhi are concluded to be the biological parents of baby of Renuka Ramesh Pardhi." Thus, it is crystal clear from the DNA report which is given after scientific examination of the blood samples of the accused, victim girl and her baby. This in unambiguous words states that the present accused is the father of the baby of victim girl. This concludes that this accused had intercourse with the victim girl and due to those intercourses victim girl conceived. It is proved that at the time of conception victim girl was minor and therefore even though for the sake of argument we accept that it was consensual intercourse, in the eyes of law this is a rape. Thus the scientific result of DNA test fully supports the case of prosecution and the same is duly corroborated by the witnesses i.e. police officers, social workers before whom the victim girl admitted that she was raped by accused against her will and from that she conceived. 26] It is vehemently argued by learned advocate for accused Shri.Deshmukh that absolutely there is no evidence on record to show that blood sample of accused for DNA test was taken and therefore DNA test report can not be held as the conclusive evidence of the paternity of the accused in respect of AVP Atro.Spl.Case 54/16 .19/­ 19 Atro.Spl.Case No.54/2016 Judgment. the baby of victim girl. By any stretch of imagination this argument is not appellable to the judicial mind. There is ample evidence on record to show that blood of this accused was sent to F.S.L. Kalina, Mumbai for DNA test. In this respect P.W.11 Laxman Bhoi, the investigating officer deposed. P.W.9 Amit Dubla deposed that he carried blood samples to Kalina. Above all there are chemical analysis reports on record which shows that blood sample of accused Ganpat, victim girl Renuka and her baby were sent for chemical analysis and DNA test and those were analyzed. After scientific analysis of blood sample for the purpose of DNA laboratory has issued report. There is no reason to doubt the report. Apart from all this there is no single suggestion to any prosecution witness on behalf of the accused that blood sample of the accused was never collected for the purpose of chemical analysis or for the purpose of DNA test. In absence of such specific suggestion regarding denial these arguments are not acceptable one. 27] It is tried to raise the defence that victim girl had married with one Rupesh and conceived from him. The baby born to victim girl is of Rupesh contended by the learned advocate for accused. However, to prove this even prima facie, absolutely no evidence is on record. No defence evidence is adduced by the accused to prove this fact or his defence. 28] As I have stated at the beginning of this judgment that AVP Atro.Spl.Case 54/16 .20/­ 20 Atro.Spl.Case No.54/2016 Judgment. there is presumption that accused has committed rape on the victim girl as per Sec.29 of POCSO Act. Accused has to rebut the said presumption. In this case to rebut the presumption absolutely no evidence is adduced on record by the accused. The presumption raised by the DNA test report is not at all rebutted. The evidence of social workers and the police personnels is also not rebutted at all. Thus to rebut the prosecution evidence and to rebut the legal presumption U/Sec.29 of POCSO Act, there is no iota of evidence on behalf of or in support of the accused. Thus, the presumption U/Sec.29 of POCSO Act stands not rebutted at all. On the contrary, the said presumption is strengthened and converted into the conclusiveness by the prosecution evidence adduced through the witnesses and through the scientific evidence of DNA test report. It is true that complainant Mukta and victim girl both turned hostile. They have not supported the prosecution on any count. However, if we consider the entire prosecution evidence in toto then it appears that both P.W.1 Mukta and P.W.2 Renuka are won over by the accused. May be some assurances, some promises might have been given on behalf of accused to the mother and daughter. Even there may be assurances or promises by and on behalf of accused to marry with the victim girl. What ever may be the reason, but the fact is that both these witnesses are won over by the accused. However, even though we ignore the evidence of P.W.1 Mukta and P.W.2 Renuka, then also there is ample evidence on record to hold accused guilty for the offence punishable U/Sec.376 of I.P.C. and U/Secs. 4 & 6 of POCSO Act. AVP Atro.Spl.Case 54/16 .21/­ 21 Atro.Spl.Case No.54/2016 Judgment. Merely because the complainant and victim girl turned hostile , otherwise reliable, acceptable and corroborative evidence of prosecution can not be thrown away at all. 29] Thus, after giving thorough consideration to the prosecution evidence on record, after considering the defence raised by the accused, I hold the accused person guilty for the offence punishable U/Sec. 376 of I.P.C. and U/Sec.4 & 6 of POCSO Act. 30] Here I take pause to hear the accused, his advocate and Ld.A.P.P. for prosecution on the point of sentence. Kalyan. (D.S. Hatarote ) 07/02/2018. Addl. Sessions Judge, Kalyan. 31] At this stage I have recorded further statement of accused U/Sec. 313 of Cr.P.C. on the point of sentence. He submitted that he has committed no offence. He is ready to marry with victim girl. He is ready to give his name to the son of victim girl. He prayed that leniency be shown to him. 32] Ld.A.P.P. urged for maximum punishment as the offence is of serious nature. He further stated that offence is against the minor girl and the accused is married and therefore he is not entitled for leniency. AVP Atro.Spl.Case 54/16 .22/­ 22 Atro.Spl.Case No.54/2016 Judgment. 33] Ld.Adv. Shri.Deshmukh for accused submitted that offence is proved only on medical evidence. In fact this statement is made without going through the judgment. Because there is other evidence than the medical evidence on record. He further submitted that complainant and victim girl have not supported the prosecution. Accused is ready to marry with the victim girl. For all these reasons he prayed leniency. 34] Considering the nature of offence, considering the submissions of both sides, in my view following sentence will meet the ends of justice. :ORDER: 1) Accused Ganpat Ika Hilam is hereby convicted for the offence punishable U/Sec.376 of I.P.C. and U/Secs.4 & 6 of POCSO Act and he is sentenced to suffer Rigorous Imprisonment for 10 years and to pay fine of Rs.5,000/­ (Rs.Five Thousand only) i.d. to suffer further Rigorous Imprisonment for one year. 2) Accused is hereby acquitted of the offence punishable U/Sec.506 of I.P.C. 3) The muddemal property being worthless be destroyed after the period of appeal is over. 4) Accused is in jail. He is entitled to get set off U/Sec.428 of Cr.P.C. in respect of his period in jail during trial. 5) It is hereby informed to the accused that he has right to prefer an appeal against this judgment and conviction order before Hon'ble High Court, Mumbai . AVP Atro.Spl.Case 54/16 .23/­ 23 Atro.Spl.Case No.54/2016 Judgment. 6) Copy of this judgment be supplied free of cost to the accused as soon as it is typed and ready. 7) This judgment is declared and dictated to stenographer in the open court. It will take time to transcript the same and provide the copy to accused. Therefore, the Jail Authorities be informed to produce the accused before this court on 14/02/2018 without fail, for receiving copy of this judgment free of costs. Kalyan. (D.S. Hatarote ) 07/02/2018. Addl. Sessions Judge, Kalyan.za AVP Atro.Spl.Case 54/16 ./­

Received on : 23­06­2014. Registered on: 23­06­2014 Decided on : 22­02­2017. Duration: 02 Y 07 M 30 D IN THE COURT OF THE ADDL. SESSIONS JUDGE ­2 AT KALYAN (Presided over by D.S. Hatarote) Atro. Special Case No. 76/2014 Exh.No.__ The state of Maharashtra Through Shahapur Police Station, .. Prosecution VERSUS Bharat Hari Bhoir, Age – 45 years, R/at : At Post­ Taharpur, Tal – Shahapur, Dist – Thane. .. Accused Offence : U/Sec. 354 of the Indian Penal Code and under section 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Appearances: ====================== Smt. Bhoir, A.P.P. for State Shri. Humane, Advocate for the accused ====================== (2) J U D G M E N T. ( Delivered in open court on 22nd February, 2017 ) 1. This accused is facing trial for the offence punishable under section 354 of the Indian Penal Code and for section 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, initiated against him by the State through Shahapur police station. Prosecution story in brief is as follows: 2. Complainant was residing at Taharpur, Taluka­ Shahapur with her parents, brother and sisters. At the time of incident she was working on the construction of accused as her father was ill. On 06/02/2014 at about 10.00 a.m. she went to the house of accused for work. On that day accused provided her lunch. Then she went to house. She returned to work at 3.30 p.m. At that time accused asked prosecutrix to bring water from his old house. She went there. Accused followed her. After bringing water accused asked prosecutrix to prepare tea. Prosecutrix was unable to light the gas stove. She stated this fact to accused. At that time accused came to her, caught hold her hand and put his hand on the breast of prosecutrix and started fondling. Prosecutrix became frightened and she ran away. She informed this incident to her father, mother and uncle Gurunath Sawar. On next day she came to police station Shahapur and lodged complaint. On her complaint crime was (3) Spl. Case No. 76/2014 (J) registered as C.R. No.46/2014. 3. One police Hawaldar Ram Banduji Kove carried investigation in said crime. He prepared spot panchanama. He recorded statements of the witnesses. He arrested the accused. Thereafter he submitted chargesheet in the court. 4. Charge against the accused is framed at Exh.2. Charge was read over and explained to accused in Marathi language. Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. His defence is of total denial. 5. Prosecution was directed to adduce its evidence. Prosecution examined in all two witnesses in this case. One is P.W. No.1 Monika Savar the prosecutrix and another is P.W. No.2 Ram Kove the I.O. Accused admitted the spot of offence panchanama. 6. Statement of accused under section 313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure was recorded. From the replies given by this accused his defence seems to be of total denial. No defence evidence is adduced by the accused. 7. I have gone through the prosecution evidence on record. I have heard both learned advocates. Following points arise for my consideration. My findings on those points are as (4) follows for the reasons stated below. POINTS FINDINGS 1) Does prosecution prove that on 06/02/2014 at about 15.30 hours at Taharpur, Taluka­Shahapur, Dist­ Thane in his house accused committed sexual assault on complainant Monika Savar aged 15 years by holding her hand and by putting his hands on her breast and No. thereby outraged her modesty and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 354 of the I.P.C.? 2) Does prosecution further prove that on the above­said date, time and place accused committed sexual assault on complainant Monika by touching her breast with sexual intent No. which involve physical contact and thereby committed an offence under section 7 punishable under section 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012? REASONS As to Points no. 1 and 2:­ 8. P.W. No.1 prosecutrix though admitted her signature on the complaint, she denied the averments in the complaint in toto. She has not uttered a single incriminating word against (5) Spl. Case No. 76/2014 (J) the accused. The alleged incident in the complaint is denied by the prosecutrix during her cross examination by learned APP. She further admitted in her cross examination that there was dispute between she herself and the accused on account of wages. And therefore, she lodged the complaint. Thus, there is nothing incriminating against the accused in the deposition of P.W. No.1 prosecutrix. 9. P.W. No.2 Ram Kove is the I.O. He narrated about the investigation he carried. In his deposition also there is nothing incriminating. He has not brought on record any incriminating facts or circumstances against the accused which will point the guilt of accused. Thus, absolutely there is no evidence on record to prove any of the guilt of the accused. 10. For want of any sort of incriminating evidence against the accused, I answer both the points in negative. In conclusion, I pass the following order. O R D E R 1) The accused Bharat Hari Bhoir is hereby acquitted of the offence punishable under Section 354 of the Indian Penal Code and under section 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. (6) 2) Bail bonds of accused shall continue for further six months under section 437(A) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Thereafter his bail bonds stands cancelled. 3) He is set at liberty. Kalyan ( D.S. Hatarote ) Date :­ 22/02/2017 Additional Sessions Judge Kalyan.

1 Anti. Bail 473/2016(Exh.1) Anticipatory Bail Application No.473/2016 Order passed below Exh.1. 1. This is an application moved by the applicant/accused Deepak Kundlik Bhoir for his release on anticipatory bail under Section 438 of Code of Criminal Procedure, in non­bailable offences punishable under Section 376(2),(i),(n), 363, 120­B, 109, 506 r/w 34 of I.P.C., Sec. 3(a), 5(a)(g), 6 & 10 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, and Section 3(1)(xi) & (xii) of the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 and amended Sec. 3(2)(v) & 3(2)(va) of Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 2015 in CR.No. I­57/2016 of Khadakpada Police Station. 2. According to him, the victim, aged 13 years lodged the FIR on 16/2/2016 stating therein that she is studying in 9th standard in Sashank Madhyamik Vidyalay, Wadeghar, Kalyan (W) and residing alongwith her mother Asha Prashant Mohod and grandmother Smt. Jaishri, aged 60 years. Her mother is maid­servant. On 15/2/2016 at about 7.30 to 8 p.m. she was waiting for her mother who had gone for maid work. She received a phone call of caller 8898468866 on her mobile phone No.99202386554 who disclosed his name as Sameep and told her to come out of the house and to go to pipeline for roaming and then cut the phone call. To ascertain the unknown mobile number, she came out of the house and noticed two boys standing on the motorcycle. One of them was the cousin brother of her friend Mayuresh Patil namely Sameep Patil and one unknown person. Sameep then made gesture to her to accompany with him but she refused. Then Sameep and his companion caught­hold her both the hands and by putting his hand on her shoulder forcibly made her to sit on the motorcycle and took her in the field near 2 Anti. Bail 473/2016(Exh.1) Shramik Vishram Building towards pipeline where there was brick­kiln and temple of God Shanker. Mayuresh, Prathamesh Bhoir and Vinayak Patil were already standing there. Sameep then forcibly removed her clothes and then removed his own clothes and committed forcible sexual intercourse with her. Nilesh Kale, the friend of Sameep then forcibly committed sexual intercourse with her and then Prathamesh committed sexual intercourse forcibly with her. Then Vinayak Patil committed sexual intercourse with her. Mayuresh was standing and watching the persons on the road. In all three boys committed rape on her one after the other and Mayuresh was watching on the road. 3. The grounds assigned by him are that he is innocent and falsely implicated in this crime. He has no concern with the alleged incident. His name is not mentioned in the FIR nor any role is assigned to him. No weapon is used during the alleged incident. Even in the statements of the witnesses his name is not mentioned. His father was aged about 100 years, who expired on 16/4/2016 at Wadeghar, Kalyan (W) and therefore, he is required to attend his funeral. He is builder by profession and therefore, he has to deal with the transaction of more than lacs of rupees in his day to day business. He used to keep blank signed cheques with his employees. He came to know the cheque bearing No.014117 drawn on Allahabad Bank, Kalyan Branch has been misused by his driver Javed Juma Tadvi by drawing the cheque on the account of the applicant/accused which is the cause for implicating him in this crime with malafide intention. He is respectable reputed person and hence, there is no possibility of his absconding. He is ready to co­operate with the investigation. Lastly, he has prayed to enlarge him on anticipatory bail on such terms and conditions as this Court may deem fit. 3 Anti. Bail 473/2016(Exh.1) 4. The Ld. APP and I.O. resisted the application by filing say at Exh.8 & 6 on the ground that the applicant/accused through his companion Javed Juma Tadvi influenced with money to the victim girl and her mother and got prepared an agreement showing that he has issued cheque worth Rs.2,00,000/­ and cash worth Rs.1,50,000/­ which has been seized during the investigation. The cash Rs.1,50,000/­ was seized from Smt. Manisha Padmakar Patil with whom the amount of Rs.1,50,000/­ was kept as she had received phone call on 16/2/2016 and the caller asked her to call Smt. Asha Mohod at her home and he would come to her house. Within short time two persons arrived at her home and gave Rs.1,50,000/­ to Shobha and went away. Smt. Asha Mohod told her to keep the money safely with her as she has no safe place. Then the police seized the cash Rs.1,50,000/­. The victim belongs to Hindu Mahar caste and all the accused to save themselves from punishment have infused the victim and her mother while recording her statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. she was compelled to give gobye to her version. The applicant/accused has issued the cheque. The agreement was entered in between the victim, her mother and one Javed Juma Tadvi for and on behalf of the accused persons. The original agreement is in the custody of the accused which is required to be seized. The applicant/accused and his companion Javed Tadvi are absconding. One more co­accused Sarvesh Patil is also absconding. However, the present applicant/accused has filed the anticipatory bail. The specimen handwriting of the applicant/accused is required to be taken and cheque book is to be seized for which the physical custody of the applicant/accused is necessary. He will pressurise and tamper with the prosecution witnesses. Because of the pressure of the accused the victim and her mother refused to lodge the FIR regarding the incident of rape 4 Anti. Bail 473/2016(Exh.1) alleged to have been committed by Sarvesh Patil on 21/2/2016 in view of the statement of the victim dated 17/3/2016. In view of Section 18 of the Schedule Caste and Schedule Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 no anticipatory bail application can be granted when the offences under the said Act are alleged to have been committed. Lastly, they have prayed to reject the application. 5. Heard the learned Advocate Shri. V.B.Gaikwad for applicant/ accused and Ld. APP Sou. J.S.Lohokare for the State, at length. 6. I have perused the application, say, copy of the FIR, copy of Adharcard and copy of ration card of the applicant/accused and investigation papers produced by the I.O. 7. The I.O. has produced ruling of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of State of M.P. & anr. Vs. Ram Krishna Balothia & anr. (1995 AIR 1198 = 1995(1) SCR 897 = 1995(3) SCC 221, wherein it is held that S.C. & S.T. (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 was enacted in order to prevent the commission of atrocities against members of Scheduled Caste and Schedule Tribes and to provide for Special Courts for the trial of offence under the Act. It also provides for the relief of rehabilitation of victims of such offences. Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure does not apply to any case involve in arrest of any person accused of having committed any of the offences under Section 18 of the Act. 8. The above ruling is binding on this Court but only condition is that the accused has committed the offence under the Act and showing prima facie case. 5 Anti. Bail 473/2016(Exh.1) 9. It appears that, the copy of the cheque produced by I.O. shows the name and bank account of the applicant/accused including his signature. The alleged agreement dated nil appears to have been executed in between Asha Prashant Mohod and Javed Juma Tadvi etc. 5, wherein C.R.No.I­57/2016 of Khadakpada Police Station is mentioned. The co­ accused are in Adherwadi Jail. To settle the dispute they agreed to pay Rs.6,00,000/­ and out of it cheque worth Rs.2,00,000/­ bearing No.014117 has been given and remaining amount was to be paid after release of the accused on bail and it also speaks that Smt. Asha Mohod promised to withdraw the case by remaining present in the Court. 10. This agreement is against the public policy and also amounts to tampering of the prosecution evidence by showing the influence on the victim as well as the witnesses. The applicant/accused putforth his defence that he is builder by profession and used to keep blank cheques but signed by him with his officials and might have been misused. After perusing the agreement in question there is no signature of the applicant/accused, however, the agreement seems to have been executed by his driver for and on behalf of the accused persons who are in jail but in favour of Asha Mohod. This agreement was executed prior to recording the statement of the victim girl under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. and impact of the said agreement was that she resiled from the version of her FIR. Therefore, prima facie there is tampering of the evidence of the prosecution at the instance of the accused persons through Javed Juma Tadvi who alleged to be the driver of the present applicant/accused. Co­ accused Prathamesh Vijay Bhoir is related to the applicant/accused and hence, the applicant/accused was interested to influence and induce the victim and her mother by paying money. For the purpose of assurance, 6 Anti. Bail 473/2016(Exh.1) the agreement appears to have been entered in between the parties. 11. The recitals in the FIR show that one Sameep Patil and one unknown boy forcibly took the minor victim, made her to sit on their motorcycle and took in a field near Shramik Vishram Building towards pipeline where there was brick kiln and temple of God Shanker. Co­ accused Mayuresh, Prathamesh and Vinayak Patil were already standing there. Then Sameep Patil after removing her clothes forcibly committed rape on the victim and then his friend Nilesh Kale, and then Prathamesh and then Vinayak Patil which amounts to a gang rape on the minor victim. The alleged offences are serious in nature and also anti­social. The victim girl belongs to S.C. or S.T. category and is from poor family as her mother is maid­servant. They are being victimised by the accused persons by inducing them on the strength of money. 12. The allegations against the present applicant/accused is no doubt serious in nature. The cheque book is required to be seized in addition to his specimen signature is to be obtained for which the custodial interrogation is necessary and hence, for the purpose of fair investigation and to book the real culprits by collecting evidence, this application deserves to be rejected, and as such, I proceed to pass the following order:­ ORDER i] The anticipatory bail application No.473/2016 filed by the applicant/accused Deepak Kundlik Bhoir, in C.R.No. I­57/2016 of Khadakpada Police Station is hereby rejected. ii] Inform to the I.O. of Khadakpada Police Station, accordingly. 7 Anti. Bail 473/2016(Exh.1) Date: 2.5.2016. (M.J.Mirza) Kalyan. Special Judge, Under Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, Kalyan.

Complainant alongwith her children including victim girl born from her first husband and also alongwith child born from the accused was residing with accused at his house at Titwala. Thereafter, complainant Poonam went to Bhoiwada Police Station, Mumbai and lodged complaint against one unknown rickshawwala alleging that he committed rape on her minor daughter. In due course the complaint was sent by Bhoiwada Police Station to Kalyan Taluka Police Station for investigation. 3] The concerned police officer of Kalyan Taluka Police Station carried further detail investigation in the matter with the victim girl. Meantime on 21/4/2014 the AVP/­ Atro.Spl.Case.No. No.78/2014 .....4/­ 4 Atro.SPl.Case No.78/2014 Judgment (CNR MHTH060013822014) victim girl was aborted. D.N.A. Sample of the foetus, of accused and the victim girl were taken and sent for D.N.A. Test to Forensic Science Laboratory, Kalina, Mumbai. No. 52/2015 [ Judg. ] below :­ POINTS FINDINGS 1] Does prosecution prove that, on 3/2/2015 at about 11.00 a.m. in the room of his residence in Prakash Kene Chawl, Dombivali (East) committed rape on the No. victim ageing about 3 years who was incapable to give her consent and hence committed offence punishable under section 376(2)(I) (J) of the Indian Penal Code ? 2] Does prosecution prove that, on the above date, place and time accused committed sexual harassment to the victim girl ageing No. about 3 years and thereby committed an offence punishable under section of 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act ? 3] What order ? Accused is acquitted. REASONS 9] The prosecution case is totally relying upon the testimony of the mother of victim child supported by the evidence of her husband and the neighbouring witnesses including chawl owner. The reliance is also placed on the medical evidence on the basis of examination report and C.A. report regarding the victim child. On the other hand it reveals from the defence that, he is implicated falsely in this afterthought concocted story to get rid of cross terms between 6 Spl.C. No. 52/2015 [ Judg. ] the husband of complainant and the accused on point of exposure of his bad dids in committing theft of clothes from Mahavir Dyeing Company. I have to consider evidence on record to see whether accused has committed alleged heinous offence or he is falsely framed as per his defence. 10] POINT NOS.1 AND 2 :­ The prosecution story discloses that the accused Rajesh Jaiswal was alone in his room as his wife and children were sent to his native place in Bihar State for the purpose of the delivery of his wife. The complainant family was residing adjacent to his room. They were on visiting terms to each other. Thus the children from both the families used to visit their houses for playing jointly. 11] It is alleged in the FIR that on 3/2/2015 complainant Ganesh came from his night duty and was taking rest in the house. His wife was taking bath and children were playing in the house. The wife of Ganesh i.e. complainant Jailalita noticed that the small child Chandani was not present in the house. Hence she gave her call and in response she found that Chandani was inside the room of accused. She peeped into the room and found the alleged act being committed by the accused. 12] To substantiate the heinous allegations made against the accused the oral evidence of complainant mother is of vital important. She alleged to have witness said 7 Spl.C. No. 52/2015 [ Judg. ] incidence. The evidence of this important witness can be scrutinized by two folds by examining the statement under section 162 Cr.P.C. and the statement recorded by learned Magistrate under section 164 Cr.P.C.. The contradiction and omissions including improvements brought on record are also liable to be considered to assert the probability of alleged offence. The other evidence including the husband of complainant adduced on record is of hearsay nature to substantiate the story putforth by the complainant mother. 13] The learned counsel Mr. Patkar on behalf of accused submitted that, the story of the prosecution is highly improbable and not acceptable on the basis of exaggerated evidence adduced by the complainant mother. The learned counsel pointed out that the version of complainant (PW 1) Jailalita suffers from material contradiction and omissions. It is pointed out that while lodging report, it is mentioned that the children were playing in the house whereas while deposing before the court she has deposed that she pushed the front door for getting bath and the children were playing outside the house. 14] Apart from this the material variance is brought on record submitting that while deposing before the court the complainant has narrated the alleged act of accused saying that the victim girl was lying under the accused and he slept over on her person on the cot. It is stated that accused was naked as he removed all his clothes and also removed the 8 Spl.C. No. 52/2015 [ Judg. ] nicker of victim girl and was kissing her vaginal part. On the other hand, there is no reference of the existence of said cot in the room of accused. Moreover it is not mentioned neither in the FIR nor in her statement under sec. 164 of Cr.P.C. that the child was made to lie and accused was on her. 15] Another variance is brought on record regarding the use of physical force at the hands of accused when the child tried to rescue from him by crying. It is pertinent to note that, while giving statement before learned Magistrate under sec. 164 Cr.P.C. the complainant went on exaggerating the act of accused saying that she has seen some semen discharge on the leg of the child. This material aspect does not find place either in the FIR or while deposing before the court. Therefore the allegations made in the FIR Exh.15 and the statement given under sec. 164 of Cr.P.C. vide Exh.16 appears to be inconsistent with each other. Moreover the deposition before court gives different story against the accused. 16] The learned counsel for defence attracted my attention towards improbable conduct of the father of the child who was awakened by his wife by narrating the sexual assault alleged to be committed by accused on his minor child. The father (PW 3) Ganesh instead of visiting the neighbouring accused went to the house of chawl owner to seek advice whether to lodge the report against the accused. The evidence adduced by (PW 3) Ganesh and the said chawl 9 Spl.C. No. 52/2015 [ Judg. ] owner (PW 4) Prakash Kene, his son (PW 8) Jayesh Kene and the neighbouring witnesses (PW 6) Manoj Das and (PW 7) Punitkumar Mahanto have narrated the story learnt by them from the mouth of (PW 3) Ganesh who received said information from his wife complainant Jailalita. Thus, the evidence of most of the examined witnesses is of third person's evidence. They have tried to demonstrate that the child ageing about 3­4 years old was unable to state verbally regarding the incidence but she has shown some gestures suggesting the alleged incidence committed by the accused. 17] On this background the child victim is examined before the court. Admittedly she was appearing about 3­4 years old but was unable to utter single word incriminating against the accused. Not only that but she was unable to state her name and other whereabouts and acquaintance with accused of her family. Therefore the examination of child witness is not helpful to the prosecution. On the contrary, it demolished the story prepared in her statement under sec. 164 Cr.P.C.. It reveals from record that the statement of the child was recorded in question­answer form by the learned trial court and she appeared to have given some rational answers regarding the incidence but while deposing before the court she was mum. Moreover her mother Jailalita admitted the fact that the child is unable to pronounce the word as "Chaddi" or "Chumma". 10 Spl.C. No. 52/2015 [ Judg. ] 18] Considering these factual aspects adduced before the court it is too difficult to held that said child might have stated anything incriminating against the accused. It is admitted position that mother Jailalita was present while recording her statement and she might have completed the statement supporting the child. In such situation the exaggerated statement of the mother regarding appearance of semen discharge on the leg of child appears to be inconsistence to the entire story putforth by the prosecution. Moreover the clothes of the victim girl are not seized to assert the presence of semen stains on the clothes. 19] Now question arises why the accused is implicated in this case at the stake of the character of female child of the complainant family. The explanation tried to be given by the accused that there were cross terms between the complainant head Ganesh Chaudhary and the accused Rajesh Jaiswal on point of stealing fabrics from Mahavir Dyeing Company. The explanation given by the accused for his prosecution is not digestable because the stake of small child is involved in this sexual assault case. However prosecution has to raise or fall on its own feet. It cannot take disadvantage of the weakness of the defence and therefore non­acceptable explanation though given by the accused but it was the prime duty of prosecution to prove the guilt of accused beyond all reasonable doubts. 11 Spl.C. No. 52/2015 [ Judg. ] 20] The learned counsel submitted that the use of physical force is stated by the complainant mother but it is not substantiated by medical evidence as no visible injury is seen on her person. Moreover the presence of child in the house of accused could have given grudge in the mind of complainant family which might have been resulted into false prosecution because initial registration of crime was under section 354 of IPC only and then it was converted into sec. 376(2)(I)(J) read with punishable sec. 8 of POCSO Act. 21] Considering all the facts and circumstances of the case and material admissions given by the complainant mother during cross­examination, it is too hard to say that the guilt of the accused is proved with cogent evidence. In such situation he is liable to be given advantage of inadequate evidence. The ingredients of alleged rape and sexual assault are not proved at all. With this conclusion I have no hesitation to answer point nos.1 and 2 in negative. 22] POINT NO. 3 :­ As I held above prosecution failed to prove necessary ingredients to prove the guilt of accused. Hence he is liable to be acquitted giving benefit of inadequate evidence to prove the charges. In the result I answer point no.3 accordingly and proceed to pass following order :­ 12 Spl.C. No. 52/2015 [ Judg. ] ORDER 1] Accused Rajesh Dudhnath Jaiswal, age 29 years R/of Prakash Kene Chawl, Manpada, Dombivali (East), Taluka­Kalyan, District­Thane, is hereby acquitted under section 235(1) of Cr.P.C. of the offence punishable under section 376(2)(I)(J) of the Indian Penal Code and section 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. 2] The accused is in Jail, he be released forthwith if not required in any other case/crime. 3] The accused is directed to furnish fresh P.B. of Rs.15,000/­. In compliance with the provisions of section 437(A) of Cr.P.C. to abide himself to appear before Appellate Court in case of appeal is preferred by the prosecution. 4] Judgment pronounced in open Court. Patil­Bhamare, Ld. APP For Complainant Shri Z.N. Kazi, Ld. Adv. For Accused ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ 2 Spl.Case No. 53/2015 [Judg. ] JUDGMENT ( Delivered on this 2nd day of August, 2016 ) 1] Accused Dhanpat Kushwah who took shelter at the house of victim at the mercy of her father has committed rape on her and also caused sexual assault repeatedly to the said minor girl. Hill Line Police Station registered this offence vide Cr. No. I­14/2015 on the report of victim girl. 2] The story of the prosecution in short is that, the native place of the victim family is from Bihar State but they are migrated to Mumbai area in search of work since long. The father of the victim is doing work as a Carpenter. The accused is hailed from Uttar Pradesh. He also migrated to Mumbai region for doing work and was working with the father of victim girl. 3] The accused was residing nearby the house of complainant family but his landlord expelled him from the rented house being rent defaulter. Hence he requested the father of victim to give him shelter till his alternative arrangement. Complainant family accepted him as their family member and allowed his accommodation. Hence he came to the complainant's house during October, 2014 in the period of Dasshera. The family of the complainant was consisting of husband and wife and their three children including victim girl. Complainant couple used to sleep in the separate room and the victim with her other siblings used to 3 Spl.Case No. 53/2015 [Judg. ] sleep in other room where one corner was given to the accused and he also used to sleep with them. 4] The accused has paid the outstanding grocery bill on behalf of complainant and said fact was not liked by victim girl. She objected the accused for making such obligations but he told her that he could not see the tension of victim girl only because of outstanding of grocery bill. One day in the month of October when victim girl was alone in the house, accused arrived there at about 5.00 p.m.. He asked sexual favour from the victim in lieu of his obligations regarding payment of grocery bill. The victim was shocked and the demand of accused as she was feeling him as her uncle. She denied and resisted the proposal but accused tied her hands, made her lie on the floor and then committed forceful intercourse with her removing the clothes against her wish. He gave threats not to disclose his act to anybody. The victim minor girl was shocked and frightened. She could not say said incidence even family members also. 5] Taking disadvantage of the fear alarmed in the mind of victim, accused has repeated sexual assaults on victim on different three occasions. It was unbearable for the victim girl. Lastly, she disclosed said fact to her father and asked him to lodge the report against accused. Initially the father was reluctant to report the matter with police due to stake and prestige of minor girl. However the accused has committed penetrative sexual assault repeatedly on her. 4 Spl.Case No. 53/2015 [Judg. ] Hence she decided to teach him lesson and hence went to the Central Police Station where she was advised to lodge report with Hill Line Police Station. The accused was brought to the Police Station on the oral narration of victim. On next day victim with her father withdrawn her report due to fear of defamation in society. Thus accused was relieved. However the superior Police Officer i.e. ACP directed concerned Police Station to take cognizance of the alleged atrocities committed by the accused. Hence victim was brought and her statement came to be recorded in presence of lady officer and NGOs. 6] PSO Hill Line Police Station registered the offence accordingly and further investigation was carried out by lady PSI Smt. Rajashree Shinde. The accused was arrested and his medical examination was done by seizing his clothes. Thereafter the clothes produced by the victim were also seized under seizure panchanama. The victim was sent for medical examination. The statements of corresponding witnesses came to be recorded. On receiving medical evidence including C.A. report and after completion of investigation I.O. has submitted chargesheet before the court. 7] The accused appeared before the court in response to the summons. I have framed charge against him vide Exh.14. It was read over and explained to him in vernacular. Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. The prosecution has examined in all three witnesses in support of it's case. I have recorded statement of the accused 5 Spl.Case No. 53/2015 [Judg. ] under section 313 of Cr.P.C.. Defence of the accused is of total denial and of false implication. 8] Considering the evidence on record and defence of the accused following points arose for my determination and my findings thereon are as under for the reasons given below :­ POINTS FINDINGS 1] Does prosecution prove that, during October, 2014 till 30/12/2014 in the residential house of victim in Dwarli Gaon, accused has repeatedly No. committed rape on the victim girl ageing about 16 years old and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 376(2) (F)(J)(N) of the Indian Penal Code ? 2] Does prosecution prove that, accused on the above dates, period, place and time caused criminal intimidation giving No. threats to the victim causing alarm of fear and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 506 of the Indian Penal Code ? 3] Does prosecution prove that, on the above period, place and time accused committed penetrative sexual assault on the minor victim girl and committed No. it by aggrievated form of penetrative sexual assault repeatedly on the victim girl and 6 Spl.Case No. 53/2015 [Judg. ] POINTS FINDINGS thereby committed an offence under sections 3 and 5 punishable under sections 4 and 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 ? 4] What order ? Accused is acquitted. REASONS 9] POINT NOS.1 TO 3 :­ The offence of rape coupled with aggrievated penetrative sexual assault on the minor victim girl is levelled against the present accused. It reveals from the prosecution story that complainant family gave shelter at their mercy but accused instead of said obligations returned it to the complainant by committing heinous offence of rape with the minor daughter of the complainant. The complainant family was still reluctant to prosecute the accused in police case considering their family relations and due to the prestige stake of the minor girl but the concerned Police Officer took cognizance of the said aggrievated offence and then investigation got in motion. Lady PSI Smt. Rajashree Shinde tried to collect adequate evidence to book the accused including medical evidence and chargesheeted him before the court. 10] However during the trial the entire scenario is changed. The victim girl who narrated entire episode of repeated sexual assault while lodging her report, she changed 7 Spl.Case No. 53/2015 [Judg. ] her mind and deposed exact contrary story during trial. Similar case is of her father. They have merely stated that there was quarrel on trifle reason as accused used to object the behaviour and friend circle company of the victim. The complainant victim was fed up by the teaching attitude of the accused and lodged report under the agony of anger. This story putforth by the complainant and her father is altogether different and contrary to the prosecution case. There is nothing incriminating against the accused. 11] Moreover the learned counsel Miss Tahsin Shaikh pointed out the medical evidence brought on record. It reveals that the accused is infected with AIDs and his HIV test is positive. However the examination of the victim with whom said accused committed physical intercourse, is negative. The aspect of improbability of commission of intercourse is tried to canvass with the help of said inconsistent medical evidence. Apart from it the material evidence adduced by the star witnesses is not whispering the commission of offence and the nexus of accused. In such situation I have no alternative but to answer point nos.1 to 3 in negative for want of adequate evidence. The accused cannot be connected with the crime only on the bare words of investigating officer. Hence I answer above points in negative. 12] POINT NO. 4 :­ As I held above prosecution failed to prove necessary ingredients to prove the guilt of accused. Hence he 8 Spl.Case No. 53/2015 [Judg. ] is liable to be acquitted giving benefit of inadequate evidence to prove the charges. The victim herself kept mum to speak against the accused. The father is also reluctant to depose against him. Thus he cannot be connected with crime only on the allegations of the FIR and bare words of the I.O.. In the result I answer point no.4 accordingly and proceed to pass following order :­ ORDER 1] Accused Dhanpat Bhagwati Kushwah, age 32 years, Occ­Labour, R/of Pindari, Post­Korya, Tal­Rudrapur, Dist­Devriya, (U.P.) is hereby acquitted under section 235(1) of Cr.P.C. of the offence punishable under sections 376(2)(F) (J)(N), 506 of Indian Penal Code and secs. 3 and 5 punishable under sections 4 and 6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. 2] The accused is in Jail, he be released forthwith if not required in any other case/crime. 3] Seized property i.e. clothes of the victim and accused being worthless, be destroyed, after appeal period is over. 4] The accused is directed to furnish fresh P.B. of Rs.15,000/­. In compliance with the provisions of section 437(A) of Cr.P.C. to abide himself to appear before Appellate Court in case of appeal is preferred by the prosecution. 5] Judgment pronounced in open Court.
