In case of wrong entry of birth date effected in the birth register, the permission of Village Development Officer is required to be obtained for the purpose of correction. 23. The Ld. Advocate for the accused submitted that the birth extract is produced at Exh.40 and 42 cannot be relied on as it has not been proved by the prosecution. He placed his reliance on the ruling of Hon'ble Bombay High Court MHLJ (CRI) 2016 3 766 = LAWS (BOM) 2015 8 81 in Criminal Appeal No.­956 of 2010 in the case of ­ Sandeep Janaji Konde Vs. The State of Maharashtra dated 4­8­2015, wherein His Lordship while considering Section 35 of the Evidence Act regarding relevancy of entry in public record. His Lordship held that the age of the person is to be proved like any other thing. The date of the birth of the person is expected to be known to his or her parents. The date of birth of person can be given by those who had witnessed the birth of the said person. In this case PW1 Bhagwan, the father of the victim has not disclosed the birth date of the victim except that her age was 12 years. Moreover, PW3 Gauri, the sister of the victim has mentioned the birth date of the victim as in the year 2000 and was studying in 8 th standard. None of them was questioned during their examination­ - 10 - Spl. Case No.-91/2014. in­chief about the date of birth of the victim. None of them has, therefore, stated directly or indirectly that the victim was below 13 years of age at the material time. The birth extract could be admissible in certain cases to prove the date of birth of the person by virtue of the provisions of Section 35 of the Evidence Act, which indicates that, to render the document admissible under it, three conditions must be satisfied, the first being, that the entry i.e. relied upon must be one in a public or other official book register or record, the second being, that it must be an entry stating a fact in issue or relevant fact and the third being that, must have been made by a public servant in discharge of his official duty or any other person in performance of duty specially enjoyed by law. An entry relating to date of birth made in School register would be relevant and admissible under Section 35 of the Evidence Act, but, it has been held that, such entry would not have much evidential value to prove the age of the person in absence of material on which the age was recorded. It is cardinal principle of the rules of evidence that the best evidence such as the nature of evidence would permit, must be given in all the cases. The age of the victim was crucial fact in determining the guilt of accused. There is no justification for not doing the ossification test. For all these reasons, His Lordship held that, ''I am unable to hold that, that the age of victim was below 16 years of age at the material time, was satisfactorily established in this case. In the light of the aforesaid weaknesses, in the evidence of this aspect, there arises a reasonable doubt about the age of the victim. At the cost of repetition, it must be held that when her own father says that she was at the material time 'of 16 years' does not give her date of birth; and the police report also refers to the victim as 'of 16 years', and when the court also understood the case put forth by the prosecution to be that the victim was 'aged 16 years' ­as is evident from the charge framed, it - 11 - Spl. Case No.-91/2014. would not be safe to conclude that she was certainly below 16 years of age at the material time.'' 24. The police though referred the victim to her medical examination to PW 5 Dr. Narhari Ankush Phad, MO RH Murbad and was on duty on 9­4­2014, however, though the victim was brought in the hospital for medical examination, but he did not examine her but referred to Central Hospital vide MLC No.­2456 dated 9­4­2014 (Article 'A'). He assigned the reason while referring the victim to Central Hospital Ulhasnagar, that she has to examine by lady Gynecologist. He has also not noted down the age, address and the name of the person who brought the victim. 25. PW 6 Dr. Mrs. Shalaka Chandrakar Thorat, the MO Central Hospital Ulhasnagar, was on duty on 9­4­2014 from 9 am to 9 pm. The Murbad police had brought the victim for her medical examination by her mother Sou. Shobha who then recorded the history that of sexual assault by 40 years male known by her at 1 am on 8­4­2014. Dr. Puri was the Gaencologist, who examined the victim (now he is not available as he has proceeded on medical leave). She tried to state that Dr. Puri prepared three pages of sexu8al assault form and signed by him but first and second page was in her handwriting. Though she has brought that the hymen of the victim was torn and the age was more than 24 hours. She has identify the handwriting of Dr. Puri in column 6 and 7 at Exh.38. But, neither this witness nor Dr. Puri referred the victim for her ossification test so as to ascertain her age after obtaining x­ray etc. 26. Thus, there is no other evidence on the point of age of the victim except the birth extract produced at Exh.40 by PW 7 Praveen - 12 - Spl. Case No.-91/2014. Shinde, the Clerk serving in Municipal Council Murbad. He has stated that the said birth register has not been maintained properly and chronologically by paging and sealing etc. nor the entry at serial No.328 in the birth register (Exh.42) was effected in the presence of Village Development Officer. Therefore, it cannot be said that, the said birth extract was made by public servant in discharge of his official duty and it is a public official book register or record I said this because the witness Praveen Shinde has stated that his Department get print of the register in Murbad itself that too without paging, sealing and certificate regarding the register containing the particular number of pages. 27. The father and sister of the victim (PW1 & PW3) have failed to state the exact birth date of the victim so as to ascertain her age on the date of alleged incident dated 8­4­2014. Therefore in absence of the age proof of the victim I hold that the prosecution has failed to prove her age. Hence, I answer point No.1, in the negative. As to point No.2 to 4 :­ 28] I have taken all these points together as they are interlinked and to avoid repetition. The victim is the only witness to the alleged incident occurred on 8­4­2014 in between 12 midnight to 2 am at ZP Girls' School No.2 Bokad Ali, Murbad. Therefore her evidence is to be taken in to consideration at very inceptional stage so as to appreciate the evidence of other witnesses to whom she has disclosed about the incident. 29. According to her, her mother is vegetable vendor and father is Cobbler. She is studying in 8th standard. Sou. Rekha Haresh Jadhav (DW2) is the daughter­in­law of her real uncle who resides - 13 - Spl. Case No.-91/2014. near her house. She knows the accused Atish Shelar who is the brother of Rekha. It is her case that, accused had come to the house of his sister Rekha for Bhaubij. She was having visiting terms to the house of Rekha and hence, she came to know that accused has come to her house. She had met the accused on previous Diwali festival at the time of Bhaubij only. Thereafter she was not visiting the house of Rekha. 30. On the day of incident i.e. 8­4­2014 at 12 midnight at the gate of ZP School No.2 Murbad the incident occurred in white coloured Tavera vehicle. At that time there was palanquin procession of Ekveera Devi was going on in her town which was begun at 11 pm from her house as the temple of Ekveera Devi is adjacent to her house. There were many people in palanquin procession including herself. When the procession reached near Gaondevi temple at 12 midnight, at that time she was feeling to go to sleep. Then she alone proceeded to a house from the road of Hanuman Temple. She reached at half of the road to her house, the accused Atish Shelar came behind her and took her in his Tavera vehicle. 31. According to her, she felt that he must be taking her to her house. She was taken her vehicle from front gate of ZP school and then accused told her that he likes her and want to marry with her. She then replied by saying that, 'Dada tuze Lagna zale aahe, tula he shobhat nahi.'' and then it is her case that accused raped her in the vehicle. Then the accused threatened to kill her if she disclosed the incident to her family members. Then she returned to her home . Due to fear she did not disclose the incident anyone. 32. On 8­4­2014, as her stomach was aching, therefore, she was - 14 - Spl. Case No.-91/2014. crying. Her elder sister Gouri (PW3) asked her as to why she is crying then she narrated the incident to her family members. Thereafter her father PW1 lodged the FIR. Police then recorded her statement in presence of her family members. She then showed the place of occurrence to the police and produced her clothes. She was then sent to the hospital for her medical examination. 33. She admits that the marriage of Rekha is love marriage and hence accuse Atish Shelar was not coming to the house of his sister Rekha. Her house is situated in thick locality. In palanquin process the people of Murbad Taluka had gathered. Area known as Bokad Ali is near Rohidas nagar in Murbad town. Sajai phata is a big road in her locality and there is big wada (house) of Darekar in front of ZP school on Sajai Phata road. There are houses of either sides of the road known as Sajai Phata road while entering in Murbad town. From Sajai Phata there is road which goes towards Jain mandir and there is small lane from Dahekar wada. According to her, her family member had also attended the palanquin procession. 34. She has stated that nobody was present on the road by which she was proceeding to her house. One would require half an hour to reach palanquin procession from ZP school. The distance in between the ZP school and her house was 5 minutes walkable distance but there were no street lights on the road from ZP school to her house. 35. The accused Atish Shelar is married having children. She known one Sagar Walanj the son of her maternal paternal aunt and there is custom to give daughter of material aunt in marrying to the son of paternal aunt. He did not know any quarrel in between Sagar Walanj and accused Atish. - 15 - Spl. Case No.-91/2014. 36. According to her, prior to 25 days she had menstrual cycle. She admitted that, her stomach aches at the time of menstrual period. During the incident she had a menstrual period. In her school there is period of physical training. On 8­4­2014, her father (PW1) had taken her to the hospital but her statement was not recorded by police. On 9­4­2014, she had gone to Central Hospital but her statement was not recorded by the police. On 10­4­2014, also her statement was not recorded by the police. 37. Before recording her statement by the police the accused was arrested but her father had lodged the FIR on 8­4­2014 (in fact on 9­4­2014) against the accused. Her father had taken her to the hospital on 8­4­2014 and she had gone to Central Hospital on 9­4­2014. 38. She had not disclosed to her father about the accused. Her sister PW 3 Gouri is residing at her matrimonial home at Thane but her statement was not recorded by the police. Before lodging the FIR, her father discussed with her, her mother, elder sister Gouri. According to her she is seeing the vehicle of accused since beginning. Her father also saw the vehicle of the accused. 39. She has stated that she was knowing the arrival and departure of accused Atish Shelar from the house of her brother wife Rekha whose house is adjacent to her house. She does not know whether her father had called accused on phone. She was in Central Hospital from 9­4­2014 to 11­4­2014 and hence, she did not return to Murbad during the said period. Her parents and one LPC were with him in the Central Hospital and after the discharge she went to her house from Central Hospital. - 16 - Spl. Case No.-91/2014. 40. Though she was taken to RH Murbad on 8­4­2014 but her medical examination was not done however she was referred to Central Hospital. She had not sustained any injury on her body. 41. On the main road in her locality, number of vehicles are being parked aside the road but there was no vehicles were parked on the road from her house to the place of palanquin processions. She has vitally admitted that on the date of incident in palanquin procession she did not see the vehicle of the accused. Further she stated that, due to procession no vehicles were parked on either side of the road. 42. The informant PW1 Bhagwan is the father of the victim. He has four daughters and one son. According to him the age of victim was 12 years at the relevant time. On 8­4­2014, there was palanquin procession in the town Murbad at 12.30 am in which the victim went behind the said procession but he was at home. His elder daughter Gauri (PW3) disclosed him about the incident as she was disclosed by the victim. The victim was in the said procession till 1.30 am. During the said period PW3 Gauri had send the victim for bringing water from her house and accordingly he took water bottled from her house. This fact has not been mentioned in the FIR and hence, it is an omission. Further, he has brought on record that the victim wanted to go to sleep and hence, she proceeded towards the home. While proceeding to her home the accused caught her, shut the mouth with his hands and then she was taken in Tavera car and committed rape on her. This fact is also brought on record as an omission. The victim was threatened by the accused so that she should not disclosed the incident to any one or else he would kill her. PW3 Gauri, the elder daughter took the - 17 - Spl. Case No.-91/2014. victim to RH Murbad where the medical officer opined that victim had been sexually assaulted. Then they all went to the police station and lodged the FIR (Exh.19) on 9­4­2014. The witness has not seen the accused on the day of incident and he has not lodged the FIR on 8.4.2014. In fact, he had not gone to attend the procession of palanquin and he was present in his house. He has specifically testified that he approached to the police after the opinion of Medical Officer, Murbad. They had not taken the victim on very night to the Medical Officer, Murbad. He admits that Rekha is the sister of the accused and daughter­in­law of his brother, whose marriage is love marriage. This witness has lodged the FIR on the basis of the opinion given by the Medical Officer, Murbad however PW5 Dr. Narhari Phad has brought on record that, he did not examined the victim but referred her to the Central Hospital, only on the reason that, she has to be medically examined by lady gynecologist. Therefore, the question of giving opinion about sexual assault on the victim does not arise. It is not the case of the informant that the victim directly disclosed the incident to him, but was disclosed by PW 3 Gauri. 43. PW 3 Gauri resides at her matrimonial home at Thane. She had gone to Murbad on 7­4­2014 to the house of her parents to attend Ekveera palanquin procession which goes from entire Murbad town. There used to be crowd and all devotees follow the palanquin procession. Rekha is the wife of her cousin brother who married in the year 2009. She also known the accused as brother of Rekha. According to her, on 7­4­2014 alongwith her son (minor) and victim had gone to attend palanquin procession at 11 pm. At 11.45 pm her son was thirsty and the victim brought the water bottle from her house within 5­10 minutes. This is all brought an - 18 - Spl. Case No.-91/2014. omission on record. At 12 midnight the victim told her that she needs sleep and at that time the procession was reached at Gavdevi temple. Therefore, she told her to go to home as her house was nearby but in opposite direction of palanquin procession. Then the victim left the procession. 44. On the next day morning when the victim woke up she was crying due to stomach aching. On her asking to the victim she disclosed her that when she left the palanquin procession while returning to her home she was caught near Maruti mandir and a vehicle parked near Marathi school which was Tavera and she was raped. Then she disclosed incident to her parents and thereafter the victim was taken to the hospital where doctor examined her and opined that she has been raped. However, PW5 Dr. Narhari Phad has brought on record that, he did not examined the victim but referred her to the Central Hospital, only on the reason that, she has to be medically examined by lady gynecologist. Therefore, the question of giving opinion about sexual assault on the victim does not arise. 45. PW 3 Gauri in her testimony stated that on the very day of the incident she along with the victim and her father had gone to the police station i.e. on 8­4­2014 (in fact none had gone) and again she had gone on 14­4­2014 when her statement was recorded. She has made out a different case by stating that she never disclosed about the incident from 8­4­2014 to 13­4­2014 to any one. This version contradicts the informant PW1 Bhagwan whose case is that PW 3 Gauri disclosed him about the incident. 46. There are adjoining houses in Rohidas wada where her father resides. She was staying with her parents till 14­4­2014 but not - 19 - Spl. Case No.-91/2014. disclosed the incident to anyone. Due to palanquin procession and crowd following the procession, the vehicles were not allowed to pass through main road. Her house is at the distance of 5 minutes walk from Gavdevi mandir and people were passing through the said road due to palanquin procession. When she was returning to her house after attending palanquin procession she did not see any vehicle on the way. The distance between Bokad ali from her house upto 3 minutes walk but according to her no one can hear call if given from Bokad ali. She stated that the victim disclosed her about the incident at 1.30 pm to 2 pm and then she was taken to female medical officer at 3.20 pm to 4 pm. but in fact her statement shows that the victim was taken by her and her parents on next day morning to female Medical Officer. In fact, the Medical Officer was male. Said lady doctor did not give anything in writing to her but had given to her father who then handed over to Ulhasnagar hospital but she did not accompany with victim to Ulhasnagar hospital. 47. She has step mother residing with her parents, who is issueless. Prior to the incident they had co­ordial relations with her uncle who is father­in­law of Rekha. Even after the marriage of Rekha there was no dispute with her cousin brother. According to her she has travelled in the vehicle of accused who is married and having two sons residing at Mumbai. She has stated that accused was arrested on 8­4­2014 in the night itself who had not come to the house of Rekha at Murbad but he was brought by the police from Titwala. She did not give her statement to the police immediately after the arrest of the accused. 48. The accused came to be arrested on 9­4­2014 at 2.35 am, therefore the version of PW 3 Gauri that he was arrested on - 20 - Spl. Case No.-91/2014. 8­4­2014 has no substance. Morevoer, PW3 Gauri has not deposed that the victim disclosed her that accused committed rape on her. What she has brought on record that on the next day morning when the victim woke up and was crying due to stomach aching, therefore, she asked her about the reason of cry who then disclosed that when she left palanquin procession and while returning home, she was caught near Maruti mandir and the vehicle was stopped near Marathi school which was Tavera and she was raped. Nowhere the name of the accused is mentioned by this witness except vehicle Tavera in which the victim was alleged to have been raped. PW3 Gauri has given contradictory version on material particulars including that she was asked to the victim to bring water bottle, female doctor was examined the victim, opinion given by the doctor that the victim has been raped, the accused was arrested on 8.4.2014 in the night and she disclosed the incident to her father. The demeanor of this witness was also recorded while recording her evidence in open Court who found to be rude and arrogant. Therefore, considering the evidence of this witness does not establish any nexus of the accused with the alleged incident. 49. The Ld. Spl.APP relied on the ruling reported in ­ 2013 CRI.L.J. 194 (SC) in the case of – State of U.P. Vs. Munesh – wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court held that, ''The primary concern both the national and international level is about the devastating increase in rape cases and relating to crime against women in the world. India is no exception to it. Although the statutory provisions provide strict penal action against such offenders, it is for the Courts to ultimately decide whether such incident has occurred or not. The Courts should be more cautions in appreciating the evidence and the accused should not be left scot­free merely on flimsy grounds. In the instant case, the accused had committed rape, which repels against moral conscience - 21 - Spl. Case No.-91/2014. as he chose a girl of 11 years to satisfy his lust and subsequently murdered her.'' The ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court is that, due to increase in rape cases and cases relating to crime against women, it is for the Court to apply strict penal action against such offender provided that Court has to decide as to whether such incident has occurred or not for which the Courts should be more cautious in appreciating the evidence and accused should not be left scot­free on flimsy grounds. 50. Another ruling cited is reported in 2012 CRI.L.J. 1129(Bom) in the case of Bhuku Tukaram Jadhav Vs. State of Maharashtra wherein, the accused was subjecting his minor daughter to sexual assault repeatedly and she disclosed the fact only after she became pregnant. Psychology of child victim is to be taken into consideration. Reasons for non disclosure of sexual assault could be many such as threats to the victim or her dear ones or psychology of the child to obey orders of rapist if he is her custodian or she is dependent on him. The accused threatening the victim that she would be killed if she disclosed his misdeeds. In these circumstances the Hon'ble High Court held that, the evidence of the was reliable. Herein, the case on hand is concerned the victim is not under the custody or dependent on the accused nor the accused is related to the victim except that he is the real brother of Rekha Haresh Jadhav. Moreover, the father and elder sister of the victim after discussion approached to the police on imaginary facts where the FIR of PW 1 Bhagwan came to be recorded. Therefore, the facts of the case on hand are quite different than that of the facts in the ruling cited. - 22 - Spl. Case No.-91/2014. 51. PW4 Mohan Gagandas Mata is the friend of PW1 Bhagwan who is hawker visiting various villages and towns on every weekly bazar i.e. Murbad, Vashind, Badlapur. Padgha and Khopoli. According to him the victim took him to a girls' school at 9 am. At that time police officer and co­panch were with him. Vehicle like Tavera was parked near the wall of the building where the spot panchnama (Exh.27) was drawn on the computer. 52. On the very day, he was again called by the Murbad police station where the accused was in police custody. Police showed him the clothes of the accused viz. blue lining shirt, chocolatee pant, maroon banian and underwear which were seized under seizure panchanam Exh.28. 53. This witness has tried to make out the case that the mother of the accused had attempted to tamper his evidence by stating that on 16­12­2015 at 3 pm one woman and male had come to his house on motor cycle by name Bharati Shelar who asked his nephew Dilip Mata where he resides but his nephew disclosed her that he has gone for business. Then said Bharati Shelar told him that tomorrow there is case of Murbad police station in the Court and asked him to ask to make phone call to her on cell No.­9561457017 and Tatpure Murbad cell No.­9323394636. These cell numbers were written on the piece of English newspaper Article A. In fact, the cell number of Bharati Shelar was in the hand writing of his nephew Dilip Mata. 54. He know the PW1 Bhagwan since last 10 years who was also accompanied with him in the Court, when his evidence was recorded. He used to keep his bags of business with PW1 Bhagwan. According to him, the weekly bazar of Murbad is on every Friday where is used to go but he did not recollect whether it was Friday - 23 - Spl. Case No.-91/2014. on 9­4­2014. The vehicle Tavera was found in front of school. This factual position is otherwise in view of seizure panchanama of vehicle (Exh.55) which was seized from Goveli phata parked in front of the house of accused. Therefore this witness is not reliable but got up witness. Moreover, this witness has stated that he is required to go to police station as and when called as he does hawker business on the road. Further, according to him, initially, the panchanama was written in handwriting and then his signature was obtained on handwritten panchanama. He did not lodge the complaint when said Bharati Shelar given the cell number to his nephew Dilip Mata. Because of his friendship with the informant he must have acted as panch witness on the say of the informant but not given material particulars to believe his testimony. 55. PW 8 Rajaram Ganpat Jadhav, who acted as Panch witness for seizure of clothes panchanama of victim at Exh.45, but he has not supported the case of the prosecution by stating that on 9­4­2014 he was called in Murbad police station and he was asked to put signature on the panchanama. Therefore, his evidence is not useful to the prosecution in any manner. Moreover, nothing incriminating was found on the clothes of the victim in view of CA report at Exh.59. 56. PW 9 the Investigating Officer Rajendra Tukaram Hulavale carried out the investigation as usual. He admits that the statement of the victim was not recorded by lady police staff though her statement was recorded after two days of the incident. The statement of the sister of the victim was recorded after 5 days. When the FIR came to be recorded, at that time, there was no medical report or no witness had stated that rape was committed on victim. Thus, there is no basis to register the crime without any - 24 - Spl. Case No.-91/2014. material before the registering the crime. He has also admitted that the house of the victim is at 2 minutes walk from ZP school. Due to palanquin procession people used to go and come during night time. He has stated that on 9­4­2014, it was Wednesday and not Friday. Moreover, he has admitted that there is proof to show that the accused was present with his vehicle at the fair of Ekveera devi. He did not verify about the passing of vehicle of the accused through toll plaza. He never recorded the statement of family members of Rekha (DW2). During personal search and arrest panchanama of the accused nothing objectionable article or thing was found with him. At the time of seizure panchanama of the vehicle the accused opened the door of the vehicle by taking key from his mother, but said fact has not been mentioned in the seizure panchanama. 57. Further he admits that the accused resides at Mumbai. At the time of FIR the accused was not present however within one hour of the registration of the crime he arrested the accused as he was found in Murbad taluka to PSI Shri. Giri but entry to that effect was not taken in the station diary. Moreover, there is no evidence to show that the accused had come in Murbad from the date of marriage of his sister till his arrest. He has also specifically stated that MO RH Murbad never opined anything about the victim but she was sent to Central Hospital , Ulhasnagar. The evidence of IO shows that he has not recorded the statements of the family members of Rekha (DW2) 58. The accused though examined two defence witnesses viz. Dasharath Sonu Jadhav at Exh.63 and his daughter­in­law DW2 Sou. Rekha Haresh Jadhav at Exh.64 to prove the fact that the relation between the accused and his sister Rekha and her family - 25 - Spl. Case No.-91/2014. members are not cordial due to love marriage performed by Rekha. Because of love marriage of Rekha, the informant was having cross terms with the accused. The circumstances show that DW 1 Dasharath had no objection for love marriage of Rekha with his son Haresh, therefore, the quarrel on that reason by the informant cannot be believed and accepted. 59. The testimony of the victim on the point of alleged incident cannot be believed on the simple reason that she had no occasion to see the accused on the date of incident including his vehicle. She had seen the accused on the previous Diwali festival at the time of Bhaubij at the house of Rekha (DW2). Moreover, the story put forth by her is that her father discussed with her, her mother and elder sister and then the lodged the FIR (Exh.19) on 9­4­2014 at 12.25 am. Her stomach was aching due to menstrual period at the time of alleged incident her menstrual period was going on. The accused came to be arrested on 9­4­2014 at 2.35 am and hence his clothes must be stained with blood but the CA certificate regarding blood and semen or vaginal fluid was detected on the clothes of the accused vide Exh.59. Even on the clothes of the victim no blood or semen was detected in view of CA certificate at Exh.58. She has also not given the requisite details of alleged rape and penetrative sexual assault. Moreover, no violence mark or injury was sustained to the victim during the alleged sexual assault. 60. Considering the evidence of the prosecution neither the ingredients of rape and penetrative sexual assault or threats given to the victim are proved by adducing cogent, reliable and trustworthy evidence, hence, I answer the point Nos. 2 to 5, in the negative. - 26 - Spl. Case No.-91/2014. 61. Resultantly, the accused deserves to be acquitted, and as such, I proceed to pass the following order : ORDER i) The accused Atish Suresh Shelar is hereby acquitted vide Section 235(1) of Cr.P.C. of the offences punishable under Sec.376 and 506 of Indioan Penal Code and Section 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offenes Act, 2012. ii) He is in Jail since 9­4­2014, hence, he shall be set at liberty forthwith if not required in any other crime or case. iii) Cloth of the victim and accused seized by police but not produced before the Court, be destroyed being worthless after the period of appeal is over. Judgment­Atro Spl.Case 89/2014 ­: JUDGMENT :­ (Delivered in open court on this 14th day of June, 2017) 1/­ Present accused is prosecuted by the State through Ambernath Police Station for the offence punishable under sections 363, 376 of Indian Penal Code and under section 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Prosecution story in brief is as follows : 2/­ One Raju Manik Abhange, father of prosecutrix filed one complaint on 01.10.2013 in Ambernath Police Station. In his complaint he alleged that, the victim girl is his daughter. She was studying in 11th standard at Chandibai College. On 28.09.2013 at about 4.00 p.m. his daughter i.e. the victim girl along with his mother went to Bangadi Bazar at Ambernath. From there all of sudden she disappeared. In spite of search, she could not found. Therefore, on 29.09.2013 this Raju Manik Abhange filed missing complaint in respect of his daughter in Ambernath Police Station bearing no.44/2013. During investigation of missing complaint it was revealed to the Investigation Officer that, one Yogesh Mukesh Indrekar and Nikhil Kailas Indrekar might have been kidnapped the minor girl of Raju Abhange. Therefore, against them the complainant Raju Manik Abhange lodged the complaint in Ambernath Police Station on 01.10.2013. During investigation of this complaint it was revealed to the Investigation Officer that, on 28.09.2013 the victim girl came to Bombay Central by local train and caught the train proceeding towards Gujarat. This accused Dpk/J­Atro. Spl Case No.89/2014 .....3/­ ..3.. Judgment­Atro Spl.Case 89/2014 was of the acquaintance of prosecutrix. She informed this accused that she is coming to Ahmadabad, Gujarat. Thereafter, this accused met the prosecutrix at Ahmadabad. Then, along with her he went to his friend Kunjal Patel's house. For some days they resided there. For some days they were also resided as paying guest. Meantime, accused told the victim girl that he loves her and he is going to marry her. Saying so, under the false promise to marry, accused committed rape on the victim girl. Accordingly, supplementary statement was recorded of the complainant Raju Manik Abhange by the Investigation Officer. 3/­ During further investigation, Investigation Officer prepared spot panchanama on 08.05.2014. He seized lodge register from Moni Hotel Lodge, Ahmadabad under panchanama on 08.05.2014. He recorded statement of the victim girl on 25.04.2014. Her supplementary statement was recorded on 15.05.2014. The Investigation Officer further recorded statements of witnesses. He seized the articles. He sent the seized articles to Forensic Science Laboratory. He caused medical examination of both accused and victim girl. He obtained the medical reports. After completion of investigation, he submitted charge­sheet in the Court. 4/­ My learned predecessor framed Charge against this accused at Exh.13 for the offence punishable under sections 363, 376 of IPC and under section 4 r/w. Section 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Charge was read over Dpk/J­Atro. Spl Case No.89/2014 .....4/­ ..4.. Judgment­Atro Spl.Case 89/2014 and explained to accused in Marathi language. Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. His defence is that of total denial. No defence witness is examined by the accused. 5/­ Prosecution was directed to adduce its evidence. In response to that, prosecution examined in all 3 witnesses in this case. PW No.1, the victim girl (Exh.15). PW No.2, the complainant and father of victim girl namely Raju Manik Abhange (Exh.16). Both these witnesses have not supported the case of prosecution. They have not uttered a single incriminating word against the accused. PW No.3 Shri Ajay Rajaram Mhetre is the Investigation Officer (Exh.24). He deposed about some documents seized during investigation. Thereafter, prosecution closed its evidence. 6/­ I have gone through the prosecution evidence on record. I have heard Ld. APP Shri D.V. Bhangre as well as Ld. Advocate Smt. K.H. Aesankar for accused at length. Following points arise for my determination. My findings on those points are as follows for the reasons stated below : Sr.No. Points Findings 1. Does prosecution prove that, in .. In the negative. between 28.09.2013 at 16.00 hrs. to 21.04.2014, accused kidnapped minor victim girl from lawful guardianship of her parents and thereby committed an offence punishable u/s.363 of IPC ? 2. Does prosecution prove that during .. In the negative. the abovesaid period, accused Dpk/J­Atro. Spl Case No.89/2014 .....5/­ ..5.. Judgment­Atro Spl.Case 89/2014 committed rape on minor victim girl and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 376 of IPC ? 3. Does prosecution prove that during .. In the negative. the abovesaid period, accused committed penetrative sexual assault on minor victim girl and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 4 r/w. Section 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 ? ­: R E A S O N S :­ As to point nos.1 to 3 : 7/­ PW No.1, the victim girl and PW No.2, her father Raju Manik Abhange i.e. the complainant has uttered no single incriminating word against this accused. Victim girl has stated her date of birth as 19.03.1995 during her examination­in­chief. It means that, on the day of alleged incident she was not minor. Rather, she was major. It is suggested on behalf of prosecution to her that, her date of birth is 19.03.1997. But, this suggestion is flatly denied by the victim girl. 8/­ The victim girl has not shown her acquaintance with this accused. She flatly stated that she do not know the accused before the Court. She has further stated that, she did not see him at any time and anywhere. If this is true, then question of kidnapping the victim girl by accused and committing rape on her does not arise at all. No other evidence regarding the age or the Dpk/J­Atro. Spl Case No.89/2014 .....6/­ ..6.. Judgment­Atro Spl.Case 89/2014 birth date of victim girl is brought on record. Ld. APP cross­ examined this witness at length. Even in her cross­examination, nothing incriminating is brought against this accused. Therefore, her evidence is of no use for the purpose of prosecution. 9/­ Similar is the fact in respect of deposition of PW No.2 Shri Raju Manik Abhange. He admitted that, he had lodged missing complaint regarding his daughter i.e. victim girl. He had expressed his suspicion on Yogesh Indrekar and Nikhil Indrekar. However, he has not uttered any word against this accused. He deposed that, victim herself informed on phone to her brother that she is doing job. Thereafter, his brother­in­law met to victim and brought her home. He further deposed that, victim never narrated anything to him. She never stated about accused to him. This fact is also evident from the complaint itself. In entire complaint, there is nothing to show that this accused was knowing the complainant or complainant was knowing the accused. On the contrary, the suspicion was expressed on somebody else and not on the accused. Thus, the evidence of this PW No.2 Raju Manik Abhange is also of no use for the prosecution. 10/­ PW No.3 Ajay Rajaram Mhetre deposed about one receipt of Rs.2,00,000/­ at Article 'A', agreement to sale at Article 'B', deed of guarantee at Article 'C', and deed of guarantee of victim girl at Article 'D'. At the out set I would like to state that, these documents are not duly proved. Contents in the documents are also not proved. Original documents are not produced on Dpk/J­Atro. Spl Case No.89/2014 .....7/­ ..7.. Judgment­Atro Spl.Case 89/2014 record. No permission was sought to adduce secondary evidence. Therefore, whatever stated by PW No.3 Ajay Mhetre during his deposition is totally irrelevant for the purpose of prosecution to prove the guilt of accused. 11/­ Even though, charge­sheet is filed against this accused, how this accused and the victim were acquainted with each other or were known to each other is nowhere brought on record. When and for what purpose accused had been to Ahmadabad is nowhere brought on record. What is the reason for the acquaintance of victim with accused is also not brought on record. Number of important things are missing from the chain of evidence of prosecution. Even there is no cogent, corroborative evidence to prove the fact that on the date of alleged incident the victim girl was minor. Considering all these facts, the circumstances and the evidence on record, it is crystal clear that whatever evidence adduced by prosecution is not at all sufficient to prove the guilt of accused. Hence, I answer point nos. 1 to 3 in the negative. 12/­ As there is no incriminating evidence against this accused, his statement under section 313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure stands dispensed with. In conclusion, I pass following order : ­: O R D E R :­ 1. Accused Aniket Sudhir Kodekar is hereby acquitted of the offence punishable under sections 363, 376 of Indian Penal Dpk/J­Atro. Hatarote) SESSIONS CASE NO. 90 OF 2014 State of Maharashtra ( Through Kinhavali police Stateion, Tal­Shahapur, Dist­Thane ) ( Cr. No. I­26/2014 ) ...Complainant Versus Jagan Ramchandra Raut, Age 28 years, Occ­Agriculture, R/at Gunde, Tal­Shahapur, Dist­Thane. ...Accused Offence punishable under section 376(2)(f) of the Indian Penal Code. ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ ...2/­ 2 S.C. No. 90/2014 [ Judg. ] Mrs. R.R. Bhoir, ld. APP for the State Mrs. Gauri Ramdurgkar, Ld. Advocate for the Accused –­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ JUDGMENT ( Delivered in Open Court On 9th day of May, 2017 ) 1] This accused is prosecuted by State through Kinhavali police station for the offence punishable under section 376(2)(f) of the Indian Penal Code. 2] Brief facts of the prosecution story are as follows :­ Complainant Ranjana Hari Raut and this accused are distinct relatives. Accused is distant uncle of the complainant. They reside nearby each other. Accused reside with his younger brother Yogesh and mother Seetabai. Three years before the complaint mother of accused undergone operation. She was ill. There was no other to prepare food and look after the house in the house of accused. As the complainant Ranjana was the distinct relative of accused, mother of complainant asked complainant to stay with accused and his mother in their house and to look after their household works. During night they were sleeping together. On one night accused asked complainant for corporal relations. Thereafter physical relations took place between complainant and accused. Thereafter also from time to time ...3/­ 3 S.C. No. 90/2014 [ Judg. ] there were sexual relations between complainant and accused. In October, 2013 complainant became pregnant. About pregnancy she came to know in that month. 3] On 27/4/2014 she was feeling abdomenal pain. She told this fact to her mother as well as mother of accused. They both advised accused to take complainant to the Sub­ District Hospital at Shahapur. Accordingly accused took the complainant to Sub­District Hospital, Shahapur. There complainant gave birth to one female baby. Thereafter the relatives of both sides came to know about the relations between accused and complainant. And thereafter complainant lodged complaint against the accused on 27/4/2014. Crime was registered at Cr. No. I­26/2014. 4] N.S. Bhoir P.S.I. carried investigation in the matter. He arrested accused. He caused medical of accused as well as complainant. He caused DNA test to be taken of the child and the accused. He recorded statements of the witnesses. He recorded memorandum of accused. Accused admitted to show the place where the offence took place. Thereafter as per memorandum accused shown the place. Then necessary documents were obtained by Investigating Officer. After completion of investigation he submitted chargesheet in the court. ...4/­ 4 S.C. No. 90/2014 [ Judg. ] 5] Accused appeared before this court. Charge against him is framed at Exh.14. Charge was read over and explained to accused in Marathi language. Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. His defence is that there were love affairs between him and the complainant. Complainant was major. Relation between them took place with the consent of both. He has committed no offence. 6] Prosecution was directed to adduce its evidence. In response to that prosecution examined in all three witnesses in this case. PW­1 Vishnu Ramchandra Rasal. He is panch witness on memorandum as well as spot panchanama. This witness turned hostile. He has not uttered a single word against the accused. However during the course of evidence accused admitted his memorandum as well as spot panchanama. And therefore those are subsequently exhibited. PW­2 Miss Ranjana Hari Raut Exh.17 is complainant. She deposed that, there were love affairs between she herself and accused. Out of that love affair corporal relations took place between she herself and accused with the consent of both. At that time she was major. Out of those relations she conceived and delivered a baby. PW­3 Sau. Anita Hari Raut is mother of complainant Ranjana. She deposed that, accused is her distinct relative. Ranjana was residing with accused and his mother in their house, when mother of accused was ill. During that period love developed between complainant and ...5/­ 5 S.C. No. 90/2014 [ Judg. ] accused. Out of that they came together, had a sexual intercourse. Then the complainant conceived and delivered a baby. No further evidence is adduced by prosecution. 7] I have gone through oral and documentary evidence of prosecution on record. I have heard both the learned advocates at length. 8] Following points arise for my consideration. My findings on those points are as follows for the reasons stated below. POINTS FINDINGS 1. Whether prosecution proves that, on 27/4/2014 at 7.00 p.m. at Mauje­Gunde, Taluka­Shahapur, District­ Thane, within the jurisdiction of Kinhavali police station, Not proved. committed rape on their distinct relative who conceived and gave birth to a female child and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 376(2)(f) of the Indian Penal Code ? REASONS 9] I have carefully gone through the prosecution evidence on record. Even if we accept the prosecution evidence as it is then also no guilt of accused is proved much ...6/­ 6 S.C. No. 90/2014 [ Judg. ] the less the guilt of committing rape on the complainant. It is specifically deposed by PW­2 Ranjana that when she was residing with accused and his mother in their house, she fall in love with accused. Out of these relations they enjoyed the sexual life and conceived from those relations. She further deposed that, at that time she was 20 years old. Her mother also deposed before the court that at the time of incident complainant was 20 years old. There were love affairs between complainant and accused. Out of that affair complainant conceived from accused and delivered a baby. This is the sum and substance of the prosecution evidence. 10] Nowhere it is stated by any prosecution witness and the complainant that accused committed rape on her. Nowhere it is brought on record by the prosecution through the mouth of any witness that accused made sexual intercourse with complainant against her will, against her consent or practicing fraud upon her, or obtaining her consent for sexual intercourse under coercion, mis­ representation etc.. On the contrary both prosecution witnesses deposed that the corporal relations took place between complainant and accused with their consent. No one was forced them to have a sexual relations with each other. And therefore the alleged act of the accused having intercourse with complainant does not fall within the definition of rape more particularly within the definition of ...7/­ 7 S.C. No. 90/2014 [ Judg. ] section 375 of the Indian Penal Code. Consequently no offence is proved against the accused more particularly the offence under section 376(2)(f) of the Indian Penal Code. 11] It is vehemently contended by learned advocate for prosecution Mrs. Bhoir that, at the time of the incident or at the time of first intercourse and subsequent intercourse complainant Ranjana was below 18 years age. And therefore her consent for sexual intercourse is totally immaterial and not considerable. However these arguments are not sustainable in the light of evidence on record. It is deposed by PW­2 Ranjana and PW­3 Smt. Anita that at the time of alleged incident complainant was 20 yeas old. No reason to disbelieve them. No other concrete evidence adduced by prosecution to show that on the date of offence the complainant was below 18 years of the age. In such circumstances I have to accept the testimony of complainant Ranjana and her mother Anita on the point of age of the complainant at the time of the incident. If that is considered then definitely the fact emerges that on the date of alleged offence complainant was major and above 18 years. As I have already stated the act of intercourse between complainant and accused was taken place with the consent of complainant as well as the accused. If this peculiar circumstance is considered then it emerges that accused has committed no offence. There is no strong, cogent, corroborative and reliable ...8/­ 8 S.C. No. 90/2014 [ Judg. ] evidence against the accused to prove his guilt under section 376(2)(f) of the Indian Penal Code. And therefore I answer the point in negative. 12] For want of incriminating evidence against accused his statement under section 313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure stands dispensed with. 13] In conclusion I pass the following order :­ ORDER 1. Accused Jagan Ramchandra Raut, age 28 years, R/at Gunde, Taluka­Shahapur, District­Thane, is hereby acquitted of the offence punishable under section 376(2)(f) of the Indian Penal Code. 2. His bail bond stands cancelled. He is set at liberty. 3. Copy of this Judgment be sent to trial court for information. Kalyan (D.S.Hatarote) Date :­09/05/2017 Dist. Judge­2 & Addl. It is surprising to note that during the course of cross­examination, this child witness has shown her natural conduct while answering the tricky questions also. In such situation, the possibility of tutoring is not sustainable. Moreover, the evidence of complainant mother Ranjana and the relative aunt Mainabai to whom the incident was disclosed immediately after the occurrence, also appears to be corroborating to the version of the victim. 15] The chance witnesses examined by the prosecution i.e. P.W.6 Archana Gaikwad and P.W.10 Shankar Pande have also whispered about the happening of something .. 11/­ .. 11 .. Atro. Special Case No. 54/2015 CNR NO. ­ MHTH060015252015 Judgment wrong with the small child of complainant. Thus, considering the nature of evidence adduced by these witnesses, it can not be doubted only because of they are close to the complainant family. I have already stated above that both the families are residing in the same area. Therefore, the neighbouring witnesses are similarly close to both. Thus, said evidence adduced on record can not be discarded by labelling it as evidence of close persons of complainant family. 16] Another fact of the present case is the medical evidence. It reveals from the prosecution that the victim girl was immediately referred to the concerned Medical Officer for her medical examination on point of alleged sexual assault. P.W.9 Dr. Seema Aravkar and P.W.12 Dr. Raju Lawangare are examined before the Court to substantiate physical assault committed by the accused and his capability to perform sexual act. No doubt, no visible injury is seen on the private part of the said victim or on the anal portion. However, the concerned Medical Officer has stated in clear words that while giving history of assault, the victim girl has stated that neighbouring known person committed penetrative sexual assault on the anal portion of the victim girl. .. 12/­ .. 12 .. Atro. Special Case No. 54/2015 CNR NO. ­ MHTH060015252015 Judgment 17] The Ld. Counsel Mr. Bhagat placed reliance on the defence witness i.e. Dr. Adwait Padhye, the Psychiatric practicing at Kalyan. It reveals from his evidence that accused Harishchandra Kamble was his patient and he had come to his hospital somewhere in the month of May, 2012 with a complaint of erectile dysfunction and premature ejaculation. It is deposed by this witness that said patient was suffering from depression since prior to four months of his examination. The Ld. Counsel Mr. Bhagat submitted that the alleged act levelled against the accused, is highly improbable as physical condition of accused clearly indicates his inability to perform such sexual act, and therefore, he can not be connected with the commission of such penetrative assault. 18] It is pertinent to note that the Investigating Officer has sent the accused for his medical examination immediately after the arrest. The concerned Medical Officer examined him and found no reason to show his incompetency to perform sexual act. Moreover, during cross­examination of defence witness Dr. Adwait Padhye, he has admitted that said patient has shown some improvements after the treatment. However, it was discontinued by him and therefore, he can not say firmly that said patient was capable to perform alleged sexual act. .. 13/­ .. 13 .. Atro. Special Case No. 54/2015 CNR NO. ­ MHTH060015252015 Judgment 19] The medical evidence brought on record by both the sides, is not of conclusive nature. However, the ocular evidence adduced by the victim and other supporting witnesses clearly established the alleged sexual act committed by the accused. It is pertinent to note that the age of accused is around 46 years old. Even if it is considered that he was suffering from erectile dysfunction and premature ejaculation, then it can not be said that he was mentally reluctant from the sexual lust. It is admitted position that the accused was alone present in the house. He dragged a small girl when she was passing from small passage of lane alone. The time of incident is of evening time i.e. around 7.30 p.m. Thus, all these circumstances and its cumulative effect clearly shows that to satisfy the sexual lust of accused, he dragged the tender aged girl into his house and by using his bodily force, he committed sexual assault on her. 20] It reveals from the provisions of Section 3 of POCSO Act that the penetration of penis, to any extent, into the vagina, mouth, urethra or anus of a child is sufficient to constitute the offence of sexual penetration. In this case, it is tried to demonstrate by the defence that accused was suffering from erectile dysfunction, hence penetration was impossible and improbable. Clause (a) of Section 3 of the said .. 14/­ .. 14 .. Atro. Special Case No. 54/2015 CNR NO. ­ MHTH060015252015 Judgment Act says that, penetration to any extent in vagina, mouth, urethra or anus is sufficient to constitute the offence. Therefore, full erection of penis is not condition precedent to estimate the act of penetrative sexual assault. Therefore, the defence of improbability on medical ground can not be accepted safely as other corresponding evidence is clinching against the accused. 21] Cross terms or enmity between the parties is two edged weapon either it can be used for false implication or it can be accepted as a mens­rea behind the act. In the present case, the evidence adduced on record clearly shows that the disclosure of the act of accused to her mother and relative witness Mainabai would not render her testimony doubtful. On the other hand, it appears natural conduct shown by the victim as well as her mother when they have reacted by scolding the accused after the disclosure. This aspect is discussed by our Hon'ble High Court in the case of Siddharth Sonde Vs. State of Maharashtra, reported in 2017, All MR (Cri) 4192. 22] The Ld. A.P.P. Smt. Patil/Bhamare has rightly placed reliance on the case of Rakesh Kumar Vs. State of H.P. reported in 2017 ALL MR (Cri) Journal 324 .. 15/­ .. 15 .. Atro. Special Case No. 54/2015 CNR NO. ­ MHTH060015252015 Judgment submitting that the testimony of the victim child witness is trustworthy as her competency to tell the truth, is ensured before the Court through the entire examination, including cross. 23] Considering the cogent evidence adduced by the complainant and her victim daughter supported with independent witness Mainabai, leads me to infer that the ocular of incident is proved with consistent evidence. Absence of injury on the anal part of the victim will not affect the trustworthiness of said evidence. The act alleged to be committed by the accused by closing the door of his house and by gagging the mouth of victim clearly indicates his culpable mental state. Therefore, the presumption laid down under Section 30 of POCSO Act can be made applicable to the facts and circumstances of this case. It is surprising to note that the defence failed to rebut the said presumption nor any attempt was made to that effect. Moreover, the offence alleged to be committed by the accused falls within the ambit of Sections 3 and 5 of the said POCSO Act. Therefore, the presumption under Section 29 of POCSO Act regarding the commission of offence at the hands of accused, can also be raised. This important aspect is totally overlooked by the .. 16/­ .. 16 .. Atro. Special Case No. 54/2015 CNR NO. ­ MHTH060015252015 Judgment defence while shaking the evidence of prosecution. In such situation, I have no hesitation to hold that the accused has committed unnatural sexual assault with the victim girl below the age of 12 years. Therefore, he is liable to be punished for the same. With this conclusion, I have no hesitation to answer point Nos 1 and 2 in affirmative. POINT NO. 3 : 24] As I held above, the prosecution succeeded in proving the required ingredients of the offence punishable under Section 377 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 4 punishable under Section 5(M) of POCSO Act, and therefore, the accused is liable to be punished. It is pertinent to note that, penetrative sexual assault is proved with physical act committed by the accused with the victim. On the other hand, the accused failed to built parallel defence story of improbability and false implication. The prosecution has proved the alleged charge beyond all reasonable doubts, and hence, the accused is liable to be punished. But before awarding the sentence, it is my duty to hear the accused on point of conviction. 25] Heard accused Harishchandra Kamble in person. He is unable to explain on point of conviction. He tried to say .. 17/­ .. 17 .. Atro. Special Case No. 54/2015 CNR NO. ­ MHTH060015252015 Judgment again and again that he has not committed any offence. The Ld. Counsel representing the accused is called repeatedly, but remained absent. However, I am of the opinion that the opportunity of submission on point of conviction through Counsel is to be given to the accused. 26] On the other hand, the Ld. A.P.P. Smt. Patil/Bhamare submitted that the nature of offence being of heinous nature and against the moral turpitude, maximum punishment may be awarded to teach a lesson that such act should not be repeated in future. On the other hand, the Ld. Counsel Mr. Wasim Shaikh on behalf of accused submitted that the present accused being an under­trial prisoner is behind bar since last three years. Moreover, he has a family including wife and children. Thus, considering his marital status and period undergone in jail, a lenient view may kindly be taken. 27] Considering the submissions of both the parties and taking into consideration the proved act committed by the accused with the girl of tender age of 11 years old, I am of the opinion that showing too much leniency will definitely cause injustice to the victim. The provisions of POCSO Act are made stringent to curb such heinous acts from the society. .. 18/­ .. 18 .. Atro. Special Case No. 54/2015 CNR NO. ­ MHTH060015252015 Judgment Therefore, the punishment prescribed for this proved offence and the age and family status of accused, is to be viewed in balanceive nature to meet the ends of justice. It is pertinent to note that the punishment for proved offence can be extended to life or upto ten years, but such harsh punishment would ruin almost life of the accused. But some stringent teaching lesson should be reflected through the quantum of punishment. It is pertinent to note that the punishment for penal section 377 of the Indian Penal Code can be equated and considered with the punishment prescribed for the offence under Section 4 punishable under Section 5(M) of POCSO Act. This aspect is also liable to be considered while passing the quantum of sentence. With this conclusion, I answer point No. 3 accordingly and proceed to pass following order : : ORDER : I] Accused Harishchandra Kachruba Kamble, Age : 46 years, R/o. Jyotinagar Zopadpatti, Ayaregaon, Dombivali (E), District­Thane, is hereby convicted under section 235(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure for the offences punishable under Section 377 of the Indian Penal Code and under Section 4, punishable under Section 5(M) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for seven years with fine of .. 19/­ .. 19 .. Atro. Special Case No. 54/2015 CNR NO. ­ MHTH060015252015 Judgment Rs. 5,000/­ ( Rs. Five Thousands only), in default to suffer simple imprisonment for six months. II] The set off be given of the period undergone by the accused in jail since his arrest as per provisions of Section 428 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. III] Seized property i.e. clothes of the victim and accused being worthless, be destroyed after appeal period is over. IV] The accused being under­trial prisoner, is directed to furnish fresh P.B. of Rs.15,000/­ ( Rs. Fifteen Thousands only) in compliance with the provisions of Section 437(A) of the Code of Criminal Procedure V] Copy of judgment be given to the accused free of cost. 1 Cri.M.A.No.39/2016 Exh.1 ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN CRI.M.A.NO.39/2016 : 1] This is an application filed by the applicant Zipa Ragho Waghe under Section 457 of the Cr.P.C. for return of Bajaj S.W.P.,Black colour motorcycle bearing registration No.MH­43­AA­3475 seized in C.R.No.I­28/16 registered with Murbad Police Station U/Secs. 363,376,366 r.w. Sec.34 of I.P.C. and U/Sec. 3 & 4 of POCSO Act. 2] The applicant contended that he is original owner of the said seized Bajaj S.W.P. motorcycle. The applicant contended that he is the registered owner of the said motorcycle. He further contended that he has purchased the said motorcycle from Popat Govind Zate, R/at: Murbad and R.C.Book of the said motorcycle is also transferred in his name. He has contended that the accused No.1 Paresh is also using the said motorcycle. He has contended that his abovesaid motorcycle was recovered from the accused No.1 Paresh by police in the alleged crime. He contended that if the said motorcycle is not in use it would be damaged. The applicant prayed for custody of the said Bajaj motorcycle. He contended that he is ready to furnish necessary bond in satisfaction of the Court for return of the said motorcycle to him and abide with the terms and conditions imposed by the court. 3] The application is resisted by the I.O. by giving say at Exh.6. He has contended that the said motorcycle bearing No.MH­AA­ 3475 was used by the accused in committing the crime. He further contended that the accused has not produced the document showing its 2 Cri.M.A.No.39/2016 Exh.1 ownership and if the motorcycle is returned to the applicant there is possibility of misusing the same. He has also contended that the informant regarding the ownership of the said motorcycle is yet to be collected from R.T.O. Kalyan. The investigation is in progress. He has prayed for rejection of the application. 4] I have heard Ld.A.P.P. for the State and Ld.Adv. for the applicant at length. 5] Question arises whether the property could not be returned as specifically argued by learned APP Shri.Kulkarni that the seized property i.e. Bajaj S.W.P.Motorcycle bearing registration No.MH­43­AA­3475 is important piece of evidence. The photographs and the panchanama of vehicle said motorcycle prepared at the time of return to the applicant would serve the purpose to establish that it was used by the accused for commission of the crime and for that it cannot be allowed to remain at the police station. 6] On the other hand, the rejection of this application for return of the seized property would be against the directions and clarification of Their Lordship of the Apex Court in the case of Sunderbhai Ambalal Desai v/s State of Gujurat AIR 2003 SC 638 wherein the courts are directed to return the property after preparing detail property panchanama, taking photographs and bonds that such articles would produced, if required at the time of trial and that appropriate condition in that regard would be imposed. 3 Cri.M.A.No.39/2016 Exh.1 7] The applicant has filed on record the copies of Certificate of Registration of Motor Vehicle, Adhar Card and Ration Card. From the said copies, it appears that the applicant has purchased the said motor cycle from one Popat Zate and the motorcycle is also transferred in his name. If the said motor cycle is kept idle at police station, it would be of no use and furthermore no purpose would also be served by keeping the same idle in the police station. 8] For these reasons, I deem fit to allow this application as the fact is not disputed that the applicant has purchased the Bajaj S.W.P.,Black colour motorcycle bearing registration No.MH­43­AA­ 3475 from one Popat Govind Zate, which was seized from the accused in C.R.No.I­ 28/2016 registered with Murbad Police Station, and so he is entitled for its possession. In the result, the following order is made. ORDER 1. The muddemal property i.e. Bajaj S.W.P.,Black colour motorcycle bearing registration No.MH­43­AA­3475 seized from the accused in C.R.No.I­28/2016 registered with Murbad Police Station, seized from the accused be delivered to the applicant Zipa Ragho Waghe who is the owner of the said motorcycle, after preparing detailed and proper panchnama of the said motorcycle besides taking photographs of it and upon furnishing indemnity bond in sum of Rs.30,000/­ (Rs.Thirty Thousand only) with condition to produce the same at the time of trial, if required and shall not alter nature of the said motorcycle in any 4 Cri.M.A.No.39/2016 Exh.1 way whatsoever, alienate, or disposed of the same in any manner. 2. Issue letter to Murbad Police Station accordingly. 3. The application is accordingly disposed of. Kalyan. ( D.S. Ghumare ) Date: 24/01/2017 Addl.Sessions Judge, Kalyan.

Nayak Road, Shahad phatak. Native at : Harkisana Post­Utrola, Taluka­Ballampur, District­Gonda, UP State. .. Accused. Appearances : Learned A.P.P. Mr. Y.M.Patil for the State. Learned Advocate Mr. M.M. Deshmukh for accused. ..2/ ..2.. Special Case No.58/2015 Exhibit No.27 :JUDGMENT: (Delivered on 1st September, 2016) 1] The accused are facing trial for the offence punishable under sections 363, 366 r/w. Sec. 34 of the Indian Penal Code and under Section 3 & 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] The prosecution case in short is that­ Complainant Ali Ahmed Abbas Ali Hashmi lodged complaint on 13/02/2015 alleging that she is having one daughter and three sons. His daughter Sajida Khatun was taking education in 8th standard in Sadhubella School. Sajida was having one friend named Sarita and both of them used to attend the same school. On 13/02/2015 at about 07:00 a.m. Sajida and her friend Sarita went to the school but did not return upto 05:00 p.m. Complainant and parents of Sarita have searched them but they could not collect them. Therefore the complainant lodged complaint against the unknown persons. 3] On the basis of complaint lodged by complainant C.R.No.I­82/2015 for the offence punishable under section 363, 366 r/w. Sec. 34 of Indian Penal Code and Section 3 & 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 ..3/ ..3.. Special Case No.58/2015 Exhibit No.27 came to be registered against accused. During investigation, IO recorded statements of the witnesses, statement of victims and statements of accused, drawn seizure and spot panchanamas, prepared muddemal receipts, obtained certificate from the school of victims. After due investigation, chargesheet came to be filed before JMFC. As the offences are triable by the Sessions Court, the case is committed to this Court. 4] After committal of the case, the charge was framed against the accused under section 363, 366 r/w. Section 34 of Indian Penal Code and Section 3 & 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 vide Exhibit 12. Its contents were read over and explained to the accused in their vernacular and accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. Their defence is that of total denial. 5] As there is no incriminating evidence against the accused, hence their statements under section 313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure are dispensed with. 6] Considering these pros and cons, following points arise for my determination. I have recorded my findings thereon for the reasons to follow­ ..4/ ..4.. Special Case No.58/2015 Exhibit No.27 NOS. POINTS FINDINGS 1 Whether prosecution proves that on 13/05/2015 at about 07:00 hours at Karotiya Nagar, Near Nana Dhamdhere, Ulhasnagar No.3 accused in furtherance of their common intention had kidnapped a minor daughter of complainant Ali Ahmed Abbas Ali Hashmi and her friend by taking them out of keeping of the lawful guardianship without consent of the lawful guardian and kept them at Titwala and committed an offence punishable under Section 363 r/w. Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code ? .. In the negative. 2 Whether the prosecution proves that on the aforesaid date, time and place the accused in furtherance of their common intention kidnapped complainant's minor daughter and her friend that they may be compelled to marry with accused Nos.1 and 2 respectively against their will or in order that accused may be forced them to illicit intercourse and thereby committed an offence punishable under Section 366 r/w. Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code ? .. In the negative. 3. Whether the prosecution proves that on the aforesaid date, time ..5/ ..5.. Special Case No.58/2015 Exhibit No.27 and place the accused committed penetrated sexual assault on victim girls aged 17 years and 13 years respectively and thereby committed an offence punishable under Section 3 & 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act ? .. In the negative. 4. What order ? As per final order accused are acquitted. : REASONS : 7] I am going to discuss all these points together as they are interlinked with each other and it will facilitate me to adjudicate the matter at once. AS TO POINT NOS.1 TO 4 : 8] In order to bring home guilt of the accused, prosecution has examined four witnesses namely, PW­1 Ali Ahmed Abbasali Hashmi at Exh.15, P.W.2­Sajida Khatun Ali Ahmed Hashmi at Exh.17, P.W.3­Jagdish Motilal Singh at Exh.19 and P.W.4­Sarita Jagdish Singh at Exh.21. The prosecution has relied on complaint at Exh. 16. 9] In the instant case, it is an allegation of the ..6/ ..6.. Special Case No.58/2015 Exhibit No.27 prosecution that the accused had kidnapped complainants minor daughter Sajida and her friend Sarita and kept illicit relations under the guise of marriage and committed penetrated sexual assault on them. 10] In this regard PW­1 Ali Ahmed Abbasali Hashmi (Exh.15) has stated on oath that his minor daughter Sajida and her friend Sarita went to the school but did not return home and they have searched them but could not collect them. He further stated that police have brought Sajida and Sarita alongwith accused Wahid from Nashik at the police station and therefrom they have collected them. It further reveals that the complainant who is father of victim Sajida stated that it did not happen that Sajida told him that she was kidnapped and raped at Titwala. Learned A.P.P. has cross examined him at length but nothing come on record to prove the prosecution story. 11] In the light of the above version PW­2 victim Sajida (Exh.17) has stated on oath that at the time of incident, she had been to the house of her friend after the school and therefore her father has lodged report and next day she arrived at her house but she has denied the factum of kidnapping and rape. She has denied all the allegations made against the accused. ..7/ ..7.. Special Case No.58/2015 Exhibit No.27 12] P.W.3­Jagdish Motilal Singh (Exh.19) who is father of victim Sarita do not know the date of birth of Sarita. He clearly admits that on 13/02/2015 Sarita had been at the house of their relatives and she came back within four hours and Sarita had not gone with the accused Akbar and they were having love affair. Learned A.P.P. has cross examined him at length but nothing come on record to prove the prosecution story. 13] P.W.4­Sarita Jagdish Singh (Exh.21) also admits that on 13/02/2015 there was no such incident that she was kidnapped by the accused and raped. Learned A.P.P. has also cross examined her at length but nothing come on record to prove the prosecution story. 14] On scanning the oral evidence of the prosecution, I find that all these testimonies could not certify that on the date of incident whether victim was minor. If at all the victim was major on the date of incident, then the offence of kidnapping is futile. The entire prosecution evidence discloses that the accused have committed no offence. 15] Considering all the facts, circumstances and available evidence on record, as there is no incriminating evidence against the accused, I hold that the prosecution has ..8/ ..8.. Special Case No.58/2015 Exhibit No.27 miserably failed to bring home the guilt of accused beyond reasonable doubt. Hence, the accused are entitled for acquittal. Consequently, I answer all the points accordingly and proceed to pass following order­ : ORDER : 1] Accused No.1­Wahid Jakir Hussain and No.2 Akbar Ali Khan are hereby acquitted of the offence punishable under sections 363, 366 r/w. Sec. 34 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 3 & 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 . 2] The bail bonds of the accused be continued for further six months. 3] Muddemal property being worthless be destroyed after appeal period is over. (N.M.Waghmare) Special Judge Kalyan under Protection of Children Date : 01/09/2016 from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, Kalyan. .. /

Common Order in Cri. Anti Bail Appln. Nos. 702/2017 and 703/2017 (Exh. 1) 2] The other co­accused Samip Patil, Nilesh Kale, Prathamesh Bhoir, Vinayak Patil, Mayuresh Patil, and Vishal Kapse are already arrested and charge­sheet is already submitted against them. The applicant/accused Javed Jumma Tadavi is arrayed alongwith the said accused on the allegations that, he has pressurized the victim girl and her mother to change their version in their statements under Section 164 Cr.P.C. by giving temptation of Rs. 1,50,000/­ cash and cheque of Rs. 2,00,000/­. It is further alleged that he has obtained some writing from the victim's mother on stamp paper under the title as 'Samjuti Patra' ( compromise will). Moreover, his master Deepak Bhoir has also tried to disappear the evidence against the accused. Moreover, they have given threat to vacate the tenanted premises of the victim family. Hence, this prosecution. 3] The applicant/accused came with the case that, his name is not mentioned in the FIR at the initial stage. Moreover, he has no nexus with the alleged commission of enticing the victim girl. However, she exaggerated the said act by implicating the applicant/accused on the above stated allegations. In fact, the applicant has no role in the commission of entire episode. The dispute regarding vacation .. 3/­ .. 3 .. Common Order in Cri. Anti Bail Appln. Nos. 702/2017 and 703/2017 (Exh. 1) of tenanted premises is given colour of criminal prosecution. Hence, prayed for the relief of pre­arrest. 4] This application is strongly opposed by the prosecution on the ground that the act alleged to have been committed by the accused is specifically reflected in the investigation papers. The documentary proof collected by I.O. and the visit of applicant/accused with the victim family is prima facie proved with cogent evidence. The victim family belongs to weaker section of the society. Moreover, the similar attempt was made by the applicant and his master Deepak Bhoir with the same victim when one Sarvesh Patil committed forceful sexual assault with the victim. Therefore, considering the active involvement of the applicant/accused in the commission of serious crime, it is submitted that the prayer for release on anticipatory bail may be rejected. 5] Heard both the sides and gone through the investigation papers including the documents relied by the applicant/accused. It is needless to say that the nature of crime prima facie reveals that it is regarding the victim girl belongs to the weaker section of the society. The alleged attempt of pressurizing the complainant to withdraw the allegations made against the main culprit, are well founded .. 4/­ .. 4 .. Common Order in Cri. Anti Bail Appln. Nos. 702/2017 and 703/2017 (Exh. 1) and supported with prima facie documentary evidence. Therefore, the act alleged to be attributed by the present applicant can not be said as remote activity regarding the crime. It is pertinent to note that, two separate offences are labelled against the present applicant alongwith the other co­ accused. Investigation is remained incomplete in respect of the role of the applicant/accused, and for that purpose, the physical presence of applicant/accused is needed before the Investigating Officer. If the applicant is set scot free, then there is again possibility of interference into the investigation of crime. Hence, considering the peculiar facts and circumstances of this case, I am not inclined to use discretionary power to protect the applicant/accused from arrest. Hence, following order : : ORDER : i] The applications for grant of anticipatory bail are hereby rejected. ii] Original order be kept in A.B.A.No. 702/2017 and copy of the same be kept in A.B.A.No. 703/2017. iii] Inform concerned police station accordingly.
