JUDGMENT (Delivered on 28th day of June, 2017) 1] The accused Mehtab Faiyyaz Shaikh stands charged for the offences punishable under Sections 377 & 506 of the Indian Penal Code besides sections 4 & 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences 2 Spl. Case No. 97/2014 Judgment Act, 2012 ( herein after referred to as POSCO Act for short). 2] The prosecution’s case, in brief, is that the informant PW 1 Fehmida Anwar Shaikh resided at Shankar Mukadam Chawl, behind wooden saw mill, Suchaknaka, Kalyan (E), Dist. Thane along with her husband and two sons Afsar and PW 4 victim boy. At the relevant time PW.4 Victim boy was aged 7 years and he was studying in second standard of Baba Bodse Hindi School. There were holidays in the school and so PW 4 victim boy was at his home. The informant PW1 Fehmida was sleeping in her house while PW 4 victim boy was playing outside the house in noon on 4/6/2014. PW.4 victim boy returned home crying and so when she queried as to why he was crying, he did not disclose anything to her and told her that he wanted to change his half pant (chaddi). Then she inquired as to why he wanted to change his half pant. And when he removing his half pant she saw that it was wet. So also on the buttock of PW 4 victim boy she found some sticky substance. She suspected something disgustful and so asked him what had happened. PW 4 victim boy thereupon disclosed her that the accused Mehetab had called him in the neighborhood room, where he was made to sleep facing to ground by him. Then, the accused Mehtab removed his half pant and by inserting his penis in his anus committed carnal intercourse upon him. PW.4 victim boy also told her that when he started shouting, the accused Mehtab pressed his mouth and threatened to assault him, if he would disclose about the incident to anyone. Then the informant PW 1 Fehmida asked him as to how many times he did same thing upon him, he replied 3­4 times at Suchak Naka, near the well and even in the neighbouring room. Thereafter, the informant PW.1 Fehmida disclosed the said incident to her husband. Thereupon, she lodged report against the accused with Kolsewadi Police Station. On the basis of her 3 Spl. Case No. 97/2014 Judgment report a crime against the accused for offences punishable under sections 377 & 506 of the Indian Penal Code besides Sec.4, 5(l)(m) & 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act,2012 was registered vide C.R.No.I­ 233/2014. 3] The investigation of the crime was conducted by P.S.I. Smt. V.K. Hire (PW.3). During the course of investigation she conducted the necessary panchanama of scene of offence. The accused was arrested in connection with the crime. The accused Mehtab as well as PW.4 victim boy were referred to the KDMC Hospital for necessary medical examination. PW.4 victim boy was then sent for medical examination to JJ, Hospital Bombay. The half pants of the victim boy and the accused were seized and same were forwarded to the Forensic Science Laboratory for chemical analysis. The blood and semen sample of the accused was collected and sent to forensic laboratory for analysis. After recording the statements of witnesses and on receipt of the medical reports, ultimately, on completion of investigation, I.O P.S.I. Smt. V.K. Hire (PW.3) filed final report under section 173(1) of Cr.P.C. in the Court. 4] My Ld. Predecessor framed the charge Exh. 21 against the accused Mehtab for the offence punishable under Sections 377 & 506 of the Indian Penal Code besides Sec.4 & 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. The charge was read over and explained to the accused. He pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. Upon completion of the prosecution evidence, the statement of accused U/Sec. 313(1)(c) of Cr.P.C. was recorded. The defence of the accused is that of total denial and false implication in the crime. 4 Spl. Case No. 97/2014 Judgment 5] The following points arise for determination and my findings are noted against each thereon for the reasons states herein below : POINTS FINDINGS 1) Whether the prosecution proves that the accused on Yes. and before 4/6/2014 at about 3 p.m. at Suchaknaka, in room near the house of complainant Sau. Fehmida Anwar Shaikh, within the jurisdiction of Kolsewadi Police Station, has committed carnal intercourse against the order of nature with a victim boy, aged 7 years ? 2) Whether the prosecution proves that accused on the Yes. above mentioned date, time and place committed penetrative sexual assault on minor victim boy, aged 7 years ? 3) Whether the prosecution proves that accused on the Yes. above mentioned date, time and place the accused on the above mentioned date, time and place, committed sexual harassment upon a minor victim boy, aged 7 years? 4) Whether the prosecution proves that accused on the Yes. above mentioned date, time and place, committed criminal intimidation by threatening a minor PW 4 victim boy with intent to cause alarm to him ? 5) What order ? As per final order. :REASONS: POINT NOS. 1 & 2 : 6] The prosecution in support of its case has examined in all five witnesses. They are the informant P.W.1­ Fehamida Anwar Shaikh, (Exh. 25), P.W.2 Sunita Panderpatte, (Exh. 29 ), PW 3 Investigation officer Smt. V. S. 5 Spl. Case No. 97/2014 Judgment Pawar (V.K. Hire) (Exh. 34), PW 4 victim boy (Exh. 49) and medical officer PW 5 Dr. Dattatray Vitthal Bhore (Exh. 61). 7] All the points are dealt with simultaneously to avoid repetition of discussion of the evidence, which is common for them. 8] Before examination of PW No.4 victim boy, he being of tender age, some questions were put to him, to ascertain his ability of understanding the nature and significance of questions. As he gave rational replies, his evidence was recorded after administering oath to him. PW 4 victim boy has specifically testified that he resided at Chakkinaka along with his mother and brother. His father does not stay with them. They reside in Ajij Chawl. The accused reside in vicinity of Ajij Chawl. He further testified that the accused Mehatab called him to the well in their locality. The accused took him to a room of one Dildar Uncle. The accused removed his pant and did dirty things. Then he deposed in clear words that the accused Mehtab put his organ used for urinating into his anus after removing his pant. He also testified that the accused Mehtab did this thing 2­3 times. He further testified that the accused Mehtab threatened him that if he told this fact to mother then accused would cut him into pieces. Later on he told this fact to his mother. 9] The Ld. Advocate Shri. Sawant for the accused submitted that the victim boy should not be believed for following reasons: (a) He is a tutored child witness and has testified at the instance of his mother the informant PW 1 Fehmida. (b) The incident had occurred at the room of Dildar and so in absence of evidence of Dildar the prosecution case should be 6 Spl. Case No. 97/2014 Judgment disbelieved. More particularly, when the informant PW.1 Fehmida had deposed that when the accused had sexually assaulted PW.4 victim boy, Dildar was sleeping in the room. (c) The incident had occurred in the crowded locality and in broad day light and as such the evidence of victim boy should not be believed without corroboration from evidence of in absence of independent witnesses. More so, when he is a child witness of tender age not exceeding 12 years. 10] As far as the above reason (a) put forth to disbelieve the evidence of PW.4 Victim Boy is concerned, it may stated that in Mangoo & Anr. v. State of Madhya Pradesh, AIR 1995 SC 959, their Lordships of the Apex Court while dealing with the evidence of a child witness observed that there was always scope to tutor the child, however, it cannot alone be a ground to come to the conclusion that the child witness must have been tutored. The Court must determine whether the child has been tutored or not. 11] After careful scrutiny I find that considering the evidence of victim boy it is not possible to say that he was just a tutored witness and simply deposing at the instance of his mother. He had unsubtly denied that he is deposing false at the instance of his mother. He specifically has stated in his cross examination his mother had not told him what he should speak before police. PW.4 victim boy was also cross examined at length but no where his evidence stood shattered. He had also clarified that the accused had sexually assaulted him at 2­3 times but he had not told this fact to his mother as he had threatened that he would cut him into pieces. Therefore, I find his evidence to quite natural and worthy of credence as it was not having any character of 7 Spl. Case No. 97/2014 Judgment tutored nature of evidence. 12] As far as the above reason (b) about absence of evidence of Dildar, put forth by the Accused to disbelieve the prosecution case is concerned, it may be stated here that there was no point in examining Dildar uncle because he was not an eye witness and even otherwise the accused could not have sexually assaulted the victim boy in presence of his uncle. No doubt the informant PW 1 Fehmida had stated that accused Mehtab's uncle was present in the room when the incident had occurred, but he was sleeping. This statement itself is cannot be stated to be of any much significance because it might be that it is a mis statement of the fact. This might be due to the fact that she might have been overawed by the court atmosphere and jumbling of facts. And even otherwise the informant PW 1 Fehmida is not a direct witness to the incident. Further by no stretch of imagination it can be said that the accused could have dared to commit such a heinous offence in presence of his uncle. Even PW.4 victim boy has not stated that Dildar uncle was present when the accused sexually assaulted him. He has testified that the accused took him to the room of Dildar. Therefore, the aforesaid reason of non examination of witness Dildar by the prosecution, is without any substance. 13] As far as the above reason (c) put forth about absence of corroboration to the evidence of PW.4 victim boy to disbelieve the prosecution case is concerned, it may be stated here that now it is settled position of law that as a rule of Law there is no need of corroboration to the evidence of victim boy. The testimony of the victim and her witnesses in such cases of sexual assault itself is vital and unless there are compelling reasons which necessitate looking for corroboration of her statement, the courts should 8 Spl. Case No. 97/2014 Judgment find no difficulty to act on the testimony of a victim of sexual assault alone to convict an accused where her testimony inspires confidence and is found to be reliable. 14] In this connection Ld APP Shri. Kulkarni rightly submitted that there is no need to corroboration to the evidence of PW.4 victim boy though he is child witness of tender age. In this connection, he rightly placed his reliance on the decision of the Honble Apex Court in the case of U.P. v. Krishna Master & Ors., AIR 2010 SC 3071, wherein their Lordships observed thus:­ “A child is always receptive to abnormal events which take place in his life and would never forget those events for the rest of his life. The child may be able to recapitulate carefully and exactly when asked about the same in the future. In case the child explains the relevant events of the crime without improvements or embellishments, and the same inspire confidence of the Court, his deposition does not require any corroboration whatsoever. The child at a tender age is incapable of having any malice or ill will against any person. Therefore, there must be something on record to satisfy the Court that something had gone wrong between the date of incident and recording evidence of the child witness due to which the witness wanted to implicate the accused falsely in a case of a serious nature.” 15] That apart, there is in fact corroboration to the evidence of PW.4 victim boy. First corroboration to his evidence is from the testimony of his mother­ the informant PW 1 Fehmida. And second corroboration is of medical evidence. 16] First it would proper to discuss the evidence of the Informant PW.1 Fehmida. who is the mother of PW.4 victim boy. Initially she testified 9 Spl. Case No. 97/2014 Judgment that at the time of incident her son PW 4 victim boy studied in Baba Bodse High School. On the day of incident it was holiday for his school. She further testified that the accused Mehtab used to visit to the house of his uncle Dildar Shaikh, who was her neighbour. She was sleeping in her room on 4/6/2014 and PW 4 victim boy was playing outside the house. He came crying to home. She asked him what had happened then he told her that accused Mehatab had beat him. She had declined that the accused had unnatural sex with her son PW 4 victim boy and due to that her child had come home crying. She further denied that the accused while performing unnatural sex had gaged mouth of PW 4 victim boy and threatened him not to tell it to anyone. However lateron, in view of application made by the Ld. APP at Exh. 51, the informant PW 1 Fehmida was recalled and again examined. The said application for recalling the informant PW.1 Fehmida was allowed as it appeared that her re­ examination was essential to the just decision of the case as earlier she had deposed under pressure. 17] After her recall, the informant PW 1 Fehmida testified that on 4/6/2014 at about 2.00 pm. PW 4 victim boy went outside house to play. When he returned home after half an hour he was frightened and his eyes were red. He was trying to take new pant from our showcase cupboard. His pant was wet and so she queried him whether someone had beat him. Thereupon, he told her that the accused Mehtab had made him to sleep on the ground and he had done bad thing with him and had pressed his mouth. He had also told him that if he tells about this thing to anyone, he would beat him. PW.4 victim boy had also told the informant PW.1 Fehmida that the accused had done the same thing with him many times. The informant PW.1 Fehmida further deposed that on that on the next day she went to the police station and 10 Spl. Case No. 97/2014 Judgment lodged the report. 18] The informant PW.1 Fehmida had testified how the victim boy had come home crying and how she had found his half pant wet. Her evidence is relevant under Sec. 6 of the Indian Evidence Act on account of its proximity of time to the act of carnal intercourse by the accused with PW.4 victim boy. Illustration 'A' to Section 6 makes it clear. It reads thus :­ "A is accused of the murder of B by beating him. Whatever was said or done by A or B or the by­standers at the beating or so shortly before or after it as to form part of the transaction is a relevant fact." 19] Here the act of finding of wet pant of the PW. 4 victim boy by the informant PW.1 Fehmida, her pronouncement that PW.4 victim boy was trying to take new pant from the cupboard and immediately after the incident PW.4 victim stating to his mother­the informant PW.1 Fehmida what accused did to him, are all circumstances so intertwined with each other by proximity of time and space that the statement of the informant PW.1 Fehmida becomes part of the same transaction. Hence, it is admissible under Section 6 of the Evidence Act. Thus under Section 6 of the Evidence Act, it is substantive evidence which could be acted upon with or without corroboration in finding guilt of the accused. 20] Ld. Advocate Shri. Sawant for the accused firstly submitted that the evidence of informant PW 1 Fehmida should not be relied upon since initially she had not supported the prosecution case and later when she was re­ examined she incriminated the accused. The informant PW 1 Fehmida's 11 Spl. Case No. 97/2014 Judgment evidence cannot be simply brushed aside even though initially she had turned hostile to the prosecution and had testified that no such incident of commission of unnatural sex upon her son victim boy. This because in her cross examination after her re­examination she has clearly reasoned that she had deposed initially falsely because many persons had approached her and told her to take the case back. She has also stated that the brother of the accused Ruksar had threatened her and also her son. Above all she also explained that even advocate Shri. Garud for the accused had sent her back three times from the Court and told her to depose false. In such factual matrix, it is quite natural for a poor woman to initially depose false and later on depose actually what had happened after gathering courage to speak truth. Actually, even it was found necessary to re­examine the informant PW.1 Fehmida as it appeared essential for just decision of the case as it was found in view of her affidavit Exh. 52 filed on record that initially she had testified false due to fear. 21] Next it was argued that the informant PW 1 Fehmida wanted the room belonging to the family of the accused and so he has been falsely implicated in the present crime. I do not find any substance in this contention to disbelieve the evidence of informant PW 1 Fehmida for two reasons. First reason is that it is not this is utter hopeless defense raised by the accused as it is not clarified as to what was the reason behind for requirement of the room of the accused when one would get accommodation on rent anywhere. Second reason is that the courts must, while evaluating evidence, remain alive to the fact that in a case of sexual assaults, no self­respecting woman would come forward in a Court just to make a humiliating statement against her child's honour such as is involved in the commission of carnal intercourse. In fact 12 Spl. Case No. 97/2014 Judgment there is inherent bashfulness of the females and the tendency to conceal outrage of sexual aggression and this factor cannot be overlook. 22] The prosecution has also relied upon the evidence of PW No.2 Sunita Panderpatte for corroboration to the testimony of PW.4 victim boy. She has testified that she is working as a member of Women Cell Committee. She was called by PSI Hire of Kolsewadi Police Station to police station for recording the evidence of child PW 4 victim boy of crime. Therefore, she reached to the police station. The PW 4 victim boy in her presence told that the accused had committed unnatural sex with him two to three times in his room and also near the well and had threatened him that he would beat him if he disclose that fact to anyone. She further testified that the mother of the PW 4 victim boy was also present at the time of recording his statement. 23] The aforesaid evidence of PW 2 Sunita is completely hearsay in nature and so I do not find proper to place any reliance on the evidence of PW 2 Sunita. That being so, her evidence stands completely excluded from consideration and as such, of no help to the prosecution to substantiate the charge against the accused. 24] The second corroboration to the testimony of the victim boy is from the evidence of PW 5 Dr. D.V. Bhore. He testified that he along with Dr. Hulhule examined the victim boy. At the relevant time Dr. Hulhule was on duty as CMO and he was the resident doctor at Forensic Medicine department. He further testified that he was called upon to advice and give medical opinion. He deposed that the mother of the PW 4 victim boy and the PW 4 victim boy himself had given alleged history of sexual assault. Upon 13 Spl. Case No. 97/2014 Judgment naked examination of PW 4 victim boy they didn't find any external injuries on his body. On local examination of anus of the victim, they found that there was no external injury over anal and perinatal region, no tear, no fissure, no piles, no scar. On digital examination of anal sphincter lateral traction test shows sphincter contraction. After his examination they collected anal swabs and blood in plain and EDTA bulb for chemical analysis. Thereafter, the report of examination of the PW 4 victim boy (Exh.62) was prepared by Dr. Hulhule and it was also signed by him. 25] PW 5 Dr. D.V. Bhore also testified that the victim boy was also referred to Pediatric Surgery Department where he was examined by the Medical Officer. On his examination, the Medical Officer noticed that the peri­anal skin of the PW 4 victim boy appears normal and there is no external mark of injury on perianal skin. There is a mild redness of mucosa and a small 0.5 cm. Mucosal breach at 3'o clock position. There is no active bleeding or dot at peri­anal region or anocutaneous junction. After history and examination concerned Medical Officer gave the opinion that the possibility of assault cannot be ruled out. Accordingly, the concerned Medical Officer issued report (Exh. 63) in his own handwriting. The said report was exhibited in evidence of PW.5 Dr. Dattatray Bhore. 26] The above medical evidence clearly suggest that there is possibility of sexual assault. No doubt, there are no external injuries, but then that itself cannot be a reason to disbelieve the medical evidence suggesting possibility of sexual assault. Had the medical evidence being of nature clearly pointing out that there is no possibility of sexual assault, then it could have been something different to say and reasonable to accept the contention of Ld. 14 Spl. Case No. 97/2014 Judgment Adv. Shri. Sawant that medical evidence disproves the prosecution case. In this regard it is also pertinent to note that the half pants were sent for chemical analysis to the Forensic Laboratory. The Forensic Report Exh. 66 states that semen was detected on the half pants. Thus, this is incriminating circumstances against the accused. Here it may be stated that Ld. Adv. Sawant has argued that even there is no penetration and so offence punishable under Sec. 4 of the POCSO Act is not attracted in the present case. He also submitted that likewise the offence under Sec. 377 is not attracted. As far as this aspect is concern, it may be stated here that Sec. 3 of the POCSO Act defines penetrative sexual assault. In this regard Clause (a) of Sec. 3 states that penetration to any extent is sufficient to constitute the penetrative sexual assault. So, the statement of the victim boy that accused put his organ used for urinating into his anus after removing pant, is quite sufficient to establish penetrative sexual assault and carnal intercourse. 27] In the present case in hand the accused had committed act of gross indecency with the victim boy. Even it could be argued that the victim boy was accomplice as there was no use of force in view of absence of major injuries on the anal part of the victim boy. It would be apposite to state here that it is unnecessary in case of the child of a tender years to ask for corroboration which could be ordinarily required in case of grown up persons. Their lordships of the Apex Court more than half century ago had laid down the rule of law that there is no rule of practice that there must, in every case, be corroboration before a conviction can be allowed to stand in such type of cases. (See Rameshwar Vs. State of Rajasthan, AIR 1952, S.C. 54. ) 15 Spl. Case No. 97/2014 Judgment 28] Much grievance is sought to be made about the contradictions in the testimony of different witnesses, particularly that of P.W. 4 as compared to the testimony of the informant PW.1 Fehmida. So also, the contradiction is stated to be in relation to the statement of the informant PW.1 Fehmida about presence of the uncle of the accused at the time of alleged incident of the sexual assault. i) That the informant PW 1 Fahmida had stated in her statement PW 4 victim boy was trying to take new pant from the cupboard whereas so has not been stated by him in his evidence. ii) The informant PW 1 Fehmida has stated that PW 4 victim boy had stated to her that he had done the same thing (sexual assault) with him for many times, whereas PW 4 victim boy has stated that the accused Mehtab had done that thing 2 to 3 times. iii) The informant PW 1 Fehmida has stated that the accused was playing outside in their locality whereas PW 4 victim boy stated that the accused had called him to the well in their locality before the incident. iv) The informant PW 1 Fehmida has stated that the pant of PW 4 victim boy was wet after the incident and so is not stated by him in his evidence. v) The informant PW 1 Fehmida has stated that her husband Anwar resided with her in Ajij Chawl, whereas PW 4 victim boy has stated that his father does not stay with them. 16 Spl. Case No. 97/2014 Judgment vi) The informant PW 1 Fehmida has stated that the accused at the time of making sexual assault had pressed his mouth, but so has not been stated in his evidence by PW 4 victim boy. 29] In this regard learned APP Shri. Kulkarni, has placed his reliance of the judgment of the Apex Court in the matter of Rammi alias Rameshwar v. State of Madhya Pradesh, MANU/SC/0596/1999 : 1999 Cri.L.J.4561 , and has submitted that the variance in the statements of the witnesses on irrelevant points cannot be sufficient to discredit the testimony of witnesses. Indeed, considering the fact that the charge was in relation to the commission of offence of unnatural sex and sexual assault defined under POSCO Act on a minor boy, the point as to whether on earlier occasion such assault had taken place many times of two­three times, is absolutely irrelevant and immaterial for the decision in the matter. Perhaps, the point regarding sexual assault more than once or repeatedly in such cases may be relevant if the accused was charged for aggravated offence under section 5(l) of the POSCO Act. As regards the difference in narration of the incident, even if there is some minor variance in the statements, the same cannot be of any assistance to the accused to persuade the Court to draw any adverse inference against the prosecution evidence or to discredit the testimony of any of the witnesses on that count. The evidence on both the points is absolute irrelevant for decision in the matter in question and considering the nature and satisfactory evidence on record in support of the charge, so called variance on the said irrelevant points does not discredit either the testimony of the informant PW.1 Fehmida or that of PW.4 victim boy. 17 Spl. Case No. 97/2014 Judgment 30] That being so, the learned APP Shri Kulkarni is justified in relying upon the judgment of the Apex Court in the matter of Rammi alias Rameshwar's case cited supra, wherein it has been clearly held that : "No true witness can possibly escape from making some discrepant details. Perhaps an untrue witness who is well tutored can successfully make his testimony totally non­ discrepant. But courts should bear in mind that it is only when discrepancies in the evidence of a witness are so incompatible with the credibility of his version that the Court is justified in jettisoning his evidence. But too serious a view to be adopted on mere variations falling in the narration of an incident (either as between the evidence of two witnesses or as between two statements of the same witness) is an unrealistic approach for judicial scrutiny." 31] The certificate issued by Baba Bodase Hindi Primary School Exh. 64 of the PW.4 victim boy clearly proves him to be of below twelve years of age at the time of the incident. It states his age as to be eight years at the time of the incident. 32] For the said reasons, the evidence on record clearly established commission of offence of carnal intercourse and sexual assault defined under section 3 of the POCSO Act for which the accused had been charged. There is nothing on record even to suggest remotely that the accused had been falsely implicated by the informant PW.1 Famida. Indeed, the material on record does not in any manner suggest false implication of the accused in the case and the evidence of the prosecution unequivocally points out the uncivilized and frightening experience that PW.4 vicitim boy had to undergo on account of sexual assault on him by the accused. Hence, point Nos.1 & 2 are answered in the affirmative. 18 Spl. Case No. 97/2014 Judgment AS TO POINT NO. 3 :­ 33] The prosecution has also further established that by removing half pant of PW.4 victim boy and even his pant the accused had even exhibited his part of body to be seen by the victim boy while doing sexual assaultt and so it is also the case of sexual harassment as defined by Sec. 11 of the POCSO Act, 2012. No doubt, it is the case of prosecution that the accused had sexually assaulted the victim boy but his those acts also do come under the ambit of sexual harassment defined in Sec. 11 of the Act. Therefore, I hold that the prosecution has also brought home the guilt of accused for the offence punishable under Sec. 12 of POCSO Act. Hence, point No.3 is answered in the affirmative. AS TO POINT NO. 4 :­ 34] The victim boy has specifically stated in his evidence that after committing sexual assault the accused had threatened him that if he would tell this fact to his mother, then he would be cut into pieces. This statement of victim boy is sufficient to hold that the accused had committed criminal intimidation by threatening the victim boy with injury to his person. Therefore, I hold that prosecution has able to bring home beyond reasonable doubt the guilt of the accused punishable under Sec. 506 of I.P.C. Hence, point No.4 is answered in the affirmative. 35 ] This takes me to hear the accused on the point of sentence. Kalyan. (D. S. Ghumre) Date : 28/06/2017 Addl. Sessions Judge, Kalyan 19 Spl. Case No. 97/2014 Judgment 36] The accused has submitted that the lenient view may be taken for imposing the punishment. Considering his age and that his parents are dependent upon him. 37] Ld.Adv. Shri. Garud for the accused submitted that the accused did not have any criminal antecedent and he is the first time offender. He also submitted that considering the age of the accused, it would not be proper to impose maximum punishment prescribed by the offence by law. He also submitted that the accused be imposed with punishment for the period he had already undergone in prison as a under trial prisoner by taking lenient view while imposing sentence. 38] As against this Ld.A.P.P. Shri. Sachin Kulkarni submitted that the offence is serious and deserves no leniency. He submitted that the offence is heinous and the victim of crime is a small child and as such, strict view would be adopted for imposing the punishment to the accused. 39] I have considered the rival submissions of Ld.A.P.P. Shri.Kulkarni and Ld. Adv. Shri. Garud for the accused. Even though the Ld.A.P.P. has argued that maximum punishment should be imposed upon the accused contending that it is heinous crime of rape on a innocent small child of tender age not more than 12 years, I do not find it justifiable to take stringent view to impose maximum punishment. This because there are following mitigating circumstances available on record, which justify minimum punishment prescribed by law : 20 Spl. Case No. 97/2014 Judgment i) First is that the accused is first time offender and is hardly of the age of 25 years. ii) Second is that the victim boy had not sustained any serious physical injuries to his person. iii) Third is that the accused appears to be swayed away by lust of sexual gratification at the time of offence. iv) Fourth is that the accused is sole bread earner in his family and the parents of the accused is dependent on the accused. 40] Considering the above noted mitigating circumstances, it would not be appropriate to award maximum punishment to the accused. On the other hand, it would be appropriate to impose minimum punishment prescribed under law. Section 4 of the P.O.C.S.O. Act provides that punishment shall not be less than seven years, if the accused is found guilty for the offence of commission of penetrative sexual assault. So also, Section 377 of I.P.C. provides punishment for unnatural offence may extent to 10 years or life imprisonment. Therefore, the accused Mehtab deserves punishment of seven years for offence punishable under Section 4 of the P.O.C.S.O. Act and also punishment of seven years for offence punishable under Section 377 of I.P.C. would be justifiable in the given facts and circumstances of the case. Besides the above substantiative punishment the accused is also liable for the punishment of fine of Rs.2,500/­ for each of the offence. The guilt of the accused Mehtab is also proved under Section 12 of POCSO Act and I deem fit to impose punishment of two years and fine of Rs.2,500/­ for the said offence. The guilt of accused Mehtab is also proved under Sec. 506 of IPC and I deem fit to impose punishment of one year and 21 Spl. Case No. 97/2014 Judgment fine of Rs.2,500/­ for the said offence. In facts and circumstances of the case the substantive sentence shall run concurrently. In the result, the following order is made : :ORDER: 1) Vide section 235 (2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the accused Mehtab Faiyyaz Shaikh is convicted for the offence punishable under Section 377 of I.P.C. and is sentenced to suffer Rigorous Imprisonment for the period of seven years and shall pay fine of Rs.2,500/­(Rupees Two Thousand Five Hundred Only) in default of payment of fine to suffer Simple Imprisonment for the period of six months. 2) Vide section 235(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure the accused Mehtab Faiyyaz Shaikh is convicted for the offence punishable under Sec. 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act,2012. and is sentenced to suffer Rigorous Imprisonment for the period of seven years and shall pay fine of Rs.2,500/­(Rupees Two Thousand Five Hundred Only) in default of payment of fine to suffer Simple Imprisonment for the period of two months. 3) Vide section 235(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure the accused Mehtab Faiyyaz Shaikh is convicted for the offence punishable under Sec. 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act,2012. and is sentenced to suffer Rigorous Imprisonment for the period of two years and shall pay fine of Rs.2,500/­ (Rupees Two Thousand Five Hundred Only) in default of payment of fine to suffer Simple Imprisonment for the period of two months. 22 Spl. Case No. 97/2014 Judgment 4) Vide section 235 (2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure the accused Mehtab Faiyyaz Shaikh is convicted for the offence punishable under Section 506 of I.P.C. and is sentenced to suffer Rigorous Imprisonment for the period of one year and shall pay fine of Rs.2,500/­ (Rupees Two Thousand Five Hundred Only) in default of payment of fine to suffer Simple Imprisonment for the period of two months. 5) All the abovesaid sentences shall run concurrently. 6) Out of the fine amount recovered from the accused Rs.7500/­ shall be paid to the PW 4 victim boy towards payment of compensation for injury caused by the offence under Sec. 357(1) of Cr.P.C. 7) The accused is in jail since 06/06/2014 and the said period undergone by him shall be given as set off U/Sec.428 of Cr.P.C. 8) Muddemal property clothes, being worthless, be destroyed after lapse of appeal period. No. 17 IN THE COURT OF ADDITIONAL SESSIONS JUDGE, KALYAN [ Presided Over by S.P. Gogarkar ] ATRO SPECIAL CASE NO. 63 OF 2015 State of Maharashtra ( Through Central Police Station, Ulhasnagar ) ( Cr. No. I­139/2015 ) ...Complainant Versus Ravindranath Jagdish Thakur, Age 29, Occ. Labour, R/o. Azadnagar, Room of Dinesh, Behind Panjabi Colony, Near High School, Ulhasnagar­3 ...Accused Offences punishable under Secs. 354, 323, 504, & 506 of IPC and Section 8 of POCSO Act,2012 ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ Mrs. A.B. Patil­Bhamare, Ld. APP For Complainant Shri Tidke, Ld. Adv. for Accused ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ 2 Judgment – Atro.Spl.C.No.63/2015 JUDGMENT ( Delivered on this 6th day of May, 2017 ) 1] Accused Ravindranath Jagdish Thakur, R/o. Azadnagar, Ulhasnagar­3 is prosecuted for the alleged commission of using criminal force to victim girl intending to outrage her modesty. He is also charge­sheeted for voluntarily causing hurt and for causing provocation to break public peace and for committing criminal intimidation to cause alarm or fear in the mind of victim. The accused is further prosecuted for commission of penetrative sexual assault on the minor child and thus Central Police Station, Ulhasnagar registered the offence vide Cr. No. I­139/2015 on the report of mother of victim­girl. 2] The story of the prosecution in short is that, the complainant Kiran Chakravarthy, the household lady resides at Barrack No.937, near Usha Kirana Store, Ulhasnagar­3. She has one daughter, aging about 9 years old, who is the victim of this case. On 20.3.2015, at about 5 p.m., complainant Kiran and her friend Sapna went to market. Her husband was sleeping in the house and the daughter Ritisha was playing with small boy Sai nearby the house where construction work was going on and pits were dugged. When complainant came back from the market with her friend, she noticed that her daughter Ritisha was in nervous mood. She came near complainant and started weeping. Complainant enquired with her, on which the daughter disclosed that 3 Judgment – Atro.Spl.C.No.63/2015 when she was playing with small boy Sai in the nearby pits, the accused­Uncle asked Sai to go to his house and then he caught hold the victim and kissed her forcefully at her neck. Then he fondled his hand at her nicker and tried to behave indecently . The victim­girl raised cry and ran towards the house. She did not disclose the incidence to her father. Thereafter, complainant took her towards the accused and asked her to show the said Uncle­accused. On seeing accused, the girl started weeping. The neighbouring persons gathered on spot. They caught hold the accused and started beating him because of his indecent behaviour. He disclosed the name as Ravindranath Thakur. Thus, police report was made and offence came to be registered accordingly. 3] PSO Central Police Station registered this offence vide Crime No.I­139/2015 on the report of complainant­ mother of the victim. Further investigation was carried out by PSI Mr. G.H. Shete. The accused was arrested. The Investigating Officer visited the spot of incidence and prepared spot panchanama by drawing rough sketch map. He has also recorded the statements of corresponding witnesses including the complainant. Victim was referred for medical examination. After receiving medical evidence and on completion of investigation charge­sheet came to be filed. 4] The accused appeared before the Court in response to the summons. I have framed charge vide Exh.9. It was read over and explained to him in vernacular. Accused 4 Judgment – Atro.Spl.C.No.63/2015 pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. The prosecution has examined only one witness. She did not depose anything incriminating against accused. On the contrary, she tried to say that the trial against the accused should be closed as early as possible. Considering the factual situation and the evidence of complainant herself, prosecution has closed its evidence by filing closing pursis Exhs.15 & 16. I have dispensed with the statement of accused under section 313 of Cr.P.C. as there is no incriminating evidence on record. Defence of the accused is of total denial and of false implication. 5] Considering the evidence on record and defence of the accused, following points arose for my determination and my findings thereon are as under for the reasons given below :­ POINTS FINDINGS 1] Does prosecution prove that the accused on 20.3.2015, in between 5 to 5.45 p.m., in front of complainant's house, Barrack No.937, Section 20, in front of Negative. Usha Kirana Store, Ulhasnagar, used crimial force to victim girl intending to outrage her modesty and thereby committed an offence punishable u/s. 354 of IPC ? 2] Does prosecution prove during the same date, time and place accused voluntarily caused Negative. hurt to victim girl and thereby 5 Judgment – Atro.Spl.C.No.63/2015 POINTS FINDINGS committed an offence punishable u/s. 323 of IPC? 3] Does prosecution prove that during the same date, time and place accused intentionally insulted and thereby gave provocation to victim girl Negative intending that such provocation would cause the said victim girl to break the public peace and thereby committed an offence punishable u/s. 504 of IPC? 4] Does prosecution prove that during the same date, time and place accused committed criminal intimidation by threatening Negative. victim girl with intent to cause alarm to her and thereby committed an offence punishable u/s. 506 of IPC? 5] Does prosecution prove that during the same date, time and place accused committed penetrative sexual assault on Negative. victim­girl and thereby committed an offence punishable u/s. 8 of POCSO Act,2012? 6] What order? Accused is acquitted. : REASONS : POINT NOS.1 TO 5 :­ 6] This prosecution is launched by the complainant who is mother of the victim­girl, who was aging around 9 years old, at the time of alleged commission of offence. It reveals from the FIR that the accused who was engaged in the digging of pits of nearby construction work was present 6 Judgment – Atro.Spl.C.No.63/2015 there in the evening time. The victim girl alongwith small child Sai were playing in the said pit. Accused expelled that small boy towards his house and then committed indecent behaviour with the victim­girl. He tried to kiss her neck, and also fondled his fingers on her private part removing the nicker. The victim­girl got frightened and raised cry. She succeeded in escaping from the clutches of the accused and went to her house. 7] The victim­girl narrated the incidence to her mother when she came back from market and was suspecting something wrong because of nervous mood of the victim­girl. Thus, it was a crime against small child alleged to be committed by accused committing sexual assault. 8] To constitute the child age, the prosecution has relied upon school I.D. card showing the date of birth as 18.12.2005. Moreover, this aspect is not seriously challenged by the defence also. It is pertinent to note that said age proof is not seriously contested or challenged by the defence. On this background, the oral evidence of the complainant is liable to be scrutinized. 9] The prosecution has placed reliance on the allegations of FIR which came to be exhibited by adducing the evidence of complainant­mother. It is pertinent to note that the complainant has identified her signature on FIR, but she denied the allegations mentioned in it saying that she has 7 Judgment – Atro.Spl.C.No.63/2015 not stated anything about the alleged commission of sexual assault. The portion marked of material omissions is rightly pointed out by Ld. Counsel Shri Tidke. 10] The medical evidence plays vital role in the case of sexual assault. In the present matter, seized clothes of the victim were sent for C.A. Examination, but surprisingly no positive evidence has come on record by the expert opinion. The oral evidence adduced by the complainant is totally contrary to the prosecution story. Moreover, the status of the victim girl is as small child. The complainant has furnished pursis Exh.15 stating therein that she do not want to examine her small child as nothing was happened as mentioned in the FIR. Therefore, non­examination of corresponding witness gave adverse effect to the prosecution case. 11] It is pertinent to note that at the time of alleged incidence, the victim was aging about 9 years old. She is not examined before the Court. Thus, the occurrence of alleged incidence remained unproved. Moreover, medical evidence is also not supporting to the prosecution story. Considering all these aspects, it appeals to my mind that the strict proof and required ingredients to connect the accused with the crime of sexual assault and outraging the modesty is not proved with cogent and consistent evidence. Moreover, the allegations of voluntarily causing hurt and insulting the victim by giving threats are also not proved at all. 8 Judgment – Atro.Spl.C.No.63/2015 Therefore, I have no hesitation to answer point Nos.1 to 5 in the negative. POINT NO. 6 :­ 12] As I held above, prosecution failed to prove necessary ingredients to prove the guilt of accused. Hence, he is liable to be acquitted giving benefit of inadequate evidence to prove the charges. In the result, I answer point No.6 accordingly and proceed to pass following order :­ ORDER 1] Accused Ravindranath Jagdish Thakur, Age : 29 years, R/at : Azadnagar, Ulhasnagar-3 is hereby acquitted under Section 235(1) of Cr.P.C. of the offences punishable under Secs. 354, 323, 504, & 506 of IPC and Section 8 of POCSO Act,2012. 2] Bail bond of accused stands cancelled. 3] Seized clothes being worthless be destroyed after the appeal period is over. 4] The accused is directed to furnish fresh P.B. & S.B. of Rs.15,000/­. In compliance with the provisions of section 437(A) of Cr.P.C. to abide himself to appear before Appellate Court in case of appeal is preferred by the prosecution. Judgment pronounced in open Court. [Through PI Kolsewadi Police Station]. ....Complainant. Vs. Vicky Parmeshwar Sakale, Age : 18 years, Occ.: Education, R/at : Mahatma Fule Nagar, Near Kadam Grocery shop, Suchak Naka, Shil road, Kalyan (E) District­ Thane ….Accused. Appearance : A.P.P.Smt. Aesankar for the accused Offences : ­ Punishable under section 376, 323, 506 of IPC & S. 4, 8 & 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act,2012 . :JUDGMENT: [Delivered on 28/10/2015, in the open Court] 1] The accused Vicky Parmeshwar Sakale is facing the trial for the offences punishable under sections 376, 323, 506 of 2 Spl. Case 68/2015 [J.] IPC & S. 4, 8 & 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] The case of the prosecution, in short, is as under : The victim is the real sister of the accused Vicky and residing with her parents and brother. Her father is labourer and her mother is working in Mahape Company at New Mumbai. They leave the house at 7 a.m. and 9 a.m. respectively. The accused and another brother Rahul are taking education with her in same college. After the school and the examination they all used to return home together. Her grand mother is residing in neighbour to her home and in the absence of her parents she used to pay attention towards them. On 1.4.2015 the examination of 7th std., was going on and on that day there was drawing paper for which she alongwith her brother(accused)and another brother Rahul attended the said examination and returned to the home. Her brother Rahul went to play out of the house. At that time she and the accused were only present in the house. At 5 p.m. the accused closed the door by latching inside and asked her to come to kitchen ota, however she refused. Then the accused started assaulting her by white waist belt and took her towards kitchen ota by dragging and made her to sleep. He then removed his clothes and committed forcible intercourse with her. When she tried to shout, he has pressed her mouth and threatened by saying that if she disclose the incident to anyone, he will assault her by belt. Two months also her brother (accused ) had committed sexual intercourse with her and at that time also she was beaten severely. Because of the threats she did not disclose the incident to anyone. However, it was unbearable for her and hence on 2/4/2015 at2­30 p.m., she disclosed the incident to her grand mother Sushila, who 3 Spl. Case 68/2015 [J.] in turn disclosed to her parents but they did not believe on her and started quarreling with her grand mother. In the morning of 3.4.2015 there was quarrel in between her mother and grand mother Sushila. Therefore, on 3.4.2015, she approached Manpada police station, Dombivali(E) without informing to anyone and narrated the incident. Manpada police took her to Kolsewadi police station for recording her FIR and her FIR was recorded in the presence of her mother Mangala Parmeshwar Sakale and grandmother Sushila Shivaji Dongare. 3] On 3.4.2015 PW­3 PSI Smt. Vrushali Sagar Pawar was on duty as PSO. She recorded the FIR of the victim at 1 p.m. as she was brought by Manpada police. At that time she was alone and not accompanied with any of her relative. Therefore, she called the grandmother of the victim and then recorded her FIR­ Exh.22.She then registered the crime at CR No.157/2015 under section 376, 323, 504 of IPC and Section 4,8 and 12 of the POCSO Act, 2012. 4] She carried out the investigation. The victim was not ready to go with her mother and hence she was taken with her grandmother at Rukminibai Hospital for her medical examination. The scene of occurrence panchanama was drawn as shown by the victim at Exh.23. AS the victim was crying and not mentally and physically fit, therefore she was taken to Balkalyan Samiti, Bhiwandi alongwith her letter Exh.24. On 4.4.2015 the accused was arrested. At that time his parents were saying that he is below 18 years, therefore, she collected bonafide certificate from Samyak Vidyalaya by issuing her letter Exh.25. The said Vidyalaya issued bonafide certificate of the accused as well as victim girl at Exh.26 and 27. She requested the Court to record the statement of the 4 Spl. Case 68/2015 [J.] victim under section 164 of Cr.P.C. Meanwhile the victim was again got medically examined in IMG hospital, Bhiwandi wherein she was found pregnant of two and half months. The parents of the victim though called but they did not consent for sonography test. She sent the blood sample, public hair and semen of the accused to FSL, Kalina alongwith her covering letter Exh.28. She recorded the statement of Sushila Dongare (PW­2). After collecting the statement of the victim recorded under section 164 of Cr.P.c., she filed the charge­sheet in this Court. 5] Charge vide Ex.12 was framed which was read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. The accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. His defence is of false involvement as per his statement recorded under Section 313 of Code of Criminal Procedure. Neither the accused stepped into the witness­box nor examined any defence witness. 6] Heard learned APP Smt. J. S. Lohokare for the State and learned Advocate Smt. K. H. Aesankar for the accused, at length. 7] The following points arise for my determination and my findings thereon are recorded against them for the reasons to follow:­ Points Findings 1 Whether prosecution has proved that on 1/4/2014 at about 17 hours, at Mahatma Fule Nagar, Near Kadam Gorcery Shop, Suchak naka, Shil Road, Kalyan(E), in the house of complainant, the accused committed rape on the victim girl, aged 16 years, punishable u/sec. 376 of IPC ? ..... Not proved. 5 Spl. Case 68/2015 [J.] 2 Whether prosecution has proved that the accused voluntarily caused hurt to the victim girl, punishable under S. 323 …Not proved. IPC? 3 Whether prosecution has proved that the accused committed criminal intimidation by threatening the victim girl with intent to cause alarm to her , punishable under Sec. 506 of IPC ? …Not proved. 4 Whether the prosecution has proved that the accused committed penetrative sexual assault on the victim girl, aged 16 years, punishable under Sec. 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 ? …Not proved. 5 Whether the prosecution has proved that the accused committed sexual assault on the victim girl, aged 16 years, punishable under Sec. 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 ? …Not proved. 6 Whether the prosecution has proved that accused committed sexual harassment on the victim girl, aged 16 years, punishable under Sec. 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 ? .. Not proved. 7 What order ? ….. Accused acquitted. REASONS : 8] To substantiate the charge, the prosecution has examined only four witnesses viz. P.W.1­ minor victim girl (Exh.15), P.W.2­ Sushila Shivaji Dongre (Exh.19), the grandmother of the victim, PW­3 PSI Smt. Vrushali Sagar Pawar at Exh.21 the IO, who carried out the investigation as usual and lastly, PW­4 Dr. Poonam Amarsingh Valvi (Exh.30), the gynecologist, Medical Officer, Rukminibai Hospital, Kalyan who 6 Spl. Case 68/2015 [J.] examined the victim on 3.4.2015 at 6 p.m.,in the presence of her grandmother Sushila and found that her hymen was intact and there was no external injuries noticed on the person of the victim. As to point No. 1,4,5 & 6: 9] I have taken all these points together for discussion, as they are interlinked. To prove the age of the victim the prosecution produced bonafide and character certificate of the victim at Exh.26 showing her birth date as 15/9/1998. This being a public document is admissible under Section 74 of the Indian Evidence Act and hence it was got proved through the mouth of IO PW­3 Smt. Pawar by the prosecution. The date of incident as alleged in the FIR is 1.4.2014. therefore, on the date of incident the age of the victim was 15 years 6 months and 16 days and hence she was minor. 10] For the offence of rape and penetrative sexual assault and sexual harassment, the testimony of the minor victim is material in addition to the evidence of her grandmother Sushila Dongare, to whom she disclosed about the incident and then Susila Dongare disclosed to the father of the victim. 11] The evidence of victim PW­1 shows that the accused Vicky is her elder brother. She has studied upto 7 th std. But now she left the school without completing 7 th std. At the time of incident she was not going to school. The accused was studying in 8th standard and younger brother in 6th std. In Samyak Vidyalaya. Her father used to do labour work at 7.30 a.m., and return at 8 p.m. her mother also goes for work at Vashi at 9­30 a.m. and she used to return at 8­30 pm. In absence of her parents she used to live with her two brothers in the house. 7 Spl. Case 68/2015 [J.] 12] At the time of incident there was drawing examination for which she and her elder brother (accused) had appeared . The timing was 7­30 a.m. to 8­30 a.m. After the said examination they both returned to home. She irritated , and therefore, she lodged case of rape against her brother Vicky. She had alone gone to Manpada police by foot and told to the police that accused Vicky asked him to remove her clothes. She has denied that she was taken by dragging up to kitchen ota and removed her clothes and accused committed sexual intercourse with her. She has also denied the threats administered by accused. 13] PW­2 Sushilia Shivaji Dongare is residing neighbour to her and has disclosed the incident to her. She has also denied the contents of the FIR but admits that she was sent for her medical examination and then kept in Bhiwandi Observation Home. Her maternal uncles Mahadev and Milind Dongare are residing near her house. Her house is owned by her grandmother. There are in all 15 persons in her relations including her family members residing adjacent to her house. The accused who is elder brother of the victim used to keep watch on them in absence of her parents. Some time she was visiting her friends in absence of her parents and at that time Vicky, the accused was not allowing her to speak with any boys. The accused used to search her and bring back home whenever she go to her friends without intimating anyone. On that ground, the accused used to assault her after bringing her at home from her friends as to why she went without intimating to anyone. Her parents are loving more to Vicky (accused) and therefore, she had grudge. She also disclose the said fact to her friends and that her brother Vicky never allows her to speak with any boys. She has named her friend as Papi, who 8 Spl. Case 68/2015 [J.] advised her to lodge the compliant against the accused Vicky but he never committed sexual intercourse with her at anytime. 14] It also reveals from the testimony of victim that she disclosed to her grandmother about quarrel on account of bringing milk as accused was suffering from epilepsy and had brought medicine but there was no money for bringing milk and hence there was quarrel between her and accused. There was also quarrel in between her mother and grandmother as there was no money to bring milk, hence her grandmother asked them to vacate her room. After the quarrel her mother had lodged the complaint against her grandmother as she has asked her to vacate the room. At that time her mother had brought police at the house of the grandmother, who asked her (victim), to come to the police station, if her mother and grandmother quarrels. The she went to the police station and lodged the FIR against her elder brother Vicky. Her maternal uncles Mahadev and Milind are not on good relations with her grandmother. She never disclosed anything to her grandmother. Twicely she was taken to the hospital by Smt. Hire Madam from Observation Home, Bhiwandi. On the say of Papi, the friend of the victim she lodged the FIR but this fact has not been mentioned either in the statement of the victim or before the Magistrate while recording her statement u/sec. 164 of Cr.P.C. 15] PW­2 Smt. Sushila Shivaji Dongare, has stated nothing about the incident as disclosed by the victim girl to her. The dispute in between her and mother of the victim Mangala, was on the account that she should give attention towards her children. This witness is the owner of the room where the victim is residing with her family members. According to this witness the financial 9 Spl. Case 68/2015 [J.] condition of Mangala, who is her daughter is poor and therefore she provided her room to them. The victim used to go to her friends without intimating her however her daughter in law and accused used to search and bring back the victim. At that time the victim used to give threats to the accused. On 3.4.2015 there was quarrel on account of vacating the room and then Mangala went to the police station due to which police had come to her house and gave an understanding to both. At that time police had asked the victim to come to the police station in case of quarrel. Milind Dongare is nephew of this witness but she had no cordial relations with him. 16] The medical evidence produced by the prosecution through Dr. Poonam Amarsing Dalvi (PW­4) shows that no external injuries were noticed onteh person of the victim who was not co­operating for her medical examination. Her hymen was intact and no injuries were noted on her private part. She has advised her for urine pregnancy test. She is then collected blood group, cross­match and finger nails and accordingly prepared case papers vide Exh.31. This witness has not internally examined the victim. In her opinion there was no sexual assault on the victim girl. After recording the history she obtained the signature of the grandmother of the victim on the case paper and register. 17] The CA report at Exh.16 and Exh.17 show the blood group “B” of accused and victim respectively but neither semen or blood detected on the clothes, nail clipping and pubic hair. 10 Spl. Case 68/2015 [J.] 18] Considering the testimonies of these witness, it is seen that no such incident had occurred as alleged in the FIR by the victim. On the contrary, it appears that the victim under angry mood approached the police and lodged serious complaint against her elder brother. Therefore, the prosecution has failed to prove by adducing cogent, reliable and trustworthy evidence, hence, I answer the point No. 1, 4,5, & 6, in the negative. As to point No. 2 & 3 : 19] None of the witnesses have stated about voluntarily causing hurt to the victim by the accused nor about criminal intimidation by threatening the victim with intent to cause alarm to her. The victim herself has not whisper anything abut the ingredients of these offences Hence, in absence of any evidence in this regard, I hold that the prosecution has utterly failed to prove the charges levelled against the accused. Hence, I answer point nos.2 &3 in the negative. 20] Resultantly, the accused deserve to be acquitted, and as such, I proceed to pass the following order : ORDER 1] Accused Vicky Parmeshwar Sakale, is hereby acquitted under S. 235(1) of Cr.P.C. of the offences punishable under Section 376, 323, 506 of IPC & S. 4, 8 & 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act,2012 2] The accused is in jail, hence he be set at liberty , if not required in any other offence. 3] No muddemal has been seized and produced, hence, no order is passed. 11 Spl. Case 68/2015 [J.] 4] The accused shall execute his P.R. and S.B. of Rs.15,000/­ to appear before the Higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect of appeal filed against this judgment as per S. 437­A of Cr.P.C. 5] Such bail shall remain in force for six months from today. Kalyan, [M.J.Mirza] Dt.­28/10/2015. Special Judge, Under Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, Kalyan

PSO of Ambernath Police Station registered the crime at C.R.No.I­281/2014 under Sec. 354­D, 323, 504 & 506 of IPC and Sec. 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 on 21/10/2014. The accused came to be arrested on 22/10/2014 under arrest panchanama (Exh.15). 5. Further investigation was carried out by W.P.S.I. Smt. M.B.Nerkar who drew the spot panchanama (Exh.14) shown by the victim. She also recorded the statements of the witnesses. After completion of investigation, she filed the chargesheet in this Special Court on 3/6/2015. 6. Charge at Exh.8 was framed by me which was read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. The accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. His defence is of false involvement as per his statement recorded under Section 313 of Code of Criminal Procedure. Neither the accused stepped into the witness­box nor examined any defence witness. 7. Heard learned Spl. P.P. Shri D.V.Bhangare for the State and learned Advocate Shri M.A.Dere for the accused, at length. 8. The following points arise for my determination and my findings thereon are recorded against them for the reasons to follow:­ Points Findings 1. Whether the prosecution proved that the victim was minor aged 17 .. Yes. years at the time of incident ? 2. Whether the prosecution has proved beyond realm of doubt that on 21/10/2015, at 8 p.m. at Shivlingnagar, Khamkarwadi, 4 Spl. Spl.Case 71/2015 [Judgment] Ambernath (W), the accused followed the victim and contacted her for personal interaction repeatedly despite a clear indication of disinterest by such victim and assaulted by fist blow on her left shoulder and abused her sister by saying “Randi” and threatened that she and her father will be defamed, punishable under .. Not proved. Sec.354­D(1)(i) of the I.P.C ? 3. Whether the prosecution has proved beyond realm of doubt that at the relevant time the accused voluntarily caused hurt to the minor victim, punishable under Sec.323 of .. Not proved. I.P.C. ? 4. Whether the prosecution has proved that at the relevant time the accused committed sexual harassment upon minor victim girl and abused her sister by uttering as “Randi”, punishable under Sec.12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual .. Not proved. Offences Act, 2012 ? 5. What order ? .. Accused acquitted. : REASONS : 9. To substantiate the charge, prosecution has examined in all three witnesses, viz. PW.1 Shekhar Hanumanta Koli (Exh.10), the 5 Spl. Spl.Case 71/2015 [Judgment] father of victim, PW.2 Smt. Sharda Shekhar Koli (Exh.11), the mother of the victim and lastly, PW.3 the victim (Exh.12), whose evidence was recorded in camera and she also knew the accused before the date of incident as there was friendship in between them. As to point No. 1 : 10. The victim has stated her age as 20 years during her evidence recorded on 5/12/2016 but she has not brought on record her exact birth date. The prosecution has produced on record the birth extract of the victim showing her birth date as 13/6/1998 issued by Ambernath Municipal Council on 17/11/1998. This birth extract being a public document falling within the purview of Section 74 of the Evidence Act, it is required to be exhibited unless the contrary is proved by the defence. The defence has not challenged the birth date of the victim during cross examination of any of the witnesses. Thus, the age of the victim at the relevant time was 16 years, 11 months & 4 days in view of the incident occurred on 21/10/2015. Therefore, I answer the point No.1, in the affirmative. As to point No.2, 3 & 4 :­ 11. As all these points are interlinked with each other, hence I discuss these points together to avoid repetition. 12. The best witness is the victim to depose about the incident. The victim being minor and in view of Sec.37 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, the trial was conducted in camera under child ­ friendly atmosphere. The age of the victim was 16 years & 11 months at the relevant time and hence, she was of the age of understanding. An oath was administered to her in view of her age and understanding capacity and also maturity. 6 Spl. Spl.Case 71/2015 [Judgment] 13. She has also brought on record that she knows the accused before the incident. Her father is car driver. She was studying in ITI, Ambernath in the year 2014 for Beauty Parlor Course. According to her, initially the accused was her friend but she denied the incident by stating that he was not stalking or caught­hold her hand nor assaulted her by fist blows on her hand nor he offered any gift to her. It appears that she had married with the accused having a child out of the wedlock. She has admitted her signature on the FIR (Exh.13) but not the contents. PW.1 Shekhar and PW.2 Sharda have also brought on record that the age of the victim was 18­19 years at the time of incident. Her father has brought on record that the victim used to go for casting vote. Before six months of the incident he found that the victim and the accused were talking on phone. He then talked with the accused and also assured him that he would speak with his parents about the marriage with victim. The victim had made phone call to him when he was on duty and asked him to go to the house of the parents of the accused. According to him, the victim had never disclosed any incident alleged to have been occurred in mobile shop when her victim daughter and elder daughter have gone to recharge the mobile. The victim had delivered a baby. Her another daughter is given in marriage in Karnataka State. The accused had performed marriage with his victim daughter before one year with whom his daughter is residing and hence, he has no grievance against the accused. The mother of the victim had also denied that any such incident had occurred with her victim daughter. 14. Section 354­D(1)(i) of I.P.C. and Section 11(iv) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 requires any man who follows woman and contact or attempted to contact such woman to 7 Spl. Spl.Case 71/2015 [Judgment] foster personal interaction repeatedly despite a clear indication of disinterest by such woman and Sec. 11(iv) of the Protection of Children from Sexual offences require that a person is said to commit sexual harassment upon a child with sexual intent repeatedly or constantly follow or watches or contacts a child either directly or through electronic, digital or any other means. 15. For the purpose of commission of offence punishable under Sec. 323 of I.P.C. voluntary causing hurt with the intention to any person or with the knowledge that he is likely to cause hurt to any person and does thereby caused hurt to any person is said “voluntarily to cause hurt”. 16. Though the prosecution examined in all three witnesses including the victim who is the best witness to throw light on the incident but she has not supported the case of the prosecution in all respects. On the contrary she has denied the incident in toto. The parents of the victim have also not supported the case of the prosecution who were on the point that victim and her elder sister had disclosed the incident immediately to them. There is nothing on record to hold that the prosecution has proved all essential ingredients for the offences levelled against the accused. 17. The spot panchanama (Exh.14) and arrest panchanama (Exh.15) though admitted by defence but nothing incriminating has come on the record. It also appears that the victim who is married with the accused before one year i.e. after the incident and out of the wedlock the victim has blessed with a child. She is residing with the accused as his legally wedded wife. This may be the reason for the witnesses and the victim to avoid the conviction and sentence to the 8 Spl. Spl.Case 71/2015 [Judgment] accused. 18. Today teenagers are exposed to more sex related issues and lot of material is also available to them. Because of their impressionable age, girls and boys both may tend to get provoked and there can be a curious and very compelling demand of the body to get into such kind of relationship. Behavioural pattern of teenagers as biologically whenever the child turns into puberty, the child starts understanding his or her sexual needs. The nature of response depends on the upbringing, peer pressure, how civilized the environment is etc. Therefore, some sects of the community have acknowledged this biological factor and therefore, the early age marriages are performed in some religions or communities. Taking into consideration this social and biological factors, the law makers have considered the age of 15 as a age of consent when the marriage is performed. 19. Under the circumstances, the record reveals that, initially the victim and the accused became the friends and out of the friendship they have married. Absolutely there is nothing incriminating against the accused to hold him guilty for any of the offence. Hence, I hold that prosecution has utterly failed to prove the charges levelled against the accused by adducing cogent, reliable and trustworthy evidence, therefore, I answer the point Nos. 2 to 4, in the negative. 20. Resultantly, the accused deserves to be acquitted, and as such, I proceed to pass the following order : ORDER i) Accused Jalindar Kondiba Kamble is hereby acquitted vide Section 235(1) of Cr.P.C. of the offences punishable under Sections 9 Spl. Spl.Case 71/2015 [Judgment] 354­D(1)(i) & 323 of I.P.C. & Section 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. ii) His bail bonds stand cancelled. iii) No muddemal property has been produced before the Court. If any seized, it shall be destroyed after the period of appeal is over. iv) The accused shall execute his P.R. of Rs.15,000/­ to appear before the Higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect of appeal filed against this judgment as per S. 437­A of Cr.P.C. v) Such bail shall remain in force for six months from today. Kalyan. [M.J.Mirza] Dt.:­13/12/2016. Special Judge, Under Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, Kalyan.

Mr. M.M.Deshmukh for accused. : JUDGMENT : (Delivered on 26th September 2017). 1] Accused named­above is prosecuted for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 376 (2)(n) of the Indian Penal Code and under Section 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] Case of prosecution in brief is that informant is the mother of the minor victim girl. The minor victim girl is aged 17 years at the time of incident. The name of the informant as well as minor victim girl is kept secret. On 08.02.2017 informant lodged her report to police that on 06.02.2017 in between the period from 5.00 p.m. to 6.00 p.m. she had gone to market for purchasing vegetables. At about 6.00 p.m. she came back to the house but the minor victim girl was not seen in the house. So, she inquired from her younger daughter about the same who replied that minor victim girl told her that she is going out and she further informed her not to inform this fact to her mother. Thereafter informant along with her son and thereafter with her husband searched for the minor victim girl but she was not traced out. So, informant lodged her report to police that some unknown person kidnapped her minor victim girl from her lawful guardianship. So, initially on the report of the informant crime for the offences punishable under Section 363 of I.P.C. was registered by Central 3 Spl. Case No.49/2017 (Judgment) Police Station vide crime No.I­34/2017. 3] However, during the investigation it is disclosed that there was love affair between the minor victim girl and the accused and that the minor victim girl with accused fled to Boisar and thereafter she along with accused by taking room on rental basis resided there at Dhalani Nagar, Boisar up to 15.02.2017 and in the meantime physical relation took place between them. On 16.02.2017 police arrested the accused with the minor victim girl. Police took personal search. Police drew arrest panchnama of the accused. Police recorded statement of witnesses. Medical examination of the minor victim girl was conducted. In the medical examination the report of doctor shows that hymen was torn. Medical examination of accused was also conducted. Panchnama of the place where accused with victim girl stayed was drawn. Statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. of the victim girl was recorded before learned J.M.F.C. Court No.3, Kalyan. After completion of investigation charge­sheet was filed. 4] Charge at Exh.4 under Sections 363, 376 (2) (n) of the Indian Penal Code and Section 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offcences Act, 2012 was framed against accused. Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 5] After recording evidence and hearing both the sides following points arise for my determination and I have noted my findings against each of them for the reason to follow:­ 4 Spl. Case No.49/2017 (Judgment) Points Findings 1. Whether it is proved by prosecution that accused kidnapped informant's minor daughter i.e. the victim girl .. Not proved. from her lawful guardianship ? 2. Whether it is proved by prosecution that accused repeatedly committed rape on the informant's minor .. Not proved. daughter i.e. the victim girl ? 3. Whether it is proved by prosecution that accused committed aggravated penetrative sexual assault on the .. Not proved. minor daughter of the informant ? 4. What offences, if any are proved .. No offence is proved against against accused ? accused. : REASONS : As to Point Nos.1 to 4 :­ 6] Perusal of the evidence of the informant (P.W.1) shows that she has deposed that the age of her daughter i.e. the minor victim girl is 19 years and the educational qualification of her daughter is upto 10th standard. Her evidence further shows that on 06.02.2017 at about 6.00 p.m. in a fit of anger her daughter left 5 Spl. Case No.49/2017 (Judgment) the house and went to their relatives. She searched for her minor victim daughter but her minor daughter was not traced out and in that respect she lodged complaint to the police station. She has identified her signature on the complaint. But she has deposed that she does not know about its contents. She is cross­examined by learned APP but she has not supported the prosecution case. So, it can be said that she has not supported the prosecution case. 7] Perusal of the evidence of minor victim girl (P.W.2) shows that her educational qualification is upto 10 th standard. Her evidence shows that she does not know the accused and that she does not know anything about the incident and that police did not record her statement and that the learned J.M.F.C. of Ulhasnagar Court did not record her statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. She has identified her signature and signature of her mother and father on her statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. by the learned J.M.F.C., Ulhasnagar. But she has deposed that its contents are not true. She is cross­examined by learned APP but nothing is brought on record to show that she has supported the prosecution case. She has also denied that doctor of Central Hospital examined her medically. She has further denied the suggestion that she along with accused filed one affidavit and in that affidavit she stated her age as 20 years. So it can be said that the minor victim girl has also not supported the prosecution case. 8] It can be said that prosecution has failed to prove its case. Accordingly, my answer to point Nos.1 to 3 is not proved and my 6 Spl. Case No.49/2017 (Judgment) answer to point No.4 is that no offence is proved against accused. Consequently, accused is entitled for acquittal. Hence, I pass following order:­ : ORDER : i. Accused viz. Ramchandar Jaykaran Yadav is hereby acquitted of the offences punishable under Sections 363, 376 (2) (n) of the Indian Penal Code and Section 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. ii. His bail bond stands cancelled and his surety is discharged. iii. Accused is required to execute bail bond of Rs.15,000/­ with one surety in the like amount under Section 437­A of Cr.P.C. to appear before the Hon'ble Higher Courts or Appellate Courts as and when the Hon'ble Higher Courts or Appellate Courts issue notices in respect of any appeal or petition filed against this Judgment and such bail bond shall be in force for six months. iv. No property is seized or produced in this case. Hence, there is no order in respect of muddemal property . Kalyan. (A.A.A.Shaikh) Date: 26.09.2017. Additional Sessions Judge, Kalyan.

Advocate Shri.Ingale for accused at length. I have perused the entire prosecution evidence and documents on record. Following points arise for my determination. My findings on those points are as follows for the reasons stated below : Sr.No. Points Findings 1. Does prosecution prove that on the date of incident i.e. on 31/12/2013 .. This date of birth is not at all challenged by the accused during the cross­ examination of any prosecution witness. No reason to discard the evidence of P.W.1 Shraddha regarding her date of birth.
