Informant lodged her report to police that on 08.12.2015 at about 11.30 noon she was walking towards the brick­kiln at Khutghar wherein her parents were working as labour. When she reached in between Hiv to Andad village, at that time Rahul Kaluram Mengal, Sunil Budhaji Bhagat, Malhari Raghunath Kalchinda all residents of her village came there from her behind by sitting on motorcycle and that Rahul Kaluram Mengal was riding that motorcycle. Rahul Mengal stopped that motorcycle and all the three persons alighted from the motorcycle. At that time Rahul Mengal told her to come with them in the jungle but she refused the said proposal. Thereafter accused Rahul Mengal caught her left hand and dragged her towards her body and when she protested accused embraced her and touched her breast. At that time Sunil Budhaji Bhagat and Malhari Raghunath Kalchinda were instigating Rahul Mengal again and again to catch the informant. Malhari Raghunath (CNR NO.MHTH06­001655­2016) 3 Atro.Spl. Case No.67/2016 (Judgment) Kalchinda caught the right shoulder of the informant and dragged her towards him but informant protested against the same and thereafter informant started crying. In the meantime they heard sound of coming of motorcycle from a distant place. So they left her and they ran away by sitting on their motorcycle. Informant came to village Aadhand and at that time her maternal uncle Ravindra Chima Wagh asked her as to what happen and she narrated all the incident to him. Ravindra Chima Wagh caused her to sit on his motorcycle and took her to Doryacha Pada in the house of her grand­mother and left her there. Thereafter her brother called her parents. But after sometime Rahul Kaluram Mengal, Sunil Budhaji Bhagat, Malhari Raghunath Kalchinda came to the house of the informant and they threatened her that she should not inform the said fact to anybody otherwise they would assault her. When the parents of the informant came to the house she informed the said fact to her parents. Thereafter her father went to search those three boys but they were not traced out. So on the report of informant aforesaid crime is registered. 3] Police drew panchnama of the place of incident and also drew map and also took photo of the place of incident. In her further statement she has stated that those three boys come there by walking. Police recorded the statement of the witnesses. Police obtained bonafide certificate of the informant wherein her date of birth is mentioned as 06.08.2001. So, on the date of incident she was minor. Police also obtained bonafide certificate of Malhari Raghunath Kalchinda wehrein his date of birth is (CNR NO.MHTH06­001655­2016) 4 Atro.Spl. Case No.67/2016 (Judgment) mentioned as 29.10.1998 as this incident took place on 08.12.2015 and at the time of incident Malhari Raghunath Kalchinda was minor and it can be said that he is juvenile in conflict with law. So charge­sheet was filed against accused Nos.1 and 2 Rahul Kaluram Mengal and Sunil Budhaji Bhagat. Statement of the informant under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. is also recorded. 4] Charge at Exh.6 under Sections 354 & 506 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code and under Section 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 was framed against accused. Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 5] After recording evidence and hearing both the sides, following points arise for my determination and I have noted my findings against each of them for the reason to follow:­ POINTS FINDINGS 1. Whether it is proved by the prosecution that accused Nos.1 and 2 alongwith the juvenile in conflict with law in furtherance of their common intention used criminal force to the informant who is minor girl intending to outrage her modesty by catching her, hugging her and by pressing her breast ? .. Not proved. (CNR NO.MHTH06­001655­2016) 5 Atro.Spl. Case No.67/2016 (Judgment) 2. Whether it is proved by prosecution that in the house of informant at Doryacha Pada accused Nos. 1 & 2 alongwith the juvenile in conflict with law in furtherance of their common intention threatened to cause injury to the informant with intent to cause .. alarm to her ? Not proved. 3. Whether it is proved by prosecution that accused Nos.1 & 2 alongwith the juvenile in conflict with law in furtherance of their common intention committed sexual assault on the minor informant by touching her hugging her .. Not proved. and pressing her breast ? 4. What offences, if any are proved .. No offence is proved against against accused ? accused. : REASONS : As to Point Nos.1 to 4 :­ 6] Perusal of the evidence of informant's mother (PW­1) shows that she has three daughters and that her brother­in­law's wife and her father­in­law and mother­in­law and her three daughters (CNR NO.MHTH06­001655­2016) 6 Atro.Spl. Case No.67/2016 (Judgment) reside with her. At the time of incident her elder daughter i.e. the victim girl was studying in 7th standard and she was going to the school. The victim girl had gone to her aunt's marriage at her house and there she stayed for two days. At that time they were going to do the work of labour in the brick­kiln. The victim girl got frightened and she took the name of all the three boys. Police did not enquired with her about the incident. 7] She is cross­examined by the learned APP. She has not identified her thumb impression on the complaint. She has denied its contents to be correct. She has admitted that both the accused and juvenile in conflict with law are resident of their village. She has denied the suggestion that compromise has taken place between accused and them. So it can be said that she has not supported the prosecution case. 8] Evidence of the victim girl (PW­2) shows that her educational qualification is upto 7th standard and she can read and write. She alongwith her brother, one sister, parents and grand­mother and grand­father reside in her house. At that time in the year 2015 her parents were going to do work at brick­kiln. Her aunt's marriage was there and therefore she went to her aunt's house and she stayed there for one night. Under the circumstances, there is no evidence to support the prosecution case. 1 ABA No. 760/17 ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN A.B.A.NO.760/2017 This is an application for grant of anticipatory bail U/Sec.438 of Cr.P.C. filed by the applicants/accused under Sec. 363, 376, 506(2), 114, 115, 118 of I.P.C. besides Sec. 3 & 4 of POCSO Act registered with Mahatma Phule Police Station. 2] The applicants/accused has contended that applicant No.1 is the father of applicant No.2. They have no criminal antecedents. They contended that they are permanent residents of Gavrai, Tal. Matha, Dist. Jalna. They contended that the offence is occurred on 6/1/2015 and main accused Raj @ Nivrutti Kashinath Gondge was arrested on 1/5/2017. They contended that at the time of incident the age of victim girl is 17 years and 4 months, therefore, Sec. 363, 376, 506(2), 114, 115, 118 of IPC and Sec. 3 & 4 of POCSO are not applicable. They contended that because of previous quarrel, the mother of victim girl namely Usha Pandharinath Shinde had lodged false complaint. They further contended that the victim girl was married and now she is staying with her husband. They have contended that there is no need of their custodial interrogation. They further contended that they are permanent resident of Gevrai and there is no possibility of their absconding or tampering with the prosecution evidence. They further contended that if they are released on bail they would co­operate the investigating officer and their release on bail would not be prejudicial to the investigating machinery. On these amongst other grounds the applicants/accused have sought for their release on anticipatory bail. 3] The I.O. has resisted the application by filing his say 2 ABA No. 760/17 Exh.10 contending that the offence is serious. He contended that accused Dilip threatened the victim girl that she should give consent for relation with his brother Raj, or else, he would see her brother. He contended that the accused would abscond if released on bail as they are resident of Dist. Jalna. He also contended that the accused would tamper with the prosecution evidence if they are released on bail. He also contended that accused would create hindrance to the investigation if they are released on bail. On above grounds amongst others, I.O. wish to reject the application. 4] The Ld. Advocate for the accused Shri. U.R. Kulkarni submitted that the accused is residents of Geverai, District Jalna and at the time of incident they are not present on the spot. He also submitted that the accused have no concern with the crime and are falsely nominated in this crime. 5] Upon hearing both sides, I find that it would not appropriate to exercise discretion to grant anticipatory bail to the applicant/accused No.2 Dilip for more than one reasons : First reason is that offence is of serious in nature. Second reason is that in supplementary statement it has been specifically stated by the prosecutrix that the applicant/accused No.2 Dilip had threatened her that if she does not give consent to the accused Raj, then he would eliminate her brother with help of his friends. If this threat is considered, I do not find any justification to grant anticipatory bail to the applicant/accused No.2 Dilip. 3 ABA No. 760/17 Third reason is that the applicant/accused had not obeyed the order of this Court by giving attendance to police station. Fourth reason is that the nature and gravity of the accusations does not warrant anticipatory bail to the accused No.2, since it does not appear that the accusation have been made with object of injuring or humiliating the applicant/ accused No.2 by having him so arrested. Fifth reason is that the accusations against the accused No.2 Dilip are well founded and without custodial interrogation the crime would not be effectively investigated. Sixth reason is that the possibility of tampering with the prosecution evidence can not be ruled out because the offence pertains to rape on minor girl and is punishable with life imprisonment. Seventh reason is that there is need of custodial interrogation of the accused as the case pertains to rape on a minor girl and the present accused seems to have helped to main accused in commission of the crime.. Eight reason is that , ordinarily, arrest is a part of the process of investigation intended to secure several purposes. The accused in present crime is of serious offence and the accused could have to be questioned in detail regarding various facets of motive, preparation, commission and aftermath of the crime and the connection of other persons, if any, in the crime. Ninth reason is that in order to enable the investigation to proceed without hindrance and to protect witnesses and persons connected with the victim of the crime, to prevent his dis­ appearance to maintain law and order in the locality, the arrest of the accused No.2 Dilip is justified. 4 ABA No. 760/17 6] For the reasons stated here­in­above I hold that it is not a fit case to grant the anticipatory bail to the applicant/accused No.2 Dilip. Hence, the application of the applicant/accused No.2 Dilip for anticipatory bail deserves to be rejected. 7] As far as applicant/ accused No.1 Kashinath is concern, I do find that he is entitled for discretionary relief of grant of anticipatory bail. This I say for more than one reason First reason is that vague allegations are made against him that he has helped the main accused Raj in commission of the crime. No specific allegations has been made against him or it has been specifically stated as to how he had helped the main accused Raj in commission of the crime. Second reason is that no father would ever help his son in committing gruesome crime and it appears to be that applicant No.1 implicated in this crime just because he is father of the main accused. Third reason is that the applicant/ accused No.1 is resident of Gevrai, Dist. Jalna and as such, it is highly improbable that he would have help the accused in commission of the crime. Fourth reason is that the prosecution case itself is that the present accused had given shelter to the main accused Raj, despite knowing that victim is minor. To my mind to investigate this allegation, custodial interrogation is not necessary. The marking of attendance at the police station till filing of chargesheet would survive the purpose. 8] For the reasons stated here­in­above I hold that it is a fit case to grant the anticipatory bail to the applicant/accused No.1 Kashinath. 5 ABA No. 760/17 Hence, the application of the applicant/accused No.1 Kashinath for anticipatory bail deserves to be granted. In the result, the following order is made : :ORDER: 1) The application for anticipatory bail to applicant/accused No.2 Dilip @ Prem Kashinath Gondge, is hereby rejected. 2) The Mahatma Phule Police Station is directed that the applicant/ accused No.1 Kashinath Piraji Gondge in C.R.No.I­26/2015 registered U/Secs. 363, 376, 506(2), 114, 115, 118 of I.P.C. besides Sec. 3 & 4 of POCSO Act, in the event of his arrest, he be released on bail on furnishing his P.B. and S.B. in sum of Rs.15,000/­ by this order of anticipatory bail. 3) The applicant/accused No.1 Kashinath Piraji Gondge shall attend the Mahatma Phule Police Station, Kalyan on every Saturday from 11.00 am. to 3.00 pm. for one month. 4) Breach of any of the conditions shall entail cancellation of bail. 5) He shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any other persons acquainted with the facts of the accusation against him so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court to any other officer. 6 ABA No. 760/17 6) Breach of any of the conditions shall entail cancellation of bail. 7) Inform to the concerned Police Station, accordingly. 1 Spl. Case 75/2015 [Judgment] Presented on : 9.6.2015. Registered on : 9.6.2015. Decided on : 29.1.2016. Duration : Y. M. D. ­ 7. 21. IN THE COURT OF SPECIAL JUDGE, KALYAN AT : KALYAN. [Presided over by : M.J.Mirza] SPECIAL CASE NO.75/2015 Exh. No. The State of Maharashtra. Through : P.I. Tokawade Police Station. ....Complainant. Vs. Chetan Kachru Birhade, Age­23 Years, Occ. Education, R/at­ Jambhurde, Tal. Murbad, Dist.­ Thane. ….Accused. Appearance : Spl.P.P.Smt. J.S.Lohakare for the State. Advocate Shri. M.M.Deshmukh for the accused. Offences : ­ Punishable under Section 363 & 376 of I.P.C. and Section 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. :JUDGMENT: [Delivered 29/1/2016, in the open Court] 1. The accused Chetan Kachru Birhade is facing the trial for the offences punishable under Sections 363 & 376 of I.P.C. and Section 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2. The case of the prosecution, in short is as under : That PW.1 Smt. Shantabai lodging the missing report on 30/9/2014 2 Spl. Case 75/2015 [Judgment] stating therein that her victim daughter after breakfast went out of the house on 30/9/2014 at 8 p.m. under the pretext to fetch water near the well of the village. She had also gone to fetch the water. When she returned with water at that time she did not notice the victim in the house. When she enquired with her son Harshal he disclosed her that he did not know where she has gone. Then she took search of her victim daughter in the village and nearby area and also made phone calls to her relatives, but on enquiry her relatives disclosed that she did not come to any one. She has given description of victim daughter in her missing report (Exh.­15). 3. After lodging the missing report she came to know from her husband, brother­in­law Ravindra and other relatives that on 15/5/2014 there was marriage of her niece at village Talavali and in the said marriage, the accused Chetan Kachru Birhade, r/at.­ Jambhurde, Tal. Murbad had come for video shooting of marriage ceremony and events and had seen the victim aged 17 years. She also got the information that the accused Chetan Kachru Birhade had induced and kidnapped her minor daughter. When her brother­in­law Ravindra made enquiry in village Jambhurde, he came to know that accused Chetan was also absconding since the time of missing of the minor victim. 4. P.S.O. registered the crime at C.R. No.I­84/2014, under Section 363 & 376 of I.P.C. and Section 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. The F.I.R. was recorded by P.S.O. Shri B.K.Salvi at Exh.­26 and then the investigation was entrusted to him. 5. He received the missing report at Exh.­15 and F.I.R. at Exh.­16 and also the birth certificate of the victim at Exh.­18. He drew the spot panchanama at Exh.­19. On 6/10/2014, he arrested the accused under arrest form. Then he recorded the statement of victim on 7/10/2014 in presence of W.P.S.I. Smt. Andhare. On 9/10/2014 he seized the Hero 3 Spl. Case 75/2015 [Judgment] Honda motorcycle used by the accused during the commission of offence. 6. The victim was sent to Central Hospital, for her medical examination and accordingly he received the medical certificate at Exh.28. Then he applied Sec.4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. The accused made disclosure statement to show the place of occurrence and accordingly the panchanama was drawn. He received the C.A. reports at Exh.­23 & 24. After completion of investigation he filed the charge­sheet in the Court. 7. Charge Exh.12 was framed against the accused which was read over and explained to him in vernacular. The accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. The defence of the accused is of false involvement as per his statement recorded under Section 313 of Code of Criminal Procedure. Neither the accused stepped into the witness­box nor examined any defence witness. 8. Heard learned Spl. A.P.P. Shri Y.M.Patil for the State and learned Advocate Shri M.M.Deshmukh for the accused, at length. 9. The following points arise for my determination and my findings thereon are recorded against them for the reasons to follow:­ Points Findings 1. Whether the prosecution proved that the victim is below 18 years ? .. Yes. 2. Whether prosecution has proved that on 30/9/2014, at 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. on 5/10/2014 at Parhe and at Janagi Farm 4 Spl. Case 75/2015 [Judgment] House, Jambhurde, Tal. Murbad, District Thane, the accused kidnapped the minor girl aged 17 years from lawful guardianship of her parents, punishable under S.363 of .. Not proved. I.P.C. ? 3. Whether prosecution has proved that at the relevant time the accused committed rape on the victim girl, aged 17 years, .. Not proved. punishable under Section 376 of I.P.C. ? 4. Whether the prosecution has proved that at the relevant time the accused committed penetrative sexual assault on the victim girl aged 17 years, punishable under S. 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual .. Not proved. Offences Act ? 5. What order ? ….. Accused is acquitted. REASONS : As to point No. 1 : 10. The informant PW.1 Smt. Shanta Sudhakar Dalvi has denied the birth date of victim as 30/09/1998 in her testimony and the victim has stated her birth date as 30/9/1996. The prosecution has produced the school leaving certificate of the victim (Exh.18) showing her birth date as 30/9/1998. However, the victim has denied the birth date mentioned on the school leaving certificate. 11. The school leaving certificate at Exh.18 shows the name of the victim and her birth date as 30/9/1998. The oral testimony of both the witnesses cannot be believed on the reason that the best possible evidence of age of the victim as the school leaving certificate at Exh.18 showing her birth date as 30/9/1998. The incident occurred on 5 Spl. Case 75/2015 [Judgment] 30/9/2014 as per the case of the prosecution. Therefore, on the date of offence, the age of the victim was 14 years as per school leaving certificate. Therefore, I hold that the prosecution has proved that the age of victim girl was 14 years and was minor on the date of occurrence. Hence, I answer the point No.1 in the affirmative. As to point Nos.2, 3 & 4 :­ 12. I have taken all these points together as they are interlinked and to avoid repetition. The prosecution has examined only three witnesses namely PW.1 Shanta Sudhakar Dalvi, the mother of the victim at Exh.14, PW.2 the victim at Exh.17 and the last witness PW.3 P.S.I. Vijay Shankar Dhumal, who carried out the investigation of the crime after registering the F.I.R. at Exh.25. 13. According to both the witnesses namely victim and her mother that since last 20 years they are residing at village Talavali as deposed by PW.1 Shantabai. Her four daughters including the victim who is her second daughter, were residing at Talavali. The victim has studied upto X th standard. However, the informant has made out altogether different case by stating that her victim daughter quarreled with her and then left her house for which she lodged the missing report at Exh.­15. Initially she admits her signature on the missing report (Exh.15), but subsequently denied for the reason best known to her. She has also denied the F.I.R. lodged by her below Exh.18 and her signature thereon and also the contents. Though the Ld. A.P.P. has cross examined the informant at length but except denial nothing fruitful has been brought on record to hold the accused guilty by proving any of the ingredients of the offences charged against the accused. 6 Spl. Case 75/2015 [Judgment] 14. The victim admits that she studied upto X th standard in Bandalpada, Vibhag High School from which she received the school leaving certificate and marklist at Exh.18. At present she is studying in S.Y.B.A. She further stated that her mother had lodged the missing report about her as she had quarreled with her and left the house and had gone to stay with her friend. She has denied any acquaintance with the accused. She has also denied the contents of her statement. Though the Ld. Spl. A.P.P. has cross examined her at length but nothing useful material has been brought on record. 15. The investigating officer PW.3 P.S.I. Vijay Dhumal has carried­out the investigation as usual and proved certain portion marked in the missing report and F.I.R. of the informant and the statement of the victim. 16. The Ld. Advocate Shri Deshmukh for the accused has admitted seizure of clothes panchanama of the victim and clothes of the accused vide Exh.29 & 30 as genuineness thereof is not disputed. 17. The C.A. report at Exh.22 to Exh.24 are produced on record by the prosecution which are admissible under Section 293 of Cr.P.C. The C.A. certificate at Exh.22 shows no semen was detected on vaginal swab and anal swab. Vide Exh.23 the blood group of the victim is “AB” and vide Exh.24 the blood group of the accused is “A”. As no blood group or semen was found either on the clothes of the victim or accused including the pubic hair and vaginal swab it do not tally with the samples collected by the medical officer to show penetrative sexual assault or rape. 7 Spl. Case 75/2015 [Judgment] 18. Under the circumstances, the offence of kidnapping punishable under Section 363 of I.P.C. cannot be held to be proved only on the ground that the victim on her own accord had left her parents home, that too in absence of her mother and had gone to stay with her friend due to which the informant lodged the missing report. 19. So far as the offence of rape and penetrative sexual assault punishable under Section 376 of I.P.C. and Section 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 is concerned nowhere the victim has brought on record regarding the alleged rape and penetrative sexual assault by the accused on her at any time. 20. The medical certificate at Exh.28 is also admitted by defence wherein the history of assault has been recorded by the Medical Officer, Central Hospital, Ulhasnagar on 6/10/2014 at 5.10 p.m. The name of the accused is also mentioned who committed sexual intercourse with the victim on two occasions on 30/9/2014 and 1/10/2014. Regarding the type of hymen in Exh.28 the Medical Officer has marked “hymen torn”. Thus, in view of the medical report which shows that there was sexual intercourse but the victim has not named the accused, however, putforth her case that she is not acquainted with the accused and she had no occasion to accompany with the accused at any time. 21. Under these circumstances, the prosecution has utterly failed to prove the charges levelled against the accused by adducing cogent, reliable and trustworthy evidence, and as such I answer the point Nos. 2, 3 & 4, in the negative. 8 Spl. Case 75/2015 [Judgment] 22. Resultantly, the accused deserves to be acquitted, and as such, I proceed to pass the following order : ORDER i] Accused Chetan Kachru Birhade is hereby acquitted vide Sec. 235(1) of Cr.P.C. of the offences punishable under Sections 363 & 376 of IPC & Section 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. ii] His bail bond stands cancelled. iii] The interim custody of Hero Honda motorcycle No.MH­05­AR­ 2490, given on bond to the witness Tanaji Yashwant Gharat, dated 4/12/2014, stands cancelled. iv] No muddemal has been produced before the Court. If any muddemal is seized, it shall be destroyed being worthless after the period of appeal is over. v] The accused shall execute his P.R. of Rs.15,000/­ to appear before the Higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect of appeal filed against this judgment as per S. 437­A of Cr.P.C. vi] Such bail shall remain in force for six months from today. Kalyan, [M.J.Mirza] Dt.:­29/1/2016. Special Judge, Under Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, Kalyan.

It apart that insertion of his male organ is not proved nor it is reflected in the allegations of the F.I.R. However, he has committed the act with sexual intent which involves actual physical contact with a minor girl may it be without penetration. It reveals from the evidence of the victim girl Swarupa that when she entered into the house of accused and was giving call to her friends ( children of the house of accused) she found that they were not at home and Baba ( accused) was alone present there. She further deposed that Baba took her on cot, made her lie by removing her pant/leggings and then slept on her and ejaculated some dirty discharge. This evidence adduced by this child witness in examination­in­chief is tried to shaken or shatter during cross­examination. Some googly questions are put by the Ld. Counsel of the accused to which the child witness nodded her head in affirmative. The Ld. Defence Counsel tried to canvass it as clean admissions given by the victim girl. But as discussed in the catena of rulings that the evidence of child witness is liable to be scrutinized minutely as there is possibility of tutoring of such witness or carrying such witness elsewhere by googly questions. .. 16/­ .. 16 .. Atro. Special Case No. 76/2015 CNR NO. ­ MHTH060017482015 ( Judgment ) 20] The alleged incident narrated by this child witness can not be labelled as only tutored exercise of her mother. It is true, she might have been refreshed the memory of child with the incident took place prior to two years. But the evidence adduced by the said child witness can not be brushed aside only on the apprehension of tutoring by mother. The substance of evidence of child witness is liable to be considered in entirety. In the present case, it appears that the child witness has deposed the act of accused whatever she has experienced during the course of alleged incident. Therefore, I have no hesitation to believe the words of victim regarding the alleged commission of act committed by the accused. In the case of Satyapal Vs. State of Haryana, reported in LEX (SC) 2009 4 90 . It is held that the duty is cast upon the Court to see whether the evidence of child witness is convincing, consistent and truthful. In the present case, the child witness Swarupa has categorically stated the occurrence of incident without any exaggeration, and therefore, I am of the considered opinion that the accused attempted to commit rape by committing sexual assault on the minor girl with preparation of removing her pant/leggings. His determination to gratify, his passion to fulfill the lust of sex clearly indicates the act alleged to be attributed by him. .. 17/­ .. 17 .. Atro. Special Case No. 76/2015 CNR NO. ­ MHTH060017482015 ( Judgment ) 21] The Ld. A.P.P. Smt. Patil/Bhamare submitted that the complainant mother has no reason to implicate the accused alleging falsely, on the stake of the character of her own daughter. Mother would not use her own daughter to get rid against the accused. In the present case, though there is no penile penetration, but accused attempted to commit rape by way of sexual assault, and for that, he is liable to be punished. The reliance is placed on the case of Arif V/s. State, reported in 2017, All MR (Cri.) Journal 480. 22] On the other hand, the Ld. Counsel Smt. Pavshe attracted my attention towards discrepancies while conducting investigation of this crime, placing reliance on the case of State of Maharashtra Vs. Krushna Ridde, reported in Criminal Confirmation Case No. 3/2016, decided by Hon'ble Bombay High Court, Bench at Aurangabad. The Ld. Counsel Smt. Pavshe has demonstrated the variance in evidence regarding production of the clothes of minor child and the variance in description of the clothes seized from the accused. It is vehemently submitted that the so­called social worker Nanda Godambe instigated the complainant mother to implicate the accused in this false case by levelling serious allegations of sexual assault. It is further .. 18/­ .. 18 .. Atro. Special Case No. 76/2015 CNR NO. ­ MHTH060017482015 ( Judgment ) submitted that both the families are on cross terms because of their civil dispute on point of disputed open land. The family witnesses of the victim admitted the fact of their dispute. However, it is too hard to digest that to get rid of civil dispute, the mother will use her own daughter of tender age to implicate the accused in false prosecution. Moreover, the minor discrepancies during the course of investigation if revealed, but other evidence of the prosecution is convincing, then such discrepancies are not fatal to the prosecution case. 23] Therefore, the explanation put­forth by the accused is not acceptable to rebut the presumption as laid down under Section 29 of POCSO Act and it reveals from the proved act of the accused that he was having culpable mental state while committing sexual assault on a minor girl. In such situation, the presumptions laid down under Sections 29 and 30 of POCSO Act can be made applicable to the facts and circumstances of this case. 24] It reveals from the evidence of family witnesses that a child entered into the house of accused as usual, but accused took disadvantage of his loneliness in the house and tried to satisfy his lust of sex by preparing for sexual assault. .. 19/­ .. 19 .. Atro. Special Case No. 76/2015 CNR NO. ­ MHTH060017482015 ( Judgment ) The conduct of accused while removing pant/leggings of a small girl like his granddaughter and to make her lie on cot, clearly suggests his preparation and intention to attempt the rape by committing sexual assault. Moreover, C.A.Report shows semen stains on his full pant. Therefore, I am of the opinion that though prosecution failed to prove the charge of rape and penetrative sexual assault, but succeeded in proving the act of accused as attempt to commit rape by causing sexual assault on a small girl, ageing about 5 years old, and for that act, he is liable to be punished. With this conclusion, I answer point Nos. 1 and 2 in negative and point No. 3 in affirmative. POINT NO. 4 : 25] The accused is facing charge for causing provocation in the mind of complainant couple to commit breach of peace as he insulted them by giving filthy abuses and by assaulting them with stick. To substantiate this charge, the evidence of P.W.1 Pushpa and P.W.2 Namdev is important being victims of alleged insult and assault. But surprisingly, there is not even whisper on record regarding the abuses alleged to be given by the accused. Moreover, the stick used for the same, is also not seized by the Investigating .. 20/­ .. 20 .. Atro. Special Case No. 76/2015 CNR NO. ­ MHTH060017482015 ( Judgment ) Officer nor any convincing evidence is produced on record, and therefore, in absence of adequate evidence, said charge can not be said as proved. Hence, I have no hesitation to answer point No. 4 in negative. POINT NO. 5 : 26] As I held above, the prosecution failed to prove the charge of rape and penetrative sexual assault punishable under Section 376 of I.P.Code and Section 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. But the prosecution succeeded in proving the act of accused for attempting to commit rape on the minor girl by committing sexual assault on her, and therefore, he is liable to be punished for the offence punishable under Section 376 r/w. Section 511 of I.P.Code and for the commission of sexual assault under Section 7 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act punishable under Section 8 of the said Act, and thus, the accused is liable to be punished for these proved offences. 27] However, before passing the sentence of imprisonment, it is my duty to hear the accused and defence on point of quantum of sentence. .. 21/­ .. 21 .. Atro. Special Case No. 76/2015 CNR NO. ­ MHTH060017482015 ( Judgment ) 28] Heard the accused Krishna Isame and the Ld. Counsel Smt. Pavshe on behalf of the defence as well as the Ld. A.P.P. Mrs. Patil­Bhamare on behalf of the State. It is submitted by the accused that he is facing trial being under­ trial prisoner and he is in Jail since the day of incident i.e. from 24/03/2015. He has undergone sufficient period for his act, and thus, a lenient view may kindly be taken while awarding the sentence, and he may be given benefit of set off of the period undergone by him. 29] The Ld. Counsel Smt. Pavshe submitted that, the accused is the only bread earner of his family. The responsibility of his family and considering his age, minimum sentence may kindly be passed. 30] On the other hand, the Ld. A.P.P. Smt. A.B.Patil/Bhamare submitted that, considering the nature of offence committed by the accused, and to pass the message in the society for such offenders, deterrent punishment may be awarded. 31] On going through the record and proceedings, it reveals that, the accused is ageing about more than 55 years .. 22/­ .. 22 .. Atro. Special Case No. 76/2015 CNR NO. ­ MHTH060017482015 ( Judgment ) old. It means, he is touching to the age of senior citizenship. At the same time, it can not be ignored that the alleged act committed by the accused with the girl, who is in his blood relations like his granddaughter, ageing about 5 years old. The mental trauma sustained by the victim girl and her family can not be viewed lightly, but the attempt of rape is proved instead of the commission of rape. Similarly, penetrative sexual assault is not proved, but the sexual assault to satisfy the lust of his sex is proved with cogent and consistent evidence. 32] It is pertinent to note that Section 42 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act speaks about alternate punishment. It reads that where an act or omission constitutes an offence punishable under this Act and also under the provisions of the Indian Penal Code, then notwithstanding anything contained in any law for the time being in force, if the offender is found guilty of such offence, he shall be liable to punishment under this Act or under the Indian Penal Code as provides for punishment which is greater in degree. In this case, for the proved offence punishable under Section 8, the punishment is for three years rigorous imprisonment, it can be extended upto five years .. 23/­ .. 23 .. Atro. Similarly, for the offence of attempting to commit rape, half of the sentence of maximum sentence is prescribed. If greater sentence as envisaged under Section 42 of POCSO Act is considered, then the accused is liable to be punished. Minimum for the period of five years rigorous imprisonment with fine. Thus, considering the submissions made by the Ld. Counsel Smt. Pavshe on behalf of the said senior citizen accused, I am inclined to consider the quantum of sentence leniently. SESSIONS JUDGE & SPECIAL JUDGE, KALYAN [ Presided Over by S.P. Gogarkar ] SPECIAL CASE NO. 79 OF 2015 State of Maharahstra ( Through Kulgaon Police Station, Badlapur, Tal-Ambernath, Dist-Thane ) Cr. No. I-19/2015 ) ...Complainant Versus Vivek Vijay Pawaskar Age 19 years, Occ.: Nil, R/at : Savarkar nagar, Ward No.5, Near Datta Mandir, Vangani, Tal-Ambernath, Dist.-Thane. ...Accused Offence punishable under secs. 376, 504, 506 of the Indian Penal Code and under secs. 4 & 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 ----------------------------------------------------- Shri S.H. Ramteke, Ld. APP For Complainant Shri P.P. Dukare, Ld. Adv. For Accused ----------------------------------------------------- 2 Spl.Case No. 79/2015 [Judg.] ORAL JUDGMENT ( Delivered on this 13th day of August, 2015 ) 1] Accused Vivek Vijay Pawaskar stands prosecuted for the alleged commission of rape upon victim aged 15 years. Kulgaon police registered this offence vide Crime No. I-19/2015 under sections 376, 504, 506 I.P.C. and also under sections 4 and 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences, Act, 2012. 2] The story of the prosecution in short is that, victim girl resides with her parent at village-Wangani. She is begotten to her mother from her earlier husband but staying with her mother alongwith the second husband of her mother. The accused Vivek resides at village-Done. He is the son of Sarpanch Vijay Pawaskar and the Ex-student of Mahatma Phule High-School, Wangani. The victim-girl was taking education in the same school and in the year 2014 she was studying in 9th standard and her date of birth was 14/02/2000. 3] Accused Vivek used to wait for her on the way of her school. Their acquaintance turned into friendship and accused started meeting the victim regularly near the school premises and behind the Gram Panchayat Office, Wangani. On 11th January, 2015 accused Vivek took the victim-girl on his motor-cycle on the pretext of celebrating his birthday. He took the victim-girl behind Gram Panchayat Office in the open space. He has shown intimacy with the victim and proposed her for marriage. The victim also attracted towards the accused Vivek and their attraction and said calf love turned into physical relations. On that day accused committed intercourse with the victim-girl in the open space 3 Spl.Case No. 79/2015 [Judg.] behind Gram Panchayat Office. Thereafter he repeated same thing with the victim in the month of January and February. Thereafter on one occasion accused visited the house of victim on the pretext of proposal of marriage and when victim was alone in her house accused Vivek committed physical intercourse at her residential house. 4] The accused repeated said relations on the pretext of marriage promise. Lastly, on the occasion of Gudhi-Padwa victim- girl gave call him from public booth and asked him as to whether really he is going to marry with her. At that time accused flatly denied for the same and asked her to forget him. The victim-girl disclosed said fact to her mother and then matter was reported to the police. 5] PSO Kulgaon Police Station registered the offence vide Cr. No. I-19/2015 under the provision of POCSA and further investigation was carried out by P.S.I. Mr. Kore. The accused was arrested and his medical examination was done by seizing his clothes. Thereafter the clothes produced by the victim were also seized under seizure panchanama. The victim was sent for medical examination. The statements of corresponding witnesses came to be recorded. On receiving medical evidence including C.A. report and after completion of investigation he has submitted chargesheet before the court. 6] The accused appeared before the Court in response to the committal order passed by learned J.M.F.C. Court. I have framed charge vide Exh.2. It was read over and explained to him in 4 Spl.Case No. 79/2015 [Judg.] vernacular. Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. The prosecution has examined in all three witnesses in support of its case. I have recorded statement of the accused under section 313 of Cr.P.C.. Defence of the accused is of total denial and of false implication. 7] Considering the evidence on record and defence of the accused following points arose for my determination and my findings thereon are as under for the reasons given below :- POINTS FINDINGS 1] Does prosecution prove that, the accused in the month of January, 2015 and February, 2015, Kudsavara in the house of complainant and on No. open ground, committed rape on victim aged 15 years and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 376 of the Indian Penal Code ? 2] Does prosecution prove that, the accused on the aforesaid date, time and place, intentionally insulted and thereby gave provocation to complainant Kumari Priyanka Malesh Garude intending that such provocation would cause the said Kumari Priyanka Malesh Garude to No. break public peace and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 504 of the Indian Penal Code ? 3] Does prosecution prove that, the accused on the aforesaid date, time and place, committed criminal intimidation by threatening No. complainant Kumari Priyanka 5 Spl.Case No. 79/2015 [Judg.] POINTS FINDINGS Malesh Garude with intent to cause alarm to her and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 506 of the Indian Penal Code ? 4] Does prosecution prove that, the accused on the aforesaid date, time and place, committed penetrative sexual assault on Kumari Priyanka Malesh Garude, aged 15 years and No. thereby committed an offence punishable under sections 4 and 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 ? 5] What order ? Accused is acquitted. : REASONS : 8] In the present case the victim and her mother are examined to prove the allegations of the FIR. (PW 3) Santosh Thakur is a chance witness examined before the court being maternal uncle of the victim girl. Surprisingly no incriminating evidence is adduced on record by the said material witnesses. Hence statement under section 313 of the Cr.P.C. came to be recorded accordingly. From this background I have to decide whether required ingredients of alleged offences are proved or not. 9] POINT NOS.1 TO 4 :- It revealsed from the prosecution story that victim-girl was taking education in the school and the accused boy is the Ex- student of the said School. He being the son of the Sarpanch of the village is a young lad wandering without any fear in the village. He used to chase victim-girl on the way of her school and developed acquaintance with her. She also attracted with him and developed 6 Spl.Case No. 79/2015 [Judg.] affection and calf love. 10] On 11/03/2015 accused took the victim-girl on his motor-cycle to celebrate his birthday with her. He brought the victim on the open space behind Gram Panchayat Office of village- Wangani. He talked in sweet language with the girl and then gradually developed physical intimacy with her. He committed physical intercourse on that day on the pretext of celebrating his birthday. The accused boy repeated same things with the minor girl in the month of January and February, 2015 taking advantage of her teen age. The victim was studying in 9th standard and was unable to understand the consequences of her act with the accused. They involved repeatedly in physical relations and lastly on the occasion of Gudhi-Padwa the victim-girl gave alarm of caution to the accused boy asking him as to whether he is going to marry with her positively. The accused boy answered in negative irresponsibly. Then victim-girl got frightened and disclosed her relations with accused. 11] To constitute these allegations the evidence of victim- girl and her mother is of vital important, but surprisingly except acquaintance with accused both these material witnesses have said nothing incriminating against the accused. To constitute the offence under section 363, 376 the age of victim and the act of accused regarding sexual intercourse is important factor. In the present case neither the age proof is produced on record nor supporting witness is examined before the court. Moreover the physical examination of victim-girl and corresponding C.A. report are not conclusive to prove that sexual attack was committed on the said minor girl. On 7 Spl.Case No. 79/2015 [Judg.] the top of it the victim herself alongwith her mother turned hostile. Thus, nothing remained on record to prove the guilt of accused either under the provisions of I.P.C. or under the statue of POCSA. Therefore I have no alternative but to held that prosecution failed to prove the offence. The act of accused remained unproved. It reveals from his defence that he being the son of Sarpanch is falsely implicated to get rid of political rivalry. However no parallel defence is set up by the accused. Thus, I find no substance to see the present prosecution from that angle, but the prosecution itself failed to prove required ingredients of alleged offences and hence I have no alternative but to answer point nos.1 to 4 in negative. 12] POINT NO. 5 :- As I held above prosecution failed to prove necessary ingredients to prove the guilt of accused. Hence he is liable to be acquitted giving benefit of inadequate evidence to prove the charge. In the result I answer point no.5 accordingly and proceed to pass following order :- ORDER 1] Accused Vivek Vijay Pawaskar age 30 years R/of Savarkar nagar, Ward No.5, Near Datta Mandir, Wangani, Tal- Ambernath, District-Thane, is hereby acquitted under section 235(1) of Cr.P.C. of the offence punishable under sections 376, 504, 506 of Indian Penal Code and also under sections 4 and 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. 2] Bail bond of accused stands cancelled. 3] Seized property i.e. clothes of the victim and accused, being worthless, be destroyed, after appeal period is over. 4] The accused is directed to furnish fresh P.B. & S.B. of Rs.15,000/-. In compliance with the provisions of section 437(A) 8 Spl.Case No. 79/2015 [Judg.] of Cr.P.C. to abide himself to appear before Appeallate Court in case of appeal is preferred by the prosecution. 5] Judgment pronounced in open Court. AS TO POINT NOS.2 & 3 : 8] It is the allegation of prosecution that before the complaint, since April 2013 this accused being husband of maternal aunt of complainant committed rape on the complainant from time to time and thereby committed an offence punishable U/Sec.376(f) of I.P.C. and U/Sec.6 of POCSO Act. They have not deposed a single incriminating word against the accused. These witnesses are cross­examined by the Ld.prosecutor at length and suggested to these witnesses that accused committed rape on her. Further suggestions to that effect are flatly denied by P.W.1 victim girl Sayli and P.W.2 Mangal her mother. There is nothing incriminating against the accused in the oral testimony of P.W.1 victim girl and P.W.2 Mangal her mother. AVP/Atro. Spl Case No.54/2017 .....6/­ ..6.. Atro Spl.Case No.54/2017 Judgment There is no other oral evidence on record. 9] In the admitted documents also there is nothing incriminating against this accused. Seizure of clothes of the victim girl and the accused is admitted fact. That does not prove the alleged offence in this case. Similarly spot panchanama, birth certificate etc. are admitted facts. These documents do not any way proved the fact that accused committed rape on the victim girl. The existing oral and documentary evidence is not at all sufficient enough to connect this accused with alleged offence and proved his guilt beyond reasonable doubt. Therefore, I answer both points in negative. In conclusion, I pass the following order : : ORDER : 1. Accused Atmanathan @ Rajan Lazarus Lorence is hereby acquitted of the offence punishable under sections 376(f) of Indian Penal Code and under section 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2. Accused is in jail. He be released forthwith and set at liberty if not required in any other case or crime. 3. Muddemal property clothes being worthless be destroyed after the period of appeal is over. 4. Accused to furnish PR & SB of Rs.15,000/­ in compliance of Section 437­A of Cr.P.C. Kalyan. (D.S. Hatarote) 18/12/2017. Additional Sessions Judge,Kalyan. AVP/Atro. Spl Case No.54/2017 ...../­

1 Spl.Case No.112/2014 Judgment Presented on : 28/08/2014 Registered on : 28/08/2014 Decided on : 07/12/2016 Duration : Y. M. D. 2 ­ 3 ­ 10 IN THE COURT OF ADDL.SESSIONS JUDGE, KALYAN (Presided over by D.S.Ghumare) Session Case No.112/2014 Exh.No. The State of Maharashtra (Through Kolsewadi Police Station) .... Prosecution V/s. Sachin @ Narhari Nagnath Raut, Age­ 22 yrs., R/at: Sant Rohidas Mitramandal, Anandwadi, Katemanivali, Kalyan(E), Dist. Thane. .... Accused ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ Shri.Kulkarni Ld.A.P.P.for State. Shri.Gaikwad, Ld.Adv.for accused. ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ JUDGMENT (Delivered on 7th day of December , 2016) 1] The accused stands charged for the offence punishable under Sections 363,366A,376 of the Indian Penal Code and under Section 3 r.w. Section 4 & 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offence Act. 2] The prosecution’s case is that the prosecutrix Kum.Tanuja aged 16 yrs. had left the house on 13/6/2014 at about 6.00 p.m. without 2 Spl.Case No.112/2014 Judgment informing anyone in the house and as she was not found, a missing report bearing No. 29/2014 dt.13/6/2014 was filed by her mother informant P.W.1 Jyoti. Later on it was found that the accused Sachin despite having knowledge that the prosecutrix Tanuja is minor had enticed her away from the custody of her parents, on the pretext of performing marriage with her. Therefore, the informant P.W.1 Jyoti lodged report with Kolsewadi Police Station. On the basis of the said report crime was registered against the accused Sachin Raut vide C.R.No.I­ 257/14 for offences punishable U/Secs.363,366A & 376 of I.P.C. and U/Sec.3 r.w.Sec.4 and 12 of P.O.C.S.O.Act. 3] The investigation of the crime was conducted by A.S.I.Naikwade. He firstly sent the prosecutrix Tanuja for medical examination at Rukhminibai Hospital, Kalyan. The accused Sachin Raut was arrested in connection with the crime on same day. He was also got medically examined from Rukhminibai Hospital,Kalyan. During the course of investigation, the panchanama of the scene of offence Exh.11, and the panchanama of seizure of clothes of accused Sachin and prosecutrix Tanuja was prepared. The investigation officer A.S.I.Naikwade recorded the supplementary statement of the informant P.W.1 Jyoti and statements of other witnesses. He also got recorded the statement of the prosecutrix PW.2 Tanuja U/Sec.164 of Cr.P.C. In due course, the investigation officer collected the medical examination report of the prosecutrix PW.2 Tanuja and the accused Sachin from the medical officer of the Rukhminibai Hospital,Kalyan. He then collected C.D.R. reports in respect of telephonic calls between the accused Sachin and prosecutrix Tanuja from the Mobile Phone company. Ultimately, 3 Spl.Case No.112/2014 Judgment after completion of the investigation, the investigation officer submitted final report under section 173 of Cr.P.C against the accused in the court. 4] The Charge Exh.5 was framed against the accused for the offences punishable under section U/Secs.363,366A,376 of I.P.C. & U/Secs.3 r.w. Sec.4 & 12 of P.O.C.S.O.Act. The charge was read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. The accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 5] The following points arise for determination and my findings are given against each thereon for the reasons given thereunder. POINTS FINDINGS 1) Whether the prosecution proves that the accused on 13/6/2014 at about 6.00 a.m. at Milindnagar,F­Cabin, Katemanivali, Kalyan(E), kidnapped or enticed away a prosecutrix minor victim girl Kum.Tanuja Deepak Bhosle aged about 16 years, out of keeping of the lawful guardianship of her parents without their consent ? No. 2) Whether the prosecution proves that on the abovesaid date,time and place the accused induced a prosecutrix minor victim girl Kum.Tanuja Deepak Bhosle aged about 16 years to go from her house with intent that she may be forced or seduced to illicit intercourse with him ? No. 3) Whether the prosecution proves that from 13/6/2014 to 17/6/2014 in the hotel at Shirdi the accused committed rape on the 4 Spl.Case No.112/2014 Judgment prosecutrix a minor victim girl Ku.Tanuja Deepak Bhosle aged about 16 years ? No. 4) Whether the prosecution proves that on the aforesaid date, time and place the accused committed penetrative sexual assault on the prosecutrix a minor victim girl Kum.Tanuja Deepak Bhosle aged about 16 years ? No. 5) Whether the prosecution proves that the accused committed sexual harassment on the prosecutrix minor victim girl Tanuja Deepak Bhosle aged about 16 years ? No. 6) What order ? As per final order. REASONS POINT NO.1 to 5 :­ 6] To bring home the guilt of the accused, the prosecution examined in all three witnesses. They are the informant PW.1 Jyoti Deepak Bhosle, the prosecutrix P.W.2­ Tanuja Deepak Bhosle, P.W.3­ Deepak Baliram Bhosle. It may be stated here that P.W.1 Jyoti and P.W.2 Deepak are parents of the prosecutrix P.W.2 Tanuja who is minor victim girl. 7] The informant P.W.1 Jyoti Deepak Bhosle and P.W.3­ Deepak had testified that they have four daughters namely Kshitija, Tanuja, Komal and Sakshi. They had testified that their daughter Tanuja was taking education in 10th standard in Dyanmandir Highschool, Kalyan in 2014. They had also testified that on 13/6/2014 as their daughter 5 Spl.Case No.112/2014 Judgment Tanuja went to her friend's house had not returned, they lodged missing complaint with the police. Thereafter, they had not supported the prosecution case by deposing that it had not happened that the accused Sachin Raut had enticed away their daughter Tanuja on 13/6/2014. 8] The prosecutrix minor girl P.W.2 Tanuja Deepak Bhosle has testified that she is residing at Katemanivli alongwith her parents and three sisters namely Kshitija, Komal and Sakshi. She has testified that in the year 2013­2014 she was taking education in 10 th std. in Dyanmandir Highscool, Kalyan. She has further testified that she had given examination of 10th standard and in June there were results of the said examination. However, she also did not support the further prosecution case by deposing that it had not happen that at the time of send off of her school she was introduced with the accused and that the accused used to visit her house. She has also testified that it had not happen that she used to accompany the accused to Mall and used to roam together and that the accused Sachin Raut had enticed her away on 13/6/2014 and took her to Shirdi where he kept physical relations with her. 9] In such background of the testimony of the prosecution witnesses, it is rather unfortunate for the prosecution that prosecutrix PW.2 Tanuja, her mother­ the informant PW.1 Jyoti and her father P.W.3­ Deepak did not support the prosecution case. Therefore, Ld.A.P.P. Shri.Kulkarni declared them as hostile witnesses and cross­ examined them at length. When they are confronted with their earlier statement wherein they incriminated the accused they denied having 6 Spl.Case No.112/2014 Judgment made. The searching cross­examination of these witnesses by Ld.A.P.P. did not yield any benefit to the prosecution as nothing material was elicited there from incriminating against the accused. Thus, there is no evidence against the accused to substantiate the charge against him of commission of rape upon the prosecutrix P.W.2 Tanuja under the pretext of marriage, against her will. 10] Here it may be stated that no purpose would have been served by examining I.O. A.S.I.Naikwade, as the material witnesses of the prosecution failed to support the prosecution case. It would be pertinent to note here that even if the circumstantial evidence, which includes panchanama of the scene of offence Exh.11, genuineness of which is admitted under section 294 of Cr.P.C. and , CA reports Exh.12 to Exh.14 are considered, still it would not have yield any benefit to the prosecution as there is no incriminating substantiative evidence against the accused. 11] As there was no incriminating evidence against the accused his statement U/Sec.313(1)(c) of Cr.P.C. was dispensed with. 12] For these reasons, I hold that the prosecution has miserably failed to bring home beyond reasonable doubt, the guilt of the accused for the offence punishable U/Secs363,366A & 376 of I.P.C. and U/Secs. 3 r.w.Sec. 4 & 12 of P.O.C.S.O Act. Hence, point No.1 to 5 are answered in the negative. 7 Spl.Case No.112/2014 Judgment In the result, the following order is made : :ORDER: 1) The accused­ Sachin @ Narhari Nagnath Raut is hereby acquitted of the offence punishable U/Secs.363,366A,& 376 of the Indian Penal Code & U/Secs.3 r.w.Sec.4 & Sec.12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act vide Section 235 (1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure Code. 2) The Accused is on bail. His bail bond stands cancelled. 3) The accused shall furnish P.B. and S.B. of Rs.15,000/­ (Rs.Fifteen Thousand only) within two weeks vide Sec. 437(A) of Code of Cr.P.C. for his appearance before the Hon’ble Appellate Court and it shall be in force for six months period. 4) The Muddemal property being worthless be disposed off after the period of appeal is over. Kalyan. ( D. S. Ghumare ) Dt. 07/12/2016. Addl. Session Judge, Kalyan

P.W.5 Ravindra Babaram Nalawade, the father of the victim produced the mobile handset (Article­B) of the victim and CD 5 Spl. Case No. 80/2015. He then sent the victim for her medical examination with her mother and police staff to MO RH Badlapur with his letter (Exh.42) and also sent the accused for his medical examination alongwith his letter (Exh.45). JMFC to record the statement of the victim under Sec.164 of Cr.P.C. He received the medical certificate (Exh.43) of the victim and the accused at Exh.47. On 25/3/2015, he sent the sample collected by the medical officer from the victim and accused to C.A., Mumbai alongwith his covering letter (Exh.53). He also sent mobile handsets, batteries of the victim and accused and C.D. alongwith his covering letter (Exh.54) to FSL, Kalina, Mumbai. The carrier obtained an acknowledgment of C.A. office. After completion of investigation, he filed chargesheet in this Special Court. 10. Charge (Exh.7) was framed by me against the accused which was read over and explained to him in vernacular. The accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. His defence is of total denial and false involvement in this crime. He has not stepped into the witness box nor examined any defence witness. 6 Spl. Case No. 80/2015. 11. Heard learned Spl.P.P. Shri D. V. Bhangare for the State and learned Advocate Shri M. M. Deshmukh for the accused, at length. 12. The following points arise for my determination and my findings thereon are recorded against them for the reasons to follow:­ Points Findings 1) Whether the prosecution proved that the victim was minor aged 17 years at the date of incident? .. In the negative. 2) Whether prosecution has proved that from November 2014 at 1 p.m. at room No.202, 2nd floor, Dharti Tower, Dipali Park, Manjarli, Badlapur (E), the accused committed rape on the minor victim, aged 17 years, punishable under Section 376 of IPC? .. In the negative. 3) Whether the prosecution has proved that at the relevant time, the accused captured the image of the minor victim engaging in a private act in circumstances where she would usually have the expectation of not being observed either by accused or by any other person at the behest of perpetrator or disseminates such image, punishable under Section 354­C .. In the negative. of IPC ? 7 Spl. Case No. 80/2015. 4) Whether the prosecution has proved that at the relevant time, the accused videographed in respect of sexual intercourse through his mobile handset and prepared video clip of an obscene act and uploaded on the social network whatsapp publicly, punishable under Section 294 of IPC ? .. In the negative. 5) Whether the prosecution has proved that at the relevant time the accused committed penetrative sexual assault upon the minor victim aged 17 years, punishable under Section 4 of the Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 ? .. In the negative. 6) Whether the prosecution has proved that at the relevant time, the accused intentionally or knowingly captured and transmitted the image of private area of the victim, aged 17 years without her consent, under the circumstances violated privacy of the victim, punishable under Section 66­E of I.T. Act, 2000 ? .. In the negative. 7) What order ? .. Accused acquitted. 8 Spl. Case No. 80/2015. REASONS 13. To substantiate the charge, prosecution has examined in all 8 prosecution witnesses, viz. PW1 Smt. Nisha Ravindra Nalavade (Exh.15), the mother of the victim who lodged the FIR (Exh.16) after showing the video clip by P.W.7 Smt. Naina Thakare to her. P.W.2 is the victim (Exh.22) who narrated the entire episode to her parents, aunt and uncle and she has disclosed her birth date as 2/12/1997. P.W.3 Sou Manisha Hemant Nalawade (Exh.24), an aunt of the victim who alongwith her husband had watched the video clip from the cell phone of P.W.7 Smt. Naina Thakare and then she was accompanied with the informant to lodge FIR. She has also acted as panch witness of arrest and personal search panchanama of the accused and seized mobile handset of accused under seizure panchanama (Exh.25) and the seizure panchanama (Exh.26) of mobile handset of the victim and CD prepared and produced by the father of the victim (P.W.5). 14. P.W.4 Shri. Dinesh Bhaskar Kadam (Exh.29) who acted as panch witness for spot panchanama (Exh.30) and seizure panchanama of the motor cycle (Exh.31) but he identified only his signatures but not supported the case of the prosecution. 15. P.W.5 Shri Ravindra Babaram Nalawade (Exh.35), the father of the victim who produced the birth extract of the victim at Exh.37 showing the birth place as Prathamesh Hospital but in photostat copy of birth extract produced before the police (Article­ A) by him the birth place mentioned as Sangita Hospital. He also produced the mobile handset of victim and CD of video clip before the police. 9 Spl. Case No. 80/2015. 16. P.W.6 Medical Officer Dr. Sou Jyotsna Sitaram Bagul, (Exh.41) MO RH Badlapur had examined the victim on 23/3/2015 brought by police alongwith letter (Exh.42) and issued the medical certificate (Exh.43) and case papers at Exh.44. She also examined the accused brought by police alongwith letter (Exh.45) and issued the medical certificate (Exh.47) and case paper at Exh.48. 17. P.W.7 Smt. Naina Vijay Thakare (Exh.51) is residing in ITI Colony, nearby the house of the victim who had received the said video clip on her cell phone on 15/3/2015 in which the victim was found sitting nude and whispering something. She showed the said video clip to the parents of the victim and police of Shivajinagar Police Station and again showed to the mother of the victim and then police prepared the C.D of said video clip from her cell phone but not in her presence. According to her, the video clip was pertaining to sex. 18. The last witness is P.W.8 Ashok Baburao Wanganekar (Exh.52) who carried out the investigation as usual after registering the crime and arrested the accused, seized mobile handsets of the accused as well as victim and CD produced by P.W.5 Ravindra. He sent the victim and the accused for their medical examination. He also seized the motor cycle, alleged to have been used during the commission of offence. The statement of the victim under Sec.164 of Cr.P.C. was recorded on the basis of his report to Ld. JMFC. He collected the medical certificates. He then sent seized articles including the sample collected from the victim and accused to FSL alongwith his covering letters (Exh.53 & 54). After completion of investigation, he filed the chargesheet. 10 Spl. Case No. 80/2015. As to point No.1 : 19. To attract the offences punishable under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, the prosecution has to prove that the victim was child below 18 years as defined under Sec.2(d) of the Act. The informant (P.W.1) has brought on record that age of the victim was 17 years at the time of incident. IO (P.W.8) has stated the birth date of the victim as 2/12/1997. The victim has also stated her birth date as 2/12/1997. P.W.5 Ravindra, the father of the victim has produced the birth extract at Exh.37 showing her birth date as 2/12/1997 issued by Ambernath Municipal Council, Ambernath and name of the hospital mentioned is 'Prathamesh Rugnalay', Ambernath. He had also produced the photostat copy of the birth certificate of the victim at Article­A showing the same date but different place of birth as 'Sangita Hospital'. The IO has tried to explain by saying that name of the hospital was changed subsequently, but there is no such proof produced. Even assuming the birth date of the victim as 2/12/1997, the alleged incident occurred in the month of November 2014, thus the probable age of the victim in November 2014 was 16 years, 11 months. 20. The learned Advocate for the accused placed his reliance on the ruling of Hon'ble Bombay High Court in the judgment of Criminal Appeal No.29 of 2015 dated 27/10/2015 [ALL MR (CRI) 2016 0 1921] in the case of Sanjay Vs. The State of Maharashtra wherein a witness Prashant (P.W.7), the Head Master of the school was examined in which the prosecutrix was taking education and had produced original admission register of the school and proved the relevant extract at Exh.24 showing the birth date as 30/12/1998. The offence of sexual intercourse was committed on 21/12/2013 and hence the victim was held to be minor. Here in the 11 Spl. Case No. 80/2015. case on hand no such school record has been produced. 21. Another judgment cited is in Criminal Appeal No.92/2015 dated 7/1/2016 (Sunil Baban Gadhave & Ors Vs. The State of Maharashtra) wherein the age of the prosecutrix was found 19 years on the basis of ossification test though the victim claimed her age was 16 years old at the time of the occurrence. 22. He also relied on the ruling reported in ALL MR (CRI) 2016 0 1433 in the case of Sandeep Janaji Konde Vs. The State of Maharashtra wherein His Lordship of the Bombay High Court was pleased to consider Sec.35 of Evidence Act, 1872 regarding relevance of entry in public record and observed in para 12 regarding school leaving certificate that, A School Leaving Certificate would be admissible in certain cases to prove the date of birth of a person by virtue of the provisions of section 35 of the Evidence Act. A reading of section 35 of the Evidence Act indicates that to render a document admissible under it, three conditions must be satisfied, the first being 'that the entry that is relied upon must be one in a public or other official book register or record; the second being 'that it must be an entry stating a fact in issue or relevant fact;' and the third being 'that it must have been made by a public servant in discharge of his official duty or any other person in performance of a duty specially enjoined by law.' An entry relating to date of birth made in a school register would be relevant and admissible under section 35 of the Evidence Act, but, it has been held, that such entry would not have much evidentiary value to prove the age of the person in the absence of material on which the age was recorded. However, this is not the case on hand. 23. He also relied on the ruling reported in ALL MR (CRI) 12 Spl. Case No. 80/2015. 2015 0 4006 in the case of Umesh Rajabhau Khandekar Vs. The State of Maharashtra in which to prove the age of the prosecutrix the Head Master was examined as witness and he has stated that the entry in the register of the school, in normal course, is taken on the basis of admission form filled­in by the parents of the student, however, the mother of the victim (P.W.2) Mangal stated in her cross­examination that the birth certificate of the victim was supplied to the school and she was born at Lohata, the maternal village of her mother. Her marriage was performed with the father of the victim about 25­26 years ago and after 2 years of the marriage she gave birth to a son Vikas and 2 years thereafter the victim was born. Thus, about 20­21 years prior to entering into the witness box in 2014 the victim was born. There was no medical evidence regarding the age of the victim, therefore, Their Lordships held that a reasonable doubt has arisen regarding the age of the victim to prove that she was below 18 years of age at the time of the incident. 24. Here, in the case on hand, the father of the victim has produced the birth extract at Exh.37 issued by Ambernath Municipal Council, Ambernath. At the stage of the investigation, he had produced the photostat copy of the certificate of birth at Article­ A showing the birth date of the victim as 2/12/1997. However, the defence disputed both the birth certificates on the reason that the place of birth mentioned are different i.e. 'Prathamesh Hospital', Ambernath as per Exh.37 and 'Sangita Hospital' as per Article­A. The birth certificate at Exh.37 appears to have been issued under Sec.35 of the Evidence Act which is admissible subject to three conditions are satisfied. The first condition is that the entry must be one in public or other official book register or record, and second, it 13 Spl. Case No. 80/2015. must be an entry seeking a fact or relevant fact, and third, it must have been made by public servant in discharge of his official duty or any other person or performance of the duty specially enjoined by law. However, except production of the birth certificate at Exh.35 no witness has been examined by the prosecution, particularly when the place of birth of the victim is shown two different hospitals. Ld. Advocate for the accused placed his reliance on the ruling reported in 2014(3) GLH 305 (SC) (Anvar P.V. Vs. P.K. 17 Spl. Case No. 80/2015. Basheer and others) wherein Their Lordships of the Hon'ble Apex Court (3 Judge Bench) held that­ “the very caption of Section 65A of the Evidence Act, r.w. 49 & 65B is sufficient to hold that special provisions of the evidence relating to electronic record shall be governed by the procedure prescribed under Sec.65B of the Evidence Act which is a complete code in itself.” Their Lordships further observed that ­ “Any documentary evidence by way of an electronic record under the Evidence Act, in view of Sections 59 and 65A, can be proved only in accordance with the procedure prescribed under Section 65B. Section 65B deals with the admissibility of the electronic record. The purpose of these provisions is to sanctify secondary evidence in electronic form, generated by a computer. It may be noted that the Section starts with a non obstante clause. Thus, notwithstanding anything contained in the Evidence Act, any information contained in an electronic record which is printed on a paper, stored, recorded or copied in optical or magnetic media produced by a computer shall be deemed to be a document only if the conditions mentioned under Sub­Section (2) are satisfied, without further proof or production of the original. The very admissibility of such a document, i.e. electronic record which is called as computer output, depends on the satisfaction of the four conditions under Section 65B(2). Following are the specified conditions under Section 65B(2) of the Evidence Act: (i) The electronic record containing the information should have been produced by the computer during the period over which the same was regularly used to store or process information for the purpose of any activity regularly carried on over that period by the person having lawful control over the use of that computer, (ii) The information of the kind contained in electronic record or of the kind from which the information is derived was regularly fed into the computer in the ordinary course of the said activity. 18 Spl. Case No. 80/2015. (iii) During the material part of the said period, the computer was operating properly and that even if it was not operating properly for some time, the break or breaks had not affected either the record or the accuracy of its contents ; and (iv) The information contained in the record should be a reproduction or derivation from the information fed into the computer in the ordinary course of the said activity.” “It is further clarified that the person need only to state in the certificate that the same is to the best of his knowledge and belief. Most importantly, such a certificate must accompany the electronic record like computer printout, Compact Disc (CD), Video Compact Disc (VCD), pen drive, etc., pertaining to which a statement is sought to be given in evidence, when the same is produced in evidence. All these safeguards are taken to ensure the source and authenticity, which are the two hallmarks pertaining to electronic record sought to be used as evidence. Electronic records being more susceptible to tampering, alteration, transposition, excision etc. without such safeguards, the whole trial based on proof of electronic records can lead to travesty of justice.” 34. Admittedly the Investigating Officer did not care to get copy of the video clip in CD received in the cell phone of P.W.7 Smt. Naina. There is no certificate attached as required under Sec. 65B and hence the evidence of electronic record is inadmissible and cannot be relied on. 35. Therefore, it is seen from the report of scientific 19 Spl. Case No. 80/2015. expert that video clip found in the mobile handset of the accused was the same video clip written on CD. Further, there is no evidence of carrier to FSL to prove that all the articles were intact in sealed condition and delivered. 36. She examined the victim and issued medical certificate (Exh.43) and case paper (Exh.44). She also issued medical certificate of the accused at Exh.47 and case paper at Exh.48. This witness has not signed the medical certificate of the victim at Exh.43 her nor ossification test was done. She admitted that due to cycling, exercise or horse riding an hymen can be ruptured.
