Thus, the testimony of this witness will go to show that she cannot opined whether there was penetrative sexual assault or rape but she has brought on record that the secondary sex character of the victim was found fully developed and no stains were found on her clothes. Her hymen was ruptured and tears were old but she has not given the position. No violence mark was found on her body. 38. The learned Advocate for the accused relied on the ruling reported in 2016 ALL MR (Cri) 4049 (Sachin Kakde Vs. State of Maharashtra) wherein the prosecution case was that the accused administered certain tablet to prosecutrix and when she was stupefied, he committed rape and also videographed said incident and thereafter threatened to make video clip public. The medical evidence regarding examination of the prosecutrix showing that her hymen was intact and no tears were found. There was no material showing that the accused has made or caused to make videograph a private part of the victim. Therefore, the conviction of the appellant under Sec.376 of IPC and Sec.6 & 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act was set aside. Here, in the case on hand except the bare testimony of the victim there is no other evidence to hold that the accused had videographed the sexual intercourse as alleged. 39. So far as the oral testimony of the victim for securing conviction on her solitary testimony, it is absolutely essential and necessary that the evidence of the victim should be trustworthy. It must inpsire confidence in the mind of the Court. As already mentioned that the victim on her own accord went to the accused at Badlapur (W) who then took her in a flat where the alleged incident 21 Spl. Case No. 80/2015. occurred. The victim has many friends on her facebook account as admitted by her. On 15/3/2015, though P.W.7 Smt. Naina Thakare informed about the video clip but no FIR was lodged promptly. Not only this, the statement of the victim was recorded after 2 days of filing of the FIR i.e. on 21/3/2015. The victim was not knowing the family status of the accused nor she made enquiry with him but chosen to join his company voluntarily to enjoy the physical relations. The video clip shown by P.W.7 Smt. Naina Thakare seems to have been formed the basis to register the crime regarding the alleged incident occurred in November 2014. The parents of the victim were not knowing anything about the said incident but they came to know only when Smt. Naina Thakare disclosed about the video clip to the informant and then the victim narrated the incident to her mother (P.W.1) and aunt (P.W.3) etc. None of the family members of the victim were knowing the accused at any time. 40. P.W.7 Smt. Naina Thakare is the Vice President of Mahila Rashtravadi Congress Thane who disclosed about the video clip to the informant. P.W.3 Sou Manisha, an aunt of the victim had gone to the house of the informant with her husband after the receipt of phone call of informant. According to P.W.3 Sou Manisha, P.W.7 Smt. Naina Thakare had personally come to the house of the informant who showed the video clip received on her cell phone. Then she alongwith her husband, informant and P.W.5 Ravindra observed the video clip but not Smt. Naina Thakare as she had given her handset of cell phone to her. Then she enquired with the victim who then narrated that she was taken to Manjarli in a room of friend of the accused, then they chit chatted and then she consented for all his acts. According to her, there was mouth sex. 22 Spl. Case No. 80/2015. They discussed and decided to lodge the FIR. Though she acted as panch witness for arrest and personal search panchanama of the accused at Exh.25 and seizure panchanama of the mobile handset of the victim and CD produced by P.W.5 Ravindra at Exh.26 but she does not know who got write (copied) the CD regarding the video clip from the cell phone of P.W.7 Smt. Naina Thakare. The accused was not given an opportunity of taking search of the panchas and the Investigating Officer when he was arrested after taking his personal search vide Exh.25. The accused was already brought in the police station before reaching the informant and other witnesses on 19/3/2015. The police informed to the informant (P.W.1) that they have arrested the accused and kept in lock up and she should come in the police station. Except the family members of the victim no other persons were present with the informant. None of the witnesses including the Investigating Officer knew from where the CD was prepared. In fact, the witness P.W.7 Smt. Naina Thakare in her evidence failed to bring on record that she showed video clip to the family members of victim at their house. According to her she showed the video clip from her cell phone in Badlapur Police Station, near Datta Mandir. She has denied that video clip in her cell phone was shown to the informant. Then question arises how the informant came to know about the video clip. This important link is missing in prosecution case. 41. The panch witness P.W.4 Dinesh Bhaskar Kadam though acted as panch witness for spot panchanama (Exh.30) drawn on 21/3/2015 and seizure panchanama of the motor cycle drawn on 23/3/2015 at Exh.31 but has not supported the case of the prosecution in toto, except his signatures identified by him. 23 Spl. Case No. 80/2015. 42. Though the witnesses came to know about the video clip on 15/3/2015 but till 19/3/2015 they did not inform or disclose anything about the video clip to anyone nor anybody enquired with P.W.7 Smt. Naina Thakare as to how she received the said video clip. The victim who used to visit the house of P.W.3 Sou Manisha at Kalyan but she never disclosed about the incident or the video clip. 43. The learned A.P.P. submitted that in absence of the medical evidence to prove the sexual intercouse, it cannot be held that the accused is innocent as there is strong evidence of the prosecutrix, by relying on the ruling reported in ALL MR (CRI) 2012 0 575 (Maroti Domaji Sadmake Vs. State of Maharashtra) wherein the victim was aged about 13­14 years and her hymen was not ruptured and the sexual intercourse was possible with slight penetration. In the said ruling the evidence of the victim was found strong, truthful and reliable evidence and hence His Lordship held that her testimony can be believed even in absence of any medical evidence regarding sexual intercourse. Here, in the case on hand it is not the case that the solitary testimony of the victim is believable or trustworthy. I say this because, the victim has not disclosed the incident to anyone. Not only this, but she was consenting party to each and every acts and her conduct is not natural one as without intimating her parents she went with the accused at various places. Even during journey from Ambernath Railway station to the place of incident i.e. Dharti Towers she did not raise for any help. All these factors shows the concensual acts of the victim. 44. Under the circumstances the oral testimony of the victim which has not been supported with medical evidence and her 24 Spl. Case No. 80/2015. testimony is neither trustworthy nor reliable, therefore, I answer the point Nos.2 & 5, in the negative. As to point Nos.3, 4 & 6 : 45. As I discussed in above points that except the victim there is no other evidence to hold that the accused captured the image of the victim engaging in a private act in any manner as the said video clip has not been proved or the accused shared the said video clip on social network whatsapp publicly. Moreover, there is no evidence on record showing that the accused intentionally or knowingly captured the images i.e. videography and transmitted the videography of private area of the victim without her consent and violated the privacy of her. Hence, the accused cannot be held guilty for these offences. Hence, I answer the point Nos.3, 4 & 6, in the negative. 46. Resultantly, the accused deserves to be acquitted, and as such, I proceed to pass the following order : ORDER i] The accused Anil Kisan Chavan is hereby acquitted vide Section 235(1) of Cr.P.C. of the offences punishable under Sec.376, 354­C, and 294 of the Indian Penal Code, Section 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offenes Act, 2012 and Section 66­E of the Information Technology Act, 2000. ii] He is in Jail since 20/3/2015, hence, he shall be set at liberty forthwith if not required in any other crime or case. iii] The seized muddemal property i.e. Samsung make mobile handset (Article­A) seized from the accused, Samsung make mobile handset (Article­B) seized from P.W.5 Ravindra Nalavade be returned to them and CD (Article­C) being worthless be destroyed after the period of appeal is over. iv] The motor cycle bearing registration No.MH­05­AD­6072 be 25 Spl. Case No. 80/2015. returned to Salim Mohammad Sharif Shaikh after the period of appeal is over. v] The accused shall execute his P.R. of Rs.15,000/­ to appear before the Higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect of appeal filed against this Judgment as per Sec.437­A of Cr.P.C. vi] Such bail shall remain in force for six months from today. Kalyan. (M.J.Mirza) Dt:­ 30/1/2017. Special Judge, Under Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, Kalyan.

On the contrary, she tried to say that the trial against the accused should be closed as early as possible. Special Case No. 85/2016 [Judg.] dispensed with the statement of accused under section 313 of Cr.P.C. as there is no incriminating evidence on record. Defence of the accused is of total denial and of false implication. 7] Considering the evidence on record and defence of the accused, following points arose for my determination and my findings thereon are as under for the reasons given below :­ POINTS FINDINGS 1] Does prosecution prove that between 25.07.2015 to 12.12.2015, accused kidnapped the minor complainant girl from the lawful guardianship of her mother and thereby committed an offence punishable u/s. 363 No. of IPC ? 2] Does prosecution prove that, during the same date, place and time accused intentionally induced the complainant with No. intent to compel her to marry with him against her wish to force and seduce her to illicit intercourse and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 366 of IPC ? 3] Does prosecution prove that, on the above mentioned date, place and time accused committed repeated physical intercourse with the minor complainant in the rented room 6 Atro. Special Case No. 85/2016 [Judg.] POINTS FINDINGS at Perangudi, Chennai of No. Tamilnadu State on the pretext of false promise of marriage and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 376 of the Indian Penal Code ? 4] Does prosecution prove during the same date, time and No. place accused committed criminal intimidation giving threats to the life of family members to cause alarm of fear in her mind and thereby committed an offence punishable u/s. 506 of IPC? 5] Does prosecution prove that No. during the above date, time and place accused committed repeated aggravated penetrative sexual assault with the victim­ complainant and thereby committed an offence punishable u/s. 6 of POCSO Act,2012? 6] What order? Accused is acquitted. : REASONS : POINT NOS.1 TO 5 :­ 8] This prosecution is launched by the victim­ complainant who was minor in age at the time of alleged commission of offence. It reveals from the FIR that she was taking education in Mothersa School at Gulbarga and during 7 Atro. Special Case No. 85/2016 [Judg.] Ramzan vacation she came to her mother's house at Dombivali and met with accused who fall in love with her knowingly that he is already married person. It appears from the prosecution case that the victim and the accused belongs to Muslim Community and governed by the Personal Law for Mohemmadans. However, while committing the criminal act he is liable to dealt with the provisions of Indian Penal Code. 9] The father of the victim girl died in the year 2011, hence her mother and brother were the earning hands of their family. In the year 2015, she was aging hardly upto 15 years as her date of birth is 1997. In such situation, her consent for the love and affection offered by the accused is having no relevance. The prosecution for kidnapping and rape coupled with penetrative sexual assault with the child of 15 years old is levelled against him. Thus, the prime consideration of this case is the minor age of the victim. 10] To constitute the minor age, the prosecution has relied upon school leaving certificate (Exh.6) produced on record. It is pertinent to note that said age proof is not seriously contested or challenged by the defence. On this background, the oral evidence of alleged minor complainant is liable to be scrutinized. 11] The prosecution has placed reliance on the allegations of FIR which came to be exhibited by adducing the evidence of complainant victim. It is pertinent to note that 8 Atro. Special Case No. 85/2016 [Judg.] the complainant has identified her signature on FIR, but she denied the allegations mentioned in it saying that she has not stated anything about the alleged enticement and forceful sexual intercourse alleged to have been committed on the pretext of false marriage promise. The portion marked of material omissions is rightly pointed out by Ld. Counsel Smt. Gauri Ramdurgkar. 12] The medical evidence plays vital role in the case of kidnapping and sexual assault. In the present matter seized clothes, the victim and accused and their collected samples of nail clippings, semen, vaginal swab and blood were sent for C.A. Examination, but surprisingly no positive evidence is come on record by the expert opinion. The oral evidence adduced by the victim is totally contrary to the prosecution story. Moreover, the status of the victim girl is now married wife of the accused. Therefore, non­examination of other corresponding witnesses gave adverse effect to the prosecution case. It is pertinent to note that at the time of alleged enticement, the victim was aging around 15 years old. She admitted in her cross­examination that she on her own accord went with the accused and their physical relations were continued with their sweet consent. I do agree the consent of minor girl has no relevance in case of rape with minor, but the understanding age of the victim to predict future consequences of her act or consent inspires me to consider that the couple knowing each other since childhood and who have decided to carry their future life as husband 9 Atro. Special Case No. 85/2016 [Judg.] and wife have committed their detemined act. The accused has not insisted her nor induced as alleged. The only age criteria of the minor victim is resulted into the present prosecution. The pursis filed on record regarding their happy marital life leads me to consider the maturity of the victim regarding forthcoming future. Considering all these aspects, it appeals to my mind that the strict proof and required ingredients to connect the accused with the crime of rape with kidnapping or to commit repeated penetrative sexual assault is not proved with cogent and consistent evidence. Therefore, I have no hesitation to answer point Nos.1 to 5 in the negative. POINT NO. 6 :­ 13] As I held above prosecution failed to prove necessary ingredients to prove the guilt of accused. Hence, he is liable to be acquitted giving benefit of inadequate evidence to prove the charges. In the result, I answer point No.6 accordingly and proceed to pass following order :­ ORDER 1] Accused Rafique Akbar Shaikh, Age : 26 years, R/at : New Govindawadi, Near Public Toilet, Kachoregaon, Dombivali (E) is hereby acquitted under Section 235(1) of Cr.P.C. of the offences punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376 and 506 of IPC and under Sec. 6 of POCSO Act,2012. 2] Bail bond of accused stands cancelled. 10 Atro. Special Case No. 85/2016 [Judg.] 3] Seized clothes being worthless be destroyed after the appeal period is over. 4] The accused is directed to furnish fresh P.B. & S.B. of Rs.15,000/­. In compliance with the provisions of section 437(A) of Cr.P.C. to abide himself to appear before Appellate Court in case of appeal is preferred by the prosecution. Judgment pronounced in open Court. Kalyan Dt : 01/12/2016 [ S.P. Gogarkar ] Dist. Judge­4 & Addl. Sessions Judge, Kalyan

1 Spl. Case No. 121/2014 [Judgment] Presented on : 10.9.2014. Registered on : 10.9.2014. Decided on : 9.9.2016. Duration : Y. M. D. 1. 11. 29. IN THE COURT OF SPECIAL JUDGE, KALYAN AT : KALYAN. (Presided over by : M.J.Mirza) SPECIAL CASE NO.121/2014 Exh. No. State of Maharashtra. Through : P.I. Shahapur Police Station. . . Complainant. Vs. Kiran Pandurang Shelke Age­24 Years, Occ. Teacher on contract basis R/at­ Agashi, Tal. Murbad, Dist.­ Thane. . . Accused. Appearance : Spl.P.P.Shri D.V. Bhangare for the State. Advocate Shri S.S.Zunjarrao for the accused. Offences : ­ Punishable under Section 509 of I.P.C., Section 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and Section 3(1)(xi) of Scheduled Castes & Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act 1989. JUDGMENT (Delivered in open Court on 9/9/2016). 1. The accused Kiran Pandurang Shelke is facing the trial for the offences punishable under Sections 509 of I.P.C. Section 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and Section 3(1)(xi) of Scheduled Castes & Scheduled Tribes (Prevention 2 Spl. Case No. 121/2014 [Judgment] of Atrocities) Act 1989 alleging that the accused outraged her modesty and uttered the words intending to insult the victim and also committed sexual harassment by writing chit and putting currency note of Rs.100/­ in her Mathematic note book. 2. The case of the prosecution, in short is as under : The informant/victim resides with her parents, two brothers and one sister. Since 1 st standard she was studying in Ashram Government English Medium School for Adivasi community. She took the admission in the year 2008. Her elder brother PW 5 Sunil was also studying in the same school. The incident occurred in the year 2014 when she was studying in 6 th standard. Smt. Maine Madam was her class teacher. The teachers for each subjects were different. The accused was teaching Mathematic subject to 6 th class students in which the victim was one of the student. 3. According to her, other boys and girls of her village were also taking education in the said school having facility of lodging and boarding. In the month of February­2014 the accused who was teaching Mathematic subject have taken the note of Mathematic subject and returned her after some time. When she opened the note book she noticed a chit on the first page on which her name was written and the said chit it was asked that she should come with him at holy festival. Again after 203 days on yellow coloured paper some dialogues in Hindi and Marathi were written and some symbol of love was also drawn stating that she should not breach the promise to roam and in English ''love you''. She was frightened, therefore, she did not tell anything to any one, however, she wrote chit stating that she should not harass her and send any chit or else she would disclose to her father. Once he had tried to give Rs.100/­ to her but she refused. 3 Spl. Case No. 121/2014 [Judgment] 4. On 12­3­2014, the accused took her Mathematic note book for checking purpose and again kept a chit in it saying whether it would be possible for her to come on 16­3­2014, on the day of Holy festival at Ajnup stop to roam. On 15­3­2014, she was asked to make phone call on her cell phone by giving mis call. Thereby the accused outraged her modesty. 5. The caste of the accused is Hindu Thakur and she belongs to Adivashi Thakur community. She then disclosed the said fact to her brother PW 5 Sunil who then informed to the Head Master Shri. Sahare sir who then made phone call to her parents. Her parents and aunt Shalubai Malu Ughade were called in the school and she disclosed the incident to them on 14­3­2014. 6. PSO of Shahapur Police Station registered the crime at C.R.No.II­11/2014 for the offences punishable under Sections 509 of I.P.C. Section 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and Section 3(1)(xi) of Scheduled Castes & Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act 1989. 7. Further investigation was carried out by SDPO Shahapur Division namely Prashant Waghunde who arrested the accused under arrest panchnama dated 16­3­2014 and drew the spot panchanama shown by the victim on 14­3­2014. He seized the note book of the victim along with the chits. The specimen handwriting of the accused was obtained and sent to handwriting expert for seeking opinion. He recorded the statements of witnesses. After completion of investigation, he filed the charge sheet in this Special Court. 8. Charge Exh.8 was framed by me which was read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. The accused pleaded not 4 Spl. Case No. 121/2014 [Judgment] guilty and claimed to be tried. His defence is of false involvement as per his statement recorded under Section 313 of Code of Criminal Procedure. Neither the accused stepped into the witness­box nor examined any defence witness. 9. Heard learned Spl. P.P. Shri D.V.Bhangare for the State and learned Advocate Shri S. S. Zunjarrao for the accused, at length. 10. The following points arise for my determination and my findings thereon are recorded against them for the reasons to follow:­ Points Findings 1. Whether the prosecution proved that the Yes. victim is minor aged 14 years ? 2. Whether the prosecution has proved that in between February­2014 to 12­3­2014 at Government Secondary Adivasi English Medium School Savroli, Tal. Shahapur the accused intending to insult the modesty of minor victim girl, uttered repeatedly by writing love chits to the effect that I love you etc. and “ek>s lkscr fQjk;yk ;s'khy dk\” intending that the same shall be heard by the minor victim, punishable under Sec.509 of I.P.C. ? ­­ Not proved. 3. Whether the prosecution has proved that at the relevant time, the accused committed sexual harassment of minor victim girl, punishable under Sec.12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual 5 Spl. Case No. 121/2014 [Judgment] Offences Act, 2012 ? ­­ Not proved. 4 Whether it is proved by the prosecution that at the relevant time and place, the accused not being a member of Schedule Caste or Schedule Tribe, intentionally insulted to the victim with intent to humiliate her within public view, punishable under S.3 (1)(x) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 ? – Not proved. 5. What order ? ­­ Accused acquitted. : REASONS : 11. To substantiate the charge, prosecution has examined in all six witnesses, viz. PW.1 the minor victim aged 17 years whose evidence was recorded in camera at Exh.14 and though she narrated about incident but not involved the accused who is responsible for writing the chits and putting in her note book nor she produced those chits before the police as she was not knowing who had kept those chits and cash Rs.100/­ in her note book but her aunt Shalubai and Sanghtana people dictated the contents of FIR and then she was asked to put signature on it. 12. PW 2 Bhaskar Kadu Ughade (Exh.16), the father of the victim had brought on record that she received phone call from the school on 13­3­2014 disclosing that some had given chits to her victim daughter but his son Sunil never disclosed him anything. PW3 Smt. Palibai Bhaskar Ughade (Exh.17), the mother of victim has brought on record that her victim daughter and son PW 5 Sunil are 6 Spl. Case No. 121/2014 [Judgment] studying at same Ashram School at Savroli but she deposed nothing about the incident. PW 4 Smt. Shalubai Malu Ughade (Exh.18), an aunt of the victim has deposed that nobody has disclosed her about the chits written to the victim. PW 5 Sunil Bhaskar Ughade (Exh.20), the brother of the victim has brought on record that some chits were found in the note book of her sister which were shown to him but he is unable to state who written those chits. Her sister also did not disclose who had written those chits to her. The last witness is PW6 Kamal Malu Ughade (Exh.21) who acted as panch witness for seizure panchanama of chits dated 14­3­2014 however, he had identified his signature on Exh.22 only. 13. The prosecution has not examined the investigating Office nor produced the opinion of handwriting expert on record. As to point No. 1 : 14. For the purpose of offence punishable under Section 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act 2012 it is necessary for the prosecution to prove that the victim is minor and below 18 years of age. Though the prosecution has produced the bonafide certificate of the victim issued by Head Master Government English Medium Ashram School, Savroli, Tal. Shahapur dated nil., showing the birth date of the victim as 31­7­1998. None of the prosecution witnesses including the victim has brought on record about her birth date. The defence has also not challenged that the victim is minor below 18 years of her age. The victim while recording his deposition on oath has stated her age as 17 years and the date of incident seems to be in February­2014. Therefore, the victim was about 15 years of age at the time of the alleged incident. Hence, I hold that the victim was minor and aged about 15 years at the time of alleged incident, and as such, I answer the point No.1 in the 7 Spl. Case No. 121/2014 [Judgment] affirmative. As to point No.2, 3 & 4 : 15. The best witness is the victim to depose about the incident. The victim being minor and in view of Sec.37 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, the trial was conducted in­camera and under child ­ friendly atmosphere. The age of the victim was 15 years at the relevant time and hence, she was of the age of understanding. An oath was administered to her considering the age and maturity. 16. She has also brought on record that she knows the accused before the incident. According to her, she was studying in the Ashram School and the accused was her Mathematic teacher. When she found chits in her note book she did not disclose to anyone. She has not brought on record that the accused was the author of those chits and also responsible for keeping currency note of Rs.100/­ in her note book who had taken her note book for checking purpose. Though she has proved her signature on the FIR Exh.15 but failed to prove the contents therein. On the contrary she has given go by to the contents of FIR by stating that she had not stated portion marked A' and 'B'. According to her, her aunt Shalubai and the members Sanghtana dictated the contents of FIR to the police and then she had put her signature only. 17. PW 2 Bhaskar Ughade and PW 3 Smt. Palibai Ughade are the parents of the victim but they have not supported the case of the prosecution in any manner. On the contrary, they have brought on record that the victim never disclosed them anything about the chits written by the accused or any other person, PW 5 Sunil Bhaskar Ughade is the real brother of the victim to whom the chits were shown by victim but he is unable to state who had written those 8 Spl. Case No. 121/2014 [Judgment] chits. The panch witness PW 6 Kadam Ughade has identified only his signature at Exh.22 and failed to prove the contents of the panchanama. Therefore, the seizure of chit has also not been proved by the prosecution in any manner. 18. For the purpose of 509 of IPC is necessary on the part of prosecution to prove that the accused insulted the modesty of a woman by uttering any words or makes any sound or gesture or exhibit any object intending that such word or sound shall be heard or such gesture and object shall be seen by such a woman or intrudes upon the privacy of such woman is necessary. No such ingredients was brought on record by the prosecution. 19. For the purpose of Section 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 it is necessary to prosecution to prove the ingredients mentioned in Section 11 defining 'Sexual harassment' viz. A person is said to commit sexual harassment upon a child when such person with sexual intention utters any word or makes any sound or makes any gesture or exhibits any object or part of the body with the intention that such word or sound shall be heard or such gesture or object or part of the body shall be seen by the child. None of the ingredients was Section 11 are proved by the prosecution. 20. For the purpose of offence punishable under Section x(1) (x) or (xi) of The Schedule Caste and Schedule Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 it is necessary to prove that, the accused should have been insulted or intimidated with intent to humiliate a member of Schedule Caste in any place within public view, but has not been proved by the prosecution. 9 Spl. Case No. 121/2014 [Judgment] 21. Under the circumstances, there is nothing on record to hold any of the accused guilty for any of the charges levelled against him. Thus, I hold that prosecution has utterly failed to prove the charges levelled against the accused by adducing cogent, reliable and trustworthy evidence. Hence, I answer the point Nos. 2 to 4, in the negative. 22. Resultantly, the accused deserves to be acquitted, and as such, I proceed to pass the following order : ORDER 1. The accused Kiran Pandurang Shelke is hereby acquitted of the offence punishable under Section 509 of I.P.C. and Section 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and under Section 3(1)(x) of Schedule Castes and Schedule Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 vide Sec. 235 (1) of Cr.P.C. 2. His bail bonds stand cancelled. 3. There is no muddemal property in the case. 4. The accused shall execute his P.R. of Rs.15,000/­ to appear before the Higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect of appeal filed against this judgment as per S. 437­A of Cr.P.C. 5. Such bail shall remain in force for six months from today. Kalyan. [M.J.Mirza] Dt.:­9/9/2016. Special Judge, Under Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, Kalyan.

When she saw in front of her, her father had come near her who then started removing clothes on his person. Said incident occurred at 2 a.m., therefore, they all went to bed. None of them had lodged the FIR. 4. On 7/7/2014 at 11.30 p.m. her father had come in the house and due to grudge regarding the incident occurred during night time, he started abusing them. At that time, they went to her grandfather Vijay Marathe, who is residing nearby her house, who then advised her mother to lodge a report with police. 3 Spl. Spl.Case 116/2014 [Judgment] 5. P.S.I. Shri G.P.Gondke carried out the investigation after registering the crime at C.R. No.I­256/2014, under Section 354 & 506 of I.P.C. and Sec. 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. He drew the spot panchanama at Exh.17, and recorded the statements of the witnesses. The accused was arrested on 8/7/2014. After completion of investigation he filed chargesheet in this Special Court. 6. Charge Exh.13 was framed by me which was read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. The accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. His defence is of false involvement as per his statement recorded under Section 313 of Code of Criminal Procedure. Neither the accused stepped into the witness­box nor examined any defence witness. 7. Heard learned Spl.P.P. Smt. J. S. Lohokare for the State and learned Advocate Shri S.R.Dhangar for the accused, at length. 8. The following points arise for my determination and my findings thereon are recorded against them for the reasons to follow:­ Points Findings 1. Whether the prosecution proved that the victim is minor aged 14 years ? .. Yes. 2. Whether the prosecution has proved that on 6/7/2014, at 10.30 p.m. at Dashahara Maidan, Indira Gandhi Bhaji Market, Section 23, Ulhasnagar­3 in the house of accused and informant, the accused used criminal force intending to outraged the modesty of victim girl aged 14 years ? 4 Spl. Spl.Case 116/2014 [Judgment] .. Not proved. 3. Whether the prosecution has proved that at the relevant time the accused threatened to the informant with intent to cause alarm to .. Not proved. her ? 4. Whether the prosecution has proved that at the relevant time the accused committed sexual harassment upon a minor victim girl, aged 14 years ? .. Not proved. 5. What order ? ….. Accused is acquitted. : REASONS : 9. To substantiate the charge, prosecution has examined in all three witnesses, viz. PW.1 minor victim girl at Exh.15, PW.2 Smt. Sangita Raosaheb Ranbagul, the mother of the victim at Exh.­16 and PW.3 A.P.I. Shri Ganpat Pandurang Gondke, Investigating Officer, who carried out the investigation in this crime at Exh.20. The minor victim girl and her mother have not supported the case of prosecution in toto. The defence has admitted the spot panchanama at Exh.17 as genuineness thereof is not disputed. As to point No. 1 : 10. The victim has brought on record in her testimony that her birth date is 10/9/2000. On the date of her evidence, her age was 15 years. Her mother PW.2 Mrs. Sangita has also stated the birth date of victim is 10/9/2000. This date has not been challenged by the defence in any manner. The investigating officer has not produced any proof of birth date of the victim on record. Under the circumstances, I hold that the birth date of the minor victim girl is 10/9/2000. The date of incident was 6/7/2014. Thus, age of the victim on the date of the incident was 5 Spl. Spl.Case 116/2014 [Judgment] 14 years and hence, she was minor. Therefore, I answer the point No.1 in the affirmative. As to point No.2 to 4 :­ 11. I have taken all these points together as they are interlinked and to avoid repetition as only two witnesses are relevant on these points. The best witness is the victim to depose about the incident in absence of her mother (PW.2) Sangita. The victim being minor and in view of Sec.37 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, the trial was conducted in camera under child ­ friendly atmosphere. She has brought on record that PW.2 Sangita is her mother and the accused is her father. He has also a brother aged 12 years but she is eldest to her parents. Since her childhood she alongwith her parents and brother are residing with her grandmother (mother's mother) at Ulhasnagar in a room owned by her grandmother which is behind the house of her grandmother. The names of her two grandmothers has also deposed by her. She has denied that no such incident of sexual assault or harassment or outraging her modesty has occurred at any time. Her mother had given her an understanding that the presence of her father is necessary for the family. The relatives of her mother's maternal home were helping her and her mother. She is unaware about the F.I.R. lodged by her was only to get compensation to the victim. 12. PW.2 Sangita is the mother of the victim who has deposed somehow same as deposed by the victim. According to her she saw that accused was found sleeping by keeping his hand on the person of victim and hence, the victim told her that she dislike to sleep by keeping the hand of her father on her person. In her testimony she has stated that her husband/accused is addicted to liquor and under the influence of liquor the hand of the accused might have fallen on the person of the victim. Because of bad vices of the accused, her family and family of her mother and neighbours were causing disturbance and therefore, she was intending to stop his habit. Only on suspicion her victim daughter lodged the F.I.R. She felt that the accused might be putting his hand on the person of her daughter out of love and affection. 14. Both these witnesses never stated anything about the alleged incident for which the charges are levelled against the accused. The last witness PW.3 A.P.I. Ganpat Pandurang Gondke has carried out the investigation as deposed. 15. Under the circumstances, there is nothing on record to hold the accused guilty for any of the offences levelled against the accused as none of the witnesses have supported the case of the prosecution in all respect. Hence, I hold that the prosecution has utterly failed to prove the charges levelled against the accused by adducing cogent and reliable evidence. Hence, I answer the point Nos. 2 to 4, in the negative. 16. Resultantly, the accused deserves to be acquitted, and as such, I proceed to pass the following order : ORDER i] Accused Raosaheb Mahadev Ranbagul is hereby acquitted vide Sec. 235(1) of Cr.P.C. of the offences punishable under Sections 354, 506 of IPC & Section 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 7 Spl. MHTH06­002066­2014 Presented on : 16/09/2014 Registered on : 16/09/2014 Decided on : 22/05/2018 Duration : Y.3 M.8 D.6 IN THE COURT OF SESSION JUDGE, THANE (Presided over by D.S.Ghumare) Session Case No. 126/2014 CNR NO. MHTH06­002066­2014 Exh. No. The State of Maharashtra (Through Central Police Station, Ulhasnagar) …... Prosecution V/S. 1] Salabuddin Jahangir Alam Pathan, Age 23 years. 2] Guddu Tarabuddin Khan, Age 20 years. Both R/at Bilassingh, Tal. & Dist. Kishanganj, State Bihar. …... Accused Offence punishable U/Sec.376, 354(1)(A)r/w. Sec. 34 of the Indian Penal Code and Sec. 3 r/w. Sec. 4, Sec. 5(m), 11 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ Ld. A.P.P. Shri Sachin Kulkarni for the prosecution. Ld. Advocate Smt. Aesankar for the Accused. ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ 2 Spl. Case (Atro) 126/14 (Judg.) CNR NO. MHTH06­002066­2014 JUDGMENT (Delivered on 22nd day of May, 2018) 1] The accused persons stand charged for the offence punishable under Sections 376, 354(1)(A)r/w. Sec.34 of the Indian Penal Code and Sec. 3 r/w. Sec. 4, Sec. 5(m), 11 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] The prosecution’s case is that the informant Sangita Surendra Chaudhary is residing with her mother Sushila and her brother Vijay along with her daughter, the victim, aged 3 years at Savitribai Phule Nagar, behind Smashan Bhumi, Ulhasnagar­3. Both the accused persons were residing in her neighbourhood. The informant's mother used to sell eggs­pav on handcart in the evening i.e. from 7.00 p.m. to 11.00 p.m. and her brother used to go at the T.V. shop at about 10.00 a.m. and used to return home at about 9.00 p.m. 3] Further case of the prosecution is that on 03/06/2014 the informant Sangita was at home for the whole day. In the evening she started preparing food and at that time her daughter, the victim, was sleeping. So when she went out of house for purchasing spices to prepare curry (Bhaji), she had asked her neighbours the accused Guddu and Salauddin to lookafter her daughter, the victim, who was sleeping at that time. When she returned home at about 9.00 p.m., she saw that her daughter, the victim, was crying loudly. The informant Sangita asked both the accused, who were standing near the victim, to go out of the house and then she asked her daughter­victim as to what happened. The victim 3 Spl. Case (Atro) 126/14 (Judg.) CNR NO. MHTH06­002066­2014 told and informed the informant by gesturs that the accused had touched her breast and other parts of the body. The informant Sangita felt that the accused had outraged her modesty. The informant Sangita then questioned the accused, whereupon many people gathered and they beat them and handed over them to police. Thereafter, P.W.1 informant lodged report against both the accused with Central Police station, Ulhasnagar on 04/06/2014. Thereupon the victim was medically examined at Sion Hospital where the medical officer had opined that hymen of the victim is torn. In sequel thereto, the offence punishable under Sec. 376 of I.P.C. and Sec. 4 of POCSO Act were added. 4] The investigation of the crime was conducted by P.S.I. Shri. J.J.Jaid, Central Police Station, Ulhasnagar. He firstly recorded statements of the witnesses. He then sent the victim for medical examination at Rukmini Hospital, Kalyan, but there she was not medically examined. Therefore, I.O. sent the victim at Sion for her medical examination. He collected medical report of victim from the Medical Officer. He recorded supplementary statement of the informant P.W.1 Sangita. He then visited the place of the incident and prepared its panchanama besides that he also drew sketch of the spot. He seized clothes of the victim and the accused persons and prepared panchanamas. He then arrested accused and crime was registered against them vide C.R.No. I­212/2014 for the offence punishable under Sec. 354(1)(A) of I.P.C. and Sec. 11 of POCSO Act, 2012. He then sent the accused for medical examination and collected medical report. Ultimately, after completion of the investigation, I.O. filed report U/S 173 of Cr.P.C in the court of Ld. Judicial Magistrate, F.C., Ulhasnagar, who after complying the provisions of sections 207 of CrPC committed the present case to the 4 Spl. Case (Atro) 126/14 (Judg.) CNR NO. MHTH06­002066­2014 Court of Sessions under section 209 of it. 5] The charge Exh.10 was framed against the accused persons for the offence punishable under Sec. 376, 354(1)(A)r/w. Sec.34 of the Indian Penal Code and Sec. 3 r/w. Sec. 4, Sec. 5(m), 11 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. The charge was readover and explained to the accused. The accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. The defence of the accused is that of total denial. They have not led any evidence in their defence. 6] The following points arise for determination and my findings are against each thereon for the reasons given thereunder. Sr.No. POINTS FINDINGS 1. Whether the prosecution proves that both the accused on 03/06/2014 at about 8.30 to 9.00 p.m., at complainant Sangita's house behind Smashanbhumi, Savitribai Phulenagar, Shnatinagar, Ulhasnagar­3, in furtherance of their common intention, committed rape on the No. prosecutrix, a minor victim girl, aged 3 years ? 2. Whether the prosecution proves that on the aforesaid date, time and place, both the accused, in furtherance of their common intention, used criminal force to said minor victim girl, aged 3 years, intending to outrage her No. modesty ? 3. Whether the prosecution proves that on the aforesaid date, time and place, both the accused committed No. penetrative sexual assault on the minor victim girl, aged 3 years ? 5 Spl. Case (Atro) 126/14 (Judg.) CNR NO. MHTH06­002066­2014 4. Whether the prosecution proves that on the aforesaid date, time and place, both the accused, committed aggravated penetrative sexual assault on the minor victim girl, aged 3 years ? No. 5. Whether the prosecution proves that on the aforesaid date, time and place, both the accused, committed sexual harassment on the minor victim girl, aged 3 years ? No. 6. What order ? The accused are acquitted. REASONS POINTS NO. 1 TO 4 :­ 7] All the points are dealt with simultaneously so as to avoid repetition of discussion of evidence which is common. 8] To bring home the guilt of the accused for the offence, the prosecution has examined four witnesses. They are the informant P.W.1 Sangita Surendra Chaudhary Exh. 16, Investigating Officer P.W.2 Gorakshnath Jayram Jaid and Medical officers P.W.3 Dr. Varun Darade and P.W.4 Dr. Sanjay Konde. 9] The informant P.W.1 Sangita is mother of the victim. She deposed that she resides with her mother at Ulhasnagar at the time of incident. She deposed that the age of her daughter was 3 years at the time of incident. However, she denied that accused Guddu and Salauddin used to reside in their neighbourhood. She also denied that on the date of incident at about 8.00 p.m., she made her daughter sleep and went to 6 Spl. Case (Atro) 126/14 (Judg.) CNR NO. MHTH06­002066­2014 market for bringing spices and asked accused Salauddin and Guddu to look after her daughter. She further denied that when she returned, she saw her daughter was crying loudly, so she asked her daughter the reason. She denied that on asking, her daughter pointed out both the accused and told that they touched her whole body therefore, she came out of the house and asked both the accused. He also denied that at that time, people gathered, caught hold the accused, beat them and handed over to police. Thus, the informant P.W.1 Sangita, who is the star witness of the prosecution had failed to support the prosecution case in its material particulars. 10] Ld. A.P.P. has declared P.W.1 Sangita hostile and cross­ examined her. During cross­examination, she denied the entire incident which she narrated while lodging the report. When she was confronted with her earlier statement wherein she incriminated the accused, she denied having made it. From the cross­examination of the informant P.W.1 Sangita, mother of minor victim, nothing material was elicited so as to incriminate the accused persons in the crime. 11] The prosecution has examined P.W.2 Gorakshnath Jayram Jaid, Investigating Officer of this crime. He deposed that initially he got medically examined the minor victim girl from Sion Hospital, Mumbai and collected medical certificate in which it is mentioned that the hymen of the victim girl is ruptured. He also wrote letter to Sion hospital to collect the samples of blood, hair from the private part for medical analysis. He then went to the spot and drawn spot panchanama in presence of two panchas. He also drawn the map of the spot of incident which are at Exh. 28 and 29 respectively. He further deposed that on 7 Spl. Case (Atro) 126/14 (Judg.) CNR NO. MHTH06­002066­2014 7/6/2014 informant P.W.1, mother of the victim girl, brought clothes of the victim in police station which were seized under panchanama Exh.30. On the same day, clothes of the accused persons were also seized vide seizure panchanama Exh.31. He also deposed that he arrested the accused on 4/6/2014 and prepared arrest panchanama Exh.32. He then recorded statements of witnesses. He also sent seized muddemal to C.A. vide letter Exh.36. He deposed that as there was sufficient evidence against the accused, he presented charge­sheet against the accused. The above evidence of the Investigating Officer P.W.2 G.J.Jaid is of not any help to substantiate the charge against the accused in absence of substantial evidence of the mother of the victim­P.W.1 informant Sangita 12] Prosecution has examined P.W.3 Dr. Varun Darade. He deposed that while he was attached to Rukminibai Hospital, Kalyan, the victim was brought by her mother and lady constable Bakkal No. 6760. He deposed that the victim was a child and did not co­operate for her medical examination, therefore, he had referred her Sion Hospital for medical examination. He had brought copy of OPD papers of MLC register which is at Exh.40. The aforesaid evidence of Dr. Varun Darade is not supporting the prosecution case as he had not in fact medically examined victim as she had not co­operated her for medical examination. 13] The prosecution has examined P.W.4 Dr. Sanjay Konde. He testified that the victim was examined and he found her hymen irregular and torn. However, he did not find blood oozing from her vagina or any other part of the body. He also testified that hymen can be torn by sexual assault. However, the aforesaid evidence only proves that hymen was torn but then it would not be appropriate to draw inference that she 8 Spl. Case (Atro) 126/14 (Judg.) CNR NO. MHTH06­002066­2014 was sexually assaulted by the present accused persons. This because victim's mother had not supported the prosecution's case as she had denied that the accused were her neighbour and she had left the house keeping the girl in their custody. It would be pertinent to note that the prosecution had not examined any other witness to substantiate the charge and the fact that the accused were found in the house of the informant Sangita, when it is the case of the prosecution that the public had gathered at her house after the incident and had even beat the accused persona and then handed over them to the police. Thus, the medical evidence itself is not sufficient to bring home guilt of the accused. 14] It may be stated here that the accused had moved application Exh.42 for closer of evidence on 09/10/2017. Thereafter the prosecution had been granted opportunity to secure the witness from time to time. But still the prosecution failed to secure the presence of the witnesses. The accused are undertrial prisoners and are in jail for more than three years. The accused have fundamental right of speedy trial. Therefore, I deem feel to allow the application Exh. 42 and close the prosecution evidence. More particularly when the informant P.W.1 Sangita, who is mother of the victim, has turned hostile and did not support the prosecution case. 15] Taking an overall view of all the facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence on record, it can be concluded that there is no evidence at all on record to establish that the accused No. 1 and 2 have committed rape upon the minor victim. For the said reasons, I hold that the prosecution has failed beyond reasonable doubt to bring home the guilt of the accused for the offence punishable under Sections 376, 354(1) 9 Spl. Case (Atro) 126/14 (Judg.) CNR NO. MHTH06­002066­2014 (A)r/w. Sec.34 of the Indian Penal Code and Sec. 3 r/w. Sec. 4, Sec. 5(m), 11 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Hence, I answer points no.1 to 5 in the negative. In the result, the following order is made. ORDER i] Vide section 235 of the code of Criminal procedure, accused No.1 and 2 Salabuddin Jahangir Alam Pathan, and Guddu Tarabuddin Khan are hereby acquitted of the offence punishable under Sections 376, 354(1)(A) r/w. Sec.34 of the Indian Penal Code and Sec. 3 r/w. Sec. 4, Sec. 5(m), 11 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. ii] The accused are in jail. They be set at liberty forthwith if not required in any other crime. iii] Muddemal property being worthless be destroyed after the appeal period is over. iv] The Accused No.1 and 2 shall furnish P.B. and S.B. of Rs.15,000/­(Rs. Fifteen Thousand only) each vide Sec. 437(A) of the Code of Criminal Procedure for their appearance before the Hon’ble Appellate Court and it shall be in force for six months. Dt. 22/05/2018. ( D. S. Ghumare ) Kalyan. Addl. Session Judge, Kalyan. 10 Spl. Case (Atro) 126/14 (Judg.) CNR NO. MHTH06­002066­2014

Shri. H.T.Watkar (P.W.7) who then carried out the investigation. As to point No. 1:­ 19. The Investigating Officer has produced the bonafide certificate at Exh.45 showing her birth date as 8.2.2001. The said bonafide certificate has been issued by Head Master, Shaskiya Madhyamik Ashram Shala, Ambivali (Gokulgaon), Shahapur, District Thane. In this case, the entries in the school register were not at all produced Indeed, whether the conditions to render a document admissible under section 35 of the Evidence Act had been satisfied in the case is doubtful, but assuming that the required conditions were satisfied, still, it was essential that the register containing the relevant entries ought to have been produced before the Court. There is, therefore, nothing to show that the School Leaving Certificate (Exhibit­28) contains an accurate record of the entries in the General Register maintained y the said New English School, even if the question of the weight to be attached to such entries in the absence of knowledge of the source of these entries, is kept aside. No person who has copied the entries in the General Register maintained by the school in the School Leaving Certificate (Exhibit­28), has been examined.” 20. Admittedly, the prosecution has not produced the register containing the relevant entry of birth date of victim but produced the bonafide certificate said to have been written on the basis of the entries made in the relevant school register. The bonafide certificate Exh.45 issued by the Head Master has not been examined by the prosecution to fulfill the conditions of Section 35 of the Evidence Act and hence there is nothing to show that the bonafide certificate Exh.45 contents and accurate record of 10 Judg. Spl. Case 129/2014 the entries of birth date in the register maintained by the school concerned. His Lordships further observed that “Even if it is presumed that the school leaving certificate contains an accurate record of the entries made in the General Register maintained by the New English School, it would be dangerous to come to the conclusion about the date of birth of the victim solely on that basis. At the time of entering the date of birth in the school register, information about the same is given generally by someone, generally the parents of the child and it is the knowledge of that person who gives the information is the basis of the entry. Here, when neither the father nor mother gives the date of birth of the victim and none of them even asked about the date of birth, it would be dangerous to conclude that the date of birth of the victim mentioned therein, must be correct date. He also seized the motorcycle owned by the accused which was used during the commission of offence from Sachin Anant Pawar, the brother of the accused under seizure panchnama (Exh.43) and obtained the receipt from muddemal clerk at Exh.44. Order below Exh.1 in Anticipatory Bail Application No.953/2018 (CNR NO.MHTH06­0002076­2018) 1] By this application filed under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. accused viz. Somnath Namdev Kathore has prayed for anticipatory bail in connection with crime No.I­255/2018 under Sections 354, 324, 323, 504, 506 read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code and under Sections 7, 11 and 23 of the Prevention of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 registered with Shahapur Police Station. 2] I have perused application and the say of I.O. submitted through learned A.P.P. I have heard both the sides. 3] Case of prosecution in brief is that informant is a minor girl aged 17 years old and her name is kept secret. On 29.05.2018 there was religious programme in Gavdevi Temple. So at 9.30 p.m. informant alongwith her parents and brother and sister went there to attend the programme. At about 10.30 p.m. she felt thirsty and she came to her house for drinking water and after drinking water when she went out of the house present accused came there and he demanded water from informant. Informant gave water to accused and thereafter accused demanded fennel from the informant. When informant was giving fennel to accused at that time accused pinched her hand. So informant got frightened and she went out of the house and when she went to the hall of their community suddenly accused came there and accused by putting his hand on the shoulder of informant and by touching breast of the informant uttered insulting words and thereby accused outraged her modesty. At that time informant gave slap to the accused and at that time informant's cousin brother Manish Dongare also came there. She informed this fact to her 2 ABA No.953/2018 (Or.Exh.1) cousin brother and at that time accused tendered her apology and went away. Informant informed this fact to her parents and brother and thereafter at about 11.30 p.m. informant's maternal uncle Manoj Chavan and informant's brother Haridas Bhoir and Jagdish Dongare went to inquire from accused as to why he outraged the modesty of the informant. At that time quarrel took place between them and they came back. In the same night at about 00.30 a.m.o co­accused Deepak Ravindra Kathore, Mayur Ravindra Kathore, Pramod Bhagwat Kathore came to the house of informant by motorcycle and they started abusing informant's family members. When informant's father and brother asked them as to why they abused them they got angry and at that time accused Pramod Kathore intended to give blow of iron rod on the head of Haridas Bhoir which he averted by putting his hand and thereby sustained injury. Thereafter informant's father and brother tried to intervene but they were assaulted by fists­blows and they were abused and threatened by them and thereafter assailants ran away on motorcycle. So, on the report of informant aforesaid crime is registered. 4] It is argued by learned advocate for accused that accused Nos.2 to 4 have been granted interim anticipatory bail and next date is 22.07.2018. It is further argued that counter C.R. is also registered against informant's family members at the instance of present accused under Section 326 and other section of IPC and that C.R. number is 260/2018. It is further argued that when the informant and her family members came to know that present accused sustained fracture injury and he was hospitalized and his father was also hospitalized, this false complaint is deliberately lodged as a counter blast to the complaint of the accused. It is further argued that he is working as Executive in Muthoot Finance Company. He has two children and that he sustained fracture injury and in that respect counter C.R. is registered. It is 3 ABA No.953/2018 (Or.Exh.1) therefore submitted that application may be allowed. 5] However, learned APP has submitted that the remaining three co­ accused who are granted interim anticipatory bail are having the role pertaining to under Section 324 of the I.P.C. and that crime was initially registered at the instance of informant and thereafter at the instance of accused the counter C.R. is registered. Accused outraged the modesty of informant by pinching her hand and putting his hand on her shoulder and touching her breast and uttering insulting word. It is therefore submitted that application may be rejected. 6] Considering the nature of allegations, prima facie it appears that accused outraged the modesty of informant who is minor by pinching her hand and by putting his hand on her shoulder and by touching her breast and by uttering insulting words to her, I am of the view that the role attributed to the present accused is not similar to the role attributed to the remaining co­accused. Hence, accused is not entitled to be released on pre­arrest bail. It is true that prima facie counter C.R. bearing No.260/2018 is also registered at the instance of present accused against the relatives of informant under Section 326 of I.P.C. and other sections of I.P.C. but that cannot be a ground for accused to be released on pre­arrest bail. Hence, I pass following order :­ ORDER Application is rejected. Kalyan (A.A.A.Shaikh) Dt.:­ 03.07.2018. Additional Sessions Judge, Kalyan.

Not proved. 6 Whether the prosecution has 6 Judgment Spl. Case No.100/2015 proved that the accused at the relevant time committed aggravated penetrative sexual assault repeatedly on the minor victim, punishable under Sec. 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 ? ….. To substantiate the charge, the prosecution has examined in all six witnesses viz. P.W.1 victim at Exh.11, who lodged the FIR but did not disclose about any incident. P.W.2 Jabbarsingh Bhursingh Chavhan (Exh.12), the panch witness for spot panchanama (Exh.16) but not supported the case of the prosecution. PW.3 Rajdatta Vishnu Mayekar (Exh.18), the panch witness in whose presence the accused produced his clothes on 5/1/2015 under his disclosure statement at Exh.19 and seizure panchanama at Exh.20. PW.4 Datta Kashinath Mhatre (Exh.21), the maternal uncle of the victim (mother's brother) but he does not know anything about the incident. He also recorded the history of sexual assault by her step father since her age of 15 years and last sexual 7 Judgment Spl. Case No.100/2015 contact was on 28/12/2014. He issued the medical certificate at Exh.26. As to Point No.1 : 10. The witness has produced her school leaving certificate showing her birth date as 15/4/1997 at Exh.12. The defence has not seriously challenged the birth date of the victim seriously. On the date of FIR the age of the victim was 17 years, 8 months and 19 days. Therefore, I hold that the victim girl was minor below 18 years of age at the relevant time. Hence, I answer point No.1, in the affirmative. As to point No.2 to 7 :­ 11. I have taken all these points together as they are interlinked and to discuss properly by avoiding repetitions. The testimony of the victim PW.1 is material for all these points as she is the only witness who can depose about the actual incidents as alleged involving the accused who is her step father on the point of rape, sexual assault, harassment, threats and penetrative sexual assault on her. The evidence of victim was recorded in camera. 12. According to her, her father Subhodh expired when she was three years old. Then her mother married with the accused Ramakant. In the year 2012, he was residing with her mother and step father at New 8 Judgment Spl. Case No.100/2015 Yogesh Building, Thakurwadi, Dombivli or at Diva. Her mother was working as maid­servant when she was residing with her mother and the accused. She admits her signature on the FIR. She has also brought on record that her medical examination was not carried out on 4/1/2015 after lodging her FIR. In her testimony she had stated that the contents of the FIR were not read over to her and she has no grievances against the accused. Thus, her testimony if considered from all the angles, it is clear that she has not attributed any overt act against the accused who is her step father and married with her mother after the death of her natural father. 13. PW.4 Datta Mhatre is the maternal uncle of the victim. He knows the accused who used to ply autorickshaw. When the victim was aged about 3 years, her father Subodh expired. This witness was having visiting terms in the house of his sister. The victim used to go to school in Gaondevi Madhyamik Vidyalaya. Except this he failed to bring anything attributing the overt act of the accused for any offence charged against him. 14. To prove the sexual assault, rape, sexual harassment and penetrative sexual assault on the victim, the prosecution has adduced the evidence of PW.5 Dr. Shri Piyush Govardhan Mahajan, who was attached to Shastrinagar Hospital who examined the victim on 4/1/2015. Her OPD number was 77636 and MLC number was 23867. The mother of the victim disclosed the age of the victim as 17 years by disclosing the birth date of the victim as 15/4/1997. He then obtained the consent of the mother of the victim and examined her. He noticed that the genitals of the victim was normal but hymen was absent and vaginal walls were irregular. No 9 Judgment Spl. Case No.100/2015 swelling or bruises were notices. He then collected sample of pubic hairs, nail clippings, vaginal swab and blood sample and handed over to accompanying police staff. According to him, the history given by victim and her mother alleging that victim had sexual contact with her step father since the age of 15 years and her last sexual contact was 28/12/2014 which was vaginal sexual intercourse. Then he issued the medical certificate (Exh.26). On perusal of medical certificate (Exh.26) the history seems to have been recorded by him and no injury marks were noticed on the private part of the victim. The hymen injury was absent but the edges were irregular. He did not opine about the rape or penetrative sexual assault on the victim. 15. It is settled position of law that a slight penetration is sufficient to constitute the offence of rape or penetrative sexual assault as held by Their Lordships of the Apex Court in the case of Aman Kumar Vs. State of Haryana (2004 S.C.C. (Cri) 1266) wherein it is held that, “Penetration is the sine qua non for an offence of rape. In order to constitute penetration, there must be evidence clear and cogent to prove that some part of the virile member of the accused was within the labia of the pudendum of the woman, no matter how little. The depth of penetration is immaterial in an offence punishable under Section 376 of I.P.C. Even a slight penetration in the vulva is sufficient to constitute the offence of rape and rupture of the hymen is not necessary. Vulva penetration with or without violence is as much rape as vaginal penetration. The statute merely requires evidence of penetration, and this may occur with the hymen remaining intact. The actus reus is complete with penetration. Thus, to constitute the offence of rape, it is not necessary that there should be complete penetration of the penis with emission of semen and rupture of hymen. Partial penetration within the labia majora of the vulva or pudendum with or without emission of semen is sufficient to constitute the offence of rape as defined in the law.” 10 Judgment Spl. Case No.100/2015 16. The FSL report at Exh.14 regarding semen, pubic hairs, nail clippings and blood sample of the accused shows that neither semen, blood was detected nor the blood group was ascertained as the results were inconclusive. The C.A. certificate regarding the samples and blood group of the victim at Exh.23 shows that no semen was detected, however, the blood group of the victim is 'AB'. 17. The panch PW.3 Rajendra Mayekar and PW.6 Nandlal Choube though identified their signatures on Exh.19 & 20 regarding the alleged disclosure statement of the accused (Exh.19) and seizure of his clothes and bedsheet from his house at Yogesh Building, 4 th floor, room No.30, however, both these witnesses have not supported the case of the prosecution in any manner. Further the C.A. report shows nothing incriminating either on the clothes of the accused or bedsheet alleged to have been seized. 18. An useful reference can be made on the point of delay in lodging the FIR, reported in 2004 Supreme Court Cases (Cri) 471 [Surjan & ors. Vs. State of M.P.], wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court held that, “The inordinate delay in lodging the complaint before the police i.e. 10 days has not been attempted to be explained. Even when she was examined as a witness in Court, no question was put to her on that long delay. Looking at the testimony of the prosecutrix from all the different angles, it is not possible to hold that the testimony is wholly reliable. In such situation, material for corroborating the testimony of the prosecutrix could not be obviated. But there is none. Therefore, the conviction and sentence passed to the appellant under Section 376 cannot be confirmed.” 11 Judgment Spl. Case No.100/2015 19. The delay has not been explained by the victim or any other witness including the investigating officer who has not been examined. Therefore, it creates doubt and does not inspire the judicial confidence in view of the fact that the accused being step father was repeatedly committing rape or penetrative sexual assault on the victim. Though he was threatening to the victim not to disclose the incident to any one but she had ample opportunity to escape and approach to the various police stations for lodging the FIR. 20. The testimony of the victim is not useful for the prosecution as she whispered nothing about any of the incidents as narrated in her FIR. On the contrary she has denied all contents of the FIR by stating that the contents therein were not read over to her. Even in her substantive evidence she has not supported the case of the prosecution in any manner. Hence, I answer the point Nos. 2 to 7, in the negative. 21. Resultantly, the accused deserves to be acquitted, and as such, I proceed to pass the following order : ORDER i) The accused Ramakantlal Tribhuvan Shrivastav, is hereby acquitted of the offences punishable under Sections 376, 504 & 506 of I.P.C. and Section 4, 6 & 12(v) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 vide Sec. 235(1) of Cr.P.C. ii) His bail bonds stand cancelled. iii) Seized muddemal property has not been produced before the Court and seized property be destroyed being worthless after period of appeal is 12 Judgment Spl. Case No.100/2015 over. iv) The accused shall execute his P.R. of Rs.15,000/­ to appear before the Higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect of appeal filed against this judgment and order vide S. 437­A of Cr.P.C. Such bail shall remain in force for six months from today. Kalyan. (M.J.Mirza) Dt.:­19/12/2016. Special Judge, Under Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, Kalyan.

ORDER BELOW EXH­16 IN SPECIAL CASE NO.98/2016. 1] By this application filed under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure accused viz. Vijay Arjun Joshi has prayed bail in connection with crime No.I­323/2016 under Sections 376 read with Section 34 of IPC and under Sections 3, 4, 5 & 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and Sections 66E and 67 of Information Technology Act registered with Vithalwadi Police Station. 2] I have perused application and the say of I.O. submitted through learned APP. I have heard both the sides. 3] Case of prosecution in brief is that informant is the mother of the victim girl and that the victim girl is aged 16 years old (name of the informant and the victim girl is kept secret). Informant lodged her report to police that for about 8 months before the lodging of this report quarrel had taken place between her and her sister Masha @ Manisha. Due to that grudge Masha in order to teach lesson to the informant induced the victim girl to have friendship with accused by saying that he would marry with her and she also provided secluded place to the victim girl and accused for that purpose. For about 6 months before the lodging of this report accused took the victim girl at Chinchapada and did sexual intercourse with her and at that time accused took video clip of that sexual intercourse in his mobile phone. When the victim girl asked accused as to why he took the video clip accused replied that she should not be afraid of that and that he would marry with her. And thereafter Masha used to show that video clip to the victim girl and used to compel the victim girl to have sexual intercourse with the accused by giving threat that otherwise she would upload the video clip on the internet, whatsapp and social media and 2 Special Case No.98/2016(Or.Exh.16) she also used to compel the victim girl to do illegal work. When the victim girl asked Masha as to why she behaved with her in this way at that time Masha replied that she wanted to teach lesson to her mother. Other relatives of Masha named in the FIR also helped her in the said offence. It is further the case of the prosecution that on 08.04.2016 when informant told Masha in the presence of Masha's relatives that whatever she did it was very bad and at that time Masha and her relatives quarreled with her and at that time Masha showed to the informant the obscene video clip of the victim girl and she further threatened that she would upload the said clip on the internet and the social media. Thereafter on 09.04.2016 the informant through her husband's friend came to know that said video clip is uploaded on the internet and whatsapp and it was also sent to her husband's mobile phone and after seeing the same informant lodged her report to police and the aforesaid crime is registered. 4] It is argued by learned advocate for the accused that there was love affair between accused and the victim girl. It is further argued that endorsement made by Medical Officer shows that the said intercourse was done with the consent of the the victim girl. Accused has been in custody since 12.04.2016. It is therefore prayed that accused may be released on bail. In support of his argument he has relied upon the authority in the case of Sunil Mahadev Patil Vs. State of Maharashtra, Bail Application No.1036/2015 decided on 3.8.2015 by the Hon'ble Bombay High Court. 5] However learned APP has submitted that age of the victim girl is 16 years and prima facie case is made out against accused. The consent of the girl cannot be said to be free consent. It is further submitted that informant has filed affidavit that she has no objection if the accused is released on bail and this fact shows that informant is 3 Special Case No.98/2016(Or.Exh.16) tampered with. It is therefore prayed that application may be rejected. 6] I have perused the aforesaid authority. Facts of the aforesaid authority are not similar to the facts of the present case because in that authority there was love affair between accused and the victim girl who was aged 15 years old and they eloped and went to the temple and performed marriage and thereafter they started residing together. Therefore this authority would not help the accused. 7] Considering the nature of the offence and role attributed to the present accused and the fact that the said video clip is uploaded on the internet and social media and the fact that the victim girl is aged 16 years old, I am of the view that accused is not entitled to be released on bail. Hence, I pass following order :­ ORDER Application is rejected. Kalyan ( A.A.A.Shaikh ) Dt. :­ 14.11.2017. Additional Sessions Judge,Kalyan.

The version of PW 4 Rohini Kalu Ghokse is that they met victim on platform no. 4 at Dombivali Railway Station but she is silent about the date. She has made out different case before the Court stating therein that on 20.9.2012 she along with Anjali and her mother had gone to Mumbai and placed order for cake in Mumbai. Considering these inconsistencies and contradictory versions in between witnesses, it appears that nobody is telling the truth regarding their movements when the victim met them at Dombivali Railway Station. Therefore, their version is not reliable and trustworthy. 49. The learned Advocate for accused placed his reliance on ruling reported in AIR 2006 S.C. 1367 (Zahira Habibullah Sheikh & Anr. Vs. State of Gujarat & Ors.) wherein Their Lordships of Apex Court ruled that ­ .....27..... Spl. Case No. 1/2013 [Judg.] "The presiding judge should not be spectator in the trial evincing intelligence, active interest and elicit all relevant materials necessary for reaching the correct conclusion, to find out the truth and administer the justice with fairness and impartiality both to the parties and to the community it serves". 50. On the basis of this ruling, the learned Advocate for the accused submitted that enquiry under section 22 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 may be initiated against PW 2 Vidya Dudhwadkar. I have already considered the testimony of the victim at whose instance the crime came to be registered against the both the accused. She has made it clear that PW 2 Vidya Dudhwadkar narrated the contents of FIR. Moreover, the chit produced at Exh.49 also supports her version that mother of Anjali insisted her to lodge the complaint by taking her to the police station. Thus, under these circumstances, it is seen that solely with the intention of humiliating the accused, PW 2 Vidya has played important role in this case making the victim as an instrumental. Therefore, the learned Advocate for the accused submitted that necessary directions to take action against PW 2 Vidya Dudhwadkar may be issued to the police, and accordingly, the directions are required to be given to the police vide Section 22(3) of the Protection of Children from the Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 51. Considering the cumulative effect of the testimony of all the witnesses, the evidence does not bring any substance to bring guilt home the accused. The medical evidence shows that the victim was habitual to intercourse as she used to stay away from the house 3­ 4 days continuously .....28..... Spl. Case No. 1/2013 [Judg.] by taking money kept in the house. Moreover, because of fear of the father of the victim, she concocted the a story of rape and threats alleged to have been administered by the accused and penetrative sexual assault on her by her father and brother. Under the circumstances, I answer point nos. 2 to 4, in the negative. 52. Resultantly, both the accused deserves to be acquitted. Hence, I proceed to pass the following order : Order 1) Accused No.1– Hardik Mahesh Pasad and the accused No.2­ Mahesh Khimji Pasad are hereby acquitted of the offences punishable under Sections 376, 506 r.w. 34 of IPC and S. 5(n) r.w. 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 under Sec. 235(1) of Cr.P.C. 2) They are in Jail. They shall be set at liberty forthwith if not required in any other crime or case. 3) The seized articles viz. nicker ­Article A, underwear Article B of accused No.1 and underwear of accused No.2­Article C, being worthless, be destroyed after the appeal period is over. 4) Both the accused shall execute their P.R. and S.B. of Rs.15,000/­ each to appear before the Higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect of appeal filed against this judgment as per Sec. 437­A of Cr.P.C. Such bail shall remain in force for six months from today. 5) The Crime Branch, Thane is directed to make investigation in respect .....29..... Spl. Case No. 1/2013 [Judg.] of P.W.2­Vidya Satyawan Dudhwadkar who provided false information against the child, knowing it to be false, thereby victimised the complainant/ victim in this case and take necessary legal action against her vide Sec. 22(3) of the Protection of Children from the Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Kalyan, (M.J.Mirza) Dt.12/8/2014. Special Judge, Under Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Kalyan.
