(POCSO) CASE NO. 29/2013 State of Maharashtra ( Through Hill Line Police Station, Ulhasnagar, Tal­Kalyan, Dist­Thane ) ( Cr. No. I­47/2013 ) … Complainant Versus Arun Dattu Madhavi, Age 37 years, R/at Post­Ghotsai, Vasar gaon, Tal­Ambernath, Dist­Thane. … Accused Offence punishable under sec. 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012 ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ Appearance : Mrs. R.R. Bhoir, Ld. APP for State Shri P.P. Dukare, Ld. Adv. For Accused ============================= ...2/­ 2 Spl. Atro.(POCSO) Case No. 29/2013 [ Judg. ] JUDGMENT ( Delivered in Open Court on 17th day of April, 2017 ) 1] This accused is facing trial initiated by the State through Hill Line police station, Ulhasnagar for the offence punishable under section 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012. 2] Brief facts are as follows :­ This accused runs electronic repairing shop by name and style as “Gavdevi Electronics” at Ulhasnagar­3. Complainant Aarti Ovhal reside in the neighbouring area of the shop of accused. Accused was running lucky draw type bhishi on 20th of every month. Mother­in­law of the complainant Aarti Ovhal was member of that bhishi. Mother­ in­law of complainant Aarti died. Thereafter on 21/3/2012 at about 12.50 hours this complainant alongwith her 17 months' baby went to the shop of accused who asked him about the amount credited by her mother­in­law in said bhishi. Accused asked her to bring the card in which all entries regarding credits are made. Complainant returned home to bring card. At that time accused asked complainant to keep her daughter Tanvi with him and he will look after her. Initially complainant refused to keep her daughter with accused. However on his insistance complainant kept her daughter with accused and went home to bring bhishi card. After 20 minutes complainant returned to the shop of accused. At that ...3/­ 3 Spl. Atro.(POCSO) Case No. 29/2013 [ Judg. ] time she saw her daughter Tanvi was frightened. There were nail abrasions on her cheek. Her neck and chest became reddish. Zip of the pant of the accused was opened. Seeing the complainant accused also become restless. Immediately complainant took her daughter Tanvi from accused and asked accused what he does with her. Complainant returned home and started weeping. Her sister­in­law came and asked complainant what happened. Thereafter complainant and her sister­in­law came to accused and asked as to why he behaved in such way. Accused scolded them and rushed towards them. Therefore they returned home. On next day at about 8.00 p.m. accused stood in front of the house of complainant and stared to her with anger. Then complainant approached the local Corporator. Thereafter on 27/3/2017 complainant lodged complaint against the accused and crime is registered. 3] Investigation in the said crime was carried by one Vinod Tejale then PSI. He prepared spot panchanama. He arrested accused. He sent victim girl to Central Hospital, Ulhasnagar for medical. He obtained medical report. He caused medical of the accused. He obtained report. He recorded statements of the witnesses. He sent victim girl to J.J. Hospital for further medical examination. He obtained report from J.J. Hospital. After completion of investigation he submitted chargesheet against the accused. ...4/­ 4 Spl. Atro.(POCSO) Case No. 29/2013 [ Judg. ] 4] Accused appeared before this court. Charge against him is framed at Exh.2 for the offence punishable under section 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012. Charge was read over and explained to accused in Marathi language. He pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. His defence is of total denial. He has not adduced any defence evidence. 5] Prosecution was directed to adduce its evidence. In response to that prosecution examined in all two witnesses in this case. PW­1 Aarti Deepak Ovhal (Exh.4) is the complainant and mother of alleged victim girl. She deposed as per her complaint. She proved her complaint which is at Exh.5. PW­2 Vinod Tejale (Exh.6) is Investigating Officer. He proved arrest panchanama at Exh.7. He proved spot panchanama which is at Exh.8. He proved report of Central Hospital at Exh.9. He proved medical examination report of accused which is at Exh.10. C.A. reports are at Exhs.11 to 14. This witness narrated the investigation carried by him in detail. Thereafter prosecution closed its evidence. 6] After completion of prosecution evidence statement of accused under section 313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is recorded. From answers given by the accused during the course of statement under section 313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure defence emerges is of total ...5/­ 5 Spl. Atro.(POCSO) Case No. 29/2013 [ Judg. ] denial. As I have stated no defence evidence is adduced by the accused. 7] I have gone through oral as well as documentary evidence on record carefully. I have heard both advocates at length. 8] Following points arise for my consideration. My findings on those points are as follows for the reasons stated below. POINTS FINDINGS 1. Does prosecution prove that, on 1.00 p.m. in their Gaodevi Electronics shop, Aakash Colony, in front of new power house, Ulhasnagar­5, the accused committed sexual Not proved. assault on complainant's daughter Tanvi Ovhal who is minor aged about 17 months' only and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012 ? REASONS 9] AS TO POINT NO.1 :­ Except the statement of complainant Aarti Ovhal there is no other oral or documentary evidence against the accused to prove his guilt beyond all reasonable doubts. ...6/­ 6 Spl. Atro.(POCSO) Case No. 29/2013 [ Judg. ] Testimony of Investigating Officer Tejale is about the procedure and the acts done by him during the investigation. Even if we accept entire documents on record as it is, then also it is crystal clear that, there is nothing incriminating in those documents against this accused. And therefore there remained only evidence of PW­1 Aarti on record for consideration. 10] After careful scrutiny of evidence of Aarti it seems that, she is not safe to rely unless her testimony is duly corroborated by independent evidence oral or documentary. The admissions given in the cross­examination by PW­1 Aarti it is crystal clear that, there was some dispute between this accused and complainant regarding the amount of bhishi deposited by late mother­in­law of Aarti with this accused. Even the evidence of PW­1 Aarti is not direct evidence on the point of alleged sexual assault by this accused on her daughter Tanvi aged 17 months' only. It seems that, this complainant herself handed over Tanvi­her daughter to accused to look after her so that she would be facilitated to go home and bring the bhishi card. Though it is deposed by her that, accused insisted her to keep Tanvi with him, this seems not possible and probable. This deposition is definitely carries doubt. In her complaint she stated that, there were nail abrasions on the cheek of Tanvi and her neck and chest were reddish. Completely contrary to this, she deposed that, ...7/­ 7 Spl. Atro.(POCSO) Case No. 29/2013 [ Judg. ] she saw nail abrasions on neck and chest of her baby. She further saw that, her skin was reddish. Thus, there is material contradiction on the point of alleged abrasions on the particular part of the body of Tanvi where the abrasions were seen by the complainant Aarti. Similarly her statement regarding keeping open the zip pant of the accused seems to be imaginary and to implead this accused in a case. It is not the case of Aarti that when she returned to the shop of accused, her daughter was weeping/crying etc.. 11] There are improvements in the deposition of complainant. She stated before this court that, she had been to the shop of accused on 20/4/2013. She stated that, after 20 minutes she returned to the shop. She stated before this court that, on next day at 8.00 p.m. accused while passing by her house gave her angry gesture. All these material facts are missing from the complaint. These are nothing but omissions amounting to contradictions. This can be taken other way as additions or improvements which are not acceptable. 12] She deposed in her deposition that, police typed her complaint at about 12.00 to 1.00 p.m.. However when she lodged complaint is not specifically stated by her. 13] There is delay of near about seven days in lodging the complaint. The delay is not satisfactorily explained. And ...8/­ 8 Spl. Atro.(POCSO) Case No. 29/2013 [ Judg. ] therefore delay in lodging the complaint is fatal to the case of prosecution. 14] The shop of accused is located in the crowded locality. Customers used to there in the shop of accused. There are people in front of the shop of the accused. In such crowded locality committing sexual assault on 17 months' old child seems to be not possible and probable. 15] There is no specific concrete allegation of committing a specific act by the accused. In entire complaint of the complainant only suspicion is expressed that accused might have been committed sexual assault on the minor girl Tanvi. It is nowhere mentioned in the complaint that how and by which method accused committed sexual assault of Tanvi. Regarding abrasions over chest, neck and cheek there are material contradictions. Those are not concretely proved. No other particular act of assault is alleged by the complainant. In such state of facts by any stretch of imagination it cannot be said that, prosecution has succeeded to prove the alleged guilt of accused beyond all reasonable doubts. And hence I answer the point in negative and pass the following order :­ ORDER 1. Accused Arun Dattu Madhavi, is hereby acquitted of the offence punishable under Section 8 of the Protection of ...9/­ 9 Spl. Atro.(POCSO) Case No. 29/2013 [ Judg. ] Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012 . 2. His bail bond stands cancelled. He is set at liberty. 3. Accused to furnish bail under section 437(A) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 4. Copy of this Judgment be sent to the trial court. Kalyan Dt : 17/4/2017 [ D.S. Hatarote ] Dist. Judge­2 & Addl. 1 Spl. Case 28/2013[J.] Presented on :­ 1/10/2013 Registered on :­ 1/10/2013 Decided on :­ 31/10/2015 Duration : Y. M. ­D. 2 ­ 0. 30 . Exh.28 IN THE COURT OF SPECIAL JUDGE, KALYAN, AT : KALYAN. Special Case No.28/2013 [Presided over by M.J.Mirza] The State of Maharashtra. Through P.I. Ambernath Police Station. ...Complainant. Vs. Rahul Kashinath Sonkar, Age : 19 years, Occ.: Labour, R/at : Char Banglow, opp. Gurudwara, Under Over bridge, On Footpath, Andheri (W), Mumbai – 53. ….Accused. Appearance : A.P.P.Smt. J.S.Lohakare for the State. Advocate Shri. R.R.Paramane for the accused. Offences : ­ Punishable under section 363, 366­A, & 376 of IPC & S. 4 r/w. Sec. 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act,2012 . :JUDGMENT: [Delivered on 31/10/2015, in the open Court.] 1] The accused Rahul Kashinath Sonkar, is facing the trial for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 366­A & 376 of IPC & S.4 r/w. Sec.8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2 Spl. Case 28/2013[J.] 2] The case of the prosecution, in short is as under : That the complainant PW­2 Sau. Rambha Ravi Bavimani lodged FIR on 15/6/2013 alleging therein that she is residing at Vadolgaon, OT Section, Ulhasnagar No.3 with her husband Ravi and victim aged 15 years in a rental room. He husband is addicted to liquor and jobless. She is working as maid servant at Nerul, which is the only source of income for her family. 3] The victim is studying in 9th std. in S. Nijlingappa Kannada High School, Nalandi road, Ambernath (W). Her school is likely to be started . Prior to Ambernath they were residing at Andheri in Apna Bazar area but there was no convent school and hence they started residing in Ulhasnagar. When they were residing at Andheri, the accused Rahul was acquainted with her minor daughter. 4] On 12/6/2013 as usual she went for work at 7 a.m. and returned at 00­30 a.m. on 13/6/2013. Her husband disclosed her that accused Rahul has made phone call to victim, to spoke with the accused by going out of the house and then she combed her hair and went out of the house under the pretext to answer the nature's call. Her neighbour Vanitabai told to the victim that bathroom is closed and she should not go there and also told her that she should go in jungle in open area. By saying so, she followed her as there was darkness. She saw the accused Rahul was standing near Railway track. When the victim reached near the accused Rahul, he caught hold her hand and took her towards Ulhasnagar Railway Station. As she was unable to walk fast, she did not follow them. This fact was disclosed to her by her husband. Then she 3 Spl. Case 28/2013[J.] rushed towards Ulhasnagar Railway Station, but her victim daughter and accused Rahul not traced and hence she returned to home. Her victim daughter had taken her cell No.9823774797, therefore, she made call on the said cell phone on 13/6/2013. She asked her where she is, who disclosed that she is with accused Rahul and she will not return to home. Therefore, the accused Rahul induced her to marry and kidnapped from her lawful guardianship on 12/6/2013 at 11­30 p.m. 5] PSO Ambernath police station registered the Crime at C.R.No. I­108/2013 under Section 363 of IPC. Further investigation was entrusted to PSI Smt.Mane who received the FIR (Exh.11), spot panchanama (Exh.12) and case diary of PSO Gosavi. She recorded the statement of the vcitim she stated that she has performed marriage with accused in Temple at Andheri and there was physical relations with the accused with her consent. She was sent for her medical examination alongwith her letter­ Exh.20. She arrested the accused on 26/6/2013. The complainant produced the clothes on the person of the victim in the police station which were seized under panchanama­Exh.14. The accused produced his clothes under discovery panchanama in pursuance of his voluntary statement­ Ex.21 before the panch witnesses. He led them to Andheri and produced his clothes which were seized under seizure panchanama­Exh.22. On 8/7/2013 she handed over investigation to PSI Dighe (PW­4). 6] PW­4 PSI Dighe obtained the bonafide certificate­ Exh.24 of the victim from her school. He also received the medical papers of the victim from Central hospital produced at 4 Spl. Case 28/2013[J.] Exh.25. According to him the victim was minor on the date of the incident. After completion of investigation, he filed charge sheet in this Special Court. 7] Charge vide Ex.6 was framed which was read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. The accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. His defence is of false involvement as per his statement recorded under Section 313 of Code of Criminal Procedure. Neither the accused stepped into the witness­box nor he examined any defence witness. 8] Heard learned APP Smt. J. S. Lohokare for the State and learned Advocate Shri R. R.Paramane for the accused, at length. 9] The following points arise for my determination. The points and my findings alongwith reasons thereon are recorded against them for the reasons to follow:­ Points Findings 1 Whether the prosecution has proved that the victim was minor on the date of incident ? .. Yes. 2 Whether prosecution has proved that on 12/6/2013 at about 11 p.m., at Vadolgaon, near railway track Ambernath and Andheri (W) Mumbai­53 the accused, kidnapped the victim, a minor under 14 years from her lawful guardianship, punishable u/sec.363 of IPC ? ..... Not proved. 3 Whether prosecution has proved that on the aforesaid date, time and place, the accused induced minor victim to go from Ambernath with intent that 5 Spl. Case 28/2013[J.] she may be forced to illicit intercourse, punishable under S.366­A …Not proved. of IPC? 4 Whether prosecution has proved that on the aforesaid date, time and place, the accused committed rape on minor victim aged 14 years, punishable under S.376 of IPC? …Not proved. 5 Whether the prosecution has proved that the accused committed penetrative sexual assault on the minor victim girl, aged 14 years, punishable under Sec. 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual …Not proved. Offences Act, 2012 ? 6 What order ? ….. Accused acquitted. REASONS : 10] To substantiate the charge, the prosecution has examined only four witnesses viz. P.W.1 the victim (Exh.9), P.W.2­ Smt. Rambha Ravi Bavimani, informant and mother of the victim, (Exh.10) who lodged the FIR (Exh.11) and set criminal law in motion, PW­3 API Smt. Manisha Shankar Mane, IO(Exh.19), who carried out the investigation partly, drew the spot panchanama­ Exh.12 and arrested the accused. She also seized the clothes of the victim produced by the informant under seizure panchanama­Exh.14. She also seized the clothes on the person of accused in view of disclosure statement made by the accused vide Exh.21 and seizure panchanama­Exh.22. Lastly, PW­4 PSI Shri. Sanket Vasantrao Dighe (Exh.23) who carried out the remaining investigation by collecting bonafide certificate of the victim at Exh.24 from the school and her medical papers at Exh.25 and then filed the chargesheet. 6 Spl. Case 28/2013[J.] As to point No. 1. 11] The informant in her FIR­Exh.11 stated that the age of victim is 14 year who was studying in Kannada High School, Ambernath(W). PW­4 IO, PSI Dighe during the investigation collected bonafide­cum­character certificate of the victim dt.3/8/2013 showing her birth date as per general register of the High school was 3/7/1998. This being the public document is admissible in evidence. It bears seal of the high school and stamp of the Head Master with signature and hence falls within the purview of S. 74 of the Indian Evidence Act. Moreover, the defence has admitted bonafide certificate as genuineness thereof is not disputed. Therefore, to determine the age of the minor victim, the bonafide certificate Exh.24 can be taken into consideration. As per the birth date mentioned therein as 30/7/1998 and the date of incident was 12/6/2013. Thus, the age of the victim on the date of the incident was 14 years 10 months and 12 days. Hence, I hold that the victim girl was minor and as such I answer point No.1, in the affirmative. As to point No.2 to 5 : 12] I have taken both these points together as they are interlinked and would be proper to discuss and analyse the evidence adduced by the prosecution. 13] The defence has admitted the spot panchanama ­Exh.12, personal search panchanama for the accused ­Exh.13 and seizure of clothes panchanama of the victim produced by the informant at Exh.14 are admitted by defence as genuineness therein is not disputed. The CA certificate produced at Exh.15, 16 & 17 are admissible under Section of 293 the Code of Criminal Procedure, hence they are exhibited. 7 Spl. Case 28/2013[J.] No semen or blood was detected on the clothes of the accused vide Exh.15 and clothes of the victim Exh.16. However her blood group is of “O”. The blood group of the accused is “A” vide Exh.17. 14] For the offence punishable under S. 363 of IPC, it is necessary for the prosecution to prove “taking'' or ''enticing'' away a minor under 16 years of age, if a male and under 18 years of age, if a female. Further, ''taking'' or ''enticing'' must be out of keeping of the lawful guardian of such minor and such ''taking'' or ''enticing'' must be without consent of such guardian. 15] For the offence punishable under Sec. 366­A of IPC it is necessary for the prosecution to prove that the accused induced victim minor girl under the age of 18 years to go from any place or to do any act with intent that such girl may be or knowing that it is likely that she will be, forced or seduced to illicit intercourse with other person. 16] For the offence punishable under Sec. 376 of IPC, it is necessary for the prosecution to prove that the accused penetrates his pennis to any extent into the vagina etc., with or without her consent when she is under 18 years of age is said to commit rape. 17] In view of these essential ingredients of the charges levelled against the accused the evidence of the prosecution is required to be assessed to prove the guilt of the accused. The evidence of the victim PW­1 has been recorded in­camera and it is brought on record that her father expired before four years who as jobless and her mother is working as 8 Spl. Case 28/2013[J.] maid servant at Nerul, Navi Mumbai. She used to leave the house at 8­30 a.m. and returns at 10­30 p. to11 p.m. she was studying in 8th std. in Nijlingappa Kannada high school, Ambernath. She states her birth date as 30/9/1998. When she was residing at 4 bungalow, Andheri in hutment area the accused Rahul was her naighbour. He was residing in the same area at two distance from her house. Therefore, she had acquaintance with him and they both were friends and fall in love. They used to roam in garden, etc. and whenever she used to meet the accused, her parents used to assault her. She states about the incident in June,2013 in noon time, she told to the accused and she is coming to him. The accused replied her to come and accordingly she went to Andheri from Ulhasnagar. The accused told her to stay with him. Then she showed her reluctance to go back to her parents home as they would assault her. Then she expressed her desire to the accused that she want to marry with him. 18] In the presence of one of the friend by name Sonu of accused, they both performed marriage in a temple at Andheri. After 2­3 days she received phone call from her mother that she is ailing therefore she went to Ulhasnagar and then her mother took her to the P{S where her statement was recorded. She had also shown the place to the police where she had gone. Thereafter she was sent for her medical examination, Since then she is staying with her mother. 19] In her testimony, she stated that on her own accord she went to Andheri from Ulhasnagnar. As per her wish she married with the accused and stayed with accused Rahul for 2­3 days but she had no physical relations with him 9 Spl. Case 28/2013[J.] 20] PW­2 Smt. Rambha Ravi Bavimani (Exh.10), the mother of the victim who lodged the FIR Exh.18 knows the accused Rahul, who was neighbour when she was residing at Andheri. She lodged the FIR against the accused Rahul with Ambernath PS as her daughter had gone with the accused at Andheri. She was knowing the love affair of her minor daughter and accused Rahul but she was disliking her relations with the accused. On that reason there was quarrel and hence her minor daughter went to the accused and she did not return to her home. According to her she lodged the FIR due to irritation. 21] PW­3 API Smt. Manisha Shankar Mane­Ex.19, the IO and PW­ 4 PSI Shri.Shankar Vasantrao Dighe (Exh.20) are the investigating officer who carried out the investigation. 22] As the victim and her mother both have brought on record that the victim left the house on her own accord and went to the accused. She married with the accused in temple at Andheri and stayed with the accused for 2­3 days in the house of his friend Sonu. The victim stated that she had no physical relations with the accused. However, the medical certificate of the victim produced at Exh.25 shows her hymen was torn, hence it can be inferred that there was physical relations in between the victim and the accused. Moreover, there is nothing on record to hold that the accused forced the victim for illicit intercourse by inducing her. Therefore, in absence of ingredients of the offences, I hold that the prosecution has proved the points no. 2 to 4, in the negative. 10 Spl. Case 28/2013[J.] As to point No. 5:­ 23] The requirement for the offence punishable under Section 8 of the POSCO Act, 2012, is that the accused penetrates his pennis to any extent into the vagina etc., of a child or makes the child to do so with him so as to cause penetration into the vagina etc. is said to commit the offence of penetrative sexual assault. Here in the case on hand, the material witness was the victim, however, she has denied any physical relations with the accused even after the marriage performed in a temple, who stayed with him for 2­3 days. Absolutely, there is nothing on record to hold that the accused committed penetrative sexual assault on the victim in any manner. Her evidence was material on this point but she has not supported the case of the prosecution. The learned APP though cross­examined the victim and the informant, with the permission of the Court but nothing fruitful has brought on record to hold the accused guilty. Hence, I answer the point No.5, in the negative. 24] Resultantly, the accused deserves to be acquitted, and as such, I proceed to pass the following order : : ORDER : 1] Accused Rahul Kashinath Sonkar, is hereby acquitted under S. 235(1) of Cr.P.C. of the offences punishable under Sections 363, 366­A and 376 of IPC & S. 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] The accused is in jail. He be set at liberty forthwith, if not required in any other crime or case. 3] Muddemal property, if any, be destroyed after appeal period is over. 11 Spl. Case 28/2013[J.] 4] The accused shall execute his P.R. and S.B. of Rs.15,000/­ to appear before the Higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect of appeal filed against this judgment as per S. 437­A of Cr.P.C. 5] Such bail shall remain in force for six months from today. ORDER BELOW EXH­3 IN ANTICIPATORY BAIL APPLICATION NO. 1068 /2018. (CNR NO.MHTH06­002284­2018) 1] By this application filed under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. accused viz. Dnyaneshwar Rajaram Shid has prayed for interim pre­arrest bail in connection with C.R.No.No.I­164/2018 under Section 376 of I.P.C. and Section 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 registered with Kalyan Taluka Police Station. 2] I have perused application and heard learned advocate for the accused. 3] Case of prosecution in brief is that informant is 17 years old minor girl and her name is kept secret. She lodged report to police that in the year 2016 after passing S.S.C. she started doing the job as Helper in Technocraft Company and there she became familiar with accused and thereafter their love affair started and thereafter in July 2016 she left the job and took admission in Goveli Colelge. Even then accused used to meet her and that during the period from August 2017 to March 2018 accused from time to time took her to Thakurpada and by the side of the road in the bushes accused without her consent kept physical relation with her by giving promise that he would marry with her and thereby accused made her pregnant and that at the time of filing complaint she was carrying pregnancy of five months. Since accused was not giving reply to the phone of informant, informant lodged this report. So, on the report of informant aforesaid crime was registered. 4] It is argued by learned advocate for accused that there was love affair between informant and accused and compromise has taken place between both the parties and that victim girl has filed 2 ABA No.1068/2018(Or.Exh.3) affidavit also. It is further submitted that the victim girl has stated that she has no objection if the anticipatory bail is granted to the accused and that she has further stated that accused always wanted to marry with her but since she was minor marriage could not be performed. It is therefore submitted that application may be allowed. 5] Considering the nature of the allegation and the fact that at the time of incident informant was minor and consent given by the informant (i.e. minor girl) for the said sexual intercourse does not amount to be the valid consent and at that at the time of lodging complaint she was carrying five months pregnancy, I am of the view that application is not tenable. Hence, I pass following order :­ ORDER 1. Application is rejected. 2. As the application Exh­3 for interim pre­arrest bail is rejected the main application for anticipatory bail is also rejected. Kalyan (A.A.A.Shaikh) Dt.:­ 03.07.2018. Additional Sessions Judge, Kalyan.

1 ORDER BELOW EXH.1 IN ANTI.BAIL APPLN.NO.1105/2018 : (CNR MHTH060023572018) 1] Read application and say of the prosecution. Perused documents. Heard Ld.A.P.P. for State and Ld. Adv. for applicant/ accused at length. 2] This is an application U/sec.438 of Cr.P.C for anticipatory bail. 3] Crime bearing No.I­30/17 is registered against these applicants/accused (1) Shanti Sudhendra Selvan and (2) Sudhendra Selvan in Ambernath police station for the offences punishable U/Secs. 363, 376 r.w 34 of I.P.C and Sec.4 of POCSO Act. As these accused apprehends their arrest by Ambernath police they have filed this application for anticipatory bail. 4] Allegation of the prosecution is that, son of these applicants viz. Manoharan kidnapped minor daughter of complainant Kum. Sneha Santosh Mishra, took her to his native at Vellanur, Tal.Awadi, Dist. Tamil Nadu and committed there rape on her against her will. It is further allegation of the prosecution that, these applicants helped absconding accused Manoharan, their son to commit the above stated offences. They instigated Manoharan to have a sexual intercourse with the minor daughter of complainant. They have not cooperated the police machinery in the investigation. 2 Therefore crime is also registered against them. 5] In this application it is the say of these applicants that, they are innocent. They have committed no offence. They are always ready to cooperate investigation machinery in the investigation. Even previously whenever the Ambernath Police had been to their village Vellanur they helped the Investigating Officer, handed over the victim girl. However, not only once but thrice the victim girl herself eloped with Manoharan. At present they did not know whereabouts of Manoharan Selvan and the minor victim. They are respectable persons in the society. They are ready to cooperate investigating machinery. They are ready to abide by any condition. They prayed that they be released on anticipatory bail. 6] This application is strongly opposed by the prosecution. It is the say of prosecution that these applicants are not cooperating the Investigating Officer. They have knowledge of the whereabouts of the victim girl and their son Manoharan Selvan. However they are not ready to provide information about them to Investigating machinery. If these accused persons released on bail they may help the main accused Manoharan Selvan to stay away from the hands of police. they will create obstructions or hindrance in the investigation process. Therefore prosecution prayed that application be rejected. 7] Offence is of serious nature. After going through papers on record it seems that, since about last one year whereabouts of 3 Manoharan Selvan and the victim girl are not traceable. Investigating machinery is trying its level best to find out them. However, it seems that these present applicants do not cooperate investigating machinery. Being a son there is every possibility and probability that these applicants may know whereabouts of their son Manoharan Selvan. To enquire about this custodial interrogation of both these applicants is necessary. The father of the victim girl i.e. complainant appeared before this court. This court heard him. Definitely his concern about whereabouts of his daughter carry much weight and that is natural one. No one knows what happened with the minor girl. Whether she is compelled to any illegal act. Where her life is safe or not. No one knows since last one year. Being the parents of Manoharan Selvan there is probability that these applicants may know the whereabouts of their son Manoharan Selvan. It is vehemently argued by Investigating officer that from the call details the Investigating Officer came to know that one mobile of Manoharan Selvan in use of this applicant No.1. There were some communication between Manoharan and these applicants. Those are to be traced out and enquired into. In my opinion these are the good grounds for asking the custody of these applicants for custodial interrogation. In these facts and circumstances it is not worth to grant anticipatory bail to these applicants. Hence, I pass the following order : :ORDER: 1) The application is rejected. 2) The applicants/accused are hereby directed to surrender 4 before Investigating Officer immediately. 3) Inform to the police station accordingly. Kalyan. (D.S. Hatarote) 22/10/2018 Addl. Sessions Judge, Kalyan.

Atro. Special Case No. 87/2017 Order Below Exh. 3 commission of offence, hence, he should be termed as Juvenile Conflict With Law, and thus, his trial should be conducted before the Ld. Juvenile Justice Board according to the Law. With this conclusion, I am inclined to allow the application by accepting the plea of juvenility, as prayed for, by the applicant on behalf of Shaileshkumar. Hence, following order : : ORDRR : I] The application for transferring the present trial before the Juvenile Justice Board is hereby allowed. II] The trial against Shaileshkumar, S/o. Suresh kumar be tried before the Juvenile Justice Board being Juvenile Conflict With Law. III] The Record and Proceeding of Atro. Special Case No. 87/2017 be sent to the Juvenile Justice Board, Bhiwandi for trial against the Juvenile Conflict With Law Shaileshkumar. 1 Atro. Spl. Case No. 143/2014 (Common Order below Exhs.1 & 17) CNR No. MHTH06­002561­2014 COMMON ORDER BELOW EXHS. 1 & 17 IN ATRO. SPECIAL CASE NO. 143/2014 CNR No. MHTH06­002561­2014 1] The accused Mohammad Shamshad Ali Ulhasan Maniyar has filed present application seeking discharge under secs. 363, 366, 376 of IPC and under secs. 3, 4 & 12 of POCSO Act which was registered at Kolsewadi police station vide Cr. No. I­327/2014. 2] The accused case in brief is that ­ He is prosecuted in Atro. Special Case No. 143/2014 wherein one victim's father Shamim Khurshid Alam Khan has lodged a report on 13/8/2014 and alleged that, he is having one daughter Suhana from his first marriage and she was running at the age of 15 years in the year 2014. On 29/6/2014 she had gone alongwith the accused who had enticed her and committed rape. Police have investigated the matter and filed chargesheet. The accused is seeking discharge under sec. 227 of Cr.P.C.. 3] The accused contention is that, the victim Suhana herself made police statement wherein she has clearly mentioned that, on the alleged date of incident she was major. Moreover, her statement was recorded under sec. 164 of Cr.P.C. before the Magistrate wherein she has mentioned her date of birth as 25/5/1995. The victim herself denied either 2 Atro. Spl. Case No. 143/2014 (Common Order below Exhs.1 & 17) CNR No. MHTH06­002561­2014 any force by the accused or the rape contention. Therefore, according to the accused, the charge itself is futile. Hence, he urged to discharge. 4] Learned APP has resisted the application by filing say that, there is iota of evidence against the accused. In the FIR itself name of the accused is clearly attributed. Moreover, the date of birth of the victim is 25/5/2001. Hence, she was minor on the alleged date of incident. Eventually, the consent of the victim cannot be considered. The allegations in respect of kidnapping needs to be considered, even if the rape allegations are vanished. This is a very premature application. Hence, learned APP urged for rejection of the application. 5] Heard both the sides. At the outset and on bare perusal of the police statement of victim Suhana, it reveals that, she has categorically stated that, on the date of alleged incident she was running at the age of 19 years. She herself went alongwith the accused and performed marriage. There were no sexual relations in between them. She has denied all the allegations levelled by her father. Thereafter, she has made statement before the court that under sec. 164 of Cr.P.C.. It is pertinent to note that, in that statement also the victim has clearly denied the alleged incident of rape and kidnapping. Nevertheless, she has categorically stated that, her date of birth is 25/5/1995, but her father has falsely shown her minor only 3 Atro. Spl. Case No. 143/2014 (Common Order below Exhs.1 & 17) CNR No. MHTH06­002561­2014 to indulge the accused in the present crime. 6] In the light of the statement of the victim, if we go through the FIR and other police statements available on record, it can be seen that, there is no iota of evidence against the accused. Even, at this juncture, date of birth of the victim is debatable, but prima facie, I find that, when the victim was not intending to make any allegations against the accused, in such situation there may be no change in the attitude or behaviour of the victim while deposing before the court also. Ultimate result would be the acquittal of the case, rather unfortunately, I find except the bare FIR of the complainant, I do not find any reasonable consonance to implead the accused in the present crime. In these set of circumstances when whole episode of the alleged incident took place at the consent of the victim or even for the sake of moment, it is assumed that, the victim was kidnapped, but in the later part, if there was no rape then the case of the prosecution has no legs and it has to be demolished at any stage. 7] After considering all the facts, circumstances and available evidence on record, I hold that, the prosecution has no case to prove the guilt of accused. The application filed for discharge is considerable and acceptable. Resultantly, the accused is entitled to get discharge. Hence I proceed to pass following order :­ 4 Atro. Spl. Case No. 143/2014 (Common Order below Exhs.1 & 17) CNR No. MHTH06­002561­2014 ORDER 1] The applications are hereby allowed. 2] The accused ­ Mohammad Shamshad Ali Ulhasan Maniyar is hereby discharged from the offence punishable under secs. 363, 366, 376 of the IPC and under secs. 3, 4 & 12 of POCSO Act which was registered at Kolsewadi police station vide Cr. No. I­327/2014. 3] His bail bond stands cancelled. 4] Muddemal property, if any, be disposed of according to law. 5] Case is accordingly disposed of. Kalyan. (N.M. Waghmare) Date :­21/2/2018 Dist. ( Delivered in open court on 10th January, 2017 ) 1. This accused is prosecuted by Manpada police station for the offence punishable under section 354(A)(1) of the Indian Penal Code and under section 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Prosecution story in brief is as follows. 2. Kum. Shantu Dilip Jagtap aged 15 years lodged complaint against this accused on 21/06/2014. She is step daughter of this accused. The complainant's mother after death of the father of complainant married with accused and started residing with accused. Obviously, the complainant started residing with this accused. On 28/05/2014 complainant came to Manpada police station and gave statement that accused beat her and abused her on the suspicion that this complainant Shantu has love affairs with one Nikhil Shinde. Therefore, on 29/05/2014 Manpada police sent the complainant to Children Rehabilitation Home at Bhiwandi. On 30/05/2014 as per the order of Children Welfare Committee she was sent to Women's Reformation Home at Ulhasnagar. It is further say of the complainant that in the month of February 2013 at about 6.30 a.m. when her mother had been to fetch water and when she was sleeping, this accused came near her, he fondled her and tried to (3) Spl. Case No. 146/2014 (J) remove her clothes. Similar incident took place after some days in the month of November 2013. At that time this accused pressed breast of the complainant. Complainant narrated this incident to her mother and grandmother, but they do not pay any heed. Therefore, complainant stated this incident to her class teachers Mirge madam and Wani madam. They took the complainant to the Manpada police station. Thereafter complaint was lodged by the complainant against this accused. On her complaint crime was registered as C.R. No.314/2014. Investigation was carried by one Dattatraya Landage then P.S.I. of Manpada police station. 3. During investigation the I.O. recorded statements of the witnesses and after completion of investigation submitted chargesheet against the accused in court. 4. Accused appeared before this court. Charge against him is framed at Exh.4. Charge was read over and explained to him in Marathi language. He pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. His defence is of total denial. 5. Prosecution was directed to adduce its evidence. In response to that prosecution examined P.W. No.1 Shantu Jagtap the complainant at Exh.7. P.W. No.2 Dattatraya Landage (Exh.8) is the I.O. Except this, no other evidence is adduced by the prosecution. 6. I have gone through the evidence on record. I have heard both learned advocates. Following points arise for my consideration. My findings on those points are as follows for the reasons stated (4) below. POINTS FINDINGS 1) Does prosecution prove that in the month of February 2013 and November 2013 at his house at Yogeshwar Photo Studio, Chera Nagar, Sagaon, Dombivali (E) accused made physical contact with complainant and advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 354(A)(1) of the I.P.C.? No. 2) Does prosecution further prove that on the above­said period and place accused committed sexual assault on complainant who is minor aged about 15 years and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 ? No. REASONS As to Points no. 1 and 2:­ 7. P.W. No.1 Shantu Jagtap the complainant has not supported the prosecution. She deposed that accused was not allowing her to talk with her friend Nikhil. And therefore, she lodged complaint against the accused. Police sent her to Sunrise Happy Children home, Badlapur. After some days police came there and (5) Spl. Case No. 146/2014 (J) obtained her signature on some paper. She denied the contents in the complaint though she admitted her signature on the complaint. The contents in the complaint are not proved. This witness is cross examined at length by learned APP. However, in her cross examination nothing incriminating against the accused is brought on record. Thus, the evidence of P.W. No.1 Shantu is not supporting to the prosecution. She has not uttered a single incriminating word against the accused. 8. P.W. No.2 Dattatraya Landage is I.O. He deposed his investigation. However, his evidence is not direct one. Even he has not uttered a single incriminating word against the accused. He simply stated that he recorded statement of complainant as well as other witnesses and thereafter submitted the chargesheet. Thus, his single statement that he found sufficient evidence against the accused to prosecute him is not at all sufficient to prove the guilt of accused beyond all reasonable doubts. 9. As there is no incriminating evidence against the accused, his statement under section 313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure stands dispensed with. 10. For want of incriminating evidence against this accused, I answer both points in negative. 11. In conclusion, I pass the following order. (6) O R D E R 1) The accused Dilip Bhika Jagtap is hereby acquitted of the offence punishable under Section 354(A)(1) of the Indian Penal Code and under section 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2) His bail bonds stands cancelled. He is set at liberty. 3) Accused to furnish bail under section 437(A) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Kalyan ( D.S. Sarswati Classes situated at Phule Road, Dombivali. At that time accused Raj Parkar along with his aforesaid two friends came there on Activa vehicle and they suddenly caught her hand and at that time accused Raj Parkar told her “you make friendship with me; if you don't make friendship with me; I will assault on your mouth; you don't talk with anybody otherwise I will kill you and your mother”. In this way he threatened her. At that time accused Raj Parkar and his two friends threatened informant's friend Shubhangi Rathod by saying “you don't interfere in our matter; if don't let us make friendship then keep in mind we will see you”. At that time aforesaid two friends who were present with Raj Parkar asked the informant to make friendship with Raj Parkar and not to talk with any other person. Because of that incident the modesty of the informant was outraged and she got very much frightened. At that time she was so much frightened that she did not inform this fact to her mother also. But since accused persons started harassing her furthermore and they started keeping watch over her and they were also keeping watch over the house of her 4 Spl. Case No.24/2013 (Judgment) terrace, she informed this fact to her mother and thereafter she lodged complaint and that on the report of the informant offences punishable under Sections 354­D, 506 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code and under Section 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 was registered by Vishnunagar Police Station vide C.R.No.I­35/2013. Police recorded statements of witnesses and police drew panchnama of place of incident and after completion of investigation charge­ sheet was filed. 4] Charge at Exh.3 under Sections 354­D, 506 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code and under Section 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 was framed against accused. Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 5] After recording evidence and hearing both the sides following points arise for my determination and I have noted my findings against each of them for the reason to follow: Points Findings 1. Whether it is proved by prosecution that accused Nos.1 to 3 in furtherance of their common intention followed informant and contacted her and attempted to contact her to foster personal interaction repeatedly despite a 5 Spl. Case No.24/2013 (Judgment) clear indication of disinterest by .. Not proved. the informant ? 2. Whether it is proved by prosecution that accused Nos.1 to 3 in furtherance of their common intention threatened the informant and the witness Shubhangi Rathod .. Not proved. with intent to cause alarm to them ? 3. What offences, if any are proved .. No offence is proved against against accused ? accused. : REASONS : As to Point Nos.1 to 4 :­ 6] Perusal of the evidence of the informant (PW­1) shows that in the year 2013 she was studying in 9 th standard of Mahatma Gandhi Vidyamandir School situated at Dombivali (W). She has identified accused Nos.1 to 3 present in the Court. Her evidence 6 Spl. Case No.24/2013 (Judgment) further shows that on 01.01.2013 at about 7.30 p.m. she went to see the Festival (programme) of Konkan Mahostav in Bagshala Ground, Dombivali (W). Crowd of person were there and she got pushed in that crowd but she did not know who pushed her in that crowd. After that incident she lodged her complaint to police. Her evidence further shows that on 02.03.2013 no incident took place. She has identified her signature on complaint but she has deposed that she does not know about its contents. She is cross­examined by learned APP but she has not supported the prosecution case. However, she has admitted in her cross­ examination that compromise has taken place between her and accused out of Court. Under the circumstances, it can be said that informant has not supported the prosecution case. 7] Evidence of Shubhangi Gopinath Rathod (P.W.2) shows that it has not happened that in her presence accused Raj Parkar came there and asked the informant (victim girl) to help him in making friendship with Prachi Jadhav. She has further deposed that it has not happened that at that time informant refused to do the same. She has further deposed that it has not happened that on so many occasions accused Raj Parkar with his two friends harassed the informant by asking her to help him to make friendship with Prachi Jadhav. Her evidence further shows that on 02.03.2013 at about 6.30 p.m. near Bhagshala Maidan no incident took place in front of her and the informant and that police did not inquire with her about the incident and that police did not record her statement. She is cross­examined by learned APP but she has not supported the prosecution case. However, 7 Spl. Case No.24/2013 (Judgment) she has also denied that compromise has taken place between accused, herself and the informant. Therefore, it can be said that this witness has also not supported the prosecution case. 8] Evidence of Ashish Gopinath Rathod (P.W.3) shows that it has not happened that his sister told her that accused Raj Parkar with his two friends from time to time harasses informant by asking her to help him in making friendship with Prachi Jadhav. His evidence further shows that it has not happened that on 02.03.2013 his sister by making phone call to him informed him about the incident pertaining to accused and that police neither inquired with him about the incident nor recorded his statement. He is cross­examined by learned APP but nothing is brought on record to show that he has not supported the prosecution case. He has also denied the suggestion that since compromise has taken place between accused and them he deposed falsely to save accused. Under the circumstances, it can be said that prosecution has failed to prove its case. Accordingly, my answer to point Nos.1 to 3 is not proved and my answer to point No.4 is that no offence is proved against accused. Consequently, accused is entitled for acquittal. 1 Order below Ex.1 in Anticipatory Criminal Bail Application No.1097/2015 Mr. Santosh Ramakant Tiwari ….. Applicant Vs. State of Maharashtra, (Through Hill Line Police Station) ….. Opponent 1/­ This is an application for anticipatory bail filed under section 438 of Cr. P.C. in C.R.No. I­268/2014 of Hill Line Police Station for the offence punishable under sections 363, 366, 376 r/w. 34 of IPC. 2/­ The applicant/accused has contended that he is practicing Advocate and he has only put his signature as identifying witness and on the declaration form of marriage of one Miss Fatima Shaikh with Mr. Sahil Aleem Shaikh. He has further contended that the document of declaration of marriage is prepared on the basis of Nikahnama dated 07.11.2014 and he has no role in performing the marriage of the victim girl with one Sahil Aleem Shaikh as same is performed by one Kazi. He has further contended that he has identified said Shaikhs as they have showed Adhar Cards as their identity proofs. He lastly prayed for granting him anticipatory bail. 3/­ The Investigation Officer has resisted the application by filing his Say at Exh.8 inter alia contending that this applicant who is Advocate by profession, in collusion with other accused has helped to perform marriage of victim girl who is minor. It is further contended that the applicant has done illegal act by identifying the victim and one Sahil alias Ajaj Aalam Abdul Ajij Shah. The Investigation Officer has further 2 contended that the applicant, if enlarged on bail will tamper with the evidence by pressurizing or threatening the informant and other witness witnesses. He lastly prayed for rejecting the application. 4/­ Heard Ld. Advocate Shri R.J. Baddam for applicant/accused and Ld. APP Ms. R.R. Bhoir for the State. 5/­ After considering the rival submissions, now it is to be seen as to whether the custodial interrogation of the applicant is necessary. After going through the contents of the FIR it is seen that the informant has lodged it contending that one Abdul, his father Abdul Rashid Shah, uncle Abdul Ajij Shah in collusion with each other kidnapped her minor daughter with intention of marrying her with one Ajij Abdul Rashid Shah. It is pertinent to note that there is no whisper against this applicant. The applicant is a practicing Advocate who has merely put his signature on the document of declaration of marriage for the purpose of identification. Apart from said act, there is no overt act on the part of the applicant. The Investigation Officer can very well obtain, if required, said document from the applicant for which he may be given directions by this Court. Therefore, I am of the opinion that there is no need of custodial interrogation of the applicant. The apprehension in the mind of Investigation Officer can be taken care of by imposing certain conditions on the applicant. Accordingly, I pass following order : ORDER 1] The application is hereby allowed. 2] In the event of arrest of applicant/accused Shri Santosh Ramakant Tiwari in C.R. No. I­268/2014 of Hill Line Police Station for the offence punishable under sections 363, 366, 376 r/w.34 of IPC, he 3 be released on his executing P.R. Bond of Rs. 25,000/­ (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand Only) with one or two solvent sureties in the aggregate amount. 3] The applicant shall mark his presence in Hill Line Police Station on every Wednesday in between 11.00 a.m. to 1.00 p.m. till further orders and shall co­operate police in investigation. 4] The applicant shall not tamper with the evidence. 5] Inform concerned Police Station accordingly. Kalyan. (S.B. Gaidhani) 03/09/2015 Addl. Sessions Judge, Kalyan.

My findings on those points are as follows for the reasons stated below : POINTS FINDINGS 1 Does prosecution prove that accused committed rape on minor victim girl, aged 9 years and thereby committed an offence punishable U/sec.376(f) of Indian Penal Code? ...Yes, it is proved. 2 Does prosecution prove that accused induced victim girl aged 16 years at various places from time to time to go from Kalyan to CST or to do acts of illicit intercourse with the passengers traveling in trains with intent that the said victim girl may be or knowing that it is likely that the said victim will be ...Yes, it is proved. forced to illicit intercourse and thereby committed an offence punishable U/Sec.366A of I.P.C. ? 3. No doubt it is suggested to this witness that, the victim girl was not brought to him on 17.4.13 and no tests were carried by him. However, this suggestion is flatly denied. Then the victim was produced before Child Welfare Committee and as per the direction of Welfare Committee the minor girl was sent to Asha Sadan Dongri on 27.2.12. Both these witnesses are cross­examined at length by the Advocate for accused. However the evidence of both these witnesses on the point of spotting the victim girl and accused in Konark Express on 30.1.12 by both these witnesses and taking them in the custody is totally remained unshaken. Both these witnesses duly proved this fact. There is no reason at all to disbelieve or discredit the evidence of both these witnesses on the point of finding victim girl alongwith accused while begging in Konark Express on 30.01.12. This fact is proved. 16] Evidence of PW.3 Indubai Kachru Kokne is on the fact that in the year 2013 and before that this accused, his wife and children were residing with this witness Indubai at Mharalgaon. This witness Indubai is mother­in­law of accused and grand mother of the complainant. She deposed supporting the GHR S.C.No.19/13 : 13 : Jud. Sessions Case No.19/13 prosecution and proved the fact that in the year 2013 and before that victim girl, this accused, the wife of this accused and other children were residing with her at village Mharalgaon. Sessions Case No.19/13 18] In this case two witnesses are most important upon which the prosecution heavily relied. Those witness are PW.1 complainant herself at Ex.14 and PW.4 Raheen Jummani, the counselor before whom for the first time this complainant narrated the entire story or entire suffering she went. PW.1 victim girl who is complainant in para 2 of her deposition stated that, when she was residing at Mharalgaon i.e. on the house of PW.3 Indubai Kokne, that time accused told her to see his physical relations with her mother. She refused to see those relations. At that time accused compelled her to see their physical relations by assaulting and pinching her. In next para she stated that after 3 to 4 days of this incident in noon time she was alone in the house. Her mother and grand mother had gone out of the house. At that time her father i.e. accused started touching her body and removed her cloths. Then he committed sexual intercourse with her. Accused committed sexual intercourse with her number of times. Accused was not liking to stay in the house of grand mother of the complainant i.e. Indubai Kokne. She further deposed that accused took her to VT station by express train. They alighted on platform No.3 of VT Station. Then she alongwith accused went on platform No.14 and boarded express train. She further deposed that in train her father i.e accused told her that GHR S.C.No.19/13 : 15 : Jud. Sessions Case No.19/13 she should keep physical relations with another persons. He further told that by doing so she may help her brother and sister to complete their education. She will get more money. When she refused to do so accused shouted on her. Then she narrated about her first incident of taking Rs.500/­ from the passenger customer and keeping physical relations with him. She further stated that such incident were taken repeatedly till 30.01.12. She also supported the fact that PW.6 Shashikala and PW.8 Vikas Patil took her in their possession on 30.1.12 in Konark Express at Dadar. Thus about the heinous act of accused the complainant in unambiguous words deposed before the court on oath. 19] It is pertinent to note that on the date of deposition this victim girl was of 17 years old. she had attended the age of understanding. Even then my Ld. predecessor tested her ability to understand the question and to give rational answers. Thereafter he recorded the evidence of victim girl and during that deposition the victim girl has given each and every account of the heinous act of the accused and atrocity committed on her by the accused. This witness is cross examined at length on behalf of the accused but there is nothing in her entire cross­examination to shatter the credibility of her deposition. Not for the first time this witness complainant deposed before the court about the atrocity she undergone at the hands of accused. Before police she narrated the same story in same words. Her deposition is completely corroborating the contents in her complaint. Not only this but for the first time this witness the minor girl disclosed the entire GHR S.C.No.19/13 : 16 : Jud. He used to have forcible relations with her. This was going on for some months. Thereafter accused started taking her to railway for begging at railway station . It is pertinent to note that, here we have to consider the relations between the accused with complainant. Irrespective of these relations the complainant dare to state each and every act of the accused before the court. There is no reason for her to state any, wrong, incorrect, imaginary story or facts against her own father. There is absolutely no reason to disbelieve the version of PW.1 complainant, the minor girl who has undergone all these travesty. The deposition of PW.4 Raheen Jummani is supportive, corroborative to the deposition of PW.1, the victim girl and that strengthen and increases the evidential value of the evidence of PW.1 victim girl. GHR S.C.No.19/13 : 17 : Jud. Sessions Case No.19/13 20] PW.5 Deepali Prakash Kadam is a social worker. She also reiterated the testimony of PW.4 Raheen Jummani. She stated before this court what was stated by Raheen Jummani to her. Raheen Jummani repeated the facts stated to her by victim girl before Deepali Kadam. It means that what was experienced by PW.1 victim girl, she stated to PW.4 Raheen Jummani, the counselor. What was heard by Raheen Jummani from victim girl was further transferred to PW.5 Deepali Kadam, the social worker and then PW.5 prepared the report and submitted the same to Child Welfare Committee, Mumbai. Not only this but PW.5 Deepali further deposed that before preparing the report and submitting the same to Child Welfare Committee she got verified the facts from complainant. During that verification again the complainant reiterated the same facts. Thus there is not a single cranny in the entire evidence of PW.1, PW.4 Raheen Jummani and PW.5 Deepali Kadam to take any sort of doubts. Therefore I accept the evidence of all these three witnesses as it is. Their evidence is credit worthy, believable and true one. Absolutely no reason to discard or disbelieve them. 21] Ld.Advocate for accused Shri.Deshmukh tried his level best to defend his client. But the facts and evidence on record do not support his efforts. He vehemently argued that there is inordinate delay in lodging the complaint. Prosecution has also admitted the fact that there is delay in lodging the complaint. GHR S.C.No.19/13 : 18 : Jud. Sessions Case No.19/13 However it cannot be said that said delay is intentional one or it is fatal to the prosecution case. Here the situation is to be considered. First of all accused is the biological father of victim girl. Atrocity is committed by accused on his own minor girl. At the time of incident the minor girl might have been of 10 to 12 years or something else. She was not at all in a position to understand consequences of the act of the accused and dare to raise voice against the atrocities of the accused on her. Relation was one of the big obstacle in that disclosure. Even otherwise the minor girl was within the complete control of accused. She deposed before the court that accused gave her threat not to disclose the atrocities on her. For that he was beating her, he was pinching her. Even accused tried to blackmail the victim girl emotionally. Victim girl stated that accused compelled her to do the prostitution in railway saying that by that business she will earn more, she will facilitate her sibling to take education. For that purpose doing the business stated by him is necessary etc. For all these reasons definitely the minor girl who has undergone such a trauma of rape on her must have been definitely frightened in mind. PW.4 Raheen Jummani as well as PW.5 Deepali Kadam, PW.6 Shashikala Kale and PW.8 Vikas Patil deposed that, initially the victim girl do not state anything about the atrocities of accused on her. She was taken to the Child Welfare Committee and then she was referred to Asha Sadan because she was found doing the business of prostitution in railway. For the purpose of rehabilitation and rescue of minor girl all initial actions were taken by the social worker, by the railway police, by Child GHR S.C.No.19/13 : 19 : Jud. Sessions Case No.19/13 Welfare Committee, by Asha Sadan and by Raheen Jummani. At that time they were totally unaware about the alleged atrocities of accused on the complainant. Till that there was no case on accused. Only after disclosure of the incident by complainant to PW.4 Raheen Jummani that too after developing the trust between them after number of counseling sittings the facts became open. Thereafter the complainant lodged the complaint and the crime was registered. Here it is worth to note that all these facts came to the light only after getting trust of complainant by PW.4 Raheen Jummani the counselor. It means that these facts were suppressed in the mind of complainant and she had not courage to disclose the atrocities or suffering she undergone at the hands of this accused. Due to these reason the delay is caused in lodging the complaint. Delay is neither intentional nor purposeful. Therefore in this case and in this background and facts delay plays no role in favour of the accused. 22] It is vehemently argued by the Ld. Advocate for accused that, there is no medical evidence on record to show that rape was committed on the complainant minor girl or she was forced to do prostitution in railway. It is highly impossible and improbable to get any medical evidence in this case. Because the medical examination of complainant as well as accused was carried only after lodging the complaint by the complainant with Kalyan Taluka Police Station. It took place after many months of the incident. Considering the lapse of period between happening of the incident and the medical examination there is no possibility GHR S.C.No.19/13 : 20 : Jud. Sessions Case No.19/13 at all to get any medical evidence i.e. finding semen, Vaginal swab etc on the cloths or in the samples taken during the medical examination of the complainant as well as accused. In these facts and circumstances medical evidence cannot be expected at all. 23] It is further vehemently argued by Ld. Advocate for accused that, absolutely no evidence on record to show that this victim girl was doing prostitution in railway in mail or express. No customer is examined by the prosecution or by the Investigation Officer. By any stretch of imagination these arguments are not acceptable. First of all it is highly impossible and improbable to get any lady or any girl doing prostitution or get in compromise position in railway because this is always a secret act. Considering the fact that, the accused was compelling complainant to do prostitution in railways it is highly impossible and improbable to get any customers in such instances. Here the victim herself is continuously and constantly stating that accused compelled her to do the prostitution in railways to earn money. She further deposed that at his instance she does the act of prostitution, got money and handover the same to accused. Why and for what reason the complainant should not be believed? Absolutely no reason to disbelieve the complainant on this point. When the deposition of complainant is trustworthy, believable and acceptable why we should we expect the other evidence for that, getting of which is near to impossible. GHR S.C.No.19/13 : 21 : Jud. Sessions Case No.19/13 24] In this entire case PW.1 the victim girl is a star witness and she has fully supported and corroborated the prosecution story. In these facts and circumstances as per Section 29 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 the entire burden shifts on accused to prove that he is innocent or it is his duty to rebut prosecution evidence especially the evidence of PW.1 the victim girl. Here no rebuttal evidence is adduced by the accused. Even in the cross­examination of prosecution witnesses carried on behalf of the accused there is nothing in that cross­examination to rebut the most reliable, believable and acceptable evidence of PW.1, the victim girl. Thus evidence of PW.1 on the point of atrocities committed by accused remained unshaken and unrebutted. 25] Thus by cogent and concrete, corroborative evidence prosecution established the fact that accused committed rape on the minor victim girl, he compelled her to do prostitution in the railway and thereby committed offences. Not only this but he further committed rape on her own daughter and compelled her to do prostitution for his livelihood. Thus accused has crossed every limit. She has no source of income. She has undergone the atrocity. She has taken shelter in rehabilitation center. For that reason helping hand of Government to this victim girl is must. IN THE COURT OF SPECIAL JUDGE, [UNDER PROTECTION OF CHILDREN FROM SEXUAL OFFENCES ACT,2012 ] KALYAN AT : KALYAN SPECIAL CASE NO.26/2013. [Presided over by M.J.Mirza] The State of Maharashtra. [Through Tilaknagar Police Station, ....Complainant Dombivli] Vs. Dnyaneshwar Madhukar Kachare, Age : 23 years, Occ.:­Nil, R/at : Kakade Chawl, Behind Kishor Niwas, Sangitawadi, ….Accused. Dombivli [E], Dist. Thane. Appearance : Special P.P.Sou. J.S.Lohokare for the State. Advocate Shri. D.R.Shaha for the accused. Offences punishable under section 363, 376 of IPC and S. 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. :JUDGMENT: [Delivered in open Court on 13/07/2015] 1] The accused is facing the trial for the offences punishable under sections 363 & 376 of Indian Penal Code and Section 4 of the 2 Spl. Case 26/2013 [Judg.] Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 on the allegations that he kidnapped the minor victim, aged 17 years, who left her home by taking gold ornaments and cash and she was raped. Further, on the allegation that the accused committed penetrative sexual assault on her. 2] The case of the prosecution, in short, can be summarized in brief, as under : P.W.1­Kanji Jesa Gothi, the father of the victim, lodged the missing report on 9/3/2013 that he is residing at Ashtavinayak Society, 3 rd Floor, Gograswadi, Dombivali [E] with his wife Radha, three sons and a victim daughter, aged 17 years. He runs a grocery shop. The victim has studied up to 10th standard and since last two years she is doing household work. On 8/6/2013 at 12 night, after taking meal they all went to bed. On 9/6/2013, at 5.30 a.m., when his wife Radha woke up for bathroom, at that time the victim was found sleeping. Thereafter, the victim left the house without intimating to anyone. On 21/10/2011 also she has repeated the same thing, at that time, he had given a complaint to Tilaknagar police station but she returned to his home in the evening. 3] He took search of the victim within Dombivali area but not traced. Then he gave description of the victim along with a passport size photograph to the Tilaknagar police and she had taken cash Rs. 10,000/­ and gold jwellery of her mother viz. Mangalsutra, necklace, two chains, ear tops and ear chains, all weighing 10 tolas. Accordingly, the police registered missing report No. 5/2013 on 9/6/2013. 4] On 10/6/2013, he filed the FIR stating therein that the victim had taken away mangalsutra weighing 55 grams, necklace weighing 45 3 Spl. Case 26/2013 [Judg.] grams, ear tops and chain weighing 17 grams, ear tops and chain weighing 15 grams & chain weighing 12 grams and cash Rs. 10,000/­ kept in the clothes. He had come to know that the victim had love affair with the accused and therefore her further education after 10 th standard was stopped. He suspected and went to the house of the accused along with his brother Nathabhai and he came to know from his mother and brother that he did not turn up to the house from 4 p.m. on 8/6/2013. Then he confirmed that accused induced the victim and kidnapped her. 5] Tilaknagar Police registered the crime bearing No. I­93/2013 under S. 363 of IPC. API Shri. Pandav who carried out the investigation recorded the supplementary statement of the informant and victim. He applied S. 376 of IPC and S. 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. He seized the jwellery and clothes of the victim under panchanama. He then sent the victim for her medical examination. He also sent the accused collecting sample of semen to M.O., Shastrinagar Hospital. He then sent seized muddemal property to C.A. He collected school leaving certificate of the victim, then recorded statements of the witnesses. After completion of investigation, he filed charge sheet in this Court. 6] I have framed the charge at Ex.20 which was read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. The accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. His defence is of false involvement as per his statement recorded under Section 313 of Code of Criminal Procedure and the suggestions put to the prosecution witnesses. He has not stepped into the witness box nor adduced any evidence of defence witness. 4 Spl. Case 26/2013 [Judg.] 7] Heard learned APP Sou. J.S.Lohokare for the State and learned Advocate Shri D.R.Shaha for the accused, at length. 8] The following points arise for my determination and my findings thereon are recorded by me against them for the reasons to follow:­ Points Findings 1 Whether prosecution has proved that age of the prosecutrix was below 18 years at the time of incident ? ..... Yes. 2 Whether prosecution has proved that on 9/6/2013 at 6 hrs. till 11/6/2013 at A­ 308, 3rd floor, Aashtavinayak Society, …Not proved. Opp. Balaji Temple, Gograswadi, Dombivli [E] & Room No. 491, Yadav Chawl, Opp. Lassi Traders, Shivsahyadri Nagar, Netivli, Kalyan [E], accused kidnapped the minor victim, aged 17 years with gold ornaments and cash, from lawful guardianship of her parents, on inducement to marry her punishable under S. 363 IPC? 3 Whether prosecution has proved that on the aforesaid date, time and place, …Not proved. the accused committed rape on the minor victim punishable under S. 376 of IPC ? 4 Whether the prosecution has proved that the accused on the aforesaid date, …Not proved. time and place, committed penetrative sexual assault on the victim, punishable under S.4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012? 5 What order ? …...Accused acquitted. 5 Spl. Case 26/2013 [Judg.] REASONS : As to point No. 1: 9] To substantiate the charge, the prosecution has examined only two witnesses viz. P.W.1­ Shri. Kanji Jesa Gothi (Exh.23), the father of the victim & P.W.2­ Victim (Exh. 27). The victim has stated her birth date as 2/3/1996. The Investigating Officer has produced her school leaving certificate at Exh. 36 with her birth date as 11/3/1996. The date of incident is 8/6/2013. Therefore, her age on the date of incident is 17 Years, 2 months and 27 days. Therefore, she was minor on the date of the alleged offences. Hence, I answer the point No. 1 in the affirmative. 10] As to point No. 2: To prove the offence under S. 363 of IPC, it is necessary for the prosecution to prove “taking or enticing away a minor under 16 years of age, if a male and under 18 years of age, if a female. Further, taking or enticing must be out of keeping of the lawful guardian of such minor and such taking or enticing must be without consent of such guardian”. 11] Where the accused was charged with kidnapping a minor girl out of the guardianship of her parents for compelling her for marriage is an offence. In order to prove this charge, though the prosecution has examined the informant P.W.1­Kanji and the victim at Exh.23 and 27 respectively, no where both these witnesses have brought on record that the accused kidnapped the victim from her lawful guardianship. The informant has proved on the missing report at Exh.24 and FIR at Exh.25 only to the extent of his signatures. He has also produced the school leaving certificate of the victim below Exh. 26 which is exhibited being a public document. The informant has sated that he has objected the 6 Spl. Case 26/2013 [Judg.] marriage of the victim with the accused, and therefore, she had left his home twicely. Therefore, he had knowledge that she is having love affair with the accused. As the victim has left his house permanently, therefore, he states that he has no concern with her as she married with the accused. Therefore, he has no grievances against the accused and he wish good future of victim and accused. 12] The victim has changed her name by naming the accused as her husband and his surname. According to her, she stayed with her parents till 14/4/2014. The Tilaknagar Police took her and accused when they were in the house of friend of the accused at Kalyan. She also states that she had also taken gold jwellery of her mother and cash from the house. She on her own accord left the house of her parents. She is now married with the accused in a temple as per Hindu Vaidik Rituals and obtained the marriage certificate. She was having love affair with the accused since last 8 years and was willing to marry with him since inception but accused has not forced her to keep any physical contacts with her. She has denied her statement recorded by police. 13] Under the circumstances, an useful reference can be made to the ruling reported in AIR 1965 SC 942 (S.Varadrajan – Vs – State of Madras) wherein the victim on her own accord had left her father's protection knowing and having capacity to know the full import of what she was doing and voluntarily joined the accused, it could not be said that accused had taken away from the keeping of her lawful guardian within the meaning of section 361 of I.P.C.. Something more had to be done in a case of that time such as inducement held out by the accused person or an active participation by him in the formation of the intention, either 7 Spl. Case 26/2013 [Judg.] immediately prior to the minor leaving her father's protection or at some earlier stage. Prima facie, it appears in case on hand that victim left her parents home on her own accord and as such, there is nothing on record that the accused induced or kidnapped the victim in view of the ratio laid down in the above cited ruling. 14] In view of the settled position of law, when the victim herself left her parents house, therefore, taking or enticing by the accused does not arise. Hence, I answer the point No. 2, in the negative. 15] As to point Nos. 3 & 4: Though the prosecution examined two witnesses but it is not the case of any of them that accused committed rape forcibly on her. For this the evidence of the victim is material who has stated that during her stay with the accused, he had no forcible intercourse with her. After marriage before one year with the accused she conceived pregnancy of six months. According to her, she was having love affair with the accused since last 8 years and willing to marry with him, however, till marriage accused never forced her to keep physical relations with him. Even she has denied her statement recorded by police in all respects. Under the circumstances, neither the ingredients of S. 376 of IPC or S. 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act are attracted. The fact remains that on the date of the alleged offence the victim was minor as her age was 17 years, 2 months and 27 days. However, she was on the verge of attaining her age of majority and was having that much understanding capacity what she was going to do and effect thereof. Moreover, there is nothing on record to hold the accused guilty for any of the offence charged. Hence, I answer the Point Nos. 2 & 3 in the negative. 8 Spl. Case 26/2013 [Judg.] 16] Resultantly, the accused deserves to be acquitted, and as such, I proceed to pass the following order : ORDER 1] Accused Dnyaneshwar Madhukar Kachare is hereby acquitted of the offence punishable under Sections 363, 376 of IPC and S. 3 r/w 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 under S. 235(1) of Cr.P.C. 2] His bail bond stands cancelled. 3] The seized muddemal articles viz. gold jwellery worth Rs. 2,95,000/­ is already returned to the informant, P.W.1­ Shri. Kanji Jesa Gothi on bond which stands cancelled. The rest of the seized muddemal i.e. clothes of the victim and accused are not produced before the Court, however, they being worthless, be destroyed after the appeal period is over. 4] The accused shall execute his P.R. and S.B. of Rs.15,000/­ to appear before the Higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect of appeal filed against this judgment as per S. 437­A of Cr.P.C. Such bail shall remain in force for six months from today. Kalyan, [M.J.Mirza] Dt.13/7/2015. Special Judge, vsi­p.c. Under Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 9 Spl.
