In order to constitute penetration, there must be evidence clear and cogent to prove that some part of the virile member of the accused was within the labia of the pudendum of the woman, no matter how little. The depth of penetration is immaterial in an offence punishable under Section 376 of I.P.C. Even a slight penetration in the vulva is sufficient to constitute the offence of rape and rupture of the hymen is not necessary. Vulva penetration with or without violence is as much rape as vaginal penetration. The statute merely requires evidence of penetration, and this may occur with the hymen remaining intact. The actus reus is complete with penetration. Thus, to constitute the offence of rape, it is not necessary that there should be complete penetration of the penis with emission of semen and rupture of hymen. Partial penetration within the labia majora of the vulva or pudendum with or without emission of semen is sufficient to constitute the offence of rape as defined in the law.” 49. Case 11/2013 [Judgment] 3] Whether prosecution has proved that at the relevant time the accused with an intention to insult the modesty of minor victim uttered the words “to come to roam in the colony” ? .. Not proved. 4] Whether the prosecution has proved that at the relevant time the accused committed sexual assault on the victim? .. Not proved. 5] Whether the prosecution has proved that at the relevant time the accused committed sexual harassment upon the minor victim ? .. Not proved. 6] What order ? ….. Accused acquitted. REASONS : 9] To substantiate the charge, the prosecution has examined only the minor victim as PW­1 but she has not supported the case of prosecution. The defence has admitted the spot panchanama Exh.18 and arrest panchanama at Exh.12 as genuineness thereof is not disputed. As to point No. 1 : 10] The victim has stated in her testimony that her age as 14 years when she tendered her evidence on 13.10.2015. The alleged incident is dated 28.2.2013 at 12.15 p.m. Therefore, her age as on the date of the incident may be 12 years. The prosecution has not produced any document showing the exact birth date of the victim on record, such as bonafide certificate or school leaving certificate or birth extract. The defence has not seriously challen ged the age of the victim therefore I hold that on the date of incident the age of victim was 12­13 years approximately. Hence, I answer point No.1, in the affirmative. 5 Spl. Case 11/2013 [Judgment] As to point No.2 to 5 :­ 11] I have taken all these points together as they are interlinked and to discuss properly. The testimony of the victim is material for all these points and she is the only witness examining by the prosecution in this case. The trial was taken in camera by following guidelines and directions by the Hon'ble Apex Court in this regard. The witness being minor no oath was administered but she was capable of giving rational answers to the questions asked to her 12] According to her, since her first standard she was studying in Yashodeep Vidyalaya, Mohane. At present she is in 9 th standard. Her school time is 12.30 p.m. to 5.40 p.m. for 5 th standard to 10th standard. Said school is at the distance of 15 minutes walk from her house and she used to go to school with her friends. She was not knowing or acquainted with any of the inhabitants on either sides of the road of her school. 13] She has denied while deposing that nothing had happened when she was studying in 6th standard. On the contrary she has brought on record that one person was harassing her friends Trupti and Sanika who was asking them to come in colony to roam. This fact was came to be known to her from her friends. She then disclosed about the said person to the aunt of her friend Trupti. Thereafter family members of the Trupti had gone to the house of the said person but he was not present in the house. She had also gone with the family members of her friend. When they all searched the said person in the colony and he was caught by the family members of her friend Trupti said person was assaulted by them and then brought to police station. Police enquired with her and she narrated the incident accordingly and also put her signature. 6 Spl. Case 11/2013 [Judgment] 14] During her testimony she has stated that her friends was not accompanied with her to the police station but her father was with her. Again she states that the family members of her friends were accompanied with her to Mahatma Phule Chowk Police Station. On the day of incident none of them had gone to the school. An omission has been brought on record that the said person was harassing her friends Trupti and Sanika who was making gestures by his hands. She also stated that said person was asking her friend whether they should come in the colony. 15] Further, the victim has stated that she does not know personally about the incident but deposing on the basis of say of her friends. Though, the allegations regarding outraging modesty or insulted the modesty of the victim or sexual assault and harassment, however there is no oral evidence of the minor victim to fulfill all the ingredients of the offences levelled against the accused. On the contrary, the minor victim has not supported the case of the prosecution for the reason best known to her. Though, the learned APP cross­examined the minor victim with the permission of the Court but nothing fruitful has been brought on the record to hold the accused guilty for the any of the offences levelled against him. Therefore, I hold that the prosecution has utterly failed to prove the charges levelled against the accused by adducing cogent, reliable and trustworthy evidence. Hence, I answer the point Nos. 2 to 5, in the negative. 16] Resultantly, the accused deserves to be acquitted, and as such, I proceed to pass the following order : ORDER 1] Accused Harishchandra Ramvilas Gujar, is hereby 7 Spl. Case 11/2013 [Judgment] acquitted vide Sec. 235(1) of Cr.P.C. of the offences punishable under Sections 354 & 509 of IPC & Secs. 8 & 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] The accused is in jail. He be set at liberty forthwith, if not required in any other crime or case. 3] No muddemal has been seized or produced before the Court, hence no order is passed to that effect. 4] The accused shall execute his P.R. and S.B. of Rs.15,000/­ to appear before the Higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect of appeal filed against this judgment as per S. 437­A of Cr.P.C. 5] Such bail shall remain in force for six months from today. Kalyan, [M.J.Mirza] Dt.:­20/11/2015. Special Judge, Under Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, Kalyan. 8 Spl. Case 11/2013 [Judgment] 9 Spl. Case 11/2013 [Judgment]

1 Spl. Case 152/2014 [Judg.] Presented on :­ 14/11/2014 Registered on :­ 14/11/2014 Decided on :­ 24/07/2015 Duration : 0 ­Y. 8­M. 10­D. Exh. IN THE COURT OF SPECIAL JUDGE, [UNDER THE PROTECTION OF CHILDREN FROM SEXUAL OFFENCES ACT,2012 ] KALYAN AT : KALYAN SPECIAL CASE NO.152/2014. [Presided over by M.J.Mirza] The State of Maharashtra. ....Complainant. [Through Ulhasnagar Police Station] Vs. 1] Mohammed Islam Mohammed Rafiq Hasmi, Age 26 years, Occ.:Mechanic, R/at : Rajiv Gandhi Nagar, A Block, .….Accused. Near Masjid, Ulhasnagar­1, Native at – Chikwa Mohalla, Kharbu Bazar, Dist. Gonda, U.P. 2] Mohammed Rafiq Mohammed Usuf Hasmi, Age 55 years, Occ.: Mechanic, R/at : Chikwa Mohalla, Kharbu Bazar, Dist. Gonda, U.P. Appearance : A.P.P.Smt. J.S.Lohokare for the State. Advocate Shri. F.H.Nizami for the accused Nos. 1 & 2. 2 Spl. Case 152/2014 [Judg.] Offences : ­ Punishable under section 363 & 376 of IPC, S. 4 & 17 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and S. 9 & 10 of the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006. :JUDGMENT: [Pronounced in the open Court on 24/07/2015] 1] The accused No.1­ Mohammed Islam Mohammed Rafiq Hasmi and accused No.2­ Mohammed Rafiq Mohammed Usuf Hasmi are facing the trial for the offences punishable under sections 363 & 376 of Indian Penal Code and Section 4 & 17 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and S. 9 & 10 of the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006. 2] The case of the prosecution, in short, can be summarized in brief, as under : That the victim, P.W.1, is minor aged 16 years, the daughter of the informant ­P.W.2 Shaharbano Nadir Khan. The victim was residing with her parents, her brothers Naeem Khan, aged 22 years, wife of her brother viz. Sakina and Sameem aged 13 years and two more sisters Najmeen, aged 9 years and Najreen, aged 7 years at Sirisan Rohidasnagar, Ulhasnagar. Her native is at Samda, Post Bigarpur, Dist. Balrampur, U.P. 3] The accused No.1 was her neighbour and residing with his ailing wife Sakina, therefore, the informant was cooking his meal. Since then she knows the accused No.1 Mohammed Islam @ Bablu. The accused No.1 used to visit her house. His ailing wife expired. Thereafter, in January, 2014 the accused No.1 came to her house and proposed the victim for his marriage. At that time the informant refused the said proposal on the reason that the caste of the accused No.1 is Dafali Muslim. Thereafter he started talking with the victim on mobile phone. 3 Spl. Case 152/2014 [Judg.] 4] On 23/5/2014, as usual the informant and her family members including the victim went to bed. On 24/5/2014 at 6 a.m. when she woke up, the victim was not found in the bed. Then she along with her husband took search of victim but not traced. When she had gone to the house of the accused No.1­Mohd. Islam @ Bablu, it was found closed. Therefore, she immediately went to Raisa, the sister of accused No.1­Bablu and enquired about the minor victim. Raisa made phone call on the cell number 8698411759 and then accused No.1­ Bablu told her that the victim is with him and they should not worry about her. The informant then spoke with him asking him to come back to Ulhasnagar and they would perform his marriage. Then accused No.1­Bablu told her that he would perform Nikah with the victim at his village and then he cut the phone call. 5] On 26/5/2014, the informant along with her husband, son and daughters and daughter­in­law boarded the train to go to the house of accused No.1­Bablu. While travelling in the train, accused No.1­ Bablu made phone call on the cell No. 8855097265 of her son and told that he has performed Nikah with the victim and asked when they would reach there. Then he cut the phone call. On 27/5/2014 they reached at village Samada, Dist. Balrampur, U.P. As they were not knowing the house of accused No.1­ Bablu, they requested the accused No.2, who is the father of Bablu to take them to the house of accused No.1­Bablu. Then accused No.1­Bablu came to the house of informant and took them to his house. The victim disclosed to the informant that she married with the accused No.1­Bablu. They stayed with the victim for two days, however, accused No.1­Bablu did not send the victim with them. Therefore, they all returned to Ulhasnagar. They were making phone calls repeatedly to the victim but 4 Spl. Case 152/2014 [Judg.] she was not speaking much. 6] In the month of August, the victim made phone call to the informant and informed that accused No.1­Bablu is intending to purchase room at Nalasopara for which he is in need of Rs.30,000/­. The informant promised the victim to pay Rs. 15,000/­ on condition that he should bring the victim to her house. Accordingly, accused No.1­Bablu showed his willingness to return to Ulhasnagar with victim, and accordingly, arrived at Ulhasnagar on 13/8/2014. The victim was left at her house and then accused No.1­Bablu went to the house of his sister Ayesha residing at Nalasopara. The victim disclosed to the informant that on 24/5/2014 at 3 a.m. accused No.1­Bablu kidnapped her and took her to Uttar Pradesh where he performed marriage with her forcibly and committed sexual intercourse with her against her wish and consent. 7] Ulhasnagar Police registered the crime bearing No. I­218/2014 under S. 363 & 376 of IPC and S. 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and S. 9 & 10 of the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006. 8] Further investigation was entrusted to PSI ­V.G.Kajari, who recorded the statements of the witnesses including the minor victim girl. He collected Nikahnama and translated in Marathi. He also collected the school leaving certificate of the victim. He seized the clothes of the victim and accused No.1 after arresting him on 17/8/2014. He then collected medical certificate of accused No.1 as well as victim. The muddemal property was sent to C.A. along with his covering letter. He received C.A. report at Exh.37. After completion of investigation, he filed charge sheet 5 Spl. Case 152/2014 [Judg.] against both the accused. 9] I framed the charge at Ex.15 which was read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. Both the accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. Their defence is of false involvement as per their statements recorded under Section 313 of Code of Criminal Procedure. None of the accused stepped into the witness box nor examined any defence witness. 10] Heard learned APP Sou. J.S.Lohokare for the State and learned Advocate Shri F.H.Nizami for the accused Nos. 1 and 2, at length. 11] The following points arise for my determination and my findings thereon are recorded by me against them for the reasons to follow:­ Points Findings 1 Whether prosecution has proved that age of the prosecutrix was below 18 years on the date of incident ? ..... Yes. 2 Whether prosecution has proved that during the period from 24/5/2014 to 15/8/2014, at Shirison Devidas Nagar, …Not proved. C Block, Near Mangalmurti Apartment, Ulhasnagar­1, accused No.1­Mohammed Islam kidnapped the minor victim girl, aged 16 years, from lawful guardianship of her parents, by inducing to marry with her, punishable under S. 363 IPC? 3 Whether prosecution has proved that the accused No.2 ­Mohammed Rafiq …Not proved. Mohammed Usuf Hasmi along with absconding accused Nisar Ahemad Hazi Mohhamad Minai (Kazi) and two more 6 Spl. Case 152/2014 [Judg.] absconding accused who were witnesses of the marriage of the victim with accused No.1, dtd. 26/5/2014, at 7 p.m., performed at Chikwa Mohalla, Kharbu Bazar, Dist. Gonda, U.P., abetted the offence by instigating/intentionally aiding the accused No.1, punishable under S. 17 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012? 4 Whether prosecution has proved that the accused No.2 -Mohammed Rafiq Mohammed Usuf Hasmi along with absconding accused Nisar Ahemad Hazi Mohhamad Minai (Kazi) and two more …Not proved. absconding accused who were witnesses of the marriage of the victim with accused No.1, dtd. 26/5/2014, at 7 p.m., performed at Chikwa Mohalla, Kharbu Bazar, Dist. Gonda, UP, by performing or instigating/intentionally aiding child marriage, abetted the offence punishable under S. 10 of the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 ? 5 Whether prosecution has proved that the accused No.1, on aforesaid said date, time and place at Chikwa Mohalla, Kharbu Bazar, Dist. Gonda, UP, being a …Not proved. male adult, above 18 years of age, contracted a child marriage with the minor victim girl, punishable under S. 9 of the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 ? 6 Whether prosecution has proved that the accused No.1, on the aforesaid date, time and place at Chikwa Mohalla, …Not proved. Kharbu Bazar, Dist. Gonda, UP, committed rape on the minor victim girl, aged 16 years, punishable under Sec. 376 of IPC ? 7 Spl. Case 152/2014 [Judg.] 7 Whether the prosecution has proved that the accused No.1, on the aforesaid …Not proved. date, time and place, committed penetrative sexual assault on the minor victim girl, aged 16 years, punishable under Sec. 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 ? What order ? …...Both accused 8 acquitted. REASONS : As to point No. 1: 12] To substantiate the charge, the prosecution has examined only three witnesses viz. P.W.1­ minor victim girl (Exh.20), the informant, P.W.2­ Smt. Shaharbano Nadir Khan (Exh.21), the mother of the victim girl & P.W.3­ I.O., PSI­ Shri. Vijay Bhaskar Kajari (Exh.26). The Investigating Officer has produced her school leaving certificate at Exh. 30 showing the birth date of the victim girl as 17/6/1998. The date of incident is 24/5/2014. Therefore, her age on the date of incident is 15 Years, 11 months and 7 days. The victim girl has stated her age as 16 years and her mother, P.W.2, states that the age of the victim girl was 15 years. The school leaving certificate is being public document within the meaning of S.74 of the Evidence Act, and hence, can be exhibited and read in evidence. The Ld. advocate for the accused has also not challenged the school leaving certificate (Exh.30). Therefore, I hold that she was minor on the date of the alleged incident. Hence, I answer the point No. 1, in the affirmative. 13] As to point No. 2: To prove the offence under S. 363 of IPC, it is necessary for 8 Spl. Case 152/2014 [Judg.] the prosecution to prove “taking or enticing away a minor under 16 years of age, if a male and under 18 years of age, if a female. Further, ''taking'' or ''enticing'' must be out of keeping of the lawful guardian of such minor and such ''taking'' or ''enticing'' must be without consent of such guardian”. 14] Where the accused was charged with kidnapping a minor girl out of the guardianship of her parents for compelling her for marriage is an offence. In order to prove this charge, though the prosecution has examined P.W.1, the victim girl and the informant, P.W.2­Shaharbano, the mother of the victim girl, no where whispered that the accused kidnapped the victim from her lawful guardianship by inducing to marry with her. The victim girl has denied that accused No.1 before the Court is acquainted by her. She has brought on record that she is still unmarried and she was not harassed sexually at any time. The informant, P.W.2­Smt. Shaharbano, has stated that she does not know the birth date of the victim or even the year of her birth, however, she was sent in school known as ''Dnyansadhana Vidyamandir, Ulhasnagar'' and she studied up to 2 nd­3rd standard. She knows both the accused present before the Court, however, subsequently she denied her acquaintance with the accused. Moreover, according to her, nothing had happened to the victim, however, she lodged the FIR at Exh.22 which bears her signature. She denied the contents therein of her FIR. The contents of the FIR were read over to her, but, she denied in toto. 15] P.W.2­Smt. Shaharbano who resiled from the contents of the FIR, therefore, the Ld. APP cross­examined her at length. In her cross­ examination by Ld. APP, she has admitted that the age of the victim was below 18 years, but she does not know her birth date as 17/6/1998. She further admits that she has produced school leaving certificate of the victim 9 Spl. Case 152/2014 [Judg.] before the police. I have gone through the statement of P.W.1, the victim girl, recorded under S. 164 of Cr.P.C.dtd. 1/9/2014 recorded y Ld. JMFC, Ulhasnagar, which shows that she on her own accord left her parents home, but, under the threats given by the accused No.1 for accompany with him to Kharsupur, Dist. Gonda, U.P. In her substantive evidence before the Court, she had given go­bye to her case. There is no substantive evidence to hold that the accused No.1 ­Mohammed Islam kidnapped the victim girl from her lawful guardianship on 24/5/2014 at 3 a.m. Therefore, I answer the point No.2 in the negative. 15] As to point Nos. 3, 4 & 5 : It is the case of the prosecution that the accused No.2­ Mohammed Rafiq, the father of the accused No.1­Mohammed Islam, along with absconding accused ­NIsar Ahemad Haji Mohd. Minai (Kazi) and two more absconding accused, who were witnesses to the marriage of the victim girl with accused No.1, alleged to have been performed on 26/5/2014 at 3 p.m. at Chikwa Mohalla, Kharbu Bazar, Dist. Gonda, U.P., abetted or instigated or intentionally aided the child marriage. Moreover, the accused No.1 being male adult contracted child marriage with the minor victim girl. For all these charges, the evidence of the victim girl is material. In the substantive evidence of the victim girl, she has put forth her case that she is still unmarried and was not kidnapped from her lawful guardianship by the accused No.1­Mohammed Islam. Even the informant is also silent on these aspects. It appears that the accused No.1­ Mohammed Islam is above 18 years of age. 16] The investigating officer, P.W.3, has produced copy of the Nikahnama and translated copy at Exh.36 showing the name of the 10 Spl. Case 152/2014 [Judg.] accused No.1 and name of the victim girl, name of the Kazi and witnesses. The said marriage appears to have been performed on 22/5/2014 and the marriage was registered with Kazi on 26/5/2014 at 6 p.m. In pursuance of the Nikahnama, the victim girl as well as the informant both have denied the marriage with the accused No.1 ­Mohammed Islam. The prosecution has not examined any witness on the point of marriage to prove Nikahnama of the victim girl and accused No.1­Mohammed Islam. Moreover, no affidavit in support of the translation of Nikahnama has produced showing the contents therein are truly translated. There is also nothing on record to hold that the Kazi, the witnesses and the accused No.2 ­Mohammed Rafique etc. were present in the said marriage and they instigated and intentionally aided and abetted the marriage of accused No.1 with the victim girl and the bridge­groom was male adult above 18 years of age and contracted the child marriage. Therefore, I answer the point Nos. 3, 4 & 5 in the negative. 17] As to point Nos.6 & 7 : For both these points the evidence of the victim girl is important who is able to depose about rape and penetrative sexual assault on her. In the substantive evidence of P.W.1, the victim girl, she has denied the alleged rape and penetrative sexual assault on her by the accused No.1­Mohammed Islam at Chikwa Mohalla, Kharbu Bazar, Dist. Gonda, U.P. In her statement recorded under S. 164 of Cr.P.C. by the Ld. Magistrate, she has stated so by saying that the accused No.1 used to give sleeping pills to her and then he used to commit forcible sexual intercourse with her after the marriage. The prosecution has produced the C.A. certificate at Exh.37 showing neither blood nor semen is detected on the clothes of the victim girl and the accused No.1­Mohammed Islam. The 11 Spl. Case 152/2014 [Judg.] victim was sent for her medical examination and medical certificate has been produced on record, but, the medical officer who examined the victim girl has not been examined by prosecution to prove the same which is dtd. 17/8/2014. Therefore, there is no medical evidence supporting the case of the prosecution. The victim girl has denied all the accusation levelled against the accused No.1­Mohammed Islam. Nothing has been brought on record by the Ld. APP during cross­examination of the victim girl. Therefore, I hold that the prosecution has failed to prove the charge punishable under S. 376 of IPC and S. 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. Hence, I answer the point Nos. 6 & 7 in the negative. 18] Resultantly, the accused Nos. 1 & 2 deserve to be acquitted, and as such, I proceed to pass the following order : ORDER 1] Accused No. 1­ Mohammed Islam Mohammed Rafiq Hasmi and No.2­Mohammed Rafiq Mohammed Usuf Hasmi are hereby acquitted under S. 235(1) of Cr.P.C. of the offences punishable under Section 363 & 376 of IPC and S. 4 & 17 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and S.9 & 10 of the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006. 2] The accused No.1 ­ Mohammed Islam Mohammed Rafiq Hasmi is in jail since his date of arrest i.e. 17/8/2014, therefore, he be set at liberty forthwith, if not required in any other case or crime. 3] The accused No.2 Mohammed Rafiq Mohammed Usuf Hasmi is on bail, hence, his bail bond stands cancelled. 12 Spl. Case 152/2014 [Judg.] 4] The seized muddemal property i.e. clothes of the accused and victim, shall be preserved for the trial of absconding accused, if any. 5] The I.O. is directed to file separate charge sheet against absconding accused. 6] The accused shall execute their P.R. and S.B. of Rs.15,000/­each to appear before the Higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect of appeal filed against this judgment as per S. 437­A of Cr.P.C. Such bail shall remain in force for six months from today. Kalyan, [M.J.Mirza] Dt.24/7/2015. Special Judge, vsi­p.c. Under Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 13 Spl. She deposed about information received by her from prosecutrix regarding the father of female child delivered by her daughter i.e. prosecutrix. PW No.4 Sudha Sidhappa Sakhare (Exh.26), PW No.5 Rupa Irappa Koli (Exh.27), PW No.7 Vijay Sidhappa Sakhare (Exh.33), PW No.8 Smt. Lata Joseph Surve Dpk/J­Atro. Spl Case No.45/2013 .....5/­ ..5.. Judgment­Atro Spl.Case 45/2013 (Exh.34) are examined by prosecution as neighbouring witness on the point that they saw accused while visiting the house of prosecutrix during noon time on many occasions. However, all these witnesses turned hostile. PW No.6 Shri Mahesh Ratilal Hajare (Exh.29) is father of prosecutrix. He supported the prosecution. He deposed in the same line that of his wife Anita. PW No.9 Dr.(Smt.) Asha Rameshwar Raigule (Exh.37) is the Medical Officer from Chhaya Municipal Hospital, Ambernath. She deposed about the delivery of female baby by the prosecutrix on 05.08.2013. PW No.10 Prashant Devidas Tawde (Exh.40) is the then PSO who recorded the complaint of the prosecutrix, which is at Exh.18. PW No.11 Prashant Rajaram Sande (Exh.43) is the Investigation Officer. He deposed about his investigation in the crime. He proved some portions specifically marked during the respective witnesses, mostly neighbouring persons, during his deposition. He proved spot panchanama and other documents on record. PW No.12 Prashant Vinayak Naik is the carrier of DNA sample to laboratory, Kalina. He deposed accordingly. 7/­ In addition to this oral evidence, some documents are also produced on record by the prosecution. In those documents DNA test report is at Exh.20, spot panchanama is at Exh.24, birth certificate of the prosecutrix is at Exh.30. Again examination report of DNA sample is produced at Exh.42. Arrest panchanama is at Exh.44. Discharge card is at Article 'A'. Letter of Investigation Officer to Regional Forensic Laboratory, Kalina dated 05.10.2013 is at Exh.45. By this letter, the DNA profile samples were sent to Dpk/J­Atro. Spl Case No.45/2013 .....6/­ ..6.. Judgment­Atro Spl.Case 45/2013 the laboratory. Thereafter, prosecution closed its evidence vide pursis at Exh.52. 8/­ All incriminating facts, evidence, statements were put to accused in his statement under section 313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and his explanation is recorded. From the answers given by the accused to the questions during statement under section 313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, his defence reveals as of total denial. He has not adduced any defence evidence. 9/­ I have gone through the oral and documentary evidence of prosecution on record. I have heard both Ld. Advocates at length. Following points arise for my determination. My findings on those points are as follows for the reasons stated below : Sr.No. Points Findings 1. Does prosecution prove that, on the .. In the negative. date of incident the victim girl was minor ? 2. Does prosecution prove that in the .. In the negative. year 2012 to 05.08.2013, at House No.914, Behind Santosh Hotel, in front of Mahant Kamaldas Hindi Vidyalaya, Buvapada, Ambernath (W), accused committed rape on prosecutrix Miss Yogita Mahesh Hajare, aged 17 years and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 376 of IPC ? Dpk/J­Atro. Spl Case No.45/2013 .....7/­ ..7.. Judgment­Atro Spl.Case 45/2013 3. Does prosecution prove that during .. In the negative. the abovesaid period and place accused committed criminal intimidation by threatening prosecutrix Miss Yogita Mahesh Hajare with intent to cause alarm to her and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 506 of IPC ? 4. Does prosecution prove that during .. In the negative. the abovesaid period and place accused committed penetrative sexual assault on prosecutrix Miss Yogita Mahesh Hajare, aged 17 years and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 3, 5(J)(2) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 ? ­: R E A S O N S :­ As to point nos.1 to 4 : 10/­ In order to avoid repetition of discussion and for logical conclusion, I have considered all these points together. Here, it is pertinent to note that, except PW No.1, the prosecutrix, there is no other competent witness to depose on the point of alleged rape or on the point of intercourse by accused with the prosecutrix. Here, I again want to mention that, PW No.3 Anita Mahesh Hajare and PW No.6 Mahesh Ratilal Hajare i.e. the parents of prosecutrix only supported the prosecution. Rest of the neighbouring witnesses turned hostile. In fact, their turning hostile does not adversely affect the case of prosecution because they have no personal knowledge about the incident. At the most Dpk/J­Atro. Spl Case No.45/2013 .....8/­ ..8.. Judgment­Atro Spl.Case 45/2013 they can depose that they saw accused while going and coming to the house of prosecutrix during noon. Even, if they do not depose that cannot adversely affect the case of prosecution. 11/­ Evidence of PW No.3 Anita Mahesh Hajare and PW No.6 Mahesh Ratilal Hajare is definitely hearsay evidence. They came to know about the incident from the mouth of prosecutrix. They have no personal knowledge. Their evidence is only relevant to the fact that they took the prosecutrix to the hospital and on the way to hospital prosecutrix delivered a female child. In fact, this fact is not at all denied by the accused. This factum of delivery of female child by the prosecutrix on 05.08.2013 is an admitted fact. 12/­ Now, the evidence of prosecutrix is important. In her deposition, she deposed that the accused was on visiting terms to her house in noon time. He was friend of her father. Accused used to touch her body after coming in the house. Then he used to commit sexual intercourse with her. She further deposed that, accused committed sexual intercourse with her for 6 to 7 times. She further deposed that, the incidence of intercourse occurred in the year 2012 or 2013. In her entire deposition she nowhere uttered a single word that the accused was making intercourse with her against her will, against her wish, against her consent or by using criminal force etc. etc. She simply stated that, accused used to commit sexual intercourse with her. From the entire deposition of prosecutrix it appears that, the relations between Dpk/J­Atro. Spl Case No.45/2013 .....9/­ ..9.. Judgment­Atro Spl.Case 45/2013 accused and herself were with consent. Even she has not uttered a single word regarding her protest for such relations. Nowhere she stated that, at any point of time she protested such relations or opposed the accused to have sexual intercourse with her. This fact further indicates the consent of the prosecutrix for such relations. Some other facts are there which also indicates that there was a consent of prosecutrix for such relations. It is pertinent to note that, during such relations or even during pregnancy period, the prosecutrix do not disclose the alleged illegal or criminal act of accused to anybody including her parents, especially to her mother. Not only this, but even after delivery of child for about two months she kept mum and thereafter she disclosed the fact that the accused is the father of the child. Thereafter, the complaint was lodged. Even in the depositions of PW No.3 Anita Mahesh Hajare and PW No.6 Mahesh Ratilal Hajare, they do not depose that the prosecutrix disclosed them that accused committed rape on her forcibly and against her will. She simply disclosed the fact that the accused had sexual relations with her out of which she became pregnant and delivered a female child. Thus, in entire prosecution evidence, the factum of forceful intercourse or intercourse against the wish or without consent of the prosecutrix is not at all proved. The DNA report which is on record at Exh.42 undoubtedly proved the fact that there had intercourse between the prosecutrix and accused and the prosecutrix and accused are biological parents of the newly born female baby. Thus, factum of intercourse by accused with prosecutrix and factum of pregnancy of prosecutrix is proved. Dpk/J­Atro. Spl Case No.45/2013 .....10/­ ..10.. Judgment­Atro Spl.Case 45/2013 13/­ From the discussion in foregoing paras, it is crystal clear that whatever relations, more specifically the sexual relations between the prosecutrix and accused were, with consent of each other. Now I have to see whether such relations or act of accused to have a sexual intercourse with prosecutrix amounts to any offence. 14/­ Under section 376 of IPC, if any person commits intercourse with a minor girl below the age of 16 years even though with her consent, that amounts to an offence of rape. In this case, birth date and age of the prosecutrix is vehemently challenged by the accused person. As per his say, on the date of alleged act of intercourse, the prosecutrix was major and 19 years old. As per prosecution story, date of birth of the prosecutrix is 30.11.1996. Now, I have to see whether this date of birth is correct one and it is proved and whether prosecution succeeded to prove that, on the date of incident the prosecutrix was minor. If the prosecution succeeds to prove that on the date of incident the victim girl was minor, then prosecution will succeed to secure the conviction. If prosecution fails to prove a fact that on the date of incident the prosecutrix was not minor or if accused succeeded to prove the fact that the prosecutrix was major on the date of incident, then the prosecution has to fail. 15/­ As I have already stated, contention of prosecution is that the date of birth of the prosecutrix is 30.11.1996. It is surprising to see that the prosecutrix does not know the date of Dpk/J­Atro. Spl Case No.45/2013 .....11/­ ..11.. Judgment­Atro Spl.Case 45/2013 her intercourse with accused. She does not know when she became pregnant or in which month she became pregnant. No particulars about that are given. Irrespective of that, surprisingly she has stated the date of birth as 30.11.1996. Similar is the evidence of PW No.3 Anita Mahesh Hajare and PW No.6 Mahesh Ratilal Hajare regarding the date of birth of prosecutrix. To support this, prosecution produced one birth certificate on record, which is at Exh.30. I have carefully gone through said birth certificate. Apparently, there is difference in the surname of father of prosecutrix as well as name of her mother. In reality the name of the mother of prosecutrix is Anita. She deposed accordingly before this Court. However, name of the mother of child whose birth is recorded in Exh.30 is Jyoti. Prosecution has not brought on record that Anita is also known by name Jyoti. Anita has not stated that, her name is also Jyoti. Why the name of mother of the child whose birth is recorded by Exh.30 appears as a Jyoti is nowhere explained by the prosecution either through PW No.3 Anita or Investigation Officer PW No.11 Prashant Rajaram Sande. Similarly, name of father of child whose birth is recorded by the extract at Exh.30 is mentioned in the extract as Mahesh Ratilal Morare. He also deposed before this Court, but, did not utter a single word giving explanation why his surname is recorded wrongly in the alleged birth certificate at Exh.30. From plain reading of the birth certificate at Exh.30 it appears that, this birth certificate does not pertain to the birth date of prosecutrix, but it is of else one. Except this, there is no other evidence on record to show that the prosecutrix was minor on the date of Dpk/J­Atro. Spl Case No.45/2013 .....12/­ ..12.. Judgment­Atro Spl.Case 45/2013 incident. Thus, whatever evidence adduced by prosecution regarding the birth date of prosecutrix is neither reliable nor acceptable. 16/­ It is continuous contention of the accused that, on the date of alleged incident the prosecutrix was 19 years old. Suggestions are given to that effect to PW No.1 prosecutrix as well as PW No.3 Anita Mahesh Hajare and PW No.6 Mahesh Ratilal Hajare, the parents of prosecutrix. It is admitted fact that, after delivery, the prosecutrix was immediately admitted in Chhaya Hospital, Ambernath. While giving particulars regarding the prosecutrix before Medical Officer of Chhaya Hospital of Ambernath Municipal Council, the prosecutrix has stated her age as 19 years. This support the contention of accused. Apart from that, proving the fact that on the date of incident the prosecutrix was minor, burden lies on the prosecution. To discharge this burden and to prove the same, no sufficient evidence on record. Therefore, I hold that the prosecution failed to prove that, on the date of incident the prosecutrix was minor. 17/­ As I have already stated, sexual relations between prosecutrix and accused are proved. However, it is not proved that such relations were against the will of the prosecutrix or those were forcible relations. On the contrary, the facts and circumstances on record and especially the admission given by the prosecutrix it is proved that those relations were with consent of the prosecutrix. Similar facts and circumstances were in case of Dpk/J­Atro. Spl Case No.45/2013 .....13/­ ..13.. Judgment­Atro Spl.Case 45/2013 (1) Siddharth Vasant Ingale Vs. State of Maharashtra & Anr. [2015 ALL MR (Cri) 2275]; (2) Prakash Jaganath Pawar Vs. The State of Maharashtra [2015 ALL MR (Cri) 3898. In both these cases Hon'ble Bombay High Court held that, “if there is a consent for sexual intercourse, then it does not amount the offence of rape”. Both these rulings are relied by Ld. Advocate for accused and those supports his contention. 18/­ As I have already stated, intercourse with a girl below the age of 16 years amounts to an offence under section 376 of IPC. In this case, it is not proved that on the date of incident the prosecutrix was below the age of 16 years. Even we accept the date of birth relied on by the prosecution for the sake of arguments, then also it appears that on the date of conception i.e. in the month of December 2012 the prosecutrix was above 16 years. Therefore, this case does not fall under the definition of rape under section 375 of IPC. 19/­ Similar is the fact in respect of the offences punishable under sections 4 and 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. It is pertinent to note that, the offences under sections 4 and 6 of the POCSO Act, 2012 are pertaining to the sexual harassment or sexual exploitation of the minors below the age of 18 years. In this case, by cogent and corroborative evidence it is not proved that on the date of offence, the prosecutrix was minor or below the age of 18 years. No ossification test was carried by the Investigation Officer for the purpose of determining Dpk/J­Atro. Spl Case No.45/2013 .....14/­ ..14.. Judgment­Atro Spl.Case 45/2013 the age of prosecutrix. The alleged birth certificate produced on record do not pertain to the birth of the prosecutrix. No explanation regarding the difference of names in the birth certificate at Exh.30 is sought by the prosecution from PW No.3 Anita Hajare and PW No.6 Mahesh Hajare when opportunity was there to bring the explanation on record. Thus, failure on the part of prosecution to prove the explanation regarding the change in the surname of father and name of mother in certificate at Exh.30 is fatal to the case of prosecution. In these doubtful circumstances, it cannot be said at all that the prosecution succeeded to prove the guilt of accused beyond all reasonable doubts. Rather, there are reasonable doubts regarding the age of prosecutrix on the date of incident. Prosecution ought to have been adduced more concrete and reliable evidence, which is not done by the prosecution. Therefore, benefit of doubt must go to the accused. 20/­ For the reasons stated and discussed above, I answer all the points in negative and pass the following order : ­: O R D E R :­ 1. Accused James Hanumanta Surve is hereby acquitted of the offence punishable under sections 376, 506 of Indian Penal Code and under sections 3, 5(J)(2) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2. Accused is in jail. He be released forthwith if not required in any other case or crime. 3. Accused to furnish PR & SB of Rs.15,000/­ in compliance of Section 437­A of Cr.P.C. Dpk/J­Atro. Spl Case No.45/2013 .....15/­ ..15.. Judgment­Atro Spl.Case 45/2013 4. This case be sent to District Legal Services Authority under section 357(A)(2) of Cr.P.C. for compensation to the prosecutrix. Her cross­ examination was conducted on 17/1/2017. Thus, there was sufficient time for accused to contact victim girl, her relatives, her parents and won over the witnesses. It seems that after 8/12/2016 the matter was compromised between complainant and accused person. This fact is admitted by P.W.4 Namibai in her cross­examination. Her deposition took place on24/1/2017. Even the evidence of P.W.5 Sushma Mukne was recorded after the compromise. A particular mode is adopted by the learned advocate for accused for extracting admissions particularly in cross­examination. If we go through the cross­examination of P.W.2 victim girl and P.W.5 Sushma Mukne , then it clearly appears that advocate for accused went on giving suggestions in his favour and the witnesses went on admitting those suggestions by saying only “yes”. The admissions during cross­examination are not brought by the way of artful cross­examination. Mere suggestions not favouring to the prosecution were given with specific intention to the witnesses to say only “yes”. Thus, the manner in which cross­examination of P.W.2 victim girl and P.W.5 Sushma Mukne is conducted clearly indicates that after examination­in­chief of P.W.2 victim girl was over and the matter was adjourned for cross­examination. During that period the witnesses, mostly the victim girl and the relatives of victim girl namely P.W.4 Namibai Bhosle and P.W.5 Sushma Mukne were won over by the accused. Here it is most interesting to note that AVP Atro.Spl.Case 120/16 .31/­ 31 Atro.Spl.Case No.120/2016 Judgment. though all other suggestions of the accused persons are admitted by victim girl. During her cross­examination she specifically denied the suggestion on the part of the accused that no rape was committed by accused on her. I would like to reproduce that suggestion which is on record from the cross­examination of P.W.2 victim girl in para 18 of her deposition. That suggestion and answer is , “It is not true that the accused never caught hold my both the hands with his one hand and then removed her nicker and pant and removed his own pant and underwear and then he forcibly committed sexual intercourse with me and he used to commit sexual intercourse with me daily for 15 days”. This suggestion regarding denial of forcible intercourse or any intercourse by accused with victim girl is flatly denied by the victim girl. This also fully supports and corroborates her deposition in examination­in­chief. 34] Thus, in view of the principle laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the cases (supra) the portion in the deposition of hostile witnesses which is cogent, corroborative, truthful and inspiring the confidence in the judicial mind can be relied by rejecting the remaining portion in the evidence of such witnesses. In view of this principle, I can rely on the examination­in­chief of P.W.2 victim girl, P.W.5 Sushma Mukne because the same is truthful and inspire full confidence in the judicial mind regarding happening of the alleged incident. Therefore, merely because during cross­examination these witnesses fall to the suggestions AVP Atro.Spl.Case 120/16 .32/­ 32 Atro.Spl.Case No.120/2016 Judgment. on behalf of the accused, their part of the truthful deposition in their evidence can not be rejected or denied outrightly. Rather the first part of their deposition seems to be genuine, truthful , corroborative to the prosecution's case in all respect. Hence, I accept that portion, rely on that portion and hold that prosecution has succeeded to prove guilt of accused U/Sec.376 of I.P.C. and U/Sec.4 of POCSO Act. 35] Now, it is proved that accused committed forcible intercourse with victim girl. This act of accused is clear indicative of the fact that accused kidnapped victim girl by inducing her to compel her to have forcible illicit intercourse with him. These circumstances further strengthen the allegation of the prosecution against this accused of the offence U/Sec.366 of Indian Penal Code. 36] At this stage, it is vehemently contended by learned advocate for accused that on the date of incident accused was minor below the age of 18 years as his date of birth is 12/6/1998. Birth certificate is produced at Exh.43. Therefore, the accused ought to have been tried by the Juvenile Court and not by the regular court. This argument is raised only at the time of final argument. This is not suggested to any investigating officer. Not a single suggestion to that effect is given to the investigating officer either P.W.12 P.S.I.Dhumal or P.W.13 A.P.I. Giri. Apart from that as per Sec.27 of Cr.P.C., “ any offence not punishable AVP Atro.Spl.Case 120/16 .33/­ 33 Atro.Spl.Case No.120/2016 Judgment. with death or imprisonment for life committed by any person who at the date when he appears or is brought before the court is under the age of 16 years may be tried by the court of Chief Judicial Magistrate or by any other court specially empowered under the Children Act, 1960 or by the Juvenile Court. Admittedly on the date of commission of offence this accused was above 16 yeas old. In this case this accused was arrested on 27/6/2016 and on the same day or next day he was produced before the learned Magistrate. Thus, on the date of his production before the Magistrate as per Sec.27 of Cr.P.C. he was above 18 years. Therefore, these arguments are not sustainable. It is also to be looked into that accused committed rape/penetrative sexual assault on victim, the crime on 12/6/2016 and thereafter for about 10 to 15 days. Considering his date of birth accused had completed his 18 years on 11/6/2016 or 12/6/2016 itself. This fact is purposely overlooked by advocate for accused. 37] As per Sec.29 of POCSO Act, 2012 there is legal presumption in favour of prosecution and that is to be rebutted by accused. Section 29 of POCSO Act reads as , “Where a person is prosecution for committing or abetting or attempting to commit any offence under Section 3,5,7 and 9 of the Act, the Special Court shall presume that such person has committed or abetted or attempted to commit the offence, as the case may be, unless the contrary is proved. In this case to prove contrary accused examined D.W.2 Gajanan Shingya Wagh, the father of the AVP Atro.Spl.Case 120/16 .34/­ 34 Atro.Spl.Case No.120/2016 Judgment. accused. He made a general statement in his examination­in­chief that on account of dispute regarding the landed property his relations with complainant are strained. In examination­in­chief he falsifies his earlier statement by admitting that there were no complaints between him and complainant against each other. Thus, the evidence of D.w.2 Gajanan Wagh itself is contradictory. It is tried to bring on record by accused through the mouth of D.W.1 Gulab Mukne that there is dispute between her family and family of the accused on account of landed property. No particulars of that dispute are specifically brought on record either through the defence evidence or through the suggestions to the prosecution witnesses. No documents regarding the alleged property dispute between these two families on record. On the contrary the father of the accused himself admitted that there were no complaints against each other between his family and family of accused. It means that only for the sake of defence this defence is raised and it carries no force at all. 38] Surprisingly contrary suggestion is given to P.W.1 Yogesh Mukne during his cross­examination that there is dispute between family of accused and the family of in­laws of this witness. It is not suggested to this witness that there is any dispute between his family and family of accused. 39] It has brought on record through the cross­ examination of P.W.12 P.S.I.Dhumal that he enquired about the AVP Atro.Spl.Case 120/16 .35/­ 35 Atro.Spl.Case No.120/2016 Judgment. rivalry between the family members of accused and the victim, but there was no rivalry or enmity. Thus, about the alleged dispute between the family of accused and victim was enquired into by P.W.12 P.S.I.Dhumal one of the investigating officer and he found existence of no such rivalry or enmity. This itself falsifies defence of accused about the rivalry. 40] One new defence is raised on behalf of accused while giving some suggestions to P.W.12 investigating officer P.S.I.Vijay Dhumal. In para 15 of his cross­examination it is suggested to him that victim while going in local train with her grandmother to Badlapur she was missing. It is further suggested to him that after 15 days the victim returned to her parents. From where this new theory is brought best known to him. Though these suggestions are given no defence evidence is adduced by the defence to prove this . It seems that accused was traveling from one defence to another to make a defence by hook or crook and ultimately he failed. 41] At this stage, I take pause to record further statement of accused U/Sec. 313 of Cr.P.C. on the point of sentence and to hear accused, his advocatge and A.P.P. on the point of sentence. Kalyan. (D.S. Hatarote ) 30/08/2017. Addl. Sessions Judge, Kalyan. AVP Atro.Spl.Case 120/16 .36/­ 36 Atro.Spl.Case No.120/2016 Judgment. 42] I have heard learned A.P.P.Shri.Bhangre. He submitted that offence is of serious nature. It is a social office. Maximum punishment be awarded to this accused. The learned advocate for accused submitted that accused is young boy. He is from poor family. This is his first offence. He prayed for leniency and minimum sentence. 43] Considering the nature of offence, considering young age of the accused, considering his economical condition, considering the fact that this accused has no criminal antecedent , the following sentence will meet the ends of justice. 44] Before that I would like to mention that offence U/Sec. 363 & 366 of I.P.C. are similar in nature except difference that U/Sec.366 of I.P.C. kidnapping or abducting must be to force the kidnapped woman or girl to marry or to illicit intercourse. Except this difference the ingredients of both the offences are similar. Therefore, it would be just and property to award a single sentence for the offence U/Sec.363 & 366 of I.P.C. 45] Similar is the fact in respect of the offence punishable U/Sec.376 and U/Sec.4 of POCSO Act, 2012. The only requirement for the offence U/Sec.4 of POCSO Act, 2012 is that the victim must be a child as defined in Sec.2(i)(d) of POCSO Act, 2012, other criterias are similar. In this case it would be just and proper to award single sentence for these two offences , AVP Atro.Spl.Case 120/16 .37/­ 37 Atro.Spl.Case No.120/2016 Judgment. considering the young age of the accused. Hence, I pass the following order : :ORDER: 1) Accused Sunil Gajanan Wagh is hereby convicted for the offence punishable U/Secs.363 & 366 of I.P.C. and he is sentenced to suffer Rigorous Imprisonment for seven years and to pay fine of Rs.1,000/­ (Rs.One Thousand only) i.d. to suffer further Rigorous Imprisonment for three months. 2) Accused is also convicted for the offence punishable U/Sec.376 of I.P.C. and U/Sec.4 of P.O.C.S.O. Act,2012 and he is sentenced to suffer Rigorous Imprisonment for seven years and to pay fine of Rs.1,000/­ (Rs.One Thousand only) i.d. to suffer further Rigorous Imprisonment for three months. 3) Accused is hereby acquitted of the offence punishable U/Sec.6 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, 2012. 4) All substantive sentences shall run concurrently. 5) Accused is in jail. He is entitled to get set off U/Sec.428 of Cr.P.C. for the days he is already in jail. 6) The muddemal property i.e. clothes being worthless be destroyed after period of appeal is over. AVP Atro.Spl.Case 120/16 .38/­ 38 Atro.Spl.Case No.120/2016 Judgment. 7) Accused is hereby informed that he is at liberty to prefer an appeal against this judgment and conviction order before Hon'ble High Court, Bombay . 8) Judgment is declared and dictated in open court. Hence, copy of this judgment be provided to the accused free of costs as soon as it is typed and ready. 9) Jail authority is hereby directed to keep this accused present before this court on 8th September, 2017 for receiving copy of this judgment free of costs. Kalyan. (D.S. Hatarote ) 30/08/2017. Addl. Sessions Judge, Kalyan. AVP Atro.Spl.Case 120/16 ./­

1 Cri.Ant.Bail 1286/17 Order below Exh.1 ORDER BELOW EXH.1 IN CRI.ANTI.BAIL APPLN.NO.1286/2017 : 1] Read application and say of the prosecution. Perused documents. Heard Ld.A.P.P. and Ld advocate for accused at length. 2] This is an anticipatory bail application under section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,1973. 3] Crime bearing No.I­356/2017 is registered against this accused in Kolsewadi Police Station for the offence punishable U/Sec.376(1)(2)(w) of I.P.C. and U/Sec.4,8 & 12 of POCSO Act, 2012. 4] It is the allegation of the prosecution that since November, 2016 to February 2017 the accused committed rape on complainant Sonam Ramlotan Kori the prosecutrix under the false promise of marring her. Subsequently without any information to prosecutrix the accused went away to his native and therefore prosecutrix lodged complaint against this accused and crime is registered. This accused apprehends his arrest by Kolsewadi Police and hence this application. 5] In this application, it is the say of applicant that he has committed no offence. False and fabricated complaint is lodged against him with ulterior motive to harass him. This applicant is resident of Kalyan. He is law abiding citizen. He will not abscond. There were love affairs between this accused and the complainant. The complainant is telling lie for pressurizing the applicant to accept the marriage proposal. Applicant is poor. His monthly payment is not more than Rs.7,000/­ p.m. The complaint is false and vexatious. Offence is not punishable with 2 Cri.Ant.Bail 1286/17 Order below Exh.1 death. There is no need of custodial interrogation. Applicant is ready to furnish bail. He is ready to abide by any condition. He prayed that he be released on anticipatory bail. 6] This application is strongly opposed by prosecution. It is the say of prosecution that yet interrogation is to be carried with this accused. His medical examination is to be carried. This accused is resident of Gram Zaliya, Post.Jigna Bazar, Tal. Mankapur, Dist.Gonda, Uttar Pradesh. If applicant/accused released on bail, there is possibility of his absconding. The offence is of serious nature. If this accused released on bail he may put pressure on the prosecution witnesses. He will not remain present in the court and therefore prosecution prayed that application be rejected. 7] Offence is of serious nature. Prosecutrix is aged about 17 years and she is minor. Even though we accept the contention of this accused that there were love affairs between himself and the prosecutrix and out of that love affairs they had sexual relations. That itself amounts an offence. As I have already stated it is the offence against the minor girl and is of serious nature. Definitely custody of this accused for custodial interrogation is must. For the purpose of medical examination of this accused custody is required. If this accused released on bail the very object of the investigation would be frustrated. 8] At this stage, the Ld.Adv. for the accused drawn my attention towards the affidavit filed by the father of prosecutrix namely Ramlotan Mataprasad Kori. Drawing my attention 3 Cri.Ant.Bail 1286/17 Order below Exh.1 towards his affidavit he submitted that now already matter is compromised and the family members of the prosecutrix do not want to proceed against this accused. Similar affidavit is filed by the father of the applicant and the applicant himself. Question of compromising the offence U/Sec.376 of I.P.C. as well as U/Secs. 4, 8 & 12 of P.O.C.S.O. does not arise at all. Consent is totally immaterial in the cases of sexual assault on minor girls. Therefore, this compromise has no meaning at all in the eyes of law. Merely because the father of prosecutrix filed affidavit stating that he do not want to prosecute the accused, anticipatory bail can not be granted. Hence, I pass the following order : :ORDER: 1) Application stands rejected. 2) Applicant is directed to surrender before the investigating officer immediately. 3) Copy of this order be sent to concerned police station for information. Kalyan. (D.S.Hatarote) Dt.07/10/2017 Addl.Sessions Judge, Kalyan.

Charge was read over and explained to accused in Marathi language. Accused pleaded not guilty. He claimed to be tried. 5/­ Prosecution was directed to adduce its evidence. Dpk/J­Atro. Spl Case No.51/2013 .....4/­ ..4.. Judgment­Atro Spl.Case 51/2013 Accordingly, prosecution examined in all 8 witnesses in this case. PW No.1 is the victim girl (Exh.12). She narrated the incident before the Court. PW No.2 Dhananjay Balasaheb Borade is the informer and Principal of Archana English Medium School, Shahapur (Exh.13). He proved his earlier complaint application to police station at Exh.14 and his FIR at Exh.15. PW No.3 Sujata Rajesh Phule (Exh.16) is the mother of victim girl. Then he forwarded the information regarding incident to the parents of victim girl. He went to PW No.2 Dhananjay Balasaheb Borade and insisted the action against the accused. All these facts are deposed by him. PW No.6 Prakash Dattatray Gumre (Exh.25) is examined on the point of birth date of the victim girl. He deposed that birth date of victim girl is 12.03.1999. He proved the birth certificate which is at Exh.26. PW No.7 Pradeep Raghunath Pitale (Exh.29) is watchman in the Archana English Medium School. He deposed that, on the day of incident accused conducted extra period for scholarship students. He saw the victim girl leaving the school first and thereafter the accused leaving the school.
