Judgment­Atro Spl.Case 51/2013 about the investigation he carried. Thereafter, vide pursis Exh.36, prosecution closed its evidence. 6/­ Statement of accused under section 313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is recorded by putting him all incriminating facts, circumstances and evidence and his explanation is sought. From the answers given by him, his defence emerges as of total denial. He examined one defence witness namely Ravindra Katod Palvi (Exh.44) on the point of no extra periods were conducted in Archana English Medium School. This witness also deposed regarding the character, behaviour of the accused. 7/­ I have gone through the oral as well as documentary evidence adduced by prosecution. I have heard Ld. APP Shri D.V. Bhangre for prosecution and Ld. Advocate Shri M.M. Deshmukh for accused at length. Following points arise for my determination. My findings on those points are as follows for the reasons stated below : Sr.No. Points Findings 1. Does prosecution prove that on the .. In the affirmative. day of incident, the victim was minor as her date of birth was 12.03.1999 ? 2. Does prosecution prove that on .. In the negative. 01.09.2013 in between 10.00 to 11.00 hrs. at Archana English Medium School, Ganga Road, accused used criminal force to minor victim girl, aged 14 years, intending to outrage her modesty Dpk/J­Atro. Spl Case No.51/2013 .....6/­ ..6.. Judgment­Atro Spl.Case 51/2013 and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 354 of IPC? 3. Does prosecution prove that on the .. In the negative. aforesaid date, time and place, accused committed sexual assault on the minor victim girl, aged 14 years and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 ? 4. Does prosecution prove that on the .. In the negative. aforesaid date, time and place, accused being the staff of Archana English Medium School committed sexual assault on the minor victim girl in that school and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 10 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 ? ­: R E A S O N S :­ As to point no.1 : 8/­ It is the contention of prosecution that, on the date of alleged incident, may it be 25.08.2013 or 01.09.2013, the victim girl was minor because her date of birth is 12.03.1999. At the time of alleged incident she was taking education in 9 th standard. Her birth certificate is produced on record. Not only this, but PW6 Prakash Dattatray Gumre, person from Shahapur Nagar Panchayat deposed before this Court and proved the birth certificate of victim girl which is at Exh.26 as true and correct as per original Dpk/J­Atro. Spl Case No.51/2013 .....7/­ ..7.. Judgment­Atro Spl.Case 51/2013 certificate. It is the contention of accused that, on the alleged date of incident victim girl was not minor. This is a contention merely raised for the sake of defence. This contention of accused carries no force at all. On the contrary, victim girl, her parents, her school principal as well as PW No.6 Prakash Dattatray Gumre, all stated that date of birth of victim girl is 12.03.1999. It means that on the alleged date of incident, may it be on 25.08.2013 or 01.09.2013, the victim girl was minor. I have no doubt in my mind about that. Therefore, I answer point no.1 in the affirmative. As to point nos.2 to 4 : 9/­ In order to avoid repetition of discussion, I would like to discuss and consider all these three points together. 10/­ Initially, allegation of prosecution was that, on 25.08.2013 this accused called the victim girl in the school for extra period. First he took extra period of scholarship students. Thereafter, he taught some English grammer to victim girl who was alone in his class. Then, he gave information regarding UPSC and MPSC examination, and when the victim girl was about to go out of the class, this accused pushed the door to some extent, tried to hug the victim to which she protested. Then he took kiss of the victim by putting his lips on her lips. Thus, the sum and substance of initial allegation of the prosecution is that, the act of molestation of the victim took place on 25.08.2013 in a classroom in Archana English Medium School. The FIR is filed in respect of that incident only by PW No.2 Dhananjay Balasaheb Borade, Dpk/J­Atro. Spl Case No.51/2013 .....8/­ ..8.. Judgment­Atro Spl.Case 51/2013 which is at Exh.15. It is now admitted fact that, on 25.08.2013 this accused appeared for MPSC examination at Thane. He was not on that day in the school. This fact is admitted by Investigation Officer in his deposition. Not only this, but, Investigation Officer PW No.8 Vijay Sadashiv Patil in his cross­ examination admitted that, he got confirmed from MPSC through correspondence that on 25.08.2013 this accused appeared for MPSC examination at Thane Center in between 10.30 a.m. to 1.30 p.m. Even other prosecution witnesses admitted during their depositions before the Court that, they subsequently came to know that on 25.08.2013 this accused appeared in MPSC examination at Thane. Thus, it is crystal clear that, no incident took place, as alleged by prosecution, on 25.08.2013. Therefore, all the allegations against the accused regarding incident dated 25.08.2013 are totally false. 11/­ Now, in second phase the prosecution raised the contention that the incident took place on 01.09.2013. The victim girl wrongly stated the date and therefore, said wrong date was forwarded by the family members of victim girl to the Principal Borade and in turn he lodged complaint pertaining to that particular wrong date. In fact, the incident took place on 01.09.2013, is the contention of the prosecution. 12/­ It is pertinent to note that, PW No.2 Dhananjay Balasaheb Borade, PW No.4 Rajesh Harishchandra Phule, PW No.7 Pradeep Raghunath Pitale as well as PW No.5 Prashant Dpk/J­Atro. Spl Case No.51/2013 .....9/­ ..9.. Judgment­Atro Spl.Case 51/2013 Harishchandra Phule, all unanimously stated that, to conduct the extra period on holiday i.e. on Sunday, prior permission from the Institution or from Principal of the Institution is must. It is the fact that, no such permission was obtained by this accused to conduct extra period for any class on Sundays. It is not the case of prosecution that, no such permission was granted by the educational institution or the Principal to the accused. In spite of that, it is tried to bring on record through the prosecution evidence especially through the deposition of PW No.2 Dhananjay Borade and PW No.7 Pradeep Pitale that accused was conducting extra period on Sundays in the month of August and September, 2013. I am very surprised as to how the Principal Dhananjay Borade (PW No.2) allowed this accused to conduct extra period on Sundays without permission is nowhere explained by the prosecution. 13/­ After going through the deposition of PW No.2 Dhananjay Borade it appears that, he is totally deposing lie or false facts. It is pertinent to note that, he gave his deposition in Court on 23.08.2016. Till that time, it is open to all that the incident took place on 01.09.2013. Irrespective of all these facts, while deposing before this Court Principal Dhananjay Borade in his cross­examination deposed that, the incident took place on 25.08.2013. He goes to the extent to say that, on that day accused was present in the school and had conducted extra classes for which he inquired with his other staff members. He further deposed that, the staff members disclosed him that accused has Dpk/J­Atro. Spl Case No.51/2013 .....10/­ ..10.. Judgment­Atro Spl.Case 51/2013 conducted the class on 25.08.2013 and it was a Sunday. He further deposed that, he came to know this fact from Watchman Pradeep Pitale. Watchman Pradeep Pitale deposed as PW No.7. He stated that, on 25.08.2013 accused did not conduct any extra class. On the contrary, on 01.09.2013 accused conducted the class and the alleged incident took place and he informed about the same to Principal on next day. Surprisingly, PW No.2 Dhananjay Borade do not utter a single word about the information given by PW No.7 Pradeep Pitale to him in respect of the incident dated 01.09.2013. It means that, either one of them or both of them are deposing falsely. Therefore, their depositions are not reliable at all. 14/­ It is deposed by PW No.7 Pradeep Pitale that, accused used to conduct extra classes in holidays for scholarship examination. It means that, only the students who appeared for scholarship examination were expected to attend the extra classes of accused. It is not the case of prosecution that, the victim girl was appearing to any scholarship examination at the time of incident. Therefore, in fact there was no reason for her to come to the school on holiday for any extra class. This creates reasonable doubt regarding the presence of victim girl in the school on 01.09.2013. 15/­ Admittedly, the victim girl was studying in 9 th standard. As per contention of prosecution, accused asked victim girl to come for extra period as he was intending to teach English Dpk/J­Atro. Spl Case No.51/2013 .....11/­ ..11.. Judgment­Atro Spl.Case 51/2013 grammer to her. It is admitted by PW No.2 Dhananjay Borade that, English was not the teaching subject of this accused in the school. On the contrary, he was teaching Social Science to the students. It is not at all expected from a teacher of Social Science to teach the students English grammer. It is not brought on record by the prosecution that this accused has acquired any mastery in English language or in English grammer. I am unable to understand how a teacher of Social Science was expected to teach English grammer to his students. The story itself seems to be doubtful. 16/­ It seems that, as per prosecution story accused had called only three students for extra classes from 9 th standard. What was the special reason for calling only three students out of 44 students in the class is best known to the prosecution because about that no explanation is brought on record. One Himanshu and Sunny were the other students than the victim who were called for extra classes by accused, as alleged by the prosecution. It is further contended by the prosecution that Himanshu and Sunny were absent on that day and only victim was present. It has come on record in the deposition of victim that, on earlier Sunday, she had been to school for extra classes but on that day also Himanshu and Sunny were absent. Therefore, on that day no extra class was conducted by the accused. Then I am unable to understand why on 01.09.2013 this victim stayed in the school when her classmates Himanshu and Sunny were absent. This is also not explained by the prosecution. Dpk/J­Atro. Spl Case No.51/2013 .....12/­ ..12.. Judgment­Atro Spl.Case 51/2013 17/­ The most important lacuna in the prosecution story is that, except the bare words of interested persons like the family members of the victim, like the principal of the school, there is no evidence on record to show that this accused had called these three students for extra classes on Sunday. In this respect evidence of Himanshu and Sunny is most important evidence. They could have been thrown light on the fact that whether this accused had called them for extra period on Sundays or not. I do not know for what reason the Investigation Officer has not examined or has not recorded statements of these two important witnesses namely Himanshu and Sunny. Had they been examined or inquired, definitely true fact would have been revealed. Thus, the Investigation Officer or for what reason the prosecution withheld the important evidence and witnesses from the court. This compels me to draw adverse inference against the prosecution regarding the fact that, whether the accused had called these three students for extra class or whether the allegation of prosecution is false. Non examining the important witnesses like Himanshu and Sunny is definitely fatal to the prosecution case. 18/­ One more interesting fact is on record which creates reasonable doubt regarding happening of the incident. Though the alleged incident took place on 01.09.2013, victim did not disclose the incident to anybody till 07.09.2013. It is contended by Ld. APP Shri Bhangre on behalf of prosecution that, she was frightened and therefore, she could not disclose the incident to anybody. This is not appellable to judicial mind. It is pertinent to Dpk/J­Atro. Spl Case No.51/2013 .....13/­ ..13.. Judgment­Atro Spl.Case 51/2013 note that, even after 01.09.2013 this victim was continuously going to the school. She was attending all classes and periods. It shows that, she was not at all frightened. Had it been the fact that she was frightened, then definitely she would have been avoided to go to the school out of fear of the accused. But, nothing of that sort has happened. It is further interesting to note that, this important incident is not disclosed by the victim to her mother or to her father. She disclosed the incident to her uncle. It is the common belief that the mother is the best friend of the girl. Even though, this incident was not disclosed by victim to her parents. This is quite unnatural. It is surprising that, parents of victim girl came to know about the incident from the uncle of the victim i.e. Prashant Harishchandra Phule. 19/­ Here, one thing is to be made clear that, evidence of PW No.2 Dhananjay Borade, PW No.3 Sujata Rajesh Phule, PW No.4 Rajesh Harishchandra Phule, PW No.5 Prashant Harishchandra Phule is totally based on hearsay. They have no personal knowledge or no direct knowledge about the incident. Atleast we can say that PW No.5 Prashant Harishchandra Phule came to know about the incident from the victim herself. But, the knowledge of other witnesses is from Prashant Phule itself and therefore, they are not much important witnesses on the point of incident at all. Even the deposition of PW No.5 Prashant Harishchandra Phule is based on hearsay and that carries no importance. Dpk/J­Atro. Spl Case No.51/2013 .....14/­ ..14.. Judgment­Atro Spl.Case 51/2013 20/­ Above all this, the admissions given by the victim during her deposition before the Court are most important. There are important omissions amounting to improvement and material contradictions in the entire deposition of PW No.1 victim girl as well as there are such types of material omissions and improvements in the deposition of PW No.3 Sujata Phule. In para 5 of the deposition of PW No.1 victim girl and during her cross­ examination she admitted that, she never stated in her statement before police that accused called her for teaching English grammer. She further admitted that, she does not state before police that accused had called Himanshu and Sunny on that day for the class. She had not stated before police that Himanshu and Sunny had not come for extra classes on 01.09.2013. She had not stated before police that, on 01.09.2013 scholarship students of 7 th standard were present in the class. The most important omission/ improvement is that, she never stated to police that when she was closing her bag, at that time accused pushed the door ahead in order to close it. She never stated to police that accused caught her hand and pushed towards wall. She never stated to police that accused attempted to hug her. However, all these facts are stated by her during her examination­in­chief. 21/­ It is admitted by PW No.8 Investigation Officer Vijay Sadashiv Patil that, all these facts were not stated by the victim girl to him when he recorded her statement during investigation. Though it is stated by victim in her deposition that, she had stated to police that accused touched her lips with his lips, but police did Dpk/J­Atro. Spl Case No.51/2013 .....15/­ ..15.. Judgment­Atro Spl.Case 51/2013 not record so, PW No.8 Vijay Patil admitted in his cross­ examination that victim girl had not stated to him that accused kissed her or put his lips on her lips. Thus, from the admissions given by victim in her cross­examination and from the deposition of PW No.8 Investigation Officer Vijay Patil it is crystal clear that the incident which is deposed by PW No.1 victim girl before this Court during her examination­in­chief was never stated by her to police officer who investigated the offence. It means that, the entire evidence of victim girl regarding the incident is nothing but an improvement. At the same time, its omission from statement before police amounting to material contradiction. How the victim can be relied with when she has not stated anything about the incident during investigation before Investigation Officer and she stated before Court a very new story of her molestation by accused. 22/­ It is pertinent to note that, during investigation none of the prosecution witnesses stated to Investigation Officer that this accused hugged the victim and kissed her and thereby outraged her modesty. The allegation of PW No.3 Sujata Rajesh Phule, PW No.2 Dhananjay Balasaheb Borade, PW No.4 Rajesh Harishchandra Phule, PW No.5 Prashant Harishchandra Phule is that, on particular day this accused outraged the modesty of the victim girl. How he outraged the modesty or what act he done with the victim girl nowhere stated during entire investigation. Mere general allegations were made against the accused. Regarding the acts allegedly done by the accused at the time of Dpk/J­Atro. Spl Case No.51/2013 .....16/­ ..16.. Judgment­Atro Spl.Case 51/2013 incident the new story was put forth by improvement in the original story. Therefore, neither the original story nor the improved story is believable. 23/­ Much stress is given by Ld. Advocate for prosecution on the deposition of PW No.7 Pradeep Pitale. He deposed that on 01.09.2013 he was on duty as a watchman. He saw victim and accused went out of the school gate. Victim girl went out first and then the accused. He informed this fact to one Swapnil Mali, the Clerk and then on next day he informed the said fact to Principal. Even if we accept his evidence as it is, that is not sufficient at all to prove the alleged act of molestation by this accused. As I have already stated, Principal Dhananjay Borade has not uttered a single word about the information given by this PW No.7 Pradeep Pitale on 01.09.2013 or on 02.09.2013. I have already disbelieved both these witnesses in foregoing paras and therefore, the facts deposed by this PW No.7 Pradeep Pitale even if accepted as it is, that is not sufficient. On the contrary, the admissions given by PW No.7 Pradeep Pitale in his cross­examination are most important. He admitted that, he never heard anything bad against the accused prior to the incident. He had no knowledge about the incident. He further admitted that, victim girl was not appearing in any scholarship examination and hence, there was no reason for her to attend the extra classes. Though, he was on duty on that day, he does not know as to which class the accused used to teach. He does not know in which class the alleged incident took place. It is much surprising that the Investigation Officer has not Dpk/J­Atro. Spl Case No.51/2013 .....17/­ ..17.. Judgment­Atro Spl.Case 51/2013 prepared the spot panchanama. School is a big building. In which classroom the incident took place is neither stated by the victim, nor by any prosecution witnesses, nor by the Investigation Officer. This shows utter negligence on the part of the Investigation Officer in the investigation. 24/­ There are some other admissions of PW No.8 Investigation Officer Vijay Sadashiv Patil which shows the fact that the investigation was not carried properly. He admitted that, he never collected any evidence that the victim was present in extra class held on 25.08.2013 or 01.09.2013. This single admission of Investigation Officer is more than sufficient enough to show that, there is no proof with prosecution to show that the victim girl was present in the school or in any classroom on 01.09.2013 or on 25.08.2013. If there is no proof regarding the presence of victim girl in a school on a particular date when the alleged incident took place, then the question of happening any incident does not arise at all. He further admitted that the victim girl never stated to him that accused caught hold her hand and pulled her. She never stated in her statement before him that accused put his lips on her lips. In spite of this, the Investigation Officer has submitted charge­sheet against the accused. This is very strange. When there was no evidence of any act of molestation by the accused, I am unable to understand why the Investigation Officer submitted the charge­sheet. 25/­ Accused examined one witness in defence i.e. Dpk/J­Atro. Spl Case No.51/2013 .....18/­ ..18.. Judgment­Atro Spl.Case 51/2013 Ravindra Katod Palvi. He stated that, there was no practice to conduct extra periods in Archana English Medium School. He deposed that, character, behaviour of the accused was good and there was no complaint against his character. Even for the sake of arguments, we keep aside the evidence of defence, then also, absolutely there is no material evidence on record to prove the alleged offences against the accused. 26/­ At this stage, it is vehemently argued by Ld. APP Shri Bhangre for the State that, there is presumption in favour of prosecution under section 29 of the POCSO Act. That presumption is to be rebutted by the accused. It is true. However, there must be prima­facie evidence to believe that the accused has committed some sort of criminal act or any offence under the POCSO Act. Then and then the burden will be on accused to prove that he has not committed any act. In this case, absolutely there is no evidence that the extra class was conducted by accused on 01.09.2013. No evidence to show that he called the victim girl for extra class. There is no proof as per the deposition of PW No.8 Investigation Officer Vijay Patil himself to show that on 01.09.2013 victim girl was present in the school. Nothing stated by victim girl or any other prosecution witness to the Investigation Officer about the alleged act of accused that he hugged the victim and kissed her. In these facts and circumstances, I am of the opinion that, there is no need for the accused to rebut any evidence of the prosecution. In fact, there is no material evidence on behalf of the prosecution which can be rebutted. Dpk/J­Atro. Spl Case No.51/2013 .....19/­ ..19.. Judgment­Atro Spl.Case 51/2013 27/­ Thus, considering the pros and cons of the prosecution evidence, it has come to me that, no guilt of the accused is proved for any offence much the less for the alleged offence. Therefore, I answer all three points in negative. In conclusion, I pass following order : ­: O R D E R :­ 1. Accused Mahesh Ramesh Choudhari is hereby acquitted of the offence punishable under section 354 of Indian Penal Code and under sections 8 & 10 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2. His bail bond stands cancelled. 3. He is set at liberty. 4. Accused to furnish PR & SB of Rs.15,000/­ in compliance of Section 437­A of Cr.P.C. Kalyan. (D.S. Hatarote) 16.06.2017. Judgment­Spl.Case 124/2015 CHARGE, PROOF AND DEFENCE : 6/­ On opening of the case by the Ld. APP for the prosecution, charge came to be framed at Exh.8 against accused. No. accused on 23.06.2015 at about 7.30 a.m. at Room No.4, Chawl No.2, Juber Chawl, Behind Arfa Timber Mart, Ambedkar Chowk, Mouje Baneli, Ambivali, Tal. Kalyan, Dist. Accused is acquitted. ­: R E A S O N S :­ As to Point Nos.1 to 3 10/­ It is the case of the prosecution that, accused committed rape by committing penetrative sexual assault on minor victim girl, aged about 12 years by extending threats. 11/­ In order to prove its case, the prosecution has examined in all two witnesses. APP and has specifically denied accused having committing rape on her by committing penetrative sexual assault by extending threats. Hatarote, Additional Sessions Judge-2, Kalyan) Special Case No. 159/2014 Exh.No.__ The state of Maharashtra Through Vishnu Nagar Police Station, .. Prosecution VERSUS Chintamani Ramchandra Kamuni, Age – 62 years, R/at : Vilas Patkar Building, Room No.7, Opposite Apurva Hospital, Dombivali (West). .. Accused Offences : U/Sec. 354-A of the Indian Penal Code and under section 11(1) (4) and 12 of the Protection of children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2 Appearances: ==================================== Smt. Bhoir, A.P.P. for State Shri. G. N. Patil, Advocate for the accused ==================================== J U D G M E N T. ( Delivered in open court on 28th November 2016 ) 1. This accused is prosecuted by Vishnu Nagar police station, for the abovesaid offences. The prosecution story in brief is as follows: 2. One Manisha Bhanushali resident of Dombivali lodged complaint against this accused in the Vishnu Nagar police station on 15/03/2014 and put the criminal law in motion against this accused. In her complaint she alleged that her daughter told her mother in law not to ask her to talk with accused. After two days her daughter Riddhi told her that accused asked her whether she want to eat chocolate. The girl asked chocolate from him. After that this accused removed his pant and asked daughter Riddhi, 'Chus le'. The daughter was frightened. She ran to the house. When this fact was stated by Riddhi to this complainant Manisha, she and her family members took the daughter to councilor Ramesh Mhatre. Accused was called there and asked. However, accused was not ready to say anything. Due to fear of defamation the complainant kept quiet and did not lodge the complaint. After two days again 3 Spl. Case no. 159/14 (Judgment) similar incident happened. And therefore, the complainant came to police station and lodged complaint against the accused. Crime was registered as C.R. No.62/2014. 3. Investigation was carried by one lady P.S.I. V. A. Bhosale. She arrested accused on 15/03/2014. on the same day she prepared spot panchanama. She recorded statement of the victim girl in presence of Special Executive Magistrate, Kashibai Jadhav. Then on 22/03/2014 she recorded statement of Shailesh Bhanushali. Before that she recorded statements of Pinky Chauhan, Ashok Bhanushali, Maniben Bhanushali etc. After completion of investigation she submitted chargesheet in the court. 4. Charge against this accused is framed at Exh.3. The charge was read over and explained to him in Marathi language. He pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. His defence is of total denial. 5. Prosecution was directed to adduce its evidence. In response to that prosecution examined two witnesses in this case. P.W. No.1 Manisha Bhanushali (Exh.6) is the complainant. P.W. No.2 Riddhi Bhanushali (Exh.7) is the victim girl. No further oral evidence adduced by the prosecution. Accused admitted spot panchanama and arrest panchanama. 6. I have gone through the oral and documentary 4 evidence on record. I have heard both learned advocates. Following points arise for my consideration. My findings on those points are as follows for the reasons stated below. POINTS FINDINGS 1) Does prosecution prove that on 15/03/2014 at about 12.00 noon in front of the house of complainant and in the open space of Vilas Patkar Building, Kopar Road, Dombivali (W) accused sexually harassed the minor daughter of complainant namely Riddhi aged 9 years by making physical contact and advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures and thereby committed an offence punishable under No. section 354(A) of the I.P.C.? 2) Does prosecution further prove that on the above-said date, time and place accused committed sexual harassment to the minor daughter of complainant namely Riddhi aged 9 years and thereby committed an offence punishable under sections 11(1)(4), 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences No. Act, 2012 ? REASONS As to Points no. 1 and 2:- 7. Though prosecution examined complainant 5 Spl. Case no. 159/14 (Judgment) Manisha and her victim daughter Riddhi, none of them supported the prosecution case. Manisha though admitted her signature on the complaint, she denied contents in the complaint. Even the victim girl Riddhi deposed before this court and stated that nothing was happened with her and she has stated nothing to police or to her mother. Both these witnesses are cross examined at length by the learned APP. However, nothing incriminating is brought on record against this accused through the cross examination of the prosecution witnesses. 8. Though arrest panchanama and spot panchanama is admitted there is nothing incriminating against this accused in both these panchanamas. 9. Absolutely no evidence on record to prove any of the guilt of the accused. It seems that the matter is compromised by the complainant with accused out of the court. And therefore, prosecution witnesses are not ready to depose anything incriminating against the accused. Whatever may be, the fact is that absolutely no evidence on record against this accused to prove any of his guilt. I answer both the points in negative. 10. As there is no incriminating evidence against this accused, his statement under section 313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure stands dispensed with. 11. In conclusion, I pass the following order. 6 O R D E R 1) The accused Chintamani Ramchandra Kamuni is hereby acquitted of the offence punishable under Section 354-A of the Indian Penal Code and under sections 11(1) (4), 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2) His bail bonds stands cancelled. He is set at liberty. 3) Accused to furnish bail under section 437(A) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Kalyan ( D.S. Hatarote ) Date :- 28/11/2016 Additional Sessions Judge Kalyan.

1 Spl. Case 164/2014 [Judgment] Presented on : 12.12.2014. Registered on : 12.12.2014. Decided on : 5.2.2016. Duration : Y. M. D. 1. 1. 23. IN THE COURT OF SPECIAL JUDGE, KALYAN AT : KALYAN. [Presided over by : M.J.Mirza] SPECIAL CASE NO.164/2014 Exh. No. The State of Maharashtra. Through : P.I. Vithalwadi Police Station, Kalyan. ...Complainant. Vs. Pradeep Popat Hande, Age­30 Years, Occ. Rickshaw driver, R/at­ Madrasi pada, Station road, Ulhasnagar­4, Dist.­ Thane. ….Accused. Appearance : Spl.P.P.Smt. J.S.Lohakare for the State. Advocate Shri S.H.Sonawane for the accused. Offences : ­ Punishable under Section 363 & 376 of I.P.C. and Section 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. :JUDGMENT: [Delivered 5/2/2016, in the open Court] 1. The accused Pradeep Popat Hande is facing the trial for the offences punishable under Sections 363 & 376 of I.P.C. and Section 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2. The case of the prosecution, in short is as under : 2 Spl. Case 164/2014 [Judgment] According to him, the informant PW.2 Sou. Jaya Suresh Bamne lodged the FIR on 28/4/2014 stating therein that she is residing at Shivajinagar, Station Road, Ulhasnagar, along with her husband Suresh, sister Bharati and two sons and the victim daughter, aged 17 years. Her husband works as coolie and she does the work of care­taker. On 22/4/2014, the accused Pradeep Popat Hande proposed the victim for his marriage, however, she refused as his age was more than her age. On 28/4/2014, at 9.30 a.m., when she returned from her work place, she came to know from her husband and sister Bharati, that the victim had left the house without giving any intimation. Then they had gone to the house of the accused to search her but he was also left his house without leaving any message to his family members. Therefore, she suspected that accused kidnapped the victim. 3. PSO, Vithalwadi Police station registered the crime at C.R. No.I­ 108/2014, under Section 363 & 366­A of I.P.C. Further investigation was entrusted to P.S.I. Shri H.A.Galinde who carried out the investigation. He seized the clothes of victim under seizure panchanama at Exh.12 and clothes of the accused at Exh.14. The victim was sent for her medical examination to Central Hospital, Ulhasnagar. The seized clothes were sent to F.S.L. alongwith his covering letter dated 25/8/2014. He recorded the statements of the witnesses including the victim (PW.1). The accused was arrested on 20/8/2014. After completion of investigation he filed chargesheet in this Special Court by adding Section 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 as the victim was found minor below 18 years of the age. 4. Charge Exh.10 was framed by me which was read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. The accused pleaded not guilty 3 Spl. Case 164/2014 [Judgment] and claimed to be tried. His defence is of false involvement as per his statement recorded under Section 313 of Code of Criminal Procedure. Neither the accused stepped into the witness­box nor examined any defence witness. 5. Heard learned Spl. P.P. Smt. J. S. Lohokare for the State and learned Advocate Shri S.H.Sonawane for the accused, at length. 6. The following points arise for my determination and my findings thereon are recorded against them for the reasons to follow:­ Points Findings 1. Whether the prosecution proved that the victim is minor aged 17 years ? .. Yes. 2. Whether prosecution has proved that on 28/4/2014, at 6 to 9.30 a.m. at Shivaji nagar, Station road, the accused kidnapped minor victim girl, aged 17 years from the lawful guardianship of her .. Not proved. parents, punishable under S.363 of I.P.C.? 3. Whether prosecution has proved that at the relevant time the accused committed rape on the minor victim girl aged 17 years, .. Not proved. punishable under Section 376 of I.P.C. ? 4. Whether the prosecution has proved that at the relevant time the accused committed penetrative sexual assault on the minor victim girl aged 17 years, punishable under S. 4 of the Protection of Children from .. Not proved. Sexual Offences Act, 2012 ? 4 Spl. Case 164/2014 [Judgment] 5. What order ? ….. Accused acquitted. : REASONS : 7. To substantiate the charge, prosecution has examined in all two witnesses, viz. PW.1 minor victim girl at Exh.­12 and PW.2 Smt. Jaya Suresh Bamane, the mother of victim at Exh.­16. They both have not supported the case of prosecution in toto. The defence has admitted the seizure panchanama of the clothes of victim at Exh.13 and seizure panchanama of the clothes of the accused at Exh.14 and medical certificate of the victim at Exh.15 as genuineness thereof is not disputed. As to point No. 1 : 8. The victim has stated in her testimony that her birth date is 15/7/1997. She has studied upto IX th standard in Takshashila School, Ambernath. The prosecution has produced the photostat copy of the birth certificate of the victim (not exhibited) alongwith the chargesheet showing her birth date as 15/7/1997. The date of incident is 28/4/2014. Hence, her age as on the date of incident was 16 years 9 months and 13 days, therefore, she was below 18 years of age at the time of incident. In her ossification test on the basis of X­ray, the radiologist has opined the age of the victim was 18 years plus – minus six months. However, in view of the exact birth date of the victim the opinion of radiologist carries no evidentiary value. Hence, it can be safely held that she was minor at the relevant time. Therefore, I answer the point No.1 in the affirmative. As to point No.2 to 4 :­ 9. I have taken all these points together as they are interlinked and to avoid repetition. The victim PW.1 since inception has stated that she has left her house voluntarily without intimating to anyone. She has 5 Spl. Case 164/2014 [Judgment] studied upto IX th standard. Because of the reason that she left her parents home, her mother lodged F.I.R. alleging that the accused has kidnapped her. It has also brought on record that she was staying with the accused for three months at Pune as she had gone with him on her own accord. However, there was physical relationship with her. When she appeared before the police she gave her statement that she has no grievances against the accused and also refused to undergo medical examination. As she was not willing to accompany with her mother after the medical examination, the police sent her to Bhiwandi Remand Home. Even in her statement recorded under S. 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure she has stated the same thing. Now she has married with the accused and leading happy married life but she never go to the house of her parents. 10. The mother of the victim PW.2 Smt. Jaya was on duty during night time on 28/4/2014. When she returned home, but her victim daughter was not found in the house and therefore lodged the F.I.R. at Exh.17. Her supplementary statement was recorded after about four months. She has also brought on record that the victim had married with the accused and residing with him. She has no grievances against the accused. Her daughter is happily residing with the accused after marriage. She has stated that at the time of marriage her daughter was major. 11. Though the clothes of the victim as well as accused were seized under seizure panchanama (Exh.13 & 14) and were sent to F.S.L. but no report thereof has been produced on record by the prosecution. The medical certificate of the victim shows that her hymen was torn and age of tears was old which indicates that there was physical relation. 6 Spl. Case 164/2014 [Judgment] 12. It is seen from the testimony of both the witnesses that the victim had love­affair with the accused, therefore she voluntarily left her parent's home and joined the company of the accused. They both stayed together for three months and thereafter surrendered to the police in view of the F.I.R. of kidnapping lodged by PW.2 Smt. Jaya. Thereafter, the victim and the accused married and residing happily. 13. Under the circumstances, I hold that the prosecution has neither proved that the victim was kidnapped by the accused from her lawful guardianship or the accused had committed rape or penetrative assault on the victim girl. Hence, I answer the point Nos. 2 to 4 in the negative. 14. Resultantly, the accused deserves to be acquitted, and as such, I proceed to pass the following order : ORDER i] Accused Pradeep Popat Hande is hereby acquitted vide Sec. 235(1) of Cr.P.C. of the offences punishable under Sections 363 & 376 of IPC & Section 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. ii] His bail bonds stand cancelled. iii] No muddemal has been produced before the Court. If any muddemal is seized, it shall be destroyed being worthless after the period of appeal is over. iv] The accused shall execute his P.R. of Rs.15,000/­ to appear before the Higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect 7 Spl. Case 164/2014 [Judgment] of appeal filed against this judgment as per S. 437­A of Cr.P.C. v] Such bail shall remain in force for six months from today. Kalyan. [M.J.Mirza] Dt.:­5/2/2016. It is settled position of law that a slight penetration is sufficient to constitute the offence of rape or penetrative sexual assault as held by Their Lordships of the Apex Court in the case of Aman Kumar Vs. State of Haryana (2004 S.C.C. (Cri) 1266) wherein it is held that, “Penetration is the sine qua non for an offence of rape. In order to constitute penetration, there must be evidence clear and cogent to prove that some part of the virile member of the accused was within the labia of the pudendum of the woman, no matter how little. The depth of penetration is immaterial in an offence punishable under Section 376 of I.P.C. Even a slight penetration in the vulva is sufficient to constitute the offence of rape and rupture of the hymen is not necessary. Vulva penetration with or without violence is as much rape as vaginal penetration. The statute merely requires evidence of penetration, and this may occur with the hymen remaining intact. The actus reus is complete with penetration. Thus, to constitute the offence of rape, it is not necessary that there should be complete penetration of the penis with emission of semen and rupture of hymen. Partial penetration within the labia majora of the vulva or pudendum with or without emission of semen is sufficient to constitute the offence of rape as defined in the law.” 54. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case, he submitted that maximum punishment imprisonment for life may be imposed. 61. On the other hand, the Ld. Advocate Shri M.B.Rai for the accused submitted that the age of the accused is 52 years who was already in jail since last 3 years and 4 months. This is first offence, therefore, he submitted that minimum punishment may be awarded. 62. As the offence of rape is concerned, it is against society and anti­social one. The gravity of offence is serious because the minor girl has became victim of rape in her house itself by her foster father (accused) and then committed rape and penetrative sexual assault on her. 63. The punishment prescribed for the offence punishable under Sec. 376 of IPC and Sec. 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 is not less than 7 years but which may extend to imprisonment for life and shall also be liable for fine. Sec.6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 provides the punishment with rigorous imprisonment which shall not be less than 10 years but which may extend to imprisonment for life and shall also be liable to fine. Therefore, considering the mitigating circumstances, the following sentence would be just and proper. Hence, I proceed to pass the following order : 26 Judgment Spl. Case No.55/2013 ORDER i] The accused Rambhavan Bansi Yadav, is hereby convicted under Sec. 235(2) of Cr.P.C. for the offence punishable under Sec. 376 of IPC, and is sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for life and to pay fine of Rs. 25,000/­ (Rs. Twenty five thousand only ), in default to under to rigorous imprisonment for one year. iii] Out of fine amount Rs.50,000/­ if recovered, Rs. 45,000/­ shall be paid to the victim. iv] The accused is in jail since 26/9/2013 hence, he is entitled to get period of detention undergone to be set off under Sec. 428 of Cr.P.C. v] Both the sentences shall run concurrently. vi] The copy of the Judgment and order shall be furnished to the accused, free of costs, forthwith. vii] The seized muddemal property I.e clothes of the victim and accused being worthless be destroyed after the period of appeal is over. 1 ABA1364/2017 Order below Exh.1. ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN A.B.A.NO.1364/2017 : This is an application for grant of anticipatory bail U/Sec. 438 of Cr.P.C. filed by the applicant/accused in C.R.No.I­1163/2017 registered with Railway Police Station U/Sec. 12 of the POCSO Act, 2012. 2] The applicant/accused has been required to move this application for anticipatory bail in sequel to FIR dt.24/09/2017 lodged by the informant Shweta Subhash Rajguru alleging that on 23/09/2017 at about 11.30 a.m. at Railway bridge above platform No.2 the applicant/ accused stuck the informant and uttered words that “Tu mala khup avadte tu maze sobat maitri kar”, caught hold her hands and tried to snatch her sack. The applicant has contended that he is innocent and is falsely implicated in this case. He has contended that he is a college student and his unwanted arrest may spoil his entire career and may be black­listed in college. He has contended that he is residing in the vicinity having his family, parents, therefore, he will not abscond if released on bail. He is ready to abide by the conditions imposed by this court. He has also contended that there is no need of custodial interrogation and no possibility of tampering with prosecution witnesses, if he is released on bail. On the aforestated amongst others ground the applicant has sought for his release on anticipatory bail. 3] I.O. has resisted the bail application by filing his say Exh.4 contending that the applicants/accused has committed serious crime. He contended that the applicant has caught hold the hand of prosecutrix in public place and tried to snatch her sack, thus, the applicant outraged the 2 ABA1364/2017 Order below Exh.1. modesty of minor prosecutrix. He further contended that inspite of notice u/s. 41­A(1) of Cr.P.C., the applicant did not remain present to police station and absconded. I.O. has further contended that if the applicant/accused is released on bail, he would threaten the prosecutrix or her relatives and would tamper with the prosecution evidence. He also contended that there is possibility of committing similar offence if released on bail and also the possibility of not attending the court dates regularly. On these grounds I.O. has wished to reject the bail application. 4] Upon hearing Ld.Adv. Bharti for the applicant/accused and Ld. A.P.P. Shri. Kulkarni for the State, it appears that the present complaint has genesis of the one sided love affair of college going students. Considering the allegations made in the F.I.R. against the applicant/accused, I do not find that there is need of any immediate custodial interrogation. Upon going through the F.I.R. and narrations of the incident, the offence is punishable under Sec. 12 of the POCSO Act and the maximum punishment of the said offence is up to 3 years. Therefore, the present anticipatory bail application would come within the ambit of directions of Their Lordship of Apex Court in the case of Arnesh Kumar V/s. State of Bihar (2014) 8 S.C.C. 273. 5] I find substance in the contention of the Ld. Advocate Bharti for the applicant that there is no necessity for arrest of the applicant/accused as per the parameters laid down under Sec.41 of Cr.P.C. Furthermore, the applicant/accused is a young college going student of 22 years of age. Therefore, considering the nature and gravity of the accusations, it will be appropriate to grant anticipatory bail to the 3 ABA1364/2017 Order below Exh.1. applicant/accused. Therefore, it would be appropriate to grant relief directing the police not to arrest the applicant/ accused in the event of his arrest. 6] It appears that the applicant is permanent resident of Titwala and there is no possibility of his fleeing away from justice. Apart from that I do not find that there is need of custodial interrogation, in view of the allegations made in the first information report. In the result, the following order is made : :ORDER: 1] The Railway Police Station is directed that the applicant/accused in C.R.No.I­1163/2017 registered with Railway Police Station U/Sec. 12 of the POCSO Act, in the event of his arrest, he be released on bail on furnishing their P.B. and S.B. in sum of Rs.15,000/­ by this order of anticipatory bail. 2] He shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any other persons acquainted with the facts of the accusation against him so as to dissuade them from disclosing such facts to the Court to any other officer. 3] He shall attend Kalyan Rly. Police station on each day from tomorrow for 8 days period from 5.00 p.m. to 7.00 p.m. and co­operate the investigating officer in investigation of the crime. 4] Breach of any of the conditions shall entail cancellation of bail. 5] Inform to the concerned Police Station, accordingly. Kalyan. (D.S.Ghumare) Dt.11/10/2017 Addl. Sessions Judge , Kalyan. 4 ABA1364/2017 Order below Exh.1. 4] Ld. Adv. Shri. Chavan for the applicants/accused submitted that as there is no prima facie case against the accused & they are entitled for bail. He also submitted that there is no evidence to connect the applicants/accused with the crime. He also contended that the applicants/ accused does not have any criminal antecedent. He contended that the said case is very vague and there are no specific roles of the applicants/accused, is mentioned in the FIR. He contended that the injuries suffered by the injured witnesses are minor injuries and therefore, this case doesn't come within the purview of Sec. 326 of IPC much less within the ambit of Sec. 307 of IP his C. He also contended that the present applicants/accused are alleged to have only assaulted the witnesses by means of fist and kick blows and not by means of any dangerous weapons. 5] Ld.A.P.P. Shri. Sachin Kulkarni submitted that there is a prima facie case against the applicants/ accused and they had played the active role in commission of the crime. He submitted that there is no 5 ABA1364/2017 Order below Exh.1. justification for the release of the accused on bail as the offence is punishable with life imprisonment. He also submitted that weapons of offence are yet to be recovered and as such, custodial interrogation is necessary. 6] After considering rival submissions, I find that the accused is not entitled for their release on bail broadly on the following grounds : i) That the name of the applicants / accused are clearly disclosed in the F.I.R. and the offence against accused are serious as it is punishable under Sec. 307 & 326 of IPC. ii) That the accused were the member of unlawful assembly which had committed the alleged crime of attempt of murder of the witness and causing of grievous hurt to the witnesses. iii) That at the investigation is yet to be completed. iv) That there is eye witness to this incident and there is prima facie evidence against the accused of their involvement and participation in unlawful assembly. v) That the weapons of offence are yet to be recovered and for that purpose custodial interrogation is necessary. vi) Medical evidence clearly point out that the witnesses had sustained grievous injuries to their person due to the assault by the accused. vii) The applicants/accused had played crucial role in commission of offence and the weapons are deadly being 6 ABA1364/2017 Order below Exh.1. chopper, iron rod and wooden rod. viii) That if the accused are released on bail, there is possibility of tampering with prosecution evidence considering the seriousness of the offence. ix) That to know the modus operandi of the crime and to collect the evidence the custodial interrogation of the accused are necessary, particularly when, by no stretch of imagination it can be stated that the accusations have been made against the applicants/accused with object of humiliating them by having them arrested. x) That there are circumstances in which the accused may provide information leading to discovery of material facts of the crime and the manner in which the crime is committed. That being so the custodial interrogation seems to be quite necessary for effective investigation of crime. xi) To unearth the motive of the applicants/accused behind commission of the crime by them thorough interrogation is certainly necessary. As such, custodial interrogation is quite justified as has been vehemently urged by the Ld. APP for the State. 7] In factual matrix of the present crime it would be far fetch to say that the applicants/accused are innocent and are falsely implicated in the case even though Ld. Adv. Chavan for the accused had strenuously urged that the accused are falsely implicated in the present crime due to political rivalry. Ld. Adv. Chavan for the accused also pointed out me some discrepancies in FIR alike venturesome nature of the informant 7 ABA1364/2017 Order below Exh.1. Tanaji coming out from the house when near about 20 persons had gathered armed with weapons like sword and iron rods outside his house. He also submitted that as per FIR itself only the accused Vinayak Barku Mharse, Sudarshan Dashrath Pashte and Arun Dattatray Kurle were armed with swords and choppers and they are not the amongst the applicants who had made application for anticipatory bail. 8] True, the FIR depicts that Vinayak Barku Mharse, Sudarshan Dashrath Pashte and Arun Dattatray Kurle were armed with swords and choppers and they have assaulted witness Suresh Kurle and had broken windows of his house and damage his car. But then the crime is registered against all of the accused as they were members of unlawful assembly. In the present crime, all the accused were also nominated in crime with the aid of Section 149 IPC. Therefore, I do not find any substance in the contention of Ld Advocate Shri. Chavan for the applicants/accused that the applicants/accused have no role in the crime and that they are falsely implicated. 9] On reading FIR and other documents it cannot be said that, there was no common object, even if, it is admitted that there was a common object, the same was not known to anybody. I do not find substance in the submission of Ld. Adv.Chavan that in facts and circumstances, the involvement of the present accused is just concocted as the FIR specifically states that Vinayak Barku Mahrase, Sudharshan Dashrath Pashte and Arun Dattraya Kurle had assaulted the victims by means of sword and chopper. 10] On the other hand, I find substance in the submission of Ld 8 ABA1364/2017 Order below Exh.1. APP Sachin Kulkarni that when the charge is under Section 149 IPC, the presence of the accused as part of unlawful assembly is sufficient for involvement of the accused, even if, no overt act is imputed to them. It may be stated here that mere presence of the accused as part of unlawful assembly is sufficient for arraigning the accused in the crime. 11] No doubt where there are party factions, there is a tendency to include the innocent with the guilty and it is extremely difficult for the court to guard against such a danger. The only real safeguard against the risk of condemning the innocent with the guilty lies in insisting for acceptable evidence which in some measure implicates such accused and satisfies the conscience of the court. But that cannot be done at this stage of deciding bail application. Even at the stage of deciding bail application, the evidence cannot be assessed on the crucible of truth or falsehood. 12] No doubt to fasten vicarious responsibility on any member of an unlawful assembly the prosecution must prove that the act constituting an offence was done in prosecution of the common object of that assembly or the act done is such as the members of that assembly knew to be likely to be committed in prosecution of the common object of that assembly. Under Sec. 149 of IPC, every member of an unlawful assembly renders himself liable for the criminal act or acts of any other member or members of that assembly provided the same is/are done in prosecution of the common object or is/are such as every member of that assembly knew to be likely to be committed. 13] For these above quoted reasons, in the present crime, as the 9 ABA1364/2017 Order below Exh.1. applicants/accused were members of the unlawful assembly their arrest seems to be inevitable part of the process of investigation. No doubt Ld. Advocate Chavan for the accused has stated earlier had urge about the innocence and false implication of the accused in the crime. But, the legality of the proposed arrest cannot be gone into in an application under Section 438 of the Code. 14] The role of the investigator is well­defined and the jurisdictional scope of interference by the Court in the process of investigation is limited. In considering the question of bail of an accused in a non­bailable offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life, it is necessary for the court to consider whether the evidence discloses a prima facie case to warrant detention of the accused for the purpose of investigation and when it is satisfied that the accused is not implicated in the crime to just humiliate him then the Court ordinarily will not interfere with the investigation of a crime or with the arrest of accused in a cognizable offence which are serious alike offence under Sec. 307 & 326 of IPC. 15] That being settled position of law an order restraining arrest of the applicants/accused, if is passed while dealing with an application under Section 438 of the Code will amount to interference in the investigation, which cannot, at any rate, be done considering the seriousness of allegation. Particularly, when from FIR it clearly appears that for effective and proper investigation of crime custodial interrogation is quite necessary. 10 ABA1364/2017 Order below Exh.1. 16] One of the most important reason to refuse anticipatory bail to the accused is that, the anticipatory bail is to be granted in exceptional circumstances and not as routine matters but only for the valid reasons. In facts and circumstances of the present case discussed hereinabove and upon considering the anticipatory bail application of the applicants/accused in proper perspective, I do not find that it would be justifiable to enlarge the accused on anticipatory bail. 17] In the present case the allegation against the applicants/accused is that they were members of unalwful assembly armed with deadly weapons and in prosecution of common object of the aforesaid unlawful assembly they had attempted to commit murder and further voluntarily caused grievous hurt to the witnesses. And as the investigating officer and the Ld. APP have opposed the application for anticipatory bail and as I am not satisfied that there are reasonable grounds for believing that the accusation against the applicants/accused have not been made with object of injuring or humiliating them by having them so arrested, I am prevented, by law, from granting them anticipatory bail. 18] For the reasons stated here­in­above, I am of the opinion that it is not a fit case to grant the anticipatory bail to the applicants/accused by exercising powers U/Sec. 438 of Cr.P.C. which are to be utilized only in exceptional cases. Hence, the application of the applicant/accused deserves to be rejected. 19] Before concluding this order, it may be stated here that the 11 ABA1364/2017 Order below Exh.1. applicant/accused was granted ad­interim anticipatory bail as the investigating officer was absent when the bail application was taken up for hearing on the last date. Therefore, that order deserves to be vacated. In the result, the following order is made : :ORDER: 1) The application Exh.1 for anticipatory bail of the applicant/ accused in C.R.No.I­102/2017 registered with Murbad Police Station for offence punishable under Secs. 307, 329, 326, 324, 452, 323, 143, 148, 149 , 504, 506, 427, of I.P.C. is hereby rejected. 2) The order dated 18/8/2017 granting ad­interim anticipatory bail stands vacated. 3) Inform to the concerned Police Station, accordingly. Kalyan. (D.S.Ghumare) Date : 22/8/2017 Addl. Sessions Judge , Kalyan.

Versus Kishor Mohan Zende, Age­121Years, Occupation­Service, R/at­ Shirish Patil Chawl, R.No. 3, Devichowk, Dombivali (W), Tal. Kalyan. District Thane. .. Accused –­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ For the offences punishable under Sections 376 of Indian Penal Code and under Sections 4 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. –­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ Ld. APP Shri S.R. Kulkarni for the State. Ld.Adv. Shri Milind Desai for the accused. –­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ . 2 Spl Case No.167/2014 (Judgment) (CNR NO.MHTH06­003131­2014). : JUDGMENT : (Delivered on 9th day of October 2018). 1] Accused is prosecuted for the offence punishable under Section 376 of Indian Penal Code and under Sections 4 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] Case of prosecution in brief is that informant is the uncle of the victim girl. The victim girl is minor aged about 16 years old and her name is kept secret. The victim girl was sent to her step sister's house in order to look after the children of her step sister and that her step sister since five years has been residing at Dombivali. On 19.04.2014 while informant was at his village victim girl's step sister by making phone call informed him that the victim girl left the house at 11.00 p.m. and she came back to the house at 2.00 a.m. They made enquiry and it was disclosed from the victim girl that on 18.04.2014 at about 11.00 p.m accused called the victim girl near pan stall as there was love affair in between accused and the victim girl and that she along with accused wandered there and that accused asked her whether she would marry with him? On that she replied she would give answer after asking her parents. Thereafter for some time they were wandering. Thereafter accused took her in the shade of rickshaws and at that time their physical relation took place. Thereafter they went to their respective houses. On the report of informant aforesaid crime is registered. 3 Spl Case No.167/2014 (Judgment) (CNR NO.MHTH06­003131­2014). 4] Police recorded the statement of victim girl and victim girl produced her Kurta, Salwar, Odani and slack and police seized the same under panchnama. Police arrested accused. Accused produced T.Shirt, half Barmuda and underwear and it was seized under panchnama. Police conducted panchnama of place of incident. Medical papers of the examination of accused and victim girl were obtained. Police obtained leaving certificate of victim girl wherein it is mentioned her birth date as 24.04.1997. Police recorded the statement of the witnesses. After completion of investigation charge­sheet was filed. 5] Charge against accused at Exh.6 under Section 376 of Indian Penal Code and under Sections 4 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 was framed against accused. Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 6] After recording evidence and hearing both the sides, following points arise for my determination and I have noted my findings against each of them for the reason to follow:­ Sr. No. Points Findings 1 Whether it is proved by ..Not proved. prosecution that accused committed rape on informant's minor niece (i.e. the victim girl)? 2 Whether it is proved by ..Not proved. prosecution that accused 4 Spl Case No.167/2014 (Judgment) (CNR NO.MHTH06­003131­2014). committed penetrative sexual assault on the informant's minor niece (i.e. the victim girl)? 3 What offences, if any are proved No offence is against accused ? proved against accused. : REASONS : As to Point Nos.1 and 2 :­ 7] Perusal of the evidence of the victim girl (P.W.1) shows that at the time of incident she was residing in her sister's house at Dombivali. She was having love affair with the accused while she was residing at her sister's house at Dombivali. Accused had given one mobile phone to her. She further deposed that she does not know as to what incident occurred. She is cross examined at length by Ld. APP. In her cross examination she deposed that her educational qualification is up to 12 th Std. She has denied the contents of her statement to be correct. Under these circumstances, there is no evidence to support the prosecution case. Accordingly, my answer to point nos. 01 and 02 as not proved and my answer to point no. 03 is that no offence is proved against accused. Consequently, accused is entitled for acquittal. Hence, I pass following order:­ : ORDER : i. Accused Kishor Mohan Zende is hereby acquitted of the offence punishable under 5 Spl Case No.167/2014 (Judgment) (CNR NO.MHTH06­003131­2014). Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code and under Sections 4 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. ii. Muddemal Property i.e. T.Shirt, half Barmuda , underwear, Kurta, Salwar, Odani and Slack sized in this case being worthless be destroyed after the appeal period is over, if notice of appeal is not received during such period; and if appeal is filed then subject to the decision of the Hon'ble Appellate Court. …..1….. Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Anticipatory Bail Application No.1251/16 Mahendra Naagardas Saapra & 1 ….. Applicants Vs. State of Maharashtra, (Through Dombivali Police Station) ….. Opponent 1/­ This is an application for anticipatory bail under section 438 of Cr.P.C. in C.R.No. I­203/2016 of Dombivali Police Station for the offence punishable under sections 354, 504, 506 r/w. 34 of Indian Penal Code and under section 8 of POCSO Act, 2012. 2/­ The applicants have contended that they are falsely implicated in this case and false complaint is lodged after delay of four hours. The custodial interrogation of the applicants is not necessary. The daughter of the applicant no.1 had already filed complaint against the husband of the informant and to give counter­blast to same, the present false FIR is lodged against the applicants. The applicants lastly prayed for allowing their application. 3/­ The Investigation Officer has resisted the application by filing his Say at Exh.7 wherein it is contended that, there will be problem in the society as well as in the building in which the applicants and the victim girls are residing, if, the applicants are granted anticipatory bail. The Investigation Officer lastly prayed for rejecting the application. 4/­ Heard Ld. Advocate G.N. Patil for applicants/accused and Ld. APP Ms. R.W. Pande for the State. …..2….. 5/­ After considering the rival submissions, now it is to be seen as to whether the custodial interrogation of the applicants is necessary or what. At the out set, I would like to state that the applicant no.1 is 59 years old and the applicant no.2 is 50 years old. Both the applicants are real brothers. They are residing in the same building in which the informant is residing and the applicants are the owners of the said building. From the FIR it reveals that, the incident has taken place when one labour had gone on the terrace to do the work of mobile tower. As per informant, when her husband asked him that labour told him that he has asked to do the work of the mobile tower by Mahendra Saapra and Narendra Saapra i.e. present applicants. The further allegation is that the applicants abused the informant, her husband and daughters. In the FIR the informant has alleged that it is say of her daughters that the applicants pressed their breasts. As stated earlier, the applicants are 59 and 50 years old respectively and the victim girls are 16 and 12 years respectively. It is pertinent to note that, on the same day the daughter of applicant no.1 has also lodged complaint against the husband of the informant on which the crime is registered under sections 509, 323, 504, 506 r/w.34 of IPC. Thus, there are counter cases against each other in which the allegations against each other are pertaining to disturbing the modesty. It is pertinent to note that the Say of the Investigation Officer no where makes out any of the ground for custodial interrogation of the applicants. Mere raising the contention of law and order problem, threatening the informant and witnesses and again doing similar act by getting annoyed cannot be termed as grounds for custodial interrogation. Thus, considering the nature of allegations and the circumstances in which the alleged incident has taken place, I am of the considered opinion that the custodial interrogation of the applicants is not justifiable one. The …..3….. applicants are entitled to pre­arrest bail with certain conditions. Accordingly, I pass following order : ORDER 1] The application is hereby allowed. 2] In the event of arrest of applicants/accused Shri Mahendra Naagardas Saapra and Shri Narendra alias Naresh Naagardas Saapra in C.R.No.I­203/2016 of Dombivali Police Station for the offence punishable under sections 354, 504, 506 r/w.34 of IPC and under section 8 of the POCSO Act, 2012, they be released on executing their P.R. Bonds of Rs.15,000/­ (Rupees Fifteen Thousand Only) with one solvent surety each in the like amount. 3] The applicants shall mark their presence in Dombivali Police Station on every Wednesday from 11.00 a.m. to 1.00 p.m. till filing of the charge­sheet and to co­operate police machinery in investigation. 4] Inform concerned Police Station accordingly. Kalyan. (S.B. Gaidhani) 10/10/2016 Addl. Sessions Judge, Kalyan.

So after informant informed the 3 Spl. Case No.134/2016 (Judgment) said fact to her mother­in­law and the informant's mother­in­law came to the house of informant on 10/06/2016 and after seeing the condition of victim girl, they decided to do the medical treatment of the victim girl. They informed this fact to the father of the victim girl. So the father of the victim girl took her to his house without taking her to the hospital. Hospital, Mumbai on 15/06/2016. Thereafter, she did not say anything as at that time she was under the influence of medicine and she remained silent. On the report of informant Crime punishable under Sections 376(2)(f) and (i) of the Indian Penal Code & under Sections 4 & 6 of the POCSO Act was registered by 4 Spl. Case No.134/2016 (Judgment) Dombivli Police station vide C.R.No.I­ 139/2016. 3] During the medical examination of the victim girl, doctor came to know from the victim girl that her father had sexually assaulted her many time alongwith some boys in the locality. Statement of the victim girl was recorded by the police wherein she stated that her father removed her clothes and did dirty work with her and she started suffering from bleeding and her father touched the place of vagina and thereafter she started feeling pain in stomach and that her father removed her blood stained clothes and washed it. She further stated that Sushil and Das teased her . She further stated before police that Sushil and Das resides as neighbour to her & she used to go for doing the work of washing clothes in their house on the monthly salary of Rs.3000/­. Sushil asked her as to whether she would marry with him and that she and Sushil chitchats with each other. When she informed this fact to her mother in the evening time, her mother scolded Sushil. She further stated before police that Sushil and Das did not do anything to her and that she left the job for two months before. So considering the statement of victim girl informant gave her further statement stating therein that she has no complaint against Sushil and Das and that she has complaint against accused, the father of the victim girl. So police arrested the accused under arrest panchanama. Police seized informant's chudidar, top, payjama and pantie under panchnama in presence of panchas. Police also did panchnama of the place of incident and from the place of incident police seized one shirt, one full pant, one Bermuda in the presence of panchas. Police recorded 5 Spl. Case No.134/2016 (Judgment) statement of witnesses. Police obtained the school leaving certificate(Exh.9) of the victim girl wherein the date of birth of victim girl is mentioned as 30/06/2003. After completion of investigation charge­sheet was filed against present accused. Statement of the victim girl was also recorded u/sec.164 of Cr.P.C. before the Ld. J.M.F.C. Court No.6 Kalyan. 4] Charge at Exh.6 under Sections 376(2)(f) & (i) of the Indian Penal Code & under Sections 4 & 6 of the POCSO Act was framed against accused. Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 5] After recording evidence and hearing both the sides, following points arise for my determination and I have noted my findings against each of them for the reason to follow: Points Findings 1. Whether it is proved by the prosecution that accused being relative of the victim girl committed rape on the minor victim girl? .. Not proved. 2. Whether it is proved by prosecution that accused committed rape on the victim girl who was at that time .. Not proved. under 16 years of age ? 3. Whether it is proved by prosecution that accused committed penetrative 6 Spl. Case No.134/2016 (Judgment) sexual assault on the victim girl? .. Not proved. 4. Whether it is proved by the prosecution that accused being the relative of the victim girl committed penetrative sexual assault on the victim girl? .. Not proved. 5. What offences, if any are proved .. No offence is proved against against accused ? accused. : REASONS : As to Point Nos.1 to 5 :­ 6] It has come in the evidence of informant P.W.2 that she knows accused as the accused is the elder brother of her husband. Accused is having two daughters and the victim girl is daughter of accused. Victim girl is 16 years old. Mother of the victim girl left the house of her husband on 04/06/2016. Thereafter on 09/06/2016 accused left the victim girl in her house. At that time victim girl was sick and she was feeling headache and throat­ache and therefore, they took her to Shastri Nagar Hospital at Dombivli. Thereafter, the victim girl was taken to Shivaji hospital, Kalwa, and thereafter to K.E.M. hospital, Mumbai. It has come in her evidence that victim girl did not tell anything about her father i.e. accused and that victim girl did not tell before them and doctor as to who kept physical relation with her. Informant has identified the signature on complaint but she 7 Spl. Case No.134/2016 (Judgment) deposed that she did not know about its contents. She is cross­ examined by the Ld. APP but nothing is brought on record to show that she has supported the prosecution case. She has denied the suggestion that since compromise took place with accused, she deposes falsely. It can be said that informant has not supported the prosecution case. 7] Evidence of the victim girl P.W.1 shows that in June 2016 her mother left the house and went away. In that respect complaint was lodged to police station as her mother was not found. Now she resides with her uncle Sandesh Tambe and his wife. Previously she used to reside with her mother and father in Tukaram Nagar, Balaram Smruti chawl, Dombivli. Her father had left her in the house of her uncle Sandesh Tambe. Her evidence further shows that since she was not feeling well, her uncle Sandesh Tambe and his wife took her to Shastri Nagar, hospital at Dombivli. Thereafter, she was taken to Shivaji Hospital Kalwa and thereafter, to K.E.M. Hospital, Mumbai. She told doctor that she was not feeling well as she was feeling headache and throat­ache. She told doctor and police that her clothes which became dirty were changed by her father. Her evidence shows that it has not happened that her father did sexual intercourse with her. She had admitted that police enquired with her. She has also admitted that on 04/07/2016 she gave her statement u/sec. 164 of Cr.P.C. before the ld. JMFC. When portion mark ''A” of her statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. was read over to her she has denied its contents to be true. She is cross­examined by ld APP . In her cross examination she has deposed that she has 8 Spl. Case No.134/2016 (Judgment) produced the clothes before police. She has further admitted that doctor medically examined her in K.E.M. hospital, at Mumbai. But she has denied portion mark ''A” of her statement to be true. Nothing is brought on record to show that she has supported the prosecution case. Under the circumstances, victim girl has not supported the prosecution case. Prosecution has failed to prove its case. Accordingly, my answer to point Nos.1 to 4 is not proved and my answer to point no.5 is that no offence is proved against accused. Consequently, accused are entitled for acquittal. Hence, I pass following order:­ : ORDER : i. Accused Deepak Hiru Tambe is hereby acquitted of the offences punishable under Sections 376 (2)(f) & (i) of the Indian Penal Code & under Sections 4 & 6 of the POCSO Act. ii. Accused be released forthwith if not required in any other case. iii Accused is directed to execute P.B. and S.B. of Rs.15,000/­ under Section 437­A of Cr.P.C. to appear before the Hon'ble Higher Courts or Appellate Courts as and when the Hon'ble Higher Courts or Appellate Courts issue notices in respect of any appeal or petition filed against this Judgment and such bail bonds shall be in force for six months. 9 Spl. Case No.134/2016 (Judgment) iv. Muddemal property i.e. one shirt, one pant, one Bermuda, one chudidar top, one pyjama, one pantie seized in this case being worthless be destroyed after the appeal period is over, if notice of appeal is not received during such period and if notice of appeal is received then subject to the decision of the Hon'ble Appellate Court. Both these boys i.e. Gurunath and Yuvraj are harassing the victim girl by making teasing comments and threatening her. If the applicant is released on bail he may pressurise the girl and the prosecution witnesses. Hence prayed for rejection. 5] Heard both the sides and gone through the investigation papers. It reveals from the record that co­accused Yuvraj Sabale is already released on bail. He also contended that appellant has sought for his released on bail for cash security and so he has not been released on bail. He contended that if the accused would be released on bail he would again commit similar offence. The ld. A.P.P.sought for dismissal of the Appeal. ­3­ 4] The following points arise for determination and my findings against each for the reasons stated below are as under : POINTS FINDINGS 1 Whether the impugned orders passed by Ld.Juvenile Justice Board,Bhiwandi are just, legal and proper ? … No. 2 Whether the appellant is entitled for bail ? …. Yes. 3 What order ? …. The accused is ordered to be released on bail. :REASONS: 5] The J.J.B. has refused bail as the juvenile in conflict with law is involved in three cases of thefts of motorcycles. The Ld.J.J.B. seems to have reached to the conclusion that the accused would commit more similar crimes in future and would not reform of he is released from remand home, as he may come in contact with criminals. It is also opined by Ld.J.J.B. that release of the juvenile is against his best interest. 6] The reasons put forth by the Ld.J.J.B. for rejecting the bail of Juvenile are quite proper and do deserve acceptance. But that cannot be an absolute ground for refusing bail to the Juvenile in conflict with law. Some stringent conditions could be imposed on the applicant in the interest of Juvenile in conflict with law so that he does not indulge in similar criminal activities in ­4­ future. Apart from that the present order can be made conditional so that he does with direction to the guardians of the juvenile to take his care to and any circumstances not to allow him in coming in contact with criminals and also imposition of condition that his bail would be cancelled, immediately if he commits any other offence. 7] For these reasons it would be in the interest of justice to allow the appeal and release the juvenile on bail with stringent conditions. In the result the following order is made : :ORDER: 1) The appeal is allowed 2) The order of the Ld.JJB., is set aside. 3) The Juvenile in conflict with law is ordered to be released on furnishing three distinct P.B.& S.B. in sum of Rs.15,000/­ in each of the three different cases. 4) The bail of the Juvenile in conflict with law is conditional and it would stand cancelled immediately upon his commission of any other crime in future. 5) Inform accordingly to the Ld.Juvenile Justice Board, Bhiwandi. Kalyan. (D.S.Ghumare) Dt.27/10/2016 Addl.Sessions Judge,Kalyan.
