1 Atro. Special Case No. 136/2015 [Judg.] Presented on : 07/10/2015 Registered on : 07/10/2015 Decided on : 15/05/2017 Duration : 01­Y 07­M 8­D Exh. No.20 IN THE COURT OF ADDITIONAL SESSIONS JUDGE, KALYAN [Presided Over by S.P. Gogarkar] ATRO.SPECIAL CASE NO.136 OF 2015 State of Maharashtra (Through Badlapur (W) P.Stn.), ( C.R. No. I­169/2014) ...Complainant Versus Omkar Sharad Deodhar, Age 31, Occ. Self employed, R/o. Gajanan Palace, Room No.5, Sarvoday Nagar, Badlapur (W). ...Accused Offence punishable under secs. 354(D)(1) & 509 of the Indian Penal Code and u/s. 11 & 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act,2012 ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ Mrs.Bhamare­Patil, Ld. APP for the State Shri A.R. Shaikh, Ld. Adv. for the Accused ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ ­­ 2 Atro. Special Case No. 136/2015 [Judg.] JUDGMENT ( Delivered on this 15th day of May, 2017 ) 1] Accused Omkar Sharad Deodhar, R/o. Kachoregaon, Dombivali (E) stands prosecuted for the alleged commission of outraging the modesty of victim girl by chasing her on the school way and by making gestures and by sounding as “Shook, Shook”. He is also charge­sheeted for insulting the modesty of minor girl uttering obscene words repeatedly as “Shook, Shook” and for committing sexual gestures towards her. Hence, PSO Badlapur (W) Police Station registered this offence vide Cr. No.I­169/14 on the report of the complainant­father of the victim. 2] The story of the prosecution in short is that, the complainant­family resides in the area of Sarodaya Nagar, Badlapur and running grocery shop under the name and style as “Poonam Grocery Shop”. The complainant has two daughters named as Poonam and Pooja. The incidence took place during the month of October,2014. At that time, victim Pooja was studying in 8th standard and Poonam was in 7 th standard. Both the sisters used to go to Hindi High School, Badlapur at 7 a.m. and used to come back at 12.30 to 1 p.m. 3] The accused Omkar Deodhar used to chase victim Pooja on her school way insisting her to accept his gifts and presentation articles. On denial, he used to force for it through his friend Monu. The victim narrated the conduct of 3 Atro. Special Case No. 136/2015 [Judg.] the accused and her parents tried to give understandings to the accused prior to the incidence. Accused has not paid any heed to the request of the victim's parents. On the contrary, he quarreled with them. 4] On 21.11.2014, at about 7 a.m., when victim­girl with her younger sister Poonam was proceeding towards school, accused made some gestures saying as “Shook, Shook”. The victim noticed the activities of the accused but ignored it, at that time, as she was already late to go to the school. On coming back from the school, she narrated the incidence to her father and then matter was reported to the Badlapur Police on the same day. 5] PSO Badlapur (W) Police Station registered this offence vide Crime No.I­169/14, on the report of complainant­father and further investigation was carried out by API Swati Petkar. The Investigating Officer visited the house of the complainant and recorded the statements of corresponding witnesses including the victim girl and her younger sister. The I.O. has collected bonafide certificates of the victim girl from her school showing her minor age. The accused was arrested and on completion of investigation charge­sheet came to be filed. 6] The accused appeared before the Court in response to the summons. I have framed charge vide Exh.3. It was read over and explained to him in vernacular. Accused 4 Atro. Special Case No. 136/2015 [Judg.] pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. The prosecution has examined victim girl, her parents and the younger sister alongwith I.O. I have recorded the statement of the accused u/s. 313 of Cr.P.C. He has examined himself on oath to substantiate his defence of false implication. 7] Considering the evidence on record and defence of the accused, following points arose for my determination and my findings thereon are as under for the reasons given below :­ POINTS FINDINGS 1] Does prosecution prove that the accused in September,2014 and on 21.11.2014, at 7 a.m., at Sarvoday Nagar, Omprakash Building Road, Badlapur (W), followed the victim­minor girl, aged 15 years and calling her by sounding as “Shook, Shook” and Negative. made gesture by hands and eyes, with intent to outrage her modesty and thereby committed an offence punishable u/s. 354(D)(1) of IPC ? 2] Does prosecution prove that, during the same date, place and time accused intending to insult the modesty of victim minor girl, aged 15 years, uttered the words repeatedly “Shook, Shook” intending that the same shall be Negative. heard by the victim and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 509 of IPC ? 5 Atro. Special Case No. 136/2015 [Judg.] POINTS FINDINGS 3] Does prosecution prove that during the above date, time and place accused committed sexual gesture towards the victim­minor girl, aged 15 years and thereby Negative. committed an offence punishable u/s. 11 & 12 of POCSO Act,2012? 4] What order? Accused is acquitted. : REASONS : POINT NOS.1 TO 3 :­ 8] This prosecution is launched by the complainant­ father of the victim who was minor in age at the time of alleged commission of offence. It reveals from the FIR that she was taking education in Hindi High School at Badlapur and she used to attend her school with her siblings daily at 7 a.m. and used to come back at 12.30 noon. The way towards her school was passing from in front of her grocery shop. To substantiate this factual aspects, and the spot of incidence, it was expected that I.O. should produce the document of spot panchanama to assert the spot of incidence, but surprisingly no such effort was made by the I.O. Therefore, in absence of spot panchanama, it is difficult to held as to where alleged incidence occurred on 21.11.2014. 9] The another facet of this case is that the victim­ girl and her relative witnesses i.e. parents and younger sisters have deposed oral evidence regarding occurrence of incidence 6 Atro. Special Case No. 136/2015 [Judg.] and earlier incidences of alleged activities of the accused. It is pertinent to note that all the four family witnesses including complainant have deposed stereotyped evidence stating therein that on 21.11.2014 when victim's sisters were proceeding towards their school, accused made some gestures palping his hands and eyes and by uttering words as “Shook, Shook”. Admittedly, the evidence of parents is hearsay evidence. He tried to demonstrate that previously he has seen the obscene activities of the accused with his daughter. But surprisingly no police complaints or any report came to be filed. It is tried to explain that they attempted to give understandings to the accused but no specific incidence with particular date or period is mentioned in their evidence. The improvement made by the complainant­father during his evidence is rightly brought on record during his cross­ examination. 10] The Ld. Counsel Mr. Shaikh tried to explain improbability of the incidence submitting that in the month of November i.e. during Winter period, sun­rise is late. The incidence took place at early morning at 7 a.m. The witnesses have not stated specifically from what distance accused made alleged gestures or uttered words “Shook, Shook”. Another fold of defence is of cross terms between the families. It is tried to demonstrate that there was quarrel between complainant­family and accused as accused­family stopped purchasing grocery articles from the complainant's shop. Moreover, accused was assisting newly established shop in 7 Atro. Special Case No. 136/2015 [Judg.] front of their house. To get rid of their grudge and to extract some monetary gain, from the service benefits of recently retired mother of the accused, this false implication is made with after thought view. 11] On the other hand, the ld. APP Smt. Bhamare­ Patil submitted that the complainant­father would not file false case at the stake of the character of his teen age daughter. On this background, the evidence of prosecution is liable to be scrutinized. The accused adduced his evidence on oath supported with document to prove the enmity between the families on point of purchasing grocery articles. Moreover, it is his case that on the day of incidence, there was quarrel between complainant­father and the accused, on the same grocery shop reason. He was not aware as to whether any police report was made against him. He went to Nepal trip with his family and after his arrival he was abruptly arrested in this false prosecution. This evidence of the accused on oath is not shattered during cross­examination except some denied suggestions. 12] It is pertinent to note that the evidence on point of alleged outraging of modesty is not consistent. At one place, victim stated that he uttered words “Shook, Shook”, but during statement u/s. 164 of Cr.P.C., she stated that accused made gestures by giving whistles and palping his eyes. The alleged activities stated by the victim in two different statements are altogether different in nature. 8 Atro. Special Case No. 136/2015 [Judg.] Moreover, the distance of alleged activities is nowhere mentioned. It is admitted position that the accused is having defective eye sight. It is even visible by naked eyes. In such circumstances, the victim­girl might have felt otherwise in confusion. It is pertinent to note that the younger sister Poonam has tried to support the deposition of complainant but she gave inconsistent estimation of alleged occurrence. The I.O. (P.W.5 API Swati Petkar) admitted in her cross­ examination that she has not followed the required procedure under POCSO while recording the statement of child witness. It is pertinent to note that the accused is facing charge of Secs. 11 and 12 of the POCSO and therefore the presumption envisages in Section 29 of the said Act is not applicable to the present case. 13] The Ld. Counsel Mr. Shaikh submitted that culpabable mental state of the accused as required u/s. 30 of the POCSO is not proved at all. Moreover, the place of incidence is shown as public road and admittedly public crowd is obvious on such main road even then the expected neighbouring witnesses are not interrogated by I.O. nor produced before the Court to substantiate the story. 14] The crux of the story that ordinarily young daughter of the complainant would not put character at stake to implicate the accused falsely. However, said approach cannot be applied universally because each case has to be determined on the touch stone of the factual matrix thereof. 9 Atro. Special Case No. 136/2015 [Judg.] The reliance is rightly placed on the case of Pandurang Bhagwant v/s. State of Maharasutra decided by Hon'ble Court on 17.12.2004 in Criminal Appeal No.1513/2004. In this case, cross­terms between the families are brought on record through cross­examination of complainant­witnesses. Therefore, possibility of false implication cannot be over looked in absence of cogent and consistent evidence. The evidence adduced on record is too scanty to prove the allegations made in the FIR. The evidence of family­witnesses is inconsistent to each other on point of alleged act of the accused. In such situation, accused cannot be connected with the crime only on the bare words of the FIR. 15] Thus, considering the short evidence of small witnesses and procedural lacuna while conducting the investigation gave adverse effect to prove the charge against the accused. On the other hand, accused succeeded in substantiating his defence by way of his unshattered evidence. Therefore, I have no alternative but to held that the required ingredients are not proved at all. Thus, I have no hesitation to answer point Nos.1 to 3 in the negative. POINT NO. 4 :­ 13] As I held above, prosecution failed to prove necessary ingredients to prove the guilt of accused. Hence, he is liable to be acquitted giving benefit of inadequate evidence to prove the charges. In the result, I answer point No.4 accordingly and proceed to pass following order :­ 10 Atro. Special Case No. 136/2015 [Judg.] ORDER 1] Accused Omkar Sharad Deodhar, Age : 31 years, R/at : Badlapur (W) is hereby acquitted under Section 235(1) of Cr.P.C. of the offences punishable under 354(D)(1) & 509 of the Indian Penal Code and u/s.11 & 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act,2012. 2] Bail bond of accused stands cancelled. 3] The accused is directed to furnish fresh P.B. & S.B. of Rs.15,000/­. In compliance with the provisions of section 437(A) of Cr.P.C. to abide himself to appear before Appellate Court in case of appeal is preferred by the prosecution. Judgment pronounced in open Court. Kalyan Dt : 15/05/2017 [ S.P. Gogarkar ] Dist. Judge­4 & Addl. Sessions Judge, Kalyan

ORDER BELOW EXH.5 IN SPECIAL CASE NO.149/2016. (Arising out of C.R.No.I­329/2016 of Manpada Police Station). 1] By this application it is prayed on behalf of applicant viz. Shamu Ramesh Yadav @ Anand that he may be sent to Juvenile justice Board on the ground that at the time of alleged incident he was juvenile and that consequently he is juvenile in conflict with law. 2] By filing say learned APP has strongly opposed this application and prayed for rejection of this application. I have heard both the sides. 3] It is submitted on behalf of Shamu Ramesh Yadav @ Anand that his date of birth as per the school leaving certificate is 27.02.1999 and that the alleged incident took place for about six months prior to 23.06.2016 and in this way on the date of alleged incident Shamu Ramesh Yadav @ Anand was juvenile in conflict with law and his case should be sent to the Juvenile Justice Board. 4] However learned APP has strongly opposed this application. She has submitted that on the date of incident applicant was more than 16 years old and therefore his case should be tried as a major accused before this Court. 5] Following point arises for my determination and I have noted my finding against it for the reasons to follow:­ 2 Spl.Case No.149/2016 (Or.Exh.5) POINT FINDING 1] Whether the case of Shamu Ramesh Yadav @ Anand is required to be sent before the Juvenile Justice Board on the ground that at the time of alleged incident he was juvenile ? .. In the affirmative. REASONS AS TO POINT NO.1:­ 6] Learned advocate of the Shamu Ramesh Yadav @ Anand has produced the school leaving certificate and mark­sheet of Shamu Ramesh Yadav @ Anand wherein his date of birth is mentioned as 27.02.1999. 7] In order to verify the contents of the same this Court issued letter to the Principal of the school requesting him to say about the authenticity about the school leaving certificate and mark­ sheet of Shamu Ramesh Yadav @ Anand. In pursuance of that letter Principal of Subhadra Laghu Madhyamik Vidyalaya Raipur via Khairighat Mahasi, Bahraich sent letter to this Court stating therein that Shamu Ramesh Yadav @ Anand studied in his school and as per his school record date of birth of Shamu Ramesh Yadav @ Anand is 27.02.1999. Under the circumferences, it can be said that prima facie the date of birth of Shamu Ramesh Yadav @ Anand is 27.02.1999. The alleged incident i.e. committing forcibly sexual intercourse with victim 3 Spl.Case No.149/2016 (Or.Exh.5) girl by Shamu Ramesh Yadav @ Anand according to prosecution case took place about 5 to 6 months prior to lodging of this FIR and this FIR is lodged on 23.06.2016. So, it can be presumed that on or about 23.12.2015 the alleged incident might have taken place and on the date of alleged incident i.e. on 23.12.2015 his age was 16 years 9 months 26 days. So, he was below 18 years of age on the date of incident and it can be said he is juvenile in conflict with law and in view of the Section 23 of the Juvenile Justice Law his case cannot be tried before this Court. Hence it is required to be sent before the Juvenile Justice Board. Under the circumstances application deserves to be allowed. My answer to point No.1 is in the affirmative. Hence, I pass following order :­ ORDER 1] Application is allowed. 2] Shamu Ramesh Yadav @ Anand is juvenile in conflict with law and his case is required to be sent before the Juvenile Justice Board. 3] I.O. is hereby directed to produce Shamu Ramesh Yadav @ Anand, juvenile in conflict with law before the Juvenile Justice Board and his entire charge­sheet be sent to the Juvenile Justice Board for enquiry according to law. 4] Inform I.O. and Jailor for information and necessary action. 5] Copy of this order be kept as a record of this case. Kalyan. (A.A.A.Shaikh) Dt.:­ 08.09.2017. Additional Sessions Judge, Kalyan.

…..1….. Order below Ex.1 in Criminal Anticipatory Bail Application No.1372/2016 Shri Deepak Pandurang Lokhande ….. Applicant Vs. State of Maharashtra, (Through Khadakpada Police Station) ….. Opponent 1/­ This is an application for anticipatory bail under section 438 of Cr.P.C. in C.R.No.I­335/2016 of Khadakpada Police Station for the offence punishable under sections 363, 376, 327 r/w.34 of IPC and under sections 4, 8, 12 of the POCSO Act, 2012. 2/­ The applicant has contended that he is innocent and false charges are levelled against him. He has not made any sexual assault on the victim and therefore, the offence punishable under section 376 of IPC is not applicable to him. His name is not mentioned in the FIR. He is political person in the locality and because of said personal enmity he is falsely implicated in this case. The FIR is fabricated one. He is ready and willing to co­operate the investigating agency. He is permanent resident of Village Umbarde, Tal. Kalyan and ready to abide by any terms and conditions. His custodial interrogation is not necessary. He lastly prayed for allowing his application. 3/­ The Investigation Officer has resisted the application by filing his say at Exhs.5 and 6 respectively wherein it is contended that, this applicant has committed serious offence along with the co­accused. This applicant has tried to destroy the evidence by using his political and economic status. The involvement of this applicant is revealed …..2….. from the statement of the victim girl. The custodial interrogation of the applicant is necessary to know his role and to know what was his intention behind said act. The Investigation Officer lastly prayed for rejecting the application. 4/­ Heard Ld. Advocate Shri S.P. Sonavane and Ld. A.P.P. Ms. R.W. Pande for the State. 5/­ After considering the rival submissions, now it is to be seen as to whether the applicant is entitled to pre­arrest bail. While deciding the pre­arrest bail the need of custodial interrogation has to be looked into. Furthermore, for deciding the aspect of custodial interrogation the nature of offences and the allegations are also required to be looked into. Here in this case in hand, the victim girl is 15 years old. No doubt, the FIR is lodged by the mother of the victim girl pertaining to kidnapping of her minor daughter against unknown person, but, the statement of the victim girl which is produced for my perusal by the Investigation Officer clearly makes out involvement of the present applicant along with the co­accused in the alleged incident of kidnapping and rape on the victim girl. Her statement makes out that, this applicant and co­accused had taken her when she had left her house in a rage of anger. It further reveals that the victim girl was addressing this applicant as uncle and the co­accused as maternal uncle (mama). Taking disadvantage of the circumstances in which the victim girl had left her house, they had taken her to one dhaba where both of them i.e. present applicant and the co­accused consumed alcohol and gave some cold­drink to the victim girl, because of which she started feeling giddiness. Her statement also makes out that she was taken to Mayur Lodge where also she was given one cold­drink and at that time …..3….. also after drinking said cold­drink she felt giddiness. Thereafter, what happened with her could not be recollected by her. Thus, the allegations are certainly serious allegations. The involvement of the present applicant is clearly revealed from the statement of the victim girl who is 15 years old. Considering the seriousness of the offence, I am of the considered opinion that this is a fit case for custodial interrogation to unearth the truth and also to unearth the role played by this applicant. Thus, the foregoing discussion leads to conclude that the applicant is not entitled to pre­arrest bail. Accordingly, I pass following order : Order 1] Application stands rejected. Kalyan (S.B.Gaidhani) 07/11/2016 Addl. Sessions Judge, Kalyan.

1 Or.Exh.1 in Cri.Ant.Bail 1406/15 Order below Ex.1 in Anticipatory Criminal Bail Application No.1406/2015 Pranay Kumar Chilukoty through his father Mr. Surendra Kumar Chilukoty ….. Applicant Vs. State of Maharashtra, (Through Mahatma Phule Chowk Police Station) ….. Opponent 1/­ This is an application for anticipatory bail filed under section 438 of Cr. P.C. in C.R.No. I­871/2015 of Mahatma Phule Chowk Police Station for the offence punishable under sections 354, 506 of IPC and under sections 8 & 12 of POCSO Act, 2012. 2/­ This application is moved by the father of the juvenile­in­conflict with law contending that the story put­forth in the FIR is not only false but improbable too. There is no need of custodial interrogation and the applicant is ready to co­operate the investigating agency. He lastly prayed for allowing the application. 3/­ The Investigation Officer has resisted the application by filing his Say at Exh.6 wherein it is contended that the juvenile­in­conflict with law, if, enlarged on bail will threaten the victim girl who is five years old. The Investigation Officer lastly prayed for rejecting the application 4/­ Heard Ld. Advocate Smt. Sudha Joshi for applicant/accused and Ld. APP Ms. R.R. Bhoir for the State. 5/­ On the point of maintainability of application for anticipatory 2 Or.Exh.1 in Cri.Ant.Bail 1406/15 bail to juvenile­in­conflict with law, the Ld. Advocate for the applicant has relied upon decision of Hon'ble Rajasthan High Court in case of Tara Chand Vs. State of Rajasthan [LAWS(RAJ)­2007­5­30] wherein Hon'ble Rajasthan High Court has held that ­ “In view with Section 12 of the Juvenile Justice (Care And Protection of Children) Act, 2000 which is having overriding effect, the application for anticipatory bail as per Section 438 of Cr.P.C. is maintainable”. Thus, the anticipatory bail application is maintainable. 6/­ After perusing the contents of the FIR, the allegation against the juvenile­in­conflict with law is that he moved his hand over the chest of the daughter of the informant. Said daughter of the informant is five years old. The applicant is 15 years old and taking education in Standard X. The Say of the Investigation Officer no where makes out any serious ground for rejecting the application. Thus, considering the nature of offences and the age of the applicant who is juvenile­in­conflict with law, I am of the considered opinion that this is a fit case to grant anticipatory bail to him. 1 Spl.Case No.152/2016 Judgment Presented on : 08/11/2016 Registered on : 08/11/2016 Decided on : 14/06/2017 Duration : Y­0. M­7 D­6. IN THE COURT OF ADDL.SESSIONS JUDGE, KALYAN (Presided over by D.S.Ghumare) Session Case No.152/2016 Exh.No. The State of Maharashtra (Through Mumbai Railway Police Station Karjat) .... Prosecution V/s. Fakir @ Sandip Sambhaji Gajbhare Age­ 22 year. R/at: At Post Upari, Tal. Pandharpur Dist. Solapur .... Accused Offence punishable U/Secs. 363, 376 of the I.P.C. and under Section 5 (j) (ii) r.w Sec. 6 of POCSO Act ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ Shri.Sachin Kulkarni Ld.A.P.P.for State. Shri. Rakesh Singh, Ld.Adv.for accused. ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ JUDGMENT (Delivered on 14th day of June , 2017) 1] The accused stands charged for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 376 of the Indian Penal Code, and under Section 5 (j) (ii) r.w Sec. 6 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offence Act. 2] The prosecution’s case is that the prosecutrix PW.1 Laxmi, 2 Spl.Case No.152/2016 Judgment aged 17 years, is the daughter of the informant P.W.2­ Leelabai Ramesh Sawale. The family of informant PW 2 is resided in Krantinagar hutment area, near Railway Station, Karjat, Dist. Raigad. The informant is a hawker. On 2/7/2016 the prosecutrix left her house telling her mother informant PW 2 Leelabai that she is going for her work as a housemaid. But thereafter she did not return to her house even on the next day. Therefore, the informant PW 2 Leelabai enquired with the persons at whose house the prosecutrix is working as a housemaid. But she had not found her daughter prosecutrix. A person by name Virendra who is also a hawker, told to the informant Leelabai that he saw her daughter prosecutrix boarding in Udyan Express. Therefore, the PW 2 informant Laxmibai had lodged the FIR with Karjat Railway Police Station stating that unknown person had enticed away her daughter. Later on the prosecutrix returned to her home on 19/9/2016 and told to the informant PW 2 Leelabai that she had went with the accused on her own accord and she had married with the accused at Pandharpur. She also told that they lived at Manchar as husband and wife and that she is two months pregnant from her relation with the accused. Thereupon the informant PW 2 Leelabai took the prosecutrix and the accused in the police station and gave her supplementary statement. On the basis of the said report crime was registered against the accused Fakir Gajbhare vide C.R.No.I­ 36/2016 for offences punishable U/Secs.363, 376 of I.P.C. and U/Sec.5 (j) (ii) r/w Sec. 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 3] The investigation of the crime was conducted by API Salunkhe. He firstly sent the PW 1 prosecutrix for medical examination 3 Spl.Case No.152/2016 Judgment at Rukhminibai Hospital, Kalyan. The accused Fakir@ Sandip Gajbhare was arrested in connection with the crime on same day. He was also got medically examined from Rukhminibai Hospital, Kalyan. During the course of investigation, the panchanama of the scene of offence Exh.21, seizure panchanama of clothes of accused Fakir Exh.19, seizure panchanama of clothes of PW.1 prosecutrix, Exh.13, were prepared in the presence of panch witnesses. He also sent the clothes of the accused Fakir and prosecutrix to F.S.L. Mumbai for its analysis. The investigation officer API Salunkhe recorded the supplementary statement of the informant P.W.2 Leelabai and statements of other witnesses. He also got recorded the statement of the PW.1 prosecutrix U/Sec.164 of Cr.P.C. In due course, the investigation officer collected the medical examination report of the prosecutrix and the accused Fakir from the medical officer of the Rukhminibai Hospital, Kalyan. He had collected C.A. reports and produced the same on record. He also collected bonafide certificate of PW 1 prosecutrix as a age proof of her minor­ship. Ultimately, after completion of the investigation, the investigation officer submitted final report under section 173 of Cr.P.C against the accused in the Court . 4] My Ld. Predecessor Shri. S. B. Gaidhani has framed the Charge Exh.5 against the accused for the offences punishable under section U/Secs.363, 376 of I.P.C. & U/Sec. 5(j)(ii) r.w Sec. 6 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. The charge was read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. The accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. The defence of the accused is that of total denial and false implication in the crime. 4 Spl.Case No.152/2016 Judgment 5] The following points arise for determination and my findings are given against each thereon for the reasons given thereunder. POINTS FINDINGS 1) Whether the prosecution proves that the No accused on 2/7/2016 at 9.00 a.m. at Kranti Nagar Zopadpatti, Near Karjat Railway Station, kidnapped victim girl Laxmi Sawale, a minor under 17 years of age from lawful guardianship of her mother ? 2) Whether the prosecution proves that the No accused on 6/7/2016, at the farmhouse of Shri. Kulkarni, at Post Shingve, Tal. Ambegaon, Dist. Pune, committed repeated rape on minor victim girl Lami Sawale against her will and without her consent ? 3) Whether the prosecution proves that on No the aforesaid date, time and place , accused committed repeated aggravated penetrative sexual assault on minor victim girl Laxmi Sawale and make the minor victim girl pregnant ? 4) What order ? As per final order. REASONS POINT NOS.1 TO 3 :­ 6] All the points are dealt with simultaneously so as to avoid repetition of the discussion of the evidence which is common for them. 7] To bring home the guilt of the accused, the prosecution has examined in all two witnesses. They are the informant PW.2 Leelabai 5 Spl.Case No.152/2016 Judgment Ramesh Sawale & PW 1 the prosecutrix. The Ld. APP Smt. Pande has filed pursis Exh. 22 stating that prosecution does not want to examine other witnesses. The pursis was moved by the Ld. APP Pande for the State since Ld. Advocate for the accused had admitted the genuineness of the school leaving certificate, medical certificates, panchanamas of the scene of offence & seizure of clothes and other documents. 8] The prosecution has examined P.W.1 prosecutrix who is victim of the crime. She has testified that she know the accused Fakir Sambhaji Gajbhare. On 2/7/2016 accused Fakir took her to Manchar. She further testified that she was having love affair with accused Fakir so she had accompanied him on her own accord. From there she went alongwith the accused to Pandharpur, where they performed marriage. She also testified that after their marriage at Pandharpur, they had kept sexual relation whereupon she became pregnant. Thereafter, she came to Karjat. Her mother had given report with Karjat Police Station. When they came to Karjat, police arrested accused Fakir. Her mother then took her to their house and that thereafter, she delivered a baby. 9] It would be pertinent to note here that PW.1 prosecutrix failed to support the prosecution case, as she denied that the accused Fakir had involved her in false love relationship and kept sexual relations with her and made her pregnant. Thus, the evidence of PW 1 prosecutrix does not support the prosecution case in its material particulars. 10] The prosecution has examined informant P.W.2 Leelabai Ramesh Sawale , who is the mother of prosecutrix. She has testified that 6 Spl.Case No.152/2016 Judgment she know the accused Fakir Sambhaji Gajbhare. On 2/7/2016 accused Fakir took her daughter prosecutrix to Manchar. She lodged report Exh.11 against the accused with Karjat Railway Police Station. 11] She further testified that when her daughter prosecutrix returned, she told her that she had went with the accused on her own accord and that they had married each other at Pandharpur. The informant PW 2 Leelabai deposed that after some days her daughter prosecutrix had telephoned her and at that time she told her that after Ganpati Festival she would come to their house alongwith her lover accused Fakira. 12] The informant PW 2 Leelabai further deposed that on 19/9/2016 her daughter prosecutrix came to her house alongwith the accused Fakira. At that time her daughter prosecutrix told her that she and the accused Fakira were resided at Manchar as husband and wife and she is two months pregnant. She further deposed that she took her daughter prosecutrix and the accused Fakira to Karjat Railway Police Station. There police inquired with both of them and registered the crime. Then her daughter prosecutrix was produced before Child Welfare Committee which gave custody of prosecutrix to her. 13] In such background of the testimony of the prosecution witnesses, it is rather unfortunate for the prosecution that PW.1 prosecutrix and her mother­ the informant PW.2 Leelabai did not support the prosecution case. The Ld.A.P.P. Smt. Pande declared P.W.1­ prosecutrix as a hostile witness and cross­examined her at length. The 7 Spl.Case No.152/2016 Judgment searching cross­examination of this witness by Ld.A.P.P. did not yield any benefit to the prosecution as nothing material was elicited there from incriminating against the accused. Thus, there is no evidence against the accused to substantiate the charge against him of commission of rape upon the P.W.1 prosecutrix under the pretext of marriage, against her will. 14] As nothing incriminating is come in the evidence of the prosecution witnesses, the statement of the accused U/Sec.313 of Cr.P.C. is dispensed with. 15] It would be pertinent to note here that even if the circumstantial evidence, which includes panchanama of the scene of offence Exh.21, genuineness of which is admitted under section 294 of Cr.P.C. and , CA reports Exh. 16 & 20 (colly) is considered, still it would not have yielded any benefit to the prosecution as there is no incriminating substantiative evidence against the accused. 16] Even assuming that the prosecutrix is marginally below 18 years of age, as contended by Ld APP Smt. Pande for the State, still the accused would not be guilty for an offence punishable under section 366 I.P.C. To make out an offence of kidnapping, it has to be established that a girl below 18 years of age was kidnapped or taken out from the lawful guardianship. 17] Section 361 I.P.C. provides that in order to constitute an offence of kidnapping, there should be taking away or enticement. In the 8 Spl.Case No.152/2016 Judgment instant case, there was neither taking away nor enticement. The prosecutrix on her own accord had gone with the accused. In this connection reference could be profitably made to the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of S. Vardarajan appellant v. State of Madras respondent, AIR 1965 SC 963 wherein in para 9 it is observed that where a minor knowing and having the capacity to know the full import of what she is doing voluntarily joins the accused, she could not be said to have been taken or enticed from her lawful guardianship. In the case before the Supreme Court also, the girl was below 18 years of age but since she and the accused were having an affair, which included telephonic conversation, their Lordships of the Apex Court took the view that inspite of the fact that she was below 18 years of age, when the accused took her away, no offence of kidnapping would be made out. Therefore, on the facts of this case, the ratio laid down in would have full application. 18] For these reasons, I hold that the prosecution has miserably failed to bring home beyond reasonable doubt, the guilt of the accused for the offence punishable U/Sec. 363, 376 of I.P.C. and U/Sec.5 (j) (ii) r.w Sec. 6 of P.O.C.S.O Act. Hence, point No.1 to 3 are answered in the negative. In the result, the following order is made : :ORDER: 1) The accused­ Fakir @ Sandip Sambhaji Gajbhare is hereby acquitted of the offence punishable U/Secs. 363, 376 of the Indian Penal Code, and under Section 5 (j) (ii) r.w Sec. 6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offence Act vide 9 Spl.Case No.152/2016 Judgment Section 235 (1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure Code. 2) The Accused is in jail and is ordered to be released forthwith, if not required in any other case. 3) The accused shall furnish P.B. and S.B. of Rs.15,000/­ (Rs.Fifteen Thousand only) within two weeks vide Sec. 437(A) of Code of Cr.P.C. for his appearance before the Hon’ble Appellate Court and it shall be in force for six months period. 4) The Muddemal property viz. clothes of prosecutrix and accused and condom pocket being worthless be destroyed after lapse of appeal period. Kalyan. ( D. S. Ghumare ) Date ­14/6/2017 Addl. Session Judge, Kalyan

Bail No.1515/2015(Exh.1) (applicant/accused) were present who disclosed her that her victim daughter is with accused Mukesh and if she lodged the FIR against Mukesh, then they would be done to death. Because of such threat she did not approach to the police. 4] On 20.10.2015, at 3.30 p.m. when she along with her son Anil were present in the house, at that time the victim arrived at home. Therefore she called Jitendra Gaikwad, her brother­in­law and his wife Savita and made enquiry with the victim where she had gone on 19.10.2015 at 8 p.m. She disclosed before all of them that after the class her friend Nikhil Bawiskar of Sambhaji Chowk, Badlapur told her that Mukesh Ahire had asked him to call her to meet as something is to be speak with her and hence she should accompany with him. Her both the friends left her there and went away. While speaking with accused and Mukesh Ahire her elder brother Anil passed from the said area but he could not see them. As accused Mukesh Ahire is terror in the area she was frightened. They were present till 11.30 p.m. near the water tank and he induced her by saying that he would marry with her and if she refused to accompany with him, then would not leave her and her family members. Therefore she sat on his motorcycle who then took her in Boudha Colony near Dakshasheela School. At that time except they both nobody was present. They took meal at 12.30 a.m. and slept on the bed. During the said night accused Mukesh Ahire committed sexual intercourse with her on 2­3 times. At 8 a.m. they both went to Hajimalang on his motorcycle and sat under the 3 Anti. Bail No.1515/2015(Exh.1) tree and were chitchatting. Then the accused Mukesh left her at Boudha Colony. 5] The grounds assigned by her are that she is innocent and falsely implicated. She had disclosed to the informant that the victim daughter of the informant is with her son Mukesh. The victim does not know the name of the places where she was taken. Due to love affair the victim went to meet the accused. There is delay in lodging the FIR. Nothing is to be seized from her. There was consensual sexual intercourse. She has not actually participated in the crime. Lastly, she has prayed to extend interim protection to her on such terms and conditions as this Court may deem fit. 6] The Ld.A.P.P. and I.O resisted the application by filing say at Exh.6 on the grounds that the applicant/accused is the mother of main accused Mukesh Ahire and she has actually participated in the crime. When the main accused Mukesh had brought the minor victim at her house, at that time knowingly the victim was sent forcibly with main accused Mukesh in auto­rickshaw and she was taken to Dombivali at Mohane to the house of his sister. Lastly they have prayed to reject the application. 7] Heard the learned Advocate Shri. V.D.Garud for the applicant/accused and Ld.A.P.P.Smt.Lohakare, at length. 8] I have perused the application, say, copy of the FIR and the documents produced with list Exh.5 viz. remand reports, election card, pan card and ration card of the applicant/accused. 9] It appears that applicant/accused is the mother of main accused Mukesh who kidnapping minor victim and had brought to his house. At that time the applicant/accused knowingly sent the minor victim with main accused Mukesh in auto­rickshaw. She was taken to Mohane at the house of sister of the accused Mukesh and committed sexual intercourse 2­3 times on her. Presented on : 10.11.2016. Registered on : 10.11.2016. Decided on : 12.09.2017. Duration : 10M. 2D. IN THE COURT OF ADDITIONAL SESSIONS JUDGE, KALYAN. AT : KALYAN (Presided over by A.A.A.Shaikh) Special Case No.154/2016. Exhibit No. . State of Maharashtra. (through Bazarpeth Police Station at the instance of Fatima Naushad Bhure R/o. Kalyan). .. Complainant Versus Bharat Devrao Nathbhanjan, Age­26 Years, R/at – Govindwadi, Retibandar, Kalyan (W). .. Accused For the offences punishable under Sections 363, 376 (2) (n), of the Indian Penal Code and Section 4 & 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ . 2 Spl. Case No.154/2016 (Judgment) Ld. APP Mr. D.V.Bhangre for the State. Ld. Adv. Mr. M.M.Deshmukh for accused. : JUDGMENT : (Delivered on 12th September 2017). 1] Accused named­above is prosecuted for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 376 (2)(n) of the Indian Penal Code and under Sections 4 & 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] Case of prosecution in brief is that on 18.03.2016 informant who is the mother of the victim girl lodged her report to police that on 18.03.2016 at about 9.00 p.m. or prior to that accused kidnapped her minor daughter aged 17 years (hereinafter referred to as 'the victim girl') from her lawful guardianship (name of the informant and the victim girl is kept secret). So, on the report of the informant crime for the offences punishable under Section 363 was registered by Bazarpeth Police Station vide crime No.I­50/2016. Thereafter police recorded further statement dated 11.08.2016 of the informant wherein she stated that she came to know from the victim girl that accused by giving promise to marry with her from time to time committed sexual intercourse with her and as a result of which she was carrying pregnancy of eight months. The victim girl was medically examined on 11.08.2016 and the report of doctor shows that the victim girl was carrying pregnancy of six months. Statement of the victim girl under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C. was recorded by the learned 3 Spl. Case No.154/2016 (Judgment) J.M.F.C., Kalyan on 03.09.2016. Police also recorded statement of the victim girl. Statement of the victim girl recorded by police shows that for last four years prior to the incident there was love affair between the victim girl and the accused and that on 18.03.2016 he alongwith the accused ran away and came to Nashik at Satpur and by taking room on rental basis she alongwith accused started residing there. Her statement further shows that after coming to the Nashik her marriage with accused was solemnized in the temple of the Gautam Boudha and thereafter while residing in the room her physical relation with accused took place and that she is carrying pregnancy of eight months from the accused; and that since the mother of the accused made phone call to the accused asking him to come to the house, she along with accused came to the police station. 3] Police seized satranji (carpet) and petticoat of the victim girl and underwear of the accused from the room wherein accused alongwith the victim girl was residing after kidnapping the victim girl. Police obtained the extract of the register of the Kudus Grampanchayat wherein it is mentioned that one daughter is born to Fatima on 26.01.1999. 4] Charge at Exh.6 under Sections 366, 376 (2) (n) of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 4 & 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offcences Act, 2012 was framed against accused. Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 5] After recording evidence and hearing both the sides 4 Spl. Case No.154/2016 (Judgment) following points arise for my determination and I have noted my findings against each of them for the reason to follow: Sr.No. Points Findings 1. Whether it is proved by prosecution that accused kidnapped informant's minor daughter i.e. the victim girl .. Not proved. from her lawful guardianship ? 2. Whether it is proved by prosecution that accused repeatedly committed rape on the informant's minor .. Not proved. daughter i.e. the victim girl ? 3. Whether it is proved by prosecution that accused committed aggravated penetrative sexual assault on the minor daughter of the informant ? .. Not proved. 4. Whether it is proved by prosecution that the accused committed sexual harassment upon the informant's .. Not proved. minor daughter ? 5. What offences, if any are proved .. No offence is proved against against accused ? accused. 5 Spl. Case No.154/2016 (Judgment) : REASONS : As to Point Nos.1 to 6 :­ 6] Perusal of the evidence of the informant (PW­1) shows that it did not happen that accused kidnapped her minor daughter from her lawful guardianship. She identified her signature on the complaint but she has deposed that she does not know about its contents. Contents of the complaint i.e. portion marked 'A' of the complaint was read over to her but she has denied it to be true. Portion marked 'A' of her further statement was read over to her but she has denied it to be true. However, she has admitted that her daughter i.e. victim girl told her that she did marriage with accused. But her evidence shows that she has denied the suggestion that at the time of incident age of her daughter was 17 years. She has also denied the suggestion that as per the record of Kudus Grampanchayat the birth of victim girl took place on 26th January 1999. So it can be said that she has not supported the prosecution case. 7] Perusal of evidence of the victim girl (PW­2) shows that she mentioned her age as 21 years. She has admitted in her evidence that on 11.08.2016 she along with accused came to Bazarpeth Police Station and that she told police that she had love affair with accused and that she did marriage with accused at Gautam Boudha temple at Nashik and thereafter they kept physical relation with each other in the room. She further admitted that she told police that she was carrying pregnancy of 6 Spl. Case No.154/2016 (Judgment) eight months from the accused. She has denied the suggestion that her statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. was recorded before the learned J.M.F.C., Kalyan. She has admitted that her marriage with accused has taken place and that she was having one daughter of eleven months old. She has denied the suggestion that as per record of Kudus Grampanchayat her date of birth is 26.01.1999. 8] In her cross­examination conducted by learned advocate for accused she has admitted that she did marriage with accused as per her own will. She further admitted that when she did marriage with accused at that time she was aged 19 years old and that after her marriage with accused one girl child was born to her from accused. There is nothing on record to show that at the time of incident when the victim girl's physical relation with accused took place at that time the victim girl was below 18 years or minor. Under the circumstances, it can be said that prosecution has failed to prove its case. Accordingly, my answer to point Nos.1 to 4 is not proved and my answer to point No.5 is that no offence is proved against accused. Consequently, accused is entitled for acquittal. Hence, I pass following order:­ : ORDER : i. Accused viz. Bharat Devrao Nathbhanjan is hereby acquitted of the offences punishable under Sections 363, 376 (2) (n) of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 4 and 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 7 Spl. Case No.154/2016 (Judgment) ii. His bail bond stands cancelled and his surety is discharged. iii. Accused is required to execute bail bonds of Rs.15,000/­ with one surety in the like amount under Section 437­A of Cr.P.C. to appear before the Hon'ble Higher Courts or Appellate Courts as and when the Hon'ble Higher Courts or Appellate Courts issue notices in respect of any appeal or petition filed against this Judgment and such bail bond shall be in force for six months. iv Muddemal property i.e. carpet, petticoat and underwear seized in this case being worthless be destroyed after appeal period is over, if notice of appeal is not received during that period. Kalyan. (A.A.A.Shaikh) Date: 12.09.2017. Additional Sessions Judge, Kalyan.

Mrs. R.G.Bhopi for accused. : JUDGMENT : (Delivered on 11th July 2017). 1] Accused named­above is prosecuted for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 376 (2) (i) (n) of the Indian Penal Code and under Sections 4 & 6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] Case of prosecution in brief is that on 25.04.2014 at about 5.45 p.m. informant Bhimrao Narayan Panpatil along with his wife and two grand­daughters viz. Aakansha and the victim girl aged about 16 years (her name is kept secret) was going towards his village and for that purpose they came to Thane Railway Station platform No.2. They boarded the staircase in order to go to platform No.5 to catch the mail express for going to their village. But at that time informant realized that victim girl was missing. So, informant tried to search for her and he also informed this fact to the Station Master who made announcement for the missing victim girl but the victim girl could not be traced out. So, informant lodged missing complaint about the missing victim girl that some unknown person kidnapped the victim girl from his lawful guardianship. On the report of informant crime No.143/2014 for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 376 (2) (I) (n) of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 4 & 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offices Act, 2012 was registered by Thane Railway Police Station. 3 Spl. Case No.156/2016 (Judgment) 3] Police recorded statements of witnesses. Police obtained the bonafide certificate of the victim girl from the school wherein her date of birth is mentioned as 02.03.1999. Police seized one T­ shirt, Barmuda and under wear of the accused under panchnama in presence of panchas. During the investigation it was disclosed that there was love affair between the accused and the victim girl and accused kidnapped her from lawful guardianship of the informant and took her to Dapoli, District Ratnagiri and that at Dapoli their marriage was solemnized and they resided there in Dapoli up to 23.09.2016 and during that period accused kept physical relation with her against her will and thereby committed rape. After completion of investigation charge­sheet was filed . 4] Charge at Exh.4 under Sections 363, 376 (2) (i) (n) of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 4 & 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offcences Act, 2012 was framed against accused. Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 5] After recording evidence and hearing both the sides following points arise for my determination and I have noted my findings against each of them for the reason to follow: Sr.No. Points Findings 1. Whether it is proved by prosecution that accused took with him the minor victim girl out of lawful guardianship .. Not proved. of the informant? 2. Whether it is proved by prosecution 4 Spl. Case No.156/2016 (Judgment) that accused did rape on the victim girl who was at that time under 16 years of age ? .. Not proved. 3. Whether it is proved by prosecution that accused committed rape on the victim girl repeatedly ? .. Not proved. 4. Whether it is proved by prosecution that the accused did penetrative sexual assault on the victim girl ? .. Not proved. 5. Whether it is proved by prosecution that the accused did aggravated sexual assault on the victim girl ? .. Not proved. 6. What offences, if any are proved .. No offence is proved against accused. against accused ? : REASONS : As to Point Nos.1 to 6 :­ 6] Perusal of the evidence of the informant Bhimrao Narayan Panpatil (PW­1) shows that on 25.04.2014 at 5.45 p.m. he went to Thane Railway Station in order to go to his village at that time his wife and his two grand­daughters were also with him. He lodged missing complaint about her in the police station. He has identified his thumb impression on the complaint but he deposed that he does 5 Spl. Case No.156/2016 (Judgment) know about its contents. His evidence further shows that he does not know the accused. He is cross­examined by the learned APP but he has not supported the prosecution case. He has denied the suggestion that compromise between accused and them has taken place. Prosecution. V/s. Abhi @ Prakash Mohan Jadhav, Age: 23 years, Occup. Driver, R/at: Bhoir Chawl No.12,Barkupada, Shiv ­Mandir road, Ambernath (E). .... Accused. ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ Offence punishable U/Sec.363, 376 of I.P.C. & U/Sec.4 of P.O.C.S.O.Act. ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ Shri.Bhangare, Ld.A.P.P. for prosecution. Smt.Bhopi, Ld.advocate for accused. ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ 2 Atro.Spl.Case No.153/2015 Judgment CNR MHTH060037542015 :JUDGMENT: (Delivered on this 22nd day of January, 2018 ) This is one more story of adolescent love. This accused is facing trial for the offences punishable U/Secs.363 & 376 of Indian Penal Code and U/Sec.4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 initiated by State through Central Police Station, Ulhasnagar. 2] Brief facts of the prosecution case are as under : i) Complainant Chaya Raja Padiyachi , the hocker in railway resides at Vinayak Hajare Chawl, Samrat Ashoknagar, Ulhasnagar­3. She has two daughters and one son by name Hemlata, Prity @ Rakhi and Sunny. They are 15 years, 11 years and 13 years old respectively. For her work Chaya used to leave her house 10.30 a.m. and return to her house in the night at 10.00 p.m. Her husband also used to leave the house early in the morning and return his house in late night due to his work. Only her daughters and son were remaining in her house. Both her daughters were not taking the education. Therefore, they used to stay in the house. ii) On 11/8/2015 at about 10.30 a.m. both daughters of complainant Chaya namely Hemlata and Prity left the house saying that they are going to their grand­mother's house. Even though there was late night the daughters do not come to the 3 Atro.Spl.Case No.153/2015 Judgment CNR MHTH060037542015 house. Therefore, the complainant Chaya went to her mother's house and asked her mother about the daughters. Mother told her that she left the girls at 8.00 p.m. near the house of complainant. Then thereafter complainant, her husband, her parents etc. took search of the daughters in the vicinity of Samrat Ashoknagar , but of no use. Till next morning none returned to the house. Even complainant went to the house of her brother at Badlapur for the search of her daughters, but they were not there. Therefore, on 14/8/2015 she lodged missing report as well as complaint alleging that some unknown person has kidnapped her daughters. Thereafter, crime was registered at C.R.No.387/2015 against unknown person for the offence punishable U/Sec.363 of I.P.C. 3] One then P.S.I.G.P.Gondake of Central Police Station, Ulhasnagar carried the investigation. On 15/9/2015 complainant received phone call from her daughter Hemlata wherein she informed the complainant that accused had taken them and kept them in one room in Patil Chawl, Barku Pada, Shivmandir road, Ambernath (E). Therefore complainant, her husband , her father etc. went there. They found both the girls in room No.11. They took the girls and straight way came to police station. The I.O. recorded statement of the victim girl and seized her clothes. He caused medical examination of the victim girl. He arrested accused on the same day and seized the clothes. He recorded further supplementary statement of Chaya 4 Atro.Spl.Case No.153/2015 Judgment CNR MHTH060037542015 Padiyachi. He took search of the room wherein the accused had allegedly kept the victim girl and her sister. He seized some clothes from that room. He recorded statements of some witnesses on 15/8/2015. Again on 17/8/2015 he recorded statements of some witnesses. He sent seized clothes , blood samples of accused and victim , nail samples of accused and victim, pubic hair of accused and victim, and other samples to F.S.L.Kalina, Mumbai for chemical analysis. He caused statement of victim girl to be recorded U/Sec.164 of Cr.P.C. on 16/10/2015. Again on 10/11/2015 he recorded supplementary statement of Chaya Padiyachi. After completion of investigation he submitted chargesheet in the court. 4] Accused was brought before my Ld.Predecessor. Charge against him is framed by my Ld.Predecessor at Exh.3. Charge was read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. His defence is of total denial. 5] Prosecution was asked to adduce its evidence in support of its case. Prosecution examined in all 11 witnesses in this case. P.W.1­ Smt.Chaya Raja Padiyachi (Exh.5) is complainant, mother of victim. She partially supported the prosecution and partially supported the case of 5 Atro.Spl.Case No.153/2015 Judgment CNR MHTH060037542015 the accused. She proved missing report which is at Exh.6. P.W.2­ Smt.Shobha Dinkar Jadhav (Exh.8) is panch witness on seizure of clothes of victim girl. This witness stated that on 15/8/2015 in her presence police seized clothes of victim. Mother of victim had brought another clothes which were handed over to victim girl and then she changed the clothes. This witness identified the clothes of victim before the court. They are at Article 'A' & 'B'. P.W.3­ Nana Ankat Dabhade (Exh.9) is panch witness on seizure of clothes of accused as well as his arrest. This witness admitted his signature on arrest and seizure panchanama Exh.10. He admitted that shirt, and underwear of the accused were seized in his presence under panchanama. It seems that in spite of this the Ld.A.P.P. declared this witness hostile. During his cross­examination by Ld.A.P.P. it is suggested to him that accused was arrested in his presence. This fact is denied by this witness. He further deposed that clothes of victim and accused were seized vide panchanama at Exh.10. C.A. Reports pertaining to the blood sample, nail clipping, pubic hair, semen of accused , and pertaining to blood sample , vaginal swab sample, pubic hair sample, anal swab sample , nail clipping 6 Atro.Spl.Case No.153/2015 Judgment CNR MHTH060037542015 of victim Hemlata are at Exh.12 & 13. The office copy of letter by which the muddemal was sent to the laboratory at Kalina is at Exh.7. P.W.4­ Manojkumar Lalji Jaiswal (Exh.15) deposed that on 17/8/2015 one boy named Jadhav came to him and asked him room on rental basis. Thereafter, he handed over the key of room No.11, Chawl No.2 Vishnu Patil Chawl Barkupada, Shivmandir Road, Ambernath. He further deposed that on same day police made enquiry with him. Police visited the room No.11, one frock of girl was lying there. There was one pair of clothes of a girl. Police seized all the clothes and panchanama was drawn which is at Exh.16. He further deposed that on 17/8/2015 accused gave him Rs.1,000/­ as deposit to Vishnu Patil and then he came in room No.11 with a girl on 19/8/2015. Chemical analysis report pertaining to seized clothes of victim girl and accused is at Exh.18. P.W.5­ Smt.Gereta Raju Kusalkar (Exh.21) is examined as a witness on the point of searching the daughters of complainant , spotting them in one room of Patil Chawl and disclosing the atrocity committed on her by the accused to this witness and other witnesses. This witness turned hostile. 7 Atro.Spl.Case No.153/2015 Judgment CNR MHTH060037542015 P.W.6­ Dr.Hemantkumar Devdatt Khambait (Exh.24) is a medical officer who first examined the victim girl clinically and generally. Then he referred the victim girl to Gynecologist. P.W.7­ Dr.Wani is Gynecologist (Exh.28) who further examined the victim girl. Both these witnesses proved the medical certificate which is at Exh.25. P.W.8­ Smt.Chandrakala Shashi Shinde (Exh.34) grandmother of victim girl. P.W.9­ Shashi Narayan Shinde (Exh.35) is grandfather of victim girl. They both supported the prosecution. P.W.10­ Dr.Tejaswini Gautam Gosavi (Exh.40) is a radiologist. This witness is examined by the prosecution on the point of age of victim girl. This witness stated that age of victim girl was in between 14 to 15 years when she was examined. P.W.11­ Ganpat Pandurang Gondake (Exh.44) is the investigating officer. He narrated about the investigation he carried. Thereafter prosecution closed its evidence. 6] Statement of accused U/Sec. 313 of Cr.P.C. is recorded by putting him all incriminating facts and circumstances in evidence. From the answers given by the accused in the statement U/Sec. 313 of Cr.P.C. it appears that 8 Atro.Spl.Case No.153/2015 Judgment CNR MHTH060037542015 his defence is of total denial. He has not adduced any defence evidence. 7] I have gone through the oral and documentary evidence of the prosecution . I have heard Ld.A.P.P. for State and Ld.Advocate for accused at length. 8] Following points arise for my consideration and my findings on those points are as under for the reasons stated below : POINTS FINDINGS 1) Does prosecution prove that on 12/8/2015 the victim girl was minor below the age of 18 years ? Proved. 2) Does prosecution prove that on 11/8/2015 at 8 p.m. at Vinayak Hajare Chawl, Samrat Ashoknagar, Ulhasnagar 3, the accused kidnapped two victim girls, aged 15 years and 11 years respectively from the lawful guardianship of their parents and that he thereby committed an offence punishable U/Sec.363 of I.P.C. ? Not proved. 3) Does prosecution prove that on 12/8/2015 and 13/8/2015 at Patil chawl, room No.11, Barkupada, 9 Atro.Spl.Case No.153/2015 Judgment CNR MHTH060037542015 Shivmandir road, Ambernath (East) at night the accused committed rape on the minor victim girl aged 15 years and thereby he committed an offence punishable U/Sec.376 of I.P.C. ? Not proved. 4) Does prosecution prove that on the aforesaid date, time and place the accused committed penetrative sexual assault on the victim minor girl aged 15 years and thereby he committed an offence punishable U/Sec.4 of P.O.C.S.O. Act ? Not proved. :REASONS: POINT NO.1 : 9] It is vehemently contended by the prosecutor that on the day of incident i.e. on 12/8/2015 the victim girl was minor below the age of 18 years. To prove the same prosecution relied on the deposition of P.W.1 Chaya Padiyachi. She stated that date of birth of prosecutrix is 22/7/2001. It is brought on record in the deposition of P.W.6 Dr.Khambait that age of the victim girl was 15 years as stated by her. He further deposed that the radiologist opined the age of victim girl is in between 14 to 15 years. P.W.7 Dr.Mukund Wani also deposed that age of the victim girl was 14 to 15 years on the date of examination 10 Atro.Spl.Case No.153/2015 Judgment CNR MHTH060037542015 of victim. Most important evidence is of P.W.10­ Dr.Tejaswini Gosavi. She deposed that on 17/8/2015 victim girl was brought to her alongwith the police yadi and alongwith x­ray of wrist, elbow and illiac crest . She further stated that she observed the x­ray plate and thereafter concluded that the age of victim girl was in between 14 to 15 years. She issued certificate accordingly which is at Exh.43 and that is duly proved by her. In the certificate at Exh.43 reasons for her conclusion are mentioned. It is pertinent to note that this concrete medical evidence adduced by prosecution on the point of age of the prosecutrix on the date of incident is not seriously challenged at all. The evidence of all three doctors and the evidence of P.W.1 Chaya is corroborative to each other and collectively established the fact that on the date of incident victim girl was in between 14 to 15 years age. Here it is worth mentioning that the age scientifically calculated by P.W.10 Dr. Tejaswini fully corroborates and supports the date of birth of victim stated by P.W.1 Chaya during her deposition. Thus cumulative effect of all these facts, circumstances and evidence is that prosecution succeeded to prove the fact that on the date of incident prosecutix was minor below the age of 18 years. I answer point No.1 in affirmative. POINT NO.2 : 10] It is contended by the prosecution that on 11/8/2015 after 8 p.m. this accused kidnapped prosecutrix and 11 Atro.Spl.Case No.153/2015 Judgment CNR MHTH060037542015 her younger daughter by taking away them from the lawful custody of the complainant Chaya and thereby committed an offence of kidnapping. To sustain this allegation I found absolutely no evidence. 'What ever' is stated by P.W.1 Chaya the mother of victim, P.W.8 Chandrakala Shinde and P.W. 9 Shashi Shinde the grandparents of victim that from 11/8/2015 victim girl and her younger sister Priti were missing . In spite of combing search they could not trace out them. On 14/8/2015 or on 15/8/2015 somebody amongst these three received phone call from victim girl who stated her address and also stated that she had come alongwith accused as she loves accused and she wanted to marry with the accused. There is one additinal fact on record that victim girl and her sister were found in room No.11 of Vishnu Patil chawl , Barku Wadi, Ambernath. Except these facts and evidence on record there is nothing on record to prove the fact that accused kidnapped the victim girl and her younger sister from the lawful custody of P.W.1 complainant Chaya. None saw accused taking away or inducing away victim girl and her sister. Even in the entire prosecution case it is no where brought on record that victim girl , her younger sister and accused were found at one place especially in the room No.11 of Vishnu Patil chawl, Barkuwadi, Ambernath. On the contrary it seems that on her own victim girl had left her house in the absence of her parents. Victim girl is no more and therefore it remained in dark what really had happened. Whatever evidence on record is not at all sufficient 12 Atro.Spl.Case No.153/2015 Judgment CNR MHTH060037542015 to prove the fact that this accused kidnapped the prosecutrix and her minor sister from the lawful custody of complainant. Therefore, I answer point No.2 in negative. POINT NOS.3 & 4 : 11] In order to avoid repetition of discussion, I would like to consider both these points together. 12] Prosecution vehemently contended that during night on 12/8/2015 this accused committed forcible rape on the minor victim girl aged about 15 yrs. in room No.11 in Vishnu Patil chawl, Barkupada, Ambernath (E). Further contention of prosecution is that after alleged kidnapping of the two victim girls accused took them towards Barkupada and kept them in room No.11, chawl No.2 of Vishnu Patil chawl, Barkupada, Ambernath. 13] Now I have to see whether the fact that accused took the victim girl and her sister to the Vishnu Patil Chawl, Barkupada, Ambernath. It is deposed by P.W.1 Chaya, P.W.8 Chandrakala and P.W.9­ Shashi that victim girl and her sister were found in one room of Vishnu Patil chawl, Barkupada. As per say of P.W.1 Chaya they were found on 15/8/2015 at 8 a.m. whereas P.W.8 Chandrakala, and P.W.9 Shashi stated that they were found on 14/8/2015 . There is variance amongst the evidence of P.W.1 Chaya, P.W.8­ Chandrakala and P.W.9­Shsshi regarding the exact date when they spotted victim girl and 13 Atro.Spl.Case No.153/2015 Judgment CNR MHTH060037542015 her sister in a room at Vishnu Patil chawl , Barkupada, Ambernath(E). It is deposed by P.W.1 Chaya that she received phone call on 15/8/2015 at 8.00 p.m. from the victim girl and at that time she disclosed the address of Ambernath to her. Contrary to her it is deposed by P.W.8 Chandrakala that the victim girl on 14/8/2015 made phone call to her husband Shashi and informed the address. It is stated by P.W.9 Shashi that on 14/8/2015 victim girl made phone call on his cell phone and that phone was received by P.W.1 Chaya . Not only this but again she gave phone call to him. Thus regarding getting information from prosecutrix about her whereabouts on phone and the date of getting information , there is material contradictions amongst these three important prosecution witnesses. The deposition of P.W.1 Chaya denotes that the victim girl was spotted on 15/8/2015 whereas P.W.8 & P.W.9 states that she was spotted on 14/8/2015. It is pertinent to note that these dates are specifically mentioned by them during their depositions before the court. Even for the sake of arguments we assume that these three witnesses spotted the victim girl and her sister in room No.11 , chawl No.2 Vishnu Patil Chawl, Barkupada, Ambernath. None of them has stated that when they went on the given address by the prosecutrix the accused was there. It is no one's case and even the case of prosecution that in the alleged room in Vishnu Patil chawl the accused was present alongwith the victim girls. 14 Atro.Spl.Case No.153/2015 Judgment CNR MHTH060037542015 14] Now I turn to the evidence of P.W.4 Manojkumar. This witness has examined by the prosecution because as per the story of the prosecution accused took the room No.11 from this person on rent. Surprisingly this P.W.4 Manojkumar stated in his deposition that on 17/8/2015 one boy by name Jadhav came to him and stated that he want a room on rental basis. He further stated that then he handed over key of room No.11 , chawl No.2 of Vishnu Patil Chawl, Barkupada,Shivmandir Road, Ambernath. He further stated that on the same date police came to him for enquiry and drawn the panchanama. He further deposed that on 17/8/2015 accused paid Rs.1,000/­ to Vishnu Patil as a deposit. In next sentence he stated that on 19/8/2015 the accused came in room No.11 with a girl. This evidence of P.W.4 Manojkumar is totally contradictory to the prosecution story. This creates reasonable doubt regarding occupation of room No.11 by accused alongwith the victim girl . When this witness Manojkumar gave room on rent to accused on 17/8/2015 and when as per his deposition the accused went to that room alongwith that girl on 19/8/2015 then there is no possibility and probability of taking the victim girl by this accused to same room on 11/8/2015 and 12/8/2015 and committed rape there. It is most surprising that prosecution has not declared P.W.4 Manojkumar hostile. Rather prosecution relied on his evidence which has destroyed the prosecution case entirely. As per the prosecution theory the accused was arrested on 15/8/2015. If this is true then there is no truth at all in the 15 Atro.Spl.Case No.153/2015 Judgment CNR MHTH060037542015 deposition of P.W.4 Manojkumar. If the deposition of Manojkumar is true because the prosecution relied on it, then other contentions of prosecution are totally false. Thus the facts and circumstances on record especially the evidence of P.w.4 Manojkumar creates reasonable doubt regarding the entire prosecution story and the alleged allegations. 15] The panch witness on arrest panchanama turned hostile. It is not specifically brought on record from where the I.O. arrested the accused. In entire evidence of prosecution oral or documentary there is no iota of evidence to show that at any point of time this accused was found in the company of victim girl or the victim girl was found with accused either in room No.11, Vishnu Patil Chawl or elsewhere. Therefore, the story of prosecution regarding kidnapping and staying with prosecutrix in the room No.11 , Vishnu Patil Chawl, of Barkupada is not proved beyond reasonable doubts. 16] The clothes of accused and prosecutrix were seized by the I.O. Seizure panchanama are proved . Those clothes were sent to F.S.L. But nothing incriminating found in the chemical examination of those clothes, against the accused. 17] Nail clippings, blood sample, semen, vaginal swab, anal swab of prosecutrix were taken and sent for chemical analysis. Reports are on record. However, prosecution has not 16 Atro.Spl.Case No.153/2015 Judgment CNR MHTH060037542015 established anything against the accused incriminating from those reports. 18] For the purpose of rape or penetrative sexual assault, the prosecution vehemently relied on medical evidence on record. After careful scrutiny the medical evidence on record including the deposition of medical officers especially P.W.7 Dr.Mukund Wani and P.W.6 Dr.Hemantkumar Khambait it revealed to me that this medical evidence has not established the factum of rape rather forcible rape on the victim girl. P.W.6 Dr. Hemantkumar Khambait stated that on 15/8/2015 victim girl was brought to him for medical examination. He examined the patient generally like pulse, B.P. etc. and further referred the victim girl to gynecologist Dr. Mukund Wani. He has not stated anything about rape in his entire deposition. He has not personally observed any sign of forceful rape on the victim. After showing the papers prepared by gynecologist he stated that hymen of the victim was torn and age of tear was fresh. This statement of P.W.6 is based on the papers prepared by Dr.Wani and not it is his personal observation or opinion. 19] P.W.7 Dr. Mukund Wani deposed that on 15/8/2015 he examined the victim girl. He collected sample of blood, pubic hair, vaginal swab of victim. He deposed that her hymen was torn at 3 O'clock position and the tears were fresh. No other injuries on her body. Thus both these doctors stated 17 Atro.Spl.Case No.153/2015 Judgment CNR MHTH060037542015 on oath that on their examination they found only hymen of victim was torn. They have not specifically deposed that this tearing of hymen was due to forcible intercourse or due to rape. Merely on the fact that at the time of examination of victim girl her hymen was torn, it can not be directly concluded that there was rape on the prosecutrix and it was committed only by accused. Because no signs of rape were found by these medical officers on victim girl at the time of her examination. 20] Ld.A.P.P. for the prosecution vehemently argued that the tear of hymen was fresh. These facts and circumstances can not lead to draw the inference that there was a rape on 15/8/2015 unless there is other corroborative, strong and cogent evidence. In this cross­examination P.W.7 Dr.Mukund Wani admitted that said hymen tear can be in an accident. He further deposed that it requires 20 to 25 days for healing the wound due to tear of hymen. This admission suggests possibility of tearing the hymen of victim girl due to any other reason and it might be one day prior or it may 5 to 10 days prior. Fresh tearing means within which period it was caused is not specifically mentioned by the doctors who deposed before the court. 21] P.W.6 Dr.Hemantkumar Khambait and P.W.7 Dr. Mukund Wani both proved the medical certificate which is at Exh.25. It is signed by both. The certificate is issued regarding 18 Atro.Spl.Case No.153/2015 Judgment CNR MHTH060037542015 the examination of victim in the light of alleged allegation of forcible rape on the victim. In the entire certificate at Exh.25 except the mention of tearing the hymen of victim girl no other incriminating fact is mentioned. Exh.25 is printed form of medical certificate signed by both the doctors P.W.6 Dr.Hemantkumar Khambai and P.W.7 Dr.Mukund Wani. I have carefully gone through the said certificate or form. There are total (xi) columns in the form. The column No. (ix) pertains to provisional opinion regarding sexual assault. This column is totally kept blank by medical officers. No opinion regarding sexual assault on the victim girl is mentioned in this column. It is pertinent to note that as per the note below column No.ix) it is mandatory on the part of medical officers to enter the brief observations in Sr.No.1 to 7 under column no. ix) in that form in handwriting. This mandate is not at all followed by the medical officers P.W.6 Dr.Hemantkumar Khambaii or P.W.7 Dr.Mukund Wani. Thus there is absolutely no opinion of the medical officers whether there was sexual assault on the prosecutrix or not. This creates a reasonable doubt regarding the allegation of the prosecution that there was sexual assault or forcible rape on the victim girls by this accused. 22] In column No.11 of the form at Exh.25 it is directed to medical officer that opinion about sexual assault can be given on the basis of finding of relevant injuries and positive results of F.S.L. It is not stated by either P.W.6 Dr.Hemantkumar 19 Atro.Spl.Case No.153/2015 Judgment CNR MHTH060037542015 Khambait and P.W.7 Dr.Mukund Wani that while issuing the certificate at Exh.25 they reserved their opinion regarding the sexual assault. The investigating officer has not tried to get opinion of medical officers regarding alleged sexual assault on the victim girl after getting the reports from F.S.L. In fact there is nothing incriminating in the reports of F.S.I. on record. There are missing links in the medical evidence on record. Due to that it is not proved beyond all reasonable doubts that there was a sexual assault or rape on the victim girl by the accused. 23] It is true that as per Sec.29 of POCSO Act burden is on accused to prove his innocence. But when absolutely there is no evidence on record to prove the fact that this accused has committed any sexual assault on the victim girl, question of discharging burden by this accused U/Sec.29 of POCSO Act does not arise at all. Thus merely because the accused has not adduced any defence evidence or he has not deposed on oath it can not be held that he has failed to prove his innocence and discharge the burden U/Sec.29 of POCSO Act. The prosecution has to establish prima facie the possibility and probability of committing offence i.e. the criminal assault by the accused on the victim girl. In absence of such proof there is no necessity for this accused to prove his innocence. 24] After considering the prosecution evidence on record thoroughly, it is revealed to me that the prosecution has failed 20 Atro.Spl.Case No.153/2015 Judgment CNR MHTH060037542015 to prove any of the guilt of accused. Even no possibility and probability is created by the prosecution through its evidence to presume that the accused has committed the alleged offence. Therefore, I answer point Nos.3 & 4 in negative. In conclusion I pass the following order : : ORDER: 1) Accused Abhi @ Prakash Mohan Jadhav is hereby acquitted of the offence punishable U/Sec. 363, 376 of I.P.C. and U/Sec. 4 of POCSO Act,2012 vide Sec.235(1) of Cr.P.C. 2) He is in jail. He be released forthwith if not required in any other case or crime. 3) Muddemal being worthless be destroyed after the period of appeal is over. 4) Accused is hereby directed to furnish bail by executing PR & SB of Rs.15,000/­ , in compliance of Sec.437(A) of Cr.P.C. 5) Copy of this judgment be sent to the Trial Court for information. Kalyan. (D.S. Hatarote ) 22/01/2018 Addl. Sessions Judge, Kalyan.
