.. 1 .. Atro. Special Case No. 157/2015 ( Judgment ) Presented on : 27/11/2015 Registered on : 27/11 /2015 Decided on : 08/12/2017 Duration : 02Y ­ 00M ­11D IN THE COURT OF SPECIAL JUDGE AND ADDL. SESSIONS JUDGE, KALYAN [Presided Over by S.P. Gogarkar] ATRO. SPECIAL CASE NO.157 OF 2015 EXH. NO. : 23 State of Maharashtra (Through Mahatma Phule Chowk Police Station), ( C.R. No. I­601/2015) .. Complainant. Versus Ganesh Anil Chincholkar, Age : 33 years, Resident of : Joshi Baug, Ibrahim Chawl, Room No. 7, Behind Saibaba Mandir, Kalyan (West) .. Accused. Offence punishable under Section 354(D) of the Indian Penal Code and under Section 11 punishable under Section 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ Mrs.Bhamare­Patil, Ld. A.P.P. for the State Shri S.B.Khandagale, Ld. Adv. for the Accused ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ .. 2/­ .. 2 .. Atro. Special Case No. 157/2015 ( Judgment ) JUDGMENT ( Delivered on this 8th day of December, 2017 ) 1] Accused Ganesh Anil Chincholkar stands prosecuted for the alleged commission of outraging the modesty of victim girl by chasing her on the shop way and by making gestures throwing coins in front of her and by trying to show obscene video clips from his mobile handset. P.S.O. Mahatma Phule Chowk Police Station registered this offence vide Crime No. I ­ 601/2015, on the report of victim complainant. 2] The story of the prosecution in short is that, the complainant family resides in the area of Joshi Baug, Kalyan (West). The victim girl is the daughter of Suman and Ramesh Paswan. The accused Ganesh Chincholkar is also resident of Joshi Baug near Saibaba Temple, hence, he is known to that area. On 18/06/2015, the complainant family was enjoying the lunch at about 1.30 p.m. The father of victim girl asked her to bring some toast from the nearby shop of that vicinity. Accordingly, the victim girl went towards the shop and returned back within short time, but she was weeping and was found in scared condition. 3] The mother of the victim enquired with her, the reason for her condition, on which victim girl told that when .. 3/­ .. 3 .. Atro. Special Case No. 157/2015 ( Judgment ) she was proceeding towards the shop, one person obstructed her way and was trying to show obscene picture / video clip from his mobile handset. She did not pay heed to his activity and went to the shop. But while coming back from the shop, said person was again on the way of complainant. He tried to attract her by making some gestures and throwing some coins in front of her asking her to pick up it and come near him. The victim girl got frightened due to the activity of said person. She rushed to the house and narrated the incident to her mother. 4] The victim's mother Suman Paswan immediately went towards wrongdoer which was shown by the victim girl from some distance. The victim's mother Suman scolded that boy who was present on the way. Till then, neighbouring persons gathered there and they whispered the name of said boy as Ganesh Chincholkar. The victim girl received shock of that incident and she was feeling giddiness. Hence, the father of victim girl took her to Rukminibai Hospital, Kalyan from where information was given to the police and police arrived there and recorded the complaint of victim girl which was treated as F.I.R. and offence came to be registered against the accused. 5] P.S.O. Mahatma Phule Chowk Police Station .. 4/­ .. 4 .. Atro. Special Case No. 157/2015 ( Judgment ) registered this offence vide Crime No. I ­ 601/2015, on the report of victim complainant and further investigation was carried out by A.P.I. Mr. Aslam Khatib. The Investigating Officer visited the house of complainant and recorded the statements of corresponding witnesses including the victim girl. The Investigating Officer has collected the birth certificate of victim girl from her parents showing her minor age. Moreover, the statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. of the victim girl came to be recorded before the Ld. Magistrate. The accused was arrested, and on completion of investigation, the charge­sheet came to be filed. 6] The accused appeared before the Court in response to the summons. I have framed charge vide Exh.5. It was read over and explained to him in vernacular. Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. The prosecution has examined victim girl, her parents and the neighbouring witness alongwith Investigating Officer and Medical Officer. I have recorded the statement of accused under Section 313 of Cr.P.C. The defence of the accused is of total denial and of false implication on the instigation of one Advocate family. However, he has not examined any defence witness to substantiate his defence of false implication. 7] Considering the evidence on record and defence .. 5/­ .. 5 .. Atro. Special Case No. 157/2015 ( Judgment ) of the accused, following points arose for my determination and my findings thereon, are as under, for the reasons given below : POINTS FINDINGS 1] Does prosecution prove that the accused on 18/06/2015, at 1.30 p.m. nearby the chawl of complainant on the road exhibited his gestures with intent to outrage her modesty and thereby committed an offence punishable under Section 354(D) .. Negative. of the Indian Penal Code ? 2] Does prosecution prove that on the above date, time and place, the accused tried to show some obscene video clip by obstructing the way of victim and by throwing some coins before her for temptation and thereby committed sexual gesture towards the victim girl, aged about 11 years and thereby committed an offence under Section 11 punishable under .. Negative. Section 12 of POCSO Act, 2012 ? 3] What order ? .. Accused is acquitted. :REASONS : 8] To substantiate the offence of outraging the modesty of a girl and to prove the sexual offence, as provided .. 6/­ .. 6 .. Atro. Special Case No. 157/2015 ( Judgment ) under Section 11 of POCSO Act, the ingredients of the alleged offences are to be proved with cogent and consistent evidence. Moreover, the presumption as laid down under Section 30 of POCSO Act regarding culpable mental state of the accused, is to be proved within four corners of law. The prosecution has placed reliance on the oral evidence of P.W.1 victim herself, P.W.2 and P.W.5 being her parents to support her story. The evidence of P.W.6 Kantabai is adduced as an independent corroborative evidence to prove the prosecution story. P.W.3 Dr. Mamta Lavande has examined the victim to prove her frightened condition. P.W.4 Police Officer Mr. Pundalik Dhum and P.W.7 A.P.I. Mr. Aslam Khatib are examined to prove the investigation. I have to consider the said evidence adduced on record on the backdrop of cross terms of accused with Advocate family, who is an instigator of the complainant. POINT NOS. 1 AND 2 : 9] It reflects from the F.I.R. Exh.8 that, on 18/06/2015, the victim girl was proceeding towards the grocery shop as her father asked her to bring some toast to eat with lunch. She was proceeding towards the nearby shop where accused was present on the way and he was trying to attract her attention towards him by making whistle and by making some gestures. She did not listen to him. But while .. 7/­ .. 7 .. Atro. Special Case No. 157/2015 ( Judgment ) returning from the shop, again he has done same activities and was trying to show some obscene picture clip to the victim girl. She got frightened and rushed to the house and narrated the incident. 10] To substantiate this story, the evidence of victim P.W.1 Disha and the evidence of her parents P.W.2 Ramesh and P.W.5 Suman is important. P.W.6 Kantabai is tried to demonstrate as an eye witness, but her status is not above than a chance witness. It is true, the victim Disha has narrated the story as per allegations of the F.I.R. The Ld. A.P.P. Smt. Patil/Bhamare submitted that the evidence of child witness can be believed to base the conviction even in absence of oath and it can be considered as per the provisions of Section 118 of the Indian Evidence Act. I do agree with the preposition of the Ld. A.P.P. But the litmus test to scrutinize the evidence of such witness is that it should be free from tutoring. It is laid down in the case of Dattu Ramrao Sakhare Vs State of Maharashtra, decided on 08/05/1997, by the Hon'ble Supreme Court that “ the only precaution which the Court should bear in mind while assessing the evidence of a child witness is that the witness must reliable one and his/her demeanour must be like any other competent witness and there is no likelihood of being tutored ”. .. 8/­ .. 8 .. Atro. Special Case No. 157/2015 ( Judgment ) 11] If this principle laid down by The Hon'ble Supreme Court is applied to the case in hand, then the cross­ examination of a child witness is liable to be considered. She has specifically admitted in her cross­examination that she had never seen the accused prior to the incident nor his description was given while disclosing the fact with the mother. It is pertinent to note that one Karanjkar Advocate was accompanying with the father of this witness while coming to the Court on 2­3 occasions who discussed this matter with the father of victim. Moreover, it is whispered through the cross­examination that there was talk of compromise between the accused and complainant family under the mediation of said Karanjkar. She has further admitted that she has not seen obscene video clip from that mobile handset of the accused. It reveals from her cross­ examination that she was taken to the Ld. Magistrate Court with her father and her statement came to be recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. But, no female member was present nor Lady Police Officer took her to the Ld. Magistrate. It is pertinent to note that her initial statement recorded at Rukminibai Hospital which is treated as F.I.R., is recorded by P.W.4 Male Police Officer Head Constable Mr. Pundalik Dhum. It is true, it is tried to say that W.P.C. Smt. Ahire was alongwith Head Constable Mr. Dhum, but no documentary proof is produced on record to show the presence of Woman .. 9/­ .. 9 .. Atro. Special Case No. 157/2015 ( Judgment ) Officer while recording the statement. It is pertinent to note that P.H.C. Mr. Dhum endorsed his signature on the statement of victim, but W.P.C. Smt. Ahire has not signed the said statement. Therefore, it can not be said firmly that the required procedure under POCSO Act is followed while recording the statement of the child victim. 12] It reveals from the evidence of the parents of the victim that their daughter has narrated entire episode of occurrence and the role attributed by the accused. It is stated that P.W.6 Kantabai Kedare was also present at the time of said narration. If the evidence of these three witnesses who are admittedly hearsay witnesses, is scrutinized, then it reveals that there is material variance in the story telling by these three witnesses. P.W.6 Kantabai appears to have been tagged as a chance witness to show independent corroboration. It is their case that the victim girl became unconscious on receiving the shock of incident. On the other hand, father of victim girl P.W.2 Ramesh has stated that she has shown the accused to her mother from some distance. These two facts can not be in existence at the same time. Similar contradiction is found in the evidence of P.W.3 Dr. Mamta Lavande. She deposed that the victim was brought at 5.05 p.m. She was in frightened condition and was not in a position to give the history of alleged assault. Her general .. 10/­ .. 10 .. Atro. Special Case No. 157/2015 ( Judgment ) condition was found below normal and was breathlessness. Therefore, immediate treatment was given. Surprisingly, in the next sentence, said doctor witness has stated that police arrived immediately after her intimation and police recorded the statement of victim girl in her presence and at that time, said doctor opined that she was in fit mental condition to give the statement. Such self contradictory opinion regarding the mental status of victim girl gave a fatal blow to the genuineness of her physical condition. It is pertinent to note that while giving intimation to the police, said doctor initially mentioned the history of phobia, but the word phobia is scratched and the word breathlessness is mentioned in its place. Such filling of lacuna, leads me to form some doubt regarding the genuineness of situation. 13] The Ld. A.P.P. Smt. Patil/Bhamare submitted on point of presumption under Section 29 of POCSO Act. But it is needless to say that said presumption can be made applicable when the case falls within the ambit of Sections 4, 5, 6, 8 and 9 of POCSO Act. In the present case, the accused is facing charge for sexual harassment under Section 11 punishable under Section 12 of the said Act. Therefore, the applicability of Section 29 of POCSO Act is not acceptable. But, the theory of culpable mental state as described in Section 30 of the said Act is liable to be considered while .. 11/­ .. 11 .. Atro. Special Case No. 157/2015 ( Judgment ) deciding such cases. To substantiate a culpable mental state of the accused, his presence on spot is to be proved first. In this case, the Ld. Counsel Mr. Khandagale vehemently gave emphasis that the spot panchanama is not drawn by the Investigating Officer to prove the place of occurrence to show the presence of accused. It is true, the spot panchanama is missing from the entire investigation. Moreover, the mobile handset alleged to be used by the accused for showing obscene video clip is also not seized during investigation nor any such evidence is collected which alleged to cause shame in the mind of victim. 14] The ingredients of outraging the modesty of victim by using criminal force is to be established with cogent evidence to prove the charge under Section 354(D) of I.P.C. In the present case, the victim girl has stated about the whistle given by the accused to attract her attention. Moreover, he alleged to have thrown some coins in front of her and asked her to pick up and come near to him by gestures. By no stretch of imagination, it can be said that the accused has used criminal force to outrage the modesty of victim girl. At the most, it can be said that he was staring towards her and was trying to attract her attention, to which she has not paid any heed. In such situation, it is too hard to .. 12/­ .. 12 .. Atro. Special Case No. 157/2015 ( Judgment ) connect the accused for the alleged use of criminal force for outraging the modesty. 15] The evidence of Investigating Officer suffers from specification. He has merely deposed on point of his general investigation without considering the procedural requirement of the said special statute. The presence of Lady Police Officer to record the statement and requirement as mentioned in Section 24, 25 and 26 of POCSO Act are not fulfilled. On the other hand, it is whispered from the defence that one Karanjkar family was behind the alleged prosecution. On the advice of said family that too with the intention of evicting the accused from the tenanted premises of their chawl, the present prosecution is launched against the accused. Thus, considering the facts and circumstances of this case, possibility can not be ruled out of afterthought implication. 16] The history of phobia which is scratched and replaced by the word of breathlessness create a doubt about the natural conduct and expected responses from the victim girl. She has whispered somewhere in the deposition that her father has stated the story narrated by her while lodging the report. It is true, there is nothing wrong in narrating the story to the parents first. The Ld. A.P.P. has placed reliance rightly on the case of Vinodkumar Vs. State decided by the Hon'ble .. 13/­ .. 13 .. Atro. Special Case No. 157/2015 ( Judgment ) Delhi High Court on 18th December, 2014. The natural conduct of the victim girl in narrating the story to her parents, more particularly to the mother is discussed in the cited case supra. However, in the case in hand, it reveals that the story put­forth by the victim girl is having some variance with the story stated by the other corresponding witnesses. In such situation, the accused can not be held guilty relying on the bare words of the victim girl which are not free from doubt and does not inspire reliable confidence to connect the accused with the alleged crime. Therefore, I have no alternative, but to answer point Nos. 1 and 2 in negative. POINT NO. 3 : 17] As I held above, the prosecution failed to prove necessary ingredients to prove the guilt of accused. The Investigating Officer failed to comply with procedural mandate of the special statute of POCSO. The evidence is scanty and inconsistent on point of identification of accused. No identification parade is conducted by the Investigating Officer. These major lacunas gave fatal blow to the prosecution case. Hence, the accused is liable to be acquitted giving benefit of inadequate evidence to prove the charges. In the result, I answer point No. 3 accordingly and proceed to pass following order : .. 14/­ .. 14 .. Atro. Special Case No. 157/2015 ( Judgment ) :ORDER: I] Accused Ganesh Anil Chincholkar, Age : 33 years, R/at : Joshi Baug, Ibrahim Chawl, Room No.7, Behind Saibaba Mandir, Kalyan (West), is hereby acquitted under Section 235(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure of the offences punishable under 354(D) of the Indian Penal Code and under section 11 punishable under Section 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. II] Bail bonds of accused stands cancelled. III] The accused is directed to furnish a fresh P.B. & S.B. of Rs.15,000/­ ( Rs. Fifteen Thousands only) in compliance with the provisions of section 437(A) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Judgment pronounced in open Court. Sd/­ Kalyan. [ S.P. Gogarkar ] Date : 08/12/2017. Special Case No. 157/2015 ( Judgment ) ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ IN THE COURT OF SPECIAL JUDGE AND ADDL. 1 Or.Exh.1 in Cri.Ant.Bail 1664/2015 Order below Ex.1 in Anticipatory Criminal Bail Application No.1664/2015 Mr. Bittu Sudhir Thakur ….. Applicant Vs. State of Maharashtra, (Through Central Police Station) ….. Opponent 1/­ This is an application for anticipatory bail under section 438 of Cr.P.C. in C.R.No.I­567/2015 of Central Police Station for the offence punishable under sections 354B, 354D, 452 r/w.34 of IPC and under sections 8 & 12 of POCSO Act, 2012. 2/­ The applicant has contended that he is 18 years old boy and his arrest will ruin his respect in society. He is suffering from mental disorder which leads to getting sudden unconscious. He is permanent resident of Maharashtra and he will not abscond. He is innocent and nothing to do with the alleged offence set out in the FIR. Further contention is that false case is registered against the applicant to counter­blast the previous FIR filed by the grandfather of the applicant against the brother of the main complainant. The applicant lastly prayed for allowing his application. 3/­ The Investigation Officer has resisted the application by filing his Say at Exh.6 wherein it is contended that the accused by entering into the house of victim girl was trying to remove her legins and on her try to shout he gaged her mouth by his hand and he moved his hands on the breasts of the victim girl. Further contention is that one another unknown colleague of the applicant was along with the applicant and that unknown colleague is absconding. It is further contended that if, 2 Or.Exh.1 in Cri.Ant.Bail 1664/2015 this applicant is granted anticipatory bail, then he will help the absconding accused to avoid his arrest. The Investigation Officer lastly prayed for rejecting the application. 4/­ Heard Ld. Advocate Shri R.O. Chaturvedi and Ld. APP Ms. R.R. Bhoir for the State. 5/­ At the out set I would like to state that the custodial interrogation is not always necessary only for the purpose of recovery of any incriminating articles or things, but, may also be necessary to unearth the truth. Here in this case in hand, a victim girl aged 11 years has lodged the FIR in which allegation is made that on 05.11.2015 at about 1.30 a.m. she felt that somebody was removing her legins when she was sleeping in the house along with her family members. When she got up, she saw the present applicant removing her legins. The FIR further makes out that when the victim girl tried to shout, the present applicant gaged her mouth by his one hand and moved his hand on the breasts of the victim girl. Her FIR further makes out that she any how removed the hand of the applicant and on her shouts the applicant started running away. At that time the victim girl saw one another boy along with the present applicant and that boy was wearing pink colour shirt and blue colour jeans pant. Thus, the allegations which are made in the FIR by the victim girl, aged 11 years are certainly serious allegations. Whether the victim girl has filed the FIR to counter­blast the FIR filed by grandfather of the applicant against the brother of the victim girl or what is also a matter which requires investigation and that cannot be the ground which makes the applicant entitled to anticipatory bail. Furthermore, the colleague of the applicant has to be traced out. For that purpose also the custodial 3 Or.Exh.1 in Cri.Ant.Bail 1664/2015 interrogation of the present applicant is necessary. 6/­ Thus, the foregoing discussion leads to conclude that this is not a fit case which entitles the applicant to anticipatory bail. With due respects to the decision of Hon'ble Bombay High Court in case of Joginder Singh Vs. State of Maharashtra in Criminal Anticipatory Bail Application 243/2013 with Criminal Application No. 181/2013 decided on 03.04.2013 will not come to the help of this applicant/accused for the reason that, in that case decided by Hon'ble Bombay High Court the applicant had co­operated with investigating agency. Here in this case in hand, there is nothing in the Say of Investigation Officer that the applicant has helped him and co­operated him in the investigation. Thus, with due respect, the said decision will not come to the help of the applicant. Accordingly, I pass following order : ORDER 1] The application stands rejected. 2] The interim order passed below Exh.3 stands vacated. Kalyan. (S.B. Gaidhani) 19/01/2016 Addl. Sessions Judge, Kalyan.

No. 16 IN THE COURT OF ADDITIONAL SESSIONS JUDGE, KALYAN [ Presided Over by S.P. Gogarkar ] SPECIAL CASE NO. 165 OF 2015 State of Maharashtra ( Through Manpada Police Station, Dombivali, Tal­Kalyan, Dist­Thane ) ( Cr. No. I­588/2014 ) ...Complainant Versus Akhilesh Harichandra Mishra, Age : 23 years, Occ.: Labour, R/at : Near Saibaba Mandir, Prakash Dube Chawl, Room No.4, Hanuman Tekadi, Navali, Palghar, Tal. Palghar, Native at : Gram Khemapur, Post­Rampur, Tal­Madiyahu, Dist.­Jaunpur, U.P. ...Accused Offence punishable under secs. 363, 366, 376 of the Indian Penal Code and under secs. 3, 4 and 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012 ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ 2 Spl. C. No. 165/2015 [ Judg. ] Shri S.H. Ramteke, Ld. APP For Complainant Shri C.P. Singh, Ld. Adv. For Accused ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ ORAL JUDGMENT ( Delivered on this 28th day of January, 2016 ) 1] Accused Akhilesh Mishra originally residing at Khemapur, District­Jaunpur (U.P.) and presently residing at Palghar is prosecuted for the alleged commission of enticing the minor girl of his village while residing at her maternal uncle's house at Kalyan and for alleged commission of forceful illicit intercourse and for committing rape knowingly that she is a minor. Manpada Police registered this offence vide Crime No. I­588/2014 on the report of maternal uncle of the victim i.e. complainant Rameshchandra Gaud. 2] The story of the prosecution in short is that, the victim girl is originally residence of village­Khemapur, Dist­ Jaunpur (U.P.). Accused is also residence of same village. He used to visit the victim's house which resulted into intimacy and love affair between the minor girl and the accused. The parents of the girl learnt said fact. They got annoyed and sent victim girl to the house of her maternal uncle at Kalyan. Hence the victim girl was migrated from Jaunpur­District to Kalyan. Accused also followed her in the zoom of their love affair. He also migrated to his uncle's house at Nalasopara 3 Spl. C. No. 165/2015 [ Judg. ] and started doing some labour work. Again they got chance to meet each other. Their regular acquaintance turned into deep love and they decided to marry each other. 3] On 27/4/2014 the victim girl left the house of her maternal uncle and came out alone to visit the accused. Then they went to Rajasthan and thereafter to Vapi, Gujarat and returned back to Palghar. They performed marriage in Jivdani Temple, Palghar and started residing jointly in a rented room at Palghar as a husband and wife. 4] Meanwhile missing complaint came to be lodged and the maternal uncle of the girl learnt that she is staying with the accused at Palghar. It was informed to the police accordingly. Said couple was brought to the Police Station and accused came to be arrested on registration of crime. The victim girl was sent for medical examination and then necessary investigation was carried out. On completion of necessary investigation chargesheet came to be filed. 5] The accused appeared before the court in response to the committal order passed by learned J.M.F.C. Court. I have framed charge vide Exh.2. It was read over and explained to him in vernacular. Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. The prosecution has examined the complainant maternal uncle and the victim girl in support of its case. I have dispensed with statement of the accused under section 313 of Cr.P.C.. Defence of the accused is of total denial and of false implication. 4 Spl. C. No. 165/2015 [ Judg. ] 6] Considering the evidence on record and defence of the accused following points arose for my determination and my findings thereon are as under for the reasons given below :­ POINTS FINDINGS 1] Does prosecution prove that, the accused from 27/4/2014 till 27/7/2015 enticed the victim girl from the custody of guardian i.e. No. complainant Rameshchandra Gaud and took her away with intention to commit crime and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 363 of the Indian Penal Code ? 2] Does prosecution prove that, on the above date, place and time, the accused induced victim girl from the house of complainant with intention that she may be forced for No. illicit intercourse and thereby committed offence punishable under section 366 of the Indian Penal Code ? 3] Does prosecution prove that, the accused during the aforesaid period place and time, committed rape on the victim minor girl and thereby No. committed offence punishable under section 376 of the Indian Penal Code ? 4] Does prosecution prove that, the accused during the aforesaid period place and time, committed No. penetrative sexual assault on the victim girl ageing about 15 years 5 Spl. C. No. 165/2015 [ Judg. ] POINTS FINDINGS old and thereby committed an offence punishable under sections 4, 8 and 12 of the Prevention of Children from Sexual Offences Act ? 5] What order ? Accused is acquitted. REASONS 7] POINT NOS.1 TO 4 :­ In the present case complainant maternal uncle of the victim girl has deposed before the court that his niece i.e. victim girl married with accused boy and now they are enjoying their happy marital life and also begotten one child out of their wedlock. On this background the prosecution case proceeded resulted into compromise outside the court by resiling from their statement. I have to consider the peculiar fact in which the material witnesses turned hostile. 8] It reveals from the allegations of the FIR that, the accused and the victim are originally hails from Jaunpur­ District. They developed love and affection in their tean age. Their relations were not agreed by the family members. The victim girl was sent to the house of her maternal uncle's house at Kalyan. However the lover boy followed her by coming to Mumbai and residing at uncle's house in the vicinity of Nalasopara. They again joint each other and stayed together till the arrest of accused. Till then they have 6 Spl. C. No. 165/2015 [ Judg. ] begotten one child. Therefore the complainant maternal uncle solemnised their marriage again and on this background he deposed before the court saying nothing incriminating against the accused. 9] It is pertinent to note while considering the prosecution under section 363 and under the provisions of POCSO the consensual sex has no relevance. However in the present case the girl was ageing about 15 years and was having age of understanding the consequences. Our Hon'ble High Court in the recent cases took a view that if the girl is enough mature to understand the consequences of her consensual physical relations with the partner then the boy cannot be held alone guilty of having sex with the girl though not attended majority. Considering the particular fact of this case in which the lover couple got married with each other irrespective of their age hurdle I find no propriety to punish them for their act when they are enjoying their happy marital life with each other. Moreover the family members of both the families are also having no grievance about their act at this stage. In such situation no incriminating evidence is adduced on record. Therefore I have no alternative but to answer point nos.1 to 4 in negative. 10] POINT NO. 5 :­ As I held above prosecution failed to prove necessary ingredients to prove the guilt of accused. Hence he is liable to be acquitted giving benefit of inadequate evidence 7 Spl. C. No. 165/2015 [ Judg. ] to prove the charge. In the result I answer point no.5 accordingly and proceed to pass following order :­ ORDER 1] Accused Akhilesh Harishchandra Mishra, age 23 years, R/of Hanuman Tekdi, Palghar, Taluka­Palghar, District­Palghar is hereby acquitted under section 235(1) of Cr.P.C. of the offence punishable under sections 363, 366, 376 of Indian Penal Code and under sections 3, 4 and 8 of Prevention of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act. 2] Accused is in Jail, he be released forthwith if not required in any other case/crime. 3] Seized property i.e. clothes of the victim and accused being worthless, be destroyed, after appeal period is over. 4] The accused is directed to furnish fresh P.B. of Rs.15,000/­. In compliance with the provisions of section 437(A) of Cr.P.C. to abide himself to appear before Appeallate Court in case of appeal is preferred by the prosecution. 5] Judgment pronounced in open Court. Kalyan Dt : 28/1/2016 [ S.P. Gogarkar ] Dist. Judge­3 & Addl. Sessions Judge, & Special Judge, Kalyan

1 BA No. 1837/2017 (Exh.1) CNR No. MHTH06­0004181­2017 ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN CRI. BAIL APPLN. NO. 1837/2017 CNR No. MHTH06­0004181­2017 1] The applicants/accused Manjunath Venkatesh Shetty and Satish Anand Shetty have moved present application to enlarge them on bail under Section 439 of Code of Criminal Procedure. 2] The applicants/accused case in brief is that, one Cr. No. I­715/2017 under secs. 370(2)(3) of IPC and under secs. 3, 4, 5 of PITA Act is registered with Manpada police station wherein the accused are involved to promote prostitution. Police have executed raid on 26/12/2017. They have seized some muddemal articles as well as the victim girls from the spot. Some of the accused were also arrested. At the instance of other accused it was transpired that the applicant No.2 is partner of that impugned Lodge and therefore his name is arrayed in the list of accused. The applicant No.1 is simply Waiter, but the police are trying to get custody of him. Now the investigation is almost completed. Nothing to be seized or investigated with the accused. The applicants have attended the police station as directed. The applicants are having no criminal antecedent. They are ready to furnish bail and abide the conditions, if any imposed by the court. 3] Learned APP and I.O. have resisted the application by filing their say at Exh.6. It is their contention that, other 2 BA No. 1837/2017 (Exh.1) CNR No. MHTH06­0004181­2017 three accused have been arrested on the spot, while doing the business of prostitution in the said Lodge. Police have caught raid handed with some articles as well as victim girls. Police have investigated the matter wherein it was transpired that the present applicants are having very role and they have played it. They are beneficiaries of the said crime. It is one of the anti­ social offence and they are having definite connection with the alleged crime. The offence itself is serious. Therefore, they urged to reject the application. 4] At the outset and on bare perusal of the FIR as well as some police statements which are submitted by I.O., it can be easily gathered that, the other three accused were caught raid handed wherein at Sai Shraddha Lodge the prostitution, business was carried. It is not in dispute at this stage that some fo the victim girls were also recovered from that Lodge. Police have recovered muddemal amount also. In further investigation some of the accused have pointed out that the present applicants are having nexus with the alleged crime. Now police are intending to dig out the case whether there is any other victim girls which are playing at the hands of present applicants. When the present applicants i.e. applicant No.2 is partner of that Lodge and the applicant No.1 is the Waiter of that Lodge. It means they are having sure nexus with the alleged crime. The offence itself is serious and anti­social. In such circumstances and for proper investigation, I hold that, the applicants are not entitled for bail because their custodial 3 BA No. 1837/2017 (Exh.1) CNR No. MHTH06­0004181­2017 interrogation is very much necessary. Ultimately, the bail application deserves to be rejected. Consequently, I pass following order :­ ORDER Application stands rejected. Kalyan ( N. M. Waghmare ) Date :­14/2/2018 Dist. Judge­2 & Addl. Sessions Judge, Kalyan

Special Case No.177/2015 Exhibit No.25 of an offence punishable under Section 376 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 4 and 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] The prosecution case in short is that­ The complainant Lalita Santosh Rathod, aged 30 years, is residing with his husband i.e. accused Santosh alongwith one daughter and two sons at Subhash Nagar Zopadpatti, Badlapur Karjat Road, Badlapur (East). Accused used to do labour work as and when got or two days in a week. He used to drink liquor from that payment of labour work. On 26/09/2015 complainant had gone for her labour work and when she came back at about 07:00 p.m. at home, her daughter Sharda told her that accused had committed rape and accused had threatened to her daughter Sharda not to disclose said fact to anybody. Thereafter, she lodged complaint to the police station. Then, police wheels come into play and arrested the accused. The victim was minor. Police have prepared seizure panchanama of cloths and spot panchanama. They prepared muddemal receipt. The IO has recorded statements of witnesses. The victim was sent for medical examination and obtained medical certificate ..3/ ..3.. Atro. Special Case No.177/2015 Exhibit No.25 and after due completion of investigation it was transpired that the accused had committed rape and threatened to minor victim, therefore, the accused is chargesheeted. As the offence is triable by the Sessions Court, the case is committed to this Court. 3] After committal of the case, the charge was framed against the accused under Section 376 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 4 and 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, vide Exhibit 5. Its contents were read over and explained to the accused in his vernacular. He pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. His defence is that of total denial. 4] As there is no incriminating evidence against the accused, hence his statement under Section 313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is dispensed with. 5] Considering these pros and cons, following points arise for my determination. I have recorded my findings thereon for the reasons to follow­ SR. NOS. POINTS FINDINGS 1 Whether prosecution proves ..4/ ..4.. Atro. Special Case No.177/2015 Exhibit No.25 that on 26/09/2015 at about 12:00 p.m. to 01:00 p.m. at the house of accused, accused committed rape on his minor daughter­victim Sharda, aged about 11 years and thereby committed an offence punishable under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code ? .. In the negative. 2. Whether the prosecution proves that on the aforesaid date, time and place accused committed criminal intimidation by threatening victim with injury to her person with intent to cause her alarm and thereby committed an offence punishable under Section 506 of the Indian Penal Code? .. In the negative. 3. Whether the prosecution proves that the accused, on the aforesaid date, time and place, committed penetrative sexual assault on his minor daughter­victim Sharda, aged 11 years, and thereby committed an offence punishable under Section 4 of the Protection of Children ..5/ ..5.. Atro. Special Case No.177/2015 Exhibit No.25 from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 ? .. In the negative. 4. Whether the prosecution proves that on the aforesaid date, time and place, accused committed aggravated penetrative sexual assault on his minor daughter­victim Sharda aged 11 years, and thereby committed an offence punishable under Section 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 ? .. In the negative. 5. What order ? As per final order accused are acquitted. : REASONS : 6] I am going to discuss all the points together as they are interlinked with each other and it will facilitate me to adjudicate the matter at once. AS TO POINT NOS.1 TO 5 : 7] In order to bring home guilt of the accused, prosecution has examined in all three witnesses i.e. P.W­1 Lalita Santosh Rathod i.e. complainant (Exh.9), P.W.2­ ..6/ ..6.. Atro. Special Case No.177/2015 Exhibit No.25 Sharda Santosh Rathod i.e. victim and PW­3 Laxman Dhingana Sabale i.e. Investigating Officer (Exh.15). 8] It was the main allegation against the accused that on the alleged day, date and time the accused committed rape on victim­Sharda who is his daughter and threatened to her. 9] P.W.1­Lalita Rathod who is mother of victim and wife of accused stepped into the witness box. But she has not supported any of her allegations. She has denied alleged factum of rape and threatening to victim Sharda at the hands of accused. Learned A.P.P. has cross­ examined her at length but nothing came on record. Even she goes to the extent that she has not filed report to the police. She has denied the contents of the report. On the contrary, she has admitted in the cross­examination that her daughter Sharda had also not made statement before police and disclosed factum of rape to police. 10] In this sequence P.W.2­Sharda Santosh Rathod who is the victim in the present crime has also categorically denied the alleged incident and factum of rape and threatening at the hands of accused. Learned A.P.P. has cross­examined her at length but nothing came ..7/ ..7.. Atro. Special Case No.177/2015 Exhibit No.25 on record. On the contrary, the cross­examination reveals that on 26/09/2015 when she was present at her house, the accused had not committed rape with her. 11] P.W.3­Laxman Dhingana Sabale (Exh.15) is the Investigating officer in the present crime. He stated that on 26/09/2015 PSI Khade, complainant­Lalita had arrived to police station and complaint was lodged by the complainant that daughter of complainant was raped and threatened by the accused. He thoroughly investigated the matter and during investigation it was transpired that the accused had committed rape with his real girl Sharda. 12] When the complainant and victim have not supported the case, then testimony of Investigating Officer is futile to prove the guilt of accused. Evidence of Investigating Officer is always hearsay evidence and it cannot be admitted in evidence unless the complainant states factum of alleged incident. In this particular case both the P.W.1­Lalita and P.W.2­Sharda have not supported the prosecution case. Hence, prosecution cannot rely on the testimony of Investigating Officer. 13] In these set of circumstances, considering the evidence of prosecution witnesses, I find that these ..8/ ..8.. Atro. Special Case No.177/2015 Exhibit No.25 testimonies do not inspire any confidence to prove the guilt of accused. Once the complainant and victim have not supported the prosecution, then the prosecution has no legs to prove the guilt of the accused. Ultimately, I hold there is no iota of evidence and accused is entitled for acquittal. Consequently, I answer all the points accordingly and proceed to pass following order­ : ORDER : 1] Accused Santosh Dhansing Rathod is hereby acquitted vide section 235(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure of the offence punishable under Section 376 and 504 of the Indian Penal Code and under Section 4 & 6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] His bail bond should be continued for further six months. 3] Accused is in jail. He be set at liberty forthwith, if not required in any other offence. 4] Muddemal property if any, be disposed of as per rules, after appeal period is over. (N.M.Waghmare) Special Judge, under Protection of Children Kalyan from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, Date :­27/09/2016. Kalyan. ../

1 ORDER BELOW EXH.1 IN CRIMINAL ANTICIPATORY BAIL APPLICATION NO. 2011/2018 : (CNR.NO.MHTH­06004359­2018) 1] Read application and say of prosecution. Perused documents. Heard Ld.APP for State and Ld. Advocate for the applicant. 2] This application is filed U/Sec.438 of Cr.P.C. Crime is registered against this applicant Imran @ Abdullah Hafizulla Khan vide C.R.No.I­292/2018 in Ulhasnagar police Station for the offences punishable U/Secs.354, 323, 504 of I.P.C. As this accused apprehends his arrest by Ulhasnagar Police Station he has approached this court. Therefore, this application for anticipatory bail. 3] It is the case of the prosecution that on 17.11.18 at about 20.15 hours this complainant was proceeding from Ulhasnagar­2. In front of Activa Show Room, Zulelal Mandir Road, Ulhasnagar­1 this accused came near the complainant. Caught her hand and asked her why she did not talk with him. He asked her to come with him to Ambernath. Then the complainant rescued herself saying that she did not want to talk with him. At that time this accused gave slap to complainant and therefore crime is registered. 4] In this application it is the say of this applicant that he has committed no offence. Offence is false one. He and the 2 victim girl are in love with each other. They are on visiting terms to each other house. Now a days this accused stopped talks with complainant. Therefore in order to pressure this applicant this false complaint is filed. The love relations between complainant and accused came to the knowledge of parents of complainant. There were quarrel between complainant and her parents. At the instance of her parents complainant has lodged this false complaint. There is delay in lodging the complaint. This accused has not outraged the modesty of complainant. He never harassed her physically or mentally. This accused is taking education. Nothing is to be seized from him. Nothing is to be interrogated with him. He is ready to furnish bail. He will not abscond. He will not tamper prosecution evidence. Therefore, he prayed that he be released on bail. 5] This application is opposed by the prosecution contending that, name of this accused is mentioned in the complaint. If released on bail he may tamper prosecution evidence. There were friendly relations between complainant and accused for about two years. However, the complainant stopped the relations and avoided to talk with this accused. Therefore the accused caught hold her hand, abused her and beat her. This accused may abscond. He may tamper prosecution evidence. Therefore, prosecution prayed that application be rejected. 6] Considering the nature of offence nothing is to be recovered from this accused and nothing is to be interrogated 3 with him. If the prosecution admitted that there were relations between complainant and accused for about 2 years, it seems that now relations are dried and therefore there is possibility that, out of frustration complaint might have been lodged. In these facts and circumstances allowing this applicant to go behind bar is not just and proper and good. Applicant is a teen ager. He is taking education. His detention in jail may damage his carrier and future also. Therefore, it is just and proper to grant anticipatory bail to this accused. Hence, I pass the following order : :ORDER: 1) Application is allowed. 2) Ad­interim anticipatory bail granted to applicant/accused is hereby confirmed on same terms and conditions. 3) Inform concerned police station accordingly. Hence victim girl was taken by him towards the bungalow. At about 6­15 p.m. when informant was cleaning the fish, she heard the noise of shout of her daughter and hence she came on the road and saw her daughter and she told her mother that the said person is following her. Therefore she went towards bungalow of Deepak Temkar. At that time victim girl was in fear condition and two unknown persons were standing there. At the relevant time one Gamdiya madam came there. On questioning Gamdiya madam told to the informant that when she alongwith her guests was standing on the terrace of the bungalow, they saw that on the terrace of ....3/­ .. 3 .. Spl.C.No.2/2015 CNR:MHTH15­000068­2015 Judgment Exh.27 bungalow of Temkar, Bhagwan Raut was removing the knickers of victim girl and he also removed his half pant. Hence they raised shouts. As a result the girl ran towards the road and Bhagwan Raut also ran away. Therefore Gamdiya madam told to unknown persons to stop the girl. However, as the informant and her family are from other State, they did not go to police station to file the complaint. On 16/12/2014 the member of Mahila Dakshata Committee of Saphala by name Jijitai came to the house of informant and asked about the incident and hence she narrated the incident. Therefore said Jijitai told the informant to accompany her to file the report with police as they are supporting to her. Hence informant went to the police station and filed the report. On the basis of the report crime bearing registration No.I­69/2014 was registered against the accused. 3. The investigation was carried out by P.S.I. Madhukar Laxman Moule. He visited the spot of the incident and prepared the spot panchanama vide Exh.20. On 18/12/2014 he recorded the statements of witnesses and further ....4/­ .. 4 .. investigation was handed over to Dy.S.P. Bajbale who carried out the investigation and during investigation the statement of the victim girl under section 164 of Cr.P.C. came to be recorded. The video recording was also done while recording the statement of the victim girl. After due investigation charge­ sheet came to be filed against the accused. 4. On securing the presence of the accused I framed the charge at Exh.2. The particulars of the offence were readover to the accused in vernacular. The accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried hence plea is recorded at Exh.3. the statement of accused under section 313 of Cr.P.C. came to be recorded. The defence of the accused is that one witness by name Gamdiya has a bungalow adjacent to the bungalow of son­in­law of accused by name Temkar and there is boundary dispute and out of that a false case is filed against the accused. 5. Heard learned A.P.P. and learned advocate for the accused. Following points arise for my determination to which I have recorded my findings for the reasons to follow : POINTS FINDINGS 1. Whether the prosecution proves that In the on 08/12/2014 at about 18­15 negative. hours on the terrace of bungalow of son­in­law of accused he took the victim girl the daughter of complainant with intention to disrobe her compelling her to be naked ? ....5/­ .. 5 .. Spl.C.No.2/2015 CNR:MHTH15­000068­2015 Judgment Exh.27 POINTS FINDINGS 2. Whether the prosecution proves that In the on the same date and at the same negative. time and place the accused committed sexual assault on the minor daughter of the complainant aged about 11 years by removing her knickers with sexual intent which involves physical contact without penetration ? 3. Whether the prosecution proves that In the on the same date and at the same negative. time and place the accused committed aggravated sexual assault on the minor girl of the age of 11 years by removing her knickers ? 4. Whether the prosecution proves that In the on the same date and at the same negative. time and place the accused committed sexual harassment on the minor victim girl aged about 11 years with sexual intent ? 5. What order ? As per final order. REASONS 6. The learned A.P.P. submitted that the accused under the pretext of giving a fruit i.e. Guava to the victim girl took her to the terrace on the bungalow of his son­in­law and there at he removed the knickers of the girl and also removed his ....6/­ .. 6 .. knickers with intent to sexually assault the victim girl. At that time the witness by name Ravikanta Gamdiya saw the incident and therefore she is the best eye witness to the incident. Hence on the basis of that witness the prosecution has proved the guilt of the accused. 7. The learned advocate for accused submitted that the informant as well as the victim girl have not supported the prosecution case. The panch witness has also not supported in respect to the spot panchanama. The only witness who supported the prosecution case is the Ravikanta Gamdiya P.W.4. However, the witness has a bungalow near the bungalow of son­in­law of accused and there is boundary dispute hence accused has been falsely implicated in this case. So also he submitted that there are material contradictions in the evidence of said Ravikanta Gamdiya and therefore on the basis of her evidence only without corroboration the accused cannot be held guilty. 8. To prove age of the girl, the prosecution has brought on record the character certificate vide Exh.27 of Rajguru H.M.Pandit Vidyalaya, Saphale wherein victim girl was studying. It shows that the date of birth of the girl is 29/05/2003. The alleged incident occurred on 08/12/2014. It means at the relevant time the girl was aged about 11 years. Therefore there is no doubt that the girl was a minor girl at the time of incident. ....7/­ .. 7 .. Spl.C.No.2/2015 CNR:MHTH15­000068­2015 Judgment Exh.27 As to Point No.1 to 4 :­ 9. P.W.1 Shakuntala Shyamdhar Prajapati the mother of victim girl has stated that on the day of incident the victim girl returned from the school and she went to play outside. She went in the 'Char­bungala' to play there. Thereafter she has denied happening of anything with her girl. Thus she has not supported the prosecution case. Hence she has been cross examined by the learned A.P.P. however nothing has been elicited in her cross examination which is helpful to the prosecution. On the contrary in her cross examination by learned advocate for accused the informant has stated that Gamdiya Madam P.W.4 came in her house and told about the incident and hence she asked her daughter as to what had happened, however nothing was told by his daughter and after 5 to 6 days of the incident P.W.4 Gamdiya Madam alongwith some other ladies came to her and threatened her to file the complaint hence she went to the police station and filed the complaint. 10. P.W.2 the victim girl has stated that she returned at about 6­00 p.m. from the school and she went out of the house to play, at that time accused who was called as Kaka by her sitting in the shop of his father and he forcibly took her in order to offer her the Guava. Thereafter the victim girl also not stated anything as to what happened. In her cross ....8/­ .. 8 .. examination by the learned A.P.P. she has disclosed nothing about the incident. In cross examination by learned advocate for accused, she has denied that accused took her forcibly to offer her the Guava. Thus the victim girl herself has not supported the prosecution case. 11. P.W.3 Nilam Gajanan Jadhav was the Surpanch of Village Saphale at the relevant time. According to her she came to know about the incident on 16/12/2014 from one Kunda Vartak the member of Mahila Dakshta Committee. However, according to her she did not pay heed considering it as a rumor. Further she has stated that in her presence and presence of member of Mahila Dakshata Committee statement of girl was recorded. However, in her cross examination she has stated that she knows the accused since prior to the incident and accused was bearing good character and regarding the incident the information was first communicated to one Gamdiya Madam P.W.4. She further has stated that on the basis of information received from Gamdiya Madam, information was given to the police and on the basis of that information complaint was also filed with police. Thus it seems that the witness has not supported the prosecution case and according to her the complaint was filed on the basis of information given by one Gamdiya Madam i.e. P.W.4. 12. P.W.4 Ravikanta Gamdiya is the important witness. According to her she was present in the terrace of her ....9/­ .. 9 .. Spl.C.No.2/2015 CNR:MHTH15­000068­2015 Judgment Exh.27 bungalow alongwith some guests and enjoying the tea at the terrace. At that time she heared the noise from nearby house of Deepak Temkar and hence she enquired as to who is there and at that time she saw that underwear of the girl was removed and one old person was there i.e. father­in­law of Deepak Temkar and the accused was also removing his underwear. At that time the girl was shouting. This is the evidence of the witness Gamdiya regarding alleged incident. However, in her statement recorded by police she has stated that when she saw towards the terrace the accused was removing the knickers of the victim girl and he had already removed his underwear. However, in her oral evidence she has stated that the underwear of the girl was already removed and accused was found removing underwear. Therefore there is material contradiction which is putforth by the learned advocate for accused in cross examination of this witness. It is to be noted here that in the F.I.R. lodged by the informant the mother of victim girl, there is mention that Gamdiya Madam was standing on the terrace of her bungalow and she saw about the incident and she alongwith her guests shouted. On the contrary it is the evidence of witness Gamdiya that she was enjoying the tea on the terrace by sitting and she heared the shouting of the girl. Moreover, I would like to mention here that Gamdiya P.W.4 has admitted in her cross examination that despite the witnessing the incident she ....10/­ .. 10 .. herself did not file the complaint with police. On the contrary it is the evidence of informant that after 5 to 6 days of the incident Gamdiya Madam alongwith some other ladies came to her and threatened her to file the complaint. It is to be noted here that the incident occurred on 08/12/2014 whereas the complaint came to be filed on 17/12/2014. Therefore the complaint is filed by delay of about 4 to 5 days. Moreover, as P.W.1, 2 and 3 have not supported the prosecution case, the evidence of the P.W.4 Gamdiya cannot be accepted without any corroboration. So also there are material contradiction in her evidence. 13. P.W.5 Swapnil Digambar Prabhudesai is the photographer and he has carried out the video shooting of the F.I.R. recorded as well as the statement recorded of the victim girl. So also he has produced the C.D. prepared by him before the police. The said C.D. has been produced on record, however it is without the certificate as required under section 65­B of the Indian Evidence Act, therefore though the statement of victim girl came to be recorded and C.D. has been prepared, it cannot be accepted. 14. P.W.6 Kisan Vasant Patil the witness for spot panchanama has not supported the prosecution case. P.W.7 Madhukar Laxman Moule, P.S.I. who carried out the initial investigation has stated that he visited the spot of the incident and prepared spot panchanama vide Exh.20. So far as the ....11/­ .. 11 .. Spl.C.No.2/2015 CNR:MHTH15­000068­2015 Judgment Exh.27 situation on the spot is concerned, the evidence of this witness can be believed because his evidence is direct evidence so far as the situation on the spot is concerned. However, nothing has been recovered or seized from the spot except there was alleged presence of the victim girl and accused. This witness has stated that the F.I.R. and the statement of victim girl was not recorded in his presence. Therefore there is no corroboration to the evidence of this witness as the statement of victim girl was not recorded in his presence. The prosecution despite opportunities failed to examine another investigation officer Dy.S.P. Bajbale. Under such circumstances the evidence on record is not trustworthy and sufficient to connect the accused with the alleged offence. The evidence of P.W.4 is having material contradictions and not corroborated by evidence of any other witness including victim girl. Under such circumstances in my opinion the prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubts. Therefore I answer my findings to point Nos.1 to 4 in the negative. Hence, I acquit the accused and proceed to pass following order. ORDER 1] The accused Bhagwan Manik Raut is hereby acquitted for the offence punishable under Section 354­B of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 8,9 punishable under Section 10 and 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act,2012 vide ....12/­ .. 12 .. section 235(1) of Cr.P.C. 2] The bail bonds of the accused shall stand cancelled. 3] The accused to furnish P.B. and S.B. of Rs.15,000/­ in compliance of section 437(A) of Cr.P.C. During investigation, it was revealed that accused enticed the victim-girl and committed sexual assault on her and 2 Bail No.09/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) therefore, provisions of Section 376 of I.P.C. were added alongwith the provisions of the P.O.C.S.O. Act. 4] The learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant/accused is falsely implicated. She submitted that victim-girl herself accompanied with the accused, as they were love affair and they performed the marriage in the temple. She further submitted that initially their marriage was not accepted by the family of the victim-girl and therefore, false F.I.R. was registered. She further submitted that now parents of the accused and victim-girl accepted their marriage. The accused is young boy of 22 years. He has no antecedents and ready to abide by any conditions imposed by the Court and prayed that accused be released on bail. 5] Per contra, the learned A.P.P. opposed the application submitting that the victim-girl is minor, aged 13 years and therefore, her consent is no consent. The investigation is in progress. There are chances of tampering of the witnesses and prayed for rejection of the application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R. it appears that 13 years minor daughter of the informant was found missing and therefore, the offence of kidnapping was registered on 17.11.2015. Thereafter, after about a month, the victim-girl was found in the custody of the accused. During the investigation, it was transpired that 3 Bail No.09/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) the accused enticed her away and performed the marriage and established physical relations with her. Though, the Ld. Counsel for the applicant made a innocent statement that the victim-girl is married with the accused and her family has also accepted their marriage, however, the fact remains that the victim-girl is only of 13 years and the consent of the minor is no consent in the eyes of law. Thus, there is serious allegation and the investigation is still in progress and therefore, it is not a fit case and proper stage to release the accused on bail. Hence I pass following order. ORDER The application stands rejected. Thane. sd/- Date : 27.01.2016 (Ms. U.M. Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act), Thane.

--1-- ORDER BELOW EXH. 25 IN SESSION CASE NO.224/2016 CNR NO.MHTH01­004935­2016 This is a second bail application filed on behalf of accused Sagar Waman Malavkar for releasing on bail under section 439 of Cr. P.C for the offence under section 302, 376 and 177 of Indian Penal Code. 2. It is contended that after rejection of the first bail application there is change in circumstance that there is no prima facie case or evidence of rape upon deceased. Postmortem report is silent on the point of rape. There is no direct evidence that the victim and accused last seen together. Prima facie case shows that deceased committed suicide due to depression. 3. Investigating Officer has given say at Exh.27. It is contended that accused had love affair with deceased Sharmila Kanti Pawar. On 27.03.2016 at about 1.00 a.m., in mid­night the accused taken her in jungle area at Shilottar village and committed sexual intercourse with her. The deceased insisted him to do marriage with her. The accused stated her that he cannot marry her because he has married and having two children. On that ground there was quarrel between them. So accused throttled the deceased with odhani and made a scene that she has committed suicide by hanging. The accused hanging body to one tree. 4. It is contended that offence is serious and there is strong prima facie case. Medical certificate of postmortem report shows that the reason of death is asphyxia due to --2-- throttling. There are witnesses who had deposed that accused and deceased were together in the night when incident took place. There are witnesses who deposed that there was love affair between accused and deceased. The accused informed to his wife that the deceased had committed suicide by hanging. There was frequent chatting on mobile phone between accused and deceased. 5. I heard Ld. Counsel on behalf of the accused. He relied upon decision in case of Babu Singh and others V/s. The State of Utter Pradesh AIR 1978 Supreme Court 527 and Laxman Irappa Hatti and another V/s. State of Maharashtra 2004(2) Bom. C.R (Cri)525. 6. I heard Ld. APP on behalf of prosecution. 7. At present trial has commenced. Charge is framed against accused. One witness has also examined. First bail application was also made by the accused after filing of the chargesheet. That was rejected by this court on merit below Exh.3 on 09.02.2017. At that time all the papers in the charge­ sheet were available and they were perused by the Ld. Counsel on behalf of the accused. So facts mentioned in this application are not newly discovered, therefore, there is no change in circumstance at all after rejection of the first bail application. Exh.3. 8. Trial is commenced. There is strong prima faice case made out. There are eye witnesses. There is also strong circumstantial evidence. The medical evidence is also prima facie shows reason of death is asphyxia due to throttling. So --3-- there is no case made out to release the accused on bail. The offence under section 302 of IPC is punishable with death or imprisonment which may extent to life. So considering all these aspects the accused is not entitled to be released on bail. .. 1 .. Anti Bail 54/2015 (Ord.Exh.1) Order below Exh.1 in Anticipatory bail appln. 54 of 2015 This application is filed by the applicant Sunil Sabhajit Singh for his release on bail under section 438 of Cr.P.C. in connection with C.R.No.I­570/2014 registered at Vartaknagar police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 420, 406, 506, 34 of I.P.C. It was contended and argued that the applicant apprehends his arrest in this crime which is registered on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant in collusion with other accused persons represented the complainant and witnesses to make available flat at Nalasopara in cheaper price and then induced them to give amount of Rs.1,75,000/­ but did not give them flat and when the complainant demanded for money back, accused refused to give them money back and cheated the complainant and also threatened not to demand the money back. It is further contended and argued that the applicant is the elder brother of main accused Amitkumar Singh and therefore he has been falsely implicated in this crime. It is further contended and argued that the F.I.R. is lodged against one Ranjeet Singh and Amitkumar Singh only. It is further contended and argued that the dispute between the parties is of civil nature. It is further contended and argued that looking to the facts and circumstance of this case the custodial interrogation of the applicant is not required. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if he is released on bail, he will co­operate with the investigation and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on anticipatory bail. .. 2 .. Anti Bail 54/2015 (Ord.Exh.1) 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution and it was contended and argued that the applicant in furtherance of common intention with other accused persons represented the complainant to make available flat at Nalasopara in cheaper price and then they showed one flat under construction in one building at Nariyanagar, Moregaon, Nalasopara (E) to the complainant and induced her to give amount of Rs.1,75,000/­. It is further contended and argued that the accused persons accepted amount of Rs.1,75,000/­ from the complainant but did not give her flat in cheaper price and when the complainant demanded the money back, accused persons warned her not to demand the money or even the flat and also threatened her of dire consequences. It is further contended and argued that in same fashion the accused persons have cheated other witnesses namely Anarkali Nishad, Nirmala Prajapati and Miradevi Nag and misappropriated the amount. It is further contended and argued that looking to the nature of offence and to do thorough investigation in this crime, custodial interrogation of the applicant is necessary. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the the complainant and prosecution witnesses. It is further submitted that possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence and even he being absconding cannot be ruled out. It is therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on anticipatory bail. 3] At first place it has to be mentioned that alongwith main application the applicant/accused also filed application for .. 3 .. Anti Bail 54/2015 (Ord.Exh.1) interim protection on the ground that the hearing of the main application and order thereon would take time and therefore applicant be granted interim protection. However, it has to be mentioned that other accused in this crime have also filed application for bail and said applications are on today's board for orders and for that purpose the papers of investigation in this crime are already available. In such circumstance since the papers are available for perusal, the main application itself is finally heard and is being decided by this order. 4] As is clear the offence charged against the applicant/ accused is of very serious nature under section 420, 406, 506, 34 of I.P.C. Then, though, as rightly submitted on behalf of applicant that the present applicant is not seen to be F.I.R. named accused and a careful perusal of F.I.R. reveal that the name of the present applicant is not mentioned therein, it has to be mentioned that the complaint is in regard to cheating by builder and it is alleged that accused Ranjeet Singh introduced the complainant to one Amit Kumar Singh as a builder and then, it is alleged that accused Amit Kumar Singh also represented that he would make flats available to them at cheaper rate and thereby induced them to pay the amount. Then, as is further clear during the investigation the name of the present applicant is alleged to have revealed to be the builder and main culprit behind the crime and therefore in the second remand report the name of the applicant/accused is mentioned as a wanted accused. 5] It is material to mention that from the investigation .. 4 .. Anti Bail 54/2015 (Ord.Exh.1) papers which are already available for perusal reveal that it is the present applicant who is seen to be the builder and not only signed the agreement to sell but also signed the receipts of accepting the amount from the complainant and event the cheques. Even it appears that the present applicant alognwith his brother Amit Kumar Singh had entered into an agreement with the complainant and received the money by saying that the construction work is undertaken by them but later on when the question of possession or delivery of flat arose, they threatened the complainant. 6] Then, though, as argued on behalf of accused the investigation is seen to be related to mainly documentary evidence, looking to the nature of offence and the manner in which it is seen to have been committed further investigation into the matter with the help of accused appear to be necessary, that is particularly in the light of the fact that the present applicant/accused was not found to be available even for enquiry purpose and was absconding. 7] The submissions on behalf of applicant that balance amount is not paid by the complainant and therefore there was no question of handing over possession etc. is concerned, on one hand, that aspect will have to be investigated into and on the other hand, in the complaint itself it is specifically mentioned that the applicant/accused alongwith his brother Amit Kumar Singh had entered into transaction in regard to same flat with 2 – 3 other persons and in that respect also it is necessary that the matter be thoroughly investigated into with the help of applicant/accused and .. 5 .. Anti Bail 54/2015 (Ord.Exh.1) therefore the submissions on behalf of applicant/accused that custodial interrogation of the applicant is not necessary, cannot be said to be sustainable. 8] Even the submissions on behalf of applicant/accused that he is ready to abide by conditions and co­operate police in investigation also do not appear to be appealing and convincing for the reason that he is the main builder and appear to have signed the agreement to sell and even the receipts for acceptance of amount. Still he appear to have come up with the case that he has no connection with the said transaction and it is his brother who is the F.I.R. named accused who is the main brain behind this crime etc. The apprehension expressed by the prosecution that the applicant may abscond if released on anticipatory bail, appear to be having some substance in the light of the fact that the accused was absconding. Even the possibility of the applicant threatening the complainant and witnesses and creating danger to their life cannot be ruled out. In such circumstance in order to do thorough investigation into the matter, the custodial interrogation of the applicant appear to be necessary in this case. 9] In view of all above discussion I am of the view that this is not a fit case wherein the applicant can be said to be entitled to be released on bail. In the result I pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is rejected. Date : 08.01.2015. (Mrs.V.V.Virkar) Additional Session Judge­1, Thane.
