.. 1 .. Bail No. 35/2016 (Order below Exhibit 1) Criminal Bail Application No. 35 of 2016 Idris Mohmad Kadir Shah .. Applicant versus The State of Maharashtra Through Kalwa P.S. .. Non­applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 By this application the applicant is seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. who was arrested on 14.11.2015 by Kalwa Police Station in connection with C.R.No.I­393/2015 registered for an offence punishable under section 376(2)(k) of I.P.C. and section 4, 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as P.O.C.S.O. Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Mr. R.S.Pawal for the applicant/accused and learned A.P.P. Mrs. Navale for State. I.O. present. Case diary produced. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 24.10.2015 at the instance of the informant/victim­girl aged about 15 years with an indictment that since 14.09.2015 to 22.10.2015 the accused who is stepfather of the victim­girl, four times .. 2 .. Bail No. 35/2016 (Order below Exhibit 1) attempted to commit sexual assault on her and misappropriated amount of ₹ 10,000/­ and gold ring. 4] The learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant­accused is falsely implicated. He submitted that the victim­girl is daughter of informant from her first husband. Thereafter, she married with the present applicant­accused. The applicant was looking after the victim­girl as his own child and the allegations are totally false. Though the allegations of repeated attempts were made, same was never disclosed to anybody. There is no penetrative assault and therefore, provisions of P.O.C.S.O. Act will not attract. There are no criminal antecedents of the applicant. He is ready to abide any conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing him on bail. 5] Per contra, the learned A.P.P. opposed the application submitting that the F.I.R. speaks in volume. In the F.I.R. the act of the accused who is stepfather of the victim­girl is clearly mentioned. She further submitted that the medical certificate supports case of prosecution and hymen appears to be torn. She submitted that it is not case of attempt to rape but it is case of rape and the accused did the act five times. The investigation is in progres. There are chances of tampering with witnesses and prayed for rejection of application. .. 3 .. Bail No. 35/2016 (Order below Exhibit 1) 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R. and police papers, it appears that the accused who is stepfather of the victim­girl aged 15 years, since 14.09.2015 to 22.10.2015 five times attempted to commit sexual assault on the victim­girl whenever informant/mother of the victim­girl was not at home. The medical certificate reveals hymen was torn at 3, 6, 9 o'clock position and clear history about sexual assault by stepfather for five times is given. Thus, there appears prima facie case against the accused. The learned counsel for applicant­accused placed reliance on the judgment in the case of Damodhar Himtaji Dongre vs. The State of Maharashtra – 2015 ALL MR (Cri) 4825 wherein it is held that provisions of P.O.C.S.O. Act will not attract as the prosecution case is not of penetrative assault. However, the facts of said case are totally different than the facts in the case in hand and the investigation is still in progress. As the accused is stepfather of the victim­girl, the apprehension of the learned A.P.P. about tampering of witnesses is well founded. Hence, no case is made out for release the applicant­accused on bail. I, therefore, pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is rejected. Thane. Date : 18.01.2016. (Ms.U.M.Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act), Thane.

Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­000068­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 1/14 Received on : 01.01.2014 Registered on : 02.01.2014 Decided on : 01.10.2018 Duration : 4Ys. 9Ms. 0 Ds. IN THE COURT OF D.J.­1 & ADDL. SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE. (Presided over by Hemant M. Patwardhan) Special Case (POCSO) No. 1/14 Exh.No. State of Maharashtra, (Naupada Police station) ..Complainant V/s. 1] Sachin Babu Choudhari @ Ketan. Age 27 years, R/at. Trimurti Chawl, R.No.1, Kamagar Hospital Road, Ramchandra Nagar no.1, Wagle Estate, Thane ..Accused Appearance:­ APP Mr. Londhe for the State. Advocate Mr. E. H. Phad for accused JUDGMENT (Delivered on this 1st day of October 2018) Accused Sachin Babu Choudhari @ Ketan was facing trial under sections 354, 509 of Indian Penal Code read with Sec. 8 and 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 on following facts. 1 OF 11 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­000068­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 1/14 1] That on 02.10.2013 at about 18.30 hrs at Gaondevi Co­ operative Housing society, room no.201. II floor, Namdev Wadi, Panchpakhadi, Thane (W) within the jurisdiction of Naupada Police station has used criminal force on victim intending to outrage her modesty and at the same time had made some sound intending same be heard by her. According to allegations as victim was minor at the relevant time by the said acts accused has also committed sexual assaults on the victim. Hence, on the complaint lodged by mother of victim offence punishable under aforesaid sections came to be registered against accused. On completion of investigation he was charge­sheeted. 2] My learned predecessor was pleased to frame charge below Exh. 5 and has certified that contents of said charge were read over and explained to accused in vernacular. Accused pleaded not guilty and claim to be tried. His defence was of total denial and that it was the mistaken identity by the complainant and victim girl. 3] On the basis of aforesaid defence prosecution with an intention to bring guilt of the accused at home has examined, her mother, victim's girl friend and I.O. as witness no. 1 to 4 respectively. After deposition of witnesses, arguments of rival advocates were heard. At the time of arguments learned P.P. has categorically pointed out that not only victim but also her mother and her friend has supported and corroborated her version. According to learned P.P. victim has categorically deposed as to how the accused has used 2 OF 11 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­000068­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 1/14 criminal force against her intending to outrage her modesty. Therefore, according to learned P.P. her sole testimony is sufficient to prove the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt. He has then pointed out that her girl friend had seen accused hurriedly leaving her house and it was the allegations of victim that she has narrated the incident to her friend. Thus, as said friend has categorically corroborated the version the same has to be believed. He has then pointed out that investigating officer has then properly conducted investigation to forward charge­sheet against accused person. He has therefore, requested to convict the accused under all said section with which accused was charged. 4] Per contra, learned defence advocate Mr. Phad has open his argument with submissions that it is mistaken identity of the accused person. According to him complaint was lodged against unknown person and the witnesses have admitted that none of them knew accused prior to the incident. Therefore, according to him first of all investigating officer was required to establish identity and for said purpose identification parade was very necessary. He has then pointed out that allegations are made against accused about having committed offence under sections 4,8 and 12 of POCSO Act there is no document on record to show that victim was really minor at the relevant time of incident. He has then pointed out the admission of I.O. that he has neither seized the birth certificate nor has collected any other document to show that victim was really minor at the relevant time. According to submissions there are contradictions in 3 OF 11 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­000068­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 1/14 the statements of witnesses thus, the said contradictory statements of witnesses cannot be believed. Hence, according to him depositions before the court are not sufficient to prove the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt. He has therefore, requested the court to acquit the accused from all the allegations. 5] After having heard the rival advocates, following points arise for my consideration and I record my findings against each of them for the reasons noted below:­ S.N. Points Findings 1] Does the prosecution prove that accused on 02.10.2013 at about ..In the negative. 18.30 hours at Gaondevi CHS, R.No.201, IInd floor, Namdev Wadi, Panchpakhadi, Thane (W), used criminal force to daughter of complainant viz. victim, a minor age­14 years, intending to outrage her modesty and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 354 of Indian Penal Code ? 2] Does the prosecution prove that accused on the same date, time and ..In the negative. place intending to insult the modesty of daughter of complainant viz. victim, a minor age­14 years, by made some sound intending that the same shall be heard by her and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 509 of Indian Penal Code ? 3] Does the prosecution prove that accused on the same date, time and ..In the negative. place, committed sexual assault on daughter of complainant viz. victim, a minor age­14 years and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 8, 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012? 4] What order ? Accused is acquitted as per final order. REASONS As to point nos. 1 to 4 :­ 6] All these points are interlinked with each other and are 4 OF 11 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­000068­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 1/14 considered at once. In the instant case prosecution has alleged that accused has not only used criminal force against victim with intention to outrage her modesty but also has made certain sounds with intention of same being heard by the victim and at the same time according to allegations as at the time of incident the deceased was minor, provisions of POCSO were also added in the allegations to say that accused has committed sexual assault on her. Prosecution was therefore, required to establish guilt of accused beyond reasonable doubt by consistent evidence. Prosecution has examined aforesaid four witnesses. Though they have deposed in terms of the prosecution's case they were cross­examined at length and certain admissions were obtained during said cross­examination. Hence, defence has argued that said contradictions are sufficient to discard evidence therefore, their depositions are require to be scrutinized in the light of said admissions and arguments advanced by the defence advocate. 7] As referred to above there are three fold allegations against accused in sense that there are allegations about outraging the modesty, making certain sound with intention to be heard by the victim and sexual assault punishable under POCSO. Before dealing with evidence and allegations under IPC section I would initially like to deal with allegations under section 8 and 12 of POCSO. The basic ingredients of POCSO is the victim must be a minor within the meaning of said section. For the said purpose prosecution was either required to establish particular fact by substantive evidence or by 5 OF 11 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­000068­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 1/14 documentary proof. On perusal of the record it is apparent that initially the age of the victim was shown as 14 years at the time of incident and she has claim to have completed 17 years at the time of incident without their being single avernments about date of birth either during victim's deposition or in the deposition of her mother. As per the admission of I.O. he has failed to obtain or collect any document which goes to establish that victim was minor within meaning of said section to attract provisions of section 8 or 12 of the said Act. Hence, in absence of either substantive evidence or evidence in the nature of document, it is difficult to accept that victim was really minor within the meaning of said section at the relevant time of incident. As per the defence of the accused she was more than 18 years on the date of incident. Thus, when the accused has disputed the age it was incumbent on the prosecution to prove that fact. However, in absence of either substantive or documentary evidence said fact cannot be said to be proved. Once court comes to the conclusion that victim was not minor as per the evidence brought before the court, then question of entertaining the allegations of prosecution under the said Act does not arise at all. 8] Now turning towards the allegation of prosecution under section 509 of IPC. On perusal of said section it is apparent that basic ingredients of the said section is some words or gestures are require to be made or there should be some exhibition of any object intending that said word or sound shall be heard or such gesture or object shall be seen by woman or introduced upon privacy of such 6 OF 11 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­000068­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 1/14 woman by such acts. Hence, prosecution was required to establish that with an intention to outrage modesty of a woman, accused has uttered some words or has made some gestures against victim. Though aforesaid three witnesses were examined none of said witness has uttered a single word about any words being uttered by the accused or any gestures of the accused with intention to insult the victim as defined under the said section. Thus, in absence of any whisper in any substantive evidence about basic ingredients of said section it is difficult to accept that accused has with said intention has committed the act punishable under section 509 of IPC. Thus, I do not hesitate to record my findings that prosecution has failed to establish that act as well. 9] Now turning to material allegation under section 354 of IPC. The basic ingredient of said section is use of criminal force with again intention of outraging modesty of victim. In the instant case accused has put forth the defence of his false implication by mistaken of identity and on various other grounds. On perusal of record it is apparent that victim in nutshell has alleged that accused after having allowed to enter the house sat by her side and has moved his hand on her body and as she opposed him and directed him to leave the house accused left the house. She has also narrated the fact that immediately after accused allegedly moved his hand over her body her friend Yogita had called her standing below her building and when the victim told Yogita to come to the house located on the second floor of the building, accused left the house. Though Yogita 7 OF 11 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­000068­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 1/14 was examined by prosecution she has narrated some different facts like when she went to the house of victim, victim was weeping, on being asked she has then narrated the facts to her and she has added that while entering the house of victim she had seen accused leaving her house hurriedly. Though the mother of victim has also stated same facts, however fact remains on record that she is not eye witness of the incident and was hear­say witness that too did not hear the facts initially directly from the victim but from her friend Yogita. Therefore, so far as allegations of the prosecution are concerned, material witnesses were victim and said Yogita. 10] Though there are serious allegations being made by the victim against accused person prosecution did not make any attempt to record her statement under section 164 of Cr.P.C. As that statement is not recorded the court has to look for corroboration of the facts narrated by her in substantive evidence. However, on perusal of her cross­examination it is apparent that neither she nor Yogita knew accused person prior to the incident. Even her mother has admitted that she was not knowing accused prior to the incident. Therefore, explanation was required atleast from the I.O. as to how he has traced out accused person without there being any independent witness examined by him who knew the accused person or had seen accused entering the building at the relevant time. Admittedly, though even the mother of the victim was not knowing accused person. From her complaint it is apparent that she has made complaint by referring the name of the accused without there being 8 OF 11 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­000068­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 1/14 any explanation as to how she came to know that name of the accused to referred in complaint. For the purposes of identification as none of the witnesses knew the accused prior to the incident, I.O. was required to conduct identification parade once suspects were apprehended by him in connection with this crime. However, there is apparently no identification parade was ever arranged to identify the accused. Therefore, though witnesses have claim that they have identified accused before the court it is difficult to accept without any explanation as to how they have identified the accused before the court. Needless to refer that all the witnesses have accompanied each other both while approaching towards police station and in the court. Hence, there is every likelihood of accused being shown to them before entering the dock therefore, only they have deposed before the court during substantive evidence that accused before the court is the same person. However, in absence of any explanation as to how identity of accused is established after accused has hurriedly left the victim's house at the relevant time it is difficult to accept that same person who has left the house of the victim is being arrested by concern police officer. 11] There are contradictory statements about the material facts in the deposition of the victim, her mother and independent witness Yogita. Victim has never herself stated before this court in her substantive evidence that she started weeping after the said incident or atleast while her friend Yogita entered her house, she has also nowhere stated that she has narrated any incident to Yogita or 9 OF 11 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­000068­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 1/14 that before said Yogita entered her house accused had left the house and while he was leaving the house Yogita had really seen him. In absence of any such facts being stated by victim it is difficult to say that Yogita had an occasion to see the accused persons leaving hurriedly from her house. Hence, said depositions of Yogita can be discarded. 12] Though Yogita has claimed that she had been to the victim for obtaining some book or textbook or notebook as the case may be, from the various admission it is apparent that victim was not student of the class where Yogita was attending such classes nor she was residing in the said area, so also from her admission it is apparent that on her way before the house of the victim other friends of Yogita are residing from whom she can very well obtain said notebook or textbook. Thus, for said reasons presence of said Yogita also become doubtful or unnatural. Said Yogita also admitted during her cross­examination that many material facts which she has stated in her deposition has not been stated before police and she is not able to narrate the reason about it. So is the case about victim. Thus, there appears to be material improvement in the depositions of said two witnesses. Hence, unless facts are properly corroborated, same need not be accepted. As already observed above though mother of the victim was examined she has never seen the incident personally nor victim has immediately disclosed it to her. She has actually heard the incident initially through Yogita but as observed above it is nowhere claim of victim herself that she has narrated the incident to 10 OF 11 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­000068­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 1/14 Yogita. Therefore, further allegation of the prosecution that Yogita had narrated it to her mother can hardly be believed. Having regards to these facts evidence brought before this court nowhere appears to be consistent, reliable and on the basis of such evidence holding accused guilty of such serious offence will be unfair. Hence, I do not hesitate to record my findings against point no.1 to 3 in negative, I proceed to pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused is acquitted from the offence punishable under sections 354, 509 of Indian Penal Code read with Sec. 8 and 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 2] Bail bonds of accused shall stand canceled. 3] Accused is directed to execute P.R. and S.B. of Rs.10,000/­ as per amended provisions of section 437(A) of Cr.P.C. and bonds so executed shall remain in force for the period of six months from the date of its execution. 4] Proceeding is accordingly closed. Thane (Hemant M.Patwardhan) Date: 01.10.2018 D.J.­1 & Additional Sessions Judge, Thane 11 OF 11

..1.. Spl.C. No.4/2014 (Exh.No. 41) Presented on :3.1.2014. Registered on :3.1.2014. Decided on :27.12.2017 Duration :03­Y 11­M 23­D IN THE COURT OF SPECIAL JUDGE (POCSO Act) THANE AT : THANE (Before R.N.Bawankar) Special Case No.4/2014 (CIS NO.010004/2014 EXH. No. 41. State of Maharashtra (Through Shantinagar Police station Bhiwandi) ... Prosecution VERSUS Sanjaykumar Bashdev Kachyoja, age 30 yrs., r/at Ramlakhan Chawl, Ghungatnagar, Kalyan Naka, near Petrol Pump, Bhiwandi, Thane. … Accused Offence punishable u/secs. 363, 354 I.P.C. & u/s 8 & 12 of POCSO Act. APPEARANCE : Ld. A.P. P. Smt. Moholkar for prosecution. Ld.Adv. Shri Kasale for accused. JUDGMENT (Delivered on 27th December 2017.) 1] Accused stands prosecuted by police station officer, Shantinagar Police Station, Bhiwandi for the charge of offences of kidnapping victim girl aged 6 years from lawful guardianship of her parents punishable u/s 363 I.P. C., using criminal force to victim with intent to outrage her modesty punishable u/s 354, for sexual assault u/s 7 punishable u/s 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act & for committing sexual harassment u/s 11 punishable u/s 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act (for short POCSO Act). ..2/- ..2.. Spl.C. No.4/2014 (Exh.No. 41) 2] In brief, it is the case of prosecution that informant Manju Vijayshankar Prajapati lodged the complaint on 6.10.2013 alleging that victim girl aged about 6 years is her daughter. On 6.10.2013 victim went out of house at 11.30 a.m. for playing. At 12.00 non when victim did not come, she came out of house in search of house and she did not find victim outside the house. She enquired with neighbours about victim but victim was not found. At about 1.30 p.m. one person brought victim to house. She enquired with him, thereupon he told his name as Rajkumar. He further told one person was taking girl by giving her ice cream to upper floor of one old building, Sainagar, Ashoknagar, Bhiwandi. He and other people went over the said building and saw that said person was putting frock of girl up and she was shouting. They caught hold said person and brought to the police station. Said girl told her address and therefore, he brought her to the house. Thereafter informant enquired with victim who told that nearby uncle who used to give eatable everyday came near her and told that he will give her ice cream and asked her to come with him. She went with him by walk. He gave her ice cream and took her to terrace of a building. When she was eating ice cream there, said uncle moved his hand on person and when he was putting her frock up, people gathered there. As she was crying, one person brought her to the house. Thereafter, alongwith husband and victim, informant went to police station. One person residing near her house was present in the police station. Police told his name as Sanjay Bashdev Kachyoja. 3] On the basis of complaint, Crime No.I­307/2013 for the offence punishable u/s 363, 354 of I.P.C. r/w S. 11 & 12 of POCSO Act was registered and API Y.R. Wayal carried out investigation. During investigation, he prepared spot panchanama and arrested accused ..3/- ..3.. Spl.C. No.4/2014 (Exh.No. 41) under panchanma. Further investigation was entrusted to P.I. Mr. Nimbalkar. He visted spot of incident. He recorded statement of victim and other witnesses. He collected birth certificate of victim and recorded statements of witnesses. On completion of investigation, submitted chargesheet before the Court against accused. 4] Charge Exh.12 was framed & explained to accused to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. His defence is that of total denial. 5] Considering the case of the prosecution following points arise for my determination and I have recorded my findings thereon for the reasons discussed below. POINTS FINDINGS 1 Does the prosecution prove that on 6.10.2013 in between 11.30 hours to 12.00 hours, opposite residence of Ramlakhan Chawl, Ghungatnagar, Kalyan Naka and at Sainagar Building No.3, Bhiwandi, accused kidnapped victim girl aged 6 years from lawful guardianship of her parents and No. thereby committed an offence punishable u/sec. 363 of I.P.C.? 2 Does the prosecution further prove that on the above mentioned date,time and place accused used criminal force to victim aged 6 years with intent to outrage her modesty No. and thereby committed an offence punishable u/sec. 354 of I.P.C.?? 3 Does the prosecution further prove that on the above mentioned date,time and place accused committed sexual assault on victim as per Sec. 7 punishable u/s 8 of PCSO Act? No. ..4/- ..4.. Spl.C. No.4/2014 (Exh.No. 41) 4 Does the prosecution further prove that on the above mentioned date,time and place accused committed sexual harassment on No. victim as per Sec. 11 punishable u/s 12 of PCSO Act? 5 What order ? As per final order. REASONS Points Nos. 1 to 4 : 6] All the points are interlinked to each other, hence in order to avoid the repetition of evidence they are clubbed together. 7] Prosecution examined in all 4 witnesses. P.W.1 Victim at Exh.19, PW 2 informant Manju at Exh.20, PW 3 Rajkumar/eyewitness at Exh.22 and PW 4 I.O. Mr. Nimbalkar at Exh.30. Then prosecution filed evidence closing pursis at Exh.32. Statement of accused recorded u/s 313 of Cr.P. C. is at Exh.33. Prosecution relied on documents viz. arrest panchanama Exh.23, spot panchanama Exh.24, photograph of building Exh.25, bonafide certificate Exh.26 & statement of victim Exh.31. 8] The Ld. APP submitted that at the time of incident, victim was 6 years old and she deposed before the Court as per the story of prosecution as on the day of Sunday when she was playing accused took her to terrace, sit on table, pick her frock up and moved his hand on her person. Therefore, the evidence of victim needs no corroboration. Inspite of that, PW3 Rajkumar who is independent eyewitness also supported to the case of prosecution and he took victim to her house and then victim narrated incident to her mother who lodged a report against accused. The evidence of I.O. is formal one. There is no material ..5/- ..5.. Spl.C. No.4/2014 (Exh.No. 41) omissions and contradictions in the prosecution evidence. The accused failed to bring any rivalry on record and as such, there is a presumption in favour of prosecution and thus, prosecution proved the case as per charge. 9] Per contra, the Ld. Counsel for accused vehemently submitted that prosecution failed to prove FIR by examining police station officer who reduced the same into writing. Secondly, the evidence of victim is not corroborated to her previous statement Exh.31. The evidence of Rajkumar is not trustworthy as he came to know about incident from one Shivaji More to whom, prosecution failed to examine. In the evidence of informant it is brought on record that since June 2013 there was quarrel between her husband and accused, which she refused. The contradiction in the evidence of informant is that, “though she stated to police that her daughter did not return home, then she went in her search and police brought her” but same was not mentioned in her FIR. The evidence of prosecution witnesses is not trustworthy and as such the prosecution failed to prove the charge beyond reasonable doubt and as victim is tutored, hence, accused is entitled for benefit of doubt. 10] It is to be noted that FIR of the crime is the vital document of prosecution as the police machinery put in motion on the basis of information mentioned in the FIR. So far as the present crime is concerned, the FIR came to be lodged by one Manju Vijayshankar Mishra on 6.10.2013 which bears the thumb impression and also bears the signature of station diary incharge. For the prosecution it is necessary to prove the FIR by examining the said station diary incharge but prosecution failed to do so. The Ld. defence Counsel vehemently ..6/- ..6.. Spl.C. No.4/2014 (Exh.No. 41) submitted that in any situation, person can state otherwise but no one forget the real name. In the present matter, PW 2 deposed her name as Manju Vijaynath Prajapati but in the FIR she mentioned her name as Manju Vijayshankar Mishra. Conveniently, I.O. recorded supplementary statement on 8.10.2013 only to rectify the name of her husband as well as surname. Thus, the doubt raised by the defence counsel that really complaint was lodged by PW 2 or not. When prosecution failed to examine the station diary incharge who recorded the FIR of informant then prosecution failed to prove the contents of FIR and that gives benefit to accused. 11] PW 1 victim categorically deposed that on the day of incident, it was Sunday and she was playing outside. That time, neighbouring uncle took her to 7 th floor by saying that he will give chocolate. He gave ice cream and when she was eating the same, that time, said uncle put her frock up and moved his hand on her person. She further deposed that at that time children playing below the building and some people came there and then beat that uncle. Thereafter, she went to home. Before adventing on her cross examination, it is necessary to consider the evidence of I.O. who deposed that he recorded statement of victim at Exh.31. On perusal of the same, it reveals that she stated that accused took her to the side of road and gave her ice cream and thereafter took her near one old building and told that he will give jeans pant and frock during Diwali Festival and asked her to come and to show her house. Taking her near one old building and offering of clothes for Diwali festival is totally missing in her deposition. Apart from that, she further stated that accused took her on the building. In the spot panchanama (which is admitted by accused) the ..7/- ..7.. Spl.C. No.4/2014 (Exh.No. 41) terrace is over the second floor of building. However, victim as well as informant deposed that accused took her to 7th floor. 12] The Ld. APP vehemently submitted that when the spot panchanama Exh.24 is admitted by accused then he has no right to deny its contents. On the contrary, the Ld. Defence counsel vehemently submitted that the evidence of victim as well as informant are contrary to the contents of spot panchanama. It is to be noted that when the evidence of victim and informant are contrary to the contents mentioned in the spot panchanama, then the two possibility are to be arrived, firstly, the facts mentioned in the panchanama are totally incorrect or secondly, victim as well as the informant have no knowledge about the facts mentioned in the panchanama and therefore, they are deferred to its contents. It is not the case of prosecution that accused took victim to 7th floor, therefore, the evidence of victim as well as the informant is not trustworthy and liable to be discarded on the count of spot. 13] It is to be noted that as per the case of prosecution, just after the incident, Rajkumar took victim to her house. But according to victim, after incident, she went to house and according to informant, police brought victim to house. Thus, the evidence of Rajkumar is not supported by victim and informant and as such, the evidence of Rajkumar is also under the shadow of doubt. The Ld. Defence counsel vehemently submitted that the evidence of Rajkumar is totally contradictory to the evidence of victim. According to Rajkumar, he alongwith his friend Shivaji More on 2 nd floor of building but according to victim, children playing below the building and some people came there. Secondly, according to Rajkumar, he saw that one half naked girl ..8/- ..8.. Spl.C. No.4/2014 (Exh.No. 41) weeping and she was holding ice candy, accused put down his pant and that girl was on his lap. But according to victim, when she was eating ice cream, accused put her frock up and he moved his hand on her person. When prosecution relied on Rajkumar as an eyewitness but victim herself has not stated to police or deposed before the Court that accused put down his pant and she was on his lap, then, it clearly shows that, his evidence is not supported to the evidence of victim, therefore, it is liable to be discarded. 14] In the cross examination of victim, it is brought on record that accused resides nearby her house and he used to give her eatables and used to take her for moving and that fact is known to her parents. These facts go to show that there were cordial relations between the family of informant and accused. The age of accused was 30 years and victim was 6 years of age therefore, there is gross difference between age of victim and accused. Under such circumstances, the defence putforth to the informant needs consideration. The informant denied that in June 2013 there was quarrel between her husband and accused so also at that time, Jamdar, the friend of accused was present there. However, said Jamdar was not examined as defence witness. 15] The evidence of victim seems to be focused on the point of main incident of moving hand by accused on her person. Thus, the submission of defence counsel that victim is tutored on the main point otherwise, she could have deposed about real spot and offering of clothes for Diwali festival. For want of consistency in the evidence of victim with her statement Exh.31, I am inclined to discard the testimony of victim. When the testimony of victim is discarded, then the presumption which is in favour of prosecution u/s 29 of the POCSO Act ..9/- ..9.. Spl.C. No.4/2014 (Exh.No. 41) is rebutted by accused. 16] So far as defence of accused is concerned, in the statement u/s 313 of Cr.P.C., accused failed to give cause of quarrel. For want of cause of quarrel and non examination of defence witness­Jamdar or accused himself, the defence putforth by accused seems to be improbable and failed to pass the test of preponderance of probability that on the count of previous quarrel, accused was falsely implicated in the crime. At the same time in view of the above discussion, the entire case of prosecution is also under the shadow of doubt. Therefore, it is just and proper to extend benefit to accused as prosecution and defence came with untrue facts and both versions have to be discarded. 17] The evidence on record is not sufficient to prove the charge levelled against accused beyond reasonable doubt for offence punishable u/s 363, 354 of IPC and the offence punishable u/s 8 & 12 of POCSO Act. With this discussion, I answer the point Nos. 1 to 4 accordingly and to proceed to pass the following order. : ORDER : 1] Accused Sanjaykumar Bashdev Kachyoja is hereby acquitted u/s 235 of Cr.P.C. from the charge of offence punishable u/s 363, 354 of I.P.C & u/s 8 & 12 of POCSO Act. 2] Bail bonds of accused shall stand cancelled. 3] Accused shall comply forthwith the provision U/Sec.437­A Cr.P.C. by furnishing fresh P.R. Bond of Rs.15,000/­ and S.B. of like amount. Dictated and declared in open Court. Place : Thane (R.N.Bawankar) Date : 27.12.2017 Special Judge (POCSO Act), Thane ../-

Presented on : 03.01.2015 Registered on : 03.01.2015 Decided on : 26.10.2017 Duration : 02Y. 09M.23D IN THE COURT OF SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE, AT : THANE. Presided over by S.C. Khalipe ­Additional Sessions Judge, Thane SPECIAL CASE NO.1/2015 Exh.No. The State of Maharashtra Through Mumbra Police Station. ….. Prosecution V/s. Kambar Ali Chandrabhan Ray Age 49 years, Occ: Caterer R/at. Saim Apartment, Room No.303, C wing, Kausa, Mumbra, Thane. ..... Accused Offence punishable under section 354(A)(1)(3), 292, 506 of Indian Penal Code and Section 8 of POCSO Act, 2012. Appearance: A.P.P. Smt.Vandana Jadhav for the prosecution. Advocate Shri.Patankar for the accused. :J U D G M E N T: (Delivered on this 26th Day of October , 2017) The case of the prosecution is that:­ On 22.03.2013 at about 5.30 p.m. the accused used criminal force to the minor daughter of the informant aged 9 years and outrage her modesty. It is also alleged that the accused showed her obscene video clip and threatened to kill her if she disclosed the incident and committed sexual assault upon her by touching her body. The mother of the victim lodged FIR in Mumbra police station on 26.06.2013 and C.R.No.I­491/2013 was registered under section 354(A)(1) (3), 292, 506 of Indian Penal Code and section 8 of POCSO Act, 2012. The investigation was done by Shri. D.D.Thokal PSI of Mumbra police station. He prepared panchanama of the spot, recorded statements of witnesses and sent charge­ sheet. 2. Charge was framed against accused at Exh.6 under sections 354(A)(1)(3), 292, 506 of Indian Penal Code and section 8 of POCSO Act, 2012. He pleaded not guilty 3. Considering the evidence on record following points arose for my determination. I have given its findings with reasons as under­ Sr.No Points Findings 1. Does prosecution prove that eight days In Negative prior to 22.03.2013 at Nasim Apartment, Room NO.303, C wing, Kausa Mumbra the accused used criminal force upon the minor victim aged 9 years with intention to outrage her modesty and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 354(A)(1)(3) of Indian Penal Code. 2. Does prosecution prove that eight days In Negative prior to 22.03.2013 at Nasim Apartment, Room NO.303, C wing, Kausa Mumbra the accused used criminal force upon the minor victim aged 9 years with intention to outrage her modesty and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 292 of Indian Penal Code? 3 Does prosecution prove that on the In Negative aforesaid date, time and place, accused committed criminal intimidation by threatening the victim aged 9 years to kill her and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 506 of Indian Penal Code? 4 Does prosecution prove that on the In Negative aforesaid date, time and place, accused committed sexual assault upon minor girl aged 9 years and thereby committed an offence punishable under seciton 8 of POCSO Act? 5. What order? As per final order REASONS AS TO POINT NOS.1 TO 5:­ 4. To prove the offence prosecution has examined mother of the victim at Exh.9, victim at Exh.10 and Investigating Officer Dilip Dashrath Thokal at Exh.13. 5. The informant and her daughter, the victim have not supported the case of prosecution and therefore, the case would not likely to be progressed, therefore, Ld. APP gave pursis Exh.14 for closing the evidence. 6. I perused the evidence of informant and her daughter. They have stated that nothing was happened with the victim aged 9 years. The informant has denied the contents in portion marked A and B in the FIR which was narrated to her during her evidence. The victim has also denied portion marked A in her statement. Investigating Officer has stated that she has done the part investigation. He had received investigation papers and birth date certificate of the victim after that he sent chargesheet. 7. The court has come to the conclusion that the prosecution could not prove any of the incriminating circumstances against the accused, therefore, statement under section 313 of Cr.P.C is dispensed with. 8. The prosecution could not prove the ingredients of the offences charged against the accused, therefore, no offence is proved against the accused. Hence, accused is liable to be acquitted. Therefore, I pass following order. ORDER 1. Accused Kambar Ali Chandrabhan Ray is acquitted under Section 235(1) of Cr.P.C. of the offence charged under sections 354(A)(1)(3), 292, 506 of Indian Penal Code and section 8 of POCSO Act, 2012. 2. Accused is directed to furnish P.B. and S.B. of Rs.15,000/­ (Rupees Fifteen Thousand Only) to comply provisions of section 437 (A) of Cr. P.C. 3. The Judgment is dictated and pronounced in open Court. Thane. (S.C. Khalipe) Date: 26.10.2017. Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

--1-- ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN CRIMINAL BAIL APPLICATION NO.43/2018 CNR NO. MHTH01­000091­2018 Applicant Omprakash Sitaram Chaudhary has applied for bail under section 439 of Cr. P.C in C.R.No.I­458/2017 registered in Navghar police station for the offence under section363, 364(A) of Indian Penal Code and section 8 of POCSO Act. 2. .. 1 .. bail 19/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 19 of 2015 This application is filed by applicant Numan Sayyed Siraj for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. I­397/2014 registered at Mira Road police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 376, 34 of I.P.C. and section 4 and 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant introduced the victim girl with the main accused and he helped the main accused in committed forcible sexual intercourse with the minor victim girl. It is further contended and argued that no such incident has happened and the applicant is falsely implicated in this crime. It is further submitted that the allegation of committing rape are against the main accused. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/ accused is released on bail, he will co­operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that the applicant introduced the victim girl with the main accused and then taking advantage of such acquaintance and her minor age the main accused induced her by giving her amount of Rs.500/­, finger ring and mobile phone of SAMSUNG company and then committed forcible sexual intercourse with her in flat no.704, building no.5 .. 2 .. bail 19/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Oswal Orchid, Kanakia, at Mira Road (E). It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl and the prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 376, 34 of I.P.C. and section 4 and 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and the girl is stated to 16 years, it appears that the accused had been arrested long back on 09.09.2014, from the F.I.R. it appears that the main allegations of rape are against co­accused and the role attributed to the present applicant/accused is that he is common friend of complainant as well as main accused and he introduced the complainant i.e. victim, to the main accused. Then it is contended on behalf of the applicant/ accused that he is falsely implicated in the crime. In such circumstance the aspect as whether the allegations against the accused are true or not, will have to be decided on merits after trial. 4] Now doubt, it is well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be gone into detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence. .. 3 .. bail 19/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) 5] In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 6] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 7] Then, it has also to be mentioned that the investigation in the matter though almost completed the charge sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 8] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Mr. Numan Sayyed Siraj is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ .. 4 .. bail 19/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) He shall attend the concerned police station on every Saturday between 3.00 p.m. to 5.00 p.m. till filing of the charge sheet and shall co­operate with the investigation. 1 Special Case No.07/2016 (Judgment) Presented on : 05.09.2015 Registered on : 05.01.2016 Decided on : 05.07.2017 Duration Y M D 01 06 00 IN THE COURT OF SESSIONS JUDGE­2 & SPECIAL JUDGE [POCSO] ACT, THANE AT : THANE (Presided over by V.V.Bambarde, Additional Sessions Judge­2 & Special Judge (POCSO) Act, Thane ) SPECIAL CASE NO.07/2016 EXH.No. 27. State of Maharashtra ( Through CBD Police Stn., Navi Mumbai ) ...Complainant Vs. Shri. Mahendra Gopichand Baviskar, Age : 22 Yrs., R/at. Ramabai Ambedkarnagar, Sector 8, R.No. 277, CBD, Navi Mumbai. ...Accused. Offence Punishable Under Sec.354­D, 509 of IPC and S.11 (4) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ Appearances : Shri. Kulkarni, Ld. Spl.P.P. for the State Mr. S.B.Patil, Ld.Advocate for the accused ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ 2 Special Case No.07/2016 (Judgment) :JUDGMENT: (Delivered on 05th day of July, 2017) 1] The accused is charged and tried for offence punishable under Sec.354­D, 509 of IPC and Sec. 11(4) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 for having been committed offence of outraging modesty of minor victim girl, passing remarks to insult her modesty and sexually harassing her by repeatedly following her on her way to tuition class. 2] Case of prosecution in brief is that : The prosecutrix was attending her tuition class at 8.00 a.m. from her home. The accused was following her, blowing whistles and was trying to go close to her. As usual accused followed her at 9.30 a.m. on 05/09/2015, blew whistles, sung songs and tried to talk with prosecutrix in the lane. The victim girl came to home, brust in tears and told her mother that accused had been following her till tuition class. The parents of victim girl discussed and lodged complaint in CBD, Vashi Police Station. 3] On the receipt of complaint, CBD Police, Navi Mumbai registered offence under Sec.354­D, 509 of IPC and S. 11 (4) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Investigation was taken up by API­ Karad. API­Karad arrested accused on 06/09/2015. He recorded statements of parents of the victim girl. The girl was taken before JMFC who recorded her statement under S. 164 Cr.P.C. API Karad collected bonafide certificate of victim showing that date of birth of girl was 10/07/2000. On completion of investigation, charge sheet filed in the Court. 4] This Court has framed charge against the accused ( Exh.3 ) for 3 Special Case No.07/2016 (Judgment) the offence under Sec. 354­D, 509 of IPC and Sec. 11 (4) of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. The contents of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 5] The defence of the accused as constructed in cross­ examination and statement under Sec. 313 Cr.P.C. is of false implication in the case. 6] I have heard Ld. Special P.P. for the State and Ld. advocate for the accused. 7] The following points arise for my determination with my findings thereon for reasons to follow: POINTS FINDINGS 01. Does the prosecution prove that on ...In the affirmative. 05/09/2015 at 9.30 hours, at CBD Aaranja Circle Chowk to residential area Ramabai Ambedkarnagar, way to the road through galli, Sector 8, CBD, Navi Mumbai, the accused followed the victim girl and tried to contact the girl to foster personal interaction despite disinterest by her? 02. Does prosecution prove that the accused, on ...In the affirmative. the aforesaid date, time and place, blew whistles, sung songs intending to insult modesty of victim girl? 03. Does prosecution prove that the accused, on ...In the affirmative. the aforesaid date, time and place, repeatedly, constantly followed the victim girl and sexually harassed her ? 02 What order ? Accused is convicted and 4 Special Case No.07/2016 (Judgment) released on Probation of Offenders Act as per final order. REASONS 8] AS TO POINT NOS.1 TO 3: Prosecution examined four witnesses to bring home the guilt of accused. Testimony of victim girl is at Exh. 8 and she is P.W.1. Mrs. Savita Dhale (P.W.2) and Mr. Ganesh Dhale (P.W.3) are parents of the victim and Mr. Ganesh Karad (P.W.4) is investigating officer. The victim girl and her parents are residing at Ramabai Ambedkar Nagar, Sector 8, CBD, Navi Mumbai. Victim was studying in 10th standard in 2015. She used to go to Samarth Classes. Mr. Ganesh Dhale (P.W.3) was taking his daughter to Samarth Classes at 8 a.m. She was coming alone while classes over by 9 a.m. The accused also hails from same locality. 9] The victim girl deposed that at 9.30 a.m. on 05/09/2015 she reached near Aarenja Circle. The accused was on motorcycle. The accused come in front of her and started blowing whistles and singing songs. The accused followed her till Ramabai Ambedkar Road. The victim girl was chased by accused on 20­25 days before. Accused was giving bike cut to her. The victim girl deposed that the accused tried to talk with her. It caused her embarrassment, insult etc. Sou. Savita Dhale (P.W.2) and Ganesh Dhale (P.W.3) deposed that the victim girl disclosed to them about stalking by the accused. They lodged complaint Exh. 16 in CBD Vashi Police Station. 10] Shri. Ganesh Karad (P.W.4), I.O. deposed that he come to know that accused was singing songs and blowing whistles. The victim girl got 5 Special Case No.07/2016 (Judgment) frightened. He arrested accused vide panchanama Exh. 18. The girl's statement was recorded before Judicial Magistrate vide Exh.9. He took girl's bonafide certificate vide Exh.11. The girl's birth date was 10/07/2000. 11] I have heard Ld. Special P.P. and Ld. Advocate for the accused. There is only testimony of victim (P.W.1). The victim has deposed that the accused was chasing her and was trying to contact her. Ld. Advocate for accused submitted that it is doubtful whether girl felt insulted while accused sung songs and blew whistles. The girl came to home and wept before her mother. It means that she felt something seriously wrong with her. She was 15 years old at the time of incident. It is strongly contended that there is no corroboration to her testimony that accused was chasing her. Mr. Ganesh Karad, I.O. (P.W.4) deposed that road leading to Ramabai Nagar is having less traffic. The girl was knowing accused but she was not knowing about exact residence of the accused. But it does not mean that the girl has nurture and hated or ill­will against the accused. There is no enmity between them. Why the girl will unnecessarily depose against anyone. Victim girl is subjected to searching cross­examination. There is nothing to disbelieve her. The victim girl has stated that she was chased and stalked by accused which caused her embarrassment. The accused tried to talk with the victim girl against her wishes so there is offence of stalking. Similarly, the accused has repeatedly and constantly followed her because she was a girl. So it is harassment with a sexual intent. The accused made gestures and insulted modesty of a victim girl. Therefore, the accused is guilty of offence under S. 354­D and 509 of IPC and under S. 11(4) of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Hence, I answer Point Nos. 1 to 3 in affirmative. Here I take pause to hear the accused on the point of sentence. 6 Special Case No.07/2016 (Judgment) 12] I heard accused on the point of sentence. He is bachelor. He intend to go for further studies. He is youth of 23 years. I have heard Ld. Special P.P. also. It is first offence of the accused. He is youth. The accused repented for his misdeed. It will be just to extend benefit of Probation of Offenders Act to the accused. So I find it just to pass following order : ORDER 1] The accused Shri. Mahendra Gopichand Baviskar is hereby convicted of offence under Sec.354­D, 509 of IPC and S. 11(4) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act,2012 and instead of sentencing him, he be released on good behaviour bond under Probation of Offenders Act of Rs.5,000/­ for one year. 2] Bail bond of the accused stands cancelled. Thane ( V.V.Bambarde ) Dt. :­ 05.07.2017 Additional Sessions Judge­2, vsi­p.c. & Special Judge (POCSO) Act, Thane. 7 Special Case No.07/2016 (Judgment)

At about 5.30 p.m. he asked victim about his illness, thereupon victim told that still he is not feeling well and kept mum. Thereafter he told that on Friday dt. 3.10.2014 at about 12.00 noon Anwar Khalu residing near his house called him in his house for watching T.V. and at that time he was alone in the house. He made victim to sit on chair and closed the door from inside and thereafter he was taking batch in naked position in bathroom in the presence of victim. He called victim near him and put his penis on his mouth and asked him to suck and move the same due to that victim vomited. Victim opposed Anwar. Thereafter he gave Rs. 10/­ to victim which he refused to accept and told that he will narrate the incident to his father. Then in anger Anwar tore note of Rs. 10/­ and threatened that if he disclosed said fact to anybody he will kill him and his father. Informant then disclosed the said facts to his neighbourers Maqsud, Fariyad and Riyaz. They also made enquiry with victim and he told them the same. 3] On the basis of complaint, Crime No.I­270/2014 for the offence punishable u/s 377, 342, 506 of I.P.C. r/w S. 4, 12 & 14 of POCSO Act was registered and PSI Shaikh carried out investigation. On the same day he arrested accused, prepared spot panchanama and sent the accused for medical examination. Victim was also sent to Civil Hospital. He recorded statements of witnesses. He seized pant and towel from accused u/s 27 of the Evidence Act. He collected medical certificates of victim and accused. He got recorded statement of victim ..3/- ..3.. Spl.C. No.4/2015 (Exh.No. 56) u/s 164 of Cr.P.C. before the Court.After completion of investigation he submitted chargesheet against accused before the Special Judge (POCSO Act), Thane. 4] Charge Exh.29 was framed & explained to accused to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. His defence is that of total denial. 5] Considering the case of the prosecution following points arise for my determination and I have recorded my findings thereon for the reasons discussed below. POINTS FINDINGS 1 Does the prosecution prove that on 3.10.2014 at bout 12.00 noon in the house of accused, opp. Mouje Gausiya Masjid Shantinagar, Ala Hajrat Chowk, Bhiwandi accused committed carnal intercourse against the order of nature by putting penis in the mouth of victim aged 9 years and thereby committed an offence punishable u/sec. 377 of I.P.C.? No. 2 Does the prosecution further prove that on the above mentioned date,time and place accused wrongfully confined victim in the room and thereby committed an offence u/s 342 of IPC? No. 3 Does the prosecution further prove that on the above mentioned date,time and place accused intentionally insulted victim by abusing him in filthy language and thereby gave provocation to him to break public peace and thereby committed an offence u/s 504 of IPC? No. ..4/- ..4.. Spl.C. No.4/2015 (Exh.No. 56) 4 Does the prosecution further prove that on the above mentioned date,time and place accused committed criminal intimidation by threatening to victim and thereby committed an offence u/s 506 of IPC? No. 5 Does the prosecution further prove that on the above mentioned date,time and place accused committed sexual assault on victim punishable u/s 7 and thereby committed an offence u/s 8 of PCSO Act? No. 6 What order ? As per final order. REASONS Points Nos. 1 to 5 : 6] All the points are interlinked to each other, hence in order to avoid the repetition of evidence they are clubbed together. 7] Prosecution examined in all 5 witnesses. P.W.1 Anwarali/informant at Exh.31, PW 2 Victim at Exh.35, PW 3 Maqsudali­ panch at Exh.36, PW 4 Iftekar antoher panch at Exh.38 and PW 5 Shaikh, I.O. at Exh.40. Then prosecution filed evidence closing pursis at Exh.49. Statement of accused recorded u/s 313 of Cr.P. C. is at Exh.50. Thereafter, accused examined DW1 Shaikh Shahid at Exh.52 in his defence and filed evidence closing pursis Exh.53. Prosecution relied on documents viz. report Exh.32, FIR Exh.33, panchanama Exh.37, arrest panchanama Exh.41, medical certificates Exhs. 42 & 43, bonafide certificate Exh.44, C.A. reports Exhs. 45 & 46, memorandum Exh.47 and panchanama Exh.48. ..5/- ..5.. Spl.C. No.4/2015 (Exh.No. 56) 8] The Ld. APP submitted that complainant Anwar Shaha is father of victim and he lodged complaint against accused as he came to know about the incident from victim and his evidence clearly shows that there is no previous enmity against accused and as such, he has no reason to lodge false complaint Exh.32. PW 2 is the victim who stated the fact of incident and his evidence is at all not shattered on the material point and as such, his evidence is reliable and free from any chance of tutoring. PW 3 & 4 are the panchas and they supported to the case of prosecution. I.O. carried investigation and collected bonafide certificate of victim which shows that victim is minor and apart from that, C.A. reports Exhs. 45 & 46 show stain marks on the towel. The evidence of defence witness is far away from truth as no matter was reported to police regarding the cognizable offence of theft. In reply, she also submitted that the neighbourers are hearsay witnesses, therefore, they are not examined by the prosecution. The Ld. APP relied on the citation Ganesan Vs. State, reported in 2017 ALL MR, 340 in which, it is held that it can be presumed that there was nothing unnatural on part of victim in not disclosing about incident till she felt pain. Nothing brought on record to rebut the same. Therefore, such delayed disclosure would not render her evidence doubtful. This ratio is not applicable to the facts of present case as complainant deposed that on 3.10.2014 victim disclosed the fact of incident to neighbours but in the FIR he himself mentioned that on 9.10.2014 for the first time, he came to know about the incident and then he disclosed the same to neighbours, who verified the same from victim. Thus, there are two contrary dates in respect of disclosure of incident. ..6/- ..6.. Spl.C. No.4/2015 (Exh.No. 56) 9] Per contra, the Ld. Counsel for accused vehemently submitted that prosecution failed to examine neighbours who are independent witness. The contradiction in the evidence of complainant goes to the root of case and that creates doubt on the entire FIR. Apart from that, victim deposed the fact which is not finding place in his police statement and he falsely denied the fact of committing theft at the house of accused. On the point of theft accused examined defence witness and his evidence is trustworthy. In order to take revenge, false complaint came to be filed against accused and as such, prosecution failed to prove the charges beyond reasonable doubt and hence, accused is entitled for benefit of doubt. The Ld. Defence counsel relied on the citation John Vs. State, reported in 2015 ALL MR (Cri.), 4052, in which, it is held that accused allegedly committed aggravated sexual assault on victim child aged about 8 years, prosecution case rests only on evidence of victim child. Evidence of mother is hearsay in nature. No medical evidence as to examination of either victim or accused. In absence of any other corroborative evidence, testimony of child victim not reliable. This ration is not applicable to the facts of present case as medical examination report of victim and accused is filed on record. He also relied on citation State Vs. Mulla, reported in 2015 C.J. (Del), 1661, in which, it is held that the evidence of a child witness must be evaluated more carefully and with greater circumspection because the child is susceptible to be swayed by what others tell him and thus a child witness is an easy prey to tutoring. This preposition is applicable as PW 2 is not only child but he is the victim himself. 10] PW 1 deposed that victim is his son. On 9.10.2014 victim was suffering from fever and cuff and as such he and his wife thought to ..7/- ..7.. Spl.C. No.4/2015 (Exh.No. 56) take him to doctor. However, in the report Exh.32, he has mentioned that on 9.10.2014 as victim was ill, therefore, he took him to Dr. Mazhar. Thus, on this point, there is a contradiction in the testimony of complainant which is not as per his report. But, victim deposed that he went to doctor due to fever. In the cross examination complainant stated that victim was taken to Dr. Mazhar but he did not disclose about the incident to doctor. This shows that victim was accompanied by anybody at the time of visit to Dr. Mazhar. However, victim deposed in his cross examination that from the date of incident till 9 th he himself did not go to dispensary but subsequently he again stated that he alone went to Dr. Mazhar. This shows that evidence of victim is not trustworthy on the point of visiting to Dr. Mazhar. The evidence of complainant is also not corroborated by the testimony of victim and the fact of visiting to dispensary of Dr. Mazhar also not established by prosecution either by examining Dr. Mazhar or by filing his prescription. Hence, the case of prosecution is under the shadow of doubt as the allegation of prosecution is that due to insertion of penis in the mouth of victim, victim was ill but prosecution failed to prove the same. 11] Complainant further deposed that victim told that on 3.10.2014 neighbouring Khalu Anwar/accused called him at his house for watching T.V., he closed the door from inside, removed his clothes, he put his penis in the mouth of victim and then victim came out and disclosed about it to neighbouring people. But as per report Exh.32, victim for the first time disclosed about incident on 9.10.2014 firstly to his parents and then complainant disclosed the same to his neighbours and they also made enquiry from victim. Thus, as per the report, incident for the first time disclosed by victim on 9.10.2014 is falsified by complainant himself by deposing that victim told the same to ..8/- ..8.. Spl.C. No.4/2015 (Exh.No. 56) neighbours on 3.10.2014 itself. The testimony of victim is that on 9 th he told about incident to his parents. Thus, his evidence is not corroborated to the evidence of complainant. This fact goes to the root of the case as alleged incident took place on 3.10.2014 and complainant came to be lodged on 10.10.2014. Thus there is a delay of 7 days. In order to explain the delay, the averment in the complaint is that on 9.10.2014 victim disclosed about the incident and on the next day, after consultation with family members and relatives complaint came to be lodged on 10.10.2014. 12] When the argument putforth by the defence counsel that whenever the incident took place, generally the neighbour came to know about the same and as such, it was incumbent on prosecution to examine the neighbours, then, non examination of neighbours raised the doubt on the story projected by the prosecution. The Ld. APP in reply submitted that neighbours are hearsay witness and as such, they were not examined. In the present matter, the evidence of complainant is that just after the incident victim disclosed the fact to the neighbours and as such, as per the provisions of S. 6 of the Evidence Act, there is a relevancy in the evidence of neighbours though they are not eyewitness to the incident. Non examination of neighbours also raised the doubt on the count of explanation of delay and also raised the question on the happening of incident. Had it been a fact that incident took place on 3.10.2014 and just after incident victim disclosed the same to the neighbours as stated by complainant, then the natural conduct on the part of neighbour would be to verify the same from accused as they were in large number and on finding substance, they either told to the parents of victim as there was no threat given by accused to the neighbours or ..9/- ..9.. Spl.C. No.4/2015 (Exh.No. 56) reported the matter to police being cognizable offence. But nothing happened and as such, it also creates a doubt on the testimony of complainant and as such, it is just and proper to discard his testimony. 13] It is to be noted that while assessing the evidence of child, it is necessary to go through the minor details as the child is to be tutored on the major facts but not on minor or vice­a­versa. In the complaint, it is mentioned that at the relevant time, accused made victim to sit on chair and victim also deposed the same. However, on going through the spot panchanama Exh.37 which is nothing but the house of accused but there is nothing mentioned about the chair. Secondly, it is mentioned in the FIR and victim also deposed that accused was taking bath in naked position in bathroom. However, complainant deposed that accused removed his clothes and he put his penis in the mouth of victim. Thus, there is no corroboration on the point of taking bath in nude. Victim also deposed that accused gave note of Rs. 10/­ to him which refused to accept then in anger accused torn note of Rs. 10/­. The I.O. though recorded memorandum of accused and also visited to the house of accused, but failed to seize or recover that torn note. One of the material point also goes to the root of the case as according to FIR, accused called victim in his house for watching T.V. But victim deposed that accused took him to his house by catch holding his hand. This piece of evidence goes to show the severeness on the part of accused that against the wish of victim accused forcibly took him. 14] The evidence of victim is totally silent on the point of stain mark on the towel allegedly used by accused at the time of committing crime, on the other hand, according to him, accused was nude and ..10/- ..10.. Spl.C. No.4/2015 (Exh.No. 56) taking bath. Thus, the stain mark on towel also compelled to raise doubt on investigation carried by I.O. Therefore, the evidence of victim seems to be focused on the point of main incident of insertion of penis in his mouth. Thus, the submission of defence counsel that victim is tutored on the main point and as such on the minor point there is no corroborative evidence is acceptable and as such, I am inclined to discard the testimony of victim also. When the testimony of complainant and victim is discarded, then the presumption which is in favour of prosecution u/s 29 of the POCSO Act is rebutted by accused. 16] PW 3 Khan deposed that police prepared spot panchanama Exh.37 in his presence and that is in respect of house of accused which consists of one room. On perusal of spot panchanama it reveals that at the corner of the room there is a bathroom i.e. W.C. However, according to victim, before the incident, he never went to the house of accused and he does not know what articles are in that house. His evidence is silent on the point of taking bath by accused in the bathroom. Thus, the spot panchanama is also doubtful. 17] PW 4 Hussein deposed that on 10.10.2014 he was called at police station and police seized shirt and pant under seizure memo Exh.39. In cross examination he deposed that he was accompanied with complainant and police seized the above clothes from complainant. However, I.O. failed to satisfy the Court as to why he seized those clothes as it is not the contention of victim that there was any stain either of blood, semen or particles of vomiting. I.O. also failed to satisfy whether those clothes were subsequently used by victim after washing the same or not. On perusal of medical certificate Exh.42 of victim, no ..11/- ..11.. Spl.C. No.4/2015 (Exh.No. 56) external injury was found by medical officer. In the same way medical certificate of accused shows that there were no injuries on his person. 18] According to I.O. he recorded memorandum of accused Exh.47 and in pursuance of that he seized towel and pant of accused under panchanama Exh.48. The duty discharged by investigating officer seems to be non application of mind as according to prosecution case at the relevant time accused was taking bath in nude position and in the same scenario he put his penis in the mouth of victim, then what is the relevancy to seize pant and towel from accused and that too on recording memorandum. On perusal of C.A. report Exh.45, it reveals that there are 4 human semen stains on towel but its group is inconclusive. On the other hand, it was expected from I.O. to seize or recover torn note of Rs.10/­ from accused which definitely boosted to the case of prosecution. There is no explanation as to what happened of that torn note. 19] So far as the defence is concerned, prior to 8 days of alleged incident, victim committed theft from pocket of accused and as such he beat him then in order to take revenge complainant lodged false report. A suggestion in that respect was also given to complainant, victim and I.O. but in vein and therefore, he examined DW 1 Yusuf who deposed that on 2.10.2014 victim committed theft of Rs. 100/­ from the house of accused. Accused caught hold victim and brought to his house. That time, victim admitted his guilt and spent Rs. 10/­ and remaining amount of Rs. 90/­ is with him and also told that not to commit theft in future. That time, mother of victim, he himself, accused and Nazir Khan were present. On that day, accused beat to victim in his house. As agreed in the meeting, no complaint was lodged regarding theft. ..12/- ..12.. Spl.C. No.4/2015 (Exh.No. 56) However, 8 days thereafter he came to know about lodging of report against accused. In cross examination he admitted that he never disclosed to police about committing of theft of money. 20] It is to be noted that as the matter was resolved at the residence of DW 1 Yusuf then but natural no complaint came to be lodged but who prevented the accused to disclose this fact during the course of investigation and more specifically, at the time of recording of his memorandum or when for the first time he was produced before the Court. Thus, the defence putforth by accused is not passed the test of preponderance of probability. At the same time in view of the above discussion, the entire case of prosecution is also under the shadow of doubt. Therefore, it is just and proper to extend benefit to accused as prosecution and defence came with untrue facts and both versions have to be discarded. 21] The evidence on record is not sufficient to prove the charge levelled against accused beyond reasonable doubt for offence punishable u/s 377, 342, 504, & 506 of IPC and the offence punishable u/s 8 of POCSO Act. With this discussion, I answer the point Nos. 1 to 5 accordingly and to proceed to pass the following order. : ORDER : 1] Accused Anwar Babu Shaikh is hereby acquitted u/s 235 of Cr.P.C. from the charge of offence punishable u/s 377, 342,504, 506 of I.P.C & u/s 8 of POCSO Act. 2] Accused be released forthwith if not reqsuired in any other crime/case. 3] Accused shall comply forthwith the provision U/Sec.437­A Cr.P.C. by furnishing fresh P.R. Bond of ..13/- ..13.. Spl.C. No.4/2015 (Exh.No. 56) Rs.10,000/­ and S.B. of like amount. 4) Seized muddemal being worthless be destroyed after period of appeal is over.
