J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 06­15 ­ S ­ 376,354 3(d).4.8.doc . .....6/­ ..6.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 06/2015.. Exh.22.. 10] The victim girl who is examined as PW2 at Exh.9 has supported the prosecution. Her deposition is recorded in question­answer form. She has deposed that she knows the accused who is having tailoring shop on their way. When she used to go to tuition accused used to call upon her. The accused used to kiss her on face and also used to touch his penis on her vagina. She narrated said fact to her mother. In order to verify said fact her mother had asked her to go to the shop of accused and she followed her. At that time her maternal aunt was also alongwith her mother. The accused called her as usual in his shop. When she went into his shop, he hold her hand. Thereafter her mother and maternal aunt immediately rushed into the shop of accused and caught him. Thereafter her mother lodged complaint in the police station. Police made inquiry with her and recorded her statement. Her statement was also recorded by Magistrate. 11] This witness is cross examined on behalf of the defence. She has denied that as there was quarrel between her mother and accused, her mother had been to police station to lodge complaint about the same. She admitted in cross examination that she had been to the police station alongwith her mother. However, on that day police merely inquired with her and her statement was recorded later on. However, she J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 06­15 ­ S ­ 376,354 3(d).4.8.doc . .....7/­ ..7.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 06/2015.. Exh.22.. has denied that accused had never misbehaved with her and had never touched her vagina with his penis. From the cross examination of the victim it is clear that she had been to police station as well as in the Court and she narrated the incident to the police and before Magistrate. Her version about the sexual assault by the accused is nowhere shakened in her cross examination. 12] The prosecution has examined investigating officer A.P.I. Shivaji Pawar. He deposed that on 23.08.2014 at about 12.00 noon, 4­5 women, two girls and accused had been to police station. The informant narrated the incident. Accordingly her complaint Exh.12 came to be recorded. After recording complaint he registered crime. He had sent the victim girl for medical examination vide Exh.13. He arrested accused and prepared arrest form vide Exh.14. He had sent the accused for medical examination vide letter Exh.15. He visited the spot of incident which was shown by the complainant. He prepared spot panchanama Exh.16. P.I. Ghuge carried out further investigation and got recorded statement of victim girl u/s.164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 13] In cross examination of this witness the defence produced and proved the N.C. dated 23.08.2014 filed by the J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 06­15 ­ S ­ 376,354 3(d).4.8.doc . .....8/­ ..8.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 06/2015.. Exh.22.. wife of the accused against the informant. He further admitted in cross examination that on 23.08.2014 the victim had been to police station, but he did not record her statement. He further admitted that he did not record the statement of any eye witness stating that the victim used to go to the shop of accused. He further admitted that the informant and the mother of another victim girl refused for medical examination of both girls. No injuries were found on the person of accused. The photographs of the spot of incident were not obtained. The accused was brought to the police station in the afternoon on 23.08.2014, but his arrest was carried out at 08.00 p.m 14] The defence witness Samshulnisa Nasrul Hasan Shaikh who is wife of accused deposed that on 23.08.2014 at about 10.30 a.m. the informant and 2­3 women had been to their house and asked about her husband. The informant had said that the accused had wrongly stitched her clothes and demanded its amount. As she refused to pay the amount the informant beat her. The informant pulled her hair and assaulted on shoulder, head and wrist. She had sustained injury on her right hand. Thereafter she had been to Mumbra police station at 12.00 noon and lodged complaint. Accordingly her N.C. was recorded. Copy of which is at Exh.18. Thereafter police referred her for medical examination. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 06­15 ­ S ­ 376,354 3(d).4.8.doc . .....9/­ ..9.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 06/2015.. Exh.22.. 15] Relying upon the prosecution evidence and deposition of defence witness advocate Mr.Jagtap submitted that the version of the victim is not supported by any independent witness. The contents of the complaint are also not duly proved. The complaint is proved through the investigating officer PW3. The victim's statement was recorded after delay of almost seven days and the delay is nowhere explained. Advocate Mr.Jagtap further submitted written arguments at Exh.21 and stated that though thousands of witnesses were available, no independent eye witness is examined. As per prosecution story maternal aunt of the victim was present at the scene of offence. They tried to verify the allegations. But she is not examined by the prosecution as witness. The defence has produced and proved N.C. registered against the informant. As such to counter the complaint filed by wife of accused, the informant lodged false complaint against the accused. 16] It is pertinent to note here that the complainant turned hostile and has not supported the prosecution. She was reluctant to pursue the matter. In cross examination on behalf of the learned A.P.P. she has denied that due to compromise she deposed falsely. Thus the complaint is certainly not duly proved in the evidence of the informant. However, the victim was just six years old at the time of incident. She had made J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 06­15 ­ S ­ 376,354 3(d).4.8.doc . .....10/­ ..10.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 06/2015.. Exh.22.. statement before police as well as before the Magistrate describing the incident. In witness box the victim girl has confidently described the acts at the hands of accused. She has specifically deposed that the accused used to remove his clothes, her clothes and used to touch her vagina by mouth. The confident statement of the victim in the Court is certainly reliable. Considering the nature of incident the complainant might have thought not to carry on the matter, but the victim did not resile from her statement and narrated the entire story as happened. Thus the statement of victim girl is sufficient to conclude that the prosecution has proved the sexual assault upon the victim girl by the accused. Hence I answer point No.1 in the affirmative. 17] The accused is charge sheeted for offence punishable u/s.376, 354 of the Indian Penal Code and section 3 and 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. The act of the accused touching vagina of the victim by mouth falls within the definition of penetrative sexual assault, as denied u/s.3 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. The punishment for the same is prescribed u/s.4 of the Act. The Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act being special provision prescribing harsher punishment, it is not necessary to convict the accused for offence under the Indian Penal Code. So also one and single act forming J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 06­15 ­ S ­ 376,354 3(d).4.8.doc . .....11/­ ..11.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 06/2015.. Exh.22.. penetrative sexual assault being proved it is not necessary to convict the accused for offence punishable u/s.8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. Thus the accused is liable to be convicted and sentenced for the offence punishable u/s.3 r.w. 4 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. At this juncture the Judgment is deferred to hear the accused on the quantum of sentence. Thane. (P.P.Jadhav) District Judge­5 and Date : 19.06.2018. Addl. Sessions Judge, Thane. 18] Heard advocate Mr.Jagtap and accused in person. It is submitted on behalf of the accused that accused being only earning member of the family, he be punished with minimum sentence. On the contrary A.P.P. Mr.Kadu argued that offence being very serious the accused be punished with maximum punishment. 19] As already observed the act committed by the accused falls within the definition of penetrative sexual assault as defined u/s.3 and punishable u/s.4 of the Act. Under such circumstances a single punishment for offence u/s.4 will be just and reasonable in this case. The section prescribes punishment of imprisonment of not less than seven years, but J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 06­15 ­ S ­ 376,354 3(d).4.8.doc . .....12/­ ..12.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 06/2015.. Exh.22.. which may extent to imprisonment for life. In the present case admittedly there is no injury to the victim girl. Accused is not having any criminal history. Considering the nature of the act minimum sentence prescribed u/s.4 of the Act will be just and proper in the present case. Hence the order. ORDER 1. Accused Mahammad Kalin Mehamood Hasan Shaikh @ Mohammad Kalim Mohammad Hasan Shaikh is hereby convicted u/s.235(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure for offence punishable u/s.376, 354 of the Indian Penal Code, u/s.3, 4 and 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act and is sentenced to rigorous imprisonment for seven years and fine of Rs.10,000/­, in default of payment of fine he has to undergo further simple imprisonment for six months. 2. The accused to surrender his bail bond. 3. The accused is entitled to set off for the period of he undergone in jail, u/s.428 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 4. Copy of Judgment be given to the accused free of cost. Sd/­... Thane. (P.P.Jadhav) District Judge­6 and Date : 19.06.2018. Addl. Sessions Judge, Thane. Non-applicant (through Narpoli P.S.) ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 1] This is an application moved under section 167(2) of Cr.P.C. for releasing the applicant/accused. 2] Heard learned advocate Miss Sarita Gaikwad for the applicant/accused. She submitted that the applicant was arrested on 14.09.2015 and produced before Court 15.09.2015 and remanded to police custody till 16.09.2015 and since then he is in judicial custody. She submitted that though 90 days has been completed, charge-sheet is not filed and therefore, the applicant is entitled for bail as per section 167(2) of Cr.P.C. by submitting that applicant is ready to furnish the bail to the satisfaction of the Court. 3] The Say of Spl.P.P. was called and the report from the Office was also called to verify as to whether the charge-sheet is submitted in present C.R. No.I- 360/2015 .. 2 .. Bail No. 83/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) registered with Narpoli Police Station in respect of the present accused. 4] The concerned office filed the report today submitting that in C.R.No.I-360/2015 registered with Narpoli police station for offence punishable under section 363, 354 r.w. sec. 34 of I.P.C. and section 8, 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act charge-sheet is not submitted till 5.00 p.m. in respect of present accused. Learned Sp.P.P. prayed for imposing stringent conditions. 5] The provision of section 167(2) of Cr.P.C. is very much clear which gives an indefeasible right to the accused if the charge-sheet has not been submitted within the period of sixty or ninety days. Thus, it is very much clear that even after completion of 60 days the charge- sheet has not been submitted in respect of the present applicant/accused in C.R.No.I-360/2015 registered with Narpoli Police Station. Thus, as per provision of section- 167(2) of Cr.P.C. the right accrues in favour of applicant/ accused and therefore, he is entitled to be released on bail as he is ready to furnish the bail and abide by the conditions imposed by the Court. Hence, I pass following order - ORDER 1) The application is allowed. 2) Applicant namely Vicky alias Vikas Dhanaji Bhosale be released on bail on his executing P.R. Bond of .. 3 .. Bail No. 83/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) ₹ 15,000/- [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one local solvent surety in the like amount on the following conditions - A] Applicant shall attend the concerned police station on every Sunday between 10.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon till filing the charge-sheet. B] Applicant shall co-operate in investigation and shall not tamper with prosecution witnesses. C] Applicant shall furnish his and his two blood relatives' address proofs and contact numbers and he is duty bound to inform I.O. and Court about the change of address, if any. D] Applicant shall not contact and pressurize victim-girl and any other witnesses in any manner and he shall maintain decency hereinafter. Thane. Date : 08.01.2016. 1 Bail No. 103/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) Criminal Bail Application No.103/2016 Sunita Dilip Batra .. Applicant versus The State of Maharashtra Through Vikramgad Police Station .. Non­applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 1] By this application the applicant is seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. who was arrested 04.01.2016 by Vikramgad Police Station in connection with C.R.No.I­ 117/2015 registered for an offence punishable under section 363, 376, 506 r/w.34 of I.P.C. and section 4 and 6 Maharashtra Prevention and Eradication of Human Sacrifice and Other Inhuman, Evil and Aghori Practices and Black Magic Act, 2013, (hereinafter in short referred to as Black Magic Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Mr. Sunil Patankar for the applicant/accused and learned Spl.P.P. Mrs. R.A. Navale for State. I.O. present. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 26/11/2015 at the instance of the informant/mother of the victim­girl aged 2 Bail No. 103/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) about 16 years with an indictment that her minor daughter was staying with her sister i.e. accused Sunita and her husband Dilip and they helped some unknown person to kidnap her minor daughter. During investigation it was revealed that accused Sarvadas Bhoir committed sexual assault on her on the pretext of doing some black magic for the rainfall of money. 4] The learned Counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant/accused is falsely implicated. He submitted that the victim is a niece of the present applicant / accused and staying with her family. He submitted that the applicant is no way concerned with the alleged offence. The allegations about the sexual assault are against accused Sarvadas Bhoir. The applicant is a married lady and having children. She has no criminal antecedents. The accused is ready to abide any conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing him on bail. 5] Per contra, the learned Spl.P.P. opposed the application submitting that the present applicant is maternal aunt of the victim and she helped the main accused and with her aid accused, main accused committed sexual on victim­girl for thrice. She further submitted that even the black magic was practiced on the victim­girl . The offence is serious and investigation is in progress. There are chances of tampering 3 Bail No. 103/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) with witnesses and prayed for rejection of application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R., it appears that initially the FIR was lodged with the allegations that accused Sarvadas Bhoir enticed and kidnapped the minor victim­girl who was staying with the accused No.2 and 3, accused No.2 and 3 abeted accused No.1 for the said offence. During investigation it was revealed that accused No.1 Sarvadas Bhoir practiced black magic on the victim­girl on the pretext for having rain shower and thrice sexually assaulted her. Further from the investigation papers, it appears that the victim­girl was found on 03/012/2015. At that time, as she was threatened by the accused, therefore, she made a statement that she was not subjected to sexual assault, neither anybody kidnapped her. However, on 02/01/2016, the supplementary statement of the victim­girl was recorded, wherein she clearly stated that as she was threatened by the accused persons, therefore, even though she sexually assaulted from time to time with an intent to have rain shower by applying the black magic, she could not give statement against the accused. The said statement of dated 02/01/2016 of the victim­girl appears to be recorded that the use of electronic media and thereafter, the offence under section 376, 506 of IPC and section 3 of Black Magic Act. The investigation is in progress. Considering the said aspect about pressurizing the victim­girl there is further possibility of 4 Bail No. 103/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) tampering the evidence and in such circumstances the apprehension of Learned APP well founded. Hence, at this stage no case is made out for releasing the accused on bail. Hence, I pass the following order ­ ORDER The application stands rejected. Thane. Date : 05/02/2016. (Ms. U.M. Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act), Thane.

I.O. present. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 09.01.2016 at the instance of the informant/ mother of the victim-girl who is aged 09 years with an indictment that on 10.12.2015 when her minor daughter had been to public tap to fill up the water, accused shown his private to her 2 Bail No.105/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) and outraged her modesty used to give indecent signals to the victim-girl. 4] The learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant/accused is falsely implicated. There is quarrel between the family of accused and the victim girl and therefore, present complaint is lodged after thought. The accused is ready to abide by any conditions imposed by the Court and prayed that accused be released on bail. 5] Per contra, the learned A.P.P. opposed the application submitting that the victim-girl is minor and accused used to give indecent signals to the victim-girl. She submitted that as the accused is staying in same vicinity, there are chances of tampering of the witnesses. She further submitted that no cognizable case registered against the accused and there are 2-3 such cases, accused is continuously harassing the victim-girl. The statement of victim-girl is to be recorded and prayed for rejection of the application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R. it appears that the F.I.R. came to registered about the allegations that accused is continuously harassing tender aged victim-girl. However, it also appears that the material part of the investigation might have been completed. The object of bail is neither punitive nor preventive but to secure the presence of the accused at the time of trial. Salunkhe, for the accused. ___________________________________________________________ JUDGMENT (Delivered on 05.03.2018.) 1] Accused Bhavesh Prakash Auti, is facing trial for the offences punishable u/s. 354(A)(1)(i) of I.P.C. and u/s. 7 punishable u/s. 8 of the 2 S.C. No. 09/2014. Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] The prosecution case is that on 11.12.13 during 3.30 to 4.00 p.m., victim along with her friend Kum. Aafsin Shaikh were playing on stair­case of the terrace of Pakiza Co­operative Housing Society at Padvalnagar, Wagle Estate, Thane. Accused came there and told them that he had lost his note of Rs.100/­ in denomination and he requested them to help them for searching. Thereafter, he was taking them towards terrace. Suddenly, brother of Aafsin Shaikh came there. He was told that the note might had been fallen down on the ground. So, accused requested him that he should search on the ground. Thereafter, accused took both the girls on stair­case between fourth and fifth floors. He asked victim for sleeping. He had removed her clothes and was touching her body. She shouted. By these allegations, Najbunisa Mustakim Manihar had lodged her report Exh.19 on 12.11.13. It was registered vide C.R. no. 272/13 u/s. 376, 511 of I.P.C. and u/s. 7 / 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Police had carried out investigation. During the course of investigation, police rushed to the spot and recorded spot panchanama. Accused was arrested. His clothes were seized. Clothes of victim were also seized. Victim was referred for her medical examination. Doctor had examined her. Accused was also referred for his examination, medically. He is also examined by the doctor. After investigation, charge­sheet was submitted in the court. 3] My learned Predecessor framed the charge against the accused for the offences punishable under section 354(A)(1)(i) of I.P.C. and u/s. 7 punishable u/s. 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012, on 18/02/2016. Details of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular, to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to 3 S.C. No. 09/2014. be tried. His defence is of total denial. 4] During trial, defence has admitted no documents. 5] To bring home the guilt of the accused for the charges leveled against him, the prosecution has examined as many as two witnesses i.e. P.W. Name of witness Exh. Description No. No. 1] Smt. Najbunisa 18 Complainant. Mustakim Manihar 2] Victim 26 Victim girl. 6] Accused did not enter into witness box. He has not examined defence witness. 7] Heard learned Special P.P. Smt. Phad for the State and learned counsel Shri. Salunkhe, for the accused. Following points arise for my determination, which are being answered for the reasons given herein­ below. POINTS FINDINGS 1] Whether prosecution proved that No. accused on 12.11.2013 at 15.30 hours to 16.00 hours at stair­case of Pakiza Apartment, Padwalnagar, Wagle Estate, Thane, committed sexual harassment to the minor victim girl aged 7 years, by inappropriately touching her body after removing her clothes ? 2] Whether prosecution further proved No. that on the same date, time and place, accused with sexual intention, committed sexual assault on victim girl 4 S.C. No. 09/2014. aged about 7 years, by physical contact, without penetration ? 3] What order ? As per final order. REASONS POINT NOS. 1 AND 2 8] It has come in the examination­in­chief of P.W.1 Najbunisa Mustakim Manihar that victim is her daughter. She was born on 22 nd November, 2006. 9] It has further come in her examination­in­chief that on 12.11.2013, at about 4.00 p.m. people were saying that accused took her daughter victim on terrace of Pakiza Apartment. She was told by her daughter victim in house that she was playing on first floor, accused told her that he had lost his money and she has to search for it, she was taken on terrace, she was asked to remove her clothes, she had not removed her clothes, one other person was passing from stair­case, so he had embraced her, again accused started removing her clothes, she shouted, the said unknown person came on terrace and started assaulting the accused, then she came to the house. Then, Najbunisa rushed to police station and lodged her report (Exh. 19). 10] It has come in the cross­examination of P.W.1 Najbunisa Manihar that since last ten years, she is residing in Pakiza Apartment. The said building is consisting of five floors. There are five blocks on each floor. On 5th floor also, people are residing. On 12.11.13 at relevant time, she was not present in the house. She had not seen the actual incident. 5 S.C. No. 09/2014. When she reached near her building, accused was already taken by police. She did not know whether neighbourers had disclosed the incident with police. Doctors had examined her daughter. However, they had not found any objectionable. Nothing was narrated by her daughter victim to her. She had no grievance against accused. 11] P.W.2 victim has not supported to the prosecution story at all. Miraj Shaikh is brother of Aafsin, a friend of victim. He was material witness, who had noticed the accused while carrying victim and Aafsin towards terrace through stair­case and who was asked by accused to search the note saying, it might had fallen on the ground. P.W.1 is not eye­ witness to the incident. 12] However, P.W.1 is hear­say witness. She had heard about the incident from the victim and accordingly, she deposed before the court. As on the date of her evidence i.e. on 06.07.17, counsel for accused was absent. Thereafter, in view of order below Exh.20, P.W.1 was recalled for her cross­examination. Her cross­examination was recorded on 18.01.18 i.e. after about five months. She had deposed in her cross­examination that nothing was narrated by her daughter to her and she had no grievance against accused. She went on some extent to say that she did not know Marathi. Undoubtedly, her report is scribed in Marathi. 13] Miraj Shaikh, brother of victim Aafsin was material and available, important witness who had seen the accused and to whom accused had requested to help him to search note on the ground, is not examined by the prosecution. The reason best known to the prosecution. 14] Ld. Counsel for the State submitted that P.W.1 Najbunisa is tampered by the accused. Her chief­examination is recorded on 06.07.17. 6 S.C. No. 09/2014. On that day, counsel for the accused was absent. Thereafter, accused by filing application Exh.20, the said witness was recalled, who had helped the accused in her cross­examination. Her cross­examination was recorded on 18.01.18. There is no material on record to show that P.W.1 Najbunisa is tampered by the accused. After the cross­examination of accused, this witness was not crossed by the prosecution, calling her for re­examination. Therefore, it is very difficult to hold that P.W.1 Najbunisa is tampered by the accused. Consequently, presumption cannot be drawn in favour of prosecution and against accused, as per section 29 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. As such, I have no other option, than to record my findings to points in the negative. In the result, I proceed to pass the following order. ORDER 1] Accused Bhavesh Prakash Auti is hereby, acquitted under sec. 235(1) of the Criminal Procedure Code, of the offences punishable u/s. 354(A)(1)(i) of I.P.C. and u/s. 7 punishable u/s. 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] Accused Bhavesh Prakash Auti be enlarged on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ with surety of like amount. The effect of this bail order will remain in force for the period of six months from today, as per section 437­(A) of Cr.P.C. 7 S.C. No. 09/2014. 3] Muddemal being worthless, be destroyed after appeal period is over. Thane, (A.S. Bhaisare) Date­ 05.03.2018. Additional Sessions Judge­2 and Special Judge (POCSO Act), Thane.

POINTS FINDINGS 1 Does the prosecution prove that on 26.10.2013 at about 12.00 hours to 12.45 hours at 3rd floor of KGN Hospital, Piranipada, Bhiwandi, accused committed rape on victim girl by inserting his finger in her private part and thereby committed an offence punishable u/sec. 376 of IPC? .. Yes. 2 Does the prosecution further prove that on the above mentioned date,time and ..4/- ..4.. Spl.C. No.11/2014 (Exh.No. 62) place accused committed penetrative sexual assault on victim girl by inserting his finger in her private part and thereby committed an offence punishable u/sec. 4 .. REASONS Points Nos. 1 & 2 : 6] Both points are interlinked to each other, hence in order to avoid the repetition of evidence they are clubbed together. 7] Prosecution examined in all 7 witnesses. P.W.1 informant Najarin at Exh.13, PW 2 victim at Exh.26,PW 3 Dr.Nazia at Exh.30,PW 4 Amir at Exh.34,PW 5 Mohd. Ansari at Exh.38,PW 6 Iftiyar at Exh.42and PW 7 Deshmukh­I.O. at Exh.53. Then prosecution filed evidence closing pursis at Exh.60. Statement of accused recorded u/s 313 of Cr.P. C.is at Exh.61. Prosecution relied on documents viz. Complaint Exh.14,medical certificates Exhs. 32 & 33, panchanamas Exhs.39,45 & 46,birth certificate Exh.55, arrest panchanama Exh.56 & C.A. reports Exhs. 57 & 58 8] The Ld. APP submitted that incident took place on 26.10.2013 at about 12.00 hours to 12.45 hours on the terrace of KGN Hospital. Then on the very day report was lodged. Prior to the incident victim was playing with her friend Amir and then accused gave Rs. 6/­ to Amir and took victim to the spot, removed her salvar and inserted finger in her vagina. Medical Officer also corroborated about injuries on vagina. The fact of identification of accused is brought on record in the evidence of victim and Amir and both are minor. There is no possibility ..5/- ..5.. Spl.C. No.11/2014 (Exh.No. 62) of false implication of accused in the crime as no rivalry/enmity is brought on record by accused. However, she fairly admitted that before lodging of complaint, complainant washed the clothes of victim but prior to that she noticed blood stains on the salvar. Prosecution proved the case of rape and penetrative sexual assault beyond all reasonable doubt as accused failed to overcome the presumption. 9] The Ld.defence counsel vehemently submitted that informant is not the eyewitness to the incident. Victim failed to state name of person who committed incident. On terrace of KGN Hospital there is a gate which is always closed by putting lock and as such, no incident took place as alleged by the prosecution. Apart form that, in that vicinity work of construction was going on and as such, no one can commit offence of rape on day time as anybody can see the same. The father of victim always boosted to victim and Amir against accused and also used to show his photo on mobile. I.O. failed to record statements of those girls who took victim to her house. There is no test identification parade and as such accused is entitled for benefit of doubt. 10] PW 1 Najarin is the mother of victim and she deposed at Exh.13 and in her evidence, complaint Exh.14 is exhibited. According to her, on the day of incident victim went out of house for play around 12.00 noon and Amir was playing with her. After about one hour, 4 girls brought victim and told that they noticed that victim was crying in front of New National School,Urdu High School,Bhiwandi. That time, victim was crying. When she enquired then she came to know that victim and alongwith Amir were playing on ground,one person came there and gave Rs.6/­ to Amir and asked her to accompany ..6/- ..6.. Spl.C. No.11/2014 (Exh.No. 62) him and stated that he would give something to eat and took her terrace of KGN Hospital. He removed her salvar and inserted his finger in the place of urination. (above incident is exactly deposed by victim in her evidence at Exh.26). 11] PW 1 Najarin also deposed that she noticed blood stains and injuries at the place of urination. She washed her legs and salvar. Thus, though PW 1Najarin is not eyewitness to the incident but when she noticed blood stains on the person and salvar of victim,then her evidence is relevant as per S.6 of the Evidence Act. So far as her cross examination is concerned, the Ld. Defence counsel submitted that witness do not know Marathi and report is in Marathi and she understands little Marathi. When report Exh.14 is exhibited then one can read the contents mentioned in it and the evidence given by the informant. Inspite of searching cross examination there is no omission and contradiction which shows that the language is not the barrier. The Ld. Defence counsel also drew attention towards her cross examination on the point of that area of hospital is crowded one. She does not know whether there is a watchman at the gate of hospital and there is lock to the door on the terrace of said hospital and key is always with the watchman. After incident, they had been there and found that there was lock to the door of terrace and she do not recollect who brought key and opened the same. At the time of incident, what was the position of that terrace regarding putting lock to door or not is not important but the relevant fact is that victim herself disclosed and showed the spot of incident. Apart from that, I.O. recorded the memorandum of accused in order to verify the spot of incident. It is to be noted that memorandum is not covered u/s 27of the Evidence Act ..7/- ..7.. Spl.C. No.11/2014 (Exh.No. 62) but important fact is that victim and accused showed one and the same spot. 12] The evidence of informant is not shattered on any point and there are no omissions and contradictions in her evidence. Defence failed put a single suggestion about any previous enmity or the nursing grudge against accused at any point of time prior to the incident. Thus, the evidence of this witness is supported to the version of victim on post incident facts, whereas, the evidence of Amir PW 4 is material and he supported to the version of victim on pre­incident facts as according to him when both were playing accused came there and gave Rs.6/­ to him and took victim on the pretext to give her something. The Ld. Defence counsel put suggestion that father of victim briefing him on the point of identification of accused during trial. When Amir identified accused in the natural course as accused gave him Rs. 6/­ then there is no substance in the contention of defence that at the instance of father of victim Amir identified accused. Evidence of this witness is not influenced by any possibility of tutoring. Thus, his evidence cannot be branded as a tutored, interested or chance witness . 13] Victim deposed about incident as mentioned in the FIR Exh.14 and deposed by informant. Therefore, it is just and proper to advent on her cross examination. She stated that Rs.6/­ means five plus one. Her father had told to identify person who did act with her. The fact of showing photograph of accused is denied by victim. That cannot mean that father of victim tutored to her to identify accused. She denied that the person committing act of fingering to her was not the accused before the Court and was some other boy. She also denied that at the instance of her parents she deposed false against the accused. ..8/- ..8.. Spl.C. No.11/2014 (Exh.No. 62) The evidence of victim is not exaggerated on any count. Apart from that, her evidence seems to be natural one. In the cross examination,there is nothing brought by the defence to prove contrary to the case of prosecution. Thus, evidence of victim is trustworthy, reliable and inspires confidence. 14] PW 3 Dr.Nazia deposed that on 26.10.2013 she was on duty as gynecologist at IGM Hospital, Bhiwandi. Police brought victim to hospital. Her parents were with her. History was given by mother of victim. She examined her and found that there was redness and swelling on her private part. There was small posterior commissure fresh tear present with minimal bleeding. She opined that injury could be possible by fingering of private part. Her hymen was found intact. She issued certificates Exhs.32 & 33. In cross examination she stated that before bringing victim to hospital, her private parts were already washed and urine was already passed. The victim was examined by doctor at 11.45 p.m. whereas incident took place about 00.45 p.m. in the noon and as such, the Ld.defence counsel vehemently submitted that there is delay of 11 hours in medical examination of victim. It is to be noted that when informant came to know about the incident, she without wasting any time went to police station, then I do not find any intentional delay in getting victim medically examined on the part of informant. Apart from that, even otherwise, there is delay in medical examination, but medical officer found above injuries on the person of victim. Thus, delay is not the sole ground to discard the medical certificates issued by this witness PW 3 Nazia, as no suggestion is given by defence either to PW 1 Najarin or PW 2 victim that self inflicted injuries caused on the private part of victim by them only with intention to drag accused in false case out vengeance. ..9/- ..9.. Spl.C. No.11/2014 (Exh.No. 62) 15] In the cross examination of PW 3 suggestion was given that the injury to private part of child is possible if it comes in contact with hard object and in that case bleeding injury cannot be observed after 11 hours. She further stated that however, if private part of child comes in contact with hard object in such cases, bleeding is not possible. She denied suggestion that no injuries as mentioned in certificate Exh.32 were found on the private part of victim. She also denied that she issued false certificate without examination. When intimacy of this medical officer with victim or at any point of time, there was grudge of this medical officer against accused is not brought on record then I find no substance in the suggestion to issue a false certificate without examination. On the contrary, medical officer is not the witness of prosecution or defence but this witness helps to Court being expert to come to right conclusion with the help of medical jurisprudence. Thus, entire cross examination is not based on medical jurisprudence. 16] PW 5 Mohd. Asad deposed that in his presence police prepared spot panchanama on 3rd floor of KGN Hospital. There construction was goingon. There were two hips of sand and police collected two samples of sand and sealed the same separately and obtained his signature on panchanama Exh.39. In his cross examination he admitted that panchanama was already prepared in police station and his signature was obtained. He had not read over the contents of panchanama. Under such circumstances, the question goes to the root of the case as to how he knows the contents of the panchanama Exh.39 which is stated in his examination in chief. Thus, it can be inferred that due to fear of accused or otherwise, witness thought it proper to support to the defence in the cross examination but that cannot ..10/- ..10.. Spl.C. No.11/2014 (Exh.No. 62) diminish the evidenciary value of his testimony as his examination in chief is corroborated to the contents of panchanama Exh.39. 17] PW6 Iftikar Ansari deposed that on 27.10.2013 police seized shirt and pant of accused under panchanama Exh.45 and thereafter, police also seized clothes of victim brought by informant under panchanama Exh.46. He identified all the six articles. In his cross examination it is brought on record that he had gone to police for enquiry of his passport and then I.O.called him as panch. He denied that panchanama was not prepared in his presence. As to why this panch was present in the police station is brought on record by the defence itself in his cross examination then I find no substance to discard his evidence on the count that he is a chance witness. 18] I.O. deposed as per the chargesheet. In the evidence of I.O. Deshmukh it is brought on record that as name of accused is disclosed in the FIR, his test identification parade was not conducted. He also denied that statement of victim and Amir was recorded as per the say of informant. Surprisingly enough, accused gave suggestion to I.O. that there was enmity between him and informant on account of money but such type of suggestion was not put up to PW 1 Najarin. Even accused failed to state that he was required to recover Rs. 25,000/­ from father of victim in his statement u/s 313 of Cr.P.C. Thus, it shows that such type of defence is nothing but an eyewash. 19] Thus, on marshalling the evidence of victim and Amir then the prosecution has proved the pre­incident presence of accused and also his identification. When the evidence of victim read with medical evidence on record then it is clear that on the day of incident, accused ..11/- ..11.. Spl.C. No.11/2014 (Exh.No. 62) inserted his finger in the private part of victim and that caused injuries whichis proved beyond reasonable doubt. In the same way the evidence of victim read with the evidence of informant, then the post incident facts regarding injuries on the private part of victim and blood stains on the person and salvar of victim boosted to the case of prosecution that due to insertion of finger in the private part of victim, accused committed rape on her as per the provision of S. 375(b) of IPC which reads as inserts, to any extent, any object or a part of body, not being the penis, into the vagina,the urethra or anus of a woman or makes her to do so with him or any other person, which is punishable u/s 376 of IPC. 20] As per S. 29 and 30 of POCSO Act, the presumption is in favour of prosecution. Inspite of searching cross examination, defence failed to overcome the presumption. The evidence of victim shows that she was though aged about 5 years at the time of incident but she was in a position to understand what was happened on that day with her. Her evidence is sufficient to establish that accused committed penetrative sexual assault as defined in S. 3 of POCSO Act as he inserted his finger in her private part. When victim is minor and accused committed penetrative sexual assault as defined in S. 3 of the POCSO Act, then accused is liable to punish for penetrative sexual assault as per S.4 of POCSO Act. With this, I record my finding to the point Nos. 1 & 2 accordingly and pause here to hear the accused on the point of sentence. He is only earning member in his family, therefore, lenient view be taken while awarding the sentence. The Ld. APP Smt. I­284/2014 registered at Shil Daighar police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 370(a) of I.P.C. and section 4, 5, 7(b)(1) of Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act (hereinafter in short ''I.T.P.A.'') and also under 2, 5(j), 6, 8 11(6), 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short ''P.O.C.S.O. It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant had forced the victim women to indulge in prostitution business and the applicant thereby earned her livelihood. It is further contended and argued on behalf of applicant that she has never indulged in conducting prostitution business. It is further contended that the applicant was serving as a maid servant with accused no.1 and therefore she is falsely implicated in this crime. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, she will co­operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that information was received by police that the accused persons were compelling the victim women to indulge in prostitution business and even also used to induce them to go with customer for prostitution and the accused were thereby earning money for own gain. It is further .. 2 .. bail 82/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victims and the prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail the accused may again repeat the offence and even she may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offence charged against the accused is of very serious nature under section 370(a) of I.P.C. and section 4, 5, 7(b)(1) of I.T.P.A and also under 2, 5(j), 6, 8 11(6), 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, the role attributed to the applicant/accused is that she was serving as a maid servant with accused no.1 who is stated to be the main accused. Then, though it is contended that provisions of P.O.C.S.O. Act may not be applicable since no allegations of sexual assault by the applicant/accused are there, such submissions on behalf of applicant cannot be said to be sustainable since the victim girl is stated to be minor aged 17 years and it is alleged that the applicant/accused with co­accused had indulged in compelling the minor girl to do prostitution. But still as mentioned above the role attributed to the applicant/accused is only that she was working as a maid servant and even the mobile phone number on which call was made by the bogus customer at the time of trap was the mobile number of the accused no.1. Then, as is clear further that the investigation in the matter is completed and charge sheet is already submitted and there appear no question of investigation being hampered because of the applicant/accused on bail. .. 3 .. bail 82/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) 4] Then, it is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. 5] In that respect it is contended by the applicant that she is permanent resident of the address given and she will not abscond if released on bail and that she is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 6] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 7] Then, it has also to be mentioned that though the investigation in the matter is completed and the charge sheet is submitted, it would take time to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 8] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ .. 4 .. bail 82/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Reshma Pradip More is released on P.R. bond of Rs.25,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one or two sureties in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ The applicant/accused shall attend the concerned police station on every Wednesday between 3.00 p.m. to 5.00 p.m. and shall co­operate in investigation. She shall not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and the prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. She shall not leave India without permission of this Court. She shall furnish proof of residence. Date : 27.02.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.

Learned Advocate Shri. D.G. Bist, for the accused. ___________________________________________________________ JUDGMENT (Delivered on 04.08.2017.) 1] Accused Ashutosh @ Aasu Madnesh Pande, is facing trial for the offences punishable u/s. 354(A)(1)(ii)(2) of I.P.C. and u/s. 7 punishable under section 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2 Special (POCSO) Case No. 12/2014. 2012. 2] It is the case of prosecution that one namely Pandit is neighbourer of informant Smt. Ishrat Khurshid Ansari. Other also are the neighbourers of her. On 14.08.13 at about 9.00 p.m., her daughter/victim aged about 5 years, had been to the house of Pandit, as to view T.V. After sometime, she went to the house of Shri. Pandit to call her daughter. At that time, neighbourer Hemavati Manjula and relative of Shri. Pandit were found there. Informant had called her daughter, but in vain. Therefore, she returned back to her house. At about 9.30 p.m., victim returned back to her house and asked for dinner. Complainant had served her dinner. While having dinner, victim had stated as “Shubham Ka Chacha Bahot Ganda Hai. Mai T.V. Dekh Rahi Thi Tab Wah Mere Pas Aake Wah Muze Uske Pantme Hat Dalneko Kah Raha Tha. Aur Muze Usne Uske Najdik Khichke Dabocha”. On enquiry, victim had shown her readiness to identify the said boy. So, she along with her daughter, went to the house of Pandit. However, none were found there. However, daughter­in­law of Pandit had stated that her nephew Ashu Pande was viewing T.V. So, there was hot talk with the family members of Shri. Pandit. People were gathered. Victim had narrated her incident. Thereafter, complainant returned back to her house. Then, she along with her co­sister (wife of her brother­in­law) Heena Salimahmed Ansari along with one Dharmendra Choube went to police station. Complainant had lodged her report Exh.22. On that basis, offence vide C.R. no. 354­A (i)(ii) and (2) of I.P.C. and u/s. 7/8 of Protection Of Children From Sexual Offences Act. W.P.S.I. Smt. Choudhary had carried out investigation. She rushed to the spot and recorded spot panchanama Exh.22. Accused was arrested by A.S.I. Shri. Khairnar (Exh.26). Statements of witnesses were recorded. Statement of 3 Special (POCSO) Case No. 12/2014. victim was recorded in question­answer form in presence of Special Executive Officer Smt. Meenal Sankhe. After investigation, she submitted her charge­sheet in the Special Court. 3] My learned Predecessor framed the charge against the accused for the offences punishable under section 354(A)(1)(ii)(2) of I.P.C. and u/s. 7 punishable under section 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012, on 26/03/2015. Details of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular, to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. His defence is of total denial. 4] During trial, defence has admitted no documents. 5] To bring home the guilt of the accused for the charges leveled against him, the prosecution has examined as many as six witnesses i.e. P.W. Name of witness Exh. Description No. No. 1] Ishrat Khurshid Ansari 11 Complainant. 2] Tehrim Khurshid Ansari 14 Minor victim girl. 3] Dharmendra Nandlal 16 The person knowing Choube complainant and accused. 4] Mustakin Ilayat Khan 18 Panch of spot panchanama. 5] Sushil Ravindra Sakpal 21 P.S.I. who prepared spot panchanama. 6] Nisha Ramesh 25 Investigating officer. Choudhary 6] Accused did not enter into witness box. But, he has examined one witness in his defence, namely Savitri Sanjaykumar Pandey, who is his aunt. 7] Heard learned A.P.P. Shri. Yogendra Madhukar Patil, for the 4 Special (POCSO) Case No. 12/2014. State and learned counsel Shri. D.G. Bist for the accused. Following points arise for my determination, which are being answered for the reasons given herein­below. POINTS FINDINGS 1] Whether prosecution proved that the No. accused on 14.08.2013 during 9.00 to 9.30 p.m., in the house of Prem Pandey, used criminal force against victim girl aged about five years, by telling her to put her hand inside his pant and pulled her near to him and pressed her with intent to outrage her modesty, thereby, committed an offence punishable u/s. 354­(A)(1)(ii), (2) of I.P.C. and u/s. 7 punishable with sec. 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 ? 2] What order ? As per final order. REASONS POINT NO. 1 8] It has come in the evidence of P.W.2 victim girl that she liked to watch T.V. There is no T.V. in her house. She used to go to her neighbourers to watch T.V. She know Shubham, who is staying in front of her house. He resides along with his parents, his grand­mother and her uncle. She only once had been to the house of Shubham to watch T.V. When she had been to the house of Shubham, she herself, uncle of Shubham and one lady were present there. At that time, accused told her to put her hand in his underwear. She told to the accused that she would tell it 5 Special (POCSO) Case No. 12/2014. to her mother. Thereafter, she returned back to her home and while having her dinner, she had disclosed the same to her mother, as Shubham's uncle is not a good man, her hand was held by him and pulled her near him. Thereafter, she along with her mother, came to the house of Shubham, but accused was not present there. 9] From her cross­examination, it can be gathered that at morning also, she was in the company of her mother and brother to police station. However, police had not enquired the matter with her. When they had been to the house of Shubham, at that time, her mother had quarreled with mother of Shubham. Since then, she was not playing with Shubham. After 15.08.13, she never had been to police station. 10] P.W.1 Ishrat Khurshid Ansari deposed in her evidence that on 14.08.13, she was present at her house. Her daughter i.e. victim had been to the house of Pandit 'Chacha' to view T.V. Victim returned back at about 9.30 p.m. and asked for meal. She served meal to her. When she was having her meal, she stated as “Shubham's uncle is not a good man” ('Shubhamke Chacha Gande Hai'). On enquiry, victim had stated that she was told by uncle of Shubham that to put her hand in his pant and he was pulling her near him. Victim told to him that she escaped anyhow and ran away from there and returned to her home. She also further deposed that thereafter, she along with victim came to the house of Pandit. But, none were found there. Thereafter, mother of Shubham came there. She admitted that accused was present. When she was disclosing the incident to the mother of Shubham, quarrel was taken place. People were gathered. Victim had disclosed the incident. Thereafter, she along with her brother­ in­law Naim Ansari and with one Choube, went to police station and lodged her report. 6 Special (POCSO) Case No. 12/2014. 11] From her cross­examination, it can be gathered that Pandit 'Chacha' is her neighbourer since many years. She knew children of Pandit by name. Room of the Pandit is small adm. 10 x 10 fts. In that room, there is T.V., bed and other articles. There are two rooms to the house of Pandit. There is lane on both sides of his room. Her house is situated behind the house of Pandit. There are other rooms adjoining to her room. Pyarelal Gupta was her relative. He was residing at some distance of her house. Pyarelal Gupta and his family were staying near the house of her father­in­ law. People used to come and go from the lane which was passing from the front side of the house of Pandit and this witness. At small distance from her house, there is Hajari Dargah which is crowded place. Her locality is quite crowded, even at the night time. Her neighbourers are also having television set at their houses. If from the house of Pandit, she calls loudly, then it is audible to her. If she calls from her lane, then same is audible to the house of Pandit. While going to the house of Pandit, victim had not informed this witness about the same. Victim after returning back, told that she had been to the house of Pandit to view T.V. Victim sometimes, used to go to the house of other neighbourers to watch T.V. Shubham is aged about 7 to 8 years. Her brother­in­law Naim Ansari resides near Hajuri Dargah. He sells Wada­Pav. She did not know whether there is any criminal case pending against Naim Ansari. Dharmendra Choube was social worker of her vicinity. Her brothers and mother are accused in the case of attempt to commit murder of Pyarelal Gupta by firing on him. They all were arrested and convicted in that case. Shubham's mother alleged that this witness was telling lie. 12] P.W.3 Dharmesh Choube deposed in his evidence that at relevant night and time, when he was proceeding, he noticed a gathering of 7 Special (POCSO) Case No. 12/2014. people. He made enquiry. Naim Ansari @ Raju told that his niece had disclosed that one boy told to her to put her hand in his under­pant. 13] He deposed in his cross­examination that when he met with Naim Ansari and disclosed the incident, at that time, he was helping to search the accused at the house of Bramhin people for around 20 minutes, to avoid any conflict between two groups. Police had not written his statement in his presence. 14] P.W.5 Sushil Sakpal deposed in his evidence that on 15.08.13 at 01.20 a.m., complainant had lodged her report. Thereafter, he rushed to the spot and recorded spot panchanama in presence of two panchas. P.W.6 is a formal witness, who has deposed as per her investigation. 15] P.W.6 W.P.S.I. Smt. Nisha Chaudhary has also deposed as per her investigation. 16] From the evidence of P.W.1 Irshad Ansari, it can be gathered that the victim was going to the house of neighbourers to view T.V. Prior to the day of incident, victim never had been to the house of aunt of accused i.e. house of Shubham, to view T.V. Besides, P.W.1 Smt. Irshad Ansari was not told by victim that she was going to the house of Shubham to view T.V. However, surprisingly and directly P.W.1 had been to the house of Shubham to see her daughter i.e. victim. At that time, victim, accused and one other woman were found there. Nothing was asked by her to them, nor she had carried victim to her house. 17] From the evidence of P.W.1 Irshad Ansari, it cannot be gathered that none from the family of Master Shubham were not present and were not viewing the T.V. From her evidence, it can be gathered that she had been to the house of Shubham. His mother was present. But, this 8 Special (POCSO) Case No. 12/2014. witness had quarreled with her. It was crowded place. There is road from both sides of the house of Shubham. There is also one Dargah. However, no independent witnesses were gathered on the spot. Husband of complainant was not in the company of her to police station to lodge the report though he was present in the house at relevant night. Dharmendra Choube, a social worker had been to police station. From the cross­ examination of victim, it can be seen that she had deposed before the court as per say of her mother. If other persons were present at relevant time on the spot, then it is difficult to believe the version of P.W.1 and 2 that in the presence of family members of Shubham, accused had done such heinous act. Undoubtedly, accused had not brought any ground why he is involved in the case by the complainant. However, the burden has to be discharged by the prosecution to prove the case against accused beyond all reasonable doubts and thereafter, the burden would shift upon the accused to discharge it. Merely on the basis of presumption, accused cannot be convicted. 18] It has come in the evidence of D.W.1 Smt. Savitri Pandey that Shubham is her son and accused Ashutosh Pandey is her nephew. She resides close to Nasareen's house and her mother's name is Ishrat Ansari. On 14.08.2013 at about 7.00 p.m., accused had come to her house and he left her house at about 07.45 p.m. At about 8.00 to 8.15 p.m., Ishrat's daughter Tehrim came to her house and stayed for about 10 to 15 minutes. Thereafter, Tehrim left her house. After some time, Ishrat came to her house and enquired about Shubham's uncle. She started making allegations against Shubham's uncle. She was also asking about accused Ashutosh. She told her that he had already left. Ishrat started fighting with her and then, lodged a police complaint. 19] It has further come in her evidence that when police came to 9 Special (POCSO) Case No. 12/2014. her house, she informed that Ashutosh had come to her house only between 7.00 to 7.45 p.m. and thereafter, he left. Police did not call her to take her statement. 20] It has come in the cross­examination of Savitri Sanjaykumar Pandey that she did not know where Ashutosh resides. She did not know where they reside. On 14.08.13, Ashutosh had been to her house. He is studying in U.P. 21] Having considered the facts and circumstances of the matter, evidence on record and discussed reasons, it can safely be said that prosecution failed to prove the alleged offence against accused beyond all reasonable doubts. I therefore, answer to the point no.1 in the negative. In the result, I proceed to pass the following order. ORDER 1] Accused Ashutosh @ Aasu Madnesh Pande, is hereby, acquitted under sec. 235(1) of the Criminal Procedure Code, of the offences punishable u/s. 354(A)(1)(ii) (2) of I.P.C. and u/s. 7 punishable under section 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] Accused Ashutosh @ Aasu Madnesh Pande, be enlarged on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ with surety of like amount. The effect of this bail order will remain in 10 Special (POCSO) Case No. 12/2014. force for the period of six months from today, as per section 437­(A) of Cr.P.C. Thane, (A.S. Bhaisare) Date­ 04.08.2017. Additional Sessions Judge­2 and Special Judge (POCSO Act), Thane.

1 Bail No. 126/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) Criminal Bail Application No.126/2016 Shehnaz Abu Baker Shaikh .. Applicant versus The State of Maharashtra (Through A.P.M.C. Police Station) .. Non­applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 1] By this application the applicant is seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. who was arrested 26/07/2015 by A.P.M.C.Police Station in connection with C.R.No. I­ 180/2015 registered for an offence punishable under section 363, 366(A), 376, 354 r/w. 34 of I.P.C. and section 4 ,6,8,10, and 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as P.O.C.S.O. Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Smt. Asma Sayyad for the applicant/accused and Spl. P.P. S.E.Phad for State. I.O. absent. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 24/07/2015 at the instance of the informant/father of the victim­girl aged about 16 years with an indictment that his minor daughter was kidnapped by some unknown persons. During investigation it was revealed that accused No.1 Sohel enticed and kidnapped the victim­girl and sexually assaulted her and accused No.2 mother of accused No.1 and accused No.3 aided and abeted the said crime. 2 Bail No. 126/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) 4] The learned Counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant/accused is falsely implicated. She submitted that present applicant is mother of accused No.1 Sohel and the victim­girl and accused No.1 Sohel were having love affair. The only role assigned to the present victim is that she wore the bangles to the victim­girl. She submitted that the present applicant has no role in the alleged crime, neither she instigated nor she abeted the crime. The applicant is lady of 58 years and since 7 months she is behind bars. The investigation is completed and charge­sheet is submitted in the court. The other lady co­accused is released on bail and the accused is entitled for the benefit of parity. The accused permanent resident of Mankhurd, Mumbai. The accused is ready to abide any conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing him on bail. 5] Per contra, Spl.P.P. strongly opposed the application submitting that the age of victim­girl is 16 years. The present applicant accused is equally involved in the serious offence. She submitted that the intention and knowledge of the present applicant is clear from the statement of the victim­girl. She abeted the serious offence. The parity is not applicable to her as her role is specified by the victim­girl. There are chances of tampering with witnesses and prayed for rejection of application. 3 Bail No. 126/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R., it appears that the initially F.I.R. was lodged by the father of the victim­girl about the kidnapping of his daughter. During investigation it was revealed that the accused Sohel enticed the victim­girl and took her to his house to accused No.2 and there he performed the marriage with the victim against her wish and the present applicant / accused abeted the said crime. It further appears that thereafter accused No.1 Sohel committed sexual assault on the victim­girl. The submission of the learned counsel for applicant tht accused No.1 and victim­girl is having love affair is required to be considered at the time of trial. As the trial is yet to be commenced, hence I restrained myself from making any further comment on the merit of the case. However, prima­ facie it appears that the prime allegatiions about the kidnapping and sexual assault are against the main accused Sohel and the present accused is stated to be the abetor. The investigation is completed and charge­sheet is recently submitted in the court. Looking to the huge pendency of cases of Under Trial Prisoners the trial of the case would take some time. Further the another lady co­accused is already released on bail whose roleis also similar to the role of present applicant. Hence, applicant is entitled for the benefit of rule of parity. The object of bail is neither punitive nor preventive but to secure the presence of the accused at the time of trial. No fruitful purpose would be served further incarceration of the accused. She is ready to abide by the conditions imposed by the Court. In such circumstances the 4 Bail No. 126/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) apprehension of Spl.P.P. about tampering of witnesses can be addressed by imposing suitable conditions. Hence, I pass the following order ­ ORDER 1) The application is allowed. 2) Applicant namely Shehnaz Abu Baker Shaikh be released on bail on his executing P.R. Bond of ₹15,000/­ [Rupees fifteen thousand only] with one local solvent surety in the like amount on the following conditions ­ A] Applicant shall not contact with the victim­girl in any manner and shall not threaten or pressurize the victim­girl and prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with prosecution evidence. C] Applicant shall furnish his and his two blood relatives' address proofs and contact numbers and he is duty bound to inform I.O. and Court about the change of address, if any. Thane. Date : 09.02.2016. (Ms. U.M. Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act), Thane.

1 Anticipatory Bail No. 131/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) Anticipatory Bail Application No.131/2016 1 ) Ramesh Chandar Mirka. 2 ) Sachin Ramesh Mirka. 3) Sojan Dashrath Mirka. .. Applicants versus The State of Maharashtra Through Nizampura P.S. .. Non-applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 1] By this application the applicants are seeking their release on anticipatory bail under section 438 of Cr.P.C. being apprehending their arrest at the hands of Niampura Police Station in connection with C.R.No.I- 7/2016 registered for an offence punishable under section 354(A) 323, 324,504 r/w 34 of I.P.C. and section 7 and 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as P.O.C.S.O. Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Mr. M.R. Khan for the applicant/accused and learned A.P.P. Mrs. R.A.Navale for State. I.O. present. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 11.01.2016 at the instance of the informant/victim-girl aged about 15 2 Anticipatory Bail No. 131/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) years with an indictment that since 2-3 months accused Sachin Mirka uttered the word with intent to sexual harassment to the victim-girl and on 4.1.2016 he outraged her modesty. Further for the said reasons on 10.0.1.216 accsued Sachin alongwith his brother and father i.e. the other accused abused and beat victim and her father by fist and kick blows and by wooden rod and also abused and beaten the persons who tried to intervene the quarrel. 4] The learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicants-accused are falsely implicated. He further submitted that in fact the allegations about outraging the modesty are against applicant no.2 Sachin only. He further submitted that the further allegation about the abuse and assault is stated to be against other accused and the Section 323, 324and 504A of I.P.C. are bailable offences and therefore, custodial interrogation of the applicants is not necessary. He even submitted that there is nothing to recover from the applicants and therefore, no custodial interrogation is necessary. They are ready to co- operate in the investigation and ready to abide by conditions imposed by the Court and prayed that the applicants be protected by the order of anticipatory bail. 5] Per contra, the learned A.P.P. opposed the application submitting that the offence is in respect of minor girl. The main accused outraged modesty of the victim girl and the other accused assaulted father and 3 Anticipatory Bail No. 131/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) brother of the informant and also used wooden rod. The investigation is in progress and the custodial interrogation of the accused is necessary and prayed for rejection of the application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R. it appears that the serious allegations about the outraging the modesty of the victim girl are made in the F.I.R. Even it is alleged that the main accused Sachin Mirka and other accused abused and assaulted the victim and her father and also used the wooden rod for that purpose and the persons who tried to intervene, they have also been assaulted by the accused persons. The Ld. counsel for the applicants in support of his submission that even the Section 324 of I.P.C. is bailable, placed his reliance on the judgment of the Ho'ble Bombay High Court in case of Mr. Chandra Kanjappa Vs. State of Maharashtra, 2013 ALL MR (Cri.), 626. Thus, as rightly submitted by the Ld. Counsel for the applicants Section 323, 324 and 504 of I.P.C. are bailable offences. However, provisions of P.O.C.S.O. Act are applied which are non-bailable offences. Perusal of the say filed by the investigating officer, does not disclose any reason warranting custodial interrogation. No recovery is stated to be made from the applicants. Therefore, considering the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case, the custodial interrogation of the present applicants does not appear necessary. Further, applicants are ready to co-operate in 4 Anticipatory Bail No. 131/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) investigation.Therefore, conditional order directing applicants to co-operate with the investigation would facilitate the investigation. Hence, I pass the following order - ORDER 1) The application is allowed. 2) In the event of arrest of applicants namely Mr. Ramesh Chandar Mirka, Mr. Sachin Ramesh Mirka and Mr. Sojan Dashrath Mirka in connection with C.R.No.I-07/2016 registered at Nizampura Police Station for an offence punishable under section 354(A), 323, 324, 504 r/w 34 of I.P.C. and section and 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, they be released on their executing P.R. Bond of ₹ 15,000/- [rupees fifteen thousand only] each with one local solvent surety each in the like amount on the following conditions - A] Applicants shall attend the concerned police station on every Sunday and Wednesday between 10.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon till filing the charge-sheet. B] Applicants shall co-operate in investigation and shall not tamper with prosecution witnesses. C] Applicants shall not leave India without prior permission of the Court. D] The applicants shall hereinafter maintain decency. Thane. Date : 19.01.2016 (Ms. U.M. Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act), Thane.

SPECIAL CASE (POCSO) NO. 13 OF 2016 CNR : MHTH01­000329­2016 Exh. No. The State (Through Koparkhairne Police Station) ..Prosecution V/s. Siddhesh Anant Kalgutkar, Age 30 years, Occ. Service, R/o.
