P.V. Vartak. ___________________________________________________________ JUDGMENT (Delivered on 20.10.2018.) 1] Accused is facing charge for the offence punishable u/s. 376, 363 of I.P.C. along with Sec. 4 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 2 POCSO Case. No. 13/2016. The prosecution case in nut­shell is as follows : 2] That victim is daughter of the informant. At the time of alleged incident, she was 17 years old. Her date of birth is 10.03.1999. On 09.11.15 at about 05.45 p.m. the wife of informant was taking tuition of students. At that time, the victim left the home without informing anybody. When the wife of informant searched for her, she found a chit wherein it was mentioned that the victim had left the home. Therefore, the wife called the informant on phone. The informant returned home and started search of victim with her friends and relatives. However, she could not be traced. Therefore, on next date, he lodged F.I.R. for kidnapping of his daughter. 3] Investigation of the matter was conducted by A.P.I. Umesh Bapurao Mundhe. He traced the victim and on 13.11.15, he received information that victim was found by anti­human trafficking department. Thereafter, he arrested the accused and produced the victim. After medical examination of victim and accused and further investigation, it revealed that the victim had gone along with the accused and they had sexual relations. Therefore, the investigating officer filed charge­sheet against the accused for the offence punishable u/s. 363 and 376 of I.P.C. along with section 3 punishable under sec. 4 of the POCSO Act. 4] My learned predecessor framed charge against the accused for the offence punishable u/s. 376, 363 of I.P.C. and u/s. 3 punishable u/s. 4 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, vide Exh.10. The contents of charge were read over and explained to the accused by my learned predecessor in vernacular, to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed for trial. 5] While dictating the judgment, it is found that the charge below 3 POCSO Case. No. 13/2016. Exh. 10 which was framed by my learned Predecessor, has some error about the place of commission of offence u/s. 376 of I.P.C. and section 4 of the POCSO Act. As per the version of prosecution, said sexual assault had taken place at the house of maternal uncle of the accused and not at house of informant bearing S.S. III, Room No. 766, Sector No. 1, Koparkhairne, Navi Mumbai. Hence, the charge is required to be altered accordingly. Therefore, the charge against the accused came to be altered accordingly. The contents of charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular and fresh pleas were recorded. The accused pleaded not guilty for the charge and considering only change of location in the charge, both the parties conceded for passing judgment on available material on record, as they proceeded with the trial as if the accused was facing charge containing proper place of alleged offence u/s. 376 of I.P.C. and section 4 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 6] In order to prove the guilt of the accused, the prosecution examined in all five witnesses, viz. Samir Shashikant Ghadashi, panch on spot panchanama at Exh.14, mother of victim at Exh.19, victim girl at Exh.20, father of victim at Exh.25 and A.P.I. Umesh Bapurao Mundhe, investigating officer at Exh. 29. Thereafter, vide pursis Exh.38, the prosecution closed the evidence. 7] The prosecution has also relied upon the following documents­ 1] F.I.R. at Exh. 26, 2] Spot panchanama at Exh.15, 3] Statement of victim u/s. 164 of Cr.P.C. at Exh.21, 4] Seizure panchanama of clothes of victim at Exh.27. 8] Statement of accused u/s. 313 of Cr.P.C. came to be recorded to the extent of only incriminating material against him. The defence of the 4 POCSO Case. No. 13/2016. accused is of total denial and false implication. 9] Heard learned P.P. Smt. Phad for the State and learned counsel Shri. P.V. Vartak, for the accused. 10] Following points emerged for my consideration and I have recorded my findings thereon for the reasons given below. Points Findings 1] Whether the prosecution has proved No. that on 09.11.2015 at about 17.45 hours, at S.S. III, Room No. 766, Sector No.1, Koparkhairne, Navi Mumbai, accused had kidnapped the minor daughter of complainant from his lawful guardianship ? 2] Whether the prosecution has proved No. that the accused had committed penetrative sexual assault on minor victim girl at the house of maternal uncle of the accused at Ratnagiri ? 3] What order ? As per final order. REASONS 11] Ld. Special P.P. Smt. Phad for the prosecution submitted that the accused is facing charge for the offence punishable u/s. 363, 376 of I.P.C. and section 4 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. There are allegations that the victim was minor and she was taken away from the lawful guardianship of the informant. The age of the victim has not denied. Though there are certain chits addressed by the victim to his parents, however, by that itself, the accused cannot get any right to take the victim from lawful custody of the guardians. 5 POCSO Case. No. 13/2016. 12] She further submitted that P.W.1 Samir Ghadashi has proved the spot. P.W.2 mother of the victim, Nafisa had deposed about the missing of the victim and finding her at Ratnagiri with the accused. The victim informed her about the intercourse. There is no question of any consent as the victim was minor. Therefore, the charges are duly proved. P.W.3 had also narrated about physical relation. Rather, in the suggestion by the defence, it was tried to prove that it was a consensual sex. Therefore, suggestion has fortified the allegations. P.W.4 father of victim and P.W.5 investigating officer had also supported the prosecution version. The medical evidence which has admitted by the defence shows that the victim had sexual intercourse. Considering these aspects, the accused may be convicted and be punished with maximum sentence prescribed for the offence. 13] On the other hand, Ld. Counsel Shri. Prasad Vartak for the accused submitted that in the present case, it was very much necessary for the prosecution to prove age of the victim, as even alleged by the prosecution, the victim was at the verge of majority at the relevant time. Therefore, without proof of age of victim, charges under the POCSO Act cannot be attracted. He further pointed out that as per letter Exh. 22, victim herself left home by leaving chits for her parents. This shows that the accused had not taken her away from the lawful custody, but she left at her own. Rather, it is mentioned that the accused had asked her to go back. However, the victim denied. Therefore, the accused cannot be said to have committed any offence. Nothing has been done against her will or by applying any force to the victim. She could have rescued her at any time. The conduct and behaviour of the prosecutrix is also required to be considered. The ossification test of the victim was not conducted. 6 POCSO Case. No. 13/2016. Therefore, there is no medical evidence to determine the age of the victim. There is no independent witness who has either seen the victim and the accused together. There is no evidence about any sexual relation between the accused and the victim. In such circumstances, the prosecution has failed to prove the allegations of kidnapping and sexual assault as well as minority of the prosecutrix. In such situation, the accused is required to be honourably acquitted from the charges. In support of his contentions, the defence relied upon the following decisions­ 1] State of Himachal Pradesh Vs. Rajeev Kumar and others, 2017 ALL MR (Cri.) Journal, 432, 2] Gurudas s/o. Bandu Pendor Vs. The State of Maharashtra, 2015 ALL MR (Cri.) 4494, 3] Umesh Rajabhau Khandekar Vs. The State of Maharashtra, 2015 ALL MR (Cri.) 4006. 14] In the light of above submissions, it is required to scrutinize the material on record. As to Points No. 1 and 2:­ 15] It has come in the evidence of P.W.1 Samir Shashikant Ghadashi, alleged panch on spot panchanama, that, on 27.12.15, when he was at home, the police called him to the house of his neighbourer Mr. Kadu along with one Santosh Shinde and prepared spot panchanama at Exh. 15. However, he expressed ignorance as to whether any bed­sheet was seized by police. Therefore, the prosecution was permitted to ask leading questions. However, this witness denied seizure of any bed­sheet. During his cross­examination, he admitted that panchanama was already 7 POCSO Case. No. 13/2016. written. 16] It has come in the evidence of P.W.2 Nafija Kharote that since last 15 years, she is residing at Koparkhairne with the victim and other daughter. The victim was born on 10.03.99. She was studying in first year in Dr. D.Y. Patil Engineering College, Nerul. On 09.11.15 at about 5.45 p.m., when she was busy in her tuitions at house, victim left the house without informing her. Therefore, she informed her husband. Her husband returned and searched for her. However, victim could not be traced. Therefore, on 10.11.15, her husband lodged F.I.R. On 12.11.15, they received phone­call from Crime Branch, inquiring details about the victim. On 13.11.15, they came to know that victim was found at Ratnagiri. Therefore, she went with her husband and police to Ratnagiri. She found her daughter as well as accused at the police station. On enquiry, she was told by her daughter that her daughter had called the accused. Therefore, he had came to Koparkhairne railway station. She went there. Then, both of them went to Vashi by railway. Then, they went to Ratnagiri by luxury bus and then to Goa. Thereafter, they returned back to the house of maternal uncle of accused at Ratnagiri and they established sexual relationship. When they tried to return back to Mumbai, police caught them. She identified the accused in the court. She further deposed that the victim was referred for medical examination to hospital at Vashi. So also, she had supplied school­leaving certificate of victim to police. 17] During her cross­examination, she expressed her ignorance as to whether the accused and victim were in love with each­other, or if they were knowing each­other. She denied the suggestion that she and her husband opposed their love. She deposed that her daughter left house at her own. Further, she denied the suggestion that her statement was 8 POCSO Case. No. 13/2016. recorded as per say of her husband or getting no information from her daughter. 18] It has come in the evidence of P.W.3 victim girl that she was born on 10.03.1999. Since her birth, she was residing at Koparkhairne and she knows the accused. In the year 2015, she was studying in D.Y. Patil Polytechnic College, Nerul. On 09.11.15 at about 5.30 p.m., she proceeded to Koparkhairne railway station along with her luggage. On the way, she called the accused. Therefore, he came to Koparkhairne railway station. Then, both of them proceeded to Vashi by railway. From Vashi, they went to Ratnagiri by bus and then from Ratnagiri, they went to Goa by train. Thereafter, they returned back to Ratnagiri at the house of maternal uncle of accused. They had stayed there for two days. During that night, accused had established sexual relations with victim. Thereafter, they tried to return back to Mumbai, but police had caught them at Ratnagiri. Her parents along with police came to Ratnagiri. Then, police had brought them to Thane. She was referred by police to Government hospital, Vashi. Doctor had examined her. Police had recorded her statement. So also, her statement was recorded by Ld. J.M.F.C., Vashi, as per her say. 19] During her cross­examination, she deposed that the letters at Exh. 22 to 24 are in her hand­writing. The accused and the witness were in love with each­other. She herself left the house. The accused did not kidnap her, nor kept any sexual relationship against her wish. The parents were opposing her love affair. She has no grievance against the accused. 20] P.W.4 Chandrakant Kharote also deposed on the same lines of P.W.2 and P.W.3. He had only changed his version about the physical relationship and deposed that his daughter told him that accused committed rape on her. During his cross­examination, he denied existence of any love 9 POCSO Case. No. 13/2016. affair between the victim and the accused. That letters at Exh. 22 to 24 were found in his house and he handed over them to police. That the victim herself left the house. Further, he denied the suggestion that accused did not commit rape on his daughter. 21] It has come in the evidence of P.W.5 A.P.I. Umesh Bapurao Mundhe that he was posted as A.P.I. with Koparkhairne police station from 31.7.15 to 26.8.17. Investigation of C.R. no. 356/15 was entrusted to him on 11.11.15. He had recorded the F.I.R. Exh.26, as per narration of father of the victim Chandrakant Kharote. On 11.11.15, he sent request letter Exh.30 to D.C.P. Zone I, Navi Mumbai, for tracing the cell­phone number 8286241707 and 9768674394. On 13.11.15, he received information from Anti Human Trafficking Department, especially P.S.I. Kshirsagar that they have taken custody of victim and the person who had kidnapped the victim i.e. the present accused at Ratnagiri. On the same day, they produced victim and accused at Koparkhairne police station along with report Exh.31 dated 13.11.15. 22] On 14.11.2015, he recorded statement of mother of victim, so also, sent the victim for medical examination along with letter Exh.32 dated 14.11.15. Accordingly, he received the medical reports Exh.33 of the victim of Casualty Medical Officer, N.M.M.C. hospital, Vashi. On 14.11.15, he seized the clothes of victim in presence of panchas vide seizure panchanama Exh.27. On 15.11.15, he sent intimation to Magistrate and Sessions Court about adding sections 3 and 4 of POCSO Act and section 376 of I.P.C. He also received photo­copy of school­leaving certificate of victim issued by Sai Holy Faith high­school, Koparkhairne. Accordingly, the date of birth of the victim was 10.03.99. Thereafter, he received medical reports of the accused Exh.34, issued by General Hospital 10 POCSO Case. No. 13/2016. Navi Mumbai Municipal Corporation Hospital, Vashi. On 20.11.15, he seized the clothes on the person of accused in presence of panchas vide seizure panchanama Exh. 35. Thereafter, he got recorded statement of the victim u/s. 164 of Cr.P.C. at Exh.21. Thereafter, by permission of superiors, he went to Ratnagiri and prepared spot panchanama Exh.15 of house of one Manohar Kadu, relative of accused, in presence of two panchas. He also recorded statements of witness Manohar Kadu and others. On 29.12.15, he sent seized muddemal articles to Forensic laboratory, Kalina, along with forwarding letter Exh.36. On 08.01.16, he obtained school­leaving certificate of the victim at Exh.37, issued by head­ mistress of Sai Holy Faith high­school. 23] It has further came in his evidence that it revealed during investigation that accused kidnapped minor victim, took her to Ratnagiri, had sexual relations with her, therefore, he submitted charge­sheet against him for the offence punishable u/s. 363, 376 of I.P.C. and sec. 3 and 4 of the POCSO Act. 24] During his cross­examination, he denied the suggestion that the accused was having love affair with victim. However, he deposed that they were having friendship. He admitted that parents of victim were not liking the said relationship. Though he further denied the suggestion that the victim left home on her own, however, admitted that she left home by leaving note. He admitted that the victim was not kidnapped by anybody. He admitted that he had not recorded statements of any employees in the school. 25] The defence has relied upon the decision in the case of 'State of Himachal Pradesh Vs. Rajeev Kumar and others: 2017 ALL MR (Cri.) Journal, 432'. In the said case, while acquitting the accused, the Hon'ble 11 POCSO Case. No. 13/2016. Lordships have observed that­ “Age of prosecutrix was not less than 18 years and she was consenting for the intercourse as no marks of violence found on her person. She voluntarily stayed at the residence of accused for 4­5 days. She accompanied accused No.1 at several places. She did not make any hue and cry”. 26] In the case of 'Gurudas s/o. Bandu Pendor Vs. The State of Maharashtra: 2015 ALL MR (Cri.) 4494', the Hon'ble Bombay High Court has observed in para 14 about the proof of age of the prosecutrix as follows­ “In the present case, in the absence of primary evidence, namely the birth certificate from the Gram Panchayat which would have a best evidentiary value as envisaged under section 35 of the Evidence Act and in absence of ossification test report of the prosecutrix, the prosecution loses credibility as regards the age of prosecutrix. Evaluation of the aforesaid, in my view, shows that the prosecution was unable to bring its case in respect of the age of prosecutrix beyond reasonable doubt. It would be hazardous to reach to a conclusion that the date of birth of the prosecutrix was 28.9.1998 in the light of evidence which is discussed hereinabove.” 27] In the case of 'Umesh Rajabhau Khandekar Vs. The State of Maharashtra: 2015 ALL MR (Cri.) 4006', it is observed by the Hon'ble Bombay High Court that, “When no examination regarding age of prosecutrix was carried and though head­master had examined, however, he deposed that the entry in the school register was effected on the basis of admission form filled by parents of the student and on the basis of oral information given by the father of the girl. Hence, it has observed that there is reasonable doubt as regards age of the complainant.” 12 POCSO Case. No. 13/2016. 28] In the light of the above observations, it is necessary to scrutinize as to whether the prosecution has succeeded in proving three things viz. 1] the victim was minor at the time of alleged incident, 2] she was kidnapped by the accused and 3] that the accused had sexual intercourse/assault on the victim, so also, if the prosecutrix proved to be major, then whether she was consenting party. 29] If the prosecution succeeded in proving that the victim was minor at the relevant time, then, the aspect of she being consenting party or not, is immaterial. Therefore, the age of prosecutrix would be a major factor for the decision as regard to both the alleged offences. Therefore, firstly it is necessary to scrutinize the evidence about age of the victim. On the point of age, the prosecution has produced duplicate copy of school­ leaving certificate of the victim issued by head­mistress of Sai Holy Faith High­School, wherein the date of birth of the victim is mentioned as 10.03.99. So also, the victim as well as her mother i.e. P.W.3 and P.W.2 have deposed the same date as the date of birth of the victim. However, the prosecution has not examined the concerned head­mistress of said school, so as to prove the said entry in the school­leaving certificate of date of birth of the victim. It is necessary to prove as to how and on what basis, the said entry was made in the duplicate school­leaving certificate. The original general register of the school was not produced in the court. Even, the birth certificate which is having best evidential value as envisaged u/s. 35 of the Evidence Act. Non­production of said birth certificate has created a flaw in the evidence of prosecution about age of the prosecutrix. 30] Moreover, though the prosecutrix was sent for medical examination, however, the doctor has not examined by the prosecution, nor the medical reports reflect that any ossification test of alleged victim was 13 POCSO Case. No. 13/2016. carried out by the concerned medical officer. In such situation, there is lack of sufficient material to ascertain the proper date of birth of the victim. The medical reports of the victim at Exh. 33, show that she had history of Menarche for four years. However, various other fields have kept blank. The overall findings are mentioned as consisting with sexual intercourse/assault. However, final opinion was kept pending till receipt of forensic science laboratory report. The medical officer has not even taken pains to score either of the words 'intercourse/assault'. Even the final report has not produced on record. In such circumstances, even the medical examination report is not helpful for determination of age of the prosecutrix. The item No. 6 about local examination of genitals etc. has also not filled up by the medical officer. In such situation, there is no material to ascertain exact date of birth of the prosecutrix and therefore, there is reasonable doubt about the age of the prosecutrix. 31] Even as per the prosecution case, she was 16 years and 9 months old at the time of alleged incident. In case, when the medical evidence of ossification test comes, there also sometimes the opinion used to be given as approximate age of the prosecutrix with variance of two years plus or minus. In such cases also, the deviation is required to be considered by the court. However, in the present case, the prosecution has failed to bring on record proper evidence. Under such circumstances, the material on record is not sufficient to ascertain that the prosecutrix was minor at the time of alleged incident and there is reasonable doubt about her minority. It is settled position of law that whenever there is reasonable doubt about the prosecution case, benefit of the same would always goes to the accused. Hence, it is required to be held that prosecution has failed to prove beyond reasonable doubt that at the relevant time, i.e. as on 09.11.15, 14 POCSO Case. No. 13/2016. the prosecutrix was minor i.e. below 18 years of age. 32] Though it is held that the prosecution has failed to prove the minority of the prosecutrix at the relevant time, however, on that ground itself, the accused cannot be acquitted from the charges. At the most, the charges under POCSO Act may not be applicable to the present case. Hence, in order to ascertain the guilt of the accused for the offence punishable u/s. 363 and 376 of I.P.C., it is necessary to ascertain as to whether the accused had kidnapped the prosecutrix, so also, whether he had any sexual intercourse with the prosecutrix and if yes, whether there was valid consent of the prosecutrix for the same. 33] In the entire evidence of prosecutrix, she has deposed that she left home on her own, rather she left some letters and chits vide Exh. 22 to 24 addressing her parents that she left home on her own. Even in the statement of the prosecutrix u/s. 164 of Cr.P.C., before Ld. Magistrate, she has deposed that she had written letters to the parents, therefore, though she called the accused at about 5.30 p.m., informing him that she had left home, the accused said that she should go home. However, as she had left the letters, therefore, she thought that she cannot go back. Even, the investigating officer has admitted that the victim left a note while leaving home. It has also come in the evidence of P.W.2 and 4, mother and father of the prosecutrix that their daughter left house on her own. In such situation, when the age of the prosecutrix has not proved to be less than 18 years and when there is material that she had left the house on her own, the allegations of kidnapping the prosecutrix from lawful guardianship cannot sustain. 34] On the point of sexual assault on the prosecutrix is concerned, the prosecutrix has categorically deposed about her sexual relations with 15 POCSO Case. No. 13/2016. the accused, on the night when they were at the house of maternal uncle of the accused. Even the defence has given suggestion that she was consenting for the said physical relationship. Due to said suggestions, it can be said to have been admitted that the accused and victim had sexual intercourse on said night. Even the medical examination reports of the prosecutrix and the accused at Exh. 33 and 34 are corroborating the same, however, when the prosecutrix has admitted that the relationship of the intercourse was occurred with her free consent and when it has not proved that she was minor at the relevant time, her consent is valid one. In such situation, in my view, the prosecution has failed to prove that the accused has committed any offence u/s. 376 of I.P.C. and consequentially, the accused is required to be acquitted from the charges u/s. 363, 376 of I.P.C. as well as section 4 of the POCSO Act. Hence, points No.1 and 2 are required to be answered in negative, by holding that the prosecution has failed to prove the allegations against the accused of kidnapping and rape beyond reasonable doubt. 35] So far as muddemal property is concerned, the muddemal property at article number 1] one pink top with green dots, 2] one faint green Chudidar Payjama, 3] one faint green Odhani, 4] one blackish underpant, 5] one grey bra, 6] one blue jeans pant, 7] one dark blue full­ shirt, 8] one faint blue underpant of Scott company and 9] one bluish­faint green bed­sheet, being worthless, need to be destroyed. Hence, in answer to point No. 3, I pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused Siddhesh Anant Kalgutkar, is hereby, acquitted under sec. 235(1) of the 16 POCSO Case. No. 13/2016. Criminal Procedure Code, from the offence punishable u/s. 376, 363 of I.P.C. and Sec. 4 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 2] Accused is in jail. Hence, jail authority is hereby, directed to release the accused forthwith, if he is not required in any case or crime. 3] Muddemal property at article number 1] one pink top with green dots, 2] one faint green Chudidar Payjama, 3] one faint green Odhani, 4] one blackish underpant, 5] one grey bra, 6] one blue jeans pant, 7] one dark blue full­shirt, 8] one faint blue underpant of Scott company and 9] one bluish­faint green bed­sheet, be destroyed after appeal period is over. 4] Accused is hereby directed to furnish bail bond of Rs.15,000/­ with a surety of like amount, so as to appear before the higher Court in compliance with Sec. 437­A of Code of Criminal Procedure. 5] Pronounced in open court. Thane, (V.Y. Jadhav) Date­ 20.10.2018. Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

1 Bail No 142/2016. (order below Exhibit 1) Criminal Bail Application No.142/2016 Sabina Usman Qureshi&1 .. Applicant versus The State of Maharashtra Through Mumbra Police Station .. Non-applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 1] By this application, applicants are seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C., who are arrested on 05/01/2016 by Mumbra Police Station in connection with C.R.No.I-11/2016 registered for an offence punishable under section 370(2)(3) of I.P.C. and section 4, 8, 17 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act), and section 3, 4, 5, of Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act (hereinafter in short I.T.P.A.) 2] Heard learned advocate Mr. S.H.Pasi for the applicant/accused and learned A.P.P. Mrs.Navale for State. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 05/01/2016 at the instance of the informant API Shri. Pralhad Thakur attached with AHTC Crime branch Thane with an indictment that secret information was received about prostitution being carried out within the jurisdiction of Mumbra police station by accused Shahnaz. Therefore, trap was led and accordingly the raid was conducted at room No.202, Mahadev Apartment, Almas colony Kausa Mumbra with the help of decoy customer 2 Bail No 142/2016. (order below Exhibit 1) and there three accused were found procuring victims for prostitution and from there three accused were arrested and three victims were rescued. 4] The learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant-accused is falsely implicated. He submitted that both the applicants are married lady and having children. He further submitted that there are no allegations about procuring the minor for prostitution against the present applicant /accused and the said allegations are against accused No.3 Mallikabibi. He submitted that in fact, the victims were not forced for prostitution and they themselves indulged in the business due to their poor financial condition. He further submitted that where the raid was conducted was residential house having only one room and therefore, the allegations are not found truthful. He submitted that accused was arrested on the basis of false information. He further submitted that the accused are permanent resident of Thane and they are ready to abide by any conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing them on bail. 5] The learned A.P.P. opposed the application on the ground that the applicant is involved in serious offence. The applicants are providing girls for prostitution. The accused was found during the trap led in the house. Their role is clear from the F.I.R. One of the girls is minor. The investigation is in progress. There are chances of tampering the witnesses and there is possibility of accused repeating the offence if released on bail and prayed for rejection of application. 3 Bail No 142/2016. (order below Exhibit 1) 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R. it appears that three accused were arrested during the raid which was conducted on receipt of secret information that prostitution is being carried out at residential house in Room No.202, Mahadev Apartment. The role of the present applicant appears from the F.I.R. itself the accused were found in the house which is residential house and used for carrying on prostitution. One of the victim girl is minor. From FIR it appears that the said room belongs to accused No.2 and accused No.1 used to arrange customers on phone and made available that room for prostitution. It also appears that accused took disadvantage of poor financial condition of the victims and forced them for prostitution. Prima-facie accused appeared to be involved in a serious offence for procuring the minor girl for prostitution. The investigation is still in progress and at nascent stage. Therefore, no case is made out for releasing the accused on bail. Hence, I pass the following order - ORDER The application stands rejected. Thane. Date : 04/02/2016. (Ms.U.M. Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act), Thane.

D.M.G.Malidwale) in O.M.A.No. 1156/2014. 2] Victim one Smt. Noorbanu Khatoon Manjur Alam was taken in custody by Shil Daighar Police Station on 27.11.2014 in C.R.No. I 284/2014 for the alleged offence under Sec. 370(A) of Indian Penal Code and Sec. 4,5,7(B), 1 of ITP Act. She has no concern or role in the alleged crime. Appellant and victim are residing together permanently at Desai gaon, behind Saibaba temple, Shil, Kalyan. His application for getting custody of the victim was turned down by the concerned court by passing impugned order on 19.12.2014. 3 Criminal Appeal No.10/2015 Exhibit No.23 4] The appellant has challenged the said order on various grounds amongst other that the said order is against the provisions of law and principles of natural justice. The concerned court failed to consider the fact that the victim involved in the crime is major and as such, the provisions of Protection of Children from Sexual Offence Act, 2012 are not attracted. She has been made scapegoat in the said crime only on suspicion. The concerned court failed to take into consideration and ignore the fact that the appellant being husband of the victim is entitled to get the custody of his wife. It has also failed to take into consideration the evidence and documents filed by the appellant. It has not properly applied its mind . Considering all these and other grounds, he has prayed that the impugned order may be quashed and set aside and the custody of the victim be given to the appellant on necessary terms and conditions. 5] The Rescue Foundation opposed the appeal by filing say (Exh.22) mainly, on the ground that the appellant has already been married and his son is taking engineering education and for meeting the expenses of the education, the victim has been involved in the illicit prostitution. Therefore, if the victim is given in custody of the appellant, then he may again coerce her in the same business. Considering all these circumstances, the appeal may be dismissed by maintaining the impugned order which is just, perfect and legal. 6] Heard Shri. Vijay Naik, Advocate for the appellant and A.P.P. Shri.Londhe,for the State and Shri. Bhandari, Advocate for Rescue Foundation. I have gone through the various documents filed in the 4 Criminal Appeal No.10/2015 Exhibit No. appeal. 7] The following points arise for my determination with my findings thereon for reasons to follow : POINTS FINDINGS 01. Whether the concerned Magistrate No. Court is justified in rejecting the claim of the appellant for getting custody of the victim? 02. Whether any interference is required ? Yes. 03. What order? Appeal is allowed REASONS AS TO POINT NOS.1 & 2 :­ 8] According to Shri. Naik, Advocate, some documents were not available with the appellant when application for getting custody was moved before the concerned Magistrate Court , but now all these documents like Nikahnama, ration card, income certificate etc. are being filed. All these documents clearly indicate that the appellant is the husband of the victim. Therefore, he is entitled to get the custody of the victim lady. The victim is in Rescue Foundation since last about 5 months in pursuance of the order of the Court and that is sufficient period and he has therefore, prayed that custody of the victim be given to the appellant. 9] A.P.P. Shri. Londhe, has strongly opposed the appeal by submitting that the appellant, the so called husband of the victim has 5 Criminal Appeal No.10/2015 Exhibit No.23 involved her in prostitution. The appellant was already married and his son is taking education in Engineering College. The appellant is doing prostitution business with the help of the victim and if the custody of the victim is given to him, then it is most likely that he may involve her in the same illicit business. Therefore, appeal may be dismissed and impugned order may be maintained. 10] Advocate Bhandari, has submitted that the concerned Magistrate Court, after making due enquiry, has rightly rejected the prayer of the appellant. The victim is taking vocational training for a period of one year and out of that, five months have already been completed. Therefore, in the interest of justice, the impugned order may be maintained by dismissing the appeal. 11] The Rescue Foundation, where the victim is being lodged for particular period, as per the order of the Court, has submitted in the say that on considering the documents on record, the appellant is undisputedly husband of the victim. So, the relations between the appellant and the victim is no more in question. It also appears from the impugned order that there is no material on record to show the nature of work and exact monthly income of the appellant and there is no material on record to establish his financial capacity. It is also doubted about the ration card produced by the appellant mainly, on the ground that the name of the victim was not shown as a wife of the appellant and copy of Nikahanama was not produced on record, but now the documents filed on record by the appellant like marriage certificate, photographs, certificate of Grampanchayat, Chapakhor, Dist. Katihar, Bihar, Voters' 6 Criminal Appeal No.10/2015 Exhibit No. identity card, pancard etc. clearly indicate that the appellant has landed property in Bihar and he is also working at Kalyan, and he is getting monthly salary of more than Rs. 9,000/­. There is no reason to disbelieve or discard the same as same has been also supported by the affidavit. There is also affidavit of opponent Sarmila @ Sarmina Khatoon, sister of the victim which also indicates that the marriage of the victim was performed with the appellant on 12.9.2013 and the appellant is her brother­in­law. There is also one affidavit of Aatar Lotifur Rehaman, cousin of the appellant. He has also supported the contentions of the appellant. There is no reason to disbelieve the averments made in the affidavit. There is absolutely no material on record to show that the appellant is involved in the crime and it is he who had involved his wife in the illicit work. The offence seems to be registered against Shobha Patil @ Bharti Shyam Thakur and Reshama More. So, it can not be said that the appellant is really involved in the crime and he seems to be genuine person. He has also sufficient source of income and he could very well maintain his wife i.e. the victim. So, he is certainly entitled to get the custody of the victim. The concerned Court rejected the claim of the appellant only because there was no sufficient documents which could inspire the confidence in the mind. But, now those documents having been filed and found to be genuine, I am of the view that the custody of the victim should be given to the appellant. There is also no material on record to show that son of the appellant is taking education in Engineering College . Considering all these facts and circumstances, I come to the conclusion that the impugned order is not just and proper and same required to be set aside by allowing this appeal. It appears that the victim lady would be the star witness on behalf of the 7 Criminal Appeal No.10/2015 Exhibit No.23 prosecution. So, her presence would certainly be required at the time of evidence in the said case arising out of the said crime. Therefore, certain conditions are required to be imposed while giving the custody of the victim to the appellant. Accordingly, I answer point Nos. 1 and 2 and proceed to pass following order : ORDER 1. Appeal is allowed. 2. The impugned order dtd. 19.12.2014 is hereby quashed and set aside. 3. The custody of victim Smt. Noorbano Khatoon Manjur Alam be given to the appellant Shri. Manjur Kasim Alam on following conditions : A] Appellant should give undertaking before the concerned Investigating Officer along with his residential address proof to the effect that he would keep the victim lady Noorbano Khatoon Manjur Alam present at the time of recording her evidence. B] He should provide his landline and mobile phone numbers to the concerned Investigating Officer. C] He should not leave jurisdiction of State of Maharashtra along with his wife till her evidence is recorded without permission of the Investigating Officer. Non­applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 1] By this application the applicant is seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. who was arrested on 23/11/2015 by Kapurbawadi Police Station in connection with C.R.No.I­ 450/2015 registered for an offence punishable under section 363, 376 of I.P.C. and section 6,7,8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as P.O.C.S.O. Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Mr.H.R.Yadav for the applicant/accused and learned Spl.P.P. Mrs. Kapre for State. I.O. absent. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 07/11/2015 at the instance of the informant/father of the victim­girl aged about 15 years with an indictment that on 06/10/2015 victim­ 2 Bail No. 156/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) girl left home with her friend and since then she did not return therefore, with the suspicion that she had been kidnapped by some unknown person, the F.I.R. was registered. During investigation the victim­girl was found with accused and they had physical relationships, therefore, offence under section 376 was added. 4] The learned Counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant/accused is falsely implicated. He submitted that the victim­girl and accused were having love affair and victim­girl was not forced by the accused to leave her house. Victim­girl on her own left the house. He further submitted that after registration of F.I.R. now the marriage of victim­girl was performed with another boy on 03/01/2016 which shows that she is a major girl. The accused is behind bar since two months. The investigation is almost completed. The accused is permanent resident of Thane. The accused is ready to abide any conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing him on bail. 5] Per contra, the learned Spl.P.P. opposed the application submitting that the offence is serius in respect of a minor girl. He submitted that she is a victim­girl of 15 years and therefore, there is no question of her consent. The accused took away the victim­girl to Ilahabad and committed sexual 3 Bail No. 156/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) assault on her. The investigation is in progress. There are chances of tampering with witnesses and prayed for rejection of application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R., it appears that initially, the F.I.R. was lodged by the father of the victim­girl about kidnapping of his daughter. However, during investigation the victim­girl was found with accused at Ilahabad. The statement of victim­girl clearly shows that she was having friendship with accused, which later on developed into their love affair. The victim­girl is aged about 15 years, which means she is about to attain the age of discretion. The statement of victim­girl further shows that accused took her at various place. However, from her statement it did not appear that she resist to the act of accused. The accused is young boy of 22 years and behind bar since two months and 13 days. By this stage, the investigation must have been practically completed. The report filed by the investigating officer, did not show any criminal antecedents against the accused. Only because the accused is resident of another State is no ground to reject his bail application. No fruitful purpose would be served by further incarceration of accused. The object of bail is neither punitive nor preventive but to secure the presence of the accused at the time of trial. He is ready to abide by the conditions imposed by the Court. Ds. 3 ­9 ­ 8 IN THE COURT OF THE SPECIAL JUDGE THANE, AT : THANE (Presided over by S. B. Bahalkar ) SPECIAL CASE NO. 13/2015 EXH. No. CNR­MHTH01­000380­2015 State of Maharashtra. (Through: Rabodi Police Station in C.R.No.I­311/2014) ...Prosecution V/s. Santosh Hiranna Pujari, Age­ 26 years, R/at: near Golai Mandir, Pardhi Pada, Kalwa, Thane (E) Also R/at : in front of Brahmand Lake on a footpath. ... Accused ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ Appearances :­­ Ld.APP Smt.Chandane, for the prosecution. Ld. Advocate Shri.Patankar for Accused. ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.13/2015 (Judgment). : 2: Special Case No.13/2015 (Judgment) CNR­MHTH01­000380­2015 J U D G M E N T. (Delivered on 23rd day of October, 2018) [1] Accused committed sexual assault on a minor girl. Hence, he is facing trial U/Secs.376(2)(i) of the Indian Penal Code (in short I.P.C.) and U/Sec. 4 & 6 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offence Act (in short POCSO Act). [2] Brief facts of the prosecution case are as under :­ i) Informant Puja is the wife of Santosh. They have two children. Victim girl is their second child and at the time of incident she was about 6 months old. Puja used to go to sell hair­ clips and other articles in trains. However, the accused was in bad habit of drinking liquor and used to not perform any kind of work. ii) On 10/10/2014 informant Puja kept her son and said minor victim daughter at the hut of her cousin sister Jayashri. Sometime thereafter, Jayashri and her husband had also proceeded to their work and at that time their daughter Kajal was at home to look after the children of Puja. On that day at about 10.00 p.m. when Puja came back to the hut of Jayashri she found that there was little bleeding from the private part of said minor girl. Therefore, she took her to Civil Hospital, Thane. Doctor examined the said minor girl and opined that such bleeding is normal thing. However, thereafter on 16/10/2014 said minor girl did not pass urine. Therefore, on 17/10/2014 Pooja again took said minor girl to Civil Hospital, Thane. Doctor examined her and AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.13/2015 (Judgment). : 3: Special Case No.13/2015 (Judgment) CNR­MHTH01­000380­2015 advised that since modern equipments are not available in the said hospital, the said minor girl should be taken to J.J.Hospital, Mumbai. Accordingly informant Puja took the said minor girl to J.J. Hospital, Mumbai. After examination the doctor admitted her in the hospital. However, the informant got doubt that her husband i.e. accused Santosh might have committed something wrong with said minor girl by which she became ill. iii) On 18/10/2014 police recorded statement of informant Puja and on the basis of said statement crime vide C.R.No. 311/2014 U/Sec. 376(C)) of I.P.C. and U/Secs.4,6,8 & 10 of P.O.C.S.O.Act, 2012 came to be registered at Rabodi Police Station. The investigation of the crime was handed over to P.S.I. Shri.Khairnar. iv) I.O. P.S.I.Shri.Khairnar on 19/10/2014 went to J.J.Hospital, Mumbai and recorded supplementary statement of informant Puja. On the same day, he visited to the spot of incident and prepared panchanama of the spot. He also seized wearing clothes of the said victim girl and prepared panchanama to that effect. Thereafter, further investigation was handed over to P.S.I. Ingale. I.O. He recorded statement of said Jayashri, her husband Yakub Naik and her daughter Kajal Naik. It was transpired that on 10/10/2014 when the said minor girl had been to the hut of Jayashri accused Santosh came there. He was under the influence of liquor. At that time Kajal Naik was present in the hut. Accused AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.13/2015 (Judgment). : 4: Special Case No.13/2015 (Judgment) CNR­MHTH01­000380­2015 Santosh put nipple of milk bottle on his finger and inserted the said finger in the private part of the said minor baby. At that time said Kajal asked accused Santosh as to what he was doing. However, the accused threatened her by showing knife and asked her not to disclose the said incident to anybody. Thereafter, the accused brought new nipple for the milk bottle. Since the said Kajal got frightened she did not disclose the said fact to anybody. On completion of the investigation the I.O. has submitted chargesheet in the court of J.M.F.C. Thane against accused U/Sec. 376(C) of I.P.C. and U/Secs.4,6,8 & 10 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, 2012. [3] Since the offences levelled against the accused are triable exclusively by the court of Sessions and Special Court, the Ld.Magistrate committed the case to this Court. [4] My Ld.Predecessor framed charge (Ex.3) against the accused U/Sec.376(2)(i) of I.P.C. and U/Sec. 4 & 6 of POCSO Act. Particulars of the offences were read over and explained to the accused to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. [5] Statements of the accused U/Sec.313 of Code of Criminal Procedure has been recorded. His defence is of total denial. AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.13/2015 (Judgment). : 5: Special Case No.13/2015 (Judgment) CNR­MHTH01­000380­2015 [6] Following points arise for my determination. I have recorded my findings thereon for the reasons stated below : S.No POINTS FINDINGS 1 Whether the prosecution proves that the accused committed rape on his daughter, a minor girl by doing sexual assault on her ? Not proved. 2 Whether the prosecution further proves that the accused committed aggravated penetrative sexual assault on his daughter, a minor girl by inserting finger in her vagina ? Not proved. 3 What order ? Accused is acquitted. REASONS AS TO POINTS NOS. 1 & 2 :­ [7] In fact informant Puja Pujari, the mother of the victim girl and Kajal Yakub Naik, the child eye witness are the important witnesses of this case. However, record shows that in spite of having many opportunities the prosecution failed to produce these witnesses before the court for their evidence. In the result their evidence could not be recorded. This is an important infirmity of the prosecution case. AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.13/2015 (Judgment). : 6: Special Case No.13/2015 (Judgment) CNR­MHTH01­000380­2015 [8] Prosecution has examined only three witnesses viz. Dr.Dhruv Pravin Gohil (P.W.1) (Exh.21), P.S.I.Yadav Rukla Khairnar (P.W.2)(Exh.36) and P.S.I. Sadhana Bhagwan Ingale (P.W.3)(Exh.41). [9] Dr.Dhruv Gohil (P.W.1) states that on 21/10/2014 he alongwith Dr.A.H.Meshram and Dr.D.V.Bhore examined the said victim girl and issued certificate vide Exh.22. Definitely Dr.Dhruv Gohil (P.W.1) is not an eye witness to the incident. His evidence would have been important if the evidence of Puja Pujari, the mother of the victim girl and Kajal Yakub Naik child eye witness would have been recorded. In the absence of evidence of these two important witnesses, solely on the basis of evidence of Dr.Dhruv Gohil (P.W.1) it cannot be inferred that the accused has committed an offence as alleged by the prosecution. [10] P.S.I.Sadhana Ingale (P.W.3) is the person who recorded statement of Kajal Naik, the child eye witness. However, it is already pointed out that in spite of having sufficient opportunities evidence of said Kajal Naik could not been recorded by the prosecution. Thus , according to me P.S.I.Sadhana Ingale (P.W.3) discharged her duties only by recording statement of a child eye witness Kajal Naik. However, her evidence is not sufficient to bring home guilt of accused. AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.13/2015 (Judgment). : 7: Special Case No.13/2015 (Judgment) CNR­MHTH01­000380­2015 [11] P.S.I.Yadav Rukla Khairnar (P.W.2) is the I.O. His evidence appears to be mechanical one. He discharged his duties by recording statements of the witnesses and by preparing panchanama of the spot of the incident and panchanama of seizure of clothes of the victim girl. In my opinion his evidence is also not helpful to prove the guilt of accused. [12] Therefore, on the basis of aforementioned evidence and material placed on record, I can safely conclude that the prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of accused U/Sec.376(2) (i) of I.P.C. and U/Secs.4 & 6 of the P.O.C.S.O. Act, 2012 beyond reasonable doubts. I, therefore answer point Nos.1 & 2 in the negative. AS TO POINT NO.3 : [13] As mentioned above, the prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of accused U/Sec.376(2)(i) of I.P.C. and U/Secs. 4 & 6 of POCSO Act. Hence, accused is entitled to be acquitted. [14] So far muddemal i.e. seized clothes of the victim girl are concerned, the same being worthless are liable to be destroyed after the appeal period is over. I, therefore, in answer to point No.3 pass the following order : AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.13/2015 (Judgment). : 8: Special Case No.13/2015 (Judgment) CNR­MHTH01­000380­2015 ­: ORDER :­ 1) Accused Santosh Hiranna Pujari is hereby acquitted of the offences punishable U/Sec 376(2)(i) of the Indian Penal Code and U/Sec.4 and 6 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 vide Sec.235(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 2) The accused is released on cash surety. His bail bond shall continue till the appeal period is over in compliance of provisions U/Sec. 437­A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 3) Muddemal property i.e. frock be destroyed, after appeal period is over. Thane. Dated: 23/10/2018 ( S. B. Bahalkar ) Special Judge, Thane, Under POCSO Act, 2012. AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.13/2015 (Judgment).

Pralhad Thakur attached with AHTC Crime branch Thane with an indictment that secret information was received about prostitution being carried out within the jurisdiction of Mumbra police station by accused Shahnaz. He submitted that in fact, the victims were not forced for prostitution and they themselves indulged in the business due to their poor financial condition. AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.18/2016 (Judgment). : 4: Special Case No.18/2016 (Judgment) (CNR MHTH­000435­2016) Therefore, on completion of the investigation the I.O. has submitted chargesheet U/Sec.363 of IPC and U/Secs.4,8 & 12 of POCSO Act. [7] Following points arise for my determination. I have recorded my findings thereon for the reasons stated below : Sr. POINTS FINDINGS No 1 Whether the prosecution proves that the accused kidnapped the minor victim girl “R”, from the lawful guardianship of her parents and took her with him ? Not proved. AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.18/2016 (Judgment). : 5: Special Case No.18/2016 (Judgment) (CNR MHTH­000435­2016) 2 Whether the prosecution further proves that the accused committed sexual assault on the minor victim girl “R” ? Not proved. 3 Whether prosecution further proves that the accused committed penetrative sexual assault on the minor victim girl “R”, Not proved. 4 Whether prosecution further proves that the accused committed sexual harassment of the said minor victim girl “R” ? Not proved. 5 What order ? Accused is acquitted. REASONS AS TO POINTS NOS. 1 to 4:­ [8] Since all the points for determination arose from the one and the same incident, I took them together for discussion. [9] When there is charge against the accused that he has committed offence under the provisions of POCSO Act prosecution must prove that at the time of the incident victim was the minor as mentioned in clause 'D' of Sec.2 of the POCSO Act. However, from the evidence adduced by the prosecution, it can be safely concluded that the prosecution has not brought sufficient and cogent material even to ascertain the date of birth of the victim girl “R”. Therefore, it is difficult to hold that at the time of the incident victim girl was minor. AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.18/2016 (Judgment). : 6: Special Case No.18/2016 (Judgment) (CNR MHTH­000435­2016) [10] Shubhangi (P.W.1) is the mother of the victim girl “R”. She states that the incident took place bout 3 years back. On that day she went to her work and came back at about 1.30 p.m. At that time her daughter “R” was not there in the house. Hence, she enquired with her husband. He disclosed that “R” had gone to the house of her friend. Therefore, Shubhangi (P.W.1) was waiting for “R” upto 8.30 p.m. However, “R” did not come back. She also took search of “R” at the house of her friends. However, “R” did not come back. Shubhangi (P.W.1) further states that she had knowledge that her daughter had love affair with the accused. Therefore, she lodged F.I.R. against the accused on suspicion. [11] “R” (P.W.2) is the victim girl who states that she do not remember the date of the incident. However, she remember that she had left her house secretly and gone out with the accused at Palghar. About one month thereafter they came back. Police enquired with her and recorded her statement. [12] It is interesting to note that in her cross­examination “R” (P.W.2) states that she and the accused had loveship and she thought that her parents would oppose to the said relationship and would not allow her to marry with the accused. Hence, at her own she left her house. It is also admitted by “R” (P.W.2) in cross­ examination that when she left her house she had completed her 18 years of age. Afterwards, with the consent of both the family AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.18/2016 (Judgment). : 7: Special Case No.18/2016 (Judgment) (CNR MHTH­000435­2016) members she got married to the accused and they are cohabiting happily with each other. [13] Shubhangi (P.W.1) also admitted in her cross­ examination that her daughter had disclosed her that she left the house secretly thinking that her relationship would be opposed. It is also admitted that with the consent of both the families the accused married with the victim girl and they are cohabiting with each other happily and even they begotten one son in the said wedlock. Subhangi (P.W.1) also admitted that she has no documentary proof regarding date of birth of “R” (P.W.2). [14] Considering the above mentioned facts and circumstances prosecution has not examined any more witness. Evidence of Shubhangi (P.W.1) and “R” (P.W.2) shows that “R” (P.W.2) at her own left the house and had gone with the accused and at that time she was 18 years old. It is already pointed out that prosecution has not adduced any cogent evidence to prove that at the time of the incident the victim girl “R” (P.W.2) was minor. Moreover, there is no whisper at all in the evidence of Shubhangi (P.W.1) or “R” (P.W.2) regarding any act or sexual act which can be said to be “sexual assault, penetrative sexual assault and sexual harassment” as defined in POCSO Act. [15] For the reasons stated above, I have no hesitation to hold that the prosecution has not proved the guilt of accused AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.18/2016 (Judgment). : 8: Special Case No.18/2016 (Judgment) (CNR MHTH­000435­2016) U/Secs. 363 of I.P.C. and U/Secs.4, 8 & 12 of POCSO Act. I, therefore, answer point Nos.1 to 4 in the negative. AS TO POINT NO.5 : [16] As mentioned above, the prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of accused U/Secs.363 of I.P.C. and U/Secs.4, 8 and 12 of POCSO Act. Hence, accused is liable to be acquitted. I, therefore, in answer to point No.5 pass the following order : ­: ORDER :­ 1) Accused Vijay Rajendra Jadhav is hereby acquitted of the offences punishable U/Sec 363 of I.P.C. and U/Sec.4, 8 and 12 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 vide Sec.235(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 2) The accused is released on bail . His bail bonds shall continue till the appeal period is over in compliance of provisions U/Sec. 437­A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Thane. Dated: 15/12/2018 ( S. B. Bahalkar ) Special Judge, Thane. Under POCSO Act, 2012. AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.18/2016 (Judgment).

After the evidence of prosecution is over, statement U/s. 313 of Cr.P.C. of the applicants/accused has been recorded by the Ld. Judge on 09/01/2017 as per Exh.84 and 85. On the said date, on behalf of the applicants, pursis Exh.86 informing the Court 9 that they wish to examine two witnesses in their defense on 17/01/2017 and 30/01/2017 was filed and said pursis was taken on record by the Ld. It appears that the accused have adopted Delaying tactics and are not ready to proceed with the matter. This application is therefore rejected.” Thereafter, the case was adjourned to 18/01/2017. 8. Shri Chavan, the Ld. Advocate appearing for the applicants submitted that on 18/01/2017 on behalf of the applicants application was made to the Ld. Judge to adjourn the hearing of the case as Criminal M.A. to transfer the case has been filed and as no hearing can be taken in the case till the Criminal M.A. for transfer of case is heard and said 10 application was rejected by the Ld. Judge and the applicants/ accused were directed to proceed with the matter as witnesses were present. Further, he submitted that on the same date, defence witness from Zilla Parishad, Thane moved application Exh.92 to the Court requesting to record her evidence. Judge, without obtaining say of the accused, passed order on the said application that in view of the failure on the part of the Ld. Advocate for the accused to comply with the directions of the Court, evidence of defence witnesses is being closed and matter is kept for final arguments tomorrow and separate order is passed below Exh.1. The Ld. Advocate further submitted that on the same day i.e. on 18/01/2017 the Ld. Judge has passed order below Exh.1 noting the incidents happened on that day and fixed the matter on next day i.e. on 19/01/2017 with direction to Ld. Advocate for the applicants 11 to maintain decorum and dignity of the Court etc. Referring above all orders, the Ld. Advocate appearing for the applicants has submitted that these orders show that the Ld. Judge is prejudiced against the applicants, and therefore, there is substance in the apprehension of the applicants that they will not get justice at the hands of the Ld. Judge, if the case is tried in the said Court. Shri Chavan, Ld. Advocate for the applicants has also made submissions in the light of complaints made by applicant No.1 against the Ld. Judge and in the light of grounds of transfer of the case referred to above in para­2 (supra) and finally submitted that the Sessions case against the applicants be withdrawn from the Court presided over by the Ld. Judge and the same may be transferred to any other Sessions Court at Thane. To support his submissions, the Ld. Advocate for the applicants has relied upon the ratio laid down in the case of “Nilesh Jap Daru Vs. State of Maharashtra”, [2004 ALL MR (Cri) 2951] wherein it was held that “in considering the expediency of directing a transfer for the ends of justice, it is essential to decide not merely the question whether there has been any real bias in the mind of a Judge but also the further question whether the incidents happened in the Court create in the mind of an accused a reasonable apprehension that he may not have a fair and impartial trial. In other words, it often becomes necessary to consider whether there is a reasonable ground for assuming the possibility of bias and whether it is likely to produce in the mind of a litigant or 12 public at large a reasonable doubt about fairness of administration of justice. It would always be a question of fact to be decided in each case.” 9. On the other hand, Shri Kulkarni, Ld. A.P.P. appearing for the opponent submitted that all the allegations made by the applicants in the application against the Ld. Judge are false and baseless. He submitted that had it been the case that the Ld. Judge did not record answers given by the witnesses not favourable to the prosecution in the examination­ in­chief of witnesses or answers given in the cross­examination of the witnesses which are favourable to the accused, the applicants or their Ld. Advocate would have made such grievance by making application to the Court at the time of recording evidence only. But no such application was given on behalf of the applicants. Therefore, the grievance in this respect made by the applicants after the evidence of prosecution is over and the statement of applicants U/s. 313 of Criminal procedure Code is recorded, is not acceptable. So also, the grounds regarding happening of the incident at the time of recording statement of accused U/s. 313 of Criminal Procedure Code, that the Ld. Judge did not record statement correctly, and that, the complainant and her daughter abused the applicants in filthy language etc. are not correct. The rojnama dtd. 09/01/2017 in the case on which date the statement of applicants U/s. 313 of Criminal Procedure Code was recorded 13 does not show happening of incident as alleged by the applicants on that date. It is further submitted that the Ld. Judge has passed appropriate orders on the applications Exh. 91 to 93 and below Exh.1 on 18/01/2017 and these orders show conduct of other side and show how otherside is pressurizing the Ld. Judge to delay the hearing of the case which dis­entitles them to the relief of transfer of the case. Moreover, it is submitted on behalf of the opponent/State that the Court cannot transfer part heard case in view of the provisions U/s. 409(2) of the Criminal Procedure Code and as such, application to transfer the case is not maintainable. Thus, the Ld. A.P.P. has submitted that the grounds on which the applicants have sought transfer of the case are not sufficient to state that the apprehension of the applicants that there would be no fair trial, is not acceptable, and thus, claimed to dismiss the application. 10. Shri Kulkarni, Ld. A.P.P. for the opponent, in support of his submission that the Court cannot transfer case in view of section­409(2) of Criminal Procedure Code, when the trial has commenced, has relied upon the ratio laid down in the case of “ State of West Bengal Vs. Gangadhar Dawn and Ors.”, [1989 Cri.L.J. 563] (CALCUTTA HIGH COURT). In the said case, “the State of West Bengal has preferred revision application against the order of the learned Sessions Judge allowing an application under section 408 of Criminal Procedure Code for 14 transfer made by the accused in Sessions case sometime after the trial of that case began before an Additional Sessions Judge.” In para­6 it was held that in view of the provisions of sub­section(2) of section 409 of Criminal procedure Code, Sessions Judge has no such power when the trial already commenced. The Revision application was allowed and the order passed by the Ld. Sessions Judge was set aside. 11. Shri Kulkarni, Ld. A.P.P. for the opponent further relied upon the ratio laid down by the Supreme Court in the case of “Usmangani Adambhai Vahora Vs. State of Gujrat & Anr.”, Criminal Appeal Nos. 1592­1593 of 2015 (@ S.L.P. (Criminal) Nos. 9374­9375 of 2015). In the said case after examination of 18 prosecution witnesses, the accused filed Criminal M.A. No. 545/2015 U/s. 408 of Criminal procedure Code, before the Principal Sessions Judge, Kheda at Nadiad for transfer of Sessions Case to any other Court in the same Sessions division. On 31/07/2015 when the sessions trial was fixed before the 3rd Additional Sessions Judge, Kheda, at Nadiad, as alleged, the second­respondent was standing in the parking area meant for the four wheelers and at that time he could overhear certain conversation between the informant and his son that the trial would be surely taken up for hearing from the next date onwards and all the accused persons would definitely be convicted. It was further alleged that the Presiding Officer said something regarding the trial which the accused 15 correlated with the conversation he had overheard between the informant and his son. The Ld. Principal Sessions Judge called remarks of the concerned Presiding Officer and after taking into consideration the remarks and adverting to the position of law, rejected the application. The Ld. Principal Sessions Judge while rejecting the application had observed that once the trial commenced, he had no jurisdiction to transfer the case in exercise of the power U/s. 408 of Cr.P.C. The said order was challenged before the High Court. The High Court set aside the order of Sessions Judge and directed to transfer the case. The Hon'ble Apex Court in para­13 observed as under : “Thus analysed, we are unable to sustain the order of transfer passed by the High Court. Consequently, the appeals are allowed in part. The finding recorded as regards the jurisdiction of the learned Sessions Judge is sustained, and as far as the direction to the Principal Sessions Judge to transfer the case from the 3rd Additional Sessions Judge to some other court being vulnerable and wholly unsustainable is set aside. The Ld. Trial judge shall proceed with the trial and dispose of the same within six months.” As regards question to exercise of power under sub­ section(1) of section 408 of Criminal Procedure Code by the Sessions Judge to transfer the case from one Additional Sessions Judge to another Additional Sessions Judge in his Sessions division after commencement of the Trial the High 16 Court has opined that the transfer petition preferred U/s. 408 of Criminal Procedure Code before the Principal Sessions Judge is maintainable. On this the Hon'ble Apex Court held that the view expressed by the High Court on this score appears to be correct, and hence, it was affirmed by the Apex Court. 12. I have gone through the facts and the ratio laid down in the above decisions relied upon by the Ld. Advocate for the applicants and the Ld. A.P.P. 13. In the wake of above admitted facts and the submissions made by the Ld. Advocate appearing for the applicants and the Ld. A.P.P. I proceed to consider whether the grounds on which the applicants have sought transfer of their case, are acceptable and sufficient to state that apprehension of the applicants that there would be no fair trial and no fair justice at the hands of the Ld. Judge, so as to state that they are entitled to transfer the case as requested. The material grounds on which the applicants have sought transfer of the case, in short, are as under: A] The Ld. Judge is having partial and opaque attitude towards the applicants throughout the Trial and she is totally prejudiced and perverse against them. B] The Ld. Judge was not recording answers given by the witness not favourable to the prosecution, and that, she used to 17 advise the witness to understand the question and reply it carefully and used to say that else she will take action and tries to avoid recording of answers given in favour of accused. C] The Ld. Judge instigated the complainant and her other daughter to interfere in the Court proceeding, allowed them to shout in the Court and to altercate with the applicants while recording statement U/s. 313 of Cr.P.C. and did not record said statement correctly. D] The Ld. Judge for no reason interacts with the complainant and her daughter while they attend the Court by taking them into witness box and assure them of giving justice to them and behaves in adamant and rude manner with the applicants throughout as if they are her enemies. 14. Before considering the above grounds, I would like to deal with the argument of the Ld. A.P.P. that the application is not maintainable as per section 409(2) of Criminal Procedure Code as the case is part heard. There is no dispute that the case is part heard as observed earlier. Considering the observation of the Apex Court in the case of Usmangani Adambhai Vahora (supra) relied upon by the Ld. A.P.P., wherein the view expressed by the High Court that transfer petition preferred U/s.408 of Criminal Procedure Code before the Principal Sessions Judge, in the case after commencement of trial was held maintainable was affirmed by the Hon'ble Apex Court, I hold that the present application U/s. 408 of Criminal 18 Procedure is maintainable and it cannot be said that it is not maintainable as submitted by the Ld. A.P.P. 15. Now coming to the grounds (a) and (b), according to the applicants the Ld. Judge is partial as she did not record examination­in­chief and cross­examination of the witnesses properly, except the words of the applicants in the application, there is no material to show that the Ld. Judge is partial and prejudiced against the applicants as she did not record the evidence properly. The applicants have not filed affidavits in support of their allegations in the application. It is seen that the Ld. Judge passed order dtd. 18/01/2017 on Exh.93­application of D.G.P. to keep the case for final argument. The applicants can challenge the said order and request to allow them to adduce evidence of defence witness. It is seen from the remarks of the Ld. Judge that on 06/02/2017 the applicants have moved application through their advocate to issue witness summons and to give summons to them by hand to effect service. In such circumstances, the Ld. Judge can issue summons to the defence witnesses, if not issued, as requested by the applicants. Therefore, when the Ld. Judge has passed judicial orders, it cannot be said that said orders have caused prejudice against the applicants as submitted by the Ld. Advocate for the applicants, I find that mere passing of orders on different applications referred by Ld. Advocate for applicants in his argument is not sufficient to state that the Ld. 19 Judge is prejudiced against the applicants, in the above circumstances. 16. According to applicants, the Ld. Judge used to record answers given by the witness not favourable to the prosecution and she advised witness to understand the question and reply it carefully and tries to avoid recording of answers given in favour of the accused. It appears that the prosecution has examined in all eight witnesses and then statement U/s. 313 of Criminal Procedure Code was recorded on 09/01/2017. There is nothing on record to show that while recording evidence i.e. examination­in­chief and cross­ examination of a particular witness, the above incident of not recording answers not favourable to prosecution and not recording answers given in favour of the applicants/accused has taken place. In fact, the applicants should have stated specifically in this respect. So also, it was possible for the applicants to take objection in this respect, in writing in the course of recording evidence of a particular witness, when the Ld. Judge was allegedly avoiding to record answers not favouring to prosecution and favouring to accused. When after recording statement U/s. 313 Cr.P.C. of accused, the applicants have filed this transfer application on 13/01/2017, I find that there is possibility that the applicants have made allegations of prejudice against them by the Ld. Judge, in the manner of recording examination­in­chief and cross­examination of the 20 witnesses, is after thought. Therefore, the grounds (a) and (b) are not acceptable. 17. As regards ground (c) that the Ld. Judge instigated the complainant and her other daughter to interfere in the Court proceeding while recording statement of accused U/s. 313 of Criminal Procedure Code, and that, she did not record said statement correctly is concerned, the said statement was recorded on 09/01/2017. The applicants could have placed on record said incident in writing on that day. But rojnama in the case of the said date does not show that they have made any grievance in the manner of recording statement U/s. 313 of Criminal Procedure Code. So also, the applicants have not filed their affidavits stating that the Ld. Judge instigated the complainant and her other daughter to interfere in the proceeding as alleged. Therefore, when it appears that till the recording of statement of applicants u/s. 313 of Criminal Procedure Code on 09/01/2017 there was no grievance made by the applicants/accused before the Court either in respect of manner of recording evidence or in respect of the manner of recording statement U/s. 313 of Criminal Procedure Code, I find that the allegation made by the applicants in respect of not recording statement correctly and allegation of allowing the complainant and her daughter by the Ld. Judge to interfere in the proceeding appears to be not correct and as per the actual circumstances present in the case. It is seen that the applicant 21 No.1 made complaint on 11/01/2017 to this Court making certain allegations against the Ld. Judge about not properly recording statement U/s. 313 of Criminal Procedure Code, but when the applicants did not inform the Court on 09/01/2017, when their statements were recorded, in respect of their said grievances, filing of such complaint alone is not sufficient to state that there is a substance in the ground in respect of not recording statement correctly. Another aspect to be noted is that, the applicants can point out to the said Court even at the time of arguing the matter how statement is not correctly recorded, and how it has caused prejudice to them. 18. As regards ground (d), that the Ld. Judge interacts with the complainant and her daughter when they attend the Court and as such favours the complainant is concerned, the applicants have not given a day or date on which the Ld. Judge allegedly interacted with the complainant and her daughter by taking them into witness box. Admittedly, the applicants have not filed affidavit in support this allegation also. The Ld. Judge as well as the opponent/State have denied the allegation in this respect made by the applicants in the application. It appears from the copy of application dtd. 23/12/2016, in the form of complaint, produced by the applicants that the applicant No.1 made application to this Court to transfer the Special Case No. 89/2013 making allegation that the Ld. Judge, after one year of recording evidence of complainant and her daughter, called 22 the complainant in Case No. 89/2013 on every date and assures her of giving decision in her favour and used to enquire about vicrim­girl of the complainant and her education. In this application also it is not mentioned that said incident took place on a particular day. Therefore, mere making application as above, by the applicant No.1 to this Court to transfer case, is not sufficient to state that the Ld. Judge encouraged the complainant and her daughter and assured them of giving justice. As regards the allegation that the Ld. Judge behaved in adamant and rude manner is concerned, the applicants have not filed their affidavit quoting any instance of rude and adamant behaviour of the Ld. Judge with the applicants. It is seen that on 19/01/2017 and 20/01/2017 the Ld. Advocate for the applicants made complaint to this court about the conduct of the Ld. Judge and it is alleged that the conduct of the Ld. Judge is malafide and not transparent. The allegations in these complaints made by the Ld. Advocate for the applicants against the Ld. Judge and the remarks of the Ld. Judge referred earlier, in detail, in which the Ld. Judge has alleged about the conduct of the Ld. Advocate for the applicants, I find that the allegations are made against each other about the manner of conducting the trial. The allegations made against the Ld. Judge in the complaints by the Ld. advocate and the allegations made in the remarks by the Ld. Judge against the Ld. Advocate, show that there were some differences on the date of recording 23 evidence of defence witness and said cannot be made basis to accept the allegations made against the Ld. Judge about her conduct, ultimately, to state that apprehension of the applicants that there would be no fair trial at the hands of the Ld. Judge is acceptable and a reasonable apprehension. 19. For all the reasons discussed above, the grounds referred above on which mainly the applicants have sought transfer of special case to other Court are not acceptable and sufficient to state that their apprehension that they would not get justice or there would be no fair trial at the hands of the Ld. Judge, is reasonable. So also, when admittedly evidence of most of the witnesses has been recorded by the Ld. Judge and after the evidence of prosecution is over, statement U/s. 313 of Criminal Procedure Code of the applicants is recorded, it would be appropriate if the case is decided by the Ld. Judge considering the request of applicants to examine defence witnesses according to law, if the Ld. Judge finds it appropriate, as they appear to have already made request in the case, in this respect, on 06/02/2017 to the Ld. Judge. Therefore, as there are no sufficient grounds to transfer the case, the application of the applicants to transfer the Special Case No. 89/2013 to other Court is liable to be rejected. In the result, the following order is passed. 24 :ORDER: 1] Application is rejected. 2] Inform the concerned Court accordingly. Date­09/02/2017. (S.M. Gavhane) Thane.
