.. 1 .. bail no.158/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 158/2015 This application is filed by applicant Mangesh Bapu Kale for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no.I­1003/2014 registered at Mumbra police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 376, 363 of I.P.C. and section 4 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant induced and then kidnapped the minor victim girl and then committed rape on her. It is further contended and argued that there was love affair between the applicant and the victim and it is a case of consent and the applicant is falsely implicated in this crime on account of personal vendetta. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co­operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that at the time of incident the accused induced the victim girl knowing that she was minor and kidnapped her out of lawful guardianship of her parents and then had forcible sexual intercourse with her. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl and the prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be .. 2 .. bail no.158/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 363, 376 of I.P.C. and section 4 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, 2012 with the allegation of committing penetrative sexual assault on the minor victim girl stated to be 14 years old, it appears that the accused had been arrested long back on 25.12.2014 and it is contended on his behalf that he had not kidnapped the girl and he is falsely implicated in the crime and that it is a case of consent. In such circumstance when the girl is stated to be below 18 years of age, the consent of minor is immaterial and the aspect as to whether the act of the accused amounts to rape or whether it is a case of consent, would be the question to be decided on merits. Even nothing is stated to be recovered from the applicant/accused. 4] It is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. 5] In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. .. 3 .. bail no.158/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) 6] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 7] Then, it has also to be mentioned that the investigation in the matter though almost completed, the charge sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 8] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is allowed. Applicants/accused namely Mangesh Bapu Kale is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ The applicant/accused shall attend the concerned police station on every Tuesday between 3.00 p.m. to 5.00 p.m. and shall co­operate in investigation. He shall not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and other prosecution .. 4 .. bail no.158/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this Court. He shall furnish proof of residence. Date : 13.03.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.

1 Bail No. 193/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) Criminal Bail Application No.193/2016 Ramsuresh Bijaybahadur Varma. .. Applicant versus The State of Maharashtra Through Bhiwandi Taluka Police Station .. Non­applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 1] By this application the applicant is seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. who was arrested 13.01.2016 by Bhiwandi Taluka Police Station in connection with C.R.No.I­ 322/2015 registered for an offence punishable under section 363, 376 of I.P.C. and section 4 and 12 The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as P.O.C.S.O. Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Mr. Sunil Lasne for the applicant/accused and learned Spl.P.P. Mrs. R.A. Navale for State. I.O. present. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 13.12.2015 at the instance of the informant/father of the victim­girl aged 2 Bail No. 193/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) about 17 years with an indictment that on 22.11.2015 accused kidnapped his daughter. Initially the informant informed that the victim­girl was 19 years and after producing the birth certificate of his daughter, the offence was registered against the accused. 4] The learned Counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant/accused is falsely implicated. He submitted that the victim­girl is major and in a missing report her age was stated as 19 years. He further submitted that it is the case of love affair, which was known to the family members of the victim­girl and not liked by them. Therefore, the victim­girl on her own run away with the accused as the marriage of victim­ girl was settled with another boy. He submitted that there was no force from the side of the accused neither the victim­girl was kidnapped. He further submitted that in fact accused married with the victim­girl and they were staying as husband and wife at their native place. But due to false F.I.R. accused came to be arrested. The accused is ready to abide any conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing him on bail. 5] Per contra, the learned Spl.P.P. opposed the application submitting that during the investigation the girl was found minor and therefore, the provisions of P.O.C.S.O. Act were applied. She submitted that as the girl is minor, there is no 3 Bail No. 193/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) question of her consent. The accused is involved in serious offence. The investigation is in progress. There are chances of tampering with witnesses and prayed for rejection of application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R., it appears that the F.I.R. is lodged by the father of the victim­girl stating that initially he lodged missing report stating the age of the victim­ girl as 19 years. However, he thereafter produced the birth certificate of the victim­girl, according to which, the age of the victim­girl was 17 years and 08 months therefore, the provisions of P.O.C.S.O. Act were added. The victim­girl completed 17 years and thus, attained the age of discretion. The accused is also a young boy of 22 years. The submission of learned Counsel for applicant about the accused and victim­girl were having love affair cannot be ruled out, however, the said aspect is required to be decided during trial. The accused is behind bars since one and half month. The material part of the investigation must have been completed. No fruitful purpose would be served by further incarceration of accused. The object of bail is neither punitive nor preventive but to secure the presence of the accused at the time of trial. He is ready to abide by the conditions imposed by the Court. In such circumstances the apprehension of learned Spl.P.P. about tampering of witnesses can be addressed by imposing suitable conditions. 4 Bail No. 193/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) Hence, I pass the following order ­ ORDER 1) The application is allowed. 2) Applicant namely Ramsuresh Bijaybahadur Varma be released on bail on his executing P.R. Bond of ₹ 15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one local solvent surety in the like amount on the following conditions ­ A] Applicant shall attend the concerned police station on every Sunday between 10.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon till filing the charge­sheet. B] Applicant shall co­operate in investigation and shall not tamper with prosecution witnesses. C] Applicant shall furnish his and his two blood relatives' address proofs and contact numbers and he is duty bound to inform I.O. and Court about the change of address, if any. Thane. Date : 01.02.2015. (Ms. U.M. Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act), Thane.

Act''). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant committing rape on the minor victim girl. It is further contended and argued that no such incident has happened and the applicant is falsely implicated in this crime. It is further contended and argued that there is long delay of 9 months in lodging the complaint about the alleged incident of rape. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co­operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that the accused who is 55 years old person had forcible committed sexual intercourse with the victim girl who is just 17 years old in the his shop. It is further contended and argued that the applicant has been named in the F.I.R. and the delay in lodging complaint need not be considered at this stage of deciding bail application. It is further submitted that the victim and the accused are residing in same locality and .. 2 .. bail 168/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) therefore in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening and pressurizing the victim girl and other prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, the offence charged against the applicant/ accused under 376, 506 of I.P.C. and section 3 and 4 P.O.C.S.O. Act is of very serious nature of commission of rape on 17 years old girl by the applicant/accused who is 55 years old. Then, though it is contended and argued on behalf of applicant/accused that there is 9 months' delay in lodging the F.I.R. and no sound reason for objecting bail is there etc. and the bail is mainly claimed on the ground that the accused is aged 55 years, it has to be mentioned that the delay in such type of offence of rape on minor girl cannot be said to be fatal or major lacuna and at least that cannot be a ground for deciding claim for bail. As is clear, the accused stated to be 55 years old person and alleged to have committed rape on 17 years old girl and it would be premature to conclude at this stage that he is falsely implicated in this crime. 4] Then, it has to be mentioned that the investigation in the matter is yet to be completed and it is stated to be in progress and therefore the possibility of the investigation being hampered if the applicant/accused is released on bail cannot be ruled out. Even the apprehension that the applicant/accused may threaten and pressurize the victim girl and other prosecution witnesses is of worth .. 3 .. bail 168/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) consideration and even the applicant/accused may abscond and may tamper with prosecution evidence if released on bail at this stage. 5] In all above circumstance I am of the view that this is not a fit case wherein the applicant/accused can be released on bail. In the result I pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is rejected. Date : 26.02.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.

B.A. No. 208/2017 3] The victim went towards her bag which was kept near the staircase. The applicant followed the victim near the staircase and started talking to her. It is further contended and argued that the applicant is falsely implicated due to previous enmity. It is further contended and argued that the investigation in the matter is mostly completed and therefore no further custody of the applicant is necessary. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co­operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The prosecution has not filed any reply to this application. Hence the application is ordered to proceed without say by passing order to that effect on Exhibit 1. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 354 of I.P.C. .. 2 .. bail 180/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) and section 8 and 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, it is contended and argued on behalf of accused that on account of previous enmity between him he is falsely implicated in the crime. In such circumstance whether the allegations against the accused are true or not, would be the question to be decided on merits. Even nothing is to be recovered from the applicant/accused. 4] It is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. 5] In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 6] Then, taking into account the fact that the offence charged against the accused are of serious nature and looking to the manner in which it is stated to have been committed the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there and but aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions on the applicant and for that reason the application cannot be rejected. 7] Then, it has also to be mentioned that the investigation in the matter is though almost completed the charge sheet is yet to .. 3 .. bail 180/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 8] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Sandeepkumar Satyanprasad Rajbhar is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ The applicant/accused shall attend the concerned police station on every Monday between 5.00 p.m. to 7.00 p.m. till filing of the charge sheet and shall co­operate with investigating machinery. He shall not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and the prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this Court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 04.02.2015 (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.

I­5/2015 registered at Vikramgad police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 354(A),(B),(D) of I.P.C. and section 3(b), 9(c), 10 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 354(A),(B),(D) of I.P.C. and section 3(b), 9(c), 10 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and also under section 3(1)(ii) of Prevention of Atrocities Act with the allegation that the accused who has been teacher in the school has molested the victim girl aged 8 years knowing the fact that she belongs to Adivasi Dhodia community by touching her private part after inserting hand in her underwear, after calling her inside the classroom when nobody was there in the classroom, it is contended on behalf of the applicant that he is falsely implicated in this crime. However, as is well settled at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be gone .. 3 .. bail 182/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) into detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the accused would abscond and would tamper with prosecution evidence if released on bail. 4] In that respect it is submitted on behalf of applicant/ accused that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond and he is ready to abide by any conditions and even it is also put forth on behalf of applicant/accused that he is to be suspended from the service on account of this case and he cannot go to school and may not communicate with any of the witnesses and therefore there is no possibility of he tampering with prosecution evidence. 5] Then, though it is argued on behalf of prosecution that the statements of witnesses are yet to be recorded and it may hamper the investigation if the applicant/accused is released on bail since the applicant/accused is teacher in said school, in that respect it is contended on behalf of applicant/accused that he is falsely implicated in this case on account of political rivalry since he participated in ''Swachhata Abhiyan''. 6] In that respect as is clear the applicant/accused is in custody since 16.01.2015 and as rightly submitted on behalf of applicant, by this time the investigation in the matter must have almost completed. 7] Then, though apprehension is expressed by the prosecution that the accused may threaten and pressurize the victim girl and other girls, that aspect can be taken care by putting .. 4 .. bail 182/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) certain conditions on him including the condition that the applicant shall not contact victim girl and other prosecution witnesses and for that reason the application for bail cannot be rejected. 8] In view of all above discussion I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­000545­2015 Special Case (POCSO) No. 16/2015 Received on : 22.01.2015 Registered on : 22.01.2015 Decided on : 04.08.2018 Duration : 3Ys. 6Ms. 13 Ds. IN THE COURT OF D.J.­1 & ADDL. SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE. (Presided over by Hemant M. Patwardhan) Special Case (POCSO) No. 16/2015 Exh.No. State of Maharashtra, (Mira Road Police station) ..Complainant V/s. Mohammad Tausif Sadar Khan. Age: 19 years, Occ. Service R/at. Room No. 001, Oswal Orchid, L. Laxmi Park, Mira Road (E) ..Accused Appearance:­ APP Smt. Moholkar for the State. Advocate Shri. S.N. Dhikale and Advocate Miss. Anuradha Pardeshi for accused JUDGMENT (Delivered on this 4th day of August 2018) Accused Mohammad Tausif Sadar Khan was facing trial under sections 354­A(1) of Indian Penal Code with Sec. 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 on following facts. 1 to 20 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­000545­2015 Special Case (POCSO) No. 16/2015 1] That on 16.08.2014, at about 12.00 hours, at N.K.Super Market, Flower Valley Complex, Sonali hotel road, Nayanagar, Mira Road (E), Dist. Thane within jurisdiction of Mira road police station, accused has sexually harassed victim, a minor girl, aged 8 years by physical contact and explicit sexual overtures and at the same time committed sexual assault on victim girl by dragging her towards him inserting his hand in her nicker and moving it on her private part with sexual intent which involves physical contact without penetration. Hence, on complaint of mother of victim an offence punishable under aforesaid sections came to be registered against him. On completion of investigation he was charge­sheeted. 2] My learned Predecessor was pleased to frame charge below Exh.3 and has certified that contents of it was read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. Accused has pleaded not guilty and claim to be tried. His defence was that of total denial and that oil tin was damaged and oil had spread on the floor of the shop and the accused was mopping that oil and the victim had slipped on said oil and the accused had helped her to stand up and due to the fall she started weeping and went to her house and then her mother had come, shouted loudly and beaten up the accused though he has tried to explain as to how he helped the girl to stood up after she fell down and then to save from the complaint being lodged by the accused against said lady, the present complaint is filed. 2 to 20 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­000545­2015 Special Case (POCSO) No. 16/2015 3] On the basis of aforesaid facts, prosecution then proceeded to record evidence of Smt. Nilophar Akhtar Hussain Shaikh, the complainant, the victim herself, Aftab Kalini and Vikram Jagtap respectively as witness no.1 to 4. Arguments of rival advocates were heard. Learned P.P. has then categorically pointed out that mother of the victim and victim herself have categorically deposed as to how and as to what incident had actually occurred and as to how accused was arrested on the spot itself. According to submissions of Learned P.P. the victim girl has categorically pointed out that as to how accused had used criminal force to involve himself in unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures and how sexual assault has been committed by him though said act was resisted by the victim by making an attempt to get herself free from the accused. According to learned P.P. victim was minor at the relevant time but she was aware that said unwelcome act is something against her will in itself is sufficient to establish that accused has outraged modest of the victim. According to learned P.P. as the victim was minor aged about 8 years and as accused had touched her private part with sexual intention thus his act itself is sufficient to inferred that accused was intending to commit the said act. According to learned P.P. making an attempt to drag the victim, inserting his hand in the nicker are itself sufficient to inferred that said act have been committed with sole intention of sexual assaults. Hence, according to learned P.P. act of victim of weeping, leaving the spot immediately 3 to 20 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­000545­2015 Special Case (POCSO) No. 16/2015 and informing her mother about it are all natural conduct of human being and thus, same are itself sufficient to substantiate the allegations. According to learned P.P. as the accused was caught on the spot itself there was no chances of misidentification or somebody else is dragged in this matter. She has then pointed out that though CCTV footage were installed and that the police have made an attempt to collect footage but as footage was not available police could not seize it but the person who has tested camera was examined to substantiate fact. According to learned P.P. depositions of victim and her mother are in itself sufficient to prove guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt and as the presence of the accused was admitted on the spot there is nothing on record to disbelieve the allegations. It was also pointed out that nothing has been brought on record to discard allegations for any reason. Hence, learned P.P. has requested to convict the accused as per law. 4] Per contra, initially advocate Mr.Dhikale has categorically argued that accused has not committed any offence but as a matter of fact accused had actually made an attempt to help the victim after she slipped on the oil spread on the floor due to oil tin damaged and though the accused had made an attempt to warn the victim about it while he was attempting to mop it, the victim did not listen to it, fell 4 to 20 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­000545­2015 Special Case (POCSO) No. 16/2015 down and started weeping. According to his arguments victim's mother immediately came on the spot and assaulted the accused and that too without hearing explanation of the accused persons and then when she realized that accused may lodged complaint against her for being assaulted, she has preferred this false complaint against him. According to his submissions said super market were having glass from all corners and if any such incident would have really occurred either any other person in the said super market or any passers­by could have easily noticed that incident. According to his submissions no independent witness is examined to substantiate the allegations in itself is sufficient to discard the depositions of victim and her mother. He has then pointed out that, victim had been to super market for purchasing eggs and eggs were found intact, in itself sufficient to disbelieve allegations. He has therefore, requested to consider defence of accused and acquit him from all allegations. 5] After the arguments, matter was actually fixed for Judgment on last occasion. However on that date again accused has preferred an application for providing him an opportunity to argue the matter on the ground that he wish to change the advocate for said purpose. In order to have fair trial, said application was allowed and advocate Miss. Pardeshi was again allowed to make her submissions for accused. Learned advocate Miss. Pardeshi has then submitted that entire incident as narrated by the victim and her 5 to 20 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­000545­2015 Special Case (POCSO) No. 16/2015 mother cannot be considered to be true as they have made contradictory statements in respect of sitting position of the accused. According to her submissions allegations are made that accused was sitting on the counter then there must be some workers working in the super market and as nobody's statement is recorded and nobody has been examined said allegations never gets corroborated. According to her submissions prosecution has never proved that the victim was really minor or has never established date of birth of Victim to apply section 8 of POCSO Act. According to her submissions when allegations are made that incident is occurred in super market then it is difficult to accept that anybody else was not able to see such heinous incident that too occurred in broad day light and on that basis itself request has been made to discard it. According to submissions there is no explanation as to why PW3 was not able to obtain CCTV footage at the time of incident and has made further submissions that it is highly improbable that footage was available prior to the time of incident and of the next day but only for the period of 4 to 5 hours said CCTV footage was not available. According to her there is no certificate filed by PW3 under section 65(B) of Evidence Act to believe his version. According to her as super market was made of glass then it is highly improbable that nobody would have seen incident either from inside or outside the shop and thus requested to discard evidence and extend benefit of doubt in favour of accused and acquit accused. 6 to 20 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­000545­2015 Special Case (POCSO) No. 16/2015 6] After having heard the rival advocates, following points arise for my consideration and I record my findings against each of them for the reasons noted below:­ S.N. Points Findings 1] Does the prosecution prove that accused on 16.08.2014, at about ..In the 12.00 hours, at N.K.Super Market, Flower Valley Complex, Sonali affirmative. hotel road, Nayanagar, Mira Road (E), Dist. Thane within jurisdiction of Mira road police station, have sexually harassed informant's daughter, a minor victim girl, age 8 years by physical contact and advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 354­A(1) of IPC? 2] Does the prosecution prove that accused on aforesaid date, time and ..In the place, committed sexual assault on informant's daughter i.e. minor affirmative. victim girl age 8 years by dragging her towards him, inserting his hand in her nicker and moving it on her private part with sexual intent which involves physical contact without penetration and thereby committed an offence punishable under Sec. 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012? 3] What order ? Accused is convicted as per final order. REASONS As to point nos. 1 to 3 :­ 7] In the instant case prosecution has alleged that accused has committed offences punishable under section 354A(1) of IPC and as the victim was minor also under section 8 of POCSO Act 2012. Prosecution was therefore required to establish necessary ingredients of both said sections. In order to bring guilt of the accused at home prosecution has examined aforesaid four witnesses. Out of said, 7 to 20 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­000545­2015 Special Case (POCSO) No. 16/2015 witness no.3 and 4 were respectively technical person who has made attempt to retrieve the footage at the time of incident and I.O. P.W.1 and 2 are respectively mother of victim and victim herself. Therefore, so far as prosecution's case is concerned, the depositions of victim and her mother being complainant in the matter were of material importance. Hence, initially their depositions are require to be considered in the light of the defence. 8] The mother of the victim PW1 has categorically deposed before this court that on the eventful date, time and place when her minor daughter had been to said super market for purchasing bread, eggs etc. around 12 noon, victim came back and she was weeping. According to complainant when she questioned her as to why she was weeping, victim had informed her that uncle who was sitting in the super market has took her aside, lifted her gown and when the victim had asked her as to what he was doing, that person had said that insect marched inside her nicker and he was taking it out and then inserted his hand inside her nicker and started fingering on her private part. The victim had questioned that person as to why he did so and started crying therefore, was left alone. According to complainant she immediately along with her husband and victim went to super market where the victim had identified the person and on being asked to that person as to why he had committed said wrong, that person initially has refused to do so and then started 8 to 20 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­000545­2015 Special Case (POCSO) No. 16/2015 apologizing for it. By that time people gathered on the spot and somebody from the said crowd informed police also and person was then handed over to police. 9] The victim was then examined as PW2 that too after administering oath on the ground that she has rational sense of understanding and on oath she has stated almost identical facts which were narrated by her mother. Both said witnesses were cross­ examined at length and accused has then attempted to bring that particular super market has entrance of glass made gate. So also remaining side of the super market are also made of glass. Accused has also put forth his defence that one oil tin was damaged due to which oil was spread on the floor and accused was mopping that oil wherein victim slept on that oil and sustained injuries on her head in fall and she started crying due to the said fall. It was also put forth that in suggestion form that after mother of victim i.e. complainant along with victim had come back to the market and had questioned the accused, he has tried to explain aforesaid facts to her but without hearing that, mother of the victim assaulted him. It was then suggested that in order to avoid complaint being filed on his behalf, mother had implicated him in this false case. Besides, said facts, some formal suggestions which were put to victim and her mother were denied by them. From aforesaid 9 to 20 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­000545­2015 Special Case (POCSO) No. 16/2015 facts, it was categorically brought by the evidence of PW1 and 2 it is apparent that both said witnesses have substantiated the act of the accused at the relevant time and though various suggestions were put to them, they were firm on the point that accused has committed aforesaid act. Hence, on the background of the said depositions of material witnesses the defence of the accused has to be scrutinized. 10] As observed above, two opportunities were granted to accused to clarify his various defence through two learned advocates. Initially learned advocate of accused has categorically put forth defence of his false implication followed by implication in order to avoid complaint being lodged by accused person due to assault by the mother of victim. However, if later defence is consider then for said defence accused person's presence on the spot has to be admitted. Therefore, once the presence of the accused at the time of incident is admitted, then onus shift on the accused to explain as to what were the grounds for victim or her mother to depose in the particular fashion against him. However, after the victim and her mother have categorically deposed about his particular act, referred to above, accused was not able to explain single circumstance beside his aforesaid defence of beating by PW1 on the basis of which PW1 and 2 will implicate him in such case. If aforesaid defence of the accused of oil being spread on the floor and accused was either attempted to save the victim from being fell down on the said oil or 10 to 20 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­000545­2015 Special Case (POCSO) No. 16/2015 his attempt to make her stand after being fell down, are considered as it is then said fact was require to be substantiated by the spot panchanama which was immediately carried out on the same day after matter was reported to police. However, on perusal of the spot panchanama there appears to be no reference of any such oil being spread on floor at relevant time of preparing the spot panchanama. On the other hand officer preparing spot panchanama Exh.20 has categorically made reference of floor of the super market was clean and neat. Thus, if the said panchanama is considered as it is, being admitted by defence in evidence, then it categorically reflects that aforesaid defence of the accused is improbable and certainly is not genuine or factual. Hence, it is difficult to accept that the particular defence of the accused at the relevant time. 11] Other defence which was raised by the accused was that in order to avoid complaint being filed he is implicated in this case. However, even if the said defence is considered as it is then also nothing prevented the accused from lodging the complaint against mother of the victim either before present complaint was lodged or even after present complaint was lodged to at least create a doubt in respect of occurrence of the allegations referred in this complaint. However, except a single suggestion that he has been implicated in this matter to avoid the complaint being filed by him there is nothing on record to say that as to what time accused has 11 to 20 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­000545­2015 Special Case (POCSO) No. 16/2015 made an attempt to lodge that particular complaint to say that circumstances which he has stated in the cross­examination were really genuine or factual. In absence of any such attempt on part of accused it is difficult to accept that just to avoid police case likely to be lodged by the accused, present complaint has been filed. Mr. Dhikale has made reference of unbroken eggs to argue that as the incident did not take place, eggs purchased by victim remain unbroken. However, there is no clarification about purchase of eggs by victim before the incident. Only reference of unbroken eggs has made in the deposition of victim. Therefore, said fact in itself will not make impact on victim's deposition. At this stage it would not be out of place to mention that minor omissions are bound to be made by minor victims. However, if reliance is placed on provisions of section 29 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 then the court has to presume occurrence of the incident on the basis of said presumption based on substantive corroborative evidence. 12] Allegations of the prosecution are that accused initially has taken a victim by the side and then on the pretext of removing an insect inserting his fingers inside the nicker of the victim and started fingering her private part, if consider in the sequence as narrated by the witnesses they are certainly sufficient to inferred that with sexual 12 to 20 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­000545­2015 Special Case (POCSO) No. 16/2015 intends only accused has committed said act. As the prosecution was under section 354­A(1) of Indian Penal Code along with Sec. 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 necessary ingredients which were require to be prima facie established on record viz. use of criminal force with sexual intend and by the depositions of the said witnesses it is apparent that while removing the gawn or inserting the fingers inside the nicker of the victim obviously criminal force was used and as observed above intentions can be gathered by the act from the moment the victim was taken aside for inserting hands in the nicker of the victim for fingering her private part. Hence, basic ingredients of both sections are apparently established by the depositions of the victim and her mother. The accused was unable to prove that he had no such mental state of which presumption is made under section 30 of POCSO Act. Thus, the court has to believe existence of such mental state of the accused. 13] Further, after the second chance was granted to learned advocate of the accused some new points were advanced and therefore, said points are also required to be dealt with while making comments on the depositions of the said two witnesses. Arguments were advanced that as the super market where the incident had occurred were made up of glasses it is highly improbable that anybody will see the incident either from insider the market or outside the market and being super market it is always flooded with 13 to 20 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­000545­2015 Special Case (POCSO) No. 16/2015 customers till no independent witness has been examined. However, though victim's mother has admitted the facts of entrance of super market being made of glass she has denied that remaining walls of the super market were made of glass. On her refusal of that particular point accused did not produce anything on record which really goes to establish that said walls were really made of glass only. Further, if we again consider the spot panchanama Exh.20 PW4 I.O. has prepared the sketch wherein he has shown iron rack being installed adjacent to four walls with material and grocery kept on the said racks. Thus, if said sketch map is consider as it is then it is difficult to accept that person outside the particular shop will be able to see the incident in the shop. Accused has failed to obtain any admission either from PW1 or from the victim herself that besides the accused there were other customers present in particular shop when the incident alleged had occurred. Thus, when the accused was not able to establish by the said admission that anybody else besides the accused was present in the shop said person would be able to see the incident going on in between iron rack flooded with grocery materials. Having regards to said facts said defence of the accused also has to be discarded. 14] Learned advocate has also made an attempt to show that as birth certificate of the victim is not properly proved the same 14 to 20 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­000545­2015 Special Case (POCSO) No. 16/2015 itself cannot be consider and if the same certificate is discarded then the provisions of POCSO Act will not be made applicable in the matter. However, even if we consider that except the reference of birth certificate being obtained by I.O. which is marked as Exh.22 the I.O. did not utter any word about it. However, since the beginning, it is apparent that from the deposition of witness no.1 and 2 that the victim is a minor and mother of the victim has referred her age as 8 years at the time of incident. The incident had occurred in the year 2015 and victim's deposition is recorded before this court on 17.03.2018. At that time the victim has stated her age as 12 years. Surprisingly, neither in the cross­examination of PW1 or PW2 defence has not even put forth any suggestion denying that victim was not aged about 8 years at the relevant time of the incident or 12 years as claim by her on the date of her deposition. Even there is no suggestion to the I.O. that Exh.22 allegedly obtained by him is forged or fabricated document. Hence, when that particular fact is nowhere denied by defence during cross­examination merely making submissions in arguments, disputing age of the victim cannot be consider at all. Opportunity was with the defence to obtain admissions to support their defence during cross­examination itself. However, for the best reasons known to the defence advocate, such suggestions were never put forth to discard the claim of the victim about her age. 15 to 20 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­000545­2015 Special Case (POCSO) No. 16/2015 Hence, fact which remains undisputed during examination­in­chief has to be consider in favour of the prosecution and against accused. Therefore, technical defence of the accused that POCSO is not applicable in the matter has to be discarded. 15] After having gone through the depositions of said witnesses it is apparent that depositions of material witnesses are sufficient to complete the link of the said particular events allegedly occurred on the date of incident. Prosecution, on the basis of that deposition have succeeded in establishing that accused had used criminal force with an intention of outraging the modesty and also committed sexual assault on a child aged about 8 years. From corroborated depositions of the witnesses there is nothing on record to disbelieve their version. The defence of accused person either argued initially or later on is certainly not sufficient to discard the said version. As a matter of fact accused was not able to create any doubt in respect of occurrence of the particular incident at the relevant time. Having regards to the said fact in my opinion depositions of the witnesses are certainly sufficient to prove the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt. The opportunity was with the accused to explain atleast a single ground to implicate him in this case. However, accused could not make out single ground which was sufficient to disbelieve the allegation against him. On the contrary he himself has admitted his presence without there being any defence of presence of other 16 to 20 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­000545­2015 Special Case (POCSO) No. 16/2015 person at the particular spot when the incident had occurred. Having regards to the said defence and in view of specific allegations of the witnesses his all said defences has to be discarded. 16] Needless to refer that reference has also been made about failure of PW3 to file certificate under section 65B of Evidence Act and to argue the point that surprisingly CCTV footage of day earlier to the incident and day after the incident are readily available but without there being any evidence on record CCTV footage of particular time itself is not available in itself is sufficient to discard the entire evidence of the prosecution. However, as a matter of fact if the deposition of PW3 is considered he has categorically deposed that on failure of the electric power the CCTV may shut down without capturing the particular images. His statement itself is sufficient to establish that there was absolutely no possibility of footage being tampered by anybody. As a matter of fact he has categorically stated that he has made an attempt to trace out the material footage. However, he could not even detect it on the hard disk as well. Hence, that particular deposition in absence of any specific cross­examination creating doubt about his deposition has to be accepted as it is. Therefore, merely because prosecution was not able to produce CCTV footage of the relevant time in itself is not sufficient to discard the deposition of victim and her mother. 17 to 20 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­000545­2015 Special Case (POCSO) No. 16/2015 The victim is a natural eye witness of the incident and her mother was immediately made aware about the incident by the victim herself. It was but natural conduct of the victim to disclose the particular act of the accused to immediately after the incident and thus, said being natural conduct of human being has to be accepted irrespective of the failure of the prosecution to produce the footage. Further reason referred in the deposition of PW3 appears to be more genuine and in absence of any specific grounds to disbelieve the allegations of victim and her mother it is certainly not fatal to the prosecution. Having regards to the said facts in my opinion the depositions of material witnesses are sufficient to establish the case of the prosecution beyond reasonable doubt. The witnesses by their depositions have completed the chain of events and thus, there is nothing on record to discard it. Having regards to the said fact in my considered opinion the prosecution has established the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt and therefore, I do not hesitate to record my findings against point no.1 and 2 in affirmative and hold accused guilty of the offence punishable under section 354­ A(1) of Indian Penal Code along with Sec. 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. As I hold accused guilty of the offence Judgment is deferred for hearing accused on sentence. 17] Heard accused on the point of sentence. He has submitted to take lenient view on the ground that he is only earning member of 18 to 20 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­000545­2015 Special Case (POCSO) No. 16/2015 the family consisting of his wife, old aged mother etc. and that he has not committed any offence. Heard learned advocate of the accused who in turn has also submitted to take lenient view in view of the said submissions of the accused.Per contra, learned P.P. has requested to impose maximum sentence as prescribed by law. 18] After having heard the rival advocates and having considered the circumstances in which the offence has been committed in my opinion the submissions for leniency offered by the accused can be considered. In my opinion following punishment will serve the purpose of both the sides. Hence, the order. ORDER 1] Accused Mohammad Tausif Sadar Khan is hereby convicted for the offence punishable under section 354­A(1) of IPC read with section 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act 2012 and he is sentenced to suffer R.I. for three years each under said sections and liable to pay fine of Rs.5000/­ each under said sections i/d. to suffer further R.I. for three months under each sections. 2] On recovery of fine amount an amount of Rs.7,500/­ be paid to victim as compensation by exercising powers under section 357(1) of Cr.P.C. 3] Both the sentences under said sections shall run concurrently. 19 to 20 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­000545­2015 Special Case (POCSO) No. 16/2015 4] Accused to surrender his bail bonds. 5] Copy of the Judgment be provided to the accused free of cost. Thane (Hemant M.Patwardhan) Date: 04.08.2018 D.J.­1 & Additional Sessions Judge, Thane. 20 to 20

1 Bail No. 220/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) Criminal Bail Application No.220/2016 Santosh Suresh Sathe .. Applicant versus The State of Maharashtra (Through Koparkhairne Police Station) .. Non­applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 1] By this application the applicant is seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. who was arrested 27/12/2015 by Koperkhairne Police Station in connection with C.R.No. I­427/2015 registered for an offence punishable under section 377, 384, 506 of I.P.C. and section 4 and 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as P.O.C.S.O. Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Mr.Sapkal for the applicant/accused and Spl.P.P. S.E.Phad for State I.O. present with case diary. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 26/12/2015 at the instance of the informant/mother of the victim­boy aged about 15 years with an indictment that accused repeatedly 2 Bail No. 220/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) committed carnal intercourse against the order of nature with the victim­boy. 4] The learned Counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant/accused is falsely implicated. He submitted that he submitted that the general allegations are made in F.I.R. without mentioning the date and time of the alleged act. He further submitted that the accused is resident of Ghatkopar and has no occasion to came down to Koparkhairne. He further submitted that there is no medical evidence to support the prosecution case. The accused is behind bars since 40 days. He further submitted that accused has no role in the alleged offence. The accused is permanent resident of the address given in the application and the only earning member of his family. The accused is ready to abide any conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing him on bail. 5] Per contra, learned Spl.P.P. strongly opposed the application submitting that the present applicant accused is involved in heinous offence. Since June­2015 accused developed friendship with the small victim­boy and shown him pornography and make him addicted to that and thereafter used to demand the money and committed unnatural sex with him. The investigation is in progress. There are chances of tampering with witnesses and prayed for rejection of application. 3 Bail No. 220/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R., it appears that the F.I.R. is lodged by the mother of the victim­boy about commission of carnal intercourse against the order of nature. The further allegations in the FIR is that the accused developed the friendship with the victim­boy aged 15 years and repeatedly committed unnatural offence. In medical certificate similar history appears to have been stated. The investigation is in progress and nascent stage. The victim­boy is minor and in the facts of the case, the apprehension of the learned Spl.P.P. about tampering of the witnesses appears to be well founded. Thus, this is not proper stage to release the accused on bail as the investigation is inprogress. Hence, I pass the following order:­ ORDER The application stands rejected. Thane. Date : 09.02.2016. (Ms. U.M. Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act), Thane.

Appln. 27/2015 judgment Received on : 22.01.2015 Registered on : 22.01.2015 Decided on : 27.02.2015 Duration : 1 months 5 days In The Court of the Session Judge, Thane (Presided over by Ms.V.V.Virkar, Additional Sessions Judge – 1, Thane) At Thane Criminal Misc. Application No. 27 of 2015 Exhibit No. 08 Gangabai Harishchandra Patil … Applicant Age 56 years, Resident of own house – Mahalakshmi krupa, Near Vitthal Hanuman Mandir, Ataligaon, Ambivali Taluka Kalyan, Dist. Thane. versus The State of Maharashtra … Opponent .. 2 .. Cri. Misc. Appln. 27/2015 judgment JUDGMENT (Delivered on 27.02.2015.) This application has been filed by the present applicant for return of auto rickshaw owned by her bearing registration no.MH­ 05­Z­3247, which was taken into custody by the police of Padgha Police Station pursuant to registration of offence under section 376 of I.P.C. and under section 3, 4, 5, 6 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act vide C.R.No.I­162/2014 at Padgha police station. It has been further contended on behalf of the applicant that she is not an accused in the said crime and she has no concern with this offence. Non­applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 1] By this application the applicant is seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C., who was arrested on 29/12/2015 by Thane Nagar Police Station in connection with C.R.No. I­289/2015 registered for an offence punishable under section 354(D),34 of I.P.C. and section 7,8 and 18 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Mr. Kanhere for the applicant/ accused and learned A.P.P. Mrs. Kapre for State. I.O. present. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 29.12.2015 at the instance of the informant victim­girl aged about 11 years with an indictment that accused used to chase her and once entered in her kitchen and on the day of incident caught hold her hand and outraged her modesty. 4] Inspite of giving sufficient opportunity, the Ld. counsel for the applicant / accused failed to argue the application. On perusal of 2 Bail No.230/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) application, the grounds raised for releasing the accused are that he is innocent and no intention to outrage modesty of child, complaint is false and concocted story, he is only earning member of family, investigation is practically completed. He is ready to abide conditions imposed by the Court and on such grounds he prayed for his release on bail. 5] Per contra, the learned A.P.P. opposed the application submitting that the offence is serious. The accused entered in the house of victim girl and he even entered in the house of other people. He is continuously harassing the victim­girl. .. 1 .. bail 185/2015 (Ord.Exh.1) Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Appln. No. 185/2015 This application is filed by applicant Pawan Ganesh Gaikwad for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with C.R.No.I-352/2014 registered at Kapurbavdi police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 354, 323, 504, 506 of I.P.C. and section 7 and 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the accused persons outraged modesty of the victim and when her mother intervened, her mother was beaten. and abused. It is further contended and argued that no such incident has happened and the applicant is falsely implicated in this crime on account of previous dispute. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/ accused is released on bail, he will co-operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that at the time of incident wanted accused held both hands of the complainant-victim with sexual intent and thereby he outraged her modesty and when her mother intervened the scuffle, the wanted accused and present applicant abused her mother in filthy .. 2 .. bail 185/2015 (Ord.Exh.1) language and also beat her. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl and the prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 354, 323, 504, 506 of I.P.C. and section 7 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012, it appears that the main allegation of molestation attracting offence under section 354 of I.P.C. is levelled against other accused and no role is attributed to this applicant in regard to molestation of victim and the allegation against him is only that there was quarrel and he abused the complainant and her mother. But then, it is submitted on behalf of applicant/accused that on account of previous dispute, he is falsely implicated in the crime. In such circumstance whether the allegations against the accused are true or not, would be the question to be decided on merits. Even nothing is to be recovered from the applicant/accused. 4] It is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the .. 3 .. bail 185/2015 (Ord.Exh.1) applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. 5] In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 6] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 7] Then, it has also to be mentioned that the investigation in the matter though almost completed the charge sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 8] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a .. 4 .. bail 185/2015 (Ord.Exh.1) fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order - ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Pawan Ramesh Gaikwad is released on P.R. bond of Rs.10,000/- [rupees ten thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions - He shall attend the concerned police station on every Monday between 5.00 p.m. to 7.00 p.m. till filing of charge sheet and shall co-operate with investigating machinery. He shall not not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and the prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this Court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 05.02.2015. (Mrs.V.V.Virkar) District Judge-1 and Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.

1 Bail No. 269/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) Criminal Bail Application No.269/2016 Kamlakar Makhan Sawra .. Applicant versus The State of Maharashtra Through Vikramgad Police Station .. Non­applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 1] By this application the applicant is seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. who was arrested on 12/01/2016 by Vikramgad Police Station in connection with C.R.No.I­/2016 registered for an offence punishable under section 363, 376 of I.P.C. and section 4 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as P.O.C.S.O. Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Mr. Sunil Patankar for the applicant/accused. Spl.P.P. absent. I.O. presenttwith case diary. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 05/01/2016 at the instance of the informant/mother of the victim­girl aged about 15 years with an indictment that on 04/01/2016 some unknown person kidnapped her daughter and expressed 2 Bail No. 269/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) suspicion against the accused. During investigation it was revealed that accused established physical relationship with the victim girl and thereafter, the provision of section 376 was added. 4] The learned Counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant/accused is falsely implicated. He further submitted that it is the case of love affair, which was known to the family members of the victim­girl and not liked by them. Therefore, the victim­girl on her own run away with the accused. He submitted that there was no force from the side of the accused neither the victim­girl was kidnapped. He further submitted that in fact accused married with the victim­girl. But due to false F.I.R. accused came to be arrested. Accused is student of 12th standard and his board examination has scheduled on 18th February. The accused is ready to abide any conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing him on bail. 5] Per contra, I.O. in person opposed the application submitting that the girl is minor and accused committed rape on her. The accused is involved in serious offence. The investigation is in progress. There are chances of tampering with witnesses and prayed for rejection of application. 3 Bail No. 269/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R., it appears that the F.I.R. is lodged by the mother of the victim­girl about her kidnapping by some unknown person and also expressed her suspicion against the accused. Perusal of medical certificate of the victim girl do not disclose any external injuries on her person. The victim­girl in her statement has clearly stated that she is having love affair with the accused which is not liked by her mother, and for that reason her mother always abused and assault her and she on her own accompanied with the accused and they were having physical relationship. The victim­girl completed 15 years and thus, about to attain the age of discretion. The accused is also a young boy of 19 years. The submission of learned Counsel for applicant about the accused and victim­girl were having love affair cannot be ruled out, however, the said aspect is required to be decided during trial. The accused is behind bars since 25 days. The material part of the investigation must have been completed. No fruitful purpose would be served by further incarceration of accused. The object of bail is neither punitive nor preventive but to secure the presence of the accused at the time of trial. He is ready to abide by the conditions imposed by the Court. In such circumstances the apprehension of investigating officer about tampering of witnesses can be addressed by imposing suitable conditions. Hence, I pass the following order ­ 4 Bail No. 269/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) ORDER 1) The application is allowed. 2) Applicant namely Kamlakar Makhan Sawra be released on bail on his executing P.R. Bond of ₹15,000/­ [Rupees fifteen thousand only] with one local solvent surety in the like amount on the following conditions ­ A] Applicant shall attend the concerned police station on every Sunday between 10.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon till filing the charge­sheet. B] Applicant shall co­operate in investigation and shall not tamper with prosecution witnesses. C] Applicant shall furnish his and his two blood relatives' address proofs and contact numbers and he is duty bound to inform I.O. and Court about the change of address, if any. Thane. .. 1 .. bail no.237/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 237/2015 This application is filed by applicant namely Nileshgiri Sajangiri Goswami for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. I­304/2014 registered at Shrinagar police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 376 of I.P.C. and section 4 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant induced the victim girl and kidnapped her and then had raped her. It is further contended and argued that no such incident of kidnapping has happened and there was love affair between the applicant and victim and the victim girl herself had left her house and it is a case of consent and that the applicant/accused is falsely implicated in this crime on account of previous enmity. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co­operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that the accused and girl were acquainted each other since before incident of kidnapping and the accused taking disadvantage of minor age of the girl, induced her by giving false assurance of marriage and then kidnapped her and had sexual intercourse with her under false pretext. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the .. 2 .. bail no.237/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) applicant/ accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl and the prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 376 of I.P.C. and section 4 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, it is clear that the accused and the victim girl were acquainted with each other and there was love affair between them and on assurance of marriage the accused alleged to have taken away the victim girl. But it is contended on behalf of applicant that he is falsely implicated and the girl is not minor and she had been with him of her own consent. In such circumstance the aspect in regard to the age of the girl and the consent would be the matter to be decided on merits. It is also to be mentioned that the accused is in jail since three and half months and even nothing is stated to be recovered from the applicant/ accused. 4] Then, it is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. .. 3 .. bail no.237/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) 5] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 6] Then, it has also to be mentioned that the investigation in the matter though almost completed, the charge sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 7] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Nileshgiri Sajangiri Goswami is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ The applicant/accused shall attend the concerned police station on every Wednesday between 10.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon till filing of the charge sheet and shall co­operate in investigation. .. 4 .. bail no.237/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) He shall not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and the prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this Court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. English dirty movies. ii) It is alleged that on 1/10/2016 at night time both the accused compelled the victim girl to drink liquor which was mixed in the milk.
