At that time she cried loudly, but accused No.2 Sandhya increased volume of T.V., so that her shouts would not go out of the house. Accused No.2 Sandhya used to say 'X' that she has to do this act, otherwise accused No.1 will not maintain her and her other sister and brother. Thereafter, accused did not allow the victim girl to go outside the house and even then they did not allow her to make phone call to anybody. Thus, they wrongfully confined her. iii) It is further alleged that on 3/11/2016 and 4/11/2016 accused No.1 again committed rape on the victim girl. Lastly on 5/11/2016 at about 7.30 a.m. accused No.1 has proceeded to his job and accused No.2 was sleeping. At that time somebody has came to collect garbage. Hence, the victim AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.29/2017 (Judgment). : 4: Special Case No.29/2017 (Judgment) CNR­MHTH01­000676­2017 girl opened the door. At the same time she saw one girl residing in the neighbourhood. The victim girl requested her that “muze bachav yahase nikalo,mere pitaji meresath jabardastise galat kam karte hai”. At the same time accused No.2 came there and dragged the victim girl inside the house and beat her. Thereafter, when accused No.2 had gone in the bathroom, the victim girl came in the gallery of the said house and by folding hands she requested persons going from the said spot to help her. Therefore, some other persons anyhow reached there and rescued the victim girl. iv) Initially the victim girl 'X' was not ready to lodge report against the accused persons. However, thereafter somebody has called police. Police came there and and took her to the police station. They enquired with her. The victim girl narrated the entire incident before the police. Police reduced into writing the said statement of the victim girl and lodged F.I.R. On the basis of the said F.I.R. C.R.No.I­311/2016 U/Secs. 120B, 323, 342, 506 r.w. Sec.34 and 376(f) of IPC and U/Secs. 5(n),6,7,8,9,10,11 and 12 of the POCSO Act came to be registered and handed over to lady PSI T.N.Khalde. [3] I.O. Smt.Khalde, PSI, on the same day visited to the spot of incident and prepared panchanama of the said house. She seized one laptop, mobile phone of Micromax Company and one bottle. Under the same panchanama she has also seized AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.29/2017 (Judgment). : 5: Special Case No.29/2017 (Judgment) CNR­MHTH01­000676­2017 wearing clothes of the victim girl. Thereafter, the I.O. seized hard­disk and memory card of the said mobile phone separately and prepared separate panchanamas to that effect. On the same day the I.O. forwarded the victim girl for medical examination to the Government Hospital. She recorded statements of some of the witnesses. Thereafter, she wrote letter to the concerned magistrate for recording statement of the victim girl U/Sec.164 of Cr.P.C. On 9/11/2016 the I.O. forwarded accused No.1 for medical examination and got done his medical examination. She has also forwarded letter on 7/11/2016 and 17/11/2016 for recording statements of the victim girl and other witnesses U/Sec.164 of Cr.P.C. Ultimately statement of the victim girl was recorded on 10/11/2016 U/Sec.164 of Cr.P.C. and thereafter on 29/12/2016 statement of 2 neighbours of the accused were recorded U/Sec. 164 of Cr.P.C. Thereafter, the I.O. forwarded the seized articles to F.S.L. Kalina for chemical analysis. On completion of the investigation the I.O. submitted chargesheet against both the accused. [4] Since the offence U/Sec.376(f) of IPC and other offences under POCSO Act leveled against the accused are triable exclusively by the court of Sessions and Special Court, the Ld.Magistrate committed the case to this Court. [5] I have framed charge (Ex.6) against the accused No.1 U/Sec.376(f) of I.P.C. and U/Secs.5(n), 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.29/2017 (Judgment). : 6: Special Case No.29/2017 (Judgment) CNR­MHTH01­000676­2017 & 12 of POCSO Act. And U/Secs.120 B, 323, 342, and 504 r.w. Sec.34 of IPC against both the accused. Particulars of the offences were read over and explained to both the accused to which they pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. [6] For want of incriminating evidence, statements of the accused U/Sec.313 of Code of Criminal Procedure are dispensed with. [7] Following points arise for my determination. I have recorded my findings thereon for the reasons stated below : S.No POINTS FINDINGS 1 Whether the prosecution prove that the accused No.1 repeatedly committed rape on his minor daughter 'X' ? Not proved. 2 Whether the prosecution prove that accused Nos.1 & 2 in furtherance of their common intention agreed to commit rape of minor girl 'X' by the accused No.1, did some act in pursuance of the said agreement to commit rape punishable with life imprisonment or rigorous imprisonment for a term of two years or upwards or a criminal conspiracy other than a criminal conspiracy ? Not proved. AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.29/2017 (Judgment). : 7: Special Case No.29/2017 (Judgment) CNR­MHTH01­000676­2017 3 Whether the prosecution prove that accused Nos.1 & 2 in furtherance of their common intention voluntarily caused hurt to minor girl 'X' ? Not proved. 4 Whether the prosecution prove that accused Nos.1 & 2 in furtherance of their common intention wrongfully confined minor girl 'X' in the room ? Not proved. 5 Whether the prosecution prove that accused Nos.1 & 2 in furtherance of their common intention, intentionally insulted the minor girl 'X' by abusing her in filthy language and thereby gave her provocation to break public peace ? Not proved. 6 Whether the prosecution prove that accused No.1 being a father of minor girl 'X' committed aggravated penetrative sexual assault on her ? Not proved. 7 Whether the prosecution prove that the accused No.1 committed sexual assault on his minor daughter 'X' by physically touching her by showing undue intimacy with sexual intent ? Not proved. 8 Whether the prosecution prove that the accused No.1 being a member of the armed forces or security forces committed aggravated penetrative sexual assault on his minor daughter 'X' ? Not proved. AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.29/2017 (Judgment). : 8: Special Case No.29/2017 (Judgment) CNR­MHTH01­000676­2017 9 Whether the prosecution prove that the accused No.1 committed sexual harassment of his minor daughter 'X' with sexual intent, by compelling her to see on T.V. English dirty movies ? Not proved. 10 What order ? Accused Nos. 1 & 2 are acquitted. REASONS AS TO POINTS NOS. 1 to 9 :­ [8] Since all the points for determination arose for one and the same incident, I took them together for discussion. [9] 'X' (P.W.1) is the victim girl. She deposed that in the month of Sept.2016 she had came to Thane just for a pleasure visit to the house of accused persons. At that time she was insisting accused No.1 to take her back to her native village for “Chatpuja”. Festival of “Chatpuja” was about to come after very few days. However, accused No.1 was not taking her back to the native place. Hence, she got angry and told this fact to the persons residing in the neighbourhood. Except this nothing had happened. She turned hostile to the prosecution. Therefore, she was cross­examined by the Ld.A.P.P. However, nothing truthful can be brought on record in favour of the prosecution. AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.29/2017 (Judgment). : 9: Special Case No.29/2017 (Judgment) CNR­MHTH01­000676­2017 [10] It is on the record that statement of the victim girl was recorded by the Ld.Magistrate U/Sec.164 of Cr.P.C. However, on going through the said statement it appears that she deposed nothing incriminating against the accused persons. In the said statement she stated that her father i.e. accused No.1 was not taking her back to the native place for “Chatpuja”. Hence, she got angry and lodged report so that he will take her back to the native place. [11] So far medical reports of the victim girl and accused No.1 are concerned, there is nothing incriminating in those reports. Similarly C.A. reports are also not supporting to the prosecution case. [12] On the background of the above evidence, prosecution has not proceeded further to record evidence of any other witness. [13] Thus, on the basis of the evidence and other material placed on record, I can safely conclude that the prosecution has not proved guilt of accused under any of the offences leveled against him. I, therefore, answer point Nos.1 to 9 in the negative. AS TO POINT NO.10 : 14] As mentioned above , prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of accused. Hence, the accused are liable to be AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.29/2017 (Judgment). : 10 : Special Case No.29/2017 (Judgment) CNR­MHTH01­000676­2017 acquitted. So far muddemal property i.e. Laptop and Micromax phone are concerned, they are liable to be returned to accused No.1 after appeal period is over. So far remaining muddemal property i.e. one bottle and clothes are concerned, they are being worthless liable to be destroyed after appeal period is over. I, therefore, in answer to point No.10 pass the following order : :ORDER: 1) Accused No.1 – Dhanraj Yadav is acquitted of the offence punishable U/Sec.376(f) of IPC and U/Secs.5(n), 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, and 12 of POCSO Act vide Sec.235(1) of Cr.P.C. 2) Accused No.1­ Dhanraj Yadav and accused No.2­ Sandhya are hereby acquitted of the offences punishable U/Secs.120B, 323, 342, and 504 r.w. Sec.34 of IPC vide Sec.235(1) of Cr.P.C. 3) Bail bonds of the accused shall stand cancelled. 4) The accused shall furnish P.R.bond of Rs.15,000/­ (Rs.Fifteen Thousand only) each and surety of like amount in compliance with the provisions of Sec.437A of Cr.P.C. 5) Muddemal property i.e. Laptop and mobile phone be returned to the accused No.1 after appeal period is over and remaining muddemal property i.e. one bottle and clothes being worthless be destroyed after appeal period is over. Thane. Dated: 21/01/2019 ( S. B. Bahalkar ) Special Judge, Thane, Under POCSO Act, 2012. AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.29/2017 (Judgment).

There is delay in filing F.I.R. and that to evict accused from the flat he is involved in false case. 12] In these circumstances following points arise for my determination and I record my finding to them for the reasons mentioned hereinafter :­ .....4/­ 4 Spl.POCSO Case 25/2014 Sr. POINTS FINDINGS No. 1] Whether prosecution proved that in In the between 04/11/2013 to affirmative. 09/11/2013 at 20.45 hours in the house of accused at Chistiya Building, Room No.1/103, Amrutnagar, Mumbra, within the jurisdiction of Mumbra police station accused tried to physically contact involving unwelcome explicit overtures to victim Fatima aged 5 years ? 2] Whether prosecution proved that In the on the said date, time and place affirmative. and during the course of same transaction, accused committed offence of sexual assault of daughter of complainant namely Kum. Father of Saba called her in the house, opened zip and of pant and touched her hand to his .....6/­ 6 Spl.POCSO Case 25/2014 private part. He caught her leg and she shouted. Non­applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 1] By this application the applicant is seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. who was arrested 26/12/2015 by Nerul Police Station in connection with C.R.No. I­352/2015 registered for an offence punishable under section 363, 376, of I.P.C. and section 3(A) & 4 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as P.O.C.S.O. Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Mr.Rathod for the applicant/accused and Spl.P.P Mrs. R.A.Navale for State. I.O. present with case diary. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 2/12/2015 at the instance of the informant/brother of the victim­girl aged about 16 years with an indictment that some unknown persons 2 Bail No. 279/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) kidnapped her. During investigation it was revealed that accused kidnapped the victim­girl and established physical relationship with her and therefore, the provisions of section 376 of IPC and section 3 and 4 of POCSO Act were added. 4] The learned Counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant/accused is falsely implicated. He submitted that in FIR itself, it is stated that the victim­girl left house on her own by writing a chit to her brother, and she was not found in the custody of accused. He further submitted that victim­girl left her own and not kidnapped by accused. Neither victim­girl stated that she was sexually assaulted by accused. She submitted that accused is young boy and is a student of 12 th std. and his examination are scheduled on 17 th February, 2016. He is ready to abide any conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing him on bail. 5] Per contra, Ld. Spl. P.P. opposed the application submitting that the date of birth of victim is 05/05/2000 and she is minor. The medical certificate of the victim shows that hymen is torn. There investigation is in progress and there are chances of tampering with witnesses and prayed for rejection of application. 3 Bail No. 279/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R., it appears that the initially the FIR was lodged about the kidnapping of the victim­girl by some unknown person . In FIR itself, it is clearly stated that the victim­girl left a note (chit) mentioning that she is leaving the house on her own as she was not liked by her father and brother. Further the statement of victim­girl did not reveal that the she was forced for physical relationship by the accused. The victim­girl has compled the age of 16 years and about to attain the age of discretion . The accused is young boy of 19 years and student of 12 th std. and his examination is scheduled in this month itself. The material part of investigation appears to have been completed. The object of bail is neither punitive nor preventive but to secure the presence of the accused at the time of trial. No fruitful purpose would be served by further incarceration of accused. Further he is not having any criminal antecedents. The accused is ready to abide by the conditions imposed by the Court. In such circumstances the apprehension of Spl.P.P. about tampering of witnesses can be addressed by imposing suitable conditions. Hence, I pass the following order ­ ORDER 1) The application is allowed. 2) Applicant namely Shubham Kailas Sawant be released on bail on his executing P.R. Bond of ₹15,000/­ [Rupees fifteen thousand only] with one local solvent surety 4 Bail No. 279/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) in the like amount on the following conditions ­ A] Applicant shall attend the concerned police station on every Sunday between 10.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon till filing the charge­sheet. B] Applicant shall co­operate in investigation and shall not tamper with prosecution witnesses. C] Applicant shall furnish his and his two blood relatives' address proofs and contact numbers and he is duty bound to inform I.O. and Court about the change of address, if any. Thane. Date : 08.02.2016. (Ms. U.M. Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act), Thane.

Code and under S. 8 and 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act on the accusations of outraging the modesty of victim girl, entering into the house of complainant, abusing, threatening and sexually assaulting a minor victim girl. 2] The case of prosecution, in brief, is that victim girl reside with her family at Ajayant Mitramandal Chawl, Ramnagar, Digha, Dist. Thane. On 10.10.2015, at about 10.30 a.m., the victim girl had come from school and was inside the room. The victim girl phoned her mother at about 13.30 hrs. and informed that accused touched his hand on the nose and made obscene gestures frequently, knock the bolt of door. After some time, the accused entered the house of victim girl and when she questioned him about entering in the house, the accused tried to come close to her by holding her hand. She got frightened, gave jerk to his hand and rushed to the house of her neighbour Chitra aunt. 3] The mother of girl Manisha Bachhav went to the police station and lodged complaint. On the basis of complaint, offence bearing C.R.No. I­209/2015 was registered u/sec. 354, 452, 504,506 of Indian Penal Code and Sec. 8, 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offence Act. Investigation was taken up by API Khatal. Police Officer went to the spot and prepared spot panchanama on 10.10.2015. Victim's statement 3 SPECIAL CASE(POCSO) NO.26/2016 CNR No.MHTH01­000723­2016 was recorded. Statements of neighbours were also recorded. The accused was nabbed. At last investigating officer filed charge­sheet in the Court. 4] My Ld. Predecessor has framed charge (Exh.2) against the accused for offence U/s.354, 452, 504,506 of I.P. Code and under S. 8 and 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. The contents of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. The defence of accused, as emerges from cross­examination and statement under Sec. 313 Cr.P.C., is of false implication. 5] The prosecution examined in all six witnesses to bring home guilt of accused. P.W.1 Manisha Bachhav mother of victim girl (P.W.4) at (Exh. 6), their neighbour P.W.2 Chitra Amar Bhilare (Exh.9), P.W.3 Gulab Ganpat Bachhav, father of victim girl (Exh.11), P.W.4 Bhagyashree Bachhav, victim girl (Exh.15), P.W.5 Police Naik Kisan Jadhav (Exh.19) and investigating officer P.W.6 Rahul Khatal (Exh.28). Prosecution has closed its evidence by filing pursis Exh.30. The prosecution has relied on F.I.R. Exh.7, spot panchanama Exh.29. 6] I have heard Ld.A.P.P. and Ld. Advocate for the accused. 7] Following points arise for my determination and I have given my findings thereon for reasons to follow : POINTS FINDINGS 01. Does prosecution prove that on SPECIAL CASE(POCSO) NO.26/2016 4 CNR No.MHTH01­000723­2016 10.10.2015, at 13.30 hrs., at R.No. 3999, …In the negative Ajantha Chawl, Ramnagar, Digha, Navi Mumbai accused threatened victim girl? 02. Does prosecution prove that on same date, ...In the negative. time and place accused gave filthy abuses and provoked victim girl to break public peace? 03. Does prosecution prove that on same date, ...In the negative. time and place accused entered into the dwelling house of victim girl having made preparation for causing hurt to her? 04. Does prosecution prove that on same date, ...In the negative. time and place accused outraged modesty of victim girl? 05. Does prosecution prove that on same date, …In the affirmative. time and place the accused have sexually u/s. 12 of POCSO assaulted victim girl? 06. What order? Accused is convicted as per final order. REASONS AS TO POINT NOS. 1 TO 6: 8] I would like to discuss all these points together being interlinked with each other. The victim girl and accused resides at Ajanta Chawl, Ramnagar, Digha, Navi Mumbai. They are neighbours. The victim girl was studying in 8th standard in Hind Mata Vidyalala. She born on 01.12.2002. The victim girl returned from school and she was alone at home. The victim girl deposed that the accused seen standing 5 SPECIAL CASE(POCSO) NO.26/2016 CNR No.MHTH01­000723­2016 by side of the house. The accused made obscene gestures by putting finger on his nose. She felt shy. She bolted the door. She heard the noise of knocking the door. She enquire as to who is there. She saw from window and accused Deepak was there. Sometime after she opened the door. The accused entered inside his house. The accused caught hold her hand and dragged towards himself. She felt shy. She rescued herself. She went to her neighbour Chitra ( P.W.2). Chitra Bhilare (P.W.2) deposed that she heard the cry of her son from outside and came out of the house. She saw accused Deepak present in the door of the victim girl. The accused saw her and then left the spot. 9] Manisha Bachhav (P.W.1) got the phone call from her daughter i.e. victim girl (P.W.4). P.W.1 Manisha was told by her daughter that the accused came in their house, caught her hand while she gave jerk and ran to house of Chitra. P.W.1 Manisha found the daughter scared. The mother of accused picked up quarrel with them and threaten them and lodged complaint to the police. Gaulab Bachhav (P.W.3) deposed that his wife Manisha (P.W.1) told him about this incident. Police Naik Kisan Jadhav (P.W.5) has recorded F.I.R. (Exh.9) A.P.I. Rahul Khatal (P.W.6) arrested accused, went to the spot and prepared spot panchanama (Exh.29). 10] I have heard Ld. A.P.P. and Ld. Advocate for accused. The victim girl (P.W.4) deposed that accused made gestures, entered inside and hold her hand and dragged her closed to him. She said to have rushed to her neighbour Chitra (P.W.2). Chitra (P.W.2) come with the alternate story that she saw the accused in front of the door of victim girl SPECIAL CASE(POCSO) NO.26/2016 6 CNR No.MHTH01­000723­2016 and on seeing her, he went away. If the girl could have been attempted to molest by the accused by entering into the house, then she definitely would have told this fact to Chitra (P.W.2). The evidence of Chitra and victim girl (P.W.4) only shows that the accused had come to the room of victim girl. Victim girl has categorically stated that the accused made gestures by putting his finger over her nose and she felt shy. Only this part of evidence is appear acceptable. 11] Manisha (P.W.1) has first time deposed in the court that the mother of the accused had threatened them to kill her husband if they dare to lodge complaint. It is evident from the material on record that there was no passing of any remark by the accused to provoke the victim girl to break public peace and has not committed criminal intimidation by passing threats . The evidence of victim girl that she was physically contacted by the accused does not appear probable as Chitra (P.W.2) saw the accused outside the door of victim girl. The defence has come with the case that neighbours have enemity and so, there is false implication. It is suggested to investigating officer Shri. Khatal (P.W.6) that the parties have old enemity but he denied this fact. It is suggested to victim girl that their family had a quarrel but she has flatly denied it. 12] Gulab Bachhav (P.W.3) father of the victim girl is also given suggestion that his mother used to give the amounts to others as a loan amount. He has admitted this fact. It is suggested in his cross­ examination that mother of Gulab Bachhav (P.W.3) gave loan amount to daughter­in­law of the aunt of accused. But, he has stated that he do not know about it. It is suggested to Manisha Bachhav (P.W.1) that they had 7 SPECIAL CASE(POCSO) NO.26/2016 CNR No.MHTH01­000723­2016 a quarrel, but she has given negative answer. There is no other evidence on record to show that there was a quarrel in between his family and family of accused prior to the incident. 13] It has come that the accused has visited the house of victim girl and made gestures by putting finger on his nose. This gesture attracts ingredients of offence u/sec. 11 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences, Act. It is sexual harassment to victim girl. So, I hold accused guilty for the offence punishable u/sec. 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. Here, I take pause to hear accused on the point of conviction. 14] I have heard accused on the point of sentence. Ld. Advocate for accused submitted that accused is 30 years old. He has two sons and one daughter. He stated that the neighbours have falsely implicated him. Ld. APP submitted that the offence is very serious and it is committed with the minor girl. It is submitted that no leniency will be shown otherwise wrong message will be sent in the Society. I have assessed all circumstances. Considering his age, his family background and no antecedents, I answer point Nos.1 to 4 in the negative and point No.5 in the affirmative for offence punishable u/sec. 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. In result, I pass following order : ORDER 1] Accused Deepak Dinkar Tayade is hereby convicted under Sec. 235(2) of Code of Criminal Procedure of offence u/s. 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 1 Order Exh.1(Cri.B.A.301/2017 ) ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN CRI. BAIL APPLN. NO. 301/2017 Sunilkumar R. Singh ...Applicant. V/s. State of Maharashtra (through Kalwa P.S.) ...Complainant. Heard Ld. Adv. Mr.Dinesh Tiwari for the applicant. Ld. A.P.P. Mr. Kulkarni for the State present. I. O. Present. 1] Applicant who is arrested by Kalwa police station, in Crime No. I­19/2017 for offence U/s. 354 of the I.P.C. and Sec. 8 & 12 of the POCSO Act, 2012, has sought his enlargement on bail. 2] It is the case of the prosecution that the applicant pulled the clothes of the minor victim aged 5 ½ years and molested the victim by running his hands on her face, chest and body. 3] Ld. Adv. Mr. Tiwari has submitted that applicant has been implicated in a false case because of enmity between both the parties. The applicant and the complainant's family has had a few serious fights which culminated in registration of false case against the applicant. There is an unexplained delay of 6 days in registering the FIR as against the alleged incident, which itself is self­explanatory that the present FIR is an outcome of a planned conspiracy against the applicant. The FIR was lodged after consultation and due deliberation and this casts a very serious doubt about the complainant's case. The applicant is gainfully employed in a private limited company and he does not work as a tutor and that the complainant herself and insisted upon the applicant that he should teach her along with 2 Order Exh.1(Cri.B.A.301/2017 ) the applicant's son. The wife and son of the applicant always continue to be at home so it is indigestible to assume that any incident as such would take place that too in the presence of the family members. There is neither any criminal force nor assault that could be attributed against the applicant and no offence under Section 354 of IPC could be said to have been made out against the applicant. The applicant and the victim reside on the same floor of the same building and are neighbours and there have been fights on trivial issues in the past due to which the present FIR has been lodged. The applicant is ready to abide by all the terms and conditions. 4] Per contra, Ld. A.P.P. has vehemently opposed the bail application on the ground that the victim is only 5 ½ years old. The applicant and the victim are next door neighbours and if the applicant is released on bail there is every possibility of threatening and tampering with the prosecution witnesses. The investigation is still in progress and charge sheet is yet to be filed. Moreover, the very act of the applicant producing a letter signed by various members of the society itself shows that the applicant and his family members are already trying to tamper with the prosecution witnesses. It is pertinent to mention that the said letter which has been produced in the court is not addressed to the IO of the concern police station but to the wife of the applicant which raises grave suspicion. 5] The investigation is in progress and charge­sheet has yet to be filed. Moreover, admittedly the applicant and the victim are neighbours. The accused came to be arrested on 18/01/2017. There appears to be some background about the previous disputes between the parties. In view thereof, I am inclined to allow the application subject to the following stringent terms and conditions only. 3 Order Exh.1(Cri.B.A.301/2017 ) ORDER [i] Bail Application is allowed. [ii] Applicants Sunilkumar R. Singh be released in Crime No.I­19/2017 for offence U/s. 354 of the I.P.C. and Sec. 8 & 12 of the POCSO Act, 2012, registered at Kalwa police station, on his executing P.R. and S.B. of ₹ 30,000/­ with one or two local sureties of like amount. [viii] The applicant is duty bound to inform the I.O. and the court about his change of address, if any. 1 Bail No. 289/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) Criminal Bail Application No. 289/2016. Yavniel Issac Naugaonkar .. Applicant versus The State of Maharashtra Through Koparkhairne Police Station .. Non­applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 1] By this application the applicant is seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C., who was arrested on 23/01/2016 by Koparkhairne Police Station in connection with C.R.No. I­29/2016 registered for an offence punishable under section 354, 506 of I.P.C. and section 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Mr. Nitesh Wagh for the applicant/ accused. A.P.P. absent, I.O. absent, case diary not produced. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 23/01/2016 at the instance of the informant/ mother of victim­girl aged about 17 years with an indictment that the accused outraged her modesty by holding her hand in presence of her mother. 4] The learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant­accused is falsely implicated. He submitted that the applicant accused is young boy and student of 12th Standard and he is 2 Bail No. 289/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) well known sports person in the school and is having good character. He submitted that the victim­girl and accused are studying in the same school and having good friendship however, informant mother of victim­girl opposed their friendship and did not allow the victim­ girl to meet accused and therefore, she lodged the false report against the accused. He submitted that the accused is permanent resident of the address given in the application and is ready to abide by any conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing him on bail. 5] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R. it appears that the allegations are about outraging modesty of victim girl aged 17 years. Further it appears that the only indictment against the present applicant accused is that he hold hand of the victim­girl and kissed her in presence of her mother. .. 1 .. bail 265/2015 (Ord.Exh.1) Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 265 of 2015 This application is filed by applicant Mrs. Rajeshree alias Sonu Santosh Bhosale for her release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. I­39/2015 registered at Kalwa police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 354, 13, 147, 149 of I.P.C. and section 8 and 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant/accused was the member of an unlawful assembly and all accused attacked the complainant and her aunty and beat them. It is further contended and argued that allegation relating to molestation is levelled against other accused and no specific role is assigned to the applicant/accused. It is further contended and argued that the applicant/accused is pregnant at present and therefore she requires prompt medical attention. It is further contended and argued that no such incident has happened and the applicant is falsely implicated in this crime on account of previous enmity. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co­operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that at the time of incident accused namely Maharaj held shoulder of the victim from backside and also made physical advances with her and then all .. 2 .. bail 265/2015 (Ord.Exh.1) accused persons formed unlawful assembly and beat the victim and her aunty who was with the victim. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl and the prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail she may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 354, 143, 147, 149 of I.P.C. and section 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012, it appear that the main allegation about sexual assault on the victim is levelled against other accused. Then, no specific role is attributed to the present applicant and she is stated to be pregnant at present. Then, it is the case put forth on behalf of the applicant/accused that she is falsely implicated in the crime on account of previous enmity. In such circumstance whether the allegations against the applicant/accused are true or not, would be the question to be decided on merits. Even nothing is to be recovered from her. 4] It is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. .. 3 .. bail 265/2015 (Ord.Exh.1) 5] In that respect it is contended by the applicant that she is permanent resident of the address given and she will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 6] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 7] Then, it has also to be mentioned that the investigation in the matter though almost completed the charge sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 8] In view of all above discussion and considering the fact that the applicant is pregnant at present and requires medial attention, I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Mrs. Rajeshree alias Sonu Santosh Bhosale is released on P.R. bond of Rs.10,000/­ [rupees ten .. 4 .. bail 265/2015 (Ord.Exh.1) thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ The applicant/accused shall attend the concerned police station as and when required and shall co­operate in investigation. She shall not not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and other prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. She shall not leave India without permission of this court. She shall furnish proof of her residence. Date : 04.02.2015. (Mrs.V.V.Virkar) District Judge­1 and Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.

(iv) A.P.I.Kolhatkar then recorded statements of some witnesses. He forwarded the said muddemal to F.S.L. Kalina for chemical analysis. On completion of investigation he submitted chargesheet against the accused U/Secs.377 and 506 of IPC and U/Secs.4,6 and 8 of POCSO Act. [4] Since the offence U/Secs.4, 6 & 8 of POCSO Act are exclusively triable by the Special Court, the Ld. J.M.F.C. committed the said case to this court. [5] I have framed charge (Exh.11) against the accused U/sec.377 and 506 of IPC and U/Secs.4, 6 & 8 of POCSO Act. Particulars of the offences were read over and explained to the accused to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. [6] Statement of the accused U/Sec.313 of Cr.P.C. is recorded. His defence is of total denial. He claimed himself to be innocent. AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.32/2017 (Judgment). : 5: Special Case No.32/2017 (Judgment) (CNR MHTH­000766­2017) [7] Following points arise for my determination. I have recorded my findings thereon for the reasons stated below : Sr. POINTS FINDINGS No 1 Whether the prosecution proves that the accused had carnal intercourse, which is against the order of nature, with a minor victim boy “X” ? Not proved. 2 Whether the prosecution proves that the accused committed criminal intimidation by threatening to a minor victim boy “X” ? Not proved. 3 Whether the prosecution further proves that the accused committed penetrative sexual assault on the minor victim boy “X” ? Not proved. 4 Whether prosecution further proves that the accused committed aggravated penetrative sexual assault on the minor victim boy “X”? Not proved. 5 Whether prosecution further proves that the accused committed sexual assault of the said minor victim boy “X” ? Not proved. 6 What order ? Accused is acquitted. REASONS AS TO POINTS NOS. 1 to 5:­ [8] Since all the points for determination arose from the one and the same incident, I took them together for discussion. AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.32/2017 (Judgment). : 6: Special Case No.32/2017 (Judgment) (CNR MHTH­000766­2017) [9] The victim boy and his father i.e. the informant are the important witnesses of this case. However, record shows that many times witness summons were issued to these witnesses. However, they were not found on the given address. In the result prosecution has failed to examine these two important witnesses. [10] Prosecution has examined in all 4 witnesses. Anagha Pawar (P.W.1) is the panch witness of the panchanama of the spot of the incident. She states that on 24/10/2016 she alongwith police had gone to the said spot. Police prepared panchanama of the scene of the spot and seized one bed­sheet and oil bottle from the said spot. Her evidence even if accepted as true and correct is not sufficient to connect the accused with the present crime. [11] A.P.I. Shevale (P.W.4) states that on 23/10/2016 he was on P.S.O.duty at Nerul Police Station. On that day Kurbanali the father of the victim boy lodged F.I.R. about the incident. Accordingly he reduced into writing the F.I.R. vide Exh.22. Thereafter, he forwarded the victim boy for medical examination to the N.M.M.C. Hospital. Then he visited to the spot of incident and prepared panchanama of the spot. [12] Unless evidence of Kurbanali, the informant is recorded, it cannot be said that the prosecution has proved the contents of the F.I.R. In the result the evidence of A.P.I. Shevale(P.W.4) is not of use to prove the guilt of accused. AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.32/2017 (Judgment). : 7: Special Case No.32/2017 (Judgment) (CNR MHTH­000766­2017) [13] A.P.I.Shinde (P.W.2) is one of the I.O. He states that on 29/10/2016 he arrested the accused and forwarded him to the N.M.M.C. Hospital for medical examination. In my opinion, his evidence is also not helpful to prove the guilt of accused. [14] Rajendra Meher (P.W.3) is the landlord of the informant where the informant alongwith his family was residing. Rajendra (P.W.3) states that he let out said room to the informant. Said informant was serving at hospital. He came to know that something wrong had happened with the son of the informant. Except this he know nothing. Thus Rajendra (P.W.3) deposed nothing incriminating against the accused. [15] Thus,on the basis of above evidence and other material placed on record, I can safely conclude that prosecution has not brought sufficient and cogent evidence to prove that the accused had carnal intercourse against the order of nature with the son of th informant i.e.“X” and thereby committed aggravated penetrative sexual assault or penetrative assault as alleged by the prosecution. Even there is no evidence to prove the guilt of accused U/Sec.506 of IPC. I, therefore , answer point Nos.1 to 5 in the negative. AS TO POINT NO.6 : [16] As mentioned above, the prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of accused U/Secs.377 and 506 of I.P.C. and U/Secs.4, 6 & 8 of POCSO Act. Hence, accused is liable to be acquitted. AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.32/2017 (Judgment). : 8: Special Case No.32/2017 (Judgment) (CNR MHTH­000766­2017) [17] So far muddemal property is concerned, it being worthless liable to be destroyed after appeal period is over. I, therefore, in answer to point No.6 pass the following order : ­: ORDER :­ 1) Accused Ashad Ali Kitab Ali is hereby acquitted of the offences punishable U/Sec 377 and 506 of I.P.C. and U/Sec.4, 6 and 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 vide Sec.235(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 2) The accused shall furnish P.R.bond of Rs.15,000/­(Rs.Fifteen Thousand only) and surety of like amount in compliance of provisions U/Sec. 437­A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 3) Muddemal property being worthless be destroyed after the appeal period is over. 4) Accused is in jail in this matter. He be released forthwith if not required in any other matter. 5) Issue letter accordingly to the Jail Authority. Thane. ( S. B. Bahalkar ) Dated: 19/12/2018 Special Judge, Thane. Under POCSO Act, 2012. AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.32/2017 (Judgment).

At the cost of repetition the presence of Sharina, eye witness Hitlar and that of accused was on the spot which is a public toilet. 18] The complaint Exh.11 was filed by mother of victim shows that daughter Sharina informed that when she attended public toilet one person aged of 25 to 26 years .....7/­ 7 Spl.POCSO Case 30/2016 caught hold her neck and she shouted. The evidence of twisting her hand is not found. 19] Similarly, statement of Sharima was taken in question answer form by I.O. and it is at Exh.14. She stated that when she attended public toilet on 31/01/2016 at about 7.30 a.m. one person aged 25­26 years caught hold her neck and twisted right hand. She shouted. 20] The last witness is P.W. Priyatama Muthe. Being I.O. in this crime she recorded the statement of victim in question answer form as referred to above. Arrest panchanama Exh.15 and submitted charge­sheet. 21] She admitted that there is heavy dirt near the public toilet and there is separate entry to ladies and gents to public toilet. 22] It appears that there is a separate entry for ladies and gents to public toilet. Even assuming that there may be dirt, there is no incident reported, nor the defence appears probable that victim was to fall in the dirt and to save her accused caught hold or eventually touched her hand. 23] The offence of sexual assault prescribed in section 354A of I.P.C. requires physical contact and involving unwelcome and sexual overture as per clause (i). The other clause may not be attracted. 24] The offrence under section 7 of POCSO Act would .....8/­ 8 Spl.POCSO Case 30/2016 require act with sexual intent touching vagina, penis, anus or breast of the child or any other act with sexual intent/involving physical contact without penetration. 25] The provisions of section 11 of the said Act prescribe sexual assault. In these facts and circumstances, considering the evidence on record this Court is of the opinion that offence under section 354 A of I.P.C. and offence punishable under section 12 of the POCSO Act is found proved. The point No.1 is answered in the affirmative and point No.2 partly in the affirmative. 26] It is here I have heard the accused on the point of sentence. He submitted that he has not committed the offence and lenient view be taken and he is doing labour work of painting. The learned APP Mr. Kulkarni submitted that maximum punishment may be imposed. In the facts and circumstances this Court is of the opinion that following sentence would be just and proper :­ ORDER 1] Accused Sheetal Shivprasad Singh is convicted for the offence punishable under section 354A of I.P.C. and sentence to suffer S.I. for six months as per section 235(2) of Cr.P.C. 2] He is also convicted for the offence punishable under section 12 of POCSO Act as per sec. 235(2) of Cr.P.C. and sentence to suffer S.I. for one year as per section 235(2) of Cr.P.C. .....9/­ 9 Spl.POCSO Case 30/2016 3] Substantial sentences of both the offences should run concurrently. 4] Set off be given to him under section 428 of the Cr.P.C. for the period which he under gone in jail i.e. from 01/02/2016 till today. 5] Inform Jail Authority. Thane. (M.M.Walimohammed) Dt. 04/04/2017. Additional Sessions Judge­6, And Spl. Judge, POCSO Thane. ...../­

Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Mr. Parmane for the applicant/ accused and learned A.P.P. Mrs. Phad for State. I.O. present. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 31/01/2016 at the instance of the informant/victim­girl aged about 16 years with an indictment that both the accused stalked the victim girl and accused Sachin Londhe outraged her modesty by holding her hand and by uttering indecent words. 4] The learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant­accused is falsely implicated. He submitted that the 2 Bail No. 318/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) applicant accused is young boy and student of college. He submitted that in fact, the FIR was lodged out of misunderstanding. Accused did not commit any wrong act. The other co­accused is already released on bail and the applicant is entitled for the benefit of parity. He further submitted that accused is permanent resident of the address given in the application and is ready to abide by any conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing him on bail. 5] Per contra, the learned A.P.P. opposed the application only on the ground that the offence is in respect of minor girl. The accused outraged the modesty of the victim­girl. The investigation is in progress. There are chances of tampering of the witnesses and prayed for rejection of application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R. it appears that the allegations are about outraging modesty of victim girl aged 16 years by holding her hand. However, nothing has been recovered or discovered at the instance of accused. The material part of investigation appears to have been completed. The accused do not have any criminal antecedents. No purpose would be served by further incarceration of applicant­accused. The object of bail is neither preventive nor punitive but to secure the presence of accused at the time of trial. The other accused is already released on bail, and thus, the accused is entitled for the benefit of rule of parity. The accused is ready to abide by any conditions imposed by the Court. The apprehension of A.P.P. can be addressed by imposing suitable conditions. Bond of ₹ 15,000/­ [Rupees fifteen thousand only] with one local solvent surety in the like amount on the following conditions ­ A] Accused shall attend the concerned police station on every Sunday in between 10.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon till filing of the charge­sheet. C] Applicant shall furnish his and his two blood relatives' address proofs and contact numbers and he is duty bound to inform I.O. and Court about the change of address, if any. I have framed charge (Exh.02) against the accused for the offences punishable under sections 354A(1)(ii), 323 of Indian 3 Spl.C.( POCSO) No. 35/2017... Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­000817­2017 Penal Code and Sec. 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Contents of charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular language, to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 4. I have recorded statement of accused under section 313 (1)(b) of the Criminal Procedure Code at Exh. 17. Defence of accused is of total denial. Accused has not shown his willingness to examine himself on oath or any other defence witness on his part. 5. I have heard APP Smt. Chandane for the State and Ld. Advocate Shri. Zanzane for the accused. 6. On perusal of record and evidence on record, following points arise for my determination and consideration and I have recorded my findings thereon for the reasons as stated below:­ POINTS FINDINGS 1. Does the prosecution prove that on In the negative. 19.05.2016 and prior to two month before 19.05.2016, accused made demand of sexual favours to the victim and thereby committed an offence punishable under Sec. 354A(1)(ii) of IPC? 2. Does the prosecution prove that during In the negative. above mentioned period, time and place accused beaten the complainant / victim and burnt her hand on gas burner and voluntarily 4 Spl.C.( POCSO) No. 35/2017... Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­000817­2017 caused hurt to her and thereby committed an offence punishable under Sec. 323 of IPC? 3. Does the prosecution prove that during In the negative. above mentioned period, time and place accused had committed sexual harassment upon the complainant, a minor victim girl aged about 16 years with sexual intent and thereby committed an offence punishable u/sec. 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012? 4. What Order ? As per final order. REASONS AS TO POINT NOS. 1 TO 4:­ 7. That, in order to establish the guilt of accused, prosecution has examined in all four witnesses. P.W.1 Complainant as well as Victim is examined at Exh. 05. P.W.2 Nikita Vidyut Ghoshal – Exh. 06­ who is mother of victim P.W.3 Najuka Popat Patil – Exh. 09­ who is police officer who had registered the complaint of the victim P.W.4 Asha Arjun Jadhav – Exh.14 – who is Social Worker. After that inspite of giving sufficient opportunity, prosecution has failed to secure the presence of other witnesses. Hence, evidence of prosecution side is closed and statement of accused has been 5 Spl.C.( POCSO) No. 35/2017... Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­000817­2017 recorded. 8. In support of the contention of victim, prosecution has relied on complaint at Exh. 13, letter issued by member of Childline at Exh.15, letter issued by member of childline dtd.02.09.2016 at Exh.16. Statement of victim at Exh.17. 9. P.W.1 and 2 i.e. victim and her mother have turned hostile. They have not supported to the prosecution version. P.W.1 victim deposed that her date of birth is 08.02.2000. Accused is her real brother. At the time of incident she was learning in 10th standard at Saint Xaviers High School. Her mother used to go to shop. She herself, her grandmother and her brother used to remain at house. At that time, her brother used to go to college. He is three years elder than her . He used to pick up quarrel with her. Therefore, she made complaint with NGO. She further deposed that quarrel took place on petty reasons. Therefore, she made complaint to NGO. Member of NGO come to her house. They made enquiry with her and they had taken her to police station. She was sitting in one room. One paper was brought to her and obtained her signature. However, she does not know the contents of the complaint. 10. That, P.W. 1 victim does not support the prosecution. Therefore, she was cross­examined by Ld. A.P.P. She specifically denied all contents of the complaint. She specifically denied that accused used to make demand of sex from her. Hence, she made 6 Spl.C.( POCSO) No. 35/2017... Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­000817­2017 phone call to NGO. She further stated that after lodging complaint, she was residing at remand home for one or two months. However, she specifically denied that as she did not want to stay with her mother, therefore, she was residing in remand home. She stated that she does not remember whether the statement was recorded at remand home and by Magistrate or not. She flatly denied that she has shown spot of incident to police. 11. P.W.1­victim was cross­examined by Advocate for accused. In the cross­examination, she admitted that on 28.03.2014, she without giving intimation to her family members went to Calcutta along with her school friend Somnath. After that missing complaint was lodged at Kashimira police station. Then, her mother and mother of Somnath went to Calcutta and brought them at Thane. She further stated that she had given statement to police on 05.04.2014 that she went along with Somnath on her own accord. She further admitted that after returning back from Calcutta, there was regular school and her father told the accused to watch on her due to incident done by her. She further admitted that due to regular watch of her brother, she was angry with him and she called NGO and lodged complaint at police station. However, she specifically denied the contents of complaint. 12. So far as the evidence of P.W.2 is concerned, she also stated that the accused is her son. He used to go to technical college at Bhayander. Her daughter had not narrated her about the incident. She does not know whether her daughter has lodged 7 Spl.C.( POCSO) No. 35/2017... Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­000817­2017 complaint at police station. She admitted that police called her at police station. She further stated that police has not recorded statement of her daughter in her presence. She further stated that she does not know as to why her daugher lodged complaint agianst the accused. P.W.1 has not supported the prosecution version. Therefore, she was cross­examined by Ld. A.P.P. She denied the correctness of contents of her statement. She admitted that after incident her daughter was not residing with her. However, she does not know whether her daughter had given in writing that she does not want to reside with her. P.W.2 has not supported to the prosecution version. Therefore, she was cross­examined by Ld. Advocate for accused. In the cross­examination she admitted that when her daughter ran away with one boy, she along with mother of that boy went to Calcutta to bring them back. She further admitted that after returning back, her daughter was in anger. She told to her son to keep watch on the victim in school and house. Hence, complainant lodged report against the accused. Evidence of P.W.1 and is not supporting to the prosecution's version. Therefore, it is not acceptable and discarded. 13. P.W.3 Najuka Patil, P.S.I. deposed in her evidence that on 19.05.2016, complainant along with two ladies of childline came to police station and lodged report at police station against her brother. Victim was 16 years old. She stated that the contents of complaint are correct. It is at Exh.10,11 and 12. She has recorded her complaint as per her say. She flatly denied that FIR was recorded at the instance of member of childline and 8 Spl.C.( POCSO) No. 35/2017... Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­000817­2017 complainant has not lodged any complaint against her brother. 14. P.W.4 Asha Jadhav who is member of Childline deposed that on 18.05.2016, her colleague Deepali Verma received phone call on No.1098. Caller informed her that her brother demanded sexual relations with her. Then, she discussed with the witness on the Project co­ordinator and she along with Deepali Varma went on the spot in the house of caller. Victim was alone in the house. She narrated about the incident that her real elder brother demanded sexual relation from her. On her refusal he used to beat her. She told that the accused asks sex from her to save her from the beating of her mother. P.W.4 further deposed that there was burn injury on her hand. She narrated about the further procedure to victim. Then, she along with victim went to police station and lodged report. P.W.4 was cross­examined by advocate for accused in which she specifically stated that her friend received phone call. Accordingly, they went on the spot and lodged report at police station. P.W.4 was cross­examined. In the cross­examination, she denied that letter Exh. 15 to keep the victim / complainant in rehabilitation center is in her handwriting. It means this letter is not written by the witness. She only put her signature on Exh.15. She further stated that police had recorded statement of victim in her presence. 15. In this matter complainant / victim with the help of NGO lodged report against her real brother. However,the complainant has not supported the prosecution story in the court. Her mother also has not supported to the prosecution story. The 9 Spl.C.( POCSO) No. 35/2017... Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­000817­2017 complainant is main witness in this matter. Police officer stated that the complainant has lodged report and as per the say of complainant, she has recorded the complaint. However, there is no corroboration to the complaint. No other independent witness has been examined by the prosecution. Complainant and accused are real sister and brother residing together along with their parents in the same house. In absence of any evidence on the part of the complainant, it is difficult for me to hold the accused guilty. Hence, I come to the conclusion that the prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of accused beyond all reasonable doubts. Hence, I answer point Nos.1 to 3 in the negative and proceed to pass the following order: ORDER 1. Accused Vinit Vidyut Ghoshal is hereby acquitted under Section 235 (1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, for the offences punishable under sections 354A(1)(ii), 323 of Indian Penal Code and S. 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2. No. 35/2016. years ? 3] What order ? As per final order. REASONS POINT NOS. 1 AND 2 10] P.W.1 complainant minor victim girl deposed in her evidence that she was born on 10.10.98. Accused came to her and told her that he wanted to talk with her. He had asked for her phone number. She stated him that she did not possess phone. No. 35/2016. working as driver on school­bus. On 24.07.15 at about 11.30 a.m., he was busy in parking of his bus at gate no. 2 and after parking his bus, he was controlling to park other buses. Amarnath Roy, bus­driver had caught hold him. Then, police were called. 13] He deposed in his cross­examination that Ghodbunder road is busy road. There are some contradictions and omissions in his evidence. However, his evidence is not impeached by the accused on the point that he heard the noise of victim, so he went to her and she had narrated the incident to him, Amarnath Roy had caught hold the accused. 14] P.W.3 Vishnu Khandagale, Police Head­Constable rushed to the school on phone­call, deposed in his evidence that school authority had kept accused in one room. They had carried him to Kapurbavdi police station. Accused told them that “eq>s ekQ djks] xyrh gks x;h- eq>s NksM nks-” 15] P.W.5 deposed in his evidence that on the phone­call, he along with Shri. J.M.F.C. It can be gathered from the said statement that accused had been to her and disclosed his intention that he wanted to talk with her. He had asked her mobile number. She was not having mobile. So, he had asked land­line number. She was not recollecting the same. So, he took her behind school­bus by catching her hand. He had tried to outrage her modesty. She gave jerk. 8 POCSO Case. No. 35/2016. 17] Victim in her report stated her age as 17 years. However, she has not stated her date of birth. However, P.W.1 victim had stated her date of birth as 10.10.98. Her date of birth nowhere denied by the accused in her cross­examination. No suggestion was also given to victim (P.W.1) that she was not born on 10.10.98. Her date of birth is remained unchallenged. No doubt, no birth certificate or school­leaving certificate of victim is placed on record. However, as date of birth is remained unchallenged, it can be considered that victim was born on 10.10.98. Incident was taken place on 24.07.15. Therefore, on the date of incident, victim was under 18 years of age, i.e. she was 16 years, 9 months and 14 days old. There was no love affair between accused and victim. 18] From the entire evidence on record, it can be gathered that on the day of incident, accused had been to victim. He had caught hold her hand and taken her behind school­bus. Accused was apprehended and taken in the office of school and thereafter, he was handed over to police, before whom accused had confessed the guilt. The evidence of witnesses are reliable and trustworthy. There is no reason to disbelieve their version. I therefore, answer both the points, accordingly. 19] As offence against accused is proved, it is my imperative duty to hear him on the point of sentence. Hence, the judgment is paused here. Thane, (A.S. Bhaisare) Date­ 26.04.2018. Special Judge (POCSO) and Additional Sessions Judge­2, Thane. 20] Heard accused in person and his counsel Shri. Kulkarni on the 9 POCSO Case. No. 35/2014. Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] The prosecution case is that on 07.12.13 at about 6.00 a.m., victim in her school dress, went to the school. Thereafter, he came to know that accused Nandan Basar had kidnapped the victim and established sexual relations with said minor victim. Offence vide C.R. no. 137/13 u/s. 363 of I.P.C. was registered. Police had carried out the investigation. Victim was referred for her medical examination. Doctor had examined her and issued medical certificate (Exh.11) (It is admitted by defence.). Statements of witnesses are recorded. Accused was referred for his medical examination. After investigation, charge­sheet was submitted in the Special Court. 3] My learned Predecessor framed the charge against the accused for the offences punishable under section 376(2)(h), 363 of I.P.C. and u/s. 3, 4 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012, on 02/07/2015. Details of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular, to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. His defence is of total denial. 4] During trial, defence has admitted certain documents on record, i.e. spot panchanama (Exh.7 and 8), seizure panchanama of victim (Exh.9), seizure panchanama of clothes of accused (Exh.10), medical report of victim (Exh.11), bonafide certificate of accused (Exh.12), O.P.D. card of accused (Exh.13). 5] To bring home the guilt of the accused for the charges leveled against him, the prosecution has examined as many as two witnesses i.e. 3 POCSO C. No. 35/2014. P.W. Name of witness Exh. Description No. No. 1] Vishnu Kashinath 4 Father of victim. Khevara. 2] Victim girl. 6 Victim. 6] Accused did not enter into witness box. Sindhudurga, then to Kaman and then to Usgaon. Thereafter, they returned back to Ganeshpuri and thereafter, they went to Anjurphata. This material witness has not supported to the prosecution story at all. On the contrary, she had deposed in her cross­examination that she married to accused and cohabiting with him. She had also a son from the accused. 10] P.W.1 Vishnu Khevara is not eye­witness to the incident. 11] Accused has admitted both spot panchanama Exh.7 and 8, seizure of clothes of victim and accused Exh. 9 and 10 and medical report of victim Exh.11. There is no material on record to show that on 13.01.16, victim was having mobile with her. On the contrary, she had specifically stated that on 14.01.16, her mother had handed over mobile hand­set to her, when she had attended her school with certain directions. Therefore, there is no substance in the entire cross of P.W.3 victim to disbelieve her evidence. On the contrary, her sole evidence is fully reliable and trustworthy. She has no reason to depose falsely against the accused. 24] P.W.2 Narayan Ganekar deposed in his cross­examination that on 13.01.16, no description of driver was stated to them. P.W.4 Sunil Gawade has deposed in his evidence that on 14.01.16, Rajashri Pande met him near the school. On 13.01.16, description of accused was narrated to them. The evidence of both these witnesses is contrary to each­other regarding the evidence that on 13.01.16, description of accused was narrated to them. However, description of accused was not material one. On the contrary, P.W.3 victim had not stated that she has disclosed the description of accused to anyone. But, she has stated about the driver of car and car number. On the basis of car number, police had caught hold to the accused. Sagar Bhapkar has deposed as per his investigation. 26] From the evidence on record, it can be gathered that by raising accelerator of the car, accused had tried to invite the attention of victim, thereby, victim had viewed to the accused. Accused had shown his private 11 S.C. No. 40/2017. part to the victim P.W.3. Accused had not touched to the victim. Section 354(D) of I.P.C. is in respect of stalking by any modes like Internet, e­mail or any other form of electronic communication. Therefore, it can safely be said that section 354(D) is not made out by the prosecution and there is no such story of the prosecution that accused had followed victim or contacted, or attempted to contact with victim (P.W.3). 27] However, it can safely be said that the prosecution had made out and proved the case against the accused under section 509 of I.P.C. and under section 11 punishable with 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. 28] Having considered the facts and circumstances of the matter, evidence on record and discussed reasons, prosecution beyond doubt, have proved the offence under section 509 of I.P.C. and under section 12 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012, against the accused. However, prosecution failed to prove the offence u/s. 354(D) of the Indian Penal Code. I therefore, answer to all the points, accordingly. 29] As accused found guilty for the offence punishable u/s. 509 of I.P.C. and under section 12 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012, it is my imperative duty to hear him on the point of sentence. Hence, the Judgment is paused here. Thane, (A.S. Bhaisare) Date­ 15.11.2017. Additional Sessions Judge­2 and Special Judge (POCSO Act), Thane. 30] Heard accused in person and through his counsel Shri. Kamble 12 S.C. No. 40/2017. on the point of sentence. They submitted that accused is driver by profession. He is sole earning member of his family. He has no antecedents on his record. He is not habitual offender. They prayed for leniency. 31] Heard Ld. A.P.P. Smt. Talhar. She submitted that maximum punishment be awarded. She further submitted for compensation. 32] Section 12 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012, prescribe punishment to the extent of three years and shall also be liable to fine, whereas section 509 prescribe punishment with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and also with fine. 33] Section 42 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 is dealt with alternative punishment. As per said section, the provisions in which greater degree in punishment is prescribed is to be considered if the offences made under Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and under I.P.C. mentioned in section 42 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 34] Having considered the facts and circumstances of the matter and evidence on record, accused is not entitled for good behaviour bond under the provisions of the Bombay Offender's Act. So also, having considered the nature of job of the accused and his income, in my view, victim is not entitled for any compensation. Hence, I proceed to pass the following order. ORDER 1] Accused Uttam Pandurang More, is hereby, 13 S.C. No. 40/2017. convicted under sec. 235(2) of the Criminal Procedure Code, of the offence punishable u/s. 12 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act and he is sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for one year and pay fine of Rs.500/­(Rupees Five Hundred Only) i/d. of payment of fine, he shall further suffer rigorous imprisonment for eight days. 2] Accused Uttam Pandurang More, is hereby, convicted under sec. 235(2) of the Criminal Procedure Code, of the offence punishable u/s. 509 of the Indian Penal Code. But, no separate sentence is passed in view of section 42 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 3] He was in custody from 14.01.2016 till 03.02.2016. Hence, he is entitled for set­off for the said period u/s. 428 of Cr.P.C. 4] Accused Uttam Pandurang More, is hereby, acquitted under section 235(1) of the Criminal Procedure Code of the offence punishable u/s. 354(D) of the Indian Penal Code. 5] Right to appeal before higher court is explained to the accused. 14 S.C. No. 40/2017. 6] Copy of this Judgment and order be given to the accused free of cost. Thane, (A.S. Bhaisare) Date­ 15.11.2017. Additional Sessions Judge­2 and Special Judge (POCSO Act), Thane.

.. 1 .. bail no. 336/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 336/2015 This application is filed by applicant Arbaj Jeneuddin Deven for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. I­19/2015 registered at Rabale MIDC police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 354 of I.P.C. and section 7 and 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant outraged modesty of the complainant victim girl. It is further contended and argued that no such incident has happened and the applicant is falsely implicated in this crime on account of personal vendetta. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/ accused is released on bail, he will co­operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that at the time of incident the accused inserted his hand in the underwear of minor victim girl with sexual intent and touched her private part and thus committed sexual harassment upon her. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl and the prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. .. 2 .. bail no. 336/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 354 of I.P.C. and section 7 and 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, 2012 with the allegation of committing sexual assault on the minor victim girl stated to be 3 years old, it appears that the accused had been arrested long back on 30.01.2015 and it is contended on his behalf that due to personal vendetta the complainant has falsely implicated him in this crime. In such circumstance whether the allegations against the accused are true or not, would be the question to be decided on merits. Even nothing is to be recovered from the applicant/accused. 4] It is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. 5] In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 6] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application .. 3 .. bail no. 336/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) cannot be rejected. 7] Then, it has also to be mentioned that the investigation in the matter though almost completed, the charge sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 8] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Arbaj Jeneuddin Deven is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ The applicant/accused shall attend the concerned police station on every Tuesday between 3.00 pm. to 5.00 p.m. and shall co­operate in investigation. He shall not not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and the prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 13.03.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.

There was no dispute between the applicant and the complainant. It is very much possible to commit such act even in crowded places. Investigation is in progress and since the applicant and the complainant are residing in the same locality, there is possibility of threatening and tampering with the prosecution witnesses. 5] The investigation is at nascent stage. Prima face, the FIR discloses the act of sexual molestation by the applicant. The apprehension of Ld. APP that there is every possibility of tampering with and threatening the prosecution witnesses is also well­founded. In view thereof, I am inclined to reject the bail application. ORDER Bail application stands rejected. Thane. ( Mridula V.K.Bhatia ) Dt:­16/02/2017. Dist. Judge – 08 and Special Judge (POCSO Act), Thane.
