(Delivered on 7th day of September, 2018) [1] Accused persons in furtherance of their common intention committed sexual assault and outraged modesty of a minor girl and threatened to kill her father. Therefore, accused are facing trial U/Secs.354 & 506 r.w. Sec.34 of the Indian Penal Code (in short I.P.C.) and U/Sec.8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offence Act (in short POCSO Act). [2] Brief facts of the prosecution case are as under :­ (i) 'J' (name is not mentioned) a minor girl is a daughter of Amarnath Rai (P.W.1). In the year 2013 'J' was about 16 years old. 'J' alongwith her two sisters, one brother and parents was residing at Indiranagar, Kalwa and the accused were also residing in the neighbourhood of 'J'. (ii) On 4/11/2013 at about 8.00 p.m. Amarnath Rai (P.W.1) came back to his house and after having meal he slept. At that time 'J' alongwith her sister and mother were preparing papad. At about 1.00 a.m. of 5/11/2013 they have completed their work of preparing papad. Thereafter, 'J' proceeded for toilet and thereafter when she was washing her hands and legs both the accused suddenly came there, gaged mouth of 'J' and took her in their house. Accused Ravindra touched her breast and cheek and told how she is looking beautiful. At that time she heard noise of AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.22/2015 (Judgment). : 3: Sessions Case No.22/2015 (Judgment) her father and mother just outside the house. Hence, she forcibly removed hand of accused Manoj from her mouth and gave call to her mother. At that time door of the house of accused Manoj was not properly closed. Hence, her father and mother entered into the house. Suddenly both the accused stand aside of 'J'. Accused Manoj threatened 'J' that “tere bap ko bol de, kisiko batana nahi, nahi to tumhare bap ko mar dalunga”. Therefore, they all got frightened and came back. They did not lodge complaint in the police station on that night. (iii) However, on the next day i.e. on 5/11/2013 they went to Kalwa Police Station, where 'J' lodged report about the incident. Police reduced into writing her statement. On that basis crime vide C.R.No.I­553/2013 U/Secs.354,506 r.w. Sec.34 of I.P.C. and U/Sec.8 of the POCSO Act came to be registered and handed over to Asst.Police Inspector Kothmire. [3] The I.O. i.e. A.P.I.Kothmire on the same day visited the spot of incident and prepared panchanama of the spot of incident. On the same day he arrested accused Manoj and prepared arrest panchanama. Thereafter, he recorded statements of the witnesses. He collected bonafide certificate of 'J' from her school. Thereafter, on 27/11/2013 he arrested another accused Ravindra Jaiswal. On completion of the investigation he submitted the chargesheet against both the accused. AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.22/2015 (Judgment). : 4: Sessions Case No.22/2015 (Judgment) [4] Since the offence U/Sec.8 of POCSO Act is triable by the court of Special Court, the matter is committed to this court. [5] I have framed charge (Ex.4) against both the accused U/sec.354 & 506 r.w. Sec.34 of I.P.C. and U/Sec.8 of POCSO Act. Particulars of the offences were read over and explained to the accused to which they pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. [6] For want of incriminating evidence statements of both accused U/Sec.313 of Code of Criminal Procedure are dispensed with. [7] Following points arise for my determination. I have recorded my findings thereon for the reasons stated below : S.No POINTS FINDINGS 1 Whether the prosecution prove that the accused persons in furtherance of their common intention, used criminal force to 'J', a minor girl , intending to outrage her modesty ? Not proved. 2 Whether the prosecution further prove that the accused persons in furtherance of their common intention, committed criminal AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.22/2015 (Judgment). : 5: Sessions Case No.22/2015 (Judgment) intimidation by threatening to 'J', a minor Not proved. girl ? 3. Whether prosecution further prove that the accused persons in furtherance of their common intention, committed sexual assault Not proved. on 'J', a minor girl ? 4 What order ? Accused are acquitted. REASONS AS TO POINTS NOS. 1 to 3:­ [8] 'J' (P.W.1)(Exh.9) is the victim girl. At the time of recording her evidence she was about 21 years old. She deposed that her birth date is 24/11/1997. In the year 2013 she alongwith her parents, brother and sisters were residing at Indiranagar, Kalwa. Both the accused were residing in the same vicinity. However, she denied that on 5/11/2013 she lodged report against the accused persons. She deposing nothing incriminating against both the accused. [9] Amarnath Rai (P.W.2)(Exh.10) is the father of 'J', the victim girl. He deposed that 'J' is his daughter. The incident took place about 5 years ago. However, he do not remember about the AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.22/2015 (Judgment). : 6: Sessions Case No.22/2015 (Judgment) incident. His daughter lodged report at Kalwa Police Station. However, police did not record her statement. He has also not deposed anything incriminating against both the accused. [10] On the background that both the important witnesses turned hostile to the prosecution, the Ld.A.P.P. as well as both the important witnesses have filed joint pursis and thereby closed further evidence. [11] Thus, on the basis of above evidence, I can safely conclude that the prosecution has not brought any evidence to prove the guilt of accused U/Secs. 354 & 506 r.w. Sec.34 of I.P.C. and U/Sec.8 of POCSO Act. I, therefore, answer point Nos.1 to 3 in the negative. AS TO POINT NO.4 : [12] As mentioned above, the prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of accused U/Secs.354 & 506 r.w.Sec.34 of I.P.C. and U/Sec.8 of POCSO Act. Hence, accused are entitled for acquittal. I, therefore, in answer to point No.4 pass the following order : ­: ORDER :­ 1. Accused Nos. (1)Ravindra Sunderlal Jaiswal and (2) Manoj­ kumar Khajel Prajapati hereby acquitted of the offences punishable under Sec. 354 & 506 r.w. Sec.34 of the Indian AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.22/2015 (Judgment). : 7: Sessions Case No.22/2015 (Judgment) Penal Code and U/Sec.8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act vide Section 235(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 2. 1 Bail No. 374/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) Criminal Bail Application No.374/2016 Sahil Aslam Ansari. .. Applicant versus The State of Maharashtra (Through Rabale Police Station).. Non­applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 1] By this application the applicant is seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. who was arrested on 08/01/2016 by Rabale Police Station in connection with C.R.No. I­33/2016 registered for an offence punishable under section 363, 366­A, 511 of I.P.C. and section 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as P.O.C.S.O. Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Miss Nandita Patil for the applicant/accused. Spl.PP Mrs.R.A.Navale I.O. present with case diary. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 08/01/2016 at the instance of the informant/mother of victim­girl aged about 5 years with an indictment that on 08/01/2016 around 03.00 2 Bail No. 374/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) p.m. accused attempted to entice her minor daughter to seduce her for illicit intercourse. 4] The learned Counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant/accused is falsely implicated. She submitted that the allegations in the F.I.R. that the girl was lured by giving ₹ 10/­ and seduced her for illicit intercourse, are totally false. The accused is behind bar since one month. He is only earning member of his family. The accused and victim­girl are staying in different area and therefore, there are no chances of tampering of witnesses. He is ready to abide any conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing him on bail. 5] Per contra, the Learned Spl.P.P. opposed the application on the ground that offence is serious in respect of minor victim­girl aged about 5 years. The F.I.R. speaks in volume. Informant caught hold the accused while taking her minor daughter and handed over to the police. The investigation is in progress. There are chances of tampering with witnesses and prayed for rejection of application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R., it appears that the F.I.R. is lodged by the mother of victim­girl specifically stating that in the afternoon her children were playing in the courtyard and around 03.00 p.m. her nephew informed her that 3 Bail No. 374/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) one boy is taking away her daughter on the hill. Therefore, she immediately rushed there and raised shout and snatched her daughter from the hands of accused and during scuffle she sustained nail scratch on her hand. Due to the shouts of the informant, the people gathered there and caught hold the accused. At that time, on asking the victim­girl disclosed that when she was playing, at that time, one uncle had been there and gave her ₹ 10/­ and kissed her and put his hand in her niker and taking her towards hill. Thereafter, the accused was handed over to the police and informant lodged the report. Thus, it prima­facie appears that the accused was caught raid handed while taking away the minor girl with ill intention. The offence is very serious in respect of minor girl aged about 5 years. The investigation is in progress and at nascent stage. The apprehension of learned A.P.P. about tampering of witnesses appears to be well founded looking to the seriousness of the offence. Hence, no case is made out for releasing the accused on bail. Hence, I pass the following order ­ ORDER The application stands rejected. Thane. Date : 23.02.2016. (Ms. U.M. Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act), Thane.

K/11, Shivprabha society, Room no. 11, Majiwada, Thane. ..Accused. ___________________________________________________________ Appearances­ Learned A.P.P. Smt. Talhar, for the State. Learned Advocate Shri. Mote, for the accused. JUDGMENT (Delivered on 15.03.2018.) 1] Accused Sanjay Namdeo Patil, is facing trial for the offences 2 POCSO Case No. 43/2017. punishable u/s. 354(A) of I.P.C. and Section 8, 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. 2] The prosecution case is that Mohan Pendse and his wife Anagha Pendse at their residential house at Vrundawan society, run music class. Accused was their student of Guitar, Mandolin, Violin and Cassio. He also runs his music classes separately at Majiwada. Rahul Karane whenever remained absent, accused used to take music class at Vrundawan society. Since 06.12.16, victim aged about 6 years, joined with Pendse music classes for cassio. The said class was run on Tuesday, Thursday and Friday during 7 to 8 p.m. On 09.12.16, victim had attended her class. Her father did not turn up to fetch her back after her class was over, she was waiting for her father in outer room. The accused who is lame by one leg, came to her, viewed obscene video on his mobile, he had removed zip of his pant and asked the victim to touch it and thereafter, he had given his penis in he hand. He had inserted his another hand in the pant of victim and touched to her vagina. By these allegations, complainant Varsha Prashanth Chandrashekhar had lodged her report Exh.11 against the accused. It is registered vide C.R. no. 299/16 u/s. 354(A) of I.P.C. and u/s. 8 and 12 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 3] P.W.5 P.S.I. Dadarao Sonawane had carried out investigation. He had seized two mobiles from accused. Accused was arrested. On 11.12.16, he rushed to the spot and recorded spot panchanama (Exh.15). Statements of witnesses were recorded. Victim was sent for giving her statement u/s. 164 of Cr.P.C. On 30.01.17, seized mobile was sent to C.A. After investigation, charge­sheet was submitted in the Special Court. 4] Heard both sides. I framed the charge against the accused for the offences punishable under section 354(a) of I.P.C. and Section 8, 12 of 3 POCSO Case No. 43/2017. the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, on 07.09.2017. Details of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular, to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. His defence is of total denial. 5] During trial, defence has admitted no documents. 6] To bring home the guilt of the accused for the charges leveled against him, the prosecution has examined as many as six witnesses i.e. P.W. Name of witness Exh. Description No. No. 1] Varsha Prashanth 10 Complainant. Chandrashekhar 2] Vrushali Vikas Kanvinde 14 Panch of spot panchanama. 3] Victim 8 Minor victim girl. 4] Mohan Shrinivas Pendse 17 Owner of music classes. 5] Dadarao Ramchandra 18 Investigating officer. Sonone 6] Atish Madhukar Atam 23 Panch of seizure panchanama of two mobiles of accused. 7] Accused did not enter into witness box. He has not examined defence witness. 8] Heard learned A.P.P. Smt. Talhar for the State. She submitted that victim was student of Cassio class. Accused was working there. On the date of incident, accused had shown obscene video from his mobile to the victim aged about 6 years and also outraged her modesty by giving his penis in her hand and by inserting his another hand in the pant of victim and by touching her vagina. Victim had stated entire story in her evidence. Mobile is seized from the accused. The evidence on record is not shaken 4 POCSO Case No. 43/2017. by the accused in their cross­examination. There is prompt report. Victim has also identified the accused. According to her, prosecution proved the offence beyond all reasonable doubts against the accused. 9] In support of her argument, Ld. A.P.P. placed her reliance on 'S.P.S. Rathore Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another, 2016 DGLS(SC) 1002', in which it is observed by Their Lordships that­ “There is devastating increase in cases relating to crime against women in the world and our country is also no exception to it. Although e statutory provisions provide strict penal action against such offenders, it is for the courts to ultimately decide whether such incident has occurred or not. Courts should be more cautious in appreciating the evidence and the accused should not be left scot­free merely on flimsy grounds.” Their Lordships further observed that ­ “In order to constitute the offence under Section 354 of the I.P.C., mere knowledge that the modesty of a woman is likely to be outraged is sufficient without any deliberate intention of having such outrage alone for its object. If intention or knowledge is one of the ingredients of any offence, it has got to be proved like other ingredients for convicting a person. But, it is also equally true that those ingredients being state of mind may not be proved by direct evidence and may have to be inferred from the attending circumstances of a given case.” 10] Heard learned counsel Shri. Mote for the accused. He submitted that evidence of P.W.3 is contrary to the evidence of P.W.1. There were 5 to 6 boys in the batch of victim. Their statements are not recorded. Accused was already arrested. Thereafter, Mr. Pendse was called at Srirang society and not on the alleged spot. There is no certain spot. The spot is changed. After the class was over, the students were 5 POCSO Case No. 43/2017. sitting in front hall. Other two students were also present. Victim was not become frightened after viewing the picture on mobile. Victim had not disclosed the incident to her father. Accused was not teacher in Pendse classes. Copy of panchanama is not handed over to accused. Mobile is not placed on record. Two mobiles were lying on the table. No demonstration was shown. Prosecution failed to prove the offence against accused. 11] Following points arise for my determination, which are being answered for the reasons given herein­below. POINTS FINDINGS 1] Whether prosecution proved that on Yes. 09.12.2016 in between 20.00 hours to 20.20 hours, at Pendse music classes, 9 B, room no. 11/12, first floor, Vrundavan society, Thane (W), accused had shown obscene video in his mobile to minor girl / victim aged 6 years, opened his zip of pant giving his private part in her hand, also inserted his hand in her under­pant and touched to her private part, intending to outrage or knowing it to be likely that he would thereby outrage her modesty, thereby, committed sexual harassment ? 2] Whether prosecution proved that on the Yes. above date, time and place, accused had shown obscene video in his mobile to minor girl / victim aged 6 years, opened his zip of pant giving his private part in her hand, also inserted his hand in her private part, thereby, committed the offence of sexual assault and sexual harassment ? 3] What order ? As per final order. 6 POCSO Case No. 43/2017. REASONS POINT NOS. 1 AND 2 12] In order to constitute the offence under Section 354 of the I.P.C., mere knowledge that the modesty of a woman is likely to be outraged is sufficient without any deliberate intention of having such outrage alone for its object. There is no abstract conception of modesty that can apply to all cases. A careful approach has to be adopted by the court while dealing with a case alleging outrage of modesty. The essential ingredients of the offence under section 354 of I.P.C. are as under­ i) that the person assaulted must be a woman; ii) that the accused must have used criminal force on her; and iii) that the criminal force must have been used on the woman intending thereby to outrage her modesty. 13] It has come in the evidence of P.W.3 victim girl that­ “In the year 2016, she was studying in Rustamji Cambridge International School. She is residing along with her parents and grand­parents. She had also joined her Cassio music class in Vrundawan society. Male teacher was teaching her Cassio. She had joined for the same since 06.12.16. On 9th December, 16, she attended her Cassio class. She was taught by male teacher. At 8.00 p.m., her class was over. She was waiting for her father to carry her to her house. Their teacher was cripple by one leg. He had shown one video on his mobile, in which a boy and girl were in naked condition. He had also removed his pant chain and he had shown his private part. He had asked her to touch his private part. He had also inserted his hand in her pant and touched to her private part and rubbed it. Thereafter, she got a ring. She felt that her father 7 POCSO Case No. 43/2017. came.” 14] She has further deposed in her evidence that­ “Accused had told her that the matter should be secret. She enquired with her father why he was late. Then, she went to her house along with her father. Her mother was present in the house. She had disclosed the incident with her. Thereafter, she along with her parents went to her music class. Then, her parents had enquired about the teacher. They were told by them that he left the class.” 15] She further deposed in her evidence that on 11.12.16, she had shown the spot to the police. Her statement was recorded by J.M.F.C. as per her say. 16] The victim had deposed in her cross­examination that­ “She knew Marathi. She was newly joined to the said Cassio music class. For three days, there were different teachers in Cassio class. She was unknown with their names. Her mother was along with her while her statement recorded by police and by J.M.F.C.” 17] She further deposed in her cross­examination that­ “There were 7­8 other students along with her for learning music. On 09.12.16, there was class in middle big hall. She did not know the name of teacher who had taught them on 09.12.16. After their class was over, she along with other students were sitting in front hall. One boy and one girl were also sitting there. When she viewed video on mobile, she was not frightened. The witness voluntarily stated that accused opened the door. At that time, Pendse family and their relatives were present in the house. She had not disclosed the incident with her father. The witness voluntarily stated that she was not fully prepared for learned Cassio.” 18] It has come in the evidence of P.W.1 Varsha Prashanth 8 POCSO Case No. 43/2017. Chandrashekhar that her daughter was born on 24.05.2010. She was studying in 1st standard in the year 2016. So also, she had joined her Pendse music classes, Vrundavan society, 9­B, first floor, room no. 11 and12, Thane (W), on 06.12.16 for learning Cassio music. Her class timing was 7.00 p.m. to 8.00 p.m. Her class was only on three days i.e. Tuesday, Thursday and Friday. She had supported to the version of P.W.3 victim. 19] She further deposed in her evidence that­ “On 09.12.16 at about 8.30 p.m., she returned back from her office to her house. Her victim daughter was found mum and nervous. She enquired the reason to her. She was told by her that her teacher had shown obscene videos on his mobile; he had opened the zip of his pant and asked her to take his private part in her hand and he had given his private part in her hand; he had also inserted his hand in her under­pant and he had touched to her private part; the said teacher is lame.” 20] It has further come in her evidence that­ “Then, she along with her husband and their victim daughter went to her music classes. Mrs. Pendse was present there. She disclosed the incident to her. However, she had shown her ignorance about the incident. Meanwhile, Shri. Pendse also came there. They were told by them that on 09.12.16, person namely Sanjay Patil had taught the music. They had requested them to call him as they wanted to talk with him. Accordingly, they had ringed him. They were told by them that Sanjay Patil was coming to Srirang society. Then, they all three along with Mr. Pendse and Mrs. Pendse went to Srirang society. Within 5­10 minutes, the said lame person namely Sanjay Patil came there. Her daughter had pointed out with him to be the same person. On enquiry, accused had declined about the incident. They ringed to Rabodi police station. Immediately police rushed there. Then, they had taken accused to police station. They also rushed to the 9 POCSO Case No. 43/2017. police station.” 21] It has come in her cross­examination that­ “During 8.30 to 8.45 p.m., they went to Pendse class. She does not know whether there is Srirang school in Srirang society. She voluntarily stated that they went to Srirang society. People are residing in Srirang society. No other persons were gathered in Srirang society. After arrival of the said boy, two­three persons were gathered. Witness voluntarily states that after arrival of police, they ran away. She had ringed to police. She was unknown with Sanjay Patil. She had not seen earlier to him. She cannot state the time when police reached at Srirang society.” 22] P.W.1 though is not eye­witness to the incident, she being mother of victim, immediately heard the story from the victim and she had lodged prompt report. She had supported to the version of P.W.3 victim. Victim had no reason to depose falsely against accused. Victim had identified the accused on the basis of his lameness. 23] P.W.4 Mohan Srinivas Pendse who runs his music classes at his residential house at Vrundawan society, wherein victim had joined for cassio classes, deposed in his evidence that accused Sanjay Namdeo Patil is his student for Gitar, Cassio and Mandolin. In his absence, they used to call the accused for supervision as a teacher of Gitar and Cassio. He has corrected his statement and deposed that accused was not teaching. He further deposed that on 09.12.16, accused was teacher in the music class of this witness Mohan Pendse. On that day, at about 8.30 p.m., he received call of his wife who has disclosed with him that the parents of victim are alleging that accused Sanjay Patil who is lame, has outraged the modesty of victim in the classes. Accordingly, he returned back to his house. Parents of victim had stated the incident to him. Thereafter, he had called accused 10 POCSO Case No. 43/2017. near Srirang Vidyalaya. Accordingly, they all went there. Accused came there. Father of victim had slapped him. 24] From the cross­examination of this witness, it can be said that nothing has been extracted to discard his evidence that on 06.12.16, accused was teacher in the music class of Mohan Pendse. 25] Victim in her statement before J.M.F.C., has also stated the incident specifically. From her evidence, it cannot be gathered that she was tutored by others. Besides, there was no reason to complainant or victim to make false allegations against the accused. Complainant and her husband were not acquainted with the accused and there were no cross terms with him. Victim had also recently joined the said classes. From the evidence on record, it can be gathered that after class was over, other two boys were present in the hall. However, there is no material on record to show that they were eye­witnesses to the incident. Therefore, non­examination of those children does not fatal the case. 26] P.W.2 is panch to the spot panchanama. P.W.5 has deposed in his evidence that he had recorded the spot panchanama. From the evidence of P.W.6 Satish Atam, it seems that two mobiles were seized from accused. The said mobiles and sim­card were sent to C.A. C.A. report was received. On examination, they have found pornography video film in the said mobile and sim­card. Victim had stated that obscene video has been shown by accused to her. The said version is corroborated by C.A. report that on the date of seizure of mobile, i.e. immediate after the incident, the pornography video file was in the mobile of accused. 27] Victim (P.W.3) on relevant time, was aged about only six years. Accused had shown obscene video to the victim from his mobile. 11 POCSO Case No. 43/2017. Not only that, he had put his hand under the pant of victim and touched her vagina. Besides, by removing his zip of pant, he had put his penis in the hand of victim. All this evidence is trustworthy and reliable one. Therefore, it can safely be said that prosecution proved the offence against the accused, as alleged by the prosecution, beyond all reasonable doubts. 28] As accused found guilty for the offence punishable u/s. 354(A) of I.P.C. and under section 8, 12 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012, it is my imperative duty to hear him on the point of sentence. Hence, the Judgment is paused here. Thane, (A.S. Bhaisare) Date­ 15.03.2018. Additional Sessions Judge­2 and Special Judge (POCSO Act), Thane. 29] Heard accused in person and through his counsel Shri. Mote on the point of sentence. They submitted that accused is lame by one leg. He is in jail since his arrest. He is young. He is having his old mother. His father is no more, who was ex­military­man. They prayed for leniency. 30] Heard Ld. A.P.P. Smt. Talhar. She submitted that maximum punishment be awarded. She further submitted for compensation. 31] Section 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012, prescribe punishment upto five years, but shall not be less than three years. Section 12 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012, prescribe punishment to the extent of three years and shall also be liable to fine, whereas section 354(A) of I.P.C. prescribe punishment upto three years and also with fine. 12 POCSO Case No. 43/2017. 32] Section 42 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 is dealt with alternative punishment. As per said section, the provisions in which greater degree in punishment is prescribed is to be considered if the offences made under Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and under I.P.C. mentioned in section 42 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 33] Having considered the facts and circumstances of the matter and evidence on record, accused is not entitled for any leniency than the punishment prescribed for section 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. Hence, I proceed to pass the following order. ORDER 1] Accused Sanjay Namdeo Patil, is hereby, convicted under sec. 235(2) of the Criminal Procedure Code, of the offence punishable u/s. 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act and he is sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for three years and pay fine of Rs.500/­(Rupees Five Hundred Only) i/d. of payment of fine, he shall further suffer rigorous imprisonment for eight days. 2] Accused Sanjay Namdeo Patil, is hereby, 13 POCSO Case No. 43/2017. convicted under sec. 235(2) of the Criminal Procedure Code, of the offence punishable u/s. 12 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act and he is sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for one year and pay fine of Rs.500/­(Rupees Five Hundred Only) i/d. of payment of fine, he shall further suffer rigorous imprisonment for eight days. 3] Accused Sanjay Namdeo Patil, is hereby, convicted under sec. 235(2) of the Criminal Procedure Code, of the offence punishable u/s. 354(A) of the Indian Penal Code and he is sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for one year and pay fine of Rs.500/­(Rupees Five Hundred Only) i/d. of payment of fine, he shall further suffer rigorous imprisonment for eight days. 4] All sentences shall run concurrently. 5] The accused was in custody from 10.12.2016 till today. Hence, he is entitled for set­off for the said period u/s. 428 of Cr.P.C. 6] Right to appeal before higher court is explained to the accused. 7] Copy of this Judgment and order be given 14 POCSO Case No. 43/2017. to the accused free of cost. 8] Muddemal mobiles be destroyed, after appeal period is over. Thane, (A.S. Bhaisare) Date­ 15.03.2018. Additional Sessions Judge­2 and Special Judge (POCSO Act), Thane.

.. 1 .. Special Case No.25/2015 Judgment Received on : 07.02.2015 Registered on : 07.02.2015 Decided on : 07.04.2015 Duration : 2 months IN THE COURT OF THE SESSION JUDGE, THANE AT THANE (Presided over by Ms.V.V.Virkar, Additional Session Judge-1, Thane) Special Case No. 25 of 2015 Exhibit No. 04 The State of Maharashtra … Complainant versus Ravi Raghuvari Kotiyan … Accused Age 36 years, Resident of Pleasant Park D/113, Mira Bhayander Road, Mira Road (E) JUDGMENT (Delivered on 07.04.2015.) The accused stands prosecuted for the offence punishable under section 354(D)(2) of I.P.C. and section 11 read with section 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short ''P.O.C.S.O. Act'') for stalking fostering personal interaction with the victim minor girl by holding her, in spite of disinterest shown by her. 2] In short the facts giving rise to the prosecution of the accused are that on 14.12.2014 at about 6.00 p.m. minor daughter of .. 2 .. Special Case No.25/2015 Judgment complainant namely Gaurangi was walking along the road in front of Royal park near Natasha Park, Penkarpada, Kashimira, and at that time the accused held her with sexual intent and tried to foster personal interaction with her but the minor girl showed disinterest and resisted and went home crying. It is further case of prosecution that when the complainant inquired with her as to why she was crying the girl disclosed about the incident of sexual assault on her. Therefore, the complainant and girl went out in search of said unknown person who committed sexual assault on the girl and on road at one turn near garage the girl saw the said unknown person i.e. the accused and pointed towards him to be the same person who outraged her modesty and on that the complainant raised shouts and people gathered there and caught hold of the accused and gave him in custody of police. Thereafter, the complainant went to police station and lodged complaint. 3] On the basis of her complaint, offence as per C.R.No. I- 483/2014 was registered at Kashimira police station and it was investigated into by P.S.I. Chavan. During the investigation panchnama of the spot was prepared. Statements of witnesses including victim girl were recorded. Copy of birth certificate of the girl showing her age was obtained. After completion of investigation, since there was sufficient against the accused, he was charge-sheeted for offence punishable under section 354D(2) of I.P.C. and section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and the charge sheet was submitted to the Special Court since provisions of P.O.C.S.O. Act are applied. 4] The accused was produced before Court by jail authorities. A charge as per Exhibit 2 was framed against the accused for offence under section 354D of I.P.C. and section 11 read with .. 3 .. Special Case No.25/2015 Judgment section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. The contents of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. The accused pleaded guilty and accepted the charges levelled against him and prayed for leniency while awarding the punishment. 5] On above facts of this case, the points which arose for my determination and my findings and reasons for the same are as under - Points Findings i) Whether the prosecution has proved that on 14.12.2014 at about 6.00 p.m. in front of Royal park near Natasha Park, Penkarpada, Kashimira, the accused was stalking the minor girl Gaurangi Vikrant Urunkar aged 11 years and tried to foster personal interaction with her by holding her in spite of disinterest shown by the girl ? Yes. ii ) Whether the prosecution has proved that the accused on the given day, date, time and place committed sexual harassment of said minor girl ? Yes. iii ) What offence, if any, is proved against the Both offences accused ? are proved. iv ) What order ? The accused is convicted. REASONS 6] As is clear the offence charge against the accused is under section 354D(2) of I.P.C. and section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act with the allegation that the accused had committed sexual harassment upon the complainant minor girl by trying to foster personal interaction with her by holding her when she was walking along the road on the given day, date, time and place. Even it is also clear from the complaint lodged by the complainant that very specific allegations are made against the accused and on that basis offence .. 4 .. Special Case No.25/2015 Judgment under section 354D(2) of I.P.C. and section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act are charged against the accused and the accused has been prosecuted for the said offence. 7] In such circumstance since the accused pleaded guilty and accepted the charges for the offence charged, he is liable to be convicted for the said charge under section 354D(2) of I.P.C. and section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. 8] At this stage the dictation of the Judgment is postponed for hearing the accused on the point of sentence. Date : 07.04.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act) Thane. Resumed. 9] The accused is made aware of the fact that he is held guilty for the offence under section 354D(2) of I.P.C. and section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and the punishment prescribed for offence under section 354D(2) of I.P.C. is Rigorous Imprisonment for a term not less than one year which may extend to three years and with fine and offence under section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act is punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine. 10] I heard the learned A.P.P. and the accused on the point of sentence. The learned A.P.P. submitted that looking to the serious nature of offence charged against the accused he is not entitled to leniency and he is liable to award maximum punishment prescribed. .. 5 .. Special Case No.25/2015 Judgment The accused prayed for showing him leniency on the ground that he is the only earning member in his family and his family is depending upon him for their livelihood. 11] Then, as is clear the offence charged against the accused is of serious nature with the allegation that the accused was stalking the minor girl and had held and her and fostered personal interaction with her in spite of disinterest shown by her. But then, it is submitted by the accused on the point of sentence that he has to look after his family members and he is the earning person in his family. 12] Then, so far as quantum of punishment is concerned, Section 42 of the P.O.C.S.O. Act provides : ''Where an act or omission constitutes an offence punishable under this Act and also under sections 166A, 354A, 354B, 354C, 354D, 370, 370A, 375, 376, 376A, 376C, 376D, 376E or section 509 of the Indian Penal Code, then notwithstanding anything contained in any law for the time being in force, the offender found guilty of such offence shall be liable to punishment under this Act or under the Indian Penal Code as provides for punishment which is greater in degree''. Then, as is clear the offence under section 354D(2) of I.P.C. is punishable with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years or with fine whereas offence under section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act is punishable with imprisonment which may extend to three years and also with fine. As such it is clear that sentence of imprisonment of either description i.e. S.I. or R.I. can be awarded for commission of offence under section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and therefore it can be said that as per provisions of section 42 of P.O.C.S.O. Act substantive sentence only for offence punishable under section 11 read with section 12 which is imprisonment of either .. 6 .. Special Case No.25/2015 Judgment description for a term which may extend to three years and also fine has to be awarded to the accused. 13] In all such circumstance I am of the view that following sentence would meet ends of justice. In the result I pass the following order - ORDER Accused namely Ravi Raghuvari Kotiyan is convicted for the offence punishable under section 354D(2) of the Indian Penal Code and also for offence punishable under section 11 read with 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and by invoking provisions of Section 42 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012, the accused is sentenced to suffer Rigorous Imprisonment for the period of six months and also to pay fine of Rs.500/- [rupees five hundred only] and in default to pay fine amount, he is sentenced to suffer S.I. for fifteen days only for offence punishable under section 11 read with 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. ii ) The accused is in jail since 14.12.2014. A set off under section 428 of the Cr.P.C. is granted to him for the term of the period of detention undergone by him during the investigation, inquiry and trial against the substantive sentence imposed upon him. iii ) Since no muddemal property is produced before Court, no order in regard to its disposal is passed. iv ) Copy of judgment be given to the accused free of cost. v) The proceeding is closed. Date : 07.04.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012) Thane.

1 Bail No.464/16 (order below Exhibit 1) Criminal Bail Application No. 414/2016. Shahalam Mukhtar Ahmad Ansari .. Applicant versus The State of Maharashtra Through Bhiwandi Police Station .. Non­applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 1] By this application the applicant is seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C., who was arrested on14/12/2015 by Bhiwandi Police Station in connection with C.R.No. I­ 350/2015 registered for an offence punishable under section 363,366(A), 354, 376 of I.P.C. and section 3,4,7,8,11,12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Mr. M.Z.G.Shaikh for the applicant/ accused and learned A.P.P. Mrs. R.A.Navale for State. I.O. present with case diary. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on14/12/2015 at the instance of the informant/father of victim­girl aged about 15 years and six months with an indictment that accused kidnapped his minor daughter and by confining her repeatedly committed 2 Bail No.464/16 (order below Exhibit 1) sexual assault on her. 4] The learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant­accused is falsely implicated. He submitted that prima­facie it is a case of consent . The victim­girl is about 16 years old and knowing the consequences of her act. He further submitted that in fact, informant is tenant of accused and there is some dispute about getting vacated the tenanted premises. He further submitted that investigation is almost completed and only formality to file charge­sheet remains. He submitted that accused is not having any criminal antecedents. He is behind bar since 75 days. He further submitted that accused is permanent resident of the address given in the application and is ready to abide by any conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing him on bail. 5] Per contra, the learned A.P.P. strongly opposed the application on the ground that offence is serious in respect of minor victim­girl aged about 15 years. She further submitted that the accused kidnapped victim on his motor cycle and then took her in a rented room and committed sexual assault on her. The victim­girl is minor and therefore, no question of her consent arise. The investigation is in progress. There are chances of tampering of witnesses and prayed for rejection of application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R. it appears that 3 Bail No.464/16 (order below Exhibit 1) there are serious allegations about kidnapping and repeated sexual assault on the minor victim­girl aged about 15 years and 6 months. The accused is aged about 35 years. Therefore, looking to the age of accused and the victim­girl, prima­facie the submission of learned counsel, that it is a case of consent, cannot be accepted at this stage. The victim­girl is below 16 years and therefore, even her consent is immaterial. In the medical certificate of the victim­girl the history about abduction by accused and had sexual inter­course for 3 to 4 times is given and the hymen appears to be torn. The statement of victim is recorded under section 164 of Cr. P.C. wherein also she had stated about confining her in a room for two days and committing forceful sexual inter­course with her against her wish. Thus, there appears prima­facie case against the accused. The offence is serious and the investigation is still in progress. Therefore, looking to the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case, as accused is facing serious charge, I found substance in the submissions of learned Spl.P.P. in respect of possibility of tampering of witnesses and fleeing away from justice. Hence, no case is made out for releasing the accused on bail. Hence, I pass following order :­ ORDER The application stands rejected. Thane. Date : 26/02/2016. (Ms. U.M. Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act), Thane.

.. 1 .. bail 406/2015 (Ord.Exh.1) Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 406/2015 This application is filed by applicant Sonu Amarjit Yadav for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with C.R.No. I­51/2015 registered at Vartaknagar police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 363, 376, 328, 506 read with section 34 of I.P.C. and section 4 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short ''P.O.C.S.O. Act''). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant helped the main accused in commission of offence of sexual assault on the minor victim. It is further contended and argued that the applicant is falsely implicated in this crime merely for the reason that he is the friend of main accused. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co­operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that the main accused Arvind Yadav induced the minor victim girl and kidnapped her and when they were travelling in rickshaw he gave her stupefying substance by mixing it with water and after drinking said water the victim felt giddiness and thereafter the main accused took her to Vapi and kept in one flat and then had forcible sexual intercourse with her and also threatened her not to disclose about said act to anybody. It is further contended and argued that the .. 2 .. bail 406/2015 (Ord.Exh.1) present applicant had abetted the main accused in commission of crime and the applicant was all the way with the main accused and the victim and that he was staying in the adjoining room of the room where the victim and main accused had stayed at Vapi. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/ accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl and the prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 363, 376, 328, 506 of I.P.C. and section 4 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and the girl is stated to be 16 years old, it is seen from the F.I.R. that the main allegations of sexual assault are made against the co­accused Arvind Yadav. Then, it is contended on behalf of the applicant that he is falsely implicated in the crime. In such circumstance whether the allegations against the accused are true or not, would be the question to be decided on merits. Even nothing is to be recovered from the applicant/accused. 4] Then, it is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. .. 3 .. bail 406/2015 (Ord.Exh.1) 5] In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 6] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 7] Then, it has also to be mentioned that the investigation in the matter though almost completed the charge sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 8] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Sonu Amarjit Yadav is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ .. 4 .. bail 406/2015 (Ord.Exh.1) He shall attend the concerned police station on every Saturday between 3.00 p.m. to 5.00 p.m. and shall co­operate in investigation. He shall not not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and other prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this Court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 04.03.2015. Accused Offence punishable under section 354­A & 506 of Indian Penal Code and under section 7 & 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Appearance ­ Spl.P.P. Mrs. R.A. Navale, for the State. Advocate Smt. N. M. Dode, for the Accused. 2 Special Case No.39/2014 (Judgment) JUDGMENT (Delivered on 2nd April, 2016.) 1] The Accused stands prosecuted for the offence punishable under section 354­A & 506 of Indian Penal Code and also under section 7 & 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act) for committing sexual assault on minor victim­girl aged about 16 years. 2] Shorn of unnecessary details, the indictment against the Accused are as under ­ [i] Informant victim­girl (P.W.1) is aged about 16 years and staying at Sainagar Slum area Ghodbunder road, Thane with her mother and siblings. She is studying in 11 th std. in Dnyanganga Education G.R. college, Ghodbunder road, Thane. [ii] Deepak Patil – accused is her neighbourer and working as a driver on the bus. Once before 2­3 months, he teased the informant. Therefore, she complained it to her parents and accused begged pardon, therefore, no complaint was lodged. [iii] On 25/09/2013 around 05.30 informant was returning from her college with her friends. At that time, accused was standing in front of the gate of college and by holding her hand, told her that, “today you are looking too sexy, came with me quietly.” She gave jerk to his hand, still he 3 Special Case No.39/2014 (Judgment) hold her and kissed her and also touched her inappropriately. He also threatened her friends to leave that place and asked victim­girl to accompany with her in a garden, else he will kill her. Therefore, informant raised shout and accused ran away. Thereafter, informant informed the incident on phone to her mother and then, lodged report against the accused. 3] On her report F.I.R. was registered against the Accused vide C.R.No.I­301/2013 for the offence punishable under section 354 & 506 of I.P.C. and under section 7 and 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. The investigation was handed over to A.P.I. Vikas Sarjerao Lokare (P.W.2) alongwith F.I.R. [Exh.11], spot panchnama [Exh.18] and arrest panchnama [Exh.17]. Statements of witnesses were recorded as per their say. Birth Certificate [Exh.19] of the victim­girl from Thane Municipal Corporation was collected. The leaving certificate was collected from the Dbyanganga Education Kasarwadavli, Thane [Exh.23]. Thereafter, investigation culminated into filing of charge­sheet in this Court being the Special designated court under P.O.C.S.O. Act. 4] The charge (Exh.5) was framed against the Accused for offence punishable under section 354­A & 506 of Indian Penal Code and also under section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. The Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial (Exh.6). The Accused took defence of total denial. 4 Special Case No.39/2014 (Judgment) 5] In response to application under section 294 of Cr.P.C. the defence has admitted arrest panchnama dated 26/09/2013 [Exh.17], spot panchnama dated 26/09/2013 [Exh.18] and birth certificate of victim­girl [Exh.19]. 6] In order to prove guilt of Accused Prosecution has examined following witnesses ­ P.W.1 Victim­girl Exh.10 P.W.3 Shri. Vikas Sarjerao Lokare Exh.21 (Investigating officer.) 7] The prosecution proved and relied on the following documents ­ Report / F.I.R.& printed F.I.R. Exhibit 11 & 12 School leaving certificate Exhibit 13 8] The prosecution closed its side of evidence by filing Pursis at Exhibit­24. The incriminating evidence came on record against the Accused was read over and explained him and his statement under Section 313(b) of Cr.P.C. was recorded. Accused neither examined himself nor examined any witness in his defence. 9] Heard learned A.P.P. Mrs. R. A. Navale for State and the learned advocate Smt. S. M. Dode for Accused. 10] On consideration of argument advanced on behalf of both the sides and on perusal of the oral & documentary 5 Special Case No.39/2014 (Judgment) evidence on record, following points arise for my determination, which are answered with the findings thereon, as under :­ Sr. Points Findings No. 1] Does the prosecution prove that on 25/09/2013 at 17.30 hrs. in front of gate of Dnyanganga Education G.R.College, accused used criminal force against the minor victim­girl aged about 16 years by demanding ..No. sexual favour and on refusal pressed breast of victim­girl and kissed her with an intent to outrage her modesty and he thereby committed an offence punishable under section 354­A of Indian Penal Code ? 2] Does the prosecution prove that on the same date, time and place, accused committed criminal intimidation by threatening the victim­girl to kill her and her friends ..No. if she refused to go with the accused, with intent to cause alarm to them and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 506 of Indian Penal Code? 3] Does the prosecution prove that on same day, time and place the Accused committed sexual assault on the said minor girl with sexual intent and he ..No. thereby committed an offence punishable under section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, 2012 ? 6 Special Case No.39/2014 (Judgment) 4] What order ? Accused is acquitted. REASONS As to Point No.1 to 3 : 11] All the points are taken up together for discussion, to avoid the repetition, as evidence about the same in common and inter­connected. 12] As the Accused is facing charge under section 354 of I.P.C. it is incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that Accused either assaults or used criminal force towards victim­girl to outrage her modesty or knowing it to be likely that he will, by his act, outrage the modesty of the victim­girl. Further, to prove charge of criminal intimidation u/s.509 of I.P.C., prosecution has to prove that the Accused threaten victim­girl and her friends to kill. So also as the Accused is facing charge under section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, therefore, it is further incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that the Accused with sexual intent touched the vagina, penis, anus, breast of a child or make the child touched vagina, penis, anus, breast of such person or any other person or does any other act with sexual intent which involves physical contact without penetration and by his such act committed sexual assault as defined in section 7 of the P.O.C.SO. Act. 7 Special Case No.39/2014 (Judgment) Age of victim­girl : 13] As the Accused is facing charge under P.O.C.S.O. Act, therefore, first of all it is incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that the victim­girl was child (minor) at the time of incident. The alleged incident took place on 25/09/2013. Informant / victim­girl (P.W.1) deposed that her date of birth is 24/08/1996 and her birth certificate which is at Exh.19 also evident her date of birth as 24/08/1996. She further deposed that in the year­2013 she was studying in 11th std. There is absolutely no challenge to the age of victim­girl. On the contrary defence has admitted birth certificate (Exh.19) of victim­girl. Thus, the prosecution proved that at the time of incident, the victim­girl was minor aged about 17 years and one month i.e. below the age of 18 years and she was a “child” as per definition given in Section 2(d) of P.O.C.S.O. Act. 15] To prove the charge against the Accused the prosecution has examined the informant / victim­girl who is the most material witness to prove the charge against the Accused. Informant /victim­girl (P.W.1)deposed that she knows accused who is her neighbourer and driver on bus. She further deposed that since 2­3 months, before the incident, accused used to try to talk with her. But she did not like it. She further deposed that on the day of incident, around 05.30 when she was returning from her college with her friends, at that time, accused caught hold her hand and told her to accompany with him. Therefore, she made phone call to her 8 Special Case No.39/2014 (Judgment) mother and returned home and then lodged complaint against the accused. Though in F.I.R. victim­girl has stated that accused by holding her hands, kissed her and touched her inappropriately and threatened her, but she did not utter a single word against the accused in her evidence. Further it is material to note that victim­girl admitted that her father did not like her talking with accused and he was under impression that victim­girl was refusing proposal for marriage due to accused. She even admitted that there was quarrel between her father and accused. Further victim­girl in her cross­ examination admitted that on the day of incident, she did not attend the college and the report was lodged by her father and everything in the report was narrated by her father to the police. Thus, the victim­girl took a dual stand before the Court and thus, her testimony is not believable. Even if, as far as holding her hand by the accused is taken as true, there is nothing to suggest that accused hold her hand with sexual intent or used criminal force to outrage her modesty. On the other hand it discerns that the Accused was friend of the victim­girl. Thus, there is absolutely no legal evidence on record to prove the charge against the Accused. The evidence of investigating officer A.P.I. Vikas Lokare (P.W.2) is formal in nature who recorded the statement of witnesses and filed the charge­sheet in the Court. 16] Thus, as the informant / victim­girl did not support the prosecution case, therefore, there is no iota of 9 Special Case No.39/2014 (Judgment) evidence against the Accused to prove the charge leveled against him. Thus, prosecution failed to prove that accused with sexual intent inappropriately touched minor victim­girl by using criminal force and outraged her modesty and committed criminal intimidation by threatening her. Hence, I answer point No.1 to 3 in negative. Therefore, in absence of any evidence against the Accused, he is entitled for acquittal. 17] In the result, I proceed to pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused Deepak Narayan Patil is hereby acquitted U/Sec. 235(1) of Cr.P.C. for the offence punishable U/Sec.354­A & 506 of Indian Penal Code and U/s. 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] His bail bonds stand cancelled and sureties are discharged. 3] The Accused is directed to furnish bail bond of the amount of ₹15,000/­ with one solvent surety in the like amount in compliance of provision of section 437­A of Cr.P.C. The judgment is dictated and pronounced in open Court. Date : 02/04/2016. (Ms. U. M. Nandeshwar), Thane Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act),Thane. District Judge ­1 and Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.
