In the night he came drunken, they had dinner and then went to sleep, but Accused did not sleep and was murmuring under the influence of liquor. P.W.4 even deposed that they were asking Accused to keep quite and sleep, but he was not listening and then he left their house. The material part of the testimony of Parvati P.W.4 is that, she even deposed that people from village came to their house and inquiring about the Accused. They all were in search of Accused, but he was not traced. She then learnt that Accused had raped victim­girl. 23] Parvati (P.W.4) is the relative of Accused and had no reason to depose falsely. Her evidence is most natural, wherein she had stated in plain and simple language about the visit of the Accused to their house on the day of incident. Even nothing has been brought in the cross­examination of this witness to disbelieve that on the day of the incident, Accused did not visit their house. On the contrary, from the evidence of P.W.4 it is very much clear that on that day Accused was under the influence of liquor and left their home in the night, and thereafter people of village came to her house in search of the Accused, which is most corroborative circumstances about taking away the victim­girl. 17 Special Case No.40/2014 (Judgment) 24] No doubt, the husband of Parvati (P.W.4) Govind Gawari (P.W.8), father­in­law of Sunita, who is sister of Accused did not support the case of prosecution on the material aspect that in the night around 01.00 a.m that he himself with the villagers took the search of Accused and victim­girl. However, Govind (P.W.8) corroborate the version of Parvati (P.W.4) in respect of the visit of Accused to their house on the day of incident and was under drunken condition and murmuring under the influence of liquor. P.W.8 even deposed that Accused said that he was to go his duty on next day, therefore, he left his house. Thus, it is fully established that on the day of incident, Accused was in the village of the informant and visited the house of P.W.4 and P.W.8 and even left their home in the night. 25] Then even from the testimony of Yamuna (P.W.2) and Kisan (P.W.3) who are the eye witnesses, who witnessed the Accused taking away the victim­girl in the clear and ample light and as discussed above, there is nothing to disbelieve the version of this witness, who are the most natural witness and their presence cannot be disputed being the relative and the neighbourer of the victim­girl. Medical Evidence :­ 26] The another important aspect of the case is the 18 Special Case No.40/2014 (Judgment) medical evidence in respect of ravishing the minor victim­girl of aged 5 years. In this respect, the testimony of Dr. Shinde (P.W.10) and Dr. Gote (P.W.11) is most material. 27] Dr. Dattatraya Shinde (P.W.10) who is medical officer attached to Primary Health Center, village Ase, Tal. Mokhada, Dist. Thane, deposed that on 20/11/2013 a girl aged 5 years was brought to the hospital from village with the history of kidnapping, for medical examination. Dr. Shinde further deposed that on examination he noticed following injuries. [i] abrasion over neck 2 cm on right side single. [ii] 3 abrasions over left side approximately 3 cm each [iii] hymen ruptured. [iv] laceration of labia majora [v] tear extended from vagina to anus. P.W.10 opined that the injuries were caused within 12 to 24 hours and the girl was sexually assaulted. He further deposed that he referred the girl to gynecologist at Cottage hospital at Jawhar and issued the medical certificate which is at Exh.48. The medical certificate below Exh.48 disclosed that the victim­girl was examined on 20/11/2013 at 02.20 p.m. at P.H.C. Ase with history of kidnapping which even corroborates the fact that the victim­girl was found in injured condition in the forest around 02.00 p.m. and then immediately taken to P.H.C. 19 Special Case No.40/2014 (Judgment) 28] In this respect the further material testimony is of Dr. Shrutika Gote (P.W.11) who deposed that in November­ 2013 she was attached to Civil Hospital, Nashik as a medical officer. On 20/11/2013 a girl aged 5 years (victim­girl) was brought to their hospital referred by medical officer Jawhar Cottage Hospital for medical examination with the history of kidnapping at 01.00 a.m. and perennial injuries. She had examined the victim­girl and noticed following injuries. [i] multiple curvilinear abrasion, reddish scabbed of size ranging (1.5 x 0.3) to (1.2 x 0.2c.m.) over left cheek front and sides of neck. [ii] abrasion reddish scan of size 5 cm x 3 cm was present over front of left side of neck 4 cm from midline 1 cm below jaw. She mentioned the discharge and foul smell as ' + +' indicating that the discharge and foul smell was severe. The '+' sign is mentioned according to gravity and severity of symptoms. On that day, sample was not collected. Police had not requested for the same. She further deposed that the vaginal swab of the victim­girl could not be obtained because the girl was operated and it was not possible to obtain vaginal swab. Next day after the police requested, samples were obtained and samples of vaginal swab, nail, blood were collected during treatment. 20 Special Case No.40/2014 (Judgment) 29] Dr. Gote (P.W.11) on the strength of examination of victim­girl opined that injuries noticed on the person of the girl was due to recent sexual assault and she was subjected to sexual inter­course. Accordingly, she issued certificate which is at Exh.50. The girl was also referred to Gynecologist and for surgery to 'on call' and surgeon. Dr. Gote (P.W.11) in cross­ examination specifically stated that victim­girl was admitted in their hospital since 20/11/2013 to 03/12/2013. 30] The medical certificate (Exh.50) about the examination of the victim­girl with the history of sexual assault clearly evident that the victim­girl was referred from Jawhar Kutir Rugnalaya with alleged history of kidnapping and perennial injury. The multiple curvilinear abrasion, reddish scabbed of size ranging (1.5 x 0.3) to (1.2 x 0.2c.m.) over left cheek front and sides of neck were seen on the person of the victim­girl. Further the injury on the neck of the victim­girl with abrasion reddish scan of size 5 cm x 3 cm was present over front of left side of neck 4 cm from midline 1 cm below jaw were also seen. Injuries on external genitalis, on Labia Majora and Labia Minora are swollen, oedematous, bruised. On fourchette, valva & perineum, fresh tear involving fourchetsh hymen, post vaginal wall, perineal body, ant wall of anorectum was present. (Exh.48­ Hymen ruptured, lacration of labia majora, tear extended from vagina to anus). 21 Special Case No.40/2014 (Judgment) 31] The above said injuries as mentioned in Exh.48 and Exh.50 discern that the tender age victim­girl was brutally ravished and even an attempt to throttle her was made. Even when the victim­girl was found in the forest, she was not able to talk or stand and was profuse bleeding from her private part. The victim­girl regained the consciousness after 3 to 4 days and was admitted in the hospital since 20/11/2013 to 03/12/2013 i.e. for 13 days. 32] P.W.Dr. Shrutika Gote (P.W.11) in cross­ examination again made it clear that the injuries found on the person of the victim­girl were fresh and caused within 24 hours. The victim­girl was firstly taken to P.H.C, Asegaon. From there she was referred to Jawhar cottage hospital and then to Civil Hospital Nashik, where she admitted on 20/11/2013 at 11.00 p.m. Further P.W.11 specifically denied that the injury on the person of victim could be possible by fall and specifically deposed that only one or two injuries at a time are possible. In such contingencies, (i.e. fall while running) and all injuries together are not possible. Thus, the medical evidence on record is very much clear about the brutal sexual assault on the victim­girl. Report of Chemical Analysis :­ 33] No semen found on clothes of victim­girl (C.A. Report Exh.39). However four semen stains each of about 1 22 Special Case No.40/2014 (Judgment) cm in diameter on front middle portion of underwear of Accused was found (C.A. Report Exh.40). So also three semen stains each of about 2 cm in diameter on front upper portion of Full Jeans pant of Accused was found (C.A. Report Exh.67). Prompt F.I.R. :­ 34] Further is significant to note that the incident took place in intervening night of 19/11/2013 & 20/11/2013 around 01.00 p.m. and the victim­girl was found in forest at the distance of 2 k.m. away from her house in ravished condition around 02.00 p.m. Then she was firstly brought home and then taken to P.H.C. Asegaon and from their the girl was referred to Jawhar Cottage Hospital and from there she referred Nasik Hospital where she was admitted for about 13 days. The F.I.R. was registered on 20/11/2013 at 19.30 hours. Few hours delay was caused as the victim­girl was found in very serious condition and therefore firstly medical aid was provided to her on priority and then report was lodged. Thus, the F.I.R. was promptly registered and therefore possibility of false implication is ruled out. Non­examination of Victim­girl :­ 35] The learned Spl.P.P. filed pursis on record at Exhibit 20 stating that victim­girl was too small at the time of incident and now she has forgotten the incident. However, learned defence counsel tried to make capital of non­ 23 Special Case No.40/2014 (Judgment) examination of victim­girl. He submitted that victim­girl was most material witness for prosecution and adverse inference is required to draw for non­examination of victim­girl. 36] Hear at the cost of repetition it must mention that victim­girl hails from very poor family from interior village. In normal course also a fluent testimony from such witness is not expected. In this case not only Spl.P.P. filed pursis about inability of victim­girl to deposed but I personally tried to interact witness to access the capacity of tender­aged victim­ girl to deposed when she was produced before me on 23/11/2015. However, victim­girl only able to state her name and she is going school. But she was unable to state any past incidence. In such circumstance I did not see any point to revise the horrified incident to victim­girl. Therefore, I took note about same on the pursis filed by Spl.P.P. below Exh.60. 37] There is no controversy about victim­girl being 5 to 6 years of age at the relevant time. It had been insisted that she was an important witness and non­examination of victim­ girl should prove fatal to the prosecution case. While, legal pleas are floated common sense cannot be left in cold store. The tender age of victim­girl who was aged about 5 years at the relevant time cannot be ignored. There is no controversy that in normal circumstances, in a case with respect to the offence punishable under Section 376, Indian Penal Code, the 24 Special Case No.40/2014 (Judgment) prosecutrix would be an important witness. But when the child is not in a position to depose properly as it is apparent in the facts of the present case, it would be travesty of facts to insist that she should have been produced as a witness. On that account the prosecution case cannot be thrown over board. This cannot be described as legal infirmity. The prosecution should examine all witnesses but not those who cannot depose properly. Reliance in this regard can very well be placed on the decision in the case of Mange v. State of Haryana, MANU/SC/0165/1979. In this appeal before the Hon'ble Supreme Court, the prosecutrix was deaf and dumb girl. She was only 13 years of age. The Supreme Court concluded that apart from being a child witness she was dumb and deaf and no useful purpose would have been served by examining her as a witness. In the case in hand, when, the victim­girl has forgotten the painful incident then there is no substance in revising from her the diabolic incident. Hear we can not over looked the capacity of tender­aged victim­girl about expressing the horrified incident or the beastly act of Accused. Therefore, the evidence of other material witnesses can not be looked with suspicion about naming the Accused. 38] On the point of non­examination of victim­girl, Ld. Spl.P.P. also rightly placed reliance on judgment of Hon'ble Bombay High Court in case of Nandakumar Jadhav vs. State of Maharashtra 2014 ALL MR (Cri)697, wherein also it was 25 Special Case No.40/2014 (Judgment) held that if victim­girl and her mother could not trace despite diligent effort then also accused can be convicted on basis of material available on record. 39] Here I would also like to mention that the non­ examination of a material witnesses is again not a mathematical formula for discarding the weight of the testimony available on record, howsoever, natural, trustworthy and convincing it may be. Thus, the line of argument so adopted by defence as the first assault must fail. Test Identification Parade (T.I.P.) :­ 40] In the present case the Test Identification parade of the Accused was conducted on 19/12/2013. As per prosecution, 8 witnesses identified the Accused during the Test Identification parade. The Test Identification parade was exhibited as Exh.53 as per provisions of Section 291­A of the Cr. P.C. However, on the application of the learned defence counsel, the S.E.O. was called for cross­examination. However, as far as the Test Identification Parade is concerned, it prima­ facie appears that the Test Identification was conduced without following the procedure given in the Criminal Manual and guidelines issued by the Hon'ble High Court. Therefore, said Identification Parade can not be believed. 41] Further the Accused was not unknown person, 26 Special Case No.40/2014 (Judgment) therefore, conducting the Test Identification parade is only a formality. Moreover, even the test identification parade is not mandatory in every case, and though, this piece of evidence is kept aside from consideration, the prosecution amply proved that the Accused took away the victim­girl who was sleeping beside her grand­mother and by taking her in the forest at the distance of 2 k.m. from the village, committed sexual assault on her. Scene of Offence :­ 42] As far as the scene of offence is concerned, the prosecution proved the spot panchnama through P.W.6 Devram Warghade who deposed that the panchnama of scene of offence was prepared in his presnce which is at Exh.24 and even the clothes of victim­girl were also seized in his presence and the panchnama about the same is at Exh.23. Nothing was brought on record during his cross­examination to disbelieve this witness. The scene of offence was shown by informant which is the house of the informant and the place in the forest which is at the distance of 2 k.m. from the village of informant where the grass having height of 5 ft. and in the area of 4 x 5 ft. the grass was seen in the scattered condition and having the dry stain of blood. One slack of small girl was also found there and the said slack and plain soil and soil with blood was seized under panchnama. From the scene of offence and its conditions, it can very well gathered that how brutally or in fact it can be said as a monster act by which tender­aged 27 Special Case No.40/2014 (Judgment) victim­girl was sexually abused. Further, even the condition of victim­girl when she found in the forest also discern the monstrous act of Accused. Post­incident Conduct of Accused :­ 43] The incidence in question took place in intervening night of 19/11/2013 to 20/11/2013 and the Accused was arrested on 23/11/2013 and his T­shirt and jeans pant was seized under panchnama (Exh.26). On 26/11/2013 Accused made disclosure statement and produced his underwear which was sized under panchnama (Exh.32 & 33). It is significant to note that API Rathod (P.W.9) deposed that at the time of arrest Accused was found staying in hotel and recorded his name as Shyam Jadhav in hotel register. P.W.9 also deposed that Govind Gavari (P.W.8) was with them in search of the Accused and he identifies the Accused to be Sanjay Warghade and after ascertaining his identity Accused was arrested. This is an additional link in the circumstance. 44] The Accused in his statement recorded under section 313 of Cr.P.C. stated that he was working in said Hotel since one year and he has been falsely implicated. However, the Accused did not examine any witness in his defence or produced any document to show that he was on duty in the said Hotel on the fateful night. 28 Special Case No.40/2014 (Judgment) Aggravated penetrative sexual assault :­ 45] Section 3 of the P.O.C.S.O. Act defines penetrative sexual assault. A person is said to commit “ penetrative sexual assault” if­ (a) he penetrates his penis, to any extent, into the vagina, mouth, urethra or anus of a child or makes the child to do so with him or any other person; or (b) ........; or (c) …....; or (d) ….... While in section 5 of P.O.C.S.O.Act “Aggravated penetrative sexual assault” is defined. As per Section 5(m) whoever commits penetrative sexual assault on a child of 12 years is defined as aggravated form of penetrative sexual assault. In the present case, the prosecution duly proved that the victim­girl is a child below the age of 18 years and most particularly, five years and six months and thus, the act of accused falls within the category of aggravated penetrative sexual assault as defined in section 5 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and the punishment thereof is provided under section 6 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. Presumption under section 29 & 30 of P.O.C.S.O.Act. 46] It is material to reproduce the provisions of section 29 and 30 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. As per Section 29 there is presumption that ''Where a person is prosecuted for committing or abetting or attempting to commit any offence under sections 3, 5, 7, and 9 of this Act, the Special Court shall presume that such person has committed or abetted or attempted to commit the offfence, as the case may be, unless 29 Special Case No.40/2014 (Judgment) the contrary is proved''. Thus, there is word 'shall' provided in Section 29 which make it obligatory on the Court that once the prosecution proves that the Accused is involved in any act under this Act, then the burden lies on the Accused to rebut it. So also, there is presumption of culpable mental state in Section 30 of the Act which includes intuition, motive, knowledge of a fact and the belief or reason to believe a fact. The learned counsel for defence argued that presumption is always rebutable and in the present case the defence has successfully rebutted said presumption by bringing on record various contradictory evidence of the prosecution witnesses. 47] As the prosecution proved beyond reasonable doubt that the Accused committed penetrative sexual assault on the tender­aged victim­girl, therefore, presumption arises in favour of prosecution and as per section 29 of the Act the burden lies on the Accused to rebut the same either through cross­examination of the prosecution witnesses or by adducing defence evidence. Admittedly Accused has not examined any witness in defence and, as discussed above, there is nothing material brought on record from the cross­examination of witnesses to disbelieve the prosecution witnesses. Thus, the Accused failed to rebut the presumption. 48] Thus, the evidence of the witnesses brought on record by the prosecution is truthful, reliable and trustworthy. 30 Special Case No.40/2014 (Judgment) There is nothing to disbelieve the version of the prosecution witnesses. There is absolutely no reason brought on record about false implication Accused. No mother would stake character of her minor daughter. Thus, the prosecution duly established that the Accused who was known to the family of the victim­girl had taken away the victim­girl in the midnight in a forest from the custody of her mother/informant and thereafter ravished victim­girl in diabolic manner in forest and left her in forest in bleeding condition and she was found on next day in afternoon in very bad condition, having bleeding from her vagina and noticed by villagers and was immediately taken to P.H.C. and then report was lodged. The medical evidence also is in corroboration to the prosecution case. 49] Further, the presumption also arising in favour of the prosecution and the Accused is failed to rebut the same. Thus, there remains no doubt that it was the Accused and Accused only who took away victim­girl for illicit intercourse and he being person in a position of trust towards the victim­ girl brutally ravished the minor victim­girl aged 5­6 years. Thus, the prosecution has proved the case beyond all reasonable doubt. Therefore, Accused Sanjay @ Sandeep @ Madkya Goving Warghade is held guilty for the offences u/s.363, 366­A, 376(2)(f) of I.P.C. and u/section 6 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and therefore the Accused is liable to be punished for the said offences charges against him. At this 31 Special Case No.40/2014 (Judgment) juncture it is necessary to hear the Accused on the point of sentence as per mandate of Section 235 of Cr.P.C. Till 01.30 p.m. the Accused is not produced from jail. Hence, I take a pause to hear the Accused on the point of sentence through video­conferance. Date : 12/02/2016. (Ms.U.M.Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act) Thane. Resume – 04.30 p.m. 50] Heard Accused on the point of sentence. Accused in person submitted that he is innocent. His old mother is depending on him and prayed for leniency. 51] Ld. Adv. Mr. Pandhre for Accused prayed that set off in sentence be given to accuse. On reminding him that minimum punishment for offences which stand proved against Accused is imprisonment for 10 years on that he prayed for leniency. 52] The Ld. A.P.P. Mrs. R. A. Navale absent. 53] I have given thoughtful consideration to the submissions advanced by the Accused in person and his Ld. Counsel. 32 Special Case No.40/2014 (Judgment) 54] Serious offences like rape on child having great impact on social order and public interest require exemplary treatment. Protection of society and stamping out criminal proclivity must be the object of law which must be achieved by imposing appropriate sentence. Undue sympathy to impose inadequate sentence would do more harm to the justice system to undermine the public confidence in the efficacy of law and society could not long endure under such serious threats. 55] In the present case conduct of Accused belies human relationship of trust and worthiness and reflects most unfortunate and abusive facet of human conduct. Child rape cases are cases of perverse lust for sex where even innocent children are not spared in pursuit of the sexual pleasure. There cannot be anything more obscene than this. It is a crime against humanity. Many such cases are not even brought to light because of social stigma attached thereto. After commission of brutally sexually assaulting the tender­aged victim­girl she was left in forest. Even attempt to throttle her eloquent from medical certificate. The minimum sentence provided for offence u/s.376(2)(f) of I.P.C. and for offence U/sec. 6 of P.O.C.S.O. Act is rigorous imprisonment for ten years. No case for imposing punishment lesser than minimum provided sentence. Therefore, in my opinion, the following sentence will meet the ends of justice. 33 Special Case No.40/2014 (Judgment) 56] In the result, I proceed to pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused Sanjay alias Sandeep alias Madkya Govind Warghade is hereby convicted U/Sec. 235(2) of Cr.P.C. for the offence punishable U/Sec.376(2) of Indian Penal Code and U/s. 6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 he is sentenced to suffer Rigorous Imprisonment for 12 (Twelve) years and to pay fine of 5,000/­ [Rupees Five Thousand only] and in default of payment of fine, to suffer the Simple Imprisonment for Five months. 2] Accused is further convicted U/Sec. 235(2) of Cr.P.C. for the offence punishable U/Sec. 366­A of Indian Penal Code and he is sentenced to suffer Rigorous Imprisonment for 4 (Four) years and to pay fine of 4,000/­ [Rupees Four Thousand only] and in default of payment of fine, to suffer the Simple Imprisonment for Four months. 3] Accused is further convicted U/Sec. 235(2) of Cr.P.C. for the offence punishable U/Sec. 363 of Indian Penal Code and he is sentenced to suffer Simple Imprisonment for 3 (Three) years and to pay fine of 3000/­ [Rupees Three Thousand only] and in default of payment of fine, to suffer the Simple Imprisonment for Three months. 34 Special Case No.40/2014 (Judgment) 4] The Accused is in jail custody since 23/11/2013. He is entitled for set off U/Sec. 428 of Cr.P.C. for the period he was in jail custody. 5] Substantive sentences to run concurrently. 6] On realization of amount of fine, an amount of ₹10,000/­ (Rupees Ten Thousand only) be paid to the victim­girl/daughter of informant. 7] Copy of the judgment be provided to the Accused free of cost as per provisions U/s. 363 of Cr.P.C. (Judgment dictated and pronounced in open Court through video­conference.) Date : 12/02/2016. (Ms. U. M. Nandeshwar), Thane Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act),Thane. .. 1 .. bail 410/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 410 of 2015 This application is filed by applicant Shravan Shrinivas Yelligetti for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no.I­24/2015 registered at Bhiwandi City police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 354A(1)(4), 354D(1)(1),(2), 341 of I.P.C. and section 11(i)(iv) and 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short ''P.O.C.S.O. Act''). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant outraged modesty of the complainant victim girl and also wrongfully restrained her from going to school and tuition. It is further contended and argued that no such incident has happened and the applicant is falsely implicated in this crime on account of previous enmity. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co­operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that the accused always used to wrongfully restrain the victim girl aged 15 years whenever she used to go to her school and tuition class. It is further contended and argued that the accused always used to tell the victim that he loves her and used to do indecent gestures and utter indecent words towards the victim whenever she refused to have any contact and conversation with the accused. It is further .. 2 .. bail 410/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) contended and argued that the accused also threatened the victim that if she refuse to develop love affair with him he will cut himself by blade and under such threat he had also expressed to perform marriage with her. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl and the prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 354A(1)(4), 354D(1)(1),(2), 341 of I.P.C. and section 11(i)(iv) and 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, the girl is stated to be 15 years old and it appears that the accused had been arrested on 29.01.2015. Then, it is also stated that the accused is falsely implicated in the crime since there previous dispute between them. Then, in the light of the fact that as per prosecution case also the accused used to express his love for the girl etc. In such circumstance whether the allegations against the accused are true or not, would be the question to be decided on merits. Even nothing is to be recovered from the applicant/accused. 4] It is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. .. 3 .. bail 410/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) 5] In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 6] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 7] Then, it has also to be mentioned that the investigation in the matter is though almost completed the charge sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 8] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Shravan Shrinivas Yelligetti is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ .. 4 .. bail 410/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) The applicant/accused shall attend the concerned police station once in a month on first Friday between 3.00 p.m. to 5.00 p.m. till filing of the charge sheet and shall co­operate in investigation. He shall not not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and the prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without previous permission of this Court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 26.02.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.

1 Bail No. 437/16 (order below Exhibit 1) Criminal Bail Application No. 437/2016. Vinod Gopal Chauhan .. Applicant versus The State of Maharashtra Through Rabale Police Station .. Non­applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 1] By this application the applicant is seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C., who was arrested on 04/02/2016 by Rabale Police Station in connection with C.R.No.I­ 57/2016 registered for an offence punishable under section 354 of I.P.C. and section 7 & 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Mr.Rajesh Kumar for the applicant/ accused and learned A.P.P. Mrs. Navale for State. I.O. present. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 03/09/2016 at the instance of the informant/mother of victim­girl aged about 12 years with an indictment that on 03/02/2016 around 08.15 p.m. informant heard cries of her daughter and when she went outside, she had seen that accused had inappropriately hold hand of her minor daughter and outraged her modesty and expressed his desire to kidnap her. 2 Bail No. 437/16 (order below Exhibit 1) 4] The learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant­accused is falsely implicated. He submitted that informant and accused are neighbourer and there are petty dispute between them. All the allegations are false. The investigation is almost completed. He further submitted that accused is only earning member of his family and permanent resident of the address given in the application and is ready to abide by any conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing him on bail. 5] Per contra, the learned A.P.P. opposed the application on the ground that accused is involved in a serious offence, in respect of a minor girl. She submitted that victim­girl timely raised alarm, otherwise, accused might have kidnapped the victim­girl. The investigation is in progress. The accused and victim­girl are staying in same vicinity and therefore, there are chances of tampering of the witnesses and prayed for rejection of application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R. it appears that the allegations are about outraging modesty of victim girl aged 12 years. As victim­girl timely raised alarm therefore, she was rescued by the informant; otherwise further untoward might have occurred. However, nothing has been seized at the instance of accused. The accused is behind bars since 25 days. The material part of investigation appears to have been completed. No doubt the offence is serious, however, no purpose would be served by further incarceration of applicant­accused. The object of bail is neither preventive nor punitive but to secure the presence of accused at the 3 Bail No. 437/16 (order below Exhibit 1) time of trial. The accused is ready to abide by any conditions imposed by the Court and in such circumstances, the apprehension of Spl.P.P. can be addressed by imposing suitable conditions. Hence, I pass the following order ­ ORDER 1) The application is allowed. 2) Applicant Vinod Gopal Chauhan be released on bail on his executing P.R. Bond of ₹15,000/­ [Rupees fifteen thousand only] with one local solvent surety in the like amount on the following conditions ­ A] Accused shall attend the concerned police station on every Sunday in between 10.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon till filing of the charge­sheet. 1. Anticipatory Bail Appln. 438/2016 Order below Exhibit 1. Anticipatory Bail Appln No.438/2016. 1] Mr. Jaysingrao D. Patil 2] Mohammad Yusuf Gulamhussain Patni ... Applicants versus State of Maharashtra (Through A.P.M.C. Police station) ... Non­applicant. ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1. 1] This is an application moved by applicant under section 438 of Cr.P.C., being apprehending their arrest in M.Case No. 224/2015 registered by A.P.M.C. Police Station for the offence punishable under section 195(A), 354(A), 503, 504, 506, 509, 510 r/w.34 of I.P. Code and section 7 and 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. 2] Heard learned advocate Mr. Gourish Kadam for the applicants/accused and Spl.P.P. Mrs. R.A.Navale for State. I.O. present. 3] The F.I.R. was registered by the order of learned Magistrate passed under section 156(3) of Cr. P.C. in O.M.A. No.1484/2015. The allegations in the complaint are that accused committed sexual harassment and threatened her and insulted the modesty of the complainant­victim. .. 2 .. Anticipatory Bail Appln. 438/2016 Order below Exhibit 1. 4] The learned Advocate for the applicants submitted that on the private complaint lodged by the complainant, the order under section 156(3) of Cr. P.C. was passed and the F.I.R. was registered against the present accused for the above mentioned offence. He submitted that in fact, the complainant has encroached on the stair­case of Natraj housing society and there was continuous complaints filed by the persons of said housing society against the complainant and her family members. He further submitted that though complainant tried to project her as a minor, she is in fact a major girl. He further submitted that the false complaint is lodged by the complainant to counter­blast the complaint preferred by applicant No.2 on behalf of Vashi Natraj Chamber premises which is registered as R.C.No.35/2016. He, thus, prayed that there is nothing to recovered from the accused. He further submitted that the accused had complied with the conditions imposed by the Court and ready to co­operate in investigation and prayed for confirmation of order of interim protection passed in favour of applicant. 5] Per contra, learned A.P.P. opposed the application only on the ground that for investigation of the crime, custody of accused is necessary and prayed for rejection of application. 3. Anticipatory Bail Appln. 438/2016 Order below Exhibit 1. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of application and documents annexed with it and say filed by the I.O., it appears that the private complaint was filed by the complainant and by the order of learned Magistrate, passed under section 156(3)of Cr. P.C. the offence was registered against the accused. Though, there are serious allegations about molestation in the complaint, however, nothing is stated to be recovered from the accused or at their instance. Further the report filed by the I.O. disclosed that complainant / victim­girl refused for her medical examination for verification of age. The learned counsel for applicants invited my attention to the F.I.R. No.127/2014 registered with A.P.M.C. police station for offence punishable under sec. 376 and 313 of I.P.C. which was registered at the instance of present complainant against one Ravi Patil. From the said F.I.R. it appears that it was registered on 02/08/2014. Thus, it appears that the complainant / victim­girl stated her age as 18 years in the year 2014. Further in O.M.A.No.1484/15 filed by complainant in the Court of J.M.F.C. CBD Belapur, Navi Mumbai. In the complaint and verification, the complainant stated her age as 16 years but refused to have test for age determination. Therefore, at this stage, it is disputed whether the victim­girl is a minor girl and the provisions of POCSO Act would be applicable to her. .. 4 .. Anticipatory Bail Appln. 438/2016 Order below Exhibit 1. 7] However, the perusal of various documents filed with application disclosed that various complaints were made by the applicants against the complainant, since the year­2014 and even there is one complaint dated 19/10/2015 against the complainant of giving false address for obtaining ration card and the said ration card is stated to be cancelled as per letter dated 04/02/2016 issued by Rationing Officer. Thus, the possibility that to pressurize the accused the complaint might have been lodged, cannot be ruled out. Therefore, considering the peculiar facts of the case, the custodial interrogation does not appear necessary. The conditional order directing accused to cooperate in investigation would facilitate the investigation. The accused had complied with the conditions imposed upon them while granting interim protection, hence, they are entitled for the confirmation of the same. Hence I pass following order ­ ORDER 1] Application is allowed. 2] The interim order dated 15/02/2016 passed in favour of applicants is hereby confirmed on the same terms and conditions. Date : 02/03/2016. (Ms. U.M. Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act), Thane.

(20 ) Special Case (POCSO) No. 44/2016 CNR No.MHTH01­001114­2016 ..................... The State of Maharashtra, Through P.S.O., Kasarvadavali Police Station, G.B.Road, Dist. Thane. ... ... ... PROSECUTION. VERSUS Navnit Ramavtar Yadav, Age 19 years, Occ. Student, R/o A/404, Sunrise Enclave, Near Suraj water Park, Waghbil, G.B.Road, Thane. ... ... ... ACCUSED. Offence punishable under sections 354­D(1)(i) and 506 of the Indian Penal Code and under Section 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ Mr. S.D.Londhe, A.P.P. for the prosecution. Mr. Atul Saroj, Advocate for the accused. 2 JUDGMENT ( Delivered on 30th day of June, 2018 ) 1) Accused Navnit Ramavatar Yadav is charge sheeted by Police Station Kasarvadavali, Thane on 15/02/2016 for having committed an offence punishable under sections 354­D(1)(i), 506 of the Indian Penal Code and under Section 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (POCSO Act) on the report of informant Victim (P.W.1) aged about 19 years, resident of Thane. 2) Prosecution case, briefly stated, is that informant Victim (PW1) was residing with her uncle Praveshkumar (PW3). Victim (PW1) is aged about 16 years having 29/08/1998 birth date. Victim (PW1) used to take her niece Anshita, studying in 2nd standard, to her school and used to bring back. Accused Navnit was acquainted through her friend Shreya. 3) Whenever Victim (PW1) used to take Anshita to school and bring back, accused Navnit was following her saying that he loved her, once invited her to his house in absence of her parents for enjoyment and more particularly saying "Shadi tak to aise hi rahegi kya?" and on refusal, was threatening to defame. 4) On 23/12/2015 Navnit gave message through Adesh and thereby invited Victim to participate drink party on the eve of new year but Victim opposed. On narrating this incident, Praveshkumar went to give understanding to the accused at his house. But there 3 Spl. Case (POCSO) No. 44/2016 Judg.Exh. CNR No.MHTH01­001114­2016 he was beaten. Not only that on the next day accused Navnit threatened Victim as to why uncle went to his house and that he will not leave her uncle. As such, Victim lodged the compliant vide Exh.8 and thereupon offence vide C.R.No. 324/2015 under Section 354(D) and 506 of I.P.C. was registered. 5) Upon report investigation was geared up. Investigating Officer API Pramod Devram Patil (PW5) carried out investigation. Statements of Victim's mother Chanchalrani (PW2), Victim's uncle Praveshkumar (PW3) and her father Rajesh (PW4) were recorded. Accused was arrested. After investigation charge­sheet was filed. 6) From the material on record, my Ld. Predecessor Mr. Ashutosh Karmarkar, Dist. Judge­1 & Addl. Sessions Judge has framed charge at Exh.4 on 16/12/2016 for the offence punishable under Sec. 354­D(1)(i) and 506 of I.P.C. and Sec. 12 of POCSO Act, 2012. The contents of charge were read over and explained to the accused Navnit in vernacular to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 7) Oral evidence of prosecution consists of informant Victim (PW1) at Exh.7, her mother Chanchalrani Rajesh Batnotra (PW2) at Exh.11, Praveshkumar Manharlal Batnotra (PW3) at Exh.13, Rajesh Manharlal Batnotra (PW4) at Exh.16 and Investigating Officer API Pramod Devram Patil (PW5) at Exh.18. Documentary evidence of prosecution consists of report at Exh.8. Prosecution closed evidence by pursis at Exh.19. 4 8) The evidence of informant Victim (PW1) clearly indicates that her birth date is 29/08/1998 and that she was residing with her uncle Praveshkumar (PW3) and used to take Anshita to her school and used to bring her back and while doing so accused Navnit was following her, teasing her, inviting her for enjoyment and on narrating the same, beaten her uncle Praveshkumar with threat that he will not leave him. Accordingly, Victim (PW1) gave complaint at Exh.8. 9) Chahchalrani (PW2), Victim's mother, has corroborated the evidence of informant Victim stating that Victim was studying in 9th class and that Praveshkumar (PW3) narrated her that when he went to give understanding the accused Navnit threatened him. Chanchalrani's evidence also revealed that her daughter informant Victim (PW1) gave report and her statement was recorded. 10) Informant Victim's uncle Praveshkumar (PW3) substantiate the evidence of Victim on the point that accused Navnit was eteasing her since 3/4 months prior to lodging the complaint and she did not tell this fact because of fear and threat and that accused Navnit also insisting her to join drink on the eve of new year party. Evidence of Praveshkumar (PW3) also reveals that when he went to give understanding to the house of accused Navnit, he was manhandled and Navnit threatened him to kill and next day complaint was lodged. 11) Victim's father Rajesh (PW4) has proved birth certificate 5 Spl. Case (POCSO) No. 44/2016 Judg.Exh. CNR No.MHTH01­001114­2016 at Exh.17 issued by T.M.C. and that discloses birth date 29/08/1998. 12) Investigating Officer API Pramod Patil (PW5) carried out investigation by recording statements of witnesses, collecting birth certificate of Victim and submitting charge­sheet. 13) As against this, accused did not adduce the defence evidence, but nevertheless contended in the statement under Sec. 313 Cr.P.C. that Victim's uncle came to his house and threw live cigarette on her mother and when his father told that complaint will be lodged against him, the false case is filed. 14) I have heard Mr. S.D.Londhe, Ld. A.P.P. for the prosecution and Mr. Atul Saroj, Ld. Advocate for the accused. Appraised the entire material on record. 15) Mr. Londhe submitted for conviction primarily on the ground that prosecution has proved the guilt of accused beyond all reasonable doubt. Mr. Londhe submitted that the sole testimony of victim is undisturbed and unshattered and therefore, it can be relied upon. Mr. Londhe submitted that the testimony of Victim clearly revealed that there was constant following and threat given to the Victim and thereby offence under Sec. 354­D(1)(i) of I.P.C. and Sec. 12 of POCSO Act are attracted. Mr. Londhe submitted that birth date proved at Exh.17 indicate that Victim is less than 18 years. Mr. Londhe submitted that nothing is surfaced in the cross­ examination as to why informant Victim with the help of her 6 parents would file false complaint against the accused and the defence contended is highly improbable. 16) Mr. Londhe submitted that Victim's evidence is duly corroborated and supported by the best possible evidence. Mr. Londhe submitted that parents and close relatives would not file false case in the ordinary course of social life and that too in respect of character assassination of Victim unless it is a fact. Mr. Londhe submitted that prosecution has clearly made out the offence alleged and charged and urged for conviction. 17) Mr. Saroj taking through the evidence resisted the prosecution case primarily on the ground that it is doubtful and benefit of doubt should be given to the accused for bulk of reasons. Mr. Saroj submitted that there are material inconsistencies and contradictions and same goes to the root of the matter. Mr. Saroj submitted that few witnesses namely Anshita, Aadesh and Shreya are not examined besides the neighbourer and their non­ examination is fatal. Mr. Saroj submitted that there is CCTV cameras installed but the CCTV footage is not collected and the non­collection is fatal to the prosecution case. Mr. Saroj submitted that testimony of Victim is improved and the improvement amounts to exaggeration and thereby sought acquittal. 18) Having regard to the submissions advanced at bar and after appraisal of entire material on record, I find merit in the submission of Mr. Londhe and demerit in the submission of Mr. Saroj for more than one reasons stated and discussed hereinbelow. 7 Spl. Case (POCSO) No. 44/2016 Judg.Exh. CNR No.MHTH01­001114­2016 Accordingly, following points arise for my consideration and determination and I record my findings against each of points as under. ­ POINTS FINDINGS 1) Does the prosecution prove that the ... In the accused Navnit was following the Victim affirmative. (PW1) aged below 18 years, between September 2015 and 24/12/2015 and thereby trying to contact her to foster personal interaction though she was disinterested ? 2) Does the prosecution prove that the ... In the accused Navnit has committed criminal affirmative. intimidation by threatening the Victim (PW1), aged below 18 years, with injury to her reputation ? 3) Does the prosecution prove that accused ... In the Navnit has sexually harassed the Victim affirmative. (PW1), aged below 18 years, during the above period ? 4) What order ? ... Accused is convicted. REASONS 19) Points No. 1 to 3 :­ These points are interlinked and therefore, taken up together for reasoning and findings. 20) Few facts either proved from the evidence on record and/or established may be stated at the outset. Chanchalrani (PW2) and Rajesh (PW4) are husband and wife and Victim (PW1) is their 8 daughter. Praveshkumar (PW3) is uncle of Victim (PW1). Victim's birth date is 29/08/1998 and her birth certificate is at Exh.17. 21) The evidence of informant Victim (PW1) is self­sufficient and omnipotent. The evidence is crystal clear. The evidence is vividly seeable. Victim (PW1) has deposed unequivocally that accused Navnit was repeatedly following her to foster the personal interaction despite here resistance. 22) Victim's evidence is duly substantiated and corroborated by her complaint at Exh.8 lodged at earliest point of time on very next day of incident on 24/12/2015. Filing complaint at earliest point of time has ruled out possibility of fabrication and implication. There isn't delay. 23) Victim's evidence is unshattered and undisturbed in the cross­examination. Nothing is surfaced in the cross­examination to discard or dislodge her evidence. Victim is primarily cross­ examined on the line that because her uncle Praveshkumar had abused his mother and threw live cigarette on her and the dispute took place and that Victim's father expressed that he will file complaint against him, the present false complaint is filed. But again the line of cross­examination is without basement. Alleged dispute is improbable. Nothing is surfaced as to why Victim's uncle Praveshkumar would go to accused Navnit's house and quarrel with his mother. 24) In fact, going of Praveshkumar (PW3) to the house of accused Navnit clearly goes to show that because of incident 9 Spl. Case (POCSO) No. 44/2016 Judg.Exh. CNR No.MHTH01­001114­2016 narrated by Victim (PW1), he had to go to the house of accused to give understanding. The suggestion by the accused Navnit in the cross­examination to the uncle Praveshkumar (PW3) goes to substantiate the version of Victim that because Navnit was repeatedly and constantly following her to foster personal interaction, he had to visit accused Navnit's home. 25) Besides, the evidence of Victim (PW1) is unquestioned on the point of her birth date 29/08/1998. There isn't cross­ examination. As such, it is clearly established that Victim was less than 18 years at the relevant time. In totality I find the sole testimony of Victim (PW1) inspires the confidence being natural and dependable. 26) Normally Victim of sexual assault and harassment would not come out with totally false case unless she is suffered and life becomes miserable to her. Mere animosity for here and there cannot be cause to lodge such complaint by putting forward the female child of the family because that would assassinate not only her character but it shall disrepute their family in society. 27) Chanchalrani (PW2) substantiate the evidence of Victim (PW1) on the point of her relation as mother and acquainted with the factual narration by the Victim that she was harassed and repeatedly followed by accused Navnit and lodging of complaint. Her evidence also revealed as to how her brother­in­law Praveshkumar (PW3) went to the house of accused Navnit to give understanding. The testimony of Chanchalrani (PW2) is again not 10 shattered in the cross­examination. 28) The narration of Victim (PW1) is further substantiated and corroborated by her uncle Praveshkumar (PW3). The conduct of Praveshkumar is found to be normal and natural that on knowing accused Navnit harassed Victim (PW1), he went to the house of accused Navnit to give him understanding, but in return he was manhandled. Even his evidence revealed that accused Navnit has threatened him to kill. Nothing is surfaced in the cross­examination of Praveshkumar (PW3) as to why he should depose false and that too against accused Navnit. Nothing is surfaced in the cross­ examination as to the cause for Praveshkumar other than in question to visit the house of accused Navnit. The cross­ examination to Praveshkumar (PW3) is baseless and without any direction. 29) Rajesh (PW4) is father of Victim (PW1). He has proved birth certificate vide Exh.17. His evidence is unchallenged in the cross­examination. The same therefore, can be accepted. 30) The Investigating Officer API Pramod (PW5) has carried out entire investigation. He has collected Victim's birth certificate at Exh.17. He has done his job. In the cross­examination, API Pramod (PW5) admits that he has not recorded the statement of neighbourers. In fact, the question of recording the statement of neighbourers does not arise. The incident was 3/4 months prior to lodging of report in the nature that accused was following repeatedly and constantly to foster his personal interaction with 11 Spl. Case (POCSO) No. 44/2016 Judg.Exh. CNR No.MHTH01­001114­2016 Victim (PW1). So there could not be witnesses in that regard. Nothing is surfaced as to why API Pramod (PW5) would file false charge­sheet. 31) Accused contended that the statement of Anshita, aged about 7 years, who was taken to school by Victim (PW1), was not recorded. But again the non­recording of Anshita's statement is not fatal and does not in any way dislodge the Victim's evidence. Anshita, aged about 7 years, would not be able to know the intention of accused Navnit in following Victim repeatedly for fostering personal interaction. Likewise non­examination of Adesh does not discredit the prosecution case and the evidence of witnesses. The flaws and defect in the investigation would not give any benefit to the accused. Merely because the statements of some of the witnesses are not recorded is not sufficient to discard the prosecution case when it is otherwise found to be creditworthy. 32) Accused contended that there are inconsistencies and variance in the evidence of Victim (PW1) and the complaint at Exh.8 but that itself would not go to the root of the matter. In fact, minor inconsistencies and variance would lend the credibility to the prosecution case. Accused contended that CCTV footage and neighbouring witnesses are not examined but again what is not done and investigated would be unending. What is to be appreciated is what is surfaced on record and what is not brought on record must be shown to be malafide with ulterior motive and directly prejudice the accused Navnit. This did not happen in the present case in hand. Nor such prejudice to accused Navnit was 12 projected from the evidence on the record. 33) There is justifiable evidence to draw the presumption in respect of culpable mental state of accused Navnit under Sec. 30 of POCSO Act. The connectivity between the accused and the Victim is clearly established being the resident in the same vicinity. Not only that, accused Navnit has admitted Praveshkumar's visit to his house though suggestion in the cross­examination to Victim (PW1). The rebuttal therefore, in respect of presumption is not at all done. 34) Now what offence is made out. From the evidence surfaced on record, prosecution has clearly made out the case that the Victim was aged below 18 years at the relevant time, accused Navnit was following her repeatedly and constantly to foster the personal interaction despite her non­interest, threatened Victim to disrepute her and repeatedly followed her and the following was to insist her for consumption of liquor, teasing that she would remain virgin till marriage and thereby proved the offences punishable under Sections 354­D(1)(i), 506 of I.P.C. and under Sec. 12 of POCSO Act. In the result, accused is convicted for the said offences and has to be sentenced. Accordingly, I answer the points in the affirmative. Now I proceed to hear the accused on the point of sentence. Thane. ( R. V. Jatale ) Date :30/06/2018. Special Judge (POSCO),Thane. 35) I have heard accused Navnit, Mr. Atul Saroj and Mr. 13 Spl. Case (POCSO) No. 44/2016 Judg.Exh. CNR No.MHTH01­001114­2016 Londhe on the point of sentence. 36 ) Accused Navnit submitted for leniency on the ground that he is a student, he has not committed offence, he is falsely implicated and he be released on probation. 37) Mr. Saroj submitted for leniency on the ground that he be released on probation being young age. 38) Mr. Londhe submitted for maximum sentence otherwise wrong message will go in the society. 39) Having regard to the submissions advanced at bar and after appraisal of entire material on record, the offence committed by accused Navnit in question is undoubtedly serious, grievous and terrorizing not only to the informant Victim but to her family member. The informant Victim and her family members are put in to disreputation. Habitation of accused Navnit in the same vicinity would be more pressurizing and disgusting. The gravity of offence against the women is perceivable from the social milieu that in case of such offences the Victim is cursed and it is considered blot on her character and family and that ruin prospects and career of Victim and defame the family in the relation and in the vicinity. Accused Navnit cannot be given benefit under the Probation of Offender Act for the obvious reason that the offence is against womanhood and it is moral turpitude. Under these circumstances, I do not find that accused should be shown special leniency while sentencing. The sentence must be commensurate with the gravity of the offence. 14 40] The offence under Sec. 354­D(1)(i) of I.P.C. is punishable with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine. The offence under Sec. 506 of I.P.C. is punishable with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extent to two years or with fine or with both. The offence under Sec. 12 of POCSO Act shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine. From this, the intention of the legislature is crystal clear to protect children from the offences of sexual assault, sexual harassment and sexual exploitation and therefore, dealt with sternly while prescribing the sentence. There isn't circumstance either surfaced on the record through the cross­examination or otherwise to show special leniency to accused Navnit. 41) In view of the observation regarding the gravity of the offence and suffering of the informant Victim along with family, accused Navnit will have to be dealt with substantive sentence so that it will be lesson to him and terror to the prospective offenders and therefore, accused Navnit is sentenced cumulatively to simple imprisonment of two (2) years and fine of Rs. 5,000/­ i/d. simple imprisonment for six month for the offence punishable under Sec. 354­D(1)(i) and 506 of the I.P.C. and Sec. 12 of POCSO Act. What leniency can be shown is only that accused can be given set off for the detention period he has undergone. 42) Now coming to Sec. 357­A of Cr.P.C., under Sec. 33(8) of POCSO Act and Rule 7 of POCSO Rule. As observed above, it is a 15 Spl. Case (POCSO) No. 44/2016 Judg.Exh. CNR No.MHTH01­001114­2016 blot and scar on the soul and mind of Victim. The entire family is under stress and social tension. Frustration is bound to be in the life of Victim. By no stretch of imagination, it can be compensated in terms of money. It is constitutional mandate of the State that it shall protect life, liberty and property of every person within the territory of India. Not only that, it should be protected but in case of violation, people should be compensated justly, fairly and reasonably. In this backdrop, I deem it fit that this matter should be referred for just, fair and reasonable compensation to the District Legal Services Authority, Thane and the District Magistrate, Thane for necessary action. 43) Perusal of record clearly reveal that there isn't muddemal therefore, there cannot be order to that effect. 44) In view of reasons and findings stated supra, the prosecution has proved the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubt for the offences charged above and therefore, he stands convicted and sentenced. Accordingly, I proceed to pass following order. ORDER 1) Accused Navnit Ramavtar Yadav is convicted under Section 235 (2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for the offence punishable under section Sec. 354­D(1)(i) and 506 of I.P.C. and under Sec. 12 of POCSO Act and thereby sentenced cumulatively to simple imprisonment for two (2) years and fine of Rs. 5,000/­ i/d. simple imprisonment for six month. 16 2) Accused Navnit shall surrender his bail bond. Accused Navnit was under detention from 24/12/2015 to 11/01/2016 and therefore, he is entitled for set off of the said period under Sec. 428 of Cr.P.C. 3) A sum of Rs. 4,000/­(Rupees Four Thousand only) be paid to the informant Victim (PW1) towards compensation out of fine amount recovered. 4) Since there isn't muddemal there isn't order to that effect. 5) Copy of Judgment and Order shall be supplied free of cost to the informant Victim (PW1) and accused Navnit. 6) Copy of Judgment and Order be forwarded with complements to the District Legal Services Authority, Thane and the District Magistrate, Thane for disbursing just, reasonable and fair compensation to the informant Victim (PW1). 7) P. & D. in the court. Thane. ( R. V. Jatale ) Date:30/06/2018 Special Judge (POCSO), Thane. 17 Spl. Case (POCSO) No. 44/2016 Judg.Exh. CNR No.MHTH01­001114­2016

Kiran Kashinath Channe Age : 24 Years R/at.: Mahapoli, Tal. Bhiwandi, Dist.Thane ...Accused Offence punishable u/sec. 354 of Indian Penal Code and Sec. 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and S.3 r/w. 181, 146 r/w. 196 of Motor Vehicle Act. Shri. More, Ld. APP for the State Shri. Shirke­Patil, Ld.Advocate for the accused. 2 Spl. Case(POCSO) No. 41/2014.. Judgment CNR No. No record present. JUDGMENT ( Delivered on this 14th day of December, 2018 ) 1. The accused is charged for the offences punishable under sections 354 of Indian Penal Code, Sec. 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and S. 3 r/w. 181 and S.146 r/w. 196 of Motor Vehicle Act. Brief facts of the prosecution case are as under :­ 2. The complainant lodged report at police station that on 12.12.2013, at about 11.30 a.m., accused had taken his daughter by his motorcycle forcibly. Accused has taken his daughter towards Konkan Saw Mill. They got down near Konkan Saw Mill and accused had taken her towards empty tin shed. Accused had moved his hand on her chest. Three persons came there and told the accused that they will lodge report at police station and brought them at Toll Naka and informed to the father of victim. Hence, her father had lodged report at police station. Police had registered offence punishable u/sec. 354 of Indian Penal Code and Sec. 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and S. 3 r/w. 181 and S.146 r/w. 196 of Motor Vehicle Act. After due investigation charge­sheet came to be filed in the court of Sessions. 3. My Ld. Predecessor had framed charge (Exh.2) against the accused for the offences punishable under sections 3 354 of Indian Penal Code and Sec. 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and S. 3 r/w. 181 and S.146 r/w. 196 of Motor 3 Spl. Case(POCSO) No. 41/2014.. Judgment CNR No. No record present. Vehicle Act. Contents of charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular language, to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 4. There is no incriminating evidence against the accused. Hence, statement of accused under section 313 (1)(b) of the Criminal Procedure Code is dispensed with. 5. I have heard APP Shri. More for the State and Ld. Advocate Shri. Shirke­Patil for the accused. 6. On perusal of record and evidence on record, following points arise from my determination and consideration and I have recorded my findings thereon for the reasons as stated below:­ POINTS FINDINGS 1. Does the prosecution prove that the In the negative. accused on 12.12.2013 at about 11.45 hrs., at Mauje Borivali, Tal. Bhiwandi Dist. Thane within jurisdiction of Padgha police station, used criminal force to victim, a minor­age 13 years intending to outrage her modesty and thereby committed an offence punishable under Sec. 354 of IPC? 2. Does the prosecution prove that the In the negative. accused on above mentioned date, time and place committed sexual assault on victim, a minor age ­13 years and thereby committed an offence 4 Spl. Case(POCSO) No. 41/2014.. Judgment CNR No. No record present. punishable under Sec. 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act? 3. Does the prosecution prove that the In the negative. accused on above mentioned date, time and place did not have any permit or licence and any document to drive motorcycle No. MH­04/FX­807 and thereby committed an offence punishable u/sec. 3 r/w. 181 of Motor Vehicle Act? 4. Does the prosecution prove that the In the negative. accused on above mentioned date, time and place drive the motorcycle No. MH­ 04/FX­807 in a public place without having insurance policy against third party risk and thereby committed an offence punishable u/sec. 146 r/w. 196 of Motor Vehicle Act? 5. What Order ? As per final order. REASONS AS TO POINT NOS. 1 TO 4 :­ 7. That, in order to establish the guilt of accused, prosecution has examined in all three witnesses. P.W.1 Maruti Tukaram Ingale, Complainant­ father of victim girl is examined at Exh.6. P.W.2 Victim is examined at Exh. 12. 5 Spl. Case(POCSO) No. 41/2014.. Judgment CNR No. No record present. P.W.3 Laxman Narayan Bhandarge – panch on spot panchanama is examined at Exh.14. Thereafter, prosecution failed to secure the presence of any witnesses in spite of sufficient opportunity. Therefore, evidence of prosecution side is closed. 8. In support of the contention, prosecution has relied on complaint Exh.7, spot panchanama Exh.15. 9. P.W.1 complainant deposed in his evidence that on 12.12.2013, he was on duty since 7.00 a.m. to 3.00 p.m. Some boys made phone call to him and called him near Dolare Petrol Pump. He further stated that his daughter and accused were at toll naka. He made enquiry with his daughter. She told him that accused had taken her on bike near Konkan Saw Mill and other people brought them on toll naka. Then, they went to police station and lodged report at police station. P.W.1 was cross­examined by Ld. Advocate for accused. In the cross­examination, he has not supported to the prosecution story and denied contents of statement recorded by police. He specifically admitted that it did not happen that on 12.12.2013, accused restrained his daughter and taken her on bike to Konkan Saw Mill. He also denied that the other people brought them at toll naka. The evidence of P.W.1 is not helpful to the prosecution version. So also, P.W.1 is hearsay witness. 6 Spl. Case(POCSO) No. 41/2014.. Judgment CNR No. No record present. 10. P.W.2 who is victim has not supported to the prosecution version. Therefore, she was cross­examined by Ld.A.P.P. However, A.P.P. failed to bring any incriminating evidence against the accused. Therefore, her evidence is not helpful to the prosecution. 11. P.W.3 who is panch witness deposed that police had prepared panchanama on 12.12.2013 at police station and prepared panchanama on the spot of incident. In the cross­ examination he admitted that when he was proceeding by the road, he was called by police at police station and his signature was obtained. He further admitted that map of the spot was already drawn and he put only his signature. Evidence of P.W.3 is also not supporting to the prosecution version. Therefore, there is nothing on record for discussion. The prosecution has also failed to bring on record any evidence regarding the Sec. 3/181 and S. 146 r/w. 196 of M.V.Act. Hence, I come to the conclusion that the prosecution has failed to prove the ingredients of Sec. 354 of IPC and S.8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act and S. 3 r/w. 181 and S. 146 r/w. 196 of Motor Vehicle act. Thus, the prosecution has totally failed to prove its case. Hence, I answer point Nos.1 to 4 in the negative. AS TO POINT NO. 5 :­ 12. In view of the above said discussion, I come to the conclusion that accused is entitled for the order of acquittal and proceed to pass following order : 7 Spl. Case(POCSO) No. 41/2014.. Judgment CNR No. No record present. ORDER 1. Accused Kiran Kashinath Channe is hereby acquitted under section 235 (1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, for the offences punishable under sections 354 of Indian Penal Code, S. 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and S.3 r/w. 181, 146 r/w. 196 of Motor Vehicle Act. 2. His bail bond stands cancelled. 3. Muddemal property i.e. Motorcycle of Fister Company bearing No. MH­04/FX 807, if not returned, it be returned to the claimant on proper identification after appeal period is over. 4. Accused – Kiran Kashinath Channe is hereby directed to comply section 437­A of Cr.P.C. and to furnish fresh P.R. Bond of Rs.15,000/­ (Rupees Fifteen Thousand Only) with surety of like amount and same shall remain in force for the period of six months from the date of this order. No. 430 of 2015 This application is filed by applicants namely Zakariya Hanif Shaikh, Faizan Hanif Shaikh, Rehan Zakariya Shaikh, Irfan Abdul Latif Ansari for their release on bail under section 438 of Cr.P.C. in connection with C.R.No.I-48/2015 registered at Shantinagar Police Station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 354, 354D, 342, 504, 506 read with section 34 of I.P.C. and section 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as P.O.C.S.O. Act). It was contended and argued that the applicants have been falsely involved in this crime with the allegation that the accused persons obstructed the victim girl and the committed sexual assault and harassment upon her and also provoked and threatened her. It is further contended and argued that the applicant no.1 and 2 are a builder by profession, applicant no.3 is son of applicant no.1 and applicant no.4 is also businessman and that the complainant i.e. mother of the girl, had purchased flat from applicant no.1 and there is dispute pending between him and complainant and on account of such rivalry this false complaint is lodged. It is also further submitted that it is a civil dispute and looking to the nature of allegations, the custodial interrogation of the applicants is not required. It is further submitted that they are permanent residents of the address given and that if the present applicants/accused is released on bail, they will co-operate with the investigation and therefore the applicants are entitled to be released on anticipatory bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply as per Exhibit 20 and it was contended and argued that at the time of incident the applicants in furtherance of their common intention followed her and obstructed the victim girl aged 15 years .. 2 .. Anticipatory Bail No.430/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) when she was going to school by giving dash of motorcycle and then also pulled her odhani with intent to outrage her modesty and also provoked her and threatened to make her naked and abused her in obscene language and it is further contended that in such manner the applicants committed sexual assault and harassment upon the victim girl. It is further submitted that if the applicants are released on anticipatory bail, there is possibility of the applicants threatening the complainant and prosecution witnesses which may hamper the investigation and even the applicants may abscond and may not be available for trial and may tamper with prosecution evidence. It was therefore contended that the applicants are not entitled to be released on anticipatory bail. 3] It is also to be mentioned that the original complainant also appeared and filed application for permission to appear through advocate to assist the prosecution and same was allowed. The original complainant also produced various documents on record. 4] As is clear, though offences charged against the applicants/accused are of serious nature under section 354, 354D, 342, 504, 506 read with section 34 of I.P.C. and section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act with the allegation that the accused persons in furtherance of common intention obstructed the victim girl road and pulled her odhani and also threated to make her naked, the fact which is also clear that the applicant no.1 is the father of applicant no.3 and applicant no.2 and 4 are stated to be businessmen. It is also to be mentioned that it is also clear from the averments in the application and also from the documents produced on record alongwith application as well as documents produced by original complainant that the applicant no.1 is builder and developer of the building in which the complainant i.e. .. 3 .. Anticipatory Bail No.430/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) mother of the girl, have purchased a flat. It is also clear that there has been previous litigations, civil as well as criminal, pending between applicant no.1 as a builder and mother of the girl and it is further clear from the documents on record that both applicant no.1 as well as complainant had filed complaints against each other and even offence of extortion stated to have been registered against the complainant in regard to some flat which is purchased by the complainant i.e. mother of the girl from applicant no.1 and in the light of that the contentions on behalf of applicants that because of previous dispute between the parties they have been falsely involved in the crime with the allegation of sexual assault only with a view to take revenge and to see that the applicants are sent behind bar, has to be taken into consideration. In the light of that the contentions on behalf of applicant that they are apprehending arrest at the hands of police and therefore they are entitled to be released on anticipatory bail, is also required to be considered. 5] Then, in the light of above if the allegations in the complaint are perused, the complaint is in regard to some instance of outraging modesty of the girl and looking to the nature of allegation and the manner in which it is stated to have been committed, I am of the view that custodial interrogation of the applicants do not appear to be necessary. Even it is contended that the applicant no.1 is a builder and applicant no.3, who is son of applicant no.1, is stated to be staying at Nashik and the applicant no.2 and 4 are businessmen and having permanent address. 6] In any case it is well settled that at this stage of deciding anticipatory bail application the evidence on record need not be gone into detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether release of .. 4 .. Anticipatory Bail No.430/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) the applicants would hamper the process of investigation or whether the applicants would abscond if released on bail and in case of anticipatory bail it is also required to be seen as to whether the custodial interrogation of the applicants is necessary. In that regard in view of above discussion custodial interrogation of the applicants do not appear to be necessary. 7] Even the apprehension expressed by the prosecution that the applicants may not be available for investigation or release of applicants on anticipatory bail would hamper the investigation etc., can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions including condition to give attendance to police station and for that purpose there appear no necessity of the custody of the applicants. 8] In that regard it is contended by the applicants that they are permanent residents of the address given and will not abscond and they are ready to abide by any conditions imposed 9] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the interim anticipatory bail already granted to the applicant can be confirmed. I therefore pass the following order - ORDER The application is allowed. 2) The interim anticipatory bail granted to the applicants namely Zakariya Hanif Shaikh, Faizan Hanif Shaikh, Rehan Zakariya Shaikh, Irfan Abdul Latif Ansari vide order dated 16.02.2015 passed below Exhibit 3 in confirmed. 3) In the event of arrest of the applicants for offence punishable under section 354, 354D, 342, 504, 506 read with section 34 of I.P.C. and section 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual .. 5 ..
