--1-- ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN RBA NO.464/2017 The applicant Pramod Pathade aged 21 years has applied for bail in Cr. No.I­357/2016 registered under section 363, 376 read with section 4 of POSCO Act. It is submitted that in the said crime the accused was arrested on 26.09.2016. The accused was remanded to police custody and then remanded to judicial custody from time to time. The investigation was over and chargesheet is filed before this court. It is further contended that there was love affair between victim and the accused for last many years and they would frequently talk with each other. They had established good relation and started liking each other. The accused has decided to marry with the victim. The victim has sexual intercourse with the accused with her own consent. The victim's mother was against the love affair of victim and accused, therefore, the victim voluntarily left the home and went with the accused at his native place at Hingoli and resided there for one month. The victim has completed the age of 18 years and they are going to marry in April 2017. 2. It is contended that the accused has only earning member of his family and his economic condition is poor. His father is unemployed due to disease. The accused has promise to marry the victim and after completion of 18 years of the victim he is going to marry with her. The accused is ready to face the trial and abide by the condition of bail so he prayed that he may be released on bail. --2-- 3. Perused the report filed by I.O. at Exh.5. it is contended that FIR was immediately lodged. The accused was immediately arrested. The statement of the victim is recorded under section 164 of Cr. P.C. There is strong evidence against the accused, so if he is released on bail he is likely to tamper the victim and witnesses, therefore, the I.O opposed for the bail. 4. Heard Ld. A.P.P. He strongly opposed for bail. 5. Heard Ld. Counsel on behalf of the accused. He submitted that there was love affair between victim and accused and the sexual intercourse were established with the consent of the victim. After completion of 18 years the victim is going to marry with him and the accused has promise to marry her. The investigation is completed, therefore, there is no use to keep the accused in jail, it will amount to conviction without trial. 6. Perused copies of investigation papers and the report of I.O. As per the investigation papers the victim is 17 years old at the time of incident. It appears that she voluntarily left home and went with the accused at his native place at Hingoli and she resided there for one month . During that period the victim's mother had given missing complaint and upon information the victim and accused were found at Hingoli and they were brought to Koparkhairne police station and thereafter the victim's statement was recorded. --3-- 7. The court is of the view that investigation is completed and chargesheet is filed. The victim was matured to understand what is consequences of the act of sexual intercourse. The accused is also matured. He is 22 years old. Both were residing at one place and therefore, there was love affair between them. The victim has stated this fact in her statement. So considering all these aspect the court is of the view that there is no use to keep the accused in jail without trial. He is ready to face the trial and ready to abide by the conditions of the bail, therefore, I pass the following order. ORDER 1. Application is allowed. 2. Accused be released on P.B. and S.B. of Rs.20,000/­ (Rupees Twenty Thousand Only) with one or two local solvent sureties in like amount. 3. Accused shall not contact with any witnesses or the victim and shall not tamper with any witnesses. 4. Accused shall not leave jurisdiction of the Court without prior permission of the Court. 5. The accused shall attend the trial without fail, if any condition is breached the bail will be cancelled. ( S.C. Khalipe ) Date : 07/06/2017. Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

--1-- ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN ANTICIPATORY BAIL APPLICATION NO.384/2018 CNR NO.MHTH01­001153­2018 The applicant Mrs. A.P.Sheila Karunan aged 57 years has applied for bail under section 438 of Cr. P.C. in C.R.No.20/2018 registered in CBD police station for the offence under section 8, 12, 3, 4 of POCSO Act, 2012. 2. It is contended that the applicant is falsely implicated in the alleged offence. The applicant is working as a teacher in Navi Mumbai School and she is law binding person and she is residing with her aged mother of 75 years old. The applicant is widow, her father is expired due to cancer in 2008. After that her brother and brother's wife and children forcibly came to reside in their house in 2012 and since then quarrel started between them. The applicant's mother had filed N.C complaints, D.V cases against her brother and brother's wife and children. Therefore, in order to counter blast the litigations filed by the applicant and her mother, the applicant's brother's wife made her child to file false complaint under POCSO Act. 3. It is submitted that the custodial interrogation of the applicant is not required and therefore, she may be granted anticipatory bail. 4. The applicant has produced the copies of complaints, N.C complaints, copy of FIR etc. 5. Investigating Officer has given say at Exh.11. It appears from the report that the alleged incident took place from June 2012 to 2015 and FIR is lodged on 31.01.2018 at 1.30 p.m. It is alleged that when informant's son aged 18 years at present when he was in --2-- 8th standard to 9th standard during 2012­2015 the present applicant would use to sexually harass him and also forced him to have oral sex. Investigating Officer has further submitted that, if the applicant is released on bail she is likely to tamper the prosecution witnesses. 6. I heard Ld. APP and accused and on behalf of the original informant. 7. From the facts and circumstances of this case it appears that present applicant is residing with her old aged mother in her house for last 25 to 30 years. When her father died in 2008 after 3­4 years in 2012 applicant's brother and brother's wife and children came to reside forcibly in their house. The applicant was maintaining them and provided monetary help to them, but inspite of that her brother's wife would use to harass and quarrel the applicant and her mother. So in 2016 applicant's mother A. P. Padmini Karunan has filed M.A.No.26/2016 in JMFC Vashi CBD Belapur for relief of injunction restraining the brother's wife and others from disturbing the possession of the applicant and accordingly the relief was granted to the applicant's mother. In 2017 the applicant's mother A. P. Padmini Karunan have given application to SDO Thane for maintenance under the provisions of Senior Citizen Act, 2007. The copy of that application is produced on record. The applicant has also produced copies of complaints lodged by applicant's mother A. P. Padmini Karunan on 01.02.2014 to Police Commissioner, Navi Mumbai and the another complaint dtd.16.11.2015 given to Commissioner of Police CBD, Navi Mumbai and copy of N.C complaint dtd. 31.01.2016 given against the applicant's brother and his wife and children. It is also alleged by the applicant that one day the applicant's brother's son had --3-- strangulated the applicant's mother and beaten her mother. At that time her mother had lodged complaint in CBD police station on 13.05.2016 under section 338, 323, 504 read with 34 of IPC. The applicant has produced the medical certificate of her mother and photographs. 8. The original informant has filed application at Exh.7 for intervention of this application. 9. Considering the facts and circumstances there are litigations going on between both the parties since 2012. The alleged incident as per FIR took place from 2012 to 2015, but the FIR was lodged on 31.01.2018. Delay in lodging FIR is not at all explained. The informant had never lodged any complaint against the present applicant in respect of sexual harassment, inspite of the informant and her children were residing in one house along with the applicant and her mother. No previous complaints were lodged. 10. From the report of the I.O. I do not find any reason about the custodial interrogation of the present applicant. Nothing is required to be seized or sought any information from the applicant and therefore, her custodial interrogation is not required. Considering these mitigating circumstances and previous complaints lodged by the applicant and her mother against the informant and her children there are mitigating circumstances to grant anticipatory bail to the applicant. The order passed below Exh.3 is liable to be confirmed. Hence, I proceed to pass following order. :ORDER: 1. Application is allowed. 2. Ad interim order below Exh.3 is hereby confirmed. --4-- 3. The applicant is directed to attend the concerned police station as and when called for the purpose of investigation, till the investigation is over. Thane. ( S.C. Khalipe ) Date :29/03/2018. Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

.. 1 .. bail no.442/2015 (Order below exhibit 1) Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 442/2015 This application is filed by applicant Aavtar Singh Barbhajansingh, Jaswindersingh Kulwantsingh and Mangaljeet Singh Balwindersingh for their release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no.I­37/2014 registered at Shrinagar police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 354, 324, 34 of I.P.C. and section 8 and 10 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O.Act) and section 4, 25(1)b of Arms Act and also under section 37(1) 135 of Bombay Police Act. It was contended and argued that the applicant no.1 is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that he outraged modesty of the complainant minor girl and other accused persons protected him when people gathered there at the time of incident. It is further contended and argued that no such incident has happened and the applicants are falsely implicated in this crime. It is further submitted that the applicants are permanent residents of the address given and that if the present applicants/accused is released on bail, they will co­operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicants are entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that at the time of incident the complainant girl was passing by .. 2 .. bail no.442/2015 (Order below exhibit 1) road and when she came in front of Mahasubhadra Medical Stores applicant no.1 came from front and moved hand over her breast and outraged her modesty and when she questioned him and raised shouts, other accused persons came for his help and they attacked the crowd there at that time the applicants/accused were holding swords and due to the attack by the accused one boy namely Sahil Shirsath sustained injury. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicants/accused are released on bail, there is possibility of the applicants threatening the victim girl and the prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicants are released on bail they may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicants are not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicants/accused are of serious nature under section 354, 324, 34 of I.P.C. and section 8 and 10 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and section 4, 25(1)b of Arms Act and also under section 37(1) 135 of Bombay Police Act with the allegation that accused no.1 outraged modesty of complainant girl and when crowd there, other accused persons came to help the accused no.1 and they all attacked the crowd with sword and one boy alleged to have sustained injury. But then, it is contended on behalf of accused that they are falsely implicated in the crime. In such circumstance whether the allegations against the accused are true or not, would be the question to be decided on merits. .. 3 .. bail no.442/2015 (Order below exhibit 1) Even nothing is to be recovered from the applicant/accused. 4] It is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicants tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. 5] In that respect it is contended by the applicants that they are permanent residents of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and that they are ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 6] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicants/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 7] Then, it has also to be mentioned that the investigation in the matter though almost completed, the charge sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer .. 4 .. bail no.442/2015 (Order below exhibit 1) time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicants/accused in jail for uncertain period. 8] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicants can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is allowed. Applicants/accused namely Aavtar Singh Harbhajansingh, Jaswindersingh Kulwantsingh and Mangaljeet Singh Balwindersingh are released on P.R. bond of Rs.20,000/­ [rupees twenty thousand only] each with one surety each in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ The applicants/accused shall attend the concerned police station on every Tuesday between 3.00 p.m. to 5.00 p.m. and shall co­operate in investigation. They shall not not contact the victim and complainant in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize them and other prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. They shall not leave India without permission of this Court. They shall furnish proof of residence. Date : 13.03.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.

Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­004624­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No. 27/2015 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­004624­2015 (POCSO) Case No.27/2015 Received on : 17.02.2015 Registered on : 17.02.2015 Decided on : 05.03.2018 Duration : 3Y.0Ms.16Ds. IN THE COURT OF D.J.­4 & ADDL. SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE (Presided over by Hemant M. Patwardhan) Special (POCSO) Case No.27/2015 Exh.No. 1.State of Maharashtra. (Turbhe, MIDC Police station) ..Complainant V/s. 1. Amit Baliram Navgire. Age :­ 23 years, R/at. Room No. 459, Ashtavinayak Chawl, Pawane Gaon, Navi Mumbai .Accused. Appearance:­ APP Smt. Varsha Chandane for the State. Advocate Shri. Dhananjay Patil for the accused. JUDGMENT (Delivered on this 5th day of March 2018 ) Accused Amit Navgire was facing trial under sections 509, 506 of IPC and under sections 11(1), 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 on following facts:­ 1 to 12 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­004624­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No. 27/2015 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­004624­2015 (POCSO) Case No.27/2015 1] That on 16.12.2014 at about 18.00 hrs. at Pavane Naka, Navi Mumbai within jurisdiction of Turbhe MIDC police station, Navi Mumbai accused intending to insult the modesty of victim had uttered certain words intending that same shall be heard by her and at the same time has committed sexual harassment of the victim. According to allegations on next evening accused had threatened the victim and her mother with dire consequences and thus on complaint lodged by victim an offence punishable under aforesaid sections came to be registered against accused. On completion of investigation he was charge­sheeted. 2] Charge was framed against accused below Exh.5 and contents of said charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. Accused pleaded not guilty and claim to be tried. His defence was of total denial of the incident and of false implication in the matter out of political rivalry. 3] As the accused has claim to be tried, trial was conducted. Prosecution has then proceeded to examine victim as PW1, her mother, Principal of the school of the victim, independent witness Mr. Madhukar Mukadam and I.O. Ganesh Bhamare as witness no.1 to 5 respectively. On completion of evidence, statement of accused was recorded. As per his say wherein he has again reiterated defence. In order to substantiate that he was having political rivalry with witness 2 to 12 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­004624­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No. 27/2015 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­004624­2015 (POCSO) Case No.27/2015 no.4 he has also filed certificate of his designation in political party. 4] Arguments of rival advocates were heard. Learned P.P. has categorically pointed out that with sexual intend certain words were categorically uttered pointing towards the victim by the accused on initial day and then on next evening incident of threating the witnesses and victim with dire consequences had not only occurred but has been categorically deposed by the witnesses. Thus, according to learned P.P. as the said facts are corroborated by the depositions of victim and her mother along with independent witness Mr. Mukadam, same are sufficient to establish the guilt. Learned P.P. has relied upon 2016 DGLS(SC) 1002 in case of S.P.S. Rathore V/s. Central Bureau of Investigation and another to substantiate her submissions and to make request that accused be convicted for having committed said offences. Per contra, defence has argued that record itself speaks that with only intention of implicating accused person complaint has been preferred. He has then pointed out that victim has failed to state many material facts which she has uttered in the deposition without there being any explanation for it. According to him material aspect in the matter is unexplained delay in lodging the complaint and delay itself is 3 to 12 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­004624­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No. 27/2015 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­004624­2015 (POCSO) Case No.27/2015 fatal to the prosecution. Hence, he has requested to acquit accused. He has also made submissions that initial incident allegedly occurred on very busy road and it is impossible to accept that nobody will witness such an incident and accused would commit such incident by standing on a busy road that too at 6.00 p.m. when the road is very busy with all sort of traffic. He has then pointed out that even the victim did not state as to who was accompanied her at the relevant time which itself goes to show that no such incident had occurred. According to him just in order to implicate the accused in this false case next evening incident has been concocted. According to him there are 'N' number of residents adjacent to the house of victim and it is highly impossible that nobody will hear such a quarrel and nobody will intervene in it at the relevant time. Hence, he has requested to discard the evidence and acquit the accused. 5] After having heard the rival advocates, following points arose for my consideration and I record my findings against each of them for the reasons noted below :­ Sr.N. Points Findings 1] Does the prosecution prove that accused on 16.12.2014 at ..Negative. about 18.00 hrs. at Pawane Naka, Navi Mumbai, in the jurisdiction of Turbhe MIDC Police staton, Navi Mumbai, intending to insult the modesly of daughter of complainant viz. Kum. Kiran Kailash Bhagat, a minor age – 14 years 10 months by made some sound intending that the same shall be heard by her and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 509 of Indian Penal Code ? 4 to 12 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­004624­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No. 27/2015 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­004624­2015 (POCSO) Case No.27/2015 2] Does the prosecution prove that on the above date, time and ..Negative. place accused committed criminal intimidation by threatening to daughter of complainant Kum. Kiran Kailash Bhagat, a minor age­ 14 years 10 months and as such thereby committed an offence punishable under section 506 of Indian Penal Code ? 3] Does the prosecution prove that on the above date, time and ..Negative. place accused committed sexual assault on daughter of complainant Kum. Kiran Kailash Bhagat, a minor age­ 14 years 10 months and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 11(1), 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012? 4] What order? Accused is acquitted as per final order. REASONS As to point no.1 to 4 :­ 6] All these points are interlinked with each other and are considered at once. In the present case the prosecution was required to establish that initial incident had occurred with sexual intend of accused and the subsequent had occurred with intention of threating the witnesses with dire consequences. No doubt prosecution has examined aforesaid five witnesses. However, out of the said prosecution witnesses only witness no.1,2 and 4 were of material importance being either alleged eye witnesses of the incident or though the witness was of hear­ say nature he was allegedly informed directly by the witnesses after the incident. Allegations of the prosecution were that incident was occurred with a minor and in order to establish the fact that victim was the minor deposition of witness no.3 was recorded. As per the deposition of witness no.3, victim was 5 to 12 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­004624­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No. 27/2015 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­004624­2015 (POCSO) Case No.27/2015 minor at the relevant time. Accused has also not denied that victim was minor and hence that fact can be considered as it is. 7] Prosecution has implicated accused in two distinct incidents occurred on two different dates. Initial incident appears to be of more serious nature wherein as per the allegations accused with sexual intend has uttered the words “ ,s vk;Ve” thrice. No doubt the victim and other two witnesses examined has corroborated the said fact. However, in the light of the defences whether the evidence of those three witnesses are sufficient to establish the fact has to be considered. 8] Admittedly, the spot of incident is very busy square and incident allegedly occurred at 6.00 p.m. when the road was busy with all sort of traffic and pedestrian. It being square named as Pavane Chowk was surrounded by various stalls, fruit shops etc. as per admitted facts in cross examination. Therefore, it is really difficult to digest that such incident can be occurred at 6.00 p.m. on such busy road that too by standing on the road itself. Further, though the allegations are of sexual harassment by sexual intent said facts are require to be proved beyond reasonable doubt with consistent and reliable evidence. However, as an admitted fact though incident had occurred on 16.12.2014 at about 6.00 p.m. no complaint was lodged on that date itself. There was ample opportunity for the victim and her parents to explain as to why the offence was 6 to 12 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­004624­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No. 27/2015 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­004624­2015 (POCSO) Case No.27/2015 not registered either immediately of the occurrence of the incident or with some reasonable delay on the same day itself. However, none of the witnesses were able to give any plausible explanation as to why no offence was registered about it on that date. As a matter of fact no whisper has been made as to why no such offence was registered. Hence, said unexplained delay itself is fatal to the prosecution. 9] No doubt attempts were made by the victim and the witnesses to indirectly placed on record that victim initially was waiting for her parents for informing them about the incident. That being natural conduct of a minor can be considered to be probable. However, admittedly by 7.00 to 7.30 p.m. parents had returned to home but in­spite of that fact they did not approach police for lodging any complaint. Reference is made that they had been to the house of corporator of that area on the same evening. However, there is no corroboration of the said fact by the corporator during his deposition. Hence, there is neither any plausible explanation on record that the offence is not registered on that day nor any whisper has been made to explain the fact as to why offence was not registered on that day. Hence, such uncorroborated facts and unexplained delay is certainly fatal to the prosecution and thus, the defence of the accused of his false implication out of the business rivalry appears to be more probable. 7 to 12 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­004624­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No. 27/2015 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­004624­2015 (POCSO) Case No.27/2015 10] Prosecution when has alleged that sexual harassment has been committed it was require to be established by consistent evidence. However, in the instant case though in the deposition victim has deposed that by pointing towards her the aforesaid words were uttered. There is nothing in her complaint or statement which substantiate it. Though, she was asked to explain as to why said fact did not appear in her complaint she was unable to explain. Further, though she has claim that her classmate was with her she has not referred her name before police. As aforesaid it is highly improbable that nobody has seen the incident on such a busy road. Hence, if we consider all these facts it is difficult to accept that incident dated 16.12.2014 had really occurred. 11] Now turning towards intend of the accused. In order to establish the sexual intend act should be of such a nature which was directing towards the victim. Admittedly during deposition from the words used in his examination­in­ chief and from the unexplained facts about it, it is difficult to accept that on such a busy road accused had pointed out the particular victim herself only to utter particular words. Hence, as the said fact remains unexplained and uncorroborated on record it is difficult to accept that such incident had really occurred or it was with sexual intend as defined under section 11 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 8 to 12 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­004624­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No. 27/2015 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­004624­2015 (POCSO) Case No.27/2015 Having regards to all these facts defence of the accused in my opinion appears to be more probable than that of the allegations of the prosecution in respect of incident dated 16.12.2014. 12] Another incident is referred of dated 17.12.2014 wherein at about 9.00 to 10.00 p.m. accused and his mother had been to the house of victim and allegedly threatened them with dire consequences. Prosecution has not made it clear as to why mother of the accused was never made an accused in this matter particularly when incident dated 17.12.2014 her presence is categorically referred along with same act of common intention. However, the I.O. would not be able to explain that fact which again itself goes to corroborate the defence itself. Though allegations are made that accused has threatened complainant and witnesses with dire consequences it is surprising that though such incident had occurred in a building occupied by every flat owner nobody had heard or seen the incident as alleged. During cross­examination it was categorically brought on record as to how many rooms are situated on each floor of the building and as to who was the next door neighbour of the accused and victim. It was also brought on record that all the owners and resident of flats in the building were present in their respective flats. Therefore, it was expected from I.O. to record their statements in respect of 9 to 12 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­004624­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No. 27/2015 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­004624­2015 (POCSO) Case No.27/2015 incident in order to get corroboration. However, as the I.O. has categorically failed to do so it is difficult to accept that said incident also had occurred as alleged. One Kiran Nikumb is the next door neighbour of the victim and accused and in spite of the said incident was going for considerable time it is highly improbable that next door neighbour will not make any attempt atleast to make him aware as to what incident actually was. There is no corroboration to the incident as well by any of the witnesses. I.O. has categorically failed to explain as to why he was not able to trace out any of the flat owners who had actually seen and hear the incident. Having regards to the said facts uncorroborated incident dated 17.12.2014 also difficult to accept. 13] Corporator was examined in the matter. He has categorically deposed in respect of incident at 11.00 a.m. on 17.12.2014 when according to him complainant and family members had approached to him with request to settle the matter. He has not made reference or whisper of even family of victim had approached to him on the evening of 16.12.2014 so as to state the incident of 6.00 p.m. occurred on 16.12.2014. He has only made reference of his attempt to settle the matter between family of the victim and family of accused at the 10 to 12 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­004624­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No. 27/2015 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­004624­2015 (POCSO) Case No.27/2015 relevant time. As he has also not corroborated the facts narrated it is difficult to say that his deposition only can be sufficient to corroborate the incident of 16.12.2014. Though he has alleged that he has heard abuses by the accused at the time of incident dated 17.12.2014 it appears to be his improvement in deposition as he has not stated that particular fact before police. Therefore, without corroboration of the particular facts it is difficult to accept that said incident had really been occurred. Further if we consider the allegatins that in the moring of 17.12.2014 if the matter has been settled between the parties allegedly, then it will be highly improbable that accused and his mother will again approach the victim and witnesses after a gap of about 10 hours to commit other incident. It is general tendency of the perosn who was got annoyed with any particular inicident to react immediately and if that is considered as common natural phenomenon then it is again difficult to accept that accused would wait for about 10 hours to react on the complaint of victim before said corporator. Hence, if we consider all these facts it is again difficult to accept said incident of 17.12.2014 as well and as evidence in respect of both the incident is neither consistent nor reliable charges cannot be said to be prove beyond reasonable doubt. As per the settled propositions of law when defence has succeeded in creating doubt in respect of occurrence of the incident benefit should be extended in favour 11 to 12 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­004624­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No. 27/2015 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­004624­2015 (POCSO) Case No.27/2015 accused. Accordingly, by extending the benefit in favour of accused, the order. ORDER 1] Accused is acquitted from the offence punishable under sections 509, 506 of IPC and under sections 11(1), 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, 2] Bail bond of accused shall stands canceled. 3] Accused is directed to execute P.R. and S.B. of Rs.10,000/­ as per amended provisions of section 437(A) of Cr.P.C. and bonds so executed shall remain in force for the period of six months from the date of its execution. 4] Proceeding is accordingly closed. Thane (Hemant M.Patwardhan) Date: 05.03.2018 D.J.­4 & Additional Sessions Judge, Thane 12 to 12

1 Bail No.476/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) Criminal Bail Application No.476/2016 Sunny Bhimrao Dere .. Applicant versus The State of Maharashtra Through Vartaknagar Police Station .. Non­applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 1] By this application the applicant is seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. who was arrested on 09/02/2016 by Vartaknagar Police Station in connection with C.R.No.I­ 62/2016 registered for an offence punishable under section 363, 366 of I.P.C. and section 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as P.O.C.S.O. Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Mr.K.S.Parkar for the applicant/accused and learned Spl.P.P. Mrs. R.A.Navale for State. I.O. absent. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 08/02/2016 at the instance of the informant/father of the victim­girl aged about 16 years with an indictment that on 08/02/2016 victim­ 2 Bail No.476/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) girl left home and since then she did not return therefore, with the suspicion that she had been kidnapped by some unknown person, the F.I.R. was registered. During investigation the victim­girl was found with accused and therefore, offence under section 366 was added. 4] The learned Counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant/accused is falsely implicated. He submitted that Victim­girl on her own left the house. He further submitted that accused never forced or enticed away the victim­girl. He did nothing wrong with the victim­girl. The accused is young boy of 21 yrs. and having no criminal antecedents. The accused is permanent resident of Thane. The accused is ready to abide any conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing him on bail. 5] Per contra, the learned Spl.P.P. opposed the application submitting that the offence is serious in respect of a minor girl. She submitted that there are five witnesses and the statement of victim­girl recorded under section 164 of Cr.P.C. disclosed that she was kidnapped by accused. The investigation is in progress. There are chances of tampering with witnesses and prayed for rejection of application. 3 Bail No.476/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R., it appears that initially, the F.I.R. was lodged by the father of the victim­girl about kidnapping of his daughter. However, during investigation the victim­girl was found with accused therefore, the provisions of section 366 were added. However, it appears that victim­girl is aged about 16 yrs. which means she has attained the age of discretion. The accused is behind bar since about one month. The material part of investigation must have been completed. The accused is young boy of 21 yrs. and report filed by the I.O. did not disclose that there is any criminal antecedents against the accused. No fruitful purpose would be served by further incarceration of accused. The object of bail is neither punitive nor preventive but to secure the presence of the accused at the time of trial. He is ready to abide by the conditions imposed by the Court. In such circumstances the apprehension of learned Spl.P.P. about tampering of witnesses can be addressed by imposing suitable conditions. Hence, I pass the following order ­ ORDER 1) The application is allowed. 2) Applicant namely Sunny Bhimrao Dere be released on bail on his executing P.R. Bond of ₹ 15,000/­ [Rupees Fifteen Thousand only] with one local solvent surety in the like amount on the following conditions ­ 4 Bail No.476/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) A] Applicant shall attend the concerned police station on every Sunday between 10.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon till filing the charge­sheet. B] Applicant shall co­operate in investigation and shall not tamper with prosecution witnesses. C] Applicant shall furnish his and his two blood relatives' address proofs and contact numbers and he is duty bound to inform I.O. and Court about the change of address, if any. Thane. Date : 02/03/2016. (Ms. U.M. Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act), Thane.

P.W.1 further deposed that on asking her daughter, she told that she like accused and she at her own went with him and denied to have any physical relationship with him. Even if the evidence of P.W.1 is believed, there is nothing to suggest that accused enticed away or took away the victim­girl. On the contrary, P.W.1 further deposed that when she brought her daughter, thereafter, she kept her daughter at village Jaunpur U.P. and for five months she stayed there and from there accused took her away. 15] Further mother of victim­girl/ informant (P.W.1) deposed that now her daughter is married and staying with accused happily and carrying pregnancy. In such eventuality even the prosecution is unable to examine the victim­girl. Even document about marriage and medical treatment of pregnancy of victim­girl is placed on record wherein in the place of name of father, the name of accused is clearly mentioned. Thus, there is absolutely no evidence that the accused enticed or took away the victim­girl from the lawful custody of her parents. Further there is no believable evidence about date of birth of the victim­girl that on the date of 9 Special Case No. 49/2014 (Judgment) incident she was minor. Thus, prosecution failed to prove basic requirement of the offence of kidnapping i.e. minority of child and thus failed to prove charge of kidnapping Similarly, as the prosecution failed to prove that victim­girl was minor child at the time of incident, therefore, the charge under provision of P.O.C.S.O. Act would not sustain. Therefore, I answer point No.1 & 2 in negative. Hence, in the absence of cogent and reliable evidence, accused is entitled for acquittal. 16] In the result, I proceed to pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused Dilip Rambali Saroj is hereby acquitted U/Sec. 235(1) of Cr.P.C. for the offence punishable U/Sec.363 of Indian Penal Code and U/s. 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] His bail bonds stand cancelled and surety is discharged. 3] The Accused shall furnish personal bond of the amount of ₹15,000/­ in compliance of provision of Section 437­A of Cr.P.C. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 55­16 ­ S­376,323,504,506,34, 3­6,16,17.doc .....20/­ ..20.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 55/2016.. Exh.87.. CNR No. MHTH01­001229­2016 23] It is pertinent to note here that the victim girl has specifically deposed that on one day while she was in 3 rd std. the Mavshi had been to their class, said something to Miss and thereafter said Miss had asked her that she should go with said Mavshi. As per prosecution story, said Mavshi is accused No.4. However, as admitted by investigating officer PW5 A.P.I., Kadam he collected record of accused No.4. As per record collected by him accused Usha Tupe had applied for service in said school on 23.06.2015. At the end of June 2015 she was appointed as bus attendant. Prior to June 2015 accused Usha Tupe was not serving in said school. PW5 further admitted that he collected certificate dated 02.12.2015 issued by Child Development Project Officer, Borivli, Mumbai. As per said certificate Exh.75, in between 01.06.2007 to 08.06.2015 accused Usha Tupe was serving in Anganwadi No.91, Shantinagar, Dongari, Dahisar (E) as helper. Thus before 23.06.2015 accused Usha Tupe was not at all serving in Sardar Vallabhabhai Patel school, wherein the alleged incident took place. Even after appointment in the school accused Usha Tupe was employed as bus attendant and not as an Aaya in school. Under such circumstances the allegations that accused Usha Tupe used to take the victim girl to the store room are disproved from the prosecution evidence itself. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 55­16 ­ S­376,323,504,506,34, 3­6,16,17.doc .....21/­ ..21.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 55/2016.. Exh.87.. CNR No. MHTH01­001229­2016 24] As already mentioned number of citations are produced on behalf of prosecution by the learned A.P.P. and independent advocate assisting to A.P.P. in the prosecution. Those various citations are on the point of delay and medical evidence. So far as delay is concerned, it is not only the delay in lodging FIR, but the conduct on the part of the parents after revealing the incident of sexual assault upon their daughter is to be taken into consideration. In the present case as deposed by informant, after victim narrated the incident, on the same day she narrated the incident to her husband. Her husband works for registration of companies. Thus he is educated and employed person. Under such circumstances after receiving information of such serious offence, they preferred to take the victim to Dr.Datar in Malad. Said doctor had advised counseling of the victim girl, whereby victim girl was taken to BHABA hospital. Interestingly as admitted by the investigating officer he recorded statement of Dr.Amey Joshi of BHABA hospital, who stated nothing about sexual assault upon the minor girl. The investigating officer further stated that it was not revealed that the victim was under treatment of Dr.Datar. Considering said fact it is not the delay but the conduct on the part of educated parents i.e. informant who is mother of the victim and victim's father appears to be unreliable. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 55­16 ­ S­376,323,504,506,34, 3­6,16,17.doc .....22/­ ..22.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 55/2016.. Exh.87.. CNR No. MHTH01­001229­2016 25] As already mentioned the medical evidence on record clearly shows that it is not suggestive of repeated penetrative perivaginal or perineal sexual assault upon the victim girl. Though one more girl was alleged to be a victim, no such girl is revealed in the investigation. Under such circumstances though victim girl and her mother corroborated the evidence of each other, it is not supported by any independent oral or medical evidence on record. Though the accused Nos.1 to 4 have not given detail explanation about their falsely implication in the offence, it is for the prosecution to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt to bring home the guilt of the accused. Certainly the evidence on record is not satisfying the test of maxim beyond reasonable doubt. 26] Section 29 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act lays down certain presumption. The section reads as under : “Where a person is prosecuted for committing or abetting or attenuating to commit any offence under sections 3,5,7 and section 9 of this Act, the Special Court shall presume, that such person has committed or abetted or attempted to commit the offence, as the case may be unless the contrary is proved”. 27] No doubt there is presumption under the Act as above. To raise such presumption there must be strong prima facie evidence against the culprit. In the present case the J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 55­16 ­ S­376,323,504,506,34, 3­6,16,17.doc .....23/­ ..23.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 55/2016.. Exh.87.. CNR No. MHTH01­001229­2016 prosecution has come with specific allegations of repeated penetrative sexual assault upon the victim girl by three teachers for a period of more than a year. When such specific allegations are levelled against the accused with specific allegations of involvement of woman employee, those are to be proved by leading oral as well as documentary evidence. Except the testimony of the informant and the victim girl, there is no single oral or documentary evidence to support the allegations levelled against the accused. As already mentioned though there are specific allegations on woman employee i.e. accused No.4, assisting accused Nos.1 to 3 in the heinous crime, it is proved by documentary evidence that during alleged period she was not even employee in said school and was employed in another institution. Under such circumstances this is not a fit case to raise presumption u/s.29 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 28] From all above observations and evidence on record it is clear that the arguments of learned A.P.P. and written arguments submitted by independent advocate and rulings cited on behalf of prosecution are not acceptable in the present case. On the contrary the prosecution has miserably failed to prove all the allegations levelled against the accused Nos.1 to 4. Hence answering point Nos.1 to 4 in the negative, following order is passed. REASONS As to Point No.1 to 3 : 11] All the points are taken up together for discussion, to avoid the repetition, as evidence about the same in common and inter­connected. 12] Before proceeding to discuss the evidence of prosecution witnesses, it would be beneficial to reproduce relevant provisions of Law for which accused is facing charge. Section 375 of I.P.C. A man is said to commit “rape” if he - (a) penetrates his penis, to any extent, into the vagina, mouth urethra or anus of a woman or makes her to do so with him or any other person; or (b)---------; or (c)---------- ; or (d) applies his mouth to the vagina, anus, urethra of a woman or makes her to do so with him or any other person, under the circumstances falling under any of the following seven 8 Spl.Case No.51/2014 (Judgment) descriptions :- First – Against her will, Secondly – Without her consent, Thirdly- –----------- to Fifthly - –----------- , Sixthly – With or without her consent, when she is under eighteen years of age. P.O.C.S.O. Act, 2012 - Section 2 (d) - “child” means any person below the age of eighteen years; Section 3 - Penetrative Sexual Assault – A person is said to commit “penetrative sexual assault” if – (a) he penetrates his penis, to any extent, into vagina, mouth, urethra or anus of child or makes the child to do so with him or with any other person; or, (b) ...........; or, (c) …...........; or, (d) …........... Section 12 - Punishment for sexual harassment - Whoever, commits sexual harassment upon a child shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fne. 9 Spl.Case No.51/2014 (Judgment) Age of victim­girl is 5 Years : 13] First of all as the accused is facing charge U/s. 4 & 12 of POCSO Act it is incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that the victim­girl was minor at the time of incident. It is the case of prosecution that the five years old girl was subjected to penetrative sexual assault by the accused by taking her to his house and lure her by giving coin of 2/­. As far as the age of the victim­girl is concerned, it is not much disputed by the defense. Informant Pushpa Mourya (P.W.1) who is the mother of victim­girl stated the age of victim­girl as 5 years at the time of incident and her date of birth is 25/12/2008. So also, in the medical certificate in respect of victim­girl which is below Exh.29, the age of victim­girl is stated as 5 years. Dr.Mugdha (P.W.7) deposed that secondary sex character of the girl were not found developed. Article­ G is birth certificate of victim­girl wherein her date of birth is mentioned as 25/12/2008. Further it is not disputed by the defence and even from the physical appearance of the victim­ girl she appears to be the girl below the age of six­seven years. Thus, the prosecution proved that at the time of alleged incident in the year 2014 the victim­girl was aged 5 years i.e., below the age of 18 years and thus 'child' as per definition given in section 2(d) of P.O.C.S.O. Act. 10 Spl.Case No.51/2014 (Judgment) Identity of Accused not disputed : 14] As far as the identity of accused is concerned, it is the admitted fact that accused, informant and her family are staying in same vicinity which is a slum area situated at Jai Ambe Nagar, Bhayander. It is further admitted fact on record that the room of accused and victim­girl are in a small chawl and all the room are adjacent to each other. There is a road in front of the chawl having width of 8 to 10 ft. and many residents of that area are in habit to sit in front of the house and on road also. Even the photographs of the area are placed on record which are at Article­A to E. Photographs at Articles­ A, B and D are of the room of accused, photograph at Article­C is of the lane and photograph at Article­E is the door of the room of accused. Further, accused in his statement recorded under section 313 of Cr. P.C. even admitted the photographs and stated that police took photograph of his house. Thus, the picture of slum locality is clear. Further, as the accused was staying in the same vicinity and known to the family of the victim­girl therefore his identity is not disputed. However, it is disputed that accused is perpetrator of the crime. Material Evidence of Victim­girl and Informant : 15] In this respect, the material evidence is of the victim­girl who is child and of her mother to whom the victim­ girl immediately disclosed the incident in question and thereafter the mother of victim­girl immediately lodged the report. 11 Spl.Case No.51/2014 (Judgment) 16] In this respect, first of all it is necessary to scrutinize the evidence of informant (P.W.1) who is mother of the small victim­girl. Pushpa Mourya (P.W.1) deposed that on 12/01/2014 at about 12.00 to 01.00 p.m. her daughter (victim­girl) came from the room of Nikhilesh (Mithlesh) and was weeping. She hold her and victim­girl was holding coin of 2/­. Informant (P.W.1) asked her who gave her money. She (victim­girl) went inside the house and took out her panty and was cleaning. She told to P.W.1 that uncle did it and shown Nikhilesh (Mithilesh)/accused. Informant (P.W.1) further deposed that victim­girl told her that uncle took out her panty and did something on her private part and accused also took out his panty. She further deposed that thereafter, she went to police station and lodged the report which is at Exh.7. Her daughter was complaining about the pain in her abdomen and that she was taken in hospital by lady police. She even corrected the name of her daughter which was wrongly spelled (written) in the police papers. 17] Here at this stage, the evidence of the victim­girl is also material. As stated above, the victim­girl is the child as defined under the P.O.C.SO. Act. When the victim­girl entered in the witness box, at that time she was aged six years and at the time of incident in question she was aged about five years. As the victim­girl is minor, her evidence is required to be dealt with great care and scrutiny. However, at the same time, the 12 Spl.Case No.51/2014 (Judgment) object of the POCSO Act is also required to be kept in mind, particularly, in the background of the provisions of presumption given in section 29 and 30 of POCSO Act. 18] Victim­girl (P.W.2) deposed that incident took place prior to about two years. She did not recollect the date, but stated that it was Sunday. Victim­girl further deposed that on that day, in the afternoon she was playing outside her house and at that time, Mithilesh uncle called her. She knows Mithilesh uncle, because he was staying beyond two houses from her house. That time, Mithilesh uncle gave her 2/­ and took her in his house. He, then closed the door of the house. Nobody else was there in the house. Then Mithilesh uncle removed her nicker and he then touched her place of urination. He inserted his place of urination (Nunni) in her place of urination. He also gave his place of urination (Nunni) in her hand. She had pain at place of her urination. She, then wore her nicker. Mithilesh uncle then opened the door. She then went home and narrated the incident to her mother. Her mother then phoned and told her father about the incident. After her father came home from work she narrated him about the incident. She then shown the house of Mithilesh uncle to her parents. Her father, then took her to police station. Her mother was also with them. The victim­girl then identified the accused and even identified the nicker and T­shirt which were on her person at the time of incident in question. 13 Spl.Case No.51/2014 (Judgment) 19] From this piece of evidence of the victim­girl it clearly appears that the victim­girl identified the accused, who was staying in front of their house and victim­girl in most natural way, stated about the incident. 20] The learned defence counsel most vehemently argued that the victim­girl is a tutored witness and she was tutored by her mother and there is clear admission in that respect in her cross­examination. He in that respect invited my attention to the last paragraph of her cross­examination wherein victim­girl admitted that her mother told her to identify the accused to be the same Mithilesh uncle committing such an act with her and therefore, she has identified him. The learned defence counsel further most vehemently argued that the accused is falsely implicated as there were frequent quarrel between the informant and accused on account of the tap water and for that purpose accused once complained to the society and on his complaint, the persons from society asked informant to vacate the house. The learned defence counsel for that purpose lend support from cross­examination of Geeta Singh(P.W.3) who is neighborer and as per prosecution she witnessed victim­girl coming from house of accused and altercation of informant and accused after incident, however, P.W.3 did not support the case of prosecution. 14 Spl.Case No.51/2014 (Judgment) 21] The learned defence counsel in support of his contention about tutored witness place his reliance on judgment of Hon'ble Bombay High Court in case of Mohammad Farooq abdul Rauf vs. State of Maharashtra 2010 Cri.L.J.1468. 22] However, in this respect, though, victim­girl admitted that there is no water tap in their house and they have to fetch watch from the water tap and even though, she admitted that there was quarrel between her mother and Mithilesh uncle on account of fetching water and her parents were asked to leave the house and her mother used to say that, because of Mithilesh, they have been asked to leave the house and they shall make complaint against Mithilesh uncle, that shows the innocence of the victim­girl. It is very common aspect in slum area or chawl to have some disputes on account of common water tap or wash­room but for that purpose no one can impute such serious allegations, staking character of small girl. Particularly in Indian society character of girl is most cherished for parent. Further, even victim­girl is a small girl and if her mother told her how to behave in court or how to answer that can not amount to tutoring. Particularly when victim­girl specifically denied the suggestion that she deposed everything in her examination­in­chief as stated by her mother. Therefore, the case law relied on by defence is not of any help to the accused. 15 Spl.Case No.51/2014 (Judgment) 23] Further there is evidence of P.W.5 Shivram Bind who is resident of same vicinity and know the accused and informant. Bind (P.W.5) deposed that incident took place before two years, but he does not recollect the date but it was Sunday at 12.00 noon. He further deposed that on that day he was sleeping in his house on the upper floor and heard the commotion and therefore, peeped from his house and that time, he had seen the victim­girl had come out of the house of accused and she was crying. P.W.5 even deposed that the girl was crying and there was quarrel and he heard that the girl stating her mother that Mithilesh had given 2/­ and done some wrong act. However, as far as this portion of evidence is concerned it is in the form of omission. Though, evidence of this witness is full of embellishments, that cannot be completely over thrown. Even though the evidence of this witness is kept out of consideration, still there is a medical evidence supporting the case of prosecution. Prompt F.I.R. 24] Informant (P.W.1) very clearly deposed that incident took place in between 12.00 hours to 01.00 p.m. and F.I.R. was registered at 13.50 p.m. which means F.I.R. was lodged promptly without wasting any time and which is of much credence and even ruled possibility of false implication. 25] Here it is further significant to note that initially on the report of informant Pushpa Mourya (P.W.1) the only 16 Spl.Case No.51/2014 (Judgment) offence punishable under section 354 of IPC and section 8 and 10 of POCSO Act was registered. However, thereafter when the victim­girl was referred for medical examination and the medical officer informed the investigating officer, that the victim­girl was sexually assaulted, thereafter the offence under section 376(2)(f) of I.P.C. was added. In this respect, the investigating officer A.P.I. Pradeep Pullarwar (P.W.9) clearly deposed about the said aspect. Which clearly shows that the tender aged victim­girl as per her understanding stated incident to her mother and in turn she narrated the incident to police and as per that report was scribed. Then after clear medical opinion the offence of rape was added. Seizer of clothes of Victim­girl and the Accused:­ 26] Prosecution proved the sizer of clothes of victim­ girl and the accused through P.S.I. Chandrakant Koli (P.W.8), who deposed that the clothes of victim­girl and accused were seized under panchanama in presence of panchas. The property search and seizer panchanama are at Exh.38 and Exh.39 respectivly. Scene of offence / Spot­Panchanam : 27] The learned defence counsel further argued that the prosecution witness Bermu Kangralkar (P.W.4) and Anil Kumar Singh (P.W.6) who are the panch to the spot panchnama, did not support the case of prosecution and thus spot panchnama is not proved by the prosecution. However, in 17 Spl.Case No.51/2014 (Judgment) this respect, it is necessary to mention that the house of accused which is in front of house of informant (P.W.1) is not disputed and as discussed above, even the accused admitted the location. PSI Chandrakant Koli (P.W.8), who investigated the crime after registration of FIR deposed that on 13/01/2014 he visited the scene of offence that is at the house of accused at Jai Ambe Nagar, Bhayander (W) and drawn the spot panchnama in presence of two panchas, and admits its contents to be correct, which is at Exh.37. In this case, as the girl is too small, and generally small kids used to go to the house of any person for playing, therefore there is no reason for the person sitting over there to doubt any foul playing.
