Further learned defence counsel argued that for obtaining the sample of semen, a particular procedure is required to be followed and it cannot be obtained in normal course. No doubt, there are some irregularity while conducting the investigation of the serious offence. It is rightly pointed out by the learned defence counsel that prosecution failed to examine any witness to show that who carries the sample to the F.S.L. and the investigating officers tried to shift its responsibility on one another. However, Exh.40 and Exh.45 which are the covering letters issued to the F.S.L. Santacruz, Mumbai for DNA examination having mention about receipt of five sealed parcels, one sealed card board, five sealed test tubes and endorsement about receipt of one sealed plash container which is in respect of the required samples of the accused as mentioned in Exh.45. By Exh.40 the cloths of the accused the victim and the samples of the victim­girl were 23 Spl.Case No.51/2014 (Judgment) forwarded for chemical analysis and DNA analysis. Similarly, all C.A. Reports have note about receipt of intact seal parcels. 38] But when the DNA report clearly shows that the sample sent for i.e. the sample of victim­girl and of the accused matched and the particular opinion that the same were from the same paternal progeny, there remains no doubt that the perpetrator of the crime was the accused. 39] Though the learned defence counsel faintly argued that there were various persons staying in the small room of the informant and there is possibility that anyone among them may be the culprit. However, no such suggesion was given to any of the witnesses and it is highly impossible for the mother of a small child to point out the accused as a sexual assaulter of her minor girl child leaving actual assaulter. Here it cannot be forget that the victim of the sexual offences are treated at par with the injured witness and there is no reason for the injured witness to screen the real offender implicating the innocent person. 40] In this respect, learned defence counsel most vehemently argued that D.N.A. report can not be believed for two reasons. Firstly, only exhibiting the documents does not amount to prove the contents of the document and further the carrier were not examined and therefore, it is doubtful that the samples provided for the chemical analysis were of the accused 24 Spl.Case No.51/2014 (Judgment) only. The learned defence counsel in support of his submission placed reliance on the Judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Sait Tarajee Khimchand and others vs. Yelamarti Satyam and others AIR1971SC1865 and in the case of Salman Salim Khan vs. State of Maharashtra, 2016 ALL MR.(Cri.) 01. 41] In that regard, it is necessary to have a look into the provisions of section 293 of Cr.P.C. which is about the reports of certain Government Scientific experts. As per provisions of section 293 of Cr.P.C. any document purporting to be the report under the hand of Government Scientific Expert to whom the section applies, upon any matter or thing duly submitted to him or examination or analysis and report in the course of any proceeding under this Code, may be used as evidence in any inquiry, trial or other proceeding under this Code. Further Section 293(4) specified the cases where the provisions of the section will apply including following Government Scientific Experts namely­ (a) Any Chemical Examiner or Assistant Chemical Examiner to the Government, (b) Chief Controller Explosive; (c)......; to (f) ­­­­­­; (g) any other Government Scientific Expert specified, by notification, by the Central Government for this purpose. 42] Thus, as per provision of Sec.293 of Cr.P.C. no formal proof is required before admitting the document in evidence. However, if accused desire he can call the author of document for cross­examination. It is pertinent to note that 25 Spl.Case No.51/2014 (Judgment) though accused raised objection for exhibiting C.A. reports, however, he did not take any steps to summon the examiner. It is true that when the report of the Chemical Analyser was sought to be admitted on record the learned defence Counsel raised objection to its admission on record. Beyond that no further steps were taken. No application to summon the concerned Chemical Analyser was moved neither at any time it demonstrates in what respect the report was deficient and necessitated the calling of the Chemical Analyser before admitting it in evidence. Therefore, mere argument doubting its authenticity would not help accused. 43] No doubt, in the case of Salman Khan (Supra) the benefit of doubt was extended to the accused considering weaknesses and shortcomings in the prosecution case. The Hon'ble High court gave emphasis to the fact that the blood samples of the accused, were not reached properly to the F.S.L. to ascertain the quantity or consumption of alcohol by the accused. Further, in that case, the procedure followed for reaching the samples to C.A. office where seen as doubtful, and the benefit was given to the accused. However, in this respect before placing the reliance on the said Judgment, with due respect, it must mention that the said Judgment of Hon'ble Bombay High Court is challenged before the Hon'ble Apex Court vide S.L.P.(Cri.)No.704/2016 State of Maharashtra vs. Salman Salim Khan and therefore, at this stage, the Judgment of cited by defence (supra) can not be taken as precedent. 26 Spl.Case No.51/2014 (Judgment) 44] Further in the case of Sait Tarajee (Supra) the question was in respect of the civil transaction wherein plaintiff wants to rely on the Exh.A­12 and A­13 i.e. the day­ book and ledger respectively and the case is in respect of the mortgage bond and therefore the facts of the case are totally different and not applicable in the facts of the present case and most particularly in view of provision of section 293 of Cr.P.C. by which report of C.A. can be read in evidence without formal proof attracting the presumption that said report was issued by following scientific method. 45] Thus, finding semen on clothes of victim­girl and further positive report of DNA profiling leave no room of doubt that accused had penovaginal sexual intercourse with victim girl and cause sexual harassment by sexually assaulting her. Social Background of Witnesses :­ 46] Here in this respect, we have to consider the social background of the victim­girl and her family. As it is admitted fact, that the victim­girl, her family and accused are staying in a slum area and are from very poor family. The capacity of such witnesses who describe the incident, to recollect the incident and to reproduce it before court is required to be considered with great sensitivity. No doubt there are some discripancies in case of prosecution like wrongly mentioning date of incident in report at Exh.7 as 11/01/2014 instead of 12/01/2014 and mentioning of name of accused in deposition 27 Spl.Case No.51/2014 (Judgment) as Nikhilesh instead of Mithilesh are of no much consequences particularly in the backdrop of reliable testimony of witnesses. Further inability of informant and victim­girl in stating date of incident is also not much material. Much was argued for non­ examination of father of victim­girl suspecting as to how on sunday he was on his work. However, in my opinion that factor also has no much bearing on case of prosecution. 47] No doubt, there are some omissions and contradictions in the evidence of P.W.1 and P.W.2 like P.W.1 informant denied that there was quarrel between accused and informant on account of the tap water. While the victim­girl admitted that there was quarrel between her mother and accused. However, in this respect, though there had been some quarrel between the family of the accused and the informant, that cannot be taken as a reason for false implication, particularly in the background of the medical report of the victim­girl which clearly disclose that on the day when she was examined, she was sexually assaulted and fresh tear was found on her examination with minimal redness of vaginal mucosa. Further the D.N.A. report Exh.30 evident the opinion that D.N.A. profiles of ex­2 inner thigh swab, ex­3 labial swab, ex­4 Hymenal swab, ex­5 vaginal swab, ex­6 anal swab of victim­ girl and ex­1 blood sample of accused in F.S.L.M.L.Case No. DNA­133/14 is from the same paternal progeny. Which clearly indicate that the victim­girl was sexually assaulted by the accused. 28 Spl.Case No.51/2014 (Judgment) 48] Witnesses are not Tape­recorder and therefore, mathematical testimony of illiterate person is not expected. Some omissions and contradictions ought to occurs depending upon the capacity of the witnesses to remember the incident and to narrate it before Court. 49] In this respect observations made by Hon'ble Justice V. R. Krisha Iyer in Inder Singh vs. state (Delhi Administration) AIR 1978 SC 1091 would be helpful. Wherein it is held that ­ “Credibility of testimony, oral and circumstantial, depends considerably on a judicial evaluation of the totality, not isolated scrutiny. While it is necessary that proof beyond reasonable doubt should be adduced in all criminal cases, it is not necessary that it should be perfect. If a case is proved too perfectly, it is argued that it is artificial; if a case has some flaws, inevitable because human beings are prone to err, it is argued that it is too imperfect. One wonders whether in the meticulous hypersensitivity to eliminate a rare innocent from being punished, many, guilty men must be callously allowed to escape. Proof beyond reasonable doubt is a guideline, not a fetish and guilty man cannot away with it because truth suffers some infirmity when projected through human processes. Judicial quest for perfect proof often accounts for police presentation of fool­proof concoction. Why fake up ? Because the court asks for manufacture to make truth look true ? No, we must be realistic.” (Emphasis added) 29 Spl.Case No.51/2014 (Judgment) 50] Further, in this respect learned Spl.P.P. also rightly placed her reliance on the landmark judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in case of State of Uttar Pradesh vs. Krishna Gopal 1989 Cr.L.J.1­145 wherein Justice Venkatchaliah observed and held that – (para­13). Doubts would be called reasonable if they are free from a zest for abstract speculation. Law cannot aford any favourite other than truth. To constitute reasonable doubt, it must be free from an over emotional response. Doubts may be actual and substantial doubts as to the guilt of the accused-person arising from the evidence, or from the lack of it, as opposed to mere vague apprehensions. A reasonable doubt is not an imaginary, trivial or a merely possible doubt; but a fair doubt based upon reason and common-sense. It must grow out of the evidence in the case. The concepts of probability, and the degrees of it, cannot obviously be expressed in terms of units to be mathematically enumerated as to how many of such units constitute proof beyond reasonable doubt. There is an unmistakable subjective- element in the evaluation of the degrees of probability and the quantum of proof. Forensic probability must, in the last analysis, rest on a robust common-sense and, ultimately, on the trained intuitions of the judge. While the protection given by the criminal process to the accused-persons is not to be eroded, at the same time, uninformed legitimization of trivialities would make a mockery of administration of criminal justice. 51] The Ld. Spl.P.P. also placed her reliance on the various judgments of Hon'ble Apex Court and Hon'ble High Court in the cases of – (1) Noor Mohd. Salim Shaikh vs. State of Maharashtra 2015 ALL MR(Cri)1725, (2) Lalmand Chaudhari vs. state 2010 ALL MR (Cri)102, (3) Sandip Subhash Dhaigude vs. State of Maharashtra 2015 ALL MR (Cri)1036, (4) Nandakumar Jadhav vs. State of Maharashtra 2014 ALL MR (Cri)697, (5) Sudhakar Shelake vs. State of H.P., 2012 Cri.L.J. 3210, (4) Deepak V/s. State of Maharashtra 2015 ALL MR (Cri)2940 (6) Sonu Kumar vs. State of H.P. 2012 Cri.L.J.3210. The ratio of above­said cases is that the sole testimony of victim of sexual assault is believable and it did not require corroboration if the version found truthful and 30 Spl.Case No.51/2014 (Judgment) reliable and C.A. report about semen found on clothes of victim and accused corroborates prosecution case, some inconsistency regarding period and time of incident cannot be material to suspect prosecution witnesses etc. 52] Thus, in the background of entire evidence brought on record, particularly of the victim­girl (P.W.2), her mother (P.W.1), medical officer (P.W.7) and C.A. Reports there remains no doubt that the victim­girl was subjected to penetrative sexual assault and the perpetrator of the crime is the accused before the court. Presumption under section 29 & 30 of P.O.C.S.O.Act. 53] In this respect, presumption as given in section 29 and 30 of POCSO Act is relevant. The said presumption is added in the Act with the particular object considering that the children required some protection from the sexual offence, and even while considering their evidence before the Court. The capacity of the children to understand such a heinous crime and their ability to describe is always required to kept in mind and therefore, in that scenario, the specific provisions were enacted in the special Act. 54] This pair­presumption under section 29 and 30 of POCSO Act is a complementary set of presumptions. This pair at first place makes a presumption in favour of the victims who are children under the age of 18 years. This pair presumption 31 Spl.Case No.51/2014 (Judgment) works to absolve children's burden of making their stand intact facing the legal intricacies during the course of trial. The first set out of this pair­presumption takes care of the child who is victim of a sexual offence and has limited capacities and capabilities of appreciation and understanding. A child is quite incapable of appreciating and understanding the mental state of others and even of himself. In all cases or most of the cases, in absence of such a pair­presumption the victim might not find itself to give a complete account of mental state and mental elements of the accused which the victim might have come across during the commission of the offence. Such contingencies would have frustrated the legislation of the POCSO Act. The Legislature with a view to ensure the proper and smooth functioning of the Act has provided this pair­ presumption. This is just to ensure the just ends of the statute. 55] It is material to reproduce the provisions of section 29 and 30 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. As per Section 29 there is presumption that ''Where a person is prosecuted for committing or abetting or attempting to commit any offence under sections 3, 5, 7, and 9 of this Act, the Special Court shall presume that such person has committed or abetted or attempted to commit the offfence, as the case may be, unless the contrary is proved''. Thus, there is word 'shall' provided in Section 29 which make it obligatory on the Court that once the prosecution proves that the accused is involved in any act under this Act, then the burden lies on the accused to rebut it. 32 Spl.Case No.51/2014 (Judgment) So also, there is presumption of culpable mental state in Section 30 of the Act which includes intuition, motive, knowledge of a fact and the belief or reason to believe a fact. The learned counsel for defence argued that presumption is always rebutable and in the present case the defence has successfully rebutted said presumption by bringing on record various contradictory evidence of the prosecution witnesses. 56] As the prosecution proved beyond reasonable doubt that the accused committed penetrative sexual assault on the tender­aged victim­girl, therefore, presumption arises in favour of prosecution and as per section 29 of the Act the burden lies on the accused to rebut the same either through cross­examination of the prosecution witnesses or by adducing defence evidence. Admittedly accused has not examined any witness in defence and, as discussed above, there is nothing material brought on record to disbelieve the prosecution 57] However, as discussed above, admittedly though there are certain omissions and contradictions in the case of prosecution, in my opinion they are not so material to demolish the case of prosecution. In the background of the discussion of evidence of witnesses it is fully established that it was the accused who took away the victim­girl by luring her by giving coin of 2/­ and then sexually assaulted her and thereafter she was immediately taken to police station and then referred for medical examination. 33 Spl.Case No.51/2014 (Judgment) 58] Though it was strongly urged that through the cross­examination of the prosecution witnesses, it is very well brought on record, that there was dispute between the family of the victim­girl i.e. particularly the informant and accused on account of tap water and accused has complained about the same to the society and thereafter, the informant was asked to vacate the room. However, as discussed above, and at the cost of repetition it must say that for the said reason no mother would stake the character of her minor daughter, leveling such a serious charge against the accused. Even if the informant want to do so, she can foist any other case like quarrel, assault, threatening etc. but she definitely would not make her daughter as an object for the said purpose. On the contrary, enmity is doubled edged weapon. Therefore, there seems reason for accused to do such heinous act. Therefore, in the facts of the case, and particularly with the supporting medical evidence, the possibility of false implication rules out. 59] Thus, the evidence of the witnesses brought on record by the prosecution is truthful, reliable and trustworthy. There is nothing to disbelieve the version of the prosecution witnesses. The reason as brought on record for false implication of accused is not sustainable. No mother would stake character of her minor daughter. Thus, the prosecution duly established that the accused who was known to the family of the victim­girl lured her by giving coin of 2/­ and had taken away the victim­girl in his house from the custody of her 34 Spl.Case No.51/2014 (Judgment) mother/informant and thereafter ravished victim­girl in diabolic manner and after returning on questioning by mother she in innocent manner disclosed the act of accused and then she was immediately taken to police station and then referred for medical examination. The medical evidence also is in corroboration to the prosecution case. Further, the presumption also arising in favour of the prosecution and the accused is failed to rebut the same. 60] Thus, there remains no doubt that it was the accused and accused only who being person in a position of trust towards the victim­girl ravished the minor victim­girl aged 5 years and committed penetrative sexual assault on her and caused sexual harrassment. Thus, the prosecution has proved the case beyond all reasonable doubt. Therefore, Accused Mithilesh Chhedi Yadav is held guilty for the offences u/s.376(2)(f)(i) of I.P.C. and u/section 4 & 12 of the P.O.C.S.O. Act and therefore the accused is liable to be punished for the said offences charges against him. At this juncture it is necessary to hear the accused on the point of sentence as per mandate of Section 235 of Cr.P.C. Hence, I take a pause to hear the accused on the point of sentence. Date : 10/02/2016. (Ms.U.M.Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act) Thane. 35 Spl.Case No.51/2014 (Judgment) 61] Heard accused on the point of sentence. Accused in person submitted that he is having two small children, his mother is blind and there is no one to look after them. He is from poor family and prayed for leniency and to give an opportunity to reform. 62] Ld. Adv. Mr. Sunil Bhatia for accused prayed that leniency be shown to accused looking to his family, while imposing the sentence. 63] The Ld. A.P.P. Mrs. R. A. Navale submitted that this is not the case of showing leniency, the victim is small child and prayed for imposing maximum sentence. 64] I have given thoughtful consideration to the submissions advanced by the accused in person, his Ld. Counsel and Ld. S.P.P. 65] Serious offences like rape on child having great impact on social order and public interest require exemplary treatment. Protection of society and stamping out criminal proclivity must be the object of law which must be achieved by imposing appropriate sentence. 66] In the present case conduct of accused belies human relationship of trust and worthiness and reflects most unfortunate and abusive facet of human conduct. Child rape 36 Spl.Case No.51/2014 (Judgment) cases are cases of perverse lust for sex where even innocent children are not spared in pursuit of the sexual pleasure. There cannot be anything more obscene than this. It is a crime against humanity. Many such cases are not even brought to light because of social stigma attached thereto. 67] The minimum sentence provided for offence u/s.376(2) of I.P.C. is rigorous imprisonment for ten years which may extend to life imprisonment and for offence U/sec. 4 of P.O.C.S.O. Act is imprisonment for 7 years which may extend to life imprisonment and for offenceu/sec.12 punishment is provided upto 3 years. However, as per provision of section 42 of P.O.C.S.O. Act punishment is required to be imposed under either I.P.C or P.O.C.S.O. which ever is grater in degree. Therefore, punishment is required to impose under Indian Penal Code for offence u/s.376(2) of I.P.C. Therefore, in my opinion, looking to nature of offence committed by accused who is neighborer keeping grudge of quarrel with the mother of informant, minimum sentence of 10 years provided in the act will meet the ends of justice. 68] In the result, I proceed to pass following order. :: ORDER :: 1] Accused Mithilesh Chhedi Yadav is hereby convicted U/Sec. 235(2) of Cr.P.C. for the offence punishable U/Sec.376(2)(f)(i) of Indian Penal 37 Spl.Case No.51/2014 (Judgment) Code r/w. Section 4 and 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and he is sentenced to suffer Rigorous Imprisonment for 10 (Ten) years and to pay fine of 5,000/­ [Rupees Five Thousand Only] and in default of payment of fine, to suffer the Simple Imprisonment for six months. 2] The accused is in jail custody since 12/01/2014. He is entitled for set off U/Sec.428 of Cr.P.C. for the period he was in jail custody. 3] Muddemal vide M.E.No.188/2015 be preserved till appeal period is over. 4] Copy of the judgment be provided to the accused free of cost as per provisions U/s. 363 of Cr.P.C. Exh.41.. : JUDGMENT : (Delivered on this 03rd day of October, 2017) The accused is prosecuted for the offence of unnatural sexual assault upon his wife and penetrative sexual assault upon his daughters aged three years and two years old. 2] The prosecution story runs as under : It is alleged by prosecution that the informant is the wife of accused. Their marriage was solemnized in the year 2009. Out of said marriage they were having two daughters aged three years and two years old respectively. Initially the informant was cohabiting with the accused at her matrimonial house at village Baliware, Tal. Karjat, Dist. Raigad. The accused is habituated to drinking and was ill­treating the informant. Therefore, the informant had left her matrimonial house and was residing at the house of her mother at village Anjurgaon. While the informant was residing with the accused at village Baliware the accused used to beat the informant in drunken condition and forcibly put his penis in her mouth. After leaving matrimonial house and residing at Anjurgaon, the accused also started residing with the informant in the house of her mother. At Anjurgaon also accused used to quarrel with the informant in drunken condition. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 29­15 ­ 377,376,506, 4,12.doc .....3/­ ..3.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 29/2015.. Exh.41.. 3] It is further alleged by the prosecution that, in the month of August 2014 the informant, her two daughters, her mother and the accused were sleeping in a room at the house of informant's mother. Informant's brother and his wife were sleeping in another room. At midnight the informant heard cries of her elder daughter who was three years old. She found that the accused and the victim daughter were sleeping facing to each other. The clothes of victim daughter were removed and the accused had put his penis on the vagina of the victim. Hearing cries of victim daughter, informant and other family members woke up. They all abused and beat the accused. However, the accused threatened the informant and her family members. Therefore, no complaint was lodged. Thereafter for 2­3 days the accused behaved properly. However, again on one night at about 12.00 midnight the accused, informant, their two daughters and informant's mother were sleeping in the room. Informant's brother and wife were sleeping in another room. At that time, the informant heard the cries of her younger daughter and woke up. She again found that the informant and younger daughter were sleeping facing to each other. The accused had removed clothes of the victim daughter. He had put his penis on the vagina of the victim. Hearing the cries of younger daughter, the informant and all family members woke up and abused the accused. Thereafter accused ran away from the house. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 29­15 ­ 377,376,506, 4,12.doc .....4/­ ..4.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 29/2015.. Exh.41.. After one month the accused apologized for his acts and started to reside with the informant and her family members. However, he again raised quarrels with the informant and left the house alongwith minor daughters. He went to his native place Baliware. The informant brought her daughters from the house of accused at Baliware. She narrated the incident to her employer with whom she was working as maid servant. As per advise she lodged complaint against the accused in Narpoli police station on 22.11.2014. 4] After receiving complaint offence u/s.377, 376, 506 of the Indian Penal Code and section 4 and 12 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act came to be registered against the accused. After investigation, charge sheet came to be filed for said offences. 5] Charge is framed against the accused at Exh.03. Accused pleaded not guilty of offence and claimed to be tried. 6] Statement of accused u/s.313 of Code of Criminal Procedure is recorded at Exh.40. The defence of the accused is that, the informant was desiring to marry with one Sunil. Therefore, she falsely implicated the accused in the offence. 7] After going through the prosecution story and evidence on record, following points arise for my J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 29­15 ­ 377,376,506, 4,12.doc .....5/­ ..5.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 29/2015.. Exh.41.. determination. I record my findings thereon for reasons as stated below. POINTS FINDINGS 1] Does the prosecution prove that in the month of August 2014 at midnight in the residential house of mother of the informant, the accused had put his penis on the vagina of his minor daughters on different occasions and thereby committed penetrative sexual assault ? …Not proved. 2] Does the prosecution further prove that prior to August 2014 in the residential house at village Baliware the accused forcefully put his penis into the mouth of informant i.e. his wife and thereby committed offence of carnal intercourse ? …Not proved. 3] Does the prosecution further prove that on above mentioned date, time and place the accused had sexually harassed his minor daughters ? …Not proved. 4] What order ? ..As per final order. : REASONS : As to the Point Nos.1 to 3 :­ 8] To bring home the guilt of accused the prosecution has examined the informant Pinki Pintya Jadhav as PW1 at Exh.10. Complaint lodged by her is at Exh.11. The panch on spot panchanama namely Mahesh Satyaram Jaiswal is J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 29­15 ­ 377,376,506, 4,12.doc .....6/­ ..6.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 29/2015.. Exh.41.. examined as PW2. His deposition is at Exh.14. The spot panchanama is at Exh.15. The victim i.e. elder daughter of accused and informant is examined as PW3 at Exh.20. Lastly the investigating officer P.I., Smt.Archana Pandharinath Daundkar is examined as PW4 at Exh.21. The prosecution has produced medical certificates of victims daughters are at Exh.35 and Exh.36. The medical certificate of the victim wife is at Exh.29. The age certificates of the victim daughters are at Exh.25 and Exh.26. The C.A. report is at Exh.48. 9] In the present case the accused has not disputed the relations with the informant and with the victim girls. He has not even disputed the age of victim girls. The alleged incident of carnal intercourse had allegedly occurred long ago. Under such circumstances there is no question of any medical evidence about the same. So far as alleged sexual assault upon minor girls are concerned, those are alleged to have occurred in the month of August 2014, whereas FIR came to be lodged on 22.11.2014. Admittedly there is delay of more than four months. There are allegations that the accused had put his penis upon the vagina of victim daughters. Thus certainly there are no allegations about any penetration by the accused. Thus in view of period lapsed from the incident and the nature of allegations there cannot be any positive medical evidence about alleged sexual assault upon victim girls. Thus J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 29­15 ­ 377,376,506, 4,12.doc .....7/­ ..7.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 29/2015.. Exh.41.. medical certificates of informant i.e. wife and that of victim daughters of the accused are rightly admitted on behalf of defence. Apparently there is no medical evidence against the accused. In the background of these facts, we have to scrutinize the evidence of informant and victim daughter. 10] PW1 the informant i.e. wife of the accused specifically deposed that the accused used to abuse her physically in drunken condition. He used to forcefully insert his penis in her mouth. In the month of August 2014 she herself, her mother, her brother and two daughters were sleeping at mother's house. They heard screaming of elder daughter. The accused and said elder daughter were sleeping in a position as facing to each other. The accused was putting his penis in the vagina of the elder daughter. After hearing screaming of said elder daughter they woke up and slapped the accused. However, accused threatened them. PW1 further narrated similar incident with her younger daughter which allegedly took place after 2­3 days from first incident with the elder daughter. At that time also they had beaten the accused. Thereafter accused threatened them and ran away from the spot. After one month accused returned home and apologized for his acts. He stayed nicely for few days and again started drinking and quarreling with her. On one day accused took away both minor daughters to village Mhasa, Tal. Murbad. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 29­15 ­ 377,376,506, 4,12.doc .....8/­ ..8.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 29/2015.. Exh.41.. She (PW1) made complaint in Karjat and brought the daughters back from the accused. Thereafter she informed about the incident to her employer Smt.Ramchandani. Thereafter she lodged FIR on 22.11.2014. 11] The victim daughter in her deposition at Exh.20 specifically deposed that one day while she was sleeping at home her father i.e. the accused removed all her clothes. The accused slept next to her. She further gestured during deposition by pointing finger to her private part and said that the accused actually did said thing with her. She further deposed that, on one day the accused had removed clothes of her younger sister and had also removed his own clothes. One day the accused had taken her alongwith younger sister to a place at far distance and had removed their clothes. 12] PW2 Mahesh Jaiswal is panch on spot panchanama. Through his evidence spot panchanama Exh.15 is proved. As stated earlier there is delay of more than four months in lodging FIR. There is no medical evidence on record about sexual assault on the complainant and her minor daughters. Considering the delay nothing could have been seized from the spot of incident which could have been incriminating against the accused. Under such circumstances the spot J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 29­15 ­ 377,376,506, 4,12.doc .....9/­ ..9.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 29/2015.. Exh.41.. panchanama and evidence of panch witness PW2 Mahesh Jaiswal is nothing but an empty formality. 13] PW4 P.I., Mrs.Daundkar the investigating officer has carried out the investigation. Her evidence is technical in respect of investigation of the offence. 14] Relying upon the evidence of PW1 and PW3 learned A.P.P. Mr.Kulkarni argued at length and submitted that PW1 the complainant has narrated almost all facts alleged in the complaint and thereby the complaint is duly proved. The victim girl demonstrated the alleged act at the hands of accused by pointing fingers towards her private part. As such the prosecution story is duly proved. 15] As argued by advocate Mrs.Arote and as already mentioned there is delay of more than four months in lodging FIR from the alleged incident of sexual assault upon minor daughters. The alleged incident of carnal intercourse is alleged to have been occurred much prior to August 2014. Thus there is inordinate delay in lodging FIR from the alleged incident. The delay is sough to be explained by merely alleging that the accused had threatened the complainant. However, there is no force in said explanation. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 29­15 ­ 377,376,506, 4,12.doc .....10/­ ..10.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 29/2015.. Exh.41.. 16] It is pertinent to note here that at the time of alleged incidents with minor daughters the accused, his wife i.e. informant, victim daughters and mother of the complainant were sleeping in one and same room. After those alleged incidents the accused was thrashed by the complainant, her brother and mother. Under such circumstances the allegations that due to threats at the hands of accused, complaint was not lodged are not reliable. The prosecution has not examined the mother, brother and brother's wife of the complainant to corroborate the evidence of the complainant. 17] It is further to be noted here that after the alleged incidents accused had fled away from the house of mother of complainant and returned after a period of one month. Thereafter accused again left the house of the mother of complainant and went to his native place at Baliware. Thereupon the complainant had made complaint against the accused in Karjat and obtained the custody of the daughters. However, in said complaint made at Karjat the complainant had not made any allegations of sexual assault against the accused. Had it been so the Karjat police would have taken action against the accused on said complaint. Only after obtaining custody of minor daughters, the complainant lodged complaint against the accused alleging sexual assault. So far J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 29­15 ­ 377,376,506, 4,12.doc .....11/­ ..11.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 29/2015.. Exh.41.. as the evidence of victim is concerned, in cross examination she has clearly admitted certain facts, which are fatal to the prosecution. She deposed in cross examination as under ; “It is true to say that I had woke up because my mother had beaten my father and hearing that I had woke up. My father did not do the action as shown by me above. It is true to say that I have deposed as above because my mother asked me to do so.... It is true to say that my mother had asked me to say so.” 18] As already mentioned though the other family members were present at the time of alleged incident of sexual assault upon minor daughters, no independent witness is examined by the prosecution. There is inordinate delay in lodging FIR. There is no medical evidence on record against the accused. Under such circumstances the allegations made by the complainant against the accused cannot be believed. The conduct on the part of complainant in obtaining custody of the daughters and thereafter lodging complaint against the accused, does not appear to be ordinary conduct. From the entire allegations in the FIR and the evidence on record it clearly appears that the complainant lodged false complaint against the accused who is her husband to get rid of him. There is nothing on record to prove allegations levelled against the accused. On the contrary from the very allegations in the FIR and evidence on record it is clear that the accused is J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 29­15 ­ 377,376,506, 4,12.doc .....12/­ ..12.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 29/2015.. Exh.41.. falsely involved in this offence. Hence answering point Nos.1 to 3 in the negative, following order is passed. ORDER 1. Accused Pintya Rajaram Jadhav is hereby acquitted u/s.235(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure for offence punishable u/s.377, 376, 506 of the Indian Penal Code and section 4 and 12 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 2. The accused is in jail. He be released forthwith if not required in any other case or crime. 3. The muddemal property being worthless be destroyed after the appeal period is over. 4. Accused is directed to furnish personal bond of Rs.15,000/­ in terms of sec.437­A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Sd/­... Thane. (P.P.Jadhav) District Judge­6 and Date : 03.10.2017. Addl. Sessions Judge, Thane. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 29­15 ­ 377,376,506, 4,12.doc ...../­

.. 1 .. bail no.510/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 510 of 2015 This application is filed by applicant Suraj Chatrapal Rajoria for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. I­72/2015 registered at Vartaknagar police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 354(d), 323, 504 of I.P.C. and section 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short 'P.O.C.S.O. Act''). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant outraged modesty of the complainant victim girl. It is further contended and argued that no such incident has happened. It is further contended and argued that there was love affair between the applicant and the victim girl and her parents were against their relations and only because of pressure from the father of victim, who is an active member of political party, the applicant is falsely implicated in this crime. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co­operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that the accused was always following the victim and he used to make indecent gestures with intent that said gestures shall be seen by her and also used to sing indecent songs in a manner that the victim shall hear the same. It is further contended and argued that even on 02.02.2015 when the complainant was watching in the house of .. 2 .. bail no.510/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) one Alka Jadhav in her locality, the accused came out of he house and made obscene gestures with intention to cause molestation of the victim girl. It is further submitted that the victim girl and the accused are residing in same locality and looking to the allegations if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant repeating the offence and even the applicant threatening the victim girl and other prosecution witnesses cannot be ruled out. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 354(d), 323, 504 of I.P.C. and section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act with the allegation that he made obscene gestures towards the victim aged 16 years whenever they came across in the way and on 02.02.2015 also the accused repeated the offence by standing outside the house of one Alka Jadhav when the victim was watching TV inside the said house. But then it is contended on behalf of applicant that the parents of the victim were against the love affair between applicant and victim and therefore he is falsely implicated with the allegations of molestation of the victim. In such circumstance whether the allegations against the accused are genuine or whether the accused is falsely implicated in this case due to pressure of father of the victim, would be the question to be decided on merits. Even nothing is to be recovered from the applicant/accused. .. 3 .. bail no.510/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) 4] It is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. 5] In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 6] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 7] Then, it has also to be mentioned that the investigation in the matter though almost completed, the charge sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. .. 4 .. bail no.510/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) 8] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Suraj Chatrapal Rajoria is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ The applicant/accused shall attend the concerned police station on every Monday between 5.00 p.m. to 7.00 p.m. and shall co­operate in investigation. He shall not not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and the prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 12.03.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.

1 Special Case No.32/2015 (Judgment) Presented on : 23.02.2015 Registered on : 23.02.2015 Decided on : 27.09.2017 Duration Y M D 02 07 04 IN THE COURT OF SESSIONS JUDGE­1 & SPECIAL JUDGE [POCSO] ACT, THANE AT : THANE (Presided over by V.V.Bambarde, Additional Sessions Judge­1 & Special Judge (POCSO) Act, Thane ) SPECIAL CASE NO.32/2015 EXH.No. 22. State of Maharashtra ( Through Thanenagar Police Stn.) ...Complainant Vs. 1] Shaharukh Saleem Kasmani, Age :- 18 years, Occ.: Education, 2] Saif Saleem Kasmani, Age :­ 18 years, Occ.: Education, …. Accused Both R/at : 201, Suraj Apartment, 'B' Wing, Mahagiri, Thane [W]. Offence Punishable Under Sec. 354­A (1)(i)of IPC and S.8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ Appearances : Shri. S.D.Londhe, Ld. Spl.P.P. for the State. Mr. Lande, Ld.Advocate for the accused. ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ 2 Special Case No.32/2015 (Judgment) :JUDGMENT: (Delivered on 27th day of September, 2017) 1] The accused in the Court dock are tried for offence under S. 354­ A (1)(i)of IPC and S.8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 on the accusation of having been sexually harassed and sexually assaulted a minor victim girl, aged 12 years. 2] Case of prosecution, in brief, is that a victim girl is resident of Saidarshan Apartment, Rajashree Park, Mahagiri, Thane. The victim girl was studying in 9th standard and was attending her tuition class nearby. The accused are boys from nearby area and were visiting Moin Sameer Kasmani, a resident of their building. The accused Moin Kasmani, Shahrukh Kasmani and Saifu Kasmani used to sit on the road opposite to their window. They blew whistles by looking at victim girl. Accused were taking name of victim girl and teasing her. Accused were asking the younger brother of victim girl “where was the victim girl”. At 10.30 a.m. on 03/09/2014, the victim girl was proceeding towards tuition class. The accused Moin and Shahrukh blew whistles. Moin hold hand of victim girl and asked “brus fnuks a l s dgkW a Fkh] dgkW a tk jgh gS ”. The victim girl frightened, gave jerk and proceeded to the tuition class. Mother of victim girl rushed to the police station and lodged complaint. 3] On the receipt of complaint, PSO of Thanenagar Police Station registered offence under S. 354­A(1)(i) of IPC and under S. 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. P.C. Pawar went to the spot and prepared spot panchanama. Investigation was taken up by Lady API Shraddha Waydande. API Shraddha Waydande arrested the accused. She recorded statement of victim girl, collected birth certificate of victim girl. She also 3 Special Case No.32/2015 (Judgment) collected N.c. filed against accused earlier. It has transpired in her investigation that accused committed offence hence on completion of investigation, she filed charge sheet in the Court. 4] This Court has framed charge against the accused ( Exh.2 ) for offence under Sec. 354­A (1)(i) of IPC and S. 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. The contents of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular to which they pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 5] Prosecution examined in all five witnesses to bring home the guilt of accused. Rizwana Rafik Qureshi (P.W.1) and Rafik Gulam Qureshi (P.W.2) are parents of the victim girl (P.W.3). Rizwana Qureshi (P.W.1) lodged report – Exh. 8. Shraddha Waydande (P.W.4) is investigating officer and Vinay Patil (P.W.5) who produced birth extract – Exh. 18 of the victim girl. 6] The defence of the accused as constructed in cross­examination and statements under Sec. 313 Cr.P.C. is that the father of victim was assaulted Moin with knife so the present false report is lodged against them to implicate them. 7] I have heard Ld. Special P.P. for the State and Ld. advocate for the accused. 8] Following points arise for my determination with my findings thereon for reasons to follow: 4 Special Case No.32/2015 (Judgment) POINTS FINDINGS 01. Does the prosecution prove that on …. In the negative. 23/09/2014 at 10.30 hours, on road in front of Saidarshan Apartment, Mahagiri, Thane, the accused, in furtherance of their common intention, sexually harassed victim girl by physical contact and advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures? 02 Does prosecution prove that on the same, …. In the negative. day, date, time and place, the accused sexually assaulted the victim girl, a minor aged 12 years? 03 What order ? Accused are acquitted as per final order. REASONS 9] AS TO POINT NOS.1 & 2 : I would like to discuss both the points together. The victim girl and her parents Rizwana (P.W.1) and Rafik (P.W.2) are resident of Mahagiri, Thane. The accused are residing in nearby area. They deposed that the accused used to come to the house of Moin, who is residing in their building. The accused used to blow whistles and tease victim girl. They used to molest the girl. They used to enquire with the younger brother of victim girl viz. Rehan in respect of the victim. 10] It has come in their evidence that at 10.30 a.m. on 03/09/2014, victim girl was proceeding to tuition. It has specifically come in the evidence of victim (P.W.3) that accused were blowing whistles on seeing her. Accused Moin caught her hand and asked her “ dgkW a tk jgh gks ] brus fnu dgkW a Fkh ”. The victim girl deposed that she did not reply and rescued herself. She went 5 Special Case No.32/2015 (Judgment) to tuition class. 11] Shraddha Waydande (P.W.4), I.O., deposed that she has collected spot panchanama. She collected birth certificate of victim girl. Vinay Patil (P.W.5) has brought birth certificate of the victim girl­ Exh. 18. It shows that victim girl born on 25/07/2001. 12] I have heard Ld. Advocate for the accused and Ld. APP. The accused Moin was stabbed and Rafik (P.W.2) was put behind the bars. The girl was alleged to be molested on 03/09/2014 and an FIR lodged by mother Rizwana (P.W.1) on 06/09/2014. There are allegations that the girl was teased by the accused with juvenile offender. They had inimical terms and so earlier quarrel resulted in injury to the accused Moin. The incident of 10.30 a.m. on 03/09/2014 was firstly alleged to have reported by a girl to her tuition teacher. The said tuition teacher is not examined by prosecution. Prosecution has not explained why there was delay of three days. The victim girl said that Moin caught her hand and asked “ dgkW a tk jgh gks ] brus fnu dgkW a Fkh ”. She rescued herself and went ahead. To establish offence under S. 8 of POCSO Act, prosecution has to establish that there has to be sexual harassment to the victim girl. There has to be utterance of word with sexual intent. It appears that the accused Moin hold hand of victim girl and asked “brus fnuks a l s dgkW a Fkh] dgkW a tk jgh gS ”. The word does not express any sexual intent. There is no touch to such a body part where the girl will fell insulted. There is mere holding of hand. The utterance of word does not explicit sexual overtures. It has been discussed above that there is delay in lodging FIR. There is animosity between parties. The main incident is not coloured with any sexual remarks and intent. Hence, I have no option but to extend benefit of doubt to the 6 Special Case No.32/2015 (Judgment) accused. In the result, I answer Point No. 1 and 2 in negative and pass following order : ORDER 1] The accused Shaharukh Saleem Kasmani and Saif Saleem Kasmani are hereby acquitted of offence under S. 354­A (1)(i) of IPC and S. 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] Their bail bonds stand cancelled. 3] Accused shall furnish P.R. bond of Rs. 15,000/­ each in view of proviso 437(A) of Cr.P.C. Thane ( V.V.Bambarde ) Dt. :­ 27.09.2017 Additional Sessions Judge­1, vsi­p.c. & Special Judge (POCSO)Act, Thane. 7 Special Case No.32/2015 (Judgment)

1 Bail No.464/16 (order below Exhibit 1) Criminal Bail Application No. 464/2016. Parvez Niyaz Hashmi .. Applicant versus The State of Maharashtra Through Kashimira Police Station .. Non­applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 1] By this application the applicant is seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C., who was arrested on 04/02/2016 by Kashimira Police Station in connection with C.R.No. I­78/2016 registered for an offence punishable under section 376 of I.P.C. and section 4 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Mr. R.K.Shukla for the applicant/ accused and learned A.P.P. Mrs. H.A.Deshmukh for State. I.O. present with case diary. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 04/02/2016 at the instance of the informant/mother of victim­girl aged about 4 years with an indictment that the accused who is the father of victim girl committed sexual assault on the victim girl by inserting his finger in her vagina and anus. 4] The learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the 2 Bail No.464/16 (order below Exhibit 1) applicant­accused is falsely implicated. He submitted that accused is husband of informant. Informant is having matrimonial dispute as accused used to come late from his work. He further submitted that informant was asking for divorce and custody of the daughter, which was refused by accused and therefore informant went to reside with her parents and to make the case for divorce and for custody of child she lodged false complaint against the accused. The Learned counsel for accused also submitted that there is delay of 15 days without any explanation. He further submitted that the F.I.R. is after thought only to pressurize the accused to fulfill demand of complainant for divorce. There is no medical report on record. He further submitted that accused is permanent resident of the address given in the application and is ready to abide by any conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing him on bail. 5] Per contra, the learned A.P.P. strongly opposed the application on the ground that offence is serious in respect of minor victim­girl aged about 4 years, who is a daughter of accused. She further submitted that for small matrimonial dispute no mother would lodge such a false complaint. She further submitted that accused is father of victim girl and involved in heinous offence. He misused the custody of the child. The investigation is in progress. There are chances of tampering of witnesses and prayed for rejection of application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R. it appears that there are serious allegations against the accused, who is non else than the father of minor victim­girl aged 4 years. From F.I.R. itself it appears 3 Bail No.464/16 (order below Exhibit 1) that accused and informant are having matrimonial dispute and therefore she had left the house of accused and staying with her parents. On 18/01/2016 victim­girl told her mother the she is missing her father, therefore, informant allowed victim­girl to talk with her father on mobile. On 19/01/2016 around 2.30 hours accused took victim­girl at his house and dropped her around 12 hours. On 20/01/2016 victim­girl was not walking properly. Since then till 26/01/2016 accused used to take his daughter and used to drop her on the next day. On 03/02/2016 the teacher of victim­girl informed the informant that victim­girl is not talking and she is having difficulty to walk. Thereafter informant requested the accused to take the victim­girl to doctor, however, he refused. Therefore, informant by taking the victim­girl in confidence asked her and on that victim­girl disclosed that her father inserted his finger in her vagina and anus for four to five times and also threatened her not to disclose it to anybody. Thereafter informant lodged the report. Thus F.I.R. disclose a serious offence. The investigation is in progress and at nascent stage. As accused is the father of minor victim­girl, therefore, in peculiar facts of case the apprehension of learned Spl.P.P. about tampering of witnesses and pressurizing the victim­girl is well founded. Thus, no case made out for releasing the accused on bail. Hence, I pass following order :­ ORDER The application stands rejected. Thane. Date : 24/02/2016. (Ms. U.M. Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act), Thane.

Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­006591­2014 Special (POCSO) Case No.52/14 Received on : 25.02.2014 Registered on : 25.02.2014 Decided on : 21.01.2019 Duration : 4Ys.10Ms.27Ds. IN THE COURT OF D.J.­1 & ADDL. SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE (Presided over by Hemant M. Patwardhan) Special (POCSO Case No. 52/14 Exh.No. 1. State of Maharashtra. (Nerul Police station) ..Complainant V/s. Abhishek Deepak Salunkhe. Age 19 years Residence, Building no.23, Room No. 104, Sector 10, Nerul, Navi Mumbai. ..Accused Appearance:­ APP Smt. Moholkar for the State. Advocate Shri. Kasale for the accused. JUDGMENT (Delivered on this 21st day of January 2019 ) Accused Abhishek Deepak Salunkhe was facing trial on following facts:­ 1 to 11 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­006591­2014 Special (POCSO) Case No.52/14 1] That on 14.08.2013 during 17.00 hours to 21.00 hours at Sector 10, Nerul, Navi Mumbai, accused took minor girl aged about 15 years, in newly constructed building, and outraged her modesty by kissing her and by pressing her breast. At that time as victim was minor within the meaning of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, said Act of the accused was considered to be within the purview of section 7 of said Act. Therefore, on the complaint lodged by father of the victim, an offence punishable under section 354 of IPC read with section 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 was registered against him. On completion of investigation he was charge­sheeted. 2] My learned Predecessor was pleased to frame charge below Exh.2 and has certified that contents of said charge were read over and explained to accused in vernacular. Accused pleaded not guilty and claim to be tried. His defence was of total denial. 3] As the accused has claim to be tried, prosecution has then proceeded to examine complainant, victim, panch witness on the spot panchanama and finally I.O. as PW 1 to 4 respectively. Statement of accused was then recorded under section 313 of Cr.P.C. Accused has initially raised the defence of his false implication on the ground of love affairs with the 2 to 11 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­006591­2014 Special (POCSO) Case No.52/14 victim which her parents disliked and as complainant is in police department has misused his office to implicate him in false case which was then reiterated in statement under section 313 of Cr.P.C. 4] Arguments of rival advocates were heard. Learned APP Smt. Moholkar has categorically pointed out that complainant and victim were material witnesses and they have supported allegation of prosecution and as each of them have corroborated the facts, the same are sufficient to establish the guilt of accused. She has therefore, requested to convict accused as per the charge. Per contra, defence has pointed out that an important aspect of this matter is delay caused in lodging first information report which itself goes to substantiate defence. According to submissions the incident was allegedly occurred on 14.08.2013 which though was revealed to complainant on 27.09.2013 he did not lodge the complaint immediately but has lodged it on 04.10.2013 without there being any explanation as to why it was lodged at such belated stage. Hence, according to learned defence advocate, said fact itself is sufficient to discard the allegation and to accept the defence as probable. He has then pointed out that there is nothing on record to substantiate that the victim was minor within the meaning of 3 to 11 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­006591­2014 Special (POCSO) Case No.52/14 Section 8 of POCSO Act to even prosecuted accused under any of the provisions of Act. To substantiate the arguments he has relied upon various Judgments referred in pursis Exh.42. He has then categorically pointed out that complainant's version has not been corroborated on material points by the victim and thus, the evidence cannot be said to be consistent in nature. He has pointed out that as per the admission of the panch witness spot of incident was not lonely place where any such incident can be easily committed and nobody will try to involve himself in an incident adjacent to the house of the complainant herself. Thus, according to him said fact also supports the defence. He has therefore requested to acquit accused from all allegations. 5] After having heard the rival advocates, I have gone through the citations relied upon by the defence which were more or less on the point that if the prosecution's evidence is silent about date of birth and such proof is not properly established then prosecution under any section of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act is not probable. Hon'ble Their Lordship in the aforesaid citations have also observed that when the basis foundation facts are not established beyond reasonable doubt, the verson of prosecution witnesses have to be discarded. On the basis of aforesaid facts and rival advocates and on the background of observations of Hon'ble their Lordship in the reported Judgment supra, following points 4 to 11 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­006591­2014 Special (POCSO) Case No.52/14 arose for my consideration and I record my findings against each of them for the reasons noted below :­ Sr.N Points Findings 1] Does the prosecution prove that on 14.08.2013 between 17.00 ..Negative. hours to 21.00 hours at Sector 10, Nerul, Navi Mumbai, in the newly constructed building accused took minor victim girl aged about 15 years, who is daughter of the complainant and kissed her and also pressed her breast and thereby outraged her modesty and thereby committed an offence punishable under Section 354 of Indian Penal Code? 2] Does the prosecution prove that accused on the same date, time ..Negative. and place touched the breast of the victim minor girl with sexual intent and thereby committed an offence of sexual assault on her which is punishable under Section 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act? 3] What order? ..Accused is acquitted as per final order. REASONS As to point no.1 to 3 :­ 6] All these points are interlinked with each other and are consider at once. In the instant case it was alleged by the prosecution that actual incident had occurred on 14.08.2013 when the accused has allegedly outraged the modesty of the victim and victim was minor within the meaning of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 while lodging the complaint, it was lodged not only under section 354 of IPC but also under section 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual 5 to 11 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­006591­2014 Special (POCSO) Case No.52/14 Offences Act, 2012. Thus, the prosecution was require to establish that said offences were really committed by consistent and reliable evidence. On perusal of record, no doubt complainant has categorically deposed in terms of prosecution's case and has given minute details as to how accused has outraged modesty of the victim. However, all his deposition was based on facts narrated to him by the victim. Thus, evidence and deposition of victim was of material importance. However, when deposition was recorded she did not put forth fact as minutely as complainant did. Thus, it was argued by the defence that evidence is inconsistent and unreliable. 7] The defence of the accused of his false implication due to love affair between victim and accused which complainant did not like and as he was in police department he has misused his office to implicate the accused in the matter. The said defence was specifically put forth during cross­ examination of both the witness no.1 and 2. In the instant case fact which goes to the root of the matter is delay in lodging the complaint. The incident allegedly occured on 14.08.2013 and first information report was lodged on 04.10.2013. The explanation put forth by the complainant while lodging the complaint was initially on the date of incident, the victim has mislead him and did not narrate true incident of that date itself but when he has kept watch on her on 27.09.2013 and was 6 to 11 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­006591­2014 Special (POCSO) Case No.52/14 found her talking with the accused had taken her in confidence and asked her as to what actual incident had occurred, she has stated that accused has taken her to an under construction building and has outraged her modesty by kissing her, by moving his hand on her breast and by inserting hand in her cloths. Even his explanation is accepted that he was unaware of the fact till 27.09.2013 he did not lodge complaint immediately on 27.09.2013 but had lodged it on 04.10.2013. There is absolutely no explanation as to why the complainant has kept mum in respect of that matter from 27.09.2013 to 04.10.2013. Therefore, his said conduct with unexplained delay itself create doubt in respect of occurrence of incident. 8] It was the prosecution's case that accused had taken her to under construction building adjacent to her own house. Panch witness was examined in order to prove the panchanama and accordingly panchanama was proved. However, during cross­examination panch has admitted that said construction site is open from all the sides and anybody passes can easily see what going on in said construction site. On such construction site it was alleged that the accused was with the victim for about 3 1/2 hours. That fact itself creates doubt in respect of occurrence of the said incident. If we consider that accused has really taken the victim to the particular spot and has really outraged her modesty after having reached there then the 7 to 11 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­006591­2014 Special (POCSO) Case No.52/14 natural conduct of the victim would be of leaving that spot immediately by scolding accused but in the instant case it was the allegation of the prosecution that they were there on the spot for about 3 1/2 hours then it is really difficult to accept that a girl whose modesty has been outraged would stay there without creating a scene of the said fact on the spot itself. Further a person who is in police department will not be able to take the victim in confidence on that day itself when she has narrated altogether different facts after her return to house late in the evening. He being in police department first immediately expected to initiate action for her daughter being confined for sometime in particular car by a Muslim couple. However, even his act of non­approaching concern police for making a complaint for said fact as well, itself goes to show that he wanted to suppress certain facts from this court. 9] Further if incident dated 14.08.2013 was accepted by him as it was stated by the victim then his further conduct of putting a watch on her after about 1 1/2 months on the victim is unaccepatable. He has stated that he has kept watch on the victim on 27.09.2013 and then found the victim talking with the accused person and as he himself has slapped his daughter she got frightened and suffered temperature and then she was 8 to 11 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­006591­2014 Special (POCSO) Case No.52/14 taken in confidence after 2­3 days and she has narrated the incident, appears to be concocted story. Said fact no where referred in first information report. Said fact never corroborated by the victim as well. Thus, facts which was stated before the court for the first time are improvement, reason behind it is obviously to implicate the accused anyhow in the matter. Thus, if all said facts are considered on the background of the observations of Hon'ble his Lordship in the aforesaid rulings then none of those facts are either consistent or reliable. As the prosecution evidence is not consistent and reliable presumption under section 29 and 30 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act cannot be pressed into service or cannot be raised itself as observed by Hon'ble Their Lordship in above referred case. Once the court has declined to raise said presumption burden was never shifted on the accused to disporve the said fact. 10] However, in the instant case accused by pointing out the facts that there was inordinate delay without explaining about lodging of the complaint at such belated stage, contradictory statements of the witnesses on the material points etc. are sufficient to discard the prosecution evidence and to accept the defence as probable. Having regards to aforesaid facts, it can be safely inferred that though the onus was never shifted on the accused to disprove the prosecution's case, if his 9 to 11 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­006591­2014 Special (POCSO) Case No.52/14 aforesaid defence is considered that seems more probable than that of the allegation of the prosecution. Having said so I do not hesitate to discard said evidence and held that prosecution has miserably failed to establish any of the allegation against accused. 11] Before parting with the findings I would like to add that defence has rightly pointed out by relying upon aforesaid Judgment that unless prosecution has established the victim was minor within the meaning of the act, the prosecution under that Act is not justified. In the instant case, except bare allegation that victim was around 15 years of age, prosecution did not either adduce evidence of the said fact or has produced any document to prove the particular fact. Having said so, I do not hesitate to record my findings that even prosecution has failed to establish that victim was minor within the meaning of the said Act. Thus prosecution under that Act is also untenable. Hence, I record my findings against point no.1 and 2 in negative and proceed to pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused is acquitted from the offence punishable under sections 354 of IPC read with section 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 10 to 11 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­006591­2014 Special (POCSO) Case No.52/14 2012. 2] Bail bond of accused shall accordingly stands cancelled. 3] Accused is directed to execute P.R. and S.B. of Rs.10,000/­ as per amended provisions of section 437(A) of Cr.P.C. and bonds so executed shall remain in force for the period of six months from the date of its execution. 4] Proceeding is accordingly closed. Thane (Hemant M.Patwardhan) Date: 21.01.2019 D.J.­1 & Additional Sessions Judge, Thane. 11 to 11

Case No.58/2016 (Delivered on this 8th day of June, 2017) 1] The accused is charge­sheeted for the offence punishable under section 509 of I.P.C. and under section 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act (POCSO). 2] The prosecution in brief alleged that the complainant Zarina Abdul Karim Ulade was residing in Rediant Society, Building No.1, Flat No.303, Nayanagar, Miraroad (E) alongwith son Adul Vahid aged 17 years and daughter Amrin aged 11 years. Her husband Abdul Karim was serving in Dubai. 3] It is alleged that daughter Amrin was learning in 6th standard in Banegar English High School in 2015. On 26/12/2015 Amrin attended the school and returned at about 10.45 a.m. being Saturday. It is alleged that at about 1.45 p.m. daughter went to the house of her friend Maimuna. She received a phone call from the house that “ Afrin ke sath kuch to huva hai ”. It is alleged that when she came Afrin was frightened and weeping and on enquiry stated that she was waiting for about 2.45 hours outside the Masjid for her friend Maimuna, by the side building at first floor from the window one person gave flying kiss and shown his private part by opening the zip of pant. That person was .....3/­ 3 Spl. Case No.58/2016 wearing spectacles aged 30 to 35 years. He thereafter ran away. 4] She lodged complaint. Concerned police registered crime No.II­25/2015 under section 509 of I.P.C. & Sec.12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act (POCSO). During investigation spot panchanama was drawn, statement of victim was recorded in question­answer form, statements of other witnesses were recorded, statement of victim U/Sec.164 of Cr.P.C. was recorded, photographs were collected, so also the copy of birth certificate of victim and bonafide certificate. On conclusion of investigation chargesheet was submitted. 5] On hearing learned APP and defence counsel charge below Exh.5 was framed under section 509 of I.P.C. and 12 of POCSO Act and same when read over and explained to the accused in vernacular he has denied it vide his statement Exh. 6. 6] The prosecution examined in all three witnesses. The accused did not examine himself nor led evidence. 7] From the statement under section 313 of Cr.P.C. .....4/­ 4 Spl. Case No.58/2016 and evidence on record the defence of accused is of denial. 8] I have heard learned APP and learned deence counsel. 9] In these circumstances following points arise for my determination and I record my finding to them for the reasons mentioned hereinafter :­ Sr. POINTS FINDINGS No. 1] Whether prosecution proved that on In the 26/12/2015 at about 14.45 hours, in negative. the campus of Rediyant Co­Op.So., opposite Rediyant Masjid , in the shade, Mira Road (E), Dist. Thane, within the jurisdiction of Nayanagar Police Station, accused was intending to insult the modesty of the daughter of complainant aged 11 years by making some gestures, intending that such gesture shall be seen by her ? 2] Whether it is proved that on the said In the date, time and place and during the affirmative. course of same transaction accused committed the offence of sexual assault on the daughter of complainant aged 11 years ? 3] What order ? As per final order .....5/­ 5 Spl. Case No.58/2016 REASONS POINT NOS. 1 AND 2 : 10] For the sake of convenient discussion points are clubbed. 11] The prosecution examined P.W.1­Zarina Abdul Karim Ulade, the mother of victim Amrin, P.W.2­ Amrin Abdul Karim Ulade, the victim girl and P.W.3­ Pravinkumar Sonbarao Salunkhe, the investigating officer. 12] Learned A.P.P. submitted that offence of sexual assault is found proved, as why a girl of 11 years would tell lie. 13] The defence counsel submitted that it is a false case and it is abuse of process of law as spot was not visible. 14] The evidence of P.W.1­Zarina Abdul Karim Ulade shows that her husband was serving at Dubai. Her victim daughter Amrin was studying in 6th standard in Banere Ghar English High School. On 26/12/2015 her daughter Amrin had been with her friend Maimuna. She saw in front .....6/­ 6 Spl. Case No.58/2016 building. One person by name Farhan gave flying kiss and shown the private part by opening zip of the pant. She lodged complaint Exh.8. She is a formal witness and admitted that she has not seen the incident. She admitted police have shown the photo of accused on mobile. 15] The only material evidence is of P.W.2 Amrin Abdul Karim Ulade. According to her, her date of birth is 1/1/2005 and she was studying in 6th standard. There is no dispute about this fact. The copy of birth certificate is at Exh.13 and copy of bonafide certificate is at Exh.14. She is on the face of record a minor on the date of offence. 16] P.W.2 Amrin further stated that her friend Maimuna had been to Masjid and she was waiting for her. Her attention has gone to one building. One person was giving flying kiss and by removing zip shown the private part. She identified the accused in the court. 17] She admitted that the place where she was standing and the building in which uncle was standing was at long distance. The actual distance has not come and it may be possible that a child may has a vision of long distance. She denied that police shown the photograph of .....7/­ 7 Spl. Case No.58/2016 accused to her. 18] The last witness is a investigating officer. He drawn the spot panchanama Exh.11, recorded statements of the witnesses, collected photographs and submitted that chargesheet. 19] The photographs are not produced on record and therefore they are not considered. 20] The offence of insulting modesty prescribed in Sec.509 of I.P.C. requires the act of any gesture with an intention to insult the modesty by uttering a word or making a sign or exehibiting an object and this gesture or object may be seen by a woman. From the evidence, the offence U/Sec. 509 of I.P.C. does not get attracted. 21] The provision of Sec.11 of P.O.C.S.O. Act requires prescribed sexual harassment. Clause (i) mentions that appearance of a word, making of sound, gesture or exhibiting an object or a part of body with intention that sound shall be heard, gesture or object shall be seen by child. 22] In the present case P.W.2­ Amrin has categorically .....8/­ 8 Spl. Case No.58/2016 stated that accused has opened the zip of the pant and shown the private part to her. The evidence of child witness is to be considered with abundant precaution to rule out the possibility of tutoring. At the same time, she had identified the accused. There is no dispute that she is minor. There is no dispute that she was present. It appears that there were some attempt as Ld.defence counsel submitted that a person has liberty to do anything with the four corners of his room. However, since the identification of accused , presence of accused is not disputed, her evidence is found partly believable. Therefore, the point No.1 is answered in negative and point No.2 is partly in the affirmative. 23] It is here I have heared the accused on the point of sentence. He requested that he may be excused. He is only earning member and handicapped. Blind father is depending upon him. Under the facts and circumstances and request made by accused, following sentence would be justified. Hence, the order :­ ORDER 1] Accused Farhan Suleman Patel is convicted for the offence punishable under section 12 of POCSO Act as per sec. 235(2) of Cr.P.C. and sentence to suffer S.I. till rising of the court and also fine of Rs.200/­ i.d. to suffer S.I. for 7 days. .....9/­ 9 Spl. Case No.58/2016 2] Accused is acquitted of the offence punishable under section 509 of I.P.C. as per section 235(1) of Cr.P.C. 3] Accused is on bail. His bail bonds are cancelled. Thane.
