.. 1 .. bail no.532/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 532 of 2015 This application is filed by applicant Rampal Ramdayal Gautam for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. I­54/2015 registered at Rabale police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 363, 366, 34 of I.P.C. and section 12 and 17 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant/ accused with the help of other accused persons kidnapped the minor victim girl under false assurance of marriage from lawful guardianship of her parents. It is further contended and argued that the applicant is already married and accused no.2 is his wife and therefore no question of he kidnapping the victim girl for performing marriage. It is further contended and argued that the applicant is not F.I.R. named accused. It is further contended and argued that the applicant is falsely implicated in this crime by the complainant on account of personal vengeance. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co­operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that the applicant/ accused gave false assurance of marriage to the victim girl and by taking disadvantage of her young age, he kidnapped her and taken her away from her house. It is further submitted that in such .. 2 .. bail no.532/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) circumstance if the applicant/ accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl and the prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 363, 366 read with section 34 of I.P.C. and section 12 and 17 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, it appears that the applicant/accused had been arrested on 18.02.2015 and he is not stated to be F.I.R. named accused. Even as is clear the applicant is stated to be married and co­accused Fatima is his wife and also having child and it is contended that he is falsely implicated in the crime and there is no question of applicant kidnapping the girl with intention to perform marriage. In such circumstance the aspect as to whether the allegations against the accused are true or not, would be the question to be decided on merits. Even nothing is to be recovered from the applicant/accused. 4] Then, it is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. 5] In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond .. 3 .. bail no.532/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 6] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 7] Then, it has also to be mentioned that the investigation in the matter though almost completed, the charge sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 8] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Rampal Ramdayal Gautam is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ The applicant/accused shall attend the concerned police station on every Saturday between 10.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon .. 4 .. bail no.532/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) till filing of the charge sheet and shall co­operate in investigation. He shall not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and the prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this Court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 18.03.2015 (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.

.. 1 .. bail 537/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 537/2015 This application is filed by applicant Mehboob Umar Naik for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no.I­184/2015 registered at Mumbra police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 377, 498A, 323, 504, 506 of I.P.C. and section 3(a) and 4 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the accused committed sexual assault on his own son in unnatural manner and had also subjected the mother of the victim boy i.e. complainant, wife of applicant, to cruelty. It is further contended and argued that no such incident of sexual assault has happened. It is further contended and argued that there is matrimonial dispute between the applicant/accused and the complainant and for that reason the applicant is falsely implicated in this crime. It is further submitted that since before the alleged incident the accused and complainant are staying separate and it is falsely contended by the complainant that at the time of incident the victim boy and complainant were staying together with the applicant/accused. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co­operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that during the .. 2 .. bail 537/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) period of cohabitation the accused has subjected the complainant to mental and physical cruelty by saying that during marriage the complainant has not brought anything by way of gifts. It is further contended and argued that the victim boy namely Arhan is the son of accused and complainant and the accused had committed sexual on Arhan by inserting penis into the mouth of Arhan and had also threatened the boy not to disclose about such act otherwise he will be killed and the accused had committed such type of assault 2 – 3 times. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim boy and the complainant. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 377, 498A, 323, 504, 506 of I.P.C. and section 3(a) and 4 of P.O.C.S.O. Act with the allegation of very serious nature under section 377 of I.P.C. that the accused had committed offence in unnatural manner by inserting his penis into the mouth of his minor son, it has to be mentioned that the complaint appear to have been lodged by his own wife i.e. mother of the victim boy, and in the light of that the further fact is also very much material to note that besides section 377 of I.P.C., other offences under section 498A, 323, 504, 506 of I.P.C. and under P.O.C.S.O. Act also have been charged. In the light of that the contentions on behalf of applicant that there has been matrimonial dispute between the applicant/accused and his wife i.e. mother of the victim boy, since long and even earlier litigation .. 3 .. bail 537/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) in that regard also is going on between them if considered in the light of the documents produced on record alongwith application, it is clear that complaint under Protection of Women From Domestic Violence Act (hereinafter in short ''D. V. Act'') bearing no.29/2014 was filed by the mother of the boy much before the present complaint. 4] Even as is clear as per the contention of the applicant after his marriage with the complainant there was divorce by mutual consent (khula talakh) on 06.12.2007 and thereafter there has been re­union between them and they performed second nikah and then they were cohabiting together and a son was born. But thereafter the complainant i.e. his wife, had left the house after quarreling with him in April, 2011 alongwith all her ornaments and in spite of repeated requests by him she never returned back and as per his further contention he had even issued notices and since then there had no matrimonial relationship between them and she was staying alongwith her son at her parents' house and in spite of repeated notices and requests by him she did not resume the cohabitation. Even it is also clear from the documents produced on record that the complainant had been making complaints in writing against the applicant and even the applicant had also filed complaint to Commissioner of Police apprehending false complaint and arrest on the basis of such complaint by his wife much before the present complaint in February, 2014. 5] It is thus clear that there has been prolonged litigation and dispute between the parties and in the light of that it is contended that the present complaint is filed by the complainant .. 4 .. bail 537/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) only with a view to see that the applicant/accused is sent to jail and such false allegations are made. Then, from the perusal of the complaint also it is clear that in the complaint also it is mentioned by the complainant that she had been staying at her parents' house alongwith son but since July, 2014 she had resumed cohabitation and her son was staying with them and then the alleged incident of insertion of penis by the applicant into the mouth of the son alleged to have taken place. But in the light of the fact that as per contention of the applicant after the complainant left the house she did not resume cohabitation and even in the light of further fact that in April, 2014 the complainant had filed petition for redressal under provisions of D. V. Act as rightly submitted on behalf of applicant/accused unless some cogent and reliable proof is brought on record to show that the parties resumed cohabitation in July, 2014 as alleged in the complaint, it cannot be said at this stage that at the time of alleged incident in January, 2015 the complainant and son were staying with the applicant. 6] Even it appears that the alleged incident stated to have taken place in January, 2015 but the complaint is lodged at a very belated stage on 14th February, 2015 and no explanation appear to have been offered by the complainant for such delay. No doubt, in such type of offences the delay in lodging the complaint may not be taken seriously or fatal to the prosecution case. But then, in the light of the peculiar facts of the present case when there has been a strained relationship between the complainant and the applicant/ accused and when proceeding under D. V. Act is still stated to be pending and when there is no prima facie material to show about the aspect that the complainant resumed cohabitation with the .. 5 .. bail 537/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) applicant/accused, the delay in lodging the complaint in regard to such serious offence assumes importance and at this stage only it can be said that that create doubt in mind about very allegation made in the complaint. Then, in any case the applicant has been in jail since 22.02.2015 and after the initial period of police custody he has been remanded to Magisterial custody. 7] Then, it is well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. 8] In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 9] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 10] Then, it has also to be mentioned that the investigation in the matter is though almost completed the charge sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation .. 6 .. bail 537/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) and submit the charge sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 11] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Mr. Mehboob Umar Naik is released on P.R. bond of Rs.25,000/­ [rupees twenty five thousand only] with one or two sureties in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ The applicant/accused shall attend the concerned police station on every Monday between 3.00 p.m. to 5.00 p.m. and shall co­operate in investigation. He shall not not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and the prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this Court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 11.03.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.

1 Bail No.544/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) Criminal Bail Application No. 544/2016 Dnyaneshwar Uttam Kotwade .. Applicant versus The State of Maharashtra Through Kashimira Police Station Nonapplicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 1] By this application the applicant is seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C., who was arrested on 27.12.2015 by Kashmira Police Station in connection with C.R.No.I-727/2015 registered for an offence punishable under section 376 of I.P.C. and section 4 & 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Mr. R.K. Shukla for the applicant/accused and learned Spl.P.P. Mrs. R.A.Navale for State. I.O. present. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 25.12.2015 at the instance of the informant/victim-girl aged 17 years with an indictment that since March, 2014 to 22.12.2015 accused harassing victim girl and on 22.12.2015 committed sexual assault on her. 4] The learned counsel for the applicant 2 Bail No.544/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) submitted that the first bail application of the accused was rejected on 27/01/2016. The accused is behind bar since 68 days. He is student of first year B.A. and his examination will be held on 08/03/2016 and as he is in jail, he is unable to appear for examination and because of which his education career will be spoiled. He submitted that there is no medical report about the rape. The investigation is almost completed. the accused is ready to abide by any condition imposed by the Court and even undertake not to enter in the vicinity of the victim- girl and prayed for releasing the accused on bail. 5] Per contra, the learned A.P.P. opposed the application submitting that the first bail application was rejected on merit. The investigation is still in progress. There is no change in circumstances. As accused is staying in same vicinity, there are chances of tampering of the witnesses and prayed for rejection of the application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R. it appears that the serious allegations about sexual assault on the minor girl are made. There appears to be two eye witnesses to the incident. It is matter of record that the first bail application of the accused vide Criminal Bail Application No.162/2016 was rejected on 27/01/2016 as there is prima-facie case against the accused and the investigation was in progress. The learned counsel for accused, on asking, pointed out that the change in circumstances is that the accused has to appear for the 3 Bail No.544/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) examination of B.A. The learned counsel for applicant also placed on record the examination schedule of Abhinav College of Arts, Commerce and Science. On perusal of the first bail application vide bail application No.162/2016. It appears that the ground about the accused has to attend the lecture and college in order to appear for academic year and to appear for examination to be held by the college authorities was raised as ground (q). The schedule of examination shows that exams are commencing from 10/03/2016 to 21/03/2016. However, there is specific note that schedule of examination is subject to change. Further it appears that the examination are internal examination conducted by the institution. Thus, considering the fact of the case, there is absolutely no material change in the circumstances. The investigation is still in progress. The accused is facing serious charge and there is prima-facie case against the accused. Thus, no material change in circumstances were pointed out to re-consider the bail application of the accused. Hence, application is devoid of merit and liable to be rejected. Hence I pass following order. ORDER The application is rejected. Thane. Date : 07/03/2016 (Ms. U.M. Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act), Thane.

Bhaisare, Additional Sessions Judge­2 and Special Judge (POCSO Act), Thane.] SPECIAL CASE (POCSO) NO. 35/2015. Exh. no. The State (Through Kapurbawdi Police Station) ..Complainant. V/s. Dilip Sunil Thakur, Age 22 years, Occ. Salesman, R/o. Siddhi­Vinayak chawl no. 1, Ganeshnagar, Church­road, Manpada, Thane. ..Accused. ___________________________________________________________ Appearances­ Learned A.P.P. Smt. Talhar, for the State. Learned Advocate Shri. Mote, for the accused. ___________________________________________________________ JUDGMENT (Delivered on 28.11.2017.) 1] Accused Dilip Sunil Thakur is facing trial for the offences punishable u/s. 376 of I.P.C. r/w. Section 3 punishable u/s. 4 of the 2 Spl. (POCSO) C. No. 35/2015. Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 2] It is the case of prosecution that accused resident of Ganeshnagar, Chitalsar, Manpada, had relations with victim girl. They used to visit each­other. Accused called the victim at his house and committed sexual intercourse on the pretext of marriage with her. Due to fear, she had not disclosed the same to anyone. Thereafter, again, after 15 days, he has committed rape on her. On 03.01.14, as usual, she went to her school. However, she was claiming pain in her stomach. It was informed by her teacher to the mother of victim. She was brought to her house and shifted to doctor. Doctor had examined the victim and found pregnancy. Thereafter, P.W.1 had lodged her report with Kapurbavdi police station, who had registered the offence vide C.R. no. 61/14. P.W.3 Vijay Takke had carried out investigation. During the course of investigation, he had recorded statement of victim. Accused was arrested. He rushed to the spot and recorded spot panchanama in presence of panchas. Accused was sent for his medical examination. Clothes of victim girl and accused were seized. School certificate of victim was obtained. She had blessed a baby. Blood sample of victim girl, baby and accused for the purpose of D.N.A. test were taken. D.N.A. kit was sent to C.A. Statements of witnesses were recorded. Victim was referred to the Magistrate as to give her statement u/s. 164 of Cr.P.C. After investigation, charge­sheet was submitted in the court. 3] Heard both sides. I framed the charge against the accused for the offences punishable under section 376 of I.P.C. r/w. Section 3 punishable u/s. 4 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act on 29/08/2017. Details of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular, to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be 3 Spl. (POCSO) C. No. 35/2015. tried. His defence is of total denial. 4] During trial, defence has admitted certain documents on record, i.e. medical examination report of accused by General Hospital, Thane (Exh.16), panchanama of seizure of clothes of accused (Exh.17), spot panchanama (Exh.18), Results of Analysis of Forensic Science Laboratory of D.N.A. of victim and accused (Exh.19), Examination Reports of Forensic Science Laboratory of clothes of victim and accused, blood, semen, pubic hairs, nail clippings of accused (Exh.20, 21), panchanama of seizure of clothes of victim (Exh. 27). 5] To bring home the guilt of the accused for the charges leveled against him, the prosecution has examined as many as three witnesses i.e. P.W. Name of witness Exh. Description No. No. 1] Jasoda Bhimsing 11 Mother of victim. Bhandari 2] Victim girl 13 Victim. 3] Vijay Mahadeo Takke 26 Investigating officer. 6] Accused did not enter into witness box. He has not examined defence witness. 7] Heard learned A.P.P. Smt. Talhar for the State and learned counsel Shri. Mote for the accused. Following points arise for my determination, which are being answered for the reasons given herein­ below. POINTS FINDINGS 1] Whether prosecution proved that prior No. 4 Spl. (POCSO) C. No. 35/2015. to 10 months of 21.02.2014 at about 20.00 hours, in the lane behind Siddhivinayak chawl, on giving false promise of marriage, accused had committed rape i.e. penetrative sexual assault on the minor daughter of complainant aged 15 years, making her pregnant of nine months ? 2] What order ? As per final order. REASONS POINT NO. 1 8] It has come in the evidence of P.W.2 victim that in the year 2014, she was studying in 9th standard. She was born on 02.07.99. In 2014, she was residing in Ganeshnagar, Chitalsar, Manpada. Accused was residing opposite to her house, hence, she had friendship with accused. They both were wandering on tour. In 2013, on one day, accused had called her to his house. So, she went to his house. He had established sexual relations with her in his house, on the promise of marriage. She had not disclosed the same with anyone. Again, after about 15 days, she was called by him at 8.00 p.m. Accordingly, at 8.00 p.m., she went to his house. On that night also, he had established sexual relations with her on the promise of marriage. 9] It has further come in her evidence that on 03.01.14, as usual, she went to her school. During class, she felt giddiness. Her Principal had informed about the same to her father on phone. Then, her mother came to school and took her to home. Thereafter, doctor had treated her and declared that she was carrying pregnancy of nine months. Then, on 5 Spl. (POCSO) C. No. 35/2015. 20.02.14, she was admitted in Swastik hospital. She delivered female baby. Police had recorded her statement. Her mother had lodged report. She was referred by police to Civil hospital, Thane. Doctor had examined her. Police had seized her clothes, took D.N.A. sample. Ld. J.M.F.C. had recorded her statement (Exh.14). 10] It has come in the cross­examination of P.W.2 victim that she came to know that her date of birth as 02.07.99 was stated by her mother in the school. In the year 2013, she was aged about 17­18 years. Due to love­ affair, she and accused were intended to marry with each­other. Accused had not forced her for sexual relations. They were ready to marry with each­other. She had no grievance against him. On the say of police, she had given statement before police and Ld. J.M.F.C. 11] P.W.1 Jasoda, mother of victim is not eye­witness to the incident. On 03.01.14, she received phone­call from the school of victim. Accordingly, she went there and brought victim to the house. Thereafter, she was referred to doctor. On examination, doctor had found that the victim was pregnant. Thereafter, on enquiry, victim had stated the incident to her. Consequently, this witness had lodged her report. Victim had also blessed a child. 12] P.W.1 Jasoda had stated the age of victim as 17 years in the year 2014, in which the incident was taken place. Victim has not stated her age. However, she had stated her date of birth as 02.07.99. 13] Victim had not stated the date of first incident. However, she had stated in her evidence that in the year 2014, she was studying in 9 th standard. Her statement u/s. 164 of Cr.P.C. was recorded vide Exh.14. In her statement, she had stated her age as 15 years. But, nowhere stated her 6 Spl. (POCSO) C. No. 35/2015. date of birth and date of first incident. Doctor is not examined. No school record is also placed on record. No birth certificate of victim is placed on record. Therefore, it is very difficult to hold that deceased was aged 14 years, 7 months and 19 days on the date of first incident. However, P.W.1 mother of victim had stated the age of victim as 17 years in the year 2014. Therefore, it creates doubt in the mind that victim was below 16 years of her age and she was not knowing the consequences of her own act. On the contrary, it can be gathered that she had attained the age of understanding and she was knowing the consequences of her own act. 14] From the evidence on record, it can be gathered that accused was residing in the vicinity of victim. There was love affair between them. They used to visit each­other. On the call of accused, victim herself went to the accused. Accused had committed sexual intercourse with her at his house. Therefore, it can be said that the sex was consensual intercourse and victim was knowing the consequences of her own act. 15] Undoubtedly, D.N.A. report Exh. 19 is placed on record. It can be gathered from the same that accused and victim are biological parents of baby of victim. Blood stains on middle portion to be washed belongs to accused. The blood group of accused was found blood group 'O'. 16] Victim has blessed a baby from the accused, as per report Exh. 19. On 01.11.17, both accused and victim had filed their joint pursis Exh.10, alleging that they had decided to marry with each­other. Therefore, they do not want to proceed with the matter. 17] Having considered the facts and circumstances of the matter, evidence on record and discussed reasons, in my view, it can be held that 7 Spl. (POCSO) C. No. 35/2015. prosecution failed to prove the alleged offence beyond all reasonable doubts. Hence, I answer point no.1 accordingly and proceed to pass the following order. ORDER 1] Accused Dilip Sunil Thakur is hereby, acquitted under sec. 235(1) of the Criminal Procedure Code, of the offences punishable u/s. 376 of I.P.C. r/w. Section 3 punishable u/s. 4 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 2] Accused Dilip Sunil Thakur be enlarged on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ with surety of like amount. The effect of this bail order will remain in force for the period of six months from today, as per section 437­(A) of Cr.P.C. 3] Muddemal if any, being worthless, be destroyed after appeal period is over. Thane, (A.S. Bhaisare) Date­ 28.11.2017. Additional Sessions Judge­2 and Special Judge (POCSO Act), Thane.

Does the prosecution prove that the In the negative. accused during above mentioned period, time and place, committed sexual harassment upon a child with sexual intent by making a child to exhibit her vagina so as to seen by you and also shown blue films in your mobile for pornographic purpose to the child, aged 17 years and thereby committed an offence defined u/sec. 11(2)(3) punishable u/sec. 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012? 6 Spl.C.( POCSO) No. 56/2014... Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­001429­2014 9. What Order ? As per final order. REASONS AS TO POINT NOS. 1 TO 9:­ 7. That, in order to establish the guilt of accused, prosecution has examined only one witness. P.W.1 Laxmi Raiba Shinde who is complainant and wife of the accused at Exh. 12. After that inspite of giving sufficient opportunity, prosecution has failed to secure the presence of other witnesses. Hence, evidence of prosecution side is closed. 8. P.W.1 Laxmi deposed in her evidence that accused is her husband. He was serving in police department. In the year 2013, she was residing at Manogaj Co­Op. Housing Society, room No. 501, in front of Bhayander Police Station, Bhayander (W), Dist. Thane. The said flat was owned by her husband. She has two daughters. They are married. .. 1 .. bail no.554/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 554 of 2015 This application is filed by applicant namely Fatima alias Radha Rampal Gautam for her release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. I­54/2015 registered at Rabale police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 363, 366, 34 of I.P.C. and section 12 and 17 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant helped the other accused in kidnapping the victim girl. It is further contended and argued that applicant has never abetted the co­accused in commission of crime and it is contended that she is the wife of accused no.1. It is further contended and argued that she is not F.I.R. named accused and that she is falsely implicated in this crime. It is further submitted that she has one sucking child with her in the jail and therefore she may be released on bail for taking proper care of the child. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/ accused is released on bail, she will co­operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that the accused no.1 in furtherance of common intention with the present applicant induced the victim girl and kidnapped her with the intention of marrying her. It is further contended and argued that the .. 2 .. bail no.554/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) applicant/accused abetted the accused no.1 in commission of offence. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl and the prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 363, 366, 34 of I.P.C. and section 12 and 17 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, it is further clear the main allegations of kidnapping the girl aged 17 years are against accused no.1 Rampal Ramdayal Gautam and the applicant/accused is stated to have abetted the accused no.1 in commission of crime. Then, the applicant is a woman and is stated to be the wife of accused no.1 having sucking child with her in the jail and she is seen to be in jail since 18.02.2015. Then, she is also stated to be not F.I.R. named accused and it is contended that she is falsely implicated in the crime. In such circumstance whether the allegations against the accused are true or not, would be the question to be decided on merits. Even nothing is stated to be recovered from the applicant/accused. 4] It is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if she is released on bail. In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is .. 3 .. bail no.554/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) permanent resident of the address given and she will not abscond if released on bail and that she is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 5] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 6] Then, it has also to be mentioned that the investigation in the matter though almost completed the charge sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 7] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Fatima alias Radha Rampal Gautam is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ .. 4 .. bail no.554/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) The applicant/accused shall attend the concerned police station on every Saturday between 10.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon till filing of the charge sheet and shall co­operate in investigation. She shall not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and other prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. She shall not leave India without permission of this Court. She shall furnish proof of residence. Date : 18.03.2015 (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.

Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Mr. R.K.Shukla for the applicant/accused and learned Spl.P.P. Mrs. R.A.Navale for State. I.O. present. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 02/02/2016 at the instance of the informant/father of the victim­girl aged 2 Bail No.552/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) about 10 years with an indictment that accused stalked and stopped the victim­girl and talking indecently and demanded her phone number. 4] The learned Counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant/accused is falsely implicated. He submitted that both the sections are bailable. He further submitted that the F.I.R.came to be register only on suspicion. The accused is behind bar since 32 days and investigation is almost completed. He submitted that the accused is permanent resident of Thane and ready to abide any condition imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing him on bail. 5] Per contra, the learned Spl.P.P. opposed the application on the ground that victim­girl is minor and accused used to stalk and harass the victim­girl and demanded her mobile number. The investigation is in progress. There are chances of tampering with witnesses and prayed for rejection of application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R., it appears that the F.I.R. is lodged by the father of the victim­girl alleging that accused used to stalk the victim­girl and used to talk indecently and he demanded her mobile number. Nothing is recovered from the accused. The accused is behind bar since 30 days. 3 Bail No.552/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) The material part of the investigation must have been completed. No doubt the offence is serious in respect of the minor victim­girl. However, the object of bail is neither punitive nor preventive but to secure the presence of the accused at the time of trial. No fruitful purpose would be served by further incarceration of accused. The accused is not having any criminal antecedents. He is ready to abide by the conditions imposed by the Court. In such circumstances the apprehension of learned Spl.P.P. about tampering of witnesses and fleeing away from justice, can be addressed by imposing suitable conditions. Hence, I pass the following order ­ ORDER 1) The application is allowed. 2) Applicant namely Jivach Sukan Kamthi be released on bail on his executing P.R. Bond of ₹ 15,000/­ [Rupees Fifteen Thousand only] with one local solvent surety in the like amount on the following conditions ­ A] Applicant shall attend the concerned police station on every Sunday between 10.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon till filing the charge­sheet. On 29/12/2015 at about 8.30 p.m. she was playing with Anup in the ground in front of house. After two houses of their house one Dada residing, to whom she was knowing. He came to her and caught hold her hand. He also told “Tu Kidhar Bhagke Jayegi, teri Kaki ko kidhar se bulake layegi”. It is also stated that she run towards house, he followed her. 3] It is alleged that she went to the house of Namu Didi and she was weeping. She told that Dada is following. Namu Didi informed the incident to her Aunt. Her mother had been to work at that time. 4] It is also alleged that before the said incident he was trying to talk with her, asking name but she did not talk. Her mother scolds her when she goes outside for playing and therefore, she did not tell about the act of Dada, as earlier .....3/­ 3 Spl.POCSO Case 60/2016 also 2­3 times he has seen him when she was out of house. 5] It is lastly alleged that her mother lodged complaint and Thane Nagar police station registered crime No. I­289/2015 under section 354A of I.P.C. and 12 of POCSO Act. 6] During investigation arrest, spot and personal search panchanama ws drawn. Statement of witnesses were recorded, statement of victim Namrata was recorded in question answer form. Copy of birth certificate was collected and after completion of investigation charge­sheet was submitted. 7] On hearing APP and defence counsel charge below Exh.8 was framed under section 354A of I.P.C. and 11, 12 of POCSO Act and same when read over and explained to the accused in vernacular, he has denied it vide his statement Exh.9. 8] Prosecution examined in all four witnesses. The accused did not examined himself nor led the evidence. 9] I have heard learned APP and defence counsel today. The APP submitted that prosecution has proved the case and the evidence of victim is believable. The learned defence counsel submitted that accused had been to bring son of the sister and he is falsely involved. From the evidence and statement under section 313 of Cr.P.C. defence of .....4/­ 4 Spl.POCSO Case 60/2016 accused is of denial. 10] In the circumstances following points arise for my determination and I record my finding to them for the reasons mentioned hereinafter :­ Sr. POINTS FINDINGS No. 1] Whether prosecution proved that In the on 29/12/2015 at about 8.30 p.m. negative. opposite Civil Hospital, Line No.5, Siddhi Hall, Thane within the jurisdiction of Thane Nagar Police station accused physically contacted victim or advanced unwelcome sexual overtures or sexual coloured remarks ? 2] Whether it is proved that on the said date, time and place and In the during the course of same affirmative. transaction accused committed sexual assault of Kumari Namrata aged 11 years by constantly following and watching her ? 3] What order ? Accused is convicted. REASONS POINTS NO. 1 & 2 : 11] For the sake of convenient discussion points are clubbed. 12] As referred to the prosecution examined P.W. .....5/­ 5 Spl.POCSO Case 60/2016 Namrata Hajari, who is victim, P.W.Aasha Gaesh Hajare, who is mother of victim, P.W. Vikas Paraskar, who was panch and P.W. Shraddha Vayadande, who was I.O. 13] The evidence of P.W. Namrata found not knowing the sanctity of oath during preliminary inquiry she stated about her learning in 6th standard and her school times are from 7.30 a.m. to 1.00 p.m. He stated that on 29/12/2015 she ws playing in front of her house at about 8.00 p.m. 14] She stated that Dada came behind and accused is same person called Dada caught hold her hand. He came behind her near the house of her Aunt and told “Kidhar Bhag Ke jayegi”. The complaint is at Exh.12 and statement in question answer form is at Exh.13. Her birth certificate is at Exh.14. 15] The original birth certificate Exh.14 records her date of birth is 13/08/2005 and obviously on the date of incident she was 11 years of age. Though she admitted that she has gone to lodge the complaint with mother, but denied that her mother informed the incident to police. The age of victim requires prime consideration even though the mother accompanied her, it is not fatal nor there is evidence that she was tutored. 16] Evidence of P.W. Aasha Hajare shows that her daughter was playing game in the evening and when she .....6/­ 6 Spl.POCSO Case 60/2016 returned to home at 8.30 p.m. Namrata told accused came behind and also told “Abhi Kidhar Jayegi”. Thereafter lodged complaint. 17] P.W. Vikas Paraskar proved the spot panchanama Exh.17 and this is not disputed. P.W. Shraddha Vaydande being I.O. in crime No.I­289/2015 drawn the arrest, seizure panchanama Exh.19, spot panchanama Exh.17. She recorded stagtement of witnesses also of victim in question and answer form and submitted charge­sheet. 18] The defence from statement shows that accused had been to bring son of his sister and victim ran away. This shows the presence of accused at the relevant time on the day of incident. 19] The false implication is not to be easily incurred unless there is dubious circumstances, inimical terms or any rivalry or other dispute. P.W. Aasha did not state that accused caught hold of hand but the words uttered are mentioned. Normally the girls are not exposed by parents in the offence alleging to their modesty or chastity. In the circumstances,thee appears no unwell com or sexual overtures or sexual coloured remarks. Therefore, offence under section 354A of I.P.C. is not found proved. 20] At the same time, section 11(iv) of POCSO prescribed that person repeatedly or constantly follows, .....7/­ 7 Spl.POCSO Case 60/2016 watches the child either directly or through electronic media he is said to have committed sexual harassment. The accused submitted that he is of 20 years and he does the job in Pan stall. He is married peson. He submitted that lenient view be taken. There appears no antecedent on record. He is in jail since 30/12/2015 till today. In the facts, circumstances, request and considering the age I am of the opinion that following sentence would be just and proper. Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­001512­2014 Special (POCSO) Case No. 59/2014 Received on : 04.03.2014 Registered on :04.03.2014 Decided on : 08.06.2018 Duration : 4Ys.3Ms.4Ds. IN THE COURT OF D.J.­2 & ADDL. SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE (Presided over by Hemant M. Patwardhan) Special (POCSO) Case No.59/14 Exh.No. 1.State of Maharashtra. (Koparkharine Police station) ..Complainant V/s. 1.Abdul Rakib Suleman Ali. Age :­ 28 years, R/at. R.I.L., C.I.S.F., Jamnagar, Gujrath ..Accused Appearance:­ DGP Mrs. Phad for the State. Advocate Shri. Gawali for the accused. JUDGMENT (Delivered on this 8th day of June 2018 ) Accused was facing trial under sections 363, 376 of IPC and under sections 3, 4, 5 and 6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 on following facts:­ 1] That on 01.12.2013 at about 20.00 hrs. at Sector 1 to 5 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­001512­2014 Special (POCSO) Case No. 59/2014 19, Koparkhairne, Navi Mumbai accused has kidnapped a minor girl from the lawful guardianship of her parents and has committed rape on her and at the same time as per the allegations he has committed penetrative sexual assault in aggravated form. Hence, on complaint lodged by father of the victim initially offence was registered under section 363 of IPC and then was converted into offence punishable under section 376 of IPC read with section 3 to 6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. On completion of investigation he was charge­sheeted. 2] Charge was framed against accused below Exh.9 and contents of said charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. Accused pleaded not guilty and claim to be tried. His defence was of total denial. 3] Prosecution in order to prove guilt of accused has examined, victim as witness no.1 and then I.O. Pramod Pawar as witness no.2. Statement of accused was recorded as per his say. Arguments of rival advocates were heard. They have submitted in terms of their respective averments and contentions. 4] On the basis of aforesaid rival arguments, following points arose for my consideration and I record my findings 2 to 5 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­001512­2014 Special (POCSO) Case No. 59/2014 against each of them for the reasons noted below :­ Sr.N. Points Findings 1] Does the prosecution prove that accused on 01.12.2013 at ..Negative. about 20.00 hrs. at Sector 19, Koparkhairne, Navi Mumbai, within the jurisdiction of Koparkhairne Police Station, Navi Mumbai kidnapped victim a minor aged 17 years 11 months from the lawful guardianship of her parents and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 363 of Indian Penal Code ? 2] Does the prosecution prove that on aforesaid date, time and ..Negative. place accused committed rape on victim a minor aged 17 years 11 months and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 376 of Indian Penal Code ? 3] Does the prosecution prove that on aforesaid date, time and ..Negative. place accused committed penetrative sexual assault on victim, a minor aged 17 years 11 months and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 3(A),4 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act? 4] Does the prosecution prove that on aforesaid date, time and ..Negative. place accused committed aggravated sexual assault on victim a minor aged 17 years 11 months and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 5(C), 6 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act? 5] What order? Accused is acquitted as per final order. REASONS As to point no.1 to 5 :­ 6] In the present matter though allegations were made of commission of rape and sexual assault in aggravated form, the main evidence was in the form of victim. However, the victim herself has denied any act has been committed by present accused. Though the attempts were made to procure the presence of other witnesses, prosecution could not procure 3 to 5 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­001512­2014 Special (POCSO) Case No. 59/2014 the presence of other witnesses. Hence, I.O. was examined. Though he has stated in terms of prosecution's case his deposition was remained uncorroborated in view of victim has declined the said facts. Though some documents were admitted thus in itself were not sufficient to establish the guilt of the accused. Allegations were also made that victim was minor. However, if we consider the medical report attached to first information report then the doctor has opined that age of the victim was 17 plus minus. Hence, if we consider the said fact prima facie it is difficult to accept that victim was really minor at the relevant time and as she has categorically denied the act of sexual harassment at the hands of the accused there is absolutely nothing on record to substantiate the allegations against accused. Having considered these facts I do not find the allegations sufficient to convict the accused as requested by learned P.P. Hence, I do not hesitate to record my findings against points under consideration in negative and proceed to pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused is acquitted from the offence punishable under sections 363, 376, 344 of IPC and under sections 3(A), 4, 5(C) and 6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 4 to 5 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­001512­2014 Special (POCSO) Case No. 59/2014 2] Bail bond of accused shall stands canceled. 3] Muddemal property being worthless be destroyed after appeal period. 4] Accused is directed to execute P.R. Bond of Rs.10,000/­ as per amended provisions of section 437(A) of Cr.P.C. and bonds so executed shall remain in force for the period of six months from the date of its execution. 5] Proceeding is accordingly closed. Counsel on behalf of accused prayed for leniency. 32] Heard Ld. P.P. Smt. Phad for the State. She submitted that accused committed sexual intercourse with his own minor daughter. The offence is against society. He is not entitled for any leniency. He be convicted for maximum punishment as prescribed under law. 33] Accused is father of victim. Victim was residing under the roof and guardianship of accused himself. However, he had taken disadvantage of the same and breached the trust. Therefore, he is not entitled for any leniency. Having considered the nature, in my view, seven years rigorous imprisonment would meet the ends of justice. Hence, I proceed to pass the following order. ORDER 1] Accused Santosh Shivram Jadhav, is hereby, convicted under sec. 235(2) of the Criminal Procedure Code, of the offences 16 POCSO Case. No. 38/2015. punishable u/s. Sec. 376 of I.P.C. r/w. I.O. present. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 25/02/2016 at the instance of the informant/ victim­girl aged about 14 years with an indictment that since August­2015 accused repeatedly made phone call to the informant and asked her to accompany 2 Bail No.592/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) for roaming and demanded money from her and when she refused threatened to cause harm to her father and brother. 4] The learned Counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant/accused is falsely implicated. He submitted that no incident as alleged in the F.I.R. has ever happened. He further submitted that accused never came in contact with the victim­girl. The accused is young boy of 21 years and having no criminal antecedents. The investigation is practically completed. The accused is ready to abide any condition imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing him on bail. 5] Per contra, the learned Spl.P.P. opposed the application only on the ground that victim­girls are minor. The investigation is in progress. There are chances of tampering with witnesses and prayed for rejection of application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R., it appears that F.I.R, was lodged at the instance of victim­girl aged 14 yrs with an indictment that accused repeatedly made a phone call to her and by expressing his love asked her to accompany with him for roaming and demanded money and on refusal threatened to cause harm to her brother and father. There is no indecency in expressing love when the accused and victim­ 3 Bail No.592/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) girl are both young. The material part of investigation appears to have been completed. The object of bail is neither punitive nor preventive but to secure the presence of the accused at the time of trial. No fruitful purpose would be served by further incarceration of accused. He is ready to abide by the conditions imposed by the Court. Hence, I pass the following order ­ ORDER 1) The application is allowed. 2) Applicant namely Siraj Altaf Momin be released on bail on his executing P.R. Special P.P. for the State and Ld. advocate for the accused. 7] The following points arise for my determination with my findings thereon for reasons to follow: POINTS FINDINGS 01. Does the prosecution prove that on ...In the negative. 08.05.2013, at about 19.30 hrs., at R.No.247, Siddhi Vinayak Chawl, Ilthanpada, Digha Navi Mumbai, the accused used criminal force to victim girl, a minor age­14 years with intent to outrage the modesty ? 02. develop acquaintance with him, it appears that subsequently time and again she was going to meet co­accused Vikrant Karadkar and even as rightly argued on behalf of applicant the call detail record produced by the prosecution itself show that there had been constant phone calls minute by minute and second by second between co­accused Vikrant Karadkar and the complainant and that therefore there appear some substance in the submission on behalf of applicant/accused that the co­accused and the complainant were having love affair. 5] It is very much material to mention that statement of the girl under section 164(5) of Cr.P.C. was recorded before the learned Magistrate and copy of which is produced alongwith .. 4 .. bail no.608/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) charge­sheet and from perusal of said statement it reveal that so far as the co­accused or the present applicant compelling the complainant to come with him etc. or pressurizing her in any manner, she appear to be totally silent; rather from her said statement recorded under section 164(5) of Cr.P.C. it appears that the complainant and the girl were having cordial relations and she had been of her own or request of co­accused staying out of house even overnight at times and absolutely no role is attributed to the present applicant. Even she attended birthday programme of accused no.1 and even as per her version the accused no.1 i.e. co­ accused, had even proposed her for marriage, which is totally contrary to her version in the complaint wherein she stated that co­ accused Vikrant Karadkar had pressurized and compelled her to come and had forcible sexual intercourse with her violently by beating her etc. and the present applicant abetted him. 6] No doubt, in her said statement she also appear to have made allegations that the co­accused had taken her to one godown and left her there and accused no.2 i.e. present applicant, raped her and she became unconscious and even she appear to have stated that co­accused demanded money and compelled and pressurized her to withdraw money from bank account of her mother by forging signature of her mother. But so far as that aspect is concerned, as is clear said allegations are only against accused no.1 (co­accused) and it is contended on behalf of applicant that only because he is maternal uncle of co­accused and parents of the girl were against her love affair with the co­accused, he is falsely implicated in the crime and in the light of above when there is prima facie discrepancy between two statements of the girl and in the .. 5 .. bail no.608/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) complainant, it appears that the complainant tried to create an impression that she had not been in love affair with co­accused and it was only under pressure, compulsion and threat she had been meeting him etc. which is contradicted by herself in her statement before the learned Magistrate. In the light of that the submission on behalf of applicant/accused that the entire story put forth in the complaint is improbable or unbelievable appear to be having some substance. That is even for the reason that as per version of the complaint she forged signature of her mother and withdrew amount from bank and that was disclosed after the bank officials enquired with her mother. In that regard the complainant in her complaint and even in statement under section 164 of Cr.P.C. appear to have stated that co­accused Vikrant Karadkar had forced her to forge signature of her mother. But then, it is unacceptable and unbelievable that a person can forge signature of somebody else unless he or she had practised the mode and manner of signature and when the girl not only admitted to have signed cheques and that is also stated to have been approved and accepted by the bank and money was disbursed to her in cash, the submission on behalf of accused that the girl herself was knowing how to forge signature of her mother and withdrew amount herself appear to be having some substance. 7] One more aspect of the matter is that the alleged instances of accused forcing or pressurizing the complainant to come and meet him and then having forcible sexual intercourse with her time and again as many as 14 to 15 times by both the accused during the period from August, 2014. Even the incident of rape by both the accused stated to have taken place in September, .. 6 .. bail no.608/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) 2014. Then, in December, 2014 she alleged to have been forced to forge the signature and withdraw amount and that was even learnt by parents of the girl immediately on the same day on 9th and 18th December and in spite of that the complaint appear to have been lodged on 2nd January, 2015. No doubt, as rightly argued on behalf of prosecution in such type of offences the delay in lodging the F.I.R. cannot be given much importance or significance and it cannot be taken as a fatal lacuna. But then, as rightly argued on behalf of accused it create doubt in the mind as to if at all such serious acts of committing rape by accused no.1 and 2 in September on girl aged 17 years had taken place, she would have stated about it to her dear ones or parents or at least friends or even to her sister. Even she alleged to have consumed phenyl and tried to commit suicide and when she was admitted in hospital she alleged to have stated to the doctor that she had quarrel with her parents and therefore under grief of anger she consumed phenyl. Even in her complaint there was reference to the quarrel of the girl with her parents and she leaving house under grief of anger and in the light of that if the aspect that it is the contention on behalf of accused that there was love affair between the co­accused Vikrant Karadkar and complainant and that was against the parents' wish and therefore the girl herself had been with the accused etc. if considered in the light of the fact that the girl herself brought the cheque book and passbook and forged signature of her mother and withdrew the amount, the delay in lodging the F.I.R. assumes importance and cannot be ignored even at this stage of deciding bail application. .. 7 .. bail no.608/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) 8] Even it is well settled principle that at the stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be gone into detail and main criteria to be considered is as to whether the applicant/accused would tamper with prosecution evidence and whether he would abscond if released on bail. In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 9] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 10] Then, it has also to be mentioned that even though charge­sheet has also been submitted to the Court, it would take time to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 11] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Roshan Vinayak Mhatre is released .. 8 .. bail no.608/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) on P.R. bond of Rs.30,000/­ [rupees thirty thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ He shall not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and the prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this Court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 06.05.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.
