.. 1 .. bail no.620/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 620/2015 This application is filed by the applicant Smt. Shabnam Anwar Shaikh for her release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. II-1/2015 registered at Navghar police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 366A, 370, 372 of I.P.C. and section 4, 5, 7 of Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act (hereinafter in short I.T.P.A.) and also under section 11(4)(6), 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant alongwith other accused procured victim minor girls for prostitution business and compelled them to do prostitution and earned livelihood. It is contended and argued by the applicant that she is falsely implicated in this crime. It is further contended and argued that the applicant has small female baby and except the applicant there is nobody to take care of said child. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, she will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will attend the Court regularly for the purpose of trial and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply on the application itself and it was contended and argued that the applicant/accused and other accused were indulged in procuring the girls for engaging them to do prostitution and for that purpose they procured the victim girls and they used to compel the victims to indulge in prostitution and used to collect money from the customers and used it for own purpose. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the .. 2 .. bail no.620/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant again indulging in same activity. It is also contended that the possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl and prosecution witnesses is also there. It is also contended that if released on bail, the applicant may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear the offences charged against the applicant/ accused are of very serious nature under section 366A, 370, 372 of I.P.C. and section 4, 5, 7 of I.T.PA. and also under section 11(4)(6), 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and it is alleged that the applicant who is also woman, has been forcing minor victim girls into prostitution. Then, though it is contended and argued that very vague allegations are there in the complaint and there is reference to the present applicant only in last paragraph of the complaint, such submission on behalf of applicant/ accused cannot be said to be appealing, convincing and sustainable, that is for the reason that the complaint is lodged by one Ravindra Chavan, Case Worker, Justice and Care (N.G.O.) and on the basis of information received, a raid was conducted and during the raid other accused including present applicant were found the applicant/accused alleged to have forced the girls into prostitution and as rightly submitted on behalf of prosecution the investigation in this matter is yet not completed and there release of applicant may hamper the investigation. In such circumstance the allegation against the applicant will have to be proved on merits after trial. 4] Then, though it is well settled that at the stage of deciding bail the evidence on record cannot be scrutinized in detail, it is to be mentioned that the prima facie material available on record showing .. 3 .. bail no.620/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) implication of the accused has to be considered and the main criteria to be considered is whether the accused would abscond and would tamper with prosecution evidence and whether she would pressurize the witnesses if released on bail. 5] In that regard looking to the nature of offence charged against the applicant/accused and the manner in which it is stated to have been committed and its impact on the society, there is possibility that the applicant/accused may threaten and pressurize the witnesses including the victim girls and may tamper with prosecution evidence which will hamper the process of investigation. Even possibility of the applicant/accused repeating the said offences is also there and the apprehension expressed by prosecution that the accused would abscond if released on bail and will not be available for trial is well founded. 6] In view of all above discussion I am of the view that this is not a fit case wherein the applicant can be said to be entitled to be released on bail. In the result I pass the following order - ORDER The application is rejected. Date : 02.04.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.

O.B. Exh.1 CRI. BAIL APPLN. NO. 528/2018 ORDER BELOW EXH.1 IN CRI. BAIL APPLN. NO. 528/2018 CNR NO.MHTH01­001604­2018 1] Accused Abdul Mukim Khan, Imran Abdul Mukim Khan and Mohsin Abdul Mukim Khan have preferred this application for grant of regular bail on the grounds that applicants are falsely implicated in the crime and have nothing to do with the same. According to them even if the prosecution case is considered as it is then also that will not come within the four corners of section 302 read with 34 of IPC. According to applicants, prosecution case does not disclose any intention of the applicants to cause death or to cause any injuries which are likely to cause death and deceased Jabbar admittedly quarrelling with the members of the society and alleged assault was in the heat of argument. According to accused, there was no intention either to cause death of said Jabbar or cause any bodily injuries on him which was likely to cause his death. According to them as per postmortem report deceased has sustained numerous contusions. However, none of the said contusions are on vital part even otherwise the assaults were by means of fist and kick blows only which clearly goes to show that there was no intention to cause his death. According to applicants alleged incident is outcome of sudden quarrel without pre­meditation that too by means of fist and kick blows and thus provisions of section 302 of IPC will not apply. Hence, applicants have prayed for relief of bail. Adjourn as court time is over. Thane (Hemant M. Patwardhan) Date:19.06.2018 D.J.­2 & Addl. Sessions Judge, Thane 1 To 8 O.B. Exh.1 CRI. BAIL APPLN. NO. 528/2018 2] Say of I.O. was called for and I.O. has filed say below Exh.4 and has categorically objected the application on the ground that complainant and other witnesses have seen applicants­accused assaulting the deceased and therefore, have made reference of their names in the complaint and statements. According to I.O. serious offence has been committed and as accused and complainant are residing in the same society they are likely to indulge in similar offence and likely to tamper with the evidence of the prosecution. Hence, request has been made to reject the application. 3] Heard rival advocates. Initially application was when placed before the court arguments of applicants' advocate was heard and matter was then fix for arguments of learned P.P. and orders. On that date it was noticed by the court that one previous application was rejected by my brother colleague and therefore I felt it necessary to point it out to Hon'ble Principal District and Sessions Judge, Thane as a custom followed in the court is that the same Judge should hear the arguments in successive bail application who has rejected initial application. Accordingly application when reported to Hon'ble Principal District and Sessions Judge, Thane he was pleased to transfer the application to my brother colleague who has rejected the earlier bail application. However, my brother colleague has refused to entertain the application on the ground that he is under the order of transfer and he is required to give charge within a day or two. Matter was again referred by applicant's advocate to Hon'ble Principal District and Sessions Judge. As per order of Principal 2 To 8 O.B. Exh.1 CRI. BAIL APPLN. NO. 528/2018 District and Sessions Judge again sent back to this court. In that process application remains pending for arguments and orders. On last occasion final arguments were heard by rival advocates. 4] Main grounds of the present application is that act of applicants was not intentional but offence was committed in a spur of anger and out of quarrel which took place moment back of occurrence of incident. Therefore, according to applicants' advocate as there was neither intention nor meeting of mind between the parties other allegations of prosecution cannot be accepted. He has then submitted that though unfortunate death of the person is occurred in the matter, the same needs to be considered by the court as occurred just due to quarrel took place between them that too on very trivial ground. Hence, by relying upon Judgment of Hon'ble parent High Court referred in pursis dated 13.04.2018 he has requested the court to consider the application of the applicants­ accused and grant relief claim by them. He has then pointed out of apprehension of I.O. now does not survive as charge­sheet has already been filed. He has then pointed out that facts before Hon'ble her Ladyship in case of Rajesh Dattatray Waghmare V/s. State of Maharashtra in Criminal Bail Application No. 1779 of 2015 is identical with the facts of this matter and Hon'ble her Ladyship has make it a point to accept those submissions of the learned advocate before Hon'ble her Ladyship and considering the fact that incident was not pre­mediated and was occurred in spur of moment has released the applicant before Hon'ble her Ladyship on bail. He has 3 To 8 O.B. Exh.1 CRI. BAIL APPLN. NO. 528/2018 then relied upon other orders of Hon'ble Lordship in other matter as well wherein similar view has been taken when applicant has not antecedent to his discredit. 5] Per contra, learned P.P. has strongly objected the application on the ground that there are eye witness of the incident who has categorically referred the fact that applicants have not only assaulted the deceased by means of kicks and fist blows but then has given a dash to deceased so that he should fall down on the steel bench causing injury to his head which ultimately resulted in his death. Hence, according to submission of the learned P.P. act of applicants­accused pre­meditated and thus, it should be considered while passing the orders and further when applicants are residing at the same place there is every likelihood of their making an attempt to threaten the applicants and indulging in similar act. Learned P.P. has therefore, requested to reject the application. 6] Initially before dealing with the arguments advanced by learned applicants' advocate I have to consider whether successive bail application on the grounds referred in the application is sufficient to reconsider the view expressed by this court in earlier bail application. Reliance is placed on Virupakshappa Gouda and another V/s. State of Karnataka and another reported in LEX(SC) 2017 3 104 to substantiate the fact that merely filing of the charge­sheet is not change in circumstance. However, learned applicants' advocate has categorically pointed out that this court has not considered merit of 4 To 8 O.B. Exh.1 CRI. BAIL APPLN. NO. 528/2018 the matter while deciding the previous application and application was rejected only on the ground that investigation is in progress. On the other hand according to his submissions in reported case application was rejected upto Hon'ble Supreme Court after considering facts and then when the application was again preferred and when upto Hon'ble Supreme Court, observations were made as referred in the said case. However, according to him as merit of the matter has not been considered by this court said ratio cannot be made applicable in this matter. 7] I have therefore, perused the previous order of my learned brother colleague who has categorically observed that he is not considering the application at the stage as the investigation is in progress and there is likelihood of applicants' tampering with the evidence. However, as the charge­sheet has already been filed question of now tampering with the evidence does not exist. As my learned brother colleague has not considered merit of the matter at the relevant time and has decided application only on the ground that investigation is in progress in my view order passed by him was not on merit of the matter. Thus, this court has to consider successive bail application on the merit. Therefore, successive bail application is consider on its own merit. 8] As the charge­sheet is already filed before this court for perusal I have perused that charge­sheet. No doubt the complainant as well as members of society whose statements are recorded has 5 To 8 O.B. Exh.1 CRI. BAIL APPLN. NO. 528/2018 categorically stated that while the deceased was chit­chatting with some member of the society, applicants have approached said spot and by uttering some unparliamentary words has asked as to why deceased is interfering in the society's matter. It appears that thereafter they have assaulted deceased by means of fist and kick blows. Finally due to their dash deceased's head was banged on the steel bench and deceased fell down there on the ground. At that time other persons gathered there, shifted him to the hospital but before admission he was declared dead. All the said quarrel which is referred by almost all the members of the society are occurred due to attempt of the applicants to collect huge amount for the painting and repair work of buildings in the society. Therefore, there appears to be no personal ground of quarrel between the said two parties. Further if we consider the fact that no weapon has been used in the particular crime or there is apparently no enmity between the deceased and the applicants­accused on any of the ground except there appears to be difference of opinion on the cost of repair work of the building. Hence, said talk on the basis of those grounds nobody will commit murder of any particular person. Hence, submissions of applicants' advocate that the incident had occurred in a spur of moment appears to be more probable. 9] Admittedly, nothing is brought before this court to bring any criminal antecedent of the applicants on record. Thus, if that fact is consider then detention of the applicants, though life has been lost in the matter, can be said to be punishment without trial. If we 6 To 8 O.B. Exh.1 CRI. BAIL APPLN. NO. 528/2018 consider the observations of Hon'ble her ladyship in Rajesh Waghmare's case then as the facts of the said observations and facts before this court are almost identical. On the basis of the said observations as well in my opinion relief can be granted though allegations of having committed murder has been made by the prosecution. As the matter is at very initial stage purposely avoiding to make comments on merit of the matter or on the facts whether particular section can be made applicable to the facts of the matter or not. All these points can only be decided on its own merit while recording its evidence or delivering the Judgment in the matter. As the incident is not occurred without pre­meditation and occurred in spur of moment and as the applicants have inflicted injuries not by any weapon but only by means of fist and kick blows it in itself sufficient prima facie to say that applicants were not intending to cause such bodily injury which would certainly resulted into death. Hence, in my opinion on the peculiar facts of the matter, detaining the applicants without trial which is not likely to commence considering huge pendency of matter before this court is certainly unjustified. Hence, in my opinion applicants can be allowed. However, while granting relief of bail having considered the various grounds of objections by the I.O. stringent conditions are required to be imposed on the applicants. With the said observation, the order. ORDER 1] Application is allowed. 2] Applicants­accused are released on their executing P.R. and S.B. of Rs.50,000/­ each with one solvent surety in the like amount. 7 To 8 O.B. Exh.1 CRI. BAIL APPLN. NO. 528/2018 3] Applicants shall produce photo identity, address proof of self and their two close relatives and shall not indulge in any act of similar nature or which endanger the life of the complainant or witnesses and shall not leave jurisdiction of this court without prior permission and shall attend the concern police station once in a month preferably on 1st day of each English calendar month between 11.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon until further order and shall report compliance on fix date of hearing. 4] Bail in concern court. Thane (Hemant M. Patwardhan) Date : 20.06.2018 D.J.­2 & Addl. Sessions Judge, Thane 8 To 8

.. 1 .. bail no. 626/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 626/2015 This application is filed by applicant Saheb Govind Sonkar for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with C.R.No. I­5/2015 registered at Turbhe MIDC police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 363, 376 of I.P.C. and section 4 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short ''P.O.C.S.O. Act''). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant induced the daughter of the complainant and kidnapped her and then had raped her. It is further contended and argued that the applicant is falsely implicated in this crime. It is further contended and argued that there was love affair between the applicant and victim girl and the applicant did not kidnap her and it is a case of consent. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co­operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that as per contention of the accused himself the girl and the accused were knowing each other and the accused was knowing that the girl was minor and taking disadvantage of her young age he induced her and kidnapped and then had forcible sexual intercourse with her repeatedly. It is further contended that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, he may threaten and .. 2 .. bail no. 626/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) pressurize the girl and complainant and may tamper with prosecution evidence. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 363, 376 of I.P.C. and also under section 4 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, the girl is stated to be 16 years 9 months old and it is seen from the F.I.R. that the girl went missing and during investigation it revealed that she had stayed with the accused for about ten days and during that period, as per prosecution case, the accused had committed forcible sexual intercourse with her more than once. But then, it is contended on behalf of the applicant that it is a case of consent since there was love affair between him and the girl and he is falsely implicated in the crime. Then, as is clear, though consent of minor is immaterial, the aspect as to whether the girl was minor or the act of the accused whether amounts to rape, will have to be decided on merits. Even nothing is to be recovered from the applicant/accused. 4] Then, it is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by .. 3 .. bail no. 626/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) any conditions imposed. 5] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 6] Then, it has also to be mentioned that the investigation in the matter though almost completed, the charge sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 7] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Mr. Saheb Govind Sonkar is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ He shall attend the concerned police station on every Friday between 3.00 p.m. to 5.00 p.m. and shall co­operate in investigation. .. 4 .. bail no. 626/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) He shall not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and other prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this Court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 31.03.2015. 1 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 44/2015 Judgment Received on :­ 09.03.2015 Registered on :­ 09.03.2015 Decided on :­ 27.06.2017 Duration :­ 2Y 3M 18 D IN THE COURT OF ADDITIONAL SESSIONS JUDGE, & SPECIAL JUDGE (POCSO) ACT, THANE AT : THANE ( Presided over by Ashutosh N.Karmarkar, District Judge­1 & Special Judge (POCSO) Act, Thane ) Special Case (POCSO) No.44/2015 Exh. No. 21 State of Maharashtra ( Through Kongaon Police Station ) …Complainant V/s. Raja Narayan Pathak Age : 25 Years, Occ. : labour R/at.: Amar Karte's stable, Kontari, Kongaon, Tal. Bhiwandi, Dist.Thane … Accused. Offence punishable under Sec. 509 of Indian Penal Code & under Secs. 11(i)(iv) r/w. 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 44/2015 Judgment Appearances : Shri. V.G.Kadu, A.P.P. for the State Shri. M.V.More, Advocate for accused JUDGMENT ( Delivered on this 27thday of June, 2017 ) 1] Accused is facing trial for the offence punishable under Sec. 509 of Indian Penal Code and under Secs. 11(i)(iv) r/w. S.12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] Prosecution Case, in brief, is as under : Victim's father is driver. Victim is studying in 8 th standard in National Urdu School, at Kalyan. Her school timing was 12.00 noon to 6.00 p.m. She used to go to school by walk. One Sohel Ghangarekar resides in the vicinity of victim. He owns a stable. On 27.12.2014, when the victim was proceeding to school, a boy who is working in that stable was following her. She ignored it. On 29.12.2014, when victim was proceeding to school, again the same boy started following her. Victim stated him that she will say about his act to his employer. That boy stated that he likes her and she shall reply at 6.00 p.m. Then, victim started proceeding school with a scarf over her face. Accused was making indecent gestures and remained present in front of her house. On 31.12.2014, at 7.00 p.m., the said boy came in front of victim's house and made indecent gestures. She narrated this fact to her parents. They came along with the said boy in the police station 3 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 44/2015 Judgment and she lodged the report. On enquiry, he stated his name as Raja Pathak. 3] On the basis of report, offence was registered vide C.R.No. II­32/2014. P.S.I. Deepali Lambhate has recorded the report. She has also investigated this crime. She has drawn spot panchanama. She has recorded statements of witnesses. After detailed investigation, she filed charge­sheet in the Court of Law. 4] My Predecessor has framed charge against accused below Exh. 5 to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. Subsequently, the matter was allotted to this court. The charge was altered / corrected. Again charge was framed at Exh.17 to which accused pleaded not guilty. After alteration / amendment of the charge, prosecution has filed pursis (Exh. 19) that they do not want to lead evidence. Accused also filed pursis (Exh.20) that the earlier evidence be treated as evidence after the fresh charge. 5] Prosecution has examined three witnesses. Then, the statement of the accused under Sec. 313 of Cr.P.C. came to be recorded. Total denial is the defence of the accused. The accused has also tried to raise defence that the another sister of this victim named Rizwana eloped with one Raja Patel and since the accused was residing with him, he is falsely implicated. 6] Ld. A.P.P. has submitted that the date of birth of the 4 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 44/2015 Judgment victim is 15.06.2001 and the incident is in between 27.12.2014 to 31.12.2014. So, the victim was minor at the relevant time. It is also submitted that the evidence itself shows that the accused has followed the victim for twice and the evidence of the victim is not shattered in the cross­examination. The suggestion pertaining to the quarrel on the count of fetching of water by the victim through borewell in stable, has been denied. On the other hand, Ld. Advocate for the applicant has submitted that though there is allegation about following the victim on 27.12.2014 and 29.12.2014, no complaint was filed. Secondly, the other students of the school also used to go with the victim. But, they are not examined. The evidence of the victim and her mother is not consistent. Victim has admitted that the friend of the accused eloped with the sister of this victim and got married. According to Ld. Advocate for the accused, the spot of incident is also changed by the victim. 7] Following points arose for my determination and I gave my findings thereon for the reasons stated below: Sr. POINTS FINDINGS No. 1. Does the prosecution prove that the No accused during 27.12.2014 at 11.30 a.m. to 31.12.2014 at 7.00 p.m., at Kailash Madhavi Chawl, Kontari, Kongaon, Bhiwandi , intending to insult the modesty of complainant Ku. Arbina Riyaz Ansari, age 14 years, uttered the 5 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 44/2015 Judgment words, ^^rq eyk vkoMrsl] eh 6-00 oktrk iqUgk rqyk HksVk;yk ;s.kkj rsOgk eyk rq>s mRrj gos vkgs-**and made some sound or gestures and exhibits some objects, intending that the same shall be heard or seen by her and that accused has thereby committed an offence punishable u/s. 509 of Indian Penal Code ? 2. Does the prosecution prove that during No. above mentioned period, time and places, accused committed sexual harassment upon a victim girl named Ku. Arbina, age 14 years by uttering words ^^rq eyk vkoMrsl] eh 6-00 oktrk iqUgk rqyk HksVk;yk ;s.kkj rsOgk eyk rq>s mRrj gos vkgs-** and making sound and gestures or exhibit any object or part of body with the intention that such word or sound shall be heard or such gestures or object or part of body shall be seen by the girl and accused also repeatedly and constantly followed and contacted the victim directly with sexual intent and thereby committed an offence punishable u/s. 11(i)(iv) r/w. 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act,2012? 3. What order? As per final order. REASONS AS TO POINT NO.1 & 2­ 8] In order to establish the guilt of accused u/sec. 509 of Indian Penal Code, the prosecution has to establish that the accused 6 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 44/2015 Judgment has uttered any words or made any gestures with intention that, that word will be heard or gesture will be seen and that act was with intention to insult the modesty of the woman. In order to establish the guilt of accused u/sec. 11(i)(iv) r/w. 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, the prosecution has to establish that the accused has repeatedly or constantly followed or contacted a child and that act was with sexual intent. 9] The prosecution has examined P.W.1 informant /victim (Exh.10), P.W.2 informant's mother Ajagiri (Exh. 13) and P.W. 3 investigation officer, P.S.I. Deepali Lambhate (Exh.14). 10] Victim has stated that there is a stable in front of her house. On 27.12.2014, she was proceeding to school by walk. The accused was following her. She did not pay attention to him. Again on 29.12.2014, she started proceeding to school. She found that accused has followed her. So, the victim stated not to follow her otherwise she will make complaint to his employer. According to her, accused stated that he likes her and she shall give reply at 6.00 p.m. Subsequently, she started proceeding to school by having a scarf on the face. The accused used to come in front of the house of the victim and used to make gestures. On 31.12.2014, at 7.00 p.m., accused came in front of her house and made gestures by hand, due to which, she felt shy. She narrated this fact to her parents. They went to police station along with accused and lodged report 7 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 44/2015 Judgment (Exh.11). This is in all testimony of the victim. 11] It is incumbent on the part of the prosecution to bring the details as to the gesture so as to ascertain that it was indecent. Such details are also required so as to come to the conclusion that the intention was to insult the modesty of the women. Such details are not stated by the victim. She has made a statement that the accused used to come in front of her house and used to make gestures and the same act was committed on 31.12.2014 also. Victim's mother has nowhere stated about the act of making gestures before 31.12.2014. Victim's mother has stated that on 31.12.2014, she was busy with cooking in her house. Hanif Shaikh is her neighbour. She has also admitted that said Hanif Shaikh is aware about the facts of the incident. 12] It is to be noted that the investigation officer Deepali Lambhate ( P.W.3) has admitted that she has not recorded the statement of other persons except victim and other relatives. Even that neighbour Mr. Hanif is not examined by the prosecution in order to substantiate the contention of victim as to incident dtd. 31.12.2014. There is already a suggestion to victim's mother by the accused that Rizwana, the sister of victim Arbina eloped with one Raja Patel and got married to him and since they were under impression that accused helped Raja Patel, false complaint is filed. This suggestion is denied. But, the victim has admitted that her sister eloped with Raja Patel. 8 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 44/2015 Judgment It is already suggested that the accused was working in the stable which is in front of victim's house. A suggestion is also given that the quarrel was raised on the point of fetching of water through the borewell in the said stable. This suggestion is also denied. But, considering these suggestions, the evidence of the witnesses are also required to be scrutinized minutely. For the reasons stated above, it will be also unsafe to rely on the mere testimony that the accused used to make indecent gestures. 13] It is the case of the victim that on 27.12.2014 and 29.12.2014 accused followed her when she was proceeding to school. On 29.12.2014, accused allegedly stated that he likes the victim and that she was to give reply at 6.00 p.m. Recitals of the report (Exh.11) reveal that the victim has made enquiry with the accused on 29.12.2014 at Durgadi bridge about his act of following victim. Victim has stated that other students of the school also used the same way to go to school. Admittedly, her friends and classmates also used to be with her while proceeding to school. So, it was possible for the prosecution to examine any of her classmates to substantiate her contention. 14] It is not the case of a victim that she has immediately narrated this incident to her parents on 29.12.2014. Admittedly, she has not lodged any complaint to police station in respect of incidents dtd.27.12.2014 and 29.12.2014 before 31.12.2014. Victim's mother Ajagiri has stated that on both the dates 9 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 44/2015 Judgment i.e. 27.12.2014 and 29.12.2014, the victim came to home from school and stated that on both dates the accused had followed her and victim also stated about the words uttered by the accused on 29.12.2014 that he likes her and to give reply in the evening. 15] It is to be noted that the victim has not stated specifically in examination­in­chief that on both the dates, she has narrated her parents about the act of following her by accused. So, it can be said that the victim's mother has tried to improve herself. Even the recitals of the report (Exh.11) also does not reveal about the narration of the incidents on 27.12.2014 and 29.12.2014 immediately by victim to her parents on those particular dates. Considering these facts, it would be unsafe to accept the version of victim and her mother as reliable and trustworthy. Even if it is accepted for a moment that the accused has uttered the words that he likes her, still it is to be seen as to whether other ingredients of Sec. 509 are established. 16] It is a common knowledge that any word, spoken or song, picture or figure exhibited which suggests lewd thought is immoral and insulting to even modesty unless the woman is consenting party. The alleged words are that the accused likes her and she shall give reply in the evening. If we consider this sentence as a whole then it will be difficult to accept that the intention of the accused was to insult the modesty of the victim. Thus, the discussion above lead me to say that the prosecution failed to 10 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 44/2015 Judgment establish all the ingredients of Sec. 509 of Indian Penal code by adducing cogent and convincing evidence. 17] In order to establish the guilt u/sec. 11(i)(iv) r/w. 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, the prosecution has to prove that the victim is child. Secondly, the accused has repeatedly followed and contacted her and that too with sexual intent. Birth Certificate is at Exh.12. Victim has stated that her date of birth is 15.06.2001. It does not appear that the accused has seriously disputed the date of birth of victim. The alleged incidents are from 27.12.2014 to 31.12.2014. So, the age of victim might be 14 years at the relevant time. Even if victim has stated that the accused followed her on 27.12.2014 and 29.12.2014, it is alleged that on 29.12.2014, victim stated the accused not to follow her otherwise, she will make complaint to his employer. Accused stated on that day that, he likes her and will expect her reply at 6.00 p.m. It is alleged that subsequent to 29.12.2014 also the accused used to come in front of her house and used to make gestures. No details of it are given. On the other hand, immediately after two days of 29.12.2014, victim lodged report. It seems that alleged incident dtd.29.12.2014 was occurred at Durgadi bridge when she was proceeding to school. Allegedly her classmates used to be with her. In absence of their evidence, it will be also unsafe to rely on the sole testimony of the victim. Mother of the victim has no direct knowledge of the incident. Her knowledge of the incident 11 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 44/2015 Judgment dtd.29.12.2014 is based upon the information given by the victim. In absence of the evidence of other friends of the victim, it will be difficult to rely on her sole testimony in respect of the alleged act of following and contacting her by accused. Even if it is accepted for a moment that the accused has repeatedly tried to contact the victim, it is to be seen that the said act was with sexual intent. Merely asking a victim that he likes her and to give reply, can not be said to be an act of following her with sexual intent. For that purpose, reliance can be placed in case of Bandu Vitthalrao Borwar V/s. State of Maharashtra, Criminal Appeal No.50 of 2016, dtd. 17.10.2016. It is held in paragraph 10 and 11 as under : Para 10 “After all intention of a person is his state of mind and has to be discerned from the surrounding facts and circumstances. If one cannot, as a human being, physically enter into a mind of another to read and see what is being cooked there, one can surely know it by evaluating all that which is perceivable or felt by human senses such as words, body­ language, gestures, reactions and everything that is a physical manifestation of working of human mind. If somebody says that he is in love with another person or asks another person as to why the other person does not love him , such expression of a feeling or expectation of a particular feeling from another person would not by itself amount to an intent exhibiting some sort of sexuality.” Para 11 “It is obvious that the intent, which is nothing but a state 12 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 44/2015 Judgment of mind, must be to establish some sort of physical contact or must be related to or associated with sex or indicative of involvement of sex in the relationship, if it is to be considered as sexual. I have already stated that the utterance indicating an expectation of a person that the other person should love him would not by itself amount to sexual intent as contemplated by the legislature. There should be something more which must suggest that the real intention is to drag in the angle of sex, if the words uttered are to be taken as conveying sexual intent.” For the reasons stated above, it will be also difficult to accept that the prosecution has established all the ingredients of Sec. 11(i)(iv) of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. 18] Evidence of P.S.I. Deepali Lambhate appears to be of formal nature. She has just drawn panchanama and recorded statements of witnesses. After collecting evidence, she has just filed charge­sheet. Hence, I answer point Nos.1 and 2 in the negative and proceed to pass following order: ORDER 1] Accused Raja Narayan Pathak is hereby acquitted under Sec. 235(1) of Code of Criminal Procedure of the offence punishable under Sec. 509 of Indian Penal Code and Secs.11(i)(iv) r/w. 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 13 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 44/2015 Judgment 2] His bail bond stands cancelled. 3] Accused shall furnish P.B and S.B. of RS. 10,000/­ under Sec. 437­A of Code of Criminal Procedure. 4] Dictated and pronounced in open Court. Thane ( Ashutosh N. Karmarkar ) Date : 27.06.2017 District Judge­1 & Special Judge (POCSO) Act, Thane

1 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 45/2015 Judgment Received on :­ 09.03.2015 Registered on :­ 09.03.2015 Decided on :­ 11.04.2017 Duration :­ 2Y 01M 2 D IN THE COURT OF ADDITIONAL SESSIONS JUDGE, & SPECIAL JUDGE (POCSO) ACT, THANE AT : THANE ( Presided over by Ashutosh N.Karmarkar, District Judge­1 & Special Judge (POCSO) Act, Thane ) Special Case (POCSO) No.45/2015 Exh. No. 17 State of Maharashtra ( Through Turbhe Police Station ) …Complainant V/s. Mohammad Nabi Hasan Ijjat Shaha Age : 36 Years, R/at.: Sai Angan Apartment, Plot No.47,48, Shop No.5, Omprakash Kiran and General Store, Sector­5, Sanpada gaon, Navi Mumbai, Native Rajpur, Post Nandi Factory, Tal. Jashpur, Dist. Nainital, State Uttaranchal … Accused. 2 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 45/2015 Judgment Offence punishable under Sec. 354­A(1)(i) of Indian Penal Code & under Secs. 8 & 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Appearances : Shri. S.D.Londhe, A.P.P. for the State Shri. M.S.Gaikwad, Advocate for accused JUDGMENT ( Delivered on this 11th day of April, 2017 ) 1] Accused is facing trial for the offence punishable under Sec. 354­A(1)(i) of Indian Penal Code and under Secs. 8 & 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] Prosecution Case, in brief, is as under : Informant is residing at Sanpada since last seven years. Victim is daughter of father's sister of the informant. Victim came to the informant due to Diwali vacation on 20.10.2014. Informant used to get minor works done through the victim. She used to send the victim to bring grocery articles to the shop adjoining to Yadav Dairy . On 9.11.2014, at 8.30 p.m., informant sent victim to the said grocery shop to bring Nirma powder. Victim refused to go there. On enquiry victim stated that the shop owner i.e. accused has moved his hand over her person and hugged her on 7 to 8 occasions. So, informant had been to accused to make enquiry. The said owner of the shop admitted his mistake. She went to bus stop as her relatives were to go outstation. While returning from the 3 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 45/2015 Judgment bus stop, she has seen that the shop owner was assaulted by the people as they learnt about the incident pertaining to victim. Then, she lodged report to police. 3] On the basis of report, offence was registered vide C.R.No. I­137/2014. The then A.P.I. Mr. Suryavanshi has recorded the report Exh.14. He drew spot panchanama. He got recorded statement of victim under Sec. 164 of Cr.P.C. After completion of investigation, he filed charge­sheet in the Court of law. 4] I have framed charge against accused below Exh. 6 to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 5] Prosecution has examined three witnesses. Then, the statement of the accused under Sec. 313 came to be recorded. Total denial is the defence of the accused. 6] Ld. A.P.P. Shri. Londhe has submitted that the victim and the informant have stated in detail about the role of the accused. Though the victim has not identified the accused, still the informant has identified him. On the other hand, Ld. Advocate for the accused has submitted that the victim has not identified the accused and the informant has no direct knowledge of the incident. There are also other shops adjoining to the shop of the accused and the said area remains crowded. According to him, no independent witness is 4 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 45/2015 Judgment examined. There was already some incident of quarrel between the accused and the other persons pertaining to the demand of his amount due from them and the accused was beaten by those persons. 7] Following points arose for my determination and I gave my findings thereon for the reasons stated below: Sr. POINTS FINDINGS No. 1. Does the prosecution prove that the No accused from 20.10.2014 to 09.11.2014, at Sanpada village, Sai Angan Apartment, Plot No.47, 48 shop No.5, Omprakash Kiran and General Store, Sector­5, Navi Mumbai, has harassed minor victim Ku. Manisha, aged 10 years by physical contact and advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures? 2. Does the prosecution prove that the No. accused on above mentioned date, time and place, committed sexual assault on minor girl Ku. Manisha by touching her breast with sexual intent? 3. Does the prosecution prove that on No. above mentioned date, time and place, accused committed sexual harassment upon a child i.e. minor girl Ku. Manisha with sexual intent? 4. What order? As per final order. 5 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 45/2015 Judgment REASONS AS TO POINT NO.1 TO 4:­ 8] In order to establish the guilt under Sec. 354­A(1)(i) of Indian Penal Code, it is to be established that the accused is the person who has physically contacted the victim. It is also to be established that the accused has either sexually assaulted or harassed the victim with sexual intent. 9] Informant has stated that the victim is the daughter of her real sister. She took the victim to her house due to Diwali vacations on 20.10.2014. On 9.11.2014, at 8.30 p.m., informant sent victim to bring some articles from the grocery shop owned by the accused. Victim came back and she was weeping. On enquiry, she stated that the accused lifted her and tried to take her inside the shop and moved his hand over her chest. Victim has also narrated that this act was earlier committed by accused on 3 to 4 occasions. Informant has further stated that she had been to the shop of the accused where he tendered pardon. The people who gathered there have beaten the accused. 10] If the evidence of this informant is compared to the recitals in the report Exh.14, it appears that the informant has tried to make out a new story. Actually, it is not mentioned in the report Exh.14 that the victim has visited the shop of the accused on 6 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 45/2015 Judgment 9.11.2014 where he moved his hand over the chest of the victim. It is stated in the report that informant asked victim to go to the shop of the accused to bring some articles. But, she refused on the ground that earlier the accused has committed act of molestation. The cross­examination of the informant itself shows that she has not seen the incident. So, the informant has no direct knowledge of any alleged incident. She has also admitted that before the date of incident i.e. 9.11.2014, victim had never stated the informant about the alleged acts of the accused. If really such incidents were occurred before 9.11.2014, then certainly the victim would have stated about it to the informant who is also her close relative. 11] Now, we will turn to the evidence of the victim. According to her, on the day of incident, she was sent to bring some articles by informant. The person in the shop lifted her and moved his hand over her chest. He has repeated this act for twice or thrice. She came to home and narrated the incident to informant. On that day, informant took her to the shop. Informant made enquiry with the person who was present there and he has tendered apology by saying that alleged incident occurred in his shop. 12] It is to be noted that the victim failed to identify the accused before the Court. She has stated that she is also unable to identify the person who has committed such alleged act stated by 7 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 45/2015 Judgment her. She has specifically admitted in the cross­examination that the shop where she went with the informant and the person who tendered pardon is not a person who has committed such acts as alleged. Considering these admissions, it will be unsafe to hold accused guilty for the offence for which he is charged. Victim has also admitted that after the incident, she has not seen the person who has allegedly committed such acts. This admission itself creates doubt about the allegation of the prosecution against the accused. 13] Informant has also admitted that there is milk dairy adjoining to the shop of the accused. Some other labours are also working in the said dairy. Investigation Officer Mr. Suryavanshi has admitted that there are four to five shops adjoining to the spot of incident and the spot remains busy. So, if the incident as alleged has taken place from 20.10.2014 to 09.11.2014, then certainly any of the independent witness would have stated. Investigation Officer Mr. Suryavanshi has also stated that no complaint against the accused was received before day to alleged incident. Even investigation officer could not get any independent witness in support of their case. 14] In this matter, victim herself has not identified the accused who committed alleged acts of molestation. Informant has no direct knowledge. No other independent witness is examined. According to informant, when she had been to accused to make 8 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 45/2015 Judgment enquiry he tendered pardon. But, the victim has stated that the person who has tendered pardon was not the person who allegedly molested her. Considering such type of evidence, it will be unsafe to rely on the evidence of the victim and informant and to hold accused guilty for the offences for which accused is charged. 15] There is allegation about commission of offence as described in Sec. 7 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. There is also certain presumption under Sec. 29 of the said Act. But, the victim has not stated that the accused is the same person who has committed alleged act. Hence, provisions of Sec. 29 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 regarding presumption will not be helpful to the prosecution in this matter. All the ingredients of the offence for which accused is facing trial are not proved by the prosecution. Hence, I answer point Nos.1 to 3 in the negative and proceed to pass following order : ORDER 1] Accused Mohammad Nabi Hasan Ijjat Shaha is hereby acquitted under Sec.235(1) of Code of Criminal Procedure of the offence punishable under Sec. 354­A(1)(i) of Indian Penal Code and Secs.8 and 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] His bail bond stands cancelled. 9 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 45/2015 Judgment 3] Accused shall furnish P.B and S.B. of RS.5,000/­ under Sec 437­A of Code of Criminal Procedure. Thane ( Ashutosh N. Karmarkar ) Date : 11.04.2017 District Judge­1 & Special Judge (POCSO) Act,Thane

Aashish Bhagwan Gaikwad, Age 22 years, Occ. Service, R/o. Bhadwadgaon, Madan Buwa Chawl, In front of Octroinaka, Bhiwandi, Dist. Thane. ..Accused. ___________________________________________________________ Appearances­ Learned A.P.P. Smt. Talhar, for the State. Learned Advocate Smt. Reena Korde, for the accused. ___________________________________________________________ JUDGMENT (Delivered on 18.08.2017.) 1] Accused Aashish Bhagwan Gaikwad, is facing trial for the offences punishable u/s. 366­A, 376, of I.P.C. and u/s. 3(a) punishable under sec. 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2 Spl. C. No. 47/2015. 2] The prosecution case is that in between 15.07.2014 at 4.00 p.m. to 24.07.14, near the house of complainant, Bhadwad, and also at Kolivali village, Ramainagar, Tal. Bhiwandi, Dist. Thane, accused by giving false promise of marriage to the victim minor girl of complainant named Pinky, aged 16 years, when she was going to private tuition, from the lawful guardianship of her parents and in about ten days, at Kolivali village, Tal. Bhiwandi, Malavali village, Lonavala, by residing with her, from time to time committed rape on her. Thereby, accused committed the offence u/s. 366­A, 376, of I.P.C. and u/s. 3(a) punishable under sec. 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Police had investigated the matter. During the course of investigation, accused along with victim were found. She was medically examined. Accused was also medically examined. Necessary samples from both were seized. Their clothes were seized. After investigation, charge­sheet was submitted in the Special Court. 3] Heard both sides. I framed the charge against the accused for the offences punishable under section 366­A, 376, of I.P.C. and u/s. 3(a) punishable under sec. 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, on 08/06/2017. Details of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular, to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. His defence is of total denial. 4] During trial, defence has admitted certain documents on record, i.e. medical certificates of I.G.M. hospital of victim girl (Exh.9) and accused Ashish Gaikwad (Exh.10), arrest­cum­seizure panchanama of accused Ashish Gaikwad (Exh.11), spot panchanama (Exh.12), C.A. reports (Exh.13, 14), letter of Shantinagar police station to Ld. J.M.F.C. for recording statement of victim as per section 164 of Cr.P.C. (Exh. 15), letter 3 Spl. C. No. 47/2015. of Asstt. Commissioner (Health), Bhiwandi­Nijampura Municipality to Shantinagar police station about information of accused (Exh.16), letter of Shantinagar police station to I.G.M. hospital about giving medical opinion about accused (Exh.17), letter of Shantinagar police station to Asstt. Commissioner (Health), Bhiwandi Municipality about information of accused (Exh.18). 5] To bring home the guilt of the accused for the charges leveled against him, the prosecution has examined two witnesses i.e. P.W. Name of witness Exh. Description No. No. 1] Smt. Meera Ashok Zha 5 Complainant. 2] Pinky d/o. Ashok Zha 7 Victim. 6] Accused did not enter into witness box. He has not examined defence witness. 7] Heard learned A.P.P. Smt. Talhar for the State and learned counsel Smt. Reena Korde for the accused. Following points arise for my determination, which are being answered for the reasons given herein­ below. POINTS FINDINGS 1] Whether prosecution proved that on No. 15.07.2014 at about 4.00 p.m., accused induced victim minor daughter of complainant aged about 16 years, with intent that she may be compelled to marry with him against her will or in order that she may be forced to illicit intercourse ? 4 Spl. C. No. 47/2015. 2] Whether prosecution proved that from No. 15.07.14 at 4.00 p.m. till 24.07.14, near the house of complainant i.e. at Bhadwad, Kolivaligaon, Malavaligaon, Tal. Bhiwandi, Dist. Thane, and at Lonavala, accused from time to time committed rape on the minor daughter of complainant ? 3] Whether prosecution proved that on the No. above date, time and place, accused committed penetrative sexual assault on victim, minor girl of complainant aged 16 years ? 4] What order ? As per final order. REASONS POINT NOS. 1 TO 3 8] P.W.2 Victim deposed in her evidence that she was studying in Swami Vivekanand Hindi high­school, Bhiwandi. She studied upto 9 th standard. Accused is residing in the same chawl where she is residing. There was love affair. She had also approved him. Thereafter, they both decided to marry with each­other by fleeing away. Accordingly, on 15.07.14, they both went to Bhiwandi Court and Lonavala. They resided at Lonavala till 23.07.14. However, there were no physical relations between them. She deposed in her cross­examination that she at her own accord went along with accused and accused had not pressurized her. She categorically deposed in her cross­examination that there were sexual relations with accused with her own consent and she had no grievance. Now, she is married and she had not pressurized her. 9] P.W.1, mother of victim deposed as per her complaint. 5 Spl. C. No. 47/2015. However, she had turned hostile on material points. Therefore, evidence of this witness is not material one. 10] Prosecution has placed on record bonafide certificate of victim. As per said certificate, she was born on 27.07.1998, whereas the incident took place on 15.07.2014. It means, on the date of incident, victim was aged about 15 years, 11 months and some days. However, she was below 16 years of her age. 11] From the entire evidence, it can be gathered that there was love affair between accused and victim. She on her own accord went along with accused. She had not raised any hue or cry. There were physical relations at her own wish. Medical report Exh. 9 goes to show that her hymen was found torn with old tear. Accused was also found capable for sexual intercourse as per medical certificate Exh.10. 12] C.A. reports vide Exh. 13 and 14 are placed on record. No blood or semen was detected on the clothes of victim or the accused. The blood group of accused was found as blood group 'O'. 13] Though there was consent theory as per version of victim, as she was below the age of 18 years, rather below age of 16 years, the accused had to suffer for own act of the victim. Victim is free. She cannot be termed as accomplish. Therefore, in my view, as victim was in the company of the accused at her own accord on account of their love affair and had free sex with her own consent, and she had attended the age of understanding and knowing the consequences of her own act, accused cannot be convicted by giving benefit to the victim for her own wrong. Hence, I have no other option to record my findings to point nos. 1 to 3 in the negative. In the result, I proceed to pass the following order. 6 Spl. C. No. 47/2015. ORDER 1] Accused Aashish Bhagwan Gaikwad is hereby, acquitted under sec. 235(1) of the Criminal Procedure Code, of the offences punishable u/s. 366­A, 376, of I.P.C. and u/s. 3(a) punishable under sec. 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] Accused Aashish Bhagwan Gaikwad be enlarged on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ with surety of like amount. The effect of this bail order will remain in force for the period of six months from today, as per section 437­(A) of Cr.P.C. 3] Muddemal property being worthless, be destroyed after appeal period is over. Thane, (A.S. Bhaisare) Date­ 18.08.2017. Additional Sessions Judge­2 and Special Judge (POCSO Act), Thane.

.. 1 .. bail no.639/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 639/2015 This application is filed by applicant Phulchand Jhagduprasad Gupta for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with C.R.No.I­108/2015 registered at Naupada police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 354A, 509, 506 of I.P.C. and section 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short ''P.O.C.S.O. Act''). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant committed an act involving unwelcome gestures towards the complainant girl and her friend were travelling in the rickshaw of the applicant. It is further contended and argued that the applicant is falsely implicated in this crime. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/ accused is released on bail, he will co­operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that the applicant/accused is a rickshaw driver and at the time of incident the complainant girl and her friend were travelling in the rickshaw of the accused and during the journey the accused made such explicit sexual overtures and gestures towards the complainant and her friend which were amounting to sexual harassment upon them. It is further contended and argued seeing this the complainant asked him to stop the rickshaw but the accused did not stop the rickshaw but speeded away the rickshaw not allowing the .. 2 .. bail no.639/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) complainant and her friend to alight. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl and the prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 354A, 509, 366 of I.P.C. and section 8 and 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act with the allegation of doing explicit sexual overtures towards the complainant and her friend while they were travelling in the rickshaw of accused, it is contended on behalf of the applicant that the F.I.R. is lodged against rickshawwala and only because the accused is also a rickshaw driver, he is falsely implicated in the crime and he has not indulged in any activity of sexual harassment upon the complainant and her friend as alleged. In such circumstance whether the allegations against the accused are true or not, would be the question to be decided on merits. Even nothing is to be recovered from the applicant/accused. 4] Then, it is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he .. 3 .. bail no.639/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 5] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 6] Then, it has also to be mentioned that the investigation in the matter though almost completed, the charge sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 7] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Phulchand Jhagduprasad Gupta is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ He shall attend the concerned police station on every Friday between 3.00 p.m. to 5.00 p.m. and shall co­operate in .. 4 .. bail no.639/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) investigation. He shall not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and other prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this Court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 31.03.2015. Ds. 3 ­ 7 ­ 23 IN THE COURT OF THE SPECIAL JUDGE THANE, AT : THANE (Presided over by S. B. Bahalkar ) SPECIAL CASE NO. 49/2015 EXH. No. CNR­MHTH01­001679­2015 State of Maharashtra. (Through: Kashimira Police Station in C.R.No.I­78/2014) ...Prosecution V/s. Ravindra Damu Khairnar, Age­ 30 years, Occup. Doctor, R/at : F/01, Sanghavi Tower, Mira Bhayandar Road, near Plezant Park,Miraroad (E), Tal., Dist.Thane. Native of Pimpalgaon,Tal.Devla, Dist.Nashik. ... Accused ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ Appearances :­­ Ld.APP Smt.Chandane, for the prosecution. Ld. Advocate Shri.Kanhere for Accused. ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.49/2015 (Judgment). : 2: Special Case No.49/2015 (Judgment) (CNR MHTH­001679­2015) JUDGMENT (Delivered on 1st day of November, 2018) [1] Accused intentionally outraged modesty of a minor girl and thereby sexually assaulted her . Hence, he is facing trial U/Secs.354, 354A, 354D and 506 of the Indian Penal Code (in short I.P.C.) and U/Secs.8 and 12 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offence Act (in short POCSO Act). [2] Brief facts of the prosecution case are as under :­ (i) In the year 2014 informant 'X' (P.W.1) was studying in school situated near Dental Clinic of the accused. Sometimes she had occasion to go to the said clinic for dental treatment. Hence, the informant 'X' and her family members had acquaintance with the accused. (ii) Whenever the informant 'X' used to go to the school the accused used to follow her. On 7/3/2014 at about 12.30 p.m. when she was coming back from the school the accused was standing in front of his clinic. He called the informant inside the clinic. Accordingly she went there. Thereafter the accused closed the door of the clinic and touched the breast of the informant. He insisted her to come with him for movie. At that time the informant told him that he is doing wrong thing. The accused threatened the informant not to disclose the said fact to anybody, otherwise he can do anything. At the same time the door of the AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.49/2015 (Judgment). : 3: Special Case No.49/2015 (Judgment) (CNR MHTH­001679­2015) clinic was knocked and father of the informant was there. He took the informant at home. However, as she got frightened she did not disclose the said incident to anybody else. (iii) Even after the said incident, the accused used to follow the informant and attempted to show undue intimacy. On 20/3/2014 at about 5.00 p.m. the informant alongwith her sister had gone to the tuition classes. Their father dropped them near the said classes. However, at that time the accused was present there. He called the informant and started to show undue intimacy and again insisted her to come with him for movie. Therefore, she came back and narrated the said incident to her father. Thereafter she alongwith her father came to Kashimira Police Station and lodged report against the accused. (iv) On the basis of the report lodged by the informant crime vide C.R.No.I­78/14 U/Sec.354,354A,354D and 506 of I.P.C. and U/Secs.8 & 12 of POCSO Act came to be registered and handed over to P.S.I.Mate for investigation. [3] P.S.I.Mate on the same day arrested the accused. He visited the spot of incident and prepared the panchanama of the said spot. Thereafter, he recorded statements of the father and mother of the informant and other witnesses. Thereafter, further investigation was handed over to A.P.I. Jadhav. He issued letter to the Don Bosco School and obtained bonafide certificate from the AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.49/2015 (Judgment). : 4: Special Case No.49/2015 (Judgment) (CNR MHTH­001679­2015) school showing the birth­date of the informant. On completion of the investigation he submitted chargesheet against the accused. [4] Since the offence U/Sec.354A & 354D of I.P.C. and U/Secs. 8 & 12 of POCSO Act are triable by the Special Court, the Ld.J.M.F.C. committed the said case to this court. [5] My predecessor framed charge (Exh.3) against the accused U/sec.354, 354A & 354D , 506 of I.P.C. and U/Secs.8 & 12 of POCSO Act. Particulars of the offences were read over and explained to the accused to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. [6] Statement of the accused U/Sec.313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is recorded. He denied the allegations made against him. [7] Following points arise for my determination. I have recorded my findings thereon for the reasons stated below : S. POINTS FINDINGS No 1 Whether the prosecution proves that the accused used criminal force to the informant 'X', a minor victim girl , intending to outrage her modesty ? Not proved. AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.49/2015 (Judgment). : 5: Special Case No.49/2015 (Judgment) (CNR MHTH­001679­2015) 2 Whether the prosecution further proves that the accused called the informant 'X', a minor victim girl in your clinic, shut the door , caught hold her hands and moved your hands on her breast and thereby you came in physical Not proved. contact with her ? 3 Whether prosecution further proves that the accused followed the informant 'X' a minor victim girl and asked her to accompany you for seeing movie ? Not proved. 4 Whether prosecution further proves that the accused at his clinic committed criminal intimidation by threatening the informant 'X' a minor victim girl ? Not proved. 5 Whether prosecution further proves that the accused with sexual intention moved his hand over the breast of the informant 'X' a minor victim girl , thereby coming in physical contact with her without penetration committed sexual assault on her ? Not proved. 6 Whether prosecution further proves that the accused committed sexual harassment by following the informant 'X' a minor victim girl ,by uttering the words “Aapan picturela kadhi jayache?” and “Aatta Aapan clinic madhe jawoo.” ? Not proved. 7 What order ? Accused is acquitted. AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.49/2015 (Judgment). : 6: Special Case No.49/2015 (Judgment) (CNR MHTH­001679­2015) REASONS AS TO POINTS NOS. 1 to 6:­ [8] Since all the points for determination arose from the one and the same incident, I took them together for discussion. [9] To bring home the guilt of accused prosecution has examined in all three witnesses. “X' (P.W.1)(Exh.12), the informant, Subhashchandra Ratandev Jha (P.W.2)(Exh.13), father of the informant and A.P.I. Kundan Jyotiram Jadhav (P.W.3) (Exh.16), the investigating officer. [10] On examination of evidence of 'X' (P.W.1), the informant it appears that she is knowing the accused as he is the family Dentist. On 7/3/2014 she had been to the clinic of the accused and discussing with the accused about the dental treatment, at that time her father came there and knocked the door. Except this nothing had happened. She denied that any incident had happened on 20/3/2014. She turned hostile. Hence, she came to be cross­examined by the Ld. A.P.P. However, in the cross­examination she denied that her F.I.R. came to be recorded as per her say. Thus, the informant herself, who is about 19 years old at the time of evidence, deposed nothing incriminating against the accused. AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.49/2015 (Judgment). : 7: Special Case No.49/2015 (Judgment) (CNR MHTH­001679­2015) [11] Subhashchandra Ratandev Jha (P.W.2) is the father of the informant. He deposed that on 7/3/2014 he found that his daughter was there in the clinic of the accused. However, he deposed no incident about outraging of modesty or any other criminal act on the part of the accused. [12] Subhashchandra Ratandev Jha (P.W.2) also deposed about the incident of 20/3/2014. However, while deposing about the said incident, he deposed nothing incriminating against the accused. Moreover, from his evidence it appears that most of his evidence is an omission or improvement over his statement recorded by police. Thus, his evidence is inconsistent to the prosecution case. His evidence also appears to be hearsay. It is already pointed out that the informant 'X' herself deposed nothing incriminating against the accused. In the circumstances, it would not be just and proper to place reliance upon the hearsay evidence of Subhashchandra Ratandev Jha (P.W.2) and to give much weightage to the said evidence. [13] I, next have the evidence of A.P.I.Jadhav (P.W.3). However, it appears that besides obtaining of bonafide certificate, he did nothing in this matter. Hence, his evidence is not helpful to connect the accused with the present crime. AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.49/2015 (Judgment). : 8: Special Case No.49/2015 (Judgment) (CNR MHTH­001679­2015) [14] Moreover, the prosecution has not examined the person who issued the said bonafide certificate showing date of birth of the informant. Hence, the said bonafide certificate is not duly proved . In the result, its contents cannot be read as evidence. Thus, it can be said that the prosecution has even failed to establish the date of birth of the victim i.e. the informant 'X'. Therefore, it is somewhat difficult to ascertain that at the time of incident, whether the victim i.e. the informant 'X' was minor or not. [15] For the reasons stated above, I hold that the prosecution has not brought sufficient and cogent evidence to prove the guilt of accused U/Secs. 354, 354A, 354D and 506 of I.P.C. and U/Secs. 8 & 12 of POCSO Act. I, therefore, answer point Nos.1 to 6 in the negative. AS TO POINT NO.7 : [16] As mentioned above, the prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of accused U/Secs.354, 354A, 354D and 506 of I.P.C. and U/Secs.8 and 12 of POCSO Act. Hence, accused is entitled for acquittal. I, therefore, in answer to point No.7 pass the following order : AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.49/2015 (Judgment). : 9: Special Case No.49/2015 (Judgment) (CNR MHTH­001679­2015) ­: ORDER :­ 1) Accused Ravindra Damu Khairnar is hereby acquitted of the offences punishable U/Sec.354, 354A, 354D and 506 of the Indian Penal Code and U/Sec.8 and 12 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 vide Sec.235(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 2) Bail bond of the accused stands cancelled. 3) The accused shall furnish P.R.bond of Rs.15,000/­ (Rs.Fifteen Thousand only) and surety of like amount in compliance of provisions U/Sec. 437­A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. (Presided over by Hemant M. Patwardhan) Special (POCSO) Case No. 65/16 Exh.No. 1.State of Maharashtra. (Kashimira Police station) ..Complainant V/s. 1] Sandip Balajipalli Shashtri, Age 38 years, R/at. 19/194, Shripad Garudiyanagar, Ghatkopar (East), Mumbai ..Accused Appearance:­ APP Smt. Chandane for the State. Advocate Mrs. Gautami Challke for accused. JUDGMENT (Delivered on this 6th day of September 2017) Accused was facing trial under section 506 of IPC and under section 8 and 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual offences Act on following facts:­ 1] That accused in between 23.10.2014 to 31.12.2014 at Artika C­504, Lodha Aqua, Opp. Thakur Mall, Miragaon, Mira Road (East) and 19/114, Shripad Garudiyanagar, Ghatkopar (East) Mumbai has committed criminal intimidation by threatening complainant with dire consequences and at the same time has Judgment Special Case (POCSO) No. 65/16 committed sexual assault on Kum. Anika, minor aged about 11 months. Thus, on the complaint lodged by mother of the victim, an offence punishable under aforesaid sections came to be registered against accused. After completion of investigation, accused was charge­sheeted. 2] Charge came to be framed at Exh.6 by my learned Predecessor and my learned Predecessor has certified that contents of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. Accused pleaded not guilty and claim to be tried. His defence was that of total denial and that he has been falsely implicated in the matter out of the matrimonial dispute between the accused and his wife. On the basis of aforesaid charge, prosecution has examined the complainant Smt. Latika Shastri as witness no.1 and then as Smt. Latika Shastri has filed pursis, informing the court that she do not wish to lead any further evidence the court was constrained to proceed on the next stage of the matter. As witness examined by the prosecution turned hostile, the formality of recording the statement was dispensed with. 3] Arguments of rival advocates were heard. Learned P.P. has argued that though the witness declared hostile, her deposition can be considered against accused. Per contra defence has submitted that the prosecution witness cannot be said to have supported prosecution as initially witness though has stated to have stated portion marked A and B before police, has again stated voluntarily Judgment Special Case (POCSO) No. 65/16 that as the complaint was in Marathi and she does not understand Marathi language cannot state what actually contents were. Hence, according to defence to such statement does not carry any evidential value to accept it. 4] On the basis of aforesaid rival arguments, following points arose for my consideration and I record my findings against each of them for the reasons noted below:­ S.N. Points Findings 1] Dos prosecution prove that accused in between 23.10.2014 to ..Negative 31.12.2014 at Artika C­504, Lodha Aqua, Opp. Thakur Mall, Miragaon, Mira Road (East) and 19/114, Shripad Garudiyanagar, Ghatkopar (East) Mumbai has committed criminal intimidation by threatening to complainant Latika Sandip Shastri with dire consequences and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 506 of IPC ? 2] Does prosecution prove that accused on aforesaid period and ..Negative places, committed sexual assault on victim Kum. Anika, a minor aged 11 months and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 8, 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act? 3] What order? ..Accused is acquitted as per final order. REASONS As to point no.1 to 3:­ 5] These points are interlinked with each other and therefore, are considered at once. In the instant case the allegations were two­fold, viz. That one was under section 506 of IPC wherein subsequent were under section 8 and 12 of POCSO. If we consider the deposition of witness, she nowhere has deposed that accused has ever threatened her at the relevant time. So far as allegations under Judgment Special Case (POCSO) No. 65/16 sections 8 and 12 of POCSO are concerned, though the witness has initially stated that she has stated portion marked A and B of her complaint before police while recording the complaint, which is marked as Exh.12. However, she has then reiterated her stand by further deposing that she is not aware of Marathi language and therefore cannot say what exact portion police has recorded on her name. Therefore, it is apparent from her deposition itself that she is not aware about the contents of portion marked A and B. She has further made statement that parties have compromise the matter out of the court and thus she does not wish to have any action against accused. Having regards to the aforesaid deposition, deposition cannot be said to be consistent and reliable to establish necessary ingredients of section with which the accused was charged. Therefore, I do not find anything on record which is sufficient to convict the accused either under the provisions of IPC or under the provisions of POCSO under which charge was framed. Hence, I do not hesitate to record my findings against point no. 1 and 2 in negative and proceed to pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused is hereby acquitted of the offence punishable under section 506 of IPC and under section 8 and 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual offences Act 2] His bail bond accordingly shall stands cancelled. Judgment Special Case (POCSO) No. 65/16 3] Muddemal property being worthless be destroyed after appeal period. 4] Accused is further directed to execute fresh P.R. and S.B. of Rs.10,000/­ in view of amended provisions of section 437(A) of Cr.P.C. and the bond so executed shall remain in force for a period of six months. In order to rebut the presumption accused has to establish proper defence either through the cross examination of prosecution witnesses or through his own evidence. Considering the different defences led at different level and consistent evidence of the victim girl and informant, the accused has failed to rebut said presumption. 21] It is further argued in defence that the investigating officer has not inquired about the ownership of the rooms. However, in deposition itself he has stated that he was not having fix timing of work. Subsequent to disclosure of act of kissing and licking of vagina, section 4 of The Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act and section 376 of the Indian Penal Code came to be applied.
