For Accused –­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ ...2/­ 2 Spl.Case No. 65/2014 [ Judg. ] JUDGMENT ( Delivered On this 18th day of February, 2017 ) 1] The accused is facing trial of the offences punishable under section 354 of the Indian penal Code and secs. 8, 9(m) of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act. 2] The prosecution case in short is that, on 13/3/2013 at about 3.45 p.m. three girls having names complainant Suraiyya Mulla aged about 11­12 years, her neighbourer Seema aged about 8 years, another neighbourer Meera Jaiprakash Verma aged about 11 years had been near Maxix Mall for collecting scrap. Then the accused approached to them with his tempo bearing No. MH­04/FJ­3487 and asked them to come with him for collecting fuel and for that purpose he would give Rs.50/­ each. So, these three girls sat in the tempo and the accused took the tempo to Murda Khadi. After reaching there, the accused told them to collect fuel. Then the accused caught left hand arm of complainant Suraiyya and also caught leg of Meera with malafide intention. So, the two girls raised alarm and started to weep. Then a person found passing on a bicycle went to them. He rescued the said girls. Other persons also gathered there. Then one of them phoned to the police station. Police came there, apprehended the accused and alongwith his tempo bearing No. MH­04/FJ­3487 took him to Bhayander Police ...3/­ 3 Spl.Case No. 65/2014 [ Judg. ] Station. 3] The complainant Kumari Suraiyya Salim Mulla filed the complaint against the accused in Bhayander police station. On the strength of the said complaint, the police registered a crime, at serial No. I­56/2013 under sec. 354 of the Indian Penal Code and secs. 8, 9(m) of POCSO Act. 4] The accused appeared before the court. Charge at Exh.6 came to be framed under sec. 354 of the Indian Penal Code and secs. 8, 9(m) of POCSO Act. The contents in the said charge came to be read over and explained to the accused in vernacular to which the accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. The defence of the accused is of total denial. 5] As to bring home the guilt of the accused, the prosecution has examined (PW 1) complainant Suraiyya Salim Mulla (victim) at Exh.9, (PW 2) Meera Jaiprakash Verma (victim) at Exh.10, (PW 3) Smt. Sati Mulla, the mother of (PW 1) Suraiyya at Exh.11, (PW 4) the I.O. Chandrakant Haweli at Exh.14. The prosecution filed evidence close purshis at Exh.17. 6] Prosecution also relied upon the complaint at Exh.16, the seizure panchanama of tempo bearing No. MH­ ...4/­ 4 Spl.Case No. 65/2014 [ Judg. ] 04/FJ­3487 at Exh.13, the tempo deposit receipt in police station at Exh.15. 7] I recorded the statement of the accused under sec. 313 of the Cr.P.C.. The accused did not give any explanation for filing the complaint against him. I heard the learned APP Shri Kadu for the State and the learned defence advocate Shri Yadav for the accused. 8] Following points arise for my determination. I have mentioned my findings against each of them for the reasons stated therefor. POINTS FINDINGS 1] Whether prosecution proves that, on 13/3/2013 at 3.45 p.m., Mauje Murda khadi, Bhayander (West), within the jurisdiction of Bhayander police In the negative. station, the accused used criminal force to complainant Kumari Suraiyya and prosecution witness Kumari Meera who were collecting the waste material near Maxis Mall intending to outrage their modesty and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 354 of the Indian Penal Code ? 2] Whether prosecution proves that, on the aforesaid date, ...5/­ 5 Spl.Case No. 65/2014 [ Judg. ] time and place the accused caughthold complainant Kumari Suraiyya's left hand and prosecution witness Kumari In the negative. Meera's leg, who were 12 years and 11 years respectively, committed aggravated sexual assault on them by giving them Rs.50/­each as labour charges for collecting wood and thereby committed offences punishable under sections 8, 9(m) of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 ? 3] What order ? As per final order. REASONS 9] AS TO POINT NOS.1 AND 2 :­ Both the points being interlinked, I have taken them together for my determination as to avoid repetition of same reasonings. 10] The prosecution examined the victim girls Miss Suraiyya Salim Mulla (PW 1) at Exh.9 and Miss Meera Jaiprakash Verma (PW 2) at Exh.10. On examination of their evidence, it is explicit that, they did not state anything incriminating against the accused. Both the witnesses have stated that, the accused requested them to accompany him to collect fuel and accordingly both the victim girls sat in his tempo bearing No.MH­04/FJ­3487 and he took them to Murda Khadi, Bhayander. Except these words the victim girls ...6/­ 6 Spl.Case No. 65/2014 [ Judg. ] did not state that the accused did any malafide act with them which would come within the purview of sexual assault which would attract section 354 of IPC as well as secs.8, 9(m) of POCSO Act which is punishable under sections 8, 12 of POCSO Act. Even if the prosecution declared both the victim girls hostile as per section 154 of Evidence Act, the learned APP did not bring anything on record against the accused. 11] Moreover, (PW 3) Smt. Sati Mulla is the mother of (PW 1) Suraiyya examined at Exh.11 had been to Bhayander police station with Suraiyya to lodge complaint and accordingly complaint came to be filed in the police station which is at Exh.16 is also not supported to the prosecution case. Nothing has been come on record in the evidence of the material witnesses (PW 1) to (PW 3) to prove the charges levelled against the accused. (PW 4) retired ASI Chandrakant Haweli examined at Exh.14 is not the material witness, being not the eye witness to the incident. He has only stated that, he seized the tempo bearing No. MH­04/FJ­ 3487 under seizure panchanama at Exh.13 and it's receipt is at Exh.15. Mere seizing the tempo by the I.O. is no ground at all to prove the charges levelled against the accused. So, the prosecution is failed in all respects to prove the charges levelled against the accused. So, I record my findings to point nos.1 and 2 in the negative. ...7/­ 7 Spl.Case No. 65/2014 [ Judg. ] 12] Considering my findings to point nos. 1 and 2 and the reasons stated therefor, the accused deserves to be acquitted of the offences punishable under section 354 of the Indian Penal Code and secs. 8, 9(m) punishable under section 12 of the POCSO Act. In the result, I proceed to pass the following order. ORDER 1] The accused Ravindra Mahadeo Dhokane, age 40 years, R/at Bhayander (West), Tal. & Dist­Thane is hereby acquitted as per the provision under section 235(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure of the offences punishable under section 354 of the Indian Penal Code and under sections 8, 9(m) of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act. 2] The bail bond executed by the accused is cancelled. Surety is discharged. 3] The muddemal property i.e. tempo bearing No. MH­04/FJ­3487 be retained with the accused cancelling the Supurtnama, after lapse of appeal period. 4] The accused is directed to furnish fresh P.B. & S.B. of Rs.5,000/­ in compliance with the provisions of section 437(A) of Cr.P.C. to abide himself to appear before Appellate Court in case of appeal is preferred by the prosecution. Thane (N.N. Shrimangale) Date:­18/2/2017 District Judge–4 & Addl. Sessions Judge & Special Judge, Thane ...8/­ 8 Spl.Case No. 65/2014 [ Judg. ] .../­

1 Bail No.636/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) Criminal Bail Application No.636/2016 Nilesh Vithoba Shigwan .. Applicant versus The State of Maharashtra Through Shrinagar Police Station .. Non­applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 1] By this application the applicant is seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. who was arrested on 20/12/2015 by Shrinagar Police Station in connection with C.R.No.I­338/2015 registered for an offence punishable under section 363, 366, 376 of I.P.C. and section 4,12,14 The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as P.O.C.S.O. Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Ms.Gaikwad for the applicant/accused and learned Spl.P.P. Mrs. R.A. Navale for State. I.O. present. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 03/12/2015 at the instance of the informant/mother of the victim­girl aged about 16 years with an indictment that some unknown person kidnapped her daughter. During investigation, it was revealed 2 Bail No.636/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) that accused enticed and committed sexual assault on the minor victim­girl, therefore, section 366 and 376 of I.P.C. and section 4,12 and 14 of P.O.C.S.O. Act were applied. 4] The learned Counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant/accused is falsely implicated. She submitted that the accused and victim­girl are friends and there is love affair between them. However, the parents of victim­girl did not like their love affair. Therefore, the false F.I.R,. was registered against the accused. Accused never kidnapped the victim­girl. He is young boy of 21 years and having no criminal antecedents. The investigation is completed and charge­sheet is submitted. The accused is ready to abide any conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing him on bail. 5] Per contra, the learned Spl.P.P. opposed the application submitting that offence is serious in respect of minor girl. She submitted that as the girl is minor, there is no question of her consent. The accused is involved in serious offence. The accused is having criminal antecedents and he is externed from the jurisdiction of Thane. There are chances of tampering with witnesses and prayed for rejection of application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R., it appears that the F.I.R. is lodged by the mother of the victim­girl about her 3 Bail No.636/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) kidnapping. The victim­girl is aged about 17 years and attended the age of discretion and at the verge of attending the majority. From the statement of victim­girl, it clearly appears that she was in love with accused which was not liked by her parents and when her marriage was settled with another girl, she herself eloped with accused and established sexual relationship with her consent. The investigation is completed and yesterday only the charge­sheet is submitted in the Court. Looking to the huge pendency of cases of Under trial Prisoners, the trial of the present case, would take some time for commencement. The accused is young boy of 21 years. No fruitful purpose would be served by further incarceration of accused. The object of bail is neither punitive nor preventive but to secure the presence of the accused at the time of trial. Although, the accused is stated to have criminal antecedents, however, the offence against him are in respect of the property. The accused is ready to abide by the conditions imposed by the Court. In such circumstances the apprehension of learned Spl.P.P. about tampering of witnesses can be addressed by imposing suitable conditions. Hence, I pass the following order ­ ORDER 1) The application is allowed. 2) Applicant namely Nilesh Vithoba Shigwan be released on bail on his executing P.R. Bond of ₹ 15,000/­ [Rupees Fifteen Thousand only] with 4 Bail No.636/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) one local solvent surety in the like amount on the following conditions ­ A] Applicant shall attend the concerned police station on every Sunday between 10.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon till filing the charge­sheet. B] Applicant shall co­operate in investigation and shall not tamper with prosecution witnesses. C] Applicant shall furnish his and his two blood relatives' address proofs and contact numbers and he is duty bound to inform I.O. and Court about the change of address, if any. Thane. Date : 19/03/2016. (Ms. U.M. Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act), Thane.

--1-- ORDER BELOW EXH.1 IN CRIMINAL BAIL APPLICATION NO. 585/2018 CNR NO. MHTH01­001763­2018 The applicant Tushar Kishor Dhanava aged 22 years has applied for bail under section 439 of Cr. P.C. in C.R.No.I­30/2018 registered in Wada police station for the offence under section 376, of IPC and Section 4, 6, 8 and 12 of POCSO Act. 2. It is contended that investigation is almost completed and applicant is ready to abide by the conditions, therefore, he may be released on bail. 3. Investigation Officer has given his say at Exh.4. It is contended that on 13.02.2018 at Kohoj Fort, Wada in bushes at 8.30 p.m., accused forcibly committed rape upon the victim. If he is released on bail he is likely to tamper the prosecution witnesses and victim as he resided in the same area. 4. I heard Ld. Counsel on behalf of accused and Ld. A.P.P. 5. I do not find any mitigating circumstances in this case because in the FIR itself it is mentioned that the victim aged 17 years had gone to Kohoj Fort for Mahashivratri Festival with her three girl friends and her brother. When her brother was not found she went to search her brother, at that time the accused forcibly taken her in bushes and committed forceful rape upon her. After that the victim was in frightened conditoin. The girl friends came back hom and reported that the victim is not forthcoming. So her mother sent another son and other persons to search the victim. At that time victim found there in the frightened condition. But on that night she did not disclose the incident to anybody. On the next day the victim consumed poison. So she was admitted in hospital. --2-- At that time she disclosed about the incident to one social worker and then FIR came to be lodged. There was no previous contact, no love affair between victim and accused. Victim had never co­ operated the accused prior to that. So there was not complaint at all given by the victim. On the day of incident also coincidently the accused was there. He had not accompanied with the victim and her girl friends. So it was not at all a consensual sexual intercourse, it was rape committed without her consent and will. Therefore, prima facie strong case is made out. If the accused is released on bail he is likely to repeat the offence and likely to tamper, pressurize the victim and informant. Therefore, he is not entitled to be released on bail. Therefore, I proceed to pass following order. :ORDER: Application for bail is rejected. Thane. ( S.C. Khalipe ) Date :28/03/2018. Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

Non­applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 1] By this application the applicant is seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. who was arrested 15.01.2016 by Shreenagar Police Station in connection with C.R.No. I­10/2016 registered for an offence punishable under section 363, 366(A), 376, 372, 342, 354 r/w. 34 of I.P.C. and section 4 , 7 and 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as P.O.C.S.O. Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Mrs. Reena Korde for the applicant/accused and Spl. P.P. Mrs. R.A.Navale for State. I.O. absent. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 08/01/2016 at the instance of the informant/mother of the victim­girl aged about 17 years with an indictment that accused No.1 Kajal 2 Bail No. 676/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) enticed and kidnapped her daughter and confined in the room with the help of accused No.3 Govind and accused No.2 Mohsin committed sexual assault on her. 4] The learned Counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant/accused is falsely implicated. The applicant is a young girl of 21 years and behind bar since 2 ½ months. She submitted that the allegations about sexual assault are against accused No.3 who is released on bail and accused No.2 is also released on bail and the applicant is entitled for the benefit of parity. The investigation is almost completed. Accused is not having any criminal antecedents. The accused is ready to abide any conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing him on bail. 5] Per contra, Spl. P.P. opposed the application submitting that name and role of the present applicant accused is clearly mentioned in the F.I.R. She further submitted that the applicant is involved in serious offence. The investigation is in progress. There are chances of tampering with witnesses and prayed for rejection of application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R., it appears that the F.I.R. is lodged by the mother of the victim­girl about the kidnapping of her daughter. However, the main allegation 3 Bail No. 676/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) about the sexual assault on the minor victim­girl is against the accused Mohsin Khan who is recently released on bail. Similarly the other co­accused who provided the premises to the victim­girl and against whom there are allegations of molestation is also released on bail. The role of present applicant­accused is not on the higher footing than the accused who are released on bail. Hence, the present applicant­accused is also entitled for the benefit of parity. The applicant is young girl of 21 yrs. and behind bar since two and half months. By this time, the investigation must have been practically completed and the only formality of filing charge­sheet must have been remained. No fruitful purpose would be served by further incarceration of accused. The object of bail is neither punitive nor preventive but to secure the presence of the accused at the time of trial. She is ready to abide by the conditions imposed by the Court. In such circumstances the apprehension of Spl. P.P. about tampering of witnesses can be addressed by imposing suitable conditions. Hence, I pass the following order ­ ORDER 1) The application is allowed. 2) Applicant namely Kajal Pratapsing Thakur be released on bail on his executing P.R. Bond of ₹15,000/­ [Rupees Fifteen Thousand only] with one local solvent surety in the like amount on the following conditions ­ 4 Bail No. 676/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) A] Applicant shall attend the concerned police station on every Sunday between 10.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon till filing the charge­sheet. B] Applicant shall co­operate in investigation and shall not tamper with prosecution witnesses. C] Applicant shall furnish her and her two blood relatives' address proofs and contact numbers and she is duty bound to inform I.O. and Court about the change of address, if any. Thane. Date : 19/03/2016. (Ms. U.M. Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act), Thane.

.. 1 .. bail no. 680/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 680/2015 This application is filed by applicant Pradeep Dadarao Kharat for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with C.R.No.I­158/2015 registered at Vartaknagar police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 354, 352, 452, 509, 504, 506 of I.P.C. and section 8 and 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short ''P.O.C.S.O. Act''). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant committed house­trespass and used criminal force against the victim girl and her mother and sister and also outraged modesty and gave provocation and did criminal intimidation. It is further contended and argued that the applicant is falsely implicated in this crime with ulterior. It is further contended and argued that the incident had occurred only due to quarrel between both families and provisions of P.O.C.S.O. Act are applied to enhance the gravity of offence. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/ accused is released on bail, he will co­operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that before the incident in question had happened, the accused had teased the complainant/victim girl twice when she was returning from .. 2 .. bail no. 680/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) tuition class and for that reason the complainant girl and her mother went to question and on that the accused abused them in filthy language and even rushed towards them with bamboo stick in hand, therefore, the complainant girl went inside the house to hide herself and it is further contended and argued that the accused also followed her and went inside the house, at that time the sister of the complainant girl namely Heena was taking bath and the accused held hand of Heena and asked her to take out complainant girl and also pushed Heena aside and then held hand of complainant girl and dragged out of house and also used obscene language at that time. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl and the prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 352, 354, 452, 506, 506, 509 of I.P.C. and section 8 and 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, the girl is stated to be 15 years old and it is stated on behalf of accused that he had not molested the girl nor committed any sexual assault on her and her sister and he is falsely implicated in this crime only on account of quarrels between both families. In such circumstance whether the allegations against the accused are true or not, would be the question to be decided on merits. Even nothing is to be recovered from the applicant/accused. .. 3 .. bail no. 680/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) 4] Then, it is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 5] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 6] Then, it has also to be mentioned that the investigation in the matter though almost completed, the charge sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. .. 4 .. bail no. 680/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) 7] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Pradeep Dadarao Kharat is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ He shall attend the concerned police station on every Friday between 3.00 p.m. to 5.00 p.m. and shall co­operate in investigation. He shall not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and other prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this Court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 31.03.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.

IN THE COURT OF ADDITIONAL SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE, AT : THANE. (Presided over by Smt. S.A. Sinha, District Judge ­ 7 & Special Judge under POCSO Act) SPECIAL CASE (Child Protection) NO.53/2018 CNR NO.MHTH01­001880­2018 Exh. No. State of Maharashtra, (Through Vashi Police Station C.R. No. I­27/2018) … Prosecution Vs. Achhemiya Najir Sayyad, Aged 41 years, R/at. R.No.1, Satyawan Patil Chawl, Sector 31, Vashigaon, Vashi, Navi Mumbai. … Accused For the offence pun. u/s.354 of IPC & u/ss. 8 & 10 of POCSO Act, 2012. Shri Mundhe, Ld. APP for the State. Shri Pisat, Ld. Advocate for the accused. JUDGMENT (Delivered on 08/02/2019) 1] Accused stands charge­sheeted for the offence punishable 2 Judg.in Spl.Case 53­2018 CNR NO.MHTH01­001880­2018 under section 354 of IPC and under sections 8 & 10 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] In brief, facts of the prosecution case, are as under : That, victim girl (avoided to mention the name) aged 13 years is the daughter of complainant Smt. Najma Achhemiya Syyed. She is residing at Vashigaon, Vashi along with her husband Achhemiya and children and she is working as a maid servant and her husband is doing painting work. She has taken divorce from her first husband Javed Shaikh in 2006 and in 2010 she performed second marriage with accused Achhemiya Najir Sayyad. She has one daughter i.e. victim girl from her first husband. 3] On 21.01.2018 at about 00.30 hrs. when she, her husband and children were sleeping, she heard the voice of victim girl and hence, she woke up and saw that victim girl was running out of the house. Hence, she also went out of house and enquired with victim as to what had happened. Upon that, victim told her that she remembered that her father Achhemiya moved his hand on her legs and was removing her payjama and hence, she ran out of the house. Hence, complainant entered into house and saw that her husband was in naked condition. Hence, she went to Vashi Police Station and lodged the report. 4] Police registered the offence vide C.R.No.I­27/2018 under section 354 of IPC and under sections 8 & 10 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Then police conducted 3 Judg.in Spl.Case 53­2018 CNR NO.MHTH01­001880­2018 the investigation, prepared the spot panchanama, collected the bonafide certificate of victim girl for showing her birth date, also get recorded the statement of victim girl under section 164 of Cr.P.C. and after completion of investigation, police have sent­up charge­sheet against the accused before the Court. 5] Accused appeared before the Court, entering into plea. He pleaded not guilty. I have framed the charge against the accused under section 354 of IPC and under sections 8 & 10 of the Protection of Children from Sexual offences Act, 2012 vide Exh.6 on dated 08.10.2018. His defence is of total denial and claimed to be tried. 6] Considering the above facts, following points arise for my determination on which I have recorded my findings for the reasons to follow : Sr.No. Points Findings. 1. Whether prosecution proves that, on In the 21.01.2018 at about 00.30 hrs. at Room negative. No.1, Satyawan Patil Chawl, Sector 31, Vashigaon, Vashi, Navi Mumbai, accused outraged the modesty of 13 years old minor victim girl by moving his hand on her legs and by trying to remove her payjama and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 354 of IPC ? 2. Whether prosecution proves that, on the In the aforementioned date, time and place, negative. accused committed sexual assault on minor victim girl of complainant by touching the vagina, anus or breast of the said victim girl with sexual intent which 4 Judg.in Spl.Case 53­2018 CNR NO.MHTH01­001880­2018 involves physical contact without penetration and thereby committed an offence under section 7 punishable under section 8 of the POCSO Act, 2012 ? 3. Whether prosecution proves that, on the In the aforementioned date, time and place, negative. accused being a step­father of the minor victim girl of complainant, commits sexual assault on such victim girl and thereby committed an offence under section 9(n) punishable under section 10 of the POCSO Act, 2012 ? 4. What order ? Accused is acquitted. :REASONS: As to point nos.1 and 2 : 7] To prove the alleged offence, prosecution has examined in all two witnesses on record. Firstly, prosecution has examined complainant Najma Achhemiya Sayyad (PW1) at Exh.12. Then prosecution has examined victim girl (PW2) at Exh.15. Both these witnesses have not supported to the prosecution case, therefore, Ld. APP has submitted that, as material witnesses are turned hostile, therefore, there will be no use of calling Investigating Officer and other witnesses. Hence, he filed the evidence close pursis on record vide Exh.16. 8] I have perused the record. It appears that age of the victim girl is not denied by the accused. Her mother has produced her bonafide certificate which was issued by Navi Mumbai 5 Judg.in Spl.Case 53­2018 CNR NO.MHTH01­001880­2018 Mahanagar Palika Prathamik Shala No.27 which shows her birth date as 09.04.2004. Incidence took place on 21.01.2018. So, on the date of incidence age of victim girl is 13 years. As said fact is admitted, so no more discussion is required. So also, it is also an admitted fact that accused is the step­father of victim girl and husband of complainant. 9] I have gone through the evidence of both the witnesses. Firstly, victim girl is a material and important witness, but, unfortunately when she entered into witness box she has stated that accused is her father. On 21.01.2018 quarrel took place between them and after taking dinner when they went for sleeping she feel that somebody moving his hand on her legs, therefore, she started shouting loudly and ran away out of the room and told to her mother regarding said fact. That time she thought that except her father nobody was present in the house and hence, thinking that her mother will drove her father out of the house she told his name to her mother and hence, her mother lodged complaint. She further stated that, she does not know the effect of her complaint and when police arrested her father and took him in jail she stated to her mother that her father has not committed said act with her. Only she has stated said fact to her mother that she will remove her father from the house as he used to quarrel with them frequently. 10] The complainant PW1 Najma Achhemiya Syyed has also stated that, as her daughter told her that accused was snatching her clothes, she lodged complaint against him in police station. 6 Judg.in Spl.Case 53­2018 CNR NO.MHTH01­001880­2018 However, when police took her husband and put him in jail, victim told her that as accused used to quarrel and used to beat them, therefore, she has stated lie. She denied the contents of her complaint and printed FIR at Exhs.13 and 14. She turned hostile and not supported. She denied the contents regarding the alleged incidence which are mentioned in portion marked 'A' of her complaint. 11] Both these witnesses are the material witnesses of incidence but they have not supported to the prosecution case. They have not deposed any single word against the accused. Naturally, if the material witnesses are not supporting to the prosecution case, then there will be no use of calling other witnesses on record. Admittedly, present offence is registered under section 354 of IPC. Therefore, there is no medical evidence on record. Therefore, I come to the conclusion that, prosecution miserably failed to prove the alleged offence against the accused as witnesses have not supported. There is no iota of evidence to prove the alleged offence against accused. Therefore, it is not proved that accused outraged the modesty of victim girl and committed the alleged offence under section 354 of IPC and under sections 8 and 10 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Hence, accused is entitled for acquittal. Therefore, I answer point nos.1 to 3 in the negative and proceed to pass the following order : Order 1] Accused Shri Achhemiya Najir Sayyad is hereby acquitted of the offence punishable under section 354 of IPC and under 7 Judg.in Spl.Case 53­2018 CNR NO.MHTH01­001880­2018 sections 8 & 10 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 vide section 232 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 2] The accused is in jail. He be set at liberty forthwith if not required in any other case. Thane. (Smt. S.A. Sinha) 08/02/2019. Special Judge, Under POCSO Act, Thane.

The accused is ready to cooperate in the investigation and ready to abide by any condition imposed by the court and prayed for releasing the accused on the Anticipatory bail. 5] Per contra, Learned Spl.P.P. opposed the application, submitting that the offence is serious and there is bar for grant of Anticipatory bail under the provisions of S.C. & S.T. (Prevention of Atrocity) Act. He further submitted that the accused used the motor cycle in the offence which is required to be seized and therefore, the custody of accused is necessary 3. Anticipatory Bail Appln. 695/2016 Order below Exhibit 1. and prayed for rejection of application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of application and case papers , it appears that the F.I.R. came to be registered at the instance of victim­girl aged of 17 years that on 14/02/2016 around 01.00 a.m. in the midnight accused entered in her house and by removing her quilt touched her breast inappropriately and when she raised shout, lured her grandmother to give ₹.500/­ and when they raised shout, he ran away. Prima­facie if the allegations are seen, the incident took place in the house which is not a public place and not within the public view. Therefore, the basic requirement for attraction of the provisions of S.C. & S.T. Act are missing and in that respect, the learned counsel for accused has rightly placed his reliance on the Judgment of Bombay High Court in the Case of Mahesh Patole V/s. State of Maharashtra, 2009 All M.R.(Cri.) 1601 wherein it is held that, “When prima­facie the provisions of S.C. & S.T. Act would not attract then there is no bar for grant of Anticipatory bail.” Further learned counsel for accused in support of his submissions for grant of Anticipatory bail, in case of P.O.C.S.O. Act and offence under section 354­A of I.P.C. placed his reliance on the Judgment of Bombay High Court in case of Joginder Sing V/s. State of Maharashtra, 2014(3), Bom.C.R., (Cri.) 91. .. 4 .. Anticipatory Bail Appln. 695/2016 Order below Exhibit 1. 7] If the allegations of the F.I.R. are considered and if the say of I.O. is perused the ground for rejection of application is mentioned as that the motor cycle which was used in the offence is required to be seized and the learned Counsel for accused submitted that the accused is ready to surrender the motor cycle in the police station, therefore, considering the peculiar facts and circumstances of the accused, the conditional order with direction to cooperate the investigation would facilitate the investigation. Moreover accused is ready to surrender the vehicle which is stated to be used in the commission of alleged offence. Hence I pass following order ­ ORDER 1] Application is allowed. 2] In the event of arrest of applicant Darshan Ramesh Bhoir in connection with I­09/2016 registered with Vikramgad Police Station for the offence punishable under section 354(A), of I.P. Code and section 7 and 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (In short P.O.C.S.O. Act) and section 3(1)(3) (XI) of Scheduled Caste­ Scheduled Tribes (Prevention) Atrocity Act, 1989. he be released on bail on his executing P. R. 5. Anticipatory Bail Appln. 695/2016 Order below Exhibit 1. bond of ₹15,000/­ with one solvent surety in the like amount on the following conditions : a] The applicants shall attend Vikramgad Police Station on every Monday between 10.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon till further order. b] The applicants shall not leave India without prior permission of the Court. c] The applicant shall not tamper with the prosecution witnesses and co­operate in the investigation. d] The accused shall surrender his motor cycle allegedly used in the commission of offence before I.O. in Vikramgad police station on 28/03/2016. Date : 22/03/2016. (Ms. U.M. Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act), Thane.

.. 1 .. bail no.692/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 692/2015 This application is filed by applicant Rahulkumar Anilkumar Verma for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. I­43/2015 registered at Thane Nagar police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 363, 366 of I.P.C. and section 17 and 18 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in ''P.O.C.S.O. Act'') and also under section 66(c) of Information Technology Act. It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant/accused kidnapped the minor victim girl by inducing her knowing it to be likely that she may be forced to have illicit intercourse with accused. It is further contended that there was no such sexual intercourse between the applicant/accused and the victim girl she was kidnapped. It is further contended and argued that no such incident has happened and the applicant is falsely implicated in this crime on account of previous enmity. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co­operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that the accused was knowing that the victim was minor girl and taking disadvantage of her age he induced her and kidnapped her and .. 2 .. bail no.692/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) taken away her to Delhi with intention that she may be forced to have illicit intercourse with the accused. It is further submitted that the applicant/accused is originally resident of Bihar State and therefore in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant fleeing away and absconding and may not be available for trial and even there is possibility that he may threaten the victim girl and complainant and may tamper with prosecution evidence. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 363, 366 of I.P.C. and section 17 and 18 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and also under section 66(c) of Information Technology Act and the girl is stated to be 16 years old and it is alleged that she stayed for six days with the accused, it appears that there are no allegation of physical relations between the girl and the accused and even it is contended on behalf of applicant/accused that though the girl is major she is intentionally shown to be minor below 16 years old so as to falsely implicate him in this case and that he is in jail since 04.03.2015. In such circumstance whether the allegations against the accused are true or not, would be the question to be decided on merits. Even nothing is to be recovered from the applicant/accused. 4] Even it is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is .. 3 .. bail no.692/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. Then, apprehension is expressed on behalf of prosecution that the accused is originally resident of Bihar State and therefore in case of his release he may abscond and may not be available for trial. In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and he is ready to furnish local surety and he will abide by any conditions imposed. 5] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 6] Then, it has also to be mentioned that the investigation in the matter though almost completed, the charge sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. .. 4 .. bail no.692/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) 7] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Rahulkumar Anilkumar Verma is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ The applicant/accused shall attend the concerned police station on every Friday between 10.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon till filing of the charge sheet and shall co­operate in investigation. I­ 711/15 u/s. 376, 354, 504 of I.P.C. and u/s. 4 and 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 4] P.W.4 Mr. Mansing Gaikwad had carried out investigation. Samples and clothes were sent to C.A. Victim was referred to J.M.F.C. for giving her statement u/s. 164 of Cr.P.C. After investigation, he has submitted his charge­sheet. 5] Heard both sides. I framed the charge against the accused for the offences punishable under section 376, 354, 506 of I.P.C. and u/s. 3, 4, 7, 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012, on 17/08/2017. Name of witness Exh. Description No. No. 1] Madhu Santosh 15 Complainant. Vishwakarma 2] Chandani Ganeshkumar 17 Victim. Warma 3] Santosh Maruti Titame 23 Panch of spot panchanama. 4] Mansing Shankar 26 Investigating officer. Gaikwad 8] Accused did not enter into witness box. He had not examined defence witness. 9] Heard learned P.P. Smt. Phad for the State. Heard learned counsel Shri. Gaikwad for the accused. POINTS FINDINGS 1] Whether prosecution proved that since No. prior to two months of 14.12.2015 till 14.12.2015 at about 20.30 hours, at Dachkulpada zopadpatti, in front of Sant Nirankari Bhawan, Kashimira, accused had 2­3 times committed rape i.e. penetrative sexual assault on minor daughter of his first wife namely Kumari Chandani, aged 10 years ? 5 POCSO Case No. 72/2016. 2] Whether prosecution proved that in the No. above period and place, accused had committed criminal force to minor daughter of his first wife namely Kumari Chandani aged 10 years, with intent to outrage her modesty or knowing it to be likely that accused would thereby outrage her modesty ? 3] Whether prosecution proved that in the No. above period and place, when minor daughter of first wife of accused namely Kumari Chandani, aged 10 years, resisted his sexual assault and rape, accused had given her threats of killing, so also given threats to complainant as she was defaming accused ? 4] What order ? As per final order. REASONS POINT NOS. 1 TO 3 11] Complainant Madhu Vishvakarma is neighbourer of accused. Accused was residing in his room as tenant. At relevant time, his wife Kiran Chavan had been to Uttar­Pradesh as her sister­in­law was not feeling well. She had carried her one issue along with her, whereas victim and her brother along with accused were residing in the spot room. The huts wherein accused was residing, was constructed with the help of tin­ sheets. Accused is father of victim. Complainant Madhu Santosh Vishvakarma is not relative of the accused. 12] Victim, at relevant time, was aged about ten years. 13] It has come in the examination­in­chief of P.W.1 Madhu 6 POCSO Case No. 72/2016. Santosh Vishwakarma, complainant that on 14.12.2015, at about 8.30 p.m., Vimala Chavan came to her and Madhu was asked to see the event what happened in the house of Ganesh Warma. So, she went to the house of Vimala Chavan and saw inside the house of Ganeshkumar by removing a tin. She noticed Ganeshkumar Warma in naked condition at his house. Chandani, Chandan were present inside the room. Ganeshkumar was removing frock of Chandani. Chandani was shouting as “,slk er djks] njn djrk gS.” Door of room of Ganeshkumar Warma was closed. Accused told to Chandani to wait for 2­4 minutes. Madhu abused accused as “HkMos ,slk djsxk rks yMdh ej tk,xh] yMdh dk tku ysxk D;k”. Then, Madhu came to the door of room of accused. She knocked the door. After 4­5 minutes, accused himself opened the door. Thereafter, she tried to take out Chandani. But, accused has obstructed them. Neighbourers were gathered and assaulted him. Chandani came to her. She had narrated all incident to her. Wife of Ganeshkumar Warma namely Kiran was not present. ( Went to her village.) 14] It has further come in the examination­in­chief of P.W.1 Madhu Vishvakarma that she was told by Chandani that yesterday also accused had established his sexual relations with her. Madhu ringed to Kiran and narrated the incident to her. Madhu was told by her that “her husband is not of such character, not to blame against him falsely, not to lodge the report.” Neighbourers had informed the incident to police. So, police came to the spot. Then, Madhu along with police, Vimaladevi and Chandani went to police station. Then, Madhu lodged her report (Exh. 16). On next day morning, police came to the spot, shown by him. 15] It has come in the cross­examination of P.W.1 Madhu Vishvakarma that Santosh Vishwakarma is her second husband. The children who were residing along with her are begotten by her from her 7 POCSO Case No. 72/2016. first husband. She had no any issue from Santosh Vishwakarma. Her marriage with Santosh Vishwakarma is love marriage. She had no visiting terms to the house of Vimala and vice versa. She had no good terms with witness Vimala Chavan. There were six rooms in their chawl. All rooms were occupied in the year 2015. The relations between accused and Vimala Chavan were not good and they used to quarrel. When accused came out from the room, he had tied towel around his waist. He had not wear nicker. At that time, Chandani had no nicker on her person. Chandani, Chandan and accused when came out from their room, peoples were gathered. She along with Chandani, Vimala, her daughter, Chandan and Madhu's husband entered into the office of senior officer in police station. Chandani was referred to hospital for her treatment. There was no talk between Chandani and police in her presence. Lady Police was present in the police station. 16] From the cross­examination of P.W.1 Madhu Vishvakarma, it seems that she has no visiting terms to the house of Vimala Chavan and vise­a­versa. So also, she has no good terms with Vimala Chavan. There were six rooms in their chawl and all the rooms were occupied. The relation between accused and Vimala Chavan were not good and they used to quarrel. There are no windows to the rooms. There is no window between the room of Vimala Chavan and accused and one cannot view from one room to another room. Chandan, son of accused was also present in the said room. Vimala Chavan was the best witness to corroborate the version of complainant Madhu Vishvakarma. Vimala Chavan is not examined by the prosecution. At relevant time, her husband was also present in his room. But, he is neither cited as witness by police, nor examined by the prosecution. When there were no visiting terms and when there were cross­terms between Vimala Chavan and Madhu Chavan, it is 8 POCSO Case No. 72/2016. very difficult to digest that Vimala Chavan had been to Madhu Chavan to narrate the incident and then, they both came to the room of accused and viewed the scene as deposed by P.W.1. 17] P.W.2 victim has not supported to the prosecution case at all. She deposed in her evidence that at about 7.30 p.m., her father returned back from his work and cooked chicken rice. At that time, she alongwith her brothers were slept. Accused had woke up them to have dinner. However, she declined to have her dinner. So, she was fired by him and compelled for dinner. He has also slapped her. So, she was crying. Neighbourer Madhu came to her house and started quarreling with her father. 18] From the cross­examination of P.W.2 victim conducted by accused, it reveals that Madhu and Vimala were not liking consumption of liquor by her father. Therefore, they had intended that her father should leave the said room. 19] Victim was referred to Magistrate. Her statement is recorded u/s. 164 of Cr.P.C. (Exh.18). In the said statement, victim had not stated anything about the alleged incident as projected by complainant Madhu Vishvakarma. On the contrary, it can be seen that she was insisting to go to the village. However, accused had declined for the same. Accused had removed his clothes. So, victim started crying. He had also tried to remove her clothes. From this version, it cannot be gathered that the accused had intention to outrage the modesty of her daughter or to commit rape on her. As he might had protested that victim should not compel him to go to her mother, he might had removed his clothes and tried to remove the clothes of victim. 9 POCSO Case No. 72/2016. 20] While giving statement by victim before Magistrate, she might be free and she was not under the pressure or control of the accused to give her statement as stated by her in her statement Exh. 18 before the Ld. J.M.F.C. 21] P.W.3 is a panch to the spot panchanama. He has deposed as per spot panchanama. So also, P.W.4 Shri. Gaikwad being investigating officer, has deposed as per his investigation. P.W.3 Santosh Titame deposed in his cross­examination that he had not seen any gap in the tin­ sheets wall. Therefore, it is very difficult to hold that P.W.1 Madhu Vishvakarma had viewed the incident from the gap of tin­sheet wall. 22] Clothes of both accused and victim were seized. They were also sent to C.A. C.A. report is not placed on record. Therefore, it cannot be said that the semen stains were found on the clothes of accused. 23] As per medical certificate of victim Exh. 25, it seems that there was history of penetrative sex for past two years. As per column III (g), it seems that medical officer had noticed redness over the right cheek. Doctor had given provisional opinion that the patient had been sexual abused with redness over the cheek with ruptured hymen. Victim has not supported to the prosecution story before this Court in her evidence. So also, she has not uttered any word about sexual intercourse at the behest of accused in her statement Exh. 18 before the Ld. J.M.F.C. Accused is in custody since his arrest. Therefore, it cannot be said that victim was tutored by accused to depose falsely before the court and accordingly, she had not supported to the prosecution story. 24] Having considered the facts and circumstances of the matter, evidence on record and discussed reasons, it can safely be said that 10 POCSO Case No. 72/2016. prosecution failed to prove the alleged offence against the accused beyond all reasonable doubts. Hence, I answer the above points in the negative and proceed to pass the following order. ORDER 1] Accused Ganeshkumar Pyarelal Warma is hereby, acquitted under sec. 235(1) of the Criminal Procedure Code, of the offences punishable u/s. 376, 354, 506 of I.P.C. and u/s. 3, 4, 7, 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] Accused Ganeshkumar Pyarelal Warma be enlarged on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ with surety of like amount. The effect of this bail order will remain in force for the period of six months from today, as per section 437­(A) of Cr.P.C. 3] Accused is in jail. The jail authority is hereby, directed to immediately release the accused, if he is not required in any case or crime. 4] Muddemal, if any, being worthless, be destroyed after appeal period is over. Thane, (A.S. Bhaisare) Date­ 01.03.2018. Special Judge (POCSO), Thane.

No.I­05/2018 registered in Kongaon Estate police station for the offence under section 370(2)(3) of IPC and section 3,4,5 of ITPA Act and Section 4, 8, 12 of POCSO Act, 2012 and section 2 of Foreigner's Act. 2. It is contended that the applicant is falsely implicated. He is innocent. The victim has visited his place of business and made inquiry of Adhar card, therefore, only with intention to help her, the applicant has contacted her with Adhar card agent. He himself has not prepared Adhar Card of the victim. The applicant has not directly or indirectly connected with the crime. There was no evidence against him. No incriminating articles are seized from him. He is permanent resident of given address. He is ready to abide by the conditions, therefore, he prayed for bail. 3. Investigating Officer has given his say at Exh.4. It is contended that as per the secrete information raid was conducted and one minor victim aged 14 to 15 years of Bangaldeshi was rescued from the hands of the accused. The present applicant had harboured the minor victim at his house and instigated her to go to prostitution and provided her for prostitution. The applicant is resident of Assam. He has not fixed resident place. He resided in rented premises. If released on bail he is likely to tamper the prosecution and will indulge her again in prostitution business. The parents of the minor victim are not known. It's inquiry is going on. The present applicant knows that the victim is minor and --2-- Bangladeshi. He made her bogus Adhar card showing that the victim is major and sent her with the help of other accused for prostitution. The present applicant is having criminal background. There is offence registered in Kasarwadavali police station for the offence under section 394, 392 of IPC. There is also offence under section 394 of IPC in Ambernath police station. He has no fix and permanent resident in Maharashtra. Therefore, if he is released on bail he is likely to repeat the offence and likely to tamper the prosecution witnesses and also likely to jump on bail. This is the second bail application on the change in circumstances. It is contended that the alleged incident took place on 01.01.2018 at 22.15 p.m. FIR was lodged on 03.01.2018. The first bail application was rejected on the ground that investigation was incomplete and therefore, accused is likely to tamper. Now the investigation is completed and chargesheet is filed. Thereafter second bail application is filed. 3. It is submitted that owner of the Raj Chinese Chicken Shop has given statement before the police that on 01.01.2018 at about 9.45 to 10.15 p.m. one woman and one girl had come to their hotel and gave Tandoori chicken order and asked “chicken fresh hai kya”. Thereafter one car came infront of their hotel and one man was got down. Then woman and girl seated in the car. The woman gave money of the chicken and then they went away. It is submitted that as per the case of prosecution when the informant and her daughter and husband had gone to Raj Chicken Center for purchasing chicken only informant had got down and applicant was seated in his car with her daughter aged 6 years and it is alleged that accused had committed fingering in the vagina of the victim and thus alleged to have committed sexual assault upon her. --2-- It is further contended that the accused is father of the victim girl and informant is mother of the victim and wife of the accused. It is submitted that after chargesheet is filed circumstance is changed because of the statement given by witness Parimal. It is made clear that the victim girl was not sitting in the car at the time of purchasing chicken. She was along with her mother, therefore, alleged incident is not probable and believable. So on this ground applicant has prayed the second bail. 3. I perused the say of Investigation Officer at Exh.4. It is submitted that the accused is father of the victim girl aged 6 years. He is alleged to have committed sexual assault upon his daughter, so if he released on bail he is likely to tamper the prosecution witnesses. 4. I heard Ld. Counsel on behalf of accused and Ld. APP. 5. Considering the facts and circumstance of this case I am of the view that there is change in circumstances after filing of the chargesheet. The statement of one witness on behalf of the prosecution makes it clear that the informant and her daughter had got down at the time of purchasing Chicken from Raj Chicken. The daughter of the informant was not sitting in the car and after purchasing the chicken they both seated in the car and then they went away. The case will be decided on merit, but at this stage there is mitigating circumstance and change in earlier circumstance which entitled the accused to release on bail. On this change in circumstance accused is entitled for second bail. The applicant is 59 years old. He is father of the victim girl. The informant is second wife of the accused and there are certain litigations between them. So under these circumstances I am of the view that case is --3-- not likely to be disposed off in near future. It will take time. However, the applicant is interior designer. His carrier will be spoiled. So it will not be justifiable to keep the applicant behind bar. So on these change in circumstance accused is entitled for second bail. Therefore, I proceed to pass following order. :ORDER: 1. Application is allowed. 2. The accused Balvindersingh Preetamsingh Bharaj shall be released on P.B. and S.B. of Rs.15000/­(Rupees Fifteen Thousand Only). 3. Applicant shall not tamper the prosecution witnesses and victim by any means. 4. Applicant shall not leave the jurisdiction of the court without prior permission of the court. 5. He shall attend the concern police station once in a month till further order. Thane. (S.C. Khalipe) Date :29.03.2018. Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

Act). 2] Heard learned Advocate Sarita Gaikwad for the applicant/accused and Spl.PP Mrs. Kapare and I.O. present with case diary. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 27/02/2016 at the instance of the informant/father of the victim­girl aged about 16 years with an indictment that his daughter and 2 Cri.Bail Apln.No. 732/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) accused had love affair and on 22/02/2016 she did not return from her school and accused kidnapped her. 4] The learned Counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant/accused is falsely implicated. She submitted that informant was knowing about the affair of the accused and victim­girl. There is delay of 5 days in lodging the F.I.R. Victim­ girl on her own went with the accused at various places like Virar and Wapi and accused never forced her. It is a case of love affair. Investigation is practically completed. The accused is ready to abide any conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing him on bail. 5] Per contra, the ld. Spl.P.P. opposed the application submitting that the offence is serious in respect of minor girl. She further submitted that as the girl is minor, therefore, her consent is immaterial. The statement of victim­girl as per provisions of Sec.164 of Cr.P.C. is yet to be recorded. The cloths of accused are recovered at his instance under the provisions of Section 27 of the Evidence Act. The investigation is in progress. There are chances of tampering with witnesses and prayed for rejection of application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R., it appears that initially, the F.I.R. was lodged by the father of the victim­girl 3 Cri.Bail Apln.No. 732/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) about the kidnapping of her daughter by accused. The offence is serious and in the facts and circumstances of the case the apprehension of Learned Spl.P.P. about tampering of evidence and fleeing away from justice is well founded. .. 1 .. bail 723/2015 (Ord.Exh.1) Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 723 of 2015 This application is filed by applicant Ramesh Suresh Mishra for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. I­56/2015 registered at Koparkhairane police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 354 of I.P.C. and section 7 and 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant outraged modesty of the complainant victim girl by hugging her and moving hand on her private part. It is further contended and argued that no such incident has happened and the applicant is falsely implicated in this crime. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co­operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that at the time of incident the victim was storing water in the house of the complainant and at that time the accused came from behind and hugged the victim girl with sexual intent and also moved his hand over her private part and thereby he outraged her modesty. It is further submitted that the applicant/accused is residing in the same building where the victim is also staying and it is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, .. 2 .. bail 723/2015 (Ord.Exh.1) there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl and may also pressurize her and other prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that the applicant/accused is originally residing in Uttar Pradesh and therefore if he is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, the offence charged against the applicant/ accused is of very serious nature under section 354 of I.P.C. and section 7 and 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act with the allegation that the applicant/accused has outraged modesty of 10 years old girl staying in the same building where the accused has been staying, by kissing and hugging her and even by moving hand on her private part. Then, though it is argued on behalf of applicant that there is delay in lodging complaint, it appears that the complaint is lodged on next day and in such type of offence involving minor girl with the allegation of outraging modesty by an inmate of the same building, such delay in lodging complaint cannot be given much importance or cannot be said to be sufficient to create doubt. Absolutely no reason is put forth as to why such complaint would be lodged to falsely implicate the accused. In such circumstance whether the allegations against the accused are true or not, would be the question to be decided on merits. 4] No doubt, it is well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of .. 3 .. bail 723/2015 (Ord.Exh.1) the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence, if he is released on bail. 5] But then, besides that, the gravity of offence and the manner in which it is stated to have been committed and also the impact of the untoward act of the accused and the aspect as to whether release of the applicant/accused on bail would hamper the investigation, are also required to be considered. In that respect as has been argued on behalf of prosecution the offence charged against the applicant/accused is of very serious nature and the investigation is stated yet to be completed and the applicant is from U.P. and in such circumstance the possibility of the investigation being hampered by release of accused is there and even the apprehension expressed by the prosecution that the accused may pressurise the victim or the complainant and may tamper with prosecution evidence appear to be well founded. 6] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is not a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is rejected. Date : 08.04.2015. (Mrs.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.

.. 1 .. bail no.724/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 724/2015 This application is filed by applicant Deepak Kailas Khandare for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with C.R.No.I­3/2015 registered at Kasar vadavali police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 363 of I.P.C. and section 7 and 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short ''P.O.C.S.O. Act''). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant kidnapped the minor victim by inducing her from lawful guardianship of her parents. It is further contended and argued that the applicant has not kidnapped the victim and she had of her own left the house of her parents and the applicant is falsely implicated in this crime. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co­ operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] No say is filed by the prosecution. Hence, the application is ordered to proceed without say by passing order to that effect on Exh.1. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 363 of I.P.C. and section 7 and 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, the girl is stated to be 16 years old and it is contended on behalf of the applicant that the girl had left house of her parents of her own and the applicant is falsely .. 2 .. bail no.724/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) implicated in the crime. In such circumstance whether the allegations against the accused are true or not, would be the question to be decided on merits. Even nothing is to be recovered from the applicant/accused. 4] Then, it is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. Then, it has also to be mentioned that though opportunity was given, the prosecution has not submitted its reply to this application. Therefore, it appears that there is no apprehension so far so as to infer that the applicant/accused may tamper with prosecution evidence or may pressurize the victim and witnesses or he would abscond if released on bail. 5] But then, looking to the nature of offence and the manner in which it is seen to have been committed, there is possibility that the applicant/accused may abscond or even may pressurize the victim and witnesses and may tamper with prosecution evidence and therefore that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions on the applicant including the condition to give attendance to police station. 6] Then, it has also to be mentioned that the investigation in the matter though may have almost completed, the charge sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge sheet and then to conclude the .. 3 .. bail no.724/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 7] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Deepak Kailas Khandare is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ The applicant/accused shall attend the concerned police station on every Monday between 3.00 p.m. to 5.00 p.m. and shall co­operate in investigation. He shall not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and other prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this Court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 16.04.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.

It is further contended and argued that the applicant is falsely implicated in this crime merely for the reason that he had put forth proposal of marriage before the complainant girl. It is further contended and argued that there was love affair between the applicant and the girl and his proposal was not accepted by the parents of the girl and therefore he is falsely implicated under the pressure of the parents of the girl. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co­operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that the accused was stalking the complainant girl and had tried to foster personal interaction with her despite her utter disinterest and also held her hand in order to pursue her. It is further contended that in this .. 2 .. bail no. 728/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) manner the accused had sexually harassed the complainant girl and committed an serious offence. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl and the prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 354, 354D of I.P.C. and section 11(4), 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, the girl is stated to be 17 years old and it is the prosecution case that the accused was pursuing the girl for marriage and even was trying to interact with her and had held her hand for making her to accept his proposal. But then, it is the contention of the accused that there was love affair between him and the girl but the parents of the girl were against their relations and under the pressure of parents, the accused is falsely implicated in this crime. In such circumstance whether the allegations against the accused are true or not, would be the question to be decided on merits. Even nothing is to be recovered from the applicant/accused. 4] Then, it is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. In that respect it is contended by the .. 3 .. bail no. 728/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 5] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 6] Then, it has also to be mentioned that the investigation in the matter though almost completed, the charge sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 7] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Anil Satyanaayan Raccha is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ .. 4 .. bail no. 728/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) He shall attend the concerned police station on every Friday between 3.00 p.m. to 5.00 p.m. and shall co­operate in investigation. He shall not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and other prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this Court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 31.03.2015. 1 Bail No.754/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) Criminal Bail Application No.754/2016 Jatin Naresh [Ramesh] Patil .. Applicant versus The State of Maharashtra Through Kalwa Police Station .. Non­applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 1] By this application the applicant is seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. who was arrested on 04/02/2016 by Kalwa Police Station in connection with C.R.No.I­38/2016 registered for an offence punishable under section 363, 366, 376 of I.P.C. and section 4 & 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as P.O.C.S.O. Act). 2] Heard learned Advocate Mr.G.W.Avasarmol for the applicant/accused and learned Spl.P.P. Mrs. R.A. Navale for State. I.O. present. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 04/02/2016 at the instance of the informant/father of the victim­girl aged about 17 years with an indictment that accused kidnapped his daughter and performed marriage with her. 2 Bail No.754/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) 4] The learned Counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant/accused is falsely implicated. He submitted that it is case of love affair. The victim­girl is aged about 17 years and having understanding of her act. Her parents were about her love affair. The girl herself left home and accused never enticed her away. He further submitted that in fact, the accused has performed marriage with the victim­girl and they stayed together for four days and provisions of section 376 of I.P.C. are not applicable in the fact of case. He further submitted that accused is young boy and behind bar since two months. The accused is ready to abide any conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing him on bail. 5] Per contra, the learned Spl.P.P. opposed the application submitting that offence is serious in respect of minor girl. She submitted that as the girl is minor, there is no question of her consent. The accused repeated the same offence earlier. The complaint about kidnapping was lodged and even the non cognizable case was registered against the accused. The investigation is in progress. There are chances of tampering with witnesses and prayed for rejection of application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R., it appears that the F.I.R. is lodged by the father of the victim­girl about her 3 Bail No.754/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) kidnapping by accused and performing marriage with her. The victim­girl is aged about 17 years and attended the age of discretion and at the verge of attending the majority. From the statement of victim­girl, it clearly appears that she was in love with accused and she herself eloped with accused and performed marriage with him and established sexual relationship with her consent. The investigation is almost completed and mere formality of filing charge­sheet remains. The accused is young boy of 20 years. He is behind bar since two and half months. No fruitful purpose would be served by further incarceration of accused. The object of bail is neither punitive nor preventive but to secure the presence of the accused at the time of trial. The accused is ready to abide by the conditions imposed by the Court. In such circumstances the apprehension of learned Spl.P.P. about tampering of witnesses can be addressed by imposing suitable conditions. He further submitted that the victim­girl is aged about 17 years and having good understanding. It is a case of consent. There was no forceful act. There is a delay of 11 days in lodging the F.I.R. since last meeting of the accused and the victim­girl. The investigation is practically completed. The accused is young boy of 24 years and permanent resident of Thane. The accused is ready to abide any conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing him on bail. 5] Per contra, the ld. Spl.P.P. opposed the application submitting that the offence is serious in respect of minor girl. She further submitted that as the girl is minor, therefore, her consent is immaterial and the victim­girl is carrying pregnancy of three months. The investigation is in progress. There are chances of tampering with witnesses and prayed for rejection of application. 3 Cri.Bail Apln.No. 762/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R., it appears that F.I.R. was lodged by the victim­girl aged about 17 years with the allegations that accused who is staying in her vicinity got acquainted with her and since six months by promising her to marry took her at various places for roaming and established physical relationship against her consent by threatening her.
