It was also contended and argued that looking to the nature of allegations and the offence charged, the custodial interrogation of the applicant is not necessary and the applicant is ready to abide by any conditions and he has prayed for his release on bail. 5] The prosecution resisted the claim of the applicant by filing reply at Exh.6 and it was contended and argued that the offence alleged against the applicant is of very serious nature of outraging and molestation of young girl aged 13 years and it was contended and argued that though notice under section 41(a) of Cr.P.C. is served upon the applicant, he has concealed himself and switched off his mobile and escaped and the investigation into the matter as to where he had concealed himself is to be done. It was also contended and argued that after the incident the applicant .. 4 .. Anticipatory Bail No.747/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) had contacted the complainant's husband on phone and stated to him to settle the dispute amicably and as such he pressurized the complainant. 6] It was also contended and argued that the applicant is a sitting corporator of the ruling party in Mira Bhayander Municipal Corporation and he is likely to misuse his power and reputation and may hamper the investigation. It was also contended and argued that the applicant and complainant are residents of same building, the victim girl is alone in the house after parents leave for their job and there is possibility of the applicant pressurizing or threatening the girl when she is alone. It was also contended and argued that the girl is under tremendous mental tension and pressure because of the said incident and if the applicant is left free he would be seen by the girl oftenly and that would further traumatize her and would cause mental stress to her. 7] It was also contended and argued that custodial interrogation of the applicant is necessary to find out as to whether any other offence of like nature is committed by the applicant and even the mobile phone of the applicant is required to be seized. It was also contended and argued that other offence under section 147, 454, 425, 457 of I.P.C. is also registered against the applicant and he had been arrested in said crime and he is having criminal antecedents. It was also contended and argued that the act committed by the applicant is condemnable and since he is granted interim protection, there is big public outrage. It was .. 5 .. Anticipatory Bail No.747/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) therefore contended and argued that looking to the nature of offence, the custodial interrogation of the applicant is necessary and the application therefore be rejected. 8] It has to be mentioned that on the very first day of appearance the complainant appeared in person and filed application Exh.7 for permission to assist the Public Prosecutor and also filed objection affidavit as per Exh.10 and it was contended and argued that offence charged against the applicant/ accused is of very serious nature since he has outraged modesty of her adopted daughter aged about 13 years. It was contended that entire story is narrated in the complaint and it is stated that the applicant has rushed to the Court with a view to save his skin from the offence committed by him against her daughter and for misusing liberty granted to him. It was contended that strong prima facie case is made out against the applicant/accused. It was also contended that the offence of sexual harassment by molestation of the girl is committed by a public servant and custodial interrogation of the applicant is necessary, just and expedient. It was also contended that the investigation in the matter is yet to be completed and statements of witnesses are to be recorded and if the applicant is released on bail he may tamper with prosecution evidence. It is also contended that the allegations in the application of the applicant about her husband Shabbir suppressing accounts of the society and misappropriation of funds of the society by Shabbir are false and Shabbir as a treasurer had himself re­accounted and audited the accounts of the society and also got audited the accounts from Chartered Accountant. The .. 6 .. Anticipatory Bail No.747/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) allegation that all society accounts are kept in the house of complainant and her husband etc. are also denied and it was contended that all records are kept in the society cupboard kept on terrace of the building since there is no office premises. It was also contended and argued that there is no question of misappropriation of property since without signature of the secretary of the society i.e. the applicant, no amount can be withdrawn from the society account and therefore it was contended that such allegations are false. 9] It was also contended that the applicant has prepared false and after thought documents purporting to be the letter addressed to the chairman of the society that no person by name V.B.Patel is the chairman of the society and therefore said letter dated 11.03.2015 is merely an attempt to create false evidence. 10] It was also contended and argued that there was no political rivalry between the applicant and the complainant and it was stated that the complainant and her husband are having no concern with any political party and it was contended that she is a teacher by profession and her husband is an accountant in a private firm and are busy in their respective occupation. It was also contended and argued that the contention that the complainant and her husband had opposed the candidature of the applicant in the election etc. are denied and it was stated that such false ground is put forth by the applicant only to obtain orders. .. 7 .. Anticipatory Bail No.747/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) 11] It was also contended and argued that the incident had taken place in the staircase of the first floor of the society building where there is no CCTV camera and therefore CCTV footage of the ground floor of the building will not be of any use. It was contended and argued that the applicant is likely to indulge in further acts of giving threats or causing physical harm and injury to them as well as to other witnesses and in such circumstances it was contended and argued that if bail is granted the applicant would certainly tamper with prosecution evidence and pressurize the witnesses. It was also contended that custody of the applicant is required for the purpose of recording statements of witnesses and recovery of other material. It was also contended and argued that the applicant is having excellent influence and political contacts in the society being the sitting corporator and there is every chance that he would misuse the liberty granted to him and it was therefore prayed that the application for anticipatory bail be rejected. 12] As is clear, the offence charged against the applicant/ accused is under section 354, 506 of I.P.C. and section 9(c) and 10 of P.O.C.S.O.Act and from perusal of the complaint it appears that as per complainant's version when the daughter of the complainant Zenab aged 13 years was returning back from school and she was in the staircase of the building around 1.45 p.m. the applicant had a shake­hand with her and asked her as to how are you and tried to caress her and hugged her from behind and moved hand on her breast and that was told to her by her daughter on phone and since the offence is registered and .. 8 .. Anticipatory Bail No.747/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) applicant apprehends arrest at the hands of police, the present application is filed. 13] Then, as is further clear from the contentions in the application it has been specifically contended that there has been previous rivalry between the applicant and parents of the victim girl and the applicant is secretary of the said society Vidya Shantinagar and father of the girl has been working as a treasurer and the applicant had raised doubts and question about accounts of the society and question as to why the accounts are not audited and it is also contended that there has been political rivalry between parties also since the applicant is stated to be B.J.P. worker and also contested corporation election while the father of the girl and his wife are active workers of Congress Party and followers of Congress Party leader one Muzaffar Hussain and as per contentions of the applicant he has been falsely implicated only with a view to see that he is sent behind bars. In the light of such contentions raised on behalf of applicant also the submissions made on behalf of prosecution the custodial interrogation of the applicant is necessary and whether the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 14] Then, so far as the grant of bail and criteria to be taken into consideration while deciding application for anticipatory bail and also the grounds on which bail can be granted, it is well settled and has been observed in the ruling cited on behalf of applicant in case of Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre vs. State of Maharashtra and others reported in 2010 ALL SCR .. 9 .. Anticipatory Bail No.747/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) 2725 that no flexible guidelines or straitjacket formula can be provided for grant or refusal of anticipatory bail. We are clearly of the view that no attempt should be made made to provide rigid and inflexible guidelines in this respect because all circumstances and situations of future cannot be clearly visualized for the grant or refusal of anticipatory bail. In consonance with the legislative intention the grant or refusal of anticipatory bail should necessarily depend on facts and circumstances of each case and the following facts and parameters can be taken into consideration while dealing with the anticipatory bail : i) the nature and gravity of the accusation and the exact role of the accused must be properly comprehended before arrest is made; ii ) the antecedents of the applicant including the fact as to whether the accused has previously undergone imprisonment on conviction by a Court in respect of any cognizable offence; iii ) the possibility of the applicant to flee from justice; iv ) the possibility of the accused's likelihood to repeat similar or the other offences; v) where the accusations have been made only with the object of injuring or humiliating the applicant by arresting him or her; vi ) impact of grant of anticipatory bail particularly in cases of large magnitude affecting a very large number of people; vii ) the Courts must evaluate the entire available material against the accused very carefully. The Court must also clearly comprehend the exact role of the accused in the case. The cases in which accused is implicated with the help of sections 34 and 149 of I.P.C., the Court should consider with even greater care and caution because over implication in the cases .. 10 .. Anticipatory Bail No.747/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) is a matter of common knowledge and concern; viii ) while considering the prayer for grant of anticipatory bail, a balance has to be struck between two factors namely, no prejudice should be caused to the free, fair and full investigation and there should be prevention of harassment, humiliation and unjustified detention of the accused; ix ) the Court to consider reasonable apprehension of tamper of the witness or apprehension of threat to the complainant; x) frivolity in prosecution should always be considered and it is only the element of genuineness that shall have to be considered in the matter of grant of bail and in the event of there being some doubt as to the genuineness of the prosecution, in the normal course of events, the accused is entitled to an order of bail. 15] In the light of above parameters and factors it is required to be seen as to whether the case for custodial interrogation of the applicant in the facts and circumstances of the present case is made out by the prosecution and whether it is necessary to arrest the applicant/accused and police custody remand is necessary. Then, so far as is clear offence charged against the applicant is of molesting young girl aged 13 years, daughter of the complainant, in the staircase of the building. Then, as rightly argued on behalf of applicant the CCTV footage of the camera in the office of the accused which is stated to be at the front portion of the society at the entrance of the building stated to show that the accused left the office and went outside the society and as per submission on behalf of prosecution and .. 11 .. Anticipatory Bail No.747/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) complainant though the applicant seen to have left his offence and went out of society around 1.40 p.m. the incident took place around 1.50 p.m. and possibility of the applicant/accused returning back and going towards the staircase is still there. But then, that would be the matter of evidence to be led and at this stage it would be premature to conclude that immediately after the applicant/accused left from the society he returned back with the intention to commit the crime. 16] Even the aspect that it is contended by the applicant that he is falsely implicated in the crime on account of previous rivalry also appear to be worth consideration and in that regard if the documents produced on record by the applicant alongwith application are perused, it appears that he has produced copy of complaint sent by him to the chairman of the society against the treasurer i.e. father of the girl, in regard to the accounts of the society etc. are seen to be dated 11.03.2015 and 18.03.2015. 17] In that respect it has been argued by the prosecution and complainant that the person by name V. B. Patel who received the complaint is not at all the chairman of the society and therefore it was argued that such contention that he had given such complaint to the chairman of the society is false and concocted only with a view to escape from liability or to create evidence to show rivalry etc. Even reliance appear to have been placed on the documents produced on record by the original complainant i.e. letter from the society dated 07.02.2010 and relying on that it is argued that the chairman of the society is one .. 12 .. Anticipatory Bail No.747/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Vijaybhai Jasani and said Vijaybhai Jasani never received any such complaint and the committee members by issuing letter dated 07.04.2015 specified that no such letter or complaint was received from the applicant in regard to misappropriation of accounts of the society etc. 18] But then in that respect it was pointed out on behalf of applicant that Vijaybhai Jasani was the chairman in the year 2010 but present chair is one V. B. Patel whom letter was addressed by the applicant and even produced on record copy of notice of meeting dated 23.07.2014 in which it is mentioned that the general body meeting of the society is to be held and one of the business of the meeting was to elect new managing committee and also one note is there at the end of the attendance sheet specifying that changing of chairman Vijay Jasani to new chairman of V. B. Patel and in the light of that in absence of any specific material to show that the present chairman of the society is not V. B. Patel but it is one Vijay Jasani, that aspect also will have to be decided and proved on merits and at this stage it cannot be concluded that V. B. Patel is not the chairman of the society. Even as rightly pointed out on behalf of applicant/accused that the letter dated 07th April, 2015 stated to be the letter issued by committee members do not bear signature of said Vijay Jasani and that also assumes importance in regard to the controversy as to who is the new chairman of the society. 19] Even keeping aside that, only material point to be considered at this stage is contention of the applicant that there .. 13 .. Anticipatory Bail No.747/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) has been rivalry between the parties and in that respect it is clear that it is contended by the applicant that he made complaints against the father of the girl in regard to the accounts of the society and even it is clear that such complaints are made by him. Then, even it is contended that there is political rivalry between them. In that regard also it is clear that in the complaint itself it is mentioned that the applicant is a corporator of B.J.P. Then, in the light of that the contentions on behalf of applicant that he is from B.J.P. and the complainant and her husband are active members of Congress Party and there is political rivalry between them since before, is required to be considered. 20] In that respect though it is argued on behalf of prosecution and the complainant that there is no issue of political rivalry in the matter and it is simple case of outraging modesty of young girl by a corporator and the applicant is unnecessary giving political colour to the issue of making such submission etc. it is material to mention that the applicant has produced on record the documents in the form of complaint to Sr.P.I. by Mira Ekta Committee on its letterhead, also copy of pamphlet and also photograph of agitations made in regard to offence in the present crime against the applicant and it is contended that said agitations and morcha have been taken out by a political party i.e. Congress Party. Even copy of letter is also produced on record addressed by Mira Bhayander Assembly Youth Congress dated 07.04.2015 addressed to Sr.P.I. requesting for taking cognizance of the offence addressing the applicant as 'B.J.P. corporator' and it is also specifically mentioned therein that Youth Congress Delegation met .. 14 .. Anticipatory Bail No.747/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) police to arrest Ashwin Kasodariya i.e. present applicant and also photographs of the banners displayed highlighting Congress M.L.S. Muzaffar Hussain condemning the alleged act stated to have been committed by the applicant. Even photograph of the Mira Road Gujarathi Samaj Mahila Sangh or Bhayander East Uttar Bhartiya Sangh submitted representation to police to arrest and from all those documents produced on record by the applicant, it is very much clear that it is the complainant and his supporters from Congress Party who appear to have publicized on huge scale the alleged incident and the Congress Party appear to have raised agitations and held morcha and that clearly exhibit the political rivalry between the applicant and the complainant and in the light of that the submission on behalf of applicant that political rivalry is also one of the grounds or reasons for making such complaint against the applicant and that also appear to be worth consideration because it appears that all efforts to see that the applicant is arrested by using political pressure as well as other social organizations like Mira Road Gujarathi Samaj Mahila Sangh or Bhayander East Uttar Bhartiya Sangh. 21] In the light of above discussion it is required to be seen if really there is need of custodial interrogation of the applicant and necessity of the applicant to be arrested. In that respect the grounds on which the claim of bail is resisted are that the applicant may pressurise the witnesses by using his political position as corporator and may tamper with investigation and he being resident of same building, he may threaten and pressurize the victim and complainant and that the girl is under tremendous .. 15 .. Anticipatory Bail No.747/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) tension and she is mentally disturbed because of the incident and that release of the applicant on bail may further traumatize her and that the applicant may indulge in similar offence in future and the mobile phone of the applicant is to be seized on which he stated to have made phone call to the complainant for setting the dispute and that the applicant is having criminal antecedents. So far as the contention that the mobile phone of the applicant is to be seized it has to be mentioned that the applicant is ready to give undertaking that he is ready to hand over his mobile phone to the police. Then, so far as the apprehension about pressurizing the complainant or threatening the victim girl etc. is concerned, I am of the view that that can be taken care of by imposing certain conditions including the condition not to enter the building and not to try to communicate the complainant or victim girl in any manner till completion of investigation. Even so far as the submission on behalf of prosecution that other offences are registered against the applicant, on one hand it is well settled that pendency of other offence cannot be a ground for rejection of bail. 22] Even so far as submission that release of accused would hamper the investigation is concerned, it is to be mentioned that time and again it has been laid down and even in the ruling in case of Siddharam Mhetre referred supra it is observed that the object of Article 21 of Constitution of India is to prevent encroachment upon personal liberty in any manner and in the same ruling it is further observed that the State can consider the following suggestions in proper perspective then perhaps it may not be necessary to curtail the personal liberty of the accused in a .. 16 .. Anticipatory Bail No.747/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) routine manner and the suggestions are : i) Direct the accused to joint investigation and only when the accused does not co­operate with the investigating agency, then only the accused be arrested; ii ) Seize either the passport or such other related documents, such as, the title deeds of properties or the Fixed Deposit Receipts/ Share Certificates of the accused; iii ) Direct the accused to execute bonds; iv ) The accused may be directed to furnish sureties of number of persons which according to the prosecution are necessary in view of the facts of the particular case. v) The accused be directed to furnish undertaking that he would not visit the place where the witnesses reside so that the possibility of tampering of evidence or otherwise influencing the course of justice can be avoided. vi ) Bank accounts be frozen for small duration during investigation. Even it is further observed therein that in case the arrest is imperative, the arresting officer must clearly record the reasons for the arrest of the accused before the arrest in the case diary. Keeping in mind above, if the facts of the present case are taken into consideration, the aspect of previous rivalry between the parties is material and in the light of that when it is specifically contended that because of such rivalry false case is filed appear to be worth consideration. Then, even looking to the allegations made the custodial interrogation of the applicant do not appear to be necessary and the purpose can be served by putting certain conditions including direction to the applicant to join the .. 17 .. Anticipatory Bail No.747/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) investigation. Even the submission on behalf of prosecution that the accused had not co­operated with the investigating agency it has to be mentioned that the applicant stated to have attended the police station and even stated to be ready to deposit his mobile phone with police and at the cost of repetition it can be said that the condition to furnish undertaking that he would not visit the place where the complainant and victim girl are residing also can be imposed. 23] Even it is well settled that at the time of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is that whether the applicant would tamper with prosecution evidence or would abscond and in that respect the applicant is stated to be permanent resident of Mira Road and is even a sitting corporator of Mira Bhayander Municipal Corporation and there is no question of he being absconding and he also stated that he is ready to abide by all conditions and is ready to co­operate with the investigating machinery. 24] In view of all above discussion I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant is entitled to be released on anticipatory bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER 1) The application is allowed. 2) The interim anticipatory bail granted to the applicant namely Ashwin Shamji Kasodariya vide order passed below Exh.3 on 25.03.2015 is hereby confirmed. .. 18 .. Anticipatory Bail No.747/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) 3) In the event of arrest of the applicant for offence punishable under section 354, 506 of I.P.C. and under section 9(C) and 10 of P.O.C.S.O. Act registered under C.R.No.I­124/2015 at Mira Road Police Station, he shall be released on furnishing P.R. bond of Rs.25,000/­ [rupees twenty five thousand only] with one or two sureties in the like amount, subject to following conditions­ a) The applicant shall attend the concerned police station on every Saturday between 5.00 p.m. to 7.00 p.m. and shall co­operate with the investigating machinery. b) He shall not visit the place where the complainant and victim are residing and shall not try to contact or communicate with them in any manner. c) He shall deposit his mobile phone with the investigating officer if called upon to do so. d) He shall not, directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer. e) He shall not leave India without the previous permission of the Court. f) He shall not tamper with prosecution evidence. Date : 07.05.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.

State of Maharashtra (Through Nizampur Police station Bhiwandi) ... Prosecution VERSUS Ehsan Ramajan Ansari, age 40 yrs., r/at Loom Factory, of Akram Seth, Machha Campa, Khadipar, Bhiwandi, Thane. … Accused Offence punishable u/secs. 376 I.P.C. & u/s 8 & 12 of POCSO Act. APPEARANCE : Ld. A.P. P. Smt. Moholkar for prosecution. Ld.Adv. Shri Pandhare for accused. JUDGMENT (Delivered on 2nd January 2018.) 1] Accused stands prosecuted by police station officer, Nizampur Police Station, Bhiwandi for the charge of offences of committing rape on victim girl aged 4 years punishable u/s 376 I.P. C. and for committing sexual assault punishable u/s 8 & for committing sexual harassment punishable u/s 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act (for short POCSO Act). ..2/- ..2.. Spl.C. No.81/2017 (Exh.No. 38) 2] In brief, it is the case of prosecution that informant Nasreen Mohammad Hussain lodged the complaint on 22.11.2016 alleging that victim girl aged about 4 years is her daughter. On 16.11.2016 she saw from the house that when victim was playing infront of house, accused Ehsan residing backside of her house lifted victim and moving his hand on her private part. Therefore, she went to take victim. That time accused took bite below the umbilicus of victim. Persons residing there came there and thereafter accused ran away. 3] On the basis of complaint, Crime No.I­186/2016 for the offence punishable u/s 376 of I.P.C. r/w S. 8 & 12 of POCSO Act was registered and API Naravane carried out investigation. During investigation, he prepared spot panchanama and arrested accused under panchanma. He recorded statement of other witnesses. He collected birth certificate of victim. He sent victim and accused for examination. He collected C.A. report in respect of victim and accused. On completion of investigation, he submitted chargesheet before the Court against accused. 4] Charge Exh.7 was framed & explained to accused to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. His defence is that of total denial. 5] Considering the case of the prosecution following points arise for my determination and I have recorded my findings thereon for the reasons discussed below. POINTS FINDINGS 1 Does the prosecution prove that on 16.11.2016 at 10.30 hours, in open place of Ahmed Road, Khadipar, Bhiwandi ..3/- ..3.. Spl.C. No.81/2017 (Exh.No. 38) committed rape on victim and thereby committed an offence punishable u/sec. 376 of I.P.C.? No. 2 Does the prosecution further prove that on the above mentioned date,time and place accused committed sexual assault on victim as per Sec. 7 punishable u/s 8 of PCSO Act? No. 3 Does the prosecution further prove that on the above mentioned date,time and place accused committed sexual harassment on No. victim as per Sec. 11 punishable u/s 12 of PCSO Act? 4 What order ? As per final order. REASONS Points Nos. 1 to 3 : 6] All the points are interlinked to each other, hence in order to avoid the repetition of evidence they are clubbed together. 7] Prosecution examined in all 3 witnesses. P.W.1 informant Nasreen at Exh.13, PW 2 Sageer at Exh.25 and PW 3 I.O. Mr. Narvane at Exh.27. Then prosecution filed evidence closing pursis at Exh.36. Statement of accused recorded u/s 313 of Cr.P. C. is at Exh.37. Prosecution relied on documents viz. C.A. report Exh.11, Aadhar Card Exh.14, Pan Card Exh.15, birth certificate Exh.16, statement dt. 22.11.2016 Exh.167, spot panchanama Exh.18, search panchanama Exh.18, medical certificate Exh.26, printed FIR Exh.29, medical certificate of accused Exh.31, letters to C.A. Exhs. 32 & 34 & C.A. reports Exhs. 33 & 35. ..4/- ..4.. Spl.C. No.81/2017 (Exh.No. 38) 8] Heard the Ld. APP and the Ld. Defence counsel. PW 1 informant deposed that nothing was happened with victim on 16.11.2016. She went to police station to lodge complaint against her husband who used to beat her under the influence of liquor and not provide amount for daily use. When she is reluctant, then the Ld. APP cross examined her at length but nothing incriminating brought on record from the mouth of informant. It is to be noted that I.O. denied that at the relevant time, informant was intending to lodge complaint against her husband. 9] PW 2 Sageer deposed that he do not know what happened on 16.12.2016 as he was present in the shop. He was also cross examined by the Ld. APP but he denied that on 16.12.2016 while victim was playing accused put her and moved his hand on her private part and he took bite below her umbilicus. He denied that he witnessed the incident. On perusal of report, the name of this witness is not mentioned. The evidence of I.O. is formal in nature. It is to be noted that when informant and the alleged eyewitness have not supported the case of prosecution, then prosecution cannot prove the charge levelled against the accused on the basis of evidence of I.O. 10] The evidence on record is not sufficient to prove the charge levelled against accused beyond reasonable doubt for offence punishable u/s 376 of IPC and the offence punishable u/s 8 & 12 of POCSO Act. With this discussion, I answer the point Nos. 1 to 3 accordingly and to proceed to pass the following order. : ORDER : 1] Accused Ehsan Ramajan Ansari is hereby acquitted u/s 235 ..5/- ..5.. Spl.C. No.81/2017 (Exh.No. 38) of Cr.P.C. from the charge of offence punishable u/s 376 of I.P.C & u/s 8 & 12 of POCSO Act. 2] Accused be set at liberty forthwith if not required in any other offence/crime. 3] Accused shall comply forthwith the provision U/Sec.437­A Cr.P.C. by furnishing fresh P.R. State of Maharashtra (Through Rabale Police station) ...Prosecution VERSUS Manoj Gorakh Gotpagar, Age 28 yrs., R/at­ Room No. 481, Chatrapati Shivajinagar, Talawali Naka, Ghansoli, Navi Mumbai. …Accused. Offence punishable u/secs. 376, 506 of I.P.C. & u/s. 6 & 10 of POCSO Act. APPEARANCE : Ld.A.P. P. Smt. Moholkar for the prosecution. Ld.Adv. Smt Bhavika Patil for accused. JUDGMENT (Delivered on 3rd May 2018) 1] Accused stands prosecuted by police station officer, Rabale Police Station for the charge of offences punishable u/sec. 376 for rape of I.P. Code and U/s. 506 for criminal intimidation and U/s.6 for aggravated penetrative sexual assault and U/s. 10 for aggravated sexual assault of POCSO Act. 2] In brief, it is the case of prosecution that informant­victim girl is residing at the house of accused as he is her cousin,who resides ..2/- CNR NO.MHTH01-002117-2017 ..2.. .. 1 .. bail no.769/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 769/2015 This application is filed by applicants namely Raghyeshyam alias Raju Brijkishor Naath for their release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no.137/2015 registered at Kashimira police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 372, 373 of I.P.C. and section 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act) and also under section 3, 4, 5, 6, and 7(1) of Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act (hereinafter in short referred to as ''I.T.P.A.''). It was contended and argued that the applicants are arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicants alongwith other accused were conducting prostitution business by procuring girls including minor and were earning livelihood from said business. It is further contended and argued that the applicants are falsely implicated on the basis of suspicion. It is further contended and argued that the applicants have not earned money from prostitution business and have not even purchased any property from such money. It is further submitted that the applicants are permanent residents of the address given and that if the present applicants/accused are released on bail, they will co­ operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply as per Exhibit 4 and it was contended and argued that on receiving secret information police conducted raid and during said raid it revealed that one minor girl namely .. 2 .. bail no.769/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Kavita Nepali was being compelled to do prostitution and was sent to give sexual pleasure to the customer. It is further contended and argued that the accused persons including the applicants were doing such illegal activity and were accepting money from the customers in the form of their livelihood. It is further contended and argued that the accused were charging Rs.1 lac from each customer to provide minor girl for ''virgin break''. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicants/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicants threatening the victim girl and other prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicants is released on bail they may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicants are not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 372, 373 of I.P.C. and section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and also section 3, 4, 5, 6, 7(1) of I.T.P.A. with the allegation that they have compelled the minor girl Kavita Nepali to do prostitution though they were knowing that she was minor aged 17 years and even it is alleged that they have been making minor girls available for prostitution and have been charging Rs.1 lac for ''virgin break'' and though it is also case of prosecution and clear from the complaint as well as panchnama of raid that the applicants/accused were caught at the time of raid and they were found in possession of some money etc., it is to be mentioned that the applicants have come up with the case that they have been falsely implicated in this crime. Then, it is also to be mentioned that though it is alleged that the .. 3 .. bail no.769/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) applicants/accused and other accused have been charging Rs.1 lac from each customer for making the girl available for ''virgin break'', no recovery of amount appear to be there. Then, so far as the aspect that the applicants/ accused have purchased huge property in their name or in the name of their relatives out of the money earned from said business, that aspect will have to be decided after the trial on the basis of evidence adduced in that regard and it would be premature to conclude at this stage that such property, if any, purchased by the applicants/accused or co­ accused is out of ill­gotten money from the prostitution business. 4] Then, it is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicants would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicants tampering with prosecution evidence if they are released on bail. In that respect it is contended by the applicants that they are permanent residents of the address given and they will not abscond if released on bail and that they are ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 5] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicants/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 6] Then, it has also to be mentioned that looking the allegations against the accused the investigation in the matter may have almost completed but the charge­sheet is yet to be .. 4 .. bail no.769/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge­sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicants/accused in jail for uncertain period. 7] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicants can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused namely Radhyeshyam alias Raju Brijkishor Naath and Bharat Kamal Haria are released on P.R. bond of Rs.20,000/­ [rupees twenty thousand only] each with one surety each in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ The applicants/accused shall not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and the prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. They shall not leave India without permission of this Court. They shall furnish proof of residence. Date : 26.06.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.

1 Spl. (POCSO) Case No. 82/2016. Presented on­ 23.03.2016. Registered on­ 23.03.2016. Decided on­ 29.11.2017. Duration­ Y­1 M­8 D­6 IN THE COURT OF SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE. [Presided over by A.S. Bhaisare, Special Judge (POCSO Act) and Additional Sessions Judge­2, Thane.] SPECIAL CASE (POCSO) NO. 82/2016. Exh. no. The State (Through Ganeshpuri Police Station) ..Complainant. V/s. Ajay Raghunath Wad, Age 20 years, Occ. Labour, R/o. Chalisgaon, Post Saywan, Tal. Vasai, Dist. Palghar. ..Accused. ___________________________________________________________ Appearances­ Learned A.P.P. Smt. Talhar, for the State. Learned Advocate Shri. Kanhere, for the accused. ___________________________________________________________ 2 Spl. (POCSO) Case No. 82/2016. JUDGMENT (Delivered on 29.11.2017.) 1] Accused Ajay Raghunath Wad is facing trial for the offences punishable u/s. 376, 363 of I.P.C. r/w. Sec. 3 punishable u/s. 4 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 2] It is the case of prosecution that victim aged about 16 years and 9 months, who was studying in 11 th standard, on 20.02.15 at about 7.00 a.m., left the house at village Saywan in the pretext to go to her school, but she did not return back for a considerable time. Enquiry was made with her girl friend Ku. Prishila Sudam Madake and with others. But, victim was not found. Enquiry about Ajay Raghunath Wad was also made, but he was not found in his house. Mobile of accused was also found switched off. By these allegations, Sadhana Ugale had lodged her report (Exh.5) with Ganeshpuri police station, in which offence vide C.R. no. I­ 18/15 u/s. 363 of I.P.C. came to be registered. P.W.3 P.S.I. Shri. Rawan carried out investigation. He rushed to the spot and recorded spot panchanama Exh. 6 in presence of panchas (It is admitted by defence.). Lastly, accused along with victim girl were found at Wada. They were taken to police station. They both were referred for their medical examination. Doctor had examined them. Clothes of accused Exh.7 and clothes of victim Exh.8 are seized. Bonafide certificate of victim was obtained. Statements of witnesses were recorded. She was referred for her occipital test and for giving statement u/s. 164 of Cr.P.C. to the doctor and Ld. Judicial Magistrate First Class, respectively. After investigation, charge­sheet was submitted in the Special Court. 3] Heard both sides. I framed the charge against the accused for 3 Spl. (POCSO) Case No. 82/2016. the offences punishable under section 376, 363 of I.P.C. r/w. Sec. 3 punishable u/s. 4 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, on 22/08/2017. Details of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular, to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. His defence is of total denial. 4] During trial, defence has admitted certain documents on record, i.e. spot panchanama (Exh.6), panchanama of seizure of clothes of accused (Exh.7), panchanama of seizure of clothes of victim (Exh.8), panchanama of condition of spots where accused had taken to victim (Exh.9), physical examination report of accused by I.G.M. hospital (Exh.10), physical examination report of victim by I.G.M. hospital (Exh.12), Age certificate of victim(Exh.13). 5] To bring home the guilt of the accused for the charges leveled against him, the prosecution has examined as many as three witnesses i.e. P.W. Name of witness Exh. Description No. No. 1] Sadhana Sadanand Ugale 4 Mother of victim. 2] Victim girl 11 Victim. 3] Anil Bhausaheb Ravan 14 Investigating officer. 6] Accused did not enter into witness box. He has not examined defence witness. 7] Heard learned A.P.P. Smt. Talhar for the State and learned counsel Shri. Kanhere for the accused. Following points arise for my determination, which are being answered for the reasons given herein­ below. 4 Spl. (POCSO) Case No. 82/2016. POINTS FINDINGS 1] Whether prosecution proved that in No. between 20.02.2015 at 07.00 hours to 02.03.2015 at 16.00 hours, at Vajreshwari, Wada, Kalwa, accused had committed rape i.e. penetrative sexual assault on the minor daughter of complainant i.e. victim aged 16 years and 9 months, after kidnapping her ? 2] Whether prosecution proved that in the No. above period and place, accused had kidnapped the minor daughter of complainant i.e. victim aged 16 years and 9 months, from the lawful guardianship of her parents ? 3] What order ? As per final order. REASONS POINT NOS. 1 AND 2 8] P.W.2 victim had stated her age during her oral testimony as 20 years. According to her, she was born on 14.05.98. She was studying in Vajreshwari New English High­School in 11 th standard in the year 2015. On 20.02.15, accused had followed her and asked her to come to the house of relatives. Accordingly, she went along with him to the house of his relatives at Kudus, Kelwe and then, they returned back to Wada. On material point, she turned hostile and had not supported to the prosecution story. 9] P.W.2 victim has not stated in her evidence that she was kidnapped by the accused without consent of her parents and out of their lawful guardianship. 5 Spl. (POCSO) Case No. 82/2016. 10] P.W.1 Sadhana Ugale deposed in her evidence that victim was aged about 19 years on the day of her evidence. Her evidence is recorded on 11.10.17. It means, on the date of incident i.e. on 20.02.15, certainly victim might be completed 17 years of her age. This witness has not stated the date of birth of victim. As per ossification test Exh.13, victim on 16.04.15 was found approximately of the age of 17­18 years. No birth certificate of the victim is placed on record. If date of birth of victim as per her evidence as 14.05.98 is considered, then on the date of incident i.e. on 20.02.15, victim was aged about 16 years, 9 months and 6 days old. She was also studying in 11th standard. She along with accused went to Kudus, Kelwe and Wada and she had visited in the public place, but there was no hue and cry. She had not made any complaint with anyone. She was knowing the consequences of her own act. She had also attended the age of understanding. Accused had not kidnapped her, but on his call, she went along with accused. So, it cannot be said that accused had taken or carried victim with him without the consent of her parents and out of lawful guardianship of her parents. Therefore, it is very difficult to hold that accused kidnapped the victim. 11] P.W.2 victim in her evidence, has not stated that accused had established his sexual relations with her without her consent or with her consent. She was suggested by Ld. A.P.P. in her cross­examination that at Kelwe and Kandivali, accused had established his physical relations with her, but she has denied both these suggestions. In her cross­examination, she deposed that she had not stated that she had love affair with accused. As per her statement, portion marked D, she has stated before police that she had love affair with the accused. 12] Victim was referred to hospital for her medical examination on 6 Spl. (POCSO) Case No. 82/2016. 03.03.15. Doctor had examined her. Medical report is placed on record vide Exh. 12. It is admitted by defence. There was history before medical officer that there was kissing, fondling and sleeping naked with Ajay. However, there was no history of penetration. P.V. examination was not done. Hymen of victim was found intact and was not torn. Victim was found able for sexual intercourse. However, doctor has found that there was no penetrative sexual intercourse. So also, no injuries were found on the private part of the victim. Therefore, it is very difficult to hold that there was any kind of sexual intercourse at the hands of accused. Consequently, it can be held that accused committed no offence of even rape. 13] Having considered the facts and circumstances of the matter, evidence on record and discussed reasons, prosecution failed to prove the alleged offence against the accused. Hence, I answer both the points accordingly and proceed to pass the following order. ORDER 1] Accused Ajay Raghunath Wad is hereby, acquitted under sec. 235(1) of the Criminal Procedure Code, of the offences punishable u/s. 376, 363 of I.P.C. r/w. Sec. 3 punishable u/s. 4 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 2] Accused Ajay Raghunath Wad be enlarged on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ with surety of like amount. The effect of this bail order 7 Spl. (POCSO) Case No. 82/2016. will remain in force for the period of six months from today, as per section 437­(A) of Cr.P.C. 3] Muddemal property being worthless, be destroyed after appeal period is over. Thane, (A.S. Bhaisare) Date­ 29.11.2017. Special Judge (POCSO Act) and Additional Sessions Judge­2, Thane.

In all such circumstance keeping aside the aspect of applicability of provisions of Muslim Personal .. 3 .. bail no.784/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Law at this stage and the documentary proof, which is of course subject to the test of evidentiary value, since it is the defence of the accused that he is falsely implicated and that it is a case of consent, the aspect as to the age of the girl and her consent and whether the act of the accused amounts to rape or not, will have to be decided on merits after trial. In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 5] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 6] Then, it has also to be mentioned that the investigation in the matter though almost completed, the charge sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge sheet and then to conclude the trial in the .. 4 .. bail no.784/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 7] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Sabir Kausar Khan is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ The applicant/accused shall attend the concerned police station as and when called till filing of the charge sheet and shall co­operate in investigation. He shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and the prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this Court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 18.04.2015 (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.

.. 1 .. Bail no.785/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exhibit 1 in Criminal Bail Application No.785/2015 This application is filed by applicant Ravi Shivaji Gavali for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. I-62/2015 registered at A.P.M.C. police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 363, 366A, 376(2)(i) of I.P.C. and section 4, 6, 8, 17 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act) and also under section 3(1)(xii), 6 of The Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act. It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the accused committed sexual assault on the minor girl aged 12 years after kidnapping her. It is further contended and argued that no such incident has happened and the applicant is falsely implicated with ulterior motive. It is further submitted that there are no criminal antecedents to the discredit of the applicant/accused. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co-operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that at the relevant time the complainant had gone down her residential building to drop her son for going to school and at that time the accused induced minor daughter of the complainant and kidnapped with intention to force or seduce her to have illicit intercourse and then committed penetrative sexual assault on said girl and thereafter over her to other accused persons who also committed rape on her. It is also submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl and the prosecution .. 2 .. Bail no.785/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear the offence charged against the applicant/accused are of very serious nature under section 376(2) (i), 506(2) of I.P.C. and section 4, 6, 8, 17 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and also under section 3(1)(xii), 6 of Prevention of Atrocities Act with the allegation that the accused had forcible sexual intercourse with the minor girl aged 12 years after kidnapping her from lawful guardianship of her parents with a view to have forcible sexual intercourse with her. No doubt, as rightly pointed out on behalf of applicant/accused he is not an F.I.R. named accused and the complaint is seen to have been lodged by mother of the girl against an unknown person and it is also mentioned in the complaint that since about one year the victim was keeping herself isolated and was becoming aggressive and even was under treatment of psychiatrist. But then, the fact cannot be ignored that as per version of the complainant, the victim girl went missing and therefore a missing complaint was lodged and during investigation names of the accused seen to have been revealed during the investigation and even from the statement of the girl it revealed that she was taken away by the accused and was raped/subjected to sexual intercourse and even it is contended that she was gang- raped by applicant and other accused. Then, it is also stated that the C.D.R. of the phone of the applicant/accused show that he was in contact with the girl. Then, looking to the nature of offence charged and the manner in which it is stated to have been committed and in view of further fact that the girl is aged 12 years and stated to be mentally disturbed and it is alleged that the applicant/accused and co -accused took disadvantage of her condition or may that they themselves are responsible for her such condition, I am of the view that thorough investigation into the matter is necessary. Then, it is stated that the investigation is yet .. 3 .. Bail no.785/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) to be completed and it is still in progress and in such circumstance release of accused on bail at this stage would hamper the investigation. Even one accused is stated to be absconding and he is also be arrested and in case of release of applicant/accused on bail at this stage, possibility of the applicant/accused helping other accused to keep himself absconding also is there. 4] No doubt, it is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. But then, it is also to be mentioned that besides that, the nature of allegation, gravity of offence and the manner in which it is stated to have been committed are also the factors to be taken into consideration while deciding the bail application wherein such serious allegations of penetrative sexual assault on minor girl are made. 5] Then, the apprehension expressed on behalf of prosecution that since the offence is of very serious nature in regard to sexual assault on minor girl the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is also there and even the apprehension that the accused may threaten and pressurize the witnesses is also well founded. 6] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is not a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail at this stage. I therefore pass the following order - ORDER The application is rejected. Date 08.05.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Additional Sessions Judge-1, Thane.

Elder daughter/victim No.1 was studying in 5 th standard and younger/victim ..2/- ..2.. Spl.C. No.88/2017 (Exh.No. 32) No.2 was studying in 3rd standard in S.M. Public High School, Bhayander. Their grandmother and other relatives told her that victims are small and therefore, she ignored and accordingly victims did not attend the tuition on that day. They also did not attend the tuition on 28.1.2017. on 29th there was Sunday being holiday to tuition. On 30.1.2017 as usual both the victims went to school. After school hours, they returned to home. Thereafter she asked victm No.1 to go to tuition at 4.00 p.m. Thereupon, victim No.1 refused to go and started crying. She took her in confidence and thereby victm No.1 told that since last 1 month to 1­1/2 months when she attended the tuition, she used to sit near the door of kitchen. That time husband of teacher Smt. Sawant used to stand behind the curtain of kitchen and used to touch his leg to her bum. He also used to upword her top/T­shirt by his leg. On one occasion, he up worded her T­shirt by his leg and by his hand hold her abdomen. Victim No.1 got frightened of him and therefore, she was not willing to attend tuition. Thereafter informant made enquiry with victim No.2 who told whenever she went to tuition at late time, she was made to sit near door of kitchen and that time husband of teacher Smt. Sawant used to touch his leg to her bum. After consultation with her husband, informant lodged the complaint. 3] On the basis of complaint, Crime No.I­43/2017 for the offence punishable u/s 354 of I.P.C. r/w S. 8 of POCSO Act was ..3/- ..3.. Spl.C. No.88/2017 (Exh.No. 32) registered and API Kolhe carried out investigation. On 31.1.2017 he prepared spot panchanama. He recorded statements of victim girls in question and answer form. He collected birth certificates and Aadhar Cards of the victims. He wrote a letter to Court for recording statements of victims u/s 164 of Cr.P.C. He got prepared map of spot from Circle Officer. He also arrested accused and recorded statement of other witnesses. After completion of investigation he submitted chargesheet against accused before the Special Judge (POCSO Act), Thane. 4] Charge Exh.4 was framed & explained to accused to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. His defence is that of total denial. 5] Considering the case of the prosecution following points arise for my determination and I have recorded my findings thereon for the reasons discussed below. POINTS FINDINGS 1 Does the prosecution prove that during 1 to 1­1/2 months prior to 25.1.2017 in Room No.504, 5th floor, A Wing, Harikrishna Dham, Pleasant Park, Mire road accused used criminal force to the victim girls aged 11 years and 9 years with intent to outrage their modesty and thereby committed an offence punishable u/sec. 354 of I.P.C.? No. 2 Does the prosecution further prove that on the above mentioned dates, time and place accused committed sexual assault on victim girls and thereby committed an offence punishable u/s 8 of PCSO Act? No. 3 What order ? As per final order. ..4/- ..4.. Spl.C. No.88/2017 (Exh.No. 32) REASONS Points Nos. 1 & 2 : 6] Both the points are interlinked to each other, hence in order to avoid the repetition of evidence they are clubbed together. 7] Prosecution examined in all 3 witnesses. P.W.1 Sita/informant at Exh.13, PW 2 Victim No.1 at Exh.16 and PW 3 Kolhe, I.O. at Exh.21. On 6.11.2017 prosecution produced victim no.2 for evidence but she does not know the sanctity of oath. Therefore, she was not examined. Then prosecution filed evidence closing pursis at Exh.30. Statement of accused recorded u/s 313 of Cr.P. C. is at Exh.31. Prosecution relied on documents viz. report Exh.14, FIR Exh.15, panchanama Exh.17, birth certificate of victims Exh.18 & 19, statements of victims Exhs. 22 & 23, letter Exh.24, statements of victims u/s 164 of Cr.P.C. Exhs. 25 & 26, statement of informant Exh.27, spot map Exh.28 and arrest panchanama Exh.29. 8] The Ld. APP submitted that the incident took place at the residence of accused. The victim girls are minor as their date of birth is at all not challenged by the accused. PW 1 Sita is the mother of victims and when she enquired from the victims the cause for not attending tuition, then she came to know the sexual harassment at the hands of accused to the victims and therefore, she lodged the complaint. Her evidence is as per the complaint. The evidence of victim No1/PW 2 is sufficient to establish that she used to attend the tuition at the residence of accused and whenever she was late in attending tuition she used to sit near curtain and during the span of 1 month to 1­1/2 months accused did act of touching her bum by leg on 5­6 times. The defence ..5/- ..5.. Spl.C. No.88/2017 (Exh.No. 32) of accused is that the parents of the victims failed to pay the tuition fees and on demand they lodged false complaint, however, accused failed to give details regarding non payment of tuition fees or any demand. For the first time in the statement u/s 313 of Cr.P.C., accused came with the defence of alibi that he used to leave house from 9.30 a.m. till 9.30 p.m. but no such evidence is brought on record. Thus, the presumption is in favour of prosecution and as such, prosecution established the charge levelled against accused. 9] Per contra, the Ld. Counsel for accused vehemently submitted that the evidence of PW 1 Sita is hearsay as she has no personal knowledge about the incident and she never visited to the house of accused prior to alleged incident, which shows that the parents of the victims failed to pay the tuition fees as it is not the case of prosecution that accused or his better half used to collect tuition fees at the residence of victims. Prosecution also failed to prove that complainant paid tuition fees to the better half of accused and as such it is established that the tuition fees was not paid by the complainant and on demand, she lodged false complaint. 10] In the evidence of victim,there are omissions and contradictions, which are proved through the evidence of I.O. and those are material one as it is the allegation of victim that on5­6 occasions accused did act of touching her bum by his leg from behind curtain but prosecution failed to prove the existence of curtain in the spot panchanama itself. The Ld. Counsel further submitted that as a matter of fact, there is no curtain in between hall and kitchen and that fact is also admitted by I.O. Even accused in his statement u/s 313 of Cr.P.C. stated the said fact. Thus, the entire case revolved around the curtain ..6/- ..6.. Spl.C. No.88/2017 (Exh.No. 32) but prosecution failed to establish the backbone of prosecution story i.e. existence of curtain. The evidence of I.O. is material one as he admitted that he made enquiry with Nidhi and Riya who are co­student in tuition and they stated that during 4 p.m. to 6.00 p.m. accused never present in the house. The contention of accused is that he used to leave house from 9.30 a.m. till 9.30 p.m. and as such it is clear that during tuition hours, accused never present in the house. He further submitted that mother of Nidhi stated to I.O. that accused did not commit any bad act. 11] He further submitted that victim No.1/PW 2 was having a capacity to differentiate good and bad act. However, non disclosing of bad act allegedly done by accused to her friends (Co­students of tuition/school), parents and grandmother, also raises doubt not only on the version of PW 2 but also creates a cloud on the entire case of prosecution. 12] The Ld. Defence counsel relied on citation Pandurang Vs. State, reported in 2005 ALL MR (Cri) 776(S.C.), in which, it is held that accused allegedly to have outraged modesty of woman by embracing her from back and touching her breasts. Strained relationship between parties over the issue of vacating premises. Witnesses giving different versions about exact place and manner of occurrence. Held that having regarding to totality of facts of the case applicant was entitled to be given benefit of doubt. The ratio laid down in the citation is not applicable to the present case as facts are different. He further relied on citation K.Venkateshwrlu Vs. State, reported in AIR 2012 Supreme Court, 2955, in which, it is held that child witness­evidence­reliance to be place only after scrutiny of its evidence in background and context of other evidence on record. This ..7/- ..7.. Spl.C. No.88/2017 (Exh.No. 32) ratio is applicable as guiding principle. 13] Admittedly, victims were studying in S.M. Public High School, Bhayander in 5th and 3rd standard respectively. They used to go to 5th floor of Harikrishna Dham building to one teacher Sawant for tuition. Victim No.1 used to go for tuition from 4.00 p.m. to 6.00 p.m. and victim No.2 used to attend tuition from 9.00 a.m. to 11.00 a.m. The age of victims is also not in dispute as they are minor on the date of alleged incident. 14] PW 1­informant deposed the incident which was narrated by the victims and as such, she has no personal knowledge about the incident and on verification, she lodged complaint. Thus, her evidence is relevant for lodging of complaint only and as such, it is necessary to concentrate on the evidence of victim No.1/Pw­2. 15] PW 2/victim No.1 deposed that husband of Sawant teacher used to come from behind and used to touch her bum. When she used to attend the class at late hours, she used to sit near curtain and that time he was doing that act. That time he used to come from bedroom and from behind the curtain he was doing such act. Such thing was done with her for 5 to 6 occasions during 1 month to 1­1/2 months. Thus the evidence of victim shows that whenever she was late she used to sit near curtain which is allegedly in between hall and kitchen. However, the spot panchanama Exh.17 is totally ..8/- ..8.. Spl.C. No.88/2017 (Exh.No. 32) silent in respect of existence of curtain. In the evidence of I.O., it is brought on record that in the panchanama Exh.17 there is no mention that there was no pelmet or curtain in between hall and kitchen. During investigation curtain was not attached. It did not so happen that even curtain was there on the spot, but deliberately said fact is not mentioned in the panchanama. Thus, the evidence of I.O. washed out the contention of victim regarding existence of curtain on the spot. Hence, non existence of curtain on the spot creates a doubt regarding happening of incident. 15] On perusal of the statement Exh.25 of victim No.1 recorded u/s 164 of Cr.P.C., it seems that there is also mention about curtain and also stated that whenever she was late, therefore, she used to sit near door in between bedroom and hall. However, in the FIR, it is mentioned that she used to sit near the door of kitchen. Thus, apparently, this is a minor thing as whenever victim was late, she used to sit near the door (which may be in between bedroom and hall or kitchen). It means, whenever she attended the tuition in time, some other student might have sat near the door but according to I.O., no other student or parents made any complaint in respect of bad act done or committed by accused. 16] The statement Exh.26 of victim No.2 is that she used to attend tuition class there is husband of teacher, he up worded her T­shirt and also touched to her bum by hand. Whether accused did bad act by leg or hand is not material as she further stated that ..9/- ..9.. Spl.C. No.88/2017 (Exh.No. 32) same act did by accused with Riya of Class 3 and Sanika of Class 9. However, the evidence of I.O. is contrary as he deposed that during enquiry, Riya stated to him that accused never present in the house. Thus, the evidence of I.O. does not support to the statement Exh.26 and that also creates a doubt on the story projected by the prosecution. 17] PW 2/victim deposed that lastly on 30th accused moved his hand on her abdomen and that thing was done by him in the class. However, FIR is otherwise, as from 28.1.2017 to 30.1.2017 victim failed to attend the tuition and therefore, no question arises to embrace her abdomen on 30.1.2017. Even in the statement Exh.25, she stated that on 25th accused put his hand on her waist. Thus, the FIR and her statement Exh.25 not corroborated to the evidence of victim. 18] It is to be noted that while assessing the evidence of child, it is necessary to go through the minor details as the child is to be tutored on the major facts but not on minor or vice­a­versa. In the complaint, it is mentioned that accused did act behind the curtain, however, on going through the spot panchanama Exh.17 which is nothing but the house of accused but there is nothing mentioned about the curtain. Secondly, victim knows the difference between good and bad act but non disclosing of the same either to her friends, grandmother or to parents creates doubt about happening of incident. 19] Therefore, the evidence of victim seems to be focused on the point of main incident of touching her bum by accused by leg in ..10/- ..10.. Spl.C. No.88/2017 (Exh.No. 32) respect of victim No.1 and in respect of victim No.2 by hand behind the curtain. Thus, the submission of defence counsel that victim is tutored on the main point and as such on the minor point there is no corroborative evidence is acceptable. It is to be noted that according to victim the bad act committed by accused behind curtain by his leg, but the question goes to the root of the case is that a person did such alleged act behind the curtain, then how victim was clear that the person behind the curtain is accused only. Under such circumstances I am inclined to discard the testimony of victim. When the testimony of victim is discarded, then the presumption which is in favour of prosecution u/s 29 of the POCSO Act is rebutted by accused. 20] So far as the defence is concerned, according to accused, complainant failed to pay tuition fees and on demand she lodged false complaint. Complainant denied the said suggestion. The Ld. APP vehemently submitted that there are no details about non payment of tuition fees by the complainant or any demand made by accused or his better half prior to incident. The defence is so vague as no details brought during cross examination of prosecution witnesses and in the statement u/s 313 of Cr.P.C. For want of details, the defence putforth by accused seems to be improbable and failed to pass the test of preponderance of probability that on the count of failure to pay tuition fees by the complainant and demand of the same by accused, false complaint filed. At the same time in view of the above discussion, the entire case of prosecution is also under the shadow of doubt. Therefore, it is just and proper to extend benefit to accused as prosecution and defence came with untrue facts and both versions have to be discarded. ..11/- ..11.. Spl.C. No.88/2017 (Exh.No. 32) 21] The evidence on record is not sufficient to prove the charge levelled against accused beyond reasonable doubt for offence punishable u/s 354 of IPC and the offence punishable u/s 8 of POCSO Act. With this discussion, I answer the point Nos. 1 & 2 accordingly and to proceed to pass the following order. :ORDER : 1] Accused Ashok Anant Sawant is hereby acquitted u/s 235 of Cr.P.C. from the charge of offence punishable u/s 354 of I.P.C & u/s 8 of POCSO Act. 2] Accused be released forthwith if not required in any other crime/case. 3] Accused shall comply forthwith the provision U/Sec.437­A Cr.P.C. by furnishing fresh P.R. Bond of Rs.10,000/­ and S.B. of like amount. Dictated and declared in open Court. Place : Thane (R.N.Bawankar) Date : 29.11.2017 Special Judge (POCSO Act), Thane ..12/- ..12.. Spl.C. 1 Bail No.804/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) Criminal Bail Application No.804/2016 Machindra Baliram Patil & 4 ors. .. Applicant versus The State of Maharashtra Through Diaghar Police Station .. Non­applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 1] By this application the applicants are seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. who were arrested on 24/03/2016 by Diaghar Police Station in connection with C.R.No.I­ 77/2016 registered for an offence punishable under section 452, 143, 147, 148 149, 354, 324, 323, 504, 506(2), 427 of I.P.C. and section 7,8,12 & 17 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as P.O.C.S.O. Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Mr.Naresh Pradhan for the applicant/accused and learned Spl.P.P. Mrs.S.E.Phad for State. I.O. present. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 24/03/2016 at the instance of the informant/father of victim­girl aged about 15 years with an indictment that accused persons with their 4 to 5 accomplish entered in their house with wooden rod and iron 2 Bail No.804/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) pipe and assaulted them by the said weapon and fist and kick blows and also outraged modesty of his minor daughter by disrobing her. 4] The learned Counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant/accused is falsely implicated. He submitted that all the accused are family members. There is political rivalry and dispute on property between the family of accused and informant. There was scuffle between the parties on the day of Holi and the accused only tried to rescue themselves and never committed any act as alleged in the F.I.R. particularly in respect of a minor girl. He further submitted that the cross case is registered from the side of accused against the informant and other person. The material part of the investigation is completed. The accused are ready to abide any condition imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing them on bail. 5] Per contra, the learned Spl.P.P. opposed the application on the ground that the offence is serious in respect of minor girl. She further submitted that the applicants are admitting their presence on the spot. The iron pipe and wooden log were used and house trespass was committed. The offence is serious and investigation is still in progress. There are chances of tampering of the witnesses and prayed for rejection of the application. 3 Bail No.804/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R., it appears that F.I.R, was lodged at the instance of father of the victim­girl aged 15 yrs with an indictment that accused persons entered in their house with iron pipe and wooden log and abused and assaulted them and also outraged the modesty of the victim­girl. However, no any injury appears to be received by the informant or any other person or by victim­girl. The wooden rod were already seized. There is cross complaint from the side of the accused persons. The material part of the investigation appears to have been completed. No doubt, the offence is serious in respect of the minor girl. However, the object of bail is neither punitive nor preventive but to secure the presence of the accused at the time of trial. No fruitful purpose would be served by further incarceration of accused. They are ready to abide by the conditions imposed by the Court. In such circumstances the apprehension of learned Spl.P.P. about tampering of witnesses and fleeing away from justice, can be addressed by imposing suitable conditions. Hence, I pass the following order ­ ORDER 1) The application is allowed. 2) Applicant namely 1] Machindra Baliram Patil, 2] Bhanudas Pandhari Patil, 3] Shatrughna Baburao Patil, 4] Bharat Baburao Patil and 5] Bholenath Baburao Patil be released on bail on their executing P.R. Bond of ₹ 15,000/­ 4 Bail No.804/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) [Rupees Fifteen Thousand only] each with one solvent surety in the like amount on the following conditions ­ A] Applicants shall attend the concerned police station on every Sunday in between 10.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon till filing of charge­sheet. B] Applicants shall not tamper with prosecution witnesses and shall not pressurize the victim­girl or her family. C] Applicants shall furnish their and their two blood relatives' address proofs and contact numbers and they are duty bound to inform I.O. and Court about the change of address, if any. D] The accused shall maintain the decency hearinafter. Thane. Date : 18/04/2016. (Ms. U.M. Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act), Thane.

Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Mr.R.K.Shukla for the applicant/accused and learned Spl.P.P. Mrs.R.A.Navale for State. The accused and victim­girl were staying in the same locality and there are chances of pressurizing the victim­ girl whose statement under section 164 of Cr. P.C. is yet to be recorded. The investigation is in progress and therefore prayed for rejection of application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R., it appears that F.I.R, was lodged at the instance of father of the victim­girl aged 13 yrs with an indictment that accused who is having a mobile shoppe used to stalk his minor daughter and by kissing her outraged her modesty and caused sexual harassment. From the indictment it appears that the material part of the investigation 3 Bail No.808/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) is completed. Nothing is to be seized from the accused. The accused is behind bar since 27 days. The material part of the investigation appears to have been completed. No doubt, the offence is serious in respect of the minor girl. However, the object of bail is neither punitive nor preventive but to secure the presence of the accused at the time of trial. No fruitful purpose would be served by further incarceration of accused. He is ready to abide by the conditions imposed by the Court. In such circumstances the apprehension of learned Spl.P.P. about tampering of witnesses and fleeing away from justice, can be addressed by imposing suitable conditions. Hence, I pass the following order ­ ORDER 1) The application is allowed. 2) Applicant namely Akhilesh Ramshabd Tiwari be released on bail on his executing P.R. Bond of ₹ 15,000/­ [Rupees Fifteen Thousand only] with one solvent surety in the like amount on the following conditions ­ A] Applicant shall attend the concerned police station on every Sunday in between 10.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon till filing of charge­sheet. B] Applicant shall not tamper with prosecution witnesses and shall not pressurize the victim­girl or her family. C] Applicant shall furnish his and his two blood 4 Bail No.808/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) relatives' address proofs and contact numbers and he is duty bound to inform I.O. and Court about the change of address, if any. D] The accused shall maintain the decency hearinafter. Thane. Date : 18/04/2016. (Ms. U.M. Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act), Thane.
