.. 1 .. bail no.812/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 812 of 2015 This application is filed by applicant Kalamuddin Sarfarazuddin Ali for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. I­62/2015 registered at A.P.M.C. police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 363, 366A, 376(2) of I.P.C. and section 4, 6, 8 and 17 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the co­accused kidnapped the victim girl and then committed rape on her and then gave her in custody of the present applicant/accused. It is further contended and argued that the applicant is falsely implicated in this crime only because he is the watchman of the building It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/ accused is released on bail, he will co­ operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that at the time of incident the complainant had gone down the building to leave her son for school and at that time the accused no.1 induced the victim girl and kidnapped her from the house of the complainant and took her to the room of his friend and committed rape on her there and thereafter he left the said girl at Turbhe Station and it is further contended that thereafter the wanted accused Ashik had taken the girl to accused no.3 Badal at Kamothe Saibaba temple and said Badal had taken her in the watchman's .. 2 .. bail no.812/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) cabin of Bista Corner sector no.19 Kamothe and he committed rape on her in the watchman's cabin and thereafter gave the victim girl in the custody of the present applicant/accused. It is further contended that the room where rape was committed on the victim girl was the watchman's cabin of the present applicant. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening and pressurizing the victim girl and the prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 363, 366A, 372(2)(I), 506(2), 34 of I.P.C. and section 4, 6, 8 and 17 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012(hereinafter in short referred to as ''P.O.C.S.O. Act''), as rightly pointed out on behalf of applicant/accused, the complaint is lodged against an unknown person referring that the act was committed by watchman and the incident took place in watchman's room and the role attributed to the applicant, even as per prosecution case, was that the girl was handed over to him and it is contended on behalf of applicant/accused that only because he is watchman of the building he has been arraigned in the offence and arrested. In such circumstance whether the allegations against the accused are true or not, would be the question to be decided on merits. Even nothing is to be recovered from the applicant/accused. 4] Even it is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is .. 3 .. bail no.812/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. 5] Even the submission on behalf of prosecution that the investigation is in progress and the accused is hailing from other State etc also, it has to be mentioned that it is well settled and even observed in a ruling cited on behalf of applicant in case of Sanjay alias Bablu alias Keja vs. State of Gujarat reported in 2002 ALL MR (Cri) 468 (S.C.) that merely because the accused is hailing from other State and he was likely to abscond, the accused cannot be kept in jail. Even it is to be mentioned that the present applicant is to get married and his scheduled date of marriage is 20.04.2015 and on that count also he has claimed for his release on bail. Copy of invitation card is brought on record. Then, though the marriage is stated to be performed at Gram Songadha, Tahsil Lalganj, District Mirzapur, Uttar Pradesh, it is stated that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and he is working as a watchman and will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 6] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions including the condition to furnish heavy surety and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 7] Then, it has also to be mentioned that the investigation in the matter though almost completed the charge sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge sheet and then to conclude the .. 4 .. bail no.812/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 8] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Kalamuddin Sarfarazuddin Ali is released on P.R. bond of Rs.20,000/­ [rupees twenty thousand only] with one or two sureties in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ The applicant/accused shall attend the concerned police station on every Wednesday between 10.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon till filing of the charge sheet and shall co­operate in investigation. He shall not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and the prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this Court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 10.04.2015 (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.

1 Spl. POCSO Case No. 77/2014. Presented on­ 04.04.2014. Registered on­ 04.04.2014. Decided on­ 03.05.2018. Duration­ Y­4 M­0 D­29 IN THE COURT OF SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE. [Presided over by A.S. Bhaisare, Additional Sessions Judge­2 and Special Judge (POCSO Act), Thane.] SPECIAL CASE (POCSO) NO. 77/2014. Exh. no. The State (Through Uttan Sagari Police Station) ..Complainant. V/s. Subodh Pandurang Shirke, Age 29 years, Occ. Service, R/o. Near Vimal Dairy, Kashinagar, 'C' Wing, Ratnasindhu, Ground floor, Room No. 103, Bhainder (E). ..Accused. ___________________________________________________________ Appearances­ Learned A.P.P. Smt. Talhar, P.P. Smt. Phad, for the State. Learned Advocate Shri. S.U. Misal, for the accused. ___________________________________________________________ JUDGMENT (Delivered on 03.05.2018.) 1] Accused Subodh Pandurang Shirke is facing trial for the 2 Spl. POCSO Case No. 77/2014. offences punishable u/s. 376, 506 of I.P.C. and u/s. 4 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 2] The prosecution case is that since prior to one year, there was friendship between complainant victim minor girl aged 16 years and accused Subodh Shirke who was residing in her neighbourhood. There was love affair between them and they were intending to marry with each­other. On Wednesday, as there was holiday, they both had been to Jyoti Park, Bhainder. However, as people were known to them, they went to Uttan Velankani beach. At that time, accused had established his sexual relations with her on the promise of marriage and thereafter, he committed sexual intercourse with her frequently. Accused had asked her that she should come whenever he would call her, else he would defame her. On 04.01.14, he had given call to her to establish sexual relations. The same was disclosed by her with her mother. By these allegations, on 05.01.14, victim had lodged her report with Uttan Sagari police station. It was registered vide C.R. no. I­ 01/2014 u/s. 376, 506 of I.P.C. and under sec. 6 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. A.P.I. Smt. Muthe had arrested the accused. Victim was referred for her medical examination. Accused was also referred for her medical examination. She rushed to the spot and recorded spot panchanama in presence of panchas which was shown by victim. Her clothes were seized. On 06.01.14, clothes of accused were seized. Statements of witnesses were recorded. After investigation, charge­sheet was submitted in the Special Court. 3] Heard both sides. I framed the charge against the accused for the offences punishable under section 376, 506 of I.P.C. and u/s. 4 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, on 18/07/2017. Details of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular, to 3 Spl. POCSO Case No. 77/2014. which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. His defence is of total denial. 4] During trial, defence has admitted no documents. 5] To bring home the guilt of the accused for the charges leveled against him, the prosecution has examined as many as seven witnesses i.e. P.W. Name of witness Exh. Description No. No. 1] Minor victim girl 6 Complainant/victim. 2] Tereja Fransis Uttankar 8 Panch of spot panchanama. 3] Rajani Shamrao Halgarg 12 Medical officer who had examined accused Subodh. 4] Kirti Suryakant Lad 13 Friend of victim girl. 5] Aasif Gani Mulani 15 Panch of seizure panchanama of clothes of accused. 6] Jayashri Milind Jadhav 16 Mother of victim. 7] Priyatama Balasaheb 18 Investigating officer. Muthe 6] Accused did not enter into witness box. He has not examined defence witness. 7] Heard learned Special P.P. Smt. Phad for the State. She submitted that victim was below 18 years of age. She was born on 19.12.97. Her date of birth was not challenged by accused. When first incident was taken place with the victim, she was aged about 15 years and was studying in 8th standard. Accused was 29 years old. She was taken by him to Velankani beach and raped thereat. Accused had not given any explanation. Mother of victim corroborated to the version of victim. There was last call of accused to the victim on 04.01.13. There was no reason to 4 Spl. POCSO Case No. 77/2014. falsely involve the accused. 8] Heard learned counsel Shri. S.U. Misal, for the accused. He submitted that there were friendly relations between accused and victim. They visited each­other frequently time to time at different places. Victim had suspected upon the character of accused. Her age is not proved. Accused is falsely involved. He has no bad antecedents. 9] Following points arise for my determination, which are being answered for the reasons given herein­below. POINTS FINDINGS 1] Whether prosecution proved that since No. one year till prior to about two months, on Velankani sea­shore on beech, in Uttan village, on giving false promise of marriage, accused committed aggravated penetrative sexual assault on complainant minor girl aged 16 years, from time to time ? 2] Whether prosecution proved that in the No. above period and place, accused had committed criminal intimidation to minor girl aged 16 years, to defame her ? 3] What order ? As per final order. REASONS POINT NOS. 1 AND 2 10] P.W.1 complainant victim minor girl deposed in her evidence 5 Spl. POCSO Case No. 77/2014. that­ She was born on 19.12.1997. In the year 2014, she was studying in 11th standard. Accused was residing near her building. When she was studying in 8 th standard, she had been to the grocery shop of Gattya. Accused was present there. At that time, he was trying to talk with her. He used to catch her on her school way and on the way of grocery shop. Thereafter, on one day, he had called her in Jyoti Park, Bhainder. So, she went there. When she was studying in 10 th, she was taken by him on tour, i.e. Velankani beach. He had asked for sex. She refused for the same. He had tortured her. Then, he had committed sexual intercourse with her forcibly. He had promised her to marry with her. Hence, she was wandering with him. Thereafter, she came to know that accused was also outraging the modesty of other girls. So, quarrel used to take place between them. On one day, he flatly refused to marry with her and he was interested only in sex. She was told by him that whenever he would call her, she would have to give her company with him. Thereafter, she had disclosed the said facts with her mother. She had given understanding to her. After about one month, he had given her a miss­call on 04.01.14. So, immediately they rushed to Bhainder police station and lodged her report, but she was directed by them to go to Uttan police station. So, on 05.01.14, she rushed to Uttan police station and lodged her report (Exh. 7). Thereafter, she was referred by police to hospital. Doctor had examined her. Her Kudta, Payjama, Odhani and nicker were seized by police. Doctor had obtained required samples. She was threatened by accused that he would defame her if she would not give her company to him. 11] It has come in her cross­examination that she was acquainted with the accused. Their relations were friendly and were visiting to each­ other. Kirti Lad and Shivani were along with her at Jyoti Park. There are some contradictions and omissions, that too, material one. She had stated 6 Spl. POCSO Case No. 77/2014. in her cross­examination that on the call of accused, she had been to Velankani beach. But, same is not found in her statement. 12] She had not stated in her report before police that when she was studying in 10th standard, accused called her at Velankani beach, he had asked her for sex, she refused for the same, but accused had committed rape forcibly on her. This material evidence is not stated by her in her report. But, for the first time, she had stated the same before the court. 13] From the cross­examination of P.W.1 victim, it can be gathered that during bail application of accused, she had filed her affidavit in which she had stated that as they were defamed in the society, she had requested the court to release the accused on bail, as there was love affair and she did not want to proceed with the case further. Now, she does not want to marry with accused though he is ready to marry with her. It can be gathered from her cross­examination that she had lodged her report to save herself from the clutches of accused that he should not torture her in future. She deposed in her evidence that accused had love affair with others and on that count, he would torture her in future. 14] P.W.6 Jayashri Milind Jadhav deposed in her evidence that­ Since last 17­18 years, she along with her family are residing in Kashinagar. Victim was aged about 14­15 years. In the year 2014, she was studying in 11th standard. She knew accused who was residing in their building in C wing. Prior to about two months of 04.01.14, at the evening, victim started weeping and Jayashri was told by her that she had love affair with accused Subodh Shirke since prior to one year, they used to visit in Jyoti Park, he used to say her that he had love with her and he would marry with her, he used to take her at Velankani beach, he used to ask for physical relations, when she used to refuse for such relations, he 7 Spl. POCSO Case No. 77/2014. used to say that she has no love upon him; and he used to establish his sexual relations; he used to call her by giving mis­call by giving threats that if she would not come, he would defame her. Jayashri had given her understanding saying that they would discuss the facts with her father. 15] It has further come in her evidence that­ On 04.01.14, accused gave miscall to victim at about 7.00 p.m. The said mis­call was shown by her to Jayashri. Jayashri disclosed the same with her husband. Thereafter, she along with her husband and victim went to police station. Victim had lodged her report. Statement of Jayashri was recorded on 05.01.14. 16] P.W.2 is a panch to the spot panchanama and seizure of clothes of victim. Accordingly, he had deposed as per both panchanamas. 17] P.W.3 Rajani Shamrao Halgarg deposed in her evidence that­ In the year 2014, she was working as Casualty Medical Officer in Civil hospital, Thane. Accused Subodh Pandurang Shirke was examined by medical officer, on 05.01.14. She collected required samples and sent to C.A. She has not examined the accused medically to find out whether or not accused was potent. 18] P.W.5 Aasif Gani Mulani deposed in his evidence that­ On 06.01.14, he was called by police at Uttan Sagari police station. Sajid Aman Khan was another panch. Accused Subodh Shirke was present in the police station. Police had seized his clothes i.e. jeans pant, T­ shirt, underwear vide seizure memo. 19] P.W.4 Kirti Lad had not supported to the prosecution story. P.W.7 P.I. Smt. Muthe had deposed as per her investigation. As per C.A. report Exh. 25, human blood was detected on the nicker of victim. However, no blood group was detected. No blood or semen stains were found on the clothes of accused. 8 Spl. POCSO Case No. 77/2014. 20] Bonafide certificate of victim is placed on record at article A. However, Principal of the said school is not examined by the prosecution. No birth certificate is placed on record by the prosecution. In absence of birth certificate, it is very difficult to hold that the victim is minor under the age of 18 years. Besides, considering love affair between accused and victim, they used to visit each­other at different places frequently. However, as victim had suspected upon the character of accused that he had affair with other girls, victim might had filed this case to save herself from the clutches of accused, as he had love affair with the victim. 21] Having considered the facts and circumstances of the matter, evidence on record and discussed reasons, prosecution failed to prove the offences charged against accused, beyond all reasonable doubts. Hence, I answer both the points in the negative and proceed to pass the following order. ORDER 1] Accused Subodh Pandurang Shirke, is hereby, acquitted under sec. 235(1) of the Criminal Procedure Code, of the offences punishable u/s. 376, 506 of I.P.C. and u/s. 4 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 2] Accused Subodh Pandurang Shirke, be enlarged on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ with surety of like amount. The effect of this bail order will remain in force for the period 9 Spl. POCSO Case No. 77/2014. of six months from today, as per section 437­(A) of Cr.P.C. 3] Muddemal property being worthless, be destroyed after appeal period is over. Thane, (A.S. Bhaisare) Date­ 03.05.2018. Additional Sessions Judge­2 and Special Judge (POCSO Act), Thane.

.. 1 .. bail no.817/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exhibit 1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 817/2015 This application is filed by applicant Pratik Dashrath Patil for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. I-278/2014 registered at Bhiwandi Taluka police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 354, 451 of I.P.C. and section 11(1) and 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in ''P.O.C.S.O. Act''). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant/accused and co-accused in furtherance of common intention used criminal force against the victim girl and outraged her after entering her house. It is further contended and argued that no such incident has happened and the applicant is falsely implicated in this crime with ulterior motive. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co-operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that at the time of incident the applicant and co-accused entered the house of the complainant and the applicant used criminal force against her and held her hand and pulled her and took her out of house and that time the complainant took a bite to his hand and shouted loudly and at that time the parents of the girl woke up and tried to catch the accused persons but they fled away and at that time the co- accused was keeping watch on the applicant/accused and the girl. It is further contended and argued that the accused and the victim are residing in same locality and therefore in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl and other prosecution witnesses and he may tamper with prosecution evidence and even .. 2 .. bail no.817/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) he may abscond and may not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 452, 354 read with section 34 of I.P.C. and section 11 and 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act the victim girl is stated to be 15 years old and it has to be mentioned that initially the complaint was lodged against unknown person. Even so far as the submission on behalf of prosecution that the investigation is in progress and the applicant was absconding is concerned, as has been submitted on behalf of applicant, the applicant had filed application for anticipatory bail bearing no. 278/2014 and he was granted interim protection and for absence of the applicant it came to finally rejected and then immediately the applicant is seen to have been arrested and in such circumstances the submission on behalf of prosecution that the applicant was absconding or tried to avoid his arrest, cannot be said to be sustainable. Then, it is contended on behalf of applicant/accused that he has been falsely implicated in this crime with ulterior motive. In such circumstance the aspect as to whether the allegations against the accused are true or not, would be the question to be decided on merits. Even nothing is to be recovered from the applicant/accused. 4] Even it is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. .. 3 .. bail no.817/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) 5] Then, so far as the apprehension is expressed on behalf of prosecution that since the offence is of serious nature in regard to sexual harassment on minor girl and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 6] Then, it has also to be mentioned that though the investigation in the matter is stated to be in progress and even the charge sheet is yet to be submitted, it would take time to complete the investigation and then submit the charge-sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 7] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order - ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Pratik Dashrath Patil is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/- [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions - He shall not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and the prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this Court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 07.05.2015. 1 Bail No. 835/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) Criminal Bail Application No.835/2016 Sheu Pandurang Jadhav .. Applicant versus The State of Maharashtra (Through Vikramgad Police Station) .. Non­applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 1] By this application the applicant is seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. who was arrested 13/03/2016 by Vikramgad Police Station in connection with C.R.No. I­6/2016 registered for an offence punishable under section 376 & 506 of I.P.C. and section 4 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as P.O.C.S.O. Act). 2] Heard learned Advocate Mr. Sachin Varale for the applicant/accused and Spl.PP Mrs. R.A.Navale and I.O. present with case diary. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 22/01/2016 at the instance of the informant/ victim­girl aged about 14 years with an indictment that her mother expired before two years 2 Bail No. 835/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) and her father used to remain out of the house for his work for 8­8 days and she alongwith her minor two brothers ad two sisters is staying alone at home. As they were alone therefore the victim­girl alongwith her sibligns used to go to the house of accused (Subhash Gaikwad) for sleeping. In the year­2015 during the Holi festival, accused by threatening the victim­girl committed sexual assault on her and thereafter, repeated the same act after two days. Therefore, the victim­girl disclosed it to the wife of accused Sudha. On that she abused and threatened her and told her not to come to her house to sleep. Since then the victim­girl was not going to the house of accused Subhash Gaikwad. However, he came to the house of victim­ girl and by threatening her and committed repeated sexual assault on her. In the month of June, the victim­girl disclosed the accused Sudha that she has missed her menses and feeling nautia. Therefore, on 11/01/2010 the accused Sudha took her to accused Shau Jadhav at Ambiste village and she aborted the fetus. Thereafter, informant disclosed the incident to her father and after holding meeting she lodged report against all the accused. 4] The learned Counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant/accused is falsely implicated. He further submitted that the applicant is old lady aged of 60 years old and all allegations are false. He further submitted that even name 3 Bail No. 835/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) of applicant is not mentioned in the F.I.R. He further submitted that if the allegations of the F.I.R. are seen then the act of rape took place in March­2015 and abortion is stated to be in January­2016 which means the fetus should be of 8 to 9 months when the abortion is impossible and further the fetus was also not found or seized by police. He further submitted that F.I.R. is nothing but the after thought story created by the victim­girl. The applicant is nowhere concerned with the alleged offence. She is old lady and ready to abide by the conditions imposed by the court and prayed for releasing him on bail. 5] Per contra, the ld. Spl.P.P. opposed the application submitting that both the applicants are ladies and they are involved in the serious offence about the abetment of rape and causing miscarriage of fetus. She further submitted that the victim­girl is teen aged girl. She has no reason to concocted false story. The main accused repeatedly committed sexual assault on her and even threatened her. She further submitted that the accused Sudha took her to another village for abortion and accused Sheu aborted the fetus of 3 months and thus, they are equally participated in the crime. She further submitted that when father of the victim­girl came to know about the incident, the report was lodged and investigation is in progress. There are chances of tampering of witnesses and prayed for rejection of application. 4 Bail No. 835/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R., it appears that the victim­girl is minor aged about 14 years only. In the F.I.R. itself, the detail act of the accused is mentioned. The victim­girl alongwith her siblings had been to the house of accused Subhash and Sudha to sleep as they were alone in the house. Thereafter, the main accused Subhash Gaikwad betrayed trust and committed repeated sexual assault on the victim­girl at his own house as well as at the house of victim­girl when she stopped going to the house of accused and because of which she carries pregnancy. When the victim­girl noticed the pregnancy, she disclosed it to accused Sudha who is wife of accused Subhash. On that she threatened her not to disclose it to anybody and initially an attempt was made for her abortion by taking her to the local nurse ( lqbZ.k ) and thereafter when her attempt was not succeed she was taken to the accused Sheu. The present accused Sheu Jadhav in very barbaric manner aborted the fetus of the tender aged victim­girl. Thus, both the accused Sudha and Sheu had equally participated in very serious and heinous offence and although they are ladies abated the heinous act of the main accused Subhash Gaikwad. As rightly submitted by learned A.P.P. no reason appears for such a minor tender aged girl to implicate the accused in false case. The offence is very serious in nature. The investigation is in progress and at nascent stage. There is prima­facie case against all the accused. Considering the peculiar facts of the case, the 5 Bail No. 835/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) apprehension of the learned Special P.P. about tampering of the witnesses and hampering of the investigation is well founded. The accused are involved in serious offence and therefore there are chances of their fleeing away from justice. Hence, absolutely no case is made out for releasing the accused on bail. Therefore, I pass the following order:­ ORDER The application stands rejected. Thane. Date : 06/05/2016. (Ms. U.M. Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act), Thane.

.. 1 .. bail no.837/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exhibit 1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 837/2015 This application is filed by applicant Akbar Hussain Jariwala for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. I-134/2015 registered at Mira Road police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 354, 504, 506 of I.P.C. and section 6 and 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in ''P.O.C.S.O. Act''). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant/accused used criminal force against the victim girl and then outraged her by touching her private part and moving hand on her breast and body. It is further contended and argued that the place of incident is stated to be in a crowded area and therefore there is no possibility of any such incident taking place there and the applicant is falsely implicated in this crime merely on suspicion. It is further submitted that the applicant is a middle aged and law abiding person and is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co-operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that at the relevant time when the victim girl came across the accused, he stated to her that her money has fallen down which the the girl denied and thereafter when the victim girl reached the ground floor of the building walking, the accused came from behind and even though he was knowing that she was minor, he used criminal force against her and held her by both hands and moved his hand over her breast and also on private part and thereby committed sexual assault on her. It is further contended and argued that the accused and the victim are residing in same locality and therefore in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the .. 2 .. bail no.837/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) applicant threatening the victim girl and complainant and may tamper with prosecution evidence and even he may abscond and may not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 354, 504, 506 of I.P.C. and section 6 and 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act with the allegation that the applicant/accused had outraged modesty of the minor girl Zarina Shaikh by catching hold of her hand from behind and moving his hand on her body and breast and inserting hand at the place of her urination, it is to be mentioned that it is contended on behalf of applicant/accused that he has been falsely implicated in this crime and it is also contended that in the complaint it is mentioned the act was done by an unknown person and later on the complainant stated to have identified the accused to be the same person and in such circumstances the identity of the accused would be the crucial question. Then, in the light of case put forth by the accused that he is falsely implicated in the matter, the aspect as to whether the allegations against the accused are true or not, would be the question to be decided on merits. Even nothing is to be recovered from the applicant/accused. 4] Even it is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and he is ready to furnish local surety and he will abide by any conditions imposed. 5] Then, though apprehension is expressed on behalf of prosecution that since the offence is of serious nature and the .. 3 .. bail no.837/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 6] Then, it has also to be mentioned that the investigation in the matter is though yet to be completed and the charge sheet is yet to be submitted, it would take time to complete the investigation and then to file the charge-sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 7] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order - ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Akbar Hussain Jariwala is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/- [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions - He shall not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and the prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this Court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 07.05.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.

Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­002326­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No.67/15 Received on : 04.04.2015 Registered on : 04.04.2015 Decided on : 03.01.2019 Duration : 3Ys.8Ms.29Ds. IN THE COURT OF D.J.­1 & ADDL. SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE (Presided over by Hemant M. Patwardhan) Special (POCSO Case No. 67/15 Exh.No. 1. State of Maharashtra. ( Kapurbavdi Police station) ..Complainant V/s. Anand Kanyaiyya Gupta. Age – 41 years, R/at. Backside of Navbal Vidya Mandir, Room of Kallu Master, Dashrath Patil Maidan, Azadnagar, Thane ..Accused Appearance:­ DGP Mr. Londhe for the State. Advocate Mr. Patankar for the accused. JUDGMENT (Delivered on this 3rd day of January 2019 ) Accused Anand Kanyaiyya Gupta was facing trial under sections 376 (2)(f)(I), 323, 504, 506 of IPC read with 1 to 14 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­002326­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No.67/15 section 4 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 on following facts:­ 1] That on 25/12/2014 at about 22.00 hours to 26/12/2014 at about 11.00 hours at Backside of Navbal Vidya Mandir, Room of Kallu Master, Dashrath Patil Maidan, Azadnagar, Thane and on 04/01/2015 at about 23.00 hours at house of mother and father of complainant, Jijamata Chawl, Ganesh Nagar, Durga Chowk, Manpada, Thane, within the jurisdiction of Kapurbavadi Police Station, Thane, accused has committed rape on victim and while committing said act has voluntarily caused hurt to the complainant and other prosecution witnesses and had given provocation to them to commit breach of public peace and at same time committing criminal intimidation by threatening the complainant and victim with injuries to their person. According to allegations victim was minor within the meaning of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 at the time of alleged incident therefore, sexual act of the accused was also treated to be penetrative sexual assault within the meaning of section 3 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (here­in­after referred as "Act" only for brevity.) Hence, on the complaint lodged by mother of the victim, an offence punishable under aforesaid sections came to be registered against accused. On completion of investigation accused was charge­sheeted. 2 to 14 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­002326­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No.67/15 2] Charge came to be framed at Exh.9 and has certified that the contents of said charge were read over and explained to accused in vernacular. Accused pleaded not guilty and claim to be tried. His defence was of total denial. 3] On the basis of aforesaid facts' prosecution has then proceeded to examine victim, complainant, medical officer Dr. Mrs. Sangita Jadhav, Dr. Mrs. Vijaya Chaudhary and finally I.O. Kalyani Patil as witness no.1 to 5 respectively. After evidence, statement of accused was recorded as per his say wherein he has reiterated his defence of false implication on the ground of his demand of huge amount paid to his wife and her mother and according to his defence in order to avoid to pay that amount he is implicated in this case. 4] Arguments of the rival advocates were heard. The sum and substance of the arguments advanced by learned DGP was that the victim who was suffered herself has categorically narrated the incident involving the accused in penetrative sexual assault and thus, according to submissions as said statement was then corroborated by complainant and medical officers same are certainly sufficient to establish the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt. According to submissions, on the basis of statement, presumption under section 29 and 30 of the Act can easily be raised against accused and once that 3 to 14 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­002326­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No.67/15 presumption are raised, accused was burdened to disprove the said presumption and accused has failed to do so same is sufficient to interfered his mental state to commit said offence. Thus, learned DGP has requested to convict the accused under the provisions of law under which accused was charged. 5] Per contra, defence has pointed out that none of the statements either of victim or the complainant is corroborated by either of them and further in view of the admissions of the medical officer the same can be discarded easily. According to his submissions there was matrimonial dispute between the parties and in order to give a counter blow to the said dispute present case, implicating the accused falsely has been filed. He has therefore, requested to discard the evidence and acquit the accused from all the allegations. 6] On the basis of aforesaid facts, following points arose for my consideration and I record my findings against each of them for the reasons noted below :­ Sr.N Points Findings 1] Does the prosecution prove that accused in between 25/12/2014 ..Negative. at about 22.00 hours to 26/12/2014 at about 11.00 hours at Backside of Navbal Vidya Mandir, Room of Kallu Master, Dashrath Patil Maidan, Azadnagar, Thane and on 04/01/2015 at about 4 to 14 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­002326­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No.67/15 23.00 hours at house of mother and father of complainant, Jijamata Chawl, Ganesh Nagar, Durga Chowk, Manpada, Thane, within the jurisdiction of Kapurbavadi Police Station, Thane, committed rape on victim a minor age – 5 years, and thereby committed an offence punishable under Section 376 (2)(F)(I) of Indian Penal Code? 2] Does the prosecution prove that accused on aforesaid period and ..Negative. places, voluntarily caused hurt to complainant and prosecution witness and you are thereby committed an offence punishable under Section 323 of Indian Penal Code? 3] Does the prosecution prove that accused on aforesaid period and ..Negative. places, intentionally insulted the complainant and prosecution witnesses by abusing him in filthy language and thereby gave provocation to them to break public peace and thereby committed an offence punishable under Section 504 of Indian Penal Code? 4] Does the prosecution prove that accused on aforesaid period and ..Negative. places, committed criminal intimidation by threatening to complainant and prosecution witness and as such you thereby committed an offence punishable under Section 506 of Indian Penal Code? 5] Does the prosecution prove that accused on aforesaid period and ..Negative. places, committed penetrative sexual assault on victim a minor age 5 years and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 4 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act? 6] What order? Accused is acquitted as per final order. REASONS As to point no.1 to 6 :­ 7] All these points are interlinked with each other and therefore, are considered at once. Prosecution has alleged that accused has committed rape within the meaning of Sub­section 2(f)(i) of section 376 of IPC and while committing said offence has also voluntarily caused hurt to the complainant and has 5 to 14 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­002326­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No.67/15 committed criminal intimidation by threatening complainant and the victim. According to prosecution as the victim was minor at the relevant time the assault on her, were treated to be penetrative sexual assault with sexual intends and thus, accused was charge­sheeted. In order to substantiate allegations, material witnesses were victim herself and her mother. In order to corroborate those facts depositions of medical officers were recorded. Hence, in the light of rival arguments court has to scrutinize the evidence of said material witnesses in order to find out whether said depositions are really sufficient to establish the guilt of the accused under various provisions of IPC and to raise presumption under section 29 and 30 of the Act to hold the accused guilty of the offence punishable under section 4 of the Act. 8] Depositions of victim was recorded without administration of oath as victim was not able to understand the importance of oath. During her deposition she has alleged that accused used to frighten her by doing like ghost and then has committed penetrative sexual assault by inserting fingers in her private part and that accused has committed same act for 15 days continuously. The witness has then summed up allegation by deposing that day before lodging the complaint her father had asked her mother to accompanied him and refusal of her to accompany him on the ground of having abdomen pain he had 6 to 14 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­002326­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No.67/15 uttered the words "“rq er vk] eq>s fj;k Hkh pyrh gS" the mother has got angry and lodged the complaint. The mother of the victim during her deposition has stated that on 25.12.2014 accused has taken victim forcibly and in the morning of 26.12.2014 accused has dropped the victim at her parent's house she found victim weeping and on inquiry she had complained of pain in private part. Therefore, she had informed the incident to her neighbourer and then took the victim to PW4. According to complainant on 29.12.2014 she along with her brother has taken the victim to civil hospital but did not approach police though asked for in order to avoid defamation of the daughter. According to her again on 04.01.2015 when the accused has insisted her to accompanied her and on refusal has narrated the words " rq ugh jgh rks eq>s fj;k Hkh pysxh". Accused then quarreled with her, assaulted her and therefore, she went to police station and lodged the complaint. 9] Thus, even on the plain reading of deposition of the witnesses it is apparent that there are total variation in their narration. It is well settled principle that the court should look for corroboration as a rule of prudence for deposition of child witness. In the instant case as the witness was not able to understand importance of oath, her deposition was recorded without administration of oath. Therefore, her deposition all 7 to 14 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­002326­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No.67/15 alone has got no sanctity in the eyes of law. The court has therefore, look for corroboration for same and has to consider surrounding circumstances in which particular incident had occurred and only on being convinced by quality of statement with surrounding circumstances has to base conviction on such statement. However, while looking for the corroboration in the particular matter except deposition of the mother of the victim, there is no material on record. Hence, the Court has to consider surrounding Circumstances. 10] On perusal of deposition of mother of victim it is apparent that she has narrated the incident of 25.12.2014 only and had sum up allegation by narrating incident dated 04.01.2015. If we consider allegation of victim that her father has committed act of insertion of finger in private part continuously for 15 days then at no stage of those 15 days she has complained about her suffering or any injury in her private part, any kind of bleeding which could have call for urgent medical attendance during those 15 days. Further, there are no allegation of victim that during those 15 days she had disclosed those facts to her mother and there is absolutely no explanation as to why she did not disclose those facts to her mother during any of those days. Hence, from said fact itself the allegations of having subjected to penetrative sexual assaults or having subjected to rape within the meaning of section 376(2)(f)(i) of 8 to 14 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­002326­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No.67/15 IPC is really difficult to accept. Further, the victim has made very vague allegation about such insertion of finger in private part without there being any details of the day, date, month and year of occurrence of the particular incident. While looking for corroboration if we perused the deposition of mother of victim then it is apparent that she has restricted her allegation about incident dated 25.12.2014 without there being any reference of any such incident being occurred by the victim herself. If said incident of 25.12.2014 is considered as it is then also when the victim's mother had noticed some blood on the inner part of the nicker of the victim she was expected to lodge complaint immediately as either with her dear one's or at least directly with police. However, from her deposition itself it can be revealed that she did not disclose those facts to any of her dear one's but has surprisingly disclosed it to her neighbour who took her to medical officer PW4. However, even said medical officer has advice her to visit Gynecologist, she did not visit said Gynecologist on same day. Thus, from the conduct of the mother of victim it is apparent that with some ulterior motive she has made an attempt to implicate the accused in the particular matter. 11] Even on 29.12.2014 as per the allegation that she has taken victim to civil hospital, there is no such document on 9 to 14 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­002326­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No.67/15 record to show that on that day also the victim was clinically examined by any gynecologist. If that incident would really had occurred the natural conduct of the mother of the victim was immediately to approach the concern police atleast on 29.12.2014. Though, she has put forth explanation that in order to avoid defamation of her daughter she went back to home is also unaccepted as the concern medical officer of the civil hospital was bound to prepare medico legal case if the allegations were really true and was bound to inform police on her own once the fact of having somebody subjected to sexual assault is made known to medical officer during said clinical examination. However, it was neither case of the prosecution that any such medico legal case was prepared on 29.12.2014 nor the matter was reported to police on the same day in itself create doubt in respect of deposition of mother of the victim either about incident dated 25.12.2014 or dated 29.12.2014 as alleged by her. The victim's mother has then made a reference of incident dated 04.01.2015. On that particular day admittedly there was absolutely no allegation of sexual assaults at the hands of accused but only allegations of having utter some abusive words viz. " rq ugh jgh rks eq>s fj;k Hkh pysxh" and allegation of accused having quarrel with her and having assaulted her. Surprisingly, the complainant has then rushed to 10 to 14 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­002326­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No.67/15 the concern police station for narrating the incident dated 04.01.2015 though in comparison to the incidents dated 25.12.2014 or 29.12.2014 it was not that of serious nature. Having regards to the conduct of the mother of the victim, the defence of accused of his false implication gets corroborated. Admittedly, though there was allegation of assault on her person, there is no medical certificate or even there is no attempt of the mother of the victim to get her examined by any of the medical officer of the civil hospital to substantiate the said facts. Thus, it is apparent from the said that incident dated 04.01.2015 is put forth just to set law in motion, otherwise she would have approached concern medical officer to get herself examined to substantiate the allegations. 12] In such matters opinion of concern medical officer is really of material importance. On plain perusal of deposition of the medical officer, PW3 it appears that though the victim was examined by PW3 she did not find any external injury nor has recorded any injuries to the internal part of the victim. Further, she has categorically made a statement that while examination she did not find any evidence of sexual assault and only on the basis of the history given she has opined that there is possibility of sexual assault. Hence, if we consider that there was continuous sexual assault for about 15 days as alleged by the victim, then she was bound to sustain some injuries on her 11 to 14 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­002326­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No.67/15 private part and also some external injuries during said sexual assault. However, there is admission of the medical officer that she did not find any such injuries. Moreover, when she found hymen intact, it is difficult to accept that even after said penetrative sexual assault for about 15 days continuously hymen will continue to be intact. The admission of the medical officer that she has based her opinion only on the basis of history given by mother of the victim therefore, is sufficient to discard the medical evidence being corroborating to allegations of victim and her mother. 13] On the basis of aforesaid scrutiny of the evidence, it is difficult to accept that the evidence brought before this court and circumstances which were brought in the depositions of the witnesses are sufficient to establish offence punishable under section 376 (2)(f)(i) of IPC and also even to substantiate or prove the allegations under sections 504, 506, 323 of IPC. Even if we consider the allegation under section 4 of POCSO then also in view of the aforesaid findings it is difficult to accept that deposition of victim or her mother is corroborating each other to accept allegation under section 4 of the said Act. An important ingredient of section 3 is assault with sexual intends. In the instant case if we consider the allegation of the victim immediately preceding to the alleged act of assault that the accused used to frighten her by doing acts like ghost then it 12 to 14 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­002326­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No.67/15 is difficult to accept that his further act even if consider as it is then also to be with sexual intends. Further, as there are so many contradictions in the deposition of victim and her mother, such allegation also nowhere sufficient to raise presumption under section 29 or section 30 of the Act. If the evidence and circumstances brought before the court are not certainly sufficient to raise presumption, onus was never shifted on the accused to disprove said presumption. Therefore, even the accused has put forth different version of defence that itself is not sufficient to accept case of the prosecution to be more probable than that of the defence of the accused. From the various contradictions and variations in the statements of the witnesses, coupled with admission of the medical officer as above are itself sufficient to discard the allegation of the prosecution even under section 4 of POCSO Act. Thus, I do not find anything on record which is really sufficient to hold accused guilt of the offence with any of the allegations or under any of the section with which he was charged. On the contrary various contradictions, omissions and circumstances brought before the court are itself sufficient to inferred false implication of the accused in the matter. Accordingly, I do not hesitate to record my findings against point no. 1 to 5 in negative and hold that accused is entitled for clear acquittal. With the said observations, the order. 13 to 14 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­002326­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No.67/15 ORDER 1] Accused Anand Kanyaiyya Gupta is acquitted from the offence punishable under sections 376 (2)(f)(I), 323, 504, 506 of IPC read with section 4 of Protection of Children from Sexual OffencesAct, 2012. 2] Accused is in jail. Hence, he be set at liberty if not required in any other case/crime. 3] The muddemal property i.e. clothes of the victim and accused being worthless be destroyed after appeal period. 4] Accused is directed to execute P.R. and S.B. of Rs.10,000/­ as per amended provisions of section 437(A) of Cr.P.C. and bonds so executed shall remain in force for the period of six months from the date of its execution. 5] Prosecution against the accused stands closed. 6] Inform jailer accordingly. Thane (Hemant M.Patwardhan) Date: 03.01.2019 D.J.­1 & Additional Sessions Judge, Thane. 14 to 14

IN THE COURT OF THE SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE (Presided over by Ms.U.M.Nandeshwar, Additional Sessions Judge­1, Thane) SPECIAL CASE No. 80 of 2014 Exhibit No. 18 The State of Maharashtra Through Kalwa Police Station Thane, District – Thane. ... Prosecution versus Jagdish Laxman Pandharbhise Age 24 years, Residence –Room No.2, Hiradevi chawl, Ashok Samrat Nagar, Kalwa, Thane. ... Accused Offence punishable under section 354 of Indian Penal Code and under section 7 & 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Appearance ­ Spl.P.P. Mrs. R.A. Navale, for the State. Advocate Mr. S.G.Sonawane, for the Accused. 2 Special Case No.80/2014 (Judgment) JUDGMENT (Delivered on 23rd February, 2016.) 1] The Accused stands prosecuted for the offence punishable under section 354 of Indian Penal Code and also under section 7 & 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act) for committing sexual assault on minor victim­girl aged about 13 years. 2] The indictment against the Accused are as under ­ [i] Informant Vaibhavi Laxmikant Bhoir (P.W.1) is resident of New Shivaji Nagar, Kalwa, Thane. She is staying there with her husband and two daughters including victim­ girl aged about 12 years. Victim­girl is studying in 7th std. in New Kalwa High School, Kalwa. [ii] Since 18th August, 2013 victim­girl was attending private tuition classes namely “Aai classes” run by Abasaheb Pandharbhise which is beyond two chawls from her house. The timings for her class was 06.00 p.m. to 08.00 p.m. [iii] Since one and half month younger brother of Pandharbhise sir namely Jagdish Pandharbhise (Accused) used to came near the victim­girl when she was alone in the class and when other students were waiting in the gallery. At that time, he used to caught hold hand of victim­girl and put his hand on her shoulder and touched her inappropriately on her thighs. Prior to two to three days, Accused touched her breast 3 Special Case No.80/2014 (Judgment) inappropriately. Due to frightening earlier victim­girl did not disclose the incident to her mother. On 30/11/2013 when victim­girl was alone in the class, at that time, Accused approached her and asked for kiss. On that victim­girl told him that she did not like it and she will disclose it to her mother. On that Accused told her that if she disclosed it to her mother, he will not talk with her. Thereafter, victim­girl disclosed it to her mother and in turn her mother lodged report against the Accused on 01/12/2013. 3] On her report F.I.R. was registered against the Accused vide C.R.No.I­595/2013 for the offence punishable under section 354 of I.P.C. and under section 7 and 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. The investigation was carried out by A.P.I. Sachin Kothmire(P.W.3). The Accused was arrested in presence of panchas. On 02/12/2013 P.W.3 visited the spot and drawn spot panchnama in presence of panchas. Statements of witnesses were recorded as per their say. Thereafter, investigation culminated into filing of charge­sheet in this Court being the Special designated court under P.O.C.S.O. Act. 4] My learned predecessor the erstwhile Special Judge Shri. H.M.Patwardhan framed the charge (Exh.2) against the Accused for offence punishable under section 354 of Indian Penal Code and also under section 7 and 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. 4 Special Case No.80/2014 (Judgment) The Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial (Exh.3). The Accused took defence of total denial. 5] In response to application under section 294 of Cr.P.C. the defence has admitted spot panchnama [Exh.10]. 6] In order to prove guilt of Accused Prosecution has examined following witnesses ­ P.W.1 Vaibhavi Laxman Bhoir Exh.7 (Informant – Mother of victim­girl) P.W.2 Victim­girl Exh.9 P.W.3 Shri. Sachin Bharat Kothmire Exh.11 (Investigating officer.) 7] The prosecution proved and relied on the following documents ­ Report / F.I.R. Exhibit 12 Portion marked 'A' in the statement of Exhibit 13 P.W.2 Arrest form of Accused Exhibit 14 8] The prosecution closed its side of evidence by filing Pursis at Exhibit­15. The incriminating evidence came on record against the Accused was read over and explained him and his statement under Section 313(b) of Cr.P.C. was recorded. Accused neither examined himself nor examined any witness in his defence. 5 Special Case No.80/2014 (Judgment) 9] Heard learned A.P.P. Mrs. R. A. Navale for State and the learned advocate Mr.S.G.Sonawane for Accused. 10] On consideration of argument advanced on behalf of both the sides and on perusal of the oral & documentary evidence on record, following points arise for my determination, which are answered with the findings thereon, as under :­ Sr. Points Findings No. 1 ) Does the prosecution prove that since 1 ½ months prior to 30/11/2013 at room No.2, Hiradevi chawl, Ashok Samrat Nagar, Kalwa, Thane Accused ..No. used criminal force against victim­girl by touching her inappropriately with intent to outrage her modesty and he thereby committed an offence punishable under section 354 of Indian Penal Code ? 2 ) Does the prosecution prove that on same day, time and place the Accused committed sexual assault on the said minor girl and he thereby committed ..No. an offence punishable under section 7 and 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, 2012 ? 3) What order ? Accused is acquitted. 6 Special Case No.80/2014 (Judgment) REASONS As to Point No.1 & 2 : 11] Both the points are taken up together for discussion, to avoid the repetition, as evidence about the same in common and inter­connected. Age of victim­girl is 13 Years : 12] As the Accused is facing charge under P.O.C.S.O. Act, therefore, it is incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that the victim­girl was child (minor) at the time of incident. The alleged incident took place in between October­ 2013 to 30/11/2013. Informant (P.W.1) deposed that in the year­2013 her daughter was aged about 12 years and studying in 7th std. in New Kalwa High school. Similarly, victim­girl (P.W.2) also deposed that her date of birth is 27/02/2002 and in the year­2013 she was studying in 7th std. There is absolutely no challenge to the age of victim­girl. Thus, the prosecution proved that at the time of incident, the victim­girl was minor aged about 12 years i.e. below the age of 18 years and she was a “child” as per definition given in Section 2(d) of P.O.C.S.O. Act. 14] Further, as the Accused is facing charge under section 354 of I.P.C. it is incumbent on the part of prosecution 7 Special Case No.80/2014 (Judgment) to prove that Accused either assaults or used criminal force towards victim­girl to outrage her modesty or knowing it to be likely that he will, by his act, outrage the modesty of the victim­girl. So also as the Accused is facing charge under section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, therefore, it is further incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that the Accused with sexual intent touched the vagina, penis, anus, breast of a child or make the child touched vagina, penis, anus, breast of such person or any other person or does any other act with sexual intent which involves physical contact without penetration and by his such act committed sexual assault as defined in section 7 of the P.O.C.SO. Act. 15] To prove the charge against the Accused the prosecution has examined the informant / mother of victim­ girl and victim­girl who are the most material witnesses to prove the charge against the Accused. Informant (P.W.1) and victim­girl (P.W.2) deposed that they both know the Accused who is younger brother of Mr. Pandharbhise who used to run Private Tuition Classes and in the year­2013 victim­girl used to attend his private tuition class by name “Aai Classes”. However, on the material point, as far as the alleged incident of outraging modesty by touching inappropriately to the victim­girl in the tuition class whenever she was alone in the class is concern, neither informant (P.W.1) nor victim­girl supported the prosecution. Though, both the witnesses were 8 Special Case No.80/2014 (Judgment) cross­examined by prosecution but nothing material elicited from their testimony to support the case of prosecution. Thus, there is absolutely no legal evidence on record to prove the charge against the Accused. The evidence of investigating officer A.P.I. Sachin Kothmire (P.W.3) is formal in nature who recorded the complaint of informant as per her say and executed the spot panchnama and recorded the statement of witnesses. 16] Thus, as the informant and victim­girl both did not support the prosecution case, therefore, there is no iota of evidence against the Accused to prove the charge leveled against him. Thus, prosecution failed to prove that accused with sexual intent inappropriately touched minor victim­girl by using criminal force and outraged her modesty. Hence, I answer point No.1 & 2 in negative. Therefore, in absence of any evidence against the Accused, he is entitled for acquittal. 17] In the result, I proceed to pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused Jagdish Laxman Pandharbhise @ Jagannath Laxman Pandharpise is hereby acquitted U/Sec. 235(1) of Cr.P.C. for the offence punishable U/Sec.354 of Indian Penal Code and U/s. 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 9 Special Case No.80/2014 (Judgment) 2] His bail bonds stand cancelled and sureties are discharged. 3] The Accused is directed to furnish bail bond of the amount of ₹15,000/­ with one solvent surety in the like amount in compliance of provision of section 437­A of Cr.P.C. The judgment is dictated and pronounced in open Court. Date : 23/02/2016. (Ms. U. M. Nandeshwar), Thane Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act),Thane. District Judge ­1 and Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

.. 1 .. bail no.868/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 868/2015 This application is filed by applicant namely Mohan Ramsubogar Jaiswal for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. I­54/2015 registered at Rabale police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 363, 366, 34 of I.P.C. and section 12 and 17 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant helped the other accused in kidnapping the victim girl. It is further contended and argued that applicant is not F.I.R. named accused and that he is falsely implicated in this crime. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, she will co­ operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that the accused no.1 in furtherance of common intention with the present applicant induced the victim girl and kidnapped her with the intention of marrying her. It is further contended and argued that the applicant/accused abetted the accused no.1 in commission of offence. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl and the prosecution .. 2 .. bail no.868/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 363, 366, 34 of I.P.C. and section 12 and 17 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, it is further clear the main allegations of kidnapping the girl aged 17 years are against accused no.1 Rampal Ramdayal Gautam and the applicant/accused is stated to have abetted the accused no.1 in commission of crime and he is seen to be in jail since 18.02.2015 and he is also stated to be not F.I.R. named accused and it is contended that he is falsely implicated in the crime. In such circumstance whether the allegations against the accused are true or not, would be the question to be decided on merits. Even nothing is stated to be recovered from the applicant/accused. 4] It is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if she is released on bail. In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and she will not abscond if released on bail and that she is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. .. 3 .. bail no.868/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) 5] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 6] Then, it has also to be mentioned that the investigation in the matter though almost completed the charge sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 7] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Mohan Ramsubogar Jaiswal is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ The applicant/accused shall attend as and when called till filing of the charge sheet and shall co­operate in investigation. .. 4 .. bail no.868/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) He shall not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and the prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this Court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 18.04.2015 (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.

1 Bail No.859/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) Criminal Bail Application No.859/2016 Abdulla Abdul ghani Shaikh. .. Applicant versus The State of Maharashtra Through Mumbra Police Station .. Non­applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 1] By this application the applicants are seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. who was arrested on 29/03/2016 by Mumbra Police Station in connection with C.R.No.I­ 158/2016 registered for an offence punishable under section 354 of I.P.C. and section 7 & 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as P.O.C.S.O. Act). 2] Heard learned Advocate Mr.Iqbal Abdulla for the applicant/accused and learned Spl.P.P. Mrs.R.A.Navale for State. I.O. present. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 29/03/2016 at the instance of the informant/victim­girl aged about 14 years with an indictment that when she went in the stationary shop of accused, he hold her hand and by touching her inappropriately outraged her modesty. 2 Bail No.859/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) 4] The learned Counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant/accused is falsely implicated. He submitted that the accused was at Saudi Arabia for 20 years and returned to India just before one year and since then started small shop of stationary. However, the people of the vicinity did not liked it and therefore, they repeatedly lodged false complaint against him with same serious allegations and prior to this also two false complaints were registered against him with the same allegations only to pressurize him to vacate the premises and to extract money from him. He further submitted that nothing is recovered from the accused. The investigation is almost completed. The accused is ready to abide any condition imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing them on bail. 5] Per contra, the learned Spl.P.P. strongly opposed the application on the ground that the offence is serious in respect of minor girl. She further submitted that the applicant is habitual to commit such kind of offence and two cases are already registered against him for molestation of the minor girls. She further submitted that the F.I.R. speaks in volume and the intention of the accused is very much clear which is detail by the victim­girl in the F.I.R. The investigation is in progress. The accused committed the offence when he was on bail. There are chances of tampering of the witnesses and prayed for rejection of the application. 3 Bail No.859/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R., it appears that F.I.R, was lodged at the instance of victim­girl aged 14 yrs with an indictment that when she had been to the stationary shop of the accused for purchasing drawing book, he hold her hand and pulled her near him and inappropriately touched her chest and outraged her modesty. The material part of the investigation appears to have been completed. No doubt, the offence is serious in respect of the minor girl. However, the object of bail is neither punitive nor preventive but to secure the presence of the accused at the time of trial. No fruitful purpose would be served by further incarceration of accused. He is ready to abide by the conditions imposed by the Court. However, as per the say filed by the investigating officer, the accused is having criminal antecedents and involved in similar kind of offence, therefore, stringent conditions were required to be imposed on the accused to address the apprehension of learned Spl.P.P. about tampering of prosecution witnesses and fleeing away from justice. Hence, I pass the following order ­ ORDER 1) The application is allowed. 2) Applicant namely Abdulla Abdul ghani Shaikh be released on bail on their executing P.R.Bond of ₹ 20,000/­ [Rupees Twenty Thousand only] with one solvent surety in the like amount on the following conditions ­ 4 Bail No.859/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) A] Applicant shall attend the concerned police station on every Sunday in between 10.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon till filing of charge­sheet. B] Applicant shall not tamper with prosecution witnesses and shall not pressurize the victim­girl or her family. C] Applicants shall furnish his and his two blood relatives' address proofs and contact numbers and they are duty bound to inform I.O. and Court about the change of address, if any. D] The accused shall maintain the decency hearinafter. E] The applicant shall take note that if he again found involved in similar kind of offence and if the complaint found the ring of truth, then his bail order shall be taken for cancellation. Thane. Date : 18/04/2016. (Ms. U.M. Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act), Thane.
