Appearance - Mrs. R.A. Navale, learned Additional Public Prosecutor (hereinafter in short A.P.P.) Mrs. Yasmin Sayyad, learned advocate for accused. JUDGMENT (Delivered on 23.07.2015) .. 2 .. Special Case No. 82/2014 Judgment The accused stand prosecuted for the offence punishable under section 363, 366A, 376(i) of I.P.C. and section 4 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as ''P.O.C.S.O. Act'') for kidnapping minor girl Poonam Ramesh Prajapati from lawful guardianship of her parents from their house at Waghobanagar no.9, Kalwa, with a view to force or seduce her for sexual intercourse with false assurance of marriage and having committed rape and sexual assault on her from time to time between 18.12.2013 to 17.01.2014. 2] In short the facts giving rise to the prosecution of the accused are that victim girl Poonam Ramesh Prajapati had been staying with her parents and siblings at Waghobanagar, Kalwa, Thane. She was studying in 10th Std. and was aged about 15 years. It is also further case of the prosecution that she used to leave the house for her classes in the morning around 7.00 a.m. and used to return around 11.00 a.m. and then used to go to her school and return home by 6.00 p.m. 3] It is also further case that maternal uncle of the victim girl was staying at Goa and once she went to her maternal uncle with her mother and stayed there for one month. There the victim girl got acquainted with the accused at Goa. Thereafter the accused came in search of her address at Kalwa and contacted and developed acquaintance with her and he got work at Ghatkopar and was staying there and he even used to come and meet her. It is also further case of the prosecution that on 18.12.2013 victim girl left the house around 7.00 a.m. for her classes. That time the accused met her on her way to classes and stated that he likes her and she should come with him and he want to marry her and if she refuse he would defame her by telling that they are .. 3 .. Special Case No. 82/2014 Judgment having love affair and being scared the victim went with the accused and accused took her to village Jobiligaon, Badlapur and there they stayed as husband and wife and the accused even introduced to labours working with him as his wife and had been threatening her not to tell about it to anybody else he would defame her. It is also case of the prosecution that during said period till 16.01.2014 when they were staying together the victim girl was subjected to sexual assault from time to time against her wish. 4] It is also case of the prosecution that in the meantime after the girl left house on 18.12.2013 and she did not return home at her usual time, her mother searched for her but she could not be traced. That time her father was out of station and he returned home on 27.12.2013 and that time he was informed by mother of the girl about missing of the girl. Then they lodged missing complaint and inquiry was being made into the missing complaint. During inquiry police and parents of the girl were in search of the girl and the accused. Then on 17.01.2014 the girl alongwith the accused was found at Dadar railway station and caught by police and parents of the girl were informed and then the girl and the accused were brought to police station. The girl then narrated the incident to her mother and her father then lodged complaint on 17.01.2014. 5] On the basis of her complaint, offence as per C.R.No. I- 49/2014 under section 363, 366A, 376(i) of I.P.C. and section 4 of P.O.C.S.O. Act was registered at Kalwa Police Station and the work of investigation was entrusted to A.P.I. Bhosale. During the investigation school certificate of the girl was obtained. The girl was referred for medical examination and her medical certificate was obtained. Clothes .. 4 .. Special Case No. 82/2014 Judgment on the person of the girl as well as accused were seized. Panchnama of the spot was prepared. Statements of witnesses were recorded. During the investigation since it revealed that there was sufficient evidence against the accused, they came to be charge-sheeted for the offence punishable under section 363, 366A, 376(i) of I.P.C. and section 4 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. 6] Since offence under P.O.C.S.O. Act is exclusively triable by Special Court, the charge sheet was submitted to this Court. 7] The accused was produced before the court. A charge for offence punishable under section 363, 366A, 376 of I.P.C. and section 4 of P.O.C.S.O. Act was framed against the accused as per Exhibit 3. The contents of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. The accused pleaded not guilty. His defence was of total denial. He claimed to be tried. 8] For establishing the charges levelled against the accused the prosecution examined P.W.1 complainant Ram,esh Prajapati, father of the girl, P.W.2 Urmila Prajapati, mother of the girl, P.W.3 Poonam Prajpati, victim girl. The documentary evidence produced, proved and relied upon by the prosecution consisted of complaint Exhibit 11, medical certificate of the girl Exhibit 16, panchnama of seizure of clothes of the girl Exhibit 17 (exhibited on admission), panchnama of seizure clothes of the accused Exhibit 18 (exhibited on admission) spot panchnama Exhibit 19 (exhibited on admission) bona fide certificate of the girl Exhibit 20, potency certificate of the accused Exhibit 21. .. 5 .. Special Case No. 82/2014 Judgment 9] Statement of accused under section 313 of Cr.P.C. He did not examine himself on oath and had not adduced any evidence in defence. 10] I heard the learned A.P.P. and the learned advocate for the accused. It was argued by the learned A.P.P. that on the basis of evidence of the girl corroborated by the testimony of her parents and medical certificate and school certificate of the girl in regard to her date of birth, it is clear that the girl was minor below 18 years of age at the relevant time and the accused had enticed her to accompany him by giving threats and false promise of marriage and had time and again forcible sexual intercourse with her and therefore offences charged against the accused are proved and the accused is liable to be convicted for the charges levelled against him. 11] As against this it was argued on behalf of accused that from the testimony of the victim girl and her parents it is clear that there was love affair between the girl and the accused and the girl had left her house of her own and had stayed with the accused as his wife as per her own wish. It was also pointed out that the accused had even married to the girl and there is no question of accused giving false assurance of marriage to the girl. It was pointed out that the girl stated her age to the accused as 19 years and even the prosecution has failed to establish that the girl was below 18 years as alleged. It was submitted that though school certificate show date of birth of the girl, that is not correct date of birth and the prosecution has brought any evidence on record to establish correct date of birth of the girl. It was, therefore, pointed out that very fact that the girl was minor below 18 years of age is not established and in such circumstances when she had left her house of her .. 6 .. Special Case No. 82/2014 Judgment own and stayed of her own wish with the accused and whatever was done was done of her free consent and no offence can be said to have been proved against the accused and the accused is entitled to be acquitted. 12] On the basis of above facts of the accused following points arise for my determination and my findings and reasons for the same are as under - POINTS FINDINGS i) Whether the prosecution has proved that on 18.12.2013 between 7.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon from Badlapur gaon, the accused kidnapped minor girl Poonam Prajapati from lawful guardianship of her parents with intent that she may be or knowing it to be likely that she will be forced or seduced to have illicit intercourse with the accused ? NOT PROVED. ii ) Whether the prosecution has proved that after kidnapping the minor girl, during period from 18.12.2013 to 17.01.2014 the accused committed rape on the victim girl by doing forcible sexual intercourse with her ? NOT PROVED. iiI ) Whether the prosecution has proved that on the given day, date, time and place the accused committed sexual assault on the victim girl ? NOT PROVED. iv ) What offence, if any, is proved against the NO OFFENCE accused ? IS PROVED. v) What order ? As per the final order. REASONS 13] As is clear as per prosecution case the accused had enticed the girl on false assurance of marriage and had kidnapped her from lawful guardianship of her parents and had taken her to village .. 7 .. Special Case No. 82/2014 Judgment Jobiligaon, Badlapur and they stayed as husband and wife and he had forcible sexual intercourse with her during their stay and therefore, as per prosecution case, the accused is guilty of the offences charged against him. In that respect if the testimony of the prosecution witnesses is perused, it is clear that the fact that on 18.12.2013 the girl left the house in the morning for going to school and she had not returned back and therefore, mother of the girl searched of her and father of the girl lodged missing complaint appear to have been stated by the witnesses and do not appear to have been disputed on behalf of accused. Even the fact that the girl had been with the accused, stayed with him from 18.12.2013 till 17.01.2014 at construction site where the accused was working and during that period the accused and the girl had stayed as husband and wife and also the fact that there had been physical relations between them also appear to have been stated by P.W.1 and 2 as well as victim girl P.W.3 in evidence and said facts also do not appear to have been disputed or denied on behalf of accused. Even the fact that the girl had sexual intercourse is also clear from the medical certificate issued by the medical officer on examination of the girl after she was referred by police which show that there was old healed hymen tear and the evidence of penetrative vaginal sexual intercourse was present. 14] Then, though it is the case of the prosecution that the accused had enticed her to accompany him on threats and / or false assurance of marriage and taken her to village Jobiligaon, Badlapur and had forcible sexual intercourse with her from time to time and even P.W.1 and 2 i.e. father and mother of the girl, in their evidence stated that when the girl and the accused were caught at Dadar railway station and brought to police station and when they asked the victim girl as to what had happened and where she had been, the girl had disclosed them .. 8 .. Special Case No. 82/2014 Judgment that the accused had taken her with him on assurance of marriage and threats that he would defame her in the society and also that the accused had sexual intercourse with her, they do not appear to have stated that the girl had stated to them that the accused had sexual intercourse with the girl. 15] No doubt, even perusal of evidence of victim girl P.W.3 also reveal that she stated that accused met her on 18.12.2013 on her way to classes and stated to her that he likes her and she should come with him and if she refuse he would defame her by telling that she is indulging in love affair with him and being scared she went with him, she appear to have further stated that she stayed with the accused for one month and during that period he had sexual intercourse with her seven times and she also do not appear to have stated anything about forcible sexual intercourse by the accused with her. 16] Then, though in her cross-examination the girl appear to have denied the suggestion on behalf of accused that she had been with the accused as per her own wish and whatever physical relations were there they were with her consent, it cannot be ignored or overlooked that in her cross-examination itself she accepted that for a period of one month they stayed as husband and wife. It is material to mention that even the girl had denied the suggestion that she was in love with the accused and her parents were against it since the accused was from Muslim community. Her such version appear to be totally falsified and contradicted by the testimony of her mother P.W.2 because in her cross- examination though initially the mother denied for want of knowledge that her daughter and accused were having love affair, she accepted that prior to about one year of incident she herself had been to Goa to her .. 9 .. Special Case No. 82/2014 Judgment brother's house and her daughter Poonam also had been with her and there they developed acquaintance with the accused and at that time she returned back but Poonam stayed back for one month. She further accepted that after her daughter returned from Goa, she had disclosed to her that she was having love affair with the accused and also further that they were not agreeable to said love affair because the accused was belonging to Muslim community. She also further accepted that since her daughter was having love affair with the accused, she had run away with the accused of her own wish. That makes it clear that version of the victim girl that there was no such love affair and that she had been with the accused without her consent etc. is not true and correct narration of the fact. Even as rightly pointed out on behalf of accused the fact is very much clear that the girl had left the house on 18.12.2013, then the mother was knowing that the girl had left the house but did not return home but no action was taken by her till 27.12.2013 for about ten days and just missing complaint appear to have been lodged on 27.12.2013. Though the reason put forth by the complainant and his wife i.e. P.W.2, for delay in lodging the complaint that father of the girl was out of station, it is unbelievable and unacceptable that if girl went missing, mother would not take any immediate action in that regard and that clearly indicate that the mother was very well aware that the girl had left the house and gone with the accused. Even keeping aside that, the fact also appear to be material and worth consideration that though as per version of the complainant she was taken away by the accused forcefully on threats and being scared she alleged to have gone with the accused, fact is further clear that admittedly she stayed with the accused for a considerably long period of one month. In that regard if her cross- examination is perused, the girl appear to have stated that there was lot of crowd in the train as well as on the platform when the had been to .. 10 .. Special Case No. 82/2014 Judgment Badlapur. She also accepted that when they were staying at Jobiligaon, lot of people used to be there around and they were staying as husband and wife. In such circumstances if at all it was so that the accused had enticed her or threatened to accompany on threats and if at all the girl really did not want to to go with the accused,s he would have kept quiet and would have resisted such act and would have at least told about such act to the people around there. Having not done so, her such version that she was taken by the accused under threat cannot be said to be believable and acceptable. 17] Then, keeping apart that, it is also to be mentioned that there was no reason for the victim girl to be scared after she was caught by police alongwith accused and brought to police station and was referred for medical examination and there she could have definitely stated about such acts of the accused. But in that regard it is very much material to mention that when she was taken to Civil Hospital for medical examination, history was given by herself to the doctor in which she do not appear to have stated about any such threats or inducement given by the accused. On the contrary, the history recorded in medical certificate Exhibit 16 seen to have been given by the victim girl herself appear to be that '' victim married Sonu Khan in Masjid on 01.01.2014 and she left her house on 14.12.2013 and she had sex since 14.12.2013, 2 - 3 times a day ''. Such history given by the victim as recorded in the medical certificate admitted on behalf of accused make it very clear that the girl had frequently indulged into sexual intercourse with the accused of her own wish and no force or compulsion was there and even there is reference to the marriage of the girl with the accused in Masjid on 01.01.2014. Such history given by the girl to the medical officer and recorded by the medical officer in the medical certificate is in full .. 11 .. Special Case No. 82/2014 Judgment support and corroboration to the defence put forth by the accused that he had married to victim girl in Masjid and they were staying as husband and wife. 18] Even at the cost of repetition it can be said that the fact that the girl left the house on 18.12.2013 and no action was taken by her parents till 27.12.2013 and the complaint came to be lodged only on 17.01.2014 after one month and till then no grievance was expressed by the girl or her parents itself go to show that whatever had happened had happened with the consent of the girl. Even it would not be out of place to mention here that the history given by the girl to the medical officer that since 14.12.2013 the girl had sexual intercourse 2 - 3 times a day, makes her version before Court and before police that there was sexual intercourse by the accused total 7 to 8 times also is not true narration of facts and that even is not in conformity with the observation of the medical officer and that is also in further support of the defence put forth by the accused that the girl had been with him and they married and whatever had happened had happened with the consent of the girl and even the prosecution case that the accused had given false assurance of marriage is also falsified in the light of the fact that not only accused but the girl seen to have stated that they had performed marriage and they had stayed as husband and wife. In view of all above discussion it has to be concluded that the the allegations that the accused had enticed the girl with a view to have sexual intercourse with her on false assurance of marriage or took away the girl by threatening to defame her and had forcible sexual intercourse with her time and again as alleged, cannot be said to have been proved. .. 12 .. Special Case No. 82/2014 Judgment 19] Much was argued on behalf of prosecution that though it is case of consent the girl is minor below 18 years of age and therefore consent of the girl is immaterial and it was, therefore, argued that since it is established that the girl had been with the accused, parents of the girl were not consenting to it and that the accused had sexual intercourse with the girl and his all such acts amount to kidnapping of the girl and committing rape on her attracting provisions of section 4 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. It was also argued that since it is clear that the accused had sexual intercourse with the girl who was minor multiple times, aggravated form of sexual assault as defined under section 5 of P.O.C.S.O. Act has also to be held as proved. In that regard, as discussed above, it is concluded that whatever had happened had happened with free consent of the girl and the girl herself left the house and went with the accused and further, act of sexual intercourse with her also was with her consent and therefore age of the girl is crucial aspect. In that regard the prosecution appear to have relied upon school certificate of the girl produced on record. Said certificate is admitted on behalf of accused to be genuine school certificate and therefore, the school certificate was marked as Exhibit 20. However, correctness of the date of birth mentioned in the school certificate was disputed on behalf of accused. In such circumstance in has to be mentioned that by admitting the school certificate, the only fact which can be said to have been established is that as per school record the date of birth of the girl is 15.09.1998 but so far as correctness and genuineness of said entry of date of birth is concerned, as is clear that has been disputed on behalf of accused and therefore, it was necessary for the prosecution to establish by cogent and reliable evidence as to on what basis said entry was made in the school record or by producing birth certificate. .. 13 .. Special Case No. 82/2014 Judgment 20] It is to be mentioned in that regard that as rightly argued on behalf of accused the entry of the date of birth in the school record cannot be said to be a conclusive proof in regard to date of birth of the girl, that is particularly when the correctness and genuineness of the school certificate is disputed on behalf of accused. It is to be mentioned that in normal course, an entry in the school record in regard to date of birth of the child is made on the basis of information given by the parents. In that regard if the fact that birth certificate of the girl is not produced is considered, in the light of the testimony of the parents of the girl who are examined as P.W.1 and 2 it is to be mentioned that father of the girl in his evidence stated that at the relevant time in the year 2013 the girl was 15 years old. Then, in her examination-in-chief mother of the girl stated that the girl was 16 years old. It is further material to mention that birth certificate of the girl issued by local authority is not produced on record and in the light of that if the cross-examination of the mother of the girl is perused, it appears that she stated that prior to about one year of incident, which must be in the month of December, 2012, she had been to her brother's house at Goa and there they developed acquaintance with the accused and Poonam stayed back for one month and she also categorically accepted that at that time Poonam was 16 years old and then in the light of that the age of the girl at the time of incident in December, 2012 if considered, the possibility of the girl being more than 18 years old cannot be ruled out. Even though the girl was referred for medical examination, no ossification test to determine her age appear to have been carried out. In the light of that non-production of birth certificate on record on the basis of which entry of date of birth of the girl in school record is made has to be held as fatal lacuna and create doubt about exact age of the girl. .. 14 .. Special Case No. 82/2014 Judgment 21] In the light of that if the defence put forth by the accused that at that time the girl stated her age as 19 years to the accused and she herself ran away with him and had stayed with him since her parents were against their love affair and about to fix her marriage with somebody else and therefore she came to him and married to him etc. appear to be more probable in the light of the fact that entire version of the victim girl is found to have totally shattered and shaken and even seen to have been falsified by her own mother and not found to be reliable and trustworthy witness. In view of above discussion the submission on behalf of accused that the prosecution has failed to prove beyond reasonable doubt that the girl at the relevant time was minor below 18 years of age and therefore, the submission on behalf of prosecution that consent of the girl is immaterial and therefore offences charged against the accused have to be held as proved cannot be said to be sustainable and acceptable. 22] In view of above discussion it has to be concluded that the prosecution has failed to establish that the accused enticed the girl and kidnapped her under threats to defame and false assurance of marriage and then had forcible sexual intercourse repeatedly. Point no.1 to 3 are therefore answered in the negative. As to point no.4 - 23] In view of above discussion it has to be held that the prosecution has failed to establish the guilt of the accused beyond all the reasonable doubt and the accused are entitled to be acquitted. Point no.4 is answered accordingly. .. 15 .. Special Case No. 82/2014 Judgment 24] Since the accused is acquitted, it is necessary that he be directed to furnish P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/- [rupees fifteen thousand only] under section 437A of Cr.P.C. to appear before the higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect of any appeal or petition, if any, filed against the judgment and that such bail bond shall be in force for six months. In the result I pass the following order- ORDER Accused namely Sonu Sobrati Khan is acquitted of the charge for offence punishable under section 363, 366A, 376 of I.P.C. and section 4 and 6 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 2) The accused shall be released from the jail forthwith if not required in any other crime. 3) The accused shall furnish P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/- [rupees fifteen thousand only] under section 437A of Cr.P.C. to appear before the higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect of any appeal or petition, if any filed against the judgment and that such bail bond shall be in force for six months. 4) Muddemal articles, being worthless, be destroyed after expiry of appeal period. 5) The proceeding is closed. Date : 23.07.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Additional Session Judge-1, Thane.

.. 1 .. bail no.880/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 880/2015 This application is filed by applicant Mr. Kiran Dinanath Kene for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. I­70/2015 registered at Thanenagar police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 385, 506 of I.P.C. and section 11(V)(VI) of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act) and also section 66(C) of I. T. Act. It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant demanded money for returning the photographs of the accused and girl and also he threatened to the girl to continue the relationship with the accused and also used the account of the girl on social website like facebook without her permission. It is further submitted that the applicant is falsely implicated in this crime. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co­operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that there was love relationship between the accused and the girl and they had clicked their photographs sitting together and when the girl demanded the said photographs the accused refused and even demanded Rs.50,000/­ for returning the photographs to the girl and had also threatened her to continue the relationship with him and also threatened to create obstacle in fixation of her marrige. It is further .. 2 .. bail no.880/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) contended and argued that the accused also used the account of the girl on social website like facebook without her permission. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/ accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl and the prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 385, 506 of I.P.C. and section 11(V)(VI) of P.O.C.S.O. Act and also section 66(C) of I. T. Act, it appears that the accused had been arrested on 03.04.2015. Then, it is also stated that the accused and the girl were well acquainted with each other but on account of previous enmity between him and family of victim, he is falsely implicated in the crime. Even it is also clear that even though the provisions of P.O.C.S.O. Act are attracted, there are no allegations of causing molestation of the girl. In such circumstance whether the allegations against the accused are true or not, would be the question to be decided on merits. Even nothing is to be recovered from the applicant/accused. 4] It is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is .. 3 .. bail no.880/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 5] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 6] Then, it has also to be mentioned that the investigation in the matter though almost completed, the charge sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 7] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Mr. Kiran Dinanath Kene is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ .. 4 .. bail no.880/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) The applicant/accused shall attend the concerned police station on every Friday between6.00 p.m. to 8.00p.m. till filing of the charge sheet and shall co­operate in investigation. He shall not contact the complainant in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the complainant and other prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this Court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. He shall furnish documentary proof to the effect that he has attend the examination of engineering course. Date : 10.04.2015 (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Additional Sessions Judge­1, Thane.

1 Bail No.895/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) Criminal Bail Application No.895/2016 Arvind Krishnakumar Patel .. Applicant versus The State of Maharashtra Through Shantinagar Police Station .. Non­applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 1] By this application the applicant is seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. who was arrested on 26/02/2016 by Shantinagar Police Station in connection with C.R.No.I­ 48/2016 registered for an offence punishable under section 363, 366 & 376 of I.P.C. and section 3 & 4 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as P.O.C.S.O. Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Mr.Sandeep Dongre for the applicant/accused and learned Spl.P.P. Mrs.R.A.Navale for State. I.O. present. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 13/02/2016 at the instance of the informant/mother of the victim­girl aged about 16 years with an indictment that on 08/02/2016 victim­ 2 Bail No.895/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) girl left home for school and since then she did not return therefore, with the suspicion that she had been kidnapped by accused, the F.I.R. was lodged. During investigation it reveals that the accused sexually assaulted the victim­girl and therefore, offence under section 376 was added. 4] The learned Counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant/accused is falsely implicated. He submitted that in fact the victim­girl is major and in the report itself initially her age is mentioned as 18 years. He further submitted that the accused and victim­girl knows each other since 1 & ½ months and it is a case of love affair. The victim­girl herself accompanied with accused and she was not kidnapped by accused. The victim­girl was with accused for 20 days. The accused is behind bar since 60 days. The investigation is almost completed. The accused is young boy of 23 years and having no criminal antecedents. The accused is permanent resident of Bhiwandi, Thane. The accused is ready to abide any conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing him on bail. 5] Per contra, the learned Spl.P.P. opposed the application submitting that the offence is serious in respect of a minor girl. She submitted that as victim­girl is minor there is no question of consent. In medical certificate the victim­girl gave the history about sexual inter­course. The statement of victim­ 3 Bail No.895/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) girl was recorded wherein she has stated that accused threatened her and committed sexual assault on her. The investigation is in progress. There are chances of tampering with witnesses and prayed for rejection of application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R., it appears that initially, the F.I.R. was lodged by the mother of the victim­girl about kidnapping of her daughter. However, during investigation the victim­girl was found with accused and sexually assaulted therefore, the provisions of section 366 & 376 of I.P.C. were added. However, it appears that victim­girl is aged about 16 years and five months which means she has attained the age of discretion. The accused and victim­girl were together for about 20 days. There appears no violence used by accused. No external injuries were found on the person of victim­girl. The accused is behind bar since about two months. The material part of investigation appears to have been completed. The accused is young boy of 23 years and report filed by the I.O. did not disclose that there is any criminal antecedents against the accused. No fruitful purpose would be served by further incarceration of accused. The object of bail is neither punitive nor preventive but to secure the presence of the accused at the time of trial. He is ready to abide by the conditions imposed by the Court. In such circumstances the apprehension of learned Spl.P.P. about tampering of witnesses 4 Bail No.895/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) can be addressed by imposing suitable conditions. Hence, I pass the following order ­ ORDER 1) The application is allowed. 2) Applicant namely Arvinda Krishnakumar Patel be released on bail on his executing P.R. Bond of ₹.30,000/­ [Rupees Thirty Thousand only] with one or two solvent surety in the like amount on the following conditions ­ A] Applicant shall attend the concerned police station on every Sunday between 10.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon till filing the charge­sheet. B] Applicant shall co­operate in investigation and shall not tamper with prosecution witnesses. C] Applicant shall furnish his and his two blood relatives' address proofs and contact numbers and he is duty bound to inform I.O. and Court about the change of address, if any. Thane. Date : 28/04/2016. (Ms. U.M. Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act), Thane.

.. 1 .. bail no.910/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exhibit 1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 910/2015 This application is filed by applicants namely Kamla Ajay Dadhich and Geeta Gopal Rana for their release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no.137/2015 registered at Kashimira police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 372, 373 of I.P.C. and section 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act) and also under section 3, 4, 5, 6, and 7(1) of Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act (hereinafter in short referred to as ''I.T.P.A.''). It was contended and argued that the applicants are arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicants were conducting prostitution business by procuring girls including minor and were earning livelihood from said business. It is further contended and argued that the applicants are falsely implicated on the basis of suspicion. It is further contended and argued that the applicants have not earned money from prostitution business and have not even purchased any property from such money. 2] It is submitted on behalf of applicants that applicant Kamla Dadhich that she is suffering from thyroid and B.P. and applicant Geeta Rana is suffering from skin disease and they are in need of proper medical attention. It is further submitted that since the applicants are in jail, there is nobody to look after their family and children. It is further submitted that the applicants are permanent residents of the address given and that if the present applicants/accused are released on bail, they will co­operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will .. 2 .. bail no.910/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 3] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that on receiving secret information police conducted raid and during said raid it revcealed that one minor girl namely Kavita Nepali was being compelled to do prostitution and was sent with customer to give sexual pleasure. It is further contended and argued that the accused persons were doing such illegal activity and were accepting money from the customers in the form of their livelihood. It is further contended and argued that the applicants were charging Rs.1 lac from each customer to provide minor girl for ''virgin break''. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicants/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicants threatening the victim girl and other prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicants is released on bail they may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicants are not entitled to be released on bail. 4] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 372, 373 of I.P.C. and section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and also section 3, 4, 5, 6, 7(1) of I.T.P.A. with the allegation that they have compelled the minor girl Kavita Nepali to do prostitution though they were knowing that she was minor aged 17 years and even it is alleged that they have been making minor girls available for prostitution and have been charging Rs.1 lac for ''virgin break'' and though it is also case of .. 3 .. bail no.910/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) prosecution and clear from the complaint as well as panchnama of raid that the applicants/accused were caught at the time of raid and they were found in possession of some money etc., it is to be mentioned that the applicants have come up with the case that they have been falsely implicated in this crime. Then, it is also to be mentioned that though it is alleged that the applicants/accused and other accused have been charging Rs.1 lac from each customer for making the girl available for ''virgin break'', no recovery of amount appear to be there. Then, so far as the aspect that the applicants/ accused have purchased huge property in their name or in the name of their relatives out of the money earned from said business, that aspect will have to be decided after the trial on the basis of evidence adduced in that regard and it would be premature to conclude at this stage that such property, if any, purchased by the applicants/accused or co­accused is out of ill­gotten money from the prostitution business. 5] Then, it is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicants would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicants tampering with prosecution evidence if they are released on bail. In that respect it is contended by the applicants that they are permanent residents of the address given and they will not abscond if released on bail and that they are ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 6] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the .. 4 .. bail no.910/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicants/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 7] Then, it has also to be mentioned that looking the allegations against the accused the investigation in the matter may have almost completed but the charge­sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge­sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicants/accused in jail for uncertain period. 8] Then, the applicants have also filed on record case papers regarding their diseases and it is submitted that the applicant Kamla Dadhich is suffering from thyroid and B.P. and applicant Geeta Rana is suffering from skin disease and they are in need of proper medical treatment. 9] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicants can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused namely Kamla Ajay Dadhich and Geeta Gopal Rana are released on P.R. bond of Rs.20,000/­ [rupees .. 5 .. bail no.910/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) twenty thousand only] each with one surety each in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ The applicants/accused shall not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and the prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. They shall not leave India without permission of this Court. They shall furnish proof of residence. Date : 26.06.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.

No.I- 117/2015 registered with Vikramgad Police Station in respect of the present accused. 4] Learned Sp.P.P. prayed for necessary orders. 5] The provision of section 167(2) of Cr.P.C. is very much clear which gives an indefeasible right to the accused if the charge-sheet has not been submitted within the period of sixty or ninety days. Thus, it is very much clear that even after completion of 90 days on 04/04/2016 the charge-sheet has not been submitted against applicant/accused in C.R.No.I-117/2015 registered with Vikramgad Police Station. .. 1 .. bail no.931/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exhibit 1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 931/2015 This application is filed by applicant Mazib Munshiraja Gujjar for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. I­60/2015 registered at Rabodi police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 363, 376 of I.P.C. and section 4 and 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant induced the minor girl and kidnapped her and then had sexual intercourse with her. It is further contended and argued that there was love affair between the applicant and the girl and she had of her own left the house and the applicant has not kidnapped and it is a case of consent and that the applicant is falsely implicated in this crime. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co­operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. . 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that the accused and the victim were knowing each other since before the incident of kidnapping and taking disadvantage of minor age of the victim girl, the accused enticed her and then kidnapped her with intention that she may be seduced to have illicit intercourse and .. 2 .. bail no.931/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) thereafter he had forcible sexual intercourse with her under false assurance of marriage. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl and the prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused are of serious nature under section 363, 366A, 376 of I.P.C. and section 4 and 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, it appears that case of consent is put forth on behalf of accused and it is contended on his behalf that there was love affair between him and the girl and she had left the house of her own and it is further contended on behalf of applicant that he is falsely implicated in the crime. In such circumstance whether the allegations against the accused are true or not, would be the question to be decided on merits. Even nothing is to be recovered from the applicant/accused. 4] Then, it is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the .. 3 .. bail no.931/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 5] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 6] Then, it has also to be mentioned that the investigation in the matter though almost completed, the charge sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 7] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Mazib Munshiraja Gujjar is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ .. 4 .. bail no.931/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) The applicant/accused shall attend the concerned police station on every Thursday between 10.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon till filing of the charge sheet and shall co­operate in investigation. He shall not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and the prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this Court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. CRI. ANTI. BAIL APPLN. NO.874/2018 Order­Exh. 1 ORDER BELOW EXH.1 IN ANTI. CRI. BAIL APPLN. NO.874/2018 MHTH01­002541­2018 1] Present application is preferred by accused Mohammad Abid Shahid Sayyed for grant of bail under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. on the ground that he is falsely implicated in the matter. The applicant did not administer any poisonous or any stupefying substances and thus entire story is false and concocted. According to applicant, offence is not punishable with death or imprisonment for life and thus, he has requested to release him on bail. 2] Say of I.O. was called for. I.O. has strongly objected the application by filing say below Exh. 4 and contended that statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. of the complainant is to be recorded and if the applicant is released on bail, he is likely to tamper with the evidence and likely to threaten witnesses. According to I.O., applicant is habitual in consumption of stupefying substances and if he released on bail, he is likely to indulge in similar offence. According to I.O., C.A. report, medical report etc. are yet to be received. Hence, request has been made to reject the application. 3] Heard rival advocates. They have submitted in terms of CRI. ANTI. BAIL APPLN. NO.874/2018 Order­Exh. 1 their respective contention and submissions. After having heard the Ld. Advocates, I have gone through the FIR. Even after the FIR is considered as it is, it is apparent that present applicant with the victim and other co­accused were under the influence of some stupefying substance and there are no specific allegation as to who actually has administered it to victim. Further, the age of the victim is more than 17 years. Therefore, it can be presumed that she understood the consequences of the act before the said substance was administered to her. Though, I.O. objected the application on the ground that the offence is under POCSO, but the allegations referred in the FIR if considered as it is then only, it is apparent prima facie that all the alleged act appears to have been committed under the influence of the said stupefying substance. Hence, considering this fact and particularly the settled proposition of law that the bail is the rule and jail is exception, in my opinion, the present peculiar facts of the application, relief claimed by the applicant can be granted. So far as, the apprehension of the I.O. is concern with the imposition of stringent conditions suffice the purpose. Hence, the order. : ORDER : 1] Application is allowed. 2] Applicant­accused is released on his executing P.R. and CRI. ANTI. BAIL APPLN. NO.874/2018 Order­Exh. 1 S.B.of Rs.30,000/­ with one solvent surety in the like amount. 3] Applicant shall attend concern police station on every 1st and 15th day of each English calender month until further order or till filing of chargesheet, which every is earlier. 4] Applicant shall produce his photo identity, address proof of self and his two close relatives and shall not indulge in similar activity. 5] Bail in concern court. Thane (Hemant M. Patwardhan) Date:04/05/2018 D.J.­4 & Addl. Sessions Judge, Thane

Presented on : 07.04.2016 Registered on : 07.04.2016 Decided on : 08.09.2017 Duration : 01 Y 05 M 2 D IN THE COURT OF SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE, AT : THANE (Presided over by P.P.Jadhav) District Judge­6 and Additional Sessions Judge, Thane Spl. Case POCSO No.92/2016 Exh.No.12. State of Maharashtra (through Narpoli Pol.Stn. Cr.No.I­346/2015) ...Complainant Vs. Sadik Irshad Ahmad, Age 24 years, Occ. Education, R/at.Building No.12, Flat No.3 Sainagar colony, Behind Ashoknagar, Gaibinagar, Bhiwandi, Dist. Thane, ...Accused For the offence punishable u/s.354A, 323, 504 of Indian Penal Code and u/s.12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. APP Mr.V.A.Kulkarni for State Adv.Mr.S.S.Bhoir for the accused J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 92­16 ­ 354, 12.doc .....2/­ ..2.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 92/2016.. Exh.12.. : JUDGMENT : (Delivered on this 08th day of September, 2017) The accused is charge sheeted for offence of assaulting the complainant, outraging her modesty and sexually harassing her minor sister. 2] The prosecution story runs as under : It is alleged by prosecution that the complainant is 19 years old girl residing at Gaibinagar, Bhiwandi alongwith her minor sister, younger brother and mother. Her father was serving at Dubai. In the year 2015 the complainant was studying in 12th Science in B.N.N. College, Bhiwandi. Complainant's minor sister was studying in same college in 11th Science. The accused is residing in the vicinity of the complainant. He used to talk with complainant's minor sister on mobile phone. The complainant had brought said fact to the notice of her mother who had convinced complainant's minor sister not to have contact with the accused. However, the accused used to phone complainant's sister during nights. Even after the complainant and her mother had convinced the accused not to phone complainant's sister, he was not listening. He used to phone her even at midnight. He used to harass the complainant and her sister while they were attending the college. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 92­16 ­ 354, 12.doc .....3/­ ..3.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 92/2016.. Exh.12.. 3] It is further alleged by the prosecution that, on 21.08.2015 at about 02.30 midnight the accused had phoned complainant's sister. He was repeatedly calling her on mobile. The complainant asked the accused not to phone at their house, but he continued to ring the phone till 05.30 a.m. On 22.08.2015 at about 11.40 a.m. while the complainant was at college, the accused was wondering outside her classroom. When the complainant was going to private tuition alongwith her friends, the accused obstructed her on the way. He hold complainant's right hand and slapped her thrice. Thereby he outraged her modesty and voluntarily caused hurt to her. Complainant's friend tried to caught hold accused, he pushed them and fled away. Thereafter the complainant approached Narpoli police station and reported the incident. 4] After receiving FIR, offence u/s.354A, 504, 323 of the Indian Penal Code came to be registered against the accused. As the accused was harassing the complainant's minor sister, aged 15 years old, section 12 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act came to be added. After entire investigation, charge sheet came to be filed against the accused for said offences. 5] Charge is framed against the accused at Exh.04. Accused pleaded not guilty of offence and claimed to be tried. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 92­16 ­ 354, 12.doc .....4/­ ..4.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 92/2016.. Exh.12.. 6] Statement of accused u/s.313 of Code of Criminal Procedure is recorded at Exh.11. The defence of the accused is that, he is well acquainted with the complainant and her minor sister. He had helped the complainant's minor sister in getting admission in B.N.N. College. Out of misunderstanding the complainant filed false complaint against him. 7] After going through the prosecution story, evidence on record and hearing arguments of both sides, following points arise for my determination. I record my findings thereon for reasons as stated below. POINTS FINDINGS 1] Does the prosecution prove that on 22.08.2015 at about 15.30 hours at B.N.N. College, Bhiwandi the accused caught hold the hand of the complainant, pulled her towards him and outraged her modesty ? …Not proved. 2] Does the prosecution further prove that on the same date, time and place the accused slapped the complainant thrice and voluntarily accused hurt to her ? …Not proved. 3] Does the prosecution further prove that on the same date, time and place the accused abused the complainant and intentionally insulted her ? …Not proved. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 92­16 ­ 354, 12.doc .....5/­ ..5.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 92/2016.. Exh.12.. 4] Does the prosecution further prove that prior to 22.08.2015 the accused used to phone the complainant's minor sister during nights and used to sexually harass her ? …Not proved. 5] What order ? ..As per final order. : REASONS : As to the Point Nos.1 to 4 :­ 8] All points are arising out of one and the same incident, hence they are discussed together. To bring home the guilt of accused the prosecution has examined the complainant Shamama Jarar Shaikh as PW1 at Exh.6. The complaint lodged by her is at Exh.7. The complainant's minor sister is examined as PW2 at Exh.8. 9] In the deposition before the Court the complainant narrated almost all facts alleged in the complaint, in her examination­in­chief. She specifically deposed that the accused used to phone her sister during night. On one occasion he had phoned her at 02.30 midnight. She had asked the accused not to phone her sister. Thereupon the accused had raised quarrel with her. On next day i.e. on 22.08.2015 while the complainant was at college, the accused raised quarrel with her and beat her. Thereupon she lodged complaint Exh.7 against him. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 92­16 ­ 354, 12.doc .....6/­ ..6.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 92/2016.. Exh.12.. 10] In cross examination PW1 has given vital admissions. She has admitted that the accused was studying in B.N.N. College and was representative of male students. She (PW1) was representative of girl students. The accused had helped her sister at the time of admission in said college. Out of said admission work, the complainant's sister used to phone the accused during nights. The accused also used to phone in respect of the same. PW1 further admitted that at the time of alleged incident in the college, there was mob of girls and boys. Both the groups had exchange of words with each other. In said mob the boys and girls scuffled with each other. In said scuffle someone had hold her hand and slapped her. She lodged complaint against the accused merely out of suspicion. 11] PW2 who is complainant's minor sister has also deposed that the accused had helped her in getting admission in B.N.N. College. In respect of the same the accused used to phone her. Her mother and sister were not happy with said fact and had asked the accused not to phone her. Her sister had told her about the assault at the hands of accused. 12] PW2 has not stated that the accused had ever sexually harassed her. On the contrary she admitted in cross examination that the accused never misbehaved with her. She further admitted that the accused is her best friend. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 92­16 ­ 354, 12.doc .....7/­ ..7.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 92/2016.. Exh.12.. 13] Thus from the evidence on record it is clear that the complaint came to be lodged against the accused merely out of suspicion. There is no reliable evidence against the accused. The prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of the accused. Hence answering point Nos.1 to 4 in the negative, following order is passed. ORDER 1. Accused Sadik Irshad Ahmad is hereby acquitted u/s.235(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure for offence punishable u/s.354, 323, 504 of the Indian Penal Code and section 12 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 2. The bail bond of accused stands cancelled. 3. Accused is directed to furnish personal bond of Rs.5,000/­ in terms of sec.437­A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Sd/­... Thane. (P.P.Jadhav) District Judge­6 and Date : 08.09.2017. Addl. Sessions Judge, Thane. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 92­16 ­ 354, 12.doc ...../­

1 Cri.Bail Apln.No. 912/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) Criminal Bail Application No.912/2016 Naushad Ali Gulam Mustufa Shah .. Applicant versus The State of Maharashtra (Through Bhihwandi city Police Station) .. Non­applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 1] By this application the applicant is seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. who was arrested on 30/03/2016 by Bhiwandi city Police Station in connection with C.R.No.I­90/2016 registered for an offence punishable under section 377 & 506 of I.P.C. and section 3(a), (c), 4,6,7,10 & 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as P.O.C.S.O. Act). 2] Heard learned Advocate Mr. Agaskar for the applicant/accused and Spl.PP Mrs.H.A.Deshmukh and I.O. present with case diary. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 30/03/2016 at the instance of the informant/father of victim­boy aged about 12 years with an indictment that accused took his minor victim­ boy in the public toilet and committed un­natural act with him. 2 Cri.Bail Apln.No. 912/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) 4] The learned Counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant/accused is falsely implicated. He further submitted that the incident stated to be taken place in public toilet in day­light is not possible. There is delay of 4 days in lodging F.I.R. and the said F.I.R. is after thought only to implicate accused falsely. He further submitted that F.I.R. was registered around 02.55 hours and the accused was arrested within half an hour at 3.31 hours, which itself shows that it is a manipulated F.I.R. He further submitted that accused is young boy of 19 years and relative of informant and informant assaulted the accused and accused had been to police station to lodge report, but his report was not taken. The accused is ready to abide by any condition imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing on bail. 5] Per contra, the ld. Spl.P.P. opposed the application submitting that the offence is serious in respect of minor boy. She further submitted accused is a tuition teacher and the victim­boy used to go to learn Arbi and accused took undue advantage and did the heinous act thrice. She further submitted that there are eye witness to the incident and even during investigation it was revealed that accused did similar act with another boy of 10 years. He further submitted that investigation is in progress and there are chances of tampering of witnesses 3 Cri.Bail Apln.No. 912/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) and prayed for rejection of application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R., it appears that report was lodged by the father of victim­boy about the carnal inter­course against the nature. The F.I.R. is detail one giving the specific act of the accused. There is specific allegations. The victim­boy disclosed that the accused thrice committed the un­ natural act with the victim­boy and when the informant refused to send his boy for class, still accused followed him and insisted him to send the victim­boy to the class. The investigation is in progress and at this stage, delay in lodging F.I.R. cannot be considered as the offence is very serious in respect of minor boy and further during investigation it reveals that another boy of 10 years was also subjected to such heinous act at the hands of accused. The investigation is at nascent stage. Looking to the serious allegations against the accused the apprehension expressed by learned Spl.P.P. about tampering of evidence by pressurizing the small victim­boy is well founded. Hence, at this stage no case made for releasing the accused on bail. Hence, I pass following order:­ ORDER The application stands rejected. Thane. Date : 29/04/2016. (Ms. U.M. Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act), Thane.

What order? As per final order. REASONS AS TO POINT NOS.1 & 2 :­ 7] Prosecution examined in all two witnesses to bring home the guilt of accused. P.W.1­Sou. Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­002573­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 84/14 Received on : 17.04.2014 Registered on : 17.04.2014 Decided on : 03.09.2018 Duration : 4Ys. 4Ms. 16 Ds. IN THE COURT OF D.J.­1 & ADDL. SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE. (Presided over by Hemant M. Patwardhan) Special Case (POCSO) No. 84/14 Exh.No. State of Maharashtra, (Mumbra Police station) ..Complainant V/s. 1] Akhtar alias Antu Khadihussain Sayyad. Age 45 years, Occ. Business, R/at. Aman Heights, R. No. 112/1, Shivajingar, Mumbra, Thane ..Accused Appearance:­ APP Mr. Londhe for the State. Advocate Mr. Javed Ansari for accused JUDGMENT (Delivered on this 3rd day of September 2018) Accused Akhtar alias Antu Khadihussain Sayyad was facing trial under sections 354 of Indian Penal Code read with Sec. 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 on following facts. 1 OF 7 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­002573­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 84/14 1] That on 03.10.2013 at about 19.00 hrs. at Aman Heights, R.No. 1/110, Shivajinagar, Mumbra, Thane used criminal force against victim by holding her from backside and by touching her breast with intent to outrage her modesty and as the victim girl was minor at the relevant time, on the complaint of complainant an offence punishable under aforesaid two sections came to be registered against accused. On completion of investigation he was charge­sheeted. 2] Charge came to be framed below Exh. 3 and contents of said charge were read over and explained to accused in vernacular. Accused pleaded not guilty and claim to be tried. His defence was of total denial. 3] Prosecution in order to bring guilt of the accused at home has then proceeded to examine victim, I.O. Harshal Kamgar, another I.O. Dattatraya Sonvalkar as PW 1 to 3 respectively. Then the statement of accused was recorded by my learned Predecessor. 4] Arguments of rival advocates were heard. Learned P.P. has categorically pointed out that victim has deposed in terms of prosecution's case and there is nothing in the cross­examination to discard her version. Thus, according to learned P.P. said unshattered testimony of the victim is sufficient to discard the evidence. Per contra, it was argued by the accused's advocate that deposition of the 2 OF 7 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­002573­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 84/14 victim is not corroborated by any other witness though first disclosure was made to the mother of the friend of the victim, police did not procure her presence before the court though she is readily available and thus as the deposition of the victim remains uncorroborated her sole testimony cannot be relied upon. According to submissions other witnesses though were examined have never seen the incident and thus their depositions are not sufficient to corroborate the victim's deposition. Hence, he has requested to acquit the accused from all the allegations. 5] After having heard the rival advocates when the matter was kept for Judgment since last 3 to 4 times the advocate of the accused has either filed application for seeking adjournment on the ground that accused is not present before the court or has orally made request with the condition of the accused was not such to ask the accused to wait throughout the day. Hence, the mater was adjourned from time to time for Judgment. In the meantime on last to last occasion accused has made another attempt of relieving him from liability of the case by filing application of original complainant for informing the court that she do not wish to proceed in the trial. However, as her deposition is already on record and as the offence with which accused is charged is not compoundable the court was not able to consider the said application. On the basis of aforesaid facts the case was proceeded. 6] After having heard the rival advocates, following points 3 OF 7 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­002573­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 84/14 arise for my consideration and I record my findings against each of them for the reasons noted below:­ S.N. Points Findings 1] Does the prosecution prove that accused on 03.10.2013 at about ..In the negative. 19.00 hrs. at Aman Heights, R.No. 1/110, Shivajinagar, Mumbra, Thane used criminal force against victim by holding her from backside and by touching her breast with intent to outrage her modesty and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 354 of Indian Penal Code ? 2] Does the prosecution prove that accused on the same date, time and ..In the negative. place caught old victim girl from backside and touched her breast and thereby committed sexual assault on the said minor girl punishable under section 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012? 3] What order ? Accused is acquitted as per final order. REASONS As to point nos. 1 to 3 :­ 7] All these points are interlinked with each other and therefore, are considered at once. In the instant case victim has categorically alleged before the court that on eventful day at about 7.00 p.m. when she alone was in the house, on the pretext to know whether the house of the victim has a bedroom, accused has entered the bedroom and then on pretext of showing something to victim had called near him and has moved his hand over the breast of the victim and when the victim has asked him to leave her otherwise she will shout she was relieved. According to victim she immediately ran 4 OF 7 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­002573­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 84/14 towards the house of her friend Ruksana and had informed her mother about the incident. Except said deposition, there is absolutely nothing on record which corroborate the incident. On the basis of said victim appears to have filed this case. Though arguments were advanced as above, court has to scrutinize whether uncorroborated testimony of victim is really sufficient to establish guilt of accused. 8] Prosecution has alleged that accused has committed offence not only under section 354 of IPC but also under section 8 of POCSO Act. In order to prima facie establish the guilt under POCSO prosecution has to establish that victim was really minor at the relevant time of the incident. However, in the present case except vague statement that victim was in 7th Std. there is absolutely nothing on record to say as to what was her date of birth and actually was her age on the date of incident. Investigating officer has categorically admitted that he has not obtained any birth certificate from the victim. Therefore, except the statement that victim was in 7th Std. there is absolutely nothing on record to substantiate the allegations of the prosecution. Hence, in absence of any substantive evidence on the said point, it is difficult to say that victim was really minor at the relevant time of incident. There are instances, children remains to be in the same standards for years together due to lack of knowledge and proper presentation in the examination. Hence, only on the basis of the fact that victim was in 7th Std. cannot be sufficient to say that she was 5 OF 7 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­002573­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 84/14 minor within the meaning of the said Act. In absence of any such evidence on record it is difficult to accept that POCSO will really applicable in the matter. 9] Now, turning towards the offence under section 354 of IPC. The intention is material ingredient in the said section. There is absolutely no rivalry between the victim and the accused which is prior to the date of incident so that the accused will certainly enter the house of the victim for purposes of committing the offence with intention of outraging the modesty of the victim. Further, according to the substantial evidence of the victim herself just after her threat of making an attempt to shout the accused has relieved her. The said fact also certainly difficult to digest when accused and allegedly entered in the house of the victim for outraging the modesty of the victim. Hence, said facts being very vague in nature are require to be substantiated or corroborated by other witnesses. However, though victim has categorically made statement that she has disclosed the said fact immediately after the incident to mother of her friend Ruksana, prosecution did not made any attempt to procure the presence of the said witness for corroborating allegations of prosecution. Hence, deposition of the victim remains uncorroborated in that sense. Further, by filing the application victim herself has now requested the concern police machinery to reconsider the matter as it was filed under misunderstanding. Though matter is not compoundable but if that particular fact is considered coupled with aforesaid uncorroborated facts it is certainly sufficient to say that the 6 OF 7 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­002573­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 84/14 particular allegations are not being properly substantiated by evidence beyond reasonable doubt. Hence, in my opinion benefit of doubt can be extended in favour of accused person. Thus, by recording my findings against point no.1 and 2 in negative, I proceed to pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused is acquitted from the offence punishable under sections 354 of IPC read with sections 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] Bail bonds of accused shall stand canceled. 3] Accused is directed to execute P.R. and S.B. of Rs.10,000/­ as per amended provisions of section 437(A) of Cr.P.C. and bonds so executed shall remain in force for the period of six months from the date of its execution. 4] Proceeding is accordingly closed. Thane (Hemant M.Patwardhan) Date: 03.09.2018 D.J.­1 & Additional Sessions Judge, Thane 7 OF 7

The accused did not examined himself, nor led the evidence. 9] From the statement under section 313 of Cr.P.C. and evidence on record his defence is of denial. 10] I have heard learned APP and learned defence counsel today. 11] In these circumstances following points arise for my determination and I record my finding to them for the .....4/­ 4 Spl.POCSO Case 85/2014 reasons mentioned hereinafter :­ Sr. POINTS FINDINGS No. 1] Whether prosecution proved that In the from September, 2013 to affirmative. 12/11/2013 near Zamzam Haull, Amrut Nagar, Mumbra, within the jurisdiction of Mumbra police station accused committed act of physical contact involving unwelcome and explicit sexual over cures and thus committed offence punishable under section 354 A of I.P.C. ? 2] Whether on the said date, time and Partly in the place and during the course of affirmative same transaction accused as offence committed an offence of sexual under assault with daughter of section 11 complainant namely Kaynat aged 9 of POCSO years ?
