--1-- ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN CRIMINAL BAIL APPLICATION NO.889/2018 CNR NO.MHTH01­002591­2018 The applicant Vivek Ramkiran Yadav has applied for bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C., in C.R.No.98/2018 registered in Rabale police station for the offence under section 363 read with 34 of IPC and Section 7, 8, 17 and 18 of POCSO Act, 2012. 2. It is contended that there was love affair between victim and accused. There is no prima facie case of threat or violent act. Investigation is completed. Offence is not punishable with death or imprisonment for life. He is ready to abide by the conditions and face the trial. 3. Investigating Officer has given say at Exh.4. 4. I heard Ld. Counsel on behalf of accused and Ld. APP. 5. As per the facts of this case the victim is 17years old and accused is 20 years old. It is alleged that the accused gave promise to marry the victim and then he took her with him and then there was alleged act of sexual intercourse between them. 6. Ld. Counsel on behalf of accused relied upon decision in case of Sunil Mahadev Patil V/s. State of Maharashtra 2016 ALL MR (Cri) 1712. The court is of the view that the fact in the case of Sunil Mahadev Patil and present case are similar. In this case also there was love affair and accused is promised to marry her. The victim is 17 years old. She is educated. She was learning in 12th standard. She has attained the age of understanding. There was love affair between victim and applicant. So considering these mitigating circumstances --2-- at present the applicant is entitled for bail. His further detention behind bar till final disposal of the case is not required. Therefore, I proceed to pass following order. :ORDER: 1. Application is allowed. 2. The applicant Vivek Ramkiran Yadav shall be released on P.B. and S.B. of Rs.30,000/­(Rupees Thirty Thousand Only) with one or two solvent sureties in like amount. 3. He shall not tamper the prosecution witnesses and victim by any means. 4. He shall attend the concerned police station as and when required for investigation. 5. He shall attend the court for trial. 6. He shall not leave the jurisdiction of the court without prior permission. Thane. ( S.C. Khalipe ) Date :17/04/2018. Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

.. 1 .. bail no.945/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exhibit 1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 945/2015 This application is filed by applicant/accused namely Farukh Chhote Ali Khan for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no.I­62/2015 registered at A.P.M.C. police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 363, 366A, 376(2) of I.P.C. and section 4, 6, 8 and 17 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the co­accused kidnapped the victim girl and then committed rape on her and then gave her in custody of co­accused Kalamuddin and thereafter the present committed rape on the girl in watchman's cabin. It is further contended and argued that the applicant has no concern with the sexual assault on the victim girl and he is falsely implicated in this crime. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/ accused is released on bail, he will co­operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that at the time of incident the complainant had gone down the building to leave her son for school and at that time the accused no.1 induced the victim girl i.e. daughter of the complainant and kidnapped her from the house of the complainant and took her to the room of his friend and committed rape on her there and thereafter he left the said girl at Turbhe Station and it is further contended that thereafter the .. 2 .. bail no.945/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) wanted accused Ashik had taken the girl to accused no.3 Badal at Kamothe Saibaba temple and said Badal had taken her in the watchman's cabin of Bista Corner sector no.19 Kamothe and he committed rape on her in the watchman's cabin and thereafter gave the victim girl in the custody of the present applicant/accused and present applicant also committed sexual assault on the girl in watchman's cabin. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening and pressurizing the victim girl and the prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 363, 366A, 372(2)(I), 506(2), 34 of I.P.C. and section 4, 6, 8 and 17 of P.O.C.S.O. Act'') with the allegation that the applicant/accused and co­accused committed gang rape on the victim girl, as rightly pointed out on behalf of applicant/accused the complaint is against an unknown person and the applicant is not F.I.R. named accused and it is the prosecution case that during investigation it revealed that accused Ravi Gavli induced the victim girl and took her to one Samir, absconding accused, and then she was taken by co­accused Ashik and Ashik handed over the girl to co­accused Badal and then she was given in custody of accused Kalamuddin and the present applicant. Then, it is contended on behalf of applicant/accused that he is falsely involved in this crime merely because he was watchman at the said place where the alleged rape took place. In .. 3 .. bail no.945/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) such circumstance whether the allegations against the accused are true or not, would be the question to be decided on merits. Even nothing is to be recovered from the applicant/accused. 4] Then, it is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. In that regard it is stated that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and he is working as a watchman and will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 5] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions including the condition to furnish heavy surety and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 6] Then, it has also to be mentioned that the investigation in the matter though almost completed the charge­sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. .. 4 .. bail no.945/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) 7] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Farukh Chhote Ali Khan is released on P.R. bond of Rs.20,000/­ [rupees twenty thousand only] with one or two sureties in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ He shall not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and the prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this Court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 08.07.2015 (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.

P.C in C.R.No.I­43/2018 registered in Bhoiwada police station for the offence under section 363, 376, 342, 506 read with 34 of IPC and section 3(A), 4,6,7,8 of POCSO Act. 2. It is contended that the role of this accused is that accused No.1 Ishrat Insari has committed penetrative sexual assault upon victim aged 15.2 years and applicant No.1 Smt. Nilofar Ansari and NO.2 Arshad Ansari being mother and brother of accused No.1 had confined the victim in their house for whole night and on the next day morning they left her at road. --1-- ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN CRIMINAL BAIL APPLICATION NO.900/2018 CNR NO. MHTH01­002610­2018 The applicant Santosh Rangabahadur Singh has applied for bail under section 167(2) of Cr. P.C. in C.R.No.I­ 76/2017 registered in Naya Nagar police station for the offence under section 354(A) of IPC and Section 8 of POCSO Act. 2. It is contended that the offence is punishable with imprisonment which may extent to 5 years and therefore limitation for filing the chargesheet is 60 days. The accused was arrested on 01.02.2018 and produced before this court on the same day. So from that date within 60 days chargesheet is not filed and therefore, he may be released on bail. 3. The report was called by the court from the concerned Registrar of the District Court whether chargesheet is filed or not. The officer has given report that ill 5.15 p.m., of 02.04.2018 no charge­sheet was filed. 4. I heard Ld. Counsel on behalf of accused and Ld. APP. 5. The offence under section 354(A) of IPC is punishable with imprisonment which may extent to 10 years and Section 8 of POCSO Act is punishable with imprisonment which may extent to 5 years, therefore, as per section 167(2)(a) (ii) of Cri.P.C., the limitation for filing the chargesheet is 60 days from the date of first production before Special Court. The accused was arrested on 01.02.2018 and produced before the Special Court on that day. So since that date the 60 days was --2-- completed on 01.04.2018 and on 02.04.2018 the application was filed on 61st day. So considering these aspect no chargesheet is filed on or before 60 days from the date of first production before the court. Hence, the applicant is entitled for bail under section 167(2)(a)(ii) of Cr. P.C. Therefore, I proceed to pass following order. :ORDER: 1. Application is allowed. 2. The applicant Santosh Rangbahadur Singh shall be released on P.B. and S.B. of Rs.15,000/­(Rupees Fifteen Thousand Only) . 3. He shall furnish residence proof, I.D proof and contact numbers of two blood relatives in the court and in the concerned police station. 4. He shall not contact the victim and witnesses and shall not threaten or pressurize them from dissuading them facts of the case. 5. .. 1 .. bail no.958/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 958/2015 This application is filed by applicant Abdul alias Firoz Kadar Shaikh for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no.I­331/2015 registered at Mumbra police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 354(A), 506(2) of I.P.C. and section 7, 8, 11 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant outraged modesty of the complainant victim girl and also showed her obscene video clips. It is further contended and argued that no such incident has happened and the applicant is falsely implicated due to previous enmity. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/ accused is released on bail, he will co­operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that since prior to one month before registration of offence, the accused was sexually harassing the victim by having physical advances with her by moving hand over and pressing her breast and also showing her obscene video clip in mobile phone. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl and the prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. .. 2 .. bail no.958/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 354A(1), 506(2) of I.P.C. and section 7, 8, 11 of P.O.C.S.O. Act with the allegation that he molested the victim girl who is stated to be 8 years old by moving hand over her breast and showing her obscene video clips in mobile phone due to previous enmity, it is contended on behalf of accused that he is falsely implicated in the crime by the complainant i.e. mother of the victim, due to previous enmity. In such circumstance whether the allegations against the accused are true or not, would be the question to be decided on merits. Even nothing is stated to be recovered from the applicant/accused. 4] It is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. 5] In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 6] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility .. 3 .. bail no.958/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 7] Then, it has also to be mentioned that looking the allegations against the accused the investigation in the matter may have almost completed but the charge sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 8] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Abdul alias Firoz Kadar Shaikh is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ The applicant/accused shall attend the concerned police station on every Monday between 10.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon till filing of the charge sheet and shall co­operate in investigation. He shall not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and the prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. .. 4 .. bail no.958/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) He shall not leave India without permission of this Court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 20.05.2015 (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.

1 Bail No.933/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) Criminal Bail Application No.933/2016 Deepak Ganpat Gholap .. Applicant versus The State of Maharashtra Through Bhiwandi Taluka Police Station .. Non­applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 1] By this application the applicants are seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. who was arrested on 11/04/2016 by Bhiwandi Taluka Police Station in connection with C.R.No.I­65/2016 registered for an offence punishable under section 354­D of I.P.C. and section 8 & 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as P.O.C.S.O. Act). 2] Heard learned Advocate Mr. Sunil Lasne for the applicant/accused and learned Spl.P.P. Mrs.R.A.Navale for State. I.O. present with case diary. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 11/04/2016 at the instance of the informant/victim­girl aged about 14 years with an indictment that on 30/03/2016 when she alongwith other girls was proceeding for prayers in the school, at that time accused uttered obscene words which make her ashamed and 2 Bail No.933/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) previously also accused inappropriately touched the victim­girl and other girl students. 4] The learned Counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant/accused is falsely implicated. He submitted that there is delay of 12 days in lodging F.I.R. which is after thought. He submitted that the applicant is head master of the school and he took a strict action against the late comer staff and therefore, some of the staff and other persons were against him and they together conspired and lodged false complaint against the accused. He further submitted that the applicant / accused left the school and tendered his resignation and joined another school and therefore, the apprehension of the A.P.P. is not sustainable. He further submitted that accused is having good character and also received various certificates during his service tenure. The applicant is permanent resident of Thane. The investigation is almost completed. The accused is ready to abide any condition imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing them on bail. 5] Per contra, the learned Spl.P.P. strongly opposed the application on the ground that the offence is serious in respect of minor girl. She further submitted that the applicant is a head master of the school and he did similar act with other girl students also. He further submitted that therefore, resolution 3 Bail No.933/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) was passed in the school and then the report was lodged. She further submitted that the investigation is in progress and there are chances of tampering of witnesses and hampering of the investigation and prayed for rejection of the application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R., it appears that F.I.R, was lodged at the instance of victim­girl aged 14 yrs with an indictment that her head master uttered obscene word and previously also he touched the other girl students inappropriately and caused sexual harassment to them. However, careful perusal of F.I.R. shows that the incident is dated 30/03/2016 and report was lodged on 18/04/2016. The material part of the investigation appears to have been completed. No doubt, the allegations are very serious against head master of the school about causing sexual harassment to the girl students. The offence under section 354­A of I.P.C. is bailable. The object of bail is neither punitive nor preventive but to secure the presence of the accused at the time of trial. No fruitful purpose would be served by further incarceration of accused. He is ready to abide by the conditions imposed by the Court. However, as there are serious allegations, therefore, stringent conditions were required to be imposed on the accused to address the apprehension of learned Spl.P.P. about tampering of prosecution witnesses and fleeing away from justice. Hence, I pass the following order ­ 4 Bail No.933/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) ORDER 1) The application is allowed. 2) Applicant namely Deepak Ganpat Gholap be released on bail on his executing P.R.Bond of ₹15,000/­ [Rupees Fifteen Thousand only] with one solvent surety in the like amount on the following conditions ­ A] Applicant shall attend the concerned police station on every Sunday & Wednesday in between 10.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon till filing of charge­sheet. B] Applicant shall not tamper with prosecution witnesses and shall not pressurize the victim­girl or her family. C] Applicants shall furnish his and his two blood relatives' address proofs and contact numbers and they are duty bound to inform I.O. and Court about the change of address, if any. D] The accused shall maintain the decency hereinafter. E] The applicant shall take note that if he again found involved in similar kind of offence and if the complaint found the ring of truth, then his bail order shall be taken for cancellation. Thane. Date : 20/04/2016. (Ms. U.M. Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act), Thane.

1 Special Case (Pocso) No. 79/2015 Judgment Received on :­ 17.04.2015 Registered on :­ 17.04.2015 Decided on :­ 27.07.2017 Duration :­ 2Y 03M 10D IN THE COURT OF ADDITIONAL SESSIONS JUDGE, & SPECIAL JUDGE (POCSO) ACT, THANE AT : THANE ( Presided over by Ashutosh N.Karmarkar, District Judge­1 & Special Judge (POCSO) Act, Thane ) Special Case (POCSO) No.79/2015 Exh. No. State of Maharashtra ( Through Turbhe M.I.D.C. Police Station ) …Complainant V/s. Ganesh Hanumant Koli Age : 26 Years, Occ. : Service, R/at.: Room No.203, Prabhakar PatilChawl, Pavane gaon, Navi Mumbai … Accused. Offence punishable under Sec. 354­A(1)(i) of Indian Penal Code and under Sec. 7 punishable under S. 8 and under Sec. 9(m) punishable under S. 10 of The Protection of 2 Special Case (Pocso) No. 79/2015 Judgment Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Appearances : Shri. S.D.Londhe, A.P.P. for the State Shri.D.P.Rathod, Advocate for accused JUDGMENT ( Delivered on this 27th day of July, 2017 ) 1] Accused is facing trial for the offence punishable under Sec. 354­A(1)(i) of Indian Penal Code and under Sec. 7 punishable under Sec. 8 and under Sec. 9(m) punishable under Sec. 10 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] Prosecution Case, in brief, is as under : Informant is the mother of the victim. Informant is serving in public relation office of the Corporator. Her office timing is 10.30 a.m. to 6.00 p.m. Her husband is mathadi worker. The timing of job of her husband is 9.30 a.m. to 10.30 p.m. Victim is studying in 5th standard. The timing of her school is 12.30 p.m. to 5.30 p.m. Accused resides adjoining to their house. So, they know him. On 6.12.2014, informant's husband had gone for his job. Victim was at home, since it was holiday on account of “Mahaparinirvan din' of Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar. Informant came from her job at 7.30 p.m.. On seeing her victim started weeping and she hugged informant. On enquiry victim stated that at 6.30 p.m., she came inside the house after fetching water. Since nobody 3 Special Case (Pocso) No. 79/2015 Judgment was in the house, the accused entered into the house and he hugged the victim and also pressed her breast. She resisted the accused. He fell her down. She raised shouts and the accused ran away. Then, she lodged the report to the police. 3] On the basis of report, offence was registered bearing C.R. No. I­290/2014. P.I. Kadam has investigated this crime. He drew spot panchanama. He referred the victim for medical examination. He recorded the statements of witnesses. After completion of investigation, he filed charge­sheet in the Court of law. 4] I have framed charge against accused below Exh. 3 to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. Total denial is the defence of the accused. 5] Prosecution has examined five witnesses. Then, the statement of the accused under Sec. 313 of Cr.P.C. came to be recorded. Total denial is the defence of the accused. After the statement under Sec. 313 of Cr.P.C., prosecution has recalled one witness i.e. Headmistress from Navi Mumbai Vidyalaya so as to prove age of the victim. Additional statement of accused under Sec. 313 of Cr.P.C. came to be recorded. The accused has tried to raise defence in statement under Sec. 313 of Cr.P.C. that the informant used to fetch water from the house of maternal uncle of accused. There was dispute between informant and accused's 4 Special Case (Pocso) No. 79/2015 Judgment maternal uncle on the count of fetching water. The accused used to intervene in the dispute which informant was not liking and so, false complaint is filed. 6] Ld. A.P.P. has submitted that the victim has specifically stated that after fetching water, the victim had taken the pipe inside the house. Accused entered into the house and hold her from backside and fell her down. The evidence of victim shows that there was sexual intent on the part of the accused. There were also marks on the chest of the victim. Medical Certificate also supports the story of victim. Evidence of victim is not shattered. On the other hand, Ld. Advocate for the accused has submitted that there is dispute between the applicant and maternal uncle of the accused and the accused used to take side of his maternal uncle. According to him, two elder members of the family in adjoining house of the informant were present in their house. One of the family members in the family of Mr. Parde and Jagtap were present in their respective houses. But, the independent witnesses are not examined. The distance between two chawls is 4 to 5 ft. He has also submitted that the Headmistress of the School is not the competent witness to prove the age. 7] Following points arose for my determination and I gave my findings thereon for the reasons stated below: 5 Special Case (Pocso) No. 79/2015 Judgment Sr. POINTS FINDINGS No. 1. Does the prosecution prove that the Yes. accused on 6.12.2014, at about 18.30 hrs., at room No.205, Prabhakar Patil chawl, Pavane gaon, Navi Mumbai have sexually harassed minor victim girl, aged 10 years by physical contact and advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures and thereby committed an offence punishable under S. 354 ­A(1)(i) of Indian Penal Code? 2. Does the prosecution prove that Yes. accused on above mentioned date, time and place, committed sexual assault on minor victim girl, age 10 years by pressing her breast with sexual intent which involves physical contact without penetration and thereby committed an offence u/s. 7 punishable u/s. 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act? 3. Does the prosecution prove that the Yes. accused on above mentioned date, time and place committed aggravated sexual assault on a child below 12 years i.e. minor girl, age 10 years and 6 months and thereby committed an offence u/s. 9(m) punishable u/s. 10 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act? 4. What order? As per final order. 6 Special Case (Pocso) No. 79/2015 Judgment REASONS 9] In the present matter, the prosecution has examined informant P.W.1 Archana (Exh. 5), her daughter, i.e. victim P.W.2 (Exh. 7), P.W.3 P.I. Pradeep Kadam, investigation officer (Exh.8) P.W.4 Dr. Yamgar (Exh.12) Subsequently, prosecution has examined P.W.5 Mrs. Minal Phale, Headmistress of Navi Mumbai Vidyalaya (Exh. 17). AS TO POINT NOS. 2 & 3 :­ 10] In order to establish the guilt of accused under Sec. 7 punishable under Sec. 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, the prosecution is required to establish that the accused has touched the parts of the body of victim as contended in Sec. 7 of the Act or does any other act with sexual intent and which involves physical contact without penetration. Provisions of Sec. 9 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act are of aggravated form and one additional ingredient which is required to be proved is that the age of the victim was below 12 years. 11] It is well settled principle of Criminal Law that in order to establish the guilt of the accused, prosecution is required to adduce cogent, convincing and trust­worthy evidence. It is well settled that the sole testimony of the witness is also sufficient to base the conviction. But, the rule is that it should be above suspicion and should inspire confidence in the mind of Court. 7 Special Case (Pocso) No. 79/2015 Judgment 12] The mother of victim has contended in the report (Exh.6) that at the time of incident, the victim was studying in 5 th standard. The informant has also stated in her oral evidence that at the time of incident, the age of victim was 10 ½ years. There might be typing mistake while mentioning the date of birth of the victim in the oral evidence. But, it is to be noted that the accused has not denied in the cross­examination about the fact that the age of the victim was 10 ½ years at the time of incident. It appears that since the victim was child witness, it was initially ascertained whether she is able to ascertain the sanctity of oath. At the time of deposition in January­2017, the victim was studying in 7th standard. So, it can be gathered that at the time of incident, she must be studying in 5th standard and her age might be upto 10 to 11 years. 13] Prosecution has also examined Mr. Minal Phale, who is headmistress in Navi Mumbai School from June­2011. She has also stated that victim was studying in their school from June­2010. Victim had got admission in their school in 1st standard. At the time of admission, her birth extract was filed on which basis entry was taken in the register of the school. This witness has also brought the copy of birth certificate on which her birth date was mentioned as 13.05.2004. She has also proved the Bonafide Certificate which was issued by the school at Exh.19. This Bonafide Certificate also shows that the date of birth of the victim is 13.05.2004. The copy 8 Special Case (Pocso) No. 79/2015 Judgment of birth certificate shows the date of birth of the victim as 13.05.2004. Rather than to shatter the evidence of the witness in the cross­examination, more details are brought on record that this witness has verified that the birth extract is correct. There is only suggestion that the Bonafide Certificate (Exh.19) is false. There is nothing in the cross­examination of this witness to disbelieve her testimony on the point of the birth date of the victim. At the time of evidence this witness had also brought the original register. So, the accused was also having opportunity to cross­examine on the basis of that register. Alleged incident has taken place on 06.12.2014. Medical Certificate of the victim also shows that her age was shown as 10 years. If we consider the date of birth of the victim and the date of the incident, it can be said that on the date of incident, the age of the victim was 10 ½ years. 14] Now, it is to be seen as to whether the prosecution has established the sexual assault on victim. Victim has stated that her father used to go to the job in between 9.00 to 10.00 a.m. and mother used to go to the job at 10.00 a.m. It was holiday on 6.12.2014 and victim was at home. She was alone in the house. She had been to near the tap in front of their house to connect a pipe for fetching water. She came inside the house after fetching water. She took the pipe inside and was rolling the same. Accused entered into the house. He came from backside of the victim and hugged her. She stated that the accused has also caught hold her chest and fell her down. She raised shouts and so accused ran 9 Special Case (Pocso) No. 79/2015 Judgment away. She locked the door from inside. Her mother came at 7.00 p.m. She narrated the incident to her. Then, her mother lodged report. Victim has also stated that there were marks on her chest. She was referred for medical examination. She has also identified the accused. Accused has brought on record in the cross­examination of victim's mother Archana that towards left side of their house, there is residence of one Jagtap family and to its left, there is residence of one Rupa Mogade. It is also brought on record that house of accused is adjoining to the house of said Rupa Mogade. The sketch along with spot panchanama (Exh.9) also shows about the residence of the accused after two to three houses of the informant. So, it appears that the accused is residing near the house of the victim. The victim was cross­examined by the accused at length. Rather than to shatter the evidence of the victim, it seems that some more details are brought on the record in the cross­ examination. It is brought on record in her cross­examination that accused entered into her house in between 6.45 to 7.00 p.m. and immediately after few minutes her mother arrived. 15] It has also brought on record that since there was festival on that day, the persons in the adjoining houses were not at home. It has brought on record in the cross­examination of the victim that Rupa Mogade was in her house. But, no incident was narrated by the victim to her. Considering the age of the victim, 10 Special Case (Pocso) No. 79/2015 Judgment one can not expect that she would immediately disclose the incident to anybody else rather than to disclose to her close relatives. It has also brought on record in the cross­examination that one Vitthal Parde is her maternal uncle and he was also not at home. 16] Investigation officer has stated that it was transpired that Mr. Parde was at home. However, the victim has stated that he resides at long distance. Accused has brought on record in the cross­examination of victim's mother Archana that house of one Narsappa, the relative of the accused was in front of their house and the houses of Shri. Jadhav and Bhatane are towards left and right side of the house of Narsappa respectively. Accused has brought on record in the cross­examination of investigation officer Mr. Kadam that one Shri. Parde was there in the house. Considering the age of the victim, it can not be expected that she will immediately rush to some other person to disclose such type of incident. There is nothing in the cross­examination of victim to disbelieve her testimony. On the contrary, the suggestion is given to the victim by the accused that at the time of incident the children were playing outside her house. This suggestion is denied. But, this suggestion itself shows that the accused had admitted presence of victim at her house. More details are brought on record that accused entered into victim's house in between 6.45 to 7.00 p.m. She raised shouts for twice as “help”. This suggestion itself supports 11 Special Case (Pocso) No. 79/2015 Judgment the contention of the victim about entry in the house of accused. 17] P.W.1 Archana, the mother of victim has stated that she came to home at about 7.00 p.m. It was closed from inside. She knocked the door. Her daughter opened the door. On enquiry why the door was closed, victim started weeping and hugged her. On enquiry victim stated to her mother about the entry of the accused in their house. She has further stated that after fetching water, victim has brought water pipe inside the house. The accused came from backside and hugged her. She caught hold her chest and fell her down. She raised cries and so, accused ran away. P.W. 1 Archana has also stated that she has noticed finger impressions on the chest of the victim. She called her husband and then approached the police station to lodge report (Exh.6) It has brought on record in the cross­examination that two aged members from Kharikwale family who resides towards right side of the house of victim were present in their house. Accused has brought on record in the cross­examination of P.W. Archana that there is one Jagtap family to the left side of the victim's house and about presence of one of their family member in their house. Accused has also brought on record in the cross­ examination of investigation officer that it was transpired that no member from the family of Mr.Jagtap were present at the relevant time. It has also brought on record that a child from the house of Renuka Bhatade was present in their house. Sketch along with spot panchanama shows that the house of said Renuka Bhatade is at 12 Special Case (Pocso) No. 79/2015 Judgment some longer distance. So, Ld. Advocate for the accused has tried to submit that none of the persons from adjoining houses are examined. But, it is already brought on record that none of the member from the adjoining houses of victim were present. Only two elder members from Kharikwale family and one small child in the house of Renuka Bhatade were present in their houses. 18] It is well settled that in every case, it is not required to have a corroboration from independent witness, when particularly the victim has no reason to depose against the accused. It is not brought on record that the victim's family is having personal grudge against the accused. It has brought on record in the cross­ examination of Archana that there is house of one Narsappa Koli in front of the house of informant and he is relative of the accused. It has also brought on record that the informant had quarrel earlier with said Narsappa. 19] Accused has tried to raise defence in the statement under Sec. 313 Cr.P.C. that the informant used to fetch water from the house of Narsappa and there was dispute between these two families on the count of fetching water in which accused used to intervene. It is also the defence that since the informant was not liking the same, false case is filed. It is to be noted that the informant has specifically denied the suggestion about fetching of water from the house of Narsappa. There is no suggestion that the accused used to intervene 13 Special Case (Pocso) No. 79/2015 Judgment in the alleged dispute between informant and Narsappa. Therefore, it would be difficult to accept that the defence is probable. Even if it is accepted that there was dispute with Narsappa, who is relative of the accused, there is no reason for the informant to depose against the accused who is having separate residence. Thus, the discussion above lead me to say that the evidence of victim gets corroboration from the evidence of her mother that the accused entered into the house of the victim when she was alone and has hugged the victim and then pressed her breast. 20] Both informant and the victim have consistently stated about the marks on the chest of the victim at the time of incident. Evidence of P.W. 4 Dr. Yamgar is that he knows Dr. Prerana Thakur as both were serving in one department since last five years. He can identify signature and hand writing of Dr. Smt. Thakur. Since the said concerned Dr. Thakur was on long maternity leave, this witness Dr. Yamgar is examined. He has stated that Dr. Thakur examined the victim and stated that victim had redness on breast. He has stated that Certificate (Exh.13) shows that the victim was examined at 11.30 p.m. and alleged incident was on the same day evening. It is mentioned in the certificate that the said injuries to the victim were within 12 hours and are simple in nature. There is nothing in the cross­examination of this witness Dr. Yamgar to disbelieve his testimony. It is to be noted that the medical evidence also supports the story of victim. 14 Special Case (Pocso) No. 79/2015 Judgment 21] Ld. Advocate for the accused has attempted to submit that no independent witness is examined. But, it is to be noted that accused could not bring on record that there was any dispute personally with the accused and that there was any reason for the victim to depose against the accused. On the contrary, it is well settled that sole testimony of the witness is also sufficient to base conviction, if it should inspires confidence in the mind of court. 22] It is but natural on the part of the victim to disclose about the incident to her mother. So, the evidence of victim appears to be natural. Evidence of victim gets corroboration from the evidence of her mother and also the medical evidence. The act of the accused to enter in the house of victim when she was alone and to hug her and to hold her breast i.e. to touch the breast of victim itself shows that said act was committed with sexual intent. Even he went ahead and fell the victim down. Since victim raised shouts, the accused ran away. So, the discussion above lead me to say that the prosecution has established the ingredients of Sec. 7 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. Prosecution has also examined the Headmistress of the school and through that witness, it is also established that the age of the victim was below 12 years at the time of incident. So, it can be said that the ingredients of Sec. 9 are also proved. So, I answer point Nos.2 and 3 in the affirmative. 15 Special Case (Pocso) No. 79/2015 Judgment AS TO POINT NO.1 :­ 23] In order to establish the guilt of accused under Sec. 354­A(1)(i) of Indian Penal code, the prosecution has to establish that the accused has committed the act of physical contact and advances involving unwelcome sexual overtures. Victim has specifically stated that on 6.12.2014, she was alone at home due to holiday. She has fetched the water. She has taken the water pipe inside the house and was rolling the same. At the same time, accused entered into the house. He came from backside and hugged her and then pressed her chest. Victim has also stated that the accused fell her down. She raised shouts and so, accused ran away. 24] It is already discussed in the foregoing paragraphs that the evidence of the victim gets support from the evidence of her mother. There is absolutely nothing in the cross­examination of both these witnesses to discard their testimony. On the contrary, more details are brought on record. Medical evidence on record also supports the prosecution story. So, the act of the accused of entering in the house of victim when she was alone and to press her breast and then to fell her down and that too without her consent itself shows that there was physical contact with advances involving unwelcome sexual overtures. Thus, the discussion above lead me to say that the prosecution has established the guilt of accused under Sec. 354­A(1)(i) of Indian Penal code. 25] Since the accused is held guilty of the offence 16 Special Case (Pocso) No. 79/2015 Judgment punishable under Sec. 354­A(1)(i) and of the offence under Sec. 7 punishable under S. 8 and under Sec. 9(m) punishable under Sec. 10 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act,accused is to be heard on the point of sentence. 26] I have heard accused personally and also his advocate Mr. Rathod and also Ld. A.P.P. Shri. Londhe for the State. Accused has submitted for lenient view since he is the only earning member of the family. His mother who is widow and his wife are dependent on him. According to him, his son of 7 months expired in the last month. Ld. Advocate Mr. Rathod for the accused has submitted that the accused is financially poor and lenient view may be taken considering all these facts. Ld. A.P.P. Shri. Londhe has submitted that in case of leniency, wrong message will go to the society and he has submitted for maximum punishment. 27] Punishment prescribed for the offence under Sec. 354­ A(1)(i) is punishment for a term which may extend to three years or with fine or with both. 28] The punishment prescribed for the offence under Sec. 7 punishable under Sec. 8 is imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than three years but, which may extend to five years and shall also be liable to fine. The punishment 17 Special Case (Pocso) No. 79/2015 Judgment prescribed under Sec. 10 for the offence described under Sec. 9 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, is imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than five years but, which may extend to seven years and shall also be liable to fine. 29] It appears that the offence under Sec. 9(m) punishable under Sec. 10 is in aggravated form of the offence under Sec. 7 punishable under Sec. 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. The ingredients of both the offences under Secs. 7 and 9(m) are almost same. One additional ingredient for the offence under Sec. 9(m) is that age of victim was below 12 years. In this matter, victim's age was 10 ½ years at the time of incident. In view of Sec. 42 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, accused is to be punished under Sec. 10 which is greater in degree along with punishment for the offence under Sec. 354­A(1)(i) of Indian Penal Code. Considering the offence against the women, I am not inclined to grant benefit of the provisions of Probation of Offenders Act. Ld. Advocate for accused has submitted for lenient view. But, the accused must realise the consequences of such type of offence. Therefore, in my opinion, the following order will meet the ends of justice. Hence, the order : 18 Special Case (Pocso) No. 79/2015 Judgment ORDER 1] Accused Ganesh Hanumant Koli is convicted under Section 235(2) of Code of Criminal Procedure of the offence under Sec. 7 punishable under Sec. 8 and of the offence under Sec. 9(m) punishable under Sec. 10 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] Accused is sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for five years and to pay fine of Rs. 1,000/­ i.d. to suffer simple imprisonment for six months. 3] No separate sentence is awarded for the offence under Sec.7 punishable under Sec. 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 in view of provisions of Sec. 42 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 4] Accused Ganesh Hanumant Koli is also convicted under Sec. 235(2) of Code of Criminal Procedure of the offence punishable under Sec. 354­A(1)(i) of Indian Penal Code. 5] He is sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for three months and to pay fine of Rs. 500/­ I.d. to suffer simple imprisonment for 15 days. 19 Special Case (Pocso) No. 79/2015 Judgment 6] Both sentences to run concurrently. 7] Bail bonds of the accused stand cancelled. 8] Accused is entitled for set off, if any, as per provisions of Sec. 428 of Code of Criminal Procedure. 9] Dictated and pronounced in open Court. Thane, ( Ashutosh N. Karmarkar ) Date : 27.07.2017 District Judge­1 & Special Judge (POCSO) Act,Thane

Case(POCSO) No. 81/2015... Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­002652­2015 Offences Act, 2012. After due investigation charge­sheet came to be filed in the court of Sessions. 3. My Ld. Predecessor had framed charge (Exh.11) against both the accused for the offences punishable under sections 143, 147, 149, 323, 354 of Indian Penal Code and Sec. 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and in alternative charge is framed u/s. 354, 323 of IPC and Sec. 8 of POCSO Act. In the alternative :­ In the negative. Does the prosecution prove that on same date, time and place accused alongwith absconding accused Renu and two unknown women used criminal force to complainant, a minor age­17 years intending to outrage her modesty and thereby committed an offence punishable u/s.354 of IPC? 5. Does the prosecution prove that on In the negative. same date, time and place accused alongwith absconding accused Renu and two unknown women voluntarily caused hurt to complainant, a minor age­17 years and prosecution witness and thereby committed an offence punishable u/s.323 of IPC? 6. Does the prosecution prove that on In the negative. same date, time and place accused alongwith absconding accused Renu and two unknown women, committed sexual assault on complainant Kum. Rubina Jainul Shaikh, a minor age­17 years and thereby committed an offence punishable under Sec. 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual offences Act ? 6 Spl. Case(POCSO) No. 81/2015... Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­002652­2015 7. What Order ? As per final order. REASONS AS TO POINT NOS. 1 to 7 :­ 7. That, in order to establish the guilt of accused, prosecution has examined in all three witnesses. P.W.1 Deepak Rajesh Gupta­ examined at Exh.27 – who is panch witness P.W.2 Mangala Mukund Mankar – Exh. 31­ who is independent witness. P.W.3 Gangadhar Ghavte – Exh. 32­ Investigating officer. Ld. P.W.1 is panch witness on spot panchanama. He has not supported to the prosecution story. He deposed in his examination­ in­chief that on 29.01.2015, police called him at Yuvraj Medical Store. One lady and police were present there. The lady told that somebody caught hold her from her backside in front of Yuvraj Medical Stores. She shown the spot of incident. He further deposed that he does not know the complainant Rubina Shaikh. P.W.1 admitted his signature on spot panchanama. 10. P.W.2 Mangala Mankar who is independent witness also turned hostile. She has not supported to the prosecution version. In the cross­examination held by Ld. A.P.P. she stated that she had not stated in her statement whatever mentioned in her statement. P.W.1 and P.W.2 have not supported the prosecution version. Therefore, their evidence is not acceptable. 11. So far as offence of investigating officer is concerned, he deposed in his evidence that in the year 2015, he was attached to Kalwa police station as A.P.I. He had registered offence bearing C.R. No.I­39/2015. Victim was 11 years old. Her name was Rubina. She lodged complaint. Accordingly, F.I.R. was registered and then he investigated the matter, prepared spot panchanama in presence of panchas. Spot of incident is situated near New Shivajinagar, Kalwa. He recorded statement of witnesses. During investigation, it was transpired that victim is aged about 17 years. Then, charge­sheet is filed against the accused under the provisions of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 12. Investigating officer further deposed that he had recorded statement of P.W.2 Mangala Mankar as per her say. In the 8 Spl. Case(POCSO) No. 81/2015... .. 1 .. bail no.966/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 966/2015 This application is filed by applicant Vishnu Suresh Patil for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. I­203/2015 registered at Vartaknagar police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 354, 509 of I.P.C. and section 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in ''P.O.C.S.O. Act''). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant/accused committed sexual harassment upon the victim girl by following her on motorcycle when she used to go of house and by whistling at her with intent to outrage her modesty. It is further contended and argued that no such incident as alleged has happened. It is further contended and argued that earlier also same complainant had filed complaint with same allegations and since the offences charged at that time were bailable the applicant was remanded to Magisterial custody on the same day and was released on bail and therefore with intention to send the accused to jail, this complaint with the allegation under P.O.C.S.O. Act is filed and the applicant is falsely implicated in this crime with mala fide intention. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co­operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. .. 2 .. bail no.966/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that the accused and complainant girl are knowing each other since they reside in same locality and the accused was in habit of following the complainant girl with intent to outrage her modesty. It is further contended that at the time of incident in question the accused was following her on motorcycle and was blowing whistle at her and thereby he committed sexual harassment upon. It is further contended and argued that at that time the accused also expressed that the father of the complainant is expired and now there is nobody to send him to jail. It is further contended and argued that since the accused and the victim are residing in same locality, if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl and other witnesses and may tamper with prosecution evidence and even he may abscond and may not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 354D, 509 of I.P.C. and section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act with the allegation of molesting victim girl who is stated to be 17 years old, it is contended and argued on behalf of applicant/accused that he is innocent and has not committed any crime and he is falsely implicated in this crime with mala fide intention and it was also contended and argued that earlier also same complainant had filed complaint with same allegations and since the offences charged at that time were bailable the applicant was remanded to Magisterial .. 3 .. bail no.966/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) custody on the same day and was released on bail on next day and the complainant's purpose of putting the applicant in jail did not serve and therefore fresh complaint with the allegations by twisted version attracting section 509 of I.P.C. and section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act etc. was lodged. Even the submission on behalf of prosecution that the applicant/accused indulged in similar activity earlier also and therefore he is not entitled to be released on bail etc. cannot be said to be appealing and convincing at this stage for the reason that as per contentions of the applicant he is falsely implicated in the crime and since he was immediately released on bail this fresh complaint is filed. In such circumstance the the truthfulness or otherwise of the allegations levelled against the applicant/accused would have to be decided on merits after trial. 4] Then, it is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and he will abide by any conditions imposed. 5] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by .. 4 .. bail no.966/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 6] Then, it has also to be mentioned that though the investigation in the matter is stated to have been almost completed, it will take time to complete the investigation and then to submit the charge­sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 7] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Vishnu Suresh Patil is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ He shall not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and the prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this Court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 07.05.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.

P.C. in C.R.No.I­150/2018 registered in Narpoli police station for the offence under Sections 354, 323, 504, 506 of Indian Penal Code and under Secs. 8 and 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2. It is contended that applicant is falsely implicated. There are marriage petition and civil disputes going on between informant and this applicant and therefore false FIR has been registered. Investigation is completed. Therefore, applicant prayed for bail. 3. Investigating Officer has given his say at Exh.03. 4. I heard the Ld. Counsel Shri. S. S. Bhoir for the applicant and Ld. A.P.P. on behalf of the State. 5. As per the facts of this case the victim is 10 years old. The informant had brought the victim from Nepal. The victim is sister's daughter of the informant. The informant had kept the victim in the house of accused for maintenance. On 10.03.2018 the victim told the informant that accused are beating, harassing and ill­treating her and the present accused is sexually assaulting her by putting his arm on her thighs, touching her breast and showing pornography. The accused had also touched her from --2-- behind when she was sitting on vehicle. It is submitted by the I.O. that the accused has applied for bail within 08 days of his arrest. Further investigation is yet to be going on. Statement of victim under section 164 of Cr.P.C. is remained to be taken. The investigation is not completed. If the accused released on bail, he is likely to tamper the investigation and tamper the victim, and informant. 6. The court is of the view that it is very serious offence in respect of the minor girl of 10 years old. Investigation is not completed. The statement of the victim is yet to the recorded. So, if the applicant/accused is released on bail he is likely to tamper prosecution witnesses and victim and it will hamper the investigation. Therefore, accused is not entitled for the bail. Hence, I pass the following order :­ :ORDER: Application for bail is rejected. Thane. ( S.C. Khalipe ) Date : 18.04.2018. Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.
