Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­002722­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 91/14 Received on : 26.04.2014 Registered on : 26.04.2014 Decided on : 21.08.2018 Duration : 3Ys. 1M. 27 Ds. IN THE COURT OF D.J.­1 & ADDL. SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE. (Presided over by Hemant M. Patwardhan) Special Case (POCSO) No. 91/14 Exh.No. State of Maharashtra, (Mira Road Police station) ..Complainant V/s. Nasir Najir Shaikh. Age : 28 years, R/at. Room No.201, Mira Mahal building, Poojanagar, Near Irani Bakery, Mira Road, Dist. Thane ..Accused Appearance:­ APP Mr. Londhe for the State. Advocate Mr. Brigenza for accused JUDGMENT (Delivered on this 21st day of August 2018) Accused Nasir Najir Shaikh was facing trial under sections 376(2)(i), 506 of Indian Penal Code read with Sec. 4, 6, 8, 1 OF 18 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­002722­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 91/14 and 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 on following facts. 1] That a year prior to 17.01.2015 accused in the residential house of victim­girl at room no. 202, Haji Yusuf Manzil, Poojanagar, Irani Bakery, Mira Road, District Thane has committed rape on victim and during that period has also committed penetrative sexual assaults with sexual intents and after having committed said assaults has threatened her with direct consequences. As victim was minor at the relevant time, on complaint lodged by aunt of victim, an offence punishable under aforesaid sections came to be registered. On completion of investigation he was charge­sheeted. 2] My learned Predecessor has framed charge below Exh.13 and has certified that the contents of said charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. Accused pleaded not guilty and claim to be tried. His defence was of total denial and that he has been falsely implicated in the matter as mother and aunt of the victim do not wish to share insurance claim amount with the accused person. Hence, trial was commenced. 3] Prosecution has then proceeded to examine Mrs. Parveen Khan, victim, panch witness Gulam Patel, I.O. Sneha Mhetar etc. as PW 1 to 4 respectively. After their depositions, statement of accused was recorded as per his say wherein he has categorically reiterated 2 OF 18 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­002722­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 91/14 his defence that he is in custody since last 41/2 years without committing any such offence and had never thought of implication in such false case on the ground of insurance policy claim. 4] Arguments of rival advocates were heard. Learned P.P. has categorically pointed out that complainant has narrated that she has received information from the victim herself and on the basis of said information she had lodged the complaint. Victim has then categorically deposed as to how accused used to commit sexual assaults with her and as to how she was threatened by the accused after commission of assault. She has then narrated that previously since about a year accused had committed penetrative sexual assault and has then on 17.01.2014 has actually committed rape on her. Hence, she had informed her aunt about incident dated 27.01.2014 and on her message further prosecution was launched. Witness no.3, a panch witness has also supported prosecution and has narrated as to how he has helped police machinery to conduct spot panchanama. I.O. has deposed as to how she has conducted investigation to come to the conclusion that offence has been committed by the accused. On the basis of the said facts learned P.P. has requested to convict the accused as per the provisions of law. 5] Per contra, defence has categorically pointed out that victim has made very vague allegations against said heinous act without making any reference of any specific date, time and place of 3 OF 18 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­002722­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 91/14 the assault. He has then pointed out that if the last incident was occurred on 17.01.2014 then why the complaint was lodged after about 10 days of said incident. He has also pointed out that investigation has not been properly carried out in the matter wherein even the investigating officer has not seized the mobile phones which were allegedly source of information of particular heinous act of accused. According to submissions investigating officer has carried out investigation in very casual manner and has implicated accused on say of aunt of the victim. According to his submissions entire concocted story was then put forth to avoid payment of share in the insurance claim which according to him, as per their personal laws, accused was entitled to get. According to submissions the victim was residing in the house of the accused with grandmother and father since long and the mother of the victim during lifetime of father of victim had separated from him and got married with another person and has also given birth to baby boy during the lifetime of father of the victim. According to submissions as she has renounced rights by getting married with another person she was not entitled to claim any insurance claim after the death of victim's father. Therefore, in order to get her share in said claim she has implicated accused in the matter with an intention to pressurize the family to get share in the claim. He has placed his reliance on Judgment in Criminal Appeal No. 606/2017 in case of Mohan Ambadas Meshram V/s. State of 4 OF 18 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­002722­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 91/14 Maharashtra through Police Station, Chandrapur to substantiate the arguments. He has then pointed out that medical evidence is totally against the victim and thus, has requested the court to acquit the accused from all charges. He has then preferred to file his written notes of arguments to again reiterated the said submissions. 6] On the basis of aforesaid rival arguments, following points arise for my consideration and I record my findings against each of them for the reasons noted below:­ S.N. Points Findings 1] Does the prosecution prove that accused since year 2013 till ..In the negative. 17.01.2014 in the residential house of victim­girl at room no. 202, Haji Yusuf Manzil, Poojanagar, Irani Bakery, Mira Road, Dist. Thane committed rape on minor victim­girl by doing forcible sexual intercourse with her and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 376(2)(i) of IPC? 2] Does the prosecution prove that accused during given period and at ..In the negative. same place during sexual assault on the said minor victim­girl, he was threatening her for not disclosing about the said act to anybody and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 506 of IPC? 3] Does the prosecution prove that accused during given period and at ..In the negative. same place committed penetrative sexual assault on said minor girl in above mentioned manner and also by inserting penis in her mouth more than once and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 4 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act? 4] Does the prosecution prove that accused during given period and at ..In the negative. same place repeatedly committed penetrative sexual assault on said minor girl in above mentioned manner and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act? 5] Does the prosecution prove that accused during given period and at ..In the negative. same place committed sexual assault on said minor girl by touching her chest and private part more than once with sexual intent and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act? 5 OF 18 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­002722­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 91/14 6] Does the prosecution prove that accused during given period and at ..In the negative. same place committed sexual harassment upon said minor girl by exhibiting his penis to her repeatedly with sexual intent and also by forcing her to handle his penis with sexual intent and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act? 7] What order ? Accused is acquitted as per final order. REASONS As to point nos. 1 to 7 :­ 7] All these points are interlinked with each other and are considered at once. In the instant case very serious allegations are made against accused of having committed rape on his own niece and having committed penetrative sexual assault on number of occasions. Defence has denied all said allegations and in order to disprove said allegations has even put forth the categorical defence of his false implication in order to avoid payment of insurance claim to him. Therefore, all said depositions of the witnesses are require to be scrutinized very minutely. In the instant case entire criminal law was set in motion on one message which was allegedly forwarded by the victim to the complainant which reads that "Chacha has raped her". On said message, aunt of the victim had approached police station for lodging the complaint and once complaint was lodged further action was initiated by investigating officer. On completion of investigation when investigating officer has come to conclusion that investigation reveals the offence, accused was charge­sheeted. 6 OF 18 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­002722­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 91/14 After framing the charge as the accused has claim to be tried trial was commenced and aforesaid four witnesses were examined. 8] No doubt, the complainant and victim have categorically stated as to how the accused has committed heinous act of rape and as to how the penetrative sexual assaults were committed by the accused. On perusal of said allegations the wording used by said witnesses is considered as it is then are certainly sufficient to say that those allegations fulfills necessary ingredients of the act viz. 'rape' 'penetrative sexual assaults' etc. as defined under section 375 of IPC read with section 3,5,7 and 9 of POCSO Act. Therefore, said allegations are require to be tested on the defence of accused. In the instant case the accused has put forth the defence of false implication and implication on the ground to avoid share of insurance claim between them. On plain perusal of the facts it is apparent that accused is uncle of victim and brother of the accused along with victim were residing with him since many years and after the accident victim's father was bed ridden for about a year and all his treatment was by accused and his family members. During the lifetime of father of the victim, she did not make any complaint either to her mother, grandmother, grandfather or even to the aunt. However, only after the death of her father she appears to have made such grievance. She has set law in motion after alleged incident dated 17.01.2014 and while lodging the complaint has then stated 7 OF 18 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­002722­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 91/14 that said act of commission of penetrative sexual assault was continued since last one year of the allegation. Thane (Hemant M.Patwardhan) Date: 20.08.2018 D.J.­1 & Additional Sessions Judge, Thane. 9] On the basis of said allegation learned P.P. has requested to raise presumption under section 29 and 30 of POCSO Act and on that basis has further requested to convict the accused. However, in order to raise presumption under section 29 or 30 of the Act, prosecution was initially required to establish allegations prima­facie by convincing evidence. In the instant case during cross­examination complainant, victim as well as investigating officer has admitted various facts which are initially sufficient to conclude that there is really convincing evidence adduced to raise presumption under section 29 and 30 of POCSO Act. If said admissions are considered then the complainant has admitted that whatever message she has received from the victim on the basis of which criminal law was set in motion was itself deleted. It was the case of the accused that in order to implicate the accused in this matter complainant herself has forwarded that message to the victim and then has directed to re­forward it to her to 8 OF 18 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­002722­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 91/14 lodge the complaint. Though it was denied by the complainant or victim, it was the duty of investigating officer to properly investigate the case from that angle. However, as per admissions of investigating officer as well she has not even obtained CDR of the mobile used in the crime since the date of allegation and has even failed to seize those two mobiles to obtain chemical analyzer's report about exchange of SMS between complainant and the victim. Hence, it is apparent lacuna in the prosecution which is apparently fatal to the prosecution as in absence of any specific record of said two mobiles it is difficult to accept that prosecution's allegations are trustworthy. Said allegations would have been corroborated if the investigating officer would have really seized those two mobiles and would have obtained history of exchange of messages as well as calls between the complainant and the victim. However, in absence of even seizure of the said mobiles it is difficult to accept that chain has been properly explained in the crime. 10] As a matter of fact particular message on the basis of which prosecution was launched was material evidence so far as allegations of prosecution are concerned. However, if we consider that said messages itself has been deleted then very material evidence is apparently disappeared. Therefore, in absence of the said message it cannot be said accepted that the said message was really forwarded by the victim to the complainant without there being any intervention of complainant. The fact that complainant would have 9 OF 18 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­002722­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 91/14 been acted with an intention to implicate the accused in the matter gets substantiated by the admission of the investigating officer that on the basis of CDR it is apparent that there were exchange of three messages on the particular day between the complainant and the victim. Neither the victim nor the complainant has explained as to why other two messages were exchanged between them is itself sufficient to create doubt about allegation and sufficient to substantiate the defence. Having regards to said facts said lacuna also is apparently fatal to the prosecution. 11] The victim has alleged that accused has indulged in activities of penetrative sexual assaults or even commission of rape in absence of her grandmother and other uncle. She has categorically made a statement that accused used to indulge in such activities whenever her grandmother has gone out of the house and her other uncle on his duty. Admittedly, the victim has neither referred any specific time of accused indulging in such acts in her statement under section 164 of Cr.P.C. nor even in deposition before this court. Therefore, such vague allegations are required corroboration in its proper sense. However, said alleged act is apparently untrustworthy in view of admission of the victim that accused used to leave house for attending his work around 9.00 a.m. and used to return by 9.00 p.m. If that was the position then admittedly throughout the day accused remains out of the house and therefore, his indulging in such heinous activities can hardly be digested. As per the victim, accused 10 OF 18 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­002722­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 91/14 used to indulge in such activities when nobody was at home. However, it is not her case that after 9.00 p.m. all family members residing with the victim used to leave house for one or the other reason regularly. Thus, in absence of any such allegation it is difficult to accept that accused had really got such time where all family members are out of his house to indulge in such heinous act. 12] On further appraisal of deposition of the victim it is apparent that nobody has restrained her from visiting either her friends or to her aunt i.e. complainant as per own will. As a matter of fact she has admitted that on every week end she used to visit her aunt's house and had also out of station with the aunt for about three days. She has admitted that her character and conduct during academic year concern was very good. Therefore, if the said admissions are considered then it is hard to digest that victim did not inform the complainant during her term of year. According to her allegations she was subjected to such assault since about a year prior to reported incident and in absence of any such specific explanation as to what made her to disclose it on 27.01.2014 said entire conduct gets suspicious. Therefore, defence on the background of these facts appears to be more probable. Any minor who is subjected to such heinous act throughout a year will certainly behave differently during daily activities most probably. Said involvement will certainly also affect curricular activities of the minor. However, when it is admitted that her conduct, character etc. was absolutely normal and 11 OF 18 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­002722­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 91/14 good during her daily curricular activities then again it is difficult to say that she was really facing such assaults. 13] The basic principle of every law is “law is not devoid of common sense” and “law does not ignore natural conduct of human being”. If on the basis of these basic principles the conduct of the victim is tested then it is really difficult to say that she was really subjected to such penetrative sexual assaults throughout a year. No doubt there cannot be any straight jacket formula for conduct of particular person while reacting particular incident. However, while considering the natural conduct of a normal human being such repeated acts will certainly make impact on day to day activities and in absence the said fact has to be discarded. 14] Victim's statement was recorded before Judicial Magistrate, first class after she was referred to said Judicial Magistrate for recording her statement under section 164 of Cr.P.C. Undoubtedly, her statement was categorically recorded by Judicial Magistrate, first class, Thane wherein in paragraph no.3 of her statement she has made specific allegations about act of the accused prior to main incident dated 17.01.2014 and along with incident dated 17.01.2014. However, while deposing before this court she has made altogether different allegations and has made contradictory statements about actual act of the accused. If we consider statement under section 164 of Cr.P.C. then it is apparent that whatever 12 OF 18 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­002722­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 91/14 admissions are being made by the accused to commit said sexual assaults has been negated by the victim and she has categorically refused to obey accused's direction at the relevant time. Then she has made reference of incident dated 17.01.2014 when according to her accused has inserted penis in her vagina for committing rape. During her said statement she has referred about incident being witnessed by her grandmother and aunt on two occasions. So also she has also made reference about criminal intimidation committed by accused and about threatening the victim with dire consequences. However, such allegations of threatening is hardly referred in message to complainant. Further, if the message allegedly forwarded by the victim to the complainant is perused as it is then the wording of the particular message is sufficient to inferred that it denotes to single incident only. Therefore, such contradictory statements are sufficient to make impact on evidential value of her statement and said makes the statement unreliable. 15] If the allegations were made that grandmother and aunt of the victim has already noticed the incident on two occasions then it is but natural that grandmother or aunt of the victim would not have spare the accused for such heinous act. However, merely making reference of incidents being witnessed by them twice there is no reference about their reaction either in statement before Magistrate or even her substantive evidence before the court. Thus, in absence of such consistency her allegations become unreliable. 13 OF 18 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­002722­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 91/14 Having regards to the aforesaid facts it is difficult to accept or say that evidence brought before this court is really convincing to raise presumption under section 29 and 30 of POCSO Act. Even if we consider the allegations on said presumptions then at the most onus will be shifted on the accused to disprove said presumption. In order to disprove the said presumption, accused has then put forth defence as above. By placing reliance on Judgment in Mohan Ambadas Meshram V/s. State of Maharashtra through Police Station, Chandrapur in Criminal Appeal No. 606/2017, defence has then submitted that when the evidence before the court is not convincing in any sense and if medical report is favouring the accused any punishment against accused is not tenable. In the instant case if we consider the defence of the accused that in order to avoid payment of share in insurance claim and in order to pressurize the family of the accused for giving up said claim he has been falsely implicated. If we consider aforesaid conduct of the victim, lacunas in the investigation by PW4 and various admissions of the complainant, victim and the investigating officer then said are certainly sufficient to upheld the said defence of the accused. 16] Above all, an important aspect which favour the accused is medical report before the court. On perusal of report of medical examination of the victim it is apparent that medical officer conducting clinical examination of the victim did not find any injuries either on the other parts of the body or on the private parts 14 OF 18 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­002722­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 91/14 of the victim. Even hymen was found to be intact by the concern medical officer. Though said medical officer has then reserves his final opinion till the receipt of forensic laboratory's report it is apparent that no such report was ever produced before said medical officer or even before this court as well to finally concluded that possibility of sexual assault cannot be ruled out. If allegations are in respect of commission of constant penetrative sexual assault with rape then it is bound to be witnessed or notice by the medical officer during clinical examination of the victim. No doubt hymen can sustain injuries or it can be torn due to various reasons but one of the main reason behind it, is sexual intercourse or assault. However, when it remains intact even after allegations of having undergone such penetrative sexual assault for number of occasions during the year and lastly on 17.01.2014 then its remaining intact will be next to impossible. However, in view of the aforesaid medical report it is apparently favouring the accused and against the victim. Hon'ble their Lordship in the above referred case on the same point has acquitted the accused. Hence, by the said medical evidence the defence of the accused gets corroborated and is certainly sufficient to disprove the presumption both under section 29 and 30 of POCSO Act. Once material is brought before the court which on the basis of preponderance of probabilities is sufficient to discard the allegations then court has to accept it and has to discard the allegations. 17] In the instant case lastly if we consider that alleged 15 OF 18 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­002722­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 91/14 last incident was of dated 17.01.2014 wherein disclosure was made about such heinous act on 27.01.2014 that too before the aunt of victim. Even after having received the information about the heinous act on 27.01.2014 the complainant did not approach the concern police immediately on the same day but had approached concern police on 28.01.2014. Needless to mention that there is no explanation either by the victim or by the complainant as to why such delay is caused in lodging the complaint or disclosing said fact. Even assuming that victim was threatened by the accused person since the beginning then explanation was certainly expected from her as to what makes her to collect the dare to disclose said fact suddenly on 27.01.2014 to her aunt. In absence of any such explanation it is difficult to say that allegations are really trustworthy on the basis of actual occurred incident. So is the case about complainant­aunt. Admittedly there is no case of the complainant that she was under threats of anybody for not approaching concern police immediately on receipt of information. However, she did not even disclose the reason for lodging the complaint on next day on receipt of information. In absence of any such explanation on her part as well her allegations are sufficient to be viewed with suspect. In the said situation thus, the defence gets substantiated and once such defence is accepted prosecution's case has to be discarded. Having regards to all these facts in my opinion prosecution has failed to establish the case by cogent, consistent and reliable evidence. Whatever evidence is brought before this court is absolutely not convincing either to 16 OF 18 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­002722­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 91/14 raise presumption or to punish the accused as prayed. I therefore, do not hesitate to record my findings against point no.1 to 6 in the negative and proceed to pass following order. ORDER 1. Accused Nasir Najir Shaikh is acquitted from the offence punishable under Sec. 376(2)(i), 506 of Indian Penal Code read with Sec. 4, 6, 8, and 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2. He is in jail since the date of his arrest. He be set at liberty forthwith if not required in any other case. 3. Inform jailer immediately accordingly about his release. Jailer is directed to report compliance of the order within the period of three days from the receipt of this order. 4. Muddemal property being worthless, be destroyed after appeal period. 17 OF 18 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­002722­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 91/14 5. Accused is directed to execute P.R. and S.B. of Rs.10,000/­ with a solvent surety in like amount under amended provisions of Section 437­A of Code of Criminal Procedure and the bond so executed shall remain in force for period of six months from the date of its execution. 6. Proceeding accordingly shall stand closed. Thane (Hemant M.Patwardhan) Date: 21.08.2018 D.J.­1 & Additional Sessions Judge, Thane. 18 OF 18

.. 1 .. bail no.1000/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 1000/2015 This application is filed by applicant Laxman alias Tillu Ambadas Bannam for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. I­75/2015 registered at Bhiwandi City police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 363, 376(A) of I.P.C. and section 4, 7, 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant gave false assurance of marriage to minor victim girl and then kidnapped her and committed rape on her from time to time. It is further contended and argued that no such incident of kidnapping has taken place and the girl herself had left the house and went with the applicant since there was love affair between them and the applicant is falsely implicated. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co­operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that the accused and the victim were knowing each other since before the incident and taking disadvantage of minor age of the victim the accused gave false promise of marriage to her and induced her and then kidnapped her and thereafter when they were staying together he committed rape on her time and again. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, .. 2 .. bail no.1000/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl and the prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 354A of I.P.C. and section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act with the allegation that he kidnapped the minor girl who is stated to be 17 years old under false assurance of marriage and then raped her time and again. But then it is contended on behalf of accused that the girl had left the house of her own and came with him and it is a case of consent and he is falsely implicated in the crime. In such circumstance when the girl is stated to be below 18 years of age, the consent of minor is immaterial and the aspect as to whether the act of the accused amounts to rape or whether it is a case of consent, would be the question to be decided on merits. Even nothing is stated to be recovered from the applicant/accused. 4] It is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. 5] In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond .. 3 .. bail no.1000/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 6] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 7] Then, it has also to be mentioned that looking the allegations against the accused the investigation in the matter may have almost completed but the charge sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 8] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Laxman alias Tillu Ambadas Bannam is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ .. 4 .. bail no.1000/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) The applicant/accused shall attend the concerned police station on every Monday between 10.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon till filing of the charge sheet and shall co­operate in investigation. He shall not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and the prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this Court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 19.05.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.

Presented on : 29.04.2014 Registered on : 29.04.2014 Decided on : 31.10.2017 Duration : 03 Y 06 M 03 D IN THE COURT OF SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE, AT : THANE (Presided over by P.P.Jadhav) District Judge­6 and Additional Sessions Judge, Thane Spl. Case POCSO No.95/2014 Exh.No.29. State of Maharashtra (through Shantinagar Pol.Stn. Cr.No.I­90/2013) ...Complainant Vs. 1. Daud Kamruddin Hasmi, Age 19 years, Occ. Welding labour, R/at.Ramnagar, Near Bouddha Vihar, Bhiwandi, 2. Saijad Kamruddin Hasmi, Age 25 years, Occ. Welding labour, R/at.Ramnagar, Near Bouddha Vihar, Bhiwandi, ...Accused For the offences punishable u/s.354, 323, 504, 34 of Indian Penal Code and u/s.7,8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 95­14 ­ 354,323,504, 7,8.doc .....2/­ ..2.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 95/2014.. Exh.29.. APP Mr.V.A.Kulkarni for State Adv.Mr.R.S.Jagtap for accused : JUDGMENT : (Delivered on this 31st day of October, 2017) The accused are prosecuted for the offence of sexually assaulting the complainant's minor daughter, physically assaulting the complainant and threatening the complainant and her family members. 2] The prosecution story runs as under : It is alleged by prosecution that complainant Shamsha Khatun Najamuddin Khan is residing at Rafiknagar, Bhiwandi. She is residing with her two minor daughters and two minor sons. She is also having a married daughter. On 26.01.2013 at about 07.30 p.m. the complainant's married daughter had called upon the complainant's minor daughter Reshma aged 12 years old. Thereupon Reshma was proceeding to the house of her married sister. At that time accused Daud Ibrahim followed her and hugged her from backside. Reshma rescued herself and returned home and narrated the incident to the complainant. The complainant being widow and having minor children, did not dare to confront the accused. Thereafter the complainant had hanged J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 95­14 ­ 354,323,504, 7,8.doc .....3/­ ..3.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 95/2014.. Exh.29.. her clothes to dry the same outside their house. At that time the accused cut the clothes of complainant's minor daughter with the help of shaving blade. When the complainant asked the accused about the same, accused Daud and his brother Saijad abused and assaulted the complainant. 3] With these allegations the complainant lodged complaint on 14.03.2013 in Shantinagar police station, Bhiwandi. After receiving complaint offence punishable u/s.354, 323, 506 r.w.34 of the Indian Penal Code and section 7 and 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act came to be registered against both the accused. After investigation, charge sheet came to be filed against them for said offences. 4] Charge is framed against the accused at Exh.02. Accused pleaded not guilty of offence and claimed to be tried. 5] Statements of accused u/s.313 of Code of Criminal Procedure are recorded at Exh.27 and Exh.28. The defence of accused is that, the complainant's hen used to spread dirt in their house. When the accused had asked the complainant about the same, the complainant's son­in­law and others had assaulted them. Thereupon a criminal case was filed against them which is pending in Bhiwandi Court. To counter said J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 95­14 ­ 354,323,504, 7,8.doc .....4/­ ..4.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 95/2014.. Exh.29.. criminal case, the complainant lodged false complaint against them. 6] After going through the prosecution story, evidence on record and hearing arguments of both sides, following points arise for my determination. I record my findings thereon for reasons as stated below. POINTS FINDINGS 1] Does the prosecution prove that on 26.01.2013 at about 19.30 hours in front of the house of complainant at Rafiknagar, Bhiwandi accused Daud hugged complainant's minor daughter Reshma from backside, sexually assaulted her and outraged her modesty ? …Not proved. 2] Does the prosecution further prove that on above mentioned date, time and place both the accused in furtherance of their common intention assaulted the complainant and her family members and voluntarily caused hurt to them ? …Not proved. 3] Does the prosecution further prove that on the above mentioned date, time and place both the accused in furtherance of their common intention intentionally abused the complainant and her family members intending to provoke them to commit breach of public peace? …Not proved. 4] What order ? ..As per final order. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 95­14 ­ 354,323,504, 7,8.doc .....5/­ ..5.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 95/2014.. Exh.29.. : REASONS : As to the Point Nos.1 to 3 :­ 7] To bring home the guilt of accused the prosecution has examined complainant Shamsha Khatun Najamuddin Khan as PW1 at Exh.11. The complaint filed by her is at Exh.12. Complainant's minor daughter Reshma Khatun Najamuddin Khan is examined as PW2 at Exh.14. The investigating officer P..SI., Yadav Ruplal Khairnar is examined as PW3 at Exh.22. The spot panchanama is at Exh.23. 8] PW1 Shamsha Khatun in her deposition at Exh.11 narrated almost all facts. She deposed that when Reshma was going to the house of married daughter Fatima, accused Daud came form behind and hugged her. Thereupon Reshma raised alarm. Hearing the commotion she (PW1) called Reshma as to what had happened. Thereafter accused Daud left her and ran away from the spot. On inquiry Reshma narrated the incident. She further deposed that Reshma had further told that accused Saijad used to follow her on way to school. He used to ask her to accompany for a movie. Both the accused used to cut a string of her clothes with the help of blade. When she confronted the accused about the same, the accused abused and assaulted them. She was in hospital for two months. Thereafter she lodged complaint. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 95­14 ­ 354,323,504, 7,8.doc .....6/­ ..6.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 95/2014.. Exh.29.. 9] Victim Reshma Khatun in her deposition at Exh.14 deposed that on 26.01.2013 her married sister Fatima had called her to look after her son. When she was going to the house of her sister Fatima, accused Daud followed her and hugged from backside. When she shouted for help, the accused ran away. Her sister asked her as to what had happened. Prior to said incident when she used to wash utensils outside their house, accused Daud used to show her pornography films on mobile. He used to stop her whenever she used to go to school. 10] Relying upon the depositions of PW1 and PW2 learned A.P.P. Mr.Kulkarni argued at length and submitted that the statement of complainant and that of the victim are corroborated by each other. From said consistent oral evidence, the offence is duly proved against both the accused. 11] As argued by learned advocate Mr.Jagtap and as appears from the documents on record there is delay of almost two months in lodging F.I.R. The complainant has stated that she was hospitalized for two months and therefore, there is delay. However, said fact is not supported by any other independent witness. Therefore, fact that section 323 of the Indian Penal Code as applied in the present case shows that the reason stated by the complainant for delay in lodging J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 95­14 ­ 354,323,504, 7,8.doc .....7/­ ..7.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 95/2014.. Exh.29.. F.I.R. is not reasonable and reliable. Apparently the delay is inordinate and unexplained. 12] It is further to be noted here that in cross examination the complainant has admitted that two months prior to the incident the complainant's elder daughter Fatima had been to their house for delivery and stayed with them for six months. Thus on the day of alleged incident complainant's elder daughter Fatima was at home, but she did not lodge any complaint against the accused. As admitted by PW2 Reshma no complaint was filed in respect of alleged stalking by the accused prior to the incident dated 26.01.2013. PW2 Reshma has further admitted in her cross examination that her mother had also filed another F.I.R. out of which Cr.No.225/2014 was registered against one Naseem Momin for offence punishable u/s.363 and 366 of the Indian Penal Code. She further admitted that on 09.04.2015 also her mother lodged F.I.R. against one Nafeez Imtiyaz Momin. 13] It is pertinent to note here that in a complaint it is not specifically mentioned that the victim had told the complainant that the accused used to stalk her on the way of school. It is also not mentioned in the complaint that the accused used to show pornography films to the victim on mobile. Even in a statement of the victim recorded by police J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 95­14 ­ 354,323,504, 7,8.doc .....8/­ ..8.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 95/2014.. Exh.29.. said fact is not mentioned. Thus the allegations about showing pornography films on mobile and stalking the victim on the way of school are improvements and after thought allegations. 14] Admittedly there is no independent witnesses to the incident which allegedly occurred outside the house and on the road. There is inordinate delay in lodging F.I.R. there are material improvements in the deposition of witnesses. Under such circumstances the prosecution has miserably failed to prove its case against the accused. Hence answering point Nos.1 to 3 in the negative, following order is passed. ORDER 1. Accused No.1. Daud Kamruddin Hasmi and No.2. Saijad Kamruddin Hasmi are hereby acquitted u/s.235(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure for offence punishable u/s.354, 323, 504 r.w. 34 of the Indian Penal Code and section 7 and 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 2. The bail bonds of accused stand cancelled. 3. Accused are directed to furnish personal bond of Rs.5,000/­ each in terms of sec.437­A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Sd/­... Thane. (P.P.Jadhav) District Judge­6 and Date : 31.10.2017. Addl. Sessions Judge, Thane. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 95­14 ­ 354,323,504, 7,8.doc ...../­

CNR NO. MHTH01­002848­2018 RECEIVED ON : 10/04/2018 REGISTERED ON : 10/04/2018 DECIDED ON : 25/05/2018 DURATION :YY MM DD 00 01 15 IN THE COURT OF ADDITIONAL SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE AT : THANE (Presided over by Mr. Vivek Gavhane ) Spl. Case No. 82/2018 EXH.23 CNR NO. MHTH01­002848­2018 PROSECUTION : The State of Maharashtra Through Police Station C.B.D. VERSUS ACCUSED : Ajay alias Gedaram Ramraj Gautam Age 20 years R/o. Pahalada Karonda, Tehsil Nanpara, District Baharaich Uttar Pradesh Offence :­ Section 376,363 of I.P.C. & Sec.4 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. APPEARANCE Smt. S.E. Phad, Ld. DGP for the State. Smt. Sarita Gaikwad, Ld. Advocate for the accused. JUDGMENT: (Delivered on this 25th day of May, 2018) A case of kidnapping and rape of a minor. ­­ 2 ­­ The prosecution's case in brief :­ The victim (a 13 years old girl) resided with her grandfather and used to sell balloons on the streets of C.B.D. Belapur. The accused worked in a sugarcane juice stall. Due to acquaintance, on 31.12.2017, the accused enticed the victim out of the custody of her grandfather and took her to his native place in Uttar Pradesh, where the victim was kept in his house. The accused would sleep with the victim and have sexual intercourse with her against her consent. The victim was thus raped 15 to 20 times until she was rescued by C.B.D. Police on 17.1.2018. 2] After the victim had gone missing and was not found for nearly 3­4 days, her grandfather lodged a complaint against the accused, suspecting his involvement in the matter. An offence (C.R.No. I­7/2018 U/sec.363 of I.P.C.) was registered at the C.B.D. Belapur Police Station. The investigating officer traced out the native place of the accused and raided it, during which, the victim was rescued and the accused was taken in custody. Both were subjected to medical examination, certificate from the victim's school about her age was collected. The I.O. recorded statements of witnesses, drew a spot memorandum at the house of the accused, seized the cloths of the accused as well as the victim for the purpose of ­­ 3 ­­ Chemical Analysis, caused witness statements to be recorded U/sec.164 of Cr.P.C. by the Ld. Magistrate and upon completion of investigation, filed a charge sheet against the accused U/sec.363 & 376 of I.P.C. as well as sec.4 & 6 of the Protection of Children from the Sexual offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter referred to as 'POCSO'). 3] A charge was framed against the accused only under section 363 & 376 of I.P.C. as well as Sec.3 punishable U/sec.4 of POCSO, to which, he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. The trial began in camera. The prosecution examined the victim (P.W.1 Exh.7), the victim's grandfather (P.W.2 Exh.9), Dr. Yogita Patil (P.W.3 Exh.11), Dr. Sanjay Yamgar (P.W.4 Exh.13) and the Investigating Officer Rakesh Gumane (P.W.5 Exh.17). The prosecution tendered in evidence the F.I.R. (Exh.10), the 164 statement of the victim (Exh.8), the medical certificate of the victim (Exh.12), her medical certificate with respect to her age (Exh.14), the spot memorandum (Exh.15), the letters written to medical officer by the I.O. (Exh.18 to 20), the medical certificate of the accused (Exh.16) before closing its evidence vide pursis Exh.21. 4] The accused admitted the medical certificate (Exh.16) which stated that he was potent and capable of ­­ 4 ­­ having sexual intercourse. The accused also admitted the spot memorandum conducted at his residence (Exh.15). 5] While answering his examination U/sec.313 of Cr.P.C., the accused admitted having taken the victim to his house in Uttar Pradesh. It is admitted that the victim is the grand daughter of the complainant and that she was 13 years old at the time of the incident. He also admitted that the victim resided in his house for about 15­17 days, but denied having ever touched her. The accused denied the alleged rape or sexual intercourse and claimed that the victim had gone with him voluntarily, as she was fed up of the household chores she was required to do by her grand father. 6] The evidence on record and the arguments advanced thereon, give rise to the following points. Points Findings 1] Whether the victim was a minor (below 18 years of age) ? .. Yes 2] Whether the victim was taken away/enticed out of the keeping of her grandfather, without his consent ? .. Yes ­­ 5 ­­ Points Findings 3] Whether the accused had sexual intercourse with the victim ? .. Yes 4] Whether the accused kidnapped the victim from lawful guardianship ? .. Yes 5] Whether the accused raped victim ? .. Yes 6] Whether the accused committed penetrative sexual assault against the victim ? .. Yes 7] What order ? .. As per final orders. REASONS 7] The alleged kidnapping was without use of physical force as the accused is said to have used his previous acquaintance with the victim for the purpose of enticing her to go with him. It is the testimony of the victim that she knew the accused as he used to work in a sugarcane juice stall near the place where she sold balloons. The victim's grandfather knew the accused too. It has been stated by the grandfather that the accused would frequent the place where he resided with the victim (below the C.B.D. bridge). The grandfather had ones asked the accused the reason why the accused frequented the said place. After the victim had gone missing on the night of ­­ 6 ­­ 31st December 2017 and was nowhere to be found, the grandfather lodged a police complaint. Since the accused was also not seen after the disappearance of the victim, the grandfather expressed, in the F.I.R., his suspicion on the accused. 8] It has been stated by the victim that the accused took her to his native (Village Karonda, Uttar Pradesh) and made her stay with him for nearly 17 days. In her cross­ examination, she has stated that she was taken to Uttar Pradesh in a train and the train tickets were bought by the accused out of the money taken from her. The victim was not only carrying money but also had a bag of spare clothes. Though the Ld. defence advocate, during cross­examination of the victim, did not ask her, if she cried for help during the alleged kidnapping, the circumstances brought on record menifest that there was no resistance from the victim. Had the accused used physical force for the purpose of taking the victim to Uttar Pradesh or had the victim raised hue and cry for help, there is simply no way the kidnapping had gone unnoticed by the thousands of railway commuters. The accused could take the victim to his native at Uttar Pradesh only because the victim did not resist. The fact that she was carrying a considerable amount of money with her, besides a ­­ 7 ­­ bag full of spare clothes, goes to show that the victim was well prepared to go with the accused, although, she claims she had no consent to marry him or have physical relation. Whatever may have been the reason behind the lack of resistance, the fact remains, the victim did go with the accused silently. 9] While facing cross­examination, the victim asserted the defence suggestion about her marriage with the accused in Bholenath temple (in U.P.) with the words “I did not marry with consent”. She added that the accused did not tie mangalsutra and that she had no knowledge about the marriage as they did it all of a sudden. These facts have been brought on record while putting up the defence theory that the victim was fed up of the household chores required to be done in the house of her grandfather and wanted a freedom. 10] It has been stated by the victim that when she was in the accused's house, the accused would sleep with her and do wrong things with her. He did inappropriate things for which, he used to remove her clothes as well as his own clothes. The victim has stated that after removing clothes, the accused used to rape her. He did it several times during her stay at his house for nearly 17 days, until she was ultimately rescued by the police. The victim has thus categorically stated ­­ 8 ­­ not only about sexual intercourse but also about lack of her consent. She did not even consent for the ceremony that was performed at the Bholenath temple, as per the defence contention. 11] Although it is undisputed that the duo went to Uttar Pradesh and resided together, the accused contends that he never had physical relation with the victim. It has been cautiously stated by the accused, while answering his examination U/sec.313 of Cr.P.C. that he gave the victim a shelter in his own house, but did not touch her. According to the accused, he has no physical infirmity and that the medical certificate (Exh.16) about his potency, is true. He however, denied a knowledge about medical examination of the victim or its outcome. 12] The witnesses have been cross­examined thoroughly but the Ld. defence advocate could not solicit answer that could discredit the veracity of the witnesses. The two doctors and the investigating officer being formal official witnesses, had no reason to depose false against the accused. Also, the accused has not laid base for the defence suggestion, as to why the witnesses would frame the accused. As regard the testimony of victim's grandfather, he has restricted his ­­ 9 ­­ statements only to the matters witnessed by him and did not step in the arena of hearsay evidence. The grandfather was not present when the victim was allegedly kidnapped and sexually assaulted. As such, there is no scope for contradiction between the statements of two witnesses. The overall impression of the prosecution witnesses is that they are all reliable. Admission of a major part of the prosecution case (about the victim staying in the accused's house for 17 days) only adds to the credibility of the prosecution case. 13] No doubt, F.I.R. has been lodged after about four days of the victim going missing from C.B.D. Belapur. To this the complainant (grandfather) has stated that he was busy in searching for the victim. The explanation may not be sufficient to account for the delay of four days but the fact remains, the victim was admittedly, taken by the accused to his native place from C.B.D. Belapur. Given the said undisputed position, the delay caused in registration of F.I.R. by the grandfather, looses significance. 14] In order to seek corroboration to the oral evidence of sexual intercourse, the prosecution has sought to rely on medical evidence. Upon being rescued and brought back to Navi Mumbai, the victim was subjected to medical examination ­­ 10 ­­ and the medical officer Yogita Patil (P.W.3) has expressed her opinion about there being evidence of sexual intercourse. According to Dr. Yogita Patil, she conducted medical examination of victim on 20.1.2018. The victim had a history of sexual intercourse with the accused for about 15 to 20 times in the previous month, with the last intercourse being just 4 to 5 days prior to her medical examination. Although during general examination, no injury marks were found on the victims body, a local examination revealed absence of hymen with no injury or bleeding on the private parts. Considering the history given and absence of hymen, the doctor opined that the evidence was suggestive of sexual intercourse. The medical certificate (Exh.12) was accordingly issued. Barring a few suggestions denying the prosecution's case, there has been no effective cross­examination of Dr. Yogita Patil. 15] Thus, the oral evidence of the victim is corroborated by reliable medical evidence. The ability of the accused to have sexual intercourse (potency) is undisputed. The defence theory of marriage ceremony of the victim and accused at the Bholenath temple, shows the attitude and approach of the accused towards the victim. She was made to reside with the accused under one roof, where he not only slept with her but had sexual intercourse with her several times, to which the ­­ 11 ­­ victim referred as 'rape'. All this evidence is too strong to be discarded on the bald statement of the accused that he did not touch the victim despite having taken her to his house and resided with her for almost 17 days. 16] The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Rajinder @ Raju V/s. State of Himachal Pradesh .. has reiterated the legal position recognized in the case of Radhu V/s. State of Madhya Pradesh 2007(12) SCC 57 wherein it was observed “It is now well settled that a finding of guilt in a case of rape, can be based on the uncorroborated evidence of the prosecutrix. They very nature of offence makes it difficult to get direct corroborating evidence. The evidence of the prosecutrix should bot be rejected on the basis of minor discrepancies and contradictions. If the victim of rape states on oath that she was forcibly subjected to sexual intercourse, her statement will normally be accepted, even if it is uncorroborated, unless the material on record requires drawing of an inference that there was consent or that the entire incident was improbable or imaginary. Even if there is consent, the act will still be a 'rape', if the girl is under 16 years of age. It is also well settled that absence of injuries on the private parts of the victim will not by itself falsify the case of rape, nor construed as evidence of consent.” 17] I am thus convinced that the accused did have sexual intercourse with the victim for several times. Though the victim has categorically stated, in so many words, that she ­­ 12 ­­ did not consent for the physical relation, a question arises, did the consent of victim even matter ? 18] It is a case of the prosecution that the victim was hardly 13 years old when the offence took place. The victim claims her date of birth to be 26.9.2005. Even the I.O. is said to have ensured the said date from the school of the victim. The medical examination and ossification test of the victim suggest her age to be 15 years with a margin of 6 months on both the sides. Most importantly, the accused does not dispute with the victim being a minor. Neither were any of the prosecution witnesses suggested that the victim was more than 18 years old nor did the accused say so, while answering his examination U/sec. 313 of Cr.p.c. In fact, initially the accused stated that he was unaware of the victim's date of birth and later he specifically admitted that the victim was 13 years old and that the complainant was her grandfather. Since, the oral evidence as well as the medical evidence, in respect of the victim's age, go hand in hand and the defence does not dispute with the age factor of the victim, I am convinced that the victim was not only minor at the time of the incident, but her age was somewhere between 13 yrs. and 15 yrs. ­­ 13 ­­ 19] Since the victim was hardly 15 years old, I do not think her consent really matters, be it moving out of the custody of her guardian (grandfather) or sexual intercourse. A glance at the following provisions should make the position clear : Sec. 361 of IPC. :­ 361 Kidnapping from lawful guardianship – Whoever takes or entices any mior under sixteen years of age if a male, or under eighteen years of age if a female, or any person of unsound mind, out of the keeping of the lawful guardian of such minor or person of unsound mind, without the consent of such guardian, is said to kidnap such minor or person from lawful guardianship. Explanation – The words “lawful guardian” in this section include any person lawfully entrusted with the care of custody of such minor or other person. The relevant portion of Section 375 IPC (as amended by Criminal Law Amendment Act, 2013) 375. A man is said to commit “rape” if he ­ (a) penetrates his penis, to any extent, into the vagina, mouth, urethra or anus of a woman or makes her to do so with him or any other person; or (b), (c), (d) under the circumstances falling under any of the following seven descriptions :­ ­­ 14 ­­ Sixthly – With or without her consent, when she is under eighteen years of age. Section 2(d) of POCSO (d) “child” means any person below the age of eighteen years; Section 3 of the POCSO A person is said to commit “penetrative sexual assault” if ­ (a) he penetrates his penis, to any extent, into the vagina, mouth, urethra or anus of a child or makes the child to do so with him or any other person; or (b) he inserts, to any extent, any object or a part of the body, not being the penis, into the vagina, the urethra or anus of the child or makes the child to do so with him or any other person; or (c) he manipulates any part of the body of the child so as to cause penetration into the vagina, urethra, anus or any part of body of the child or makes the child to do so with him or any other person; or (d) he applies his mouth to the penis, vagina, anus, urethra of the child or makes the child to do so to such person or any other person. Section 29 of POCSO Where a person is prosecuted for committing or abetting or attempting to commit any offence under sections 3,5,7 and section 9 of this Act, the Special Court shall presume, ­­ 15 ­­ that such person has committed or abetted or attempted to commit the offence, as the case may be unless the contrary is proved. Sec. 114A of Indian Evidence Act In a prosecution for rape under clause (a), clause (b) clause(c), clause(d), clause (e), clause (f), clause (g), clause(h), clause (i), clause(j), clause(k), clause (l), clause(m) or clause(n) of sub­section (2) of section 376 of the Indian Penal Code, where sexual intercourse by the accused is proved and the question is whether it was without consent of the woman alleged to have been raped and such woman states in her evidence before the court that she did not consent, the court shall presume that she did not consent. Explanation – In this section, “sexual intercourse” shall mean any of the acts mentioned in clauses (a) to (d) of section 375 of the Indian Penal Code'.. 20] It is thus clear from the above provisions that anyone taking or enticing a minor female (under the age of 18 yrs.) out of the keeping of the lawful guardian, without the consent of such guardian, commits the offence of kidnapping from lawful guardianship. The consent of the guardian is required to be obtained and the consent of the minor is immaterial. In the case in hand, the victim was between 13 yrs ­­ 16 ­­ and 15 yrs of age and was under the care and custody of her grandfather. The grandfather (P.W.2) not only lodged a missing complaint blaming the accused but also deposed in the court about the alleged kidnapping. The evidence is a manifesto of absence of consent of the grandfather. The ingredients of the offence of kidnapping are thus made out. 21] Sec. 114A of the Evidence Act lays down a presumption that if the case false in clause (i) of Sub­section 2 of Section 376 of I.P.C. and where sexual intercourse by the accused is proved and the woman states in her evidence that she did not consent, the court has to presume that she did not consent. In the case in hand, the victim being less than 16 years of age, her case falls under Sec.376(2)(i) of I.P.C. and the accused is burdened with the responsibility to rebut the presumption. Except denial of the prosecution case, there have been no efforts from the accused to show that the victim consented for the intercourse. 22] There is enough evidence (as discussed above) about the accused committing sexual intercourse with the victim. As regard consent of the victim, she referred to the physical acts done by the accused as 'wrong and inappropriate ­­ 17 ­­ things'. According to her, the accused raped her. The victim also stated categorically that she did not consent for it. Thus the victim, in so many words, expressed that the sexual intercourse was against her consent. 23] I believe, even if the accused had adduced evidence showing consent of the victim, the same would be immaterial, given the provision in the 6 th description of Sec.375. The provisions says that if any of the acts mentioned in clause (a) to (d) are committed against a woman under 18 years of age, it constitutes an offence of rape irrespective of whether she consented for such acts or not. Thus, consent of a female below the age of 18 years of age, is immaterial and proof of sexual intercourse is sufficient to hold the accused guilty U/sec.375 of IPC. 24] As regard the offence of penetrative sexual assault (u/sec.3 of the POCSO Act), the provision no where speaks about consent of the child. Actus Rea is sufficient to make out an offence as specified in section 3. A person below the age of 18 years is treated as child in view of the provision in section 2(d) of the Act. ­­ 18 ­­ 25] Thus, the victim may not have resisted the accused while she was taken from C.B.D. Belapur to Uttar Pradesh, the act of the accused in enticing her to go with him on the basis of previous acquaintance, without the permission of her grandfather (guardian) and keeping her in his own house for over a fortnight, amounts to kidnapping. Consent of the victim, be it for moving her out of the control and custody of her grandfather or for sexual intercourse, was immaterial, given her tender age of less than 15 years. It is evident that after taking the victim to his own house in Uttar Pradesh, the accused established sexual intercourse with her for several times. It is evident that the victim did not consent for the intercourse. The victim was rescued by the C.B.D. Police and her medical reports go hand in hand with her testimony as regard sexual intercourse. The defence that the accused never touched the victim, despite having resided with her under one roof is unbelievable. The accused has failed to rebut the presumptions in sec.114A of the Evidence Act or sec.29 of POCSO. I am thus convinced that the ingredients of section 361 & 375 of IPC. as well as Sec.3 of the POCSO Act have been made out, for which I hereby hold the accused guilty U/sec.361 & 375 of Indian Penal Code and also Sec.3 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. ­­ 19 ­­ 26] At this point of time, I have heard the accused, the Ld. DGP and the Ld. defence advocate, on the point of sentence. The accused has prayed for leniency stating that his parents are illiterate and they depend totally on him for their livelihood. He claims, he has to bear the expenses of his younger siblings and his absence in the family for a long period would have disastrous effects on the family. The Ld. Defence advocate too prayed for leniency citing the young age of the accused. It has been submitted that the accused has no criminal antecedents and he deserves minimum punishment awardable under sec. 376 of IPC. 27] The Ld. DGP on the other hand, referred to the tender age of the victim while submitting in respect the quantum of punishment. According to the DGP, the wide spread menace of the child abuse and child rape is only increasing day by day and leniency in sentence would frustrate the purpose of the various amendments carried out in criminal law by way of The Criminal Law Amendment Act, 2013. 28] There is no denying that instances of child abuse are at their peak. Penetrative sexual assault against a child is the worst kind of offence these days. The accused has been held guilty, not only U/sec.376(2)(i) of IPC but also U/sec.3 p/u/s. ­­ 20 ­­ Sec.4 of the POCSO. The provision in sec.42 of the Act plays an important role on the point of sentence. It says, the offender found guilty of the offence punishable under POCSO and also under any other law for time being in force, can only be punished under the law that provides for a greater degree of punishment. 29] Since sec.4 of POCSO provides for a punishment of minimum 7 years of imprisonment whereas sec.376(2) prescribes a punishment of rigorous imprisonment for not less than 10 years. The maximum punishment awardable under both the provisions of law is imprisonment for life. In case of sec.376(2), imprisonment for life means imprisonment for the remainder of the person's natural life. 30] It is thus clear that punishment under sec.376(2) is of greater degree and the mandate of Sec.42 of POCSO is of awarding punishment under the law providing a greater decree of punishment. 31] The present offence of kidnapping and rape has to be differentiated from those kidnapping and rape cases wherein the victims are unknown and the accused just pounce upon the pedestrian victim, throw her inside a van, drive her ­­ 21 ­­ to a secluded place and rape her animalistically before throwing her back on the streets. Here, the accused enticed the victim of previous acquaintance and resided with her in his own house, which was occupied by his parents. No doubt, he raped her but the element of drawing animalistic pleasure from the victim was missing. There is nothing to show that the accused was cruel or unreasonable on the victim except for the act of rape. The said distinction between the facts of the present case and the extra ordinary cases which predominantly led to the amendments by way of Criminal Law Amendment Act, has to be borne in mind. Given the said difference in the factual matrix, I am convinced to award minimum term of imprisonment awardable under sec.376(2) of IPC while being moderate in the sentencing under Sec.363 of IPC. The accused must also be fined under both the provisions of law and an amount of Rs.25,000/­ under each of the provisions should suffice. An amount of Rs.45,000/­ out of the fine recovered, can be utilized for compensating the victim. Hence, the order. ORDER 1] The accused is hereby convicted for the offence punishable U/sec.363 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 for which, he is hereby sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 3½ years (three and a half years) with a fine of ­­ 22 ­­ Rs.25,000/­ (Rs. Twenty Five Thousand), in default of which, he shall undergo rigorous imprisonment for a further period of 3 months. 2] The accused is hereby convicted for the offence punishable U/sec.376(2) of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 for which, he is hereby sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 10 years (ten years) with a fine of Rs.25000/­ (Rs. Twenty Five Thousand), in default of which, he shall undergo rigorous imprisonment for a further period of 3 months. 3] Both the sentences shall run concurrent. 4] Out of the fine recovered, an amount of Rs.45,000/­ (Rs. Forty Five Thousand) be paid to the victim by way of compensation. 5] The period of imprisonment already undergone by the accused from 17.1.2018 till today, be set off against the above period of imprisonment vide Section 428 of Cr.P.C. 6] The muddemal property be disposed of as per rules, after expiry of the period of appeal. ­­ 23 ­­ 7] A copy of judgment be given, free of cost, to the accused and he be informed about his right to free legal aid before the Appellate Court. (The case has been tried and hereby disposed of as per the provisions of Chapter XVIII of Cr.P.C.) (Pronounced in the open Court) Sd/­ Date :­25.5.2018 (Vivek Gavhane) Additional Sessions Judge, Thane

1 POCSO Case. No. 104/2017. Presented on­ 24.04.2017. Registered on­ 24.04.2017. Decided on­ 22.05.2018. Duration­ Y­1 M­0 D­28 IN THE COURT OF SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE. [Presided over by A.S. Learned Advocate Smt. Reena Korde, for the accused. ___________________________________________________________ JUDGMENT (Delivered on 22.05.2018.) 1] Accused Vishal Babu Manchekar, is facing trial for the offences punishable u/s. 341, 354, 506 of I.P.C. and u/s. 8, 12 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 2 POCSO Case. No. 104/2017. 2] It is the case of prosecution that victim aged about 17 years and 3 months, lodged her report (Exh.12) alleging that she joined her tuition class since 1st October, 2016. Accused was chasing her and proposing her. She had neglected his request. In November after Diwali, accused came near her class and threatened her that he would give trouble to her father if she had not joined him as a friend. On 08.01.17 at about 9 a.m. when victim was proceeding towards her class, accused came to her and by force, she was taken by him and kissed her. The offence vide C.R. no. 15/17 u/s. 341, 354, 506 of I.P.C. and u/s. 8 and 12 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act came to be registered. P.W.5 Shri. Mundhe had carried out investigation. He requested D.C.P. to trace out location of the accused on the basis of his mobile. On 17.01.17, copy of F.I.R. was sent to Collector and resettlement board. Thereafter, he rushed to the spot and recorded spot panchanama in presence of panchas. Accused was arrested. Bajaj motor­cycle was seized from him. Statements of witnesses were recorded. After investigation, charge­sheet was submitted. 3] Heard both sides. I framed the charge against the accused for the offences punishable under section 341, 354, 506 of I.P.C. and u/s. 8, 12 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, on 05/08/2017. Details of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular, to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. His defence is of total denial. 4] During trial, defence has admitted no documents. 5] To bring home the guilt of the accused for the charges leveled against him, the prosecution has examined as many as ten witnesses i.e. 3 POCSO Case. No. 104/2017. P.W. Name of witness Exh. Description No. No. 1] Kiran Namdev Zemse 7 Panch of spot panchanama. 2] Meenakshi Bala Murgan 9 Teacher of victim girl. 3] Victim girl 11 Complainant/victim girl. 4] Vinda Rahul Singh 14 Mother of victim girl. 5] Umesh Bapurao Munde 17 Investigating officer. 6] Accused did not enter into witness box. He has not examined defence witness. 7] Heard learned Special P.P. Smt. Phad, for the State and learned counsel Smt. Reena Korde for the accused. 8] Following points arise for my determination, which are being answered for the reasons given herein­below. POINTS FINDINGS 1] Whether prosecution proved that in No. between 01.10.16 to 08.01.2017 at about 09.00 a.m., at sector no. 6 to near Gulab Sons dairy at sector no. 15, when complainant victim girl aged 17 years was going to her class, accused came on motor­cycle without number and wrongfully restrained her and made her to sit on his motor­cycle ? 2] Whether prosecution proved that in the No. above period and place, accused had chased complainant victim girl aged 17 years and when she was going to her class, accused came on motor­cycle without number and using criminal 4 POCSO Case. No. 104/2017. force, made her to sit on his motor­ cycle, took her near the class at sector no. 15 and took a kiss of her cheek, intending to outrage or knowing it to be likely that he would thereby outrage her modesty and committed the offence of sexual assault and sexual harassment ? 3] Whether prosecution proved that in the No. above period and place, accused had chased complainant victim girl aged 17 years and gave threats to her of torturing her and her parents if she would not keep friendly relations with him and committed criminal intimidation ? 4] What order ? As per final order. REASONS POINT NOS. 1 TO 3 9] P.W.3 complainant victim girl had deposed in her examination­in­chief that­ In the year 2017, she was studying in 12th standard in Tilak Junior College, Vashi. She had joined her tuition classes with Goodwill Tutorial near Gulabson's dairy, Koparkhairne, since 2016. She knew accused. He used to chase her to her tuition classes. He used to ask her to become his friend, else he would see her parents. He used to force her to sit on his scooter. He had also kissed her. She disclosed the same with her parents. He had chased her for about 4­5 days. Then, she went to police station along with her parents and she had lodged her report (Exh. 12). She was born on 04.10.1999. True copy of her birth certificate is at article A. Her statement is at Exh. 13. 5 POCSO Case. No. 104/2017. 10] It has come in her cross­examination that­ Then, she was running her 18th year of age. Near the spot, there were shops of jewelers having traffic on road. At the time of her tuition class also, there used to be crowd on the road. So also, pupils of tuition class used to remain there. There, people might gather on her call. She did not know that to all shops of jewelers, there are C.C.T.V. cameras. Six chits shown to her were in her hand­writing. Mobile number 8767342016 belongs to her mother. She had also sent messages to accused from mobile of her mother, as 'I love you, I miss you ­­­­­'. She was waiting for him. In the three coloured photographs shown to her, she herself along with accused were seen. In the said photographs, she embraced the accused. There was love between her and accused. Her parents came to know about it. Witness voluntarily stated that accused was married person and he had concealed the same fact from her. 11] No birth certificate of victim is placed on record to prove the age of victim. However, prosecution had placed on record true copy of birth certificate at article A. Original birth certificate or school leaving certificate is not placed on record. No concerned authority is examined to prove the date of birth of victim, rather her age on the date of incident that at relevant time, victim was minor. 12] From the cross­examination, it can be seen that she was using mobile of her mother and used to send the message to the accused as “I love you, I miss you ­­­­­”. Coloured photographs of accused and victim are placed on record, in which they both jointly can be viewed. 13] From the cross­examination of P.W.3 victim, it can be further gathered that on the way of her tuition class, there used to be crowd on the road. So also, pupils of tuition class used to remain present there. But, no such persons are examined by the prosecution to prove any of the incident 6 POCSO Case. No. 104/2017. that victim was followed by the accused and he was compelling her to love with him. 14] P.W.1 is panch to the spot panchanama. P.W.2 Meenakshi, a girl friend of victim deposed in her evidence that she was told by victim that accused was chasing her after her tuition class. On 08.01.17, she noticed the accused while standing outside of their tuition class. On 09.01.17, victim had attended her class as usual. But, nothing has been narrated by her to this witness. 15] Statement of victim u/s. 164 of Cr.P.C. was recorded by J.M.F.C. (Exh.13). It can be seen from it that there were love affairs between accused and victim. However, she came to know that the accused had already married person. Statement of victim seems to be recorded by Ld. J.M.F.C. Shri. J.A. Kotnis. However, it can be seen that it does not bear the signature of Shri. J.A. Kotnis, J.M.F.C., Vashi, on the statement of victim. Certainly, there is signature of Ld. J.M.F.C. Shri. J.A. Kotnis on certificate below statement Exh.13. 16] From the statement u/s. 164 of Cr.P.C. and chits of victim written in favour of accused, it can be gathered that there was love affair. However, when victim had noticed that the accused was married person, she might had filed her report against the accused. 17] Victim had performed her routine duty, even after the alleged incident. Therefore, there was no question of threat. It is not proved by the prosecution. 18] P.W.4 Vinda Singh deposed in her evidence that in the year 2016, she was told by victim that accused was chasing her. So, she along with her husband and his friend Ajit had given understanding to the 7 POCSO Case. No. 104/2017. accused. However, accused had not discontinued his illegal act of chasing her daughter. 19] Having considered the facts and circumstances of the matter and evidence on record, it is clear that there was love affair between accused and victim and out of love affair, accused might had been present in front of tuition classes of the victim. When she noticed that the accused was married person, victim might had discontinued her relations with the accused and lodged the report. Victim as per her evidence, had completed 17 years and 3 months. She was knowing the consequences of her own act. Therefore, it is very difficult to hold that accused had committed the offence. Prosecution had failed to prove the alleged offence beyond all reasonable doubts. Consequently, I record my findings to all the points, accordingly. In the result, I proceed to pass the following order. ORDER 1] Accused Vishal Babu Manchekar, is hereby, acquitted under sec. 235(1) of the Criminal Procedure Code, of the offences punishable u/s. 341, 354, 506 of I.P.C. and u/s. 8, 12 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 2] Accused Vishal Babu Manchekar, be enlarged on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ with surety of like amount. The effect of this bail order will remain in force for the period of six months from today, as per section 8 POCSO Case. No. 104/2017. 437­(A) of Cr.P.C. 3] Muddemal motor­cycle be returned to its registered owner, after appeal period is over. Thane, (A.S. Bhaisare) Date­ 22.05.2018.
