Ld. Advocate for the accused has submitted that the informant has improved her story and that creates doubt about her evidence. According to him, no overtact of these accused of the incident in the past is stated. There is no specific allegation against the accused Prakash in the F.I.R. Admittedly, there was some incident of beating by accused Vishnu to the son of the sister of witness Shilpa's husband. So as to give counterblast to it, these accused are falsely implicated. It is also submitted that Rupesh, the cousin of victim is serving in police department and the father of victim was also follower of Shivsena and so, it was possible for them to take assistance of police. 7] Following points arose for my determination and I gave my findings thereon for the reasons stated below: Sr. POINTS FINDINGS No. 1. Does the prosecution prove that the Yes. accused on 20.11.2014, in area of Only against Lokmanya Nagar, pada No.4, in accused No.1 furtherance of their common intention, followed a woman i.e. girl namely Ku. Shrutika Yerunkar, aged 17 years and accused No.1 contacts or attempts to contact her to foster personal interaction repeatedly despite a clear indication of disinterest by her ? 2. Does the prosecution prove that the No. accused on above mentioned date, time 6 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 87/2015 Judgment and place, in furtherance of their common intention wrongfully restrained Ku. Shrutika Yerunkar? 3. Does the prosecution prove that on No. above mentioned date, time and place, accused in furtherance of their common intention committed criminal intimidation by threatening Ku. Shrutika Yerunkar with injury to her person with intent to cause alarm to her or to cause her to do an act which she is legally bound to do? 4. Does the prosecution prove that on No. above mentioned date, time and place, accused committed sexual harassment upon a minor girl, aged 17 years with sexual intent? 5. What order? As per final order. REASONS AS TO POINT NO.1:­ 8] It is well settled that in order to bring home the guilt of accused, prosecution is required to adduce cogent, convincing and reliable evidence. It is also settled that a sole testimony of the witness is sufficient to base a conviction but the rule is that it should be above suspicion and should inspire confidence in the mind of the Court. Prosecution has examined informant /victim at Exh.10, her mother Shilpa Yerunkar at Exh.13 and investigation officer Mr. Deepak R. Kumbhar at Exh.15. 7 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 87/2015 Judgment In order to prove the guilt u/sec. 354­(D)(1), the prosecution is required to establish that the accused were following victim or contacting or attempting to contact her so as to force her personal interaction repeatedly though there was clear indication of disinterest by victim. It is not disputed seriously that at the time of incident, victim was studying in 10th standard. Victim has stated her date of birth as 08.09.1998. Since the defence had no objection to exhibit, School Leaving Certificate was given Exh.12. The alleged incident is from March­2014 to September­2014. So, at the time of incident, it appears that the victim was of the age of 16 years. 9] Victim has stated that she was allotted examination center for the 10th examination at Raj Thakur Vidyalaya, at Lokmanya Nagar, Thane. She was having her first paper on 03.03.2014. Accused used to be present near her examination center. On 03.03.2014, when she was proceeding to home after the examination is over, all three accused were present at the exit gate of the school and they gave whistle. Accused Vishnu stated that he likes her and he asked her to give reply to his question. When the victim has stated that she will narrate about it to her father, accused Vishnu replied that he has no fear of it and to say about it. Then, victim's father convinced said accused and then, the situation was normal for one month. According to her, she was out of station after 10th examination. She has further stated that after declaration of results of 10th standard, she got admission in college 8 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 87/2015 Judgment at Mulund. Accused Vishnu and his one friend Shrikant used to be present in the college. They used to board the same bus by which she used to proceed to the college and used to occupy front or rear side of the seat and used to sing a song. After alighting from the bus, accused Vishnu used to ask victim to respond his question. She used to ignore it and used to go to college. She has further stated that accused Vishnu used to follow her frequently. When she used to board the bus, accused Vishnu either used to hold her hand or bag and used to ask her to reply his question. This is in all testimony of the informant. 10] So far as the first part relating to the incident during the examination of 10th standard is concerned, the recitals of the report at Exh.11 shows that she has alleged about following her by accused Vishnu. It appears that the version of the informant so far as the act of accused Vishnu to follow her during the examination is consistent to allegation in the report. Evidence of victim also appears to be consistent with the report that in the month of March­2014, accused followed her and he told her that he likes her and she should reply his question. It seems that informant / victim has improved story to some extent by saying in the examination­in­ chief that all accused used to remain present at the gate of the school and used to give whistles. Though the victim has stated about following her by all the accused during the period of examination in examination­in­chief, she has not specifically alleged about it against other accused Prakash and Shrikant in 9 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 87/2015 Judgment report Exh.11. 11] The version of the victim is also appearing to be consistent with the report Exh.11. So far as the act of Vishnu that he used to board the same bus by which she was proceeding to her college and used to occupy her rear or front seat and used to whistle, her evidence is also consistent with the report Exh.11 that accused Vishnu used to follow her and while boarding the bus, he used to hold her bag and used to ask her to give reply to his question. It is also to be noted that informant has made allegation about boarding the same bus against all three accused in the report Exh.11. But, the informant has made such type of allegation of boarding the same bus against only accused Vishnu and Shrikant in her examination­in­chief. Informant has not stated in detail about the exact role of accused Shrikant nor she has stated in detail about the song which they sung. But, the informant has specifically stated the role of Vishnu of following her in the same bus and by holding the bag he used to ask her to reply the question. This victim was cross­examined by advocate for all accused at sufficient length. But, the evidence of the victim on the point of following or attempting to contact the victim by accused Vishnu is not shattered in the cross­examination. On the contrary, it seems that more details pertaining to the accused Vishnu are brought on record. 12] Accused Vishnu has suggested the victim in the cross­ examination that he had put a proposal of marriage through one 10 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 87/2015 Judgment Manoj Tandel. It was denied. But, then victim has admitted that accused Vishnu put proposal of marriage when she was in 10 th standard. Vishnu has also given a suggestion that victim stated that she will reply subsequently which is denied. Accused Vishnu has given another suggestion that he had gifted her a cadbury on one occasion. This suggestion is also denied by victim. These suggestions itself indicate that the accused was either following or contacting or attempting to contact the victim. The victim has specifically stated that when accused Vishnu has stated that he likes her and was seeking reply of his question, she has already instructed that she will narrate the fact to her father. Even father of victim had already convinced the accused Vishnu. This act of convincing Vishnu is not disputed in the cross­examination. Victim has also stated that while alighting from the bus, accused Vishnu used to ask her to reply his question. But, she used to ignore it and used to go to college. Even on 20.11.2014, victim had stated Vishnu not to follow her. This itself shows that the victim has shown her disinterest at all the time and still accused Vishnu has followed her. There is also no reason for the victim to depose against the accused. It can be gathered from the evidence that the victim was also having good understanding capacity as she was studying in 10 th and 11th standard at the time of incident. 13] Evidence of the victim also gets support from the evidence of her mother Shilpa. P.W.2 Shilpa has stated that her daughter informed her about the act of the accused. She used to 11 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 87/2015 Judgment accompany victim while she was proceeding for examination. But, the victim used to be returned alone. On 3.3.2014, while returning from examination, accused Vishnu followed her and gave whistles and this fact was stated by victim to her. Her husband approached accused Vishnu and convinced him. She has further stated that her daughter used to go alone to the school. Informant had also stated that the accused used to board the same bus of the victim and used to occupy front or rear seat. According to her, other two accused also used to be with Vishnu. Vishnu used to ask her daughter to reply his question and this fact was narrated by victim to her. This witness is also cross­examined by the accused. But, her evidence is also not shaken on material points. It is just brought on record that on a day before the day of report i.e. on 19.11.2014, there was one programme of Gondhal­Jagran in the adjoining house of the victim where the sound services of accused Vishnu were availed. The suggestion is given that she insisted accused Vishnu to minimize the sound. 14] Another attempt is made to raise a defence by giving suggestion that on a day before the day of report, accused Vishnu assaulted the son of her husband's sister. It is brought on record that no complaint was filed in respect of the assault by Vishnu. A suggestion is given that this report is filed so as to give counterblast to the incident dtd. 19.11.2014 in which accused Vishnu had assaulted son of her husband's sister. But, only to implicate the accused in respect of beating dtd. 19.11.2014, no person will file 12 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 87/2015 Judgment such a complaint involving a daughter. So, there is no substance in the defence. Her version appears to be cogent and reliable. It is to be noted that Shilpa has not seen the incident. But, it is but natural on the part of the victim to disclose about the act of the accused to P.W.2 Shilpa who is her mother. The discussion above lead me to say that the evidence of victim and victim's mother appears to be cogent and convincing and it is inspiring the confidence of the court to hold that accused Vishnu has followed, contacted or attempted to contact the victim to foster personal interaction repeatedly though there was clear indication of disinterest by the victim. Hence, the accused Vishnu has committed an offence under Sec. 354­(D)(1)(i) of Indian Penal Code. 15] It is also to be noted that in the first part i.e. during the examination of 10th standard, absolutely no allegation against accused Prakash is made in the report Exh.11. Though the allegation as to following victim is made against all the accused in the report Exh.11 when she was proceeding to college, victim has only alleged about following her against accused Vishnu and Shrikant. But the evidence of the victim also shows that the exact role of accused Shrikant is not given except a version that Shrikant also used to board a bus and used to sing a song. Victim has specifically stated about the act of Vishnu following her in school and in college and also about holding her bag and asking her to reply the question. So, I find that the prosecution failed to establish 13 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 87/2015 Judgment offence under Sec. 354­(D)(1)(i) against accused Prakash and Shrikant. Therefore, I answer point No.1 accordingly. AS TO POINT NO.4:­ 16] In order to establish the guilt under Sec. 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, it is for the prosecution to establish that the accused has committed sexual harassment upon a child. Sec. 11(4) of this Act says about the repeated and constant following of a child by direct means or by electronic mode or by any other means. It is discussed in the foregoing paragraphs that the accused Vishnu used to follow her and contact her repeatedly. But the most important aspect so as to prove offence under Sec. 12 of POCSO Act is that the accused has committed this act with sexual intent. Victim has stated that she was proceeding by bus to the college. Accused used to board the same bus and at that time, accused Vishnu used to hold her hand or bag and used to ask her to reply his question. Victim had not mentioned specifically in the report ( Exh.11 ) about holding of her hand. This act of the accused Vishnu was having relation with the earlier act as he has stated the victim that he likes her and to give reply to his question. Recitals of the report ( Exh.11 ) does not reveal about physical contact. Merely asking the victim to give reply to his question, in my mind, can not be said to be an act of following victim with sexual intent. Reliance also can be place on judgment of Hon'ble High Court in case of Bandu Vithhalrao Borwar V/s. State of 14 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 87/2015 Judgment Maharashtra in Criminal Appeal No.50 of 2016, dtd. 17.10.2016. It is held in Paragraph No.10 of the Judgment that; “After all intention of a person is his state of mind and has to be discerned from the surrounding facts and circumstances. If one cannot, as a human being, physically enter into a mind of another to read and see what is being cooked there, one can surely know it by evaluating all that which is perceivable or felt by human senses such as words, body­ language, gestures, reactions and everything that is a physical manifestation of working of human mind. If somebody says that he is in love with another person or asks another person as to why the other person does not love him , such expression of a feeling or expectation of a particular feeling from another person would not by itself amount to an intent exhibiting some sort of sexuality.” It is also held in paragraph No. 11 that ; “It is obvious that the intent, which is nothing but a state of mind, must be to establish some sort of physical contact or must be related to or associated with sex or indicative of involvement of sex in the relationship, if it is to be considered as sexual. I have already stated that the utterance indicating an expectation of a person that the other person should love him would not by itself amount to sexual intent as contemplated by the legislature. There should be something more which must suggest that the real intention is to drag in the angle of sex, if the words uttered are to be taken as conveying sexual intent.” 15 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 87/2015 Judgment 17] In this matter, it is already discussed that victim has not stated about physical contact by accused Vishnu in the report (Exh.11). Victim has stated that while boarding the bus, accused used to hold either her hand or her bag. But, her mother P.W.2 Shilpa has not stated that the victim stated her about holding her hand by accused Vishnu during this incident. For the reasons stated above, it is difficult to accept that the said act of following the victim was with sexual intent. Hence, all the accused can not be held guilty for the offence under Sec. 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Therefore, I answer point No.4 in the negative. AS TO POINT NOS.2 & 3 :­ 18] In order to prove offence under Sec. 341, prosecution has to establish that the accused has obstructed the victim so as to prevent from proceeding in particular direction. It is to be noted that victim has just stated that during the examination of 10 th standard, accused told her in the way that he likes her and to give reply to his question. She has stated that she will narrate this fact to her father. She has nowhere stated that at that time she was obstructed by the accused so as to prevent her to proceed further. Even the recitals of the report (Exh.11) also does not show that victim was prevented to go ahead. Victim has also stated that while alighting from the bus, accused Vishnu used to ask to respond his question. She used to ignore it and used to go to college. So, it also does not reveal that accused obstructed her or prevented her in a 16 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 87/2015 Judgment manner that she may not proceed in a direction to which she has right. 19] In order to establish the guilt under Sec. 506, the prosecution also required to establish that the accused have threatened to cause injury to person, reputation or property of informant and so as to cause that person to do any act which she is not legally bound to do or to cause him to omit to do an act which that person is legally entitled to do. Victim has just stated that on 20.11.2014, she was proceeding to college. On that day, she stated Vishnu not to follow her. Then Vishnu has stated that ^^rq tkLr cksyk;yk ykxyh vkgsl] rqyk tkLr eLrh vkyh vkgs**- The words ^^rqyk tkLr eLrh vkyh vkgs** allegedly uttered by accused Vishnu are not stated in report Exh.11. These words does not indicate that either accused Vishnu has attempted to intimidate to cause any injury. Evidence of victim's mother Shilpa also does not reveal that on 20.11.2014, accused had threatened her to cause injury to her person or reputation. So, the evidence of victim falls short to prove the guilt under Sec. 506 of Indian penal Code. Therefore, I find that prosecution for want of satisfactory evidence failed to establish the offence under Sec. 341, 506 r/w. 34 of Indian Penal code. Hence, I answer point Nos.2 and 3 in the negative. 20] Since accused Vishnu is held guilty for the offence under Sec. 354­(D)(1)(i) of Indian Penal code, he has to be heard on the point of sentence. 17 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 87/2015 Judgment 21] I have heard accused and his advocate on the point of sentence. It is submitted to take lenient view considering the young age of the accused. On the other hand, Ld. A.P.P. has submitted that if only on the ground of young age lenient view is taken, then it would lead to wrong message in the society. There is no need to take lenient view. It is already discussed that the accused Vishnu had repeatedly followed the victim though there was indication of disinterest. Considering all these facts, I am not inclined to grant benefit of Probation of Offenders Act. While striking the balance, age of victim also can not be ignored. Incident is occurred at her age of 16 years. In order to check such type of increasing offence, I am not inclined to take lenient view. 22] Punishment which is prescribed for the offence under Sec. 354­(D) is imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years and shall also liable to fine in case of first conviction. Accused has submitted that he is not convicted earlier in similar type of case. The prosecution has also not brought any material to show that he is already convicted. Considering these facts, I am of the opinion that following order will meet ends of justice. Hence, following order: ORDER 1] Accused No.1 Vishnu Suresh patil is convicted under Sec. 235(2) of Code of Criminal Procedure of the offence punishable under Section 354­(D)(1)(i) of Indian Penal Code 18 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 87/2015 Judgment and is sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 1 ½ year and to pay fine of Rs. 1,000/­ i.d. to suffer simple imprisonment for three months. 2] Accused No. 1 Vishnu Suresh Patil is acquitted under Sec. 235(1) of Code of Criminal Procedure of the offence punishable under Sec. 341, 506 r/w. 34 of Indian Penal Code and Sec. 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 3] Accused No.2 Prakash Suresh Patil and No. 3 Shrikant Sachin Mayekar are acquitted under Sec. 235(1) of Code of Criminal Procedure of the offence punishable under Sec. 354­(D)(1) (i), 341, 506 r/w. 34 of Indian Penal Code and Sec.12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 4] Bail bonds of all accused stand cancelled. 5] Accused No.1 Vishnu Suresh Patil is entitled for set off under Sec. 428 of Criminal Procedure Code, if any as per rule. 6] Accused Nos.2 and 3 shall furnish P.B. and S.B. of Rs. 5000/­ each as per Sec.437­A of Code of Criminal Procedure. [ Dictated and pronounced in open Court. ] Thane, ( Ashutosh N. Karmarkar ) Date : 28.02.2017 District Judge­1 & Special Judge (POCSO) Act,Thane 19 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 87/2015 Judgment

1 Spl.Case No. 100/2014 [ Judg. ] Received On : 06/05/2014 Registered On : 06/05/2014 Decided On : 14/03/2017 Duration : Y M D 2 10 9 Exh. No. IN THE COURT OF ADDITIONAL SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE ( Presided Over By N.N. Shrimangale ) SPECIAL CASE NO. 100 OF 2014 State of Maharashtra ( Through N.R.I.Sagari Police Station, Dist­Thane ) ...Complainant. ( Cr. No. I­134/2013 ) Versus Mohammad Mustafa Abdul Gafur Shahabadi, Age­ 40, R/at: Chita Camp, Trombay, Mankhurd, Mumbai. …Accused. –­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ Offences punishable under sec. 354 of the Indian Penal Code and under secs.7,8, & 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. –­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ Shri V.G. Kadu, Ld. APP for the State Smt.Jyoti Patil, Ld. Adv. for Accused –­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ 2 Spl.Case No. 100/2014 [ Judg. ] JUDGMENT ( Delivered On this 14th day of March, 2017 ) 1] The accused is chargesheeted of the offences punishable under section 354 of the Indian penal Code and Secs. 7,8 & 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act. 2] The prosecution case in short is that, on 11/11/2013 at about 8 pm. The complainant Dharmesh Narendra Batawiya had been to the shoes shop of the accused, with his daughter Yeshvi aged about 12 yrs. to purchase shoes for her. The accused showed shoes to Yeshvi. Said Yeshvi put on shoes and then the accused called Yeshvi in inner portion of the said shop under the pretext to check the shoes. When Yeshvi went in the inner portion of the shop, the accused did unwarranted activity with the girl Yeshvi. But Yeshvi did not tell about it to the complainant her father. So the complainant reached Yeshwi to the house. Then Yeshvi, the victim girl started to weep before her mother and narrated the facts of the unwarranted behaviours of the accused to her mother. So, the wife of the complainant told to the complainant on phone about the incident. Complainant went to his house and then Yeshvi told about the incident of moving hand on her person by the accused and about his pulling her to him. Then the complainant went 3 Spl.Case No. 100/2014 [ Judg. ] to the said shop and told about the incident to the employer of the accused. 3] On the very day complaint came to be lodged with N.R.I. Police Station about the incident by Dharmesh, the father of the victim girl Yeshvi. 4] On the strength of the same complaint , the police registered the crime at C.R.No.I­ 134/2013 registered under Section 354 of the Indian penal Code. 5] The police carried out the investigation and filed the chargesheet against the accused under Section 354 of the Indian penal Code and Secs. 7,8 & 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act. 6] The accused appeared before the Court. The charge under Section 354 of the Indian penal Code and Secs. 7,8 & 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act came to be framed at Exh.4. The contents of the said charge came to be read over and explained to the accused in vernacular to which the accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. The defence of the accused is of total denial. 7] As to prove the charge, the prosecution examined 4 Spl.Case No. 100/2014 [ Judg. ] the complainant P.W.1 Dharmesh Narendrabhai Batawiya, the father of the victim girl Yeshvi at Exh.9, P.W.2­ Miss.Yeshvi Dharmesh Batawiya, the victim girl at Exh.12 and P.W.3­ Mrs. Meenal Dharmesh Batawiya, the mother of the victim girl at Exh.13. 8] After examination of P.W.3 Meenal the evidence of the prosecution came to be claosed. 9] I recorded the statement of the accused U/Sec. 313(1)(c) of Cr.P.C. In his statement the accused did not give explanation as to why the present complaint came to be filed against him and why the prosecution witnesses are stating against him. 10] I heard the Ld.Adv. Smt.Jyoti Patil for the accused and the Ld.A.P.P.Shri.Kadu for the State. 11] Following points arise for my determination and I have mentioned my findings against each of them for the reasons stated therefor. POINTS FINDINGS 1] Whether prosecution proves that, on 11/11/2013 at 21.10 hours at Inmode Shoes Mall, Sector 42, Seawood, Nerul, Navi Mumbai, within the jurisdiction In the negative. of N.R.I. Sagari police station, 5 Spl.Case No. 100/2014 [ Judg. ] Navi Mumbai, the accused used criminal force to daughter of complainant namely Kumari Yeshvi Dharmesh Batawiya aged 12 yrs. intending to outrage her modesty and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 354 of the Indian Penal Code ? 2] Whether prosecution proves that, on the aforesaid date, time and place the accused committed sexual assault on daughter of complainant namely Kumari Yeshvi Dharmesh Batawiya aged In the negative. 12 yrs. and thereby committed an offences punishable under sections 7,8 & 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 ? 3] What order ? As per final order. REASONS 12] Before going to discuss the points, I think it would be just and proper to reproduce Sec.7 & 11 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, which reads as under : Section 7: Whoever, with sexual intent touches the vagina, penis,anus or breast of the child or makes the child touch the vagina, penis, anus or breast of such person or any other person, or does any other Act with 6 Spl.Case No. 100/2014 [ Judg. ] sexual intent which involves physical contact without penetration is said to commit sexual assault. Section 11 : A person is said to commit sexual harassment upon a child which such person with sexual intent, (i) utters any word or makes any sound, or makes any gesture or exhibits any object or part of body with the intention that such word or sound shall be heard, or such gesture or object or part of body shall be seen by the child; ­­­­­­­­­ 13] On bare perusal of Sec.7 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 , it is expected that the accused must have intention to cause sexual harassment of a minor child and for that it is expected to touch the vagina, penis, anus or breast of the child. As to attract Sec.11 of the said act, the accused must utter the word or do the gestures or exhibits object or part of his body with the intention that the said word should be heard or such gestures or body should be seen by said child. Considering these contents of Sec.7 & 11 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 , I have to assess the evidence of the prosecution evidence on record. 14] AS TO POINT NOS.1 AND 2 :­ Both the points being interlinked, I have taken them together for my determination as to avoid repetition of same reasonings. 7 Spl.Case No. 100/2014 [ Judg. ] 15] On perusal of the evidence of P.W.1­ Dharmesh and P.W.3 Meenal it is explicit that, they did not see the accused while doing bad conduct with Yeshvi likely to outrage her modesty or causing her sexual harassment. 16] It is also material to consider that as per the evidence of P.W.1­ Dharmesh examined at Exh.9 that after purchasing shoes for Yeshvi from the shop of the accused, the victim girl Yeshvi went with P.W.1 Dharmesh to the house. This victim girl Yeshvi did not state anything about the incident to her father in the shop of the accused , as well as while coming to her house with her father,P.W.1 Dharmesh from the shop of the accused. Considering the evidence of P.W.2 Yeshvi examined at Exh.12, it appears to me that the victim girl Yeshvi being scared she did not dare to tell about the incident to her father immediately after occurrence of the incident at the hands of the accused. The contention of the victim girl Yeshvi for not telling about the incident to her father does not look me acceptable. The reason is that when her father was with her , she was not expected to shy to disclose the facts of the incident immediately after occurring the same with her at the hands of the accused. 17] Moreover, the victim girl Yeshvi is examined at Exh.12. She herself has stated in her examination­in­chief 8 Spl.Case No. 100/2014 [ Judg. ] itself that the size of the store room was small one and when she was coming out of store room/partition, there is likelyhood of receiving the dash of the hands of the accused. This contention of the victim girl is sufficient that even if she would have received the dash of the hands of the accused there was no intention of the accused to outrage the modesty of the victim girl Yeshvi. 18] The victim girl Yeshvi also stated in her cross­ examination that when she came out of the store room/ partition after putting the said shoes on, the accused was taking some shoes from the storeroom. Then due to the narrow space in between the store room/partition and front portion of the said shop, she received the dash of the accused. It means there was no malafide intention on the part of the accused to cause modesty to the victim girl Yeshvi by touching to her body. 19] Ld.A.P.P. tried to submit before the Court that in his statement the accused has stated something against his interest. Saying something against interest of an accused is no garb to convict the accused, but it may be a corroborative ground to support the prosecution case. Here, in this case, the prosecution is failed to prove the charges levelled against the accused. 9 Spl.Case No. 100/2014 [ Judg. ] 20] P.W.3 Meenal examined at Exh.13 who is the mother of the victim girl Yeshvi is also not supporting the prosecution case. 21] Sec.7 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 makes it explicit that the accused should touch some particular part of a body of the victim girl which is likely to cause molestation to the victim girl. But, here in this case in complaint proved at Exh.10, there is no specific mentioning about any part of the victim girl which was touched by the accused as to outrage her modesty. 22] The prosecution witnesses i.e. P.W.1­Dharmesh and P.W.3­ Meenal have stated that the matter is settled between them and they d0 not want to proceed the matter against the accused. Moreover, thye victim girl Yeshvi was aged about 12 yrs. At the time of incident and she was school going girl. So, she is expected to have understanding capacity. But, the victim girl Yeshvi did not support to the prosecution case, as she has not stated that the accused outraged her modesty or he caused molestation to her by holding her hands. So, there is no iota of evidence against the accused to hold that the charges levelled against the accused are proved. So, I record my findings to point Nos.1 & 2 in the negative. 10 Spl.Case No. 100/2014 [ Judg. ] 23] Considering my findings to point Nos.1 & 2 in the negative and the reasons stated therefor, the accused is entitled to acquittal of the offences punishable U/Sec.354 of I.P.C. and Secs. 7,8 & 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Hence, I proceed to pass the following order : ORDER 1. The accused Mohammad Mushtafa Abdul Gafur Shahabadi is hereby acquitted as per the provision under section 235(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure of the offences punishable under Section 354 of the Indian Penal Code and under Sections 7, 8 & 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act. 2. The bail bond executed by the accused stand cancelled. Surety is discharged. 3. The accused is directed to furnish fresh P.B. & S.B. of Rs.5,000/­ in compliance with the provisions of section 437(A) of Cr.P.C. to abide himself to appear before Appellate Court in case of appeal is preferred by the prosecution. Thane (N.N. Shrimangale) Date:­14/3/2017 District Judge–4 & Addl. Sessions Judge & Special Judge, Thane

IN THE COURT OF THE SPECIAL JUDGE (P.O.C.S.O.ACT), THANE. (Presided over by Ms.U.M.Nandeshwar, District Judge­1 & Addl. Sessions Judge, Thane) SPECIAL CASE No. 102 of 2014 Exhibit No.28. The State of Maharashtra Through Rabale Police Station District – Thane. ... Prosecution versus Saurabh Narsinh Joshi Age 27 years, Residence –Colony Ashram near Nimkar society,Mulund colony(W) Dist. Thane. ... Accused Offence punishable under section 354­A & 354­B of Indian Penal Code and under section 8 & 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Appearance ­ Spl.P.P. Mrs.S.E.Phad Mrs. R.A. Navale, for the State. Advocate Mr. N.W.Gaikwad, for the Accused. 2 Special Case No. 102/2014 (Judgment) JUDGMENT (Delivered on 6th May, 2016.) 1] The Accused stands prosecuted for the offence punishable under section 354­A & 354­B of Indian Penal Code and also under section 8 & 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act) for causing sexual harassment to minor victim­girl aged about 4½ years. 2] Shorn of verbiage, the indictment against the Accused are as under ­ [i] Informant Ashwini N. Mane (P.W.1) is resident of Airoli, Navi Mumbai. The victim­girl aged about 4½ years is her daughter and studying in D.A.V. Public School in Jr. K.G.. The victim­girl was having vacation since 06/03/2014. On 10/03/2014 around 05.00 p.m. The victim­girl had been to play in the court­yard. However, around 06.00 p.m., the informant could not find her daughter/victim­girl with the other boys who were playing in court­yard. The informant also heard the noise of children from 'C' wing of the building, therefore, she went there. There she had noticed that one person had put his hand in the pant of her daughter victim­girl and doing some obscene act. The informant asked her daughter what that person was doing with her. On that victim­girl told that said person by inserting his hand in her 3 Special Case No. 102/2014 (Judgment) pant was asking her “whether you liked it” (Tula Chaan wat­te ka?). Therefore, informant disclosed the incident to her brother and mother and thereafter, by caught holding that person went to the police station, where the name of the person was learnt as Saurabh Joshi(Accused). Therefore, the informant lodged report against him. 3] On her report F.I.R. was registered against the Accused vide C.R.No.I­62/2014 for the offence punishable under section 354­B of I.P.C. and 8 and 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. The investigation was carried out by A.P.I. Adinath Gawade (P.W.2). The Accused was arrested. The spot panchnama was drawn in presence of panchas. Statements of witnesses were recorded. Medical certificates of victim­girl and accused were collected. The statement of victim­girl was recorded as per her say in question­answer form. Thereafter, investigation culminated into filing of charge­sheet in this Court being the Special designated court under P.O.C.S.O. Act. 4] The charge (Exh.4) was framed against the Accused for offence punishable under section 354­A & 354­B of Indian Penal Code and also under section 8 & 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. The Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial (Exh.5). The Accused took defence of total denial. 5] In response to application under section 294 of 4 Special Case No. 102/2014 (Judgment) Cr.P.C. the defence has admitted spot panchnama [Exh.18], Medical certificates of victim­girl dated 10/03/2014 [Exh.14] and medical certificate of accused [Exh.15]. 6] In order to prove guilt of the Accused Prosecution has examined following witnesses ­ P.W.1 Ashwini Navnath Mane Exh.12 Informant /mother of victim­girl. P.W.2 A.P.I. Adinath Ananda Gawade Exh.20 (Investigating officer) 7] The prosecution proved and relied on the report / F.I.R. [Exh.21 & 22]. 8] The prosecution closed its side of evidence by filing Pursis at Exhibit­25. The incriminating evidence came on record against the Accused was read over and explained to him in vernacular and his statement under Section 313(b) of Cr.P.C. was recorded vide Exh.27. Accused neither examined himself nor examined any witness in his defence. 9] Heard learned A.P.P. Mrs. R. A. Navale for State and the learned Advocate Mr. B.W.Gaikwad for Accused. 10] On consideration of argument advanced on behalf of both the sides and on perusal of the oral & documentary 5 Special Case No. 102/2014 (Judgment) evidence on record, following points arise for my determination, which are answered with the findings thereon, as under :­ Sr. Points Findings No. 1] Does the prosecution prove that on 10/03/2014 in the passage of Iden Park society B wing, Airoli in between 17.30 to 18.00 hours Accused committed ..No. sexual assault to victim­girl aged 4½ years by disrobing her and he thereby committed an offence punishable under section 354­A & 354­B of Indian Penal Code ? 2] Does the prosecution prove that during same period accused committed sexual assault on the victim­girl in above given manner and thereby he committed an ...No. offence punishable under section 12 of the P.O.C.S.O. Act? 3] What order ? Accused is acquitted. REASONS As to Point No.1 to 3 : 11] All the points are taken up together for discussion, to avoid the repetition, as evidence about the same is common and inter­connected. 6 Special Case No. 102/2014 (Judgment) 12] As the Accused is facing charge under section 354­A & 354­B of I.P.C. it is incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that the Accused outrage the modesty of minor victim­girl aged about 4½ years by disrobbing and putting his hand in her underwear and doing some obscene act. So also as the Accused is facing charge under section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, therefore, it is further incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that the accused has committed sexual harassment to the victim­girl with sexual intent, either utters any word or makes any sound, or makes any gesture or exhibits any object or part of body with the intention that such work or sound shall be heard, or such gesture or object or part of body shall be seen by the child; or repeatedly or constantly follows or watches or contact a child either directly or through electronic, digital or any other means etc. as defined in section 11 of the Protection Of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2002 (P.O.C.S.O. Act). Age of victim­girl : 13] As the Accused is facing charge under P.O.C.S.O. Act, therefore, first of all it is incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that the victim­girl was child (minor) at the time of incident. The alleged incident took place on 10/03/2014. The informant (P.W.1) who is the mother of victim­girl stated the date of birth of victim­girl as 15/06/2009 7 Special Case No. 102/2014 (Judgment) and at the time of incident she was 4½ years and studying in Jr. K.G. in D.A.V Public School. The victim­girl was not examined, as her mother/informant was reluctant to bring the victim­girl in the Court. However, the medical certificate of the victim­girl is on record wherein her age is stated as 5 years. Further the defence did not challenge the age of the victim­girl and therefore, there is no hurdle to hold that victim­girl was minor aged about 4½ years i.e. below the age of 18 years and she was a “child” as per definition given in Section 2(d) of P.O.C.S.O. Act. 14] To prove the charge against the Accused the most material witnesses were victim­girl and her mother/informant (P.W.1). However, as the informant/ mother of victim­girl (P.W.1) is reluctant to keep victim­girl present before the court for evidence, the prosecution could not examine the victim­girl and even considering the tender age of the victim­girl, no coercive steps were taken to secure her presence for recording her evidence. Further the informant/mother of victim­girl (P.W.1) did not support the case of prosecution and failed to identify the accused. Therefore, the prosecution, with the permission of the Court, cross­examined the informant/ mother of victim­girl at length. But nothing material is brought on record to prove the charge leveled against the accused. The material portion wherein there are allegations that the informant has witnessed that accused had put his 8 Special Case No. 102/2014 (Judgment) hand in the pant of victim­girl and doing some obscene act, which was proved through the investigating officer (P.W.2). However, as the material witness did not support the prosecution, therefore, the evidence of the investigating officer would of the least help to the prosecution. Even the medical certificate of the victim­girl which is at Exh.14 did not reveal any injury over private part or breast and thus, there is absolutely no evidence against the accused to prove charge against him. 15] Thus, the prosecution failed to prove that the Accused used criminal force and committed sexual assault on minor victim­girl aged about 4½ years by disrobing her. Hence, I answer point No.1 & 2 in negative. Therefore, in absence of any evidence against the Accused, he is entitled for acquittal. 16] In the result, I proceed to pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused Saurabh Narsinh Joshi is hereby acquitted U/Sec. 235(1) of Cr.P.C. for the offence punishable U/Sec.354­A & 354­B of Indian Penal Code and U/s. 8 & 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] His bail bonds stand cancelled and sureties are discharged. 9 Special Case No. 102/2014 (Judgment) 3] The Accused shall furnish personal bond of ₹15,000/­in compliance of provision of Section 437­A of Cr.P.C. The judgment is dictated and pronounced in open Court. Date :06/05/2016. (Ms. U. M. Nandeshwar), Thane Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act),Thane. District Judge ­1 and Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

--1-- ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN CRIMINAL BAIL APPLICATION NO.1038/2018 CNR NO.MHTH01­002944­2018 The applicant Vikas Kashinath Patil has applied for bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C., in C.R. No.I­12/2018 registered in Bhiwandi Taluka police station for the offence under section 376 (2)(i)(n) of IPC and Section 4, 8 of POCSO Act, 2012. 2. It is contended that the applicant is falsely implicated. There is delay of five days in filing FIR. Investigation is practically completed. The accused is permanent resident of the given address. He is young and looking to age, career and future, he may be released on bail on condition. 3. Investigating Officer has given his say at Exh.4. 4. I heard Ld. Counsel on behalf of accused and Ld. APP. 5. The case of prosecution is that the two accused persons including this applicant committed penetrative sexual assault upon two minor victims aged 6 years. The name of this applicant is mentioned in the FIR as well as statements of the victims recorded under section 161 and 164 of Cr. P.C. The medical examination of the two victims is done. It is alleged that the accused induced the victim for giving money for eatables and committed penetrative sexual assault. The accused is the uncle of the victim. There is statement of eye witness, who has seen while accused taking the victim. There is one witness who had seen the accused was going with the victim on the terrace of the house of one witness. The court is of the view that there is strong prima facie case made out against accused. It is heinous crime committed upon victim aged --2-- below 12 years. There are eye witnesses. There is medical certificate. There is statement recorded of victim under section 164 of Cr. P.C. so prima facie strong case made out against the accused. If accused is released on bail he is likely to tamper the prosecution witnesses and victim and it will affect merit of the case. So considering nature of offence and punishment provided for the offence it is not desirable to release the accused on bail. .. 1 .. bail no.1064/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 1064/2015 This application is filed by applicant Deepak Dinesh Adilwal for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. I­92/2015 registered at Navghar police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 363, 366(A), 376(i)(n) of I.P.C. and section 4, 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant kidnapped the minor victim girl and then had forcible sexual intercourse with her by giving false assurance of marriage. It is further contended and argued that no such incident of kidnapping has taken place and the girl herself had left the house without knowledge of the applicant. It is further contended and argued that there was love affair between the girl and the applicant and parents of the girl were against their love affair and therefore due to pressure of the parents, the girl has falsely implicated the applicant in this crime. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co­operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that the accused and the victim were knowing each other and he had enticed her and taking disadvantage of minor age of the victim the accused gave false promise of marriage to her and kidnapped her and took .. 2 .. bail no.1064/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) her to Tamil Nadu State and there at different places he had committed forcible sexual intercourse with her. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl and the prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 363, 366(A), 376(i)(n) of I.P.C. and section 4, 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act with the allegation that he kidnapped the minor girl who is stated to be 13 years old by inducing her and then raped her time and again. But then it is contended on behalf of accused that the girl had left the house of her own without knowledge of the applicant and when the parents of the girl came to know about her whereabouts, they brought her back and forced her to falsely implicate the applicant in this crime. In such circumstance though the girl is stated to be below 18 years of age, the consent of minor is immaterial, still the aspect of proof of age of the girl and also as to whether the act of the accused amounts to rape or whether it is a case of consent, would be the question to be decided on merits. Even nothing is stated to be recovered from the applicant/accused. 4] It is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any .. 3 .. bail no.1064/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. 5] In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 6] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 7] Then, it has also to be mentioned that looking the allegations against the accused the investigation in the matter may have almost completed but the charge sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 8] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is allowed. .. 4 .. bail no.1064/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Applicant/accused Deepak Dinesh Adilwal is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ The applicant/accused shall attend the concerned police station on every Monday between 10.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon till filing of the charge sheet and shall co­operate in investigation. He shall not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and the prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this Court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 21.05.2015. Act). 2] Heard learned Advocate Mrs. Reena Korde for the applicant/accused and learned Spl.P.P.Mrs.R.A.Navale for State. I.O.absent. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 21/04/2016 at the instance of the informant/mother of victim­girl aged about 8 years with an indictment that on 19/04/2016 around 11.00 a.m. accused inappropriately touched the minor victim­girl aged about 8 years and asked her to hold his penis and caused sexual harassment to her. 2 Bail No.1053/2016 (order below Exhibit 1) 4] The learned Counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant/accused is/ are falsely implicated. He is ready to abide any condition imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing them on bail. 5] Per contra, the learned Spl.P.P. opposed the application submitting that conduct of such senior citizen is very objectionable. Presented on­ 28.04.2015. Registered on­ 28.04.2015. Decided on­ 02.08.2018. Duration­ Y­ 3 M­3 D­4 IN THE COURT OF SESSIONS, THANE, AT THANE. (Before V.Y. Jadhav, Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.) SPECIAL CASE (POCSO) NO. 89 OF 2015 CNR : MHTH01­002968­2015 Exh. No. The State (Through Rabale M.I.D.C. Police Station) ..Prosecution V/s. Vijay Sarjerao Kolse, Age 22 years, Occ. Nil, R/o. Room No. 7, Saisadan chawl, Bindumadhav nagar, Digha, Navi Mumbai. ..Accused. Appearance :­ ___________________________________________________________ For State : P.P. Smt. S.E. Phad. For Accused : Adv. Smt. Reena Korde. ___________________________________________________________ JUDGMENT (Delivered on 02.08.2018.) 1] Accused Vijay Sarjerao Kolse is facing charge for the offence punishable u/s. 376, 506 of I.P.C. and sec. 4(l), 6 of the Protection of 2 POCSO Case. No. 89/2015. Children From Sexual Offences Act. The prosecution case in nut­shell is as follows : 2] That the victim aged 17 years is elder daughter of the informant. The informant and her husband used to go for work by leaving the victim and other children at home. The victim used to stay at home while other two children were studying in school. 3] On 26.09.2013, the informant and her husband left home for work. At about 4.00 p.m., the informant went to Virar to see daughter of neighbourer Suvarna Salvi. At about 6.00 p.m., other neighbourer Kashinath Bhoir called the informant on phone and informed that one boy had entered in the house of informant and the door was closed from inside. Therefore, the informant returned home immediately. On arrival, she was informed by Bhoir and Baban Salvi that her daughter i.e. victim and accused Vijay Kolse were inside the house by closing the door and in spite of knocking the door, they did not open it. Therefore, they have informed to Rabale M.I.D.C. police station about it and thereafter, police took both of them to police station. 4] Thereafter, the informant went to police station. On enquiry with her daughter, she came to know that the accused is friend of victim. He came in the house of the informant at noon when the siblings of the victim were at school. Finding the victim alone at home, the accused made demand of physical intimacy. However, the informant expressed her inability. However, the accused had forcible physical relationship with the victim and after the intercourse, he had threatened the victim for life, if she would tell about the same to anybody. Accordingly, the informant lodged F.I.R. Exh. 75 with Rabale M.I.D.C. police station. According to said 3 POCSO Case. No. 89/2015. F.I.R., C.R. No. 87/2013 came to be registered with M.I.D.C. police station. A.P.I. Rahul Khatal conducted investigation of the same. After completion of investigation, he filed charge­sheet against the accused for the offence punishable u/s. 376, 506 of I.P.C. and u/s. 4(l) and 6 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 5] Charge came to be framed against the accused vide Exh.7. The contents of charge were read over and explained to the accused by my learned predecessor in vernacular, to which the accused pleaded not guilty and claimed for trial. 6] In order to prove the prosecution case, the prosecution has examined in all six witnesses i.e. 1] father of victim at Exh. 8, 2] Baban Sripat Salvi at Exh. 9, 3] Sunil Mahadev Shirsat at Exh. 11, 4] mother of victim at Exh. 14, 5] the victim at Exh. 16, and 6] Rahul Somnath Khatal at Exh. 18. 7] The prosecution has also relied upon the following documents­ 1] F.I.R. at Exh. 15, 2] Arrest panchanama of accused at Exh.17, 3] Medical certificate of accused at Exh. 19, 4] Medical certificate of victim at Exh. 20, 5] Portion marked 'A' out of statement of the informant at Exh. 21, 6] Seizure panchanama at Exh. 12, 7] Spot and seizure panchanama at Exh. 13, 8] Photo­copy of school­leaving certificate of victim at Exh. 23, 9] C.A. report of clothes of victim and accused at Exh. 24. 4 POCSO Case. No. 89/2015. 8] Thereafter, vide pursis at Exh. 25, the prosecution closed the evidence. 9] Statement of accused u/s. 313 of Cr.P.C. came to be recorded to the extent of only incriminating material against him. The defence of the accused is of total denial and false implication. 10] Heard learned P.P. Smt. Phad for the State and learned counsel Smt. Reena Korde for the accused. 11] Following points emerged for my consideration and I have recorded my findings thereon for the reasons given below. Points Findings 1] Whether the prosecution has proved No. that on 26.09.13, in between 15 hours to 17 hours, the accused entered in the house of the informant and committed penetrative sexual assault on the daughter of informant ? 2] Whether the prosecution has proved No. that the accused threatened the victim for life, if she would inform about the incident of rape to anybody ? 3] What order ? As per final order. REASONS 12] Ld. P.P. submitted that though in the present case, the victim and her mother have not supported the prosecution version about the incident of sexual assault and criminal intimidation. However, if the F.I.R. Exh. 15 would perused, the averments about sexual assault and threat are 5 POCSO Case. No. 89/2015. mentioned in the same. Similarly, in the evidence of P.W.1, father of the victim, he has deposed that his daughter informed him that the accused raped her. In such circumstances, there is sufficient evidence to convict the accused for the offence punishable u/s. 376, 506 of I.P.C. and section 4(1), 6 of POCSO Act. Hence, he may be convicted and sentenced for maximum imprisonment prescribed for the said offence. 13] On the other hand, Ld. Counsel Smt. Reena Korde for accused submitted that in the present case, the informant herself has disowned the allegations in the F.I.R. about sexual relations as well as criminal intimidation. It is mentioned in the evidence of P.W.4 the informant that the accused only came to the house of informant. However, she has denied the specific suggestions by Ld. A.P.P. about forceful physical relationship or about criminal intimidation. Similarly, the victim who is P.W.5, has also denied any such incident. In such circumstances, when the victim as well as her mother who are the material witnesses, have denied occurrence of alleged incident and averments in the F.I.R. to that effect. The accused requires to be acquitted from the charges. 14] She further submitted that it is not the case that the victim or the witnesses were pressurized or for any other reason, they have resiled from their statements. Factually, no incident of physical relationship had occurred. However, only due to arrival of neighbours and knocking the doors, the victim got frightened. It has in fact, came on record that the neighbours called police and handed over accused and victim to the police. The fact that the accused was in the house of victim, has not denied by anybody. However, as deposed by the victim herself, she called the accused at her house. Therefore, even an offence of house trespass or any other offence would not be made out against the accused and he is required 6 POCSO Case. No. 89/2015. to be honourably acquitted. 15] In the light of above submissions, it is necessary to scrutinize the material on record. 16] It has come in the evidence of P.W.1 Suresh Khandekar that victim is his daughter. This witness and his wife used to go for work. As the victim was not studying, she used to look after the other children of the couple. On 26.09.13, as usual, he went for work. At about 6.00 to 6.30 p.m., Pawan Salvi called him and informed that the accused is present in his house and this witness was asked to come to police station. He was told that his daughter and accused Vijay Kolse had been to their house and it was told by his daughter that accused had committed rape on her. During his cross­examination, he admitted that there is a road in front of his house. There are rooms of others on left and right side of his house. He admitted that people use the said road even in between 3.00 p.m. to 5.00 p.m. During that period, if a person enters into house, then on shout, the neighbours would gather. He deposed that his daughter did not raise hue and cry after entrance of accused. Rather, she told that she had called him in the house and there was love affair between them. She also stated that accused had not committed forcible sexual intercourse with her. 17] P.W.2 Baban Sripati Salvi deposed that on 26.09.13 when he returned from work, at that time, people gathered near room of Suresh Khandekar. Therefore, he went there. Door of room of Suresh Khandekar was closed. He called at Rabale police station. Police came there and opened the door. Accused and victim were found there. Police took them to police station. During his cross­examination, he deposed that he did not hear any hue and cry from inside. 7 POCSO Case. No. 89/2015. 18] It has come in the evidence of P.W.3 Sunil Shirsat that on 27.09.13, police called him at Rabale M.I.D.C. police station. Accused was present there. His T­shirt and track­pant were seized in presence of this witness vide panchanama at Exh. 12. So also, clothes i.e. gown and nicker of victim were also seized vide seizure panchanama at Exh. 23. During cross­examination, he expressed inability to recollect colour of clothes. 19] It has come in the evidence of P.W.4 Sugandha Suresh Khandekar that the victim is her daughter. This witness and her husband had gone for work. On 26.09.13, both of them had gone for work and her two children Yash and Sonali went to school. Victim alone was at house. At about 5.00 p.m., wife of Kashinath Bhoir informed her that one boy had entered into her house, therefore, this witness had returned back. On arrival, she came to know that the victim and the boy were taken to Rabale police station. Therefore, she went there. The accused and the victim were present in the police station. The victim informed that both were in the house and they were talking. Then, she lodged F.I.R. at Exh. 15. She denied the suggestion that her daughter told that the accused forcibly committed sexual intercourse with her and threatened to kill her, if she would disclose the same to anybody. She denied the statement in F.I.R. which is marked as portion marked A. She had also deposed that the matter was settled between them. 20] P.W.5 victim deposed in the same lines of P.W.4 about working of her parents. She further deposed that on 26.09.13, as usual, her parents had gone for work and her brother and sister went to school. Therefore, she was alone in the house. On her call, the accused came in the house. He did nothing to the victim. That her date of birth is 17.11.1996. As the witness did not support the prosecution version, therefore, 8 POCSO Case. No. 89/2015. permission was given to Ld. A.P.P. to ask leading questions. However, the witness denied that the accused committed rape on her or threatened to kill her if she would disclose about the incident to anybody. She denied the suggestion that Kashinath Bhoir, Baban Salvi and others came and knocked the door. She deposed that after arrival of Kashinath Bhoir, Baban Salvi and others, she started weeping. She further deposed that the matter has settled, however, denied the suggestion that she is deposing false, in order to save the accused. 21] P.W.6 Rahul Somnath Khatal, A.P.I. deposed in his evidence that he was posted as A.P.I. with Rabale police station from June, 13 to June, 16. He was on duty on 27.09.13. A.S.I. Khurade was the police station officer. A.S.I. Khurade recorded F.I.R. Exh.15 of Sugandha Suresh Khandekar as per her narration. Accordingly, C.R. No. 87/2013 was recorded with Rabale police station for the offence punishable u/s. 376, 504, 506 of I.P.C. and u/s. 4(l) and 6 of the POCSO Act. Initial investigation of said crime was conducted by A.P.I. Datta Gawade. He prepared spot panchanama at Exh. 22 in presence of panchas. So also, he seized clothes of victim in presence of panchas vide seizure panchanama Exh. 23. He also arrested the accused. Victim and accused were sent for medical examination. The investigation of said crime was subsequently handed over to P.W.6 on 28.09.13. He received the investigation papers from A.P.I. Gawade. He had also received medical examination reports of accused and victim at Exh. 19 (admitted by defence) and 20 respectively. He also recorded statements of witnesses. 22] On 17.10.13, P.S.I. Seema Suresh Mundhe recorded statement of victim. A.P.I. Khatal was present at that time. He proved portion marked A and B of said statement at Exh. 21 and 22. He had also collected 9 POCSO Case. No. 89/2015. photo­copy of school­leaving certificate of victim at Exh.23 which is admitted by defence. He also collected chemical analysis report of the clothes of the victim as well as blood samples of victim and accused (Exh.24). As it revealed during investigation that the accused had committed sexual assault on minor victim, hence, he filed charge­sheet against the accused, accordingly. During the cross­examination, he denied the suggestion that it revealed during investigation that the accused and victim were having love affair. So also, he denied the suggestion that the statements of witnesses were not recorded as per their actual narration or that he filed false charge­sheet. 23] If the entire evidence of prosecution is perused, there are in all five witnesses on the point of incident. Out of them, neighbour Sunil Shirsat and Baban Salvi have deposed that they have just seen the accused and victim coming out of the room. This fact is not denied by the defence also. It has also come on record that both the parents of the victim were not on the spot and they reached when the victim and accused were taken to police station. Therefore, their evidence is also hearsay in nature. Moreover, P.W.4 mother of the victim has disowned the prosecution case. Therefore, on the point of actual incident, the evidence of victim is important. She has categorically deposed that she was alone in the house. Therefore, she called the accused. She has further deposed that the accused did nothing to her. In spite of granting permission to ask leading questions, this witness has denied each and every suggestion put by the prosecution. Similarly, the mother of the informant who is P.W.4, has also disowned the contents of portion marked 'A' out of the F.I.R., which are in respect of the sexual intercourse as well as criminal intimidation. In such circumstances, thee is a serious doubt about the actual incident of sexual assault or 10 POCSO Case. No. 89/2015. criminal intimidation. Moreover, it is required to be considered that at the time of incident, the victim was more than 17 years old. It is not the case that she was not of the age of understanding. There is also no suggestion of threatening or pressurizing the witnesses. 24] Though it is mentioned in the evidence of P.W.4 and 5 that the matter has settled, however, by that itself, it cannot be inferred that the accused might have committed any offence punishable u/s. 376 or 506 of I.P.C. or any offence under the provisions of POCSO Act. There is no direct or indirect evidence against the accused to prove the guilt or rather indicate forward occurrence of any offence. Though the material witnesses are present, they are not supporting the prosecution version. In such circumstances, conviction of accused on the sole basis of contents of F.I.R. proved by the investigating officer, would not be sufficient. In my view, the burden cannot be put on the accused to disprove the allegations, especially when the victim herself denying the allegations. 25] In the above scenario, in my view, there is no material evidence on record to prove the guilt of the accused. Hence, it is required to hold that prosecution has failed to prove the case of any sexual assault on the victim or any criminal intimidation by the accused to the victim and therefore, the prosecution has failed to prove the charges against the accused. Not only this, the prosecution has also failed to prove that the accused has committed any other minor offence of which the charge has framed against him. Hence, considering the entire material on record, it is necessary to hold the accused not guilty of commission of any offence punishable u/s. 376, 506 of I.P.C. or section 4(l) and 6 of the POCSO Act or of any other offence punishable by any law in force. Consequently, he is required to be acquitted from the charges. Hence, points No. 1 and 2 are 11 POCSO Case. No. 89/2015. answered in the negative. 26] So far as muddemal property is concerned, the charge­sheet does not show any muddemal article submitted along with charge­sheet. Hence, order of disposal of the same is not warranted. Hence, in answer to point No. 3, I pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused Vijay Sarjerao Kolse is hereby, acquitted under sec. 235(1) of the Criminal Procedure Code, from the offence punishable u/s. 376, 506 of Indian Penal Code and u/s. 4(l), 6 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 2] His bail bond stands cancelled and sureties are discharged. 3] Accused is hereby directed to furnish bail bond of Rs.15,000/­ with a surety of like amount, so as to appear before the higher Court in compliance with Sec. 437­A of Code of Criminal Procedure. 4] Pronounced in open court. Thane, (V.Y. Jadhav) Date­ 02.08.2018. Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

1 ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN CRI. BAIL APPLICATION NO. 1077/2016 Heard : Ld. Advocate Mr. Arbaz Agaskar for the applicant. Ld. A.P.P. Mrs. Kamthe for the State. I.O. present. 1] This application is filed by the accused U/s. 439 of Cr.P.C. for releasing him on bail as he was arrested by Padgha Police station in connection with crime No. I­12/2016 for offence U/s. 363, 366­A and 376 of the I.P.C. and Sec. 3(a), 4, 5 (i)(m)(p) and 6 of the PROTECTION OF CHILDREN FROM SEXUAL OFFENCES ACT, 2012. 2] The case of the prosecution in brief is that the applicant has kidnapped the minor victim, while she had gone for tution, from her lawful guardianship without the consent of her parents by inducing her for marriage and took her to U.P. and had a sexual intercourse with her. 3] Ld. Adv. Mr. Agaskar has submitted that the victim was in a love relationship with the applicant and that the charge­sheet has been filed and therefore, the application should be allowed. He has placed reliance on an unreported Judgment of the Hon'ble Bombay High Court dated 3rd August, 2015 in the case of Sunil Mahadev Patil V/s. The State of Maharashtra, Bail Application No. 1036/2015. He has submitted that on the basis of this Judgment, the bail application should be allowed. 4] Per contra, Ld. A.P.P. and I.O. have vehemently opposed the bail application on the ground that the victim was merely 15 years old when she was abducted by the applicant to U.P. The applicant has taken undue advantage of the victim's age. They have submitted that there was no prior 2 love relationship between the two. Moreover, the applicant is not a permanent resident of Padgha and there is every possibility of his fleeing from justice. 5] The Judgment relied upon by the Ld. Adv. for the applicant itself states that at the time of deciding such bail applications, the court should consider the age of the prosecutrix. A girl of 15 years of age is not capable of giving consent. Moreover, even if the argument of the Ld. Adv. for the applicant is accepted, merely having a love relationship with a girl does not entitle a male to have sexual intercourse with her. The offence is serious in nature. The accused is not a permanent resident of Thane District. There is every likelihood of tampering with the evidence and fleeing from justice. In view thereof, I am inclined to reject the application. ORDER The application is rejected. Thane. ( Mridula V.K. Bhatia ) Date : 27/06/2016. Dist. Judge­07 & Special Judge (POCSO) Thane.

.. 1 .. bail no.1072/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Application No.1072/2015 This application is filed by applicant Mrs. Nita Ramnaresh Mishra for her release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. Act). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with false allegation that the applicant aided the sexual assault on the victim girl by not taking any action against the co­accused. It is further contended and argued that no sexual assault as alleged has taken place. It is further contended and argued that the applicant is mother of the victim girl and the applicant is falsely implicated in this crime. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co­ operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that the applicant is mother of the victim girl and other accused are father and brothers of the victim girl. It is further contended and argued that accused no.1 who is father of the girl had committed rape on her and he always used to have physical advances with her. It is further contended and argued that the other co­accused who are brothers of the girl and are juvenile in conflict with law, have also committed .. 2 .. bail no.1072/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) sexual assault on her time and again. It is further contended and argued that the victim girl had complained of such repeated sexual assault on her to her mother i.e. applicant and it is further contended and argued that at the connivance of the applicant the victim girl has been subjected to repeated sexual assault by co­ accused. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl and the prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 376, 354, 323 of I.P.C. and section 4, 5(l), 5, 10, 12, 17 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, it is contended on behalf of applicant that the role attributed to the applicant/accused is to the extent of overlooking the complaint of alleged sexual assault made by the victim girl and it is further contended that the applicant has been falsely involved in this crime merely on the basis of suspicion. In such circumstance the allegation made against the applicant/accused will have to be decided on merits. Even nothing is stated to be recovered from the applicant/accused. 4] It is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if she is released .. 3 .. bail no.1072/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) on bail. In that respect it is contended by the applicant that she is permanent resident of the address given and she will not abscond if released on bail and that she is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 5] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 6] Then, it has also to be mentioned that looking the allegations against the accused the investigation in the matter may have almost completed but the charge sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 7] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail.
