.. 1 .. Bail No. 1075/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1.) Order below Exhibit 1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 1075 / 2015 This application is filed by applicant/accused Mohd Munna Madrang Rain alias Munna Kaka for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. I-47/2015 registered at Bhayander police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 376 of I.P.C. and section 48 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that committed rape on his niece aged 13 years. It is further contended and argued that no such incident of rape has happened and the applicant is falsely implicated in this crime. It is further contended and argued that there is substantial delay in lodging the F.I.R. and there is no support from medical evidence to the prosecution case. It is further contended and argued that since charge-sheet is also submitted, there is no of further custody of the applicant/accused. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it is contended and argued that the accused is husband of maternal aunt of the complainant girl and at the time of incident the complainant girl and the accused were present in the house and at the time when the minor complainant girl was washing utensils in her house, the accused came from behind and held her sleep on floor and then after removing his own clothes and also clothes of the girl, he committed rape on the girl and threatened her that if she disclose about it she would be defamed. It is further submitted that in such .. 2 .. Bail No. 1075/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1.) circumstance since the accused and girl are knowing each other, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl if released on bail and he may pressurize the victim and other prosecution witnesses also. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear the offences charged against the applicant/accused are of very serious nature under section 376 of I.P.C. and section 4 of P.O.C.S.O. Act with the allegation of rape by the applicant/accused on his own niece aged 15 years. The, though in the application it is alleged that he is falsely implicated in this case and the medical evidence is not supporting the prosecution case, such submission on behalf of applicant/accused appear to be totally wrong and not in conformity with the papers. It is very much clear that the complainant had given clear history of sexual assault by the accused and then there are various injuries present on the person of the complainant on her breast, waist, elbow and age of the injuries is stated to be fresh within 24 hours. The applicant/accused is stated to be uncle of the victim and he originally hails from Bihar State and stated to have been there to the house of the complainant from Bihar for a week and during that period he stated to have committed such an act which was immediately reported to police. The submission that there is delay in lodging the F.I.R. also cannot be said to be sustainable because the complaint is lodged on the same day. Even the submission that it is more a matter of consent than force, also appear to be having no base because the complainant is a minor girl aged 15 years and there appear strong prima facie material to show implication of the applicant/accused in the crime. .. 3 .. Bail No. 1075/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1.) 4] Then, though it is well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail, besides that the gravity and serious nature of offence and the manner in which it is stated to have been committed has to be looked into and a wrong message may go to society if bail is granted to the accused especially in such type of matter in which a serious allegation of sexual assault on niece is levelled against the accused. 5] Then, though the investigation is completed and even the charge-sheet is also submitted, keeping in mind the pre-acquaintance of the victim girl with the accused since the girl is stated to be niece of the accused, the apprehension expressed by the prosecution that the accused may threaten and pressurize the victim girl and her family members is well founded. Then, the accused is stated to be native of Bihar State and therefore the possibility of accused being absconded and not available for trial cannot be ruled out. 6] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is not a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order - ORDER The application is rejected. Date : 24.06.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Additional Session Judge-1, Thane.

Mitigating circumstances and the aggravating circumstances have to be balanced and in the balance­sheet of such circumstances, the fact that the case rests on circumstantial evidence has not role to play. In fact, in most of the cases where death sentences are awarded for rape and murder and the like, there is practically no scope for having an eye witness. They are not committed in public view. Only available evidence in such cases is circumstantial. If the said evidence has been found to be credible, cogent and trustworthy for the purpose of recording conviction, to treat that evidence as a mitigating circumstance would amount to consideration of an irrelevant aspect. It was held by the Apex Court that the said plea was unsustainable and that the case fell in the category of rarest of rare cases. Circumstances proved had established the depraved acts of the accused and they call for only one sentence, i.e., death sentence. Accordingly, the Apex Court in this matter confirmed the Judgment of the High Court confirming the conviction and sentence of death imposed by the Trial Court. [v] Bantu V/s. State of U.P., 2008 ALL MR (Cri.) 2907 (S.C.). In this matter, the accused was convicted for the rape and murder of a 5 year old girl. It was held by the Apex Court that undue sympathy to 57 Spl. C. No. 107/2014 (Judgment) impose inadequate sentence would do more harm to the justice system to undermine the public confidence in the efficacy of law and society could not long endure under such serious threats. It has been further held that :­ “21. The physical scar may heal, but the mental scar will always remain. When a woman is ravished, what is inflicted is not merely physical injury but the deep sense of some deathless shame. In the instant case, the victim aged about five years was not only raped, but was murdered in a diabolic manner. 22. The law regulates social interests, arbitrates conflicting claims and demands. Security of persons and property of the people is an essential function of the State. It could be achieved through instrumentality of criminal law. Undoubtedly, there is a cross cultural conflict where living law must find answer to the new challenges and the courts are required to mould the sentencing system to meet the challenges. The contagion of lawlessness would undermine social order and lay it in ruins. Protection of society and stamping out criminal proclivity must be the object of law which must be achieved by imposing appropriate sentence. Therefore, law as a corner­stone of the edifice of "order" should meet the challenges confronting the society. Friedman in his "Law in Changing Society" stated that, "State of criminal law continues to be ­ as it should be ­ a decisive reflection of social consciousness of society". Therefore, in operating the sentencing system, law should adopt the corrective machinery or the deterrence based on factual matrix. By deft modulation sentencing process be stern where it should be, and tempered with mercy where it warrants to be. The facts and given circumstances in each case, the nature of the crime, the manner in which it was planned and committed, the motive for commission of the crime, the conduct of the accused, the nature of weapons used and all other attending circumstances are relevant facts which would enter into the area of consideration. For instance a murder committed due to deep­ seated mutual and personal rivalry may not call for penalty of death. But 58 Spl. C. No. 107/2014 (Judgment) an organised crime or mass murders of innocent people would call for imposition of death sentence as deterrence. In Mahesh v. State of M.P. (1987) 2 SCR 710), this Court while refusing to reduce the death sentence observed thus: "It will be a mockery of justice to permit the accused to escape the extreme penalty of law when faced with such evidence and such cruel acts. To give the lesser punishment for the accused would be to render the justicing system of the country suspect. The common man will lose faith in courts. In such cases, he understands and appreciates the language of deterrence more than the reformative jargon." 23. Therefore, undue sympathy to impose inadequate sentence would do more harm to the justice system to undermine the public confidence in the efficacy of law and society could not long endure under such serious threats. It is, therefore, the duty of every court to award proper sentence having regard to the nature of the offence and the manner in which it was executed or committed etc. This position was illuminatingly stated by this Court in Sevaka Perumal etc. v. State of Tamil Naidu (AIR 1991 SC 1463). 24. The criminal law adheres in general to the principle of proportionality in prescribing liability according to the culpability of each kind of criminal conduct. It ordinarily allows some significant discretion to the Judge in arriving at a sentence in each case, presumably to permit sentences that reflect more subtle considerations of culpability that are raised by the special facts of each case. Judges in essence affirm that punishment ought always to fit the crime; yet in practice sentences are determined largely by other considerations. Sometimes it is the correctional needs of the perpetrator that are offered to justify a sentence. Sometimes the desirability of keeping him out of circulation, and sometimes even the tragic results of his crime. Inevitably these considerations cause a departure from just desert as the basis of punishment and create cases of apparent injustice that are serious and widespread. 59 Spl. C. No. 107/2014 (Judgment) 25. Proportion between crime and punishment is a goal respected in principle, and in spite of errant notions, it remains a strong influence in the determination of sentences. The practice of punishing all serious crimes with equal severity is now unknown in civilized societies, but such a radical departure from the principle of proportionality has disappeared from the law only in recent times. Even now for a single grave infraction drastic sentences are imposed. Anything less than a penalty of greatest severity for any serious crime is thought then to be a measure of toleration that is unwarranted and unwise. But in fact, quite apart from those considerations that make punishment unjustifiable when it is out of proportion to the crime, uniformly disproportionate punishment has some very undesirable practical consequences. 38. The case at hand falls in the rarest of rare category. The depraved acts of the accused call for only one sentence that is death sentence.” [vi] Shivu & Anr. V/s. R. G. High Court of Karnataka & Anr., 2007 ALL MR (Cri.) 1386 (S.C.). In this case, the death sentence awarded by the Trial Court and confirmed by the High Court was held to be appropriate by the Apex Court where two accused aged about 20 and 22 years were sexually obsessed youngsters who had earlier attempted to molest two girls and Panchayat had warned them to mend their ways. Emboldened by the escape from punishment, they committed rape on a young girl of 18 years and to avoid detection, committed heinous and brutal act of her murder. It was held that the said case falls in the rarest of rare category. 60 Spl. C. No. 107/2014 (Judgment) [viii] State of U.P. V/s. Satish, (2005) 3 Supreme Court Cases 114. In this matter, the Apex Court considered whether the rape and murder of minor aged less than 6 years would fall in the rarest of rare category. It was held that rape is one of the most depraved acts. Such iniquitous, flagitious act becomes abominable when the victim is a child. The diabolic act reaches the lowest level of humanity when the rape is followed by brutal murder. The Supreme Court held that it had no hesitation in holding that the present case falls in the rarest of rare category and death sentence awarded by the Trial Court was appropriate. [viii] The State of Maharashtra V/s. Raju Jagdish Paswan, 2013 ALL MR (Cri.) 1431. In this matter, the accused was found guilty of committing rape on victim and thereafter throwing her into a well. The accused committed said gruesome act on the victim who was aged merely 9 years. Accused was aged about 22 years at the time of incident. It was held that age of offender ceases to be a mitigating circumstance in manner in which offence is committed is taken into consideration, the age of the victim and the total bestiality which is shown by the accused. In this matter, the accused did not show any regret or repentance at having committed the offence. There was no possibility of accused being reformed. It was therefore, held by the Division Bench of the Bombay High Court that the case falls in the category of rarest of rare cases and the death sentence awarded to the accused was confirmed. 61 Spl. C. No. 107/2014 (Judgment) [ix] Vasanta Sampat Dupare V/s. State of Maharashtra, 2015 ALL MR (Cri.) 398 (S.C.). In this matter also, the death sentence was confirmed by the Apex Court for the rape and murder of a minor girl. It was held by the Apex Court as follows :­ “57. Presently, we shall proceed to dwell upon the manner in which the crime was committed. Materials on record clearly reveal that the appellant was well­acquainted with the inhabitants of the locality and as is demonstrable he had access to the house of the father of the deceased and the children used to call him "uncle". He had lured the deceased to go with him to have chocolates. It is an act of taking advantage of absolute innocence. He had taken the deceased from place to place by his bicycle and eventually raped her in a brutal manner, as if he had the insatiable and ravenous appetite. The injuries caused on the minor girl are likely to send a chill in the spine of the society and shiver in the marrows of human conscience. He had battered her to death by assaulting her with two heavy stones. The injured minor girl could not have shown any kind of resistance. It is not a case where the accused had a momentary lapse. It is also not a case where the minor child had died because of profuse bleeding due to rape but because of the deliberate cruel assault by the appellant. After the savage act was over, the coolness of the appellant is evident, for he washed the clothes on the tap and took proper care to hide things. As is manifest, he even did not think for a moment the trauma and torture that was caused to the deceased. The gullibility and vulnerability of the four year girl, who could not have nurtured any idea about the maladroitly designed biological desires of this nature, went with the uncle who extinguished her life spark. The barbaric act of the appellant does not remotely show any concern for the precious life of a young minor child who had really not seen life. The criminality of the conduct of the appellant is not only depraved and debased, 62 Spl. C. No. 107/2014 (Judgment) but can have a menacing effect on the society. It is calamitous. In this context, we may fruitfully refer to a passage from Shyam Narain V. State (NCT of Delhi)[40], wherein it has been observed as follows: "The wanton lust, vicious appetite, depravity of senses, mortgage of mind to the inferior endowments of nature, the servility to the loathsome beast of passion and absolutely unchained carnal desire have driven the appellant to commit a crime which can bring in a "tsunami" of shock in the mind of the collective, send a chill down the spine of the society, destroy the civilised stems of the milieu and comatose the marrows of sensitive polity". In the said case, while describing the rape on an eight year old girl, the Court observed: "Almost for the last three decades, this Court has been expressing its agony and distress pertaining to the increased rate of crimes against women. The eight year old girl, who was supposed to spend time in cheerfulness, was dealt with animal passion and her dignity and purity of physical frame was shattered. The plight of the child and the shock suffered by her can be well visualised. The torment on the child has the potentiality to corrode the poise and equanimity of any civilised society. The age­old wise saying that "child is a gift of the providence" enters into the realm of absurdity. The young girl, with efflux of time, would grow with a traumatic experience, an unforgettable shame. She shall always be haunted by the memory replete with heavy crush of disaster constantly echoing the chill air of the past forcing her to a state of nightmarish melancholia. She may not be able to assert the honour of a woman for no fault of hers." 58. In the case at hand, as we find, not only the rape was 63 Spl. C. No. 107/2014 (Judgment) committed in a brutal manner but murder was also committed in a barbaric manner. The rape of a minor girl child is nothing but a monstrous burial of her dignity in the darkness. It is a crime against the holy body of a girl child and the soul of the society and such a crime is aggravated by the manner in which it has been committed. The nature of the crime and the manner in which it has been committed speaks about its uncommonness. The crime speaks of depravity, degradation and uncommonality. It is diabolical and barbaric. The crime was committed in an inhuman manner. Indubitably, these go a long way to establish the aggravating circumstances. 59. We are absolutely conscious that mitigating circumstances are to be taken into consideration. Learned counsel for the appellant pointing out the mitigating circumstances would submit that the appellant is in his mid fifties and there is possibility of his reformation. Be it noted, the appellant was aged about forty­seven years at the time of commission of the crime. As is noticeable, there has been no remorse on the part of the appellant. There are cases when this Court has commuted the death sentence to life finding that the accused has expressed remorse or the crime was not pre­meditated. But the obtaining factual matrix when unfolded stage by stage would show the premeditation, the proclivity and the rapacious desire. Learned counsel would submit that the appellant had no criminal antecedents but we find that he was a history­ sheeter and had number of cases are pending against him. That alone may not be sufficient. The appalling cruelty shown by him to the minor girl child is extremely shocking and it gets accentuated, when his age is taken into consideration. It was not committed under any mental stress or emotional disturbance and it is difficult to comprehend that he would not commit such acts and would be reformed or rehabilitated. As the circumstances would graphically depict, he would remain a menace to the society, for a defenceless child has become his prey. In our considered opinion, there are no mitigating circumstances. 60. As we perceive, this case deserves to fall in the category 64 Spl. C. No. 107/2014 (Judgment) of rarest of the rare cases. It is inconceivable from the perspective of the society that a married man aged about two scores and seven make a four year minor innocent girl child the prey of his lust and deliberately cause her death. A helpless and defenceless child gets raped and murdered because of the acquaintance of the appellant with the people of the society. This is not only betrayal of an individual trust but destruction and devastation of social trust. It is perversity in its enormity. It irrefragably invites the extreme abhorrence and indignation of the collective. It is an anathema to the social balance. In our view, it meets the test of rarest of the rare case and we unhesitatingly so hold.” 97] Per contra, the Ld. Advocate for the accused has submitted that leniency be shown to the accused considering his age of only 26 years at the time of the offence. 98] The accused when questioned by the court about the quantum of punishment, has expressed no remorse whatsoever for the offence that he has committed. It was observed: The community may entertain such sentiment in the following circumstances: 1) When the murder is committed in an extremely brutal, grotesque, diabolical, revolting, or dastardly manner so as toarouse intense and extreme indignation of the community. (3) When murder of a member of a Scheduled Caste or minority community, etc. is committed not for personal reasons but in circumstances which arouse social wrath; or in cases of `bride burning' or `dowry deaths' or when murder is committed in order to remarry for the sake of extracting dowry once again or to marry another woman on account of infatuation. (4) When the crime is enormous in proportion. For instance when multiple murders, say of all or almost all the members of a family or a large number of persons of a particular caste, community, or locality, are committed. (5) When the victim of murder is an innocent child, or a helpless woman or old or infirm person or a person vis­`­vis whom the murderer is in a dominating position, or a public figure generally loved and respected by the community." If upon taking an overall global view of all the circumstances in the light of the aforesaid propositions and taking into account the answers to the questions posed by way of the test for the rarest of rare cases, the circumstances of the case are such that death sentence is warranted, the court would proceed to do so.” 91] In the case of Shivaji (supra) the Apex Court has held that :­ 66 Spl. C. [v] The accused then throttled minor Shehnaz with the intention and knowledge that her death will occur. The said act was done in order to screen himself. [viii] The minor child had to endure excruciating pain and torture at the hands of the accused for no fault of hers. [ix] The accused executed this diabolical crime after due deliberation and planning as mentioned above. MITIGATING CIRCUMSTANCES :­ Although I have searched very minutely, I could not find a single mitigating circumstance except that the accused was 26 years old at the time of the commission of the offence (if that can be called a mitigating circumstance !). 94] It has come in the evidence of the I.O. that after the body of Shehnaz was found at the instance of the accused, several villagers were infuriated and had gathered outside the Wada police station to lynch the accused. It satisfies the preventive theory as it would physically prevent the present accused from committing such crimes in future. It satisfies the retributive theory as the 69 Spl. C. No. 107/2014 (Judgment) a moment the trauma and torture that was caused to the deceased. The gullibility and vulnerability of Shehnaz who had seen only 6 summers of her life, who could not have nurtured any idea about the maladroitly designed biological desires of this nature, went with the 'uncle' who extinguished her life spark. The barbaric act of the appellant does not remotely show any concern for the precious life of a young minor child who had really not seen life. In fact, it was deliberate and preplanned. As the circumstances would graphically depict, he would remain a menace to the society, for a defenceless child has become his prey. 103] Rape is one of the most depraved acts. JUDGMENT (Delivered on 30th September, 2015) Accused stands prosecuted for the offences punishable under sections 354, 504, 506 of Indian Penal Code and punishable under sections 11 and 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual .. 2 .. Special case No. 110/2014 Judgment Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter referred as P.O.C.S.O Act in short) for outraging modesty of victim girl Anita Gupta by moving his hand over breast and kissing her on lips and thereby insulting her and threatening not to tell anybody, in Room No. 1, Bhagwan chawl, Bhavani chowk, Nalpada, Kapurbawdi, Thane and also threatening her brother when he questioned about the incident to the accused. 2] In short the facts giving rise to the prosecution of the accused are that the accused has been maternal uncle of the complainant Anita Gupta aged about 15 years and complaiant was staying in Room No. 1, Bhagwan chawl, Bhavani chowk, Nalpada, Kapurbawdi, Thane with her two real brothers, her two cousin brothers. Accused Munna Sahu also had been staying with them since about three months prior to the incident. At the relevant time she was studying in 10th Standard. That all the brothers of the complainant used to go out for work and accused also used to go out for his work. 3] It is further case of the prosecution that on 17/08/2013 after four brothers of the complainant went out for work, she was doing daily work. Around 10.30 a.m. accused had been to house of complainant and started watching T.V. and called complainant to watch T.V., but she refused. Then accused dragged her towards him to sit near him, moved his hand on her breast and kissed her on lips. When she shouted he ran away. It is also the case of the prosecution that complainant was scared a lot and therefore she went to the shop of her brother and narrated him entire incident. Her brother Brijesh phoned accused and questioned him, but that time accused also .. 3 .. Special case No. 110/2014 Judgment abused him and also threatened to kill him. Therefore, her brother took complainant to the police station and her complaint was recorded. 4] On the basis of her complaint, offence under C.R. No. I 269/20013 under sections 354, 504 506 of Indian Penal Code and section 11 of P.O.C.S.O Act was registered and work of investigation was entrusted to PSI V. P. Bhingardive. During the investigation, panchnama of the spot was prepared. The statements of witnesses were recorded including Brijesh Gupta, the brother of the complainant. Accused was arrested and panchnama of arrest was prepared and after completion of investigation since there was sufficient evidence against the accused, accused came to be chargesheeted under sections 354, 504, 506 of I.P.C. and section 11 of P.O.C.S.O Act. 5] Since offences under sections P.O.C.S.O Act are triable by Special Court and since this is a Special Court for trying offence in respect of P.O.C.S.O Act, the charge­sheet came to be submitted before this Court. 6] Accused appeared before the Court. A charge under sections 354, 504, 506 of I.P.C. and section 11 r/w. section 12 of P.O.C.S.O Act was framed against the accused vide Exh.05. Contents of charge was read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. He pleaded not guilty. His defence was of total denial and was that there was quarrel between accused and brother of the complainant .. 4 .. Special case No. 110/2014 Judgment and on account of that false complaint was lodged with false allegations. He claimed to be tried. 7] For establishing the offences charged against the accused, prosecution examined P.W.1 complainant – victim girl Anita Darshanlal Gupta, P.W.2 Brijesh Darshanlal Gupta – brother of the complainant and P.W.3 API Vishwas Prakash Bhingardive – Investigating officer. The documentary evidence produced, proved and relied upon by prosecution consists of spot panchnama at Exh.20, arrest panchnama at Exh.21 and complaint Exh.24. 8] Statement of accused under section 313 of Cr.P.C. was recorded. Accused did not examine himself on oath and had not examined any witness in his defence. 9] I heard both Ld. A.P.P. And Ld. Advocate for the accused. 10] On the basis of above facts of case, points which arose for my determination and my reasons and findings for the same are as under. POINTS FINDINGS 1. Whether prosecution proved that 17/08/2013 around 10.30 a.m. in the residential house of the complainant victim girl at Room No.1, Bhagwan chawl, Bhawani chowk, Nalpada, Kapurbawdi, Thane, accused used criminal force and assaulted the .. 5 .. Special case No. 110/2014 Judgment complainant namely Anita Darshanlal Gupta and made her to sit by his side and moved hand over her breast and also kissed her lips intending to outrage or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby outrage her modesty? ... No. 2. Whether prosecution proved that on the given date, time and place accused intentionally insulted and thereby gave provocation to the complainant intending or knowing it to be likely that such provocation will cause her to break public peace or to commit any other offence? ... No. 3. Whether prosecution proved that on the given date, time and place accused threatened the complainant and her brother with injury to their person and reputation with intent to cause alarm to them or to cause them to do any act as the means of avoiding the execution of such threat? ... No. 4. Whether prosecution proved that on the given date, time and place accused committed sexual harassment by making complaint to sit by his side and then moved hand over her breast and also kissed her lips? ... No. 5. What offence, if any, is proved against the accused? ... No offence is proved. 6. What order? ... Accused is acquitted. .. 6 .. Special case No. 110/2014 Judgment REASONS AS TO POINT Nos. 1 TO 4 :­ 11] All these points are interconnected and required to be decided on the basis of same evidence, I therefore discuss and decide all the points together. 12] As is clear that the accused is charged with the allegations that he had outraged modesty on the complainant who is girl aged about 15 years and therefore, offence under provisions of P.O.C.S.O. Act are applied. However, surprisingly enough prosecution has not brought any evidence in regard to the age of the girl at the relevant time. Then even complainant girl as well as her brother do not appear to have stated anything about the age of the girl at the relevant time. The investigating officer was also unable to explain as to though the offence charged under P.O.C.S.O. Act why evidence in regard to the age of the complainant is not obtained. In absence of any evidence in regard to the exact age of the girl no conclusion that at the time of incident the girl was child within the meaning of P.O.C.S.O. Act can be drawn and therefore at this stage it can be concluded that no offence under section of P.O.C.S.O. Act can be said to have been established. 13] Even keeping apart that and accepting that the girl stated in her evidence her age is 18 years in the year 2015 and that is again unchallenged since there is no cross examination, and as such in the year 2013 the girl must be below 18 years of age and .. 7 .. Special case No. 110/2014 Judgment therefore, provisions of P.O.C.S.O. Act are applicable and it is required to be seen whether evidence brought on record by the prosecution is sufficient to establish the guilt of the accused for the offence charged. 14] In that regard it is to be mentioned that both the material witnesses P.W.1 Anita Gupta and P.W.2 Brijesh Gupta, the brother of the complainant do not appear to have supported the prosecution case in regard to the allegations against accused about outraging modesty of the girl. Though the girl in her evidence stated that on the day of incident when nobody was there in the house, accused threatened her to kill since there was quarrel between accused and her brother, she has not stated anything about the alleged act of molesting her as she had stated in the complaint. Even the brother of the girl stated only that on the day of the incident complainant had been to his shop and she was crying and accused had beaten and threatened her. But no such case is put forth in the complaint and his version is also not in corroboration to the prosecution case. 15] No doubt P.W.3 the Investigating officer in his evidence stated that on 17/08/2013 when he was on duty as P.S.O. at Kapurbawdi police station P.W.1Anita Gupta had been to the police station and lodged complaint as per Exh.24 and he recorded complaint correctly as per narration of the complainant and he also specifically stated that portions marked A and B were stated by the complainant. There is nothing on record to show that witness was .. 8 .. Special case No. 110/2014 Judgment lying. There appear no reason for police officer to record the complaint with such allegations, if at all no such complaint was made by the complainant and therefore fact that complaint as per Exh.24 with such allegations against the accused was lodged by the complainant has to be held to have been proved. But then so far as contents of the complaint are concerned, as discussed above complainant has not deposed so in her substantive evidence. Therefore the contents of the complaint cannot be said to have been established and fact which can be said to be established on the basis of the evidence of P.W.3 Police officer is only that complaint with such allegations was lodged by the complainant. 16] One more the aspect of the matter that the accused has specifically put forth his defence that there was quarrel between brother of the complainant and him and on that count complainant lodged complaint and quarrel took place between accused and brother of the complainant on that day. That fact is also clear from the testimony of P.W.1 Anita and P.W.2 Brijesh and in such circumstances when the complainant stated that because of that quarrel accused beat her and therefore she went to the police station and lodged complaint, the probability and possibility of defence of accused is also there. In any case in absence of any allegation in regard to outraging modesty of the complainant, merely on the basis of the fact that the complainant lodged complaint with such allegations against accused in regard to molestation and threatening cannot be said to have been established. Similarly, though brother of the complainant is examined, he has not stated anything about .. 9 .. Special case No. 110/2014 Judgment threat given by the accused to him and therefore such allegation also cannot be said to have been established. In view of above discussion none of the allegations against the accused can be said to have been proved and accused is entitled to be acquitted. Point Nos. 1 to 4 are therefore answered in the negative. AS TO POINT No.5 :­ 17] In view of my findings on point Nos. 1 to 4, none of the charges levelled against the accused can be said to have been established and accused is entitled to be acquitted. Point No.5 is therefore answered accordingly. 18] Since the accused is acquitted, it is required that he be directed to furnish P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [Rupees Fifteen Thousand only] under Section 437­A of Cr.P.C. to appear before the higher Court as and when such Court issue notice in respect of any appeal or petition, if filed against the judgment. ORDER Accused namely Munna Ramphal Sahu is acquitted of the charge for the offence punishable under Sections 354, 504, 506 of Indian Penal Code and also under Sections 11 r/w. section 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 2) The bail bond of accused stands cancelled and surety is discharged. 3) The accused shall furnish P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] under section 437A of Cr.P.C. to appear before the higher Court as and when such Court issue notice in respect of any appeal or petition, if filed against the judgment and .. 10 .. Special case No. 110/2014 Judgment that such bail bond shall be in force for six months. 4) No muddemal article is seen to be submitted to the Court. Hence, no order in respect of its disposal is passed. 5) The proceeding is closed. Date : 30/09/2015 (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012, Thane)

.. 1 .. Special case no.94/2015 judgment Received on : 02.05.2015 Registered on : 02.05.2015 Decided on : 12.06.2015 Duration : 1 month 10 days IN The Court of The Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012) Thane At Thane (Presided over by Ms. V.V.Virkar) Special Case No. 94 of 2015 Exhibit No. 04 The State of Maharashtra … Complainant versus B. G. Arunkumar Laxman … Accused Age 35 years, Resident of Mumbra, Dist. Thane. JUDGMENT (Delivered on 12.06.2015.) The accused stands prosecuted for the offence punishable under section 354 of I.P.C. and section 11 read with section 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short ''P.O.C.S.O. Act'') for stalking the complainant minor girl Darshana Bondare, blinking eye and giving her flying kiss when she travellling by rickshaw. .. 2 .. Special case no.94/2015 judgment 2] In short the facts giving rise to the prosecution of the accused are that on 09.03.2015 at about 21.10 the complainant minor girl was travelling in rickshaw on Manisha nagar raod, the accused was following her in another rickshaw and when her rickshaw reached in front of Shelter Hotel, Old Mumbai Pune road, Kharegaon, Kalwa, the accused came near to her rickshaw in another rickshaw and at that time the accused was sitting on front sear near the driver of another rickshaw, tried to foster personal interaction with the complainant by blinking eye at her and also giving flying kiss to her. Therefore, the complainant asked to stop her rickshaw and then getting down, she informed the passersby about the act of the accused. Then the persons gathered there caught hold of the accused and gave him in custody of police and the complainant also went to police station alongwith her father and lodged complaint. 3] On the basis of her complaint, offence as per C.R.No. I- 7/2013 was registered at Rabale police station and the work of investigation was entrusted to P.S.I. Bhamre. During the investigation panchnama of the spot was prepared. Statements of witnesses including victim girl were recorded. Birth certificate of the girl showing her age was obtained. After completion of investigation, since there was sufficient against the accused, he was charge-sheeted for offence punishable under section 354D of I.P.C. and section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and the charge sheet was submitted to the Special Court since provisions of P.O.C.S.O. Act are applied. 4] The accused was produced before Court by jail authorities. A charge as per Exhibit 2 was framed against the accused for offence under section 354D of I.P.C. and section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. .. 3 .. Special case no.94/2015 judgment Act. The contents of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. The accused pleaded guilty and accepted the charges levelled against him and prayed for leniency while awarding the punishment. 5] On above facts of this case, the points which arose for my determination and my findings and reasons for the same are as under - Points Findings i) Whether the prosecution has proved that on 09.03.2015 at about 21.10 the accused was stalking the complainant by travelling in another rickshaw and when rickshaw of complainant reached in front of Shelter Hotel, Old Mumbai Pune road, Kharegaon, Kalwa, the accused tried to foster personal interaction with the complainant minor girl by blinking eye at her and by giving flying kiss to her with intent to outrage her modesty Yes. ii ) Whether the prosecution has proved that the accused on the given day, date, time and place committed sexual harassment of said minor girl ? Yes. iii ) What offence, if any, is proved against the Both offences are accused ? proved. iv ) What order ? The accused is convicted. REASONS 6] As is clear the offence charge against the accused is under section 354D of I.P.C. and section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act with the allegation that the accused had committed sexual harassment upon the complainant minor girl by trying to foster personal interaction with her by blinking eye at her and by giving flying kiss to her after he followed her in rickshaw. Even it is also clear from the complaint lodged .. 4 .. Special case no.94/2015 judgment by the complainant that very specific allegations are made against the accused and on that basis offence under section 354D of I.P.C. and section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act are charged against the accused and the accused has been prosecuted for the said offence. 7] In such circumstance since the accused pleaded guilty and accepted the charges for the offence charged, he is liable to be convicted for the said charge under section 354D of I.P.C. and section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. 8] At this stage the dictation of the Judgment is postponed for hearing the accused on the point of sentence. Date : 12.06.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act) Thane. Resumed. 9] The accused is made aware of the fact that he is held guilty for the offence under section 354D of I.P.C. and section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and the punishment prescribed for offence under section 354D of I.P.C. is Rigorous Imprisonment for a term not less than one year which may extend to three years and with fine and offence under section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act is punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine. 10] I heard the learned A.P.P. and the accused on the point of sentence. .. 5 .. Special case no.94/2015 judgment The learned A.P.P. submitted that looking to the serious nature of offence charged against the accused he is not entitled to leniency and he is liable to award maximum punishment prescribed. The accused prayed for showing him leniency on the ground that he is the only earning member in his family and his family is depending upon him for their livelihood. 11] Then, as is clear though the offence charged against the accused is of very serious nature, the allegations is only that he had taken the victim minor girl inside the public toilet in an uncoming manner and then with sexual intent removed her underwear. But then, it is submitted by the accused on the point of sentence that he has to look after his family members and he is the earning person in his family. 12] Then, so far as quantum of punishment is concerned, Section 42 of the P.O.C.S.O. Act provides : ''Where an act or omission constitutes an offence punishable under this Act and also under sections 166A, 354A, 354B, 354C, 354D, 370, 370A, 375, 376, 376A, 376C, 376D, 376E or section 509 of the Indian Penal Code, then notwithstanding anything contained in any law for the time being in force, the offender found guilty of such offence shall be liable to punishment under this Act or under the Indian Penal Code as provides for punishment which is greater in degree''. Then, as is clear the offence under section 354D of I.P.C. is punishable with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years or with fine whereas offence under section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act is punishable with imprisonment which may extend to three years and also with fine. As such it is clear that sentence of imprisonment of either description i.e. S.I. or R.I. can be awarded for commission of offence under section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. .. 6 .. Special case no.94/2015 judgment Act and therefore it can be said that as per provisions of section 42 of P.O.C.S.O. Act substantive sentence only for offence punishable under section 11 read with section 12 which is imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years and also fine has to be awarded to the accused. 13] In all such circumstance I am of the view that following sentence would meet ends of justice. In the result I pass the following order - ORDER Accused namely B. G. Arunkumar Laxman is convicted for the offence punishable under section 354D of the Indian Penal Code and also for offence under section 11 read with 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and by invoking provisions of Section 42 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012, the accused is sentenced to suffer Rigorous Imprisonment for the term he has already undergone in jail during investigation, inquiry or trial of this case and to pay fine of Rs.500/- [rupees five hundred only] and in default of payment of fine, to suffer S.I. for five days for commission of offence punishable under section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act only. 2) The accused shall be released from jail forthwith if not required in any other crime. 3) Since no muddemal property is submitted before Court, no order regarding its disposal is passed. 4) Copy of judgment be given to the accused free of cost. 5) The proceeding is closed. Date : 12.06.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012) Thane.

Spl.C.No 111/2016 (Judg.) CNR NO. MHTH01­003111­2018 Sr. Points Findings No. 1. Does the prosecution prove that on 07.03.2016 at about 19.30 hours at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Ground, Kalher, Tal. Said act was committed with her prior to 15 days of the alleged incident. Then the entire facts of alleged incident was narrated by the victim to her mother and the relatives, so also her evidence also corroborated by the evidence of her mother as well as her maternal uncle and investigating officer also. Mrs. Hivrale has argued that there is sufficient evidence to show that the accused has molested the victim as well as committed sexual assault. It is further argued that there is amble evidence on record to show that the accused has committed such offence. Apart from the evidence of complainant, other witnesses have also materially corroborated to the version of victim so also to the story of prosecution. It is submitted that the prosecution is able to discharge its bounden duty to prove the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubt and has proved the charge levelled against the accused. Therefore, the prosecution has requested to convict the accused in accordance with the law for the offence punishable under Sec. 354 of I.P.Code and Sec. 7 & 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 8] Per contra, Shri M.T.Patil, the Ld. Advocate appearing for the accused has submitted that the accused is falsely implicated in this case. MHTH01­003111­2018 exaggerations, therefore, their testimonies cannot be relied upon safely. Moreover, the prosecution has not examined any independent witness and P.W.2 and P.W.3 are the close relatives of the victim, it means they are interested witnesses. It is further submitted that in any case, the above offence is not proved against the accused. Mr. Patil has submitted that the prosecution has failed to bring home the guilt against the accused beyond all reasonable doubt therefore, the benefit of doubt be given to the accused. 9] On carefully going through the entire evidence on record, it is seen that all the witnesses have supported to the case of prosecution materially. She further admitted that the victim had already seen the accused prior to alleged incident and on second occasion also the same person tried to contact her and therefore, she is properly knowing and identifying the accused person. The counsel for defence put some suggestion to this witness but could not attract any material substance against the prosecution case. 12] P.W.3 Shashikant Arjun Khilare deposed in his evidence that the victim is his niece. The mother of victim is his sister. She was residing with him along with her daughters. Her husband is .. 9 .. Spl.C.No 111/2016 (Judg.) CNR NO. MHTH01­003111­2018 expired in the year 2017. It is further appeared from her evidence that prior to 15 days of the alleged incident, the victim came at home. She was afraid and narrated that when she was playing on the ground of Kabbaddi, at that time, accused took her behind the stage and rubbed his hand on her private part. Thereafter he himself and his family members along with the victim came on the spot but the accused was not there. In cross­examination, the counsel for defence merely put denial suggestion to this witness as the wrong person shown by the victim but this witness specifically denied such suggestion and admitted in his evidence that the accused was shown by the victim from 10 ft. distance. 13] P.W.4 Laxman Billu Rathod, investigating officer, it is appeared from his evidence that on 07/03/2016 he was posted at Police station Narpoli as A.P.I. On 07/03/2016 complainant lodged report against the accused. Accordingly, it was registered and investigation was started. During the course of investigation, he collected the statement under Sec. 164 of Cr.P.C. as well as bonafide certificate of the victim and after completion of investigation, charge­sheet filed in the court against the accused. He visited the spot of incident on dated 08/03/2016. He further admitted that he has not recorded the statement of independent witnesses than the family members of the complainant. 14] I have duly considered the above submissions of both sides, so also I have gone through the evidence on record. On going through the evidence of P.W.1 victim, P.W.2 Nargis Digambar Phalke as well as P.W.3 Shashikant Khilare, it is seen that they have deposed in one voice that the accused took the victim girl behind the stage of Kabbadi and then rubbed his hand fingers on her private part. It appears to me that their testimony is natural, credible and having a ring of truth. There is no reason to discard their evidence, which is materially supported to each other. 15] In short, after going through the entire evidence on record together, one thing is clear beyond reasonable doubt that when the victim girl narrated the fact of incident to her mother P.W.2 Nargis and her maternal uncle P.W.3 Shashikant Khilare, then they immediately reached on the spot and the victim has pointed out the accused from 10 ft. distance. On seeing to them, accused tried to run away but the maternal uncle of the victim by name Shashikant Khilare chased him and caught hold and took him in police station. It is pertinent to note that the victim has narrated the entire facts of alleged incident to her mother and maternal uncle. The Investigating Officer also fully supported to the case of prosecution. 16] Thus the moot question arises for consideration is such an eventuality is as to what is the offence that has been committed by the accused. From the evidence and circumstances on record, it is clear that the main intention of the accused was to sexually assault to the victim girl. Therefore, considering the facts of the case, the evidence of P.W.1 victim and her mother P.W.2 Nargis and .. 12 .. Spl.C.No 111/2016 (Judg.) CNR NO. There is no explanation about the delay in lodging or recording said complaint. 14] It is further to be noted here that as alleged in the complaint itself, at the time of incident 2­3 more children were playing in the house of accused. However, their statements are not recorded. No inquiry is made with those children. Their names are also mentioned in the complaint. In complaint itself the informant has mentioned that the accused had told her that the victim girl had fallen in the bathroom while playing with the children. This fact is specifically admitted by the accused. Under such circumstances the injury on private part of th victim girl cannot be ruled out. The prosecution has examined Dr.Mamata Ramteke as Medical Officer and medical certificate is proved through her evidence, but she had not examined the victim girl. Under such circumstances no detail cross examination could be conducted in respect of injuries found in local examination of the victim girl. J-Spl.Case POCSO - 117-16 - S-376, 4,8,9.doc .....9/­ ..9.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 117/2016.. Exh.50.. CNR No. MHTH01­003164­2016 15] It is interesting to note here that during the investigation the statement of victim girl was not recorded by investigating officer. She is examined on application u/s.311 of the Code of Criminal Procedure by learned A.P.P. As such there is no explanation of any contradictions or omissions brought on record through defence. Under such circumstances the possibility of tutoring the victim girl cannot be ruled out. 16] From the entire evidence on record and above observations it is clear that the prosecution has not proved the guilt of accused beyond reasonable doubt. Hence answering point Nos.1 and 2 in the negative following order is passed. ORDER 1. 1 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 116/2016 Judgment Received on :­ 04.05.2016 Registered on :­ 04.05.2016 Decided on :­ 25.04.2017 Duration :­ 0Y11M 21 D IN THE COURT OF ADDITIONAL SESSIONS JUDGE, & SPECIAL JUDGE (POCSO) ACT, THANE AT : THANE ( Presided over by Ashutosh N.Karmarkar, District Judge­1 & Special Judge (POCSO) Act, Thane ) Special Case (POCSO) No.116/2016 Exh. No. 24 State of Maharashtra ( Through Vikramgad Police Station ) …Complainant V/s. 1] Mahesh Vishnu Masmare Age : 20 Years, Occ. : Agriculture 2] Naresh Valkya Batra Age : 28 Years, Occ. : Agriculture 3] Gondya Madhya Bond Age : 21 Years, Occ. : Agriculture All R/at. : Dadade paiki Masmarepada, Tal. Vikramgad, Dist. Palghar … Accused. 2 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 116/2016 Judgment Offence punishable under Sec. 354­A(1)(i) r/w.34 of Indian Penal Code & under Sec.8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Appearances : Shri. S.D.Londhe, A.P.P. for the State Shri. R.G.Khilare, Advocate for accused JUDGMENT ( Delivered on this 25th day of April, 2017 ) 1] Accused are facing trial for the offence punishable under Sec. 354­A(1)(i) r/w. 34 of Indian Penal Code and under Sec. 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] Prosecution Case, in brief, is as under : The victim is residing with her parents, grandparents, brother and sisters. They are required to fetch water from the well which is situated near Vikramgad to Talwade road. One minor witness Alka came to the informant as the guest. On 25.03.2016, at about 5.00 p.m, informant / victim and the above noted relative had been to the said well to fetch water. After fetching water, they started returning to the home. They were carrying pitchers over their head. These accused and one juvenile in conflict with law (in short, 'J.C.W.L.') Mithun were coming from village Satkor side towards village Dadade side. At about 5.15 p.m., victim and her relative came on the road near their side. That J.C.W.L. has stated that they all will make her to wet. When the victim stated not to do 3 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 116/2016 Judgment so, said J.C.W.L. has taken out the pitcher which was over her head and poured the water on her person. Accused Mahesh and Naresh caught hold her hands and the accused Gondya came from backside of the victim and hold her and pressed her chest. She narrated the incident to her parents. She approached to police and lodged report. 3] On the basis of report, offence was registered vide C.R.No. I­28/2016. P.S.I. Mr. Waydande has investigated this crime. He drew spot panchanama (Exh.15). He recorded statement of witnesses. He got the victim examined medically. He collected documents from the school to ascertain the age of victim. After completion of investigation, he filed charge­sheet in the Court of law against these three accused. Investigation officer was to file charge­sheet against J.C.W.L.Mithun before the Juvenile Justice Board. 4] Initially, I have framed charge against accused Nos.1 to 3 below Exh. 7 to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. During pendency of this matter, I have altered/amended the charge which is at Exh.17. The accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. After alteration / amendment of the charge, prosecution has filed pursis (Exh.22) that they do not want to lead evidence. Accused also filed pursis (Exh.21) that the earlier evidence be treated as evidence after the fresh charge. 4 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 116/2016 Judgment 5] Prosecution has examined four witnesses. Then, the statement of the accused under Sec. 313 of Cr.P.C. came to be recorded. Total denial is the defence of the accused. The accused have tried to raise the defence that there was some quarrel between informant's uncle and mother of juvenile in conflict with law and since the present accused are the friends of juvenile in conflict with law, they are falsely implicated. 6] Ld. A.P.P. Shri. Londhe has submitted that the age of victim was below 16 years at the time of incident. She has already stated the specific role of each accused. The accused are resident of her locality. So, she identified them. Evidence of victim and her father is not shattered in the cross­examination. There are no residential houses near the spot of incident. According to him, the accused have uttered that they will make the victim wet and this itself shows the intention of the accused. Victim has also stated the same story in her statement under Sec. 164 Cr.P.C. On the other hand, Ld. Advocate for the accused has submitted that it appears that the report was recorded in presence of one lady social worker. But, the victim states that she is not acquainted to her. So, report itself becomes doubtful. It is submitted that the victim has admitted in the cross­examination that the mother of J.C.W.L. has filed complaint against her father and uncle in Vikramgad police station. P.W.2 Alka was not knowing the names of present accused. The walkable distance between the victim's house and the well is of five minutes. The 5 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 116/2016 Judgment clothes on the person of victim were not seized. P.W.2 Alka does not know about the incident. It is also submitted that P.W. 3 i.e. father of the victim has omitted to state that at the relevant time, he was sitting on the platform i.e. ota of the house. 7] Following points arose for my determination and I gave my findings thereon for the reasons stated below: Sr. POINTS FINDINGS No. 1. Does the prosecution prove that the Yes. accused along with juvenile accused Mithun Bandu Bond, in furtherance of common intention, on 25.3.2016, at about 5.15 p.m., at mauje Dadade, Satkor road paiki, Kokatripada village, at a distance of 150 ft. on northern side from the house of complainant, near pakka road, have sexually harassed minor victim Ku. Yogita Pagi, aged 15 years, by physical contact and advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures? 2. Does the prosecution prove that the Yes. accused along with juvenile accused Mithun Bond, on above mentioned date, time and place, committed sexual assault on minor girl Ku. Yogita Pagi, aged 15 years with sexual intent? 3. What order? As per final order. 6 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 116/2016 Judgment REASONS AS TO POINT NO.1 TO 3:­ 8] The prosecution has examined informant / victim P.W.1 (Exh.8), her relative i.e. minor girl Alka P.W.2 (Exh.11), victim's father Chintu Janu Pagi P.W.3 (Exh.13) and P.S.I. Waydande P.W.4 (Exh.14). 9] It appears that the accused have admitted the copy of School Leaving Certificate of the victim which is on record which is now given Exh.23. It is well settled principle that the sole testimony of a witness is sufficient to base a conviction. But, the rule is that it should inspire confidence in the mind of Court and should be above suspicion. 10] In order to prove the guilt under Sec. 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, prosecution has to establish that the accused has touched the breast of the child with sexual intent or does any other act with sexual intent which involves physical contact without penetration. 11] It appears from the material on record that on the day of incident, the age of victim was below 16 years. Victim has stated that on the day of incident at about 5.00 p.m., she had been to well to fetch water which is situated at Talwada to Vikramgad road. P.W.2 Alka was with her. After fetching water in the pitcher they started returning. When they came near their house, all these 7 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 116/2016 Judgment accused and one J.C.W.L. came there. They have all uttered the words “rqyk fHktosy”. She opposed them as the pitchers were over her head. She has specifically stated that accused Mahesh has taken out the pitcher. J.C.W.L. Mithun and accused Naresh caught hold her hands and the accused Gondya moved his hand over her chest. She started weeping and went to house. She narrated the incident to her parents. Then, she went to police station and lodged the report (Exh.9). She has identified these three accused. She is also residing in the same village. The victim was cross­examined by the accused at sufficient length. Evidence of victim is not shattered in the cross­ examination in respect of evidence of incident. The accused has brought on record in the cross­examination of victim that P.W. Alka was guest and was new in the village. Admittedly, she was not knowing the accused by their names. It is also brought on record in the cross­examination of victim that Alka was proceeding ahead of her by 15 to 20 ft. 12] P.W.2 Alka has stated that her date of birth is 19.09.2000. So, her age was also about 16 years at the relevant time. Her age is also not seriously disputed by the accused. She has also stated that on the day of incident, she had been to fetch water at the well near Talwada­Vikramgad road along with victim. After fetching water in the pitcher, they started returning. She was proceeding ahead of victim. She has identified the accused before the Court who came from opposite direction. She has specifically 8 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 116/2016 Judgment admitted in the cross­examination that she does not know as to what act the accused have committed. However, the evidence of P.W.2 Alka corroborates the evidence of the victim to the extent that she has seen these accused while coming from opposite side and they went behind her back. So, this fact itself shows the presence of the accused at the spot of incident. 13] P.W.3 Chintu Pagi, the father of the victim has stated that the incident occurred at the time of Holi festival in last year. On the day of incident, informant and P.W.2 Alka had been to well to fetch water. Alka came earlier than the victim. Informant / victim stated the role of each accused during the incident. He has further stated that he was sitting on the platform ( ota) of his house and he has seen these accused proceeding to the direction where informant had gone. Ld. Advocate for the accused has submitted that this witness has omitted to state that he has seen the accused while proceeding towards the direction of the well. But, it is to be noted that the accused has not proved such omission, if any, by suggesting the same to the investigating officer P.S.I. Waydande. So, such submission of Ld. Advocate for the accused has no force at all. Evidence of P.W.3 Chintu is also material on the point that he has seen accused proceeding towards direction of the well. Secondly, the victim has narrated the incident and the exact role of each accused to him. P.W.3 Chintu is father of victim. It is but natural on the part of the victim to say the incident to her father. 9 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 116/2016 Judgment There is nothing in the cross­examination of Chintu to discard his testimony. 14] It appears that more details are brought on record in the cross­examination of victim. It is brought on record that walkable distance from the victim's house to the well is of five minutes. It is also brought on record that there are no other houses by the side of the road which go towards the well. P.S.I. Waydande has stated that during investigation, he has drawn the spot panchanama in presence of panchas at Exh.15. Ld. Advocate for the accused has submitted that independent panch witness on the said panchanama is not examined. P.S.I. Waydande is also the best witness to prove the panchanama. There is nothing in the cross­ examination that he is having any reason to depose against the accused or that he is having personal grudge against the accused. Spot panchanama (Exh.15) shows that spot of incident is at a distance of 150 ft. from the house of victim. P.S.I. Waydande has also stated that the sketch of the spot is also prepared which is part of the panchanama. Panchanama and sketch itself shows that there are no other houses by the side of the spot of incident. So, it can be said that the spot where alleged incident has taken place is isolated. 15] It also appears that the incident has taken place in daylight. Accused are resident of the same village of victim. So, victim has identified them. Victim has also specifically stated that 10 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 116/2016 Judgment all the accused uttered the words as “rqyk fHktosy”. She has also stated that the accused Mahesh has taken out pitcher, accused Naresh caught hold her hand and accused Gondya moved hand over her breast. If all these facts are considered together then, intention of the accused can be gathered from their utterances “Tula Bhijwel”, that too, at isolated place. 16] Sec. 7 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act says that whoever with sexual intent touches the breast of a child is said to commit sexual assault. Later part of this section also says that whoever does any other act with sexual intent which involves physical contact without penetration is said to commit sexual assault. In this matter, victim has specifically stated against Gondya about touching the breast. She has particularly stated that the accused Naresh caught hold her hand and accused Mahesh has taken out a pitcher over her head. So, it is clear that the accused Naresh and Mahesh had intention to facilitate Gondya to assault the victim sexually and they have actually helped him. So, the act of the accused Naresh and Mahesh can be said to be sexual assault as shown in the later part of Sec. 7 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. The victim has further stated that after the incident she started weeping and immediately after reaching home, she narrated the incident to her parents. So, subsequent conduct of the victim itself also makes her story as natural and reliable. 11 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 116/2016 Judgment 17] Ld. Advocate for the accused has submitted that the mother of juvenile in conflict with law Mithun had dispute with the uncle and father of the victim and complaint was also lodged. The accused have also tried to raise defence that they are the friends of J.C.W.L. Mithun. His mother had dispute with victim's uncle and so, they are falsely implicated. It is true that victim has admitted that the accused are the friends of J.C.W.L. Mithun. Victim has also admitted that mother of J.C.W.L. Mithun had filed complaint against her uncle and father. Accordingly, defence under Sec. 313 Cr.P.C. is raised that there was dispute between mother of J.C.W.L. Mithun and the uncle of the victim named Sanjay. It is not stated by the accused in the statement under Sec. 313 of Cr.P.C. that there was any dispute between mother of J.C.W.L. Mithun and the father of the victim. Even, the accused have not suggested in the cross­ examination to the victim's father Chintu about dispute between him and the mother of J.C.W.L. Mithun. It was also possible for the accused to place on record the copy of the said complaint, if any, by the mother of J.C.W.L. Mithun against the father of victim. The accused have also not stated the details of the allegations in that complaint, if any. Even if it is accepted for a moment that there is such complaint against the father and uncle of the victim by the mother of J.C.W.L. Mithun only, then there was no reason for the victim to lodge complaint with such allegations against the present three accused. In natural course, no father will help his minor daughter to make such allegations. So, such defence can not be 12 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 116/2016 Judgment accepted as reliable. 18] The victim has specifically stated the role of each accused. It is already discussed in foregoing paragraphs that the accused Gondya has touched the breast of the victim and other two accused have helped him. They are also involved in physical contacts of the victim. Now, it is to be seen whether such acts of the accused were with sexual intent. In order to ascertain the meaning of sexual intent, a reliance can be placed in the Judgment in case of Bandu Vitthalrao Borwar V/s. State of Maharashtra, in Criminal Appeal No. 50 of 2016, before Hon'ble Bombay High Court, Nagpur Bench. It is held in the judgment in para 10 as under : “After all intention of a person is his state of mind and has to be discerned from the surrounding facts and circumstances. If one cannot, as a human being, physically enter into a mind of another to read and see what is being cooked there, one can surely know it by evaluating all that which is perceivable or felt by human senses such as words, body­language, gestures, reactions and everything that is a physical manifestation of working of human mind.” It is also held in the said judgment by the Hon'ble Bombay High court in para 11 as under : “It is obvious that the intent, which is nothing but a state of mind, must be to establish some sort of 13 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 116/2016 Judgment physical contact or must be related to or associated with sex or indicative of involvement of sex in the relationship, if it is to be considered as sexual.” It is further held that; “There should be something more which must suggest that the real intention is to drag in the angle of sex, if the words uttered are to be taken as conveying sexual intent.” 19] It is already discussed that the alleged incident has taken place in daytime that too, at isolated place. There are no other houses by the side of spot of incident. There is no personal rivalary between the victim and the accused. They have initially uttered the words as “rqyk fHktosy”. Victim has stated that the accused Gondya moved the hand over her chest. In order to facilitate him, accused Naresh caught hold her hand and accused Mahesh has taken out the pitcher over her head. So, it is clear that the accused have not only uttered the words “rqyk fHktosy” but, they went one step ahead and have played their independent role so as to have physical contact with the victim. So, it is clear that the said acts were committed by the accused with sexual intent. So, the discussion above lead me to say that the accused Nos.1 to 3 have committed an offence punishable under Sec. 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. Therefore, I answer point No.2 in the affirmative. 14 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 116/2016 Judgment 20] In order to establish the guilt under Sec. 354­A(1)(i) of Indian Penal Code, it is to be established that the man has committed the acts i.e. physical contact and advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures. It appears from the evidence of the witnesses that the victim was proceeding by the side of the road. There were no houses adjoining to the said spot. Victim was carrying water in a pitcher over her head. Accused have initially uttered the words “rqyk fHktosy” and in order to succeed in their act of physical contact, they have proceeded one step ahead and have played their independent role of removing the pitcher over her head and catching hold her hand. 21] It is already discussed in the foregoing paragraphs that there is no substance in the defence which they have raised. Oral evidence of the victim as to role of each accused is consistent to the allegations in the report Exh.9. It is clear from the evidence of victim that the accused have committed the acts of physical contacts and advances involving explicit sexual overtures. Considering the evidence of the victim which is found reliable in foregoing paragraphs, it can be said that the accused are guilty for the offences under Sec. 354 ­A(1)(i) of Indian Penal Code. Reliance also can be placed in case of T. Manikadan V/s. The State ( Govt of NCT of Delhi) and Anr., Criminal Revision Petition No. 404/2016. In that matter, initially, the petitioner was acquitted of the offence u/sec. 354/354A of Indian Penal code and 15 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 116/2016 Judgment in the appeal filed by the State the Ld. Additional Sessions Judge convicted the appellant for offence punishable under Secs. 354/354A of Indian Penal. It is necessary to reproduce the paragraph 10 of this Judgment. “ In the present case the allegations proved against the petitioner are that he fondled the breast of the prosecutrix with ill intention and thereafter touched her private parts. Thus the offence committed by the appellant fulfils the ingredients of Section 354 IPC and not merely Section 354A IPC which punishes even a physical contact with advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures. Since criminal force has been used by the appellant and the modesty of the prosecutrix had been outraged by an act beyond physical contact with sexual overture, ingredients of both Sections 354 and 354A IPC being fulfilled, this Court finds no illegality in the conviction of the appellant for the offences punishable under Section 354 and 354A IPC and the sentences awarded.” 22] In present matter in order to facilitate the accused Gondya, other accused have also played an independent role and accordingly had physically contacts with the victim and advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures. There is also presumption under Sec. 29 of the 16 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 116/2016 Judgment Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act,2012. Victim has already stated in detail about involvement of accused in this crime by saying their individual role. It is already discussed that evidence of victim is not shaken in cross­examination. Evidence of victim is not rebutted. Hence, I find that the prosecution has established all the ingredients of Sec. 354­A(1)(i) of Indian Penal Code also. Therefore, I answer point No.1 in the affirmative. 23] Since the accused Nos.1 to 3 are held guilty for the offence for which they are charged, they are to be heard on the point of sentence. 24] I have heard both the sides on the point of sentence. Ld. Advocate Mr. Khilare for the accused has submitted that these accused had no criminal antecedents. They are behind the bar for about two months in this matter. Considering their age and other facts leniency may be shown. On the other hand, Ld. A.P.P. Shri. Londhe has submitted that in case of leniency, there would be a wrong message in the society and the accused may again commits such offence. He has prayed for maximum sentence. 25] Punishment prescribed for the offence punishable under Sec. 354­A(1)(i) of I.P.C. is rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years or with fine or both. Punishment prescribed for the offence punishable under Sec. 8 of the Protection 17 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 116/2016 Judgment of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, is imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than three years or which may extend to five years and shall also be liable to pay fine. 26] It appears that the alleged incident is against minor girl. In order to check such type of offence in future, the accused are to be dealt with and therefore, I am not inclined to grant benefit of Probation of Offenders Act to them. Taking into consideration, submissions from both the sides, the age of the accused and other factors, following order will meet the ends of justice. In result, I proceed to pass following order : ORDER 1] Accused No.1] Mahesh Vishnu Masmare, No.2] Naresh Valkya Batra and 3] Gondya Madhya Bond are convicted under Sec. 235 (2) of Code of Criminal Procedure of the offence punishable under Section 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and they each are sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 3 years and to pay fine of Rs. 500/­ each i.d. to suffer simple imprisonment for six months. 2] Accused No. No.1] Mahesh Vishnu Masmare, No.2] Naresh Valkya Batra and No. 3] Gondya Madhya Bond are convicted under Sec. 235(2) of Code of Criminal Procedure of the 18 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 116/2016 Judgment offence punishable under Section 354­(A)(1)(i) r/w. 34 of Indian Penal Code and each accused is sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 1 year and to pay fine of Rs. 500/­ each i.d. to suffer simple imprisonment for three months. 3] Both the sentences to run concurrently. 4] Bail bonds of all accused stand cancelled. 5] Accused Nos. 1 to 3 are entitled for set off under Sec. 428 of Criminal Procedure Code, if any as per rule. [ Dictated and pronounced in open Court. ] Thane, ( Ashutosh N. Karmarkar ) Date : 25.04.2017 District Judge­1 & Special Judge (POCSO) Act,Thane
