No. 98/2015. 16 and 14 years from the lawful guardianship of complainant Satyanarayan Komarayya Jadala without his consent ? 3] Whether prosecution proved that on the No. above date, time and place, accused induced two minor daughters of complainant aged 16 years and 14 years, to go out of the lawful guardianship of complainant Satyanarayan Komarayya Jadala without his consent, with intent that the minor girls may be, or knowing that it is likely that they will be forced or seduced to illicit intercourse with him ? 4] Whether prosecution proved that on the No. above date, time and place, at the room of Jagdish Patil at Ovali village, Bhiwandi, accused had committed rape on minor victim girl aged 14 years, for twice and then, by making her to wear 'Kumkum' on forehead and to wear 'Mangalsutra' and by telling lie with the people thereat, thus, caused disappearance of evidence of offence and gave false information to people to screen himself from legal punishment ? 5] What order ? As per final order. REASONS POINT NOS. 1 TO 4 10] P.W.1 minor victim girl had deposed in her evidence that­ She was born on 30.01.2001. In the year 2015, she was studying in 9th standard. Her school time was from 7.00 5 POCSO Case. No. 98/2015. a.m. to 12.00 noon. Her grand­mother from father's side, was residing in Anjurphata. Accused used to come there. Accused is her boy­friend. Other victim girl is her elder sister. One day, they both sisters along with accused went to Varhaldevi temple, Bhiwandi. Her maternal uncle had noticed them. Then, they both sisters were taken by him. He had brought her father at Varhaldevi temple. They became frightened on seeing their father. Thereafter, accused took her to Kamatghar, at the house of his friend. Then, they went to village Ovali. They stayed thereat for seven days. She was told by accused to inform about their whereabouts to her parents. But, she had not contacted with them. During that seven days, accused had established sexual relations with her. Thereafter, on 07.02.15, complainant came to Ovali and they were taken by him to police station. She lodged her report (Exh.12). She was referred by police to hospital. They had examined her. They had obtained required samples from her. Clothes of they both sisters were seized under seizure memo (Exh. 13). Her statement was recorded by Child Welfare Committee on 11.02.15. 11] It has come in her cross by Ld. A.P.P. that she is married with accused. She has a daughter from accused. 12] P.W.2 complainant had deposed in his evidence that­ On 01.02.15, he had been to his labour work. Both minor victim girls had been to Varhaldevi temple, Bhiwandi to have Prasad. However, they both did not return back up to 8.00 p.m. So, he lodged his report (Exh. 15). After 3­4 days, both victim girls were found at village Ovali. Then, they were taken to police station. He had not talked with them. They both were referred to hospital by police. He was told by younger victim girl that she would marry with accused. Police had recorded his statement. 13] It has come in his cross­examination by Ld. Counsel for accused that the younger victim girl had married with accused. She had 6 POCSO Case. No. 98/2015. delivered a female child. She had attended marriageable age. 14] P.W.1 victim girl had stated her date of birth as 30.01.2001. However, no birth certificate or school­leaving certificate are placed on record. It further seems that she is married to accused and she has blessed a child. She is leading her marital life happily. As no birth certificate of victim is placed on record, it is very difficult to hold that victim was minor below 18 years of her age. 15] From the evidence on record, it can be gathered that both P.W.1 and 2 used to give their company with the accused. So, it cannot be said that accused had kidnapped the victim. C.A. reports Exh. 18, 19 are placed on record. However, no semen was detected in vaginal swab of victim. In nail clippings or on pubic hair, no blood or any tissue matter nor semen nor vaginal fluid was detected. 16] Having considered the relations between accused and victim and evidence on record, in my view, prosecution failed to prove that the accused had kidnapped the victim from the custody of her lawful guardianship without their consent and committed rape on victim beyond all reasonable doubts. Hence, I answer all the points in the negative and proceed to pass the following order. ORDER 1] Accused Akshay @ Banti Suresh Sahajrao, is hereby, acquitted under sec. 235(1) of the Criminal Procedure Code, of the offences punishable u/s. 376(1) of I.P.C. r/w. Section 3(A) punishable u/s. 4 of the Protection of 7 POCSO Case. No. 98/2015. Children from Sexual Offences Act, u/s. 363, 366(A), 201 of I.P.C. 2] Accused Akshay @ Banti Suresh Sahajrao, be enlarged on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ with surety of like amount. The effect of this bail order will remain in force for the period of six months from today, as per section 437­(A) of Cr.P.C. 3] Muddemal property being worthless, be destroyed after appeal period is over. It was registered vide C.R. no. 67/17 u/s. 354 of I.P.C. and u/s. 8 and 12 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. P.W.5 Madhuri Ghadge had carried out investigation. She rushed to the spot, verified it and recorded statements of witnesses. Victim was referred to give her statement u/s. 164 of Cr.P.C. After investigation, charge­sheet was submitted in the Special Court. 3] Heard both sides. I framed the charge against the accused for the offences punishable under section 354 of I.P.C. and u/s. 8, 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, on 18/07/2017. Details of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular, to 3 POCSO Case. No. 109/2017. which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. His defence is of total denial. 4] During trial, defence has admitted no documents. 5] To bring home the guilt of the accused for the charges leveled against him, the prosecution has examined as many as six witnesses i.e. P.W. Name of witness Exh. Description No. No. 1] Minor victim girl 12 Minor victim/complainant 2] Urmila Vinod Pangale 15 Mother of victim girl 3] Vinod Vishnu Pangale 16 Father of victim girl 4] Sheetal Shashikant 17 Neighbourer of complainant Navele 5] Madhuri Jagannath 22 Investigating officer. Ghadge 6] Sanjay Amawas Ram 25 Panch of spot panchanama. 6] Accused did not enter into witness box, but he has examined one defence witness Mr. Ganesh Arvind Mungale, P.S.I., in his defence (Exh.30). 7] Heard learned Special P.P. Smt. Phad for the State. She submitted that accused had not denied his presency on the spot. Victim at relevant time was aged about 14 years, is also not denied by the accused. So, victim was child at the relevant time. Victim and Sheetal Navele had supported to the prosecution story. Nothing was forwarded by the accused to disbelieve their evidence. Both had corroborated to each­other. There is no reason to implicate the accused in false case. Lastly, she prayed for conviction. 4 POCSO Case. No. 109/2017. 8] Heard learned counsel Shri. Anand Awasarmol, for the accused. He submitted that all the witnesses were known to each­other. Victim in her report has not stated her date of birth. So also, she had not stated her date of birth in her statement u/s. 164 of Cr.P.C. Birth certificate or school­leaving certificate are not placed on record and they are not proved. So also, there is no ossification test report to prove her age on the date of incident. The alleged incident was taken place on 04.03.17 at about 11.30 a.m., whereas report came to be lodged on 05.03.17 at belated stage. The statement of victim before police and before J.M.F.C. are contrary to each­other. Victim had not called to any other independent witnesses. No other person except Sheetal Navele was gathered on the spot. If mouth of victim was tied by towel, then she was not in position to call anyone or to shout. However, according to her, on her shout, Sheetal Navele came there. The area around the houses of accused and victim was crowded. There is material omission regarding pressing of chest. Prosecution failed to prove the alleged incident including age of victim. He placed his reliance on the following authorities­ 1] Ravi Anandrao Gurpude Vs. State of Maharashtra, 2017 ALL MR (Cri.) 1509, wherein Their Lordships observed that­ From the provisions of POCSO Act, it is crystal clear that the prosecution is under bounden duty to prove that the victim is a child. Unless the prosecution successfully establishes that the victim is a child within the meaning of clause (d) of section 2 of the Act, a person cannot be convicted for the offence punishable under section 6 of the Act. 2] Sujit Bhurandas Borkar Vs. State of Maharashtra, 2016 ALL MR (Cri.) 2029, wherein His Lordship observed that­ Certified copy of bonafide certificate issued by the 5 POCSO Case. No. 109/2017. school showing the date of birth of prosecutrix is placed on record. However, entry is not proved through concerned head­master or school authority. By merely tendering or by merely exhibiting a certificate, date of birth cannot be said to have been proved. 3] John @ Vivek Ramesh Jadhav Vs. State of Maharashtra, 2015 ALL MR (Cri.) 4053, wherein His Lordship observed that­ Accused allegedly committed aggravated sexual assault on victim child aged about 8 years. Evidence of mother is hearsay in nature. No medical evidence as to examination of either accused or victim. In absence of any other corroborative evidence, testimony of child victim is not reliable. 4] Jagdish Balaram Narangikar Vs. State of Maharashtra, 2012 ALL MR (Cri.) 2044, wherein Their Lordships observed that­ Prosecution case that accused a neighbourer took victim, a minor girl to his home and ravished her. Conduct of complainant, mother of victim taking victim to police station and thereafter to hospital after four days from the date of incident is unnatural. Evidence of complainant is not inspiring confidence nor supported by medical evidence. Defence of the accused that on account of dispute regarding monetary transaction, he was falsely roped in, appears to be probable defence. Conviction of accused solely on the basis of uncorroborated evidence of complainant, is liable to be set aside. 9] Following points arise for my determination, which are being answered for the reasons given herein­below. POINTS FINDINGS 1] Whether prosecution proved that on No. 05.03.2017 at Sadguru Hardev chawl, Waghobanagar No. 09, Kalwa, Thane, 6 POCSO Case. No. 109/2017. accused used criminal force to complainant minor victim girl aged 14 years, by putting hand on her mouth, pulling her inside his house and pressing her chest, intending to outrage or knowing it to be likely that he would thereby, outrage her modesty ? 2] Whether prosecution proved that on the No. above date and place, accused committed sexual assault and sexual harassment on victim minor girl aged 14 years ? 3] What order ? As per final order. REASONS POINT NOS. 1 AND 2 10] P.W.1 minor victim girl deposed in her evidence that­ She was born on 29th November, 2003. She is studying in Sanjeevani Madhyamik Vidyalaya, Ishwarnagar, Kalwa, in 9th standard. In last year, she was studying in 8th standard. Her school time is from 7.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon. However, on Saturday, their school timing is upto only 10.00 a.m. She knows accused Kailas Yadav. He is residing opposite to her house. On 04.03.17 at 11.00 a.m., there was parent's meeting in the school. So, her mother had been to her school. Her father had been to his work at 6.30 a.m. So, she alone was present in her house. There is open place near their house. They had pet dog. So, at about 11.15 a.m., she had carried their pet dog in the said ground. At that time, accused was standing in his door. He had enquired with her whereabouts of her parents. She told him that her mother went to her school and her father went to his work. Then, she carried her dog in the ground. Within five to seven minutes, she returned back towards her 7 POCSO Case. No. 109/2017. house. At that time also, accused was present in the door of his house. When she came in front of the door of accused, at that time, he had caught hold her hand and pulled inside his room. He had pressed her chest. She felt bad and she shouted. Neighbourer Sheetal Navele came running on hearing her shouts. Accused was frightened on noticing her. Then, accused pushed her out of the door. She was taken by Sheetal Navele to her house. She had narrated the incident to her. She had ringed to victim's parents. Victim's parents immediately came to the house. Sheetal Navele had narrated the incident to them. Victim had also narrated the incident to them. Then, victim along with her parents went to police station. She lodged her report (Exh. 13). Thereafter, Ld. J.M.F.C. had recorded her statement (Exh. 14). 11] It has come in her cross­examination that­ They were in talking terms with the family members of accused. They used to come to victim's house. Family members of victim were not visiting their house. Victim was studying in Shivaji Vidya­Mandir, Bhandup, in 7th standard. On 04.03.17, she went out to bring her pet dog. There was no belt around the neck of dog. They were maintaining dog since last two years. Accused had also tied her mouth by towel. She was tied by him to the pole by rope. He had put the bolt of door and had been to first floor. Then, he got down and went out from the room. Sheetal Navele came there for searching her as Simran. She was not in position to talk as her mouth was tied. Her statement was recorded on 05.03.17. There is no floor to the house of accused. Her statement was recorded by J.M.F.C. on 18.03.17. Many people are residing nearby their house. There is lane in two rows of houses. People are passing by the said lane. Sheetal Navele is her neighbourer. There was quarrel between Sheetal Navele and accused. Quarrel was going on for about half an hour. Thereafter, Sheetal Navele had ringed to her parents. 12] P.W.4 Sheetal Shashikant Navele deposed in her evidence 8 POCSO Case. No. 109/2017. that­ Vinod Vishnu Pangale is her neighbourer. Victim is his daughter. On 04.03.17, she was present in her house. On that day, at about 11.15 a.m., victim had carried their pet dog to ground. At relevant time, she heard noise of victim from the house of accused Kailas Yadav. She went there. She noticed that accused Kailas had pressed her chest by his both hands. On noticing her, he had pushed victim out of the house. She took victim to her house and offered water. She was weeping. Sheetal enquired with her reason of weeping. Sheetal was told by her that she had carried pet dog in the ground, thereafter, she was coming back, accused was standing in the door of his house, he enquired whereabouts of her mother, she replied that her mother went to school, thereafter, he had enquired whereabouts of her father, she replied that he went to his work, he had caught hold her hand and took her inside his room, he had put his hand on her mouth, then, he had pressed her chest. 13] It has further come in her evidence that­ Then, she gave ring to the mother of victim. However, she had not attended her 2­3 calls. Lastly, she had attended her phone. She disclosed the entire incident to her. Then, she also gave ring to father of victim. She was threatened by accused that she should not disclose the incident to the parents of victim, else her life would be ruined. Then, accused ran away. Thereafter, her parents came and tried to search for accused. She narrated the incident to the parents of victim. Police had recorded her statement. 14] It has come in her cross­examination that­ Before about six years, they came to Waghobanagar, Kalwa, for residence, with the help of father of victim. Room of victim is opposite to her house. Room of accused is situated after one room from her room in the row of her room. People are using the lane situated 9 POCSO Case. No. 109/2017. between their house. 15] She further deposed in her cross that­ She had told to police in her statement that she noticed that the accused had put his both hands on the chest of victim; she was threatened by accused that she should not disclose the incident to the parents of victim, else he would ruin her life, then accused ran away. 16] From the evidence of P.W.1 victim who in her report Exh. 13, had stated her age as 14 years, had stated in her evidence before the court her date of birth as 29th November, 2003. P.W.2 Urmila Pangale and P.W.3 Vinod Pangale, parents of victim, had not stated the date of birth of the victim in their evidence. Xerox copy of school leaving certificate of victim is placed on record as article A. It is also not proved. Therefore, merely victim herself had stated her age on oath, is not sufficient to hold that she was born on 29th November, 2003, in absence of any proof. Head­master or school authority is not examined by the prosecution. No original birth certificate is also placed on record. Therefore, merely xerox copy of school leaving certificate marked as article A, cannot said to be proved. 17] The entire case is based on sole testimony of victim herself. P.W.4 Sheetal Navele is produced before the court as eye­witness to the incident. However, she deposed in her evidence that she noticed that accused Kailas had pressed her chest by his both hands, on one hand. However, immediately on the other hand, she deposed that victim was crying, so she had enquired with the victim. Victim had stated before her that accused had caught hold her hand and took her inside his room, he had put his hand on her mouth and then, he had pressed her chest. Besides, the material evidence that she had noticed that the accused had put his both 10 POCSO Case. No. 109/2017. hands on the chest of victim; victim was threatened by accused that she should not disclose the incident to her parents, else he would ruin her life and then, he ran away, is material omission. Therefore, the evidence of P.W.2 is not reliable one. 18] P.W.1 victim deposed in her evidence that by holding her hand by accused, pulled her inside his room, he had pressed her chest, she shouted, so neighbourer Sheetal Navele came on her shout. However, in her cross­examination, she deposed that accused had tied her mouth by towel. She was also tied to pole by rope. He had put the bolt of door and had been to the first floor. Then, he got down and went out from the room. Sheetal Navele came there for searching her as Simran. She was not in position to talk as her mouth was tied. The evidence of the victim is also contrary to her statement before police. She had exaggerated her evidence. 19] It can be further seen from the evidence on record that the incident took place on 04.03.17 at about 11.15 to 11.30 a.m. Within some time, parents of victim returned back to the house. Victim and Sheetal Navele had disclosed the incident with them. However, the report was lodged on 05.03.17 at late time. No explanation is forwarded by the prosecution for such inordinate delay in lodging F.I.R. 20] P.W.2 Urmila, mother of victim herself turned hostile on material point that accused had put his hand on the chest of her daughter. P.W.3 Vinod is not eye­witness to the incident. P.W.5 in her evidence, has not stated that she had recorded spot panchanama. 21] Accused, victim and Smt. Navele are residing in the same vicinity. Father of complainant was helped by relative of accused to settle in the said Waghobanagar, Kalwa. They both were known to each­other. 11 POCSO Case. No. 109/2017. Delay is not explained by the prosecution. Victim had stated different story before Ld. J.M.F.C. in her statement u/s. 164 of Cr.P.C. (Exh.14), than the story before police in her report (Exh.13). 22] Undoubtedly, no need to corroborate the evidence of victim and her sole evidence can be relied upon for the conviction, subject to its reliability, trustworthiness and inspiring confidence. In the present matter, alleged incident took place at 11.30 a.m. Immediately after some time, her parents returned back and disclosed the incident to them. However, no report was lodged immediately on the date of incident. On the contrary, on 05.03.17, report was lodged at belated stage. There are contradictory statements before different authorities, i.e. police and before Ld. J.M.F.C. in statement u/s. 164 of Cr.P.C. The evidence of material eye­witness i.e. P.W.4 does not inspire confidence. Other witnesses are not material one. P.W.6 is a panch to the spot panchanama. Spot panchanama is proved. Merely spot panchanama is proved, is not sufficient to convict the accused. 23] Having considered the evidence on record, prosecution failed to prove the age of victim that at relevant time, she was below 18 years of age. Therefore, provisions of POCSO are not attracted. Besides, evidence on record is not sufficient to hold guilt of the accused and evidence of victim is not solely reliable as the house of accused and victim are surrounded in the area like chawl. The alleged incident was not taken place at odd time. Therefore, certainly the occupants of rooms in the chawl might had present in their rooms. However, prosecution failed to produce any of them except P.W.4 who had cross terms with the accused. Therefore, I have recorded my findings to both the points in the negative. In the result, I proceed to pass the following order. 12 POCSO Case. No. 109/2017. ORDER 1] Accused Kailas Biharilal Yadav, is hereby, acquitted under sec. 235(1) of the Criminal Procedure Code, of the offences punishable u/s. 354 of I.P.C. and u/s. 8, 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. 2] Accused Kailas Biharilal Yadav, be enlarged on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ with surety of like amount. The effect of this bail order will remain in force for the period of six months from today, as per section 437­(A) of Cr.P.C. 3] Muddemal, if any, being worthless be destroyed after appeal period is over. Koparkhairne, Navi Mumbai the accused hold the hand of victim girl, pulled her towards him, applied kumkum on her forehead and thereby sexually assaulted her ? …Not proved. 2] What order ? ..As per final order. : REASONS : As to the Point No.1 :­ 7] To bring home the guilt of the accused the prosecution has examined victim's mother Mrs.Heera Mahadev Chakravarti as PW1 at Exh.6. --1-- ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN CRIMINAL BAIL APPLICATION NO.1140/2018 CNR NO. MHTH01­003276­2018 The applicant Sorab Sardar Khan has applied for bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C.,in C.R.No.I­84/2018 registered in Shantinagar police station for the offence under section 376, 354 of IPC and Section 4,8,12 of POCSO Act, 2012. 2. It is contended that the applicant is falsely implicated. The applicant has strain relation with the informant. There was exchange of words took place between them. There is delay in lodging FIR. As per the medical certificate it is not evident of sexual assault. There is no criminal antecedent. Therefore, applicant prayed for bail. 3. Investigating Officer has given say at Exh.4. It is contended that the applicant has committed fingering with the minor girl aged 4 years. The victim has immediately reported the incident to her parents and FIR was lodged immediately. The offence is serious in nature, if the applicant is released on bail he is likely to tamper the prosecution witnesses. The applicant is resident of another State. He is not likely to remain present for the trial. 4. I heard Ld. Counsel on behalf of accused and Ld. APP. 5. I perused investigation papers which are produced before the court for perusal. The victim has given statement before the police that the accused has inserted finger into her private part. She shouted, therefore, accused ran away. She reported the incident to her parents. In 164 Cr. P.C statement --2-- also she narrated the same incident. As per the medical certificate her hymen is turned in 6'O clock position. The incident took place at 9.30 p.m. She reported the incident to her mother immediately. There is no delay in lodging FIR. There are three witnesses who had heard shouting and they asked to the accused above incident. Accused prayed apology by saying “Galti maff karo, mai yaha nahi rahunga”. So considering these investigation papers on record there is strong prima facie case made out. Accused is 30 years old and victim is 4 years old. Accused is resident of another State. The offence is very heinous in nature, therefore, if the accused is released on bail he is likely to tamper the victim and witnesses and will jump on bail and will repeat the offence. Therefore, I proceed to pass following order. :ORDER: Application is rejected. Thane. ( S.C. Khalipe ) Date :18/06/2018. Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­003280­2016 Special Case (POCSO) No. 124/2016 Received on : 11/05/2016 Registered on : 11/05/2016 Decided on : 11/10/2018 Duration : 2Ys. 6Ms. 0Ds. IN THE COURT OF D.J.­1 & ADDL. SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE. (Presided over by Hemant M. Patwardhan) Special Case (POCSO) No.124/2016 Exh.No. 32 State of Maharashtra, (Shrinagar Police station, Thane) ..Complainant V/s. Shankar Mandari Shinge Age : 55 years. R/o.: Ramnagar, Amma Chawl, behind Hanuman temple, Wagle Estate, Thane. ..Accused Appearance:­ APP Mr. Londhe for the State. Advocate Shri. O.P.Singh for accused JUDGMENT (Delivered on this 11th day of October 2018) Accused Shankar Mandari Shinge was facing trial under sections 354­A(1)(i), 363, 342 of Indian Penal Code read with Sec. 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 on following facts:­ 1 OF 14 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­003280­2016 Special Case (POCSO) No. 124/2016 1] That on 16/02/2015 at about 13.30 hrs. at Ramnagar, Amma Chawl, Wagle Estate, Thane within the jurisdiction of Shrinagar police station, the accused sexually harassed victim­girl aged about 3 years by physical contacts and advances involving the unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures and accused has committed said sexual harassment after having kidnapped minor girl from the lawful guardianship of her parents and by wrongfully confining her in the room where he was residing. According to the allegations, at the relevant time, as the victim­girl was only 3 years old, the act of the accused also involved punishment under section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. Hence, on complaint of mother of the victim, an offence under aforesaid sections came to be registered against the accused. 2] My Ld. Predecessor has framed charge against the accused below Exh.5 and has certified that contents of said charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. Accused pleaded not guilty and claim to be tried. His defence was of total denial and that in order to avoid payment of security deposit of Rs.10,000/­, the victim's mother has implicated him in this false case. 3] Prosecution was then proceeded to examine complainant Shabana Firoz Shaikh, independent witness Zarina Shaikh and investigating officer Smt. Lalita Shankar Gavit as the witnesses No.1 to 3 respectively. On completion of their depositions, the statement of accused was recorded as per his say wherein he has again reiterated his defence as above. 2 OF 14 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­003280­2016 Special Case (POCSO) No. 124/2016 4] The arguments of the rival Advocate were heard. Ld. P.P. has categorically pointed out that, all witnesses examined have categorically deposed and support prosecution as per allegations. He has pointed out that, initially, Pw/2 has seen the incident and has then, immediately intimated it to the mother of the victim viz. Pw­1 Shabana Firoz Shaikh and then the mother of the victim, the said witness along with other family members had immediately rushed to the room of the accused and as per the instructions of Pw­2 they saw through the window that, the accused has made the victim lying on mattress and accused himself was wearing towel on his person, he has moved maxi of the victim on the upper side and nicker on lower side and moving his hands over her private part. Therefore, mother of the victim has shouted, knocked the door rigorously and when the accused had opened the door, they went inside the room, have made the victim to wear the cloths and then immediately rushed to police station to lodge complaint. Hence, according to the Ld. P.P., there is absolutely no room for the witnesses to have a second thought about the implication of the accused in the matter therefore, their depositions are sufficient to prove the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt. According to Ld. P.P. Pw­2 who initially witnessed the incident, has also corroborated the version of the complainant and stick­up to her own version with minor variances in her deposition. Hence, said depositions are sufficient to substantiate allegations. While making submissions, on defence that, he was falsely implicated 3 OF 14 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­003280­2016 Special Case (POCSO) No. 124/2016 in the matter to avoid the payment of security deposit, it is submitted by the Ld. P.P. that, there is absolutely nothing on record to show that, there was no dispute in respect of refund of amount of the security deposit of the accused person, at any point of time between the parties. Hence, according to him, the said defence can easily be discarded and the accused has to be convicted as per the allegations leveled against him. 5] Per contra, defence has filed written notes of arguments below Exh.31 thereby contending that, the accused has been falsely implicated in the case. All the witnesses have given false and fabricated statement. According to defence, though, the witnesses have claimed to have seen the incident from the window of the particular room, as a matter of fact, there is no such window to the said room and thus, all avernments of the witnesses about it can be easily discarded. According to arguments, the original complainant is the owner of the room where the accused is residing and there was a dispute about payment of security deposit amount of Rs.10,000/­ and though, the accused was claiming that amount of security deposit from complainant, for one or the other reason, the complainant had avoided it and in order to avoid it permanently, the complainant has implicated the accused in this matter. According to the accused, he has no criminal antecedents till the date of his implication in this matter therefore, allegation has to be discarded. According to him, there is no direct role of the accused in commission of any of the alleged offences or the requirement of 4 OF 14 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­003280­2016 Special Case (POCSO) No. 124/2016 sections 363, 342 are not being properly established. Thus, according to the accused he is entitled to be acquitted from all the said accusations. 6] After hearing Ld. Advocates, following points arise for my consideration and I record my findings against each of them for the reasons noted below:­ S.N. Points Findings 1] Does the prosecution prove that accused on 16/02/2015 at about ..In the 13.30 hrs. in afternoon, at Ramnagar Amma chawl, behind affirmative. Hanuman temple, Wagle Estate, Thane, within jurisdiction of Shrinagar police station, have sexually harassed informant's daughter i.e. minor victim­girl aged 3 years, by physical contact and advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 354­A(1) (i)of IPC? 2] Does the prosecution prove that accused on aforesaid date, time and ..In the place, kidnapped a minor victim­girl aged 3 years out of keeping of negative the lawful guardianship of her parents without her consent and thereby committed an offence punishable under Sec. 363 of Indian Penal Code? 3] Does the prosecution prove that accused on aforesaid date, time and ..In the place, wrongfully confined informant's mother victim­girl aged 3 negative. years and thereby committed an offence punishable under sec.342 of Indian Penal Code? 4] Does the prosecution prove that accused on aforesaid date, time and ..In the place, committed sexual assault on minor victim­girl, aged 3 years affirmative. by moving his hand on private part of the victim and sexual intent which involved physical contact without penetration and thereby committed an offence punishable under Sec. 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012? 5] What order ? Accused is convicted as per final order. 5 OF 14 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­003280­2016 Special Case (POCSO) No. 124/2016 REASONS As to point nos. 1 to 5 :­ 7] All these points are interlinked with each other and are discussed at once. The prosecution has alleged that, on 16/02/2015 at about 13.30 hrs. in a room of the accused situated at Ramnagar, Amma chawl, behind Hanuman temple, wagle estate, Thane, within the jurisdiction of Shrinagar police station, the accused had initially kidnapped a minor victim­girl aged about 3 years out of the keeping of the lawful guardianship of her parents, without her consent and then has confined the minor victim­girl wrongfully in a room and then has sexually harassed her by his act with sexual intent. Therefore, the prosecution was required to prove the said allegations by consistent and reliable evidence. The prosecution, in order to prove guilt of the accused, has examined aforesaid three witnesses. Out of the said three witnesses Pw­1 and Pw­2 are eye witnesses of the incident, whereas Pw­3 is the investigating officer. Though, the prosecution has not examined panch witnesses, the said panchnama of spot was duly proved during the deposition of I.O. The said spot panchnama is not seriously challenged by the defence. Hence, even though, the panch witnesses were not examined, then also the panchnama can be considered in view of aforesaid facts. After the depositions of said witnesses, rival Advocates have made aforesaid arguments thereby claiming relief in their favour. Therefore, the Court has to consider the deposition of said witnesses on the background of the defence put forth by the accused person. 6 OF 14 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­003280­2016 Special Case (POCSO) No. 124/2016 8] The prosecution witness No.1 is the complainant­eye witness and witness No.2 is eye witness who initially has seen the wrong done by the accused with the daughter of the complainant and rushed to inform the complainant about it. According to the deposition of Pw­1 after having heard, the witness No.2 who has narrated the fact in short to her, she along with her family members immediately rushed towards the room of the accused person and when they reached near the room witness No.2 had asked her to see as to what actually had happening in the room through the window. Therefore, as per the substantive evidence of the complainant, when she had seen through the window, she has found that, the accused has made the victim to sleep on the mattress and has knowingly removed her nicker and was moving his hand over her private part. As a matter of fact, according to her substantive evidence, she has then shouted rigorously and forced the accused to open the door, entered the house of the accused, made victim to wear cloths properly and rushed to the police station. 9] Pw­2 has also categorically deposed during her substantive evidence that, she herself heard some noise and then came down to see as to the source of the noise and had seen that, the accused has committed said act in his room, from his window and then immediately rushed to the house of the mother of victim, informed her about the incident. Both the witnesses were cross­examined at length. Except there being some variance of facts prior to their 7 OF 14 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­003280­2016 Special Case (POCSO) No. 124/2016 visiting the room of the accused, the defence was not able to illicit any admission from the witnesses which are sufficient to create even doubt about the happening of the incident. Though, there is some variance in the deposition of Pw­2 Zarina, the said variance would bound to occur in view of the passage of time. As a matter of fact, the variance was about hearing some noise by the said witness. As a matter of fact, in her police statement, she has never made any reference about hearing any noise at the relevant time, but she has stated that on the above date, time and place, the accused has taken the victim in his house therefore, she has seen from the window as to what the accused is doing and then, has seen the aforesaid act of the accused as narrated by her. Therefore, the only contradiction in her statement is about hearing of noise which is missing during her statement. However, said contradiction or variance in her statement can be easily discarded being not of materially importance. 10] The material defence in the matter were, there was no window to the room, so none of the witnesses could be able to say anything as what was happening in the room and that, the accused person is a tenant of the complainant and before vacating the premises, he wish to recover the amount of Rs.10,000/­ towards security deposit but the complainant was avoiding to pay it and in order to avoid it, has implicated him in this case. No doubt, in the notes of argument and in the statement, reference has been made about said security deposit and his demand for said security deposit. 8 OF 14 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­003280­2016 Special Case (POCSO) No. 124/2016 However, during substantive evidence of the original complainant, there is absolutely no reference made of said fact. The original complainant being owner of the room, was the best available witness from whom the defence could easily obtain admission about said dispute, if the said dispute really exist as narrated by the accused persons. However, when the accused, for the best reason known to him, has failed to make whisper about said defence to the original complainant, then it is difficult to accept that, any such dispute was really pending between the original complainant and accused person. Said defence was only put forth by Pw­2 who has nothing to do with either ownership of the room or repayment of security deposit of the room. Therefore, when the said suggestions were put forth, she was bound to deny it and accordingly said witness had denied it. Having regard to this, it is difficult to accept that, there was any such dispute really going on between the parties, to implicate the accused in such case. Accused would have easily created a doubt about occurrence of the incident by either his own substantive evidence or by evidence of any other independent witness who is aware of the dispute between the complainant and the accused on the point of payment of said security deposit. It is nowhere case of accused that, he has vacated the room, so that, it was not possible for him to recover it in any other way. As a matter of fact, if the accused is in possession of the room, he could recover security deposit by remaining in the lease 9 OF 14 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­003280­2016 Special Case (POCSO) No. 124/2016 premises, that too, without payment of either rent or license fee, as the case may be till the time of recovery of his amount of Rs.10,000/­ as claimed by him. 11] So far as the defence of the accused that there was no window in the said room therefore all said allegations of witnesses having seen the incident from the said window can be easily discarded. However, the said defence can be easily discarded on two­ fold grounds viz. that there is hardly any specific suggestion to the witness that the room is without the window and secondly that the said fact has been categorically referred in spot panchanama which the defence has not challenged seriously. Though panch witnesses were not examined, I.O. has categorically made reference of having conducted the spot panchanama in presence of the panchas making reference of window in it. In absence of said being challenged properly can be considered against the defence. Therefore, in absence of any such fact on record, it is difficult to say whatever defence put forth by the accused is really sufficient to consider any occurrence of the incident as alleged by the witness. There is absolutely no other reason which was put forth by the accused or any reference is made about it, to implicate accused in any such false case. Having regard to these facts, as the defence is not sufficient to create doubt about occurrence of incident, the presumption under section 29 of the POCSO Act has to be raised. Having regard to the said fact, the evidence of said witness appears to be consistent, 10 OF 14 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­003280­2016 Special Case (POCSO) No. 124/2016 reliable to raise such presumption. The case of the prosecution has proved beyond reasonable dobut. 12] Now, turning towards the crucial point as to under which sections of which act the offence really is established. In the instant case, the allegations are made under section 363 and 342 of I.P.C. which deals with kidnapping of any person from legal guardianship of parents and about wrongful confinement. In the instant case, though the allegations are made under said sections only on the basis of the fact that, the victim was found in the room of the accused person. However, nobody has adduced any evidence before the Court or has claimed to have seen the accused himself abducting or kidnapping the victim or a particular place where she was allegedly playing, as per the substantive evidence of original complainant. Therefore, there is absolutely no evidence before this Court as to how the victim has reached the room of the accused person. Hence, unless that link is established before the Court, it is difficult to accept that, it is the accused alone himself who has kidnapped or abducted from lawful guardianship from her parents. If that fact is not established, subsequent allegations under section 342 of I.P.C. also are not said to be properly established. Having regard to this fact, I am not inclined to accept the allegations to convict under such sections. 13] So far as the allegations under section 354­A(1)(i) of I.P.C., and under section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act are concerned, the 11 OF 14 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­003280­2016 Special Case (POCSO) No. 124/2016 depositions of the witnesses are really sufficient to establish the necessary ingredients of Section 354­A of I.P.C. If we consider act alleged against accused at the relevant time, moving his hand over the private part of the female­child, when she was only left alone in room, also can be considered as intentional outraging her modesty. So also, if the intention of the accused can be gathered which is material ingredient of Section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, then, by his act of being himself on towel on him and by having moved maxi of the victim on upper side and nicker on the lower side, and moving his hand over her private part is sufficient to establish, his intentional sexual harassment. Hence, in my opinion, allegations of the prosecution under section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act or under sec. 354 of I.P.C. can be said to be established beyond reasonable doubt, as the evidence brought before this Court is consistent and reliable, so far as the allegations under this section are concerned. As referred above, the said evidence are certainly sufficient to raise presumption referred under section 29 of P.O.C.S.O. Act as well as considering the mental state of the accused at the relevant time. Once that presumption is raised, onus was shifted on accused to disprove it, but even when the onus was shifted on him, he was not able to even establish the slightest doubt in respect of the occurrence of the particular incident, to destroy any evidence. The defence put forth by the accused, in view of aforesaid finding is certainly insufficient to create any doubt about the occurrence of the incident or to discard said presumption. Hence, Court has to accept the said allegations, as 12 OF 14 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­003280­2016 Special Case (POCSO) No. 124/2016 the prosecution has established the guilt of the accused under section 354­A(1) (i) r/w Section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. I do not hesitate to record my findings, so far as said allegations are concerned, I record my findings that, the accused is guilty of the offence. As I hold the accused guilty of the offence, the Judgment is deferred for hearing accused on the point of sentence. Thane (Hemant M. Patwardhan) Date: 05.10.2018. D.J.­1 & Addl. Sessions Judge, Thane. 14] Heard the accused on the point of sentence. Accused has requested to take lenient view considering that there was no criminal antecedents to his discredit and his age. Also, heard learned advocate of the accused Mr. Singh who has requested to release the accused on good behaviour bond by exercising power under section 360 of Cr.P.C. Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor Mr. Londhe has strongly objected the submissions of accused's advocate of granting him relief under section 360 of cr.P.C. on the ground that heinous offence has been committed and if such accused are granted relief under that section that will be a wrong signal in the society. 15] After having heard the rival advocates, I have gone through the said provisions. However, though the relief under the said 13 OF 14 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­003280­2016 Special Case (POCSO) No. 124/2016 section has been claimed, considering the nature of offence and special status of the Act, the facts and circumstances in which the offence has been committed in my opinion the said submissions of the defence advocate of extending the benefit under section 360 of Cr.P.C. has to be discarded. Once it is discarded sufficient punishment has to be awarded. Considering the said circumstance in my opinion following order would serve the purpose of both the sides. Hence, the order. ORDER 1] Accused Shankar Mandari Shinge is hereby convicted for the offence punishable under section 354(A)(1) of IPC read with section 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and he is sentenced to suffer R.I. for three years under section 8 of POCSO Act and shall also liable to pay fine of Rs.500/­ in default to suffer further R.I. for 10 days and six months under section 354(A) (1) of IPC 2] All the sentences shall run concurrently and set off is granted under section 428 of Cr.P.C. for the period already undergone by the accused while the accused was in judicial custody. 3] Accused to surrender his bail bonds forthwith. 4] Muddemal property clothes etc. being worthless be destroyed after appeal period. Thane (Hemant M. Patwardhan) Date: 11.10.2018. D.J.­1 & Addl. Sessions Judge, Thane. 14 OF 14

ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 1] By this application the applicant is seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C., who was arrested on 01/05/2015 by Mumbra police station in connection with C.R.No.I­441/2015 registered for an offence punishable under section­ 324 of I.P. Code & section­ 3 (b), 4, 7 & 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] Heard learned advocate Mr. Javed Shaikh for the applicant/accused and Ld. A.P.P. Mrs. S.E. Phad for State. I.O. Present with case diary. 3] The FIR came to be registered on 01/05/2015 at the instance of informant Lal Mohammed Thaga Shaikh with an indictment that accused is his second wife, who injured his five years old daughter by inserting her finger in her private part. 4] The Ld. Counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant is falsely implicated. He submitted that the real mother of the victim­child left her and the present applicant is looking after her. He submitted that applicant called the victim­child for food but she was running and when accused tried to caught her at 2 Bail Appln. No.1230/2015(O/Exh.-1) that time, due to fall, she received injuries to her private part. He submitted that FIR came to be registered on second day only due to pressure of the neighbours. The applicant was not having any intention to cause any injury to the girl. She is behind bar since one month. There is nobody to look after her small girl. The applicant is ready to abide by any conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing her on bail. 5] Per contra, the Ld. A.P.P. strongly opposed the application submitting that the offence is serious. The applicant who is step­mother of the victim­child aged about 5 years, injured her private parts by inserting her finger. The victim­child in her statement also stated about the act of accused. The Medical certificate clearly shows injury on her private parts. The Investigation is still in progress. There are chances of tampering of witnesses and prayed for rejection of application. 6] Upon perusal of FIR, it is evidence that the accused who is a step­mother of minor girl­child, committed penetrative sexual assault by inserting her finger into vagina of minor girl. The statement of victim­child shows that accused used to commit such act with her frequently. The medical examination certificate of victim of sexual assault shows multiple scratches over pubic and vulva region, contusion over supra pubic region, multiple scratches found present on labia majora and labia minora. These statutes have been enacted in the recent past though not effectively implemented. Given this situation, we are of opinion that a few facts need to be acknowledged and accepted. Firstly, a child is and remains a child regardless of the description or nomenclature given to the child. It is universally accepted in almost all relevant statutes in our country that a child is a person below 18 years of age. Therefore, a child remains a child whether she is described as a street child or a surrendered child or an abandoned child or an adopted child. Similarly, a child remains a child whether she is a married child or an unmarried child or a divorced child or a separated child or a widowed child. At this juncture I defer the Judgment to hear the accused on the quantum of sentence. Thane. (P.P.Jadhav) District Judge­6 and Date : 02.12.2017. Addl. On the contrary the learned A.P.P. vehemently submitted that the offence being serious, maximum punishment prescribed for the Act be imposed upon the accused. 19] As already observed while recording finding on above points, the parents being custodians of minor girl are entrusted with her welfare. Certainly during the age of minority the parents having right over the custody of minor child, kidnapping of such a minor is an offence against them. It certainly badly effects their reputation as well as frustrate J­SplCase ­129­16 ­ 363,376(2)(n), 366­A,IPC & 8 POCSO.doc .....13/­ ..13.. 1 Special Case No.119/2014 (Judgment) Presented on : 05/06/2014 Registered on : 05/06/2014 Decided on : 05/03/2016 Duration :1­year,9­Months,00­days. IN THE COURT OF THE SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE (Presided over by Ms.U.M.Nandeshwar, Additional Sessions Judge­1, Thane) SPECIAL CASE No. 119 of 2014 Exhibit No. 21. The State of Maharashtra Through Vartaknagar Police Station Thane, District – Thane. ... Prosecution versus Manoj Bhagwat Khatekar Age 27 years, Residence –Lokmanyanagar, Samarth colony, Pada No.3, Choutinagar, Thane. ... Accused Offence punishable under section 354 of Indian Penal Code and under section 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Appearance ­ Spl.P.P. Mrs. R.A. Navale, for the State. Advocate Mr.B.R.Jaiswal, for the Accused. 2 Special Case No.119/2014 (Judgment) JUDGMENT (Delivered on 5th March, 2016.) 1] The Accused stands prosecuted for the offence punishable under section 354 of Indian Penal Code and also under section 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act) for committing sexual assault on minor victim­girl aged about 13 years. 2] The indictment against the Accused are as under ­ [i] Informant victim­girl (P.W.1) is residence of Lokmanyanagar Pada, and staying there with the family of her uncle. Victim­girl was student of 9 th std. and attending private tuition class by name 'Decent Academy' at Yashodara Nagar, Thane. [ii] On 18/12/2013 informant/victim­girl (PW.1) as usual attended her class at 03.00 p.m. and her tuition teacher Manoj Khatekar (Accused) was alone present in the class who used to taught her History and Geography. At that time, accused asked victim­girl to switch off the fan and when she entered in the room, accused followed her and closed the door. Victim­girl asked her why he closed door, on that accused put his hand on her waist and told her not to worry. Victim­girl resisted and by opening door, went away. Victim­ girl narrated incident to her Aunt. On advise of her Aunt, victim­girl stopped going to tution­class. 3 Special Case No.119/2014 (Judgment) [iii] On next day, victim­girl's friend Jayashree Wayal told her that accused used to did the similar act with other girl students and they have also stopped going to the class of accused. Therefore, informant narrated the incident to her neighbourer uncle Ajay Kadam on 01/01/2014. On 05/01/2014 informant with her uncle and friend Jayashree had been to class to verify and confirm information, but accused was not present there. Thereafter, on next day on asking, accused gave vague answers. Therefore, on 06/01/2014 the informant lodged report against the accused. 3] On her report F.I.R. was registered against the Accused vide C.R.No.I­09/2014 for the offence punishable under section 354 of I.P.C. and under section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. The investigation was carried out by A.P.I. Avinash Mahajan (P.W.2). The Accused was arrested in presence of panchas. On 07/01/2014 P.W.2 visited the spot and drawn spot panchnama in presence of panchas. Statements of witnesses were recorded as per their say. Thereafter, investigation culminated into filing of charge­sheet in this Court being the Special designated court under P.O.C.S.O. Act. 4] My learned predecessor the erstwhile Special Judge Shri. H.M.Patwardhan framed the charge (Exh.6) against the Accused for offence punishable under section 354 of Indian Penal Code and also under section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. The 4 Special Case No.119/2014 (Judgment) Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial (Exh.7). The Accused took defence of total denial. 5] In response to application under section 294 of Cr.P.C. the defence has admitted arrest panchnama [Exh.17] and spot panchnama [Exh.18]. 6] In order to prove guilt of Accused Prosecution has examined following witnesses ­ P.W.1 Informant­ victim­girl Exh.15 P.W.2 Shri. Avinash Ramdas Mahajan Exh.19 (Investigating officer.) 7] The prosecution proved and relied on the report /F.I.R. (Exh.16). 8] The prosecution closed its side of evidence by filing Pursis at Exhibit­20. The incriminating evidence came on record against the Accused was read over and explained him and his statement under Section 313(b) of Cr.P.C. was recorded. Accused neither examined himself nor examined any witness in his defence. 9] Heard learned A.P.P. Mrs. R. A. Navale for State and the learned advocate Mr.B.R.Jaiswal for Accused. 10] On consideration of argument advanced on behalf 5 Special Case No.119/2014 (Judgment) of both the sides and on perusal of the oral & documentary evidence on record, following points arise for my determination, which are answered with the findings thereon, as under :­ Sr. Points Findings No. 1 ) Does the prosecution prove that on 18/12/2013 around 03.00 p.m. in 'Decent Academy' Yashodhan Nagar, Thane(W), accused used criminal ..No. force and touched victim­girl's waist with intent to outrage her modesty and he thereby committed an offence punishable under section 354 of Indian Penal Code ? 2 ) Does the prosecution prove that on the same date, time and place, accused touched the waist of the victim with sexual intent and thereby ..No. committed sexual assault on the said minor girl and he thereby committed an offence punishable under section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, 2012 ? 3) What order ? Accused is acquitted. REASONS As to Point No.1 & 2 : 11] Both the points are taken up together for discussion, to avoid the repetition, as evidence about the same in common and inter­connected. 6 Special Case No.119/2014 (Judgment) Age of victim­girl is 14 Years : 12] As the Accused is facing charge under P.O.C.S.O. Act, therefore, it is incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that the victim­girl was child (minor) at the time of incident. The alleged incident took place on 18/12/2013. Informant (P.W.1) deposed that her date of birth is 28/09/1999 and in the year­2013 she was studying in 9 th std. There is absolutely no challenge to the age of victim­girl. Thus, the prosecution proved that at the time of incident, the victim­girl was minor aged about 14 years i.e. below the age of 18 years and she was a “child” as per definition given in Section 2(d) of P.O.C.S.O. Act. 13] Further, as the Accused is facing charge under section 354 of I.P.C. it is incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that Accused either assaults or used criminal force towards victim­girl to outrage her modesty or knowing it to be likely that he will, by his act, outrage the modesty of the victim­girl. So also as the Accused is facing charge under section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, therefore, it is further incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that the Accused with sexual intent touched the vagina, penis, anus, breast of a child or make the child touched vagina, penis, anus, breast of such person or any other person or does any other act with sexual intent which involves physical contact without penetration and by his such act committed sexual assault as defined in section 7 Special Case No.119/2014 (Judgment) 7 of the P.O.C.SO. Act. 14] To prove the charge against the Accused the prosecution has examined the informant / victim­girl who is the most material witnesses to prove the charge against the Accused. Informant / victim­girl (P.W.1) deposed that in the year­2013 she was studying in 9th std. and was attending 'Decent Academy' for private coaching class. Her class time were 03.00 p.m. to 06.00 p.m. Accused was her teacher who used to teach her History and Geography. The victim­girl further deposed that the incident is of the year­2013 when she attended the class as usual. On that day, she went inside the room to switch off the fan. At that time, accused came inside the room and closed door. She questioned him why he closed the door. On that he said not to worry and will not do anything to her, but put his hands on her waist and she opened the door and came outside. She further deposed that she narrated the incident to her uncle and stopped going to the class and then lodged report against the accused by going to police station with her neighbourer uncle Ajay Kadam. 15] The bare perusal of the evidence of victim­girl did not disclose the date of incident. Further if FIR which is at Exh.16 is perused, as per the FIR the incident in question was taken place on 18/12/2013 and FIR came to be lodged on 06/01/2014. Thus, there appears a delay of about 19 days in 8 Special Case No.119/2014 (Judgment) lodging the FIR. However, victim­girl did not give any explanation about the delay caused in lodging FIR. Further, in cross­examination the victim­girl clearly admits that there are about 18 to 20 students in the class including 14 to 15 girl students and on the alleged date of incident, other students were also present in the class. In such circumstances, there is some scope for doubt, whether the accused, had really touched the victim­girl inappropriately in presence of various students. Further victim­girl admits that no other girl student had ever lodged any complaint of sexual harassment against the accused. Further material admission given by the victim­girl is that she lodged the report against the accused out of mis­ understanding, which again create a lot of doubt about the actual happening of the incident. It is significant to note that victim­girl admits that now she has no complaint or grievance against the accused. Thus, the testimony of victim­girl is sketchy and shaky and does not inspire confidence. 16] The evidence of investigating officer A.P.I. Avinash Mahajan (P.W.2) is formal in nature who recorded the complaint of informant as per her say and executed the spot panchnama and recorded the statement of witnesses. Thus, there is no cogent proof and believable evidence on record to support the prosecution version. Thus, prosecution failed to prove beyond reasonable doubt that accused with sexual intent inappropriately touched minor victim­girl by using criminal 9 Special Case No.119/2014 (Judgment) force and outraged her modesty or committed sexual assault on her. Hence, I answer point No.1 & 2 in negative. Therefore, the Accused is entitled for acquittal. 17] In the result, I proceed to pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused Manoj Bhagwat Khatekar is hereby acquitted U/Sec. 235(1) of Cr.P.C. for the offence punishable U/Sec.354 of Indian Penal Code and U/s.8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] His bail bonds stand cancelled and sureties are discharged. 3] The Accused is directed to furnish bail bond of the amount of ₹15,000/­ with one solvent surety in the like amount in compliance of provision of section 437­A of Cr.P.C. The judgment is dictated and pronounced in open Court. Date : 05/03/2016. (Ms. U. M. Nandeshwar), Thane Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act),Thane. District Judge ­1 and Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

1 Special Case No.113/2015 (Judgment) Presented on : 19.05.2015 Registered on : 19.05.2015 Decided on : 13.11.2017 Duration Y M D 02 03 25 IN THE COURT OF SESSIONS JUDGE­1 & SPECIAL JUDGE [POCSO] ACT, THANE AT : THANE (Presided over by V.V.Bambarde, Additional Sessions Judge­1 & Special Judge (POCSO) Act, Thane ) SPECIAL CASE NO.113/2015 EXH.No. 28. State of Maharashtra ( Through Thanenagar Police Stn.) ...Complainant Vs. Rahulkumar Verma, Age :­Adult, …. Accused R/at No. 17/441, 'H' Block, Near Janata Public School, Sangam Vihar, New Delhi. Offence Punishable Under Sec. 363,366 of IPC, S.17 & 18 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and S. 66 (C) of Information Technology Act, 2000. ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ Appearances : Shri. S.D.Londhe, Ld. Spl.P.P. for the State. Mr. Rajeshkumar, Ld.Advocate for the accused. ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ 2 Special Case No.113/2015 (Judgment) :JUDGMENT: (Delivered on 13th day of November, 2017) 1] The accused in the Court dock is tried for offence under S. 363, 366 of IPC, S. 17 & 18 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and S. 66 (C) of Information Technology Act, 2000 on the accusation of having been kidnapping minor victim girl, forcing her for illicit intercourse, sexually assaulting her and chatting with her on the face book. 2] Case of prosecution, in brief, is that a victim girl was studying in 11th standard in M.H.Junior College, Thane. She received request from the accused on Face Book which she accepted. The accused started communication on the face book. The victim girl accepted the request of accused to have friendship. She was informed that accused is studying in 12 th standard and was working at call center. The accused met the girl. The accused promised her to marry. The accused induced her and took her to Delhi. They had physical relations. Thus, on the pretext of marriage the accused took minor victim girl from the lawful guardianship of her parents and sexually assaulted her. 3] On the receipt of complaint from the mother of victim girl, police registered offence. The accused was nabbed at his house of Delhi with victim girl. Police brought victim girl and her statement was recorded before Judicial Magistrate. Accused was arrested. Statement of the house owner is also recorded. After completion of investigation, P.I. ­ Ramesh Chavan filed charge sheet in this Court. 4] This Court has framed charge against the accused ( Exh.10 ) for 3 Special Case No.113/2015 (Judgment) offence under Sec. 363, 366 of IPC, S. 17 & 18 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and S. 66 (C) of Information Technology Act, 2000. The contents of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 5] Prosecution examined in all five witnesses to bring home the guilt of accused. Victim girl is (P.W.3). Prosecution examined mother of the victim, Sou. Shilpa Abhay Chachad (P.W.1) and her father, Abhay Chachad (P.W.2). Ramesh Chavan (P.W.4) is investigating officer. Vinay Balaram Patil (P.W.5) is Sub Registrar in Death and Birth Registration Section. 6] The defence of the accused as constructed in cross­examination and statements under Sec. 313 Cr.P.C. is that of false implication. 7] I have heard Ld. Special P.P. for the State and Ld. advocate for the accused. 8] Following points arise for my determination with my findings thereon for reasons to follow: POINTS FINDINGS 01. Does prosecution prove that at around 15.30 …. In the negative. hours at 201, Anand apartment, Bhandar Ali, Opp. Prabhat Talkies, Thane [W], on 28/02/2015, accused kidnapped minor victim girl from the lawful guardianship of her parents? 02 Does prosecution prove that on the aforesaid …. In the negative. date, time and place, accused induced victim girl to leave her home with intent to marry 4 Special Case No.113/2015 (Judgment) her ? 03 Does prosecution prove that on the aforesaid …. In the negative. date, time and place, accused committed sexual assault on a minor girl? 04 Does prosecution prove that during the said …. In the negative. period accused fraudulently got acquainted with the victim girl on Face Book? 05 What order ? Accused is acquitted as per final order. REASONS 9] AS TO POINT NOS.1 TO 4 : I would like to discuss all the points together being interlinked with each other. Shilpa Chachad (P.W.1) is mother of victim girl and serving lady. Abhay Chachad (P.W.2) is father of victim girl. Shilpa (P.W.1) and Abhay (P.W.2) saw that their daughter did not turn up at around 8 p.m. on 28/02/2015. Shilpa (P.W.1) has phoned to Coaching Classes. She learnt that her daughter was absent in Karate Class. They took search of their girl. Shilpa (P.W.1) lodged complaint Exh. 13 about kidnapping of her daughter. Ramesh Chavan (P.W.4) took up charge of this case. He received information that victim girl had been to Delhi. Ramesh Chavan (P.W.4) went to Sangam Vihar Police Station, Delhi, took help of police, collected location of the accused and nabbed him. He come to know that victim girl was in the house of accused. Victim girl was taken in custody and brought to Thane with accused. 10] Victim girl born on 16/02/1999. She was studying in 11 th standard in M.H. High School, Thane. She was having her own face book account in the mobile hand set. One unknown person started chatting with 5 Special Case No.113/2015 (Judgment) her through face book. She consented for friendship. The person told her that he was in first year B.A. Thereafter the boy told her that he is appearing for 12th standard. He told that he is working in call center, in gas agency and at last in private firm. That person asked her to come to Delhi along with all the documents, he will get her all education completed at Delhi and after getting completed 18 years he will marry with her. That boy come to Thane and met her on 14/02/2015. He insisted girl to come with him to Delhi. He again visited her on 27th February, 2015. They met outside M'cdonald Shop. The accused told her to come with him on next day. The accused forcefully took her to Delhi on 28/02/2015. She stayed at his house till 02/03/2015. The boy went for job on 03/03/2015. Police arrived in the house of accused and arrested him. 11] I have heard Ld. Special P.P. and Ld. Advocate for the accused. The victim girl was 17 years old and was studying in 11 th standard. It has come in her cross­examination that she disclosed her age to the accused in the chat. She was referring accused as “ Janu, Hubby and Babu”. She does not remember that she sent proposal to accused to marry. She does not remember that she sent message to the accused that he was her last hope. But she has admitted that they have love affair and accused has approached her first. They had continuous chat on facebook. On 28/03/2014 she came out side her house with all documents. The girl was above 16 years. She was knowing that she was leaving house for some purpose. It is not in her examination­in­chief that accused has ravished her. It has also come in her cross­examination that accused took her to his home at Delhi directly where his parents reside. It has come in her cross­examination that she has stated to police that she was under pressure of studies and she wanted to share with someone. The mobile 6 Special Case No.113/2015 (Judgment) number of accused was in the mobile handset of Shiopa (P.W.1). It means that mother had a chance to know about a boy since his number was in her handset. 12] The evidence on record does not show that accused has compelled or induced the girl to leave Thane for Delhi. It does not appear that the accused was interested in ravishing the girl. The girl above 16 years on her own accord left the house. She had sufficient maturity to know what was right and what was wrong. There is no copy of alleged communication produced in the Court. Similarly, there is no evidence that the accused fraudulently or dishonestly induced the girl. Hence, the accused is entitled for benefit of doubt. In view of this, I answer Point Nos. 1 to 4 in negative and pass following order : ORDER 1] The accused ­Rahulkumar Verma is hereby acquitted of offence under S. 363, 366 of IPC, S. 17 & 18 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and S. 66 (C) of Information Technology Act, 2000. 2] His bail bond stands cancelled. 3] Muddemal property i.e. black coloured mobile (Article No.1), being worthless, be destroyed after appeal period is over. 4] Accused shall furnish P.R. bond of Rs. 15,000/­ in view of proviso 437(A) of Cr.P.C.
