1 Spl.Case (POCSO) No.114/2015 Judgment...Exh.No.17 Received on :­ 20.05.2015 Registered on :­ 20.05.2015 Decided on :­ 18.02.2017 Duration :­ 1Y 8M 28 D IN THE COURT OF ADDITIONAL SESSIONS JUDGE, & SPECIAL JUDGE (POCSO) ACT, THANE AT : THANE ( Presided over by Ashutosh N.Karmarkar, District Judge­1 & Special Judge (POCSO) Act, Thane ) Special Case (POCSO) No.114/2015 Exh. No. 17 State of Maharashtra ( Through Shantinagar Police Stn. Bhiwandi) …Complainant V/s. Mohammad Saiban Iqubal Ansari Age : 25 Years, Occu. : Rickshaw driver R/at.: House No. 3997, Sayara Nagar, Gayatrinagar Road, Shan Hotel, Bhiwandi … Accused. Offence punishable under Sec. 354­A of Indian Penal Code & under Sec. 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2 Spl.Case (POCSO) No.114/2015 Judgment...Exh.No.17 Appearances : Shri. S.D.Londhe, A.P.P. for the State Shri. S.R. Waghmare, Advocate for accused JUDGMENT ( Delivered on this 18th day of February, 2017 ) 1] Accused is facing trial for the offence punishable under Sec. 354­A of Indian Penal Code and under Sec. 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] According to prosecution, informant is residing with her husband Mohd. Ayaz Siddiqui and daughter ( victim) of 12 years of age. The victim is studying in 5th standard. On 20.3.2015, at 7.15 a.m., the victim was proceeding to school by rickshaw. She came back to home at 10.15 a.m. She was looking frightened. Informant made the enquiry. She informed that she was proceeding by rickshaw No. MH­04/AR­3210 at 7.00 a.m. Nobody was in the rickshaw. Rickshaw driver moved his hand over her thigh and leg and uttered the words “Tere ko dekhata hu to mera ru ru khada hota hai”. She was frightened. She alighted from the rickshaw. Informant narrated the incident to her husband. They took search of the rickshaw driver. They learnt that his name was Mohammad Saiban Iqubal Ansari. Then, the mother of the victim approached to police and lodged report. 3] On the basis of report, offence was registered vide 3 Spl.Case (POCSO) No.114/2015 Judgment...Exh.No.17 C.R.No. I­92/2015. P.S.I. Smt. Gaikwad has registered the crime and investigated it. She took the rickshaw involved in the crime and the accused in custody. She drew panchanama of the seizure of rickshaw Exh.14. After completion of investigation, she filed charge­sheet. 4] I have framed charge against accused below Exh. 6 to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. Accused has raised defence that one Zakir was residing in the lane of informant with whom they had talkative terms. There was dispute between said Zakir and accused. Said Zakir has demanded Rs. 50,000/­ from accused and has threatened him that on failure to pay it, he will implicate the accused in a false case. 5] Prosecution has examined four witnesses. Then, the statement of the accused under Sec. 313 came to be recorded. Both the parties are heard. 6] Ld. A.P.P. Shri. Londhe has submitted that the age of victim is not at all disputed. The accused has enquired about the age of the victim and has moved hand over the thigh and leg of the victim and uttered the words as “Tere ko dekhata hu to mera ru ru khada hota hai.” According to him, this fact itself shows that the accused has committed this act with sexual intention. Evidence of victim appears to be natural as she has disclosed the incident to her mother. Their evidence is consistent. According to him, defence is 4 Spl.Case (POCSO) No.114/2015 Judgment...Exh.No.17 also not sustainable since the accused could not bring on record relation between the said Zakir and the informant. It is also submitted that the evidence of rickshaw owner also shows that at the relevant time, the rickshaw involved in the crime was with the accused. The defence has no evidence to save the accused. On the other hand, Ld. Advocate for the accused has submitted that the informant has narrated the incident to her husband but he is not examined. According to him, victim has admitted that while proceeding to school, there are houses and shops to both the sides of the road. Some of the guardians of the students also took them to the school. So, the victim could have stated about the incident to them. It is also submitted that P.W.3 Raees is not having any document to show that rickshaw was handed over to the accused to do the business. Even the said act is not possible while driving the rickshaw. In natural course, the victim could have stated about the incident immediately to the teachers in the school. There is also a police chowky in the way and she could have approached there. 7] Following points arose for my determination and I gave my findings thereon for the reasons stated below: Sr. POINTS FINDINGS No. 1. Does the prosecution prove that the Yes. accused on 20.3.2015, at about 7.30 a.m., at Gayatri Nagar Road, near Datta temple, Bhiwandi, Dist. Thane 5 Spl.Case (POCSO) No.114/2015 Judgment...Exh.No.17 assaulted or used criminal force by causing physical contact and advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures to victim girl, aged 12 years i.e. minor daughter of informant with intention to outrage her modesty? 2. Does the prosecution prove that on Yes. above mentioned date, time and place, accused committed sexual harassment upon a child, aged 12 years by moving his hand on her thigh and uttering words “Tere ko dekhata hu to mera ru ru khada hota hai” with sexual intention? 3. What order? As per final order. REASONS AS TO POINT NOS.1 TO 3 :­ 8] It is well settled that in order to bring home the guilt of accused, prosecution is required to adduce cogent, convincing and reliable evidence. It is also settled that sole testimony of witness is sufficient to base conviction but the rule is that it should inspire confidence in the mind of the Court. Prosecution has examined informant Nafisabano who is the mother of the victim (Exh.8), victim (Exh.10), rickshaw owner Raees Ahmed (Exh.11) and investigation officer Smt. Gaikwad (Exh.13). In order to prove the guilt u/sec. 354­A, the prosecution has to establish that the accused has committed act of physical 6 Spl.Case (POCSO) No.114/2015 Judgment...Exh.No.17 contact and made advances involving sexual overtures. In order to prove the guilt u/sec. 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, prosecution has to establish that the accused uttered any word with the intention that such word shall be heard by the child and it was done with sexual intent. 9] P.W.1 Nafisabano has stated that the victim is her daughter. At the time of incident, the age of victim was 12 years and was studying in Bhiwandi Nizampura Corporation School No.6 in 5th standard. The victim has also stated the same fact that she was studying in 5th standard at the relevant time and her date of birth is 22.9.2003. It is to be noted that the accused has not disputed this fact that the victim was studying in 5 th standard and was of 12 years of age. The accused has not at all denied the said date of birth as stated by victim in her cross­examination. So, I have no hesitation to accept that the victim was minor at the relevant time. 10] P.W.1 Nafisabano has stated that on 20.3.2015, she was at home. Victim went to school at 7.00 a.m. by rickshaw which was of accused. Victim came back from the school at 10.15 a.m. Victim was looking frightened. She made enquiry with victim. Victim has disclosed that the accused touched her thigh and leg in rickshaw. She was alone in rickshaw. Victim has also informed that the accused has uttered the words as “Tere ko dekhata hu to mera ru ru khada hota hai.” Victim has also informed that since she was 7 Spl.Case (POCSO) No.114/2015 Judgment...Exh.No.17 frightened, she alighted from the rickshaw and went to the school. Informant has narrated this fact to her husband on his arrival. They took search of rickshaw driver. Even they lodged report Exh. 9. Admittedly, this witness has not personally seen the incident. Her evidence is based upon the information given by the victim. 11] Victim has also stated that on 20.3.2015, she was proceeding by rickshaw No.MH­04/AR­3210. She was alone in the rickshaw. Rickshaw driver made enquiry about her age. She has shown reluctance to tell her age. The accused has moved his hand over her leg and asked her to accompany him. She objected this act of the accused. Then, rickshaw driver has uttered the words as “Tere ko dekhata hu to mera ru ru khada hota hai.” So, she frightened. She asked rickshaw driver to stop the vehicle. It was stopped. She rushed to the school after throwing fare in the rickshaw. She came to home and narrated the incident and also the rickshaw number to her mother. This witness is cross­examined at length. It does not appear that her evidence is shattered in the cross­examination on material points. The accused has just brought on record in the cross­examination that the victim has omitted to state that the accused asked her to come with him and that the victim had thrown the amount of fare in the rickshaw. 12] Ld. Advocate for the accused has submitted that the victim has admitted that 15 minutes are required to go by rickshaw from Fatimanagar to School. Some of the students go to school by 8 Spl.Case (POCSO) No.114/2015 Judgment...Exh.No.17 walk or parents of some of them takes them to school. It is also admitted by victim that there is Shantinagar police chowky in the way to the school. It is also admitted that there are various shops and houses on the road which go towards her school. So, according to Ld. Advocate for the accused, it was possible for the victim to inform about the incident to any of the person. Even she could have approached the police station. But, the victim is of tender age. Normally, the victim of such age may not approached the police station. In natural course, such victim will certainly narrate such type of incident, if any, to her parents who are very close to her. So, merely because the victim has not approached the police and merely because she has not narrated the incident to her teachers or other person on the way, her testimony can not be disbelieved. There is also nothing in the cross­examination of the victim to hold that there is any reason for the victim to depose against them. In present matter, victim has disclosed about incident to her mother immediately, on returning from school. 13] The evidence of victim gets corroboration from the evidence of her mother. She had also stated the same story as to physical contact by touching the thigh by the accused and utterances of sexually coloured remarks by the accused. There is also nothing in the cross­examination of the informant to discard her testimony. Ld. Advocate for the accused has submitted that the informant has admitted that she can not read and write Marathi. But, the informant has denied that she does not know the 9 Spl.Case (POCSO) No.114/2015 Judgment...Exh.No.17 contents in the report and that police have not recorded her report as per her say. There is also no reason for the informant to report against the accused. The victim has identified the accused. He was a rickshaw driver. She has specifically stated that accused made enquiry about her age when the victim was proceeding by rickshaw. This particular act of the accused itself shows his ill intention. Subsequently, the victim has stated that the accused has moved his hand over her thigh and legs and then, accused uttered the words “Tere ko dekhata hu to mera ru ru khada hota hai.” The evidence of victim also shows that she has opposed the said act of the accused. It makes it clear that the accused has committed this alleged act against the will of the victim. There is also no reason for victim to depose against accused. Her evidence appears to be natural. So, the discussion above lead me to say that the accused has committed the act of physical contact and has made advances involving sexual overtures. 14] The accused has attempted to raise defence that he is implicated on the say of one Zakir who is residing in the lane of the victim and with whom he had a dispute. Victim has just admitted in the cross­examination that one Zakir Ahmad Husein Shaikh was residing in their lane and family of the victim were having talkative terms with said Zakir. The informant has admitted that said Zakir was doing meson work and rickshaw driving work. Informant has also admitted that they were having cordial relations with Zakir. But, the informant and victim have no knowledge about any 10 Spl.Case (POCSO) No.114/2015 Judgment...Exh.No.17 dispute between accused and Zakir in respect of the rickshaw business. Both these witnesses have denied that Zakir has threatened the accused that if amount of Rs. 50,000/­ is not paid to him, he will implicate the accused in the crime. Victim has also denied that since the accused has not paid Rs. 50,000/­ to Zakir she has implicated the accused on say of Zakir. 15] Ld. A.P.P. has rightly submitted that accused could not bring on record any details to show that said Zakir is in close relations with the victim. Nothing has been brought on record by the accused to show that victim's family had a reason to act as per the say of Zakir. In natural course, the victim or her mother will not make such allegations only on the say of one stranger to implicate this accused. So, the discussion above lead me to say that there is no substance in the defence. 16] According to Ld. Advocate for the accused, the accused was not driving rickshaw at the relevant time. But, victim has identified that this accused was rickshaw driver at the relevant time. Accused has brought on record in the cross­examination that 15 minutes are required to go from victim's Fatimanagar to the school. There is allegation of molestation. So, certainly the victim had ample time to observe the accused who has committed this alleged act. 17] Prosecution has examined P.W. Raees who is the owner 11 Spl.Case (POCSO) No.114/2015 Judgment...Exh.No.17 of rickshaw MH­04/AR­3210. Victim has also specifically stated this number of rickshaw by which she was travelled on the day of incident. P.W. Raees Ahmed has stated that he knows the accused Saiban. He has handed over his above noted rickshaw to the accused for driving the same on the condition that he shall give Rs. 250/­ per day to P.W. Raees. The accused was to do rickshaw business for 24 hours. This rickshaw was handed over to the accused in the month of December­2014 and he was doing the business of rickshaw for next 3 to 4 months. He got information about the existence of the rickshaw in police station and that it was seized. It is just brought on record in the cross­examination that this witness was not having document to show that his rickshaw was handed over to the accused for rickshaw business. But, merely because of absence of the documents, the testimony of P.W. Raees can not be discarded. The suggestion is given by accused to P.W. Raees that on the day of incident rickshaw was not in working condition and was in garage. This suggestion itself shows that the accused had concern with the said rickshaw. So, this evidence of P.W. Raees also supports the prosecution story that on the day of incident, rickshaw was with the accused. 18] In order to establish the guilt under Sec. 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, the prosecution is required to establish that the accused communicated the act of uttering any words with intention that it shall be heard by the child and that too with sexual intent. The informant has also stated 12 Spl.Case (POCSO) No.114/2015 Judgment...Exh.No.17 exact words uttered by the accused as “Tere ko dekhata hu to mera ru ru khada hota hai.” Whether such utterance was with sexual intent can be gathered from the facts of particular case. The intention of a person is a state of mind. The accused has also enquired about the age of victim. He has moved his hand over the leg of the victim. Victim had objected his act. Victim was alone in the rickshaw. All these facts show that the accused was having sexual intent to utter such words and there was his involvement in sexual intention. 19] It is already discussed that the evidence of the victim is natural and reliable and it gets corroboration from the evidence of her mother. It is also discussed that the accused has not disputed the age of victim at the time of incident and so she was child within the meaning of Sec. 2(d) of Protection of Children from Sexual offences Act, 2012. So, the discussion above lead me to say that the prosecution has established the offence punishable under Sec. 354­A(1)(i) of Indian Penal Code and also under Sec. 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Since the accused is held guilty, he has to be heard on the point of sentence. 20] Accused has submitted for lenient view considering his age. Ld. Advocate for the accused has submitted that the accused is the only earning member of the family. He has no criminal antecedent. So, lenient view may be taken by imposing fine. Ld. A.P.P. has submitted that the accused has 13 Spl.Case (POCSO) No.114/2015 Judgment...Exh.No.17 committed heinous offence. If the lenient view is taken then, wrong message would go to the society. He has submitted for maximum punishment. Though the accused has prayed for lenient view on the ground of his young age, at the same time, age of the victim is also not to be ignored. Such type of offences are increasing nowadays. 21] Considering the nature of the offence, I am not inclined to grant benefit of Probation of Offenders Act to the accused. The punishment prescribed for the offence under Sec. 354­A(1)(i) is rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years or with fine or with both. The punishment for the offence under Sec. 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act is imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine. The muddemal is already handed over to P.W. Raees Ahmed as stated by him. So, there shall be no order as to muddemal. Considering the submissions and the facts of the case, following order will meet the ends of justice. ORDER 1] Accused Mohammad Saiban Iqubal Ansari is convicted under Sec. 235(2) of Code of Criminal Procedure of the offence punishable under Sec. 354­(A)(1)(i) of Indian Penal Code and is sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 1 ½ year and to pay fine of Rs. 500/­ i.d. to suffer simple imprisonment for three months. 14 Spl.Case (POCSO) No.114/2015 Judgment...Exh.No.17 2] Accused is also convicted for the offence punishable under Sec. 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and is sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 1 ½ year and to pay fine of Rs. 500/­ i.d. to suffer simple imprisonment for three months. 3] Both sentences of imprisonment to run concurrently. 4] His bail bond stands cancelled. 5] Accused is entitled for set off under Sec. 428 of Criminal Procedure Code, if any. 1 Special Case No.122/2014 (Judgment) Presented on : 07/06/2014 Registered on : 07/06/2014 Decided on : 18/04/2016 Duration :1­year,10­Months,11­days. IN THE COURT OF THE SPECIAL JUDGE (P.O.C.S.O.Act), THANE. (Presided over by Ms.U.M.Nandeshwar, Additional Sessions Judge­1, Thane) SPECIAL CASE No. 122 of 2014 Exhibit No.23. The State of Maharashtra Through Rabale Police Station Thane, District – Thane. ... Prosecution VERSUS Sandesh Brahma Dongare Age 22 years, Residence –1383, Sathenagar, NOUCIL Naka, Ghansoli, Navi Mumbai, Dist.­ Thane ... Accused Offence punishable under section 354 of Indian Penal Code and under section 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Appearance ­ Spl.P.P. Mrs. R.A. Navale, for the State. Advocate Shri.D.V. Thakur, for the Accused. 2 Special Case No.122/2014 (Judgment) JUDGMENT (Delivered on 18th April, 2016.) 1] The Accused stands prosecuted for the offence punishable under section 354 of Indian Penal Code and also under section 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act) for committing sexual assault on minor victim­girl aged about 16 years. 2] Shorn of verbiage, the indictment against the Accused are as under ­ [i] Informant / victim­girl (P.W.1) is resident of Sathenagar, Ghansoli, Navi­Mumbai and studying in 9th std. [ii] On 06/05/2014 informant with her 10 months nephew was proceeding from lane towards NOUSIL naka to call her younger brother Pawan. At that time Sandesh (Accused) come from front side and kissed her. Therefore, informant shouted and abused the Accused and hence he run away from there. [iii] Informant returned home and narrated the incident to her mother (P.W.2) and her elder brother Santosh and then on the same day, she lodged the report against the Accused. 3] On her report F.I.R. was registered against the Accused vide C.R.No.I­116/2014 for the offence punishable 3 Special Case No.122/2014 (Judgment) under section 354 of I.P.C. and under section 7 and 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. The investigation was carried out by A.P.I. Arvind Jahadu Walvi (P.W.3). He visited the spot i.e. lane at Sathe Nagar, Nocil Naka in front of house No.1383 which was shown by informant and drawn spot panchnama [Exh.18]. Statements of witnesses were recorded as per their say. The Accused was arrest. Thereafter, investigation culminated into filing of charge­sheet in this Court being the Special designated court under P.O.C.S.O. Act. 4] The charge (Exh.7) was framed against the Accused for offence punishable under section 354 of Indian Penal Code and also under section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. The Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial (Exh.8). The Accused took defence of total denial. 5] In response to application under section 294 of Cr.P.C. the defence has not admitted any document. 6] In order to prove guilt of Accused Prosecution has examined following witnesses ­ P.W.1 Victim­girl Exh.11 P.W.2 Parvati Asaram Wani Exh.14 P.W.3 Shri.Arvind Jahadu Walvi Exh.17 (Investigating officer.) 7] The prosecution proved and relied on the following documents ­ 4 Special Case No.122/2014 (Judgment) Report & printed F.I.R. Exhibit 12 & 13 Spot panchnama Exhibit 18 Arrest form of accused Exhibit 19 8] The prosecution closed its side of evidence by filing Pursis at Exhibit­20. The incriminating evidence came on record against the Accused was read over and explained to him and his statement under Section 313(b) of Cr.P.C. was recorded. Accused neither examined himself nor examined any witness in his defence. 9] Heard learned A.P.P. Mrs. R. A. Navale for State and the learned advocate Shri. D. V. Thakur for Accused at length. 10] On consideration of argument advanced on behalf of both the sides and on perusal of the oral & documentary evidence on record, following points arise for my determination, which are answered with the findings thereon, as under :­ Sr. Points Findings No. 1] Does the prosecution prove that on 06/05/2014 at 13.00 hours at Sathenagar, Noucil Naka, Talawali, Navi Mumbai, accused used criminal force against the minor victim­girl aged about 16 years and kissed her ..No. with intent to outrage her modesty 5 Special Case No.122/2014 (Judgment) and he thereby committed an offence punishable under section 354 of Indian Penal Code ? 2] Does the prosecution prove that on same day, time and place the Accused committed sexual assault on the said minor girl with sexual intent in above ..No. manner and he thereby committed an offence punishable under section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, 2012 ? 3] What order ? Accused is acquitted. REASONS As to Point No.1 & 2 : 11] Both the points are taken up together for discussion, to avoid the repetition, as evidence about the same in common and inter­connected. 12] As the Accused is facing charge under section 354 of I.P.C. it is incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that Accused either assaults or used criminal force towards victim­girl to outrage her modesty or knowing it to be likely that he will, by his act, outrage the modesty of the victim­girl. So also as the Accused is facing charge under section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, therefore, it is further incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that the Accused with sexual intent touched the vagina, penis, anus, breast of a child or make the 6 Special Case No.122/2014 (Judgment) child touched vagina, penis, anus, breast of such person or any other person or does any other act with sexual intent which involves physical contact without penetration and by his such act committed sexual assault as defined in section 7 of the P.O.C.S.O. Act. Age of victim­girl : 13] As the Accused is facing charge under P.O.C.S.O. Act, therefore, first of all it is incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that the victim­girl was child (minor) at the time of incident. The alleged incident took place on 06/05/2014. Informant / victim­girl (P.W.1) deposed that her date of birth is 18/03/1999 and in the year­2014 she was studying in 9th std. However, except the version of the victim­ girl (P.W.1) there is absolutely no documentary evidence on record in support of the age of the victim­girl. Neither the school leaving certificate is filed on record. In present case as the victim­girl girl stated to be at the verge of attending majority therefore it is required to prove with cogent documentary evidence. As there is no such proof on record therefore it is difficult to hold that the victim­girl was minor. Thus, the prosecution failed to prove that at the time of incident, the victim­girl was minor aged about 16 years i.e. below the age of 18 years and she was a “child” as per definition given in Section 2(d) of P.O.C.S.O. Act. 7 Special Case No.122/2014 (Judgment) 14] To prove the charge against the Accused the prosecution has examined the informant / victim­girl who is the most material witness to prove the charge against the Accused. Informant /victim­girl (P.W.1) deposed that she knows accused who is her neighbourer. Victim­girl further deposed that date of birth is 18/03/1999 and at the time of incident, she was studying in 9th std. in Vitthal Rukmini Vidyalaya at Gothivli, Navi Mumbai. P.W.1 further deposed that on 06/05/2014 around 01.00 p.m. her younger brother Pawan was playing. She was proceeding to call him from the lane besides her house. At that time, Sandesh Brahma Dongre (accused) who is staying in their neighbour came towards her and hold her face and kissed her. Therefore, she raised shout and abused the accused and then returned to home. Then she narrated the incident to her mother and brother Santosh. When she abused accused, he ran away from there. Thereafter, she went to Rabale police station and lodged report (Exh.12 & 13)against the accused. Evidence of victim­girl is without any omissions or contradictions. 15] However, in this respect, before proceeding to scrutinized the cross­examination of the victim­girl, it is pertinent to note that it is not the case of prosecution that accused continuously stalking her or prior to this incident he had made any such attempt to outraged the modesty of victim­ girl by making any sound or signals or gesture. In this 8 Special Case No.122/2014 (Judgment) background now from the cross­examination of victim­girl her veracity is required to be tested. The victim­girl (P.W.1) admitted that accused is staying beyond 2 to 3 house from her house and prior to the present incident, her father lodged complaint against the brother of accused in respect of the quarrel. She even admits that said complaint was registered as a non­cognizable case and since then both the families were not on talking terms. Thus, it eloquent that there is dispute between the families of victim­girl and accused. Therefore, there is possibility of false implication and evidence of victim­ girl requires thorough scrutiny. From the tenor of the cross­ examination of the victim­girl, it discerns that the locality where alleged incident took place is thickly populated and having a small lane admeasuring 3 fts. and there are houses on both the sides. Further victim­girl (P.W.1) in cross­ examination stated that accused hold her for about 1.5 minute (90 seconds) and she returned and reached home within 4 to 5 seconds. Which means her house is at the distance of a call and as rightly submitted by learned defence counsel that it is highly impossible that in such a thickly populated locality that too during broad day light the Accused might have hold her for such long time, particularly when the accused and victim­girl's family were not on good terms. Further P.W.1 admitted that at that particular time, the construction of work of her house was in progress and two mesons were working on the site. Therefore, in such circumstances, victim­girl can easily call help from them. But it was not so done which again makes the 9 Special Case No.122/2014 (Judgment) version of the victim­girl doubtful and don't appear probable. 16] Even the mother of victim­girl Parvati (P.W.2) also admits about not having good relationship with the family of accused and the reason is also brought on record, i.e. the accused's family was once the tenant of the parents of the victim­girl and there was dispute about vacating the tenanted premises. Although P.W.2 denied that there is dispute between her family and family of accused, however, she further admits that her husband lodged complaint against accused in the Rabale police station. Unless the person have any complaint or grievance he would not approach the police station. Paevati (P.W.2) even stated that initially accused's family stayed in their house on rent and they did not pay the rent and tried to take forcible possession of their house. Therefore, her husband lodged complaint against father of accused and that complaint was lodged before 9 to 10 years. Thus, it is eloquent that there was and is dispute between both families and on such wake the defence taken by the accused about false implication is most probable. Thus, the evidence of informant/ victim­girl (P.W.1) and her mother (P.W.2) does not inspire confidence and they don't appear to be truthful witnesses. 17] Further the prosecution has examined PS.I. Arvind Walvi (P.W.3) who is investigating officer in the present case. However, from the cross­examination of this witness, it eloquent that this witness do not know the factual position of 10 Special Case No.122/2014 (Judgment) the case and he deposed about the location of the spot and of the house of victim­girl contrary to the location mentioned in the spot panchnama which is at Exh.18. Further, even the investigating officer deposed that immediately after registration of the FIR he proceeded to arrest the accused and he was found at his house. However, as per documents, it appears that the report was lodged on 06/05/2014 and the accused was arrested on 13/05/2014. The arrest form is at Exh.19. Thus, it clearly evident that the investigating officer has no knowledge about it and he entered in the witness box in most casual manner. The casual approach of investigation further discern when investigating officer failed to collect any evidence about the age of victim­girl when the sections of POCSO Act are applied against the accused. Thus, the possibility of the false implication of the accused due to previous enmity cannot be ruled out. 18] Thus, as prosecution failed to prove that the victim­ girl is child, therefore, charge under the P.O.C.S.O. Act would not sustain and therefore even the twin presumption given in section 29 and 30 of the P.O.C.S.O. Act about committing of offence under section 3, 5, 7 & 9 of the Act would not arise and would not come to the help of prosecution. 19] Thus, prosecution failed to prove that accused with sexual intent inappropriately touched minor victim­girl by using criminal force and outraged her modesty. Hence, I 11 Special Case No.122/2014 (Judgment) answer point No.1 & 2 in negative. Therefore, in absence of any reliable and cogent evidence against the Accused, he is entitled for acquittal. 20] In the result, I proceed to pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused Sandesh Brahma Dongare is hereby acquitted U/Sec. 235(1) of Cr.P.C. for the offence punishable U/Sec.354 of Indian Penal Code and U/s. 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] His bail bonds stand cancelled and sureties are discharged. 3] The Accused is directed to furnish bail bond of the amount of ₹15,000/­ with one solvent surety in the like amount in compliance of provision of section 437­A of Cr.P.C. The judgment is dictated and pronounced in open Court. Date : 18/04/2016. (Ms. U. M. Nandeshwar), Thane Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act),Thane. District Judge ­1 and Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

1 Special Case No. 121/2014 (Judgment) Presented on : 07/06/2014 Registered on : 07/06/2014 Decided on : 20/04/2016 Duration :1­year,10­Months,14­days. IN THE COURT OF THE SPECIAL JUDGE, THANE. (Presided over by Ms.U.M.Nandeshwar, Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O.Act) Thane) SPECIAL CASE No. 121 of 2014 Exhibit No.33 The State of Maharashtra Through Rabale MIDC Police Station Thane, District – Thane. ... Prosecution versus Anil Narayan Suradkar Age 23 years, Residence –Near Nimboni Buddha vihar, Ambedkarnagar, Digha, Navi Mumbai. Dist. Thane. ... Accused Offence punishable under section 452 and 354 of Indian Penal Code and under section 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Appearance ­ Spl.P.P. Mrs. R.A. Navale, for the State. Advocate Mrs Reena Korde for the Accused. 2 Special Case No. 121/2014 (Judgment) JUDGMENT (Delivered on 20th April, 2016.) 1] The Accused stands prosecuted for the offence punishable under section 452 & 354 of Indian Penal Code and also under section 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act) for committing sexual assault on minor victim­girl aged about 16 years by entering in her house. 2] Shron of unnecessary details, the indictment against the Accused are as under ­ [i] Informant Dilip Laxman Kharat (Pw­1) is resident of Digha Navi Mumbai. His maternal uncle Manoj Bhise is also staying in his neighbourhood with his family including daughter /victim­girl aged about 16 years. The accused is also staying in front his house and used to came to their house. [ii] On 10/04/2014 in the wee hours around 03.45 a.m. victim­girl alongwith her younger brother Ravi rushed to the house of informant. They were very much frightened and disclosed that their parents took their new born sister to the hospital around 03.30 p.m. and victim­girl forget to latch the door and when she was sleeping, she felt that somebody is touching to her body and moving his hand on her breast. Therefore, she screamed and therefore, her younger brother Ravi switched on the light and noticed that accused was 3 Special Case No. 121/2014 (Judgment) present there and touching her inappropriately. Therefore, informant searched the Accused outside the house and seen the accused running away from there. Informant tried to catch hold the Accused, but taking advantage of the darkness he ran away. Therefore, informant lodged report against the accused on 10/04/2014. 3] On his report F.I.R. was registered against the Accused vide C.R.No.I­59/2014 for the offence punishable under section 452 & 354 of I.P.C. and under section 7 & 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act by Police Nail S.S.Bhoir. The investigation was carried out by A.P.I. Samadhan Vasant Bile (Pw­3). The spot panchnama was drawn. Accused was arrested. The statements of witnesses were recorded. Intimation about registration of offence was given to Child Welfare Committee and District Probation Officer. Thereafter, investigation culminated into filing of charge­sheet in this Court being the Special designated court under P.O.C.S.O. Act. 4] My learned Predecessor erstwhile Special Judge Mrs. V. V. Virkar framed the charge (Exh.2) against the Accused for offence punishable under section 452 & 354 of Indian Penal Code and also under section 7 & 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. The Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial (Exh.3). The Accused took defence of total denial. 4 Special Case No. 121/2014 (Judgment) 5] In response to application under section 294 of Cr.P.C. the defence has admitted spot panchnama [Exh.20] and arrest form of accused [Exh.19]. 6] In order to prove guilt of Accused Prosecution has examined following witnesses ­ P.W.1 Dilip Laxman Kharat Exh.16 Informant / uncle of victim­girl P.W.2 Ravi Manohar Bhise Exh.18 (Brother of victim­girl) P.W.3 Samadhan Vasant Bile Exh.26 (Investigating officer) 7] The prosecution proved and relied on the report / F.I.R. Exh.17. 8] The prosecution closed its side of evidence by filing Pursis at Exhibit­30. The statement of accused under Section 313(b) of Cr.P.C. was recorded. Accused neither examined himself nor examined any witness in his defence. 9] Heard learned A.P.P. Mrs. R. A. Navale for State and the learned Advocate Mrs. Reena Korde for Accused. 10] On consideration of argument advanced on behalf of both the sides and on perusal of the oral & documentary evidence on record, following points arise for my 5 Special Case No. 121/2014 (Judgment) determination, which are answered with the findings thereon, as under :­ Sr. Points Findings No. 1] Does the prosecution prove that on 10/04/2014 around 03.45 hours at the residential house of victim­girl, accused committed house trespass after ..No. preparation to cause hurt or assault to any person and he thereby committed an offence punishable under section 452 of Indian Penal Code ? 2] Does the prosecution prove that during same period after committing house trespass, accused used criminal force against the minor victim­girl aged about 16 years and made physical advances by ..No. moving his hand on her breast and entire body intending to outrage or knowing it to be likely that accused will thereby outraged her modesty and he thereby committed an offence punishable under section 354 of I.P.C. ? 3] Does the prosecution prove that during same period accused outraged the modesty of victim­girl in same manner and thus committed an offence of sexual ...No. assault on minor victim­girl and thereby committed an offence defined in section 7 and punishable under section 8 of the P.O.C.S.O. Act? 4] What order ? Accused is acquitted. 6 Special Case No. 121/2014 (Judgment) REASONS As to Point No.1 to 3 : 11] All the points are taken up together for discussion, to avoid the repetition, as evidence about the same in common and inter­connected. 12] As the Accused is facing charge under section 452 & 354 of I.P.C. it is incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that accused committed house tress­pass by entering in the dwelling house of informant, having preparation to cause hurt or assault or wrongful restraint to the victim­girl and by using criminal force with intent to outraged or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby outraged her modesty touched her inappropriately. So also as the Accused is facing charge under section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, therefore, it is further incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that the Accused with sexual intent touched the vagina, penis, anus, breast of a child or make the child touched vagina, penis, anus, breast of such person or any other person or does any other act with sexual intent which involves physical contact without penetration and by his such act committed sexual assault as defined in section 7 of the P.O.C.SO. Act. 7 Special Case No. 121/2014 (Judgment) Age of victim­girl : 13] As the Accused is facing charge under P.O.C.S.O. Act, therefore, first of all it is incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that the victim­girl was child (minor) at the time of incident. The alleged incident took place on 10/04/2014. It is material to note that the prosecution failed to examine the victim­girl and filed detail pursis in that respect that the victim­girl is now married and her family members are not willing to produce her before the Court apprehending that her matrimonial life will be ruined. Further, even though the prosecution has examined the brother of the victim­girl Ravi (P.W.2) and her cousin /the informant Dilip (P.W.1), however, both did not state the date of birth of the victim­girl and most importantly there is absolutely no authenticated document on the record in support of the date of birth of the victim­girl. Only xerox copy of the Adhar card of the victim­girl is placed on record which is not even proved by the prosecution. Thus, the prosecution failed to prove that at the time of incident, the victim­girl was minor aged about 16 years i.e. below the age of 18 years and she was a “child” as per definition given in Section 2(d) of P.O.C.S.O. Act. 14] As prosecution failed to prove that victim­girl was minor child at the time of incident, therefore, the provisions of P.O.C.S.O. Act would not applicable. Further, therefore, even twin presumption given in section 29 and 30 of P.O.C.S.O. Act 8 Special Case No. 121/2014 (Judgment) about offence u/sec. 3, 5, 7 & 9 of the P.O.C.S.O. Act and about culpable mental state of Accused would not come to the help of prosecution. Now it is required to see that whether prosecution proved house­trespass and outraging modesty of victim­girl. 15] To prove the charge against the Accused the prosecution has examined the informant / cousin of victim­girl (P.W.1) and her brother (P.W.2) who are the most material witnesses to prove the charge against the Accused, particularly when prosecution failed to examine the victim­girl. Identity of the Accused is not disputed. Informant (P.W.1) and eye­witness (P.W.2) both deposed that they know the Accused who is staying in front of their house. 16] Informant Dilip (P.W.1) deposed that on 10/04/2014 in the wee hours around 03.45 a.m. his cousin victim­girl and her brother Ravi came to his house and told that somebody entered in their house and touched the victim­ girl inappropriately. But at that time he was in drowsy condition. Ravi (P.W.2) brother of victim­girl also deposed that on the day of incident, his parents took his new born sister to the hospital and they were sleeping in their house and he woke up due to the shouts of his sisters. His sister / victim­girl was frightened and she felt that some person came near her. Therefore, they went to the house of his brother­in­law Dilip 9 Special Case No. 121/2014 (Judgment) (P.W.1). However, both informant(P.W.1) and eye­witness Ravi (P.W.2) failed to identify the accused and did not support the case of prosecution on the material part. Therefore, prosecution has cross­examined them with the permission of the Court, but nothing material was elicited from their cross­ examination. As per the case of prosecution P.W.2 witnesses the incident as by hearing shouts of his sister victim­girl he wakeup and switched on the light and seen accused standing near his sister. But P.W.2 denied to have make any such statement to police. 17] Thereafter, the prosecution has made a feeble effort to prove the contents of report through the investigating officer P.S.I. Bile (P.W.3). The prosecution proved the contents of the report through P.W.3. However, as informant himself and even the eye witness did not support the case of prosecution, therefore, the evidence of investigating officer remains as a mere formality. There is no iota of evidence against the accused and thus, there is absolutely no proof against the accused to prove the charge levelled against him. 18] Thus, prosecution failed to prove that accused committed house tresspass in the dwelling house of victim­girl and with sexual intent inappropriately touched minor victim­ girl by using criminal force and outraged her modesty. Hence, I answer point No.1 to 3 in negative. Therefore, the accused is 10 Special Case No. 121/2014 (Judgment) entitled for acquittal. 19] In the result, I proceed to pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused Anil Narayan Suradkar is hereby acquitted U/Sec. 235(1) of Cr.P.C. for the offence punishable U/Sec.354 & 452 of Indian Penal Code and U/s. 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] The Accused is in jail. He shall be forthwith be released on bail if not required in any other offence. 3] The Accused shall furnish personal bond of the amount of ₹15,000/­ in compliance of provision of Section 437­A of Cr.P.C. The judgment is dictated and pronounced in open Court. Date : 20/04/2016. (Ms. U. M. Nandeshwar), Thane Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act),Thane. District Judge ­1 and Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

He issued letter to Medical Officer for medical examination of accused and collection of medical samples. By letter Exh.42, he has sent samples of victim and accused for C.A. report. On 11.05.2015 the victim delivered a child. Thereafter he sent letter Exh.43 for D.N.A kit. He sent letter Exh.44 for D.N.A. sample of the new born child. By letter Exh.45 he had sent samples for D.N.A. report. 18] The investigating officer is cross examined at length. Through his cross examination it is brought on record J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 115­15 ­ S­376, 506 ­ 4.doc .....13/­ ..13.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.–115/2015.. Exh.49.. CNR No. MHTH01­003375­2015 that he has not collected documents about the hospitalization of victim's mother (PW1). It is further brought on record that he has not collected documents about the treatment of victim on 10.02.2015 and onwards i.e. before lodging complaint. He did not record the statements of sisters and brothers of the victim. It is further brought on record that from 10.02.2015 to 22.02.2015 no information was received from the hospital about the incident. It is suggested that he first confirmed the name of the accused and thereafter investigated the crime to implicate the accused accordingly. The same is denied. It is further brought on record through his cross examination that he did not record statements of school friends and teacher of the victim. He did not collect birth certificate of the victim who was born at Zarkhand. 19] Advocate Mr.Sagar Kolhe argued at length and disputed the entire prosecution story. First of all he challenged the birth date of the victim girl. He argued that PW1, the mother of the victim has stated that she could not state the birth date of the victim. On the point of birth date, the prosecution has examined Head Master of municipal school. As per his evidence and documentary evidence on record, no birth certificate was submitted at the time of admission of victim in the school. The birth date is mentioned on the basis of application/affidavit of victim's mother and letter issued by J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 115­15 ­ S­376, 506 ­ 4.doc .....14/­ ..14.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.–115/2015.. Exh.49.. CNR No. MHTH01­003375­2015 Counselor. The application submitted by the victim's mother is at Exh.32 and the letter issued by Counselor is at Exh.33. In the absence of any reliable document about the birth date of the victim, the birth date mentioned in the school record cannot be accepted. On this point advocate Mr.Kolhe relied upon the devision of Hon'ble Bombay High Court in case between Shri.Amit s/o. Ranglal Shende Vs. State of Maharashtra reported in 2018 All M.R. (Cri) 1915. In said case the victim was alleged to be of 17 years old. There was no record of ossification test. There was no record of Grampanchayat or concerned authority about the birth date of the victim girl. Under such circumstance it was held that the prosecution failed to prove that the victim was aged below 198 years of age. 20] In the present case the birth date of the victim is 18.12.2000. The incident occurred in the month of July 2014. Thus at the time of incident the victim as below 14 years of age. Considering said age and the fact that the victim was studying in 8th std., the school record about the birth date of the victim cannot be disputed. In the ruling cited above the victim was about to attains the majority. Under such circumstances benefit of doubt was given to the accused. In the present case considering the very age of the victim, the ruling cited by advocate Mr.Kolhe and his arguments are not J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 115­15 ­ S­376, 506 ­ 4.doc .....15/­ ..15.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.–115/2015.. Exh.49.. CNR No. MHTH01­003375­2015 acceptable. The school record showing the birth date of victim as 18.12.2000 has to be accepted as it is. The victim delivered a child on 11.05.2015. On the date of delivery of victim she was below 15 years of age. Under such circumstances the prosecution has proved that the victim was minor at the time of incident. 21] Advocate Mr.Sagar Kolhe challenged the prosecution story on the ground of delay in lodging FIR. He argued that as per complaint the victim had complained stomachache on 10.02.2015. On the same day she was taken to hospital wherein it was revealed that she was pregnant. However, complaint came to be lodged on 20.02.2015. The delay of ten days is inordinate. Under such circumstances the accused is falsely implicated in the offence. 22] It is pertinent to note here that the investigating officers PW6 PSI Dilip Thokal and PW7 API Dilip Jadhav did not take efforts to collect the documents of hospitalization of the victim on 10.02.2015. Certainly it is lacuna and negligence on the part of the prosecution. However, even after 20.02.2015 when the victim was referred for medical examination, she was found pregnant. Thus the non collection of medical papers about the treatment in between 10.02.2015 to 20.02.2015 is certainly not fatal to the prosecution. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 115­15 ­ S­376, 506 ­ 4.doc .....16/­ ..16.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.–115/2015.. Exh.49.. CNR No. MHTH01­003375­2015 Interestingly in cross examination of the victim it is brought on record that she was discharged from hospital on 20.02.2015 and the complaint came to be lodged on 20.02.2015 itself. Thus only after being discharged from the hospital complaint is lodged. Considering the continuous pregnancy and subsequent delivery and all other facts on record, the delay in lodging complaint after disclosure of pregnancy is certainly not fatal. Under such circumstances the arguments of advocate Mr.Sagar Kolhe are not acceptable. 23] Advocate Mr.Sagar Kolhe assailed the evidence of PW1 and PW2. Both these witnesses admitted that the complainant i.e. PW1 is having three daughters and three sons and husband. They further admitted that other customers used to attend their house for meal in theirs mess. The house is situated in residential area. Relying upon the residence advocate Mr.Kolhe submitted that the allegation that victim girl was alone at home and accused had forcible sexual intercourse with her are not acceptable. 24] It is pertinent to note here that the victim was pregnant and had delivered a child. Under such circumstances it itself is the conclusive evidence about the penetrative sexual intercourse with her. Now the question is whether the assailant was an accused or someone else. In cross J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 115­15 ­ S­376, 506 ­ 4.doc .....17/­ ..17.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.–115/2015.. Exh.49.. CNR No. MHTH01­003375­2015 examination PW1 and PW2 it was suggested that the victim was pregnant from someone else, but the same is denied. It is pertinent to note here that, in statement u/s.313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure the accused has not stated anything about the pregnancy. He not even alleged that the victim girl was pregnant from third person. In cross examination of PW1 and PW2 it is specifically admitted on behalf of the accused that he used to visit their house for meal. Even he visited the hospital when victim's mother i.e. complainant was hospitalized in respect of fracture of leg. Considering these admitted facts, the evidence of PW1 and PW2 about the visit of accused to their house and sexual intercourse with the victim girl, cannot be discarded. 25] It is pertinent to note here that the complainant has specifically alleged that she was in hospital due to fracture of leg. She deposed that she was hospitalized for six months an was bed­ridden for about nine months after discharge from the hospital. However, in cross examination she stated that she got fracture injury on 15.12.2014, whereas the complaint is lodged on 20.02.2015. Thus, the period from sustaining injury and discharge from hospital is not six months. The documents about the hospitalization of the complainant are not produced on record. Considering these facts, advocate Mr.Sagar Kolhe argued that, the allegations that, during her J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 115­15 ­ S­376, 506 ­ 4.doc .....18/­ ..18.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.–115/2015.. Exh.49.. CNR No. MHTH01­003375­2015 hospitalization, the accused had sexual intercourse with the victim, are not reliable. 26] It is pertinent to note here that the complainant is not educated lady. She may not be in a position to state exact date of her hospitalization. Unfortunately the investigating officer did not bother to collect the documents about the hospitalization of the complainant. However, the fact of accused visiting house of victim girl and his sexual intercourse is duly proved through oral and medical evidence on record. Under such circumstances merely because there is contrary evidence about the period of hospitalization of victim's mother it cannot be said that the entire prosecution story is false. 27] PW3 Dr.Mamta Ramteke has deposed that the victim had narrated the history of physical sexual intercourse with the accused since 4­5 months. The victim was 32 weeks pregnant. Pointing out these facts, advocate Mr.Kolhe argued that if the accused had sexual intercourse with the victim since 4­5 months prior to the complaint, she could not be pregnant from accused for 32 weeks. Advocate Mr.Kolhe further argued that in medical certificate it is alleged that the accused had sexual intercourse on four occasions, whereas in deposition the victim narrated single incident of sexual intercourse. Hence the victim was not pregnant from the accused. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 115­15 ­ S­376, 506 ­ 4.doc .....19/­ ..19.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.–115/2015.. Exh.49.. CNR No. MHTH01­003375­2015 28] It is pertinent to note here that in the complaint Exh.17 it is specifically mentioned that in July 2014 the accused had sexual intercourse with the victim girl on pretext of marriage. The victim also deposed in Court that in the month of July 2014 the accused had sexual intercourse with her when her mother was hospitalized. Under such circumstance the mere reference as 4­5 months in medical certificate, does not falsify the entire prosecution story and evidence on record. The fact that the victim was pregnant and her specific allegation that she was pregnant from the accused, is itself sufficient to rely upon the prosecution story. Under such circumstances the arguments of advocate Mr.Kolhe are not acceptable. 29] It is pertinent to note here that in the present case there are documents on record suggesting that D.N.A. samples of the victim girl, accused and the child delivered by the victim were collected. However, D.N.A. report is not produced on record. Relying upon said fact, advocate Mr.Kolhe submitted that it is not proved that the accused is the biological father of the child delivered by the victim. Relying upon oral evidence, advocate Mr.Kolhe argued that from the evidence on record it is not clear who had collected D.N.A samples. Therefore, the prosecution story is not reliable. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 115­15 ­ S­376, 506 ­ 4.doc .....20/­ ..20.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.–115/2015.. Exh.49.. CNR No. MHTH01­003375­2015 30] As already observed, the visit of the accused at the house of victim girl, the pregnancy of the victim girl and delivery of child is duly proved by the prosecution. The victim has specifically alleged and deposed on oath in the Court that the accused had forcible sexual intercourse with her on pretext of marriage and thereby she became pregnant. Under such circumstance, though there is no D.N.A. report on record, it cannot be said that the accused had no penetrative sexual intercourse with the victim girl. Here the presumption u/s.29 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act is to be raised. As already mentioned in statement u/s.313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure the accused has not given any explanation, though in cross examination of victim girl and her mother it was suggested that the victim was pregnant from someone else. Considering the entire evidence on record and presumption u/s.29 of the Act, the absence of D.N.A. report is certainly not fatal to the prosecution story. Hence the arguments of advocate Mr.Kolhe are certainly not applicable. 31] From the entire evidence on record, the prosecution has clearly established that the accused had sexual intercourse with the victim girl whereby the victim was pregnant and delivered a child. The victim has specifically deposed that the accused had threatened to kill her and her family members if J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 115­15 ­ S­376, 506 ­ 4.doc .....21/­ ..21.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.–115/2015.. Exh.49.. CNR No. MHTH01­003375­2015 she disclose the incident to anyone. Under such circumstances the offence punishable u/s.376, 506 (2) of the Indian Penal Code and section 4 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act are duly proved against the accused. Hence point Nos.1 and 2 are answered in the affirmative. 32] As offence u/s.376 and 506 (2) of the Indian Penal Code and section 4 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act is proved against the accused, he deserves to be convicted and sentenced for the same. It is necessary to hear the accused on the quantum of sentence. Hence the Judgment is deferred to hear the accused on the quantum of sentence. Thane. (P.P.Jadhav) District Judge­4 and Date : 04.01.2019. Addl. Sessions Judge, Thane. 33] Heard the accused and his advocate Mr.Sagar Kolhe on quantum of sentence. It is argued that the accused is young person aged 21 years old. He is not having any criminal antecedents. Hence leniency be shown to him. On the contrary A.P.P. Shri.Kadu submitted that maximum punishment prescribed under the Act be inflicted. 34] It is pertinent to note here that the accused was visiting the house of victim for having meal in their mess. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 115­15 ­ S­376, 506 ­ 4.doc .....22/­ ..22.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.–115/2015.. Exh.49.. CNR No. MHTH01­003375­2015 Parents of the victim were having faith upon him. However, taking disadvantage of said fact, the accused had ravished the victim who is just 14 years old girl. Considering said fact he deserves to be punished with proper sentence and fine. The accused is held guilty for the offence of penetrative sexual assault punishable u/s.376 of Indian Penal Code and section 4 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. The later Act being special enactment, single punishment under said Act will serve the purpose. It is not necessary to inflict punishment u/s.376 of Indian Penal Code. Section 4 of the Act prescribes punishment of imprisonment for not less than seven years and which may extent to imprisonment for life. In view of above observations and the prescribed punishment following order is passed. ORDER 1. Accused Mohammad Mansur Aalam Ansari is hereby convicted u/s.235(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure for offences punishable u/s.376 and 506 (2) of the Indian Penal Code and u/s.4 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 2. For offence punishable u/s.4 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act he is sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for ten years and fine of Rs.25,000/­ (Rs.Twenty Five Thousand only), in J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 115­15 ­ S­376, 506 ­ 4.doc .....23/­ ..23.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.–115/2015.. Exh.49.. CNR No. MHTH01­003375­2015 default of payment of fine he has to undergo further simple imprisonment for six months. 3. For offence punishable u/s.506(2) of the Indian Penal Code he is sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for one year and fine of Rs.3,000/­ (Rs.Three Thousand only), in default of payment of fine he has to undergo further simple imprisonment for one month. 4. The accused is entitled to set off for the period he has already undergone in jail, u/s.428 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 5. Copy of Judgment be given to the accused free of cost. Sd/­... Thane. MHTH01­003381­2018 The applicant Abhimanyu Narasu Patil has applied for bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C.,in C.R.No.I­105/2018 registered in Kapurbavadi police station for the offence under section 324, 504,506 read with 34 of IPC and Section 11(1) and 12 of POCSO Act, 2012. 2. It is contended that the applicant is falsely implicated. Investigation is practically completed. The applicant is ready to co­operate for the investigation and to face the trial. Incident took place on 22.03.2018 at 8.00 p.m., till 30.03.2018 upto 10.00 p.m. FIR was not lodged. There is delay in lodging FIR. Offence is not punishable with death or imprisonment for life. The another two accused persons are released on bail, therefore, on the ground of parity this applicant may be released on bail. 3. Investigating Officer gave his say at Exh.6. It is contended that the present applicant has followed the victim from time to time and made obscene gesture and assaulted her and molested her. Accused had demanded mobile phone number of the victim. She did not give it and did not respond the applicant. The victim's brother had given instruction to the present applicant not to follow the victim, but even then applicant used to follow the victim. On 30.03.2018 at 10.00 p.m, the present applicant along with accused Nos.2 and 3 went in the house of the victim and assaulted victim's cousin --2-- CRI. BAIL APPLICATION NO.1166/2018 brother and broke the windows and door of the house of informant. Therefore, if the applicant is released on bail he is likely to repeat the offence and tamper the prosecution witnesses. 4. I heard Ld. Counsel on behalf of accused and Ld. APP. 5. The court is of the view that the investigation is almost completed. The role of this accused is different than the accused nos.2 and 3. Against this applicant one more C.R.No.I­ 403/2019 under section 354(1), 307, 366, 324, 143, 144, 147, 148, 149, 323, 504, 506 of IPC and section 7,8 of POCSO Act is pending in Kapurbavadi police station. As per the case of prosecution this applicant was following the prosecutrix from time to time since many days. She had not express any interest in the applicant, but the applicant was following her and assaulting her with sexual intent. He had passed obscne remarks. 6. The brother of the victim had given understanding to the present applicant, but he did not improve instead of that he took the help of accused Nos.2 and 3 and came in the house of prosecutrix and assaulted his brother and brother's friend Vicky with 'Kada' in his hands and they broke the door and windows of the house of victim with sticks and made damages of her house and assaulted the victim's brother and abused them and threatened them. Considering the story of the prosecution it reveals that what is the conduct of this present applicant previously and on the day of incident. It appears that victim's --3-- CRI. BAIL APPLICATION NO.1166/2018 brother had given instruction to him, therefore, he became angry and assaulted the victim's brother and brother's friend with sticks and caused damages to the victim's house. 7. So considering the nature of offence and role of this accused it appears that if he released on bail he is likely to repeat more serious offence and likely to continue to tease the victim and he has no fear of law. The safety of the victim is also equally important. The victim is learning. She is not safe if the accused released on bail. If released on bail he is also likely to jump on bail and will not remain present for the trial. There is criminal antecedent of this accused as there is offence under section 354A, 307, 366 registered against this applicant. So considering the role of this applicant he is not entitled to be released on bail on the ground of parity. His role is totally different. So considering conduct and background of the applicant it is not desirable to release the accused on bail. Hence, I proceed to pass following order. :ORDER: Application for bail is rejected. Thane. Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­003392­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No. 118/15 Received on : 22.05.2015 Registered on : 22.05.2015 Decided on : 10.07.2018 Duration : 3Ys.1M.18Ds. IN THE COURT OF D.J.­1 & ADDL. SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE (Presided over by Hemant M. Patwardhan) Special (POCSO) Case No.118/15 Exh.No. 1.State of Maharashtra. ( Rabodi Police station) ..Complainant V/s. 1. Santosh Shamlal Yadav. Age 28 years, Occ. Service, R/at. Vaishalinagar, In front of Petrol Pump. Mulund, Mumbai. ..Accused Appearance:­ DGP Mrs. Moholkar for the State. Advocate Shri. Yadav for the accused. JUDGMENT (Delivered on this 10th day of July 2018 ) Accused Santosh Yadav was facing trial under sections 354(A)(1)(i) of Indian Penal Code read with sections 8 and 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 on following facts:­ 1 to 11 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­003392­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No. 118/15 1] That on 01.08.2014 at about 8.30 hrs. and on 02.08.2014 at about 8.30 hrs. at public toilet, near Sadhana building, Naralipada, Thane (W) within the jurisdiction of Rabodi Police station, Thane accused have sexually harassed minor victim aged about 8 years by physical contact and advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures and at the same time with sexual intent which involves physical contact without penetration inclusive of sexual harassment. Thus, on the complaint lodged by father of victim an offence punishable under aforesaid sections came to be registered against accused. On completion of investigation he was charge­ sheeted. 2] My learned Predecessor was pleaded to frame charge below Exh.7 and has certified that contents of said charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. Accused pleaded not guilty and claim to be tried. His defence was of total denial and that he has been falsely implicated in the matter on two fold reasons' viz. that he has denied selling milk on lower rate to complainant and that accused has scolded daughter of the complainant when she attempted to give jerks to his bicycle having milk can. On the basis of aforesaid facts prosecution has examined complainant, victim, panch witness and I.O. as witness no.1 to 4 respectively. Then statement of accused was recorded under section 313 of 2 to 11 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­003392­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No. 118/15 Cr.P.C. as per his say wherein he has categorically put forth both the defences. 3] Arguments of rival advocates were heard. Learned P.P. Smt. Moholkar has categorically pointed out that accused has exhibited private part of the body and touches the vagina of the child victim with intention of sexual assault while victim child was attending her nature's call and as he was caught raid handed on the spot, the offence is prima facie established. According to learned P.P. the court can always presume the commission of said act under section 29 unless contrary is proved and in present matter as all the suggestions put forth by the defence has been denied by the victim and his father, said defence is certainly not sufficient to otherwise disprove the act. Hence, learned P.P. has requested to convict the accused as per provisions of law. She has further added that contradictions in depositions of father and victim are very minor contradictions and thus, can be ignored having regards to the age of victim. Hence, she has prayed accordingly for conviction of accused. Per contra, defence advocate Mr. Yadav has categorically pointed out that as a matter of fact accused was asked by the complainant to provide milk to his tea stall at a lower rate without showing honesty to his employer and also there was incident of scolding the daughter of the complainant 3 to 11 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­003392­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No. 118/15 prior to the present incident which annoyed the complainant and in order to implicate him in a criminal matter, the victim has been projected in this case as amongst the other children she is smart enough to narrate the incident as tuitored by her father. According to him contradictions in the statement of victim and complainant are major contradictions in itself are sufficient to discard their depositions. Hence, he has requested to acquit the accused. 4] On the basis of aforesaid rival arguments, following points arose for my consideration and I record my findings against each of them for the reasons noted below :­ Sr.N. Points Findings 1] Does the prosecution prove that accused on 01.08.2014 at ..Negative. about 8.30 hrs. and on 02.08.2014 at about 8.30 hrs. at Public toilet, near Sadhana building, Naralipada, Thane (W) within the jurisdiction of Rabodi Station, Thane have sexually harassed minor victim age 8 years by physical contact and advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 354­A(1)(i) of Indian Penal Code ? 2] Does the prosecution prove that on aforesaid date, time and ..Negative. place accused committed sexual assault on minor girl age 8 years with sexual intent which involves physical contact without penetration and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act? 3] Does the prosecution prove that on aforesaid date, time and ..Negative. place accused committed sexual harassment upon the minor victim girl of the complainant age 8 years with sexual intent and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act? 4] What order? Accused is acquitted as per final order. 4 to 11 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­003392­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No. 118/15 REASONS As to point no.1 to 4 :­ 5] Prosecution has alleged that accused has sexually harassed minor victim with physical contact and at the same time with sexual intent which involves physical contacts assaulted her and harassed her sexually. Thus, he has committed aforesaid offences. In order to establish it, material witnesses examined are complainant and victim herself. Though panch and I.O. were also examined they were certainly not eye witness of the incident. Thus, their depositions in itself was not sufficient to establish the guilt of accused. Therefore, entire prosecution was rest on the depositions of PW1 and 2. Hence, on the background of the defence their evidence is to be scrutinized. 6] Complainant has deposed that on 01.08.2014 her daughter had told her mother about some misbehaviour of one person at about 8.30 a.m., in the evening of that day at about 6.30 p.m. Therefore, his wife had informed him about the incident. According to him even on the next morning when his daughter had been to ladies toilet he has followed her. Again one person entered into ladies toilet in which daughter went. That person took out his pant and asked his daughter to touch his private part. Therefore, his daughter shouted, he went there and pick up that person. Therefore, the complaint was lodged. 5 to 11 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­003392­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No. 118/15 7] Victim has categorically stated that three years prior at about 8.30 a.m. when she went to attend nature's call in the public toilet, a boy had come there and asked her where is gent's toilet and when she had informed it about he left. Again on next morning same man came inside the toilet, went close to her and touches her private part though she has made an attempt to push him. Therefore, she got frightened. Her grandmother came there and that man ran away. On the basis of said depositions of the complainant and victim, learned Public prosecutor has requested to convict the accused under aforesaid sections. 8] In order to convict the accused the prosecution was required to establish that the particular act of the accused was with sexual intention and harassment also involves unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures. On perusal of provisions of section 7, the main ingredient of said section which defines sexual assault is "sexual intent". So also in order to prove the offence under section 354A(1)(i) of IPC, prosecution has to establish sexual harassment with unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures. Prosecution in order to establish the guilt of the accused has relied upon aforesaid two witnesses as observed aforesaid. However, apparently on perusal of their depositions it appears that both the witnesses have made altogether different allegations against particular accused. 6 to 11 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­003392­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No. 118/15 Therefore, court has to consider whether contradictions are of material nature or not. On perusal of allegation of complainant he has alleged misbehaviour by the accused even on the first day wherein victim has not made whisper about misbehaviour on initial day. Hence, if there is no allegation of misbehaviour by victim, her intimating family members about it nowhere appears to be natural conduct of the victim. A person is bound to disclose untoward incidents to the family members as a natural conduct of that particular person. However, merely asking anybody as to where the gents toilet is situate cannot be said to be misbehaviour with the particular child which requires indulgence of the family members. Therefore, if that fact is consider then it is difficult to accept that child had informed about it really to her mother. Further, complainant has made reference of information by the victim child to her mother. Hence, her mother was very material witness so far as allegation of 1st August 2014 were concerned. However, prosecution has neither cited her as a witness nor adduce her evidence before the court for the reasons best known to the prosecution. Hence, it is apparent that best available material evidence is withheld by prosecution without there being any proper explanation. 9] So is the case about incident dated 02.08.2014. As observed aforesaid when there was actually no untoward 7 to 11 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­003392­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No. 118/15 incident had occurred on 01.08.2014 there was no reason for the complainant to follow the victim in the morning while she had been to public toilet for attending her nature's call. Again there are major contradictions while deposing about incident dated 02.08.2014. As per the complainant accused himself has taken out his pant and asked his daughter to touch his private part wherein victim has alleged that accused had touches her private part. All these two facts are not only contradictory to each other but change nature of allegation in itself. As victim was minor as per the settled propositions of law the court is required to look for corroboration about particular statement of the minor child. However, as the father complainant has made altogether contradictory statement, the deposition of the victim minor girl was never corroborated by any evidence. 10] Again at the cost of repetition it has said that victim has alleged that on second occasion, grandmother came there therefore accused ran away. Said grandmother must have seen the accused or victim as her natural conduct must have informed about the incident initially to the grandmother. However, grandmother was never produced before the court for deposition for the best reasons known to the prosecution. Hence, again as the material witness is withheld by the prosecution it is difficult to accept that particular deposition is disclosure of true facts. 8 to 11 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­003392­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No. 118/15 11] Sexual intent is a material ingredient in the matter. However, even if we consider deposition of both the material witnesses, intention of the accused has not been categorically referred by any of the witness. Hence, the said basic ingredient is missing in prosecution evidence. Further though suggestion of the accused in respect of grounds of his involvement in the crime referred to above are denied by the witnesses said grounds in view of the contradictory statements made by the material witnesses appears to be more probable. Having regards to said facts as the victim's version is not corroborated properly by the father and as the material witness viz. mother and grandmother of the victim are withheld by the prosecution it can be said that prosecution has not established link to raise presumption in the matter. Further, as a matter of fact presumption under section 29 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 is in respect of other offences and not in respect of section 8 and 12 of the Act and thus, that presumption unless preliminary allegations are established on record cannot be raised in favour of the prosecution. 12] Another important aspect which was pointed out by Mr. Yadav is that complainant has projected his other daughter as victim as she was smart enough to deposed than others as tutored by him. The statement in respect of status of the daughters referred in the complaint and in cross­examination 9 to 11 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­003392­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No. 118/15 he has pointed out that complainant has admitted that victim was in Jr. Kg. at the time of incident i.e. in the year 2015 and on the date of deposition was in 6th Std. as per the admission. Thus, as the deposition was recorded in 2017 it is highly probable that student of Jr. K.G. will directly pramoted to 6th Std. during two years of academic year. The said fact also get corroborated by deposition of victim wherein she has admitted that on the date of particular deposition she was in 5th Std. Hence, in view of the contradictory statements in respect of actual status of academic year of the victim girl, defence of the learned advocate that complainant had smartly changed the daughter and projected witness no.2 as a victim just to implicate accused in the matter gets substantiated it. Hence, defence has succeded in proving the defence or atleast creating a doubt in respect of either occurrence of the incident or involvement of the accused in the matter, then as per settled propositions of law he is entitled to get benefit of doubt in respect of that fact. Having regatrds to aforesaid facts in my opinion evidence brought before the court is neither consistent nor reliable and the contradictory statements made by the material witnesses are fatal to the prosecution. So far as other two witnesses are concerned as they are merely panch witness and I.O. but as the main icident is not established properly their 10 to 11 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­003392­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No. 118/15 depositions will not certainly make any impact on either prosecution or defence. Hence, I do not hesitate to record my findings against point no.1 to 3 in negative and proceed to pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused Santosh Shamlal Yadav is acquitted from the offence punishable under sections 354­A(1)(i) of I.P.C. and 8 and 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] Bail bond of accused shall stands canceled. 3] Muddemal property clothes being worthless be destroyed after appeal period. 4] Accused is directed to execute P.R.& S.B. of Rs.10,000/­ as per amended provisions of section 437(A) of Cr.P.C. and bonds so executed shall remain in force for the period of six months from the date of its execution. 5] Proceeding is accordingly closed. Thane (Hemant M.Patwardhan) Date: 10.07.2018 D.J.­1 & Additional Sessions Judge, Thane 11 to 11
