Presented on : 23/05/2016. Registered on : 23/05/2016. Decided on : 18/12/2018. Duration­ ; Y M D 02 06 25 IN THE COURT OF SESSIONS, THANE, AT THANE. (Before V.Y. Jadhav, Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.) SPECIAL CASE (POCSO) NO. 134 OF 2016 CNR : MHTH01­003421­2016 Exh. No. The State } (Through Kapurbavdi Police Station) } ..Prosecution V/s. Suraj Nakchatare Singh, } Age 28 years, R/o. Hanuman road, } Valmikinagar, Babhanpada, } Near public bathroom, } Own house at Andheri, Mumbai. } ..Accused. Appearance :­ ___________________________________________________________ For State : Special P.P. Shri. Kulkarni. For Accused : Adv. Smt. Kawale. ___________________________________________________________ JUDGMENT (Delivered on 18.12.2018.) 1] Accused is facing charge for the offence punishable u/s. 376, 363 of I.P.C. along with Sec. 4 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 2 POCSO Case. No. 134/2016. The prosecution case in nut­shell is as follows : 2] That the informant is mother of the victim. At the time of incident, the victim was 15 years old and was taking education in 10 th standard at Vidyaprasaran High­School, Balkum. She was going to R.J. Coaching Classes. She used to leave home at 01.15 p.m. and return at about 5.30 p.m. Her son Hitesh was also studying in same school in 8 th standard. The informant used to go for work at 8.00 a.m. and used to return at 5.00 to 6.00 p.m. 3] On 26.08.15, the victim aged 15 years, did not go to school on the pretext that she was suffering from stomach ache. The informant left home at 8.00 a.m. and returned at 5.30 p.m. However, the victim did not return home till 6.30 p.m. Her school bag also could not be seen. Therefore, the informant enquired with a student in the class of victim by name Dipali on phone as to at what time, the class was over and where was the victim. She was informed that class was over at regular time. However, the victim had not attended the class. Therefore, the informant took search of the victim in nearby places. However, she could not be traced. Therefore, she lodged F.I.R. contending that her daughter was kidnapped by some unknown person. It is also mentioned in the F.I.R. that she was having Rs.3000/­ for payment of tuition fees. As per F.I.R., C.R. No. 378/15 came to be registered with Kapurbawdi police station. A.P.I. Mr. Pravin Pandurang Bangosavi and police Naik Mr. More had conducted the investigation. 4] After nearabout six months i.e. on 28.02.16, the victim was found at Gaondevi police station with accused and had revealed that she had physical relationship with the accused. Therefore, after investigation, the investigating officer filed charge­sheet against the accused for the 3 POCSO Case. No. 134/2016. offence punishable u/s. 363, 376 of I.P.C. and sec. 3 and 4 of the POCSO Act. 5] After submission of charge­sheet, my learned Predecessor framed charge against accused for the offence punishable u/s. 376, 363 of I.P.C. and section 3 r/w. 4 of the POCSO Act, vide Exh.7. The contents of charge were read over and explained to the accused to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 6] In order to prove the guilt of accused, the prosecution has examined two witnesses namely P.W.1 Ashwini Vasant Raut informant at Exh. 19, P.W.2 A.P.I. Pravin Pandurang Bangosavi investigating officer at Exh. 24. In spite of repeated attempts, the victim could not be traced. Therefore, ultimately the prosecution closed its evidence vide pursis at Exh. 36. 7] The prosecution has also relied upon following documents i.e. F.I.R. at Exh. 21, a chit left by victim in her hand­writing Exh.20, photographs of victim Exh.22, letter by the investigating officer for inclusion of provisions of the POCSO Act­ Exh.25, bonafide certificate of the victim issued by head­mistress of the school­ Exh.26, spot panchanama­ Exh.27, seizure panchanama of clothes of victim­ Exh.28 and letter dated 08.03.16, whereby muddemal was sent for chemical analysis ­Exh.31. 8] Statement of accused u/s. 313 of Cr.P.C. came to be recorded to the extent of only incriminating material against him. The defence of the accused is of total denial and false implication. 9] Heard learned Special P.P. Shri. Kulkarni for the State and learned counsel Smt. Kawale for the accused. 4 POCSO Case. No. 134/2016. 10] Following points emerged for my consideration and I have recorded my findings thereon for the reasons given below. Points Findings 1] Whether the prosecution has proved No. that on 26.08.2015 after 01.00 hours, accused had kidnapped minor daughter of informant, aged 15 years, from the lawful guardianship of her parents ? 2] Whether the prosecution has proved No. that in between 26.08.2015 and 28.02.2016, in the house of accused, accused had committed penetrative sexual assault on the minor daughter of informant ? 3] What order ? As per final order. REASONS 11] Ld. Special P.P. Shri. Kulkarni for the prosecution submitted that in the present case, the victim is not traceable. So also, the informant has deposed that the victim has left home on her own and she left a chit that she was going along with her class­mate. Therefore, though prima facie it may appear that ingredients of section 363 of I.P.C. are not proved, however, at the relevant time, the victim was minor and she was found with the accused. Therefore, it can be safely concluded that the prosecution has proved the ingredients of section 363 as well as section 376 of I.P.C. r/w. Sec. 4 of the POCSO Act, and he may be punished for maximum sentence prescribed for the offence. 12] On the other hand, Ld. Counsel Smt. Kawale for the defence 5 POCSO Case. No. 134/2016. submitted that the victim in the present case is not traceable. Therefore, the prosecution has examined only two witnesses. Now, the material witness is P.W.1 who is also mother of the victim. She has specifically deposed that her daughter left with a chit Exh. 20 wherein, it has mentioned that her daughter left house at her own and she was going with a boy who was her class­mate. Admittedly, the accused is not her class­mate. Therefore, the victim had not gone with the accused. Even, she was not found with the accused. The police had just called the accused from Mahalaxmi temple and he was alone there. There was crowd and he does not know whether victim was there in the crowd. 13] In the cross­examination of P.W.1, she has specifically admitted that she does not have personal information as to with whom her daughter left home. She also does not know as to whether her daughter had came into physical relationship with accused or any other person. She has also admitted that accused had not taken away her daughter. Therefore, the allegations of commission of offence u/s. 363 of I.P.C. has been disproved by the informant herself. Now, considering the allegations of section 376 of I.P.C. and provisions of the POCSO Act, there is no material to show that the accused and victim were found together. There is no such panchanama on record. 14] There is no material to show the date of birth of the victim. Though the bonafide certificate of the victim has placed on record, however, the investigating officer has admitted that it does not bear any inward or outward number. The investigating officer has not recorded statement of the head­mistress who issued said certificate. A copy of relevant extract of school register has not brought on record. There is no material about the physical relationship between accused and victim. 6 POCSO Case. No. 134/2016. Rather, there is no material at all against the accused to show that at any point of time, they were together. The medical evidence about the physical relationship has not at all proved by the prosecution. In the cross­ examination, the informant has deposed that she is having original birth certificate of her daughter. However, the same has not produced. It creates a doubt about real age of the victim. Hence, even considering the evidence led by the prosecution as it is, then also, there is no material on record to hold the accused guilty of any of the alleged offence. Hence, the accused may be acquitted from the charges. 15] In the light of above submissions, it is required to scrutinize the material on record. As to Points No. 1 and 2:­ 16] It has come in the evidence of P.W.1 Smt. Ashwini Vasant Raut that in August, 2015, she was residing in Patil chawl, Balkum pada 3. Victim is her daughter. She also has a son. In August, 15, victim was studying in 10th standard in Vidya­Prasarak High­School. Her date of birth was 16.04.2001. In her bonafide certificate, her date of birth is shown as 16.04.2001. She was going to R.J. Classes at Thane. P.W.1's son Nitesh was also studying in same school in 8th standard. Victim used to go for tuition at 1.15 p.m. and used to return at 5.30 p.m. The school timing of both children was 7.15 a.m. to 12.30 p.m. P.W.1 was working as maid in Lodha Complex at Balkum. She used to go for work at 8 a.m. and used to return at 5 to 6 p.m. In August, 15, her daughter said that there was pain in stomach and she would not go for school. Thereafter, she went for work. Her daughter went for tuitions. In the morning, she had paid Rs.3000/­ to the victim for tuition fees. When she returned home at the evening, she saw that her daughter did not return from tuitions. She enquired with her 7 POCSO Case. No. 134/2016. son, however, he said that she had not returned. She called her friend on phone and asked her. She informed her that the tuition is over, however, her daughter had not attended the tuition on that day. P.W.1 made enquiry about her in their vicinity and her friends. She found that she was taken away by somebody. She found her chit Exh.20 at home. The said chit Exh.20 is in the hand­writing of her daughter. Hence, she lodged F.I.R. at Exh. 21. The photographs of her daughter are at Exh. 22. 17] She further deposed that police were searching for her daughter and they found her with accused at Gaondevi, Mumbai. Her daughter informed that she had gone with him at her free will and did not narrate anything else to her. She has further deposed that her daughter had informed about her physical relationship with accused on various occasions. However, she further deposed that after returning home, her daughter left home by quarreling with her. Currently, she does not know her whereabouts. She has further volunteered that again she returned back with Punjabi person and said that he was her husband. They resided separately in her vicinity, borrowed some money from neighbouring persons on false pretext and fled away. Again, once she returned back, however, she does not know her whereabouts. 18] During her cross­examination, she deposed that she has birth certificate of both the children. Before admitting the victim in Vidyaprasarak school, she was in another school namely G.S.S. school, Majiwada. Before that, she was learning at Municipal school. Her daughter was bright in education. At the relevant time, she was studying in S.S.C. Therefore, the informant was insisting her for study and she was expecting good marks in S.S.C. examination. She has admitted that the school was having boys and girls as students, however, the accused was not 8 POCSO Case. No. 134/2016. class­mate of her daughter. She admitted that she does not have any personal knowledge as to with whom her daughter had left home. So also that, she does not have any knowledge about sexual relations of her daughter with anybody. She also admitted that the accused did not take her daughter away and she had gone on her own wish. She has also admitted that as the informant was insisting that the victim should study well, therefore, the victim left home on her own. She further admitted that she cannot tell as to whether her daughter had physical relationship with the accused or any other person. 19] It has come in the evidence of P.W.2 Pravin Pandurang Bangosavi that in the years 2015 and 2016, he was posted as A.P.I. with Kapurbavdi police station. Investigation of C.R. No. 378/15 was entrusted to him on 01.03.16. Prior to that, Shri. P.N. More had conducted the investigation. Initially, crime was registered u/s. 363 of I.P.C. On 28.02.16, the victim was found at Gaondevi police station, Mumbai. During preliminary enquiry, it revealed that she had physical relationship though she was minor. Therefore, investigation of the crime was entrusted to him. Thereafter, he collected copy of F.I.R. Exh.21, chit of victim Exh.20, her photographs at Exh.22 as well as other investigation papers. 20] It has further come in his evidence that thereafter, on 01.03.16, he recorded statement of victim. Thereafter, he submitted report to the Sessions Court for applying section 376 of I.P.C. and sec. 3 and 4 of POCSO Act against accused, vide letter dated 01.03.16 (Exh.25). He had also received a bonafide certificate dated 18.05.16 (Exh.26) issued by head­ mistress of school of Vidyaprasarak Sanstha, Balkum. As per same, date of birth of victim was 16.04.2001. Thereafter, on 03.03.16, he prepared spot panchanama by visiting the spot in presence of panchas. The spot was 9 POCSO Case. No. 134/2016. shown by accused. It was the room where accused and victim were residing on rent. He had seized clothes of accused i.e. blue shirt and black pant from the spot vide panchanama dated 03.03.16 (Exh.27). On 01.03.16, mother of victim produced clothes on the person of the victim. They were seized in presence of panchas. Accordingly, seizure panchanama dated 01.03.16 (Exh.28) was prepared. Thereafter, he received report dated 02.03.16 (Exh.29) of medical examination of victim from the medical officer. Thereafter, the victim was sent for psychological test. He submitted that report Exh.30 of psychological test of victim in the investigation papers. 21] Thereafter, vide letter dated 08.03.16, he sent seized articles to forensic laboratory, Kalina, for chemical analysis vide letter Exh.31 dated 08.03.16. Thereafter, he sent accused for medical examination on 04.03.16 and received report Exh.32 of the same. It has admitted by defence. On 05.03.16, he again recorded supplementary statement of informant. He arrested the accused on 28.02.16 vide Arrest form Exh. 33 (admitted by defence). Thereafter, he recorded statements of other witnesses. Statements of victim and her mother were recorded u/s. 164 of Cr.P.C. (Exh. 34 and 35). As it revealed during investigation that the accused had kidnapped the minor victim from lawful guardianship of informant and had physical relationship with her, therefore, he filed charge­sheet against the accused for the offence u/s. 363, 376 of I.P.C. and sec. 3, 4 of POCSO Act. The witness identified the accused present before the court. 22] During his cross­examination, he admitted that the bonafide certificate Exh. 26 does not reflect any inward or outward number. That he has not recorded statement of author of said bonafide certificate. He admitted that he has not conducted investigation in accordance with the chit 10 POCSO Case. No. 134/2016. left by the victim while leaving home. He also admitted that he has not conducted investigation as to with whom the victim was having physical relationship. He also admitted that during his entire investigation, it did not reveal that the accused had taken away victim from custody of the informant. Further, he denied other suggestions about wrong investigation and submitting false charge­sheet, etc. 23] If the entire evidence of prosecution is considered, it is clear that the victim is not traceable and it has almost become impossible for the prosecution to secure her presence. Therefore, the prosecution has relied upon the evidence of her mother i.e. P.W.1 and investigating officer. If evidence of both above­said witnesses would perused, on the point of kidnapping of the victim as well as her physical relationship with accused, then the picture reveals that the victim was having love affair with a boy who was her class­mate and she left a chit to her mother Exh. 20, mentioning the same. 24] Admittedly, the accused is not her class­mate. Secondly, there is no material to show that actually the accused and victim were caught together. The investigating officer has admitted that there is no material to show that accused had taken away the victim with him. The mother of victim has also admitted that her daughter had left on her own. She has deposed that as it was the crucial year of the education of victim, mother was insisting for study and expecting good marks and due to said pressure, the victim left home. She has also admitted that she does not have any personal knowledge about physical relationship between accused and victim. On this point, it is necessary to consider the statements of victim and the mother u/s. 164 of Cr.P.C. No doubt, the defence has not got an opportunity to cross­examine the victim, therefore, any incriminating 11 POCSO Case. No. 134/2016. material in said statement of victim cannot be directly a basis of conviction. However, certainly it can be taken into consideration for proper decision of the case, as a corroborative material, though a weak piece of evidence. However, in the present case, in the statement u/s. 164 of Cr.P.C. of the victim, she has not uttered a single word about her physical relationship with accused. The said statements were recorded immediately on 18.03.2016. In the same, she had though mentioned that she had gone with the accused, however, there is no reference of any physical relationship in between accused and victim. Similarly, if the statement of her mother would perused, the same is also not reflecting anything about the accused enticing her away or physical relationship between victim and accused. In the circumstances, tough the report of medical examination of victim Exh. 29 is on record, the same cannot help the prosecution to establish any physical relationship between accused and victim. 25] In above circumstances, when there is no evidence on record to show that victim was taken away by the accused or she had gone with the accused, so also, there is no evidence that victim was found with the accused, there is no evidence about exact age of the victim at the relevant time, there is no evidence about actual physical relationship between victim and accused at any point of time, so also, absence of any such averment in the statement of victim u/s. 164 of Cr.P.C. recorded immediately after she was found by police, in my view, there is lack of sufficient material to prove the guilt of the accused. Rather, there is no evidence to substantiate allegations of section 363 or section 376 of I.P.C. 26] So far as presumption u/s. 29 of the POCSO Act is concerned, the age of the victim has not properly proved by the prosecution. On this point, one can place reliance upon following two decisions of Hon'ble 12 POCSO Case. No. 134/2016. Bombay High Court­ 27] In the case of 'Gurudas s/o. Bandu Pendor Vs. The State of Maharashtra: 2015 ALL MR (Cri.) 4494', the Hon'ble Bombay High Court has observed in para 14 about the proof of age of the prosecutrix as follows­ “In the present case, in the absence of primary evidence, namely the birth certificate from the Gram Panchayat which would have a best evidential value as envisaged under section 35 of the Evidence Act and in absence of ossification test report of the prosecutrix, the prosecution loses credibility as regards the age of prosecutrix. Evaluation of the aforesaid, in my view, shows that the prosecution was unable to bring its case in respect of the age of prosecutrix beyond reasonable doubt. It would be hazardous to reach to a conclusion that the date of birth of the prosecutrix was 28.9.1998 in the light of evidence which is discussed hereinabove.” 28] In the case of 'Umesh Rajabhau Khandekar Vs. The State of Maharashtra: 2015 ALL MR (Cri.) 4006', it is observed by the Hon'ble Bombay High Court that, “When no examination regarding age of prosecutrix was carried and though head­master had examined, however, he deposed that the entry in the school register was effected on the basis of admission form filled by parents of the student and on the basis of oral information given by the father of the girl. Hence, it has observed that there is reasonable doubt as regards age of the complainant.” 29] Under the circumstances, the presumption u/s. 29 of the POCSO Act cannot be made applicable to present case and except the bare words of the investigating officer, there is no evidence on record to indicate 13 POCSO Case. No. 134/2016. towards the guilt of the accused. Even the investigating officer has admitted that he could not gather any material to show that accused had kidnapped the victim. The evidence about physical relationship between accused and victim is also not sufficient. Moreover, the age of the victim is not duly proved. Therefore, the prosecution has also failed to prove the charges u/s. 376 of I.P.C. and section 4 of the POCSO Act, due to lack of sufficient evidence. Hence, points No. 1 and 2 are answered in the negative. 30] So far as muddemal property is concerned, the clothes of accused and victim being worthless, need to be destroyed. As to Point No. 3:­ 31] As the accused has held not guilty of commission of offence punishable u/s. 363, 376 of I.P.C. r/w. Sec. 4 of the POCSO Act, consequentially, he is required to be acquitted from the charges. Hence, in answer to point No. 3, I pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused Suraj Nakchatare Singh, is hereby, acquitted under sec. 235(1) of the Criminal Procedure Code, from the offence punishable u/s. 376, 363 of I.P.C. along with Sec. 4 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 2] His bail bond stands cancelled and sureties stand discharged. 14 POCSO Case. No. 134/2016. 3] Accused Suraj Nakchatare Singh is hereby directed to furnish bail bond of Rs.15,000/­ with a surety of like amount, so as to appear before the higher Court in compliance with Sec. 437­A of Code of Criminal Procedure. 4] Muddemal property articles No. 1 to 6 i.e. the clothes of accused and victim be destroyed after appeal period is over. 5] Pronounced in open court. Thane, (V.Y. Jadhav) Date­ 18.12.2018. Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

1 Cri.Bail Appln. 1263/16 Order Exh.1 ORDER BELOW EXH.1 IN CRI.BAIL APPLN.NO. 1263/2016 Heard Ld. Adv. Mr. Rajan Salunke for the applicant. Ld. A.P.P. Mrs. Nayna Kamthe for the State. 1] Applicant who is arrested by Kashimira police station, in Crime No. I­349/2016 for offence U/s. 354­A(1)(2), 323 of I.P.C. and Sec. 12 of POCSO Act has sought his enlargement U/s. 439 of Cr.P.C. 2] It is the case of the prosecution that since last 2 months, the applicant has been insisted his younger sister/victim to have physical relation in absence of the family members. Shrikant Tulshiram Gaikwad Age 22 years, R/at.Santoshi Mata Chawl, Owned House, Ashirwad Niwas Road No.22, Annabhau Sathenagar Wagale Estate, Thane .. 2 .. S.C.C No. 121/2015 (Judgment) ==================================== Appearances : Ld. APP Shri.Y. M. Patil for Complainant Ld. Counsel Shri.Sanjay Kanhere for accused No.1 Ld. Counsel Shri.Arun Navale for accused no.2 ==================================== :JUDGMENT: (Delivered on 23rd day of September, 2017) 1. Accused are facing trial for the offence punishable u/sec. 363, 366 r.w 34 of Indian Penal Code and Sec.17 & 18 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2. In short case of prosecution is as follows:­ 2.1. On 3.3.15 in between 11 hours to 17.30 hours at Bedekar College, CIDCO Road, Thane (West) in furtherance of common intention the present accused alongwith absconding accused Jinu Yashodharan Panikar kidnapped minor victim ( Name of the victim is not disclosed to protect her identity) from the lawful guardianship of her parents knowingly that she will be compelled or likely to compel illicit intercourse and thereby committed the offence U/sec.363, 366 r.w 34 of Indian Penal Code and offence U/Sec.17 & 18 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 3. The FIR was lodged against unknown person by mother of victim. On the basis of said FIR Crime No. I­48/2015 came to be registered. After completion of all the formalities of investigation the present chargesheet came to be filed. .. 3 .. S.C.C No. 121/2015 (Judgment) 4. The Charge was framed vide Ex.8 against the accused for the offence punishable u/sec. 363, 366 r.w 34 of Indian Penal Code and offence U/Sec.17 & 18 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 5. In support of its case the prosecution has examined following witnesses:­ PW No. Ex.No. Prosecution Witness 1 15 Vaishali ­ Mother of victim. 2 17 Victim (Name of the victim is not disclosed to protect her identity.) 3 18 Anil ­ Father of Victim. (The full name of PW.1 Vaishali­mother of victim, PW.2 Victim and PW.3 Anil­ Father of victim are not written in the judgment to protect the identity of victim.) 6. In view of the oral evidence adduced on record on behalf of prosecution it is transpired that, there is no incriminating circumstances and evidence available on record against the accused for their statement prescribed U/sec.313 (1) (b) of the Cr.P.C., to afford an opportunity to explain the incriminating circumstances on record. Therefore there was no any alternative but to dispense with the statement of accused as envisaged U/sec.313 of the Cr.P.C in this case. Hence the requisite order came to be passed to that effect. 7. After considering the case of prosecution following points arise for my determination. I recorded my findings against each of .. 4 .. S.C.C No. 121/2015 (Judgment) them for the reasons stated below:­ S.No. Points Findings 1. Whether the prosecution proves that accused alongwith absconding accused in furtherance of their common intention kidnapped victim No. from the lawful guardianship of her parents? 2. Whether the prosecution proves that accused alongwith absconding accused in furtherance of their common intention kidnapped or No. abducted a victim with intent that she may be compelled to or knowingly it likely that she will be compelled to or may be forced to illicit intercourse? 3. Whether the prosecution proves that accused alongwith absconding accused in furtherance of their No. common intention committed sexual assault on minor victim? 4. What order? Accused are acquitted. :REASONS: AS TO POINT NO. 1 TO 3 :­ 8. To prove the case, prosecution has examined PW.1 informant­ mother of victim at Ex.15. She deposed that, she used to reside with her family including victim. The incidence happened in 2015 with her daughter­victim aged 16 years. The birth date of victim is 26.12.98. The incident happened when she was .. 5 .. S.C.C No. 121/2015 (Judgment) studying in Bedekar college. She used to attend college since 11 a.m to 5.30 p.m. On 3.3.15 at about 11 a.m she dropped victim to college, thereafter at about 1.30 p.m she met with Kore Madam and came to know that the attendance of victim in college is very less. Thereafter she returned to her house. On that day till 8 to 8.30 p.m victim did not return to their house therefore she went to Thane Nagar Police station and at about 10 p.m lodge FIR Ex.16. 9. Thereafter police searched her daughter­victim and informed her on next day that she found and called her to Thane Nagar police station. When she reached to police station she came to know from police that her friend taken her with them by enticing her. Police given custody of victim to her. Thereafter police recorded her statement. Victim did not told her the name of her friends. 10. PW.2 Victim did not support the prosecution case. She did not told anything incriminating against present accused. 11. PW.3 Anil­ father of victim deposed about absence of her daughter and fact of filing FIR by her wife PW.1. He told that he came to know about the incidence from Victim and her wife. After perusal of his evidence it appears that, he do not have any personal knowledge regarding incidence. 12. Considering the evidence given by PW.1 to 3 and the hostility of victim, the Ld. APP wisely closed the evidence of .. 6 .. S.C.C No. 121/2015 (Judgment) prosecution by filing purshis at Ex.19. 13. There is nothing incriminating to be put to the accused for explanation u/sec.313 of Cr.P.C. Therefore after hearing Ld.APP and Advocate for accused, I am inclined to dispense with the statement u/sec.313 of Cr.P.C. Accordingly I passed order below Ex.8 and dispensed with the statement. 14. So considering all these facts and circumstances discussed above, there is nothing which shows that accused committed any offence as alleged u/sec. 363, 366 r.w 34 of Indian Penal Code and offence U/Sec.17 & 18 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, therefore the accused are entitled for order of acquittal. Hence, I answer Point No.1 to 3 are in negative. AS TO POINT NO.4:­ 15. Considering the reasoning and finding as to point No.1 to 3 in answer to point no.4 , I proceed to pass following order:­ ORDER 1] Accused (1) Sahil Prasanna Wagholikar Shrikant and (2) Tulshiram Gaikwad are hereby acquitted u/sec.235 (2) of Cr. P. C. of the offence punishable under 363, 366 r.w 34 of Indian Penal Code and Sec.17 & 18 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] The accused shall execute P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ each in compliance of Sec.437­A of Cr.P.C. .. 7 .. S.C.C No. 121/2015 (Judgment) 3] Muddemal property Samsung Black Mobile GT­1500, IMEI No.357160047039251 alongwith SIM Card be returned to accused no.1. 4] Muddemal property Nokia Black/Red Mobile, Model No.5130C­3, IMEI No.358293032467937 alongwith SIM Card be return to Informant. 5] The other muddemal being worthless be destroyed as per Sec.452 of Cr.P.C., after expiration of appeal period. .. 1 .. bail no.1375/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exhibit 1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 1375/2015 This application is filed by applicant Harish Kankaiah Khyatam for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. I-73/2015 registered at Bhiwandi City police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 363, 366A, 376, 406 of I.P.C. and section 3 read with section 4 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant induced the minor girl and kidnapped her out of lawful guardianship of her parents and had forcible sexual intercourse with her. It is further contended and argued that no such incident of kidnapping has happened and the girl herself had come with the accused of her own wish since there was love affair between them and it is case of consent. It is further contended and argued that they intended to marry each other and now the girl has become major and they have got married to each other. It is further contended and argued that the applicant is falsely implicated in this crime since the complainant was against the love affair of the accused and the girl. It is further submitted that since charge-sheet is also submitted before Court, there is no need of further custody of the applicant/accused. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. .. 2 .. bail no.1375/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution and it is submitted that the accused was knowing that the victim girl was minor aged 16 years and taking disadvantage of her young age, the accused induced and enticed her and kidnapped her and took her to one lodge at Shirdi and then had sexual intercourse with her. It is further contended and argued that the girl had taken with her amount of Rs.1,50,500/- while leaving the house and said amount has been produced by brother of accused one Naresh and same came to be seized. It is further submitted that in such circumstance there is possibility of the applicant threatening and pressurizing the victim girl if released on bail and he may pressurize other the prosecution witnesses also. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 363, 366A, 376, 506 of I.P.C. and section 3 read with section 4 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, the girl is stated to be 14 years old, it is contended on behalf of applicant that there was love affair between him and the girl and the girl had of her own came with him and he had not kidnapped the girl. Even it is the specific contention of the applicant/accused that the girl and accused had intended to marry each other and now the girl has become major and they have married to each other. In the light such particular contention, the allegations against the .. 3 .. bail no.1375/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) accused are true or not, would be the question to be decided on merits. Even nothing is stated to be recovered from the applicant/accused. 4] Then, it is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 5] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 6] Then, it has also to be mentioned that though the investigation in the matter is completed and even charge-sheet is also stated to have been submitted, it would take time to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail .. 4 .. bail no.1375/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) for uncertain period. 7] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order - ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused namely Harish Kankaiah Khyatam released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/- [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions - The applicant shall not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and the prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this Court. He shall furnish proof of residence. Date : 10.07.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.

1 Cri.Bail No. 1340/16 Order Exh.1 ORDER BELOW EXH.1 IN CRI. BAIL APPLICATION NO. 1340/2016 Heard Ld. Adv. Mr. C.B. Deshpande for the applicant. Ld. A.P.P. Mrs. Deshmukh for the State. I.O. Present. 1] The applicant has filed this bail application for her release in C.R.No. I­211/2016 for offence U/s. 370 of the I.P.C. and Sec. 4, 5 and 7 of the PITA Act registered at Kashimira police station. 2] The case of the prosecution in brief is that the applicant forced the victim for prostitution and accepted the amount of Rs. 3,000/­ for the prostitution business. Raid to that effect was conducted by the police where a bogus customer was provided with a girl and the money was also accepted for the business of prostitution. A panchanama to that effect was also carried out. 3] Ld. Advocate Mr. Deshpande has submitted that in the F.I.R. it is mentioned that Rs. 12,000/­ has been recovered, whereas only Rs. 3,000/­ is recovered from the applicant. He has further submitted that the offence U/s. 370 is not made out. He has submitted that the alleged raid took place on a road and not in a brothel. He has also relied upon a Judgment of the Hon'ble Bombay High Court in the case of Laxman Irappa Hatti and another V/s. State of Maharashtra, 2004 Cri.L.J. 3802 wherein it has been held that order rejecting second application for bail filed after filing of charge­sheet on ground that filing of charge­sheet is not a substantial change of circumstances, is not proper. 2 Cri.Bail No. 1340/16 Order Exh.1 4] The Ld. A.P.P. and the I.O. have submitted that Rs. 3,000/­ came to be recovered from the applicant as her commission. The balance of amount has been returned to the NGO which had helped in carrying out the said raid. They have submitted that the applicant was caught read handed while taking the commission. The role of the applicant as a trafficker has clearly been mentioned in the F.I.R. 5] In the Judgment dated 30/10/2015 in Criminal P.I.L. No. 4/2015 Freedom Firm V/s. Commissioner of Police, Pune & Ors., guidelines have been laid down by the Bombay High Court for judicial officers while dealing with the cases of human trafficking. In this matter, it has been held that the court would, as a general principle, refuse bail to an accused who is shown as a trafficker in human beings as such accused pursues a career in such crime, which is prone to repetition, which is expected to have antecedents and which is generally indisposed to intimidation and threats. The Court would certainly release on bail such of the accused or co­accused as are themselves not traffickers but may be shown to have played some minor role in the commission of the offence”. 6] The Judgment cited by the Ld. Advocate for the accused is by a single Judge of the Bombay High Court and is prior in point of time. Moreover, the Judgment in Criminal PIL No. 4/2015 is very specific to the offences of human trafficking. Therefore, in view of the ratio decidendi and the guidelines laid down in the case of Freedom Firm (supra), this is not at all a fit case for granting bail. The applicant was caught red handed committing the offence of trafficking. In view 3 Cri.Bail No. 1340/16 Order Exh.1 thereof, I am inclined to reject the application. ORDER Application stands rejected. Thane. ( Mridula V.K.Bhatia ) Dt:­23/06/2016. Dist. Judge – 07 and Addl. Sessions Judge, Thane.

Hanuman Tekdi, behind Rehana hotel, Ground floor, plus two storied Kunthankhana, Originally Bakhtarpur, Post Thane Khaliyapur, Dist. Gazipur (Bangladesh) 2. Soni alias Fatima Islamuddin Khan. Age 25 years, Occ. R/at. Hanuman Tekdi, behind Rehana hotel, Ground floor, plus two storied Kunthankhana, Originally Bakhtarpur, Post Thane Khaliyapur, Dist. Gazipur (Bangladesh) ..Accused Appearance:­ APP Shri. Mishra for the State Advocate Shri. S.M. Gaikwad for the accused 1 to 11 Judgment Special Case No. 126/2014 JUDGMENT (Delivered on this 12th October 2015) Accused were facing trial under sections 372, 373, 366A, 366B, 368 read with 34 of IPC, 3(2), 4, 5, 6(1)(a)(b) of PITA Act and under section 3 and 4 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and 14A(b) and 14(c) of the Foreigners Act on following facts :­ 1] That accused in furtherance of their common intention on 01.04.2014 at about 1.30 p.m. has sold victim girl for unlawful and immoral purposes viz. prostitution and for committing the said offence has brought victim girls from other country i.e. Bangladesh to do an act of beneficiaries with intention that said victim girl may be or knowingly were forced to illicit intercourse with customers and actually after importing her into India has forced her to illicit relations with another person and for the said purpose of illicit intercourse with another persons she was wrongfully confined in the house of accused. According to the prosecution accused knowingly lives, wholly or in part, on the earnining of the prostitution of said victim and for that purpose procures or attempts to procure without consent for the purpose of prostitution and detained the victim girl in a room where prostitution was carried out to induce the victim to have sexual intercourse with a person who is not a spouse of accused and thus on the complaint lodged by the complainant offence under aforesaid sections came to be 2 to 11 Judgment Special Case No. 126/2014 registered against accused. On completion of investigation, charge­sheet came to be filed against them. 2] Throughout the trial accused were in jail. The charge was framed below Exh.7 by my learned predecessor and when charge was explained to the accused in vernacular they have pleaded not guilty and claim to be tried. Their defence is of total denial. On the basis of aforesaid facts, trial was conducted on merit. 3] Prosecution has examined Jitendra Nikam i.e. complainant Exh.11, the victim at Exh.14, I.O. Rajan Saste at Exh.19. Statement of accused no.1 was recorded. As per her say during the statement also accused has put forth defence of their false implication in the matter. After evidence of prosecution arguments on merit were heard. 4] Learned APP has submitted that all the witnesses of prosecution has supported its case that the victim was found in premises where accused were carrying on prostituion. Hence, according to learned APP said fact are sufficient to establish guilt of accused beyond reasonable doubt. According to the prosecution the victim was minor at the time of offence therefore mere her presence with accused at the relevant time without there being any relation with the accused are itself sufficient to prove the offence that by trafficking victim she was 3 to 11 Judgment Special Case No. 126/2014 brought at particular place with the ulterior motive of inducing her to have sexual intercourse with the customers. On these facts, learned APP has requested to convict accused. 5] On the other hand it was pointed out by accused's advocate that none of the ingredients of section with which accused were charge­sheeted are established to say that offence has been proved beyond reasonable doubt. According to learned advocate when accused were charge­sheeted under the various provisions of PITA Act, prosecution was supposed to follow all the mandatory provisions of the Act while carrying out investigation and in the present matter none of the provisions has been followed. He has made reference of section 13 of the PITA Act so as to argue that Special Officer has to investigate the matter that too of the rank of Police Inspector wherein in the present matter said section itself not complied with, though raid was conducted in the house of lady accused even raiding party was not consisting of lady police officers to properly follow the provisions of the Act and according to him the victim has not stated anything against the accused person so as to establish their guilt beyond reasonable doubt. He has therefore requested to acquit the accused from all charges. 6] On the basis of aforesaid rival argument, following points arise for my consideration and I record my findings 4 to 11 Judgment Special Case No. 126/2014 against each of them for the reasons noted below:­ S.N. Points Findings 1] Does the prosecution prove that accused in furtherance of ..Negative common intention on 01.04.2014 at 1.30 p.m. at Hanuman Tekdi, behind Rehan hotel, Ground floor, plus two storied Kunthankhana, sold a person below eighteen years of age i.e. victim girl or for any unlawful and immoral purposes, namely prostitution and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 372 read with 34 of Indian Penal Code? 2] Does the prosecution prove that accused in furtherance of ..Negative common intention on the same date, time and place, bought victim girl who at that time was below eighteen years of age with intent that the said victim girl shall be employed for the purpose of prostitution and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 373 read with 34 of I.P.C.? 3] Does the prosecution prove that accused in furtherance of ..Negative common intention on the same date, time and place, inducted victim girl, a minor girl under the age of eighteen years to go from Bangladesh or to do act of prostitution with intent that the said victim girl may be or knowing that it is likely that the said victim girl will be forced to illicit intercourse with customers and that thereby committed an offence punishable under section 366A read with 34 of I.P.C.? 4] Does the prosecution prove that accused in furtherance of ..Negative common intention on the same date, time and place, imported into India from Bangladesh a country outside India victim girl under the age of twenty one years with intent that she may be forced to illicit intercourse with another persons and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 366B read with 34 of I.P.C. 5] Does the prosecution prove that accused in furtherance of ..Negative common intention on the same date, time and place, wrongfully confined victim girl knowing that victim girl has been kidnapped and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 368 read with 34 of I.P.C.? 6] Does the prosecution prove that accused on the same date, ..Negative time and place, occupied the premises at the time of commission of offence and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 3(2) of PITA Act? 7] Does the prosecution prove that accused on the same date, ..Negative time and place, you knowingly lives, wholly or in part, on the earnings of the prostitution and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 4 of PITA Act? 8] Does the prosecution prove that accused on the same date, ..Negative 5 to 11 Judgment Special Case No. 126/2014 time and place, procures or attempts to procure without consent for the purpose of prostitution and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 5 of PITA Act? 9] Does the prosecution prove that accused on the same date, ..Negative time and place detained the victim girl where prostitution is carried on in the premises with intent that such person may have sexual intercourse with a person who is not the spouse of such person and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 6(1)(a)(b) of PITA Act 10] Does the prosecution prove that accused accused on the ..Negative same date, time and place you abetted the customers to sexually assault minor girl and thereby committed an offence under section 3 and 4 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012? 11] Does the prosecution prove that who are citizen of ..Negative Bangladesh in furtherance of your common intention within the jurisdiction of Bhiwandi City Police Station entered and remained in India in contravention of order of Indian Government under Foreigners Act, 1946 and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 14 A(b) and 14(c) of the Foreigners Act ? 12] What order ? Accused are acquitted as per final order. REASONS As to point nos. 1 to 12 :­ 7] As observed above, prosecution has to establish the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt. Two police officers with victim were examined in this matter. Material witenss was the victim who allegedly has suffered in the entire incident. Before recording deposition of victim arrangements were made for appointment of interpreter to grant opportunity to the victim to explain the truth in her mother tongue. Various primary questions were ask to her before her examination in chief was recorded and after having satisfied that witness was 6 to 11 Judgment Special Case No. 126/2014 able to understand questions through interpreter her evidence was recorded. The victim through the interpreter has specifically deposed that accused no.2 is her father's sister and accused no.1 is her neighbour at Gajipur at Bangladesh and both the accused had brought her to Mumbai for taking care of her would be child. Though she has stated that she has stayed with the accused for five months for taking care of the child 3­4 days after her arrival one person came to the house of accused no.1. Accused no.1 the ask her to remove her clothes and were ask her to do filthy job but when she started crying that person who came to house of ccused no.1 has left the house and therefore no incident occured on that day. She has then only stated that person who visited the house has insisted to do Gandha Kam but she has refused. She was then ask whether any person had sexual intercourse with her. Initially she has refused but then admitted the said fact. During the cross examination she has admitted the fact no such incident of sexual intercourse had happened as stated by her examination. As referred to above the material witness was that of the victim and as her evidence itself is inconsistent in respect of the any of the allegations it is difficult to say that she was initially either induced by the accused persons or accused have themselves imported her from her native Bangladesh for the purpose of selling her for prostitution. Issue before the court was whether the prosecution has established the fact that 7 to 11 Judgment Special Case No. 126/2014 trafficking victim from Bangladesh to India was for the purposes of selling or using minor female girl for the purpose of illicit intercourse which means sexual intercourse between persons not united by marriage, or by any union or tie which, though not amounting to a marriage, is recognized by the personal law or custom of the community to which they belong or, where they belong to different communities, of both such communities, as constituting between them a quasi­marital relation. In the instant case in view of the aforesaid deposition of the victim herself itself difficult to accept that she was imported from Bangladesh for any such illicit purpose. On the contrary she herself has admitted fact that accused have brought her to Mumbai for taking care of their child. 8] Though allegations were made that the accused were also involved in prostitution at their residence where alleged raid was conducted by raiding party, except the allegations there is nothing on record to show that such prostitution was really going on at the house of the accused at any time particularly on the date on which raid was condcuted. There is nothing on record to show that any attempts were made by prosecution to confirm their conducting said business at their residence by sending any bogus customer to them. There is nothing on record to show that any incriminating material or article was found at their residence during raid to show that 8 to 11 Judgment Special Case No. 126/2014 they were involved in such prostitution. Even, the prosecution has alleged contravention of PITA Act. On perusal of the entire evidence it appears that investigation which was required to be carried out by the Special Police Officer appointed by the State Government in this behalf, has not been carried out by any such officer nor any such appointment letter has been produced on record to show that person who is carried out the investigation has authority to do so under the special provisions of section 13 of the Act. It was the duty of concern officer under Sub­section 5 of the section 13 to immediately take said victim before the Magistrate after rescue operations and to record the statement of the victim in respect of the incident. However, in the present matter it appears that statement of victim was not recorded in presence of CWC immediately after her rescue but it was recorded on 13.04.2014. Though the averments were made that her statement was not recorded in presence of CWC as she was under the mental pressure, there is no document in form of medical opinion to substantiate the said fact. There is also no endorsement of CWC officer on the statement as admitted by witness no.3 so as to say that she was either produced before CWC on 04.04.2014 or any day thereafter. I.O. has admitted the fact that lady police officer was not member of the raiding party is itself sufficient to inferred that the basic provisions of 9 to 11 Judgment Special Case No. 126/2014 the Special Act i.e. PITA has not been followed in its true sense either at the time of conducting raid or later on also to follow the mandatory provisions referred in Section 13 of the Act. Having regards to all these facts the evidence before the court no where appears to be cogent, consistent and reliable to hold any of the allegations proved beyond reasonable doubt. Hence I do not hesitate to record my findings against points under consideration in negative and further I do not hesitate to hold that in view of the nature of the evidence on record accused are entitled for acquittal. With the said observation, the order. ORDER 1] Accused are hereby acquitted from the offence punishable under section 372, 373, 366A, 366B, 368 read with 34 of IPC, 3(2), 4, 5, 6(1)(a)(b) of PITA Act and under section 3 and 4 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and 14A(b) and 14(c) of the Foreigners Act 2] Accused are in jail. Therefore, they be set at liberty forthwith, if not required in any matter. 3] Accused however, are directed to furnish P.R. of Rs.5000/­ each under the amended provisions of section 437(A) of Cr.P.C. and the bonds so executed shall remain in force for the period of six months. 10 to 11 Judgment Special Case No. 126/2014 4] Issue release letter informing the jailer about the decision of the court. 5] Muddemal property if any, being worthless be destroyed after appeal period as the same is not claimed by anybody. Thane (Hemant M.Patwardhan) Date: 12.10.2015 D.J.­7 & Additional Sessions Judge, Thane. 11 to 11

1 ABA 1346/2016 Order Exh.1 ORDER BELOW EXH.1 IN A.B.A. NO. 1346/2016 Heard Ld. Adv. Mr. Kanhere for the accused. Ld. A.P.P. Mr. Hinge for the State. Advocate Mr. Kanhere for the applicant has submitted that the present applicants being the father and brother of the main accused, merely helped him by providing their house for the victim to stay. 4] Per contra, Ld. A.P.P. and I.O. have submitted that the applicants have helped the main accused in kidnapping as well as by providing residential facilities to the victim and the main 2 ABA 1346/2016 Order Exh.1 accused who had kidnapped the victim to keep illicit relations with her by promising her for marriage. 5] In view of the facts stated in para No. 3 above, the custodial interrogation of the applicants is not required. Hence, I am inclined to allow the application. ORDER [i] Application is allowed. [ii] In the event of arrest of applicants by Rabale MIDC police station in Crime No. I­112/2016 for the offence U/s. 363, 366,366­A and 376 of the I.P.C.and Sec.4, 8 of POCSO Act, 2012, they be released on P.R. and S.B. of Rs. 50,000/­ each with one or more solvent sureties of like amount on the following terms and conditions :­ [a] The applicants shall attend Rabale MIDC police station every Friday at 5.00 p.m. till filing of charge­sheet. [d] The applicants shall furnish identity proof and contact details of two blood relatives to 3 ABA 1346/2016 Order Exh.1 the Investigating Officer. --1-- ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN REGULAR BAIL APPLICATOIN NO.1433/2017 The applicant Vikaskumar Brahmadin Yadav has applied for bail under section 439 of Cr. P.C. in C.R.No.I­141/2017 registered in Rabale police station for the offence under section 376of Indian Penal Code and section 4 and 5 of POCSO Act, 2012. 2. It is contended that the accused is falsely implicated. He is innocent. He has not committed any offence. He has been arrested only on suspicion. There were property dispute between informant and accused family and therefore the false report has been lodged. Accused is married, therefore, he may be released on bail. 3. Investigating Officer has given his report at Exh.4 that there is prima facie case made out against the accused. The name of the accused is mentioned in FIR. The age of victim is below 15 years. The accused is resident of Utter Pradesh and at present he resides in the vicinity of the informant, therefore, he is likely to tamper the prosecution witnesses. 4. I heard the Ld. Counsel on behalf of the accused and Ld. APP. 5. I perused the statement of victim under section 164 of Cr. P.C. She is mentioned that when she was sleeping in the house and door was closed from inside, she realized that somebody was sleeping near her she weak up and shouted, but the accused gagged her mouth and she saw that he was Vikas Yadav. He forcibly removed her clothes and committed forceful sexual assault upon her. She has mentioned that accused came in the bed room on the first floor of their house from the terrace as the accused resides in --2-- the adjoining house. 6. I perused the School Leaving Certificate of Vivekanand Hindi High School, MIDC Road, Digha. The victim was learning in 9th standard. Her birth date is 26.06.2003. The date of offence is 18.05.2017. On that day the victim was only 13 years 10 months old. The accused is married. He is 25 years old. The accused resides at the adjoining house of the informant. After the incident the informant was very much frightened. Her family members took her in confidence then the victim disclosed the incident. 7. The court is of the view that the victim is very small and she has no affair with the accused. She had no friendship with him. All of a sudden the accused entered into the house of informant through terrace as the house of accused is also adjoining and there was nobody in the house except the victim. The accused took its benefit and committed sexual assault upon victim. The court is of the view that there is prima facie case made out against the accused. There are no mitigating circumstances to release the accused on bail. If the accused is released on bail he is likely to tamper the prosecution witnesses and also repeat the more serious offence. He is also likely to jump on bail. There is no guarantee, therefore, accused is not entitled for bail. Hence, the order. ORDER Application for bail is rejected. Thane. ( S.C. Khalipe ) Date : 20/07/2017. Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

They have committed gang rape upon victim aged 17 years. The statement under section 164 of Cr.P.C of the victim is yet tobe recorded. However, charge­sheet is filed, investigation is completed. If this accused is released on bail it will benefited to the absconding accused. 5. I heard Ld. Counsel on behalf of applicant and Ld. APP. --2-- 6. Considering the case of prosecution that on 07.02.2018 at Bhiwandi in the house of informant four accused persons entered forcibly into her house. 1 ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN CRI. BAIL APPLICATION NO. 1377/2016 Heard : Ld. Advocate Mr. Khilare for the applicant. Ld. A.P.P. Mrs. Navle for the State. I.O. present. 1] This application is filed by the accused U/s. 439 of Cr.P.C. for releasing him on bail as he was arrested by Jawhar Police station in connection with crime No. I­42/2016 for offence U/s. 376 and 504 of the I.P.C. and Sec. 4, 8 and 12 of the PROTECTION OF CHILDREN FROM SEXUAL OFFENCES ACT, 2012. 2] The case of the prosecution in brief is that the accused used to call the minor victim by making gestures of hand and used to take her in the house or 'Wadi' and also used to commit rape on her all the times. On 21/4/2016 and 25/4/2016 the accused committed rape by removing her clothes. He also used to go behind her when she used to take bath at the river. 3] Ld. Adv. Mr. Khilare has submitted that the victim used to on her own go to the accused whenever he used to call her and therefore, Sec. 376 of the I.P.C. is not attracted. The applicant is the Mama of the victim and the said F.I.R. is falsely filed due to property dispute. 4] Per contra, Ld. A.P.P. and the I.O. have vehemently opposed the bail application on the ground that the prosecutrix is merely 13 years old and that the intention of the applicant is demonstrated by the F.I.R. which reveals that he used to keep following her even when she used to go to the river for a bath. The prosecutrix has described in detail the nature of the sexual assault by the accused. 2 5] The offence is prima­facie made out and is serious in nature. There is every chance of intimidating the prosecutrix and trying to tamper the prosecution witnesses. In view thereof, I am inclined to reject the application. ORDER The application is rejected. Thane. ( Mridula V.K. Bhatia ) Date : 29/06/2016. Dist. Judge­07 & Special Judge (POCSO) Thane.

Presented on : 20.06.2014 Registered on : 20.06.2014 Decided on : 06.10.2017 Duration : 03Y.03M. 16D IN THE COURT OF SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE, AT : THANE. Presided over by S.C. Khalipe ­Additional Sessions Judge, Thane SPECIAL CASE NO.128/2014 Exh.No. The State of Maharashtra Through Padgha Police Station. ….. Prosecution V/s. Santosh Ganpat Dalvi Age 20 years, Occ:Agriculturist R/at. Shelar Pada, Wafe Post Kunde, Taluka Bhiwandi, Dist. Thane. ..... Accused Offence punishable under section 341, 354, 323, 506 of Indian Penal Code and section 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Appearance: A.P.P. Smt. Tallar for the prosecution. Advocate Shri.S. E. Lasane for the accused. :J U D G M E N T: (Delivered on this 06th Day of October, 2017) 1. The case of the prosecution is that:­ The accused Santosh Ganpat Dalvi would follow the victim aged 15 years (hereinafter she is described as miss 'X') while she was going to school and tell her “I love you, I do not look at any other girl”. Inspite of disinterest expressed by the victim the accused would followed her. On 05.03.2014 the victim was going to her school at 7.00 a.m., on the road the accused was hidden behind one tree. He came forward and suddenly pulled the victim miss “X'. The victim shouted, the accused gagged her mouth. While her girl friend came there she called the father of the victim, so accused also put hands on her mouth and then he ran away. Thereafter the accused followed the victim near her school and threatened to kill her and her friend that if she disclose incident to anybody. 2. The victim miss 'X' therefore, lodged FIR in Padgha police station on 05.03.2014. Accordingly C.R.No.I­29/2014 registered under section 354, 341, 323, 506 of Indian Penal Code and section 8 of POCSO Act. 3. Investigation was carried out by Police Head Constable Ramchandra Pandurang Pashte of Padgha Police Station. He prepared panchanama of the spot, recorded statement of witnesses and sent chargesheet. 4. Charge is framed against the accused at Exh.3 under section 341, 354, 323, 506 of Indian Penal Code and section 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. He pleaded not guilty. 5. Considering the evidence on record following points arose for my determination. I have given its findings with reasons as under­ Sr.No Points Findings 1. Does prosecution prove that on In 05.03.2014 at about 7.00 a.m. at Waphe, Affirmative Kandali Road, the accused restrained victim miss 'X' aged 15 years and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 341 of Indian Penal Code? 2. Does prosecution prove that on the same In date, time and place the accused within Affirmative intention to outrage modesty of victim miss 'X' touched her, pulled her and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 354 of Indian Penal Code? 3. Does prosecution prove that accused In voluntarily caused hurt to the victim miss Affirmative 'X' on the same place and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 323 of Indian Penal Code? 4 Does prosecution prove that the accused In committed criminal intimidation by Affirmative threatening victim miss 'X' and her girl friend to kill them, if they disclosed the incident to anybody and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 506 of Indian Penal Code? 5 Does prosecution prove that the accused In committed sexual assault upon the minor Affirmative victim aged 15 years by pulling her near bushes with sexual intent and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 8 of POCSO Act. 6 What order? As per final order. REASONS AS TO POINT NOS.1 TO 6:­ 6. The prosecution has examined victim miss 'X' at Exh.10. She has deposed that her date of birth is 19.09.1999 and in the year 2014 she was learning in 9th standard in Pashapur Vidhalaya. The accused has not denied the birth date of the victim. The age of the victim is not at all challenged by the accused. In the statement under section 313 of Cr. P.C., the question was asked to the accused regarding the victim was learning in 9th standard in the year 2014. He admitted this fact. So it is no doubt that the prosecution has proved that the victim was below 18 years at the time of incident. 7. As per the evidence of victim the accused would tell her that, “I love you, I am not looking at any other girl” and he would followed her whenever she go to her school. The victim did not take any interest in the accused and she had resisted him and given him understanding. But the accused did not stop so on 05.03.2014 when the victim was going to school at about 6.45 a.m., to 7.00 a.m. the accused was standing on the road behind one tree, suddenly he came forward and caught the victim and pulled her behind the bushes. The victim was shouting so the accused put hands on her mouth at that time the victim sustained injury below her eye with the nail of accused. The victim's girl friend also came there and she called father of the victim. At that time the accused put hands on the mouth of her girl friend and he ran away. 8. After that the victim and her girl friend were going to school. Near the school the accused came there on his motor cycle at Ghotavade Phata and threatened the victim and her girl friend that he will kill them if they disclosed the incident to anybody. 9. The victim then went to school and after the school hours she came home and disclosed the incident to her parents and then lodged FIR in Padgha Police Station vide Exh.11. The contents in the FIR are corroborated the evidence of P.W.1 victim. 10. The victim thereafter sent to hospital for treatment of her injury below her eye and she brought the certificate. 11. There is no admission given by the victim in her cross examination. She denied that there was traffic on the road at morning. She denied that the people were going to their agricultural lands. She denied that there was boundary dispute between accused land and their land. She denied that the animal of the accused eat the vegetable crop of their land and therefore there was quarrel between them. She denied that, therefore, she lodged false complaint against the accused. 12. The panchanama of the spot is proved from the evidence of P.W.2 Pandurang Kathod Jadhav. The panchanama is at Exh.13. The spot of incident mentioned in the panchanama is corroborated the evidence of P.W.1. 13. P.W.3 Police Head Constable Ramchandra Pashte has stated what investigation he has done. He stated that the statements of witnesses were recorded as per their say and he prepared panchanama of the spot. 14. Considering evidence on record it appears that the victim has not at all given any admission and she has no reason to depose false against the accused. There is no enmity between them and there was no friendship or love affair between them. The victim had never co­operated the accused and therefore there is no reason to disbelieve the evidence of victim. 15. The Ld. Counsel on behalf of the accused submitted that there is delay in lodging FIR. In this respect the court is of the view that the victim is only of 15 years old at the time of incident. After the incident she went to her school and thereafter narrated the incident to her parents and after discussion she lodged FIR. The FIR is lodged at about 7.00 p.m. There is no delay at all and therefore the case of prosecution cannot be disbelieved. 16. Considering the evidence on record the prosecution has proved that the accused had restrained the victim while going to her school and thereby proved the ingredients of offence under section 341 of Indian Penal Code. Accused had also committed criminal force against minor victim aged 15 years with intention to outrage her. He pulled her behind bushes. He was standing near one tree on the road, it shows that he had intention to meet the victim and do something and thereby he had pulled her towards him and also gagged her mouth. It shows that the accused had intention to affect the modesty of the victim. So prosecution has also proved the ingredients of the offence under section 354 of Indian Penal Code. 17. The accused while putting his hands on the mouth of the victim, the victim sustained nail injury below her eye. The victim thereafter took the treatment from the hospital. So the prosecution has also proved the ingredients of the offence under section 323 of Indian Penal Code. 18. The accused also threatened to kill the victim and her girl friend if they disclosed the incident to anybody and thus the prosecution also proved the ingredients of offence under section 506 of Indian Penal Code. 19. The accused with sexual intent pulled the victim near the bushes and put his hands on her mouth and touched her with sexual intent. The victim was minor below 18 years at that time. So prosecution has also proved offence under section 7 punishable under section 8 of POCSO Act, 2012. 20. I, therefore, come to the conclusion that the prosecution has proved all the offences charged against the accused and therefore the accused is liable to be convicted. Date: 06.10.2017 (S. C. Khalipe) Thane. Additional Sessions Judge, Thane. 21. Before passing sentence I heard accused on the point of sentence. He submitted that he is only earning source of his family. There is no criminal antecedent. He is young. The Ld. Counsel on behalf of the accused submitted that he may be given chance for improvement his conduct. 22. In reply Ld. A.P.P. Smt.Tallar submitted that the offences are proved beyond doubt, therefore, accused may be convicted with maximum punishment. 23. The offence under section 354 of IPC is similar with the offence under section 7 of POCSO Act. However, as per the provision of section 42 of the said Act the punishment for the said offence is greater under section 354 of IPC. 24.
