On the background of submissions of both the learned counsels it will be helpful to see the settled law regarding appreciations of evidence in sexual offences. 16. In Vijay v. State of M.P., (2010) 8 SCC 191 honorable Supreme Court discussed about legal issue­ "sole evidence of Victim" in sexual offences as follows :­ : 13 : Spl.C. No.128/2015 (Judgment) “ Sole evidence of prosecutrix 9. In State of Maharashtra v. Chandraprakash Kewalchand Jain [(1990) 1 SCC 550 : 1990 SCC (Cri) 210 : AIR 1990 SC 658] this Court held that a woman, who is the victim of sexual assault, is not an accomplice to the crime but is a victim of another person's lust and, therefore, her evidence need not be tested with the same amount of suspicion as that of an accomplice. The Court observed as under: (SCC p. 559, para 16) “16. A prosecutrix of a sex offence cannot be put on par with an accomplice. She is in fact a victim of the crime. The Evidence Act nowhere says that her evidence cannot be accepted unless it is corroborated in material particulars. She is undoubtedly a competent witness under Section 118 and her evidence must receive the same weight as is attached to an injured in cases of physical violence. The same degree of care and caution must attach in the evaluation of her evidence as in the case of an injured complainant or witness and no more. What is necessary is that the court must be alive to and conscious of the fact that it is dealing with the evidence of a person who is interested in the outcome of the charge leveled by her. If the court keeps this in mind and feels satisfied that it can act on the evidence of the prosecutrix, there is no rule of law or practice incorporated in the Evidence Act similar to Illustration (b) to Section 114 which requires it to look for corroboration. If for some reason the court is hesitant to place implicit reliance on the testimony of the prosecutrix it may look for evidence which may lend assurance to her testimony short of corroboration required in the case of an accomplice. The nature of evidence required to lend assurance to the testimony of the prosecutrix must necessarily : 14 : Spl.C. No.128/2015 (Judgment) depend on the facts and circumstances of each case. But if a prosecutrix is an adult and of full understanding the court is entitled to base a conviction on her evidence unless the same is shown to be infirm and not trustworthy. If the totality of the circumstances appearing on the record of the case disclose that the prosecutrix does not have a strong motive to falsely involve the person charged, the court should ordinarily have no hesitation in accepting her evidence.” 10. In State of U.P. v. Pappu [(2005) 3 SCC 594 : 2005 SCC (Cri) 780] this Court held that even in a case where it is shown that the girl is a girl of easy virtue or a girl habituated to sexual intercourse, it may not be a ground to absolve the accused from the charge of rape. It has to be established that there was consent by her for that particular occasion. Absence of injury on the prosecutrix may not be a factor that leads the court to absolve the accused. This Court further held that there can be conviction on the sole testimony of the prosecutrix and in case, the court is not satisfied with the version of the prosecutrix, it can seek other evidence, direct or circumstantial, by which it may get assurance of her testimony. The Court held as under: (SCC p. 597, para 12) “12. It is well settled that a prosecutrix complaining of having been a victim of the offence of rape is not an accomplice after the crime. There is no rule of law that her testimony cannot be acted upon without corroboration in material particulars. She stands at a higher pedestal than an injured witness. In the latter case, there is injury on the physical form, while in the former it is both physical as well as psychological and emotional. However, if the court of facts finds it difficult to accept the version of : 15 : Spl.C. No.128/2015 (Judgment) the prosecutrix on its face value, it may search for evidence, direct or circumstantial, which would lend assurance to her testimony. Assurance, short of corroboration as understood in the context of an accomplice, would do.” 11. In State of Punjab v. Gurmit Singh [(1996) 2 SCC 384 : 1996 SCC (Cri) 316 : AIR 1996 SC 1393] this Court held that in cases involving sexual harassment, molestation, etc. the court is duty­ bound to deal with such cases with utmost sensitivity. Minor contradictions or insignificant discrepancies in the statement of a prosecutrix should not be a ground for throwing out an otherwise reliable prosecution case. Evidence of the victim of sexual assault is enough for conviction and it does not require any corroboration unless there are compelling reasons for seeking corroboration. The court may look for some assurances of her statement to satisfy judicial conscience. The statement of the prosecutrix is more reliable than that of an injured witness as she is not an accomplice. The Court further held that the delay in filing FIR for sexual offence may not be even properly explained, but if found natural, the accused cannot be given any benefit thereof. The Court observed as under: (SCC pp. 394­96 & 403, paras 8 & 21) “8. … The court overlooked the situation in which a poor helpless minor girl had found herself in the company of three desperate young men who were threatening her and preventing her from raising any alarm. Again, if the investigating officer did not conduct the investigation properly or was negligent in not being able to trace out the driver or the car, how can that become a ground to discredit the : 16 : Spl.C. No.128/2015 (Judgment) testimony of the prosecutrix? The prosecutrix had no control over the investigating agency and the negligence of an investigating officer could not affect the credibility of the statement of the prosecutrix. … The courts must, while evaluating evidence, remain alive to the fact that in a case of rape, no self­respecting woman would come forward in a court just to make a humiliating statement against her honor such as is involved in the commission of rape on her. In cases involving sexual molestation, supposed considerations which have no material effect on the veracity of the prosecution case or even discrepancies in the statement of the prosecutrix should not, unless the discrepancies are such which are of fatal nature, be allowed to throw out an otherwise reliable prosecution case. … Seeking corroboration of her statement before relying upon the same, as a rule, in such cases amounts to adding insult to injury. … Corroboration as a condition for judicial reliance on the testimony of the prosecutrix is not a requirement of law but a guidance of prudence under given circumstances. … *** 21. … The courts should examine the broader probabilities of a case and not get swayed by minor contradictions or insignificant discrepancies in the statement of the prosecutrix, which are not of a fatal nature, to throw out an otherwise reliable prosecution case. If evidence of the prosecutrix inspires confidence, it must be relied upon without seeking corroboration of her statement in material particulars. If for some reason the court finds it difficult to place implicit reliance : 17 : Spl.C. No.128/2015 (Judgment) on her testimony, it may look for evidence which may lend assurance to her testimony, short of corroboration required in the case of an accomplice. The testimony of the prosecutrix must be appreciated in the background of the entire case and the trial court must be alive to its responsibility and be sensitive while dealing with cases involving sexual molestations.” 12. In State of Orissa v. Thakara Besra [(2002) 9 SCC 86 : 2003 SCC (Cri) 1080 : AIR 2002 SC 1963] this Court held that rape is not mere physical assault, rather it often distracts (sic destroys) the whole personality of the victim. The rapist degrades the very soul of the helpless female and, therefore, the testimony of the prosecutrix must be appreciated in the background of the entire case and in such cases, non­examination even of other witnesses may not be a serious infirmity in the prosecution case, particularly where the witnesses had not seen the commission of the offence. 13. In State of H.P. v. Raghubir Singh [(1993) 2 SCC 622 : 1993 SCC (Cri) 674] this Court held that there is no legal compulsion to look for any other evidence to corroborate the evidence of the prosecutrix before recording an order of conviction. Evidence has to be weighed and not counted. Conviction can be recorded on the sole testimony of the prosecutrix, if her evidence inspires confidence and there is absence of circumstances which militate against her veracity. A similar view has been reiterated by this Court in Wahid Khan v. State of M.P. [(2010) 2 SCC 9 : (2010) 1 SCC (Cri) 1208] placing reliance on an earlier judgment in Rameshwar v. State of Rajasthan [AIR 1952 SC 54 : 1952 Cri LJ 547] . 14. Thus, the law that emerges on the issue is to the : 18 : Spl.C. No.128/2015 (Judgment) effect that the statement of the prosecutrix, if found to be worthy of credence and reliable, requires no corroboration. The court may convict the accused on the sole testimony of the prosecutrix.” 17. In the light of above observations, now let us scrutinies the evidence of PW­3 Victim whether her evidence is trustworthy to base conviction of accused on her sole testimony or requires corroborations. 18. It is admitted fact on record that, birth date of victim is 05.09.04 and her age at the time of incidence dated 12.04.15 was 10 years 7 months. The defence did not disputed the age of victim. At the time of recording evidence of victim her age was above 12 years therefore after verifying the fact that she understands the sanctity of oath, in view of Sec.4 of Oaths Act, 1969, oath was administered to her before recording her evidence. 19. PW3 Victim categorically deposed that :­ 19.1. She born on 5.9.2004 and is studying in 7th standard. She is residing in Society at Kalwa. She know Accused Rahul Gondhale and Rohit Shinde. Both were residing in her society. 19.2. She further deposed that the incidence occurred on 12.4.15. On that day she was playing near their : 19 : Spl.C. No.128/2015 (Judgment) building at about 7.30 p.m. When she was playing with her friend, that time Rohit Shinde came there and he told her that mother of Rahul calling her. Therefore she proceed towards the house of Rahul. She saw that Rahul was standing on staircase. She enquired with him regarding his mother. He told that she is in kitchen. Therefore she entered into the flat of Rahul. When she entered into flat of Rahul someone closed the door of flat and switched off the light. Thereafter Rahul forced her to sleep on sofa. He removed her cloths. Rahul and Rohit also removed their cloths. Thereafter both slept over her body. Rahul forced her to drink white colored discharge. Rohit told her to shake his private part. While she was leaving Rohit caught hold her mouth and Rahul also caught hold her hands. Her friends came at the flat of Rahul and enquired about her with Rahul. Rahul told them that she is not there. She told Rahul to leave her otherwise she will told the incidence to her mother. That time Rahul told her to told some reason that something happened to brother and also told her to go through terrace. 19.3. Then she left through terrace and told all facts to her friend Rutuja. She was frightened, therefore did : 20 : Spl.C. No.128/2015 (Judgment) not told the same to anyone that day except Rutuja. When her mother returned on next day in afternoon she narrated said fact to her. Police recorded her statement. 20. In her cross­examination, after facing long cross­ examination when Ld.Advocate for accused was putting suggestions (denials) to victim that time she burst and voluntarily deposed (in para 25 of her deposition) that Rahul touched his penis to her private part and tried to insert. Rahul also told her to drink white discharge which was coming from his penis. Rahul also pressed her neck therefore there was a marking on her neck. 21. In her cross­examination Victim (PW3) deposed that she stated to police that :­ 21.1. She inquired with Rahul regarding his mother and he told her that she is in kitchen and therefore she entered into the flat. 21.2. Thereafter door was closed, however she did not narrated that, "someone" closed the door. 21.3. She narrated to the police that, "both of them slept over my body." 21.4. She narrated to police that, " I told Rahul to leave me : 21 : Spl.C. No.128/2015 (Judgment) otherwise I will told the fact to my mother. That time Rahul told me to told some reason that something happened to brother." 21.5. She narrated to the police that, "I was frightened, therefore did not told the same to anyone that day except Rutuja. When my mother returned on next day in afternoon I narrated said fact to her." 21.6. She narrated to the police that, " My friends came at the flat of Rahul and enquired about me with Rahul. Rahul told them that I am not there." 21.7. She narrated to the police that, "While she was leaving Rohit caught hold her mouth and Rahul also caught hold her hands." She cannot assign any reason why these statements are not appearing in her police statement. 22. It is argued on behalf of the accused that all these statements are material omissions amounts to contradictions. However, I am not agree with this submission. The above statements cannot be treated as omissions because defense is failed to prove the said statements as omissions. The victim categorically stated that she stated said fact to police. So, to prove the said : 22 : Spl.C. No.128/2015 (Judgment) statements as “omissions” defence ought to have confront said statements to Police officer, Madhuri Ghadge (PW­ 10) who recorded statement of Victim, by putting question to her whether these statements/fact were stated by victim to her. However, after perusal of evidence of PW­10 PSI Ghadge it can be seen that these statements except the statement that “at the time of incidence her two friends came to the flat of Rahul” were not confronted to her. Therefore, I am of the view that defense failed to prove that these statements are omissions. 23. Even if the above referred statements are treated as omission then also they cannot be treated as “material omissions' amounting to contradictions covered by the Explanation under Section 162 of Cr.P.C. After reading the evidence of Victim as whole, whatever statements pointed out by the defence cannot be treated as dishonest omissions or improvements capable of dislodging the prosecution case, creating doubt about the version of Victim. These statements are neither contradictory to the prosecution case nor so material. 24. In that respect, I am relying on the observations made by the honorable Supreme Court in case of Shyamal Ghosh v. State of W.B., (2012) 7 SCC 646, wherein it is observed that :­ : 23 : Spl.C. No.128/2015 (Judgment) 68. From the above discussion, it precipitates that the discrepancies or the omissions have to be material ones and then alone, they may amount to contradiction of some serious consequence. Every omission cannot take the place of a contradiction in law and therefore, be the foundation for doubting the case of the prosecution. Minor contradictions, inconsistencies or embellishments of trivial nature which do not affect the core of the prosecution case should not be taken to be a ground to reject the prosecution evidence in its entirety. It is only when such omissions amount to a contradiction creating a serious doubt about the truthfulness or creditworthiness of the witness and other witnesses also make material improvements or contradictions before the court in order to render the evidence unacceptable, that the courts may not be in a position to safely rely upon such evidence. Serious contradictions and omissions which materially affect the case of the prosecution have to be understood in clear contradistinction to mere marginal variations in the statement of the witnesses. The prior may have effect in law upon the evidentiary value of the prosecution case; however, the latter would not adversely affect the case of the prosecution. 69. Another settled rule of appreciation of evidence as already indicated is that the court should not draw any conclusion by picking up an isolated portion from the testimony of a witness without adverting to the statement as a whole. Sometimes it may be feasible that admission of a fact or circumstance by the witness is only to clarify his statement or what has been placed on record. Where it is a genuine attempt on the part of a witness to bring correct facts by clarification on record, such statement must be seen in a different light to a situation where the contradiction is of such a nature that it impairs his evidence in its entirety. : 24 : Spl.C. No.128/2015 (Judgment) 70. In terms of the Explanation to Section 162 Cr.P.C which deals with an omission to state a fact or circumstance in the statement referred to in sub- section (1), such omission may amount to contradiction if the same appears to be significant and otherwise relevant having regard to the context in which such omission occurs and whether there is any omission which amounts to contradiction in particular context shall be a question of fact. A bare reading of this Explanation reveals that if a significant omission is made in a statement of a witness under Section 161 Cr.P.C, the same may amount to contradiction and the question whether it so amounts is a question of fact in each case. (Sunil Kumar Sambhudayal Gupta v. State of Maharashtra [(2010) 13 SCC 657 : (2011) 2 SCC (Cri) 375] and Subhash v. State of Haryana [(2011) 2 SCC 715 : (2011) 2 SCC (Cri) 689] .) 71. The basic element which is unambiguously clear from the Explanation to Section 162 Cr.P.C is use of the expression “may”. To put it aptly, it is not every omission or discrepancy that may amount to material contradiction so as to give the accused any advantage. If the legislative intent was to the contra, then the legislature would have used the expression “shall” in place of the word “may”. The word “may” introduces an element of discretion which has to be exercised by the court of competent jurisdiction in accordance with law. Furthermore, whether such omission, variation or discrepancy is a material contradiction or not is again a question of fact which is to be determined with reference to the facts of a given case. The concept of contradiction in evidence under criminal jurisprudence, thus, cannot be stated in any absolute terms and has to be construed liberally so as to leave desirable discretion with the court to determine whether it is a contradiction or material contradiction which renders the entire evidence of the witness untrustworthy and affects the case of the : 25 : Spl.C. No.128/2015 (Judgment) prosecution materially.” 25. Advocate for accused though there are some defects in investigation how victim can be hold responsible for that defects because she has no control over investigating agency. If the investigating officer did not conduct the investigation properly or was negligent in immediate recording in statement, how can that become a ground to discredit the testimony of the Victim? The victim had no control over the investigating agency and the negligence of an investigating officer could not affect the credibility of the statement of the Victim. In this respect I am relying on the observations of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case : 32 : Spl.C. No.128/2015 (Judgment) of State of Orissa vs. Thakara Besra, AIR 2002 SC 1963 wherein Hon'ble Supreme Court observed that, the testimony of prosecutrix must be appreciated in the background of the entire case and in such cases, non examination of other witnesses may not be serious infirmity in the prosecution case, particularly where the witnesses had not see the commission of the offence. Admittedly in this case there is no eye witness other than victim. Therefore the non examination of friend of victim and aunt of victim will not fatal the case of prosecution. No self­respecting minor girl would come forward in a court just to make a humiliating statement against her honor for the minor quarrel as suggested by the accused. No mother or grandmother would allow or tutor a minor girl to make such false allegations only because there is a minor quarrel between victim and accused. 37. In that respect, I am relying on the observations made by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of C. Muniappan v. State of Tamil Nadu, (2010) 9 SCC 567, Hon'ble Supreme Court explained the law on this point in the following manner: “There may be highly defective investigation in a case. However, it is to be examined as to whether there is any lapse by the IO and whether due to such lapse any benefit should be given to the : 33 : Spl.C. No.128/2015 (Judgment) accused. The law on this issue is well settled that the defect in the investigation by itself cannot be a ground for acquittal. If primacy is given to such designed or negligent investigations or to the omissions or lapses by perfunctory investigation, the faith and confidence of the people in the criminal justice administration would be eroded. Where there has been negligence on the part of the investigating agency or omissions, etc. which resulted in defective investigation, there is a legal obligation on the part of the court to examine the prosecution evidence dehors such lapses, carefully, to find out whether the said evidence is reliable or not and to what extent it is reliable and as to whether such lapses affected the object of finding out the truth. Therefore, the investigation is not the solitary area for judicial scrutiny in a criminal trial. The conclusion of the trial in the case cannot be allowed to depend solely on the probity of investigation.” 38. I agree with the submission of Ld. Advocate that the evidence of C.A. report is not incriminating against accused. 39. Now at this stage I must have to see whether prosecution : 37 : Spl.C. No.128/2015 (Judgment) proved offence of rape or attempt of rape For that purpose it will be relevant to see the definition of rape U/sec.375 of I.P.C., which reads as follows:­ "Sec. 375:­ A man is said to commit “rape” if he­ (a) penetrates his penis, to any extent, into the vagina, mouth, urethra or anus of a woman or makes her to do so with him or any other person; or (b) inserts, to any extent, any object or a part of the body, not being the penis, into the vagina, the urethra or anus of a woman or makes her to do so with him or any other person; or (c) manipulates any part of the body of a woman so as to cause penetration into the vagina, urethra, anus or any ~ of body of such woman or makes her to do so with him or any other person; or (d) applies his mouth to the vagina, anus, urethra of a woman or makes her to do so with him or any other person, under the circumstances falling under any of the following seven descriptions:— First.—Against her will. Secondly.—Without her consent. Thirdly.—With her consent, when her consent has been obtained by putting her or any person in whom she is interested, in fear of death or of hurt. Fourthly.—With her consent, when the man knows that he is not her husband and that her consent is given because she believes that he is another man to whom she is or believes herself to be lawfully married. : 38 : Spl.C. No.128/2015 (Judgment) Fifthly.—With her consent when, at the time of giving such consent, by reason of unsoundness of mind or intoxication or the administration by him personally or through another of any stupefying or unwholesome Substance, she is unable to understand the nature and consequences of that to which she gives consent. Sixthly.—With or without her consent, when she is under eighteen years of age. Seventhly.—When she is unable to communicate consent. Explanation I.—For the purposes of this section, “vagina” shall also include labia majora. Explanation 2.—Consent means an unequivocal voluntary agreement when the woman by words, gestures or any form of verbal or non­verbal communication, communicates willingness to participate in the specific sexual act: Provided that a woman who does not physically resist to the act of penetration shall not by the reason only of that fact, be regarded as consenting to the sexual activity. Exception I.—A medical procedure or intervention shall not constitute rape. The victim has categorically deposed that, when she entered into flat of Rahul someone closed the door, Rahul : 39 : Spl.C. No.128/2015 (Judgment) forced her to sleep on sofa, he removed her cloths. Chhaigaon Makhan, District Khandwa (M.P), Criminal Appeal No.490 of 2014, LEX (MPH) 2016 11 97. b) The State of Maharashtra vs. Mithilesh Harishchandra Yadav, 2016 ALL MR (Cri) 2203. 55. Ld.APP Smt.S.E. Phad submitted that the offence is of serious nature and section itself prescribes minimum punishment and therefore Probation of Offenders Act is : 43 : Spl.C. No.128/2015 (Judgment) not applicable to the present facts and circumstances. She prayed for maximum punishment prescribed under law. 56. At the outset I must say that the citations cited by Ld. Advocate for defence are not on point and differs due to the difference in facts in hand. Admittedly the section under which accused is held guilty prescribes minimum punishment, therefore I am of the view that the benefit of provisions of Probation of Offenders Act, 1958 cannot be extended to accused. Hence, the application of accused at Ex.68 stands rejected. 57. As per the document before me the age of accused at the time of offence is 19 years old. There is no evidence on record that the accused is previously convicted in any criminal case. So considering all facts and circumstances and the fact that the legislature itself prescribed a minimum punishment for the offence, I am of the view that the minimum punishment prescribed by legislature is sufficient to serve the purpose in this case. 58. Though the offence proved against accused is punishable under Sec.6 for aggravated penetrative sexual assault, the charge under said section is not framed. Therefore, I am bound to consider Sec.4 only for punishment to accused. However the non framing of a charge u/sec.6 of POCSO Act will not cause any prejudice to accused or prosecution : 44 : Spl.C. No.128/2015 (Judgment) because the charge u/sec.376 (2) (i) is framed which is having a similar ingredients and punishment like Sec.6 of POCSO Act. 59. The accused is found guilty of the offence u/sec.376(2) (i) of I.P.C. and also offence U/sec.3 punishable with Sec.4 of POCSO Act having quite similar ingredients. Therefore it is necessary to consider the special provision made in Sec.42 of POCSO Act which reads as follows:­ "42. Alternative punishment : Where an act or omission constitutes an offence punishable under this Act and also under section 166A, 354A, 354B, 354C, 354D, 370, 370A 375, 376, 376A, 376C, 376D, 376E or section 509 of the Indian Penal Code, then, not with standing anything contained in any law for the time being in force, the offender found guilty of such offence shall be liable to punishment under this Act or under the Indian Penal Code as provides for punishment which is greater in degree." 60. No.128/2015 (Judgment) persons natural life and shall also be liable to fine. 61. In view of provision of Sec.42 of POCSO Act the punishment for offence U/Sec. 376 (2) (i) is greater in degree than Sec. 4 of POCSO Act and therefore accused is liable for punishment only under Sec.376 (2) (i) of I.P.C. and not U/sec.4 of POCSO Act. Considering facts and circumstances of the present case the minimum sentence provided under said section that is rigorous imprisonment for 10 years and fine of Rs.25,000/­ will be sufficient under this section. 62. Considering facts and circumstances of the present case the minimum sentence provided under said section that is rigorous imprisonment for 20 years and fine of Rs.25,000/­ will be sufficient under this section. 63. A conjoint reading of Sec.71 of I.P.C., Sec.222 of Cr.P.C. and Sec.42 of POCSO Act makes it clear that though the acts committed leading to the offence of "penetrative sexual assault" include some acts which by themselves : 46 : Spl.C. No.128/2015 (Judgment) may amount to the lesser offence of "sexual assault" ­ and in some cases even the offence of "sexual harassment", if they were committed in the course of same transaction, the offender may not be punished for more than one of such offences. The accused is held guilty u/sec.376 (2) (i) and 376(D) and going to be punished under that section therefore the offence U/sec.8 & 12 do not warrant separate punishment. 64. 1 Order Exh.1 Cri.Bail 1385/16 ORDER BELOW EXH.1 IN CRI. BAIL APPLICATION NO. 1385/2016 Heard Ld. Adv. Mr. Arun Singh for the applicant. Ld. A.P.P. Mr. Hinge for the State. I.O. present. 1] The applicant has filed this bail application for his release in C.R.No. II­39/2015 for offence U/s. 4,5,7 of PITA Act, 1956 and Sec. 3, 8 and 16 of POCSO Act, 2012 registered at Kashimira police station. 2] The case of the prosecution in brief is that the applicant along with the absconding accused have accepted the amount on a public place by providing girls to the customers for prostitution knowing that one of them is a minor. 3] Ld. Advocate Mr. Singh has submitted that his client is innocent and has no role to play in the offence. He has submitted that the police has arrested the wrong person and that the accused No.1 has been granted bail. 4] Per contra, ld. A.P.P. and I.O. have submitted that the police had conducted a raid in Shivani Lodging at Kashimira where the applicant was working as a trafficker and used to supply girls for prostitution. However, he fled from the spot and was absconding for one year. There is another co­accused by name of Sonu Singh whose mobile number has also been found in the mobile number of the applicant. Sonu Singh is absconding. However, there is a nexus between these two 2 Order Exh.1 Cri.Bail 1385/16 accused persons. 5] In the Judgment dated 30/10/2015 passed by the Hon'ble Bombay High Court in Criminal P.I.L. No. 4/2015 Freedom Firm V/s. Commissioner of Police, Pune & Ors., guidelines have been laid down for judicial officers while dealing with the cases of human trafficking. In this matter, it has been held that the court would, as a general principle, refuse bail to an accused who is shown as a trafficker in human beings as such accused pursues a career in such crime, which is prone to repetition, which is expected to have antecedents and which is generally indisposed to intimidation and threats. The Court would certainly release on bail such of the accused or co­accused as are themselves not traffickers but may be shown to have played some minor role in the commission of the offence”. 6] The Hon'ble High Court in the above case has also set out in the guidelines that bail should be denied to habitual offenders (traffickers) except upon exceptional, special and compelling reasons upon the most stringent conditions. 7] Therefore, in view of the ratio decidendi and the guidelines laid down in the case of Freedom Firm (supra), this is not at all a fit case for granting bail. The applicant was caught red handed committing the offence of trafficking. In view thereof, I am inclined to reject the application. 3 Order Exh.1 Cri.Bail 1385/16 ORDER Application stands rejected. Thane. ( Mridula V.K.Bhatia ) Dt:­16/06/2016. Dist. Judge – 07 and Special Judge, (POCSO), Thane.

.. 1 .. bail no.1421/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 1421/2015 This application is filed by applicant namely Md. Irfan Nanhe Shaikh for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. I-124/2015 registered at Koparkhairane police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 363, 366, 376 of I.P.C. and section 3 and 4 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant kidnapped the victim girl by inducing her and then had sexual intercourse with her. It is further contended and argued that no such incident of inducement and kidnapping has happened and the applicant is falsely implicated. It is further contended and argued that there was love affair between the applicant and victim and it is a case of consent. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co- operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that the accused and victim were knowing each other before the incident and accused was knowing that the victim girl was minor. It is further contended and argued that taking disadvantage of minor age of the victim the accused induced her by giving false promise of marriage and then kidnapped her and took her to Uttar Pradesh and then under false pretext he had sexual intercourse with her. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl and the prosecution witnesses. It is also .. 2 .. bail no.1421/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 363, 366, 376 of I.P.C. and section 3, 4 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, the girl is stated to be 17 years old and it is contended on behalf of applicant that since the accused and girl were in love with each other, the girl herself had come with him and he had not kidnapped her and it is a case of consent. But then, it is to be mentioned that though case of consent is put forth by the applicant, the victim girl is stated to be minor and therefore the consent of the minor immaterial. In such circumstance looking to the allegation against the accused, the aspect as to whether act of the accused amounts to rape or it is a case of consent, will have to be decided on merits after trial. Even nothing is stated to be recovered from the applicant/accused. 4] It is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 5] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain .. 3 .. bail no.1421/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 6] Then, it has also to be mentioned that looking the allegations against the accused the investigation in the matter may have almost completed but the charge sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 7] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order - ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused namely Md. Irfan Nanhe Shaikh is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/- [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions - The applicant/accused shall attend the concerned police station on every Friday between 10.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon till filing of the charge sheet and shall co-operate in investigation. He shall not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and the prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this Court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 29.06.2015 (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.

While they --2-- were playing on the ground the accused took them on the second floor of the society building and touched them and kissed them. So there is no guarantee that accused will not repeat the offence and will not tamper the prosecution witnesses. The accused resides in the same area were the small victims are resides. --1-- ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN REGULAR BAIL APPLICATOIN NO.1460/2017 The applicant Shahnawaz Jafar Shaikh has applied for bail in Cr. No.I­198/2017 registered in Kasarvadawali police station for the offence under section 354 of Indian Penal Code and Section 8 and 12 of POCSO Act, 2012. 2. It is contended that applicant is the real father of the victim and he is falsely implicated and false story is made by the victim. The victim has stated that the present applicant is her step father and also stated that she has step mother and step siblings. The applicant contended that the victim was love affair with one Fardin and she was eloped away before few months on 16.10.2016. The present applicant also lodged FIR with Kapoorbawadi police station vide CR. NO.I­272/2016 under section 363 of Indian Penal Code. The present applicant and his wife daily go for work for whole day and they come together after their work. The victim does not like to do household work and she likes to remain outside of the house for whole day. She has love affair with Fardin. Therefore, she has lodged false FIR against the applicant. It is contended that the offence under section 354 of Indian Penal Code and Section 8 and 12 of POCSO Act is not punishable with death or imprisonment for life. The presence of the accused in the jail is not necessary for further investigation. He is ready to face trial and ready to abide by the conditions of bail. Therefore, he prayed for bail. --2-- 3. Perused the report of I.O vide Exh.4. It is the story of prosecution that the present applicant is the step father of the victim and he used to sexually harass the victim. So if he released on bail he likely to tamper the prosecution witness and likely to repeat the offence. 4. The applicant's Advocate have filed the copy of Adhar card, ration card, birth certificate of the victim. From all these documents it appears that the victim is the real daughter of the present applicant. The copy of FIR dated 15.10.2016 is perused. It is contended that the applicant is having Tuber cullasis. His medical reports are produced on record. 5. Considering the facts and circumstances of this case the court is of the view that the offence is not punishable with death or imprisonment for life. From the documents on record it appears that the victim is the real daughter of the present applicant, inspite of that she alleged that the present applicant and his mother are her step parents. There was previous complaint lodged by the applicant when the victim had left the home. So in such circumstances, the court is of the view that there is prima facie case made out to release the accused on bail. If certain conditions are imposed he is not likely to repeat the offence and not likely to tamper the prosecution witnesses. Hence, the following order. ORDER 1. Application is allowed. 2. Applicant Shahnawaz Jafar Shaikh be released on PB --3-- and SB of Rs.20,000/­ (Rupees Twenty Thousand Only) with one or two local solvent sureties in like amount. 3. Applicant shall not tamper the victim and the prosecution witnesses by any means. 4. The applicant shall co­operate for the investigation as and when necessary and shall appear before the concerned police station. 5. The applicant shall not leave the jurisdiction of the court without prior permission of this court. 6. If any condition is breached the bail will be cancelled. ( S.C. Khalipe ) Date : 19/06/2017. Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

MHTH01­003746­2017 9 S.C.NO. 128/2017 (J) 16] In the cross­examination of P.W.2­ the informant, it is suggested that Shyam Chauhan has filed criminal case against her relatives and therefore, she has filed false case for pressurizing Shyam Chauhan to withdraw the case but she denied this suggestion and stated that she has no concern with those persons. Considering this suggestion, it appears that, the accused have admitted the fact that they had taken two victims by rickshaw. 17] The investigation officer S.G. Tungerwar has stated about what investigation he has done. He arrested both accused on 08/04/2017. He sent two victims for recording statement U/s. 164 of Cr.P.C. Whether they are near relatives or whether they are distant relatives. No such suggestion is made, and therefore, the defence raised by the accused No.1 Shyam Chauhan does not appear to be probable and believable. That case was registered in 2013 and the present incident took place in 2017 and the informant has not admitted at all any relation with accused in that case. But it has come on record that P.W.1 to P.W.4 have identified both accused persons and stated that these two persons had taken two victims by their rickshaw. MHTH01­003746­2017 11 S.C.NO. 128/2017 (J) 20] Victim­B­P.W.3 has stated in her cross­ examination that her father is also a rickshaw driver but she denied that whenever the friends of her father comes their home by rickshaw, she sits in the rickshaw of the friend of her father. 21] P.W.4 has denied the suggestion in her cross­ examination that two victims were playing and while playing they had gone at long distance, and therefore, the accused had brought them by rickshaw to home. 22] The FIR is corroborated with the oral evidence of P.W.2. Patankar argued that when accused No.1 was arrested he called his friend accused No.2 there and accordingly, accused No.2 was also arrested. The Court is of the view that CNR NO. MHTH01­003746­2017 12 S.C.NO. 128/2017 (J) this submission is not at all tenable because no such suggestion is made to the I.O. or witnesses. This submission is after thought, and therefore, not tenable. He further argued that the victims are tutored and after teaching them they have deposed. However, considering the evidence of both witnesses it does not appear that they have been tutored and they have denied this suggestion in their cross­examination. So this submission is also not tenable. 24] Ld. Counsel on behalf of accused No.1 Smt. Gaikwad argued that Victim­A admitted in her cross­ examination that Shyam Kaka has not done anything. The Court is of the view that it does not mean that accused Shyam Chauhan is not involved in this case. It is proved that, he was driving the rickshaw and as per the evidence on record both the accused had forcibly seated victims in the rickshaw and one of the accused was sitting on the back seat of the rickshaw. So he has also shared the common intention with accused No.2, therefore, he is also responsible for the offence. 25] The Counsel Smt. Gaikwad further argued that the victims have stated that the accused purchased wine but there is no investigation and no medical certificate of the accused about drinking of liquor. The Court is of the view that it was the duty of the investigating officer and he has stated in his evidence that he had searched about ice­creamwala and about the liquor but he did not get any witness to that effect. The Counsel on behalf of accused No.1 further argued that CNR NO. MHTH01­003746­2017 13 S.C.NO. 128/2017 (J) other boys are not examined, with whom the victims were playing. The Court is of the view that statements of those children are not recorded, therefore, they are not examined. 26] Considering the evidence on record, the prosecution has proved that the accused persons with common intention kidnapped victims while they were playing, by rickshaw and took them far away from the residential area at night. They did not take the consent of their parents for taking them. They had taken two minor victim­girls forcibly. It sows that what was the intention behind that. Both of them offered ice­cream and pen, pencil to them and moved hands on their chest and also kissed one of the victims. But as soon as victims were disappeared from the play ground the victim's mother immediately contacted the mother and brother of accused No.1 and immediately, thereafter, within 15­20 minutes both accused brought the victims at home. So the prosecution proved that with common intention accused kidnapped the victims with sexual intent. 27] One of the accused kissed victim and moved hands on her chest with sexual intent and thereby both victims started crying and shouted. So, prosecution has proved the ingredients of offence U/s. 363, 354 of I.P. Code and section­8 of POCSO Act, 2012. So presumptions U/s. 29 and 30 of the POCSO Act are applicable to the case of prosecution. The burden lies upon the accused to rebut the presumption. The accused have failed to rebut the presumptions. CNR NO. MHTH01­003746­2017 14 S.C.NO. 128/2017 (J) 28] I therefore, come to the conclusion that offence U/s. 363, 354 r/w sec. 34 of I.P. Code and U/s. 8 of the POCSO Act, 2012 is proved against both the accused beyond all reasonable doubts. Date­31/01/2018. (S.C. Khalipe) Thane. Additional Sessions Judge, Thane. 29] Both accused are produced before the Court from Jail Authorities. I heard them on the point of sentence. They submitted that they have not done anything. They are poor. They have family members. Their advocate Shri S.J. Patankar and Smt. Sarita Gaikwad are present before the Court. They prayed for minimum sentence. The Ld. A.P.P. Smt. Moholkar submitted that the accused may be punished with maximum sentence. 30] Considering the nature of offence, I do not find any mitigating circumstance for lenient view. I pass following order. :ORDER: 1] The accused No.[1] Shyam Hitendra Chauhan and accused No.[2] Pradeep Laxman Gaikwad are convicted under section 235(2) of Cr.P.C. for the offence punishable U/s. 363, 354 r/w 34 of I.P. Code and section­8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. CNR NO. MHTH01­003746­2017 15 S.C.NO. 128/2017 (J) 2] The accused No.[1] Shyam Hitendra Chauhan and accused No.[2] Pradeep Laxman Gaikwad are sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for the period of four years and to pay fine of Rs.1,000/­ each (Rs. One Thousand Only each) for the offence punishable U/s. 363 r/w sec. 34 of I.P.Code. In default of payment of fine they shall suffer simple imprisonment for 15 days each. 3] The accused No.[1] Shyam Hitendra Chauhan and accused No.[2] Pradeep Laxman Gaikwad are sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for the period of three years and to pay fine of Rs.1,000/­ each (Rs. One Thousand Only each) for the offence punishable U/s.8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 read with section 354 of I.P. Code. In default of payment of fine they shall suffer simple imprisonment for 15 days each. 4] Both the sentences of imprisonment shall run concurrently. 5] The District Legal Services Authority is directed to pay compensation to the victims as per rules. 6] The seized rickshaw bearing No.MH­03/BN­3311 be returned to the registered owner after appeal period. 7] The accused are in jail from 08/04/2017. --1-- ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN REGULAR BAIL APPLICATION NO.1487/2017 The applicant Mohammad Hanif Abbas Shaikh has applied for bail under section 439 of Cr. P.C. in C.R.No. 258/2017 registered in Kashimira police station for the offence under section 376(2) (I) of Indian Penal Code and section 4, 8 of POCSO Act. 2. The accused was arrested on 01.06.2017 as per the FIR lodged by the prosecutrix on 31.05.2017. The applicant was in custody till 09.06.2017, then police remanded to judicial custody. The applicant has claimed bail on the ground that he has been falsely implicated to grab money. The applicant has having kidney problem. He is permanent resident and he is ready to face the trial. Investigation is almost completed, therefore, his further custody is not required. 3. Investigating Officer has given his report at Exh.4. It is contended that the victim is 16 years old and accused is 35 years old. He committed sexual intercourse with the victim many times in lodge and the victim is pregnant. Therefore, if accused is released on bail he is likely to tamper the prosecution witnesses. 4. The applicant has produced the affidavit of the victim and victim's mother stating that the false FIR ought to have been registered at the instance of NGO. In fact the accused has not committed any offence. --2-- 5. Heard Ld. Counsel on behalf of the applicant and A.P.P. 6. Perused the FIR. It is specifically mentioned in the FIR that when the victim was resided along with her family members at Mira Road she was working with the accused in tailoring business and she had love affair with him and accused had promise to marry her. After that they were meeting each other in lodge and at various times the accused committed sexual intercourse with her own consent. After that she went to her native place at Hariyana were she came to know that she was pregnant and through one NGO she gave FIR. 7. The victim is mentioned her age as 17 years. The court is of the view that the victim is sufficient grown up she knows consequence of sexual intercourse. She specifically mentioned that she meet with the accused at various lodges and accused committed sexual intercourse with her as per her own consent. So prima facie there is no force or pressure used by the accused for committing sexual intercourse. 8. In case of Sunil Mahadev patil V/s. State of Maharashtra in 2016 ALL M.R.(Cri) 1712. The Honourable High Court held that there is evidence of love affair and after that there is sexual intercourse between the prosecutrix and accused this is the mitigating factor to release the accused on bail. In case of Akshay Manoj Jaisinghani V/s. The State of Maharashtra In Anticipatory Bail NO.2221/2016 decided on 09.1.2017 the Honourable Lordship of High Court have held that, “there should be some material on record to believe --3-- prima facie that the girl was induced by the accused to such an extent that she was ready to have sexual intercourse with him. Promise to marry cannot be said to be an inducement in these types of cases.” 9. In the present case the victim herself has mentioned that the accused has committed sexual intercourse with her own consent and the victim herself continued to go with the accused at lodge. She did not disclose this fact to anybody. This is the mitigating factor to release the accused on bail. Hence, the order. ORDER 1. Application is allowed 2. The applicant be released on P.B. and S.B. of Rs.20,000/­ (Rupees Twenty Thousand Only) with one or two solvent sureties in like amount. 3. The applicant shall not contact the victim by any means and shall not tamper the victim and witnesses. 4. The applicant shall not leave jurisdiction of the Court till final disposal of the case. 5. The accused shall not repeat the offence. Thane. ( S.C. Khalipe ) Date : 29/06/2017. Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

The photographs of the spot of incident were also t aken by photographer. After completion of investigation charge­sheet came to be filed for offences u/s.377, 376 (2) (f)(I)(j)(k) of I.P. Code and u/s. 4 & 8 of POCSO Act. The accused is in jail since the date of arrest. 4] My Ld. Predecessor has framed charge u/s. 377, 376 (2) (f) (I)(j) (k) of I.P. Code and u/s. 4 & 8 of POCSO Act and explained to accused to which he pleaded not guilty. Plea of accused was recorded through interpreter as the accused as unable to understand Marathi and Hindi language and he was knowing only Bengali language. The prosecution examined P.W.1­Shriram Sitaram Ekhankar­panch witness, P.W.2­Dr. Mamta Sukhdev Ramteke, medical officer, who examined victim, P.W.3­Kiran Ramchandra Gogale­photographer and P.W.4­ Najma Mohammed Ajgar Shaikh­neighbourer of complainant and accused, P.W.5­ Shri Murlidhar Karkar­Investigating officer and P.W.6­ Dilip Daniyal Randive­ PSO The complainant and victim were deported from India in Bangladesh, and therefore, prosecution failed to examine them as witnesses. The statement of accused u/s. 313 of Cr.P.C. is recorded through interpreter. I heard argument of Ld. A.P.P. Smt. Moholkar for State and Ld. Adv. Shri Nadeem Shaikh for accused, in the matter. 5] Following points arise for my determination and I have recorded my findings thereon for the reasons discussed below. ..4/- CNR NO. MHTH01-003811-2015 ..4.. Spl.C. No.133/2015 (Judgment) Sr.No. Points Findings 1] Does prosecution prove that on 24/03/2015 at 1.00 p.m. at Sumitra Chawl, Shanti Mafatlal slum area, Kalwa, ..No. accused had carnal intercourse with victim­ girl against order of nature? 2] Whether prosecution further proved that ..No. on the above date, time and place accused committed unnatural sex with victim? 3] Whether prosecution proved that accused ..No. committed sexual assault on minor victim­ girl? 4] Whether prosecution proved any of the ..No. charges against any of the accused? 5] What order? As per final order. R E A SO N S As to Point Nos. 1 to 4 :­ 6] P.W.1­ Shriram Ikhankar, witness on seizure memo about clothes of accused have stated about calling him to Kalwa police station by police asking him to sign panchanama by saying that police seized two clothes of accused and accordingly, he signed the same which is at Exh.28. He failed to identify the clothes by saying that those were not shown to him by police. P.W.3­Kiran Ghogle, the photographer deposed about having photographs of the house of accused at Shanti Mafatlal slum area in Sumitra Chawl and taking photographs as stated by police, developing the same and handing over to police. The photographs on record were shown to him and he admitted that those were obtained by him and six photographs disclosing the tin shed room with tin­sheet walls having hole at one side i.e. to the tin­sheet wall towards the side of the house witness. From accused side it is submitted that no photographs were taken by him. ..5/- CNR NO. MHTH01-003811-2015 ..5.. Spl.C. No.133/2015 (Judgment) 7] P.W.4 Najma Shaikh, who is shown as a person noticed the incident has deposed partly as per her previous statement. As per her evidence, she resides at Shanti Mafatlal Zopadpatti area, Kalwa. The accused was residing after two houses from her house. Meera Ansari and Imran Ansari were residing adjoining to her hut. Salma was residing at some distance from her house. Salma used to keep her daughter with daughter of son of accused. She deposed that on the day of incident before three years, she was present at home and she heard voice of shouting of Meera and she went near the house of Meera. She heard voice of cry of daughter of Salma coming from the house of accused. People were gathered and knocking the door. Salma and her husband came there and they made quarrel with the accused. That time she was standing near the house of Meera. She further deposed that when daughter of Salma was crying she saw through hole of tin­sheet wall of the house of accused that daughter of Salma was in arms of accused and accused was trying to pacify her. The suggestion was given as to whether it was happened that she saw accused in naked condition and that accused was doing any bad thing with the daughter of Salma but she replied in negative. The portion marked 'A' in her police statement was referred to her by explaining it. She stated that she has not disclosed the same to police and she do not know why it is written so. As the witness resiled from her previous statement, she was declared hostile and cross­examined by putting suggestive questions. However, she denied that she has seen the incident as mentioned in her statement marked as 'A'. She denied that she had disclosed the same to police by deposing false. In cross examination she stated that she is unable to read and write Marathi. She do not know what is written by police in the statement. She denied that she had not seen anything what she stated earlier. ..6/- CNR NO. MHTH01-003811-2015 ..6.. Spl.C. No.133/2015 (Judgment) 8] P.W.2­Dr.Mamta Ramteke, gynecologist working at Shivaji Hospital, Kalwa deposed about examination of victim on 24/03/2015 after taking consent of her mother. The victim gave history of assault that her neighbourer removed her clothes and handled her private part. But in local examination she found redness on vaginal mucosa and abrasion over labia minora (near hymen). She opined that there was evidence of vaginal intercourse and she issued certificate. The witness admitted her signature on Exh.36. The Medical certificate is issued by her. The witness deposed about collection of samples and sending it to chemical analysis. In cross­examination, witness admitted that as per history of assault there was only handling and there was no external injuries on private part. Witness denied that without thorough examination she has given her opinion about vaginal intercourse and she gave opinion due to pressure of police. 9] The evidence of P.W.6 Dilip Randive is about arrival of complainant to police station, recording her complaint by lady PSI Ghadge in his presence, registration of C.R.No.I­173/2015 on its basis. He admitted his signature on complaint Exh.59 and FIR Exh.59. He deposed about bringing the accused to police station by police staff at 4.00 p.m., his arrest made by him, seizure of banian and lungi; clothes wore by accused and preparation of arrest panchanama Exh.60 having his signature and of panchas and thumb impression of accused . He deposed that the clothes of complainant i.e. frock and knicker were also seized by preparing seizure panchanama Exh.62. He deposed about muddemal receipts by both seized cloth articles vide Exh.61 and 63. He deposed about sending the victim and accused for medical examination with letter Exh. 64 and 65 respectively. He deposed about visit to spot alongwith P.I. Karkar, preparation of spot memo in presence of panchas ..7/- CNR NO. MHTH01-003811-2015 ..7.. Spl.C. No.133/2015 (Judgment) as shown by Meera Ansari vide Exh.66 having his signature and of panchas.He stated that there were two holes to the tin­sheet wall of the room of accused where the incident happened. In cross­examination he stated that complainant was not with him when he visited the spot. He denied that statement of witnesses were not recorded as per their say and that seized clothes were not of accused. He denied suggestion that false complaint was lodged by complainant due to old dispute about room with accused. 10] P.W.5­ P.I. Karkar deposed about registraztion of crime on the basis of the complaint of complainant, conducting primary investigation by PSI Randive, visited the spot by him by PSI Randive, conducting further investigation with effect from 26/03/2015 by him. He stated about sending the accused for further medical examination on that day, giving intimation to different Government officers about the incident with letters. He stated about recording statement of different witnesses from time to time. Portion marked 'A' in the statement of Najma was recorded by him and it was marked as Exh.52. He stated about sending victim for age determination test with letter Exh.53 and certificate of doctor about her age as 3½ years. He deposed about sending clothes and samples for chemical analysis to Kalina with letters about the same. He deposed about addition of section­376(2)(f)(i) in the crime. He deposed about filing of charge­sheet as he found that accused committed rape on victim, committed unnatural act. In cross­ examination he stated that C.A. reports are not received, he denied that there was dispute between accused and complainant about room and on that count false complaint was registered. He denied that he had not recorded statement of witnesses as per their say including statement of Najma. He denied that nothing was done by the accused. He stated that ..8/- CNR NO. MHTH01-003811-2015 ..8.. Spl.C. No.133/2015 (Judgment) police staff by whom accused was brought from the spot to police station was not recorded. 11] Ld. A.P.P. submitted that the minor victim and her mother are not examined but that does not make any difference as the presence of the accused inside the room with victim is proved by P.W. Najma as she has specifically deposed about the same. Though witness failed to disclose whole incident as her prosecution story, the evidence shows that the accused had connection with the incident as medical evidence supports the allegations. Observations made by the medical officer in certificate clearly disclose about sexual assault on the victim. Ld. A.P.P. drawn my attention to the contents of the injuries in medical certificate Exh.36 to that effect. She further submitted that I.O. and police witness who conducted spot inspection have deposed consistent to that effect and there is no specific denial on material aspect. P.W. Najma is not cross­examined in detail and her version that she saw accused with victim inside the room when victim was crying is not challenged by way of cross­examination and by putting suggestions in cross­examination. When there is no challenge in cross­examination, it shall be deemed as proved for the same. Reliance is placed on the case of 'Kundan Nanaji Pendor Vs. The State of Maharashtra' reported in Criminal Appeal No. 313/2014 decided on 21/10/2016, to that effect. There was no previous enmity brought on record from accused side to show that complainant had no reason to lodge false complaint against him. Ld.a.P.P. submitted that considering the evidence on record supported with medical evidence, the case is proved by the prosecution. 12] On the other hand, Ld. Counsel for accused submitted that perusal of medical certificate on record clearly discloses contrary facts ..9/- CNR NO. MHTH01-003811-2015 ..9.. Spl.C. No.133/2015 (Judgment) noted in it in respect of exact opinion formed by Medical officer. Certain changes are made in the certificate by scoring earlier portion. He submitted that the word 'normal' in clause­8 of certificate is found scored and addition is made in respect of abrasion on private part. As per his submission, false certificate is issued by doctor on the pressure of police. As per his submissions though Najma stated about finding of accused inside the room with victim, she has not deposed anything to show about commission of any act by the accused. Her evidence cannot be accepted and as it is the evidence of hostile witness, it has to be thrown away. There is no corroboration to her evidence to disclose what exactly happened and therefore, the medical evidence is of no use and whole allegations are not proved against the accused. On this count, he prayed for acquittal. 13] On going through whole evidence on record what transpires is that the material evidence in respect of happening of the incident which was required to be on record is not there. So evidence of P.W.4 Najma is to be considered whether it is sufficient to draw conclusion that the accused was with victim, that he handled the victim aged 3 ½ years and that anything was happened as alleged in the complaint. So far as her version is concerned, she deposed that the accused was inside the room and victim was in his arms and he was pacifying her. The prosecution case as disclosed in FIR is some what different and three persons have noticed the incident and out of it only one is examined and she is not deposing to that effect. The medical evidence as stated by A.P.P. appears there showing some sort of positive evidence supporting to prosecution but the allegations as mentioned in the complaint are totally different and no such act is shown committed by the accused as mentioned in the complaint. ..10/- CNR NO. MHTH01-003811-2015 ..10.. Spl.C. No.133/2015 (Judgment) 14] So, in my view, though the presence of victim with accused is disclosed by this witness, the allegations as mentioned in complaint are different as compared to the case put­forth by the complainant and other witnesses in their statement and FIR. Secondly, the medical evidence can be used as corroborative piece and as stated earlier, sole witness who had an opportunity to depose about full incident have not stated so. In the circumstances, the conviction cannot be based on the evidence which is only to the extent of presence of accused and victim in the room and no other further activities. The corroboration of the medical evidence cannot be taken in the manner stated by Ld. APP. So the allegations made in the chargesheet levelled against the accused cannot be said as proved beyond reasonable doubts and in absence of any positive evidence to show involvement of accused in the incident, no finding about holding the accused responsible for the act can be recorded. In view of the above, I have no option but to hold that prosecution failed to prove the incident of unnatural act by the accused, committing carnal intercourse with victim and sexual assault on victim. Hence, I answer point Nos. 1 to 3 in the negative. Allegations against the accused are not proved, the charges against him also not proved and hence, I answer point No.4 in the negative. 15] As the charge levelled against the accused is not proved the accused is entitled for acquittal. Seized articles cloths be destroyed as per rules. The accused has to furnish P.B. & S.B. of Rs. 15,000/­ in case of any appeal in future by prosecution and he shall be released on bail after compliance of section 437­A of Cr.P.C. In view of the above, following order is passed. ..11/- CNR NO. MHTH01-003811-2015 ..11.. Spl.C. Kumasaka, Post Benheke, Tal.Ajanala, Dist.Amrutsar, State Punjab, 2. Jaswindersingh Kulwantsingh, Age 23 years, Occ. R/at. Kumasaka, Post Benheke, Tal.Ajanala, Dist.Amrutsar, State Punjab, 3. Mangaljitsingh Balwindersingh, Age 39 years, Occ. Bilowada, Tal. and Dist.Amrutsar, State Punjab ...Accused J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 145­15 ­ 354,323 8,10, Arms BPAct.doc . .....2/­ ..2.. For the offence punishable u/s.354, 323 r.w. 34 of Indian Penal Code, u/s.8,10 of P.O.C.S.O.Act u/s.25(1) (2) Indian Arms Act and u/s.37(1) r.w. 135 of Bombay Police Act APP Mr.Vivek G. Kadu for State Adv.Mr.B.G.Bansode for accused : JUDGMENT : (Delivered on this 04th day of April, 2018) The accused are prosecuted for the offence of sexual assault upon minor girl aged 13 years old, possessing sword and causing hurt to a boy. 2] The facts are as under : It is alleged by prosecution that, on 06.02.2015 the victim girl aged 13 years old was returning from her school. She was studying in New Saraswati English School, Patlipada in 9th standard. At about 01.30 p.m. when she had reached near Maha Subhadra Medical Stores at Shukla Chowk two persons belonging to Sikh community obstructed her on the way. One of them moved his hands over her chest. When she objected, those two persons tried to assault her. Thereupon the victim girl raised alarm. After hearing her commotion people gathered on the spot. Meanwhile one more colleague J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 145­15 ­ 354,323 8,10, Arms BPAct.doc . .....3/­ ..3.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 145/2015.. Exh.35.. of those assailants had been to the spot possessing sword. He tried to assault the people gathered on the spot. Meanwhile police had been to the spot of incident and took those three persons to Kasarwadavli police station. The victim also approached to police station alongwith her mother. In the police station she came to know the names of those three persons as Avatarsingh Harbhajansingh, Jaswindersingh Kulwantsingh and Mangaljitsingh Balwindersingh i.e. accused Nos.1 to 3. The victim also learnt that when the accused No.3 was brandishing sword one boy namely Sahil Shirsat had sustained injury by said sword. Accordingly she lodged complaint against accused Nos.1 to 3 in Kasarwadavli police station. 3] After receiving complaint offence punishable u/s.354, 324 r.w.34 of the Indian Penal Code, section 8 and 10 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, section 4 r.w. 25(1)(b) of Arms Act and section 37(1) r.w. 135 of Maharashtra Police Act came to be registered against the accused. After investigation, charge sheet came to be filed against the accused for said offences. 4] Charge is framed against the accused at Exh.09. Accused pleaded not guilty of offence and claimed to be tried. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 145­15 ­ 354,323 8,10, Arms BPAct.doc . .....4/­ ..4.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 145/2015.. Exh.35.. 5] Statement of accused u/s.313 of Code of Criminal Procedure are recorded at Exh.32, Exh.33 and Exh.34. The defence of accused is of total denial. 6] After going through the prosecution story, evidence on record and hearing arguments of both sides, following points arise for my determination. I record my findings thereon for reasons as stated below. POINTS FINDINGS 1] Does the prosecution prove that on 06.02.2015 at about 13.40 hours at Shukla Chowk, Ghodbandar Road, Dongaripada, Thane accused Nos.1 to 3 in furtherance of their common intention sexually assaulted the victim girl aged 13 years old ? …Not proved. 2] Does the prosecution further prove that on the above mentioned date, time and place the accused Nos.1 to 3 in furtherance of their common intention were possessing deadly weapon like sword without having license of authority ? …Not proved. 3] Does the prosecution further prove that on the above mentioned date, time and place the accused Nos.1 to 3 in furtherance of their common intention voluntarily caused hurt to Sahil Shirsat by means of said sword? …Not proved. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 145­15 ­ 354,323 8,10, Arms BPAct.doc . .....5/­ ..5.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 145/2015.. Exh.35.. 4] Does the prosecution further prove that on the above mentioned date, time and place the accused Nos.1 to 3 in furtherance of their common intention were found possessing deadly weapon like sword in prohibition of order of Commissioner of Police ? …Not proved. 5] What order ? ..As per final order. : REASONS : As to the Point Nos.1 to 4 :­ 7] All points are arising out of one and same incident, hence those are discussed together. The prosecution has examined victim girl as PW1 at Exh.17. She deposed that she was studying in New Saraswati English High School. On 06.02.2015 she was returning home from the school after 01.30 p.m. When she had reached near Subhadra Medical two persons were proceeding from opposite side. One of them had dashed against her. However, people gathered there and were saying that something had happened. After seeing mob of people she was scared and started crying. Accused Avatarsingh had brushed against her. The people gathered on the spot started to beat accused Avatarsingh. Accused Jaswindersingh was also present there. Thereafter she was taken to police station and police made inquiry with her. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 145­15 ­ 354,323 8,10, Arms BPAct.doc . .....6/­ ..6.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 145/2015.. Exh.35.. 8] Thus from the chief examination of the victim, it is clear that there was accidental dash by accused Avatarsingh to the victim on busy and crowdy road. The victim specifically denied that the accused Avatarsingh had obstructed her on the way and moved his hand over her chest. 9] The prosecution has examined injured Sahil Shirsat as PW3 at Exh.30. He also deposed that on 06.02.2015 he was returning from his school Sanket Vidyalaya, Manpada. When he had reached near Shuklanaka Chowk one Sikh person had outraged modesty of one girl. People had gathered on the spot. Said Sardarji called upon two more Sardarji. One of them was possessing sword. While he was brandishing sword in the air, he was standing by his side. The sword shit on his head and he sustained head injury. Meanwhile police had been to the spot and took those three Sardarji to the police station. The police had referred him to Civil Hospital for treatment. 10] The prosecution has examined investigating officer Mrs.Rupali Patil as PW2 at Exh.23. She deposed that on 06.02.2015 while she was present at Kasarwadavli police station, she was on duty as police station officer. On that day at about 01.30 p.m. she received phone call that persons from Sikh community were threatening people by means of sword J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 145­15 ­ 354,323 8,10, Arms BPAct.doc . .....7/­ ..7.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 145/2015.. Exh.35.. and there was huge crowd on the spot. Accordingly she had been to Shukla Chowk, Dongaripada. The victim girl was present at the spot. She was frightened. Accused were also present on the spot. One of the accused was possessing sword. One boy by name Sahil Shirsat had sustained injury by sword. They had taken accused to the police station. The victim, her teacher, mother and injured Sahil Shirsat also approached to police station. Sahil Shirsat was referred for medical treatment. She recorded complaint of victim girl in the presence of her teacher and mother. Said complaint is at Exh.23. She had drawn spot panchanama Exh.24. She arrested accused vide Exh.25, Exh.26 and Exh.27. Accused Jaswindersingh made statement before her and produced sword from the gutter situated by the side of Gurudwara. Said sword was seized vide panchanama Exh.29. She had recorded statement of victim's teacher and mother. She got recorded statement of victim girl u/s.164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. She filed charge sheet against accused for above offences. 11] Relying upon the evidence of PW1, PW2 and PW3 A.P.P. Mr.Kadu argued that all the witnesses have stated about presence of the accused possessing sword. The complaint of victim girl is duly proved and exhibited in evidence of PW2 investigating officer. The evidence of PW1 J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 145­15 ­ 354,323 8,10, Arms BPAct.doc . .....8/­ ..8.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 145/2015.. Exh.35.. and PW3 is not properly challenged and disproved. Hence prosecution has proved its case. 12] As already mentioned and as argued by advocate Mr.Bansode representing accused, the victim girl has denied that any of the accused had moved hand over her chest and outraged her modesty. As pointed out by advocate Mr.Bansode the investigating officer has specifically stated that when she reached at the spot of incident, accused Nos.1 to 3 were present there and one of them was possessing sword. However, she further stated that after taking accused to the police station, she recorded memorandum of accused Jaswindersingh and as per memorandum accused Jaswindersingh produced muddemal sword from gutter. From the evidence of PW2 and PW3 it does not reveal as to who was possessing sword at the time of incident. The recovery and seizure of sword by the investigating officer is doubtful. 13] As argued by advocate Mr.Bansode the injury sustained by PW2 Sahil Shirsat is not duly proved. PW3 specifically deposed in chief examination itself that he does not remember who was holding sword. Under such circumstances it is not duly established that at whose hands Sahil Shirsat sustained head injury. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 145­15 ­ 354,323 8,10, Arms BPAct.doc . .....9/­ ..9.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 145/2015.. Exh.35.. 14] Thus from the evidence of PW1 to PW3 it is not proved that the accused were possessing sword, they outraged the modesty of the victim and voluntarily caused hurt to injured Sahil Shirsat. The prosecution has failed to prove the charges levelled against the accused. Hence answering point Nos.1 to 4 in the negative, following order is passed. ORDER 1. Accused No.1. Avatarsingh Harbhajansingh, No.2. Jaswindersingh Kulwantsingh and No.3. Mangaljitsingh Balwindersingh are hereby acquitted u/s.235(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure for offence punishable u/s.354, 323 r.w. 34 of Indian Penal Code, u/s.8, 10 of Probation of Children From Sexual Offences Act u/s.25(1)(2) Indian Arms Act and u/s.37(1) r.w. 135 of Bombay Police Act. 2. The bail bond of accused stands cancelled. 3. The muddemal sword be sent to District Magistrate for disposal according to law, after the appeal period is over. 4. Accused are directed to furnish personal bond of Rs.5,000/­ each in terms of sec.437­A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Sd/­... Thane. (P.P.Jadhav) District Judge­6 and Date : 04.04.2018. Addl. --1-- ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN CRIMINAL BAIL APPLICATION NO.1337/2018 CNR NO. MHTH01­003818­2018 The applicant Sehbaaz Kamruddin Shaikh has applied for bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C., in C.R. No.I­240/2018 registered in Mumbra police station for the offence under section 354, 354(D) of Indian Penal Code and section 8 and 12 of POCSO Act. 2. It is contended that the applicant is falsely implicated. The relatives of the informant had trapped accused and caught him and beaten him mercilessly and on the next day FIR came to be lodged. In fact, the victim aged 16 years used to contact the accused on PCO and expressed her love towards him. The accused is disinterested. On the next day of incident the victim had called him at her building and threatened him if the accused did not come to meet her she will cut her vein. So accused had gone to the building of the victim and gave understanding to her and recovered blade and that time he was caught and beaten by the relatives of the victim. 3. It is contended that the applicant has fixed residence place. He has no father, he is poor man working in one Kirana shop as a helper. He is suffering from heart disease and also ill in the jail. So he may be released on bail. 4. Investigating Officer has given his say at Exh.6. 5. I heard Ld. Counsel on behalf of accused and Ld. APP. 6. The court is of the view that considering the nature of offence further custody of the accused is no more required till final disposal of the case. The victim is 16 years old. She is --2-- matured enough, therefore, there is no possibility of tampering the victim and witnesses. Accused does not reside in the same building of the victim. The mobile phone of the accused is seized. There is no previous antecedent. Considering the elements of the accused it is decided to release him on condition. Hence, I proceed to pass following order. :ORDER: 1. Application is allowed. 2. The applicant Sehbaaz Kamruddin Shaikh shall be released on P.B. and S.B. of Rs.15,000/­(Rupees Fifteen Thousand Only). 3. He shall not follow and sexually harass the victim by any means and shall not tamper her and shall not repeat the incident. 4. He shall not leave the jurisdiction of the court without prior permission. 5. He shall attend the concerned police station for further investigation, if any. Thane. ( S.C. Khalipe ) Date :06/06/2018.
