IN THE COURT OF THE SPECIAL JUDGE (P.O.C.S.O.ACT), THANE. (Presided over by Ms.U.M.Nandeshwar, Additional Sessions Judge­1, Thane) SPECIAL CASE No. 131 of 2014 Exhibit No. 19. The State of Maharashtra Through Kasarwadavli Police Station Thane, District – Thane. ... Prosecution versus Kashish Pyarelal Bharati Age 24 years. Resident of Murli Sheth's chawl, Room No.857, Raojinagar, Kalyan road Bhiwandi . …Accused. Offence punishable under section 363, 366, 376 of Indian Penal Code and under section 3, 4 & 14 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Appearance ­ Spl.P.P. Mrs. R.A. Navale, for the State. Advocate Mrs. Reena Korde, for the Accused. 2 Special Case No.131/2014 (Judgment) JUDGMENT (Delivered on 18th March, 2016.) 1] The Accused stands prosecuted for the offence punishable under section 363, 366, 376 of Indian Penal Code and also under section 3, 4 & 14 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act) for kidnapping, enticing for immoral purpose and committing rape and penetrative sexual assault on minor victim­girl aged about 17 years. 2] Shorn of verbiage, the indictment against the Accused are as under ­ [i] Informant Shakunatala Kailas Sing (Pw­2) is resident of Shastrinagar Bhiwandi. She is having son and daughter / victim­girl (Pw­1) aged about 15 years. [ii] Victim­girl (Pw­1) studied upto 9th std. On 30/04/2013 the victim­girl on the pretext of attending birthday of one of their acquaintance left home, but did not return till late night. Therefore, informant and her family members took her search, but she was not found. Therefore, initially, informant lodged missing report with Bhiwandi City police station, then informant learns that Kashish Pyarelal Kadojia @ Harijan (Accused) kidnapped her daughter. Therefore, she lodged report against him. 3 Special Case No.131/2014 (Judgment) 3] On her report firstly F.I.R. was registered against the Accused vide C.R.No.I­94/2013 for the offence punishable under section 363 of I.P.C. and during investigation section under section 3, 4 and 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. During investigation the victim­girl was found with Accused at Ajamgarh, U.P. From there accused was arrested and brought to Bhiwandi. The accused and victim­girl were referred for medical examination and their medical certificates were collected. Spot panchnama was drawn in presence of panchas. Statements of witnesses were recorded as per their say. Thereafter, investigation culminated into filing of charge­sheet in this Court being the Special designated court under P.O.C.S.O. Act. 4] The charge (Exh.3) was framed against the Accused for offence punishable under section 363, 366 and 376 of Indian Penal Code and also under section 4 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. There was no material on record to frame charge of using child for pornographic purpose as per section 14 of P.O.C.S.O.Act. The Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial (Exh.5). The Accused took defence of total denial. 5] In response to application under section 294 of Cr.P.C. the defence has admitted Marriage certificate of Victim­girl and Kashish (Accused) [Exh.13], Panchnama of scene of offence [Exh.14], medical certificate of accused [Exh.15], medical certificate of victim [ Exh.16], Age 4 Special Case No.131/2014 (Judgment) determination certificate of victim­girl [Exh.16­A] and C.A. reports and D.N.A. reports [Exh17]. 6] In order to prove guilt of Accused Prosecution has examined following witnesses ­ P.W.1 Victim­girl Exh.10 P.W.2 Shakuntala Kailas Sing Exh.11 (informant / mother of victim­girl) 7] The prosecution proved and relied on the report (Exh.12). 8] The prosecution closed its side of evidence by filing Pursis at Exhibit­18. As there is no incriminating evidence came on record against the Accused, therefore, his statement under Section 313(b) of Cr.P.C. is dispensed with. Accused neither examined himself nor examined any witness in his defence. 9] Heard learned Spl.P.P. Mrs. R. A. Navale for State and the learned advocate Mrs. Reena Korde for Accused. 10] Having bestowed my deep and anxious consideration on an evidence on record in the spectrum of legal position and argument advanced before me, I record my finding as per final order, for the reasons herein below :­ 5 Special Case No.131/2014 (Judgment) Sr. Points Findings No. 1 ) Does the prosecution prove that in between 30/04/2013 to 08/04/2014 accused kidnapped the daughter of informant i.e. victim­girl aged 17 years ..No. from lawful guardianship of her mother and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 363 of Indian Penal Code? 2) Whether prosecution prove that on the same date, time and place the accused procured minor girl aged 17 years, by inducing her by any means to go from any place or to do any act with intent that said ...No. girl may be or knowing that it is likely that she will be forced or seduced to illicit intercourse with another person and he thereby committed an offence punishable under section 366 of Indian Penal Code ? 3 ) Does the prosecution prove that on the same date, time and place, accused repeatedly committed rape on minor victim­girl aged 17 years, and thereby ..No. committed an offence punishable under section 376 of Indian Penal Code? 4) Does the prosecution prove that on the same day, date, time and place, accused committed sexual penetrative assault on ..No. minor victim­girl aged about 17 years as defined in section 3 and he thereby committed an offence punishable under section 4 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, 2012 ? 5) What order ? Accused is acquitted. 6 Special Case No.131/2014 (Judgment) REASONS As to Point No.1 to 4 : 11] All the points are taken up together for discussion, to avoid the repetition, as evidence about the same in common and inter­connected. 12] Firstly, as accused is facing charge under section 363 & 366 of IPC, it must be established that the minor victim­girl was enticed or taken away from lawful guardianship of her parent and she was so kidnapped or abducted with an intention to force her to marry any person, or seduce her to illicit intercourse. Further prosecution is required to prove that accused committed sexual intercourse with the victim­girl without her consent to prove charge of rape. Age of victim­girl : 13] As the Accused is facing charge of kidnapping minor for illegal/immoral purpose and also under P.O.C.S.O. Act, therefore, it is incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that the victim­girl was child (minor) at the time of incident. The alleged incident of kidnapping took place on 30/04/2013. There is school leaving certificate of the victim­ girl filed on record and as per it her date of birth is 12/04/1996, however, it is only a xerox copy. The victim­girl was referred for ossification test on 19/04/2014 and as per the X­ray report and Age determination Certificate (Exh.16­A) the approximate radiological age of victim­girl is stated as 18 to 19 7 Special Case No.131/2014 (Judgment) years which means the victim­girl was major at the time of incident. Thus, prosecution failed to prove that at the time of incident, the victim­girl was minor i.e. below the age of 18 years and she is a “child” as per definition given in Section 2(d) of the P.O.C.S.O. Act. 14] As the prosecution failed to prove that at the time of incident in question the victim­girl (P.W.1) was child below age of 18 years therefore charge of section 363 & 366 of I.P.C. and section 4 of P.O.C.S.O. Act fails and now it has to see whether prosecution is able to prove that accused committed rape on victim­girl. 15] To prove the charge against the Accused the prosecution has examined the informant/victim­girl (P.W.1). She deposed that on 30/04/2013 she herself took accused with her at Ajamgarh and performed marriage in the Court and thereafter, in the temple. She further deposed that since then they were staying at Ajamgarh as a husband and wife and delivered a male child on 05/01/2014. Thereafter, police took her and her husband in custody and brought to Bhiwandi and she was sent to Observations Home Bhiwandi for two months. Her husband i.e. accused was in jail for four months and thereafter, they again started staying together as husband and wife and then delivered a girl child on 26/10/2015. She even categorically deposed that she is happy in her married life and having no complaint against the accused and her mother 8 Special Case No.131/2014 (Judgment) lodged complaint out of misunderstanding. Informant Shakuntala Sing (P.W.2) who is mother of victim­girl also deposed on same line expressing that her daughter married with accused and blessed with two children and leading happy married life and having no complaint against the accused. She did not whisper about sexual assault. Thus, there is no iota of evidence against the accused to prove charge framed against him. 16] Even the marriage certificate of the victim­girl and accused are on record which is at Exh.13 which shows that accused and victim­girl legally married on 07/05/2013. They are blessed with two children and now they are living happily. Thus, this is a case of very sorry state of affair where though victim­girl was major and in fact by ossification test her age is stated as 18 to 19 years, still the victim­girl has to remain in the correction home for two months and accused has to languished in jail for four months. Be it as it may be, from the evidence of victim­girl and informant nothing incriminating come against accused on record. Here it is also required to mention that looking to real state of affair learned Spl.P.P. very fairly filed pursis on record closing evidence without examining the investigating officer. Thus, absolutely no charge is proved against the accused. Therefore, I answer point Nos. 1 to 4 in the negative. Thus, in absence of any legal proof against the accused, he is entitled to be acquitted. 17] In the result, I proceed to pass following order. 9 Special Case No.131/2014 (Judgment) ORDER 1] Accused Kashish Pyarelal Bharati is hereby acquitted U/Sec. 235(1) of Cr.P.C. for the offence punishable U/Sec.363, 366 and 376 of Indian Penal Code and U/Sec.4 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] His bail bonds stand cancelled and sureties are discharged. 3] The Accused is directed to furnish personal bond of the amount of ₹15,000/­ in compliance of provision of section 437­A of Cr.P.C. The judgment is dictated and pronounced in open Court. Date : 18/03/2016. (Ms. U. M. Nandeshwar), Thane Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act),Thane. District Judge ­1 and Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

IN THE COURT OF D.J.­1 & ADDL. SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE. (Presided over by Hemant M. Patwardhan) Special Case (POCSO) No. 134/2015 Exh.No. State of Maharashtra, (Nijampura Police station, Bhiwandi) ..Complainant V/s. Dhirendra Vijay Yadav. Age : 35 years, R/at. House No. 413, Yadav Building, Opp. Maharaja Hotel, Kambegaon, Tal. Bhiwandi, Dist. Thane ..Accused Appearance:­ APP Mr. Londhe for the State. Advocate Shri. G.B. Chavan for accused JUDGMENT (Delivered on this 14th day of August 2018) Accused Dhirendra Vijay Yadav was facing trial under sections 376(2)(e) of Indian Penal Code read with Sec. 4, 6 and 10 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 on following facts. 1 OF 19 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­003839­2015 Special Case (POCSO) No. 134/2015 1] That on 24.04.2015 , at about 2.30 hours to 4.00 hours in Ayush Hospital, in the ICU Ward, Ajaynagar, Bhiwandi, Dist. Thane within jurisdiction of Nijampura police station, accused has committed rape on victim a minor girl and at the same time she being a minor committed penetrative sexual assault in aggravated form. Hence, on complaint lodged by victim an offence punishable under aforesaid sections came to be registered against him. On completion of investigation he was charge­sheeted. Adjourn as court time is over. Thane (Hemant M.Patwardhan) Date: 13.08.2018 D.J.­1 & Additional Sessions Judge, Thane 2] My learned Predecessor Mrs. M.V. Bhatia, the then District Judge­7 and Addl. Sessions Judge, Thane has framed charge below Exh.15 and she has attached certificate that contents of said charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. However, while the matter was being prepared by me, for Judgment it is noticed that she inadvertently has not signed said charge. Hence, as she has already completed all formalities of recording evidence during her tenure, I have signed that charge with dated signature. Accused has put forth defence of his false implication in order to save victim's skin. 3] On the basis of aforesaid facts, prosecution then 2 OF 19 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­003839­2015 Special Case (POCSO) No. 134/2015 proceeded to examine victim, her mother, panch witnesses Mr. Haresh Shinde, Monohar Ghadge, Nimesh More, Police Station officer Deepak Barge, Medical officer Dr. Amol Bidkar and finally I.O. Vandana Viranak as PW 1 to 8 respectively. Then statement of accused was recorded as per his say wherein he has only reiterated his defence of false case being made out against him. Accused has examined Dr. Rameshkumar Jaiswal as defence witness. Arguments of rival advocates were heard. Learned P.P. has pointed out that victim and mother of victim has categorically stated and deposed the incident as it is. According to learned P.P. panch witnesses have also supported prosecution and their deposition are corroborating facts, alleged by the victim and her mother. According to P.P. there was no reason for the minor victim to implicate the accused in any such false case. Thus, according to learned P.P. prosecution has proved the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt and has further requested the court to convict him as per the provisions of law. 4] Per contra, learned Sr. advocate of the accused has categorically pointed out, unnatural conduct of victim of using washroom attached to the private ward by avoiding the washroom in ICU itself, her failure to inform about the incident to any of the staff members, treating doctor and even to her mother who was present in the waiting room adjacent to incident spot, immediately after the incident and also for about 10 to 12 hours after the incident in itself is sufficient to inferred that no such incident had ever occurred. He has then pointed out that after discharge, the victim has behaved in 3 OF 19 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­003839­2015 Special Case (POCSO) No. 134/2015 very causal manner and has completed all her daily affairs on that date without there being any change in her behaviour. According to him that fact itself goes to show that such incident had never occurred. He has then pointed out that if topography of ICU is considered then it is highly improbable that any incident of such a nature could not be seen or even heard by a person sitting or sleeping adjacent to said ICU. According to him it was a very small hospital consisting of ICU, waiting hall, consulting room and general ward with attached washroom. Therefore, as the rooms are situated adjacent to each other it is obvious that anything had happened in any of said rooms can be easily witnessed or atleast can be heard by the persons present in the adjacent room. According to him as there is no case of the prosecution witnesses as such it is again created a doubt in respect of occurrence of the incident itself. He has then pointed out that medical evidence is not supporting prosecution. Hence, entire allegations cannot be said to be proved beyond reasonable doubt. He has then pointed out that accused has categorically put forth that victim was having some relations with one aged person in the society and was under impression that accused will inform her family members about it and in order to save her own skin from the information being parted by accused person to her family members she has implicated accused. 5] While making comments on statement of her mother as well he has categorically pointed out that conduct of the mother was 4 OF 19 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­003839­2015 Special Case (POCSO) No. 134/2015 also against the conduct of natural human being as she even did not ask her daughter as to why she did not disclose the facts immediately after the incident nor she had asked the victim as to why she has stated lie to the doctor that her stomach was paining and the reason behind it. It was also pointed out that witnesses even did not hear noise of screaming or crying or any call being made by victim during that night from ICU. She has categorically stated that victim did not make an attempt to wake her up when she was outside the ICU and she could not hear any conversation that night from the ICU. Hence, according to learned advocate the admissions of the mother are also sufficient to discard the evidence of the victim. He has therefore, requested to acquit the accused by discarding of the said evidence. 6] After having heard the rival advocates, following points arise for my consideration and I record my findings against each of them for the reasons noted below:­ S.N. Points Findings 1] Does the prosecution prove that accused on 24.04.2015 at about ..In the 2.30 hrs. to 04.00 hrs in Ayush Hospital, in ICU Ward, Ajaynagar , affirmative. Dist. Thane in the jurisdiction of Nijampura police station, Bhiwandi committed rape on victim, a minor aged 14 years and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 376(2)(e)of IPC? 2] Does the prosecution prove that accused on aforesaid date, time and ..In the place, committed penetrative sexual assault on victim, a minor aged affirmative. 14 years and thereby committed an offence punishable under Sec. 4 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012? 3] Does the prosecution prove that accused on aforesaid date, time and ..In the negative. place, committed aggravated penetrative sexual assault on victim, a minor aged 14 years and thereby committed an offence punishable under Sec. 6 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012? 5 OF 19 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­003839­2015 Special Case (POCSO) No. 134/2015 4] Does the prosecution prove that accused on aforesaid date, time and ..In the negative. place, committed aggravated penetrative sexual assault on victim, a minor aged 14 years and thereby committed an offence punishable under Sec. 10 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012? 5] What order ? Accused is convicted as per final order. REASONS As to point nos. 1 to 5 :­ 7] All these points are interlinked with each other and are discussed at once. In the instant case prosecution has categorically made allegation that on eventful time when the victim was admitted at Ayush Hospital with complaints of breathing problem, Dr. Jaiswal has started treating her by admitting her in ICU. According to allegations Dr. Jaiswal has removed saline, oxygen and B.P. machine around 2.30 a.m. and left ICU and then victim and Dr. Yadav i.e. accused were only left in ICU. According to allegation then Dr. Yadav got up, came towards her and on his own had asked victim whether she was facing any difficulty and whether her stomach is paining. Dr. Yadav has then asked whether the victim had sex with anybody and whether had affair with anybody and asked her whether the stomach is paining and then started pressing her stomach and started asking her whether it is paining where he is pressing. Hence, according to allegations accused then asked the victim to pull up her maxi and again started pressing her stomach. The victim was then 6 OF 19 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­003839­2015 Special Case (POCSO) No. 134/2015 asked to remove her panty and though she has resisted for it, accused had told her that he will apply ointment on her stomach and that will stop pain and on that pretext the victim has removed her panty, then accused took one ointment from the table and started applying it on her vagina by his finger and inserted finger in vagina for about five minutes. According to allegations, then accused asked her to wear panty and advised her to have sex in every alternative day and her problem will be resolved and went to bed and slept. On perusal of depositions of the victim, she has categorically stated said incident and has also admitted that she was discharge around 6.00 a.m. but from 6.00 a.m to 6.00 p.m. she did not disclose that fact to her mother and by 6.00 p.m. when her mother came back she informed about entire incident to her and then her mother had informed that fact to her aunt. They went to Ayush hospital to meet Mr. Yadav but he was not there. Accused was called on phone but he did not come though they have waited for long therefore, by 3.00 a.m. on next morning visited the concern police station and lodged the complaint Exh.23. 8] In the present matter victim was only material eye witness of the incident and accordingly she has categorically referred the incident with minute details. The victim was cross­examined at length and it was specifically brought on record that in that particular hospital when she was admitted attendant by name Imran was present there while ECG was taken she did not inform that either her stomach or her vagina is paining. She has also admitted 7 OF 19 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­003839­2015 Special Case (POCSO) No. 134/2015 that waiting room of the hospital is admeasuring around 10 to 12 feet situated soon after entering the hospital. She has also admitted that toilet is on right side of ICU which is before entering ICU and after that waiting room is situated followed by reception and rest room of doctor. She has also admitted that after incident she understood that incident is inappropriate and she went to toilet which is situated in the general ward. She has also admitted the fact that while going to the toilet she has seen her mother and felt it that she should inform about incident to her mother but did not inform her. She also admitted that she did not cry while going to toilet and while coming back from the toilet. She has also admitted that she should not felt that she should intimate Dr. Jaiswal while going and coming back from the toilet but she did not inform the same to Mr. Jaiswal as well. Hence, on the basis of said admissions aforesaid arguments were advanced by learned defence advocate. In view of the arguments advanced by rival advocates aforesaid evidence has to be scrutinized in the light of facts brought before this court. 9] At the outset if the charge is considered then it is under section 376(2)(e) of IPC read with section 4,6 and 10 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. However, even if we consider the provisions of section 6 to section 10 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 then it is apparent that said sections speaks about punishment for aggravated penetrative sexual assaults and aggravated penetrative sexual assaults are categorically defined under section 5 and section 9 of the 8 OF 19 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­003839­2015 Special Case (POCSO) No. 134/2015 particular Act. If we consider section 5 and section 9, it relates to police officer, a public servant or management or on the staff of a jail, remand home, protection home, management or staff of a hospital, management or staff of an educational institution or religious institution etc. In the instance case though the offence is alleged against a medical officer attached to a particular hospital, however it nowhere appears that there are any allegations of accused being members of the particular staff of the hospital at the relevant time. On the contrary it is alleged that he himself was under treatment at the relevant time of alleged act. Therefore, on plain perusal and plain reading of the allegation put forth, it is difficult to say that accused can be covered within the definition of section 5 or section 9 of POCSO Act to punish him under section 6 and or section 10 of Act. Having considered the definition of the particular section and Act alleged against particular accused, in my opinion, it is difficult to hold accused guilt of the offence punishable under aforesaid two sections. Hence, I record my findings against point no.3 and 4 in negative. 10] Accused was also charged with section 376 of IPC and section 4 of POCSO wherein said section 4 described the punishment for penetrative sexual assault wherein section 3 defines penetrative sexual assault. In the said section Sub­Clause (b) has categorically lays down that a person is said to commit penetrative sexual assault if he inserts to any extent, any object or a part of the body, not being the penis, into the vagina of a child or makes the child to do so is 9 OF 19 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­003839­2015 Special Case (POCSO) No. 134/2015 said to have committed offence of penetrative sexual assault. So is the case of section 376 of IPC wherein section 376 defines punishment and section 375 defines the meaning of section. As per amended provisions of section 375, even an insertion of any object or part of the body not being penis into the vagina of a woman or make her to do it or any other person also is rape within the meaning of said section. Hence, after having gone through the definition of said section this court has to consider whether the act of the accused really comes within the purview of any of the said two sections. 11] In the instant case it has been categorically alleged by the victim that after the instrument of saline, blood pressure etc. were removed she herself along with accused were only remain in ICU when accused has approached her and has committed the act of inserting the finger in her vagina on the pretext of applying ointment after having asked her whether she had any affair or had sex with any other person. Hence, if we consider the specific allegation of the eye witness and the victim, then insertion of his finger in the vagina of the child certainly comes within the definition of section 3 of the particular Act and section 375 of IPC. Hence, it is apparent from the allegations and deposition of victim that particular act itself is sufficient to complete the offence as defined respectively under section 375 of IPC and section 3 of POCSO Act. After having considered the specific allegations of the victim, same has to be tested on the defence of the accused person. In the present case presence of the accused on the spot is an admitted position. 10 OF 19 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­003839­2015 Special Case (POCSO) No. 134/2015 Therefore, if the allegations of the victim are considered as it is then this court has to apply presumption referred under section 29 and 30 of POCSO Act in favour of the victim and against the accused person. The onus was then shifted on the accused to show that he was not in such mental state referred in section 30 of act and for said purpose he was just required to establish his defence by preponderance of probabilities. 12] In the instant case accused had denied occurrence of any such incident and then has also put forth the defence that victim had some affair with old aged person in her building and as the doctor was about to disclose it to her family members she has implicated him in this false case. However, it is apparent that subsequent defence was categorically put forth to the victim and she has denied the particular suggestion. Though defence of the accused that victim being interested in aged person of the building is put forth, there is no explanation from the accused person from where accused has got knowledge of the particular act of the victim. It is nowhere case of victim that though she was treated by the accused himself on two previous occasions, she had ever informed him about her being involved in any such affairs. Hence, in absence of any such explanation about the source of knowledge of the particular fact it is difficult to accept any such defence to discard mental state as referred under section 30 of POCSO Act. 13] Dr. Jaiswal was examined as defence witness to 11 OF 19 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­003839­2015 Special Case (POCSO) No. 134/2015 substantiate defence. Dr.Jaiswal did not support prosecution though he was cross­examined at length by the learned P.P. he was firm on the point that no such incident had occurred. However, during his deposition he has made a statement that he himself has informed the accused about the affair of the victim. However, at cost of repetition I would like to say that there is no explanation from Dr. Jaiswal as well about the source of such information and in absence of any such source it is difficult to accept that Dr.Jaiswal was aware of the particular fact to disclose it to the accused person. Admittedly, Dr.Jaiswal had treated victim for the frist time at the time of incident. Therefore, unless he disclosed his source of information, his said act is unacceptable. Having regards to the said facts, I do not find any substance in the defence of the accused to say that onus after being shifted on the accused to disprove about his mental state as defined under section 30 of the Act has been established even by preponderance of probabilities. 14] When the presence of the accused was admitted on the spot and when admittedly victim was not under his treatment his approaching the victim for even asking whether she was feeling well or not in itself is sufficient to inferred about her mental state of involving himself in act with sexual intent. Otherwise, he has no business to treat the victim even though she has made a complaint to him about pain in the stomach as he himself was being admitted in the hospital as patient for treatment or has alleged to have taking rest in ICU patient. Therefore, it was expected from him, even if any 12 OF 19 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­003839­2015 Special Case (POCSO) No. 134/2015 complaint was made to him to immediately call treating doctor to attend the victim. At particular stage, however as he did not call said doctor who was treating the victim, and as per further allegation has asked victim to have sex on alternative day in itself sufficient to inferred his intention. As the victim has categorically alleged that as to how accused has committed penetrative sexual assault by insertion of the finger in her vagina then accused was required to disprove it by some cogent and consistent facts which clearly goes to disprove the allegations even by preponderance of probabilities. However, as aforesaid subsequent defence of the accused has to be discarded on the aforesaid grounds. Therefore, only defence available with the accused is of his false implication. 15] However, there is absolutely no ground for the victim to implicate accused in such false case particularly when subsequent defence is discarded by the court. During the arguments much hue and cry was made about unnatural conduct of the victim after the said incident. However, there cannot be any straight jacket formula about the conduct of a victim immediately after particular incident. It differs from person to person as to how the person would react on particular incident or after being victim of the particular incident. In the instant case, it was categorically brought by the learned defence advocate himself that victim was patient of depression and was obtaining treatment for it. Hence, it is apparent from defence itself that her mental state was certainly not like that of natural human being which reacts immediately as expected by learned defence 13 OF 19 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­003839­2015 Special Case (POCSO) No. 134/2015 advocate. Hence, merely because witness did not state particular fact immediately to her mother in itself, in my opinion, considering the aforesaid depressed mental state of the victim can be neglected. Further, during cross­examination, defence itself has categorically brought it on record that she felt it necessary to inform inappropriate incident to her mother while she was going to washroom and has seen her mother will be in the waiting room. However, victim might have thought it improbable to inform her mother in presence of accused person or being felt insecure or might have felt depressed. Further, if we consider the depressed state of mind then said alleged unnatural act of the victim can be ignored. Reference is made of nobody has heard noise when alleged act was committed. However, said defence needs no consideration as it is not case of victim that at that time she has either shouted for help or in pain. Therefore, there was no question of hearing it. Further, if we consider incident's time, then nobody will enter ICU when both patients admitted were only resting there. Having regards to said circumstance in my opinion unnatural conduct of the victim in itself cannot be sufficient to discard the allegations particularly when there was no reason for her to implicate the accused in such false case. 16] Arguments were also advanced that there is no corroboration by Dr. Jaiswal or the victim did state the particular fact immediately to Dr. Jaiswal though while discharging her she met 14 OF 19 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­003839­2015 Special Case (POCSO) No. 134/2015 Dr. Jaiswal and other staff members in the hospital. However, at the cost of repetition I would like to say that if we consider depressed state of mind of the victim then such act is bound to occur and in the said state of depression she might not have disclosed such heinous act to staff members immediately. It is the case of the victim that she has disclosed the incident initially to her mother and therefore, mother can only corroborate said incident which she did. During her examination­in­chief though she was categorically asked did she ask the victim as to why she lie to the doctor that her stomach is paining. The witness though has answered that she did not ask, said answer also in my opinion is not favouring the defence at all in view of the fact that victim herself has never made complaint on her own about stomach pain before accused person but it was the accused who appears to have started conversation by asking her whether her stomach is paining. Though the victim has then answered that it was paining that answer to the query of the accused and not on her own. Therefore, in my opinion said fact though put forth to the mother of the victim in itself are not sufficient to discard aforesaid allegations. Having regards to the said fact in my opinion none of the defence of accused are sufficient to discard the allegations of prosecution and in view of the corroboration by victim and her mother with panch witnesses the act of the accused is proved on record. 17] The defence has also raised in respect of some lacuna in investigation and about favourable medical report on record. No doubt when the medical officer was examined he has made reference 15 OF 19 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­003839­2015 Special Case (POCSO) No. 134/2015 of his opinion that there is possibility that finger might have been put or might not have been put as alleged during cross­examination. However, it we consider the report itself which is at Exh.53 then it appears that as a matter of fact, Doctor has opined that possibility of finger being inserted in the victim's vagina cannot be ruled out. Therefore, in my opinion particular opinion of the doctor is not favouring the accused but is favouring the victim's version. No doubt medical officer did not find injuries to the private part of the victim. However, it was alleged that ointment which was used by the accused in the act was anesthetic drug which on application makes particular part senseless temporarily. Said fact is referred in cross­ examination of Dr. Jaiswal. Therefore, if on its application if said part become senseless, the victim might not have resisted insertion after its first application which might be cause of injuries not being caused to her private part. So far as lacunas referred in the investigation is concerned, merely because deposition of some witnesses were not recorded by I.O. in itself cannot be sufficient to discard allegation which otherwise appears to be trustworthy. Further on perusal of deposition of I.O. it appears that when she seized attendance register of the staff, she found no female nurse present in the hospital at the time of incident. Thus, as the said fact is not declined by the accused person, deposition of the defence witness Dr. Jaiswal appears to have been formatted just to make an attempt to disprove the presumption referred under section 29 and 30 of POCSO Act. If Mr. Jaiswal's 16 OF 19 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­003839­2015 Special Case (POCSO) No. 134/2015 deposition is considered as it is then he has made contradictory statements about condition of the patient which goes to show that he was trying to help colleague by said deposition. For instance during his examination­in­chief initially he has stated that when the victim was brought to hospital and he examined her found her B.P. was high and then in further statement he had made contradictory statement that he has started saline as B.P. was low. Hence, it is apparent that Mr. Jaiswal was not keen to state true facts before the court and intention behind it is apparently to help his colleague doctor. Therefore, I do not find either lacunas in particular investigation is fatal to the prosecution or defence is sufficient to disprove the allegations. Having regards to all these facts in my opinion prosecution has established guilt of accused under section 376 of IPC read with section 4 of POCSO Act are concerned. Accordingly, I do not hesitate to record my findings against those points in affirmative and hold the accused guilt of the offence. As I hold accused guilt of the offence, it is necessary to hear the accused on the point of sentence. Judgment is therefore, deferred to hear the accused on the point of sentence. 18] Heard accused on the point of sentence. He has requested to impose minimum sentence and has submitted that he still maintained that he is innocent. Learned advocate Mr. Patil holding for Sr. Advocate Shri. Chavan has also requested the court to take lenient view on the ground that accused is having tender aged children, old aged parents and he is only earning member of family. 17 OF 19 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­003839­2015 Special Case (POCSO) No. 134/2015 Heard learned P.P. He has submitted that the patient gets admitted in particular hospital for having trust on the doctors. He has then quoted Marathi idiom "daqi.kp 'ksr [kkrs"- However, if said doctor commit breach of trust then has to be viewed seriously. According to him if such accused is not punished properly wrong signal will go to the society. Hence, he has requested to impose maximum punishment. 19] Having heard the rival advocates and accused on the point of sentence, in my opinion considering the facts and circumstances in which offence has been committed following order will serve purpose. Hence, I proceed to pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused Dhirendra Vijay Yadav is hereby convicted for the offence punishable under section 376(1) of IPC read with section 4 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act 2012 and he is sentenced to suffer R.I. for seven years each under said sections and liable to pay fine of Rs.10,000/­ each under said sections i/d. to suffer further R.I. for four months under each sections. 2] On recovery of fine amount an amount of Rs.15,000/­ be paid to victim as compensation by exercising powers under section 357(1) of Cr.P.C. towards expenditure and cost of particular proceeding and remaining amount be credited to State. 18 OF 19 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­003839­2015 Special Case (POCSO) No. 134/2015 3] Both the sentences under said sections shall run concurrently. 4] Accused Dhirendra Vijay Yadav is hereby acquitted from the offence punishable under section 6, 10 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act 2012. 5] Muddemal property tube being worthless be destroyed after appeal period. 6] Set off is hereby granted for period already undergone by accused in judicial custody by exercising powers under section 428 of Cr.P.C. 7] Copy of the Judgment be provided to the accused free of cost. Resident of Room No.4 Chawl No.86, Sector­21, Bank of India Road, Turbhe Navi Mumbai, Dist. Thane. …Accused. [ii] On 03/04/2014 the victim­girl (P.W.2) complained that she is having stomach­ache and filling giddiness therefore, she was taken to the hospital at Chembur, Mumbai. Thereafter, after examining the victim­girl, Doctor disclosed that she is carrying pregnancy of four months. Therefore, the informant by taking the victim­girl in confidence asked her. On that victim­girl disclosed that between November­2013 to March­2014 accused lure her to give money and used to take in the bushes near Vashi Railway station and committed sexual assault on her from time to time and also threatened her not to 3 Special Case No.133/2014 (Judgment) disclose it to anybody otherwise he will kill her. Therefore, on 03/04/2014 informant with victim­girl, one Sonabai and her relatives had been to the accused to question him and accused threatened them to do whatever they want. Therefore, the informant lodged report against the accused. 3] On her report F.I.R. was registered against the Accused vide C.R.No.I­110/2014 for the offence punishable under section 363, 376, 506 & 506(2) of I.P.C. and under Section 4 of POCSO Act and 3(xi) of Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocity) Act and 7(b) Protection of Civil Rights Act by P.S.I Neelam Pawar (P.W.4). The victim­girl was referred for medical examination. The statement of victim­girl was recorded with the help of translator as per her say, as she did not understand Marathi. The cloths of victim­girl were seized. Spot panchnama was drawn in presence of panchas. Statements of witnesses were recorded as per their say. Further investigation was carried out by A.P.I. Nandkumar Mohanrao Kadam (P.W.7) who issued letter for DNA and collected required samples of accused for DNA test. The cloths of accused and victim­girl were sent for C.A. to F.S.L. He recorded statement of witnesses as per their say. Copy of birth certificate, school leaving certificate and caste certificate were collected. The victim­girl belongs to scheduled caste and scheduled tribes therefore provisions of S.C. & S.T. (Prevention) of Atrocity Act were applied and investigation was carried out by A.C.P. Arun Valthare, Vashi Division, Thane. C.A. reports and D.N.A. reports were 4 Special Case No.133/2014 (Judgment) collected. Thereafter, investigation culminated into filing of charge­sheet in this Court being the Special designated court under P.O.C.S.O. Act. 4] My learned predecessor the erstwhile Additional Sessions Judge, Thane framed the charge (Exh.6) against the Accused for offence punishable under section 363, 376 & 506 of Indian Penal Code and also under section 7 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and section 3(xi) of S.C. & S.T. (Prevention) of Atrocity Act. The Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial (Exh.5). The Accused took defence of total denial. 5] In response to application under section 294 of Cr.P.C. the defence has admitted opinion of radiologist about age of victim­girl (Exh.60). 6] In order to prove guilt of Accused Prosecution has examined following witnesses ­ P.W.1 Lata Ganpat Pawar Exh.17 (Informant / mother of victim­girl) P.W.2 Victim­girl Exh.18 P.W.3 Pramodini Pravin Jadhav Exh.22 (Councillor attached with Women Cell) P.W.4 P.S.I. Neelam Prakash Pawar Exh.28 (Investigating officer) P.W.5 Dr. Sachin Tukaram Waghmare Exh.35 (Medical officer – Examined Accused) P.W.6 Dr. Sanjay Yashwant Mhatre Exh.42 (Sonologist NMMC Hospital) P.W.7 Nandkumar Mohanrao Kadam Exh.52 (Investigating officer) 5 Special Case No.133/2014 (Judgment) 7] The prosecution proved and relied on following documents. 1] Arrest panchnama of accused Exh.23 2] portion marked 'A' of report of informant Exh.29 3] F.I.R. Exh.30 4] Seizure panchnama of cloths of victim­ Exh.31 girl 5] Medical certificate of accused Exh.36 6] Medical certificate of victim­girl Exh.37 7] Letter for getting DNA kit Exh.53 8] letter to NMMC hospital for collecting Exh.54 samples 9] letter to F.S.L. for forwarding samples Exh.55 for DNA 10] letter sending cloths of accused for C.A. Exh.56 11] letter producing victim­girl before C.W.C Exh.57 12] C.A. reports Exh.58 & 59 13] D.N.A. report Exh.49 . 8] The prosecution closed its side of evidence by filing Pursis at Exhibit­61.The incriminating evidence came on record against the Accused was readover and explained to him in vernacular and his statement under Section 313(b) of Cr.P.C. was recorded. Accused neither examined himself nor examined any witness in his defence. 9] Heard learned Spl.P.P. Mrs. R. A. Navale for State and the learned advocate Mr. Rajesh More for Accused at length. 6 Special Case No.133/2014 (Judgment) 10] Having bestowed my deep and anxious consideration on an evidence on record in the spectrum of legal position and argument advanced before me, I record my finding as per final order, for the reasons herein below :­ Sr. Points Findings No. 1 ) Does the prosecution prove that in between November­2013 to March­2014 at Jugaon, Vashi, Sector­11 Navi Mumbai, accused kidnapped the victim­girl aged 14 ..No. years from lawful guardianship of her mother and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 363 of Indian Penal Code? 2 ) Does the prosecution prove that on the above date, time and in front of Raghuleela Mall, Kaccha road in front of Vashi railway station accused committed ..No. rape on minor victim­girl from time to time and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 376 of Indian Penal Code? 3) Does the prosecution prove that on the same date, time and place, accused committed criminal intimidation by threatening the victim­girl to kill, if she ..No. disclosed about rape on her to anybody and thus committed an offence punishable under section 506 of I.P.C.? 4) Does the prosecution prove that on the same day, date, time and place, accused committed penetrative sexual assault on minor victim­girl aged about 14 years as defined in section 5 by kidnapping her and ..No. 7 Special Case No.133/2014 (Judgment) made her to be pregnant in consequent of his act and he thereby committed an offence punishable under section 6 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, 2012 ? 5) Does the prosecution prove that on the same date, time and place accused committed sexual assault on the minor victim­girl aged about 17 years who belongs to Schedule Caste and Scheduled .. No. Tribes and thereby he committed an offence punishable under section 3(xi) of Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention) of Atrocity Act ? 6) What order ? Accused is acquitted. REASONS As to Point No.1 to 5 : 11] All the points are taken up together for discussion, to avoid the repetition, as evidence about the same in common and inter­connected. 12] Firstly, as accused is facing charge under section 363 of IPC, it must be established that the minor victim­girl was enticed or taken away from lawful guardianship of her parent and she was so kidnapped or abducted with an intention to force her to marry any person, or seduce her to illicit intercourse. Further prosecution is required to prove that accused committed sexual intercourse with the victim­girl without her consent to prove charge of rape. 8 Special Case No.133/2014 (Judgment) Age of victim­girl : 13] As the Accused is facing charge of kidnapping minor girl for illegal/immoral purpose and also under P.O.C.S.O. Act, therefore, it is incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that the victim­girl was child (minor) at the time of incident. It is pertinent to note that neither victim­ girl (P.W.2) nor her mother (P.W.1) stated her date of birth. Neither there is any document about the date of birth i.e. School Leaving or birth certificate on record. To prove the age of victim­girl, prosecution has examined Dr. Sachin Waghmare (P.W.5) who deposed that on 03/04/2014 he has examined a patient / victim­girl as she was referred for age determination. He further deposed that clinically her age was 12 to 14 years and he reserved his opinion for X­ray report and accordingly, issued certificate which is at Exh.37. However, he specifically admitted in the cross­examination that x­ray report is necessary for giving opinion about determination of age and he never had an occasion to see the x­ray report of the patient. Then it is significant to note that x­ray report was on record and the defence had admitted the x­ray report which is in respect of ossification test wherein opinion on the basis of X­ ray is given. As per said report the radiographic age of victim­ girl is 17 years plus minus 6 months. As there is no exact date of birth on record, and P.W.­5 stated clinical age of victim­girl as 12­14 years reserving his opinion for x­ray report and as per x­ray report radiographic bone­age of victim­girl is 17 years plus or minus with the margin of 6 months therefore, it will not safe to hold that the victim­girl was minor on the date of 9 Special Case No.133/2014 (Judgment) incident as there remains doubt about the age of the victim­ girl. Thus, the prosecution failed to prove that at the time of incident, the victim­girl was minor i.e. below the age of 18 years and she is a “child” as per definition given in Section 2(d) of the P.O.C.S.O. Act. 14] As the prosecution failed to prove that at the time of incident in question the victim­girl (P.W.1) was child below age of 18 years therefore charge of section 363 of I.P.C. and section 4 of P.O.C.S.O. Act fails and now the only question remains as to whether accused committed sexual intercourse with the victim­girl from time to time and because of which she carries the pregnancy. 15] In this respect, the evidence of the victim­girl (P.W.2) is most material. In the present case, when the F.I.R was recorded, at that time, the victim­girl was not knowing Hindi or Marathi and only knowing the Kannada language, therefore, her statement was recorded with the help of one translator Sonabai who claims to know Marathi and Kannada languages. However, at the time of evidence when the victim­ girl entered in witness­box she stated that she knows Marathi and on preliminary inquiry she could answer the question reasonably and even knows the sanctity of oath therefore, her evidence was recorded. However, victim­girl did not state her date of birth and taking into consideration the police papers wherein her age is mentioned, the approximate age of the victim­girl is mentioned as 12 to 13 years. The victim­girl 10 Special Case No.133/2014 (Judgment) (P.W.2) deposed that she is staying with her parents and younger sister. Her parents used to sell flowers at signal. She did not attend the school. Sometimes, she also accompanied with her parents for selling flowers. However, she refused to identify the accused and denied being sexually assaulted by the accused and about threats extended by him. She denied all the suggestions about the occurrence of the incident or her statement recorded by one social worker ­ Pramodini Jadhav (P.W.3). Thus, this evidence of the victim­girl (P.W.2) is of no assistance to the prosecution. 16] Further the informant / mother of victim­girl Lata Pawar (P.W.1) also did not support the prosecution case and even denied having lodged any report against the accused about commission of rape on her daughter and also refused to identify the accused and deposed that she did not know him. 17] In the background of such evidence of the victim­ girl (P.W.2) and the informant (P.W.1), now it is required to see whether there is any other evidence on record either in the form of document or oral testimony of the expert witnesses to prove that the victim­girl was sexually assaulted and accused is the perpetrator of the crime. 18] Yet another Aspect of this case is that when the F.I.R. was registered and statement of victim­girl was recorded, at that time, as per the prosecution case itself, she was not conversant with Hindi or Marathi language and 11 Special Case No.133/2014 (Judgment) therefore, the help of translator was taken for recording her statement and the said statement of the victim­girl was recorded by Pramodini Jadhav (P.W.3) who is attached with Mahila cell and worked as counselor and she deposed that on 13/04/2014 she recorded statement of the victim­girl who was allegedly sexually assaulted and that too, in presence of police in the question­answer form as per the say of the victim­girl. In the cross­examination she stated that the statement of the victim­girl was recorded in police station. However, there is material contradictory evidence given by PSI Neelam Pawar (P.W.4) who recorded the report of informant. She, in her cross­examination stated that the statement of the victim­girl was recorded in the hospital. Thus, the contradictory evidence of P.W.3 and P.W.4 creates considerable doubt about the recording of the statement of the victim­girl. 19] Another significant aspect of the case is that the translator Sonabai who stated to have helped at the time of recording of the statement of the victim­girl, is not at all examined before the court. Neither there is any document on record to show that Sonabai was conversant with the language of victim­girl or she was conversant with the Kannad or Marathi language. Even the investigating officer A.P.I. Kadam (P.W.7) did not make any efforts of collecting any such documentary evidence to prove that Sonabai Kale knew both the languages. Therefore, a serious doubt about the credibility of the presence of P.W.3 and the recording of statement of the victim­girl by her is arises. 12 Special Case No.133/2014 (Judgment) 20] Now let us see whether there is any medical evidence in support of prosecution case. The prosecution has examined Dr. Sachin Waghmare (P.W.5) who is attached to the NMMC Hospital at Vashi. He examined the accused as well as the victim­girl. As far as the medical fitness of the accused is concerned, it is not at all challenged. P.W.5 deposed that nothing has been found to suggest the patient (Accused) is impotent and the medical certificate of the Accused is at Exh.36. 21] It is the case of the prosecution that on 03/04/2014 victim­girl complaint about stomach­ache and giddiness therefore she was taken in hospital where doctor on examination of victim­girl disclosed that she is carrying pregnancy of four months. To prove said aspect the prosecution has examined Dr. Sanjay Mhatre (P.W.6) who is Sonologist attached to NMMC General hospital at Vashi. On 04/04/2014 Dr. Mahtre has examined the patient victim­girl. She was referred as medico­legal case for sonography. P.W.6 further deposed that the patient stated her age as 12 years and she was carrying single fetus aged 19 weeks and 6 days pregnancy and accordingly he issued Sonography report. However, the original Sonography report is never filed in the court and only xerox copy of said report is placed on the record, therefore, Xerox copy was not exhibited and it is marked as Article­A. 13 Special Case No.133/2014 (Judgment) 22] Further, another significant aspect of this case is the DNA examination report of the victim­girl, which is placed on record and marked as Exh.49. Exhibit 49 – DNA examination report eloquent that DNA extracted from blood of Rahman Sakir Khan (Accused) and blood of victim­girl was typed at 15 STR Loci and gender specific Amelogenin locus using PCR amplification technique and for all 15 different genetic systems analysed with PCR Rehman Khan (Accused) failed to match the obligate paternal alleles present in the Foetus of victim­girl at 7 loci. Thus, as per final opinion accused is excluded to be biological father of the Foetus of victim­girl and victim­girl is concluded to be the biological mother of foetus she was carrying. Thus, even the medical evidence is clearly in favour of accused. 23] As far as charge under Schedule caste & scheduled Tribes (Prevention) of Atrocity Act is concern, there is absolutely no evidence on record to prove that victim­girl belongs to scheduled Tribes. Neither victim­girl nor her mother / informant stated their caste. The caste certificate of victim­ girl is also not produced on record only xerox copy without any attestation is placed on record which is nothing but a piece of paper as it no way going to help the prosecution. 24] Thus, there is absolutely no evidence on record to prove the charge against the accused and specifically the charge of sexual assault on the victim­girl and accused is entitled to be acqitted. Therefore, I answer point No. 1 to 5 in 14 Special Case No.133/2014 (Judgment) negative. 26] In the result, I proceed to pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused Rehman Saakir Khan is hereby acquitted U/Sec. 235(1) of Cr.P.C. for the offence punishable U/Sec.363, 376 & 506 of Indian Penal Code, U/Sec.6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and 3(xi) of Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention) of Atrocity Act. 2] The accused is in jail. He be released forthwith if not required in any other case. 3] The Accused is directed to furnish personal bond of the amount of ₹15,000/­ in compliance of provision of section 437­A of Cr.P.C. The judgment is dictated and pronounced in open Court. Date : 07/05/2016. (Ms. U. M. Nandeshwar), Thane Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act),Thane. District Judge ­1 and Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

--1-- ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN CRIMINAL BAIL APPLICATION NO.1374/2018 CNR NO. MHTH01­003875­2018 The applicant Ashraf Ali @ Mohd. Ahmad Maraz Siddique has applied for bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C., in C.R. No.I­268/2018 registered in Mumbra police station for the offence under section 354 of IPC and Section 8, 12 of POCSO Act, 2012. 2. It is contended that the applicant is falsely implicated. The story of the prosecution is not believable. The offence is not punishable with death or imprisonment for life. There is no criminal antecedent, therefore, applicant prayed for bail. 3. Investigating Officer has given his say at Exh.4. It is contended that the victim is 12 years old. While victim was going to market the accused caught her hands and said, “muze tera mobile number de, nahi degi to jabardasti karunga” and further pressurized her and moved hands on her chest and said “andar chal koi nahi hai, suhagrat manayenge”. I.O. has contended that previously also accused had followed the victim and affected her modesty. Accused has no residence place. If he released on bail he is likely to tamper the prosecution witnesses, therefore, bail may be rejected. 4. I heard Ld. Counsel on behalf of accused and Ld. DGP. 5. It is clear from the say of the I.O that the victim is 12 years old. She is minor and previously accused had assaulted victim with intent to affect her modesty and for the second time he caught the victim and pressurizing her and forced her to give her mobile number and threatened that, if not given he will do force upon her. He moved hands on her chest and said “andar chal koi nahi hai, --2-- suhagrat manayenge”. This repeated act of the accused shows what was his intension. This is serious offence. Accused has no residence place. Accused has produced I.D card and one license agreement of his brother, but he has no fix residence place in Mumbai. So, if released on bail he is likely to tamper the prosecution witnesses and fly away from the bail. He is likely to repeat the offence because previously he had molested the same girl and therefore, there is most likely to repeat the offence and commit more serious offence and therefore, considering all the facts and circumstances of this case it is not a fit case to release the accused on bail. Bail No.1502/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exhibit 1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 1502/2015 This application is filed by applicant Praduman Gokul Shahu for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. I-55/2015 registered at Shil Daighar police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 366B, 370, 370(a) of I.P.C. and section 3, 4, 5, 6, 9 of Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act (hereinafter in short referred to as I.T.P.A.). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant imported the victim girl namely Nipa Papri from Bangladesh by administering her sedative and then handed over her to co-accused who then forced the girl to do prostitution. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co-operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that the applicant imported the victim girl namely Nipa Papri from Bangladesh by administering her sedative for engaging her to do prostitution and then handed over her to co-accused Rabbi Mulla who gave her false of promise of marriage and then engaged her for prostitution and compelled her to do prostitution. It is further contended and argued that all accused including wanted accused and present applicant have been indulged in conducting prostitution and conduct such business in Aman Heights at Shil Daighar. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the .. 2 .. Bail No.1502/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) victim girl and the prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused are of serious nature under section 366B, 370, 370(a) of I.P.C. and section 3, 4, 5, 6, 9 of I.T.P.A. and from the perusal of F.I.R. the role attributed to the applicant is that he had administered some sedative to the victim girl and kidnapped her and then handed over her to co-accused Rabbi Mulla, it is contended by the applicant that he had not played any role and he was merely standing near the spot where raid was effected and he is falsely implicated in this crime. In such circumstance whether the allegations against the accused are true or not, would be the question to be decided on merits. Even nothing is stated to be recovered from the applicant/accused. 4] Then, the applicant is seen to be in jail since 05.03.2015 and the investigation in this matter may have almost completed by this time. 5] Then, it is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. .. 3 .. Bail No.1502/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) 6] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 7] Then, it has also to be mentioned that looking the allegations against the accused the investigation in the matter may have almost completed but the charge-sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge- sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 8] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order - ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Praduman Gokul Shahu is released on P.R. bond of Rs.20,000/- [rupees twenty thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions - The applicant/accused shall attend concerned police station on every Friday between 10.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon and shall co-operate in investigation. He shall not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and the prosecution witnesses and .. 4 .. Bail No.1502/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this Court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 13.07.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.

After completion of investigation, charge sheet came to be filed. 6] The defence of the accused as constructed in cross­examination and statements under Sec. 313 Cr.P.C. is that the he is falsely implicated. 7] I have heard Ld. Special P.P. for the State and Ld. advocate for the accused. 8] Following points arise for my determination with my findings thereon for reasons to follow: POINTS FINDINGS 01. Does the prosecution prove that before one …. In the negative. and half months on 27/03/2015 at VPMs College, CIDCO road, Thane [W], accused put victim girl in fear of exposing her in order to commit extortion? 02 Does prosecution prove that during the said …. In the negative. 4 Special Case No.139/2015 (Judgment) period accused threatened complainant to injure her reputation with intent to cause alarm? 03 Does prosecution prove that during the said …. In the negative. period accused committed sexual assault on a minor girl? 04 Does prosecution prove that during the said …. Accused is acquitted as per final order. REASONS 9] AS TO POINT NOS.1 TO 4 : I would like to discuss all the points together. Prosecution examined victim girl (P.W.1), her father Bhagwan (P.W.2) and I.O.­Kavita Gaikwad (P.W.3). The victim girl deposed that the victim girl born on 04/08/1997. The accused was close friend of complainant. They had been to Titwala temple. Some of the boys from their area informed to her father. Bhagwat Tupe (P.W.2) deposed that when he enquired victim about photograph, victim told him that in the college accused and herself were behaving like friend in their friend circle. Bhagwat Tupe (P.W.2) met him and pacified him. Thereafter accused loaded photographs on the website. Bhagwat Tupe (P.W.2) again met him. While victim girl was avoiding the accused, the accused threatened her by throwing acid on her person. The accused demanded Rs. 50,000/­ being spent on her. Joint photographs of herself and accused were in mobile handset of accused. The victim girl deposed that 5 Special Case No.139/2015 (Judgment) accused threatened her to hand over those photographs to her. Accused also threatened her to throw out of the train. Dipika, her friend, also informed her that she should pay Rs. 50,000/­ to accused otherwise he will push her from the train. 10] Kavita Gaikwad (P.W.3) had taken up investigation. She had recorded statement of victim girl under S. 156(3) Cr.P.C. She arrested accused under seizure panchanama – Exh. 16. The accused gave user I/d and password of the facebook account of victim girl which was recorded in the presence of panchas under panchanama – Exh. 17. On 08/04/2015, uncle of accused produced CPU of the P.C. which was in the use of accused. It was seized under panchanama – Exh. 18. Kavita Gaikwad (P.W.3) deposed that she seized hard disk of CPU under panchanama – Exh. 19. It was sent to FSL, Kalina, Santacruz vide letter Exh. 20. 11] I have heard Ld. APP and Ld. Advocate for the accused. The victim girl was then 17 years old at the time of incident. She had family relations with the accused. She has also deposed in the cross­examination that she had affair with the accused. They had love affair for 1­1/2 years. The accused uploaded photographs which were taken in Titwala. There were allegations against accused that he had demanded money to takeout photographs. It has come in the evidence that one boy Gajare had informed her family members. It has further come in her evidence that they decided to get married. Let us see evidence of Kavita Gaikwad (P.W.3). There is no copy of photograph on record to see whether it was bad or good. Prosecution has not examined any panch to support that photograph was uploaded. The girl has deposed that a message has passed through her friend Dipika that victim 6 Special Case No.139/2015 (Judgment) should pay Rs. 50,000/­ to accused otherwise he will push her from the train. But said Dipika was not examined by prosecution. Since there is no independent witness coming forth, I find it risky to believe victim girl and her father. In the result, I answer Point Nos. 1 to 4 in negative and pass following order : ORDER 1] The accused Kiran Rangnath Kene is hereby acquitted of offence under S. 385, 506(2) of IPC, S. 11 (iv)(v) r/w S. 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and S. 66 (C) of Information Technology Act, 2000. 2] His bail bond stands cancelled. 3] Muddemal property i.e. Article No.5­ black coloured CPU be returned to Bhagwan Kene, uncle of accused, on proper identification, after appeal period is over. 4] Accused shall furnish P.R. bond of Rs. 15,000/­ in view of proviso 437(A) of Cr.P.C.
