A.P.P.Mr.V.G.Kadu for the State Adv.Mr.Eknath Phad for the accused : JUDGMENT : (Delivered on this 11th day of July, 2017) The accused are prosecuted for offence of sexual assault on minor girl aged 17 years old, scuffling with her and other witnesses and abusing and threatening them. 2] Facts are as under : It is alleged by prosecution that the victim is 17 years old girl. She was residing in Punarvasan Vasahat, Manpada, Thane alongwith her mother. On 03.10.2014 there was immersion procession of Ma Durga. On that day at about 07.00 to 08.00 p.m. the victim, her mother, other women and member of Dugramata Mandal namely Tasvirsingh had been to Kolshet creek in a vehicle of Tasvirsingh for immersion of Ma Durga. After said immersion ceremony the victim and all others returned in the vehicle of Tasvirsingh to the pendol of Durgadevi Mandal. The victim was proceeding towards pendol and was followed by her mother and other women. At that time accused Digambar Gaikwad was sitting on chair outside the pendol. While victim was passing through him, he hold both hands of her. She tried to rescue herself but accused J­Spl. Case POCSO ­ 141­15.doc .....3/­ ..3.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.–141/2015.. Exh.39.. Digambar was not leaving her hands. Meanwhile victim's mother had rushed to said spot and rescued the victim. At that time accused Digambar abused and scuffled with the mother of the victim. The witness Tasvirsingh and Smt.Ambubai Ravale intervened and tried to convince accused Digambar. However, accused abused them. Meanwhile accused Pawan who is brother of accused Digambar had been to the spot. He abused victim's mother, scuffled with her and also extended threats. Accused Digambar used to obstruct the victim while she was attending the college. The victim had complained against him to her mother. On the day of incident also the accused had hold both her hands saying that though he was proposing her she was neglecting him. 3] After the incident the victim and her mother approached Kapurbawadi police station. The victim lodged report against both the accused. Accordingly Cr.No.I­ 352/2014 for offences punishable u/s.354, 323, 504, 506 r.w. 34 of the Indian Penal Code came to be registered against both the accused. After investigation charge sheet came to be filed against both the accused for said offences. 4] Charge is framed against the accused at Exh.06. Accused pleaded not guilty of offence and claimed to be tried. J­Spl. Case POCSO ­ 141­15.doc .....4/­ ..4.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.–141/2015.. Exh.39.. 5] Statement of accused u/s.313 of Code of Criminal Procedure is recorded at Exh.37 and Exh.38. The defence of the accused as emerges from the cross examination of the witnesses and in statement u/s.313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is that, the witness Tasvirsingh, victim's mother and other members of the Mandal had committed theft of electricity for pendol and misappropriated funds. They were playing speakers in the pendol very loudly. The accused had complained against them in Kapurbawadi police station. Thereafter witness Tasvirsingh was angry upon them. The further defence of the accused is that, the other women witnesses were asking mother of the accused to have illicit relations with Tasvirsingh. On her refusal and protest, false case is filed against them. 6] After going through the prosecution story, evidence on record and hearing arguments of both sides, following points arise for my determination. I record my findings thereon for reasons as stated below. POINTS FINDINGS 1] Does prosecution prove that on 03.10.2014 at about 22.15 hours to 22.30 hours in Durgamata Pendol near Punarvasan Vasahat, Happy Valley, Tikujiniwadi Road,Chitalsar, Manpada, Thane accused Digambar J­Spl. Case POCSO ­ 141­15.doc .....5/­ ..5.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.–141/2015.. Exh.39.. in collusion with accused Pawan caught hold the hands of victim, a minor girl aged 17 years old with …Proved only sexual intention and thereby against accused outraged her modesty ? Digambar. 2] Does the prosecution further prove that on the above mentioned date, time and place both the accused in collusion with each other voluntarily caused hurt to victim's mother and other witnesses by scuffling with them? ...Not proved. 3] Does the prosecution further prove that on the above mentioned date, time and place both the accused in collusion with each other abused the victim and other witnesses in filthy language ? ...Not proved. 4] Does the prosecution further prove that on the above mentioned date, time and place both the accused in collusion with each other criminally intimidated the victim and other witnesses by threatening them ? ...Not proved. 5] What order ? ..As per final order. : REASONS : 7] In order to bring home the guilt of the accused the prosecution has examined the complainant i.e. the victim as PW3 at Exh.20. The report lodged by her is at Exh.21. PW1 Lady Police constable Smt.Ashwini Navnath Kale had recorded J­Spl. Case POCSO ­ 141­15.doc .....6/­ ..6.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.–141/2015.. Exh.39.. the complaint lodged by victim. Her deposition is at Exh.11. PW2 Smt.Vijayalaxmi Madhusudan Dambe is the mother of victim and her deposition is at Exh.15. PW4 Tasvirsingh Ansasingh Kaloriya is alleged eye witness. PW5 Suman Jayesh Rathod is also alleged eye witness. Deposition of PW4 and PW5 are at Exh.24 and Exh.30 respectively. PW6 Dashrath Shrimant Gharge is a panch on spot panchanama. His deposition is at Exh.31 and panchanama is at Exh.32. Lastly the investigation officer P.S.I., Bajirao Gangaram Bhusare is examined as PW7 at Exh.34. The birth certificate of victim is at Exh.35. As to the Point Nos.1 to 4 :­ 8] All the points are arising out of one and same incident, hence those are discussed together. The victim in her deposition at Exh.20 narrated almost all facts alleged in the complaint. She specifically deposed that on 03.10.2014 she herself, her mother and other women were returning to the pendol of Durgadevi after attending immersion procession in a four wheeler of one Tasvirsingh. After returning to the spot they all got down from the vehicle and she was walking ahead of her mother and other witnesses. Accused Digambar and others were sitting near the pendol. While she was passing, accused Digambar caught her hands. She tried to free herself from the accused, J­Spl. Case POCSO ­ 141­15.doc .....7/­ ..7.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.–141/2015.. Exh.39.. but accused said that prior thereto he had proposed her on several occasions. She further deposed that her mother was following her and after seeing the incident freed her hands from the accused. Thereupon the accused abused them and scuffled with her mother. Accused Pawan also rushed to the spot of incident and abused them. He also scuffled with her mother and other women. Witness Tasvirsingh Ansasingh Kaloriya intervened in the incident. The victim further deposed that prior to the incident accused Digambar used to follow her while she used to go to college. Because of the behaviour of accused Digambar she felt very shameful and therefore, she lodged complaint. The victim further deposed that her birth date is 22.01.1998. Through her evidence the complaint Exh.21 is duly proved. 9] Through her cross examination certain improvements are brought on record. She had not stated in the complaint that accused Digambar was sitting alongwith others near pendol. It is also not mentioned that accused Pawan had been to the spot and he abused and scuffled with other women. In the complaint her birth date is also not mentioned. 10] PW2 Smt.Vijayalaxmi Dambe, the mother of the victim has also supported the prosecution and deposed that on J­Spl. Case POCSO ­ 141­15.doc .....8/­ ..8.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.–141/2015.. Exh.39.. 03.10.2014 at about 09.45 p.m. after attending immersion procession of goddess Durga at Kolshet creek, she herself, her daughter (victim) and other women returned to the pendol in an Innova car. At about 10.30 p.m. all got down from the vehicle. Victim was proceeding towards pendol to attend Aarti and she (PW2) followed her. The victim was at the distance of 15 feet ahead of her and she could see her. She found that accused Digambar who was sitting in chair near said pendol caught hold both hands of victim. The victim was trying to free herself. Thereupon she approached the accused and rescued the victim. At that time accused Digambar pushed her whereby she fall down. Meanwhile accused Pawan had been to the spot and rushed to assault them. 11] PW4 Tasvirsingh Kaloriya also supported the prosecution and deposed that on the night of 03.10.2014 after attending the function of immersion of Durgadevi goddess at Kolshet, he himself, the victim, victim's mother and other women had returned in his vehicle. The victim and other women were proceeding to pendol to perform Aarti of goddess. After parking the vehicle he was returning to the pendol and found that there was a quarrel. He found that accused Digambar had caught hold the hands of the victim. He tried to convince accused Digambar to leave hands of victim. Meanwhile accused Pawan, the elder brother of J­Spl. Case POCSO ­ 141­15.doc .....9/­ ..9.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.–141/2015.. Exh.39.. accused Digambar, had been there and scuffled with him saying that who he was to intervene in the incident. Thereafter he settled the dispute. Thereafter police recorded the statement. 12] PW5 Suman Rathod, the alleged eye witness, in her deposition at Exh.30 supported the prosecution. She also deposed that on 03.10.2014 after the immersion of Durgamata she had returned to pendol alongwith her sons and others. At that time accused Digambar had hold hands of one girl. The mother of said girl rescued her. Thereupon there was exchange of words. Meanwhile accused Pawan had been there for settling the quarrel. Again there was quarrel between them. After said quarrel the mother of the victim had been to police station alongwith victim and lodged report. Said incident had occurred at about 10.00 to 10.30 p.m. 13] PW1 Lady PC Smt.Ashwini Kale is formal witness who merely recorded the complaint of the victim. Obviously she supported the prosecution and deposed that she had recorded complaint of the victim. 14] PW6 Dashrath Gharge is also a formal witness on spot panchanama. Nothing is recovered from the spot which will be incriminating against the accused. However, through J­Spl. Case POCSO ­ 141­15.doc .....10/­ ..10.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.–141/2015.. Exh.39.. his cross examination it is brought on record that, when the police had been to the spot of incident, quarrel was going on. Thus in fact the spot of the quarrel is confirmed through the cross examination of these witnesses. 15] All these witnesses are cross examined at length by advocate Mr.Eknath Phad representing the accused. Various minor discrepancies and improvements in the deposition of witnesses are brought on record through their cross examinations and cross examination of the investigating officer PW7 P.S.I., Bhusare. Through the cross examination of PW2 Smt.Vijayalaxmi Dambe it is brought on record that in her police statement it is not mentioned that she alongwith victim and other women had gone for immersion ceremony in Innova car. It is also not mentioned in her statement before police that the victim was walking at the distance of 15 feet ahead of her. It is also not mentioned that accused Digambar pushed her and thereby she fell down. She also did not state before police that accused Pawan rushed to assault them. In cross examination of PW4 it is brought on record that PW4 Tasvirsingh had not stated before police that first he got down from the vehicle thereafter other women got down and he went for parking his vehicle. It is also not mentioned in his statement before police that after immersion of goddess Durga he alongwith victim, victim's mother and Suman J­Spl. Case POCSO ­ 141­15.doc .....11/­ ..11.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.–141/2015.. Exh.39.. Rathod returned to the pendol in a vehicle. It is also not mentioned in his statement before police that the victim, her mother, Suman Rathod were going to pendol to attend Aarti of goddess Durgadevi. It is also not mentioned in his statement before police that after parking his vehicle when he was returning to pendol, he found that there was a quarrel by the side of pendol. He asked accused Digambar to leave the hands of victim. In cross examination of PW5 Suman Rathod it is brought on record that she had not stated before police the names of her friends. It is not mentioned in her statement before police that accused Digambar had hold hands of victim and victim's mother had been to rescue her and there was exchange of words and quarrel. It is also not mentioned in her statement before police that for immersion of goddess Durga they had gone to Krushna Nagar. 16] Relying upon the depositions of witnesses and their cross examinations advocate Mr.Phad argued that there are no allegations against accused Pawan about outraging the modesty of the victim. In the evidence of witnesses there are no specific allegations of assault at the hands of accused. The words of threats and abusement are neither mentioned in the complaint nor stated by any witness. The spot of incident as stated by PW2 i.e. the mother of victim and PW4 Tasvirsingh J­Spl. Case POCSO ­ 141­15.doc .....12/­ ..12.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.–141/2015.. Exh.39.. are totally different from each other. All the witnesses have improved the prosecution story in their respective depositions. Under such circumstances the story of prosecution is not reliable. All the witnesses are interested. There is no concrete evidence about the birth date of victim. There is no proper corroboration of evidence. Hence the prosecution has failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt. 17] Both accused are charge sheeted for the offences of abusing the victim and witnesses in filthy language and threatening them. However, on perusal of the entire evidence on record and particularly the deposition of the victim, her mother and two independent witnesses namely Tasvirsingh and Suman Rathod it is clear that no one has stated the words of abusement and threats given by both the accused. Under such circumstances certainly there is no evidence against both the accused in respect of said offences. 18] So far as offence of voluntarily causing hurt is concerned, admittedly there is no medical or oral evidence on record to show what injury was suffered by victim's mother at the hands of the accused. On the point of assault and scuffling there is variance in the evidence of victim, her mother and independent witnesses. The very alleged injured i.e. victim's mother PW2 has deposed that accused Digambar pushed her J­Spl. Case POCSO ­ 141­15.doc .....13/­ ..13.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.–141/2015.. Exh.39.. and thereby she fell down. Thereafter accused Pawan had rushed towards them to assault. Victim PW3 has deposed that accused Digambar abused them and scuffled with her mother. Accused Pawan had been to pendol and abused them as well as scuffled with her mother and other women. PW4 Tasvirsingh has deposed that accused Pawan and Digambar scuffled with him saying that who he was to interfere in the incident. Whereas PW5 Suman Rathod specifically deposed that when the mother of victim' had been to rescue her, there was exchange of words. Meanwhile accused Pawan had been there for settling the quarrel and there was quarrel between them. 19] Thus, on assault and voluntarily causing hurt the evidence of all four witnesses examined by the prosecution is different from each other. As already mentioned there is neither medical nor oral evidence about any hurt sustained by victim's mother in the incident. As such the offence of voluntarily causing hurt is also not proved against both the accused. 20] So far as outraging the modesty of the victim and sexually assaulting her is concerned, there are allegations against accused Digambar alone. In the entire evidence it has not brought on record that accused Pawan and accused J­Spl. Case POCSO ­ 141­15.doc .....14/­ ..14.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.–141/2015.. Exh.39.. Digambar in collusion with each other obstructed the victim and sexually assaulted her. On the contrary on scrutiny of evidence of all witnesses it is clear that after altercation between accused Digambar, victim and other witnesses accused Pawan had been there and intervened. PW5 Suman Rathod has clearly deposed that accused Pawan had been there to settle the quarrel. However, there was quarrel between them. Thus it is clear that there is no evidence of sexual assault upon the victim at the hands of accused Pawan. 21] It is pertinent to note here that the victim, victim's mother, independent witnesses PW4 Tasvirsingh and PW5 Suman Rathod all have categorically deposed that accused Digambar had hold the hands of the victim. The fact that accused Digambar had hold hands of victim is corroborated by all witnesses examined by the prosecution. Though the defence has raised various defences mentioned earlier, the fact that accused Digambar had hold hands of victim has been clearly established by the prosecution. 22] Thus on scrutiny of the entire evidence on record, it is clear that only offence punishable u/s.354 of the Indian Penal Code and section 7 and 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act is proved against accused Digambar. The rest of the offences alleged against accused J­Spl. Case POCSO ­ 141­15.doc .....15/­ ..15.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.–141/2015.. Exh.39.. Digambar are not duly proved. So also the prosecution has not proved any offence against accused Pawan. Hence I answer point Nos.1 to 4 accordingly. 23] In view of above findings it is clear that, offence punishable u/s.354 of the Indian Penal Code and r.w. section 7 and 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act is proved against accused Digambar alone. He is liable to be convicted for the same. Hence at this stage I defer the Judgment for hearing the accused on the quantum of sentence. Thane. (P.P.Jadhav) District Judge­8 and Date : 06.07.2017. Addl. Sessions Judge, Thane. 24] Advocate Mr.Pandhare on behalf of advocate Mr.Phad argued that the accused is very young. There are no criminal antecedents. Hence leniency be shown and minimum punishment be inflicted. On the contrary A.P.P. Mr.Kadu submitted that the offence is very serious. It is against minor girl. Hence without showing any leniency maximum punishment be inflicted. J­Spl. Case POCSO ­ 141­15.doc .....16/­ ..16.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.–141/2015.. Exh.39.. 25] The offence u/s.354 of Indian Penal Code and section 7 r.w. 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act is proved against accused Digambar. POCSO Act being special Act while inflicting punishment the provisions in said Act are to be considered. Though sections under Indian Penal Code and POCSO are applied, there is single act of sexual assault at the hands of accused and therefore, single punishment as prescribed u/s.8 of POCSO Act will serve the purpose. The punishment prescribed u/s.8 is not less than three years, but which may extent to five years and fine also. Considering the nature of the act and entire evidence on record, the minimum punishment prescribed u/s.8 of POSCO Act is proper, reasonable and just. With these observations following order is passed. ORDER 1. Accused Digambar Ramesh Gaikwad is hereby convicted u/s.235(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure for offence punishable u/s.354 of the Indian Penal Code and section 7 r.w. section 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act and is sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for three years and fine of Rs.1,000/­ (Rs.One Thousand only), in default of payment of fine he has to undergo simple imprisonment for one month. Accused Pawan Ramesh Gaikwad is hereby acquitted u/s.235(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure off the offence punishable u/s.354, 323, 504, 506 r.w. 34 of Indian Penal Code and section 7 r.w. 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 4. The accused Digambar shall surrender his bail bond. 5. Accused Pawan Ramesh Gaikwad is in jail and he be released forthwith. 6. Copy of Judgment be given to the accused Digambar Gaikwad free of cost. Victim girl used to go in his shop to take the grocery articles and sometime chocolates. 3] On 02.04.2018 at about 8.20 p.m. victim girl went in the shop of accused to take the shampoo and oil. But, till late time she has not come at the house, therefore, her brother by name Sumit went to see his sister in the shop of accused. After sometime he brought his sister at the house and told to the complainant that accused Dinesh Uncle took the victim girl in his room by stating that he will give her chocolate and he removed knicker of the victim girl and moved his hand over her private part. That time, brother of victim girl went there and gave a slap to the accused and brought his sister at the house. Therefore, peoples gathered there and they also beat to the accused by fist and kick blows. Then they all went at police station. Thereafter, mother of victim girl by name Seemadevi Agrahari filed a complaint against the accused in the police station that he outraged the modesty of her minor daughter. 3 Judg.in Spl.Case 125­2018 CNR NO.MHTH01­004018­2018 4] Police registered the offence vide C.R.No.I­115/2018 under section 354 of IPC and under section 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Then police conducted the investigation, prepared the spot panchanama, collected the bonafide certificate of victim girl for showing her birth date, also get recorded the statement of victim girl under section 164 of Cr.P.C. and after completion of investigation, police have sent­up charge­sheet against the accused before the Court. 5] Accused appeared before the Court, entering into plea. He pleaded not guilty. I have framed the charge against the accused under section 354 of IPC and under section 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual offences Act, 2012 vide Exh.9 on dated 04.12.2018. His defence is of total denial and claimed to be tried. 6] Considering the above facts, following points arise for my determination on which I have recorded my findings for the reasons to follow : Sr.No. Points Findings. 1. Whether prosecution proves that, on In the 02.04.2018 in between 8.20 p.m. to 8.30 negative. p.m. at the Kirana Store situated at Mafatlal Shantinagar Zopadpatti, Kalva, Thane, accused assaulted or used criminal force to minor victim girl aged about 8 years, intending to outrage or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby outrage her modesty, and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 354 of IPC ? 2. Whether prosecution proves that, on the In the aforesaid date, time and place, accused negative. 4 Judg.in Spl.Case 125­2018 CNR NO.MHTH01­004018­2018 committed sexual assault on 8 years old minor daughter of complainant by removing her knicker and moving his hand on her person with sexual intent which involves physical contact without penetration and thereby committed an offence under section 7 punishable under section 8 of the POCSO Act, 2012 ? 3. What order ? Accused is acquitted. :REASONS: As to point nos.1 and 2 : 7] To prove the alleged offence, prosecution has examined in all three witnesses on record. Firstly, prosecution has examined victim girl (PW1) at Exh.13. Then prosecution has examined complainant Seemadevi Umesh Agrahari (PW2) at Exh.14. Thereafter, brother of victim girl by name Sumit Agrahari (PW3) is examined at Exh.16. All three witnesses have not supported to the prosecution case, therefore, Ld. APP has submitted that, as material witnesses are turned hostile, therefore, there will be no use of calling Investigating Officer and other witnesses. Hence, he filed the evidence close pursis on record vide Exh.17. 8] I have perused the record. It appears that age of the victim girl is not denied by the accused. Her mother has produced her bonafide certificate which was issued by Kalva Hindi Vidyamandir which shows her birth date as 21.04.2011. Incidence took place on 02.04.2018. So, on the date of incidence age of 5 Judg.in Spl.Case 125­2018 CNR NO.MHTH01­004018­2018 victim girl is 8 years. As said fact is admitted, so no more discussion is required. 9] I have gone through the evidence of all three witnesses. Firstly, victim girl is a material and important witness, but, unfortunately when she entered into witness box she has stated that she does not know the accused. He has not committed any bad act with her. She has not stated anything to her mother. Thereafter, when accused shown to her, she has not identified him before the Court. he has not supported to the prosecution case. Thereafter, complainant PW2 has also stated that, nothing was happened with her daughter. People took her in the police station and police obtained her signature on the complaint at Exh.15. She does not know about its contents. She turned hostile and not supported. She denied the contents regarding the alleged incidence which are mentioned in portion marked 'A' of her complaint. 10] Moreover, thirdly, brother of victim girl by name Sumit Agrahari has been deposed vide Exh.16. He has also stated that nothing was happened with his sister. He identified the accused but has stated that he has not done any bad act with his sister and he never removed the knicker of his sister and not moved his hand over her body. 11] All three witnesses are the material witnesses of incidence but they have not supported to the prosecution case. They have not deposed any single word against the accused. Naturally, if the 6 Judg.in Spl.Case 125­2018 CNR NO.MHTH01­004018­2018 material witnesses are not supporting to the prosecution case, then there will be no use of calling other witnesses on record. Admittedly, present offence is registered under section 354 of IPC. Therefore, there is no medical evidence on record. Therefore, I come to the conclusion that, prosecution miserably failed to prove the alleged offence against the accused as witnesses have not supported. Therefore, it is not proved that accused outraged the modesty of victim girl and committed the alleged offence under section 354 of IPC and under section 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Hence, accused is entitled for acquittal. Therefore, I answer point nos.1 and 2 in the negative and proceed to pass the following order : Order 1] Accused Shri Dinesh Gaurishankar Gupta is hereby acquitted of the offence punishable under section 354 of IPC and under section 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 vide section 232 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 2] The accused is in jail. He be set at liberty forthwith if not required in any other case. Thane. (Smt. S.A. Sinha) 07/02/2019. Special Judge, Under POCSO Act, Thane.

.. 1 .. bail no.1544/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 1544/2015 This application is filed by applicant Mohd. Rizwan Nazir Shaikh for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. I­56/2014 registered at Turbhe MIDC police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 363 of I.P.C. and section 7 read with section 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant induced the minor daughter of the complainant and kidnapped the girl out of her lawful guardianship. It is further contended and argued that no such incident of kidnapping has happened and the girl herself had come with the accused of her own wish and the applicant is falsely implicated since he belong to different religion. It is further submitted that since charge­sheet is also submitted before Court, there is no need of further custody of the applicant/accused. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that the accused and girl were knowing each other since before the incident and it is further contended that taking disadvantage of such acquaintance and knowing very well that the girl is minor by age, the accused .. 2 .. bail no.1544/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) induced and enticed her and kidnapped her from lawful guardianship of her parents and committed sexual assault on her. It is further submitted that in such circumstance since the accused and girl are knowing each other, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl if released on bail and he may pressurize other the prosecution witnesses also. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 363 of I.P.C. and section 7 and 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, the girl is stated to be 15 years old and it is contended on behalf of applicant that there was love affair between him and the girl and the girl had of her own came with him and he had not kidnapped the girl and it is also contended that since the accused belong to different religion, he is falsely implicated in this crime. In such circumstance whether the allegations against the accused are true or not, would be the question to be decided on merits. Even nothing is stated to be recovered from the applicant/accused. 4] It is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if .. 3 .. bail no.1544/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 5] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 6] Then, it has also to be mentioned that though the investigation in the matter is completed and even charge­sheet is also submitted, it would take time to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 7] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Mohd. Rizwan Nasir Shaikh is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ He shall not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and the prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. .. 4 .. bail no.1544/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) He shall not leave India without permission of this Court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 16.07.2015 (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.

Maximum punishment be awarded and compensation be given to the victim. 29] Having considered the nature of offence, in my view, prescribed punishment would meet the ends of justice. 30] As prosecution proved the offence of rape under Indian Penal Code and under the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012, but as per section 42 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012, accused cannot be sentenced for both offences, but punishment can be awarded which is greater in degree. Hence, I proceed to 12 S.C. No. 154/2016. pass the following order. ORDER 1] Accused Prabhakar Laxman Gangode, is hereby, convicted under sec. 235(2) of the Criminal Procedure Code, of the offence punishable u/s. 376 of I.P.C. and he is sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for seven years and pay fine of Rs.1000/­ (Rupees One Thousand Only) i/d. of payment of fine, he shall further suffer rigorous imprisonment for three months. 2] Accused Prabhakar Laxman Gangode, is hereby, further convicted under sec. 235(2) of the Criminal Procedure Code, of the offence punishable u/s. 3 punishable u/s. 4 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012, however, no separate sentence is awarded against the accused for it. 3] Accused Prabhakar Laxman Gangode, is hereby, further convicted under sec. 235(2) of the Criminal Procedure Code, of the offence punishable u/s. 417 of I.P.C. and he is sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for six months and pay fine of Rs.500/­(Rupees Five­hundred Only) i/d. 13 S.C. No. 154/2016. of payment of fine, he shall further suffer rigorous imprisonment for eight days. 4] Both sentences shall run concurrently. 5] He is in custody from 28.03.2016 till today i.e. 27.02.2018. Hence, he is entitled for set­off for the said period u/s. 428 of Cr.P.C. 6] Right to appeal before higher court is explained to the accused. 7] Copy of this Judgment and order be given to the accused free of cost. 8] Accused Prabhakar Laxman Gangode, is hereby, acquitted u/s. 235(1) of Cr.P.C. of an offence punishable u/s. 506 of I.P.C. 9] Seized property being worthless, be destroyed, after appeal period is over. Thane, (A.S. Bhaisare) Date­ 27.02.2018. Special Judge (POCSO Act), Thane.

POINTS FINDINGS 1] Does the prosecution prove that on 16.06.2014 at about 06.30 p.m. at Room No.204, Gaikwad Chawl, Lokmanyanagar Pada No.4, Thane the accused intentionally sexually assaulted the victim, a minor girl, by putting his hand inside her top, pulled her brassier and inappropriately touched her breast ? …Proved. 2] Does prosecution further prove that during above mentioned date, time and place the accused voluntarily caused hurt to the informant ? …Proved. 3] Does prosecution further prove that during above mentioned date, time and place the accused intentionally insulted the informant and her family members by abusing them with intention to provoke them to commit breach of public peace ? …Proved. 4] What order ? ..As per final order. : REASONS : 8] To bring home the guilt of the accused the prosecution has examined the informant Kiran Ramesh Solanki as PW1 at Exh.17. The complaint lodged by her is at Exh.18. The prosecution has examined complainant's mother Devi Ramesh Solanki as PW2 at Exh.22. Head Mistress of Yogeshwar Vidhya Mandir wherein the victim was studying is examined as PW3. Her deposition is at Exh.28. The extract of J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 141­14 ­ S­354,323, 504, 8,12.doc .....6/­ ..6.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 141/2014.. It is further admitted by accused that he used to visit J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 141­14 ­ S­354,323, 504, 8,12.doc .....7/­ ..7.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 141/2014.. Exh.45.. the house of Shaila Halde. In the background of these admitted facts, we have to scrutinize the evidence on record. 10] The informant Kiran Solanki has narrated almost all facts alleged in the complaint. She has specifically deposed that in the month of May 2014 accused had followed her and had said that as her sister's marriage was performed, he was liking the informant. At that time he threatened to sexually assault her. Out of fear she had not lodged any complaint against the accused. On 16.06.2014 the accused had been to the house of Shaila Halde. Neighbours had rescued her. At that time the accused threatened that he would not spare informant's brother when he would be out of house during night. Thereafter she lodged complaint in Vartaknagar police station. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 141­14 ­ S­354,323, 504, 8,12.doc .....8/­ ..8.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 141/2014.. Exh.45.. Her birth date is 24.04.1998, but it is wrongly mentioned as 2000 on Aadhar card. After registration of complaint, she had produced brassier before the police, which was seized. 11] PW2 Devi Solanki deposed that the accused used to visit the house of Shaila Halde. He used to abuse them while attending the house of Shaila Halde because of their quarrels with Shaila. In the month of June at about 06.30 p.m. accused had gone in front of their house and asked about her husband. The accused started to abuse her. When she had gone out of the house accused pushed her and she fell down. Her daughters Kiran and Meena had been to rescue her. The accused pulled her saree. The accused put his hand inside the top of her daughter Kiran. The accused tried to drag her towards the house of Shaila Halde. At that time her neighbour Gauri Solanki, her son­in­law Amar Rathod and elder daughter Meena had been to rescue the informant. The accused was saying that he was liking her daughter Meena, but she got married. The accused also said to informant in vernacular “Tu Mala Far Awadate, Chal Tula Dakhavto”. The accused had threatened to kill her son Vijay. Thereafter the complaint came to be lodged. 12] The informant PW1 Kiran Solanki is cross examined at length by advocate Mr.Shribad. In her cross examination it J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 141­14 ­ S­354,323, 504, 8,12.doc .....9/­ ..9.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 141/2014.. Exh.45.. is suggested that the informant belongs to Gujarati family, the accused is activist of Maharashtra Navnirman Sena, therefore, false complaint is lodged against him. It is denied by the informant. The informant has admitted in her cross examination that in respect of the earlier incident she had not lodged any complaint and she had not stated the date and time of said incident while lodging complaint. It is further brought on record that after the incident the family members had discussed about the incident and thereafter went to lodge the complaint. 13] In cross examination of PW2 Devi Solanki, conducted by advocate Mr.Kushwah, it is brought on record that she don't remember the date of incident. She has further admitted that their house is surrounded by residential houses and it is crowdy area. At the time of incident 2­3 neighbours had gathered at the spot. It is suggested that she had not seen the accused putting his hand inside the top of the victim and pulling her brassier. However, she has denied said suggestion. 14] From the suggestions and above mentioned admissions in cross examination of victim and her daughter it is tried to establish that the incident had not occurred. However, in cross examination of the victim it is brought on record that when she was going to shop on earlier occasion J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 141­14 ­ S­354,323, 504, 8,12.doc .....10/­ ..10.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 141/2014.. Exh.45.. the accused had followed her and said in vernacular “Tu va Tuzi Bahin Khup Sundar Dista, Tuzya Bahiniche Lagna Zale Ahe, Tyamule Tula Mi Ek Divas Ghatta Pakadnar”. In cross examination of the informant's mother Devi it is brought on record that the accused had quarreled with them and he had beaten Devi Solanki. It is further brought on record that at the time of incident, her daughter i.e. the victim and accused were in front of each other. Considering the cross examinations of the victim and her mother it is clear that their evidence is not at all shattered. On the contrary the incident and assault by the accused is further confirmed from their cross examinations. 15] The prosecution has examined Head Mistress of Yogeshwar Vidhya Mandir, Lokmanyanagar, Thane as PW3. Through her deposition the extract of school admission register is produced and proved at Exh.30. As per said admission register the birth date of victim is 24.04.2000. In cross examination this witness has admitted that she had not personally verified the birth certificate of the victim to confirm the date. The victim has deposed that her birth date is 24.04.1998, but the same is wrongly mentioned as 2000. Even considering the birth date of the victim as 24.04.1998, on the date of incident i.e. on 16.06.2014 she was aged about 16 J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 141­14 ­ S­354,323, 504, 8,12.doc .....11/­ ..11.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 141/2014.. Exh.45.. years and 2 months. Thus she was minor. The birth date of the victim is nowhere disputed in cross examination of the victim as well as in cross examination of PW2 Devi Solanki. Thus from the oral and documentary evidence on record it is clear that the victim was minor at the time of incident. 16] The prosecution has examined the investigating officer A.P.I., Vishal Patole. He has deposed that while attached to Vartaknagar police station he recorded complaint Exh.18 and registered crime against the accused. He obtained photocopies of school identity card and Aadhar card for the age of victim. The victim was 14 years old. The victim had produced her clothes which were seized vide panchanama Exh.34. He visited spot of incident and prepared spot panchanama Exh.33. He arrested the accused vide arrest form Exh.35. 17] DW1 Smt.Shaila Halde in her deposition at Exh.40 supported the accused. She deposed that on 16.06.2014 she had quarrel with the mother and other family members of informant out of tap water. At that time Smt.Gophane, Smt.Tiwari and others were present. The victim Kiran Solanki and accused were not present on the spot. The accused works with her husband. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 141­14 ­ S­354,323, 504, 8,12.doc .....12/­ ..12.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 141/2014.. Exh.45.. DW2 Ganesh Gophane also supported the accused and deposed that on 16.06.2014 at about 06.30 p.m. there was quarrel near the house of Solanki. After hearing commotion he had been to the spot. There was quarrel between Shaila Halde and Devi Solanki. At the time of said quarrel 40­50 people had gathered on the spot. The victim Kiran and accused were not present on the spot of incident. 18] DW1 and DW2 are cross examined by learned A.P.P. Mr.Kadu. DW1 Shaila Halde told the name of her husband as Ijaj Khan, who is engaged in sand business. When she was suggested that there are about ten crimes registered against the accused in Vartaknagar police station, she replied that she don't know about the same. DW2 Ganesh Gophane also replied in cross examination that he don't know that there are ten crimes registered against the accused in Vartaknagar police station. The DW1 Shaila Halde and DW2 Ganesh Gophane have deposed in defence that they know the accused who visits the house of Shaila Halde, however, the fact that they don't know about the crimes registered against the accused is certainly not reliable. 19] Advocate Mr.Kushwah representing accused argued at length and submitted that in quarrels of Shaila Halde with the family of informant the accused used to support Shaila J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 141­14 ­ S­354,323, 504, 8,12.doc .....13/­ ..13.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 141/2014.. Exh.45.. Halde. It is the motive to lodge false complaint. He further argued that at one point the prosecution is saying that the accused used to say that he was liking the informant and at another point it is said that he sexually assaulted her. Both the things cannot be true at the same time. Advocate Mr.Kushwah further argued that though informant has admitted that she had told about the earlier incident to her parents, no action was taken against the accused. The informant has deposed that there was terror of the accused in the locality, but no independent witness is examined. The informant PW1 and her mother PW2 both have stated that accused pulled saree of PW2, but the same is not mentioned in the complaint Exh.18. The prosecution has not examined the doctor. The prosecution has not examined panchas on spot panchanama. The birth date of the victim is disputed. The complaint is not recorded by female. Under such circumstances the prosecution has not proved its case. To support the arguments advocate Mr.Kushwah relied upon following rulings. i] Hanumandas s/o. Pandurang Raut Vs. State of Maharashtra and another reported in 2012 All M.R. (Cri) 1527 ii] Sopanrao s/p.Kisanrao Jadhao Vs.The State of Maharashtra reported in 2014 Al M.r. (Cri) 3942 J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 141­14 ­ S­354,323, 504, 8,12.doc .....14/­ ..14.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 141/2014.. Exh.45.. 20] It is pertinent to note here that the informant Kiran and her mother Devi Solanki have narrated the entire incident in their depositions in the Court. Though there are no independent witnesses the very defence has further confirmed the incident by putting questions and suggestions in cross examination of the victim and her mother. In the cross examination of the informant and her mother, not only the incident but the threats and abuses given by the accused are brought on record in vernacular i.e. in the language used by the accused. As already mentioned the prosecution has produced at Exh.43 list of seven crimes registered against the accused in Vartaknagar police station. Considering said facts it is clear that the accused is having criminal background naturally the neighbours who witnessed the incident were having fear about the consequences of deposing against the accused. As already observed even in the absence of independent witnesses the incident is got confirmed in the cross examination of the victim and her mother. So far as recording of complaint by male police officer, considering the allegations and accusations against the accused I did not find the same to be totally illegal. So far as spot panchanama is concerned, in cross examination of the prosecution witnesses and by examining defence witnesses the spot as well as the incident being admitted, examination of independent panchas is not at all necessary. Certainly nothing incriminating is J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 141­14 ­ S­354,323, 504, 8,12.doc .....15/­ ..15.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 141/2014.. Exh.45.. seized from the spot of incident. The spot panchanama in the present case being empty formality, the examination of independent panchas was not at all necessary. 21] From all above observations and evidence on record the prosecution has proved beyond reasonable doubt that the accused had scuffled with the victim and her mother. The prosecution has categorically proved that the accused put his hand inside the top of victim and pulled her brassier, thereby outraged her modesty. Though the medical officer is not examined the victim has specifically deposed that she had sustained abrasion on her chest, when she tried to restrain the accused from assaulting her. In case of causing voluntarily hurt even slightest criminal force causing some pains to the victim is enough. Considering the nature of allegations and nature of hurt, the non examination of doctor is certainly not fatal in the present case. So far as words of abusement are concerned those are brought on record in chief examination of the victim as well as in cross examination of victim's mother Devi Solanki. In cross examination of victim's mother Devi Solanki it was specifically suggested that, the accused had never said to her “Apaki Ijjat Ki Wat Lagaunga”. It is denied by witness Devi Solanki. This fact is brought on record on behalf of defence itself, so it has to be believed as it is. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 141­14 ­ S­354,323, 504, 8,12.doc .....16/­ ..16.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 141/2014.. Exh.45.. 22] Considering the entire evidence on record the arguments of advocate Mr.Kushwah and ruling cited by him are not squarely applicable in the present case. On the contrary the prosecution has proved the offence u/s.354, 323, 504 of the Indian Penal Code and section 8 of The Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act against the accused. Hence point Nos.1 to 3 are answered in the affirmative. 23] As accused is held guilty for offences punishable u/s.354, 323, 504 of the Indian Penal Code and section 8 of The Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, it is necessary to here him on the quantum of sentence. 24] Heard accused on the point of sentence. He submitted that leniency be shown to him and minimum punishment be inflicted. Advocate Mr.Kushwah submitted that the accused is only earning member of his family. His wife, children and old parents are depending upon him. The accused submitted that he is having old aged mother and had already lost his father. On these grounds advocate Mr.Kushwah submitted that leniency be shown to him. 25] As already mentioned there are as many seven crimes registered against the accused in Vartaknagar police station. It shows the criminal background of the accused. It further confirms allegations of prosecution that the accused is J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 141­14 ­ S­354,323, 504, 8,12.doc .....17/­ ..17.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 141/2014.. Exh.45.. having terror in local area wherein the informant is residing. However, unfortunately the accused has tried to give political colour to the incident during cross examination of the victim and her mother. Considering the conduct of the accused and the nature of assault he deserves to be sentenced little more than lesser punishment and less than the maximum punishment prescribed u/s.8 of The Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. At the same time he deserves to be sentenced for offences u/s.323 and 504 of the Indian Penal Code independently. So far as section 354 of the Indian Penal Code is concerned, section 8 of The Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act being special enactment prescribing harsher punishment it is not necessary to give separate punishment under Indian Penal Code for said offence. With these observations following order is passed. ORDER 1. Accused Sameer Javed Naik @ Kammo is hereby convicted u/s.235(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure for offence punishable u/s.354, 323, 504 of the Indian Penal Code, u/s.8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 2. For the offence punishable u/s.8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act the accused is sentenced to rigorous imprisonment for four years and fine of Rs.10,000/­ (Rs.Ten Thousand only), in J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 141­14 ­ S­354,323, 504, 8,12.doc .....18/­ ..18.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 141/2014.. Exh.45.. default of payment of fine he has to undergo further simple imprisonment for six months. 3. For the offence punishable u/s.323 of the Indian Penal Code the accused is sentenced to rigorous imprisonment for six months and fine of Rs.1,000/­ (Rs.One Thousand only), in default of payment of fine he has to undergo further simple imprisonment for fifteen days. 4. Presented on:­ 30/7/2013 Registered on:­ 30/7/2013 Decided on:­ 20/5/2015 Duration:­ Y.1M.9D.20 IN THE COURT OF SPECIAL SESSIONS JDUGE, THANE AT : THANE (Presided over by Ms. V.V.Virkar) SPECIAL CASE NO. 29/13 EXH. NO. The State of Maharashtra (Through Kasarvadavali P.S) .....Complainant. Vs. 1] Pintu Ranka Shetty, Age 21 years, R/at At the construction site of Sattar Shety, Jogeshwari, Majas gaon, Mumbai. 2] Kallu Abhiram Shetty, Age 28 years, R/at Hiranandani Labour Camp Slum, Patlipada, G.B,Road, Thane(W). ....Accused ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ Appearances :­ Learned Addl. Public Prosecutor Shri Khamkar for the State Learned Advocate Shri Mahendra Gaikwad for accused ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ Spl.C.No.0100029/13 2 SPL.C.29/13 Judgment Exh. JUDGMENT (Delivered in open court on this 20th day of May, 2015) Both the accused stand prosecuted for the offences punishable U/s. 363, 323, 504, 506 r/w. Sec. 34 of I.P.C. for kidnapping minor girl Khushboo from lawful guardianship of her father in furtherance of their common intention and voluntarily causing hurt to the father of the girl and intentionally insulting her father when he questioned about the girl to them and accused No.1 is also prosecuted for the offence U/s. 376 of I.P.C. for committing rape on the minor girl Khushboo on construction site of 22 storeyed building at G.B,Road, Thane on 23/3/2013 from 6.30 a.m. to 1.00 p.m. and accused No.2 is also prosecuted for the offence of abetting the commission of the said offence by accused No.1 i.e. for committing offence U/s. 376 of I.P.C. and Sec. 4 of Protection of Child from sexual Offences Act (hereinafter referred for short as POCSO). 2] In short, facts giving rise to the prosecution of accused are that one Anitadevi Ramesh Ram was staying at Hiranandani Labour camp, G.B.Road, Thane along with her husband Ramesh Ramchand Ram and children including Spl.C.No.0100029/13 3 SPL.C.29/13 Judgment Exh. daughter Khushboo Ramesh Ram, aged about 12 years, and she was studying in 4th standard in Patlipada Municipal Corporation School. It is also case of the prosecution that accused Pintu Shetty, who was also working on the same construction site, was troubling girl Khushboo by giving missed calls and the father of the girl Ramesh complained to the owner of the site one Mr. Yusuf Sheth and on his complaint, Yusuf Sheth had removed said Pintu Shetty from the said site and he was sent to other site at Jogeshwari and accused Pintu got annoyed with the father of the girl and even threatened that he would kidnap the girl. 3] It is also case of the prosecution that on 23/3/2013 girl Khushboo and other children of the complainant had been to the school as usual, but girl Khushboo did not return home at her usual time. Therefore, complainant and her husband searched for the girl but she could not be traced. Father of the girl then made inquiries with accused No.2 Kallu Shetty, who was staying in the same labour camp and was relative of accused Pintu Shetty, but he avoided answering. 4] It is also case of the prosecution that on Spl.C.No.0100029/13 4 SPL.C.29/13 Judgment Exh. 21/3/2013 prior to two days of the girl went missing, accused Pintu Shetty had been to the house of Kallu Shetty and had stayed there for two days and the father of the girl realized that the accused must have kidnapped her. It is also further prosecution case that on the next day i.e. on 24/3/2013 girl Khushboo had phoned from mobile No. 992073299 which was the number of accused Pintu, and informed that accused Pintu had taken her away from Patlipada and took her to some unknown place and therefore, she was not able to return back. When again father of the girl had been to the house of Kallu Shetty to make inquiry of Pintu, he had assaulted father of the girl and voluntarily caused him hurt. Mother of the girl therefore, went to police station and lodged complaint on 24/3/2013. 5] On the basis of her complaint, crime was registered vide C.R.No. I­107/13 for offence U/s. 363 and 114 of I.P.C. and work of investigation was entrusted to A.P.I. Vasave. During investigation, statements of witnesses including father of the girl were recorded. The tower location of the mobile phone of Pintu Shetty was traced on the basis of CDR and the girl was traced and was brought to police station. Both the accused were also traced and Spl.C.No.0100029/13 5 SPL.C.29/13 Judgment Exh. arrested. Statements of further witnesses were recorded. Clothes on the person of the girl were seized. Accused as well as the girl were referred for medical examination. Supplementary statement of the parents of the girl and other witnesses were recorded. Father of the girl, who had also sustained injuries, was also referred for medical examination. Seized muddemal and samples obtained were sent to C.A. for chemical analysis. Further statements of witnesses were recorded during investigation. 6] It is further case that since from the statement of the girl, offence U/s. 323, 504, 506 of I.P.C. revealed, the said sections were added and necessary report was submitted to the Magistrate. Since the girl was reported to be minor below 18 years of age, school record of the girl in regard to her date of birth was procured. Then after completion of investigation, accused were charge­sheeted for the offence U/s. 363, 365, 323, 504, 506 r/w. 34, Sec. 376 of I.P.C. r/w. Sec. 114 of I.P.C. and Sec. 4 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 7] Offences under the provisions of POCSO Act are exclusively triable by the Special Court and this being trial of Spl.C.No.0100029/13 6 SPL.C.29/13 Judgment Exh. the case under POSCO Act, charge­sheet was submitted to this court. 8] Accused appeared before the court. A charge as per Exh.13 was framed against the accused U/s. 363, 365, 323, 504, 506 r/w. 34, Sec. 376 of I.P.C. r/w. Sec. 114 of I.P.C. and Sec. 4 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. The contents of the charge were readover and explained to the accused in vernacular. They pleaded not guilty. Their defence was of total denial and was that father of the girl intended that accused Pintu Shetty shall work on the same site and he was working on another construction site and refused offer to work on the same construction site, and therefore, he was having grudge against him and implicated them falsely. Their claimed to be tried. 9] To establish the guilt of accused, prosecution examined P.W.1, medical officer Dr. Sachin Rajput who examined the girl, and P.W.2 A.P.I.Jaymala Vasave, who investigated the crime. Here only it has to be mentioned that inspite of repeated summonses issued to the witnesses including the victim girl and her parents, the said witnesses Spl.C.No.0100029/13 7 SPL.C.29/13 Judgment Exh. were not traceable and therefore, the prosecution closed oral evidence. The documentary evidence produced, proved and relied upon by prosecutions are consisted of complaint Exh.33, seizure panchanama of the clothes of victim Exh.34, spot panchanama Exh. 27, seizure panchanama Exh.28 medical certificate Exh.38, M.L.C. Exh.39, letter sent to C.A. Exh.40, date of birth certificate of victim Exh.41. 10] On the basis of the facts of the case, following points arise for my determination and I record my findings thereon for the reasons given below. POINTS FINDINGS [i] Does prosecution prove that on 23/3/13 between 6.30 to 13.00, at the house of complainant at Hiranandani Labour Camp Slum, Patlipada, G.B.Road, Thane (w), accused persons, in furtherance of their common intention, kidnapped the minor girl named Khushbu Ramesh Ram, aged 12 years, who is daughter of the complainant, from the lawful guardianship of the complainant with intent to cause her to be secretly and wrongfully confined ? No. [ii] Does the prosecution prove that on Spl.C.No.0100029/13 8 SPL.C.29/13 Judgment Exh. 24/3/2013 at the above said place in furtherance of their common intention, voluntarily caused hurt to father of the above named minor girl when he asked the accused about the said minor girl ? No. [iii] Does the prosecution prove that on 24/3/2013 at the above said place in furtherance of their common intention, intentionally insulted the father of the said minor girl and thereby gave provocation to him intending or knowing it to be likely that such provocation will cause him to break public peace or to commit any other offence ? No. [iv] Does the prosecution prove that on 24/3/2013 at the above said place in furtherance of their common intention, threatened and abused father of said minor girl when he asked accused about her and you have thereby committed offence of criminal intimidation ? No. [v] Does the prosecution prove that accused No. 1 during above said period, at the construction site of 22 storied building, in one room made of tin sheets, committed rape by penetrative intercourse on the above named minor girl from time to time ? No. Spl.C.No.0100029/13 9 SPL.C.29/13 Judgment Exh. [vi] Does the prosecution prove that both the accused, during the above said period and at the above said places, abetted each other in committing above mentioned offences and both were present at the time of committing offences, which were committed in pursuance of their abetment, and thereby both accused must be deemed to have committed the offence punishable U/s. 114 r/w. Sec. 363, 365, 376, 323, 504, 506 of I.P.C. ? No. [vii] What offence, if any, is proved No offence against the accused ? is proved. [viii] What order ? The accused are acquitted. R E A S ON S Points No. 1 to 7 :­ 11] As is clear, as per the prosecution case, the accused and the father of the victim girl were working on the same construction site and since the accused was troubling the victim girl by giving her missed calls oftenly, her father made complaint to their employer and therefore, accused was removed from the job and being annoyed with that, the accused had kidnapped the girl. It is also the case of the prosecution that the girl at the relevant time was minor, aged Spl.C.No.0100029/13 10 SPL.C.29/13 Judgment Exh. about 12 years, and accused after kidnapping her, took her to the place which was unknown to the girl and accused No.1 had forceful sexual intercourse with the girl and the girl and accused were caught etc. and accused No. 2 abetted such crime by accused No.1. 12] Then from the perusal of the evidence adduced by the prosecution, it appears that so far as the fact that the girl was aged about 14 to 15 years and she was subjected to sexual intercourse, testimony of P.W.1 Dr. Sachin Rajput appear to be material wherein he stated that on 28/3/2013 when he was on duty as gynecologist at Civil Hospital, Thane, one girl Khushboo was brought by police and the girl herself had given history of sexual assault by a known person many times and last sexual assault was on 27/3/2013 and on examination, he noticed that the girl was not having any external injury on her private part and her hymen was found torn and the tear was old. He also specified that on the basis of X­ray and radiologist's report, the girl was found to be 14 to 15 years of age. As such, as per his opinion, there was no recent signs of forcible sexual intercourse and accordingly he issued certificate Exh.23. No doubt entire version has gone unchallenged. Therefore, the fact that the girl Khushboo was Spl.C.No.0100029/13 11 SPL.C.29/13 Judgment Exh. referred for medical examination and was found to have undergone sexual intercourse and that she was aged about 14 to 15 years, has to be held as established. 13] But then so far as the aspect that the person who had sexual intercourse with the girl and the circumstances in which the girl had been subjected to sexual intercourse etc. is concern, as rightly submitted on behalf of accused, absolutely no evidence is brought on record by the prosecution. As is clear, neither the girl nor her parents or any other witness appear to have been examined by the prosecution to substantiate the allegations that it was the accused who had taken away the girl, and the accused No.1 had subjected her to sexual intercourse. 14] No doubt from the report on the summons issued to the said witnesses, including the victim girl, it appears that the said witnesses were not available on the address given, and therefore, their presence could not be secured and they were not examined by the prosecution. Even it is also to be mentioned that even as per the prosecution case itself the complainant and her husband and victim girl were staying on the construction site of Hiranandani Labour Camp and that Spl.C.No.0100029/13 12 SPL.C.29/13 Judgment Exh. does not appear to be their permanent address and the report on the summons issued frequently to the witnesses revealed that the witnesses had left the address most probably for the reason that it was their temporary address and in such circumstances, since their presence could not be secured inspite of due diligence and efforts of prosecution, the prosecution can not be blamed for not examining the prosecution witnesses. 15] But the aspect cannot be overlooked that the substantive evidence of victim girl, who can be the only material witness in regard to the actual role played by each of the accused, and the very act of forcible sexual intercourse alleged to have been committed by accused with her, is not available. Even the evidence of parents of the girl and the neighbouring persons, who had stated to have seen the accused giving threats that he would kidnap the girl etc., is also not available. 16] No doubt from the testimony of P.W.2, it is clear that he stated that he had recorded the complaint of complainant, mother of the girl, as per her narration and the complaint is marked at Exh.33. But then on the basis of his Spl.C.No.0100029/13 13 SPL.C.29/13 Judgment Exh. testimony, the only fact that can be said to have been established is that the complaint Exh.33 was recorded by him as per narration of the mother of the girl. But so far as the correctness and truthfulness of the allegations made in the complaint, it was necessary to have the presence of complainant and then to substantiate the allegations made in the complaint, the direct evidence of the victim girl was very much necessary. As such for want of such evidence, merely on the basis of medical evidence brought on record by the prosecution, the allegations against the accused cannot be said to have been established. 17] As is clear, the defence putforth by the accused in their statement recorded U/s. 313 of Cr.P.C. is that they are falsely implicated in the crime on account of rivalry between the father of the girl and the accused No.1 Pintu Shetty because he intended that the accused shall work on the same construction site, but he refused and was working in different construction site, and in the light of that when complainant and victim girl did not come forward to state about the allegations against the accused, the presumption U/s. 29 of the Act cannot be said to be attracted in the facts and circumstances of the present case and the probability and Spl.C.No.0100029/13 14 SPL.C.29/13 Judgment Exh. possibility of the defence putforth by the accused being truthful, is also there. 18] In any case, in absence of any evidence in regard to the allegations made against the accused, it cannot be said that the prosecution has established that the accused had kidnapped the girl or had assaulted the father of the girl, or accused No.1 had committed rape on the girl or that accused No. 2 had abetted the commission of alleged act of accused No.1 and none of the offences charged against the accused can be said to be proved and accused are entitled to be acquitted. Points No. 1 to 7 are therefore, answered in negative. 19] Since the accused are acquitted, it is required that they be directed to furnish P.R.Bond of Rs. 15,000/­ each (Rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount under Section 437A of Cr.P.C.to appear before the higher court as and when such court issues notice in respect of any appeal or petition, it any, filed against the Judgment. In the result, I pass the following order. Spl.C.No.0100029/13 15 SPL.C.29/13 Judgment Exh. ORDER [i] Accused persons namely Pintu Ranka Shetty and Kallu Abhiram Shetty are acquitted of the charge for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 365, 323, 504, 506 r/w. 34, Sec. 376 of I.P.C. r/w. Sec. 114 of I.P.C. and Sec. 4 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. [ii] The accused shall be released from jail forthwith if they are not required in any other crime. [iii] The accused shall furnish P.R.bond of Rs.15,000/­each (rupees fifteen thousand only) with one surety each in the like amount under Section 437­A of Cr.P.C. to appear before the higher court as and when such court issues notice in respect of any appeal or petition, if any, filed against the Judgment and that such bail bond shall be in force for six months. [iv] Muddemal articles being worthless, be destroyed after expiry of appeal period. [v] The proceeding is closed. Thane. [ Ms.V.V.Virkar ] Dt:­20/5/2015. Additional Sessions Judge­1 Thane.
