.. 1 .. bail no.1556/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 1556/2015 This application is filed by applicant Mohammad Sayed A. Jalil Shaikh for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. I­347/2015 registered at Mumbra police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 363, 366A of I.P.C. and section 3, 4, 16 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as P.O.C.S.O. Act). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant compelled the victim girls including minor girl to do prostitution business and earned money from the customer for said purpose. It is contended and argued on behalf of the applicant that he is falsely implicated in this crime and that he is not F.I.R. named accused and no specific role is attributed to him. It is further contended and argued that the victim is major girl and she is addicted to drug consumption. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will attend the Court regularly for the purpose of trial and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that the applicant/accused used to induce and compel the victim girls to indulge in prostitution business and thereby the applicant earned livelihood from said business. It is further submitted that the accused was knowing the complainant is minor girl and even then he forced by the accused to do prostitution. It is further submitted that in such .. 2 .. bail no.1556/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girls and prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if released on bail, the applicant/accused may abscond and will not be available for trial and may again indulge in such activity. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant 363, 366A of I.P.C. and section 3, 4, 16 of P.O.C.S.O. Act are of serious nature, as rightly pointed out on behalf of applicant/accused, he is not seen to be F.I.R. named accused and his name stated to have revealed during investigation. It is also to be further mentioned that the girl alleged to be the victim is major and it has been contended on behalf of applicant/accused that she is habitual drug addicted. It is also alleged that she is doing prostitution business of her own wish and that no specific role is attributed to the applicant in the F.I.R. and further that he is falsely implicated in the matter because his wife was caught at the time of raid and he went to police station alongwith his wife he was arrested. In such circumstance the aspect as to whether the allegations against the accused are genuine or the case put forth by the accused that he is falsely implicated only because the other accused is his wife, will have to be decided on merits after trial. 4] Then, it is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released .. 3 .. bail no.1556/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) on bail. In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 5] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 6] Then, it has also to be mentioned that looking the allegations against the accused the investigation in the matter may have almost completed but the charge sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 7] One more aspect is that it is contended by the applicant that his wife is in jail in same crime and since both parents are in jail their children are suffering and their 7 years old daughter Gausiya is to be operated and medical reports of the girl on record show that she is undergoing some brain problem and is having convulsions at regular intervals and it is contended that the applicant intend to get their daughter operated and for betterment of his daughter his presence is needed. That appear to be worth consideration .. 4 .. bail no.1556/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) particularly in the light of the fact that his wife i.e. mother of the girl, is also in the jail. The submission on behalf of prosecution that the test identification parade is to be conducted and therefore bail cannot be allowed is concerned, it is to be mentioned that the applicant is arrested in April, 2015 and since then no efforts shown to have been taken by the prosecution to conduct test identification parade. The investigation in the matter must have been by now completed. 8] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Mohd. Sayeed A. Jalil Shaikh is released on P.R. bond of Rs.20,000/­ [rupees twenty thousand only] with one or two sureties in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ He shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and the prosecution witnesses in any manner and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this Court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 20.07.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Additional Sessions Judge­1, Thane.

Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­004059­2014 Special (POCSO) Case No.142/14 Received on : 11.07.2014 Registered on : 11.07.2014 Decided on : 30.11.2018 Duration : 4Ys.4Ms.19Ds. IN THE COURT OF D.J.­1 & ADDL. SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE (Presided over by Hemant M. Patwardhan) Special (POCSO Case No. 142/14 Exh.No. 1. State of Maharashtra. ( Bhayandar Police station) ..Complainant V/s. 1] Gulabi Dalsingar Yadav Age – 58 years, R/at. R.No.5, Chawl No.8, Zhangriyanagar, Motinagar Road, Bhayander (west) 2] Dinesh @ Chiku Dalsingar Yadav Age – 58 years, R/at. R.No.5, Chawl No.8, Zhangriyanagar, Gandhinagar, Motinagar Road, Bhayander (west) 3] Nilesh @ Pintu Dalsingar Yadav Age – 31 years, R/at. R.No.5, Chawl No.8, Zhangriyanagar, Motinagar Road, Bhayander (west) ..Accused Appearance:­ APP Mrs. Varsha Chandane for the State. Advocate Mr. V.D. Patil for the accused. 1 to 17 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­004059­2014 Special (POCSO) Case No.142/14 JUDGMENT (Delivered on this 30th day of November 2018 ) Accused were facing trial under sections 323, 504, 509, 506 of IPC read with section 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 on following facts:­ 1] That on 26/10/2013 at about 19.45 hours at R.No.6, Chawl No.8, Near Mahavir Nagar, ‘A’ Building, Motinagar, Near Jay Ambe Mata Mandir, Bhayander (West), within the jurisdiction of Bhayander Police Station, Dist. Thane, accused in furtherance of their common intention, voluntarily caused hurt to the complainant and her mother and at the same time, place and date in furtherance of their common intentions gave provocations to said witnesses with intention that they should break public peace and also committed criminal intimidation by threatening them. According to prosecution accused in furtherance of their common intentions while committing said offence has uttered some words intending that same shall be heard by the complainant and her mother with intention to insult modesty of the complainant and her mother. According to prosecution as at the relevant time victim was minor within the meaning of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, uttering the words “intending to insult the modesty” also was within purview of section 11 of the said Act. 2 to 17 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­004059­2014 Special (POCSO) Case No.142/14 Thus, on the complaint lodged by victim an offence punishable under aforesaid sections came to be registered against accused. On completion of investigation they were charge­sheeted. 2] Charge came to be framed at Exh.9 against accused and contents of said charge were read over and explained to accused in vernacular. Accused pleaded not guilty and claim to be tried. Their defence was of total denial and that they have been falsely implicated in matter merely because they are relatives of Pappu Yadav. 3] It would not be out of place to mention that initially prosecution was against four accused persons including that of accused Pappu Yadav. However, later on he was able to establish that he himself was minor at the relevant time of the incident therefore, separate charge­sheet was filed against him before Juvenile Justice Board. Thus, remaining three accused were only charged. 4] After accused have claim to be tried prosecution in order to bring their guilt at home has then proceeded to examine the victim, her mother, their neighbour Pushpavndan Jadhav, Kshitesh Joshi, person whose SIM card is being used by the victim, I.O. Dipti Karpe, Darshana Shivsharan etc. as witness no.1 to 6 respectively. On completion of their 3 to 17 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­004059­2014 Special (POCSO) Case No.142/14 depositions statements of accused were recorded as per their say. Accused in the statements as well, have reiterated their defence as above. 5] Arguments of rival advocates were heard. As per learned APP, victim and her mother were both eye witnesses of the incident and injured themselves therefore, their depositions in itself is sufficient to establish guilt of the accused. According to submissions neighbour Mr. Jadhav has also substantiated the allegations and thus his corroborative evidence is sufficient to prove occurrence of the incident as alleged by the prosecution. According to him panch examined also supports prosecution and thus said facts also substantiated allegations of prosecution. Hence, as per submissions of learned P.P. said evidence is sufficient not only to prove allegations under IPC but also words with intention to insult modesty of the victim and her mother were uttered with sexual intent and intention which should be heard by the victim and her mother, same are sufficient to prove the prosecution under section 12 of POCSO. Thus, prosecution has submitted to convict the accused under all sections with which accused were charged. 6] Per contra, learned defence advocate has pointed out that so­called eye witnesses did not support each other's version and their depositions contains so many contradictions 4 to 17 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­004059­2014 Special (POCSO) Case No.142/14 and omissions. Thus, according to his submissions entire allegation itself can be discarded. He has then pointed out that on 26.10.2013 only N.C. was lodged without there being any reference of even any injuries being sustained by the victim or her mother and about any wording being uttered intending to insult their modesty which clearly goes to show that no such incident occurred as claim by the victim and her mother. He has then pointed out that whatever allegations are made by the prosecution about exhibiting certain words with intent to insult modesty or with sexual intends were uttered by juvenile offender. Thus, according to submissions these accused cannot be held guilty of any offence which they have not committed. 7] He has then made submissions that there are lot of improvements both in the deposition of victim and her mother which categorically goes to show that with only intention of implicating accused said act has been committed. He has then pointed out that though incident alleged to have been started from exhibition of the words with sexual intends on mobile, the fact that only mobile was produced before police machinery without producing a SIM for almost a month and fact that said mobile was never placed in proper custody for a month are itself goes to show that accused are falsely implicated in this false case only because they are relatives of juvenile offender. According to submissions even if allegations of uttering certain 5 to 17 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­004059­2014 Special (POCSO) Case No.142/14 words are considered to be genuine then also as the same were by juvenile offender accused would not have been implicated in the matter. According to submissions there is no reason or motive for present accused to involve in the dispute between juvenile offender and the victim. Thus, as per the submissions their false implication is apparent on record. He has therefore requested to acquit accused from all charges. 8] After having heard rival advocates, following points arose for my consideration and I record my findings against each of them for the reasons noted below :­ Sr.N Points Findings 1] Does the prosecution prove that accused on 26/10/2013 at about ..Negative. 19.45 hours at R.No.6, Chawl No.8, Near Mahavir Nagar, ‘A’ Building, Motinagar, Near Jay Ambe Mata Mandir, Bhayander (West), within the jurisdiction of Bhayander Police Station, Dist. Thane, in furtherance of their common intention, intending to insult the modesty of complainant­victim and prosecution witness Shila Puriya by made some sound intending that the same shall be heard by them and that thereby committed an offence punishable under Section 509 r/w. 34 of Indian Penal Code? 2] Does the prosecution prove that accused on aforesaid date, time ..Negative. and place, in furtherance of their common intention, voluntarily caused hurt to complainant­victim and prosecution witness Shila Puriya and thereby committed an offence punishable under Section 323 r/w. 34 of Indian Penal Code? 3] Does the prosecution prove that accused on aforesaid date, time ..Negative. and place, in furtherance of their common intention, intentionally insulted complainant­victim and prosecution witness Shila Puriya by abusing them in filthy language and thereby gave provocation to them to break public peace and thereby committed an offence punishable under Section 504 r/w. 34 of Indian Penal Code? 6 to 17 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­004059­2014 Special (POCSO) Case No.142/14 4] Does the prosecution prove that accused on aforesaid date, time ..Negative. and place, in furtherance of their common intention, committed criminal intimidation by threatening to complainant ­victim and prosecution witness Shila Puriya and thereby committed an offence punishable under Section 506 r/w. 34 of Indian Penal Code? 5] Does the prosecution prove that accused on aforesaid date, time ..Negative. and place, committed sexual assault on victim, a minor girl of age 16 years and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act? 6] What order? Accused are acquitted as per final order. REASONS As to point no.1 to 6 :­ 9] All these points are interlinked with each other therefore, are discussed at once. Prosecution has alleged that initially juvenile has forwarded a message on Whatsapp account of the victim intending to insult the modesty of the complainant and with sexual intent and then had apologized about his said mistake on the count that he has committed it under the influence of liquor and victim also did not file any complaint about it. However, according to victim again on 26.10.2013 while she herself along with her mother were returning from market found juvenile standing on road along with his friends and when her mother has been to him to know as to why he has forwarded such messages he has again uttered 7 to 17 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­004059­2014 Special (POCSO) Case No.142/14 the words ^;s nksuks jkaM gS] /kank djds vk;s gS* As per allegation then again immediately accused no.1 before this court Smt. Gulabi Yadav has also come on that spot and abused them by using the word “fN.kky”. 10] Second incident was then started while the victim and her mother were about to enter their house and while they were discussing to lodge a complaint at police station accused no.1 has pulled her mother and forced her to fell down and when she tried to rescue her other accused including the juvenile accused has also pulled her down and assaulted her by means of hand blows. According to her, her mother had sustained bleeding injury on her nose and clothes of her mother were also torn. Therefore, they both went to police station where police did not record their complaint but only N.C. was recorded. Then she has made complaint to Superintendent of police, Thane and on instance of order of said Superintendent of police on 29.10.2013 her complaint was registered. 11] In order to substantiate said allegations aforesaid witnesses were examined. Admittedly, mother of victim and alleged eye witness Mr. Jadhav has substantiated allegations as per the submissions of learned P.P. and on the basis of those depositions only learned P.P. has requested the court to convict the accused. However, court has to consider not only the 8 to 17 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­004059­2014 Special (POCSO) Case No.142/14 allegations of prosecution but also defence of the accused person while deciding matter on its own merit. As per settled propositions of law if the defence succeeds in either creating a doubt in respect of prosecution's case or by preponderance of probabilities established that their defence is more probable than that of the allegations then court has to accept it above prosecution. Therefore, though submissions were made that depositions of witnesses are corroborative in nature, unless said is tested on defence conclusion cannot be drawn. Hence, evidence is scrutinized in the background of defence. 12] Accused has categorically put forth that all of them have been falsely implicated in the matter just because they are relatives of juvenile offender. On perusal of the depositions of material witness viz. The victim and her mother it is apparent that present accused before this court has nowhere involved in incident dated 24.08.2013 when initially juvenile offender has forwarded a message in abusive language and which can also be termed as message with sexual intent. Further, no complaint was lodged in respect of incident dated 24.08.2013. The only explanation put forth by the victim was apology of said juvenile offender having committed that particular act. It appears from conduct of the victim of deciding not to lodge complaint about it in itself was sufficient to inferred that particular incident has ended there and there only. Thus, as till that time accused 9 to 17 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­004059­2014 Special (POCSO) Case No.142/14 present before the court were not at all in picture considering the said facts against them is unjustified. 13] Present accused were directly involved in incident dated 26.10.2013. According to allegations on that particular day at about 19.45 hrs. while victim and her mother were returning from market, juvenile offender was standing on the road along with his friends and he himself after being asked as to why he has forwarded messaged dated 24.08.2013 had again abused the victim and her mother by using aforesaid offending language which the said witnesses have taken it with sexual intent. Thus, even if we consider the allegations of the victim and her mother as it is till that particular point there was no involvement of any of the accused facing trial before this court. Thus, it can be considered that present accused were not part of the said intents. 14] Victim has then pointed role initially to accused no.1 before this court by referring that she had approached that particular spot where juvenile offender along with his friend has offended the victim. The victim has then alleged that accused no.1 Gulabi Yadav has abused her by uttering the word “fN.kky”. Therefore, the victim and her mother went towards their house and while they were about to enter house as they were discussing about filing of the complaint against accused 10 to 17 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­004059­2014 Special (POCSO) Case No.142/14 no.1 to 3 before this court with juvenile offender has assaulted them, committed criminal intimidation with intention that they should commit breach of peace and therefore, victim has allegedly lodged this complaint. No doubt the first part of the allegation of the victim about abuses being made by juvenile offender is being corroborated by her mother. However, there is no corroboration of the particular fact of appearance of accused no.1 at a particular spot and allegation of being abused by her. Therefore, said fact itself has to be considered against said victim and her mother. 15] Further, incident though is corroborated by victim and even alleged eye witness Mr. Jadhav then also the defence has made it point to argue that all those facts are improvements and thus, needs to be discarded. On perusal of record it is apparent that there are categorical admission of victim and her mother about their various improvements without there being any explanation to that effect. No doubt the victim has tried to put forth explanation that as the police had asked particular facts she has stated those facts only but said explanation is nowhere appears to be acceptable in view of the fact that victim and her mother were aware as to what incident had actually occurred and when those particular facts were never appeared in the complaint and statement of the victim then as per the natural conduct they were bound to react against police 11 to 17 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­004059­2014 Special (POCSO) Case No.142/14 machinery at that time alone. Further, as per the allegations of the victim concerned police were directed by Superintendent of police to register the crime and thus, if direction are from Sr. officer, the junior officer who has recorded the complaint will certainly not dare to miss the important facts relating to the incident. Therefore, if we consider these facts it is difficult to accept that though victim and her mother had narrated the incident as referred by them before this court while recording their statements but concern police did not record it properly. There were ample opportunity for the victim and her mother to raise grievance about the said fact even till date of their recording deposition before the court. However, in absence of any such fact it is difficult to accept that any such grievance was ever attempted to put forth by them and thus, only presumption which can be drawn safely, is said improvements are being made by them only for implicating accused before this court. 16] Every criminal act is being committed with particular motive. However, though there are 'N' number of cases wherein it has also held that merely because there is absence of motive allegations cannot be discarded. However, even on the background of the said settled propositions of law if we consider entire allegation then there is apparently no motive for present accused to commit particular crime. Even 12 to 17 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­004059­2014 Special (POCSO) Case No.142/14 the allegations against applicant­accused either about sudden appearance of accused no.1 on the spot where juvenile was allegedly offending victim and her mother by using certain abusive words is not explained. Further, though the allegations were made that all accused while the victim and her mother were about to enter the house has assaulted them, committed criminal intimidation and also abused them, Said facts are not corroborated by each other's version. The victim has narrated that due to assaults her mother has sustained bleeding injury and her clothes were torn wherein her mother herself has not supported her said version and on the contrary has claimed that bleeding injury was caused on her lips and blood oozed out of it. Apparently and admittedly victim or her mother were never forwarded to medical examination even after having received such bleeding injuries and there is no reference of the clothes of mother being torn by the accused persons by mother herself. Therefore, on the material facts deposition of said material eye witnesses differs from each other. As referred to above, accused have categorically put forth defence of their false implication only being relatives of juvenile offender. Therefore, if the aforesaid contradictory statements, improvements and failure of the victim to cooperate each other's version are considered then the said defence appears to be more probable. 17] Investigation in the particular matter also appears 13 to 17 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­004059­2014 Special (POCSO) Case No.142/14 to have been conducted with only intention of implicating the accused in the matter as argued by learned defence advocate. In the said submissions making reference of only one fact thus suffice the purpose. While the investigating officer's deposition was recorded, defence has categorically obtained admission of said officer though panchanama of seizure of mobile was carried out on 30.10.2013 said mobile was deposited as per the receipt on 30.11.2018 which has been admitted by the I.O. and when she was asked reason about it she has stated that mobile was without SIM. Thus, as entire incident has allegedly started when mobile message was forwarded on 24.08.2013 and when police machinery has admitted having seized mobile without SIM card in itself is sufficient to say that with intention of implicating the accused every attempt are made by machinery to manipulate the facts. SIM card was the material evidence which was sufficient to implicate present accused including that of juvenile offender and if that was the fact police machinery was bound to seize that SIM card immediately while seizure of mobile was carried out. However, allowing the victim to withheld that SIM card for a month itself is sufficient to create doubt in respect of allegation of prosecution. Further, there is no explanation as to where particular mobile was kept for such a long period of a month. Admittedly, receipt was prepared on 30.11.2013 which itself 14 to 17 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­004059­2014 Special (POCSO) Case No.142/14 means that mobile was in custody of I.O. without there being any accountability to it. Thus, there was every possibility of manipulating it during that period. Having regard to the said fact investigation also appears to have been conducted with motive of implication of accused in the present matter. 18] Though eye witnesses have to some extent corroborated the allegation of assault being committed on victim and her mother then also as there is no proper corroboration to the particular acts and as different allegations are made by victim and her mother about having sustained injuries on particular part of the body it is difficult to accept particularly in absence of medical evidence that any such assault were really being made. At this stage it would not be out of place to mention that on same day immediately victim has attempted to lodge complaint which according to her was registered only as N.C. If we consider particular N.C. which is filed on record there is no reference of either of any bleeding injury being sustained or clothes of the victim being torn in the particular incident. There are only allegation of assaults being made along with abuses without there being any specification of the said abuses. Thus, it is apparent that vague N.C. was being registered immediately after the incident which also nowhere corroborates the version of victim and her mother. Apparently, after pressure being applied on the machinery by 15 to 17 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­004059­2014 Special (POCSO) Case No.142/14 the victim and her mother an offence being registered after about 3 days. Hence, considering all these facts it is difficult to accept that any of the incident is established on record by consistent and reliance evidence. As referred to above most of the abuses are allegedly uttered by juvenile offender against whom separate case is already pending. Thus, it is difficult to say that these accused have abused with sexual intends or to insult the modesty of either the victim or her mother. Though there are allegation of being threatened by the accused persons all those allegations as referred to above are vague in nature and particularly on the background of doubt being created by occurrence of initial incident itself it is difficult to accept that subsequent incident has been taken place as alleged by the victim and her mother. Thus, as the prosecution was not able to establish any allegations by consistent and reliable evidence accused are entitled for acquittal. Accordingly, I record my findings against point no.1 to 5 in negative and proceed to pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused are acquitted from the offence punishable under sections 323, 504, 509, 506 of IPC read with section 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 16 to 17 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­004059­2014 Special (POCSO) Case No.142/14 2] Bail bonds of accused accordingly stand cancelled. 3] Accused are directed to execute P.R. and S.B. of Rs.10,000/­ each as per amended provisions of section 437(A) of Cr.P.C. and bonds so executed shall remain in force for the period of six months from the date of its execution. 4] Proceeding is accordingly closed. Thane (Hemant M.Patwardhan) Date: 30.11.2018 D.J.­1 & Additional Sessions Judge, Thane 17 to 17

1 Special Case ( POCSO ) No. 155/2016 CNR No.MHTH01­004084­2016 Presented on : 20.06.2016 Registered on : 20.06.2016 Decided on : 27.03.2018 Duration Y M D 01 09 07 IN THE COURT OF SPECIAL JUDGE, THANE AT : THANE (Presided over by V.V.Bambarde, Additional Sessions Judge­1& Spl. Judge (POCSO), Thane ) Special Case ( POCSO ) No. 155/2016 CNR No.MHTH01­004084­2016 EXH.No. 37 State of Maharashtra ( Through Rabodi Police Stn. ) ...Complainant Vs. Govind Suresh Chintalgiri Age : 25 years, R/at : Redekar Chawl, R.No.503, Azadnagar No.2, Backside of Jarimari Mandir, Thane (W). ...Accused. ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ Offence Punishable Under Sec. 354(A) the Indian Penal Code and S. 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ 2 Special Case ( POCSO ) No. 155/2016 CNR No.MHTH01­004084­2016 Appearances : Smt. Moholkar, Ld. A.P.P. for the State. Shri. Kasale, Ld.Advocate for the accused. ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ :JUDGMENT: (Delivered on 27th March, 2018) 1] The accused is charged for offence punishable under Sec 354(A) of the I.P. Code and under S. 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act on the accusation of using criminal force to victim girl and sexually assaulted her. 2] The case of prosecution, in brief, is that on 24.03.2016, at 6.00 p.m., victim girl was playing in the courtyard of their house at Mukta Chawl, behind Jarimari temple, Gokulnagar, Thane. The accused went close to her. The accused told her that her brother was calling her. The accused was dragging girl towards public toilet. The girl was frightened and ran away. While running away her frock was torn. 3] Mrs. Suneeta Wankhede rushed to the police station and lodged complaint. On the basis of complaint, offence bearing C.R.No. I­ 88/2016 was registered u/sec. 354(A) of Indian Penal Code and Sec. 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offence Act. Investigation was taken up by API Shri. Gholap. He visited the spot and prepared spot panchanama (Exh.20) in presence of panch Munni Kambale. Investigating Officer recorded statement of the victim girl. Investigating officer also got recorded her statement through Judicial Magistrate, F.C. , I.O. Suresh Gholap arrested accused. After investigation charge­sheet is filed in this court. 3 Special Case ( POCSO ) No. 155/2016 CNR No.MHTH01­004084­2016 4] My Ld. Predecessor has framed charge (Exh.02) against the accused for offence U/s.354(A) of I.P. Code and under S. 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. The contents of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. The defence of accused, as constructed in cross­examination and statement under Sec. 313 Cr.P.C., is of false implication. 5] The prosecution examined in all five witnesses to bring home guilt of accused. Sunita Wankhede (P.W.1) is complainant and mother of victim girl (Exh.8) who lodged FIR at Exh. 9, P.W.2 is a victim girl (Exh.10). P.W.3 Kiran Gautam Sawant is the panch witness (Exh.13) in whose presence clothes i.e. frock ­Article 1 of victim girl was seized under seizure panchanama Exh.14. P.W.4 Smt. Munni Kambale is panch witness ( Exh.19 ) to spot panchanama Exh. 20. P.W.5 Suresh Gholap, P.I. is investigating officer ( Exh.24 ). Prosecution has closed its evidence by filing pursis Exh.27. The prosecution has relied on F.I.R. Exh. 9, seizure panchanama Exh. 14, spot panchanama Exh. 20, birth certificate of accused Exh.15 and birth certificate of victim girl at Exh.16 and statement of victim under Sec. 164 Cr.P.C. Exh.25. 6] I have heard Ld.A.P.P. and Ld. Advocate for the accused. 7] Following points arise for my determination and I have given my findings thereon for reasons to follow : POINTS FINDINGS 01. Does prosecution prove that on 4 Special Case ( POCSO ) No. 155/2016 CNR No.MHTH01­004084­2016 24.03.2016, at 18,00 hrs., at Gokulnagar, …In the Near Public toilet, Azadnagar No.2, Thane, affirmative. accused used criminal force to victim girl intending to outrage her modesty? 02. Does prosecution prove that on same date, …In the time and place the accused have negative. committed sexual assault on the victim girl? 03. What order? Accused is convicted as per final order. REASONS AS TO POINT NOS. 1 & 2 : 8] I would like to discuss both these points together being interlinked with each other. It has come in the evidence of P.W.1 Sunita that her daughter was playing outside their house at around 6.00 p.m. on 24.03.2016. Victim girl (P.W.2) has deposed that their house is at Azadnagar, behind Jarimari temple. The accused has come and told her that her brother was calling her upstairs. The accused dragged her. She tried to escape, but accused pulled her frock and frock was torn. Frock­ Article 1 was torn. Sunita (P.W.1) deposed that the victim girl came to her weeping and she was frightened. On enquriy, victim narrated her about the incident. Thereafter, she went to the house of accused, but he ran away. Sunita (P.W.1) went to the police station and lodged complaint Exh.9. Investigating Officer Suresh Gholap ( P.W.5) has collected birth certificate (Exh.16) of the victim girl. It shows date of birth of victim girl as 13.01.2009. It means that the girl was 7 years old at the time of incident. Suresh Gholap (P.W.5) got recorded statement of 5 Special Case ( POCSO ) No. 155/2016 CNR No.MHTH01­004084­2016 victim girl u/sec. 164 of Cr.P.C. (Exh.25). The frock of girl­ article 1 was seized in presence of Kiran Sawant (P.W.3). Investigating Officer has drawn spot panchanama (Exh. 20) in presence of Munni Kambale (P.W.4). 9] I have heard Ld. A.P.P. and Ld. Advocate for the accused. It is not disputed that the accused and victim girl hails from the same area of Azadnagar No.2, Jarimari temple, Thane. The presence of accused at the time of incident is also not disputed. It is contention of Ld. Advocate for accused that maternal uncle of victim girl is friend of accused. It is suggested to Sunita (P.W.1) that there was fight between accused and her brother. It is admitted by Sunita that it was a day of Dhulivandan (Festival of colours). The people gathered for Dhulivandan. It is argued by Ld. Advocate for accused that there was rivalary between the parties and so, accused is falsely implicated. The story of rivalary does not appear probable. 10] It has come in the evidence of victim girl that accused pulled her and while pulling, her frock was torn. It is not the case of girl that either accused touched her private part. It appears that the accused outraged her modesty by pulling her, but sexual intention of that grave nature is not seen. So, whatever evidence is there is of S. 354 of Indian Penal Code and not u/sec.7 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. So, I hold accused guilty of offence u/sec. 354 of Indian Penal Code and take pause to hear him on the point of sentence. 11] I have heard accused on the point of sentence. Ld. Advocate 6 Special Case ( POCSO ) No. 155/2016 CNR No.MHTH01­004084­2016 for accused Shri. Kasale submitted that accused was under psychiatrist treatment. He has been in jail for last two years. He undertakes to improve himself by taking proper psychiatrist treatment. He shall be given lesser punishment. Ld. APP submitted that the offence is very serious and it is committed with the minor girl. It is submitted that no leniency will be shown otherwise wrong message will be sent in the Society. I have assessed all circumstances. The victim girl is only 9 years old. So, I do not find it just and proper to extend benefit of Probation of Offenders Act to the accused. Considering this, I find it just to answer point No.1 in affirmative and point No.2 in negative. In answer to point No.3 I pass following order : ORDER 1] Accused Govind Suresh Chintalgiri is hereby convicted under Sec. 235(2) of Code of Criminal Procedure of offence u/s. 354(A) of Indian Penal Code. 2] Accused is sentenced to suffer simple imprisonment of 1 year and six months and fine of Rs. 500/­ i.d. to suffer simple imprisonment for fifteen days. 3] Accused Govind Suresh Chintalgiri is hereby acquitted under Sec. 235(1) of Code of Criminal Procedure of offence u/s. 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 7 Special Case ( POCSO ) No. 155/2016 CNR No.MHTH01­004084­2016 4] Accused is in jail since 24.03.2016 till 21.03.2018. He is given set of as per Sec. 428 of Code of Criminal Procedure for the period already undergone in jail. 5] He shall surrender his bail bonds. 6] Muddemal property i.e. frock being worthless be destroyed after appeal period is over. 7] Pronounced and dictated in open court. Order below Exhibit 1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 1567/2015 This application is filed by applicant namely Shayam Narayan Bhagawati Shukla for his release on bail under section 167(2) of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no.131/2015 registered at Vashi police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 354a of I.P.C. and section 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). It was contended and argued that after the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime 21.03.2015 and still charge sheet is not submitted in court. It is further submitted and therefore the applicant/accused is entitled to be released on bail under section 167(2) of Cr.P.C. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co-operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] A report was called for in regard to submission of charge sheet in Court and it is reported by the Office vide report dated 02.07.2015 on Exhibit 4 that till 12.0 noon of 02.07.2015 the charge sheet had not been filed in the present crime. 3] As is clear, the applicant is claiming for his release on bail on the ground that charge is not submitted within period of 90 days since after the arrest of the accused in this crime on 21.03.2015. The application is filed on 30.06.2015. As is further clear the offences charged against the accused under section 354A of I.P.C. is punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to five years and as rightly submitted on behalf of applicant/accused, charge sheet has not been submitted in Court even after expiry of sixty days after arrest of the applicant/accused in the present crime. In above circumstance I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail as per provisions of section 167(2) of Cr.P.C. 4] In all such circumstance I am of the view that since no charge sheet is so far submitted against the present applicant/accused, this is a fit case wherein the applicant/accused can be released on bail under section 167(2) of Cr.P.C. I therefore pass the following order - ORDER The application is allowed as per Section 167(2) of Cr.P.C. Applicant/accused namely Shayam Narayan Bhagawati Shukla is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/- [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions - He shall attend the concerned police station for the purpose of interrogation as and when called till filing of the charge sheet and shall co- operate in investigation. He shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and other prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this Court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 06.07.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.

Case POCSO ­ 28­13.doc .....19/­ ..19.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.–28/2013.. Exh.128.. contradictory to each other. From their evidence it can be gathered that Nisha was one of the prostitute working in said brothel and merely used to collect amount from the customers in the absence of main culprit Reena. Certainly none of the victim has stated that the accused No.1 had procured them for prostitution. On the contrary the main culprit Reena had taken them in said room at Turbhe and was compelling them to engage in prostitution. Thus from the entire evidence on record it can be said that the accused No.1 herself was victim of the business of prostitution and was compelled to do prostitution by main culprit. Except uncorroborated evidence of PW4 Tumpa Mandal there is nothing on record to hold accused No.1 guilty for the offence. 23] It is further to be noted that there is nothing on record to show that the room wherein raid was conducted was either owned or obtained on rent by accused No.2. As already mentioned there is variance in the evidence of PW1, PW2 and PW3 as to who accepted the amount from decoy customer. The very decoy customer wrongly identified accused No.2. Under such circumstances the prosecution has failed to prove beyond reasonable doubt that the accused No.1 who was running brothel and who procured and compelled victims to do prostitution. Hence answering all points in the negative following order is passed. J­Spl. Case POCSO ­ 28­13.doc .....20/­ ..20.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.–28/2013.. Exh.128.. ORDER 1. Accused No.1. Nisha Usman Shaikh and No.2. Sarita Ratnakar Tambe are hereby acquitted u/s.235(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure for offence punishable u/s.370A(1)(2), 372, 373 r.w. 34 of the Indian Penal Code and section 3, 4, 5, 6 and 9 of the Prevention of Immoral Trafficking Act and u/s.12 and 17 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 2. The accused are in jail and they be released forthwith. 3. The muddemal property cash amount be credited to state and the rest of the muddemal property being worthless, be destroyed, after the appeal period is over. 4. Accused are directed to furnish personal bond of Rs.10,000/­ each in terms of sec.437­A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Sd/­... Thane. (P.P.Jadhav) District Judge­8 and Date : 02.08.2017. Addl. ..1.. Bail Appln. No.1484/13 (O) ORDER BELOW EXH.1 IN CRI. BAIL APPLICATION NO. 1484/2013 Applicant Shekhar Shanidas Patil has moved this application under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure apprehending his arrest in connection with the offences under Sections 354, 342, 337, 506 r.w. Sec. 34 and under Section 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 in C.R.No.I 513/2013 registered with Mumbra Police Station. 2] Heard Mr.Munir Ahmed the Learned Advocate appearing for applicant. Heard Mr.Kadri the Learned Public Prosecutor for the State. 3] It is the case of the prosecution that on 6.7.2013 at about 10 p.m. the victim girl Ketaki aged 17 years was going towards her house after fetching water from public tap. At that time the applicant and other two co­accused obstructed the victim girl in front of the shop of Ashok Wani at Nagwadi. At that time applicant told victim girl that he had taken her photographs in his mobile which have been loaded in his computer and he would prepare her nude photographs and upload them on the face book. At that time victim snatched mobile from applicant. The applicant caught right hand of the victim girl and pulled her and thereafter pressed her breast. The victim girl threw the mobile in a water pond. At that time somebody out of three assailants pulled hair and T­shirt of the victim girl, as a result of which she had fallen and sustained abrasions on her right hand and left elbow. Applicant threatened victim girl that she will have to accompany her lest entire world will see her on face book. ..2.. Bail Appln. No.1484/13 (O) Consequently the complainant lodged F.I.R. and the aforesaid crime was registered. 4] Co­accused Amit Tare and Sumit Tare were arrested on 7.7.2013. They were remanded to police custody till 11.7.2013. However, the applicant was not traceable. During remand applicant was shown wanted accused. 5] Mr.Munir Ahmed the Learned Advocate appearing for applicant vehemently urged that the applicant has been falsely implicated only because of strained relationship. He submitted that the victim girl and applicant are friends. Because of some reason the relations were deteriorated and therefore, applicant has been falsely implicated. It is also stated that the victim girl has attained the age of understanding and she is not child within the meaning of Section 2(d) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. There are no criminal antecedents against the applicant. The custodial interrogation of the applicant is not warranted. 6] Mr.Kadri the Learned Public Prosecutor resisted the application on the ground that the applicant had threatened victim girl that he has already taken photographs of victim girl in his computer and he would upload the photographs on face book. The computer is required to be recovered after taking the applicant in custody. The detail interrogation is necessary for the purpose of recovery of computer. Mr.Kadri submitted that the broken mobile of Samsung make has been recovered from the house of the applicant. There are direct allegations in the F.I.R. ..3.. Bail Appln. No.1484/13 (O) Hence, applicant is not entitled to be released on anticipatory bail. 7] Mr.Munir Ahmed the Learned Advocate appearing for applicant referred to and relied on the decision in the case of Khemlo Sakharam Sawant Vs. State of Maharashtra. reported in B.C.R.2002 page 689 wherein His Lordship of Hon'ble Bombay High Court while considering the grant of regular bail for offences under Section 12 of Prevention of Corruption Act was pleased to observe that Sessions Court while rejecting the bail application was more influenced by morality than law and Sessions Court observed that the offence in question was serious in nature. The legislative intent of treating the offence serious is eloquent from the sentence provided for the said offence. The punishment for offence under Section 12 is minimum six months and may extend upto a period of five years and therefore this offence cannot be equated with a serious offence like murder. It is further observed that court should not be swayed away by the perception of morality. 8] In the aforesaid Judgment his Lordship was pleased to rely on the decision of Joginder Kumar v. State of U.P. reported in AIR 1994 S.C. page 1349 wherein Their Lordships of Apex Court was pleased to observe that:­ “the above guidelines are merely the incidents of personal liberty guaranteed under the Constitution of India. No arrest can be made because it is lawful for the Police Officer to do so The existence of the power to arrest is one thing. The justification for the exercise of it is quite another. The Police Officer must be able to justify the arrest apart from his power to do so. Arrest and detention in police lock­up of a person ..4.. Bail Appln. No.1484/13 (O) can cause incalculable harm to the reputation and self­esteem of a person. No arrest can be made in a routine manner on a mere allegation of commission of an offence made against a person. It would be prudent for a Police Officer in the interest of protection of the constitutional rights of a citizen and perhaps in his own interest that no arrest should be made without a reasonable satisfaction reached after some investigation as to the genuineness and bona fides of a complaint and a reasonable belief both as to the persons complicity and even so as to the need to effect arrest. Denying a person of his liberty is a serious matter. The recommendations of the Police Commission merely reflect the constitutional concomitants of the fundamental right to personal liberty and freedom. A person is not liable to arrest merely on the suspicion of complicity in an offence. There must be some reasonable justification in the opinion of the officer effecting the arrest that such arrest is necessary and justified. Except in heinous offences, an arrest must be avoided if a Police Officer issue notice to persons to attend the Station House and not to leave station without permission would do”. 9] In the case of Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre Vs. State of Maharashtra reported in 2011 AIR (SC) page No. 312 Their Lordships of Hon'ble Apex Court were pleased to observe that :­ “The following factors and parameters can be taken into consideration while dealing with the anticipatory bail: i. The nature and gravity of the accusation and the exact role of the accused must be properly comprehended before arrest is made; ii. The antecedents of the applicant including the fact as to whether the accused has previously undergone imprisonment on conviction by a Court in respect of any cognizable offence; ..5.. Bail Appln. No.1484/13 (O) iii. The possibility of the applicant to flee from justice' iv. The possibility of the accused's likelihood to repeat similar or the other offences. v. Where the accusations have been made only with the object of injuring or humiliating the applicant by arresting him or her. vi. Impact of grant of anticipatory bail particularly in cases of large magnitude affecting a very large number of people. vii.The courts must evaluate the entire available material against the accused very carefully. The court must also clearly comprehend the exact role of the accused in the case. The cases in which accused is implicated with the help of sections 34 and 149 of the Indian Penal Code, the court should consider with even greater care and caution because over implication in the cases is a matter of common knowledge and concern; viii.While considering the prayer for grant of anticipatory bail, a balance has to be struck between two factors namely, no prejudice should be caused to the free, fair and full investigation and there should be prevention of harassment, humiliation and unjustified detention of the accused; ix. The court to consider reasonable apprehension of tampering of the witness or apprehension of threat to the complainant; x. Frivolity in prosecution should always be considered and it is only the element of genuineness that shall have to be considered in the matter of grant of bail and in the event of there being some doubt as to the genuineness of the prosecution, in the normal course of events, the accused is entitled to an order of bail. 10] In the case of Siddharam Mhetre cited supra the Hon'ble Apex Court have observed that the alleged arrest of accused should be last option and it should be restricted to those exceptional cases where ..6.. Bail Appln. No.1484/13 (O) arresting the accused is imperative in the facts and circumstances of the case. 11] Considering the legal proposition laid down in the aforesaid ruling by the Hon'ble Apex Court, the crucial question that falls for consideration is as to whether custodial interrogation and arrest of applicant is imperative. It must be borne in mind that day in and day out the offences of sexual assault on children are increasing. Besides this, there are direct allegations against the applicant that he has taken photographs in his mobile and computer and computer of the applicant is required to be recovered. Unless applicant is arrested and interrogated the computer cannot be recovered. If the applicant is not arrested and computer is not seized there would be serious prejudice to prosecution and investigation shall remain incomplete for ever. The possibility that applicant may misuse the photographs of the victim cannot be ruled out. The object for grant of anticipatory bail is to protect innocent persons from false implication. There is nothing to demonstrate that allegations made against the applicant are false. After considering the entire material on record against applicant he is not entitled to be released on anticipatory bail. Hence, I pass the following order:­ ORDER Application for grant of anticipatory bail is hereby rejected. Thane, (P.H.Mali) Dt. 5.8.2013. Special Judge,(PCFSO Act),Thane.

Presented on : 23.06.2017 Registered on : 23.06.2017 Decided on : 13.10.2017 Duration : 00Y.03M.20D IN THE COURT OF SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE, AT : THANE. Presided over by S.C. Khalipe ­Additional Sessions Judge, Thane SPECIAL CASE NO.141/2017 Exh.No. The State of Maharashtra Through Nayanagar Police Station. ….. Prosecution V/s. Aizaz Nabban Khan Age 55 years, Occ: Furniture shop R/at. Chandan Valley A­B wing, Watchman Room, Near Bramhadev Temple, Naya Nagar, Mira Road (E). Originally R/at. Khanna Katakiya, Lakad Mandi, Hari Singh Firm, Shahdat Ganj, Lukhnow, Utter Pradesh. ..... Accused Offence punishable under Sections 354A(i) of Indian Penal Code and section 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act,2012. Appearance: A.P.P. Smt.Tallar for the prosecution. Advocate Shri. S.J. Patankar for accused. :J U D G M E N T: (Delivered on this 13th Day of October, 2017) The case of the prosecution is that:­ 2. The accused had sexually harassed the victim girl aged four year on 15.03.2017 at 9.30 a.m. to 11.00 a.m. Accused was working as watchman since last one year of the incident in Chandan Valley Society Building at Mira Road. The victim's mother was working as maid servant in that building. On the day of incident victim's mother left the victim on sand below the building for playing. After work was over the victim's mother saw that the victim was not there so she searched her. She came to know that the accused had lifted her and again left her near her house. 3. The victim's mother inquired with the victim. The victim told that the watchman uncle took her at stair case of the building, removed her kicker, seated her on his thighs and touched her private part. Therefore, the victim's mother lodged F.I.R in Nayanagar Police Station on 15.03.2017. Accordingly C.R.No.I­72/2017 was registered under section 354A(i) of Indian Penal Code and Section 8 of POCSO Act,2012 4. The accused was arrested on 25.04.2017. He was absconding since the date of incident. Investigation was carried out by A.P.I. Shri. P.S. Salunkhe. He recorded statement of witnesses and victim and sent the chargesheet. 5. Charge was framed at Exh.3 against the accused under section 354A(i) of Indian Penal Code and section 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. The accused pleaded not guilty. 6. The defence of the accused raised in his statement under section 313 of Cr. P.C., that he was working as watchman in Chanda Valley society. There was one coconut tree and coconut was fell in front of the house of the informant so he would asked the informant to give back the coconut, but she refused to return coconut so there was quarrel between them and because of that she lodged false complaint against him. Accused has admitted that victim's mother was residing at Bharti Park near Chandan Valley society. He also admits that he was working as security guard through MTS security Agency in Chandan Valley Building and he was on duty on the day of incident. He admits that he was doing shift duty and watchman were on shift duty of 12 hours duty. He also admits that the victim's mother was working as maid servant in Chandan Valley Building and on 15.03.2017 she had left her daughter on sand for playing. He admits that victim was not found to her mother. He admits that witness Dulali Nikhil Rai knows victim's mother and victim and she had seen the victim was playing on sand. However he has denied that he had lifted the victim and took her below the stair case and sexually harassed her and then after some time he left her near the house of victim. 7. Considering the evidence on record following points arose for my determination. I have given its findings with reasons as under­ Sr.No Points Findings 1. Does prosecution prove that on In 15.03.2017 at about 9.30 a.m. to 11.00 Affirmative a.m., at Chandan Valley Society, Mira Road, Thane the accused committed sexual harassment of minor girl aged four year by removing her knicker and touching her vagina and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 354A(i) of Indian Penal Code? 2. Does prosecution prove that accused In committed sexual assault by touching the Affirmative vagina of the victim girl aged 4 years with sexual intent which involved physical contact without penetration and thereby committed an offence under section 7 punishable under section 8 of the POCSO Act,2012? 3 What order? Accused is convicted REASONS AS TO POINT NOS.1 TO 3:­ 8. To prove the offence prosecution has examined victim aged four years at Exh.6, victim's mother at Exh.7, Dulali Nikhil Rai at Exh.10, security agency owner Imran Naziar Hussain Sayyed at Exh.12, Pravinkumar Sonbarao Salunkhe at Exh.13. 9. The prosecution closed the evidence vide pursis at Exh.16. The statement of accused under section 313 of Cr. P.C. is at Exh.17. 10. From the evidence of Imran Nasir Hussain Sayyed it has come on record that the accused was appointed as security guard in Chandan Valley Building one month prior to the incident. There were three watchmen appointed by the MTS security Agency. On the day of incident accused did not come for work. The Investigating Officer has stated that the watchmen were doing shift duty of 12 hours. There is A wing and B wing in Chandan Valley Society. This evidence shows that at the time of incident only one watchman was working on shift duty. 11. The accused has admitted in his statement under section 313 of Cr. P.C Exh.17 that he was working as watchman in Chandan Valley Society and on the day of incident he was on duty. It is not the case of accused that there were another watchmen also on duty on the day of incident. 12. It has come in the evidence of informant that she was residing in Naya Nagar Zopadpatti near Chandan Valley Society at Mira Road Thane and she was working as maid servant. She has only one daughter i.e. victim who was aged four years at the time of incident. On the day of incident at about 9.00 a.m. she went to Chandan Valley Society for work. She would take her daughter with her for work. On that day she left her daughter below building to play on sand. After work was over in Chandan Valley Society she was going to Green Avenue Building. At that time she saw Gauri was not on sand. So she searched her, but she could not be found. Her neighbouring woman Dulali Nikhil Rai P.W.3 told her that she had seen the watchman while lifting her daughter and watchman had left her daughter near her house. So she asked her daughter where did the watchman uncle had taken her, her daughter told her that the watchman uncle had taken her in the stair case of the terrace and seated her on his thighs and removed her chaddi and made her “naga punga” (it means her chaddi was removed) and moved his hands on the place of her su su (her private part i.e. vagina). So the informant told this fact to her husband and then they went to police station and lodged FIR. She identified the watchman of Chandan Valley Society before the court. Her FIR is at Exh.8. It bears her signature. Her evidence is not at all shaken in her cross examination and no reason is made out why she should be disbelieved. 13. The victim's evidence is recorded at Exh.6. Some questions were asked to her whether she could understand the nature of question and could give rational answer, it was found that the victim was understanding the nature of question and she could give rational answers. She stated that there was watchman uncle in Chandan Valley Building. Her mother was working in Chandan Valley Building. The accused called her as 'baby' and she called that watchman as 'uncle'. On that day she was playing on sand. The watchman uncle told her “mummy udhar hai tu udhar chal” and said “mai tuze tere mummy ke pass chodta hu” and then he took her at the stair case and removed her knicker and he touched her on the place of her susu (vagina). Then he went down to search key and then he left her below the building. She told this fact to her mummy. The victim's evidence is also not shaken and no reason is made out why she should be disbelieved. 14. The witness No.3 Dulali Nikhil Rai (at Exh.10) has stated that she knows the victim and her mother. They were residing in her neighbourhood. On the day of incident she saw in the morning the victim was playing in front of Chandan Valley Society. She saw the watchman of Chandan Valley Society lifted the victim and taken her away. After some time she saw that the watchman left victim near her house. She identified the watchman before the court. 15. In her cross examination she has stated that she has not given description of the clothes of the watchman to the police. No other reason is made out why she should be disbelieved. She also identified the accused who was produced before the court on Video Conferencing. 16. Investigation was done by Pravinkumar Salunkhe API of Nayanagar Police Station. He stated that he arrested accused on 25.04.2017 vide panchanama Exh.14 and he investigated C.R.No.72/2017. He stated that he has not collect any documentary evidence from the society about appointment of watchman in the building and not collected documentary evidence to show that the accused was on duty on that day. He stated that the security agency has given statement that accused was the watchman in that building and he was on duty on that day. 17. I heard Ld. Counsel on behalf of accused and Ld. A.P.P. 18. Ld. APP submitted that there is no reason made out to disbelieve victim, her mother and witness Dulali Nikhil Rai. They have identified the watchman, who is accused and their evidence is corroborated on the material points. 19. In reply Ld. Counsel on behalf of accused Shri.S. J. Patankar submitted that there was no documentary evidence to show that the accused was working as watchman on that day and his description was not stated by the witness to the police. 20. In this respect court is of the view that the accused was appointed one month prior to the incident. The process of registration of the security agency was going on and therefore there is no documentary evidence produced by the security agency before the police. However, security agency owner Imran Nazir Hussain Sayyed has stated on oath that accused was appointed through their Agency as watchman in Chandan Valley Building at Mira Road Thane and on the day of incident he was on duty. This is sufficient compliance to prove that the accused was on duty on that day. This fact is not denied by the accused. On the contrary, in his statement under section 313 of Cr. P.C., he has admitted that on the day of incident he was on duty as watchman in Chandan Valley Building at Mira Road. 21. The accused has also not denied that the victim and her mothers were residing at Naya Nagar Zopadpatti near the Chandan Valley Building. He was knowing the victim and her mother and witness Dulali. At question No.24 in the statement under section 313 of Cr. P.C., he stated that he gave the victim to her mother. Therefore, there is no doubt about identification of the accused. 22. The accused has raised defence in his statement under section 313 of Cr. P.C. that the victim's mother was taking coconut of the tree of Chandan Valley Society and on that reason there was quarrel between them. That defence is not raised and asked in the cross examination of the witnesses and therefore his defence cannot be taken into consideration. Even it is accepted as true nobody will blame accused and implicate him in such a serious offence. So this defence does not appear to be probable and believable. 23. I come to the conclusion that the prosecution has proved beyond doubt that the accused has lifted the victim aged four years while she was playing on sand. There was no other boys or girls playing there. So the accused took advantage of this fact and secretly lifted the victim and taken her on the stair case and he seated the victim on his thighs, removed her chaddi and touched her vagina and thereafter he left the victim near the house of the victim and witness Dulali has seen the accused while lifting the victim and after some time he left the victim near her house. She told this fact to the victim's mother. The victim also narrated the incident immediately to her mother, so the incident is proved by the prosecution beyond all reasonable doubt. 24. The prosecution has proved ingredients of the offence under section 354A of Indian Penal Code and Section 7 punishable under section 8 of POCSO Act, 2012. 25. As per the provisions of section 42 of the POCSO Act, 2012 alternate punishment is to be awarded which is greater in degree. 26. The offence under section 7 punishable under section 8 of POCSO Act has provided punishment of imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than three years but which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine. 27. Under section 354A(i) punishment is with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extent to three years or with fine or with both. 28. Considering the punishment provided under both Acts for sexual assault I think that the punishment provided under section 8 of POCSO Act, 2012 is greater in degree. Therefore, the accused is liable to be punished under section 8 of POCSO Act, 2012. 29. The court is of the view that the fine amount shall be paid to the victim as compensation. However, the accused is under trial prisoner so he is not in position to pay higher amount of fine. So the victim could not be given adequate amount of compensation. Therefore as per the provisions of sections 357A(3) I recommend the District Legal Services Authority to award compensation to the victim as per rules after necessary inquiry. Date:13.10.2017 (S. C. Khalipe) Thane. Additional Sessions Judge, Thane. 30. In the afternoon session the accused is produced form jail authority. I heard accused on the point of sentence. He has not submitted anything. 31. The Ld. APP submitted that the maximum punishment may be awarded. 32. Considering the facts and circumstance of this case I do not found any mitigating circumstance. Accordingly, I pass following order. ORDER 1] The accused Aizaz Nabban Khan is convicted under section 235(2) of Criminal Procedure Code for the offence punishable under section 8 of POCSO Act, 2012 read with section 354 A (1) (i) of Indian Penal Code. 2 The accused Aizaz Nabban Khan is sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for the period three years and to pay fine of Rs.1,000/­ (Rupees One Thousand only) for the offence punishable under Section 8 of POCSO Act, 2012 read with section 354A (1)(i) of Indian Penal Code, in default of payment of fine he shall suffer S.I. for the period of one month. 3. After realization of fine amount the amount of Rs.1,000/­ (Rupees One Thousand Only) shall be paid to the victim as compensation after the appeal period. 4. The District Legal Services Authority is recommended to award compensation to the victim as per rules. 5. The accused Aizaz Nabban Khan was arrested on 25.04.2017 and he is in jail till today therefore set off be given under section 428 of Cr. P.C. for this period. 6. The Judgment is dictated and declared in open court. 7. The copy of Judgment shall be given to the accused free of costs. Thane. (S.C. Khalipe) Date:13.10.2017. Additional Sessions Judge,Thane.

--1-- CRI. BAIL APPLI. NO.1528/2018 ORDER BELOW EXH.1 IN CRIMINAL BAIL APPLICATION NO.1528/2018 (CNR NO.MHTH01­004206­2018 ) The applicant No.1 Sarfraz Chand Qureshi, No.2 Bilal Sikandar Qureshi, No.3 Hanif Zakir Shaikh and Krushna @ Kisan Balu Chauhan have applied for bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C., in C.R. No.I­279/2018 registered in Mumbra police station for the offence under section 452, 354, 323, 504, 427, 506(2), 143, 144, 147, 148, 149 of Indian Penal Code and section 8 of POCSO Act, 2012. 2. It is contended that the applicants are innocent and falsely implicated. They are permanent resident of given address. They are ready to co­operate for investigation and ready to abide b y conditions. Nothing has been recovered at the instance of these applicants. It is first bail application. So considering the nature of offence applicants are prayed for bail. 3. Investigating Officer has given his say at Exh.4. 4. I heard Ld. Counsel on behalf of accused and Ld. APP. 5. It is the case of prosecution that on 23.05.2018 at about 3.00 p.m. this accused along with other 7 to 8 accused persons entered into the house of informant under suspicion that she was selling liquor. It is alleged that the accused persons were armed with iron pipe, wooden rod, stump etc and broke the house of the accused and damaged the house and pulled out informant from the house. At that time one of the accused namely Shanu had sexually assaulted informant's minor daughter. --2-- CRI. BAIL APPLI. NO.1528/2018 6. As per the report of the I.O during police custody the iron rod, wooden rod etc. are not seized inspite of police custody remand was given. It appears that the statement of the victim girl under section 164 of Cr.P.C., is yet to be recorded. I.O has objected for the bail on the ground that, if the accused are released on bail they are likely to repeat the offence and tamper the prosecution witnesses. They are likely to destroy the weapons and there is no guarantee that they will remain present for the trial. 7. The court is of the view that the accused were arrested on 23.05.2018 and since then he is in jail. Investigation is almost completed. Instead of PCR was granted the weapon is not recovered, therefore, there is no likelihood that the weapon will be recovered. Offences are not punishable with death or imprisonment for life. They are punishable which may extent to 7 years. So considering the role played by the accused the court is of the view that there is no necessity to keep the applicant behind bar till final disposal of the case. Therefore, on condition he is entitled tobe released on bail. Therefore, I proceed to pass following order. :ORDER: 1. Application is allowed. 2. The applicant Nos.1 to 4 be released on P.B. and S.B. of Rs.20,000/­(Rupees Twenty Thousand Only) each with one or two sureties in like amount. --3-- CRI. BAIL APPLI. NO.1528/2018 3. Applicants shall not enter into the area where the informant was resides and shall not pressurize, threaten the informant and any other witnesses by any means. 4. They shall not repeat any offence. 5. They shall attend the concern police station once in a month till further order. 6. They shall not leave the jurisdiction of the court without prior permission. She has admitted that on the date of lodging the F.I.R., no wrong had occurred with her, i.e., no rape had occurred with her. She has admitted that she had a fight with her father that day. 32] Therefore, as per the case of the victim (complainant) and the I.O., the victim was more than 16 years old at the time of registration of the offence. As per Sec. 22 of the POCSO Act, 2012 if a child being less than 16 years makes a false complaint or provides false information, then no punishment shall be imposed on such child. However, where a false complaint has been made or false information has been 17 Spl. C. No. 146/2014 (Judgment) provided by any child being more than 16 years, and it is proved that the complaint was made or information was provided with her own informed decision, in such case, the child shall be sent to the Juvenile Justice Board constituted under Section 4 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2000, for suitable remedial action. In this case, though the age of the victim is not proved by the prosecution, however, it is also not proved that she was an adult at the time of lodging the F.I.R. 33] The complainant in this case has undoubtedly misused the Provisions of POCSO Act and lodged a false complaint against her own father thereby causing him grave hardship and mental agony and trauma. He has spent close to 3 years in jail owing to the serious allegations levelled against him. Since the victim herself was the complainant in this matter and since she was more than 16 years old as per record and the complaint was made and the information provided was as per her own informed decision, no fine or jail term can be imposed upon her as per Provisions of Sec. 22 of the POCSO Act, 2012. However, she can be sent to Juvenile Justice Board U/s. 4 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2000 for remedial action. The provisions of law should not be misused. The complainant was admittedly a major at the time of deposition. Therefore, perjury proceedings be initiated against her. 34] The burden of proving the guilt of the accused rests on the prosecution. The constitutional mandate of innocence prevails unless the prosecution succeeds in proving by satisfactory evidence the guilt beyond reasonable doubt of the accused which it has failed to do in this case. I therefore, answer point No.1 and 2 in the negative. In view of the 18 Spl. C. No. 146/2014 (Judgment) foregoing discussion and in view of the facts and circumstances of the present case, the following order would meet the ends of justice. ORDER 1] The accused Azad Ramji Mishra is hereby acquitted vide section 235 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for the offences punishable under sections 376(2)(f) and (n) of the Indian Penal Code and Sec. 5(l)(n) r/w. Sec. 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] The accused is in jail. He be set at liberty forthwith if not required in any other case. 3] Muddemal if any be destroyed after the appeal period is over. 4] The accused shall execute a fresh P.R. bond of ₹15,000/­ to appear before the Appellate Court as and when such court issues notice in respect of any appeal or petition filed against this judgment, in terms of section 437­A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 5] Perjury notice U/s 193 of the I.P.C. be issued against the complainant/victim. 6] The complainant/victim be sent to Juvenile Justice Board U/s. 4 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2000 for remedial action 7] The complainant should refund the compensation amount (if any, received by her) to the State. Thane. (Mridula V. K. Bhatia) Date : 22/12/2016. District Judge­08 & Special Judge (POCSO Act), Thane.
