Ds. 4 ­ 5 ­ 22 IN THE COURT OF THE SPECIAL JUDGE THANE, AT : THANE (Presided over by S. B. Bahalkar ) SPECIAL CASE NO. 147/2014 EXH. No. CNR­MHTH01­004259­2014 State of Maharashtra. (Through: Wada Police Station in C.R.No.I­55/2014) ...Prosecution V/s. Nagesh Madhukar Wagh Age­ 24 years, R/at: Kharivali Kohoj, Tal.Wada, Dist. Thane. ... Accused ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ Appearances :­­ Ld.APP Smt.Chandane, for the prosecution. Ld. Advocate Shri.Kanhere for the accused. ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.147/2014 (Judgment). : 2: Special Case No.147/2014 (Judgment) (CNR MHTH­004259­2014) JUDGMENT (Delivered on 11th day of January, 2019) [1] Accused kidnapped a minor girl­ 'P' (name is not mentioned) from the lawful guardianship of her parents and took her with himself and established sexual relation with her. Therefore, the accused is facing trial U/Sec.376, 363 and 366A of the Indian Penal Code (in short I.P.C.) and U/Secs.6 and 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offence Act (in short POCSO Act). [2] Brief facts of the prosecution case are as under :­ (i) 'P', The victim girl is the daughter of informant Mohan Zate. In the year 2014 she was about 17 years old and was working in a company. On 17/04/2014 at about 8.00 a.m. she went to her job as usual. However, when she did not come back till evening time, her parents and other relatives started to take her search. However, she could not be found. Therefore, on 18/4/2014 her father i.e. informant Mohan Zate lodged missing report at Wada Police Station. (ii) Thereafter, on 20/4/2014 one Deepak Dhanva resident of the same village informed the informant that on 17/4/2014 at about 10.00 a.m. he saw that 'P' was sitting behind the accused on the motorcycle and they were proceeding towards Abjephata. Therefore, the informant went to the said spot and found that his AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.147/2014 (Judgment). : 3: Special Case No.147/2014 (Judgment) (CNR MHTH­004259­2014) daughter 'P' was there. On enquiry his daughter disclosed him that on 17/4/2014 the accused forcibly kidnapped under the fake promise of marriage and thereafter he took her to Shahapur and under the fake promise of marriage he established sexual relations with her. (iii) Thereafter the informant came to Wada Police Station and lodged F.I.R. against the accused. On the basis of said information crime vide C.R.No.I­55/2014 U/Secs.376, 363 & 366­ A of IPC and U/Secs.6 & 8 of the POCSO Act came to be registered and handed over to PSI Salunkhe for investigation. [3] I.O. PSI Salunkhe on 20/4/2014 visited to the spot of incident where the victim girl was taken and he also visited to the room at village Kasghar where the accused kept the victim girl in the night time and committed sexual assault. The I.O. has prepared panchanama of both the said spots in presence of panch witnesses. On the same day he seized wearing clothes of the victim girl under the panchanama. On that day he also recorded statements of parents of the victim girl and other witnesses. [4] Thereafter on 26/4/2014 when the accused was in police custody he made confessional statement and showed his willingness to show the spot, where he concealed the motorcycle which was used to kidnap the victim girl. Accordingly the I.O. AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.147/2014 (Judgment). : 4: Special Case No.147/2014 (Judgment) (CNR MHTH­004259­2014) recorded the said confessional statement of the accused in presence of panch witnesses and thereafter he alongwith the accused and panch witnesses went to the said spot as led by the accused and seized one motorcycle. Under the same panchanama the I.O. has also seized wearing clothes of the accused. [5] In the meanwhile the victim girl was forwarded to I.G.M. Hospital, Bhiwandi for medical examination. Accordingly her medical examination was conducted. [6] Thereafter, the I.O. has recorded statements of other witnesses and collected birth certificate of the victim girl. He forwarded the seized clothes and other articles to F.S.L. Kalina for chemical analysis. On completion of investigation he submitted chargesheet against the accused U/Secs.376, 363 & 366­A of IPC and U/Secs.6 & 8 of the POCSO Act. [7] Since the offences charged against the accused are triable exclusively by the Sessions and the Special Court, the Ld. J.M.F.C. committed the said case to this court. [8] I have framed charge (Exh.7) against the accused U/secs. 376, 363 & 366­A of IPC and U/Secs.6 & 8 of the POCSO Act. Particulars of the offences were read over and explained to the AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.147/2014 (Judgment). : 5: Special Case No.147/2014 (Judgment) (CNR MHTH­004259­2014) accused to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. [9] For want of incriminating evidence against the accused, his statement U/Sec.313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is dispensed with. [10] Following points arise for my determination. I have recorded my findings thereon for the reasons stated below : Sr. POINTS FINDINGS No 1 Whether the prosecution proves that the Not proved. accused committed rape on minor girl 'P' ? 2 Whether the prosecution proves that the accused kidnapped the minor girl 'P' from the lawful guardianship of her parents and took her with him ? Not proved. 3 Whether the prosecution proves that the accused induced minor girl 'P' to go with him with intent that he may be forced to Not proved. illicit intercourse ? 4 Whether prosecution further proves that the accused committed aggravated penetrative sexual assault on the minor Not proved. victim girl 'P' ? 5 Whether prosecution further proves that the accused committed sexual assault on the said minor victim girl 'P' ? Not proved. 6 What order ? Accused is acquitted. AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.147/2014 (Judgment). : 6: Special Case No.147/2014 (Judgment) (CNR MHTH­004259­2014) REASONS AS TO POINTS NOS. 1 to 5:­ [11] Since all the points for determination arose for one and the same incident, I took them together for discussion. [12] Mohan Zate (P.W.1) is the father of the victim girl. He states that in the year 2014 his daughter 'P' was about 17 yrs. Old and she used to go for job in a company. On that day she went to the job at about 8.00 a.m. However, as usual she did not come back till 5.00 p.m. Hence, he took her search and waited till night and on the next morning he went to Wada Police Station and lodged missing report. About 3 days thereafter one Deepak Dhanva residing near his house informed him that about 2 days before he saw that accused Nagesh was taking 'P' on his motorcycle. Therefore, Mohan(P.W.1) lodged F.I.R. against the accused. In his cross­examination Mohan Zate (P.W.1) admits that he did not know birth date of any of his children. He do not know birth date of his daughter 'P' also. [13] On examination of Mohan Zate (P.W.1) it appears that he nowhere disclosed that his daughter 'P' disclosed him that the accused established sexual relations with her nor he disclosed that the accused forcibly took her with him. Thus, in my opinion evidence of Mohan Zate (P.W.1) is not sufficient to prove the guilt of accused. AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.147/2014 (Judgment). : 7: Special Case No.147/2014 (Judgment) (CNR MHTH­004259­2014) [14] 'P' (P.W.3) is the victim girl. She states that about 3 years back she got married. Prior to that she alongwith her parents and sister was residing at Khanivli. In the year 2014 she used to go for a job in a company at Khanivli and the accused was also working in the said company. She had friendship with the accused. She categorically states that nothing had happened between them. She turned hostile, hence, the Ld.A.P.P. cross­ examined her. However, in the said cross­examination nothing fruitful could be brought on the record in favour of the prosecution. 'P' (P.W.3) denied that she had stated before police that accused took her with him under the fake promise of marriage and then established sexual relation with her. Thus, the evidence of 'P' (P.W.3) is also not helpful to prove the guilt of accused. [15] Prosecution has also examined Ganesh Jadhav (P.W.2). According to the prosecution he is panch witness of panchanama of both spot the spot of incidents, as well as of the panchanama of seizure of clothes of the victim girl, accused as well as the motorcycle. Said Ganesh Jadhav (P.W.2) denied that police prepared panchanama of the spot of the incident in his presence. He also denied that police seized clothes of the victim girl and the accused. He also denied that police seized motorcycle at the instance of the accused in his presence. Thus, evidence of Ganesh Jadhav (P.W.2) is not of use to bring home the guilt of accused. AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.147/2014 (Judgment). : 8: Special Case No.147/2014 (Judgment) (CNR MHTH­004259­2014) [16] So far medical examination report of the victim girl and sending the seized clothes to F.S.L. Kalina and the chemical analysis report are concerned, the same are admitted by the accused. So also the prosecution has not brought on record sufficient legal evidence to prove that at the time of incident the victim was minor. [17] On the basis of above evidence , I can safely conclude that prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of accused U/Secs. 376, 363 and 366A of IPC and U/Secs.6 and 8 of POCSO Act. I, therefore, answer point Nos.1 to 5 in the negative. AS TO POINT NO.6 : [18] As mentioned above, the prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of accused U/Secs.376, 363 and 366A of I.P.C. and U/Secs.6 and 8 of POCSO Act. Hence, the accused is entitled to be acquitted. So far muddemal property i.e. seized clothes of the victim girl and the accused and one bed­sheet are concerned, they being worthless are liable to be destroyed after appeal period is over. I, therefore, in answer to point No.6 pass the following order : ­: ORDER :­ 1) Accused Nagesh Madhukar Wagh is hereby acquitted of the offences punishable U/Sec.376, 363, 366­A of the Indian Penal Code and U/Secs. 6 & 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 vide Sec.235(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.147/2014 (Judgment). : 9: Special Case No.147/2014 (Judgment) (CNR MHTH­004259­2014) 2) Bail bond of the accused stands cancelled. 3) The accused shall furnish P.R.bond of Rs.15,000/­ (Rs.Fifteen Thousand only) and surety of like amount in compliance of provisions U/Sec. 437­A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 4) Muddemal property being worthless be destroyed after the appeal period is over. Thane. ( S. B. Bahalkar ) Dated: 11/01/2019 Special Judge, Thane. Under POCSO Act,2012. AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.147/2014 (Judgment).

--1-- ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN ANTICIPATORY BAIL APPLICATOIN NO.1633/2017 The applicant Firoz Rifakat Ali has applied for bail under section 438 of Cr. P.C. in C.R.No.I­204/2017 registered in Mira Road police station for the offence under section 328, 376, 506 of Indian Penal Code and Section 4 and 6 of POCSO ACT. 2. It is contended that the applicant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated. He has submitted the documents and affidavit which shows the applicant is married with the victim on 23.03.2017. Thereafter the applicant and the prosecutrix have stayed together as husband and wife. So the allegations in the FIR are not applicable to the present applicant. The case falls under section 375 exception 2 of Indian Penal Code. The victim was not below under fifteen years at the time of marriage. Therefore, sexual intercourse with the own wife does not amount to rape. The age of prosecutrix was 17.5 years at the time of marriage. 3. It is contended that the prosecutrix had told her age was above 18 years and she had intimated to the Kazi her age as 18 years. She has specifically signed the Nikahnama. She has co­habited with the applicant as his wife. It is contended that one Momin Ansari who has promised the family of prosecutrix that he will give job to the prosecutrix in film industry as she is very beautiful and the prosecutrix was taken --2-- away from the custody of the applicant. The applicant had complaint to the Commissioner of Police on 12.06.2017. After that FIR has been lodged. The applicant has produced some photographs which shows that the prosecutrix was happily residing with the applicant and she has enjoyed her martial life. There was no force used by the applicant. It is submitted that the prosecutrix was in bad company and the applicant had married her to put her in a normal life. 4. So considering all these aspects the applicant has prayed for anticipatory bail. It is contended that there is no recovery. The applicant had no criminal background. He is from very respectable family. He is ready to co­operate for the investigation. 5. The applicant has produced the copy of FIR, copy of Nikahnama, copy of Joint Marriage Affidavit, copy of affidavit cum declaration, bunch of photographs, copy of complaint given by the applicant, his Adhar Card. 6. Investigating Officer has given his say at Exh.12. It is contended that from 24.04.2017 to 31.05.2017 the present applicant administered some intoxicant in Beer, Vodka, and wine and also gave cigarate to smoke to the prosecutrix and committed sexual intercourse with her and then threatened to kill her and threatened that “maine tumari adult clip banai hai, jayada hushari ki to sabko dikha dunga”. So the prosecutrix --3-- has lodged FIR on 26.06.2017 in Mira Road police station. 7. It is contended that the applicant has administered some intoxicant in the cold drink, therefore, the interrogation of the applicant is necessary in respect to that. The medical examination of the applicant is necessary and the adult clip has to be seized. So considering all these aspects Investigating Officer has prayed for rejection of anticipatory bail. 8. The present application is also contested by the prosecutrix. She has given written notes of arguments through her Advocate. 9. I heard Ld. A.P.P. She relied upon decision in case of State Rep. By the C.B.I V/s. Anil Sharma in 1997 CRI. L.J.4414 Supreme Court. It is hled that consideration for anticipatory bail need not be same as for an application to release on bail after arrest. 10. The Ld. Counsel on behalf of the applicant argued that the prosecutrix is married with the present applicant voluntarily and she has signed the Nikahnama and Nikahnama is also attested by two witnesses. The prosecutrix has stated her age above 18 years at the time of marriage. Only because the prosecutrix wants to do carrier in film industry she want to take divorce from the applicant and to get separate. The false FIR has been lodged. Ld. Counsel submitted that photographs --4-- shows that prosecutrix was happy with the applicant and she has enjoyed her marital life with him. The age of applicant was above 15 years at the time of alleged act of sexual assault, therefore, it falls under the exception No.2 in Section 375 of IPC. So no case made out. He submitted that nothing is required to be seized. He has already appeared before the police and he has co­operate for investigation and therefore, he may be released on bail. 11. The Ld. Counsel on behalf of the applicant relied upon decision in case of State of A.P. V/s. P. Narasimha and another in (1994) 4 Supreme Court 453. It is held that, “proseuctrix having married with the accused, her consent can well be presumed even for sexual acts prior to the marriage. In case of Sunil Mahadev Patil V/s. The State of Maharashtra 2016 ALL MR (Cri) 1712. It was held that, “the prosecutrix is 15 years old and accused is 20 years old. The statement of prosecutrix and witnesses showing that they were in love with each other, so they eloped and went to temple and according to them they were garlanded each other and according to them performed marriage and thereafter they started residing together in house of their relative. In view of so many mitigating factors, bail granted to accused on certain conditions.” In case of Akshay Manoj Jaisinghani V/s. State of Maharashtra in Anticipatory Bail Application No.2221/2016 dtd.09.01.2017. It was held that in para­6 of the Judgment that, “ when a woman is major and educated --5-- and depending on facts on the case, she is supposed to be fully aware of the consequences of having sexual intercourse with a man before marriage. In the event of consent obtained by fraud, inducement is a necessary ingredient. There should be some material on record to believe prima facie that the girl was induced by the accused to such an extent that she was ready to have sexual intercourse with him. Promise to marry cannot be said to be an inducement in these types of cases.” 12. I perused the FIR. FIR was lodged on 24.06.2017. In the FIR prosecutrix has mentioned her age as 17.6 years. It is mentioned that she was learnt upto 10th standard and she was originally residing at Hyderabad. She want to have carrier in film industry, therefore, she came to Mira Road, Thane. She took the flat on rent after that she came to know present applicant. They were frequently calling each other on phone and they fell in love. In April 2017 the prosecutrix mother came to know about the love affair, therefore, she left her house and went to the house of present applicant. It is alleged that on 23.04.2017 the present applicant administered some intoxicant in the sprite and then the applicant lost her consciousness and present applicant committed sexual assault upon her and after that it is alleged that the present applicant took the prosecutrix to Masjid and performed marriage with her. For that marriage the friends of the applicant and his wife were present. --6-- 13. Considering the facts and circumstances of this case the court is of the view that the prosecutrix was above 17 years, she is learnt upto 10th standard, she is matured. She herself came to Mira Road, Thane for having carrier in film industry. She fall in love with the present applicant and then she herself went to the house of present applicant. Though she has alleged that some intoxicant has been administered and applicant committed sexual assault with her, the court is of the view that the FIR was lodged at very late stage and therefore, it is impossible to interrogate and seized what type of intoxicant was mixed in her cold drinks. If the photographs which are produced by the applicant are perused it appears that the prosecutrix had love affair with the present applicant. Nikahnama was also executed by her. Affidavit cum declaration and affidavit of marriage is signed by the prosecutrix. In those documents the applicant is mentioned her age above 18 years. 14. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case the court is of the view that nothing is required to be seized from the applicant, therefore, his custodial interrogation is not necessary. His medical examination can be done without having any police custody. The applicant is ready to co­ operate for the investigation. The applicant is also ready to attend concerned police station for investigation and to produce any document or anything as require by the Investigating Officer. He has no criminal antecedent so --7-- considering these aspects and the observations made in above cited cases the court is of the view that it is a fit case to grant anticipatory bail. Hence, the order. ORDER 1. Application is allowed. 2. Ad­interim bail order below Exh.3 is hereby confirmed. 3. It is directed that the applicant shall attend the concerned police station daily between 11.00 a.m. to 2.00 p.m., till the investigation is over. 4. The other conditions will remain as it is. Thane. ( S.C. Khalipe ) Date : 28/07/2017. Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

.. 1 .. Special case 151/2015 judgment Received on : 04.07.2015 Registered on : 04.07.2015 Decided on : 31.07.2015 Duration : 24 days IN THE COURT OF THE SESSION JUDGE, THANE AT THANE (Presided over by Ms.V.V.Virkar,Additional Sessions Judge-1,Thane) Special Case No. 151 of 2015 Exhibit No. 04 The State of Maharashtra … Complainant versus Balaji Satvaji Ratte, … Accused Age 28 years, Residence – Shraminkanagar Slum, Turbhe MIDC Navi Mumbai JUDGMENT (Delivered on 31.07.2015.) The accused stands prosecuted for the offence punishable under section 354, 323, 504, 506 of I.P.C. and section 7 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short ''P.O.C.S.O. Act'') for outraging modesty of minor girl Ashwini aged 15 years when she was playing outside her house at Shramiknagar, near Kalubai temple, Khairane village, Navi Mumbai. .. 2 .. Special case 151/2015 judgment 2] In short the facts giving rise to the prosecution of the accused are that on 15.03.2015 the complainant and her sister Meera was cooking food for dinner and the victim girl and the daughters of Meera were playing outside house. At about 8.30 p.m. the victim girl Ashwini came inside the house crying and informed the complainant that the accused who is resident of same locality held her hand and stated to her that he likes her. Thereafter, the complainant, her husband and other members of family questioned the accused about the alleged act but the accused avoided them. Therefore, the complainant lodged complaint to Turbhe MIDC police station about the alleged act of sexual assault on her minor daughter by the accused. 3] On the basis of her complaint, offence as per C.R.No. II- 14/2015 was registered at Turbhe MIDC police station and it was investigated into. During the investigation panchnama of the spot was prepared. Statements of witnesses including victim girl were recorded. Birth certificate of the girl showing her age was obtained. Bona fide certificate showing date of birth of the girl was collected from her school. After completion of investigation, since there was sufficient against the accused, he was charge-sheeted for offence punishable under section 354, 323, 504, 506 of I.P.C. and section 7 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and the charge sheet was submitted to the Special Court since provisions of P.O.C.S.O. Act are applied. 4] The accused was produced before Court by jail authorities. A charge as per Exhibit 2 was framed against the accused for offence under section 354A(1)(i) of I.P.C. and section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. The contents of the charge were read over and explained .. 3 .. Special case 151/2015 judgment to the accused in vernacular. He pleaded guilty and accepted the charges levelled against him and prayed for leniency while awarding the punishment. 5] On above facts of this case, the points which arose for my determination and my findings and reasons for the same are as under - Points Findings i) Whether the prosecution has proved that on 15.03.2015 at about 8.30 p.m. at Shramiknagar slum Khairane MIDC, Navi Mubai, the accused had physical contact and advances with minor victim girl Ashwini aged 15 years which was involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures? Yes. ii ) Whether the prosecution has proved that the accused on the given day, date, time and place committed sexual harassment of said minor girl ? Yes. iii ) What offence, if any, is proved against the Both offences are accused ? proved. iv ) What order ? The accused is convicted. REASONS 6] As is clear the offence charge against the accused is under section 354A(1)(i) of I.P.C. and section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act with the allegation that the accused had sexually harassed minor girl Ashwini aged 15 years by taking holding her hand in order to have physical contact with her and staying to her that he likes her. Even it is also clear from the complaint lodged by the complainant that very specific allegations are made against the accused and on that basis offence under section 354A(1)(i) of I.P.C. and section 11 read with section 12 of .. 4 .. Special case 151/2015 judgment P.O.C.S.O. Act are charged against the accused and the accused has been prosecuted for the said offence and the accused pleaded guilty. Even as per section 29 of P.O.C.S.O. Act the accused is presumed to have committed the charges levelled against him unless the contrary is proved. 7] In such circumstance he is liable to be convicted for the said charge under section 354A(1)(i) of I.P.C. and section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. 8] At this stage the dictation of the Judgment is postponed for hearing the accused on the point of sentence. Date : 31.07.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Additional Session Judge-1, Thane. Resumed. 9] The accused is made aware of the fact that he is held guilty for the offence under section 354A(1)(i) of I.P.C. and section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and the punishment prescribed for offence under section 354A(1)(i) of I.P.C. is Rigorous Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years or with fine and offence under section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act is punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine. 10] I heard the learned A.P.P. and the accused on the point of sentence. The learned A.P.P. submitted that looking to the serious nature of offence charged against the accused he is not entitled to leniency and he is liable to award maximum punishment prescribed. .. 5 .. Special case 151/2015 judgment The accused prayed for showing him leniency on the ground that he is the only earning member in his family and his family is depending upon him for their livelihood. 11] Then, as is clear though the offence charged against the accused is of very serious nature, the allegations is only that he had taken the victim minor girl inside the public toilet in an uncoming manner and then with sexual intent removed her underwear. But then, it is submitted by the accused on the point of sentence that he has to look after his family members and he is the earning person in his family. 12] Then, so far as quantum of punishment is concerned, Section 42 of the P.O.C.S.O. Act provides : ''Where an act or omission constitutes an offence punishable under this Act and also under sections 166A, 354A, 354B, 354C, 354D, 370, 370A, 375, 376, 376A, 376C, 376D, 376E or section 509 of the Indian Penal Code, then notwithstanding anything contained in any law for the time being in force, the offender found guilty of such offence shall be liable to punishment under this Act or under the Indian Penal Code as provides for punishment which is greater in degree''. Then, as is clear the offence under section 354A(1)(i) of I.P.C. is punishable with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years or with fine whereas offence under section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act is punishable with imprisonment which may extend to three years and also with fine. As such it is clear that sentence of imprisonment of either description i.e. S.I. or R.I. can be awarded for commission of offence under section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and therefore it can be said that as per provisions of section 42 of P.O.C.S.O. Act substantive sentence only for offence punishable under section 11 read with section 12 which is imprisonment of either description .. 6 .. Special case 151/2015 judgment for a term which may extend to three years and also fine has to be awarded to the accused. 13] In all such circumstance I am of the view that following sentence would meet ends of justice. In the result I pass the following order - ORDER Accused namely Balaji Satvaji Ratte is convicted for the offence punishable under section 354A(1)(i) of the Indian Penal Code and also for offence under section 11 read with 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and by invoking provisions of Section 42 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012, the accused is sentenced to suffer Rigorous Imprisonment for the term of five months and to pay fine of Rs.500/- (rupees five hundred only) and in default of payment of fine to suffer S.I. for five days for commission of offence punishable under section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act only. 2) The accused was in jail since 16.03.2015. A set off under section 438 of Cr.P.C. is granted to him for the term of the period of detention undergone by him during the investigation, inquiry and trial against the substantive sentence imposed upon him. 3) Since no muddemal property is produced before Court, no order regarding its disposal is passed. 4) Copy of judgment be given to the accused free of cost. 5) The proceeding is closed. .. 1 .. Special case 30/2013 Judgment Received on : 01/08/2013 Registered on : 01/08/2013 Decided on : 31/08/2015 Duration : 02 Y. 00 M. 30 D. In The Court of the Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012, Thane) At Thane (Presided over by Mrs.V.V.Virkar ) Special Case No. 30 of 2013 Exhibit No. 27 The State of Maharashtra (Through Wagle Estate police station Bhiwandi) … Complainant Versus Brijesh Rama Rane Age 29 years, Residing at Thakur chawl, Room No.1, M.S.Mohan Sundarji Road, Zarande wadi, Raghunath Nagar, Wagle Estate, Thane. … Accused Appearances :­ A.P.P. Mrs. N. A. Navle for the State. Advocate Mr. S. J. Kanhere for the accused. JUDGMENT (Delivered on 31st August, 2015) Accused stands prosecuted for the offences punishable under sections 376, 506 of Indian Penal Code and punishable under .. 2 .. Special case 30/2013 Judgment sections 4 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter referred as P.O.C.S.O Act in short) for committing rape and sexual assault on minor victim girl Mrunal Mahadev Lingayat on 06/01/2013 around 12.30 p.m. at the house of complainant at 303, B/2, New Anand Park, Raghunath Nagar, Wagle Estate, Thane and for threatening her to defame her in her family and society when she resisted. 2] In short the facts giving rise to the prosecution of the accused are that one Mrunal Mahadev Lingayat aged about 16 years lodged complaint on 06/01/2013 that she is staying with her parents at New Anand park, Wagle Estate, Thane, her father is the Branch Manager in Dena Bank, Shrinagar branch and he used to go for duty since 8.30 in the morning till 7.30 p.m. At the relevant time in the year 2013, she was studying in 10th standard and was to appear for examination externally. It was also contended by her that accused Brijesh Rama Rane was staying in Zarande wadi and was of acquaintance with her and they were having family relations with each other and they were on visiting terms. That about one month before, accused had been to her house and was having talk in regard to the loan with her mother and around 12.30 in noon on 06/01/2013 her mother left house, and then she herself and accused were only in the house and accused started forcing her to dance with him and when she resisted he started physical advances with her. He then had forced her to lay on the bed in the hall and had forcible sexual intercourse with her by removing his own clothes as well as her clothes and then left by threatening that she should not disclose about incident to anybody else he would defame her. It was also .. 3 .. Special case 30/2013 Judgment contended by her that she was scared because of incident and threats and therefore she did not disclose about the incident to her mother. But then on 05/01/2013 she had disclosed about the incident to her friend Mujafar and Mujafar informed about the incident to her mother and then she went to the police station and lodged complaint. 3] On the basis of her complaint, offence under C.R. No. I 10/20013 under sections 376, 506 of Indian Penal Code and section 4 of P.O.C.S.O Act was registered and work of investigation was entrusted to A.P.I. R. A. Shaikh. During the investigation, panchnama of the spot was prepared. The clothes on the person of the victim girl were seized from the spot under the same panchanama. Since the girl was reported to be minor, school certificate in regard to her date of birth was obtained. Statements of the witnesses including her mother and friend Mujafar were recorded. Accused came to be arrested. The girl as well as accused were referred for medical examination. It is also case of the prosecution while in police custody accused made statement that he would discover his clothes which were on his person at the time of incident and in accordance with the statement he discovered said clothes as per his statement and same came to be seized under panchnama. It is also further case of the prosecution that seized muddemal and samples obtained were sent to C.A. for chemical analysis alongwith letter and since there was sufficient evidence against the accused, accused came to be chargesheeted under sections 376, 506 of I.P.C. and section 4 of P.O.C.S.O Act. .. 4 .. Special case 30/2013 Judgment 4] It has to be mentioned that since offences under section P.O.C.S.O Act is applied, charge­sheet was submitted to this Court as a Special Court for trying offence in respect of P.O.C.S.O Act. 5] Accused appeared before the Court. A charge under sections 376, 506 of I.P.C. and section 3 r/w. section 4 of P.O.C.S.O Act was framed against the accused vide Exh.03. Contents of charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. He pleaded not guilty. His defence was of total denial. He claimed to be tried. 6] For establishing the offences charged against the accused, prosecution examined P.W.1 Mahadev Dattaram Lingayat – the father of the victim girl and P.W.2 P.I. Vaishali Rajendra Pawar who recorded the complaint of complainant. The documentary evidence produced, proved and relied upon by prosecution consisted of spot panchnama at Exh.08, school leaving certificate of victim girl at Exh.14, medical examination papers and certificate of victim girl at Exh.15 to 18, medical examination certificate and paper of accused at Exh.19 and 20 respectively, memorandum statement of accused at Exh.21 and complaint at Exh.25. 7] Statement of accused under section 313 of Cr.P.C. was recorded. Accused did not examine himself on oath and had not examined any witness in his defence. .. 5 .. Special case 30/2013 Judgment 8] I heard both Ld. A.P.P. And Ld. Advocate for the accused and on the basis of above facts of case, points which arose for my determination and my reasons and findings for the same are as under. POINTS FINDINGS 1. Whether prosecution proved that one month prior to 06/01/2013 at about 12.30 p.m., at 303, B/2, New Anand Park, Raghunath Nagar, Wagle Estate, Thane accused committed rape on complainant namely Mrunal Mahadev Lingayat by doing forcible sexual intercourse with her? ... No. 2. Whether prosecution proved that on the given date time and place, whenever the complainant resisted the act of accused, accused committed criminal intimidation to her by threatening her to defame her and her family members? ... No. 3. Whether prosecution proved that on ... No. the given date, time and place accused committed penetrative sexual assault on the complainant? 4. What offence, if any, is proved against accused? ... No offence is proved. 5. What order? ... Accused is acquitted. REASONS AS TO POINT Nos. 1 TO 3 :­ 9] As is clear as per the prosecution case the accused had .. 6 .. Special case 30/2013 Judgment committed rape on minor girl Mrunal and sexual assault on her and threatened her to defame if she disclose about it to anybody and complaint came to be lodged by girl herself in regard to the said incident. As is clear P.W.2 P.I. Pawar has stated in her evidence that on 06/01/2013 when she was on duty, the girl Mrunal Lingayat had been to the police station and lodged complaint and she recorded complaint as per her narration as per Exh.25. There is no reason for the police officer to depose falsely that complaint was lodged by complainant at the given time and place with the allegations made in the complaint. 10] However, as is clear the fact which can be said to have been established by the testimony of P.W.2 is only that such complaint with such allegations was lodged by girl on that day. But so far as allegations made in the complaint is concerned, testimony of the girl herself is only material evidence. However, in that regard, it has to be mentioned that prosecution has not examined victim girl. It is also material to mention that father of the girl is examined by the prosecution who stated in his evidence that on 06/01/2013 his wife informed him that she is going to lodge complaint against accused that he was troubling and harassing his daughter Mrunal and even when he returned home, his daughter Mrunal also stated that accused has been eve teasing her. But then P.W.1 also stated that daughter did not state anything else. 11] It is further material to mention that victim girl though summoned earlier did not appear before the Court and then her .. 7 .. Special case 30/2013 Judgment father in his evidence on oath also stated that his daughter Mrunal is now staying at her matrimonial house in Chiplun and she is not in position to come for deposition because that would create problem in her matrimonial life if her in­laws come to know about case with the allegations of commission of rape on his daughter. In such circumstances it is clear that though prosecution intended to examine the girl, the girl herself is not in position to come before the Court. As such prosecution cannot be blamed for that. But still the fact cannot be ignored or overlooked that testimony of the girl is not available. 12] Then, so far as allegations against the accused that he had committed rape on girl and threatened to defame her, in absence of substantial evidence of the girl and merely on the basis of fact that complaint was lodged with such allegations of the rape on her on that day, no conclusion in regard to the guilt of the accused for the offence can be arrived. It is also material to mention that even fact that allegations in the complaint about commission of rape and threat given by the accused, etc., are not even stated to have been told by the girl to her father and her father only stated in his evidence that the girls stated to him that accused was eve teasing her and nothing else. Even mother of the girl who took her to the police, is also not examined. As such, there is no evidence even to establish that prosecution is lodged on the basis of truthful averments. 13] The accused came up with specific case that he was not .. 8 .. Special case 30/2013 Judgment knowing the girl and false case is filed against him and he has not committed any offence. Even it is very much clear that father of the girl categorically denied in his cross examination on behalf of the prosecution after he was declared hostile that girl had also stated to him that time that accused was doing physical advances with her and also had sexual intercourse with her and threatened to defame her. Even though police officer stated that complaint was recorded as per narration of complainant, genuineness and truthfulness of the allegations in the complaint appear to be doubtful and therefore presumption under Section 29 of P.O.C.S.O. Act cannot be said to be of any use to the prosecution for establishing guilt of the accused or it cannot be said that allegations are proved beyond all the reasonable doubts and accused therefore is entitled to be acquitted. Point Nos. 1 to 3 are therefore answered accordingly. AS TO POINT No.4 :­ 14] In view of my findings on point Nos. 1 to 3, none of the charges levelled against the accused can be said to have been established and accused is entitled to be acquitted. Point No.4 is therefore answered accordingly. 15] Since the accused is acquitted, it is required that he be directed to furnish P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [Rupees Fifteen Thousand only] under Section 437­A of Cr.P.C. to appear before the higher Court as and when such Court issue notice in respect of any appeal or petition, if any, filed against the judgment. .. 9 .. Special case 30/2013 Judgment In the result, I pass the following order ­ ORDER 1) Accused namely Brijesh Rama Rane is acquitted of the charge for the offence punishable under Sections 376, 506 of Indian Penal Code and also under Section 3, r/w. section 4 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 2) His bail bonds stand cancelled and sureties are discharged 3) The accused shall execute P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] under section 437A of Cr.P.C. to appear before the higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect of any appeal or petition, if any, filed against the judgment and that such bail bond shall be in force for six months. 4) No muddemal article seen to have been submitted to the Court. Hence no order in respect of its disposal is passed. 5) The proceeding is closed. Date : 31/08/2015 (Mrs.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012, Thane)

.. 1 .. Special Case No.31/2013 Judgment Received on : 01.08.2013 Registered on : 01.08.2013 Decided on : 20.03.2015 Duration : 1 year 7 months 20 days IN THE COURT OF THE SPECIAL JUDGE (PROTECTION OF CHILDREN FROM SEXUAL OFFENCES ACT), THANE AT THANE (Presided over by Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Case No. 31 of 2013 Exhibit No. 16 The State of Maharashtra … Complainant versus 1] Akbar Munsharif Ansari, Age 22 years, Residence – house no.1620, Taibanagar, behind Hanuman Temple, Shantinagar, Bhiwandi. 2] Asagar Munsharif Ansari, Age 24 years, Residence – house no.1620, Taibanagar, behind Hamuman Temple, Shantinagar, Bhiwandi. … Accused Appearance - Mr. A.K.Khamkar, learned Additional Public Prosecutor (hereinafter in short A.P.P.) Mr. Thakkar, learned advocate for accused. JUDGMENT (Delivered on 20.03.2015) .. 2 .. Special Case No.31/2013 Judgment The accused stand prosecuted for the offence punishable under section 354, 323, 34 of I.P.C. and section 7, 11, 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as ''P.O.C.S.O. Act'') for outraging modesty of minor girl complainant Saleha Mohammad Ansari by using criminal force and then moving hand on her private part and breast and causing her sexual harassment and also voluntarily causing hurt to her brother Parvez when he tried to intervene. 2] In short the facts giving rise to the prosecution of the accused are that one Salehabanu lodged complaint on 21.03.2013 that she is aged 16 years and is residing alongwith her parents and brothers at Tayabbanagar, Shantinagar, Bhiwandi and both accused are resident of same area staying at the back side of their house and they have been harassing and chasing her since about four months. It was also further contended that on 20.03.2013 when she was proceeding to the house of her paternal aunt namely Sajma Mohammad Harun Ansari by walking the accused accosted her. Accused Asgar caught hold of her hand and took her besides and moved his hand on her breast and private part and accused Akbar did same thing. She was scared and had shouted. By the time her brother Parvez had been there and tried to intervene but both the accused had assaulted him by fist and leg blows and ran away. 3] On the basis of her complaint, offence as per C.R.No. I- 96/2013 under section 354, 323 read with section 34 of I.P.C. and section 3, 4, 7, 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act was registered at Shantinagar police station and the work of investigation was done by P.S.I. Pore. During the investigation panchnama of the spot was prepared. Complainant and her brother were sent for medical examination and their certificates were obtained. Since the girl was minor, proof of her date of birth was obtained. During the investigation since it revealed that there was sufficient evidence against the .. 3 .. Special Case No.31/2013 Judgment accused, they came to be charge-sheeted for the offence punishable under section 354, 323 read with section 34 of I.P.C. and section 3, 4, 7, 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. 4] Since offence under P.O.C.S.O. Act is exclusively triable by Special Court, the charge sheet was submitted to this Court. 5] The accused appeared before the court. A charge as per Exh.3 for offence punishable under section 354, 323 read with section 34 of I.P.C. and section 3, 4, 7, 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act was framed against the accused. The contents were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. The accused pleaded not guilty. Their defence was of total denial. They claimed to be tried. 6] For establishing the charges levelled against the accused the prosecution examined P.W.1 complainant Salehabanu Mohammed Jahid Ansari and P.W.2 Mohammed Parvez Mohammed Harun Ansari. The documentary evidence produced, proved and relied upon by the prosecution consisted of spot panchnama Exh.10, copy of leaving certificate of the girl Exh.11, injury certificate of witness Parvez (all documents are exhibited on admission by defence). 7] I heard the learned A.P.P. and the learned advocate for the accused. 8] On the basis of above facts of the accused following points arise for my determination and my findings and reasons for the same are as under - .. 4 .. Special Case No.31/2013 Judgment POINTS FINDINGS i) Whether the prosecution has proved 21.03.2013 at 2100 hours near one platform (katta) at Taiyyabanagar in front of Anganwadi shop, Shantinagar, Bhiwandi, both accused in furtherance of common intention used criminal force against the victim girl with intent to outrage or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby outrage her modesty? NOT PROVED. ii ) Whether the prosecution has proved that on the given day, date, time and place the accused committed sexual assault on the victim girl ? NOT PROVED. iii ) What offence, if any, is proved against the NO OFFENCE IS accused ? PROVED. iv ) What order ? As per the final order. REASONS 9] As is clear though the accused alleged to have outraged modesty of the complainant who was then minor while she was proceeding to the house of her paternal aunt on 20.03.2013 and when her brother intervened the accused had even assaulted him and caused him grievous hurt. When the complainant and her brother deposed before Court, they have not supported the prosecution case and totally denied of having any such incident taken place and they were declared hostile and were cross-examined but nothing contrary to their version in the examination-in-chief appear to have been brought on record on the basis of which it can be concluded that they were deposing falsely or whatever was mentioned in the complaint is true narration of the facts. No doubt, the medical certificate which is produced on record and admitted on behalf of accused and marked as Exh.10 shows that when he was referred for medical examination on 23.03.2013 by Shantinagar police station, P.W. Parvez Mohammad Hasan Ansari was found to have sustained injuries as mentioned in the certificate. The aspect .. 5 .. Special Case No.31/2013 Judgment that the said injuries were caused to him by the present accused is material which, as mentioned above, has not been even stated by either the complainant or her brother i.e. injured. Even so far as the incident of the accused accosting the complainant on her way to her parental aunt's house and both the accused one after another outraging her modesty also not corroborated by the complainant herself and even the police official who recorded her complaint also is not examined by the prosecution. Therefore, the fact that such complaint was lodged by the complainant with such allegations itself cannot be said to have been established. Therefore, even though from the copy of school leaving certificate produced on record at Exh.11 (exhibited on admission) the age of the girl is seen to be below 18 years, in absence of evidence in regard to the allegations of outraging modesty of the girl by the accused persons, no conclusion in regard to guilt or the accused can be arrived at. It has also to be mentioned that under section 29 of P.O.C.S.O. Act it is provided that ''Where a person is prosecuted for committing or abetting or attempting to commit any offence under sections 3, 5, 7 and 9 of this Act, the special Court shall presume that such person has committed or abetted or attempted to commit the offence, as the case may be, unless the contrary is proved''. But then it has to be mentioned though the complainant made allegations in the complaint, in their evidence before Court the complainant or the witness had not supported the allegations against the accused and in such circumstances when the accused has come up with specific defence of total denial, I am of the view that when the basic requirement of the prosecution in establishing the allegations by cogent and reliable evidence is not fulfilled, there is no question of raising presumption under section 29 of the P.O.C.S.O. Act. Point no.1 and 2 are therefore answered in the negative. 10] In view of above discussion it has to be held that the prosecution has failed to establish the guilt of the accused beyond all the .. 6 .. Special Case No.31/2013 Judgment reasonable doubt and the accused are entitled to be acquitted. Point no.3 is answered accordingly. 11] Since the accused are acquitted, it is necessary that they be directed to furnish P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/- [rupees fifteen thousand only] in the like amount under section 437A of Cr.P.C. to appear before the higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect of any appeal or petition, if any, filed against the judgment and that such bail bond shall be in force for six months. In the result I pass the following order - ORDER Accused Akbar Munsharif Ansari and Asagar Munsharif Ansari are acquitted of the charge for offence punishable under section 354, 323 read with section 34 of I.P.C. and section 3, 4, 7 and 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 2) Bail bonds of both accused stand cancelled and sureties are discharged. 3) Both accused P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/- [rupees fifteen thousand only] each with one surety in the like amount under section 437A of Cr.P.C. to appear before the higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect of any appeal or petition, if any filed against the judgment and that such bail bond shall be in force for six months. 4) No muddemal article is seen to be submitted to the Court. Hence, no order in respect of its disposal is passed. 5) The proceeding is closed. Date : 20.03.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.

Offence is not punishable with death or imprisonment for life, --2-- CRI. BAIL APPLI. NO.1583/2018 therefore, applicant prayed for bail. 4. Investigating Officer has given his say at Exh.3. CNR NO.MHTH01­004317­2018 1 A.B.A.1588/2018 ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN ANTI. BAIL APPLICATIOIN No.1588/2018 (CNR No. MHTH01­004317­2018) 1] The applicant Mahendra Gupta has filed this application for grant of anticipatory bail u/s.438 of Cr.P.C. in C.R.No.I­178/2018 registered at Bhayander Police Station U/Section­377, 324, 323, 504 of I.P. Code and u/s.4, 8 and 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. 2] Brief facts of the prosecution case are as under:­ Complainant Bhanmati Prajapati lodged complaint to police station Bhayander on 05/05/2018. As per this complaint, she was residing on given address at Bhayander and hr husband was working as driver. On 04/05/2018 at about 8.00 p.m. her minor son came home and he was frightened and he disclosed that he had gone to his neighbour Dhiraj Gupta to watch TV and that time, accused committed carnal intercourse with him. Th complainant went to the house of Dhiraj Gupta to meet his parents but there was no present. Then her husband came back and she narrated the incident. But they again went to house of Dhiraj Gupta but they were not present. On 05/05/2018 at 7.00 a.m. they again went and met parents of Dhiraj Gupta, they were not listening anything. Anticipatory Bail Appln. 1627/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exhibit 1 in Anticipatory bail application no.1627/2015 This application is filed by the applicants/accused namely Shivram Shridhar Shetty and Dinesh Sanjeeva Shetty for their release on bail under section 438 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. II- 44/2015 registered at Kashimira police station for offence punishable under section 366A, 370(3), 372 of I.P.C. and section 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 of Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act (hereinafter in short referred to as I.T.P.A.) and also under section 16, 17 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act (hereinafter in short referred to as P.O.C.S.O. Act). It was contended and argued that the applicant no.1 is running K-Night Bar at Mira Road since about 5 to 6 months and the applicant no.2 has been working as a manager in other bar and restaurant named Shivali Garden Bar and Restaurant at Mira Road and that they are associated with various social welfare activities in Mira Road and Bhayander and having no criminal antecedents to their discredit and they hail from respectable family and also having good reputation and image in the society. 2] It was also contended and argued that the applicants have been shown as wanted accused in the above crime with the allegation that the girls for prostitution have been supplied on demand by K-Night Bar to neighbouring lodge and on such intimation a raid was conducted at Panchratna Lodge and two major girls namely Anjali Guhariya and Puja Bhantu were arrested. It is also contended and argued that raid was not effected in the bar of the applicant no.1 and applicants have no connection with said lodge where raid was effected. It was submitted that even it is not the case of the prosecution that the girls were sent from K-Night Bar on that particular day. It was also submitted that the applicants are falsely implicated in the crime only because applicant no.1 has been running said K-Night Bar. It was also pointed out that 13 girls found in the bar were the employees of said bar and they have no connection with the offence alleged. It was also contended and argued that when the girls were sent for medical examination they were reported to be aged .. 2 .. Anticipatory Bail Appln. 1627/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) between 17 to 18 years and therefore it was argued that considering the margin of error in regard to age determination on the basis of medical evidence they cannot be said to be minor and provisions of P.O.C.S.O. Act cannot be attracted. Reliance was placed on various rulings with which I will discuss at its proper place. It is argued that there is absolutely no material showing involvement of the applicants in the crime and the applicant no.1 was only running bar and had taken it for running on contract and the applicant no.2 has absolutely no connection with the bar in question. It was also contended and argued that they are ready to abide by any condition and co-operate police in investigation. It was also pointed out that the accused who have been arrested at the spot have already been released on bail by the learned Magistrate and other accused also is released on bail and they both being employees of the applicant have been removed from the job. It was also pointed out that from the statement of the girl it is clear that they went to Panchratna Lodge as per their own wish and they were not stated to have been forced to go there. It is further argued that there is no direct evidence against the accused and the case is based on circumstantial evidence and when two possibilities are there, one which is favourable to the accused need to be accepted and the applicants are required to be held as not involved in the crime. It was therefore argued that the applicants are apprehending arrest and they are entitled to be released on anticipatory bail. 3] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply at Exhibit 7 and it was contended and argued that on receipt of information from the sources a raid was conducted and the accused who have been arrested were caught on the spot at Panchratna Lodging and Boarding. It was also contended and argued that the applicant no.1 has taken said K-Night Bar for running by agreement and as per statement of the girls caught at the time of raid both the applicants have been the owner and conducting the bar and they were appointed as women waiter in K-Night Bar and the girls for prostitution were provided from K-Night Bar and at the relevant time girls were sent from K-Night Bar for prostitution and the conductor of .. 3 .. Anticipatory Bail Appln. 1627/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) the bar as well as staff members of the bar have been utilizing the money earned from such prostitution business. It was contended and argued that the applicants are the persons who have been running said K-Night Bar and when it is there on record that the girls were provided for prostitution from said K-Night Bar they cannot escape from the responsibility. It was also pointed out that the girls have been enticed by the applicants and their employees to indulge into prostitution and further investigation in the crime with the help of applicants is necessary. It was also contended and argued that other absconding accused in the present crime are also to be arrested and if the applicants are released on anticipatory bail, that may hamper the investigation. It was further contended and argued that for all above reasons the application is liable to be rejected. 4] As is clear the offences alleged against the applicants/ accused are of very serious nature under section 366A, 370(3), 372 of I.P.C. and section 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 of I.T.P.A. and also under section 16, 17 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. As is further clear, as per version of the applicants in the application itself the applicant no.1 had taken the K-Night Bar for running on agreement. Then, though it is contended that the applicant no.2 has no connection with the said bar and he has been working in as a manager in another Lodge, from the perusal of papers of investigation and statements of witnesses, particularly the girls who were working in the said bar and even the victim girls it appears that they stated that both the applicants were the owners as per their version and they have been conducting the bar and in such circumstances it would be premature to conclude that the applicant no.2 has no connection with K-Night Bar. Even as per prosecution case the girls were provided for prostitution business from K-Night Bar and they were sent to other lodges including Panchratna Lodge. In the light of that if the F.I.R. and the investigation papers are perused, it is clear that initially the punter and panch witness had been to K-Night Bar and from there they were sent to Panchratna Lodge. .. 4 .. Anticipatory Bail Appln. 1627/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) 5] Then, though, as has been argued on behalf of applicant/accused that, it is not there in the F.I.R. or panchnama that even the girls who were caught in Panchratna Lodge were seen coming out from K-Night Bar and going to Panchratna Lodge, merely on that basis the entire prosecution case that the girls were being provided from K-Night Bar and were sent to other lodges for prostitution business cannot be disbelieved at this stage. 6] It is also material to mention that from the perusal of the statements of the witnesses recorded during investigation very specific statement appear to have been made by said witnesses that the girls were being provided from K-Night Bar and in the light of that when the panch and punter went to K-Night Bar, and then from there they were stated to have been directed to go to Panchratna Lodge and accordingly they went there and in the raid the girls were fund indulging in prostitution business, such submissions on behalf of applicant at this stage cannot be said to be appealing and convincing. 7] Then, even so far as the submission on behalf of applicants that both the girls were reported to 17 to 18 years old as per medical examination and therefore possibility of the girls being major is there considering margin of error in regard to age determined on the basis of medical evidence is concerned, no doubt in the ruling cited on behalf of applicants in case of Jaya Mala vs. Home Secretary, Government of J. and K. and others reported in 1982 CRI.L.J. 1777(1) it is observed that according to medical jurisprudence error in age ascertained on the basis of radiological examination is two years, plus or minus, on either side and in another ruling in case of Balasaheb vs. The State of Maharashtra reported in 1994 CRI.L.J. 3044 it is observed that according to medical jurisprudence error in case of age based on ossification test may of + three years. But then, it is also to be mentioned that the medical examination is done only to ascertain prima facie apparent age of the girls and the investigation is still in progress and it is for the investigating agency to collect evidence in regard to exact age of .. 5 .. Anticipatory Bail Appln. 1627/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) the girls and therefore it cannot be concluded at this stage that the girls are major. Then, even taking into consideration the margin of error in the age determined on the basis of medical examination, the possibility of the girls being below 17 years or 16 years of age also is there and in that regard the investigating agency must be given an opportunity to further investigate into the matter to collect evidence in regard to exact age of the girls and it would be premature to conclude at this stage that the girls are major and provisions of P.O.C.S.O. Act are not attracted. For the same reason the ruling cited on behalf of applicants in case of Suresh Dadarao Kapse vs. State of Maharashtra and another reported in 2004 ALL MR (Cri) 138 wherein it is observed that where on the evidence two possibilities are open, one which goes in favour of prosecution and another benefits accused, the accused is entitled to benefit of doubt, also cannot be said to be of much use to the applicants since it is not the stage where guilt or otherwise of the accused is to be decided. 8] Then, it is well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be gone into detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether release of the applicants would hamper the process of investigation or whether the applicants would abscond if released on bail and so far the claim of anticipatory bail is concerned, the important and material aspect is whether the custodial interrogation of the applicant is necessary. In the light of that if the facts of the present case are considered, it is very much clear from the papers of investigation that actual raid was effected and from statements of the victim girls or even other girls working in the hotel, the applicants are revealed to be the persons who were conducting the business in said K-Night Bar and they are even referred to as owner of the said bar. In such circumstances it is difficult to believe at this stage that they were not knowing about the activities going on in their hotel. Even the submission on behalf of applicants that names of the girls who are caught is not there in the list of the employees of the hotel and therefore involvement of the applicants is not there in this crime etc. is concerned, also it is to be .. 6 .. Anticipatory Bail Appln. 1627/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) mentioned that as per prosecution case the accused were supplying girls for prostitution from their K-Night Bar and sending the girls to other lodges and therefore it is not necessary that said girls would be there on the pay-roll or list of employees of the said bar. Even it is to be mentioned that if any such activities are carried out in said bar involving some girls, it is not even expected that names of the girls would be thee in the pay-roll or list of employees. 9] It is also to be mentioned that very serious allegations are there against the applicants that they have been supplying girls major as well as minor to other lodges for prostitution and detail investigation into the matter is required to be done with the help of accused. Therefore, the submission on behalf of prosecution that custodial interrogation of the applicants is very much necessary appear to be appealing and convincing. 10] Even in the light of the fact that other co-accused are also to be traced and arrested and their names revealed in the investigation and it is specifically mentioned in the F.I.R.. that the girls are provided from K-night Bar and the applicants are seen to be the persons running said K-Night Bar, it cannot be said that there is no material prima facie showing their involvement in this crime and therefore merely because the applicants were not present at the time of raid or merely because their names are not mentioned in the F.I.R. the submission on behalf of applicants that their involvement in the crime is not clear also is not appealing and convincing. 11] Even so far as the submission that other accused released on bail and the applicants are entitled to be released on bail on the ground of parity also it has to be mentioned that they were caught at the spot at the time of raid and they were employees of the applicants and even as per version of the complainant they have been removed from job. In such circumstance they being only employees of the present applicants and their role was limited and only because they are now released on bail after their police custody and sufficient .. 7 .. Anticipatory Bail Appln. 1627/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Magisterial custody, the present applicants who are not arrested cannot claim bail on the ground of parity; rather the present applicants since stated to be the owner / conducting the business in the K-Night Bar, must be having detail information and for the purpose of investigation their custody appear to be necessary. 12] In the light of above discussion and in view of serious allegations against the applicants, I am of the view that further investigation into the matter with the help of applicants is necessary and this is not a fit case wherein the applicants can be released on anticipatory bail. In the result I pass the following order - ORDER The application is rejected. Date : 17.07.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Additional Sessions Judge-1, Thane.

.. 1 .. bail no.1632/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 1632/2015 This application is filed by applicants namely Rakesh Remeshwar Yadav and Shankar Kukara Shetty for their release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no.II-44/2015 registered at Kashimira police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 366A, 370(3), 372 of I.P.C. and section 16, 17 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act and also section 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 of I.T.P.A. with the allegation that they were conducting prostitution business by compelling victim girls to give sexual pleasure to customers in exchange of money, it is specifically contended on behalf of applicants that they are serving in said KNight Bar and were working as cashier and Lodge manager respectively in said bar and they have no concern with any illegal activity being conducted there and they are falsely implicated in this crime on suspicion. In the light such specific contention, the allegations that the accused were conducting prostitution business in KNight Bar will have to be proved on merits after trial. .. 3 .. bail no.1632/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) 4] Then, it is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicants would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicants tampering with prosecution evidence if they are released on bail. In that respect it is contended by the applicants that they are permanent residents of the address given and they will not abscond if released on bail and that they are ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 5] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicants/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 6] Then, it has also to be mentioned that though the investigation in the matter is stated to be in progress, it will take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge-sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicants/accused in jail for uncertain period. 7] Then, other accused persons are stated to have been ordered to be released on bail by the Court of J.M.F.C. and on .. 4 .. bail no.1632/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) the ground of parity the present applicants are also entitled to be released on bail. 8] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicants can be released on bail. Charegsheet is filed against first accused and he has been released on bail, therefore, ground of parity be given. The applicant is permanent resident. She is having children and grand child. She is sick and old suffering from diabetes and B.P, therefore, she prayed for bail. 3. Investigating Officer has given his report at Exh.4. It is contended that the informant had lodged FIR in NRI Sagari police station in the year 2014. The accused no.1 was arrested on 18.08.2014 and he has been released on bail. The present accused was arrested on 27.06.2017. 4. The facts of the case as per police papers are that:­ The informant is serving in BARC. The accused NO.1 Sanjay is the husband of informant and two victims aged 11 and 6 years are the daughters of the informant and accused --2-- no.1. There was family dispute between the informant and accused no.1 and therefore, they were residing separately. The present accused Pramodini was baby sitter working at the house of informant. 5. It is alleged that both the accused in furtherance of their common intention committed sexual assault, penetrative sexual assault upon the minor girls and they have threatened the victims to kill them and they have also given burn injuries to them. The statement of victims have been recorded. Investigation of this accused is going on. If she is released on bail she is likely to tamper the prosecution witnesses and will jump on bail. Ms.A.B. Arote, Advocate for the accused. 2 JUDGMENT ( Delivered on 20th day of June, 2018 ) 1) Accused Babulal Sana Gohil is charge sheeted by Police Station Shantinagar, Bhiwandi on 24/07/2014 for having committed an offence punishable under sections 376 of the Indian Penal Code and under Sections 3, 4, 5(l) & 5(n) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (POCSO Act) on the report of informant Bhavna Babulal Gohil (P.W.1), mother of Victim. 2) Prosecution case, briefly stated, is that informant Bhavna (P.W.1) and Rekha (P.W.2) are real sisters.
