On 24/04/2014 at about 12.00 noon accused Babulal came to the house of Raju Parmar and insisted informant Bhavna to send Victim along with him at Bhiwandi and upon her refusal assaulted and beaten and therefore, N.C. was registered against the accused Babulal in this regard. 3 Spl. Case (POCSO) No.149/2014 Judg.Exh. CNR No.MHTH01­004348­2014 5) On 24/04/2014 when informant Bhavna (P.W.1) and Rekha (P.W.2) inquired with Victim, she disclosed that since one year accused Babulal was committing forcible sexual intercourse with her under threat that if she tells to anybody then her mother and step brothers would be killed. Victim therefore, kept quiet. Upon this disclosure, informant Bhavna rushed to the police station and lodged report Exh.8 and thereby offence vide C.R.No. 116/2014 under Section 376 of I.P.C. and Sec, 3, 4, 5(l) & 5(n) of POCSO Act, 2012 was registered. 6) Upon report, investigation was geared up. I.O. A.P.I. Sopan Nangare (P.W.5) has carried out investigation. statements of witnesses were recorded. Statement of Victim girl was recorded. The medical examination of Victim was carried out. Spot panchanama was drawn. N.C. against the accused Babulal was collected. Birth certificate of Victim was collected which disclosed her birth date as 29/07/2001. C.A. report was collected. After investigation charge­sheet was filed. 7) My Ld. Predecessor Mr. H.M. Patwardhan, 7th Additional Sessions Judge, Thane has framed charge against vide Exh. 4 on 29/07/2015 against accused for having committed an offence punishable under sections 376 of the Indian Penal Code and Sec, 3, 4, 5(l) & 5(n)of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. The contents of charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 4 8) The oral evidence of prosecution consists of informant Bhavna Babulal Gohil (PW1) at Exh.7, Rekha Raju Parmar (PW2) at Exh.16, the Victim girl (PW3) at Exh.20, Medical Officer Dr. Amol Prabhakar Bidkar (PW4) at Exh.23 and Investigating Officer A.P.I. Sopan Abasaheb Nangare (PW5) at Exh.30. 9) Documentary evidence of prosecution consists of informant Bhavna's report at Exh.8, medical examination report of Victim at Exh.24, N.C. report against accused at Exh.32, birth certificate of Victim at Exh.33 and C.A. report at Exh. 34. Prosecution closed evidence by pursis at Exh.35. 10) The evidence of Victim (P.W.3) disclosed that Babulal is her step father and she was residing along with him and informant Bhavna who is her real mother. Her evidence clearly discloses that when she had been to her maternal uncle's house at Kalyan, accused Babulal approached them and insisted her to come to home but she refused therefore, he beat her. She refused to go with her father accused Babulal because he was ravishing her. Her evidence also revealed that accused Babulal has raped her many times in absence of informant Bhavna, her mother, and this continued for one year and Victim did not disclose to her mother Bhavna because the accused was threatening to kill her mother and brothers. The Victim informed these facts to her mother and maternal aunt Rekha stating that lastly the accused raped her on 18/04/2014. 11) The evidence of informant Bhavna (P.W.1) and Rekha (P.W.2) revealed that when informant Bhavna was in the house of 5 Spl. Case (POCSO) No.149/2014 Judg.Exh. CNR No.MHTH01­004348­2014 Rekha for stay, accused Babulal insisted on 24/4/2014 for sending Victim with him. But on refusal, he has abused, assaulted, beaten and thereafter ran away. Their evidence reveal that when they inquired with Victim in this regard and Victim has disclosed that she was continuously raped by the accused Babulal and therefore, she denied to accompany him and report came to be lodged at Exh.8. 12) Medical Officer Dr. Amol (P.W.4) has examined Victim on 26/04/2014 and prepared medical examination report at Exh.24 and the same disclosed that there was old hymen tear and her vagina was patulous and there wasn't fresh injury. 13) I.O. A.P.I. Sopan (P.W.5) carried out entire investigation. He has drawn spot and seizure panchanama besides collected the documents in the form of N.C. report at Exh.22, birth certificate of Victim at Exh.32, C.A. report Exh.32 and submitted charge­sheet. 14) As against this, accused did not adduce the evidence in defence but nevertheless contended that false case is filed because he declined to provide money to informant Bhavna's parental home and that her maternal brother­in­law i.e. husband of Rekha (P.W.3) wanted to force Victim to prostitution and by that time informant Bhavna committed suicide. 15) I have heard Mr. S.D.Londhe, Ld. A.P.P. for the prosecution and Ms. A.B.Arote, ld. Advocate for the accused. Appraised the entire material on record. 16) Mr. Londhe submitted that prosecution has proved the guilt against the accused beyond all reasonable doubt. Mr. Londhe 6 submitted that nothing is surfaced on record as to why Victim should be disbelieved in respect of sexual assault. Mr. Londhe submitted that Victim has disclosed reason as to why she could not disclose to her parents at earliest point of time. Mr. Londhe submitted that the insistence of accused Babulal to take Victim forcibly to home on 24/04/2014 revealed his intention which he realized since one year and thereby urged for conviction. It may be mentioned that written notes of argument at Exh.39 has submitted for complainant. 17) Ms. Arote taking through the written notes of argument at Exh.37 submitted the failure of prosecution to prove the guilt of accused beyond all reasonable doubt. Ms. Arote submitted that all witnesses are related and interested. Ms. Arote submitted that there is delay in lodging the report and defence is probable. Ms. Arote relied upon Tulia Kali V/s. State of Tamilnadu (AIR 1973 S.C. 501) to substantiate her submission. 18) Having regard to the submissions advanced at bar and after appraisal of entire material on record, I find merit in the submission of Mr. Londhe and demerit in the submission of Ms. Arote. Accordingly, following points arise for my consideration and determination and I record my findings against each of points as under. ­ 7 Spl. Case (POCSO) No.149/2014 Judg.Exh. CNR No.MHTH01­004348­2014 POINTS FINDINGS 1) Does the prosecution prove that accused ... In the Babulal has repeatedly committed rape affirmative. on Victim (P.W.3) aged about 14 years since one year prior to 18/04/2014 ? 2) Does the prosecution prove that accused ... In the has repeatedly committed aggravated affirmative. penetrative sexual assault on the Victim (P.W.3) aged about 14 years since one year prior to 18/04/2014 ? 3) What order ? ... Accused is convicted. REASONS 19) Points No. 1 & 2 :­ These points are interlinked and therefore, taken up together for reasoning and finding. 20) At the outset, I may state facts which are either clearly proved from the evidence on record or established for want of denial. Informant Bhavna (PW1) and Rekha (PW2) are real sisters. Informant Bhavna (PW1) got married with deceased Himmat in 1999 and Himmat died in 2008. Accused Babulal is second husband of informant Bhavna (PW1). Victim (PW3) is daughter of informant Bhavna (PW1) from her first husband deceased Himmat. Victim (PW3) is aged about 14 years having her birth date 29/07/2001. 21) The evidence of Victim (PW3) is self­sufficient and omnipotent. The evidence is crustal clear. The evidence can be seen vividly. Unequivocally Victim has deposed that accused 8 Babulal being her step father has raped her for about one year and because of fear and threat given by him, she could not disclose to anybody. Nothing to discard her evidence. Victim's evidence is unshaken in the cross­examination. Nothing is emerged in the cross­examination of the Victim as to why she should depose false against accused Babulal. The probable defence suggested by the accused Babulal to her in the cross­examination that she is deposing on the say of mother informant Bhavna (PW1) is denied by her. Victim also denied in the cross­examination that she had any concern with Vijay Parmar. Accused Babulal did not bring any evidence either through cross­examination or otherwise to establish connectivity between the Victim and Vijay Parmar. It is therefore, I find the evidence of Victim is worth reliable and nothing to discard. It establishes connectivity between the accused Babulal and aggravated penetrative sexual assault on Victim. 22) Informant Bhavna (PW1) and Rekha (PW2) are real sisters. Victim made disclosure in respect of repeated sexual assault on her to her mother Bhavna (PW1)and maternal aunt Rekha (PW2). Her conduct in disclosing regarding rape to her mother and maternal aunt is natural. Nothing is surfaced on record as to why both informant Bhavna (PW1) and Rekha (PW2) should depose against accused Babulal. In fact, accused Babulal is husband of informant Bhavna. Mere relation is not sufficient to discard the testimony when otherwise it is reliable. 23) Informant Bhavna (PW1) was cross­examined on the line that because she wanted to hide relation between Victim and Vijay 9 Spl. Case (POCSO) No.149/2014 Judg.Exh. CNR No.MHTH01­004348­2014 Parmar, false complaint is filed, but it is denied. Informant Bhavna was also suggested in the cross­examination that accused Babulal was not providing money to her parental home and therefore, false report is filed, but it is denied. In fact, informant Bhavna's brother does not require any financial assistance from the accused Babulal for simple reason that Raju i.e. husband of Rekha (PW2) was working in KDMC. So the cross­examination to informant Bhavna (PW1) in this regard is baseless and without foundation. Above all, why mother should file totally false case against her husband merely because he did not provide some economical assistance to her parental home. 24) Rekha (PW2) was cross­examined on the line that she and her husband hatched plan to falsely implicate accused Babulal but without any basis. Rekha (PW2) has no grievance against the accused Babulal. There wasn't animosity. In that sense, she is the independent witness. 25) Thus, I find informant Bhavna (PW1) and Rekha (PW2) are the natural and best witnesses in whose presence the incident dated 23/04/2014 was occurred where accused Babulal insisted Victim (PW3) to accompany him but she was not sent and thereby he made hue and cry by assaulting Victim. In this regard, N.C. at Exh. 32 came to be lodged against accused Babulal with Bazarpeth police station. The conduct of the accused Babulal at the relevant time, his aggravation and his violence is clearly established by N.C. Exh.32. 10 26) Medical Officer Dr. Amol (PW4) had examined the Victim (PW3) at earliest point of time and found that there is old tear in the hymen. As such, his testimony at Exh. 23 substantially corroborate the testimony of Victim. 27) Investigating Officer A.P.I. Sopan (PW5) has carried out investigation including the spot panchanama and collected birth certificate at Exh.33. The entire evidence of Investigating Officer API Sopan went unchallenged on the point of birth certificate and the age of the Victim. 28) I must observe there isn't delay in lodging the report. It is surfaced on record that the accused Babulal was raping the Victim since one year but she was unable to disclose because she was threatened and that threat was to kill her brother and mother. The evidence appeared to be very much natural in this regard. Anybody at such age group would be under severe fear to disclose anything because she herself would be falsified and disbelieved by her parents and relatives, if such disclosure is made. Hence many a time, victim of sexual assault are under severe fear and anxiety in respect of disclosure rather do not disclose unless circumstances compelled. 29) It has vividly surfaced on record that on 23/04/2014 disclosure was made because of violent behaviour of accused Babulal with Victim girl. Immediately thereafter informant Bhavna (PW1) approached police station and lodged report. So the report is lodged at the earliest point of time so as to explain as to why 11 Spl. Case (POCSO) No.149/2014 Judg.Exh. CNR No.MHTH01­004348­2014 delay caused. Besides, parent think hundred times before lodging the report regarding rape on their child because of social pressure and defamation even if the incident is true. Parent also think that such disclosure would defame their family and child would be deprived of her future including matrimonial life. 30) Thus, in this way the prosecution has clearly established from the evidence on record that accused Babulal being the step father of Victim has repeatedly committed rape and aggravated penetrative sexual assault for about one year on her, who was about 14 years. It is fit case where presumption under Sec. 29 of POCSO Act can be drawn against the accused Babulal and the same is not rebutted by accused Babulal. Not only that there is more than sufficient material to raise the presumption in respect of culpable mental state of accused Babulal under Sec. 30 of POCSO Act because whenever informant Bhavna (PW1) was out of house, accused Babulal was committing rape on the Victim girl. This presumption is also not rebutted. 31) To conclude, prosecution has proved beyond all reasonable doubt that the accused Babulal being the step father of Victim had repeatedly committed rape and aggravated penetrative sexual assault for about one year on her when she was aged about 14 years that is to say below 16 years being child and thereby guilty of offence punishable under Sec. 376 of I.P.C., 3,4,5(1) and 5(n) of the POCSO Act. Needless to mention that the consent of Victim being is irrelevant. Accused therefore, stands convicted and liable to be sentenced. Accordingly, I proceed to hear the accused on the 12 point of sentence. ( R. V. Jatale ) Thane. Additional Sessions Judge Date : 20/06/2018. & Special Judge (POCSO Act), Thane. 32) I have heard accused Babulal, Ms. Arote and Mr. Londhe on the point of sentence. 33) Accused Babulal and Ms. Arote submitted for leniency on the ground that accused Babulal has small three children and nobody is there to look after them, accused Babulal is in jail since four years and set off may be given to him. 34) Mr. Londhe submitted that offence is serious, offence is against women and therefore, sought stringent sentence. 35) Having regard to the submissions advanced at bar and after appraisal of entire material on record, I find that the offence committed by the accused is heinous, serious, grievous, inhuman, touches to the conscience of mankind and in any case does not deserve for special leniency. Such offences are increasing day­by­ day. The worst thing is that those who are near and dear of the child are committing such offences. In the case in hand, accused being a step father has committed rape for about one year. It is a permanent blot on Victim and on her family. It is a permanent scar on the mind and soul of the Victim. Because of ill­deed of accused Babulal, Victim has been lowered in the eyes of society and relatives. Victim has to rise above and has to face the mental and 13 Spl. Case (POCSO) No.149/2014 Judg.Exh. CNR No.MHTH01­004348­2014 psychological trauma throughout the life. 36] Undoubtedly the offence of rape is grievous by nature itself. It is more so when perpetrator is the father of Victim and it becomes rarest of rare case and therefore, warrant strong and deterrent sentence to as to give apt message to the prospective offender and lesson to the perpetrator himself. In the case at hand, accused Babulal is the step father of the Victim, who is a child. The sentence must go hand in hand with the gravity of offence. It is then only will meet the ends of justice. 37] The offence under Sec. 376 of I.P.C. is punishable with imprisonment for a term not less than 7 years and it may extend to 10 years but which may be for life and fine. Likewise, offence under Section 3, 4 r/w. Sec. 5(l), 5(n) of POCSO Act, 2012 is punishable with rigorous imprisonment for a term not less than 10 years but which may extend to imprisonment for life and shall also be liable to fine. From this, the intention of the legislature is crystal clear that the perpetrator of the offence of rape in such conditions and circumstances should be dealt with sternly. There isn't circumstance either surfaced on the record through the cross­ examination or otherwise to show leniency to accused Babulal. 38) In view of the observation regarding the gravity of the offence and suffering of the Victim, accused stands convicted for the offence punishable under Sec. 376 of I.P.C. and under Sec. 3, 4, 5(l) & 5(n) of POCSO Act and thereby cumulatively sentenced to rigorous imprisonment of ten (10) years and fine of Rs. 10,000/­ 14 i/d. rigorous imprisonment for two (2) years and that will meet the ends of justice. 39) Now coming to Sec. 357­A of Cr.P.C., under Sec. 33(8) of POCSO Act and Rule 7 of POCSO Rule. As observed above, it is a blot and scar on the soul and mind of Victim. The entire life of Victim is ruined. By no stretch of imagination, it can be compensated in terms of money. It is constitutional mandate of the State that it shall protect life, liberty and property of every person within the territory of India. Not only that, it should be protected but in case of violation, people should be compensated justly, fairly and reasonably. In this backdrop, I deem it fit that this matter should be referred for just, fair and reasonable compensation to the District Legal Services Authority, Thane and the District Magistrate, Thane for necessary action. 40) Perusal of record clearly reveal that muddemal property vide M.E.No. 45/2016 is in the nature of worthless clothes and same is liable to be destroyed. 41) In view of reasons and findings stated supra, the prosecution has proved the guilt of the accused under Sec. 376 of I.P.C. and Sec. 3, 4, 5(l) and 5(n) of POCSO Act, 2012 and that accused stands convicted and sentenced. Accordingly, I proceed to pass following order. ORDER 1) UTP Babulal Sana Gohil is convicted under Section 15 Spl. Case (POCSO) No.149/2014 Judg.Exh. CNR No.MHTH01­004348­2014 235 (2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for the offence punishable under section 376 of the Indian Penal Code and under Sec. 3, 4, 5(l), 5(n) of POCSO Act, 2012 and thereby sentenced cumulatively to Rigorous Imprisonment for 10 years and fine of Rs. 10,000/­ (Rs. Ten Thousand) i/d. R.I. for two [2] years. 2) Accused Babulal is arrested on 26/04/2014 and therefore, he is entitled for set off since then under Sec. 428 of Cr.P.C. 3) A sum of Rs. 8,000/­(Rupees Eight Thousand only) be paid to the Victim (PW3) out of fine amount recovered towards compensation. 4) Muddemal vide M.E.No. 45/2016 being worthless clothes shall be destroyed after appeal period is over but in accordance with Criminal manual. 5) Copy of Judgment and Order shall be supplied free of cost to the accused Babulal and Victim (PW3). 6) Copy of Judgment and Order be forwarded with complements to the District Legal Services Authority, Thane and the District Magistrate, Thane for disbursing just, reasonable and fair compensation to the Victim (PW3). 7) P. & D. in the court. ( R. V. Jatale ) Thane. Additional Sessions Judge Date : 20/06/2018. & Special Judge (POCSO Act), Thane. 16 17 Spl. Case (POCSO) No.149/2014 Judg.Exh. CNR No.MHTH01­004348­2014

It is contended that the incident appears to be after thought and false. There is delay of 4 to 5 hours for lodging the FIR. The applicant is poor. His family residing at Utter Pradesh. He alone resided at Mumbra. There is nothing to recover from him. Therefore, applicant prayed for bail. 3. Investigating Officer has objected for bail by filing his say at Exh.4. 4. I heard Ld. In fact, the victim and the applicant are not talking with each other and they always used to quarrel and therefore, she has made such allegations. It is submitted that the investigation is almost completed and therefore, no purpose will be served to detain the applicant behind the bar. Nothing is seized from the applicant. The victim's statement under section 164 of Cr. P.C., is recorded, therefore, the custody of the present applicant is not necessary. The offence is not punishable with death or imprisonment for life, therefore, he has prayed for bail. 3. The applicant has produced copy of FIR, remand reports, his Adhar Card, School Leaving Certificate and ration card. 4. Investigating Officer has given his say at Exh.4. He has strongly objected for the bail on the ground that since last five years when the victim was 12 years old the accused threatened, quarrel, beat the victim and he used to sexually harassed the victim. He has touched the breast and body of the victim several times. He has also shown her nude video films and every time the victim had refused to co­operate him and therefore, the accused --2-- has beaten and threatened. Once the accused has cut his wrist with knife as the victim refused to have sexual intercourse with him. After that also the accused threatened and pressurized the victim for co­operating him for sexual intercourse. The victim had disclosed this fact to her parents and the parents had given understanding to the accused many times, but there was no change in his conduct. Investigating Officer has submitted that the victim is not ready to reside with her parents, brother because there is danger to her life and the accused is likely to commit more serious offence with her and therefore, the victim is kept in safe custody. There is no guarantee that he will improve his conduct inspite of his parents had instructed him not to behave like that, but there was no improvement in his conduct. So after release on --3-- bail his conduct will not be improved and he will take disadvantage and will dare to commit more serious offence with respect to the victim as well as with respect to other girls and therefore, the court is of the view that it is not fit case to release the accused on bail. .. 1 .. Bail No. 1647/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1.) Order below Exhibit 1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 1647/2015 This application is filed by applicant Monu Tilak Sharma for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. I-99/2015 registered at Navghar police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 363, 366A of I.P.C. and section 8(c) of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as ''P.O.C.S.O. Act''). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant/accused induced the minor victim girl by giving false assurance of marriage and then kidnapped her and then also sexually assaulted her by touching her breast and other parts of body with sexual intent. It is further contended and argued that no such incident of kidnapping and sexual assault as alleged has happened and the applicant is falsely implicated in this crime merely on suspicion. It is further contended and argued that there was love affair between applicant and the girl and she came with the applicant of her own. It is further submitted that looking to the nature of allegation, further custody of the accused is not required. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co-operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that the applicant/accused and the girl were knowing each other and taking disadvantage of the minor age of the girl, the accused enticed her and then by giving false promise of marriage he kidnapped her and then touched her body and breast with sexual intent. It is further submitted that the accused is .. 2 .. Bail No. 1647/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1.) native of Uttar Pradesh and in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility that the applicant may abscond and may not be available for trial and even possibility of threatening the victim girl and other prosecution witnesses cannot be ruled out. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 363, 366A of I.P.C. and section 8(c) of P.O.C.S.O. Act, the victim girl is stated to be 16 years old and it is contended on behalf of applicant/accused that he has been falsely implicated in this crime with ulterior motive and it is further stated that there was love affair between the accused and the girl and she had of her own left her house and the accused had not kidnapped her nor sexually assaulted her. Even from statement of the girl it is seen that she stated that they were having love affair and wanted to marry and therefore ran away from the house. In such circumstance the aspect as to whether the allegations against the accused are genuine or the contention of the accused that he is falsely implicated is probable, would be the question to be decided on merits. Even nothing is to be recovered from the applicant/accused. 4] Then, it is also stated on behalf of applicant/accused that though the investigation in this matter is in progress, looking to the nature of allegation further custody of the accused is not required in this crime. 5] Then, it is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant .. 3 .. Bail No. 1647/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1.) tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 6] Then, so far as the apprehension is expressed on behalf of prosecution that since the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 7] Then, it has also to be mentioned that though the investigation in the matter is stated to be in progress and even the charge sheet is yet to be submitted, it would take time to complete the investigation and then submit the charge-sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 8] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order - ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Monu Tilak Sharma is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/- [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions - .. 4 .. Bail No. 1647/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1.) The applicant/accused shall attend the concerned police station as and when called for the purpose of investigation/enquiry till filing of the charge-sheet and shall co-operate in investigation. He shall not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and the prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this Court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 30.07.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Additional Sessions Judge-1, Thane.
