.. 1 .. Special Case No. 32/2013 Judgment Received on : 06.08.2013 Registered on : 06.08.2013 Decided on : 30.06.2015 Duration : 1 year 10 months 24 days IN THE COURT OF THE SESSION JUDGE, THANE AT THANE (Presided over by Ms.V.V.Virkar, Additional Session Judge-1, Thane) Special Case No. 32 of 2013 Exhibit No. 38 The State of Maharashtra … Complainant versus Habib Kadar Sayyad … Accused Age 47 years, Resident of room no.48, 2nd floor, Habibi Building, Jeevan Bag, Station road, Mumbra, Tal. and Dist. Thane. Appearance - Mrs. R.A. Navale, learned Additional Public Prosecutor (hereinafter in short A.P.P.) Mrs. Rajesh Kumar, learned advocate for accused. JUDGMENT (Delivered on 30.06.2015) .. 2 .. Special Case No. 32/2013 Judgment The accused stands prosecuted for offences punishable under section 376 of I.P.C. and section 4 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as P.O.C.S.O. Act) for committing penetrative sexual assault on mentally challenged victim girl aged 16 years on 18.05.2013 between 3.30 p.m. to 5.00 p.m. in his house at Habibi Building, second floor, room no.48, Jeevan Bag, Mumbra. 2] In short the facts giving rise to the prosecution of the accused that one Zeenat aged 28 years lodged complaint on 20.05.2013 contending that she is staying at Habibi Building, second floor, room no.50, station road, Mumbra since six months. Victim girl Nehmatunissa aged 16 years is her sister and has been staying with her and she is mentally retarded. It was also contended that she herself as well as her husband used to go for work and the victim girl used to be at home. It is also case of the prosecution that the accused is resident of same building in the neighbourhood of the complainant and has been staying there with her family including daughter Afrin who is friend of the victim girl. It is also further case of the prosecution that on 18.05.2013 when the complainant had been out for her work and the victim girl was alone the accused had caught hold of her hand and took her inside the house, removed his clothes and also her clothes and committed forcible sexual intercourse with her and also had caught hold of her breast as well as back. After the complainant returned home around 5.00 p.m. she noticed that the victim girl was sitting there on the steps of the house .. 3 .. Special Case No. 32/2013 Judgment and was crying and when she asked her as to what happened the victim girl narrated her the incident. It is also further case that the victim girl was having pain and therefore the complainant took her to a lady doctor one Dr. Nikhat Mulani who examined her and stated that she has been raped and directed them to go to police station. The complainant therefore went to police station and lodged complaint on 20.05.2013. 3] On the basis of her complaint offence as per C.R.No. I- 407/2013 for offence under section 376 of I.P.C. and section 4 of P.O.C.S.O. Act was registered and initially the work of investigation was entrusted to P.S.I. Patil and since it was a serious offence, further work of investigation was done by P.I. Nagarkar. During the investigation the victim girl was referred for medical examination to Chhatrapati Shivaji Hospital, Kalwa and since the girl was reported to be minor she was also medically examined for age determination and medical certificates were obtained. Sample of vaginal swab and blood also were obtained. Panchnama of the spot was prepared. Statements of witnesses were recorded. Accused came to be arrested. He was referred for medical examination. Further statements of witnesses including Dr. Nikhat Mulani were recorded. After completion of investigation, since there was sufficient evidence against the accused, he came to be charge-sheeted for offences punishable under section 376 of I.P.C. and section 4 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. .. 4 .. Special Case No. 32/2013 Judgment 4] Since offences under P.O.C.S.O. Act are triable by Special Court, the charge-sheet came to be submitted to this Court. 5] The accused was produced before Court. A charge for offence punishable under section 376 of I.P.C. and section 3 read with section 4 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and section 5(k) read with section 6 of P.O.C.S.O. Act was framed against him as per Exhibit 3. Contents of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. The accused pleaded not guilty. His defence as it revealed from the cross-examination of witnesses and his statement under section 313 of Cr.P.C. was that the accused had given amount of Rs.5,000/- to the complainant for treatment of her husband and on 18.05.2013 there was quarrel between the accused and the complainant on account of said money and that the complainant taking benefit of mentally retardedness of her sister, has made false complaint with false allegation against the accused. He claimed to be tried. 6] For establishing guilt of the accused the prosecution examined complainant Zeenatunissa Sagiruddin Shaikh, P.W.2 victim girl Zeenatunissa, P.W.3 Dr. Ms. Nikhat Husain Mulani who examined the girl initially, Dr. Sonal Choudhary, medical officer who examined the girl at Shivaji Hospital, Kalwa and P.W.5 P.S.I. Amar Patil, I.O. The documentary evidence produced, proved and relied upon by the prosecution was in the form of complaint Exhibit 19, medical certificate Exhibit 26, spot panchnama Exhibit 32. .. 5 .. Special Case No. 32/2013 Judgment 7] Statement of the accused was recorded under section 313 of Cr.P.C. He did not examine himself and had not adduced any defence evidence. 8] I hearned the learned A.P.P. and learned advocate for the accused. 9] On the basis of above facts of the case, the points which arose for my determination, my reasons and findings for the same are as under - Points Findings i) Whether the prosecution proved that the victim girl was having mental disability at the time of incident ? No. ii ) Whether the prosecution proved that on 18.05.2013 between 3.30 p.m. to 5.00 p.m. at his house at room no.48, 2nd floor, Habibi Building Jeevan Bag, Station road, Mumbra, committed rape and sexual assault on the mentally retarded girl by doing forcible sexual intercourse with her ? No. iii ) Whether the prosecution proved that the accused taking disadvantage of mental disability of the victim girl committed penetrative sexual assault No. on her ? iv ) What offence, if any, is proved against No offence is the accused ? proved. v ) What order ? The accused is acquitted. .. 6 .. Special Case No. 32/2013 Judgment REASONS 10] As is clear as per prosecution case victim girl Nehmatunissa is a mentally retarded child and was aged 14 to 15 years at the relevant time and the accused taking disadvantage of her minor age as well as mental disability had committed act of sexual assault by having penetrative sexual intercourse with her. Then, so far as the fact that the victim girl was mentally retarded at the relevant time or that since her birth she was mentally retarded is concerned, it appears that the complainant stated in her evidence that since birth the girl is mentally retarded. Her such version do not appear to have been challenged or disputed on behalf of accused. Even in her cross-examination though she accepted that she had not taken her sister to any doctor and obtained certificate about her mental condition, she clarified that her sister is not mentally ill and she is having less understanding. It is to be mentioned here that the accused is neighbouring person and is of acquaintance with the complainant as well as the girl and that fact do not appear to have been denied or disputed. In the light of that if the fact that it is not specifically suggested to the complainant that the victim girl is not mentally retarded or is not having any problem in understanding assumes importance. It is also to be mentioned that when the girl was examined before Court it was observed that and even such observations are noted down by putting certain questions to the girl and it was noticed that she was found to be not having complete understanding and also was having some pronunciation problem and it was clearly visible that she was having less understanding of the things and it was also noted down and that is in full corroboration to .. 7 .. Special Case No. 32/2013 Judgment the version of the complainant that the girl was having less understanding but was not mentally ill. 11] Then, so far as the fact that after the complaint was lodged the girl was referred for medical examination and medical certificate in regard to her medical examination is concerned, and so far her age is concerned , that fact appear to have been stated by the complainant in her evidence that the victim girl is aged 14 to 15 years and on the day of incident after the girl narrated her about incident she took her to doctor and she was reported to be raped and therefore she took her to police station and lodged complaint as per Exhibit 19 and then the girl was referred for medical examination to Chhatrapati Shivaji Hospital. 12] A careful perusal of the testimony of the complainant reveal that her version that the girl was aged 14 to 15 years at the relevant time also do not appear to have been disputed or challenged. Then, so far as medical evidence is concerned, the investigating officer P.W.5 in his evidence appear to have stated that after the complaint was registered he sent the victim girl and accused for medical examination and obtained their medical certificates. Medical officer Dr. Sonal Choudhary P.W.4 in her evidence stated that on 21.05.2013 when she was on duty as medical officer, one girl Nehmatunissa was brought by police for medical examination with the history of forceful sex with her by neighbour and she had examined the girl and found that hymen of the girl to be torn and ruptured and accordingly she issued certificate as per .. 8 .. Special Case No. 32/2013 Judgment Exhibit 26. Then, a careful perusal of her cross-examination she appear to have accepted that hymen tear can be there by jumping, cycling. Then, though she clarified that that is possible only if there is trauma to the private part, fact is also clear that she accepted that she did not find any injury on the body or private part of the girl. But she appear to have stated in her examination-in-chief that on the basis of her examination of the girl in her opinion there was sufficient evidence that the girl was subjected to sexual intercourse. However, a careful perusal of medical certificate Exhibit 26 reveal that no such opinion appear to have been given by the medical officer. 13] In the light of that if the prosecution case in regard to allegations against the accused of having forceful sexual intercourse with the girl is considered, it is material to mention that as per prosecution case the accused had taken the girl into his house and had forcible sexual intercourse with her. It is also case of the prosecution that immediately sister of the girl had noticed the girl crying and the girl narrated her the incident and the girl was taken to Dr. Nikhat Mulani and Dr. Nikhat Mulani, who is examined as P.W.3, examined the girl and opined that the girl was raped and therefore the girl was taken to police station and complaint was lodged. 14] In that respect though the complainant in her evidence appear to have stated said facts, P.W.3 Dr. Nikhat Mulani who is an independent witness do not appear to have supported the prosecution .. 9 .. Special Case No. 32/2013 Judgment case in that regard. Though she stated that one mentally challenged girl was brought by her sister, she stated that she was brought with complaints of pains in stomach and she had examined the girl only for her complaints of pains in stomach and had given her pain killer and had also stated that she had not stated that the girl was raped and had not given any advice to lodge complaint. As such version of the complainant in that respect is not corroborated by the independent witness P.W.3. Though P.W.3 was declared hostile and was cross- examined on behalf of prosecution at length, nothing could be elicited from her cross-examination on the basis of which it can be inferred that the girl taken to her was the victim girl or even if the girl was the victim girl, on examination she was noticed to be raped by the witness. Though in her cross-examination on behalf of prosecution she initially denied that when the girl was brought for examination with complaints of stomachache, that time sister of the girl told that the girl had been raped and that time she told her that it is a police case and she should be taken to police station. She again clarified by saying that that was not stated by the sister of the girl when she was brought for examination and that was told by the sister of the girl in her next visit and she appear to have of her own explained that. 15] But in any case the prosecution case that the girl was examined by the doctor and the doctor opined that the girl was raped and therefore complainant went to police station and lodged complaint etc. is not at all supported by this witness. Even from the fact that the girl was taken to this witness P.W.3 Dr. Nikhat Mulani .. 10 .. Special Case No. 32/2013 Judgment itself also appear to be doubtful because absolutely no document in that regard appear to have been produced and the doctor has not specified any date or time when the girl had been to her. 16] Then, keeping apart that even if the testimony of the complainant and the victim girl in regard to alleged incident if perused carefully, it appears that as per version of the complainant on the day of incident she had been out for her work and when she returned around 5.00 p.m. she noticed the girl i.e. her sister Nehmatunissa crying and that time she pointed out towards the accused who was standing near the door of his house and stated that father of Afrin i.e. accused, took her inside house and had forcible sexual intercourse with her and she also specified the words alleged to have been used by the girl i.e. viuk ftLe esjs ftLeesa Mkyk But then, careful perusal of the testimony of the girl reveal that she had not described the alleged act of the accused in the words as has been stated by the complainant and she had described the act as father of Afrin had removed her clothes, his own clothes, made her to lie on bed and laid on her and done wrong act and she had stomachache and then her sister took her to doctor madam and doctor madam gave her medicine. 17] As such, there appear variance between testimony of the complainant and the victim girl in regard to actual act alleged to have been committed by the accused and the actual words in which the victim girl described the act. No doubt, such variance in regard to manner in which the act is committed and its nature or the actual .. 11 .. Special Case No. 32/2013 Judgment use of words cannot be given much importance and it is required to be seen as to what is the main purport of the matter and whether said main purport is narrated by the witnesses and whether it inspires confidence in the mind in regard to its truthfulness and correctness. 18] In that regard though, as rightly argued on behalf of prosecution no such false allegations can be made involving character of minor girl and such possibility is not there and unless such incident took place, no such complaint would be lodged with such allegations of sexual assault on minor girl, in that respect also it is to be mentioned that very specific defence is put forth by the accused that there had been quarrel between accused and his wife on one side and the complainant on the other side and it is contended and alleged on behalf of accused that on account of such rivalry the complainant made such false allegations with false contentions in the complaint though no such incident had taken place and also had tutored the victim girl to depose so. 19] In the light of such defence if the testimony of the complainant as well as the girl is perused, it appears that the complainant in her cross-examination denied that there was dispute between herself and accused on account of money and therefore she had lodged false complaint but in next breath she also appear to have stated that it may be that such dispute was there and she had lodged complaint in that regard. But then, it is material to mention that in that regard the victim girl in her cross-examination accepted that there was quarrel taken place between the accused and his wife and .. 12 .. Special Case No. 32/2013 Judgment her sister which on one hand falsifies version of the complainant that there was no such quarrel and on the other hand, support the defence put forth on behalf of accused and there appear some substance in submission on behalf of accused that because of such quarrel and dispute the accused is falsely implicated. Even in the light of that if the cross-examination of the victim girl is perused carefully, it appears that she accepted that she was brought to the Court for deposition by her Apa (sister). She also categorically accepted that Apa told her what to tell in Court. She also further stated in her cross-examination that name of Habib was told to her by Apa. That further support defence put forth by the accused that the girl was tutored one. 20] One more aspect of the matter so far as testimony of the girl is that, as discussed above, the girl was first taken to Dr. Nikhat Mulani and as per complainant's version said doctor reported or opined that the girl was subjected to sexual intercourse and therefore the girl was taken to another doctor and then next day to police station. However, such case put forth by the prosecution is not supported and corroborated by the testimony of Dr. Nikhat Mulani. If at all it was so that doctor had opined that the girl was subjected to sexual assault, there was no reason for her not to state so before Court and though she was cross-examined on behalf of prosecution after she was declared hostile, nothing could be elicited from her in her cross-examination on behalf of prosecution to show that she was not telling true facts. .. 13 .. Special Case No. 32/2013 Judgment 21] Even as rightly pointed out on behalf of accused, the medical certificate of the girl do not support the prosecution case in regard to sexual assault on the girl on the given day, date, time and place and therefore also the aspect that Dr. Nikhat Mulani who reported to have examined the girl at first instance had not noticed any such symptom of sexual assault, is fatal to the prosecution case. Otherwise also version of the complainant and the girl before Court do not appear to be believable or acceptable because if at all the girl who was unmarried was subjected to sexual assault by the accused who was a grown-up man, the girl should have definitely sustained some injury to her private part and that would have reflected at the time of her medical examination. But, as discussed above, the medical evidence is not supporting the prosecution case and therefore the testimony of the complainant in that regard appear to be doubtful and from the cross-examination of the girl said suspicion and doubt is further strengthened because she categorically accepted that she was told by her Apa as to what is to be deposed in Court. 22] One more aspect of the matter in regard to the averments in the complaint as well as testimony of the complainant before Court vis-a-vis testimony of the girl is that in the complaint the complainant has narrated the incident as has been stated by the girl to her in minute details. To be specific, in the complaint it is mentioned that when asked the girl as to what happened, the girl started crying and had pointed out towards the accused who was standing in front of his house and stated that he had caught hold of her hand, removed her chappal and thrown it in the mori (bathroom) .. 14 .. Special Case No. 32/2013 Judgment in the house, removed his own clothes, removed her clothes, made her lie on bed, took out his penis and inserted the same in the place of urination and moved it up and down 10 to 15 times and also had caught hold of her breast and back strongly and had sexual intercourse with her and subjected her to sexual assault. It is unbelievable and unacceptable that the girl aged about 16 years, who is as per version of the complainant was of less understanding, would have really described the act of sexual assault in the manner in which the complainant had described in her complaint. In the light of that if the aspect that the girl stated that she was told by her sister what to depose in the Court is considered, that create strong suspicion and doubt about the truthfulness and correctness of the version of the complainant that the girl had stated her so. In her statement before police nor before court the girl has described said act in said manner and in the light of that even the aspect that the defence of the accused that on account of previous rivalry such false complaint is lodged and even the fact of rivalry is on record, assumes importance. 23] It is also material to mention that there is delay in lodging the F.I.R. which is not satisfactorily explained by the prosecution. It is to be mentioned that the girl is reported to have been assaulted on 18.05.2013 in the afternoon and as per version of the complainant immediately after she returned at about 5.00 p.m. the victim girl had narrated her the incident. But as per her version she has taken the girl to Dr. Nikhat around 10.30 p.m. Then, as per her version she was advised to go to police station but still for no .. 15 .. Special Case No. 32/2013 Judgment satisfactory explanation she had not been to police station immediately or on next day and appear to have gone to police station on third day and her complaint is seen to have been recorded on 20.05.2013 at 7.30 p.m. and such delay is not explained at all, much less satisfactorily explained. It is material to mention that if at all that was so that incident of sexual harassment or assault on the girl, as has been described in the complaint, was disclosed by the girl to the complainant, the complainant would not have waited for a day or two and would have immediately approached police, that is particularly when as per her version Dr. Nikhat had advised so on the same day and then got the girl medically examined or at least when the girl complained of stomachache with the history of sexual assault by the accused in the manner as described in the complaint, the girl would have been taken immediately to hospital but that do not appear to have been done. 24] It is argued on behalf of prosecution that as per Section 29 of P.O.C.S.O. Act the Court is required to draw presumption that the accused committed offence unless the contrary is proved and the accused needs to be held guilty since the accused is prosecuted after investigation in the crime. But then, in that respect as is clear section 29 of the Act itself makes it clear that such presumption is to be drawn unless the contrary is proved. Then, it is also well settled that burden to establish the defence put forth is not as heavy as that on the prosecution to prove the guilt of the accused and the preponderance of probability only is to be shown by the accused to rebut the presumption and even if suspicion or doubt is created .. 16 .. Special Case No. 32/2013 Judgment about prosecution case, the presumption needs to be held as rebutted. In the light of that if the facts and circumstances of the present case brought on record is considered, as discussed above, entire story of prosecution is doubtful and improbable and even not corroborated by medical evidence and version of the complainant herself found to be not reliable and untrustworthy since she had improved case a lot and even from the answers given by the girl in the cross-examination, it is clear that possible of the girl had been tutored is there since she stated that she deposed before Court at the instance of her sister and in the light of that the admission given the girl that there was previous dispute between the accused and the complainant on account of giving and taking money, the presumption has to held as rebutted and since possibility of defence put forth by the accused being probable is there and since the complainant is not found to be truthful and reliable witness, I am of the view that the allegations against the accused cannot be said to have been established beyond all the reasonable doubt and the accused is entitled to the benefit of reasonable doubt. Point No. 1 to 3 are answered accordingly in the negative. As to point no.4 - 25] In view of above discussion it has to be held that the prosecution has failed to establish the guilt of the accused beyond all the reasonable doubt and the accused is entitled to be acquitted. Point no.4 is therefore answered accordingly. .. 17 .. Special Case No. 32/2013 Judgment 26] Since the accused is acquitted, it is necessary that he be directed to furnish P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/- [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount under section 437A of Cr.P.C. to appear before the higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect of any appeal or petition, if any, filed against the judgment and that such bail bond shall be in force for six months. In the result I pass the following order- ORDER Accused namely Habib Kadar Sayyad is acquitted of the charge for offence punishable under section 376 of I.P.C. and section 4 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 2) The accused shall be released from the jail forthwith if not required in any other crime. 3) The accused shall furnish P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/- [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount under section 437A of Cr.P.C. to appear before the higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect of any appeal or petition filed against the judgment and that such bail bond shall be in force for six months. 4) No muddemal articles are seen to have been produced before court. Hence, no order regarding its disposal is passed. 5) The proceeding is closed. Date : 30.06.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Additional Session Judge-1, Thane.

.. 1 .. Spl. 33/2013 judgment Received on : 07.08.2013 Registered on : 07.08.2013 Decided on : 14.11.2014 Duration : 1 yr. 3 mths. 7 days In The Court of the District Judge – 1 and Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act), Thane At Thane (Presided over by Mrs.V.V.Virkar) Special Case No. 33 of 2013 Exhibit No. 21 The State of Maharashtra … Complainant versus Bablu alias Vilas Hari Vathare, … Accused Age 21 years, Residence – near house of Sambhaji Kamble, at Phulenagar no.1, Bhiwandi. Offence punishable under section 354 of I.P.C. and section 3(b) of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. .. 2 .. Spl. 33/2013 judgment Appearance - Mr. A.K.Khamkar, A.P.P. for the State. Mr. Rahul S. Waghmare, Advocate for accused. JUDGMENT (Delivered on 14.11.2014.) The accused stands prosecuted for the offence punishable under section 354 of I.P.C. and section 3(b) of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as ''P.O.C.S.O. Act'') for outraging modesty of minor girl Mrunal d/o Mahendra Phatke on 10.04.2013 around 8.15 p.m. in the house of maternal uncle of the complainant by touching her private part and moving his hand over her body by undressing her. 2] In short the facts giving rise to the prosecution of the accused are that complainant Sheetal Mahendra Phatke aged 28 years stay alongwith her mother and daughter Mrunal aged 4 years. Accused Bablu alias had been staying in their neighbourhood and they were acquainted with each other and they had been on visiting terms to each other's house. It is also further case of the prosecution that the accused being neighbour used to always take the victim girl Mrunal to his house for playing. That on 10.04.2013 the accused took the victim girl to his house by inducing her by offering chocolate and then had removed her nicker and moved his hand on her stomach as well .. 3 .. Spl. 33/2013 judgment as place of urination. The victim girl after returning home around 8.15 p.m. informed about said incident to her mother and also had showed the house of the accused to her mother where the incident took place and then her mother went to police station and lodged complaint. 3] On the basis of her complaint, offence as per C.R. No.I-67/2013 under section 354A(1) of I.P.C. and section 3(2) of P.O.C.S.O. Act was registered at Bhiwandi City police station and the work of investigation was done by P.S.I. Patil. During the investigation panchnama of the spot was prepared. Statements of witnesses including the victim girl aged 4 years were recorded. Since the girl was of tender age 4 years, her statement was recorded in presence of Women Protection Cell of Bhiwandi City Police. After completion of investigation since there was sufficient evidence against the accused, he was charge-sheeted for the offence punishable under section 354A(1) of I.P.C. and section 3(2) of P.O.C.S.O. Act. 4] Since offence under P.O.C.S.O. Act is exclusively triable by Special Court, the charge sheet was submitted to this Court. 5] The accused was produced before the court. A charge under section 354 of I.P.C. and section 3(b) of P.O.C.S.O. Act was framed against the accused as per Exh.3 .. 4 .. Spl. 33/2013 judgment The contents were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. The accused pleaded not guilty. His defence was of total denial. He claimed to be tried. 6] For establishing the charges levelled against the accused the prosecution examined P.W.1 complainant Sheetal Mahendra Phatke and victim girl P.W.2 Mrunal Mahendra Phatke and P.W.3 P.S.I. Jitendra Yuvraj Patil, I.O. The documentary evidence produced, proved and relied upon by the prosecution consisted of complaint Exh.9 (excluding portion marked A), spot panchnama Exh.20 (exhibited since admitted by defence). 7] I heard the learned A.P.P. and the learned advocate for the accused. 8] On the basis of above facts of the accused following points arise for my determination and my findings and reasons for the same are as under - POINTS FINDINGS 1. Whether the prosecution has proved that on 10.04.2013 at about 20.15 in the house of son of complainant's maternal uncle Karamchand Saravade at Phulenagar no.1, Bhiwandi, the accused committed assault on the victim girl aged 4 years by moving his hand on her person and private part .. 5 .. Spl. 33/2013 judgment after undressing with intent to outrage or knowing it to be likely that he will NOT thereby outrage her modesty ? PROVED. 2. Whether the prosecution has proved that on the given day, date, time and place the accused committed penetrative sexual assault on the victim NOT girl ? PROVED. 3. What offence if any committed by the NO OFFENCE accused ? IS PROVED. 4. What order ? As per the final order. REASONS 9] As is clear the accused is charged for offence punishable under section 354 of I.P.C. and section 3(b) of P.O.C.S.O. Act and it is alleged that the accused committed assault on the victim girl aged 4 years by moving his hand on her person and private part after undressing with intent to outrage or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby outrage her modesty and also committed penetrative assault on her. For establishing offence under section 354 of I.P.C. the prosecution is required to establish that the accused committed assault on the victim girl with intent to outrage her modesty. In this regard Section 354 runs as under - Whoever assaults, or uses criminal force to any woman, itnending to outrage or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby outrage her modesty, shall be punished with ….......... .. 6 .. Spl. 33/2013 judgment Even since the girl is stated to be 4 years old, the provisions of P.O.C.S.O. Act are stated to have been attracted and since it is alleged that the accused had touched private part of the victim girl, offence under section 3(b) of P.O.C.S.O. Act is also charged. Then, for establishing offence under section 3(b) of P.O.C.S.O. Act it is necessary that the prosecution shall establish that the accused had inserted, to any extent, any object or any part of the body, not being the penis, into the vagina, the urethra or anus of the child or made the child to do so with him and it is required to be seen as to whether the evidence brought on record by the prosecution is sufficient to establish the ingredients of section 354 of I.P.C. or section 3(b) of P.O.C.S.O. Act. 10] In that regard as is clear as per the complaint the accused on the given day, date, time and place had removed the nicker of the girl, lifted her frock upward and touched her private part. Then, a careful perusal of the testimony of the complainant before court on oath reveal that though she stated that on the date of incident her daughter Mrunal had been to the house of her maternal uncle where the accused was staying for playing and after returning she told that the accused had lifted her frock up and removed her nicker, she stated that her daughter told that the accused moved his hand on stomach and therefore she went to police station and lodged complaint. As .. 7 .. Spl. 33/2013 judgment such so far as inserting any part of body into the vagina of the girl or even to the extent that the accused had touched private part or vagina of the girl after removing her nicker, the complainant do not appear to have supported the prosecution case. 11] It is very much material to mention that the complainant's evidence in regard to the incident is on the basis of what the victim girl i.e. her daughter had told her. In the light of that the testimony of the daughter would have been material and important But then, though the victim girl is examined before court, she do not appear to have stated anything in regard to the incident. It has to be mentioned that the girl was called more than once for making her comfortable and finally atmosphere was created so that she can open up and state the facts but even when the girl was found to be very much comfortable, smiling, shying and answering the questions put to her and was not at all noticed to be under any pressure or tension. Even a very specific note had been taken to the effect that ''the witness though asked many questions repeatedly by even referring the name of the accused and though asked as to whether anybody by name Bablu uncle or without referring name of accused whether any untoward incident had taken place with her involving any elder male person, or even specifying the alleged incident of male person touching her private part or moving his hand on her private part by .. 8 .. Spl. 33/2013 judgment removing her frock etc. is keeping quiet and not saying anything. The girl also do not appear to have been scared or embarrassed and is seen to be normal at ease. She appear to be naturally shy as per her tender age to strangers''. 12] No doubt the girl being of very tender age of 5 years at the time of her deposition before Court and being naturally shy as per tendency of the girl of her age while deposing before Court, the aspect that the girl did not speak much or rather anything is natural and cannot be taken as a serious lacuna in the prosecution evidence and it is well settled that even in such cases where the victim girl is of very tender age, in absence of evidence of victim also the conclusion about the guilt of the accused can be arrive if there is sufficient evidence on record in regard to the allegations against the accused. 13] In the light of that if in the present case the other evidence brought on record is perused, it is clear that it is only the testimony of the mother of the girl which is available in that regard, but, as discussed above, she do not appear to have stated about the main allegations against the accused as has been alleged to have been stated by the girl i.e. her daughter, about the accused touching her private part or inserting his finger in her private part. In such circumstances absence of testimony of the girl even to the extent that there had been some instance with her involving the accused and she had narrated the incident .. 9 .. Spl. 33/2013 judgment to her mother, such allegations cannot be said to have been established. Even as is clear though she stated that she had lodged complaint to police station against the accused, it was marked as Exh.9 including portion marked A since the complainant refused to have stated so to police. 14] It is also material to mention that since P.W.1, mother of the girl, has not supported the prosecution in regard to actual act alleged to have been done by the accused or stated to have been done by the accused, she was declared hostile and was cross examined on behalf of prosecution. It is further material to mention that in her cross examination by the learned A.P.P. she appear to have accepted that her complaint was recorded by police as per her narration and she also accepted that the portion marked A in her complaint referring to the alleged act of the accused who touched private part etc., was stated by her to police since her daughter had told her about it and also further that portion marked A is correctly recorded. But then, when a pinpointed question was asked to the complainant in cross examination on behalf of prosecution itself as to why in examination-in-chief she had stated that her daughter had not stated portion marked A to her and therefore the complainant appear to have answered that sometimes her daughter tells lies and also further that even in regard to this incident also at times her daughter stated that the accused had moved his hand on her place of urination and sometimes she did .. 10 .. Spl. 33/2013 judgment not tell so and therefore she had stated so in her examination-in- chief. 15] That makes it further clear that even if her version that her daughter had stated so that the accused had acted in that manner with her is accepted for a while, that cannot said to be true version or true narration of the facts because as per her own statement the daughter sometimes do not tell the true facts. In the light of that when the girl though appeared before court and efforts were made to see that she is comfortable and is in an atmosphere to open up and tell true facts, she was just keeping quiet and was not saying anything and was not even ready to speak a word in the Court, the submissions on behalf of accused that possibility of the accused being falsely implicated in the crime are there appear to be having some substance. 16] No doubt, as rightly pointed out on behalf of prosecution the incident alleged to have taken place in the night around 8.15 p.m. and if at all no such incident had taken place, there was no reason for the complainant to go all the way to police station and lodge complaint. But then, as is clear the complainant do not appear to have even lodged the complaint immediately on the same day and though the incident took place on 10.04.2013 and though it was reported to her mother by the girl around 8.15 p.m. the complaint was not lodged on that day or even on next day morning and it appear to have been lodged .. 11 .. Spl. 33/2013 judgment and offence is registered on the next day in the night at 0030 hours on 12.04.2013. In the light if the version of the complainant on oath taken into consideration that the girl sometimes stating that accused had touched her private part or sometimes was not stating so and at times she lies also if considered, that create doubt in the mind about actual happening of the incident and about true narration of the facts by the girl to the mother and in the circumstances the delay even of one day in lodging the complaint assumes importance. Even it is to be mentioned that except the complainant the prosecution has not examined any other witness in support of at least the fact that the girl had been to the house of the accused on that day and had reported such incident to her mother etc. 17] In view of above discussion it cannot be said that the evidence brought on record by the prosecution is sufficient to establish the guilt of the accused beyond all the reasonable doubt and the accused is entitled to be benefit of reasonable doubt and therefore acquittal. Point no.1 to 3 are answered accordingly. 18] Since the accused is acquitted, it is necessary that he be directed to furnish P.R. bond of Rs.10,000/- [rupees ten thousand only] with one surety in the like amount under section 437A of Cr.P.C. to appear before the higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect of any appeal or petition, if .. 12 .. Spl. 33/2013 judgment any, filed against the judgment and that such bail bond shall be in force for six months. In the result I pass the following order - ORDER Accused Bablu alias Vilas Hari Vathare is acquitted of the charge for offence punishable under section 354(a)(i) of I.P.C. and section 3(2) of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 2) He shall be released from jail forthwith if not required in any other crime. 3) He shall furnish P.R. bond of Rs.10,000/- [rupees ten thousand only] with one surety in the like amount under section 437A of Cr.P.C. to appear before the higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect of any appeal or petition, if any filed against the judgment and that such bail bond shall be in force for six months. 4) No muddemal article is seen to be submitted to the Court. Hence, no order in respect of its disposal is passed. 5) The proceeding is closed. Date : 19.11.2014. (Mrs.V.V.Virkar) Dist. Judge-1 and Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.

.. 1 .. bail no.1669/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 1669/2015 This application is filed by applicant Arvind Hiralal Uppadhyay for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. I-371/2015 registered at Kashimira police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 354D of I.P.C. and section 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant used to follow the victim girl and at the time of incident he asked the victim girl to sit in his car with intent to outrage her modesty. It is further contended and argued that no such incident has happened and the applicant is falsely implicated with a view to harass him and the complaint is filed with mala fide intention. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co-operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that the accused always used to follow the victim girl whenever she used to to attend dance class at Hatkesh and he always attempted to foster personal interaction with her despite clear disinterest shown by her. It is further contended and argued that at the time of incident the accuse with intent to outrage her modesty was following her and questioned her as to whether she would sit in his vehicle. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl and the prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. .. 2 .. bail no.1669/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 354D of I.P.C. and section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act the girl is stated to be 12 years old , it appears that the accused had been arrested on 10.07.2015. Then, as per prosecution case the accused was allegedly following the victim girl whenever she used to go to attend her dance class and even at the time of incident in question the accused followed her and even asked her whether she would sit in his vehicle. But then, d it is contended on behalf of accused that he is falsely implicated in the crime only with a view to harassment and the complaint is filed with mala fide intention. In such circumstance whether the allegations against the accused are true or not, would be the question to be decided on merits. Even nothing is stated to be recovered from the applicant/accused. 4] It is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 5] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 6] Then, it has also to be mentioned that looking the allegations against the accused the investigation in the matter may .. 3 .. bail no.1669/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) have almost completed but the charge sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 7] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order - ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Arvind Harilal Uppadhyay is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/- [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions - The applicant/accused shall attend the concerned police station on every Monday between 10.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon till filing of the charge sheet and shall co-operate in investigation. He shall not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and the prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this Court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 24.07.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Additional Sessions Judge-1, Thane.

Received on : 08.08.2013 Registered on : 08.08.2013 Decided on : 06.07.2015 Duration : 1Y.10Ms.28Ds. IN THE COURT OF D.J.­6 & ADDL. SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE (Presided over by Hemant M. Patwardhan) Special Case No. 35/2013 Exh.No. State of Maharashtra, (Through Kasarvadavali Police station, Thane) ..Complainant V/s. Keshav Manohar Dhanve Age 22 years, R/at. Aakhada Balapur, Tal. Kalmanuri, Dist. Hingoli ..Accused Appearance:­ APP Shri.Mishra for the State Advocate Shri. Bhalerao for the accused JUDGMENT (Delivered on this 6th day of July, 2015) Accused Keshav was facing trial on following facts:­ 1] That on 03.10.2012 at about 11.00 a.m. behind Bramhand Phase No.8, Turfepada, G.B. Road, Thane(W) 1 to 6 accused has kidnapped, victim aged about 16 years from lawful guardianship of her parents and after kidnapping victim, compelled her to marry against her will to have illicit intercourse. Hence on complaint lodged by Priti Sanjay Khade present offence came to be registered against him. On completion of investigation he was charge­sheeted. 2] In response to the summons accused Keshav appeared before the court and when the charge was framed below Exh.6 has claimed innocent, do not pleaded guilty and claim to be tried. Hence trial on merit was conducted. 3] Prosecution has examined victim, the complainant and police station officer in order to substantiate the allegations againt the accused. Defence has admitted documents like arrest panchanama, seizure panchanama of clothes etc. therefore witnesses on those points were given up. After evidence of the prosecution, opportunity was granted to the parties to argue the matter on merit. 4] Heard Learned advocate for accused and Learned APP for the State. It was submitted by the Learned APP that as the victim was minor at the relevant time though she did not support the case of the prosecution, other documents in terms of medical examination of the accused and the victim are sufficient to hold the accused guilty of the offence. On the contrary it was submitted by the learned defence advocate that 2 to 6 as the victim and parent of the victim have turned hostile, no evidence is on record to connect the accused with the alleged crime. He has further requested to acquit the accused from all the allegations. On the basis of the rival arguments, following points arise for my consideration and I record my findings against each of them for the reasons noted below :­ S.N. Points Findings 1] Does the prosecution prove that on 03.10.2012 at about ..No. 11.00 a.m. behind Bramhand Phase No.8, Turfepada, G.B. Road, Thane (W) accused has kidnapped the victim aged about 16 years from the lawful guardianship of her parents and thus committed an offence punishable under section 363 of IPC? 2] Does the prosecution prove that on the aforesaid date, ..No. time and place kidnapping of the victim girl was with an intention to compel her or knowingly that she will be compelled by such kidnapping or likely that she would be forced to illicit intercourse and thus accused has committed an offence punishable under section 366 of IPC? 3] Does prosecution prove that during 03.10.2012 to ..No. 05.05.2013 at village Pargaon, Tal.Shrigonda, Dist. Ahmadnagar accused has committed rape on the said victim from time to time and thus committed an offence punishable under section 373 of IPC? 4] What order? Accused is acquitted as per final order. REASONS As to point nos. 1 and 4:­ 5] All these points are interlinked with each other, therefore are consider at once. Prosecution has alleged that on the eventful date, time and place initially accused has 3 to 6 kidnapped the victim a minor girl aged about 16 years from the lawful guardianship of her parents and it was further alleged that kidnapping or inducing of the victim was to compel for marriage or to have illicit intercourse with the accused and thereafter, accused has actually committed rape during period 03.10.2012 to 05.05.2013. Prosecution in order to prove the aforesaid allegations, accordingly have examined material witnesses viz. victim as PW1, her guardian father as PW2 and then police station officer who has recorded statement of the victim and her father. Material witnesses of the prosecution, however did not support the case or any of the allegations against accused. It was the case of prosecution that PW2 had lodged initially, missing complaint and then when the minor was traced out missing complaint was converted into the aforesaid offences after statement Exh.11 was recorded. As on date of recording evidence minor victim has turned major and therefore was aware about consequence of giving false evidence before court. In spite of that fact when she entered into witness box, she did not support case of prosecution and categorically denied that accused either abducted her or kidnapped her from the lawful guardianship of her parents or induced either to perform marriage or seduced to illicit relationship with another person. As a matter of fact she has specifically denied the fact of accused having any physical relationship with her during the period when she was away from the custody of her parents and she has specifically 4 to 6 denied the fact that accused had intercourse with her against her will though at the time of the offence as she was minor her consent was immaterial. However as she has denied the fact that accused had not sexual intercourse with her at any time it is difficult to link the accused with the alleged crime. 6] Though submissions were made by Learned APP that other documents are admitted by the defence, the same are sufficient to corroborate the allegations against the accused. However mere admission of the fact that accused was arrested or clothes of the accused etc. were seized and medical examination was performed are itself not sufficient to come to the conclusion that accused has actually committed offence as alleged by the prosecution. Prosecution has to its allegations by substantial evidence before the court. If both witnesses have failed to support the case of the prosecution, said allegations remained unproved. Other material witness was, the father of victim who actually had lodged missing complaint which was then turned into complaint of serious allegations of kidnapping and rape. However the witness has also failed to support the case of the prosecution and has stated before the court that his minor daughter was never found missing. As initially allegation of kidnapping itself is not supported by the parents, further allegations in respect of inducing or commission of rape cannot be considered to be proved. Having regards to this fact in my opinion as the prosecution has failed to establish the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt, accused is entitled for 5 to 6 acquittal. With the said observation, I record my finding against point no.1 in the negative and proceed to pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused is acquitted from the offence punishable under sections 363, 366, 376 of IPC. 2] His Bail bonds shall accordingly stands cancelled. 3] Muddemal property being worthless be destroyed after appeal period is over. 4] Accused is directed to execute P.R. of Rs.5000/­ with one solvent surety in the like amount as per and the bond so executed shall remain in force for six months from the date of its execution as per amended provisions of section 437(A) of Cr.P.C. 5] Accused to comply accordingly. Thane (Hemant M.Patwardhan) Date: 06.07.2015 D.J.­6 & Additional Sessions Judge, Thane 6 to 6

However, there is no single witness stating or deposing that they had ever seen the accused in their school. The presence of the accused in the school that also on working day and during school time, cannot be believed to have gone unnoticed by any student, teacher or staff member of the school. It is further to be noted here that as per prosecution story, the rape upon the victim was committed by an unknown person. Under such circumstances for proper identification of the assailant, it was necessary to conduct identification parade of the accused No.2. In the absence of identification parade of accused No.2, the identification of him by the victim in the Court cannot be relied upon. The investigating officer has miserably failed to conduct test identification parade in order to get identified the accused No.2 through the victim. On the contrary the victim and other witnesses have deposed that they had seen the accused in the police station and in the Court. J­Sess.Case ­ 158­15 ­ 376,323,504,506,34 3,4,16,17.doc .....13/­ ..13.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 158/2015.. Exh.56.. 21] As admitted by PW4 in cross examination, it is difficult to opine as to how old was the injury of the victim. No witness from the school except the informant is examined. As already observed the evidence of informant also is not trustworthy and reliable being hearsay one. There is no proper identification of assailants by conducting identification parade. Under such circumstances there is no sound and reasonable ground to raise presumption u/s.29 and 30 of The Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act in favour of prosecution. Unless and until there is reliable or sound reason to raise presumption in favour of the prosecution, the defence cannot be called upon J­Sess.Case ­ 158­15 ­ 376,323,504,506,34 3,4,16,17.doc .....14/­ ..14.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 158/2015.. Exh.56.. to rebut the same. The entire evidence on record does not inspire any confidence to rely upon the prosecution story. The evidence on record is certainly not reliable to prove the case against the accused beyond reasonable doubt. Certainly the benefit of doubt has to be weighed in favour of the accused. With these observations, answering point Nos.1 to 4 in the negative, following order is passed. ORDER 1. Accused No.1. Gulab Rajesh Koli and No.2. Dnyaneshwar Vishwanath Pawar are hereby acquitted u/s.235(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure for offence punishable u/s.376, 323, 504, 506 r.w. 34 of the Indian Penal Code and u/s.3, 4 16 and 17 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offenes Act. 2. –1– ABA 1623/2018 ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN ANTICIPATORY BAIL APPLICATION NO.1623/2018 CNR NO.MHTH01­004455­2018 The applicant Krishna Pal Yadav has applied for bail under section 438 of Cr.P.C., in C.R. No.I­460/2017 registered in Naupada police station for the offence under section 363, 376, 376(l), 468 read with 34 of Indian Penal Code and Section 4,8 and 12 of POCSO Act, 2012. 2. It is contended that there is no role of this applicant in the offence under section 363, 376 of IPC and secton 4, 8,12 of POCSO Act. Only allegation against this applicant is that he is an Advocate, therefore, he has prepared agreement of marriage of victim and accused at Utter Pradesh. It is alleged by the prosecution that he has prepared affidavit without verifying the real age of the victim. In the agreement of marriage it is mentioned that the victim is major. But in fact the victim is minor. The applicant has submitted that he is not supposed to inquire in detail regarding age of the victim. There is no allegation that the signatures on the agreement is forged and stamp is forged. Agreement is seized by police during investigation. It is submitted that the boy and girl eloped away to Utter Pradesh and married with each other as per their own wish and then they prepared agreement of marriage and as per their information he has mentioned age of victim and accused in the agreement. There is no allegation that he has forced the –2– ABA 1623/2018 victim and accused to marry with each other. It is submitted that nothing is required to be seized from him, therefore, he may be given protection before arrest. 3. Investigating Officer has given say at Exh.6. It is contended that he has prepared agreement of marriage between victim and accused without verifying documents of age proof of the victim and he was called in the police station for inquiry, but he did not appear. He is resident of Utter Pradesh, therefore, he is not likely to remain present for the trial. Therefore, his anticipatory bail may be rejected. 4. I heard Ld. Advocate on behalf of accused and Ld. APP. 5. The court is of the view that so called agreement is already seized in the investigation. Therefore, nothing is remained to be seized from the present applicant. In fact, victim is also more than 16 years old and accused is 28 years old. They eloped away from Thane to Utter Pradesh and they performed marriage and resided there as husband and wife. Offences regarding 363, 376 of IPC and section 4,8,12 of POCSO Act are not applicable to the present applicant. He has not instigated applicant and victim to get married and there is no allegation that he has prepared forged Adhar Card and PAN Card of the victim and stamp is forged. His only role that he has prepared affidavit without verifying age proof. Therefore, considering the role played by this accused and the allegation made against accused the court is of the view that nothing is –3– ABA 1623/2018 required to be seized from him, therefore, he is entitled for the protection of pre arrest. Therefore, I proceed to pass following order. :ORDER: 1. Application is allowed. 2. In case of arrest of applicant Krishna Pal Yadav in C.R. No.I­460/2017 registered in Naupada police station for the offence under section 363, 376, 376(l), 468 read with 34 of Indian Penal Code and Section 4,8 and 12 of POCSO Act, 2012 he shall be released on P.B. and S.B. of Rs.30,000/­(Rupees Thirty Thousand Only)with one or two solvent sureties on condition that:­ (a) He shall submit his I.D proof, photograph in the police station and in the court. (b) He shall give undertaking in writing that he shall remain present before the police for the purpose of investigation as per direction of this court. (c) He shall attend the concerned police station for the purpose of investigation on Monday and Thursday between 11.00 a.m. to 5.00 p.m. till the investigation is over till then he shall not leave the jurisdiction of the court and shall co­operate for the investigation. –4– ABA 1623/2018 (d) He shall not tamper the prosecution witnesses and victim by any means. Thane. (S.C. Khalipe) Date :26.07.2018. Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

COMMON ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN CRIMINAL BAIL APPLICATION NO. 1684 /2015 AND A.B.A. 1696/2015. Perused both applications and say thereon. Perused the case diary. Heard Ld. counsel Shri. S.E. Lasne for applicant, Ld.P.P. Shri. Kadri for the State. 2. It is the case of prosecution that on 09.07.15 at about 21.00 hours, both accused in furtherance of their common intention, kidnapped victim aged 17 years and 8 months, from the lawful custody of her parents and Rohit Lasne has committed rape on her, thereby, committed an offence punishable u/s. 363, 376 r/w. 34 of I.P.C. and u/s. 4, 8, 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 3. Ld. counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant Rohit Lasne had love affair with the victim aged about 17 years 8 months. The said affair was known by both the families. However, parents of victim had not approved the said relations. Victim has attended age of her discretion. Applicant Shubham Lasne, cousin brother of Rohit had no role. He had only allowed to Rohit to stay at his farm­house. Both applicants are permanent resident of village Kawad, Tal. Bhiwandi. Custody of Shubham is not required. 4. Ld. P.P. Mr. Kadri submitted that victim is minor. Investigation is in progress. She has specifically stated entire episode in her report. 5. Victim is aged about 17 years 8 months. Complainant has stated her age as 17 years 9 months. As per school­leaving certificate, victim was born on 01.10.97. As per statement of victim Pratiksha, there was love affair between accused Rohit and herself and they had decided to flee away. On 07.07.15, Pratiksha herself has given call to the accused on Tata phone of her uncle Ladku Dagdu Naik that they would run away. The said proposal is accepted by Rohit. It means, she herself left the house of her parents. She had attended the age of her discretion. She was knowing the consequences of her own act. 6. Sessions Judge Thane & The Designated Judge Under Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012) SPECIAL CASE NO.153/2014 EXH. No.14 STATE OF MAHARASHTRA, through Vashi Police Station ...Prosecution Vs. Dinesh Madhukar Thakur Age 23 years, Occ. Service ...Accused R/at.Near Jugaon Talav, Sector 11, Vashi, Navi Mumbai ==================================== Appearances : Ld. APP Shri.V.A. Kulkarni for Prosecution, Ld. Counsel Shri.Sanjay Kanhere for accused. ==================================== .. 2 .. Spl.Case No. 153/2014 (Judgment.) :JUDGMENT: (Delivered on 15th day of December, 2017) 1. Accused is facing trial for the offence punishable u/sec. 363, 366A, 376 of Indian Penal Code (hereinafter as IPC) and Sec.4 & 6 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter referred as POCSO Act). 2. Name of the victim, full name of her family members, place of incidence, name of school are not mentioned in the judgment to avoid disclosure of identity of Victim as per Section 33(7) of the POCSO Act. 3. In short case of prosecution is as follows:­ On 22.5.14 between 4 to 5 p.m at present accused kidnapped minor victim from the lawful guardianship of her parents knowingly that she will be compelled or likely to compel illicit intercourse and he also committed rape on her and thereby committed the offence u/sec. 363, 366A, 376 of Indian Penal Code and Sec.4 & 6 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 4. The FIR was lodged against accused by mother of victim. On the basis of said FIR Crime No. I­193/2014 came to be registered. After completion of all the formalities of investigation the present chargesheet came to be filed. 5. The Charge was framed by my predecessor vide Ex.4 against .. 3 .. Spl.Case No. 153/2014 (Judgment.) the accused for the offence punishable u/sec. 363, 366A, 376 of Indian Penal Code and Sec.4 & 6 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 6. In support of its case the prosecution has examined following witnesses:­ PW No. Ex.No. Prosecution Witness 1 07 Victim. 2 11 Nirmala­ Mother of Victim (Name of the victim is not disclosed to protect her identity.) 7. Considering the evidence given by PW.1 and 2 and the hostility of victim, the Ld. APP wisely closed the evidence of prosecution by filing purshis at Ex.13 to save the valuable time of court and prosecution machinery. 8. After considering the case of prosecution following points arise for my determination. I recorded my findings against each of them for the reasons stated below:­ S.No. Points Findings 1. Whether the prosecution proves that accused kidnapped victim from the No. lawful guardianship of her parents? 2. Whether the prosecution proves that accused induced minor victim to leave the house of her parents with intent that she may be or knowing No. .. 4 .. Spl.Case No. 153/2014 (Judgment.) that it is likely that she will be, forced or seduced to illicit intercourse with another person? 3. Whether the prosecution proves that accused committed rape on minor No. victim from time to time? 4. Whether the prosecution proves that accused committed penetrative sexual No. assault on minor victim? 5. What order? Accused is acquitted. :REASONS: AS TO POINT NO. 1 TO 4 :­ 9. To prove the case, prosecution has examined PW.1 Victim at Ex.07. PW.1 Victim did not support the prosecution case. She did not told anything incriminating against present accused. She specifically stated that on 22.5.14 accused Dinesh did not abducted her by giving false promise to marry and he did not committed rape on her. Though prosecution declared him hostile and put the question in the nature of cross­ examination, prosecution failed to brought any incriminating circumstances against accused. She further deposed that she married with accused after she became major. She further deposed that, she left the house on 22.5.14 on her own wish due to the quarrel with her mother. She did not stated that she left the house alongwith accused. .. 5 .. Spl.Case No. 153/2014 (Judgment.) 10. PW.2 Nirmala mother of victim deposed that on 22.5.14 she was sleeping at about 4 p.m as she was not well. She woke up at about 5.30 p.m., that time she noticed that victim­her daughter is not in house. Therefore she searched her here and there and also enquired with relatives but she did not get any information. She further deposed that she also went to the house of accused and she came to know that accused is also not in his house. Therefore on suspicion she lodged FIR against accused at Ex.12 that her daughter is kidnapped by accused. She further deposed that after some days police searched victim and handed over custody of victim to her. She further deposed that after victim became major she married with accused. Now she do not have any intention that accused be punished. 11. In her cross­examination she admitted that at the time of lodging missing complaint she stated to police that victim left the house by her sweet will. She admitted that she lodged complaint against accused on suspicion. She admitted that, when victim became major she married with accused and presently residing with accused. 12. In view of the oral evidence adduced on record on behalf of prosecution it is transpired that, there is absolutely no incriminating evidence came on record to be put to the accused for explanation u/sec.313 of Cr.P.C. Therefore after hearing Ld.APP and Advocate for accused, I am inclined to dispense with the statement u/sec.313 of Cr.P.C. Accordingly I .. 6 .. Spl.Case No. 153/2014 (Judgment.) passed order below Ex.4 and dispensed with the statement. 13. So considering all these facts and circumstances discussed above, there is absolutely no evidence to suggest that accused committed any offence as alleged u/sec.363, 366A, 376 of Indian Penal Code and Sec.4 & 6 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, therefore the accused is entitled for order of acquittal. Hence, I answer Point No.1 to 4 are in negative. AS TO POINT NO.5:­ 14. Considering the reasoning and finding as to point No.1 to 4 in answer to point no.5 , I proceed to pass following order:­ ORDER 1] Accused Dinesh Madhukar Thakur is hereby acquitted u/sec.232 of Cr. P. C. of the offence punishable u/sec. 363, 366A, 376 of Indian Penal Code and Sec.4 & 6 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] The bail bond of accused stands cancelled and surety stands discharged. 3] The muddemal property being worthless be destroyed as per Sec.452(1) of Cr. P. C., after expiration of appeal period. .. 7 .. Spl.Case No. 153/2014 (Judgment.) 4] The accused shall execute P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ and surety in like amount, in compliance of Sec.437­A of Cr.P.C. Thane ( Prakash R. Kadam ) Dated: 15.12.2017 Designated Judge Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, Thane
