--1-- ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN REGULAR BAIL APPLICATOIN NO.1697/2017 The applicant Ajit Rohidas Gaikwad has applied for bail under section 439 of Cr. P.C. in C.R.No.I­161/2017 registered in Rabale MIDC police station for the offence under section 376 of Indian Penal Code and section 4 of POCSO Act 2012. 2. It is contended that the applicant is falsely implicated. It is contended that the victim is 17 years 8 months old. Her birth date is not mentioned in FIR. There was love affair between victim and accused and victim herself mislead her mother by saying that she has suffering from Thyroid inspite of that she was pregnant from the accused. The victim went to her friend's house and resided there for 11 days, but her parents did not lodge any missing complaint. After that the victim told her mother that she was at Ajit Gaikwad and she disclosed her mother that from October 2015 she had love affair with Ajit. It is submitted that the investigation is almost completed. The custody of the accused in jail is no more required and it will be unjustifiable to keep him behind the bar without trial. He is ready to face the trial. He is permanent resident. He will co­operate for investigation. Hence he is prayed for bail. 3. The applicant has produced copy of FIR, remand reports and statement of victim under section 164 of Cr. P.C. 4. Investigating Officer has given his report at Exh.3. It is contended that the victim is nine months pregnant. If the --2-- accused is released on bail he is likely to tamper the victim and the prosecution witnesses. 5. Heard Ld. Counsel on behalf of applicant. He relied upon decision in Sunil Mahadev Patil V/s. State of Maharashtra 2015 DGLS (Bom) 433. It was the case under section 363, 366A and 376 of Indian Penal Code. In that case the prosecutrix was 15 years old and the accused was 20 years old. They eloped away and performed marriage in the temple and started residing together. It was held that there are many mitigating factors to release the accused on bail. 6. I heard Ld. APP. She submitted that the victim is nine months pregnant due to forceful sexual intercourse by the accused to her and therefore, accused is likely to tamper her. The accused is 33 years old. 7. I perused FIR. It is mentioned that the victim had not mensuration course and therefore her mother had asked to her but the victim did not tell anything to her. Her mother asked her to come to doctor, but the victim told her that she is suffering from Thyroid. On 30.05.2017 the victim went to her friend's house and resided there till 11.06.2017. Then the victim's mother called the victim and took her in confidence. The victim disclosed that since October 2015 she had love affair with Ajit and he had committed sexual intercourse with her by promising to marry her. Then synography test of the victim was done. It was transpired that she was 8 months pregnant and after that the present FIR was lodged on 12.06.2017. --3-- 8. In the FIR it is mentioned that the victim was 18 years 5 months old at present, but her birth date is not mentioned. No proof of birth date is produced on record. The court is of the view that the victim had love affair with the accused and since October 2015 she has in contact with the accused. She had resides with her friend's house for 11 days. During that victim's mother did not take any action. Even the victim was secretly meeting with the accused. Her mother did not take any objection even the victim lost her mensuration course. Her mother did not take any proper action and till she became eight months 10 days pregnant no proper care was tken by her mother and the victim also did not disclose her mother about any love affair or sexual intercourse committed by the accused with her. So these are the mitigating circumstances likely in the case of Sunil Mahadev Patil V/s. State of Maharashtr cited supra. The court is of the view that the investigation is almost completed so it will not be justifiable to keep the applicant behind the bar. He is ready to co­operate for the investigation and ready to face the trial. So upon conditions he is entitled for bail. Hence, I pass following order. ORDER 1. Application is allowed. 2. The applicant be released on P.B. and S.B. of Rs.30,000/­ (Rupees Thirty Thousand Only) with one or two local solvent sureties in like amount. 3. The applicant shall not contact the victim and the --4-- prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper or pressurize them by any means. 4. The applicant shall co­operate for the investigation as and when necessary. 5. The applicant shall not leave the jurisdiction of the court without prior permission of the court and shall attend the court. Thane. ( S.C. Khalipe ) Date : 21/07/2017. Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

.. 1 .. Bail No. 1701/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1.) Order below Exhibit 1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 1701/2015 This application is filed by applicant Manish Rajaram Bharati for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. I-379/2015 registered at Kashimira police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 354D of I.P.C. and section 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as ''P.O.C.S.O. Act''). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant/accused used to stalk the victim girl and at the time of incident he obstructed her by applying criminal force against her and pulled her clothes on her person and also held her hand with intent to outrage her modesty. It is further contended and argued that no such incident as alleged has happened and the applicant is falsely implicated in this crime with ulterior motive with a view to harass him and to cause mental tension to him. It is also submitted that the accused is a student and his incarceration is causing obstruction in his studies. It is further submitted that looking to the nature of allegation, further custody of the accused is not required. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co-operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that the applicant/accused was always following the victim girl and used to stalk her with intent to foster personal interaction with her. It is further contended and argued that at the time of incident the accused obstructed the victim girl in front .. 2 .. Bail No. 1701/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1.) of public toilet on public road and made her to stop by catching hold of her clothes on her person and then also held her hand so as to compel her to come with him and in this manner he outraged her modesty. It is further contended and argued that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl and other prosecution witnesses and he may tamper with prosecution evidence and even he may abscond and may not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 354D of I.P.C. and section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, the victim girl is stated to be 15 years old and it is contended on behalf of applicant/accused that he has been falsely implicated in this crime with ulterior motive only with a view to cause mental tension to him and he has not indulged any activity of outraging modesty of the victim girl. In such circumstance the aspect as to whether the allegations against the accused are genuine or the contention of the accused that he is falsely implicated is probable, would be the question to be decided on merits. Even nothing is to be recovered from the applicant/accused. 4] Then, it is also stated on behalf of applicant/accused that though the investigation in this matter is in progress, looking to the nature of allegation further custody of the accused is not required in this crime. Then, it is also stated that he is a student and since he is jail he is missing his studies. 5] Then, it is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail .. 3 .. Bail No. 1701/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1.) and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 6] Then, so far as the apprehension is expressed on behalf of prosecution that since the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 7] Then, it has also to be mentioned that though the investigation in the matter is stated to be in progress and even the charge sheet is yet to be submitted, it would take time to complete the investigation and then submit the charge-sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 8] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order - ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Manish Rajaram Bharati is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/- [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety .. 4 .. Bail No. 1701/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1.) in the like amount, subject to following conditions - The applicant/accused shall attend the concerned police station as and when called for the purpose of investigation/enquiry till filing of the charge-sheet and shall co-operate in investigation. He shall not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and the prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this Court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 30.07.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Additional Sessions Judge-1, Thane.

(Delivered on 29th day of January, 2019) [1] The accused committed rape on a minor girl 'S' (name of the victim girl is not mentioned) and threatened her to kill. Hence, accused is facing trial U/Sec.376 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code (in short I.P.C.) and U/Sec.4 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (in short POCSO Act.) [2] Brief facts of the prosecution case are as under : i) 'S',the victim girl is the daughter of Lilawati (PW 7). On 14/4/2016 'S' alongwith her mother and one neighbour Kusum(P.W.3) were proceeding to market. On the way 'S' felt giddiness and collapsed. Therefore, her mother and said Kusum took her to the dispensary of Dr. Mrutyunjay Prasad (P.W.4). After examination said Dr.Mrutyunjay informed the mother of the victim girl that said 'S' is pregnant. Thereafter, on enquiry 'S' disclosed her mother that about 6 months prior to that day she had acquainted with accused Wasim who was residing in the same building and they had talking terms with each other. ii) 'S' further disclosed that in the month of November, 2015 when she alone had been to the house, accused Vasim entered in the house at about 6.00 p.m. and removed her salwar and own pant and after laying her on the bed committed rape on her. At that time he threatened her that if she AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.173/2016 (Judgment). : 3: Special Case No.173/2016 (Judgment) CNR­MHTH01­004590­2016 disclosed the said incident to anybody he will kill her. Therefore, she did not disclose the said incident to anybody. After 2 days of 'Chatpuja' the accused again entered into her house and committed rape and that time also he threatened her to kill. Therefore, Lilawati, the mother of the victim girl disclosed the same to her husband and thereafter on 15/4/2016 they went to Mumbra Police Station and lodged report about the incident. At the time of the said incident the victim girl was about 14 yrs. old. iii) On the basis of F.I.R. lodged by the informant crime vide C.R.No.I­187/2016 U/Sec.376 506 of I.P.C. and U/Sec.4 of the POCSO Act came to be registered and handed over to API Bendre for investigation. [3] I.O. API Bendre on 15/4/2016 visited to the spot of incident and prepared panchanama of the spot in presence of panch witnesses. On the same day, he got recorded statements of 'S' through woman Police Constable Desai. Thereafter, he arrested the accused on the same day and prepared panchanama to that effect. On 16/4/2016 the I.O. forwarded 'S' for medical examination to the Chatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Hospital, Kalwa. Thereafter, he recorded statements of the witnesses and collected bonafide certificate of 'S' from her school. On 19/4/2016 the I.O. got medically examined the accused from Chatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Hospital, Kalwa. In AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.173/2016 (Judgment). : 4: Special Case No.173/2016 (Judgment) CNR­MHTH01­004590­2016 the meanwhile he got report from the medical officer showing that the 'S' was carrying about 21 weeks pregnancy. Therefore, he got collected DNA sample of the victim girl and the accused through doctors of Chatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Hospital, Kalwa. Thereafter, on 22/4/2016 he got done ossification test of the victim girl for determining her age. Thereafter, he forwarded the said blood sample to F.S.L. Kalina for chemical analysis. On completion of the investigation he submitted chargesheet against the accused U/Secs. 376 & 506 of I.P.C. and U/Sec.4 of the POCSO Act. [4] Since the offences leveled against the accused are triable by the Court of Sessions and the Special Court, the Ld. Magistrate committed the said case to this Court. [5] I have framed charge against the accused U/Sec.376 and 506(2) of IPC and U/Sec.4 of the POCSO Act. Particulars of offences were read over and explained to the accused to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. [6] Statement of the accused U/Sec.313 of Cr.P.C. is recorded. He denied that he committed rape on the victim girl. However, according to him he and the victim girl was having loveship and they want to marry each other. At that time she was about 18 years old. Since he was belonging to Muslim religion and she was belonging to Hindu religion, her parents AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.173/2016 (Judgment). : 5: Special Case No.173/2016 (Judgment) CNR­MHTH01­004590­2016 were opposing to the said relationship and therefore they have falsely implicated him in the present matter. [7] Following points arise for my determination. I have recorded my findings thereon for the reasons stated below : Sr. POINTS FINDINGS No. 1 Whether the prosecution proves that the accused committed rape on the minor victim girl 'S' ? Not proved. 2 Whether the prosecution proves that the accused committed criminal intimidation by threatening to minor victim girl 'S' with injury to her person with intent to cause alarm to her ? Not proved. 3 Whether the prosecution proves that the accused committed penetrative sexual assault on minor victim girl 'S' ? Not proved. 4 What order ? Accused is acquitted. REASONS AS TO POINTS NOS. 1 to 3 :­ [8] Since all the points for determination arose for one and the same incident, I took them together for discussion. AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.173/2016 (Judgment). : 6: Special Case No.173/2016 (Judgment) CNR­MHTH01­004590­2016 [9] To attract ingredients of the Sec.4 of the POCSO Act, the victim must be child. As per Sec.2(d) of the POCSO Act “Child” means any person below the age of 18 years. Thus, first of all it is for the prosecution to prove that at the time of incident 'S', the victim girl was below the age of 18 yrs. [10] 'S' (P.W.6) is the victim girl. According to her oral evidence her birth date is 07/02/2002. Lilawati (P.W.7) is the mother of 'S'. According to her birth date of 'S' is 07/01/2002. However, it is interesting to note that in her cross­examination Lilawati (P.W.7) was asked one question and she answered to the said question as follows : Question­ Whether at the time of admission of 'S' in 5 th standard in Sumantai Chavan School have you stated her date of birth as 07/01/2001 ? Answer: Yes. We had disclosed the same date, however, school administration informed us that her date of birth will be recorded as per earlier school certificate which is according to us is wrong. [11] Lilawati (P.W.7) also admitted in her cross­ examination that her daughter 'S' was born at Gorakhpur, U.P. She has not supplied birth certificate of 'S' to the school which was issued by Gorakhpur Municipality. [12] Suresh Chavan (P.W.10) the Head­Master of Sumanai Chavan Vidyalay where the victim girl was admitted in AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.173/2016 (Judgment). : 7: Special Case No.173/2016 (Judgment) CNR­MHTH01­004590­2016 6th standard. The said head­master issued bonafide certificate (Exh.52) showing the date of birth of 'S' as 10/10/2003. [13] In his cross­examination Suresh Chavan (P.W.10) admitted that they had not called for any record from the earlier school to verify birth date of 'S'. They have also not called for birth certificate of 'S'. [14] As regards to discrepancy regarding the birth­date of the victim girl, Ld. A.P.P. Smt.Chandane by placing reliance upon the case law, Ayub Babu Irani V/s. The State of Maharashtra, 2018 ALL MR (Cri) 55 and submitted that the alleged incident took place in the month of November, 2015. At that time the victim girl was about 14 years old. She was minor. No doubt, there is discrepancy in evidence regarding the date of birth amongst the prosecution witnesses, however, since ossification test shows her age below 18 years, such discrepancy regarding stating incorrect date of birth is irrelevant and thus the prosecution has proved that at the time of the incident the victim girl was minor. [15] The Ld.A.P.P. Smt.Chandane further submitted that there is no procedure prescribed under the POCSO Act for determining the age of child victim. However, in view of provisions of Sec.42A of POCSO Act the court can very well AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.173/2016 (Judgment). : 8: Special Case No.173/2016 (Judgment) CNR­MHTH01­004590­2016 follow the procedure contemplated in the Juvenile Justice Rules for the said purpose. The prosecution has take the every effort to prove the age of the victim girl. Ossification test of the victim girl was also conducted and from the available material on record, it is proved that at the time of the incident the victim girl was below the age of 18 years. In support of her argument she relied upon the case law, Subramaniam V/s. The State of Tamil Nadu, 1017 ALL MR (Cri) JOURNAL 170 (Madras High Court). [16] It is further submitted by the Ld.A.P.P.Smt.Chandane that date of birth of the victim girl has been proved by the prosecution. When the victim had alone been to her house, the accused entered in her house and committed rape on her and also threatened her to kill. Her evidence is supported by her mother as well as the medical evidence that the victim girl was carrying pregnancy and later on she gave birth to a baby. Moreover, DNA report of the said baby concluded that the accused and the victim girl are biological parents of the said baby. This much evidence is sufficient and cogent to prove the guilt of accused for the charges leveled against him. In support of her argument Ld. A.P.P. relied upon the case law, Sonu @ Suraj s/o. Dhanraj Pathdevate V/s. The State of Maharashtra, 2017 ALL MR (Cri) 1480. AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.173/2016 (Judgment). : 9: Special Case No.173/2016 (Judgment) CNR­MHTH01­004590­2016 [17] On the other hand, Ld. Advocate Shri.Bhamre for the accused submitted that provisions of the POCSO Act being stringent, the prosecution has to prove that at the time of the incident, the victim was minor. For that purpose prosecution has to establish date of birth of the victim beyond reasonable doubts. In support of his argument he relied upon the case law, Deepak s/o. Jitendra Sawant V/s. The State of Maharashtra, 2017 ALL MR (Cri) 2058, wherein the Hon'ble Division Bench of Bombay High Court (Nagpur Bench) observed that “there is no whisper in the F.I.R. about the date of birth of the prosecutrix. I.O. did not bother to collect material to prove date of birth. Thus, the prosecution failed to prove that victim was a child at the time of incident. Therefore, accused cannot be convicted under the POCSO Act”. It is further observed that “victim did not disclose the incident for two years. She was not a child of too tender age. She was a girl of sufficient maturity. Therefore, conduct of prosecutrix does not rule out theory of consent. Consent would be irrelevant if she is proved to be a minor. Therefore, it was essentially for the prosecution to prove case beyond reasonable doubt including the age of the prosecutrix which it failed to do. In such case sole testimony of the prosecutrix cannot be relied upon to hold conviction of the accused”. AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.173/2016 (Judgment). : 10 : Special Case No.173/2016 (Judgment) CNR­MHTH01­004590­2016 [18] Ld.Advocate for the accused also relied upon the case law, Umesh Rajabhau Khandekar V/s. The State of Maharashtra, 2015 ALL MR (Cri) 4006. In this case also the Hon'ble Single Bench of High Court of Bombay held that prosecution failed to prove beyond reasonable doubt that the victim was below 18 years old at the time of incident. Hence, the accused is entitled for acquittal. [19] It is further argued by the Ld.Advocate for the accused that no doubt the prosecution has examined Dr.Rajeshwar Patil(PW 8) who allegedly conducted ossification test of the victim girl and opined the age of the victim girl to be of 14 years plus or minus 6 month. However, evidence of Dr.Rajeshwar Patil is not reliable because though at the time of said ossification test x­rays of bones of the victim girl were taken, neither the said x­ray plates have been produced before him nor before the Court. Similarly Dr. Rajeshwar Patil is not a radiologist. The prosecution has not examined the person who took x­rays or the radiologist who gave his opinion regarding the age of the victim girl on the basis of said x­rays. Therefore, the evidence of Dr.Rajeshwar Patil (P.W.8) is not of use to ascertain the age of the victim girl. In support of his argument Ld.Advocate for the accused relied upon the case law, Prashant s/o. Daulat Korwate V/s. State of Maharashtra, 2018 ALL MR (Cri) 3909, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Bombay AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.173/2016 (Judgment). : 11 : Special Case No.173/2016 (Judgment) CNR­MHTH01­004590­2016 observed that “primary evidence regarding date of birth of victim though available was not produced by the prosecution. Ossification test report stating that prosecutrix appears to be of age between 15 to 16 years, however, x­ray plates on the basis of which Radiologist formed such opinion and handed over to I.O. not filed along with chargesheet. Moreover, the Radiologist stated that he has not taken the x­rays as it was not his duty. Person who took x­ray, not examined by the prosecution. Thus, nothing on record to show that it is only x­ray of victim which were placed before Radiologist on the basis of which he formed his opinion. Hence, evidence of Radiologist cannot be relied to determine age of the victim”. [20] Ld.Advocate for the accused further relied upon the case laws, Kiran s/o. Ashok Gawali V/s. The State of Maharashtra, 2018 ALL MR (Cri) 1551 and Mohan Ambadas Meshram V/s. State of Maharashtra, 2018 ALL MR (Cri) 4362, wherein it is mainly held that evidence of the prosecutrix falls in the category of witness that was neither wholly reliable nor wholly unreliable. Corroboration of her evidence becomes crucial for proving the prosecution case. [21] In the light of above mentioned case laws and the arguments advanced by both the sides, it appears that the AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.173/2016 (Judgment). : 12 : Special Case No.173/2016 (Judgment) CNR­MHTH01­004590­2016 victim girl stated her date of birth as 7/2/2002, whereas her mother Lilavati (P.W.7) categorically admitted that date of birth recorded in her school is not correct. 'S' (P.W.6) the victim girl was born at Gorakhpur. However, the I.O. has not taken that much pains to go to the birthplace of the victim girl and collect her birth certificate from the local authority. Similarly Suresh Chavan (P.W.10) the Head­master has admitted that date of birth shown in the bonafide certificate (Exh.54) is recorded as per the record of previous certificate of the victim girl. He has not called for any other record to verify the correctness of the birth­date given in the said documents. [22] So far as ossification test of the victim girl is concerned, it appears that Dr.Rajeshwar Patil (P.W.8) is not the person who took x­ray of the victim girl nor he is the Radiologist. The prosecution has not examined the Radiologist who opined about the age of the victim girl on the basis of said x­rays , nor examined the technician who took x­rays. Thus, nothing on record to show that it is only x­ray of victim which were placed before Radiologist on the basis of which he formed his opinion. Therefore, in my opinion evidence of Dr.Rajeshwar (P.W.8) is also not sufficient and cogent to determine the age of victim girl. Thus, in short it can be said that the prosecution has not brought sufficient and cogent evidence to prove the age of the victim girl. AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.173/2016 (Judgment). : 13 : Special Case No.173/2016 (Judgment) CNR­MHTH01­004590­2016 [23] Prosecution mainly relied upon the DNA report (Exh.19) wherein the accused and 'S', the victim girl are concluded to be the biological parents of baby 'S' the victim girl. However, before placing reliance upon the said DNA report, the prosecution must prove beyond all reasonable doubts that the DNA samples which were given to F.S.L. Kalina were of the accused, the victim girl and the baby of the victim girl. In his evidence A.P.I. Bendre (P.W.9), the I.O. states that he got collected DNA sample of the victim girl and the accused. However, he has not recorded the statement of the doctor or the person who actually collected the said DNA sample. [24] Dr.Sheweta Pandya (P.W.5) is the person to whom the victim girl was referred to for medical examination at Chatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Hospital, Kalwa. Her evidence shows that on 16/4/2016 the victim girl was brought before her by Woman Police Constable for medical examination. However, the victim girl did not give consent for medical examination. Therefore, she could not examine her medically. Her evidence further shows that the victim girl was referred for sonography of abdomen and pelvis. Thereafter, her sonography was done and on going through the said sonography report it was found that the victim girl was carrying 21 weeks pregnancy. Therefore, they advised her not to abort the pregnancy, but to AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.173/2016 (Judgment). : 14 : Special Case No.173/2016 (Judgment) CNR­MHTH01­004590­2016 deliver the child. However, it is pertinent to note that the prosecution has not produced any material to show that the sonography examination of the victim girl was conducted and the expert medical person opined about pregnancy of the victim girl. The person who actually conducted Sonography has not been examined by the prosecution. In absence of such material evidence on the record it is difficult to hold that the alleged Sonography of the victim girl was conducted and she was found pregnant of 21 weeks. Dr.Shweta Pandya also admitted in her cross­examination that she has not collected DNA sample of the victim girl, since the said facility was not available in the said Chatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Hospital, Kalwa. Therefore, question remains that when and how the I.O. got collected DNA sample of the victim girl and the accused. These, unanswered and unexplained questions create doubt about the genuineness of the prosecution case. Therefore, it cannot be held that the victim girl was carrying 21 weeks pregnancy and DNA samples of the victim girl and the accused were collected as alleged by the prosecution. [25] A.P.I.Bendre the I.O. (P.W.9) states that after completion of the investigation he submitted chargesheet against the accused. Thereafter, the victim girl delivered the child. He got blood sample of the said child through the medical officer of Chatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Hospital, Kalwa and AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.173/2016 (Judgment). : 15 : Special Case No.173/2016 (Judgment) CNR­MHTH01­004590­2016 forwarded the same to F.S.L. Kalina for examination and thereafter he produced DNA report on the record. However, there is no evidence adduced by the prosecution that on what date and place the said victim girl delivered a child. So also there is no evidence on the part of the prosecution that who, when and where collected blood sample of child of the victim girl for DNA purpose. On the contrary, evidence of Dr. Shweta Pandya (P.W.5) is inconsistent to the evidence of A.P.I.Bendre (P.W.9) which shows that there was no facility of taking DNA sample at Chatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Hospital, Kalwa. Therefore, it cannot be concluded that the DNA samples which were forwarded to F.S.L.Kalina for analysis were of the victim girl, the accused and the baby of the victim girl. Therefore, the said DNA report (Exh.19) cannot be said to be reliable to ascertain that the victim girl and the accused are the biological parents of the said baby of the victim girl. [26] So far oral testimony of the victim girl is concerned, as per the case law Mohan Ambadas Meshram V/s. State f Maharashtra, 2018 ALL MR (Cri) 4362 , her evidence is neither wholly reliable nor wholly unreliable. Therefore, corroboration of her evidence is crucial for proving the prosecution case. There is no eye witness to the incident. On the contrary, 'S' (P.W.6) the victim girl in her cross­examination stated that at the time of recording statement before police she AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.173/2016 (Judgment). : 16 : Special Case No.173/2016 (Judgment) CNR­MHTH01­004590­2016 has not stated that the accused forcibly raped her twice. She has further admitted that she disclosed before the said lady Dr.Shewta Pandya (P.W.5) that she had love affair with accused Vasim. She has also disclosed before the said lady doctor that alleged sexual intercourse was done with her consent. It also appears that the victim girl did not disclose the incident for about 6 months. She was not a child of too tender age. It also appears that she was a girl of sufficient maturity. Therefore, conduct of the victim girl does not rule out theory of consent. Consent of the victim girl would have been irrelevant if she would have been proved to be minor. It was necessary for the prosecution to prove case beyond reasonable doubt including the age of the victim girl which it failed to do. In such circumstances, sole testimony of the victim girl cannot be relied upon to hold the accused guilty. [27] On going through the material placed on record and for the reasons stated above, I can safely conclude that the prosecution has not brought sufficient and cogent evidence to prove the guilt of accused U/Sec.376 and 506(2) of IPC and U/Sec.4 of POCSO Act. I, therefore, answer point Nos.1 to 3 in the negative. POINT NO.4 : [28] As mentioned above the prosecution has failed to prove guilt of accused U/Secs. U/Sec.376 and 506(2) of IPC AVP/­ Spl.Case.No.173/2016 (Judgment). : 17 : Special Case No.173/2016 (Judgment) CNR­MHTH01­004590­2016 and U/Sec.4 of POCSO Act. Hence, the accused is entitled to be acquitted. I, therefore, in answer to point No.4 pass the following order : :ORDER: 1) Accused Wasim Khurshid Shaikh is hereby acquitted of the offences punishable U/Sec 376 and 506(2) of the Indian Penal Code and U/Sec.4 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 vide Sec.235(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 2) The accused shall furnish P.R.bond of Rs.15,000/­ (Rs.Fifteen Thousand only) and surety of like amount in compliance with the provisions of Sec. 437­A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 3) Accused is in jail. He be released forthwith, if not required in any other matter. 4) Issue letter accordingly to the concerned Jail Authority. Thane. Dated: 29/01/2019 ( S. B. Bahalkar ) Special Judge, Thane. Sadashiv Ramchandra Ghatal Age 57 years, Occ:Labour R/at. Varlipada, Adivasi Chawl, Near water tank, Shrinagar, Wagle Estate, Thane. ..... Accused. Offence punishable under Sections 354,323,504,506 of Indian Penal Code and Section 7 punishable under 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offence Act, 2012. Appearance: A.P.P. Shri.Vinit Kulkarni for the prosecution. Advocate Shri.Bhanushali for the accused. JUDGMENT (Delivered on this 13th Day of September, 2017) The accused is charged for the offence under section 354, 323, 504, 506 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 7 punishable under section 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offence Act, 2012. The case of the prosecution is that:­ 2. On 03.06.2014 at about 10.00 p.m., at Warlipada, New Water tank, Shrinagar, Wagle Estate, Thane, accused committed sexual assault upon the minor victim aged 17 years. He also beat her, abused and threatened her. It is also alleged that the accused with sexual intent to outraged the modesty of minor victim. Therefore, the victim lodged FIR in Shrinagar police station Thane. C.R.No.I­146/2014 was registered under section under section 354, 323, 504, 506 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 7 punishable under section 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offence Act, 2012. Investigating Officer Shri.P.P.Gonjari investigated the offence. He recorded the statements of witnesses, prepared panchanama of the spot, arrested the accused and after routine investigation he sent chargesheet. 3. Charge was framed against accused at Exh.8 under section under section 354, 323, 504, 506 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 7 punishable under section 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offence Act, 2012. The accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 4. Considering the evidence on record following points arose for my determination. I have given its findings with reasons as under:­ Sr.No Points Findings 1. Does prosecution prove that on In the Negative. 03.06.2014 at about 10.00 p.m., at Varlipapda, near water tank, Shrinagar, Wagle Estate,Thane, accused committed assault or used criminal force with intent to outrage modesty of minor victim aged 17 years and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 354 of the IPC ? 2. Does prosecution prove that on the In the Negative same, date, time and place accused voluntarily caused hurt to the victim aged 17 years and thereby committed an offence under section 323 read with 34 of the IPC ? 3 Does prosecution prove that on the In the Negative same, date, time and place accused intentionally insulted the victim in filthy language and thereby gave provocation to break the public peace and thereby committed an offence under section 504 of Indian Penal Code? 4 Does prosecution prove that on the In the Negative same, date, time and place accused committed criminal intimidation by threatening the victim to cause injury to her and her reputation with intent to cause alarm to the victim and thereby committed an offence under section 506 of Indian Penal Code? 5 Does prosecution prove that on the In the Negative same, date, time and place accused committed sexual assault on the minor victim aged 17 years and thereby committed an offence under section 7 punishable under section 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offence Act, 2012? 6 What order? As per final order. REASONS AS TO POINT NO.1 TO 4:­ 5. To prove the offence prosecution has examined the victim at Exh.10. P.W.2 mother of the victim at Exh.13. P.W.3 Head Constable Priyanka Pankaj Gonjari at Exh.18. The prosecution closed the evidence by pursis at Exh.20. 6. It has come in the evidence of P.W.1 that the she resides at Varlipada. She does work of cutting vegetables and pack it. She used to go to her work at 9.00 a.m. and come back at 3.00 p.m. She knows the accused as he resides in her neighbourhood. The victim's father has habit to drink liquor. Accused used to come to her father for drinking liquor. If her father did not give him liquor he used to abuse him. Once the accused has asked her father to give his daughter to him he will become father of his daughter, but at that time she had not lodged complaint. 7. It has further come in her evidence that on 03.06.2014 at 9.30 p.m. the victim was going for bringing bread. While she was going through lane near their house the accused was standing there. The accused touched her breast. She she asked him why he did so. The accused replied that what happened if he had touched her. Then two daughters of accused came there and beaten her. Then she lodged FIR at Exh.11 on 05.06.2014. The victim's mother P.W.2 has supported the victim that victim had narrated the incident to her. 8. It has come in the cross examination of the victim that on 03.06.2014 she had lodged N.C complaint against accused and his two daughters Laxmi and Parvati in Shrinagar police station. That complaint is marked at Exh.12. In that complaint she had mentioned that Laxmi and Parvati stretched her hairs and given abuses. She informed this incident to Father Joseph. She admitted that she had not gone to the police station on 04.06.2014. She discussed with her mother for lodging the complaint. She admitted that while lodging N.C complaint Exh.12 she has not stated about insulting and affecting modesty of her by the accused. She admits that she was feeling better on 04.06.2014, but she did not lodge complaint to police on that day. 9. Investigating Officer P.W.3 admitted that she has not examined persons who were playing cards in the lane on the day of incident. She admitted that there was quarrel between victim and daughter of accused before the incident and in the N.C complaint the victim has not stated the act of assaulting modesty. 10. I heard the Ld. A.P.P on behalf of the prosecution. The victim herself had also engaged private Advocate who has given some points of arguments and relied on certain case laws as below:­ In case of State of Punjab V/s. Gurmit Singh and others in Criminal Appeal No.616/1985 decided on 16.01.1996 S.C. It was held that, “ minor contradictions or insignificant discrepancies in the statement of the prosecutrix, which are not of a fatal nature, to throw out an otherwise reliable prosecution case. If evidence of the prosecutrix inspires confidence.” In case of Childline India Foundation and Another V/s. Allan John Waters and Ors in Criminal Appeal Nos.1205­1207 and 1208­1210 of 2008 decided on 18.03.2011 S.C. It was held that, “delay in divulging the facts of beating and also of sexual abuse to any other person does not mean that there is no sexual exploitation or abuse or that they were deterred on that they were deposed falsely as per the design of some other person. In case of Rajinder @ Raju V/s. State of H.P. Criminal Appeal No.670/2003 decided on 07.07.2009 S.C. It was held that, “ conviction in case of sex crimes may be based on sole testimony of prosecutrix.” 11. In reply the Ld. Counsel on behalf of the accused submitted that there is delay of three days in lodging the FIR that delay is not explained in the FIR or in the evidence of the prosecutrix. However, the prosecutrix has immediately lodged N.C complaint in Shrinagar police station which is at Exh.12. It disclosed that there was altercation between the two daughters, accused and one woman and there were abuses against each other. In that complaint no where mentioned about the assaulting against her modesty. The Counsel argued that the victim discussed with her mother and father Joseph and after thought she lodged complaint. It is false because at the first instance she has not disclosed about the assault against her modesty and therefore, no reliance can be placed upon the evidence of prosecutrix and her mother. Therefore, he prayed that accused may be acquitted. 12. Considering the evidence on record the court is of the view that it is evident that on 03.06.2014 the alleged incident took place in the lane near the house of victim at about 10.00 p.m. The victim immediately went to the concerned police station and lodged N.C complaint that N.C complaint is on record at Exh.12. It is mentioned in that N.C complaint that it was lodged at about 10.30 p.m. on 03.06.2014 against Laxmi and Parvati and father of Laxmi and Parvati and one woman, her name is not mentioned. It is mentioned that when the prosecutrix was going through the narrow lane near her house the father of Laxmi and Parvati was coming from opposite side. The prosecutrix asked her whether he could not walk properly at that time the unknown woman told her that he has not dashed her so why she was talking in that manner. At that time the father of Laxmi and Parvati abused her and Laxmi and Parvati stretched her hairs and beat her with fist blows. In that complaint she has no where mentioned that the father of Laxmi and Parvati touched her breast with sexual intent. 13. From the contents in the N.C complaint Exh.12 it appears that one more woman was also present at the time of incident and two daughter of the accused were also present there. In her evidence she admits that two persons were playing cards in the lane. Even the prosecutrix did not receive any dash of the accused she had asked the accused whether he could not walk properly and upon that instigation there was altercation between them 14. It appears from the N.C complaint that she immediately lodged N.C to the concerned police station. She is 17 years old and she working so she is matured enough. She has mother and father so she could have immediately complained to the police about the incident. She could have narrated above sexual assault immediately. There was no difficulty for her, but she did not disclose about the sexual assault in the N.C complaint nor she had reported immediately thereafter. But after three days on 05.06.2014 she lodged the F.I.R at about 9.15 p.m. in which there is no explanation of delay is mentioned. In her evidence she has stated that on 04.06.2014 she was feeling better so on that day she could have lodged FIR. But she did not do so. The court is of the view that the prsoecutrix is aged 17 years she is attained the maturity, she knows the nature of conduct . She knows what is bad and what is good. She has understanding capacity so non disclosure of the incident immediately to the concerned police station is fatal to the case of prosecution. The complaint which is lodged on 05.06.2014 appears to be after thought, concocted and false. In the N.C complaint she did not narrate the above alleged sexual assault and therefore, delayed FIR appears to be after thought. Therefore, no reliance can be placed upon the evidence of prosecutrix. 15. As per the evidence of prosecutrix in the lane some persons were sitting for playing cards. Those persons are not examined. One woman was also present there against whom N.C complaint was lodged. Her statement was also not recorded. Two daughters of the accused are not made accused in this case and therefore, there is no investigation in respect of the offence under section 323, 504 and 506 of Indian Penal Code. Therefore the prosecution could not prove the offences beyond doubt. 16. Considering the reasons given above the court is of the view that the case of prosecution appears to be doubtful and therefore, the benefit of doubt goes in favour of accused. 17. I am of the view that the facts of above cited cases are different than the present facts. Hence, I answered the points in the negative and proceed to pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused Sadashiv Ramchandra Ghatal is acquitted under Section 235(1) of Cr.P.C. of the offence charged under sections 354, 323, 504, 506 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 7 punishable under section 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offence Act, 2012. 2] Accused is directed to furnish P.B. and S.B. of Rs.15,000/­ (Rupees Fifteen Thousand Only) to comply provision of section 437 (A) of Cr. P.C. 3] The Judgment is dictated and pronounced in open Court. Thane. ( S.C. Khalipe ) Date: 13/09/2017 Additional Sessions Judge,Thane.

.. 1 .. Special Case No. 42/2013 Judgment Received on : 19.08.2013 Registered on : 19.08.2013 Decided on : 09.10.2015 Duration : 2 years 1 month 20 days IN THE COURT OF THE SESSION JUDGE, THANE AT THANE (Presided over by Ms.V.V.Virkar, Additional Session Judge-1, Thane) Special Case No. 42 of 2013 Exhibit No. 21 The State of Maharashtra … Complainant versus Mahendra Ramlal Choudhary ... Accused Age 37 years, Resident of near Ghansoli creek, at construction site, Ghansoli, Navi Mumbai. Appearance - Ms. R.A.Navale, learned Additional Public Prosecutor (hereinafter in short A.P.P.) Accused in person. JUDGMENT (Delivered on 09.10.2015) The accused stands prosecuted for the offence punisable under section 354 of I.P.C. and section 7 read with section 8 and section 11 read with section 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences .. 2 .. Special Case No. 42/2013 Judgment Act (hereinafter in short referred to as ''P.O.C.S.O. Act'') for outraging modesty of victim girl Rutuja Sarpane aged 11 years on 09.03.2013 around 10.00 a.m. at Ghansoli, Navi Mumbia, on road by accosting her from time to time and using criminal force and moving his hand on her breast on the given date and committing act of sexual assault and harassment upon her. 2] In short the facts giving rise to the prosecution of the accused are that girl Rutuja was staying with her parents ar Arjunwadi, Ghansoli, in room no.2281 and was studying in 5 th Std. in N.M.M.C. school and her school timing was from 12.00 noon to 5.30 p.m. The accused had been staying in the same area and therefore was of acquaintance of her parents and also the girl. It is also case of the prosecution that since about one month prior to complaint the accused used to chase the girl and had tried to offer her chocolate but she refused and the girl had even stated about it to her parents and they had even persuaded the accused but there was no change in his behaviour and he continued with his activities. That on 09.03.2013 around 10.00 a.m. the left the house for repairing her schoolbag and when she was on her way the accused accosted her, offered her chocolate and had moved his hand on her breast and face, she was scared and immediately returned home crying and narrated the incident to her mother. Her mother then informed about it to her husband after her returned home and then they went to police station and she lodged complaint. In the meantime the people gathered at the spot had caught the accused and had beaten him and had taken him to police station. 3] On the basis of her complaint, offence as per C.R.No. 106/2013 for offences punishable under section 354 of I.P.C. and section 7, 8, 11, 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act was registered at Rabale Police Station .. 3 .. Special Case No. 42/2013 Judgment and the work of investigation was done by A.P.I. Vinod Gholve. During investigation the panchnama of the spot was prepared. Accused brought by people gathered was arrested. Since he was found to have sustained injuries, he was referred for medical examination. Statements of witnesses were recorded and after completion of investigation accused was charge-sheeted for offence punishable under section 354 of I.P.C. and under section 7, 8, 11, 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. 4] Offence under P.O.C.S.O. Act is triable by Special Court and therefore the charge-sheet was submitted to this Court. 5] The accused was produced before the Court. A charge for offences punishable under section 354 of I.P.C. and section 7 read with section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act was framed against the accused as per Exhibit 3. Contents of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. He pleaded not guilty. His defence was of total denial. He claimed to be tried. 6] For establishing guilt of accused, the prosecution examined P.W.1 complainant Vaishali Pappu Sarpane, mother of the girl, P.W.2 victim girl Rutuja Sarpane, P.W.3 panch witness Chandrakant Gaikwad, P.W.4 Radhakrishna Parkar, witness and P.W.5 A.P.I. Vinod Gholve, I.O. The documentary evidence produced, proved and relied upon by the prosecution was in the form of complaint Exhibit 10, arrest panchnama Exhibit 14, spot panchnama Exhibit 18. 7] Statement of the accused under section 313 of Cr.P.C. was recorded. He did not examine himself on oath and had not examined any witness in defence. .. 4 .. Special Case No. 42/2013 Judgment 8] On the basis of above facts of this case, the points which arose for my determination, my reasons and findings thereon are as under - Points Findings i) Whether the prosecution proved that on 09.03.2013 around 10.00 a.m. the accused used criminal force against the victim girl, daughter of the complainant, and moved his hand over her breast and face and Yes. thereby outraged her modesty ? ii ) Whether the prosecution prove that on the given day, date, time and place, the accused committed sexual assault and sexual harassment upon the minor victim by accosting her in her way and moving hand over her breast and Yes. face with sexual intent ? iii ) What offence, if any, is proved Offence u/s 354 of I.P.C. against the accused ? and sec. 7 read with sec. 8 and also sec. 11 read with sec. 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act are proved. iv ) What order ? As per the final order. REASONS As to point no.1 and 2 - Both points are interconnected and are to be decided on the basis of same evidence. I therefore discuss and decide them together. 9] As is clear, the accused alleged to have outraged modesty of the girl by chasing her time and again and also stated to have committed act of sexual assault and harassment upon girl Rutuja. In that .. 5 .. Special Case No. 42/2013 Judgment regard if the testimony of the girl P.W.2 is perused, she has categorically stated that on her way to school one person used to follow her and offer her chocolate and she used to refuse it. She also further stated that she narrated about it to her parents and her mother had even persuaded said person not to do such act again. She appear to have narrated the incident that on her way to school when she was going to repair schoolbag the same person offered her chocolate and when she refused he moved his hand on her breast and she was scared and went home and narrated incident to her mother. It is also material to mention that though she was not able to tell name of said person, she stated that she can identify said person if said person is shown and when single visibility curtain was removed, she identified the accused to be the same person. It has to be mentioned that the girl at the relevant time being child witness, it was ascertained that she was able to understand the questions put and answer it coherently and noticed that she was able to understand the question and answer it coherently and also was knowing the sanctity of oath. It is also further material to mention that in the light of that the aspect that she had narrated the facts in all material particulars , there is no reason to doubt the credibility or trustworthiness of the witness. Even as is clear the entire testimony of the witness has gone unchallenged since there is no cross-examination on behalf of accused except suggestion that no such incident had taken place and she is deposing falsely, which she denied. 10] It is material to mention that her version that she had narrated the instances of accused chasing her earlier and on the day of incident the instance of accused moving his hand on her breast etc. to her mother immediately, is corroborated by the testimony of her mother P.W.1 in all material particulars and the version of P.W.1 in that regard also has gone unchallenged and undisputed. Even so far as the fact that .. 6 .. Special Case No. 42/2013 Judgment the accused was caught by people gathered at the spot of incident and was taken to police station, also appear to have been stated by the complainant, the mother of the girl and also police witness P.W.5 I.O. Even that do not appear to have been disputed on behalf of the accused and only defence put forth by the accused in that regard is that without any reason people had caught him and took him to police station which cannot be said to be acceptable and believable even in preponderance of probability. 11] One more aspect of the matter that the complaint is lodged without any delay. Absolutely nothing is brought on record to show that there was any enmity, grudge or grievance against the accused to the complainant or the girl for which they could possibly make false complaint against the accused. It is not probable that without there being any enmity or previous rivalry, any such complaint with such allegations involving character of a minor girl would be made by the mother of the girl. If at all no such incident had taken place, there was no reason for the mother of the girl all the way to go to police station with the girl and file such complaint at the risk of defamation of her own daughter in the society making such false allegations and therefore, there appear no scope for any doubt that the allegations in the complaint are false. 12] Then, as is clear the accused is stated to be of acquaintance with mother of the girl as well as the girl and even the girl identified him before the Court to be the same person committing such act with her and therefore also there is no scope for any doubt that the accused was the person who committed such an act with the girl. 13] Then, from the material on record it has to be held that the prosecution has established that the accused had been chasing the girl .. 7 .. Special Case No. 42/2013 Judgment and offering her chocolate time and again and did not improve in spite of persuasion by her parents and even further on the date of incident also he accosted the girl, offered her chocolate and touched her body by moving hand on her breast and face when she refused to accept the chocolate. Needless to say that such an act committed by the accused with the girl of moving his hand on her breast was with culpable mental state of causing sexual intention. Even in the light of subsequent event of accused moving his hand on her breast when she refused to accept the chocolate offered by him, his earlier acts of chasing the girl and offering chocolate also has to be held as to have been committed with similar intention to commit such an act of sexual harassment. Even as per section 30 of P.O.C.S.O. Act in any prosecution for offence under this Act which require culpable mental state on the part of accused, the Special Court shall presume the existence of such mental state. No doubt, it is further provided in said section that it shall be a defence for the accused that he has no such mental state with respect to the act charged as an offence in that prosecution. However, in the present case the accused come up with the defence of total denial which is found to be not probable and acceptable and on the contrary, it is proved that the accused had committed such an act and therefore such presumption of culpable mental state of accused can be safely drawn. 14] Then, as per section 29 of the P.O.C.S.O. Act when a person is prosecuted for committing offence under section 7 and 9 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, the Special Court is empowered to presume that the accused committed such an act unless contrary is proved. Then, as discussed above, the accused has not brought any material on record to rebut the presumption and has not proved contrary to what the witnesses have stated and rather at the cost of repetition it can be said that the allegations against the accused are seen to have been .. 8 .. Special Case No. 42/2013 Judgment established beyond reasonable doubt and therefore under section 29 of P.O.C.S.O. Act also it has to be presumed that the accused has committed such an act. 15] As is clear, section 354 provides that ''Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any woman, intending to outrage or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby outrage her modesty, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than one year but which may extend to five yeas, and shall also be liable to fine. Section 7 of P.O.C.S.O. Act say that ''Whoever, with sexual intent touches the vagina, penis, anus or breast of the child or makes the child touch the vagina, penis, anus or breast of such person or any other person, or does any other act with sexual intent which involves physical contact without penetration is said to commit sexual assault ''. Section 11(iv) of P.O.C.S.O. Act defines sexual harassment that ''A person is said to commit sexual harassment upon a child when such person with sexual intent repeatedly or constantly follows or watches or contacts a child either directly or through electronic, digital or any other means ''. As such the acts which the accused is proved to have committed with the girl squarely fall within the definitions of said offences. 16] It is also to be mentioned that since the offences charged against the accused are under the provisions of P.O.C.S.O. Act, the prosecution is required to establish that the girl at the relevant time was child within the meaning of section 2(d) of P.O.C.S.O. Act. In that regard the mother of the girl as well as the girl stated that the girl at the relevant time was 11 years old and at the time of her evidence she stated her age .. 9 .. Special Case No. 42/2013 Judgment as 13 years. Then, though as per prosecution case the girl was 11 years old at the relevant time, no documentary evidence in regard to age of the girl is produced and therefore no conclusion in regard to the exact age of the girl can be drawn. However, the fact also cannot be ignored that the girl was examined before the Court and she was found to a child and her age was noticed to be around 13 years at the time of her evidence and even the testimony of the witnesses in regard to age stated by the girl and her mother has gone unchallenged therefore it has to be concluded that the girl was below 18 years of age at the relevant time and absence of birth certificate or documentary proof in that regard cannot be said to be fatal to the prosecution case in the facts and circumstances mentioned above. 17] Then, though it is argued on behalf of prosecution that the girl at the relevant time was 11 years old and therefore the act committed by the accused is an aggravated form of sexual assault and harassment as defined in section 9 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, it has to be mentioned that in absence of cogent and reliable evidence in regard to the exact age of the girl at the relevant time and when there is marginal difference in the age stated by the girl as around 11 years and for attracting the provisions of section 9 the girl is required to be below 12 years of age, I am of the view that such submissions on behalf of prosecution that the act of the accused falls within the purview of section 9 of the Act cannot be said to be sustainable. 18] In view of above discussion since the fact that the accused had outraged modesty and committed sexual assault and harassment upon the victim girl on the given day, date, time and place is established, the offences under section 354 of I.P.C. and section 7 read with section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and also under section 11 read with section 12 of .. 10 .. Special Case No. 42/2013 Judgment P.O.C.S.O. Act have to be held as established against the accused. Therefore, I hold the accused guilty for offence punishable under section 354 of I.P.C. and section 7 read with section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and also under section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and convict him for said offences. Point no.1 and 2 are answered accordingly in the affirmative. 19] At this stage the dictation of the Judgment is postponed for hearing the accused on the point of sentence. Date : 09.10.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Additional Session Judge-1, Thane. Resumed. 20] The accused is made aware of the fact that he is held guilty for the offences under section 354 of Indian penal Code and section 7 read with section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and also under section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and it is informed to him that the punishment prescribed for offence punishable under section 354 of I.P.C. is Imprisonment which shall not be less than one year but which may extend to five and also fine and punishment prescribed for offence under section 7 read with section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act is imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than three years but which may extend to five years and also fine and punishment prescribed for offence under section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act is imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and also fine. 21] I heard the learned A.P.P. and the accused on the point of sentence. The learned A.P.P. submitted that looking to the serious .. 11 .. Special Case No. 42/2013 Judgment nature of offence charged against the accused he is not entitled to leniency and he is liable to award maximum punishment prescribed. The accused prayed for showing him leniency on the ground that he is the only earning member in his family and his family is depending upon him for their livelihood. 22] So far as the quantum of sentence is concerned, it has to be mentioned that it is well settled that it is the duty of the Court in every case to award proper sentence, having regard to the nature of the offence, the manner in which it is committed and to all mitigating circumstances. Even it is also well settled that in the matter of fixation of punishment for any particular crime, the Court should take into consideration the nature of offence, the circumstances in which it was committed and the degree of deliberation shown by the offender and also that the measure of punishment should be proportionate to the gravity of the offence and it is also the responsibility of the Court to see that the sentence should not be excessive and at the same time it should not be too lenient or liberal. 23] Then, as is clear the offence charged against the accused is of serious nature with the allegation that he has outraged modesty of the minor girl by using criminal force against her and accosting her in her way and by moving his hand over her breast and face. 24] In the light of that I am of the view that following sentence would meet ends of justice. In the result I pass the following order - ORDER Accused namely Mahendra Ramlal Choudhary is convicted for offences punishable under section 354 of the Indian Penal Code and section 7 read with section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and also under section .. 12 .. Special Case No. 42/2013 Judgment 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. 2) The accused is sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for the period of six months and also to pay fine of Rs.100/- [rupees one hundred only] and in default of payment of fine amount, he shall undergo imprisonment for one day for offence punishable under section 354 of Indian Penal Code. 3) The accused is also sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for the period of three years and also to pay fine of Rs.500/- [rupees five hundred only] and in default of payment of fine amount, he shall undergo imprisonment for five days for offence under section 7 read with section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. 4) The accused is also sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for the period of six months and also to pay fine of Rs.100/- [rupees one hundred only] and in default of payment of fine amount, he shall undergo imprisonment for one day for offence punishable under section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. 5) All the substantive sentences shall run concurrently. 6) The accused is in jail since 09.03.2013. A set off under section 438 of Cr.P.C. is granted to him against the substantive sentence for the term of the period of detention undergone by him during the investigation, inquiry and trial. 7) Since no muddemal property is produced before Court, no order regarding its disposal is passed. 8) Copy of judgment be given to the accused free of cost. 9) The proceeding is closed. Thane. Date : 09.10.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Additional Session Judge-1,Thane.

Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­004624­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No. 162/2015 Received on : 17.07.2015 Registered on :17.072015 Decided on : 20.02.2018 Duration : 2Y.7Ms.3Ds. IN THE COURT OF D.J.­4 & ADDL. SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE (Presided over by Hemant M. Patwardhan) Special (POCSO) Case No.162/2015 Exh.No. 1.State of Maharashtra. (Wada Police station) ..Complainant V/s. 1. Sainath Krishna Thotaga Age :­ 22 years, R/at. Mangarul, Tal. Wada, Dist. Palghar ..Accused Appearance:­ APP Smt. Varsha Chandane for the State. Advocate Sms. Renu Sawang for the accused. JUDGMENT (Delivered on this 20th day of February 2017 ) Accused was facing trial under sections 363, 376, 344 of IPC and under sections 4, 8 and 10 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 on following facts:­ 1] That during 03.04.2015 at about 08.00 p.m. to 1 to 6 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­004624­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No. 162/2015 19.04.2015 at Mangarul, Tal. Wada, Dist. Palghar within jurisdiction of Wada police station accused has kidnapped a minor from the lawful guardianship of her parents and after kidnapping her has committed rape on her and also confined her for 10 days or more. According to allegation at the same time accused has committed penetrative sexual assault on a minor and continue to commit it in aggravated form. Hence, on complaint lodged by one Ashok Lote, an offence punishable under aforesaid sections came to be registered against accused. On completion of investigation he was charge­sheeted. 2] Charge was framed against accused below Exh.5 and contents of said charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. Accused pleaded not guilty and claim to be tried. His defence was of total denial. 3] Prosecution in order to prove guilt of accused has examined, victim as PW1 and complainant Ashok Lote as PW2. Then statement of accused was recorded as per his say wherein he has claim to be implicated in false case. Arguments of rival advocates were heard as prosecution has filed pursis informing the court that prosecution do not wish to adduce any further evidence. 4] Learned P.P.has pointed out that admission 2 to 6 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­004624­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No. 162/2015 obtained from complainant by defence in order to substantiate the fact same are sufficient to inferred the commission of offence by the accused and hence, requested to convict him as per the provisions of law. Per contra, it as argued by the defence that there is no evidence on record to show that accused himself has abducted the minor and then has committed rape on her. Hence, request has been made to acquit him. 5] On the basis of aforesaid rival arguments, following points arose for my consideration and I record my findings against each of them for the reasons noted below :­ Sr.N. Points Findings 1] Does the prosecution prove that accused in between ..Negative. 03.04.2015 at about 08.00 p.m. to 19.04.2015 at Mangarul, Tal. Wada, Dist. Palghar, within the jurisdiction of Wada Police Station, Dist. Palghar, kidnapped victim a minor aged 15 years 11 months from the lawful guardianship of her parents and that thereby committed an offence punishable under section 363 of Indian Penal Code ? 2] Does the prosecution prove that on the above date, time and ..Negative. place accused committed rape on victim a minor aged 15 years 11 months and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 376 of Indian Penal Code ? 3] Does the prosecution prove that on the above date, time and ..Negative. place accused wrongfully confined victim a minor aged 15 years 11 months for 10 days or more and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 344 of Indian Penal Code 4] Does the prosecution prove that on the above date, time and ..Negative. place accused committed penetrative sexual assault on victim a minor aged 15 years 11 months and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 4, 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act? 3 to 6 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­004624­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No. 162/2015 5] Does the prosecution prove that on the above date, time and ..Negative. place accused committed aggravated sexual assault on victim a minor aged 15 years 11 months and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 10 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 6] What order? Accused is acquitted as per final order. REASONS As to point no.1 to 6 :­ 6] Prosecution in order to establish the guilt of accused has examined aforesaid two witnesses. Out of which one was victim and other was the complainant­father of the victim. On perusal of victim's deposition it is apparent that she has categorically denied that accused has ever abducted her or kidnapped her from the lawful guardianship of her parents and then has either committed rape or aggravated form of sexual assault as alleged by the complainant. On the contrary she has claim that she on her own had been to her friend during that period and her father has misunderstood and has lodged the complaint. Though victim's father has claim that accused himself has abducted or kidnapped the victim in the cross­ examination he has admitted that as on date of deposition he do not wish to continue with the prosecution. Hence, if we consider said fact then prima facie it appears that initially though he has grudged against accused now he do not wish to continue it. 4 to 6 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­004624­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No. 162/2015 7] On the background of this evidence the court is required to consider whether the said evidence is sufficient to establish the necessary ingredients of the offence with which accused was charged. Admittedly as the prosecution has not examined any other witnesses other facts are not proved before the court. Victim when has categorically denied the fact of she being kidnapped by the accused or has been raped by him. It is difficult to accept that merely because complainant has alleged that accused has kidnapped her and has committed rape on her offence is committed. Further on perusal of the Analyst report it is apparent that Analyst nowhere opined about any aggravated form of sexual assault or commission of rape. Analyst has further observed that even no semen was detected on Exh.3,6,7 and 8. Having regards to the said facts, it is difficult to accept that any such act has been committed by the accused as alleged. Evidence before this court is inclusive, inconsistent accused cannot be convicted. Hence, I do not hesitate to record my findings against point no.1 to 5 in negative and proceed to pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused is acquitted from the offence punishable under sections 363, 376, 344 of IPC and under sections 4, 8 and 10 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 2] Bail bond of accused shall stands canceled. 5 to 6 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­004624­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No. 162/2015 3] Muddemal property being worthless be destroyed after appeal period. 4] Accused is directed to execute P.R. Bond of Rs.10,000/­ as per amended provisions of section 437(A) of Cr.P.C. and bonds so executed shall remain in force for the period of six months from the date of its execution. 5] Proceeding is accordingly closed. Thane (Hemant M.Patwardhan) Date: 20.02.2018 D.J.­4 & Additional Sessions Judge, Thane 6 to 6

--1-- ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN REGULAR BAIL APPLICATOIN NO.1729/2017 The applicant Sarvajeet Sewa Singh has applied for bail under section 439 of Cr. P.C. in C.R.No.I­132/2017 registered in Rabodi police station for the offence under section 354(1)(a),(b),(c) , 354(d) of Indian Penal Code and section 8, 12 of POCSO Act, 2012 read with 67 (B) (b) and (c) of Information Technology Act, 2000. 2. It is contended that the applicant is falsely implicated. He is innocent and he was arrested only on suspicion and misunderstanding. The offence is not punishable with death or imprisonment for life. The investigation is almost completed, therefore, the further custody of the applicant is not required. The applicant is ready to face the trial. Therefore, he may be released on bail. 3. The applicant has produced copy of FIR, his Adhar card, copy of Pan Card, electricity bill. 4. Investigating Officer has given his say at Exh.4. It is contended that after release of the accused he will tamper the prosecution witnesses and will repeat the offence. He has committed breach of trust. He is not permanent resident of the given address. 5. I heard Ld. Counsel on behalf of the accused and Ld. A.P.P. 6. The court is of the view that considering the nature of offence it is not punishable with death or imprisonment for life. The investigation is almost completed, therefore, further --2-- custody of the applicant is no more required. The applicant is ready to face the trial. There are no criminal antecedent and the applicant has given his address proof and he is ready to face the trial and abide by the conditions of bail. Hence, the order. ORDER 1. Application is allowed. 2. The applicant be released on P.B. and S.B. of Rs.20,000/­ (Rupees Twenty Thousand Only) with one or two local solvent sureties in like amount. 3. The applicant shall not leave the jurisdiction of the court. 5. The applicant shall not enter into the area where the victim and informant resides. 6. The applicant shall attend the court for trial. 7. The applicant shall not repeat the offence. 8. If any condition is breached the bail will be cancelled. Thane. ( S.C. Khalipe ) Date : 19/07/2017.
