1 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 163/2015 Judgment Received on :­ 17.07.2015 Registered on :­ 17.07.2015 Decided on :­ 20.04.2017 Duration :­ 1Y 09M 3 D IN THE COURT OF ADDITIONAL SESSIONS JUDGE, & SPECIAL JUDGE (POCSO) ACT, THANE AT : THANE ( Presided over by Ashutosh N.Karmarkar, District Judge­1 & Special Judge (POCSO) Act, Thane ) Special Case (POCSO) No.163/2015 Exh. No. State of Maharashtra ( Through Rabale Police Station ) …Complainant V/s. Jitendra Saybanna Jigjeni Age : 25 Years, Occ. : Driver, R/at.: Bhimnagar, Rabale, in front of Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar statue, Navi Mumbai. … Accused. Offence punishable under Sec. 354 of Indian Penal Code & under Sec.12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 163/2015 Judgment Appearances : Shri. S.D.Londhe, A.P.P. for the State Shri. B.N.Waghmare, Advocate for accused JUDGMENT ( Delivered on this 20th day of April, 2017 ) 1] Accused is facing trial for the offence punishable under Sec. 354 r/w. 34 of Indian Penal Code and under Sec.12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] Prosecution Case, in brief, is as under : Informant has one son and daughter. On 01.05.2015, there was some programme of “Jagran­gondhal' at her house. Her relatives and neighbour Laxmi and 13 year old daughter of Laxmi also attended the programme. When the programme was going on, daughter of informant and the daughter of Laxmi, both wanted to go for urination. Informant sent her son Laxman with them. They both proceeded for urination in a lane in front of one Shivshakti Jewellers. Within five minutes Laxman came and stated that when both victims went in a lane in front of Shivshakti Jewellers, two unknown persons came on motorcycle. Out of them one person got down and caught hold the hand of both the victims and Laxman gave kick to him. He narrated the incident to relatives. The persons named Anil, Manoj and Sachin have started searching to those two persons. Those persons were running away on motorcycle. One of the persons so caught, was taken to police station where report was lodged. 3 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 163/2015 Judgment 3] On the basis of report, offence was registered vide C.R.No. I­179/2015. A.P.I. Bhavikatti has recorded the report Exh.14. He has drawn spot panchanama. He has recorded the statements of witnesses and collected school certificate of victims. After collection of evidence, he filed charge­sheet in the Court of law. 4] I have framed charge against accused below Exh. 4 to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 5] Prosecution has examined the four witnesses. Then, the statement of the accused under Sec. 313 came to be recorded. Total denial is the defence of the accused. 6] Following points arose for my determination and I gave my findings thereon for the reasons stated below: Sr. POINTS FINDINGS No. 1. Does the prosecution prove that the No accused along with one unknown companion, on 1.5.2015, at about 11.30 p.m., in a lane in front of Shivshakti Jewellers, Navi Mumbai, in furtherance of common intention, assaulted or used criminal force to the minor victim girls intending to outrage or knowing it to be likely that accused will thereby outrage their modesty? 4 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 163/2015 Judgment 2. Does the prosecution prove that the No. accused along with one unknown person on above mentioned date, time and place, committed sexual harassment upon the minor victim girls named Ku. Jagruti, age 11 years and Ku. Sandhya, age 13 years with sexual intent? 3. What order? As per final order. REASONS AS TO POINT NO.1 TO 3:­ 7] In order to establish the guilt under Sec. 354 of Indian Penal Code, prosecution is required to prove that the accused has either assaulted or used criminal force and that was used on women knowing thereby to outrage the modesty. In order to hold accused guilty under Sec. 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, prosecution has to establish sexual harassment by the accused as provided under Sec. 11 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 8] It is well settled that sole testimony of a witness is sufficient to base the conviction but the rule is that it should inspire confidence in the mind of Court and it should be above suspicion. If a single grain of doubt is appeared in the prosecution story, then the defence gets benefit of it. 5 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 163/2015 Judgment 9] Informant Ranjana is mother of one of the victims of 11 years. The informant and her daughter have just stated that there was some religious programme at their house and the informant's friend Laxmi and her daughter have attended the programme. Informant and her daughter both have not supported the prosecution story. They both have stated that it did not happen that there was some incident of catching hold of the hands of the informant's daughter and the daughter of her friend Laxmi. A.P.I. Mr. Bhavikatti has stated that he has recorded the report of Ranjana as per her say (Exh.14). He has also recorded the contents in passage 'A' and 'B' (Exh. 16 & 17) respectively of the statements of victim who is daughter of informant as per her say. But, the victim i.e. informant's daughter has stated that she has not stated the contents in passages 'A' and 'B' i.e. Exh.16 & 17 to police. Informant has stated that she does not know about the recitals of the report nor it was read over to her. Even if the evidence of both these witnesses is accepted as it is that will not be sufficient to hold accused guilty for the offence for which accused is charged. 10] Another victim i.e. daughter of informant's friend has stated that she attended the house of victim on 01.05.2015 for programme. Both the victims had gone for urination. Son of informant was with them. They both went to one corner. This victim has stated that about three to four persons came on motorcycle. Out of them two persons caught hold the hands of 6 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 163/2015 Judgment both the victims. Laxman rescued them. They pushed both the persons and rescued themselves. According to the second victim, this accused before the Court had caught hold her hand. The accused had not disputed the school certificate of the victim whose date of birth is 01.10.2003. So, the age of this victim at the time of incident was less than 18 years. This victim has admitted in the cross­examination that their house is situated by the side of road. Hence, the recitals of the report (Exh.14) reveals that incident has taken place at about 11.30 p.m. on 01.05.2015. 11] This second victim has admitted in the cross­ examination that there was no arrangement of electricity at the spot where they had gone for urination. So, it appears that the alleged incident has taken place in the night where there was no electric facility. This victim has deposed after about two years of incident. This victim has also not given description. When there was no electric facilities at the spot of incident where victims had gone for urination, then it is difficult to accept the version of the victim as to on what basis, she has identified this accused. At the relevant time, the informant's daughter and son Laxman was also there. Age of Laxman also appears to be 13 years at the relevant time. 12] According to A.P.I. Mr. Bhavikatti, report (Exh.14) was recorded as per say of informant. The prosecution has not examined said Laxman to support the contentions of the victim. 7 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 163/2015 Judgment Another victim has not supported the prosecution. If really the incident has taken place in respect of two victims, then the evidence of both the victims would have been consistent. One of the victims is saying that no such incident of catching hold of hand has taken place. 13] The recitals of the report also reveal that after narration of the incident to the relatives, they have taken search of the culprit who was running away on vehicle. None of these relatives are examined. In absence of evidence of such material witnesses, it would be certainly unsafe to rely on the testimony of only one victim. It will be also doubtful as to how the second victim has identified the accused when there was dark. This second victim has also just stated about catching hold of the hand. She has not stated any other act which can be said to be suggestive of sex. Victim has also not stated any other act so as to bring the accused within the ambit of Sec. 11 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. It is also difficult to ascertain that there was sexual intent on the part of the accused. For the reasons stated above, it is difficult to hold accused guilty for the offences for which he is charged. The accused is entitled for the benefit of doubt. The learned advocate for accused has submitted that the vehicle which is seized in this crime is already returned to the accused. So it may be proper to direct him to retain the same after appeal period is over. Hence, I answer the point Nos.1 and 2 accordingly and pass following order : 8 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 163/2015 Judgment ORDER 1] Accused Jitendra Saybanna Jigneni is hereby acquitted under Sec.235(1) of Code of Criminal Procedure of the offence punishable under Sec. 354 of Indian Penal Code and Sec. 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] His bail bond stands cancelled. 3] Muddemal property i.e. Motorcycle bearing No. MH­43/AK­ 6917 is already returned to its original owner i.e. accused. Same be retained with him after appeal period is over. 4] Accused shall furnish P.B and S.B. of RS.5,000/­ under Sec 437­A of Code of Criminal Procedure. Thane ( Ashutosh N. Karmarkar ) Date : 20.04.2017 District Judge­1 & Special Judge (POCSO) Act,Thane

--1-- ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN CRIMINAL BAIL APPLICATION NO.1669/2018 CNR NO.MHTH01­004638­2018 Applicant Lavkush Shatrohan Morya, aged 22 years, has applied for bail under section 439 of Cr. P.C in C.R.No.I­143/2018 registered in Narpoli police station for the offence under section 376, 506 of Indian Penal Code and section 3 and 4 of POCSO Act. 2. It is contended that there was love affair between victim and accused. The victim is more than 17 years old and applicant is ready to perform marriage with the victim. The applicant is falsely implicated. There is no criminal antecedent. There is no incriminating circumstances. Applicant is ready to co­operate with the investigating machinery and ready to remain present for trial. He is ready to abide by all the conditions. He resides at the given address permanently therefore, he prayed for bail. 3. Investigating Officer has given his say at Exh.4. From the report it appears that the victim is 17 yeas old. The victim's statement under Sec. 164 Cr.P.C. has been recorded. The victim is two months pregnant. It is submitted that the accused had committed sexual intercourse with the victim on the day of her birthday and before that many time. 4. Ld. Counsel for the accused submitted the affidavit of the informant that she is ready to perform the marriage of her daughter with the accused. The affidavit of informant's husband is also given. 5. I heard the Ld. Counsel on behalf of the accused and Ld. A.P.P. 6. The court is of the view that the victim is 17 years old and --2-- she is matured enough. It is not only one episode of penetrative sexual assault but there were many such incidents prior to the date of 11/12/2017. It appears that there was love affair between victim and accused as contended by the accused in his application. It is also corroborated from the affidavit given by the informant and her husband. Considering this mitigating circumstances, the court is of the view that it is a fit case to release the accused on bail. The offence is not punishable with death or imprisonment for life. The investigation is almost complete. Nothing is remained to be seized or recovered from this applicant. Therefore, he is entitled to be released on bail. Hence, I pass following order. :ORDER: 1. Application is allowed. 2. Applicant Lavkush Shatrohan Morya shall be released on PB and SB of Rs.30,000/­ (Rupees Thirty Thousand only) with one or two sureties. 3. He shall furnish his identify proof, residential proof in this court. 4. He shall also furnish the contact number of two blood relatives in this court. 5. He shall not tamper and pressurize the victim and other witnesses by any means. 6. He shall not leave the jurisdiction of the court without prior permission. Thane. ( S.C. Khalipe ) Date : 12/07/2018. Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

1 Special Case No. 44/2013 (Judgment) Presented on : 22/08/2013 Registered on : 22/08/2013 Decided on : 25/05/2016 Duration : 2­ Years 9­ Month 3 Days In The Court of The Special Judge(P.O.C.S.O.Act), Thane. (Presided over by Ms. U. M. Nandeshwar, District Judge­1 & Addl. Sessions Judge, Thane.) Special Case No. 44 of 2013 Exhibit No. 84. The State of Maharashtra Through Police Station Officer Kalwa Police Station, Thane. … Prosecution. VERSUS Ganesh Sudhir Parab Age 25 years, Residence ­ Near Saibaba Mandir, by the side of dairy, Saybanagar, Kalwa, Thane. ... Accused. Offences punishable under sections 363, 376 of Indian Penal Code and section 4 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Appearance ­ Spl.P.P. Mrs. R. A. Navale, for State. Advocate Mrs. Reena Korade for Accused. 2 Special Case No. 44/2013 (Judgment) JUDGMENT (Delivered on 25th May, 2016.) 1] The Accused stands prosecuted for the offence punishable under section 363 & 376 of Indian Penal Code and also under section 4 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act) for committing sexual assault on the minor victim­girl aged about 14 years by kidnapping her and committed rape on her. 2] Shorn of verbiage, the indictment against the Accused are as under ­ [i] Informant Geeta Jaiswal (P.W.1) is resident of Saibaba Nagar Kalwa, Thane. She is staying there with her two sons and two daughters including victim­girl aged about 14 years. [ii] Prior to 8 months informant's son Rahul got acquainted with Ganesh Parab (Accused) and they became friends. Ganesh Parab (Accused) told that his father is a big officer in police department. He used to visit the house of informant and had meal with them and thus took them in confidence. He also used to talk with victim­girl and once he expressed his desire to marry with the victim­girl. At that time, informant told him to call to his father. However, the accused's father never turn­up for talk of marriage. Therefore, 3 Special Case No. 44/2013 (Judgment) informant asked him not to come to her house. Since, then accused was not going to the house of informant. However, accused used to meet the victim­girl when she had been to public tap to fill­up water and they continued their love affair. [iii] On 27/05/2013 around 04.00 p.m. the accused enticed and took away the victim­girl. Therefore, on the same day, informant lodged report against the accused. 3] On her report, initially F.I.R. was registered vide C.R.No.I­253/2013 for offence punishable under section 363 of I.P.C. PSI Pramod Pardeshi (P.W.9) carried out the investigation and he directed the Crime Detection Branch to search the kidnapped girl and accused. On next day P.W.9 received information that kidnapped girl and accused were found by Crime Detection Branch at Khopat S.T.Bus station. On next day, Police Naik Shelar (P.W.6) and two police officers brought and produce accused and victim­girl and accused was arrested on 28/05/2013. On the same day, the victim­girl was sent for medical examination and her medical certificate was collected which is evident about the penetrative vaginal sexual intercourse and therefore offence under section 376 of I.P.C. and section 4 of P.O.C.S.O. Act were added. On 29/05/2013 the panchnama of scene of offence at the house of victim­girl was drawn. On 30/05/2013 informant produced the cloths of victim­girl which were seized under panchnama. The accused was also sent for medical examination and his 4 Special Case No. 44/2013 (Judgment) medical certificate was collected. On 01/06/2013 the cloths of accused were seized under panchnama. The statement of witnesses were recorded. Thereafter, investigation culminated into filing of charge­sheet in this Court being the Special designated court under P.O.C.S.O. Act. 4] My learned Predecessor erstwhile Special Judge, Thane, framed the charge (Exh.2) against the Accused for offence punishable under section 363 & 376 of Indian Penal Code and also under section 4 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. The Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial (Exh.3). The Accused took defence of total denial. 5] In response to application under section 294 of Cr.P.C. the defence has admitted medical certificate of Accused (Exh.66). 6] In order to prove guilt of Accused Prosecution has examined following witnesses ­ P.W.1 Geetadevi Shaligram Jaiswal Exh.8 (Informant ­ Mother of victim girl) P.W.2 Victim­girl. Exh.10 P.W.3 Dr. Supriya Tushar Mahajan Exh.19 (Medical officer who examined the victim girl.) P.W.4 Shriram Sitaram Ikhankar Exh.21 (Panch to seizure panchnama of clothes of accused and seizure panchnama of C.D. of CCTV footage) 5 Special Case No. 44/2013 (Judgment) P.W.5 Vinod Banvari Savner (Hostile) Exh.25 (Panch to spot panchnama) P.W.6 Police Naik Sunil Bhagwan Shelar Exh.41 (Witness who took the victim girl and accused from the Khopat bus stand. ) P.W.7 Ananda Pundalik Suryanvanshi Exh.48 (Witness ­ Principal of Sharda Vidya Mandir Naupada, Thane ­ examined in regard to Date of birth of victim girl.) P.W.8 Dilip Bharat Saroj Exh.53 (Panch to spot panchnama) P.W.9 Pramod Ramsing Pardeshi Exh.60 (Investigating Officer) 7] The prosecution has proved and relied on the following documents ­ Report Exh.9 Medical certificate of victim­girl. Exh.20 Panchnama of seizure of clothes of Exh.22 accused. Panchnama of seizure of C.D. of CCTV Exh.23 footage. Bonafide Certificate of victim girl Exh.49 Extract of General register maintained at Exh.50 School of victim girl. General register maintained at School of Exh.52 victim girl. Spot panchnama. Exh.54 Copy of leaving certificate of victim­girl. Exh.58 Arrest form of accused. Exh.61 Letter dtd.28.05.2013 to refer victim­girl Exh.62 for medical examination. 6 Special Case No. 44/2013 (Judgment) Seizure panchnama of clothes of victim­ Exh.63 girl. Muddemal receipt in regard to deposit of Exh.64 the clothes of victim girl. Letter dtd.01.06.2013 to refer accused for Exh.65 medical examination. Muddemal receipt in regard to deposit Exh.67 clothes of accused. Letter dtd.03.06.2013 to F.S.L. for C.A. of Exh.68 seized muddemal. Muddemal receipt in regard to deposit CD Exh.69 of CCTV footage. 8] The prosecution closed its side of evidence by filing Pursis at Exhibit­74. The statement of accused under Section 313(b) of Cr.P.C. was recorded. Accused neither examined himself nor examined any witness in his defence. 9] Heard learned A.P.P. Mrs. R. A. Navale for State and the learned Advocate Mrs. Reena Korde for Accused at length. 10] On consideration of argument advanced on behalf of both the sides and on perusal of the oral & documentary evidence on record, following points arise for my determination, which are answered with the findings thereon, as under :­ 7 Special Case No. 44/2013 (Judgment) Sr. Points Findings No. 1] Does the prosecution prove that on 27/05/2013 at about 16.00 hrs. near grocery shop of Pujari by the side of Sevalal Mandir, MIDC pipeline, at ..No. Jaibhim Nagar, Saybanagar, Kalwa, Thane, kidnapped the minor victim­girl aged 14 years from lawful guardianship of the her mother and he thereby committed an offence punishable under section 363 of Indian Penal Code ? 2] Does the prosecution prove that during same period and in one room by the side of Sevalal Mandir, MIDC Pipeline Jaibhimnagar, Kalwa, committed rape on ..No. victim­girl and he thereby committed an offence punishable under section 376 of I.P.C. ? 3] Does the prosecution prove that during same period accused committed penetrative sexual assault on the victim­ ...No. girl and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 4 of the P.O.C.S.O. Act? 4] What order ? Accused is acquitted. REASONS As to Point No.1 to 3 : 11] All the points are taken up together for discussion, to avoid the repetition, as evidence about the same in common and inter­connected. 8 Special Case No. 44/2013 (Judgment) 12] As the Accused is facing charge under section 363 & 376 of I.P.C. it is incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that accused kidnapped the victim­girl aged below 18 years from lawful guardianship of her mother and accused committed rape on minor victim­girl. So also as the Accused is facing charge under section 4 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, therefore, it is further incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that the Accused with sexual intent touched the vagina, penis, anus, breast of a child or make the child touched vagina, penis, anus, breast of such person or any other person or does any other act with sexual intent which involves physical contact without penetration and by his such act committed sexual assault as defined in section 4 of the P.O.C.SO. Act. Age of victim­girl : 13] As the Accused is facing charge of kidnapping and under P.O.C.S.O. Act, therefore, first of all it is incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that the victim­girl was child (minor) at the time of incident. It is the case of prosecution that the victim­girl was aged about 14 years at the time of incident which allegedly took place on 27/05/2013. The victim­girl (P.W.2) stated her date of birth as 15/03/2001. The prosecution has examined Anand Suryavanshi (P.W.7) headmaster of Sharda Vidya Mandir Naupada, Thane. He deposed that as per the entry in General Register of the school, victim­girl took admission in 8th standard on 17/06/2013 and 9 Special Case No. 44/2013 (Judgment) entry about it is at Sr. No.8374 and as per school record, her date of birth is 15/03/2001. The relevant extract of the General Register is at Exh.50. P.W.7 also produced School Leaving Certificate of previous school attended by the victim­ girl and said School Leaving Certificate issued by Thane Municipal Corporation by School No.69 which is at Exh.58 wherein the date of birth of the victim­girl is mentioned as 15/03/2001. Here it is pertinent to note that defence never challenged the age of victim­girl during her cross­examination or cross­examination of her mother Geeta Jaiswal (P.W.1). Thus, on the basis of authenticated documents produced on record by the responsible person i.e. Head Master of Sharda Vidya Mandir, Naupada, Thane, cannot be disbelieved. Thus, the prosecution proved that at the time of incident, the victim­ girl was minor aged about 13 years & 2 months i.e. below the age of 18 years and she was a “child” as per definition given in Section 2(d) of P.O.C.S.O. Act. 14] As the prosecution proved that the victim­girl was minor on the date of incident, therefore, now it is required to see that whether accused enticed and took away the said minor girl and had established physical relationship with her and was subjected her to penetrative sexual assault. In this respect, the most material evidence is of the victim­girl (P.W.2) and her mother informant (P.W.1). It is admitted fact on record that accused is friend of the son of informant by 10 Special Case No. 44/2013 (Judgment) name Rahul and he used to visit the house of informant and used to talk with the victim­girl. 15] In this respect, as per the prosecution and as per the version of P.W.1 and P.W.2 accused told them that his father is a big officer in police department and showed his willingness to marry with the victim­girl. In this respect the victim­girl (P.W.2) deposed that as accused frequently came to their house and used to have meal at their house and she used to serve him meal and gradually they developed acquaintance and love with each other. She further deposed that accused used to come to her house when her family members were there in the house and also used to come to her house when nobody was in the house. She further deposed that even during that period the accused had sexual intercourse with her for 3 times, however, she did not disclose it to her mother at any time about the visit of accused to their house. Visit of accused to the house of informant being a friend of son of informant, is also corroborated by the informant (P.W.1). Informant Geetadevi (P.W.1) deposed that accused told that his father is big officer in Kalwa Police chowki and when informant asked him to bring his father for talk of marriage, he gave excuses that he did not get time to come and meet them. Therefore, she asked him not to come to their house. Since then for 15 days, he did not go to their house. But P.W.1 learnt that accused is still communicating with her daughter 11 Special Case No. 44/2013 (Judgment) and was asking her daughter to bring meal from their house and therefore she scolded her daughter and asked her to stop meeting with accused. 16] In respect of alleged kidnapping by the accused to the victim­girl informant Geetadevi Jaiswal (P.W.1) deposed that on 27th in summer, 2013 (she did not recollect the exact month) she went to the house of her neighbour Mr. Pathan around 04.00 p.m. and when she return home, she noticed that the victim­girl was not there in the house. Therefore, she took her search, at that time one small boy told her that he had seen the accused around their house. She further deposed that accused has expressed his intention to marry with her daughter and she prevented him from coming to their house and meeting her daughter, therefore, she thought that accused must have been taken her daughter. Therefore, she went to police station and lodged report against the accused for kidnapping of her daughter. The said report is at Exh.9. Thus, it appears that the informant had not witnessed the accused actual taking away her daughter but she lodged the report only on suspicion against accused about kidnapping of her daughter. 17] Now, to know the exact nature as to whether the victim­girl was really enticed away by the accused can be gathered from the evidence of the victim­girl. Victim­girl 12 Special Case No. 44/2013 (Judgment) (P.W.2) in that respect deposed that prior to 2­3 months of the incident accused had stated to her mother that he went to marry with her. At that time, her mother/informant informed it to the victim­girl and her father, but her father said that they would see it later on and even asked accused to bring his parents. The victim­girl further deposed that accused used to tell that his father is police Commissioner and did not bring his father for talk of marriage under the pretext that his father is sick or his father is not having time etc. She further deposed that her mother asked him to stop coming to their house and therefore, the accused stopped coming to their house. However, she used to meet him whenever she went out of her house for some work, but did not tell about it to her mother. 18] In respect of alleged incident of alleged kidnapping the victim­girl (P.W.2) deposed that on one day i.e. on 27 th, however, she did not tell the month and year, the accused asked to come out from the corner of her house by giving signal by sign. Therefore, she went out of the house on the pretext of going to the shop and met accused. Accused then stated that they shall run away. Thus, they took a rickshaw and they went to Talavpali, Thane railway station and then to Khopat bus­stop and then they went to Talavpali for hiring room. As they were not having identity card therefore, they could not get the room and when they were sitting at Khopat bus­stop on bench, Kalwa police caught both of them and took 13 Special Case No. 44/2013 (Judgment) to Kalwa police station. Then police intimated to her parents and they were in the police station for entire night and her mother came in the police station on next morning. 19] Thus, as per the evidence of victim­girl on 27 th day, accused called her at friend's house and then suggested her to run away and therefore, she accompanied with him. Now, in the present case, there is only material evidence about enticing the victim­girl by the accused is of the victim girl, who on oath deposed before the court that accused suggested running away and therefore, she accompanied with him. Therefore, in the background of the case, it is required to see whether such suggestion given by the accused amount to and comes within the definition of enticing as given in Section 361 of I.P.C. 20] The careful scrutiny of the evidence of the victim­ girl shows that accused suggested running away, but nowhere he particularly stated her where to go or for what purpose he is suggesting her to run away and still she accompanied with the accused. However, the truthfulness of the testimony of the victim­girl is also required to be tested. It is significant to note that even the victim­girl deposed that when they were sitting at Khopat, Kalwa police had been there and caught both of them. In this respect, the evidence of investigating officer PSI Pardeshi (P.W.9) is relevant who deposed that when the report about kidnapping was registered, thereafter he directed Crime 14 Special Case No. 44/2013 (Judgment) Detection Branch to take search of victim­girl and accused and he received information that the said victim­girl and boy were found by Crime­detection branch at Khopat bus­stand and on next day police Naik Shelar (P.W.6) and other police officers brought and produced them (accused & victim­girl) before him. However, there is absolutely no other evidence on record to show that in fact, the accused and the victim­girl were taken in custody by the police from Khopat bus­stand. 21] Police Naik Sunil Shelar (P.W.6) deposed that on 27/05/2013 he was on night duty and his senior directed him to take the accused in custody from Khopat bus stand in respect of crime registered against him. Therefore, he alogwith police Naik Manoj Shirsat had been to Khopat bus stand at 11.00 p.m. and took the accused Ganesh Parab and victim­girl in custody and brought to police station and handed over to PSO and there the accused was arrested. However, P.W.­6 Shelar admitted that no entry in the station diary, about the leaving the police station as per order by his Senior officer, was taken. Further it is pertinent to note that no any panchnama was executed there at that particular time when the accused and victim­girl were allegedly taken in custody from Khopat bus stand, neither any station diary entry is on record in respect of said part of investigation. Therefore, it is hard to believe that in fact the accused and the victim­girl were taken in custody from Khopat bus­stand and the 15 Special Case No. 44/2013 (Judgment) prosecution failed to prove the said fact with any cogent evidence. Thus, now in such background even the question arise whether the victim­girl had been accompanied with the accused only on his say to run away. 22] The careful scrutiny of the evidence of the victim­ girl (P.W.2) eloquent that her evidence is full of omissions and she exaggerated various statements before the Court. She first time stated before the Court that her father even asked accused to bring his parents to have talk about the marriage and accused told her that his father is Police Commissioner. She even first time stated before the Court that on 27 th day accused asked her to come out from her house by giving signal by signing and she went out of the house on the pretext of going to shop and met accused. Even as per the version of victim­girl before the Court that accused asked her to run away is also in the form of omission and further they had been to Talaopali in rickshaw and then to railway station and then to lodge near Talaopali, is also in the form of omission. Further, it appears that the victim­girl in her statement recorded by police stated that on 27/05/2013 around 04.00 p.m. When she was present to grocery shop accused met her on the way and by telling that he want to marry with her, asked her to accompany with him and they proceeded to Kalwa by rickshaw. Thus, as far as the enticement is concerned, the evidence of the victim­girl is very much doubtful and do not 16 Special Case No. 44/2013 (Judgment) inspire any confidence. Thus, when the evidence of material witness, i.e. the victim­girl is suffered from material various omissions and contradictions, then it does not inspired confidence and even not believable. Then there is no other evidence on record in respect of the enticement caused by the accused to the victim­girl or about taking her by him. 23] As discussed in earlier paragraphs, the informant had lodged the report about kidnapping only on the suspicion and she never witnessed the accused taking away his daughter. One boy who allegedly told informant that he had seen accused around their house on the relevant day, is also not examined by the prosecution. Thus, there is absolutely no other witness about taking away the victim­girl by accused and as such the prosecution failed to prove that accused took away the victim­girl or enticed her to accompany with him. 24] Now, as far as the allegations of sexual assault is concerned, it is most significant to note that the victim­girl was examined by the medical officer Dr. Supriya Mahajan (P.W.3). It is eloquent that the victim­girl was examined on 28/05/2013. In that connection the history stated by the victim­girl to the medical officer is of prime importance. Dr. Mahajan (P.W.3) deposed that victim­girl and her mother gave history that she went with one Ganesh Parab, but she did not give any history of sexual assault. However, on examination, 17 Special Case No. 44/2013 (Judgment) there was evidence of penetrative sexual intercourse was present and accordingly, she issued the certificate which is at Exh.20. The medical Certificate (Exh.20) clearly eloquent that in the column of history, victim­girl denied the history of sexual assault, still there is evidence of penetrative vaginal sexual intercourse found present. 25] In connection of the medical evidence the testimony of victim­girl (P.W.2) is again required to be scrutinized in respect of said aspect. It is significant to note that the statement of the victim­girl was recorded on 02/06/2013 i.e. after her medical examination which was conducted on 28/05/2013 and even the victim­girl admits said fact in her cross­examination. She even admits that at the time of medical examination the Doctor asked her whether she had sexual contact with anyone and she denied it.sShe further admits that Doctor inquired with her even before and after medical examination, but still she answered in negative.sThe victim­girl in her statement stated that accused had established physical relationship with her and in evidence she deposed that when accused used to come to her house when nobody was present and during that period he had sexual intercourse with her for 3 times. In this respect again the evidence of medical officer shows that she admits that there are other reasons for tearing hymen other than sexual intercourse. Therefore, in this case there remains doubt whether the 18 Special Case No. 44/2013 (Judgment) accused had sexual intercourse with her because the victim­girl after considerable period of 4 days of her medical examination stated accused had committed sexual intercourse with her. 26] In the background of case, there is possibility that as the medical report suggests that there is evidence of penetrative vaginal intercourse, therefore the victim­girl might had stated that it was committed by the accused as marriage talk between them was going without knowing its consequences. Again it is significant to note that though the victim­girl deposed that for 3 times accused had sexual intercourse with her, but she is unable to state the period during which the alleged act was committed. Even there is contradiction in the evidence of informant and the victim­girl, in respect of expression given by accused about his desire to marry with the victim­girl. Informant Geetadevi Jaiswal (P.W.1) deposed that prior to 5 to 6 months of the incident. The accused had stated that he like Sita and wants to marry her. While the victim­girl deposed that prior to 2­3 months of the incident accused had stated to his mother that he wants to marry her (victim­girl). Thus even the period also varies and it is not minor contradiction, but it appears major & material contradiction which goes to the root of the prosecution case. Again there is room for suspicion about, had the accused expressed about marriage with the victim­girl prior to 2­3 months, then whether really he had an occasion to established 19 Special Case No. 44/2013 (Judgment) sexual intercourse with the victim­girl lies, that too, at her house which is stated to be thickly populated area. The spot panchnama (Exh.54) about the house of the victim­girl shows that it is in the populated area and surrounded with various hut­ments and the doors of other houses used to remain open. Further there is material admission given by the victim­girl that her mother never leaves her alone, then in such background there is remote possibility about committing any sexual intercourse with the victim­girl by the accused. Thus, there is no cogent or believable evidence on record to show that accused had established physical relationship with the victim­girl and subjected her to penetrative sexual assault. 27] As far as the story given by the victim­girl and her mother that though the victim­girl was minor aged about 14 years, the accused proposed her for marriage and her mother also called his father for proceeding with the talk of marriage is not believable. However, victim­girl (P.W.2) admits that she hail from U.P. and in their society there is custom of marriage during minority of the girl. Therefore, in such background the defence of the accused that in fact the parents of the victim­ girl were desired to settle her marriage with accused, however, as the accused is from Maharashtra therefore his family was against such child marriage as the victim­girl was aged about 14 years only and therefore, her mother lodged false complaint against the accused. 20 Special Case No. 44/2013 (Judgment) 28] As far as the execution of spot panchnama is concerned, the panch Vinod (P.W.5) did not support the prosecution. Therefore, to prove it, prosecution examined another panch Dilip Saroj(P.W.8) who deposed about the execution of the spot panchnama. He appears to be neighbourer of victim­girl. The careful scrutiny of the spot panchnama shows that the house of the victim­girl is the small room of 10 x 15 ft. having partition of tin and having cloth curtain. The said room is situated in chawl No.8 in a hutment area and surrounded with various houses. 29] The prosecution has examined one Shriram Ikhankar (P.W.4) who is panch on the point of seizure of cloths of accused which was executed on 01/06/2013 and also the panch to the panchnama of seizure of C.D. from Samudra Lodging and Boarding. However, as far as the seizure of C.D.is concerned, admittedly, there is no certificate on record in compliance of section 65­B of Evidence Act and therefore, said C.A. is absolutely of no help to the prosecution and even the execution of panchnama about seizure of C.D. is very much doubtful as panch was unable to state that how many floors were there at Samudra Lodging and Boarding which creat doubt about his actual presence at the time of execution of said panchnama. Further it is significant to note that the said panchnama about the seizure of C.D.is at Exh.23. The time of 21 Special Case No. 44/2013 (Judgment) commencement of panchnama and its conclusion has kept blank and even the investigating officer (P.W.9) admits it which again creates doubt about the actual execution of said panchnama of seizure of C.D. 30] Even the panchnama of seizure of cloths of accused and the victim­girl appears to be of bare formality completed by the investigating officer and both the panchnamas about seizure of cloths of accused and victim­girl which are at Exh.22 and 23 are executed in police station. The investigating officer stated that the seizure of cloths of accused and victim­girl and the required sample were sent for Chemical Analysis. The C.A. Report is at Exh.70 and 71. But there is nothing favourable to the prosecution. Neither blood nor semen were detected on any of the articles. The only blood group of victim­girl is detected as 'A' and of accused is 'O'. Further as the victim­girl even could not state about the period of intercourse, therefore, even the C.A. Report would not of any help to the prosecution. 31] Thus, in the backdrop of above discussion the prosecution case is very much doubtful. The testimony of victim­girl does not inspire confidence and report appers to be lodged on suspicion only. Further medical evidence speaks against the version of victim­girl. Thus, there is no cogent and believable evidence on record. It is cardinal principle of criminal law that whenever there is any doubt in prosecution 22 Special Case No. 44/2013 (Judgment) case then its benefit goes to the accused. Therefore, accused is entitled for benefit of doubt. The twin presumption given in section 29 & 30 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, for committing or abetting or attempting to commit any offence under sections 3, 5, 7, and 9 of this Act or about culpable mental state would arise only when first of all prosecution proved its case beyond reasonable doubt. However, as prosecution failed to prove the charges against accused beyond reasonable doubt therefore the said presumption would not come to help of the prosecution. Hence, I answer Point No.1 to 3 in negative. 32] In the result, I proceed to pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused Ganesh Sudhir Parab is hereby acquitted U/Sec. 235(1) of Cr.P.C. for the offence punishable U/Sec.363 & 376 of Indian Penal Code and U/s. 4 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] The accused is in jail. He be released forthwith if not required in any other case. 3] Muddemal deposited in Court vide M.E.No. 83/2015 being worthless be disposed off after appeal period is over. 23 Special Case No. 44/2013 (Judgment) 4] The Accused shall furnish P.R. bond of the amount of ₹15,000/­ and one solvent surety in the like amount in compliance of provision of Section 437­A of Cr.P.C. The judgment is dictated and pronounced in open Court. Date : 25/05/2016 (Ms. U. M. Nandeshwar), Thane Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act),Thane. District Judge ­1 and Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

Section 375 of I.P.C. A man is said to commit “rape” if he - (a) penetrates his penis, to any extent, into the vaginie, mouth urethre or anus of a woman or makes her to do so with him or any other person; or (b)------ (c)------ (d) applies his mouth to the vagina, anus, urethra of a woman or makes her to do so with him or any other person, under the circumstances falling under any of the following seven descriptions :- First – Against her will Secondly – Without her consent, Thirdly to Fifthly -........ On asking she provided her address to the police. Then two police persons and two other ladies proceeded by train and when they reached at Kalyan Railway Station, she told them that she do not want to go to home. They asked her reason and victim­ girl narrated them that her step­father had done forcible sexual intercourse with her and therefore, she does not want to go home. The victim­girl in her own language stated that the Accused did 'Sharirik Sambandh' with her. On that the then erstwhile Special Judge clarified that whether she knows the meaning of the said term. On that, victim­girl explained in her own language and note about it was taken down in her deposition, from which, it appears that the victim­girl had knowledge about that term. 17] Victim­girl (P.W.5) thereafter deposed that then police took her to Bhiwandi Police Station and recorded her complaint and its contents were explained to her in Hindi. She even deposed that at that time Sweelta Didi(P.W.3) and two other women were there and then her report was recorded which is at Exh.24. 18] Victim­girl (P.W.5) further deposed that she was then sent to Bhiwandi Children Home and then hospital for medical examination. From Bhiwandi Children Home she was transferred to Sneh­Sadan Institution. 19] The victim­girl was cross examined at length and an attempt was made to bring on record that she want to go to her father Arvind Chaourasiya, which was not liked by her step­father (Accused) and on that count, there was quarrel between herself, her mother and her step­father and for that reason she had lodged false report against the Accused at the instance of Sweelta Didi (P.W.3). Apart from that, nothing material is brought on record during the cross­examination of this witness. Some admissions were extracted from this witness that at first instance she did not disclose the incident to Sweelta Didi (P.W.3) when she met her at Dadar Railway Station or even to police at Dadar Police Station. However, it is no way helpful to the defence, as victim­girl herself has stated in her examination­in­chief when she was about to reach at her house, at that time at Kalyan Railway Station she disclosed that she do not want to go to home and thereafter on asking, she disclosed about the act of the Accused. Nothing material is brought on record in the cross­examination as far as incident in question is concerned. P.W.5 withstood in the cross­ examination. Absolutely no convincing reason is brought on record for false implication of the Accused. Particularly, when the victim­girl deposed that her mother married with the Accused prior to two years and since then she alongwith her mother and two sisters were staying with the Accused. Thus, it appears that the victim­girl was staying away from her real father, as her mother performed marriage with the Accused. The victim­girl even did not know the whereabout of her father. She only stated that her father is stayed at Ulhasnagar and worked as mason. Though, it is admitted by her that her mother had some disputes with her real father, however, she further deposed that she and her other sisters were used to meet her father and which was not liked by her step­father. But that cannot be said to be any reason for false implication of the Accused. No girl of such young age would implicate her step­ father at the cost of her reputation who infact sheltered them. 20] In this respect ordeal of the victim­girl is required to be considered as her mother left her real father and married with Accused and staying with him since two years and when Accused committed a heinous act with the girl and even repeated the same after 15 days and when she disclosed it to her mother, her mother did not support the victim­girl and on the contrary, asked the Accused to drop her at Kalyan Railway Station. Thus, prima facie it appears that the mother of the victim­girl shown total indifferent attitude towards her own daughter and instead of helping and standby with the victim­ girl in her difficult situation, her mother behaved in very uncalled fashion with her own daughter. Thus, it appears that the victim­girl has no one to share her ordeal when her mother refused to help her by her indifferent approach. It is quiet obvious and natural for such young girl that she did not open up immediately before unknown person. Therefore, there appears nothing unnatural when victim­girl at first instance did not disclose about the incident to Sweelta Demonti (P.W. 3) or to police at Dadar Police Station. But when police and P.W. 3 then taken her to her house and when victim­girl found that she will be again put in the hands of the Accused and she will have to face similar act at the hands of the Accused, she disclosed about the act committed by the Accused to the police. Testimony of Independent Witnesses :­ 21] The version of Victim­girl (P.W.5) is duly corroborated by the version of P.W.3 Sweelta Demonity who is the social worker attached to Sneh­Sadan Social Organization, Andheri, Mumbai, since 2013. Sweelta (P.W.3) even deposed that the organization is participated in activities of rehabilitation work of abandoned or missing children found on western and central Railway platforms besides other activities of Children Home and rescue work of minor girls from sexual harassment, etc. Thus, it is clear that P.W.3 is an independent witness having no concern with the Accused or the victim­girl and she absolutely has no reason to implicate the Accused in any crime particularly, in a serious and heinous crime for which he is facing trial. 22] Sweelta Demonti (P.W.3) further deposed that on 02.06.2013 she alongwith her colleague was taking round at Dadar Western Railway Station around 9.00 a.m. to 9.30 a.m. At that time she noticed that on platform No.1 at the place where First Class ladies middle boggie come, one girl (victim­ girl) aged 17 years was sat with one bag and two boys were also there beside her. She apprehended that girl is alone. Therefore, she talked with the girl and the girl disclosed her name and told that she has come there from Kalyan. P.W.3 further deposed that the girl was initially scared and not open up thinking that they are police persons and on explaining that they are not police and belongs to one Sanstha, she told that she do not want to go home, but she did not state the reason. Therefore, they took her to G.R.P. office at Dadar Railway Station. 23] Sweelta (P.W.3) further deposed that when they were proceeding towards Bhiwandi to reach her to her house, at that time she told that she do not want to go home and her father Kashif Shaikh (Accused) had done wrong act with her and had been sexually harassing her many times and that last act was committed by her father recently before two days and her mother had learnt about it. Therefore, they took the victim­girl to Bhiwandi Taluka Police Station. From there, they went to the house of girl with police and the Accused was brought to the police station. At that time Accused did not disclose his real name. Thereafter, the victim­girl lodged the report. 24] Sweelta (P.W.3) was cross­examined but absolutely nothing is brought on record to disbelieve version of this witness who is an independent witness. Only because no enquiry was made by P.W.3 about the boys who were sitting with the girl had no consequences and no concern with the incident in question. Thus, the testimony of P.W.3 fully corroborates the version of the victim­girl that she was abandoned at Kalyan Railway by her step­father/Accused and from there she had been to Dadar Railway Station where P.W. 3 happened to meet her and as a part of her job, she enquired with the girl by taking help of the police and was about to reach the girl to her house, but girl disclosed about the act of Accused and then she was taken to Bhiwandi Police Station and then the report was lodged and Accused was arrested form his house. 25] Even the version of Victim­girl (P.W.5) and Sweelta Demonti (P.W.3) is further corroborated by the evidence of P.W.7­ Police Hawaldar Baliram Khopkar who was attached with Mumbai Central Railway Police in the year 2013. Khopkar (P.W.7) deposed that on 02.04.2013 he was on duty at Dadar Railway Station (Western Railway). He was present in police chowky at the railway station. One woman and one man both social workers had been police chowky and one girl was with them. They asked police aid by stating that they found the abandoned girl who is aged about 14 years to 15 years and that girl disclosed her name and address. P.W.7 further deposed that the social workers approached their officer P.S.I. Shaikh and he directed to escort the girl to Kalyan. Then he (P.W.7) alongwith one lady police constable Ghadge took the girl at Kalyan by local train and both the social workers were with them. They got down at Kalyan and the girl stated that her house is at Bhiwandi and then they took the girl for proceeding towards Bhiwandi. But the girl stated that she do not want to go home and on asking, she disclosed that her step­father was troubling her, and beating. He further stated that girl initially only stated about troubling and beating and then disclosed that her father was sexually assaulting her. Therefore, they took back her to Bhiwandi Taluka Police Station and there on enquiry, the victim­girl narrated the entire incident of sexual assault by her father in detail and he was also present there. He further deposed that the girl stated that her step­father Rahul Sinha committed rape on her twice. He even deposed that therefore, they handed over custody of the girl to Bhiwandi Taluka Police Station alongwith report and that report is at Exh.32. Further, in the cross­examination of this witness nothing to disbelieve his version is brought on record. Only because the girl was sitting with the social workers during the journey, it cannot be said that she was tutored by the social workers and at their instance victim­girl deposed against the Accused. There appears absolutely no reason for the social workers to implicate the Accused having no enmity with him. 26] It is now settled principal of law that sole testimony of the victim­girl is sufficient to convict the Accused in case of sexual offenes if the testimony of the victim­girls finds truthful and reliable. If the version of the victim­girl is believable then further corroboration is not necessary. In this respect, landmark judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Gurmit Singh Vs. State of Punjab, AIR 1996S.C.1393, where in the criteria to test the testimony of the victim­girl who is victim of sexual offence, is described. The victim of sexual offence is not accomplice and in fact she is as par with the injured witness and there is no reason to disbelieve the version of injured witness. Seeking corroboration to the version of the victim of sexual offence is nothing but adding insult to her injury. There is absolutely no Rule to throw away the testimony of the victim­girl for want of corroboration. Rape is not merely a physical assault – it is often destructive of the whole personality of the victim. A murderer destroys the physical body of his victim, a rapist degrades the very soul of the helpless female. The Court, therefore, shoulder a great responsibility while trying an accused on charges of rape. They must deal with such cases with utmost sensitivity. The Courts should examine the broader probabilities of a case and not get swayed by minor contradictions or insignificant discrepancies in the statement of the prosecutrix, which are not of a fatal nature, to throw out an otherwise reliable prosecution case.” Medical Evidence :­ 27] Even in this case apart from testimony of victim­ girl, there is medical evidence on record. Testimony of P.W.6 Dr. Amol Bidkar attached with I.G.M. Hospital, Bhiwandi is relevant who examined the victim­girl aged about 14 on 03.04.2013 who was brought by lady police constable. P.W.6 deposed that the victim­girl had given the history of alleged sexual intercourse by her father on 19.02.2013. He examined the girl and noticed that her hymen was torn. It was old tear. Vagina was non­fatulous. Dr. Bidkar (P.W.6) on the basis of observations, opined that there was sexual intercourse with girl and accordingly issued the certificate which is at Exh. 28. Thus, even the P.W. 6 gave the clear opinion that 14 years girl to whom he had examined, was subjected to sexual intercourse. It is pertinent to note that the victim teen aged girl is of 14 years and was unmarried. In such circumstances, if the hymen was torn and vagina was non­fatulous having old tear then definitely it can be said that she was sexually assaulted. Only because P.W. 6 admits the possibility that if any foreign body enters in the vagina, the similar observations will be there. But it is further significant to note that no such suggestion was given to this witness that in case of the victim­ girl to whom he had examined on 03.04.2013 the injury noticed or observation made in medical certificate below Exh. 28, was due to any such reason or particularly for that reason. 30] The Ld. Defence counsel most vehemently argued that in the present case the medical evidence is not supporting the case of prosecution in the background of the admission given by the Medical Officer (P.W. 6) that he cannot give confirm opinion about sexual intercourse and there is possible of similar observation if any foreign body enters in the vagina. He in support of his submission, placed reliance on the Judgment of Hon'ble High Court in a case of John @ Vivek Ramesh Jadhav Vs. State of Maharashtra, 2015 ALL MR (Cri) 4053, wherein the evidence of the victim child of 8 years was not believed as the evidence of mother found to be of hearsay nature and there was no medical evidence as to examination of either victim or Accused. However, the facts of the case were totally different. In the case cited by the Ld. defence counsels there is absolutely no medical evidence as to examination of either victim or Accused. However, in the case in hand, there is medical evidence at Exh.28 about the examination of the victim aged 14 years and as observed in earlier paragraph, the testimony of P.W.6 is believable who had given the clear opinion in Exh.28 that victim­girl was subjected to sexual intercourse. No doubt, P.w.6 even admits that on the basis of medical evidence, no confirmed opinion about sexual intercourse can be given. But when there is inspiring version of the victim­girl there is no reason to disbelieve the version of the minor victim­girl. Spot­Panchnama & Seizer Panchanama :­ 28] Prosecution examined P.W.2 Ananta Mhatre who is panch to the spot panchanama. The spot is the house of Accused, which is one room in Hanuman Tare Chawl, Yavai village. It was shown by the victim­girl and from there clothes of the victim­girl were seized. The spot­cum­seizure panchanama is at Exh.14. It is pertinent to note that the fact that in the said house Accused alongwith victim, her mother and two sisters were staying, is not denied by the Accused. During the cross­examination the only suggestion given to this witness is that he is the habitual panch, which he denied. Thus, Nothing material has been brought on record to disbelieve this witness. 29] As far as seizure of the clothes of Accused is concerned, as per prosecution, the clothes were seized at the instance of the Accused from his house which were kept under the cot in one bag. Prosecution examined P.W.4 Shahid Shaikh who is a panch witness to the memorandum statement of the Accused about producing his clothes which he had kept under a cot in his house. The disclosure statement is at Exh.20 and recovery panchanama is at Exh.21. However, the said panchanama is not of much help for the prosecution and even the Chemical Analysis Report (C.A. report) which is at Exh.50 and Exh.51 are also not helpful to the prosecution as no blood or no semen were detected on the clothes which were seized under panchanama. Here it is significant to note that the incident in question was stated to be of dt.19.03.2013 and the report was lodged on 03.04.2013 i.e. after about 15 days and thereafter the clothes of the Accused and victim were seized on 04.04.2013 and 05.04.2013. In such circumstances it is but obvious that the C.A. reports would not help the prosecution. Delay in lodging F.I.R. :­ 30] The Ld. Defence counsel faintly argued that there is considerable delay in lodging the F.I.R. However, now it is settled principle that in cases of sexual offences the delay is but obvious and it is bound to occur. The delay in lodging F.I.R. in sexual offence has to be considered with a different yardstick. In this respect, the Ld. Spl. P.P. right placed her reliance on the judgment of Hon'ble Bombay High Court in case of Devaji Rama Padave Vs. State of Maharashtra, 2013 ALL MR (Cri.)2025 wherein it is held that in cases of rape, there is invariably delay in lodging the F.I.R., it is to be borne in mind that in a rape case the prosecutrix is worried about her future. She is in a traumatic state of mind. The family of the victim generally shows reluctance to go to the police station because of societies attitude towards the victim. Society casts doubt and shame upon her rather than comfort or sympathise with her. The family remains concerned with honour and reputation of the prosecutrix and that of the family. As far as delay in lodging F.I.R. in rape cases is concerned, no straitjacket formula can be laid down in this regard. In case of sexual offences, the criteria may be different altogether. As honour or the family is involved, its members have to decide whether to take the matter to the Court or not. In such fact situation, near relations of the prosecutrix may take time as to what course of action should adopted. Thus, delay is bound to occur. 00] Even the facts of above cited cases and present case are quite similar. In Devaji's case also accused who is step­ father of victim­girl of 13 years sexually assaulted her thrice and threatened her and her mother did not come forward for her rescue. In the case in hand also similar is situation ney even worse then that. The mother of victim­girl not only refuse to standby her when she disclosed her ordeal but ask the Accused to drop her at Kalyan Railway station. The F.I.R. eloquent that when victim­girl disclosed the incident to social worker Sweelta (P.W.3) and to Bhiwandi police thereafter her mother was called and the F.I.R. was registered. However, mother of victim­girl did not took the girl with her and the victim­girl was admitted in Seva­Sadan social institution and till today she is there. Record even eloquent that the prosecution had made an effort to serve summons to mother of victim­girl but she left the house which address was given by her and could not tress out as she changed her address. Thus, when the step­father/accused threaten the victim­girl to kill if she disclosed the incident to anybody and when her real mother was not willing to come for help of victim­girl of 14 years, in such circumstances it is not expected that a young girl of 14 years would go on her own and lodged the report or to disclosed it at first instance to any unknown person. 37] The Ld. Spl.P.P. placed her reliance on the various judgments of Hon'ble Apex Court and Hon'ble High Court in the cases of – (1) Shamim Anwar Khan V/s. State of Maharashtra 2015 ALLMR (Cri) 3218, (2) Sonu Kumar V/s. State of H.P., 2012 CRIL.J. 3210, (3) State of UttarPradesh V/s. Krishna Gopal, 1988­LAWS(SC)­8­29, (4) Deepak V/s. State of Haryana 2015 CRI L.J. 2049 (5) Devaji Rama Padave V/s. State of Maharashtra, 2013 ALL MR (Cri) 2025, (6) R. Shaji V/s. State of Kerala, 2013 ALL MR (Cri) 1469 (S.C.) The ratio of above­said cases is that the sole testimony of victim of sexual assault is believable and it did not require corroboration if the version found truthful and reliable and when Accused is step­father then no reason to disbelieve victim and offence called for maximum punishment. Social Background of witnesses :­ 38] In the present case the social background of the witnesses and their mental trauma as well as their capacity to explain the incident is also relevant to consider. In this case the victim­girl (P.W.2) is teenaged girl and her mother performed second marriage with accused and girl is staying away from her father. No doubt, there are some omissions and contradictions in the testimony of victim girl as she could not state exact date and time of incident, however, as discussed above the as far as incident in question is concern there is nothing to disbelieve victim­girl, therefore such omissions or contradiction does not affect the case of prosecution. 40] Thus, mathematical testimony of teenaged victim­ girl is not expected. Witnesses are not Tape­recorder. Some omissions and contradictions ought to occurs depending upon the capacity of the witnesses to remember the incident and to narrate it before Court. In the present case the trauma of the victim­girl when even her mother refused to support her need to have been considered in that particular situation. 41] In this respect observations made by Hon'ble Justice V. R. Krisha Iyer in Inder Singh vs. State (Delhi Administration) AIR 1978 SC 1091 would be helpful. Wherein it is held that ­ “Credibility of testimony, oral and circumstantial, depends considerably on a judicial evaluation of the totality, not isolated scrutiny. While it is necessary that proof beyond reasonable doubt should be adduced in all criminal cases, it is not necessary that it should be perfect. If a case is proved too perfectly, it is argued that it is artificial; if a case has some flaws, inevitable because human beings are prone to err, it is argued that it is too imperfect. One wonders whether in the meticulous hypersensitivity to eliminate a rare innocent from being punished, many, guilty men must be callously allowed to escape. Proof beyond reasonable doubt is a guideline, not a fetish and guilty man cannot away with it because truth suffers some infirmity when projected through human processes. Judicial quest for perfect proof often accounts for police presentation of fool­proof concoction. Why fake up ? Because the court asks for manufacture to make truth look true ? No, we must be realistic.” (Emphasis added) Presumption under Section 29 & 30 of P.O.C.S.O.Act. 42] It is material to reproduce the provisions of section 29 and 30 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. As per Section 29 there is presumption that ''Where a person is prosecuted for committing or abetting or attempting to commit any offence under sections 3, 5, 7, and 9 of this Act, the Special Court shall presume that such person has committed or abetted or attempted to commit the offfence, as the case may be, unless the contrary is proved''. Thus, there is word 'shall' provided in Section 29 which make it obligatory on the Court that once the prosecution proves that the Accused is involved in any act under this Act, then the burden lies on the Accused to rebut it. So also, there is presumption of culpable mental state in Section 30 of the Act which includes intuition, motive, knowledge of a fact and the belief or reason to believe a fact. 43] The learned counsel for defence argued that presumption is always rebutable and in the present case the defence has successfully rebutted said presumption by bringing on record various contradictory evidence of the prosecution witnesses. However, in the present case as discussed above, there appears no cogent or believable reason for false implication of the Accused. The defence failed to rebut the said presumption though the victim­girl was cross examined at length. 46] As the prosecution proved beyond reasonable doubt that the Accused committed repeated penetrative sexual assault on his stepdaughter / the tender­aged victim­girl who was in his foster care and living in same shared household, as defined in section 3(a) and section 5(l)(n) of P.O.C.S.O. Act, therefore, presumption arises in favour of prosecution and as per section 29 of the Act the burden lies on the Accused to rebut the same either through cross­examination of the prosecution witnesses or by adducing defence evidence. Admittedly Accused has not examined any witness in defence and, as discussed above, there is nothing material brought on record to disbelieve the prosecution witnesses. Even no explanation was tendered in the statement of accused recorded under section 313 of Cr.P.C. Thus, the Accused failed to rebut the presumption. 47] Thus, the evidence of the witnesses brought on record by the prosecution is truthful, reliable and trustworthy. There is nothing to disbelieve the version of the prosecution witnesses. There is absolutely no reason brought on record for false implication of the Accused. No teenage girl would stake her character by implicating step­father for such graver offence. Thus, the prosecution duly established that the Accused who is step­father of the victim­girl had ravished the victim­girl in diabolic manner by threatening her when her mother was not at home. The medical evidence also is in corroboration to the prosecution case. Further, the presumption also arising in favour of the prosecution and the Accused is failed to rebut the same. Thus, there remains no doubt that it was the Accused and Accused only who sexually assault victim­girl. Thus, the prosecution has proved the case beyond all reasonable doubt. Therefore, Accused Kasif Hamid Shaikh @ Rahul Sinha is held guilty for the offences u/s. 375 of I.P.C. and u/section 3 and section 5(l)(n) r/w of P.O.C.S.O. Act and therefore the Accused is liable to be punished for the said offences u/sec.376 of I.P.C. and u/sec.4 & 6 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, 2012. Hence, I answer point No.1 & 2 in affirmative. At this juncture it is necessary to hear the Accused on the point of sentence as per mandate of Section 235 of Cr.P.C. Hence, I take a pause to hear the Accused on the point of sentence. Date : 30.01.2016. (Ms.U.M.Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act) Thane. Resume ­ 48] Heard Accused on the point of sentence. Accused in person submitted that he is innocent and prayed for leniency. Ld. Adv. Mr. Patankar for Accused also prayed that leniency be shown to Accused, he is behind bar since 3 years and minimum sentence may be imposed. 49] The Ld. A.P.P. Mrs. R. A. Navale submitted that this is not the case of showing leniency, the victim is step­daughter of Accused and he committed heinous crime and prayed for imposing maximum sentence. 50] I have given thoughtful consideration to the submissions advanced by the Accused in person, his Ld. Counsel and Ld. Spl.P.P. 51] Serious offences like rape on child having great impact on social order and public interest require exemplary treatment. Protection of society and stamping out criminal proclivity must be the object of law which must be achieved by imposing appropriate sentence. 52] In the present case conduct of Accused belies human relationship of step­father and daughter and reflects most unfortunate and abusive facet of human conduct. Due to such kind of incidents it would be difficult for any daughters to trust their relative or step­father. Child rape cases are cases of perverse lust for sex where even innocent children are not spared in pursuit of the sexual pleasure. There cannot be anything more obscene than this. It is a crime against humanity. Many such cases are not even brought to light because of social stigma attached thereto. 53] The minimum sentence provided for offence u/s.376(2) of I.P.C. and U/sec. 6 of P.O.C.S.O. Act is rigorous imprisonment which shall not less ten years but which may extend to life imprisonment. Similarly, as per provision of section 42 of P.O.C.S.O. Act punishment is required to be imposed under either I.P.C or P.O.C.S.O. which ever is grater in degree. Looking to nature of offence committed by step­father on his step­daughter who was under his foster care and living in same house, no case for imposing lesser sentence then minimum sentence. For both the offences similar punishment is provided, therefore, in my opinion, the following sentence will meet the ends of justice. 54] In the result, I proceed to pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused Kasif Hamid Shaikh @ Rahul Sinhas is hereby convicted U/Sec.235(2) of Cr.P.C. for the offence punishable U/Sec.376 of Indian Penal Code r/w. u/section 3 r/w section 4 and section 5(l)(n) r/w Section 6 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and he is sentenced to suffer Rigorous Imprisonment for Ten (10) years and to pay fine of 5,000/­ [Rupees Five Thousand only] and in default of payment of fine, to suffer the Simple Imprisonment for six (6) months. 2] The Accused is in jail custody since 03/04/2013. He is entitled for set off U/Sec. 428 of Cr.P.C. for the period he is in jail custody. 3] Muddemal vide M.E.No.187/2014 be preserved till appeal period is over. 4] Copy of the judgment be provided to the Accused free of cost as per provisions U/s. 363 of Cr.P.C. Judgment dictated and pronounced in open Court. Date : 30/01/2016 (Ms. U. M. Nandeshwar), Thane Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act),Thane.

JUDGMENT (Delivered on 30.11.2015.) 1] The accused stands prosecuted for the offence punishable under section 376, 292 of Indian Penal Code (hereinafter in short I.P.C.) and under section 4 & 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Rehana used to help accused and used to go to the house of customers for supplying the articles. [ii] On 25.05.2013 at about 8.00 p.m. Rehana (P.W.1) .. 3 ..
