At about 5.30 p.m. he saw his daughter/victim­girl at Nahur railway station alongwith her maternal aunt Kamrunissa (P.W.6). [iii] Kamrunissa (P.W.6) brought victim­girl (P.W.2) to the house of Rehana (P.W.1). At that time victim­girl disclosed that since four months when she was alone at home, accused repeatedly used to press her breast and touch private part and committed penetrative sexual assault on her and he also used to show her obscene clips in mobile phone and had also threatened her not to disclose about the act to anybody else he would kill her and her mother and due to fear she could not disclose about it to her mother (P.W.1). On 25.05.2013 at about 7.30 when she was doing work in kitchen, accused again molested her. She also disclosed that accused on various occasions committed sexual assault on her when she was alone at home and therefore, the victim­girl had been to the house of her maternal aunt and disclosed the incident to her. Therefore, the report was lodged. 3] On her report, C.R.No.I­422/2013 came to be registered against the accused for offence punishable under section 376, 292 of I.P.C. and section 4, 8, 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. The investigation was carried out by P.S.I. Vishwas Bhaskar (P.W.8). He arrested the accused and seized his clothes, drawn .. 4 .. Special Case No 45/2013 Judgment spot panchnama in presence of panchas. The victim girl was referred for medical examination and her clothes were seized under panchnama. Further investigation was carried out by Lady P.I. Usha Suradkar (P.W.7). She collected medical report of the accused and victim and forwarded muddemal for chemical analysis and collected C.A. report and filed it in the Court. Then investigation culminated into filing of charge­ sheet before this Court, being Special Court under P.O.C.S.O. Act, 2012. 4] My learned predecessor, the erstwhile Additional Sessions Judge­1 Mrs. V. V. Virkar framed the charge (Exh.9) against the accused for offence punishable under section 376, 292 of Indian Penal Code and also under section 4, 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. The contents of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. The accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial (Exh.10). His defence gathered from cross­examination of witnesses and his statement recorded under section 313 of Cr.P.C. was of total denial and further that his daughter was having love affair with one boy Mashak Ali and also having relationship with him which was learnt by accused and therefore he scolded her and threatened that he will marry her with another body and transfer his house in the name of daughter of his second wife and therefore he has been falsely implicated. .. 5 .. Special Case No 45/2013 Judgment 5] In response to application under section 294 of Cr.P.C. the defence has admitted [i] C.A. report (Exhibit 46) and [ii] school leaving certificate issued by Thane Municipal School No.96 of victim­girl (Exhibit 54). 6] Prosecution in order to prove guilt of accused has examined following witnesses ­ P.W.1 Rehana Mohammad Farid Shaikh Exh.16 (Informant – mother of victim­girl) P.W.2 Victim­girl Exh.18 P.W.3 Dr. Sunita Milind Ubale Exh.30 (Examined victim­girl) P.W.4 Fatima Shahid Ali Sayyed Exh.32 (Panch to cloth seizer of victim­girl) P.W.5 Dr. Dattatray Vishnu Kulkarni Exh.35 (conducted ossification Test) P.W.6 Kamroon Latif Shaikh Exh.38 (maternal Aunt of victim­girl) P.W.7 P.I. Usha Suradkar (I.O.) Exh.43 P.W.8 P.S.I. Vishwas Bhaskar (I.O.) Exh.49 7] The prosecution proved and relied on the following documents ­ Sr.No. Particulars of Document Exhibit [i] F.I.R. dated 25.05.2013 Exh.17 [ii] Spot panchnama dated 25.05.2013 Exh.51 [iii] Arrest panchnama (form) Exh.50 .. 6 .. Special Case No 45/2013 Judgment [iv] panchnama of seizure of clothes of Exh.32 victim­girl [v] medical certificate regarding age of Exh.36 the victim­girl 8] The prosecution close its side of evidence by filing Pursis at Exhibit 55. The incriminating evidence came on record against the accused was read over and explained to him and his statement under Section 313(b) of Cr.P.C. was recorded vide Exhibit 57. Accused neither examined himself nor examined any witness in his defence. 9] Heard learned A.P.P. Mrs. R. A. Navale for State and learned Advocate Mr. S. J. Patankar for accused. 10] On consideration of argument advanced on behalf of both the sides and on perusal of the oral and documentary evidence on record, following points arise for my determination, which are answered with the findings thereon, as under :­ Sr. Points Findings No. 1. Does prosecution prove that on 25.05.2013 at his residential house at Rashid Compound, Mumbra, and since before four months of said date, the accused committed rape on his minor daughter i.e. victim­girl, by doing .. 7 .. Special Case No 45/2013 Judgment forcible sexual intercourse with her and he thereby committed offence under ..No. section 376 of I.P.C.? 2. Does the prosecution prove that on the given date, time and place accused, used to show obscene clips / pictures to the victim­girl with sexual intent and thereby he committed offence punishable under section 292 of I.P.C. ? ..No. 3. Does the prosecution prove that during the given period and place accused committed penetrative sexual assault on the victim­girl by doing forcible sexual intercourse with her and thereby he committed offence punishable under section 4 of P.O.C.S.O. Act ? ..No. 4. Does the prosecution prove that during the given period and place accused committed sexual harassment upon the victim­girl by molesting her by touching and pressing her body inappropriately with sexual intent and thereby he committed offence punishable under section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act ? ..No. 5. What order ? ..As per final order. REASONS As to Point Nos.1 to 4 ­ 11] All the points are taken up together for discussion to avoid the repetition as they are interconnected and evidence for the same is common. .. 8 .. Special Case No 45/2013 Judgment 12] In this case serious allegation of repeated sexual assault is made against the accused who is none else than the father of the victim­girl. Therefore, the evidence of witness is required to be scan more carefully. Furthermore, the well established cannon of criminal justice “fouler the crime higher the proof” is also required to be kept in mind. Though, the twin pair of presumption is given under section 29 and 30 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, however, presumptions, are rules of evidence and do not conflict with the presumption of innocence of the accused and the burden to prove its case, beyond all reasonable doubt, still remains intact and prosecution is required to discharge said burden. 13] As accused is facing charge under P.O.C.S.O Act, it is incumbent on part of prosecution to prove that victim­girl was minor at the relevant time. To prove the age of the victim­ girl, the prosecution has examined Dr. Dattatray Kulkarni (P.W.5), Professor, Forensic Medicine, Rajeev Gandhi Medical College, Kalwa. He deposed that on 27.05.2013 he clinically examined the victim­girl after obtaining her consent and also done dental examination and ossification test. On the basis of his observations of clinical examination and ossification test and X­ray report, the age of the victim­girl at the time of her examination was 13 years + / ­ 6 months. Accordingly, he issued certificate Exhibit 36. Only simple suggestion that he is .. 9 .. Special Case No 45/2013 Judgment deposing falsely was given to him. Thus, there is no challenge to his testimony and the age of victim­girl is not much disputed by defence and even at latter stage of trial, defence admitted school leaving certificate of victim­girl which is at Exhibit 54. According to school leaving certificate the date of birth of victim­girl is 06/11/2000. Thus, the prosecution proved that the victim­girl was aged about 13 years at the relevant time and she is 'child' as per definition provided under P.O.C.S. Act. 14] Now in the background of serious allegations against the father himself, the testimony of the victim­girl (P.W.2), informant/wife of accused (P.W.1) and maternal Aunt of victim­girl (P.W.6) is most crucial. Firstly, it would be relevant to discuss the evidence of P.W.2 victim­girl. Victim­girl (P.W.2) deposed that the accused is her father and in the year 2013 she herself with her mother (P.W.1), father (accused) and her brother were staying together at Rashid Compound, Mumbra. She had attended municipal school at Mumbra but left the school. She stated her age as 14 years in the year 2013. She deposed that her father was doing embroidery work and her mother was also doing same work. Her mother used to go out to the house of customers on alternate day to supply the articles prepared by them and she used to out for about one and half hour. At that time she (P.W.2 victim­girl) and her father (Accused) used to be alone at home. Her brother also .. 10 .. Special Case No 45/2013 Judgment used to be out at the house of her paternal aunt and was not there in the house. Thereafter, the victim­girl also narrated in detail the act of accused about molesting her. 15] Victim­girl (P.W.2) further deposed that accused also attempted to commit penetrative sexual assault on her but she resisted him. She also deposed that accused/her father used to show her obscene films in mobile phone and used to touch, press and suck her breast and sometimes if her mother returned he used to stop doing such acts. She deposed that that her father continued to do such act for 2 to 3 months. He used to threaten her that if she discloses it to her mother he will kill her and her mother, therefore, she was scared and did not disclose it to her mother. She also deposed that on the day of incident i.e. the day when the F.I.R. was lodged, her mother was sleeping and she was cleaning utensils in 'mori' and at that time also accused came there and pressed her breast, she resisted and got scared that her father will beat her. Thereafter, her father sent her to bring milk and buns and therefore she went out of house and being scared of her father(accused), went to the house of her younger maternal aunt Kamrunissa (P.W.6) at Nahur and narrated her the incident. She also deposed that at that time her another aunt from Ghatkopar was also there. Then, both her aunts brought her to Mumbra and she met her father at Nahur station. Then she went to Mumbra and her mother lodged complaint. .. 11 .. Special Case No 45/2013 Judgment 16] In the background of this testimony of the victim­ girl the veracity of this witness is required to be tested. It is pertinent to note that P.W.1 Rehana, mother of the victim­girl and wife of the Accused, also deposed that she was helping her husband in his embroidery work and her husband used to prepare articles and she used to go to the house of customers to give those articles and at that time her husband and daughter used to be there in the house. She (P.W.1) also deposed that on the day when F.I.R. was lodged, at about 8.30 p.m. her daughter left the house for buying buns but she did not return for a considerable long time and therefore her husband/accused started searching her. She further deposed that at around 12.00 to 12.30 noon accused found her daughter/victim­girl at the house of his sister at Nahur. She also deposed that her daughter was left there at the house of her sister at Nahur and accused and she herself went to the house of his mother (her mother­in­law) at Mumbra. Then police came there to the house of mother of accused and then they went to police chowky, there she had seen her daughter. She asked her daughter as to why she had left the house, that time her daughter disclosed her about the incident. 17] However, during cross­examination Rehana (P.W.1) and victim­girl (P.W.2) both admitted that the victim­girl was having love affair with one boy Mashak Shaikh and it was not .. 12 .. Special Case No 45/2013 Judgment liked by the accused. P.W.1 and P.W.2 both admitted that when the accused was in jail, victim­girl (P.W.2) got married with said Mashak Shaikh. It is also admitted by victim­girl (P.W.2) that the house where her mother and stepsister are staying is in the name of her father. She also admits that her father is having good relations with his daughter from first wife (step­ sister) and her father / accused intended to transfer the house in the name of his step­daughter. However, Rehana (P.W.1) denied that the accused intended to transfer the house in the name of daughter of Fatima, daughter of his second wife and she (P.W.1) had objection for the same. 18] Further, it is also pertinent to note that the victim­ girl (P.W.2) had stated about the incident of molestation by her father during the period of 2 – 3 months before filing the complaint. However, no particular dates or period were stated by her. In this respect the evidence of P.W.3 Dr. Sunita Ubale who examined the victim­girl is also relevant. While giving history the victim­girl has stated to this witness that since 3­4 months, she was daily sexually assaulted by her father when her mother was not around and last rape was on 25.05.2013 around 7.30 a.m. However, the evidence of P.W.2 victim­girl itself discloses that on that day no sexual assault was committed on her but on that day as per her own version her father had only molested her by pressing her breast. Further, from the evidence of victim­girl (P.W.2) it is also clear that the .. 13 .. Special Case No 45/2013 Judgment accused only attempted to commit sexual assault but she always resisted it and thus, as per her own version she was only molested and forced to watch obscene clip on mobile phone and was touched inappropriately. The alleged obscene mobile clips/pictures were never seized. Even it is not case of prosecution that the mobile of accused which was seized under panchanama was having any such objectionable material. 19] Thus, testimony of victim­girl (P.W.2) amply clear that there was no penetrative sexual assault by the Accused. Whereas, Dr. Sunita Ubale (P.W.3) who examined victim­girl opined that there was evidence of penetrative vagina intercourse and medical certificate at Exhibit 31 stands to its testimony. It gives a large space to room of doubt and the defence taken by the Accused that his daughter victim­girl (P.W.2) was having love affair with one Mashak and also having relationship with him appears to be probable. In such background even FSL report which is at Exh.46 is also not helpful for prosecution which indicate blood grouping inconclusive and no semen were detected on any of the Articles. 20] Thus, meticulous evaluation of testimony of victim­ girl (P.W.2) does not inspire confidence in the background of admission given by her in respect of her having love affair with one Mashak Shaikh. From the day one it is the defence of the .. 14 .. Special Case No 45/2013 Judgment accused that his daughter was having love affair and relations with said Mashak Shaikh which was objected by him. So also, his sister­in­law protected his son who was not listening to him and therefore, he had threatened that if they shelter his son and the victim­girl continued her relations with Mashak Shaikh, he will transfer the house in the name of his daughter from first wife and therefore, he has been falsely implicated. The accused in his statement under section 313 of Cr.P.C. also has answered all the relevant questions by sticking up to his defence and he specifically stated said defence in his statement under section 313 of Cr.P.C. 21] Further, the story narrated by the victim­girl in her evidence that on that day of F.I.R. she ran away due to fear of her father and then firstly went to the house of her maternal aunt Kamrunissa (P.W.6) and disclosed the incident to her and while returning she met her father at Nahur railway station is concerned, there is clear contradiction from the mouth of her mother Rehana (P.W.1) who deposed that her daughter found missing since 8.30 a.m. and the accused went to search her and around 12.00 to 12.30 p.m. the accused found his daughter at the house of her sister at Nahur who is P.W.6 Kamrunissa. Further, in this respect it is also necessary to scrutinize the evidence of Kamrunissa (P.W.6), sister of Rehana (P.W.1). .. 15 .. Special Case No 45/2013 Judgment 22] A plain reading of testimony of maternal Aunt of victim­girl namely Kamrunissa (P.W.6) shows that she is not a believable witness. She put forward some another story. She deposed that on 25.05.2013 at about 10.30 a.m. the victim­girl (P.W.20 alone had been to her house. On that she asked as to how all of a sudden she had been there. On that she disclosed that her father is committing wrong act and used to show her obscene picture on mobile. She also deposed that the accused used to commit wrong act in the night and he used to threaten her at the point of knife that if she tell about it to anybody he will kill her and therefore she did not tell about it to anybody. This new story is put forth by P.W.6 when it is not the case of the P.W.1 or P.W.2 that the accused molested the victim­girl (P.W.2) and committed sexual assault on her in the night and threatened her on the point of knife. 23] Furthermore, even testimony of Rehana (P.W.1) is also does not found to be truthful. P.W.1 only sketch the incidence. At the cost of repetition it must state that neither P.W.1 nor P.W.2 stated about the timings when P.W.1 had been out of house for reaching articles to the customer. Further there is clear contradiction in their testimony whether P.W.1 being out of house daily or on alternate day. Thus, the evidence of P.W.1, P.W.2 and P.W.6 do not inspire confidence and on the contrary support the submission of accused that it is a concocted story put forth to restrain the accused from .. 16 .. Special Case No 45/2013 Judgment transferring his house in the name of his daughter from his first wife. Further, it is not believable that for 2 – 3 months the victim­girl has not disclosed about it to anybody only because of threat that she will be killed. On the contrary, she also admits that during that period she used to meet her boyfriend and it shows that she was having easy access outside and not narrating said incident to her mother or to P.W.6 before that, cannot be believed in the facts of the case. Further, the marriage of the victim­girl (P.W.2) with her boyfriend Mashak immediately when the accused was put behind bars when the victim­girl was barely 14 years old also supports the defense of the accused that he was implicated in false case with ulterior motive. Thus, the evidence of prosecution witnesses No.1, 2, & 6 does not inspire confidence and they do not appear to be a truthful witness. In such background evidence of Panch witness i.e. P.W.4 and investigating officers i.e. P.W.7 and P.W.8 which is of formal in nature also not of any help to prosecution. 24] The learned Spl.P.P. while submitting that minor victim­girl and her mother has no reason to depose falsly and delay is obvious in such cases of sexual assult, placed her reliance on the judgment of Honble Apex Court in case of Harpal Singh vs. state of H.P. AIR1981 S.C.361(1) and of Hon'bel Bombay High Court in case of Raju Chavan vs. State of Maharashtra 2015 ALL MR(cri)1968 & Mohan Kadam vs. State .. 17 .. Special Case No 45/2013 Judgment of Maharashtra 2015ALl MR(Cri)1972. There is absolutely no two opinion that in cases of sexual offenses, delay might have occurred for various reason and sole testimony of victim­girl is sufficient to record conviction if it inspires confidence. However, in the backdrop of above discussion and evaluation of evidence of material witnesses the case law relied on by prosecution would of no assistance to it. 25] Thus, the prosecution case is shrouded with thick clouds of doubt and prosecution failed to prove the serious charges leveled against the accused beyond reasonable doubt. Therefore, the prosecution is even not entitled for the benefit of twin presumption given under section 29 and 30 of the P.O.C.S.O Act. Therefore, the accused is entitled to be acquitted from all the charges leveled against him. Hence, I answer point Nos. 1 to 4 in the negative. 26] In the result, I proceed to pass following order; ORDER 1] The accused Mohammad Farid Shaikh alias Malau Shaikh is hereby acquitted under Section 235(1) of Criminal Procedure Code from the charge of the offence punishable under Section 376 & 292 of Indian Penal Code and under section 4 & 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. 2] The accused be released from jail forth with if not .. 18 .. Special Case No 45/2013 Judgment required in any other crime. 3] Muddemal property vide M.E.No.269/2015 being worthless be disposed of after appeal period and Mobile V.M.E.No.108/2015 be return to informant on her application after expiry of appeal period. 4] The accused is directed to furnish bail bond of the amount of 15,000/­ with one solvent surety of like amount, in compliance with provision of section 437­A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Judgment dictated and pronounced in open Court. Date : 30.11.2015. (Ms. U. M. Nandeshwar), Thane. Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act), Thane.

--1-- ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN REGULAR BAIL APPLICATOIN NO.1768/2017 The applicant Iqbal Sharif Khan has applied for bail under section 439 of Cr. P.C. in C.R.No.I­112/2017 registered in Thane Nagar police station for the offence under section 354(A)(B) of Indian Penal Code and Section 9 and 18 of POCSO Act, 2012. 2. It is contended that the name of the present applicant is not mentioned in FIR, but it is mentioned that he was knowing to the informant. It is contended that the offence is not punishable with death or imprisonment for life. He is earning member of the family. He is permanent resident of the given address. Therefore, there is no purpose will suffice by keeping the present applicant behind the bar. 3. In reply Investigating Officer at Exh.3 contended that the alleged sexual harassment is committed upon the victim who is nine years old. Previously the present applicant had asked for 4 to 5 times to the mother of the victim for taking the elder daughter of the informant to lodge in consideration of money. The informant and her family resides on road in hut. The victim is 9 years old. So if the applicant is released on bail he is likely to commit serious offence. He is not permanent resident of Thane. He is originally resident of Utter Pradesh. So after releasing he will tamper the prosecution witnesses. 4. Considering the facts and circumstances of this case it appears that previously the present applicant had asked the informant to provide her elder daughter for taking her to lodge --2-- in consideration of money and on the day of incident the accused entered into the hut of the informant and removed her knicker and he was attempting to commit wrong with her. At that time he was caught by the informant and police. If he was not arrested at that time he would have committed serious offence. The victim is only 9 years old. The informant and her family resides on road. So if the applicant is released on bail he will likely to commit more serious offence. The conduct of present applicant appears to be heinous as he has demanded elder daughter of the informant in consideration of money to take her to lodge. So he was constantly harassed the informant and his family members and on the day of incident he attempted to commit offence and therefore court is of the view that there is no guarantee that the applicant will improve his conduct. He is likely to commit more serious offence in respect to the informant's family members and likely to commit offences against other girls. He is also likely to tamper the prosecution witnesses because they are very poor and resides on footpath. Therefore, I am of the view that it is not a fit case to release the applicant on bail. Hence, I pass following order. ORDER Application for bail is rejected. Thane. ( S.C. Khalipe ) Date : 28/07/2017. Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

.. 1 .. Special Case No.169/2015 Judgment Received on : 22.07.2015 Registered on : 22.07.2015 Decided on : 01.09.2015 Duration : 1 months 10 days IN THE COURT OF THE SESSION JUDGE, THANE AT THANE (Presided over by Ms.V.V.Virkar, Additional Session Judge-1, Thane) Special Case No. 169 of 2015 Exhibit No. 05 The State of Maharashtra … Complainant versus Sunil Raj Parocha … Accused Age 30 years, Resident of Walmiki pada, Ambedkar chowk, Indiranagar, Wagle Estate, Thane JUDGMENT (Delivered on 01.09.2015.) The accused stands prosecuted for the offence punishable under section 7 read with section 8 and section 11 read with section 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short ''P.O.C.S.O. Act'') for committing sexual assault and sexual harassment upon the victim minor boy by holding his penis and moving it backward and forward and for threatening him not to disclose about it to anybody. .. 2 .. Special Case No.169/2015 Judgment 2] In short the facts giving rise to the prosecution of the accused are that on 16.05.2015 at about 4.15 p.m. minor son of complainant namely Shivam aged 8 years had gone to public toilet which near the house of the parents of the complainant and at that time the accused accosted him and held his penis by hand with sexual intent and moved it backward and forward and also threatened said boy not to disclose about it to anybody. It is further case of the prosecution that within short time the the father of the complainant appeared there and he saw the boy was crying and when inquired, the boy disclosed about the incident to him and also told that said person his hidden in the said public toilet. It is further case of the prosecution that thereafter the father of the complainant called the persons from surrounding and told them about the incident and thereafter took out into custody the accused and produced him before the police. Thereafter, the complainant went to police station and lodged complaint. 3] On the basis of her complaint, offence as per C.R.No. II- 30/2015 was registered at Shreenagar police station and the investigation was assigned to head constable Kadam. During the investigation panchnama of the spot was prepared. Statements of witnesses including victim boy were recorded. Copy of birth certificate of the boy showing her age was obtained. After completion of investigation, since there was sufficient against the accused, he was charge-sheeted for offence punishable under section 506 of I.P.C. and section 7, 11 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and the charge-sheet was submitted to the Special Court since provisions of P.O.C.S.O. Act are applied. 4] The accused was produced before Court by jail authorities. A charge as per Exhibit 2 was framed against the accused for offence under section 7 read with section 8 and section 11 read with section 12 of .. 3 .. Special Case No.169/2015 Judgment P.O.C.S.O. Act. The contents of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. The accused pleaded guilty and accepted the charges levelled against him and prayed for leniency while awarding the punishment. 5] On above facts of this case, the points which arose for my determination and my findings and reasons for the same are as under - Points Findings i) Whether the prosecution has proved that on 16.05.2015 at about 4.15 p.m. in open place near public toilet at Hanumannagar, Wagle Estate, Thane, the accused committed sexual assault and sexual harassment upon the victim boy by holding his penis in hand and Yes. moving it forward and backward with sexual intent? ii ) What offence, if any, is proved Offence of committing against the accused ? sexual assault and sexual harassment are proved. iii ) What order ? The accused is convicted. REASONS 6] As is clear the offence charge against the accused is under section section 7 read with section 8 and ection 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act with the allegation that the accused had committed sexual assault and sexual harassment upon the minor son of the complainant by holding his penis in hand and moving it forward and backward with sexual intent on the given day, date, time and place. Even it is also clear from the complaint lodged by the complainant that very specific allegations are made against the accused and on that basis offence under section 7 read with section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and section 11 read with section 12 of .. 4 .. Special Case No.169/2015 Judgment P.O.C.S.O. Act are charged against the accused and the accused has been prosecuted for the said offence. 7] In such circumstance it has to be mentioned that since the accused pleaded guilty and accepted the charges for the offence charged, the presumption under Section 29 of P.O.C.S.O. Act is applicable. Section 29 provides that ''Whether a person is prosecuted for committing or abetting or attempting to commit any offence under sections 3, 5, 7 and 9 of this Act, the Special Court shall presume, that such person has committed or abetted or attempted to commit the offence, as the case may be, unless the contrary is proved''. Thus, it is clear that in view of plea of guilty by the accused he is liable to be convicted for the said charge under section 7 read with section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. I therefore hold the accused guilty for offences under section 7 read with section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. 8] At this stage the dictation of the Judgment is postponed for hearing the accused on the point of sentence. Date : 01.09.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Additional Session Judge-1,Thane. Resumed. 9] The accused is made aware of the fact that he is held guilty for the offence under section 7 read with section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and the punishment prescribed for offence under section 7 read with section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act is punishable with imprisonment of minimum term of three years which may extend to five years and also with fine and offence under section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act is punishable with .. 5 .. Special Case No.169/2015 Judgment imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine. 10] I heard the accused and the learned A.P.P. on the point of sentence. The accused prayed for showing him leniency on the ground that he is the only earning member in his family and his family is depending upon him for their livelihood and submitted that he be awarded the sentence to the extent of term of imprisonment already undergone by him. The learned A.P.P. submitted that looking to the serious nature of offence charged against the accused which prescribes minimum punishment he is not entitled to leniency and he is liable for maximum punishment prescribed for offences proved. 11] Then, as is clear the offence charged against the accused is of serious nature with the allegation that the accused had committed sexual assault and sexual harassment upon the victim boy who was stated to be only 8 years old by holding his penis in hand and moving it forward and backward with sexual intent. But then, it is submitted by the accused on the point of sentence that he has to look after his family members and he is the earning person in his family. 12] Then, so far as quantum of punishment is concerned, as is clear the allegations made against the accused are much serious of committed sexual assault on a boy who was just 8 years old by holding penis of the boy in hand and by moving it backward and forward with sexual intent. Then, as is further clear the minimum punishment prescribed for offence under section 7 read with section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act is imprisonment for three years which may extend to five years and also fine whereas offence under section 11 read with section 12 of .. 6 .. Special Case No.169/2015 Judgment P.O.C.S.O. Act is punishable with imprisonment which may extend to three years and also with fine. 13] In all such circumstance, taking into consideration the serious charges levelled against the accused and the punishment prescribed therefor, I am of the view that following sentence would meet ends of justice. In the result I pass the following order - ORDER Accused namely Sunil Raj Parocha is convicted for the offence under section 7 read with section 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and is sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for three years and to pay fine of Rs.300/- [rupees three hundred only] and in default of payment of fine, he shall suffer S.I. for three days. II ) The accused is also convicted for offence under section 11 read with 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and is sentenced to suffer Rigorous Imprisonment for six months and also to pay fine of Rs.200/- [rupees two hundred only] and in default to pay fine amount, he shall suffer S.I. for two days. III ) Both sentences shall run concurrently. IV ) The accused is in jail since 17.05.2015. A set off under section 428 of the Cr.P.C. is granted to him for the term of the period of detention undergone by him during the investigation, inquiry and trial against the substantive sentence imposed upon him. V) Since no muddemal property is produced before Court, no order in regard to its disposal is passed. VI ) Copy of judgment be given to the accused free of cost. VII ) The proceeding is closed. Date : 01.09.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Additional Session Judge-1, Thane.

.. 1 .. Bail No. 1779/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1.) Order below Exhibit 1 in Criminal Bail Appln. No. 1779/2015 This application is filed by applicant namely Kaushal Suresh Kakde for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with C.R.No.I-347/2015 registered at Mumbra Police Station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 366A, 370, 376 read with section 34 of I.P.C. and section 5, 9 of Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act (hereinafter in short referred to as I.T.P.A.) and also under section 3, 4, 16 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as P.O.C.S.O. Act). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that accused persons compelled complainant/victim girl to do prostitution and earned money from said business. It is further contended and argued that the applicant is serving in Police Department and he is falsely implicated in this crime merely suspicion and with ulterior motive. It is further contended and argued that the applicant/accused has not been identified during test identification parade and no role is attributed to him. It is further submitted that co-accused has been ordered to be released on bail and therefore on the ground of parity the applicant/accused is also entitled to be released on bail. It is further submitted that since charge-sheet is also submitted, there is no need to further detain the applicant/accused in jail. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will attend the Court regularly for the purpose of trial and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. .. 2 .. Bail No. 1779/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1.) 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply 4 and it was contended and argued that the accused persons in furtherance of common intention had compelled the victim girl to indulge in prostitution and had earned money by indulging in said activity. It is further submitted that the complainant/victim girl has stated in her statement recorded as per Section 164 of Cr.P.C. in question-answer that two police personnel namely Kakde and Khan used to come to the house of co-accused Shabana alias Parveen and they also used to do wrong act with her and used to give money to Shabana for doing said act. It is further contended and argued that the girl has further stated in her statement that said policemen were also threatening her not to lodge complaint against said act otherwise they will book her mother in jail. It is further contended and argued that the girl has clearly stated about involvement of the present applicant in this crime. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening and pressurizing the victim girl and prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if released on bail, the applicant may abscond and will not be available for trial and may again indulge in such activity. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/ accused are of serious nature under section 366A, 370, 376 read with section 34 of I.P.C. and section 5, 9 of I.T.P.A. and also under section 3, 4, 16 of P.O.C.S.O. Act with the allegation .. 3 .. Bail No. 1779/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1.) that the applicant/accused was also committing sexual assault on the victim girl by going to the house of co-accused Shabana alias Parveen. But then, it is the contention of the applicant/accused that though the girl has named the applicant in her statement under section 164 of Cr.P.C. as the person committing sexual assault on her, she has not identified the applicant in the test identification parade and therefore it creates doubt about the very fact that the girl has made such statement voluntarily and without any coercion. Then, fact is also clear that the accused is in jail since 26.06.2015 and even charge-sheet is also stated to have been submitted. In such circumstance the aspect as to whether the allegations against the accused that he committed sexual assault on the girl are true or whether the contention of the accused that he is falsely implicated with mala fide intention is probable, would be the question to be decided on merits. 4] Then, it is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 5] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility .. 4 .. Bail No. 1779/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1.) of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 6] Then, it has also to be mentioned that though charge- sheet is submitted in the case, it will take time to take up the case for hearing and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 7] Then, it is material to mention that other accused are stated to have been ordered to be released on bail and therefore, the present applicant is also entitled to be released on bail on the ground of parity. 8] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order - ORDER The application is allowed. 1 Special Case (Pocso) No. 172/2015 Judgment Received on :­ 23.07.2015 Registered on :­ 23.07.2015 Decided on :­ 20.07.2017 Duration :­ 1Y 11M 27D IN THE COURT OF ADDITIONAL SESSIONS JUDGE, & SPECIAL JUDGE (POCSO) ACT, THANE AT : THANE ( Presided over by Ashutosh N.Karmarkar, District Judge­1 & Special Judge (POCSO) Act, Thane ) Special Case (POCSO) No.172/2015 Exh. No. State of Maharashtra ( Through Rabale M.I.D.C. Police Station ) …Complainant V/s. Gopal Chandrakant Khamkar Age : 19 Years, Occ. : Unemployed R/at.: Room No.14, Ganeshnagar, Chinchpada, Navi Mumbai … Accused. Offence punishable under Sec. 354(B) 506,323 of Indian Penal Code and under Sec.7 r/w. S. 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2 Special Case (Pocso) No. 172/2015 Judgment Appearances : Smt. Talhar, A.P.P. for the State Smt. Reena Korde, Advocate for accused JUDGMENT ( Delivered on this 20th day of July, 2017 ) 1] Accused is facing trial for the offence punishable under Sec. 354(B), 323, 506 of Indian Penal Code and under Sec. 7 and 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] Prosecution Case, in brief, is as under : Informant is the mother of victim. She is a news editor for India T.V. News, at Kalyan. Before incident she has seen that accused was holding hand of her daughter. The accused had also molested her. On 24.05.2015, in the noon she came to home. Victim had gone for her dance class. She came at 9.00 p.m. along with her friends. They narrated the incident that accused caught hold the hand of victim near bavadi area. Victim has also narrated that the accused pushed her and threatened to throw acid on her if she fails to act as per his say. Informant had been to that area at about 10.00 p.m. When she made enquiry about his act, accused threatened by uttering words “rqe ;gk ls tkvks ojuk eS rqedks Hkh /kks Mkyqaxk] ;gk ls pyh tk ugh rks eS rsjk vkSj rsjh csVh dk psgjk rstkc Mky ds tyk nqaxk** Then accused pushed her and his associate made her clothes to tear. She lodged report to police. Offence was registered vide C.R.No. I 109/2015. 3 Special Case (Pocso) No. 172/2015 Judgment 3] A.P.I. Kambale has investigated this crime. He drew spot panchanama. He has seized clothes on the person of victim under panchanama Exh.12. He recorded statements of witnesses. After detail investigation, he filed charge­sheet in the Court of law. 4] I have framed charge against accused below Exh. 4 to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 5] Prosecution has examined three witnesses. Then, the statement of the accused under Sec. 313 of Cr.P.C. came to be recorded. Total denial is the defence of the accused. The accused has also tried to raise defence in statement under Sec. 313 of Cr.P.C. that accused and victim were having love affair which was noticed by the informant. She stated about it to her son Aniket who came along with 15 to 20 boys to accused and beat him. The family members of the victim were not liking their affair and so, he is falsely implicated. 6] I have heard both the sides. 7] Following points arose for my determination and I gave my findings thereon for the reasons stated below: Sr. POINTS FINDINGS No. 1. Does the prosecution prove that the No accused along with absconding accused 4 Special Case (Pocso) No. 172/2015 Judgment Raju on 24.05.2015, in between 20.00 to 22.00 hrs., at well and fruit market, near Hanuman temple, Chinchpada, Digha, Navi Mumbai, assaulted or used criminal force to a minor victim girl of complainant, age 14 years with intention of disrobing her or compelling her to be naked and thereby committed an offence punishable under S. 354(B) of Indian Penal Code? 2. Does the prosecution prove that on Yes. above mentioned date, time and place accused along with absconding accused Raju committed criminal intimidation by threatening the complainant and minor victim girl with injury to their person with intent to cause alarm to them or to cause them to do an act which they are not legally bound to do and thereby committed an offence punishable under S.506 of Indian Penal Code? 3. Does the prosecution prove that No. accused along with absconding accused Raju on above mentioned date, time and place, voluntarily caused hurt to complainant's daughter minor victim girl and thereby committed an offence punishable under Sec. 323 of Indian Penal Code? 4. Does the prosecution prove that No. accused along with absconding accused Raju on above mentioned date, time and place, accused committed sexual assault on minor girl, age 14 years by pushing her with hand and putting his 5 Special Case (Pocso) No. 172/2015 Judgment hand on her chest with sexual intent involving physical contact without penetration and thereby committed an offence defined u/s. 7 punishable u/s. 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act? 5. What order? As per final order. REASONS 8] It is well settled principle of Criminal Law that in order to establish the guilt of the accused, prosecution is required to adduce cogent, convincing and reliable evidence. It is well settled that the sole testimony of the witness is also sufficient to base the conviction. But, the rule is that it should be above suspicion and should inspire confidence in the mind of Court. Prosecution has examined P.W.1 informant Renu (Exh.6), P.W.2 victim (Exh.10) and P.W. 3 I.O. Shri. Kambale (Exh. 16). AS TO POINT NO.4 :­ 9] In order to establish the guilt of accused under Sec. 7 r/w. 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, prosecution has to establish that the accused has touched part of the body of the victim as contended in Sec. 7 of the Act and that too with sexual intent. 10] It is alleged in the charge­sheet that on 24.05.2015, 6 Special Case (Pocso) No. 172/2015 Judgment accused put his hand over the chest of victim. Informant has stated that victim is her daughter. At the time of incident, age of victim was 14 years. She is acquainted to accused as he resides in their vicinity. According to her, incident occurred on 24.05.2015. Victim came home along with her friends and narrated the incident that accused caught hold her hand and has threatened to throw acid on her person on failure to act as per his say. So, the informant had been to make enquiry with the accused alone. When the informant tried to enquire with him, he threatened by uttering the words “rq>s Hkh /kks;sxk] rsjs mij Hkh rstkc Qsdqaxk**- She has further stated that accused pushed her and the associate of the accused torn clothes on the person of the informant. She was rescued by the people on the spot. She was frightened. On next day, she lodged report. The knowledge of the incident of informant is based upon the information given by the victim. 11] Victim has stated that her date of birth is 07.04.2000. In 2015, she was studying in Mahatma Gandhi High School, Airoli. She used to attend dance class along with her friends in between 6.00 to 9.00 p.m. She further stated that on 24.5.2015, she was returning to home from class. At that time, accused caught hold her hand on the road and stated that if she does not act as per his say then, he will give troubles to her and also to her family members. So, the victim has also not stated that the accused has touched the parts of the body of victim which are specifically mentioned in Sec. 7 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. The later 7 Special Case (Pocso) No. 172/2015 Judgment part of Sec. 7 is that whoever does any act with sexual intent which involves physical contact without penetration is said to commit sexual assault. Victim has just stated about catching hold of her hand by the accused. 12] The accused has come with the defence that there was love affair between the informant and the accused. Once the victim's mother had seen it and so he is implicated. Victim has admitted the joint photographs of the victim and the accused which are taken at Koparkhairane railway station and in the garden. Victim had voluntarily stated that earlier she used to talk to accused properly. This support the contention of the accused regarding the affair. Mere version of catching hold of hand will not be sufficient to bring the accused within the ambit of S. 7 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. 13] There is also variance in respect of the utterances of words by the accused in the evidence of victim and her mother. Informant has stated that she was told by the victim that the accused stated that if she does not act as per his say, then he would throw acid on her face and he is giving threats to kill. The victim has just stated that the accused told that if she fails to act as per his say then he would give trouble to her and her family members. So, the evidence of both these witnesses does not make it clear as to what accused wanted to say which the victim was required to act. Even the version of her giving the troubles by accused appears to be 8 Special Case (Pocso) No. 172/2015 Judgment vague. Both these witnesses tried to say about some sort of threats. It is already discussed that there is variance in the evidence of victim and her mother. It would be unsafe to rely on their testimony to hold accused guilty for the offence under Sec. 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. Even if it is accepted for a moment that there was physical contact by holding hand, still it has to be proved that, that act was done with sexual intent. On the basis of alleged utterances of the accused that on failure to act as per his say, he would give troubles will not sufficient to accept that there was sexual intent behind this alleged act. 14] So far as aspect of considering 'sexual intent', a reliance can be placed in case of Bandu Vitthalrao Borwar V/s. State of Maharashtra, Criminal Appeal No. 50 of 2016, ( Bombay High Court). It is held in paragraph 10 as under : Para 10 “After all intention of a person is his state of mind and has to be discerned from the surrounding facts and circumstances. If one cannot, as a human being, physically enter into a mind of another to read and see what is being cooked there, one can surely know it by evaluating all that which is perceivable or felt by human senses such as words, body­ language, gestures, reactions and everything that is a physical manifestation of working of human mind. It is held in Para 11 as under : 9 Special Case (Pocso) No. 172/2015 Judgment Para 11 “It is obvious that the intent, which is nothing but a state of mind, must be to establish some sort of physical contact or must be related to or associated with sex or indicative of involvement of sex in the relationship, if it is to be considered as sexual. There should be something more which must suggest that the real intention is to drag in the angle of sex, if the words uttered are to be taken as conveying sexual intent.” 15] Keeping in mind these observations of Hon'ble High Court, it will be difficult to accept that the alleged act of the accused as stated by the victim can not be said to be with sexual intent. The prosecution has also not examined any other witness to support the contention of the victim. For these reasons, accused can not be held guilty for the offence punishable under S. 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. AS TO POINT NO.1:­ 16] The evidence on record of the victim and her mother does not reveal that the accused has used criminal force towards the victim with the intention of disrobing or compelling her to be naked. Even if the evidence of both these witnesses is accepted as it is, it will fall short to prove the guilt of accused under Sec. 354(B) of Indian Penal Code. Therefore, I answer point No.1 in the negative. 10 Special Case (Pocso) No. 172/2015 Judgment AS TO POINT NO. 3:­ 17] The charge is framed under Sec. 323 pertaining to causing of hurt to the victim. It is alleged in the charge­sheet that the accused pushed the victim and then put his hand over her chest. The victim has nowhere stated that accused pushed her due to which she sustained injury. Victim's mother has also not stated about it. The medical report (Exh.14) of victim on record is admitted by the defence. It shows that no external injury was seen on the person of the victim. Hence, accused can not be held guilty for the offence under Sec. 323 of Indian Penal Code. Hence, I answer point No.3 in the negative. AS TO POINT NO. 2:­ 18] It is alleged in the charge­sheet that the accused has threatened the victim and her mother on 24.05.2015. In order to establish the guilt under Sec. 506 of Indian Penal Code, prosecution has to prove the following points.: (1) That the accused threatened the complainant or some other person. (2) That the threat was of some injury to him. (3) That it was given to cause alarm to him or to cause him not to do or to omit to do any act which he is legally entitled to, or was not bound to do. 11 Special Case (Pocso) No. 172/2015 Judgment The gist of the offence under Sec. 506 of Indian Penal code is causing of alarm to another person for doing a thing which he shall not bound to do. 19] It is already discussed in foregoing paragraphs that there is variance in the evidence of victim and her mother regarding threats to victim. Victim's mother has stated that the victim disclosed her that while returning from class, accused caught hold her hand and stated ^^ eS rsjs mij rstkc Qsdqaxk] rq>s tku ls ekj MkyqWsxk] vxj rq esjh ckr ugh ekusxh-** Victim has further disclosed about threats by accused to the victim. But, victim has just stated that accused has uttered the words ^^eh rqÖ;k dqVqafc;kauk =kl nsbZu-**So far as the allegation of threats to victim is concerned, it will be difficult to rely upon the evidence of victim and her mother considering the variance in their statement. The alleged utterance as to threats by the accused as stated by the victim appears to be vague. 20] Charge is also framed in respect of alleged threat to cause injury to the victim's mother. Victim's mother has stated that on disclosure of the incident by victim, she had been to near Hanuman temple and made enquiry with the accused in respect of alleged molestation. According to her, accused has threatened by uttering words “rq tk ugh rks rq>s Hkh /kks;sxk] rsjs mij Hkh rstkc Qsdqaxk-** When the informant reacted on it, accused pushed her. Then the associate of the accused tore clothes on the person of informant. 12 Special Case (Pocso) No. 172/2015 Judgment There is only denial in the cross­examination of informant. The manner of threats to the informant which is given by the accused appears to be consistent with the allegation of threat in the report Exh. 7. 21] It appears that the accused has not waited after utterance of such alleged words of threat but he then pushed the informant. Even the associate of the accused tore clothes on her person. Victim has also stated that after narration of the incident to informant, the informant went to make enquiry with the accused. When informant came back to home, victim noticed that clothes of her mother i.e. informant were in torn condition. There is also nothing in the cross­examination of the victim to shatter her testimony on this aspect. The accused has admitted the panchanama as to seizure of the clothes. 22] P.W.3 Kambale, investigation officer of this matter has also stated that he has seized the clothes on the person of the informant under panchanama Exh.12. He has also proved the receipt of the said muddemal on record (Exh.17). Receipt shows the description that the said clothe was in torn condition. All these circumstances discussed above clearly shows that there was clear indication as to what the accused was going to do after giving threats. 23] Evidence of informant also shows that after she was 13 Special Case (Pocso) No. 172/2015 Judgment pushed and her clothe was torn, she was frightened and has stayed at a home in the night. The evidence of both these witnesses makes it clear that the accused has threatened the informant to cause some injury to her person. Further action of the accused of pushing the informant itself shows that the said threat was given to cause alarm to the informant. The statement of accused under Sec. 313 shows that the accused has raised defence that the informant has seen the affair between accused and the victim. She told about it to her son Aniket who came with 15 to 20 boys. Accused has also stated in defence that at that time, the informant herself tore her clothes and went to home. This stand itself supports the informant's version of the incident of threat. 24] It is already discussed that the informant's evidence got support from the evidence of victim. There is no reason to disbelieve the informant in respect of the alleged threat to her. Discussion above lead me to say that the prosecution has established the guilt of accused under Sec. 506 of Indian Penal Code. Accused is to be heard on the point of sentence. 25] I have heard both the sides on the point of sentence. 26] Ld. Advocate for the accused has submitted that the accused has recently got job in house keeping section in one of the company. His mother is widow. His brother is also not well. So, it is 14 Special Case (Pocso) No. 172/2015 Judgment submitted that the lenient view may be taken. Ld. Advocate Smt. Korde has also submitted that the accused was in jail for three months. Ld. A.P.P. has submitted for maximum punishment. 27] The punishment prescribed for the offence u/sec. 506 of Indian Penal Code is imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years or with fine or with both. Considering the allegation as to offence against the women, I am not inclined to give benefit of the provisions of Probation of Offenders Act. At the same time, it can not be ignore that age of the accused as shown in the charge­sheet is 19 years. It also appears that he is facing trial since last 2 years. It is submitted by the Ld. Advocate for the accused that initially accused was in jail almost for three months. At the same time, accused must realize the consequences of such type of offence. While striking the balance on the basis of the submissions from both the sides, I am of the opinion that lenient view is required to be taken so as to give opportunity to the accused at his young age to improve himself. Considering the punishment prescribed for the offence, I think that the following order will be just and proper. Hence, I pass following order : ORDER 1] Accused Gopal Chandrakant Khamkar is convicted under Sec. 235 (2) of Code of Criminal Procedure of the offence punishable under Section 506 of Indian Penal Code. 15 Special Case (Pocso) No. 172/2015 Judgment 2] He is sentenced to suffer simple imprisonment till rising of the Court and to pay fine of Rs. 500/­ i.d. to suffer simple imprisonment for two months. 3] Accused Gopal Chandrakant Khamkar is acquitted under Sec. 235(1) of Code of Criminal Procedure of the offence punishable under Section 354 (B), 323 of Indian Penal Code and under Sec. 7 & 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 . 4] His bail bond stands cancelled. 5] Muddemal being worthless be destroyed after appear period is over. [ Dictated and pronounced in open Court. ] Thane, ( Ashutosh N. Karmarkar ) Date : 20.07.2017 District Judge­1 & Special Judge (POCSO) Act,Thane

1 Special Case (Pocso) No. 173/2015 Judgment Received on :­ 24.07.2015 Registered on :­ 24.07.2015 Decided on :­ 19.07.2017 Duration :­ 1Y 11M 25D IN THE COURT OF ADDITIONAL SESSIONS JUDGE, & SPECIAL JUDGE (POCSO) ACT, THANE AT : THANE ( Presided over by Ashutosh N.Karmarkar, District Judge­1 & Special Judge (POCSO) Act, Thane ) Special Case (POCSO) No.173/2015 Exh. No. 20 State of Maharashtra ( Through Kalwa Police Station ) …Complainant V/s. Jaychand Santoshkumar Yadav Age : 26 Years, Occ. : Labour R/at.: Siddhivinayak Chawl, Aatkoneshwar Nagar, Kalwa, Thane … Accused. Offence punishable under Sec. 363 of Indian Penal Code and under Sec. 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2 Special Case (Pocso) No. 173/2015 Judgment Appearances : Shri. S.D.Londhe, A.P.P. for the State Shri. Sunil Patankar, Advocate for accused JUDGMENT ( Delivered on this 19th day of July, 2017 ) 1] Accused is facing trial for the offence punishable under Sec. 363 of Indian Penal Code and under Sec. 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] Prosecution Case, in brief, is as under : Informant is the father of victim. Informant is a contractor. House of father­in­law of the informant is at Kalwa, Thane. The victim had been to the house of informant's father­in­ law since last one month. Informant has also entered into contract of house repairs in the same Kalwa area. He used to visit house of his father­in­law. Accused was also residing adjoining to the house of brother­in­law of the informant. On 10.05.2015, at 10.00 a.m., informant came to his site. On that day at 3.00 p.m., he went to the house of his father­in­ law. Victim met him and stated that when she was playing outside the house, at that time, the accused hold her tightly and after lifting her she was taken to his house andhe asked her “chal roti bana”. Then victim rescued herself and came to home. She has also stated that same incident was happened prior to 4­5 days. The informant and his brother­in­law went in search of accused. He was not found at his home. Accused was found at 8.15 3 Special Case (Pocso) No. 173/2015 Judgment p.m. in front of one hardware shop at Shivshakti Nagar Naka. Informant went along with victim there. Victim has pointed towards the accused who has committed the act of lifting her. On enquiry, accused stated that he did nothing. So, brother­in­law of the informant assaulted him. Accused fell unconscious. Police came there and they took him to the hospital. Then, informant lodged report. 3] On the basis of report, crime was registered vide C.R.No. I­214/2015. A.P.I. Bodhgire has investigated this crime. He drew spot panchanama and has recorded statements of witnesses. After completion of investigation, he filed charge­sheet in the Court of Law. 4] I have framed charge against accused below Exh. 6 to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 5] Prosecution has examined five witnesses. Then, the statement of the accused under Sec. 313 of Cr.P.C. came to be recorded. Total denial is the defence of the accused. The accused has also tried to raise defence that the accused was working with informant and his some amount was due from informant. Informant was not paying the dues. So, he demanded. Therefore, he is being falsely implicated. 6] I have heard both the sides. 4 Special Case (Pocso) No. 173/2015 Judgment 7] Ld. A.P.P. has submitted that the victim has stated in detail that she was hold tightly by the accused and after biting accused, she rescued herself. According to him, her evidence get support from evidence of her parents and witness Usha. According to him, there is no substance in the defence as nobody will keep character of his own daughter at stake. Ld. Advocate for the accused has submitted that the witnesses have admitted that the accused was working as labour with informant. Though the victim has stated in evidence about biting, she has stated that she does not remember whether it was narrated to police. According to him, there is nothing in the evidence to establish the guilt under Sec. 7 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. 8] Following points arose for my determination and I gave my findings thereon for the reasons stated below: Sr. POINTS FINDINGS No. 1. Does the prosecution prove that the No accused on 10.05.2015, at about 15.00 hrs., at Mauje Siddhivinayak Chawl, Aatkoneshwar Nagar, Kalwa, Thane kidnapped daughter of complainant i.e. minor victim girl Ku. Prajakta Ghole, age 7 years from lawful guardianship of her parents and thereby committed an offence punishable under S. 363 of Indian Penal Code? 5 Special Case (Pocso) No. 173/2015 Judgment 2. Does the prosecution prove that on No. above mentioned date, time and place, accused committed sexual assault on minor girl Ku. Prajakta Ghole by lifting her forcibly and touching her chest with sexual intent involving physical contact without penetration and thereby committed an offence defined u/s. 7 punishable u/s. 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act? 3. What order? As per final order. REASONS AS TO POINT NO.1 & 2­ 9] In order to establish the guilt of accused under Sec. 7 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, prosecution has to establish that the accused has touched part of body of the victim as contended in Sec. 7 that too with sexual intent. In order to establish the guilt of accused under Sec. 363 of Indian Penal Code, the prosecution has to establish that the age of victim was below 18 years at the time of alleged kidnap. Secondly, that victim was in the keeping of lawful guardian and thirdly, the accused took or enticed the victim out of such keeping without consent of guardian. 10] The prosecution has examined informant Rupesh Ghole, P.W.5 (Exh.18), P.W.1 his wife Rupali Ghole (Exh.10), P.W.2 6 Special Case (Pocso) No. 173/2015 Judgment victim Prajakta (Exh.12), P.W.3 Usha Samarth (Exh.13) and P.W.4 investigation officer , A.P.I. Bodhgire (Exh.15). 11] It is well settled that in order to prove the guilt of accused, it is incumbent on the part of the prosecution to adduce cogent, convincing and reliable evidence. It is well settled that the sole testimony of witness is also sufficient to base the conviction. But, the rule is that it should be above suspicion and should inspire confidence in the mind of court . 12] It is admitted by P.W.1 Rupali and P.W.3 Usha in the cross­examination that the accused was working with informant Rupesh. P.W. 3 Usha has also admitted that accused was residing behind their house. It is also contended in the report (Exh.16) that the accused was residing adjoining to the house of his brother­in­ law where victim had gone on the day of alleged incident. 13] P.W. 1 Rupali has stated that on 10.05.2015, she was at the house of her mother. Her mother, brother's wife and sister were also in the house. Victim was playing outside the house. Victim came to home by running. She enquired with the victim as she was frightened. Victim narrated that Patar uncle i.e. the accused caught hold her from her backside and pressed her chest and lifted her. She further stated that he took victim to his house and stated her to prepare roti. Victim rescued herself. Then P.W.1 Rupali went to make enquiry with the accused. He was not at home. She called 7 Special Case (Pocso) No. 173/2015 Judgment her husband and brother. They found the accused near one shop in between 4.00 to 5.00 p.m. Victim pointed out towards the accused who committed the offence. Victim had also stated her mother that the accused has committed same offence four to five days before. Her husband lodged report. 14] P.W.5 Rupesh has also stated that the victim narrated the same incident to him on his arrival at home. He has stated some different story that they could trace out the accused at 8.00 p.m. This witness has nowhere stated that the victim has stated that this accused has committed similar offence before 4 to 5 days. 15] It is to be noted that P.W.1 Rupali has admitted in the cross­examination that the accused was working as labour with her husband. She has admitted that their economical condition is not so sound. It is admitted that there are some incidents in the past that the concerned customers whose work is undertaken by her husband, have not paid his charges. She has also admitted that there are also incidents that there were dispute between her husband and the labours on the count of non­payment of the labour charges to the labours. P.W.1 Rupali has denied this suggestion of the accused that the amount of Rs.20,000/­ of the accused was due from her husband. On considering these admissions, the evidence of P.W.1 Rupali and P.W.5 Rupesh is to be scrutinized minutely. 16] It is already discussed that there is major contradiction 8 Special Case (Pocso) No. 173/2015 Judgment in the evidence of P.W.1 Rupali and P.W.5 Rupesh as to the timing when the accused was traced out. Evidence of both these witnesses show that the victim has pointed out towards the accused in front of one shop. It is to be noted that the P.W.1 Rupali had admitted that accused resides in their area. It is also contended in the report (Exh.16) that the accused resides adjoining to the house of his brother­in­law where victim and her mother had gone on the day of incident and he is well acquainted to accused. 17] P.W. 3 Usha who is grandmother of the victim has also stated that the accused resides behind their house. If really the accused is residing adjoining to the house of victim's grandmother and when the accused was admittedly working with victim's father, there was no need to have identification of the accused with victim. Evidence of all these witnesses Rupali, Rupesh and Usha show that their knowledge as to incident is based upon information given by the victim. 18] It is the case of prosecution that at the relevant time, age of victim was 7 years. The evidence of victim also shows that she does not understand the sanctity of oath. Looking to these facts, the evidence of the victim is required to be scrutinized cautiously. According to victim, she was in first standard at the time of incident. She was playing outside the house. She has further stated that the accused i.e. Patar uncle caught hold her tightly and took her to the doorcase of his house and told her as 9 Special Case (Pocso) No. 173/2015 Judgment “Roti Banao”. It is to be noted that the prosecution has not examined any witness from the corporation or the witness from the school where victim is studying to prove her age. 19] In order to establish the guilt of accused under Sec. 7 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, the prosecution has to establish that the accused has touched the parts of the body as contended in it. According to P.W.1 Rupali and P.W.5 Rupesh, victim has narrated that the accused pressed the chest of victim. But, the victim has not stated specifically this fact in her evidence. Victim has stated that the accused hold her tightly and took her to the doorcase. P.W.1 Rupali, P.W.5 Rupesh and P.W.3 Usha have stated that the victim has stated that the accused took her to his house. The informant has also stated while lodging report (Exh.16) that accused took victim to his house and nobody was in the house. Victim has not stated this fact. Victim has stated that after taking her to doorcase, accused stated as “Roti Banao”. She rescued herself after biting him. According to her, on its next day, accused again lifted her and took her. It is to be noted that the alleged incident was of 10.05.2015. It appears that the accused was arrested on next day in the morning at 9.50. 20] Recitals of the report Exh.16 also reveal that on 10.05.2015, in the evening accused was beaten by the informant's 10 Special Case (Pocso) No. 173/2015 Judgment brother­in­law. So, he was unconscious and police took him to the house. So, this fact creates doubt as to whether there was possibility to commit similar type of offence by the accused on next day. Considering these facts it would be unsafe to rely on the testimony of victim. 21] According to P.W.1 Rupali, victim has stated her that similar type of offence was committed by accused before 4 to 5 days. This fact is not stated by the victim in her evidence. Considering these facts, age of the victim at the relevant time and her non­understanding as to sanctity of oath, it will be difficult to rely on the testimony of the victim. 22] Even if the evidence of victim is accepted as it is, prosecution is expected to establish that this act of the accused was with 'sexual intent'. In order to ascertain as to whether there was 'sexual intent', other circumstances are required to be taken into consideration. According to victim, accused took the victim to his doorcase and stated as “Roti banao”. Considering the age of victim of 7 years, it would be difficult to accept that nobody would say in such a manner to a victim of seven years. If really, there was 'sexual intent' on the part of accused, he would not have stated the victim as “Roti bano''. If really there was such intent, then accused would have certainly taken her inside the house. So, evidence on record can not be said to be sufficient to hold that there was sexual intent on the part of the accused. 11 Special Case (Pocso) No. 173/2015 Judgment So far as aspect of considering 'sexual intent', a reliance can be placed in case of Bandu Vitthalrao Borwar V/s. State of Maharashtra, Criminal Appeal No. 50 of 2016, ( Bombay High Court). It is held in paragraph 10 as under : Para 10 “After all intention of a person is his state of mind and has to be discerned from the surrounding facts and circumstances. If one cannot, as a human being, physically enter into a mind of another to read and see what is being cooked there, one can surely know it by evaluating all that which is perceivable or felt by human senses such as words, body­ language, gestures, reactions and everything that is a physical manifestation of working of human mind. It is held in Para 11 as under : Para 11 “It is obvious that the intent, which is nothing but a state of mind, must be to establish some sort of physical contact or must be related to or associated with sex or indicative of involvement of sex in the relationship, if it is to be considered as sexual. There should be something more which must suggest that the real intention is to drag in the angle of sex, if the words uttered are to be taken as conveying sexual intent.” 23] In view of this citation also and considering the evidence on record as discussed above, it will be rather difficult to accept that the real intent of the accused was to drag the victim in 12 Special Case (Pocso) No. 173/2015 Judgment the angle of sex. The victim has stated that she rescued herself after biting the accused. If it was the fact then investigation officer should have referred him for medical examination. It is not stated by the investigation officer that at the time of incident he had noticed human bite injury and that was recorded in the arrest panchanama. 24] On the other hand, accused has raised defence that the amount of Rs. 20,000/­ towards his work was due from the informant and he was demanding the same. According to him, the informant has implicated him so that he should not demand the amount. It is undisputed that the accused was working with informant as labour. It is admitted by the informant's wife that there used to be dispute between her husband and the labours in connection with non­payment of labour charges. According to Ld. A.P.P,.the suggestion of the accused that the amount was due from the informant and he is falsely implicated has been denied. So, the defence is not probable. Considering the discussion in the foregoing paragraphs, it can not be accepted that the defence of the accused is improbable. 25] Since it is discussed in the foregoing paragraphs that the evidence of victim and her parents and P.W. Usha are not consistent, it will be also difficult to accept that the accused has either taken or enticed the victim. It is also discussed that the 13 Special Case (Pocso) No. 173/2015 Judgment victim has just stated about taking her to doorcase of the accused and again on next day, accused has repeated the same thing. It is discussed that since accused was arrested on next day in the morning it will be difficult to accept about possibility of repeating this crime. The victim's mother is saying about similar incident by the accused before 4 to 5 days. But, this fact is not stated by the victim. 26] Considering the evidence of all these witnesses, it will be difficult to accept that true account of the incident has been brought on record by the prosecution. So, the benefit of doubt of these facts is required to be given to the accused. It is also discussed that the prosecution has not examined any material witness to bring on record the exact age of the victim. So, I find that the prosecution for want of satisfactory and cogent evidence, failed to establish the guilt of the accused for which accused is charged. Hence, I answer point Nos.1 & 2 in the negative and proceed to pass following order: ORDER 1] Accused Jaychand Santoshkumar Yadav is hereby acquitted under Sec.235(1) of Code of Criminal Procedure of the offence punishable under Sec. of Indian Penal Code and Sec. 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] His bail bond stands cancelled. 14 Special Case (Pocso) No. 173/2015 Judgment 3] Accused shall furnish P.B and S.B. of RS. 10,000/­ under Sec. 437­A of Code of Criminal Procedure. 4] Dictated and pronounced in open Court.
