Received On : 11/07/2017 Registered On : 11/07/2017 Decided On : 31/08/2018 Duration : Y. M. D. 01 01 20 IN THE COURT OF AD HOC DISTRICT JUDGE­3, & ADDITIONAL SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE AT : THANE [ Presided Over by Shri.R.S.Patil (Bhosale)] SPL. CASE (CHILD PROT.) NO. 157 OF 2017 CNR­MHTH01­004772­2017 Exh. No. State of Maharashtra ( Through Sanpada, Navi Mumbai Police Station ) … Prosecution Vs. Bhagwan Budhaji Araj, Age : 23 years, R/at : Room No.1, Sambhare Chawl, Near Hanuman Temple, Kalambe, Taluka­Shahapur, District­Thane. … Accused. Offence Punishable Under Sec. 363, 376(1) of the Indian Penal Code, Section 3(a), 4, 5(j)(ii), 6 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2 Spl. Case No.157/2017(Judg.) Appearances : Shri. V. A. Kulkarni, Ld. A.P.P. for the State Smt. Rina Korde, Ld. Advocate for the accused. JUDGMENT ( Dictated and delivered on day of 31st August, 2018 in Open Court ) 1] In this case accused is prosecuted for the offence punishable under section 363, 376(1) of the Indian Penal Code, Section 3(a), 4, 5(j)(ii), 6 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 2] Prosecution's case in short is as follows : Complainant Laxmi Dattaram Desai who was working as Supervisor in Vatsalya Trust, Sanpada, Navi Mumbai lodged complaint in Sanpada police station on 02/08/2016 alleging that victim girl Soni Santosh Shaha age 17 years residing in Vatsalya Trust, is kidnapped by unknown person. Police investigated said offence and it was transpired that victim girl Soni Santosh Shah was having love affair with accused since the year 2010. On 18/03/2015, victim girl Soni Santosh Shaha was eloped with accused and performed marriage in one temple at Shahapur. At that time said victim girl was residing in a hostel run by Naya Jivan Sanstha as her father and mother had died when she was child. Hence, Smt. Trija Dabre a care taker of said hostel lodged complaint in Shahapur police station. On the basis of said complaint, Shahapur police registered C.R. No.87/2015 under 3 Spl. Case No.157/2017(Judg.) section 363 of IPC. Then victim girl and accused appeared before Shahapur police on 19/03/2015 and accused was arrested. He was released on bail. Then chargesheet was submitted against the accused. At that time victim girl Soni was below the age of 18 years. Hence, she was produced before Child Welfare Committee who admitted her in the Vatsalya Trust, Sector­2, Sanpada, Navi Mumbai. Victim girl was residing in said Trust since 19/05/2015 who was educated up to the 9th standard and trying to give examination of 10th standard as an external student. Nursing training was imparted to victim girl in said Trust and she was doing practice in D.Y. Patil Hospital, Nerul. At that time accused met her in the month of October 2015 and December 2015. On one occasion mother of accused also saw her. After completing age of 18 years accused and his mother were intending to take victim girl to their house and perform their marriage. Meanwhile, accused was keeping contact with victim girl on phone. In the month of February 2016, victim girl went to Sahapur and met accused. At that time accused has given mobile phone to her. On 01/08/2016 victim girl went to Smile Care Dental Clinic for practice from Vatsalya Trust. Then she called accused and informed that she is coming towards him. At that time accused informed her that she should come by railway at Ambernath. At that time without informing to any person, victim girl went to Ambernath. Victim girl and accused resided at Ram Mandir, Phule nagar, Ambernath in one room on rent for about three months. She was in touch with accused on phone. In the month of February 2016, when victim girl went to the house of accused, at that time they have kept physical relation with each other. In the month of July 2016, victim 4 Spl. Case No.157/2017(Judg.) girl came to know that she became pregnant from accused. She informed said fact to accused. At that time victim girl came to know that her age is below 18 years and as she is pregnant she will not be allowed to reside in Vatsalya Trust and they will not perform her delivery. Therefore, she eloped from Vatsalya Trust alongwith accused on 01/08/2016. Then victim girl delivered a son in Chhaya Hospital, Ambernath on 14/11/2016. Meanwhile, on 02/08/2016 Laxmi Desai lodged above mentioned complaint alleging that victim girl is kidnapped. 3] On the basis of said complaint lodged by Laxmi Desai, Sanpada police registered C.R. No. I­114/2016 and assigned its investigation to Shri. G.G. Survade, PSI of Sanpada police station. He investigated the offence, recorded statements of the witnesses, got medically examined victim girl and as sufficient evidence is gathered against accused, lodged chargesheet against him on 11/07/2017. He arrested accused on 14/04/2017. Accused is released on bail on 30/05/2017. 4] Charge against accused is framed at Exh.2 on 25/07/2018. Particulars of the charge were read over and explained to accused in vernacular. But accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. Hence, this prosecution. In his defence accused denied entire evidence adduced by prosecution against him. 5] The points arise for my determination with my findings thereon are as follows : 5 Spl. Case No.157/2017(Judg.) SR. NO. POINTS FINDINGS 1] Does prosecution prove that on 01/08/2016 at Smile Care Dental Crinic, Sector­2, Sanpada, Navi Mumbai, accused kidnapped … In the negative. minor girl Soni from the lawful custody of Vatsalya Trust ? 2] Does prosecution prove that in the month of February 2016 and afterwards from time to time in his house and in one rental room … In the negative. taken by accused at Ram mandir, Phulenagar Ambernath, accused committed rape on victim girl ? 3] Does prosecution prove that on the same dates, time and place by committing above mentioned act … In the negative. accused has committed penetrative sexual assault on minor victim girl Soni ? 4] Does prosecution prove that on the same date, time and place by committing above mentioned act … In the negative. accused has committed aggravated penetrative sexual assault on minor victim Soni and make her pregnant as a consequence of sexual assault ? 5] What order ? … As per final order. :REASONS: 6] In order to prove alleged guilt of the accused, prosecution has examined P.W.No.1 Soni Santoshkumar Shaha, a victim girl at Exh.4. Prosecution has produced her birth certificate and birth 6 Spl. Case No.157/2017(Judg.) certificate of her son Aditya at Exh.5 and 6 respectively. Advocate for accused has admitted complaint lodged by Laxmi Desai, panchanama of the spot of incident, medical examination papers of accused, Forensic medical examination of accused, medical examination paper of victim girl Soni Shaha, Forensic medical examination report of victim girl, out patient record of accused which are at Exh.8, 11, 9, 10, 12, 13, 14 respectively. Prosecution has produced evidence close pursis at Exh.15. 7] In the light of the above mentioned evidence adduced by prosecution, I proceed to record my findings on each point as follows : AS TO POINT NOS. 1 TO 4 : 8] P.W. No.1 Soni Shaha, a victim girl has stated in her evidence that her father and mother had died when she was child. Therefore, she was residing in hostel of Naya Jivan Sanstha for nine years for education from 1st standard to 9th standard. Her birth date is 20/12/1998. The said witness has admitted her birth certificate which is at Exh.5. Triza Dabare was care taker of her hostel. She know accused. She identified accused in the court. P.W. No.1 has stated in her evidence that accused was in her school. On 18/03/2015 she performed marriage with accused in temple at Asangaon, Taluka­Shahapur. Her marriage is love marriage. At that time she was taking education in 9 th standard. She directly went for marriage without obtaining permission. After marriage she was produced before Child Welfare Committee as her age was below 18 years. The said committee kept her in Vatsalya 7 Spl. Case No.157/2017(Judg.) Trust, Sanpada, Navi Mumbai where nursing training was given to her. At that time she was doing practice in D.Y. Patil Hospital, Nerul. In the year 2016 she was practicing in Smile Care Dental Clinic. On 01/08/2016 she went alongwith accused to Ambernath. She resided with accused in Ambernath, Fulenagar in one rented room for three months. Nothing was happened when she was residing in said room. The said witness has admitted in her cross examination that whenever she went alongwith accused, on each time she went alongwith accused on her own wish and at that time accused never misbehaved with her. 9] It is the prosecutions case through statement of victim girl dated 14/04/2017 that on 01/08/2016 she went from Vatsalya Trust to Smile Care Dental Clinic for practice and from said clinic she phoned to accused and informed him that she is leaving the Vatsalya Trust and wants to come with accused. Therefore, accused stated her to come at Ambernath by railway. Accordingly, she went there. So, above stated prosecutions case and evidence adduced by victim girl on record clearly show that victim girl has on her own accord left her hostel on 18/03/2015, 01/08/2016 and went towards accused. At the both said times accused has neither played active role nor any passive role to elope victim girl with him. It is pertinent to note here that birth certificate of victim girl at Exh.5 shows that her date of birth is 20/12/1998. Hence, on the date of marriage i.e. on 18/03/2015 victim girl is about 16 years. So also, on 01/08/2016 when victim girl left Vatsalya Trust, at that time she was about 17 years eight months and at the verge of attaining majority age and attained the age of discretion. She is educated 8 Spl. Case No.157/2017(Judg.) one. She knows what is man and woman and relationship between them. She knows what are the consequences of the act going to be committed by her. Therefore, considering all said facts on record, I am of the view that accused has not kidnapped her from the lawful guardianship. On this point reference with profit can be made of a reported case S. Varadarajan Vs. State of Madras, AIR 1965, S.C. 942, in which it has been observed by Hon'ble Apex Court that, “ 5.... There is no suggestion in Savitri's evidence, who, it may be mentioned had attained the age of discretion and was on the verge of attaining majority that she was made by the appellant to accompany him by administering any threat to her or by any blandishments. The fact of her accompanying the appellant all along is quite consistent with Savitri's own desire to be the wife of the appellant in which the desire of accompanying him wherever he went was of course implicit. In these circumstances we find nothing from which an inference could be drawn that the appellant had been guilty of taking away Savitri out of the keeping of her father. She willingly accompanied him and the law did not cast upon him the duty of taking her back to her father's house or even of telling her not to accompany him. She was not a child of tender years who was unable to think for herself but, as already stated, was on the verge of attaining majority and was capable of knowing what was good and what was bad for her. She was no uneducated or un­ sophisticated village girl but a senior college student who had probably all her life lived in a modern city and was thus far more capable of thinking for herself and acting on her own than perhaps an unlettered girl hailing from a rural area. The learned Judge of the High Court has referred to the decision In re : Abdul Sathar(1) in which it was held that where the evidence disclosed that, but for something which the accused consented to do and ultimately did, a minor girl would not have left her husband's house, or would not have been able to leave her husband's house, there was sufficient taking in law for the purpose of S. 363 and expressing agreement with this statement of the law observed: "In this case the minor, P.W. 4, would not 9 Spl. Case No.157/2017(Judg.) have left the house but for the promise of the appellant that he would marry her." Quite apart from the question whether this amounts to blandishment we may point out that this is not based upon any evidence direct or otherwise. In Abdul Sathar's case(1) Srinivasa Aiyangar J., found that the girl whom the accused was charged with having kidnapped was desperately anxious to leave her husband's house and even threatened to commit suicide if she was not taken away from there and observed : "If a girl should have been wound up to such a pitch of hatred of her husband and of his house or household and she is found afterwards to have gone out of the keeping of her husband, her guardian, there must undoubtedly be clear and cogent evidence to show that she did not leave her husband's house herself and that her leaving was in some manner caused or brought about by something that the accused did." In the light of this observation the learned Judge considered the evidence and came to the conclusion that there was some legal evidence upon which a court of fact could find against the accused. This decision, therefore, is of little assistance in this case because, as already stated, every essential step was taken by Savitri herself : it was she who telephoned to the appellant and fixed the rendezvous, she walked up to that place herself and found the appellant waiting in the car; she got into the car of her own accord without the appellant asking her to step in and permitted the appellant to take her wherever he liked. Apparently, her one and only intention was to become the appellant's wife and thus be in a position to be always with him.” In this reported case Hon'ble Apex Court acquitted appellant/accused from the offence punishable under section 363 of the I.P.C. 10] In the case in hand, as stated above victim girl Soni has 10 Spl. Case No.157/2017(Judg.) stated in her evidence that on 18/03/2015 she performed marriage with accused. It is the love marriage. The said witness has also admitted in her cross examination that she is happily enjoying married life with accused and having no complaint against him. She has stated to police on 14/04/2017 that she has no complaint against accused. The said witness has also admitted in her cross examination that before marriage accused never kept physical relation with her. So, above stated evidence of victim girl shows that at the time of marriage victim girl was about the age of 16 years. Explanation 2 to proviso to section 375 of the IPC states that sexual intercourse or sexual acts by a man with his own wife, the wife not being under 15 years of age, is not rape. In Sunil Mahadev Patil Vs. State of Maharashtra, ABC, 2016 (I) 34 Bom. Criminal Bail application No.1036/2015, it has been observed by Hon'ble Bombay High Court that, under section 375 proviso to its section 2 if the age of a woman is 15 years but she is married, then it would not amount to rape. Therefore, in the event of marriage, the minimum age of capability to have sex is fifteen years. On this backdrop, though victim girl has admitted medical documents on record and stated that accused is father of her son and birth date of her son Aditya is 14/11/2016, it will not amount to rape. 11] The object behind POCSO Act is to protect children from offences of sexual assault, sexual harassment and pornography and provide for establishment of Special Courts for trial of such offences and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. In the case in hand, status of victim girl is not of child but is of wife. 11 Spl. Case No.157/2017(Judg.) When the alleged act against accused is not offence under the provisions of section 363, 376 of the I.P.C. then there is no offence under the provisions of POCSO Act. Hence, for all above stated reasons, prosecution has failed to prove alleged guilt of the accused. Hence, I am recording my findings on point No. 1 to 4 in the negative. 12] Hence, I proceed to pass following order :­ ORDER 1. Accused Bhagwan Budhaji Araj is hereby acquitted under Section 232 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, of the offence punishable under Section 363, 376(1) of the Indian Penal Code and Section 3(a) 4, 5(j)(ii), 6 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2. He be set at liberty forthwith if not required in any other offence. 3. Accused is hereby directed to execute P.B. & S.B. of Rs.15,000/­ under section 437­A of the Code of Criminal Procedure for his appearance before the Hon'ble Higher court as and when such court issues notice in respect of any appeal or petition filed against this judgment and such bail bonds shall be in force for six months. .. 1 .. Bail No. 1797/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1.) Order below Exhibit 1 Criminal Bail Application No. 1797/2015 This application is filed by applicant/accused namely Shivmani Ramdular Jaiswar for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no.I­329/2015 registered at Wagle Estate police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 376(2) of I.P.C. and section 3, 4 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as P.O.C.S.O. Act) filed with the allegation that the applicant/accused committed sexual assault on the victim girl repeatedly. It was contended and argued that the applicant/accused is falsely implicated in this case with ulterior motive. It is further contended and argued that there was dispute on account of money between the accused and mother of the girl and therefore a false complaint is lodged against the accused. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co­operate with investigating machinery and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply vide Exhibit 6 and it was contended and argued that the present applicant is acquainted with the complainant and children and he used to visit them frequently. It is further contended and argued that it revealed during the investigation that whenever the complainant i.e. mother of the victim girl was out of home for work, the accused used to come to her home and used to .. 2 .. Bail No. 1797/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1.) send younger sister and brother of the victim girl out of house by giving them money to purchase eatables and thereafter, after closing the door from inside he used to commit penetrative sexual assault on the minor victim girl aged 10 years. It is further contended and argued that the accused was committing sexual assault on the girl since about two months before lodging the complaint. It is further contended and argued that the accused had also threatened the victim girl to kill her if she disclose about the act to anybody. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl, complainant and other prosecution witnesses including child witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of very serious nature under section 376 of I.P.C. and section 3, 4 of P.O.C.S.O. Act with the allegation that the accused frequently committed sexual assault on the minor girl aged 10 years by doing forcible sexual intercourse with her. Then, from perusal of complaint it reveal that the accused used to come to the house of complainant when she was not home and he then used to send younger brother and sister of the victim girl out of house by giving them money to purchase eatables. Even the complainant also appear to have stated in detail the manner in which the accused was committing sexual assault and it is also contended that the accused was always threatening the girl to beat her if she disclose .. 3 .. Bail No. 1797/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1.) about the act to her mother. On the other hand, the accused has come up with the case that there is rivalry between him and the mother of the girl on account of money and therefore, this false complaint is lodged with false allegations. But then, looking to serious allegations of sexual assault on the girl, such allegations will have to be decided on merits and at this stage it would be premature to conclude that on account of previous replay in connection with money transaction the applicant/ accused is falsely involved in the crime. 4] No doubt it is well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. However, it has to be mentioned that besides that the gravity and serious nature of offence and the manner in which it is stated to have been committed also has to be looked into and looking to the nature of offence and the manner in which it is alleged to have been committed, a wrong message would be sent to the society in case of release of accused on bail in such type of matter wherein serious allegations of murder are made. 5] Then, it is also to be mentioned that investigation in the matter is stated to be in progress and and looking to serious nature of allegation and the manner in which offence is stated to have been committed there is possibility that the accused may threaten and pressurize the complainant and girl and other .. 4 .. Bail No. 1797/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1.) witnesses including child witnesses and may tamper with prosecution evidence. Then, the accused is stated to be native of Uttar Pradesh State and therefore the possibility of accused being absconded and not being available for trial also cannot be ruled out. No doubt it is also well settled that merely on the ground that the accused is from other State bail application cannot be rejected. But then, in that regard also it is to be mentioned that that is not the sole ground in this case to negate the claim of bail and as discussed above on other grounds also he is not found to be entitled to bail. 6] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is not a fit case wherein the applicant/accused can be said to be entitled to be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is rejected. Date : 05.10.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Additional Session Judge­1, Thane.

Case No.47/2013 (Judgment) :JUDGMENT: (Delivered on 18th day of June, 2015) 1] The accused put to trial for offence under Sec. 354 of Indian Penal Code and Sec. 7 and 9(m) of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012, on accusation of having tried to outrage modesty of his daughter. 2] The prosecution case, in brief is as under : On 15.3.2013, at 2.00 a.m., prosecutrix screamed. Seema Raj rushed to their daughter's room. She asked frightened prosecutrix what had happened. She told that her father was only wearing underwear, came and sleep close to her. Her father moved hand on her whole body. She woke up and yelled. 3] On the complaint of mother of prosecutrix Seema Raj, offence registered against the accused. Investigating Officer proceed to the spot and prepared spot panchanama. Investigating Officer arrested accused on 15.3.2013. Statement of prosecutrix was recorded by Special Executive Officer. On finding substance in the accusations, the investigating officer filed charge­sheet in the court. 4] Special Judge (Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act), Thane (Smt.V.V.Virkar) has framed charge (Exh.3). A.P.P. and defence Counsel. After considering the evidence on record and submissions of the defence counsel, the following points arise for my determination with my findings thereon for reasons to follow: POINTS FINDINGS 01. Whether the prosecution has proved that Not proved. the accused on 15.3.2013 around 2.11 a.m. in his residential house when the victim girl Sanjana aged 10 years was slept in the bed room, he went there and slept by her side and moved hand over her body with intent to outrage her modesty or knowing it to be likely that he would thereby outrage her modesty? 02. Whether the prosecution has proved that Not proved. on aforesaid date, time and place, when the victim girl Sanjana aged 10 years was slept in the bed room, he committed sexual assault on her by moving hand over her body with sexual intent? 03. What order? Accused is acquitted. REASONS AS TO POINT NOS.1 TO 3:­ 7] The prosecution examined mother of prosecutrix, Seema Raj (P.W.1). She deposed that there was dispute in the family. Special Case No. 161/2014 (Judgment) Presented on : 18/08/2014 Registered on : 18/08/2014 Decided on : 25/05/2016 Duration :1­year,9­Months,7­days. IN THE COURT OF THE SPECIAL JUDGE(P.O.C.S.O.Act), THANE. (Presided over by Ms.U.M.Nandeshwar, District Judge­1 & Addl. Sessions Judge, Thane) SPECIAL CASE No. 161 of 2014 Exhibit No.26. The State of Maharashtra Through Rabale MIDC Police Station Thane, District – Thane. ... Prosecution VERSUS Sudhir Bahadursing Sonar Age 27 years, Residence –Mahatma Phule Nagar, Behind Vitawa Petrol pump, R.No.607, Ganpati pada, Dist.Thane. ... Accused Offence punishable under section 354 of Indian Penal Code and under section 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Appearance ­ Spl.P.P. Mrs. R.A. Navale, for the State. Advocate Mrs. Reena Korde for the Accused. Special Case No. 161/2014 (Judgment) JUDGMENT (Delivered on 25th May, 2016.) 1] The Accused stands prosecuted for the offence punishable under section 354 of Indian Penal Code and also under section 8 & 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act) for committing sexual assault on minor victim­girl aged about 16 years. 2] Shorn of verbiage, the indictment against the Accused are as under ­ [i] Informant / victim­girl (P.W.1) aged about 17 years is staying at Mahatma Phule Nagar, Ganpati Pada, Thane. Sudhir Sonar (Accused) is also staying in her neighbourhood and used to tried to talk with the victim­girl, but she used to avoid him. [ii] On 28/07/2014 around 01.00 p.m. when the victim­girl was with her friend Dhananjay Verma near Hanuman Temple, at that time, suddenly accused came there and by caught holding her hand, asked her to accompany with him and tried to pull her. The victim­girl gave jerk to his hand and while running pelted brick towards him. But it did not hit to him. Thereafter, the victim­girl narrated the incident to her mother and then on the same day, lodged report against the accused. Special Case No. 161/2014 (Judgment) 3] On her report F.I.R. was registered against the Accused vide C.R.No.I­214/2014 for the offence punishable under section 354 of I.P.C. and under section 8 & 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act by Police Hawaldar Bhoir. The investigation was carried out by P.S.I. Santosh Narayan Pimpale (P.W.3). The spot panchnama was drawn. Accused was arrested. The statements of witnesses were recorded. The birth certificate of the victim­girl was collected. Thereafter, investigation culminated into filing of charge­sheet in this Court being the Special designated court under P.O.C.S.O. Act. 4] My learned Predecessor erstwhile Special Judge Mr. V. V. Bambarde framed the charge (Exh.3) against the Accused for offence punishable under section 354 of Indian Penal Code and also under section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. The Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial (Exh.4). The Accused took defence of total denial. 5] In response to application under section 294 of Cr.P.C. the defence has admitted spot panchnama [Exh.17] and arrest form of accused [Exh.18]. 6] In order to prove guilt of Accused Prosecution has examined following witnesses ­ Special Case No. 161/2014 (Judgment) P.W.1 Informant / victim­girl Exh.12 P.W.2 Sunita Ramchandra Vishwakarma Exh.15 (mother of victim­girl) P.W.3 P.S.I. Santosh Narayan Pimpale Exh.20 (Investigating officer) 7] The prosecution proved and relied on the report / F.I.R. (Exh.13) and school leaving certificate of the victim­girl (Exh.21). 8] The prosecution closed its side of evidence by filing Pursis at Exhibit­22. The statement of accused under Section 313(b) of Cr.P.C. was recorded. Accused neither examined himself nor examined any witness in his defence. 9] Heard learned Spl.P.P. Mrs. R. A. Navale for State and the learned Advocate Mrs. Reena Korde for Accused. 10] On consideration of argument advanced on behalf of both the sides and on perusal of the oral & documentary evidence on record, following points arise for my determination, which are answered with the findings thereon, as under :­ Sr. Points Findings No. 1] Does the prosecution prove that on 28/07/2014 around 13.00 hours near the house of informant near the temple Special Case No. 161/2014 (Judgment) of Lord Shankar and Lord Hanuman, ..No. behind Vitava petrol pump, Ganpati Pada, Navi Mumbai accused used criminal force against her holding her left hand with intent to outrage her modesty and he thereby committed an offence punishable under section 354 of Indian Penal Code ? 2] Does the prosecution prove that during same period accused committed sexual assault on the minor girl in above manner and thereby committed an ...No. offence defined in section 7 and punishable under section 8 of the P.O.C.S.O. Act? 3] What order ? Accused is acquitted. REASONS As to Point No.1 & 2 : 11] Both the points are taken up together for discussion, to avoid the repetition, as evidence about the same in common and inter­connected. 12] As the Accused is facing charge under section 354 of I.P.C. it is incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that accused by using criminal force with intent to outrage modesty or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby outraged her modesty touched her inappropriately. So also as Special Case No. 161/2014 (Judgment) the Accused is facing charge under section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, therefore, it is further incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that the Accused with sexual intent touched the vagina, penis, anus, breast of a child or make the child touched vagina, penis, anus, breast of such person or any other person or does any other act with sexual intent which involves physical contact without penetration and by his such act committed sexual assault as defined in section 7 of the P.O.C.SO. Act. Age of victim­girl : 13] As the Accused is facing charge under P.O.C.S.O. Act, therefore, first of all it is incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that the victim­girl was child (minor) at the time of incident. The victim­girl stated her date of birth as 29/11/1996 and as per school record, her date of birth is 17/02/1998 and the alleged incident took place on 23/07/2014. If the date of birth of the victim­girl is considered as 29/11/1996 as per her own version, then on the date of incident which took place on 28/07/2014, the victim­girl was aged about 17 years and 8 months and her School Leaving Certificate is placed on record which is at Exh.21, wherein her date of birth is mentioned as 17/02/1998. However, the prosecution failed to prove the contents of Leaving Certificate through any concerned authority and there remains doubt about the actual date of birth of the victim­girl as she herself is stating her date of birth as 29/11/1996 which means she was Special Case No. 161/2014 (Judgment) at the verge of attaining majority. Therefore, in absence of any cogent proof, the date of birth mentioned in the Leaving Certificate cannot be believed. Thus, the prosecution failed to prove that at the time of incident, the victim­girl was minor aged about 17 years i.e. below the age of 18 years and she was a “child” as per definition given in Section 2(d) of P.O.C.S.O. Act. 14] As prosecution failed to prove that victim­girl was minor child at the time of incident, therefore, the charge under P.O.C.S.O. Act would not sustain. Further, therefore, even twin presumption given in section 29 and 30 of P.O.C.S.O. Act about offence u/sec. 3, 5, 7 & 9 of the P.O.C.S.O. Act and about culpable mental state of Accused would not come to the help of prosecution. Now it is required to see that whether prosecution proved charge of outraging modesty of victim­girl. 15] To prove the charge against the Accused the prosecution has examined the victim­girl (P.W.1) and her mother (P.W.2) who are the material witnesses. However, the evidence of the mother of victim­girl (P.W.2) Sunita Vishwakarma is of hearsay in nature and therefore, the only material evidence is of the victim­girl. The victim­girl (P.W.1) deposed that she know accused since her child­hood and he stays beyond 4­5 rooms from her house and he used to try to talk with her and tease her. The victim­girl further deposed Special Case No. 161/2014 (Judgment) that accused used to caught her hand and hold her and used to tease her on her school route. However, this is an exaggerated statement made by the victim­girl which is in the form of omission. Further the victim­girl deposed about the incident that on 28/07/2014 around 01.00 p.m. when she was talking with her friend Dhananjay Verma near Shankar and Hanuman temple, at that time, accused came there and by caught holding her hand asked her to accompany with him and teased her. She gave jerk to his hand and pelted piece of brick. But it did not hit to him, thereafter, she went to home and narrated the incident to her mother and then had been to police station and lodged report against accused which is at Exh.13. 16] However, it is material to note that there is single allegation against accused that on the date of incident, he caught hold her hand and asked her to accompany with him. From his act his intention that he caught hold her hand and asked to accompany him with sexual intention is not at all clear which is basic requirement of the offence under section 8 of POCSO Act and for offence punishable under section 354 of I.P.C. also the accused must have an intention to outrage the modesty of the victim­girl. But from bare perusal of the contents of F.I.R. and evidence of victim­girl no such intention of the accused reveal. Special Case No. 161/2014 (Judgment) 17] Further, it is pertinent to note that the victim­girl admitted in the cross­examination that on the day of incident, she met with her friend Dhananjay Verma as her mobile was not working. Further, even though suggestion that victim­girl herself snatched mobile of accused from the hand of accused and therefore, accused caught hold her hand, was denied by the victim­girl, but same appears to be the most probable defence. Even P.W.2 Sunita Vishwakarma, mother of victim­ girl also deposed that victim­girl had been near temple as her mobile was not working. Therefore, it prima­facie appears that only out of mis­understanding the F.I.R. came to be registered. 18] Further the place where alleged incident took place is public place and spot panchanama (Exh.17) evident that fact but no independent witness was examined including one Dhananjay in whose presence the alleged incident took place. Therefore, no intention of the accused to outrage the modesty is clear from the single alleged act of holding hand of the victim­girl and asking her to accompany with him is reflected. Thus, even the evidence of the victim­girl is taken as true, still the basic ingredients of the offence about having intention to commit such an act to outrage the modesty of the victim­girl does not appear. Thus, the prosecution failed to prove that accused caught hold the hand of victim­girl with an intention to outrage her modesty. Thus, evidence of the investigating officer (P.W.3) remains as formal in nature. Thus, there is no Special Case No. 161/2014 (Judgment) cogent and believable evidence on record to prove the charge against the accused about outraging modesty of victim­girl by holding her hand inappropriately. Hence, I answer point No.1 to 3 in negative. Therefore, the accused is entitled for acquittal. 19] In the result, I proceed to pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused Sudhir Bahadursing Sonar is hereby acquitted U/Sec. 235(1) of Cr.P.C. for the offence punishable U/Sec.354 of Indian Penal Code and U/s. 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] His bail bonds stand cancelled. 3] The Accused shall furnish P.R.Bond of the amount of ₹15,000/­ with one solvent surety in the like amount compliance of provision of Section 437­A of Cr.P.C. The judgment is dictated and pronounced in open Court. Date : 25/05/2016. (Ms. U. M. Nandeshwar), Thane Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act),Thane. District Judge ­1 and Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

On 29.05.2013, at about 08.00 p.m., she went for bringing vegetables at vegetable market, Bhiwandi. She came home crying with vegetables. On asking by Afsana Khatun, she told her that while she was coming home, at about 08.50 p.m., her neighbourer Sharif Raza, aged 22 years, by coming near her, pressed her chest and kissed her lips. Hence, she shouted. He ran away. By these allegations, Afsana Khatun Parvez Alam Ansari lodged her report Exh. 14, on which basis, offence vide C.R. no. 176/13 u/s. 354 of I.P.C. and u/s. 11, 12 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012, came to be registered. P.W.3 Arjun Ghodepatil has carried out investigation. He rushed to the spot and recorded spot panchanama in presence of panchas (Exh.15) and recorded statements of witnesses including victim. Medical certificate is obtained. On that basis, offence u/s. 376 of I.P.C. was added. Seized property was sent to C.A. After investigation, charge­sheet was submitted in the court. 3] My learned Predecessor framed the charge against the accused for the offences punishable under section 363, 366A, 376 of I.P.C. and u/s. 3 r/w. Sec. 4 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012, on 18/02/2015. Details of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular, to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. His defence is of total denial. 4] During trial, defence has admitted no documents. 5] To bring home the guilt of the accused for the charges leveled against him, the prosecution has examined as many as three witnesses i.e. 3 POCSO Case No. 49/2013. P.W. Name of witness Exh. Description No. No. 1] Afsana Khatun Parvez 7 Complainant. Alam Ansari 2] Parvez Alam Ahmed 8 Mother of victim. Husen Ansari 3] Arjun Keshav Ghodepatil 13 Investigating officer. 6] Accused did not enter into witness box. He has not examined defence witness. 7] Heard learned P.P. Smt. Phad for the State and learned counsel Shri. Vinod Gupta for the accused. Following points arise for my determination, which are being answered for the reasons given herein­ below. POINTS FINDINGS 1] Whether prosecution proved that on No. 09.05.2013 at 7.00 p.m. and on 17.05.2013, accused kidnapped the minor daughter of complainant namely Hajra Khatun @ Rani aged 12 years from lawful guardianship of complainant ? 2] Whether prosecution proved that on the No. above date, time and place, accused induced the victim minor girl to go from her house or to do any act with intent that the said minor girl may be, or knowing that it is likely that she will be forced or seduced to illicit intercourse with accused ? 3] Whether prosecution proved that on No. 4 POCSO Case No. 49/2013. 17.05.2013, accused took the said minor girl to one Lodge at Ulhasnagar and there, he committed rape on the above named girl by doing forcible sexual intercourse with her against her wish ? 4] Whether prosecution proved that on the No. above date, time and place, accused committed penetrative sexual assault on the above named minor girl ? 5] What order ? As per final order. REASONS POINT NOS. 1 TO 4 8] Parvez Alam Ahmad Husen Ansari deposed in his evidence that in the year 2013, his daughter / victim was studying in 4 th standard. Victim was born in the year 1999. On 29.05.13, he was told by victim that she was kidnapped and raped by accused Sharif Raza. 9] P.W.1 is mother of victim who has stated before the court that on 29.05.13 at 8.00 p.m., victim was present in the house. 10] Both P.W.1 Afsana and P.W.2 Parvez Alam have not supported to the prosecution story. Nothing has been extracted from their evidence after seeking permission to put leading questions. 11] P.W.1 in cross­examination of Ld. P.P., deposed in her evidence that accused is her neighbourer. At present, her daughter is in Children Home, Bhoisar. She has good relations with accused and his family. 12] From the cross­examination of P.W.2 Parvez, it can be 5 POCSO Case No. 49/2013. gathered that his statement was recorded on 03.06.13. 13] P.W.3 Arjun Ghodepatil has deposed as per his investigation. Nothing has been extracted from his cross­examination. 14] Medical officer is not examined by the prosecution. However, if medical report is perused, it can be gathered that hymen of the victim was found torn. No physical injuries were found on vagina of victim. No birth certificate of victim is placed on record. Xerox of her school­leaving certificate article A is placed on record. Head­master is not examined. P.W.2 Parvez Alam had stated that the victim was born in the year 1999. The incident was taken place in the year 2015. However, birth of victim is not proved by the prosecution. Besides, prosecution has not examined the victim though sufficient chance was given to the prosecution. Consequently, it can be held that prosecution failed to prove the alleged offence beyond doubt. I therefore, answer all the points, accordingly. ORDER 1] Accused Sharif Hashim Raza, is hereby, acquitted under sec. 235(1) of the Criminal Procedure Code, of the offences punishable u/s. 363, 366A, 376 of I.P.C. and u/s. 3 r/w. Sec. 4 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] Accused Sharif Hashim Raza, be enlarged on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ with surety of like amount. --1-- ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN CRIMINAL BAIL APPLICATION No.1800/2017 The applicant Vaibhav Vishnu Basvat has applied for bail under section 439 of Cr. P.C. in C.R.No.I­42/2017 registered in Vikramgad police station for the offence under section 376(2), 506 of Indian Penal Code and section 4, 6 of POCSO Act. 2. It is contended that the applicant is innocent and has not committed any offence. The offence is not punishable with death or imprisonment for life. The informant was consenting party for the sexual relation. The informant is 17 years old. She is major enough. She had love affair with the accused and she has voluntarily consented with the sexual intercourse, therefore, offence under section 376 is not prima facie made out. There is delay of six months in lodging the FIR, therefore, it is prayed that the applicant may be released on bail. 3. Investigating Officer gave say at Exh.4. It is contended that the victim is 17 years old. She is of Adiwasi community. The applicant has promise to marry her and committed sexual intercourse with her repeatedly and therefore, she has became pregnant from the accused. Therefore, it is submitted that if the accused is released on bail he is likely to tamper the prosecution witnesses. 4. Ld. Counsel on behalf of the applicant relied upon decision in case of Akshay Chandrakant Mahadalkar V/s. The State of Maharashtra and another in Bail Application No.898/2017 decided on 13thJuly 2017. In that case offence --2-- was under section 376(2), 376(I), (n), 354, 509, 506 and 500 of IPC and section 4, 8 and 12 of POCSO Act. The victim was 16 years and 3 months old having love affair with the applicant. The applicant/accused was willing to marry the victim girl after she attains the age of majority. An affidavit of her parents and of victim was tendered before the court and expressed that they are desire to get marry. In that case Honourable High Court granted bail to the applicant on certain conditions. 5. Likewise in this case it is submitted that the present applicant is ready to marry with prosecutrix and accordingly the applicant has tendered the affidavit of his parents in the court. In that it is expressed that they are ready to perform marriage of the prosecutrix and applicant, after prosecutrix attain the age of majority. 6. I heard Ld. A.P.P. She submitted that, if the applicant is ready to perform marriage with the prosecutrix, then she has no objection to release the applicant on bail. 7. Considering the present facts and circumstances of this case and observations made in above reported case I am of the view that the facts in both the cases are similar. There is love affair between prosecutrix and the present applicant. The applicant is 19 years old and the prosecutrix is 17 years old. The prosecutrix has became pregnant from the applicant. There is delay of six months in lodging the FIR. It appears that if the applicant refuse to marry wit the prosecutrix she lodge FIR. So there are certain mitigating circumstances to release --3-- the applicant on bail. Hence, I proceed to pass following order. :ORDER: 1. Application for bail is allowed. 2. The applicant Vaibhav Vishnu Basvat be released on P.B. and S.B. of Rs.25,000/­ (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand Only) with one or two local solvent sureties in like amount. 3. The applicant shall not pressurize, threaten, tamper the prosecutrix and prosecution witnesses. 4. The applicant shall not leave the jurisdiction of the court without prior permission of the court. 5. The applicant shall attend the concerned police station once in a month till further order. 6. If any condition is breached his bail will be cancelled. Thane. ( S.C. Khalipe ) Date : 06/09/2017. Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

.. 1 .. bail no.1818/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exhibit 1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 1818/2015 This application is filed by applicant Akshay Sikhbir Walmiki for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no.I-403/2015 registered at Vartaknagar police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 363, 376 of I.P.C. and section 4 and 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant induced his minor sister-in-law by giving false assurance of marriage and kidnapped her from lawful guardianship of the complainant and then had sexual intercourse with her. It is further contended and argued that no such incident of kidnapping has happened and the applicant is falsely implicated. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co-operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that the minor victim girl is sister-in-law (sister of wife) of the accused and it is contended that the accused enticed her by giving false promise of marriage and then kidnapped her and then had sexual intercourse with her though knowing that the girl was minor at the relevant time. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the .. 2 .. bail no.1818/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) applicant threatening the victim girl and other prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 363, 376 of I.P.C. and section 4, 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act with the allegation that the accused kidnapped and committed rape on his own minor sister-in-law (sister of his wife) who is stated to be 15 years old, from the perusal of complaint itself it appears that the allegations are that the accused had enticed the girl on false assurance of marriage etc. and apparently it is a case of consent. But then, though the consent of minor is immaterial, the aspect as to whether the girl is minor and whether there was enticement by the accused by giving false assurance of marriage, would be the question to be decided on merits. Even nothing is stated to be recovered from the applicant/accused. Then, the investigation in the matter must have almost completed by this time and the accused is seen to be in jail since 29.06.2015. 4] It is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if .. 3 .. bail no.1818/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 5] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 6] Then, it has also to be mentioned that looking the allegations against the accused the investigation in the matter may have almost completed but the charge-sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge-sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 7] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order - ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Akshay Sikhbir Walmiki is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/- [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions - The applicant/accused shall attend the concerned police station on every Monday between 10.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon .. 4 .. bail no.1818/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) till filing of the charge sheet and shall co-operate in investigation. He shall not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and the prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this Court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 02.09.2015 (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Additional Session Judge-1, Thane.

Thereafter, accused Bablu had left the said premises. 3] It is further case of prosecution that Gudiya aged about 17 years has left the house and went along with accused Bablu. After three days, father of Bablu Yadav i.e. namely Ramcharan Yadav had informed to informant that his sister Gudiya is present in their house at Ulhasnagar. He was also requested to take back her sister. Accordingly, she was taken back. However, Gudiya was talking with accused on mobile. On 13.03.14, accused kidnapped her and carried her to U.P. Victim was referred for her medical examination. Doctor had examined her and issued medical certificate (Exh.20). Accused was also referred for her medical examination. I framed the charge against the accused for the offences punishable under section 376, 363, 366, 366­A of I.P.C. r/w. Sec. 3 punishable u/s. 4 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, on 27/07/2017. Details of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular, to which he pleaded not guilty and 3 Spl. C. No. 163/2014. claimed to be tried. His defence is of total denial. 6] During trial, defence has admitted certain documents on record, i.e. arrest panchanama of accused (Exh.14), spot panchanama (Exh.15), panchanama of seizure of clothes of victim girl Gudiya (Exh.16), panchanama of seizure of clothes of accused (Exh.17), letter to C.A. Vishvakarma 3] Gudiya Kisan Yadav 13 Victim girl. 8] Accused did not enter into witness box. He has not examined defence witness. 9] Heard learned A.P.P. Smt. Talhar for the State and learned counsel Smt. Ashlesha Tambe for the accused. Following points arise for my determination, which are being answered for the reasons given herein­ below. POINTS FINDINGS 1] Whether prosecution proved that on No. 13.03.14 at about 07.00 p.m., in 4 Spl. C. No. 163/2014. between complainant's house to Kalyan Phata naka, Dist. Thane, accused had committed rape i.e. penetrative sexual assault on minor sister of complainant after kidnapping her ? 2] Whether prosecution proved that on the No. above date, time and place, accused had kidnapped by giving enticement of performing marriage to minor sister of complainant, from the lawful guardianship of complainant Sunil Ahir ? 3] Whether prosecution proved that on the No. above date, time and place, accused had kidnapped minor sister of complainant from the lawful guardianship of complainant Sunil Ahir, in order that she may be forced or seduced to illicit intercourse ? 4] Whether prosecution proved that on the No. above date, time and place, accused had induced minor sister of complainant by giving enticement of performing marriage with her, to go out with you from lawful guardianship of complainant, with intent that she may be or knowing that it is likely that she will be forced or seduced to illicit intercourse with you ? 5] What order ? As per final order. REASONS POINT NOS. 1 TO 4 10] It is not in dispute that complainant in his complaint has stated 5 Spl. C. No. 163/2014. the age of victim as 17 years. As per admission card, S.S.C. examination, October, 2013, date of birth of victim was recorded as 01.05.96. It means, in the month of December, 2013, victim was more than 16 years of her age. Till 13.03.14, rather 18.03.14, Sunil Ahir has not lodged his report for the first incident. 11] Undoubtedly, on the day of incident, victim Gudiya was in the custody of her brother P.W.1 Sunil Ahir. Without his consent and from his lawful guardianship, she was taken by the accused along with him and also got married with her. 12] It has come in the evidence of P.W.1 Sunil Kisan Ahir, complainant that Gudiya is his sister. Now, she is aged about 19 years. He knew Bablu Yadav since last two years. He was residing in Ulhasnagar. In the month of December, as usual, he had been to his work. He came to know that his sister Gudiya was missing. They had searched for her, but she was not found. After three days, Ramcharan Yadav had ringed them and informed that Gudiya was present in their house and he requested them to take Gudiya back. Then, he along with his friend Rajesh went to Ramcharan Yadav and he had brought her to his house. On enquiry, nothing was stated by Gudiya. 13] It has further come in his evidence that on 13.03.14, his sister Gudiya again went to the house of accused. On 18.03.14, he lodged his report against the accused (Exh. 11). 14] It has come in the evidence of P.W.3 Gudiya Kisan Yadav victim that she was born on 01.05.1996. In the year 2013, she was studying in 10th standard. In the year 2013, they were residing in Bharat Apartment. Accused Bablu Yadav was residing in same building on fourth floor. They were in love. She went to the house of accused. Her brother 6 Spl. C. No. 163/2014. had taken her back. On 13.03.14, she went along with accused to Pratapgad, U.P. On 01.05.14, she married with accused. Thereafter, they started residing jointly. Police had taken them to police station. Doctor had examined her and taken required samples. Her statement was recorded by police on 24.05.14 and 28.05.14. It did not happen that accused had kidnapped her and he had committed rape on her. She married to accused. She is cohabiting with him. Now, she is pregnant for seven months from the accused. 15] P.W.3 Gudiya has not supported to the prosecution story on material point. It is to be noted here that victim got married with the accused and now, she is happily cohabiting with him. P.W.1 Sunil Ahir deposed in his evidence that his sister Gudiya is cohabiting with the accused happily and he has no grievance against accused. So also, he has no concern with Gudiya. 16] P.W.3 in her cross­examination conducted by accused, deposed that she herself had joined the company of accused with her own accord and she has no grievance against accused. 17] P.W.3 Gudiya was suggested by Ld. A.P.P. in his cross­ examination that accused had kidnapped her, and raped her. But, she has denied both these material suggestions. From the evidence of P.W.3, it can be gathered that she married to accused and happily cohabiting with him and at present, she is pregnant for seven months from the accused. 18] Prosecution had proved the seizure panchanama of clothes of victim and accused, too. Not only that, prosecution proved the spot panchanama. So also, prosecution has proved that the accused was able to do sexual intercourse. From the medical examination of victim, it can be gathered that hymen was found ruptured and old torn at 1, 3, 7 and 9 'O' 7 Spl. C. No. 163/2014. clock. There is evidence of penetrative vaginal intercourse. 19] However, on the date of incident, victim was aged about 17 years. She herself went to the house of accused. She has not made any hue and cry till her journey up to Utter­Pradesh. She herself has submitted before the court. She got married with him. She is pregnant for about seven months from the accused. Victim was knowing the consequences of her own act. Therefore, it cannot be said that accused from lawful guardianship of the victim, has kidnapped the victim and raped her. Therefore, it can safely be said that prosecution has failed to prove the alleged offence against the accused beyond all reasonable doubts. In the result, I proceed to pass the following order. Victim at relevant time was aged about only 10 years. Her age is not seriously denied by the accused. 13] Alleged incident is taken place at the house of accused i.e. at Simran Baby Sitting. During relevant night, wife of accused and one other child were also present in the house. The entire prosecution story is based on sole testimony of victim. Sole testimony of the victim can be relied upon for conviction if such evidence is reliable, trustworthy. No corroboration is required in that circumstances. 14] It has come in the examination­in­chief of P.W.2 minor victim girl that­ Her old name was Bhakti Sureshkumar Sankpal. Suhas is her mother. She was studying in Saint Fransis High­ school, Bhainder (E). Her mother Smt. Suhas Khare was working with Saint George Hospital, Mumbai. Victim was born on 28.04.2003. In the year 2013, she was studying in 5th standard. When her mother used to go to her job, she used to keep her with one baby­ sitting. She knew accused Rohit @ Lohit. He runs his baby­sitting where victim was kept by her mother. Victim only resided two days in the said baby­sitting. 15] It has further come in her examination­in­chief that­ On 14.05.13, at 6.00 p.m., she along with her mother had been to Bhainder railway station. Accused had been there to take victim. Then, she along with him 7 POCSO Case. No. 50/2013. went to his baby­sitting. Her mother left for her duty. She was frightened and slept facing towards wall. He had done such act for twice. Due to that, she could not sleep. Thereafter, accused called his wife on bed and she slept between victim and accused. 16] It has further come in her examination­in­chief that­ On next day at about 10.30 to 10.45 a.m., on the message of her mother, she was carried by accused to Bhainder railway station. Her mother came there. Then, she along with her mother proceeded to return back to her house by auto­rickshaw. During travel, she disclosed her intention with her mother that she would not go to the said baby­sitting. After reaching to the house, she had disclosed the entire incident to her mother. On 14.05.13, she was on night duty from 6.00 p.m. At Bhainder station on 14.05.13, accused met her and took victim to Simran baby­sitting. 19] She further deposed in her examination­in­chief that­ On 15.05.13, at about 10.00 to 10.30 a.m., she returned back from her duty at Bhainder railway station. Accused had left victim with her at railway station. Thereafter, she along with victim were proceeded to return back to their house. No. 50/2013. had directed the bathroom; due to fear, she could not disclose the incident to anyone. 20] It has further come in her examination­in­chief that­ On receiving the facts, she also became frightened. She called her cousin brother Shekhar Khade from Mira Road. She narrated the incident to him. Then, she along with him and victim went to Bhainder police station and lodged her report (Exh. 11). Message received by her on her mobile is at article A. She had also given copy of I­card of victim and her birth­ certificate and copy of gazette to police. They are at article B, C, D. She had shown the spot to the police. 21] She deposed in her cross­examination that­ Shivdas Khare is her father. She had married to Sureshkumar Sankpal on 24.05.2002 at Malgaon, Tal. Miraj, Dist. Sangli. After marriage, she went to the house of her husband at Malgaon. Since 2005, she is serving as nurse. It was decided between her and Simran baby­sitting that they would take care of her daughter for 12 hours. It was decided to pay the advance. She had no personal knowledge about the incident. 22] From the evidence on record, it can be gathered that during night of 14­15 May, 2013 at the house of accused, the incident had taken place. While returning back to the house, victim had narrated her mother that since hereinafter, she would not go to Simran Baby Sitting. After arrival of them to their house, victim had narrated the incident to her mother and thereafter, they rushed to police station and informant had lodged her report at 15.45 hours on 15.05.13. Victim has no reason to depose falsely against the accused. 23] Victim was joined with Simran Baby Sitting belonging to 10 POCSO Case. No. 50/2013. accused, since from 13.05.13. Immediately on next day i.e. during the night of 14.05.13 and 15.05.13, the incident had taken place. Within two days, there was no question to demand extra charges for extra time. From the cross­examination of P.W.1 Smt. Suhas, it can be gathered that it was decided between Simran Baby Sitting and informant that they would take care of victim for 12 hours and it was also decided to pay the advance. Suggestions to P.W.1 were given by the accused that on account of extra amount, there was quarrel between them and she had threatened the accused that she would lodge report against him. But, both these suggestions were denied by her. 24] Reena is wife of accused. Merely because the incident was not disclosed with Reena, the evidence of P.W.2 cannot be doubted. P.W.2 in her cross­examination deposed that she had stated before the police in her statement that wife of accused along with small child were slept on the ground. But, the same statement cannot find place in her statement. The said omission does not go to the root of the matter. 25] The evidence of P.W.2 victim is found reliable and trustworthy. Her evidence is not impeached by the accused. She is a child. On the date of incident, she was aged only about 10 years. Accused had not discharged his burden u/s. 29 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 26] Prosecution beyond doubt, proved the case against the accused punishable u/s. 354 of I.P.C. and u/s. 8, 9(m) of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. Hence, I answer the points, accordingly. 27] As the accused found guilty for the offence punishable u/s. 354 and u/s. 8, 9(m) of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, it 11 POCSO Case. No. 50/2013. is my imperative duty to hear him on the point of sentence. Hence, the judgment is paused here. Thane, (A.S. Bhaisare) Date­ 23.05.2018. Special Judge (POCSO) and Additional Sessions Judge­2, Thane. 28] Heard accused and his counsel on the point of sentence. They submitted that accused is the only earning member of his family. He is having female child. It will affect on the mind of minor child. Lastly, they prayed for minimum punishment. 29] Heard Ld. Special P.P. Smt. Phad. She submitted that recently Supreme Court has taken serious view in the cases of sexual assault on children. Offence committed by accused is against society, though he is having female child and a wife. Lastly, she prayed for maximum punishment and heavy compensation. 30] Section 42 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 provides for alternate punishment as under­ “Where an act or omission constitutes an offence punishable under this Act and also under sections 166­ A, 354­A, 354­B, 354­C, 354­D, 370, 370­A, 375, 376, 376­A, 376­C, 376­D, 376­E or section 509 of the Indian Penal Code, then, notwithstanding anything contained in any law for the time being in force, the offender found guilty of such offence shall be liable to punishment under this Act or under the Indian Penal Code as provides for punishment which is greater in degree.” 31] Undoubtedly, offence u/s. 354 of I.P.C. and u/s. 8 and 9(m) are proved by the prosecution. Having considered the nature of offence proved 12 POCSO Case. No. 50/2013. and in view of section 42 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, no separate punishment needs to be awarded u/s. 354 of I.P.C. and u/s. 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, when accused may sentenced for offences in aggravated form like section 9(m) of POCSO Act. 32] Accused runs Simran Baby Sitting. With good faith and trust upon the accused, people used to keep their child under the care and protection of accused who runs Simran Baby Sitting. But, he has taken disadvantage of the same and committed heinous offence against child below 12 years of age who was temporarily under his custody. Therefore, in my view, accused needs to be sentenced as per section 9 punishable under section 10 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. As such, I proceed to pass the following order. ORDER 1] Accused Rohit @ Lohit Mohanraj Arven, is hereby, convicted under sec. 235(2) of the Criminal Procedure Code, of the offences punishable u/s. 9 (m) punishable u/s. 10 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act and he is sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for five years and pay fine of Rs.1000/­(Rupees One Thousand Only) i/d. of payment of fine, he shall further suffer rigorous imprisonment for three months. 2] Accused Rohit @ Lohit Mohanraj Arven, is 13 POCSO Case. No. 50/2013. hereby, convicted under sec. 235(2) of the Criminal Procedure Code, of the offences punishable u/s. 354 of I.P.C. and u/s. 7 punishable u/s. 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. However, no separate sentence is passed. 3] Accused was in jail since 15.05.2013 till 21.06.2013. So, he is entitled for set­off for the said period. 4] Right to appeal before higher court is explained to the accused. 5] Copy of this Judgment and order be given to the accused free of cost. 6] Muddemal, if any, being worthless, be destroyed after appeal period is over. Thane, (A.S. Bhaisare) Date­ 23.05.2018. Special Judge (POCSO) and Additional Sessions Judge­2, Thane.

Act). It was contended and argued that the applicants are arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicants in furtherance of common intention with co-accused compelled victim girl to do prostitution and earned money from said business. It is further contended and argued that the applicants have not committed sexual assault on the girl and that they have been falsely implicated in this crime merely suspicion and with ulterior motive. It is contended by the applicants that co-accused has been ordered to be released on bail and therefore on the ground of parity the applicant/accused is also entitled to be released on bail. It is further submitted that charge-sheet is also submitted before Court and therefore, there is no need to further detain the accused in jail. It is further submitted that the applicants are permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, they will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will attend the Court regularly for the purpose of trial and .. 2 .. Bail No. 1830/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1.) therefore the applicants are entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply as per Exhibit 4 and it was contended and argued that the applicant in furtherance of common intention with co-accused had compelled the victim girl to indulge in prostitution and had earned money by doing said profession and also committed sexual assault on the girl. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicants/accused are released on bail, there is possibility of the applicants threatening and pressurizing the victim girl and prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if released on bail, the applicant may abscond and will not be available for trial and may again indulge in such activity. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/ accused are of serious nature under section 366A, 370, 376 read with section 34 of I.P.C. and section 5, 9 of I.T.P.A. and also under section 3, 4, 16 of P.O.C.S.O. Act with the allegation that the accused had forced victim girl to do prostitution and also committed sexual assault on her, it is the contention of the applicant/accused that the applicants are not F.I.R.-named accused and their names are revealed in supplementary statement of the girl recorded after submission of charge-sheet against other accused. It is also material that the present applicant not stated to have been identified by the girl in test identification parade and that they are falsely implicated in the crime with ulterior motive. In such circumstance whether the .. 3 .. Bail No. 1830/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1.) allegations against the accused are true or not would be the question to be decided on merits. 4] Then, it is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicants would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicants tampering with prosecution evidence if they are released on bail. In that respect it is contended by the applicants that they are permanent residents of the address given and they will not abscond and that they are ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 5] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicants/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 6] Then, it has also to be mentioned that though charge- sheet is stated to have been submitted in the matter, it would take time to take up the case for hearing and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. .. 4 .. Sanap, it can be gathered that he had not verified the age of victim as she had stated her age as 20 years. To snap photo on mobile, facility of camera needs to be there. He had not seized any phone or I­phone from victim or the accused. From the mobile, location can be detected. He had not traced out the location of all mobile numbers supplied by victim. He had also not found any obscene video clip. P.W.4 Shri. Sanjay Satav is a formal witness who after investigation, submitted his charge­sheet. 11 POCSO Case No. 53/2013. 27] P.W.4 deposed in his cross­examination that he had not collected any document to show that accused along with victim had been to any Lodge. He had not found any independent witness who may state that the accused had kidnapped the victim. No smart phone is seized. Even if data is deleted, the same can be restored from Meta Data. He had also not seized the suspected clip. 28] P.W.2 victim in her evidence had stated her date of birth as 23.09.93. She also deposed in her evidence that she had love affair since 2007. Report is lodged in the year 2013. The last incident seems to be taken place in the month of March to July, 2012. Mother of victim has not stated the age of victim. No birth certificate or school­leaving certificate of victim is placed on record. Victim was not sent for her ossification test as to determine her age. Undoubtedly, victim had delivered a baby. Unfortunately, the said newly born child died within two days. Merely because victim delivered a child, it cannot be said that on the day of incident, victim was minor and she had not attended the age of her discretion and was not knowing consequences of her own acts. On the contrary, P.W.2 in her cross­examination, deposed that she used to go alone with the accused at her own accord. She had not lodged previously her report about forcible sexual intercourse. She was knowing the consequences of her own act. She has not grievance against the accused. 29] As per evidence of P.W.2 victim, first incident i.e. physical relations of the accused with victim were taken place at the house of her girl friend. The said girl friend is not examination by prosecution to establish that at relevant time, victim had been to the house of her girl friend and accused was already present in her house. Her girl friend for some work, left the house. This evidence is also not stated by victim in her 12 POCSO Case No. 53/2013. evidence. 30] Victim was having a simple phone without android facilities. Mobiles were not seized. No alleged clip is seized. Therefore, the version of victim creates doubt whether really accused had threatened the victim that he would defame the victim on the basis of that obscene clip. 31] From the evidence of P.W.2 victim, it seems that even after her engagement, she had kept relations with the accused. After marriage, she had left the house of her husband Sanjay Choudhary and thereafter, she again remarried with one Srikant Lahu Patil. 32] Sarpanch of Group Gram­Panchayat, Surai Sarang, Tal. Bhiwandi, has informed to the police that in the meeting dated 10.03.11, accused agreed to marry with victim. However, now he has declined to marry with her (Exh.45). As per article A dated 10 th Thursday at about 2.00 p.m., victim herself had given in writing that the accused entered into her house and told in presence of her mother and her aunt that he would marry with victim. This writing is also not helpful to the prosecution. 33] Having considered the facts and circumstances of the matter, evidence on record and discussed reasons, it can be gathered that due to deep love affair between accused and victim, sexual relations between them were established with the consent of each­other and there was no forcible sexual intercourse. It can be further inferred that victim was well acquainted with her own act and consequences of it. Even after her engagement of marriage, she had kept her sexual relations with the accused. Not only that, after marriage, she left the house of her husband. As accused declined to marry with her, she went to the house of her sister and thereafter, she married to another person. All this material goes in 13 POCSO Case No. 53/2013. favour of accused to say that he has not established the sexual relations without consent of victim and without her wish. She has not made any hue or cry at any point of time. She has also not disclosed about the same to anybody. There is no material on record to show that accused along with one other had kidnapped the victim from the house of her husband. I therefore, answer to all the points, accordingly. In the result, I proceed to pass the following order. ORDER 1] Accused Rupesh Likarya Patil is hereby, acquitted under sec. 235(1) of the Criminal Procedure Code, of the offences punishable u/s. 366­A, 376 of I.P.C. and sec. 4, 8, 12 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] Accused Rupesh Likarya Patil be enlarged on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ with surety of like amount. The effect of this bail order will remain in force for the period of six months from today, as per section 437­(A) of Cr.P.C. 3] Muddemal, if any, being worthless, be destroyed after appeal period is over. Thane, (A.S. Bhaisare) Date­ 21.04.2018. Additional Sessions Judge­2 and Special Judge (POCSO Act), Thane.
