Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­004970­2016 Special Case (POCSO) No. 190/16 Received on : 22.07.2016 Registered on : 22.07.2016 Decided on : 11.10.2018 Duration : 3Ys. 1M. 27 Ds. IN THE COURT OF D.J.­1 & ADDL. SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE. (Presided over by Hemant M. Patwardhan) Special Case (POCSO) No. 190/16 Exh.No. State of Maharashtra, (Jawhar Police station) ..Complainant V/s. Soma Janu Sambare Age : 60 years, Occu. : Agriculture R/at.: Hiradpada, Tal. Jawhar, Dist. Palghar ..Accused Appearance:­ APP Mr. Londhe for the State. Advocate Mr. Khillare for accused JUDGMENT (Delivered on this 11th day of October 2018) Accused Soma Janu Sambare was facing trial under sections 376, 506 of Indian Penal Code read with Sec. 4, 8 and 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 on following facts. 1 OF 9 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­004970­2016 Special Case (POCSO) No. 190/16 1] That prior to two months till 25.4.2016 at residence and field of complainant at Mauje Hiradpada, Tal. Jawhar, within jurisdiction of Jawhar Police station, committed rape on victim and while committing rape has also threatened the complainant with dire consequences if victim caused alarm about commission of the offence by the accused and as the victim was minor within the meaning of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 accused has also allegedly committed penetrative sexual assault and sexual harassment of the victim minor girl. Thus, on complaint lodged, an offence punishable under aforesaid sections came to be registered. On completion of investigation he was charge­sheeted. 2] My learned Predecessor was pleased to frame charge below Exh.4 and has certified that the contents of said charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. On the basis of said charge prosecution has examined witnesses as well. However, at the time of preparing for Judgment in the matter some discrepancies about name of accused is noticed. Hence, in order to remove that discrepancies in the name of the accused I consider it to be fit to alter charge accordingly. Accordingly, on 17.09.2018 charge was altered and name was corrected. Defence has filed pursis to proceed on same evidence even after charge was altered to correct discrepancy in the name of accused. Hence, the evidence already recorded was considered for said purpose. Accused initially when the charge was framed by my learned Predecessor and when it was 2 OF 9 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­004970­2016 Special Case (POCSO) No. 190/16 altered by him has denied having committed any offence as stated in the charge and claim to be tried. His defence was of total denial. On the basis of aforesaid facts prosecution was then proceeded to examine victim, panch witness, parents to the victim and I.O. in the same sequences as PW1 and 5 respectively. After their depositions statement of accused was recorded as per his say wherein he has again reiterated defence of his false implication in the matter. After having recorded evidence of the aforesaid witnesses arguments of rival advocates were heard. 3] Learned P.P. has categorically pointed out that victim has supported the prosecution and in that sense has supported her own version against accused and there is nothing on record to disbelieve her version. According to learned P.P. if presumption under section 29 of POCSO is made applicable in the matter then even sole testimony of the victim is sufficient to prove the guilt of the accused. He has therefore, requested to convict accused on the basis of said version. He has fairly admitted that parents of the victim did not support the prosecution. 4] Per contra, as per the defence the bare words of the victim without there being any specific dates, time and place and without corroboration of the said version cannot be accepted as proof of offence alleged against accused. Reference has been then made about the admissions of the parents about having filed present 3 OF 9 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­004970­2016 Special Case (POCSO) No. 190/16 matter out of the dispute on the agricultural land and according to said admission there was sufficient reason for the witnesses to implicate accused in the matter. He has therefore requested the court to acquit the accused from all the said allegations. 5] After having heard the rival advocates, following points arise for my consideration and I record my findings against each of them for the reasons noted below:­ S.N. Points Findings 1] Does the prosecution prove that accused since last two months till ..In the negative. 25.4.2016 at residence and field of complainant at Mauje Hiradpada, Tal. Jawhar, within jurisdiction of Jawhar Police station, committed rape on complainant victim age 13 years and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 376 of IPC? 2] Does the prosecution prove that accused during aforesaid period ..In the negative. and at above mentioned place, committed criminal intimidation by threatening the complainant­victim to cause her death with intent to cause alarm to her and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 506 of IPC? 3] Does the prosecution prove that accused during aforesaid period ..In the negative. and at above mentioned place, committed penetrative sexual assault on complainant i.e. minor child age 13 years and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 4 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act? 4] Does the prosecution prove that accused during aforesaid period ..In the negative. and at above mentioned place, committed sexual assault on informant i.e. minor victim girl, age 13 years with sexual intent and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act? 5] Does the prosecution prove that accused during aforesaid period ..In the negative. and at above mentioned place, committed sexual harassment upon informant i.e. minor victim girl, age 13 years with sexual intent and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act? 6] What order ? Accused is acquitted as per final order. 4 OF 9 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­004970­2016 Special Case (POCSO) No. 190/16 REASONS As to point nos. 1 to 6 :­ 6] All these points are interlinked with each other and are considered at once. In the instant case prosecution has alleged that two months prior to 25.04.2016 accused has committed frequent rape on victim and as at the particular time victim was minor within the meaning of POCSO prosecution was launched not only under section 376 but also under section 8 and 12 of POCSO. According to allegations accused has committed criminal intimidation by threatening the victim at the time of committing rape therefore, prosecution was required to prove said allegations by consistent and reliable evidence. No doubt, sole testimony of victim if found to be reliable is sufficient to accept the prosecution and to punish the accused as per the provisions of law. In the instant case as well as per fair admission of the learned prosecutor except victim material witnesses like that of the parents of the victim are turned hostile. Though panch witness in whose presence the seizure was made has supported prosecution during examination­in­chief but during cross examination he has admitted facts that he has signed on already written panchanama and on the say of Naik Saheb. He was also not able to tell colour of the clothes seized and has further admitted that he did not talk anybody else than Mr. Naik. Hence, due to his admission in cross­examination it is difficult to accept that any such seizure did occur in his presence. Therefore, entire case was based on 5 OF 9 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­004970­2016 Special Case (POCSO) No. 190/16 sole testimony of the victim. Court therefore has to consider whether the said testimony is reliable, sufficient to hold the accused guilty of the offence. On perusal of the deposition of the victim it appears that victim has made allegations of accused having committed forcible rape while she had been to river for taking bath and has also alleged that after committing the said act accused has threatened her with dire consequences. She has also alleged that whenever she used to be alone at home accused used to come to her house and used to commit rape and used to threatened that if she makes any alarm about his act accused will kill her. According to her allegation due to the act of the accused of commission of rape caused bleeding injuries on her private part and also caused trouble while passing urine. Hence, she was forced to disclose the fact to her father and after her disclosure complaint was lodged on 26.04.2016. The victim was cross­examined at length and it was categorically brought on record that she is unable to state date of incident, she was not even knowing full name of the accused, that like her there are other women and girls who used to take bath in the river and she is accompanied by her friends while either proceeding towards the river or towards her house, that her parents were with her while she had been to police station for lodging the complaint and her father himself has narrated the incident to police and police recorded it. On the basis of said admissions learned defence advocate has requested the court to discard her sole 6 OF 9 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­004970­2016 Special Case (POCSO) No. 190/16 testimony. Admittedly learned Prosecutor has requested to consider sole testimony of the victim but if we consider very vague allegations of the victim in the examination­in­chief then it is difficult to accept the submissions of the learned public Prosecutor. On perusal of record it is apparent that my learned Predecessor has recorded substantive evidence of the victim in a routine manner without even making efforts of concluding whether the victim really knows about the importance of oath or even without making an attempt to know whether she is able to understand the rational questions put forth by the court or is able to give rational answer it in proper way. Therefore, if that particular fact is considered the court has to look for corroboration of the said deposition. Admittedly, parents did not corroborate her version and thus, the only source of obtaining corroboration was the medical evidence produced by the prosecution. 7] On perusal of medical certificate it is apparent that defence has admitted it wherein medical officer has opined that possibility of sexual assault cannot be ruled out but medical officer himself has reserved her official opinion till receipt of Chemical Analyzer report. On further perusal of the record it is apparent that apparent indication of having undergone sexual assault were not recorded by the medical officer in Sub­Column A to Z in Column No.6 of MLC report dealing with local examination of genitals, anus and oral cavity. Therefore, once the said indications are not 7 OF 9 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­004970­2016 Special Case (POCSO) No. 190/16 recorded the court has again to look for the corroboration on the basis of chemical analyzer's report. Hence, same are considered minutely. 8] On perusal of the said reports it is apparent that an important analysis conducted by the expert were in the form of finding DNA in the samples like that of Cervical Swab etc. wherein that test is reported negative so far as male DNA present in the said samples. Therefore, it is apparent from the report of Chemical Analyzer that though the medical officer has opined that possibility of sexual harassment is not ruled out does not become conclusive. Having regards to the said inconclusive evidence before the court it is difficult to accept said fact that accused has really committed sexual assault on the victim as claim by her. Various admissions referred to above were sufficient to raise doubt about occurrence of the incident or accused being having a chance of committing such offence without being seen by any other person accompanying the victim. Further, said admissions if considered with vague allegations put forth by the victim during examination­in­chief itself then are certainly sufficient to disbelieve the version of the prosecution's evidence. Having regards to the said fact said lacunas are certainly sufficient to discard the evidence of the victim. Her sole testimony therefore cannot be considered to be reliable, cogent and consistent to held accused guilty of any of the said charge. Having regards to the said fact I am not inclined to accept the said sole testimony and 8 OF 9 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­004970­2016 Special Case (POCSO) No. 190/16 on that basis to hold the accused guilty of the offence. Having observed so, I do not hesitate to record my findings against point no.1 to 5 in negative and proceed to pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused Soma Janu Bambare is acquitted from the offence punishable under Sec. 376, 506 of Indian Penal Code read with Sec. 4, 8, and 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] His bail bond shall accordingly stands cancelled. 3] Muddemal property i.e clothes being worthless, be destroyed after appeal period. 4] Accused is directed to execute P.R. and S.B. of Rs.10,000/­ with a solvent surety in like amount under amended provisions of Section 437­A of Code of Criminal Procedure and the bond so executed shall remain in force for period of six months from the date of its execution. 5] Proceeding accordingly shall stand closed. Thane (Hemant M.Patwardhan) Date: 11.10.2018 D.J.­1 & Additional Sessions Judge, Thane. 9 OF 9

--1-- ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN REGULAR BAIL APPLICATION No.1850/2017 The applicant Santosh Panchami Prasad @ Santosh Panchamiprasad Jaiswal has applied for bail under section 439 of Cr. P.C. in C.R.No.I­309/2016 registered in Bhayander police station for the offence under section 363, 376 of Indian Penal Code and 4, 8 and 12 of POCSO Act. 2. It is contended that the applicant is very young and he is totally innocent. He has been falsely implicated. In fact the applicant has married with the victim under the provision of Hindu Marriage Act. The victim has became marriageable age. She is attend 18 years. Investigation is almost completed. Further custody of the accused is no more required for any purpose of investigation. The applicant has produced Declaration­cum­affidavit of marriage and intimation letter to Bhayander police station by victim and accused not to take legal action against them and marriage registration certificate. 3. Investigating Officer has given his say at Exh.4. It is contended that the victim and accused are residing n the same area, therefore, after release he is likely to tamper prosecution witnesses. 4. I heard Ld. Counsel on behalf of accused. He relied on decision in case of Sunil Mahadev Patil V/s. The State of Maharashtra 2016 ALL MR (Cri) 1712. In that case also the victim was 15 years old and the offence under sections 376, 363, 366A of Indian Penal Code and section 3,4,5 and 6 of POCSO Act. It was found that the victim had love affair with the accused. So it was held in para­10 that, “there are --2-- instances of rape where a man and a woman both are in love with each other and get involved into sexual relationship due to either physical or psychological need and in such type of rape, there is no violence which exists in other types of rape.” It was held that as per facts of the case the prosecutrix had love affair with the accused and they eloped and went to temple and they garlanded with each other and according to them they performed marriage and after that they residing together. So it was held that there was many mitigating fact, bail may be granted to the applicant. 5. The Counsel for the applicant has produced Adhar card of the victim. As per Adhar card age of the victim was 17 years and when the marriage was registered the victim was 18 years old. It appears that after the alleged incident the victim resides with the accused for 7 to 8 months and they resides as husband and wife. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case the court is of the view that further custody of the applicant no more require. It will not justifiable to keep the applicant in jail without trial. There are so many mitigating factors to release the applicant on bail. The documents which are produced on record such as marriage certificate declaration affidavit, intimation given to the Bhayander police station which shows that the applicant and victim had love affair and they were eloped from their house and they have performed marriage. So these are the mitigating factors to release the applicant on bail. Hence, I proceed to pass following order. --3-- :ORDER: 1. Application is allowed 2. Applicant be released on P.B. and S.B. of Rs.20,000/­ (Rupees Twenty Thousand Only) with one or two local solvent surety on the like amount. 3. The applicant shall not tamper the victim and prosecution witnesses by any means. 4. Applicants shall not leave the jurisdiction of the court without prior permission of the court. 5. Applicants shall attend the concerned police station for investigation purpose as and when necessary. 6. They shall attend the trial without fail. 7. If any condition is breached the bail will be cancelled. Thane. ( S.C. Khalipe ) Date : 03/08/2017. Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

S.C.C No. 165/2014 (Judgment) :JUDGMENT: (Delivered on 25th day of September, 2017) 1. Accused is facing trial for the offence punishable u/sec. 376, 323,504, 506 of Indian Penal Code and Sec.3, 4 & 5 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2. In short case of prosecution is as follows:­ On 15.6.14 at about 10.30 p.m in the house of informant at House No.538 Room of Shrimanta Kannada Wadi, Behind Ekta Vidhyalaya, Bhimanagar, Rabale Navi Mumbai committed rape on victim girl aged about 13 years and 6 months who is step daughter of accused and threatened her to kill if she disclosed the incidence to anybody and thereby committed offence U/sec.376, 323, 504, 506 of Indian Penal Code and offence U/Sec.3, 4, 5 and 6 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 3. The FIR was lodged against accused by victim. On the basis of said FIR Crime No. I­94/2014 came to be registered. After completion of all the formalities of investigation the present chargesheet came to be filed. 4. The Charge was framed by my predecessor vide Ex.4 against the accused for the offence punishable u/sec. 376, 323,504, 506 of Indian Penal Code and Sec.3, 4 & 5 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. .. 3 .. S.C.C No. 165/2014 (Judgment) 5. In support of its case the prosecution has examined following witnesses:­ PW No. Ex.No. Prosecution Witness 1 34 Victim (Name of the victim is not disclosed to protect her identity.) 2 35 Bhimabai ­ Mother of Victim. (The full name of PW.1 Victim and PW.2 Bhimabai­ Mother of victim are not written in the judgment to protect the identity of victim). The prosecution closed their evidence by filing purshis at Ex.36. 6. In view of the oral evidence adduced on record on behalf of prosecution it is transpired that, there is no incriminating circumstances and evidence available on record against the accused for his statement prescribed U/sec.313 (1) (b) of the Cr.P.C., to afford an opportunity to explain the incriminating circumstances on record. Therefore there was no any alternative but to dispense with the statement of accused as envisaged U/sec.313 of the Cr.P.C in this case. Hence the requisite order came to be passed to that effect. 7. After considering the case of prosecution following points arise for my determination. I recorded my findings against each of them for the reasons stated below:­ S.No. Points Findings 1. Whether the prosecution proves that accused committed rape on victim No. girl aged 13 years and 6 months? .. 4 .. S.C.C No. 165/2014 (Judgment) 2. Whether the prosecution proves that accused voluntarily caused hurt to No. victim girl? 3. Whether the prosecution proves that accused intentionally insulted the victim girl by abusing and thereby No. gave provocation to her intending or knowing it to be likely that such provocation will cause victim girl to break public peace? 4. Whether the prosecution proves that accused committed criminal intimidation by threatening the victim girl with injury to her person with No. intention to cause alarm to her or to cause hurt to do an act which she is legally bound to do or to cause hurt to omit to do an act which she is legally bound to do? 5. Whether the prosecution proves that accused committed penetrative sexual No. assault on the minor girl? 6. What order? Accused is acquitted. :REASONS: AS TO POINT NO. 1 TO 5 :­ 8. To prove the case, prosecution has examined PW.1 victim at Ex.34. She deposed that, in June 2014 she used to reside at Rabale. Accused Rajesh Gangaya Naik is her step father. She identified accused. She further deposed that she did not remember exact date of incidence. On that day she was talking with her neighbor Sachin with whom she wanted to marry. .. 5 .. S.C.C No. 165/2014 (Judgment) Her step father saw them and therefore he beat her. Therefore she filed the complaint to police against him. She do not know the contents in FIR. She declared hostile by the APP. Nothing revealed in her cross­examination for the support of prosecution case. 9. PW.2 Bhimabai­ Mother of victim deposed that Victim is her daughter. She did not remember her birth date. Accused Rajesh Naik is her second husband. She did not remember date of incidence. On that date when they returned from their work victim told her that she complained to police because accused beaten her and refused to perform her marriage with Sachin. She declared hostile by the APP. Nothing revealed in her cross­ examination for the support of prosecution case. 10. Considering the hostility of PW.1 victim and PW.2 Bhimabai the Ld. APP wisely closed the evidence of prosecution by filing purshis at Ex.36, to save the previous time of court. 11. There is nothing incriminating to be put to the accused for explanation u/sec.313 of Cr.P.C. Therefore after hearing Ld.APP and Advocate for accused, I am inclined to dispense with the statement u/sec.313 of Cr.P.C. Accordingly I passed order below Ex.4 and dispensed with the statement. 12. So considering all these facts and circumstances discussed above, there is nothing which shows that accused committed any offence as alleged u/sec. 376, 323,504, 506 of Indian Penal Code and Sec.3, 4 & 5 of The Protection of Children .. 6 .. S.C.C No. 165/2014 (Judgment) from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, therefore the accused is entitled for order of acquittal. Hence, I answer Point No.1 to 5 are in negative. AS TO POINT NO.6:­ 13. Considering the reasoning and finding as to point No.1 to 5 in answer to point no.6, I proceed to pass following order:­ ORDER 1] Accused Rajesh Gangayya Naik is hereby acquitted u/sec.232 of Cr. P. C. of the offence punishable under 376, 323,504, 506 of Indian Penal Code and Sec.3, 4 & 5 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and he be set at liberty. 2] The accused shall execute P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ and furnish surety in like amount, in compliance of Sec.437­A of Cr.P.C. 3] Muddemal property being worthless be destroyed as per Sec.452 of Cr.P.C. after expiration of appeal period. The accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 6] At the trial, to bring home the guilt of the accused, the prosecution examined in all 4 witnesses, viz., Sujit Shyamnarayan Yadav (P.W.1) (the complainant and father of the victim), the victim (P.W.2), Sayli Jayendrakumar Chavan (P.W.3) A.P.I., who recorded the statement of the victim, Santosh Suresh Kulkarni (P.W.4), Investigating Officer. 7] After the prosecution closed it's evidence the statement of the accused under section 313 of Cr.P.C. came to be recorded. The defence of the accused during deposition and while recording statement U/s. 313 Cr.P.C. is of bare denial. 8] In the light of the charge against the accused, evidence led by the prosecution, statement of accused under section 313 of Cr.P.C., the defence taken by the accused and the submissions across the bar, the 4 following points arise for my determination. [ii] Whether the prosecution further proves that during the given period and the said place accused committed sexual assault on the victim­girl in the aforesaid manner and thereby committed an offence punishable U/s. 8 and 10 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act (P.O.C.S.O. Act) ? …...No [iii] What order ? As per final order. :REASONS: AS TO POINT NO. 1 & 2 :­ 9] The prosecution has examined 4 witnesses in order to prove the guilt of the accused. 10] It would be relevant to proceed with the appreciation of evidence in respect of the charges levelled against the accused. To this end, it would be necessary to briefly summarize the salient features of evidence of the prosecution witnesses. It would be appropriate to have recourse to the testimony of the informant Sujit Shyamnarayan Yadav (P.W.1) who unfolded the prosecution. He has deposed that he resides in Subhash Nagar since his childhood. He has four daughters Anjali (14 5 years), Ruchi (10 years), Sonam (8 years) and Khusboo (3 years) in the year 2015. He is working in a grocery shop in Bandra. 11] On 22/03/2015 he returned home at 08.30 p.m. At that time, his daughter Sonam informed him that in the afternoon at about 03.00 p.m. when she was playing on the road, one uncle came to her and asked her name, held her hand and started caressing her head. When she informed her name, he pulled her towards him and started caressing her chest. She pushed him aside and ran away. He told her that if she sees this person again, she should inform him. He informed about this incident to his brother Manoj Yadav, who resides above his house. 12] On 28/03/2015, at 09.30 p.m. he had sent Sonam to purchase match­box. She came running home and informed him that the person who had molested her on the previous date is standing on Subhash Nagar Naka. Therefore, he, Sonam and Manoj went to the Subhash Nagar Naka to speak to him. His daughter showed him this person, who was present there. When he asked him why did he molest his daughter, he started running. He and Manoj caught him and brought him to Vartaknagar police station. In the police station, he informed his name as Jagdish Rai. He then lodged the F.I.R. at the police station. It is at Exh. 18. 13] It has come in the evidence of the victim (P.W.2) that in 2015 she used to go to Shivaji Vidhyalay, Subhash Nagar, Thane. At that time she was studying in 5th Standard. She was 10 years old at that time. Her date of birth is 07/06/2005. Her school timing was 7.30 to 12.30. The school was at a distance of 5 minutes from her house. She used to walk to the school. 14] She has further deposed that on 22/03/2015 she had gone 6 with her friends to play on the road in her area i.e., Subhas Nagar. This uncle was present there. He asked her her name and where she stays. When she told him, he pulled her hand towards him and caressed her chest and head. She got scared and she pushed his hand away and ran home. She did not inform her mother as she got scared. At night, her father came and she informed him. Her father told her to inform him whenever she sees him next. 15] She has further deposed that after about 5 to 6 days, when she went to purchase the match­box to Subhash Nagar Naka at 09.30 p.m., she saw this person. She ran home and informed her father that she saw this person again. Her father and Manoj uncle accompanied her to the Naka. When her father started talking to him, he started running. Her father and uncle caught him and took him to the police station. The police made enquiries with her after about 3 days. 16] It has come in the evidence of Sayli Jayendrakumar Chavan (P.W.3), P.S.I., that he was posted at Vartaknagar police station from October 2013 till June 2016. As a part of my job, he used to record statements of victims including women and children. She had recorded the statement of victim Sonam Sujit Yadav on 05/04/2015. She recorded statement of victim Sonam Sujit Yadav. It is at Exh. 28. When she recorded Sonam's statement, her father was present there and he signed it. 17] It has come in the evidence of Santosh Suresh Kulkarni (P.W.4) that he has been posted as P.S.I., Vartaknagar since 2015. On 04/04/2015 he was handed over the investigation of C.R. No. 195/2015. On 28/03/2015 PSI Mahajan had recorded the F.I.R. and arrested the accused on the same day. The F.I.R. and other papers were handed over to him. He perused the F.I.R. and recorded statements of witnesses. He also 7 collected the birth certificate of the victim (Exh. 31). Her date of birth is 07/06/2005. He completed the investigation and submitted the charge­ sheet in the Court. From the investigation, he concluded that the accused held the victim's hands and touched her breast in an inappropriate manner. 18] It has come in the cross­examination of P.W.1 that Sonam did not give him th description of the molester. He has denied that on 28/03/2015 he did not send his daughter to buy match­box. He registered the offence at about 09.00 to 09.30 p.m. He did not find anything suspicious on seeing this person. He has denied that his daughter showed him the wrong person. He has admitted that he did not file the F.I.R. on 22/03/2015. The police did not ask him to describe the molester in the F.I.R. He has denied that the accused did not molest his daughter Sonam. 19] It has come in the cross­examination of P.W.2 that she has denied that her school and house are opposite each other. She plays in the school playground. She has admitted that on the date of the incident also, she was playing in the school playground. That day there was only one friend. Her name is Aanchal. She is her classmate. She knows her full name Aanchal Babulal Yadav. She goes to the school alone. Nobody comes to pick her up from school. School is at a distance of 5 minutes walk from her house. It was a holiday on that day. She has admitted that the area near the school is very well inhabited and there are shops there. That day she was playing after the school was over. They play only when there is school. That day Aanchal was with her. The accused came after Aanchal had left. She did not go to the police station on the day the accused was arrested. She does not know who all saw him that day. Aanchal did not see him. She alone saw him that day. Her statement was read over and explained to her. She could recognize him (the accused) 8 because he had misbehaved with her. 20] In the cross examination she has deposed that she did not give the description of the accused to her parents on the date of the incident. She did not give his description to the police when she went there after 3 to 4 days. Police had asked her whether accused is the same person and she said 'yes'. She had become frightened after the said incident. She had gone for one or two days after the incident to play. After that, she did not go to play. She has denied that after the incident she used to not step out of the house. After the said incident, her parents used to take care to not allow her to step out of the house after evening. She has admitted that they used to tell her to return home by evening and not go out at night. 21] In the cross examination she has deposed that she does not know where her father works. Her father returns from work at 9.00 to 9.30 p.m. everyday. She has admitted that when her father is away, her mother looks after her. She has denied that her parents do not allow them to go out after sunset. They allow them for 1 minute. She plays in her friend's house. Her mother knows in which friend's house she plays. She used to go even to her Badi Mammy's house. She used to go for two minutes to the shop. She has denied that her father never sent her to buy the match­box. She did not see the accused on that day and did not recognize him. She has denied that she identified the wrong person in the police station. 22] It has come in the cross­examination of P.W.3 that Sonam did not give the physical description of the accused. She has admitted that Sonam did not inform the exact place at which she saw the accused for the first time. She has not informed what the accused was doing at the said place. She did not inform as to who nabbed the accused first. She has 9 denied that the said statement was not made by Sonam. 23] It has come in the cross­examination of P.W.4 that there was delay in lodging the F.I.R. because the accused was being traced. The place where the incident took place is densely populated. The said incident took place in the afternoon. The victim showed the accused at night. The victim's father lodged the F.I.R. No independent witness has been examined. The accused is a senior citizen aged 62 years. 24] At the conclusion of the trial, I have heard Ld. DGP Mrs. S.E. Phad for the State and Ld. Advocate Mr. Patankar for the accused. 25] Ld. D.G.P. Mrs. Phad has submitted that the evidence of P.W.1 is well­corroborated by the evidence of P.W.2. There was no reason for P.W.2 to wrongly identify and implicate the accused. There was no reason for P.W.1 also to falsely implicate the accused. The presumption under Section 30 of the POCSO Act has not been rebutted by the accused. There is no reason for the complainant and the victim to falsely depose against the accused. The prosecution has proved its case beyond reasonable doubt and hence, the accused is liable to be convicted. 26] Per contra, Ld. Advocate for the accused has submitted that apart from the bare word of the victim, there is nothing to indicate that the present accused in fact sexually molested her. There is no other eye witness to the incident and it could be a case of mistaken identity. 27] I have perused the entire material on record. A perusal of the evidence indicates that the testimony of P.W.1 is well­corroborated by the evidence of P.W.2. There was no reason for P.W.2 to wrongly identify and 10 implicate the accused. There was no reason for P.W.1 also to falsely implicate the accused. There is no reason for the complainant and the victim to falsely depose against the accused. However, from the material on record and the evidence it is seen that the accused had tried to molest and sexually assault the victim as defined u/s. 354 of IPC and 8 and 10 of the POCSO Act. In view thereof, the accused is liable to be convicted only for attempt to commit the offences under Section 354 of IPC and section 8 of the POCSO Act. The accused will therefore be liable to be convicted as per Section 18 of the POCSO Act and one half of the longest term of imprisonment provided for the offences stated above. It is seen from the record that the accused had engaged an advocate through legal aid. The learned advocate for the accused has submitted that the accused could not even apply for bail due to his poverty. In view thereof, no fine is being imposed on the accused. It is seen from the record that the accused came to be arrested on 28/03/2015 and since then he is in judicial custody. In view of the foregoing discussion, the following sentence would meet the ends of justice : ORDER 1] The accused Jagdish Ramlakhan Rai is hereby convicted vide Sec. 235(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure Code for attempting to commit the offence punishable Under Sec. 354 of the Indian Penal Code and Sec. 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] The accused is sentenced to undergo 18 months simple imprisonment for attempting to commit the above offences. 3] All the sentences shall run concurrently. 4] Set off be given to the accused as per Section 428 of the Code 11 of Criminal Procedure for the period he has already undergone in jail. 5] The accused shall execute a fresh P.R. and S.B. of Rs.15,000/­ to appear before the higher court as and when such court issues notice in respect of any appeal or petition filed against this judgment, in terms of Section 437­A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 6] Copy of the judgment be provided to the accused free of cost as per provision U/s. 363 of Cr.P.C. Thane. (Mridula V. K. Bhatia) Date : 07/02/2017. District Judge­08 & Special Judge (POCSO Act), Thane.

So also as the Accused is facing charge under section 4 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, therefore, it is further incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that the Accused committed “penetrative sexual assault” on the victim­girl either by penetrating his penis, to any extent, into vagina, mouth, urethra or anus of child (victim­girl) or makes the child (victim­girl) to do so with him or with any other person or does any such other act as defined in section 3 of the P.O.C.S.O. Act. Age of victim­girl : 13] First of all as the accused is facing charge U/s. 363 of I.P.C,. and under section 4 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, it is incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that the victim­girl was minor at the time of incident. It is the case of prosecution that .. 8 .. Special Case No.54/2013 (Judgment) victim­girl aged 13­14 years was kidnapped and subjected to penetrative sexual assault by the accused. The informant Ramesh Rajbansi (P.W.1) as well as the victim­girl (P.W.3) failed to state the exact date of birth of the victim­girl. The victim­girl only stated that her birth­date as 7 th July, but unable to state the year and so also informant Ramesh (P.W.1) failed to state her date of birth. Ramesh (P.W.1) only stated that in the year 2013 his daughter was aged about 14 years and victim­girl (P.W.3) deposed that at the time of incident she was aged about 13 years. Except that there is no other documentary evidence placed on record to support the date of birth of the victim­girl and thus, there is absolutely no evidence on record about the date of birth of victim­girl (P.W.3). Even though the investigating officer (P.W.5) deposed that letter was issued to St. Catherin Home, Andheri where victim­girl was studying for obtaining bonafide certificate of victim­girl, however, only xerox copy of bonafide certificate was collected and same was not even proved by the prosecution. Thus, the prosecution failed to proved that at the time of incident, the victim­girl was minor aged about 14 years i.e. below the age of 18 years and she was a “child” as per definition given in Section 2(d) of P.O.C.S.O. Act. 14] As prosecution failed to prove that victim­girl was minor, therefore, the charge under section of P.O.C.S.O. would .. 9 .. Special Case No.54/2013 (Judgment) and the charge of kidnapping will not sustain. 15] Now remains the question, whether accused committed sexual assault / rape on the victim­girl against her wish and without her consent. In this respect the most material evidence is of the victim­girl (P.W.3). However, as the victim­girl is most material witness therefore taking recourse of provisions of section 311 of Cr.P.C., the victim­girl was summoned and examined by the court. During the evidence of the victim­girl a very shocking and surprising fact came before the Court, is that the informant Ramesh (P.W.1) is step­father of the victim­girl and he used to sexually abused the victim­girl. In such background, now the evidence of the victim­girl requires thorough scrutiny. 16] Victim­girl (P.W.3) deposed that at the time of incident she was aged about 13 years and studying in second standard in Sr. Cathrin school Andheri. Special Case No.54/2013 (Judgment) he questioned her and scolded her and warned her not to keep the friendship with the accused. Thereafter, once informant (P.W.1) seen victim­girl and accused together and then he took victim­girl to home and beaten her. She did not like the reaction of her father. Therefore, she left home and went to the house of Sabir (Accused) at Vashi and told him that her father had beaten her and stayed at his house. There accused had kept sexual relations with her and committed sexual intercourse with her. She further deposed that thereafter, accused took her to the house of his acquaintance and there they both stayed together for two months and during that period also accused had sexual intercourse with her. Thus, this part of the evidence of the victim­girl clearly shows that accused never enticed her away and neither forced her to leave her house. Further the physical relationship with the accused also appears to be with the consent of the victim­girl. In fact, the victim­girl in very clear term deposed that she was staying with accused by her own wish and will. She further deposed that on 07/10/2013 when she returned to her father to meet him, her father called police and then police took her in custody. It is further significant to note that since then the victim­girl (P.W.3) is staying in the Observation Home and did not return to the informant. The evidence of victim­girl (P.W.3) further discern that her mother expired in the year 2012 and prior to that her biological father was expired. It also .. 11 .. Special Case No.54/2013 (Judgment) appears that after death of her mother she was sent to St. Catherin School which is a boarding school. 17] The twist came in the matter during the cross­ examination of the victim­girl when she admits in her cross­ examination that while stating history before the medical officer, she stated that her father used to harass her and he used to physically harass her. On asking what physical harassment means, the victim­girl explained that her father i.e. informant (P.W.1) used to commit forcible sexual intercourse with her and used to administer some pills to her, because of which she used to have bleeding for 12 to 15 days and thus he physically abused her. Here it is worth to mention that even medical certificate (Exh.27) manifest the same history that victim­girl willingly left home due to harassment of her father and medical officer Dr. Rekha Anand (P.W.2) corroborates the version of victim­girl. Victim­girl also deposed that her father used to restrict her from talking to any other boy and used to lodge false complaints against them. 18] The conduct of the informant/step­father of the victim­girl is also required to be noted that the victim­girl was kept in the boarding school and even though she was find missing on 02/05/2013, the report about her missing and kidnapping came to be lodged on 06/06/2013 i.e. after the .. 12 .. Special Case No.54/2013 (Judgment) delay of more than one month. A fragile explanation given by the informant (P.W.1) that the victim­girl phone called him and informed that she will return home after 2 to 4 days, is not convincing, as if the informant had really concerned with the victim­girl, he should have immediately reported the matter to police and to take search of his daughter, however, no such efforts were made by the informant. Further, even in the F.I.R. the name of accused is mentioned as Sameer while the accused before the Court is Sabir Nisar Khan. 19] Although, prosecution examined one Arif Rafiq Mohd. Khan (P.W.4) who deposed that the accused and the victim­girl were stayed at his house for one and half month as husband and wife, but the evidence of this witness is very vague and did not inspire any confidence as there is no other corroborative evidence on record. Even the victim­girl (P.W.3) could not state the name of person in whose house she claimed to be stayed with accused for about two months. 20] The learned Spl.P.P. argued that through Dr. Rekha Anand (P.W.2) the prosecution has proved that the minor girl was raped. Dr. Anand (P.W.2) deposed that on 10/07/2014, she examined 14 years' girl and her hymen was torn having old tears and admit two fingers easily and had given history of abortion. Even if the evidence of the medical .. 13 .. Special Case No.54/2013 (Judgment) officer Dr.Anand (P.W.2) is taken as it is, it would no way connect the accused with the crime, particularly in the background of allegations put forth by the victim­girl before the court on the oath that it was her step father i.e. informant (P.W.1) sexually abused her. Medical certificate of the victim­ girl which is at Exh.27 eloquent that in column of history which was given by victim­girl herself that she went with boy (Sabir Khan 22 years) by her own will to avoid harassment by her father. 21] The evidence of the informant Ramesh Rajbansi (P.W.1) is not believable in respect of the kidnapping of his daughter by the accused as he lodged report against the accused only on suspicious and he has never witnessed accused taking away the victim­girl. Therefore, there is absolutely no iota of evidence against accused. There is absolutely no evidence that the victim­girl was minor and therefore, the charge of the kidnapping and P.O.C.S.O. would not sustained and as far as the allegations of sexual assault by accused is concerned, the sexual intercourse appears to with the consent of victim­girl. Thus, there is no evidence to prove the charge against the accused. On the contrary in the present case, after recording the evidence of victim­girl (P.W.3) when it was revealed that she was subjected to sexual assault by her step­father/informant (P.W.1), she was facilitated to attend .. 14 .. Special Case No.54/2013 (Judgment) the police station and where she lodged report against the informant/ her step­father (P.W.1) and then the offence was registered against the present informant (P.W.1) for offence under section 376 of I.P.C. and Section 4 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. 22] It is cardinal principle of law that justice should not only be done but it must appear to have been done. Similarly, the investigation must not only be fair but it must appear to have been conducted in fair manner and said principles is reiterated by Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Common Cause vs. Union of India – 2015 (6) SCC 332. However, in the present case the investigation does not appear to be conducted fairly and the investigating officer without any explanation failed to record the statement of the victim­girl. Had the investigating officer (P.W.5) recorded the statement of the victim­girl fairly then definitely the fate of the accused might have been different and he might be out from the jail long back. The casual investigation eloquent from the fact that without recording statement of victim­girl sections of sexual assault were applied and the accused is booked under the stringent provisions of P.O.C.S.O. Act without collecting any authentic document in support of age of victim­girl. This observation is necessary in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in case of State of Gujrath vs. Kishanbhai (2014)5 S.C.C.108 = MANU/SC/0004/2014. .. 15 .. Special Case No.54/2013 (Judgment) 23] It is a case of very sorrow affair that the young boy of 22 years has to remain behind bar for about three years due to the false implication by the main culprit who is none else then the step­father of the victim­girl. Further, it is matter of record that accused even could not afford to engaged the lawyer to represent him and the matter was proceeded only after providing him legal aid. It is further painful that Accused was in jail since 2013 and as he could not afford to engage advocate to represent him, Advocate Mr. S.S. Shetty was appointed through legal­aid on 05/12/2015. However, as Adv. Shetty since his appointment never turned up in the court, this court on 30/01/2016, taking note of this fact passed speaking order and Adv. Yasmin Shaikh & Adv. Sunil Patanker were appointed to represent the accused at state's cost and thereafter only matter was proceeded further. 24] Thus, in the overall background of the case prosecution utterly failed to prove the charge against the accused mainly due to casual and unfair investigation. On the contrary, it came on record that it is a case of totally false implication at the behest of informant to save his own skin, therefore, accused is entitled for clean­chit and acquittal. Therefore, I answer point No. 1 to 3 in negative. .. 16 .. Special Case No.54/2013 (Judgment) 25] In the result, I proceed to pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused Sabir Nisar Khan is hereby acquitted U/Sec.235(1) of Cr.P.C. for the offence punishable U/Sec.363 and 376 of Indian Penal Code r/w. Sec.4 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] The accused is in jail. He shall be released forthwith if not required in any other case. 3] Muddemal deposited in the court vide M.E.No.63/2015 being worthless be disposed of after appeal period is over. 4] The Accused is directed to furnish P.R.Bond / bail bond of the amount of ₹15,000/­ with one solvent surety in the like amount in compliance of provision of section 437­A of Cr.P.C. Bail No.1888//2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exhibit 1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 1888/2015 This application is filed by applicant/accused Riteshkumar Chourasiya for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. I-18/2015 registered at Nayanagar police station (Thane Rural) on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 354, 363, 376 of I.P.C. and section 4 and 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act (hereinafter referred to as P.O.C.S.O. Act for short) It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant induced the minor daughter of the complainant and had kidnapped her and then committed sexual assault on her. It is further contended and argued that there was love affair between him and the girl and the girl of her own had come with him to Ajmer and accused had not kidnapped her. It is further contended and argued that the accused had surrendered before the learned Magistrate and at that time the girl was in custody of her parents who were against the love affair of accused and the girl and at the instance of parents of the girl he is falsely involved in this crime. It is further submitted that looking to the nature of allegation against the accused, there is no need of further custody of the applicant/accused. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply as per Exhibit 4 and it is contended and argued that that the accused and the girl were knowing each other since before the incident and it is further contended that taking disadvantage of such .. 2 .. Bail No.1888//2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) acquaintance and young age of the girl, the accused gave false assurance of marriage to the girl and induced and enticed her and under such false pretext, he had kidnapped her and had taken her to Ajmer and during her stay with the accused, he had committed sexual assault on her by using criminal force against her by inserting finger in her private part and pressing her breast. It is further submitted that in such circumstance, since the accused and girl are knowing each other, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the girl if released on bail and he may pressurize her and other prosecution witnesses also. It is also contended that if the applicant/accused is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 354, 363, 376 of I.P.C. and section 4, 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, the girl is stated to be aged 15 years 8 months and it is contended on behalf of applicant that there was love affair between the girl and accused and the girl had herself gone with the accused out of love for him and it is further contended and argued that since the parents of the girl were against their love affair, this false complaint is filed. In such circumstance the aspect as to whether the allegations against the accused are true or not, would be the question to be decided on merits. Even nothing is stated to be recovered from the applicant/accused. 4] Then, it is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. In that .. 3 .. Bail No.1888//2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 5] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 6] Then, it has also to be mentioned that the investigation is stated to be in progress and it will take time to complete the investigation and then to submit the charge-sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 7] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. Exh.20.. : JUDGMENT : (Delivered on this 24th day of April, 2018) The accused is prosecuted for the offence of sexually assaulting minor girl, outraging her modesty and threatening her. 2] The facts are as under : It is alleged by prosecution that, informant Radhika Ramesh Karekadan is residing at Koparkhairne, Navi Mumbai alongwith her three daughters. Her husband is serving at abroad. The victim is second number daughter of the informant. At the time of incident she was 17 years old. The accused and victim girl were studying in St. Mary School, Vashi Navi Mumbai. The accused was classmate of elder daughter of the informant. The accused used to harass the informant's victim daughter when he was in her school. It is further alleged by the prosecution that on 22.01.2016 at about 12.30 at noon the informant had gone to vegetable market at Koparkhairne. At that time accused had been there and hold the right hand of the victim girl. He said to the victim in vernacular “Tum Muze Bahot Achhi Lagti Ho, Mai Tumse Pyar Karta Hu”. When the victim girl tried to restrain him, the accused hold her near waist and kissed her on right cheek. The informant tried to rescue her daughter. J-Spl.Case POCSO - 181-16 - 354,506 8.doc . .....3/­ ..3.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 181/2016.. Exh.20.. Thereupon the accused pushed the informant and left the spot threatening the victim girl that he would look after her father and mother and whole family. The informant raised alarm. The people had gathered on the spot. It is further alleged by the prosecution that after the incident the informant and her daughter returned to their home. The informant did not dare to narrate the incident to her husband who had returned from abroad on leave. On next day the informant narrated the entire incident to her husband. Thereafter they went to Koparkhairne police station and lodged complaint against the accused. 3] After receiving complaint offence punishable u/s.354, 506 of the Indian Penal Code and section 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act came to be registered against the accused. After investigation, charge sheet came to be filed against the accused for said offences. 4] Charge is framed against the accused at Exh.05. Accused pleaded not guilty of offence and claimed to be tried. 5] Statement of accused u/s.313 of Code of Criminal Procedure is recorded at Exh.19. Exh.20.. 6] After going through the prosecution story, evidence on record and hearing arguments of both sides, following points arise for my determination. I record my findings thereon for reasons as stated below. POINTS FINDINGS 1] Does the prosecution prove that on 22.01.2016 at about 12.30 hours in the vegetable market at Sector­15, Koparkhairne, Navi Mumbai the accused hold the hand of victim girl, kissed her on her right cheek, expressed his love towards her and thereby sexually assaulted her ? …Not proved. 2] Does the prosecution further prove that on the same date, time and place the accused criminally intimidated the victim girl by threatening her ? …Not proved. 3] What order ? ..As per final order. : REASONS : As to the Point Nos.1 and 2 :­ 7] Both points are arising out of one and same incident, hence those are discussed together. To bring home the guilt of the accused the prosecution has examined informant Radhika Karekadan as PW1 at Exh.8. The complaint lodged by her is at Exh.9. The victim girl is examined as PW2 at Exh.13. The statement of victim recorded by Magistrate u/s.164 of the Code of Criminal J-Spl.Case POCSO - 181-16 - 354,506 8.doc . .....5/­ ..5.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 181/2016.. Exh.20.. The copy of the same is at Exh.15. 8] The informant in her deposition at Exh.8 narrated almost all facts alleged in complaint and mentioned earlier. To avoid repetition, those facts are not reproduced here. 9] Interestingly the victim girl in her deposition at Exh.13 denied the very allegations levelled against the accused by the prosecution and in the complaint. She specifically deposed that on 22.01.2016 she had gone to meet the accused alongwith her friend. At that time her mother and father had gone for check­up. As the accused had not met her she tried to contact him, but he did not attend her call. Therefore, she was roaming in the area of house of accused on her scooty. She had not gone to vegetable market alongwith her mother. The accused never misbehaved with her as alleged in the complaint. 10] Thus the very victim has not supported the prosecution. In cross examination by learned A.P.P. she denied the contents of her statement. On the contrary she admitted the contents of her statement recorded u/s.164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 1 Spl. C. No. 56/2013 (Judgment) Received on : 16/09/2013 Registered on : 16/09/2013 Decided on : 27/04/2017 Duration : Y­3, M­7, D­12 IN THE DISTRICT AND SESSIONS COURT, THANE AT ­ THANE. (Presided over by Ms. Mridula V. K. Bhatia, District Judge­08 & Special Judge (POCSO Act), Thane) SPECIAL CASE NO. 56/2013 Exhibit No. State of Maharashtra (Through Narpoli Police Station, Dist. Thane, State of Maharashtra) .... Prosecution. V/s. Shankar Kisan Tare, Age­ 21 yrs., R/at: Dhamangaon, Post­Wadpe, Tal.Bhiwandi, Dist.Thane. …. Accused. Appearance : Learned A. P. P.Shri.Kulkarni for the State. Learned Advocate Smt.Nafees Momin for the accused. ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ : JUDGMENT : (Delivered on 27th day of April, 2017) The accused has been prosecuted for the offences Under Sections 363,366(A) and 376 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) and Secs.4, 7 & 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (POCSO Act). 2 Spl. C. No. 56/2013 (Judgment) 2] The case of the prosecution is as follows : Complainant (P.W.2) Dinesh Shankar Gohil used to reside alongwith his wife, daughter­ Manisha, victim daughter and son Sudarshan since 20 years. He was serving in T.M.C. as labour. On 18/6/2013 at about 10.00 p.m. his wife and elder daughter Manisha were at home and he was not present in the house. At that time his victim daughter left the house without informing anybody. They searched for her with relatives and her friends, but she was not found. Therefore, they went to the police station , where they learnt that the accused Shankar Kisan Tare enticed away his victim daughter under the pretext of marriage, out of his custody. Therefore, he lodged F.I.R. against accused as he had enticed away his victim daughter. Thus, the informant lodged F.I.R. against the accused. 3] The police registered crime vide C.R.No. I­204/2013 against the accused for offences under Sections 363,366(A) and 376 of the Indian Penal Code and Secs.4,7 & 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. F.I.R./complaint was registered at the Police Station on 19/06/2013. 4] The supplementary statement of the complainant (P.W.2) was also recorded on 20/6/2013 in which he has stated that before lodging the complaint about the missing of his victim daughter, she informed his younger brother Manoj Gohil that she was with a boy namely Shankar Tare at Bhiwandi. Therefore, he lodged complaint about the same with Narpoli Police Station. Then Narpoli Police arrested the accused Shankar Tare and also taken victim in their custody, sent her for medical treatment. Thereafter, victim was given in the custody of the complainant (P.W.2) 3 Spl. C. No. 56/2013 (Judgment) Dinesh Gohil. Victim informed him that she was in love with accused Shankar Tare since one year. On 18/6/2013 when she was talking with accused Shankar, her uncle Manoj Gohil objected and scolded her. Therefore, she left the house and went with accused Shankar at his aunt's house at Padgha, there they had physical relations. 5] Charge (Exh.10) was framed by my predecessor against the accused for the offences punishable under sections 363,366(A) & 376 of the Indian Penal Code and Secs.4, 7 & 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. It was read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. The accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 6] At the trial, to bring home the guilt of the accused, the prosecution examined two witness viz. P.W.1 ­ victim (Exh.13) and the complainant P.W.2­ Dinesh Shankar Gohil (Exh.15). 7] As there is no incriminating evidence against the accused, his statement U/Sec.313 of Cr.P.C. is dispensed with. 8] In the light of the charge against the accused, evidence led by the prosecution and the submissions across the bar, the following points arise for my determination. I have recorded my findings against each of them for the reasons stated below :­ POINTS FINDINGS [1] Whether prosecution proves that on 18/6/2013 at No. about 22.00 hours at Sadicha Co.Op. Society, Khodiyar Ma Mandir, Shanti Niwas, Anjurphata, Charnipada, Bhiwadi, Dist.Thane, the accused kidnapped the informant Dinesh's daughter­victim out of his lawful guardianship without his consent and thereby committed an offence punishable U/Sec.363 of I.P.C. ? 4 Spl. C. No. 56/2013 (Judgment) [2] Whether the prosecution proves that on the same No. date, time and place the accused procured minor victim girl aged below 18 yrs. by inducing by any means to go with him with intent that she may be forced or seduced to illicit intercourse with him and thereby committed an offence punishable U/Sec. 366(A) of I.P.C. ? [3] Whether the prosecution proves that on the aforesaid date, time and place, the accused committed rape on the minor victim girl aged about 15 yrs. without her consent and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 376 of I.P.C. ? [4] Whether the prosecution proves that on the No. aforesaid date, time and place the accused committed sexual penetrative assault on the minor victim girl and thereby committed an offence of aggravated penetrative sexual assault punishable U/Sec.4 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 ? [5] Whether the prosecution proves that on the aforesaid date, time and place the accused committed sexual assault on the minor victim girl with sexual intent and thereby committed an offence punishable U/Secs. 7 & 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 ? [6] What order ? As per final order. :REASONS: AS TO POINT NO. 1 TO 6 :­ 9] The prosecution has examined two witnesses in order to prove the guilt of the accused. The learned Advocate for accused has admitted the arrest panchanama of the accused, seizure panchanama of clothes of accused, seizure panchanama of clothes of victim girl, medical certificate of victim girl, medical certificate of accused, C.A. reports. 5 Spl. C. No. 56/2013 (Judgment) 10] It would be relevant to proceed with the appreciation of evidence in respect of the charges leveled against the accused. To this end, it would be necessary to briefly summarize the salient features of evidence of the prosecution witnesses. 11] It has come in the evidence of the victim (P.W.1) that she had love affair with accused Shankar Tare and she got married with him on 20/1/2017. She disclosed her date of birth as 31/12/1998 and that she was major at the time of her marriage with the accused. She deposed that she was residing happily with the accused as husband and wife. As she was not supporting to the prosecution, she was declared hostile and cross­ examined by Ld.A.P.P. She denied the contents of her statement before the police. She has produced marriage certificate, affi davit and other documents (Exh.14). She has no complaint of any nature against the accused. 12] It has come in the evidence of the complainant P.W.2­ Dinesh Gohil that accused Shankar is his son­in­law and that his victim daughter Ravina got married with accused Shankar before 4 to 5 months. He was declared hostile by the prosecution. In his cross­exam. by Ld.A.P.P. he has only admitted his signature on his statements dt. 19/6/2013 & 20/6/2013 but denied its contents. 13] P.W.1 ­victim girl and complainant P.W.2­ Dinesh both deposed that they have no complaint of any nature against the accused, as the victim and accused were married and staying together happily. Cross­ examination of both witnesses has been declined by the defence. 6 Spl. C. No. 56/2013 (Judgment) 14] Ld. A.P.P. Mr.Kulkarni has submitted that appropriate orders be passed considering the evidence which has come on record. 15] Ld. Advocate for the accused has submitted that nothing incriminating has come in the evidence of P.W.1­victim and P.W.2­ complainant Dinesh against the accused. She has submitted that the victim and the accused are residing happily as husband and wife and that the accused therefore, deserves to be acquitted. 16] The evidence of P.W.1 (victim) does not disclose any offence against the accused. She has deposed that she was in love with accused Shankar, they got married on 20/1/2017 and she was major at the time of their marriage. They both are residing happily as husband and wife and she has no complaint against the accused. P.W.2 (complainant) has also deposed that the accused and his daughter P.W.1(victim) got married before 4 to 5 months and they are residing together happily as husband and wife. He has only admitted his signatures on his statements before the police, but denied its contents. 17] The burden of proving the guilt of the accused rests on the prosecution. The constitutional mandate of innocence prevails unless the prosecution succeeds in proving by satisfactory evidence the guilt beyond reasonable doubt of the accused which it has failed to do in this case. I therefore, answer points No.1 to 5 in the negative. In view of the foregoing discussion and in view of the peculiar facts and circumstances of the present case, the following order would meet the ends of justice. 7 Spl. C. No. 56/2013 (Judgment) ORDER 1] The accused Shankar Kisan Tare is hereby acquitted vide section 235(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure for the offences punishable under sections 363,366(A) and 376 of the Indian Penal Code and Secs.4, 7 & 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] The accused shall execute a fresh P.R. bond of ₹15,000/­ to appear before the Appellate Court as and when such court issues notice in respect of any appeal or petition filed against this judgment, in terms of section 437­A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 3] The victim to refund the compensation amount (if any, received by her) to the State within a period of four weeks from today. Thane. (Mridula V. K. Bhatia) Date : 27/04/2017. District Judge­08 & Special Judge (POCSO Act), Thane.

Bail No.1920//2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exhibit 1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 1920/2015 This application is filed by applicant/accused Sandeep Jagannath Marathe for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. I-34/2015 registered at Rabale police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 363, 376(1), 417 of I.P.C. and section 5(j), 6 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to P.O.C.S.O. Act). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant induced the minor niece of the complainant and kidnapped the girl out of lawful guardianship of the complainant and had forcible sexual intercourse with her. It is further contended and argued that no such incident of kidnapping has happened and the girl herself had come with the accused of her own wish since there was love affair between them and it is case of consent. It is further contended and argued that the applicant is falsely implicated in this crime on suspicion. It is further submitted that looking to the nature of allegation the investigation may have completed and there is no need of further custody of the applicant/accused. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it is contended and argued that the accused and the girl were knowing each other since before the incident and it is further contended that taking disadvantage of such acquaintance and knowing very well that the girl is minor by age, the accused induced and enticed her and kidnapped her from lawful guardianship of the complainant and committed aggravated penetrative sexual assault on her. It is further submitted that in such circumstance since the accused and girl are .. 2 .. Bail No.1920//2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) knowing each other, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl if released on bail and he may pressurize other the prosecution witnesses also. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 363, 376(1), 417 of I.P.C. and section 5(j), 6 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, the girl is stated to be 16 years old, it is contended on behalf of applicant that there was love affair between him and the girl and the girl had of her own came with him and he had not kidnapped the girl and it is a case of consent. Then, though it is contended on behalf of prosecution that consent of minor is immaterial, in the light particular contention on behalf of accused that there was love affair between him and girl and she herself left her house, the aspect as to whether the allegations against the accused are true or not, would be the question to be decided on merits. Even nothing is stated to be recovered from the applicant/accused. 4] Then, it is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 5] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the .. 3 .. Bail No.1920//2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 6] Then, it has also to be mentioned that though the investigation in the matter is yet to be completed and even charge-sheet is yet to be submitted, it would take time to complete the investigation and to submit the charge-sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 7] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order - ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Sandeep Jagannath Marathe is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/- [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions - The applicant/accused shall make himself available for interrogation by a police officer as and when called till filing of the charge-sheet and shall co-operate in investigation. He shall not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and the prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this Court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 19.08.2015 (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Additional Sessions Judge-1, Thane.

ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN CRIMINAL BAIL APPLICATION NO. 1925 /2015. Perused application and say thereon. Perused the case diary. Heard Ld. counsel Shri. Rajan Salunkhe, for applicant, Ld.A.P.P. Shri. Bahiram, for the State. 2. It is the case of prosecution that the accused persons are supplying girls who are working as singer and waiter in Millennium 2000 Orchestra Bar for sexual relations on demand by customers. On the date of raid, punter was sent. Accordingly, the said customer went to 'Samadhan' Lodging through Millennium Orchestra Bar. He has asked for a girl. Accordingly, one girl was followed him to Samadhan Lodge from Millennium 2000 Orchestra Bar. Accordingly, raid was effected. Girls were found there. It is further case of the prosecution that said Samadhan Lodge was supplying rooms for said human trafficking for illegal purpose by paying some amount to such girls and for their own benefit, thereby, committed an offence u/s. 370(3) r/w. sec. 34 of I.P.C.and under section 3, 4, 5, 6, and 7 of Prevention of Illegal Trafficking Act, 1956. 3. Ld. counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant had no concern with Millennium 2000 Orchestra Bar. He is serving in Samadhan Lodge as a manager. He has no control over the business. His role, at the most, would be restricted that he has given facility of the room. No illegal action was taken at Samadhan Bar. 4. Ld. counsel Shri. Bahiram submitted that owner of both Samadhan Lodge and Millennium 2000 Orchestra Bar and others are still absconding. Applicant has active role in the commission of crime. Offence is of serious nature. If the application is allowed, he may tamper the evidence and may also abscond. 5. Offence is serious one. About ten girls were found in the raid. Investigation is in progress. It is not completed. Offence is against woman. Bar and hotel seem to be used for illegal purpose like brothel. Hence, at this stage, it will not be just and proper to exercise the discretion in favour of the applicant. Hence, the order. ORDER Application is hereby, rejected. Date­ 17.08.2015. (A.S. Bhaisare) rd 3 Addl. Sessions Judge, Thane.

1 Criminal M.A. NO.382/2018. CNR NO. MHTH01­005149­2018. Amiya Kumar Bhagiraht Maiti. ..Applicant. Vs. State of Maharashtra (through Navghar P.S.) ..Respondent. : ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 : The applicant who claimed himself as father of victim in the matter relating to Crime No.I­42/2018 u/s. 366­A, 370, 372 r/w 34 of I.P.Code, u/s. 4 & 5 of Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act and u/s. 18 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act has moved this application for getting the custody of the victim to him. The applicant submitted that he is doing labour work at his native place mentioned in the application. The applicant is his daughter residing with him at native place, the victim is mother of 13 and 15 years old children, her husband has left her, and that, since then victim was residing with applicant. The applicant submitted that the victim was doing work of maid servant in the village. Accused was knowing her, who belongs to Midinapur and victim was residing with accused in his family since last two years and doing services. The applicant came to know that victims was allegedly involved in prostitution work and on all these submissions, the applicant is claiming her custody. In support of his contention, the applicant has submitted different documents on record as to identity of his own, as to identity of his daughter. 2] Investigating officer submitted say and opposed application with contention that there is possibility of re­involvement of the victim in prostitution work, for her welfare it is necessary to keep her in remand home and allegations were that the accused persons were receiving the amount by engaging the victim in prostitution work. 2 3] After filing this application, the victim was called before Court and she was inquired about her willingness. She stated that she wish to go with her father at her native place and that, she was residing with accused in his family and she was arrested when she was in restaurant. She also stated that he had come to her hostel. What transpires from all inquiry conducted in the matter and on perusal of the case record in respect of the crime is that, the victim was residing with the family of accused. It transpires that even after keeping victim in protection home there appears some suspect that the accused was trying to keep contact with her. The victim claimed herself as original resident of West Bengal and the trial in the matter is not yet started. Victim is the main witness in the matter and in my view, in such circumstances, till recording evidence of the victim it will not be proper to hand over the custody of victim to her father. As stated earlier, the victim is married woman and having children of 13 and 15 years and she was allegedly involved in the prostitution work. Considering the allegations, it will not be safe and secured to grant custody of victim to her father. The applicant will have liberty to apply after recording evidence of the victim in the matter in due course of time. Considering the same, application cannot be allowed at this stage. Hence, following order is passed. :ORDER: Application for grant of custody of the victim, moved by applicant Amiya Kumar Bhagiraht Maiti is rejected. Date­08/08/2018. (S.P. Gondhalekar) Thane. Kadam conducted investigation of the crime. After completion of investigation, P.I. Kamble filed charge­sheet against the accused for commission of above­said offences. 6] My learned predecessor framed charge against the accused for the offence punishable u/s. 376, 370, 366­A, 506 r/w. Sec. 34 of I.P.C., 4 POCSO Case. No. 199/2016.
