Amrita Jayantilal Jain­ medical officer who had examined the victim at Exh.29 as P.W.5, P.I. Rajendra Ganpatrao Kamble­ investigating officer at Exh. 32 as P.W.6. 8] The prosecution has also relied upon the following documents­ 1] F.I.R. ­ Exh.17 2] Statement of informant u/s. 164 of Cr.P.C.­ Exh. 18 3] Ultra­sound report and consent papers of victim­ Exh. 30 collectively. 4] House­search panchanama of the accused­ Exh. 33 5] Letter issued by investigating officer to Sr. P.I., Exh. 34 Crime Branch, Mumbai, for receiving original medical papers of the victim­ 6] Letter issued to medical officer by investigating Exh.35 officer for opinion and samples for blood, semen 5 POCSO Case. No. 199/2016. and D.N.A., etc. of accused­ 7] Letter for forwarding seized articles and samples Exh.36 to Forensic Laboratory for chemical analysis­ Thereafter, by pursis at Exh.37, the prosecution closed its evidence. 9] Statement of accused u/s. 313 of Cr.P.C. came to be recorded to the extent of only incriminating material against him. The defence of the accused is of total denial and false implication. 10] Heard learned A.P.P. Shri. Kulkarni for the State and learned counsel Smt. Sarita Gaikwad, for the accused. 11] Following points emerged for my consideration and I have recorded my findings thereon for the reasons given below. Points Findings 1] Whether the prosecution has proved No. that from 2013 to 03.04.16, the accused persons performed marriage of the victim with accused No. 3 Saddam though the victim was minor ? 2] Whether the prosecution has proved No. that accused Saddam had kept sexual relationship with victim, though she was minor and without her consent and accused No. 1 and 2 had intentionally abetted the same ? 3] Whether the prosecution has proved No. that during 2013 to 03.04.16, the accused persons along with absconding accused Lipi and Rahul forced the victim to keep sexual relations with said Rahul and some other persons for prostitution and detained her for 6 POCSO Case. No. 199/2016. prostitution against her will and they lived on her earnings of prostitution ? 4] Whether the prosecution has proved No. that the accused persons had intimated the parents of victim by saying that accused Saddam would commit suicide if they would not perform her marriage with Saddam, though she was minor at the relevant time ? 5] What order ? As per final order. REASONS 12] Ld. A.P.P. Shri. Kulkarni for the State submitted that in the present case, though victim P.W.1 does not know her date of birth, however, doctor P.W.5 has deposed that at the time of examination, the victim was 17 years old and she was 22 weeks pregnant. There is no suggestion put by the defence, thereby, denying the marriage between the victim and accused Saddam. Therefore, sections 4 and 6 of the POCSO Act and section 376 of I.P.C. are clearly applicable against accused Saddam while the provisions under the Prevention of Immoral Trafficking Act are applicable to all the accused persons, as it has come in the evidence of P.W.1 that one Rahul used to pay money to accused No. 1 for immoral trafficking of the victim. However, the investigating officer could not trace said Rahul and therefore, he has shown as absconding. 13] If the statement of victim u/s. 164 of Cr.P.C. would perused, it also reveals same allegations. Cross­examination of victim shows financial condition of both the families. In para No. 3 of her cross­examination, she has deposed that she was liking accused Saddam Shaikh. Both were Muslim. She was not happy with the marriage. She was not interested in 7 POCSO Case. No. 199/2016. the marriage itself. P.W.2 and P.W.3 are the social workers while P.W.5 is the doctor. When there is no denial of age of the victim, it is required to hold that the allegations of rape and sexual assault on child are considered to be proved. Hence, the accused may be held guilty of the charge and be punished with maximum sentence prescribed for the offence. 14] On the other hand, Ld. Counsel Smt. Gaikwad submitted that as per F.I.R. dated 26.04.2016, age of the victim is shown as 17 years. As per allegations, the marriage was performed in the year 2013. It means, at the time of alleged marriage, age of the victim must be 14 years, which is hard to believe. There is no proof to the allegations of threat to commit suicide. So also, there are no allegations of threat of any dire consequences against family members of the victim. Then, it is also hard to believe as to why parents of victim would succumb to it as it was not threat to their life. So also, if the F.I.R. and the statement of the victim would perused, there are so many improvements in the evidence of victim. Accused No. 1 Karimon is shown as mother­in­law, accused No. 2 Mohammad is shown as father­in­law while accused No. 3 Saddam is shown as husband. 15] As per her own version, marriage was performed in presence of society in Masjid with consent of parents. However, there is no complaint for more than three years even after marriage. Even as per her allegations, till 03.04.16, she was residing with the accused persons. F.I.R. came to be lodged on 30.04.16. There is delay of 27 days. That the marriage between accused No. 3 and victim was with the consent of parents. Informant was liking another person by name Imran and she has admitted in her cross­examination that after marriage with Saddam Shaikh, her parents and relatives again performed her marriage with another boy. She left the house of Saddam Shaikh and went with her second husband 8 POCSO Case. No. 199/2016. and resided there for three months. She was also visiting one boy named Tutul, who was a hawker. He used to spend 2­3 hours with him in garden and she used to visit him daily at 5.00 p.m. She had also left her house along with said Tutul for one month at Nalasopara and again joined the house of Saddam. She has also admitted that father of victim as well as father of accused Saddam were labourers. They were living their life on their earning of labour work. Saddam also used to leave home at 9.00 a.m. for labour work and used to return at 7.00 p.m. Accused Karimon also used to come for work as maid on all days of week. They have even not celebrated the festival jointly. It means, they were not at home for entire day. Therefore, there is no question of harassment. The victim used to visit her parents about twice a week. She used to help her parents economically even prior to marriage. Her parents and relatives were residing in nearby house. Her mother used to visit her matrimonial house. She used to serve her with food. It shows that she can do whatever she wish at her free will and there was no restriction on her. 16] She has also admitted that name of her second husband was Buddha. After her marriage, Buddha and his parents had been to the house of accused Saddam to take her back to their house. There was quarrel between both the husbands. She was happy with Buddha. There was physical relationship between her and Buddha. Due to minor quarrels with him, she returned back to house of Saddam Shaikh. She does not have any details as to when she went to the house of Buddha and when she left his house. After she returned back to the house of Saddam, there was quarrel. They assaulted each­other. Parents of Saddam enquired as to why she left the house. She has also deposed that thereafter, there was no problem in the matrimonial home. She has also deposed in para 9 that when she left 9 POCSO Case. No. 199/2016. the house of Buddha, she was pregnant. She has also admitted that accused have nicely maintained her. So also that, she had lodged the report as per directions of social worker. She had also mentioned that she did not supply any proof of her date of birth to social worker or police. Apart from the victim P.W.1, there is no other witness to marriage or any other allegations. 17] She further submitted that in the light of above situation, when there is only one witness on the point of the allegations, there is no evidence about age of the victim. Except the oral version of the victim, there is no evidence about actual performance of marriage or its date. So also, when the victim herself is saying that when she left the house of her other husband Buddha, she was pregnant. Moreover, in her cross­ examination, she has deposed to the extent that she was happy with the accused persons. She was treated well by the accused persons. Her relatives and parents were residing in the nearby vicinity. It has also came in her evidence that all the accused were earning their livelihood by doing labour work and for entire day, they used to be out of house. The informant was free to meet her parents and she was meeting them twice in a week. Her mother used to visit the house of accused. The victim was daily visiting the boy by name Tutul and used to spend two­three hours with him in garden. She had performed second marriage. 18] She further submitted that not only this, it has come in his evidence that one Mogal was her cousin brother­in­law. There was case against him in respect of woman. She was told by Mogal that she can earn money from prostitution. She was interested in keeping relations with Tutul, Rahul and Mogal, but it was objected by the accused persons. She told by them that accused could be detained in jail and due to anger, she lodged her report against accused. She has also deposed that she had 10 POCSO Case. No. 199/2016. lodged her report on the say of social worker. 19] She further submitted that her statement was not read over to her by police. She does not know contents of the same. She does not know the reason behind the case. The person Rahul used to come to their house and used to talk to her. Therefore, by the cross­examination of the informant, it is clear that there is no evidence about her minority. There is no evidence about her pregnancy due to physical relationship with accused Saddam. Rather, the story which reveals from her cross­examination is, 'the informant herself was interested in keeping relations with boys namely Tutul, Rahul and Mogal. However, it was objected by accused persons and those three boys told her that accused should be detained in jail and therefore, out of anger, false F.I.R. came to be lodged against accused persons. There is no ossification test to show the age of the victim. Moreover, though she is shown as pregnant, there is no D.N.A. test of foetus. So also, as per the version of informant herself, when she left the house of Buddha her other husband, she was pregnant. Therefore, most probably, she was pregnant from said Buddha. She had left house of said other husband also on her own. Therefore, the version in the F.I.R. itself is not believable. The accused persons were earning their livelihood by doing labour work. Therefore, neither they have performed child marriage of informant nor pressurized her for immoral trafficking. Therefore, the allegations against the accused are not at all proved. 20] She further submitted that if the entire F.I.R., other material produced by prosecution would perused, there is not a single sentence against accused No. 2 father­in­law of the victim. He has not attributed any role. Therefore, he is required to be honourably acquitted while rest of the accused are required to be acquitted by disbelieving the prosecution case. 11 POCSO Case. No. 199/2016. She further submitted that in cross­examination of the investigating officer, it is clear that the investigating officer has not collected any documentary evidence about travel or stay of victim at Gujarat. The investigating officer has also admitted that the accused persons and the informant were arrested as illegal immigrants from Bangladesh and at the relevant time, it was revealed that she was pregnant, therefore, case came to be filed. In the circumstances, the prime witness is indicating false implication of the accused due to her own anger against the accused. There is no evidence about age of the victim or physical relationship between accused Saddam and victim before she attaining majority. There is no material against the accused. The statements of witnesses including Pratima the sister­in­law of the victim girl were recorded. Then in between the victim girl phoned and had informed her paternal aunt that she is with the accused. Police had then traced the accused and caught the accused as well as victim girl and brought them to the police station. The victim girl was then sent for medical examination. The accused was got arrested and also was referred for medical examination , clothes on the person of accused as well as victim girl were seized under panchanama . The panchanama of the spot was also prepared. Further statement of the witnesses were recorded. The rent agreement in regard to the room where the accused and the victim girl were stayed was obtained and statement of landlord was recorded. The medical certificates of the victim girl and the accused were obtained. The C.D.R. record of the mobile phone numbers of the accused and the victim girl were obtained. The samples obtained and seized clothes were sent for chemical analysis to C.A. alongwith the letter. Since during the inquiry it is revealed that missing complaint in regard to the same girl was filed by the complainant, enquiry papers in regard to the said missing papers were called for and after completion of investigation , since there was sufficient evidence against the accused, accused came to be chargesheeted for the offence punishable 363, 366 & 37 of I.P.C. U/Sec.4 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act,2012. Since the offence under Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act,2012 is exclusively triable by the Special Court the chargesheet was submitted to this court. 3] The accused produced before the Court. A charge U/Secs. 363, 366 & 376 of I.P.C. U/Sec.4 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act,2012 was framed against the accused. The contents of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular and explained to the accused in vernacular . His defence as it is revealed from the cross­examination of the witness and his statement recorded U/Sec.313(1)(b) of Cr.P.C. that he is falsely implicated in the crime. That the girl was in love with him. But her paternal aunt wanted to perform her marriage with the boy of her choice but the girl was not ready and therefore she ran away and falsely implicated him in the case . He claimed to be tried . 4] For establishing the charges levelled against the accused prosecution has examined in all 8 witnesses as under : P.W.1­ Sau.Vimal Ashok Patange, the complainant and paternal aunt of the victim girl Sheetal Ingle. P.W.2­ Sheetal Ashok Ingle, the vitim girl. P.W.3­ Pratima Anil Patange sister­in­law of the victim girl Sheetal. P.W.4­ Sainath Shalik Wayle, the panch on the spot panchanama. P.W.5­ Sachin Kashinath Choudhary, the panch witness on panchanama of seizure of clothes of accused . P.W.6­ Namdev Dunda Jadhav, the landlord of the room where the accused and victim girl were staying. P.W.7­ Sandeep Tukaram Waghole the Head­Master of the school in which the victim girl was studying. P.W.8­ P.I. Kisan Govind Gavit who investigated the crime. 5] The documentary evidence produced, proved and relied upon by the prosecution consisted of missing complaint Exh.13, complaint Exh.14, spot panchanama Exh.26, seizure panchanama of clothes of victim girl Exh.26, arrest panchanama Exh.27, seizure panchanama of clothes of accused Exh.28, the extract of school register Exh.33, medical papers of victim girl at Exh.38, letters by which the muddemal seized and samples were sent to C.A. at Exh.46 & 47, C.A. reports at Exh.48 to 50 and agreement of Leave & License at Exh.51. 6] The statement of accused U/Sec.313(1)(b) was recorded . The accused did not examine himself on oath and had not examined any defence witness . 7] I have heard both Ld.A.P.P. and Ld.Adv. for accused. It was argued by the Ld.A.P.P. that from the testimony of the Head­Master corroborated by the documentary evidence, the girl is proved to be 13 yrs. old. It is also pointed out that from the testimony of the complainant as well as victim girl that accused took the girl to the Shantisagar Resort and then he hired the room and stayed in the room alongwith girl and also married with her. It is also pointed out from the testimony of the girl that the accused had sexual intercourse with the girl who was 13 yrs. old. It was pointed out that though no force used to have been done, from the testimony of the girl it is clear that the accused had induced her to go with him and have sexual intercourse with her on the false pretext that they are married, in fact the girl being minor her consent is not a valid consent. It was therefore argued that the offences U/Secs.363, 366 & 376 of I.P.C. are proved and even Sec. 4 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 is also established against the accused and accused is liable to be convicted for the said offences. As against this it was argued on behalf of the accused that the evidence on record is not sufficient to prove the guilt against the accused and the accused be acquitted. 8] On the basis of above facts of the case, the points which arose for my determination , my findings and reasons for the same are as under : POINTS FINDINGS 1) Whether the prosecution has proved that on 15/6/2013 at about 16.00 hours at Jambhulpada, public toilet, Veer Savarkarnagr, Thane the accused kidnapped the minor girl named Kumari Sheetal Ashok Ingale aged 13 yrs. from the lawful guardianship of the complainant ? Not proved. 2) Whether the prosecution has proved that on the abovesaid date, time and place the accused kidnapped the minor girl Kum.Sheetal Ingale with intention that she may be compelled or knowing it to be likely that she will be compelled, to marry him against her will, or in order that she may be forced or seduced to illicit intercourse, or knowing it to be likely that she will be forced or seduced to illicit intercourse ? Not proved. 3) Whether the prosecution has proved that during the period from 16.00 hours on 15/6/13 to 5/7/13 at room no.2, Jadhav chawl, in front of Shantisagar Resort, Vasatgaon, Ambernath, Dist. Thane accused committed rape on the minor girl Sheetal Ingale ? Not proved. 4) Whether the prosecution has proved that on the given day, date, time and place the accused committed penetrative sexual assault on the victim girl ? Not proved. 5) What order ? As per final order. : REASONS: AS TO POINT NOS.1 TO 4 : 9] All these points are interconnected and required to be decided on the basis of same evidence. Therefore, I discuss and decide them together. 10] As is clear as per the prosecution case the accused has kidnapped the minor girl Sheetal Ingale aged about 13 yrs. from lawful guardianship of the complainant with a view to seduce her to have illicit intercourse and for committing rape on her and since the girl was minor Sec. 4 Protection of Children From Sexual Offiences Act, 2012 also is applied. 11] It would be desirable to mention some facts which are clear from the record and are not disputed on behalf of the accused that the victim Sheetal was staying with the complainant Vimal Patange who is her paternal aunt. That Vimal the complainant was working at Bhuvan Maharaj Caterer, Mulund and Sheetal also used to accompany her for work. It is also clear and not in dispute that the accused was also working with the same caterer and therefore the complainant victim girl Sheetal, accused and witnesses were well acquainted with each other. It is also clear and not in dispute that on the day of incident on 14/6/2013 there was some quarrel between the victim girl and Vilas the son of complainant and since Vilas has assaulted the victim girl , she had left the house and went to Thane station. Then as per the prosecution case the accused met the victim girl at Thane Station and then went with him and then they stayed in a rented room and there the accused alleged to have sexual intercourse with her. 12] As such from the clear admitted facts on record, it is apparent that on the day of incident, the girl had left the house under the grief of anger being annoyed with the son of the complainant. Even the victim girl in her evidence specifically stated that on that day she had hot altercations of words with Vilas son of her paternal aunt, the complainant and she got annoyed and left the house by telling that she is going to answer the call of nature. As such it is very much clear that the accused has no role to play in victim girl leaving the house on that day. Even it is not alleged that accused has induced her to come to Thane Station with a view to have illicit intercourse with her . 13] Then so far as the allegations that the accused had kidnapped the said minor girl from lawful guardianship of the complainant, it has to be mentioned that the complainant is not the mother or the father of the girl and is stated to be the paternal aunt of the girl and can not be said to be lawful guardian. Absolutely nothing is brought on record to show that at the relevant time the girl was in lawful custody of the complainant. The parents of the girl are not examined by the prosecution and therefore even it is clear that when the girl has left the house on her own for her own reasons without accused having any role to play therein, it has to be concluded at this stage only that the allegations of the accused had kidnapped the girl from lawful guardianship with a view to have illicit intercourse with her are not established. 14] Then so far as the aspect that the accused had taken away the girl from Thane Railway Station with him and stayed in a rented room and performed marriage with the girl and have sexual intercourse with her for 3 times etc. is concerned, it has to be mentioned that as per the version of the complainant after the girl left the house they were searching for her but as she not traced, she has lodged complaint as per Exh.13. Even as per her version she was knowing the accused and even asked him to search for girl , but he was avoiding and therefore she was suspected and asked whether the girl was with him and then accused himself disclosed that the girl was with him. Then she went to the police station and lodged complaint as per Exh.14 and then with the help of police the girl and the accused were traced. 15] Similar is the testimony of victim girl Sheetal who also stated that when she was at Thane , accused was also there and then she went to Ambernath with the accused, accused then hired a room there and she stayed with the accused for 8 days and then police had caught her and accused. It is material to mention in this respect that as per the defence put forth by the accused the girl and the accused were in love with each other and were intending to marry and even the accused had married the girl and the complainant disliked it and in fact she wanted to perform marriage of Sheetal with her son Vilas and therefore she left the house of complainant and went with the accused, and she filed false complaint falsely implicating accused. 16] It is very much material in this respect that the victim girl in her evidence do not appear to have stated anything about accused inducing her to come with him or forcing her to stay with him or having forcible sexual intercourse. She appear to have simply stated that she went to Thane Station , accused was also there and then she went to Ambernath alongwith the accused. She also further stated that accused hired a room and there she stayed with accused for 8 days and they have bought household utensils etc. and there she had physical relations with accused for 3 times. Then it is also material to mention that in her cross-examination she appear to have accepted that she had stated before police in portion marked 'A' that she had married with the accused and stated that therefore it is so recorded by police. In the light of that if the cross-examination of the complainant in that regard is perused, she appear to have accepted that on 17th accused had phoned her and informed her that he was at Hydrabad with Sheetal and they have married. That makes it clear that not only the victim girl had been with accused at her own wish, the accused and the girl even performed marriage. In the light of that if the further cross-examination of the victim girl is perused, she appear to have stated that she had stated portion marked 'A' in her statement, in that regard to her marriage to the police, but that is not correct and she has stated so falsely. She has also further stated that she had also wrongly stated to police in statement that after she left the house on 14/6/13 she stayed at the house of her friend Pranali and on next day accused met her and she went with him on 15/6/13. She also further accepted that she had stated wrongly to police in her statement that on 30/6/13 she phoned her mother and informed her that she had married with the accused. It is thus clear that the witness is not a reliable and truthful witness and has no botheration even to make false statement before police and is not a person worthy of credence and has been changed her stand now and then to suit her purpose. Not only that but from her such version, it is very much clear that it is a case of consent and is in full support of defence put forth by the accused that the girl had been with him at her own wish and since there was love affair between them, they had even performed marriage in temple and stayed together and only because the paternal aunt of the victim girl was against that and want to perform marriage of Sheetal with her son, he is falsely implicated. 17] In the light of that if the cross-examination of the victim girl is perused she appear to have denied that she herself and accused were in love with each other and also that she herself had phoned and called the accused to come to Thane station . But in the light of the further events which took place that the victim girl had been to the railway station under the grief of anger , there is no explanation as to how the accused could know that the victim had been to Thane railway station and how he went there. Then the subsequent conduct of the victim girl that she went with the accused and stayed with him for 8 days even performed marriage and her version that they had bought household utensils etc. make it clear that there was no compulsion or inducement that she had been there with the accused and the only inference is that after going to Thane railway station, she herself had intimated the accused and called him and therefore accused had been there and that further makes it clear that she denied falsely in her deposition that they are having love with each other. 18] It is also very much material to mention here that P.W.1 the complainant as well as P.W.2 victim girl have both accepted in their cross- examination that Sheetal got married with Vilas, the son of complainant on 26/12/2013. It is further material to mention the fact that the marriage of the victim was performed with the son of the complainant appear to have been concealed by the complainant and the victim girl intentionally from the Court while deposing on oath i.e. in her examination-in- chief the complainant stated that Sheetal is her niece and she had not stated that she is her daughter-in-law and it is only in her cross-examination that marriage of Sheetal was performed with Vilas in Dec., 2013 and when asked the reason as to why she has not stated that Sheetal is not her daughter-in-law and she had concealed the fact of marriage of Sheetal with her son and that she is her niece . The witness accepted that she made the mistake and she did not state about the marriage. Similarly the victim girl also in her examination- in-chief do not disclose the fact of her marriage with the son of the complainant. Right from stating her name she lied by telling her name as Sheetal Ashok Ingle only with a view to conceal her marriage with the son of complainant and refer the complainant as her paternal aunt instead of her mother-in-law. Even in her cross-examination on behalf of accused in that regard she accepted that her name is changed to Sheetal Vilas Patange since after the marriage and she was unable to explain the reason as to why she has not stated her changed name after marriage and stated her maiden name and she also apologized by stating that she has stated her name falsely as Sheetal Ashok Ingale and appear to have accepted the fact that she has concealed her marriage. The reason for mentioning all these facts in detail is that both the complainant as well as the victim girl appear to have been very less respect for the truth and do not appear to be bothering for making wrong and false statement at different point of time suitng their purpose. The fact that within a period of less than a year of the incident the marriage of victim girl was performed with the son of the complainant is in full support and corroboration of the defence put forth by the accused that the complainant wanted to marry Sheetal with her son and disliked the affair between the victim girl and the accused and therefore when the girl left the house being aggrieved, she had filed the complaint implicating the accused and therefore the submission on behalf of the accused that for that reason the accused is falsely implicated in the crime and the girl under the pressure of her paternal aunt i.e. the complainant made such a statement that the accused had forcible sexual intercourse with her appear to be sustainable, that is even corroborated by the testimony of the victim girl, wherein absolutely nothing is stated by her about any force or inducement by the accused to go with him. 19] In that respect, it is argued on behalf of the prosecution that though it is a case of consent, the girl was aged about 14 yrs. at the relevant time and therefore her consent is not a valid consent in the eyes of law and even if the girl is stated to have been with the accused it is a case of her consent, the accused is guilty of the offence U/Sec. 363 as well as U/Sec.376 of I.P.C. 20] In that respect, it is to be mentioned that it appear to be a case of consent and it is clear that the girl left on her and went with the accused on her own wish , the aspect of age of the victim girl is very much material and important. Then as per the prosecution case the girl at the relevant time was aged about 14 yrs. and her date of birth is 10/05/2001 as per school record. No doubt P.W.7-Sandeep Waghole the Sr. Teacher in the school where the girl is stated to have been studied stated that as per the school record the date of birth of the girl is 10/05/2001 and Exh.33 is the extract of birth register of the girl . But then it is material to mention that the accused has come up with the case that the girl at the relevant time was above 18 yrs. , then in regard to the entry in the school register the P.W.7 appear to have stated that the entries in the school register are made at the time of admission of the student on the basis of birth certificate or earlier school certificate. But as is clear he has no such document on the basis of which such entry in school record is made is produced and in his cross-examination P.W.7 accepted that he has not brought the document on the basis of which the entry in regard to the date of the birth of concern girl was made. His evidence was recorded in Nov.2014 and in spite of the matter was pending since then till today the prosecution has not produced on record the said document on the basis of which the entry in the school record was made. In the light of that if the admission by P.W.7 in his cross-examination that he can not say anything that the entry of the date of birth of the girl in the school record is wrong assumes importance. It is further material in the light of the fact that if the age of the girl is calculated on the basis of the date of birth of the girl i.e. 10/5/2001 as on the date of incident the age of the girl comes to 12 yrs. In the light of the aspect that the girl was also referred for medical examination for age determination is considered, it is clear that as per the medical report at Exh. 38. On the basis of medical examination and x-ray of the girl the approximate radiological age of the girl was between 14 to 16 yrs. which is also totally contrary to the prosecution case that the date of the birth of the girl is 10/5/2001 and it is difficult to believe that if the girl is 12 yrs. her radiological age would be between 14 to 16 yrs. and it has to be concluded that the girl at the relevant time was below 16 yrs. Then considering the margin of error in regard to the age determined on the basis of medical examination the possibility of the girl more than 16 yrs. of the age can not be ruled out and the prosecution has to be held as failed to prove that at the relevant time the girl was below 16 yrs. of age. In the light of that since the girl is above 16 yrs. age the sexual intercourse if any by the accused with her since being with her consent would not amount to rape. Then even so far as offence of kidnapping also since it is observed that the girl had left the house for some different reason and the accused had no role to play in her leaving the house and going with him it can not be said that there is no any inducement or enticement by the accused and therefore offence of kidnapping with a view to induce her to have illicit sexual intercourse can not be said to have established. 21] In view of above discussion it has to be concluded that no offence is proved against the accused and therefore accused is entitled to be acquitted. Point nos. 1 to 4 are answered accordingly. 22] Since the accused is acquitted, it is necessary that he be directed to furnish separate P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [Rupees Fifteen Thousand only] with one surety under section 437A of Cr.P.C. to appear before the Higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect of any appeal or petition, if any, filed against the judgment. In the result I pass the following order : ORDER 1) Accused Anand Suresh Reddy is acquitted of the charge for offence punishable under sections 363, 366 & 376 of I.P.C. & U/Sec. 4 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act,2012. 2) Bail bond of the accused stands cancelled and surety is discharged. 3) The accused shall furnish P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [Rupees Fifteen Thousand only] with one surety in the like amount under section 437A of Cr.P.C. to appear before the higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect of any appeal or petition, if any, filed against the judgment and that such bail bond shall be in force for six months. 4) All muddemal articles being worthless be destroyed after expiry of appeal period. 5) The proceeding is closed. Date : 28/01/2015 (Mrs.V.V.Virkar) Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

.. 1 .. bail no.1939/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 1939/2015 This application is filed by applicant Mohd Aaftab Abdul Hamid Khan for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. I-230/2015 registered at Shantinagar police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 354(A) of I.P.C. and section 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant outraged modesty of the complainant victim girl more than once by using criminal force against her. It is further contended and argued that no such incident has happened and the applicant is falsely implicated with ulterior intention on account of enmity between brother of complainant and the applicant. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co-operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that on 25.06.2015, 05.07.2015 and 26.07.2015 the accused has committed sexual assault on the complainant minor girl by applying criminal force against her and hugging her and moving hand over her private part and breast. It is further contended and argued that even though the accused was knowing that the girl was minor, he has committed sexual assault on her. It is further submitted that in such .. 2 .. bail no.1939/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl and the prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 354A(1) of I.P.C. and section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act with the allegation of sexual assault on minor girl the girl is stated to be 16 years old and it appears that it is specifically contended on behalf of accused that due to rivalry between the brother of the complainant and applicant, the applicant is falsely implicated in the crime. In such circumstance whether the allegations against the accused are true or not, would be the question to be decided on merits. Even nothing is stated to be recovered from the applicant/accused. 4] It is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. .. 3 .. bail no.1939/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) 5] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 6] Then, it has also to be mentioned that looking the allegations against the accused the investigation in the matter may have almost completed but the charge sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 7] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order - ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Mohd Aaftab Abdul Hamid Khan is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/- [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions - The applicant/accused shall make himself available for interrogation by a police officer and shall attend the concerned police station as and when called for till filing of the charge sheet and shall co-operate in investigation. .. 4 .. bail no.1939/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) He shall not contact the complainant girl in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize her and the prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not abscond and shall attend the Court regularly for the purpose of trial. He shall not leave India without permission of this Court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 26.08.2015 (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Additional Session Judge-1, Thane.

1 Special Case No. 171/2014 (Judgment) Presented on : 09/09/2014 Registered on : 09/09/2014 Decided on : 22/04/2016 Duration :1­year,7­Months,13­days. IN THE COURT OF THE SPECIAL JUDGE (P.O.C.S.O.ACT), THANE. (Presided over by Ms.U.M.Nandeshwar, Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O.Act) Thane) SPECIAL CASE No. 171 of 2014 Exhibit No.22. The State of Maharashtra Through Bhiwandi City Police Station Thane, District – Thane. ... Prosecution versus Mahesh Baban Bhosale Age 23 years, R/o. –Chandrakant Lad chawl, behind Ashok Nagar, Nhavipada Bhiwandi, Dist. Thane. ... Accused Offence punishable under section 354­D of Indian Penal Code and under section 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Appearance ­ Spl.P.P. Mrs. R. A. Navale, for the State. Advocate Miss Nafis Momin, for the Accused. 2 Special Case No. 171/2014 (Judgment) JUDGMENT (Delivered on 22nd April, 2016.) 1] The Accused stands prosecuted for the offence punishable under section 354­D of Indian Penal Code and also under section 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act) for causing sexual harassment to minor victim­girl aged about 15 years and threaten her. 2] Shorn of unnecessary details, the indictment against the Accused are as under ­ [i] Informant victim­girl aged about 15 years was staying at Bhiwandi with her family and studying in 9 th std. Her school timing were from 11.30 a.m. to 05.00 p.m. However, her semester examination were going on and therefore, her school timings were 07.30 a.m. to 10.30 a.m. [ii] On 22/10/2013 victim­girl was proceeding to her school around 07.00 a.m. with her friends. At that time, she noticed that one boy on his motor­cycle was staring at her and while returning also he followed them on his motor­cycle and then by taking motor­cycle in front of her, accused was watching her in the mirror and followed her uptill her house. [iii] On 24/10/2013 he repeated the same act and when she was returning from school, he came behind her and told that he will not came from tomorrow and shall he go? 3 Special Case No. 171/2014 (Judgment) Thereafter, he went away from there. Therefore, the informant disclosed it to her mother (Pw­2)and brother. [iv] On 25/10/2013 when informant/ victim­girl was returning from school, her mother watched her and there she again seen the accused viewing her from the mirror of motor­ cycle. Therefore, informant shown that boy to her mother and stated that he is the same boy who followed her. Therefore, her mother (Pw­2) caught him and the people gathered there and they thrashed that boy and took to the police station. There that boy disclosed his name as Mahesh Baban Bhosale [Accused]. Therefore, the informant lodged the report against the accused. 3] On her report F.I.R. was registered against the Accused vide C.R.No.I­203/2013 for the offence punishable under section 354­D of I.P.C. The investigation was carried out by A.P.I. Suresh Ganpat Chopde(Pw­3). The Accused was arrested. The spot panchnama was drawn. Statements of witnesses and victim­girl were recorded. School leaving certificate of the victim­girl was collected. Then the offence under section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act was added. Thereafter, investigation culminated into filing of charge­sheet in this Court being the Special designated court under P.O.C.S.O. Act. 4] The charge (Exh.4) was framed against the Accused for offence punishable under section 354­D of Indian 4 Special Case No. 171/2014 (Judgment) Penal Code and also under section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. The Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial (Exh.5). The Accused took defence of total denial. 5] In response to application under section 294 of Cr.P.C. the defence has admitted spot panchnama [Exh.15], Arrest form [Exh.16] and school leaving certificate of victim­ girl [Exh.13]. 6] In order to prove guilt of Accused Prosecution has examined following witnesses ­ P.W.1 Informant – victim­girl Exh.10 P.W.2 Vandana Navnath Waghmare Exh.14 (Mother of victim­girl) P.W.3 P.S.I. Suresh Ganpat Chopde Exh.17 (Investigating officer) 7] The prosecution proved and relied on the report / F.I.R. [Exh.11]. 8] The prosecution closed its side of evidence by filing Pursis at Exhibit­19. The incriminating evidence came on record against the Accused was read over and explained to him in vernacular and his statement under Section 313(b) of Cr.P.C. was recorded vide Exh.21. Accused neither examined himself nor examined any witness in his defence. 5 Special Case No. 171/2014 (Judgment) 9] Heard learned Spl.P.P. Mrs. R. A. Navale for State and the learned Advocate Miss. Nafin Momin for Accused. 10] On consideration of argument advanced on behalf of both the sides and on perusal of the oral & documentary evidence on record, following points arise for my determination, which are answered with the findings thereon, as under :­ Sr. Points Findings No. 1] Does the prosecution prove that during the period from 22/10/2013 around 07.30 a.m. to 25/10/2013 around 11.00 hrs. from Padmashree Annasaheb Jadhav ..No. college to the residence of informant accused followed and attempted to contact the minor victim­girl aged 14 years to foster personal interaction repeatedly despite a clear indication of disinterest by her and he thereby committed an offence punishable under section 354­D(i) of Indian Penal Code ? 2] Does the prosecution prove that during same period accused repeatedly followed her on the way to her school and used to watch her from the mirror of the bike ...No. and thereby he committed an offence punishable under section 12 of the P.O.C.S.O. Act? 6 Special Case No. 171/2014 (Judgment) 3] What order ? Accused is acquitted. REASONS As to Point No.1 to 3 : 11] All the points are taken up together for discussion, to avoid the repetition, as evidence about the same in common and inter­connected. 12] As the Accused is facing charge under section 354­D of I.P.C. it is incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that the Accused followed the woman [victim­girl] and contacts or attempt to contact to foster personal interaction repeatedly despite a clear indication of disinterest by such woman. So also as the Accused is facing charge under section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, therefore, it is further incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that the accused has committed sexual harassment to the victim­girl with sexual intent, either utters any word or makes any sound, or makes any gesture or exhibits any object or part of body with the intention that such work or sound shall be heard, or such gesture or object or part of body shall be seen by the child; or repeatedly or constantly follows or watches or contact a child either directly or through electronic, digital or any other means etc. as defined in section 7 Special Case No. 171/2014 (Judgment) 11 of the Protection Of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (P.O.C.S.O. Act). Age of victim­girl : 13] As the Accused is facing charge under P.O.C.S.O. Act, therefore, first of all it is incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that the victim­girl was child (minor) at the time of incident. The alleged incident took place in between 22/10/2013 to 25/10/2013. Victim­girl (P.W.1) deposed her date of birth as 13/10/2000 and in the year­2013 she was studying in 9th std. Further the defence admitted the school leaving certificate of the victim­girl issued by Vidyashram Marathi School Bhiwandi which is at Exh.13 wherein also the same date of birth is mentioned. Thus, as the date of the victim­girl is not challenged, therefore, there is no hurdle to believe the school leaving certificate which is admitted by the defence. Thus, on the day of incident, the victim­girl was aged about 13 years. Thus, prosecution proved that at the time of incident, the victim­girl was minor aged abut 13 years i.e. below the age of 18 years and she was a “child” as per definition given in Section 2(d) of P.O.C.S.O. Act. 14] To prove the charge against the Accused the prosecution has examined the informant / victim­girl and her mother who are the most material witnesses to prove the 8 Special Case No. 171/2014 (Judgment) charge against the Accused. Informant (P.W.1) and her mother (P.W.2) deposed that at the relevant time, the school timings of the victim­girl were 07.30 a.m. to 02.30 p.m. and on her school way one boy used to chase her on his motor­cycle. The victim­girl further deposed that on 24/10/2013 that boy came near her and told her that he will not come tomorrow and shall he go. She further deposed that she disclosed it to her mother and on 25/10/2013 her mother accompanied her and when that boy came on motor­cycle her mother caught hold that boy and public gathered there and thrashed that boy and then taken to police station and then she lodged the report. However, the victim­girl failed to identify the accused as a same boy who followed her and tried to foster interaction with her. 15] Moreover, the mother of victim­girl Pw­2 did not support the version of the victim­girl that she narrated the incident to her mother and then she accompanied with her and caught hold that boy. Thus, although the victim­girl is believed about following by one boy to foster interaction with her still the identity of accused is not proved. Thus, the prosecution failed to prove that the accused is the same boy who followed the victim girl and attempted to contact with her to foster personal interaction with her despite of clear indication of disinterest by the victim­girl and harassed her. 9 Special Case No. 171/2014 (Judgment) 16] Thus, there is absolutely no legal evidence on record to prove that accused stalked the victim­girl to foster personal interaction and caused sexual harassment to her. 17] Thus, as the informant/victim­girl though stated about followed by one boy but she failed to identify the accused as the same boy. Further the witness mother of victim­ girl (Pw­2) though as per the prosecution caught hold the accused and taken to police station did not support the prosecution case, therefore, there is no iota of evidence against the Accused to prove the charge leveled against him. Thus, prosecution failed to prove that accused caused sexual harassment to victim­girl by stalking her. Hence, I answer point No.1 & 2 in negative. Therefore, in absence of any evidence against the Accused, he is entitled for acquittal. 18] In the result, I proceed to pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused Mahesh Baban Bhosale is hereby acquitted U/Sec. 235(1) of Cr.P.C. for the offence punishable U/Sec.354­D of Indian Penal Code and U/s.12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] His bail bonds stand cancelled and sureties are discharged. 10 Special Case No. 171/2014 (Judgment) 3] The Accused shall furnish personal bond of the amount of ₹15,000/­in compliance of provision of Section 437­A of Cr.P.C. and the earlier surety will continue for further six months. The judgment is dictated and pronounced in open Court. Date :22/04/2016. (Ms. U. M. Nandeshwar), Thane Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act), District Judge ­1 and Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 5] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 6] Then, it has also to be mentioned that looking the allegations against the accused the investigation in the matter may have almost completed but the charge-sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge-sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 7] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. On 08.07.2014 parents of victim girl had gone to their native place at Narayanpeth, Dist. Mastar, Andhra Pradesh. On 08.07.2014 the victim girl and her elder sister had gone to do labour work as usual. After returning home they were sleeping in their hut. The victim's maternal uncle Hanmanta Rathod and his wife were also sleeping in the hut of the victim as her parents had gone to their native place. While victim and her sister were sleeping in the hut, at about 03.00 a.m. of 09.07.2014 the accused entered their hut and slept in between the victim and her sister. The accused moved his hand over the chest of the victim. He touched her inappropriately. Thereby the victim woke­up and raised alarm. Victim's sister and maternal uncle also woke­up and caught hold the accused. The accused told his name as Sautiya Behara, resident of Krushna Hotel, Sector­42, Seawood, Nerul. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 173­14 ­ 354, 12.doc .....3/­ ..3.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 173/2014.. Exh.30.. The accused was apprehended on the spot itself. The accused was taken to the police station. The police recorded complaint of the victim and registered crime against the accused for the offences punishable u/s.354 of the Indian Penal Code. As the victim was 15 years old and minor, section 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act came to be added during investigation. After investigation charge sheet came to be filed against the accused for offence punishable u/s.354 of the Indian Penal Code and u/s.8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 3] Charge is framed against the accused at Exh.05. The accused pleaded not guilty of offence and claimed to be tried. 4] Statement of accused u/s.313 of Code of Criminal Procedure is recorded at Exh.29. The defence of the accused is that, on the night of incident at about 12.00 midnight he was passing through the lane in front of the hut of victim. He was drunken. He was caught hold by 15 to 20 persons and was assaulted out of suspicion. Thereafter false case came to be lodged against him. 5] After going through the prosecution story, evidence on record and hearing arguments of both sides, following J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 173­14 ­ 354, 12.doc .....4/­ ..4.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 173/2014.. Exh.30.. points arise for my determination. I record my findings thereon for reasons as stated below. POINTS FINDINGS 1] Does the prosecution prove that on 09.07.2014 at about 03.00 a.m. in the hut of victim at Karavegaon, Nerul, Navi Mumbai the accused slept in between the victim and her elder sister, touched her breast inappropriately and thereby sexually assaulted her as well as …Proved. outraged the modesty of victim ? 2] What order ? ..As per final order. : REASONS : As to the Point No.1 :­ 6] To bring home the guilt of the accused the prosecution has examined the victim as PW1 at Exh.16. The victim has narrated the entire facts as mentioned in the complaint in her deposition before the Court. She specifically deposed that the incident had occurred in the month of July 2014. At that time her parents had gone to their native place in Andhra Pradesh. The victim, her elder sister, maternal uncle and his wife were sleeping in their hut. The maternal uncle and his wife were sleeping on cot, whereas the victim and her sister were sleeping on the ground. At about 03.00 a.m. the accused entered their hut and slept between the victim and her sister. He touched the breast of victim. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 173­14 ­ 354, 12.doc .....5/­ ..5.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 173/2014.. Exh.30.. Thereupon the victim raised alarm. While the accused was trying to run away, he was caught hold and was taken to the police station. In the police station police recorded her complaint Exh.17. 7] PW2 is the elder sister of the victim. She also supported the prosecution and specifically deposed that at the time of incident she was sleeping alongwith victim on the ground. Her maternal uncle and aunt were sleeping on the cot. At about 03.00 a.m. the accused entered their hut and slept in between her and the victim. The accused touched the victim inappropriately, whereupon the victim raised alarm. Thereafter her maternal uncle and aunt woke­up. They caught hold the accused and took him to police station. 8] PW3 Hanmanta Rathod is the maternal uncle of the victim. He also supported the prosecution. He specifically deposed that the victim is the daughter of his sister. The family of his sister is residing in his neighbourhood at Karavegaon. They are residing adjacent to each other. The incident had occurred on 08.07.2014. Few days before the incident his sister and her husband had gone to their native place. On 08.07.2014 he, his wife, victim and her sister were sleeping in the house of victim. While he was sleeping on the cot alongwith his wife, the victim and her sister were sleeping J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 173­14 ­ 354, 12.doc .....6/­ ..6.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 173/2014.. Exh.30.. on the ground. At about 03.00 a.m. the accused slept in between the victim and her sister and moved his hand over the chest of victim. Thereupon the victim raised alarm. Hearing her alarm he woke­up and caught hold the accused. Thereafter the accused was taken to the police station. 9] The victim PW1 and her sister PW2 both have admitted in cross examination that at the time of incident the door of the hut was latched from inside. They further volunteered that the accused had broke open the door of said hut. PW3 Hanmanta Rathod has deposed that as the hut was made of plastic paper, it cannot be locked from inside. Relying upon this contradiction in the evidence of witnesses, advocate Mr.Mokal argued that the evidence of witnesses is not reliable. PW1, PW2 and PW3 have admitted in their cross examinations that the accused was not residing in their vicinity. They further admitted that they were not acquainted with the accused and had not even seen him prior to the incident. Relying upon these facts, advocate Mr.Mokal argued that it is not reliable that the accused entered the hut of unknown person and committed alleged act. PW3 has admitted in his cross examination that by the side of the hut i.e. the spot of incident there is a road proceeding to liquor shop. Relying upon the said fact advocate Mr.Mokal argued that as stated by the accused he was drunken at the time of incident. As he had J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 173­14 ­ 354, 12.doc .....7/­ ..7.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 173/2014.. Exh.30.. created nuisance in the vicinity of the spot of incident, he was beaten by the maternal uncle of the victim. In said beating accused had sustained bleeding injuries. In order to avoid prosecution on complaint by accused, false complaint came to be lodged against him. 10] It is admitted fact that the accused was not at all acquainted with the victim and other witnesses. Under such circumstances there is no reason to concoct false story against the accused. So far as assaulting the accused for creating nuisance is concerned, said fact is not established in the evidence of any of the witness. The fact that accused was manhandled after the incident can be confirmed from the photograph of the accused which depict head injury. However, it cannot be said that the incident had occurred outside the hut and the accused had not at all misbehaved with the victim. The complaint and statement of victim is corroborated in detail particulars by PW2 and PW3. Under such circumstances the evidence of PW1, PW2 and PW3 cannot be discarded. 11] The prosecution has examined P.S.I., Arvind Sankhe as Pw4 at Exh.21. He has deposed that on 08.07.2014 he was attached to N.R.I. police station and was on night duty from 09.00 p.m .to 09.00 a.m. on next day. On that night at J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 173­14 ­ 354, 12.doc .....8/­ ..8.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 173/2014.. Exh.30.. about 03.00 to 03.30 a.m. he received phone call of P.S.O. who informed him that there was some incident in Seawood area. Accordingly he had been to Seawood, Gaymukh outpost. At that time the accused was already taken to said outpost and he was manhandled. On inquiry the victim, her sister and maternal uncle narrated the incident. Thereafter the victim and others were taken to N.R.I. police station. Head Constable Damde recorded the complaint and handed over investigation to him (PW4). He verified said complaint Exh.17. Accused was arrested and arrest panchanama Exh.22 was carried out by HC Damde. Thereafter he visited spot of incident on the same day and carried out panchanama Exh.23. He recorded statement of witnesses. As there was no birth certificate of the victim, he got examined her in Vashi Hospital for confirmation of age. He also recorded the statement of victim u/s.164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. He received medical certificate showing age of victim as 15 to 16 years. During investigation he recorded statement of PW2 and PW3 on 10.07.2014 and 11.07.2014 respectively. 12] This witness is also cross examined in detail. He also admitted that there are liquor shops and bars in the slum area of Karavegaon. He further admitted that the medical examination of the victim was carried out after two months for confirmation of her age. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 173­14 ­ 354, 12.doc .....9/­ ..9.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 173/2014.. Exh.30.. 13] The prosecution has examined Dr.Babasaheb Patil of N.M.M.C. General Hospital, Vashi as PW5 at Exh.26. He deposed that on 08.09.2014 the victim girl was produced by women PC Kadam of N.R.I. police station. He conducted general examination and obtained x­rays. On examination of x­rays the age of the victim was revealed as 15 to 16 years approximately. Accordingly he issued certificate Exh.27. In cross examination this witness has admitted that the ossification test is based on guess and fusion of joints. 14] Relying upon the cross examination of Investigating Officer PW4 and Medical Officer PW5 advocate Mr.Mokal argued that the accused was manhandled for creating nuisance in the vicinity of hut of the victim. He had sustained injuries. Therefore, in order to avoid own prosecution the maternal uncle of the victim got registered a false complaint. Advocate Mr.Mokal further argued that though all witnesses were present on 09.07.2014, statements of PW2 and PW3 are falsely prepared later on. The age of the victim is not duly proved. The test being guess work is not a conclusive evidence about the minority of the victim. 15] It is pertinent to note here that after the incident the accused was taken to the police outpost by the maternal uncle of the victim and others. Considering the nature of J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 173­14 ­ 354, 12.doc .....10/­ ..10.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 173/2014.. Exh.30.. incidents, manhandling of the accused is natural reaction. Under such circumstances it cannot be said that the accused is falsely implicated in such a incident. So far as age of the victim is concerned, it is based on the medical test. It being opinion of an expert, it cannot be discarded in toto. Therefore, arguments of advocate Mr.Mokal are not sustainable. The presence of witnesses i.e. PW2 and PW3 is mentioned in F.I.R. itself. Under such circumstances delay in recording their statements is not fatal. 16] Thus from unshattered evidence of the victim which is corroborated by PW2 and PW3, incident of sexual assault is duly proved. Through independent scientific evidence the age of victim is also proved. The prosecution has proved beyond reasonable doubt that the accused sexually assaulted the victim girl by touching her breast inappropriately. Hence I answer point No.1 in affirmative. 17] As accused is held guilty for the offence, he is to be heard on the quantum of sentence. Hence the Judgment is hereby deferred to hear the accused on the quantum of sentence. Thane. (P.P.Jadhav) District Judge­6 and Date : 08.09.2017. Addl. Sessions Judge, Thane. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 173­14 ­ 354, 12.doc .....11/­ ..11.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 173/2014.. Exh.30.. 18] Heard leaned A.P.P. Shri.Kulkarni for state. .. 1 .. Special Case no.174/2014 judgment Received on : 10.09.2014 Registered on : 10.09.2014 Decided on : 30.03.2015 Duration : 6 months 20 days In The Court of the Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012, Thane) At Thane (Presided over by Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Case No. 174 of 2014 Exhibit No. 05 The State of Maharashtra … Complainant versus Samsher Nudhuddi Shaikh … Accused Age 32 years, Resident of Handi compound, behind public toilet, Bhiwandi. JUDGMENT (Delivered on 30.03.2015.) .. 2 .. Special Case no.174/2014 judgment The accused stands prosecuted for the offence punishable under section 509 of I.P.C. and section 11 read with section 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short ''P.O.C.S.O. Act'') for subjecting minor girl to sexual harassment. 2] In short the facts giving rise to the prosecution of the accused are that on 07.09.2013 at 6.30p.m. the victim girl namely Arati Ambadas Bitla aged 16 years had gone to the handpump which was there in front of their residential chawl to fetch water. When she was pumping water, she noticed that one unknown person was standing in the window of the building of the powerloom factory which was near the said handpump and said person was looking at her and thereafter she saw that said person was holding mobile phone in his hand in a manner that he was clicking her photograph and then he clicked her photograph by said mobile phone and also blinked an eye at her. She therefore raised shouts and hearing her shouts the some persons gathered there and she narrated them the incident of clicking photograph and blinking of eye by said person. It is further case of prosecution that the persons gathered there then searched for the said person and accosted him and also beat him at that time and by that time the police persons on patrolling duty arrived at the spot took the said person into custody. Thereafter the victim lodged complaint against the accused. .. 3 .. Special Case no.174/2014 judgment 3] On the basis of her complaint offence under section 509 of I.P.C. and also under section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act was registered as per C.R.No. II-53/2013 at Bhoiwada police station and the work of investigation was entrusted to P.S.I. Nikam. During the investigation panchnama of the spot was prepared. Statements of witnesses including victim girl were recorded. Copy of school leaving certificate of the girl showing her date of birth was obtained and after completion of investigation, since there was sufficient evidence against the accused, he was charge-sheeted for offence punishable under section 509 of I.P.C. and section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and the charge sheet was submitted to the Special Court since provisions of P.O.C.S.O. Act are applied. 4] The accused was produced from jail. A charge under section 509 of I.P.C. and section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act was framed against the accused as per Exh.3. The contents of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. He pleaded guilty and accepted the charges levelled against him and prayed for leniency while awarding the punishment. 5] On above the points which arose for my determination and my findings and reasons for the same are as under - Points Findings i ) Does the prosecution prove that on 07.09.2013 at 6.30 p.m. near the water handpump at Dudhbavdi, Bhiwandi, the .. 4 .. Special Case no.174/2014 judgment accused, intending to insult the modesty of minor girl named Arati Ambadas Bitla made gesture by blinking eye at said minor girl and also clicked her photograph by his mobile phone, intending that his said gesture shall be seen by said minor girl ? Yes. ii ) Does the prosecution prove that the accused on the given day, date, time and place, the accused, intending to insult the modesty of minor girl named Arati Ambadas Bitla made gesture by blinking eye at said minor girl and also clicked her photograph by his mobile phone, intending that his said gesture shall be seen by said minor girl and thereby subjected her to sexual harassment ? Yes. iii ) What offence, if any, is proved against Both offences the accused ? are proved. iv ) What order ? The accused is convicted. REASONS 6] As is clear the offence charge against the accused is under section 509 of I.P.C. and section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act with the allegation that the accused had sexually harassed minor girl Arati Bitla by behaving in indecent manner and making obscene gesture by blinking an eye at her intending that said gesture shall be seen by her and also clicked her photograph in his mobile phone. Even it is also clear from the complaint lodged by the complainant that very specific allegations are made against the accused and on that basis offence under section 509 of I.P.C. and section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act are charged .. 5 .. Special Case no.174/2014 judgment against the accused and the accused has been prosecuted for the said offence. Then, as is clear the accused pleaded guilty and accepted the charges for the offence charged. Then, even as per provisions of section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act a person is said to commit sexual harassment upon a child when such person with sexual intent utters any word or makes any sound, or makes any gesture or exhibits any object or part of body with the intention that such word or sound shall be heard, or such gesture or object or part of body shall be seen by the child and looking to the allegations made against the accused and in the light of the fact that he has pleaded guilty and accepted the charges so levelled against him, it has to be held as proved that the accused has committed offence under section 509 of I.P.C. and section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and he is liable to be convicted for the said charge. I therefore hold the accused guilty for commission of offence under section 509 of I.P.C. and section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and convict him for the said offence. 7] At this stage the dictation of the Judgment is postponed for hearing the accused on the point of sentence. Date : 30.03.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From sexual Offences Act, 2012) Thane. Resumed. 8] The accused is made aware of the fact that he is held guilty for the offence under section 509 of I.P.C. and section 11 .. 6 .. Special Case no.174/2014 judgment read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and the punishment prescribed for offence under section 509 of I.P.C. is imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and also with fine and offence under section 12 read with section12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act is punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine. 9] I heard the learned A.P.P. and the accused on the point of sentence. The learned A.P.P. submitted that looking to the serious nature of offence charged against the accused he is not entitled to leniency and he is liable to award maximum punishment prescribed. The accused prayed for showing him leniency on the ground that there is nobody in his family to look after his family and he is the only earning member in his family and it is his first offence and he be punished with imprisonment of the term already undergone. 10] Then, as is clear though the offence charged against the accused is of very serious nature, the allegations are only that he blinked an eye at said minor girl and clicked her photograph. But then, the fact is also clear and has been stated by the accused that he is the only bread earner in his family and his family is depending upon him. 12] Then, so far as quantum of punishment is concerned, .. 7 .. Special Case no.174/2014 judgment Section 42 of the P.O.C.S.O. Act provides : ''Where an act or omission constitutes an offence punishable under this Act and also under sections 166A, 354A, 354B, 354C, 354D, 370, 370A, 375, 376, 376A, 376C, 376D, 376E or section 509 of the Indian Penal Code, then notwithstanding anything contained in any law for the time being in force, the offender found guilty of such offence shall be liable to punishment under this Act or under the Indian Penal Code as provides for punishment which is greater in degree''. Then, as is clear the offence under section 509 of I.P.C. is punishable with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and also with fine whereas offence under section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act is punishable with imprisonment which may extend to three years and also with fine. As such it is clear that sentence of only simple imprisonment can be awarded for commission offence under section 509 of I.P.C. whereas since it is not specified in section 12 about nature of imprisonment, sentence of imprisonment of either description i.e. S.I. or R.I. can be awarded for commission of offence under section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and therefore it can be said that as per provisions of section 42 of P.O.C.S.O. Act substantive sentence only for offence punishable under section 11 read with section 12 which is imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years and also fine has to be awarded to the accused. 11] In all such circumstance I am of the view that following sentence would meet ends of justice. In the result I pass .. 8 .. Special Case no.174/2014 judgment the following order - ORDER Accused namely Samsher Nudhuddi Shaikh is convicted for the offence punishable under section 509 of the Indian Penal Code and also for offence under section 11 read with 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and by invoking provisions of Section 42 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012, the accused is sentenced to suffer Rigorous Imprisonment for the term of the period of detention undergone by him during the investigation, inquiry and trial and also to pay fine of Rs.500/- [rupees five hundred only] and in default to pay fine amount, he is sentenced to suffer S.I. for fifteen days, for commission of offence punishable under section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act only. ii ) The accused is in jail since 07.09.2014. A set off under section 428 of the Cr.P.C. is granted to him for the term of the period of detention undergone by him during the investigation, inquiry and trial against the substantive sentence imposed upon him. iii ) Since no muddemal property is produced before Court, no order in regard to its disposal is passed. iv ) Copy of judgment be given to the accused free of cost. vii ) The proceeding is closed. Date : 30.03.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012) Thane. .. 9 .. Special Case no.174/2014 judgment

.. 1 .. bail no.1965/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 1965/2015 This application is filed by applicant Mohammad Zuber Shaikh for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no.I­672/2015 registered at Mumbra police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 363 of I.P.C. and section 18 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant induced and kidnapped the minor daughter of the complainant. It is further contended and argued that no such incident of kidnapping as alleged has happened. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co­operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that at the time of incident the victim girl was going to the house of her grandmother situated at Jeevanbag, Mumbra and thereafter she went missing. It .. 2 .. bail no.1965/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) is further contended and argued that the applicant/accused taking disadvantage of young age of the girl, had enticed her and kidnapped her with ill intention. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl and the prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial.
