.. 1 .. Bail No. 1969/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) Criminal Bail Application No. 1969/2015. Alauddin Noorusalam Mandal .. Applicant versus The State of Maharashtra Through Kashimira Police Station .. Non­applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 1] By this application the applicant is seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C., who was arrested on 08.06.2015 by Kashimira Police Station in connection with C.R.No.I­292/2015 registered for an offence punishable under section 306, 376 of I.P.C. and section 4, 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Mr.Fakhruddin for the applicant/accused and learned A.P.P. Mrs. R.A.Navale for State. I.O. present after issuance of show cause notice. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 08.06.2015 at the instance of the informant/mother of the deceased Jahanara with an indictment that before four months her daughter left her house with accused and was staying with him as his wife and accused used to frequently quarrel with her daughter without any reason .. 2 .. Bail No. 1969/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) and therefore, her daughter committed suicide due to the accused. Therefore, the report came to be lodged. 4] The learned Counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant­accused is falsely implicated. He submitted that F.I.R. came to be registered only on hearsay evidence. He submitted that the informant did not have any knowledge and only learnt through her minor son and on that basis the report was lodged. He further submitted that informant mentioned age of the her deceased daughter as 20 years while lodging the F.I.R. However, the provisions of P.O.C.S.O. A ct were added later on stating the victim was minor. He submitted that in fact there was love affair between the deceased and the accused and the deceased on her own ran away with the accused prior to four months and they were staying happily. No complaint was ever lodged by the victim­girl within the period of these four months. He submitted that there is no evidence to show that the deceased committed suicide due to the accused. He further submitted that the F.I.R. is doubtful. He submitted that the ossification test of the accused was conducted, according to which his age is between 18 to 20 years. he further submitted that if the margin of two years is taken into consideration, then accused is minor and therefore, his case is required to be tried before Juvenile Court. He further submitted that the accused is behind bars since five months. This is his first bail application. The accused is permanent resident of the address given in the application. He is ready to abide by any conditions imposed by the Court including heavy surety and prayed for releasing him on bail. .. 3 .. Bail No. 1969/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) 5] Per contra, the learned A.P.P. opposed the application submitted that the birth certificate of the victim­girl is on record according to which she was aged about 15 years, therefore her consent is of no consequences. She further submitted that the statement of brother of the victim­girl is recorded who stated that there were frequent quarrels between accused and his deceased sister. She further submitted that the D.N.A. report is awaited, however, there is prima facie case against the accused. There are chances of tampering of witnesses and prayed for rejection of application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of investigation papers it appears that the present bail application was pending since long as I.O. failed to file the say. During the pendency of this application the charge­sheet was filed in the Court. Upon perusal of charge­ sheet it appears that the F.I.R. came to be registered at the instance of mother of the deceased Jahanara who is not having any personal knowledge about her daughter. In the F.I.R. itself it is stated that her daughter left home before four months with the accused and since then she was not in contact with the informant. It is further pertinent to note that during this period of our months no missing complaint was lodged by the informant. Though charge­sheet is submitted in the Court, there is absolutely no evidence to substantiate the charge of sexual assault. Even the post mortem report is not on record. Only provisional cause of death certificate is filed with the charge­sheet according to which the cause of death .. 4 .. Bail No. 1969/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) is stated as asphyxia due to hanging. The charge­sheet is recently submitted and trial is yet to be commenced. Therefore, without making any further comment on the merit of the case, I find that as the investigation is already completed, there is no point in keeping the accused behind bars and no purpose would be served by his further incarceration. The object of bail is neither preventive nor punitive but to secure the presence of accused at the time of trial. The accused is ready to abide by any conditions imposed by the Court. The apprehension of A.P.P. can be addressed by imposing suitable conditions. Hence, I pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is allowed. 2) Applicant Alauddin Noorusalam Mandal Khan be released on bail on his executing P.R. Bond of ₹ 25,000/­ [rupees twenty five thousand only] with one or two local sureties in the like amount on the following conditions ­ A] Applicant shall not tamper with prosecution witnesses. B] Applicant shall furnish his and his two blood relatives' address proofs and contact numbers and he is duty bound to inform I.O. and Court about the change of address, if any. C] Applicant shall not contact and pressurize any other witnesses in any manner. Thane. Date : 17.11.2015. (Ms. U.M. Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act), Thane.

CNR No. MHTH01-005278-2014 Special Case No.177/2014 1 (Judgment) Presented on : 12.09.2014 Registered on : 12.09.2014 Decided on : 01.02.2018 Duration Y M D 03 03 20 IN THE COURT OF SESSIONS JUDGE­1 & SPECIAL JUDGE [POCSO] ACT, THANE AT : THANE (Presided over by V.V.Bambarde, Additional Sessions Judge­1 & Special Judge (POCSO) Act, Thane ) SPECIAL CASE NO.177/2014 [CNR No. MHTH01­005278­2014] EXH.No.31. State of Maharashtra ( Through Mumbra Police Stn. ) ...Complainant Vs. Shri. Abdullah Abdul Gani Shaikh, Age : 42 Yrs., R/o. Room No. 21, Second Floor, Yasmin Apartment, Rashid Compound, Near Ashrafiya Manzil, Kausa, Mumbra, Tal. Dist. Thane. ...Accused. Offence Punishable Under Sec.354, 506 of IPC and S.8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ Appearances : Shri. Londhe, Ld. Spl.P.P. for the State Mr. Iqbal Abdulla, Ld.Advocate for the accused ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ CNR No. MHTH01-005278-2014 2 Special Case No.177/2014 (Judgment) :JUDGMENT: (Delivered on 01st day of February, 2018) 1] The accused is charged and tried for offence punishable under Sec.354, 506 of IPC and Sec. 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 for having been committed offence of outraging modesty of minor victim girl, threatening to kill her and sexually assaulting her. 2] Case of prosecution, in brief, is that : The accused had a shop at Sabistan Chawl, Devripada, Kausa, Mumbra. The victim girl at around 20.30 hours on 29/05/2014 went to bring milk from the shop adjacent to the shop of the accused. The accused hold hand of victim girl, dragged her close to him and moved his hand on her breast. The accused expressed her that he likes her. The girl felt shy. The accused also threatened the girl that if she dare to disclose this fact to the family members, she would be killed. Mrs. Jarina Abutalik Sayyed, mother of the victim girl, went to police station and lodged FIR. 3] On the receipt of complaint, Mumbra police registered offence under Sec.354, 506 of IPC and S. 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Investigation was taken up by API­Jadhav. API­Jadhav registered crime. He went to the spot and prepared spot panchanama in the presence of panchas. API Jadhav recorded statement of victim girl. PSI Vikas Babar recorded statement of witnesses, collected birth certificate of victim girl. On finding substance in the accusation, PSO Mumbra Police Station filed charge sheet in the Court. 4] This Court has framed charge against the accused ( Exh.5 ) for CNR No. MHTH01-005278-2014 Special Case No.177/2014 3 (Judgment) the offence under Sec. 354, 506 of IPC and Sec. 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. The contents of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 5] The defence of the accused as constructed in cross­ examination and statement under Sec. 313 Cr.P.C. is of false implication in the case. 6] Prosecution examined three witnesses to bring home the guilt of accused. P.W.2 is victim girl. Her mother is examined as P.W.1 and P.W.3 is Mr. Vikas Babar, I.O. Prosecution marked exhibit birth certificate of victim girl as Exh. 20. The accused Mr. Abdulla Abdulgani Shaikh examined himself. He has filed photographs Articles D­1 to D­4. He has marked exhibit N.C. report – Exh. 28. 7] I have heard Ld. Special P.P. for the State and Ld. advocate for the accused. 8] The following points arise for my determination with my findings thereon for reasons to follow: POINTS FINDINGS 01. Does the prosecution prove that on ...In the affirmative. 29/05/2013 at 20.30 hours, at Sabistan Chawl, Devaripada, Kausa, Mumbra, the accused used criminal force with intent to outrage modesty of victim girl? 02. Does prosecution prove that the accused, on ...In the negative. the aforesaid date, time and place, CNR No. MHTH01-005278-2014 4 Special Case No.177/2014 (Judgment) intimidated the victim girl by threatening her to kill? 03. Does prosecution prove that the accused, on ...In the affirmative. the aforesaid date, time and place, assaulted victim girl with sexual intent? 04 What order ? Accused is convicted as per final order. REASONS 9] AS TO POINT NOS.1 TO 3: I would like to discuss all the points together being interlinked with each other. The victim girl has born on 18/12/2003. She was studying in Abdulla Patel School, Mumbra. The accused had a shop at Sabistan Chawl, Devripada, Kausa, Mumbra. The victim girl and accused are living in a very close vicinity. Zarina (P.W.1) sent her daughter to bring milk at 8 p.m. on 29/05/2014. Victim girl (P.W.2) deposed that accused caught her hand, twisted her cheek, moved his hand over her breast and back and dragged her towards him. She somehow rescued herself. The accused threatened her if she will dare to disclose this fact to anybody he will kill her. The accused also stated her that “Tum muze achhi lagti ho”. Zarina (P.W.1) deposed that she went to police station but she was called on next day. Police recorded her complaint Exh. 20. Vikas Babar (P.W.3) has drawn spot panchanama. Spot of offence is not disputed. The accused has filed photographs of his shop. It shows that it is on the road. There is usual traffic on the road. The victim has stated that the shop of accused is adjacent to the shop of milk. 10] I have heard Ld. Special P.P. and Ld. advocate for the accused. Ld. Advocate for the accused submitted that complaint is lodged against CNR No. MHTH01-005278-2014 Special Case No.177/2014 5 (Judgment) present accused deliberately. It is pointed out that son of Zarina Sayyed (P.W.1) is bodyguard of the then Corporator Samad Qureshi. Zarina (P.W.1) denied that her son is involved in criminal activities. The complaint ­ Exh. 19 is lodged at 3 a.m. Zarina (P.W.1) has stated that they have waited for inspector but he did not turn up. The complainant has lodged complaint and N.C.s after the incident. So that they do not carry importance. It is submitted that the girl had been to milk shop but accused had a stationery shop. It is pertinent to note that milk shop is adjacent to the shop of accused depicted in photographs filed by accused. 11] Ld. Advocate for the accused has placed reliance on authority John @ Vivek Ramesh Jadhav V/s The State of Maharashtra, 2015 ALL MR (Cri.) 4053. It is observed by Their Lordships that there is only substantial evidence of child. It was admitted position in that case was that the accused was the landlord of the chawl where in one of the rooms the parents of the victim girl reside as tenants. They had inimical relations. In the present case such is not a situation. Ld. Advocate for accused has placed reliance on another State of Rajasthan V/s Babu Meena, Criminal Appeal No. 570 of 2007. It is observed that oral testimony can be classified into three categories viz. (i) wholly reliable, (ii) wholly unreliable and (iii) neither wholly reliable nor wholly unreliable. In case of wholly reliable testimony of a single witness, the conviction can be founded without corroboration. The situation in present case is that a girl about 10 years has immediately disclosed to her mother that accused moved his hand over the girl. It is pointed out by Ld. advocate for the accused that there is always big usual crowd in the area. It appears that the girl had somehow rescued herself and without any hue and cry rushed abode. Usual crowd will not nullify her testimony as she preferred to rescue herself. Ld. Advocate for accused has placed reliance on authority Natasha Santosh CNR No. MHTH01-005278-2014 6 Special Case No.177/2014 (Judgment) Jagdhane V/s State of Maharashtra & others., Writ Petition No. 178 of 2017. What is ratio and how it is applicable is not pointed out. Ld. advocate for accused has also placed reliance on authority Ratha Jena V/s State of Orissa, 1986 Cri. L.J. 490. This authority is on lapses on the part of I.O. It is not helpful to the accused. It is deposed at the cost of repetition that the alleged report made by accused is after the incident so it is of no use. 12] I have carefully perused evidence of victim girl. She has no reason to depose against accused. The accused moved his hand on her breast, cheek and back. Ten years girl was grown up. She had sense of modesty. The moving of hand on inappropriate part of body shows sexual intention. But it was no so grave to cause her a serious sexual assault. 13] There seem no intent to cause alarm to victim girl as she rescued immediately. So there is no offence under S. 506 of IPC. Hence, I answer Point Nos. 1 and 3 in affirmative and point No.2 in negative. So offence under S. 354 and S. 8 of POCSO are attracted. Therefore, I hold accused guilty of offence under S. 354 of IPC and under S. 8 of POCSO Act. Here I take pause to hear the accused on the point of sentence. 14] I have heard the accused on the point of sentence. Accused submitted that he has a big family to maintain. If he is put behind the bars his reputation in the Society will be malign. Advocate for accused prayed to show leniency. Ld. APP prayed to give maximum punishment. Looking to the age of the girl and seriousness of offence, no benefit of Probation of Offenders Act or CNR No. MHTH01-005278-2014 Special Case No.177/2014 7 (Judgment) any leniency can be shown to the accused. In the result, I pass following order: ORDER 1] The accused Abdullah Abdul Gani Shaikh is hereby convicted of offence under S. 354 of IPC and is sentenced to suffer Simple Imprisonment of six months. 2] The accused is hereby convicted of offence under S. 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and is sentenced to suffer Simple Imprisonment of three years. 3] Both sentences shall run concurrently. 4] Accused is acquitted under S. 506 of IPC. 5] His bail bond stands cancelled. .. 1 .. Bail No. 1977/2015 Order below Exhibit 1. Order below Exhibit 1 in Anticipatory Bail Application No. 1977/2015 This application is filed by applicant Anand Ramdas Balla for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no.I-194/2015 registered at Shantinagar police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 376 read with section 34 of I.P.C. and section 3, 4 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act) and also under section 2 of Maharashtra Prevention and Eradication of Human Sacrifice and other Inhuman, Evil and Aghori Practices and Black Magic Act, 2013 (hereinafter in short referred to as ''Black Magic Act''). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that applicant and other accused induced the victim girl that they will cause the money to fall like rainfall for the victim girl by doing magic and thereby induced her to perform marriage with co-accused and thereafter the co-accused Salim Ansari committed rape on the minor victim girl. It is further contended and argued that the applicant is falsely implicated on suspicion and he has no concern at all with the present offence. It is further contended and argued that the applicant has not played any role in this offence and he only had given room and he was not knowing for what purpose his room is going to be used. It is further contended and argued that. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that the victim girl is from .. 2 .. Bail No. 1977/2015 Order below Exhibit 1. a very poor family and her father is working in loom factory at Bhiwandi and it is further contended that taking disadvantage of such situation, the accused persons had induced the victim girl that accused no.2 Salim Ansari will pay black magic and will cause showering of money like rainfall and for that purpose the victim will have to marry said accused. It is further contended and argued that thereafter said accused Salim Ansari married to victim girl and then he had sexual intercourse with her under false pretext. It is further contended and argued that the present applicant had provided room to the co-accused wherein the girl was raped. It is further contended and argued that all accused persons including the applicant were knowing that false representation is made to the victim girl and her father that money will fall like rainfall and it is further contended and argued that all accused in furtherance of their common intention have committed sexual assault on minor victim girl by inducing her by telling that by use of black magic there will be showing of money. It is further contended and argued that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the complainant and her family members and may tamper with prosecution evidence. It is also contended and argued that the applicant/accused he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant/accused is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, the offences charged against the applicant/ accused is are serious nature under section 376 read with section 34 of I.P.C. and section 3, 4 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and also under section 2 of Black Magic Act, 2013 with the allegation that all accused persons including the applicant in furtherance of their common intention had made false representation to the victim girl who is stated to be 17 years old that they will shower money by playing black magic and for that .. 3 .. Bail No. 1977/2015 Order below Exhibit 1. purpose they induced her to marry accused no.2 Salim Ansari and thereafter said accused married to her and then committed sexual assault on her under false pretext and the applicant had provided room wherein the alleged offences have been committed. 4] Then, though it is argued on behalf of applicant that role of the present applicant in the crime is limited only to the extent that he had provided room to the main accused for the alleged illegal activities, the fact cannot be ignored and overlooked that the applicant is also stated to have given his room for all meetings in hatching conspiracy. Even it is also clear from the papers of investigation and statements of witnesses recorded during investigation that the applicant also had participated in the meetings and gave his premises for the purpose of performing nikah of the minor girl and at this stage when the investigation is in regard to progress, it would be premature to conclude that the applicant do not have active role in the alleged crime. 5] Even so far as submission on behalf of applicant that the applicant/accused is not there in the F.I.R. and the entire story is concocted and developed later on during investigation etc. is concerned it has to be mentioned that the fact is also kept to be kept in mind that the allegations are that all the accused including the applicant conspired together and indulged into activity of causing the money to fall like rainfall and it is well settled that conspiracy is to be judged on the basis of facts and circumstances and there may not be any direct evidence in regard to conspiracy. Even the submissions on behalf of accused that he is arrested only as co-accused and his role is minor and therefore he is entitled to be released on bail also it is to be mentioned that, as discussed above, role of the applicant is not restricted to only giving premises and even it is to be mentioned that .. 4 .. Bail No. 1977/2015 Order below Exhibit 1. giving premises for such activities itself is major role and it would be premature to conclude at this stage that the applicant was not having any knowledge as to what activities are being carried out in his premises. It is also to be mentioned that the offences charged are of very serious nature and they are stated to have been committed in a very different and unique manner and thorough investigation into the matter is necessary. In such circumstance when the investigation is in progress and it would hamper the investigation if the applicant is released on bail at this stage. For the same reason the observation in the ruling cited on behalf of applicant in case of Krishnaiah s/o Mudaiah vs. State reported in Criminal Petition No. 3486/2014 C/W Criminal Petition No. 3497/2014 that ''As the material produced by the prosecution goes to show that these petitioners only assisted the accused no.1 and allegations that they helped the accused no.1 in getting rented house and also taking victim girl in the car. The said offence are not exclusively punishable by death or imprisonment for life and these petitioners have undertaken to abide by any reasonable conditions to (may) be imposed by this court. Hence by imposing stringent conditions to secure the presence of the present petitioners they can be admitted to bail '' cannot be said to be of any help to the applicant/accused in this case at this stage. 6] Then, though it is well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail, besides that the gravity and serious nature of offence and the manner in which it is stated to have been committed has to be looked into and looking to the nature of offence and the manner in which it is alleged to have .. 5 .. Bail No. 1977/2015 Order below Exhibit 1. been committed, a wrong message would be sent to the society in case of release of accused on bail in such type of matter wherein serious allegations of sexual assault on a minor girl are made. 7] Even the apprehension expressed by the prosecution that the accused may threaten and pressurize the girl and her family members is well founded and even the possibility of accused being absconded and not available for trial cannot be ruled out. 8] In all such circumstance looking to the serious nature of offence and the manner in which it is stated to have been committed, I am of the view that this is not a fit case wherein the applicant/accused can be said to be entitled to be released on bail at this stage. I therefore pass the following order - ORDER The application is rejected. Date : 04.09.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Additional Session Judge-1, Thane.

She was stopped at bus stop situated near Saint Xavier's school to catch a bus to go to her college. Then the accused followed her and the accused no.1 uttered the words “Too Fukat Ka Natak Karti Hai, Too Aaj College Kaise Jaati Hai Mai Dekhata Hoo” and caught her hand and also moved his hand on her breasts likely to cause her to shy or create shame in her mind. The accused nos.3 and 4 also uttered the words “Nakhare Mat Kar Bhari Padega”. So, the complainant ..3/­ 3 Spl.Case No. 202/2016 [ Judg. ] Priya filed complaint against the accused, out of which accused Pankaj Pandit @ Pankaj Chandrashekhar Mishra and Salman Niyaj Ahmed Qureshi are. 3] The police registered a crime at serial No. I­ 707/2015 against the accused under secs. 354(D), 504, 506 read with 34 of the Indian Penal Code and sec. 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. 4] The police carried out necessary investigation of the crime and after its completion the police filed the chargesheet against the accused Pankaj and Salman under secs. 354(D), 504, 506 read with 34 of the Indian Penal Code and sec. 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. 5] The accused appeared before the court. I framed chargesheet against the accused under secs. 354(D), 504, 506 read with 34 of the Indian Penal Code and sec. 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act at Exh.5. The contents of the said charge came to be read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. The accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. The defence of the accused is of total denial. 6] As to bring home the guilt of the accused, the prosecution examined (PW 1) Mantu Brijnath Yadav the ..4/­ 4 Spl.Case No. 202/2016 [ Judg. ] father of the victim girl at Exh.19. (PW 1) the father stated in his evidence before the court that, his daughter Priya got married after the incident and she is passing her marital life with her husband in U.P. in a happy way. So, it is his contention that, if his daughter Priya came to be called by the court for her evidence in the present matter which is somewhat serious and likely to affect her marital life adversely. So, he prayed to close the matter here only. Considering the urge of the father of the victim girl and the delicate situation, I thought it better to close the matter here only. Accordingly, the prosecution evidence came to be closed by the court without examination of the victim girl Priya. 7] This court closed the evidence of the prosecution as per its order dt. 27/2/2017. I recorded the statements of the accused under sec. 313 of Cr.P.C.. The accused did not state any reason as to why they came to be prosecuted by the prosecution. They both denied commission of the crime. 8] I heard the learned APP Shri Kadu. I also heard the respective defence advocates Smt. Pooja Singh for accused no.1 and Shri Jogendra Thakur for accused No.2. 9] Following points arise for my determination and I record my findings against each of them for the reasons stated therefor. ..5/­ 5 Spl.Case No. 202/2016 [ Judg. ] POINTS FINDINGS 1] Whether prosecution prove that, the accused nos.1 and 2 alongwith absconding accused namely Najib Shaikh and Shahrukh Shaikh on 14/12/2015 at about 12.30 p.m. at Mauje Kashigaon, on St. Not proved. Zavier Bus stop of Mandavi Pada, Kashimira, Dist­Thane, within the jurisdiction of Kashimira police station, in furtherance of their common intention, used criminal force to complainant namely Kum. Priya Mantu Yadav, a minor age­17 years, intending to outrage her modesty and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 354(D) read with 34 of the Indian Penal Code ? 2] Whether prosecution prove that, the accused nos.1 and 2 alongwith absconding accused Not proved. Najib Shaikh and Shahrukh Shaikh on the aforesaid date, time and place, in furtherance of their common intention, intentionally insulted the complainant namely Kum. Priya Mantu Yadav, a minor age­17 years by abusing her in filthy language and thereby gave provocation to her to break public peace and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 504 ..6/­ 6 Spl.Case No. 202/2016 [ Judg. ] read with 34 of the Indian penal Code ? 3] Whether prosecution prove that, the accused nos.1 and 2 alongwith absconding accused Najib Shaikh and Shahrukh Not proved. Shaikh on the aforesaid period and place, in furtherance of their common intention, committed criminal intimidation by threatening to victim complainant Kum. Priya, a minor age­17 years with intention to cause alarm to her and that the accused thereby committed an offence punishable under section 506 read with 34 of the Indian Penal Code ? 4] Whether prosecution prove that, the accused nos.1 and 2 alongwith absconding accused Najib Shaikh and Shahrukh Shaikh on the aforesaid period and place, in furtherance of Not proved. their common intention, committed sexual assault on complainant namely Kum. Priya Mantu Yadav, a minor age – 17 years and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act ? 5] What order ? As per final order. ..7/­ 7 Spl.Case No. 202/2016 [ Judg. ] REASONS 10] POINT NOS.1 TO 4 :­ As all the points are interlinked, I have taken them together for my determination. 11] The prosecution examined (PW 1) Mantu Brijnath Yadav the father of the victim girl Priya at Exh.19. On perusal of his evidence, it appears to me that, on 14/12/2015 one person Najib alongwith other 4­5 persons including the accused threatened to his daughter Priya in his presence. It is also his contention that, on 15/12/2015 his daughter Priya was present at a bus stop located near St. Xavier's school located within the jurisdiction of Kashimira police station where from he received phone call of his daughter Priya about the shameful conduct of the accused with Priya and when he went there the same persons absconded from the spot. It means there is every likelihood of witnessing the incident dt. 15/12/2015 by others who were present at the bus stop. Moreover, as per the request of (PW 1) Mantu Yadav this court did not think it better and just to call Priya in witness box as her marriage has been taken place after the incident and she is passing her marital life with her husband in a happy way. So, it is his submission that, his daughter Priya may not be called before the court for her evidence as the married life of Priya is likely to have adverse effect. So, this court closed the prosecution evidence and the learned ..8/­ 8 Spl.Case No. 202/2016 [ Judg. ] APP also filed purshis at Exh.17 in that regard. So, the main witness Priya is remained to be examined before the court and (PW 1) did not witness the incident. 12] In his cross­examination also (PW 1) has stated that, he only found both the accused present with the other accused Najib who is not traced out yet and seeing both the accused present with the other accused Najib the complainant suspected that the accused are likely to have concern in commission of the crime. Mere presence of the accused on the spot with other accused Najib is not sufficient to come to the conclusion that, the accused committed any offence against the daughter of the complainant Priya. This witness further admitted that, at the time of the incident he was present at home. So, it is apparent that, the complainant did not witness the incident. 13] So, when the star witness Priya is not coming before the court to depose about the incident which alleged to be occurred with her, it is unsafe to hold that, the accused committed any offence with Priya the daughter of (PW 1). Therefore, there is no iota of evidence against the accused to prove the charges levelled against the accused. 14] In his evidence (PW 1) did not state in what manner the accused threatened to his daughter Priya in his evidence before the court. So, no charge levelled against the ..9/­ 9 Spl.Case No. 202/2016 [ Judg. ] accused is proved against the accused. So, I record my findings to point nos.1 to 4 in the negative. 15] Considering my finding to point nos.1 to 4 and the reasons stated therefor, the accused deserve for acquittal of the charges under secs. 354(D), 504, 506 read with 34 of the Indian Penal Code and sec. 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. Hence, I proceed to pass the following order. ORDER 1] The accused No.1] Pankaj Pandit @ Pankaj Chandrashekhar Mishra, age 22 years and No.2] Salman Niyaz Ahmed Qureshi, age 23 years, both R/at Kashimira, Dist­Thane are hereby acquitted as per the provision under section 235(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure of the offences punishable under sections 354(D), 504, 506 read with 34 of the Indian Penal Code and under section 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act. 2] The bail bonds executed by the accused are cancelled. Surety are discharged. 3] The accused are directed to furnish fresh P.B. & S.B. of Rs.5,000/­each in compliance with the provisions of section 437(A) of Cr.P.C. to abide themselves to appear before Appellate Court in case of appeal is preferred by the prosecution. Bail No.1980/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exhibit 1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 1980/2015 This application is filed by applicant Mrs. Shabbo Singh for her release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with C.R.no.I-190/2015 registered at Mira Road police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 366A, 372, 373 read with section 34 of I.P.C. and section 4, 9 of Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act (hereinafter in short referred to as I.T.P.A.) and also under section 4, 6, 14, 17 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as P.O.C.S.O. Act). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant in furtherance of common intention with co-accused compelled minor girl who is her niece to do prostitution and earned money from said business. It is contended by the applicant that she is paternal aunt of the girl and she has not concern with this crime and the mother of the girl herself had forced the girl to do prostitution. It is further contended and argued that the girl was in love with one Naresh Mahalinge and had run away with her and she got pregnant from said Naresh and had aborted her pregnancy. It is further contended and argued that the applicant is falsely implicated in this crime. It is further submitted that co- accused Surjit Singh who is father of the victim girl has been ordered to be released on bail and therefore on the ground of parity the applicant/accused is also entitled to be released on bail. It is further submitted that now the investigation is completed and even charge-sheet is also submitted and there is no need of further custody of the applicant/accused. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the .. 2 .. Bail No.1980/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) present applicant/accused is released on bail, she will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will attend the Court regularly for the purpose of trial and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that the applicant is paternal aunt of the victim girl aged 16 years and other accused are father and grandmother of the victim girl and it is further contended that all accused in furtherance of common intention had compelled the victim girl to indulge in prostitution. It is further contended and argued that co-accused Rajesh had also demanded for sexual pleasure for himself and had forced her to do prostitution with customers. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening and pressurizing the victim girl and prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if released on bail, the applicant may abscond and will not be available for trial and may again indulge in such activity. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/ accused are of serious nature under section 366A, 372, 373 read with section 34 of I.P.C. and section 4, 9 of I.T.P.A. and also under section 4, 5, 14, 17 of P.O.C.S.O. Act with the allegation that the accused had forced minor girl aged 16 years to do prostitution, it is the contention of the applicant/accused that no active role is attributed to the applicant and she has no concern with .. 3 .. Bail No.1980/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) this crime. Then, though as per prosecution case the girl was forced to do prostitution in Orchestra Bar, it is contended on behalf of applicant that the girl had love affair with one Naresh Mahalinge and she had run away with said Naresh Mahalinge and had even got pregnant from said Naresh and her pregnancy was also aborted. In such circumstance whether the allegations against the accused that she had forced the girl to do prostitution or the contention of the accused that she is falsely implicated, are true or not, would be the question to be decided on merits. 4] Then, it is also clear that the applicant is a woman and is in jail since 07.05.2015 and her first bail application was rejected for the reason that the investigation was in progress at that time. But now the investigation is stated to have completed and charge-sheet has also been submitted and nothing is stated to be recovered from the applicant/accused. Then, as rightly submitted by the applicant, co-accused Surjit Singh has been ordered to be released on bail and therefore the applicant is also entitled to be released on bail on the ground of parity. 5] Then, it is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if she is released on bail. In that respect it is contended by the applicant that she is permanent resident of the address given and she will not abscond and that she is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. .. 4 .. Bail No.1980/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) 6] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 7] Then, it has also to be mentioned that though the investigation in the matter is completed and the charge-sheet is also submitted, it would take time to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 8] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order - ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Mrs. Shabbo Singh is released on P.R. bond of Rs.20,000/- [rupees twenty thousand only] with one or two local sureties in the like amount, subject to following conditions - She shall not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize her and other prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. She shall not abscond and shall attend the Court regularly for the purpose of trial. .. 5 .. Bail No.1980/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) She shall not leave India without permission of this Court. She shall furnish proof of her residence. Date : 21.09.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Additional Session Judge-1, Thane.

Offence Punishable Under Sec. 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ Appearances : Shri. S.D.Londhe, Ld. Spl.P.P. for the State Mr. Azim Shaikh, Ld.Advocate for the accused ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ :JUDGMENT: (Delivered on 22nd day of February, 2017) 1] The accused is charged and tried for offence punishable under 2 Special Case No.68/2013 (Judgment) Sec. 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 for being outraging the modesty of minor victim girl. 2] Case of prosecution in brief is that prosecutrix and her elder sister were at home at Mahesh Apartment, Plot No. 23­A/B, Sector 5, Ghansoli, Navi Mumbai on 25/07/2013. Their parents were out of station. Prosecutrix and her elder sister were going to have dinner at the house of Manoj Singh in the same building at 10.10 p.m. The accused is watchman. The accused was asked to leave the girls in Apartment 'C'­ 103. The accused took advantage of dark and put hand on the shoulder of girl and moved the second hand on the breast of the victim girl. The accused also tried to kiss her. The victim girl gave jerk. She rang the bell. The accused ran away. 3] On the receipt of complaint, Koparkhairne Police registered offence under S. 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Spot panchanama was drawn. API P.G.Pawar recorded statement of witnesses. Lady Police Sub Inspector ­V.U.Kamble recorded statement of victim. The accused was arrested on 26/07/2013. On completion of investigation, charge sheet was filed in the Court. 4] This Court has framed charge against the accused ( Exh.5 ) for the offence under Sec. 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. The contents of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 5] The defence of the accused as constructed in cross­ examination and statements under Sec. 313 Cr.P.C. is of false implication 3 Special Case No.68/2013 (Judgment) in the case. 6] I have heard Ld. Special P.P. for the State and Ld. advocate for the accused. 7] The following points arise for my determination with my findings thereon for reasons to follow: POINTS FINDINGS 01. Does the prosecution prove that on Not proved. 25/07/2013 at 10.10 hours, at Mahesh Apartment, in the stair­case of 'C' Wing, Ghansoli, the accused with sexual intent touched breast and other parts of the girl's body? 02 What order ? Accused is acquitted as per final order. REASONS 8] AS TO POINT NO.1: Prosecution examined three witnesses to bring home the guilt of accused. Laxmi Kurdiya (P.W.1) and Meghraj Kurdiya (P.W.3) are parents of the victim girl. Mr. Pramod Pawar (P.W.2) is investigating Officer. The victim and her family were residing at Mahesh Apartment, Sector 5, Ghansoli, Navi Mumbai. The accused is watchman in the same Society. It has come in the evidence of parents of the victim that they went to Rajasthan on 08/07/2013. They received call at 10.30 p.m. on 25/07/2013. They were informed that accused misbehaved with their daughter. 9] It has come in the evidence of Laxmi (P.W.1) that they do not 4 Special Case No.68/2013 (Judgment) want to bring their daughter Pooja in the Court. Meghraj (P.W.3) deposed that he does not want to put his daughters on stress by bringing them in the Court. Whatever evidence of Laxmi (P.W.1) and Meghraj (P.W.3) is of hearsay evidence. They have heard from their daughters that accused misbehaved with her. Mr. Pramod Pawar (P.W.2), I.O., has recorded statement of witnesses and filed charge sheet. 10] The evidence of Laxmi (P.W.1) and Meghraj (P.W.3) is hearsay evidence. There is nothing incriminating against accused. Hence, I find it just to answer Point No.1 in negative and pass following order : ORDER 1] The accused Raju Rajaram Pal is hereby acquitted under S. 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act,2012. 2] His bail bond stands cancelled. 3] Accused shall furnish P.R. bond of Rs. 15,000/­ in view of proviso 437(A) of Cr.P.C. Thane ( V.V.Bambarde ) Dt. :­ 22.02.2017 Additional Sessions Judge­2, vsi­p.c. & Special Judge (POCSO) Act, Thane. 5 Special Case No.68/2013 (Judgment)

No. 1995/2015 This application is filed by applicant namely Shabana Bano alias Parveen Sayeed Shaikh for her release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with C.R.No.I-347/2015 registered at Mumbra Police Station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 366A, 370, 376 read with section 34 of I.P.C. and section 5, 9 of Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act (hereinafter in short referred to as I.T.P.A.) and also under section 3, 4, 16 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as P.O.C.S.O. Act). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that applicant/accused compelled complainant/victim girl to do prostitution and earned money from said business. It is further contended and argued that wanted accused namely Beli had addicted the complainant girl to consumption of intoxicant powder i.e. MD powder, and while carrying the MD powder the girl was taken into custody by the police. It is further contended and argued that said Beli was also compelling the complainant girl to do prostitution to earn money. It is further contended and argued that the girl for doing prostitution voluntarily for her survival and the applicant has no concern with said activity and the applicant is falsely implicated in this crime. It is further submitted that co-accused Mohammad Saeed Shaikh, who is husband of present applicant, has already been ordered to be released on bail and therefore the present applicant entitled to be released on bail on the ground parity. It is further submitted that .. 2 .. Bail No.1995/2015 Order below Exhibit 1. daughter of applicant is suffering from brain disease and she has been advised to operate for the same. It is further submitted that now charge-sheet is also submitted in the crime and therefore, there is no need to further detain the applicant/accused in jail. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, she will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will attend the Court regularly for the purpose of trial and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that the accused persons including the applicant in furtherance of common intention had compelled the victim girl to indulge in prostitution and had earned money by indulging in said activity. It is further submitted that the complainant/victim girl has stated in her statement recorded as per Section 164 of Cr.P.C. in question- answer that said two police personnel namely Kakde and Khan used to come to the house of co-accused Shabana alias Parveen i.e. present applicant and they also used to do wrong act with her and used to give money to Shabana for doing said act. It is further contended and argued that the girl has clearly stated about involvement of the present applicant in this crime. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening and pressurizing the victim girl and prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if released on bail, the applicant may abscond and will not be available for trial and may again indulge .. 3 .. Bail No.1995/2015 Order below Exhibit 1. in such activity. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused are of serious nature under section 366A, 370, 376 read with section 34 of I.P.C. and section 5, 9 of I.T.P.A. and also under section 3, 4, 16 of P.O.C.S.O. Act with the allegation that the the present applicant was compelling the complainant minor girl to do prostitution and even two co-accused who are police personnel were also committing sexual assault on the girl by coming to the house of present applicant, it is contended by the applicant that she has never compelled the victim girl to do prostitution but it was the wanted accused Beli who was forcing the girl to do prostitution and said Beli had also addicted the girl to consume intoxicant powder i.e. MD powder and the applicant has no concern with any illegal activity of prostitution being carried out by the complainant girl. In the light of such rival contentions the allegations against the applicant/accused will have to be proved on merits after trial. 4] Then, fact is also clear that the accused is in jail since 08.04.2015 and even charge-sheet is also stated to have been submitted. 5] Then, it is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether .. 4 .. Bail No.1995/2015 Order below Exhibit 1. there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. In that respect it is contended by the applicant that she is permanent resident of the address given and she will not abscond and that she is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 6] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 7] Then, it has also to be mentioned that though charge- sheet is stated to have been submitted in this crime, it will take time to take up the case for hearing and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 8] Then, it is material to mention that other accused Mohammad Saeed Shaikh, who is husband of the applicant, is stated to have been ordered to be released on bail and therefore, the present applicant is also entitled to be released on bail on the ground of parity. Besides, the daughter of the applicant is stated to have been advised for operation for her brain disease. .. 5 .. Bail No.1995/2015 Order below Exhibit 1. 9] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order - ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Shabana Bano alias Parveen Sayeed Shaikh is released on P.R. bond of Rs.20,000/- [rupees twenty thousand only] with one local surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions - The applicant/accused shall not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize her and other prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. She shall not abscond and shall attend the Court regularly for the purpose of trial. She shall not leave India without permission of this Court. She shall furnish proof of her residence. The victim was already caught by the people in hugging position the victim was not resisting which shows that the act was consensual. The victim went to the house but she was not disclosed anything to the police on that day. The story of the FIR is concocted and false. There is no criminal background to the present applicant. He is ready to abide by the conditions, therefore, he prayed for bail. 3. Investigating Officer has given his say at Exh.8. Exh.26.. : JUDGMENT : (Delivered on this 23rd day of January, 2018) The accused is prosecuted for the offence of sexually assault upon 8 years old minor girl. 2] The facts are as under : It is alleged by prosecution that, the informant was residing at Girish Tower, Room No.407, Samrat Nagar, Mumbra alongwith her husband, son and daughter. At the time of incident her son was 4 years old and victim daughter was 8 years old. On 15.06.2013 at about 05.30 p.m. the informant, her husband, son and daughter were returning from Mumbra railway station. They hired the share rickshaw. After some distance the accused got into said auto­rickshaw as a passenger. The informant was sitting on one side and the accused was sitting on another side in the auto­rickshaw. The informant's husband was sitting in between them. The four years old son was with the informant. The informant's husband was holding bag. Therefore, victim daughter was standing in the auto­rickshaw. The accused asked the victim girl to sit on his lap. When the rickshaw reached near Samrat Nagar the informant, her husband, the victim daughter and son got down and rickshaw proceeded towards Mumbra. The J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 183­15 ­ 354 7,8.doc .....3/­ ..3.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 183/2015.. Exh.26.. victim was crying. On inquiry she told that the accused had put his hand into her pant and moved the same on her private part. After disclosure of said fact, the informant's husband ran behind said auto­rickshaw and halted the same. He inquired with the accused about the incident. Meanwhile people gathered. On learning that the accused had misbehaved with the small girl, the mob started assaulting the accused. Meanwhile police had been to the spot and took the accused to Mumbra police station. The informant, her husband and their children also went to the police station. Informant lodged complaint against the accused. 3] After receiving complaint offence punishable u/s.354, of the Indian Penal Code and section 7 and 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act came to be registered against the accused. After investigation, charge sheet came to be filed against the accused for said offences. 4] Charge is framed against the accused at Exh.05. Accused pleaded not guilty of offence and claimed to be tried. 5] Statement of accused u/s.313 of Code of Criminal Procedure is recorded at Exh.23. The defence of accused is that, at the time of incident he was not travelling in auto­ rickshaw with victim and her family. In fact he was travelling J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 183­15 ­ 354 7,8.doc .....4/­ ..4.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 183/2015.. Exh.26.. in another auto­rickshaw. He is falsely implicated in the offence. 6] After going through the prosecution story, evidence on record and hearing arguments of both sides, following points arise for my determination. I record my findings thereon for reasons as stated below. POINTS FINDINGS 1] Does the prosecution prove that on 15.06.2013 at about 05.30 to 05.45 p.m. in between Mumbra railway station to H.P. Gas Office, Samrat Nagar, Mumbra, Thane, while travelling in auto­rickshaw, the accused put his hand in to the pant of 8 years old minor girl, touched her private part and thereby sexually assaulted her and outraged her modesty ? …Proved. 2] What order ? ..As per final order. : REASONS : As to the Point No.1 :­ 7] To bring home the guilt of accused the prosecution has examined the informant as PW1 at Exh.10. The complaint lodged by her is at Exh.11. Victim's father is examined as PW2 at Exh.12. P.S.I. D.D.Thokal who merely filed charge sheet is examined as PW3 at Ex.14. The victim is examined as PW4 at J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 183­15 ­ 354 7,8.doc .....5/­ ..5.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 183/2015.. Exh.26.. Exh.16. A.P.I. Mahendra Patil who recorded the complaint and arrested the accused is examined as PW5 at Exh.18. The arrest panchanama which is admitted on behalf of the accused is at Exh.15. Lastly A.P.I. Shri.P.B.Pawar who carried the investigation is examined as PW6. His deposition is at Exh.20. The statement of victim which was referred in his cross examination is at Exh.21. 8] In the present case the relation of informant with the victim and her age is not disputed. It is also not disputed that on the day of incident the informant, victim, victim's father and younger brother had travelled in an auto­rickshaw. The accused has admitted that he was manhandled by informant's husband i.e. PW2 Abbas Bharuchwala and thereafter he was taken to the police station. The accused has denied that he was travelling in the auto­rickshaw of the informant and victim. As per his defence he was traveling in another auto­rickshaw and because of mis­identity false complaint came to be lodged against him. In the backdrop of these admitted facts and defence, we have to scrutinize the actual evidence about the incident. 9] PW1 the informant in her chief examination specifically deposed that on 15.06.2013 while returning from Mumbra railway station they were travelling in auto­rickshaw. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 183­15 ­ 354 7,8.doc .....6/­ ..6.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 183/2015.. Exh.26.. The accused was sitting on one side and the informant's husband was sitting by the side of the accused. The informant was sitting on another side of auto­rickshaw. Her son was alongwith her. The victim was standing in auto­rickshaw. The accused asked the victim to sit on his lap. Accordingly the victim was sitting on his lap. When they got down from the auto­rickshaw, the victim started to cry. On inquiry the victim told that the accused had put his hand inside her slack (pant) and touched her private part. Thereafter her husband chased the auto­rickshaw. The rickshaw was halted for collecting passengers. Her husband dragged the accused from auto­ rickshaw and started to beat him. Thereafter police and people gathered on the spot. The police took the accused to police station. She also went to the police station alongwith her husband and children and lodged complaint Exh.11. 10] PW2 the father of the victim has deposed that, in the auto­rickshaw his wife was sitting by one side and the accused was sitting on another side. He was sitting in between them. Their son was with his wife. As they were having luggage, the victim daughter was sanding. The accused asked victim to sit on his lap. Accordingly the victim sat on the lap of the accused. When they had alighted from the auto­rickshaw near Mumbra police station the victim was crying. On inquiry by wife, the daughter told that the accused had put his hand J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 183­15 ­ 354 7,8.doc .....7/­ ..7.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 183/2015.. Exh.26.. inside her slack. The wife informed said fact to him. Meanwhile the rickshaw had proceeded ahead to collect passengers. He halted the same and started to beat the accused. At that time people and police had been to the spot. 11] PW4, the victim has deposed at Exh.16. As she is 12 years old at the time of deposition her deposition was being recorded in the open Court. But she was frightened and was crying, therefore, her remaining statement came to be recorded in the chamber. She deposed that at the time of incident she was studying in 3rd std. On the day of incident she was travelling with her family in auto­rickshaw from Mumbra railway station. While traveling in said auto­rickshaw her brother was sitting on the lap of her mother. Accused had sat besides her father, her father was sitting in between her mother and accused. There was luggage with them. She was standing in the auto­rickshaw. The accused asked her to sit on his lap. Accordingly she sat on his lap. While travelling, after some distance the accused inserted his hand in her slack and touched her vagina. When she realized the same, she turned and saw on backside. After some time accused repeated the same incident. When they got down from auto­rickshaw, she started crying. On inquiry she narrated the incident to her police. Thereafter her father chased the auto­rickshaw, halted it and dragged the accused. Her father started to beat him. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 183­15 ­ 354 7,8.doc .....8/­ ..8.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 183/2015.. Exh.26.. Police had been to the spot and took the accused to police station. 12] In cross examination of the informant it is brought on record that, in her statement it is not mentioned that she was sitting on one side and the accused was sitting on another side in auto­rickshaw. It is also not mentioned in the complaint that, after alighting from auto­rickshaw her husband chased said auto­rickshaw which was halted for passengers. During the cross examination of PW4 the victim, it is brought on record that it is nowhere mentioned in her statement before police that, she had stated that after accused put his hand inside her slack, she had turned around and saw who was there. It is also not mentioned in her statement that she started to cry and narrated the incident to her parents and thereafter her father ran behind the auto­rickshaw. It is also not mentioned in her statement before police that the accused had touched her private part (vagina). The statement of victim is further referred in cross examination of PW6, investigating officer A.P.I. Pawar, who recorded the same. Certainly in the statement of the victim before police, it is merely mentioned that the accused had put his hand inside her slack. In the deposition of PW1, PW2 and PW4 it is mentioned that at the time when the accused was manhandled, number of people and police had gathered on the spot. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 183­15 ­ 354 7,8.doc .....9/­ ..9.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 183/2015.. Exh.26.. 13] Relying upon the deposition of informant, her husband and the victim it is submitted in written arguments, on behalf of the accused, that the prosecution has not examined any independent witness though available on the spot. It is further argued that the informant and her husband being parents of the victim are interested witnesses. Independent witnesses though available are not examined. Hence prosecution story is not reliable. It is further submitted that the number of auto­rickshaw in which the informant and her family was travelling is not mentioned. The statement of driver of said auto­rickshaw is also not recorded. There are material improvements, omissions and contradictions in the evidence of PW1, PW2 and PW4. The victim PW4 whose statement is recorded in the chamber has not identified the accused. It is further argued that the arrest panchanama of the accused is not carried out. It shows negligence on the part of the prosecution in the investigation. The investigating officer not even recorded the statement of other passengers in the auto­rickshaw. There is no independent witness to state that the accused was travelling in the auto rickshaw with informant and her family. 14] It is pertinent to note here that, there is nothing on record to suggest that the informant and her family was having any enmity with the accused. The victim was just 8 J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 183­15 ­ 354 7,8.doc .....10/­ ..10.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 183/2015.. Exh.26.. years old at the time of incident. Her deposition was recorded in question answer form by PW6. In said statement the victim had rightly stated that the accused had put his hand into her slack. Under such circumstances even if it is not appearing in the statement that the accused had touched private part of the victim, considering her age and description of the acts of the accused, it cannot be said to be material discrepancy. So far as the sitting arrangement in the auto­rickshaw is concerned it is but natural that the informant being woman was sitting on one side and the accused was sitting on the another side and the informant's husband sat in between them. It is not material omission in the complaint which does not disclose said sitting arrangement. It is not disputed that in Mumbra area there are share auto­rickshaws. Under such circumstances it is but natural that after informant and her family got down from the auto­rickshaw, the accused continued to travel in said auto­rickshaw and the rickshaw driver proceeded further to collect other passengers. The accused was chased and apprehended immediately after the incident. Therefore, there is no question of mis­identity. So far as presence of other people, rickshaw driver and passengers is concerned, the main incident had occurred in an auto­ rickshaw wherein the informant and her family members only were present. The accused was chased and apprehended subsequent to the incident of sexual assault. The accused has J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 183­15 ­ 354 7,8.doc .....11/­ ..11.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 183/2015.. Exh.26.. not disputed that he was taken to Mumbra police station after the incident. Under such circumstances non examination of independent witnesses is not fatal to the prosecution. Certainly the father and mother of the victim had not personally seen the incident. They came to know about the incident only after the victim narrated the same to them. 15] Section 29 of The Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act lays down the presumption in such case. It reads as under: “29. Presumption as to certain offence : Where a person is prosecuted for committing or abetting or attempting to commit any offence under sections 3, 5, 7 and section 9 of this Act, the Special Court shall presume, that such person has committed or abetted or attempted to commit the offence, as the case may be unless the contrary is proved”. In view of the presumption and unshattered evidence of the victim, the accused has failed to rebut the same. So far as identification of the accused in the Court is concerned, the deposition was being recorded in open Court wherein the accused was sitting,but victim being afraid and crying her remaining statement came to be recorded in the chamber. She rightly stated that the accused is present in the Court. Advocate Mr.Fakih and his assistant were present in the chamber and with their consent and understanding it was J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 183­15 ­ 354 7,8.doc .....12/­ ..12.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 183/2015.. Exh.26.. recorded in the chamber. Under such circumstances the said evidence cannot be challenged as being after thought. 16] PW3 P.S.I. Thokal merely filed charge sheet. PW5 A.P.I. Patil had arrested the accused who was brought to the police station. The arrest form is at Exh.15. The investigation was carried out by PW6 A.P.I. Pawar. He recorded statements and filed charge sheet. In view of the nature of the incident, the evidence of PW3, PW5 and PW6 is formal. Nothing is brought on record through their cross examinations, suggesting that the accused is falsely implicated in the offence. 17] In view of the evidence of the victim and her parents and the presumption u/s.29 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act the offence is duly proved by the prosecution. Hence answering point No.1 in the affirmative, the Judgment is deferred here to hear the accused on the quantum of sentence. Thane. (P.P.Jadhav) District Judge­6 and Date : 23.01.2018. Addl. Sessions Judge, Thane. 18] Heard advocate Mr.Fakih and accused in person. It is argued on behalf of the accused that the accused is not J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 183­15 ­ 354 7,8.doc .....13/­ ..13.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 183/2015.. Exh.26.. having any criminal antecedents. He is the only earning member of the family. Hence leniency be shown towards him. Advocate Mr.Fakih further argued that the benefit of provisions under Probation of Offenders Act be given to the accused and he be released on bond of good behaviour. 19] The accused is charged with the offence punishable u/s.354 of Indian Penal Code and section 7 and 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. However, POCSO Act being special enactment, conviction and sentence u/s.354 of the Indian Penal Code is not required. Conviction the accused and sentencing him for offence punishable u/s.8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act will be proper and justifiable. 20] The accused is held guilty for the offence under section 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. This is a special enactment under which the provisions of Probation of Offenders Act cannot be applied. The prescribed punishment is not less than three years which may extent to five years. The parents of the victim had allowed the victim to sit on the lap of the accused at his own request. However, he indulged in a very serious immoral act with a girl aged eight years old only. Under such circumstances there is no question of any leniency or releasing him on bond of good behaviour. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 183­15 ­ 354 7,8.doc .....14/­ ..14.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 183/2015.. Exh.26.. Considering the nature of the offence and prescribed punishment, following order is passed. ORDER 1. Accused Ehasanulla Ajaharulla Siddiqui is hereby convicted u/s.235(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure for offence punishable u/s.354 of the Indian Penal Code r.w. section 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act and he is sentence to suffer rigorous imprisonment for three years and six months and to pay fine of Rs.10,000/­ and in default of payment of fine he has to undergo simple imprisonment for three months. 2. The accused to surrender his bail bonds. 3. Accused was in jail from 16.06.2013 to 08.07.2013. He is entitled to set off u/s.428 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 4. A copy of Judgment be given to the accused free of cost. Sd/­... Thane. (P.P.Jadhav) District Judge­6 and Date : 23.01.2018. Addl. Sessions Judge, Thane. --1-- ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN CRIMINAL BAIL APPLICATION 1969/2017 Accused Nagesh Laxmanrao Vathore has applied for bail under section 439 of Cr. P.C. in C.R.No.I­227/2017 registered in Mumbra police station for the offence under section 376 of Indian Penal Code and section 4 of POCSO Act, 2012. 2. It is contended that the investigation is completed. The applicant is falsely implicated. The victim has voluntarily kept physical relation with the present applicant. So there are so many mitigating factors to release the accused on bail. The applicant is ready to abide by the conditions of bail and to face the investigation and trial. So he has prayed for bail. 3. Investigating Officer has given say at Exh.4. It is contended that the victim is 17 years old. Accused has took disadvantage of the poor condition of the victim and her mother and gave them room to residence. The accused driven the victim's mother from that room and kept physical relation with the victim and because of that victim became pregnant. Then accused went to his native place and did not contact the victim. If the accused is released on bail he is likely to pressurize the victim and their family because they are residing at footpath and they are very poor they have no support of anybody. --2-- 3. I heard Ld. Counsel on behalf of accused. He submitted that there is no proof of DNA, no proof that the victim is pregnant from the accused. The medical report of the age determination of the victim is not believable. No immediate FIR was lodged. Accused is married with another girl. So he may be released on bail. 4. The Ld. Advocate on behalf of the accused relied upon decision in case of Thulia Kali V/s. The State of Tamilnadu AIR 1973 Supreme Court 501. It was held that, “when the occurrence is not reported for more than 20 hours after the occrrence even though the police station is only two miles from the placed occurrence it is unsafe to base conviction. In case of Raja Ram V/s. State of Himachal Pradesh Cr. M.P. No.689/2015 decided on 08.07.2015. It was held that, “prosecutrix having delivered a baby girl not fathered by the bail applicant also acquires significance in as much as, in sequel, if a period of nine months therefrom is counted in reverse then her conception is to be computed to have occurred either in May or June 2014. As a further natural corollary then at the relevant time in as much as on 02.08.2014 her pregnancy was approximately three months old. Therefore, there is suppression of the material fact in the FIR and on such mitigating factor the bail was granted.” In case of Mahesh Balkrishna Dandane V/s. The State of Maharashtra 2015 ALL MR (Cri) 2805 it was held that, “every breach of promise to marry cannot be said to be either a --3-- cheating or rape. Whether relationship between parties were consensual or not, is to be tested independence, depending on the facts and circumstances of each case.” 5. I perused the contents in the FIR. As per case of prosecution it appears that the victim's mother was working as labour at Ghansoli petrol pump and Mumbai CST in laundry. At that time the accused came with the contact with the mother of victim. The victim was learning in Ashram school, but her mother's physical condition was not good, therefore, she left her hostel and came to reside with her mother. They would reside at Ghansoli at foot path and doing as labour work. Accused induced the victim's mother that he will provide them room to reside and accused took victim and her mother at Diva and gave them one room to reside. The accused gave rent of that room and would used to come frequently to that room. After that accused driven out mother of the victim from that room and therefore, he visit that room and committed sexual intercourse for 10 to 12 times with the victim. Because of that victim became pregnant. After that victim contacted the accused, but he did not received phone call. He went to his native place and married with another girl. 6. The victim is below 18 years. The accused is 35 years old. The court is of the view that the victim and her mother are poor and illiterate. They trusted the accused and came to --4-- reside in the room provided by the accused. Intension behind that of the accused is very clear. He wanted to take disadvantage of the condition of the victim and her mother and he driven out the victim's mother from room and committed sexual intercourse with the victim. 7. The court is of the view that the consent under which circumstances the accused has taken of the victim for sexual intercourse is not free consent. It cannot be said that it was love affair and therefore, the court is of the view that there is strong prima facie case made out against the accused. The ratio laid down in above cited cases are not applicable in the present case. The court is of the view that if the accused is released on bail he will definitely tamper the prosecution witnesses and the victim because they are very poor and they have no financial support. The victim is pregnant of 22 weeks at present. In such circumstances, he is likely to tamper the prosecution witness. So it is not fit case to release the accused on bail. Hence, I pass following order. ORDER Application for bail is rejected. Thane. ( S.C. Khalipe ) Date : 08/08/2017. Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

Order below Exhibit 1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 2031/2015 This application is filed by applicant/accused Anil Haricharan Sav for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with C.R.No.I-164/2015 registered at Shil Daighar Police Station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 370(2), 372 read with section 34 of I.P.C. and section 3, 4, 5, 7 of Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act (hereinafter in short referred to as I.T.P.A.) and also under section 4, 8, 14 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as P.O.C.S.O. Act). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant in furtherance of common intention with co-accused compelled minor girl to do prostitution and sexually harassed her. It is contended by the applicant that he has no concern with this crime and the illegal activity of prostitution being conducted at Shagun Lodge where he was serving as a waiter. It is further contended and argued that the applicant is falsely implicated in this crime and nothing incriminating has been recovered from him. It is further contended and argued that no specific role has been attributed to him. It is further submitted that co-accused Rajeshkumar Dipan Yadav who was also working as waiter in said Shagun Lodge has already been ordered to be released on bail and therefore on the ground of parity the applicant/accused is also entitled to be released on bail. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will attend the Court regularly for the purpose of trial and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. .. 2 .. Bail No. 2031/2015 Order below Exhibit 1. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that on receiving secret information police conducted raid at Shagun Lodge and at that time it revealed that the applicant and other accused persons were conducting prostitution business there and they used to induce and compel the victims to indulge in prostitution business and thereby the accused persons earned livelihood from said business.
