It is also contended that if released on bail, the applicant may abscond and will not be available for trial and may again indulge in such activity. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/ accused are of serious nature under section 370(2), 372 read with section 34 of I.P.C. and section 3, 4, 5, 7 of I.T.P.A. and also under section 4, 8, 17 of of P.O.C.S.O. Act with the allegation that the accused persons were conducting the prostitution business in Shagun Lodge and were compelling the victim girl to indulge in prostitution and also were earning livelihood from such business, it is the contention of the applicant/accused that no role is attributed to him and he was working as a servant in said Shagun Lodge and he has no concern with any prostitution business being conducted there and that he is falsely implicated in the crime. In such circumstance whether the allegations against the accused are true or not, would be the question to be decided on merits. .. 3 .. Bail No. 2031/2015 Order below Exhibit 1. 4] Then, it is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. In that respect it is contended by the applicant that she is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 5] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 6] Then, it has also to be mentioned that though the investigation in the matter is yet to be completed and the charge-sheet is ye to be submitted, it would take time to complete the investigation and then to submit the charge-sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 7] Then, as rightly submitted on behalf of applicant, co- accused Rajeshkumar Yadav who was also working as waiter in Shagun Lodge has already been ordered to be released on bail and therefore the present applicant is also entitled to be released on bail on the ground of parity. .. 4 .. The Ld. Defence counsel vehemently submitted that in the complaint Exh.9 informant stated about computer but as a matter of fact no such computer is seized by police. The Ld. APP submitted that in the said complaint word 'laptop' is also used which is seized by the police and as such, this omission is not material one. The Ld. Defence counsel submitted that when accused is not claiming ownership over laptop then it is necessary for prosecution to prove ownership. It is to be noted that ownership is not material but important fact is that prosecution has to prove that there is obscene material which was shown to victim by accused. 14] Victim PW 2 deposed that her date of birth is 23.7.2007. On the day of incident, after school hours, she was waiting for her sister and was standing at the gate of school. That photo was of man and woman without having any clothes on their person. He touched her urinate place by his hand. He pressed ..8/- ..8.. Spl.C. No.183/2014 (Exh.No. 35) her mouth and caught her hand. Thereafter he again left her at school. He told her at that time we will do like in the photo. 15] Victim further deposed that thereafter she came to house and told about it to her parents. Then they went to police station. At the time of incident, that boy was having little beard. She showed his house to police. That time that boy was present there but he removed his beard. She showed laptop to police and thereafter they all went back to police station. Thereafter, police and Court recorded her statement. Statement u/s 164 of Cr.P.C. is at Exh.12. On perusal of the same, it reveals that the Ld. Magistrate, Vashi recorded the said statement on 23.7.2014 and in which,she stated that the obscene picture was shown on the computer and remaining contents of her statement is same as she stated in her examination­in­chief. 16] In her cross examination, it is brought on record that she used to go alongwith friend Sandhya. After school hours, when she was standing at gate, that time, usually other students and staff of school used to be there. Without permission student cannot go out of gate. It is also brought in her cross examination that on 21.7.2014 she did not come out of gate and was waiting for her sister. After her sister came, she alongwith sister by school van went to house. She denied that on that day she was not taken by any boy to his house and no incident took place as stated in her examination in chief. The evidence of victim is on the point of touching her private part by accused but on the contrary, according to informant, accused put his penis in the vagina of victim. On perusal of medical certificate Exh.19 of victim, it reveals that there is no injury found on her person. Under such circumstances, the evidence of informant cannot ..9/- ..9.. Spl.C. No.183/2014 (Exh.No. 35) be considered on the point of rape as what was happened with victim was known only to her. Thus, the victim is the only witness to the incident and as such her testimony needs no corroboration which clearly goes to show that the act done by accused comes with in the per view of outrage of modesty and not of rape. 17] PW 3 Maruti deposed that on 21.7.2014 police called him Rabale Police Station, obtained his consent to act as panch, then they went to house of accused which was shown by informant, police prepared panchanama Exh.15 and also seized laptop as per Exh.16. Police also seized nickers of victim and accused as per seizure memo Exh.17. On 23.7.2014 police again called him at the police station and seized pant and shirt of accused as per panchanama Exh.18. In his cross examination he denied that panchanamas Exhs. 15 to 18 were already written by police and he only signed them. He cannot tell the brand of laptop. The evidence of this witness is at all not shattered inspite of searching and lengthy cross examination and as such, I have no hesitation to rely on his evidence. 18] PW 5 Pimpale I.O. deposed that on 21.7.2014 he received case diary, consisting of FIR and complaint. Then in the presence of panchas he prepared spot panchanama Exh.15. On perusal of the same, it reveals that spot shown by informant and it is the house of accused. He seized articles viz.chair, laptop and clothes of victim as per panchanamas Exhs.16 & 17. He also arrested accused. In cross examination he admitted that he has not collected evidence regarding ownership of accused over laptop. He denied that all panchanamas were prepared at police station. There is nothing brought on record to ..10/- ..10.. Spl.C. No.183/2014 (Exh.No. 35) disbelieve the version of this witness. The Ld. APP vehemently submitted that when the laptop was shown by accused to victim and then just after the incident that laptop was found in the house of accused then it is not necessary for the prosecution to prove the ownership of accused and only conscious possession is sufficient. 19] PW 4 Bhavikatti I.O. deposed that on 23.7.2014 he recorded memorandum Exh.18 of accused before the panchas and in pursuance of the same, he seized pant,T­shirt and underwear of accused as per panchanama Exh.25. He collected birth certificate of victim Exh.30 and on perusal of the same, it reveals that it is issued by N.M.M. Corporation in which,the date of birth of victim is mentioned as 23.7.2007. The incident took place on 21.7.2014. Thus on the day of incident the age of victim was near about 7 years. In the cross examination,he admitted that surrounding to the spot of incident there are residential houses and he had not recorded statement of persons residing nearby house of accused. The Ld. Defence counsel vehemently submitted that it was incumbent on the part of I.O. to record statement of adjoining neighbourers. The Ld. APP submitted that when the incident took place in the house of accused and that too by closing its door by accused himself, then there is no necessity to record statement of neighbourers. I do agree with the submission of the Ld. APP as incident took place within the 4 corners of house of accused then there is no point to record statement of adjoining persons. 20] So far as the charge for the offence punishable u/s 363 of IPC is concerned, the allegation of prosecution is that accused took victim from the school on the pretext that her father sent to him to ..11/- ..11.. Spl.C. No.183/2014 (Exh.No. 35) receive her, then she went alongwith accused and after incident he also left her near the school. At that time victim was not in the lawful guardianship of her parents but she was in the temporary custody of school authorities. It is also brought on record that there is a gate to the school and without permission student cannot go out of gate. As per report Exh.9, victim was waiting outside the school but according to victim she was standing at the gate of school. In the cross examination she admitted that she did not come out of gate. Thus, these facts are established inconsistency which goes to the root of case as it is material one. According to prosecution, accused took her on the false pretext and that are not the ingredients of kidnapping. So far as abduction u/s 362 of IPC is concerned, the deceitful means induces by person to go from any place is said to be abducted that person but abduction is not punishable under the IPC. Thus, the charge of kidnapping u/s 361 or abduction u/s 362 of IPC is not proved and as such, I recorded my finding to point No.1 in the negative. 21] So far as the charge for the offence punishable u/s 376 of IPC is concerned, prosecution has to prove the penetration of penis or insert to any extent any object or part of body not being penis as defined in S.375 (a) & (b) of IPC. It is to be noted that rape is committed when male organ penetrates, at least partial, the female organ. In between complete rape and attempt to commit rape,there is a rear area covered by S. 354 of IPC i.e. assault or criminal force to woman with intent to outrage her modesty or indecent assault. The dividing line between attempt to commit rape and indecent assault is not only thin but also is practically invisible. For an offence of attempt to commit rape, the prosecution is required to establish that the act of ..12/- ..12.. Spl.C. No.183/2014 (Exh.No. 35) accused went beyond the stage of preparation. At the same time, Court also gathered the intention of accused when victim and accused were alone present in the house, then the only fact known to victim regarding that act and as such the evidence of victim is material. 22] According to victim, at the time of incident accused closed the door, removed his pant, he also removed her slacks and nicker, made to sit her on his lap. He touched her urinate place by his hand. Thus, it is not the version of victim herself that accused committed rape or attempted to commit rape. The medical certificate Exh.19 also shows that there is no injury on the person of victim more particularly on her private part. Thus, on marshalling the evidence of victim and medicals certificate on record, then it is clear that on the day of incident accused outraged the modesty of victim by making her naked and touching her private part by his hand. However, there is no corroborative evidence in respect of penetration of penis in her vagina as deposed by informant. Considering this act and keeping in mind the thin line between rape and outrage of modesty, the provision of S. 354 of IPC is attracted and not offence punishable u/s 376 of IPC. Therefore, I answer point No.2 accordingly. 23] So far as the charge for the offence punishable u/s 293 of IPC and S. 11(iii) of POCSO Act are concerned, it is necessary for prosecution to prove that obscene act exhibited to victim. On perusal of seizure memo Exh.16, it reveals that police seized the laptop from accused. As per report Exh.9 and statement of victim u/s 164 of Cr.P.C (Exh.12), obscene was shown by accused on the computer however police seized the laptop. There is a difference between computer and ..13/- ..13.. Spl.C. No.183/2014 (Exh.No. 35) laptop. However, the question goes to the root of case that I.O. failed to collect further evidence whether in the laptop there is obscene material or not and in what format it was stored in the said laptop. I.O. ought to have taken assistance of the expert in that regard but it seems that he simply seized laptop. Therefore, there is no evidence before the Court to show that in the said laptop there is any obscene material which was shown by accused to victim and shown the same for pornographic purpose. Secondly, as per report Exh.9, before lodging complaint, police took laptop to police station and then it was seized from accused on 21.7.2014 but accused was arrested on 22.7.2014. Thus, it shows that the said laptop was seized prior to arrest of accused, which creates a doubt about seizure of same laptop. As such, prosecution failed to prove the charge for the offence punishable u/s 293 of IPC & u/s 11(iii) of POCSO Act. I answer point Nos. 3 & 6 in the negative. 24] So far as the charge for the offence u/s 7 & 9(m) punishable u/s 8 & 10 of POCSO Act is concerned, there is no dispute regarding date of birth of victim as 23.7.2007. On perusal of birth certificate Exh.30, it reveals that date of birth of victim is mentioned as 23.7.2007. The incident took place on 21.7.2014. As per S. 29 and 30 of POCSO Act, the presumption is in favour of prosecution and that has to be rebutted by accused. Inspite of cross examination to informant and victim, the defence failed to overcome the presumption. Even in the statement u/s 313 of Cr.P.C., accused failed to state that due to any old enmity the report came to be lodged against him and prosecution witnesses deposed falsely. Thus, on the date of incident age of victim was below 12 years and as stated above, accused touched the vagina of victim by his hand. The evidence of victim is sufficient to establish that accused ..14/- ..14.. Spl.C. No.183/2014 (Exh.No. 35) committed sexual assault and aggravated sexual assault as he touched her private part and on the day of incident, victim was below 12 years old. Thus, accused committed sexual assault u/s 7 punishable u/s 8 and aggravated sexual assault u/s 9(m) punishable u/s 10 of the POCSO Act. With this I answer the point Nos. 4 & 5 accordingly. 25] As per charge Exh.3, accused is facing trial for offence punishable u/s 376 of IPC, but as per oral and documentary evidence, prosecution proved beyond reasonable doubt that accused committed offence punishable u/s 354 of IPC. The punishment prescribed for offence punishable u/s 376 of IPC is of 7 years which may extent to imprisonment of life, whereas, u/s 354 of IPC punishment is from one year to 5 years. Thus, charge Exh.3 put for major offence whereas prosecution proved charge of minor offence, hence, as per the provisions of S. 222 of Cr.P.C., accused may be convicted for minor offence without framing separate charge of that minor offence. With this, I record my finding to all points accordingly and pause here to hear the accused on the point of sentence. Defence Counsel prayed for leniency and also submitted that accused was not previously convicted. ..15/- ..15.. Spl.C. No.183/2014 (Exh.No. 35) 27] So far as awarding of sentence is concerned, that punishment not served the purpose of the trial, but that must be given message to the society at large. The evidence on record clearly shows that accused committed offence relating to aggravated sexual assault with victim who is aged about 7 years. This incident not only gives fear in the mind of victim but also other students.Therefore, no question arises regarding leniency. However, considering the age of victim and the nature of crime, the Ld. 1 SPL .C. No. 182/2014. Presented on­ 18.09.2014. Registered on­ 18.09.2014. Decided on­ 10.10.2017. Duration­ Y­3 M­0 D­22 IN THE COURT OF SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE. [Presided over by A.S. Bhaisare, Additional Sessions Judge­2 and Special Judge (POCSO Act), Thane.] SPECIAL CASE (POCSO) NO. 182/2014. Exh. no. The State (Through Vashi Police Station) ..Complainant. V/s. Govind Bapurav Chavan, Age 23 years, Resident of room no. 125, Lane no. 3, Nahur road, Mumbai. ..Accused. ___________________________________________________________ Appearances­ Learned A.P.P. Smt. Talhar, for the State. Learned Advocate Shri. S.R. Parad, for the accused. ___________________________________________________________ JUDGMENT (Delivered on 10.10.2017.) 1] Accused Govind Bapurav Chavan, is facing trial for the offences punishable u/s. 363, 366A, 376, 417, 506 of I.P.C. and u/s. 3 punishable u/s. 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2 SPL .C. No. 182/2014. 2] It is the case of prosecution that on 11.06.14, accused who was selling balloons, has kidnapped Pooja aged about 14 years and 9 months and committed rape on her. By these allegations, mother of victim has lodged her report. It is registered vide C.R. no. 222/14 on 14.06.14. Police had carried out investigation. Lastly, accused along with victim were found in Santacruz area. They were taken to police station. Informant was called there. Victim was referred to hospital for her medical examination. Accused was also referred for her medical examination. Spot panchanama was recorded. Statements of witnesses were recorded. After investigation, charge­sheet was submitted in the court. 3] My learned Predecessor framed the charge against the accused for the offences punishable under section 363, 366A, 376, 417, 506 of I.P.C. and u/s. 3 punishable u/s. 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, on 28/01/2015. Details of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular, to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. His defence is of total denial. 4] During trial, defence has admitted certain documents on record, i.e. X­ray report of victim (Exh.23), medical examination certificate of accused (Exh.30). 5] To bring home the guilt of the accused for the charges leveled against him, the prosecution has examined as many as five witnesses i.e. P.W. Name of witness Exh. Description No. No. 1] Taya Ashok Kale 14 Mother of victim. 2] Victim 16 Victim girl. 3] Mukund Vasantrao 19 Investigating officer. Kulkarni 3 SPL .C. No. 182/2014. 4] Santosh Prakash Kale 25 Elder cousin brother of victim 5] Dr. Mahesh Babasaheb 27 Medical officer who had Late examined the victim girl. 6] Accused did not enter into witness box. He has not examined defence witness. 7] Heard learned A.P.P. Smt. Talhar for the State. She submitted as per the prosecution story. 8] Heard learned counsel Shri. S.R. Parad for the accused. He submitted that there is difference between taken and carried. There was love affair. Victim herself has left the house of her lawful guardian and joined the accused. She had knot made any hue and cry. She was knowing the consequences of her own act. There is no sexual intercourse. Her hymen was found intact. He has filed the following authorities in support of his argument. 1] 1965­AIR(S.C.)­0­942, 1965­SCR­1­243, S. Varadarajan Vs. State of Madras, in which Their Lordships observed that­ “She was not a child of tender years who was unable to think for herself but, as already stated, was on the verge of attaining majority and was capable of knowing what was good and what was bad for her.” 2] The State of Maharashtra Vs. Ramesh Babulal Rewatkar, 2017 ALL MR (Cri.) 3980, in which Their Lordships observed that­ “Penal Code (1860), Ss. 376, 366, 363­ Rape on minor­ Proof of age­Prosecution claiming age of prosecutrix to be 15 years on date of offence. To prove said claim, leaving certificate of secondary school as well as admission register of that school brought on record. These documents were based on leaving certificate of 4 SPL .C. No. 182/2014. primary school. However, no data from primary school brought on record. Data of secondary school therefore not reliable. Evidence from first attended school is necessary in such matters. Prosecution failed to establish status of victim as minor. Prosecutrix was consenting party hence, accused entitled to acquittal.” 9] Following points arise for my determination, which are being answered for the reasons given herein­below. POINTS FINDINGS 1] Whether prosecution proved that on No. 11.06.2014 at about 19.00 hours, accused kidnapped the minor girl aged 14 years and 9 months, from lawful guardianship of her parents from vegetable market, sector no. 9, Vashi, Navi Mumbai ? 2] Whether prosecution proved that on the No. above­said date, time and place, accused induced the minor girl to go from her house or to do any act with intent that the said minor girl may be, or knowing that it is likely that she will be forced or seduced to illicit intercourse with the accused ? 3] Whether prosecution proved that on the No. above­said date, time and place, when the said minor girl under the age of sixteen had gone to bathroom, accused committed rape on her at that place, by doing forcible sexual intercourse with her ? 4] Whether prosecution proved that on the No. above­said date, time and place, accused cheated the said minor girl by 5 SPL .C. No. 182/2014. dishonestly inducing her to do sexual intercourse with him by giving false promise of marriage to her, which caused damage to her body, mind and reputation ? 5] Whether prosecution proved that on the No. above­said date, time and place, accused committed forcible sexual intercourse with said minor girl by giving threats to her and thereafter also, threatened her not to disclose about the said act to anybody ? 6] Whether prosecution proved that on the No. above­said date, time and place, accused committed penetrative sexual assault on the above­said minor girl ? 7] What order ? As per final order. REASONS POINT NOS. 1 TO 6 10] It has come in the evidence of P.W.1 Taya Ashok Kale, mother of victim that ­ She was dealing her business of flowers in Vashi, sector 9. Victim is her daughter. She was born on 21st of month of Ashhadi of 1999. On 11.06.2014 at about 6.00 to 6.30 p.m., victim went for bathroom from her shop. But, she did not return back. She had searched for her here and there including her relatives. But, victim was not found. Lastly, after two days, she went to police station and lodged her report (Exh. 15). Her statement was recorded by police. At evening of lodging her complaint, victim was found in Santacruz, Mumbai. Then, she along with her husband went to Santacruz police station. Accused Govind Chavan 6 SPL .C. No. 182/2014. along with her daughter were found in Santacruz. Then, they were taken to Vashi police station by police. She was told by her daughter victim that she was taken by accused forcibly, if she did not turn up with him, he would pick up her from anywhere, he had committed rape on her. Victim was referred to Navi Mumbai Municipal Corporation hospital for her examination. 11] She has deposed in her cross­examination that accused was selling balloons near her flower shop. Now, Pooja is married and has a daughter of 2.5 years and a son of one year. She had five daughters and a son. Sangita is her elder daughter, but she cannot state her date of birth. So also, she did not know date of birth of her other issues including Pooja. She had given qualified admission in her cross­examination that she was unknown that accused had kidnapped her daughter. There was love affair between accused and Pooja. 12] It has come in the evidence of P.W.2 victim girl that­ On 11.06.14, at about 6.00 p.m., she went for bathroom from her shop. Govind Chavan had followed her. He was selling balloons. She was asked by him whether she was coming along with him. She replied in the negative. She was threatened by him that if she did not turn up with him, he would commit suicide. Then, she was taken by him to the house of his friend at Kadavali. He had committed rape on her on both days. Then, they went to Mulund. Then, they went to Santacruz. They were accosted by her brother Santosh at Santacruz. They were taken to Santacruz police station. Her parents came to Santacruz police station. Thereafter, they were taken by police to Vashi police station. She was taken by police to hospital of Navi Mumbai. Doctor had examined her. Police had recorded her statement. Her birth certificate is at Exh. 17. 13] Victim deposed in her cross­examination that her father was 7 SPL .C. No. 182/2014. having mobile. None from her family members were talking with accused on the said mobile. Sangoda is her girl friend. She originally belongs to Barshi, Dist. Solapur. In the month of Jan. 14, there was family religious program in Barshi. Accused had attended the said program. He was not residing in Barshi or Solapur District. 14] From the evidence of P.W.2 victim, it can be gathered that accused had committed rape on her on both days. However, from medical report Exh. 28, it can be gathered that her hymen was found intact. There were no even tear marks on her private part or on her body. Only tip of finger was admitted in vagina. Therefore, it is very difficult to hold that accused had committed sexual intercourse upon the victim on continuous two days. 15] Birth certificate Exh. 17 of victim is placed on record. It seems from it that she was born on 27.08.99 at Mumbai. The birth was also registered with Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai, on 16.10.99. Exh. 17 seems to be issued on 08.01.2008. P.W.1 mother of victim had not stated the age of victim. Not only that, she did not know the date of birth of any of her issues. 16] No doubt, Exh. 17 birth certificate is issued by authority of Municipal Corporation. Therefore, there is presumption u/s. 35 of Indian Evidence Act. However, there is no exact place of birth of victim mentioned in the birth certificate Exh. 17 whether she was born at her house or in the hospital. 17] It has come in the evidence of P.W.5 Dr. Mahesh Babasaheb Late that­ Since October, 2013 till December, 2014, he was 8 SPL .C. No. 182/2014. attached with N.M.M.C., Vashi hospital as medical officer. On 15.06.14, he was on duty. On that day, victim was brought by P.S.I. Shri. Kamble of Vashi police station for her medical examination. He had also received requisition from police. She had given consent for her medical examination. On examination, he found no external injuries on the person of victim. On genital examination, hymen was found intact, there was no any evidence of tear of hymen. Hymen was admitting tip of finger. He collected vaginal swab, blood sample, pubic hair, nail clippings. He referred her to radiologist for determination of her age. Accordingly, he issued medical certificate (Exh. 28). 18] It has come in his cross­examination that he had obtained history from the patient. According to history, there was love affair between victim and accused Govind Chavan. Victim had also stated that there were no physical, sexual contact. 19] Having considered the facts and circumstances of the matter, evidence on record and discussed reasons, it can be held that victim was knowing the consequences of her own act and she was aged about more than 16 years of age at the date of alleged incident. There was no hue and cry on the part of victim. On the contrary, they had been to Santacruz to meet their cousin brother Santosh Kale. Accordingly, they had visited him. Prosecution failed to prove the alleged offence against the accused beyond all reasonable doubts. Hence, I answer all the points accordingly and proceed to pass the following order. ORDER 1] Accused Govind Bapurav Chavan, is hereby, acquitted under sec. 235(1) of the Criminal Procedure Code, of the offences 9 SPL .C. No. 182/2014. punishable u/s. 363, 366A, 376, 417, 506 of I.P.C. and u/s. 3 punishable u/s. 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] Accused Govind Bapurav Chavan, be enlarged on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ with surety of like amount. The effect of this bail order will remain in force for the period of six months from today, as per section 437­(A) of Cr.P.C. 3] Muddemal if any, being worthless, be destroyed after appeal period is over. Thane, (A.S. Bhaisare) Date­ 10.10.2017. Additional Sessions Judge­2 and Special Judge (POCSO Act), Thane.

Though the accused denied that he was beating the children under the influence of liquor and appear to have putforth a defence and stated that he was in habit of drinking liquor and that he used to scold and beat the girls and son as well, because they were not studying, as discussed above absolutely nothing is brought on record on behalf of accused to show preponderance of probability of such defence put-forth by the accused. But it is there on record that only two girls i.e. victim Roshni and Muskan were taken to the complainant by the grandmother and son was not taken. In such circumstances the only inference in that regard is that obvious reason for that is the act of sexual assault and harassment committed by the accused = 23 = Spl. Case No.69/2013. with the girl. At the cost of repetition it can be said that it is there on record in the cross examination of the evidence of PW.2 - Muskan that after grandmother learnt about such acts committed by her father with Roshni, Uncle had beaten her father i.e. accused and then her grandmother taken them to one Didi. Her such version appear to have not been disputed and denied. It is thus clear that the decision to send both the girls to remand home or Orphanage was taken by the grandmother and the reason for that was the wrong acts committed by the accused and therefore also such defence put-forth by the accused do not appear to be probable and plausible. 34. One more aspect of the matter is that the girl Roshni is stated to be of 11 years old at the time of the incident. Then after if the complaint was lodged, she was immediately referred to the hospital alongwith the letter and then she was medically examined by the medical officer in the hospital and PW.3 Dr. Aruna Rajkumar Belure - medical officer stated in her evidence that she examined the girl and stated that the girl herself has given the history that her father Subhash Duglas has been committing oral as well as vaginal sexual intercourse with her and last intercourse was four months back and also that her father used to drink and beat her and that her mother died three years back etc. Even as per her version, on examination of the girl she noticed that her hymen was ruptured and could admit one finger and on the basis of such observations in her opinion she was habituated to sexual intercourse and accordingly she issued certificate as per Exh.-30. = 24 = 35. Even on careful perusal of the Exh.-30 reveal that a very clear opinion that the girl was habituated to sexual intercourse is given by the medical officer. Then though in her cross examination on behalf of accused it is accepted by her that hymen rupture was possible by cycling or any other sports. However, no such suggestion is put to the girl that at the relevant time she was doing cycling or having any sports activities because of which there could be hymen rupture. Then keeping aside that it is clear that a very specific opinion is given by the medical officer that on the basis of observations of the girl, in her opinion the girl was habituated to the sexual intercourse. Her version do not appear to have been challenged or disputed on behalf of the accused. Even she denied specific suggestion that if vagina admits only one finger, there cannot be a case of rape. She further stated that actually tissue of vagina is fibro- muscular with elasticity character and therefore during sex it gets expanded and only after 2-3 deliveries two fingers PV is possible and normally in case of habitualness, one finger is admitted. 36. In view of such explanation given by the doctor it is very much clear that only in case of 2-3 deliveries two fingers PV is possible and normally in case of habitualness, one finger PV is possible and on the basis of that when the vagina of the girl admitted one finger she had opined that the girl was habituated to the sexual intercourse and it was not the case of mere hymen rupture. = 25 = Spl. Case No.69/2013. 37. Even the submissions on behalf of the accused that there was no injury on the private part of the girl and therefore the possibility of girl being raped is not there etc., it has to be mentioned that the girl stated that the last intercourse was four months before and even as per her version such acts were committed by the accused for about two months continuously every day and that is fully corroborated and supported by the medical opinion that the girl was habituated to the intercourse. 38. It cannot be left out of the consideration that the girl was hardly about 11 years old at the relevant time and even it is brought on record in the cross examination of the medical officer that the girl had yet to start her menstruation. In such circumstances when on the basis of the medical examination and observations it revealed that the girl was habituated to the sexual intercourse and when the girl stated that such act of forcible sexual intercourse initially and then in usual course everyday was committed by the accused, there is no scope for any doubt that the act as has been stated by the girl has been committed by the accused. Even the girl also has specified the incidents of the accused giving his penis in the mouth of the girl which is dirtiest and heinous act on the part of the father to commit with his own daughter aged about 11 years and it is unacceptable and unbelievable that such story would be concocted by the girl or any of the social worker without the girl having undergone to the experience. = 26 = 39. Even in the ruling cited on behalf of the prosecution in the case of Lalmand Nabhik Chaudhary Vs. State (through the Mapusa Police Station) reported in 2010 ALL MR (Cri) 102, it is observed that statement made by the victim to the doctor examining her and other witnesses after the incident, the evidence of doctor and the said other witnesses cannot be simply discarded as hear-say evidence. In the same ruling it is further observed that even though the victim turned hostile under the pressure from mother on the basis of the statement of the doctor and the other witnesses to whom she had disclosed about the incident the accused can be held guilty. In the light of that, the testimony of the other witnesses including medical officer has to be held as reliable and even the present case is on better footing, since the victim girl as well as her sister also supported the prosecution case. 40. Even so far as the submissions that there is delay in lodging the F.I.R. and the girl did not disclose about such incidents to anybody etc. as discussed above it is there on record that the girl has stated about such acts to the grandmother and who also stated her not to tell about it to anybody and then nothing more can be expected from the 11 years old girl who was staying with the father and whose mother also was not there and support her and it has to be said that the girl had tolerated such sexual harassment and only when she was taken by her grand-mother to social worker she stated about the said incidents to her that too even after 5-6 days and no fault can be found with the girl in that regard and therefore delay in disclosing the facts by the girl can not be said to be fatal lacuna. = 27 = Spl. Case No.69/2013. 41. Even in a ruling in case of Devaji Rama Padave Vs. The State of Maharashtra, reported in 2013 ALL MR (Cri) 2025, it is held that the version of the prosecutrix that she was rapped thrice by her step father is corroborated by medical evidence and since she is young girl, some discrepancies are bound to occur in her evidence and since there was no omission or contradiction on the aspect of role played by accused, her evidence can be safely relied upon. Even in the same ruling is on the similar facts in the case of Devaji Rama Padave Vs. The State of Maharashtra referred supra that no importance can be given to the fact of delay in such case. 42. In the light of that, if the testimony of PW.4 - Prabhavati Kamble is perused as discussed above that is also in full corroboration and full support to the version of the girl. Even at the cost of repetition it can be said that there was no reason for the said witness PW.4 - Prabhavati Kamble to make such false allegations against the father of the girl who was totally unknown to her till the time she met her at the house of complainant. Even the complainant did not have any reason or grudge or grievance to make such false allegations against the accused. 43. It is also material to mention that as discussed above the fact that accused had been beating and abusing the girls is even accepted by the accused. Even this fact is also not denied that he was addicted to drink liquor. Then it is also clear that after learning about the same the mother of the accused herself had decided to send the girls to remand home or = 28 = Orphanage and for that purpose she had sent the girls to the complainant and that fact is also totally against the defence putforth by the accused that he had decided to send the girls to remand home. 44. It is also to be mentioned that as per the testimony of the PW.5 - Ramji Ramnarayan Yadav, the clothes of the accused and the girl were discovered and seized, showed by the accused from the cup-board of his house. Then though the said witness was cross examined at length on one hand, nothing contrary to his version is brought on record to show that he was not telling truth and on the other hand the fact that the clothes were taken out by the accused from the cup-board while he was in police custody is even accepted by the accused in his statement recorded U/sec.- 313 of Cr.P.C. It is further clear that the said seized muddemal and samples obtained were sent to Chemical Analyser for chemical analysis and the C.A. report received is produced on record. That fact is also clear from the testimony of the investigating officer and not seen to have been disputed. Though the C.A. report is negative that cannot have any bearing on the merits of the case because as per the prosecution case itself the last episode of sexual intercourse by the accused with the girl was four months before and no finding of semen or vaginal swab etc. on the clothes of the girl do not have any bearing or relevance in regard to the truthfulness or otherwise to the testimony of the witnesses. 45. It is also clear that on the basis of complaint, the offence is registered and the accused is prosecuted for the offences charged against = 29 = Spl. Case No.69/2013. him. Even as discussed above from the testimony of the victim girl corroborated by the other material including the medical evidence and testimony of the sister of the girl who is also eye witness to the incident to some extent it is clear that the accused had been committing forcible sexual intercourse with the girl for about two months preceding the date 27/06/2013 and also was committing act of sexual assault on her by putting his penis in her mouth time and again with sexual intention oftenly. 46. It has to be mentioned that section 29 of the POCSO Act provides :- " 29. Presumption as to certain offences. - Where a person is prosecuted for committing or abetting or attempting to commit any offence under section 3, 5, 7 and section 9 of this Act, the Special Court shall presume, that such person has committed or abetted or attempted to commit the offence, as the case may be unless the contrary is proved." 47. No doubt as rightly argued on behalf of the prosecution that the presumption is rebutable and if the contrary is proved the presumption cannot be attracted or applied. But, then except stating that the accused is falsely implicated nothing contrary to the prosecution case is contended or even preponderance of probability of such defence is also not established. At the cost of repetition it can be said that if at all there was no such incident, the girl would not have stated so in so many words and there was no reason for the social worker to approach the police with = 30 = such complaint and even the medical evidence is also in full support of the prosecution case. In such circumstances since nothing contrary is proved by the accused, it is to be presumed that the accused had committed the offence charged against him. 48. It is also to be mentioned that the girl is stated to be 11 years old at the relevant time and the prosecution has produced on record the school leaving certificate of the girl which is proved by the PW.8 - Subhash Balasaheb Mhaske. As per the birth certificate, the date of birth of the girl is 18/11/2002 and if calculated on the basis of that the age of the girl at the relevant time was 2 years, 10 months and 20 days and she is the child within the meaning of section 2 of POCSO Act. Even the accused is the father of the girl and therefore, it was within his personal knowledge as to what was the age of the girl and since he has not disputed or denied the age of the girl or the genuineness or the correctness of the school leaving certificate. There is no scope or doubt that at the time of incident the girl was child below 12 years old. 49. As such from the evidence brought on record and the evidence of girl corroborated by the medical evidence and other evidence on record it is to be held that the prosecution has established beyond all the reasonable doubt that the accused had committed forcible intercourse with the girl Roshni and also had been sexually harassing her by giving his penis in her mouth and he had committed such an acts repeatedly. = 31 = Spl. Case No.69/2013. 50. Then as is clear section 5(m) and (n) of POCSO Act defines aggravated sexual assault as under :- "5(m) - whoever commits penetrative sexual assault on a child below twelve years, 5(n) - whoever being a relative of the child through blood or adoption or marriage or guardianship or in foster care or having a domestic relationship with a parent of the child or who is living in the same or shared household with the child, commits penetrative sexual assault on such child;" and section 9 of the POCSO Act defines sexual assault as under :- "9 (m) - whoever commits sexual assault on a child below twelve years. (n) whoever, being a relative of the child through blood or adoption or marriage or guardianship or in foster care, or having domestic relationship with a parent of the child, or who is living in the same or shared household with the child, commits sexual assault on such child; " 51. Even in the light of the fact that the girl at that time was 11 years old i.e. below 12 years of age and also that the accused has committed such act with the girl repeatedly and further that the accused is real father of the girl and he has blood relation, penetrative sexual assault and sexual assault seems to have been committed by the accused also comes within the purview of aggravated sexual assault and such an act of the accused = 32 = falls within the purview of aggravated penetrative sexual assault under section 3 read with 5 and aggravated sexual assault under section 7 read with 9 of POCSO Act. I therefore held the accused guilty and convict him for the said offences. 52. At this stage the dictation of the Judgment is postponed for hearing the accused on the point of sentence. Date : 08.10.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Additional Session Judge­1, Thane. Resumed. 53. The accused is made aware of the fact that he is held guilty for the offence punishable under section 376 (2) (f) of Indian penal Code and section 5(m)(n) read with section 6 and section 9(m) and (n) read with section 10 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and the punishment prescribed for the offence under section 376(2)(f) of Indian Penal Code is Rigorous Imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than seven years but which may be for life or for a term which may extent to ten years and shall also be liable to fine and offence under section 5(m) (n) read with section 6 of POCSO Act is punishable with Rigorous Imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than ten years but which may extend to imprisonment for life and shall also be liable to fine and section 9(m) and (n) punishable under section 10 of POCSO Act is punishable with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than five years but which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine. = 33 = Spl. Case No.69/2013. 54. I heard the learned A.P.P. and the accused on the point of sentence. 55. It was submitted by the accused that it is his first offence and leniency be shown to him. It was also submitted on behalf of the accused by learned advocate representing him that, though the offences proved against the accused are of serious nature, it is not rarest of rare case wherein the maximum punishment can be warranted. It was also argued that the accused has old mother and one son. He has to maintain and look after them and his both daughters are already sent to remand home and he be shown leniency and he be awarded minimum punishment to the extent already undergone by him. 56. As against this the learned A.P.P. submitted that looking to the serious nature of offence charged against the accused he is not entitled to leniency and he is liable to award maximum punishment prescribed. 57. Then, so far as the quantum of sentence is concerned it has to be mentioned that, it is well settled that it is the duty of the Court in every case to award proper sentence, having regard to the nature of the offence, the manner in which it is committed and to all mitigating circumstances. Even it is also well settled that in the matter of fixation of punishment for any particular crime, the Court should take into consideration the nature of offence, the circumstances in which it was committed and the degree of deliberation shown by the offender and also that the measure of punishment should be proportionate to the gravity of the offence and it is = 34 = also the responsibility of the Court to see that the sentence should not be excessive and at the same time it should not be too lenient or liberal. 58. Keeping in mind the above well settled principles, the quantum of punishment in regard to offences punishable U/sec.­376 and 377 of I.P.C. is required to be decided in the present case. In this regard in the present case the father of the girl had repeatedly committed aggravated sexual assault on the girl in various ways by having penetration vaginal intercourse as well as by giving his penis in the mouth of the girl which is to be termed as most heinous act. Even the ruling cited on behalf of the prosecution in case of State of Himachal Pradesh Vs. Asha Ram, reported in LAWS (SC)­2005­11­41, it is observed that :­ "There can never be more graver and heinous crime than the father being charged of raping his own daughter. He not only delicts the law but it is a betrayal of trust. The father is the fortress and refuge of his daughter in whom the daughter trusts. Charged of raping his own daughter under his refuge and fortress is worst than the gamekeeper becoming a poacher and treasury guard becoming a robber." 59. In such circumstances when the own daughter is subjected to sexual harassment and assault by the accused, the aspect that he is having liability to maintain his own mother cannot be the mitigating circumstances, even the aspect cannot be ignored that the girls have stated in their evidence that they had narrated about such acts by accused to their grandmother and the accused cannot be said to be entitled to be any leniency and the submissions on behalf of the prosecution that the accused is liable for maximum punishment provided for the offence = 35 = Spl. Case No.69/2013. appear to be appealing and convincing. In view of all the above discussion I am of the view that the facts and circumstances of the case, following sentence would meet the ends of justice. In the result, I pass the following order :- ORDER Accused namely Subhash Ramkisan Duglas @ Duglach is convicted for the offence punishable under section 376(2)(f) of the Indian Penal Code and section 5(m) and (n) read with section 6 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and he is sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for life and to pay fine of Rs.5,000/­ [Rupees Five Thousand only] and in default of payment of fine, to suffer S.I. for 50 days on both the counts. (2) The accused is also convicted for the offence punishable U/sec.­9(m) and (n) read with section 10 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 7 years and to pay fine of Rs.1,000/­ [Rupees One Thousand only] and in default of payment of fine, to suffer S.I. for 10 days. (3) Both the substantive sentences shall run concurrently. (4) The accused is in jail since 08/07/2013. A set off under section 438 of Cr.P.C. is granted to him against the substantive sentence for the term of the period of detention undergone by him during the investigation, inquiry and trial. = 36 = (5) The accused is acquitted for the offence punishable U/sec.­ 377 of the Indian Penal Code. (6) Muddemal property being worthless be destroyed after period of appeal. (7) Copy of judgment be given to the accused free of cost. (8) The proceeding is closed. Date : 08.10.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Additional Session Judge­1, Thane.
