.. 1 .. Special case 70/2013 Judgment Received on : 01/10/2013 Registered on : 01/10/2013 Decided on : 19/05/2015 Duration : 01 Y. 07 M. 18 D. In The Court of the Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012, Thane) At Thane (Presided over by Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Case No. 70 of 2013 Exhibit No. 27 The State of Maharashtra (Through Kapurbawdi police station) … Complainant Versus Mahendra Hirasheth Soni Age 54 years, Residing at Near Dashrath Patil ground, Azad Nagar, Thane. … Accused Appearances :­ A.P.P. Mr. A. K. Khamkar for the State. Advocate Mr. Santosh Sawardekar for the accused. JUDGMENT (Delivered on 19th May, 2015) Accused stands prosecuted for the offences punishable under section 354 of Indian Penal Code and punishable under .. 2 .. Special case 70/2013 Judgment section 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter referred as POCSO Act in short) for using criminal force on minor girl Kasturi aged 5 years, out raging her modesty by removing her clothes and his own clothes and moving his hand on her entire body and committing sexual assault on victim girl on 08/06/2013 and since about before one month before 08/06/2013 near Dashrath Patil Ground, Azad Nagar, Thane. 2] In short the facts giving rise to the prosecution of the accused are that victim girl Kasturi had been staying with her parents and siblings at Ghadwali chawl, near Vishal Trading Kirana Stores, Azad Nagar, Thane on rental basis. Her parents had been doing job. Both used to leave the house in the morning and return in the evening. Victim girl and her siblings used to be at home and her elder sister used to look after Kasturi and her brother. 3] It is also case of the prosecution that accused had been staying near Dashrath Patil ground at Azad Nagar and he was working in cardboard company. Accused used to visit the house of person staying in neighbourhood of the girl Kasturi and therefore they were acquainted and he was known to the girl Kasturi and her parents by face. The victim girl Kasturi as well as other children used to call accused as Mahendra uncle. 4] It is further case of the prosecution that accused used to go to the house of girl Kasturi and used to take girl Kasturi to his house by enticing her by giving biscuits and chocolates and by removing his clothes and by removing her clothes he used to move .. 3 .. Special case 70/2013 Judgment his hand on entire body of the girl and he used to do such act since about one month prior to 07/06/2013. It is further case that on 07/06/2013 girl Kasturi alongwith other children was playing in front of their house and that time Kasturi had disclosed neighbouring women Annu Danial Khema about act committed by accused since about one month with her. After mother of girl returned home, neighbouring women Annu informed her mother about act committed by accused with her daughter. Then, when her mother questioned girl Kasturi about it, Kasturi narrated same facts to her. Then again on 09/06/2013 in the evening accused had been to the house of girl Kasturi and that time her sister Suman questioned him about the act committed by him with Kasturi and was shouting at him and therefore, neighbouring persons had gathered there. Then, after knowing about the act committed by accused, they caught him, beat him and took him to the police station. Thereafter, after learning about it, mother of girl went to the police station and lodged complaint and police arrested the accused, since he was already taken to the police station. 5] On the basis of complaint offence under C.R. No I 215/13 was registered under section 354 of IPC and under section 8 of POCSO Act and work of investigation was done by PSI Mandavkar. During the investigation statement of girl was recorded in question and answer form. Panchanma of spot was prepared and statements of witnesses including neighbouring women Annu Danial Khema were recorded and after completion of investigation since there was sufficient evidence against accused, he came to be chargesheeted for .. 4 .. Special case 70/2013 Judgment the offences punishable under section 354 of IPC and section 8 of POCSO Act. 6] Since the offences punishable under POCSO Act are triable Special Court, this being Special Court for trying cases under POCSO Act, charge­sheet was submitted to this Court. The accused was produced before the Court. A charge under section 354 of IPC and section 8 of POCSO Act was framed against the accused vide Exh. 6. Contents of charge was read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. He pleaded not guilty. His defence as revealed from the cross examination of witnesses and statement of accused recorded under section 313 of Cr.P.C. was of total denial. He claimed to be tried. 7] For establishing the offences charged against the accused, prosecution examined P.W.1 complainant ­ the mother of the girl, Shardadevi Kailash Jaiswal, P.W.2 victim girl Kasturi Kailash Jaiswal, P.W.3 Annu Danial Khema ­ neighbouring women, P.W.4 Danial Yunus Khema ­ Panch, P.W.5 Police officer Sanjay Bhagwandas Sadigale, who recorded the complaint of complainant and P.W.6 father of girl Kailasnath Satai Jaiswal. The documentary evidence produced, proved and relied upon by prosecution consists arrest panchanama at Exh.18 and complaint at Exh.22. 8] Statement of accused under section 313 of Cr.P.C. was recorded. Accused did not examine himself on oath and had not examined any witness in his defence. .. 5 .. Special case 70/2013 Judgment 9] On the basis of above facts of case, following points which arises for my determination and I record my findings thereon for the reasons mentioned as under. POINTS FINDINGS 1) Whether prosecution proved that since one month before of 08.06.2013 near Dashrath Patil ground, Azad Nagar, Thane, within the jurisdiction of Kapurbawdi police station, accused used criminal force on Kasturi, a minor daughter of complainant aged five years, by removing her and his clothes and moving hand over her whole body intending to outrage her modesty or knowing it to be likely that he would thereby outraging her modesty? ... Yes. 2) Whether prosecution proved that on the date, day, time and place and during the period of one month as mentioned above, accused committed sexual assault on the victim girl Kasturi aged about Five years by outraging her modesty? ... Yes. 3) What offence, if any, is committed by ... Committed an offences accused? punishable under section 354 of IPC and section 8 of POCSO Act. 4) What order? ... The accused is convicted and punished as per final order. .. 6 .. Special case 70/2013 Judgment REASONS AS TO POINT Nos. 1 TO 3 :­ 10] All these points are interconnected and required to be decided on the basis of same evidence, I therefore discuss and decide all the points together. 11] As it is clear as per the prosecution case, the complainant, victim girl and accused have been acquaintance of each other. As per the prosecution case, victim girl at the time of incident was aged about 5 years and accused who is said to be aged about 53 years is stated to have committed such an act of sexual assault with girl either by going to her house when her parents were not there and/or taking her to his house and alleged to have committed such an act for about one month before the accused actually was caught on 09/06/2013. Then since the accused is charged for offences punishable under section 354 and also under section 8 of POCSO Act, it is required to see as to what are the ingredients to establish offence against accused. Section 354 provides; "Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any woman, intending to outrage or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby outrage her modesty, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than one year but which may extend to five years, and shall also liable to fine." .. 7 .. Special case 70/2013 Judgment Then, section 7 of POCSO Act defines "Sexual assault" as under; "Whoever, with sexual intent touches the vagina, penis, anus or breast of the child or makes the child touch the vagina, penis, anus or breast of such person or any other person, or does any other act with sexual intent which involves physical contact without penetration is said to commit sexual assault." 12] Then since it is alleged that accused, by coming to the house of victim girl and/or by taking her to his house, and removin clothes of girl Kasturi and also clothes on his person moved his hand on the body of girl by using criminal force, it can be said that the act alleged against the accused fall within the purview of section 354 of IPC and section 7 of POCSO Act, which is punishable under section 8 of said Act. Then it is required to see whether such allegations are proved by the prosecution by cogent and reliable evidence. 13] In that respect it is material to mention that complainant in her evidence appear to have stated that on the day when accused was caught when she returned from job, neighbouring women Annu Danial Khema informed her that accused has been beaten by public and they are taken him to Kapurbawdi police station and her daughter was also taken to the police station because of the act done by accused with her daughter Kasturi. She also further stated that she then went to Kapurbawdi police station and her daughter was there in the police station. Then though she .. 8 .. Special case 70/2013 Judgment did not support the prosecution case in regard to lodging of complaint or complaint being recorded as per her narration, etc. in her further evidence she appear to have stated that when she asked her daughter Kasturi, she told her that Mahendra uncle removed her nicker and Annu aunty had beaten him. She even clarified that it was stated to her by her daughter Kasturi before her thumb impression was obtained on the complaint. 14] So far as aspect as to whether when the complaint was lodged by complainant i.e. mother of girl and whether it was recorded as per narration of the complainant, etc., I would deal with on and at this stage only material aspect is, what is evidence about acts alleged to have been committed by accused. In that respect as discussed above from the testimony of the complainant, it is clear that accused and girl were taken to the police station and then the girl had narrated her mother i.e complainant that accused had removed her nicker and accused was beaten by people. 15] In the light of that if the testimony of the girl perused carefully, it has to be mentioned that the girl at the time of deposition was aged 7 years. Therefore, to ascertain as to whether she is able to understand the questions put to her and answer it coherently and relevantly, certain questions were put to her about her name, address, school and she was found to be able to understand the questions and had answered it properly and coherently. Even further to ascertain that she knows the sanctity of oath, certain question were put to her and from the answers given by .. 9 .. Special case 70/2013 Judgment her it was confirmed that she knows the sanctity and importance of oath and therefore oath was administered to her. 16] As such after ascertaining capacity of the child witness to answer questions coherently when her evidence was recorded, in her evidence she appear to have said that she knows accused and she calls him Mahendra uncle. She also specified that accused had been to their house once. Then in her further evidence she stated that once she was returning home from school, Mahendra uncle took her to his house, which is near to the school and nobody else was there in the house of accused and accused that time removed her nicker and also his clothes and slept over her. He touched her back and after two minutes he left her, then she wore her pant. She also further stated that then again one day accused wanted her to take to his house but she ran away. She also specified that Annu aunty asked her as to what had happened and she narrated entire incident to her and then Annu aunty and others had beaten Mahendra uncle and they were taken to police station. 17] Her such version that she narrated incident to Annu aunty is also corroborated by the testimony of P.W.3 Annu Danial Khema who stated that on one day at about 4.00 p.m., Kasturi was playing in front of their house and that time she stated that Mahendra uncle called her at his house and even come to their house, give her chocolate, biscuit and remove her clothes and his clothes and move his hand on her entire body. She further stated that after mother of girl Sharadadevi returned from her job she .. 10 .. Special case 70/2013 Judgment informed entire incident to her and mother of the girl had warned Kasturi not to go with accused. She also further stated that once accused had come to the house of complainant and that time girl Kasturi and her elder sister started shouting at him while he was behaving same with her sister that time people gathered there, caught and beaten accused, then police came and took him to the police station. 18] As is further clear P.W.6 is father of the girl Kasturi Jaiswal, who also stated that he knows accused since accused was staying in the same area Azad Nagar and on 07/06/2013 when he returned home, his wife told that accused Mahendra had done wrong act with Kasturi by removing her nicker and when he asked her daughter, she also told same thing and neighbouring persons also told same thing and then his wife lodged complaint. On careful perusal of cross examination of the witnesses on behalf of accused, it reveals that nothing contrary is brought on record on the basis of which it can be said that they deposing falsely. 19] Even the fact that accused was caught and beaten by public and handed over to the police, is also clear from the testimony of the said witnesses and also from the testimony of P.W.5 PSI Sanjay Sadigale and Panch witness P.W.4 Danial Khema. As is clear Panch witness P.W.4 stated that on 09/06/2013 he was called by police of Kapurbawdi police station. Accused was there and he was having signs of beaten like swelling eyes, injury to knee and it was reported that accused was beaten by public and police arrested .. 11 .. Special case 70/2013 Judgment him and prepared panchnama of arrest as per Exh.18. Even the fact that he was caught by public and was taken to police station when put to the accused in his statement recorded under section 313 of Cr.P.C., appear to have answered in affirmative. 20] Then, so far as actual incident of girl being taken to house of accused and committing an act of sexual harassment and assault on the girl, it has to be mentioned that testimony of the girl as mentioned above, appear to have totally gone unchallenged and undisputed since except suggesting that accused had not done any act and she deposing falsely which she denied, nothing contrary was brought on record in her cross examination to falsify her version and/or even to create any reasonable doubt about her testimony. In that regard it has to be mentioned that age of the girl was about 7 years and she appear to have stated and narrated facts as per per her understanding. No doubt no witness has stated the actual dates of the incident. But in the light of the fact that girl is very small about 5 to 7 years age and witnesses being rustic witnesses, the aspect that they were not able to tell the dates, cannot be given much importance and as is clear that main purport of the matter has been stated by them. Even, when the statement of the girl was recorded in question and answer form, the girl narrated facts and not only that even she was testified before the court and she narrated the same fact and her version that she narrated all the facts on the same day to Annu aunty also corroborated by evidence of P.W.3 Annu Khema. .. 12 .. Special case 70/2013 Judgment 21] No doubt complainant in her evidence has not supported the prosecution case in regard to the lodging of complaint and appear to have resiled from her earlier statement that complaint was lodged by her and contents thereof were recorded as per her narration. But then in that respect also it has to be mentioned that initially P.W.1 complainant appear to have stated that after she learnt that accused and her daughter were taken to the police station, she went to the police station and lot of public gathered there and then she lodged complaint. However, there after she contradicted herself by stating that before she went to the police station, the complaint and statement of her daughter was recorded and she did not want to lodge complaint, however her thumb impression was obtained on complaint already written. But then if her testimony in the examination­in­chief itself is perused, it is clear that she stated that her daughter Kasturi had narrated facts to her before her thumb impression was obtained on complaint. That make it clear that her version about complaint was already prepared and her thumb impression was obtained by police is not truthful version. 22] It is very much material to mentioned that at end of her examination in chief she has clearly stated that she do not want to proceed with the complaint and do not have any grievance against accused and that make the intention of complainant very clear not to support the prosecution case. Even it is further clear from the cross examination of the said witness on behalf of the accused that, she accepted that accused had not done any act of removing nicker of her daughter at any time. But then it is also material to note that she .. 13 .. Special case 70/2013 Judgment had denied suggestion that she deposed falsely and appear to have clarified that she stated whatever was told by her daughter to her and even her complaint also appear to be on the basis of facts narrated by her daughter to her. 23] In the light of that if testimony of P.W.5 PSI Sadigale is perused he stated that on 09/06/2013 Sharadadevi Jaiswal had been to the police station and lodged complaint and he recorded the complaint as per her narration and obtained her thumb impression and also specified that her statement at Exh.22 was recorded by him as per narration of the complainant correctly. In the light of the fact that complainant was unable to explain as to why police recorded said fact in her complaint, is to be considered and assumed importance and lead to the inference that only because such facts were stated by her, they were recorded by police and that also has been stated by P.W.5 PSI Sadigale. 24] Even it is evident and apparent that complainant did not support prosecution that she lodged complaint as per Exh.22 only for the reason as stated by her in her examination in chief that she did not want to proceed with the complaint and do not have grievance against accused. And even it is very much clear that fact that mother of the girl was lodged complaint was also stated by other witnesses including father of the girl P.W.6 Kailasnath. Therefore it has to be concluded that the complaint was lodged by mother of the girl on the basis of facts narrated by her daughter to her. .. 14 .. Special case 70/2013 Judgment 25] Then as discussed above the facts have been stated by the girl in regard to the act committed by the accused are even corroborated by the testimony of other witnesses in regard to the conduct of the girl narrating said facts to them. 26] Even so far as act alleged to have been committed by the accused and the important, relevant and material aspect which struck to me appear to be appealing and convincing, is that, in her cross examination when it was suggested to her by accused in person that accused has not done any such act with her and she is deposing falsely, she appear to have denied said suggestion and even voluntarily added by categorically saying that her friend Rupali would also say the same thing. That it makes it clear that such an act was committed by accused within the knowledge of her friend Rupali. 27] One more aspect of matter is that though accused come up with the case that he has not committed any such act, and he is falsely implicated in the crime, there is absolutely no material brought on record and no reason is put forward by accused for which such complaint with such false allegations in regard to the minor girl aged about 5­6 years would be made by the complainant against him. It is very much material to mention that from the testimony of the mother of the girl it appears that mother came up with case that she do not have any grievance with accused, must be for the reason that elders have settled the dispute. But girl is ignorance and innocent appear to have not understood the reason for which mother .. 15 .. Special case 70/2013 Judgment do not support the prosecution case and appear to have stated during evidence. It is to be mentioned that at the time of girl also found to be under pressure of her mother because initially at the one point of time she appear to have said that she do not know the accused. But again in next breath she appear to know him and call him Mahendra uncle. Similar is her conduct while deposing before the court when she stated that Mahendra uncle had been to their house in the night when her mother was at home. But then in her further evidence she stated that once accused took her to his house when nobody was there and appear to have stated about the incident. Even from the perusal of entire testimony of the girl as a whole and her version in cross examination by accused, it is very much clear that accused had committed such act of taking girl to his house and removed her clothes and moved his hand on her body. Even from her version it is clear that even again he had been to the house of girl and that time he was caught. 28] In view of above all discussion, it is clear from the testimony of the girl Kasturi corroborated the testimony of other witnesses that accused took the girl to his house, removed clothes on the person of the girl and had removed his clothes and slept over her and also moved his hand on her body which is an act of sexual assault as defined under section 7 of POCSO Act and thereby he outraged the modesty of the girl. It has to be mentioned that as per section 29 of POCSO Act there is presumption and it provides that where a person is prosecuted for committing any offence under sections 3, 5 and 7 of the Act, Court shall presume that such person .. 16 .. Special case 70/2013 Judgment has committed such offence unless contrary is proved. However, as is clear the accused has not brought anything contrary to what is stated by victim girl as mentioned above. Absolutely nothing is brought on record even to create doubt in the mind that such act was not done by accused. In such circumstances when nothing contrary is proved by the accused and when as discussed above evidence brought on record by prosecution, is held to have been sufficient to prove allegations against the accused, it has to be concluded that prosecution has established that accused has committed such act. It is also to be mentioned that when the act proved to have been committed by the accused is of nature of removing clothes of the girl and sleeping over her, culpable mental state of the accused to commit such an act with sexual intention is very much clear. Even as per section 30 of POCSO Act, there is presumption of existence of such culpable mental state. Then even at the cost of repetition it can be said that accused had not taken up any defence that he had no such culpable mental state. 29] In view of all the above discussion, it has to be concluded that prosecution has established beyond all the reasonable doubt that accused used criminal force on minor girl Kasturi aged about 5 years and moved his hand on her entire body by removing her clothes and his clothes with a view to outraging her modesty and slept over her and his such an act is sexual assault within purview of Section 7 of POCSO Act and I therefore hold accused guilty for the offences punishable under section 354 of IPC and under section 8 of POCSO Act and convict him for the said offences. .. 17 .. Special case 70/2013 Judgment 30] At this stage the dictation of the Judgment is postponed for hearing the accused on the point of sentence. Date : 19/05/2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012) Thane. 31] It is informed to the accused that offence punishable under section 354 of IPC and section 7 of POCSO Act is proved against him and that offence under section 354 IPC is punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to five years and is also liable to fine and offence under section 7 r/w. 8 of POCSO Act is punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to five years and is also liable to fine and that he can submit on the point of sentence. 32] I heard the accused and the learned A.P.P. on the point of sentence. 33] It was submitted by the accused that he is having family to maintain and the member of family are depending on him and the accused is the only earning member in his family. It is further submitted that it is first offence of the accused. Even it is submitted by the accused that he is repenting over such act. It was therefore submitted that accused may be given an opportunity to reform and he may be shown leniency and be awarded with punishment as has .. 18 .. Special case 70/2013 Judgment already been undergone by him. 34] It is submitted by the learned A.P.P. that the offence proved against the accused is of very serious nature. It is further submitted that in such circumstance the accused does not deserve leniency and maximum punishment prescribed for offences proved against the accused, may be imposed upon the accused. 35] So far as the quantum of sentence is concerned, it has to be mentioned that it is well settled that it is the duty of the Court in every case to award proper sentence, having regard to the nature of the offence, the manner in which it is committed and to all mitigating circumstances put forward. Even it is also well settled that in the matter of fixation of punishment for any particular crime, the Court should take into consideration the nature of offence, the circumstances in which it was committed and the degree of deliberation shown by the offender and also that the measure of punishment should be proportionate to the gravity of the offence and it is also the responsibility of the Court to see that the sentence should not be excessive and at the same time it should not be too lenient or liberal. 36] Taking into consideration the above settled principles in respect of grant of punishment the quantum of punishment for offence under section 354 of IPC and section 8 of POCSO Act is required to be decided in the present case. .. 19 .. Special case 70/2013 Judgment 37] In that respect it is to be mentioned that accused is an old person aged above 50­55 years and he appear to have been indulging in such crime against minor girl aged about 5 years and even it appears that he had been indulging in such an act for more than one instance and on the day, accused caught by public when he had been to the house of victim girl again and even it is clear that such an act is proved to have been committed by accused is made a serious offence under the provisions Special Act on Protection of Children from Sexual Offences providing minimum punishment for three years. But then the aspect also cannot be ignored that accused is an old person aged above 55 years and even it is submitted by the accused that it is his first offence and he is repenting over such act. Though that cannot be reason for showing leniency, in the light of the fact that accused who is of age of grandfather of the child indulged such heinous act, the submission on behalf of the prosecution that accused be punished for maximum term also cannot be said to be sustainable and acceptable for the reason that no criminal antecedents against accused are averred or established and the accused is seen to be repenting over his act. 38] Then, so far as quantum of punishment to be awarded to the accused in the present case when both offences under section 354 of IPC and section 7 r/w. 8 of POCSO Act are proved, the provision of section 42 of POCSO Act appear to be material and important. Section 42 of the POCSO Act provides : ''Where an act or omission constitutes an offence punishable under this Act and also under sections 166A, 354A, 354B, 354C, 354D, 370, 370A, 375, 376, 376A, .. 20 .. Special case 70/2013 Judgment 376C, 376D, 376E or section 509 of the Indian Penal Code, then notwithstanding anything contained in any law for the time being in force, the offender found guilty of such offence shall be liable to punishment under this Act or under the Indian Penal Code as provides for punishment which is greater in degree''. Then, as is clear the offence under section 354 of I.P.C. is punishable with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years or with fine whereas offence under section 7 read with section 8 of POCSO Act is punishable with imprisonment which shall not be less than 3 years and may extend to five years and also with fine. As such it is clear that sentence of imprisonment which can be awarded for commission of offence under section 7 read with section 8 of POCSO Act is severe and greater in degree as compared to section 354 of IPC. Therefore it can be said that as per provisions of section 42 of POCSO Act substantive sentence only for offence punishable under section 7 read with section 8 which is imprisonment greater in degree can be awarded to the accused. 39] In such circumstance looking to the facts and circumstance of the case, nature of offence proved and the manner in which the offence is stated to have been committed and looking to the further fact that the accused have been in jail since the date of his arrest on 09.06.2013, I am of the view that the accused need to be punished under section 7 r/w. section 8 of POCSO Act only and following sentence would meet ends of justice. In the result, I pass the following order ­ .. 21 .. Special case 70/2013 Judgment ORDER 1 ) Accused namely Mahendra Hirasheth Soni is convicted for the offences punishable under section 354 of the Indian Penal Code and also for offence punishable under section 7 read with section 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and by invoking provisions of Section 42 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012, the accused is sentenced to suffer Rigorous Imprisonment for the term of three years and to pay fine of Rs.500/­ [rupees five hundred only] and in default of payment of fine amount, to suffer S.I. for fifteen days for commission of offence punishable under section 7 read with section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act only. 2 ) The accused is in jail since 09/06/2013. A set off under section 438 of Cr.P.C. is granted to him for the term of the period of detention undergone by him during the investigation, inquiry and trial against the substantive sentence imposed upon him. 3 ) Since no muddemal property is produced before Court, no order regarding its disposal is passed. 4 ) Copy of judgment be given to the accused free of cost. 5 ) The proceeding is closed. Date : 19/05/2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012) Thane.

Bail No.2041//2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exhibit 1 in Criminal Bail Application No.2041/2015 This application is filed by applicant Sunil @ Prakash Kautik Patil for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. I-380/2015 registered at Vashi police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 344, 346, 363, 365, 366, 370, 376 of I.P.C., section 4, 5, 6 of Prevention of Immoral Traffic Act and section 3, 4, 5, 6 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that he used to come with his friends in the house at Jugaon where complainant was staying with other accused and used to do sexual intercourse with other girls in the exchange of money. It is further contended that accused Shivam Kalawat had kidnapped complainant and forcibly committed sexual intercourse with her and accused Shivam Kalawat, Archana Kalawat and Sita Kalawat in furtherance of common intention confined the complainant, compelled complainant and other girls to do prostitution and earned money from said business. It is further contended and argued that he is innocent and he is falsely implicated in the offence. It is further contended and argued that applicant has not made sexual assault on the victim girls. It is further contended and argued that looking to the nature of allegations, the investigation in the matter may have almost completed and therefore, there is no need of further custody of the applicant/accused. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. .. 2 .. Bail No.2041//2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply as per Exhibit 3 and it is contended that the accused persons including the applicant used to force the victim girls to indulge into prostitution and that the accused were thereby earning livelihood in the form of money accepted from the customers. It is further contended and argued that the aspect as to whom the complainant girl was sold has to be investigated into. It is further submitted that there is possibility of the applicant/accused threatening the complainant if released on bail and he may pressurize other victim girls and other prosecution witnesses also. It is also contended and argued that if released on bail, the possibility of the applicant repeating the offence cannot be ruled out. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under sections 344, 346, 363, 365, 366, 370, 376 of I.P.C. and sections 3, 4, 5, 6 of P.O.C.S.O. and sections 4, 5, 6 of P.I.T.A with the allegation of forcing the complainant and other victims to do prostitution by doing sexual intercourse with other persons and the applicant himself, it is contended on behalf of applicant that other accused persons were forcing the complainant and other girls to indulge in prostitution and applicant is alleged to be a customer and that he has not committed any offence. In such circumstance the allegations the aspect as to whether the allegations against the accused are true or not, would be the question to be decided on merits. Even nothing is stated to be recovered from the applicant/accused. 4] Then, it is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be .. 3 .. Bail No.2041//2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 5] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 6] Then, it has also to be mentioned that the investigation in this case is yet not completed and it will take to time to complete the investigation and then to file the charge- sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 7] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant/accused can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order - ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Sunil @ Prakash Kautik Patil is released on P.R. bond of Rs.20,000/- [rupees twenty thousand only] with one or two surety/sureties in the like amount, subject to following conditions - He shall not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and the .. 4 .. Bail No.2041//2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this Court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 16.09.2015 (Mrs.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.

Bail No.2046/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exhibit 1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 2046/2015 This application is filed by applicant Pawan Satranj Singh for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. I-196/2015 registered at Bhiwandi Taluka police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 375 of I.P.C. and section 4, 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant had induced minor daughter of the complainant and then had sexual intercourse with her by giving false assurance of marriage. It is further contended and argued that there was love affair between the girl and the accused and it is a case of consent. It is further contended and argued that the applicant has no criminal antecedents and that he is falsely implicated. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co- operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that taking disadvantage of minor age of daughter of the complainant the accused induced and enticed her by giving false promise of marriage and then had sexual intercourse with her. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl, complainant and other prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. .. 2 .. Bail No.2046/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 376 of I.P.C. and section 4, 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act with the allegation of committing sexual assault victim girl who is stated to be 17 years old, it is contended on behalf of accused that the girl and the accused were in love with each other and it is a case of consent and that he is falsely implicated in the crime. In such circumstance whether the allegations against the accused are true or not, would be the question to be decided on merits. Even nothing is stated to be recovered from the applicant/accused. 4] Then, it is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 5] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 6] Then, it has also to be mentioned that looking the allegations against the accused the investigation in the matter may have almost completed but the charge-sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge- sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to .. 3 .. Bail No.2046/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 7] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order - ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Pawan Satrang Singh is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/- [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one local surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions - The applicant/accused shall attend the concerned police station as and when called till filing of the charge-sheet and shall co- operate in investigation. He shall not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and the prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this Court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 21.09.2015 (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Additional Session Judge-1, Thane.

Hence, he is facing trial under Section 354 of the Indian Penal Code ( in short “the IPC) and U/sec.7 r.w 8 of the Prevention of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 ( in short “POSCO Act”) :2 : S.C.C.No.71/13(Jud.) [2] Brief facts of the prosecution case are as under :­­ Informant Chandrakant Panmand alongwith his wife and daughter – “X” (name is not mentioned) and his brother Suresh, Nanda­w/o Suresh and his sons are jointly residing at Vashi, Navi Mumbai. He was carrying business of Road Transportation. In the year 2013, his daughter X was studying in 3rd standard Rayon School, Nerul, Navi Mumbai. X used to go for private tuitions everyday in between 6 p.m to 8 p.m., conducted by the accused and his wife in the building situated near the house of the informant. [3] That on 25.07.13 as usual X went to the tuition class at the house of the accused at 6 p.m. At about 7.30 p.m she came back and she was scared. Therefore, Anita­wife of the informant made phone call to the informant and informed him that something had happened with X and she was crying. Therefore, immediately thereafter he came to his house. He enquired with X, at that time she disclosed that, on that day the tuition class was ended early and the accused asked X to wait. Therefore, she was alone waiting in the class. Thereafter the accused gave X a chocolate and took her near him. The accused inserted his hand in her dress and touched her chest. Thereafter the accused made X to seat on his lap and touched her private part by finger. At that time he realised that somebody else has entered in the class. Therefore he released X. Then the accused told X not to disclosed this thing to anybody. Therefore, she came back. :3 : S.C.C.No.71/13(Jud.) [4] Thereafter, the informant alongwith his wife and daughter X went to the house of the accused and called him out. Therefore, the accused came out. X pointed out her finger towards the accused and disclosed that, he committed said act with her. The informant enquired with the accused. At that time there was hot talk between them. Therefore, people gathered there and they beat the accused by fist and kick blows. Thereafter, the informant and others took the accused to Vashi Police Station, where the informant lodged information about the incident. On the basis of the said information, crime vide C.R. No.266/2013 under Section 354 of IPC and U/sec.7 r.w 8 of the POSCO Act came to be registered and handed over to API Kadam (PW.6) for investigation. [5] API Kadam forwarded the victim girl i.e. X to the Municipal Hospital Navi Mumbai for medical examination. Thereafter, he arrested the accused and prepared arrest panchanama. On the same night he visited to the spot of incident and prepared panchanama of the spot in presence of panch witnesses. Further investigation of the crime was handed over to PI Gaikwad (PW.7). [6] PI Gaikwad recorded statements of the witnesses. In the meanwhile on 28.07.13 WPSI V. U. Kamble recorded statement of the victim girl – X. PI Gaikwad then collected copy of the birth certificate of the victim girl and also collected her medical certificate. On completion of the investigation, he submitted chargesheet against the accused under Section 354 of the IPC and U/sec.7 r.w 8 of the POSCO Act, in the Court of JMFC, Vashi. :4 : S.C.C.No.71/13(Jud.) [7] Since the offence under Section 7 r.w 8 of the POCSO Act is triable exclusively by the Special Court , the Ld. JMFC, Vashi committed the case to this Court. [8] My Ld. Predecessor framed Charge (Ex.3) against the accused under Sections 354 of the IPC and U/sec.7 r.w 8 of the POSCO Act. Particulars of the offence were read over and explained to the accused to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. [10] Statement of the accused under Section 313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is recorded. He denied allegations made by the prosecution. His defence is that X was studying in his tuition class. After 8 days of her admission in the class he asked for fees, however parents of X were avoiding to pay the fees. As he repeatedly demanded fees from them, they have filed false case against him. [11] Following points arise for my determination. I have recorded my findings thereon for the reasons stated below. SNO POINTS FINDINGS 1 Whether prosecution prove that the accused by using criminal force sexually assaulted X, a minor girl and thereby outraged her modesty Yes and committed offence U/sec.354 of the IPC? 2 Whether prosecution prove that the accused sexually assaulted X, a minor girl and thereby committed offence U/sec.7 r.w 8 of the Yes. POCSO Act? 3 What order ? Accused is convicted. :5 : S.C.C.No.71/13(Jud.) REASONS [12] AS TO POINTS NO. 1 AND 2 :­ After an amendment Sec.354 of the IPC speaks thus:­ "354. Sexual Assault and Punishment for sexual assault:­ (1) The following acts shall constitute the offence of sexual assault:­ (a) Intentional touching of another person when such act of touching is of a sexual nature and it without the recipient's consent; (b) Using words, acts or gestures towards or in the presence of another person which create an unwelcome threat of a sexual nature or result in an unwelcome advance. Explanation: For the purposes of this section, 'acts' shall include the display and dissemination of pornographic material." [13] Sec.7 of the POCSO Act speaks thus:­ "7. Sexual assault.­ Whoever, with sexual intent touches the vagina, penis, anus or breast of the child or makes the child touch the vagina, penis, anus or breast of such person or any other person, or does any other act with sexual intent which involves physical contact without penetration is said to commit sexual assault." [14] Thus, on plain reading of the provision U/sec.354 of the IPC and U/sec.7 of the POCSO Act, it appears that, ingredients of these sections are almost similar. Only to establish offence U/sec.7 of the POCSO Act the victim should be a child. As per Sec.2 (d) of the POCSO Act, “child” means any person below the age of 18 years. :6 : S.C.C.No.71/13(Jud.) [15] According to the prosecution the incident took place on 25.07.13 and birth date of X ­the victim girl is 21.10.04. Therefore at the time of the incident she was about 9 years old minor girl. However, from the defence taken by the accused it appears that, he has not admitted that, the victim girl was 9 years old. Ld. Advocate for the accused submitted that, though the prosecution witnesses has stated that, the victim girl was born on 21.10.04 and she was child, no reliable evidence has been produced on the record. Hence, it cannot be held that, at that time of the incident the victim girl was child. [16] In this connection, on perusal of the evidence of the prosecution, it appears that, Chandrakant (PW.1) father of X­ the victim girl states that, her birth date is 21.10.04. X­ (PW.2) herself deposed before the court that, her birth date is 1.10.04 and in the year 2013 she was studying in 3rd standard. During the investigation PI Gaikwad (PW.7) collected copy of the birth certificate of X, which is produced on the record. It is uncertified photo copy of the birth certificate. It shows date of birth of X as 21.10.04. No doubt uncertified copy of such birth certificate cannot be relied upon. [17] However, the prosecution has adduced evidence of Dr. Meenakshi (PW.5) who medically examine the victim girl and issued medical certificate (Ex.40). It has come in her evidence and it is mentioned in the said certificate that, x­ray of shoulder and elbows of the victim girl were taken and the concern radiologist opined that, the said girl was < 14 years ? 9 years. :7 : S.C.C.No.71/13(Jud.) [18] Ld.Advocate for the accused submitted that, Dr.Meenakshi (PW.5) in her cross­examination admitted that, she has not recorded remark regarding age of the victim girl in the said medical certificate (Ex.40). Therefore, her evidence cannot be taken into consideration. Moreover the prosecution has not examine the said radiologist who recorded his opinion about the age of the victim girl. In the absence of such evidence it cannot be held that, the victim girl was child. [19] No doubt the prosecution has produced on record authenticated copy of the birth certificate of the victim girl. Similarly the prosecution has not examine the radiologist who opined that the victim girl is < 14 years ? 9 years' child. However, it is interesting to note that, the accused through his cross­ examination and in his statement U/sec.313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure has admitted that, in the year 2013 the victim girl was studying in 3rd standard and she was studying in his tuition classes. Therefore, if the above mentioned facts and circumstances taken into consideration together it will revealed that, by stretch of any imagination any prudent man cannot said that, a girl studying in 3rd standard is not a minor girl. Therefore, having regard to the material placed on the record, I have no hesitation to hold that, at the time of the incident X­ the victim girl was studying in 3 rd standard and she was “child” as defined in Sec.2 (d) of the POCSO Act. [20] Chandrakant (PW.1), the father of the victim girl states that, on 25.07.13 at about 8.30 p.m he received a phone call from :8 : S.C.C.No.71/13(Jud.) his wife. She informed him that, X is frightened and something is happened, hence come immediately. Therefore within 15 minutes he reached to his house. He found that, X was in the bed room alongwith his wife and sister­in­law. He enquired with X, at that time she disclosed that, “Garud Sir (the accused) sent all students early and stopped her for some time. Thereafter, he enquired with her what she want to learn. Thereafter, he gave her a chocolate and took her near him. Thereafter he moved his hand over her breast by inserting his hand in her top. Thereafter, he inserted his hand in his nicker and moved his hand over her nunni (private part). Thereafter he made her to seat over his lap and he took her on his private part and shake her body up and down”. X further disclosed him that, “she was frightened. At that time, some sound was heard, therefore Garud Sir (the accused) released her and told her not to speak with anybody”. [21] Chandrakant (PW.1) further states that, thereafter he alongwith his wife and daughter X went to the house of the accused and called his out. When he came out X confirmed that, he was the same person who committed the said act. Thereafter there was exchanges of hot words between them. Therefore, people gathered there and they beat the accused by fists and kicks blows and thereafter took him to Vashi Police Station. Chandrakant (PW.1) lodged report (Ex.30). [22] X (PW.2)­ the victim girl was examined by the prosecution. At the time of giving evidence before the court her age was about 13 years. She states that, on 25.7.13 she went to the :9 : S.C.C.No.71/13(Jud.) tuition class as usual. On that day, wife of Garud Sir, the accused was not present, hence Garud Sir was teaching them. He took class of general knowledge and mental maths. On that day at about 7.10 p.m., the class was over. Thereafter all other students went away. Garud Sir told her to wait. Thereafter he enquired with her as to what she want to learn. He offered her a chocolate. She told him that, she want to learn first Chapter of general knowledge subject. Thereafter he took her on his lap and inserted his hand in her T­ shirt and touched her breast. Thereafter, he inserted his hand in her nicker and touched her private part. Thereafter, he made her to seat on his private part and shake her body up and down. At that time he heard sound of something therefore, he presumed that, someone has came. Hence, he released her. She was scared and crying. Immediately thereafter he left the said spot and came back to home. She narrated the incident to her mother. Immediately thereafter her mother called her father. She narrated the incident to her father also. Thereafter, they went to the house of the accused. Her father called him out. When the accused came out she confirmed that, the accused is the person who committed the said act. The people gathered on the spot assaulted the accused and thereafter he was taken to the police station. [23] Ld.Advocate for the accused submitted that, evidence of Chandrakant (PW.1) and X (PW.2) is inconsistent to each other. Moreover they have improved their versions before the court. Therefore, their testimony cannot be believed. [24] The incident took place on 25.07.13. Evidence of Chandrakant (PW.1) was recorded on 26.12.17 whereas evidence : 10 : S.C.C.No.71/13(Jud.) of X (PW.2) was recorded on 11.01.18. It means their evidence came to be recorded in the court after lapse of about 4 to 5 years period. Therefore, some inconsistency and improvements are bound to be occurred in their evidence. Even if the improved part of their evidence is ignored it will revealed that, these two witnesses stick up with the prosecution story. Therefore, in my opinion other minor discrepancies and inconsistency are not fatal to their testimonies. [25] Ld.Advocate for the accused submitted that, according to the prosecution case, after lodging of FIR the victim girl was forwarded to Municipal Hospital for medical examination. However, on going through the material placed on the record and the evidence of Dr.Meenakshi (PW.5) it appears that, prosecution evidence is inconsistent even in respect of the alleged medical examination of the victim girl. Hence, reliance cannot be placed upon the said medical evidence and the accused cannot be held guilty. [26] Evidence of Chandrakant (PW.1) and X (PW.2) shows that, after lodging of FIR API Kadam (PW.6) forwarded the victim girl to Municipal Hospital, Navi Mumbai for medical examination. No doubt there is discrepancy in their evidence as regards to sending of the victim girl by police vehicle or any other vehicle. According to Chandrakant (PW.1) he took his daughter X by his own motorcycle to the Municipal Hospital, whereas X (PW.2) states that, she went to Municipal Hospital by police vehicle. : 11 : S.C.C.No.71/13(Jud.) [27] Dr.Meenakshi (PW.5) states that, she medically examined the victim girl. She was stated history that, the victim girl had gone to the class and the person tried to touch her private part, chest and back. According to her there was no external injury on the person of the victim girl. The examination findings were not suggesting regarding penetration. She issued a medical certificate (Ex.40). [28] In the circumstances, evidence of Chandrakant (PW.1), X (PW.2) and Dr.Meenakshi (PW.5) taken into consideration together it reveals that, on 26.07.13 at about 1.20 a.m the victim girl was medically examined by Dr.Meenakshi (PW.5). Even if the manner discrepancies in the evidence of these three witnesses are considered, I found that, the said discrepancies are not fatal to the prosecution case. Moreover, it is pertinent to note that, prosecution is not giving much importance to the said medical evidence because nothing incriminating was found against the accused in the said medical examination. Therefore, even if it is held that the prosecution has not proved that, the victim girl was examined by Dr.Meenakshi (PW.5) it will make no difference for the prosecution. [29] Ld. Advocate for the accused further submitted that, in order to prove fact of preparation of the spot panchanama prosecution has examined two witnesses viz. Bharat Patel (PW.3) (Ex.37) and Kiran Patel (PW.4) (Ex.38). However, both of them turned hostile and declined to support the prosecution case. Therefore, their evidence cannot be relied upon. Prosecution has adduced evidence of API Kadam (PW.6) (Ex.43). According to him : 12 : S.C.C.No.71/13(Jud.) he prepared panchanama of the spot vide Ex.44. However, as mentioned above panch witnesses are not supporting to the prosecution case, hence the prosecution failed to prove the spot of the incident. [30] However, in my opinion even if above prosecution witnesses failed to prove preparation of the spot panchanama it will make no difference for the prosecution case, because it is no where disputed by the accused that, he was conducting tuition classes in his house and the victim girl was student in his said tuition classes. Moreover, nothing incriminating has been found or seized by the I.O from the spot of the incident. Therefore, non proving of spot panchanama in this case not fatal to the prosecution case. [31] Ld. Advocate for the accused submitted that, in the present matter investigation conducted by the I.O is not proper. There are many mistakes in investigation. He has not produced entries of station diary to support his testimony. The I.O has not recorded statements of students who were studying alongwith the victim girl. So also prosecution has not examine the persons who witness the incident of quarrel which had allegedly taken place at the house of the accused. All these infirmities show that, the prosecution has not adduced sufficient and cogent evidence to prove the guilt of accused. Hence, the accused is entitled to be acquitted. In support of his argument he relied upon the decision of the Hon'ble High Court in the matter of Karuppaiah vs. State, Criminal Appeal No.659 of 2014 dated 18.01.16. : 13 : S.C.C.No.71/13(Jud.) [32] So far non examination of the persons who witnessed the incident of quarrel taken place between the accused and the father of the victim girl at the hands of the accused is concern, in my opinion evidence of the said witnesses was not important in order to prove the guilt of accused. Because the accused himself admitted that, father of the victim girl alongwith other persons had came to his house and there was exchanges of hot words between them. He has also admitted that, he was beaten by those persons and thereafter they took him to police station. Therefore, non examination of the said witnesses makes no difference. [33] Ld. Advocate for the accused also raised the point that, mother of the victim girl was the important witness in this case. However, prosecution has not examine her. It is well settled that, evidence is to be assessed on its quality and not on the quantity. Moreover, it is well settled that, solitary testimony of an eye witness is sufficient to prove the guilt of accused. In the circumstances non examination of the mother of the victim girl is not fatal to the prosecution case. [34] Ld. Advocate for the accused further raised the point regarding recording of statement of the victim girl by police officer or the Magistrate. According to him as per Sec.26 of the POCSO Act, the statement of the victim girl was required to be recorded by police or the Magistrate in presence of the parents of the child or any other person in whom the child has trust or confidence. However, in this case it has come in the evidence that, the statement of a victim girl was recorded about 3 days after the : 14 : S.C.C.No.71/13(Jud.) incident i.e. on 28.07.13. Moreover, at the time of recording of her statement nobody was present there. Her parents were kept outside the said room. Therefore, there is no compliance of Sec.26. Hence, the statement of the victim girl cannot be relied upon. [35] Sec.26 of the POCSO Act, reads as under:­ "26. Additional provisions regarding statement to be recorded.­ 1. The Magistrate or the police officer, as the case may be, shall record the statement as spoken by the child in die presence of the parents of the child or any other person in whom the child has trust or confidence. 2. Wherever necessary, the Magistrate or the police officer, as the case may be, may take the assistance of a translator or an interpreter, having such qualifications, experience and on payment of such fees as may be prescribed, while recording the statement of the child. 3. The Magistrate or the police officer, as the case may be, may, in the case of a child having a mental or physical disability, seek the assistance of a special educator or any person familiar with the manner of communication of the child or an expert in that field, having such qualifications, experience and on payment of such fees as may be prescribed, to record the statement of the child. 4. Wherever possible, the Magistrate or the police officer, as the case may be, shall ensure that the statement of the child is also recorded by audio­video electronic means." [36] On examination of the provisions U/sec.26 as above it appears that, it is an additional provision enacted for recording of statement of the victim child. In my opinion, the said provision : 15 : S.C.C.No.71/13(Jud.) compels to record statement of the child by Magistrate or the Police Officer. Therefore, word shall is used in the said provision. However later part of the said provision regarding presence of parents of the child or other person in whom the child has trust or confidence is concern, in my opinion the said provision is made so that the victim child should not scared of the police officer of the Magistrate while making statement and there should be conducive atmosphere around him so that the child should feel secured and comfortable while making statement before the Magistrate or the Police Officer. [37] In the present matter, the FIR regarding the incident was lodged immediately after the incident. It is well settled that, lodging of FIR immediately after the incident inspires the confidence. In the present matter WPSI Kamble recorded statement of the victim girl at the house of victim herself. However, at the time of recording of statement parents of the victim girl were kept outside the said building. However, it appears that, the statement of the victim girl recorded by police officer and her statement recorded before the court is consistent with the prosecution case as well as with the testimony of her father i.e. Chandrakant (PW.1). In the circumstances, only because at the time of recording of statement of the victim girl by police officer her parents were not present does not make the said statement worthless or unreliable. [38] It is well settled that, conviction of an accused can be based on the testimony of solitary witness. However, the testimony of the sole witness should be of sterling quality which should : 16 : S.C.C.No.71/13(Jud.) inspired the confidence of the court for its implicit acceptance. In the present case, on the basis of evidence adduced by the prosecution it appears that, testimony of X­the victim girl (PW.2) is sufficient and cogent to prove the guilt of accused. Moreover, her testimony is corroborated by her father Chandrakant (PW.1). Minor discrepancies and inconsistencies in their evidence are not fatal. I found no reason to disbelieve their testimonies. [39] It takes me to examine the defence taken by the accused. According to the accused victim girl was studying in his tuition class. After her admission her fees was not paid for about 8 days. However, they avoided to pay the fee. Therefore, he insisted her and her parents to pay the fee. Hence, parents of the victim girl lodged false case against him. [40] However, in my opinion the defence taken by the accused appears not probable. Because, in an Indian Society it is observed that, modesty of an woman has much importance. If any women faces sexual assault at the hands of any person even then many times she keeps quiet only because she is afraid of stigmas which will be attached to her character in such cases. Therefore, it is highly impossible and improbable that only because the accused insisted the parents of the victim girl to pay fees of tuition classes, they by putting future of their own daughter on the stake lodge false complaint that too relating the sexual assault. Moreover, the accused has not put forth any details regarding payment of fees of the other students of the class and non payment of the fees regarding the victim girl. He was expected at least to put on record : 17 : S.C.C.No.71/13(Jud.) handwritten notes maintained by him showing fees paid by the students. In the circumstances, defence taken by the accused appears improbable and not acceptable. I, therefore find no reason to disbelieve the testimony of X­ the victim girl (PW2) and her father Chandrakant (PW.1). [41] For the reasons stated above, I hold that the prosecution has adduced sufficient, cogent material t prove the guilt of accused U/sec.354 of the IPC and U/sec. 7 r.w 8 of the POCSO Act. I, therefore, answer point No.1 and 2 in the affirmative. AS TO POINT NO.3:­ [42] As mentioned above the prosecution has proved guilt of accused U/sec.354 of the IPC and U/sec. 7 r.w 8 of the POCSO Act. Hence, the accused is liable to be convicted. [43] Before parting with the judgment, I would like to hear the accused on the point of sentence. Thane ( S. B. Bahalkar ) Dated: 06.08.2018 Designated Judge Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, Thane. [44] I have heard the accused in person. He submitted that, his minor son is taking education. He is only earning hand in his family. Therefore, lenient view may be taken while awarding sentence. : 18 : S.C.C.No.71/13(Jud.) [45] Ld.Advocate for the accused also prayed that, lenient view may be taken while awarding the sentence. [46] On the other Ld. APP submitted that, the accused has committed heinous crime. Hence, maximum punishment may be awarded and no leniency should be shown to the accused. [47] It is no doubt that, the accused has committed heinous offence when he was playing role of a teacher of the victim girl. In our society teachers are the respectable persons to whom we assume to be next to the God. Hence, the accused is deserving for some deterrent punishment. However, at the same time it is to be keep in mind that, the accused is only earning hand in his family and his minor son is studying in school. I, therefore, considering the above mentioned facts and circumstances, pass the following order:­ ­: ORDER :­ 1. Accused Sainath Ganpat Garud is hereby convicted for the offence punishable under Sec.354 of Indian Penal Code and U/sec.7 r.w 8 of the Prevention of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 vide Section 235(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 2. For the offence punishable U/sec.354 of the Indian Penal code the accused is hereby sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment of 3 years and fine of Rs.10,000/­(Rupees Ten Thousand only). In default of payment of fine he shall undergo to suffer simple imprisonment for six months. : 19 : S.C.C.No.71/13(Jud.) 3. For the offence punishable U/sec.7 r.w 8 of the Prevention of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, the accused is hereby sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 3 years and fine of Rs.15,000/­ (Rupees Fifteen Thousand Only). In default of payment of fine he shall undergo to suffer simple imprisonment for six months. 4. The substantive sentences shall run concurrently. 5. The accused shall surrender his bail bonds. 6. Accused be given set off vide Section 428 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 7. Amount of fine, if recovered, be paid to the victim girl as compensation U/sec.357 of Code of Criminal Procedure, after expiry of appeal period. 8. The State Government to pay adequate compensation to victim under Sec.357­A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, under Victims Compensation Scheme or other schemes or funds. 9. Copy of this judgment be supplied to accused free of costs. 10.Copy of judgment be sent to District Magistrate, Thane as per Sec.365 of Cr.P.C. Thane ( S. B. Bahalkar ) Dated: 06.08.2018 Designated Judge Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, Thane.

CNR NO.MHTH01­005493­2018 1 B.A.1957/2018 ORDER BELOW EXH.1 IN BAIL APPLICATIOIN No.1957/2018 (CNR No. MHTH01­005493­2018) 1] The applicant Sunilkumar Shri Kailas Mourya has filed this application for grant of regular bail u/s.439 of Cr.P.C. in C.R.No.I­ 373/2018 registered at Nayanagar police Station U/Section­354­A(1) of I.P. Code and u/s. 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual offences Act. 2] Brief facts of the prosecution case are as under:­ On 03/07/2018 the minor victim­girl aged 12 years lodged complaint to police station Nayanagar, that she resides with her parents. She is learning in the school at Mira Road in 8 th standard. She used to go to school in the morning and used to return at 12.30 p.m. She noticed that one person aged 23 to 24 years is looking towards her for long period, then she also noticed that said person was calling her by her name on 02/07/2018. When she started to go towards home, he followed her. Then on mobile of her mother phone call of unknown number was noticed and when it was checked, whatsapp account was found and her mother shown the photo to the complainant and she identified said person as a person following her. Then on 03/07/2018 similar incident was repeated, said person pulled her sack and then she informed about it to her father and then came to police station and lodged complaint. On its basis above referred crime for the above referred offences came to be registered. Accused came to be arrested and investigation was started. 3] The accused by filing this application prayed for bail on different grounds including his innocence, having no involvement in offence, non­possibility of such type of incident in broad day light in CNR NO.MHTH01­005493­2018 2 B.A.1957/2018 crowded area. The applicant also mentioned that he was knowing the complainant having love affair with her and the complaint appears to be lodged at late hours. The allegations made in the complaint are false and fabricated. The investigation is over, he is ready to co­operate in investigation and complainant has tried to cause harm to the reputation of the applicant and no purpose will serve by keeping him in jail. On this count, the bail is sought. 4] In reply, I.O. and Ld. A.P.P. in reply opposed the application with contention that accused followed the minor victim, tried to make contact with her, offence is serious, the accused have no permanent place of residence, he may abscond and may pressurize the complainant and witnesses. 5] I heard the submissions of Ld. Adv. for applicant/accused and Ld. A.P.P. Perused case diary. 6] What appears from the contentions made by both sides and papers on record is that, complaint is registered on allegation of following the minor victim by accused having much difference in age. One incident is shown happened when the accused is tried to pull the sack of the minor. Then report came to be lodged. The accused in application submitted about love affair between both but no one can be compelled or no one can be pressurized for any purpose in a manner what the activities are shown done by the accused. The incident is reported long back and investigation is almost over and in my view, the case is of a nature that on stringent terms and conditions bail can be granted by securing safety of minor victim, CNR NO.MHTH01­005493­2018 3 B.A.1957/2018 presence of accused on trial in future. Hence, the following order is passed. ORDER 1] Application is allowed. 2] The applicant/accused Sunilkumar Shri Kailas Mourya in respect of C.R.No.I­373/2018 registered at Nayanagar police Station U/Section­354­A(1) of I.P. Code and u/s. 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, be released on bail on his furnishing P.B. & S.B. of Rs.15,000/­with surety of like amount. 3] The applicant/accused shall not enter into the area of residence of the complainant­victim in any manner. 4] The applicant/accused shall not make contact with victim, shall not pressurize the victim and the witnesses to the incident. 5] The applicant/accused shall attend Nayanagar police station on every Sunday from 9.00 a.m. to 11.00 a.m. for four weeks. 6] Breach of any condition will be a cause for prosecution to apply for cancellation of bail. Thane (S.P. Gondhalekar) Date ­ 17/08/2018. Additional Sessions Judge,Thane. CNR NO.MHTH01­005493­2018 4 B.A.1957/2018

CNR NO.MHTH01­005510/2018 1 B.A.1963/2018 ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN BAIL APPLICATIOIN No.1963/2018 (CNR No. MHTH01­005510­2018) 1] The applicant Nitesh @ Raju Ramti Chavan has filed this application for grant of regular bail u/s.439 of Cr.P.C. in C.R.No.I­80/2018 registered at Ganeshpuri police station U/Section­363, 376(2)(n), 376(3), 34 of I.P. Code and u/s. 4, 8 & 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences act. 2] Brief facts of the prosecution case are as under:­ The complainant Chanda balaram Mukne resident of Mahapoli, Kajubandhanpada, Bhiwandi lodged complaint on 14/07/2018 to Ganeshpuri police station. As per this complaint, he was doing labour work his minor daughter Savitri aged 15 years is the victim. Accused was working on construction site of school near the house of complainant. Victim was going for work on that site. Before 15 days victim told complainant that accused asked her as to whether she will marry with him and she denied. Then on 11/07/2018 complainant had gone to field. Victim was at home. At evening victim was not found and he started to trace her but did not find. On 14/07/2018 near office of Shramajivi Sanghatana, he found victim near the office. In said office, he took victim and she was inquired by persons present there, that time she disclosed that on 11/07/2018 accused Nitesh @ Raju Ramti Chavan called her at Angaon. Accused asked her to go with him and that they will perform marriage. She was taken at Thane railway station then at Kalyan and then at Nagpur by train. On 12/07d/2018 they reached to Nagpur, Nitesh met one advocate and then he took her back at Kalyan. On 13/07/2018 at night time and then again went to Vasai at the friend of accused. However, neighbours CNR NO.MHTH01­005510/2018 2 B.A.1963/2018 started to inquire with them and they went back to Vasai station and stayed on platform the on 17/07/2018 accused took her at Akloli at Manisha Guest House in a room. He started to commit forcible physical relation with her and on her refusal, he insisted and he pretended that they are now married and committed sexual intercourse with her. Then by hearing this, the complainant took the victim at police station and lodged complaint. On its basis, above referred crime came to be registered. 3] Ld. Counsel for the applicant/accused submitted that the allegations are false, victim was knowing the accused as stated in complaint, nothing was happened as stated in complaint, investigation is already over, the accused is falsely implicated in the matter, nothing is to be recovered from him, he has no previous criminal antecedents, presence can be secured and bail can be granted to him. 4] Ld. Counsel for the applicant further submitted that the incident is not of a nature that any ravish act is committed by the applicant and if altogether incident is concerned, it appears to be by consent and there is no use of criminal force or assault or violence. 5] Ld. A.P.P. Shri Londhe submitted that the age of the victim is 14 years and accused had taken her at different places with bad intention and it is not a case of love affair. The accused had taken undue advantage of her tender age and committed offence and he is not entitled for bail. 6] I heard the submissions of Ld. Adv. for applicant/accused and Ld. A.P.P. Perused case diary. 7] What transpires from the complaint of the complainant is that, CNR NO.MHTH01­005510/2018 3 B.A.1963/2018 his minor daughter was taken by accused with him on 11/07/2018 and then she was brought back on 14/07/2018. During these three days, incident is shown happened in respect of complainant. The age of the victim is shown as 15 years and her date of birth is disclosed as 11/02/2002. The statement of victim is also shown recorded and she has disclosed about the act committed against her. It appears from her statement that though the victim had gone with him, he has stated that they will marry, however, he used force against her, he committed assault on her and it appears that the accused has committed rape on her. The investigation is going on and it appears that there is prima facie material on record going against the accused. Considering all these facts and circumstances, this is not a fit case where the contention of the applicant can be considered that no physical force or violence is used. FIR is registered on the complaint of complainant and then subsequent investigation, statement of victim discloses that accused used force against her against her wish. Admittedly in POCSO Act, consent has no meaning in respect of minor victim and this fact will go against the applicant. Considering the same, I found no reason to consider this bail application. Hence, following order is passed. ORDER Bail application of applicant/accused Nitesh @ Raju Ramti Chavan in respect of C.R.No.I­80/2018 registered at Ganeshpuri police station U/Section­ 363, 376(2) (n), 376(3), 34 of I.P. Code and u/s. 4, 8 & 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, is hereby rejected. Thane (S.P. Gondhalekar) Date ­ 27/08/2018. Additional Sessions Judge,Thane.
