--1-- ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN CRIMINAL BAIL APPLICATION No.2031/2017 The applicant Sandeep Mahdeu @ Madhavrao Gaikwad has applied for bail under section 439 of Cr. P.C. in C.R.No.I­ 145/2017 registered in Kashimira police station for the offence under section 376, 363, 504, 506 read with 34, 420, 465, 468, 469, 471 of Indian Penal Code and section 4 and 6 of POCSO Act. 2. It is contended that he is innocent and falsely implicated. There is delay in lodging the FIR. The accused has not forged the documents of the victim. The victim herself has made affidavit that her birth date is 14.02.1999. She had full consent to marry with the accused. There is no inducement, force, threatening to the victim. The victim after the incident has refused to go with her parents. The accused is belonging to lower caste than the victim and therefore, her parents are opposed for the marriage of accused and the victim. It is submitted that the offence is not punishable with death. The applicant is ready to face the trial and he undertakes that he will not tamper the prosecution witnesses. Hence he prayed for bail. 3. The applicant has produced the certified copies of remand report, F.I.R, affidavit of the victim dtd.04.03.2017, 23.03.2017, marriage certificate, Adhar card of the victim. 4. Investigating Officer has contested the bail application by filing say at Exh.4. It is contended that the accused has forged some documents and made her major and accused committed marriage with the victim and he kidnapped the victim to marry with her and he performed marriage with the victim and thereafter he kept the physical relation with the victim. --2-- 5. I heard Ld. Counsel on behalf of the accused. He submitted that there was love affair with the victim and accused. The victim was above 17 years old and accused is 25 years old. The victim herself eloped away with the accused and they have performed marriage. He relied upon the decision in case of Sunil Mahadev Patil V/s. The State of Maharashtra in Bail Application NO.1036/2015 decided on 03rd August 2015. In that case also the victim was 15 years old and the accused is 20 years old. Statement of prosecutirx and witnesses showing that they were in love with each other, so they eloped and went to temple. There they garlanded each other and according to them performed marriage and thereafter they started residing together in the house of their relative. In such mitigating factors the bail was granted to the accused. 6. I perused the copy of FIR. In the FIR it is mentioned that the victim was 17 years old and on 25.02.2017 she left her house and did not come back so. Informant searched her. After 5 to 6 days the victim herself phoned upon elder sister's phone that, “don't take her search she is with Sandeep Gaikwad and they have married with each other.” Thereafter she switched off her mobile phone. In the report of the Investigating Officer it is mentioned that as per the school leaving certificate age of the victim is 17 years. Her birth date is 14.02.2000 and accused has forged some documents and married with her. 7. It is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the victim has refused to go with her parents and therefore she has been kept in some re­rehabilitation Centre. 8. Considering the facts and circumstances of this case the court is of the view that it appears that there was love affair --3-- between victim and the accused and she herself eloped away and married with the accused and resided with him voluntarily. So this is the mitigating factor to release the accused on bail. In view of the observations made in above cited case , therefore, I am of the view that further custody of the applicant in the jail without trial is not justifiable. Hence, he is entitled for bail. So I proceed to pass following order. :ORDER: 1. Application for bail is allowed. 2. The applicant Sandeep Mahdeu @ Madhavrao Gaikwad be released on P.B. and S.B. of Rs.20,000/­ (Rupees Twenty Thousand Only) with one or two local solvent sureties in like amount. 3. The applicant shall not pressurize, threaten and tamper the victim and any other witnesses by any means. 4. The applicant shall attend the concerned police station as and when necessary for further investigation and shall co­operate for investigation. 5. Applicant shall not leave the jurisdiction of the court without prior permission of the court. Thane. ( S.C. Khalipe ) Date : 19/08/2017. Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

.. 1 .. bail no.2065/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 2065/2015 This application is filed by applicants namely Wasim Lalmohammad Ansari and Mohd. Jasim Lalmohammad Ansari for their release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. I-345/2015 registered at Narpoli police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 354D, 323, 504 of I.P.C. and section 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicants were outraging modety of the complainant girl by fostering personal interaction with her by following her on motorcycle when used to return home from her college. It is further contended and argued that no such incident has happened and the applicants are falsely implicated with ulterior motive on account of strained relations between applicants and brother of complainant girl. It is further submitted that the applicants are permanent residents of the address given and that if the present applicants/accused are released on bail, they will co-operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicants are entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that the accused persons always following the minor complainant girl on motorcycle whenever she used return home from her college and the accused persons were trying to foster personal interaction with her in spite of disinterest shown by her and it is further contended that in this manner the accused persons had committed sexual harassment upon the complainant girl. It is further contended and argued that when the brother of the girl Sushant had questioned the accused persons about such harassment of the girl, they had beaten him by fist blows and also abused him. It is further submitted .. 2 .. bail no.2065/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) that in such circumstance if the applicants/accused are released on bail, there is possibility of the applicants threatening the victim girl and the prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicants are released on bail they may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicants are not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 354D, 323, 504 of I.P.C. and section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act the girl is stated to be 16 years old and it appears that it is the contention of the applicants that on account of quarrel between them and brother of the girl, they have been falsely implicated in the crime with ulterior motive. In such circumstance whether the allegations against the accused are true or not, would be the question to be decided on merits. Even nothing is stated to be recovered from the applicants/accused. 4] It is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicants would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicants tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. In that respect it is contended by the applicants that they are permanent resident of the address given and they will not abscond if released on bail and that they are ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 5] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicants/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. .. 3 .. bail no.2065/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) 6] Then, it has also to be mentioned that looking the allegations against the accused the investigation in the matter may have almost completed but the charge-sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge- sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 7] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order - ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Wasim Lalmohammad Ansari and Mohd. Jasim Lalmohammad Ansari are released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/- [rupees fifteen thousand only] each with one surety each in the like amount, subject to following conditions - The applicants/accused shall make themselves available for interrogation by a police officer and shall attend the concerned police station as and when called for said purpose till filing of the charge sheet and shall co-operate in investigation. They shall not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize her and other prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. They shall not leave India without permission of this Court. They shall furnish proof of their residence. Date : 27.08.2015 (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Additional Session Judge-1, Thane.

APP Kadu & V.A.Kulkarni for State Adv.Miss.Sushma Mishra for accused : JUDGMENT : (Delivered on this 16th day of June, 2017) The accused is prosecuted for offence of sexually assaulting the minor girl aged nine years old and outraging her modesty. 2] The facts are as under : It is alleged by prosecution that the complainant, the mother of the victim is residing with her two daughters, husband, father­in­law and mother­in­law. The complainant and her husband both are working. The complainant used to leave home for work at 07.45 a.m. and used to return at 08.00 p.m. On 30.05.2014 she had left her home for work as usual. At about 08.30 p.m. while she was returning home, her friend Sneha met her on the way. Said Sneha told the complainant that on that day at about 12.30 at noon complainant's nine years old elder daughter had been to the vegetable shop of the accused to purchase coriander and tomato. Sneha found the victim minor girl sitting on the lap of the accused. The accused was moving his hands through the hairs of the victim and was kissing on her cheek. Sneha called upon the victim and inquired about her parents. Thereafter Sneha asked the victim J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 188­14 ­ 354, 8,12.doc .....3/­ ..3.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 188/2014.. Exh.30.. to go to her home. The complainant narrated said incident to her husband when he returned from work. Thereafter they approached Kashimira police station on 30.05.2014 itself and lodged complaint against the accused. 3] After receiving complaint offence punishable u/s.8 and 12 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act and u/s.354 of the Indian Penal Code came to be registered against the accused. P.S.I., Jagdish Valvi carried out the investigation and filed charge sheet against the accused for said offences. 4] Charge is framed against the accused at Exh.03. He pleaded not guilty of offence and claimed to be tried. 5] Statement of accused u/s.313 of Code of Criminal Procedure is recorded at Exh.29. The defence of the accused is that the complainant had purchased vegetables on credit and was liable to pay Rs.400/­ to him. The complainant and her friend approached him, asked for diary in which the account was maintained and torn the same. Out of said due amount there was a dispute whereby false complaint came to be lodged against him. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 188­14 ­ 354, 8,12.doc .....4/­ ..4.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 188/2014.. Exh.30.. 6] After going through the prosecution story, evidence on record and hearing arguments of both sides, following points arise for my determination. I record my findings thereon for reasons as stated below. POINTS FINDINGS 1] Does the prosecution prove that on 30.05.2014 at about 12.30 at noon in a vegetable shop, in front of Agarwal Complex, Mira Road, Thane the accused forced the victim girl aged 9 years old to sit on his lap, moved his hand through her hairs, kissed her on her cheek and thereby sexually assaulted and harassed her and outraged her modesty ? …Not proved. 2] What order ? ..As per final order. : REASONS : As to the Point No.1 :­ 7] To bring home the guilt of the accused the prosecution has examined complainant i.e. mother of the victim at Exh.13. Complaint lodged by her is at Exh.14. Complainant's friend Sneha Kakade is examined as PW2 at Exh.15. Victim is examined as PW3 at Exh.17. One Krushna Hari Sawant who is panch on spot panchanama is examined as PW4 at Exh.22. The panchanama is at Exh.8. Victim's grandfather is examined as PW5 at Exh.24. Lastly J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 188­14 ­ 354, 8,12.doc .....5/­ ..5.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 188/2014.. Exh.30.. investigating officer Jagdish Valvi is examined as PW6 at Exh.25. 8] In the present case the complainant is not the witness to the incident. She lodged complaint after receiving information from her friend Sneha (PW2) and the victim (PW3). Thus, certainly PW1 is a formal witness, so far as the incident is concerned. 9] PW2 Sneha Kakade is the friend of the complainant and they were serving together. She has deposed that on 30.05.2014 at the main gate of their building she was waiting for auto­rickshaw for herself and her grandmother who was following her. In front of said main gate there is a road and on opposite side of said road, there is a vegetable shop of accused. When she was waiting for an auto­rickshaw she found that the victim was sitting on the lap of the accused in his shop. She called upon the victim. The accused was kissing her on her cheek. When she called victim, the accused was not allowing her to go. However, the victim came out of the shop and approached her. On inquiry victim told that her mother had gone for work. Thereafter she (PW2) left the spot in auto­ rickshaw alongwith her grandfather. At about 08.00 t0 08.30 p.m. she met complainant near Mahalaxmi temple and narrated the incident to her. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 188­14 ­ 354, 8,12.doc .....6/­ ..6.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 188/2014.. Exh.30.. 10] The victim in her deposition at Exh.17 specifically deposed that her grandparents had asked her to purchase tomato and coriander from the vegetable shop located in front of their residential building. When she had gone to the shop, accused alone was present there. She asked the accused for tomato and coriander by taking weight of the same. The accused agreed to weight the tomato and coriander, but asked her to go inside the shop. When she went inside the shop, the accused put her some questions about whereabouts of her brother and caused her to sit on his lap. He moved his hand on her head and kissed on her cheek. She found Sneha teacher (PW2) at the main gate of their residential building. Said Sneha called upon her from the gate itself. Thereupon she pushed the accused and went outside the shop. Thereafter she put coriander and tomato in the carrier of her bicycle and proceeded to the gate of the building. Sneha teacher asked her about her parents and also asked her to return home. The victim further deposed that she did not narrate the incident to anyone as she was frightened. She even not narrated the incident to her grandfather and grandmother. After her mother returned home in the evening, she narrated the incident to her. Thereafter alongwith the father and mother she went to the police station wherein her mother lodged complaint. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 188­14 ­ 354, 8,12.doc .....7/­ ..7.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 188/2014.. Exh.30.. 11] Relying upon the evidence of prosecution witnesses learned A.PP. Mr.Kulkarni argued at length and submitted that the victim, PW3 and eye witness Sneha Kakade (PW2) have narrated the incident in detail. As stated by both the witnesses the accused had caused the victim to sit on his lap, was kissing her and was not allowing her to go outside the shop when called by PW2 Sneha Kakade. A.P.P. Mr.Kulkarni further submitted that as provided u/s.29 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, when a person is prosecuted u/s.7 and 9 of the Act the Special Court shall presume that such person has committed an offence unless the contrary is proved. A.P.P. Mr.Kulkarni further relied upon section 30 of the Act and submitted that the mental status while committing an offence is to be presumed to be in existence. Learned A.P.P. Mr.Kulkarni vehemently submitted that from the evidence on record the prosecution has proved its case beyond reasonable doubt and he accused deserves to be punished for the same. 12] The accused is prosecuted for offence of sexual assault and sexual harassment. Under such circumstances it is necessary to go through the definition of sexual assault and sexual harassment given in section 7 and 11 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. Section 7 and 11 of the Act reads as under : J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 188­14 ­ 354, 8,12.doc .....8/­ ..8.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 188/2014.. Exh.30.. 7. Sexual assault : Whoever, with sexual intent touches the vagina, penis, anus or breast of the child or makes the child touch the vagina, penis, anus or breast of such person or any other person, or does any other act with sexual intent which involves physical contact without penetration is said to commit sexual assault. 11. Sexual harassment : A person is said to commit sexual harassment upon a child when such person with sexual intent,­ (i) utters any word or makes any sound, or makes any gesture or exhibits any object or part of body with the intention that such word or sound shall be heard, or such gesture or object or part of body shall be seen by the child; or (ii) makes a child exhibit his body or any part of his body so as it is seen by such person or any other person; or (iii) shows any object to a child in any form or media for pornographic purposes; or (iv) repeatedly or constantly follows or watches or contacts a child either directly or through electronic, digital or any other means; or (v) threatens to use, in any form of media, a real or fabricated depiction through electronic, film or digital or any other mode, of any part of the body of the child or the involvement of the child in a sexual act; or (vi) entices a child for pornographic purposes or gives gratification therefor. 13] As provided u/s.7 of the Act a person is said to have committed sexual assault when he touches the various private parts of the body of minor or compels the minor to touch his own private part with sexual intention which J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 188­14 ­ 354, 8,12.doc .....9/­ ..9.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 188/2014.. Exh.30.. involves even any other physical conduct without penetration. In the present case neither the victim nor the eye witness Sneha Kakade or even the complainant has stated that the accused had sexual intention. Though there is presumption u/s.29 of the Act, there must be at least allegations by the prosecution to that effect. In the present case there is no allegation of any sexual intention on the part of the accused. So also there is no whisper of the accused outraging the modesty of the minor victim. Certainly the act on the part of the accused do not fall within the definition of sexual harassment as provided u/s.11 of the Act. 14] It is pertinent to note here that the eye witness Sneha Kakade had witnessed the alleged incident at about 12.30 at noon. Even after witnessing the alleged incident she proceeded towards her routine work without complaining about the incident to anyone. She allegedly narrated the incident to the mother of the victim i.e. the complainant at about 08.00 to 08.30 p.m. Certainly there is delay of almost eight hours. This very fact shows that the eye witness had not found it necessary to inform the alleged incident to the complainant or other family members of the victim, nor she found it proper to make a complaint in person. Admittedly at the time of alleged incident the grandparents of the victim were at home. Under such circumstances the behaviour of the J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 188­14 ­ 354, 8,12.doc .....10/­ ..10.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 188/2014.. Exh.30.. victim immediately after the alleged incident is of paramount consideration. The grandfather of victim is examined as PW5. In his deposition at Exh.24 he has deposed that “after returning house with tomatto my grand­daughter kept the said tomatto in house and started to play in house as usual”. Thus certainly there was no indication of any fear in the behaviour of the victim. Under such circumstances the facts deposed by victim that, as she was frightened she did not tell about the incident to others and her grandparents, is certainly not believable and reliable. 15] In the present case though the complainant and eye witness Sneha Kakade have denied that the complainant was liable to pay to the accused for purchasing vegetables on credit and the accused had failed to prove his defence, this does not by itself proves the prosecution case beyond reasonable doubt. Certainly it is fundamental principle of criminal law that the prosecution has to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt. Considering the very nature of the incident, the acts alleged against the accused, the possibility of tutoring the victim cannot be ruled out. Considering the delay, the behaviour of the victim after alleged incident and other facts on record, the prosecution has certainly not proved its case beyond reasonable doubt. The benefit of doubt is to be given J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 188­14 ­ 354, 8,12.doc .....11/­ ..11.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 188/2014.. Exh.30.. to the accused. Hence answering point No.1 in the negative, following order is passed. ORDER 1. Accused Krupashankar Ramakant Tiwari is hereby acquitted u/s.235(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure for offence punishable u/s.354 of the Indian Penal Code and u/s.8 and 12 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 2. The bail bond of accused stands cancelled. 3. Accused is directed to furnish personal bond of Rs.5,000/­, in terms of sec.437­A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Sd/­... Thane. (P.P.Jadhav) District Judge­8 and Date : 16.06.2017. Addl. Sessions Judge, Thane. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 188­14 ­ 354, 8,12.doc ...../­

Bail No.2078//2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exhibit 1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 2078/2015 This application is filed by applicant Muddatssir @ Mudu Yusuf Shaikh for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no.I­351/2015 registered at Mumbra police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 354 of I.P.C. and section 7 and 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant outraged modesty of the victim girl and committed sexual assault on her by threatening complainant to come with him else he would upload her photo on WhatsApp to defame her and also showed her photo on his mobile and then he dragged her towards him and moved his hand on her breast. It is further contended and argued that there is no incriminating evidence against the accused. It is submitted that there is love affair between applicant/accused and victim girl. It is further contended and argued that no ingredients of Sec. 354 of I.P.C. are made out against accused. It is further submitted that investigation may have mostly completed and therefore there is no need to further detain the accused in jail. It is further submitted that there is no criminal antecedent of the applicant and that he is permanently residing at the given address and applicant/accused and victim girl both are residing in different locality. It is further submitted that if the present .. 2 .. Bail No.2078//2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) applicant/accused is released on bail, he will not abscond and he is ready to abide all the conditions imposed by Court and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that at the relevant time accused knocked the door of the house of the complainant­victim girl Afrin Shaikh aged 15 years and when she opened the door applicant/accused showed her photograph to her on his mobile and threatened her to come with him else he will upload her photo on WhatsApp and defame her and and then he dragged her towards him and moved his hand on her breast and thereby committed sexual assault on her. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl and the prosecution witnesses. It is further submitted that both applicant/accused and victim girl are residing in same locality therefore there is possibility of repeating the offence from accused. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 354 of I.P.C. and section 7, 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act with the allegation that .. 3 .. Bail No.2078//2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) applicant/accused threatened the complainant to come with him else he would upload her photograph saved in his mobile on WhatsApp and then he dragged her towards him and moved his hand over her breast, it is contended by the applicant/accused that there is love affair between the applicant/accused and victim girl and he is falsely implicated in the crime. In such circumstance whether the allegations against the accused are true or whether the case of false implication put forth by the accused is probable, would be the question to be decided on merits. 4] Then, the applicant/accused is seen to be in jail since 11.08.2015 and looking to the nature of allegations the investigation may have completed by now. Even nothing is stated to be recovered from the applicant/accused. 5] Then, it is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 6] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the .. 4 .. Bail No.2078//2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 7] Then, it has also to be mentioned that looking the allegations against the accused the investigation in the matter may have almost completed but the charge­sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge­sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 8] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Muddatssir @ Mudu Yusuf Shaikh is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ He shall not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and the prosecution .. 5 .. POINTS FINDINGS 1] Does prosecution prove that on 30.05.2015 in between 21.15 to 23.00 hours on Apatale Kalsheti road within the limits of Jawhar police station the accused kidnapped Suvarna Kinar aged 16 years of age with intention to sexually assault her ? ...Proved. 2] Does prosecution further prove that on above said date, time and place J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 194­15 ­ S­363,376, 4.doc .....5/­ ..5.. J­Spl.Case POCSO­194/2015.. Exh.54.. CNR No.NHTH01­005567­2015 the accused had forcible penetrative sexual intercourse with the victim ? ...Proved. 3] What order ? ..As per final order. : REASONS : As to the Point Nos.1 and 2 :­ 7] Point Nos.1 and 2 are arising out of one and same incident. Hence those are discussed together. To bring home the guilt of the accused, prosecution has examined the victim Suvarna Kinar at Exh.14. Complaint lodged by her is at Exh.15. Prosecution has examined Dilip Jiwa Khutade as PW2 at Exh.21. He is an independent eye witness. PW3 Pratap Jayprakash Targe is panch on spot panchanama. His deposition is at Exh.24 and panchanama is at Exh.26. PW4 Bhagwan Ganga Chibhade is panch on seizure of clothes of accused. His deposition is at Exh.29. Panchanama is at Exh.30. PW5 Dr.Prashant Sudhakar Rajguru is Medical officer who examined the victim. His deposition is at Exh.33. Medical certificate is at Exh.34. He had also examined the accused. PW8 Rajesh Kushalrao Kagane is in­charge Head Master or Z.P.School of J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 194­15 ­ S­363,376, 4.doc .....6/­ ..6.. J­Spl.Case POCSO­194/2015.. Exh.54.. CNR No.NHTH01­005567­2015 Biwaldhar. His deposition is at Exh.46. The extract of school admission register is at Exh.50. 8] PW1 the victim in her deposition at Exh.14 narrated almost all facts alleged in the complaint. She specifically deposed that after attending the marriage at Apatale she herself, other women and girls were returning in jeep driven by the accused. When they reached at Apatale all other women and girl got down from the jeep. They were unknown to her. The accused forced her to remain in the jeep and closed all window glasses. She raised alarm and shouted, but accused did not allow her to got down from the jeep. The accused drove the jeep to Nehale and thereafter Kalsheti. It was 11.00 at night. At Kalsheti accused stopped the jeep, switched off the light and removed her clothes. She was crying. However, the accused had forcible sexual intercourse with her. She requested the accused to take her to her house. Thereafter while accused was driving the jeep towards Apatale her father obstructed the same near one stone crusher. Her father was accompanied by 4­5 other persons. She narrated the incident to her father. Thereafter they went to Jawhar police station. The police recorded her complaint Exh.15. The police had referred her for medical examination to Jawhar hospital. In the hospital she was examined by doctor. Thereafter she had shown the spot of incident to the police. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 194­15 ­ S­363,376, 4.doc .....7/­ ..7.. J­Spl.Case POCSO­194/2015.. Exh.54.. CNR No.NHTH01­005567­2015 Police prepared map and also obtained photographs of the spot of incident. Her statement was also recorded in the Court. The police seized her clothes. 9] PW2 Dilip Khutade corroborated the evidence of victim. He specifically deposed that on 30.05.2015 he had gone to attend marriage of Subhash Kinar at Bhevardachapada alongwith victim's father Sitaram Kinar. After returning from said marriage they were sitting in the house of sister of Sitaram. At about 09.15 a.m. Poonam Kinar had been there and told that accused Asif Kotwal had taken away victim Suvarna in his jeep. Thereafter he himself and Sitaram Kinar proceeded on motorcycle in search of victim Suvarna. They found the jeep of the accused near one Dhaba at Raytale. They chased the jeep and obstructed it near one stone crusher at Kaparichapada. After halting the jeep accused ran away, but he was chased and caught by Sitaram. Victim Suvarna was found in the jeep. She narrated the incident of rape at the hands of accused. Thereafter they had taken the accused to police station. He further deposed that police seized the jeep No.5795 in his presence vide panchanama Exh.22. 10] The victim girl and PW2 are cross examined at length. Both admitted that there were 15 to 20 passengers in J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 194­15 ­ S­363,376, 4.doc .....8/­ ..8.. J­Spl.Case POCSO­194/2015.. Exh.54.. CNR No.NHTH01­005567­2015 each jeep in which the victim and other relatives had attended the marriage. In cross examination of the victim it is specifically suggested that there was quarrel with the accused on the ground of fare charges. However, the victim denied the same. In cross examination of PW2 it is specifically suggested that he regularly visits police station, but he also denied the same. It is pertinent to note here that in cross examination of the victim it is specifically brought on record by the defence itself that on that night victim's father and other villagers were searching the victim and the accused. As already mentioned the accused himself admitted that on that night he was driving the jeep and victim was with him. He further admitted that the father of the victim obstructed the vehicle and assaulted him. He has denied sexual intercourse with the victim. However, in the complaint and in the deposition the victim has described in detail about sexual intercourse by the accused with her. Under such circumstances the evidence of PW1 and PW2 cannot be discarded. It is further to be noted that in cross examination of the victim it is suggested that there was dispute with the accused on fare charges. However, in statement u/s.313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure the accused has stated that the father of victim was having dispute with the owner of the jeep. Thus the defence of the accused is contradictory. On the contrary the evidence of PW1 and PW2 is consistent and corroborative to each other. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 194­15 ­ S­363,376, 4.doc .....9/­ ..9.. J­Spl.Case POCSO­194/2015.. Exh.54.. CNR No.NHTH01­005567­2015 11] PW3 Pratap Jayprakash Targe is Awwal Clerk in Jawhar Tahasil office. Being public servant he was called for panchanama of spot of incident. The spot panchanama is at Exh.26. He has supported the prosecution and the panchanama is duly proved. As the accused had already admitted that he was driving the jeep and it was obstructed by father of victim, the spot panchanama is mere a formal document. In cross examination of this witness nothing is brought on record to disprove the spot panchanama. 12] PW4 Bhagwan Chibhade deposed that on 31.05.2015 police had called upon him at Jawhar police station. The accused was present in the police station. Police obtained clothes of accused comprising blue pant and shirt and seized the same vide panchanama Exh.30. In cross examination this witness admitted that he frequently visits police station. He further admitted that the clothes like muddemal are available in the market. However, the accused himself admitted that he was taken to the police station. The seizure of clothes of accused is also a mere formality. In cross examination of PW4 also nothing is brought on record to disprove the seizure of clothes and panchanama of the same. 13] PW5 Dr.Prashant Rajguru deposed that on 31.05.2015 while he was present in Jawhar Sub­District J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 194­15 ­ S­363,376, 4.doc .....10/­ ..10.. J­Spl.Case POCSO­194/2015.. Exh.54.. CNR No.NHTH01­005567­2015 Hospital as Medical Officer the victim Suvarna Kinar was brought to the hospital by lady constable Sayyed of Jawhar police station. He had examined the victim with her consent. The victim had narrated history that accused Asif Kotwal had kidnapped her in a vehicle and had forceful sexual intercourse with her in said vehicle. On her physical examination he had found that everything was normal. On her vaginal examination he found that hymen was absent. On examination he had revealed that there was penetrative sexual assault upon the victim. Accordingly he issued certificate/report Exh.34. He further deposed that ossification test of the victim was also conducted. Opinion of Dental examination was obtained. The approximate age of victim was found to be 16 to 17 years. PW5 further deposed that on 01.06.2015 accused was brought to the hospital by PC Chaudhary of Jawhar police station. On medical examination of the accused he found that sexual intercourse by him with the victim cannot be ruled out. Accordingly he submitted report Exh.35. In cross examination of this witness various suggestions about the examination of the victim and denying forceful sexual intercourse are put by the defence. However, those suggestions are negatived by the witness. Nothing is brought on record through the cross examination to disbelieve this witness. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 194­15 ­ S­363,376, 4.doc .....11/­ ..11.. J­Spl.Case POCSO­194/2015.. Exh.54.. CNR No.NHTH01­005567­2015 14] PW8 Rajesh Kagane is Head Master of Z.P. School Biwaldhar. He deposed that in School Admission form Exh.49 the birth date of victim girl is mentioned as 10.04.1999. As per said school admission form the birth date is mentioned in the school register, extract of which is produced at Exh.50. In cross examination of this witness it is merely suggested that at the time of admission of victim girl the mother of the victim girl had attended the school and had not produced any document. From said suggestion it cannot be held that the school record about birth date of the victim is false one. 15] PW7 is the investigating officer. He has narrated in detail as to how the investigation was carried out by him. In cross examination the investigating officer has admitted that except the sister of victim, statement of no other female passengers in the jeep are recorded. He did not collect the documents to show that the jeep owner had appointed drivers on those two jeeps. All other suggestions are denied by this witness. As already mentioned the accused himself has admitted that he was driving the jeep in which the victim was travelling. He has specifically admitted that when he was taking the victim alone in his jeep, victim's father obstructed the same. Under such circumstances the investigation carried out by PW7 cannot be disputed. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 194­15 ­ S­363,376, 4.doc .....12/­ ..12.. J­Spl.Case POCSO­194/2015.. Exh.54.. CNR No.NHTH01­005567­2015 16] In the present case from the school record the birth date of the victim girl is proved to be 10.04.1999. As per said birth date on the date of incident i.e. on 30.05.2015 the victim was 16 years, 1 month and 20 days old. As per ossification test her age is 16 to 17 years. The school record and medical record corroborates each other. Under such circumstances the prosecution has proved that the victim girl was minor at the time of incident. The victim girl has described in detail as to how the accused committed penetrative sexual assault. The medical evidence also corroborates penetrative sexual intercourse with the victim. Under such circumstances the prosecution has proved beyond reasonable doubt that the accused had kidnapped the victim in his jeep and had forcible sexual intercourse with her. Hence point Nos.1 and 2 are answered in the affirmative. 17] As accused is held guilty for the offence punishable u/s.363, 376 of Indian Penal Code and section 4 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, he is liable to be convicted and sentenced for the sames. At this juncture I heard the accused on quantum of sentence. 18] Heard the accused on quantum of sentence. He submitted that he is having two years old small daughter and age old mother. There is no one to look after them. Hence J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 194­15 ­ S­363,376, 4.doc .....13/­ ..13.. J­Spl.Case POCSO­194/2015.. Exh.54.. CNR No.NHTH01­005567­2015 leniency be shown to him. A.P.P. Shri.Kadu submitted that offence being serious maximum punishment be inflicted. 19] The offence u/s.363 of the Indian Penal Code is punishable with imprisonment upto seven years. The offence u/s.4 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act is punishable with imprisonment not less than seven years and which may extent to imprisonment for life. Certainly, there are no special reasons to inflict the punishment less than the lesser punishment provided under the provisions of law. At the same time the fact that the accused is not having any criminal antecedents can be considered to inflict the lesser punishment provided by the Act. It is further to be noted here that the offence u/s.376 of the Indian Penal Code and section 4 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act is made out in respect of one and same incident, the later Act being special enactment, single punishment under the later Act will serve the purpose. With these observations following order is passed. ORDER 1. Accused Aashif Akabar Kotwal is hereby convicted u/s.235(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure for offences punishable u/s.363, 376 of the Indian Penal Code and u/s.4 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 194­15 ­ S­363,376, 4.doc .....14/­ ..14.. J­Spl.Case POCSO­194/2015.. Exh.54.. CNR No.NHTH01­005567­2015 2. For the offence punishable u/s.4 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act the accused is sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for seven years and fine of Rs.10,000/­ (Rs.Ten Thousand only), in default of payment of fine he has to undergo further simple imprisonment for three months. 3. For the offence punishable u/s.363 of Indian Penal Code the accused is sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for three years and fine of Rs.5,000/­ (Rs.Five Thousand only), in default of payment of fine he has to undergo further simple imprisonment for one month. 4. Substantive sentences shall run concurrently. 5. The accused to surrender his bail bond. 6. Accused is entitled to set off for the period he has already undergone in jail u/s.428 of Code of Criminal Procedure. 7. The muddemal property clothes being worthless be destroyed after the appeal period is over. 8. Muddemal Max Jeep bearing No.MH­15/BW­5795 is already returned to its registered owner. It be retained with him and the bond executed by him shall stand cancelled, after the appeal period is over. 9. Free copy of Judgment be given to the accused Sd/­... Thane. Special Case No.73/2013 Judgment Received on : 25.10.2013 Registered on : 25.10.2013 Decided on : 10.04.2015 Duration : 1 year 5 months 16 days IN THE COURT OF THE SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE AT THANE (Presided over by Ms.V.V.Virkar, Additional Sessions Judge-1, Thane) SPECIAL CASE NO. 73 of 2013 Exhibit No. The State of Maharashtra .. Complainant versus 1] Rahul Ramvilas Yadav Age 24 years, Resident of Gram Dhoilkatoli Dist. Darbhanga, State Bihar, 2] Pankajkumar Siyacharan Jamedar, Age 27 years, Residence – room of Balasheth, Kataigaon, Bhiwandi. .. Accused Appearance - Mr. A.K.Khamkar, learned Additional Public Prosecutor (hereinafter in short A.P.P.) Mr. B.T.Tavre, learned advocate for the accused. JUDGMENT (Delivered on 10.04.2015.) .. 2 .. Special Case No.73/2013 Judgment The accused stands prosecuted for the offence punishable under section 363, 366A of I.P.C. and section 3 and 4 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as ''P.O.C.S.O. Act'') for kidnapping minor girl aged 16 years from lawful guardianship of her parents in furtherance of their common intention with a view to induce the said girl to go with accused no.1 at places namely Delhi and Bihar and force or seduce her to have illicit intercourse with accused no.1 and accused no.1 having committed forcible sexual intercourse with her and accused no.2 having abetted the accused no.1 in commission of crime. 2] In short the facts giving rise to the prosecution of the accused are that victim girl Mahananda is the daughter of complainant Subhash Laxman Rathod and she was aged 16 years at the relevant time and was staying with her brother, father and sister and was studying in P.R.High School in 8th Std. That accused no.2 Pankajkumar Jamedar is the friend of the accused no.1 Rahul Yadav and the accused no.2 was staying in the neighbourhood of the girl and the accused no.1 used to go the house of the accused no.2 and accused no.1 thus had developed acquaintance and love affair with the girl and assured her of marriage and induced her to run away with him by taking disadvantage of young age of the girl and when the parents of the girl learnt about it they had even warned the accused no.1 not to indulge in such activities and shall not keep any contact with girl Mahananda and they had also persuaded the girl that she is of tender age and she shall not roam around with the accused. However, the accused did not listen to it. It was also case of the prosecution that in the month of April, 2013 in last week both the accused contacted the victim girl when she was in the market at Nizampura Police Station and accused no.1 expressed love for and stated that he would not be able to live without her and accused no.2 gave assurance of love of accused no.1 for her and persuaded her to run away from house with accused no.1 and that he would .. 3 .. Special Case No.73/2013 Judgment give them Rs.5,000/- for running away and for performing marriage. It is further case of prosecution that keeping faith on their version the girl being of tender age had run away from the house with accused no.1 and the accused no.2 had given Rs.5,000/- to accused no.1 for that purpose and thereby abetted the accused no.1 to kidnap the girl from lawful guardianship of her parents. It is also case of the prosecution that the accused no.1 took the girl first to Kalyan station and then on false assurance of marriage he had sexual intercourse with her in the staircase of booking office at Kalyan. It is also case of the prosecution that the accused then took her to Vajreshwari, Ganeshpuri and then to his house at Katai and there also the accused no.1 had sexual intercourse with her. Then, he took her to his native place in Bihar and stayed there at the house of his relative and she stayed their for eight days. She was also feeling homesick and that time the accused assured her that he would take her back to her parents' house. 3] It is also case of prosecution that in the meantime when the girl went missing, the parents of the girl searched for her but when she could not be traced, her father Subhash Rathod lodged missing complaint on 07.05.2013 and it was enquired into and even after that the parents of the girl were in search of the girl and while searching for her, they learnt that accused no.1 Rahul Yadav also is missing from his house since 05.05.2013 and therefore the father of the girl realized that the accused must have kidnapped the girl and therefore he lodged complaint against the accused. 4] On the basis of his complaint, offence as per C.R.No.I- 85/2013 was registered under section 363, 366A of I.P.C. and the work of investigation was entrusted to A.P.I. Patil and the offence was investigated into by him. It is also case of the prosecution after the offence was registered, the accused no.2, who was aware of the activities of the accused no.1 with the girl, had intimated the accused no.1 that offence is registered and parents are in search of .. 4 .. Special Case No.73/2013 Judgment him and the girl and even had told them not to come to Katai. But then the accused no.1 did not have money for their further expenses and therefore they decided to return back and when they reached Kalyan station they were caught by police. Statement of the girl was then recorded and since in her statement it revealed that the accused no.1 had sexual intercourse with her, offence under section 376 of I.P.C. and under P.O.C.S.O. Act were added and report was accordingly submitted to the Court. It is also case of the prosecution that during the investigation further statements of witnesses were recorded. Panchnama of the spot was also prepared. The girl and the accused were went for medical examination. Since the girl was reported to be minor below 18 years, her school leaving certificate in regard to date of birth was obtained. Samples obtained and muddemal seized was sent for chemical analysis. 5] It is also case of the prosecution that while in police custody the accused made statement that he would show the spot where he had sexual intercourse with the girl and also would discover the clothes concealed by him in his room which were on his person at the time of incident. Memorandum of his statement was recorded and in accordance with his statement the accused showed the spot and discovered the clothes and the same came to be seized under panchnama. After completion of investigation since it revealed that there was sufficient evidence against the accused, they came to charge-sheeted for offence punishable under section 363, 366A, 376 read with section 34 of I.P.C. and section 4, 17 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. 6] Since provisions of P.O.C.S.O. Act are applied, the charge sheet came to submitted in this Court which is a Special Court for trying the cases under P.O.C.S.O. Act. 7] The accused no.1 was produced before Court by jail authority and accused no.2 appeared before Court. A charge for .. 5 .. Special Case No.73/2013 Judgment offence punishable under section 363, 366A, 376 read with section 34 of I.P.C. and section 4, 17 of P.O.C.S.O. Act was framed as per Exhibit 8 against the accused. Contents of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. The accused pleaded not guity and claimed to be tried. their defence was of total denial. 8] For establishing guilt of the accused, the prosecution examined complainant P.W.1 Subhash Laxman Rathod, father of the girl, P.W.2 Digambar Rajaram Shinde, headmaster of the school where the girl was studying, P.W.3 Dr. Jayashree Mhaske, medical officer, and P.W.4 A.P.I. Arvind Vasant Patil, I.O. The documentary evidence produced, proved and relied upon by the prosecution consisted of missing report Exhibit 15, complaint Exhibit 16, bona dide certificate of girl Mahananda Exhibit 21, spot panchnama Exhibit 26 (exhibited on admission), medical certificate of the girl Exhibit 27 (exhibited on admission), panchnama of seizure of clothes on the person of accused Exhibit 28( exhibited on admission) and memorandum statement of accused Exhibit 30 and discovery panchnama Exhibit 31 (both exhibited on admission). 9] I heard the leanred A.P.P. and learned advocate for the accused. 10] On above facts of the case, the points which arose for my determination and my reasons and findings against them are as under - Points Findings i) Whether the prosecution proved that on 05.05.2013 around 4.45 p.m. accused no.1 kidnapped minor girl Mahananda Subhash Rathod from lawful guardianship of her parents by inducing her with the intent that said girl may be or knowing that it is likely that she will be forced or seduced to illicit intercourse with accused no.1 ? No. .. 6 .. Special Case No.73/2013 Judgment ii ) Whether the prosecution proved that after kidnapping said minor girl, on the given day, date, time and place, the accused no.1 had committed rape on her by doing forcible sexual intercourse with her time and again ? No. iii ) Whether the prosecution proved that on the given day, date, time and place, the accused no.1 committed penetrative sexual assaut on the said minor girl ? No. iv ) Whether the prosecution proved that the accused no.2 abetted the accused no.1 in commission of offence by convincing the minor girl to go with the accused no.1 and by giving Rs.5,000/- to the accused no.1 for said purpose ? No. v) What offence, if any, is proved ? No offence is proved against any of the accused. vi ) What order ? Both accused are acquitted. REASONS 11] As is clear the allegations against the accused no.1 are that he had developed love affair with the girl who was aged 16 years old at the relevant time and had induced her to run away with him by living her parents' house and with a view to have illicit sexual intercourse with her and actually took her with him and had sexual intercourse with her time and again and accused no.2 abetted him in commission of crime by persuading the girl to leave the house and go with accused no.1 and even by offering financial help for that purpose. 12] In that respect it is to be mentioned that the testimony of the girl would have been the best evidence in regard to the allegations against the accused. But then, as is clear the prosecution has not examined the girl. No doubt, the prosecution put forth reason for not examining the girl that the girl is now .. 7 .. Special Case No.73/2013 Judgment married and she is staying at her matrimonial house in Karnataka. Even the complainant i.e. the father of the girl, in his evidence on oath stated that in his view it will not be proper to call his daughter because she is married and he had not disclosed about this incident and case to her in-laws and it may create problem in her matrimonial life if her in-laws learn about it and therefore he feel that she shall not be called. As such it appear that for the reason stated by the father of the girl the prosecution chose not to call the girl for evidence. 13] In that respect it is to be mentioned that though for future married life of the girl it was proper and desirable not to call the girl for deposing before Court, the aspect which is material and important so far the present case is that the girl is the only material and important witness who is an eye witness of the incident taken place in regard to her and her evidence is not available so as to ascertain the guilt or otherwise of the accused. 14] No doubt, since the prosecution has explained the reason for not examining the girl and that appear to be justifiable and proper reason and therefore, the prosecution cannot be blamed for not examining the girl. But the fact still remains that the testimony of the girl is not available to ascertain the truthfulness or otherwise of the allegations against the accused in the present matter. 15] Then, it was also argued on behalf of prosecution that though the girl is not examined, material evidence brought on record show that the girl was minor at the time relevant time. Then, even from the medical evidence it is clear that the girl was habituated to sexual intercourse. It was therefore argued that the allegations that the accused kidnapped the girl from lawful guardianship and had sexual intercourse with minor girl who was below 16 years of age is proved and therefore the offence charged against the accused has to be held as established. .. 8 .. Special Case No.73/2013 Judgment 16] But in that respect it is to be mentioned that from the perusal of testimony of the complainant, father of the girl, it revealed that though he stated that on the day of incident the girl left the house without telling anybody and therefore he lodged missing complaint as per Exhibit 15 and also further that since they learnt that even accused no.1 Rahul was not attending his work and was missing he had suspicion against him and therefore he lodged missing complaint and though he further stated that after two months his daughter was traced with accused Rahul, he appear to have stated that when his daughter came to his house and when he enquired with her, she did not state anything. Then, though he further stated that his daughter had stated her mother as to what had happened, as is clear, the mother of the girl is not examined by the prosecution and no explanation is offered for same. 17] Then, as discussed above, the evidence of the girl is not available and therefore so far as the allegations that the accused no.1 had taken away the girl and the accused no.2 had helped him or further that the accused no.1 had sexual intercourse with the girl etc. cannot be said to have been established. No doubt P.W.2, the headmaster of the P.R. High School where the girl was studying, deposed that as per school record the date of birth of the girl is 20.06.1997 and the relevant entry is also produced on record at Exh.20 and if the age of the girl is calculated on that basis, the age of the girl at the relevant time when the girl went missing comes below 18 years. Even it is also clear from the testimony of the medical officer Dr. Jayashree Mhaske, P.W.3 that on 13.07.2013 when she had examined the girl she had noticed that the girl was under age and was raped and accordingly she issued certificate Exhibit 25. 18] But in that respect also it is to be mentioned that in her evidence she also stated that the girl did not have any external .. 9 .. Special Case No.73/2013 Judgment injury and in her cross-examination she accepted that she did not find any signs of forceful intercourse and in such circumstance her opinion that the girl was raped cannot be said to be correct opinion. In any case the medical officer at the most can opine as to whether the girl had undergone sexual intercourse or whether there was any forceful sexual intercourse. But in the present case, as mentioned above, the medical officer stated that there was no external injury. Even the history alleged to have been given by the girl as has been mentioned in the medical certificate is that she had gone with accused Rahul whom she knows since one year and on 5th May to Delhi and stayed for 15 days and then they had gone to Bihar and history given was of sexual intercourse 10 to 15 times at Delhi and last was on 07.07.2013. As such, from the history given also no allegations of forceful sexual intercourse were even made by the girl while stating history to the medical officer. In such circumstances as rightly pointed out on behalf of accused the opinion given by the medical officer that the girl was raped is on the face of it was wrong. 19] In any case when it is clear from the medical evidence on record that the girl had undergone sexual intercourse, in absence of any cogent and reliable evidence to show that it was the accused who had sexual intercourse with the girl and in absence of evidence of the girl in regard to the aspect as to she had been taken away by the accused no.1, the allegations against the accused no.1 cannot be said to have been established. Therefore, the submission on behalf of prosecution that the girl was minor below 18 years of age and she is seen to have been subjected to sexual intercourse and therefore offence of kidnapping and rape have to be held as proved etc. cannot be said to be sustainable. Even there is absolutely no evidence in regard to the allegations against the accused no.2 that he abetted the commission of crime by accused no.1 Rahul Yadav. Point no. 1 to 4 are answered accordingly. .. 10 .. Special Case No.73/2013 Judgment 20] In view of my finding to point no.1 to 4 no offences are proved against the accused persons and they are entitled to be acquitted. Point no.5 is therefore answered accordingly. 21] Since the accused are acquitted, it is necessary that they be directed to execute P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/- [rupees fifteen thousand only] each in the like amount under section 437A of Cr.P.C. to appear before the higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect of any appeal or revision if any filed against the judgment. In the result I pass the following order - ORDER Accused namely Rahul Ramvilas Yadav and Pankajkumar Siyacharan Jamedar are acquitted of the charge for offene punishable under section 363, 366A, 376 of Indian Penal Code and also under section 4 and 16 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 2) Bail bonds of accused stand cancelled and sureties are discharged. 3) The accused shall execute P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/- [rupees fifteen thousand only] each under section 437A of Cr.P.C. to appear before the higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect of any appeal or revision, if any, filed against the judgment and that such bail bond shall be in force for six months. 4) Muddemal articles being worthless after expiry of appeal period. 5) The proceeding is closed. Date : 10.04.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.

CNR NO.MHTH01­005571­2018 1 A.B.A.1993/2018 ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN ANTI. BAIL APPLICATIOIN No.1993/2018 (CNR No. MHTH01­005571­2018) 1] The applicant Bhushan Ashok Bhandari has filed this application for grant of anticipatory bail u/s.438 of Cr.P.C. in C.R.No.I­ 75/2018 registered at Ganeshpuri Police Station U/Section­376(n) of I.P. Code and u/s.4, 8 and 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. 2] Brief facts of the prosecution case are as under:­ On 02/07/2018 the complainant Rina Yadav aged 20 years lodged complaint to police station Ganeshpuri. As per that complaint she was residing with her parents at Vasai. She was working in Minakshi Industries. She came in contact with accused. He proposed for friendship, obtained her phone number and started to make communication with her, then they fell in love, they used to frequently go for outing. On 18/05/2015 they both went to Vajreshwari temple, stayed at lodge. The accused compelled her to keep physical relation with her by saying that he will marry with her. He took her in temple and pretended that they performed marriage. Then they were meeting with each other frequently, they had sexual relationship with them from time to time. Till 2017 these all things were continued. Then she came to know that accused have love affair with another girl and on being asked to him, he refused about the same. Then he avoided to receive her phone calls, she was insisting for marriage but he was avoiding. Then she came to know that in March 2018 he performed marriage with other girl and also came to know that she is cheated by the accused. Accordingly, she lodged complaint and on its basis, above referred crime came to be registered. CNR NO.MHTH01­005571­2018 2 A.B.A.1993/2018 3] The applicant/accused contended that he is innocent, have not committed any offence, he belongs to reputed family, he has no concern with the matter and the custody is not necessary for investigation. On this count, he prayed for bail. 4] In reply, Ld. A.P.P. and I.O. submitted say and opposed the application with contention that investigation is yet to be completed, the accused committed sexual intercourse with the victim when she was minor, she was taken from time to time at different places, entries about their stay in Tansa Lodge, Akloli are obtained by the I.O., there is evidence about their stay at different places, the accused may tamper witnesses, investigation and interrogation is necessary. 5] I heard the submissions of Ld. Adv. for applicant/accused and Ld. A.P.P. Perused case diary. 6] Ld. Counsel for the applicant/accused submitted that the very contention made in FIR disclosed that victim was minor in 2005 and she has narrated the incident shown happened on 18/05/2015. Thereafter, she attained majority and subsequently she kept physical relations with him. As per his submissions no case of cheating or rape is made out and allegations are false. 7] Ld. A.P.P. on the contrary submitted that considering the allegations, interrogation is necessary and custody of accused is require and that when victim was minor, till that time, physical relations are kept and the complainant is cheated. CNR NO.MHTH01­005571­2018 3 A.B.A.1993/2018 8] After registration of FIR the accused moved this application and also application for interim relief vide Exh.3 and said application was allowed on 08/08/2018 and interim protection was granted to him. 9] What appears from the contentions of both sides, documents on record and contents of FIR is that, long back in the year 2015 the victim came in contact with accused, having physical relations between them and then she continued those relationship for about two years. She came to know about love affair of accused with another girl and then only she started asking him to marry and she came to know about his marriage also. So everything was going on with consent and so far as the incident of the year 2015 is concerned, no complaint is lodged within time or moderate period and now only because at the time of incident in the year 2015 she was minor, provisions of POCSO Act are made applicable. So considering fact that relationship was shown with consent after attaining majority, in my view, this is a fit case to consider for grant of anticipatory bail and the relief previously granted can be continued with terms and conditions. Hence, following order is passed. ORDER 1] Application for anticipatory bail is allowed. 2] In the event of arrest, the applicant Bhushan Ashok Bhandari in respect of C.R.No.I­75/2018 registered with Ganeshpuri police station for offence punishable U/s. 376(n) of Indian Penal Code and u/s. 4, 8 & 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, be released on bail on his executing P.B & S.B. of Rs.30,000/­ with CNR NO.MHTH01­005571­2018 4 A.B.A.1993/2018 one or two solvent sureties of like amount. 3] The applicant/accused shall attend concerned police station on every Sunday from 10.00 a.m. to 11.00 a.m. for four weeks and shall co­operate in investigation. 4] The interim relief granted earlier on 08/08/2016 is continued. M.M.Walimohammed Additional Sessions Judge­5, Thane AND Special Judge, POCSO Act) Spl.POCSO Case No.209/2016 Exh.No.21 State of Maharashtra (Through Mira Road Police station). ..... Complainant. V/s. Pankaj Ramsevak Singh. Age 25 years. R/at A­1204, Dev Paradise, Near Market Point, Kanakia, Mira Road (E), Tal. & Dist. Thane. ..... Accused. Learned APP Smt. Shilpa Talhar for prosecution. Learned Advocate Shri Ram Pande for accused. …..................... Offence punishable under section 354 of I.P.C. and under section 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act (POCSO). …................ 2 Spl.POCSO 209/2016 JUDGMENT (Delivered on this 14th day of July, 2017) 1] The accused is charge­sheeted for the offence punishable under section 354 of I.P.C., under section 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act (POCSO). 2] In brief the prosecution alleged that complainant Sangita Murari Singh is residing in Goregaon, Mumbai(E) alongwith daughter Nikita, son Sourabh and younger daughter Hetal since last 16 years. Her husband is doing business of Real Estate and she is attending the business of Beauty Parlour. Her daughter is attending Royal Academy, Goregaon in 8th standard. 3] It is alleged that on 2nd November,2014, her younger daughter Hetal and brother Dinesh had been to Mira Road in vacation. On 09.11.2014, at about 12.00 hours night, her husband brought Hetal to house at Goregaon. 4] It is alleged that on 16.11.2014, her brother Dinesh Singh gave a phone call that on 09.11.2014, at about 9.30 p.m. Hetal, Prerana and Isha were playing in the campus of A Wing Building. The accused Pankaj is residing 3 Spl.POCSO 209/2016 in the same building asked them that he will coach how to play basket ball. On inquiry, daughter Hetal was frightened and by taking into confidence she reported that when she, Prerana and Isha were playing basket ball, Pankaj Ramsevak Singh informed that he will coach how to play basket ball and taken them in parking lawn. It is alleged that said accused caught hold hand of Prerana and put hand on her chest. She rescued hand. Thereafter, Pankaj told Hetal, “Tu bahut Acchi Hai” and caught hold her hand and moved hand on her chest. She rescued hand. Her husband went to parking lawn and accused Pankaj was found present. He again caught hold hand of Hetal and moved hand on her chest and told I love you. 5] She, therefore, lodged complaint and concerned police of Mira Road police station registered crime No I­ 544/2014 under section 354 of I.P.C. and under section 7, 8 of POCSO Act. 6] During investigation spot panchanama alongwith rough map was drawn, statement of witnesses were recorded also question and answer form, copies of birth certificates of 4 Spl.POCSO 209/2016 Hetal and Prerana were collected, accused was arrested and on completion of investigation charge­sheet was submitted. 7] On hearing learned APP, defence counsel and considering record charge below Exh. 6 was framed under section 354 of I.P.C. and under section 8 of POCSO Act and the same when read over and explained to the accused in vernacular, he has denied the same vide his statement Exh.7. 8] The prosecution examined in all five witnesses. The accused did not examine himself, nor produced the evidence. 9] From the evidence and statement under section 313 of Cr.P.C. his defence is of total of denial and that he is falsely involved. 10] I have heard learned APP and learned defence counsel today. 11] The learned APP submitted that evidence of victims in particular namely Prerana and Hetal is sufficient to believe 5 Spl.POCSO 209/2016 the offence of sexual assault. There is no reason for prosecution to involve the accused falsely. 12] On the other hand learned defence counsel submitted that false case is filed because of some quarrel. He submitted that though accused resides in the same building, but he did not commit any offence. 13] In these circumstances following points arise for my determination and I record my finding to them for the reasons mentioned hereinafter :­ Sr. POINTS FINDINGS No. 1] Whether prosecution proved that In the on 09/11/2014 at about 09.30 p.m. affirmative. in the compound of Dev Paradise Building, Mira Road (E) within the jurisdiction of Mira Road Police Station,accused used criminal force to victims Hetal Singh age 13 years, Prerana age 12 years, intending to outrage their modesty ? 2] Whether it is proved that on the In the said date, time and place and affirmative. during the course of same transaction, accused committed offence of sexual assault on victims 6 Spl.POCSO 209/2016 Kumari Hetal and Kumari Prerana age 13 and 12 years ? 3] What order ? Accused is convicted as per final order REASONS POINT NOS. 1 AND 2 : 14] For the sake of convenient discussion points are clubbed. 15] The prosecution examined P.W. Geeta Singh, sister­in­law of complainant, P.W. Prerana Singh, victim, P.W. Hetal Singh another victim, P.W. Sangita Singh, mother of Hetal, and P.W. Somnath Divakar, Investigating Officer. 16] The facts that accused is residing in the same building where victim was putting on so as to say his identity is not disputed. 17] The evidence of P.W. Geeta Singh shows that Sangita is her sister­in­law. In Dipawali vacation of 2014, daughter of sister­in­law Hetal had come to their house. On 16.11.2014, her daughter Prerana was frightened and on her 7 Spl.POCSO 209/2016 inquiry, she reported that when they were playing basket ball, Pankaj (accused) came and told that he will give coaching of basket ball. He has taken daughter to parking and there was no electricity. He caught hold hand of her daughter and put hand on her chest. Her daughter also informed that similar incident took place with daughter of sister­in­law Hetal. She admitted that she came to know about the incident from the occupants of the building. She denied that no incident took place. She is formal witness. 18] The evidence of P.W. Sangita shows that Hetal is her daughter, and on inquiry with daughter she informed that accused put hand on her chest. She therefore lodged FIR at Exh.15. She is the person who set the law in motion. She received phone call from her brother on 16.11.2014. The incident alleged before that. The present nature of the case requires consideration as there appears no deliberate delay. It is also to be taken into account that matter pertaining to the modesty of the growing girls, the parents may not be ready to easily indulge and expose daughters to such nature of offence. 8 Spl.POCSO 209/2016 19] This takes me to discuss the evidence of victims. The evidence of Prerana shows that in 2014 she was learning in6th standard. During the Dipawali vacation, she had been to her parental aunt,she and Hetal were playing foot ball on 09.11.2014. Meanwhile Pankaj (accused) came and asked that he will coach how basket ball was playing. 20] Her evidence shows that he (accused) has taken her and Hetal at parking lawn, there was no electricity. He caught hold her hand and put hand on her chest. He did the same thing with Hetal. She rescued herself. She informed the incident to the parents on 16.11.2014. Her date of birth is 21.03.2003 and bonafide certificate is at Exh.10. So far as date of birth referred to concerned, her learning 6th standard in 2014 is not disputed. She was therefore obviously minor. 21] She was put up about her school times and she did not inform the incident to watchman. She also put up that there was quarrel between Nikhil Singh and accused and she she involved the accused in false case. There appears no believable evidence that Nikhil is related to the victim and complainant was having any animosity and engineered the false implication. 9 Spl.POCSO 209/2016 22] The evidence of P.W.Hetal shows that her date of birth is 01.01.2002. In Dipawali vacation of 2014, they had been to the house of Uncle at Mira Road. She, Prerana and Isha were playing basket ball, accused came and told that he will teach basketball playing. He touched her hand and chest. She was put up at the instance of her family members, she disclosed the incident to the police. 23] The victims were of growing girls and obviously minors. They are not of so teen age that they were totally incapable of understanding and above all were tutored. On that date of recording of evidence in April,2014, Hetal informed her age 16 years and Prerana 14 years. On the date of incident obviously both were minors. In the circumstances, identity of the accused being not disputed, their evidence is of not only believable but trustworthy I am of the opinion possibility of tutoring is ruled out. 24] The alleged dispute that Nikhil also informed by accused while answering these statement u/s. 313 of Cr.P.C. appears to have no foundation. There appears no reason for the victims and parents of falsely implicating the accused. There appears no oblique motive behind the prosecution. 10 Spl.POCSO 209/2016 25] In last witness Somnath Divakar Investigating Officer received the investigation of Crime No.544/2014 drawn spot panchanama Exh.17, collected birth certificate and after recording the statements of the witnesses submitted charge­sheet. He was only put up that he did not record statements of the witnesses as per their say. 26] At the cost of repetition, the evidence of the victims Prerarna and Hetal is not only consistent but trustworthy and believable. I have discussed that there is no reason of false implication of accused for the simple reason any inimical terms or rivalry nor any animosity nor any property dispute is found related. I have also referred that parents may not be easily ready to indulge their daughters to expose them before society regarding the matter pertaining to their modesty, chastity. Having found the evidence in particular of the victims discernable and believable, the prosecution succeeds in proving the guilt. 27] It is here I have heard the accused on the point of sentence. He submitted that his age is 26 years. He is serving as Sales Officers in I.C.A. Pidilite Pvt. Ltd., Mumbai. He is having parents and his marriage is yet to be performed. He 11 Spl.POCSO 209/2016 requested that lenient view may be taken. 28] There appears no antecedent on record. In the facts and circumstances, and request I am of the opinion that following sentence would be just and proper. ORDER 1] Accused Pankaj Ramsevak Singh is convicted for the offence punishable under section 354 of I.P.C. as per section 235(2) of Cr.P.C. and sentenced to suffer S.I. till rising of the Court and pay fine of Rs.500/­ in default to suffer S.I. for one month. 2] The accused is also convicted for the offence punishable under section 8 of POCSO Act and sentenced to suffer S.I. for three years and pay fine of Rs.500/­ in default to suffer S.I. for six months. 3] Substantial sentences shall run currently. 4] The accused to surrender his bail bonds. Thane. (M.M.Walimohammed) Dt. 14/07/2017. Additional Sessions Judge­5, And Spl. Judge, POCSO Thane.
