Bail no.2094/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 2094/2015 This application is filed by applicant Rahul alias Monu Rakesh Kathara alias Rai for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. I-86/2015 registered at N.R.I. Sagri police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 363, 366A, 376 of I.P.C. and section 4, 8, 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). It is contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant committed rape on the minor daughter of the complainant. It is further contended and argued that the applicant and victim girl were in love with each other and applicant had promised to marry her and girl of her own had left her house and they had physical relations with each other and it is a case of consent. It is further contended and argued that the applicant is falsely implicated on the basis of a delayed complaint lodged on the basis of an after thought story. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co-operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it is contended and argued that the applicant had induced the victim girl by giving false assurance of marriage and had kept physical relations with her. Itis further .. 2 .. Bail no.2094/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) contended and argued that name of the present application is stated by the girl while lodging the F.I.R. It is further contended and argued that co-accused who is friend of the present applicant had also committed rape on the girl when he had gone to her house in the night to watch TV he had also threatened to kill her and her mother if she disclose about the act to anybody. It is further contended and argued that fact of sexual assault on the was revealed only when the girl was found pregnant. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl and the prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, the offences charged against the applicant/accused are of serious nature under section 363, 366A, 376 of I.P.C. and section 4, 8, 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act with the allegation that the applicant/accused and co-accused committed rape on the minor victim girl. But then it is contended by the applicant that it is a case of consent since there was affair between him and the girl. Then, the applicant is seen to F.I.R. named accused wherein serious allegations of repeated sexual assault on the minor girl are made. Then, the submissions on behalf of applicant/accused that there is delay in lodging the F.I.R. and only after the girl noticed to be pregnant the complaint came to be lodged etc. it is to be mentioned that the delay in lodging the F.I.R. in such type of offence cannot be said to be fatal lacuna .. 3 .. Bail no.2094/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) and that cannot be a ground for coming to the conclusion at this stage that the F.I.R. is concocted or false or applicant is falsely involved in the crime. The offence alleged is of very serious nature and the investigation is in progress and release of accused on bail would cause hurdle in the investigation. 4] Then, though it is well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail, besides that the gravity and serious nature of offence and the manner in which it is stated to have been committed has to be looked into and looking to the nature of offence and the manner in which it is alleged to have been committed, a wrong message would be sent to the society in case of release of accused on bail in such type of matter wherein serious allegations of sexual assault on a minor girl are made. 5] Then, keeping in mind the pre-acquaintance of the victim girl with the applicant/accused since it is alleged by the applicant there was love between him and the girl, the apprehension expressed by the prosecution that the accused may threaten and pressurize the victim girl and her family members is well founded and even possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded and not available for trial cannot be ruled out. .. 4 .. Bail no.2094/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) 6] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is not a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail at this stage. I therefore pass the following order - ORDER The application is rejected. Date : 14.09.2015 (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Additional Session Judge-1, Thane.

Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­0005616­2014 Special (POCSO) Case No.190/14 Received on : 25.09.2014 Registered on : 25.09.2014 Decided on : 30.10.2018 Duration : 4Ys.1M.5Ds. IN THE COURT OF D.J.­1 & ADDL. SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE (Presided over by Hemant M. Patwardhan) Special (POCSO) Case No. 190/14 Exh.No. 1.State of Maharashtra. ( Mokhada Police station) ..Complainant V/s. 1. Mahesh @ Babalya Mahadu Bhoye, Age 30 years, Occ. Nil R/at. Osarvira paiki Ghodichapada, Tal. Mokhada, Dist. Thane ..Accused Appearance:­ APP Mrs. Varsha Chandane for the State. Advocate Mrs. Swati Chitnis for the accused. JUDGMENT (Delivered on this 30th day of October 2018 ) Accused Mahesh @ Babalya Bhoye was facing trial under sections 376(2)(i)(k)(n) of IPC read with section 4 of 1 to 12 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­0005616­2014 Special (POCSO) Case No.190/14 Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 on following facts:­ 1] That since prior 1 ½ years to 25.06.2014 at Jawhar Phata, Mokhada accused has repeatedly committed rape on minor girl below age of 16 years under the pretext of keeping her in his house and as the girl was minor at the relevant time accused with sexual intent has committed penetrative sexual assault on her. Thus, on the basis of complaint lodged by father of victim, an offence punishable under aforesaid sections came to be registered against accused. On completion of investigation he was charge­sheeted. 2] Charge came to be framed at Exh.3 and contents of said charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. Accused pleaded not guilty and claim to be tried. His defence was of total denial and that he has been made scapegoat to save relative of the victim who actually has in sexual relationship with the victim. 3] Prosecution was then proceeded to examine victim, her father, medical officer Dr. Sunil Jadhav who has clinically examined victim for determination of her age, private medical practitioner Dr. Anita Patil who has initially examined victim and has determined her pregnancy and finally I.O. Ghanshyam 2 to 12 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­0005616­2014 Special (POCSO) Case No.190/14 Adhav as witness no.1 to 5 respectively. Then statement of the accused was recorded as per his say wherein again he has reiterated his defence as above. 4] Arguments of rival advocates were heard. Learned P.P. though admitted fact that DNA report is favouring the accused but she has submitted that said fact can only established that pregnancy of the victim was not due to accused person but according to her that cannot be a fact which conclusively determined that accused did not commit rape on the victim. According to learned P.P. there was no reason for the accused to take the victim to witness no.4 for medical check up without informing her parents, once he was made aware about pregnancy of the victim. Thus, according to prosecution attempt of accused to suppress particular fact from victim's parents in itself is sufficient to substantiate the allegations of prosecution. According to learned P.P. all defence put forth to victim and her father has been categorically denied. Thus, learned P.P. has requested the court to place its reliance on version of the victim and her father to held accused guilty of the offence. 5] Per contra, according to defence's submissions, the deposition of the victim is not corroborated by any other's deposition. She has then pointed out that residential place of 3 to 12 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­0005616­2014 Special (POCSO) Case No.190/14 accused is too small wherein his mother also was residing. Thus, in presence of his mother there was no possibility of making such an act. She has then pointed out that victim was residing with accused as his children's care taker, she used to visit her parents in every fortnight and in spite of the said fact she did not make reference of her condition with anybody itself is sufficient to discard allegation against accused. According to her submissions if accused would have really committed said offence, victim would have informed her parents when she had been to them immediately after detection of her pregnancy. She has then submitted that as a matter of fact victim had an affair with her relatives by name Anil and pregnancy was due to their sexual relations and in order to save said Anil, accused has made scapegoat. She has then pointed out that though there was an attempt to settle the matter before Village Panchayat and though particular facts were known to parents of the victim, neither parents nor I.O. has made any attempt to even record statement of said Anil. Thus, that fact is apparently fatal to the prosecution. According to her above all when police have forwarded blood samples of accused, victim etc. to DNA Analysis, Analyzer has categorically opined that accused is not biological father of that child. Thus, according to her that particular opinion of analyzer in itself is sufficient to establish accused's innocence. She has therefore, requested court to acquit the accused. 4 to 12 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­0005616­2014 Special (POCSO) Case No.190/14 6] After having heard rival advocates, following points arose for my consideration and I record my findings against each of them for the reasons noted below :­ Sr.N. Points Findings 1] Does the prosecution prove that accused since prior 1 ½ years ..Negative. to 25.06.2014 at Jawhar Phata, Mokhada repeatedly committed rape on minor girl below age of 16 years under the pretext of keeping her in his house and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 376(2)(i)(k)(n) of Indian Penal Code? 2] Does the prosecution prove that on the aforesaid time and ..Negative. place, accused has committed penetrative sexual assault on the victim girl while his act of actual commission of repeated rape and thus thereby committed an offence under section 4 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012? 3] What order? Accused is acquitted as per final order. REASONS As to point no.1 to 3 :­ 7] All these points are interlinked with each other and are considered at once. In the instant case prosecution has made two­fold allegations viz. that the accused has repeatedly committed rape and as the victim was a minor said act of commission of rape also comes within purview of penetrative sexual assault with sexual intent. Thus, prosecution was required to prove said allegations with substantive evidence. Prosecution though has examined aforesaid five witnesses, considering nature of offence only victim was the best available 5 to 12 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­0005616­2014 Special (POCSO) Case No.190/14 evidence so far as allegations are concerned. No doubt victim has alleged that accused himself has committed rape on her. However, during cross­examination she has admitted that she was residing with accused whose family was consisting of his wife, daughter and mother. She has also admitted that she used to visit her parents frequently after 15 days of stay with the accused but she did not inform any such incident to her parents even after she came to know about her pregnancy. Though she has claim to have informed about act of the accused to her younger sister, neither her statement is recorded by police nor she was examined as a witness. Thus, defence has categorically pointed out that as her deposition is not corroborated by anybody else, said needs to be discarded. 8] Thus, prosecution proceeded to examine her father who has categorically deposed that accused and his father­in­ law had visited his house after victim had resided with accused for about 1 ½ years and informed him that victim is pregnant. He has also alleged that accused tried to terminate pregnancy but could not succeed. He also accepted in examination­in­chief that they have tried to settle dispute before village panchayat but said also could not work out and as his daughter named accused responsible for the act, complaint was then lodged. Therefore, even if we consider the deposition of father of victim then also he himself has nowhere made any avernments of he 6 to 12 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­0005616­2014 Special (POCSO) Case No.190/14 being informed by the victim. Thus, though there are specific allegations of the victim against accused court has to consider whether those allegations are really trustworthy or defence of the accused is more probable. Therefore, said depositions are tested on the basis of defence advanced by the accused. 9] Accused has categorically raised the defence that situation in the house was not such to have sexual relationship with victim and that he had never such relationship with her. On the contrary victim had an affair with one Anil Pardhi but in order to save him from the allegations, accused has been made a scapegoat. Accused has then categorically put forth said defence before both victim and her father and was succeeded to obtain admissions like that the mother of the accused used to live in the said house even after wife and children of the accused used to leave house, that victim used to visit her parents after about fortnight and in spite of that she did not inform her parents about the act of the accused alleged by her, that there was an attempt made by the accused to put forth his grievance before village panchayat wherein he has categorically made allegation against relative of the victim named above being in sexual relationship with the victim and being father of the child in womb of the victim. Then also it is apparent that victim, her parents or village panchayat members did not initiate any action against said relative of the victim. Thus, it is 7 to 12 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­0005616­2014 Special (POCSO) Case No.190/14 apparent from the admission of the witnesses that there was ample opportunity for the victim to inform her parents about the alleged act of the accused immediately after occurrence of the first incident. 10] It is alleged that accused used to commit said act repeatedly for about 1½ years. If that allegations are considered then after commission of the alleged act for the first time it was open to victim to inform her parent immediately during her visit to them after the said incident. There are absolutely no allegations either by the victim or by her father about they being under any threat from the accused to keep mum even after their particular visit. When parties have admitted having taken said matter before the village panchayat at that time also if act of the accused would have really prima facie established, the parents were at liberty to immediately approach concern police. However, their failure to approach police even at that time, makes allegations doubtful and on and on the contrary defence of the accused becomes more probable. 11] If we consider admission of I.O. about nature of room in which accused was residing that too along with his family and his mother then it is difficult to really accept that accused would dare to commit such act before his mother who remain to be in house even after wife of accused left for her 8 to 12 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­0005616­2014 Special (POCSO) Case No.190/14 job. Further, house of the accused is surrounded by other residence of the villagers and though allegations were made of having recorded statements of neighborers, no such neighbour was brought before the court for substantiating the allegations of prosecution. 12] Medical officer who has initially examined the victim has categorically deposed that accused himself has brought victim and when she has suspected her to be pregnant and on even asked why the parents of the victim did not come, accused has replied to be a guardian of victim and has followed her instruction of getting her sonography report on next day. On the basis of that report she has confirmed about the pregnancy of the victim. However, she has admitted that she on her own did not inform police as there is custom in community of the victim of having relationship of such nature and around 30% of pregnancy arise out of such relationship. She has also made statement voluntarily that initially when she has made an attempt to inform police about it but police were unwilling to register such complaints. Thus, she did not inform police even after she has noticed pregnancy on the basis of the report produced by the accused before her. If we consider the said custom and categorical deposition of said medical officer who is practicing in said area itself since long then it is apparent that there is custom of being in such relationship in 9 to 12 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­0005616­2014 Special (POCSO) Case No.190/14 the community to which victim belongs. Thus, defence of the accused about she being in such relationship with other person can be considered to be probable. Above all one important fact which really favours accused in this matter is report of expert in DNA. Blood samples were collected both of the victim and accused after complaint was lodged and those blood samples were forwarded for DNA test. Analyzer has then forwarded report to this court which is filed at Exh.7. On perusal of said report it is apparent that analyzer Mr. Patil has categorically opined that after analysis Mr. Mahesh Bhoye in case no. DNA–944/14 is excluded to be biological father of baby of victim. Thus, said candid opinion of C.A. in itself is sufficient to establish defence and innocence of the accused. Though, learned P.P. has made an attempt to convince the court that said candid opinion can only be consider to discard the fact being biological father but that in itself cannot be considered to be fact of allegations of having committed rape on the victim are false. However, said submissions of learned P.P. cannot be considered in view of behaviour of victim and her father, admission of parties about having made an attempt before village panchayat and even after failure of the said attempt their failure of lodging the complaint immediately, the act of the victim of her failure to inform her parents even though there were no allegations of 10 to 12 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­0005616­2014 Special (POCSO) Case No.190/14 she being placed in such threats of accused not to disclose the said fact etc. considered at once then the conduct of the victim or her father nowhere appears to be conduct of natural human being who has come to know about the particular fact. Having regards to the said facts, the deposition of the victim nowhere appears to be consistent, reliable and due to aforesaid conduct does not inspire confidence about her allegation. The failure of the I.O. even to make investigation about relationship between the victim and said Anil therefore, appears to be more fatal to the prosecution. Having regards to the said fact as the evidence brought before the court is inconsistent and does not inspire confidence, same cannot be form basis of conviction of the accused. On the contrary whatever defence has been put forth appears to be more probable which is substantiated by expert opinion. Hence, by accepting it, the court has to conclude that accused has been falsely implicated in this matter. Thus, I do not hesitate to record my findings against point no.1 and 2 in negative and by holding that accused is entitled for clear acquittal, proceed to pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused is acquitted from the offence punishable under section 376(2)(i)(k)(n) of IPC read with section 4 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 11 to 12 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­0005616­2014 Special (POCSO) Case No.190/14 2] Bail bond of accused accordingly shall stands cancelled. 3] Accused is directed to execute P.R. and S.B. of Rs.10,000/­ as per amended provisions of section 437(A) of Cr.P.C. and bonds so executed shall remain in force for the period of six months from the date of its execution. 4] Proceeding is accordingly closed. Thane (Hemant M.Patwardhan) Date: 30.10.2018 D.J.­1 & Additional Sessions Judge, Thane 12 to 12

Offence punishable under Sec. 354­A(1)(i), 354­D(1)(i)(2), 341 of Indian Penal Code and under Sec. 11(i)(iv) and 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2 Special Case (Pocso) No. 195/2015 Judgment Appearances : Smt. Sunil Patankar, Advocate for accused JUDGMENT ( Delivered on this 26th day of July, 2017 ) 1] Accused is facing trial for the offence punishable under Sec. 354­A(1)(i), 354­D(1)(i)(2), 341 of Indian Penal Code and under Sec. 11(i)(iv) punishable under Sec. 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] Prosecution Case, in brief, is as under : Informant is the victim. She is residing with her parents, brother and sister. Her father runs pan shop. Victim is studying in 10th standard. She go to school alone. Her school timing is from 7.00 a.m. to 1.00 p.m. The timing of her tuition class is from 4.00 p.m. to 8.00 p.m. The accused Shravan was following the victim since the time when victim was in 8th standard. He used to insist her to talk to him. He used to say that he loves her and he wants to marry her. He used to inflict injury on his hand with the help of razer so that she should talk to him. She narrated the incident prior to one year to her mother. Her mother convinced the accused by visiting his house. There was no change in his attitude. He used to prevent her while proceeding to school or tuition. He used to utter words “ dsGh [kkrs dk;\** He used to utter indecent words. On 28.01.2015, at 9.00 p.m., accused came alone to her house and called victim. He stated the victim's mother that he 3 Special Case (Pocso) No. 195/2015 Judgment wants to marry victim. Victim's mother resisted him. Then, the father of the accused came and took the accused with him. Then, the victim lodged report to police station. 3] On the basis of report, offence was registered vide C.R.No. I­24/2015. A.P.I. Patil has investigated this crime. He arrested the accused. He drew arrest­cum­personal search panchanama. He recorded statements of witnesses. After completion of investigation, he filed charge­sheet in the Court of Law. 4] I have framed charge against accused below Exh. 2 to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 5] Prosecution has examined four witnesses. Then, the statement of the accused under Sec. 313 of Cr.P.C. came to be recorded. Total denial is the defence of the accused. The accused has also tried to raise defence that the victim was having love on accused since she was in 8th standard. Her parents got suspicion on it. On 26.01.2015, the mother of the victim had seen the victim and the accused while chatting. Victim lodged false complaint due to the pressure of her parents. 6] I have heard both the sides. 7] Ld. P.P. Smt.Phad has submitted that the F.I.R. was 4 Special Case (Pocso) No. 195/2015 Judgment lodged promptly. Evidence of victim is supported by other witnesses. Accused has not given any explanation in the statement under Sec. 313 of Criminal Procedure Code. Though the defence is about chatting on mobile but, the accused has not made available the mobile number of the victim. So, the defence is false and that is one of the strong circumstances to prove the guilt. On the other hand, Ld. Advocate for the accused has submitted that father of the victim has stated that he made grievance about molestation to the Headmaster of the School. But, this fact is not stated by victim. The victim or her parents have not filed any complaint in respect of the alleged incident during two years before 28.01.2015. Parents of the victim have stated some different story about attempt to commit suicide by victim and this fact is not stated by victim. He has also submitted that there is no spot panchanama in this matter and investigation officer could not ascertain the spot of incident. He has also invited my attention to the contents in the report (Exh.12) and the statement of the victim under Sec. 164 of Cr.P.C. and submitted that there is variance in it. 8] Following points arose for my determination and I gave my findings thereon for the reasons stated below: Sr. POINTS FINDINGS No. 1. Does the prosecution prove that the No accused since last two years till 28.01.2015, at about 21.00 hrs., at the house of informant, in Phenagaon, 5 Special Case (Pocso) No. 195/2015 Judgment Kamatghar area, Bhiwandi has sexually harassed the informant i.e. minor victim girl age 15 years by physical contact and advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures and thereby committed an offence punishable under S. 354­A(1) (i) of Indian Penal Code? 2. Does the prosecution prove that on No. above mentioned date, time and place, accused followed the informant minor victim girl age 15 years and contacts, or attempts to contact her to foster personal interaction repeatedly despite a clear indication of disinterest by her and thereby committed an offence punishable under Sec. 354­D(1)(i)(2) of Indian Penal Code? 3. Does the prosecution prove that on No. aforesaid date, time and place, accused wrongfully restrained minor victim girl, age 15 years and thereby committed an offence punishable under Sec. 341 of Indian Penal Code? 4. Does the prosecution prove that on No. aforesaid date, time and place, accused committed sexual harassment upon a informant i.e. minor victim girl, age 15 years by uttering obscene words with intention that same shall be heard by her and giving blows of blade on his hand with intention that same shall be seen by her and repeatedly or constantly follow or contact her with sexual intent and thereby committed an offence under Sec. 11(i)(iv) punishable 6 Special Case (Pocso) No. 195/2015 Judgment under Sec.12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012? 5. What order? As per final order. REASONS AS TO POINT NO.1, 2 & 4 :­ 9] In order to establish the guilt of accused, it is incumbent on the part of prosecution to adduce reliable and trust worthy evidence. 10] The prosecution has examined victim P.W.1 Prabhakar, father of the victim (Exh.5), P.W.2 Ashwini, mother of the victim (Exh.8), P.W.3 Victim (Exh.11) and P.W.4 A.P.I Patil, investigation officer (Exh.14). It is well settled that a sole testimony of witness is sufficient to hold accused guilty, but the rule is that it should be worthy of reliance. 11] In order to prove the guilt under Sec.11 &12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, prosecution has to establish that the age of victim was below 18 years. The accused has not disputed the age of victim since accused has given no objection to exhibit the birth certificate of the victim. It is given Exh.6. It appears that on the day of incident, age of victim was below 18 years. 7 Special Case (Pocso) No. 195/2015 Judgment 12] In order to prove the guilt under Sec. 354­A (1)(i), the prosecution has to establish that the accused has committed the act of physical contact and also advances involving unwelcome sexual overtures. In order to establish the guilt under Sec. 11(i) and (iv) punishable under Sec. 12, prosecution has to establish that the accused uttered any word with the intention that it shall be heard and that too with sexual intent. It has also to be proved that the accused has repeatedly or constantly followed the victim that too with sexual intent. 13] Victim has stated that her school timing was 7.00 a.m. to 1.00 p.m. and the tuition timing was 4.00 p.m. to 8.00 p.m. She was attending the tuition to one Chandrashekhar Sir at Kamatghar area. Sometimes, the said Chandrashekhar Sir used to drop the victim at her house. Victim has stated that while proceeding to school, accused used to molest her. He was doing the same act since she was in 8th standard. He used to tease her by referring her name and by uttering words ^^vfdyk rw dsyk [kk;sxh D;k\**He used to say ^^ eS rq>ls I;kj djrk gqWa] rw eq>ls ckr dj-** Accused used to inflict injury to himself with the help of razer. She narrated this fact to her mother and convinced the parents of the accused. Even then, accused continued his acts. Then, she has just stated the incident on 28.01.2015 in between 8.00 to 9.00 p.m. According to her, the accused came to her house at that time and stated that he want to talk to victim. 8 Special Case (Pocso) No. 195/2015 Judgment But, her mother sent him back. Accused told her mother that she should perform her marriage with him. Victim's mother called the father of accused who took him to their house. Then, the report (Exh.12) was lodged. This is in all testimony of the victim. 14] It appears that at the time of lodging report, the victim was in 10th standard. The victim wants to say that accused used to molest her as stated in her evidence since prior to two years of her report. It is expected from the victim to state the details as to when such incident of following her and uttering indecent words has taken place. Such details are not stated by the victim in her oral evidence. Mere version that accused used to molest the victim since she was in 8th standard will not be sufficient to hold accused guilty. 15] It appears that the alleged incidents were on the way to her school or tuition. So, the incidents must have occurred in daylight. There is nothing to show that any independent person has seen such incident. 16] P.W.1 Prabhakar, the father of victim has not specifically stated about the incident which the victim has stated. P.W.1 Prabhakar has just stated that since the victim was in 8 th standard, accused was following her and was molesting her. According to him, the accused was also using indecent words. He has further stated that such acts of the accused were narrated by the victim to her mother, who in turn narrated to him. He has 9 Special Case (Pocso) No. 195/2015 Judgment stated in the cross­examination that he has made complaint to Headmaster of the School in respect of the troubles from the accused. He has also admitted that he had not moved any written complaint about the alleged act of the accused nor the headmaster has called him and the accused. P.W.1 Prabhakar has specifically admitted that in respect of the alleged acts of the accused during the period when victim was in 8th standard till her 10th standard, no complaint was lodged against the accused to police. If really there was such trouble from accused for a long period of two years, then certainly in natural course, victim or her parents would have approached the police from where they could get relief. In absence of such action on the part of the victim or her parents, it would be difficult to accept the oral evidence in the initial part of the victim to be natural. 17] It appears from the evidence of victim that sometimes the tuition teacher Mr. Chandrashekhar used to drop her to home. So, if there were incidents on the way from the place of tuition till her home, then Mr. Chandrashekhar would have also stated about it. This witness is not examined by the prosecution. 18] Victim's mother Ashwini has stated that since victim was in 8th standard, accused was following her. He used to ask her^^ esjsls I;kj djks*- He inflicted injury on his hand with the help of razer. Victim was opposing this attitude of the accused. Victim used to say 10 Special Case (Pocso) No. 195/2015 Judgment about these facts to her. She had convinced the parents of the accused by visiting the house of accused. But, there was no change in the attitude of the accused. P.W.2 Ashwini has further stated that accused used to ask the victim ^^dsyk [kk;sxh D;k\** So, this witness has also nowhere stated in the examination­in­chief about the specific incidents of particular kind of troubles from the accused. Victim or her mother have not stated as to exactly where such incidents have occurred and the timing of it. 19] Ld. Advocate for the accused has invited my attention to the cross­examination of A.P.I. Mr. Patil who has stated that spot panchanama is not on record. The suggestion is given to the investigation officer Mr. Patil that he could not ascertain the spot of alleged incident. In the ferist ( list) of the charge­sheet also, it is not revealed about drawing of any spot panchanama. So, the testimony of victim and her mother on such alleged act can not be said to be satisfactory. It is to be noted that the victim has specifically admitted that since she was acquainted to accused, she used to chat with the accused. This admission supports the defence of the accused about the affair between accused and victim and that while chatting on 26.01.2015, mother of the victim had seen them. Even if it is accepted for a moment that accused has followed the victim repeatedly still, another important aspect which prosecution has to establish is that the said attempt of following was there despite clear indication of disinterest by the victim. But, the admission by 11 Special Case (Pocso) No. 195/2015 Judgment the victim that since she was acquainted to accused, she used to chat with him, itself creates doubt about the indication of disinterest by victim. 20] It is already discussed in the foregoing paragraphs that initial part of the examination­in­chief of the victim can not be said to be satisfactory in absence of details. The said evidence in initial part can be said to be vague. Then, the victim has just stated that on 28.1.2015, accused came to her home and has stated his mother to perform his marriage with victim. This single incident will also not be sufficient to prove the guilt under Sec. 354­D(1)(i)of Indian Penal Code.. 21] Sec. 354­A(1)(i) required physical contact and also advances involving sexual overtures. Victim or her parents have nowhere stated about any incident of physical contact by the accused with the victim. 22] The parents of the victim have also tried to make out somewhat different story in their evidence. P.W.2 Ashwini, the mother of victim has stated that due to the alleged acts of the accused, victim had gone towards Varhaldevi lake for committing suicide. P.W.1 Prabhakar has stated that the victim has stated to commit suicide due to the troubles by the accused and accordingly, she had gone towards Varhaldevi lake for the purpose of suicide. But, this fact is not at all stated by the victim in oral evidence. 12 Special Case (Pocso) No. 195/2015 Judgment P.W.2 Ashwini has stated that when the victim went towards Varhaldevi lake, the boys in that area took the victim to her house. P.W.2 Ashwini has stated that the boy named Naresh Nandai in their area had seen the victim while she proceeded for alleged suicidal purpose. The said Naresh Nandai is not examined by the prosecution. So, that also creates doubt about the allegations against the accused. 23] Victim and her mother have stated that the accused used to utter words “rq dsyk [kk;sxh D;k\** It is already discussed above that no specific instance of such alleged act of the accused is stated by the victim or her mother. In order to establish the sexual harassment as given in Sec. 11 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, it is to be established that such utterances of the words by the accused were with sexual intent. Victim has stated that the accused used to tease ^^rq dsyk [kk;sxh D;k\** It is admitted that the victim was chatting with the accused as they were acquainted to each other. So, it can not be said merely on the basis of this version without having details that the said utterance was only with sexual intent. Considering the acquaintance between them, the possibility can not be ruled out about such utterance in jesting. 24] Victim has also stated that the accused used to utter words ^^eS rqels I;kj djrk gqWa] rq eq>ls ckr dj-** For that purpose, accused inflicted injury on his hand. In order to ascertain the 13 Special Case (Pocso) No. 195/2015 Judgment meaning of 'sexual intent', reliance can be placed in case of Bandu Vitthalrao Borwar V/s. State of Maharashtra, Criminal Appeal No. 50 of 2016, ( Bombay High Court). It is held in paragraph 10 as under : Para 10 “After all intention of a person is his state of mind and has to be discerned from the surrounding facts and circumstances. If one cannot, as a human being, physically enter into a mind of another to read and see what is being cooked there, one can surely know it by evaluating all that which is perceivable or felt by human senses such as words, body­ language, gestures, reactions and everything that is a physical manifestation of working of human mind. If somebody says that he is in love with another person or asks another person as to why the other person does not love him, such expression of a feeling or expectation of a particular feeling from another person would not by itself amount to an intent exhibiting some sort of sexuality.” It is held in Para 11 as under : Para 11 “It is obvious that the intent, which is nothing but a state of mind, must be to establish some sort of physical contact or must be related to or associated with sex or indicative of involvement of sex in the relationship, if it is to be considered as sexual. There should be something more which must suggest that the real intention is to drag in the angle of sex, if the words uttered are to be taken as conveying Sexual intent.” 14 Special Case (Pocso) No. 195/2015 Judgment 25] It is already discussed above that the victim and her mother have not stated the specific instance of such incident of utterance and so, their evidence on this point is not satisfactory. Even if evidence of victim is accepted as it is for a moment, still in view of the observations in this judgment, mere utterance that ^^eS rqels I;kj djrk gqWa] rq eq>ls ckr dj-**can not be said to be the utterance with sexual intent. If the alleged act is considered then, it can be said to be expectation that the other person should love him. Thus, the discussion above lead me to say that the evidence of prosecution would fall short so as to prove the ingredients of the offence under Sec. 354­A(1)(i), 354­D(1)(i) of Indian penal code and also under Sec. 11(i)(iv) punishable under Sec. 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. AS TO POINT No.3 :­ 26] In order to prove the guilt under Sec. 341 of Indian Penal Code, the prosecution has to establish that; (a) A person causes obstruction to any person; (b) such obstruction is caused voluntarily; (c) The obstruction prevents a person obstructed from proceeding in any direction in which he has a right to proceed. 27] Victim has stated that since she was in 8 th standard, accused was obstructing her when she was proceeding to school for 15 Special Case (Pocso) No. 195/2015 Judgment the reason that she should talk to him. It is already discussed in the foregoing paragraphs that the said version of the victim is vague and can not be accepted as satisfactory as she has not stated the details of the timing and place of such incident. Victim has admitted that she used to chat with the accused as they were acquainted to each other. So, it will be also difficult to accept that the accused has voluntarily obstructed the victim in the way. 28] It is not the case of victim that due to such incident, she could not proceed further after the alleged incident. Thus, the evidence of victim even if accepted in a whole will not be sufficient to hold accused guilty for the offence under Sec. 341 of Indian Penal Code. 29] Since it is held that the evidence of victim and her parents is not satisfactory and it is doubtful, the benefit of it is required to be given to the accused. For the reasons stated above, I answer the points in the negative and pass folloiwng order. ORDER 1] Accused Shravan Shrinivas Yeligetti is hereby acquitted under Sec. 235(1) of Code of Criminal Procedure of the offences punishable under Sec. 354­A(1)(i), 354­D(1)(i), 341 of Indian Penal Code and Sec.11(i)(iv) punishable under Sec.12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 16 Special Case (Pocso) No. 195/2015 Judgment 2] His bail bond stands cancelled. 3] Accused shall furnish P.B and S.B. of Rs. 15,000/­ under Sec. 437­A of Code of Criminal Procedure. Thane ( Ashutosh N. Karmarkar ) Date : 26.07.2017 District Judge­1 & Special Judge (POCSO) Act,Thane

--1-- ORDER BELOW EXH.1 IN CRIMINAL BAIL APPLICATION NO.2063/2017 The applicant Miraz Ahmed Irshad Ahmed Ansari has applied for bail under section 439 of Cr. P.C. in C.R.No.I­214/2017 registered in Shanti Nagar police station for the offence under section 354(A) of Indian Penal Code and Under section 8 of the POCSO Act, 2012. 2. It is contended that the false FIR is lodged against the present applicant. The house of the victim and the present applicant situated in thickly populated area. It is contended that the investigation is practically completed. The further custody of the present applicant is no more required. He is ready to co­operate for the investigation and abide by the conditions. 3. Investigating Officer has given his say at Exh.4. It is contended that the victim is five years old. The accused had called her and gave her Rs.2/­ to bring water pouch and the victim brought the water pouch. The accused took her inside his house and lifted her frock and seated her on his thighs and moved his hands on her chest. So if the applicant is released on bail he is likely to tamper the prosecution witnesses. He is resident of other State and therefore he is no likely to remain present for the trial. 4. I heard Ld. Counsel on behalf of the applicant and Ld. A.P.P. 5. The court is of the view that the investigation is almost completed, therefore, further custody of the present applicant in the jail without trial will not be justifiable. The applicant is resident of given address and he is ready to co­operate for further investigation and remain present for the trial. There are thousands --2-- of cases of such nature pending in the court. So if this applicant keep in jail his trial will not be commenced in near future and will not complete in a short period. It will take much time, therefore, court is of the view that till then it will not be justifiable to keep the applicant in jail. Hence, I proceed to pass following order. :ORDER: 1. Application is allowed. 2. Applicant be released on P.B. and S.B. of Rs.30,000/­ (Rupees Thirty Thousand Only) with one or two local solvent surety on the like amount. 3. The applicant shall give the address and contact numbers of two blood relatives situated in Thane District. 4. He shall not contact the victim, witnesses, informant and shall not pressurize, threaten them from dissuading them from the facts and circumstances of the case. 5. He shall not repeat any offence. 6. He shall not leave the jurisdiction of the court without prior permission of the court. 7. He shall remain present before the concerned police station once in a month till the trial is over and shall keep diary of attendance in the concerned police station. 8. If any condition is breached his bail will be cancelled. Thane. ( S.C. Khalipe ) Date : 01/09/2017. Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

.. 1 .. bail 1965/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 1965 of 2014 This application is filed by applicant Mrs. Farhat Sarjil Ahmed for her release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. I­25/2014 registered at Mira Road police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 324, 323, 317, 370, 374, 34 of I.P.C. and section 7, 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and section 23 of Child Act. It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant in furtherance of common intention with co­accused procured the victim girl who is minor, for household work and the co­accused Sarjil sexually abused her when the victim was staying in their house. It is further contended and argued that no such incident has happened and the applicant is falsely implicated in this crime. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/ accused is released on bail, she will co­operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that the applicant alongwith her husband i.e. co­accused Sarjil, had purchased the victim girl who is minor, from her mother i.e. another co­accused and brought her home as a maid servant. It is further contended and argued that the applicant and her husband used to physically torture her by beating her by belt. It is also contended and argued that the accused had applied chilli powder to the private part of the victim .. 2 .. bail 1965/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) when she failed to do her work correctly. It is also contended and argued that even co­accused Sarjil had committed sexual assault on the victim time and again at the connivance of the present applicant/ accused. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicants threatening the victim girl and the prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail she may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 324, 323, 317, 370, 374, 34 of I.P.C. and section 7, 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and section 23 of Child Act, the fact as has been pointed out on behalf of accused that the allegations of sexual abuse and assault are not directly against the present applicant It is also further material to mention that earlier the present applicant had filed application for anticipatory bail bearing no.215/2014 which came to be rejected by this Court and even another application filed by the applicant after submission of charge sheet against the co­accused bearing no.1033/2014 also was rejected and it is also clear that thereafter the applicant/accused came to be arrested on 20.09.2014 and she was remanded to police custody till 25.09.2014 and since then she is in Magisterial custody. As such there appear some substance in the submission of the accused that so far as investigation in regard to allegation against the present applicant is concerned, sufficient opportunity and time was there for the investigating officer to investigate into the matter even with the .. 3 .. bail 1965/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) help of present applicant. The, as is clear from the averments and the statements of witnesses, the allegations against the present applicant are that she had been harassing and torturing the minor girl by beating her and forcing her to do household work etc. Then, as is further clear the charge sheet against the co­accused is already submitted after completion of investigation and only work which is remained is to submit supplementary charge sheet in regard to the present applicant. It is also to be mentioned that the co­accused is the husband of the present applicant and he is in jail. In the light of that if the contentions of the applicant that she is having two years old child who is staying with her mother and there is nobody else to look after the child and for that purpose it is necessary to release her on bail, also appear to be worth consideration. Even as is clear the offences charged against the applicant are not punishable with death or imprisonment for life and therefore as rightly pointed out on behalf of applicant/accused the bar under section 437 of Cr.P.C. will not come in the way. Then, it is also to be mentioned that as per proviso to section 437 of Cr.P.C. if the accused is under the age of 16 years or is a woman or is sick or infirm, such person is entitled to be released on bail and since the applicant is a woman she is also entitled to be released on bail on that count. 4] The submissions on behalf of prosecution that charge sheet is filed only against co­accused and the investigation in regard to present applicant is still to be completed etc. or even the submissions that the accused is not permanent resident of the jurisdiction of this Court and is originally from out of State etc. is concerned, it is contended on behalf of applicant/accused that the .. 4 .. bail 1965/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) applicant/accused has a flat in her name and as rightly submitted on behalf of applicant, only because the applicant is not permanent resident of jurisdiction of this Court her prayer for bail cannot be rejected. In such circumstance the allegations against the accused will have to be decided on merits and at this stage only point to be decided is whether the applicant is entitled to be released on bail and in that respect the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence. 4] In that respect it is contended by the applicant that she is permanent resident of the address given and she will not abscond if released on bail and that she is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 5] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 6] Then, it has also to be mentioned that though charge sheet is submitted against the co­accused, it would take considerable time to submit charge sheet against the present applicant and then for conclusion of trial and looking to the workload in this court and the fact that the present matter is comparatively new one, it would not be desirable and proper to keep the applicant/accused in jail for .. 5 .. bail 1965/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) uncertain period, that is particularly in the light of the fact that the applicant/accused is stated to be a woman having two years old child and she do not appear to be main accused. 7] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ .. 6 .. bail 1965/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) Criminal bail application no. 1965/2014 Order below Exh.1. OPERATIVE ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Mrs. Farhat Sarjil Ahmed is released on P.R. bond of Rs.30,000/­ [rupees thirty thousand only] with one or two sureties in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ She shall attend the concerned police station on every Saturday between 3.00 p.m. to 5.00 p.m. till filing of the charge sheet and shall co­operate with the investigation. She shall not threaten and pressurize the victim girl and prosecution witnesses in any manner and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. She shall not leave India without permission of this court. She shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 26.11.2014. (Mrs.V.V.Virkar) District Judge­1 and Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.

State of Maharashtra ( Through Kapurbavdi Police Stn.) ...Complainant Vs. Mohammad Hadis Mohammad Islam Raien, …. Accused Age : 24 years, Occ.: R/at : In the gala of Nawab Ali (Banana godown), near first Bus stop going towards Hiranandani Fish Market, Patalipada, Thane. Native village Post Dhingavas, Tahasil Lalganj, Dist. Pratapgad, State – U.P. Offence Punishable Under Sec. 354­A (1)(i)of IPC and S.8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ Appearances : Shri. V.G.Kadu, Ld. Spl.P.P. for the State. Mr. Parvej Pathan, Ld.Advocate for the accused. ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ 2 Special Case No.197/2015 (Judgment) :JUDGMENT: (Delivered on 24th day of October, 2017) 1] The accused in the Court dock is tried for offence under S. 354­A (1)(i)of IPC and S.8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 on the accusation of having been sexually harassed and sexually assaulted a minor victim girl, aged 09 years. 2] Case of prosecution, in brief, is that a victim girl, nine years of age, went at around 2.00 pm. on 11/01/2015 to bring bananas from the banana­cart of accused near their house. The accused was selling bananas on his hand­cart. The accused asked the girl to let her friends go. Thereafter accused inserted his hand in her T­shirt and trouser. The girl screamed for help. People gathered there. The neighbour Amar Athawale took photographs on his mobile and showed to the parents of the victim girl. Father of victim girl went to police station and lodged complaint. 3] On the receipt of complaint, PSO of Kapurbavdi Police Station registered offence vide Crime No. I­18/2015 under S. 354­A(1)(i) of IPC and under S. 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Investigation was taken up by PSI­Amruta Chaure. She went to the spot and apprehended accused. She recorded statement of victim's father and victim. She also recorded statement of witnesses. PSO­ Kapurbavdi police station filed charge sheet against the accused. 4] This Court framed charge against the accused ( Exh.04 ) for offence under Sec. 354­A (1)(i) of IPC and S. 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. The contents of the charge were read over and 3 Special Case No.197/2015 (Judgment) explained to the accused in vernacular to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 5] Prosecution examined in all four witnesses to bring home the guilt of accused. Vinaykumar Gupta (P.W.1) is father of the victim girl who lodged report Exh. 9. P.W.2 is victim girl. Amar Aathawale (P.W.3) is neighbour of victim who informed to the father of victim girl and Smt. Amruta Chaure (P.W.4) is investigating officer who went to the spot and apprehended accused, recorded statement of victim's father and victim and also recorded statement of witnesses. 6] The defence of the accused, as constructed in cross­examination and statements under Sec. 313 Cr.P.C., is of false implication. 7] I have heard Ld. Special P.P. for the State and Ld. advocate for the accused. 8] Following points arise for my determination with my findings thereon for reasons to follow: POINTS FINDINGS 01. Does the prosecution prove that on …. In the affirmative. 11/01/2015 at 15 hours, on public road in front of Sanket School, Manpada, Thane [W], the accused sexually harassed victim girl by physical contact and sexual overtures? 02 Does prosecution prove that on the same, …. In the negative. day, date, time and place, the accused sexually assaulted the victim girl, a minor aged 09 years by touching the part of victim's 4 Special Case No.197/2015 (Judgment) body with sexual intent? 03 What order ? Accused is convicted as per final order. REASONS 9] AS TO POINT NOS.1 & 2 : I would like to discuss both the points together. The accused sells bananas on hand­cart at Manpada, Thane. The victim girl went to bring bananas on 11/01/2015 at around 2.00 pm. It has come in the evidence of victim girl that the accused asked her to let the other friends go. The accused caught her hand. The accused inserted his hand in the T­shirt and trouser of victim girl. The girl screamed. Amar Athawale (P.W.3) was in his shop. He saw the girl was pulled by accused. The accused put his hand inside the clothes of victim girl. People gathered there and gave understanding to the accused. Amruta Chaure (P.W.4) received the call and she rushed to the spot. She saw that the victim girl was weeping. She took the complaint – Exh. 09 of Vinaykumar Gupta (P.W.1). Vinaykumar Gupta (P.W.1) deposed that his daughter informed him that accused inserted his hand inside her T­shirt and trouser. 10] It is admitted fact that victim girl was 9 yeas old. Ld. Advocate for accused submitted that there was no sexual assault as such. The victim girl went to bring banana with his friends. It is strongly contended that those friends of victim girl are not examined. Ld. Advocate for accused has strongly contended that the said mobile which recorded misbehaviour of accused is seized but not produced before the Court. It is strongly contended that father had not seen incident. It is strongly contended that Amar Athawale (P.W.3) is 5 Special Case No.197/2015 (Judgment) interested witness. It is strongly contended that accused is beaten up by Amar Athawale (P.W.3) without any cause. Victim girl has no reason to depose against the accused. She is a small child. Why she will speak against the accused. She has stated in clear terms that the accused has moved hand over her body. It is a sexual harassment. Careful perusal of victim's evidence shows that the accused inserted hand in her T­shirt and trouser. She was nine years old girl. It is not her contention that accused touched her sensitive parts. There has to be a sexual assault by touching a sensitive part of the girl. So, prosecution has made out offence under S. 354(A)(1)(i) of IPC but offence under S. 7 of POCSO is doubtful. Hence, I answer Point No.1 in affirmative and Point No.2 in negative. Here I take pause to hear the accused on the point of sentence. 11] I have heard accused on the point of sentence. He submitted that he is a married person and have one son. He further submitted that he has to maintain his family. The accused has sense of repentance. Hence, I find that the accused shall be punished for the period undergone by him in jail. In the result, I pass following order : : ORDER : 1] The accused Mohammad Hadis Mohammad Islam Raien is hereby convicted of offence under S. 354­A (1)(i) of IPC and is sentenced to suffer Simple Imprisonment for two months and to pay fine of Rs. 500/­ in default to suffer further Simple Imprisonment for 15 days. 2] The accused was in jail from 11/01/2015 till 27/03/2015. He is entitled to get set off as per S. 428 of Cr.P.C. 6 Special Case No.197/2015 (Judgment) 3] The accused is acquitted of offence under S. 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 4] His bail bond stands cancelled. .. 1 .. Anti Bail 1966/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) Order below Exh.1 in Anticipatory Bail Appln. No. 1966 of 2014 This application is filed by the applicant Mr. Sharukh Salim Kasmani and Mr. Saif Salim Kasmani for their release on bail under section 438 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. I­ 142/2014 registered at Thane nagar police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 354A read with section 34 of I.P.C. and under section 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. It was contended and argued that the applicant apprehend arrest in this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that at the time of incident when the victim was passing by the road, the applicants alongwith co­accused Moin were sitting on the wall by the side of road and co­accused Moin blew whistle towards the victim and held her hand and uttered words with intent to outrage her modesty. It is It is further submitted that looking to the allegations levelled, custodial interrogation of the applicants is not required. It is further submitted that they are permanent residents of the address given and that if the present applicants/accused is released on bail, they will co­operate with the investigation and will not abscond and therefore the applicants are entitled to be released on anticipatory bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that the accused persons used to sit on the wall in front of house of the victim and used stare at the house of the complainant through window and also to tease the victim by blowing whistle. It is further submitted that at the time of incident the accused were sitting on the wall as .. 2 .. Anti Bail 1966/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) usual and blew whistle towards the victim and accused Moin then held her hand and asked her as to where she was going and as to where she was in past some days and thereby the accused outraged modesty of the victim. It is further submitted that custodial interrogation of the applicants/accused is necessary to enquire in those matter. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/ accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant being absconded which may hamper the investigation. It is further submitted that the applicants may threaten and pressurize the victim if released on anticipatory bail. It was therefore contended that the applicants are not entitled to be released on anticipatory bail. 3] As is clear though the offence charged against the applicants/accused is of serious nature under section 354A read with section 34 of I.P.C. and under section 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012, it is contended on behalf of the applicants that they have been falsely implicated because of previous rivalry. In that respect it is material to mention that the applicant has produced on record copy of remand report in connection with crime no.I­115/2014 under section 326, 324 of I.P.C. registered at Thanenagar police station in which one Moinuddin Sameer Kasmani lodged complaint against husband of complainant in the present case who is also one of the accused in the present case and the present applicants are stated to be the witnesses in the said matter. It is also contended that supporting documents produced on record show that accused Moinuddin sustained serious injury in the said .. 3 .. Anti Bail 1966/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) incident and offence is registered against husband of present complainant and in such circumstance the submission on behalf of applicants that because of said complaint only to pressurize the applicants, the present complaint is filed by the complainant appear to be having some substance. In any case offence charged is only under section 354A read with section 34 of I.P.C. and under section 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and custodial interrogation of the applicants do not appear to be necessary and the apprehension expressed by the prosecution that they may not be available for investigation or release of applicants on anticipatory bail would hamper the investigation can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and for that purpose there appear no necessity of the custody of the applicants. 4] Then, it is contended by the applicants that they are permanent residents of the address given and are ready to abide by any conditions imposed and in all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the interim anticipatory bail already granted to the applicant can be confirmed. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER 1) The application is allowed. 2) In the event of arrest of the applicants namely Mr. Shahrukh Salim Kasmani and Mr. Saif Salim Kasmani for offence punishable under section 354A read with section 34 of I.P.C. and under section 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 registered under C.R.No.I­142/2014 at Thanenagar .. 4 .. Anti Bail 1966/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) Police Station, they shall be released on furnishing P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] each with one surety each in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ a) The applicants shall attend the concerned police station on every Friday between 10.00 a.m. to 1.00 p.m. and shall co­operate with the investigating machinery. b) They shall not, directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer. c) They shall not leave India without the previous permission of the Court. d) They shall not tamper with prosecution evidence. .. 1 .. Bail No.2107/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1.) Order below Exhibit 1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 2107/2015 This application is filed by applicant Yasin Aasif Ali Sheikh for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no.212/2015 registered at Nerul police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 376 of I.P.C. and section 6 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant had forcible sexual intercourse with minor girl more than once though knowing that she was minor. It is further contended and argued that there was love affair between girl and accused and it is a case of consent. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co- operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply at Exhibit 4 and it is contended and argued that taking disadvantage of minor age of the girl the accused enticed her and then had sexual intercourse with her against her wish because of which she became pregnant. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl and prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. .. 2 .. Bail No.2107/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1.) 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 376 of I.P.C. and section 6 of P.O.C.S.O. Act with the allegation that the accused though knowing that the girl was minor, had sexual intercourse with her against her wish, on perusal of complaint it reveal that the girl had developed love affair with the accused and they were having physical relations with each other because of which she became pregnant. In such circumstance whether the allegations against the accused are true or not, would be the question to be decided on merits. Then, the applicant/accused is seen to be in jail since his arrest on 26.07.2015 and looking to the nature of allegations the investigation may have completed by now. Even nothing is stated to be recovered from the applicant/accused. 4] Then, it is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 5] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. .. 3 .. Bail No.2107/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1.) 6] Then, it has also to be mentioned that looking the allegations against the accused the investigation in the matter may have almost completed but the charge-sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge- sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 7] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order - ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused namely Mr. Yasin Aasif Ali Sheikh is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/- [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one local surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions - The applicant/accused shall attend the concerned police station on every Tuesday between 10.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon till filing of the charge-sheet and shall co-operate in investigation. He shall not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and the prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this Court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 16.10.2015 (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Additional Session Judge-1, Thane.

Accused was arrested and after completion of investigation charge­sheet was submitted. 6] On hearing APP, defence counsel and considering the record charge below Exh.4 for the offence punishable under section 354A of I.P.C. and under section 8 of POCSO Act was framed and when it was read over and explained to the accused in vernacular he denied the same vide his statement Exh.5. 7] Prosecution examined in all four witnesses. The accused did not examine himself nor led the evidence. From the statement under section 313 of Cr.P.C. his defence is of denial. 8] The learned APP submitted that prosecution .....4/­ 4 Spl.POCSO Case 211/2016 proved the case under section 8 of POCSO Act to believe the sexual assault and attempt to outrage modesty of minor girl. The defence counsel submitted that on the humanitarian ground accused went to install the cylinder and there was quarrel between husband of Shital and accused on account of Rs.1,000/­. He submitted that Rs.1,000/­ hand loan was given by accused and to disown the said liability he is involved. 9] In the circumstances following points arise for my determination and I record my finding to them for the reasons mentioned hereinafter :­ Sr. POINTS FINDINGS No. 1] Whether prosecution proved that In the on 10/05/2016at about 6.45 p.m. negative. in the room of watchman of Mira Co­Op Housing Society, near Kokan Bank, Mira Road, Tal. & Dist. Thane within the jurisdiction of Naya Nagar police station accused used criminal force to the daughter of complainant namely Arushi aged five years with intention to outrage her modesty ? 2] Whether it is proved that on the said date, time and place and In the during the course of same affirmative. transaction accused committed act .....5/­ 5 Spl.POCSO Case 211/2016 of sexual assault to daughter of complainant namely Arushi Shankar Singh and thus committed an offence punishable under section 8 of POCSO Act ? 3] What order ? Accused is convicted. REASONS POINTS NO. 1 & 2 : 10] For the sake of convenient discussion points are clubbed. 11] The prosecution examined P.W. Arushi who is victim, P.W. Shital, her mother, P.W. Shankar Singh, her father and Pravin Salunkhe, who was Investigating Officer. 12] At the out set it is to be mentioned that victim Arushi stated her age six years when her evidence was recorded in January, 2017. Her birth certificate Exh.13 prescribes her date of birth is 28/09/2010. She was therefore, of five years on the date of incident. The identity of accused is also not disputed and the residence of victim with parents and other family members. 13] The evidence of P.W. Arushi shows that she was at home, was attending 1st standard in Rosary English Medium school. In their building on 3rd floor Javed (accused) is residing and he came to change cylinder. Accused caught .....6/­ 6 Spl.POCSO Case 211/2016 hold her right hand and touched to her penis. He has taken her brother to provide Kababa and biscuits. He also told not to tell the incident to parents. She identified accused through video conferencing. 14] Though she admitted that her grand mother was present at the time of incident and therefore, learned defence counsel found fault with the investigation that the incident did not take place in lonely place but there is presence of her grand mother and therefore it is false. The incident alleged hardly taken few seconds and therefore, the false implication cannot be believed. 15] P.W. Shital Sing is mother of victim. According to her husband is serving as watchman in Asmita Super Market. Ayushi was studying in 1st standard in Rosary English Medimum school. On 10/05/2016 she returned from job at about 10.30 p.m. and her daughter informed that Javed has come and touched her right hand to his penis, given Kabab and Biscuits. She lodged complaint Exh.10. The question answer form statement of victim and Umesh are at Exh.11 and 12. She also identified accused. 16] Her evidence shows that she attends job from 6.00 p.m. to 9.30 p.m. and they were having one gas cylinder in their house. She denied that there was quarrel between her husband and accused on account of Rs.1,000/­ and to disown .....7/­ 7 Spl.POCSO Case 211/2016 the liability husband caused her to file false case. 17] P.W. Shankar Singh is father of victim and according to him he attends job from 8.00 a.m. to 10.00 p.m. and on his return children told him about the incident and thereafter wife lodged complaint. Though he admitted that in case of need he has to obtain loan from friends but also admitted that he was knowing Javed earlier. He was put up that he is having friendship with accused and about quarrel between him and accused for Rs.1,000/­ hand loan. He categorically denied about the quarrel, hand loan and that to disown the liability he is falsely involved. 18] The evidence discussed so far reveal that victim was residing with her parents, brothers, mother is attending job of maid servant, father is serving as watchman for whole day and he was not present in the house on the day of incident. I have discussed earlier that identify of accused is not disputed. The alleged earlier quarrel on account of hand loan of Rs.1,000/­ is not found believable nor reveal the animosity between father of victim and accused. 19] It appears that P.W. Shital is having two sons and daughter victim and is residing with niece and nephew and mother­in­law. It may be mentioned that mother may not be easily ready to expose her minor daughter in the offence pertaining to her modesty. .....8/­ 8 Spl.POCSO Case 211/2016 20] The offence prescribed in section 354A of I.P.C. requires physical contact or advance involving unwelcome sexual overtures or a demand or request for sexual favours or act by showing pronography against the will of the woman or act of making sexually coloured remarks. The evidence discussed above would not attract physical contact or advancing enforcement of unwelcom sexual overtures. The offence of sexual assault is prescribed in section 7 of the POCSO Act. It requires any person who touches the vagina, penis, anus or breast of the child or make the child touch to vagina, penis, or breast or such person, is said to have committed sexual assault. The plain reading coupled with the evidence of P.W. Arushi reveals that her evidence is not only believable but trustworthy so far as offence of sexual assault prescribed under section 7 of POCSO Act is concerned. This answers point No.1 in the negative and point No.2 in the negative. 21] It is here I have heard accused on the point of sentence. He requested that he has to maintain wife and small children. He is innocent and his son is hospitalized for serious illness and therefore leniency may be shown. The learned APP submitted that maximum punishment be imposed. The punishment prescribed under section 8 of the POCSO Act reveals that it may extent to five years and shall .....9/­ 9 Spl.POCSO Case 211/2016 not be less than three years. There appears to discretion left to the Court even if special reasons are to be recorded. 22] In the circumstances, as the offence under section 354A is not found proved, the accused is in Jail from 24/06/2016 till today. Considering his request I am of the opinion that following sentence would be just and proper. ORDER 1] Accused Javed Alam Khalikujjama Khan is convicted for the offence punishable under section 8 of POCSO as per sec. 235(2) of Cr.P.C. and sentence to suffer S.I. for three years. 2] Set off be given to him under section 428 of Cr.P.C. from 24/06/2016 till today as he is in jail. 3] He is acquitted for the offence punishable under section 354A of I.P.C. as per section 235(1) of Cr.P.C. 4] Inform Jail Authority accordingly.
