1 Special Case No.193/2014 (Judgment) Presented on : 26/09/2014 Registered on : 26/09/2014 Decided on : 16/03/2016 Duration 1­year,05­Months,19­days. IN THE COURT OF THE SPECIAL JUDGE (P.O.C.S.O.ACT), THANE (Presided over by Ms.U.M.Nandeshwar, Additional Sessions Judge­1, Thane) SPECIAL CASE No. 193 of 2014 Exhibit No.31. The State of Maharashtra Through C.B.D. Police Station,Navi Mumbai Thane, District – Thane. ... Prosecution versus Daulat Shalik Katkari Age 25 years. Resident of Katkari Wadi, Agroli village Sector­29, CBD, Belapur, Navi Mumbai. …Accused. Offence punishable under section 354, 354­B, 452, 323 of Indian Penal Code and under section 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Appearance ­ Spl.P.P. Mrs. R.A. Navale, for the State. Advocate Mr.K. Rajan, for the Accused. 2 Special Case No.193/2014 (Judgment) JUDGMENT (Delivered on 16th March, 2016.) 1] The Accused stands prosecuted for the offence punishable under section 354, 354­B, 452 and 323 of Indian Penal Code and also under section 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act) for confining and committing sexual assault on minor victim­girl aged about 5 years and for outraging her modesty. 2] The indictment against the Accused are as under ­ [i] Informant Sangita Katkari (Pw.1) is resident of Agroli village, Navi Mumbai. She is staying there with her husband and two daughters including victim­girl aged about 5 years. Her husband is peon in Dnyanpushpa Highschool in C.B.D. Sector No.4. [ii] On 06/07/2014 as there was yearly religious ceremony (shraddha) of deceased grand mother­in­law of the informant, therefore, her husband had been to grave­yard for performing some religious rituals. The elder daughter of informant was playing outside and the younger daughter (victim­girl) was sleeping in the hall. Around 05.30 p.m. Informant went to bathroom for changing cloths, and when she came out she had seen that her neighbour Daulat Katkari 3 Special Case No.193/2014 (Judgment) (Accused) was sitting beside her daughter and moving his hand on her chest, and her daughter was screaming. Therefore, she raised voice and asked him what he is doing and caught hold him. On that accused gave a jerk to her hand and ran away from there. Informant's sister­in­law also tried to caught hold the accused, but he ran away. Therefore, informant lodged report against the accused. 3] On her report F.I.R. was registered against the Accused vide C.R.No.I­79/2014 for the offence punishable under section 354, 354­B, 452, 323 of Indian Penal Code and also under section 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). The investigation was carried out by A.P.I. Rajesh Sheshrao Kadu (P.W.3). The Accused was arrested in presence of panchas. P.W.3 visited the spot and drawn spot panchnama in presence of panchas. Medical certificate was collected. Bonafide and birth certificate of victim­girl were collected. Statements of witnesses were recorded as per their say. Thereafter, investigation culminated into filing of charge­sheet in this Court being the Special designated court under P.O.C.S.O. Act. 4] My learned predecessor the erstwhile Special Judge Smt. V.V.Virkar framed the charge (Exh.4) against the Accused for offence punishable under section 354, 354­B, 452 & 323 of Indian Penal Code and also under section 8 of 4 Special Case No.193/2014 (Judgment) Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). The Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial (Exh.5). The Accused took defence of total denial. 5] In response to application under section 294 of Cr.P.C. the defence has admitted spot panchnama [Exh.22], medical certificate of victim­girl [Exh.23], bonafide certificate and birth certificate of victim­girl [Exh.24]. 6] In order to prove guilt of Accused Prosecution has examined following witnesses ­ P.W.1 Sangita Abhimanyu Katkari Exh.18 Informant (mother of victim­girl) P.W.2 Victim­girl Exh.21. P.W.2 PSI Rajesh Sheshrao Kadu Exh.25 (Investigating officer.) 7] The prosecution proved and relied on the report and printed F.I.R. (Exh.19 & 20) and arrest form of accused (Exh.27). 8] The prosecution closed its side of evidence by filing Pursis at Exhibit­28. The incriminating evidence came on record against the Accused was read over and explained to him and his statement under Section 313(b) of Cr.P.C. was 5 Special Case No.193/2014 (Judgment) recorded. Accused neither examined himself nor examined any witness in his defence. 9] Heard learned Spl.P.P. Mrs. R. A. Navale for State and the learned advocate Mr. K. Rajan for Accused. 10] On consideration of argument advanced on behalf of both the sides and on perusal of the oral & documentary evidence on record, following points arise for my determination, which are answered with the findings thereon, as under :­ Sr. Points Findings No. 1 ) Does the prosecution prove that on 06/07/2014 around 05.30 p.m. accused committed house trespass by entering into the house of informant Sau.Sangita ..No. Abhimanyu Katkari Aagroligaon, C.B.D. Belapur, Navi Mumbai used as a human dwelling with preparation to outraged modesty of her minor daughter victim­girl and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 452 of Indian Penal Code? 2) Whether prosecution prove that on the same date, time and place accused used criminal force against victim­girl aged 05 years, by moving his hand over her breast with intent or knowing to be likely that he ...No. 6 Special Case No.193/2014 (Judgment) would thereby outrage her modesty and he thereby committed an offence punishable under section 354 of Indian Penal Code ? 3) Whether prosecution prove that on the same date, time and place while Sangita Katkari came to catch the accused voluntarily caused hurt to informant by …No. hand and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 323 of Indian Penal Code? 4 ) Does the prosecution prove that on the same date, time and place, accused committed sexual assault on victim­girl as ..No. defined in section 7 and he thereby committed an offence punishable under section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, 2012 ? 5) What order ? Accused is acquitted. REASONS As to Point No.1 to 4 : 11] All the points are taken up together for discussion, to avoid the repetition, as evidence about the same in common and inter­connected. 12] As the Accused is facing charge under section 354 of I.P.C. it is incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove 7 Special Case No.193/2014 (Judgment) that Accused either assaults or used criminal force towards victim­girl to outrage her modesty or knowing it to be likely that he will, by his act, outrage the modesty of the victim­girl. Further, to prove offence u/sec 452 of I.P.C. prosecution has to prove that the Accused entered in dwelling house of informant having made preparation for ouraging modesty of victim­girl and caused hurt to informant and minor victim­girl. So also as the Accused is facing charge under section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, therefore, it is further incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that the Accused with sexual intent touched the vagina, penis, anus, breast of a child or make the child touched vagina, penis, anus, breast of such person or any other person or does any other act with sexual intent which involves physical contact without penetration and by his such act committed sexual assault as defined in section 7 of the P.O.C.SO. Act. Age of victim­girl is 5 Years : 13] First of all as the Accused is facing charge under P.O.C.S.O. Act, therefore, it is incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that the victim­girl was child (minor) at the time of incident. The alleged incident took place on 06/07/2014. Informant (P.W.1) deposed that the victim­girl who is her daughter is aged about 6 years. Further, the accused has admitted the birth certificate and bonafide certificate of the victim­girl which is at Exh.24. According to 8 Special Case No.193/2014 (Judgment) which the date of birth of victim­girl is 29/06/2009, which means at the time of incident the victim­girl was aged about 05 years. Thus, I have no hesitation to hold that the prosecution proved that at the time of incident, the victim­girl was minor aged about 05 years i.e. below the age of 18 years and she is a “child” as per definition given in Section 2(d) of P.O.C.S.O. Act. 14] To prove the charge against the Accused the prosecution has examined the informant /mother of victim­girl Sangita Katkari (P.W.1). She deposed that incident took place before one and half year i.e. prior to 7­8 days of Rakshabandhan festival in the year­2014. On that day, her husband had been to grave­yard for performing religious rituals (shraddha) of her deceased grand mother­in­law. At that time, her younger daughter victim­girl (P.W.2) was at home with her and elder daughter had been out of home for playing. Victim­girl was sleeping in the hall. She went in bathroom to change the cloths. She heard cries of her daughter victim­girl. Therefore, she came outside and seen that accused was sitting near her daughter and his hands were on the neck and breast of her daughter. Therefore, she raised shouts and tried to caught him, however, he ran away from there. Her neighbourers and sister­in­law came there. She further deposed that incident took place around 05.30 pm. and therefore, she lodged report against accused. 9 Special Case No.193/2014 (Judgment) 15] The prosecution has also examined the victim­girl as P.W.2, who is now aged about 6 years and at the time of incident, she was aged about 5 years. Victim­girl (P.W.2) deposed that she knows accused who is staying in her neighbourhood. At the time of incident she was in first standard. She further deposed that Daulat (Accused) moved his hand on her body, specifying neck and chest and she raised shout, therefore, her mother came from bathroom and Daulat ran away. 16] Though the identification of the accused is not challanged, however, as the victim­girl is tendered age girl of 6 years, therefore, precaution is required to take while scrutinizing her evidence, as there are chances of tutoring the minor girl. From the tenor of evidence of the informant (P.W.1) and victim­girl (P.W.2), it appears that the incident took place within a very short time or can say within 1­2 minutes as Informant deposed that she had been in bathroom to change clothes and by hearing scream of her daughter came out and seen accused sitting beside her daughter. Although, the victim­girl stated that on the day of incident, Daulat (Accused) moved his hand on her body i.e. neck and chest, however, she did not state that at that time, she was sleeping. While as per prosecution case, the victim­girl was sleeping and informant was in the bathroom when the alleged incident took 10 Special Case No.193/2014 (Judgment) place. If the victim­girl was sleeping then also it is doubtful as to how she noticed the Accused. Further there are omissions, in respect of raising shout by victim­girl and approaching her mother from the bathroom. 17] The evidence of informant (P.W.1) is also suffered with improvement in respect of raising shout by her daughter, by hearing which she came out from the bathroom. There is no independent evidence on record to support the version of informant and victim­girl. Further, though informant (P.W.1) deposed that she had seen the accused, and his hand were on the breast and neck of her daughter, however it does not prove the intent of accused that he touched so to the victim­girl with any sexual intent. Particularly when informant admits that accused is her distinct relative and used to come to her house. Thus, the possibility can not be ruled out that accused by hearing cries of victim­girl had patted her to calm down her or to make her sleep. 18] Further there is absolutely no evidence that how and from where accused entered in the house of informant. Neither informant nor victim­girl deposed anything about as to how the Accused entered in their house. In fact, the evidence of the informant (P.W.1) is not sufficient to prove that accused entered in her house with an intent to commit any crime, and with sexual intent touched breast of her daughter. 11 Special Case No.193/2014 (Judgment) 19] As per the case of prosecution, the neighborers including the sister­in­law of the informant by name Hira came there by hearing her shouts and even Hira tried to catch hold the accused, however, the prosecution failed to examine Hira or any other neighborer. There is absolutely no evidence that accused caused any harm either to the victim­girl or to the informant. Neither the evidence of informant and victim­girl is of such quality to believe or inspire confidence about the allegations made against the accused, in respect of sexual assault or outraging the modesty of the victim­girl with the sexual intent. 20] The evidence of investigating officer A.P.I. Rajesh Kadu (P.W3) is formal in nature, who recorded the report of informant and drawn spot panchnama and referred the victim­ girl for medical examination. The spot panchnama Exh.22 is not disputed by the defence. Neither the arrest of accused is disputed. There are no injuries found on the person of victim­ girl. Further it is relevant to note that although informant and victim­girl knew the Accused by name his name is not stated in the history given to medical officer who examined the victim­ girl on the same day of incident. 21] Thus, the cumulative effect of the evidence brought on record by the prosecution is not sufficient to prove that accused with intent to commit an offence entered in the house 12 Special Case No.193/2014 (Judgment) of informant and committed sexual assault and outraged modesty of victim­girl aged about 5 years or caused any hurt to her. Thus, there is absolutely no believable evidence and cogent proof on the record to support the prosecution version. Thus, prosecution failed to prove beyond reasonable doubt that accused with sexual intent inappropriately touched breast of minor victim­girl by using criminal force and outraged her modesty or committed sexual assault on her by wrongfully entering in the house of victim­girl or caused any hurt to the informant or victim­girl. Therefore, the twin presumption given in section 29 and 30 of P.O.C.S.O. Act about offence u/sec. 3, 5, 7 & 9 of the P.O.C.S.O. Act and about culpable mental state of Accused would not arise. Hence, I answer point No.1 to 3 in negative. Therefore, the Accused is entitled for acquittal. 22] In the result, I proceed to pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused Daulat Shalik Katkari is hereby acquitted U/Sec. 235(1) of Cr.P.C. for the offence punishable U/Sec.452, 354­A & 323 of The Indian Penal Code and U/Sec.8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] The Accused is in jail. He shall be released forthwith if not required in any other case. 13 Special Case No.193/2014 (Judgment) 3] The Accused is directed to furnish bail bond of the amount of ₹15,000/­ with one solvent surety in the like amount in compliance of provision of section 437­A of Cr.P.C. The judgment is dictated and pronounced in open Court. Date :16/03/2016. (Ms. U. M. Nandeshwar), Thane Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act),Thane. District Judge ­1 and Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

It is further submitted that he is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co­operate with the investigation and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on anticipatory bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that at the time of incident in question the applicant collected information that the victim is alone in the house and the the main accused Riyaz Gafur Pathan entered entered her house and had embraced the victim girl with sexual intent and when she resisted and raised shouts, the accused persons threatened her not to shout and also threatened to kill her mother and brother. It is further submitted that in such circumstance in order to do thorough investigation in this crime, the custodial interrogation of the applicant/accused is necessary. It .. 2 .. Anti Bail 1977/14 (Ord.Exh.1) is further submitted that if the applicant is released on anticipatory bail, there is possibility of he threatening the victim and prosecution witnesses and also being absconded which may hamper the investigation. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on anticipatory bail. 3] As is clear though the offence charged against the applicant are serious under section 354A(1)(F), 452, 506, 34 of I.P.C. and section 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012, the offence alleged against the applicant is under Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and the main allegation of molestation and sexual assault on the victim is against the main accused Riyaz Pathan and the present applicant is stated to have given threats etc. to the applicant and it is contended on behalf of the applicant/accused that at the time of incident he was at Nashik. In such circumstance the allegation against the applicant will have to be decided on merits after trial and his custodial interrogation do not appear to be necessary. 4] Then, the apprehension expressed by the prosecution that the applicant may not be available for investigation or release of applicant on anticipatory bail would hamper the investigation, can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions including condition to give attendance to police station and for that purpose there appear no necessity of the custody of the applicant. 5] Then, it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and is ready to abide by .. 3 .. But then, it is contended on behalf of the applicant/accused that he is falsely implicated in the crime and the girl had come with him of her wish and he did not induce her. In such circumstance whether the allegations against the accused are true or not, would be the question to be decided on merits. Even nothing is to be recovered from the applicant/accused. 4] It is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application to be decided is whether the applicant is entitled to be released on bail and in that respect the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence. 5] In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 6] Then, though the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. .. 3 .. bail 1999/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) 7] Then, it has also to be mentioned that the investigation in the matter though almost completed the charge sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and therefore there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 8] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. Act). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that applicant/accused by giving phone call to victim girl, he called her and asked to come down her residential house and after she came down he induced her to show a gainful thing to her and then he along with his friend i.e. absconding accused took her to Upvan in rickshaw and there applicant/accused kissed her and moved hand on her breast by removing her top (Kurta) and also dragged her towards himself and hugged her. It is contended and argued that the applicant is falsely implicated only because the victim girl was found talking with him on mobile and that the incident as alleged had never taken place. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will not abscond and make him available to face the trial and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. .. 2 .. bail no.2130/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that at the relevant time applicant/accused gave call on mobile of victim girl Payal Dayaram Garg aged 14 years and asked her to come down of her residential house by inducing her to show her a gainful thing and after she came down, applicant/accused and his friend i.e. absconding accused took her to Upvan area by rickshaw and there applicant/accused kissed her, removed his top (kurta) and moved her hand on her breast and also hugged her and thereby committed sexual assault and sexual harassment upon said victim girl. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl and the prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 354, 354A, 354B and 354D of I.P.C. and section 7, 8, 11 and 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act with the allegation of taking the girl to Upvan removed her top and moved hand on her breast and hugged her, it is contended on behalf of applicant that he is falsely implicated in the crime and that there was love affair between the girl and the applicant/accused. In such circumstance whether the allegations against the accused are true or not, .. 3 .. bail no.2130/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) would be the question to be decided on merits. 4] Then, the applicant/accused is seen to be in jail since 22.08.2015 and looking to the nature of allegations the investigation may have completed by now. Even nothing is stated to be recovered from the applicant/accused. 5] Then, it is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 6] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 7] Then, it has also to be mentioned that looking the allegations against the accused the investigation in the matter may have almost completed but the charge­sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation .. 4 .. bail no.2130/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) and submit the charge­sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 8] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is allowed. Order below Exhibit 1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 2140/2015 This application is filed by applicant Nitin Deepak Satpal for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no.II­34/2015 registered at Vashi Police Station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 7, 8, 9(i) of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). It is contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the accused committed sexual assault on minor victim boy. It is further contended and argued that the applicant is falsely implicated. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co­operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it is contended and argued that at the time of incident the victim boy had to the house of the applicant/accused to sleep and at that time the accused held the private part of the victim boy and moved it backward and forward and caused injury to his private part and committed sexual assault on him. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim boy and the prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was .. 2 .. Bail No. 2140/2015 Order below Exhibit 1. therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, the offences charged against the applicant/accused are of serious nature under section 7, 8, 9(i) of P.O.C.S.O. Act in regard to and connection with victim boy aged about 5 years with the allegation that he had sexually assaulted the boy and also caused injury to the private part of the boy, it is material to mention that the prosecution case of sexual assault on the boy is even apparently corroborated by medical evidence and in such circumstances as has been rightly argued on behalf of prosecution, the investigation in the matter is still in progress and thorough investigation into the matter is required to be done in the light of peculiar nature of allegations made against the accused in the crime. Then, though it is argued on behalf of accused that there had been previous rivalry, on one hand it is to be mentioned that no such averments are there in the application and on the other hand, absolutely no material appear to have been brought on record to substantiate such allegation. The applicant is F.I.R. named accused and very clear description of the act alleged to have been done by the accused is given in the complaint by the complainant. In such circumstance the allegations against the accused will have to be proved on merits after trial. 4] Then, though it is well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether .. 3 .. Bail No. 2140/2015 Order below Exhibit 1. there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail, besides that the gravity and serious nature of offence and the manner in which it is stated to have been committed has to be looked into and looking to the nature of offence and the manner in which it is alleged to have been committed, a wrong message would be sent to the society in case of release of accused on bail in such type of matter wherein serious allegations of sexual assault on a minor boy are made. 5] Then, the apprehension expressed by the prosecution that the accused may threaten and pressurize the victim boy and his family members is well founded and even possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded and not available for trial cannot be ruled out. 6] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is not a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail at this stage. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is rejected. Date : 15.10.2015 (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Additional Session Judge­1, Thane.

She used to go to school at 7.00 a.m. and used to return back to the house at about 2.00 p.m. In the year 2012, she was studying in 8th standard. Her friend Pratik Thorat had introduced with accused Sunil Kori. Since then, accused was in contact with victim. After some days, Pratik Thorat disclosed with victim that accused had approved her only and he had love with her. When victim was studying in 9th standard, accused had gifted wrist­watch of Fasttrack company. However, her parents had returned the same with the parents of accused. On 5th May, 2013, accused tried to talk with the victim forcibly. Victim had neglected the accused. However, she was threatened by the accused. By these allegations, informant had lodged her report (Exh.14). It is registered vide C.R. no. 198/14 u/s. 354(D), 504 of I.P.C. and u/s. 11(iv) of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. P.W.4 had carried out investigation. He rushed to the spot and recorded spot panchanama and statements of witnesses. He had collected call details of mobile of father of victim and copy of birth certificate of victim. After investigation, he submitted charge­sheet. 3] My learned Predecessor framed the charge against the accused for the offences punishable under section 354(D) of I.P.C. and u/s. 11(iv) of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, on 08/03/2016. Details of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular, to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. His defence is of total denial. 4] During trial, defence has admitted no documents. 3 POCSO Case. No. 195/2014. 5] To bring home the guilt of the accused for the charges leveled against him, the prosecution has examined as many as four witnesses i.e. P.W. Name of witness Exh. Description No. No. 1] Shweta Sudhakar Margaj 18 Mother of victim. 2] Sudhakar Balkrishna 19 Father of victim. Margaj 3] Victim 23 Victim 4] Girish Krishna Bhalachin 26 Investigating officer. 6] Accused did not enter into witness box. He has not examined defence witness. 7] Heard learned P.P. Smt. Phad for the State and learned counsel Shri. S.N. Dhikale for the accused. 8] Following points arise for my determination, which are being answered for the reasons given herein­below. POINTS FINDINGS 1] Whether prosecution proved that since No. from 2012 till 15.06.14, accused used to contact victim aged about 15 years, on phone, despite a clear indication of disinterest in him and thereby, committed offence u/s. 354(D) of I.P.C. and u/s. 11(iv) of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act ? 2] What order ? As per final order. 4 POCSO Case. No. 195/2014. REASONS POINT NO. 1 9] It is not in dispute that victim was born on 01.04.99 and she was studying in Dalmiya high­school. Pratik Thorat was friend of victim who had introduced the accused with the victim. Accused and victim used to talk interse. He had also gifted watch of Fasttrack company to victim. However, her parents had returned the same with parents of accused with an understanding that he should not talk with her. 10] P.W.3 victim is material witness to the alleged incident dated 15.006.14. For the previous relations between the accused and victim, P.W.1 to 3 had specifically deposed about the same in their respective evidence. The same has also not been challenged by the accused. On the contrary, accused had admitted the same in his statement u/s. 313 of Cr.P.C. 11] P.W.3 victim had deposed in her evidence that lastly on 5 th May, 2013, accused met her in the way and threatened her as “rw cksyyh ukgh rj eh dk; djsu gs rqyk ekfgr vkgs- ” Thereafter, he started chasing her at her school and her tuition classes. She was threatened by accused that her father has the same way and he would see her father. 12] It has come in the cross­examination of victim that five minutes are required to reach the house of accused from her house. Pratik Thorat is residing in her building. They both were close friends interse. She was told by Pratik Thorat that he has a friend and he has desire to become her friend. At that time, she had not seen accused. Prior to about 1­2 months of Valentine day, she was acquainted with accused. During that period, they might had visited 1­2 times. Accused was working at Dahisar Check Naka. In the year 2015, mother of accused was admitted in the 5 POCSO Case. No. 195/2014. hospital. She visited her mother in the hospital. Thakur Vidyamandir is situated at Kandivali. In the year 2015­2016, she was studying in 12 th std. They were also in contact with each other on mobile. 1 St April is her birth date. 13] It has further come in her cross­examination that her parents had strongly objected their relationship. Though her mother persuade her twice, she was talking with accused. Victim volunteered that she was threatened by him. Her parents had never visited the parents of accused and alleged about his act. Her parents had not given understanding to the accused by calling him to their house or by meeting him on the way. Accused never had been to their house. There was no talk between her and accused, he has not tried to talk with her. 14] From the evidence on record, it can be gathered that there was love affair between accused and victim. On account of love affair, accused had gifted wrist­watch of standard company like Fasttrack and the same might be costly wrist­watch. The said watch was accepted by victim from the accused as a gift on the day of Valentine. However, victim had falsely stated with her parents that on account of her birth­day. But, the same was returned by the parents of victim to the parents of accused and they had tried to discontinue the relations between accused and victim. As the parents of victim were not liking the relations between accused and victim, they might had lodged the report through their daughter in order to pressurize the accused to discontinue his relations with victim. 15] Having considered the evidence on record, it cannot be said that the accused with an intention, used to try to make contact with victim on phone or on the way of her school or tuition classes. Therefore, it is very difficult to hold that the accused had proved the offence as charged 6 POCSO Case. No. 195/2014. though victim was minor below 18 years of age. I therefore, answer to the point in the negative. In the result, I proceed to pass the following order. ORDER 1] Accused Sunil Dulhare Kori, is hereby, acquitted under sec. 235(1) of the Criminal Procedure Code, of the offences punishable u/s. 354(D) of I.P.C. and u/s. 11(iv) of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 2] Accused Sunil Dulhare Kori is in jail. Hence, jail authority is hereby, directed to release him forthwith, if he is not required in any other case or crime. 3] Accused Sunil Dulhare Kori be enlarged on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ with surety of like amount. The effect of this bail order will remain in force for the period of six months from today, as per section 437­(A) of Cr.P.C. Thane, (A.S. Bhaisare) Date­ 24.05.2018. Applicant Age 25 years, Occupation – service, Resident of room no.105, D wing, Matoshri Apartment, Savarkarnagar Thane (W). versus The State of Maharashtra .. Opponent Application for relaxation of condition. JUDGMENT (Delivered on 03.10.2015.) .. 2 .. Criminal Misc. Appln. No.316/2015 Judgment Applicant Yogesh Prakash Pandit has filed this application with a prayer for relaxation of condition of attendance to be given by the applicant to the concerned police station on every Wednesday between 10.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon, which was imposed upon him while granting bail to him vide order dated 30.04.2015 passed in Criminal Bail Application No. 825/2015. It is contended on behalf of the applicant that he has been continuously attending the police station without fail as directed by the court. It is further contended that now the applicant has joined new job and it has become for him impossible to attend the concerned police station every week on Wednesday because he has to attend his new duty regularly without any leave. It is further contended that the investigation in the matter is practically completed he is ready to attend the concerned police station as and when called and to co­operate in investigation and therefore it is prayed that the condition of regular attendance to police station may be relaxed. 2) The prosecution has filed its say at Exhibit 7 and objected for relaxation of condition to give regular attendance and it is contended that the investigation is in progress and therefore if the relaxation in question is granted the accused may not co­ operate in investigation which may hamper the investigation. It is contended that therefore the application may be rejected. .. 3 .. Criminal Misc. Appln. No.316/2015 Judgment 3) It appears from the documents filed on record on behalf of applicant that the applicant has been attending the police station regularly as directed. Besides, the police also have not filed any report contending that the applicant has not complied with the said direction of giving attendance to the concerned police station. Then, looking to the nature of allegations the investigation may have almost completed by now. In all above circumstance I am of the view that the condition to give regular attendance to concerned police station by applicant can be relaxed and he can be directed to attend the concerned police station as and when called for the purpose of interrogation/ inquiry in this crime. JUDGMENT (Delivered on 13th October 2017.) 1] The accused persons stand prosecuted by police station officer, Nizampur Police Station for the charge of offences of kidnapping punishable u/s 363 of IPC, for procuration of victim punishable u/sec. 366A, for outraging modesty of victim punishable u/s 354 r/w 34 I.P. C., for committing sexual assault on victim u/s 7 punishable u/sec. 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act (for short POCSO Act). ..2/- ..2.. Spl.C. No.77/2013 (Exh.No. 30) 2] In brief, it is the case of prosecution that informant Rohin lodged the complaint on 24.4.2013 alleging that victim is her daughter and her date of birth is 7.3.2001. On 23.4.2013 as usual she left her house at 5.30 a.m. for her job. That time in the house her parents, brother and son were present. On that day at about 7.30 p.m. to 8.00 p.m. her brother made phone call to her that victim did not return to home, he searched for her and to come home immediately.She returned to home at about 10.30 p.m. Thereafter she made enquiry with friends of victim but she did not found. At about 11.00 p.m. victim made phone call infront of one saloon on mobile of her brother and asked him to come to take her. They went there and brought victim to house. Victim that time told that at about 3.30 p.m. to 4.00 p.m. she alongwith two friends Akshay and Raghav went to Regent Hotel at Bhiwandi for breakfast. As mobile of Akshay was remained in house, he left hotel and after some time he came back. Thereafter they both went by saying that they are going to take pan but did not return. Then she started to go to house. On the way two boys met her to whom she asked about time. She took mobile of accused No.1 and tried to make call but it was in vein. Thereafter she started to walk but forcibly both the accused made to sit her on their motorcycle. They took her to field and tried to outrage her modesty. She resisted and shouted. Hence on frightening, they both left her there and started to go but she requested them to leave her to house. They left her infront of Sangam Hair Art at Vanzarpatti Chowk. 3] On the basis of complaint, Crime No.77/2013 for the offence punishable u/s 363,354 r/w 34 of IPC r/w u/s 7 & 8 of POCSO Act was registered and investigation was carried out by PSI Barge. Victim girl was sent for medical examination. On 26.4.2013 accused ..3/- ..3.. Spl.C. No.77/2013 (Exh.No. 30) persons were arrested. On 29.4.2013 panchanama of spot was prepared. He seized vehicle from the brother of accused under panchanama. He collected bonafide certificate of victim. He recorded statements of witnesses. After completion of investigation he submitted chargesheet against the accused persons before the Special Judge (POCSO Act), Thane. 4] Charge Exh.2 was framed and explained to accused person to which they pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. Their defence is that of total denial. 5] Considering the case of the prosecution following points arise for my determination and I have recorded my findings thereon for the reasons discussed below. POINTS FINDINGS 1 Does the prosecution prove that on 23.4.2013 in between 20.30 hours to 23.00 hours at Regent Hotel, Wada Road, next to Shelargaon, near road in the farm accused persons in furtherance of their common intention kidnapped victim girl from the lawful guardianship of her parents and .. No. thereby committed an offence punishable u/sec. 363 r/w 34 of IPC? 2 Does the prosecution further prove that No. on the above mentioned date,time and place accused persons in furtherance of their common intention that victim may force to illicit intercourse with another person and thereby committed an offence punishable u/sec. 366A r/w 34 of I.P.C.? 3 Does the prosecution further prove that on the above mentioned date,time and place accused persons in furtherance of their ..4/- ..4.. Spl.C. No.77/2013 (Exh.No. 30) common intention to outrage modesty of victim and thereby committed an offence No. punishable u/sec. 354 r/w 34 of I.P.C.? 4 Does the prosecution further prove that on the above mentioned date,time and place accused persons in furtherance of their common intention committed sexual assault on victim and thereby committed an offence No. u/s 7 punishable u/sec. 8 of POCSO Act? 5 What order ? As per final order. REASONS Points Nos. 1 to 4 : 6] These points are interlinked to each other, hence in order to avoid the repetition of evidence they are clubbed together. 7] Prosecution examined in all 4 witnesses. P.W.1 Sunil panch at Exh.9, PW 2 informant Rohini at Exh.12, PW 3 victim at Exh.16 & PW 4 Barge, I.O. at Exh.18. Then prosecution filed evidence closing pursis at Exh.27. Statement of accused persons recorded u/s 313 of Cr.P. C. are at Exhs.28 & 29. Prosecution relied on documents viz. Seizure panchanama Exh.10, leaving certificate Exh.13, Complaint Exh.14, printed FIR Exh.15, spot panchanama Exh.19, muddemal receipt Exh.20, bonafide certificate Exh.21, letter Exh.22, vehicle registration Exh.23, vehicle insurance Exh.24, tax receipt Exh.25 and arrest panchanama Exh.26. 8] The Ld. APP submitted that victim was 12 years old at the time of incident and the accused persons kidnapped her with intent to do bad act with her. The accused persons outraged her modesty and during investigation, police arrested the accused persons and I.O. went to the spot which was shown by accused and as such, there is nexus ..5/- ..5.. Spl.C. No.77/2013 (Exh.No. 30) between accused and crime. Thus, the accused persons committed offence of sexual assault with victim and as such, prosecution proved the case beyond the reasonable doubt. The argument of Ld.defence counsel is heard. 9] PW 2 Rohini deposed at Exh.12 that date of birth of victim is 7.3.2001. On 23.4.2013 as usual she left house at 5.30 a.m. for job. That time in the house her parents,brother and son were present. On that day at about 7.30 p.m. to 8.00 p.m. her brother made phone call to her and stated that victim did not return to home, he searched for her and to come home immediately. She returned to home at about 10.30 p.m. Thereafter she alongwith her brother went to Nizampur Police Station & lodged complaint. It is to be noted that said complaint may be about missing of victim and not about the charge levelled against the persons. At about 11.00 p.m. victim made phone call infront of one saloon on mobile of her brother and asked him to come to take her. That time her brother went to saloon at Shelar and brought her to police station. However, on perusal of report Exh.14, it reveals that informant mentioned in it that her brother brought victim to house and then they all went to police station. Thus, there is a contradiction. 10] Further evidence of informant is nothing but hearsay and as such, it is just and proper to advent on the testimony of victim, who deposed that on 23.4.2013 she went out of house for taking biscuits. That time her friends Akshay and Raghav met her and they asked to come with them for moving and therefore, she went with them in Regent garden. They took breakfast there. That time mobile of Akshay was remained in the house and therefore he went to his house. Then ..6/- ..6.. Spl.C. No.77/2013 (Exh.No. 30) Akshay came there alongwith his friend and thereafter they went to take pan but they did not return. 11] Victim further deposed that two boys were standing there alongwith bike. She asked them about time and they told that it was 8.30 p.m. It means she was not acquainted with their name and that is the place near about Regent garden. However, in the complaint the names of the accused persons are mentioned, which also creates a doubt about evidence of victim. She furher deposed that those two boys came to her and told her that they will reach her at her home and as such she sat on their motorcycle but they took her to another place. This evidence is not attracted the charge of kidnapping as she willfully asked them about the time and also ready to sit on their motorcycle. It is to be noted that this alleged incident took place in front of Regent Hotel which is a crowdy area and apart from that as per the evidence of I.O. Barge, there is a big circle abutting to Regent Garden and there used to be a traffic police. Towards right side of Regent Garden at some distance there is office of ACP and then offices of Tahsil, SDO and Bhiwandi Court. Ahead of these offices,there is Vanzarpattinaka Police Chowky, which goes to show that if the accused persons kidnapped her with intent to do bad act with her then she was every opportunity to ask for help by shouting but she did nothing and as such, charge of offence of kidnapping and procuration of victim punishable u/s 363 and 366A r/w 34 of IPC is not proved by the prosecution. 12] She further deposed that they tried to remove her clothes. They also tried to keep physical relations with her. She opposed them. They left her there and started to go from there. Therefore, she told ..7/- ..7.. Spl.C. No.77/2013 (Exh.No. 30) them that if they left her there, then she will tell all to her parents and thereafter, they left her near the saloon at Vanjarpatti Naka. This piece of evidence clearly goes to show that no act of outrage of modesty or force to keep physical relation with her done by the accused persons and apart from that, she put rider on them that if they left her to her house, then she will not narrate anything to her parents. This piece of evidence goes to show that threat was given by victim herself to the accused persons. It is to be noted that for proving any offence, the spot of incident is material. In the evidence of victim, no fixed spot was disclosed. On the other hand, prosecution failed to prove the spot panchanama Exh.19 by examining independent panch. It is to be noted that on the point of seizure of motorcycle, prosecution examined PW 1 Sunil who is reluctant to the case of prosecution and he was declared hostile but nothing brought on record from the mouth of this witness to boost the case of prosecution. The spot panchanama though exhibited, but prosecution failed to prove the same by examining the independent witness. The feeble attempt made by the Ld. APP to convince the Court that the accused persons shown the spot to I.O. as per panchanama Exh.19. Therefore, it is not necessary to prove the same. As a matter of fact, the spot of incident is allegedly known to victim, then it was expected from I.O. to prepare panchanama of spot shown by victim. Thus, the investigation on this point is faulty and apart from that, the evidence of victim is insufficient to locate the spot of incident. Therefore, the accused persons are entitled for the benefit of doubt on this crucial point. ..8/- ..8.. Spl.C. No.77/2013 (Exh.No. 30) 13] The evidence of victim is not sufficient to show that which accused made attempt to outrage her modesty and committed sexual assault. The evidence of victim is not established the charge of offence punishable u/s 354 IPC and u/s 7 of POCSO Act and as such, the accused persons are entitled for benefit of doubt. With this discussion, I answer the point Nos. 1 to 4 accordingly and to proceed to pass the following order. : ORDER : 1] The accused persons Mangaldas @ Mayuresh Chintamani Patil, & Sachin Bhagwan Patil are hereby acquitted u/s 235 of Cr.P.C. from the charge of offence punishable u/s 363, 366A and 354 of I.P.C & u/s 7 of POCSO Act. 2] Bail bonds of the accused persons stand cancelled. 3] The accused person shall comply forthwith the provision U/Sec.437­A Cr.P.C. by furnishing fresh P.R. Bond of Rs.10,000/­each and S.B. of like amount. 4) Seized muddemal i.e. motorcycle is already returned. Dictated and declared in open Court. Desai for accused No.3 and 5. :: J U D G M E N T :: (Delivered on this 3rd Day of August , 2015) 1] The accused are chargesheeted for the offence punishable under section 143, 147, 148, 307, and 387 of IPC. 2] Facts in brief alleged by the prosecution are that, The complainant Ashok Yadav is residing with his family members in Bansbahaddur chawl, Gandhinagar, Kalwa and runs a grossary shop in the house. He is originally from Bilriganj Tal Sagani Dist. Ajamgarh U.P. He knows accused Kalya Ganya @ Ganesh Shinde and accused Sachin @ Tilya. 3] It is alleged that on 07/07/2013 he was sitting in front of his house, on the chair and talking with Janardan Kanojia at about 11.45 a.m. Meanwhile Ganesh Shinde @ Kala Ganya, Sachin @ Tilya came with 4 to 5 companions and asked," A Gandu Paisa Nikal , nahito Kat Dalunga." He threatened him with the chopper and assaulted by saying "Mereko Puchta hai, hai ka paisa? Tu mereko Janata nahi kya? Pahila Paisa Nikal." He assaulted with chopper which he missed . 4] It is alleged that meanwhile Janardan Kanojia intervened, he was assaulted by the companions of Kalya Ganya with bat and fist blows. The neighbours shut the door, due to fear of Kalya Ganya. He was shouting . 5] It is alleged that to save the life, he and Janardan Kanojia went to the house and were closed the door. Those persons kicked the door. Kanojia hold the door and he brought the revolver from the drawer of cupboard and those persons will come in the house, therefore, due to fear, he fired and those persons ran away. 6] It is alleged that after opening the door, he found that there was nobody, but blood stains were found at the towel on the chair, bat and chopper were lying. 7] It is lastly alleged he gave call to Municipal corporator Mukund Keni . He fired for self protection and he came to know that accused Ganesh Shinde @ Kalya Ganya was hit by the bullet and was taken to hospital. 8] He, therefore, lodged complaint and concerned police registered crime NO. I 271/13 under section 143, 147, 148, 307, 387, of IPC . During investigation, Spot panchnama, seizure panchnama of revolver of complainant and seizure panchnama of cloths were recorded, statement of witnesses were recorded. The memorandum panchnama of Sachin Jadhav and recovery panchnama of accused Atul Mhatre was recorded. Injury certificate of Ashok Yadav and Janardan Kanojia was collected. Muddemal was sent to forensic science lab. CA report is awaited. After completion of investigation, concerned police submitted chargesheet. 9] The learned Magistrate, found the offence punishable under section 307 of IPC, exclusively triable by Sessions court, he, therefor,e committed case by passing order below Exh.1. 10] On hearing learned APP and defence counsel and considering the record, charge below Exh. 15 was framed under section 143, 147, 148, 307, 387, r/w.149 of IPC and the same when read over and explained to accused in vernacular, they have denied it vide their statement Exh.16 to 21. 11] From the statement under 313 of Cr. P.C. and evidence on record, defence of accused is of denial. 12] I have heard learned APP and defence counsel . 13] The learned defence counsel submitted that accused Ganesh @ Kalya Ganya suffered bleeding injuries and he ldoged FIR, but it is not known what happened to that. He submitted that neither accused were identified nor identification parade was arranged. He submitted that 7 to 8 persons were closing the door, complainant took some time to bring revolver and therefore, how the complainant sustained injury. 14] The defence counsel also submitted that injuries are simple and there is no panchnama of inside the house. It is submitted that no independent witnesses are examined and that accused are falsely involved. 15] The other defence Advocates argued that Municipal Corporator Mr. Keni is not examined, nor dying declaration of accused Kalya is recorded. They submitted that so called memorandum and recovery panchanama udner section 27 is not proved. 16] On the other hand, learned APP submitted that weapons of assault i.e. chopper, bat and stump were found, and this shows the conduct of the accused. He submitted that identification in the court is sufficient. He submitted that there is no material contradiction in the evidence of eye witnesses. 17] Under the circumstances, following points arise for my determination and findings to them are as under:- Sr. POINTS FINDINGS No . 1] Whether the prosecution prove that Not on 07/06/2013 at 01.45 hrs. at proved Bansbahaddr chawl, in front of complainant Ashok Bansbahaddur Yadav, Gandhinagar, KalwaThane were members of unlawful assembly common object of which is to commit offence ? 2] Whether it is proved by the Not prosecution that on the same date, proved time and place and during the course of same transaction were the members of an unlawful assembly and in prosecution of common object of the said assembly, committed riot? 3] Whether it is proved by the Not prosecution that on the same date, proved time and place, and during the course of same transaction were the members of an unlawful assembly and at that time, armed with deadly weapons used as a weapon of offence? 4] Whether it is proved by the Not prosecution that on the same date, proved time and place, and during the but course of same transaction were offence the members of an unlawful under assembly and in prosecution of section common object of the said 324 of IPC assembly, you all accused gavea is found blows of bat and stump and proved chopper to the complainant Ashok against Bansbahaddur Yadav with such accused intention or knowledge and under No.3 such circumstacnes that, if by that Ganesh . Act you had caused the death of above persons, you would have been guilty of murder ? 5] Whether it is proved by the Not prosecution that on the same date, proved. time and place, and in prosecution of common object of the said assembly, and in prosecution of common object of the said assembly put the complainant and his family in fear of death in orer to committing of extortion ? 6] what order? Accused No.3 is convicted of the offence punishabl e under section 324 of IPC. ::REASONS :: 18] For the sake of convenient discussioon points are clubbed. 19] The prosecution has examined in all 11 witnesses. Pw Ashok Bansbahaddur Yadav who is complainant, Pw Janardan Kanojia witness, Pw Urmila Yadav wife of complainant, Pw Vinod Bansbahaddur Yadav brother of complainant, Nisha Vinod Yadav niece of complainant, Omprakash Gourishankar Jaiswal panch witness, Pw Rakesh Chedilal Yadav panch witness, Pw Raju Adhagale panch witness , Pw Prakaash Nilewad ACP Devnar Mumbai, investigating officer, Pw.Dr.Yogesh Srirang More, Raghu Baburao Bhilare another investigating officer. 20] The facts that complainant Ashok Yadav is residing in Bansbahaddur chawl, Gandhi nagar, Kalwa, having grocery shop , accused Ganesh @ kalya Ganya is known to him, said accused had been to the spot to iron the cloths, complainant Ashok Yadav, for self protection, fired in the air from inside the house, by using licensed revolver are not disputed. It is also not disputed that revolver of cmoplainant was recovered and it is returned to him. 21] So far as the evidence of injured and eye witnesses are concerned, the first one is Ashok Yadav who stated that on 07/06/2013 in 11.40 to 11.45 a.m. he was sitting in the chair in his house, 4-5 persons came with chopper and cricket bat and demanded ransum and threatened him. Chopper was thrown on him, which he missed. He went inside his house because of fear and accused Ganesh and his companions were pushing the door. He stated that he fired in the air with his revolver and accused ran away. The panchnama was drawn , and he lodged complaint as per Exh.29. He admitted that he knows one accused. It is not disputed that Kanojia is running laundry shop. He was put up that chopper and cricket bat were lying in front f his house. Though he admitted that he does not know reading and writing Marathi, but denied that he was not read over the complaint. 22] The evidence further shows that he, Kanojia, his family members were trying to close the doors of his house, revolver was kept in the drawer of the table . There is single door to his house which opens inside. 23] The witness does not know that accused Ganesh had been to press the cloths to Kanojia. He was put up that he fired on accused Ganesh Shinde by coming outside his house. This obviously bring the presence of not only of complainant, but accused Ganesh on the spot. The omission is found in the complaint which is silent that accused Tilya was having chopper. 24] The other eye witness is Pw Janardan Kanojia. According to him on 07/06/2013 he was present, and was talking with accused Ashok (Complainant). He stated that accused Ganya came and assaulted him. He went inside the house because of fear and they were trying to close the door. Her assaulted Ganya at his rigth hand. The examination in chief itself shows that he does not know other accused except Ganya. 25] The prosecution was permitted to put the questions to his own witness as that of cross- examinatiion. He admitted that that accused Kalya Ganya assaulted at the neck of Ashok Yadav, but he missed it. He admitted that accused Atul, Sachin and Kiran assaulted him with stump or bat and police recorded statement as per his instructions. 26] In the further cross-examination by accused No.2 and 6 that he does not know the assailant except Ganya. He was not knowing the names of assailant. He, therefore, ruled out the role of other accused , except Ganesh @ Ganya. 27] In the cross-examination on behalf of accused No.3 Ganesh, the evidence shows that he and accused tried to close the door, and 5-6 persosn trying to open the door. He was holding the door till Ashok Yadav brought the revolver. This again shows presence of complainant and himself on the spot. The assault to him by cricket bat is not found in the statement. 28] In this context, Pw Janardan Kanojia was injured eye tienss and in the cross-examination, he admitted the facts. It is true that the evidence of witness who tried to change the version is to be appreciated with abandunt precaution. It appears equally true that merely the prosecution was allowed to cross-examine his own witness, his testimony cannot be outrightly brushed aside. 29] In this behalf, the evidence of Pw Urmila Yadav, who is wife of complainant, shows that she knows Kalya Ganya. On 07/06/2013 she and other members present in the house, accused Kalya demanded amount from husband, he did not give, he started beating. The accused was having bat and chopper. She stated that accused kaya Ganya and other 4-5 persosn were pushing the door, complainant fired and accused ran away. Though she admitted that she does not know the talk between her husband and accused Kalya which was told to her by her husband. She was not called for identification parade. 30] It may be noted that she was put up that accused Kalya Ganya had been to press his cloths to Kanojiya (Witness), interestingly she was put up that her husband raised quarrel with accused Kalya Ganya and shocked by the revolver. Therefore, the presence in view of the facts on record, particularly, accused Kalya Ganya, alongwith injured eye witnesses, is to be believed. 31] The other eye witness on behalf of prosecution is Pw Nisha Yadav who is niece of complainant. According to her, on 07/06/2013 her uncle was sitting on chair outside the house at about 11.30 to 11.40 a.m. accused came with 4-5 persons Her uncle refused therefore, accused assasulted with hand and thereafter, with chopper and bat. She stated that her uncle and Janardan Kanojia came inside the house, accused were pushing the door, and uncle fired in the air. she only knows accused Ganesh. She admitted that she was inside the house, when accused Ganesh came, and uncle keep revolver in the cupboard. Her presence is also believable in view of the her trustworthy evidence, and also of complainant Ashok Yadav and witness Janardan Kanojia and nevertheless of accused Ganesh. 32] The evidence of Vinod Yadav shows that complainant Ashok is his brother, informed him about the incident and therefore, he came to the spot , found the cricket bat and stump lying near the door. He was put up that his brother gave abuses to accused Kalya Ganya and fired with bullet. He is the witness having heard the complainant, his brother about true facts, and therefore, he is not the eye witness. 33] The other facet of the evidence is of memorandum and recovery panchnama. Pw Rakesh Yadav shows that on 26/06/2013 accused Sachin Yadav gave a memorandum that he will produce stump as per Exh.55. The said accused produced the same from his room, near public toilet which was seized under panchnama Exh.56. He admitted that panchas were asked that while drawing the memorandum, police did not type his name. 34] The other panch Pw Raju did not support the prosecution. He was panch of memorandum give by accused Tilya. 35] In this context, the evidence of Pw Prakash Nilewad shows that he received investigation in crime NO. I 272/13 and accused Sachin gave memorandum at Exh.55 and at his instance , stump was seized under panchnama Exh.56. He also stated that accused Atul gave memorandum about the production the bat which he produced was seized under panchnama Exh.74. 36] Firstly the voutnary nature of the statement either by accused Sachin or Atul Mhatre and seconly, consequent upon such disclosure discovery of fact and recovery of article could not be proved within the ambit of section 27 of Evidence ACt. 37] The other point brought to my notice by defence counsel is copy of complaint filed by accused Ganesh Shinde Exh.78. The I.O. admitted it and that he has taken cross-complaint. He admitted that complaint of accused Ganesh Shinde was investigated by P.I. Shri Malekar. Neither prosecution nor defence reported the result of investigation, pendency of chargesheet, or decision, if any. 38] Pw Raghu Bhilare his evidence shows that he was also investigating officer in C.R. NO.271/13. According to him on 11/06/2013 accused Ajit Sudke gave memorandum that he will produce the chopper which is at Exh.61. and he produced it from Vanjarpada slum area. It was seized under panchnama Exh.62. 39] His evidence further shows that accused Kiran gave memorandum that he will produce stump which was recorded as per Exh.63 and accused produced it from the roof Vanjarpada slum area. Seizure panchnama is at Exh.64. 40] At the cost of repetition, volutnary nature of the statement of the panch witnesses of accused Ajit Sudke, Kiran Dalwi is not found proved. The requirement of section 27 of Evidence Act are found not fulfilled, and therefore, recovery at the behest of those accused is difficult to be belived. 41] This takes me to discuss the evidence of medical officer Dr. Yogesh More. On 07/06/2013 he examined Janardan Kanojia at CSM hospital, Kalwa, and found following injuries. 1] Abrasion at left side of front trominance of 2 c.m. x 0.5 c.m. 2] abrasion at right hand elbow of 6 c.m. x 1 cm. x1 c.m. He issued injury certificate Exh.81. 42] He also examined on that day, Ashok Yadav and found following injuries. 1] Swelling elbow at elbow joint painful movement at right hand upper 1/3, no fracture / dislocation. 2] Blunt trauma, upper aspect of right index finger. His injury certificate is at Exh.82. The Doctor opined that injuries in the certificate are simple in nature and caused by hard and blunt object or with bat. In the cross-examination he has given second opinion that injuries are possible by fall on the ground. 43] The magnitude of the offence prescribed in section 307 of IPC requires cogent and discernable evidence. The offence prescribed in the said section requires intention or knowledge on the part of assailant that, by the act he would be guilty of either murder or imprisonment which may extend of ten years and if hurt is caused imprisonment may be of life imprisonment. At the cost of repetition in the present case, the presence of accused Ganesh, complainant Ashok Yadav, witness Janardar Kanoia and his family members is very much found and also brought in the cross-examination. It is worth to be noted that identification of other accused, could not be proved, nor their role in committing either the offence riot or that they were armed with deadly weapon or they threatened complainant or put even his family members, in fear of death for the purpose of extortion. 44] The identification parade was not arranged. I have already discussed the presence of accused Ganesh @ Kalya Ganya and his acquaintence with complainant and witnesses. The injury certificate Exh. 81, 82 of complainant Ashok Yadav and injured Janardan Kanojia reveal the simple injury. The submission of the defence counsel that they were inside the house, and therefore, how they can sustain injury, would not be acceptable for the simple reason complainant Ashok Yadav was outside the house, after some time they were inside. 45] The severity of offence under section 307, or formation of unlawful assaembly the object of which was to commit riot or other offence, or extortion by putting complainant and his family member into fear of death could not be found proved. 46] Nevertheless, the evidence of complainant Ashok Yadav, Pw Janardan Kanojia and other witnesses coupled with the admited fact of presence of accused Ganesh @ Kalya Ganya shows and the evidence on record, in the opinion of this court, is sufficient to believe the act of assault on his part. 47] In the facts and circumstances, the evidence discussed above, the lessor offence prescribed in section 324 is found proved, but only asgainst accused Ganesh @ kalya Ganya, therefore, he is held guilty. 48] I have heard accused on the point of sentence. He requested to take lenient view. He is in jail since 21/06/2013 till today. He is entitled for set off. 49] The above discussion leads me to pass the following order:- :: ORDER :: 1] Accused No.3 Ganesh Rangnath Shinde @ Kalya Ganya is convicted for the offence punishable under 324 of IPC under section 235(2) of Cr. P.C. and he is sentenced to suffer simple imprisonment for the period of 2 years . 2] Set off be given under section 428 of Cr. P.C. for the period undergone in jail i.e. from 21/06/2013 till today. 3] He is acquitted under section for the offence punishable under section 143,147, 148, 307and 387 r/w.149 of IPC and all other accused 1] Tillya @ Ajit Maruti Sudke, 2] Kiran Bansi Dalwi 4] Sachin Narayan Jadhav, 5] Devidas Rabaji Gadekar, and 6} Atul Kamlakar Mhatre are acquitted of the offence punishable under above sections. 4] Inform the jail authority immediately to release accused Atul Kamlakar Mhatre if not required in any other crime. 5] Bail bonds of accused who are on bail be cancelled. 6] Muddemal property revolver having been returned to complainant be retained by him and other muddemal being worthless, be destroyed after appeal period is over. 7] The accused to comply the provisions of Section 437(A) of Cr. P.C. Thane. (M.M.Walimohammed) Dt.03/08/2015. Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

Under such circumstances arguments of advocate Mr.Mane about examining the victim J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 213­16 ­ S­363,366.376, 4.doc .....9/­ ..9.. J­Spl.Case POCSO – 213/2016.. Exh.48. CNR No.MHTH01­005784­2016 within 24 hours of sexual intercourse and ruling on said point are not applicable. 14] The prosecution has examined Dr.Priti Deshmukh as PW5 at Exh.31. She had examined the accused. She has deposed that on examination of the accused she find nothing to suggest that he was impotent. In view of admission of sexual intercourse by the accused with the victim, the evidence of PW5 is merely of formal nature. 15] The prosecution has examined PW3 Sanjay Angatrao Gavhane the Assistant Traffic Inspector as panch witness. Through his evidence prosecution has proved the panchanama of seizure of motorcycle used by accused in the offence. By said panchanama clothes of accused were also seized. Said panchanama is at Exh.24. The prosecution further proved panchanama of seizure of clothes of victim and panchanama of Room No.105 of hotel Spiceland, Alibag. Those panchanamas are at Exh.25 and Exh.26. In view of facts admitted by the accused it is not necessary to discuss the evidence of PW3 in detail. 16] The prosecution has examined investigating officer P.S.I. Babar as PW6. He specifically deposed that the age of the victim was 16 years. He further deposed that after J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 213­16 ­ S­363,366.376, 4.doc .....10/­ ..10.. J­Spl.Case POCSO – 213/2016.. Exh.48. CNR No.MHTH01­005784­2016 recording complaint of kidnapping he revealed that the accused was also missing. Therefore, they had obtained mobile number of the accused and requested for CDR. He has further deposed as to how the accused was arrested, the victim was referred for medical examination, the visit to Alibag and preparing panchanamas of seizure of motorcycle, clothes of accused, clothes of victim and spot panchanama. In view of facts admitted by the accused on oath, it is not necessary to dispute the evidence of PW6 and to discuss the same in detail. 17] The complainant, Laxmi Boge has specifically stated that the age of victim was 16 years. On the basis of the same complaint of kidnapping was recorded. The prosecution has produced the original birth certificate of the victim at Exh.42. As per said birth certificate the birth of the victim took place at Devnar Maternity Home and the birth date is 31.12.2001. The incident is dated 18.06.2016. Thus on the date of incident the victim was below 15 years of age. 18] On the point of birth date of the victim advocate Mr.Mane has relied upon following decisions : i] Deepak Jitendra Sawant Vs. State of Maharashtra reported in 2017 All M.R. (Cri) 2058 ii] Ravi Anandrao Gurpude Vs. State of Maharashtra reported in 2017 Al M.R.1509 J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 213­16 ­ S­363,366.376, 4.doc .....11/­ ..11.. J­Spl.Case POCSO – 213/2016.. Exh.48. CNR No.MHTH01­005784­2016 iii] Decision of Hon'ble Madras High Court in Criminal Appeal No.363/2005 dated 10.03.2011 Relying upon above rulings advocate Mr.Mane argued that except the birth certificate no other document to prove age of victim is produced on record. In order to prove said birth date it is necessary to prove where the birth took place. He further submitted that the prosecution has to prove the birth date by producing reliable documents about the birth of the victim. 19] In the present case the birth certificate was produced alongwith charge sheet in the form of photocopy. The original birth certificate is produced during trial. As mentioned in the birth certificate the victim was born at Devnar Maternity Home and her birth date is 31.12.2001. So far as the decision in case Deepak Sawant (Supra) is concerned the birth date was stated for the first time during the evidence recorded in the Court. The investigating officer had not bothered to collect the birth certificate. In view of facts in present case the decision in case of Deepak Jitendra Sawant is certainly not applicable in present case. So far as decision in case of Ravi Gurpude (Supra) is concerned in said case the prosecution had failed to prove the age of victim. As already mentioned in present case the J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 213­16 ­ S­363,366.376, 4.doc .....12/­ ..12.. J­Spl.Case POCSO – 213/2016.. Exh.48. CNR No.MHTH01­005784­2016 original birth certificate is produced on record. So also in said case the charge for offence u/s.376 of Indian Penal Code was not framed and in the absence of evidence about birth date the accused was acquitted. The situation in present case is altogether different. The prosecution has come with specific age of the victim with birth certificate. Hence said ruling and arguments on said point are not applicable in present case. 20] In case of Surmani and others of Hon'ble Madras High Court and referred above, there was no document showing birth date. The age was determined on the basis of report of Radiologist. The Radiologist had reported the age between 17 to 18 years. It was further observed that scientifically it can be said that from the fusion of iliac crust a girl as completed 18 years of age. In our case the prosecution has come with specific allegations and original birth certificate of the victim. As such the ratio in this Judgment is also not applicable to the present case . 21] In the present case the complaint of kidnapping was lodged by paternal aunt of the victim. The accused has come with specific defence that the victim herself compelled him to elope with her to avoid her marriage fixed by her paternal aunt. Advocate Mr.Mane argued that the complainant with her own consent sat on the motorcycle of the accused J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 213­16 ­ S­363,366.376, 4.doc .....13/­ ..13.. J­Spl.Case POCSO – 213/2016.. Exh.48. CNR No.MHTH01­005784­2016 and went to Alibag, Panvel, Solapur, etc. There was no force at the hands of accused and therefore, there was no kidnapping as contemplated u/s.363 of the Indian Penal Code. He further argued that in view of the consent and compulsion at the hands of victim the offence u/s.366 of the Indian Penal Code is also not duly proved. On these points advocate Mr.Mane relied upon following decisions. i] Jinish Lal Sah Vs. State of Bihar, reported in (2003)1 Supreme Court Cases 605 ii] Kavita Chandrakant Lakhani Vs. State of Maharashtra reported in A.I.R. 2018 Supreme Court 2099 iii] S Wardharaja Vs. State of Madras reported in A.I.R. 1965 Supreme Court 942 22] In present case the informant/complainant is the paternal aunt of the victim. As deposed by her the victim girl was residing with her at her house. In cross examination conducted by advocate Mr.Mane it is brought on record that the victim is residing with her since she was three months old. Thus, it is not the case that the victim was residing at the house of the informant merely for education. Under such circumstances, as observed in case of S.Wardharaja (Supra) it cannot be said that the guardianship of father of the victim was continuous. It is further to be noted here that though there are no documents showing any adoption of victim girl by the informant the victim states her name as her daughter. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 213­16 ­ S­363,366.376, 4.doc .....14/­ ..14.. J­Spl.Case POCSO – 213/2016.. Exh.48. CNR No.MHTH01­005784­2016 Even in deposition recorded on oath the victim stated her name as Anjali Mallesh Sakhare @ Anjali James Boge. Thus the victim was under the guardianship of the informant Laxmi Boge. Hence arguments of advocate Mr.Mane and ruling cited by him are certainly not applicable here. 23] So far as section 366 of the Indian Penal Code is concerned, in the cross examination of victim it is suggested on behalf of defence that she had sexual intercourse with the accused. The accused has taken the victim to the lodge at Alibag and had sexual intercourse with her. Considering the age of victim, her consent is no consent in the eyes of law. While taking the room in the lodge, the accused was well awared or rather was having intention to have sexual intercourse with the victim. Thus, it was within his knowledge that the victim would be seduced to illicit intercourse and he committed said act. Thus arguments of advocate Mr.Mane and rulings cited by him on the point of offence u/s.366 of the Indian Penal Code are not acceptable. 24] From all above observations and admitted facts on record the offences punishable u/s.363, 366 and 376 of the Indian Penal Code and section 4 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act are proved against the accused J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 213­16 ­ S­363,366.376, 4.doc .....15/­ ..15.. J­Spl.Case POCSO – 213/2016.. Exh.48. CNR No.MHTH01­005784­2016 beyond reasonable doubts. Hence I answer point Nos.1 to 3 in the affirmative and proceed to hear accused on quantum of sentence. 25] Heard accused and advocate Mr.Mane on the point of quantum of sentence. It is argued that the accused is very young. He is only earning member in his family. His age old parents are depending upon him. Hence minimum punishment be inflicted. A.P.P. Mr.Kadu submitted that maximum punishment be inflicted. 26] In the present case offence u/s.363, 366 and 376 of the Indian Penal Code and 4 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act are proved against the accused. Section 4 of the Act prescribing punishment for penetrative sexual assault being special provision it is not necessary to give punishment u/s.376 of the Indian Penal Code for said offence. Section 4 prescribes punishment of imprisonment not less than seven years which may extent to imprisonment for life and with fine also. Under such circumstances single punishment for penetrative sexual assault and separate punishments for section 363 and 366 are to be inflicted upon accused. With these observations following order is passed. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 213­16 ­ S­363,366.376, 4.doc .....16/­ ..16.. J­Spl.Case POCSO – 213/2016.. Exh.48. CNR No.MHTH01­005784­2016 ORDER 1.
