Code and u/s. 8 & 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual offences Act. 2] Brief facts of the prosecution case are as under:­ On 31/07/2018 the complainant Balasaheb Bhiku Gholap lodged complaint to Rabale police station that he resides at Airoli with wife, son and minor victim­girl aged 15 years. His wife runs printing shop and his children are taking education. On 30/07/2018 he was taking his minor victim­girl to cloth shop and he noticed that one unknown boy is looking towards his daughter and after some distance, he noticed that said boy is following his daughter. They went to printing shop of wife. He heard shouting of his wife and brother of wife that said boy is pulling her daughter. He saw that said boy hold hand of his daughter. Anyhow she was rescued and said boy ran away. That time, his daughter disclosed his name as Vishal Sable and that he was following her since six months and giving trouble to her. Then all came to police station and lodged complaint on next day evening. On its basis, above referred crime came to be registered, accused was arrested and remanded to jail. 3] The applicant/accused in bail application submitted that he was working as a driver on Uber Company car. The applicant/accused and complainant are from same village and due to grudge in the mind of complainant, he lodged false complaint. He submitted that he is innocent, CNR NO.MHTH01­005799­2018 2 B.A.2087/2018 he has not committed any offence, nothing was done by him. He has co­ operated in investigation, he will abide all the terms and conditions. On this count, he sought bail. 4] I.O. and Ld. A.P.P. submitted say and opposed application with contention that offence is serious, he used force against the minor victim, statement of victim is yet to be recorded in Court. He may repeat the crime, he committed offence against the minor victim, he may give trouble to victim in future, he may create hurdle in investigation. 5] I heard the submissions of Ld. Adv. for applicant/accused and Ld. A.P.P. Perused case diary. 6] Ld. Counsel for applicant submitted that considering the allegations, investigation appears to be over and the evidence of witnesses is to be recorded to prove the guilt and till then it is not necessary to detain the accused in jail and he will abide all the terms and conditions. 7] Ld. A.P.P. submitted that considering the nature of allegations, the age of victim, the accused may repeat the crime. 8] What appears from the contention of both sides is that the accused was allegedly following the complainant's daughter, tried to hold her hand and then complainant disclosed about trouble by accused since six months. Before it nothing was disclosed. The accused has denied all the allegations and claimed innocence. Admittedly, trial will take its own time and considering the facts and circumstances, safety and security of victim CNR NO.MHTH01­005799­2018 3 B.A.2087/2018 and for securing presence of accused and prevention of repetition of incident in future, the accused can be released on bail on terms and conditions, considering his age also. Hence, following order is passed. ORDER 1] Application is allowed. 2] The applicant/accused Vishal Bhaskar Sable in C.R.No.I­ 311/2018 registered at Rabale police Station U/Section­354, 354­A of I.P. Code and u/s. 8 & 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual offences Act, be released on bail on his furnishing P.B. & S.B. of Rs.15,000/­ with surety of like amount. 3] The applicant/accused shall attend Rabale police station on every Tuesday from 8.00 a.m. to 10.00 a.m. for four weeks and shall not make attempt to contact with victim and complainant. 4] The accused shall not threaten the prosecution witnesses. 1 Special Case No.79/2013 (Judgment) Presented on : 15/10/2013 Registered on : 15/10/2013 Decided on : 05/05/2016 Duration :2­year,6­Months,21­days. IN THE COURT OF THE SPECIAL JUDGE, THANE. The State of Maharashtra Through Bhiwandi Taluka Police Station Thane, District – Thane. ... Prosecution versus Namdeo Chintaman Tambde Age 29 years, Residence –Banglapada Kharbao, Bhiwandi, Tal. Bhiwandi.Dist. Thane. ... Accused Offence punishable under section 324, 509, 504, 506 of Indian Penal Code and under section 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Appearance ­ Spl.P.P. Mrs. R.A. Navale, for the State. Advocate Mrs. Devyani Patil for the Accused. 2 Special Case No.79/2013 (Judgment) JUDGMENT (Delivered on 5th May, 2016.) 1] The Accused stands prosecuted for the offence punishable under section 324, 509, 504 & 506 of Indian Penal Code and also under section 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act) for giving indecent gesture with intent to insult the modesty and for causing sexual harassment to minor victim­girl aged about 17 years and for causing hurt and threatening the informant. 2] Shron of verbiage, the indictment against the Accused are as under ­ [i] Informant Anil Dashrath Jadhav (P.W.1) is resident of Kharbao, Bhiwandi. He is labour on the site of sand excavation and accused Namdeo Tambde is also working there. [ii] The accused, although married and having children proposed the cousin sister of informant/victim­girl aged about 17 years for marriage. However, his proposal was rejected by the informant's family and they restrained the accused from coming to his house. [iii] On 20/02/2012 (2013) around 09.30 p.m. accused parked his motor cycle in front of the house of the informant and by blowing horn gave indecent gesture to the victim­girl. 3 Special Case No.79/2013 (Judgment) On that informant (P.W.1) questioned the Accused, therefore, accused abused him and threatened him and even assaulted by wooden plank on his head. The people intervened their quarrel and then accused ran away from there. Therefore, on 21/02/2013 the informant lodged report against the Accused. 3] On his report F.I.R. was registered against the Accused vide C.R.No.I­46/2013 for the offence punishable under section 324, 509, 504 & 506 of I.P.C. and under section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. The investigation was carried out by A.S.I. Kisan Baburao Kute (P.W.2). The Accused was arrested. The spot panchnama and the sketch map of scene of offence was drawn. The informant was sent for medical examination and collected injury certificate. Statements of witnesses were recorded. Thereafter, investigation culminated into filing of charge­sheet in this Court being the Special designated court under P.O.C.S.O. Act. 4] The charge (Exh.3) was framed against the Accused for offence punishable under section 324, 509, 504 & 506 of Indian Penal Code and also under section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. The Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial (Exh.4). The Accused took defence of total denial. 5] In response to application under section 294 of Cr.P.C. the defence has admitted spot panchnama [Exh.13] 4 Special Case No.79/2013 (Judgment) and sketch map of scene of offence [Exh.14] and seizure panchnama of wooden log [Exh.15]. 6] In order to prove guilt of Accused Prosecution has examined following witnesses ­ P.W.1 Anil Dashrath Jadhav Exh.11 Informant P.W.2 A.S.I. Kisan Baburao Kute Exh.19 (Investigating officer) 7] The prosecution proved and relied on the report / F.I.R. [Exh.11], Arrest form [Exh.20] & injury certificate of the informant [Exh.21]. 8] The prosecution closed its side of evidence by filing Pursis at Exhibit­22. The statement of the Accused under Section 313(b) of Cr.P.C. was recorded. Accused neither examined himself nor examined any witness in his defence. 9] Heard learned A.P.P. Mrs. R. A. Navale for State and the learned Advocate Mrs. Devayani Patil for the Accused. 10] On consideration of argument advanced on behalf of both the sides and on perusal of the oral & documentary evidence on record, following points arise for my determination, which are answered with the findings thereon, 5 Special Case No.79/2013 (Judgment) as under :­ Sr. Points Findings No. 1] Does the prosecution prove that 20/02/2013 at 21.30 hours near Grampanchayat at village Phirangipada, Dist. Thane voluntarily caused hurt to ..No. the informant Anil Dashrath Jadhav by assaulting him with wooden plank and he thereby committed an offence punishable under section 324 of Indian Penal Code ? 2] Does the prosecution prove that on the same date and place accused intending to insult the modesty of cousin sister of informant/victim­girl of 17 years by ..No. making indecent gestures with intent to insult modesty of victim­girl and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 509 of I.P.C. ? 3] Does the prosecution prove that on the same date and place accused intentionally insulted the informant in filthy language and thereby gave ..No. provocation to break public peace and he thereby committed an offence punishable under section 504 of I.P.C. ? 4] Does the prosecution prove that on the same date and place accused committed criminal intimidation by threatening the informant with intent to cause alarm to him and he thereby committed an 6 Special Case No.79/2013 (Judgment) offence punishable under section 506 of I.P.C.? 5] Does the prosecution prove that during same period accused committed sexual harassment to victim­girl aged 17 years ...No. by making indecent gestures and there by committed offence punishable u/sec.12 of P.O.C.S.O.Act? 6] What order ? Accused is acquitted. REASONS As to Point No.1 to 5 : 11] All the points are taken up together for discussion, to avoid the repetition, as evidence about the same in common and inter­connected. 12] As the Accused is facing charge under section 324 of I.P.C. it is incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that accused voluntarily caused hurt by dangerous weapon to the informant and further the accused is also facing charge under section 504 & 506 of I.P.C. the burden lies on the prosecution to prove that accused intentionally insulted the informant or victim­girl and thereby gave provocation to break the public peace and he committed criminal intimidation by threatening the informant (P.W.1). Further, as the accused is 7 Special Case No.79/2013 (Judgment) also facing charge under section 509 of I.P.C. the prosecution is required to prove that the accused with intent to insult the modesty of the victim­girl made some sound intending that it shall be heard by the victim­girl. So also as the Accused is facing charge under section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, therefore, it is further incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that the accused has committed sexual harassment to the victim­ girl with sexual intent, either utters any word or makes any sound, or makes any gesture or exhibits any object or part of body with the intention that such work or sound shall be heard, or such gesture or object or part of body shall be seen by the child etc. as defined in section 11 of the P.O.C.S.O. Act. Age of victim­girl : 13] As the Accused is facing charge under P.O.C.S.O. Act, therefore, it is incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that the victim­girl was child (minor) at the time of incident. Prosecution could not examine the Victim­girl in spite of genuine efforts made to serve summons to her. Informant Anil Jadhav (P.W.1) who is cousin brother of victim­girl did not even utter the age of victim­girl at the time of incident. Neither there is any document in charge­sheet in support of date of birth of the victim­girl. Thus, there is absolutely no evidence on record about the age of the victim­girl. Thus, the prosecution failed to prove that at the time of incident, the 8 Special Case No.79/2013 (Judgment) victim­girl was minor aged about 17 years i.e. below the age of 18 years and she was a “child” as per definition given in Section 2(d) of P.O.C.S.O. Act. 14] To prove the charge against the Accused the prosecution has examined the informant Anil Dashrath Jadhav (P.W.1)/ cousin brother of the victim­girl who is the most material witness for prosecution to prove the charge against the Accused. However, informant (P.W.1) resiled from his report and statement and did not support the prosecution case on the material aspect of the incident. He only admits his signature on the report. He was thoroughly cross­examined by the prosecution, but nothing material is elicited from him to prove the charge framed against the accused. 15] The prosecution then made a feeble attempt to prove the contents of the F.I.R. through the investigating officer, A.S.I. Kisan Kute(P.W.2). A.S.I. Kute (P.W.2) deposed about the information lodged by the informant and material allegations against the accused. However, as informant did not support the prosecution case, therefore, the evidence of the investigating officer merely remains as a formality. 16] Further it is pertinent to note that the most material witness victim­girl is not examined by the prosecution as informant in very clear term stated that the victim­girl is 9 Special Case No.79/2013 (Judgment) now married and as they do not want to ruin her matrimonial life, therefore, he will not keep her present in the Court. In such circumstances, even the prosecution become helpless and therefore the learned Spl.P.P. filed a pursis (Exh.22) to that effect and closed their evidence. 17] Thus, prosecution failed to prove that accused caused hurt to informant with wooden plank and threaten him or intentionally insult him to provoke to break breach of public peace and further failed to prove that accused with intent to insult the modesty of victim­girl make indecent gestures and intentionally caused sexual harassment to her. Hence, I answer point No.1 to 5 in negative. Therefore, the accused is entitled for acquittal. 18] In the result, I proceed to pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused Namdeo Chintaman Tambde is hereby acquitted U/Sec. 235(1) of Cr.P.C. for the offence punishable U/Sec.324, 509, 504 & 506 of Indian Penal Code and U/s. 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] His bail bonds stand cancelled and sureties are discharged. 10 Special Case No.79/2013 (Judgment) 3] The Accused is directed to furnish personal bail bond of the amount of ₹15,000/­ in compliance of provision of section 437­A of Cr.P.C. The judgment is dictated and pronounced in open Court. Date : 05/05/2016. (Ms. U. M. Nandeshwar), Thane Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act),Thane. District Judge ­1 and Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

In The Court of the Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012, Thane) At Thane (Presided over by Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Case No. 81 of 2013 Exhibit No. 26 The State of Maharashtra (Through Wada police station) … Complainant. Versus Santosh Mangal Savla Age 23 years, Residing at Mhasval, Handipada, Taluka Wada, Dist. Thane. … Accused. Appearances :­ Spl.P.P. Mr. A. K. Khamkar for the State. Advocate Mrs. Swati Chitnis for the accused. JUDGMENT (Delivered on 05th August, 2015) Accused stands prosecuted for the offences punishable under sections 363, 366A, 376 of Indian Penal Code and punishable under sections 4 and 6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter referred as POCSO Act in short). .. 2 .. Special case 81/2013 Judgment 2] In short the facts giving rise to the prosecution of the accused are that victim girl Sonu had been staying with her parents, brother and sister at village Mhasval Umbarpada, Tal. Wada, District Thane and she was aged about 16 years in the year 2013 and was studying in Nav Jeevan Vidyalaya, Kalyan in 10 th standard and stayed at Malhar Nagar, Kalyan for about 1 year and used to go at native place in Mhasval Umbarpada in vacation. In the year 2013 when she had been to her native place at Mhasval Umberpada she developed acquaintance with accused Santosh Savla and they developed love affair. It is also the case of the prosecution that on 23/05/2013 she had been to the house of her maternal aunt for attending marriage of aunt's son Sunil and accused also attended said marriage and dinner, and they were dancing. Accused called victim girl early in the morning at about 4.00 a.m. and told that they will marry and induced her sweetly and went to Mahalaxmi hill and stayed there for about 20 to 22 days, they used to sleep under tree and during that period accused had sexual intercourse with victim girl many times. Then they went to Umbrothe and stayed there for one day and on next day went to Pali Posheri hill and stayed there for about 5 to 6 days. 3] It is also the case of the prosecution that in the meantime after the accused took away girl from marriage ceremony without intimating her parents, her parents searched for the girl, but they could not trace her. Then her father lodged complaint about missing of her daughter on 26/05/2013. On the basis of his complaint missing complaint was registered and was enquired into. .. 3 .. Special case 81/2013 Judgment Then parents and relatives of the girl further enquired about her and it revealed that girl is with the accused at Handipada and stayed with him and also that he had kidnapped girl from lawful guardianship of the parents of the girl. Thereafter her mother lodged complaint 4] On the basis of her complaint, offence as per C.R. No. I­ 119/20013 was registered and it was investigated into by P.S.I. R. M. Chavan. During the investigation statements of the witnesses were recorded, girl and accused were traced and accused came to be arrested. Accused and victim girl were sent for medical examination and their medical certificates were obtained. The statement of victim girl was recorded and since in her statement it revealed that accused had sexual intercourse with girl, Section 376 of IPC and 4 and 6 of POCSO Act were added and report was sent to the the Ld. Magistrate. Since girl reported her age about 16 years, her school leaving certificate was obtained. Seized muddemal and blood samples were sent for chemical analysis and after completion of investigation, since it revealed that accused kidnapped victim girl from the lawful guardianship of her parents and had sexual intercourse with her during the period when they stayed together, he came to be chargesheeted for the offences punishable under sections 363, 366A, 376 of IPC and sections 4 and 6 of POCSO Act. 5] Since the offences punishable under POCSO Act are triable by Special Court, this is being Special Court for trying cases under POCSO Act, charge­sheet was submitted to this Court. The accused was produced before the Court. .. 4 .. Special case 81/2013 Judgment 6] A charge for offences under sections 363, 366A and 376 of IPC and sections 4 and 6 of POCSO Act was framed against the accused vide Exh. 2. Contents of charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. He pleaded not guilty. His defence as it revealed from the cross­examination of witnesses and statement of accused recorded under section 313 of Cr.P.C. was that girl and he were having love affair, girl insisted him to run with her and whatever had happened was with free consent of the girl. He claimed to be tried. 7] For establishing the offences charged against the accused, prosecution examined in all 3 witnesses P.W.1 Savita Sagar Rathad ­ mother of the girl/complainant, P.W.2 Sonu Sagar Rathad ­ victim girl and P.W.3 Murlidhar Balwant Musale – Head Master of Nav Jeevan school in which girl was studying. The documentary evidence produced, proved and relied upon by prosecution consists complaint at Exh.10, seizure panchnama of clothes of accused at Exh.17, seizure panchnama of clothes of victim girl at Exh.18, spot panchnama at Exh.19, medical certificate of age determination of victim girl at Exh.20, medical examination report of victim girl at Exh.21, forensic medical examination report of victim girl at Exh.22, forwarding letters to C.A. for sending obtained samples and seized clothes at Exh.23 and 24. 8] Statement of accused under section 313 of Cr.P.C. was recorded. Accused did not examine himself on oath and had not examined any witness in his defence. .. 5 .. Special case 81/2013 Judgment 9] On the basis of above facts of case, points which arose for my determination and my reasons and findings for the same are as under. POINTS FINDINGS 1) Whether prosecution proved that on 23.05.2013 at Torne – Dhavarpada, Wada accused kidnapped minor victim girl Sonu Rathad from lawful guardianship of her parents by inducing her by giving false assurance of marriage to the said minor victim girl and induced her to go away from that place with intent that said girl may be, or knowing it is likely that she will be forced or seduced to illicit intercourse with him? ... No. 2) Whether prosecution proved that after kidnapping accused committed rape on said victim girl? ... No. 3) Whether prosecution proved that after kidnapping accused committed aggravated penetrative sexual assault on said minor victim girl by committing rape on her? ... No. 4) What offence, if any, is proved against the accused? ... No offence is proved. 5) What order? ... Accused is acquitted. REASONS AS TO POINT Nos. 1 TO 3 :­ 10] All these points are interconnected and required to be .. 6 .. Special case 81/2013 Judgment decided on the basis of same evidence, I therefore discuss and decide all the points together. 11] As is clear that as per the prosecution case, accused had kidnapped minor girl with intention to have forcible intercourse with the girl and had taken away the girl and stayed with her and also have sexual intercourse with her. In regard to the allegations against the accused and in the light of defence put forth by the accused that the girl and he himself were having love affair and the girl compelled him to run way, the aspect as to whether it was matter of consent and whether girl at the relevant time was minor i.e. below 18 years of age is crucial. In that regard so far as age of the girl is concerned, testimony of P.W.3 is material. He stated that as per the school record date of birth of the girl is 13/02/1997. He also produced the extract of the school register in which the date of birth of the girl is seen to have been mentioned as 13/02/1997. Then, if calculated the age of the girl on the basis of birth date as 13/02/1997, her age on the date of incident comes to 16 years 03 months. But then the aspect cannot be ignored that as per the versions of the Head master i.e. P.W.3 in the cross examination that girl was admitted in their school in 2013 in 10 th standard. He also accepted that at the time of admission birth certificate of girl was not obtained, but earlier school leaving certificate was obtained. However, he had even not brought said earlier school leaving certificate. Nothing is brought on record as to on what basis entry of the date of birth of the girl was made in the school register. In absence of any proof of earlier school leaving certificate and birth certificate issued by Municipal corporation, entry of the date of birth .. 7 .. Special case 81/2013 Judgment of the girl made in the school register of the school in which girl was admitted directly in 10th standard and when entry in the school register is disputed and denied on behalf of the accused, fact that date of birth of the girl is correctly recorded cannot be established and the submission on behalf of the accused that girl is not below 18 years is having some substance. Even since the genuineness of school leaving certificate is disputed, the medical evidence in that regard also brought on record if considered it appears that as per medical certificate at Exh.20, on the basis of x­rays report and radiology report, approximately the age is between 16 to 17 years. It is well settled that in case of the age of the victim on the basis of medical examination, there is margin of error of 2 years on either side and that position is also well settled with the observations of the Hon'ble High Court and Supreme Court in various rulings. In such circumstances when the age of the girl is determined on the basis of medical examination as stated to be 16 to 17 years, there is possibility that girl is more than 18 years. The absence of certificate of date of birth of girl has to be held as fatal lacuna and it has to be concluded that it cannot be sufficient to prove that the girl is below 18 years of age at the relevant time. 12] Then so far as aspect that the accused had kidnapped the girl from the lawful guardianship of the parents and had sexual intercourse with her is concerned, as rightly pointed from the testimony of the girl as well as mother of the girl, there had been love affair between accused and girl. Then though, when after one month of missing the girl was not traced and she was found with accused and then they went to Kudus and brought the girl and then .. 8 .. Special case 81/2013 Judgment the mother of the girl lodged complaint, she has stated further that she has not enquired with her daughter as to where and how she had been with the accused. In the light of the testimony of the girl, wherein she specifically stated that she got acquaintance with the accused and the accused used to come Umbarpada and when she went at Dhavarpada for attending marriage of her cousin brother on 23/05/2013, she herself and accused ran away since there were love affair and stayed in Mahalaxmi temple, Mumbai. That makes it clear that she went with accused with free consent. Then so far as allegations that accused had sexual intercourse with her, girl appears to have stated that there was no sexual intercourse when they stayed together. No doubt the girl was declared hostile to that extent and in her cross examination she accepted that when she was staying with accused, she herself had sexual intercourse with him with her consent and portion marked “A” was stated to the police and also she further accepted in cross examination by A.P.P. that she falsely denied that there was sexual intercourse with accused. She also stated that she decided to marry accused and her marriage is to be performed in May 2016 and also her parents was agreeable to it. 13] Even medical examination report of the girl shows that there was evidence of sexual intercourse. The aspect cannot be ignored that it is very much clear that what had happened had happened with consent of the girl and girl is not proved to be below 18 years of age at the relevant time. When whatever had happened had happened with consent of the girl it has to be concluded that the allegations against the accused that he kidnapped girl and raped on .. 9 .. Special case 81/2013 Judgment her cannot be to have been established. 14] Even assuming for a while that the date of birth of the girl mentioned in the school leaving certificate is correct date, and the girl was below 18 years of age at the relevant time and also the age of the girl is above 16 years, the girl is seen to be having good understanding and is matured enough to know consequences of the physical act done with the accused and therefore it has to be held that she was in the age of desecration. Even her decision to marry with the accused stated to have been proved by the accused that after attending marriage ceremony she herself had run with accused. In such circumstances if the girl is assumed to be below 18 years since it appears from the record that girl herself left the house and there is no force on the part of the accused of any act and the accused ran away with girl and having sexual intercourse with her, none of the allegations can be said to have been established. Hence I answer point Nos. 1 to 3 in the negative. AS TO POINT No. 4 :­ 15] In view of my findings, on point Nos. 1 to 3, none of the charges leveled against accused can be said to have been established and accused is entitled to be acquitted. Point No.4 is therefore answered accordingly. 16] Since the accused is acquitted, it is required that he be directed furnish P.R.bond of Rs.15,000/­ [Rupees Fifteen Thousand only] under section 437A of Cr.P.C. to appear before the higher Court as and when such Court issue notice in respect of any appeal .. 10 .. Special case 81/2013 Judgment or petition, if any, filed against the judgment. In the result, I pass the following order ­ ORDER 1) Accused namely Santosh Mangal Savla is acquitted of the charge for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366­A and 376 of Indian Penal Code and also under Sections 4 and 6 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 2) The accused be released from jail forthwith if not required in any other crime. 3) The accused shall furnish P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] under section 437A of Cr.P.C. to appear before the higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect of any appeal or revision, if any, filed against the judgment and that such bail bond shall be in force for six months. 4) Muddemal property being worthless, be destroyed after expiry of appeal period. 5) The proceeding is closed. Date : 05/08/2015 (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012, Thane)

Presented on : 07.10.2014 Registered on : 07.10.2014 Decided on : 19.09.2017 Duration : 02Y. 11M. 12 D IN THE COURT OF SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE, AT : THANE. Presided over by S.C. Khalipe ­Additional Sessions Judge, Thane SPECIAL CASE NO.202/2014 Exh.No. The State of Maharashtra Through Naupada Police Station. ….. Prosecution V/s. Sureshkumar Lalmani Yadav Age 30 years, Occ:Rickshaw Driver R/at. Banshi Sheth Chawl, Chandanwadi, Almeda Road, Thane (E). ..... Accused Offence punishable under section 354(D) of Indian Penal Code and Section 8,11(1) of POCSO Act, 2012. Appearance: A.P.P. Smt. Hiwrale for the prosecution. Advocate Shri.Manoj Aher for the accused. :J U D G M E N T: (Delivered on this 19th Day of September, 2017) The offence is under section 354(D) of Indian Penal Code and Section 11 punishable under section 12 of POCSO Act, 2012. The case of the prosecution is that:­ 2. Four to five days prior to 25.08.2014 accused was following minor daughter of the informant at Raigad lane. He touched and slapped the victim. On the day on 25.08.2014 the so called accused had winked his eyes on the prosecutrix, so she shouted and told this fact to one woman and then her father was called there. Police and people had also come there. The people beat that man and handed over to the police. 3. After that the FIR was lodged by father of the prosecutrix in Naupada police station. C.R.NO.I­339/2014 was registered and investigated by Subhash Gokul Kale. He recorded statement of witnesses and recorded statement of victim and after the investigation he sent charge­sheet. 4. Charge was framed against the accused at Exh.8 under section 354(D) of Indian Penal Code and Section 8, and 12 of POCSO Act. He pleaded not guilty. 5. Considering the evidence on record following points arose for my determination. I have given its findings with reasons as under­ Sr.No Points Findings 1. Does prosecution prove that on 25.08.2014 at In Negative about 6.00 p.m. at Raigad Galli, near office of Corporator Narayan Pawar, Panchpakhadi, Thane (West) accused used criminal force to minor daughter of the informant aged 12 years with intention to outrage her modesty and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 354(D) of Indian Penal Code? 2. Does prosecution prove that on the same In Negative date, time and place accused committed sexual assault upon the minor daughter of the informant and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 8, and 12 of POCSO Act. 3 What order? As per final order REASONS AS TO POINT NOS.1 TO 3:­ 6. To prove the offence prosecution has examined witness Satyanarayan Changdev Thite at Exh.11, but he has not stated that the man who was sexually harassed was caught on the spot. He came to know about the incident from his friend who is informant. He does not know that who had sexually harassed the daughter of informant. 7. P.W.2 is the victim. As per her evidence she would go to leave her younger sister to class at Raigad Galli. On the day of incident accused had winked his eye at her so she shouted and disclosed this fact to one woman who then phoned her father. People also gathered there and police also come there. She stated that three to four days prior to that, that man would touch her and followed her. However, she does not identify the accused who was present before the court and specifically stated that the accused who is present before the court was seen by her for the first time and the present accused has not done anything with her. 8. P.W.3 father of the victim has also not supported on the point of identification of the accused. He has denied the suggestion that the present accused had sexually harassed his daughter. 9. Investigating Officer P.W.4 Subhash Gokul Kale has stated what investigation he has done. 10. Considering the evidence on record the court has come to the conclusion that the prosecution could not prove any of the ingredients of offences against accused. The prosecutrix and the father of the prosecutrix have not identified the present accused and they have specifically denied that the present accused had sexually harassed the victim. One independent witness is also not supported on the point of identification of the accused. It appears that informant has compromised with the accused out of the court. 11. Considering the evidence on record the prosecution failed to prove any of the ingredients of the offence and therefore, I answer above points in the negative. Accordingly, I pass following order. ORDER 1. Accused Sureshkumar Lalmani Yadav is acquitted under Section 235(1) of Cr.P.C. of the offence charged under sections 354(D) of Indian Penal Code and Section 11 punishable under section 12 of POCSO Act, 2012. 2. Accused is directed to furnish P.B. and S.B. of Rs.15,000/­ (Rupees Fifteen Thousand Only) to comply provisions of section 437 (A) of Cr. P.C. 3. The Judgment is dictated and pronounced in open Court. Thane. (S.C. Khalipe) Date: 19.09.2017. Additional Sessions Judge,Thane.

.. 1 .. Bail No.2180/2015 Order below Exhibit 1. Order below Exhibit 1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 2180/2015 This application is filed by applicant namely Smt. Chandrika Naresh Panchal for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with C.R.No.II-3116/2015 registered at Vartaknagar police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 4, 5 of Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act (hereinafter in short referred to as ''I.T.P.A.'') and also under section 3, 4, 5, 6 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act (hereinafter in short referred to as P.O.C.S.O. Act). It was contended and argued that the applicants are arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant was conducting prostitution business by procuring girls including minor and was earning livelihood from said business. It is further contended and argued that the place where the police conducted raid is bus stop and a crowded place and there is no lodge nearby where prostitution could be carried out and there is no evidence showing her involvement in the offence and no specific role is assigned to the applicant. It is further contended and argued that the applicant is falsely implicated on the basis of suspicion. It is further contended and argued that the investigation is practically completed in the crime and therefore, there is no need of further custody of the applicant/accused. It is further submitted that the applicant is a woman and is in jail since 20.08.2015. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent residents of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, she will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply as per Exhibit 5 and it was contended and argued that on .. 2 .. Bail No.2180/2015 Order below Exhibit 1. receiving secret information police conducted raid and during said raid it revealed that victim girls including minor girl were being compelled to do prostitution by the applicant/accused. It is further contended and argued that the applicant was were engaged in conducting such illegal activity and was accepting money from the customers in the form of own livelihood. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girls and other prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 4, 5 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and also section 3, 4, 5, 6 of I.T.P.A. and as per prosecution case the accused has compelled victim girls, it is to be mentioned that the applicant has come up with the case that the place where alleged raid was conducted was a crowded place and the illegal activity in question cannot be carried out at such place and the applicant/accused is involved in this crime merely on suspicion and no role is attributed to her in the crime. In such circumstance the aspect as to whether the allegation against the accused is true or whether the defence of accused that she is falsely involved is probable, will have to be decided on merits after trial. 4] Then, the applicant is a woman and is stated to be in jail since 20.08.2015 and investigation may have almost completed by now. 5] Then, it is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail .. 3 .. Bail No.2180/2015 Order below Exhibit 1. and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if she is released on bail. In that respect it is contended by the applicant that she is permanent resident of the address given and she will not abscond if released on bail and that she is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 6] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 7] Then, it has also to be mentioned that the investigation may have almost completed but yet charge-sheet is to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit charge-sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 8] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order - ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Smt. Chandrika Naresh Panchal is released on P.R. bond of Rs.20,000/- [rupees twenty thousand only] with one local surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions - .. 4 .. Bail No.2180/2015 Order below Exhibit 1. The applicant/accused shall attend the concerned police station on every Monday between 10.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon till filing of the charge-sheet and shall co-operate in investigation. She shall not contact the victims in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize victims and prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. She shall not leave India without permission of this Court. She shall furnish proof of her residence. Date : 07.10.2015 (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Additional Session Judge-1, Thane.

Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Mr. R.R.Yadav for the applicant/accused and learned A.P.P. Mrs. R.A.Navale for State. I.O. is absent. Case diary is not produced. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 26.07.2015 at the instance of the informant with an indictment that applicant­ accused kidnapped the victim­girl i.e. daughter of the informant, and committed sexual assault on her. Therefore report was lodged. .. 2 .. Bail No. 2197/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) 4] The learned Counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant­accused is falsely implicated. He submitted that earlier missing report was registered at the instance of father of the victim girl. He submitted that the girl is aged 15 years and she knows the accused. They are having friendship which later on developed in love affair. He submitted that the girl was not kidnapped by the accused but she willingly accompanied the accused. The accused is a young boy of 18 years. He has no criminal antecedents. The investigation is almost completed. The applicant­accused is ready to abide by any stringent conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing him on bail. 5] Per contra, the learned A.P.P. strongly opposed the application submitting that the offence is serious involving victim girl aged 14 years only and her consent is immaterial. The investigation is in progress. There are chances of tampering witnesses and fleeing away from justice and prayed for rejection of application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R. and documents annexed with the application, it appears that the accused is aged aged 18 years. The allegation are that the victim girl aged 14 years was kidnapped by the accused and she was sexually assaulted. The learned counsel for accused produced some letters claiming that same were written by the victim­girl which shows her deep affinity towards the accused. He also produced some call data .. 3 .. Bail No. 2197/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) record of the accused showing that the victim girl frequently called the accused. --1-- ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN CRIMINAL BAIL APPLICATION No.2158/2017 The applicant Jane Alam Mohammad Naseer aged 22 years has applied for bail under section 439 f Cr. P.C. in C.R.No.I­ 65/2017 registered in Kongaon police station for the offence under section 363, 365 of Indian Penal Code and section 3 and 4 of POCSO Act. 2. The applicant was arrested on 01.08.2017 from Lucknow and from 09.02.2017 the applicant was remanded to judicial custody. It is contended that the false case is filed. The victim herself stated in her statement that she is 20 years old. She was run away from Bhiwandi with the accused and reached at Kanpur station and called the present applicant, therefore, offences are not attracted against the accused. As per the school leaving certificate of the prosecutrix her birth date is 05.05.1998. So on the date of incident she was above 18 years. In the medical certificate issued by the Medical Officer, Siddhartha Nagar it is mentioned that she was above 18 years. 3. It is contended that the applicant is already married with the prosecutrix on 15.01.2017 at Arya Samaj Mandir and their marriage registered at Lucknow . The applicant is converted into another religion and thereafter there was physical relation between them. 4. It is submitted that the applicant has fixed residence. He has produced his Adhar card. The custodial interrogation of the applicant is over, therefore, he prayed for bail. 5. The applicant has produced medical papers, Adhar card, marriage certificate, religion conversion certificate. --2-- 6. Investigating Officer given his say at Exh.4. It is contended that the present applicant had kidnapped the minor victim aged 17 years form Bhiwandi and taken to Utter Pradesh Bareli and confined her in one hut and he committed sexual assault with her. The victim is 8 months pregnant because of the sexual assault of the accused. The applicant is of Utter Pradesh so, if released on bail he is likely to jump on bail. 7. I heard Ld. Counsel on behalf of accused and Ld. A.P.P. 8. Considering the facts and circumstances of this case the court is of the view that there are certain mitigating factors on record. I perused the statement of the victim. She has mentioned in her statement that there was love affair between she and present applicant for one and half years. The documents which are produced by the accused i.e. conversion certificate and marriage register certificate shows that the present applicant is already married with the victim and therefore, he has committed sexual intercourse with the victim. This fact is not denied by the accused. So considering the mitigating factors on record the court is of the view that further custody of the present applicant is no more required. It will unjustifiable to keep the applicant behind bard. The applicant is ready to face the trial and abide by the conditions. Hence, I proceed to pass following order. :ORDER: 1. .. 1 .. bail 2108/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 2108 of 2014 This application is filed by applicant Jagdish Solanki for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. I­202/2014 registered at Wage Estate police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 376(1), 328 read with section 34 of I.P.C. and section4, 8 and 17 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant/accused in collusion with co­accused threatened the victim to defame by making her obscene photographs public on internet and then called her at the spot of incident and committed rape on her. It is further contended and argued that no such incident has happened. It is further contended and argued that there is pre­acquaintance between the applicant and victim and they were in regular communication with each other and the applicant is falsely implicated in this crime. It is further submitted that the charge sheet is submitted in court and therefore there is no possibility of applicant causing obstruction in process of investigation. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/ accused is released on bail, he will co­operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that the applicant/ accused threatened the victim to defame her by making public her indecent photographs on internet and via Whatsapp and called near .. 2 .. bail 2108/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) Eternity Mall and took her in one room made of tin. It is further contended and argued that in that room the applicant forced her to drink beer and then had forcible sexual intercourse with her. It is further submitted that the applicant/accused is resident of same locality where the victim is staying and in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl and also the prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offence charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 376(1), 328 read with section 34 of I.P.C. and section 4, 8 and 17 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and allegations are made that the applicant/accused had forcible sexual intercourse with the victim girl and also that he had sent obscene messages etc. it is to be mentioned that it is contended on behalf of applicant/ accused that there was friendship between him and the victim and even it is argued that the call records of both applicant and victim show that they have been in communication with each other frequently and the last call was by the victim herself to the accused. It is also contended that the applicant/accused is falsely implicated in the matter. In such circumstance the aspect whether the allegations in the complaint are true or whether the contentions put forth on behalf applicant/accused are sustainable, would be the question to be decided on merits. .. 3 .. bail 2108/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) 4] It is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence need not be gone into in detail and the only point to be decided is whether the applicant is entitled to be released on bail and in that respect the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence. 5] In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 6] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and the purpose would be served if the applicant is directed to furnish heavy surety and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 7] Then, it has also to be mentioned that though the investigation in the matter is completed and the charge sheet is submitted, it would take time to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period and Even it is also to be mentioned that no criminal antecedents of the applicant/accused are shown. .. 4 .. bail 2108/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) 8] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Jagdish Solanki is released on P.R. bond of Rs.25,000/­ [rupees twenty five thousand only] with one or two sureties in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ He shall not threaten and pressurize the prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 03.12.2014. 1 Order Exh.1 in Cri.Bail Appln. No. 2202/2016 ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN CRI. BAIL APPLICATION NO.2202/2016 Heard Ld. Adv. Mr. Ram Pandey for the applicant. Ld. A.P.P. Mr. Londhe for the State. I.O. present. 1] Applicant who is arrested by Mira­road police station, in Crime No. I­190/2016 for offence U/s. 354(A) and 506 of the I.P.C. and Sec. 8 of the POCSO Act, 2012, has sought his enlargement on bail. 2] It is the prosecution case that on 07/08/2016 at 7.30 p.m. the applicant has called the victim alone to his house on the pretext of explaining something to her during tution, sat on the dining table, insert his hand in the T­shirt of the victim, who is only 12 years, pressed her breast and thus, molested her. The applicant has also threatened the victim not to disclose this to anybody. 3] Ld. Adv. Mr. Pandey has submitted that a compromise has been effected between the victim and the applicant and that he will be filing the consent terms within 2 days. 4] Per contra, Ld. A.P.P. has vehemently opposed the bail application on the ground that the victim is only 12 years old. The applicant called the victim alone to his house, inserted his hand in the T­ shirt of the victim, pressed her breast and thus, molested her when he was alone at home on the pretext of explaining something to her during 2 Order Exh.1 in Cri.Bail Appln. No. 2202/2016 tution when his wife was away. The accused is 40 years old. 5] The practice of trying to compromise POCSO matters is highly deprecated by this court. The offence is serious in nature. The victim is only 12 years old while the accused is 40 years old. He has prima­facie misused the trust reposed in him by the victim and her family. The investigation is in progress and there is every possibility of tampering with the prosecution evidence. In view thereof, I am inclined to reject the bail application. ORDER Bail Application is rejected. Thane. ( Mridula V.K.Bhatia ) Dt:­19/09/2016. Dist. Judge – 08 and Special Judge (POCSO), Thane.

(Presided over by Ms. Mridula V. K. Bhatia, District Judge­08 & Special Judge (POCSO Act), Thane) SPECIAL CASE NO. 89/2013. Exhibit No.135 State of Maharashtra (Through Narpoli Police Station, Dist. Thane, State of Maharashtra) .... Prosecution. V/s. 1] Sushant Ramesh Dubey, Age : 20 years. 2] Mamta Ramesh Dubey, Age : 36 years, Both R/at : Flat No. 107, Samarpan Apartment, Oswalwadi, Anjurphata, Bhiwandi, Dist. Thane. .... Accused. Appearance : Learned D.G.P. Ms. S. E. Phad for the State. Learned Advocate Mr. G. B. Chavan & Mr.Raje Gikwad for both the accused. 2 Spl.Case No.89/2013 Judgment. : JUDGMENT : (Delivered on 17th day of April, 2017) The accused have been prosecuted for the offences Under Sections 376(2)(i) and 506 r/w. Sec. 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Sec. 4 and 17 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (POCSO Act). 2] The case of the prosecution is as follows : (a) The complainant is the mother of the victim. * She is residing with her husband and children including the victim at Ambernath. Her daughter Beena, aged 24 years, was working with the accused in their Motor Training School at Manorama Nagar, Thane since 6 months prior to the incident. (b) Thereafter, after 15 days, the accused No. 2 Mamta Dubey had come to the complainant's house and told that her leg was fractured and a rod was inserted in her leg. Therefore, it is difficult for her to do household work. Accused No.2 Mamta Dubey asked them to send the victim to her house for some days to help her in the household work. She told them that the victim will reside with her in her house. The complainant therefore, sent the victim with Mamta Dubey (accused No.2) to her house at Flat No. 107, Samarpan Apartment, Oswalwadi, Anjurphata, Bhiwandi. * (The name of the victim is not being disclosed in the Judgment with a view to protect her identity as stipulated under Section 228A of the I.P.C.) 3 Spl.Case No.89/2013 Judgment. (c) On 28/07/2013, the complainant went to meet the victim to accused's house at Bhiwandi. At that time, victim told her that the accused No.2 Mamta Dubey got done all the household work from her. She also informed the complainant that 4 months prior, when no one was at home, accused No.1 Sushant raped her and threatened her not to disclose this to anyone. Although the victim informed this to accused No.2 Mamta Dubey, she told her not to disclose this to any one otherwise the victim and her parents will be defamed and nobody will marry her. The victim informed the complainant that accused No.2 Mamta told her that she will get her married to her son Sushant (accused No.1). (d) The accused No.1 Sushant thereafter raped her frequently. The victim again informed about this to accused No.2 Mamta Dubey. Mamta Dubey threatened the victim to kill her and her parents and told her to keep such relations with her son Sushant (accused No.2). The victim informed all this to her mother (complainant) on her visit to accused's house. The complainant, therefore, went to the police station and lodged complaint against both the accused. 3] The police registered crime vide C.R.No. I­254/2013 against the accused for offences under Sections 376 (2)(i) and 506 r/w. Sec. 34 of the Indian Penal Code and Secs. 3, 4, 7 and 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. F.I.R./complaint (Exh. 29) was registered at the Police Station on 4 Spl.Case No.89/2013 Judgment. 28/07/2013. 4] As the offence is exclusively triable by the Court of Sessions, the case came to be committed to this Court u/s. 209 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Cr.P.C.). 5] Charge (Exh. 16) was framed by my learned Predecessor against the accused for the offences punishable under sections 376(2)(i) and 506 r/w. Sec. 34 of the Indian Penal Code and Secs. 4 and 17 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. It was read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. The accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 6] At the trial, to bring home the guilt of the accused, the prosecution examined in all 8 witnesses, viz., Reshma Harikant Shukla (P.W.1) (the complainant and mother of the victim), the victim (P.W.2), Jaymala Jayant Vasave (P.W.3) A.P.I., who came to record the statement of the victim, Dr. Dattatray Vishnu Kulkarni (P.W.4), who conducted ossification test of the victim, Dr. Sai Sharad Jadhav (P.W.5), who recorded the victim's statement, Mrs. Pushpa Gautam (P.W.6), Head Mistress of the school, Dr. Amol Prabhakar Bedkar (P.W.7), Medical Officer of IGM Hospital, Bhiwandi and Sanjay Pandharinath Satav (P.W.8), an Investigating Officer. 7] After the prosecution closed it's evidence the statement 5 Spl.Case No.89/2013 Judgment. of the accused under section 313 of Cr.P.C. came to be recorded. The accused examined one witness Rajesh Shukla ,Gram Vikas Adhikari, Bhogwara,Dist.Allahabad to show that the victim was not a minor at the time of commission of the offence. The defence of the accused during deposition and while recording statement U/s. 313 Cr.P.C. is that the case is false. If they would have committed this offence, then the father of the victim would not have visit Sushant Dubey in the jail on 4 occasions. Sonam Mishra and Meena Dubey both sisters of the victim merely want and they have all conspired to extract money from them and filed a false case against them. However, later on when the I.O. collected his certificate from the school, it was revealed that he was a major and accordingly he came to be arrested. It is a part of record that the accused have tried their best to subvert the judicial process in various ways. They have also misused the bail granted to them and were absconding for a considerable period of time and were arrested and brought by the police. The minimum sentence prescribed under Sec. 376(2)(i) of the I.P.C. and Section 4, 17 of the POCSO Act, 2012 is 10 years Rigorous Imprisonment which may extend upto life imprisonment. The punishment for aiding/abetting an offence U/Sec.17 of the P.O.C.S.O. Act is equivalent to the punishment provided for that offence. It has also to be considered that the offence of sexual assault was committed more than once upon the victim who was a child and was living in the same household as the accused. An offence like rape has 89 Spl.Case No.89/2013 Judgment. serious repercussions on the psychological well­being of the victim. 95] Ld.Adv.for the accused has submitted that it has already come on record that the accused are financially well­to­do and have their own house and two driving schools. It has also come on record that they have all the white goods in their house like T.V., A.C. and fridge. He has therefore not filed any affidavit disclosing their assets. He has submitted that the compensation amount be awarded accordingly. 96] It has come on record that the victim has left her studies after 7th standard. I am therefore of the opinion that the compensation amount should be utilized by her for further studies or for obtaining vocational training of her choice, so that she becomes self­reliant. Considering the seriousness of the offence and the overall facts and circumstances of the case, the following sentence would meet the ends of justice: ORDER 1] The accused No.1 Sushant Ramesh Dubey is hereby convicted vide Sec. 235(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure Code for the offence punishable Under Secs. 376(2)(i) and 506 r/w. Sec. 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Sec. 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (POCSO Act). 90 Spl.Case No.89/2013 Judgment. 2] The accused No.2 Mamta Ramesh Dubey is hereby convicted vide Sec. 235(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure Code punishable U/Sec.17 of the P.O.C.S.O.Act ,for intentionally aiding/abetting the commission of the offences punishable U/Sec. 376(2)(i) of I.P.C. and U/Sec.4 of P.O.C.S.O. Act by accused No.1 Sushant Ramesh Dubey upon the victim and also the offence punishable Under Secs. 506 r/w. Sec. 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 . 3] The accused No.1 Sushant Ramesh Dubey is sentenced to undergo Rigorous Imprisonment for 15 years for the offence punishable U/s. 376(2)(i) of the Indian Penal Code along with fine of ₹ 1,000/­. In default of payment of said fine, the accused to undergo further Rigorous Imprisonment of 15 days. He is also sentenced to undergo Rigorous Imprisonment for 15 years for the offence punishable U/s. 4 of the P.O.C.S.O.Act along with fine of ₹ 1,000/­. In default of payment of said fine, the accused to undergo further Rigorous Imprisonment of 15 days. 4] Both the sentences shall run concurrently. 5] The accused No.2 Mamta Ramesh Dubey is sentenced to undergo Rigorous Imprisonment for 10 years for the offence punishable U/s. 17 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. along with fine of ₹ 1,000/­. 1 Order Exh.1 in Cri.Bail Appln. No. 2217/16 ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN CRI. BAIL APPLICATION NO.2217/2016 Heard Ld. Adv. Mr. D.S.Patekar for the applicant. Ld. A.P.P. Mrs. Jadhav for the State. I.O. present. 1] Applicant who is arrested by Rabale police station in Crime No. I­225/2016 for offence U/s. 3, 4, 5(d)(1) of the PITA and Sec. 11(2) and 12 of the POCSO Act, 2012, has sought her enlargement on bail. 2] It is the case of the prosecution that the applicant has forced and induced a minor girl and a lady for prostitution and earned money from the same for her livelihood. 3] Ld. Advocate for the applicant has submitted that the applicant was arrested 80 days prior and that the applicant is ready to abide by any terms and conditions. 4] Per contra, Ld. A.P.P. has vehemently opposed the bail application on the ground that the applicant had taken a house on rent in Airoli and in the raid conducted by police pursuant to the information received by them, the applicant was caught red­handed by the police at the spot. The currency notes given by the bogus customer were recovered from her. One major and one mior girl aged 15 years were also rescued from the spot. 5] In the Judgment dated 30/10/2015 passed by the Hon'ble Bombay High Court in Criminal P.I.L. No. 4/2015 (Freedom Firm V/s. 2 Order Exh.1 in Cri.Bail Appln. No. 2217/16 Commissioner of Police, Pune & Ors.), guidelines have been laid down for judicial officers while dealing with the cases of human trafficking. In the said guidelines, it has been interalia laid down in para 28 that “the court would, as a general principle, refuse bail to an accused who is shown as a trafficker in human beings as such accused pursues a career in such crime, which is prone to repetition, which is expected to have antecedents and which is generally indisposed to intimidation and threats. The Court would certainly release on bail such of the accused or co­accused as are themselves not traffickers but may be shown to have played some minor role in the commission of the offence”. 6] In the present case, the role of the applicant in trafficking girls including minors has clearly emerged. Therefore, in view of the ratio decidendi and the guidelines laid down in the case of Freedom Firm (supra), this is not at all a fit case for granting bail. In view thereof, I am inclined to reject the application. ORDER Bail Application is rejected. Thane. ( Mridula V.K.Bhatia ) Dt:­05/10/2016. Dist. Judge – 08 and Special Judge (POCSO), Thane.

The case of the prosecution is that on 20.05.2017 at about 8.30 to 9.00 p.m., at Sector­16, in K type Building No.4, on first floor, Vashi accused lured the the five years old girl for goving chocolate and took her in adjacent building and said JUDGMENT 2 Spl. case No. 184/2017 CNR NO. MHTH01­005996­2017 that he will show her magic. Then he inserted his penis into her mouth. 2. The mother of the victim lodged FIR in Navi Mumbai Vashi police station. C.R.No.207/2017 was registered on 31.0.5.2017. A.P.I. R.P. Gunjal done the investigation. He recorded statements of witnesses. He sent victim for medical examination and he recorded statement of victim and sent her for recording statement under section 164 of Cr.P.C to the JMFC. He arrived at conclusion that accused had committed offence. Therefore, he sent charge­sheet against him under section 377 of IPC and section 4 of POCSO Act, 2012. 3. Charge is framed against accused under section 377 of Indian Penal Code and Section 4 of POCSO Act, 2012. He pleaded not guilty. 4. Following points arose for my determination. I have given its findings with the reasons, as under :­ Sr.No. Points Findings 1. Does prosecution prove that on 20.05.2016 at about 8.30 to 9.00 p.m. at Building NO.4, Sector­16, Vashi In the negative. accused committed unnatural sex with the victim aged 5 years by inserting his penis into her mouth and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 377 of Indian Penal Code? 2. Does prosecution prove that on the In the negative. aforesaid date, time and place, accused committed penetrative sexual assault upon minor victim aged 5 years by penetrating his penis into her JUDGMENT 3 Spl. case No. 184/2017 CNR NO. MHTH01­005996­2017 mouth and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 4 of POCSO Act, 2012? 3. What order? As per final order. :REASONS: As to Point No.1 to 3 :­ 5. To prove the offence prosecution has examined four witnesses. Victim at Exh.12 and mother of victim at Exh.13, P.W.3 API Sudhir Samadhan Wagh examined at Exh.19, P.W.4 Rajendra Pandharinath Gunjal API of Vashi police station is examined at Exh.22. 6. As per the evidence of victim when she was playing infront of her house with Nirja and Tinu one man took her in the building on first floor. He tied strip of cloth upon her eyes. Then he said that he will do magic with finer and he inserted fingers into her mouth. After removing strip on her eyes she saw that man. She stated that she cannot identify that man, if shown to her. Accused shown to the victim, but she did not identify him. 7. The victim's mother stated that the victim girl is 6 years old. She lodged FIR. She stated that on 20.05.2017 her daughter went for playing at 8.30 p.m. then her daughter's friend Vanashree told her that victim gone with one 'dada'. But Vanashree did not tell who was that 'dada' because she did not saw that man. Then her daughter told her that one 'dada' took her in one building and tied strip of cloth on her eyes and said JUDGMENT 4 Spl. case No. 184/2017 CNR NO. MHTH01­005996­2017 that he will give her lollipop and he did magic with finger. Then that man left her below the building. Thereafter the mother of the victim saw that building. 8. P.W.2 further stated that there was no CCTV camera in that building, where the incident took place but there is CCTV camera in their building. As per that CCTV footage it was seen that her daughter is going behind one boy, but the face of that man was not seen in that footage. Then on 30.05.2012 people in that area took the accused in the police station and police told her that this is the boy. Therefore, she lodged complaint vide Exh.15. She stated that she cannot tell definitely that the accused before the court is same, who had taken her daughter in the building. She admitted in her cross­ examination that the incident took place on 20.05.2017 but till 31.05.2017 she did not lodge report to the police. She admitted that in her statement before the police she has not mentioned that the man had tied strip of cloth upon the eyes of her daughter. 9. Investigating Officer P.W.3 Sudhir Wagh has stated that he arrested accused and prepared arrest panchanama vide Exh.20. He also prepared panchanama of the spot vide Exh.21. He admitted that there is delay of 11 days for filing FIR and he has not recorded statement of victim. He stated that the accused was arrested in the police station. He stated that he has not seen CCTV footage. He admitted that he has not taken information from any flat owners. JUDGMENT 5 Spl. case No. 184/2017 CNR NO. MHTH01­005996­2017 10. P.W.4 Rajendra Pandharinath Gunjal has stated that he sent victim and accused for medical examination and statement of victim was recorded in presence of WPSI. He took CCTV footage in the pen drive. He sent samples to FSL Kalina. 11. In his cross examination P.W.4 admitted that the victim had gone for playing with Vanashree aged 8 years and only Vanashree was accompanied with the victim at that time, but he has not recorded statement of Vanashree. He stated that he has not sent CCTV footage to FSL. He has not sent the photographs of the accused to FSL. 12. I heard Ld Counsel on behalf of accused and Ld. APP. 13. From the evidence on record it has come on record that the victim has not identified accused before the court and victim has not stated that accused had done any penetrative sexual assault upon her. She has no where stated that accused had inserted penis into her mouth. Her mother was also not identified accused and victim had not reported her mother that accused had inserted penis into her mouth. 14. It appears that some people at that area had brought accused in the police station and after that FIR came to be recorded on 30.05.2012. There is delay of 11 days for lodging FIR. There is no explanation given. It appears that people brought the accused to the police station on believing that this is the same person and FIR was given against the accused. But in CCTV footage which the informant had seen was not clearly made out that accused was the person who was taking her daughter into the building. The face of the accused was not JUDGMENT 6 Spl. case No. 184/2017 CNR NO. MHTH01­005996­2017 seen in that footage which was seen by the informant only back side was seen. I.O has admitted that he has not taken photograph of the accused and they were not sent to FSL Kalina to verify the CCTV footage and photograph of the accused whether it is of the same person. Therefore, informant did not identify accused before the court. She stated that she cannot definitely say that accused before the court is the same person who had taken her daughter in the building. She had also improved in her statement that the man had tied the strip upon her daughter which is not mentioned in her previous statement before the police station. 15. I.O P.W.3 stated that he had not seen that CCTV footage it means that he has also not verified CCTV footage and whether accused had seen in that footage while taking the victim. So prosecution could not prove that accused is the same person, who had taken daughter of the informant at another building for the purpose of committing offence. The prosecution also not proved that accused had committed penetrative sexual assault by inserting his penis into her mouth. The victim and her mother has not supported on this point, therefore, ingredients of the offence under section 377 of IPC and section 4 of POCSO Act are not at all proved by the prosecution. The identity of the accused is also not proved by the prosecution and therefore, I come to the conclusion that no offence is proved against accused, therefore, he is liable to be acquitted. Hence I answered points in the negative and pass following order. JUDGMENT 7 Spl. case No. 184/2017 CNR NO. P.C. 3] Accused be released forth with if not require any other case. 4] Issue letter to the jail authority. 5] The Judgment is dictated and pronounced in open Court. Thane. ( S.C. Khalipe ) Date: 05/07/2018. Additional Sessions Judge,Thane.

.. 1 .. Bail No. 2250/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) Criminal Bail Application No.2250/2015. Chedilal Ramlal Gupta .. Applicant versus The State of Maharashtra Through Vashi Police Station .. Non­applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 By this application the applicant is seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. who was arrested on 21.07.2015 by Vashi Police Station in connection with C.R.No.I­334/2015 registered for an offence punishable under section 376(2)(i) of I.P. Code and section 5(l)(n) of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as P.O.C.S.O. Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Ms. Sarita Gaikwad for the applicant/accused and learned A.P.P. Mr. Pujari for State. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 20.07.2015 at the instance of the informant with an indictment that the accused who is father of the victim­girl has been committing penetrative sexual assault on her since 6 to 7 years before lodging of F.I.R. and her mother was giving her some tablets to eat. Hence, F.I.R. was lodged. .. 2 .. Bail No. 2250/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) 4] The learned Counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicants­accused is falsely implicated. He submitted that form the contents of F.I.R. it appears that the informant learnt about the incident a month prior to lodging of the F.I.R. and the delay of one month has not been explained. He submitted that the victim­girl has not disclosed the incident for about 6 to 7 years cannot be believed. The applicant is the only earning member of the family and is a patient of diabetes. The investigation is completed and charge­sheet is filed. The applicant­accused is ready to abide any stringent conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing him on bail. 5] Per contra, the learned A.P.P. opposed the application submitting that the offence is serious. She submitted that the applicant­accused is father of the victim­girl and he committed heinous offence for about 6 to 7 years. As the applicant­accused is the father of the victim­girl, there are chances of pressurizing the victim­girl and prayed for rejection of application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R., it appears that the F.I.R. came to be lodged at the instance of the social worker working with an N.G.O. Chetana Foundation. F.I.R. discloses that when the informant had been to the school at Vashi to address a lecture on 'mental health' at that time she noticed that one girl is staring at her and found under pressure. When the girl was inquired by taking her in confidence, she disclosed that since she was of six years, her father has repeatedly committed sexual .. 3 .. Bail No. 2250/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) assault on her and her mother is well aware about that and she used to administer her some pills. Thereafter, the F.I.R. was lodged. The statement of the victim­girl was recorded in presence of social worker wherein she disclosed the entire incident and narrated her ordeal. The medical certificate of the victim­girl also supports the case of prosecution. The minor girl is repeatedly subjected to sexual assault by the applicant­accused who is none other than the father of the victim­girl. Even the mother of the victim­girl did not help her though knowing about the alleged offence. The accused is involved in a serious and heinous offence. There is prima facie case against the accused. Further, the apprehension of the learned A.P.P. about the tampering of witnesses is well founded. Hence, no case is made out for releasing the applicant­accused on bail. I, therefore, pass the following order ­ ORDER The application stands rejected. Thane. Date : 04.11.2015. (Ms. U.M. Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act), Thane.
