IN THE COURT OF THE SPECIAL JUDGE(P.O.C.S.O.Act), THANE. (Presided over by Ms.U.M.Nandeshwar, District Judge­1 & Addl. Sessions Judge, Thane) SPECIAL CASE No. 90 of 2013 Exhibit No.53. The State of Maharashtra Through Srinagar Police Station Thane, District – Thane. ... Prosecution VERSUS Vicky Raju Doiphode Age 24 years, Residence –Satyamevjayte Rahiwasi Sangh chawl, Ambedkar chowk, Rupadevi pada No.2, Indiranagar, Wagle Estate, Thane. ... Accused Offence punishable under section 451, 354­A, 354­B & 323 of Indian Penal Code and under section 7 & 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Appearance ­ Spl.P.P. Mrs. R.A. Navale, for the State. Advocate Mr. S.T.Waghmare, for the accused. 2 Special Case No.90/2013 (Judgment) JUDGMENT (Delivered on 12th April, 2016.) 1] The Accused stands prosecuted for the offence punishable under section 451, 354(A), 354(B) & 323 of Indian Penal Code and also under section 7 & 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act) for committing sexual assault on minor victim­ girl aged about 13 years. 2] Shorn of verbiage, the indictment against the Accused are as under ­ [i] Informant Sau.Meeta Ramsagawat Bind is resident of Indira Nagar, Valmiki pada, Thane. She is staying there with her husband Ramsagawat (P.W.2) and six daughters including victim­girl (P.W.1) aged about 13 years. [ii] On 03/08/2013 around 11.00 p.m. informant and her family went to sleep after dinner. Informant Meeta, her husband (P.W.2) and two youngest daughters were sleeping on mezzanine floor (potmala) and her other four daughters including victim­girl (P.W.1) were sleeping on ground floor. Around 02.00 a.m. informant heard scream of her daughter, therefore, she woke up her husband (P.W.2) and went downstairs. There they had seen accused Vicky Raju Doiphode ran away from there by opening the door. On asking victim­ girl(P.W.1) disclosed that accused untied her string of Salwar 3 Special Case No.90/2013 (Judgment) and touched her breast inappropriately. Informant and her husband searched accused outside the house and when they were about to caught hold accused, he pushed them and during the scuffle due to fall accused received injuries on his face. Informant called help of neighbourers by shouting 'chor, chor'. Therefore, neighbourers gathered there, but accused ran away from there. Therefore, informant/mother if victim­girl immediately lodged report against accused on 04/08/2013 around 04.45 a.m. 3] On her report F.I.R. was registered against the Accused vide C.R.No.I­186/2013 for the offence punishable under section 451, 354(A), 354(B) & 323 of I.P.C. and under section 7 and 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act by PHC Dinesh Vishnu Chavan(P.W.3). Police Hawaldar Dumbre (P.W.5) arrested the accused (Exh.39). P.W.5 visited the spot and drawn spot panchnama (Exh.43). API Barve (P.W.6) recorded the statements of witnesses as per their say. On 05/08/2013 accused was sent for medical examination and his medical certificate was collected. Informant and her husband were also sent for medical examination and their medical certificates were collected. Thereafter, investigation culminated into filing of charge­sheet in this Court being the Special designated court under P.O.C.S.O. Act. 4 Special Case No.90/2013 (Judgment) 4] The charge (Exh.15) against the Accused was framed for offence punishable under section 451, 354(A), 354(B) & 323 of Indian Penal Code and also under section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. The Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial (Exh.16). The Accused took defence of total denial. 5] In response to application under section 294 of Cr.P.C. the defence has admitted [1] Arrest Form of accused (Exh.39), [2] Medical Certificate of Minta Bind­informant (Exh.32), [3] Medical certificate of Ramsagawat Bind (P.W.2) (Exh.33), [4] Report­Card of victim­girl (P.W.1) issued by Dnyanodaya Vidya Mandir(Exh.41) and [5] Medical certificate of Accused issued by V. S. General Hospital (Exh.40 & 44). 6] In order to prove guilt of Accused Prosecution has examined following witnesses ­ P.W.1 Victim­girl Exh.26 P.W.2 Ramsagawn Dhaneshar Bind Exh.27 (Father of Victim­girl) P.W.3 Police Head Constable Dinesh Exh.26 Vishny Chavan (who recorded the report/F.I.R.) P.W.4 Nandkishor Sakharam Jadhav Exh.36 (Panch on spot panchnama.) P.W.5 Police Hawaldar Tukaram Natahji Exh. 42 Dumbre (Investigating officer) P.W.6 A.P.I. Shaberao Pandurang Barve Exh.48 (Investigating officer). 5 Special Case No.90/2013 (Judgment) 7] The prosecution proved and relied on the following documents ­ Report & F.I.R. Exhibit 29 & 30 Spot Panchnama Exhibit 43 Copy of Covering letter for Exhibit 49 medical examination 8] The prosecution closed its side of evidence by filing Pursis at Exhibit­50. The incriminating evidence came on record against the Accused was read over and explained to him and his statement under Section 313(b) of Cr.P.C. was recorded. Accused neither examined himself nor examined any witness in his defence. 9] Heard learned Spl.P.P. Mrs. R. A. Navale for State and the learned advocate Mr. S. T. Waghmare for Accused at length. 10] On consideration of argument advanced on behalf of both the sides and on perusal of the oral & documentary evidence on record, following points arise for my determination, which are answered with the findings thereon, as under :­ Sr. Points Findings No. 1] Does the prosecution prove that on 04/08/2013 at 04.45 hrs. at the 6 Special Case No.90/2013 (Judgment) residence of informant accused committed house trespass by entering into the dwelling house of informant ..No. in order to commit the offence of outraging modesty of minor victim­ girl aged about 10 years and he thereby committed an offence punishable under section 451 of Indian Penal Code ? 2] Does the prosecution prove that during same period accused committed sexual harassment to the minor victim­girl by touching her ..No. breast inappropriately and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 354(A) of Indian Penal Code? 3] Does the prosecution prove that during same period accused used criminal force to the minor victim­girl aged about 10 years, by trying to ..No. disrobe her and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 354(B) of Indian Penal Code? 4] Does the prosecution prove that during same period accused voluntarily caused hurt to the informant, her husband and victim­ ..No. girl aged about 10 years and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 323 of Indian Penal Code? 7 Special Case No.90/2013 (Judgment) 5] Does the prosecution prove that during same period the Accused committed sexual assault on the said minor girl by touching her breast inappropriately and by trying to ..No. disrobe her and he thereby committed an offence defined under section 7 and punishable under section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, 2012 ? 6] What order ? Accused is acquitted. REASONS As to Point No. 1 to 5 : 11] All the points are taken up together for discussion, to avoid the repetition, as evidence about the same in common and inter­connected. Age of victim­girl : 12] As the Accused is facing charge under P.O.C.S.O. Act, therefore, it is incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that the victim­girl was child (minor) at the time of incident. The alleged incident took place on 04/08/2013. Victim­girl (P.W.1) and her father (P.W.2) did not state her date of birth. However, victim­girl (P.W.1) and her father (P.W.2) deposed that incident took place on 03/08/2013 and at that time she was studying in 5th std. The age of the victim­ 8 Special Case No.90/2013 (Judgment) girl is not seriously challenged by the defence. On the other hand, the defence admitted the report­card of the victim­girl of the academic year­ 2012­2013, wherein her date of birth is mentioned as 15/12/2003. According to the said date of birth, on the date of incident i.e. in the intervening night of 03/08/2013 to 04/08/2013, the victim­girl was aged about 9 years and 8 months. Thus, the prosecution proved that at the time of incident, the victim­girl was minor aged about 10 years i.e. below the age of 18 years and she was a “child” as per definition given in Section 2(d) of P.O.C.S.O. Act. 13] Further, as the Accused is facing charge under section 354­A & 354­B of I.P.C. it is incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that Accused either committed any act of physical contact and advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures or assaults or used criminal force towards victim­girl with an intention to disrobe her and to outrage her modesty or knowing it to be likely that he will, by his act, outrage the modesty of the victim­girl. So also as the Accused is facing charge under section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, therefore, it is further incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that the Accused with sexual intent touched the vagina, penis, anus, breast of a child or make the child touched vagina, penis, anus, breast of such person or any other person or does any other act with sexual intent which involves physical contact without penetration and by his such act committed 9 Special Case No.90/2013 (Judgment) sexual assault as defined in section 7 of the P.O.C.SO. Act. 14] To prove the charge against the Accused the prosecution has examined the victim­girl (P.W.1) and father of victim­girl (P.W.2) who are the most material witnesses to prove the charge against the Accused. It is material to note that the prosecution failed to examine informant who is the mother of victim­girl and who set the law in motion by lodging F.I.R., with the reason that the informant is carrying pregnancy of 9 months and therefore, she is unable to attend the court. Therefore, to prove the F.I.R. prosecution has examined Police Head Constable Dinesh Chavan (P.W.3) who recorded the report lodged by the informant which is at Exh.29. 15] The evidence of victim­girl (P.W.1) eloquent that on 03/08/2013 she alongwith her three sisters was sleeping in her house and her father, mother and other two sisters were sleeping at mezzanine floor. In the midnight at around 02.00 a.m. Vicky (Accused) entered in her house from the window and untied the string of her salwar. Therefore, she woke­up. She tried to raise shout by calling her mother. At that time accused gagged her mouth but her sister wakeup and raised shouts, and their mother and father came downstairs and by seeing them accused ran away. It is material to mention that the father of victim­girl Ramsagawat Bind (P.W.2) also deposed on the same line and corroborates the version of 10 Special Case No.90/2013 (Judgment) victim­girl (P.W.1). Thus, in short, it is the case of prosecution that in the intervening night of 03/08/2013 to 04/08/2013 in the midnight around 02.00 a.m. accused entered from the window which was not having grill and untied the string of salwar of the victim­girl and touched her breast inappropriately. However, it is pertinent to note that the victim­girl only deposed about untying the string of salwar, while her father (P.W.2) deposed about untying of string of salwar as well as touching her breast inappropriately by the accused. 16] In this respect, the learned Defence Counsel most vehemently argued that the window from where prosecution claims that accused entered in the house of victim­girl, is at the height of 7 to 8 feet from ground and it is not possible to enter from the said window. He further argued that it is unbelievable that the parents of such young girls kept open the window, which do not have the grill. In this respect, the spot panchnama is the most material piece of evidence and similarly, the testimony of the panchas also carries weight­age. However, one of the panchas to the spot panchnama i.e. one Nandkishor Jadhav who is examined as P.W.4 did not support the case of prosecution and nothing material was elicited from the cross­examination conducted by learned Spl.P.P. Therefore, to prove the spot panchnama, the prosecution has examined Police Hawaldar Tukaram Dumbre (P.W.5) who 11 Special Case No.90/2013 (Judgment) carried out some part of the investigation after registration of the offence. 17] Police Hawaldar Dumbre (P.W.5) deposed that he took search of the accused, but he was not found at his home and around 6 a.m. when Accused found, he was arrested by drawing arrest panchnama which is at Exh.39. Dumbre (P.W.5) further deposed that on 04/08/2013 he visited the scene of offence i.e. the house of informant at Indira Nagar zopadpatti, Rupadevi Pada No.2. P.W.5 further deposed that the house was of load bearing having mezzanine floor and there was window towards West side. Accordingly, the spot panchnama was drawn in presence of panchas which is at Exh.43. However, it is significant to note that P.W.5 could not state at what height the window is. Further P.W.6 PSI Barve who is one of the investigating officers, though deposed that he had visited the scene of offence and seen the window from outside, however, he categorically admitted that he did not take measurement of the height of window from outside and even unable to state the approximate height of the window. P.W.6 even did not deny that it is at the height of 8 feet from the floor. 18] In this respect, the another significant factor is that Police Hawaldar Dumbre (P.W.5) investigating officer, in his examination­in­chief deposed that on Western side of the 12 Special Case No.90/2013 (Judgment) house there is window without grill on mezzanine floor. Further P.W.5 did not find it necessary to draw a sketch map of the scene of offence. Further, in this background, if the spot panchnama which is at Exh.43 have been seen carefully, then there is no mention about the window without grill and on which side it is and at what height it is. While in Exh.43 it has been narrated the story stated by the victim­girl that from open window accused entered in the house and further story of prosecution. But the spot­panchnama is silent about the material thing i.e. window from where allegedly accused entered in the house of informant. 19] Thus, the contrary evidence of the investigating officer i.e. P.W.5 & 6 creates a considerable doubt about the height of the window from the ground and even its direction. Further if the evidence of P.W.5 about having the window on the mezzanine floor is believed for sake of argument, then it almost washed out the case of the prosecution. As per victim­ girl (P.W.1) and her father (P.W.2), P.W.2 along with his wife/informant and two daughters were sleeping on the mezzanine floor, then if the case of prosecution is believed, then accused might have first be at mezzanine floor where informant with her husband were sleeping and they did not even notice about entering of the accused in the house. Further when there is no clear evidence about the height of the window from the floor, then it is hard to believe that accused 13 Special Case No.90/2013 (Judgment) could have managed to entered easily from the window. 20] It is specific defence of the accused that prior to two days of the incident, the father of victim­girl Ramsagawat (P.W.2) had quarreled with him for reason of liquor and on the day of incident, Ramsagawat (P.W.2) with the help of his neighbourers, assaulted him (accused) and implicated him in the false case. It is his further defence that accused himself approached police station prior in time and complained against Ramsagawat (P.W.2) and his wife and neighbourer. However, his report was not taken down and he was sent for medical examination and by that time, the false report of the informant was registered. 21] In this respect, it is significant to note that accused took said defence since the beginning of trial. Further it is pertinent to note that, P.S.I. Barve (P.W.6) who investigated the matter, admitted that accused was sent for medical examination on 04/08/2013 and in the medical certificate (Exh.40), it is mentioned that accused received injury by blunt object. However, P.S.I. Barve (P.W.6) did not inquire with the accused about the injury. Though, it is the case of prosecution that informant­Meeta and Ramsagawat (P.W.2) received injuries due to the assault of the accused, however, P.W.2 did not utter a single word about any assault caused by the accused or receiving of any injury. 14 Special Case No.90/2013 (Judgment) 22] Upon perusal of medical certificate of the accused (Exh.40), it discerns that accused was sent for medical examination with MLC No.15822 to V. S. General Hospital on 04/08/2013 at 04.50 p.m. and Dr. Deshmukh examined him. While the report (Exh.29) is recorded on 04/08/2013 at 04.45 hours which also support the defence that he at first point of time, had been to the police station and was sent to medical examination and during that period the report of the informant was registered. 23] In the medical certificate of Accused which is at Exh.40 the alleged history of assault by unknown persons at 02.30 a.m. at Indiranagar by hand, stick etc is mentioned and it is also mentioned that the patient is under alcohole influence. Further, blunt trauma to head, neck, chest and back is shown with the history of bleeding from mouth and vomiting is stated. In this respect, it is further material to note that the accused was arrested in the present case on 04/08/2013 and the arrest and personal search panchnama is at Exh.39 which appears to be commenced at 07.45 a.m. and concluded at 08.20 p.m. Exh.39 thus, fully supports the version and defence taken by the accused that he had been to the police station with the complaint of assault by P.W.2 and his neighbourers, however, instead of taking his complaint, he was sent to medical examination and then the report of the informant was taken down. 15 Special Case No.90/2013 (Judgment) 24] If as per Arrest panchnama (Exh.39) the accused was arrested around 07.45 a.m., then it is highly impossible that he was sent for medical examination in due course of investigation before arrest of accused with MLC No.15822. In fact Accused was sent for medical examination after his arrest with MLC No. 15905 and that another medical certificate of the accused which is at Exh.44 and he was examined by Dr. Trupti on 05/08/2013 with the history of assault by public on 03/08/2013 at Indiranagar. In the said certificate also abrasion on the backside were shown with the complaint of pain at chest region. Thus, it appears that the accused was sent for medical examination during investigation with MLC No.15905 which is at Exh.44. 25] Further when accused has received any injury in the course of same transaction, it is for the prosecution to explain the said injuries. However, in the present case, prosecution failed to give any explanation about the injuries received by the accused, particularly when the accused came with the specific defence that he was beaten up by P.W.2 Ramsagwat Bind, his wife and his neighbourers. Thus, there found substance in the submission of learned defence counsel that when accused was sent for medical examination, during that intervening period, informant and her husband (P.W.2) with the fear that case may be registered against them, cooked false story and lodged false report against the accused. 16 Special Case No.90/2013 (Judgment) 26] Further although, there are specific allegations and charge against the accused about disrobing the victim­girl for untying string of her salwar, the cloths of victim­girl were not seized and therefore, there is no supportive evidence to show that any such attempt was made to disrobe the victim­girl. Even in this respect, the submissions of learned defence counsel that when the victim­girl is minor aged below 10 years, in normal course, it is not expected that such a small child would wear salwar suit, that too during the night time. 27] Thus, if overall circumstances of the case have been considered and the documentary evidence on record have been perused, the testimony of the victim­girl (P.W.1) and her father Ramsagawat (P.W.2) is not believable. Further there is contradictory testimony of P.W.1 and P.W.2 in respect of searching and caught holding the accused. Ramsagawat (P.W.2) deposed that when victim­girl disclosed the incident, thereafter, they took search of accused and he found outside their house and he caught hold him by raising shouts as 'chor, chor' however, accused pushed them and ran away and they had been to the police station to lodge the report. While victim­girl (P.W.1) deposed that when she narrated the incident to her mother (informant) thereafter, her mother and father tried to chase the accused, but he ran away. She further deposed that therefore, her parents returned home and 17 Special Case No.90/2013 (Judgment) accused again came in front of their house and then her parents caught hold accused and accused pushed her parents and he fell down. Therefore, her parents shouted and neighbourers gathered there and accused ran away. The testimony of victim­girl shows that the accused had been in front of her house twice while her father deposed about caught holding the accused immediately after the incident. Thus, the contradictions in the evidence of material witnesses is not minor as per submissions of learned Spl. P.P. but which goes to root of the matter which create room for suspicion about the actual happening of the incident as claimed by the prosecution and therefore, the contradictions are in fact, fatal to the prosecution. 28] No doubt, there is a presumption under section 29 and 30 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, still in that circumstances, it is for the prosecution to prove the case against the accused and then only, the presumption as to certain offences and of culpable mental state as per provisions of section 29 and 30 of P.O.C.S.O. Act would arise. However, in the backdrop of above discussion, prosecution failed to prove that accused entered from the window in the house of informant and by disrobing the victim­girl outraged her modesty or caused hurt to any of the prosecution witnesses. Therefore, the presumption would not arise in favour of the prosecution. 18 Special Case No.90/2013 (Judgment) 29] Thus, prosecution failed to prove the charge against the accused beyond reasonable doubt, about committing house tress­pass by entering in the dwelling house of informant in order to commit offence of outraging modesty of victim­girl and by physical contact and advance involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overture and that using criminal force to disrobe the victim­girl, the accused had committed any offence of such nature. Further prosecution failed to prove that the accused caused hurt to the victim­girl or the prosecution witnesses and committed sexual assault on the minor victim­girl. Hence, I answer point No.1 to 5 in negative and accused is entitled for acquittal. 30] In the result, I proceed to pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused Vicky Raju Doiphode is hereby acquitted U/Sec. 235(1) of Cr.P.C. for the offence punishable U/Sec.451, 354­A, 354­B & 323 of Indian Penal Code and U/s. 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] The accused is in jail and he shall be released forthwith if not required in any other case. 19 Special Case No.90/2013 (Judgment) 3] The Accused is directed to furnish bail bond of the amount of ₹15,000/­ with one solvent surety in the like amount in compliance of provision of section 437­A of Cr.P.C. The judgment is dictated and pronounced in open Court. Date : 12/04/2016. (Ms. U. M. Nandeshwar), Thane Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act),Thane. District Judge ­1 and Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

Offence Punishable Under Sec.354, 506 of IPC and S.8,10 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ Appearances : Shri. Londhe, Ld. Spl.P.P. for the State Mr. Iqbal Abdulla, Ld.Advocate for the accused ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ CNR No. MHTH01-006006-2015 2 Special Case No.205/2015 (Judgment) :JUDGMENT: (Delivered on 01st day of February, 2018) 1] The accused is charged and tried for offence punishable under Sec.354 of IPC and Sec. 8,10 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 for having been used criminal force intending to outrage modesty of victim girl and sexually assaulted her with sexual intent. 2] Case of prosecution, in brief, is that : The accused had a shop at Sabistan Chawl, Devripada, Kausa, Mumbra. On 23/03/2015 at 18 hours the victim girl was passing by the shop of accused. The accused dragged her inside the shop. The accused brushed his hand on her back and buttock and then pinched on buttock and touched her breast. The victim girl went to home and informed her mother. Mrs. Husna Salim Khan, mother of the victim girl, rushed to the police station and lodged complaint. 3] On the receipt of complaint, Mr. Sachin Tukaam Bendre, API, recorded statement of Husna Salim Khan. He registered the offence under Sec.354 of IPC and S. 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Mr. Sachin Tukaam Bendre, API, I.O. went to the spot and prepared spot panchanama in the presence of two panchas. PSI Mahajan carried further investigation. Thereafter API­Chavan carried further investigation. He formally arrested the accused. On finding substance in the accusation, PSO Mumbra Police Station filed charge sheet in the Court. 4] This Court has framed charge against the accused ( Exh.6 ) for the offence under Sec. 354 of IPC and Sec. 8 and 10 of Protection of Children CNR No. MHTH01-006006-2015 3 Special Case No.205/2015 (Judgment) from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. The contents of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 5] The defence of the accused as constructed in cross­ examination and statement under Sec. 313 Cr.P.C. is of false implication in the case. 6] Prosecution examined in all six witnesses to bring home the guilt of accused. Husna Salim Khan (P.W.2) is examined along with her daughter, victim girl (P.W.3). Fayyaz Ahmad Patel (P.W.1) is father of one girl who was also sexually abused by the accused. Mr. Shantaram Mahajan (P.W.4), Mr. Dushyant Chavan (P.W.5) and Mr. Sachin Bendre (P.W.6) are investigating officers. The accused Mr. Abdulla Abdulgani Shaikh examined himself as D.W.1. 7] I have heard Ld. Special P.P. for the State and Ld. advocate for the accused. 8] The following points arise for my determination with my findings thereon for reasons to follow: POINTS FINDINGS 01. Does the prosecution prove that on ...In the negative. 22/03/2015 at 18.00 hours, at Anjarwala Complex Building, in stationery shop, Mumbra, Dist. Thane, the accused used criminal force with intent to outrage modesty of victim girl? 02. Does prosecution prove that on the aforesaid ...In the negative. CNR No. MHTH01-006006-2015 4 Special Case No.205/2015 (Judgment) date, time and place, the accused, assaulted victim girl with sexual intent? 03 Does prosecution prove that on the aforesaid ...In the negative. date, time and place, the accused, committed aggravated sexual assault on minor girl? 04 What order ? Accused is acquitted as per final order. REASONS 9] AS TO POINT NOS.1 TO 3: I would like to discuss all the points together being interlinked with each other. The victim girl and accused are residing nearby. The victim girl born on 18/08/2004. She was in 7 th standard. She was attending school from 7 a.m. to 12 pm. Her tuition time was from 2 p.m. to 6 p.m. Victim girl urged that incident took place in the evening of 23/03/2015. She had gone to tuition. She took some money from her mother. She went to purchase one chart and sticker in he shop. The accused twisted her cheeks and pressed her breast. The accused caught her hand and put hand over her back. She rescued herself and ran away. Husna Khan (P.W.2) urged that at around 10.30 p.m. her daughter returned home from tuition. She went to sleep. While sleeping victim girl got frightened and started crying. Victim girl told what had happened with her. Victim girl had narrated to one Zarina, mother of her friend. Mr. Fayyaz Patel (P.W.1) is from same locality. Aksa is his daughter. Mr. Fayyaz Patel (P.W.1) deposed that his daughter complained him that the accused gave her eatable chivda and touched her body. Mr. Sachin Bendre (P.W.6), I.O., recorded statement of victim girl. He drew spot panchanama­ Exh.20. Dushyant Chavan (P.W.5),I.O., arrested the accused. The accused entered into witness box and deposed that he complained against the CNR No. MHTH01-006006-2015 5 Special Case No.205/2015 (Judgment) informant on 06/04/2015. I have heard Ld. Special P.P. and Ld. Advocate for the accused. 10] The spot of offence is a Gala bearing No.4, Anjarwala Complex, Shrilanka, Kausa, Mumbra. It is a shop of selling articles useful in a school. There is road in front of the shop leading to Shrilanka Colony. There is one building Anjarwala Complex behind the shop. The victim girl and her parents are residing in a very close vicinity. The victim girl says that she goes to tuition class at 2 pm. and come back at 6 pm. Then she says that she has visited shop of the accused. It has also come in her evidence that she went to the shop of the accused while proceeding to tuition at 2 pm. She urged that she has narrated this incident to her friend Ayesha. Ayesha is not examined. It has come in the evidence of Shantaram Mahajan (P.W.4), I.O., that victim girl stated to him that she has not stated that she used to go to the tuition at 2 p.m. Husna Khan (P.W.2) deposed that at around 10.30 pm. victim girl returned from tuition. Once Husna (P.W.2) stated that her daughter went to purchase a pencil. The victim girl stated that she went to purchase chart and sticker. In the cross­examination Husna Khan (P.W.2) deposed that her daughter came from tuition at 6 pm. Victim girl (P.W.3) has stated in chief that incident occurred in evening while she was proceeding for tuition. So the timing of visit of the victim girl to the shop of the accused differs. There is variance in the timing. Similarly, the friend of victim girl viz. Ayesha is not examined. So it does not inspire judicial mind. Hence, I find it just to answer Point Nos. 1 to 3 in negative. In the result, I pass following order : ORDER 1] The accused Abdullah Abdul Gani Shaikh is hereby acquitted of CNR No. MHTH01-006006-2015 6 Special Case No.205/2015 (Judgment) offence under S. 354 of IPC and S. 8 & 10 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] His bail bond stands cancelled. 3] Accused shall furnish P.R. bond of Rs. 15,000/­ in view of proviso 437(A) of Cr.P.C. Thane ( V.V.Bambarde ) Dt. :­ 01.02.2018 Additional Sessions Judge­1, vsi­p.c. & Special Judge (POCSO)Act, Thane.

CNR NO.MHTH01­006033­2018 1 B.A.2199/2018 ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN BAIL APPLICATIOIN No.2199/2018 (CNR No. MHTH01­006033­2018) 1] The applicant Altaf Mohammed Ibrahim Ansari has filed this application for grant of regular bail u/s.439 of Cr.P.C. in C.R.No.I­ 235/2018 registered at Shantinagar police Station U/Section­ 376 & 420 of I.P. Code and u/s.4 & 6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. 2] Brief facts of the prosecution case are as under:­ The complainant­victim aged 18 years 10 months of Bhiwandi lodged complaint to police station Shantinagar on 08/08/2018. As per this complaint her date of birth is 24/09/1999. She learnt upto 10 th standard. In January 2015 when she was 16 years old, she came in contact with accused as she was working with him about packing work. He started talking with her. In June 2015 by making phone call, he called victim near Avaliya Masjid and he took her at his house as no one was there in house, he by threatening her by showing knife committed rape on her. He told that he has recorded video clip and he will show it to others and shown the video clip to her. Then he promised her to marry. Due to fear she had not disclosed about it to anyone. Thereafter, the accused started calling her at different places and keeping physical relations with her. Since October 2017 she stopped going for work. In 2016 she had Rs. 1,00,000/­of Bhisi and accused demanded that amount on the pretext of purchase of house and she gave it to him in August 2017. Then in that month itself the accused kept physical relations with her by calling her in Garment work place. He was avoiding to marry. On 21/06/2018 he again threatened her when she made phone call to him and asked about the marriage and money. Then on next day she alongwith her sister went to the house of accused and made CNR NO.MHTH01­006033­2018 2 B.A.2199/2018 demand of Rs. 1,00,000/­ to return but he and his brother abused and threatened them. Then she lodged N.C. and thereafter, made complaint to Police Commissioner, Bhiwandi and then gave he statement. It was treated as FIR for crime No. I­235/2018 and above referred crime came to be registered. In due investigation, the accused was arrested, he was inquired and then sent to Jail. 3] The accused in bail application raised different grounds including grounds of innocence, false implication, no evidence against him, taking money by her from him, threatening him to implicate in false case. No incident happened as stated, there is no possibility of tampering evidence, and on other grounds sought bail. 4] I.O. and Ld. A.P.P. in reply, submitted that name of accused is mentioned in FIR. From time to time he committed rape on her giving threats and showing video clipping. He obtained Rs. 1,00,000/­ from her, there is sufficient evidence against her. The victim was found pregnant, offence is serious one, accused may threaten witnesses. 5] I heard the submissions of Ld. Adv. for applicant /accused and Ld. A.P.P. for State. Perused case diary. 6] Ld. Counsel for applicant submitted that all allegations as mentioned are false, victim was working in his factory, she was not working, the accused used to ask her to work, she made different complaints with false allegations, no complaint was lodged immediately CNR NO.MHTH01­006033­2018 3 B.A.2199/2018 after first incident, there is money transaction so happened between them and those were under threats and she received Rs. 80,000/­ from him. 7] Ld. A.P.P. submitted that considering the allegations and threats by the accused, there is no reason to release the accused on bail. 8] What appears from the material on record is that the accused and victim were knowing each other. Before three years, the accused committed rape on her in his own house under the pretext of marriage and by threatening her to show video clip. It appears that, even thereafter, the victim was in his contact, she was going everywhere when he called and kept physical relations with him. Then she herself paid Rs.1,00,000/­ and now demanded the same. Last episode was happened on 21/06/2018 when she made contact with accused and when he threatened her. What appears is that, she was giving response to accused and she stated that it was done due to threats of accused. Initial incident on January 2015 is shown happened when she was 16 years old, Subsequently, she become major and thereafter, also no complaint appears to be made. In N.C. reports filed in Jun 2018 there is no reference of allegation of rape. 9] So considering all the facts and circumstances on record that there was money transaction between them, that no prompt complaints were lodged and at the same time, victim was keeping contact with accused, in my view, without touching to the merits of the matter it can be said that this is a case where accused will be entitled for bail as the allegations are though about act of rape, the victim was knowing him for long period. They had contact with each other and considering the same CNR NO.MHTH01­006033­2018 4 B.A.2199/2018 there appears no substantial reason to deny the application when material part of investigation can be said as over. Victim is shown pregnant in police report but she has not disclosed anything in her report. Considering the same, application deserves to be allowed on terms and conditions. Hence, following order is passed. ORDER 1] Application is allowed. 2] The applicant/accused Altaf Mohammed Ibrahim Ansari in C.R.No.I­235/2018 registered at Shantinagar police Station U/Section­ 376 & 420 of I.P. Code and u/s.4 & 6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, be released on bail on his furnishing P.B. & S.B. of Rs.30,000/­with one or two solvent sureties of like amount. 3] The applicant/accused shall attend Shantinagar police station on every Saturday from 10.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon for two months. 4] The applicant/accused shall not make attempt to threaten or pressurize the witnesses in any manner. Thane (S.P. Gondhalekar) Date – 01/09/2018. Additional Sessions Judge,Thane. CNR NO.MHTH01­006033­2018 5 B.A.2199/2018

.. 1 .. Bail No.2272/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exhibit 1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 2272/2015 This application is filed by applicant Deepak Kumar alias Vinod Brijbhushan Mishra for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no.I-124/2015 registered at Kopar Khairane police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 363, 366, 376, 201 read with section 34 of I.P.C. and section 3, 4 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the accused persons kidnapped the minor girl and then accused Mohammad Irfan committed sexual assault on the girl. It is further contended and argued that no such incident of kidnapping has happened. It is further contended and argued that the girl and the co-accused Mohammad Irfan were in love with each other which was disliked by parents of the girl and the girl of her own had gone with the accused. It is further contended and argued that the applicant is falsely implicated in this crime with the allegation of abetting the co-accused in kidnapping the girl. It is further contended and argued that the allegations of sexual assault are not made against the present applicant. It is further submitted that charge-sheet is also submitted in Court and therefore there is no need of further custody of applicant. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co- operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. .. 2 .. Bail No.2272/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that the accused persons induced the minor victim girl aged 17 years by giving false assurance of marriage with co-accused Mohammad Irfan and then accused persons kidnapped her and took her to Uttar Pradesh and there accused Mohammad Irfan committed sexual assault on her. It is further contended and argued that the present applicant has aided and abetted accused Mohammad Irfan in committing offence of kidnapping and sexual assault and he was always with them in their journey and stay in Uttar Pradesh. It is further contended and argued that when the police were in search of the accused and the girl, the accused persons threw the mobile phones to cause disappearance of evidence of kidnapping in the form of call details. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl and the prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 363, 366, 376, 201 read with section 34 of I.P.C. and section 3, 4 of P.O.C.S.O. Act with the allegation of taking the minor girl who is stated to be 17 years 8 months old under false assurance of marriage, it is contended on behalf of applicant that the girl of her own left the house and went with co-accused Mohammad Irfan since they were in love with each other, and since the parents of the girl were against said love affair the accused are falsely involved in this case .. 3 .. Bail No.2272/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) and as rightly pointed out on behalf of applicant/accused, the allegations of sexual assault are made against co-accused Mohammad Irfan and not against the present applicant. In such circumstance whether the allegations against the accused are true or not, would be the question to be decided on merits. Then, so far as allegation of causing disappearance of evidence by throwing the mobile phones is concerned those allegations will have to be proved on merits by adducing evidence in that regard in the form of call details and subscribers' details. 4] Then, it is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 5] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 6] Then, the applicant/accused is stated to be in jail since 03.08.2015 and even the charge-sheet is also stated to have been .. 4 .. Bail No.2272/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) submitted in the Court. 7] Then, it has also to be mentioned that though the investigation is completed and even charge-sheet is also submitted in Court, it would take time to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 8] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order - ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Deepak Kumar alias Vinod Brijbhushan Mishra is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/- [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one local surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions - He shall not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and the prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this Court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 19.09.2015 (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Additional Session Judge-1, Thane.

It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co­operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that at the time of incident the accused held hand of the victim and pulled her aside and expressed to her that he likes her very much and thereby he outraged her modesty. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicants threatening the victim girl and the prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be .. 2 .. bail 2142/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 354, 451 of I.P.C. and section 7, 8, 11(1) and 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012, it appears that the accused had been arrested long back on 01.10.2014. Then it is contended on behalf of the applicant/accused that he is falsely implicated in the crime and there is delay in lodging the F.I.R. which create doubt in the mind. In such circumstance whether the allegations against the accused are true or not, would be the question to be decided on merits and at this stage only point to be decided is whether the applicant is entitled to be released on bail and in that respect the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence. 4] In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and is ready to abide by any conditions imposed and that he will not abscond if released on bail. 5] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. .. 3 .. bail 2142/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) 6] Then, it has also to be mentioned that the investigation in the matter though almost completed and the charge sheet is yet to be submitted, it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter. 7] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. 1 Special Case No. 93/2013 (Judgment) Presented on : 28/10/2013 Registered on : 28/10/2013 Decided on : 06/05/2016 Duration :2­years,6­Months,09­days. IN THE COURT OF THE SPECIAL JUDGE, THANE. (Presided over by Ms.U.M.Nandeshwar, Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O.Act) Thane) SPECIAL CASE No. 93 of 2013 Exhibit No.34 The State of Maharashtra Through Wada Police Station Thane, District – Thane. ... Prosecution versus Sandesh Narayan Satvi Age 23 years, Residence –Lohape, Tal. Wada, Dist. Thane. ... Accused Offence punishable under section 363 and 366­A of Indian Penal Code and under section 8 & 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Appearance ­ Spl.P.P. Mrs. R.A. Navale, for the State. Advocate Mr. Khilare for the Accused. 2 Special Case No. 93/2013 (Judgment) JUDGMENT (Delivered on 6th May, 2016.) 1] The Accused stands prosecuted for the offence punishable under section 363 & 366­A of Indian Penal Code and also under section 8 & 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act) for committing sexual assault and harassment to minor victim­ girl aged about 16 years by kidnapping her for seducing her for illicit intercourse. 2] Shron of verbiage, the indictment against the Accused are as under ­ [i] Informant Surekha Sukra Satvi (Pw­1) is resident of village Lohape Tal. Wada. The victim­girl aged about 16 years is her daughter and studying in 11th standard. [ii] On 17/02/2013 the victim­girl went outside, but did not return, therefore, her search was conducted. At that time, it was learnt that Sandesh Narayan Satvi (Accused) is also not present in his house. Therefore, F.I.R. was lodged against accused that he kidnapped the victim­girl by inducing her to compel for marriage. 3] On her report F.I.R. was registered against the Accused vide C.R.No.I­53/2013 for the offence punishable under section 363 & 366­A of Indian Penal Code and under 3 Special Case No. 93/2013 (Judgment) section 4, 7, 8 & 9 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. The investigation was carried out by A.S.I. Dilip Waghchoude (Pw­3). The spot panchnama and sketch map (Exh.19) was drawn. Accused was arrested. The statements of witnesses were recorded. Thereafter, investigation culminated into filing of charge­sheet in this Court being the Special designated court under P.O.C.S.O. Act. 4] My learned Predecessor erstwhile Special Judge, Thane, framed the charge (Exh.4) against the Accused for offence punishable under section 363 & 366­A of Indian Penal Code and also under section 8 & 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. The Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial (Exh.5). The Accused took defence of total denial. 5] In response to application under section 294 of Cr.P.C. the defence has admitted spot panchnama [Exh.18], Map of scene of offence [Exh.19], arrest form of accused [Exh.20] and letter to C.A. [Exh.21]. 6] In order to prove guilt of Accused Prosecution has examined following witnesses ­ P.W.1 Surekha Sukrya Satvi Exh.15 Informant / mother of victim­girl P.W.2 victim­girl Exh.25 P.W.3 ASI Dilip Vasant Waghchoude Exh.26 (Investigating officer) 4 Special Case No. 93/2013 (Judgment) 7] The prosecution proved and relied on the report / F.I.R. [Exh.16]. 8] The prosecution closed its side of evidence by filing Pursis at Exhibit­27. The statement of accused under Section 313(b) of Cr.P.C. was recorded. Accused neither examined himself nor examined any witness in his defence. 9] Heard learned A.P.P. Mrs. R. A. Navale for State and the learned Advocate Mr. Khilare for Accused. 10] On consideration of argument advanced on behalf of both the sides and on perusal of the oral & documentary evidence on record, following points arise for my determination, which are answered with the findings thereon, as under :­ Sr. Points Findings No. 1] Does the prosecution prove that on 17/02/2013 at about 12.00 hours at Lohape village, Wada Dist. Thane, accused kidnaped victim­girl aged 16 ..No. years from lawful guardianship of her parents and he thereby committed an offence punishable under section 363 of Indian Penal Code ? 5 Special Case No. 93/2013 (Judgment) 2] Does the prosecution prove that during same period accused induced victim­girl (a minor girl under the age of eighteen years) to go from Wada with intent that she will be forced to illicit intercourse ..No. with other persons and he thereby committed an offence punishable under section 366­A of I.P.C. ? 3] Does the prosecution prove that during same period accused with sexual intent committed sexual assault and harassment to victim­girl in above ...No. mannered and thereby committed an offence defined in section 7 & 11 and punishable under section 8 & 12 of the P.O.C.S.O. Act? 4] What order ? Accused is acquitted. REASONS As to Point No.1 to 3 : 11] All the points are taken up together for discussion, to avoid the repetition, as evidence about the same in common and inter­connected. 12] As the Accused is facing charge under section 363 & 366­A of I.P.C. it is incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that accused kidnapped the victim­girl aged below 18 years from lawful guardianship of her mother and accused 6 Special Case No. 93/2013 (Judgment) induced her by any means to go from any place or to do any act with intent that said girl may be, or knowing that it is likely she will be forced or seduced to illicit intercourse with any other person. So also as the Accused is facing charge under section 8 & 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, therefore, it is further incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that the Accused with sexual intent touched the vagina, penis, anus, breast of a child or make the child touched vagina, penis, anus, breast of such person or any other person or does any other act with sexual intent which involves physical contact without penetration and by his such act committed sexual assault or committed sexual harassment by enticing child for pornographic purpose etc. as defined in section 7 & 11 of the P.O.C.SO. Act. Age of victim­girl : 13] As the Accused is facing charge of kidnapping and under P.O.C.S.O. Act, therefore, first of all it is incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that the victim­girl was child (minor) at the time of incident. The alleged incident took place on 17/02/2013. The victim­girl (Pw­2) deposed that her date of birth is 22/07/1996 and her mother deposed that at the time of incident victim­girl was aged about 16 years. However, except their bare version there is absolutely no documents on record to prove the date of birth of victim­girl and therefore only version of witnesses in absence of any 7 Special Case No. 93/2013 (Judgment) documentary proof cannot be believed. Thus, the prosecution failed to prove that at the time of incident, the victim­girl was minor aged about 16 years i.e. below the age of 18 years and she was a “child” as per definition given in Section 2(d) of P.O.C.S.O. Act. 14] As prosecution failed to prove that victim­girl was minor child at the time of incident, therefore, the provisions of P.O.C.S.O. Act would not applicable. Even to prove offence under section 363 and 366­A of I.P.C. minority of child is most material aspect therefore it was prime responsibility of prosecution to prove the date of birth of victim­girl that she was minor at the time of incident. However, prosecution failed to discharge that burden with cogent and believable evidence. 15] Further, in the present case, the material evidence is of the victim­girl. The victim­girl deposed that accused Sandesh was staying at her neighbourhood and they are having love affair which was opposed by her family and her family used to restrained her from talking with the accused and used to threaten the accused. She further deposed that initially she ran away at Palghar at the house of her maternal aunt, there she learnt that her parents lodged complaint against accused about kidnapping her. As far as this part of evidence of victim­girl is concern there is absolutely no omissions or contradiction. She further deposed that now she 8 Special Case No. 93/2013 (Judgment) is married with the accused and blessed with one son and staying happily. Considering the evidence of the victim­girl, although informant deposed that accused took away her minor daughter, therefore, she lodged report which is at Exh.16, still in the background of the evidence of the victim­girl, no offence appears to have been committed by the accused. Neither he enticed away the victim­girl and forced for marriage. 16] On the contrary, it appears that victim­girl married with the accused when she attained the majority, now she is blessed with a son and staying with the accused happily. With such background the evidence of investigating officer A.S.I. Waghchoude (P.W.3) remains as bare formality. Thus, there is no iota of evidence against the accused and there is absolutely no proof against the accused to prove the charge levelled against him. Therefore, the accused is entitled for acquittal. 17] In the result, I proceed to pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused Sandesh Narayan Satvi is hereby acquitted U/Sec. 235(1) of Cr.P.C. for the offence punishable U/Sec.363 & 366­A of Indian Penal Code and U/s. 8 & 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] His bail bonds stand cancelled and surety is discharged. 9 Special Case No. 93/2013 (Judgment) 3] The Accused shall furnish personal bond of the amount of ₹15,000/­ in compliance of provision of Section 437­A of Cr.P.C. The judgment is dictated and pronounced in open Court. Date : 06/05/2016 (Ms. U. M. Nandeshwar), Thane Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act),Thane. District Judge ­1 and Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

However, nothing is brought on record through her cross examination to disbelieve her. Even the defence that the accused had beaten the victim by pen, is also not suggested in her cross examination. 12] The victim, PW2 in her deposition specifically narrated the incident. She has deposed that on 04.10.2013 at about 04.15 p.m. accused had been to their house to teach her. At that time her mother, younger brother and father were present at home. So far as call record is concerned, it is not the evidence about the incident. It is only relating to the communication in between the victim and her mother on phone while she was at the house of her friend. The prosecution story is not based upon communication on J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 92­13 ­ 354 and 7.doc .....10/­ ..10.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 92/2013.. Exh.23.. mobile phone and land­line phone. Under such circumstances collection of call records is not material in present case. The absence of call records cannot be treated as material fault on the part of investigation. 17] So far as non examination of the father and lady constable who recorded statement of the victim is concerned, it is also not required as their evidence is hearsay and already main witnesses are examined by the prosecution. It is held in number of cases by the Superior Courts that it is not a quantity, but the quality of evidence which has to be considered. The victim alone being eye witness as a victim herself, it was not necessary to examine all other witnesses to whom she narrated the incident or who came to know about the incident on the basis of hearsay information. Therefore, non examination of other witnesses is certainly not fatal to the prosecution. 18] Section 29 of The Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act provides for presumption. It is as under: “29. Presumption as to certain offence : Where a person is prosecuted for committing or abetting or attempting to commit any offence under sections 3, 5, 7 and section 9 of this Act, the Special Court shall presume, that such person has committed or abetted or attempted to commit the offence, as the case may be unless the contrary is proved”. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 92­13 ­ 354 and 7.doc .....11/­ ..11.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 92/2013.. Exh.23.. In the present case the victim has narrated the incident in detail. Her version is supported by the evidence of her mother. There is nothing on record to show that the evidence of victim and her mother is false one. The defence has not brought on record as to why the victim should state falsely against the accused. In view of unscattered evidence of victim and her mother, the defence has failed to rebut the presumption u/s.29 of the Act. In view of the prosecution story, evidence on record, non collection of record of land­line phone or number of mobile phone of accused, informant and her husband is certainly not fatal to the prosecution. 19] Thus considering the entire evidence on record the prosecution has proved beyond reasonable doubt, that the accused had pressed the chest of the informant twice and sexually assaulted her and outraged her modesty. Thus the offence punishable u/s.354 of the Indian Penal Code r.w. section 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act is duly proved against the accused. Hence answering point No.1 in the affirmative, the Judgment is deferred here to hear the accused on the quantum of sentence. Thane. (P.P.Jadhav) District Judge­6 and Date : 19.01.2018. Addl. Sessions Judge, Thane. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 92­13 ­ 354 and 7.doc .....12/­ ..12.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 92/2013.. Exh.23.. 20] Heard advocate Mr.Jaiswar and accused in person. Advocate Mr.Jaiswar argued that the accused is very young person. His old mother is depending upon him. He is a Professor/Maulana teaching Arabic language. There are no criminal antecedents. He was never engaged in any criminal activities. As on today he is teaching Arabic language to various children. Hence leniency be shown to him. 21] The accused is charge sheeted for offence u/s.354 of Indian Penal Code and section 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. The Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act being special enactment prescribing severe punishment it is not necessary to convict and sentence the accused u/s.354 of Indian Penal Code. As provided u/s.8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act the minimum punishment is not less than three years and which may extent to five years. The accused was teaching the victim as a Maulana and was deposed with faith by entire family upon him. Despite the relations, as a teacher­student, he has committed a very serious offence. Under such circumstances certainly this is not a case where minimum punishment can be inflicted. Considering said relations of accused with the victim and the nature of the act the accused deserves to be punished with more than the minimum and less than the maximum. With these observations following order is passed. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 92­13 ­ 354 and 7.doc .....13/­ ..13.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 92/2013.. Exh.23.. ORDER 1. Accused Aftab Dayan Shaikh is hereby convicted u/s.235(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure for offence punishable u/s.354 of the Indian Penal Code r.w. section 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act and he is sentence to suffer rigorous imprisonment for four years and to pay fine of Rs.10,000/­ and in default of payment of fine he has to undergo simple imprisonment for three months. 2. The accused to surrender his bail bond. 3. A copy of Judgment be given to the accused free of cost. Sd/­... Thane. (P.P.Jadhav) District Judge­6 and Date : 19.01.2018. Addl. Sessions Judge, Thane. P.C. in C.R.No.I­208/2017 registered in Kalwa police station for the offence under section 376, 342, 506 of Indian Penal Code and Section 3, 4 and 12 of P POCSO Act,2012. 2. It is contended that the prosecutrix has attained the age of majority. The offence is not punishable with death or imprisonment for life. No purpose will be served by keeping the applicant in the custody. He is only earning member of his family. There is no criminal antecedent. The applicant is permanent resident of given address. Therefore, he may be released on bail. 3. The applicant has produced copy of F.I.R, copy of first and second remand reports, copy of Adhar Card and copy of Passbook. 4. Investigating Officer has given his say at Exh.4. It is contended the victim is 17 years 8 months old. She was alone at her house. The accused called her to come to his house he has some important work. Then accused took her at his house and led her forcibly on matt and forcibly removed her clothes and committed rape upon her. Thereafter accused latched the door from the outside and confined the victim inside his house and threatened her not to disclose this to anybody and he ran way. Investigating Officer submitted that the accused is likely to tamper the prosecution witnesses, if he released on bail. 5. I perused the copy of F.I.R in which she has categorically mentioned that one day on 28.06.2017 at 5.00 p.m. when the victim was alone at her home accused took her at his house and --2-- accused closed the door. The victim shouted at him that why he has closed the door. The accused pushed her on Matt and forcibly removed her clothes and committed forceful rape upon her. Thereafter accused threatened her not to disclose this to anybody and confined her in the room. The accused latched the door from outside. The victim knocked the door but it was raining and therefore, nobody hear the sound. After 10­15 minutes her mother came there and opened the door. Then she narrated the incident to her mother and father and they went to police station and lodged FIR. 6. The court is of the view that considering the contents in the FIR the victim appears to be minor and she is not at all consenting party. She had no affair with the present applicant. The accused forcibly induced her to come at his house and then forcibly committed rape upon her, therefore, there is strong prima facie case made out. The accused is double the age of the victim. Therefore the accused is likely to tamper the victim and the witnesses and likley to repeat the offence. Order below Exhibit 1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 2296/2015 This application is filed by applicant namely Sanju Shyam More for his release on bail under section 167(2) of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no.I-567/2015 registered at Mumbra police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 376(2), 498A, 506(2), 323 of I.P.C. and section 4, 8, 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). It was contended and argued that after the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime 13.06.2015 and still charge-sheet is not submitted in court. It is further submitted and therefore the applicant/accused is entitled to be released on bail under section 167(2) of Cr.P.C. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co-operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] A report was called for in regard to submission of charge- sheet in Court and it is reported by the Office vide report dated 14.09.2015 that on 14.09.2015 at about 3.15 p.m. charge-sheet has been submitted. 3] As is clear, the applicant is claiming for his release on bail on the ground that charge-sheet is not submitted within period of 90 days since after the arrest of the accused in this crime on 13.06.2015. Then, as rightly submitted on behalf of applicant that though the charge-sheet is submitted on the same date i.e. 14.09.2015 on which date the application for bail is filed, it is clear that the charge-sheet is submitted after filing of application and therefore the right of applicant/accused to get bail under section 167(2) of Cr.P.C. does not extinguish. Even in case of Rajubhai alias Jacob Mathew Pinto and another vs. State of Maharashtra reported in 2005 ALL MR (Cri) 290 it is observed that the accused was arrested on 22.07.2004 and was released on bail after he filed application for bail on 21.10.2004 at 11.00 a.m. and therefore though prosecution filed charge-sheet at 3.00 p.m. on same day of filing the bail application i.e. after 90 days, the applicant/accused was held entitled to be released on bail. In the light of above observations in the present case also though charge-sheet was filed on the same day on which the application for bail was filed, since the application for bail is filed prior in time and since the charge-sheet itself is filed after period of 90 days, to be precise on 94th day, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail under section 167(2) of Cr.P.C. I therefore pass the following order - ORDER The application is allowed as per Section 167(2) of Cr.P.C. Applicant/accused namely Sanju Shyam More is released on P.R. bond of Rs.30,000/- [rupees thirty thousand only] with one or two local sureties in the like amount, subject to following conditions - He shall attend the concerned police station for the purpose of interrogation as and when called till filing of the charge-sheet and shall co- operate in investigation. He shall not threaten and pressurize the complainant and other prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this Court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 23.09.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Additional Session Judge-1, Thane.
