Does prosecution prove that on 15/08/2013 at about 13.30 hours accused kidnapped victim­girl from lawful guardianship of her parents from ..No. Vimalnagar, Kharegaon and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 363 of Indian Penal Code ? 2. Does the prosecution prove that on the given date, time and place, accused gave false assurance of marriage to the said minor victim­girl and induced her to go away from that place with intent that said girl may be, or knowing it is ..No. likely that she will be, forced or seduced to illicit intercourse with him and thereafter also confined her wrongfully and he thereby committed an offence punishable under section 366­A & 365 of Indian Penal Code ? 3. Does the prosecution prove that on the given day, date, time and place, the accused after kidnapping the victim­girl .. 7 .. Special Case No.96/2013 Judgment committed rape on her by doing forcible sexual intercourse with her and he ..No. thereby committed an offence punishable under section 376 of Indian Penal Code ? 4. Does the prosecution prove that on the given day, date, time and place, accused committed penetrative sexual assault on her by doing forcible sexual intercourse ..No. with her and also committed sexual harassment on her and thereby accused committed an offence punishable under section 4, 8 and 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, 2012? 4. What order ? As per the final order. REASONS As to Point No.1 to 4 : 11] All the points are taken up together for discussion, to avoid the repetition, as evidence about the same is common and interconnected. Age of victim­girl : 12] As the Accused is facing charge of kidnapping minor girl for illegal/immoral purpose and also under P.O.C.S.O. Act, therefore, it is incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that the victim­girl was child (minor) at the time of incident. .. 8 .. Special Case No.96/2013 Judgment 13] The prosecution has examined the victim­girl (P.W.2) who stated her age as 14 years when entered in the witness box on 20/06/2015. As per the evidence of victim­ girl in the year­2013 she was studying in Padmavati High School Kharegaon in 7th standard. But nowhere she stated her date of birth. Informant Hemant Gadkari (P.W.1) who is father of the victim­girl also did not stated the date of birth of the victim­girl and although, he deposed that he is having original birth certificate of his daughter with him, he had not produced it on record and deposed that he had given the copy of birth certificate of his daughter to the police. The father of the victim­girl (P.W.1) deposed that in the year­ 2013 his daughter victim­girl was aged about 13 years. But he did not state anything about the school of the victim­girl where she was studying. 14] It is pertinent to note that even the copy of birth certificate of the victim­girl which is on record is not proved by the prosecution and during the evidence of investigating officer it is marked as Article­C. The prosecution in order to prove the date of birth of the victim­girl examined Head Mistress, Joisy Lomte(P.W.5) of Padmavati Vyankatesh High School and Jr. College Kalwa, who brought General Register of her school and as per entry No.1943, the victim­girl is student of their school and her date of birth is 28/06/2001. The entry is at Exh.45. In the cross­examination the Head .. 9 .. Special Case No.96/2013 Judgment Mistress Mrs. Lomte (P.W.5) it has been brought on record that Identity card was issued to the victim­girl for the standard 7th wherein her General Register number is mentioned as 2551 for the Academic Year­2013­2014. While in School Register it is mentioned as 1943. Even though, P.W.5 clarified that the General Register Entry mentioned in the I­card is to be changed in every Academic year. However, she admitted that she did not brought the birth certificate or copy of it submitted by the parents at the time of admission of the girl student. 15] As far as the age of victim­girl is concerned, it is significant to note that in the cross­examination of the victim­ girl (P.W.2) or her father who is informant (P.W.1), the age of victim­girl was not at all challenged. However, the aspect of age was vehemently urged at the time of argument. The learned Counsel for accused in that respect, placed his reliance on the Judgment of Hon'ble Kerala High Court the case of Chandran V/s. State of Kerama, Criminal Appeal NO.438/2006 decided on 03/04/2013 and submitted that the prosecution failed to produce the admission form of the school which would have been a primary evidence regarding the age of victim­girl and the Age Determination Test of the victim­girl was not conducted therefore, the date of birth stated by P.W.5 cannot be believed. In this respect, it is pertinent to note that it required that the either of the parents .. 10 .. Special Case No.96/2013 Judgment or guardian who entered the name of the student in the school should have deposed before the Court about the date of birth and taking its entry in the school record and then the supportive evidence of school record can be believed when any further proof of the most authenticated documents about the date of birth is brought. In the present case although the xerox copy of birth certificate was on record, the prosecution failed to proved the said document by examining the witness, but the original birth certificate was not produced on record. 16] Thus, although the prosecution vehemently argued that the date of birth has been proved through P.W.5, however, still there remains some doubt about the exact date of birth of the victim­girl. It is settled principle of Law that when the accused is facing prosecution for serious offences, the serious responsibility lies on the shoulder of prosecution to prove the allegations against the accused beyond reasonable doubt. In this case, particularly when the accused is facing the charge under P.O.C.S.O. Act, it is foremost duty of the prosecution to prove that the victim­girl was minor on the date of incident, with the cogent and believable evidence. In this respect, at this stage, even it is relevant to note that the consideration of the evidence of the victim­girl it appears that she is having knowledge and understanding of her act and its consequences. Even the conduct of victim­girl in the court is required to be noted here that before entering in the .. 11 .. Special Case No.96/2013 Judgment witness box, the victim­girl made it clear to this Court that if her parents remain present in the Court, she would not be able to state whatever she wanted to really state. Therefore, her parents went outside the court hall, even though, as per the provisions of P.O.C.S.O. Act, the parents of the victim­girl are allowed to sit in the court hall at the time of recording the statement of the victim­girl. Thus, as father of victim­girl failed to deposed about date of birth and name of school of the victim­girl, therefore the evidence of head­mistress (P.W.5) remains doubtful. Thus, the prosecution failed to prove that at the time of incident, the victim­girl was minor i.e. below the age of 18 years and she is a “child” as per definition given in Section 2(d) of the P.O.C.S.O. Act. 17] As the prosecution failed to prove that at the time of incident in question the victim­girl (P.W.1) was child below age of 18 years therefore charge of section 363, 366­A & 365 of I.P.C. and section 4, 8 & 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act fails and twin presumption given in section 29 & 30 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, for committing or abetting or attempting to commit any offence under sections 3, 5, 7, and 9 of this Act or about culpable mental state would not arise and would not come to help of the prosecution. Therefore, now the only question remains as to whether accused committed sexual intercourse with the victim­girl against her wish and without her consent. .. 12 .. Special Case No.96/2013 Judgment 18] In this background, now evidence of the victim­ girl and informant who is father of the victim­girl is required careful scrutiny. P.W.1­Hemant Gadkari deposed that on 15/08/2013 as it was holiday therefore he was at home and watching T.V. and the victim­girl had been to the house of his mother­in­law and his other daughter was playing outside. He further deposed that around 1.50 p.m. his younger daughter Nikita came home with 2 to 5 boys by name Sagar, Aman and Nishant. They called her daughter / victim­girl outside the house of his mother­in­law and then they both went away. The evidence of informant P.W.1 is further on the lines that he knew that the boy Rajendra Khapre who was staying in their vicinity and he learns that his daughter and that boy were having love affair and his wife had even shown that boy to him. P.W.1 further deposed that they took search of their daughter and even of the boy and had been to the house of accused. But he was not found and they collected the mobile number of the accused. But as his daughter was not found, therefore, he lodged missing report. 19] The victim­girl (P.W.2) deposed that she knew the accused and first time, she met with him in the engagement ceremony of one of her acquaintance/relative and then one of the friends of accused has given mobile number of accused and told to call him. But she did not call immediately. The victim­girl further deposed that after some .. 13 .. Special Case No.96/2013 Judgment day, she called him and since then, she used to talk with him. The victim­girl further deposed that thereafter, the accused started coming to her school and used to stand outside the school and then they started meeting and then they used to roam around the garden. She deposed that accused's friend was having laundry near her house and accused used to come there to meet her and had a general talk. Thereafter, the accused expressed his love for her and she accepted the same. The victim­girl further deposed that she had not disclosed about it to her mother, but her mother learnt about it as somebody had seen them. Thereafter, her mother persuaded her and the accused not to indulge in such activity as she was small (minor), still accused continued to call her to meet. The victim­girl deposed that when she used to avoid accused, he pressurized her that if she did not come, he will not talk her. 20] Further part of evidence of victim­girl (P.W.2) discern that there was quarrel between the accused and victim­girl for reason of one boy on the suspicion that the victim­girl has written a chit to that boy expressing her love for that boy and therefore, the accused proposed her to run away and she agreed and therefore, on 15/08/2013 he took her in rickshaw to his fostered maternal aunt whose name she did not recollect and there they stayed for one or two days. If this much evidenced of the victim­girl and the relevant .. 14 .. Special Case No.96/2013 Judgment evidence of the father is taken together, then it clearly appears that accused had not exercised any force or induced her in any manner for running away from the house. On the contrary, the victim­girl deposed that when accused pressed her for running, she agreed for it. Thus, the prosecution failed to prove that the main ingredient of section 365, 366­A of I.P.C. that accused enticed the minor victim­girl from the custody of her lawful guardian. 21] As far as the allegations of sexual assault; so also the allegations of penetrative sexual assault is concerned, the most important evidence is of the victim­girl and supportive evidence of medical officer and documents about the medical certificate etc. In this respect, it is necessary to have a close look at the deposition of the victim­girl and the respective evidence about sexual inter­course by the accused with the victim­girl. In that respect, the victim­girl (P.W.2) deposed that after running away with the accused on 15/08/2013 accused took her to his fostered maternal aunt, whose name she did not recollect and stayed there for 4­5 days. She further deposed that accused introduced the victim­girl as his friend. The victim­girl further deposed that in the house of his maternal aunt, accused was sleeping with her cousin brother and she was sleeping with his sister. She further deposed that then on the next day in the night when the other family members of his maternal aunt were on the ground floor, she .. 15 .. Special Case No.96/2013 Judgment herself and accused went to potmala (mezzanine floor) of the house and there they had sexual inter­course with each other. The victim­girl further clarified that it was only once when they were staying at the house of maternal aunt of the accused. She further deposed that thereafter, when they had been out for roaming around to his cousin sister, somebody had seen them and informed about it to her mother. At that time, cousin brother of accused stated that they should go somewhere else they were noticed and her parents learnt about their whereabouts. The victim­girl further deposed that accused took her at the house of his friend at Jogeshwari. But that friend did not allow them to stay with him anticipating some complications and thus they were proceeded in rickshaw and police noticed them and police caught them and brought to Jogeshwari police station. Then police called her father and taken to Thane police station and then she was sent for medical examination. Thus, as per version of victim­girl, the accused and she had sexual inter­ course in the house of fostered maternal aunt of accused once only after they ran away on 15/08/2013 and she stated that it was on the second day which means the act of sexual intercourse was done on 16/08/2013. The plain reading of the evidence of the victim­girl clearly indicate that she was consented for sexual intercourse and as per the victim­girl it was in the night when all the family members were sleeping on the ground floor of the house where they took shelter after .. 16 .. Special Case No.96/2013 Judgment running away from the house. 22] In this respect now even the evidence of medical officer is required close/minute scrutiny. As far as the medical examination of the victim­girl is concerned, she was examined by Dr. Tripti Payghan. However, it is pertinent to note that the prosecution failed to examine Dr. Tripti Payghan as she was on maternity leave at Solapur and unable to attend the Court. Thus, to prove the contents of the medical certificate, the prosecution made an attempt to prove it by examining Dr. Gopalkrishna Paradkar who is Professor and H.O.D. of Gynac section of Chatrapati Shivaji Hospital Kalwa and is head of said department since the year 2002. Dr. Paradkar (P.W.10) deposed that Dr. Tripti Payghan was registered for a tenure of 6 months and in August­2013 she was working in the said hospital. 23] Dr. Paradkar (P.W.10) further deposed that as per MLC register which he had brought in the Court, patient / victim­girl was examined by Dr. Tripti Payghan on 19/08/2013 around 09.00 p.m. wherein she gave history that she had inter­course on 16/08/2013 and 17/08/2013 with the accused. He further deposed that patient was 13 years and no injuries were found on her person, but on local examination her hymen was found ruptured and torn and admits one finger and Dr. Tripti Payghan examined patient .. 17 .. Special Case No.96/2013 Judgment and issued certificate which is in her handwriting. However, it is most significant to note that medical certificate about the examination of the victim­girl was not found signed by the medical officer i.e. by Dr. Tripti Payghan and therefore, that document could not be exhibited in the evidence of P.W.10, though the prosecution made every effort to prove it through Dr. Paradkar (P.W.10). However, said xerox medical certificate was marked as Article­A. Further, in support of it, the prosecution filed the case papers about the examination of patient which was in the handwriting of Dr.Tripti Payghan and signed by her which is at Exh.80. Exh.80 is having the same contents as stated in the certificate about the medical examination of victim­girl which is at Article­A. Now if the evidence in the form of Exh.80 has been believed, the victim­ girl has stated the history of sexual inter­course on 16/08/2013 and 17/08/213 which is contrary to her oral evidence wherein she has stated of having sexual inter­course only once and probably i.e. on 16/08/2013. 24] Further, in this respect Dr. Padalkar (P.W.10) further deposed that the patient was admitted in hospital since 19/08/2013 to 20/08/2013 i.e. for two days. While victim­girl (P.W.2) in her cross­examination stated that on 16/08/2013 and 17/08/2013 she was in Shivaji Hospital, Kalwa. Thus, the evidence of the victim­girl and the medical officer is not consistent about the admission of the patient in .. 18 .. Special Case No.96/2013 Judgment the hospital. Further no injuries were found on the person of victim­girl, particularly on the private part etc. and even the victim­girl herself has stated that it was an act done with her consent. 25] As far as the place of incident is concerned, which as per the prosecution is the house of one Sunita Raghunath resident of Room No.50, Kama lane, Kirol road, Ghatkopar (W) Mumbai. The prosecution to prove the scene of offence has relied on the spot panchnama which is at Exh.70 which was proved through the panch witness Dhanaji Gurav (P.W.9). However, it is pertinent to note that Dhanaji (P.W.9) deposed that police obtained his consent for panchnama and then took him at Kalwa in one room which belongs to one Nitin Dewale which was his rented room, of which the panchnama was drawn. It is significant to note that this witness initially denied putting signature on the spot panchnama and when confronted before the Court by taking his signature in the court, he admitted that the panchnama bears his signature. However, the close scrutiny of his evidence reveals that spot stated by him is totally contrary to the spot panchnama which is at Exh.70. Exh.70 eloquents the scene of offence is room No.50, Kama Lane, Ghatkopar. In this respect evidence of witness Nitin Dewale (P.W.6) is carrying much weightage. .. 19 .. Special Case No.96/2013 Judgment 26] Nitin Dewale (P.W.6) deposed that his mother is having a room at Gholai Nagar, Kalwa and accused stayed there on rent. He further deposed that on 15/08/2013 in the evening at 06.30 p.m. the accused alongwith victim­girl had been to his house and informed that he married with the said girl and required a rented room. As per the evidence of P.W.6 he is residing at Ghatkopar(W). Again it is significant to note that he had not given any particular address of his house and only stated about staying at Ghatkopar. Nitin Dewale (P.W.6) further deposed that he told accused that rented room is not available, however accused was allowed to stay with him for a day and therefore, they stayed in his house and slept at mezzanine floor. He further deposed that his wife and daughter slept with the victim­girl. On the next day, he went to his work and other members of his family was also left for their work and at that time accused and victim­girl were alone at his house. He further deposed that they had physical relationship and stayed at his house for two days and thereafter, they went away. In this respect, the evidence of P.W.9 is full of omission and as far as asking the room on rent and had talk with accused is also in the form of omissions. Even the accused and victim­girl never disclosed about their physical relationship to P.W.9 therefore, it is difficult to believe about his knowledge about the personal act of the accused and victim­girl. .. 20 .. Special Case No.96/2013 Judgment 27] Now again coming to the spot of incident, as discussed above, P.W.9 did not give complete address of his house and P.W.7 stated the scene of offence which is the house of Nitin Dewale (P.W.6). The learned Spl.P.P. argued that in fact, the spot panchnama is proved through another panch Vinayak (P.W.12) who deposed that on 28/08/2013 he was called at the house of Nitin Dewale at room No.50 near Kama lane, Pipeline Ghatkopar i.e. the address mentioned in the spot panchnama which is at Exh.90. P.W.12 deposed that another panch Dhanaji Gurav (P.W.9) was also present and spot was shown by the victim­girl and police drawn the spot panchnama. The learned counsel for accused argued that this witness earlier attended the court but he was not supporting the prosecution by stating that he do not know anything therefore, he was not examined. Same suggestions were given to him, however, P.W.12 denied that suggestions. 28] Further it is significant to note that as per the prosecution case, the accused and the victim­girl were arrested within the jurisdiction of Jogeshwari police station and then they were brought to the Kalwa police station. However, in this respect learned Defence counsel rightly submitted that there is absolutely no evidence brought on record about the taking of the accused and the victim­girl in custody by Jogeshwari police station. Neither the statement .. 21 .. Special Case No.96/2013 Judgment of any of the police office of Jogeshwari police station have been recorded, neither they were examined before the court, which itself again bring the case of prosecution under shadow of doubt. 29] Even the recovery about the cloths of accused and victim is also not in accordance with the law. The execution of the panchnamas are surrounded with the doubt, as in Exh.57, it has been mentioned that there was T­shirt on the person of the accused at the time of his arrest and in the seizure panchnama the shirt is shown as seizured. Further in panchnama, it has been mentioned that the accused himself produced the cloths while drawing the muddemal receipt about the said articles which is at Exh.90, the reference has been made that the friend of accused, one Ganesh has produced the said cloths which was seized under panchnama. The careful perusal of Exh.57 and 90 supports the defence contention that the seizure panchnama was prepared only to suit the prosecution case. 30] Further, the evidence of the victim­girl is full of embellishment and which is duly proved through the investigating offcer (P.W.11). The whole story put up by the victim­girl in her deposition is in the form of omission which was duly proved through I.O. Thus, the careful scrutiny of the evidence of the victim­girl does not inspire confidence and .. 22 .. Special Case No.96/2013 Judgment the most material part of the case which revolves around the age of the victim­girl. In that respect, it is again significant to note that the prosecution failed to prove that the victim­girl was minor on the date of incident i.e. aged about 13 years as the birth certificate was not proved by the prosecution. Neither the reliable evidence is brought on record in respect of the age of the victim­girl and neither her father P.W.1 deposed about her date of birth. Therefore, it cannot be taken as proved by the prosecution. In the background of the evidence lead by the prosecution, the prosecution case is under the shadow of doubt as firstly that the victim­girl is minor is not proved, therefore, the charge under section 363 is goes away as the consent of victim­girl from her conduct is clearly revealed. Moreover, arresting the accused and finding victim­girl in his custody is also doubtful. Even the prosecution failed to prove the medical certificate and even if the case papers of the victim­girl have been seen, it clearly shows that she was a consenting party for the act of the sexual intercourse, if had it been taken place at any point of time. Sexual intercourse with a girl above the age of 16 years not rape as per defotion of rape given in section 16. It is cardinal principle of criminal law that whenever there is the slightest doubt then its benefit goes to the accused. Thus, in absence of the clear, cogent and believable evidence, the accused is entitled for the benefit of doubt. .. 23 .. Special Case No.96/2013 Judgment 31] In the result, I proceed to pass following order; ORDER 1] Accused Rajendra Shekhar Khapre is hereby acquitted U/Sec.235(1) of Cr.P.C. for the offence punishable U/Sec.363, 366A, 365 and 376 of Indian Penal Code and u/Sec.4, 8 & 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] The accused is in jail. He shall be released forthwith if not required in any other case. 3] Muddemal deposited in the court vide M.E.No.434/2015 being worthless be disposed off after period of appeal is over. 4] The Accused is directed to furnish bail bond of the amount of ₹15,000/­ with one solvent surety in the like amount in compliance of provision of section 437­A of Cr.P.C. Judgment dictated and pronounced in open Court. Date : 03/05/2016 (Ms. U. M. Nandeshwar), Thane Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act),Thane.

Code and u/s. 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. 2] Brief facts of the prosecution case are as under:­ Complainant minor victim­girl aged 16 years lodged complaint to police station Shantinagar on 07/08/2018 that she was knowing accused as marriage of her sister was fixed with him. She used to talk with accused. In March 2018 accused with his friend came on motorcycle on road when she was returning to home from school and uttered some words intending to her. Then in second week of March, when she was on terrace, the accused hold her hand and then complaint was lodged by sister of complaint was lodged by sister of complainant to police station about cheating by the accused. The complainant also lodged this complaint in respect of incident happened with her. On its basis, offence came to be registered. The accused was thereafter, arrested. 3] The applicant/accused has raised contention of innocent, false implication, completion of investigation, his antecedents, no purpose to detain him in jail and on many other grounds sought bail. 4] I.O. and Ld. A.P.P. in reply, opposed the application and contended that name of accused is mentioned in FIR, there is another crime CNR NO.MHTH01­006117­2018 2 B.A.2234/2018 against him in Shantinagar police station, he may repeat the crime, may pressurize witnesses and may remain absent on trial. 5] I heard the submissions of Ld. Adv. Ms. Sarita Gaikwad for applicant/accused and Ld. A.P.P. Shri Londhe for State. Perused case diary. 6] Ld. Counsel for applicant submitted that considering the facts, delay in FIR, age of the accused, the accused be released on bail. Ld. A.P.P. submitted that looking to the allegations, the accused may repeat the crime and may threaten witnesses. 7] What appears from the contention of both sides and allegations on record is that the accused on road had threatened victim, uttered some words intending to her and then at another time, hold her hand. It appears that the marriage of applicant/accused was fixed with elder sister of victim. The incident is over. Part of the investigation is also over. Considering all the things, in my view, bail can be granted subject to terms and conditions so as to maintain safety of victim and prevent interruption in evidence. Hence, order. Code and u/s. 8 & 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. 2] Brief facts of the prosecution case are as under:­ As per the allegations incident took place during January 2018 till 07/08/2018 at Vartaknagr Naka and Bhimnagar slum area in the house of complainant Angura Tilakdhari Bharti at Bhimnagar. As per the allegations in the complaint, the accused entered into the house of complainant when her minor daughter aged 13 years was alone. The accused made sexual assault on her, hold her, used insulting language and threatened her when she shouted. Thereafter, the complaint came to be lodged on 08/08/2018. Thereafter, the accused was arrested on same day. After due investigation, he was remanded to Jail custody. 3] The applicant/accused has raised contention in application that he is innocent, has not committed any offence, there is no evidence against him, there are no criminal antecedents, section charged are not applicable, the accused have permanent place of residence, he will abide all the terms and conditions. 4] I.O. and Ld. A.P.P. in reply, submitted that the offence is serious one, against minor, there are witnesses to the incident, the accused CNR NO.MHTH01­006131­2018 2 B.A.2240/2018 may threaten witnesses and complainant and victim, he may repeat the crime, he may abscond. 5] I heard the submissions of Ld. Adv. for applicant /accused and Ld. A.P.P. for State. Perused case diary. 6] Ld. Counsel for applicant submitted that offence is serious one and allegations are false and accused is implicated in the matter and charge levelled does not attract. Ld. A.P.P. stated that the victim is minor, attempts were made for repetition of crime since long period and after last incident report was lodged. Admittedly, the allegations are serious and at the same time, totality of circumstances will show that on conditions, bail can be considered so that safety of the complainant and victim can be secured. .. 1 .. Special case no.218/2014 judgment Received on : 27.10.2014 Registered on : 27.10.2014 Decided on : 13.03.2015 Duration : 4 months 14 days In The Court of the Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012, Thane) At Thane (Presided over by Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Case No. 218 of 2014 Exhibit No. 06 The State of Maharashtra … Complainant versus Shailesh Bhanaji Parmar, … Accused Age 50 years, Resident of Mira Road, Thane Original residence – Navabandar, Kathiyavad, Gujarat. JUDGMENT (Delivered on 13.03.2015.) .. 2 .. Special case no.218/2014 judgment The accused stands prosecuted for the offence punishable under section 509 of I.P.C. and section 11 read with section 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short ''P.O.C.S.O. Act'') for outraging modesty of minor girl Smruti aged 10 years at Shanti Park, near Happy Home Complex at Mira Road (E), District Thane. 2] In short the facts giving rise to the prosecution of the accused are that one Ushakiran Jaysharan Kumar lodged complaint on 13.06.2014 that on the same day her daughter Smruti aged 10 years was playing cycle near the housing society where she was residing. At about 11.00 a.m. one Lona Fernandez resident of her society living in room no.105 informed her that one person is standing outside the society premises and showing his penis to her daughter by taking it out of pant. Therefore, the complainant immediately went there and saw that one person was showing his penis to her daughter by taking it out of pant. Therefore, the complainant phoned the police. The police reached the spot immediately and took the accused in custody. Thereafter the complainant went to Mira Road police station and lodged complaint. 3] On the basis of her complaint offence punishable under section 509 of I.P.C. and also under section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act was registered vide C.R.No. II-49/2014 at Mira Road police station and it was investigated into. During the investigation panchnama of the spot was prepared. Statements of witnesses .. 3 .. Special case no.218/2014 judgment including victim girl and Lona Fernandes supplementary statement of the complainant were recorded. Birth certificates of the girls showing their age were obtained and after completion of investigation, since there was sufficient against the accused, he was charge-sheeted for offence punishable under section 509 of I.P.C. and section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and the charge sheet was submitted to the Special Court since provisions of P.O.C.S.O. Act are applied. 4] The accused was produced from jail. A charge under section 509 of I.P.C. and section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act was framed against the accused as per Exh.4. The contents of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. He pleaded guilty and accepted the charges levelled against him and prayed for leniency while awarding the punishment. 5] On above the points which arose for my determination and my findings and reasons for the same are as under - Points Findings i ) Does the prosecution prove that on 13.06.2014 at about 11.00 a.m. outside the premises of the housing society of the complainant at Shanti Park, near Happy Home Complex, Mira Road (E), Dist. Thane the accused intending to insult the modesty of minor girl named Smruti aged 10 years, daughter of the complainant, exhibited his penis after taking it out of his pant and also made obscene gestures, intending that his penis and the obscene gestures shall be seen by said minor girl ? Yes. .. 4 .. Special case no.218/2014 judgment ii ) Does the prosecution prove that the accused on the given day, date, time and place, the accused intending to insult the modesty of minor girl named Smruti aged 10 years, daughter of the complainant, exhibited his penis after taking it out of his pant and also made obscene gestures, intending that his penis and the obscene gestures shall be seen by said minor girl and thereby committed sexual harassment of said girl ? Yes. iii ) What offence, if any, is proved against Both offences the accused ? are proved. iv ) What order ? The accused is convicted. REASONS 6] As is clear the offence charge against the accused is under section 509 of I.P.C. and section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act with the allegation that the accused had sexually harassed minor girl Smruti by showing her his penis in an indecent manner and also made obscene gestures intending it shall be seen by her. Even it is also clear from the complaint lodged by the complainant that very specific allegations are made against the accused and on that basis offence under section 509 of I.P.C. and section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act are charged against the accused and the accused has been prosecuted for the said offence. Then, as is clear the accused pleaded guilty and accepted the charges for the offence charged. Then, even as per provisions of section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act a person is said to commit sexual harassment upon a child when such person with sexual intent utters any word or makes any sound, or makes any gesture or exhibits .. 5 .. Special case no.218/2014 judgment any object or part of body with the intention that such word or sound shall be heard, or such gesture or object or part of body shall be seen by the child and looking to the allegations made against the accused and in the light of the fact that he has pleaded guilty and accepted the charges so levelled against him, it has to be held as proved that the accused has committed offence under section 509 of I.P.C. and section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and he is liable to be convicted for the said charge. I therefore hold the accused guilty for commission of offence under section 509 of I.P.C. and section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. 7] At this stage the dictation of the Judgment is postponed for hearing the accused on the point of sentence. Date : 13.03.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From sexual Offences Act, 2012) Thane. Resumed. 8] The accused is made aware of the fact that the is held guilty for the offence under section 509 of I.P.C. and section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and the punishment prescribed for offence under section 509 of I.P.C. is imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and also with fine and offence under section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act is punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine. .. 6 .. Special case no.218/2014 judgment 9] I heard the learned A.P.P. and the accused on the point of sentence. The learned A.P.P. submitted that looking to the serious nature of offence charged against the accused he is not entitled to leniency and he is liable to award maximum punishment prescribed. The accused prayed for showing him leniency on the ground that he is only earning member in his family and his family is depending upon him. 10] Then, as is clear though the offence charged against the accused is of very serious nature, the allegations are only that he had shown his private part to the minor girl in obscene and indecent manner. Even it is clear that he had repeated the said act. But then, the fact is also clear and has been stated by the accused that he is the only earning member in his family and his family is depending upon him. 11] In all such circumstance I am of the view that following sentence would meet ends of justice. In the result I pass the following order - ORDER Accused namely Shailesh Bhanaji Parmar is convicted for the offence punishable under section 509 of the Indian Penal Code and he is sentenced to suffer Rigorous Imprisonment for six months. 2) The accused is also convicted for the offence punishable under section section 11 read with section 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and he is sentenced to .. 7 .. Special case no.218/2014 judgment suffer Rigorous Imprisonment for six months and to pay fine of Rs.500/- [rupees five hundred only] and in default of payment of fine, the accused shall suffer S.I. for five days. 3) Both substantive sentences shall run concurrently. 4) The accused is in jail since 13.06.2014. A set off under section 438 of Cr.P.C. is granted to him for the term of the period of detention undergone by him during the investigation, inquiry and trial against the substantive sentence imposed upon him. 5) Since no muddemal property is produced before Court, no order regarding its disposal is passed. 6) Copy of judgment be given to the accused free of cost. 7) The proceeding is closed. Victim girl narrated the incident to her mother. Informant phoned her husband, called him in the home and narrated the incident. Lady PSI – D.M.Lambhate prepared spot panchanama in the presence of panchas. Lady PSI Lambhate recorded statement of victim girl in question answer form. She also recorded statement of witnesses. Judicial Magistrate recorded statement of victim girl under S. 164 Cr.P.C. on 16/06/2015. The accused was arrested on 04/04/2015. On completion of investigation, charge sheet is filed in the Court. 3 Special Case No.211/2015 (Judgment) 4] This Court has framed charge against the accused ( Exh.3 ) for offence under Sec. 354(A) of IPC and S. 11,12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Sou. Sangeeta Mhatre (P.W.1) is mother of the victim girl. Smt. Deepali Lambhate (P.W.2), PSI is investigating officer. She went to the spot and drawn spot panchanama in the presence of panchas, arrested accused, recorded statement of witnesses. She also recorded statement of victim girl in question answer form. 6] The defence of the accused as constructed in cross­examination and statements under Sec. 313 Cr.P.C. is of false implication in the case. 7] I have heard Ld. Bhiwandi, the accused used 4 Special Case No.211/2015 (Judgment) criminal force to victim, a minor aged 12 years, intending to outrage her modesty? 02 Does the prosecution prove that on the same, …. In the negative. day, date, time and place, the accused committed sexual assault on victim girl, a minor aged 12 years? 03 What order ? Accused is acquitted as per final order. She born on 16/08/2003. On 04/04/2015 her husband went for work. Her daughter came from school at 10.30 a.m. The accused entered inside their house. When she went inside, the victim girl started weeping and told her that accused asked her whether were she had hair on body. It has also come in evidence of Sangeeta Mhatre (P.W.1) that accused ran away. She went and lodged complaint (Exh.8). Mrs. Sangeeta Mhatre passed a pursis (Exh.9) that she does not want to bring her daughter in the Court. Mrs. Sangeeta Mhatre (P.W.1) deposed in her cross­examination that she told police that they had compromise. She has no complaint against the accused. PSI Deepali Lambhate prepared spot panchanama (Exh.13). She recorded statement of victim girl in question answer form. Judicial Magistrate recorded statement of victim girl. 10] I have heard Ld. Special P.P. and Ld. advocate for accused. It has come in the evidence of Sangeeta Mhatre (P.W.1) that they had compromise. 5 Special Case No.211/2015 (Judgment) She has no grudge against the accused. Evidence of Sangeeta Mhatre (P.W.1) is hearsay evidence from her victim daughter. .. 1 .. Special Case No.97/2013 Judgment Received on : 30.10.2013 Registered on : 30.10.2013 Decided on : 20.06.2015 Duration : 1 year 7 months 20 days IN THE COURT OF THE SESSION JUDGE, THANE AT THANE (Presided over by Ms.V.V.Virkar, Additional Session Judge-1, Thane) Special Case No. 97 of 2013 Exhibit No. 20 The State of Maharashtra … Complainant versus Naseem Abbas Sadiq Raza Sayyad, … Accused Age 36 years, Resident of Shriram chawl, Ambedkarnagar, near Kabrastan, Amrutnagar, Mumbra, Dist. Thane. Appearance - Mr. A.K.Khamkar, learned Additional Public Prosecutor (hereinafter in short A.P.P.) Mr. Patankar, learned advocate for accused. JUDGMENT (Delivered on 20.06.2015) .. 2 .. Special Case No.97/2013 Judgment The accused stands prosecuted for offences punishable under section 354, 292, 342, 506 and section 11 read with section 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter referred to as P.O.C.S.O. Act for short) for outraging modesty of his own daughter complainant Fatima Naseem Abbas for removing her clothes by using criminal force and showing her obscene film and threatening her if she disclose about such act to anybody. 2] In short the facts giving rise to the prosecution of the accused are that one Fatima lodged complaint on 24.06.2013 that accused is her father. Her mother expired prior to two years and since then her father is staying alone in rented room near Kabrastan. It was also stated by her that since about two years she had been admitted in orphanage by name Sakina Girls Home at Andheri and was studying in school at Andheri in 4th Std. It was also contended that at the relevant time in April, 2013 there was work of repairs going on in her Ashram and therefore she had been staying at the house of her grandmother. It was further contended that on 15.04.2013 her father had brought her to his house at Amrutnagar, Mumbra and then in the night when all were sleeping he had removed her clothes and her own clothes and moved her hand on her private part and also showed her blue film on his mobile phone and asked her to do what the girl in the film is doing by telling that the man in the film is father of the girl. She shouted for help and her brother woke up and had seen herself and her father in naked condition. Then she herself and her brother had beaten her father and shouted for help and then her father ran away by latching the door from outside and the neighbouring woman opened the door. Then she made phone call to her grandmother’s house Shahida and intimated her about the incident. Then her grandmother phoned her father and asked her to reach the complainant as well as other children to their house but the maternal uncle of the girl refused to allow them to stay with them and stated that the father of the girl has not been paying any money for their maintenance and therefore she was forced to go and stay with the father and again in the night her father repeated the act and threatened her not .. 3 .. Special Case No.97/2013 Judgment to tell about it to anybody and also that he would defame her and sell her and earn money etc. Then, thereafter in the month of June when she had been to the house of her grandmother she had narrated the incident to her grandmother and then they went to police station and lodged complaint. 3] On the basis of her complaint, offence as per C.R.No.I- 490/2013 was registered for offence punishable under section 354, 292, 342, 506 of I.P.C. and section 8, 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act at Mumbra police station and the work of investigation was done by P.S.I. Patil. During the investigation panchnama of the spot was prepared. Victim girl was sent for medical examination in regard to her allegation about sexual assault and also for age determination. After medical report of the girl was received, offence under section 376 of I.P.C. was added and the accused was caught. Statements of witnesses were recorded. Clothes on the person of the victim girl as well as accused were seized. Seized muddemal and samples obtained were sent for chemical analysis and after completion of investigation, since there was sufficient evidence against the accused, he came to be charge-sheeted for offences punishable under section 354, 292, 342, 506 of I.P.C. and section 8, 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act 4] Offence under P.O.C.S.O. Act is triable by Special Court and therefore the charge-sheet submitted to this Court. 5] The accused was produced before the Court. A charge for offences punishable under section 354, 292, 342, 506 of I.P.C. and section 11 read with section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act was framed against the accused as per Exhibit 7. Contents of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. He pleaded not guilty. His defence as it revealed from his statement recorded under section 313 of Cr.P.C. was that his daughter was staying in boarding school and he was aksing her to study and not to roam around she was annoyed because of that and when she had been to the houseof her grandmother (mother-in-law of accused) during vacation, his mother-in- .. 4 .. Special Case No.97/2013 Judgment law demanded money from him for their expenses and when he refused the girl filed complaint against him. He claimed to be tried. 6] For establishing guilt of accused, the prosecution examined P.W.1 complainant girl Batul Fatima Sayyed Nasim Abbas and P.W.2 Shahidabanu Moziz Hussain Sayyed, grandmother of the girl. The documentary evidence produced, proved and relied upon by the prosecution was in the form of medical certificate of victim girl Exhibit 14, medical certificate of accused Exhibit 15. 7] Statement of the accused under section 313 of Cr.P.C. was recorded. He did not examine himself on oath and had not examined any witness in defence. 8] I heard the learned A.P.P. and learned advocate for the accused. 9] On the basis of above facts of this case, the points which arose for my determination, my reasons and findings thereon are as under - Points Findings i) Whether the prosecution proved that during period from 15.04.2013 to 22.04.2013 at his residential house the accused, showed indecent/obscene video film in his mobile phone to his daughter i.e. complainant, which was tend to deprave and corrupt her ? No. ii ) Whether the prosecution prove that on the given day, date, time and place, the accused used criminal force against the complainant aged 12 yeas and then removed her clothes and his own clothes and with sexual intent moved hand over her private part intending to outrage or knowing it to be likely that he would thereby outrage her No. modesty ? iii ) Whether the prosecution prove that on the given day, date, time and place, at the time when the .. 5 .. Special Case No.97/2013 Judgment accused was committing sexual harassment upon the girl, brother of the girl woke up and thereafter the accused left the place by latching the house from outside and thereby he wrongfully confined No. the complainant and her brother inside the house ? iv ) Whether the prosecution prove that on the given day, date, time and place, the accused intimidated the complainant and her brother not to disclose about the act of sexual harassment upon the girl ? No. v) Whether the prosecution prove that on the given day, date, time and place, the accused committed sexual harassment upon the girl ? No. vi ) What offence, if any, is proved against the accused No offence is ? proved. vii ) What order ? As per the final order. REASONS 10] All the points are interconnected and are to be decided on the basis of same evidence. I therefore discuss and decide them together. At the outset it has to be mentioned that so far as the fact that the girl is daughter of the accused and also that her mother had expired appear to be matter of record and not in dispute. Even fact is clear from the avements in the complaint and testimony of the complainant as well as her grandmother i.e. mother-in-law of the accused, and also do not appear to have been disputed that the complainant had been admitted in an orphanage and was staying there and on account of holidays she had been to the house of her grandmother. Then, so far as happening of the incident it is to be mentioned that the complainant in her evidence appear to have stated that at the relevant time since her grandmother had gone out of station for attending marriage she and .. 6 .. Special Case No.97/2013 Judgment her siblings were staying with her father i.e. accused and stayed for a week. She also stated that on the day of incident in night around 11.00 to 12.00 midnight somebody came and did obscene act with her and then left and next day morning she informed about the incident to neighbouring woman Shabnam aunty. It is very much material to mention that from the testimony of the girl it appears that the fact of sexual assault was committed on the girl appear to be clear and even do not appear to have been disputed on behalf of accused since there is no cross-examination on behalf of accused. Even that is also further corroborated by the medical evidence i.e. medical certificate of the girl which is at Exhibit 14 (exhibited on admission) by the defence wherein hymen of the girl is reported to be torn and tear is reported to be old. Even fact is also clear from medical certificate that the girl at the relevant time was 12 to 13 years old and that aspect also do not appear to have been disputed. 11] Then, as per prosecution case it was the accused who had committed said act of sexual assault on the complainant girl. But in that respect it is to be mentioned that the complainant do not appear to have supported the prosecution case. Not only that she appear to have stated that on that day her father had gone for night duty and returned home at 10.00 a.m. next day. Her such version do not appear to have been shattered or shaken in cross-examination on behalf of prosecution after she was declared hostile and absolutely nothing appear to have been brought on record to show that she was lying before Court. Even the police officer who had recorded the complaint do not appear to have been examined by the prosecution. No doubt, the prosecution took steps to serve summons on said police officer but his presence could not be secured. In such circumstances the fact that complaint with the allegation that it was the accused who committed sexual assault on his daughter i.e. complainant and showed her blue film and threatened her not disclose about said act is found to have been established by the prosecution. Then, assuming for a while that such complaint was lodged, in the light of the fact that the complainant did not support the prosecution case in that regard, the allegations against the accused cannot be said to have been established. No .. 7 .. Special Case No.97/2013 Judgment doubt, in the medical certificate Exhibit 14 in the history given by the girl it appear to have been mentioned that the girl herself had given history that her father showed her photo and removed her clothes and asked her to do oral sex and also accused tried to touch her everywhere and also have tried to have sexual intercourse with her and that medical certificate is admitted on behalf of accused. But merely on that basis when the complainant in her evidence on oath categorically stated that the accused did not commit any such act and it was some unknown person who had been there in the night and committed such act with her, no conclusion that such act was committed by the accused can be drawn. 12] It is also very material to mention that very specific defence is put forth by the accused that the girl and other children had been to the house of grandmother on account of holidays and the grandmother demanded money for their maintenance and since he did not pay the money such false complaint is filed and also that the girl was annoyed with him because he was asking her to study and behave properly. In that regard the averments in the complaint appear to be in support of the defence wherein it is contended by the complainant herself that in spite of the girl stated about first instance to her grandmother, her grandmother asked the accused to send her to her (grandmother’s) house but maternal uncle of the girl refused on the ground that the accused is not paying money for maintenance of the girl and thereby forced the girl to stay at the house of her father i.e. accused. That in a way support the defence put forth by the accused. In the light of that when the grandmother also did not support the prosecution case that the girl had narrated the incident of alleged acts committed by the accused, such allegations against the accused cannot be said to have been established. Point no.1 to 5 are therefore answered accordingly. 13] In view of my findings to point no.1 to 5 no offence can be said to have been proved against the accused. Point no.6 is therefore answered accordingly and the accused is held to be entitled to acquittal. .. 8 .. Special Case No.97/2013 Judgment 14] Since the accused is acquitted, it is necessary that he be directed to furnish P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/- (rupees fifteen thousand only) as per section 437A of Cr.P.C. to appear before the higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect of any appeal or petition if any filed against the judgment. In the result I pass the following order - ORDER Accused namely Naseem Abbas Sadiq Raza Sayyed is acquitted of the charge for offene punishable under section 354, 292, 342, 506 of Indian Penal Code and also under section 11 read with section 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 2) The accused shall be released from jail forthwith if not required in any other crime. 3) The accused shall furnish P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/- [rupees fifteen thousand only] under section 437A of Cr.P.C. to appear before the higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect of any appeal or petition, if any, filed against the judgment and that such bail bond shall be in force for six months. 4) No muddemal is produced before Court. Hence, no order regarding its disposal is passed. 5) The proceeding is closed. Date : 20.06.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Additional Session Judge-1, Thane.

She has submitted that from the perusal of the allegations, it is clear that the applicants had the clear intention of committing rape on the minor victim, who is only 13 years old. He used to drive tempo and whenever he had been to the house of informant to meet her brother, he used to inquire about her brother with the victim­girl. [iii] On 13/09/2013 victim­girl and her grand­father were alone at home as her mother and brother had been to her maternal aunt at Vasai on 10/09/2013 for Ganesh festival. On that day, as usual she went to sleep in the bedroom and her grand­father was sleeping the hall. The window of the bedroom could not be closed properly as it was swollen due to rainwater. Around 11.45 p.m. victim­girl felt that somebody is 3 Special Case No. 98/2013 (Judgment) standing near her. Therefore, she wakes up and switched on the light and seen that accused Sagar Bhagat was standing there and giving some gestures to her. Then the victim­girl called her grand­father. Accused threatened her not to shout and keep quiet. Her grand­father came there. By that time accused by giving indecent gesture to the victim­girl ran away from the window. Victim­girl and her grand­father tried to caught hold the accused, but he ran away and thereafter, on the next day, around 11.00 p.m. she lodged report against the accused. 3] On her report F.I.R. was registered against the Accused vide C.R.No.I­197/2013 for the offence punishable under section 452 & 509 of I.P.C. and under section 11(1) (4) & 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. The investigation was carried out by P.I. Sukhdeo Rakh (P.W.3). The Accused was arrested. The spot panchnama and the sketch map of scene of offence was drawn. Statements of witnesses were recorded. The document about resident of victim i.e. the tax receipt in the name of Tukaram Jadhav was collected. School leaving certificate of the victim­girl was also collected. Thereafter, investigation culminated into filing of charge­sheet in this Court being the Special designated court under P.O.C.S.O. Act. 4] My learned Predecessor has framed charge (Exh.3) against the Accused for offence punishable under section 452 4 Special Case No. 98/2013 (Judgment) & 509 of Indian Penal Code and also under section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. The Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial (Exh.4). The Accused took defence of total denial. 5] In response to application under section 294 of Cr.P.C. the defence has admitted spot panchnama [Exh.14], Tax receipt in the name of Tukaram Jadhav [Exh.15] and school leaving certificate of victim­girl [Exh.16]. 6] In order to prove guilt of Accused Prosecution has examined following witnesses ­ P.W.1 Informant – victim­girl Exh.10 P.W.2 Laxmi @ Sarita Balaram Jadhav Exh.13 (Mother of victim­girl) P.W.3 Sukhdeo Manaji Rakh Exh.20 (Investigating officer) 7] The prosecution proved and relied on the report / F.I.R. Exh.11 & 12, sketch map of scene of offence [Exh.21] & Arrest form of accused [Exh.22]. 8] The prosecution closed its side of evidence by filing Pursis at Exhibit­23. The statement of the Accused under Section 313(b) of Cr.P.C. was recorded. Accused neither examined himself nor examined any witness in his defence. 5 Special Case No. 98/2013 (Judgment) 9] Heard learned A.P.P. Mrs. R. A. Navale for State and the learned Advocate Mr. Lasne for Accused at length. 10] On consideration of argument advanced on behalf of both the sides and on perusal of the oral & documentary evidence on record, following points arise for my determination, which are answered with the findings thereon, as under :­ Sr. Points Findings No. 1] Does the prosecution prove that on 13/09/2013 at 23.45 hours at residential house of informant, Kawad Gaon, Post Angaon, Tal. Bhiwandi, Dist. Thane, Accused committed house tresspass by entering into the dwelling house of ..No. informant / victim­girl having made preparation for causing hurt to the said informant/ victim­girl and he thereby committed an offence punishable under section 452 of Indian Penal Code ? 2] Does the prosecution prove that during same period intending to insult the modesty of informant / victim­girl by making some sound intending that the ..No. same shall be heard by her and he thereby committed an offence punishable under section 509 of I.P.C. ? 3] Does the prosecution prove that during same period accused committed sexual assault on the minor victim­girl aged 6 Special Case No. 98/2013 (Judgment) about 13 years with sexual intent and ...No. thereby he committed an offence punishable under section 12 of the P.O.C.S.O. Act? 4] What order ? Accused is acquitted. REASONS As to Point No.1 to 3 : 11] All the points are taken up together for discussion, to avoid the repetition, as evidence about the same in common and inter­connected. 12] As the Accused is facing charge under section 452 of I.P.C. it is incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that accused committed house tress­pass by entering in the house of informant which is used as human dwelling, having preparation to cause hurt or to insult the modesty of the victim­girl and as the Accused is further facing charge under section 509 of I.P.C. the prosecution is required to prove that the accused with intent to insult the modesty of the victim­girl made some sound intending that it shall be heard by the victim­girl. So also as the Accused is facing charge under section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, therefore, it is further incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that the accused has committed sexual harassment to the victim­girl with sexual 7 Special Case No. 98/2013 (Judgment) intent, either utters any word or makes any sound, or makes any gesture or exhibits any object or part of body with the intention that such work or sound shall be heard, or such gesture or object or part of body shall be seen by the child etc. as defined in section 11 of the P.O.C.S.O. Act. Age of victim­girl : 13] As the Accused is facing charge under P.O.C.S.O. Act, therefore, it is incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that the victim­girl was child (minor) at the time of incident. The alleged incident took place on 13/09/2013. Informant/ victim­girl (P.W.1) deposed her date of birth as 04/12/2000 and in the year­2013 she was studying in 8th std. The School Leaving Certificate issued by Z.P. School Kawad in the name of victim­girl is admitted by defence which is at Exh.16 and according to said certificate also the date of birth of the victim­girl is 04/12/2000. Thus, it appears that, on the day of incident, the victim­girl was aged about 13 years and 2 months. The defence did not dispute the date of birth of the victim­girl and there is absolutely no challenge to the age of victim­girl. Thus, the prosecution proved that at the time of incident, the victim­girl was minor aged about 13 years i.e. below the age of 18 years and she was a “child” as per definition given in Section 2(d) of P.O.C.S.O. Act. 8 Special Case No. 98/2013 (Judgment) 14] To prove the further charge against the Accused the prosecution has examined the informant / victim­girl (P.W.1) and mother of victim­girl (P.W.2) who are the most material witnesses to prove the charge against the Accused. It is admitted fact on record that Accused is friend of brother of Informant / victim­girl (P.W.1) and therefore victim­girl (P.W.1) and her mother (P.W.2) both know the Accused who used to come to their house. 15] Informant victim­girl (P.W.1) deposed that the incident took place on 13/09/2013 and on the day, she and her grand­father were alone present in the house. She further deposed that her mother (P.W.2) and brother Bhavesh had been to maternal aunt at Vasai on 10/09/2013 for the festival of Lord Ganesha. She even deposed that before going to sleep around 11.00 p.m., she shut the window, but it could not properly shut as it was swollen due to rain water. Her grand­ father was sleeping in the hall and she was sleeping in the bedroom. Around 11.45 p.m. she woke up as she felt that somebody is touching her by hand. She wakes up and see that accused Sagar was standing there. Then she switched on the light and then seen accused. She gave call to her grand­father by shouting. At that time, accused ran away from window and gave her indecent gestures [ Wakde Tikde Ishare kele.]. 9 Special Case No. 98/2013 (Judgment) 16] However, it is material to note that although victim­girl even deposed that she narrated the incident to her mother but her mother Laxmi (P.W.2) did not support the version of victim­girl on the material aspect about narrating the incident of the act of accused. 17] It is pertinent to note that accused used to visit the house of victim­girl to meet her brother but it is not the case of prosecution that accused continuously stalking victim­girl or prior to this incident he had made any such attempt to outraged the modesty of victim­girl by making any sound or signals or gesture or any of his act was objectionable. On the other hand mother of victim­girl Laxmi (P.W.2) certified that she knows accused since his birth and he is good boy. In such background, now it is required to scrutinize whether on the day of incident, the accused entered from the window in the house of informant and with intent to insult her modesty gave some indecent gesture to her. In this respect, except the bare version of the victim­girl there is no corroborate piece of evidence. Although, in the spot panchnama, which is at Exh.14, there is mention of one window on the Southern side of the bedroom admeasuring 2 x 2 ft without grill. However, the height of the window is not mentioned in the spot panchnama. Neither the victim­girl (P.W.1 ) is able to state the height of the window from the ground. Although, the P.S.I. Rakh (P.W.3) stated the height of window is at the distance of 10 Special Case No. 98/2013 (Judgment) 2 and ½ ft. from the ground, however, same was not supported by the spot panchnama. Therefore, the most important question remains whether from the said window, any person can entered in the house. Further, though the prosecution claimed that the grand­father of the victim­girl had also witnessed the incident and came in the bedroom, hearing shout of the victim­girl and tried to catch hold the accused, however, prosecution failed to examine said witness, who could have been the material witness to the prosecution. 18] It is further significant to note that the victim­girl (P.W.1) in her cross­examination admitted that one Ramesh who is her relative and member of grampanchayat accompanied with her in the police station for lodging the report against the accused. She even admitted that her cousin Manoj Raut, son of Ramesh Raut had assaulted accused. Further it has been brought on record that during the alleged incident, there was Ganesh festival in the village and people used to wake­up till late night and therefore, non examination any independent witness, also proved as a fatal for the prosecution. Even the evidence of the victim­girl (P.W.1) in respect of entering of the accused in her house is also somewhat suspicious, as she deposed that she went to sleep and then she felt that somebody is standing near her and touching her by hand. It means she did not witness from where the accused entered in the house. Even the evidence of 11 Special Case No. 98/2013 (Judgment) victim­girl is shaky, in respect of noticing the accused and calling help from the grand­father and approaching her grand­ father in the bedroom. She further deposed that she felt that somebody touching her hand and noticed the accused and again deposed that thereafter, she switched on the light and seen accused, which also creates room for suspicion whether really the victim­girl had seen the accused at the relevant time or only on suspicion or for the reason that her cousin Manoj Raut assaulted accused and to save him on the say of his father Ramesh Raut, the accused has been falsely implicated. Thus, the evidence of the victim­girl does not inspire confidence. Even the indecent gestures were not explained by the victim­ girl which can really amounts to insult the modesty of the woman. 19] No doubt, as rightly submitted by the learned Spl.P.P. that the small girl will not come forward with the allegations staking her character. However, when the accused is facing serious charge, the serious responsibility lies on the shoulder of the prosecution to prove the charge beyond all reasonable doubt. However, in the background of the above discussion as the evidence of the victim­girl does not inspire confident, and not even supported by P.W.2 and therefore no reliance can be placed on sole testimony of victim­girl. Thus, prosecution case is under shadow of doubt and it is well settled law that benefit of doubt always goes to accused. 12 Special Case No. 98/2013 (Judgment) 20] Thus, prosecution failed to prove that accused having preparation to insult the modesty of the minor victim­ girl committed house­trespass and with sexual intent to insult the modesty of the victim­girl made some sound or gestures intending that it shall be heard or seen by the victim­girl. Hence, I answer point No.1 to 3 in negative. Therefore, the accused is entitled for acquittal. 21] In the result, I proceed to pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused Sagar Janardan Bhagat is hereby acquitted U/Sec. 235(1) of Cr.P.C. for the offence punishable U/Sec. 452 & 509 of Indian Penal Code and U/s. 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] His bail bonds stand cancelled and sureties are discharged. 3] The Accused is directed to furnish bail bond of the amount of ₹15,000/­ with one solvent surety in the like amount in compliance of provision of section 437­A of Cr.P.C. The judgment is dictated and pronounced in open Court. Date : 18/04/2016. (Ms. U. M. Nandeshwar), Thane Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act),Thane. District Judge ­1 and Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.
