.. 1 .. bail 2188/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 2188 of 2014 This application is filed by applicant Nikhil Naresh Bhoir for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. II­14/2014 registered at Bhiwandi Taluka police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 509, 323, 504, 506 of I.P.C. and section 11(1) and 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant uttered words towards the victim girl intending to outrage her modesty. It is further contended and argued that no such incident has happened and the applicant is falsely implicated in this crime and that he is in since since last seven months. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co­operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2) The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that at the time of incident the victim girl had participated in procession of Durga Devi immersion and that time the accused made gestures and raised hands towards the victim with intent to outrage her modesty and asked her to give kiss and when the victim and her parents question the accused, he attacked on them and voluntarily caused hurt to them and also did criminal intimidation. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/ accused is released on bail, .. 2 .. bail 2188/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl and complainant and other prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3) As is clear, as per prosecution case offence under section 509, 323, 504, 506 of I.P.C. and section 11(1) and 12 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 are alleged against the present applicant and the victim girl is stated to be 12 years of age and he is stated to have uttered words and made gestures towards the victim with intent to outrage her modesty. But then, as per the applicant he has done nothing and is falsely implicated in this crime. In this circumstance the aspect as to whether the allegations in regard to the sexual assault on the victim are genuine or not, will have to be proved on merits after trial Even nothing is to be recovered and further detention of the applicant/accused do not appear to be necessary. 4) Further it has to be mentioned that the mother of the victim Surekha Dinesh Jadhav has filed on record affidavit stating therein that her daughter kumari Sunita has lodged complaint against the applicant/accused due to misunderstanding and that they do not want to pursue this matter any further. 5) Then, it has also to be mentioned that the investigation in the matter though almost completed and the charge sheet is yet to be submitted, it would take time to complete the investigation and .. 3 .. bail 2188/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) submit the charge sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter. 6) Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 7) Then, it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and is ready to abide by any conditions imposed and in all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER 1] The application is allowed. 2] Applicant/accused Nikhil Naresh Bhoir is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ 3] He shall attend the concerned police station on every Monday between 3.00 p.m. to 5.00 p.m. till filing of the charge sheet and shall co­operate with the investigation. 4] He shall not threaten and pressurize the prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. .. 4 .. bail 2188/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) 5] He shall not leave India without permission of this court. 6] He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 17.11.2014. (Mrs.V.V.Virkar) District Judge­1 and Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.

.. 1 .. bail 2191/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 2191 of 2014 This application is filed by applicant Karam Haisiyat Ali Hussain for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. I­442/2014 registered at Mira Road police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 376, 363 of I.P.C. and section 3, 4 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant kidnapped the minor victim under false assurance of marriage and then had forcible sexual intercourse with her. It is further contended and argued that the applicant has never kidnapped the minor victim nor he had forced her for doing sexual intercourse with applicant and it is a case of consent. It is further contended that the applicant is falsely implicated in this crime. It is further submitted that the charge sheet is submitted in this matter and therefore there is no need to further detain the applicant in jail. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co­operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that the accused developed acquaintance with the victim girl who is minor and then by giving false promise of marriage he kidnapped her and taken her away and then also had forcible sexual intercourse with her. It is .. 2 .. bail 2191/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl and complainant and other prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that the applicant has permanent residence here and he hails from other State and therefore if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 376, 363 of I.P.C. and section 3, 4 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 the girl is stated to be 17 years old and the allegations are that the applicant/accused kidnapped the minor girl on false assurance of marriage etc. In the light of that the contentions raised on behalf of applicant that the girl herself had gone out of house and the applicant brought her back, appear to be worth consideration. Then, it is also contended on behalf of the applicant/accused that he is falsely implicated in the crime In such circumstance whether the allegations against the accused are true or not, would be the question to be decided on merits. 4] Even it is well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence. .. 3 .. bail 2191/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) 5] In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 6] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 7] Then, it has also to be mentioned that the investigation in the matter is though completed and the charge sheet is submitted, it would take time to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and therefore, there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 8] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Karam Haisiyat Ali Hussain is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ .. 4 .. bail 2191/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) He shall not contact the victim in any manner. He shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and complainant and other prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 19.01.2015. (Mrs.V.V.Virkar) District Judge­1 and Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.

.. 1 .. Special Case No.224/2014 Judgment Received on : 29.10.2014 Registered on : 29.10.2014 Decided on : 15.06.2015 Duration : 7 months 20 days IN THE COURT OF THE SESSION JUDGE, THANE AT THANE (Presided over by Ms.V.V.Virkar, Additional Session Judge­1, Thane) Special Case No. 224 of 2014 Exhibit No. 34 The State of Maharashtra … Complainant versus 1] Ajay Gulzar Yadav, Age 26 years, Residence – room no.1 Jay Ambenagar, slum no.2, Bhayander (W), 2] Gulzar Triveni Yadav, Age 46 years, Residence – room no.1 Jay Ambenagar, slum no.2, Bhayander (W), … Accused Appearance ­ Mr. A.K.Khamkar, learned Additional Public Prosecutor (hereinafter in short A.P.P.) Mr. Javed Ansari, learned advocate for accused. JUDGMENT (Delivered on 15.06.2015) .. 2 .. Special Case No.224/2014 Judgment Accused no.1 and 2 stand prosecuted for the offence punishable under section 363, 376, 504, 506 of I.P.C. and section 4 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as ''P.O.C.S.O. Act'') and section 3 of Child Prohibition Act for kidnapping and having sexual intercourse with her by accused no.1 and for having performed marriage with the daughter of the complainant one Suman Yadav though she was aged below 18 years in contravention of provisions of Child Marriage Restraint Act and for threatening and provocation. 2] In short facts giving rise to the prosecution of the accused are that one Shakuntala Radhesham Yadav lodged complaint to police station on 24.07.2014 that victim girl Suman is her daughter and she was aged 16 years at the relevant time in the year 2011 and she was staying with them at Jay Ambe Nagar near Bhayander Station and she was studying in 7th Std. and that time she developed acquaintance with one boy Ajay Yadav i.e. accused no.1 and they developed love affair. It was also contended that on 22.03.2013 accused Ajay had kidnapped her daughter Suman from her lawful guardianship and took her to Saibaba Temple at Shirdi and performed marriage but no entry of their marriage was made at Sai Baba temple. It was also the contention that thereafter accused Ajay brought her to Bhayander and that time her daughter informed them that she had married to accused and also showed one stamp paper executed at Bandra Court. That time father of the girl had stated to the father and uncle of accused Ajay that he .. 3 .. Special Case No.224/2014 Judgment would lodge complaint but that time father and uncle of accused Ajay had threatened them not to lodge complaint, else they would see them and therefore complaint was not lodged. It was also contended that accused Ajay and girl Suman stayed together as husband and wife for about eleven months and accused no.2 and 3 were helping them in their household requirements and also were visiting their house. However, after eleven months there started quarrels between accused and Suman and accused no.2 and 3 started pressurizing Suman to leave accused Ajay and accept money and if she fail to do so they would teach her lesson. Then, accused Suman had even once beaten Suman and when she wanted to lodge complaint accused Ajay threatened her not to lodge complaint and then he had left the house and was not responding to her telephonic communication and he had switched off his phone. They searched for him but he could not be traced. She, therefore, went to police station and lodged complaint. 3] On the basis of his complaint, offence as per C.R.No.I­ 144/2014 was registered under section 363, 376, 504, 506 of I.P.C. and section 4 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and section 4 of Child Marriage Restraint Act and the work of investigation was entrusted to P.S.I. Patil. During the investigation panchnama of spot from where the girl was kidnapped shown by the girl was prepared. Copy of birth certificate of the girl was obtained. The marriage declaration form submitted by the complainant was obtained. School record in regard date of birth of the girl was obtained. Panchnama of the spot where accused Ajay and the girl stayed and also panchnama of seizure of clothes of the complainant were prepared. Accused no.1 .. 4 .. Special Case No.224/2014 Judgment Ajay came to be arrested. Both accused as well as the girl were referred for medical examination and their medical certificates were obtained. Statement of the girl under section 164 of Cr.P.C. was recorded. Accused no.2 also was arrested. Since from the medical certificate the girl was reported to have undergone sexual intercourse, provisions of section 4 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and section 376 of I.P.C. Seized muddemal and samples obtained were sent to C.A. for chemical analysis. After completion of investigation, since there was sufficient evidence against the accused, accused came to be charge­sheeted for the offence punishable under section 363, 376, 504, 506 of I.P.C. and 4 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and section 4 of Child Marriage Restraint Act. 4] Since provisions of P.O.C.S.O. Act are applied, the charge­sheet came to be submitted to this Court. 5] Accused no.1 was produced before Court and accused no.2 appeared before Court. A charge for offence punishable under section 363, 376, 504, 506 read with section 34 of I.P.C. and section 4 of P.O.C.S.O. Act was framed as per Exhibit 3 against the accused. Contents of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. The accused pleaded not guilty. Their defence was of total denial. They claimed to be tried. 6] For establishing guilt of the accused, the prosecution examined complainant P.W.1 Shakuntala Yadav, mother of victim girl, P.W.2 victim girl Suman Yadav, P.W.3 Dr. Nikhil Jagtap and P.W.4 I.O. P.S.I. Kranti Sarjerao Patil. The documentary evidence .. 5 .. Special Case No.224/2014 Judgment produced, proved and relied upon by the prosecution consisted of complaint Exhibit 12, papers of medical examination of the girl Exhibit 20, 21, 22, spot panchnama Exhibit 24 and 30, panchnama of seizure of clothes of the girl and accused Ajay as per Exhibit 25 and 26 respectively, birth certificate of the girl Exhibit 27, document pertaining to declaration of marriage Exh.32. 7] Statements of accused no.1 and 2 under section 313 of Cr.P.C. were recorded. They did not examine themselves on oath and had not examined any defence witness. 8] I heard the leanred A.P.P. and learned advocate for the accused. 9] On above facts of the case, the points which arose for my determination and my reasons and findings against them are as under ­ Points Findings i) Whether the prosecution proved that after kidnapping the minor girl Suman Yadav on 22.03.2013, the accused no.1 Ajay performed marriage with her though knowing that she was minor No. and the accused no.2 abetted him in performing such marriage ? ii ) Whether the prosecution proved that on 22.03.2013 around 11.00 a.m. accused no.1 Ajay kidnapped minor girl Suman Yadav by giving false assurance of marriage from lawful guardianship of her parents ? No. .. 6 .. Special Case No.224/2014 Judgment iii ) Whether the prosecution proved that after kidnapping the minor girl Suman Yadav, accused no.1 had committed rape on her several times at the place of their residence at Vasai and No. Bhayander ? iv ) Whether the prosecution proved that on the given day, date, time and place, in furtherance of their common intention the accused persons intentionally insulted the girl and thereby gave provocation to her intending or knowing it to be likely that such provocation will cause her to break the public peace and also No. criminally intimidated her and beat her ? v) Whether the prosecution proved that on the during given period and place, the accused no.1 committed penetrative sexual assault on the girl No. Suman Yadav? vi ) What offence, if any, is proved ? No offence is proved against any of the accused. vii ) What order ? Both accused are acquitted. REASONS As to point no.1 ­ 10] At the outset it has to be mentioned that on the face of it, it appears that so far as allegations against the accused in regard to provisions of section 4 of Child Marriage Restraint Act is concerned, from the perusal of complaint and statements of witnesses it appears that the accused alleged to have performed .. 7 .. Special Case No.224/2014 Judgment marriage with girl Suman Yadav on or around 22.03.2013. However, the complaint appear to have been lodged on 14.07.2014 beyond the period of one year after the alleged marriage and therefore since offence under section 3, 4 of Child Marriage Restraint Act are punishable with imprisonment which may extent to three months, as per provisions of section 468(2)(b) of Cr.P.C. no cognizance of offence can be taken after the period of one year and therefore the case against the accused so far as offence under section 3, 4 of The Child Marriage Restraint Act is concerned has to be held as time barred. 11] Then, even keeping apart that it is also to be mentioned that as per complainant's version only the marriage was performed in Shirdi but no entry of marriage is there. Then, even though it is case that the accused performed marriage with the victim girl in Bandra Court, no documentary proof in regard to performance of legal and valid marriage is produced. Document at Exhibit 32 the declaration of marriage, which is admitted, appear to be a document of marriage on stamp paper but that cannot be said to be a proof of performance of legal and valid marriage. Not only that from the statement of the girl itself it is clear that she stated that when they went to Bandra Court for marriage, she was not having any proof of her age, therefore marriage could not be legally performed and in view of that also the allegation against the accused that accused performed child marriage and is liable for action under the provisions of Child Marriage Restraint Act cannot be said to be established. Even the exact date of marriage though do not appear to have been stated either in the complaint or .. 8 .. Special Case No.224/2014 Judgment statements of witnesses and even the witnesses have not stated any specific date of marriage in their evidence on oath before Court and therefore also unless exact date of marriage is established, no conclusion about marriage being a child marriage can be arrived at. In any case the complaint itself is beyond the period of one year after the alleged marriage, therefore, no cognizance can be taken and point no.1 is therefore required to be answered in the negative. As to point no. 2 to 5 ­ 12] Then, as per prosecution case accused kidnapped minor girl and had taken her to Shirdi and told her that their marriage is performed and then had sexual intercourse with the girl. In that regard it is to be mentioned that from the testimony of the witnesses and from the defence put forth on behalf of accused the facts which are clear are that the accused and the girl had been staying together for eleven months as husband and wife and from the averments in the complaint and evidence on record, it is clear that the complaint came to be lodged only after there started quarrels between accused and victim girl Suman during the period of eleven months when they were staying together. Even the fact as has been stated by the girl that during their stay together they had sexual intercourse with each other also do not appear to have been denied and even the defence put forth on behalf of accused is that it was the father of the girl who had performed their marriage and only because mother of the girl was against him they instigated the girl to leave the accused and then lodged complaint etc. and in the light of that also the aspect that the accused no.1 and the girl went together to Shirdi, stayed together as husband and wife and also .. 9 .. Special Case No.224/2014 Judgment had sexual intercourse with each other appear to be clear from record and not in dispute. 13] Even it is clear from the testimony of the witnesses and also not disputed on behalf of accused that girl Suman and accused Ajay developed acquaintance and then love affair and they they left house and performed marriage and then started staying together as husband and wife. Then, as observed while discussing point no.1, marriage stated to have been is not seen to be a legal and valid marriage for want of necessary rituals or legal documents. The fact which is clear and not in dispute is that accused no.1 and the girl had stayed together for a considerable period of eleven months as husband and wife and even during that period they had sexual intercourse with each other. Even that fact is also clear from the medical certificate of the medical examination of the girl. 14] Then, as is clear from the testimony of P.W.1 and 2 i.e. the complainant and the girl herself, the accused and the girl had stayed together as husband and wife for eleven months. Then, even though it is stated by the victim girl and the complainant that the accused had kidnapped the girl from lawful guardianship of her parents, from the testimony of the girl and her cross­examination on behalf of accused it is very much clear that the girl and accused Ajay had developed acquaintance and love affair and then decided to run away and perform marriage. Even from the statement of accused no.1 Ajay recorded under section 313 of Cr.P.C. it is clear that the accused stated that since his parents were against his marriage with the girl they ran away and it was the father of the .. 10 .. Special Case No.224/2014 Judgment girl who had performed their marriage by mentioning age of the girl as 19 years, it would be material to mention her that a very specific defence is put forth by the accused and it was also suggested to the mother and the victim girl that the father of the girl had performed marriage of the girl with accused Ajay but the prosecution has not examined father of the girl to deny said fact. The fact is further clear from the testimony of P.W.1 and 2 that even after the marriage the girl was on visiting terms to her parents' house and they were leading happy married life and even from the testimony of the girl it is also clear that they were staying together happily for eleven months after marriage and thereafter there was quarrel and then she went to her parents' house and then as per her version since the accused was not responding to her telephone calls and that she asked him to return back after she could communicate with him on phone he refused to come, she lodged complaint. It is thus clear that grievance of the complainant as well as the girl was that the accused had quarreled with the girl and had left her after performing marriage with her and after staying with her for eleven months. Even very fact that the girl had stayed with the accused for eleven months as per prosecution case itself it appear to be case of consent. 15] Not only that, from the testimony of the girl coupled with statement of accused recorded under section 313 of Cr.P.C. it is also clear that the parents of the girl were against the love affair with the accused and they they had run away and father of the girl performed marriage, his such defence is corroborated by the fact that immediately after they ran away and stated to have performed .. 11 .. Special Case No.224/2014 Judgment marriage the girl intimated about it to her parents but the father of the boy appear to have stated that he learnt about fact of marriage after six months. That also further supports the defence put forth by the accused that father of the girl was very well aware of the fact of marriage and he stated age of the girl as 19 years at the time of marriage and that fact is even clear from the document of marriage declaration produced on record by the prosecution wherein age of the girl is mentioned as 19 years. 16] Even absolutely nothing is produced on record to show that at the relevant time the accused no.1 did know the exact age of the girl. Even the fact that the girl was staying with the accused no.1 for a considerable period of eleven months and they stayed together as husband and wife and also had physical relations is also clear from the testimony of witnesses and corroborated by medical evidence showing that there was evidence of penetrative sexual intercourse with the girl and that also appear to be not disputed or denied. In such circumstances it appear to be very clear case of consensual sex and running away from the house of the parents. Even the consent of the parents appear to be there because though the parents were knowing about the fact that the girl was staying with the accused they allowed her to stay with him as his wife and did not raise any objection for that and objection raised only when there was some quarrel between accused and the girl. It is very much clear and only because there alleged to be quarrel between accused Ajay and the girl, the girl appear to have complained to her parents and then the complaint in present case with the allegation of kidnapping and sexual intercourse with her though knowing that .. 12 .. Special Case No.224/2014 Judgment she was below 18 years of age appear to have been made. 17] No doubt, as rightly argued on behalf of prosecution as per amended provisions of I.P.C. and the definition of rape as per Section 375 of I.P.C. sexual intercourse with a girl is with or without her consent when the girl is below 18 years of age amounts to rape and even as per section 361 of I.P.C. also if the girl is below 18 years of age, taking away or enticing the girl without consent of parents amounts to an offence of kidnapping and in that respect the age of the girl appear to be very much material aspect. In that regard the prosecution appear to have produced copy of birth certificate of the girl on record at Exhibit 27 which show that the date of birth of the girl was 04.10.1997. Keeping apart the aspect that original birth certificate is not produced and accepting for a while that the birth certificate Exhibit 27 which is seen to be the certified copy of the birth certificate issued by Registrar of Death and Birth and that can be taken into consideration, the age of the girl, if calculated on the basis of date 04.10.1997, on the date of commission of alleged crime of kidnapping, comes to 15 years 5 months 18 days. Then, it is very much material to mention that the prosecution also had referred the girl for medical examination for age determination and as per medical officer's version on the basis of X ray report and dental examination the age of the girl on the date of her examination was 16.21 years, plus or minus 1.2 years which is contrary to the calculation of her age on the basis of her date of birth. .. 13 .. Special Case No.224/2014 Judgment 18] In the light of that if the fact that the mother of the girl did not tell the date of birth of the girl and also has not explained as to on what basis and who had got the date of birth of the girl entered into the municipal record and further fact that the father of the girl did not come forward to state about date of birth of the girl assumes importance. 19] Then, even keeping apart that and accepting for a while the evidence adduced by the prosecution on record as it is, it is also material to mention that in the complaint and in the statement of the girl recorded by police the date of alleged incident is stated to be 22.03.2013. But as is clear in their evidence neither the complainant nor the victim girl appear to have stated the date of alleged incident either specifically or even by approximation and therefore it is difficult to ascertain as to exactly when the alleged incident of the accused and the girl running away from the house and performing alleged marriage had taken place. The document of marriage declaration though appear to be dated 18th April, 2013 and exhibited on admission, that cannot be a conclusive proof of the alleged marriage and, as discussed above, very fact that there was such marriage performed between the victim and the accused and even the document appear to be merely colour xerox copy of the declaration of marriage form and therefore cannot be said to be a document sufficient to come to any conclusion in that regard. 20] Then, it is also to be mentioned that it is a case of very peculiar nature wherein before the complaint came to be lodged the accused and the girl stated to have stayed together as husband and .. 14 .. Special Case No.224/2014 Judgment wife for a considerable long period, that too with the consent of the parents of the girl if the marriage is stated to have been performed by the father of the girl. That fact is not even denied by the father of the girl by entering into witness box. Then the accused appear to have come up with very specific case that he was not knowing age of the girl at the relevant time and he was told that age of the girl was 19 years and that is also mentioned in the marriage declaration form as per Exhibit 32 and in such circumstances when physical relations between the accused and the girl were with free consent of the girl and when the girl is seen to have reached age of desecration and the girl also appear to be mature enough to understand the things and even when the parents of the girl were not only very much aware of entire incident but also consenting to it, the submission on behalf of prosecution that consent of minor girl is immaterial and the act of accused having sexual intercourse with the girl amounts to rape, cannot be said to be sustainable and for the same reason the allegations that the act of the accused amounts to sexual assault as defined in section 3 of P.O.C.S.O. Act cannot be said to be acceptable and convincing. 21] So far as section 363 of I.P.C. is concerned also it is very much clear that the parents of the girl were very well aware of the love affair and there appear absolutely nothing on record to show that the accused had played any role in the victim girl leaving the house. Not only that, the subsequent conduct of the parents of the girl that after she intimated them that she was with the accused and has performed marriage etc. they not only did not object to it but even appear to have connived said act and did not take any .. 15 .. Special Case No.224/2014 Judgment action in that respect and therefore, the prosecution that offence of kidnapping is established, also cannot be said to be sustainable. 22] As is clear, absolutely no evidence is there on record to show involvement of accused no.2 in said crime. No role is attributed to him who is father of the boy. Even to a pinpointed question, P.W.1 who is complainant and lodged complaint against father of the boy, in her cross­examination appear to have answered that she do not know what role was played by accused no.2 in accused no.1 running away from the house with the girl and that her daughter must be knowing about it and the role attributed to accused no.2 by the victim girl also is only to the extent, as has been clarified in her examination­in­chief itself, that accused no.2 and 3 are father and uncle of accused no.1 and though she narrated them the acts committed by accused no.1 they did not help her and accused no.2 threatened her not to lodge complaint and leave accused Ajay by accepting money etc. and even in her cross­ examination also she appear to have stated that she filed case because accused no.1 left her and cheated her, which is totally contrary to the prosecution case and further that she mentioned names of accused no.2 and 3 as they had threatened her to leave accused Ajay and asked her to accept money and she did not speak about any threats. Even it is to be mentioned that the incident alleged to have taken place prior to about almost one and half years of the complaint and no reason is explained as to though the incident alleged to have taken place prior to about one and half year, why no complaint was lodged and said delay in lodging the complaint in the peculiar circumstances of the case appear to be .. 16 .. Special Case No.224/2014 Judgment fatal to the prosecution case and create doubt about very allegations made against the accused and in such circumstances also though it appear to be an admitted fact that accused Ajay and the girl ran away from the house and performed marriage, though not a legal and valid marriage, stayed together as husband and wife for a considerable long period and then separated and during their such cohabitation they had sexual intercourse with each other it being clear case of consent of not only the girl but also parents of the girl, I am of the view that none of the allegations against the accused can be said to be proved. Point no.2 to 5 are therefore answered accordingly. As to point no. 6 ­ 23] In view my findings against point no. 2 to 5 it has to be concluded that none of the offence is proved against the accused. Point no.6 is therefore answered accordingly. 24] Since the accused are acquitted, it is necessary that that they be directed to furnish P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] each with one surety each in the like amount under section 437A of Cr.P.C. to appear before the higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect of any appeal or petition, if any filed against the judgment and that such bail bond shall be in force for six months. In the result I pass the following order ­ ORDER Accused Ajay Gulzar Yadav and Gulzar Triveni Yadav are acquitted of the charge for offence punishable under section .. 17 .. Special Case No.224/2014 Judgment 363, 376 read with section 34 of I.P.C. and section 3 and 4 of The Child Marriage Restraint Act and also section 4 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2) Accused Ajay Yadav shall be released from jail forthwith if not required in any other crime. 3) Bail bonds of accused Gulzar Yadav stand cancelled and sureties are discharged. 4) Both accused shall furnish P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] each with one surety each in the like amount under section 437A of Cr.P.C. to appear before the higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect of any appeal or petition, if filed against the judgment and that such bail bond shall be in force for six months. 5) No muddemal article is seen to be submitted to the Court. Hence, no order in respect of its disposal is passed. 6) The proceeding is closed. Date : 15.06.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.

Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­006202­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 223/14 Received on : 29.10.2014 Registered on : 29.10.2014 Decided on : 19.09.2018 Duration : 3Ys. 11Ms. IN THE COURT OF D.J.­1 & ADDL. SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE. (Presided over by Hemant M. Patwardhan) Special Case (POCSO) No. 223/14 Exh.No. State of Maharashtra, (Rabale Police station) ..Complainant V/s. Mahesh Mukund Jadhav. Age : 21 Years, Occ. : Business R/at.: House No. 2/196, Prabhuvada, Kalngut, Bardesh, Goa ..Accused Appearance:­ APP Mr. Londhe for the State. Advocate Mr. Tiwari for accused JUDGMENT (Delivered on this 19th day of September 2018) Accused Mahesh Mukund Jadhav was facing trial under sections 509 of Indian Penal Code read with Sec. 11 and 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 on following facts. 1 OF 5 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­006202­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 223/14 1] That on 30.8.2014, at about 11.00 hrs., at H­01/77, Sector No. 3, Airoli, Navi Mumbai, within jurisdiction of Rabale police station, Navi Mumbai, intending to insult the modesty of Ku. Sneha Ramji Singh, age 16 years, uttered the words “Tu mala khup avadates, tuzya sobat mala ratri zopayala avadel, maze barobar Lagna kartes ka” intending that same shall be heard by her and at the same time as the victim was minor, on the complaint he was not only charge­sheeted under section 509 of IPC but also section 11(iv) and section 12 of POCSO Act. 2] My learned Predecessor was pleased to frame charge below Exh.6 and has certified that contents of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. Accused pleaded not guilty and claim to be tried. His defence was of total denial. 3] On the basis of aforesaid facts' prosecution has then proceeded to examine complainant Ramji Singh father of the victim and victim. Defence has then admitted spot panchanama etc. After the evidence of prosecution as nothing incriminating was found on record. Statement of accused was dispensed with. Arguments were heard. Parties have submitted in terms of their respective avernments. 4] On the basis of aforesaid facts, following points arise for my consideration and I record my findings against each of them for the reasons noted below:­ 2 OF 5 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­006202­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 223/14 S.N. Points Findings 1] Does the prosecution prove that accused on 30.8.2014, at about ..In the negative. 11.00 hrs., at H­01/77, Sector No. 3, Airoli, Navi Mumbai, within jurisdiction of Rabale police station, Navi Mumbai, intending to insult the modesty of victim, age 16 years, uttered the words “Tu mala khup avadates, tuzya sobat mala ratri zopayala avadel, maze barobar Lagna kartes ka”, intending that the same shall be heard by her and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 509 of Indian Penal Code? 2] Does the prosecution prove that accused on above mentioned date, ..In the negative. time and place committed sexual harassment upon a girl i.e. victim age 16 years by repeatedly or constantly contacting her through mobile phone with sexual intent and thereby, committed an offence punishable under S. 11(iv) of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012? 3] Does the prosecution prove that accused , on above mentioned date, ..In the negative. time and place, committed sexual harassment upon a minor girl i.e. victim age 16 years with sexual intent and that thereby, committed an offence punishable under S. 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012? 4] What order ? Accused is acquitted as per final order. REASONS As to point nos. 1 to 4 :­ 5] In the instant case main allegation against accused is that on mobile call accused has uttered the word “Tu mala khup avadates, tuzya sobat mala ratri zopayala avadel, maze barobar Lagna kartes ka” and by using those words has intended to insult modesty of the victim. Victim was minor at the relevant time therefore, as observed above aforesaid charge­sheet was preferred not only under the provisions of IPC but also under the provisions of POCSO. However, in order to establish the guilt of the accused prosecution is required to prove the necessary ingredients of all said offences. Though, prosecution has examined aforesaid two witnesses, it is apparent on 3 OF 5 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­006202­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 223/14 record that victim herself did not support prosecution and has categorically refused during examination­in­chief itself that the accused had ever called her particularly on 30.08.2014 at about 11.00 a.m. to utter words 'rq eyk [kqi vkoMrsl vkf.k rq>s cjkscj eyk njjkst jk«kh >ksik;yk vkoMsy] Eg.kqu rq ek>s cjkscj yXu djrsl dk? Therefore, as the victim herself has denied occurrence of the incident, complainant deposition before the court that one person by name Mahesh used to make call to his daughter and uttering the words 'rq eyk [kqi vkoMrsl vkf.k rq>s cjkscj eyk njjkst jk«kh >ksik;yk vkoMsy] Eg.kqu rq ek>s cjkscj yXu djrsl dk? particularly when he himself has neither heard accused using those words or he himself has even failed to identify accused as Mahesh can not be believed. Therefore, even if we consider his deposition as it is then also it is in itself is not sufficient to establish ingredients of any of the aforesaid sections as the victim herself has turned hostile and at the time of recording her evidence she has almost attained the age of majority her deposition has to be accepted as it is. Once it is accepted none of the ingredients can be said to be established. Thus, prosecution evidence is certainly not sufficient to hold the accused guilty of the offence. Accordingly, I record my findings against point no.1 and 2 in negative and proceed to pass following order. Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­006202­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 226/14 Received on : 29.10.2014 Registered on : 29.10.2014 Decided on : 11.09.2018 Duration : 3Ys. 10Ms. 13 Ds. IN THE COURT OF D.J.­1 & ADDL. SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE. (Presided over by Hemant M. Patwardhan) Special Case (POCSO) No. 226/14 Exh.No. State of Maharashtra, (Vartaknagar Police station) ..Complainant V/s. 1] Sanjay Rajaram Walunj. Age 21 years, R/of : Suresh Jagtap Chawl, in front of Nilkanth bus stop, Konkanipada, Pokhram Road No.1, Thane ..Accused Appearance:­ APP Mr. Londhe for the State. Advocate Mr. Rajurkar for accused JUDGMENT (Delivered on this 11th day of September 2018) Accused Sanjay Rajaram Walunj was facing trial under sections 354 (D) (i) of Indian Penal Code read with Sec. 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 on following facts. 1 OF 8 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­006202­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 226/14 1] That during 20.12.2013 to 25.12.2013 accused has attempted to contact victim on her telephone and has exchanged message as "I Love You" and thus allegedly committed offence punishable under section 354(D)(1) of IPC read with Sec. 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Thus, on the complaint an offence punishable under aforesaid two sections came to be registered against accused. On completion of investigation he was charge­sheeted. 2] Initially my learned Predecessor has framed charge under sections 354 (D) (i) of Indian Penal Code read with Sec. 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. However, while preparing for Judgment as I felt that charge under section 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 is improperly framed and as a matter of fact charge under section 12 was require to be framed, the charge was accordingly altered. Needless to mention that as case was for Judgment prosecution has already led evidence of required witnesses after the alteration of charge, rival advocates have filed pursis Exh.38 intimating the court that parties do not wish to adduce any further evidence after alteration of the charge. Hence, case was accordingly proceeded. Needless to mention that my learned Predecessor while framing initial charge has certified that contents were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. So is the case after alteration of the charge as the charge was read over and explained to the accused in vernacular by me on both the dates accused pleaded not 2 OF 8 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­006202­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 226/14 guilty and claim to be tried with defence of false implication in the matter. 3] On the basis of aforesaid facts prosecution has examined victim, father of the victim, friend of father of victim, Investigating officer, Panch witness etc. as witness no.1 to 5 respectively. After completion of their depositions statement of accused was recorded as per his say wherein he has reiterated the defence of his false implication in the matter. Arguments of rival advocates were heard. Learned P.P. has categorically pointed out that witnesses examined have supported the prosecution and their depositions are certainly sufficient to prove the charge against accused. Per contra advocate Mr. Rajurkar has submitted that if the admissions of the witnesses are considered then is itself clearly indicates that accused is implicated in the matter in which even accused would not have been charge­sheeted. According to him investigating officer who has initially investigated the matter has categorically admitted that till he was investigating he did not implicate accused itself goes to show that with some ulterior motive as the original culprit either was not found or complainant was not interested in his prosecution accused has made a scapegoat. Hence, he has requested to acquit the accused from all the charges. 4] After having heard the rival advocates at length as above and on the basis of facts and circumstances of the matter, following 3 OF 8 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­006202­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 226/14 points arise for my consideration and I record my findings against each of them for the reasons noted below:­ S.N. Points Findings 1] Does the prosecution prove that accused during 20.12.2013 to ..In the negative. 25.12.2013 accused has attempted to interact victim on telephone by sending message a "I Love You" and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 354(D)(1) of Indian Penal Code ? 2] Does the prosecution prove that accused during the same date, time ..In the negative. and place has committed sexual harassment upon victim who happens to be a child by uttering words like "I Love You" with sexual intent and thus committed an offence punishable under section 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012? 3] What order ? Accused is acquitted as per final order. REASONS As to point nos. 1 to 3 :­ 5] Prosecution in order to establish the guilt of the accused has examined aforesaid witnesses. As the accused was charge­ sheeted under section 354(D)(1) of IPC read with section 12 of POCSO prosecution was required to establish essential ingredients of both the sections. In order to prove offence under section 354(D) prosecution was required to prove that the accused was involved in the matter of stalking by attempting to contact the victim and that attempt was to foster personal interaction repeatedly despite a clear indication of disinterest by such woman wherein in order to establish the guilt under section 12 of POCSO prosecution was required to establish that the accused has indulged in act of sexual harassment 4 OF 8 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­006202­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 226/14 with sexual intent so that accused shall be punished under section 12 of the Act. Hence, depositions of the said witnesses are require to be considered in the light of necessary ingredient referred to above. On plain perusal of depositions of material witnesses viz. complainant, victim etc. it is apparent that they themselves have alleged that one Mayuresh Sakat had removed SIM card from her mobile number 8108472841 and after removal of that SIM card some messages were sent on that changed SIM card but the victim did not inform about the receipt of the messages to her father till on 25.12.2013 victim's father himself has seen the said messages while he was checking the mobile of the victim. Same fact has been narrated by the victim herself and both of them have categorically admitted that neither that person Mr. Sakat nor the present accused has contacted the victim on her aforesaid SIM No. 8108472841 either for interacting with or for sending any message to her. Hence, it is apparent that said messages must have been forwarded by the person attempting to call on SIM inserted in victim's mobile for somebody else. 6] Investigating officer did not make any attempt to trace out as to whose SIM card was actually inserted in the mobile of victim nor he has made any attempt to interrogate said Sakat for making himself aware of purpose of inserting SIM card in the mobile phone of the victim. At the same time the conduct of the victim is also against natural conduct of human being. The victim was expected to immediately inform her father or any of the family members after change of SIM card by Mr. Sakat. It is not the case of 5 OF 8 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­006202­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 226/14 the prosecution that behind her back SIN card has been changed. Therefore, if the SIM card was changed in presence of victim by said Sakat, she was expected to either resist Mr. Sakat to change the SIM card or to inform family members immediately after the said act. Investigating officer was also not able to state as to what happened to initial SIM card of the victim after Mr. Sakat has changed that SIM card. As a matter of fact as that fellow Mr. Sakat was never properly interrogated by the investigating officer, aforesaid facts were not brought before this court. Hence, from depositions and admissions of the witnesses themselves it is apparent that accused has neither changed that SIM card nor had any intention of sending such messages to the victim nor was interested in contacting the victim. Thus, if we consider these facts particularly admissions of I.O. then it is apparent that investigating officer did not make any attempt to trace out real culprit but only has forwarded charge­sheet on such incomplete investigation. Thus, on such incomplete investigation allegations against accused cannot be said to be proved. 7] Needless to mention that even if we consider the act of the accused as alleged also as he himself was not aware as to in whose mobile said card was inserted cannot be said to be acted with certain intention he was making voice call or has forwarded particular message to the victim. For attracting the provision of section 354D of IPC two acts are important material viz. following or attempting to contacting a woman that too with foster personal interaction repeatedly despite a clear indication of disinterest by the 6 OF 8 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­006202­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 226/14 woman. In the instant case there appears to be no attempt on part of the victim either to make a clear indication of her disinterest nor it is the case of the victim that she has actually received call from the accused or after reading message named above has intimated the accused about her disinterest in such messages. Thus, as there is absolutely no evidence about attempting to contact such woman to foster personal communication repeatedly that too after the victim has shown her disinterest very ingredient of section 354 cannot be said to be established. 8] So is the case in respect of section 12 of POCSO Act. Section 12 is in respect of punishment for sexual harassment wherein sexual harassment is defined in section 11 of the Act which clearly goes to show that when any person uttered any words with sexual intent or makes any gestures or exhibited any object or part of the body with intention that such words, gesture etc. shall be seen by the child is within the meaning of sexual harassment. However, as referred to above person was making calls or who has forwarded message was himself was not aware as to whom he has contacted or has forwarded message as SIM card was not inserted by him in the mobile of the victim but it was inserted by one Mr. Sakat. Therefore, Mr. Sakat can only be material witness to clarify with what intention he has indulging any such act. However, as he was not shown as the accused or material witness in matter said fact remain unexplained. Thus, due to said unexplained facts evidence brought before this court cannot be said to be sufficient beyond reasonable doubt to 7 OF 8 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­006202­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 226/14 establish any act which can be covered within the meaning of section 11 of the Act. Thus, accused also cannot be held guilty under the said Act. Under such circumstances I do not find anything on record which is sufficient to hold accused guilty of the offence punishable under all the aforesaid sections. Hence, by recording my findings against point no.1 and 2 in negative, I proceed to pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused is acquitted from the offence punishable under sections 354 (D) (1) of IPC read with sections 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] Bail bond of accused shall stands canceled. 3] Accused is directed to execute P.R. and S.B. of Rs.10,000/­ as per amended provisions of section 437(A) of Cr.P.C. and bond so executed shall remain in force for the period of six months from the date of its execution. 4] Proceeding is accordingly closed. It is further contended and argued that no such incident has happened and the applicant is falsely implicated. It is further contended and argued that there is delay of 16 days in lodging complaint. It is further contended and argued that the accused is not native of the area where Ashram School is situated and he has completed his M.A. B.Ed. from Latur District and there was unrest amongst public on the issue of employment of outsiders instead of local candidates and the said issue was politicized and therefore the applicant/accused is falsely implicated in this case out of local politics. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co-operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. .. 2 .. bail no.2331/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that at the relevant time the victim girl aged 15 years was sleeping with other girl students in the Ashram School and it is further contended and argued that at that time the accused went to said place where the girl was sleeping and in spite of knowledge that the girl is minor and belongs to reserved caste the accused outraged her modesty by holding her hand with sexual intent and committed sexual harassment upon her. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl and other prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 354 of I.P.C. and section 7, 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and section 3(1)(x) and 3(1)(xii) of Atrocities Act with the allegation of committing sexual harassment upon minor girl who is stated to be 15 years old and belonging to scheduled caste, it is the contention of the applicant/accused that he is falsely implicated in the crime due to local politics since there was unrest because of employment of outsiders instead of local candidates and the applicant/accused is also not native of the area of Ashram School and therefore he is falsely implicated in this crime on the basis of complaint which is .. 3 .. bail no.2331/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) lodged with delay of 16 days. In such circumstance whether the allegations against the accused are true or not, would be the question to be decided on merits. Even nothing is stated to be recovered from the applicant/accused. 4] Then, it is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 5] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 6] Then, it has also to be mentioned that looking the allegations against the accused the investigation in the matter may have almost completed but the charge-sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge-sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new .. 4 .. bail no.2331/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 7] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order - ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Keshav Dyanoba Pawar is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/- [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one local surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions - The applicant/accused shall attend the concerned police station on every Monday between 10.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon till filing of the charge-sheet and shall co-operate in investigation. He shall not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and the prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this Court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 28.09.2015 (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Additional Session Judge-1, Thane.

.. 1 .. Special Case No.221/2014 Judgment Received on : 29.10.2014 Registered on : 29.10.2014 Decided on : 13.08.2015 Duration : 9 months 15 days IN THE COURT OF THE SESSION JUDGE, THANE AT THANE (Presided over by Ms.V.V.Virkar, Additional Session Judge­1, Thane) Special Case No. 221 of 2014 Exhibit No. 06 The State of Maharashtra … Complainant versus Asha Deepak Shetty, … Accused Age 45 years, Resident of chawl of Ramchandra Gopal Patil, room no.2, sector no.5, Sanpada, Navi Mumbai. JUDGMENT (Delivered on 13.08.2015.) The accused stands prosecuted for the offence punishable under section 7 read with section 8 and section 17 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short ''P.O.C.S.O. Act'') for aiding and abetting the main accused in commission of sexual assault on the victim girl. .. 2 .. Special Case No.221/2014 Judgment 2] In short the facts giving rise to the prosecution of the accused are that on 12.04.2014 complainant returned home from her job around 10.00 p.m. That time her daughter i.e. victim girl Payal aged 7 years informed her that in the afternoon around 3.00 p.m. she had gone to the house for Asha Shetty (accused) for playing and at that time one person was present in the house of Asha Shetty. It is further case of the prosecution that thereafter after some time Asha Shetty went out to bring milk and thereafter said person took victim girl Payal inside house of Asha Shetty and he had physical advances with her with sexual intent and also kissed her and moved hand over her body and because of such act Payal scared and she pushed said person and escaped and came out of house of Asha Shetty. It is further case of prosecution that at that time Asha Shetty was standing outside her house and the girl narrated her entire incident and thereafter the girl rushed to her house. 3] It is further case of prosecution that after the girl narrated the incident to the complainant, the complainant met accused Asha Shetty and asked her about the incident of sexual assault committed on victim girl by co­accused Sirajuddin but Asha Shetty i.e. present accused, expressed ignorance about said incident. Thereafter complainant went back home and after her husband returned from job, she narrated the incident to her husband Thereafter the complainant went to police station and lodged complaint. 4] On the basis of her complaint, offence as per C.R.No. I­ .. 3 .. Special Case No.221/2014 Judgment 55/2014 under section 354 of I.P.C. and section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act was registered at Turbhe police station and it was investigated into by P.S.I. R.G.Lahigude. During the investigation panchnama of the spot was prepared. Statements of witnesses including victim girl and supplementary statement of complainant were recorded. Copy of bona fide certificate of the girl showing her age was obtained from her school. The accused no.1 could not be traced and arrested. Present accused was arrested and after completion of investigation, since there was sufficient against the accused, she was charge­ sheeted for offence punishable under section 8 read with section 17 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and the charge­sheet was submitted to this Court, it being Special Court, since provisions of P.O.C.S.O. Act are applied. 5] The accused was produced before Court by jail authorities. A charge as per Exhibit 2 was framed against the accused for offence under section 8 read with 17 of P.O.C.S.O. Act by my learned predecessor. The contents of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. The accused pleaded guilty and accepted the charges levelled against her and has also filed application pleading guilty vide Exhibit 5 and prayed for leniency while awarding the punishment. 6] On above facts of this case, the points which arose for my determination and my findings and reasons for the same are as under ­ .. 4 .. Special Case No.221/2014 Judgment Points Findings i) Whether the prosecution has proved that on 12.04 at about 3.00 p.m. in the house of present accused Asha Shetty, she facilitated and abetted commission of sexual assault on minor victim girl Payal aged 7 years by accused Sirajuddin in her house ? Yes. ii ) What order ? The accused is convicted and sentenced as per final order. REASONS 7] As is clear the offence charge against the accused is under section 8 and 17 of P.O.C.S.O. Act with the allegation that the she abetted co­accused who is main accused in commission of sexual assault on minor victim girl aged 7 years on the given day, date, time and place. Even it is also clear from the complaint lodged by the complainant that very specific allegations are made against the accused and on that basis offence under section 354) of I.P.C. and section 8 and 17 of P.O.C.S.O. Act are charged against the accused and the accused has been prosecuted for the said offence. 8] Then, it is also to be mentioned that main accused is stated to be absconding and only role attributed to the present accused which is seen to have been accepted by her by filing application at Exhibit 5 is that she left house for bringing milk when co­accused was there inside the house with the girl and even from perusal of complaint it appears to have been mentioned that when the girl came out of house the accused was standing there .. 5 .. Special Case No.221/2014 Judgment and in the evening when the complainant questioned her she replied that she is not knowing anything and as such the allegation against the present accused is that she avoided disclosing about the alleged act of sexual assault and that is accepted by the accused. Even though the fact is clear that the act is not stated to have been committed in her presence and she cannot be said to have any reason to believe that the co­accused would commit such act. But the aspect cannot be ignored that it is apparent that she left the house though the co­accused was there in the house and the girl also was there and also expressed ignorance about the facts when the complainant questioned her and therefore knowledge that possibility of co­accused committing such act is there, has to be attributed to her though no knowledge as to exactly what act could have been committed by the accused can be attributed to her. Even as is clear the accused pleaded guilty of the offence. 9] In such circumstance since the accused pleaded guilty and accepted the charges for the offence charged, she has to be held as guilty and liable to be convicted for the said charge under section 8 read with section 17 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. I, therefore, hold her guilty and convict her for the offence punishable under section 8 read with section 17 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. 10] At this stage the dictation of the Judgment is postponed for hearing the accused on the point of sentence. Date : 13.08.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Additional Sessions Judge­1, Thane. .. 6 .. Special Case No.221/2014 Judgment P. T. O. Resumed. 11] The accused is made aware of the fact that she is held guilty for the offence under section 8 and 17 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and the punishment prescribed for offence under section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act is Imprisonment for a term which may extend to five years and also fine and offence under section 17 of P.O.C.S.O. Act is punishable with the term of imprisonment provided for offence under section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and also with fine. 12] I heard the learned A.P.P. and the accused on the point of sentence. The learned A.P.P. submitted that looking to the serious nature of offence charged against the accused he is not entitled to leniency and he is liable to award maximum punishment prescribed. The accused prayed for showing her leniency on the ground that she has to take care of her family members who are depending upon her. 13] Then, as is clear the offence charged against the accused is of serious nature with the allegation that she abetted the co­accused in commission of sexual assault on the minor girl. But then, it is submitted by the accused on the point of sentence that she has to take care of her family members who are depending upon her. In such circumstances and looking to the role attributed to the accused and the manner in which it is committed and also .. 7 .. Special Case No.221/2014 Judgment the aspect that sentence of imprisonment of either description i.e. S.I. or R.I. can be awarded for commission of offence under section 8 and 17 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and the accused is stated to be in jail since last one and half year, I am of the view that purpose would be served if she is awarded sentence to the extent which he has already undergone during investigation, inquiry or trial of this case and that much sentence would meet ends of justice. In the result I pass the following order ­ ORDER Accused namely Asha Deepak Shetty is convicted for the offence punishable under section 17 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and is sentenced to suffer Rigorous Imprisonment for the period she has undergone during the investigation, inquiry or trial of this case and also to pay fine of Rs.100/­ [rupees one hundred only] and in default to pay fine amount, she is sentenced to suffer S.I. for one day ii ) The accused is in jail since 16.04.2014. A set off under section 428 of the Cr.P.C. is granted to her for the term of the period of detention undergone by her during the investigation, inquiry and trial against the substantive sentence imposed upon her. iii ) Since no muddemal property is produced before Court, no order in regard to its disposal is passed. iv ) Copy of judgment be given to the accused free of cost. v) The proceeding is closed. Date : 13.08.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) .. 8 .. Special Case No.221/2014 Judgment Additional Session Judge­1, Thane.

Code and section 10 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as P.O.C.S.O. Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Mr.Kanhere for the applicant/accused and learned A.P.P. Mrs. Kapre for State. I.O. present with case diary. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 24.07.2015 at the instance of the informant with an indictment that on that day when between 11.30 to 11.45 a.m. when her minor daughter aged 9 years was alone at home, at that time accused who is staying in the same building in flat no.401 called her daughter and outraged her modesty. .. 2 .. Bail No. 2342/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) 4] The learned Counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant­accused is falsely implicated. The applicant­accused is staying in the same building. He is aged about 55 years. The concocted story is put forward. The investigation is almost completed. Accused is permanent resident of the address given in the application. He is behind bars since one and half months. He is not having any criminal antecedents. He is ready to abide by the conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing him on bail. 5] Per contra, the learned A.P.P. opposed the application submitting that the offence is serious. She submitted that name of accused is mentioned in the F.I.R. He is resident of same building and therefore, there are chances of pressurizing the informant and victim girl. The investigation is in progress. There are chances of tampering of witnesses and prayed for rejection of application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R, it appears that the allegations are about outraging modesty of victim girl aged about 9 years by calling her outside her flat. Looking to the allegations made in the F.I.R. and the reasons put forth by the investigating officer opposing the bail application, it appears that material part of the investigation is already completed. The accused is behind bar since one and half month. Considering the peculiar facts, no purpose would be served by further incarceration of the accused. The object of bail is neither preventive nor punitive but to secure .. 3 .. Bail No. 2342/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) the presence of accused at the time of trial. Accused is ready to abide by the conditions imposed by the Court. The apprehension of A.P.P. can be addressed by imposing stringent conditions. Hence, I pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is allowed. 2) Applicant Dilip Lotanrao Patil be released on bail on his executing P.R. Bond of ₹.15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount on the following conditions ­ A] Applicant shall attend Vartaknagar police station on every Friday in between 10.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon till filing charge­sheet. B] Applicant shall co­operate in investigation and shall not tamper with prosecution witnesses. C] Applicant shall furnish his and his two blood relatives' address proofs and contact numbers and he is duty bound to inform I.O. and Court about the change of address, if any. D] The applicant shall not contact victim­girl or any other witnesses in any manner and he shall maintain decency hereinafter. Thane. Date : 27.10.2015. (Ms. U.M. .. 1 .. Bail No.2351/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exhibit 1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 2351/2015 This application is filed by applicant Wasim Nasim Khan for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. I-294/2015 registered at Narpoli Police Station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 363, 366A, 376 of I.P.C. and section 3, 4 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant had induced minor daughter of the complainant and kidnapped her from lawful guardianship of complainant by giving false assurance of marriage and then had sexual intercourse with her. It is further contended and argued that the applicant has no criminal antecedents and that he is falsely implicated on the basis of concocted complaint which was lodged due to pressure by the complainant. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co-operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that taking disadvantage of minor age of daughter of the complainant the accused induced and enticed her by giving false promise of marriage and then had sexual intercourse with her. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl, complainant and other prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. .. 2 .. Bail No.2351/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 363, 366A, 376 of I.P.C. and section 4, 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act with the allegation of committing sexual assault victim girl who is stated to be 14 years old, it is contended on behalf of accused that the complainant pressurized the girl to falsely implicate the accused in this crime. In such circumstance whether the allegations against the accused are true or not, would be the question to be decided on merits. Even nothing is stated to be recovered from the applicant/accused. 4] Then, it is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 5] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 6] Then, it has also to be mentioned that looking the allegations against the accused the investigation in the matter may have almost completed but the charge-sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge- sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to .. 3 .. Bail No.2351/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 7] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order - ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Wasim Nasim Khan is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/- [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one local surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions - The applicant/accused shall attend the concerned police station on every Thursday between 10.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon till filing of the charge-sheet and shall co-operate in investigation.
