JUDGMENT 1 Special case No. 227/2016 CNR NO. MHTH01­006244­2016 Presented on : 20.09.2016 Registered on : 20.09.2016 Decided on : 23.07.2018 Duration : 01Y 10M 03D IN THE COURT OF THE SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE, AT : THANE. (Presided over by S.C. Khalipe, Additional Sessions Judge, Thane ) SPECIAL CASE NO.227/2016 (CNR NO.MHTH01­006244­2016) EXH. NO. The State of Maharashtra (Through Officer Incharge of Bhiwandi Police Station, Thane.) ….. Prosecution V/s. Kalpesh Gurudas Kene Age 24 years, Occ: Education All Residing at Gorai, Taluka Bhiwandi, Dist. Thane. ..... Accused Offence punishable under Section 354(D)(i) of Indian Penal Code and Section 12 of POCSO Act, 2012. Appearance: A.P.P. Smt.Vandana Jadhav APP for State. Advocate Shri.Dhananjay Patil for accused. JUDGMENT (Delivered on this 23rd day of July 2018) 1. The case of the prosecution is that accused would follow the victim when she would go to her school. He would JUDGMENT 2 Special case No. 227/2016 CNR NO. MHTH01­006244­2016 also take rounds on his motor cycle at her house and he defamed that he loved with the victim. One day he forcibly entered into the house of the victim. So on 23.07.2016 the victim aged 16 years lodged FIR against accused in Thane Gramin police station. C.R.No.168/2016 was registered and investigated by P.I. Dhanaji Khsirsagar. He recorded statement of witnesses and sent the charge­sheet. 2. Charge is framed against accused at Exh.11 under section 354(d)(i) of IPC and section 12 of POCSO Act, 2012. He pleaded not guilty. His defence is that he had friendship with the victim, but it was disliked by her parents. Victim had wrote him love letter. She lodged false FIR at the instance of her parents. 3. Following points arose for my determination. I have given its findings with the reasons, as under :­ Sr.No. Points Findings 1. Does prosecution prove that two years prior to 23.07.2016 at Chavindra Gaon, Savde, Taluka Bhiwandi, near In the negative. the house of informant and near her school the accused would follow the victim aged 16 years and attempted to contact her to foster personal interaction repeatedly despite a clear indication of disinterest by her and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 354(D)(i) of IPC ? 2. Does prosecution prove that on the In the negative. aforesaid period and place accused JUDGMENT 3 Special case No. 227/2016 CNR NO. MHTH01­006244­2016 repeatedly following and watching the above named victim and also entered in her house and pretended that she had love affair with her and thereby committed an offence punishable under sectoin 12 of POCSO Act, 2012? 3 What order? As per final order. :REASONS: As to Point No.1 to 3 :­ 4. To prove the offence prosecution has examined in all two witnesses i.e. victim at Exh.14 and victim's mother at Exh.23. On examining two witnesses the prosecution evidence was closed. 5. The victim had stated in her evidence that she would reside with her parents, brother and sister at Savande, Thaluka Bhiwandi. She was learning in 10th standard. She would go to New English School at Chavindra by walk. Accused would come there on motor cycle and take rounds around her. One day she was going to school. Accused came there on motor cycle and called her by her name infront of the students of her school, but she did not give attention to him. She told him that don't call her otherwise she will tell her parents. From that day her girl friends stopped come with her. After 2­3 days of the above incident two persons had come in the house of the victim and told them that Kalpesh Kene had given mobile phone to the victim and she talks with him, at that time her parents went to JUDGMENT 4 Special case No. 227/2016 CNR NO. MHTH01­006244­2016 police station, but Murlidhar Kene, the Sarpanch of the village of accused came there and took responsibility of the accused. So at that time no complaint was lodged. 6. The victim has further stated that accused would come infront of their house to see her, therefore, she stopped to go her school because the accused would harassing her. One day when the mother, brother and sister of the victim were at home at 8.30 p.m., accused forcibly entered in to their house. Her mother tried to catch him, but accused pushed her mother and ran away. Her mother told this incident to her uncle Sainath Patil. So Sainath Patil went to Kalpesh Kene's house and reported the incident to his mother. Accused mother assured that he will not repeat the incident, but he did not improve his conduct. He would come infront of his house on the motor cycle. Therefore, she lodged FIR on 23.07.2016 vide Exh.15. 7. It has come in the cross­examination of the victim that accused would reside at Gorsai and to go to Gorsa, he has to go via Sawande. Victim resides at Sawande and accused resides at Gorsai. The victim denied that she had friendship with the accused. She admits that she herself stopped to go to school. She admit that on that day her mother had saw the accused had entered forcibly, but she did not see him. She denied that she had written the chit to the accused. One chit which was seized by the police during investigation was shown to her. She denied its' hand writing. JUDGMENT 5 Special case No. 227/2016 CNR NO. MHTH01­006244­2016 8. The victim's mother (Exh.23) has stated as per the victim. She has stated that one day the electricity light was off in their building. There was dark in their building. At that time she saw one boy was climbing in stair case. She felt that he might be Kalpesh Kene. Therefore, her daughter lodged FIR. In her cross­examination she has admitted that she cannot tell surely that Kalpesh had entered in their house. In para­4 of her cross­examination she has stated that she cannot tell on which day, date and time accused stalking her daughter and she cannot tell when Murlidhar Kene intermediate their case. 9. The school bonafide certificate of the victim is marked at Exh.25. Her birth date is 10.03.1999. So there is no dispute that she was 16 years at the time of incident. 10. One seizure panchanama of the love letter dtd.26.08.2016 is admitted by the accused. By that panchanama one chit was seized from Gurunath Kene, the father of the accused. It was the chit written on A/4 size paper on two sides and it was love letter. 11. It is defence of the accused that he had friendship with the victim, but victim and her mother has denied it. The chit which is allegedly written by the victim was seized from the accused father. That chit does not bear the signature of the victim and it's hand writing is denied by the victim and her mother. 12. The witnesses P.W.1 and 2 have not stated any particular day, time and place about the incident of stalking, but it took place two years prior to the filing of the FIR when JUDGMENT 6 Special case No. 227/2016 CNR NO. MHTH01­006244­2016 the victim was learning in 10th standard. It has come on record that victim herself has stopped to go her school. The name of two persons is disclosed in the evidence of P.W.1 and 2 i.e. Murlidhar Kene and Sainath Patil. Murlidhar Kene was the Sarpanch of the village of accused who had intermediate in the quarrel of victim and he had assured on behalf of the accused, but he is not examined by to prove the incident that really the victim had lodged complaint against accused, but because of his mediation the complaint was taken back. So also Sainath Patil uncle of the victim was sent to the house of accused to give him understanding that witness is not examined, therefore, these two incidents are not proved by the prosecution beyond doubt. One incident is stated by the victim that one day accused had entered into their building, but she did not see accused, her mother had seen one boy. However, the mother has stated that it was a dark in their building the electricity was off it was 8.30 p.m., at that time she had seen one boy was climbing in stair case of their building. So she suspected that it might be Kalpesh Kene, but she could not said surely that he was Kalpesh Kene. So that incident is also not proved beyond doubt by the prosecution that accused Kalpesh had entered forcibly into the house of victim. It is also not proved that the accused had entered in to the house of victim. Only victim's mother had seen that one boy had climbing stair case of their building that does not mean that accused had entered forcibly into the house of victim. JUDGMENT 7 Special case No. 227/2016 CNR NO. MHTH01­006244­2016 13. Investigating Officer is not examined by the prosecution and therefore, it has not come on record what investigation he has done in respect of the chit which was seized form the father of the accused. Prosecution has to explain why that chit was seized from the accused's father and whether it was in the hand writing of the victim or not. Prosecution itself had seized that chit and produced on record. So it was duty of the Investigating Officer to find out whether really the victim had wrote letter to the accused, but that part is not at all proved by the prosecution and therefore it causes injustice to the accused. If really the investigation would have been done in respect of that chit and it was transpired that the chit was in the handwriting of the victim then friendship of the victim and accused would have been disclosed. It does not matter that the chit does not bears signature of the victim. The handwriting of the chit is important. The victim has denied it's hand writing, but accused says that it was written by the victim to him and therefore, that chit was produced by his father before the police. 14. The court is of the view that there is delay in lodging FIR. So also no particular date, time and place of stalking is proved. Two material witnesses are not examined. Investigating Officer is also not examined. So evidence of the prosecution is not satisfactorily proved and it could not proved beyond doubt offences against accused. The evidence of the victim cannot be believed because the defence of the accused is of having friendship with the victim and by non examining the JUDGMENT 8 Special case No. 227/2016 CNR NO. MHTH01­006244­2016 Investigating Officer the evidence of the victim appears to be suspicious. Therefore, the benefit of doubt goes in favour of the accused. 15. I, therefore, come to the conclusion that the defence raised by the accused that there was having friendship between victim and accused cannot be ruled out. So for the reasons given above I answered points in the negative and proceed to pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused Kalpesh Gurudas Kene is acquitted under Section 235(1) of the Cr.P.C. of the offences charged under Sections 354(d)(i) of Indian Penal Code and Section 12 of POCSO Act, 2012. 2] The accused is directed to furnish P.B. and S.B of Rs.15,000/­ to comply provision of Section 437A of Cr. P.C. 3] Bail bond of the accused is cancelled, surety is discharged. 4] The muddemal motor cycle bearing No.MH­04­DP­1085 Honda Shine of Black colour be returned to the registered owner after appeal period. 5] The Judgment is dictated and pronounced in open Court. Thane. (S.C. Khalipe) Date: 23.07.2018. Additional Sessions Judge,Thane. JUDGMENT 9 Special case No. 227/2016 CNR NO. MHTH01­006244­2016

Bail No. 2366/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) 4] The learned Counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant­accused is falsely implicated. He submitted that the applicant­accused is a gardener and working in said society since four years and there is no single complaint against him within this period. He submitted that victim's father had once quarreled with the applicant­accused and keeping grudge of that incident, the applicant­accused is falsely implicated. He submitted that entire investigation is almost completed. He is ready to abide any conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing him on bail. 5] Per contra, the learned A.P.P. opposed the application submitting that the offence is serious in respect of child. The investigation is still in progress. There are chances of tampering of witnesses and prayed for rejection of application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R., it appears that there is delay of two days in lodging the F.I.R. From the F.I.R. itself it appears that the victim­girl immediately disclosed the incident to her teacher. The F.I.R. also reveals that when gardener entered the lift, another boy of the building also entered with them. Thus, there appear room for suspicion about the allegation made in the F.I.R. Further, there is no explanation given in the F.I.R. for the delay. The material part of the investigation appears to have been .. 3 .. Bail No. 2366/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) completed. The object of bail is neither preventive nor punitive but to secure the presence of accused at the time of trial. The applicant­accused is behind bars since one and half month. Act for short) It was contended and argued that the applicant has been falsely involved in this crime with the allegation that the applicant and other accused had used criminal force against the minor victim girl and outraged her modesty and when complainant i.e. mother of the girl, questioned them, they abused and threatened the complainant and girl. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co-operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on anticipatory bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that at the time of incident the victim girl had gone to buy sandwich and at that time co-accused Imran held her hand with sexual intent and also used .. 2 .. Then, it is also contended that since the police have inquired with the applicant in connection with this offence which is registered on the basis of complaint lodged by the complainant, he apprehend arrest in this crime. Anticipatory Bail No.2368/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) applicant do not appear to be necessary. 4] Then, it is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be gone into detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether release of the applicants would hamper the process of investigation or whether the applicants would abscond if released on bail and in case of anticipatory bail it is also required to be seen as to whether the custodial interrogation of the applicant is necessary. --1-- ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN CRIMINAL BAIL APPLICATION NO.2308/2017 The applicant Bhawani Rameshwar Keer has applied for bail under section 439 of Cr. P.C. in C.R.No.I­99/2017 registered in Bhayander police station for the offence under section 363, 376(2) of Indian Penal Code and section 4,8 and 12 of POCSO Act. 2. It is contended that the applicant is falsely implicated. The investigation is practically completed. Further custody of the present applicant is not required. The applicant is well reputed person. There is no criminal antecedent. Nothing has been seized from the present applicant. Therefore, the applicant may be released on bail. This is the first bail application. 3. Investigation Officer has given say at Exh.6. 1 Order Exh.1 in Cri.Bail Appln. No. 2364/16 ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN CRI. BAIL APPLICATION NO.2364/2016 Heard Ld. Adv. Mr. Prashant Vishe for the applicant. Ld. A.P.P. Mrs. Jadhav for the State. Advocate for the applicant has submitted that he has no role to play in the said offence. His name does not appear in the F.I.R. and his full name is Charnindra Singh Ravindra Singh Soni whereas the police actually wanted to apprehend one person by the name Vicky. 4] Per contra, Ld. A.P.P. and I.O. have vehemently opposed the bail application on the ground that the name of the applicant was revealed during further investigation. The I.O. has pointed to the court that the mobile number of the present applicant was recovered from the Call Data Record of the accused No.1. The present applicant although discarded his previous sim card, however, the new sim card which he used was from the mobile phone bearing the same IMEI number. The present applicant is a habitual Pimp. One of the victims was a minor. The victim in her Sec. 164 Cr.P.C. statement has revealed his name as Vicky. He was known by the 2 Order Exh.1 in Cri.Bail Appln. No. 2364/16 name Vicky popularly but his real name is Charnindra Singh Ravindra Singh Soni. He is a habitual trafficker. 5] In the Judgment dated 30/10/2015 passed by the Hon'ble Bombay High Court in Criminal P.I.L. No. 4/2015 (Freedom Firm V/s. Commissioner of Police, Pune & Ors.), guidelines have been laid down for judicial officers while dealing with the cases of human trafficking. In the said guidelines, it has been interalia laid down in para 28 that “the court would, as a general principle, refuse bail to an accused who is shown as a trafficker in human beings as such accused pursues a career in such crime, which is prone to repetition, which is expected to have antecedents and which is generally indisposed to intimidation and threats. The Court would certainly release on bail such of the accused or co­accused as are themselves not traffickers but may be shown to have played some minor role in the commission of the offence”. 6] In the present case, the role of the applicant in trafficking girls has clearly emerged. Therefore, in view of the ratio decidendi and the guidelines laid down in the case of Freedom Firm (supra), this is not at all a fit case for granting bail. In view thereof, I am inclined to reject the application. ORDER Bail Application is rejected. Thane. ( Mridula V.K.Bhatia ) Dt:­05/10/2016. Dist. Judge – 08 and Special Judge (POCSO), Thane. 3 Order Exh.1 in Cri.Bail Appln. No. 2364/16

Judgment Special Case No. 231/2014 Received on : 06.11.2014 Registered on : 06.11.2014 Decided on : 27.10.2015 Duration : 0Ys.11Ms.21Ds. IN THE COURT OF D.J.­6 & ADDL. SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE (Presided over by Hemant M. Patwardhan) Special Case No. 231/2014 Exh.No. 1.State of Maharashtra, (Kalwa Police station, Thane) ..Complainant V/s. 1. Rony Narendra Datta Age 35 years Occ. R/at. Jailaxmi Apartment, 2nd floor, R.No. 204, Near Lakadi pool, Lokmanyanagar Pada no.3, Thane ..Accused Appearance:­ APP Shri. Mishra for the State Advocate Shri Baba Shaikh for the accused JUDGMENT (Delivered on this 27th day of October, 2015) Accused Rony Datta was facing trial under sections 372, 373, 366A, 370, 376 read with 34 of IPC read with section 4,7,8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and further 4,5,6 and 9 of PITA Act on following facts. 1 to 14 Judgment Special Case No. 231/2014 1] That during April, 2014 to 11.08.2014 at Ravikiran Co­op. Hsg. Society, A­Wing, R.No.1, Manishanagar, Old Mumbai Pune road, Kalwa, Thane at Jailaxmi Apartment, R. No. 204, Lokmanya Nagar Pada No.3, near Lakadi pool, Thane, Durga Residency Lodging and Boarding, R. No. 108, Ganesh Industrial Estate, behind Night lover, Upwan Pokhran No.1, Thane (W) and Bangalore accused has sold the victim for immoral and unlawful purpose viz. prostitution and at the same time and place bought the victim girl knowingly that she was below age of 18 years with intent to employ her for purposes of prostitution. According to allegation accused along with absconding accused in furtherance of their common intention had abducted minor victim from Bangladesh to compel her do the act of prostitution and were knowingly or likely that said victim will be forced to illicit intercourse with customers and accordingly had detained her for forcible illegal act and during aforesaid period has actually committed rape on victim girl. According to the allegations, accused during said period has committed penetrating sexual assault on the victim girl and were living on the earning on the victim girl during the said period and for that purpose has detained the victim girl in his premises for carrying on prostitution and thus accused person was prosecuted and after completion of investigation was charge­sheeted for having committed aforesaid offences. 2 to 14 Judgment Special Case No. 231/2014 2] Accused since the date of arrest was in judicial custody. My learned predecessor was pleased to frame charge on 02.05.2015 at Exh.6 and has certified that the contents of the said charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. Accused has pleaded not guilty and claim to be tried. His defence was that of total denial and that he has been falsely implicated in the case, though he has tried to help the victim to come out of the situation. On the basis of aforesaid facts following points arise for my consideration and I record my findings against each of them for the reasons noted below:­ S.N Points Findings 1] Does prosecution prove that accused along with absconding ..Negative accused in furtherance of common intention from April, 2014 to 11.08.2014 at Ravikiran Co­op. Hsg. society, A­wing, R. No.1, Manishanagar, Old Mumbai Pune road, Kalwa, Thane, at Jailaxmi Apartment, R. No. 204, Lokmanya nagar Pada no.3, near Lakadi pool, Thane, Durga Residency Lodging and Boarding, R. No. 108, Ganesh Industrial Estate, behind Night lover, Upwan Pokhran no.1, Thane (W) and Bangalore sold a person below eighteen years of age i.e. victim girl or for any unlawful and immoral purposes, viz. prostitution and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 372 read with 34 of Indian Penal Code? 2] Does prosecution prove that accused along with absconding ..Negative accused in furtherance of common intention on the same date, time and place, bought victim girl who at that time was below eighteen years of age with intent that the said victim girl shall be employed for the purpose of prostitution and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 373 read with 34 of I.P.C? 3] Does the prosecution prove that accused along with absconding ..Negative accused in furtherance of common intention on the same date, time and place, inducted victim girl, a minor girl under the age of eighteen years to go from Bangladesh or to do act of prostitution with intent that the said victim girl may be or 3 to 14 Judgment Special Case No. 231/2014 knowing that it is likely that the said victim girl will be forced to illicit intercourse with customers and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 366A read with 34 of I.P.C.? 4] Does the prosecution prove that accused along with absconding ..Negative accused in furtherance of common intention on the same date, time and place, sold victim girl, the person in question against her will and detained her for illegal act and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 370 read with 34 of I.P.C.? 5] Does the prosecution prove that accused along with absconding ..Negative accused in furtherance of common intention on the same date, time and place, committed rape on victim girl and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 376 read with 34 of I.P.C.? 6] Does the prosecution prove that accused along with absconding ..Negative accused on the above said day, date, time and place, committed penetrative sexual assault on the victim girl by penetrating your penis and you have thereby committed an offence under section 4 of Protection of Children From Sexual offences Act, 2012 ? 7] Does prosecution prove that accused, along with absconding ..Negative accused on the above said day, date, time and place, committed offence of sexual assault on victim girl punishable under section 7 read with section 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012? 8] Does the prosecution prove that accused along with absconding ..Negative accused on the same date, time and place, you knowingly lives, wholly or in part, on the earnings of the prostitution and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 4 of PITA Act ? 9] Does the prosecution prove that accused along with absconding ..Negative accused on the same date, time and place, procures or attempts to procure without consent for the purpose of prostitution and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 5 of PITA Act? 10] Does the prosecution prove that accused along with absconding ..Negative accused on the same date, time and place detained the victim girl in a premises where prostitution is carried on and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 6 of PITA Act? 11] Does the prosecution prove that accused along with absconding ..Negative accused on the same date, time and place having custody of said victim girl abets the seduction for prostitution of that victim girl and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 9 of PITA Act? 12] What order ? Accused is acquitted as per final order. 4 to 14 Judgment Special Case No. 231/2014 REASONS As to point nos. 1 to 12 :­ 3] All these points are interlinked with each other, therefore are discussed and consider at once. Prosecution in the present matter has initially alleged that accused no.1 with the help of absconding accused in furtherance of their common intention has initially abducted minor victim from Bangladesh to India with an intent to use her unlawfully and immorally for the purpose of prostitution with further intention of involving her in such immoral activities has not only detain in the room owned by accused no.1 in the matter but at the same time during her stay in the room of accused no.1 has committed rape, penetrating sexual assaults on the victim girl and also knowingly lives on the earning of the prostitution during that period. At the same time it was also alleged that the accused person had procured the consent of the victim by force and thus, they have committed all aforesaid offence. Prosecution in order to prove the guilt of the accused has accordingly examined victim, independent witness Bharat Dagadu, panch witness Sanjay Ram, independent witness Ravindra Chavan, woman Kamble, I.O. Out of the said witness examined, witness no.2 is the transporter of luggage of the accused from one place to other, 5 to 14 Judgment Special Case No. 231/2014 witness no.5 is the servant of the social organization by name Justice and Care who has received the information about transportation of victim from Bangalore to Vashi and who has allegedly rescued the victim while she was at Vashi Bus stand, witness Vijay Kamble has recorded the statement of victim at the relevant time with the help of victim and interpreter Smt. Bora, witness no.8 was the owner of the premises where Rony Datta was allegedly residing at the relevant time of his arrest. PW7 was investigating officer who has investigated the matter and has charge­sheeted the accused. Therefore, out of these eight witnesses the material witness was victim herself viz. P.W.1. Therefore, her evidence has to be scrutinized in the light of the allegations of the prosecution in the matter. 4] Before scrutinizing the evidence of the victim, it would not be out of place to mention that after the evidence of the prosecution, statements of the accused were recorded and arguments of rival advocates were heard. Advocate of victim has filed written notes of arguments at Exh.25 through the learned APP. Also heard Learned APP on behalf of the State. Learned APP has specifically pointed out that the victim has specifically deposed in terms of the case of the prosecution so far as present accused is concerned and has requested to convict the accused atleast for the offence punishable under section 4 and 5 of PITA Act, section 370 of IPC for having 6 to 14 Judgment Special Case No. 231/2014 detained the victim for his unlawful and immoral purposes viz. prostitution. On the other hand according to defence, prosecution has miserably failed to prove guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt. According to defence the victim has admitted the fact that present accused has not only helped her to make a telephonic call to her brother for her help and has further admitted the fact that present accused has forced her to leave the company of others on the ground they are not good person to be resided with. Hence, according to learned advocate of the defence as a matter of fact present accused has tried to help her out from the situation and he himself was unnecessarily implicated in the matter. According to the defence there was absolutely no allegations either about committing any sexual assault by the present accused nor in respect of living on the earning of the victim by the present accused. Hence, he has requested to acquit the accused. 5] Victim’s advocate in written argument Exh.25 has elaborated the way in which victim was abducted and induced by the accused in furtherance of their common intention and as to how accused was forced to do prostitution during her stay with the present accused. It was also pointed out that accused was living on the earning of the victim and thus, he has committed offence under section 4 and 5 of PITA Act. It was also pointed out that act of abducting minor victim from her 7 to 14 Judgment Special Case No. 231/2014 country was itself with an intention to use her for immoral purpose of prostitution and from the date of her abduction till her rescue she was not only assaulted by absconding accused but her transportation was for the specific purpose of inducing her to do an act of prostitution. Hence, according to victim’s advocate prosecution has proved guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubt and requested to convict the accused as per the provisions of law. Learned advocate has relied upon series of Judgments including the Judgment of parent High Court in case of Mahadev Jagtap V/s. State of Maharashtra that conviction of the accused can be based on the sole testimony of victim wherein the testimony of the victim was wholly truth worthy, reliable and need not be require corroboration in support thereof. On the basis of aforesaid rulings referred and attached with the arguments, victim’s advocate has requested to convict the accused. On aforesaid rival arguments now the deposition of the victim is scrutinized. 6] In the present matter victim was examined on oath as on the date of recording of her statement she has already completed the age of majority. She has specifically narrated as to how accused Farhad has forced her to leave her house, had sexual intercourse with her while she was forced to live with Farhad in her own country at Bangladesh and then as to how accused Farhad brought her to India with the help of 8 to 14 Judgment Special Case No. 231/2014 his friends and accused Salim. Till her journey from her own country to Kalwa there was absolutely no allegations against present accused either that accused had any common intention with said accused Farhad or Salim or had played any active or indirect role in transportation of the victim from her own country to India. Therefore, even there are specific allegations in initial part of her deposition against the absconding accused they are certainly not sufficient to establish the nexus between the absconding accused and the present accused. As per the settled proposition of law to substantiate evidence before the court is of material importance to prove the guilt of accused. In the instant case as observed above till her arrival at Kalwa as there are absolutely no allegations against the present accused either in respect of sale or commission of rape or commission of penetrative sexual assault during that period. 7] Allegations are appears to be made against the present accused by uttering the facts that she was resided in the house of Rony for about 5 to 6 days and during that period accused Rony had ask her to do Gandha Kam. However, except said statement the victim has no where made any allegations of any force being used by the present accused for inducing her to involve in prostitution. It was further contended by her that accused Rony had allowed her to make telephonic call to her brother where she had informed her brother about other 9 to 14 Judgment Special Case No. 231/2014 details and her brother had ask accused Rony to take care of the victim. Further allegations were made that after her stay of 5 to 6 days with accused Rony accused Rony had just reached her to a room at Lokmanyanagar where some girls were residing. There are absolutely no avernments and allegations that Rony was anyway connected with room at Lokmanyanagar where the victim was residing with other 3­4 girls for 3­4 days or till she was departed to Bangalore. Allegations are made that some other person had come there and took her to Durga hotel where she was require to do Gandha Kam with customers. It was also alleged by her that one Anjali had sent her to Bangalore. The victim though has made specific allegations against said Anjali or person who had taken her to Durga hotel, the investigating officer was not able to trace them out so as to link the allegations with the present accused. During the entire deposition the victim has no where alleged that present accused himself has abducted her from her country to Kalwa or that induced her to go to Bangalore for doing prostitution work and any amount she has received by doing prostitution is used by this accused. On the other hand during her cross examination she has admitted that some other person had taken her to Bangalore and had induced her to continue with her work of prostitution. It was also admitted by her that from 10 to 14 Judgment Special Case No. 231/2014 Bangalore she has contacted Rony who asked her to leave company of those persons on the ground that they are not good persons. Having regards to the said admission it is difficult to say that present accused was directly or indirectly involve in kidnapping the victim or inducing her to continue in the prostitution work or had actually committed the offence of living on the earning of the work of prostitution allegedly carried out by victim. 8] Prosecution in the present matter was required to establish the link of chain between the various spots were the alleged incident had occurred and then was required to establish and prove the fact that house where alleged raid was conducted by prosecution were possessed by the present accused. However, panch witnesses examined by prosecution to prove said fact has turned hostile and did not support the case of prosecution. Further, though allegations were made by the prosecution that 3­4 other ladies were also rescued from the room possessed by the present accused none of them were produced before the court for deposing in respect of the said incident or in respect of the fact that accused Rony was really living on the earning of the prostitution. Prosecution could have easily complete the chain of link by procuring presence of those victim girls who allegedly were rescued from the house of present accused. However, for the reason best known to the 11 to 14 Judgment Special Case No. 231/2014 prosecution said witnesses were never produced before the court so as to complete the link and to establish nexus between the allegation and the accused. Having regards to all these facts though solitary testimony of victim as held by the parent High Court is sufficient to convict the accused, it was further held by their Lordship that it should be reliable and trust­worthy and it need not require any corroboration in support thereof. In the instant case as a matter of fact the victim in her sole testimony has neither alleged any of the ingredients of the offence with which the present accused was charge­sheeted and in absence of the corroborative evidence it is difficult to accept that her testimony is really truth worthy as argued by the victim’s advocate. In view of this particular facts though various other Judgments were relied upon by the victim’s advocate the court need not refer those Judgments in absence of cogent and consistent proof of accused having committed the aforesaid offences. At the cost of repetition I would like to state that victim being the material witness was required to make specific allegation so far as the role attributed to the present accused by the prosecution in the matter. However, in the substantive evidence as observed above she has not categorically stated any of the ingredients or any of the facts which really make her testimony reliable and truth worthy so far as allegations of prosecution are concerned. Having regards 12 to 14 Judgment Special Case No. 231/2014 to all above facts it is difficult to accept that prosecution has establish the guilt beyond reasonable doubt. As observed above, remaining witnesses were formal witnesses who have neither seen the offence allegedly committed by the accused nor were present on the spot when the alleged offence were committed. They were only transporter of the luggage between the two premises, owner of the premises where accused was residing and the witnesses who have rescued the victim after her return from Bangalore. Therefore, none of the deposition of the said witnesses were useful to say that accused Rony has really committed offence as alleged by the prosecution in the matter. On the contrary as per the admission of the victim herself he appears to have help her to come out of the situation. In view of the said facts I do not hesitate to record my findings against points in the negative and proceed to pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused is hereby acquitted of the offence punishable under sections 372,373, 366A, 370, 376 r/w 34 of IPC read with section 4,7,8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and 4,5,6 and 9 of PITA Act. 2] Accused be set at liberty if not require in any other matter as he is in judicial custody since the date of his arrest till date. 13 to 14 Judgment Special Case No. 231/2014 3] Inform jailer accordingly. 4] Muddemal property clothes etc. being worthless be destroyed after appeal period. 5] Accused however, is directed to execute P.R. bond of Rs.5000/­ under amended provisions of the section 437(A) of Cr.P.C. and the bonds so executed shall remain in force for a period of six months. Thane (Hemant M.Patwardhan) Date: 27.10.2015 D.J.­6 & Additional Sessions Judge, Thane. 14 to 14

Investigating Officer recorded the statement of witnesses. He arrested the accused and sent the charge­sheet. 4. My Ld. Predecessor has framed the charge against the accused at Exh.3 under section 354(A)(D) of Indian Penal Code and section 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. He pleaded not guilty. 5. Considering the evidence on record following points arose for my determination. I have given its findings with reasons as under­ Sr.No Points Findings 1. Does prosecution prove that in between In Negative June 2014 to 23.08.2014 at Manishnagar, Gate No.1, Near Swimming Pool, Kalwa, Thane the accused used criminal force to the victim aged 16 years with intent to outrage her modesty and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 354(A)(D) of Indian Penal Code? 2. Does prosecution prove that during the In Negative said period the accused committed sexual assault upon the minor victim aged 16 years and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 8 of POCSO Act? 3. What order? As per final order REASONS AS TO POINT NOS.1 TO 3:­ 6. The prosecution has examined victim at Exh.6, her father at Exh.8 and Investigating Officer Sachin Bharat Kothmire at Exh.12. The name of the victim and her father need not be disclosed. 7. As per the evidence of victim in August 2014 she was 16 years old. She was knowing accused Sagar as he would visit her society and they were talking with each other on facebook for about one year. In June 2014 she had gone with her friends for picnic. After that she met the accused Sagar Rode. He disliked it and therefore, he slapped her. She disclosed that incident to her parents, at that time her parents were at Silvasa. Her father gave understanding to accused on phone. After that also accused would follow victim that was continued for many days, therefore, her parents gone to the house of accused and given him understanding, but he did not listen it. 8. On 23.08.2014 when the victim was going to college the accused was standing near Taran Talao. The accused came near her, so she shouted, the accused went away. So finally she lodged FIR in Kalwa police station which is at Exh.7. 9. The father of the victim has stated that there was friendship between his daughter and accused on face book. In June 2014 his daughter had gone for outing with her friends. So accused slapped her, after that he was following her. So he met the accused personally and asked to stop this. He further stated that on 23.08.2014 his daughter was going to college. Accused caught her hands and made comments upon her and therefore, his daughter sustained mental pains. 10. The victim has admitted in her cross­examination that there were talking between she and accused on face book. She would meet the accused on the terrace of their building along with her friend Shubhangi. She admits her mobile no. 9619502813 and she would chatting on mobile phone and that chatting was continued till August 2014. She admitted that Remya was friend of accused and Remya was residing adjacent to her house. She admits that she would meet accused at Remya's house when her mother and father was not at home. She stated that she and her elder sister were residing with their grand parents at Kalwa. She further admits the print out of whatsapp chatting between she and accused. She admits mobile number in that print out. She admits the contents in the chatting were correct. She admits that her parents did not know that she was chatting with accused on mobile phone. Her parents did not know that she was chatting with the accused on facebook. She did not tell her parents that she used to chat with accused on facebook and mobile. She admits that in that chatting there is reference of Angha her cousin sister and Remya and she admits that there was chatting about meeting between she and accused at Remya's house when there was nobody at her house. She admits that in June 2014 accused Sagar slapped her, but she did not complain to police station because it was a minor thing, therefore, she did not lodge complaint to police. She admits that till August 2014 her daily routine was going on. 11. The father of the victim has admitted that he did not know that his daughter was chatting with accused on mobile phone and face book and he did not know that accused would meet his daughter on their house and they would meet with each other at Remya's house. In June 2014 he came to know for first time that Sagar was the friend of his daughter. 12. The accused has put the defence in the cross examination and in the statement under section 313 of Cr.P.C statement that he was good friend of victim, but the victim would consumed Vodka and Beer and that was disliked by him. He would gave understanding to the victim not to consume Vodka and Beer, otherwise he will tell her parents, but she did not listen and due to fear that he will disclose this fact to her parents the victim has made false complaint against him. 13. I heard the Ld. Counsel on behalf of accused. He submitted that there was no complaint when the accused allegedly slapped the victim in June 2014. The victim herself says that it was a minor thing and that incident was took place on 23.08.2014, but FIR was given on 25.08.2014. There is delay of 2 and half day and it is not explained. He relied upon the decision in following cases on the point of delay in lodging the FIR. State of Andhra Pradesh V/s. M. Madhusudhan Rao 2009ALL MR (Cri) 547(S. C.). Criminal Procedure Code (1973) S.154­ Penal Code (1860), “S. 498A­Delay in lodging F.I.R­ Delay, unless satisfactorily explained, held, is fatal to the prosecution case. In the present case, the order of acquittal of the respondent is well merited and does not call for interference, particularly when the First Information Report was lodged by the complainant more than one month after the alleged incident of forcible poisoning. Time and again, the object and importance of prompt lodging of the First Information report has been highlighted. Delay in lodging the First Information Report, more often than not, results in embellishment and exaggeration, which is a creature of an afterthought. A delayed report not only gets bereft of the advantage of spontaneity, the danger of the introduction of coloured version, exaggerated account of the incident or a concocted story as a result of deliberations and consultations, also creeps in, casting a serious doubt on its veracity. Therefore, it is essential that the delay in lodging the report should be satisfactorily explained”. The State of Maharashtra V/s. Sanjay Sheshrao Suryawanshi and ors 2015 ALL MR (Cri) 1927. “Criminal P.C (1973) S.154­FIR­Delay in lodging­Has to be satisfactorily explained. Delay in lodging the First Information Report, more often than not, results in embellishment and exaggeration, which is a creature of an afterthought. A delayed report not only gets bereft of the advantage of spontaneity, the danger of the introduction of coloured version, exaggerated account of the incident or a concocted story as a result of deliberations and consultations, also creeps in, casting a serious doubt on its veracity. Therefore, it is essential that the delay in lodging the report should be satisfactorily explained”. Mohammed Farooq Abdul Rauf V/s. State of Maharashtra 2010 Cri. L. J. 1468. It is held that, “Rape­ victim a minor girl­ mother of victim admitting previous dispute between her family and accused. Incident allegedly occurred in afternoon, however, prosecutrix and her mother admitting in cross­examination that prosecutrix attended school from 10.00 a.m. to 5.30 p.m. on day of incident. Prosecutrix also admitting in her cross that her parents had beaten her when she had not deposed about incident on previous date. Indicating that prosecutrix was tutored witness. Non examination of alleged eye witnesses. Though hymen of prosecutrix was torn no other injuries found on her person. Probability of false accusation cannot be ruled out”. 14. The Counsel further submitted that the victim has concealed certain facts from the police and from her parents. She would meet the accused at Remya's house when there were nobody at her house. She would also meet accused on the terrace of their building. She would also chat with the accused on mobile phone and face book. The accused disliked that she consumed Vodka and Beer and therefore, due to fear of that the false complaint was lodged. 15. In reply the Ld. A.P.P. submitted that the offence under section 354(A)(D) of Indian Penal Code and section 8 of POCSO Act clearly proved by the prosecution beyond doubt, therefore, accused may be convicted. 16. Considering the evidence on record the court is of the view that it is admitted fact that the victim and accused were friends. They would chat on facebook and mobile phone. This is admitted fact that they would meet with each other on the terrace of victim's building and at Remy's house whenever nobody at her house and that was continued for more than one year. The victim admits that the chatting was continued till August 2014. 17. The victim herself says that the incident of slapping her by the accused was a minor thing, therefore, she did not disclose it to police and did not complaint about that. Therefore, there is no question before this court about that incident. The father of the victim has also not complained about that incident when he came to know about that incident. There is no reason why they had not complaint about that. 18. The victim thereafter continued to chat with the accused on mobile phone and facebook till August 2014. Therefore, the victim herself had waived that incident. 19. It is evident that the victim did not disclose to her parents and grand parents where she was residing that she would use to chat with the accused on mobile phone and facebook and she would meet accused at terrace and at Remya's house whenever nobody at her house. 20. It is evidence that the parents of the victim did not know that accused was the friend of victim till the incident of June 2014. 21. The mobile chatting was produced by the accused and its contents are admitted by the victim. In that chatting there was reference of victim's cousin sister Angha and Remya. There was chatting about the meeting between them when there would be nobody in Remya's house. 22. There is no corroboration between victim and her father on the material points and particulars. The victim does not say that on 23.08.2014 the accused caught her hand and made comments upon her. But her father says so. The victim does not say that she has disclosed that accused had caught her hands and made comments. So on this point there was no corroboration between victim and her father. 23. Considering the admitted facts that the victim would meet the accused at Remya's house and on the terrace on their building, but she does not complain that the accused had sexually assaulted her during those meetings. There was opportunity to sexually assault to victim, but accused did not do so when there where nobody in the Remya's house and on the terrace. 24. Coming to the incident of 23.08.2014 it is evident that when the victim was going to her college the accused came near her, but she does not say that accused had touch her private parts or touched her breast so as to outrage her modesty with sexual intent. Therefore, merely by standing accused on the way does not mean that there was sexual intent. The accused did not touch the victim at that time and did not comment upon her. He did not utter any word, did not disclose anything to her. He did not say anything to her. So it is very difficult to infer that he had any sexual intent at that time when the accused was standing on the road near Taran Talao. The accused came near her, but when the victim shouted he went away. If really the accused had any sexual intent to molest the victim he would have touch her or did something, but he did not do so. Even prior to that also when he had any opportunity he would have done something with the victim. The court is of the view that the alleged incident of slapping in June 2014 is already waived by the victim and therefore, that cannot be considered together with the incident of 23.08.2014 and incident of 23.08.2014 is very insufficient to attract the offence under section 354(A)(D) and Section 8 of POCSO Act. 25. So considering the facts and circumstances of this case the court come to the conclusion that the prosecution has failed to prove the ingredients of the offence beyond doubt and therefore, accused cannot be held guilty. Accordingly, I pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused Sagar Nivrutti Rode is acquitted under Section 235(1) of Cr.P.C. of the offence charged under sections 354(A)(D) of Indian Penal Code and section 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2 Accused is directed to furnish P.B. and S.B. of Rs.15,000/­ (Rupees Fifteen Thousand Only) to comply provision of section 437 (A) of Cr. P.C. 3 The Judgment is dictated and pronounced in open Court. Thane. (S.C. Khalipe) Date: 27.09.2017. Additional Sessions Judge,Thane.

Judgment Sessions Case No. 233/14 Received on : 13.08.2014 Registered on : 13.08.2014 Decided on : 13.05.2016 Duration : 1Y. 9 Ms. 0Ds. IN THE COURT OF D.J.­6 & ADDL. SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE (Presided over by Hemant M. Patwardhan) Special Case No. 233/2014 Exh.No. 1.State of Maharashtra, (Bhoiwada Police station, Bhiwandi) ..Complainant V/s. Abdul Kalam Shaikh. Age 45 years, Occ. Shopkeeper, R/at. R. No. 668, Sabaj Kirana Stores, Bhiwandi, Dist. Thane Dist. Thane ..Accused Appearance:­ APP Smt. Kapare for the State Advocate Shri. Patankar for the accused JUDGMENT (Delivered on this 13th day of May, 2016) Accused was facing trial under section 376(2)(L) of IPC read with section 3 and 4 of The Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 on following facts. 1] That accused prior to 11.08.2014 at his room at 3 rd 1 To 18 Judgment Sessions Case No. 233/14 galli, Devunagar, behind Alamgir video, New Taware compound, Bhiwandi Dist. Thane committed rape on victim girl aged about 13 years from time to time by giving enticement to her by giving Rs.10/­ and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 376(2)(L) of Indian Penal Code. According to the accusation accused during aforesaid date, time and place committed penetrative sexual assault on the victim and thus on complaint lodged by the complainant an offence punishable under aforesaid sections came to be registered against him. After completion of investigation, he was charge­ sheeted. 2] My learned predecessor was pleased to frame charge against accused on 27.03.2015 and certified that particulars of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. Accused pleaded not guilty and claim to be tried. His defence was of total denial and that he has been falsely implicated in the matter to avoid payment of huge outstanding of purchase of grocery material from him. 3] On the basis of aforesaid facts, trial was conducted. Prosecution in order to prove the guilt of the accused has examined victim as PW1, support person Bharati Choudhari as PW2, Dr. Aditya Jevale as PW3, mother of victim as PW4, 2 To 18 Judgment Sessions Case No. 233/14 independent witness Sarfuddin Ansari as PW5, medical officer Dr. Mrs. Swati Raju Kale as PW6, PSO Mr. Dyaneshwar Tambe, I.O. Suresh Aher PW8, Dr. Rucha Joshi, Medical officer of Thane Mental Hospital as PW9. After evidence of the prosecution, statement of accused was recorded as per his say. During his statement also accused has reiterated his stand of his false implication to avoid payment of amount which the complainant's parents owes to him. After recording the statement arguments of rival advocates were heard. 4] At the time of argument learned APP has specifically pointed out that all the witnesses examined by the prosecution has supported the case and has proved the fact that accused has committed heinous act as alleged against him. According to the submissions though delay is caused in lodging the complaint, the same has been properly explained by the father of the victim and thus same is not fatal to prosecution. According to the submissions of learned APP the victim has narrated as to how the accused used to commit rape and her deposition has been corroborated by her statement under section 164 of Cr.P.C. and deposition of her parents. According to learned APP medical report has corroborated the allegations. Hence, learned APP by relying upon Judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in pursis dated 28.04.2016 has requested to convict the accused. 3 To 18 Judgment Sessions Case No. 233/14 5] On the other hand it was specifically pointed out by the defence that though learned APP has argued that delay has been properly explained, the same is not corroborated on record as neither the victim nor her mother who are the material witnesses in the matter have made any whisper as to why the delay was caused. Further it was pointed out that though the complaint was lodged about alleged act of rape on 11.08.2014, the victim has never stated that any such sexual assault was made on that date. According to submissions though allegations were made about forcible commission of rape or commission of penetrative sexual assault on the victim girl, no such evidence is brought on record about the same. According to the submissions if there would have been really such heinous act on 7 to 8 occasions earlier, then the victim either would have made grievance of it before her parents, either immediately of the incident or at­least later on. According to the submissions if such act of forcible rape is really committed then the minor victim would not have able to sustain from the said act of accused and her physical conduct would have sufficient to revealed the act itself. However, when no allegations were made about her making complaint on any earlier occasion or any grievance of her parents on those occasions, the defence of the accused of his false implication for 4 To 18 Judgment Sessions Case No. 233/14 avoiding payment of the amount due is more probable. According to defence medical evidence is not supporting prosecution and medical officer has clearly admitted that insertion of foreign body in the present case is not ruled out. Hence, according to the submissions as the deposition of the victim is not corroborated by any other evidence and as it does not inspire the confidence, the same is not sufficient to convict the accused under such serious offence. Hence, he has requested to acquit the accused from all the charges. 6] On the basis of aforesaid facts and rival arguments, following points arise for my consideration and I record my findings against each of them for the reasons noted below:­ S.N Points Findings 1] Does prosecution prove that accused since prior to 11.08.2014 ..Negative at his room at 3rd galli, Devunagar, behind Alamgir video, New Taware compound, Bhiwandi Dist. Thane committed rape on victim girl aged about 13 years from time to time by giving enticement to her by giving Rs.10/­ and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 376(2)(L) of Indian Penal Code? 2] Does prosecution prove that accused on the same date, time ..Negative and place committed penetrative sexual assault on the victim girl by penetrating his penis and thereby committed an offence under section 3 and 4 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012? 3] What order ? Accused is acquitted as per final order. 5 To 18 Judgment Sessions Case No. 233/14 REASONS As to point nos. 1 to 3 :­ 7] These three points are interlinked with each other and therefore are consider at once. In the present matter the victim has claimed that accused on 11.08.2014 and 7 to 8 occasions prior to that date has committed forcible rape on her by giving enticement of Rs.10/­ and at the same time has committed penetrating sexual assault on aforesaid occasions. Hence, prosecution was required to establish the particular allegations by reliable and consistent evidence which inspire confidence about occurrence of the incident at the particular time, place and date. Prosecution in order to establish it has accordingly examined aforesaid witnesses. 8] As per the allegations of the prosecution on 11.08.2014 accused has committed rape on the victim and also that on 7 to 8 occasions prior to that date he has committed same act by giving enticement of Rs.10/­ after each such assault. Hence, material witness of the prosecution was the victim and her mother as according to allegations the victim has informed her mother about the said incident immediately after incident dated 11.08.2014. 9] On perusal of the deposition it appears that the 6 To 18 Judgment Sessions Case No. 233/14 victim has clearly stated that the incident occurred on 11th of April at about 6.00 p.m. when the accused asked her to visit his house and immediately left her house. She then immediately followed him but as neighbourer of the accused Mr. Mulla i.e. P.W. No. 5 has seen her going towards the house of the accused, accused had asked her to go back. Then Mr. Mulla had intimated about said fact to her mother. It was further deposed by the victim that her mother then made inquiries with her as to why she visited the house of accused and then she had informed her mother about the incident. She disclosed that the accused previously on around ten occasions had committed “gandha kam” with her and has paid Rs.10/­ after it. 10] The victim was cross­examined at length and it has brought on record that she never visited the shop of accused and has admitted that her parents are customer of the shop of accused and family of the accused is residing with him and on the date of incident family was present in the house which is situated above the shop. She has further admitted that she has narrated the incident to support person and then she has narrated it before police. 11] In the present matter it is allegation and accusation of the prosecution that the victim is handicap and mentally 7 To 18 Judgment Sessions Case No. 233/14 retarded person and she was not able to disclose the incident properly before police therefore only her complaint was recorded through support person Smt. Bharati Choudhari. The said support person was called as witness no.2. Her services were also utilized by the court while recording deposition of the victim, as victim was not able to depose before the court by independently understanding the meaning and importance of her deposition. Hence, her deposition was recorded with the help of the support person. Though, accusations were made that victim is mentally retarded and prosecution has tried to bring that fact through witness no.9 Dr. Mrs. Rucha Joshi wherein she has only deposed that patient was referred to her for examination and certificate Exh.50 was issued by her wherein she has recorded impression “epilepsy with sub­normal intelligence”. She has explained that intelligence of the victim was below normal and therefore such patient may not be in a position to understand the words spoken by others and it would be difficult for the patient to express the incident occurred with him or her. During cross examination she has admitted that she has not conducted any further test like I.Q. Level test of the patient as such facility was not available at Thane Mental Hospital. Hence, from the deposition of the said doctor it 8 To 18 Judgment Sessions Case No. 233/14 appears that intelligence level of the victim was below normal and in view of the deposition of Dr. Joshi it is difficult for her to express the incident occurred to her. On the background of Doctor's evidence now deposition of the victim girl has to be scrutinized in the light of the defence of the accused person. 12] Accused has taken a defence of his false implication on the ground of avoiding payment of amount which the complainant's parents owes to him in sale and purchase transaction of grocery articles. It is not in dispute that the accused is running grocery shop and parents of the victim were his customers. The mother of the victim has specifically admitted it along with an amount of Rs.10,000/­ is outstanding against them. As observed above as victim was not of normal intelligence level she was not expected to describe the incident with minute details. However, when she described the incident broadly that has to be consider against accused provided the same is corroborated by the deposition of either parents of the victim or other independent witnesses. 13] Learned APP has relied upon Judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in case of State of Rajasthan V/s. Omprakash, (2002)5 Supreme Court Cases 745 in which Hon'ble their Lordship of Hon'ble Apex Court has specifically held that 9 To 18 Judgment Sessions Case No. 233/14 testimony of the child witness needs to be carefully evaluated and must find adequate corroboration before it can be relied upon. Hence, while appreciating the evidence the court must look for corroboration to the testimony of the child witness in normal course also. In the present matter the victim being patient of below intelligence her deposition has to be carefully evaluated with corroboration of the other witnesses. As it is the case of the prosecution after the incident dated 11.08.2014 the victim has immediately inquired by her mother about the incident and then she has disclosed all those facts. Therefore, evidence of her mother is to be scrutinized to find out whether the same really corroborate victim's deposition or not. 14] On perusal of her deposition it appears that her mother PW4 has stated that one Sarfuddin informed her that the complainant had gone to the house of the accused and therefore she went to the house of the accused but could not find complainant there and when she returned back to her house she found complainant there. She then only deposed that complainant has informed her that on some previous occasions also accused had molest her and therefore, on 13.08.2014 she lodged the complaint. Hence, from the deposition of the witness it nowhere appears that she has really corroborated the deposition of the victim. 10 To 18 Judgment Sessions Case No. 233/14 15] The material allegation against the accused was in respect of the incident dated 11.08.2014. However, even if we consider the deposition of both the witnesses as it is then also except visiting the house of accused on that date nothing had happened which can be made punishable either under section 376 of IPC or under section 3 and 4 of POCSO Act. Mere using the word that the accused has committed “gandha kam” on 7 to 8 previous occasions will itself not suffice the purpose of the prosecution. Prosecution was required to establish that fact by evidence which inspire confidence. In the instant case though the victim has stated that she has lodged the complaint herself the deposition of PSO and mother of the victim along with evidence of medical officer goes to show that the victim was not able to state facts about the incident while recording the complaint and therefore, either the support person has stated the facts before the PSO or mother of the victim has stated those facts. 16] Further as observed aforesaid on the date i.e. 11.08.2014 there was absolutely no incident occurred which can be said to be covered under the provisions of section 376 of IPC or 3 and 4 of POCSO Act. Even if we consider the allegation of the victim that on 7 to 8 previous occasions accused has 11 To 18 Judgment Sessions Case No. 233/14 raped her then also conduct of the victim or her parents were absolutely against natural conduct of human being. The victim was about 13 years old on the alleged date of incident dated 11.08.2014 and she has made complaint that prior to that date on 7 to 8 occasions accused has sexually assaulted her. It will be the natural conduct of the human being on the first occasion of such sexual assault to be under frightened condition even after couple of hours even though her intelligence was below the normal level. The physical condition of person sexually assaulted for the first time can be immediately noted by atleast mother of the victim either immediately after the incident or atleast later on. In the present matter it is the allegation of the victim that the accused used to pay Rs.10/­ after every such assault and she used to purchase eatable out of the said amount and used to consume it in presence of her brother, sister and mother. However, she has admitted that none of them had made any inquiry as to how she had purchased that eatable. It is really difficult to accept that mentally retarded victim girl of tender age purchase some eatables without asking for the amount from the parents, consume it before them and they did not even inquire the source of amount or the source from where eatables are made available to her. It is the natural conduct of the human being to make such inquiries particularly when the mental condition of the victim was below normal. Hence, it is 12 To 18 Judgment Sessions Case No. 233/14 difficult to accept that prior incident as alleged has really occurred as alleged by the victim. 17] As per the observations of Hon'ble Apex Court in reported Judgment supra evidence of the minor has to be evaluated on the basis of corroboration of the evidence. No doubt in such a case independent corroboration is always ruled out. However, corroboration by the parents as they are supposed to know, understand either from the victim or by her physical appearance after the incident and the parents will be the proper witnesses to corroborate said facts. However, though it is alleged by the victim that she has narrated the incident of 11.08.2014 to her parents as there actual no incident occurred about sexual assault on that date, question of corroborating it does not arise at all. So far as alleged previous incidences are concerned, the mother had only alleged that allegations of molesty were made by the victim against the accused. Act of committing sexual assault and molest has altogether different act and therefore there appears to be no corroboration to the victim's deposition by her mother. 18] Further though the prosecution has examined independent witness Mr. Sarfuddin, his deposition was only in respect of incident dated 11.08.2014 wherein he has only 13 To 18 Judgment Sessions Case No. 233/14 deposed that he has suspected that victim was in the room of the accused. However, he could not actually get an opportunity to see the victim in accused's room at the relevant time. According to his deposition in the cross­examination he was not able to say whether the movements of clothes which were noticed by him in accused's room was that of male, female or any child. It is therefore, difficult to accept his deposition to be material piece of evidence. In the present matter the spot of incident also is not been properly established. Victim girl has alleged that the incident was occurred in the house of the accused wherein her mother has alleged that the incident took place in the room owned by the sister of the accused. If we consider the location of the shop and residence of the accused it appears to be in the market area having adjacent shop and according to the admission of the witnesses his family members were present in the house when incident dated 11.08.2014 was allegedly occurred. If family members were present in the house, accused will certainly not commit such heinous act atleast in presence of his family members. Hence, when the spot of incident itself differs from witness to witness it is difficult to accept that the incident was really occurred as alleged on the particular spot. 19] It was also argued by learned APP that if witness 14 To 18 Judgment Sessions Case No. 233/14 no.5 would not have seen the victim in the house of accused, the accused would not have quarreled with witness no.5 on next morning. No doubt witness no.5 had made a reference of altercation between them on 12.08.2014, the same has not been corroborated by any other witness. Further, the witness himself has admitted the fact that he has not stated portion marked 'A' before the police and there is no satisfactory explanation as to why this portion marked is inserted in his statement. From the aforesaid facts it appears that PW 5 having close friendly relations with parents of the victim has shown as independent witness just to suite the allegation of the complainant. 20] In the present matter the evidence of medical officer who has examined witness after the incident is also of material importance. Though, Dr. Mrs. Swati Kale has deposed that she has examined the patient and accordingly issued certificate Exh.36 wherein she has noted hymen tear 3 and 7 O'clock position. She has further deposed that patient has given history of sexual assault since last 2­3 months and lastly 4 to 5 days prior to the examination. However, in the cross examination she has admitted that as the victim was not able to communicate with her, victim's mother has given the history of assault. She has further stated the fact that any foreign body is inserted in vagina there is possibility of hymen being torn and 15 To 18 Judgment Sessions Case No. 233/14 in present matter possibility cannot be ruled out. Hence, medical evidence is not fully corroborating the facts and by the admission of the doctor, there is a scope two interpretations. As per the settled proposition of law, in such a case of two interpretations, interpretation which favours accused has to be accepted. Doctor has not even opined that the patient was habitual to such sexual intercourse. When history of forcible assault has been made there must be some injuries on the private part of the victim which were never noticed by Dr. Mrs. Kale. Hence, it appears from the medical evidence also that it is not corroborated to the deposition of the victim herself. Having regards to these facts though support person, PSO and I.O. has supported the case of prosecution, the same against the evidence of victim, her parents and independent witness nowhere inspire confidence which is sufficient for convicting the accused. The evidence brought before this court appears to be of weak nature and is not supported by the medical evidence. Further conduct of the victim and the parents is apparently against the natural conduct of human being and therefore, is sufficient to raise doubt about occurrence of the incident at the relevant time. As defence has succeeded in raising doubt in respect of occurrence of the incident, as per settled principle of law benefit has to be extended in favour of the accused. Having 16 To 18 Judgment Sessions Case No. 233/14 regards to these facts I do not hesitate to hold that prosecution has not established the allegations by cogent, consistent and reliable evidence which inspire confidence. Before parting with the findings I would like to add that there is a delay of about two days in lodging the complaint. Prosecution though has relied upon Apex Court Judgment in pursis supra, in all those cases the prosecution was succeeded in explaining the delay by plausible grounds and reasons. However in the present matter though the incident alleged to have occurred on 11.08.2014 and though victim had informed her mother about the incident on the same day itself, FIR was not lodged either on the same day or even next morning also. It was alleged on 13.08.2014 without there being any plausible explanation of delay in lodging the FIR at such belated stage either by the victim or by the mother of the victim. Even if we consider that victim's intelligence was below normal and on that ground she was not able to explain delay, her mother could have easily explained it during her statement either before the police or during her substantive evidence before the court. However, there is no such explanation in the substantive evidence before the court. Hence, such unexplained delay is obviously fatal to the prosecution. In view of the admission of the mother of the victim about transaction of sale 17 To 18 Judgment Sessions Case No. 233/14 of the grocery material and amount outstanding against her is sufficient to say that whatever defence of false implication has been put forth by the accused is probable. Having regards to all these facts I am constrained to record my findings against point no.1 and 2 in the negative and proceed to pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused is hereby acquitted from the offence punishable under section 376 of IPC and 3 and 4 of The Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] Accused is in jail since date of his arrest. Hence, he be set at liberty forthwith if not required in any other matter. 3] Muddemal property i.e. clothes of the victim and accused etc. being worthless be destroyed after appeal period. 4] Accused is further directed to execute fresh P.R. of Rs.10,000/­ in view of the amended provisions of the section 437(A) of Cr.P.C. and the bond so executed shall remain in force for a period of six months from the date of its execution. 5] Inform jailer accordingly. Thane (Hemant M.Patwardhan) Date: 13.05.2016 D.J.­6 & Additional Sessions Judge, Thane. 18 To 18

She further deposed that, on 4.4.14 at about 6.45 a.m her sister Kirti went to school. That time she was alone in house with her father. That time she :8 : Spl.C No.235/2014 (Jud.) was coming out of bed to carry the household work. That time her father told her to sleep for some time. Therefore she sleep. (Papa Ye Kya Kar Rahe Ho Aaisa Mat Karo). He told her that, keep quite, he is doing this lovingly as a father, don't misunderstand him. ("Tu Chup Baith, Ye Sab Mai Baap Ki Hasiyat Se Pyar Se Kar Raha Hu, Tu Galat Matlab Mat Nikal). He repeated his act. She resisted, therefore he threatened her to keep quite otherwise he will beat her. He tried to come closure therefore she went for bath immediately. 12.5. She further deposed that, on that day at about 8.30 a.m her mother returned to their house. She narrated the incidence to her mother. 12.6. she further deposed that this type of act her father was doing with her since last 3 years prior to 4.4.14. He used to threat her therefore she did not disclosed said incidence to anybody. When she disclosed said incidence to her mother she took her to police station. She lodged FIR Ex.18 at police station. She :9 : Spl.C No.235/2014 (Jud.) shown the spot of incidence to police. 13. In her cross­examination she deposed that:­ 13.1. Till 10th standard she was good in study. As she failed in 11th standard her father changed her college. He used to drop her and used to pick up her from college some times.
