He used to scold her if she went to wander with her friends and used to tell to do study. He also used to tell her to concentrate on study as he come to the conclusion that she is not concentrating on study. 13.2. She further deposed that, her mother is having 4 sisters and one brother. Her mother's sister used to reside at Manorama Nagar, Kolshet, Ambernath and Ulhasnagar and brother used to reside at Kolshet. She used to visit her maternal aunts and uncle frequently. She admitted that, she is residing in Kolshet since her birth and they are residing in Moreshwar Patil building since 2 to 3 years prior to the incidence. She further admitted that the said building is situated at thickly populated area. She further admitted that, the relations between her father and her maternal uncle are not good. : 10 : Spl.C No.235/2014 (Jud.) 13.3. She denied the suggestion one Komal Chiku assaulted her as she used to wander with her husband. 13.4. She admitted that on 3.4.14 Mukund Gharat told her father that she used to wander with someone. That time her mother was not in home. She further admitted that, her father came to know on 3.4.14 that she used to wander at creek with someone. She admitted that there was a dispute in their family since 1.4.14 but she denied that it was due to the reason that she used to wander here and there and not concentrating on study. 13.5. On 3.4.14 when her mother left their house her father was at home. Her mother left their house without giving any information to her father. Her father came to know that she used to wander with someone after her mother left the house. When she came to know that her father informed by Mukund Gharat that she was wandering here and there with some one, she did not went to her uncle or aunt to avoid beating from the hands of her father. Her father went outside their house on 3.4.14 at about 3 p.m and returned after 5 minutes. No one was with her when he returned. He immediately : 11 : Spl.C No.235/2014 (Jud.) inquired with her after his return that with whom she was wandering? That time her younger sister was at home. That time he scolded her and also beat her. She and her sister shouted for help. No one came for help. Due to the said assault she sustained injury on her head and abdomen. She did not sustained visible injury. After incidence of beating she did not went to the house of her uncle or aunt or did not inform to her mother. She did not inform anybody regarding beating by her father. 13.6. After incidence of beating she, her father and her sister were in house only till 6.45 a.m of 4.4.14. In the night of 3.4.14 she and her sister took dinner. Her father did not have dinner. Their house consist only hall and kitchen alongwith bathroom (mori) only. In the night of 3.4.14 they all sleep in hall on a two different mattress as usual. Usually when they used to wake up her father also used to wake up but he used to remain lying on mattress till 9 a.m. 13.7. After incidence at 6.45 a.m she did not stated said incidence to anybody outsider. When her mother returned to their house at about 8.30 p.m her father was in home. When her father went to fetch water : 12 : Spl.C No.235/2014 (Jud.) she narrated the incidence to her mother. When her mother returned to their house, within 5 to 10 minutes she narrated the incidence to her mother and then they immediately went to police station. 13.8. When she narrated incidence to her mother, her mother did not inquired with her father and she immediately took her to police station. Her mother did not asked any explanation from her father. When they left the house her father was not at home. Before leaving to police station her mother or she did not disclosed incidence to anybody. They went to Kapurbawadi Police station by auto­ rickshaw within 10 minutes. 13.9. She further admitted that, the information first time given to police by her mother and thereafter her. After they reach to police station within 20 to 25 minutes police brought her father in police station. Police inquired with her father in her presence. That time he stated to police that as she used to wander here and there with someone he assaulted her. Her father is short tempered. She was in fear that her father will assault her as he came to know that she used to wander here and there. She denied the suggestion that therefore she lodged false FIR with : 13 : Spl.C No.235/2014 (Jud.) allegation as alleged in FIR. 13.10. She further admitted that when police brought her father in police station on 4.4.14 they arrested her father immediately and after his arrest her statement/FIR was recorded by police. She denied the suggestion that she lodged FIR at the instance of her mother. 13.11. She admitted that, after filing FIR she alongwith her mother and sister alongwith their baggage went to reside on different place and after FIR there is no relations between their family and her father. She denied the suggestion that as her mother and she wants to reside separately from her father she filed false FIR against her father with collusion with her mother. 14. On the background of this evidence it is necessary to see whether her version is corroborated by other witnesses on material aspects. 15. PW.2 Kamladevi deposed exactly same in respect of age of victim and the routine of accused. She also narrated the incidence that Mukund Gharat given information to accused that victim used to wander here and there with someone and threat given by the accused to victim. She : 14 : Spl.C No.235/2014 (Jud.) also narrated the material incidence of outraging modesty of victim exactly same as narrated by victim. She deposed that said fact has stated by victim to her when she returned to her house on 4.4.14 at about 8.30 a.m. She also deposed that accused used to threat them that if they failed to act as per his wish he will throw them from auto­ rickshaw. She further deposed that to get privacy with victim accused willfully beat to her with intention that she may leave the house. She further deposed that accused used to beat her with the help of wooden log. 16. In her cross­examination she admitted that in 2012 her husband lodged missing complaint and she and her daughter were missing. She further admitted that due to the compromise done by Purnekar she again came to reside with accused. 17. She further deposed that she filed 3 to 4 time complaint to police station against her husband in respect of beating to her but she did not filed complaint against her husband stating that she used to beat her daughters and used to do physical assault on daughters. 18. She further deposed that on 3.4.14 at about 4.30 p.m she left her house and went to the house of sister at Azad Nagar by walk and reached to her house by 5 p.m. She admitted that on that day victim was using mobile. The : 15 : Spl.C No.235/2014 (Jud.) suggestion given by the defence that on 3.4.14 at about 12.30 noon she left the house with intention not to return and went to Kapurbavadi police station and filed complaint against accused and thereafter went to the house of her sister is denied. 19. She admitted that in a statement given to police on 4.4.14 she given her address as address of her sister Shraddha Bhelkar. She further admitted that after filing complaint on 4.4.14 she left the house permanently after two days and went to reside at Kalher alongwith her daughters. She further admitted that after registration of FIR she do not have any contact with accused. She denied that as she want to live separately she filed false FIR through victim. 20. The material instance that PW.2 Kamladevi filed NC against accused on 3.4.14 is appears to be suppressed by PW.2. It also appeared that PW.5 PSI Amruta Chaure, I.O also tried to suppress the previous NC dated 3.4.14 filed by PW.2 Kamladevi against accused. In cross­examination PW.5 Amruta admitted that they made every entry regarding NC and FIR in station diary. She admitted that PW.2 Kamladevi lodged NC No.449/14 dated 3.4.14 at Ex.36 to police station against accused. She also admitted the letter issued by D.R. Gore, ACP Information Officer of : 16 : Spl.C No.235/2014 (Jud.) Vartak Division Thane at Ex.37. PW.5 deposed that on 3.4.14 she was not on duty as SHO however when Ex.36 NC No.449/14 shown to her she admitted that, the said NC is having her signature as SHO which mentioned the time 13.00 hours dt.3.4.14. This evidence of PW.5 shows that she is suppressing the material facts from the court. Inspite of NC at Ex.36 on record she made a false statement that she was not on duty on 3.4.14. If she was not on duty on 3.4.14, how her signature appears on NC at Ex.36 as SHO is not at all explained by her. 21. The reason behind the suppression of this fact is not at all explained by the prosecution though put to the prosecution witnesses. 22. PW.4 Kirti Mishra deposed that on 4.4.14 at about 6.30 a.m she went to school from her house. At about 10 a.m her examination paper was over. When she returned her sister victim was narrating the incidence to her mother and she heard the said narration. 23. In her cross­examination she deposed that on that day her examination timing was 7 to 10 a.m. The distance between her house and school is about 30 minutes by walk. She reached at her house at about 10.30 a.m. When she reached to her house she came to know that police taken her father to police station already on the basis of : 17 : Spl.C No.235/2014 (Jud.) complaint lodged by her mother. She further deposed that at about 11.15 to 11.30 a.m by auto­rickshaw they reached to Kapurbavadi police station and when they reached to police station her father was already sitting in police station. She further deposed that on same day police inquired with her and recorded her statement. She further deposed that she never visited police station after 4.4.14. 24. The evidence of PW.4 Kirti is not corroborating the evidence of PW.1 victim and PW.2 Kamladevi. According to PW.1 and 2 Kalmadevi they went to police station within 10 to 15 minutes after 8.30 a.m on 4.4.14, it means they both went to police station at about 8.45 to 9 a.m. Both these witness do not speak that PW.4 Kirti was with them. However PW.4 Kirti is stating that when she returned from the school at about 10.30 victim was narrating the incidence to PW.2 Kamladevi and she heard the narration and after that at about 11.15 to 11.30 a.m they reached to police station by auto rickshaw. Now question remain if they reached to police station on 11.15 to 11.30 a.m then how FIR was lodged at about 10.10 a.m. It is admitted by the PW.4 Kirti that her examination was completed on 10 a.m on that day and then at about 10.30 a.m she reached to her house. It means prior to : 18 : Spl.C No.235/2014 (Jud.) 10.30 a.m she was definitely not in police station. PW.5 I.O Amruta Chaure deposed that informant and her both daughters were with her in police station at the time of lodging FIR. Before recording FIR she inquired with them. Now if she inquired with all of them before lodging FIR they must have reach to the police station at about 9 to 9.30 a.m., but it is impossible for PW.4 Kirti to reach police station prior to 10 a.m. because she was in examination till 10 a.m. So it appears that the evidence of PW.1 and PW.2 at one side regarding the presence of PW.4 at the time of recording of FIR in police station and the timing of FIR and the evidence of PW.4 and PW.5 is at one side. If I believe evidence of PW.1 and PW.2 then I must say that PW.4 and PW.5 are narrating false facts. If I believe evidence of PW.4 and PW.5 then I must say that the PW.1 and PW.2 are deposing false. 25. So considering all evidence on record the evidence of all prosecution witness do not corroborate with each other. The defence taken by accused that PW.2 Kamladevi alongwith her daughters PW.1 & PW.4 wants to reside separately and therefore they lodged false FIR against accused cannot be ruled out. In view of the ratio laid down by Hon'ble Supreme court in Aher Raja Khima vs. State of Saurashtra, AIR 1956 SC 217, whereby Hon'ble : 19 : Spl.C No.235/2014 (Jud.) Supreme Court observed as follows:­ “8. Now it may be possible to take two views of this statement but there are two important factors in every criminal trial that weigh heavily in favour of an accused person: one is that the accused is entitled to the benefit of every reasonable doubt and the other, an off­shoot of the same principle, that when an accused person offers a reasonable explanation of his conduct, then, even though he cannot prove his assertions, they should ordinarily be accepted unless the circumstances indicate that they are false.” 26. As the defence taken by accused is a possible defence in view of the facts and circumstances on record the accused is entitled for benefit of doubt. 27. So considering all these facts and circumstances on record, I am of the view that prosecution failed to prove the charge against accused beyond all reasonable doubt. Hence, I answer point No.1 to 4 are in negative and in answer to Point No.5 , I pass the following order:­ :: ORDER :: 1. Accused Vishwanath Kashinath Mishra is hereby : 20 : Spl.C No.235/2014 (Jud.) acquitted u/sec. 235 (1) of Cr.P.C. of the offence punishable under U/sec.354(A) (1) (i) and Sec.7 r.w 8, 9(1) and 9(n) of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2. Bail bond of accused stands cancelled and surety is discharged. 3. Accused shall execute P. R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ and furnish surety in the like amount in compliance of Sec.437­A of Cr.P.C. Thane ( Prakash R. Kadam ) Dated: 22.08.2017 Special Judge & Addl Sessions Judge­05, Thane

.. 1 .. bail 2267/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) Order below Exh.1 Criminal Bail Appln. No. 2267 of 2014 This application is filed by applicant Kalpesh Ashok Mirashi for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no.I­415/2014 registered at Kashimira police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 342 of I.P.C. and section 8, 11(2) and 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant committed sexual assault on victim boy. It is further contended and argued that no such incident has happened and the applicant is falsely implicated in this crime. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co­operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that at the time of incident touched the penis of the victim boy with sexual intent and also moved his hand over his body with sexual purpose and thereby committed sexual assault on the victim body. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim boy and the prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. .. 2 .. bail 2267/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) 3] As is clear, though the offence charged against the applicant/ accused is of serious nature under section 342 of I.P.C. and section 8, 11(2) and 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012, it has to be taken into consideration that as per contentions raised the complainant and the applicant/accused are residents of same society and there has been dispute between the complainant and accused on account of society matters and as per contentions of the accused he is falsely implicated in the matter. In such circumstance the aspect whether the allegations in the complaint are true or whether the contentions put forth on behalf applicant/accused are sustainable, would be the question to be decided on merits and at this stage the only point to be decided is whether the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. In that respect as is clear the applicant to seen to have been arrested on 02.11.2014 and after police custody remand till 05.11.2014 he is remanded to judicial custody and sufficient time was there with the police for investigating the matter and the investigation must have almost completed. In such circumstance the allegation against the applicant/accused will have to be decided on merits after trial. Even nothing is to be recovered from him. 4] It is well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. .. 3 .. bail 2267/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) 5] In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he has produced on record copy of ration card which show that he has deep roots in the society. It is also stated on behalf of applicant that he will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 6] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 7] Then, it has also to be mentioned that though the investigation in the matter is almost completed and the charge sheet is yet to be submitted, it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter. Even it is also to be mentioned that no criminal antecedents of the applicant/accused are shown. 8] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ P. T. O. .. 4 .. bail 2267/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused namely Kalpesh Ashok Mirashi is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ He shall attend the concerned police station on every Friday between 6.00 p.m. to 8.00 p.m. and shall co­operate with the investigating machinery. He shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and other prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 08.12.2014. (Mrs.V.V.Virkar) District Judge­1 and Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.

He did not seize bed­sheet from the house of accused. He did not record the statement about the presence of the accused at his home. 16] It is pertinent to note here that the accused himself has admitted that the informant had taken her son from his house in his presence. Thus not only the spot of incident, but the presence of the accused is admitted by accused himself. Under such circumstances collection of CC Tv footages or recording of statements of other witnesses is not at all necessary. This is not an offence of penetrative sexual assault upon a female child. As such seizure of bed­sheet from the J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 218­15 ­ 7,8,9(i).doc . .....12/­ ..12.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 218/2015.. Exh.59.. house of accused is also not necessary in present case. Nothing is brought on record through his cross examination to disbelieve his investigation. 17] Lastly the prosecution has examined A.P.I. Sushilkumar Bhimrao Gaikwad as PW5 at Exh.43. He merely recorded the complaint Exh.16 and prepared arrest form of the accused who was already present in the police station. Said panchanama is at Exh.44. In cross examination it is brought on record that in arrest panchanama the date is mentioned as 03.05.2015. The accused was arrested on 02.08.2015 at 21.15 hours. It is admitted on behalf of the accused that on 02.08.2015 he was called in police station and came to be arrested. Under such circumstances PW5 has rightly stated that date 03.05.2015 mentioned in the panchanama is by mistake. 18] As already mentioned the accused has admitted the presence of victim boy at his home and his own presence on the day of incident. However, he has examined Kiran Devendra Thakur and Deepak Kisan Sharma as defence witnesses. Their depositions are at Exh.51 and Exh.52. Through their depositions the accused has tried to bring on record that on 01.08.2015 at 08.30 p.m. to 05.30 a.m. of 02.08.2015 he was at the house of DW3 Deepak Sharma on J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 218­15 ­ 7,8,9(i).doc . .....13/­ ..13.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 218/2015.. Exh.59.. occasion of ritual of Jagran. However, in cross examination of the informant and victim boy it is nowhere suggested that the accused was not at home at the relevant period. On the contrary the accused himself stated that on 02.08.2015 at 06.00 a.m. informant Pranali had taken the victim boy from his house forcibly and by dragging him. Under such circumstances the evidence of DW Kiran Thakur and Deepak Sharma is not at all helpful to defence. 19] The accused also examined his sister Mrs.Nisha @ Hema Deepak Satpal at Exh.50. She deposed that after the present case the informant had contacted her on 2­3 occasions. At that time she had requested the informant that the accused had not committed any crime. The informant had demanded Rs.5,00,000/­ from her. At that time the informant had talked with her for about 20 minutes. She told informant that she could not arrange such a huge amount. Lastly she demanded Rs.1,00,000/­ and cut the call. She has recorded the entire communication on her mobile. 20] It is pertinent to note here that in the cross examination of informant it is nowhere suggested that in order to extract money she filed false complaint against the accused. It is merely suggested whether she had demanded any amount from the sister of accused, which she denied. The J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 218­15 ­ 7,8,9(i).doc . .....14/­ ..14.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 218/2015.. Exh.59.. accused also nowhere stated in his statement u/s.313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure that the informant had demanded any amount form him. 21] From the entire evidence on record it is clearly established by the prosecution that on 02.08.2015 in between 00.15 hours to 10.00 hours while the victim boy was sleeping at the house of accused, the accused sexually assaulted him by rubbing/jerking his penis. Thus the offence defined u/s.7 and 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act is duly proved against the accused. Section 9 of the Act describes aggravated form. Sub­clause (m) of said section provides that when sexual assault is upon a child below 12 years of age, it amounts aggravated sexual assault. In the present case the victim boy is five years old. Thus section 9 of the Act clearly applies to the present case for which punishment is prescribed u/s.10 of the Act. Thus the accused is liable to be convicted and punished for offence punishable u/s.10 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. Hence point No.1 is answered in the affirmative. 22] It is pertinent to note here that after recording the evidence of defence witnesses, on 20.01.2018 advocate Mr.Shaikh representing the accused attempted to physically produce one CD alleging that it contains the communication J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 218­15 ­ 7,8,9(i).doc . .....15/­ ..15.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 218/2015.. Exh.59.. between the informant and sister of the accused. Said CD was merely physically produced whereupon the advocate of accused was informed that proper procedure has to be followed for producing said evidence. Thereafter on 20.01.2018 itself he prepared the alleged transcription of alleged communication recorded on CD and produced it alongwith affidavit of Hema Deepak Satpal. He also produced a certificate alleging u/s.65­B of Evidence Act. The affidavit is at Exh.55. The certificate is at Exh.56. However, the transcription is not at all prepared properly. There is no mention of any date, time and place as to the communication. So also as per procedure it ought to have produced during the evidence of witness Hema Satpal. Therefore, the transcription and the contents of CD are not duly proved in the evidence of defence. 23] The said entire record including affidavit Exh.55 and certificate Exh.56 were produced on 20.01.2018 after 06.00 p.m. Those are taken on record on 25.01.2018. On 25.01.2018 advocate Mr.Shaikh orally submitted that the CD be exhibited. However, as the CD and transcription is not duly proved, those are not exhibited. Advocate Mr.Shaikh was unable to argue as to how those record can be exhibited. Thereupon he filed application Exh.57 for time to approach Higher Court, but he failed to convince as to against which J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 218­15 ­ 7,8,9(i).doc . .....16/­ ..16.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 218/2015.. Exh.59.. order he desires to move to Higher Court. As the prayer was not proper, the application Exh.57 came to be rejected and matter was fixed on 30.01.2018 for final arguments. 24] On 30.01.2018 again adjournment application came to be filed on behalf of the accused. As the matter was for final arguments, arguments of A.P.P. were heard and matter was adjourned for arguments of defence. The matter was fixed on 05.01.2018. On 05.01.2018 when the matter was fixed for arguments of accused, the accused attended the Court, but his advocate did not remain present. No application came to be moved for adjournment. As the accused was deliberately prolonging the hearing, the matter came to be fixed for Judgment and adjourned till 07.02.2018. 25] As the accused is held guilt for the offence punishable u/s.10 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, he is liable to be punished and convicted for the same. Hence at this juncture the Judgment is deferred here to hear the accused on the quantum of sentence. Thane. (P.P.Jadhav) District Judge­6 and Date : 07.02.2018. Addl. Sessions Judge, Thane. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 218­15 ­ 7,8,9(i).doc . .....17/­ ..17.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 218/2015.. Exh.59.. 26] The conviction of accused came to be declared at 01.15 p.m. A.P.P. Mr.Kulkarni argued that maximum prescribed punishment be given to the accused. The accused submitted that his advocate is going to attend the Court. However, even after waiting till 03.15 p.m. the advocate of accused did not attend the Court. The accused refused to say anything on the quantum of sentence. 27] The accused has committed act of sexual assault upon a boy of five years old. Admittedly there is no record of any criminal antecedents against the accused. A single act of sexual assault is alleged and proved against the accused. Section 8 of The Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act prescribes punishment which shall not be less than three years, but which may extent to five years and fine. Section 10 which deals with aggravated sexual assault prescribes punishment which shall not be less than five years but which may extent to seven years and fine. Considering the nature of offence and punishments prescribed u/s.8 and 10 of the Act, the purpose will be served by punishing the accused with imprisonment of five years and fine. 1 Order Exh.1 in Cri.Bail Appln. No. 2431/16 ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN CRI. BAIL APPLICATION NO. 2431/2016 Heard Ld. Adv. Mr. Nitin Saabde for the applicant. Ld. A.P.P. Mrs. Jadhav for the State. The victims are studying in 5th standard in this school and they are 10 and 12 years old. The school timing of the victims is 11.00 a.m. to 3.00 p.m. On 22/08/2016 when the victims were entering the school at 11.00 a.m., at the school gate itself, the applicant pressed the mouths of both the victims and forcibly took them in the watchman room, locked the door from inside, showed them obscene video of naked man and woman taking bath and forcefully removed their petticoats, put his hands in their private part (vaginal portion) and tried to click the photographs of the victims from his mobile in such state. At that time, the one of the victim pulled the applicant's legs, another victim beat the applicant by iron pipe lying nearby and opened the door and went to the classroom and narrated the incident. 3] Ld. A.P.P. has vehemently opposed the bail application on the ground that both the victims have very clearly stated about the role of the applicant. Case diary not produced. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 15.08.2015 at the instance of the informant with an indictment that as he opposed to marry his minor daughter with accused no.1 Parmeshwar alias Vicky, accused Parmeshwar with other accused kidnapped his .. 2 .. Bail No. 2451/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) minor daughter, assaulted her, robbed her mobile and Parmeshwar alias Vicky committed sexual assault on her. He submitted that the victim girl is having love affair with accused no.1 Parmeshwar which was not liked by her parents and therefore though victim left house on her own, they were implicated falsely in the present case. II­56/2014 registered at Shantinagar police station, Bhiwandi on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 7, 13(1)(d) read with section 13(2) of Prevention of Corruption Act. It was contended and argued that the applicant has been arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant demanded and accepted illegal gratification while serving as a public servant. It is further contended that the applicant/accused has been falsely implicated in this crime. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co­operate with the investigation and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that demanded and accepted bribe of Rs.4,000/­ from the complainant to do favour to him. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the complainant and hampering the prosecution. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offence charged against the accused is of serious nature and it is a social offence, the amount .. 2 .. bail 2311/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) involved in the offence is a meagre amount and the same has also been recovered since it is a trap case. Even keeping apart that, fact is also clear that though the investigation in the matter is almost completed, it would take some time to complete the investigation and then to submit the charge sheet and then to conclude the trial and therefore there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter. 4] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 5] Then, it is contended by the applicant that he is a Government servant and is stated to have permanent residence at the address given and he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed and in all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. 1 Order Exh.1 B.A. 2460/16 ORDER BELOW EXH.1 IN CRIMINAL BAIL APPLICATION NO. 2460/16 Heard Ld. Advocate Mr. Naresh Pradhan for the applicant. Ld. A.P.P. Mr. S.D.Londhe for the State. I.O. present. 1] The applicant has filed this bail application for his release in C.R.No. I­293/2016 for offence U/s. 370, 372, 373 r/w. Sec. 34 of the I.P.C., Sec. 3,4 and 5 of PITA Act and Sec. 3(a), 4 and 17 of POCSO Act registered at Nerul police station. 2] The case of the prosecution in brief is that the applicant and absconding accused, in furtherance of their common intention, were human traffickers who indulged in the business of providing girls for prostitution and accepted money for their livelihood. 3] Ld. Advocate for the applicant has submitted that the applicant has been falsely implicated in this crime. He is not a human trafficker but was working as the servant of Mushtaq who was a human trafficker. The investigation is complete. The applicant is a permanent resident of Navi Mumbai and will not abscond if bail is granted. He is ready to abide by the conditions imposed by this court. 4] Per contra, Ld. A.P.P. has submitted that the applicant came to be arrested pursuant to a raid. The statements of three victims girls have revealed that the applicant used to provide girls for prostitution. He is a trafficker and not merely a servant as submitted by the Ld. Advocate for the applicant. Prima­facie case is made out against him which shows that he is 2 Order Exh.1 B.A. 2460/16 earning his livelihood from this human trafficking business. The accused was nabbed red­handed at the spot in the raid and one of the victims is a minor. 5] During the investigation, it is brought out that the applicant is a human trafficker. He used to provide girls for prostitution. He is doing the business of trafficking and is earning his livelihood from the said business, i.e., human trafficking. The statements of the victims, i.e., Dulali Shabikul Khan (aged 16 years), Asma Khan and Ayesha Kakkad have also revealed this fact. In the Judgment dated 30/10/2015 passed by the Hon'ble Bombay High Court in Criminal P.I.L. No. 4/2015 (Freedom Firm V/s. Commissioner of Police, Pune & Ors.), guidelines have been laid down for judicial officers while dealing with the cases of human trafficking. In this Judgment, it has been held that the court would, as a general principle, refuse bail to an accused who is shown as a trafficker in human beings. In this matter, it has been laid down that the Court would certainly release on bail such of the accused or co­accused as are themselves not traffickers but may be shown to have played some minor role in the commission of the offence. 7] Therefore, in view of the ratio decidendi and the guidelines laid down in the case of Freedom Firm (supra), this is not a fit case for granting bail as the role of the applicant has emerged as a trafficker. In view thereof, I am inclined to reject the application. ORDER Application stands rejected. Thane. ( Mridula V.K.Bhatia ) Dt:­09/11/2016. Dist. Judge – 08 and Special Judge (POCSO), Thane. 3 Order Exh.1 B.A. 2460/16

1 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 220/2015 Judgment Received on :­ 01.10.2015 Registered on :­ 01.10.2015 Decided on :­ 05.05.2017 Duration :­ 1Y 07M 4 D IN THE COURT OF ADDITIONAL SESSIONS JUDGE, & SPECIAL JUDGE (POCSO) ACT, THANE AT : THANE ( Presided over by Ashutosh N.Karmarkar, District Judge­1 & Special Judge (POCSO) Act, Thane ) Special Case (POCSO) No.220/2015 Exh. No. 20 State of Maharashtra ( Through Naupada Police Station ) …Complainant V/s. Deepak Tukaram Shelke Age : 32 Years, Occ. : Sweeper, R/at.: Bhagu Mavashi Chawl, behind Chandiwala complex, Thane Chandanwadi … Accused. Offence punishable under Sec. 354­A(1)(i) of Indian Penal Code & under Secs. 8 & 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 220/2015 Judgment Appearances : Shri. S.D.Londhe, A.P.P. for the State Shri. Sunil Patankar, Advocate for accused JUDGMENT ( Delivered on this 5th day of May, 2017 ) 1] Accused is facing trial for the offence punishable under Sec. 354­A(1)(i) of Indian Penal Code and under Secs. 8 & 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] Prosecution Case, in brief, is as under : Victim is the informant. Her sister is serving in Texon company. Victim is studying in 7th standard. Accused is residing adjoining to their house. One Paresh Bhoir, the brother­in­law of the accused is also residing adjoining to the house of informant. On 30.05.2015, at about 9.30 p.m., victim / informant had been to the house of said Paresh Bhoir to see the T.V. Programme. At that time, accused Deepak, Paresh and wife of Paresh were present. After sometime, accused left their house. He again came back at 10.45 p.m. At that time, the wife of Paresh was busy with her household work in kitchen. Mr. Paresh was not present at house. Nobody was present in the hall. Victim was sitting on the bed. Accused came there. He put hand over the shoulder of the victim. He has shown the indecent picture in his mobile and has moved his hand over the person of the victim. He also threatened the victim to kill in case of disclosure. Victim was 3 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 220/2015 Judgment frightened. On next day, victim narrated this incident to her sister who has further stated the incident to her mother. On that day, there was quarrel between the accused and the mother of victim. Since accused was neighbour, no complaint was lodged. On 04.06.2015, at 5.00 p.m., accused again came in front of house of victim and made indecent gestures. So, the victim along with her mother and sister came to police station and lodged report. 3] On the basis of report, offence was registered vide C.R.No. I­279/2015. P.S.I. Trupti Khalde has investigated this matter. She has recorded statements of witnesses. She has seized mobile. She drew seizure panchanama. After completion of evidence, she filed charge­sheet in the Court of Law. 4] I have framed charge against accused below Exh. 6 to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 5] Prosecution has examined three witnesses. Then, the statement of the accused under Sec. 313 of Cr.P.C. came to be recorded. Total denial is the defence of the accused. The accused has also tried to raise defence that his some of the amount was due from the mother of victim due to which some dispute has taken place. 6] Ld. A.P.P. Shri. Londhe has submitted that on the day of 4 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 220/2015 Judgment incident, the accused came to the house of Paresh where victim was also present. Actually he left the house, but again came back after short time. According to him, the victim has stated about her molestation. The accused had also threatened to kill in case of disclosure. According to him, more details are also brought on record in cross­examination. It is also submitted that the accused could not brought on record any material that his amount was due from victim's mother. Evidence of victim is also corroborated by her mother. On the other hand, Ld. Advocate for the accused has submitted that the alleged incident is of 30.05.2015 and the report came to be filed on 04.06.2015. No satisfactory explanation has been put forth for delay in F.I.R. According to him, victim has also admitted that the victim and her family members are acquainted to one constable Jadhav who frequently helps the family of victim in case of their needs. According to him, the delay in F.I.R. itself creates doubt. 7] Following points arose for my determination and I gave my findings thereon for the reasons stated below: Sr. POINTS FINDINGS No. 1. Does the prosecution prove that the No accused on 30.05.2015 at 20.45 hrs., and 4.6.2015, at about 17.00 hrs., at Bhagu Mavshi Chawl, behind Chandiwala Complex, Chandanwadi, 5 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 220/2015 Judgment Naupada, Thane has sexually harassed minor victim Ku. Nandini, aged 14 years by physical contact and advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures ? 2. Does the prosecution prove that the No. accused on above mentioned date, time and place, committed sexual assault on informant i.e. minor victim girl Ku. Nandini, age 4 years by moving his hand on her body with sexual intent which involves physical contact without penetration ? 3. Does the prosecution prove that on No. above mentioned date, time and place, accused committed sexual harassment upon informant i.e. minor victim girl, age 14 years by showing her obscene clips on his mobile with sexual intent ? 4. What order? As per final order. REASONS AS TO POINT NO.1 TO 4:­ 8] In order to establish the guilt under Sec. 354­A(1)(i) of Indian Penal Code, prosecution has to prove that there was act of physical contact including advances involving unwelcome sexual overtures by the accused. Prosecution is also required to prove that the accused has sexually assaulted or harassed the victim as provided under 6 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 220/2015 Judgment Sec. 7 and 11 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act and that too with sexual intent. 9] The prosecution has examined victim P.W.1 (Exh.8), her mother Asha Arun Sambre P.W.2 (Exh.10), P.S.I. Trupti Khalde P.W.3 (Exh.12). It is well settled that in order to prove the guilt of accused, prosecution is required to adduce cogent and convincing evidence. It is well settled that the sole testimony of witness is also sufficient to base the conviction. But, the rule is that it should inspire confidence in the mind of court and should be above suspicion. If a single grain of doubt appears in the prosecution story then, defence get benefit of it. 10] It appears that the accused has not disputed the bonafide certificate of the victim (Exh.16). It appears from the said document that on the day of incident, the age of victim might be about 14 years. Victim has stated that at the time of incident she was studying in 7th standard. On 30.5.2015, at 9.30 p.m., she had been to the house of maternal uncle Paresh to see T.V. Programme. Accused came there. Actually he left that house but again came back at 10.45 p.m. Paresh had gone outside. His wife was busy in kitchen. According to victim, the accused put his hand over her shoulder and has moved the hand over her breast by showing obscene pictures on the mobile handset. Same type of story is stated by the mother of the victim. 7 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 220/2015 Judgment 11] It is to be noted that in the report (Exh.9) itself victim has not specifically stated about moving of hand over her breast. It is contended in the report that accused has moved hand over her person. The victim has further stated that she will disclose about the incident to her mother on which accused threatened her to kill. On that day, she did not narrate the incident to anybody though she went to home. On next day, she narrated the incident to her sister Jyoti who in turn narrated the same to her mother. Then, there was quarrel between victim's mother and accused. But, the complaint was not lodged on the same day. 12] Evidence of P.W.2 Asha, the mother of victim shows that she is treating Mr. Paresh Bhoir as her brother. On 31.05.2015, victim had been to the house of Paresh. She came back at 11.30 p.m. She was silent. On next day, she made enquiry with the victim. At that time, victim narrated the incident to her. The victim has stated somewhat different story that she narrated the incident to her sister Jyoti who in turn stated to P.W.2 Asha. It appears from the evidence of P.W.2 Asha that on next day i.e. on 31.05.2015, she had been to the house of Paresh where accused was present to make enquiry. She demanded mobile of accused. He went to bring mobile but did not come. He came along with his brother who stated not to lodge the report and so she avoided to give a report. It is brought on record in the cross­ examination of P.W. 2Asha that sister of Mr. Paresh Bhoir is the wife of the present accused. This accused is not actually in relation 8 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 220/2015 Judgment of the victim. 13] P.W.3 P.S.I. Khalde has stated that she has seized the mobile from the accused on which he has shown the alleged obscene picture to the victim. She has stated that the said muddemal was sent for report of forensic expert as per letter Exh.15. The report was subsequently filed on record. Panchanama (Exh.13) also shows that the Samsung made mobile was seized from the accused. The report of forensic expert being public document is required to be exhibited. It is given Exh.20. The allegation of the victim is that the accused has shown the obscene pictures in the said mobile and has moved hand over her person. The report of forensic expert shows that the case related video file as mentioned in the case forwarding letter was not found in the mobile phone. It is also important to note that simcard does not have facility to store image or video file. So, the allegation of the victim does not get support from the report of forensic expert. 14] If the accused was not closely related to the victim and if such alleged act was committed then certainly the victim's mother would have taken action immediately when she learnt about the incident on 31.5.2015. P.W.2 Asha has stated that on 31.5.2015, she made enquiry with the victim and victim narrated the incident. On that day, she had been to the accused to make enquiry. But, he came with his brother and stated not to lodge report and so, she did not lodge the report. But, this reason for not lodging the report 9 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 220/2015 Judgment early is not stated by the victim. It is contended in the report (Exh.9) that since the accused was neighbour, no complaint was lodged. This is not the reason which is stated by the witness Asha for non lodging of the report early. 15] Evidence of victim will show that on 31.5.2015, there was quarrel between mother of the victim and accused and accused was beaten. But the evidence of P.W.2 Asha will shows that on 4.6.2015, she herself and her daughter have beaten the accused. The evidence of P.W. 2 Asha reveals that there was a dispute between Asha and the accused on 31.05.2015. According to victim, on 4.6.2015, accused has made indecent gestures on seeing her. Same fact is stated by P.W.2 Asha. According to both these witnesses, on 4.6.2015, they went to police station and the report was lodged. Evidence of both these witnesses does not show the details of the alleged gestures by the accused so as to prove them as indecent. Both the witnesses have also not stated the details of the alleged gestures which they felt as indecent. They only gave suggestion to the victim that the mother of the victim had taken amount of Rs. 10,000/­ from the accused and the accused and his wife were demanding the same. This suggestion is denied. The victim has also admitted in cross­examination that she knows one police constable Mr. Jadhav, police from Wagle Estate police station. She has admitted that he used to help victim and her family members in their needs. The suggestion is also 10 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 220/2015 Judgment given to P.W. 2 Asha that the report was lodged as advised by P.C. Mr. Jadhav. P.W.2 Asha has also admitted in the cross­examination that her family members and the others obeys her directions. Victim has also admitted that several independent persons were present at the time of alleged quarrel dtd. 04.06.2015. All those persons were favouring mother of victim. P.W.2 Asha had been to police station along with all those persons. It is to be noted that no satisfactory explanation had been put forth by the victim or her mother for not lodging the report immediately after alleged incident dtd.30.5.2015 in respect of which P.W.2 Asha learnt on 31.05.2015. It is already discussed that the details of alleged gestures on 04.06.2015 were not stated. So, all these facts certainly create doubts as to the allegations of prosecution against the accused. 16] P.S.I. Smt. Khalde has also admitted that she has not recorded the statement of the persons who are residing in the house where alleged incident has taken place. Victim has stated that other persons were also present in adjoining houses. At least the prosecution should have recorded the statement of Mrs. Bhoir in whose house the alleged incident has taken place. Her evidence or the evidence of neighbour should have been recorded to show at least the presence of the accused in the house of Paresh Bhoir. In absence of such evidence, it will be also unsafe to hold accused guilty. For the reasons stated in foregoing paragraphs, it will be difficult to accept that the prosecution has established the guilt 11 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 220/2015 Judgment under Sec. 8 or 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act or under Sec. 354­A(1)(i) of Indian Penal Code. I find that the evidence of the prosecution is not upto the mark to bring the accused within four corners of Sec. 354­A(1)(i) of Indian Penal Code and Sec. 8 and 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. So, I answer point Nos.1 to 3 in the negative and proceed to pass following order : ORDER 1] Accused Deepak Tukaram Shelke is hereby acquitted under Sec.235(1) of Code of Criminal Procedure of the offence punishable under Sec. 354­A(1)(i) of Indian Penal Code and Secs.8 and 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] His bail bond stands cancelled. 3] Muddemal be confiscated to the State as per rule. 4] Accused shall furnish P.B and S.B. of RS.5,000/­ under Sec 437­A of Code of Criminal Procedure. Thane ( Ashutosh N. Karmarkar ) Date : 05.05.2017 District Judge­1 & Special Judge (POCSO) Act, Thane

Mr. Reena Korde, learned advocate for the accused. .. 2 .. Special Case No.109/2015 Judgment JUDGMENT (Delivered on 03.09.2015.) The accused stands prosecuted for offence punishable under section 377 of I.P.C. and section 3 read with section 4 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as P.O.C.S.O. Act) for doing unnatural sex with minor victim boy. 2] In short the facts giving rise to the prosecution of the accused are that victim boy Shibi aged 14 years was staying with his uncle Sher Singh at room no.3303 Bhimnagar, Rabale and was studying in 3rd Std. in Sharada Vidyalay and his school timing was from 12.00 noon to 6.00 p.m. That he is originally from Mahakali Zone, West Nepal and was brought to Navi Mumbai for the purpose of his treatment for his big head. It is further case of the prosecution that on 24.08.2013 it was Saturday and after returning home from school early in the evening, Shibi had been to public toilet for answering call of nature. That accused took him with him on the pretext of giving vadapav and took him to the canteen of Chandramani Sharma at Saibaba Nagar and then gave him some eatables like chapati, potato bhaji and took him inside the room near canteen and then closed the door of the room and started pinching him, when he shouted he gagged his mouth, removed his half pant and had inserted his penis in his anus, Shibi was scared and therefore could not resist. After some time accused .. 3 .. Special Case No.109/2015 Judgment left him. Said boy Shibi had severe pain at his anus. Said boy Shibi was not knowing the accused at that time and because of pain he was sitting there in the canteen being scared. But then the canteen owner came there and made enquiries with him but he could not tell anything about him being scared. The canteen owner then informed uncle of boy Shibi about it. His uncle then came and then took him home and made enquiries with him and that time he narrated the incident to his uncle. His uncle again took him to the canteen and that time the accused was there and the boy pointed out towards accused to be the same person who committed act of sexual assault on him and then said person revealed to be the accused Ramchandra Adhikari. His uncle then took boy Shibi to police station and uncle Rakesh Singh then lodged complaint. 3] On the basis of his complaint, offence as per C.R. No.78/2013 for offences punishable under section 377 of I.P.C. and section 3 read with section 4 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and the work of investigation was done by A.P.I. Gholve, During the investigation panchnama of the spot was prepared. Statements of boy Shibi as well as other witnesses including owner of the canteen were recorded. Boy Shibi was referred for medical examination. Clothes on his person were seized. The accused was caught and was referred for medical examination. His medical certificate and sample of semen etc. were obtained. Statements of further witnesses were recorded. Samples .. 4 .. Special Case No.109/2015 Judgment obtained and muddemal seized was sent for chemical analysis alongwith letter. Medical certificate of boy was obtained. It is also case of the prosecution that since the boy was reported to be minor, certificate in regard to his date of birth was obtained from his school and after completion of investigation since there was sufficient evidence against the accused, accused came to be charge­sheeted for offences punishable under section 377 of I.P.C. and section 3 read with section 4 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. 4] Since offence under P.O.C.S.O. Act has been applied and since this Court is Special Court to try offences under P.O.C.S.O. Act, the charge­sheet came to be submitted to this Court. 5] The accused was produced before the Court by jail authority. A charge for offence punishable under section 377 of I.P.C. and section 3 read with section 4 of P.O.C.S.O. Act was framed against the accused as per Exhibit 3. Contents of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. The accused pleaded not guilty. His defence was of total denial. He claimed to be tried. 6] For establishing guilt of the accused the prosecution examined complainant P.W.1 Rakesh Ram Singh, complainant and canteen owner P.W.2 Chandramani Sharma. .. 5 .. Special Case No.109/2015 Judgment In spite of repeated chances given to the prosecution, the prosecution could not secure presence of victim boy or even the investigating officer. The documentary evidence produced, proved and relied upon by the prosecution consisted of complaint Exhibit 13, spot panchnama Exhibit 16 (exhibited on admission), medical certificate of accused Exhibit 24 (exhibited on admission), medical certificate of victim boy Exhibit 25 (exhibited on admission). 7] Statement of accused under section 313 of Cr.P.C. was recoded. He did not examine himself on oath and had not adduced any evidence in defence. 8] I heard the learned A.P.P. and learned advocate for accused. 9] On the basis of above facts of the case, the points which arose for my determination, my reasons and findings for the same are as under ­ Points Findings i) Whether prosecution proved that on 24.08.2013 between 18.00 to 21.15 at eating house of Chandramani Sharma at Saibabanagar, Rabale MIDC, Navi Mumbai, the accused had carnal intercourse with minor victim boy named Shibi which is against the order of nature ? No. .. 6 .. Special Case No.109/2015 Judgment ii ) Whether the prosecution proved that on the given day, date, time and place, the accused committed penetrative sexual assault on minor victim boy by doing carnal intercourse with him which is against the order of nature ? No. iii ) What offence if any is proved against No offence is the accused ? proved. iv ) What order ? The accused is acquitted. REASONS As to point no.1 and 2 ­ 10] As is clear as per prosecution case the accused had unnatural sex with minor boy Shibi on the given day, date, time and place by having anal unnatural sexual intercourse with the boy. In that regard so far as the aspect that the boy was minor at the relevant time the prosecution has produced on record the bona fide certificate of the boy which is produced on record and exhibited on admission. From said certificate it is clear that date of birth of boy Shibi is 13.02.2000 and if calculated on that basis the age of the boy at the time of incident on 24.08.2013 is said to be 13 years old at the time of incident and therefore it has to be concluded that the fact that the boy was 'child' within the meaning of definition of 'child' under P.O.C.SO. Act is established. .. 7 .. Special Case No.109/2015 Judgment 11] Then, so far as the allegations that the accused had unnatural sex with the boy is concerned, at the outset it has to be mentioned that the presence of the boy could not be secured in spite of repeated chances given to the prosecution and therefore, primary direct evidence of the boy in regard to the allegations against the accused is not available. No doubt, repeated summons are issued and the report shows that the boy was not found at the address given and he left for his native place and even in his evidence the complainant also appear to have stated that victim boy Shibi is staying with his parents in Nepal and he will not be in a position to bring Shibi to give evidence and Shibi had stated that he won't come for giving evidence and his parents also sated that they would not send him even for deposing before Court and they are not ready to send him anywhere because of such incident. In such circumstances the prosecution cannot be blamed for not examining boy Shibi. However, fact remains that the evidence of the boy which is the only direct evidence in regard to the allegation, is not available. 12] No doubt, merely because the evidence of the boy is not available the allegations against the accused cannot be said to have been established and it is required to be seen as to whether other evidence on record is sufficient to establish the guilt of the accused and whether the presumption under section 29 of P.O.C.S.O. Act is rebutted. .. 8 .. Special Case No.109/2015 Judgment 13] In that regard the other evidence on record is the testimony of the complainant and medical evidence. Then, so far as the testimony of the complainant he appear to have stated that on the day of incident the boy Shibi did not return home at his usual time and after waiting for him till 8.30 to 8.45 p.m. they went in search for the boy but he could not be traced and then he received phone call from one Chandramani Sharma, owner of hotel at Saibaba nagar, that boy Shibi is there in his hotel. It is also clear that he also stated that he then went to the hotel and that time the boy Shibi narrated him the incident that one person asked him to accompany him by saying that he would give him vadapav and sabji and took him inside the room and closed the door and removed his pant, gagged his mouth, removed his own pant and then said person inserted his penis in his place of passing stool 2 to 3 times, he shouted being scared, the boys in the hotel came there and he raised and wore his clothes and came and sat in the hotel and also further that boy Shibi then pointed out towards the person sitting in the hotel and then they caught said person and took him to police station and he was the accused in the present case Ramchandra Adhikari. He then lodged complaint as per Exhibit 14. 14] However, a careful of his cross­examination on behalf of accused reveal that his testimony in regard to what .. 9 .. Special Case No.109/2015 Judgment the boy had stated to him, exactly when the hotel owner informed him that boy Shibi was there and when he went there has been shattered and shaken Even he accepted in his cross­examination that when Shibi left home for going to toilet, he was not there in the house and also that the hotel owner Chandramani had not stated anything on phone as to with whom Shibi had been to hotel or with whom he had seen Shibi coming or going. 15] In the light of that if the aspect that as per prosecution case the boy was referred for medical examination immediately and his medical certificate is on record at Exhibit 24 (exhibited on admission) is material. However, if the medical certificate Exhibit 24 is perused, it reveal that no injuries were noticed on his private part and even no external injuries were noticed per anal. It is very much material to mention that as per the version of the complainant in his complaint and even his version on oath, the boy was sexually assaulted by gagging his mouth and in spite of his resistance the act of forcible anal intercourse was committed with him by the accused. If at all it was so, as rightly submitted on behalf of the accused, some injury or at least some signs of such sexual assault should have been there at his anus or some injuries must have been there on some part of body. Even the complainant in his cross­examination accepted that when he saw the boy at that time, he noticed no injury on the person of .. 10 .. Special Case No.109/2015 Judgment the boy. It is highly improbable that there would be no injury in the case of sexual assault by unnatural anal intercourse with an underage boy. 16] In the light of that if the aspect that the hotel owner P.W.2 Chandramani Sharma has not supported the version of the complainant in regard to the allegation against the accused assumes importance. It is material to mention that P.W.2 Chandramani Sharma though stated that on the day of incident Shibi had been to his canteen and he asked him as to why he had been there, he stated that he had come to meet him and since it was night time he phoned his uncle and informed that Shibi had been there and his brother then came and took Shibi took with him, but he had not stated anything about boy Shibi and his brother i.e. complainant coming again to the complainant and Shibi pointing out towards the accused who was working as waiter in hotel. It is material to mention that though the witness was declared hostile and cross­ examined on behalf of prosecution, absolutely nothing is brought on record to show that he was not stating true facts and in fact Shibi had pointed out towards the accused to be the person having sexual assault on him. Even no other witness is seen to have been examined the prosecution to establish the aspect that Shibi and accused were there in the hotel at the relevant time. It is also to be mentioned that the incident alleged to have taken place in hotel where normally .. 11 .. Special Case No.109/2015 Judgment other waiters, other employees of the hotel and also the customers must have been there. Then, as per the prosecution case when the accused had committed such an act with the boy, the boy shouted and that he gagged his mouth but nobody alleged to have heard his shouting and that none of the said witnesses have been examined by the prosecution. 17] In the light of that the defence put forth by accused in his statement under section 313 of Cr.P.C. that he is falsely implicated in the case and was wrongly caught by police, appear to be worth consideration and in absence of the testimony of the boy in regard to the alleged act and the very material aspect that the medical evidence is not supporting the prosecution case, the possibility and probability of false implication of the accused is also there. In view of all above discussion the allegations against the accused cannot be said to have been established beyond all the reasonable. Point no.1 and 2 are answered accordingly in the negative. As to point no. 3 ­ 18] In view of my findings to point no.1 and 2 no offence can be said to have been proved against the accused and the accused is entitled to be acquitted. Point no.3 is therefore answered accordingly. 19] Since the accused is acquitted, it is necessary that he be directed to furnish P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ (rupees .. 12 .. Special Case No.109/2015 Judgment fifteen thousand only) with one surety in the like amount as per section 437A of Cr.P.C. to appear before the higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect of any appeal or petition filed against the judgment. In the result I pass the following order ­ ORDER Accused namely Ramchandra Durgaprasad Adhikari is acquitted of the charge for offence punishable under section 377 of Indian Penal Code and also under section 3 read with section 4 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 2) The accused shall be released from jail forthwith if not required in any other crime. 3) The accused shall furnish P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount under section 437A of Cr.P.C. to appear before the higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect of any appeal or revision, if any, filed against the judgment and that such bail bond shall be in force for six months. 4) Muddemal quilt being worthless be destroyed after expiry of appeal period. 5) The proceeding is closed. Date : 03.09.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Additional Session Judge­1, Thane.

.. 1 .. bail no.2465/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Order below Exhibit 1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 2465/2015 This application is filed by applicant Lahu Shantaram Salake for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no.I­79/2015 registered at A.P.M.C. police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 363, 376,m 494, 495 of I.P.C. and section 4, 6, 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant induced the victim girl and then kidnapped the her and had sexual intercourse with her. It is further contended and argued that no such incident as alleged has happened. It is further contended and argued that there was love affair between girl and accused and therefore, the girl had come with him. It is further contended and argued that the girl and the accused have married to each other. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co­operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that taking disadvantage of young age of the girl, the accused induced her and then kidnapped her and then had forcible sexual intercourse with her at various places. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is .. 2 .. bail no.2465/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl and the prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 376, 363, 494, 495 of I.P.C. and section 4, 6, 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act with the allegation of kidnapping minor girl and then committing sexual assault on her, it is contended on behalf of accused that he is falsely implicated in the crime and it is also specifically contended by the accused that the girl and the accused have now married to each other and that the accused has no criminal antecedents. In such circumstance whether the allegations against the accused are true or not, would be the question to be decided on merits. Then, the applicant/accused is seen to be in jail since 29.09.2015 and looking to the nature of allegations the investigation may have completed by now. Even nothing is stated to be recovered from the applicant/accused. 4] Then, it is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by .. 3 .. bail no.2465/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) any conditions imposed. 5] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 6] Then, it has also to be mentioned that looking the allegations against the accused the investigation in the matter may have almost completed but the charge­sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge­sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 7] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Lahu Shantaram Salake is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one local surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ The applicant/accused shall attend the concerned police station on every Friday between 10.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon till filing of the charge­sheet and shall co­operate in investigation. .. 4 .. bail no.2465/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) He shall not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and the prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this Court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 05.10.2015 (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Additional Session Judge­1, Thane.

1 POCSO Case No. 234/2016. Presented on­ 30.09.2016. Registered on­ 30.09.2016. Decided on­ 06.03.2018. Duration­ Y­1 M­5 D­6 IN THE COURT OF SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE. [Presided over by A.S. Bhaisare, Additional Sessions Judge­2 and Special Judge (POCSO Act), Thane.] SPECIAL CASE (POCSO) NO. 234/2016. Exh. no. The State (Through Bhiwandi Taluka Police Station) ..Complainant. V/s. 1] Rohit Rajaram Lasne, Age 23 years, Occ. Labour, R/o. Kawad village, Tal. Bhiwandi, 2] Shubham Prakash Lasne, Age 20 years, Occ. Service, R/o. Kawadgaon, Tal. Bhiwandi. ..Accused. ___________________________________________________________ Appearances­ Learned Special P.P. Smt. Phad, for the State. Learned Advocate Shri. Lasne, for the accused. ___________________________________________________________ JUDGMENT (Delivered on 06.03.2018.) 1] Both accused Rohit Rajaram Lasne and Shubham Prakash 2 POCSO Case No. 234/2016. Lasne, are facing trial for the offences punishable u/s. 376 r/w. Sec. 34 of I.P.C. and u/s. 3 r/w. Sec. 4, 8, 12, 17 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] It is the case of prosecution that in last year victim aged about 17 years and 8 months had been to Rohit Lasne to deliver her best wishes on account of his birth anniversary. Since then, they fell in love. However, her parents were against it. They had decided to marry after her age of 18 years is completed. 3] On 07.07.2005 at the evening, she had been to the house of her uncle and ringed accused Rohit Lasne on mobile. She had informed him that her parents are going to arrange her marriage. If he is interested to marry with her, they had to run away and to marry. Accordingly, on 09.07.15 during night time, with her luggage, she went to Bhatsa colony in one empty room. Thereafter, they both ran away to village Kawad naka and then to Shirdi. However, during night, they resided in Tabela behind Vishal hotel and during that night, he had established his sexual relations with her. Then, by S.T., they went to Shahapur from Bhiwandi. However, as they had lost their money, they returned back to Bhiwandi police station. Shubham Prakash Lasne is friend of Rohit Lasne. As victim was not found, her mother Nanda Naik had lodged her report against both the accused. It was registered vide C.R. no. 172/15 u/s. 363, 34 of I.P.C. After arrival of both accused and victim, she was referred to hospital for her medical examination. Accused was also referred for his medical examination. Spot panchanama was recorded (Exh.13and 15). Clothes of victim are seized (Exh.14). So also, clothes of accused are seized (Exh.16). Statements of witnesses were recorded. Seized property was sent to C.A. After investigation, charge­sheet was submitted in the court. 3 POCSO Case No. 234/2016. 4] Matter is made over to this Court for trial. 5] Heard both sides. I framed the charge against the accused for the offences punishable under section 376, 363 r/w. Sec. 34, sec. 180 of I.P.C. and u/s. 4, 8, 12, 17 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012, on 15/11/2017. Details of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular, to which they pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. Their defence is of total denial. 6] During trial, defence has admitted spot panchanamas (Exh.13 and 15), seizure panchanama of clothes of victim girl (Exh.14), seizure panchanama of clothes of accused no.1 Rohit (Exh.16), M.L.C. of I.G.M. hospital of victim (Exh.17), M.L.C. of accused no.1 Rohit (Exh.18), Forensic examination reports (Exh.19 to 21) and letter of Group Grampanchayat, Pariwali to Bhiwandi Tal. Police Station (Exh.22). 7] To bring home the guilt of the accused for the charges leveled against them, the prosecution has examined as many as two witnesses i.e. P.W. Name of witness Exh. Description No. No. 1] Nanda Balaram Naik 10 Complainant. 2] Pratiksha Balaram Naik 12 Victim. 8] Accused did not enter into witness box. They had not examined defence witness. 9] Heard learned Special P.P. Smt. Phad for the State and learned counsel Shri. Lasne for the accused. Following points arise for my determination, which are being answered for the reasons given herein­ below. 4 POCSO Case No. 234/2016. POINTS FINDINGS 1] Whether prosecution proved that in No. between 09.07.2015 at 21.00 hours to 10.07.2015 at 17.15 hours, in village Kawad, in front of the house of complainant, at Koliwali village, Tal. Bhiwandi, behind the bungalow of witness Rakesh Kulkarni in empty stable, in furtherance of their common intention, accused no.1 Rohit had committed rape i.e. penetrative sexual assault and sexual harassment on the minor daughter of complainant i.e. victim girl aged 17 years and 9 months, and accused no.2 Shubham had committed the abetment of the offence of rape by engaging with accused no.1 Rohit in conspiracy ? 2] Whether prosecution proved that in the No. above period and place, in furtherance of their common intention, accused no. 1 Rohit had kidnapped the minor daughter of complainant i.e. victim girl aged 17 years and 9 months, by giving promise of marriage for keeping sexual relations, from the lawful guardianship of her mother i.e. complainant without her consent ? 3] Whether prosecution proved that in the No. above period and place, accused no.2 Shubham had instigated accused no.1 Rohit for kidnapping the minor daughter of complainant i.e. victim girl aged 17 years and 9 months, and abetted in the commission of offence of rape committed by accused no. 1 Rohit ? 5 POCSO Case No. 234/2016. 4] What order ? As per final order. REASONS POINT NOS. 1 TO 3 10] Victim was in love with accused Rohit. However, her family members were opposed and they had decided to perform her marriage with another boy. Victim and accused are resident of same village. As per victim herself, on the day of her statement before police, had stated her age as 17 years and 9 months. Xerox of her school­leaving certificate is placed on record. As per said certificate, she was born on 01.10.97. The alleged incident was taken place on 07.07.15. If date of birth of the victim and date of incident is considered, then it can be said that certainly on 07.07.15, victim had completed her 17 years of age. 11] P.W.2 (victim) in her evidence before the court has stated her age as 21 years on 20.02.2018. On this count also, it can be inferred that victim had to attend the age of majority on the day of incident i.e. on 07.07.15. 12] P.W.1 Nanda had also stated in her evidence that victim is aged about 21 years. She is not eye­witness to the incident. She had stated nothing against the accused. After two days of the incident, victim along with accused Rohit were found. On enquiry, victim had not stated that accused had established his sexual intercourse with her. 13] P.W.2 victim deposed in her evidence that on 07.07.15 at about 9.00 p.m., as per her advise, accused no. 1 Rohit Lasne came in front of her house and then, they both went behind Vishal hotel tower and stayed 6 POCSO Case No. 234/2016. in one Tabela. During that night, accused had established his sexual relations. 14] From the evidence of this witness, it can safely be gathered that victim herself had called the accused. She joined the company of accused Rohit Lasne and stayed along with him in Tabela, wherein she herself had submitted before him. There was no forcible sexual intercourse against her consent or against her wish. She was knowing the consequences of her own act. She had attended the age of understanding. Accused Rohit Lasne had not kidnapped her nor forcibly committed rape. 15] Medical certificates are admitted by the accused. 16] C.A. reports are placed on record. The blood group of victim was detected as blood group A whereas blood group of Rohit Lasne was detected as blood group O. It is to be noted here that on the clothes of victim as per C.A. report Exh. 20, no blood nor semen was detected on her clothes. 17] There is no iota of evidence against accused no. 2 that he had abetted the crime. 18] Having considered the facts and circumstances of the matter and evidence on record, prosecution failed to prove the alleged offence. No presumption u/s. 29 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012, can be drawn in favour of prosecution and against accused. Consequently, I record my findings to all the points, accordingly and proceed to pass the following order. ORDER 1] Both accused Rohit Rajaram Lasne and 7 POCSO Case No. 234/2016. Shubham Prakash Lasne, are hereby, acquitted under sec. 235(1) of the Criminal Procedure Code, of the offences punishable u/s. 376, 363 r/w. Sec. 34, sec. 108 of I.P.C. and u/s. 4, 8, 12, 17 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] Both accused Rohit Rajaram Lasne and Shubham Prakash Lasne, be enlarged on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ each with surety of like amount each. The effect of this bail order will remain in force for the period of six months from today, as per section 437­ (A) of Cr.P.C. 3] Muddemal, if any, being worthless, be destroyed after appeal period is over. Thane, (A.S. Bhaisare) Date­ 06.03.2018. Special Judge (POCSO), Thane.
