Special Case No.111/2013 Judgment Received on : 20.11.2013 Registered on : 20.11.2013 Decided on : 19.09.2015 Duration : 1 year 10 months IN THE COURT OF THE SESSION JUDGE, THANE AT THANE (Presided over by Ms.V.V.Virkar, Additional Session Judge-1, Thane) Special Case No. 111 of 2013 Exhibit No. 21 The State of Maharashtra … Complainant versus Prashant Vijay Suryavanshi ... Accused Age 30 years, Resident of G-104, Sector 4, Airoli, Navi Mumbai. Appearance - Ms. R.A.Navale, learned Additional Public Prosecutor (hereinafter in short A.P.P.) Accused in person. .. 2 .. Special Case No.111/2013 Judgment JUDGMENT (Delivered on 19.09.2015) The accused stands prosecuted for offences punishable under section 354 and section 7 read with section 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter referred to as P.O.C.S.O. Act for short) for causing sexual assault and sexual harassment upon the victim complainant girl by calling her 'item item' and for committing act of physical advances in an unwelcome manner with her in spite of disinterest shown by her by catching hold of her hand and hugging her and thereby outraging her modesty. 2] In short the facts giving rise to the prosecution of the accused are that girl Namrata Kashinath Bele aged 14 years was staying with her parents at room no.A-90, sector no.4, Airoli and was studying 9th Std. at Airoli Madhyamik Vidyalay and also was attending tuition class at Airoli and her class timing was from 3.00 p.m. to 6.00 p.m. It was also case of the prosecution that on 09.06.2013 when she was returning back from school, accused was following her and was eve teasing her by calling her ' item item ' and he also caught hold of her at waist, she resisted but he caught hold of her hand, she somebody escaped and rushed home but the accused was chasing her and again caught her hand. It is further case of the prosecution that at that time she noticed two police persons coming on motorbike and she stopped them and narrated them about the incident and pointed out towards the accused. Then said police persons immediately caught the accused and took him to police station. The girl then went home and narrated the incident to her mother and then her mother took her to police station and the girl lodged complaint. .. 3 .. Special Case No.111/2013 Judgment 3] On the basis of her complaint, offence as per C.R.No.25/2013 was registered for offence punishable under section 354 of I.P.C. and section 7, 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act at Rabale police station, Navi Mumbai, and the work of investigation was done by P.S.I. Valvi. During the investigation the accused was arrested and arrest form was filled in. Statements of witnesses were recorded. Since the girl was seen to be minor and the acts committed by the accused was falling within the purview of P.O.C.S.O. Act, section 7 and 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act were applied and after completion of investigation, since there was sufficient evidence against the accused, he came to be charge-sheeted for offences punishable under section 354 of I.P.C. and section 7, 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act 4] Offence under P.O.C.S.O. Act is triable by Special Court and therefore the charge-sheet submitted to this Court. 5] The accused was produced before the Court. A charge for offences punishable under section 354 of I.P.C. and section 7 read with section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act was framed against the accused as per Exhibit 9. Contents of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. He pleaded not guilty. His defence as it revealed from his statement recorded under section 313 of Cr.P.C. was that he had not committed any offence and that on the day of incident his friend one Sachin was taken to police station and therefore, after returning from his work he had been to police station and there he was taken into custody by police and a false case is filed against him. He claimed to be tried. 6] For establishing guilt of accused, the prosecution examined P.W.1 complainant girl Namrata Kashinath Bele, her mother P.W.2 Nagamma Bele, P.W.3 Police Naik Santosh Avaghade, who caught the accused at the spot and P.W.4 A.P.I. Arvind Valvi I.O. The .. 4 .. Special Case No.111/2013 Judgment documentary evidence produced, proved and relied upon by the prosecution was in the form of complaint Exhibit 13 and arrest form of accused Exhibit 17. 7] Statement of the accused under section 313 of Cr.P.C. was recorded. He did not examine himself on oath and had not examined any witness in defence. 8] I heard the learned A.P.P. and learned advocate for the accused. 9] On the basis of above facts of this case, the points which arose for my determination, my reasons and findings thereon are as under - Points Findings i) Whether the prosecution proved that on 09.07.2013 around 6.00 p.m. the accused used criminal force against the complainant minor girl by hugging her and catching hold of her waist in spite of her resistance and thereby her outraged her modesty ? Yes. ii ) Whether the prosecution prove that on the given day, date, time and place, the accused committed sexual assault on the complainant minor girl ? No. iii ) What offence, if any, is proved against the Only offence accused ? under section 354 of I.P.C. is proved. iv ) What order ? As per the final order. .. 5 .. Special Case No.111/2013 Judgment REASONS As to point no.1 and 2 - 10] Both points are interconnected and are to be decided on the basis of same evidence. I therefore discuss and decide them together. As is clear the accused is charged for offences punishable under section 354 of I.P.C. and 7 read with section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act with the allegation that the accused had outraged modesty of the girl by accosting her and calling her ' item item ' and also by having physical advances with her in an unwelcome manner by hugging her at waist. In that regard the testimony of the girl who is the only eye witness and material witness is very much relevant. In her evidence she categorically stated that on the day of incident on 09.06.2013 when she returned from tuition classes around 6.00 p.m. one unknown person aged 20 to 22 yeas had come there from opposite direction and called her ' item item ' and caught hold of her waist and though she escaped and proceeded further he again came from behind and again caught hold of her from behind, she somehow escaped but he caught hold of her both hands and when she shouted loudly being scared, he left her hands. She also further stated that she then proceeded towards her house but said person was chasing her and she noticed two constables coming on bike, she stopped them and narrated incident and pointed out towards the accused and said police constables then caught said person on the spot. She also stated that said person's name revealed to be Prashant Suryvanshi, that is, name of the accused and also further, she identified the accused to be the .. 6 .. Special Case No.111/2013 Judgment same person. Her entire version has gone unchallenged since there is no cross-examination on behalf of accused. 11] Even her version that she noticed police persons on motorbike and narrated them incident and the accused was caught is also corroborated by the testimony of P.W.3 Police Naik Santosh Avaghade, buckle no.2083, who also narrated same incident and categorically stated that on the say of girl said person was caught and he told his name as Prashant Suryavanshi and that the accused is the same person. He further stated that the accused was taken to police station and the girl then came to police station and lodged complaint. His such version that the accused was taken to police station is further corroborated by P.W.4 A.P.I. Arvind Valvi, I.O. who also stated that on 09.06.2013 when she was on duty at police station, Police Naiks Avaghade and Desale brought one person by name Prashant Suryavanshi to police station and reported that he was shown by the girl stating that he had outraged her modesty and then he was arrested and offence was registered on the basis of complaint of the girl. 12] It is also material to mention that the girl stated that immediately after the incident, she went home and narrated about the incident to her mother. Her such version is also corroborated by her mother P.W.2 Nagamma Bele who also stated that on 09.06.2013 her daughter Namrata returned late than her usual time from tuition class and then she narrated that one boy caught hold of her and was not leaving her and she shouted and escaped but still he was chasing and she noticed police people coming on bike and she went to them and narrated them the incident. She also stated that she then went to police station alongwith her daughter and said person was also there in the police station and she also identified the accused to be the same person. As such, from the testimony of the girl as well as P.Ws. 2 and 3 .. 7 .. Special Case No.111/2013 Judgment it is very much clear that on the given day, date, time and place, the accused had accosted the girl, called her ' item item ' and also used criminal force against her by hugging her at her waist. It is also material to mention that the accused was not known to the girl or her mother or police officials who caught him and in the complaint also there is reference of unknown person but the fact is also clear that he was caught on the spot after the girl pointed out towards him and then he was taken to police station. There is no reason for the girl to state so falsely or even no plausible explanation is offered by the accused for said witness to depose against him falsely. 13] No doubt, in his statement recorded under section 313 of Cr.P.C. he appear to have put forth defence that on the day of incident his friend Sunil was taken by police to police station and therefore on the same day after returning from his work, he had been to police station and there the police had taken him into custody and a false case is lodged against him and it was suggested to the I.O. in cross- examination by the accused in person that his friend Sunil and Tole and mother of said Sunil were caught by police and his friend had then informed him about it and therefore he himself had been to police station on that day to see in that matter and was falsely involved in this case. However, said suggestion was denied by the I.O. and absolutely no material is brought on record even to show preponderance of probability of the defence put forth by the accused. Then, on request of accused vide Exhibit 19 summons were issued to witnesses by name Sachin Tole and Anita Tole proposed to be examined on behalf of accused and summonses were also served upon said witness. But subsequently vide Exhibit 20 the accused submitted that he do not want to examine any witness in defence. In any case, as discussed above, the accused being unknown to the complainant girl and her .. 8 .. Special Case No.111/2013 Judgment mother and there appear no reason for them to go all the way to police station and lodge complaint with such allegations against the accused. 14] It is also to be mentioned that there is presumption as to certain offences under P.O.C.S.O. Act and section 29 of P.O.C.S.O. Act provides that '' Where a person is prosecuted for committing or abetting or attempting to commit any offence under sections 3, 5, 7 and 9 of this Act, the Special Court shall presume, that such person has committed or abetted or attempted to commit the offence, as the case may be, unless the contrary is proved ''. However, as discussed above, the accused has not brought any material on record to show preponderance of his defence and therefore it has to be conclude that the presumption is not rebutted. 15] In view of all above discussion it has to be concluded that the allegation against the accused that he had outraged modesty of the complainant girl by using criminal force against her by hugging her at waist and also had physical advances in an unwelcome manner with her in spite of disinterest shown by her, is established. 16] It is also to be mentioned that the accused is charged for the offence punishable under section 7 read with section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and therefore the aspect about age of the girl is also material for coming to the conclusion in regard to guilt or otherwise of the accused in regard to offence under section 7 read with section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. In that regard as is clear the prosecution has not produced on record any documentary proof in regard to age of the girl. The fact also cannot be overlooked and ignored that the complainant victim girl in her evidence also has not stated her age and only stated that at the relevant time she was studying in 9th Std. Even mother of the girl also in her evidence stated nothing about either the age of the girl or her date of birth. .. 9 .. Special Case No.111/2013 Judgment 17] It is submitted on behalf of prosecution that the girl in her deposition while stating her name, address etc. stated her age as 16 years and on that basis it has to be inferred that the girl at the relevant time in the year 2013 was 14 years old and her such version has gone unchallenged since there is no cross-examination. But in that regard it is to be mentioned that when the provisions of P.O.C.S.O. Act are applied, it was necessary for the prosecution to establish the fact that the girl was child below 18 years of age at the time of incident by cogent and reliable evidence. In that respect though provisions of P.O.C.S.O. Act are applied, the investigating officer has not bothered or cared to collect evidence in regard to age of the girl and no satisfactory explanation is offered as to why even birth certificate of certificate from school of the girl in regard to her date of birth is not obtained though the girl stated that at that time she was studying in 9th Std. The girl was not even referred for medical examination for age determination and in such circumstances merely on the basis that at the time of telling her name and age etc. before Court the girl stated her age to be 16 years and in absence of any statement in her evidence about her age or her date of birth and absence of any documentary evidence it cannot be concluded that the prosecution has established that the girl was child within the meaning of provisions of P.O.C.S.O. Act and therefore, the offence under section 7 read with section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act cannot be said to be established. 18] In view of above discussion since the fact that the accused had outraged modesty of the complainant girl on the given day, date, time and place is established, the offence under section 354 of I.P.C. has to be held as established against the accused. However, since the fact that the girl was child at the relevant time is not proved by cogent and reliable evidence, the offence under section 7 read with section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act cannot be said to have been established .. 10 .. Special Case No.111/2013 Judgment and the accused is entitled to be acquitted of the charge for offence under section 7 read with section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. In view of above discussion I hold the accused guilty for offence punishable under section 354 of I.P.C. and convict him for the said offence. Point no.1 is answered accordingly. 19] At this stage the dictation of the Judgment is postponed for hearing the accused on the point of sentence. Date : 19.09.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Additional Session Judge-1, Thane. Resumed. 20] The accused is made aware of the fact that he is held guilty for the offence under section 354 of Indian penal Code and the punishment prescribed for said offence is Imprisonment which shall not be less than one year but which may extend to five and also fine 21] I heard the learned A.P.P. and the accused on the point of sentence. The learned A.P.P. submitted that looking to the serious nature of offence charged against the accused he is not entitled to leniency and he is liable to award maximum punishment prescribed. The accused prayed for showing him leniency on the ground that he is the only earning member in his family and his family is depending upon him for their livelihood. 22] So far as the quantum of sentence is concerned, it has to be mentioned that it is well settled that it is the duty of the Court in .. 11 .. Special Case No.111/2013 Judgment every case to award proper sentence, having regard to the nature of the offence, the manner in which it is committed and to all mitigating circumstances. Even it is also well settled that in the matter of fixation of punishment for any particular crime, the Court should take into consideration the nature of offence, the circumstances in which it was committed and the degree of deliberation shown by the offender and also that the measure of punishment should be proportionate to the gravity of the offence and it is also the responsibility of the Court to see that the sentence should not be excessive and at the same time it should not be too lenient or liberal. 23] Then, as is clear the offence charged against the accused is of serious nature with the allegation that he has outraged modesty of the complainant girl by pulling her hand and holding her at waist again and again in spite of her resistance and by calling her as ' item item '. 24] In the light of that I am of the view that following sentence would meet ends of justice. In the result I pass the following order - ORDER Accused namely Prashant Vijay Suryavanshi is convicted for the offence punishable under section 354 of the Indian Penal Code and is sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for the term he has already undergone in jail and also to pay fine of Rs.500/- [rupees five hundred only] and in default of payment of fine amount, he shall undergo imprisonment for five days. ii ) The accused is in jail since 09.07.2013. A set off under section 438 of Cr.P.C. is granted to him against the substantive sentence for the term of the period of detention undergone by him during the investigation, inquiry and trial. .. 12 .. Special Case No.111/2013 Judgment iii ) The accused is acquitted of the charge for offence punishable under section 7 read with section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. iv ) Since no muddemal property is produced before Court, no order regarding its disposal is passed. v) Copy of judgment be given to the accused free of cost. vi ) The proceeding is closed. Date : 19.09.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Additional Session Judge-1, Thane.

No particular number of witnesses is required for proving a certain fact. It is the quality and not the quantity of the witnesses that matters. Evidence is weighed and not counted. The said evidence does not find place in her statement before police and it can be said that she had improved her evidence before the court. 16] It has come in the chief­examination of P.W.2 Suvarna Rajbali Vishvakarma that­ “Suhana is her younger sister. The same does not find place in her statement before police. P.W.3 A.P.I. Mr. Vishvas Patil has stated that P.W.2 Suvarna had not stated the same in her statement. 18] P.W.3 A.P.I. Mr. Vishvas Ramchandra Patil has deposed as per his investigation. 19] From the evidence of P.W.1 victim, it can be gathered that she had not disclosed the incident either with her mother or with her sister P.W.2. No. 112/2013. available on 28.07.13. In her statement before police, she had not stated that 'her elder sister had followed her, she viewed the incident from the window of the house of accused, the said incident is narrated by her elder sister to her mother, thereafter, her mother had been to the house of accused to fire him, but, accused was not found, on next day, she again came to the house of accused, accused was present in his house, on noticing the incident by the neighbourers, they gathered there and assaulted the accused and taken him to police station.' So also, she had not stated in her statement before police that the accused had given his penis in her mouth. 22] P.W.2 Suvarna deposed in her cross­examination that she had stated before the police in her statement that accused was pressing chest of the victim. P.W.3 Vishvas Patil has stated in his evidence that Suvarna had not stated before him that the accused had pressed the chest of victim. 23] Spot panchanama is placed on record at Exh. 17. It goes to show that on 28.07.13, victim had shown the spot. It is room no. 575 of Patil compound, Sathenagar, Digha, Navi Mumbai. The spot seems to be the house of accused, rather bed. One T.V. was found on the day of incident. However, from the said spot panchanama, it cannot be gathered that there was V.C.R., V.C.D., C.D. player or pen­drive by which cinema or pictures can be viewed on T.V. Therefore, it is very difficult to rely upon the evidence of P.W.1 victim that on previous day, accused had shown her pornography on his T.V. set. 24] P.W.2 Suvarna deposed in her evidence that at about 3.00 p.m., she noticed the accused while taking the victim to his house. She followed them. She has not stated in her evidence that she had called her sister victim. Easily she could have called her sister, if the accused was taking the victim to his house. No witnesses are examined by the 13 S.C. No. 112/2013. prosecution on that point. Other students might have been on the road due to recess. But, the students have also not been examined. Room of the accused is situated in the chawl. But, no neighbourers have been examined to show that the accused along with victim entered into his house and thereafter, victim came out from the house of accused. 25] P.W.2 Suvarna further deposed in her evidence that accused along with victim were present in the house. Door of his house was found closed. However, window was open. Her sister was found in the naked condition. Accused was found while pressing her chest and her private part. P.W.2 Suvarna now is aged about 17 years. At relevant time, she might be aged about 14 years. She was knowing the consequences of the act of accused and victim. But, Suvarna has not raised any hue or cry. She easily could have collected the neighbourers by raising hue and cry. 26] Besides, from the spot panchanama, it cannot be gathered that there is window to the house of accused. 27] P.W.2 Suvarna further deposed in her evidence that thereafter, she rushed to her house and disclosed the facts to the mother. But, informant has not done anything. Thereafter, P.W.2 Suvarna went to her school. After sometime, victim also came to the school. If such incident could have taken place, certainly the informant along with her both daughters or alone, would have been to the house of accused for asking job. But, she has done nothing. P.W.2 Suvarna happily went to the school. She has not disclosed the incident to the teachers or to any students or class­ teacher. Victim also attended the school. But, she has also not stated the incident either to her mother, sister, teachers, class­teacher or class­mate. 28] P.W.2 Suvarna further deposed in her evidence that at about 14 S.C. No. 112/2013. 5.00 p.m., they both returned to their house from the school and they had narrated the incident to their mother. Then, her mother went to her sister Seeta Dindor to disclose the incident. This witness has not stated that her mother had been to the house of accused to inquire about the incident. But, as accused was not found in his house, the informant had kept mum. 29] The alleged incident took place on 26.07.2013 during noon time i.e. at about 3.00 p.m. The incident was narrated by P.W.2 to the informant, immediately after the incident. So also, at evening time after school was over, the incident was also disclosed to the informant. However, the report was lodged on 28.07.2013 at about 15.05 noon. The delay in lodging F.I.R. is not explained by the prosecution satisfactorily. 30] No doubt, there is no evidence on record from the side of accused to show that why prosecutrix rather her mother had filed her report against the accused. It is not explained by the accused during cross­ examination of P.W.1 to 3. Merely because accused has not explained the same, it cannot be said that prosecution has proved the case. Prosecution has to prove their case beyond all reasonable doubt. They cannot take the benefit of weakness of defence i.e. accused. It cannot be overlooked that the sole testimony of the victim can be relied upon and sufficient for conviction on her own sole evidence, subject to reliability, trustworthiness, truthfulness in her evidence. 31] In the present case, evidence of P.W.1 and 2 creates doubt in the mind for the reasons stated supra in foregoing paragraphs of my judgment. As such, it can safely be said that prosecution failed to prove the alleged offence against accused beyond all reasonable doubts. In the result, I answer all the points in the negative and proceed to pass the following order. 15 S.C. No. 112/2013. ORDER 1] Accused Raju Namdev Suryavanshi, is hereby, acquitted under sec. 235(1) of the Criminal Procedure Code, of the offences punishable u/s. 354, 506 of I.P.C. and u/s. 7 punishable under section 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] Accused Raju Namdev Suryavanshi, be enlarged on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ with surety of like amount. The effect of this bail order will remain in force for the period of six months from today, as per section 437­(A) of Cr.P.C. Thane, (A.S. Bhaisare) Date­ 23.08.2017. As a matter of fact, the victim herself was knowing accused prior to incident and there is no scope of any suspicion. 26] Accused has a right to take inconsistent defence but that cannot mean to confuse the witness on one point to other point. It is brought on record in cross examination of victim that none of the persons to whom she had stated about the incident on the day of incident, had ever communicated or contacted with her mother in regard to incident. It is borne in mind that according to victim, on 2.9.2013 when she had bleeding from her place of urination, then she ..19/- ..19.. Spl. C. No.113/2013 (Exh.No.96) narrated the fact to Nilofar. However, it is brought on record in the cross examination that Nilofar has informed about the incident to her mother on phone and she knows that because she was present there and she talked to her mother on phone. Such type of cross examination is not sufficient to disbelieve the version of witness but rather can be said in order to confuse the witness the facts put to her. Had it been a fact, then that has to be put to mother of victim in her cross examination. There is no probable explanation as to how accused came to know that Nilofar narrated the incident to informant on phone. Any suggestion put to witness during the cross examination is on the basis of the material provided by accused to his counsel. Thus, inspite of lengthy and searching cross examination there is nothing brought on record that before stepping down into witness box by victim, she was tutored by anyone or due to any grudge, victim deposed against accused. 27] The evidence of victim is trustworthy and having inspiring confidence. As a matter of fact, there is no material omission and contradiction in her evidence so that to disbelieve her version. By examining I.O. PW 8 prosecution proved portions marked 'A' & 'B' from the police statement of PW 10 Rehana. Prosecution also explained the delay caused due to fear in filing complaint. 28] In the citation Tukaram cited supra, His Lordship held in para No.13 that in a case of rape, rape is committed when male organ penetrates, at least partial, the female organ. In between complete rape and attempt to commit rape,there is a rear area covered by S. 354 of IPC i.e. assault or criminal force to woman with intent to outrage her modesty or indecent assault. The dividing line between attempt to ..20/- ..20.. Spl. C. No.113/2013 (Exh.No.96) commit rape and indecent assault is not only thin but also is practically invisible. For an offence of attempt to commit rape, prosecution is required to establish that the act of accused went beyond the stage of preparation. According to victim, accused removed her clothes by making her to lie on bed, caught hold of her legs and when she tried to shout, he gagged her mouth and had led on her after removing his clothes. He slept over her and had touched her private part by his hand. Thus, it is not the version of victim herself that accused committed rape or attempted to commit rape. According to expert, there is no evidence of injury, blood or semenal stains on perineum and introitus. Hymen was found intact. Thus, on marshalling the evidence of victim and medical evidence on record then it is clear that on the day of incident, accused outraged the modesty of victim by naked her and also slept over her. However, there is no evidence in respect of penetration of penis in her vagina or made any attempt to commit rape. Thus, accused committed offence punishable u/s 354 of IPC and not offence punishable u/s 376 of IPC. 29] As per S. 29 and 30 of POCSO Act, the presumption is in favour of prosecution. Inspite of searching cross examination, defence failed to overcome the presumption. The evidence of victim is sufficient to establish that accused committed sexual assault as he touched her private part. When victim is minor and accused committed sexual assault as defined in S. 7 of the POCSO Act, then accused is liable to punish for sexual assault as per S.8 of POCSO Act. ..21/- ..21.. Spl. C. No.113/2013 (Exh.No.96) 30] So far as the charge u/s 450 of IPC is concerned, one of the ingredient of house trespass for committing any offence punishable with imprisonment for life. In view of the above discussion, accused committed offence punishable u/s 354 of IPC and not u/s 376 of IPC. Punishment prescribed for offence punishable u/ 354 of IPC is year upto 5 years and not for life. Thus, the point No.2 (charge u/s 450 of IPC) is redundant in view of finding recorded to point No.1. 31] As per charge Exh.6, accused is facing trial for offence punishable u/s 376 of IPC r/w S. 6 & 8 of POCSO Act, but as per oral and documentary evidence, prosecution proved beyond reasonable doubt that accused committed offence punishable u/s 354 of IPC r/w S. 8 of POCSO Act. The punishment prescribed for offence punishable u/s 376 of IPC is of 7 years which may extent to imprisonment of life, whereas, u/s 354 of IPC punishment is from one year to 5 years. Punishment u/s 6 of POCSO Act is from 10 years to life imprisonment whereas u/s 8 of POCSO Act is from 3 years to 5 years. Thus, charge Exh.6 put for major offence whereas prosecution proved charge of minor offence, hence, as per the provisions of S. 222 of Cr.P.C., accused may be convicted for minor offence without framing separate charge of that minor offence. With this, I record my finding to the point Nos. 1 to 3 accordingly and pause here to hear the accused on the point of sentence. Place : Thane (R.N.Bawankar) Date : 4.7.2017 Special Judge (POCSO Act), Thane. 32] I heard accused on the point of sentence, who submitted that he is having three kids. His mother and wife are also depending ..22/- ..22.. Spl. C. No.113/2013 (Exh.No.96) upon him. He is only earning member in his family and this is the first offence therefore, lenient view be taken while awarding the sentence. The Ld. APP Smt. Hivrale submitted that maximum punishment be awarded looking to the nature of crime. The Ld. Defence Counsel prayed for leniency and also submitted that accused was not previously convicted. 33] So far as awarding of sentence is concerned, that punishment not served the purpose of the trial, but that must be given message to the society at large. The evidence of record clearly shows that accused was well acquainted with victim who is minor. The evidence on record also shows that previously like nature of offence was registered against accused and same was compromised. Due to fear of accused, nobody from locality came forward inspite of knowledge of incident. Thus, it is clear that in the vicinity of accused, there is fear in respect of accused regarding sexual assault on minor. Therefore, no question arises regarding leniency. However, considering the age of victim and the nature of crime, the Ld. APP rightly submitted for maximum sentence to be awarded. Thus, I am of the opinion the following punishment is sufficient to meet the ends of justice. : ORDER : 1] Accused Mohammad Alam Mohammad Aslam Shaikh, aged 40 years is held guilty u/s 235 of Cr.P.C. for the offence punishable u/s 354 of I.P.C. and he is sentenced to suffer R.I. for three years with fine of Rs. 5,000/­ (Rs. Five Thousand only), in default, to suffer R.I. for six months. 2] Accused Mohammad Alam Mohammad Aslam Shaikh, aged 40 years is held guilty for the offence punishable u/s 8 of Protection of Children From ..23/- ..23.. Five Thousand only), in default, to suffer R.I. for one year. 3] Both the sentences are ordered to run concurrently with further benefits u/s 428 of Cr.P.C. 4] Accused Mohammad Alam Mohammad Aslam Shaikh, aged 40 years is hereby acquitted u/s 235 of Cr.P.C. from the charge of offence punishable u/s 376 and 450 of I.P.C. 5] Bail bond of accused is surrendered. 6] Accused was in police custody from 3.9.2013 and thereafter he was in jail till 5.5.2014. Accused Offence punishable under Section 363, 376 and section 366A read with 34 of Indian Penal Code and section 6 of POCSO Act, 2012. Appearance: A.P.P. Smt.Tallar APP for State. Advocate Shri.B. W. Gaikwad for accused. JUDGMENT (Delivered on this 29th day of March 2018) 1. The accused Nos.1 and 2 have alleged to have committed an offence under section under section 363, 366A, 376 read with 34 of Indian Penal Code and section 6 of POCSO Act. JUDGMENT 2 Spl.case No.115/2013 (CNR NO. MHTH01­006507­2013) 2. The case of the prosecution projected from police report is that accused No.1 kidnapped the minor victim aged 15 years out of the custody of her aunt from Pradnya Nagar, Plot No.78, Kalwa on 16.03.2013 and kept her in his possession till 03.10.2013 and committed repeated penetrative sexual assault and raped her without her consent and will and made her pregnant. On 17.03.2013 the informant who is aunt of the victim lodged FIR in Kalwa police station. C.R.No.I­126/2013 was registered and investigated by PSI. Sachin Bharat Kothmire. He recorded statements of witnesses , done routine investigation and sent charge­sheet. 3. Charge is frame against accused No.1 and 2 under section 363, 366A, 376(I) and section 5 (i)(ii) punishable under section 6 of POCSO Act, 2012. Accused pleaded not guilty. 4. Following points arose for determination of the court. Its' findings are given with the reasons, as under :­ Sr.No. Points Findings 1. Does prosecution prove that on 16.03.2013 at 15.30 to 03.10.2013 at Pradnya Nagar, Plot No.76 at Kalwa In negative. accused No.1 kidnapped minor girl aged 15 years from the lawful guardianship of her aunt and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 363 read with 34 of IPC ? JUDGMENT 3 Spl.case No.115/2013 (CNR NO. MHTH01­006507­2013) 2. Does prosecution prove that on the In the negative. aforesaid date, time and place, accused Nos. 1 and 2 in furtherance of their common intention induced the minor victim aged 15 years to go from any place with intent that such girl may be or knowing that it is likely that she will be forced or seduced to illicit intercourse with another person and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 366A read with 34 of IPC? 3 Does prosecution prove that on the In the negative. aforesaid date, time and place, accused No.1 committed repeated rape upon minor victim aged 15 years and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 376(I) of IPC? 4 Does prosecution prove that on the In the negative. above place accused No.1 from 16.03.2013 to 03.10.2013 committed aggravated penetrative sexual assault upon the minor victim aged 15 years and made her pregnant and committed offence punishable under section 5(j)(ii) punishable under section 6 of POCSO Act, 2012? 5 What order? As per final order. :REASONS: As to Point No.1 to 5 :­ 5. Prosecution has examined in all three witnesses i.e. victim herself at Exh.12, she is aged 19 years at the time of recording her evidence. She has got married with accused no.1 JUDGMENT 4 Spl.case No.115/2013 (CNR NO. MHTH01­006507­2013) since the date of incident. According to the victim, her mother died in 2008 and therefore, she was residing with accused No.2 at her house. Accused family was residing adjoining to the aunt's of the victim and therefore, accused had maintained her after death of her mother. She does not know where her father resides. She was learning in 8th standard at Thane. After leaving her education she was residing with accused Nos.1 and 2. She has stated that nothing was happened on 16.03.2013. In her cross­examination she has stated that nothing was happened denied that accused No.1 kidnapped her and committed sexual assault upon her repeatedly. She denied that she was made pregnant by accused No.1. She stated that she is married with accused No.1 and therefore, she does not want to say anything and she has no complaint against accused Nos.1 and 2. 6. The informant P.W.2 is examined at Exh.16. According to her, victim was residing for some days in her house. After her mother's death in 2013 the victim left home. Then she thought that accused might have kidnapped her so she lodged FIR vide Exh.17. She admitted that the accused would residing in her neighbourhood and they would visit each other. She admitted that in 2013 the victim herself left home without informing anybody. 7. P.W.3 Manjusha Mandhukar Bhosale is the API of Kalwa police station. She recorded FIR as per say of informant. The investigation was done by API Kothmire. JUDGMENT 5 Spl.case No.115/2013 (CNR NO. MHTH01­006507­2013) 8. The victim herself turned hostile and she got married with accused No.1, therefore, she has not supported the case of prosecution. Sufficient chances were given to the prosecution for examining the other witnesses and Investigating Officer. But Investigating Officer did not remain present. Considering the evidence on record it appears that even examining the other witnesses the case is not likely to be progressed. Therefore, the court closed the evidence of the prosecution. Nothing incriminating was proved, therefore, the statement under section 313 of Cr. P.C is also dispensed with. 9. Considering the evidence the victim herself has married with the accused No.1. There was no force committed at that time and after that. She was attained the age of majority, at the time of incident she was 15 years old. At that time she was knowing what is good and what is bad. Her father was not maintaining her. Her mother was dead and therefore, accused No.2 who is mother of accused No.1 was maintaining the victim and victim was residing in the house of accused. There was no force inducement committed by the accused. The important witness i.e. victim herself has not supported and therefore, the prosecution could not prove any of the ingredients of the offences. The evidence of P.W.2 also does not improve the case of prosecution, therefore, her evidence is also not helpful to the prosecution. I therefore, come to the conclusion that prosecution has failed to prove offences against accused beyond doubt. Therefore, I answered JUDGMENT 6 Spl.case No.115/2013 (CNR NO. MHTH01­006507­2013) above point in the negative and pass the following order. Thane. Appearance ­ Mrs. R.A.Navale, learned Additional Public Prosecutor (hereinafter in short A.P.P.) Accused in person. JUDGMENT (Delivered on 25.08.2015) .. 2 .. Special Case No. 116/2013 Judgment The accused stand prosecuted for the offence punishable under section 363, 366A, 376 of I.P.C. and section 4, 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as ''P.O.C.S.O. Act'') for kidnapping minor girl Karishma Mudgal aged 14 years from lawful guardianship of her parents from with a view to force or seduce her for sexual intercourse with the accused and for having committed rape and sexual assault on her on 25.08.2013 at platform no.2 of Pune railway station. 2] In short the facts giving rise to the prosecution of the accused are that on 26.08.2013 one Mrs. Sundar Sunil Mudgal lodged complaint that she is staying with her husband and children including her daughter Karishma 12 years old and said Karishma was studying in 8th Std. in Kanya Shala. That one Ramesh Ramane and his wife were staying in their neighbourhood and Sumit Sakpal i.e. accused, used to come to their house. Both were working with one caterer and therefore they developed acquaintance. Girl Karishma oftenly used to talk to accused but she (complainant) disliked it and therefore she had warned her daughter not to talk to him. Still accused used to call her daughter to the house of his friend and used to talk to her but she did not think it proper and had prevented her daughter from talking to accused. That on 25.08.2013 her daughter left house around 7.00 p.m. on the pretext that she would going to shop but she did not return home. They searched for her but she could not be traced. She then went to the house of Ramesh Ramane in search of her .. 3 .. Special Case No. 116/2013 Judgment daughter but she was not there. She then contacted the accused on his mobile phone from mobile phone of one Sanjay Khatri who was working with him and inquired about her daughter and that time accused told that her daughter is with him and he is going to marry her. She then contacted Ramesh Ramane, friend of accused, and he also told that they are together and would be performing marriage of the accused with the girl. Since the girl was minor aged 12 years she went to police station and lodged complaint. 3] On the basis of her complaint offence as per C.R.No.I­ 420/2013 under section 363, 366A, 376 of I.P.C. and section 4, 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act was registered at Kalwa Police Station and the work of investigation was entrusted to P.S.I. Pardeshi. During the investigation statements of witnesses including victim girl was recorded. The girl was referred for medical examination and after obtaining her medical certificate and on the basis of statement of the girl since it revealed that the accused had sexual intercourse with the girl, additional charge under section 376 of I.P.C. was also applied. Statements of witnesses were recorded from time to time. Accused came to be arrested and was also referred for medical examination. Clothes on the person of the accused as well as girl were seized and samples obtained and clothes seized were sent for chemical analysis to C.A. Since the girl was reported to be minor, certificate about her age was obtained and after completion of investigation since there was sufficient evidence against the accused, he came to be charge­sheeted for offence punishable under section 363, 366A, 376 of I.P.C. and section 4, 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. .. 4 .. Special Case No. 116/2013 Judgment 4] This Court being Special Court to try the offences punishable under P.O.C.S.O. Act, the charge­sheet was submitted to this Court. 5] The accused was produced before court by jail authority. A charge for offences punishable under section 363, 366A, 376 of I.P.C. and section 4, 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act was framed against the accused as per Exhibit 3. Contents of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. The accused pleaded not guilty. His defence was of total denial. He claimed to be tried. 6] Since there is no incriminating evidence appearing on record against the accused, his statement under section 313 of Cr.P.C. is dispensed with. 7] On the basis of above facts of the case the points which arose for my determination, my reasons and findings for the same are as under ­ Points Findings i) Whether the prosecution proved that on 25.08.2013 around 7.00 p.m. near the house of complainant at Shanti Nagar Slum, near Ramdata Mandir, in front of New Shivaji nagar, Kalwa (E), the accused kidnapped the victim girl from lawful guardianship of her parents with intent to force or seduce her to have illicit intercourse with himself ? Not proved. .. 5 .. Special Case No. 116/2013 Judgment ii ) Whether the prosecution proved that after kidnapping the girl, the accused committed rape and sexual assault on the girl by doing forcible sexual intercourse with her ? Not proved. iii ) What offence, if any, is proved against No offence is the accused ? proved. iv ) What order ? The accused is acquitted. REASONS As to point no.1 and 2 ­ 8] As is clear though the complaint was filed by mother of the girl about kidnapping and abduction of the minor girl and even though the girl in her statement alleged to have stated about forceful sexual intercourse by the accused with her time and again and also about kidnapping, it is to be mentioned that the prosecution had not examined any witness. Then, it is also clear that in spite of repeated chances given to the prosecution since after charge was framed on 01.07.2014 the prosecution had not taken proper steps to secure presence of witnesses. Witness summons on the request of prosecution was issued to the complainant and her daughter i.e. victim girl. But, as is clear, the summons report show that they had left the address and were not available at the address given and they were reported to have left for their native place and the prosecution had not been able to secure new address of said witnesses and no steps to examine other witnesses were taken in spite of sufficient time was granted to the prosecution and therefore, as per order below Exhibit 1 the prosecution evidence was closed. It is clear that though offence .. 6 .. Special Case No. 116/2013 Judgment under section 363, 366A, 376 of I.P.C. and section 4, 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act is of serious nature, material witnesses i.e. complainant as well as the victim girl did not come forward to state anything against the accused and therefore the averments in the complaint cannot be said to have been proved and in absence of any evidence, none of the allegations against the accused can be said to have been established. It is also to be mentioned that the accused was in jail all along since 29.08.2013 and in spite of sufficient opportunity given to prosecution, it was not able to adduce any evidence to substantiate the charges and therefore no allegations against the accused can be said to have been proved. Point no. 1 and 2 are answered accordingly in the negative. As to point no.3 ­ 9] In view of my above findings no offence can be said to have been proved against the accused and the accused is entitled to be acquitted. Point no.3 is therefore answered accordingly. 10] Since the accused is acquitted, it is necessary that he be directed to furnish P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] under section 437A of Cr.P.C. to appear before the higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect of any appeal or petition, if filed against the judgment and that such bail bond shall be in force for six months. In the result I pass the following order­ ORDER Accused namely Sumit Eknath Sakpal is acquitted of the charge for offence punishable under section 363, 366A, 376 of .. 7 .. Special Case No. 116/2013 Judgment I.P.C. and under section 4 and 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2) The accused shall be released from the jail forthwith if not required in any other crime. 3) The accused shall furnish P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] under section 437A of Cr.P.C. to appear before the higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect of any appeal or petition, if any filed against the judgment and that such bail bond shall be in force for six months. 4) Muddemal articles, being worthless, be destroyed after expiry of appeal period. 5) The proceeding is closed. It is further submitted that in such circumstance in order to make thorough investigation regarding the communication made by the applicant with the deceased for demanding sexual enjoyment with her, the custodial interrogation of the applicant/accused is necessary. Anti Bail 2317/14 (Ord.Exh.1) suicide due to harassment at the hands of accused no.1, the present applicant apprehends his arrest in this crime on account of false implication by the complainant. Act). It was contended and argued that the applicants are arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the the applicant committed sexual assault and rape on minor girl i.e. daughter of the complainant. It is further contended and argued that the applicants are falsely implicated. It is further contended and argued that nothing incriminating is found with the applicant and there is no direct evidence against him. It is further submitted that two women co­accused have already been ordered to be released on bail and therefore the present applicant is also entitled to be released on bail. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co­operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that on the day of incident the complainant had sent victim girl Rehana to grocery soap to bring soap but thereafter the girl did not return home and the complainant lodged missing report. It is further contended and argued that on her way to home girl Rehana had met co­accused .. 2 .. bail no.2476/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Reena who took her to her house by telling that nobody was there in her house. It is further contended and argued that present applicant/accused Javed met them in their way to home of accused Reena, they three thereafter were roaming at Vashi and thereafter Reena and victim girl went to the house of Reena. It is further contended and argued that victim girl Rehana had stayed there and slept in the house of Reena in that night and it is further contended that in the night time Rehana woke up from sleep and saw that applicant/accused Javed was sat by her side and Reena was also standing there and thereafter Reena left and it is further contended that Javed then caught hold of her and gagged her mouth and started removing her clothes and at that time victim Rehana resisted but Javed committed rape on her and left the place. It is further contended and argued that after incident of sexual assault, victim Rehana disclosed about it to Reena and her mother Durga i.e. present applicant no.2, but both of them warned her not to disclose about the act of Javed to anybody. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl and other prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, the offences charged against the applicants/accused are of serious nature under section 363, 376 read with section 34 of I.P.C. and section 3, 4 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and it is the allegation that applicant/accused Javed committed sexual assault on the victim girl in the house of co­accused Reena and Durga and at .. 3 .. bail no.2476/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) that time said two women accused also were present in the house and at their connivance present applicant committed sexual assault on the victim girl and as per prosecution case the said women accused also threatened the victim girl not to disclose about the act of sexual assault made by present applicant. Then, the investigation in the matter is stated to be in progress. Then, though it is contended on behalf of accused that he is innocent and he is falsely implicated in this case, it is to be mentioned that no girl would inflict her own character by lodging false complaint that she is being subjected to sexual assault and further, looking to serious allegations of sexual assault on minor girl, such allegations will have to be decided on merits and at this stage it would be premature to conclude that the applicant/accused is falsely involved in the crime. 4] No doubt it is well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. However, it has to be mentioned that besides that the gravity and serious nature of offence and the manner in which it is stated to have been committed also has to be looked into and looking to the nature of offence and the manner in which it is alleged to have been committed, a wrong message would be sent to the society in case of release of accused on bail in such type of matter wherein serious allegations of sexual assault on minor girl are made. 5] Then, it is also to be mentioned that investigation in the matter is stated to be in progress and and looking to serious nature .. 4 .. bail no.2476/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) of allegation and the manner in which offence is stated to have been committed there is possibility that the accused may threaten and pressurize the complainant and victim girl and other witnesses. Even the possibility of accused being absconded if released on bail is also there. 6] Then, so far ground of parity is concerned, the role assigned to the said two women accused who have been ordered to be released on bail is that the incident is alleged to have been taken place in the house of said two accused and after the incident the girl disclosed about the incident to them whereas the present applicant/accused is named as the person who actually committed sexual assault on the minor victim girl and even also threatened her not to disclose about the said and therefore when a clear role is assigned to the present applicant, prima facie there is material against him showing his implication in commission of offence and therefore, ground of parity to claim bail is not available to him. 7] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is not a fit case wherein the applicant/accused can be said to be entitled to be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is rejected. Date : 12.10.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Additional Session Judge­1, Thane.

I­ 403/2015 registered at Kapurbnavdi Police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 307, 354(1)D, 336, 324, 143, 147, 148, 149, 323, 504, 506 of I.P.C. and section 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). It is contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that accused persons including the applicants attacked the complainant and witnesses with intent to cause their murder. It is further contended and argued that the applicants were present at the spot and they intervened the scuffle between the accused and witnesses and at that time police suddenly came and took the applicants into custody while the main culprits fled away on motorcycles. It is further contended and argued that the applicants have been falsely implicated in this crime with ulterior motive. It is further submitted that the applicants are permanent residents of the address given and that if they are released on bail, they will co­operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicants are entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it is contended and argued that co­accused .. 2 .. Bail No.2477/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) Akshay Khavare was following and stalking the minor daughter of complainant namely Guddi aged 15 years and was always eve teasing her and therefore the wife of the complainant had given him understanding but that time there was hot exchange of words between them and even the accused had also threatened to take away Guddi. It is further contended and argued that after said quarrel, on 23.09.2010 the complainant, his family members and other witnesses were returning home after Ganapati immersion and it was around 10.00 p.m. when the co­accused Akshay Khavare in furtherance of common intention with present applicants/accused attacked the complainant and witnesses and beat them with beer bottle, bricks and also by fist blows and caused serious injury to witnesses Sampat and Akash and others. Act in regard to stalking the minor daughter of the complainant namely Guddi aged 15 years and also attempting to commit murder at the time of incident in question, from perusal of complaint, copy of which is filed on record, it appears that co­accused Akshay Khavare has been named in the .. 3 .. In such circumstance the aspect as to whether the allegations against the accused are true or whether the defence of false implication put forth by the accused is probable, will have to be decided on merits. 4] Then, it is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. Presented on­ 13.11.2014. Registered on­ 13.11.2014. Decided on­ 29.09.2018. Duration­ Y­ 3 M­10 D­16 IN THE COURT OF SESSIONS, THANE, AT THANE. (Before V.Y. Jadhav, Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.) SPECIAL CASE (POCSO) NO. 239 OF 2014 CNR : MHTH01­006517­2014 Exh. No. The State (Through Srinagar Police Station) ..Prosecution V/s. Arun Raju Vaidya, Age 21 years, Occ. Sweeping, R/o. Besides Datta temple, Hanumannagar, Wagle Estate, Thane. ..Accused. Appearance :­ ___________________________________________________________ For State : P.P. Smt. S.E. Phad. For Accused : Adv. Shri. Mahendra Gaikwad. ___________________________________________________________ JUDGMENT (Delivered on 29.09.2018.) 1] Accused Arun Raju Vaidya, is facing charge for the offence punishable u/s. 354, 323, 504 of I.P.C. and sec. 3 punishable u/s. 4 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 2 POCSO Case. No. 239/2014. The prosecution case in nut­shell is as follows : 2] That the informant victim was 14 years of age at the time of incident. Since her birth, she was residing at Ambedkar Nagar chawl, Hanuman Nagar Road, Thane (W). The accused was residing in the vicinity of the informant near Datta temple and she was knowing him. 3] On 27.04.14 at about 17.30 hours, the informant went along with her neighbourer by name Pal Bhabi for answering nature's call of defecation, nearby hill. At that time, accused was standing there. The neighbourer Pal said the accused that they had came there for answering nature's call, therefore, accused should leave the spot. However, accused did not leave the spot. Therefore, the informant said that “rqedks ek] cgu ugh gS D;k \ rqe ;gkls pys tko”. On that, the accused got angry and he abused her as “eknjpksn lkyh] jaMh] rq>s vkSj rqEgkjh ekWa dks iksyqaxk”. Thereafter, he scratched her neck by nail, held right hand of the informant and held the waist of informant by other hand, pulled her near him and thereby, outraged her modesty. At that time, the informant shouted, hence, the accused ran away. On returning home, the informant narrated the incident to her parents and subsequently, she lodged F.I.R. against him. A.P.I. Sopan Ravji Borade conducted investigation of the matter and thereafter, due to his transfer, P.S.I. Mr. K.Y. Sawant submitted charge­sheet against the accused for the offence punishable u/s. 354, 323, 504 of I.P.C. and section 4 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 4] My learned predecessor framed charge against the accused for the offence punishable u/s. 354, 323, 504 of I.P.C. and under sec. 3 punishable u/s. 4 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, vide Exh. 12. The contents of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular, to which the accused pleaded not guilty and 3 POCSO Case. No. 239/2014. claimed for trial. 5] In order to prove the allegations against the accused, the prosecution examined in all three witnesses, i.e. complainant victim as P.W.1 at Exh. 14, Mr. Raju Dnyaneshwar Yadav, panch of spot panchanama as P.W.2 at Exh. 16, and Mr. Sopan Ravji Borade, investigating officer as P.W.3 at Exh. 22. Thereafter, vide pursis Exh. 25, the prosecution closed the evidence. 6] The prosecution has also relied upon the following documents­ 1] F.I.R. at Exh. 15, 2] Spot panchanama at Exh.17 3] School­leaving certificate at Exh.23, 4] Arrest panchanama at Exh. 24, 7] Statement of accused u/s. 313 of Cr.P.C. came to be recorded to the extent of only incriminating material against him. The defence of the accused is of total denial and false implication. 8] Heard learned P.P. Smt. Phad for the State and learned counsel Shri. Mahendra Gaikwad, for the accused. 9] Following points emerged for my consideration and I have recorded my findings thereon for the reasons given below. Points Findings 1] Whether the prosecution has proved No. that on 27.04.14, at about 17.00 hours, on a hill near Ambedkar chawl, at Hanumannagar, Wagle Estate, Thane, the accused caught hold the hand and waist of victim and thereby, committed 4 POCSO Case. No. 239/2014. sexual assault on the complainant minor girl ? 2] Whether the prosecution has proved No. that on the above date, time and place, the accused had abused the complainant victim girl, thereby, intentionally insulted her ? 3] What order ? As per final order. REASONS 10] Ld. P.P. Smt. Phad submitted that in the present case, the informant has deposed categorically as per the contents of F.I.R. She has duly proved the occurrence of alleged incident. Therefore, though the prosecution could not examine other eye­witness i.e. Smt. Pal, sole version of the informant cannot be disbelieved and the accused is required to be held guilty for offence punishable u/s. 354, 323 and 504 of I.P.C. along with section 3, 4 of POCSO Act. 11] On the other hand, Ld. Counsel Shri. Mahendra Gaikwad for accused submitted that prosecution examined three witnesses, P.W.1 is alleged victim, P.W.2 is alleged panch of spot panchanama and P.W.3 is investigating officer. As per the version in the F.I.R., the informant is resident of same locality and knows the accused even before the incident. She does not know full name of accused, but knows his age. This is surprising. So also, she went along with one Pal­Bhabhi. However, she does not know full name of said lady. When accused did not leave the spot, she quarreled with him. Even the investigating officer has admitted that there are frequent quarrels amongst the members of the society on account of dumping, garbage, playing cricket and using the area for 5 POCSO Case. No. 239/2014. answering natural call of defecation. There is a temple of God Murgan in the area of the community of the accused and the society of the informant used to put dirt around it and that is the reason for frequent quarrels and due to said quarrels, the accused has falsely implicated. 12] He further submitted that as per version of informant, the accused had scratched on the neck of the informant by nail, pulled her by waist. The informant was sent for medical examination. However, the same is not reflecting in the F.I.R. Even the medical report or memorandum of medical examination has not produced on record. The I.O. does not know about medical examination. The entire prosecution case is based on the sole version of the informant and though an eye­ witness was available, no efforts were made to examine her. The informant has also deposed that she does not know Marathi. She did not read the F.I.R. 13] Further, the investigating officer has also admitted that informant and accused are from different communities. Though it has come on record that boys used to play cricket in that area and as the alleged time of the incident is just 5.30 p.m., it was not dark. However, the prosecution has not named any other person than Smt. Pal, as the witness. If really, the informant had shouted, then certainly some people would have gathered there. There is no document on record to show the age of the informant. The witness has admitted that she was going to school and the school timing was 1.00 a.m. to 6.00 p.m. 14] Considering the entire material on record as well as the contradictions in the F.I.R. and oral evidence of informant, it is clear that the informant has falsely implicated the accused. In the F.I.R., it is mentioned that the accused caught the informant by waist and pulled her 6 POCSO Case. No. 239/2014. near him, while in her oral evidence, it has deposed that accused touched the informant by chest and waist. This portion of touching chest has not mentioned in the F.I.R. It shows that the informant wants to implicate the accused by hook or crook and therefore, she has improved her version. 15] He further submitted that the applicant is a young boy of 24 years. He is sole bread­winner of family and working as scavenger. There is no corroboration to the version of the informant though the witness was allegedly available. That there is improvement in the oral version. There is no medical paper on record though allegedly the informant had gone to the doctor as per directions of police. So also, there is nothing on record to attract section 3 or 4 of the POCSO Act. It is necessary to acquit the accused by holding that the prosecution has failed to prove guilt of the accused. 16] In the light of above submissions, it is necessary to scrutinize the material on record. 17] It has come in the evidence of P.W.1 the informant and victim that her date of birth is 03.02.2000. On 27.04.14 at about 5.00 p.m., she went along with Smt. Pal. She went for answering natural call of defecation towards hill. At that time, the accused was there. Smt. Pal asked him to leave the place. However, he declined and said that they should go to other side. The informant said that “Tumhare Ghar Pe Ma Bahan Nahi Hai Kya ?” On that, the accused abused her in filthy language. Accused came to her, pressed her neck, caused abrasion by his nail to her neck. He also touched her chest and waist. She shouted. Then, he left the place. Thereafter, the informant along with Smt. Pal returned to house. She narrated the incident to her father. She went to police station with her father and gave report. She proved the F.I.R. at Exh. 15. Police referred 7 POCSO Case. No. 239/2014. her to hospital. She had shown the police the spot of incident and handed over police photo­copy of her school­leaving certificate. She identified the accused before the court. 18] During the cross­examination, she deposed that she is acquainted with the jungle and hill adjoining her vicinity. Boys used to go in the jungle for playing cricket. However, she denied that at about 4.00 to 6.00 p.m., boys go there for playing cricket. That at about 5.00 p.m., it was not dark. Prior to the incident, there was no quarrel of the informant with the accused. Accused belongs to sweeper family. His parents are sweepers. She denied that on 27.04.14, there was quarrel between accused and Smt. Pal on the hill. After the F.I.R., she was referred to hospital. Further, she denied the suggestions about non­occurrence of any such incident as mentioned in the F.I.R. 19] P.W.2 Raju Dnyaneshwar Yadav, alleged spot panch, deposed that on 27.04.14, he went along with police to the spot and police prepared spot panchanama in his presence. He proved said panchanama at Exh. 17. However, during cross­examination, he deposed that he does not know Marathi. He had not gone through the contents of panchanama and he put his signature as per say of police. 20] P.W.3 Sopan Ravji Borade, the I.O. deposed that in the year 2014, he was posted as P.S.I. with Shrinagar police station. Investigation of C.R. No. 102/14 was entrusted to him. He verified contents of F.I.R. from informant. On the same day, he prepared spot panchanama at Exh. 17. He recorded statement of witness Guddi Pal, Kailasi Gupta, Anita Gupta, Ramashish Gupta. He obtained photo­copy of school­leaving certificate of the informant at Exh. 23, arrested the accused and completed the investigation. After his transfer, P.S.I., A.Y. Sawant submitted charge­ 8 POCSO Case. No. 239/2014. sheet. 21] During cross­examination, he admitted that accused and informant are from different communities. He admitted that there is temple of Lord Murgan near the spot. So also that boys used to play cricket on the spot of incident. He also admitted that residents of the spot always used to quarrel on account of littering on the spot and on account of playing cricket and for answering natural calls on the spot. He did not receive any document to show that the informant was referred to doctor. Neither the informant nor her parents produced any document about her treatment. He admitted that there is no independent eye­witness to the incident. He also admitted that he did not receive any additional document to show sexual assault on the victim. 22] Before assessing the evidence of prosecution, it is necessary to mention that there are no allegations of any penetrative sexual assault in the matter and therefore, sections 3 or 4 of the POCSO Act may not be applicable to the present case. However, there are allegations of commission of offence as per section 7 of the POCSO Act. However, considering that section 7 can be treated as minor act of section 3, therefore, the charge has not altered considering the stage of the matter, as the evidence is already over and the matter has listed for arguments. 23] As per the prosecution case, the informant has gone along with one Smt. Pal, however, she has not mentioned full name of said lady. She has deposed about Smt. Pal asking the accused to go away and further quarrel with the accused. She had also deposed that the informant said to the accused “Tumhare Gharme Ma Bahen Nahi Hai Kya ?”. On that, the accused choked her throat, she got abrasion to her neck, so also, the accused touched her chest and waist. However, in the F.I.R., it is 9 POCSO Case. No. 239/2014. mentioned that the accused had pulled her by waist and there is no reference of touching the chest. Touching chest of lady is a serious offending act. However, the same is not mentioned in the F.I.R. Not only this, but the informant has narrated that she was sent to the hospital by police along with report. But, neither the medical report nor the police medical memo has produced on record. The I.O. could not explain this. Rather, the I.O. has deposed that, he did not receive any document showing that the informant was referred to medical examination. The I.O. has further admitted that he did not find any additional material about sexual assault on the informant. The above aspect clearly gives rise to suspicion about the version of informant, as she is improving her version about the alleged act committed by the accused. So also, she has improved her version about sending her to the hospital for medical examination. 24] Another aspect of the matter is the other witness Smt. Pal was allegedly present along with the informant. However, he informant was not knowing her full name. The prosecution did not take any efforts to examine her by tracing her. Moreover, as per the version of investigating officer himself, the spot is near the temple of Lord Murgan. Even in spot panchanama, it is mentioned that the distance between the spot of incident and the temple is just 100 fts. It has also come on record that boys used to play cricket on the spot nearby the Murgan temple. The time of alleged incident was of 5.00 p.m. The informant herself has admitted that it was not dark. In such situation, when the boys used to play cricket at a distance of 100 fts. From the spot, firstly, there is possibility of having so many witnesses near the spot of incident. Moreover, if the informant would really had shouted, then some of the nearby persons must have gathered near the spot. However, the informant is not deposing about the same. 10 POCSO Case. No. 239/2014. 25] The informant has also admitted that boys used to play cricket nearby the temple. Therefore, certainly there must be so many boys nearby the spot. In such circumstances, it is firstly hard to believe that two ladies had gone to answer natural call at 5.00 p.m., nearby said temple and secondly, none of the witnesses except Smt. Pal had seen the incident. Considering these aspects coupled with the contradictions and improvements in the evidence of the informant, in my view, there is a doubt about the version of prosecution. The prosecution could have examined other independent witnesses of whose statements were recorded u/s. 161 of Cr.P.C. 26] The investigating officer has also admitted that the accused is from family of scavengers and usually, quarrel used to take place between two communities on account of littering nearby the temple. Therefore, there is possibility that some quarrel might had taken place between the informant and the accused. However, where the actual incident of she going to answer natural call near the temple and the further allegations about outraging her modesty had ever taken place or not, is doubtful. Certainly, if the incident would have taken place, then the boys playing nearby and other visitors of the temple would have become witnesses to the incident. However, the investigating officer has admitted that he could not get any independent witness. It is not the case of prosecution that the witnesses were available, they refused to give evidence. Hence, considering above situation, in my view, the prosecution has failed to prove occurrence of the alleged incident beyond reasonable doubt. 27] No doubt, there is presumption of culpable mental state of the accused. However, for the same, it is initially necessary that at­least the occurrence of alleged facts must be proved, then only there would be 11 POCSO Case. No. 239/2014. presumption of culpable mental state. However, in the present case, the occurrence of alleged incident itself is doubtful. Therefore, the presumption u/s. 30 of the POCSO Act cannot be invoked against the accused. Hence, after considering the entire evidence on record, it is necessary to hold that the prosecution has failed to prove the occurrence of alleged incident itself and therefore, to prove that the accused has committed any offence as alleged. Hence, he is required to be acquitted from the charges. 28] The prosecution has even failed to prove that the accused had committed any other or minor offence, of which charge has came to be framed against him. Consequentially, he is required to be acquitted from the charges. Hence, point No. 1 is answered in the negative. So far as muddemal property is concerned, the charge­sheet does not reveal any muddemal articles. Hence, no order for disposal of the same is warranted. 29] As the accused held not guilty and point No. 1 is answered in the negative, in answer to point No. 2, I pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused Arun Raju Vaidya, is hereby, acquitted under sec. 235(1) of the Criminal Procedure Code, from the offence punishable u/s. 354, 323, 504 of I.P.C. and sec. 3 punishable u/s. 4 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 2] His bail bond stands cancelled and sureties are discharged. 12 POCSO Case. No. 239/2014. 3] Accused is hereby directed to furnish bail bond of Rs.15,000/­ with a surety of like amount, so as to appear before the higher Court in compliance with Sec. 437­A of Code of Criminal Procedure. 4] Pronounced in open court. Thane, (V.Y. Jadhav) Date­ 29.09.2018. Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.
