No.236/2016 (Exh.No. 24) 2] In brief, it is the case of prosecution that informant Soniparvin Mustkin Shaikh lodged the complaint on 16.2.2016 alleging that victim girl aged about 9 years is her daughter. On 15.2.2016 at about 10.00 p.m. when she was present in her house, one Salam Islam Ansari residing in the vicinity, came running to her house and told that grocery shop owner Mohammad Nasim outraged modesty of her daughter in his shop, some people caught hold him and were assaulting him. Immediately she and her husband went to said shop and saw that Nasim was caught hold by people and her daughter was made to sit there by the people. When she enquired with her daughter/victim, she told by crying that shop owner on saying that he will give chocolate to her, took her inside the shop, moved his hand on her chest and outraged her modesty. Thereafter with the help of people she brought Mohammad Nasim Abbulais Shaikh to police station and lodged the complaint. 3] On the basis of complaint, Crime No.I­24/2016 for the offence punishable u/s 354(A) of I.P.C. r/w S. 7 & 8 of POCSO Act was registered and PSI Smt. Virnak carried out investigation. During investigation, she prepared spot panchanama in presence of panchas which was shown by informant. She recorded statement of victim in question and answer form. She wrote letter to Court for recording statement of victim u/s 164 of Cr.P.C. which was recorded by Court. On the same day she arrested accused under arrest panchanama. She collected birth certificate of victim and recorded statements of witnesses. Due to her transferred P.I. Bedare, on completion of investigation, submitted chargesheet before the Court against accused. ..3/- ..3.. Spl.C. No.236/2016 (Exh.No. 24) 4] Charge Exh.4 was framed & explained to accused to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. His defence is that of total denial. 5] Considering the case of the prosecution following points arise for my determination and I have recorded my findings thereon for the reasons discussed below. POINTS FINDINGS 1 Does the prosecution prove that on 15.2.2016 at bout 22.00 hours at MHADA Colony, Solapuri Chawl, Bhiwandi, accused used criminal force to victim aged 9 years with intent to outrage her modesty and thereby committed an offence punishable u/sec. 354(A) of I.P.C.? No. 2 Does the prosecution further prove that on the above mentioned date,time and place accused wrongfully confined victim in the shop and thereby committed an offence u/s 342 of IPC? No. 3 Does the prosecution further prove that on the above mentioned date,time and place accused committed sexual assault on victim punishable u/s 7 and thereby committed an offence u/s 8 of PCSO Act? No. 4 What order ? As per final order. REASONS Points Nos. 1 to 3 : 6] All the points are interlinked to each other, hence in order to avoid the repetition of evidence they are clubbed together. ..4/- ..4.. Spl.C. No.236/2016 (Exh.No. 24) 7] Prosecution examined in all 5 witnesses. P.W.1 Victim at Exh.7, PW 2 informant Soniparvin at Exh.8, PW 3 Amina­panch at Exh.12, PW 4 Salam at Exh.15 and PW 5 Smt. Virnak, I.O. at Exh.16. Then prosecution filed evidence closing pursis at Exh.22. Statement of accused recorded u/s 313 of Cr.P. C. is at Exh.23. Prosecution relied on documents viz. report Exh.9, FIR Exh.10, panchanama Exh.13, statement of victim Exh.17, letter Exh.18, statement of victim u/s 164 of Cr.P.C. Exh.19, arrest panchanama Exh.20 and birth certificate Exh.21. 8] The Ld. APP submitted that the incident took place on 15.2.2016 at the shop of accused and there is no delay in lodging FIR. When victim went to the shop of accused at about 10.00 p.m., accused called her inside the shop on the pretext of offering chocolate. Then he closed the shutter and by removing clothes, he moved his hand on her chest with sexual intent. That time she was crying which was heard by, PW 4 from outside the said shop. Then he entered in the shop and rescued the victim, otherwise, possibility could not be ruled out of committing further more serious offence. Thereafter, people gathered there and one of them informed to mother of victim who rushed on the spot alongwith her husband and then went to police station and lodged complaint. Investigating officer prepared spot panchanama which is proved by PW 3 and the birth certificate of victim clearly shows that she was aged about 9 years at the time of incident. The evidence of prosecution witnesses not shattered on any count inspite of detailed cross examination. The defence putforth that on account of demand of credit amount of grocery articles, informant lodged false complaint against accused is at all not just and proper for want of details about credit amount, period of credit amount and mode of demand. ..5/- ..5.. Spl.C. No.236/2016 (Exh.No. 24) 9] Per contra, the Ld. Counsel for accused vehemently submitted that there is delay of 3 hours in lodging complaint and that time spent by informant for making conspiracy against accused in order to entangle him in the crime. The evidence of victim and independent witness PW 4 is not corroborated to each other. PW 4 is not resident of the same vicinity and as such, he is a chance witness. The evidence that victim was wrapped with clothes is the improvement in the statement of PW 4. I.O. failed to seize said frock which was allegedly removed by accused. PW 3 is the regular panch of police and she admitted that she has signed panchanama at police station. Victim is tutored, however, she admitted that there is arrears of bill of grocery articles. On the contrary, informant denied that she took grocery on credit and accused used to demand the same due to which, she got angry and lodged false complaint against accused. He further submitted that when there is contradiction in the version of victim and informant, spot panchanama not proved by prosecution, the testimony of witness is a chance witness and in order to take revenge, false complaint came to be filed against accused then prosecution failed to prove the charges beyond reasonable doubt and hence, accused is entitled for benefit of doubt. 10] The Ld. Defence counsel relied on the citation State Vs. Mafizuddin, reported in AIR 1983 Supreme Court, 274, in which, it is held that child witness the only eyewitness of the occurrence was found tutored throughout, then it is unsafe to rely on the testimony of child witness. This ratio is not applicable to the present case as victim is the affected by the alleged incident. He further relied on citation Munna Vs. State, reported in 1985 Cri.L.J., 1925, in which, it is held that child witness­Unsafe to base conviction on uncorroborated evidence of child witness. In this ..6/- ..6.. Spl.C. No.236/2016 (Exh.No. 24) case, when the alleged incident took place in the shop of accused and that too by closing shutter in night hours, therefore, it is not necessary to corroborate the testimony of victim and as such, the ratio is not applicable to the present case. Lastly he relied on citation Sukhram Vs. State, reported in 1995 Cri. L.J., 595 in which, it is held that evidence of child of tender age tainted with infirmities of description on point of proper identification. Evidence also showing that child was tutored. The facts in the citation case and the present case are altogether different. Therefore, ratio is not applicable to the present case. 11] Victim's birth certificate Exh.21 discloses her date of birth as 24.11.2005. On the of alleged incident she was minor. PW 1/victim girl deposed that there is bathroom outside her house. However, she admitted in her cross examination that inside the house, there is a bathroom and public toilet is out of house. I.O. admitted in her cross examination that behind the shop near public latrine there is a house of informant. In between shop of accused and public latrine there are residential houses. It is mentioned in the statement of victim Exh.17 that when she was returning from bathroom to house, there was a shop of accused and he called her on the pretext of offering chocolate and then the incident took place. As per the statement of victim Exh.17, at about 10.00 p.m. she went to bathroom and while returning from the same, accused gave call for chocolate. However, in the evidence, victim deposed that she went out of house of urination. That time her mother asked her to bring biscuits and as all the shops were closed therefore, she went to shop of accused. Thus, there is material contradiction on the point of entry in the shop of accused of victim. When there is a bathroom in the house of ..7/- ..7.. Spl.C. No.236/2016 (Exh.No. 24) victim, then there was no necessity to go outside for urination and that too in the night hours. Secondly, the cause of visiting to the shop of accused also goes to root of case as the victim deposed that her mother asked her to purchase biscuits and that too at late hours. The evidence of informant mother also not putforth any explanation about purchasing of biscuits at late hours. As matter of fact, in the report Exh.9 and in the evidence of informant PW 2 there is nothing mention about asking victim to purchase biscuits. Thus, the very cause of the inception of crime is doubtful. 12] Victim further deposed that when she went to shop of accused, he asked her to take chocolate, called her inside and he moved his hand on her breast. In her evidence, there is nothing mentioned that when she entered the shop of accused, that time, anybody was present outside the shop. Even, on going through her statement Exh.17, there is nothing mentioned that somebody was present outside the shop. However, in the statement recorded u/s 164 of Cr.P.C. at Exh.19, she stated that 3­4 boys were chitchatting there. Under such circumstances, it is necessary to advent on the evidence of PW 4 Salam who deposed that on 15.2.2016 at about 9.30 p.m. to 10.00 p.m. he was sitting outside the shop of accused and seeing picture on mobile. That time, his friends were present. Shutter of shop was closed and they heard the sound of weeping of girl, which clearly shows that the boys referred by the victim in her statement Exh.19 are not the boys including PW 4, otherwise, PW 4 could depose that he saw victim going to the shop of accused. 13] Thus, on the point of presence of PW 4 at the relevant time, is also under the suspicion as victim herself deposed that she went to ..8/- ..8.. Spl.C. No.236/2016 (Exh.No. 24) the shop of accused at 10.00 p.m. but according to PW 4 he was present there at about 9.30 p.m. to 10.00 p.m. but he failed to notice presence of victim and closing of shutter by accused. On the contrary, he stated that shutter of shop was closed. Therefore, the submission on behalf of accused that PW 4 is a chance witness needs consideration. 14] Victim further deposed that she started crying and shouting. People opened the shutter from outside. Accused pushed her in one corner. People asked him as to where was girl. When people were returning, she shouted loudly. PW 4 deposed that shutter of shop was closed and they heard sound of weeping of girl. Shutter of that shop was opened upto 4” from bottom, they saw from where the sound of weeping was coming. That time, lights inside the shop were on. They peeped into the shop and saw that accused was not having clothes on his person. Thus, apparently, the testimony of PW 4 corroborated to the testimony of victim to some extent, however, on going through the statement of victim at Exh.17, she stated that by her legs she hammered the shutter, then the boys who were chitchatting outside opened the shutter. She also stated the same fact in her statement Exh.19. This clearly shows that the evidence of victim and PW 4 though corroborated to each other on the point of hearing of cry, but it is not corroborated to the previous statement of victim as per Exhs. 17 & 19 on the point of hammering of shutter by her legs, which clearly brought the contradiction in the evidence of victim as well as PW 4 and that is sufficient to raise doubt on the testimony of victim as well as PW 4. 15] Victim did not depose that accused removed her clothes from her person and when she was rescued from the hand of accused, there were no clothes on her person. However, PW 4 Salam deposed ..9/- ..9.. Spl.C. No.236/2016 (Exh.No. 24) that victim has no clothes on her person, then some people put clothes on her person and took her to her mother. It is to be noted that removal of clothes is the material fact and that has to be stated by the victim in the evidence which she stated in her statement Exhs.17 & 19. Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW 4 that at the relevant time there were no clothes on the person of victim and that she was wrapped with clothes by the people is not corroborated by the evidence of victim. When as per complaint Exh.9 people caught hold accused and took him to police station and spot panchanama was prepared thereafter, then it was expected from I.O. to seize the clothes of victim from the spot but there is no such evidence brought by I.O. On the other hand, she admitted that frock of victim was not seized from the spot. Thus, on the point of removal of clothes, the case of prosecution is also under the shadow of doubt. 16] PW 3 Amina deposed that on 16.2.2016 she was called by police of Nizampu Police Station to act as panch. Thereafter, they alongwith police went to the shop of accused. That shop is at Nadinaka, Zopadpatti, Bhiwandi. It is a grocery shop. In their presence police prepared panchanama Exh.13 in the shop. That time informant was also present there. In the cross examination she admitted that she runs Mahila Mandal at Nadinaka area. She further admitted that she used to visit Nizampur Police Station in respect of the complaints received by Mahila Mandal. Therefore, police used to call her for work. On that day police made call to her and she signed on the panchanama in the police station. On perusal of panchanama Exh.13, it reveals that it was prepared at shop of accused. Thus, the evidence of PW 3 Amina is not corroborated to the contents mentioned in the panchanama Exh.13 and ..10/- ..10.. Spl.C. No.236/2016 (Exh.No. 24) that also creates a doubt on the preparation of panchanama at the spot. 17] It is to be noted that while assessing the evidence of child, it is necessary to go through the minor details as the child is to be tutored on the major facts but not on minor or vice­a­versa. In the complaint, it is mentioned that at the relevant time, victim went to the shop of accused however no cause mentioned in it. Surprisingly enough victim and complainant deposed that for purchasing biscuit she went to the shop but in the statement of victim at Exhs. 17 & 19 there is nothing mentioned of the same. This clearly shows that before entering into the witness box victim and informant had discussed this point and deposed the same which did not find place in FIR Exh.9 and statement Exhs. 17 & 19. Thus, on this count, victim is tutored. 18] The evidence of victim is totally silent on the point of removal of her frock. As a matter of fact, when it is the case of prosecution that her frock was removed by accused, then it was utmost necessary to depose by victim but she failed to state so. I.O. also failed to state about the said frock. Therefore, it seems that victim is tutored on the main point that accused moved his hand on her breast, otherwise, she ought to have deposed about removal of frock before moving hand on her breast. Therefore, the evidence of victim seems to be focused on the point of main incident of moving hand by accused on her chest. Thus, the submission of defence counsel that victim is tutored on the main point and as such on the minor point there is no corroboration/omission is acceptable and as such, I am inclined to discard the testimony of victim. When the testimony of victim is discarded, then the presumption which is in favour of prosecution u/s 29 of the POCSO Act ..11/- ..11.. Spl.C. No.236/2016 (Exh.No. 24) is rebutted by accused. 19] The Ld. Counsel for accused vehemently submitted that in the report Exh 9 the word 'obscene' is inserted subsequently which was not stated by informant and that has to be done by I.O. only to get the seriousness to the case of prosecution. This argument is at all not palatable as the obscene can be seen from the fact narrated in the complaint or the facts disclosed by the victim or the act done by accused. Therefore, insertion of word 'obscene' is not so material which change the entire case of prosecution. 20] PW 4 Salam deposed that on 15.2.2016 at about 9.30 p.m. to 10.00 p.m. he was sitting outside the shop of accused and seeing picture on mobile. That time his friends Jaeed & Shahrukh were with him. That time shutter of shop was closed and they heard sound of weeping of girl. Shutter of that shop was opened upto 4” from bottom. they saw from where that sound of weeping was coming. There were no clothes on the person of victim and accused. However, in the evidence of I.O., she admitted that Salam did not state the above facts to her. Thus, these improvements go to the root of case and as such, it also creates a doubt on the testimony of PW 4 Salam. 21] So far as the defence is concerned, according to accused, he is running grocery shop and informant is his customer and he used to sell grocery articles on credit. Victim admitted the fact of purchase of articles on credit, however, informant denied the same. The Ld. APP vehemently submitted that if a person sold articles on credit, then but natural he used to maintain the record of it and most probably that record is to be kept in the shop and customer also maintains the said ..12/- ..12.. Spl.C. No.236/2016 (Exh.No. 24) record. The defence is so vague that no where put about the details of articles sold on credit such as the date of transaction, details of articles, cost of the same and any amount paid or entirely on credit. Even in the statement u/s 313 of Cr.P.C., accused failed to give above details. For want of details, the defence putforth by accused seems to be improbable and failed to pass the test of preponderance of probability that on the count of demand of credit amount, informant made wild allegations against accused and that too on the count of outraging modesty of her minor daughter. At the same time in view of the above discussion, the entire case of prosecution is also under the shadow of doubt. Therefore, it is just and proper to extend benefit to accused as prosecution and defence came with untrue facts and both versions have to be discarded. 22] The evidence on record is not sufficient to prove the charge levelled against accused beyond reasonable doubt for offence punishable u/s 354(A) & 342 of IPC and the offence punishable u/s 8 of POCSO Act. With this discussion, I answer the point Nos. 1 to 3 accordingly and to proceed to pass the following order. : ORDER : 1] Accused Mohammad Nasim Abbulais Shaikh is hereby acquitted u/s 235 of Cr.P.C. from the charge of offence punishable u/s 354(A) & 342 of I.P.C & u/s 8 of POCSO Act. 2] Bail bonds of accused shall stand cancelled. 3] Accused shall comply forthwith the provision U/Sec.437­A Cr.P.C. by furnishing fresh P.R. Bond of Rs.10,000/­ and S.B. of like amount. Dictated and declared in open Court. Place : Thane (R.N.Bawankar) Date : 7.11.2017 Special Judge (POCSO Act), Thane ..13/- ..13.. Spl.C. 1 Special Case (Pocso) No. 222/2015 Judgment Received on :­ 03.10.2015 Registered on :­ 03.10.2015 Decided on :­ 20.07.2017 Duration :­ 1Y 9M 17D IN THE COURT OF ADDITIONAL SESSIONS JUDGE, & SPECIAL JUDGE (POCSO) ACT, THANE AT : THANE ( Presided over by Ashutosh N.Karmarkar, District Judge­1 & Special Judge (POCSO) Act, Thane ) Special Case (POCSO) No.222/2015 Exh. No. State of Maharashtra ( Through Bhiwandi City Police Station ) …Complainant V/s. Vijay Manik Ghadge Age : 23 Years, R/at.: House No. 878, Bhayyasaheb Ambedkar Nagar, Patel Compound, Dhamankar Naka, Bhiwandi, Dist. Thane … Accused. Offence punishable under Sec. 354, 354­D, 504 of Indian Penal Code and under Sec. 11(iv), 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2 Special Case (Pocso) No. 222/2015 Judgment Appearances : Smt. S.E.Phad, P.P. for the State Shri. Sonavane, Advocate for accused JUDGMENT ( Delivered on this 20th day of July, 2017 ) 1] Accused is facing trial for the offence punishable under Sec. 354, 354­D of Indian Penal Code and under Sec. 11(iv), 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] Prosecution Case, in brief, is as under : Informant/victim is residing with her grandmother and brother and mother's sister. Accused is residing in the vicinity of the informant. She knows him. The accused was frequently following her on motorcycle. On 24.04.2015 at 8.30 p.m., she had been to vegetable market. She came in front of Pathare compound. Accused came from backside on motorcycle. He caught hold her hand and started behaving indecently. She tried to resist. He started abusing. Her brother's friend came. On seeing him, accused left the spot. She narrated the incident to her mother's sister and then lodged report. 3] On the basis of report, crime was registered vide C.R.No. I­132/2015. P.S.I. Pawar has investigated this crime. He drew spot panchanama and has recorded statements of witnesses. After completion of investigation, he filed charge­sheet in the Court of Law. 3 Special Case (Pocso) No. 222/2015 Judgment 4] I have framed charge against accused below Exh. 6 to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 5] Prosecution has examined four witnesses. Then, the statement of the accused under Sec. 313 of Cr.P.C. came to be recorded. Total denial is the defence of the accused. The accused has raised defence that there was love affair between victim and P.W.Sagar which is noticed by accused. He stated victim that he will say about it to her family members and so, he is falsely implicated. 6] I have heard both the sides. 7] Following points arose for my determination and I gave my findings thereon for the reasons stated below: Sr. POINTS FINDINGS No. 1. Does the prosecution prove that the No accused on 24.04.2015, at about 20.45 hrs., at Pathare Compound, on public road from Padmanagar Vegetable Market to Varhaldevi lake, Bhiwandi assaulted or used criminal force to a informant i.e. minor victim girl age 13 years intending to outrage or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby outrage her modesty and thereby committed an offence punishable under S. 354 of Indian Penal Code? 4 Special Case (Pocso) No. 222/2015 Judgment 2. Does the prosecution prove that on No. above mentioned date, time and place, accused followed the informant i.e. minor victim girl and contacts, or attempts to contact her to foster personal interaction repeatedly despite a clear indication of disinterest by her and thereby committed an offence punishable under Sec. 354­D of Indian Penal Code? 3. Does the prosecution prove that on No. aforesaid date, time and place, accused intentionally insulted the informant i.e. victim, her mother, maternal aunt and brother by abusing them in filthy language and thereby gave provocation to them knowing that it will break public peace and thereby committed an offence punishable under Sec. 504 of Indian Penal Code? 4. Does the prosecution prove that on No. aforesaid date, time and place, accused committed sexual harassment upon a minor victim girl, age 13 years by repeatedly or constantly contacting her by following her on motorcycle with sexual intent and thereby committed an offence punishable under Sec. 11(iv) of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012? 5. Does the prosecution prove that on No. aforesaid date, time and place, accused committed sexual harassment upon a minor girl, age 13 years with sexual intent and thereby committed an offence punishable under Sec. 12 of 5 Special Case (Pocso) No. 222/2015 Judgment The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012? 6. What order? As per final order. REASONS AS TO POINT NO.1 TO 5 :­ 8] It is well settled that in order to prove the guilt of accused, it is incumbent on the part of the prosecution to adduce cogent, convincing and reliable evidence. It is well settled that the sole testimony of witness is also sufficient to base the conviction. But, the rule is that it should be above suspicion and should inspire confidence in the mind of court . 9] The prosecution has examined victim P.W.1 (Exh.11), her mother Surekha P.W.2 (Exh.15), investigation officer P.S.I. Pawar,P.W.3 (Exh.17) and P.W.4 Mr. Sagar (Exh.20). 10] Informant / victim has stated that she is residing with her mother's sister and brother. She knows accused. He used to follow her. It is further stated by victim that on 24.04.2015, at 8.30 p.m., she had been to vegetable market and was returning to home. Accused followed her on motorcycle and caught hold her hand and started behaving in indecent manner. At the same time, her brother's friend came. On seeing him accused left the victim free. Accused started abusing her brother's friend named Sagar. Then, she lodged report to police Exh. 12. This is in all testimony of the 6 Special Case (Pocso) No. 222/2015 Judgment victim. Leaving Certificate of the victim is admitted by the accused. He had no objection for exhibiting the said certificate. It appears from the said certificate that the age of the victim on the day of incident was about 16 years. 11] P.W. 4 Sagar has stated that on 24.04.2015, at 8.30 p.m., he was proceeding on motorcycle by the road adjoining to Pathare Compound. According to him, victim and the accused were present there and there was some quarrel between them. So, he went there. Then, accused left the spot on motorcycle. So, it appears that there is total variance in the evidence of victim and P.W.4 Sagar. Evidence of victim shows that P.W.4 Sagar has witnessed the fact of catching hold of her hand by the accused. However, the evidence of P.W.4 Sagar does not show that he has seen the accused holding the hand of victim. He has just stated that the quarrel between victim and the accused was going on for two to three minutes. No details of such quarrel are given by P.W.4 Sagar. According to the victim, the accused has behaved indecently. But, P.W. 4 Sagar has not stated this fact. Even if the version of the victim is accepted for a moment that the accused behaved indecently, that will not be sufficient to hold the accused guilty for the offence under Sec. 354 of Indian Penal Code in absence of specific details of it. 7 Special Case (Pocso) No. 222/2015 Judgment 12] P.W.2 Surekha, the mother of victim has just stated that she was informed by her sister about the incident. She was also informed that on 24.4.2015, when victim was returning from vegetable market, one boy caught hold her hand. This witness does not say that she was also informed about the alleged indecent behaviour of the accused. P.S.I. Pawar has admitted that witness Sagar has not stated in his statement that accused was holding hand of the victim. Investigation officer Mr. Pawar also could not get independent and impartial witness. Cross­examination of the victim reveal that the vegetable market is at a distance of ½ km. from his house and the road which go towards vegetable market always remain busy. So, there was possibility of having independent witness. But, there is no any evidence to support the contention of the victim. Ld. Advocate for the accused has also submitted about totally different story in the statement of victim under Sec. 164 Cr.P.C. Considering the variance in the evidence of victim and P.W.4 Sagar on material aspect, it would be unsafe to hold accused guilty for the offence under Sec. 354 of Indian Penal Code. 13] Informant has just stated in oral evidence that the accused used to follow her. She does not remember the dates of such incidents. No details are given by the victim about alleged incident of following her by accused. In order to establish the guilt under Sec. 354­D of Indian Penal code, prosecution has to establish that the accused has followed the victim repeatedly despite clear 8 Special Case (Pocso) No. 222/2015 Judgment indication of disinterest by victim. There is no satisfactory evidence on record to show the repeated attempts by the accused of following the victim. Victim has also not stated that she had already shown her disinterest in respect of such attempt of following her by the accused. Thus, the evidence on record is not upto the mark to prove the ingredients of Sec. 354­D and to hold accused guilty. 14] The victim has stated in her report (Exh.12) that on the day of incident, the accused abused her and her brother and mother's sister. Victim has stated in her oral evidence that on seeing arrival of P.W.4 Sagar, accused made said victim free and then, he abused P.W.4 Sagar. P.W.4 Sagar has not stated about abuses to him. The knowledge of P.W.4 Sagar about abuses by accused is based on information given by the victim. Even the details of specific abusive words are not stated by any of the witnesses. So, accused can not be held guilty under Sec.504 of Indian Penal Code. 15] In order to establish guilt of accused under Sec. 11(4) r/w. 12, prosecution has to establish that the accused has repeatedly and constantly followed the victim either directly or through electronic means and that too with sexual intent. It is already discussed in the foregoing paragraphs that the evidence on record is not sufficient to accept that the accused has repeatedly followed the victim directly. Even it is also discussed that the evidence of the victim on the point of incident dtd. 24.04.2015 of holding her hand is also not believable. That single incident even if 9 Special Case (Pocso) No. 222/2015 Judgment accepted as it is, it will not be sufficient to prove the guilt under Sec. 11(4) r/w. S. 12 of The Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 16] It is also discussed that the prosecution has not established that the accused behaved indecently. None of the ingredients of the offence for which accused is charged can be said to be proved for want of satisfactory evidence. For the reasons stated above, I answer point Nos.1 to 4 accordingly and pass the following order: ORDER 1] Accused Vijay Manik Ghadge is hereby acquitted under Sec. 235(1) of Code of Criminal Procedure of the offences punishable under Sec. 354, 354­D, 504 of Indian Penal Code and Sec.11(iv),12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] His bail bond stands cancelled. 3] Accused shall furnish P.B and S.B. of RS. 10,000/­ under Sec. 437­A of Code of Criminal Procedure. 4] Dictated and pronounced in open Court. Thane ( Ashutosh N. Karmarkar ) Date : 20.07.2017 District Judge­1 & Special Judge (POCSO) Act,Thane

--1-- ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN CRIMINAL BAIL APPLICAITON NO.2416/2017 The applicant Abhijeet Sitaram Vethekar has applied for bail under section 439of Cr. P.C. in C.R.No.I­349/2017 registered in Vashi police station for the offence under section 354, 354D, 509 of Indian Penal Code and Section 11(1)(4), 12 of POCSO Act. 2. It is contended that the investigation is almost completed. The offence is bailable. It is not punishable with death or imprisonment for life. The present applicant is ready to face the trial, therefore, he may be released on bail. 3. Investigating Officer has given his say at Exh.3. It is contended that the victim is 15 years old. There is prima facie case made out. The accused had caught hands of victim and asked kiss from her and thus he has sexually harassed her. If the accused is released on bail he is likely to tamper and repeat the offence. 4. I heard Ld. Counsel on behalf of the accused and Ld. APP. 5. .. 1 .. Bail No. 2485/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) Criminal Bail Application No.2485/2015. Bablu alias Hameed Haidar Pahan .. Applicant Vs. The State of Maharashtra Through Shantinagar P.S. .. Non­applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 By this application the applicant is seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C., who was arrested on 29.07.2015 by Shantinagar police station in connection with C.R.No. I­194/2015 registered for an offence punishable under section 376 read with section 34 and 120B of I.P. Code and section 3 read with 4 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and also under section 2 of Maharashtra Prevention and Eradication of Human Sacrifice and other Inhuman, Evil and Agori Practices and Black Magic Act, 2013. 2] Heard learned advocate Mr. Thanke for the applicant/accused and learned A.P.P. Mrs. R.A.Navale for State. I.O. present with case diary. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 29.07.2015 at the instance of the informant­victim girl with an indictment that her father told her that Baba Salim Ansari of Diwan Shah Dargah, Bhiwandi knows magic and he can have rainfall of money if he marry with unmarried girl having long hair and without any mole and constrained her to marry with said Salim Ansari. Thereafter .. 2 .. Bail No. 2485/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) Salim Ansari committed rape on the victim girl and other accused facilitated and were present during their marriage ceremony. 4] The learned Counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant­accused is falsely implicated. The only role assigned to him is that he was present during the marriage ceremony. Except that he has no role to play in the crime. All the allegations are against co­ accused Salim. He submitted that there is delay of 23 days in lodging the F.I.R. The fabricated story is put up implicating the accused therein. The accused is behind bars since two months. Accused is permanent resident of the address given in the application. He is not having any criminal antecedents. He is ready to abide by the conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing him on bail. 5] Per contra, the learned A.P.P. strongly opposed the application submitting that the offence is serious. She submitted that F.I.R. speaks in volume. All the accused are equally involved in this serious offence. The father of victim girl lured her to marry with Baba Salim Ansari with assurance that he know magic and after marrying there would have been rainfall of money. She submitted that all the accused were present during the marriage and their intention is very clear to facilitate the marriage of minor girl. She further submitted that bail application of co­accused Anand who is owner of flat, is already rejected by this Court. The investigation is in progress. There are chances of tampering of witnesses and prayed for rejection of application. .. 3 .. Bail No. 2485/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R, it prima facie appears that minor girl was lured by her father to marry with Baba Salim Ansari by assurance that there would be rainfall of money if she being unmarried, marry with him. Further, from F.I.R. itself it is clear that friends of Salim had facilitated the marriage and they were present during the marriage ceremony. All the accused are major, knowing very well that minor's marriage is prohibited. Further, there are allegations forming criminal conspiracy. It is well settled that conspiracy is to be judged on the basis of facts and circumstances of each case and there may not be any direct evidence in regard to conspiracy. Here the name of co­accused Arun is very well mentioned therein and involvement of other 3 to 4 persons is shown The investigation is still in progress. Further, there are serious charges of committing rape on minor girl. Though as per the submission of learned counsel for the applicant that allegations are against accused Salim, however, all the accused facilitated the marriage as well as facilitated to provide the room to accused Salim and thereafter serious offence has been committed. Thus, it appears that each accused participated in serious crime against minor victim girl. Therefore, at this stage as the investigation is in progress, there are chances of tampering with witnesses and hampering of investigation. Therefore, at this stage no case is made out for bail. Hence, I pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is rejected. Date : 20.10.2015. (Ms. U.M. Nandeshwar) Thane. Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act) Thane.

Case (POCSO) No.223/2015 Judg.Exh. CNR No.MHTH01­006573­2015 accused Nitin. 4) Upon report investigation was geared up. Investigating Officer PSI Vikrant Mahadev Kharkar carried out investigation. Statements of witnesses were recorded. Spot panchanama was drawn. After investigation charge­sheet was filed. 5) From the material on record, my Ld. Predecessor Mr. Ashutosh Karmarkar, Dist. Judge­1 has framed charge at Exh.3 on 19/12/2016 for the offence punishable under Sec. 354­A(1)(i) of I.P.C. and Sec. 8 of POCSO Act, 2012. The contents of charge were read over and explained to the accused Nitin in vernacular to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 6) Oral evidence of prosecution consists of Victim's father Roshan Manohar More (PW1) at Exh.11, Victim's mother Rohini More (PW2) at Exh.12, PSI Vijaya Laxman Venare (PW3) at Exh.15 and Investigating Officer PSI Vikrant Mahadev Kharkar at Exh.17. 7) Documentary evidence of prosecution consists of complaint at Exh.16, spot panchanama at Exh.18 and medical reports at Exh. 21 & 22. Prosecution closed evidence by pursis at Exh.23. 8) The evidence of Roshan (PW1) and Rohini (PW2) reveal that Victim is their daughter aged about 15 years having her birth date 25/05/2002 and studying in Saint Augastine School and they have 3 BHK flat and out of that one room is used for children, one 4 room for family and one room for guest. It is also revealed from their evidence that accused is their close relative. 9) Their evidence revealed that accused Nitin visited their house on 02/07/2015, slept in the guest room in their house, the children were sleeping in the bed room and accused Nitin left the house at about 5.00 a.m. in the morning and their children went to the school as usual. 10) PSI Vijaya (PW3) has recorded the Victim's complaint vide Exh.16 and handed over further investigation. 11] Investigating Officer PSI Vikrant (PW4) carried out investigation and thereby drawn the spot panchanama Exh. 18. His evidence also revealed that he recorded statements of Roshan (PW1) and Rohini (PW2) and portion marked A in their statements is recorded as per their versions. 12) As against this, accused did not adduce defence evidence, but nevertheless in his statement under Sec. 313 Cr.P.C. contended that the informant is his relative and that he did not give permission to construct house therefore, false case is filed. 13) I have heard Mr. S.D.Londhe, Ld. A.P.P. for the prosecution and Ms. Sandhya Waingankar, Ld. Advocate for the accused. Appraised the entire material on record. 5 Spl. Case (POCSO) No.223/2015 Judg.Exh. CNR No.MHTH01­006573­2015 14) Mr. Londhe submitted for adjudication on merit. Ms. Waingankar submitted that the prosecution has failed to prove the guilt beyond all reasonable doubt because Victim is not examined, there isn't corroboration, accused and Victim are relatives and because of family animosity, false case is filed. 15) Having regard to the submissions advanced at bar and after appraisal of entire material on record, I find merit in the submission of Ms. Waingankar and demerit in the submission of Mr. Londhe for following additional reasons. Accordingly, following points arise for my consideration and determination and I record my findings against each of points as under. ­ POINTS FINDINGS 1) Does the prosecution prove that in the ... In the night of 03/07/2015 at about 1.45 negative. hours, at Golden Nest Apartment, Plot No. 498, Room No. 206, 207, Sarsole village, Nerul, Sector­6, Navi Mumbai, accused Nitin has sexually harassed minor Victim, aged 13 years, by physical contact and advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures? 2) Does the prosecution prove that on the ... In the aforesaid date, time and pace, accused negative. Nitin has touched Victim's chest with sexual intention to have physical contact without penetration ? 3) What order ? ... Accused is acquitted. 6 REASONS 16) Points No. 1 & 2 :­ These points are interlinked and therefore, taken up together for reasoning and findings. 17) Relations are not in dispute. From material on record, it is clearly established that Victim is daughter of Roshan (PW1) and Rohini (PW2) and Vicitm is below 18 years having birth date 25/05/2002. 18) It may be mentioned at the outset that Victim is not examined. Victim is prime witness. Victim is sufferer. Admittedly both Victim and accused Nitin are close relatives. Non­examination of Victim is undoubtedly fatal to the prosecution. 19) The testimony of Roshan (PW1) and Rohini (PW2) clearly revealed that their daughter Victim is under mental trauma and they are not willing to bring her to adduce evidence in the court of law because her future will be spoiled. The net result is that the prosecution has failed to examine the Victim. As such the best evidence is not forthcoming. That clearly damaged the prosecution case. Accused therefore, must be benefited in this regard. 20) Both parents Roshan (P.W.1) and Rohini (PW2) have declined to support the prosecution case that the accused Nitin came in the bedroom, slept besides Victim, moved her hand on the person of Victim and upon resistance, left the flat. Nothing is extracted from the cross­examination by the prosecution. As such 7 Spl. Case (POCSO) No.223/2015 Judg.Exh. CNR No.MHTH01­006573­2015 their evidence is good for nothing to establish guilt of the accused. 21) Both Roshan (PW1) and Rohini (PW2) feel that adducing the evidence of Victim in the court of law would add to their suffering, disrepute their family in the society and carrier of the Victim and therefore, not examined. In many case, the benefit must go to the accused for want of evidence of Victim. After all parents have moral right to visualize future of their ward. 22) Nothing to discard the evidence of Vijaya (PW3). She has proved the compliant Exh.16. Mere exhibiting the complaint would not prove contents thereof. Contents of complaint Exh.16 are not proved. Accused therefore, should be benefited. 23) The evidence of Investigating Officer PSI Vikrant (PW4) is ceremonial. He has recorded the spot panchanama Exh.18 and recorded statements of witnesses. But that would not connect the accused with the offence in absence of best possible evidence. 24) All in all, prosecution has miserably failed to adduce dependable evidence to establish the offence punishable under Sec. 354­A(1)(i) of Indian Penal Code and Sec. 8 of POCSO Act, that is to say, that the accused has made physical advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures and touched her person to have physical contact but without penetration. Accordingly, I answer both points in the negative. 25) Since there isn't muddemal there isn't order to that effect. 8 26) In view of the reasons and findings stated supra, I conclude prosecution has miserably failed to prove the guilt of the accused for the offence alleged and charged and therefore accused is entitled for acquittal. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following order. ORDER 1) Accused Nitin Shankar Pawar is acquitted under section 232 235(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 of the offences punishable under sections 354­ A(1)(i) of the Indian Penal Code and under Sections 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and he is set at liberty forthwith. 2) His bail bond stand cancelled and surety is discharged. 3) Since there isn't muddemal property, there isn't order to that effect. 4) The accused shall furnish the bail bond in the sum of Rs.15,000/­( Rs. Fifteen thousand ) and the like amount of surety in accordance with the section 437­A of the Cr.P.C. for requiring them to appear before the appellate court, if any. 5) P. & D. in the Open Court. ( R. V. Jatale ) Thane. Additional Sessions Judge Date:25/06/2018. & Special Judge (POCSO Act), Thane. 9 Spl. Case (POCSO) No.223/2015 Judg.Exh. CNR No.MHTH01­006573­2015 10

--1-- ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN CRIMINAL BAIL APPLICAITON NO.2435/2017 The applicant Manoj Suresh (Billu) Dulgaj has applied for bail under section 439 of Cr. P.C. in C.R.No.I­148/2016 registered in Turbhe MIDC police station for the offence under section 363, 376(2) (I)(N), 506 of Indian Penal Code and Section 5(J)(2)(L), 6 of POCSO Act. 2. It is contended that the applicant is innocent. He is permanent resident of the given address. Investigation is almost completed. The victim is 16 years old. She is capacity to understand what is good and what is bad, moral and immoral. There was love affair between victim and accused. The victim eloped away with the accused on 05.09.2016 and they were caught by the police on 13.09.2017 at Hariyana. They were residing together for one year. It is submitted that after the incident the victim did not disclose the act of sexual relation to anybody. It is submitted that the applicant is ready to abide by the conditions and face the trial, therefore, he may be released on bail. 3. Investigating Officer filed his say at Exh.4. It is contended that the accused kidnapped the victim aged 16 years and took her at Hariyana on 05.09.2016 and after one year on 15.09.2017 they were caught by police at Hariyana and brought to Thane. The victim is 8 months pregnant. The DNA sample is required to be taken. If the accused is released on bail he is --2-- likely to jump on bail and will go to Hariyana and will tamper the prosecution witnesses. 4. I heard Ld. Advocate on behalf of accused. He submitted affidavit of the original informant stating that no such incident took place. He is ready to perform marriage of his daughter with the accused and accused is also ready to marry with the victim and FIR was given by misunderstanding. The victim was also sent letter to the court by post. It is marked at Exh.5. She has written in her letter that she has married with the accused and she is pregnant for nine years from the accused and she needs the accused for his pregnancy and delivery and no such incident took place, therefore, accused may be released on bail. 5. Ld. Counsel relied upon decision in case of Akshay Chandrakant Mahadalkar V/s. State of Maharashtra and another in Bail application No.898/2017 decided on 28 th July 2017. In that case also victim was 13 years old at the time of incident and at the time of bail she was 16 years old. The parents of both the victim and accused gave affidavit before the court that after attaining the majority they will perform the marriage of victim with accused and on that affidavit the accused was released on bail. 6. Ld. A.P.P submitted that in this case also the victim and her father had given affidavit stating about the marriage between victim and accused. --3-- 7. I sent the affidavit and letter of the victim for verification to the concerned police station. P.I. of concerned police station gave report that he has verified the affidavit and letters of the victim and it was transpired that the informant himself has made the affidavit and signed below. He also verified with the judicial section of the Thane Sessions Court. The officer of the court also stated that the informant has made affidavit through his Advocate and it is true. 8. I heard Ld. A.P.P on behalf of State. She submitted that DNA test of the applicant is remained. The victim's delivery date is 20.11.2017. 9. Considering the facts and circumstances of this case the court is of the view that victim had resided with the accused at Hariyana for one year. The photographs of the marriage is produced by the accused, affidavit is produced, victim has also sent letter to the court stating about her marriage took place with the accused and she had voluntarily residing with the accused. So considering the facts and above reported case the court is of the view that further custody of the applicant is not necessary behind the bar till the final disposal of the case. There are certain mitigating factors and prima facie case made out to release the accused on bail. Hence, I proceed to pass following order. :ORDER: 1. Application is allowed. 2. The applicant Manoj Suresh (Billu) Dulgaj shall be --4-- released on P.B. and S.B. of Rs.30,000/­(Rupees Thirty Thousand Only) with one or two local solvent sureties in like amount. 3. He shall attend the concerned police station once in a month till final disposal of the case. 4. He shall not tamper the victim or witnesses by any means. 5. He shall attend the court for trial without fail. Thane. ( S.C. Khalipe ) Date : 24/11/2017. Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

.. 1 .. Special Case no. 117/2013 Judgment Received on : 25.11.2013 Registered on : 25.11.2013 Decided on : 13.03.2015 Duration : 1 year 3 months 16 days IN THE COURT OF THE SPECIAL JUDGE (PROTECTION OF CHILDREN FROM SEXUAL OFFENCES ACT) THANE (Presided over by Ms.V.V.Virkar) SPECIAL CASE No. 117 of 2013 Exhibit No. 19 The State of Maharashtra ... Complainant versus 1] Islam Jumerat Ali Shaikh Age 25 years, Resident of house no.372/B, in front of Apsara Talkies, Nehrunagar, Navi Vasti, Bhiwandi. 2] Imran Jumerat Ali Shaikh Age 29 years, Resident of house no.372/B, in front of Apsara Talkies, Nehrunagar, Navi Vasti, Bhiwandi. ... Accused Appearance - Mr. A.K.Khamkar, learned Additional Public Prosecutor (hereinafter in ''A.P.P.'') Mr. Sanjay Shrivastav, learned advocate for the accused. .. 2 .. Special Case no. 117/2013 Judgment JUDGMENT (Delivered on 13.03.2015.) The accused stands prosecuted for the offence punishable under section 354D(1)(i), 506 read with section 34 of I.P.C. and section 11(iv) read with section 12 and section 16 read with section 17 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act) for outraging modesty of the complainant victim girl Anisa Ansari by frequently proposing her for marriage and by catching hold of her hand and when she refused, by threatening her and her parents that they would throw acid on her face if they refused for marriage of the girl with accused no.1. 2] In short the facts giving rise to the prosecution of the accused are that victim girl Anisa Ansari had been staying at her house bearing no.72, Ashrafiya chowk, near office of Asif, Nehrunagar, Navi Vasti, Bhiwandi, alongwith her parents and younger sister. That accused Islam Shaikh had been staying in same area and was addicted to drink liquor. That he was behind complainant and was oftenly proposing her that she should marry her and even had put such proposal to the parents of the girl but since he was addicted to drink liquor, her parents and the girl had refused such proposal. But thereafter also he continued to follow the complainant and insistently putting forward proposal of marriage and when she was not responding favourably said Islam Shaikh had been to the house of the complainant on 08.10.2013 around 9.00 p.m. and had threatened her in presence of her parents that if she .. 3 .. Special Case no. 117/2013 Judgment refuse to marry they would case her burn injury by throwing acid on her face. The mother of the complainant had driven him out of house. Thereafter after some time Islam again came there with his brother Imran Shaikh, accused no.2 and both of them threatened them in similar manner. The complainant and her parents were scared and therefore they did not go to police station on the same day and next day went to police station and the complainant lodged complaint in regard to the incident to police station on 09.10.2013. 3] On the basis of said complaint, offence as per C.R.No.I- 193/2013 under section 354D(1)(i), 506 read with section 34 of I.P.C. and section 11(iv) read with section 12 and section 16 read with section 17 of P.O.C.S.O. Act was registered at Bhiwandi City police station and the work of investigation was entrusted to P.S.I. Wagh. During the investigation the statements of witnesses including parents of the girl and other witnesses were recorded. Since the girl was minor, her school leaving certificate was obtained as proof of her date of birth. Since provisions of P.O.C.S.O. Act wee also found to have been attracted, a report to that effect was submitted and section 11(iv) read with section 12 and section 16 read with section 17 of P.O.C.S.O. Act were applied and after completion of investigation since there was sufficient evidence against the accused, they came to be charge-sheeted for offence under section 354D(1)(i), 506 read with section 34 of I.P.C. and section 11(iv) read with section 12 and section 16 read with section 17 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. .. 4 .. Special Case no. 117/2013 Judgment 4] Since provisions of section 11(iv) read with section 12 and section 16 read with section 17 of P.O.C.S.O. Act are applied, the charge sheet was submitted to this Special Court. 5] The accused appeared before the Court. A charge for offence under section 354D(1)(i), 506 read with section 34 of I.P.C. and section 11(iv) read with section 12 and section 16 read with section 17 of P.O.C.S.O. Act was framed against the accused as per Exh.2. The contents of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. The accused pleaded not guilty. Their defence was of total denial. They claimed to be tried. 6] For establishing the guilt of the accused, the prosecution examined P.W.1 Anisa d/o Mehmud Ansari, P.W.2 Latifa w/o Mehmud Ansari, P.W.3 Kiran Namdev Wagh, P.S.I. The documentary evidence produced, proved and relied upon by the prosecution was in the form of copy of school leaving certificate Exh.12 and complaint Exh.15. 7] Statement of both accused under section 313 of Cr.P.C. were recorded. The accused did not examine themselves on oath and had not examined any witness in defence. 8] I heard the learned A.P.P. and the learned advocate for the accused. 9] On the basis of above facts of the case, the points which arose for my determination and my findings and reasons for the same are as under - .. 5 .. Special Case no. 117/2013 Judgment Points Findings i) Does prosecution prove that since prior to three months of lodging the complaint the accused persons in furtherance of their common intention were following the victim girl and used to contact said girl to foster personal interaction repeatedly with her with proposal of marriage of accused no.1 with her, despite a clear indication of disinterest by said girl ? No. ii ) Whether the prosecution has proved that on t08.10.2013 at the residential house of the victim girl, the accused persons in furtherance of their common intention threatened the girl and her family members to disfigure face of the girl by throwing acid and also threatened them to make their life impossible there ? No. iii ) Whether the prosecution has proved on the given day, date, time and place the accused persons were following the victim girl and were persuading her to perform marriage with accused no.1 and when she refused they threatened to disfigure her face by throwing acid and thereby they committed sexual harassment of said girl and the accused no.2 in above said manner abetted accused no.1 in commission of offence ? No. iv ) What offence, if any, is proved ? No offence is proved. v ) What order ? The accused are acquitted. .. 6 .. Special Case no. 117/2013 Judgment REASONS As to point no.1 to 3 - 11] As is clear the allegations against the accused are that the accused no.1 was addicted to drinking liquor and had been putting forward proposal of marriage with the complainant and in spite of complainant refused said proposal, he insistently was saying so and even lastly he had been to the house of the complainant and threatened her to throw acid on face and accused no.2 who is elder brother of the accused no.1 also alleged to have threatened the complainant and pressurized her to perform marriage with accused no.1. However, if the evidence of the complainant and her mother in regard to said incident is perused, it appears that both of them have stated that accused Islam had put forth proposal of marriage with complainant girl and even had been to their house with said proposal and also further that even after refusal the accused again and again saying same thing, absolutely nothing is stated by both these witnesses in regard to the alleged threats given by the accused. What is clear from the testimony of P.W.1 and 2 is that the accused simply put forth proposal of marriage and repeatedly persuaded them for said marriage and even though they refused accused were insistently putting proposal and therefore they felt troubled and went to police station and lodged complaint but merely putting forward proposal of marriage may not amount to outraging modesty of woman as contemplated under section 354 of I.P.C. or may not amount to ''sexual harassment'' as contemplated under P.O.C.S.O. Act. .. 7 .. Special Case no. 117/2013 Judgment 12] No doubt, P.W.3 P.S.I. Kiran Wagh appear to have stated in his evidence that the complainant had lodged complaint with the allegation that the accused had threatened the complainant to throw acid on face and cause her burn injuries if she refuse to marry etc. and also stated that he had recorded complaint of the complainant as per her narration and further also portion marked A in the complaint and statement of mother of the complainant was recorded as per her narration, on the basis of that mere fact which can be said to have been established is that such complaint was lodged by the complainant but when the complaint in her evidence on oath before Court has not substantiated such allegations, said allegations cannot be said to have been established. Then, it is also to be mentioned that under section 29 of P.O.C.S.O. Act it is provided that ''Where a person is prosecuted for committing or abetting or attempting to commit any offence under sections 3, 5, 7 and 9 of this Act, the Special Court shall presume that such person has committed or abetted or attempted to commit the offence, as the case may be, unless the contrary is proved''. But then, it has to be mentioned that though the complainant made allegations in the complaint, in their evidence before Court the complainant or the witness had not supported the allegations against the accused and in such circumstance when the accused has come up with specific defence of total denial, I am of the view that when the basic requirement of the prosecution in establishing the allegations by cogent and reliable evidence is not fulfilled, there is no question of raising presumption under section 29 of the P.O.C.S.O. Act. Then, as discussed above merely on the basis of the fact that the accused repeatedly put forth proposal of marriage, the allegation against the .. 8 .. Special Case no. 117/2013 Judgment accused cannot be said to have been established. Point no.1 to 2 are answered accordingly in the negative. As to Point no.4 - 13] In view of my above findings no offence can be said to have been proved against the accused persons and the accused are entitled to be acquitted. Point no.4 is answered in the negative. 14] Since the accused are acquitted, it is necessary that they be directed to execute P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/- [rupees fifteen thousand only] each in the like amount under section 437A of Cr.P.C. to appear before the higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect of any appeal or revision if any filed against the judgment. In the result I pass the following order - ORDER Accused namely Islam Jumerat Ali Shaikh and Imran Jumerat Ali Shaikh are acquitted of the charge for offene punishable under section 354D(1)(i) and 506(2) read with section 34 of Indian Penal Code and also under section 11(iv) read with section 12 and Section 16 read with section 17 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 2) Bail bonds of the accused stand cancelled and sureties are discharged. 3) The accused shall execute P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/- [rupees fifteen thousand only] each under section 437A .. 9 .. Special Case no. 117/2013 Judgment of Cr.P.C. to appear before the higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect of any appeal or revision, if any, filed against the judgment and that such bail bond shall be in force for six months. 4) Since muddemal articles are produced before Court, no order regarding its disposal is passed. 5) The proceeding is closed. Date : 13.03.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.

.. 1 .. Bail No. 2498/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) Criminal Bail Application No.2498/2015 Sangeeta Haribhau Bhangare .. Applicant versus The State of Maharashtra Through Vartaknagar P.S. .. Non­applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 By this application the applicant is seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C., who was arrested on 28.09.2015 by Vartak Nagar Police Station in connection with C.R.No.I­ 534/2015 registered for an offence punishable under section 370­ (2)(3) of I.P. Code and section4, 8, 17 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as P.O.C.S.O. Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Mr.S.H.Butala for the applicant/accused and learned A.P.P. Mrs. Navale for State. I.O. present with case diary. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 28.09.2015 at the instance of the informant P.S.I. Sharad Panje attached with A.H.T.C. Thane with an indictment that on secret information the raid was conducted at room no.401 Panchamrut Apartment, Lokmanya nagar, Pada no.4, Thane and there accused Alka and Sangeeta found indulging five ladies including two minor girls in the prostitution business. They are living on their earning and not .. 2 .. Bail No. 2498/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) giving any remuneration to the victim ladies and girl. Therefore, F.I.R. came to be registered. 4] The learned Counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant­accused is falsely implicated. He submitted that the only allegation against present applicant­accused is that she provided the place for prostitution. She became the scape­goat of entire situation. He submitted that the applicant­accused was not knowing about any such thing. She had only provided the premises to help them. There is neither any abettment on her part nor she participated in the crime. He submitted that two girls are stated to be minor however they are about 17 years of age and are about to attain majority. The section levelled are not attracted in the facts of the case. The applicant­accused has no criminal antecedents. She is ready to abide any conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing her on bail. 5] Per contra, the learned A.P.P. opposed the application submitting that the offence is serious. She submitted that the F.I.R. speaks in volume. From the F.I.R. itself the intention of both accused is very clear. They were having knowledge about entire things and conducted business for their own benefit. Both accused were caught red handed during the raid. There is recovery of money and condom from the house of the accused. The investigation is still in progress. There are chances of tampering of witnesses and prayed for rejection of application. .. 3 .. Bail No. 2498/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R., it appears that the raid was conducted on secret information at the house of accused Alka Madke. The victim­girls were found in the bedroom in her house with decoy customer. During their search the amount of Rs.4000/­ was found and two mobile phones of accused also came to be seized. It prima facie appears that out of five victim­girl, two girls were minor aged about 17 years. The F.I.R. prima facie shows that the accused are involved in serious and heinous offence and indulged in exploiting needy and poor ladies by their undue advantage of their situation. Providing bedroom where the victim­ girl and decoy customer used to come and go clearly shows that both accused were aware about the business carried out by them and they were living on the earning of prostitution without paying remuneration to victim­girls. The investigation is still in progress. Further, the apprehension of A.P.P. about tampering of witnesses find base as the accused are involved in serious offence. Hence, no case is made out for releasing the accused on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is rejected. Thane. Date : 29.10.2015. (Ms. U.M. Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act), Thane.

.. 1 .. Bail No. 2501/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) Criminal Bail Application No.2501/2015 Alka Bhausaheb Yedke .. Applicant versus The State of Maharashtra Through Vartaknagar P.S. .. Non­applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 By this application the applicant is seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C., who was arrested on 28.09.2015 by Vartak Nagar Police Station in connection with C.R.No.I­ 534/2015 registered for an offence punishable under section 370­ (2)(3) of I.P. Code and section4, 8, 17 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as P.O.C.S.O. Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Mr. Sanjay Kanhere for the applicant/accused and learned A.P.P. Mrs. Navale for State. I.O. present with case diary. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 28.09.2015 at the instance of the informant P.S.I. Sharad Panje attached with A.H.T.C. Thane with an indictment that on secret information the raid was conducted at room no.401 Panchamrut Apartment, Lokmanya nagar, Pada no.4, Thane and there accused Alka and Sangeeta found indulging five ladies including two minor girls in the prostitution business. They are living on their earning and not .. 2 .. Bail No. 2501/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) giving any remuneration to the victim ladies and girl. Therefore, F.I.R. came to be registered. 4] The learned Counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant­accused is falsely implicated. He submitted that the allegation against present applicant­accused is that she used to compel the victim­girls and ladies to do prostitution. He submitted that the other accused is alleged to be providing room for conducting prostitution activity. He further submitted that two girls are stated to be minor however they are about 17 years of age and are about to attain majority. The section levelled are not attracted in the facts of the case. He also submitted that accused are arrested after raid and thus most of the part of investigation has been completed. The applicant­accused has no criminal antecedents. She is ready to abide any conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing her on bail. 5] Per contra, the learned A.P.P. opposed the application submitting that the offence is serious. She submitted that the F.I.R. speaks in volume. From the F.I.R. itself the intention of both accused is very clear. They were having knowledge about entire things and conducted business for their own benefit. Both accused were caught red handed during the raid. There is recovery of money and condom from the house of the accused. The investigation is still in progress. There are chances of tampering of witnesses and prayed for rejection of application. .. 3 .. Bail No. 2501/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R., it appears that the raid was conducted on secret information at the house of accused Alka Madke. The victim­girls were found in the bedroom in her house with decoy customer. During their search the amount of Rs.4000/­ was found and two mobile phones of accused also came to be seized. It prima facie appears that out of five victim­girl, two girls were minor aged about 17 years. The F.I.R. prima facie shows that the accused are involved in serious and heinous offence and indulged in exploiting needy and poor ladies by their undue advantage of their situation. Providing bedroom where the victim­ girl and decoy customer used to come and go clearly shows that both accused were aware about the business carried out by them and they were living on the earning of prostitution without paying remuneration to victim­girls. The investigation is still in progress. Further, the apprehension of A.P.P. about tampering of witnesses find base as the accused are involved in serious offence. Hence, no case is made out for releasing the accused on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is rejected. Thane. Date : 29.10.2015. (Ms. U.M. Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act), Thane.

.. 1 .. Anticipatory Bail 2363/14 (Order below exhibit 1) Order below Exh.1 in Anticipatory Bail Appln. No. 2363/2014 This application is filed by applicant Pankaj Ramsevak Singh for his release on bail under section 438 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. I­544/2014 registered at Mira Road police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 354 of I.P.C. and under section 7 and 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). It was contended and argued that the applicants have been falsely involved in this crime with the allegation of causing sexual harassment of the victim girls by outraging their modesty. It is also submitted that the applicant has been implicated in this case with ulterior motive. It is further contended and argued that there is delay in lodging F.I.R. It is also submitted that looking to the allegations made in this case, for the purpose of investigation the custodial interrogation of the applicant is not required. It is further submitted that they are permanent residents of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co­operate with the investigation and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on anticipatory bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that at the time of the incident the victim girls were playing basket ball and at that time the applicant/accused went to them and took them in the parking lot on the pretext of teaching them to basket ball and then committed sexual assault on them by moving hand on their breast and also stated to victim girl Hetal that he likes her. It is further submitted that in such circumstance to make thorough investigation into the .. 2 .. Anticipatory Bail 2363/14 (Order below exhibit 1) matter, the custodial interrogation of the applicant/accused is necessary. It is further submitted that the applicant is also residing in the same building where the victims are staying and therefore if the applicant is released on anticipatory bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girls and the complainant and also being absconded which may hamper the investigation. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on anticipatory bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 354 of I.P.C. and section 7 and 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, it is stated that there is delay in lodging the F.I.R. and in the light of that the contentions on behalf of applicant that there had been previous rivalry between the parties is concerned, that appear to be material aspect in the light of the fact that as per contentions of the applicant the entire story put forth by the applicant is improbable. Then, even looking to the nature offence and the manner in which it is stated to have been committed the custodial interrogation of the applicant do not appear to be necessary and the apprehension expressed by the prosecution that the applicant may not be available for investigation or release of applicant on anticipatory bail would hamper the investigation, can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions including condition to give attendance to police station and for that purpose there appear no necessity of the custody of the applicant. 4] Then, it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and is ready to abide by any .. 3 .. Anticipatory Bail 2363/14 (Order below exhibit 1) conditions imposed and in all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the interim anticipatory bail already granted to the applicant can be confirmed. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER 1) The application is allowed. 2) The interim anticipatory bail granted to the applicant namely Pankaj Ramsevak Singh vide order passed below Exh.3 on 28.11.2014 is hereby confirmed. 3) In the event of arrest of the applicant for offence punishable under section 354 of I.P.C. and section 7 and 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act registered under C.R.No.I­544/2014 at Mira Road Police Station, he shall be released on furnishing P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ a) The applicant shall attend the concerned police station on every Monday between 3.00 p.m. to 5.00 p.m. and shall co­operate with the investigating machinery. b) He shall not, directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer. c) He shall not leave India without the previous permission of the Court. d) He shall not tamper with prosecution evidence. Date : 26.03.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Additional Session Judge­1, Thane.

Though the accused has examined defence witnesses, in order to establish that the victim was pregnant from someone else, the defence evidence is certainly not sound and reliable. The victim being minor her consent is not a consent in the eyes of law. It is pertinent to note here that the accused is a married man having children. Despite said fact he lured the victim in the sexual relations with him. He forced himself upon her and committed sexual intercourse. He has even gone to the extent of causing miscarriage of the victim girl. Under such circumstances the arguments of advocate Mr.N.S.Khan are not acceptable. Hence point Nos.1 and 2 are answered in the affirmative. 26] The prosecution has proved single act of sexual intercourse and miscarriage of pregnancy of the victim. Under such circumstances there is no question of harassment as charged against the accused. So also there are no specific words of threats alleged and proved against the accused. J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 227­15 ­ S­376,312, 506(2), 4.doc .....18/­ ..18.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 227/2015..Exh.51.. Under such circumstances point Nos.3 and 4 are answered in the negative. 27] As accused is held guilt for the offences punishable u/s.376, 312 of the Indian Penal Code and u/s.4 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, he is liable to be convicted and punished for the same. At this juncture the Judgment is deferred to hear the accused on the quantum of sentence. Thane. (P.P.Jadhav) District Judge­4 and Date : 31.07.2018. Addl. Sessions Judge, Thane. 28] Heard advocate Mr.N.S.Khan and accused in person. It is submitted that accused is having two children. His family is depending upon him. Under such circumstances considering the age of the victim and other circumstances minimum sentence be inflicted by giving special reasons. On the contrary A.P.P Mr.Vivek Kadu argued that the offence is very serious. Hence maximum punishment be inflicted upon the accused. 29] The accused is held guilty for the offence punishable u/s.376 and 312 of the Indian Penal Code and section 4 of The Protection of Children From Sexual Offence J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 227­15 ­ S­376,312, 506(2), 4.doc .....19/­ ..19.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 227/2015..Exh.51.. Act. Section 4 of The Protection of Children From Sexual Offence Act being provision under special enactment, it is not necessary to punish the accused u/s.376 of the Indian Penal Code. Section 4 of The Protection of Children From Sexual Offence Act prescribes imprisonment not less than seven years and which may extent to imprisonment for life as well as fine. As already observed the accused who is married person has committed penetrative sexual assault upon the victim who is minor. Under such circumstances there is no reason to inflict the punishment lesser than the minimum prescribed by the Act. Considering the nature of act and suffering of the victim, the accused deserves to be punished with proper sentence and fine. With these observations following order is passed. ORDER 1. Accused Shabbir Rafik Mulani is hereby convicted u/s.235(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure for offence punishable u/s.376, 312 of the Indian Penal Code, u/s.4 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 2.
