JUDGMENT ( Delivered on this 10th day of October, 2017) 1] Accused are charged for the offence punishable under Sec. 370(1)(2)(3)(4) of Indian Penal Code, Sec. 3,4,5,6 of Immoral Traffic ( Prevention ) Act,1956 and S. 11(i) r/w. 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 for having been indulged in prostitution and trafficking minor victim girls on false assurance of marriages and sexual harassment to have intercourse with the unknown person. 2] Prosecution's case, in brief, is as under : On 14.08.2013, at about 12.30 in noon, Crime Branch, Thane got the tip that on the ground floor of 'Kamal Palace' Pappya @ Harihar is running brothel with the help of his wife Asma. The information was designated to the Senior Officials. One decoy customer and panchas were called. The decoy customer was given four currency notes of denomination of Rs. 500/­ and their numbers were noted down. The party proceeded to Dighar village. The decoy customer was sent at Kamal Palace Hotel. The decoy customer Vinod Baby Mallappa went to accused Pappya @ Harihar and demanded the sexual favour from a lady. He gave those four currency notes of Rs. 500/­ to the accused. Vinod Mallappa gave signal by missed call to raiding party. Raiding party proceeded to 3 Special Case No. 120/2013 Judgment. the spot with panchas. They asked the name of accused. He told his name as Pappya @Harihar Shankarsan Sahu. One lady was present there. She was cooking. It was one bedroom, hall and kitchen flat. One half naked girl was sitting with the decoy customer in the bedroom. The girl told her name as Pooja Laltu Jana Mandal. There was one other minor girl named Tuni Mandal. Investigation officer took search of accused and found four currency notes of denomination of Rs. 500/­ in his possession. L.P.C. P.U.Manore, came to police station and lodged report. Investigation was taken up by P.I. Vikram Karkud. During the course of investigation, he went to the spot and prepared spot panchanama Exh. 81. He sent victim girls for medical examination and age determination. He recorded statement of victim girls. He has collected Medical Certificate from Nair Hospital. He recorded statements of police staff. He got recorded statement of victim girls under Sec. 164 Cr.P.C. After completion of investigation, charge­ sheet came to be filed in the Court of J.M.F.C. who in turn committed this case to the Court of Sessions. 3] My Ld. Predecessor has framed charge against these two accused below Exh.12 to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 4] After recording of evidence of the witnesses of prosecution, statement of the accused under Sec. 313 came to be recorded. Total denial is the defence of the accused. 4 Special Case No. 120/2013 Judgment. 5] I have heard Ld. A.P.P. and Ld. Advocate Shri. Pande for the accused. Following points arose for my determination and I gave my findings thereon for the reasons stated below: Sr. POINTS FINDINGS No. 1. Does the prosecution prove that the No accused along with absconding accused Panchanan Gurupada Das in furtherance of their common intention on 14.08.2013 around 14.05 hrs., at Kamal Palace, Gr. Does the prosecution prove that the No. accused on above mentioned date, time 5 Special Case No. 120/2013 Judgment. and place committed sexual harassment by saying to do sexual intercourse with unknown person i.e customer in the bedroom, to minor victim girl by name Tuni Mandal? 5. What order? As per final order. REASONS 6] In order to establish the guilt of accused, the prosecution is required to adduce cogent and convincing evidence. The prosecution has examined L.P.H.C. Pratima Manore, P.W.1 who is complainant at ( Exh.35 ), Chandrakant Mane, P.W.2, Retired A.S.I.at (Exh.,57), Dhananjay Tiwari, P.W.3, panch witness on pretrap panchanama (Exh.65), Vikram Karkud, Dy.S.P., P.W.4 who is investigating officer at (Exh. 77). The prosecution has also relied on Report (Exh. 36), Curreny notes ( total 4 ) Exh. 66, pre­ trap panchanama (Exh. 67), Panchanama (Exh.67/2), spot panchanama ( Exh. 81) and statements of victim girls u/s. 164 Cr.P.C. (Exh. 82 & 83 ). AS TO POINT NOS.1 TO 5 :­ 7] I would like to discuss all these points together. Vikram Karkud (P.W.4) then, P.I. at S.T.C. Thane received tip that the accused was running brothel at their residence at Kamal Palace, Diaghar. He designated information to his seniors. He called two panchas with the hep of staff. Similarly one bogus customer was 6 Special Case No. 120/2013 Judgment. also called. They were given information. 8] It has come in the evidence of P.W.1 Pratima Manore, L.P.C. , P.W.2 Chandrakant Mane, retired A.S.I., P.W.3 Dhananjay Tiwari, panch and P.W.4 Vikram Karkud, P.I that they were present in Diaghar police station. On 14.8.2013, a secret informant give a tip in the office of Sr.P.I., that at Diaghar village one person by ame Pappay @ Harihar and his wife Asma carrying out prostitution in their house. P.I. Vikram Karkud (P.W.4) took necessary entries in the station diary. Vikram Karkud (P.W.4) had handed over four currency notes of denomination of Rs. 500/­ to the decoy customer. They prepared pre­trap panchanama (Exh.67) in presence of panchas. They went to Kamal Palace, at Diaghar. They sent decoy customer with those currency notes in room No.6, Ground floor. Decoy customer was given instructions that he shall give signal by missed call after getting prostitute. Decoy customer and one panch and staff proceeded near the said room. It has further come in their evidence that decoy customer gave missed call. Then, P.W.1 L.P.C. Pratima Manore, P.W.2 Chandrakant Mane, P.W.3 Dhananjay Tiwari and P.W. 4 Vikram Karkud went to Kamal Palace, room No.6. They found decoy customer in the bedroom of accused. He was sitting on bed. The house of accused has one bedroom, hall and kitchen. They introduced themselves to the accused and explained purpose of their visit. They have asked the accused whether they wanted to take search of police personnel. They enquired with the girl who was present with decoy customer on the 7 Special Case No. 120/2013 Judgment. bed. She told her name as Pooja Mandal. Decoy customer told that he gave money to accused Pappya @ Harihar. Police took personal search of accused Pappya @ Harihar. They found four currency notes of Rs. 500/­ in the pant pocket of Pappya @Harihar. The numbers of those currency notes were same as noted in the pre­trap panchanama in presence of panchas. Those currency notes were taken in custody and put in envelope which was sealed. The girl told that they were brought by accused Harihar and his wife and they were forced in prostitution. Investigation Officer drew panchanama Exh. 67 in presence of panchas. The statements of victim girls under Sec. 164 Cr.P.C. was recorded. They had stated their false names but while recording statements under Sec. 164 Cr.P.C., they have told their correct names. 9] Pratima Manore P.W.1 deposed that she has lodged F.I.R. She has mentioned name of decoy customer as Vinod Babu Mallappa. 10] P.W.2 Chandrakant Mane is also a police witness. He has also deposed about the procedural part of laying trap. He has also stated the name of decoy customer as Vinod Mallappa. His evidence is not challenged by the accused. 11] P.W.3 Dhananjay Tiwari is the panch witness. He has stated that police officer told him that they will be conducting a raid at Kamal Palace, Baithi chawl since they have learnt that 8 Special Case No. 120/2013 Judgment. prostitution business goes on at the said place. But, thereafter, he deposed that he does not recollect what had happened on the said date. However, during the course of cross­examination by Ld. P.P., he has supported the prosecution story. 12] P.W.4 Vikram Karkund has stated that it has come to his notice that victim girls Pooja Mandal and Pinky are from West Bengal and they were minor. Those girls were missing. He got recorded their statements under Sec. 164 of Cr.P.C. At the time of recording statement, they have stated their correct names. It is pertinent to note that the investigation officer has carried out the investigation as per procedure. His evidence is of formal nature. The prosecution has failed to examine any independent witness. Most important witnesses i.e. decoy customer and victim girls are also not examined by the prosecution. Therefore, in absence of any cogent and reliable evidence, the evidence of P.W.4 Mr. Karkund can not be accepted as it is to prove the guilt of accused. 13] I have heard Ld. A.P.P. and Ld. Advocate for accused. L.P.C. Pratima Manore, P.W.1 has lodged the report but, she is unable to give exact address, location or the situation of the house of accused. In her evidence she has deposed that two bogus customers were sent to the house of accused. She deposed that Tiwari was the bogus customer. But, it appears that Tiwari was not the bogus customer. In fact, he is a panch witness. In cross­examination, she deposed that she do not 9 Special Case No. 120/2013 Judgment. remember whether she has mentioned the name of decoy customer as Shri. Tiwari in F.I.R. She has stated in cross­examination that she has narrated that the three girls were sitting on the cot and it was a one room compartment. She has also narrated that there was curtain. But, all these things do not find place in the F.I.R. In stead in the F.I.R. it is mentioned that the room in Kamal Palace which was allegedly used as brothel was consisting of one bedroom, hall and kitchen. There was only one girl found sitting with the decoy customer Vinod Mallappa on the bed. In F.I.R., she has not stated that there were two decoy customers. She has also not mentioned the name of decoy customer as Tiwari in F.I.R.. Thus, there are variations in the F.I.R. and the evidence of P.W.1 Pratima. Therefore, the evidence of P.W.1 Pratima is not much reliable. 14] It appears that the prosecution has failed to examine the most important witnesses i.e. decoy customer Vinod Mallappa and the victim girl Pooja who alleged to be found sitting with him on the bed in so called brothel at Kamal Palace. These two persons have played important role in the trap. Therefore, non­ examination of these two witnesses is fatal to the prosecution's case. So, also there are variations in the evidence of P.W.1 Praima Manore who lodged report. Her evidence is inconsistent with the report. As per evidence of P.W.4 Mr. Karkund victim girls were missing. Therefore, the evidence of victim girls is not on record. In absence of evidence of victim girls or decoy customer, it is risky to believe the prosecution story that the accused have detained minor 10 Special Case No. 120/2013 Judgment. victim girls in Kamal Palace, Room No. 6 at Diaghar village for the sake of prostitution and was living wholly on their income from prostitution. As such, accused are entitled to get benefit of doubt. In result, I answer point Nos.1 to 4 in the negative and proceed to pass following order: ORDER 1] Accused Nos.1 and 2 namely Papya @ Harihar Shankarsan Sahu and Aasma Sattar Abdul @ Rita Harihar Sahu are hereby acquitted under Sec. 235(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure of the offence punishable under Sec. 370(1)(2) (3)(4) of Indian Penal Code and Sec. 3,4,5,6 of Immoral Traffic ( Prevention ) Act,1956 and S. 11(i) r/w. 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act,2012. 2] Accused are in jail. They be released forthwith if not required in any other case. Inform the Jail Superintendent accordingly. 3] Muddemal property being worthless, be destroyed after appeal period. 4] Accused shall furnish P.B and S.B. of RS.10,000/­ each under Sec.437­A of Code of Criminal Procedure. Thane, ( V.V.Bambarde ) Date : 10.10.2017 Additional Sessions Judge­1, Thane 11 Special Case No. 120/2013 Judgment. 12 Special Case No. 120/2013 Judgment.

1 Special Case No. 121/2013 (Judgment) Presented on : 02/12/2013 Registered on : 02/12/2013 Decided on : 30/03/2016 Duration :2­year,2­Months,28­days. IN THE COURT OF THE SPECIAL JUDGE (P.O.C.S.O.ACT), THANE. (Presided over by Ms.U.M.Nandeshwar, Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O.Act) Thane) SPECIAL CASE No. 121 of 2013 Exhibit No.17. The State of Maharashtra Through Mumbra Police Station Thane, District – Thane. ... Prosecution versus Jakir Jafar Shaikh Age 21 years, Residence –Alishan Building, B­wing, Room No.203 2nd floor, Rashid Compound, Mumbra Dist. Thane. . ... Accused Offence punishable under section 354­A and 506 of Indian Penal Code and under section 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Appearance ­ Spl.P.P. Mrs. R. A. Navale, for the State. Advocate Mr. N. S. Khan, for the Accused. 2 Special Case No. 121/2013 (Judgment) JUDGMENT (Delivered on 30th March, 2016.) 1] The Accused stands prosecuted for the offence punishable under section 354­A & 506 of Indian Penal Code and also under section 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act) for causing sexual harassment to minor victim­girl aged about 15 years and threaten her. 2] Shron of unnecessary details, the indictment against the Accused are as under ­ [i] Informant / victim­girl (P.W.1) aged about 15 years is staying with her family at Rashid Compound Kausa, Mumbra. She was studying in 10th standard and attending National Coaching classes near police chowki Kausa from 05.00 p.m. to 07.30 p.m. [ii] Accused is staying beyond two buildings from the house of informant and used to stalk her when she used to proceed to her tuition class and used to wait outside her tuition class and again follow her while returning from the class. Before two months he asked mobile number to the informant and when she refused, he threatened her to kill her brother and give his own number to her and before one month he holds her hand and threatened her and forced her to call him on mobile. Informant due to fear of accused and with the 3 Special Case No. 121/2013 (Judgment) fear that her parents may stop her studies did not disclose act of accused to her parents. [iii] On 13/10/2013 when informant was proceeding in a rickshaw with her friends, at that time accused threatened to cause harm to himself by cutting his hand and asked her to sit on his motor cycle and roamed her in the area of Mumbra. One of the acquaintance of the informant seen then roaming and objected it, therefore, accused left her and ran away from there. Therefore, informant lodged report against the accused. 3] On her report F.I.R. was registered against the Accused vide C.R.No.I­770/2013 for the offence punishable under section 354­A & 506 of I.P.C. and under section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. The investigation was carried out by A.P.I. M.D.Sawant. The Accused was arrested. The spot panchnama was drawn in presence of panchas. Statements of witnesses were recorded. Thereafter, investigation culminated into filing of charge­sheet in this Court being the Special designated court under P.O.C.S.O. Act. 4] The charge (Exh.5) was framed against the Accused for offence punishable under section 354­A & 506 of Indian Penal Code and also under section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. The Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial (Exh.6). The Accused took defence of total denial. 4 Special Case No. 121/2013 (Judgment) 5] In response to application under section 294 of Cr.P.C. the defence has admitted spot panchnama [Exh.14] and Arrest form [Exh.15]. 6] In order to prove guilt of Accused Prosecution has examined following witnesses ­ P.W.1 Informant – victim­girl Exh.10 P.W.2 Fatima Abdul Razak Shaikh Exh.12 (Mother of victim­girl) 7] The prosecution proved and relied on the report / F.I.R. [Exh.11]. 8] The prosecution closed its side of evidence by filing Pursis at Exhibit­16. As there is no incriminating evidence came on record against the Accused therefore his statement under Section 313(b) of Cr.P.C. was dispensed with. Accused neither examined himself nor examined any witness in his defence. 9] Heard learned A.P.P. Mrs. R. A. Navale for State and the learned Advocate Mr. N. S. Khan for Accused. 10] On consideration of argument advanced on behalf of both the sides and on perusal of the oral & documentary evidence on record, following points arise for my determination, which are answered with the findings thereon, 5 Special Case No. 121/2013 (Judgment) as under :­ Sr. Points Findings No. 1] Does the prosecution prove that since prior to six months of 13/10/2013 on the route of Rashid compound, Kausa Mumbra to National Coaching classes, in ..No. front of Kausa chowki, Mumbra accused caused sexual harassment to the minor victim­girl aged about 15 years by chasing her, holding her hand tried to make physical contact and caused sexual harassment to her and he thereby committed an offence punishable under section 354­A of Indian Penal Code ? 2] Does the prosecution prove that during same period accused committed criminal intimidation by threatening the victim­ girl to kill her brother with intent to ..No. cause alarm to her and he thereby committed an offence punishable under section 506 of I.P.C. ? 3] Does the prosecution prove that during same period accused committed sexual harassment to the minor victim­girl aged about 15 years with sexual intent in ...No. above said manner and thereby he committed an offence punishable under section 12 of the P.O.C.S.O. Act? 4] What order ? Accused is acquitted. 6 Special Case No. 121/2013 (Judgment) REASONS As to Point No.1 to 3 : 11] All the points are taken up together for discussion, to avoid the repetition, as evidence about the same in common and inter­connected. 12] As the Accused is facing charge under section 354­A of I.P.C. it is incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that the Accused caused sexual harassment to victim­girl by physical contact and advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overture with minor victim­girl by holding her hand and roaming her on his motor­bike for pursuing her to develop acquaintance with him. So also as the Accused is facing charge under section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, therefore, it is further incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that the accused has committed sexual harassment to the victim­ girl with sexual intent, either utters any word or makes any sound, or makes any gesture or exhibits any object or part of body with the intention that such work or sound shall be heard, or such gesture or object or part of body shall be seen by the child; or repeatedly or constantly follows or watches or contact a child either directly or through electronic, digital or any other means etc. as defined in section 11 of the Protection 7 Special Case No. 121/2013 (Judgment) Of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2002 (P.O.C.S.O. Act). Age of victim­girl : 13] As the Accused is facing charge under P.O.C.S.O. Act, therefore, first of all it is incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that the victim­girl was child (minor) at the time of incident. The alleged incident took place in between March­2013 to 13/10/2013. Victim­girl (P.W.1) entered in witness­box on 23/03/2016 and stated her age as 17 years. However, neither victim­girl (P.W.1) nor her mother (P.W.2) stated her date of birth and there is no single document on record in support of her date of birth. Thus, except oral version of victim­girl there is absolutely no evidence on record to prove that at the time of incident, the victim­girl was minor i.e. below the age of 18 years and she was a “child” as per definition given in Section 2(d) of P.O.C.S.O. Act. 14] As prosecution failed to prove that the victim­girl was child (minor) on the date of incident, therefore, now it is only required to see whether prosecution proved charge of sexual harassment to the victim­girl (P.W.1). 15] To prove the charge against the Accused the prosecution has examined the informant / victim­girl and her 8 Special Case No. 121/2013 (Judgment) mother who are the most material witnesses to prove the charge against the Accused. Informant (P.W.1) and her mother (P.W.2) deposed that they both know the Accused who is staying in their neighbourhood and he knows victim­girl and used to talk with her. Informant / victim­girl (P.W.1) also deposed that her family did not like her talking with accused. Except that neither informant/ victim­girl (P.W.1) nor her mother (P.W.2) stated anything against the accused to prove charge against him. 16] Further the victim­girl (P.W.1) categorically admitted that the accused never harassed her in any manner, Even her mother (P.W.2) admits that she did not like talking of accused with her daughter, therefore, she took her daughter to the police station and lodged complaint against accused, which shows that report was recorded as per dictation of P.W.2 and not according to narration of informant/victim­girl (P.W.1) Further P.W.2 admits that she was afraid that the studies of her daughter might be disturbed due to frequent talking of accused with her daughter and she even gave understanding to the accused and her daughter. But they did not listen, therefore, she lodged the complaint. Thus, it appears that only to prevent the victim­girl from talking with the accused, the report against the accused came to be lodged out of misunderstanding. Thus, there is absolutely no legal evidence on record to prove that accused caused sexual 9 Special Case No. 121/2013 (Judgment) harassment to her by chasing her or by forcing to call him etc. or threatened to kill her brother with intent to cause alarm to them. Further, even considering the evidence of victim­girl the prosecution did not examine the investigating officer and closed their side of evidence. 17] Thus, as the informant and victim­girl both did not support the prosecution case, therefore, there is no iota of evidence against the Accused to prove the charge leveled against him. Thus, prosecution failed to prove that accused caused sexual harassment to victim­girl by holding her hand, forcing calling him on his mobile or roaming her around or threatened her in any manner. Hence, I answer point No.1 to 3 in negative. Therefore, in absence of any evidence against the Accused, he is entitled for acquittal. 18] In the result, I proceed to pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused Jakir Jafar Shaikh is hereby acquitted U/Sec. 235(1) of Cr.P.C. for the offence punishable U/Sec.354­A & 506 of Indian Penal Code and U/s. 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] His bail bonds stand cancelled and sureties are discharged. 10 Special Case No. 121/2013 (Judgment) 3] The Accused is directed to furnish bail bond of the amount of ₹15,000/­ with one solvent surety in the like amount in compliance of provision of section 437­A of Cr.P.C. The judgment is dictated and pronounced in open Court. Date : 30/03/2016. (Ms. U. M. Nandeshwar), Thane Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act),Thane. District Judge ­1 and Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

Satish Digambar Gaikwad at Exh.34, P.W.9 Medical Officer Dr. Sanjay Uttamrao Yamgar at Exh.53 and P.W.10 Dr. Alka Jadhav, Medical Officer of Lokmanya Tilak Municipal General Hospital of Sion at Exh.59. It has come in th evidence that P.W.1 is the mother of the victim. She resides with her five children. The victim aged 6 years is her third daughter. She resides at Koparkhairne, Sector­18 Khadi Kinari, Navi Mumbai. She used to work as a maid servant at neighbouring houses. Usne muze roti khane ko diya or usme ande ka masala dala tha or muze dhamki di ki tune kisi to bataya to tuze dariya mein fek dunga”. Then she had giddiness. 13. The informant has denied the suggestion in her cross examination that her sister had extra marital relation with her husband and there was dispute between them. She denied that her fourth sister's husband did not get any share in her landed property, therefore, false case is filed against accused. In her cross­examination also she has stated what her daughter had told her after she became conscious. She narrated that her daughter told her that “Taklya nana ne mere sath gandha kiya, ande me masala dala, ghar mei bacche the unko bahar nikala and then caught her and committed gandha with her. 14. The victim is aged six years. She has also deposed that she had gone to her aunt's house for watching T.V at her maternal aunt's house. Taklya Nana is the grand father of her aunt's son. Accused put masala in 'anda' and gave her to eat. Then accused seated her on his thigh and committed 'gandha' with her. Accused touched her body and he made her unconscious. P.W.4 Dr. Meenakshi Sawant is the Medical Officer of NMMC Hospital, Vashi. On 28.08.2014 the victim was brought by her mother. The victim was not well oriented as to time and place. Her private part her hymen was torn and there was reddish dis colouration in the vagina indicating some recent injury to the vulva. She took her vaginal swab and blood sample and issued medical certificate Exh.21. There is no admission given by medical officer in her cross examination. 17. P.W.5 Nookrija Begum Mangta Shaikh is the maternal aunt of the victim. She stated that the accused is father­in­law of her younger sister and informant is also her sister. Informant had five children. The victim is her sister's daughter. She stated that the accused, victim and adjoining small children used to come to her house for watching T.V in her house and accused is known as “Taklya Nana”. It has come in the evidence of P.W.5 that on 28.08.2014 she had gone to her work and came at 3.00 p.m. At that time her daughter Amina was ill. So she and Jamirul took her daughter to hospital. While going to hospital she did not lock her hut it was opened. While going to the hospital she saw accused was going to her hut. 18. P.W.7 Shahalam Ranjan Shaikh is the relative of P.W.3 Asadul Shaikh. He had also known to the family of the informant and the victim. On 28.08.2014 he had also come to NMMC Hospital along with Asadul P.W.3 and he also came to know what happened with the victim. 19. P.W.6 Nandkishor Rajendra Goswami is the panch in whose presence on 01.09.2014 the accused gave disclosure statement that he will show the place of incident, statement of the accused is recorded vide Exh.25. It appears thumb impression of accused and his signature and signature of I.O. Accused took police and panchas at Koparkhairne, Sector­19 near one latrine in Zopadpatti in one hut and show the place of incident. It's panchanama is recorded at Exh.26. Then on 02.09.2014 accused again gave disclosure statement to the police that he will show the place where he had kept the intoxicant power packet. His statement was recorded vide Exh.27. It bears thumb impression of accused, his signature and signature of police. Then accused took police and panchas at Koparkhairne Sector­19, near public latrine in one hut. Accused showed the place above the bath room in the hut and produced one plastic bag containing three packets On that packet there were label in Bengali language. One packet was half opened. Packets were seized and sealed in paper packet and prepared its panchanama vide Exh.28. This witness also says that on 30.08.2014 accused was arrested in his presence vide panchanama Exh.29. At that time one full shirt, one lungi was seized from the accused. Nothing is brought on record during cross examination of this witness. No admission is given by this witness. 20. Investigation in C.R.No.268/2014 was done by P.W.8 Satish Digambar Gaikwad. The crime was registered by API Mane, on 29.08.2014 at about 1.35 a.m., I.O recorded statements of witnesses, he searched accused. He found that the accused was missing from the area since the date of incident, FIR was given against unknown person. The victim was admitted in the NMMC Hospital and then she was transferred to Sion Hospital. Medical Officer gave report that victim is not able to speak vide report Exh.35. On 29.08.2014 and 30.08.2014 he sent blood swab, annal swab, vaginal swab etc., of the victim to FSL, Kalina vide his letters Exh.36 and 37. He arrested the accused on 30.08.2014. Accused produced his shirt and lungi it was seized by preparing panchanama and it was sealed in presence of panchas. He deposited those clothes in the police station vide receipt Exh.38. He sent accused for medical examination on 30.08.2014 vide his letter Exh.39. On 31.08.2014 stomach wash of the victim was sent to FSL Kalina vide his letter Exh.40. On 31.08.2014 he sent the blood sample, pubic hair, nail, semen of the accused to FSL Kalina by his letter vide Exh.41. 21. Investigating Officer further stated that on 31.08.2014 the victim was not in condition to speak. On 01.09.2014 the accused gave disclosure statement that he will show the place of incident and accordingly his statement was recorded and panchanama of the spot was drawn. On 02.09.2014 again accused gave another disclosure statement that he will show the place where he had concealed the packets of powder which was mixed in the 'anda bhurji' and gave it to the victim. Accordingly his statement was recorded and seizure panchanama of the packets were done. 22. The Investigating Officer further deposed that on 10.09.2014 the victim was discharged from hospital, but doctor told him that the victim was not mentally stable, therefore, not to inquire her immediately and she should be inquired after 10­ 15 days. So on 30.09.2014 the statement of the victim was recorded by woman police officer in presence of Mahila Dakshata Committee Member Vaishali Ghorpade and her mother. 23. Investigating Officer sent packets of intoxicant powder to FSL by his letter vide Exh.46. On 10.09.2014 he sent letter to Din of Sion Hospital about issuing certificate of injuries caused to victim's private part vide his letter Exh.47. On 07.11.2014 he sent four bottles of stomach wash of the victim to FSL Kalina vide his letter Exh.49. In the cross­examination of the Investigating Officer no any suggestion is given and no admission is given by Investigating Officer. 24. The accused was examined by P.W.9 Dr.Sanjay Uttamrao Yamghar of NMMC Hospital, Vashi. On 30.08.2014 he gave report vide Exh.54 that there is nothing to suggest that he is impotent. 25. The prosecution examined P.W.10 Dr. Alka Jadhav, Medical Officer of Lokmanya Tilak Municipal General Hospital, Sion. She deposed that the victim admitted on 29.08.2014 and discharged on 10.09.2014. The victim was transferred from NMMC Hospital, Vashi to their hospital. It was a case of Orgono Phosphorus Poisoning and sexual assault. The condition of the victim was very serious and she was unconscious. Her pupils were small pin point. She had low blood pressure and fast heart rate. Her Coma score was 3 X 15. It was suggestive of Orgono Phosphorus Poisoning. To confirm this finding they sent blood for ACH level which came low conferring our diagnosis of Orgono Phosphorus poisoning. On general examination there were no external injury mark present, but on genital examination there was a verbal edema and redness. Hymen was ruptured suggestive of penetrative sexual abuse. Child was kept on ventilator for 48 hours. After 48 hours her repeat ACH level was normal. Child recovered well and discharged on 10th September 2014. Before discharge the psychiatric reference and NGO reference was taken. Respective samples were sent for FSL. She gave report vide Exh.61. 26. The C.A report of blood vaginal swab of victim is at Exh.62 vide MLC No.B­5510/14. It was reported that blood is haemolysed hence unsuitable for blood grouping. No semen is detected on vaginal swab. 27. The C.A report of three blood samples of victim vide report Exh.63 vide MLC No.B­5540/14. It was reported that blood group is of 'B'. 28. The C.A report of Perineal swab, vaginal swab, anal swab and oral swab of the victim vide MLC report No.B­ 5539/14 is at Exh.64. All these samples were referred to DNA. 29. The C.A report of Pubic hair, nail clipping, blood, semen of the accused, its C.A report is at Exh.65 vide MLC No.B­5538/14. It is reported that the blood group is of 'AB' and nail clipping, pubic hair were referred to DNA. 30. C.A report of full shirt and lungi of the accused is at Exh.66 vide MLCNo.B­5537/14. It is reported that the lungi has four semen stains of 1 cm in diameter at one side middle portion. Semen is of human and its group is inconclusive. 31. I heard Ld. Counsel on behalf of accused and Ld. APP. The Counsel on behalf of the accused argued that false case is made against the accused only because the accused has not given any share in his property to the informant's sister's husband. He further argued that accused was with his wife at the time of incident and therefore there were semen stains on his lungi. He submitted that the hymen can be ruptured by itching only. He submitted that victim is 6 years old, if she is raped more injury would have been caused. So according to him, accused was arrested on suspicion. He submitted that panch witness is habitual witness. 32. The argument of Ld. Counsel for the accused is not considerable because no documents are produced about any property dispute. It appears that the suggestions are given without any substance. The accused has not examined his wife to state he was with his wife at the time of incident, therefore, there are semen stains on his lungi. Therefore, this submission is also not considerable. The medical officer has denied that the hymen can be ruptured only because of itching therefore this submission is also not considerable. The Counsel submitted that if the 6 years old girl is raped then more injury on private part would have been caused. In this respect the injury on private part of victim is mentioned in the report Exh.21 and 61 more or less injury is not significant. 33. Ld. APP submitted that the case of the prosecution is proved beyond all doubt and evidence of sole testimony of the victim is found reliable and trustworthy. No corroboration is required. In this case victim's testimony is corroborated by mother and doctor. It is heinous crime. Intoxicant drug administered by accused to victim. The victim was taken name of accused and identified him before the court. Therefore, there is no doubt that accused has committed offence. 34. Ld. A.P.P. relied upon the decision in case of Hakkim V/s. State of Tamil Nadu 2017 ALLMR (Cri) 329. It was the case of aggravated penetrative sexual assault upon a minor victim aged 12 years. As per the medical evidence there was absence of spermotzoa in vaginal smear of victim. It was held that the victim stated only about penetration and not about ejaculation of semen by accused. Therefore, there is no chance for any semen being present in vaginal smear. Even assuming that there was ejaculation, victim was examined after five days due to passing of urine or washing. Semen would have been washed off. Therefore, absence of spermatozoa in vaginal smear would not go to create any doubt in the case. 35. In another case Vijay @ Chinee V/s. State of Madhya Pradesh (2010)8 Supreme Court cases 191. It was held that in case of rape conviction on sole testimony of prosecutrix held statement of the prosecutrix, if found to be worthy of credence and reliable, requires no corroboration. Court may convict the accused on the sole testimony of the prosecutrix. 36. In the case at the hands it is proved by the prosecution that the accused is father­in­law of the informant's younger sister and he resides in the neighbouring hut. Accused is relative of the informant The victim used to go her aunt's house for watching T.V. On the day of incident victim had gone to her aunt's house for watching T.V. At that time accused had also gone there. P.W.5 Nookrija Begum had seen accused while going to her hut in the afternoon when she was going to take her daughter to hospital. 37. It is proved by the prosecution that victim came back home at about 8.00p.m. and she immediately felled down and became unconscious. She was taken to hospital immediately. On the medical examination doctor told that she was raped, her private part is injured and bleeding and some intoxicant is administered to her. 38. It is proved by the prosecution that the FIR was lodged on 29.08.2014 at about 1.35 a.m., i.e. after mid­night against unknown person. Investigating Officer found that accused was went missing from that area after incident so he searched and arrested him on 30.08.2014. Accused gave disclosure statement an admitted guilt that he has committed wrong with the victim and became ready to show place of incident. Accordingly he showed same place which was adjacent hut of the informant's sister. In respect of place of incident it is corroborated by P.W.1 and P.W.5 where the victim used to go to watch T.V. Thereafter accused gave another disclosure statement and he showed the place where he had concealed intoxicant powder. The three packets were produced by the accused containing some Bengali language wrapper. Investigating Officer seized that, one packet was half opened. Investigating Officer has sent those packets to FSL, Kalina, but unfortunately it's FSL report is not received. 39. The statement of accused is relevant and admissible under section 27 of Evidence Act. It is discovered where the incident took place and where the accused had concealed the packets of the powder. 40. From the evidence of victim it is evident that she had gone to her aunt's house for watching T.V. At that time adjoining children were there. Accused Taklya Nana was also there. Accused driven out all other children and gave masala in the 'anda bhurji' and gave it to the victim to eat. After having it accused seated her on his thighs and committed wrong with her. The victim had narrated this incident in her own word as 'Gandha'. Accused also threatened her not to disclose it, otherwise he will throw her in the 'dariya'. The evidence of the victim is corroborated by her mother P.W.1. 41. It is evident from the evidence of P.W.10 Dr. Alka Jadhav that victim's condition was very serious and she was on ventilator for 48 hours and it was confirmed that it was a case of Orgno Phosphorus poisoning and of sexual assault. The report of the Medical Officer vide Exh.61 discloses that the penetrative sexual assault and Orgono Phosphorus poisoning was administered upon the victim. 42. Though there is no FSL report about the contents in the packet which are seized at the instance of accused, but if we link the medical report Exh.61 with the evidence of victim and the recovery of the packets at the instance of accused under section 27 it will prove beyond doubt that the contents in the packet must have orgono photographs poisoning because the victim says that accused mixed some 'masala' in 'anda bhurji' and gave to her and after that she went in giddiness. After that she did not realize what happened with her. After the incident she came back to her house, she felled down and became unconscious. Doctor gave treatment and gave stomach wash. So considering the medical report Exh.61 and evidence of P.W.2 the victim , it proves that accused had mixed powder in the packets which were seized from him and that powder containing orgono photographs poisoning. 43. It is proved from the C.A report Exh.66 that there were four semen stains on the lungi which was seized from the accused at the time of his arrest on 30.08.2014. The victim has not stated in her evidence whether there was ejaculation or not, but there may be possibility of ejaculation of the accused at the time of incident. The medical report Exh.21 given by NMMC Vashi Hospital, is also very relevant. It shows that there was recent injury to her vagina and opinion of sexual intercourse was given by the doctor. 44. There is no admission, no contradictions, no omission proved in the evidence of any of the witnesses. There is no reason made out to disbelieve the witnesses. There is no enmity with the accused and the informant and witnesses , so there is no reason to depose false against the accused. All the witnesses found trustworthy, reliable and natural. 45. The statement of accused under section 313 of Cr. P.C., vide Exh.62 can be taken into consideration as the additional incriminating circumstances against the accused because accused has admitted what is relation between informant and him. He admits that there he was residing in the neighbouring hut of the informant and he admits that he used to go to the house of Nookrija for watching T.V. where victim and other children were also come there. The victim has deposed that she had gone to her aunt's house for watching T.V and accused had come there and did wrong with her. So answers given by the accused in his statement under section 313of Cr. P.C., can be used as additional incriminating circumstances against him in consonance with the evidence of the victim and other witnesses. 46. As per the provisions under section 29 and 30 of the POCSO Act, 2012 the presumptions are in favour of the prosecution. In view of the proved circumstances on record the presumptions are required tobe rebutted by the accused. But the accused has failed to rebut those presumptions. 47. I come to the conclusion that the prosecution has proved beyond doubt the ingredients of the offence under section 376 of Indian Penal Code read with section 5 of the POCSo Act. It is proved by the prosecution that the victim's private part i.e. hymen is ruptured, there was fresh injury reddish in colour. So there is no doubt that the accused has committed penetrative sexual assault upon the victim. Therefore, the ingredients of offence under section 376 read with section 6 of the POCSO Act is proved beyond doubt. The victim was six years old at the time of incident. So ingredients of the offence under section 5(m) penetrative sexual assault upon a child below 12 years is proved by the prosecution. Hence, the ingredients of the offence under section 5 (m) punishable under section 6 of the POCSO Act is proved by the prosecution. 48. Accused is also charged for the offence under section 328 of Indian Penal Code. It is proved by the prosecution that from the medical report Exh.61 that it was the case of Orgono photographs poisoning and some packets of powder having Bengali wrapper seized from the accused, so there is no doubt that the accused had administered poisonous substance. Therefore, it is proved that the accused had administered intoxicant drug in the food of the victim with intent to facilitate him to commit offence. The victim goes in giddiness and then it was facilitated the accused to commit penetrative sexual assault upon her. So ingredients of the offence under section 328 of Indian Penal Code are also proved beyond doubt by the prosecution. 49. It is proved by the prosecution beyond doubt that accused has threatened the victim not to disclose the incident, otherwise he will throw her in 'dariya'. Therefore, the prosecution also proved ingredients of the offence under section 506 of Indian Penal Code. 50. The accused is also charged for the offence under section 377 of Indian Penal Code i.e. unnatural offence i.e. carnal intercourse against the order of nature. However, victim has not narrated in respect of any carnal intercourse is committed against the order of nature with her, therefore, I do not find that the ingredients of this offence is proved by the prosecution. 51. The accused is liable to punish for the offence punishable under section 376, 328, 506 of Indian Penal Code and section 5(m) punishable under section 6 of the POCSO Act. Date­08/02/2018. (S.C. Khalipe) Thane. Additional Sessions Judge, Thane. 52. Today the accused is produced before the court from jail authority. His Advocate Shri.O.P. Singh and Ld. APP are present. 53. Heard accused on point of sentence. He has submitted that he do not know anything. His Advocate submitted that accused is in jail for last three and half years, therefore, set off be given. 54. Ld. A.P.P. Smt.Hiwrale submitted that the offences are proved beyond doubt, therefore, accused may be convicted with maximum punishment. 55. Considering the nature of offence I found following aggravated circumstances that:­ ­ The accused has committed heinous crime upon a girl of 6 years old by administering poison to her in anda bhurji and made her unconscious and did the penetrative sexual assault. The victim was on ventilator for 48 hours and admitted for 13 days in the hospital. She was very serious and only because the proper and immediate treatment was given she could have survive. The victim has no reason to depose false against the accused. She has identified the accused before the court and also stated his name in her statement before the police. 56. I did not find any mitigating circumstance for taking lenient view in this case. The accused is at present 56 years old is not a mitigating factor. 57. Considering the nature of offence I am of the view that accused is liable to be punished with maximum sentence and with fine and the fine amount is liable to be paid to the victim's mother as compensation and I found that the fine amount is not an adequate compensation, therefore, the District Legal Services Authority is requested to give adequate compensation to the victim's mother as per rules. I pass following order of sentence which is sufficient for ends of justice. ORDER 1. Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­006758­2016 Special (POCSO) Case No. 255/16 Received on : 14.10.2016 Registered on : 14.10.2016 Decided on : 27.07.2018 Duration : 1Y.9Ms.13Ds. IN THE COURT OF D.J.­1 & ADDL. SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE (Presided over by Hemant M. Patwardhan) Special (POCSO) Case No.255/16 Exh.No. 1.State of Maharashtra. ( Ganeshpuri Police station, Bhiwandi) ..Complainant V/s. 1.Sanjay Chandrakant Medha. Age : 22 years, R/at. Usgaon Bandhara, Post Ganeshpuri, Tal. Bhiwandi, Dist. Thane ..Accused Appearance:­ APP Shri. Londhe for the State. Advocate Mrs. Aarote for the accused. JUDGMENT (Delivered on this 27th day of July 2018 ) Accused Sanjay Medha was facing trial under sections 354, 323, 504, 506 of IPC read with sections 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 on following facts:­ 1 to 11 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­006758­2016 Special (POCSO) Case No. 255/16 1] That on 05.06.2016 at about 17.00 hrs. on road of Usgaon to Usgaon Badhara, Near Moravi,Usgaon, Post Ganeshpuri, Tal. Bhiwandi, Dist. Thane within the jurisdiction of Ganeshpuri Police station, Bhiwandi accused used criminal force to complainant intending to outrage her modesty and then has voluntarily caused hurt to complainant and at the same time has given provocation to complainant and prosecution witnesses to break public peace and also committed offence of criminal intimidation. According to prosecution accused on aforesaid date, time and place has also committed sexual assault on the complainant. Hence, on complaint lodged by complainant, an offence punishable under aforesaid sections came to be registered against accused. On completion of investigation he was charge­sheeted. 2] My learned predecessor was pleased to frame charge below Exh.2 and has certified that contents of said charge were read over and explained to accused in vernacular. Accused pleaded not guilty and claim to be tried. His defence was of false implication on the ground of various quarrels between him and maternal uncle of the victim on the ground of theft of electricity by said maternal uncle from D.P. of accused. 3] Prosecution has then examined victim, grandmother of the victim, maternal uncle of victim, panch witness Sainath 2 to 11 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­006758­2016 Special (POCSO) Case No. 255/16 Bhoir, I.O. Arjun Shelke, another I.O. Kundan Jadhav etc. as witness no.1 to 6 respectively. Then statement of accused was recorded as per his say wherein he has categorically stated that he did not commit any offence. Arguments of rival advocates were heard. Learned P.P. has categorically pointed out that victim, her relatives have categorically substantiated allegations that accused has not only used criminal force with intention of outraging modesty but at the same time has committed offence of provocation to witnesses and criminal intimidation by giving threats to them. According to learned P.P. as the victim was minor at relevant time of incident, in addition to prosecution under IPC sections, he was also prosecuted for committing sexual assaults on victim under POCSO. According to learned P.P. even said witnesses have not only deposed about the allegations under IPC but have deposed as per allegations of prosecution under POCSO Act. Having regards to corroboration of witness no.1 to 3 their statements has to be accepted. According to learned P.P. though some defence of theft of electricity has been raised by accused, as the witnesses have denied all said facts, the same can be easily discarded. Hence, according to learned P.P. accused is require to be convicted on the basis of said depositions. 4] Per contra, learned advocate of accused has categorically pointed out that all the three witnesses have made 3 to 11 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­006758­2016 Special (POCSO) Case No. 255/16 contradictory statements in respect of alleged act of the accused. It was then pointed out that statement of the victim before police and under section 164 of Cr.P.C. is also contradictory and above all she did not make any allegations against accused about assault, provocation, criminal intimidation against her. Thus, contradictions in the statement of witnesses itself are sufficient to discard her evidence. According to submissions there was rivalry between the parties as maternal uncle of victim used to commit theft of electricity from D.P. used by the accused for providing electricity to his house and in order to avoid any action by accused against maternal uncle, this complaint was lodged. Hence, defence has requested to acquit the accused. 5] On the basis of aforesaid rival arguments, following points arose for my consideration and I record my findings against each of them for the reasons noted below :­ Sr.N. Points Findings 1] Does the prosecution prove that accused on 05.06.2016 at ..Negative. about 17.00 hrs. on road of Usgaon to Usgaon Badhara, Near Moravi,Usgaon, Post Ganeshpuri, Tal. Bhiwandi, Dist. Thane within the jurisdiction of Ganeshpuri Police station, Bhiwandi used criminal force to complainant­victim, a minor aged 16 years intending to outrage her modesty and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 354 of Indian Penal Code ? 2] Does the prosecution prove that on aforesaid date, time and ..Negative. place accused voluntarily caused hut to complainant­victim, a minor aged 16 years and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 323 of Indian Penal Code? 4 to 11 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­006758­2016 Special (POCSO) Case No. 255/16 3] Does the prosecution prove that accused on aforesaid date, time ..Negative. and place intentionally insulted the complainant­victim, a minor aged 16 years and prosecution witness, by abusing them in filthy language and thereby gave provocation to them to break public peace and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 504 of Indian Penal Code? 4] Does the prosecution prove that accused on aforesaid date, time ..Negative. and place committed criminal intimidation by threatening to complainant­victim, a minor aged 16 years and as such thereby committed an offence punishable under section 506 of Indian Penal Code? 5] Does the prosecution prove that accused on aforesaid date, time ..Negative. and place accused committed sexual assault on complainant­ victim, a minor aged 16 years and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act? 6] What order? Accused is acquitted as per final order. REASONS As to point no.1 to 6 :­ 6] All these points are interlinked with each other and are considered at once. Prosecution has alleged that accused has used criminal force with intention of outraging modesty. The complainant has initially made allegations against accused also of committing assault, provocation and criminal intimidation against her. Accordingly, it appears that my learned Predecessor has framed charge. Learned Public Prosecutor has argued that witness no.1 to 3 have corroborated each other's version, the same is sufficient to convict the accused. However, on perusal of the record, it is apparent that 5 to 11 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­006758­2016 Special (POCSO) Case No. 255/16 said three witnesses who are material witnesses of prosecution have made contradictory statements. Initially allegation of the complainant when her statement under section 164 of Cr.P.C. was recorded by learned Magistrate was that accused has used criminal force for outraging her modesty by holding her hand and by uttering the word 'I like you'. According to prosecution she was then made allegations of assaults by the accused on her person while her said statement was recorded by learned Magistrate. She has only made allegation that accused has threatened her maternal uncle during her said statement. However, in the substantive evidence before the court, she has alleged that accused has used criminal force against her for outraging her modesty by holding her hands and by uttering the words 'I like you'. Except the said act she did not make any allegation either about assault or about criminal intimidation, provocation etc. against her by the accused at the relevant time. On the contrary she has categorically made reference of assault, provocation and abuses being given to her maternal uncle by the accused when her maternal uncle had asked the accused as to why he has hold the hand of the victim. Thus, there appears to be contradictory statements made by the witnesses and victim herself both in statement before police, statement before magistrate and in substantive evidence before this court. Thus, the court is required to look for corroboration 6 to 11 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­006758­2016 Special (POCSO) Case No. 255/16 to said fact in order to conclude that prosecution has established the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt. 7] In order to corroborate the version of victim, her grand mother and maternal uncle were examined. Before scrutinizing their evidence court has to consider the facts which were brought on record by spot panchanama and deposition of panch witness. Panch witness has categorically supported the prosecution and has proved contents of panchanama Exh.18. On perusal of said Exh.18 it is apparent that the house of the complainant is at far distance from the spot and even house of Nima Bhoir and other persons are situated not less than 40 feet away from the spot of incident. Therefore, even if we consider the fact as deposed by the victim that after the accused had held her hand she shouted in the name of grandmother PW2 as it is then if we consider distance between the spot of incident and house of victim then it is highly improbable that shouts of victim girl could reach to her own house which is situated at far distance from the spot of incident and then her grandmother could immediately approached the spot. Hence, though distance between the spot and house of victim is not categorically brought on record by the defence, it can be inferred from the sketch prepared by police. Therefore, if said distance is considered then all said allegations 7 to 11 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­006758­2016 Special (POCSO) Case No. 255/16 of victim that immediately after hearing shouts, her grandmother approached the spot or reached the spot nowhere appears trustworthy. Needless to mention that when neighbourers are at the distance of 40 feet could not hear shouts of victim, it is difficult to say that her grandmother residing far away from the spot could hear her shouts. Hence, that facts itself create suspicion about occurrence of the incident at the relevant time. 8] On the background of said fact, if deposition of grandmother is considered then she has only stated that when she reached the spot she has seen the accused near the victim. She did not utter anything about act of the accused in her presence. Thus, she cannot be termed as eye witness of the incident. She has also nowhere claims that her nephew Sachin had informed her about either assault or act of criminal intimidation by the accused. Thus, when it is nowhere claim of Sachin that he had informed PW2 about the said act then all the avernments made by her about that by PW2 create doubt about her presence either immediately on the spot or about her becoming aware of incident occurred with her nephew Sachin. 9] On perusal of deposition of Sachin i.e. maternal uncle of victim it is apparent that he has deposed that accused had slapped him only. Said witness did not make any whisper 8 to 11 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­006758­2016 Special (POCSO) Case No. 255/16 of either any act of provocation or criminal intimidation by the accused person. Thus, the allegations against accused about provocation, criminal intimidation etc. nowhere substantiated by the depositions of PW2 and 3. Needless to mention that in statement under section 164 the victim has alleged that she herself was assaulted and the act of provocation, criminal intimidation etc. was attempted against her itself. Thus, it is apparent that victim has changed her version time and again which does not corroborate by the material witnesses PW2 and 3 or circumstances brought by Exh.18 on record. Having regards to said facts, evidence being inconsistent and unreliable is certainly not sufficient to establish guilt of accused beyond reasonable doubt. 10] In the present matter accused has categorically raised the defence of false implication on the ground of his rivalry with maternal uncle of on the ground of theft of electricity. Though there is no documentary evidence to that effect he has succeeded in proving the fact that said witness by name Sachin is in habit of committing theft of electricity. Said fact is also admitted by victim etc. Having regards to the said fact admission of victim about theft of electricity when consider along with defence of accused said appears to be more probable than that of allegations made against him. When defence appears to be more probable, his further avernments 9 to 11 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­006758­2016 Special (POCSO) Case No. 255/16 that in order to avoid action being initiated by him, false complaint is filed through victim appears to be more probable. Needless to mention that material witness, maternal uncle of victim Sachin has admitted that when alleged incident occurred he was accompanied with his 4 to 5 friends. However, none of them were examined to substantiate the evidence and further it is highly improbable that accused alone will dare to slap a person having surrounded by his 4 to 5 friends. Therefore, all said allegations also apparently concocted and appears to have been made just to implicate accused in the case. Therefore, I do not find evidence of the prosecution trustworthy to held the accused guilty of the offence. I therefore, discard the evidence of prosecution as unreliable, untrustworthy and improbable. Hence, I record my findings against point no.1 to 5 in negative and proceed to pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused is acquitted from the offence punishable under sections 354, 323, 504, 506 of IPC read with sections 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] Bail bond of accused shall stands canceled. 10 to 11 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­006758­2016 Special (POCSO) Case No. 255/16 3] Accused is directed to execute P.R. and S.B. of Rs.10,000/­ as per amended provisions of section 437(A) of Cr.P.C. and bonds so executed shall remain in force for the period of six months from the date of its execution. 4] Proceeding is accordingly closed. Thane (Hemant M.Patwardhan) Date: 27.07.2018 D.J.­1 & Additional Sessions Judge, Thane 11 to 11

CNR No. MHTH01­006799­2013 :JUDGMENT: (Delivered on 5th day of May, 2018) 1] The accused is tried for the offence punishable under Sec.354 of IPC and Sec. 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 for having been committed offence of outraging modesty of victim girl and sexually assaulted her. 2] Case of prosecution, in brief, is as under : The victim girl went to attend Dahihandi function in Sector No.10, at around 9.30 p.m. There was crowd and people were watching Dahihandi. The accused came closed to her, lifted her cousin sister on his shoulder, pulled the T­shirt of victim girl up and moved hand over her breast and tried to open the chain of her pant. The girl alarmed. Her family members came to rescue her. The accused was from Bombay Central Govinda Pathak. FIR lodged by Sanjana Parab, the mother of victim. 3] On receipt of information, offence bearing C.R.No.I­234/2013 registered under Sec.354 of IPC and S. 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Accused was arrested on . Investigation was carried out by PSI Wagh. Investigating officer went to spot and prepared spot panchanama in presence of panchas. He recorded statements of witnesses. On finding substance in the accusations, investigating officer filed charge sheet in the Court. 4] This Court has heard Ld. Advocate for accused and Ld. A.P.P. for the State and framed charge against the accused ( Exh. 02) for the offence under Sec. 354 of IPC and Sec. 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual 3 Spl.Case (Pocso) No.122/2013... Jud. CNR No. MHTH01­006799­2013 Offences Act, 2012. The contents of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 5] The defence of the accused as constructed in his statement u/sec. 313 Cr.P.C is of total denial. 6] The prosecution examined in all five witnesses. Those are victim girl ( P.W.2), her mother Sanjana Parab ( P.W.1), maternal uncle of victim girl named Ravindra Sawant (P.W.3), API Atish Wagh (P.W.4) is investigating officer and Suresh Mallav (P.W.5) is also investigating officer who took up further investigation. Statement of accused is recorded. He has denied involvement in the offence. 7] The following points arise for my determination with my findings thereon for reasons to follow: POINTS FINDINGS 01. Does the prosecution prove that on ...In the affirmative. 29.08.2013, at about 9.30 p.m., at Sector­10, Nerul, Navi Mumbai, accused used criminal force with intention to outrage the modesty of victim girl aged 12 years ? 02. Does prosecution prove that on the aforesaid ...In the negative. date, time and place, the accused, sexually assaulted the victim girl by raising the T­shirt and touching the breast with sexual intent? 03 What order ? Accused is convicted as per final order. 4 Spl.Case (Pocso) No.122/2013... Jud. CNR No. MHTH01­006799­2013 REASONS AS TO POINT NOS.1 TO 3: 8] Victim girl (P.W.2) deposed that on 29.08.2013 they went to see Gokulashtami festival. Rajesh Bhor organized Dahihandi at sector­10, Nerul. It has come in evidence of Sanjana (P.W.1) and Ravindra Sawant (P.W.3) that victim girl was standing at some distance and Ravindra (P.W.3) was standing along with his friends. There was group from Bombay Central to break dahihandi. Victim girl deposed that accused come close to her. She was standing on a step near the shop with her younger cousin on her shoulder. Accused climbed on that step. The accused took her cousin on his shoulder. Victim girl stated that accused pulled her T­shirt up and touched her breast and even tried to open the chain of her pant. P.W.2 victim girl shouted. However, there was loud sound. Accused handed over her cousin to her and ran away. Sanjana (P.W.1) and Ravindra Sawant (P.W.3) deposed that victim girl told that accused molested her. Ravindra (P.W.3 ) has spotted the accused. The accused was identified by Sanjana (P.W.1), her brother Ravindra (P.W.3) and victim girl (P.W.2). 9] Atish Wagh (P.W.4) has taken down complaint of Sanjana (P.W.1). He registered offence under Sec. 354 of Indian Penal Code and Sec. 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. Investigating Officer visited the spot and prepared spot panchanama Exh.23 ( Admitted by accused ). Shri. Mallav ( P.W.5 ) deposed that he recorded statement of witnesses on 02.09.2013. 10] The accused was in the team of Bombay Central. It is tried to demonstrate that accused had no concern with the girl. There was crowd. 5 Spl.Case (Pocso) No.122/2013... Jud. CNR No. MHTH01­006799­2013 People were standing on all sides. The girl was a minor studying in 10 th standard. Her birth date is not disputed by the accused. The stage was at a distance of hardly 2 minutes walking. The girl went to the stage along with her mother . They were on stage for about 5 to 10 minutes. There were 100 to 150 peoples. DJ music was also playing loudly. It is tried to demonstrate that girl could not identify accused as there was big crowd. Since the girl has seen the accused while lifting her cousin, there is no scope for mistaken identity. 11] It has come in evidence of victim girl that the boys of Bombay Central Govinda players left the spot while she went to inform about the incident. It is tried to demonstrate that T­shirt and shorts is the common dress for the pathaks. The fact remains that the girl has identified the accused by face. It is strongly contended that there was no identification parade, but the victim girl herself had shown the accused to her uncle Ravindra (P.W.3) and he nabbed the accused on the spot. So, there is no question of identification. It is strongly contended that when the accused was nabbed then why he was arrested after some time. Investigation officer (P.W. 5) has stated that he has examined accused about the hole in ear. He has not seized earrings from the accused. There was no seizure but, it does not go to the root of the crime when girl identified the accused at the very moment of incident. 12] The girl has stated that accused had lifted her cousin on his shoulder. The accused climbed up one step. There was a crowd. They were close to the stage. The accused was behind the girl and pulled her T­shirt up . The fact remains that whether accused had gone to touch her breast and tried to open chain of her pant. There was crowd and everyone was close. There was no space for the accused to go ahead of the girl by holding a little girl on 6 Spl.Case (Pocso) No.122/2013... Jud. CNR No. MHTH01­006799­2013 his shoulder. The accused must have pushed her while holding a little girl on his shoulder. So, it can only be accepted that accused pulled the victim girl from backside with intent to outrage her modesty. But, it is not established that he had moved his hand over her breast. So, only offence u/sec. 354 of Indian Penal code is made out against accused. Hence, I answer point No.1 in the affirmative and point No.2 in the negative. Here, I take pause to hear the accused on the point of sentence. 13] I have heard accused in person and Ld. Advocate for accused. I also heard Ld. A.P.P. Shri. Londhe. The accused submitted that he is married now and had one son who is no more. Leniency may be shown to him. Ld. A.P.P. Shri. Londhe submitted that the offence is serious. Victim girl is minor and if he is acquitted, wrong message will go in the society. So, leniency should not be shown. Considering the age of the accused and the depth of offence, I find it just to pass following order: ORDER 1] Accused Pravin Rajaram Makwana is hereby convicted under Sec. 235(2) of Code of Criminal Procedure of offence u/s. 354 of Indian Penal Code. 2] Accused is sentenced till rising of the Court and he shall pay fine of Rs. 500/­ i.d. to suffer simple imprisonment for fifteen days. 3] Accused Pravin Rajaram Makwana is hereby acquitted under Sec. 235(1) of Code of Criminal Procedure of offence 7 Spl.Case (Pocso) No.122/2013... Jud. CNR No. MHTH01­006799­2013 u/s. 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 4] He shall surrender his bail bonds. 5] Copy of this judgment be given to the accused free of cost. 6] Pronounced and dictated in open court.
