Mr.G.B.Chavan for the accused at length. 28] Ld. D.G.P. Mrs. Phad has submitted that the age of the victim has not been challenged. It is not disputed that victim was 5 yrs. old at the time of the commission of the offence. She has submitted that P.W.1 is the mother of the victim and in the F.I.R. itself the name of the accused is mentioned. Therefore, there is no question of identification of the accused. He was admittedly a neighbour and it is not challenged at all that the victim and her mother knew the accused and vice­versa. The accused was alone at home at the time of commission of the offence and he closed the door of the house and committed the offence. She has submitted that P.W.1 has categorically deposed about what the victim has deposed. They therefore corroborate each­other's testimony. 29] Since the victim was very young and was crying inconsolably, her evidence was recorded in chamber after the judge comforted her and she was asked to sit in her mother's lap. Considering her age and trauma, certain leading questions were put to her by the Ld. D.G.P. However, she has on her own deposed about the act of sexual assault by the accused. She has categorically deposed about the nature and manner of sexual assault. The deposition of the victim is very­well corroborated by the testimony of 12 Spl. Case No. 123/2013 (Judgment) P.W.3 Baby Nanda Gaikwad, member of District Women Cell, who has categorically deposed that the minor victim's statement was recorded in her presence. This statement of the victim is very­well corroborated by her testimony as well as by the testimony of P.W.1. Although the medical officer P.W.5 has deposed that the hymen of the victim was intact, however, the case is not of penetrative sexual assault, but of fondling of genitals and of making the young child hold the penis of the accused in her hand. 30] Ld.D.G.P.Mrs.Phad has submitted that the accused has not rebutted the presumption under the P.O.C.S.O. Act and that there is no reason whatsoever for the minor victim and her mother to implicate the accused falsely in such an offence. She has submitted that visibly the victim was deeply traumatized by the sexual assault and that the said assault has had an adverse mental impact on the child. She has submitted that language of Sec.7 of the P.O.C.S.O. Act is very clear that whosoever with sexual intent touches the vagina, penis, anus or breast of the child or makes the child touch the vagina, penis anus or breast of such person or any other person, or does any other Act with sexual intent which involves physical contact without penetration is said to commit sexual assault. She has submitted that in the present case, it is obvious that the accused had sexual intent towards the minor victim, who was just a little child. It has been proved by the prosecution by the testimony of P.W.1,2 & 4 that the accused touched her vagina and also made the child touch his penis. She has submitted that the prosecution has thus proved its case beyond reasonable doubt. 31] Per contra, Ld. Adv. Mr. G. B. Chavan for the accused has submitted that the accused was residing in a small house admeasuring only 6 ft. x 10 ft. He has submitted that all the women 13 Spl. Case No. 123/2013 (Judgment) of his house are working and therefore it was not possible for the accused to commit the offence in his own house. He has submitted that the chawl is a thickly populated area and as such it is not possible to commit the offence in a chawl. Chanda Gavhankar with whom the complainant used to admittedly leave her daughters with, has not been examined. The statement of the child may be a creation of the police. The I.O. has deposed in his cross­examination that he does not even know as to who resides in the house of the accused. The child being young can be easily tutored or coerced. Therefore, her testimony can not be relied upon. In order to buttress his contention further , he has placed reliance upon the following two citations : i) K.Venkateshwarlu V/s. State of U.P., reported in AIR 2012 Supreme Court 2055. In this matter it has been held that a child witness, by reason of his tender age, is a pliable witness, He can be tutored easily either by threat,coercion or inducement. Therefore, the Court must be satisfied that the attendant circumstances do not show that the child was acting under the influence of someone or was under threat or coercion. Evidence of a child witness can be relied upon if the Court, with its expertise and ability to evaluate the evidence, comes to the conclusion that the child is not tutored and his evidence has a ring of truth. It is safe and prudent to look for corroboration for evidence of a child witness from the other evidence on record, because while giving evidence a child may give scope to his imagination and exaggerate his version or may develop cold feet and not tell the truth or may repeat what he has been asked to say not knowing the consequences of his deposition in the Court. Careful evaluation of the evidence of a child witness in the background and context of other evidence on record is a must before the Court decides to rely upon it . 14 Spl. Case No. 123/2013 (Judgment) ii) Jagannath V/s. State. reported in AIR 1952 Rajasthan 153. In this matter it has been held that Children witnesses are risky as they often mistake dreams for reality, repeat glibly as of their own knowledge what they have heard from others and are greatly influenced by fear of punishment, by hope of reward and by desire of notoriety. It is necessary for a Court before examining a child of tender years as witness to satisfy itself that the child is sufficiently intellectually developed to comprehend what he has seen and to give an intelligent account of it to the Court. If the Court is of the opinion that by reason of tender years or defective or immature understanding, the child could not have perceived the particular incident to prove which he is produced as a witness, the Court should not only refrain from administering the oath to him but should also decline to examine him as a witness. 32] I have given anxious consideration to the arguments advanced by both the Ld. Advocates and have also perused the entire material on record. The victim was a small child of 5 yrs at the time of the commission of the offence. Her age has not been challenged by the defence . P.W.1 is the mother of the victim and in the F.I.R. itself the name of the accused is mentioned. Therefore, there is no question of identification of the accused. He was admittedly a neighbour (admitted even in staement U/Sec.313 of Cr.P.C. of the accused) and it is not challenged at all that the victim and her mother knew the accused and vice­versa. The accused was alone at home at the time of commission of the offence and he closed the door of the house and committed the offence. P.W.1 has categorically deposed about the incident as narrated by the victim. They corroborate each other's testimony. 15 Spl. Case No. 123/2013 (Judgment) 33] Since the victim was very young and was visibly traumatized, her evidence was recorded in chambers after comforting her and by allowing her to sit on her mother's lap. Considering her age and inconsolable crying, when the Ld.D.G.P. put certain leading questions to her , she has on her own deposed about the act of sexual assault by the accused. She has categorically deposed about the nature and manner of sexual assault. The deposition of the victim is very well­corroborated by the testimony of P.W.3 Baby Nanda Gaikwad, member of District Women Cell, who has categorically deposed that the minor victim's statement was recorded in her presence. The victim's testimony is very well­ corroborated by her testimony as well as by the testimony of P.W.1. Although the medical officer (P.W.5) has deposed that the hymen of the victim was intact, however, the case is not of penetrative sexual assault, but of fondling of genitals and of making the young child hold the penis of the accused in her hand. The accused has not rebutted the presumption under Sec.30 of the P.O.C.S.O. Act and that there is no reason whatsoever for the minor victim and her mother to implicate the accused falsely in such an offence. 34] It would be worthwhile to reproduce the following sections : Sec. 354(A) (1) (i) of the I.P.C. reads as under :­ 354­A Sexual harassment and punishment for sexual harassment – (1) A man committing any of the following acts­ (i) physical contact and advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures; (ii) ­­­­­­ (iii)­­­­­­ shall be guilty of the offence of sexual harassment. 16 Spl. Case No. 123/2013 (Judgment) Sec. 7 & 8 of POCSO Act, 2012 reads as under :­ 7. Sexual assault.­ Whoever, with sexual intent touches the vagina, penis, anus or breast of the child or makes the child touch the vagina, penis, anus or breast of such person or any other person, or does any other act with sexual intent which involves physical contact without penetration is said to commit sexual assault. 8. Punishment for sexual assault. ­Whoever, commits sexual assault, shall be punishable with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than three years bu which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine. 35] The language of Sec.7 of the P.O.C.S.O. Act is very clear that whosoever with sexual intent touches the vagina, penis, anus or breast of the child or makes the child touch the vagina, penis anus or breast of such person or any other person, or does any other Act with sexual intent which involves physical contact without penetration is said to commit sexual assault. In the present case, the accused had sexual intent towards the minor victim, who was just a little child and it has been proved by the prosecution by the testimony of P.W.1,2 & 4 that the accused touched her vagina and also made the child touch his penis. Obviously, this act was committed only with sexual intent and with no other intent. Similarly, it has also been proved by the prosecution that the accused made physical contact with the child (victim) by removing her pantie and touching her vagina and further by giving his penis in her hand which involved unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures. 36] The ingredients of Sections 7 & 8 of POCSO Act, 2012 have been made out in the present case. In the case of K.Venkateshwarlu V/s. State of U.P.(cited supra) it has been held by the Apex Court that careful evaluation of the evidence of a child 17 Spl. Case No. 123/2013 (Judgment) witness in the background and context of other evidence on record is a must before the Court decides to rely upon it. In the present case, I have carefully evaluated the evidence of the child witness and I am fully satisfied that the attendant circumstances did not show that the child was acting under the influence of someone or was under threat or coercion. I have carefully observed the demeanor of the child witness in this case. She was indeed traumatized by the sexual assault. She was a truthful witness and therefore I draw the conclusion that the child was not tutored and that her evidence had a ring of truth. Even though she has deposed in her cross­examination that her mother told her what has to be deposed, she has not deposed that the said deposition was false. She has categorically deposed about the acts of the accused and has categorically denied that the said offence did not take place. 37] In the present case neither the accused has rebutted the presumption under Sec.30 of the P.O.C.S.O. Act, nor any plausible explanation is forthcoming in that regard. Merely because the accused stays in a small house with his family, does not mean that he can not commit sexual offence in the small house. It is absolutely possible that on the date of the incident the family members of the accused would have gone out of the house. It has come in the deposition of P.W.2 that when she went to the house of the accused to confront him, he was alone at home. The accused on finding the minor victim playing in the neighbourhood preyed on her and made her a target of his unnatural lust and in a planned way enticed the minor child by giving her a chocolate and took her to his house and committed the above sexual assault. It is a well­settled proposition of law that minor omissions, contradictions and improvements are bound to occur if the witnesses are truthful. Witnesses do not have a 18 Spl. Case No. 123/2013 (Judgment) photographic memory. In the present case, the minor omissions and contradictions do not go to the root of the matter. All the witnesses have withstood the test of the cross­ examination. 38] The minor child's statement was recorded in the presence of the Member of Mahila Dakshata Samiti. The argument sought to be advanced by the Ld.Adv. for the accused that the police would have themselves prepared the said statement is not convincing. There was no animosity between the police , Member of Mahila Dakshata Samiti and the accused to fabricate the statement. In view of the foregoing discussion, I am of the considered opinion that the prosecution has proved it's case beyond reasonable doubt and as such the accused is liable to be convicted U/Sec.354(A) (1) (i) of the Indian Penal Code and Sec. 7 & 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 39] I pause here to hear the accused on the point of sentence. Thane. (Mridula V. K. Bhatia) Date : 26/04/2017 District Judge­08 & Special Judge (POCSO Act), Thane. 40] At this stage heard the accused as well as the Ld.D.G.P. on the quantum of sentence. 41] The accused has submitted that considering his old age, this Court may pass appropriate orders. Per contra, Ld.D.G.P. has submitted that it is a settled view by the Apex Court as well as by the Bombay High Court that age should not be a factor to be considered in such offences as they are serious in nature. She has submitted that 19 Spl. Case No. 123/2013 (Judgment) the maximum punishment stipulated under the P.O.C.S.O.Act should be awarded to the accused alongwith compensation. 42] The minimum sentence which can be awarded U/Sec.8 of the P.C.O.C.S.O. Act is 3 years imprisonment. However, the punishment under Sec.8 of the P.O.C.S.O. Act may extend to 5 years alongwith fine. The accused has sexually assaulted a minor girl of only 5 years taking undue advantage of her vulnerability. Sympathies of the Court can not be misplaced. If a lesser punishment is awarded, it would send a wrong message to the society and would also make other young children vulnerable to the sexual assaults by the accused. People with sexual interest in children harm the very soul of an innocent child. 43] In view of the foregoing discussion and the overall facts and circumstances of the case, the following sentence would meet the ends of justice: ORDER 1] The accused Vitthal Muttayya Konda is hereby convicted vide Sec. 235(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure Code for the offence punishable Under Sec. 354(A) (1) (i) of the Indian Penal Code and Sec. 7 and 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] The accused is sentenced to undergo Rigorous Imprisonment for three years for the offence U/s. 354 (A) (1) (i) of the Indian Penal Code along with fine of ₹ 10,000/­. The said amount be withdrawn by the victim. In default of payment of said fine, the accused to undergo further Rigorous Imprisonment of 15 days. 20 Spl. Case No. 123/2013 (Judgment) 3] The accused is sentenced to undergo Rigorous Imprisonment for five years for the offence U/s. 7 & 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 alongwith fine of ₹ 10,000/­. In default of payment of said fine, the accused to undergo further Simple Imprisonment of 15 days. 4] All the sentences shall run concurrently. 5] The accused is directed to pay a compensation of ₹ 30,000/­ to the victim within eight weeks from today. 6] In addition, the State Government is directed to pay a compensation of ₹ 30,000/­ to the victim within one month of the receipt of this order, under Sub­Sec.(8) of Section 33 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act read with sub­ sections (2) and (3) of Section 357­A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 7] Set off be given to the accused as per Section 428 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for the period he has already undergone in jail. 8] Copy of the judgment be provided to the accused free of cost as per provision U/s. 363 of Cr.P.C. 9] Copy of the judgment be sent to the District Magistrate, Thane as per provision U/s. 365 of Cr.P.C. Thane. (Mridula V. K. Bhatia) Date : 26/04/2017. District Judge­08 & Special Judge (POCSO Act), Thane.

State of Maharashtra ( Through Koparkhairane Police Stn.) ...Complainant V/s. 1] Yashwant Krishna patil Age : 51 Years R/o.: Near Hanuman Mandir, Sector­19,Koparkhairne gaon, Navi Mumbai. 2] Shivaji Narayan Jogdand Age : 28 Years, R/at.: Backside of Ranjandevi Mandir, Pushpak Rekored, R.No.3, Sector­19, Koparkhairne gaon, Navi Mumbai ...Accused. Offence Punishable Under Secs. 509, 504, 506 of IPC and S. 11, 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ 2 Spl.Case (Pocso) No.256/2014... Jud. CNR No. MHTH01­006801­2014 Appearances : Shri. Londhe, Ld. Spl.P.P. for the State Mr. P.P. Patil, Ld. Advocate for the accused ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ :JUDGMENT: (Delivered on 4th day of May, 2018) 1] The accused in the court dock are charged for offence punishable under Secs. 509, 504, 506 of IPC and Sec. 11, 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 on the accusations of having been committed offence of insulting modesty of victim girl, abusing her in filthy language, committing criminal intimidation by threatening her and sexually assaulting the victim girl. 2] Case of prosecution, in brief, is as under : Victim girl resides with her parents at 202, Sector­19, Koparkhairane village, Navi Mumbai. The accused No.2 sell kerosene on the downstairs of the building. At around 7.15 p.m. on 24.03.2014, victim girl went to purchase vegetables from vegetable market. The accused come on motorcycle. The accused No.1 said her to come with him and he will pleased her by paying Rs. 5,000/­. The girl stated that she will inform to her parents. Accused No.2 threatened her that if she disclosed this, he will kill her. Thus, they have outraged the modesty of the victim girl, sexually assaulted her and intimidated her. 3] Victim girl rushed to police station at about 19.30 on 24.03.2014. Offence bearing C.R.No. II 08/2014 was registered against accused for offence u/sec. 509, 504, 506 r/w. 34 of Indian Penal Code and S. 11 and 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual offences Act. Investigation was taken up by API Pawar. API Pawar arrested accused filling memo of their descriptions. 3 Spl.Case (Pocso) No.256/2014... Jud. CNR No. MHTH01­006801­2014 Investigating officer has recorded statements of witnesses. He also collected birth certificate of victim girl. PSO Koparkhairane filed charge­sheet in this court. 4] I have framed charge against both the accused ( Exh. 04) for the offence under Secs. 509, 504, 506 of IPC and Sec. 11 & 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 of IPC. The contents of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular to which they pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. The defence of the accused as constructed in statement u/s. 313 of Cr.P.C. is of false implication. 5] In order to establish the guilt of accused, prosecution examined victim girl (P.W.1), her sister Varsha Solanki (P.W.2), Nandkishor Goswami (P.W.3)­ panch to the spot panchanama and investigating officer Pramod Goraksh Pawar (P.W.4). Prosecution has closed its evidence by filing pursis Exh.25. Prosecution has relied on complaint Exh.11, spot panchanama Exh.19, muddemal receipt Exh.23, Letter sent to Principal of ICL College, Vashi, Navi Mumbai Exh.24. 6] I have heard Ld. Special P.P. for the State and Ld. advocate for the accused. 7] The following points arise for my determination with my findings thereon for reasons to follow: POINTS FINDINGS 01. Does the prosecution prove that on ...In the negative. 24.03.2014, at about 19.30 hrs., Opp. Ganesh Kirana stores, Vegetable Market, Sector­19, Koparkhairane, Navi Mumbai accused in furtherance of their common intention insulted the modesty of victim girl ? 4 Spl.Case (Pocso) No.256/2014... Jud. CNR No. MHTH01­006801­2014 02. Does the prosecution prove that the accused ...In the negative. on aforesaid date, time and place in furtherance of their common intention intentionally insulted victim girl by abusing her in filthy language and thereby gave provocation to her to break the public peace? 03. Does prosecution prove that on the aforesaid ...In the negative. date, time and place, the accused, in furtherance of their common intention threatened complainant­victim girl to kill? 04. Does prosecution prove that on the aforesaid ...In the negative. date, time and place, the accused, in furtherance of their common intention sexually assaulted her? 05. What order ? Accused are acquitted as per final order. REASONS AS TO POINT NOS.1 TO 5: 8] Victim girl (P.W.1 )and her elder sister Varsha (P.W.2) resides at Om Jyot Building, Room No.202, Sector 19, Koparkhairne. On 24.3.2014, their parents went outside and they were to cook food. Varsha (P.W.2) asked victim girl to go downstairs and bring vegetables. Victim girl (P.W.1) went to vegetable market at about 7.15 p.m. Shivaji Natha came there and offered Rs. 5,000/­ to victim girl and asked her to come with him. When the victim girl scolded Shivaji Natha and told him that she will tell his name to her parents, accused Yashwant Patil threatened her to beat all her family members. People gathered on the spot and police arrived. 9] Mr. Pramod Pawar (P.W.4) was on duty at Teen Taki Police Chowki, Koparkhairane. On 24.3.2014, he took down complaint Exh.11 of 5 Spl.Case (Pocso) No.256/2014... Jud. CNR No. MHTH01­006801­2014 victim girl Poonam Narayan Solanki. Pramod Pawar (P.W.4) went to the spot and prepared spot panchanama (Exh.19) in presence of panch Nandkishor (P.W.3). It is spot at Sector­ 19, near Ganesh Kirana Stores. Pramod Pawar seized motorcycle No MH­04­AF­3723 and deposited it in malkhana and obtained receipt Exh.23. He brought birth certificate Exh.24 of victim girl. There was one day to become victim girl of 18 years old. So, he has applied provisions of POCSO. 10] I have heard Ld. A.P.P.. It is submitted that it is a heinous act. Accused No.1 is old person and he has helped the accused No.2 with pre­ decided plan. They had shared common intention. Ld. Advocate for accused submitted that there is business rivalary as girl’s father also sells kerosene . Accused No. 1 is known to victim girl because his daughter studying with her in the same class. When she knows them since prior to the incident, then why their name is not there in the FIR. It has come in the evidence of P.W.2 that police arrived on the spot whereas P.W.4 deposed that victim girl went to the police station while police caught hold of the accused then why nobody came forward to depose. The girl has got licence before 5 years. So, she was above 18 years at the time of incident. The girl herself has submitted that the place of offence was crowded. 11] I have carefully scanned the evidence on record. School has issued letter to PSO Koparkhairane Exh.12. It is noted that the girl is studying in 12th standard and her date of birth is noted as 25.03.1996. She born at Sindkhed Raja, Buldhan. She has not submitted the original extract of her birth. Xerox copy of her birth certificate is at Art.A. Her birth date is mentioned in Art.A as 10.03.1998. She has stated that her date of birth is 25.3.1997. She has clarified that her mother wanted that she should get education early, so she has given birth date 25.3.1997. The birth certificate of 6 Spl.Case (Pocso) No.256/2014... Jud. CNR No. MHTH01­006801­2014 Grampanchayat is valid birth certificate. Her birth is shown on 10.3.1998 in Grampanchayat register. The incident occurred on 24.3.2014. It means that she was 16 years old at the time of incident. 12] It has come in the evidence of (P.W.1) victim girl that Yashwant Patil (Accused No.1) was at his shop and accused No.2 Shivaji came on bike. It has come in FIR that accused No.2 was on motor bike and accused No.1 was pillion rider. While this part is pointed out to victim girl, she stated that complaint is written down wrongly on this point. Victim girl (P.W.1) deposed that she knows Yashwant Patil as his daughter was studying with her. She also stated that she knows accused No.2 Shivaji, but she was unable to know about his full name in the police station. She has stated name of Yashwant Patil to police but she could not give reason why it is not appearing in the FIR. It has come in the cross­examination of Pramod Pawar (P.W.4) who recorded FIR Exh.11 that when girl came to police station she was knowing the accused. It has come in FIR Exh.11 that one boy was riding bike and one old man was pillion rider. She has given their names as Shivaji Natha Jogdand and Yashwant Krishna Patil. It has come in her evidence that she knows Yashwant Patil and their family from 7 to 8 years. The accused was purchasing kerosene from her father and selling it. They had dealing continued from 1 to 1 ½ year. There were 7 to 8 cases pending against her step father. She pleaded ignorance about dispute between her father and the accused . 13] It is seen from the evidence that the victim girl went with the parents to police station. The accused No.2 and step father of victim girl are from the same profession. Pramod Pawar (P.W.4) has deposed that the incident took place in a crowded place. He has examined two independent witnesses but those two independent witnesses does not come forward to depose in the court. It has come in evidence of Varsha (P.W.2) that her father 7 Spl.Case (Pocso) No.256/2014... Jud. CNR No. MHTH01­006801­2014 and accused No.1 had joint kerosene business. The evidence on record shows that there was rivalary between accused No.1 and father of the victim girl. It appears that the victim girl says that both the accused come on bike. But subsequently she improves her version that one came on bike and other followed him. It appears that some remarks were passed. While remark was passed somebody must be there to intervene in their quarrel. Those persons in the crowd are not examined by the prosecution. There is no independent evidence to connect the accused persons with the said offence. The sole testimony of victim girl does not inspire my confidence because of their rivalary. Hence, benefit of doubt is required to be given to the accused . Hence, I answer point Nos.1 to 4 in the negative and pass following order: ORDER 1] The accused No.1 Yashwant Krishna Patil and accused No.2 Shivaji Narayan Jogdand are hereby acquitted under Sec. 235(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure from the offence under Secs. 509,504, 506 of IPC and S. 11 &12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] Their bail bond stands cancelled. 3] Muddemal property­ Kawasaki bike bearing NO. MH­04­AF­3723 be returned to the accused No.2 Shivaji Jogdand on execution of indemnity bond after appeal period is over. 4] Accused shall furnish P.R. and S.B. of Rs. 15,000/­ each in view of proviso 437(A) of Cr.P.C. 1 Order Ex.1 Anti. Bail Appln. No.2588/16 ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN ANTICIPATORY BAIL APPN.NO.2588/2016 Heard Ld. Adv. Mr. Rajay Gaikwad for the applicant. Ld. A.P.P. Mrs. Kamthe for the State. I.O. present. 1] The applicant has approached this court apprehending his arrest by Shreenagar police station, in Crime No. I­215/2016 for offence U/s. 354, 354(a), 354(b) and 506 of the I.P.C. and Sec. 8 and 12 of the POCSO Act, 2012. 2] It is the prosecution case that the applicant had been chasing the victim since about 1½ months while she used to go to the school and class. He used to insist the victim to establish friendship with him. When she refused for the same, he threatened to kill her brother Atish. 3] Ld. Adv. Mr. Gaikwad has submitted that they both had a consensual relationship which is evident from the what's app chats annexed along with the bail application. He has submitted that when the parents of the girl discovered it, they forced her to file a complaint. Custodial interrogation is not necessary in the facts and circumstances of the present case. He has submitted that the applicant has attended the police station as directed by the Court. 4] Per contra, Ld. A.P.P. Mrs. Kamthe has vehemently opposed the bail application on the ground that the victim is only 15 years old and that custodial interrogation is necessary. 2 Order Ex.1 Anti. Bail Appln. No.2588/16 6] Upon the perusal of the F.I.R. and the allegations contained therein, custodial interrogation is not required. However, since the vicitm is a minor and there may be chances of stalking/repeating the offence, I am inclined to allow the bail application in terms of the following order. ORDER [i] Anticipatory Bail Application (Exh.1) is hereby allowed by confirming interim order (Exh.3) granted on 17/10/2016 by adding following terms and conditions :­ [a] The applicant shall continue to attend Shreenagar police station on every Friday at 5.00 p.m. till filing of the charge­sheet. [b] He shall not commit similar offence, failing which his bail shall stand cancelled. [c] The applicant shall furnish identity proof and contact details of two blood relatives to the Investigating Officer. [d] The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer. [e] Applicant shall attend the court dates regularly. [f] Applicant shall not leave the jurisdiction of this court without prior permission thereof. 3 Order Ex.1 Anti. Bail Appln. 1 Order Exh.1 in Cri.Bail Appln. No. 2595/16 ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN CRI. BAIL APPLICATION NO.2595/2016 Heard Ld. Adv. Mr. P. S. Thombre for the applicant. Ld. A.P.P. Mrs. Kamthe for the State. I.O. present. 1] Applicant who is arrested by Nayanagar police station in Crime No. I­313/2016 for offence U/s. 376, 354 and 507 of the I.P.C. and Sec. 3, 4 and 8 of the POCSO Act, 2012, has sought his enlargement on bail. 2] It is the case of the prosecution that in May 2016 the applicant kissed the victim while she was alone with him in his house. On the next day, he raped her when nobody was in his house. Thereafter on 15/09/2016 between 15.30 and 17.30 hours, the applicant took the victim in a rickshaw, brought her to flat No.501, Ablee Paradise, Near DMART, Bhayander (West) and raped her on the false promise of marriage. The applicant threatened the victim on her mobile to defame her by showing video clips of the said sexual act. 3] Ld. Advocate for the applicant has submitted that the sexual intercourse was consensual. The applicant was operated for Kidney stone at Tunga Hospital and it was impossible for him to have sexual intercourse with the victim. The applicant is ready to abide by any terms and conditions imposed by the court. There is delay in lodging the F.I.R. He has relied on an unreported Judgment of the Bombay High Court in the case of Sunil Mahadev Patil V/s. State of Maharashtra, Bail Application No. 1036/2015 dated 3rd August, 2015. In the said matter, the Bombay High Court has laid down the various factors to be considered by the court 2 Order Exh.1 in Cri.Bail Appln. No. 2595/16 when a boy and a girl are in love with each other and choose to live with each other without consent of their parents. 4] Per contra, Ld. A.P.P. has vehemently opposed the bail application on the ground that the offence is serious in nature. Two pen drives were recovered from the applicant during his personal search. These pen drives were seized under a panchanama. The said videos are submitted by the I.O. which show explicitly the sexual acts committed by the applicant against the victim. The I.O. has also placed on record the original birth certificate of the victim which shows her age as 14 years. Consent of a minor is not valid consent under the eyes of law. The I.O. has placed on record the medical certificate issued by the doctor to show that the accused was capable of sexual intercourse despite the operation. The Judgment relied on by the Ld. Adv. for the applicant is not applicable to the facts of the present case since this is a case of a much married 35 years old man having 'sex' with a minor who is less than 15 years of age. This is not at all a case of a 'love affair' between a boy and a girl. 5] The offence is serious in nature. The investigation is in progress. The victim is less than 15 years of age. There is every possibility of tampering with the prosecution witnesses. In view thereof, I am inclined to reject the application. ORDER Bail Application is rejected. Thane. ( Mridula V.K.Bhatia ) Dt:­16/11/2016. Dist. Judge – 08 and Special Judge (POCSO Act), Thane. 3 Order Exh.1 in Cri.Bail Appln. No. 2595/16

About two months before lodging the F.I.R. when she was walking along the road, at that time the applicant­accused called her and told that her mother is calling her. Therefore the informant .. 2 .. Bail No. 2583/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) went to the house of applicant­accused. He asked her to wait by telling his mother is in bathroom and then offered water to drink. After drinking that water the informant felt giddiness and she fainted. She also realized that the leggings on her person was quite loose in fitting. Thereafter around 6.45 she returned home and went to attend nature's call and at that time she saw blood was oozing from her place of urination and therefore she realized that applicant­ accused has committed sexual assault on her. Therefore her mother questioned her and at that time the informant disclosed about the incident of sexual assault on her by the applicant­accused and accordingly the F.I.R. came to be lodged. 4] The learned Counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant­accused is falsely implicated. He submitted that there is delay of two months in lodging the F.I.R. No particulars about date and time of the incident had been mentioned in the F.I.R. The victim­ girl voluntarily went to the house of the accused. He submitted that nowadays a new trend has come up to implicate the accused in such kind of case without giving any particulars by only stating that some .. 3 .. Bail No. 2583/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) stupefying substance was administered to the victim­girl and therefore she did not know anything. He submitted that in fact the girl is interested in the accused and wants to marry him but marriage of accused is settled with another girl and scheduled on 12th November and therefore this false F.I.R. came to be registered to pressurize the applicant­accused to marry with the complainant girl. There are chances of tampering witnesses and fleeing away from justice and prayed for rejection of application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R. and police papers it appears that the incident is stated to have occurred before two months. It is alleged that on that day the accused called the victim­ .. 4 .. Bail No. 2583/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) girl at his house on the pretext that his mother is calling her. Mr.B.P.Pandey submitted his written notes of arguments at Exh.60 and also submitted oral arguments at length. In written arguments the deposition of all witnesses, particularly their chief examinations are reproduced and the evidence is discussed at length. I have gone through the same. Special P.P. Mr.Pandey argued that the evidence of victim girl PW4 is supported and corroborated by PW1 to PW3. PW3 Dr.Zarana Pujara is an independent witness. She also narrated the entire incident disclosed by the victim girl. The entire evidence is described in the letter Exh.22 issued by PW3. Special P.P. Mr.Pandey argued that in cross examination of victim girl hundreds of photos were shown to establish that after strained relations she was not invited for any birth day party of the daughters of accused. All the witnesses are unnecessarily cross examined at length. But nothing is brought on record through J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 124­13 ­ 354, 7,11.doc . .....13/­ ..13.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.–124/2013.. Exh.61.. their cross examinations to discard their testimonies. Spl.P.P. Mr.Pandey argued that there is presumption u/s.29 and 30 of the Act in favour of the victim and against the accused. In view of corroborated evidence of PW1 to PW4 the prosecution has proved its case and the presumption as laid u/s.29 and 30 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act has to be raised in favour of prosecution. 20] As already observed PW1 and PW2 i.e. mother and father of the victim girl have deposed in the Court on the basis of hearsay evidence. They deposed the facts which were allegedly narrated by the victim daughter to them. Certainly the same story in almost same words is deposed by the prosecution witnesses Nos.1 to 4 in their chief examinations. However, whether from the evidence of thee witnesses, offence is proved beyond reasonable doubt or not has to be ascertained. 21] As already mentioned the alleged incident was disclosed by the victim to the doctor on 16.09.2013, whereas the complaint is lodged on 18.09.2013 at 00.40 hours i.e. after a considerable delay. As per the prosecution story the victim's father Premchand Sharma was working as Manager in the office of Home Makers at Nariman Point, Churchgate, Mumbai. Thus he is educated person. However, there is an J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 124­13 ­ 354, 7,11.doc . .....14/­ ..14.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.–124/2013.. Exh.61.. inordinate delay in lodging of FIR after disclosure of the alleged incident. The reason behind the same as given in the FIR that they were feeling awkward and after discussing amongst adult members of the family, the complaint came to be lodged, is certainly not a proper and reasonable. 22] As argued by advocate Mr.Brigenza, in the entire prosecution story there is no whisper about the day, date and time of alleged sexual assault upon the victim girl. Neither the victim girl PW4 nor her parents PW1 and PW2 have deposed in Court the day, date and time of alleged incident. Moresoever the day, date and time of alleged last episode of sexual assault is also not stated by any of the witnesses examined by the prosecution. 23] The prosecution story is entirely based upon the alleged disclosure of sexual assault by the victim girl to Dr.Zarana Pujara. Under such circumstances the evidence of Dr.Zarana Pujara and the alleged letter issued by her plays very important role in the present case. The contents of letter are already reproduced herein before. On perusal of said letter Exh.22 it reveals that, at the top of the letter the date is mentioned as 16.09.2013. However, on the third line of said letter there is eraser in the date and the same is appears to be initially mentioned as 17/9 and subsequently corrected as J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 124­13 ­ 354, 7,11.doc . .....15/­ ..15.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.–124/2013.. Exh.61.. 16/9. On further perusal of the letter some interesting words are appearing therein. It is mentioned in the letter “she narrated that the accused used to molest her......”. Certainly till lodging of complaint and launching the prosecution, word “accused” is certainly nowhere used by anyone. As in ordinary course the victim girl would have named the person who molest her or would have described him as the father of her friends. But interestingly the molester is described as an accused at the very first alleged disclosure to the doctor, which is not acceptable and reliable. On further perusal of the letter, as rightly pointed out by advocate Mr.Brigenza, it reveals that victim girl had narrated the incident to her mother and thereafter she was taken to clinic of Dr.Zarana Pujara. However, in the entire prosecution story and even in the evidence of prosecution witnesses it is pretended to establish that for the first time the victim girl disclosed about the incident before Dr.Zarana Pujara in the presence of her father and mother. Had the victim girl was feeling awkward to disclose about the incident to her parents, the disclosure of the same to doctor in the immediate presence of parents and without any hesitation, is not reliable. 24] It is pertinent to note here that in the FIR and in the depositions of PW1 and PW2 it is mentioned that as the J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 124­13 ­ 354, 7,11.doc . .....16/­ ..16.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.–124/2013.. Exh.61.. victim girl was continuously crying, scared and was not eating well, the parents took her to Dr.Zarana Pujara. However, the victim girl in her deposition has specifically deposed that she herself asked her parents to take to her to the doctor. In ordinary case it would not be of material importance as to who and on whose instance victim was taken to the doctor. In the present case, certainly there is no physical injury to the victim girl. The facts about the incident are not certain. Under such circumstances the contradictions in the evidence of witnesses as to how the victim was taken to the family doctor, have evidenciary value while deciding the guilt of the accused. 25] In the present case the parents themselves had approached their family doctor with the victim girl. After the alleged examination and alleged disclosure of the incident by victim girl and at the request of parents Dr.Zarana Pujara had issued letter Exh.22 and after obtaining said letter the informant and her husband approached to police station with the same. Interestingly for proper and better investigation the victim is not referred to any Government Hospital or independent doctor for her check­up. 26] Admittedly u/s.29 of The Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act there is a presumption in favour of the prosecution and against the accused. U/s.30 of the said J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 124­13 ­ 354, 7,11.doc . .....17/­ ..17.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.–124/2013.. Exh.61.. Act there is presumption about culpable mental state on the part of the accused. However, in order to raise said presumptions, the evidence led by prosecution must be cogent, reliable and inspiring confidence. In the present case the prosecution story is based upon the alleged disclosure of incident by the victim girl to a doctor and thereafter knowledge about the same to the parents. While disclosing the incident to the doctor and police, the victim girl did not state about the date and time of said incident. As already mentioned there is even no evidence about the alleged last episode of sexual assault. The very conduct on the part of Dr.Zarana Pujara and issuing letter at the request of parents of victim, is doubtful. More particularly reference of an assailant in said letter as an accused raises doubt for the reasons already discussed. Under such circumstances the evidence of prosecutrix PW4 and other witnesses about the actual incident is certainly not reliable and inspiring confidence about the prosecution story. Hence this is not a fit case to raise presumption against the accused as provided u/s.29 of 30 of the said Act. 27] In the present case the accused has raised defence that out of jealousy and previous enmity false complaint is lodged against him. To prove his defence accused deposed on oath at Exh.50. In his deposition he has narrated the facts J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 124­13 ­ 354, 7,11.doc . .....18/­ ..18.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.–124/2013.. Exh.61.. prior to the alleged incident of lodging FIR and subsequent conduct of the complainant after lodging FIR. He also examined his student Mohammad Alauddin Abdul Gafan Ansari as DW2 at Exh.53. He has deposed about the conduct of accused and timing of his class. DW3 Anand Prakash Mishra in his deposition at Exh.56 narrated about his friendship with the accused. He further deposed about the conduct of the accused and subsequent conduct of Premchand Sharma about affixing newspaper cutouts in the vicinity of class of the accused. Through defence witnesses and by deposing in Court as well as by producing bundle of documents the accused has tried to establish that he is falsely implicated in the offence. From the entire evidence on record one thing is clear that there were strained relations between the family of the victim and the accused. However, in order to prove that the prosecution story is entirely false one, there must be concrete evidence, e.g. if plea of alibi is raised there must be strong evidence of defence showing the absence of the accused at scene of offence and his presence elsewhere. As already mentioned, in the present case the prosecution has nowhere alleged day, date and time of incidents of alleged sexual assault. Under such circumstances there cannot be a evidence to prove the absence of the accused at the scene of incident when the very allegations are vague one. So also merely because of strained relations it cannot be said that the J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 124­13 ­ 354, 7,11.doc . .....19/­ ..19.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.–124/2013.. Exh.61.. accused was falsely implicated. In order to establish that informant lodged false complaint and accused is falsely involved in the offence, there must be strong defence evidence. In the absence of said strong and concrete evidence it cannot be adjudged that the prosecution story is false one and accused is falsely implicated. 28] Certainly in every criminal prosecution it is the duty of the prosecution to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt. The lapses on the part of the defence cannot be formed basis for holding accused guilty of the offence. As already mentioned in the entire prosecution story there is no whisper of day, date and time of alleged incident. There are mere vague allegations against the accused. The evidence of doctor and the letter issued by her is certainly doubtful. The evidence of the victim and her family is also very vague and unreliable. As such, as already mentioned the evidence of victim and other prosecution witnesses is not inspiring confidence to raise statutory presumption against the accused. As such the prosecution has failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt. Hence answering point Nos.1 and 2 in the negative, following order is passed. ORDER 1. Accused Chanchalkumar Sinheshwar Rai is hereby acquitted u/s.235(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 124­13 ­ 354, 7,11.doc . .....20/­ ..20.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.–124/2013.. Exh.61.. for offence punishable u/s.354 of the Indian Penal Code and section 7 and 11 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 2. The bail bond of accused stands cancelled. 3. The album of photographs produced by accused be returned to him on his demand. 4. Accused is directed to furnish personal bond of Rs.15,000/­ with one surety in like amount, in terms of sec.437­A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Sd/­... Thane. .. 1 .. bail 2461/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 2461 of 2014 This application is filed by applicant namely Hazrat Ali alias Papa Mohammed Jibran Ansari and Saddam Mushtaque Shaikh for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with C.R.No.I­301/2014 registered at Bhiwandi City police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 363, 34 of I.P.C. and section 11(4) and 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicants kidnapped the victim girls from their residential house and then harassed them sexually. It is further submitted that the applicants had not kidnapped the girls but the girls had left the house of their own. It is further contended and argued that no such incident has happened and the applicant is falsely implicated in this crime. It is further submitted that the applicants are permanent residents of the address given and that if the present applicants/accused is released on bail, they will co­ operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicants are entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that the accused persons were contacting the victims girl personally and by phone calls and they induced the girls and kidnapped them and then subjected them to sexual harassment. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicants/accused are released on bail, there is possibility of the applicants threatening the victim girls and .. 2 .. bail 2461/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) the prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicants are released on bail they may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicants are not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicants/accused is of serious nature under section 363 read with section 34 of I.P.C. and section 11(4) and 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012, as rightly pointed out on behalf of accused, the complaint is in regard to missing of the girls and subsequently offence under section 363 of I.P.C. was applied. Then, though offence under section 363of I.P.C. is applied, from the statement of the girls it appears that the girls had left the house of her own. Then, though it is argued on behalf of prosecution that the girls were minor at the time of incident, the aspect about the age of the girls would have to be decided after trial on merits and in the light of the fact that the applicants have come up with the case that the girls have left the house of their own and the applicants have been falsely implicated in this crime, such allegations will have to be decided on merits. Even nothing is stated to be recovered from the applicants/accused. 4] Then, it is well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be gone into detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicants would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicants tampering with prosecution evidence. .. 3 .. bail 2461/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) 5] In that respect it is contended by the applicants that they are permanent residents of the address given and they will not abscond if released on bail and that they are ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 6] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicants/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 7] Then, it has also to be mentioned that the investigation in the matter though almost completed and the charge sheet is yet to be submitted, it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicants/accused in jail for uncertain period. 8] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicants can be released on bail. It is contended that at present the parents of informant and parents of the victim and the accused are ready to perform the marriage of victim with the accused and the parents have filed affidavit. The applicant is not habitual. There was love affair between victim and accused. There is no chance of tampering or jump on bail. If the applicant is not released on bail, his future will be spoiled. He undertakes to obey the directions of the Court and attend for the trial. 2] The investigation officer has given say at Exh.6. It is contended that accused has committed penetrative sexual assault upon the minor victim and made her Arif Usman Haji Momin pregnant. if the accused is released on bail, he is likely to tamper the witnesses. 3] I heard Ld. Counsel on behalf of accused and Ld. A.P.P. 4] The learned Counsel on behalf of accused submitted that the parents of victim and the accused have stated that they are ready to perform their marriage. He also relied upon the decision in the case of Akshay Chandrakant Mahadalkar V/s. State of Maharashtra and Anr.Bail application --2-- No.897/2017 dated 28/07/2017. In that case, the offence was under section 376(2), 376(I) (N), 354, 509, 506 of I.P.C. and 8,12 of POCSO Act. The victim was 13 years old and at the time of bail, she was 16.2 years old. Their parents had tendered affidavit stating that they have resolved their dispute and the victim girl has expressed her desire to marry at the age of majority with the applicant. In that background, bail of accused was allowed. 5] In this case, the parents of the victim and accused have filed affidavit. The age of the victim and accused have filed affidavit. The age of the victim at the time of incident was 15 to 16 years old. There was love affair between victim and the accused. The victim become pregnant at this stage. The accused and the victim have resolved their dispute out of the Court. So, considering the facts and circumstances of this case, this Court is of the view that further custody of the accused behind bar till final disposal of the case is not warranted. He is entitled for bail. Under these mitigating circumstances, I pass the order:­ :ORDER: 1] Application is allowed. 2] Applicant Sujil Nandlal Machhi be released on PB and SB of Rs.30,000/­ (Rs.Thirty Thousand only) with one or two sureties. 3] The accused shall not repeat the offence and he shall not tamper the prosecution witnesses and victim by --3-- any means. 4] He shall attend the Court for trial. 5] He shall not leave the jurisdiction of the Court without prior permission. Thane. ( S.C. Khalipe ) Date : 15/11/2017. Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

.. 1 .. bail 2463/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 2463 of 2014 This application is filed by applicants namely Ismail Mohammed Gaus Sayed and Aslam Mohammed Gaus Sayed for their release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with C.R.No.I­883/2014 registered at Mumbra Police Station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 376, 377 read with section 34 of I.P.C. and section 3 and 4 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. It was contended and argued that the applicants are arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that both accused committed sexual assault on the victim girls. It is further contended and argued that no such incident has happened and the applicants are falsely implicated in this crime on account of matrimonial dispute between applicant no.1 and his wife i.e. mother of victim. It is further submitted that the applicants are permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicants/accused is released on bail, they will co­operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicants are entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that the victim girls are daughters of applicant no.1 and applicant no.2 is his brother. It is further contended and argued that the accused no.1 and 2 have time again committed sexual assault on the victim girls. It is further submitted that in such circumstance since the applicants/accused are directly related to the victim girls, they are released on bail, there is possibility of the applicants threatening the complainant and victim girls and other prosecution witnesses. It is also .. 2 .. bail 2463/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) contended and argued that if the applicants are released on bail they may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicants are not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, the offences charged against the applicants/accused is of serious nature under section 376, 377 read with section 34 of I.P.C. and section 3 and 4 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 with the allegation that the applicants/accused who are father and real uncle of the victim girls had sexually assaulted and abused them and even forced them to have oral sex with them. 4] It is also clear that the F.I.R. is lodged by the mother of the girls. It is submitted on behalf of the applicants that they have been falsely implicated in this crime on account of matrimonial or family dispute between mother of the girl and accused etc. However, as rightly submitted on behalf of prosecution the offence charged against the applicants/accused is of very serious nature and it is a heinous crime and possibility of mother of the girls making such false allegations implicating father and uncle of the girls is remote and even the allegations are supported by medical evidence and in such circumstance it would be premature to conclude at this stage when the investigation is still in progress that the applicants are falsely implicated in this crime and are entitled to be released on bail at this stage. 5] No doubt, it is well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized and .. 3 .. bail 2463/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) only prima facie material showing implication of accused is to be seen and the main criteria to be considered is whether the accused would tamper with prosecution evidence and would abscond if released on bail. 6] In that regard it has to be mentioned that the investigation in the matter is still in progress and as rightly submitted on behalf of prosecution since the accused persons are relatives of the victim girls being father and uncle, looking to the gravity of offence and the manner in which it is stated to have been committed, the apprehension that the applicants/accused would pressurize the victim girls and also their mother i.e. complainant and would tamper with prosecution evidence, is well founded. Then, the possibility of the accused being absconding if released on bail also cannot be ruled out at this stage. 7] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is not a fit case wherein the applicants/accused can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is rejected. Date : 02.02.2015. (Mrs.V.V.Virkar) Additional Session Judge­1, Thane.

No. IN THE COURT OF ADDITIONAL SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE ( Presided Over By N.N. Shrimangale ) SPECIAL CASE NO. 127 OF 2013 State of Maharashtra ( Through Kalwa Police Station, Dist­Thane ) … Complainant. ( Cr. No. I­268/2013 ) Versus Pappu Sukulal Rai, Age­ 27 yrs., R/at: Karlad Chawl, Vitawa, Thane. … Accused. –­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ Offences punishable under sec. 354 of the Indian Penal Code and under Sec.8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. –­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ Shri V.G. Kadu, Ld. APP for the State Shri.Sonawane, Ld. Adv. for Accused –­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ 2 Spl.Case No. 127/2013 [ Judg. ] JUDGMENT ( Delivered On this 7th day of April, 2017 ) 1] The accused is chargesheeted of the offences punishable under section 354 of the Indian penal Code and Sec. 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act. 2] The prosecution case in short is as under : i) The complainant Renu Rinku Vishwakarma the mother of victim girl Achal filed complaint against the accused with Kalwa Police Station on 6/6/2013. ii) The complaint in short is that said Renu Vishwakarma resides with her family including her daughter Achal who was 3 yrs. on the date of filing the complaint. The complainant was present in her house on 5/6/2013 during noon time with her daughter Achal, son Ishan. The accused Pappu came to her house and asked for mixer as his mixer was become out of order. He collected the mixer and went to his house. iii) On 6/6/2013 the husband of the complainant went for his job at Wadala. The complainant did her household work and at about 1.30 p.m. she sent her daughter Achal to the house of accused to bring the mixer. Accordingly victim Achal went to his house and returned without bringing the mixer and she/Achal told to the complainant that the accused Pappu is bringing the said mixer and again Achal 3 Spl.Case No. 127/2013 [ Judg. ] went to the house of accused and after 5 minutes the complainant­mother went to the house of accused and found the door of the house of the accused was closed, but not latched from its inner side. Then, the complainant called her daughter and pushed the door of the house of the accused and found her daughter Achal lying on the bed. The complainant took Achal and raised voice. So the persons residing in neighbouring area gathered there. They caught the accused and thereafter the complainant went to Kalwa Police Station to file complaint alongwith victim girl Achal. Very day on 6/6/13 at about 8.35 p.m. she filed complaint against accused. iv) The police registered a crime at C.R.No.I­268/13 U/Sec.354 of I.P.C. and Sec.18 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 3] The accused appeared before the court. I framed charge against the accused at Exh.6 U/Sec.354 of I.P.C. and Sec.8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. The contents in the charge read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. The accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. The defence of the accused is of total denial. 4] Though the police mentioned Sec.18 Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, in chargesheet, the 4 Spl.Case No. 127/2013 [ Judg. ] complaint at Exh.13 is clear to attract Sec.8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. So, I framed U/Sec. 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. and not U/Sec.18 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 5] As to bring home the guilt of the accused the prosecution succeed to examine following witnesses : 1 P.W.1 Renu Rinku Vishwakarma, the Exh.9 complainant who is the mother of the victim girl Achal 2 P.W.2 Miss.Achal Vishwakarma, the victim Exh.11 girl. 3 P.W.3 Bhupendra @ Rinku Shribhagwati Exh.12 Vishwakarma, father of the victim girl Achal 4 P.W.4 Sou.Bhagyashree Rahul Gaikwad, Exh.15 the neighbourer of the complainant 5 P.w.5 Vikas Pundalik Bansode, the panch Exh.16 to the spot panchanama. 6 P.W.6 A.P.I. Sachin Sitaram Ambre, the Exh.19 investigating officer. 6] The prosecution also relied upon the documents which are as under : 1 Complaint filed by the complainant Renu Exh.10 Rinku Vishwakarma against the accused. 2 Spot panchanama Exh.17 5 Spl.Case No. 127/2013 [ Judg. ] 7] The Ld.A.P.P. filed evidence close pursis at Exh.20 8] I recorded the statement of the accused U/Sec.313 of Cr.P.C. at Exh.21. The accused stated that Renu, the mother of Achal and himself are from same native place, so the accused was having visiting terms with the house of Renu, which was not liked by Rinku the husband of Renu. Therefore, there was a quarrel in between him and Rinku the father of Achal prior of the incident. It is also stated that said Rinku threatened to the accused to send him behind the bars. Therefore, as per the contentions of the accused the complainant filed this false complaint at the instance of her husband Rinku. 9] I heard the Ld.A.P.P.Shri.Kadu for the State and the Ld.defence Adv. Shri.Sonawane for the accused. 10] Following points arise for my determination. I have mentioned my findings thereon for the reasons stated below : POINTS FINDINGS 1) Whether the prosecution proves that on 6/6/2013 at Karlad Chawl, Vitawa, Thane the accused used criminal force to complainant's minor daughter Achal,aged about 6 Spl.Case No. 127/2013 [ Judg. ] 3 years, intending to outrage her modesty by removing her nicker and by touching his hand on her body and thereby committed an offence punishable U/Sec.354 of I.P.C. ? In the negative. 2) Whether the prosecution proves that on the aforesaid date,time and place the accused committed sexual assault on complainant's minor daughter by removing her nicker and by touching his hand on her body and thereby committed an offence punishable U/Sec.8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 ? In the negative. 3) What order ? As per final order. :REASONS: POINT NOS.1 & 2 : 11] Both the points being interlinked, I have taken them together for my determination to avoid repeatation of same reasonings. 7 Spl.Case No. 127/2013 [ Judg. ] 12 ] The complaint is proved at Exh.10. In the said complaint it is mentioned that when the complainant Renu pushed the door of the house of the accused , she found her daughter Achal lying on the bed in naked condition facing to the sky and her nicker was found removed and the accused was found touching/moving his hand on her body. So the complaint itself shows that she did not see the person who removed the nicker from the person of Achal. 13] Considering the complaint , I am to consider the evidence of complainant Renu examined at Exh.9. Her evidence makes it clear that she sent her daughter Achal aged about 3 yrs. to the house of the accused to bring her mixer which was given to the accused one day prior of the incident. The age of Achal is shown as 3 yrs. So, it appears to me that such small girl is not expected to bring the mixer from the house of the accused. It is also necessary to mention that the complainant Renu knocked the door of the house of the accused and pushed it and after entering into the house of the accused, she found her daughter Achal lying on bed in naked condition and a nicker of her daughter removed and kept by her side. It means the door of the house of the accused was likely to be pushed ahead and not latched from inner side. If , the accused would have a malafide intention , the accused was expected to latch the door of his house from inner side. 8 Spl.Case No. 127/2013 [ Judg. ] 14] In her cross­examination the complainant Renu admitted that the accused resides in neighbouring premises and it was easy for the complainant to call the accused to return the mixer from her own house. So, when the house of the accused is situated abutting to the house of complainant, I think that there was no need of sending Achal to the house of accused to bring mixer. Moreover, it is also clear from the evidence of the complainant that first time the complainant sent her daughter Achal to the house of the accused to bring the mixer , but the accused told to Achal that he himself is bringing the mixer to the house of the complainant. Then also the complainant not expected to send Achal to the house of the accused to bring the mixer again. 15] The evidence of Renu further reveals that after raising her voice/alarm after seeing the condition of Achal neighbouring persons gathered there, amongst whom some social workers also gathered. But no such social worker or karyakarta is examined by the prosecution before the court. 16] The material witness victim Achal Vishwakarma is examined at Exh.11, wherein this witness has categorically stated that her parents gave necessary instructions to her as to what is to be stated before the court. Achal further stated that when she was taken to the police station by her mother, her mother instructed her what is to be told before the police. 9 Spl.Case No. 127/2013 [ Judg. ] She further stated that the police did not ask anything to her. Achal also stated that her parents instructed her to give her evidence against accused in the court on the day of her evidence before the court and that is why she gave her evidence before the court against the accused. So, if the evidence of this material witness victim girl Achal considered altogether, there is every likelyhood of tutoring the material witness victim girl Achal by her parents about giving evidence against the accused. So, the evidence of the victim girl Achal is totally shrouded by the clouds of doubts. This witness Achal also admitted in her cross­examination that there was a quarrel in between her father and the accused Pappu prior of the incident. Therefore, the victim girl is expected to make false statement against the accused. 17] The another material witness is Sou.Bhaghyashri Rahul Gaikwad examined at Exh.15 who is the neighbourer of the complainant. On perusal of her evidence it is explicit that the complainant Renu was able to call the accused from the house to bring the mixer. It is further clear that the complainant Renu was not interested to file complaint against the accused, but her husband compelled her to file present complaint against the accused, as well as the social worker Manisha was also accompanied the complainant while lodging the complaint. This witness admitted that the victim girl Achal was not able to bring the mixer from the house of 10 Spl.Case No. 127/2013 [ Judg. ] the accused. So, if the evidence of complainant, her daughter Achal and the neighbouring lady Bhagyashri Gaikwad considered alongwith the circumstances of the case, it is hard to believe that the victim girl Achal had been to the house of the accused to bring the mixer and the accused removed the wearings of Achal and moved/touched his hand on the body of girl Achal. 18] Moreover, the I.O. A.P.I.Sachin Ambre is examined at Exh.19 . It has come in his evidence that the accused Pappu was residing with Ranjit Sharma the husband of the sister of the accused. It means the accused was not living alone in the house. So, the accused is not expected to do such shameful conduct with Achal or the other persons residing in the house are not expected to allow the accused to do such conduct with victim girl Achal. The I.O. also admitted that he did not record the statement of lady social worker Manisha Karlad who visited to the house of accused alongwith the others. Then it was the duty of the I.O. to record the statement of such independent witness pertaining to the incident, but not recorded. 19] The spot panch P.W.5 Vikas Bansode examined at Exh.16 did not support to the prosecution case. He denied about going to the house of the accused i.e. spot of incident to act as spot panch. So the contents in the spot panchanama 11 Spl.Case No. 127/2013 [ Judg. ] are not proved. 20] P.W.3 Bhupendra @ Rinku who is the husband of the complainant Renu is not the eye witness of the incident and his statement came to be recorded on 12/6/13 after lapse of 6 days. So, his evidence carries no weightage. But his evidence make it clear that the weight of the mixer was about 1 to 1 ½ kg. Considering the weight of the mixer , I think the victim girl Achal being aged about 3 yrs. is not expected to move the same from the house of accused to her own house. 21] Therefore, if the evidence of the prosecution considered alongwith the circumstances of the case, the prosecution is failed to prove that the accused removed the nicker of the victim girl Achal and moved his hand on her body likely to create shame in the mind of Achal. So, I record my finding to point Nos. 1 & 2 in the negative. 22] Considering my findings to point Nos.1 & 2 in the negative and the reasons stated therefor, the accused is entitled to acquittal of the offences punishable U/Sec.354 of I.P.C. and Sec.8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Hence, I proceed to pass the following order : 12 Spl.Case No. 127/2013 [ Judg. ] ORDER 1. The accused Pappu Sukulal Rai, is hereby acquitted as per the provision under section 235(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure of the offences punishable under Section 354 of the Indian Penal Code and under Section 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act. 2. The bail bond executed by the accused stand cancelled. Surety is discharged. 3. The accused is directed to furnish fresh P.B. & S.B. of Rs.15,000/­ in compliance with the provisions of section 437(A) of Cr.P.C. to abide himself to appear before Appellate Court in case of appeal is preferred by the prosecution. Thane (N.N. Shrimangale) Date:­7/4/2017 District Judge–4 & Addl. Sessions Judge & Special Judge, Thane

Special P.P. for the State and Ld. advocate for the accused. 7] The following points arise for my determination with my findings thereon for reasons to follow: POINTS FINDINGS 01. Does the prosecution prove that on ...In the negative. 04.10.2014, at about 3.00 hours at Bhawaninagar Chawl, R.No.12, Near Smashanbhumi, Penkar pada, Mira Road (E), accused used criminal force to daughter of complainant, a minor aged ­15 years 4 Spl.Case (Pocso) No.258/2014... Jud. CNR No. MHTH01­006919­2014 intending to outrage her modesty? 02. Does prosecution prove that on the aforesaid ...In the negative. date, time and place, the accused, committed sexual assault on daughter of complainant, a minor aged­15 years ? 03. What order ? Accused is acquitted as per final order. REASONS AS TO POINT NOS.1 TO 3: 8] Suneeta Rajbhar (P.W.1) deposed that victim girl born on 18.1.2000. The accused is 20 years old. Her family including herself, her husband, three daughters, her brother­in­law Rajbir and accused Ajay were residing together. It is undisputed that victim girl and accused were sleeping in the same hall on the floor on fateful day. It has come in the evidence of Suneeta Rajbhar (P.W.1) that she saw Ajay's hand on the breast of her daughter. Victim girl (P.W.2) deposed that her two brothers and she herself slept towards wall. The accused slept besides her brothers. Her uncle Rambridge slept beside his son. She woke up at 3.00 a.m.. She saw that Ajay Rajbhar was beside her. Her mother had woke up her. Her uncle Rambridge also woke up and slapped his son. Kundan Jadhav (P.W.3) has deposed that he recorded complaint (Exh. 15). 9] It has come in evidence of Suneeta Rajbhar (P.W.1) that she woke up because of barking of dog. She doubted the accused and so lodged complaint. Victim girl deposed that she was in deep sleep. So, she does not know what had happened. She does not want to speak against her cousin. It has come in evidence of victim girl and her mother that they have not seen the 5 Spl.Case (Pocso) No.258/2014... Jud. CNR No. MHTH01­006919­2014 accused moving the hand on the breast of the victim girl. It appears that Suneeta (P.W.1) woke up and suspected accused of molesting her daughter. Victim girl deposed that she do not want to go ahead with the case. It appears that the informant has suspected that accused had put the hand on the body of her daughter. It also appears that the boy and the girl were in the deep sleep. Thus, it appears that the prosecution story is based on suspicion. Victim girl herself do not want to say that her cousin had a bad intention. Hence, I extend benefit of doubt to accused and answer point Nos.1 and 2 in the negative. In result, I proceed to pass following order: ORDER 1] The accused Ajay Rambridge Rajbhar is hereby acquitted under Sec. 235(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure from the offence under Secs.354 of IPC and S. 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] His bail bond stands cancelled. 3] Accused shall furnish P.R. and S.B. of Rs. 15,000/­ in view of proviso 437(A) of Cr.P.C.
