Presided over by S.C. Khalipe ­Additional Sessions Judge, Thane SPECIAL CASE NO.259/2014 Exh.No. The State of Maharashtra Through Turbhe M.I.D.C. Police Station. ….. Prosecution V/s. Bhaurao Undaraji Jadhav. Age 47 years, Occ:Agriculturist R/at. R.No.551, Ashtavinayak Chawl, Pavanegaon, Navi Mumbai. ..... Accused Offence punishable under section 354 of Indian Penal Code and section 5(M),8,9 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Appearance: A.P.P. Smt. Hiwrale for the prosecution. Advocate Smt. Reena Korade for the accused. :J U D G M E N T: (Delivered on this 14th Day of November, 2017) 1. The case of the prosecution is that:­ The accused Bhaurao Undaraji Jadhav, aged 48 years 2 Judgt. Spl. Case No.259/2014 resides in the neighbourhood of the informant. The informant's daughter is aged 6 years old. The alleged incident took place on 09/05/2014. The accused removed the nicker of the victim. Previously, the accused had given his penis into the hands of the victim. The victim narrated this incident to her grand mother. Accordingly, the grand mother lodged F.I.R. against accused on 10/05/2014 in Turbhe M.I.D.C. police station. C.R.No.I­117/2014 was registered and investigated by Shri.Prashant Bhalchandra Potdar. He recorded the statement of witnesses, prepared panchnama of the spot, seized clothes of victim and the accused and sent it to FSL, Kalina. The victim's statement under section 164 of Cr. P.C. was also recorded. Then he sent the charge­sheet. 2] My learned predecessor framed charge against accused under section 354 of I.P.C. and 5(M),8,9 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. The accused pleaded not guilty. 3] Considering the evidence on record following points arose for my determination. I have given its findings with reasons as under­ Sr.No Points Findings 1. Does prosecution prove that on In 09/05/2014 in the afternoon the accused Negative used cirminal force upon the victim aged 6 3 Judgt. Spl. Case No.259/2014 yrs. intending to outrage her modesty and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 354 of Indian Penal Code? 2. Does prosecution prove that on the same In date, time and place accused committed Negative sexual assault upon the minor victim aged 6 years and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 5(M),8,9 of POCSO Act? 3. What order? As per final order. REASONS AS TO POINT NOS.1 TO 3:­ 4] To prove the offence, the prosecution has examined victim (Exh.9), informant Pw­2(Exh.10) and the investigation officer Shri. Prashant Bhalchandra Potdar (Exh.12). The age of the victim is not disputed by the accused. The accused is neighbour of the victim. It is also not disputed. 5] From the evidence on record of the victim and her grand mother, they have not supported the case of prosecution. The victim has stated that the accused did not do anything with her. The accused did not remove her knicker and nothing was happened with her. The informant­Pw­2 stated that she has not narrated the portion marked 'A' in her 4 Judgt. Spl. Case No.259/2014 F.I.R. to the police. The Pw­2 grandmother of victim has stated that she has told this fact to her sons. Her sons stated that their friends Ganesh Billu Rathod, Nitin Shankar Chavan had seen accused in the gallery of Shivnarayan Jaypal Sing. Her son stated that his friends had seen that accused had given his private part in the hands of the victim­Pw­1. In the cross­examination Pw­2 has admitted that she do not know about the incident and she has stated nothing and her grand­ daughter i.e. victim is mental. Therefore, she does not remember anything. She has no complaint against the accused. 6] The investigation officer Shri. Prashant Potdar has stated that he has prepared the panchnama of the spot. Portion marked 'A' in the F.I.R. was recorded as per the say of informant. He seized the clothes of the victim and accused. He collected school leaving certificate of the victim. 7] The prosecution has not examined any other witness to prove the alleged incident. Thus, there is no eye witness. The victim and the informant have not supported the case of prosecution, therefore, alleged incident could not be proved by the prosecution. The previous incident as alleged by the prosecution is also not proved because the prosecution has not examined eye witnesses on that point. Therefore, there is no evidence absolutely against the accused. Therefore, the 5 Judgt. Spl. Case No.259/2014 offences charged against the accused are not at all proved. Therefore, I answer the points in the negative. The accused is, therefore, liable to be acquitted. I pass following order:­ ORDER 1] The accused Bhaurao Undaraji Jadhav is hereby acquitted under section 235(1) of Criminal Procedure Code for the offence punishable under section 354 of Indian Penal Code and section 5(M),8,9 of POCSO Act, 2012. 2] The bail bonds of accused is canceled and surety is discharged. 3] The accused is directed to furnish PB and SB of Rs.15,000/­(Rs.Fifteen Thousand only) to comply the provisions of section 437(A) of Criminal Procedure Code. 4] The muddemal clothes being worthless be destroyed as per rules. D. 00 10 14 IN THE COURT OF AD HOC DISTRICT JUDGE­3, & ADDITIONAL SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE AT : THANE [ Presided Over by Shri.R.S.Patil (Bhosale)] SPL. CASE (CHILD PROT.) NO. 236 OF 2017 CNR­MHTH01­007005­2017 Exh. No. State of Maharashtra ( Through Bhayandar Police Station ) … Prosecution Vs. Bhavani alias Golu Rameshwar Kir, Age 21 years, R/at: Laukhar Talai, Tal. Post­ Thane Shivani Malva, Dist.­ Houshangabad, Madhya Pradesh. … Accused. Offence Punishable Under section 363, 376(2) of the Indian Penal Code and section 4 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 Appearances : Shri. S.D. Londhe, Smt. U.P. Moholkar, Smt. R.N. Hiwrale, V.A. Kulkarni, Ld. A.P.P. for the State Shri. G.J. Bhowar, B. W. Gaikwad, Ld. Advocates for the accused. 2 Spl. Case No. 236/17 (Judg.) JUDGMENT ( Dictated and delivered on 27 th day of August, 2018 in Open Court ) 1] In this case accused is prosecuted for the offence punishable under section 363, 376(2) of the Indian Penal Code and section 4 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] Prosecution's case in short is as follows : Complainant Ramnaresh Ramsabar Mourya is residing at Indiranagar, Kalwa, Thane alongwith his wife Rutha, sons Santosh, Ajay, Sunny and daughter Kajal and Achal. His daughter Kajal was of 14 years on 06/03/2017. On that day at about 17.00 hours said Kajal left her paternal house by stating that she is going to the house of her maternal uncle namely Chhotkan Mourya, resident of Ganesh Deval Nagar, Bhayandar (W) on the eve of Holi. On 14/03/2017 complainant phoned to said Chhotkan and enquired that festival of Holi is over and why he has not sent Kajal to his home. At that time Chhotkan informed to complainant that on 10/03/2017 at about 17.00 hours, he made boarded to Kajal in the bus at Bhayandar proceeding towards Thane. But Kajal did not return to house of her father. Therefore, on 17/03/2017, complainant lodged complaint against unknown person alleging that he has kidnapped his daughter from his lawful guardianship. 3 Spl. Case No. 236/17 (Judg.) 3] On the basis of said complaint C.R. No. I­99/2017 was registered and assigned it for investigation to Vijay Patil, PSI. He investigated the offence. He found out the location of accused on the basis of mobile of accused having No.7440609648 from said mobile. It was transpired that accused is at Shriram Nagar, Lasudiya Mori, in front of Reliance Tower, Laxmi Petrol Pump, Devas nagar, Lasudiya, Indore, M.P. Therefore, I.O. went to said place, took help of local police, enquired with Ravi Boria about accused and victim girl. At that time he informed him that accused, victim girl and father and mother of accused are residing in his room on rent since last three months. Accordingly, Ravi Boria produced accused, victim girl Kajal and mother of accused before I.O. I.O. enquired with them. On said place I.O. prepared panchanama of the spot of incident, recorded statements of victim girl and other witnesses, I.O. collected birth date certificate of victim girl, got medically examined accused and victim girl, took necessary samples and forwarded to Forensic Science Laboratory, Kalina, Santacruz, Mumbai and as sufficient evidence is gathered against accused, he lodged chargesheet against him on 13/10/2017. I.O. arrested accused on 30/07/2017. Accused is in jail till today. Hence, case is tried as under trial prisoner. 4] Charge against accused is framed at Exh.5 on 18/05/2018. Particulars of the charge were read over and explained to accused in vernacular. But accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. Hence, this prosecution. In his defence accused denied entire evidence adduced by prosecution against 4 Spl. Case No. 236/17 (Judg.) him. 5] The points arise for my determination with my findings thereon are as follows : SR. NO. POINTS FINDINGS 1] Does prosecution prove that on 10/03/2017 at about 5.00 p.m. within the jurisdiction of Bhayandar police station accused … In the negative. kidnapped victim girl Kajal, age 14 years from his lawful guardianship ? 2] Does prosecution prove that since 10/03/2017 till 29/07/2017 accused committed rape on victim girl Kajal from time to time at … In the negative. Madhya Pradesh ? 3] Does prosecution prove that on the same dates, time and place accused committed penetrative … In the negative. sexual assault on victim girl Kajal ? 4] What order ? … As per final order. :REASONS: 6] In order to prove alleged guilt of the accused, prosecution has examined P.W.No.1 Kajal Ramnaresh Mourya, P.W. No.2 her father complainant Ramnarayan Ramsabar Mourya, P.W. No.3 Smt. D.D. Shivsharan, Lady police constable, P.W. No.4 Shri. B.R. Gosavi, an I.O., P.W. No.5 Shri. N.D. Lahange, API, an I.O. and P.W. No.6 Dr. Pradnya Baral at Exh. 11, 12, 18, 24, 28 and 37 5 Spl. Case No. 236/17 (Judg.) respectively. Prosecution has produced complaint, panchanama of the spot of incident, forwarding letters sent to Forensic Science Laboratory, Kalina, Mumbai alongwith sample dated 01/08/2017 and 10/08/2017, letter sent to Rescue Foundation dated 11/09/2017, a letter sent to medical officer for examination of accused and victim girl Kajal, examination paper of accused at Exh.13, 25, 29, 30,31, 38, 39 and 40 respectively. Prosecution has produced Forensic medical examination report of victim girl, age certificate of victim which are at Exh.44 and 45 respectively. Prosecution has filed evidence close pursis at Exh.46. 7] In the light of the above mentioned evidence adduced by prosecution, I proceed to record my findings on each point as follows : AS TO POINT NOS. 1 TO 3 : 8] P.W. No.1 Kajal, a victim girl has stated in her evidence that she is of 18 years. She cannot state her birth date and not taken education. Accused is not known to her. She has specifically stated in her evidence that it did not happen that at the time of incident in the year 2017 when she alighted at Thane bus stop, somebody took her to village Itarsi, Madhya Pradesh and that person took her to his village, promised to marry with her and then kept physical relations with her. The said witness has specifically stated in her evidence that it is not so happened that therefore, she became pregnant of three months. Hence, on oral request of Ld. APP for State said witness was declared hostile and permitted to be 6 Spl. Case No. 236/17 (Judg.) cross examined. But in her cross examination also, Ld. APP for State could not elicit material in support of his case. So, above mentioned evidence of victim girl Kajal shows that she is not supporting prosecutions case and adducing any evidence against accused. 9] P.W. No.2 Ramnaresh Mourya, a complainant and who is father of victim girl Kajal has stated in his evidence that two days prior to Holi festival in the year 2017, his daughter Kajal went to the house of her maternal uncle. But she did not return to home. Therefore, he went to police station and lodged complaint. P.W. no.2 has identified his signature on complaint and admitted contents of it which is at Exh.13. The said witness has also stated in his evidence that he does not know the contents of complaint and he cannot read and write. So, above stated evidence of P.W. No.2 shows that on one place he is supporting prosecutions case on the point of contents of complaint and on another place he is not supporting prosecutions case on the point of contents of the complaint. The said witness has further stated in his evidence that after some days police find out his daughter and handed over to him. The said witness has specifically stated in his examination in chief that he does not know with whom his daughter eloped. The said witness has specifically admitted in his cross examination that he has no complaint against accused. So, above stated evidence of P.W. No.2, a complainant shows that he is also not supporting prosecutions case and adducing any incriminating evidence against accused. 7 Spl. Case No. 236/17 (Judg.) 10] P.W. No.3 Darshana Shivsharan, L.P.C., B. No.382 has stated in her evidence that on 30/07/2017 she was appointed in Bhayandar police station and on that day she recorded statement of victim girl Kajal Maurya in presence of social worker Madhuri Roy. The said witness has stated in her evidence that the portions marked by letter A to E in the statement of victim girl Kajal were mentioned as stated by her. The said portions marked by letter A to E are marked as Exh. 19 to 23 respectively. But as stated above, victim girl Kajal has denied that said statement was recorded as stated by her. Therefore, the said evidence of P.W. No.3 cannot be relied upon. Hence, I am rejecting her evidence. 11] P.W. No.4 Bharat Gosavi has stated in his evidence that in the month of July 2017 he was appointed in Bhayandar police station as PSI and investigation of this offence i.e. C.R. No.99/2017 was assigned to him. At that time complaint was handed over to him. Then he received movement order issued by his senior officer and he went to Madhya Pradesh for investigation. On the basis of CDR report he went to Commissioner office, Indore. Then he proceeded to police outpost Lasudiya Mori. Then he went near Cadbury company. In said place one Ravi Boria met him. He inquired with him about the accused. The said Ravi Boria showed him the house in which accused was residing. When he went to that house, at that time victim girl, accused and mother of accused were present there. The said house was owned by Ravi Boria. He has given one room having size 10 feet x 10 feet on rent to accused. He prepared panchanama of the said place in presence of panch 8 Spl. Case No. 236/17 (Judg.) witnesses Udaysingh and Arvind Singh. P.W. No.4 has produced said panchanama at Exh.25 which is admitted by advocate for accused. But as stated above, victim girl Kajal has stated in her evidence that she has not been with any person to Itarsi, Madhya Pradesh and she has not supported prosecutions case. Therefore, document of said spot panchanama and above mentioned evidence of P.W. No.4 is not useful for prosecution to prove alleged guilt of the accused. 12] P.W. No.4 has further stated in her evidence that then he recorded statements of two witnesses namely Ravi Boria and Ankit Chauhan and further investigation was carried out by API Lahange. Then he returned to Bhayandar police station alongwith victim girl and accused. The said witness has stated in his cross examination that accused was not using mobile phone. But victim girl used to phone her maternal uncle. Therefore, on CDR he found out her location. Prosecution has not tendered so called CDR record in evidence. So, from the above stated evidence of P.W. No.4, at the most it can be inferred that P.W. No.4 has found out victim girl. But it is not sufficient to prove involvement of accused in the alleged offence. The said witness has specifically admitted in his cross examination that victim girl has not made any complaint against accused with him. 13] P.W. No.5 Navnath Lahange, API has stated in his evidence that on 30/07/2017 he was appointed in Bhayandar police station and this offence i.e. C.R. No.99/2017 was assigned to 9 Spl. Case No. 236/17 (Judg.) him for the investigation. Before that initial investigation was done by API Vijay Patil and he applied section 376(2)(i) of I.P.C. and section 4, 8, 12 of POCSO Act. But in spite of sufficient opportunities, prosecution has not examined said I.O. namely Vijay Patil. Therefore, prosecution has failed to explain as to why and on what basis said I.O. applied section 376(2)(i) of IPC and section 4, 8, 12 of POCSO Act. 14] P.W. No.5 Navnath Lahange has further stated in his evidence that he produced arrested accused Bhavani before court and obtained his PCR. Then he medically examined accused and victim girl. He took DNA test of accused and victim girl. He forwarded C.A. samples to Forensic Science Laboratory, Kalina, Mumbai. The said witness has produced forwarding letters dated 01/08/2017 and 10/08/2017 at Exh.29 and 30 respectively. The said witness has further stated in his evidence that then he produced victim girl before Child Welfare Committee, Ulhasnagar. As per direction of said committee, he admitted victim girl in Rescue Foundation. As sufficient evidence is gathered against accused, he lodged chargesheet against him. The said witness has identified accused in the court. The said witness has also produced a letter sent to Rescue Foundation dated 11/09/2017 at Exh.31. So, above stated evidence of P.W. No.5 shows that he is in general supporting prosecutions case. But he has not played any vital role in the investigation except medically examining accused and victim girl and forwarding their samples to Forensic Science Laboratory, Kalina, Mumbai. But as stated above, victim girl P.W. No.1 Kajal 10 Spl. Case No. 236/17 (Judg.) and P.W. No.2 Ramnarayan, a complainant, the father of victim girl have not supported prosecutions case. Hence, above mentioned evidence of P.W. No.5 is not useful for prosecution to prove alleged guilt of the accused. 15] P.W. No.6 Dr. Pradnya Baral has stated in her evidence that on 01/08/2017 she was on the duty of casualty medical officer in Civil Hospital. On that day she received two letters from police for examination of accused and victim girl Kajal. The said witness has produced both said letters at Exh. 38 and 39 respectively. 16] P.W. No.6 Dr. Pradnya has further stated in her evidence that then she medically examined accused, took his DNA sample, samples of blood, nails, pubic hair and referred him for opinion to surgeon in respect of genital examination. Accordingly, she took notes on hospital paper which is at Exh.40. The said witness has further stated in her evidence that then she sealed samples and handed over to concerned police constable. P.W. No.6 has also stated in her evidence that she has generally examined victim girl and admitted her in gynecology ward. She has taken her blood sample for DNA examination and handed over to concerned police constable. Further medical examination of victim girl was done in gynecology department by concerned doctor. The said witness has admitted in her cross examination that she has not personally conducted ossification test of the victim girl and inquired about date of birth to her. The said witness has also admitted in her cross examination that she has not conducted test of potency of the 11 Spl. Case No. 236/17 (Judg.) accused. 17] So above stated evidence of P.W. No.6 clearly shows that except collecting samples of accused and victim girl, said witness has not played vital role in the investigation of this case. In spite of sufficient opportunities, prosecution has not produced single blood sample or DNA report of victim girl and accused on record. Prosecution has not examined a medical officer or surgeon who has done genetic examination of accused. Prosecution has also not examined the concerned medical officer who examined her in gynecology department. Hence, evidence of P.W. No.6 is not useful for prosecution to prove alleged guilt of the accused. 18] It is pertinent to note here that advocate for accused has admitted Forensic medical examination report of alleged victim of rape which is at Exh.44. But said document is in respect of preliminary information and consent of victim girl, details of alleged sexual assault etc. In the said report there is specific averment that victim was having sexual relationship with her boy friend since January 2017. But there is no existence of blood stains, semens or injury on her body. The provisional opinion shows intercourse was six months back (January). The said report is dated 01/08/2017 and as per prosecutions case victim girl eloped with accused on 10/03/2017. So, it appears that victim girl was having physical relationship with her boy friend prior to alleged eloping. 19] Therefore, though there is averment in said report that 12 Spl. Case No. 236/17 (Judg.) victim is pregnant of 13 weeks, it cannot be considered as the incriminating evidence against accused. 20] Advocate for accused has also admitted age certificate of victim which shows that on 02/08/2017 age of victim girl was 14 to 16 years. So, all above stated facts and said medical certificate on record shows that victim girl is well aware about the physical relationship and its consequences. As stated above, P.W. No.1 victim girl Kajal and P.W. No.2 Ramnaresh a complainant and father of victim girl have not adduced single incriminating evidence against accused. Prosecution has also not adduced sufficient evidence on record in order to prove alleged guilt of the accused. Therefore, prosecution has failed to prove alleged guilt of the accused i.e. kidnapping of victim girl Kajal by accused and committing rape and penetrative sexual assault on victim girl. Hence, I am recording my findings on point No.1 to 3 in the negative. 21] Hence, I proceed to pass following order :­ ORDER 1. Accused Bhavani alias Golu Rameshwar Kir is hereby acquitted under Section 232 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, of the offence punishable under Section 363, 376(2) of the Indian Penal Code and Section 4 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2. He be set at liberty forthwith if not required in any other offence. 13 Spl. Case No. 236/17 (Judg.) 3. Accused is hereby directed to execute P.B. & S.B. of Rs.15,000/­ under section 437­A of the Code of Criminal Procedure for his appearance before the Hon'ble Higher court as and when such court issues notice in respect of any appeal or petition filed against this judgment and such bail bonds shall be in force for six months. Thane. [ R.S.Patil (Bhosale)] Dt : 27/08/2018 Ad­hoc District Judge­3, & Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

Non­applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 This is an application is moved by applicant under section 438 of Cr.P.C. apprehending arrest in C.R.No.I­249/2015 registered with Wada police station for the offence punishable under section 354, 323 of I.P. Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Mr. N.P.Mokashi for the applicant/accused and A.P.P. Mr. Pujari. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 12.10.2015 at the instance of informant/victim­girl with an indictment that the accused harassed, threatened and sexually assaulted her. 4] The learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant is falsely implicated. He submitted that bare perusal of F.I.R. does not attract provisions of P.O.C.S.O. Act. He further .. 2 .. Anticipatory Bail No.2623/2015 Order below Exhibit 1. submitted that the incident is stated to have taken place in crowded place and therefore, allegations are not believable. There is unexplained delay of 11 hours in lodging the F.I.R. He submitted that the F.I.R. clearly shows that the accused and the girl were having love affair. Nothing is to be recovered from the applicant. The applicant has complied with conditions imposed on him at the time of granting interim protection and prayed for confirmation of the same. 5] Per contra, the learned A.P.P. opposed the application submitting that offence is serious involving minor girl. There are chances of tampering of witnesses and pressurizing the victim and even fleeing away from justice. He further submitted that custodial interrogation of the applicant is necessary and prayed rejection of application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R., it appears that offence under section 4 of P.O.C.S.O. Act is charged against the accused which is about penetrative sexual assault. However, the F.I.R. did not disclose such offence. The only allegations are that the accused forced the victim girl for marrying. Further allegations are that for that purpose he threatened the girl. Looking to the allegations made in the F.I.R. nothing appears to be recovered from the accused. Therefore, looking to the allegations made in the F.I.R. custodial interrogation of the applicant does not appear to be necessary. Anticipatory Bail No.2623/2015 Order below Exhibit 1. learned A.P.P. insisted to impose condition that the accused shall not enter in the village of the informant/victim­girl and the counsel for the applicant also consented for that. In the result, I pass following order ­ ORDER The application is allowed. 2) The interim protection order dated 20.10.2015 passed in favour of the applicant is hereby confirmed on same terms and conditions 3) The applicant­accused is further directed that he shall not enter in the village of the victim­girl and shall not try to contact her and pressurize her in any manner. --1-- ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN ANTICIPATORY BAIL APPLICATION NO.2624/2017 The applicant Nilesh Pralhad Thorat, Vidhyadhar Balkrushan Mane and Rajendra Dattatraya Nalge have applied for bail under section 438 of Cr. P.C. in C.R.No.I­265/2017 registered in APMC police station for the offence under section 376(2) (N) and 366 of Indian Penal Code and section 4, 8, and of POCSO Act. 2. It is contended that the applicants are innocent. The offence is not punishable with death or imprisonment for life. The victim has voluntarily consenting party to act of alleged kidnapping. The victim has not complaint to her parents about rape and kidnapping. The offence under section 376 of IPC is not made out against the present applicants. The offence under section 366 of IPC is also not attributed to the applicants. The victim has voluntarily left the house of parents and joined the accused. The victim moved with the accused during the journey. The present applicants are the relatives of accused No.1. The applicants are ready to co­operate for the investigation. 3. Investigating Officer has given say at Exh.9. It is contended that the victim has alleged that from 2014­2017 the accused Rahul Dhole had kept physical relation with her forcibly and took video clip and transmitted it on Internet and threatened to defame her and kill her parents and with the help of the present applicants accused No.1 kidnapped the victim and committed sexual intercourse with her. Then all the accused persons took the victim at Bandra Marriage Court and forcibly performed her marriage with accused No.1. --2-- 4. Investigating Officer submitted that the present applicants are not residing at the address since lodging of the FIR. The car is to be seized which is used for kidnapping the victim. The alleged incident of rape took pace in the house of accused No.3 and that has to be investigated. If the accused is released on bail the proper chance for investigation will not be given. Accused No.3, if released on bail he is likely to pressurize and threaten the informant and victim. 5. Ld. Counsel on behalf of accused submitted that victim has married with accused No.1 and marriage certificate is produced on record. The present applicants have signed the marriage certificate as witnesses. The victim had sent love letters to accused No.1. Photographs of the victim and accused No.1 are also produced showing that she was happy with accused No.1. 6. Ld. Counsel on behalf of accused relied upon decision in case of Sunil Mahadev Patil V/s. State of Maharashtra in Bail application No.1036/2015 decided on 3rd August 2015 and Ravi Krishna Naidu V/s. State of Maharashtra in Cri. Application No.203/2007 decided on 01.02.2008. 7. The court is of the view that the allegation in the case are serious. The victim has categorically stated in the FIR that since beginning the accused No.1 threatened to defame her and forcibly raped and took video clip and continue to threaten to her. Lastly the accused No.1 with the help of these applicants kidnapped her and forcibly married with her. So facts of these case and above reported cases are different. In this case house where the alleged incident took place is to be verified and it is necessary for investigation to prepare panchanama of the spot. It is also necessary to seize car which was used for kidnapping of the victim. --3-- So custodial interrogation of the applicant is necessary without that the investigation cannot be properly done. So also if the applicants are released on bail they will not fear of law. They are likely to tamper the victim and pressurize her. So considering the nature of offence the application is liable to be rejected. Hence, I pass following order. :ORDER: Anticipatory bail application is rejected. Thane. ( S.C. Khalipe ) Date : 21/11/2017. Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

No.2515/2014 ORDER 1) The application is allowed. 2) In the event of arrest of the applicant namely Manoj Vasant Sadakale for offence punishable U/Secs.354,452 of I.P.C. registered under C.R.No.I­644/2014 at Kalwa Police Station, he shall be released on furnishing P.R.bond of Rs.15,000/­ (Rs.Fifteen Thousand only) with one surety in the like amount, subject to the following conditions : 3) The applicant shall attend Kalwa Police Station on every Tuesday between 10.00 a.m. to 1.00 p.m. and shall co­operate with the investigating machinery. 4) He shall not directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer. 5) He shall not leave India without the previous permission 6) He shall not tamper with prosecution evidence. Thane. (Mrs.V.V.Virkar) Date : 29.12.2014. Additional Sessions Judge­1, Thane. This application has been filed by the applicant Manikrao Shrigiri for his release on bail under section .. 2 .. Anti bail 2515/14 (Ord.Exh.1) 438 of Cr.P.C. in connection with an offence punishable under section 354, 354(d), 354(f)(i), 506(2) of I.P.C. and section 11 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 registered vide C.R.No.I­128/2014 at Bhiwandi City police station. It is contended and argued on behalf of the applicant that he is the father of co­accused Krushna Giri and that provisions of section 354 of I.P.C. does not attract to him. It is further contended that the victim is his niece and his son and the victim were having love affair, however when such proposal was put forth to the parents of the victim they refuse the proposal. It is also contended that therefore the applicant and his son have been falsely implicated in this case. It is further submitted that in such circumstance his custodial interrogation is not required and that he will not tamper with prosecution evidence in any way if released on anticipatory bail and therefore it is prayed that the applicant be released on anticipatory bail. 2] As is clear after grant of interim anticipatory bail, at the time of extension of said interim anticipatory bail the prosecution raised objection that the accused have been trying to communicate with the complainant/victim and continue his threats etc. and therefore an additional condition that the applicant shall not enter Bhiwandi city except for attending the police station as per order, was also put. 3] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it is contended that on refusal of .. 3 .. Anti bail 2515/14 (Ord.Exh.1) the marriage proposal of son of the applicant put forth by the applicant and his family, the son of the applicant i.e. co­accused threatened the victim to take her away and also to rape her if she does not marry him. It is further contended that even after refusal of marriage proposal, the applicant tried to contact the family of the victim to persuade them for the said marriage. It is also further contended that there is possibility of the applicant threatening the family of the victim since both the families are residing in the same locality and that the possibility of repeating the said offence cannot be ruled out. Therefore, it is prayed that the applicant may not be released on anticipatory bail. 4] As is clear the complainant is stated to be 17 years old girl. As is further clear the mother of the complainant is the sister of the applicant and the complainant is stated to be the daughter of said sister of the applicant. From perusal of the complaint and the averments in the application it appears that a marriage proposal was put forth on behalf of the present applicant in regard to the marriage of the accused no.1 with the complainant and it is alleged that since that was turned down by the complainant and her parents, the alleged incident of the accused trying to communicate with her and threatening etc. is alleged to have taken place. As is clear the main allegation in regard to offence under section 354, 354(d), 354(f)(i), 506(2) of I.P.C. and section 11 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 are against the son of the present applicant and the only allegation against the present applicant is that he .. 4 .. Anti bail 2515/14 (Ord.Exh.1) has been trying to communicate with the complainant and her parents and is insisting for marriage. The role attributed to the applicant is only under section 506 of I.P.C. about the threats etc. It is to be mentioned that the offence is registered on 23.05.2014 and the investigation in the matter is almost completed and there appear no need of custodial interrogation of the applicant for which the arrest of the applicant is necessary. Even it is stated that the applicant is ready to abide by any conditions and even a statement is made while arguing the application that if the complainant is not ready for marriage, no such insistence would be there on the part of the applicant. Even an apprehension was expressed by the prosecution that if the applicant go to Bhiwandi City police station to give attendance as per directions of the Court, the applicant may indulge in activities like threatening and pressurizing the complainant and it was therefore prayed that purpose would be served if the applicant is directed to attend before Thane nagar police station and if directions are given that the applicant shall not enter the area where the complainant is residing. In such circumstance the prayer for grant of anticipatory bail by the applicant cannot be denied. 5] In view of the above discussion I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant is entitled to be released on anticipatory bail. In the result I pass the following order ­ ORDER .. 5 .. Anti bail 2515/14 (Ord.Exh.1) The application is allowed. The interim anticipatory bail already granted to the applicant Manikrao Shrigiri vide order dated 31.05.2014 is hereby confirmed on following conditions ­ The applicant shall attend Thane Nagar Police Station on every Monday between 10.00 a.m. to 1.00 p.m. and shall co­operate with the investigating machinery. The applicant shall not enter the area where the complainant is residing. The applicant shall give undertaking that he will not try to communicate the complainant and her family in any manner. The applicant shall not tamper with prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without prior permission of the Court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 16.07.2014. 1 Special Case (Pocso) No. 235/2015 Judgment Received on :­ 20.10.2015 Registered on :­ 20.10.2015 Decided on :­ 24.07.2017 Duration :­ 1Y 09M 04D IN THE COURT OF ADDITIONAL SESSIONS JUDGE, & SPECIAL JUDGE (POCSO) ACT, THANE AT : THANE ( Presided over by Ashutosh N.Karmarkar, District Judge­1 & Special Judge (POCSO) Act, Thane ) Special Case (POCSO) No.235/2015 Exh. No. State of Maharashtra ( Through Turbhe M.I.D.C. Police Station ) …Complainant V/s. Ravindar @ Devendra Ramsudan Pratap Age : 23 Years, Occ. : Service, R/at.: Ambedkar Road, Turbhe Store, Navi Mumbai. Native Rampur Shakarwadi, Tal. Akbarpur, Dist. Ambedkar Nagar, State – Uttar Pradesh … Accused. Offence punishable under Sec. 354 of Indian Penal Code and under 2 Special Case (Pocso) No. 235/2015 Judgment Sec.7 r/w. S. 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Appearances : Shri. S.D.Londhe, A.P.P. for the State Shri. Goswami, Advocate for accused JUDGMENT ( Delivered on this 24th day of July, 2017 ) 1] Accused is facing trial for the offence punishable under Sec. 354 of Indian Penal Code and under Sec. 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] Prosecution Case, in brief, is as under : Victim is residing with her parents, brother, sister, cousin and son of her maternal uncle. She is studying in 11 th standard. On 2.8.2015, she was at home as it was holiday. She was present along with her family members. On that day, at 8.00 p.m., she had been to Chamunda grocery shop which is at some distance from his house. She was returning to home. Accused caught hold her hand and uttered the words “eS rqEgkjsls I;kj djrk gqWa] esjsdks lrkvks er.”She felt shy. She started weeping. She went to home. She narrated the incident to her mother, cousin and son of maternal uncle. Then, her mother and brothers Baliram and Vinod had been to the accused to make enquiry. He gave evasive answers. Some of the people beat him. When the accused was being taken to the police station, he ran away. Then she lodged report. A.P.I. Shedge has recorded the report. 3 Special Case (Pocso) No. 235/2015 Judgment 3] On the basis of report, he registered offence bearing C.R. No. I­182/2015. A.P.I. Shedge has investigated this crime. Victim's supplementary statement was recorded. He also got recorded statement of victim under Sec. 164 of Cr.P.C. After detail investigation, he filed charge­sheet in the Court of law. 4] I have framed charge against accused below Exh. 5 to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. Total denial is the defence of the accused. 5] Prosecution has examined five witnesses. Then, the statement of the accused under Sec. 313 of Cr.P.C. came to be recorded. Total denial is the defence of the accused. The accused has also tried to raise defence in statement under Sec. 313 of Cr.P.C. that he himself and the victim used to meet outside. Both are from different caste. The family members of the victim were not liking it and so, they are deposing falsely. 6] Ld. A.P.P. has submitted that P.W.5 Azim Shaikh has proved School Leaving Certificate of the victim. He has shown that the victim was of 16 years at the time of incident. According to him, defence is taken about friendship between victim and the accused. But, this suggestion was denied by the victim. Evidence of victim gets corroboration from the evidence of her mother. According to him, the defence witness has stated about the affair between him and victim. But, this fact was not stated by him in his 4 Special Case (Pocso) No. 235/2015 Judgment statement before police. 7] On the other hand, Ld. Advocate for the accused has submitted that P.W.1 Ramlagan has no knowledge of incident. He has admitted that the accused used to reside for about six months adjoining to their house. But, this fact is suppressed by the prosecution. According to him, the victim has admitted in the cross­ examination that there are four to five rooms near the spot of incident wherein families are residing. But, none of them is examined. According to him, the victim has also admitted that after the alleged incident, the brothers of the victim have been to accused where some quarrel took place. This fact is also suppressed by the prosecution. When the victim had carried the grocery articles from the shop at the relevant time and when there was such alleged incident then, how she came to home safely. It is also submitted that the investigation officer has admitted about beating to the accused. But, this fact is also suppressed and he did not take care to find out real reason of beating. It is submitted that the prosecution has suppressed the genesis of the incident of assault by the brothers of the victim. 8] Following points arose for my determination and I gave my findings thereon for the reasons stated below: 5 Special Case (Pocso) No. 235/2015 Judgment Sr. POINTS FINDINGS No. 1. Does the prosecution prove that the Yes. accused on 02.08.2015, at about 20.00 p.m., at Ambedkar Road, Turbhe Store, Navi Mumbai, assaulted or used criminal force to a complainant i.e. minor victim girl age 16 years intending to outrage or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby outrage her modesty and thereby committed an offence punishable under S. 354 of Indian Penal Code? 2. Does the prosecution prove that No. accused on above mentioned date, time and place, committed sexual assault on minor victim girl, age 16 years i.e. complainant by holding her hand and pressing it and expressing his one side love to her by saying “eS rqEgkjsls I;kj djrk gqWa] esjsdks lrkvks er.” with sexual intent involving physical contact without penetration and thereby committed an offence defined u/s. 7 punishable u/s. 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act? 3. What order? As per final order. REASONS 9] It is well settled principle of Criminal Law that in order to establish the guilt of the accused, prosecution is required to adduce cogent, convincing and reliable evidence. It is well settled 6 Special Case (Pocso) No. 235/2015 Judgment that the sole testimony of the witness is also sufficient to base the conviction. But, the rule is that it should be above suspicion and should inspire confidence in the mind of Court. Prosecution has examined father of victim P.W.1 Ramlagan (Exh.8), P.W.2 victim (Exh.9), mother of victim P.W. 3 Guddi (Exh.11), P.W.4 I.O. Shri. Shedge (Exh. 12). Subsequently, prosecution has examined P.W.5 Mr. Azim Shaikh, Headmaster of Navjeevan Hindi High School (Exh.22). Accused has adduced evidence of defence witness Mr. Vijay Vitkar at (Exh.17). AS TO POINT NO. 2 :­ 10] In order to establish the guilt of accused defined under Sec. 7 punishable under Sec. 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, the prosecution is required to establish that the accused has touched the parts of the body of victim as contended in Sec. 7 of the Act or does any other act with sexual intent and which involves physical contact without penetration. 11] Victim has stated that her date of birth is 03.07.1999. The alleged incident is dtd. 02.08.2015. P.W.5 Azim Shaikh, the Headmaster of Navjeevan High School has stated that the victim is student of their school. She got admitted to the school in 2012. They run classes from 1st to 10th standard in their school. He is the Headmaster of secondary school. It is further stated that the victim got admitted in their school in 1 st standard. After passing 7th 7 Special Case (Pocso) No. 235/2015 Judgment standard, she got School Leaving Certificate and it was submitted in the secondary school while getting admission in 8 th standard. According to him, date of birth of victim is 03.07.1999. Nothing is brought on record in the cross­examination to disbelieve his testimony. Even accused has brought on record in the evidence of victim's father that he was married on 1994 and victim was born after five years of their marriage. Considering the evidence and School Leaving Certificate on record, it can be said that on the date of incident, the victim was below 18 years of her age. 12] According to victim, on 02.08.2015, at about 8.00 p.m., she had been to Chamunda Kirana Store to bring some articles on say of her mother. She was returning to home. Accused was present in the lane. He caught hold her hand and uttered the words “eS rqEgkjsls I;kj djrk gqWa] esjsdks lrkvks er.” Victim has also stated that accused has seen towards her in such a manner so that she shall feel shy. She started weeping. She rescued herself. She went to home and narrated the incident to her family members. Then, her mother had been to the accused along with brothers of victim. The accused gave evasive reply. The people who gathered there, beat him. They were taking the accused to police station, but he ran away. She lodged report Exh. 10. But, the oral evidence of the victim does not reveal that the accused has touched the parts of her body as given in Sec. 7 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. 8 Special Case (Pocso) No. 235/2015 Judgment 13] The mother of the victim has also stated that the victim came to home and was weeping. She narrated that the accused caught hold her hand. She rescued herself. She has also stated the words uttered by the accused which were stated by the victim in her evidence. Both these witnesses have identified the accused. The accused himself has brought on record in the cross­ examination of father of victim that accused was residing in front of their house for six months and then, he resided for 6 to 7 months adjoining to their house. Ld. Advocate for the accused has submitted that the fact that accused was residing nearby the house of victim is suppressed by the prosecution. 14] It is to be noted that the recitals of the report (Exh.10) itself shows about the residence of this accused nearby the house of victim. So, it is difficult to accept the submissions of Ld. Advocate for the applicant. It is already discussed that the victim has nowhere stated that the accused has touched the part of her body as given in Sec. 7 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. It is also to be established that the alleged act of the accused was with sexual intent. 15] In order to ascertain the meaning on the said point of expression “ Sexual intent”, reliance is to be placed in case of Bandu Vitthalrao Borwar V/s. State of Maharashtra, Criminal Appeal No. 50 of 2016, ( Bombay High Court). It is held in paragraph 10 as under : 9 Special Case (Pocso) No. 235/2015 Judgment Para 10 “After all intention of a person is his state of mind and has to be discerned from the surrounding facts and circumstances. If one cannot, as a human being, physically enter into a mind of another to read and see what is being cooked there, one can surely know it by evaluating all that which is perceivable or felt by human senses such as words, body­ language, gestures, reactions and everything that is a physical manifestation of working of human mind. If somebody says that he is in love with another person or asks another person as to why the other person does not love him, such expression of a feeling or expectation of a particular feeling from another person would not by itself amount to an intent exhibiting some sort of sexuality.” It is held in Para 11 as under : Para 11 “It is obvious that the intent, which is nothing but a state of mind, must be to establish some sort of physical contact or must be related to or associated with sex or indicative of involvement of sex in the relationship, if it is to be considered as sexual. There should be something more which must suggest that the real intention is to drag in the angle of sex, if the words uttered are to be taken as conveying Sexual intent.” So, in view of above citation, it will be difficult to accept that the alleged act of accused was with sexual intent. The evidence on record will fall short to establish the guilt of accused defined under 10 Special Case (Pocso) No. 235/2015 Judgment Sec. 7 and punishable under Sec. 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Therefore, I answer point No.2 in the negative. AS TO POINT NO.1:­ 16] In order to establish the guilt under Sec. 354 of Indian Penal Code, prosecution is required to establish that; 1) That the person aggrieved was a woman; 2) That the accused assaulted or used criminal force to her; 3) That he did so intending to outrage her modesty or intending that he was likely to do so. 17] Victim has stated that on 02.08.2015, at 8.00 p.m., she was returning from Chamunda Grocery Store. Incident occurred in the lane. The accused caught hold her hand and has stated“eS rqEgkjsls I;kj djrk gqWa] esjsdks lrkvks er.” Victim has also stated that the accused has seen towards her in such a manner that she should feel shy. She rescued herself. She started weeping. She went to home and narrated the incident to her mother and brothers. Then, her mother and brothers had been to accused to make enquiry. He gave evasive reply. They were taking accused to police station. But, he ran away . Then, the report was lodged. Her evidence also gets support from the evidence of her mother. She has also stated exactly the same story. 11 Special Case (Pocso) No. 235/2015 Judgment 18] It is but natural that the victim will narrate such type of incident to her close relatives and P.W.2 who is the mother of victim. The accused himself has brought on record that the accused is also residing in the same vicinity of victim. It is brought on record that initially accused was residing in front of the house of victim. Then, he resided for few months adjoining to their house. There is nothing in cross­examination of victim to discard her testimony on this material aspect. 19] According to Ld. Advocate for the accused, the victim has admitted that there are rooms to both the sides of the spot where alleged incident took place and five to six families are residing there. It is submitted that it is improbable that none of those family members have seen the incident. But, it is to be noted that the accused has not brought on record that at the relevant time, the persons were actually residing in those rooms and were present there. Similarly, also, there is nothing in the cross­ examination of P.W.3 Guddi, mother of the victim to disbelieve her testimony. However, some suggestions to the victim itself show that there was some incident. 20] It is suggested that after the incident both the brothers of the victim had been to the accused to make enquiry. The suggestion is also given to P.W.3 Guddi that when they had been to police station, they were intending to settle the dispute. Accused has also examined defence witness Mr. Vijay Vitkar. We will discuss 12 Special Case (Pocso) No. 235/2015 Judgment his evidence later on. But, it has come on record in the cross­ examination of D.W. Vijay that he does not know about the incident. He learnt about the incident from his wife. But, these details support the evidence of the victim. 21] The accused has also tried to suggest in the cross­ examination of the victim that victim and the accused were having visiting terms with each other and the victim's father was not liking it. Same type of suggestion was given to P.W. 3 Guddi. Both the witnesses have denied this suggestion. Same type of defence was tried to be taken by the accused during his statement under Sec. 313 of Cr.P.C. But, there is nothing in the cross­examination of victim or her mother to support the stands of the accused. 22] Defence witness Vijay has stated that the victim is residing in front of his house. Accused used to reside with other persons adjoining to the house of victim. According to him, he has seen love affair between the victim and the accused. He has not given the details of it. In the cross­examination, he has admitted that at the time of incident, he was busy with his job. He learnt about the incident from his wife. He has also admitted that his statement was recorded by police in which he has not stated about the love affair between victim and the accused. So, this makes it clear that this defence witness has stated about the love affair afterthought. So, his evidence will not be helpful to the accused. 13 Special Case (Pocso) No. 235/2015 Judgment 23] Investigation Officer Mr. Shedge has stated that he visited the spot and drew spot panchanama Exh. 13. The accused has just suggested that the false panchanama was drawn. But, there is no reason for A.P.I. Mr. Shedge to depose against the accused. The spot panchanama (Exh.13) reveals that the incident occurred in the lane having width of 4ft. and length of 13 mtrs. This panchanama itself shows that there is only one room towards north from the spot which is locked. So, it appears from the evidence of victim and other material on record that the incident has taken place in a lane. It has not taken place in day light. Incident is of 8.00 p.m. The accused was residing in the same lane and the victim was knowing him. Victim has specifically stated that accused caught hold her hand and uttered the words “eS rqEgkjsls I;kj djrk gqWa] esjsdks lrkvks er.” She has also stated that accused was looking in such a manner that she should feel shy. So, this clearly indicates that the accused had used force and had caught hold the hands of victim and that force becomes criminal as it has done against the consent of victim. 24] The evidence of victim clearly indicates that there was intention in committing an offence or to cause injury and to cause annoyance to the victim. The ultimate test for ascertaining whether the modesty had been outraged is whether the criminal force used against the victim by the accused is capable of shocking the sense of decency of woman. Reaction on the part of the victim after the incident is also required to be seen. Victim has stated that after 14 Special Case (Pocso) No. 235/2015 Judgment catching hold of her hand and utterances of words as stated by her she felt shy. She started weeping. She has immediately narrated the incident to her mother and family members. So, it was a natural conduct of the victim. Even the report was also lodged by the victim immediately after the incident. So, all these facts stated above, are sufficient enough to fix the necessary knowledge. There is also no reason for the victim to depose against the accused and to implicate him falsely. 25] The accused has tried to raise defence that on the day of incident, at 7.30 p.m., he came to home. Vinod Prajapati, Baliram Prajapati, the brothers of the victims and other 5 to 6 persons who were follower of Shivsena party came to his house and they started beating him. According to him, he stated that he will lodge report. He tried to lodge report. But, his complaint was not recorded. Ld. Advocate for the accused has attempted to make submission that investigation officer has also admitted that the accused was beaten. But, he has not taken care to find out the reasons behind beating. There is nothing to substantiate the contention of the accused that accused has tried to put his grievance about beating by moving application to police or his superior officer. So, it will be difficult to accept his submissions. 26] The discussion in foregoing paragraphs lead me to say that the evidence of the victim is worthy of reliance. There is no reason to disbelieve her testimony. Evidence on record shows that 15 Special Case (Pocso) No. 235/2015 Judgment the accused has used force with intention to outrage the modesty or that the accused has knowledge that he would likely to do so. Thus, the prosecution has proved the guilt of accused under Sec. 354 of Indian Penal Code. Accused is to be heard on the point of sentence. 27] Ld. Advocate for the accused has relied in case of Rajabhau Dnyandeo Kharat & Ors. V/s. State of Maharashtra and Ors., 2014 ALL MR (Cri) 4662 and submitted that the history of quarrel and the genesis of the offence is withheld by the prosecution. It is also submitted by the accused that the prosecution has suppressed the fact that the accused was residing in the same lane and about the incident of beating. But, it appears that both these facts are mentioned in the report itself. Facts of this citation appears to be different and it is not helpful to accused. 28] I have heard the accused on the point of sentence. He has submitted that he is serving in the company and is earning member of the family. He has no criminal antecedents. So, lenient view may be taken. On the other hand, Ld. A.P.P. Shri. Londhe has submitted that maximum punishment may be awarded considering the nature of offence. If the leniency is shown then, wrong message will go to the society. 29] Age of the accused appears to be of 23 years. The matter is pending since last two years. The punishment prescribed 16 Special Case (Pocso) No. 235/2015 Judgment for the offence under Sec. 354 of Indian Penal Code, is the imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than one year and which may extend to five years and shall also be liable to fine. Considering the fact that crime is against the woman, I am not inclined to give benefit of the provisions of Probation of Offenders Act. Taking into consideration the age of the accused and earning member of his family and that he is facing trial for last two years, I am of the opinion that following order will meet the ends of justice. ORDER 1] Accused Ravindar @ Devendra Ramsudan Pratap is convicted under Sec. 235 (2) of Code of Criminal Procedure of the offence punishable under Section 354 of Indian Penal Code. 2] He is sentenced to suffer simple imprisonment for one year and to pay fine of Rs. 1,000/­ i.d. to suffer simple imprisonment for two months. 3] Accused Ravindar @ Devendra Ramsudan Pratap is acquitted under Sec. 235(1) of Code of Criminal Procedure of the offence under Section Sec. 7 punishable under Sec. 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 . 4] His bail bond stands cancelled. 17 Special Case (Pocso) No. 235/2015 Judgment 5] Accused is entitled for set off if any as per provisions of S. 428 of Code of Criminal Procedure. [ Dictated and pronounced in open Court. ] Thane, ( Ashutosh N. Karmarkar ) Date : 24.07.2017 District Judge­1 & Special Judge (POCSO) Act,Thane
