Judg.in Special Case (Child Protection) No.263/2016 CNR NO.MHTH01­007029­2016 JUDGMENT (Delivered on 31/01/2019) 1] Accused stands charge­sheeted for the offence punishable under sections 363, 366, 354 of IPC and under section 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] In brief, facts of the prosecution case, are as under : That, complainant Manisha Rajendra Gaikwad was residing at Vashi, Navi Mumbai along with her husband, 3 daughters and one son. Victim girl (avoided to mention the name) is her elder daughter aged 17 years. She used to go in St. Mery School and studying in 12th Standard. She used to leave the house for going to her college at about 6.00 a.m. and used to come back at about 12.45 p.m. every day. So also, she used to attend private coaching class and for attending said coaching class she used to leave the house at about 6.30 p.m. and used to come back at about 9.30 p.m. 3] On 20.06.2016, at about 6.00 p.m., victim girl has left the house by stating that, she is going to class, but, within the time she has not returned to the house. Therefore, her mother made enquiry everywhere. She has also taken the search with the relatives and with her friends. Moreover, she also made enquiry in her class, but they have stated that, on that day victim girl never attended the class. Parents of victim girl taken the search of her. They have also contacted on her mobile but it was switched off. Therefore, mother of victim girl has filed missing complaint in the …..3….. Judg.in Special Case (Child Protection) No.263/2016 CNR NO.MHTH01­007029­2016 police station against the unknown person as her daughter is missing. She has given detail description of her daughter while giving the complaint. Thereafter, police had taken the search. That time, victim girl was found and they brought her in Vashi Police Station and called parents of victim girl. Complainant identified her daughter and enquired with her. That time, her daughter has stated that, accused took her with him without the permission of her parents and they also went at Raghulila Mall. Then they went at Pune and thereafter stayed in one room. In that room there was no physical relations took place between them but accused hugged and kissed to the victim girl and outraged her modesty. Moreover, he has also made a false promise of marriage to the victim girl and then he left her at Swargate Bus Depot and went away from that spot. On that spot said girl was found and police brought her in the police station. Therefore, police recorded the supplementary statement of her mother and also recorded the statement of victim girl. 4] Police registered the offence vide C.R.No. I­219/2016 under sections 363, 366, 354 of IPC and under section 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Then police conducted the investigation, forwarded the accused and victim girl for medical examination, seized clothes of victim girl and recorded the statements of witnesses. After completion of investigation police have sent up charge­sheet against the accused before the Court. …..4….. Judg.in Special Case (Child Protection) No.263/2016 CNR NO.MHTH01­007029­2016 5] Accused appeared before the Court, entering into plea. He pleaded not guilty. My learned predecessor framed the charge against the accused under sections 363, 366, 354 of IPC and under section 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual offences Act, 2012 vide Exh.12 on dated 24.08.2017. His defence is of total denial and claimed to be tried. 6] Considering the above facts, following points arise for my determination on which I have recorded my findings for the reasons to follow : Sr.No. Points Findings. 1. Whether prosecution proves that, on In the 20.06.2016 from Room No.7, Sector 31, negative. Om Sai Niwas, Vashi Gaon, Navi Mumbai, accused took or enticed the minor victim girl of aged 17 years out of the keeping of her lawful guardian without their consent and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 363 of IPC ? 2. Whether prosecution proves that, on the In the same date, time and place, accused negative. kidnapped the minor victim girl and committed sexual assault upon her with intent to compel her to marry with him against her will or in order to force her or seduced to illicit intercourse and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 366 of IPC ? 3. Whether prosecution proves that, on the In the same date at Pune in one hotel accused negative. used criminal force to minor victim girl with intend to outrage her modesty and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 354 of IPC ? …..5….. Judg.in Special Case (Child Protection) No.263/2016 CNR NO.MHTH01­007029­2016 4. Whether prosecution proves that, on the In the same date at Pune in one hotel accused negative. with sexual intent touched the private parts of the minor victim girl and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 7 punishable under section 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual offences Act, 2012 ? 5. What order ? Accused is acquitted. :REASONS: As to point nos.1 to 4 : 7] In order to prove the guilt of accused prosecution examined in all three witnesses. Manisha Rajendra Gaikwad (PW1) is the complainant. She is examined vide Exh.15. Victim girl (PW2) deposed vide Exh.18. Lastly, prosecution examined Investigating Officer API Ajit Mahadeo Gondhali (PW3) vide Exh.25. 8] In the present matter it is an admitted fact that, victim girl is the daughter of complainant Mrs. Manisha Rajendra Gaikwad. Moreover, to prove the age of victim girl her mother produced certified copy of birth certificate at Exh.17. It is a public document issued by Solapur Municipal Corporation which shows her birth date as 31.10.1999. The alleged incidence took place on 20.06.2016. It does mean that till the date of incidence victim girl has not completed her 18 years of age. Moreover, said fact is also not denied by the accused also. Therefore, on the point of age proof of victim girl no more discussion is required. …..6….. Judg.in Special Case (Child Protection) No.263/2016 CNR NO.MHTH01­007029­2016 9] Now I would like to come on the discussion of the offence punishable under section 363 of IPC. It is the allegation of prosecution that, accused took minor victim girl with him without the consent of her parents. Therefore, I would like to reproduce section 361 of IPC where kidnapping from lawful guardianship is given. Section 361 of IPC speaks that ­ “Whoever takes or entices any minor under 16 years of age if a male, or under eighteen years of age if a female, or any person of unsound mind, out of the keeping of the lawful guardian of such minor or person of unsound mind, without the consent of such guardian, is said to kidnap such minor or person from lawful guardianship”. The punishment for kidnapping is given in Section 363 of IPC that such person shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine”. 10] Therefore, for proving the kidnapping, it is necessary to prove for the prosecution that, accused took that girl with him. Therefore, in the present matter evidence of victim girl is very much important. She has been deposed before the Court as PW2 vide Exh.18. She has stated that, on 20.06.2016 she herself phoned to accused and told him to take her with him. She herself went at Raghulila Mall to meet the accused at Vashi. Thereafter, they went at Pune and stayed in hotel. They both were decided to perform …..7….. Judg.in Special Case (Child Protection) No.263/2016 CNR NO.MHTH01­007029­2016 the marriage. No physical relation was took place between them. She has also stated that, she narrated the said entire story to her mother. Moreover, in her cross­examination she has stated that, it is true to say that she herself made phone call to accused. Furthermore, from Vashi to Panvel they travelled by railway and thereafter from Panvel to Pune they travelled by bus. But during the travelling accused never made any forceful act with her. 11] On this point, I would like to rely on the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India i.e. S. Varadarajan V/s State of Madras, reported in AIR 1865 S.C. 942, wherein Section 361 of I.P.C has been discussed that, ' “ Taking” out of lawful guardianship, college going girl on verge of majority, telephoning accused and meeting him and going with him to Sub­Registrar's office for registering marriage agreement, no threat or inducement on part of accused, girl's insistence on marrying him, held no taking, father of girl keeping her at his relative's house, guardianship of father continues.' 12] In the present matter it has come on record that, age of the victim girl was 17 years at the time of alleged incident, she has attained the age of maturity. If any person took such type of girl with him forcibly then she has an opportunity to shout loudly and call people for her help. But it has come on record that they travelled together, stayed together but she never called anybody for her help by raising shouts and also never called police for her help. The mother of victim girl i.e. PW1 Manisha Rajendra Gaikwad has …..8….. Judg.in Special Case (Child Protection) No.263/2016 CNR NO.MHTH01­007029­2016 been deposed before the Court vide Exh.15 and stated that, accused kidnapped her daughter without her consent. But considering the version of victim girl it is not proved that accused took away the victim girl from the custody of her guardians without their consent. Moreover, there is no eye witness examined by the prosecution to prove that anybody had seen the accused while taking said victim girl with him. 13] Prosecution has examined Investigating Officer (PW3) who has conducted investigation in the present matter i.e. API Ajit Mahadeo Gondhali at Exh.25. He has also stated that, when offence bearing no. I­219/2016 was registered, in that matter PSI B.R. Ilag has conducted the investigation and thereafter it was handed over to him. He arrested the accused, seized his mobile phone from his possession by preparing panchanama vide Exh.21 and prepared its receipt vide Exh.26. He collected the medical papers. Moreover, he has visited at Hotel Rajdhani where the accused stayed along with victim girl and that concerned Manager of said hotel shown the entry of their names as Pankaj Kamble and Nikita Kamble. Those documents are produced by him at Exhs.30 and 31. Furthermore, he has forwarded the sample of accused which was obtained by Medical Officer at Kalina vide Exh.32 and then recorded the supplementary statement of victim girl and also produced her for recording her statement under section 164 of Cr.P.C. which is at Exh.33. Moreover, for proving the conversation between the accused and victim girl he has issued a letter to Nodal Officer to get the CDR and SDR vide Exh.36. After getting sufficient …..9….. Judg.in Special Case (Child Protection) No.263/2016 CNR NO.MHTH01­007029­2016 evidence, he has added section 354 of IPC and Section 8 of POCSO Act as accused outraged the modesty of minor victim girl by kissing her and hugging her against her will. After completion of investigation, he submitted charge­sheet against the accused. 14] As I discussed above, victim girl herself has not supported to the prosecution case. When police recorded her statement as per section 161 of Cr.P.C. on 24.06.2016, she has not stated regarding said fact against the accused. Thereafter, she developed her statement on 31.08.2016 and added the said allegations against the accused. Moreover, when she entered into witness box, she has not stated single word that accused kissed and hugged her. There is a contradiction in her statement which is not reliable and trustworthy to prove the act against the accused. As I discussed above, prosecution miserably failed to prove that accused took the victim girl and kidnapped her from the custody of her parents without their consent. I have gone through the oral version of all three witnesses and documents produced on record. She herself has stated that, there is no physical relations took place between them. Moreover, medical evidence is also not supported to said fact. Medical report of both the persons speak that they are normal and there were no injuries found on their person regarding the sexual assault. 15] Furthermore, it is the allegation of complainant that, accused has made a false promise of marriage with her and tried to commit an illicit intercourse with victim girl. To that respect also …..10….. Judg.in Special Case (Child Protection) No.263/2016 CNR NO.MHTH01­007029­2016 she has stated that, they both were decided to perform marriage and when they came out of the hotel accused went to take some articles, that time when she was waiting for him, police came there and took her at Vashi Police Station. Therefore, it cannot be said that, accused has made false promise of marriage to the victim girl and tried to commit any forceful illicit intercourse with the victim girl. 16] Upon considering the evidence it appears that, there is no corroborative version with the evidence of complainant on record. Oral testimony of victim girl is material which is not corroborated with the version of her mother. Medical evidence has also not supported to the prosecution case. Therefore, only oral testimony of Investigating Officer is not sufficient to hold the accused guilty. Therefore, I come to the conclusion that, it is not proved by the prosecution that accused kidnapped the victim girl by taking her from the lawful custody of her parents and took her forcibly with him. Moreover, it is also not proved that accused stayed with victim girl in the hotel and kissed her and hugged her without her consent and outraged her modesty. Moreover, no evidence is brought on record that he has made a false promise of marriage to the victim girl and tried to commit the forceful illicit intercourse with her as alleged. Therefore, I am of the view that prosecution miserably failed to prove the alleged offence against the accused. Hence, I answer point nos.1 to 4 in the negative. 17] Considering the above said reasons and findings on the …..11….. Judg.in Special Case (Child Protection) No.263/2016 CNR NO.MHTH01­007029­2016 points, certainly accused is entitled for acquittal. Hence, I proceed to pass the following order : Order 1] Accused Bhimratna @ Pankaj Jairaj Kamble is hereby acquitted of the offence punishable under sections 363, 366, 354 of IPC and under section 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, vide section 235(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 2] His bail bond stands cancelled. 3] The muddemal property viz. I­Phone Model A­1387 having SIM Card of Idea Company be handed over to accused after period of appeal is over. 4] Rest of the muddemal property being worthless be destroyed after period of appeal is over. 5] The accused to furnish Personal Bond of Rs.15,000/­ with one solvent surety of like amount in compliance of Section 437­A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. (Pronounced in open court) Thane. (Smt. S.A. Sinha) 31/01/2019. Addl. Sessions Judge, Thane.

1 Special Case No.131/2013 (Judgment) Presented on : 13/12/2013 Registered on : 13/12/2013 Decided on : 07/03/2016 Duration:02­year,02­Months,23­days. IN THE COURT OF THE SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE (Presided over by Ms.U.M.Nandeshwar, Additional Sessions Judge­1, Thane) SPECIAL CASE No. 131 of 2013 Exhibit No. 33. The State of Maharashtra Through Kasarwadavli Police Station Thane, District – Thane. ... Prosecution versus Iman Husain Khaibarmiya Age 27 years. Resident of Room No.19, Om Sai chawl, Kingkong nagar, Waghbil, Thane. …Accused. Offence punishable under section 342, 354­A of Indian Penal Code and under section 7 & 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Appearance ­ Spl.P.P. Mrs. R.A. Navale, for the State. Advocate Mr.Sarkar, for the Accused. 2 Special Case No.131/2013 (Judgment) JUDGMENT (Delivered on 7th March, 2016.) 1] The Accused stands prosecuted for the offence punishable under section 342 & 354­A of Indian Penal Code and also under section 7 & 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act) for confining and committing sexual assault on minor victim­ girl aged about 4 years and for outraging her modesty. 2] The indictment against the Accused are as under ­ [i] Informant Sujata Suresh Das (P.W.1) is resident of room No.15, Om Sai chawl, Kingkong Nagar, Waghbil Naka, Thane. She is staying there with her husband, two sons Sushant and Sandeep and Sushant's daughter i.e. grand­ daughter/victim­girl aged about 4 years. Victim­girl's mother is staying at Dasipur, Tal. Aundh, Dist. Kendrapada, State ­ Orisa. [ii] On 13/10/2013 around 02.00 p.m. victim­girl had been to her neigbourer Megha Soni on the occasion of Navratri for lunch (Kanya­Bhojan). However, the victim­girl did not return for quite sometime. Therefore, informant took her search and found that the door of the house of one Vishwakarma was closed, therefore, she opened the door and seen that one man was laying in naked condition and made the victim­girl to sit on his stomach and moving his hand on her private part. Therefore, informant immediately picked up her grand­daughter and on asking that men disclosed his name as Imam Husein Khaibermiya (Accused) and stated that he was playing with the victim­girl. Therefore, informant lodged 3 Special Case No.131/2013 (Judgment) report against the accused. 3] On her report F.I.R. was registered against the Accused vide C.R.No.I­323/2013 for the offence punishable under section 342 & 354­A of I.P.C. and under section 7 & 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. The investigation was carried out by A.P.I. Amol Sadashiv Walzade (P.W.2). The Accused was arrested in presence of panchas. On 13/10/2013, P.W.2 visited the spot and drawn spot panchnama in presence of panchas. Statements of witnesses were recorded as per their say. Thereafter, investigation culminated into filing of charge­sheet in this Court being the Special designated court under P.O.C.S.O. Act. 4] My learned predecessor the erstwhile Special Judge Smt. V.V.Virkar framed the charge (Exh.4) against the Accused for offence punishable under section 341 & 354 of Indian Penal Code and also under section 7 & 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. The Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial (Exh.5). The Accused took defence of total denial. 5] In response to application under section 294 of Cr.P.C. the defence has admitted spot panchnama [Exh.26] and medical certificate of victim­girl [Exh.27]. 6] In order to prove guilt of Accused Prosecution has examined following witnesses ­ 4 Special Case No.131/2013 (Judgment) P.W.1 Sujata Suresh Das – Informant Exh.15 (Grand­mother of victim­girl) P.W.2 PSI Amol Sadashiv Walzade Exh.28 (Investigating officer.) 7] The prosecution proved and relied on the report and printed F.I.R. (Exh.29 & 30). 8] The prosecution closed its side of evidence by filing Pursis at Exhibit­32. As there is no incriminating evidence came on record against the Accused, therefore, his statement under Section 313(b) of Cr.P.C. is dispensed with. Accused neither examined himself nor examined any witness in his defence. 9] Heard learned A.P.P. Mrs. R. A. Navale for State and the learned advocate Mr. U. K. Sarkar for Accused. 10] On consideration of argument advanced on behalf of both the sides and on perusal of the oral & documentary evidence on record, following points arise for my determination, which are answered with the findings thereon, as under :­ Sr. Points Findings No. 1 ) Does the prosecution prove that on 13/10/2013 in the house situated at Om Sai Chawl, Kingkong Nagar, Waghbil, Thane, accused wrongfully confined the ..No. minor grand­daughter of the informant 5 Special Case No.131/2013 (Judgment) aged 4 years and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 342 of Indian Penal Code? 2) Whether prosecution prove that on the same date, time and place the accused made victim­girl to lie on his stomach and he was naked and moved his hand on her private part and used criminal force ...No. against the victim­girl intending to outrage her modesty and he thereby committed an offence punishable under section 354 of Indian Penal Code ? 3 ) Does the prosecution prove that on the same date, time and place, accused committed sexual assault on victim­girl as defined in section 7 and he thereby ..No. committed an offence punishable under section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, 2012 ? 4) What order ? Accused is acquitted. REASONS As to Point No.1 to 3 : 11] All the points are taken up together for discussion, to avoid the repetition, as evidence about the same in common and inter­connected. Age of victim­girl is 4 Years : 12] As the Accused is facing charge under P.O.C.S.O. Act, therefore, it is incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that the victim­girl was child (minor) at the time of 6 Special Case No.131/2013 (Judgment) incident. The alleged incident took place on 13/10/2013. Informant (P.W.1) deposed that the victim­girl who is her grand­daughter was aged about 4 years at the time of incident. In medical certificate (Exh.27) of victim­girl, her age is stated as 4 years. There is absolutely no challenge to the age of victim­girl. Thus, I have no hesitation to hold that the prosecution proved that at the time of incident, the victim­girl was minor aged about 04 years i.e. below the age of 18 years and she is a “child” as per definition given in Section 2(d) of P.O.C.S.O. Act. 13] Further, as the Accused is facing charge under section 354 of I.P.C. it is incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that Accused either assaults or used criminal force towards victim­girl to outrage her modesty or knowing it to be likely that he will, by his act, outrage the modesty of the victim­girl. So also as the Accused is facing charge under section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, therefore, it is further incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that the Accused with sexual intent touched the vagina, penis, anus, breast of a child or make the child touched vagina, penis, anus, breast of such person or any other person or does any other act with sexual intent which involves physical contact without penetration and by his such act committed sexual assault as defined in section 7 of the P.O.C.SO. Act. 14] To prove the charge against the Accused the prosecution has examined the informant / grand­mother of 7 Special Case No.131/2013 (Judgment) victim­girl (P.W.1) who is the most material witnesses to prove the charge against the Accused, as the victim­girl is of very tender age. Informant (P.W.1) deposed that on 13 th day in the year­2013 around 02.00 p.m. at the time of Navratri festival her grand­daughter / victim­girl had been to her neighbourer Megha Soni for lunch on account of Pooja in their house. Informant went in the house of Megha Soni to bring victim­ girl, but she was not there and Megha told that victim­girl had just left their house. Therefore, informant looked for the victim­girl in their chawl and surrounding area. While searching she noticed that the door of the room of one Vishwakarma was closed which was opened by the informant and found that victim­girl was playing with accused. She specifically deposed that nothing else was happened. But she got scared and shouted and therefore, the people gathered there and somebody called police and recorded her complaint. As the witness resiled from the material portion of her report, therefore, she was cross­examined by the Spl.P.P. However, informant denied of occurrence of any uncalled act in respect of her grand­daughter/victim­girl done by the accused. Thus, from the evidence of the informant, nothing is brought on record to prove the guilt of accused, as informant did not utter a single word against the accused. 15] Further informant (P.W.1) in very specific words stated that her grand­daughter is at her parents' house at their native place and she will not bring the victim­girl for evidence before the Court. Even prosecution did not made any efforts 8 Special Case No.131/2013 (Judgment) to secure presence of the victim­girl and failed to examine her. Further the victim­girl is of too tender age and neither her statement was recorded during the investigation. 16] Further it is not the case of prosecution that accused caused any injury to the victim­girl and even the medical certificate of victim­girl which is below Exh.27, also stated that no external injury were found on perineum and introitus (Private part). 17] The evidence of investigating officer P.S.I. Amol Walzade (P.W.2) is formal in nature, who verified the report of informant which was recorded by W.P.S.I. Patil. He executed the spot panchnama and recorded the statement of witnesses. The portion marked 'A' of the report was proved through this witness. However, as informant did not utter a single word against the accused, therefore, mere proving the filing of F.I.R. is of no help to the prosecution. Thus, there is absolutely no believable evidence and cogent proof on the record to support the prosecution version. Thus, prosecution failed to prove beyond reasonable doubt that accused with sexual intent inappropriately touched minor victim­girl by using criminal force and outraged her modesty or committed sexual assault on her or wrongfully confined the victim­girl in the house of one Vishwakarma. Hence, I answer point No.1 to 3 in negative. Therefore, the Accused is entitled for acquittal. 18] In the result, I proceed to pass following order. 9 Special Case No.131/2013 (Judgment) ORDER 1] Accused Iman Husein Khaibarmiya is hereby acquitted U/Sec. 235(1) of Cr.P.C. for the offence punishable U/Sec.342 & 354 of Indian Penal Code and U/Sec.8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] His bail bonds stand cancelled and sureties are discharged. 3] The Accused is directed to furnish bail bond of the amount of ₹15,000/­ with one solvent surety in the like amount in compliance of provision of section 437­A of Cr.P.C. The judgment is dictated and pronounced in open Court. Date : 07/03/2016. (Ms. U. M. Nandeshwar), Thane Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act),Thane. District Judge ­1 and Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

1 Spl.POCSO Case 268/2016 Received on : 24/10/2016 Registered on : 24/10/2016 Decided on : 16/05/2017 Duration. :Y­00, M­06 D­21 IN THE COURT OF ADDITIONAL SESSIONS JUDGE­5 THANE. (Delivered by Shri. M.M.Walimohammed Additional Sessions Judge­5, Thane AND Special Judge, POCSO Act) Spl.POCSO Case No.268/2016 Exh.No. State of Maharashtra (Through Nizampura Police station). ..... Complainant. V/s. Abdul Mannan Mohd. Riyazuddin Ansari. Age 34 years. R/at In the Power loom Factory of Babu Hasan, 72 Gala, Bhiwandi, Dist. Thane. ...... Accused. Learned APP Smt. Khandagale for prosecution. Learned Advocate Shri Patankar for accused. …..................... Offence punishable under section 354A, 509 of I.P.C. and under section 8 & 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act (POCSO). …................ 2 Spl.POCSO Case 268/2016 JUDGMENT (Delivered on this 16th May, 2017) 1] The accused is charge­sheeted for the offence punishable under section 354A, 509 of I.P.C. and under section 8 & 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act (POCSO). 2] The prosecution in brief alleged that complainant Harshal Zaveri is residing at Gandharva Apartment, Rambag­ 4, Kalyan alongwith his family members. Her husband is serving with Kalyan Jewellers. On 01/10/2016 she had come to her mother's house at Bhiwandi. 3] It is alleged that on 03/10/2016 at about 10.00 p.m. She, her elder daughter Dhanashree aged 14 years, son Swaraj aged 5 years and her brother Shirish and his daughters Prarthana aged 11 years and Prachiti aged 9 years, her sister Rani and her daughter Ankita aged 21 years had been to the shop of Dominoz Pizza, near the office of Nizampura Corporation. They occupied the chair. 4] It is alleged that one unknown person of 42 to 45 years age having beard and was having rosary in hand was watching her. She ignored and thereafter they received the pizza as per order. 5] It is alleged that said unknown person came to her and was watching her. He was using vulgar language. She 3 Spl.POCSO Case 268/2016 informed the facts to the waiter and waiter asked that unknown person to go out. She reported the incident to his brother Shirish and thereafter lodged complaint. 6] During supplementary statement she stated that the said unknown person caught hold the hand of Prarthana, tried to molest her. She informed the fact to the Restaurant Manager and this fact was not mentioned in the complaint because of fear of elderly person in the house. However, as a aware citizen she is giving supplementary statement. 7] On this complaint Nizampura Police Station initially registered crime No.72/2016 under section 509 of I.P.C. During investigation spot panchanama was drawn, CC TV footage was collected. Statement in question answer form of victim Prarthana, Prachiti were recorded. Statement of other witnesses were recorded. Birth certificate of Prarthana was collected. 8] The accused was arrested. The identification parade was arranged and report was collected. 9] It appears that concerned police requested the Magistrate to add section 8/12 of POCSO Act. The Magistrate appears to have passed order “seen and filed”. Thus after completion of investigation charge­sheet was submitted. 10] On hearing learned APP, defence counsel and considering record charge below Exh.5 was framed for the 4 Spl.POCSO Case 268/2016 offence punishable under section 354A, 509 of I.P.C. and under section 8/12 of POCSO Act. 11] The prosecution examined four witnesses. The accused did not examine but produced the copies of documents Exh.24 comprising of joint photograph of family members. The copy of ration card from Darbhanga (Bihar) and xerox copy of affidavit. 12] From the statement under section 313 of Cr.P.C. and evidence on record his defence is of denial. 13] I have heard learned APP and defence counsel today. The APP submitted that evidence of victim coupled with the CC TV footage is sufficient to believe the offence. The learned defence counsel submitted that initially complaint was against unknown person and that too under section 509 of I.P.C. Thereafter though there was attempt to add the POCSO Act, he submitted that accused is religious person was chanting rosary and he did not commit any offence. 14] In these circumstances following points arise for my determination and I record my finding to them for the reasons mentioned hereinafter :­ Sr. POINTS FINDINGS No. 1] Whether prosecution proves that on In the 5 Spl.POCSO Case 268/2016 03/10/2016 at about 10 p.m. near affirmative. Nizampura Municipal Corporation office in Dominoz Pizza Restaurant, Bhiwandi within the jurisdiction of Nizampura police station accused committed an act of physical contact and advance, involving unwelcome explicit sexual overture with niece of complainant namely Prarthana Zaveri aged 11 years ? 2] Whether prosecution proved that In the on the said date, time and place negative. and during the course of same transaction accused tried to insult modesty of niece of complainant Prarthana Zaveri aged 11 years making some sound ? 3] Whether it is proved that on the Partly in the said date, time and place and affirmative. during the course of same transaction accused committed offence of sexual assault/harassment with the niece of complainant namely Prarthana Zaveri aged 11 years ? 4] What order ? Accused is convicted. REASONS ALL POINTS TOGETHER : 15] For the sake of convenient discussion points are 6 Spl.POCSO Case 268/2016 clubbed. 16] The prosecution examined P.W. Harshada Zaveri, who is complainant, P.W. Prarthana Zaveri, victim, P.W. Kiran Wagh, I.O. and P.W. Chirag Chunawala, who was serving as Manager with Dominoz Pizza, Andheri. 17] The fact that initially the complaint was against unknown person and under section 509 of I.P.C. are not disputed. There appears no dispute that subsequently requested to add offence punishable under section 8 and 12 of POCSO Act was made to the concerned Magistrate and he should have allowed the application instead of passing criptic order “ Seen and filed”. There appears no dispute that there was identification parade and original report is at Exh.2. 18] The evidence of P.W. Harshada shows that on 03/1o/2016 she, her two children, two daughters of her brother, daughter of her sister had been to Dominoz Pizza near Municipal Corporation, Bhiwandi. One person seeing her was using filthy language and was saying “Kya chij hai, mal mast hai”. He was wearing cap, white trouser and khamij and was having rosary. I have just discussed that there is no dispute about identification and report of identification parade is at Exh.2. 19] The evidence of P.W. Harshada shows that said person caught hold hand of daughter of her brother 7 Spl.POCSO Case 268/2016 Prarthana. She shouted, Pizza owner caused him to take out. Thereafter she lodged complaint Exh.10. In her supplementary statement she stated that said person touched his hand to thigh of Prarthana and she identified him through video conferencing. 20] The witness attempted filthy language is not mentioned in the complaint. She denied that accused was chanting in the name of God on rosary. She was put up that victim Prarthana was tried to throw salt bottle and to save himself he caught her hand. This in turn shows presence of accused at relevant time on the date of incident but also substantiate his identity. 21] The other material evidence is of P.W. Prarthana. She stated that she is learning in Scholer's English High School, Bhiwandi. On 03/10/2016 her Aunt (complainant), her son, daughter, daughter of another Aunt have gone to Dominoz Pizza, Bhiwandi. One person came and touched her thigh and thereafter caught hold her hand. He told “ Ye mere sath ana chahati hai”. Dominoz Pizza owner caused that person to be out. The said person identified as accused through video conference linkage through jail. 22] The victim admitted that accused was holding rosary and it is chanted by religious person or grand parents. However, she denied that accused was Sadhu and was 8 Spl.POCSO Case 268/2016 chanting rosary in the name of God. She admitted that she felt that he may be changing in the name of God. At the same time denied when put up that she tried to beat accused by throwing salt bottle and to save himself he obstructed her by holding her hand. 23] On the face of record this shows that witness and family members were present in shop and the defence put up that she tried to throw bottle appears improbable. 24] In this context the evidence of P.W. Chirag Chunawala shows that he is serving he is serving as Asstt. Managar, Maintenance with Dominoz Pizza, Andheri. There is a recording of DVR for 20 days. He provided the cassette, pen drive of CC TV footage as per Nizampura police station. He has given certificate under section 65 of Indian Evidence Act as per Exh.18. 25] The muddemal pen drive was allowed to be displayed from the laptop brought by I.O. Shri Wagh in open Court and in presence of defence counsel and as per order on application Exh.19. However, laptop was not working, therefore, in open Court in presence of APP, defence counsel pen drive is watched in the LCD computer of Court. Note was taken that accused is seen having caught hold hand of victim and touched her person. 26] The witness admitted that technically while taking 9 Spl.POCSO Case 268/2016 picture one can cut off and can be pasted another. The learned defence counsel therefore submitted that due to advance technology this is possible to make picture of other place and person can be easily pasted. The submission is not acceptable for the simple reason that nature of case, age of victim, presence of other children, occasion of attendance of Dominoz Pissa leads me to believe that there appears no mischief or any fabrication. The witness Chirag Chunawala has no oblique motive in tampering CC TV footage. 27] This takes me to discuss the evidence of P.W. Kiran Wagh. He received the investigation in crime No.160/2016, recorded supplementary statement of Harshada, drawn spot panchanama Exh.13, collected photographs, recorded statement of witnesses. The copy of birth certificate of victim is at Exh.14. This copy of birth certificate of victim Prarthana shows her date of birth as 08/11/2005. On the face of record she was minor on the date of incident. 28] The evidence of I.O. Shows that he issued notice to shopkeeper of Dominoz Pizza at Exh.15, arranged identification parade and arrested the accused. He submitted charge­sheet. 29] The photographs filed before the Court collectively article 'A' shows the presence of accused and that of victim. The accused is seen having caught hold hand of victim. 10 Spl.POCSO Case 268/2016 30] Now revolving upon the defence firstly that victim thrown the bottle of salt and to save himself accused caught hold her hand is not only unbelievable but improbable. Secondly, the Dominoz Pizza shop where all customers invariably visit including children and family members was not the proper place to chant rosary. 31] At the same time the evidence of P.W. Harshada shows that “ Kya chis hai, mal mast hai” is not whispered by Prarthana. Prarthana stated that accused told “Ye mere sath ana chati hai”. The evidence of P.W. Harshada shows that accused was having rosary. 32] The complaint Exh.10 shows that some vulgar language was used by accused which was audible to hear. However, there is no whisper in her complaint, nor in the evidence. Therefore, the offence prescribed in section 509 of I.P.C. Which requires insult to the modesty of woman by uttering words, making a sound of gesture. The P.W. Harshada is only witness who has come with complaint that she heard vulgar language but what was uttered is not before the Court. Therefore, offece under section 509 of I.P.C. is not proved. 33] So far as offence under section 354A is concerned it requires that if person committed the following act namely physical contact and advance involving unwelcome and 11 Spl.POCSO Case 268/2016 explicit sexual overture or demand or request for sexual favour or show pornography against the will of woman or making sexual colour remarks. The evidence reveals that catching of hand is not disputed by accused. Therefore, there appears physical contact. There were elderly person, other child, waiter, person attending the counter and therefore, they would have control the situation and not the accused who is said to be customer. 34] In this context the complainant Harshada as aware citizen has dare to expose her niece. I find no reason to disbelieve the evidence of particularly victim Prarthana about the catching of hand. 35] The prosecution alleged that offence of sexual assault prescribed in section 7 of POCSO Act. It prima facie requires that whoever with sexual intent touches vagina, penis, anus or breast of the child or make child touch the vagina, penis, anus or breast of such person or does any other act with sexual intent. The requirement on regarding section by necked eye reveals that no such acts are found proved and therefore, the evidence under section 7 punishable under section 8 of POCSO Act is not made out. 36] Never­the­less the offence prescribed in section 11 of POCSO Act of sexual harassment shows that if the person watches or contacts a child either directly or through 12 Spl.POCSO Case 268/2016 electronic, digital or any other means and in this case act under section 11(iv) would be attracted. 37] Having considered factual and legal aspect of the matter, this Court is of the opinion that prosecution succeed in proving the offence punishable under section 354A of I.P.C. and under section 11 of POCSO Act. The point No.1 is answered in the affirmative and point No.2 in the negative and point No.3 partly in the affirmative as offence punishable under section 12 of POCSO is found proved. 38] The last aspect is mentioned as submitted by the defence counsel today that the documents field by accused in statement under section 313 of Cr.P.C. shows family photograph and copy of ration card of Darbhanga, Bihar. There appears copy of affidavit and learned Advocate submitted that accused is mentally of ill health. The fact is not put up to the defence nor there is any prima facie evidence that accused was incapable of making his defence, understanding particulars of charge and therefore, this aspect requires no consideration, being after thought. 39] It is here I have heard the accused on the point of sentence. He requested that he was not having good mental health. It is his first offence. He is reported has age of 35 years. He is in jail from 06/10/2016. In the facts and circumstances and request I am of the opinion that following 13 Spl.POCSO Case 268/2016 sentence would be just and proper. ORDER 1] Accused Abdul Mannan Mohd. Riyazuddin Ansari is convicted for the offence punishable under section 354A of I.P.C. as per sec. 235(2) of Cr.P.C. and sentence to suffer S.I. for one year. 2] He is also convicted for the offence punishable under section 12 of POCSO Act as per sec. 235(2) of Cr.P.C. and sentence to suffer S.I. for one year and to pay fine of Rs.300/­ i.d. to suffer S.I. for one month. 3] Substantial sentences shall run concurrently. 4] Set off be given to them under section 428 of the Cr.P.C. for the period which he under gone in jail i.e. from 06/10/2016 till today. 5] The accused is acquitted of the offence punishable under section 509 of I.P.C. as per section 235(1) of Cr.P.C. 6] Muddemal Pen drive and CD be destroyed being worthless after appeal period is over. 7] Inform Jail Authority immediately. Thane. (M.M.Walimohammed) Dt. 16/05/2017. Additional Sessions Judge­5, & Spl. Judge, POCSO Thane.

Presented on : 24.10.2016 Registered on : 24.10.2016 Decided on : 23.09.2017 Duration : 00Y. 10M.29D IN THE COURT OF SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE, AT : THANE. Presided over by S.C. Khalipe ­Additional Sessions Judge, Thane SPECIAL CASE NO.266/2016 Exh.No. The State of Maharashtra Through Kalwa Police Station. ….. Prosecution V/s. Krushnanand Rammilan Prajapati Adult, Occ: Construction Business R/at. Jaihind Chawl, Near Chota Durga Mata Temple, Waghoba Nagar, Kalwa (E). ..... Accused. Offence punishable under Sections 354(D), 509, 506 of Indian Penal Code and section 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act,2012. Appearance: A.P.P. Smt.Tallar for the prosecution. Advocate Shri. Vishwakarma for accused. :J U D G M E N T: (Delivered on this 23th Day of September, 2017) The case of the prosecution is that:­ 2. From six months prior to 24.04.2016 the accused was following the victim aged 14 years and he would threatened her that “shadi nahi karogi to tujko uthake leke jaunga”. He would also followed her in public latrine and would tell her “kitna din ghar mein chup baitogi”. He also disclosed his friends that victim is their “Bhabi” and thus he was sexually harassing the victim. The victim therefore lodged FIR in Kalwa police station and C.R.No.I­152/2016 was registered against the accused. 3. Investigation was done by P.S.I.Shri. S.S.Kesare. He recorded statements of witnesses, arrested the accused and sent the charge­sheet. 4. Charge was framed at Exh.2 against the accused under section 354(D), 509, 506 of Indian Penal Code and section 11 punishable under section 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. The accused pleaded not guilty. 5. Considering the evidence on record following points arose for my determination. I have given its findings with reasons as under­ Sr.No Points Findings 1. Does prosecution prove that since six In months prior to 24.04.2016 the accused Affirmative was following the victim aged 14 years and attempted to contact her to foster personal interaction repeatedly despite clear indication of dis interest by the victim and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 354(D) of Indian Penal Code? 2. Does prosecution prove that accused In intending to insult the modesty of the Affirmative victim utters the words or makes sound or gesture intending that such word or sound shall be heard by the woman and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 509 of Indian Penal Code? 3 Does prosecution prove that the accused In committed criminal intimidation by Affirmative threatening the victim with injury to her and her parents and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 506 of Indian Penal Code? 4 Does prosecution prove that accused with In sexual intent utters any words or made Affirmative sound or gesture with intention that such words or sound shall be heard by the victim and thereby committed an offence under section 11 punishable under section 12 of the POCSO Act,2012? 5 What order? Accused is convicted REASONS AS TO POINT NOS.1 TO 5:­ 6. To prove the offences prosecution has examined victim at Exh.5, victim's mother at Exh.9 and Investigating Officer P.S.I.Kesare at Exh.11. 7. It has come in the evidence that victim and her mother were residing at Kalwa, Thane. The victim was learning in M.B.S Hindi High School and she used to go to her school at 7.30 a.m. and come back at 3.00 p.m. Her birth date is 19.01.2002. With respect to determination about age of the victim Investigating Officer gave letter to M.B.S Hindi High School and accordingly Bonafide Certificate was given by the said school at Exh.7. It shows that the birth date of victim is 19.01.2002. The question was asked to the accused in statement under section 313 of Cr. P.C. regarding the birth date of the victim. He has admitted that the victim was learning in M.B.S School in 8th standard and her birth date was 19.01.2002. He has not strictly challenged the age of the victim. The fact admitted need not be proved as per the provision of section 58 of the Evidence Act. The age of the victim is not strictly challenged in the cross examination of the victim, her mother and Investigating Officer, therefore, considering the evidence on record the court is of the view that the prosecution has proved that on the date of incident the victim was 13 years 7 months old. 8. It has come on record that the accused was also residing in the area where the victim resides with her family. The accused would follow the victim and would tell her “shadi nahi karegi to utha ke le jaunga” and he would also tell her that “shadi karna padega nahi to jaher pi ke mar jaunga”. He would tell his friends that the victim is their “Bhabi”. Whenever the victim would go to public latrine the accused would follow her, at that place also. Accused would tell the younger brother of the victim that he is his “Jija” and call him as “Jija”. The accused had also threatened the victim that if she gave complaint to the police he would release within one or two days. The accused would stand at the gate of the school of the victim after the school hours. The accused would tell her “Ghar me kitne din chup baithogi” and this was continued for about six months, therefore, the victim gave complaint to the police which is marked at Exh.6. The victim identified the accused before the court.The eivdnece of victim is corroborated with her FIR Exh.6. 9. It has come on record that the victim's mother had previously married with first husband, therefore, in the bonafide certificate of the victim in the school name of her first father was mentioned and after the second marriage of her mother her name was changed as in the name of step father. Accordingly Investigating Officer recorded the supplementary statement of the victim and her mother. 10. The evidence of the P.W.1 the victim is corroborated by her mother P.W.2. Her mother has stated that the victim has disclosed about the incident to her from time to time. She has also stated that the accused threatened her that if any complaint is lodged against him he will be released within two days. She has also stated that after her second marriage the name of her daughter was changed. 11. The statement of the victim was recorded under section 164 of Cr. P.C., before the J.M.F.C. Investigating Officer has denied the suggestion that there was love affair between victim and the accused. The victim has also denied the suggestion in the cross examination that she was talking with the accused on mobile phone and there was love affair between them. So mere suggestions cannot be taken into consideration. 12. Except these suggestions the accused has not brought any other circumstances which tend to disbelieve the evidence of P.W.1 and 2. 13. Considering the evidence on record the court has come to the conclusion that the accused has not disproved the case of prosecution. Accused has not brought any reason to disbelieve the evidence of witnesses. The accused was residing in the same vicinity it is not denied by him, therefore, the evidence of P.W.1 and 2 appears to be probable, believable and trustworthy. There is no reason to disbelieve the victim and her mother. 14. It has come on record that the accused would following the victim for six months prior to 24.04.2016 and he would tell her that he will commit suicide, if she will not marry with him and also threatened her that if she did not marry with her he will kidnap her. He also threatened to cause injury to her and her parents and also threatened to commit suicide by leaving a chit in her name. 15. Considering the evidence on record the court come to the conclusion that prosecution has proved offences under sections 354(D), 509, 506 of Indian Penal Code and section 11 punishable under section 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. 16. The offence under section 11 of POCSO Act is also punishable under section 354(D) of Indian Penal Code. The sentence for the sexual harassment under the POCSO Act and under section 354(D) is with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine. The prosecution has also proved the ingredients of the offence under section 506 and 509 of Indian Penal Code, therefore, the accused is liable to be convicted for all the offences. Date:23.09.2017 (S. C. Khalipe) Thane. Additional Sessions Judge, Thane. 17. Before passing sentence I heard accused on the point of sentence. He submitted that he has not contacted the victim after the incident. The Ld. Counsel on behalf of the accused submitted that he may be given chance for improvement his conduct. 18. In reply Ld. A.P.P. Smt.Tallar submitted that the offences are proved beyond doubt, therefore, accused may be convicted with maximum punishment. 19. Considering the facts and circumstance of this case I do not found any mitigating circumstance. Accordingly, I pass following order. ORDER 1] The accused Krushnanand Rammilan Prajapati is convicted under section 235(2) of Criminal Procedure Code for the offence punishable under section 354(D), 509, 506 of Indian Penal Code and Section 12 of POCSO Act, 2012. 2 The accused Krushnanand Rammilan Prajapati is sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for the period six months and to pay fine of Rs.10,000/­ (Rupees ten thousand only) for the offence punishable under Section 354(D) read with section 12 of POCSO Act, 2012., in default of payment of fine he shall suffer S.I. for the period of three months. 3. The accused Krushnanand Rammilan Prajapati is sentenced to pay fine of Rs.1,000/­ for the offence punishable under section 506 of Indian Penal Code. In default of payment of fine he shall suffer S.I. for the period of one month. 4. The accused Krushnanand Rammilan Prajapati is sentenced to suffer rigorus imprisonment for six months and to pay fine of Rs.4,000/­ (Rupees Four Thousand Only) for the offence punishable under section 509 of Indian Penal Code. In default of payment of fine he shall suffer S.I. for the period of two month. 5. After realization of fine amount the amount of Rs.10,000/­ (Rupees Ten Thousand Only) shall be paid to the victim P.W.1 as compensation after the appeal period. 6. The sentence of imprisonment of above offences shall run concurrently. 7. The accused Krushnanad Rammilan Prajapati was arrested on 30.04.2016 and he was released on bail on 17.05.2016 therefore set off be given under section 428 of Cr. P.C. for this period. 8. The Judgment is dictated and declared in open court. 9. The copy of Judgment shall be given to the accused free of costs. Thane. (S.C. Khalipe) Date:23.09.2017. Additional Sessions Judge,Thane.

IN THE COURT OF THE SPECIAL JUDGE (PROTECTION OF CHILDREN FROM SEXUAL OFFENCES ACT) THANE AT THANE. (Presided over by Ms. V.V.Virkar) Special Case No. 132 of 2013. Exh.No.44. State of Maharashtra (Through- P.I., Kalwa P.S. Dist.- Thane.) ..... COMPLAINANT. VERSUS Omprakash Ramchandra Parikh, Age 46 years. R/at: Room No.301, 3rd Floor, Om Ganesh Society, Ganpatipada, Vitava, Kalwa, Thane. .....ACCUSED. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Offence U/sec. 354, 506, 376(2)(f) & (i) of Indian Penal Code and Section 3 read with section 4 and section 7 read with section 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Appearances :- Mrs. R.A.Navale - A.P.P. for the State. Mr. P.B.Kulkarni - Advocate for the Accused. JUDGMENT (Delivered on 29th September, 2015) 1. The accused stands charged for the offences punishable U/sec.-354, 506, 376(2)(f) & (i) of Indian Penal Code and Section 3 read with section 4 and section 7 read with section 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (here-in-after referred-to as POCSO Act for short). =2= 2. In short the facts giving rise to the prosecution of the accused are that, the victim girl Krupali Omprakash Parikh, aged about 12 years, in the year 2013 was staying with her mother Ratnaprabha Omprakash Parikh and the step father i.e. accused Omprakash Ramchandra Parikh at Ganesh Society, 3rd floor, Room No.301, Ganpatipada, Vitava, Thane. That she was the daughter of her mother from her first husband, her mother had divorced her first husband Atul Shankar Shirke and thereafter she married to accused Omprakash Parikh and had been staying with him alongwith her daughter Krupali and one Swapna Shirke - sister of her first husband was also staying with them. 3. It is also the case of the prosecution that, after her marriage with accused, the mother of the girl had changed her name and also the name of the girl by notification in the official gazette. It is further case of the prosecution that, the accused had evil eye on the girl Krupali and since before the complaint, he committed acts of physical advances with her and used to wink eye towards her, tried to kiss her, even used to see through when she used to go for taking bath in the bathroom, used to touch her private part or press her breast and even at some times stood naked infront of her. He used to threaten her not to tell about it to her mother else he would leave them and they would require to beg on the road. 4. It is also the case of the prosecution that, on 18/09/2013 when the victim girl and the accused were watching T.V., the accused had pressed the breast of the girl and even touched her private part. That time the =3= Spl.C.No.132/2013. mother of the girl was working in the kitchen, but the girl being scared did not disclose the same to mother, but because of the incident the girl did not sleep in the night. Then her mother asked her as to what had happened. Then the girl gathered the courage and stated all the facts to the mother. Her mother took her immediately to the police station and the complaint of the girl was recorded in presence of her mother. 5. On the basis of her complaint, the offence was registered as C.R.No.I-461/2013, U/sec.-354, 506 of I.P.C. and Section 8 of POCSO Act and work of investigation was entrusted to A.P.I. Mr. Kale. During the investigation, the panchanama of the spot was prepared. The girl was produced before the Child Welfare Committee and her statement was recorded before Child Welfare Committee. The girl was referred for medical examination and the certificate in regard to her date of birth was obtained and sample of blood etc. and vaginal swab etc. was obtained. The copy of gazette notification in regard to change of her name also was obtained. The statement of witnesses were recorded. On receipt of medical certificate since it revealed that the girl was rapped, offence U/sec.-376 of I.P.C. was added and such report was submitted to the Learned Judicial Magistrate. The accused came to be arrested and he was referred for medical examination and samples of his semen were obtained and samples obtained and seized muddemal were sent for Chemical Analysis alongwith the letter and after completion of investigation since there was sufficient evidence against the accused, the accused came to be charge-sheeted for the offences punishable U/sec.-354, 506, 376(2)(f) & (i) of I.P.C. and Section 4 & 10 of POCSO Act. =4= 6. The offence under the provisions of POCSO Act are triable by the Special Court and therefore, the charge-sheet was submitted before this court as the Special court for trial of cases under the POCSO Act. 7. The accused was produced before the court. The charge at Exh.-11 was framed against the accused U/sec.-354, 506, 376(2)(f) and (i) of Indian Penal Code and section 4 and 10 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. The contents of charge were read over and explained to accused in vernacular. He pleaded not guilty. His defence as is revealed from cross examination of the witnesses and his statement recorded U/sec.-313 of Cr.P.C. was that there was no marriage between himself and the mother of the girl and they were staying together and had decided to marry after Diwali of the year 2013 and he has falsely implicated in the crime. He claimed to be tried. 8. For establishing the charges levelled against the accused, the prosecution examined PW.1 Ratnaprabha Omprakash Parikh - the mother of the girl, PW.2 - Krupali Omprakash Parikh - the victim girl and the complainant herself, PW.3 - Dr. Supriya Tushar Mahajan - the medical officer who examined the girl, PW.4 - Shriram Sitaram Ikhankar - the panch witness of spot panchanama and PW.5 - I.O. A.P.I. Prashant Tulshiram Kale. The documentary evidence produced, proved and relied upon by the prosecution as per list Exh.-37, which consisted of original Gazette at Exh.-38, true copy of decree of divorce at Exh.-39, original Marriage Photographs two in numbers at Exh.-40 (Collectively) and original birth certificate at Exh.41. =5= Spl.C.No.132/2013. 9. I heard Learned A.P.P. and Learned Advocate for the accused and also perused the oral as well as documentary evidence on record and also rulings cited on behalf of both the parties. 10. It is argued on behalf of the prosecution that, accused is the stepfather of the victim girl and from the testimony of the girl as well as mother of the girl it is clear that the accused had sexually assaulted the girl and committed rape on her and such acts of sexual harassment were committed by the accused for longer period of three years since before the complaint. It is also argued that, the testimony of the complainant girl is corroborated by the medical evidence and also the circumstances that immediately after the girl disclosed about the incident to the mother she had immediately took the girl to the police station and lodged the complaint. It was pointed-out that there is no reason for the girl or the mother of the girl to depose against the accused falsely, who is the husband of the mother of girl and there is no reason to disbelieve the testimony of the girl as well as the mother of the girl. It is also argued that the charges levelled against the accused are required to be held as proved and accused is liable to be convicted. It was also argued that U/sec.-29 of the POCSO Act once the prosecution is lodged, there is a presumption that the offence has been committed by the accused unless contrary is proved and it was submitted that absolutely nothing is brought on record by the accused to rebut the presumption. 11. As against this, it was argued on behalf of the accused that the very fact that mother of the girl and accused were married is not established =6= and not proved and nothing is produced by the prosecution to show that they were married. It was pointed-out that the testimony of the girl is shattered and shaken in all the respect and if at all it was so that the girl was sexually harassed for years together, it is improbable that she would not tell to the mother who is real mother. It was also pointed out that even the fact that the accused has raped the girl was not stated by the girl in her complaint and it is totally an after thought version and concocted story that the accused has committed rape on the girl. Therefore, it was argued that the allegations against the accused cannot be said to be established. It was also argued that presumption is always rebutable and from the circumstances brought on record it is clear that the entire story putforth by the girl as well as mother is concocted and false and presumption has to be held as rebutted and the accused is entitled to be acquitted. 12. On the basis of above facts of the case, following points arose for my determination and I record my findings thereon for the reasons mentioned as under :- Points Findings 1 Whether the prosecution proves that, the accused on 18/09/2013 around 20.30 hrs. in his residential house and even before the said date since year 2011 at same place, he was using criminal force against minor victim girl i.e. his step-daughter namely Krupali, by using to make physical advances her, used to press her breast, used to insert finger in her private part, with intent to outrage or knowing it to be likely that he would ...... Yes. thereby outrage her modesty? =7= Spl.C.No.132/2013. 2 Whether the prosecution proves that on the given day, date, time and place, the accused committed rape on said girl by inserting penis in her private ...... Act and the punishment prescribed for offence under section 354 of I.P.C. is Rigorous Imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years or with fine or with both and offence under section 3 read with section 4 of P.O.C.S.O. Act is punishable with imprisonment of not less than 7 years and which may extend to imprisonment for life and also fine and offence under section 7 read with section 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act is punishable with imprisonment for a term not less than 3 years which may extend to 5 years and also fine. 47. I heard the learned A.P.P. and the accused on the point of sentence. 48. It was submitted by the accused that it is his first offence and leniency be shown to him. It was also submitted on behalf of the accused by learned advocate representing him that, though the offences proved against the accused are of serious nature it is not rarest of rare case wherein the maximum punishment can be warranted. It was also argued that the accused be given chance to reform and he be shown leniency and he be awarded minimum punishment. = 31 = Spl.C.No.132/2013. 49. As against this the learned A.P.P. submitted that looking to the serious nature of offence charged against the accused he is not entitled to leniency and he is liable to award maximum punishment prescribed. 50. Then, so far as the quantum of sentence is concerned it has to be mentioned that, it is well settled that it is the duty of the Court in every case to award proper sentence, having regard to the nature of the offence, the manner in which it is committed and to all mitigating circumstances. Even it is also well settled that in the matter of fixation of punishment for any particular crime, the Court should take into consideration the nature of offence, the circumstances in which it was committed and the degree of deliberation shown by the offender and also that the measure of punishment should be proportionate to the gravity of the offence and it is also the responsibility of the Court to see that the sentence should not be excessive and at the same time it should not be too lenient or liberal. 51. Keeping in mind the above well settled principles, in regard to the quantum of punishment if the facts and circumstances of the present case are taken into consideration it is clear that the accused had outraged the modesty of 14 years old girl who was staying with him as a daughter of woman who has been admittedly staying with him as his wife and not only that he even had been pressurizing and coercing her not to tell all such acts even to her mother. Even he had been committing such heinous acts for a considerable long period of 2­3 years and kept the girl = 32 = always in pressure, trauma and tension and in such circumstances I am of the view that he do not deserve any leniency. But, the aspect also cannot be ignored and over­looked that the allegations of penetrative sexual intercourse and sexual intercourse U/sec.­376 of I.P.C. are not proved and under such circumstances I am of the opinion that the following sentence would meet the ends of justice. In the result I pass the following order ­ ORDER Accused namely Omprakash Ramchandra Parikh is convicted for the offences punishable under section 354 & 506 of the Indian Penal Code and under section 3 read with section 4 and also under section 7 read with section 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. ( II ) The accused is sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for seven years and to pay fine of Rs.5000/­ [Rupees Five Thousand only] and in default of payment of fine, to suffer S.I. for fifty days for offence under section 3 read with section 4 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. ( III ) The accused is sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for three years and to pay fine of Rs.1,000/­ [Rupees One Thousand only] and in default of payment of fine, to suffer S.I. for ten days for offence under section 7 read with section 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. = 33 = Spl.C.No.132/2013. ( IV ) The accused is sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for six months and to pay fine of Rs.500/­ [Rupees Five Hundred only] and in default of payment of fine, to suffer S.I. for five days for offence under section 354 of Indian Penal Code. (V) The accused is sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for one year and to pay fine of Rs.500/­ [Rupees Five Hundred only] and in default of payment of fine, to suffer S.I. for five days for offence under section 506 of Indian Penal Code. VI ) All the substantive sentences shall run concurrently. VII) On realization of amount of fine, an amount of Rs.5,000/­ (Rupees Five Thousand only) be paid to the victim girl Krupali. VIII ) The accused is in jail since 19/09/2013. A set off under section 438 of Cr.P.C. is granted to him against the substantive sentence for the term of the period of detention undergone by him during the investigation, inquiry and trial. IX ) The accused is acquitted of the charge for offence punishable under section 376(2)(f) and (i) of Indian Penal Code. = 34 = X) Since no muddemal property is produced before Court, no order regarding its disposal is passed. XI ) Copy of judgment be given to the accused free of cost. XII ) The proceeding is closed. Date : 29.09.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Additional Session Judge­1, Thane.

Accused is facing trial for the offence punishable u/sec. 363, 376 of Indian Penal Code (hereinafter as IPC) and Sec.4 & 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter referred as POCSO Act). 2. Name of the victim, full name of her family members, place of incidence, name of school are not mentioned in the judgment to avoid disclosure of identity of Victim as per Section 33(7) of the POCSO Act. 3. In short case of prosecution is as follows:­ It is alleged by the prosecution that on 23.6.14 accused kidnapped victim girl age about 17 years and 10 months from the lawful guardianship of her parents knowingly that she will be compelled or likely to compel illicit intercourse and he also committed rape on her and thereby committed the offence u/sec. 363, 376 of Indian Penal Code and Sec.4 & 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 4. Spl.Case No. 262/2014 (Judgment.) offence punishable u/sec. 363, 376 of Indian Penal Code and Sec.4 & 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 6. In support of its case the prosecution has examined following witnesses:­ PW No. Ex.No. Prosecution Witness 1 06 Victim. 7. Considering the evidence given by PW.1 and the hostility of victim, the Ld. APP wisely closed the evidence of prosecution by filing purshis at Ex. 7 to save the valuable time of court and prosecution machinery. 8. Heard ld. Advocate Shri.Sagar Kolhe for accused and Ld. APP Shri.Kulkarni for state. 9. After considering the case of prosecution following points arise for my determination. I recorded my findings against each of them for the reasons stated below:­ S.No. Points Findings 1. Whether the prosecution proves that accused committed rape on minor No. victim? .. 4 .. Spl.Case No. 262/2014 (Judgment.) 3. Though prosecution declared her hostile and put the question in the nature of cross­examination, prosecution failed to brought any incriminating circumstances against accused. She further deposed that she married with accused in court. After appreciating her evidence it appears that, she married with accused and at the time of deposition she is major and she deposed without any pressure. Having grudge with the said complaint, present applicant/accused along with other two accused caught the complainant and outraged her modesty. They also abused and threatened her. Hence, complainant went to police station and lodged the complaint. 3] The applicant has contended that, he is innocent and falsely implicated in this offence. He is young person only of 20 years of age. He has a permanent place of residence and has strong roots in the society. His custodial interrogation is not necessary. He is ready to abide by any terms and conditions. Nothing is to be recovered at his instance. The co­accused Shri Yasir Sarwar Sayed is already granted anticipatory bail hence, he is also entitled for anticipatory bail on the ground of parity. He lastly prayed for allowing his application. 4] Say of IO was called. The Investigating Officer resisted this application on the ground that, the complainant is minor. ..2.. Cri. Ant. Bail Appln. No.2605/2018 (Shri Aamir Usman Sayyed V/s State of Maharashtra) C.R.No.I­461/2018 of Nayanagar Police Stn. CNR NO. MHTH01­007128­2018 Accused was absconding since the date of commission of offence. Advocate Shri Noor Memon for the applicant/accused and Learned A.P.P. Smt. S.H. Mhatre for the State at length. 6] I have gone through the entire papers. .. 1 .. bail 2546/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Appln. No. 2546 of 2014 This application is filed by applicant Niket Ninad Mahadik for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. I­535/2014 registered at Vartaknagar police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 354D, 504, 506 read with section 34 of I.P.C. and section 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant and co­accused Maruti Vitkar used to follow the victim girl and at the time of incident they accosted the victim girl and co­accused Maruti asked her to develop love affair with him and they also threatened her of bad consequences if she refused to do so. It is further contended and argued that no such incident has happened and the applicant is falsely implicated in this crime. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co­operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that the applicant/ accused and co­accused Maruti Vitkar used to pursue the victim by saying that she should develop affair with co­accused Maruti Vitkar and when the victim girl refused to do so by saying that co­accused Maruti Vitkar is a married person and she cannot develop love relations with him, the applicant/accused threatened her of bad .. 2 .. bail 2546/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) consequences and also provoked her by saying that he will do such act that will prevent her from going anywhere out of house and the applicant/accused thereby outraged her modesty. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl and the prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 354D, 504, 506 read with section 34 of I.P.C. and 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and the girl is stated to be 14 yeas old, it appears that the allegations of pursuing the victim to develop love affair with the co­accused Maruti vitkar are made against said co­ accused and the applicant/accused is only stated to have threatened the victim when she refused to do so. But then it is contended on behalf of the applicant/accused that he is falsely implicated in the crime. In such circumstance whether the allegations against the accused are true or not, would be the question to be decided on merits. Even nothing is to be recovered from the applicant/accused. 4] Then, it is well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released .. 3 .. bail 2546/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) on bail. 5] In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 6] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 7] Then, it has also to be mentioned that the investigation in the matter though almost completed the charge sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and therefore, there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 8] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is allowed. .. 4 .. bail 2546/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) Applicant/accused Niket Ninad Mahadik is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ He shall attend the concerned police station on every Saturday between 3.00 p.m. to 5.00 p.m. till filing of the charge sheet and shall co­operate with the investigation. Accused Offence punishable under Section 354, 506 of Indian Penal Code and Section 9(c), 10 of POCSO Act, 2012. Appearance: A.P.P. Smt.Tallar APP for State. Advocate Shri. Rajan Salunkhe for accused. JUDGMENT (Delivered on this 30th day of July, 2018) 1. The case of the prosecution is that the informant resides with her husband and 13 years old daughter at Vidhya Shantinagar Society, Building NO.A/7, Room No.404 and JUDGMENT 2 Spl. case No. 240/2015 CNR NO.MHTH01­007144­2015 accused resides in the same building in Room No. 202. It is alleged that on the day of incident on 20.03.2015 at 13.45 hours informant's daughter i.e. victim 13 years came from school and she was climbing stair case of their building. At that time accused with sexual intent gave shake hand to the victim and he touched her waist and breast, therefore, the victim started crying. Accused then threatened her and went away. Victim reported this incident to her parents and thereafter on the same day on 20.03.2015 FIR was lodged in Mira Road police station. 3. C.R.No.I­124/2015 was registered under section 354, 506 of Indian Penal Code and section 9(c), 10 of POCSO Act, 2012. Investigation was done by PSI R.G. Shaikh. He recorded statement of victim in question and answer form in presence of society members. Investigating Officer prepared panchanama of the spot. He took CCTV footage and its' print out and footage of the gate of the building where the accused and victim resides. He prepared C.D of CCTV footage and its' hard disk was seized. Mobile phone of the accused was seized. Investigating Officer further recorded statements of witnesses and sent chargesheet. 4. Charge was framed at Exh.19 under section 354, 506 of Indian Penal Code and section 9(c), 10 of POCSO Act, 2012. He pleaded not guilty. Accused raised defence that victim's father was the Treasurer of their society, but he did not give accounts of the society, therefore, he had made complaint JUDGMENT 3 Spl. case No. 240/2015 CNR NO.MHTH01­007144­2015 application against victim's father on 11.03.2015 before the Chairman of the Vidhya Shanti Nagar Co­operative Housing Society. Chairman of the society had also sent complaint application of the accused to Dy. Registrar of the Co­operative Societies on 16.03.2015. Then the second complaint application given by accused to the Chairman of Vidhya Shanti Nagar Co­operative Housing Society on 18.03.2015 stating that the informant had not given accounts inspite of he had demanded accounts from him. It is therefore, contention of the accused that due to that victim's father had grudge against him and therefore, he had lodged false complaint against him due to the politically rivalry and political pressure. 5. Accused has examined one defence witness namely Vallabhbhai B. Patel, Chairman of the Vidhya Shanti Nagar Co­ operative Housing Society. 6. Following points arose for my determination. I have given its findings with the reasons, as under :­ Sr.No. Points Findings 1. Does prosecution prove that on 20.03.2015 at about 13.45 hours, in the stair case of Vidhya Shanti Nagar In negative. Co­operative Housing Society , Sector­ 6, Mira Road, East, Thane accused used criminal force to the complainant's daughter aged 13 years intending to outrage her modesty and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 354 of IPC ? 2. So she was weeping. Thereafter informant reported this incident to her husband and returned home at 4.30 p.m. Then she lodged FIR at Exh.26.Then her supplementary statement was also recorded.
