This is an appeal preferred by the appellant/accused challenging his conviction for offence punishable under section 10 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. It was suggested during cross­examination of the P.W.1 that there were arrears of rent and landlord was demanding arrears of rent to the father of the girl and also the landlord had asked father of the girl to vacate the premises. On this count, there was dispute. In the considered opinion of this court this was the probable defence raised on behalf of the accused and the prototype evidence of P.W 1 and 2 would have been critically examined by the trial court in the light of the said defence. However, the trial court has failed to appreciate the said evidence and believe the testimony of the child witness. The evidence of P.W.1 is hearsay evidence. Child witness was 8 years old. Held that, it was definitely risky to rely upon the evidence of child witness when there is no other corroborative evidence. It was held that in the considered opinion of this court when the offence is of serious nature and attracting minimum punishment for five years and maximum it can be up to seven years, great care and caution would have been taken by the trial court while appreciating the evidence of JUDGMENT 9 Spl. case No. 240/2015 CNR NO.MHTH01­007144­2015 the child witness. It was held that trial court had fallen in an error in appreciating the evidence brought before it and as such the said judgment and order is required to be interfered with in this appeal. So consequently,the Judgment and order was, quashed and set aside. 16. Relying upon the aforesaid case the Ld. Long procession of the congress party leader were taken in the police station, it shows that there was pressure given on the concerned police station because accused was the BJP candidate and informant had taken help of congress party. 22. She phoned her mother and at 4.30 p.m. victim's mother came home and thereafter they decided to lodge FIR. The alleged incident took plae at 1.45 p.m. The victim's mother did not come back immediately and did not lodge FIR immediately. The victim's mother i.e. informant took help of congress party leader for lodging FIR. This is made clear from the admission given by the informant in her cross examination. 23. The court is of the view that accused himself had given complaints against the father of the victim and accused is the BJP candidate and is the Corporator of Mira Bhayander Municipal Corporation and he knew that the informant is party of congress. So it is highly impossible and improbable that he will touched the victim with sexual intent and i.e. in the stair case when there is CCTV camera affixed at the gate at his house as well as at the gate of his office. The court is of the view that he will not dare to take risk. The stair case is common place to up and down. There is CCTV camera at the gate of the building and at the front side of his house. So in such circumstances he will not dare to touch the victim because he had lodged complaints 2 to 3 times against victim's father and before that also he had raised this issue many times. 24. The court is of the view that defence raised by the accused appears to be probable and believable. The court is of the view that only due to the political rivalry and due to the pressure of the political parties FIR came to be lodged in the background that the accused had made complaints against the father of the victim. 25. The victim is 13 to 14 years old at the time of incident. She used to play even with the children of the accused. As per the evidence of the victim she had gone to her aunt's house, but till arrival of her parents her aunt did not call any of the occupier of the building. Even parents of the victim did not met accused and did not ask him about the alleged JUDGMENT 14 Spl. case No. 240/2015 CNR NO.MHTH01­007144­2015 incident. So silence on the part of the aunt of the victim does not appear to be natural. The victim has admitted in her cross examination that Heet is the son of accused and he was her friend. So in such circumstances it is impossible that accused would have therefore touched the victim with sexual intent. The court is of the view that the evidence of the informant and victim does not appear to be natural, trustworthy and reliable. There is no independent eye witness. No other corroborative piece of evidence, defence raised by the accused appears to be trustworthy and believable. Therefore, court has come to the conclusion that prosecution could not prove the offence beyond all reasonable doubt and benefit of doubt goes in favour of the accused. That make it further clear that daughter of the accused was also there nearby and in the light of that also though she denied the suggestion that the daughter of the accused was playing outside and therefore he had kept the door open, very fact that the door of the house was kept open and in the light of the fact that daughter of the accused also entered house alongwith complainant, possibility of accused having committed such act do not appear to be there and that create doubt in the mind about version of the complainant. 19] Even as discussed above there appear some variance between the testimony of the girl and the complainant in regard to said aspect since the girl in her evidence appear to have stated a different .. 12 .. Special Case No.134/2013 Judgment story that she was playing with the daughter and son of the accused and the accused was there inside the house. Even as per version of the complainant when she gave call to her daughter, her daughter gave her call back and told that she is in the house of the accused and she would be coming and after waiting for some time she went inside the house of the accused, it is highly improbable and unacceptable that when the accused was committing such an act with the girl and when the girl had heard the call of her mother and gave call back telling that she is in the house of the accused and would be coming soon the accused would continue to do such act, particularly in the light of the fact that his own children were there nearby, the door of the house was not latched and accused would be in same position under bed sheet with the girl till the complainant come there and entered his house and gave another call and that also makes the theory put forth by the complainant highly improbable and unacceptable. 20] Then, as mentioned above the girl appear to have narrated the incident in explicit words and also that she narrated the incident to her mother after her mother came there. It is very much material to mention that in her cross-examination she appear to have accepted that on the day of incident she was playing inside the house of the accused which falsifies the theory put forth by the complainant that she was playing outside the house. Then, she further accepted that daughter and son of the accused were also playing with her, meaning thereby that they were also there in the house. She further accepted that they were playing running and chasing inside the house and also were coming outside and also going inside the house while playing and that make it clear that the victim and the accused were playing inside and outside the house of the accused making it clear that the door of the house was open. It is further material to mention .. 13 .. Special Case No.134/2013 Judgment that in an answer to a pinpointed question that who told you to tell that accused applied spittle to his hand and removed her nicker, the girl had pointed out towards her mother who was sitting in the Court and that fully support the submission on behalf of accused that the girl was tutored by her mother to tell about the incident. 21] Then, though she denied further suggestion in next moment that no such incident as stated by her had ever taken place, it is very much material to further mention that in next breath she also accepted that when her mother had been there to call her in the house of accused, that time also daughter and son of the accused were playing in the house and that totally wipe about entire story put forth by the complainant that when she went inside house of the accused, nobody else was there and the accused and the girl were lying on the floor covered by bed sheet etc. 22] Then, though the submission on behalf of prosecution that there is no reason for mother of 5 years' old girl to make such false complaint and very fact that such allegations are made and the girl supported the prosecution case is sufficient to conclude that such an incident had taken place etc. can be said to be acceptable and it is unbelievable or unacceptable in normal course that such type of false allegations involving minor daughter would be made by mother. But then, in that respect also it is to be mentioned that very specific defence is put forth by the accused that he had helped police in tracing and arresting brother-in-law of the complainant in one theft case and therefore, there was grievance and dispute and that fact do not appear to have been denied by the complainant and she only denied such contentions for want of knowledge. .. 14 .. Special Case No.134/2013 Judgment 23] Even it is further material to mention that as per version of the complainant and also the girl the accused had applied spittle to his finger and had forcibly inserted it in her anus. But it is material to mention that when the girl was referred for medical examination, no signs of forceful intercourse or penetrative intercourse or no external or internal injuries were noticed to her anus or private part of the girl or any part of her body. It is to be mentioned that the incident stated to have taken place around 3.30 p.m. and immediately in the evening complaint came to be lodged and the girl was referred for medical examination and negative medical certificate is totally against the prosecution case. 24] It is further material to mention that anal swab and vaginal swab of the girl were taken as sample but in the light of allegations that accused had applied spittle to his finger and inserted the finger into her anus or private part, report of vaginal swab as well as sample of spittle of accused obtained also appear to be material and important piece of evidence. But no such report of chemical analysis has been produced on record. Therefore though the submission on behalf of prosecution that the sole testimony of the victim girl is sufficient to come to the conclusion about guilt of the accused even if accepted for a while, in the circumstances mentioned above in absence of any corroborative evidence and in the light of the admissions given by the girl that it was her mother who had asked her to state said facts and further the admissions that at the time when her mother came in the house of the accused children of the accused were there, the absence of corroboration by medical evidence has to be held as fatal to the prosecution case. .. 15 .. Special Case No.134/2013 Judgment 25] Even so far as submission on behalf of prosecution that once after thorough investigation the prosecution is launched against the accused for the offence under section 354A(1)(i) of I.P.C. and section 4 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, as per section 29 of P.O.C.S.O. Act it is to be presumed that such act is committed unless contrary is proved and the accused has not brought any evidence in rebuttal and as per presumption the accused has to be held as guilty and liable to be convicted. But in that respect also under section 29 of P.O.C.S.O. Act it is provided that ''Where a person is prosecuted for committing or abetting or attempting to commit any offence under sections 3, 5, 7 and 9 of this Act, the Special Court shall presume that such person has committed or abetted or attempted to commit the offence, as the case may be, unless the contrary is proved. But then, it is to be mentioned that in the light of words ''unless the contrary is proved'' it is clear that the presumption is rebuttable. Then, so far as the presumption and rebuttal thereof, it is well settled and has been observed in the ruling cited on behalf of in case of Krishna Janardhan Bhat vs. Dattatraya G. Hegde reported in 2008 ALL MR (Cri) 1164 (S.C.) it is observed therein that '' a statutory presumption has an evidentiary value. The question as to whether the presumption whether stood rebutted or not, must, therefore, be determined keeping in view the other evidences on record. It is further observed that where the chances of implication cannot be ruled out, the background fact and the conduct of the parties together with their legal requirements are required to be taken into consideration. In the light of said observations if evidence on record in present case is perused, as discussed above, sufficient material is brought on record in cross-examination of the witnesses on the basis of which it can be said that the defence put forth by the accused that when the girl was playing, his own children were also playing with her and further that there is also reason to believe that there was previous .. 16 .. Special Case No.134/2013 Judgment enmity between the complainant and the accused for which such complaint could have been lodged and the probability and possibility of the defence put forth by the accused being probable cannot be ruled out and therefore the submission on behalf of prosecution that as per Section 29 of the Act it is to be presumed that the accused is guilty and and he should convicted, cannot be said to be sustainable. In view of all above discussion it has to be concluded that the prosecution has failed to establish the guilt of the accused beyond all the reasonable doubt and the accused is entitled to the benefit of doubt. Point no. 1 and 2 are therefore answered accordingly. 26] In view of above discussion it has to be held that no offence is proved against the accused and he is entitled to be acquitted. Point no.3 is answered accordingly. 27] Since the accused is acquitted, it is necessary that he be directed to furnish P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/- [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount under section 437A of Cr.P.C. to appear before the higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect of any appeal or petition, if any, filed against the judgment and that such bail bond shall be in force for six months. In the result I pass the following order - ORDER Accused Rajendra Kamlakar Sharma is acquitted of the charge for offence punishable under section 354A(1)(i) of I.P.C. and section 3 read with section 4 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 2) Bail bonds of the accused stand cancelled and sureties are discharged. .. 17 .. Special Case No.134/2013 Judgment 3) The accused shall furnish P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/- [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount under section 437A of Cr.P.C. to appear before the higher Court as and when such Court issues notice in respect of any appeal or petition, if any filed against the judgment and that such bail bond shall be in force for six months. 4) No muddemal article is seen to be submitted to the Court. Hence, no order in respect of its disposal is passed. 5) The proceeding is closed. Date : 23.06.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Additional Session Judge-1, Thane.

It is admitted by the informant (P.W.2) that accused to go for work in the morning and return in the late night and 18 Special Case No. 263/2014 (Judgment) during that period she was at work where she is working as house­maid, then again the question remains that if accused had committed such act during night then informant was very much present in the house and further it is doubtful whether during such time, accused could have been done such act with his own children. None of these witnesses had deposed the particular time either of day or night about the commission of the act. The witnesses had deposed in very vauge manner and their testimony does not inspire confidence, particularly in the background of the admissions given by the witnesses about the working hours of the accused and the informant. 28] Now, the question remains as to why the children are deposing against their father and informant had lodged report against her own husband. In this respect, though the accused came with the defence that informant was working at the house of one Mr. and Mrs. Nirvan and she used to listen them and used to discuss of her problem with them and Mr. Nirvan is also a Civil Contractor. However, in such circumstances, though the defence of the accused is not probable, still even the story put forth by the prosecution remains doubtful, in the background of testimony of the victim­children and their mother. No doubt, there is force in the submission of learned Spl.P.P. that the mother of such tender aged children could not stake character of children. 19 Special Case No. 263/2014 (Judgment) However, though clear reason is not brought on record about the false implication, still the evidence of the witnesses is not of such nature to believe it and to hold that the prosecution has proved the case beyond reasonable doubt. In this respect, even the exaggerated statement of the informant is required to be scrutinized. Informant (P.W.2) even deposed that her husband/accused also did same un­natural act with the son of her sister by name Jay, on the pretext that by doing such act height of the children will be increased. However, the mother of said boy is testified as (P.W.1), but she did not whisper about any such act had been committed by accused with her son Jay. Thus, there is no corroboration to the exaggerated statements of the informant (P.W.2) 29] Further the prosecution had examined P.W.6 Kiran More who is a member of Child Welfare Committee (C.W.C.) and he recorded statement of victim­boy and victim­ girl. The learned Spl.P.P. submitted that as statement of the children were recorded before C.W.C. who is an independent person and there also children had stated against their father, therefore, his testimony is required to be believed. In this respect, Kiran More (P.W.6) in his cross­examination stated that the statement of victim­boy and victim­girl were in the hand­writing of one Vidya Atpatkar who is also the member of C.W.C. Thus it appears that infact statements of children were recorded by Vidya Atpatkar who is not examined by the 20 Special Case No. 263/2014 (Judgment) prosecution. The learned defence counsel argued that when the statement of the children was recorded before C.W.C. at that time, their mother was present. However, the submission of learned defence counsel has no force as the provisions are incorporated in the P.O.C.S.O. Act which permits presence of parents at the time of recording of statement of victim­ children. However, in the present case, both the children (P.W.3 & P.W.4) are appeared to be under total influence of their mother (P.W.2) and used to act as per her dictate. Therefore, if the children are stated the same thing before the members of C.W.C., still it lost its authenticity as the children appears to be tutored by their mother. Therefore, the evidence of P.W.6 is of little help to the prosecution. 30] The informant (P.W.2) in her cross­examination stated that her children i.e. her son might have disclosed about the act of their father, probably during summer vacation in the month of April or May, while the F.I.R. eloquent that the victim­boy disclosed the incident to his mother on 15/07/2014 and the F.I.R. was lodged on 15/09/2014. From the F.I.R. it appears that since the disclosure of the incident by her son to the informant, thereafter also she lodged report after two months. While deposing before the Court, the informant stated that when her children disclosed the act of accused, thereafter, for one month, the accused was not at home, and after his return for 21 Special Case No. 263/2014 (Judgment) 15 to 20 days she keeps on asking him (accused), but him did not answer. Thereafter, she lodged report, which means the report ought to have been lodged in the month of August­ 2014. However, the F.I.R. is registered on 15/09/2014. Thus, even the delay is not properly explained. 31] Thus, the testimony of the material witnesses i.e. victim­boy(P.W.4), and victim­girl(P.W.3) and informant (P.W.2) is not of such a nature to inspire confidence and except their version, there is absolutely no documentary evidence on record, even the medical certificates of the victim­children did not disclose any injury, particularly to the victim­boy. Thus, the prosecution failed to prove the charge against accused beyond reasonable doubt. Therefore, the accused is entitled for benefit of doubt. Hence, I answer point No.1 to 4 in the negative and accused is entitled for acquittal. 32] In the result, I proceed to pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused Ashok Amar Singh is hereby acquitted U/Sec. 235(1) of Cr.P.C. for the offence punishable U/Sec.377 & 354 of Indian Penal Code and also under section 3, 4, 7 & 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 . 22 Special Case No. 263/2014 (Judgment) 2] The Accused is in jail. He shall be released forthwith if not required in any other offence. 3] The Accused is directed to furnish bail bond of the amount of ₹15,000/­ with one solvent surety in the like amount in compliance of provision of section 437­A of Cr.P.C. The judgment is dictated and pronounced in open Court. Date : 24/05/2016. (Ms. U. M. Nandeshwar), Thane Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act),Thane. District Judge ­1 and Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

Presented on : 26.10.2015 Registered on : 26.10.2015 Decided on : 18.11.2017 Duration : 02Y. 0M. 22D IN THE COURT OF SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE, AT : THANE. Presided over by S.C. Khalipe ­Additional Sessions Judge, Thane SPECIAL CASE NO.241/2015 Exh.No. The State of Maharashtra Through Wada Police Station. ….. Prosecution V/s. Radheyshyam Jagdish Chaurasiya Age 35 years, Occ: Worker R/at. Gulwa Nasirpur, Jienpur, Dist. Azamghad, Utter Pradesh. Now R/at. Om Sai Dhaba, Kudus, Taluka Wada, Dist. Palghar. ..... Accused Offence punishable under Sections 363, 376(2) (I) of Indian Penal Code and section 4, 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act,2012. Appearance: A.P.P. Smt.Hiwrale for the prosecution. Advocate Shri. S.J. Patankar for accused. :J U D G M E N T: (Delivered on this 18th Day of November, 2017) The accused is charged for the offence under section 363, 376(2)(i) of Indian Penal Code and section 4, 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act,2012. The case of the prosecution is that:­ 2. On 22.07.2015 the accused kidnapped the minor daughter of the informant aged 14 years by promising to marry her and taken her to Shirdi and Haridwar and committed penetrative sexual assault and rape against her will. The father of the victim lodged FIR in Wada police station. C.R.No.I­204/2015 registered under section 363, 376(2)(i) of Indian Penal Code and section 4, 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act,2012. 3. The investigation was carried out by A.P.I. S N. Chaudhar of Wada police station. He went to Haridwar and brought the victim and accused with the help of local police. He visited Sai Krupa Lodge at Shirdi and prepared the panchanama of the room. He recorded statement of victim. He sent the victim and accused for medical examination. The victim stated before police that the accused promise to marry her and taken her to Haridwar. He took her at Shirdi and committed sexual intercourse with her against her will. He also then taken her to Haridwar where the police caught them. Investigating Officer then seized the clothes of victim and accused and sent it to FSL Kalina. The blood sample, vaginal swab and nail clipping also sent to FSL Kalina. The victim was also sent to medical examination to Civil Hospital, Thane. After investigation it was transpired that the accused has committed offences, therefore, he sent chargesheet. 4. Charge was framed against the accused under section 363, 376(2)(i) of Indian Penal Code and section 4, 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act,2012. The accused pleaded not guilty. 5. Considering the evidence on record following points arose for my determination. I have given its findings with reasons as under­ Sr.No Points Findings 1. Does prosecution prove that on In 22.07.2015 the accused kidnapped the Affirmative minor daughter of the informant aged 14 years without consent of her parents out of their lawful guardianship and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 363 of Indian Penal Code? 2. Does prosecution prove that between In Negative 22.07.2015 to 24.07.2015 at Shirdi accused committed rape upon the victim aged 14 years and thereby committed an offence under section 376(2)(i) of Indian Penal Code? 3 Does prosecution prove that between In the 22.07.2015 to 24.07.2015 the accused Negative committed penetrative sexual assault upon minor victim aged 14 years and thereby committed an offence under section 4 of POCSO Act? 4 Does prosecution prove that the accused In the has committed sexual assault upon the Negative minor victim aged 14 years during 22.07.2015 to 24.07.2015 at Shirdi and Haridwar and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 8 of POCSO Act? 5 What order? Accused is convicted for the offence under section 363 of Indian Penal Code REASONS AS TO POINT NOS.1 TO 5:­ 6. To prove the offence prosecution has examined informant i.e. the father of the victim at Exh.13. According to him, he runs Om Sai Dhaba at Kuduas, Taluka Wada, Dist. Thane. Accused Radheyshyam was running Pan Tapari at his Dhaba. On 22.07.2015 his daughter went missing so he lodged complaint to police. After 2­3 days he received phone call from Haridwar police station that the accused and his daughter were caught by the police. Then he took the custody of his daughter form the police. He then lodged FIR. He admitted the contents in FIR and his signature. It is marked at Exh.14. He had gone to Haridwar police station. Accused and his daughter were in the police station. 7. The informant did not support the further part of the prosecution story. He stated that his daughter did not tell anything what happened with her. 8. The victim P.W.2 is examined at Exh.15. She stated that accused is her cousin brother. He was married, but his wife does not reside with him. The accused was running Pan shop since last five months in the Dhaba of her father. On 22.07.2015 she had stomach pain so the accused took her to hospital and gave her medicine. Thereafter the accused told her that he want to meet his aunt, who was residing at Haridwar and asked her whether she can come with him. She said 'yes'. Then the accused told her that he will inform her parents about that. Thereafter accused took her by rickshaw at 2­3 places and took her by bus at one railway station. Then accused took her at Haridwar. They stayed at railway station, at that time the police caught them. The accused told the police that she was his wife, but she told police that he was her brother. 9. The victim does not support the further part of the prosecution story. She stated that the accused did not do anything wrong with her. Her statement was recorded in Wada Court, but that statement is not correct. The portion marked A regarding the sexual assault is also not admitted by her. She stated that she had told this portion about sexual assault to the police due to the pressure of police. 10. Ld. A.P.P. declared the victim as hostile and took her cross examination. It is revealed in her cross examination that accused would bring eatables and gives her money. Accused had told her that he was feeling loneliness as his wife does not reside with him. The accused wife had left him and his wife had filed case against him. She further stated that the accused has told her that if she will not marry with him he will commit suicide. She told him that she is 14 years old and he was of her mother's age. 11. The victim further stated that her father had given complaint against the accused that he had taken her to Haridwar. She stated that accused had taken her to Haridwar without her parents consent. She also stated that accused had taken her in one hotel, but she do not remember that place. In her para No.7 of her cross examination she has stated that her statement was recorded before J.M.F.C court Wada. There was nobody with her except Judge madam and clerk and Judge madam has not pressurized her, but she stated that the police had told her that what she should depose before the court. In para No.9 of her cross examination she has stated that after she was taken from Haridwar she was taken to doctor and her medical examination was done. She had stated before the doctor what she had stated before the court. 12. P.W.3 Sanjay Namdev Chaughar is the API of Wada police station. He done the investigation from 30.07.2015. Initially the offence under section 363 of Indian Penal Code was registered and after recording statement of victim offence under section 376 of Indian Penal Code and POCSO Act Sections 4 and 8 was added. He seized clothes of victim vide panchanama Exh.20. He deposited the clothes of the accused and victim in the police station. The clothes of accused were seized vide panchanama Exh.21. He sent victim for medical examination. He collected medical report. He sent sample of blood swab, vaginal swab, nail clipping to FSL Kalina vide its letter Exh.31. He sent the accused for medical examination, he prepared panchanama at Shirdi in Sai Krupa Lodge. He recorded the statement of waiter in that hotel. He collected receipt of charges paid in the hotel and copy of admission register. He sent victim to J.M.F.C. Court Wada for recording statement under section 164 of Cr. P.C. He collected C.A report and school leaving certificate of the victim and original mark­sheet. 13. P.W.4 Smita Sitaram Patil is examined at Exh.17. As per her statement the victim's statement was recorded on 30.07.2015 in her presence. The age of the victim is 14 years. The victim had stated in her presence that accused Radheyshyam had taken her Shirdi by cheating her and committed sexual intercourse with her. The statement was recorded in question and answer form. 14. P.W.5 Uttam Ashok Patil is the panch witness in whose presence the panchanama of the room of Sai Krupa Lodge of Shirdi was prepared on 03.08.2015. The register of the lodge was verified. There was entry of the accused on page No.13 dated 22.07.2015, room No.7 was allotted to the accused. The panchanama of that room is marked at Exh.37. 15. P.W.6 Kishor Shantaram Mali is police Naik of Wada police station. He prepared panchanama of the spot which was shown by the informant. On 28.07.2015 he and other police staff went to Haridwar and they took the victim to Wada police station. 16. P.W.7 Dr. Vandana Patil is examined at Exh.39. She was casualty medical officer in Thane Civil Hospital on 31.07.2015. She examined the victim. She took the history of the victim. The victim has stated that she was taken on 22.07.2015 by giving sedative orally at 3.00 p.m. by Maruti car. She wake up for 2­3 times, but again sedative given and slept. On 23.07.2015 at 6.00 a.m. she was given food and to watch T.V and then she was taken to station and went to Haridwar by train. The victim further stated that she was tried for intercourse at Shirdi at 22nd night and 23rd early morning. She took the vaginal swab, blood samples and nail sample and sent to FSL. She further stated that the victim was examined after nine days of the incident and therefore, her opinion will depend upon FSL report. FSL report is marked at Exh.26 which is negative. Doctor further stated that the victim has taken bath, changed clothes, passed urine. Therefore, no injuries on the body of the victim. The medical report is marked at Exh.40. 17. The statement under section 313 of Cr. P.C of the accused is recorded at Exh.42. The accused admitted that he was the relative of the informant and he was running Pan shop in the Dhaba of the informant. But the further incriminating circumstances are not admitted by him. 18. From the oral evidence on record it is clear that the victim and accused were found at Haridwar. The victim's father had given complaint on 24.07.2015 in Wada police station that his daughter went missing. So initially offence under section 363 of Indian Penal Code was registered. Police were searching the victim and accused. Investigating Officer, informant and the victim has stated that the victim was found in Haridwar and with the help of local police and the Wada police station brought her at Wada. The victim has stated her age as 14 years. Before the medical officer and one social worker Smita Sitaram Patil this fact is not denied by the accused strictly. The school leaving certificate of the victim is admitted on behalf of the accused. It is marked at Exh.23. As per the school leaving certificate it was issued by one school at Azamghad, Utter Pradesh. Her birth date is 05.07.2001. As per this birth date the victim's age was 14 years at the time of incident. So it is crystal clear that the victim was below 18 year at the time of incident. 19. I heard Ld. Counsel on behalf of the accused and Ld. A.P.P. 20. Ld. A.P.P submitted that though the witnesses have not supported on the point of sexual assault, but there is evidence to prove the offence under section 363 of Indian Penal Code. He relied upon the decision in case of Devraj V/s. State of Chhattisgarh (2016) 13 Supreme Court 366. It was held that, “the evidence of hostile witness can be relied on, if there are some other material, on basis of which said evidence can be corroborated.” In another case Madavan V/s. The State of Tamil Nadu 2017 ALL MR (cri) 190. In that case also the victim has turned hostile, but there was other corroborative piece of evidence and on the basis of that the accused was convicted.” 21. The Ld. A.P.P. submitted that the offence under section 363 is proved beyond doubt, therefore, accused may be convicted. 22. In reply Ld. Accused on behalf of accused submitted that the accused is the cousin brother of the victim and he had taken her to Haridwar for Tirthyatra. There was nothing wrong committed by him without her consent, therefore, no offence is proved by the prosecution. 23. To prove the offence under section 363 of Indian Penal Code the use of pressure or force need not be proved, only taking of a child i.e. female child below age of 18 years out of the custody of her parents without the consent of her parents is required to be proved. In this case from the evidence of victim the accused had taken the victim without informing her parents. The accused had taken her by saying that he wanted to meet his aunt, who is at Haridwar and to meet his aunt he took her with him. The accused told her that he will inform her parents, but he did not inform her parents about taking her to Haridwar. The victim's father had lodged FIR about missing of his daughter on 24.07.2015 stating that his daughter went missing from 22.07.2015 that itself shows that the victim was taken from custody of her father without his consent. 24. The evidence of the victim and Investigating Officer, police Naik Kishor Mali it is clear that the accused and the victim were caught by the police at Haridwar railway station and they were brought to Wada police station. Therefore, it is no doubt that the accused had taken the victim from Wada to Haridwar. It is also proved by the prosecution that the accused had stayed the victim at Shirdi in Sai Krupa Lodge, its panchanama was recorded in presence of Uttam Ashok Patil. The register of the lodge was also verified by police. There was entry of the accused name in the register. The victim has also stated that the accused had taken her in one lodge. From this evidence it is also clear that the accused had taken her at Shirdi as well as to Haridwar. 25. Therefore, I come to the conclusion that the prosecution has proved beyond all reasonable doubt that the victim was below 18 years at the time of incident and she was taken by the accused without her father's consent out of his guardianship and he took her at Shirdi and Haridwar, therefore, the ingredients of the offence under section 363 of Indian Penal Code are proved beyond doubt. 26. The victim has stated that the accused had not committed anything wrong with her. No sexual assault or penetrative sexual assault was done with her. She denied portion marked A regarding sexual assault and rape in her statement before the police. She stated that she gave statement before police and J.M.F.C., Wada regarding sexual assault upon her due to the pressure of police, therefore, the victim is not supported on the point of sexual and penetrative sexual assault. The victim's father has also not stated anything about sexual assault and rape upon his daughter. The victim has not stated the name of the accused before the doctor. The evidence of the doctor is only corroborative piece of evidence, it is not substantive piece of evidence. FSL report is negative, so considering all these evidence on record the court is of the view that the prosecution has failed to prove offence under section 376(2)(i) of Indian Penal Code and Section 4, 8 of POCSO Act, therefore, I answered point Nos.2 to 4 in the negative. 25. I held the accused guilty for the offence punishable under section 363 of Indian Penal Code only. Date:18.11.2017 (S. C. Khalipe) Thane. Additional Sessions Judge, Thane. 28. In the afternoon session the accused is produced form jail authority. I heard accused on the point of sentence. He has prayed for leniency. The Ld. Counsel on behalf of the accused also prayed for leniency. 29. I heard Ld. A.P.P.Smt. Hiwrale. She submitted that accused may be convicted with the maximum punishment and compensation may be given to the victim. 30. Considering the facts and circumstance of this case I do not found any mitigating circumstance. The offence under section 363 of IPC is punishable with imprisonment which may extent to seven years and with fine. I also of the view that compensation should also be awarded to the victim. Accordingly, I pass following order which is sufficient for the ends of justice. 31. The muddemal property i.e. the clothes of the victim and accused being worthless are liable to be destroyed after the appeal period. Hence, I pass following order. ORDER 1] The accused Radheyshyam Jagdish Chaurasiya is convicted under section 235(2) of Criminal Procedure Code for the offence punishable under section 363 of Indian Penal Code. 2 He is sentenced to suffer rigours imprisonment for the period of seven years and with fine of Rs.10,000/­(Rupees Ten Thousand Only), in default of payment of fine he shall suffer simple imprisonment for the period of six months. 3 On payment of fine amount it shall be given to the victim as compensation after appeal period. 4 The accused is acquitted under section 235(1) of Cr.p.C of the offence charged under section 376(2)(i) of Indian Penal Code and Section 4, 8 of POCSO Act, 2012. 5 The muddmeal property being worthless be destroyed after appeal period. 6. The accused is in jail from 30.07.2015 till today therefore set off be given under section 428 of Cr. P.C. for this period. 7. The Judgment is dictated and declared in open court. 8. The copy of Judgment shall be given to the accused free of costs. Thane. (S.C. Khalipe) Date:18.11.2017. Additional Sessions Judge,Thane.

From the F.I.R. it is seen that the applicant and other accused had targeted the minor victim girl. Even looking to the nature of offence and the manner in which it is stated to have been committed and in the light of the fact that the complainant was traumatized and was threatened to kill if she disclose about it to anybody, the submissions on behalf of applicant/accused that there is delay in lodging the F.I.R. and though the incident is alleged to have taken place between year 2011 to 2013 the complaint is lodged at a very belated stage in the year 2014 and therefore it create doubt in the mind etc. cannot be said to be appealing and convincing at this stage. For the same reasons the submissions made on behalf of applicant/accused that since the charge sheet is submitted in Court there is no question of .. 5 .. bail 2561/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) investigation being hampered and therefore the applicant/ accused is entitled to be released on bail, also cannot be said to be sustainable. 5] Then, it is also clear that the applicant and other accused are stated to have forced the victim to consume psychotropic substances like ganja, charas, brown sugar and when she was under its influence, the applicant and co­ accused Justin Dhanaraj had committed rape on her frequently and even she was forced to do prostitution and was also threatened to kill etc. and therefore the apprehension that if the accused is released on bail he may again indulge in same activity is well founded. Even the possibility of the accused repeating such crime also cannot be ruled out and possibility that the accused may influence the victim and may pressurize the prosecution witnesses and possibility of accused being absconding is also there. 6] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is not a fit case wherein the applicant/accused can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is rejected. Date : 31.01.2015. (Mrs.V.V.Virkar) Additional Session Judge­1, Thane.

Counsel Shri.M. D. Joshi for accused. ==================================== .. 2 .. Spl.Case No. 243/2015 (Judgment.) :JUDGMENT: (Delivered on 28th day of March, 2018) 1. Accused is facing trial for the offence punishable u/sec. 363, 366 of Indian Penal Code (hereinafter as IPC) and Sec.8 & 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter referred as POCSO Act). 2. Name of the victim, full name of her family members, place of incidence, name of school are not mentioned in the judgment to avoid disclosure of identity of Victim as per Section 33(7) of the POCSO Act. 3. In short, case of prosecution is as follows:­ It is alleged by the prosecution that, accused was having love affair with victim, daughter of informant. It is alleged that on 21.11.14 victim went for her school but she did not returned and therefore missing complaint was lodged on 22.11.14. Thereafter informant lodged FIR against unknown person on 25.12.14 alleging that, someone kidnapped her from the lawful guardianship knowingly that she will be compelled or likely to compel illicit intercourse and thereby committed the offence u/sec. 363, 366 of Indian Penal Code and Sec.8 & 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 4. The FIR was lodged against accused by Mother of victim. On the basis of said FIR Crime No. I­385/2014 came to be registered at Rabale Police Station. After completion of all the .. 3 .. Spl.Case No. 243/2015 (Judgment.) formalities of investigation the present chargesheet came to be filed. 5. The Charge was framed by my predecessor vide Ex.4 against the accused for the offence punishable u/sec. 363, 366 of Indian Penal Code and Sec. & 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 6. In support of its case the prosecution has examined following witnesses:­ PW No. Ex.No. Prosecution Witness 1 6 Mother of victim­Informant. 2 9 Victim. 7. Considering the evidence given by PW.1 Informant and PW.2 Victim and the hostility of victim, the Ld. APP wisely closed the evidence of prosecution by filing purshis at Ex.19 to save the valuable time of court and prosecution machinery. 8. After considering the case of prosecution following points arise for my determination. I recorded my findings against each of them for the reasons stated below:­ S.No. Points Findings 1. Whether the prosecution proves that accused kidnapped victim from the No. lawful guardianship of her parents? 2. Whether the prosecution proves that accused induced minor victim to .. 4 .. Spl.Case No. 243/2015 (Judgment.) leave the house of her parents with No. intent that she may be or knowing that it is likely that she will be, forced or seduced to illicit intercourse with another person? 4. Whether the prosecution proves that accused has committed sexual No. harassment on minor victim? 5. Whether the prosecution proves that accused has committed sexual assault No. on minor victim? 6. What order? Accused is acquitted. :REASONS: AS TO POINT NO. 1 TO 5 :­ 9. To prove the case, prosecution has examined PW.1 Informnt, mother of victim at Ex.6 but she did not support the prosecution case. She deposed that on 21.11.14 her daughter left the house for school but did not return and therefore she lodged missing report at Ex.7 on 22.11.14. She further deposed that on 25.12.14 she lodged FIR at Ex.8 against unknown person. As she did not support Ld.APP sought permission to put her question in the nature of cross­ examination and the said request was granted. However nothing revealed in cross­examination against present accused. 10. The prosecution also examined PW.2 Victim at Ex.9 but she .. 5 .. Spl.Case No. 243/2015 (Judgment.) also did not support the prosecution case. She did not told anything incriminating against present accused. She specifically stated that her birth date is 5.8.97 and in support of said contention the prosecution is relied on Ex.10 & 11 school leaving certificate and hall ticket of victim respectively. She further deposed that on 21.11.14 it was a birthday of accused Sagar and therefore she went alongwith Sagar for roaming. In her entire deposition she has not stated any incriminating circumstances against accused. She further deposed that she married with accused after completion of her 18 years. She further deposed that, prior to marriage accused used to touch her and hug her lovingly but he used to hug only with love and not under lust or sexual intention. 11. In view of the oral evidence adduced on record on behalf of prosecution it is transpired that, there is absolutely no incriminating evidence came on record to be put to the accused for explanation u/sec.313 of Cr.P.C. Therefore after hearing Ld.APP and Advocate for accused, I am inclined to dispense with the statement u/sec.313 of Cr.P.C. Accordingly I passed order below Ex.4 and dispensed with the statement. 12. So considering all these facts and circumstances discussed above, there is absolutely no evidence to suggest that accused committed any offence as alleged u/sec.363, 366, of Indian Penal Code and Sec. 8 & 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, therefore accused is entitled for acquittal. Hence, I answer Point No.1 to 5 are in negative. .. 6 .. Spl.Case No. 243/2015 (Judgment.) AS TO POINT NO.6:­ 13. Considering the reasoning and findings as to point No.1 to 5 in answer to point No.6 , I proceed to pass following order:­ ORDER 1] Accused Sagar Mohan Jadhav is hereby acquitted u/sec. 232 of Cr. P. C. of the offence punishable u/sec.363, 366, of Indian Penal Code and Sec.8 & 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] The bail bonds of accused stands cancelled and surety stands discharged. 3] There is no entry in respect of seizure of any muddemal property, hence no order in respect of muddemal property. 4] The accused shall execute P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ and surety in like amount, in compliance of Sec.437­A of Cr.P.C. --1-- ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN CRIMINAL BAIL APPLICATION NO.2702/2017 The applicant Mohammad Shafiq Mohammad Saeed Ansari aged 45 years has applied for bail under section 439 of Cr. P.C. in C.R.No.I­143/2017 registered in Bhoiwada police station for the offence under section 376 of Indian Penal Code and section 3(b), 4,7, and 8 of POCSO Act. 2. It is contended that the applicant is falsely implicated. FIR is concocted ,false and unbelievable. There is no criminal antecedent. There is no eye witness. The investigation is almost completed. The applicant is ready to face the trial, therefore, he may be released on bail. 3. Investigating Officer has given say at Exh.4. It is contended the victim is 4 years 8 months old. The accused runs general store. Whenever victim goes to purchase chocolate in the shop of accused he used to sexual assault upon her. He removed her chaddi and inserted his finer into his vagina and also kissed her. Previously also accused has done this act. The adjoining people gave understanding to the accused, but there were no improvement. On 25.09.2017 he repeated the same thing. The victim narrated the incident to her parents and then FIR was lodged. The accused is HIV patient and his wife is also HIV patient. There is likelihood of the repetition of offence. He is of criminal nature and therefore, if released on bail there is danger to the victim. Hence, he prayed for rejection of bail. 4. I heard Ld. Counsel on behalf of accused and Ld. APP. 5. Ld. Counsel on behalf of the accused relied upon decision in case of Nimmagadda Prasad V/s. Central Bueraue of --2-- Investigation 2013 CRI. L.J. 3449. It is held that, “while granting bail, the court has to see that there is genuine case against accused and prosecution will be able to produce prima facie evidence in support of charge”. In case of Atul Rao V/s. State of Karnataka 2009 CRI L.J.634 it was held that, “ while deciding the application for bail under section 439 of Cr. P.C., court has to see nature of offence, character of offence, circumstances which are peculiar to accused, possibility of not securing presence of accused at trial, reasonable apprehension of witnesses and larger interest of public or of State.” 6. Considering the facts of this case, the court is of the view that accused had repeated the same things again and again. The victim's parents and other people had given warning to her, but there were no improvement. So accused if released on bail he is likely to tamper the prosecution witnesses and also likely to repeat the offence. The offence is very serious and it is against minor girl of aged 4.8 years old. There is strong prima facie case made out. Accused is of HIV patient as contended by him in the application. So it is not desirable to release him on bail. Hence, I pass following order. :ORDER: Application for bail is rejected. Thane. ( S.C. Khalipe ) Date : 23/11/2017. Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 2593 of 2014 This application is filed by applicant Premshankar Bariya for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. I­370/2014 registered at Rabodi police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 354 of I.P.C. and section 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant outraged modesty of the complainant/victim girl. It is further contended and argued that no such incident has happened and the applicant is falsely implicated in this crime. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/ accused is released on bail, he will co­operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that at the time of incident the accused forcibly pulled the victim inside his house and after latching the door from inside, he moved his hand over her breast and thereby he outraged her modesty. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl and the prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 354 of I.P.C. and section 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and he is alleged to have dragged the complainant girl who is aged 16 years into his house and after closing the door, molested her by moving his hand over her breast etc. and only when somebody was there, he stopped the act when the door was knocked and the door was opened the sister and brother of the girl were there in the door. Then, the submissions on behalf of applicant/accused that such story put forth in the complaint is improbable etc. it would be premature to draw any conclusion in that regard at this stage when the investigation is in progress. As is clear the accused is stated to be 32 years old man who is alleged to have molested a minor girl aged 16 years and looking to the nature of offence and the manner in which it is alleged to have been committed, I am of the view that thorough investigation into the matter is necessary and the investigation would be hampered if applicant is released on bail at this stage. 4] Then, it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused pressurizing the victim and other prosecution witnesses and being absconded and tampering with prosecution evidence is there is also there. 5] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is not a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is rejected. Date : 08.01.2015. (Mrs.V.V.Virkar) District Judge­1 and Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.

( ) Special Case (POCSO) No. 269 of 2014 CNR No.MHTH01­007296­2014 The State of Maharashtra, Through P.S.O., Police Station, Bhiwandi Taluka, Tal. Bhiwandi, Dist. Thane. ... ... ... PROSECUTION. VERSUS Santosh Parshuram Labade, Age 25 years, R/o Paye, Tal. Bhiwandi, Dist. Thane. ... ... ... ACCUSED. ­­­­­ Offence punishable under sections 354, 451 of the Indian Penal Code and under Sections 11(1) r/w. 12, 7 r/w. Sec. 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. ==================================== Mr.S.D.Londhe, A.P.P. for the prosecution. Mr. Gaurish Kadam, Advocate for the accused. 2 JUDGMENT ( Delivered on 25th day of June, 2018 ) 1) Accused Santosh Parshuram Labade is charge sheeted by Police Station Bhiwandi Taluka, Dist. Thane on 20/12/2014 for having committed an offence punishable under sections 354, 451 of the Indian Penal Code and under Sections 11(1)/12, 7, 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (POCSO Act) on the report of informant Victim (P.W.1) aged about 15 years, resident of Paye, Tal. Bhiwandi, Dist. Thane. 2) Prosecution case, briefly stated, is that informant Victim (PW1) and Rajesh (PW2) are children Premabai Chipat (PW3). Accused Santosh is their neighbour. The incident took place in the night between 01/10/2014 and 02/10/2014 at about 02.30 hours while informant Victim (PW1) along with her mother Premabai (PW3) and other family members were sleeping in the house. Informant 's father is dead. 3) At the relevant time, while the informant along with her mother Premabai and others were sleeping, accused Santosh entered in the house and pulled her legs stating that she likes him and threatened not to shout. On shout of Victim (PW1) Premabai got up and thereby accused Santosh ran away. This was seen in the light. 4) Thereafter, the informant Victim (PW1) along with Premabai (PW3) rushed to the house of accused Santosh and 3 Spl. Case (POCSO) No.269/2014 Judg.Exh. CNR No.MHTH01­007296­2014 intimated his wife Sugandha in this regard but she said that she did not know where was accused Santosh. Both then approached to village Sarpanch Geetabai Govardhan Labade and she promised that action will be taken in the morning. As such, in the morning both approached to the police station and informant Victim lodged report and thereby offence vide C.R.No. I­216/2014 under Section 354, 451 of I.P.C. and Sec. 11(1)/12, 7/8 of POCSO Act, 2012 was registered against accused Santosh. 5) Upon report investigation was geared up. Investigating Officer API Rajiv Sarjerao Patil carried out investigation. He has drawn spot panchanama. Statement of witnesses were recorded. Accused was arrested. After investigation charge­sheet was filed. 6) From the material on record, my Ld. Predecessor Mr. Ashutosh Karmarkar, Dist. Judge­1 has framed charge at Exh.6 on 13/01/2017 for the offence punishable under Sec. 354, 451 of I.P.C. and Sec. 11(1) r/w. Sec. 12 and Sec. 7 r/w. Sec. 8 of POCSO Act, 2012. The contents of charge were read over and explained to the accused Santosh in vernacular to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 7) Oral evidence of prosecution consists of informant Victim (PW1) at Exh.7, spot pancha Rajesh Shantaram Chipat (PW2) at Exh.9, Premabai Naglya Chipat (PW3) at Exh.12 and Investigating Officer API Rajiv Sarjerao Patil (PW4) at Exh.19. 8) Documentary evidence of prosecution consists of report at 4 Exh.8 and spot panchanama at Exh.10. Prosecution closed evidence by pursis at Exh.20. 9) The evidence of Victim (PW1) reveals that her father is dead and the incident took place in the night when she along with her mother and sister were sleeping in the house. Her evidence also revealed that her birth date is 26/03/1999 and that on the day of incident her brother had been out of home for job. The evidence of Victim (PW1) discloses that in the night time accused entered in the house and kept his hand on her person and gave threat by uttering "Ghongat Karu Nako Nahitar Maren" and upon that her mother Premabai got up and accused Santosh ran away and she lodged report Exh.8. Her evidence is also on the point that she was studying in the Zilha Parishad school. 10) Accused Santosh cross­examined Victim (PW1) on the line that she is more than 18 years of age and there is dispute between his family and her family on account of election of Sarpanch and therefore, false case is filed. 11) Rajesh (PW2) is brother of Victim. His evidence is on the point that he was present for spot panchanama and the spot panchanama is at Exh.10. Accused cross­examined Rajesh (PW2) on the line that he is deposing false being brother of Victim. 12) Premabai (PW3) is Victim's mother. Premabai (PW3) has supported the version of Victim (PW1) in respect of relations and occurrence of incident and giving of report on the next day in the 5 Spl. Case (POCSO) No.269/2014 Judg.Exh. CNR No.MHTH01­007296­2014 police station. Accused cross­examined Premabai (PW3) on the line that because of dispute between his family and the family of Premabai on the point of election of Sarpanch, false case is filed. 13) Investigating Officer API Rajiv (PW4) has carried out investigation. He drew the spot panchanama Exh.10. He has recorded the statements of witnesses and submitted the charge­ sheet. Accused cross­examined Rajiv (PW4) on the line that he has not collected the birth certificate of Victim and filed false charge­ sheet. 14) As against this, accused did not adduce evidence in the defence and contended false case is filed against him and prayed for acquittal. 15) Heard Mr. S.D.Londhe, Ld. A.P.P. for the prosecution and Mr. Gaurish Kadam, Ld. Advocate for the accused. Appraised the entire material on record. 16) Mr. Londhe submitted that prosecution has proved the guilt against the accused for the offence charged beyond all reasonable doubt. Mr. Londhe submitted that accused Santosh being neighbourer, is very much acquainted with the Victim's family and knowing the fact that Victim's father is dead and brother is out of house for job, outraged her modesty in the night time. Mr. Londhe submitted that nothing to discard or disbelieve the testimony of informant Victim (PW1) and nothing is surfaced in the cross­examination or otherwise to discard the same. Mr. Londhe 6 submitted that the evidence of informant Victim is duly substantiated and corroborated by her mother Premabai (PW2) who is the best natural witness present on the spot. Mr. Londhe therefore, urged for conviction. 17) Mr. Kadam retaliated the submission of prosecution on the ground that there is delay of two days in lodging the report and the delay is not explained. Mr. Kadam submitted that there isn't independent witness to corroborate and the testimony of informant Victim (PW1) and the same is affected by material omission. Mr. Kadam submitted that prosecution failed to prove that the informant Victim was aged below 18 years. Mr. Kadam submitted that the witnesses namely Rajesh (PW2) and Premabai (PW3) are related and therefore, interested and urged for acquittal. 18) Having regard to the submissions advanced at bar and after appraisal of entire material on record, I find merit in the submission of Mr. Londhe and demerit in the submission of Mr. Kadam for following additional reasons. Accordingly, following points arise for my consideration and determination and I record my findings against each of points as under. ­ POINTS FINDINGS 1) Does the prosecution prove that on ... In the 02/10/2014 at about 2.30 a.m. accused affirmative. Santosh committed criminal trespass by entering in the house of Victim (PW1) situated at village Paye, Tal. Bhiwandi, Dist. Thane and outraged her modesty by using criminal force ? 7 Spl. Case (POCSO) No.269/2014 Judg.Exh. CNR No.MHTH01­007296­2014 2) Does the prosecution prove that on the ... In the aforesaid date, time and pace, accused affirmative. Santosh committed sexual assault by touching the person of informant Victim (PW1) by entering in her house ? 3) Does the prosecution prove that on the ... In the aforesaid date, time and pace, accused affirmative. Santosh committed the sexual harassment of informant Victim (PW1) by uttering "Ghongat Karu Nako Nahitar Marin" ? 4) What order ? ... Accused is convicted. REASONS 19) Points No. 1 to 3 :­ These points are interlinked and therefore, taken up together for reasoning and findings. 20) Few facts either admitted or proved from the evidence on record may be stated at the outset. Premabai (PW2) is mother of Victim (PW1) and Rajesh (PW3). Informant Victim's father is dead. Informant Victim's brother was not in the house at the relevant time. Informant Victim and accused Santosh are neighbourers. 21) The evidence of informant Victim (PW1) is self sufficient and omnipotent. The evidence is crystal clear. The evidence can be seen vividly. Unequivocally she has deposed in respect of her birth date, in respect of occurrence of incident, in respect of keeping of hand on her person by accused, in respect of threat given by the accused, in respect of awaking her mother Premabai and lodging of 8 report. The evidence is unshattered and undisturbed in the cross­ examination. Nothing to discard or disbelieve. Normally woman would not tell lie and lodge false case where her character is going to the questioned publicly. It is for the accused Santosh to make out a strong case that he is falsely implicated but that did not happen. 22) Accused Santosh cross­examined Victim (PW1) on the line that because of political animosity false case is filed but the same cannot be accepted. There might be dispute between two families but for that no family assassin the character of the female member of that particular family. The circumstances and more particularly the circumstance that Victim's father is dead and brother is out of house for job in the night time speaks in volume as a favourable circumstance to the accused to commit the offence. 23) Informant Victim (PW1) admitted in the cross­ examination that her age is more than 18 years, but that admission is undoubtedly appear slip of tongue, sporadic, without awareness and casually without knowing the consequences because she has specifically stated in her examination­in­chief that her birth date is 26/03/1999 and that accused Santosh did not make out specific case as against this that her birth date is not 26/03/1999 or otherwise. Informant Victim has specifically deposed that her birth date is 26/03/1999 and therefore, nothing to discard the same. All in all, the testimony of Informant Victim (PW1) inspire confidence being natural and dependable. 9 Spl. Case (POCSO) No.269/2014 Judg.Exh. CNR No.MHTH01­007296­2014 24] Premabai (PW3) is the best natural witness present on the spot. Merely Premabai is related to the Victim as a mother does not mean that she is interested. Though Premabai admits in cross­ examination that at the relevant time uncle of the accused Santosh was Sarpanch but at the same time she has clearly denied that there was dispute between her family and family of Santosh on account of election of sarpanch. No mother will go to the extent to speak false in respect of assassination of character of her daughter unless it is a fact. Rift between the two families in the normal course cannot give cause of action for filing false case which may decharacterise and disrepute female member and family as a whole in the relative and society at large. It is therefore, the contention of accused that because there was family dispute, false case is filed, is not acceptable. In other word, Premabai (PW3) supports, substantiates and corroborates testimony of informant Victim (PW1) in respect of her watching the incident, age of the informant Victim and therefore, acceptable and dependable. 25] The evidence of Rajesh (PW2) in the cross­examination revealed that police have prepared panchanama and he has signed. But in the chief examination he clearly admitted that spot panchanama Exh. 10 is drawn in his presence. Accused did not dispute the geography of the spot. 26] Besides the evidence of investigating officer API Rajiv (PW4) is unshaken in the cross­examination in respect of carrying out the investigation. Though investigating officer API Rajiv (PW4) admitted in the cross­examination that he has not collected birth 10 certificate of informant Victim but that itself does not dislodge the evidence of informant Victim on the point of specific mention of birth date and the corroboration to that by Premabai. In fact, mother and children are the best witnesses to tell about their birth date. Oral evidence regarding birth date is not dislodged or shaken by accused Santosh by dependable evidence. So there is sufficient evidence to establish and prove that the informant Victim was below 18 years. 27] The contention of the accused that there is some variation, some omission and contradictions in the testimony of informant Victim but again that does not discredit the testimony of informant Victim (PW1). Some variation here and there do not go into the root of the testimony and the incident narrated but some variation lend credibility to the testimony of witness being a natural witness. The memory of witness cannot be a xerox one. So some variation are bound to be in the testimony of witness for the obvious reason that witness narrates the incident after lapse of year or so and that sometime witness is bewilder and puzzled while giving the evidence through the witness box in the serious atmosphere in the court room. Though informant Victim (PW1) admitted in cross­examination that the accused has kept his hand on her person, is not mentioned in her statement recorded by police but the same is not put to investigating officer API Rajiv (PW4). It is very trivial likewise the words "Nahitar Marin" though not mentioned in the statement, but the said are not referred to I.O. API Rajiv (PW4). As such there isn't material omission and 11 Spl. Case (POCSO) No.269/2014 Judg.Exh. CNR No.MHTH01­007296­2014 contradictions and therefore, minor omissions and contradictions will have to be ignored and neglected since it does not discredit the testimony of informant Victim. 28] Accused Santosh contended that there is delay in lodging the report but the same is not digestible. On the very next day of incident, report was lodged. Normally whenever the offences against the women take place, family members do not immediately rush to the police station to lodge the report for the obvious reason that they feel that lodging of report may bring Victim and family to disrepute and it is considered social stigma and therefore, it is only after deliberation and after mental preparation family lodges the report. So in such cases, one cannot say there is delay in lodging the report. There isn't case contended by the accused Santosh that delay was caused so as to falsely implicate accused withe ulterior motive and there was deliberation to that effect. So there isn't delay. 29] In addition to this, this is a fit case where presumption under Sec. 29 of POCSO Act has to be drawn against the accused Santosh that he has committed the offence under Sec. 7 of POCSO Act and the same is not rebutted by accused Santosh. Not only that there is more than sufficient material to raise the presumption in respect of culpable mental state of accused Babulal under Sec. 30 of POCSO Act. Both presumptions are unbuttered for want of rebuttal evidence. 30] Now what offence is made out. From the evidence 12 surfaced on record prosecution has proved beyond all reasonable doubt that accused Santosh has committed house trespass by entering into the dwelling house of informant Victim, outraged the modesty of informant Victim by using the criminal force, sexually assaulted informant Victim by keeping his hand on Victim's person and sexually harassed her by giving threat on 02/10/2014 at about 2.30 a.m. and that informant Victim below age of 18 years and thereby committed offences under Sec. 354, 451 of I.P.C. and under Sec. 7 r/w. Sec.8 and 11(1) r/w. Sec. 12 of POCSO Act. Accused therefore, is convicted for the above said offence and has to be sentenced. Accordingly, I answer the points in the affirmative. Now, I am going to hear the accused on the point of sentence. ( R. V. Jatale ) Thane. Additional Sessions Judge Date : 25/06/2018. & Special Judge (POCSO Act), Thane. 31) I have heard accused Santosh, Mr. Gaurish Kadam and Mr. Londhe on the point of sentence. 32) Accused Santosh submitted for leniency on the ground that he is only earning in his family and he has small children. 33) Mr. Kadam submitted for leniency on the ground that it is a first offence, accused has small children and he is the only earning member in his family. 13 Spl. Case (POCSO) No.269/2014 Judg.Exh. CNR No.MHTH01­007296­2014 34) Mr. Londhe submitted for severe sentence in accordance with law since offence is serious. 35) Having regard to the submissions advanced at bar and after appraisal of entire material on record, the offence committed by accused Santosh in question is undoubtedly serious, grievous and terrorizing not only to the informant Victim but ot her family member. The informant Victim and her family member put to disreputation. Accused Santosh being a neighbourer has committed the said offence. The offence against the women are serious for the reason that it defamed the entire family and the future of Victim ruins. Under these circumstances I do not find that accused should be shown special leniency while sentencing. The sentence must be commensurate with the gravity of the offence. 36] The offence under Sec. 354 of I.P.C. is punishable with imprisonment of either discretion for a term which may extend to two years or with fine or with both. The offence under Sec. 451 of I.P.C. is punishable with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years and shall also be liable to fine. The offence under Sec. 7 r/w. Sec. 8 of POCSO Act is punishable for a term which shall not be less than three years but which may extend to five years and shall also be liable to fine. The offence under Sec. 11 r/w. Sec. 12 of POCSO Act is punishable with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine. From this, the intention of the legislature is crystal clear that the perpetrator of such offence should be dealt with sternly. There isn't circumstance either 14 surfaced on the record through the cross­examination or otherwise to show special leniency to accused Santosh. 37) In view of the observation regarding the gravity of the offence and suffering of the informant Victim, accused will have to be sentenced for the offence punishable under Sec. 354 and 451 of I.P.C. and under Sec. 7 r/w. Sec.8 and Sec. 11(1) r/w. Sec. 12 of POCSO Act and thereby cumulatively sentenced to simple imprisonment of three (3) years and fine of Rs. 5,000/­ i/d. simple imprisonment for six month and that will meet the ends of justice. What leniency can be shown is only that accused can be given set off for the detention period he has undergone. 38 ) Now coming to Sec. 357­A of Cr.P.C., under Sec. 33(8) of POCSO Act and Rule 7 of POCSO Rule. As observed above, it is a blot and scar on the soul and mind of Victim. The entire life of is ruined. By no stretch of imagination, it can be compensated in terms of money. It is constitutional mandate of the State that it shall protect life, liberty and property of every person within the territory of India. Not only that, it should be protected but in case of violation, people should be compensated justly, fairly and reasonably. In this backdrop, I deem it fit that this matter should be referred for just, fair and reasonable compensation to the District Legal Services Authority, Thane and the District Magistrate, Thane for necessary action. 39) Perusal of record clearly reveal that there isn't muddemal therefore, there cannot be order to that effect. 15 Spl. Case (POCSO) No.269/2014 Judg.Exh. CNR No.MHTH01­007296­2014 40) In view of reasons and findings stated supra, the prosecution has proved the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubt for the offences charged above and therefore, he stands convicted and sentenced. Accordingly, I proceed to pass following order. ORDER 1) Accused Santosh Parshuram Labade is convicted under Section 235 (2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for the offence punishable under section Sec. 354 and 451 of I.P.C. and under Sec. 7 r/w. Sec.8 and Sec. 11(1) r/w. Sec. 12 of POCSO Act and thereby sentenced cumulatively to simple imprisonment for three (3) years and fine of Rs. 5,000/­ i/d. simple imprisonment for six month. 2) Accused Santosh shall surrender his bail bond. Accused is taken in the custody. Issue jail warrant. Accused Santosh was under detention from 11/10/2014 to 20/11/2014 and therefore, he is entitled for set off of the said period under Sec. 428 of Cr.P.C. 3) A sum of Rs. 4,000/­(Rupees Four Thousand only) be paid to the informant Victim (PW1) out of fine amount recovered towards compensation. 4) Since there isn't muddemal there isn't order to that effect. 5) Copy of Judgment and Order shall be supplied free of cost to the informant Victim (PW1) and accused Santosh. 6) Copy of Judgment and Order be forwarded with 16 complements to the District Legal Services Authority, Thane and the District Magistrate, Thane for disbursing just, reasonable and fair compensation to the informant Victim (PW1). 7) P. & D. in the court. ( R. V. Jatale ) Thane. Additional Sessions Judge Date:25/06/2018 & Special Judge (POCSO Act), Thane. 17 Spl. Case (POCSO) No.269/2014 Judg.Exh. CNR No.MHTH01­007296­2014 Spl. Case No. 269/2014

Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Mr.Dhaware for the applicant/ accused and learned A.P.P. Mrs. Kapre for State. I.O. present. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 24.10.2015 at the instance of the informant/victim­girl with an indictment that the accused persons outraged her modesty by singing filmy songs with intent that it shall be heard by the girl and also hit a wooden strip on her back portion with intent to outrage her modesty. Therefore, the report came to be lodged. 2 Bail No. 2710/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) 4] The learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant­accused is falsely implicated. He submitted that during Navratri festival while Garba dancing by mistake stick was hit to the girl and therefore there was hot exchange of word and therefore this false complaint came to be lodged. He submitted that in fact the victim­girl is having love affair with another boy in the locality which was known by all the residents except the parents of victim­girl and during quarrel the parents of victim­girl came to know about the affair of victim­girl and therefore victim­girl consumed phenyl. He is permanent resident of the address given in the application and is ready to abide by any conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing him on bail. 5] Per contra, the learned A.P.P. opposed the application only on the ground that victim­girl is staying in the same vicinity and therefore there are chances of tampering of the witnesses and further the offence is serious in respect of minor girl and prayed for rejection of application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R. it appears that the allegations are about outraging modesty of victim girl aged 16 years.
