.. 1 .. bail 2618/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 2618 of 2014 This application is filed by applicant Kumar Roshan Ganesh Pandav alias Sushant Mohite for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. I­503/2014 registered at Vartaknagar police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 354D, 323, 506 of I.P.C. and section 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. It was contended and argued that the applicant and the complainant girl had become friends on facebook and then started chatting with each other and they also developed love relations with each other. It is further contended and argued that the applicant has been falsely involved in this crime with the allegation that when the complainant girl refused to meet him alone, the applicant/accused held her hand and also slapped and threatened her. It is further contended and argued that no such incident has ever happened. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co­operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that the accused and the complainant girl had become friends of each other on facebook. It is further contended and argued that on 21.11.2014 at 4.00 p.m. when the complainant girl was standing at the main gate of junior college at Shivai nagar with her friends, the accused came there and asked her to meet him alone but when she refused, the accused held .. 2 .. bail 2618/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) her hand and slapped and also told her ''tu mazhi nahitar konachich nahi'' and made criminal intimidation to her. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the complainant and other prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 354D, 323, 506 of I.P.C. and section 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012, the allegations in the complaint are that the complainant and the accused had become friends on facebook and started chatting with each other and then the accused followed the complainant and proposed for marriage etc. and that thereafter the accused had even slapped the complainant and threatened her etc. As rightly pointed out on behalf of applicant/accused the facts which are apparent from plain reading of the complaint are that the complainant and the accused had developed friendship on internet. Then, even from the perusal of record of chat communication produced on record by the applicant, the fact is clear that the complainant and the accused had developed friendship and as rightly pointed out on behalf of applicant/accused the complainant also was equally responding to the messages sent by the applicant/ accused. In the light of that the contentions raised on behalf of applicant/accused it was one sided story of the complainant and she was forcing the applicant/accused to marry her and then the .. 3 .. bail 2618/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) complainant herself cut her vein and caused herself injury and when the applicant/accused avoided to meet her etc. assumes importance and the aspect as to whether the allegations in the complaint made against the accused are true or whether the submissions on behalf of applicant/accused are genuine, would be the question to be decided on merits. Even nothing is stated to be recovered from him. 4] Then, it is well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be gone into detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence. 5] In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 6] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 7] Then, it has also to be mentioned that the investigation in the matter though almost completed the charge sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and .. 4 .. bail 2618/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) submit the charge sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 8] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused kumar Roshan Ganesh Pandav alias Sushant Mohite is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ He shall attend the concerned police station on every Wednesday between 3.00 p.m. to 5.00 p.m. till filing of the charge sheet and shall co­operate with the investigation. He shall not contact the victim in any manner. He shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and other prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 09.01.2015. (Mrs.V.V.Virkar) District Judge­1 and Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.

.. 1 .. Special Case No.137/2013 Judgment Presented on : 26.12.2013 Registered on : 26.12.2013 Decided on : 24.11.2015 Duration : 01 Y. 10 M. 29 D. IN THE COURT OF THE SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE (Presided over by Ms. U. M. Nandeshwar, Special Judge under POCSO Act, Thane) SPECIAL CASE No. 137 of 2013 Exhibit No.28. The State of Maharashtra through Police Station Kasarvadavli District Thane ... Prosecution. versus Vipul Vijay Tivatane. Age 33 years, Residence – Madli Bungalow, Anand Nagar, Bhigwan Road, Baramati, District Pune. ... Accused. Offence punishable under section 363, of Indian Penal Code and under section 11 r/w. section 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Appearance ­ A.P.P.Mrs. R.A.Navale, for the State. Advocate Mr. Eknath Phad, for the accused .. 2 .. Special Case No.137/2013 Judgment JUDGMENT (Delivered on 24th November, 2015.) 1] The accused stands prosecuted for the offence punishable under section 363 of Indian Penal Code and under section 11 r/w. section 12 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act) for kidnapping minor victim­girl aged 8 years. 2] The indictment against the accused are as under ­ ( i ) Informant Kisan Shrimant Kale is resident of Patalipada, near over bridge, Ghodbunder road, Thane. He was staying there with his wife, brother and niece victim­girl aged about 8 years. ( ii ) On 09.06.2013 as his hut was having leakage and the rain water was dripping in his house and therefore he along with his family including victim­girl were sleeping under the over bridge. (iii) On 10.06.2013 at about 2.45 a.m. he heard screaming of his niece victim­girl. At that time he had seen that one person was taking away his niece in car towards Brahmand signal. He raised shout but as it was night time therefore he could not get any vehicle. Therefore, to chase the vehicle he started running towards Brahmand signal. .. 3 .. Special Case No.137/2013 Judgment (iv) There informant had seen one white colour Indica car having registration number MH­04­ES­9178 was met with an accident by dashing to the road­divider. He had heard scream of his niece/victim­girl from that vehicle. At the same time one police vehicle approached there. Police took out his niece/victim­girl and the driver from the vehicle. (v) On asking the driver disclosed his name as Vipul Vijay Tivatane i.e. accused and victim­girl narreted that when she was sleeping with her aunt at that time the driver of vehicle took her away and thrust her in the vehicle and when she tried to raise shout he gagged her mouth by his hand and when he proceeded with the vehicle at some distance, the vehicle met with an accident near divider. Therefore, the report was lodged. 3] On his report the F.I.R. was registered against the accused vide C.R.No.I­193/2013 for the offence punishable under section 363 of I.P.C. and under section 11 r/w. section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. P.W.3­ Rafiq Shaikh police Hawaldar recorded report. The investigation was carried out by P.W.2­API Sharad Murkute. He visited spot and spot­panchnama was drawn and Indica car bearing registration No. MH­04/ES­9178 was seized from the sopt. Statements of witnesses including victim­girl were recorded. Her scool certificate for verification of date of birth was collected. Thereafter, investigation culminated inti filing of charge­sheet in this Court being the .. 4 .. Special Case No.137/2013 Judgment Special designated court under POCSO Act. 4] My learned predecessor the erstwhile Additional sessions Judge Mrs. V. V. Virkar framed the charge (Exh.2) against the accused for offence punishable under section 363 of Indian Penal Code and also under section 11 r/w. section 12 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. The accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial (Exh.3). The accused took defence of total denial. 5] In response to application under section 294 of Cr.P.C. the defence has admitted [i] certificate issued by Thane Municipal School No.53 in respect of age of victim­girl (Exh.18). 6] Prosecution in order to prove guilt of accused has examined following witnesses ­ P.W.1 Anant Gopinath Ahire Exh.13 P.W.2 API Sharad Haribhau Murkute Exh.14 P.W.3 Head Constable Rafiq Babu Shaikh Exh.23 7] The prosecution proved and relied on the following documents­ Sr.No. Particulars of Document Exhibit [i] Report & FIR dtd. 10/06/2013 Exh. 24 [ii] Spot panchnama dtd 10/06/2013 Exh.15 .. 5 .. Special Case No.137/2013 Judgment [iii] Muddemal receipt Exh.16 [iv] letter issued to Principal Municipal School Exh.17 Patlipada, Thane [v] Certificate issued by Municipal School Exh.18 Patlipada, Thane in respect of birth date of victim­girl. 8] The prosecution close its side of evidence by filing Pursis at Exh.25. The incriminating evidence came on record against the accused was read over and explained to them and their statement under Section 313(b) of Cr.P.C. are recorded vide Exh.27. Accused neither examined himself nor examined any witness in his defence. 9] Heard learned A.P.P. Mrs. R. A. Navale for State and the Ld. Advocate Mr.Eknath Phad for accused. 10] On consideration of argument advanced on behalf of both the sides & on perusal of the oral & documentary evidence on record, following points arise for my determination, which are answered with the findings thereon, as under :­ Sr. No. Points Findings 1. Does prosecution prove that on 10/03/2013 accused kidnapped minor victim­girl from lawful guardianship of informant Kisan Shrimant Kale while she was sleeping alongwith the informant on ..No. the road below the Patalipada bridge, Thane and thereby committed offence u/sec.363 of I.P.C.? .. 6 .. Special Case No.137/2013 Judgment 2. Does the prosecution prove that on the given date, time and place accused, after ..No. kidnapping the minor victim­girl committed sexual harassment on her by gagging her mouth by his hand and thereby committed offence punishable u/sec.11 r/w sec.12 of POCSO Act? 3. What order ? ..As per final order REASONS As to Point Nos.1 and 2 : 11] Both the points are taken up together for discussion to avoid the repetition as they are inter­connected and evidence for the same is common. 12] As the accused is facing charge under section 11 r/w. section 12 of POCSO Act and also under Section 363 of IPC it was incumbent on the part of prosecution to prove that the victim girl was minor on the date of incident. 13] To prove the age of the victim­girl, prosecution is relying on certificate issued by Thane Municipal School No. 53 which is at Exh.18. According to which the date of birth of the victim­girl is 23/01/2003. It means at the relevant time victim girl was child below 18 years of age. The said document is also admitted by the defence and thus the age of the victim­girl is not disputed. Exh.18 is sufficient to prove that the victim­girl .. 7 .. Special Case No.137/2013 Judgment was minor on the date of incident. 14] However, it is pertinent to note that though summons were issued to time and again to the informant and victim­girl, they could not be traced out and therefore prosecution could not examine the said witnesses who are the most material witnesses for the prosecution to prove the charge against the accused. The prosecution case thus received serious blow for non­examination of the material witnesses. 15] The prosecution to prove the recording of FIR examined Rafiq Shaikh (P.W.3) who was Police Hawaldar attached to Kasarvadavli police station at the relevant time. He took the report of informant Kisan Shrimant Kale and on his report C.R. No.I­193/2013 was registered which is at Exh.24. Thus, this witness is only formal witness examined by the prosecution to prove the registration of crime. Nothing material to disbelieve this witness is elicited in cross­ examination. However, though the registration of FIR is proved, it is of not much help to the prosecution for want of evidence of informant and victim­girl. 16] The prosecution in support of its case examined P.W.1 ­ Anant Gopinath Ahire, who is the registered owner of white colour Indica car bearing No. MH­04­ES­9878. He deposed that he had given the said car to one call center and .. 8 .. Special Case No.137/2013 Judgment accused was appointed as driver. On 09.06.2013 the car was with accused as he was driver on the said car and he had taken away same for work. He further deposed that on next day morning he was called by Kasarvadavli police station and informed that his car was seized in respect of some crime. Thus, as per P.W.1 on the day of incident the car was in possession of the accused. However, in cross­examination he admitted that whenever car was not sent for work, it was parked at Navnath garage. He gave another material admission that at the relevant time the car was parked in the garage, though he stated that its keys were with the accused. Except this witness prosecution failed to examine any other independent witness. The evidence of P.W.1 is not sufficient to point out the guilt of the accused. 17] The evidence of P.W.2 API Shrad Murkute is also formal nature who deposed about the investigation carried out by him. Thus, there is absolutely no evidence to prove the charge against the accused that he kidnapped the victim­girl from her lawful guardian­informant and cause sexual harassment to minor victim­girl. Thus, prosecution miserably failed to prove the guilt of the accused in absence of substantive evidence of informant and victim­girl. Therefore, I have no option than to acquit the accused. Hence, I answer point Nos. 1 and 2 in the negative. .. 9 .. Special Case No.137/2013 Judgment 18] In the result, I proceed to pass the following order. 1 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 271/2014 Judgment Received on :­ 20.12.2014 Registered on :­ 20.12.2014 Decided on :­ 22.06.2017 Duration :­ 2Y 6M 2 D IN THE COURT OF ADDITIONAL SESSIONS JUDGE, & SPECIAL JUDGE (POCSO) ACT, THANE AT : THANE ( Presided over by Ashutosh N.Karmarkar, District Judge­1 & Special Judge (POCSO) Act, Thane ) Special Case (POCSO) No.271/2014 Exh. No. 16 State of Maharashtra ( Through Wagle Estate Police Station ) …Complainant V/s. Rakesh Nivrutti Kesarkar Age : 24 Years, Occ. : Business R/at.: Silvesiya Society, 2rd floor, Room No.22, Revati mata chowk, Savarkarnagar, Thane … Accused. Offence punishable under Sec. 354­D(1)(i) of Indian Penal Code & under Secs. 11(i) r/w. 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 271/2014 Judgment Appearances : Shri. V.G.Kadu, A.P.P. for the State Shri.G.G.Dhaware, Advocate for accused JUDGMENT ( Delivered on this 22nd day of June, 2017 ) 1] Accused is facing trial for the offence punishable under Sec. 354­D(1)(i) of Indian Penal Code and under Secs. 11(i) r/w. S.12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] Prosecution Case, in brief, is as under : Informant / victim is residing with her parents and younger sister in Sambhaji lane, Shripad Yadav Chawl, Room No.2, Thane (W). Informant and her younger sister are studying in Rustomaji Academy for Global Career Institute. They both go to college at 10.45 a.m. and comes at 6.00 p.m. On 01.09.2014, informant had been to college. She was returning at 6.00 p.m. along with her sister. Somebody gave call from backside. She noticed the present accused. She did not respond. He followed the victim. He was giving calls. Victim did not respond. This accused came from backside and caught hold her hand, due to which she felt shy. She rescued herself. Her mother came there. Then, they approached to police station and lodged the report. 3] On the basis of report, offence was registered vide C.R.No. I­227/2014. P.S.I. Shubhangi Gavate had investigated this 3 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 271/2014 Judgment crime. Initially H.C.More has recorded the report. She collected birth Certificate of the victim. She drew spot panchanama. She has recorded statements of witnesses. After completion of investigation, she filed charge­sheet in the Court of Law. 4] I have framed charge against accused below Exh. 3 to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. Total denial is the defence of accused. 5] Prosecution has examined three witnesses. Then, the statement of the accused under Sec. 313 of Cr.P.C. came to be recorded. Total denial is the defence of the accused. The accused has also tried to raise defence that there was love affair between the accused and the victim and family members of the victim were not liking it. So, her parents forced her to lodge report against him. 6] I have heard both the sides. 7] Following points arose for my determination and I gave my findings thereon for the reasons stated below: Sr. POINTS FINDINGS No. 1. Does the prosecution prove that the No accused on 01.09.2014 at 18.05 hrs., in front of Kamgar Hospital, on road No.33, going towards Kamgar Hospital from Nitin Naka, Wagle Estate, Thane 4 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 271/2014 Judgment followed informant i.e. minor victim girl aged 17 years contacts, or attempts to contact her to foster personal interaction repeatedly despite a clear indication of disinterest by her ? 2. Does the prosecution prove that on No. above mentioned date, time and place, accused committed sexual harassment upon informant i.e. minor victim girl, age 17 years with sexual intent? 3. What order? As per final order. REASONS AS TO POINT NO.1 & 2­ 8] It is well settled that in order to prove the guilt of accused, prosecution is required to adduce cogent and convincing evidence. It is well settled that the sole testimony of witness is also sufficient to base the conviction. But, the rule is that it should inspire confidence in the mind of court and should be above suspicion. If a single grain of doubt appears in the prosecution story then, defence get benefit of it. 9] The prosecution has examined P.W.1 informant's mother Vandana Chavan (Exh. 6), P.W.2 informant /victim (Exh.9) and P.W. 3 investigation officer , P.S.I. Shubhangi Gavate (Exh.12). 10] In order to establish guilt under Sec. 354­D(1)(i) of 5 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 271/2014 Judgment Indian Penal Code, the prosecution is required to prove that the accused has followed the victim and contacted to foster personal interaction repeatedly and that act was despite clear indication of disinterest by the victim. Bare perusal of the provisions of Sec. 354­ D(1)(i) shows that there has to be repeated acts of following or contacting the victim. 11] P.W.2 Pallavi has stated that at the time of incident, her age was 17 years and she was studying automobile diploma course. She used to return from Academy at 6.00 p.m. Incident occurred at Dyandeshwar Nagar naka, Wagle Estate. Her sister was with her. Accused came from backside. He gave call. She did not respond. Then, he caught hold her hand which she did not like. Her mother also came there. Then, report (Exh.11) was lodged. Examination­ in­chief of victim does not reveal that the accused was repeatedly following and trying to contact the victim. It appears from the cross­examination of the victim and her mother that the victim and accused were residing in same vicinity. Victim's mother was acquainted to accused and his family members. Victim also admits that she knows as to exactly where the accused is residing, she also knows that the accused has studied upto 10th standard and he is resident from Konkan. Accused and victim were having friendship. At the second moment, victim has stated that she was not having friendship with the accused. Subsequently, victim has admitted that during 'Dahihandi' programme, accused met with an accident and was admitted in the 6 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 271/2014 Judgment hospital on 14.08.2013 and she went to meet him in hospital. On 30.03.2014 also when accused was admitted in Lokmanya Nagar Hospital, she went to meet him. She had also admitted that on 22.04.2014, she had been to Avasari Manchar. At the same time accused had been to Manchar to attend marriage of his friend. It is also admitted that victim and her sister met accused at Manchar bus stand. She has further stated that on 23.04.2014, she came with accused from Manchar to Swargate and they both came by Konark­Bhuvaneshwar Express from Pune to Thane. They reached at 3.00 a.m. at Thane. Her friend Ravi Gopreddy came to receive her at station and she went to his house, where she stayed till 2.00 p.m. Admittedly, she did not state these facts to her parents. At one place, she has stated that she had no affair with accused, but the accused had love from his side. At the second moment, victim has admitted that one Jadhav family reside near her house and they have two daughters named Kadambari and Kavita. Victim has specifically admitted that Kadambari was knowing about victim's love affair. 12] Accused has also brought on record some photographs (Exh. 15) wherein the photographs of the present victim and accused are appearing. Victim has admitted that these photographs are taken during their visits at different places. It seems that these photographs are also admitted by the victim. In the backdrop of these facts, evidence is to be scrutinized. 7 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 271/2014 Judgment 13] Already a suggestion was given to the mother of the victim that they were not liking the affair between victim and the accused. The defence is already taken during the statement u/sec. 313 of Cr.P.C. that since the family members of the victim were not liking the relations between the victim and the accused, he is being falsely implicated. 14] It appears that the incident occurred at public place i.e. at Dyaneshwar Nagar Naka. Spot panchanama Exh.30 shows that there are shops to one side of the spot. P.W.1,Vandana is mother of the victim. She has admitted that road where incident occurred is busy road. People always move from the said road. Incident occurred at 6.00 p.m. It was possible for the prosecution to have independent witness. They have not examined any independent/ impartial witness. Secondly, there is no consistency in the evidence of the victim and her mother. It is the case of the mother of victim that she had been to college to take victim back. On the day of incident, the accused caught hold the hand of the victim and started dragging her forcibly. So, she raised shouts. But, the victim has nowhere stated that the accused started dragging her and her mother raised shouts. Therefore, it is difficult to accept the evidence of the victim and her mother as reliable. Sister of the victim was also present with her. But, she is not examined. 15] In order to establish the guilt u/sec. 354­D(1)(i), it is to 8 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 271/2014 Judgment be established that the accused followed her repeatedly to foster personal interaction. It is already discussed that the victim has not specifically stated about repeated attempts on the part of accused of following her. It is to be noted that since prior to the incident, accused and victim are knowing each other and have visited at different places. It also does not reveal that there was clear indication on the part of the victim as to disinterest towards the accused. On the contrary, the evidence of victim shows that she accompanied the accused while travelling from Manchar to Swargate and Pune to Thane. Victim has also stated about her visits with the accused at different places and photographs are taken. Victim's mother has also not stated that accused gave call to victim from backside and she did not respond. The victim's mother has stated that victim has narrated her that accused is following her when she used to go to college. But, this fact of narration to the mother is not stated by the victim in her oral evidence. So, the evidence of the victim and her mother does not appear to be consistent, reliable and satisfactory so as to prove the guilt of accused for which he is charged 16] In order to prove the guilt under Sec.11(i) r/w. S. 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, prosecution has to establish that the accused has committed sexual harassment and with sexual intent uttered any word or makes any sign or makes any gesture or exhibits any object or part of body with the 9 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 271/2014 Judgment intention that such word, sound shall be heard or gesture shall be seen. 17] Since accused's advocate has no objection with copy of birth extract of the victim (Exh.7), it appears that the date of birth of victim is 21.03.1997. Alleged incident is of 01.09.2014. So, age of the victim at the time of incident was about 17 ½ years. She was taking education. Even if it is accepted for a moment that age of victim was below 18 years, she has not stated that the accused has uttered any words or has made any sign or gesture so that she will see it. Even if it is accepted for a moment that there was utterance of any word or making of sign or gesture, it is for the prosecution to establish that this act was done with sexual intent. Reliance is to be placed in case of Bandu Vitthalrao Borwar V/s. State of Maharashtra, Criminal Appeal No. 50 of 2016, ( Bombay High Court). It is held in paragraph 10 and 11 as under : Para 10 “After all intention of a person is his state of mind and has to be discerned from the surrounding facts and circumstances. If one cannot, as a human being, physically enter into a mind of another to read and see what is being cooked there, one can surely know it by evaluating all that which is perceivable or felt by human senses such as words, body­ language, gestures, reactions and everything that is a physical manifestation of working of human mind. 10 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 271/2014 Judgment Para 11 “It is obvious that the intent, which is nothing but a state of mind, must be to establish some sort of physical contact or must be related to or associated with sex or indicative of involvement of sex in the relationship, if it is to be considered as sexual. I have already stated that the utterance indicating an expectation of a person that the other person should love him would not by itself amount to sexual intent as contemplated by the legislature. There should be something more which must suggest that the real intention is to drag in the angle of sex, if the words uttered are to be taken as conveying sexual intent.” 18] It is already discussed in foregoing paragraphs that evidence of victim and her mother pertaining to the incident does not appear to be reliable and satisfactory. Even the evidence of victim does not appear to be of a nature that the intention of the accused was to drag in the angle of sex. For the reasons stated above, it will be also difficult to accept that the prosecution has established the guilt by proving ingredients u/sec. 11(i) of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. 19] P.S.I. Shubhangi Gavate has conducted the investigation in routine manner. She drew spot panchanama and recorded statements of witnesses. She has no direct knowledge of the incident. Her evidence appear to be of formal nature. 11 Spl.Case (POCSO) No. 271/2014 Judgment 20] Considering the evidence on record, I found that the prosecution for want of satisfactory evidence failed to prove the guilt of accused for the offences for which he is charged. Hence, I answer point Nos.1 and 2 in the negative and proceed to pass following order: ORDER 1] Accused Rakesh Nivrutti Kesarkar is hereby acquitted under Sec.235(1) of Code of Criminal Procedure of the offence punishable under Sec. 354­D(1)(i) of Indian Penal Code and Secs.11(i) r/w. 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] His bail bond stands cancelled. 3] Accused shall furnish P.B and S.B. of RS. 10,000/­ under Sec. 437­A of Code of Criminal Procedure. 4] Dictated and pronounced in open Court. Thane ( Ashutosh N. Karmarkar ) Date : 22.06.2017 District Judge­1 & Special Judge (POCSO) Act, Thane

1 Bail No. 2729/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) Criminal Bail Application No.2729/2015. Pramod Jagan Manje .. Applicant versus The State of Maharashtra Through Padgha Police Station .. Non­applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 By this application the applicant is seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. who was arrested on 26.10.2015 by Padgha Police Station in connection with C.R.No.I­169/2015 registered for an offence punishable under section 376(2)(n) of I.P. Code and section 3, 4, 5, 6 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as P.O.C.S.O. Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Mr. S.E.Lasne for the applicant/ accused and learned A.P.P. Mrs. Kapre for State. I.O. present. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 25.10.2015 at the instance of the informant/victim­girl aged about 14 years with an indictment that accused is staying in her village and known to each other. The accused developed intimacy with her and promised her to marry and believing his words, the victim­girl used to meet him. On the pretext of marriage accused committed sexual assault on her because of which she carries pregnancy. However, accused and his 2 Bail No. 2729/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) parents denied their relations and refused to marry them and therefore, the report was lodged. 4] The learned Counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant­accused is falsely implicated. He submitted that accused is a young boy of 18 years and he is not even aware of the consequences of sexual relationship. He submitted that though victim is aged 14 years, it is clear case of love affair. He further submitted that only because the marriage was refused, false F.I.R. came to be registered. He further submitted that the parents of the accused are ready to marry their son to the victim­girl after she attaining majority. The applicant­accused is ready to abide any conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing him on bail. 5] Per contra, the learned A.P.P. opposed the application submitting that the offence is serious. She submitted that victim­girl is a minor girl of 14 years and therefore her consent is no consent in the eyes of law. Further, she carries pregnancy because of the sexual assault committed by the accused. The investigation is in progress. There are chances of tampering with witnesses and prayed for rejection of application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R., it prima facie appears that the victim­girl is aged about 14 years and therefore, in the facts of case her consent is no consent in the eyes of law. It further appears that due to the sexual relationship with the accused, now the minor girl of 14 years is carrying pregnancy. Though it was 3 Bail No. 2729/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) innocently argued that the accused does not know the consequences of his act, ignorance of law is not an excuse. The applicant­accused is involved in serious offence. The investigation is at nascent stage. As the victim­girl and accused are staying in same village, there are every chances of tampering of witnesses and pressurizing the victim­ girl. Therefore, no case is made out to release the accused on bail. Hence, I pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is rejected. Thane. Date : 07.11.2015. (Ms. U.M. Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act), Thane.

1 Bail No. 2732/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) Criminal Bail Application No. 2732/2015. 1) Sonu alias Suraj Ramesh Thakare 2) Subramani alias Mani Parimal Traveda .. Applicants versus The State of Maharashtra Through Shreenagar Police Station .. Non­applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 1] By this application the applicants are seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C., who were arrested on 26.10.2015 by Shreenagar Police Station in connection with C.R.No.I­305/2015 registered for an offence punishable under section 354D read with section 34 of I.P.C. and section 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Mr.J.G.Shingade for the applicants/accused and learned A.P.P. Mrs. Kapre for State. I.O. present. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 24.10.2015 at the instance of the informant/victim­girl with an indictment that the accused persons outraged her modesty by singing filmy songs with intent that it shall be heard by the girl and also hit a wooden strip on her back portion with intent to outrage her modesty. Therefore, the report came to be lodged. 2 Bail No. 2732/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) 4] The learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicants­accused are falsely implicated. He submitted that during Navratri festival while Garba dancing by mistake the stick was hit to the girl and therefore there was hot exchange of word and therefore this false complaint came to be lodged. He submitted that in fact the victim­girl is having love affair with another boy in the locality which was known by all the residents except the parents of victim­girl and during quarrel the parents of victim­girl came to know about the affair of victim­girl and therefore victim­girl consumed phenyl. The accused are not responsible for her decision to take phenyl. He submitted that the accused are young boys and are behind bar since their arrest. They are permanent residents of the address given in the application and are ready to abide by any conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing them on bail. 5] Per contra, the learned A.P.P. opposed the application only on the ground that victim­girl is staying in the same vicinity and therefore there are chances of tampering of the witnesses and further the offence is serious in respect of minor girl and prayed for rejection of application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R. it appears that the allegations are about outraging modesty of victim girl aged 16 years. Further it appears that the alleged incident about teasing the girl by singing a filmy song took place on 22.10.2015, however, the F.I.R. is lodged on 24.10.2015. It appears a case of eve teasing. All the four accused are of age group of 18 to 19 years. The material part of 3 Bail No. 2732/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) investigation appears to have been completed. No purpose would be served by further incarceration of applicants­accused. The object of bail is neither preventive nor punitive but to secure the presence of accused at the time of trial. The accused are ready to abide by any conditions imposed by the Court. The apprehension of A.P.P. can be addressed by imposing suitable conditions. Hence, I pass the following order ­ ORDER 1) The application is allowed. 2) Applicants namely Sonu alias Suraj Ramesh Thakare and Subramani alias Mani Parimal Traveda be released on bail on their executing P.R. Bond of ₹ 15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] each with one local surety each in the like amount on the following conditions ­ A] Applicants shall attend the concerned police station on every Monday in between 10.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon till filing of the charge­sheet. B] Applicants shall not tamper with prosecution witnesses. C] Applicants shall furnish their and their two blood relatives' address proofs and contact numbers and they are duty bound to inform I.O. and Court about the change of address, if any. D] Applicants shall not contact and pressurize victim­girl and any other witnesses in any manner and they shall maintain decency hereinafter. Thane. Date : 07.11.2015. (Ms. U.M. Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act), Thane.

Tushar Raut, for the accused. ___________________________________________________________ JUDGMENT (Delivered on 22.03.2018.) 1] Accused Mehboob Badshah Shaikh is facing trial for the offences punishable u/s. 376 of I.P.C. and u/s. 3 / 4 and 7 / 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2 POCSO Case No. 272/2016. 2] It is the case of prosecution that on 22.07.2016 at about 2.00 p.m., victim aged about 16 years, was not found in the house. So, Rajendra Murlidhar Mishra had lodged his report on 23.07.2016. It is registered vide C.R. no. 220/2016 u/s. 363 of I.P.C. Police had carried out their investigation. On 26.07.16, victim had disclosed the incident that on 22.07.2016, at about 2.00 p.m., Sudha Rajendra Mishra had been to hand­ cart to have 'Wada­Pav'. Her friend Mehboob Shaikh was found at Tulshidham. She asked him as “rw b/kj D;q vk;k \” He replied as, “eS elftnes uekt ds fy;s vk;k Fkk- rks ,slsgh b/kj ?kqeus ds fy;s vk;k gw- ” Thereafter, he asked her to wander some time. She sat down on his motor­ cycle and taken towards Ghodbunder road. At that time, she asked him as “rw eq>dks fd/kj ysds tk jgk gS \” He replied as, “eS rqedks fojkjds ftonkuh eanhj ysds tk jgk gw-” She requested him not to go to Jeevdani, but he had not heard her. At about 5.00 p.m., they both reached there. She was asked to wait in front of temple. After about 15 to 20 minutes, accused came there and she was taken to one house near the temple. He had disclosed his intention that they would reside therein for some days and they would marry. Meanwhile, he had received phone­call from his mother. She had informed him that her family members had lodged the report. During that night, he had established his sexual relations with her twice. On next day, they returned back to the house of accused. His mother and sister had taken her to Kapurbawdi police station. Police rushed to the spot and recorded spot panchanama Exh.9 and seized clothes of victim and accused (Exh.10 and 11). Victim was referred for her medical examination. Doctor had examined her and issued medical certificate (Exh.12). Accused was also referred for his medical examination (Exh.13). School­leaving certificate of victim is obtained (Exh.15). Seized property is sent to C.A. 3 POCSO Case No. 272/2016. (Exh.16). After investigation, charge­sheet was submitted in the special court. 3] Heard both sides. I framed the charge against the accused for the offences punishable under section 376 of I.P.C. and u/s. 3 / 4 and 7 / 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012, on 08.09.2017. Details of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular, to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. His defence is of total denial. 4] During trial, defence has admitted spot panchanama (Exh.9), seizure panchanama of clothes of victim (Exh.10), seizure panchanama of clothes of accused (Exh.11), Forensic Medical Examination Report of victim (Exh.12), and M.L.C. of General Hospital, Thane, of accused (Exh.13). 5] To bring home the guilt of the accused for the charges leveled against him, the prosecution has examined as many as three witnesses i.e. P.W. Name of witness Exh. Description No. No. 1] Rajendraprasad 6 Complainant. Murlidhar Mishra 2] Victim girl. 8 Victim girl. 3] Pravin Pandurang 14 Investigating officer. Bangosavi 6] Accused did not enter into witness box. He had not examined defence witness. 7] Heard learned Special P.P. Smt. Phad for the State. 4 POCSO Case No. 272/2016. 8] Heard learned counsel Shri. Tushar Raut, for the accused. He has placed his reliance on the following authorities­ 1] Ashok Bhaurao Gaikwad Vs. State of Maharashtra, 2009 ALL MR (Cri.) 131, in which His Lordship has observed that­ Ss. 366, 376 of I.P.C.­ Offences under­ Conviction­ Age of prosecutrix on the verge of majority. She was well acquainted with accused. She voluntarily accompanied him to Mumbai without raising any alarm. She did not attempt to flee from the company of accused. Medical evidence not positive to show that she was below 16 years. No evidence that she was induced or forced to accompany appellant to Mumbai. Alleged sexual intercourse was voluntary and medical evidence did not locate any injury on her private parts. Her mother was aware about intimacy between her daughter and appellant and on her disappearance no hectic search was made. Conviction set aside. 2] Sandeep Janaji Konde Vs. State of Maharashtra, 2016 ALL MR (Cri.) 1433, in which His Lordship has observed that­ Section 35 of the Evidence Act­ Admissibility of document­Entry relating to date of birth made in a school register­ Would be relevant and admissible u/s. 35. But such entry has no evidentiary value in absence of material on which age was recorded. Section 376 of I.P.C.­ Rape­ Age of prosecutrix­ Prosecution case that accused repeatedly committed forcible sexual intercourse with minor daughter of informant aged 16 years. No material showing that school leaving certificate of victim contains an accurate record of entries in General Register maintained by school in which she was studying. Neither father nor mother giving date of birth of victim. Evidence of age of victim was not satisfactory. It cannot be said that victim was below 16 years of age. It appears that she was consenting party to act of sexual intercourse between her and accused. Accused entitled to be given 5 POCSO Case No. 272/2016. benefit of doubt and acquitted. 9] Following points arise for my determination, which are being answered for the reasons given herein­below. POINTS FINDINGS 1] Whether prosecution proved that on No. 22.07.2016 at about 02.00 hours, at Nalpada and Jeevdani, Virar, in one house, accused had committed rape i.e. penetrative sexual assault on the minor daughter of complainant i.e. victim aged 16 years ? 2] Whether prosecution proved that on the No. above date, time and place, accused had kidnapped the minor daughter of complainant i.e. victim girl aged 16 years, without the consent of complainant, from the lawful guardianship of her parents ? 3] Whether prosecution proved that on the No. above date, time and place, accused had kidnapped the minor daughter of complainant i.e. victim girl aged 16 years and enticed her of performing marriage with her for pornographic purposes and kept illegal sexual relations with her, thereby, committed the offence of sexual harassment ? 4] What order ? As per final order. REASONS POINT NOS. 1 TO 3 10] P.W.1 Rajendraprasad Mishra deposed in his evidence that 6 POCSO Case No. 272/2016. victim in the year 2016 was aged about 16 years. She had left in 8 th standard. He had not stated the date of birth of victim. P.W.2 victim girl deposed in her evidence that she was born on 19.04.2000. She was studying in Sarvodaya Hindi High­School. She was residing along with her sister Manisha since before two months of the incident. She was working in school­bus as a conductor. P.W.3, investigating officer Shri. Bangosavi deposed in his evidence that he had collected school­leaving certificate of the victim (Exh.15). It goes to show that victim was born on 19.04.2000 in Jaunpur, U.P. No head­master is examined by the prosecution. Birth certificate of victim issued by Government authority is not placed on record. P.W.1 Rajendraprasad has not stated the date of birth of victim. However, considering the date of incident as 22.07.2016 and date of birth as 16.04.2000 as per school­leaving certificate of the victim, it can be inferred that on the date of incident, victim was 16 years, 3 months and 6 days old. 11] P.W.1 Rajendraprasad Mishra is not eye­witness to the incident. On 23.07.16, he came to know from one Raja on phone that his daughter / victim was in his house at Azadnagar. Accordingly, she was brought to police station. According to him, he was told by victim that she was kidnapped by one Shaikh at Jeevdani. From his cross­examination, it can be gathered that victim was mentally sound. He had not searched for her at her place of birth. 12] P.W.2 is a victim. According to her, on 22.07.16 at about 2.00 p.m., she returned back to her home from the school. She herself called accused to Tulshidham. She also went to Tulshidham. Accused came there on his mobile. There was quarrel with her sister. She asked him that she wanted to go to Jeevdani temple. Accordingly, they proceeded towards 7 POCSO Case No. 272/2016. Jeevdani temple, but on the way, his motor­cycle became out of order. Then, by leaving motor­cycle thereat, they both went to temple on foot. She had not supported to the prosecution story at all. She further deposed in her evidence that her statement was recorded by J.M.F.C. as per her say. She deposed in her cross­examination that as per say of police, she had stated before the Judicial Magistrate First Class in her statement u/s. 164 of Cr.P.C. 13] Victim was referred for her medical examination (Exh.12). It is admitted by defence. It can be seen from the said medical certificate that no fresh injuries were found on the person of victim. However, there was history of sexual intercourse by known person. Accused known to victim since prior to 2­3 years. Last intercourse was taken place on 22.07.16. No condom was used. No bath was taken. 14] C.A. reports are placed on record vide Exh. 20 and 21. No semen was detected on pubic hair, vulval swab, vaginal swab and cervical swab of victim. So also, neither blood nor tissue matters were detected in her nail clippings. However, her blood was found of blood group 'B'. 15] As per C.A. report Exh. 21, neither blood nor any tissue matter is detected in nail clipping of accused. Neither semen nor vaginal fluid is detected in pubic hair of accused. Blood group of accused was found to be blood group 'B'. 16] As on the date of incident, victim was found aged about 16 years, 3 months and 6 days, she had attended the age of understanding and she was knowing the consequences of her own act. As per evidence of victim, she herself had called the accused and she had joined his company. She had not raised any hue or cry. She had also not objected for sexual 8 POCSO Case No. 272/2016. intercourse. Victim had not supported to the prosecution story at all. Therefore, it cannot be said that the prosecution proved the offence against the accused. On the contrary, it can safely be held that prosecution miserably failed to prove the alleged offence against the accused beyond all reasonable doubts. Therefore, I have no option than to record my findings on all the points, accordingly. In the result, I proceed to pass the following order. ORDER 1] Accused Mehboob Badshah Shaikh, is hereby, acquitted under sec. 235(1) of the Criminal Procedure Code, of the offences punishable u/s. 376 of I.P.C. and u/s. 3 / 4 and 7 / 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] Accused Mehboob Badshah Shaikh, be enlarged on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ with surety of like amount. The effect of this bail order will remain in force for the period of six months from today, as per section 437­(A) of Cr.P.C. 3] Muddemal being worthless, be destroyed after appeal period is over. Thane, (A.S. Bhaisare) Date­ 22.03.2018. Special Judge (POCSO), Thane.

.. 1 .. bail 2651/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 2651/2014 This application is filed by applicant Sakib Abdul Samal Nachinkar for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with C.R.No.I­958/2014 registered at Mumbra police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 363, 376 of I.P.C. and section 4 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as ''P.O.C.S.O. Act''). It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant kidnapped the victim from lawful guardianship of her parents and then committed rape on her. It is further contended and argued that no such incident has happened and the applicant is not the father of the child begotten to the victim girl. It is further contended and argued that the applicant is falsely implicated in this crime. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co­operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that the accused kidnapped the minor girl by misrepresenting her from lawful guardianship of he parents and then he committed rape on her due to which she became pregnant. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl and the prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that the applicant is .. 2 .. bail 2651/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) original resident of Gujarat State and therefore if he is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 363, 376 of I.P.C. and section 4 of P.O.C.S.O. Act and as rightly pointed out on behalf of applicant/accused, the alleged incident of kidnapping and rape is stated to have been committed by the accused in June, 2014 but when the victim girl alleged to have been taken to hospital in November, 2014 she was diagnosed of carrying for six months. Even it is clear that for the period of six months the girl do not appear to have stated about the alleged incident of rape by the accused. In the light of that the contentions on behalf of the applicant/accused that he has no concern or connection with the girl and he has not committed any offence and he is falsely implicated in this crime has to be taken into consideration 4] It has also to be mentioned that the aspect which is material in the present case is that the applicant/accused himself has filed one application in this Court for directing the investigating officer to conduct DNA test of the child delivered by the complainant. Even it is clear from the documents produced on record, earlier also in December, 2014 the brother of the accused appear to have addressed one application to the Commissioner of Police with same prayer that DNA test of the foetus carried by the victim be conducted and in spite of that, so far, no DNA test is stated to have been conducted and no report is produced on record. .. 3 .. bail 2651/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) 5] In the light of that it has to be mentioned that the aspect as to whether the allegations of kidnapping and rape against the accused are true and or the defence put forth by the accused that he is falsely implicated in this case, would be the question which will have to be decided on merits after trial. Even nothing is stated to be recovered from the accused. 6] No doubt, it is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and only prima facie material showing implication of the accused is to be seen and that the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. 7] In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 8] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 9] Then, it has also to be mentioned that the investigation in the matter though almost completed the charge sheet is yet to be .. 4 .. bail 2651/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 10] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Sakib Abdul Samal Nachinkar is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ The applicant/accused shall attend the concerned police station on every Saturday between 10.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon till filing of the charge sheet and shall co­operate in investigation. He shall not not contact the victim in any manner and shall not threaten and pressurize the victim and other prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this Court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 17.03.2015 (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.

Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­0007427­2016 Special (POCSO) Case No.277/16 Received on : 07.11.2016 Registered on : 07.11.2016 Decided on : 20.10.2018 Duration : 1Y. 11Ms.13Ds. IN THE COURT OF D.J.­1 & ADDL. SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE (Presided over by Hemant M. Patwardhan) Special (POCSO) Case No.277/16 Exh.No. 1.State of Maharashtra. ( Shantinagar Police station) ..Complainant V/s. 1. Abdul Kudyus Suphi Abdulla Ansari. Age : 25 years, Occ. Electrician. R/at. House No. 936, Near Taiba Masjid, Shantinagar, Bhiwandi, Thane. 2. Abdul Ajij Suphi Abdulla Ansari. Age : 31 years, Occ. Electrician. R/at. As above. 3. Mohd. Isak Suphi Abdulla Ansari. Age : 20 years, Occ. Education. R/at. As above. 4. Mohd. Suphi Abdulla Shabuddin Ansari (Dead). ..Accused Appearance:­ APP Shri. Londhe for the State. Advocate Shri. Dhananjay Patil for the accused. 1 to 11 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­0007427­2016 Special (POCSO) Case No.277/16 JUDGMENT (Delivered on this 20th day of October 2018 ) Accused were facing trial under sections 354­A(1) (i), 323, 504, 506, 34 of IPC read with section 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 on following facts:­ 1] That on 03.08.2015 at about 3.00 p.m. in front of House No. 695/1, Taibanagar, in front of Taiba Masjid, Shantinagar, Bhiwandi within jurisdiction of Shantinagar Police station, Bhiwandi, accused in furtherance of their common intention voluntarily caused hurt to victim and at the same time has abused informant, her family members thereby gave provocation to them, knowing that there is every likelihood of their committing breach of peace and has committed criminal intimidation by threatening the informant with injury on their person with intent to cause alarm to them. According to prosecution accused no.1 while committing aforesaid acts, in furtherance of their common intention has committed act of sexual harassment by physical contact and advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures and as the victim was minor, his said physical contact were considered with sexual intends. Thus, on the complaint of mother of the victim an offence punishable under aforesaid sections came to be registered against accused. On completion of investigation they were charge­sheeted. 2 to 11 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­0007427­2016 Special (POCSO) Case No.277/16 2] My learned Predecessor was pleased to frame charge below Exh.5. Needless to mention that before framing charge itself, accused no.4 Mohammad Suphi was reported dead. Therefore, his name though was included in the charge my learned Predecessor has already marked it that he is dead. Thus, case was only proceeded against accused no.1 to 3. My learned Predecessor has then certified that contents of said charge were read over and explained to accused in vernacular. Accused pleaded not guilty and claim to be tried. Their defence was of total denial and that there was previous dispute between the family of the accused and family of the victim about house property and on that dispute present complaint has been filed just to harass them. 3] Prosecution was then proceeded to examine informant, victim and I.O. as witness no.1 to 3 respectively. Then statement of accused no.1 to 3 were recorded as per their say wherein they have again reiterated fact of their false implication in the matter. Arguments of rival advocates were heard. According to learned P.P. all prosecution witnesses have supported it and has substantiated allegation against accused. According to learned P.P. there was nothing on record to disbelieve the allegation of informant and victim and only because of the enmity between the parties, victim would have implicated accused in such offence at the cost of her reputation. 3 to 11 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­0007427­2016 Special (POCSO) Case No.277/16 Hence, learned P.P. has requested to upheld said testimony of informant and victim and requested to convict the accused as per provisions of law. 4] Per contra, defence advocate has categorically pointed out that an hour just prior to alleged incident, there was a quarrel between family of the victim and the accused persons and both the families were at police station to lodge N.C.'s against each other around 4.00 p.m. onwards wherein on the basis of said N.C.'s the husband and son of the informant was detained by concerned police and in the N.C. lodged by husband of the informant there was no allegation of any such incident allegedly occurred at 3.00 p.m. According to him, if such incident would have been occurred, informant husband would have immediately referred it either separately or in the said N.C. itself and police would have taken immediate cognizance of it considering seriousness of allegation. However, failure of making any such reference by the informant and her husband in itself is sufficient to discard the allegation. He has then pointed out that enmity between the parties is admitted on record and that was the only reason to implicate the accused in the matter. He has pointed out that there is delay of about 21 days which is unexplained therefore, in itself is fatal to the prosecution. He has therefore, requested the court to discard the allegation and acquit the accused. 4 to 11 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­0007427­2016 Special (POCSO) Case No.277/16 5] After having heard rival advocates, following points arose for my consideration and I record my findings against each of them for the reasons noted below :­ Sr.N. Points Findings 1] Does the prosecution prove that on 03.08.2015 at about 3.00 ..Negative. p.m. in front of House No. 695/1, Taibanagar, in front of Taiba Masjid, Shantinagar, Bhiwandi within the jurisdiction of Shantinagar Police station, Bhiwandi in furtherance of their common intention accused no.1 Abdul Kudyus has sexually harassed informant's daughter i.e. minor victim age 14 years by physical contact and advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 354­A(1)(i) read with 34 of Indian Penal Code? 2] Does the prosecution prove that accused on aforesaid date, ..Negative. time and place, in furtherance of their common intention, voluntarily caused hurt to informant's daughter i.e. minor victim girl and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 323 read with 34 of Indian Penal Code? 3] Does the prosecution prove that accused on aforesaid date, ..Negative. time and place, in furtherance of their common intention, intentionally insulted the informant Sayara A. Ansari and her family members by abusing them and thereby gave provocation to them knowing that it will break public peace and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 504 read with 34 of Indian Penal Code? 4] Does the prosecution prove that accused on aforesaid date, ..Negative. time and place, in furtherance of their common intention, committed criminal intimidation by threatening the informant Sayara A. Ansari and her family members with injury to their person with intent to cause alarm to them or to cause them to do an act which they are legally bound to do and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 506 read with 34 of Indian Penal Code? 5] Does the prosecution prove that accused no.1 on aforesaid date, ..Negative time and place, committed sexual assault on minor victim girl age 14 years of the informant by moving your hand on her chest and torn her clothes with sexual intent involving physical contact without penetration and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012? 6] What order? Accused are acquitted as per final order. 5 to 11 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­0007427­2016 Special (POCSO) Case No.277/16 REASONS As to point no.1 to 6 :­ 6] All these points are interlinked with each other and therefore, are considered at once. In the present matter prosecution has alleged that initially accused persons in furtherance of their common intention has committed offence of assault on the victim, gave provocation to informant and also committed offence of criminal intimidation and while other accused were committing said offence accused no.1 Abdul Kudyus has committed sexual overture and committed sexual assault with sexual intent on the victim. Therefore, prosecution has required to establish it by consistent and reliable evidence. In order to bring guilt of the accused at home, prosecution has examined informant and victim as witness no.1and 2 respectively. Though said witnesses have deposed in terms of prosecution and on the basis of their deposition, prosecutor has requested this court to convict the accused persons, defence has pointed out various contradictions and admissions of the said witnesses to request the court to discard their depositions. Hence, said depositions are scrutinize on the background of defence advanced by the accused. 7] Informant has claim that on 03.08.2015 at about 3.00 p.m. while she along with her husband and son were 6 to 11 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­0007427­2016 Special (POCSO) Case No.277/16 present in the house they heard shouts of her daughter i.e. victim and when they came out of the house had seen victim weeping. Therefore, they made inquiry as to why she was weeping wherein she told the informant that accused Abdul Kudyus moved his hand on her back and breast and also torn her clothes. Thereafter, she somehow escaped from the clutches of the accused. According to informant accused Kudyus has threatened her to kill. Therefore, she did not visit police station for about 21 days. On perusal of the deposition of the victim, it is apparent that she has claimed to have seen accused no.1 to 4 while she was on her way to tuition class and initially accused no.1 Kudyus had slapped on her back and when shouted loudly and started weeping her parents came and in presence of parents accused Kudyus has moved his hand over her chest and torn her clothes. Even if we consider the depositions of both the witnesses as it is then also mere allegation of other accused being present on the spot there is absolutely no allegations made against them under any of the sections with which accused were charged. Therefore, even without considering the defence on the basis of substantive evidence of witness no.1 and 2 allegations against remaining accused i.e. accused no.2 and 3 cannot be said to be established by the evidence of the witnesses. Thus, this court need not even consider the defence of the accused as above and straightway record finding so far as those accused ae concerned in negative. 7 to 11 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­0007427­2016 Special (POCSO) Case No.277/16 8] Now turning towards the defence of accused no.1 is concerned. Admittedly, all allegations are made against accused no.1 alone. However, he has raised categorical defence of his false implication on the basis of old dispute between the parties. Needless to mention that witness no.1 and 2 have categorically admitted about old dispute pending between them about house property. Thus, if that particular defence is consider, it is certainly sufficient to say that implication cannot be ruled out in view of said old enmity. 9] In the instant case even if we consider the depositions of both witnesses there are material contradictions about the allegations made against accused Kudyus. The informant has claim that she has heard about entire incident from the victim after entire incident had occurred. However, according to victim only incident of slap on her back had occurred while she was alone wherein further incident of accused Kudyus moving his hand on the breast and of torning her clothes etc. has occurred in presence of informant and other family members when they appeared on the spot. Thus, such material contradictory statements are itself sufficient to say that depositions of informant and victim are not consistent in nature. 10] Except allegation that accused Kudyus had 8 to 11 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­0007427­2016 Special (POCSO) Case No.277/16 threatened them with dire consequences after the incident and therefore, only complaint was not lodged for 21 days there is absolutely no other explanation of informant as to why complaint was lodged after about 21 days of occurrence of the incident. However, if we consider admission of the informant that she had been to police station around 4 to 4.30 p.m. on the day of said incident as her son and husband were detained by police and was there in the police station for sufficient time, then there was no reason for her not to immediately disclose about the incident in question to concern police. Even the N.C. lodged by her husband which was registered after 4 o'clock, as per admitted position there is absolutely no reference of occurrence of any such incident around 3 O'clock. If incident would have really occurred then husband would have certainly made reference of said act of the accused which was of serious nature than that of allegation of scuffle. Therefore, when though the informant and her husband were in police station did not make any reference of the incident either orally or in writing then it is difficult to accept that incident had really occurred. If they were really under the fear of accused Kudyus then they would not have dared to file even N.C. about the incident occurred at about 2.00 p.m. on the particular date. Thus, it is apparent that just to put forth the explanation said 9 to 11 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­0007427­2016 Special (POCSO) Case No.277/16 reason of she being under the fear of accused Kudyus appears to have been put forth. Thus, as her conduct is against natural conduct of human being it is difficult to accept her said explanation. If that explanation is discarded there is nothing on record to condone said unexplained delay of 21 days about lodging of the complaint and thus delay is apparently fatal to the prosecution. 11] In the instant case though investigation was carried out by lady officer she did not even care to seize the alleged torn clothes of the victim to atleast substantiate the allegations of the said incident. Failure of said I.O. to seized said clothes and further failure of the victim or informant to produce those clothes before the police in itself are sufficient lacuna which again constrained the court to disbelieve the allegations of informant­victim. Further, though there are allegations of having committed offence under sections 504, 506, 323 of IPC in view of said material placed on record even said material against accused no.1 is not sufficient to prove any of the ingredients under sections 504 and 506 of IPC. In view of the aforesaid findings and reasons recorded above, it is difficult to even accept any of the allegations under remaining section either of IPC or POCSO. Having regards to these facts it is apparent on record that defence of the accused persons is apparently more probable than that of allegations of informant 10 to 11 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­0007427­2016 Special (POCSO) Case No.277/16 and victim. A per the settled propositions of law when defence is more probable, the court has to discard prosecution's case in toto. Accordingly, I record my findings against point no.1 to 5 in negative even so far as accused no. 1 is concerned and proceed to pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused are acquitted from the offence punishable under sections 354­A(1)(i), 323, 504, 506, 34 of IPC read with section 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. 2] Bail bonds of accused accordingly stands cancelled. 3] Accused ar directed to execute P.R. and S.B. of Rs.10,000/­ each as per amended provisions of section 437(A) of Cr.P.C. and bonds so executed shall remain in force for the period of six months from the date of its execution. 4] Proceeding is accordingly closed. Thane (Hemant M.Patwardhan) Date: 20.10.2018 D.J.­1 & Additional Sessions Judge, Thane 11 to 11
