Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­007439­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 278/14 Received on : 24.12.2014 Registered on : 24.12.2014 Decided on : 01.10.2018 Duration : 3Ys. 9Ms. 7 Ds. IN THE COURT OF D.J.­1 & ADDL. SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE. (Presided over by Hemant M. Patwardhan) Special Case (POCSO) No. 278/14 Exh.No. State of Maharashtra, (Wagle Estate Police station) ..Complainant V/s. Ajit Eknath Khade. Age 29 years, R/of. Banjarvasti, Sevalalnagar, Near Mental Hospital, Wagle Estate, Thane ..Accused Appearance:­ APP Mr. Londhe for the State. Advocate Mr. Arun Singh for accused JUDGMENT (Delivered on this 1st day of October 2018) Accused Ajit Eknath Khade was facing trial under sections 342, 376(I), 366A of Indian Penal Code and under section Sec. 4, 6, 1 OF 7 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­007439­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 278/14 8, 10 and 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 on following facts. 1] That on 27.09.2014 in between 13.00 to 14.25 hrs. and since prior to two months of the said date, in residential house of accused at Banjarvasti, Sevalalnagar, Near Mental Hospital, Wagle Estate, Thane accused has wrongfully confined minor victim girl and her brother after kidnapping them from the custody of their guardian or natural parents for seduction to illicit intercourse and after having committed the said offences during aforesaid time and place accused has committed rape. According to allegations as the victim was minor at the relevant time said act of the accused was also covered within purview of sexual assault, sexual harassment and sexual penetrative assault on minor victim. Hence, on complaint lodged, an offence punishable under aforesaid sections came to be registered. On completion of investigation he was charge­sheeted. 2] My learned Predecessor has framed charge below Exh.14 and has certified that the contents of said charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. Accused pleaded not guilty and claim to be tried. His defence was of total denial. 3] On the basis of aforesaid facts, prosecution has then proceeded to examine panch witness on spot and seizure as PW1 and medical officer as PW2. Then though prosecution has made several 2 OF 7 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­007439­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 278/14 attempts to procure presence of victim and or complainant i.e. mother of the victim, prosecution could not secure their presence as they have left premises in which they were residing at the relevant time of incident. Thus, the court has also made an attempt to procure presence of those material witnesses by summoning the I.O. in the matter. Though once I.O. has appeared before the court said officer also was not able to procure presence of material witnesses. Hence, considering the fact that accused is in jail since the date of his arrest, court was constrained to proceed on next stage of case. Statement of accused was recorded as per his say wherein he has flatly refused to have committed offence and claim to be innocence having falsely implicated in the matter. Arguments of rival advocates were heard. They have submitted in terms of their respective avernments and contentions. 4] On the basis of aforesaid rival arguments, following points arise for my consideration and I record my findings against each of them for the reasons noted below:­ S.N. Points Findings 1] Does the prosecution prove that accused on 27.09.2014 in between ..In the negative. 13.00 to 14.25 hrs. and since prior to two months of the said date, in residential house of accused at Banjarvasti, Sevalalnagar, Near Mental Hospital, Wagle Estate, Thane wrongfully confined the minor victim­girl and her brother children of informant Sunita Yadav and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 342 of IPC? 2] Does the prosecution prove that accused on the given date, time and ..In the negative. place committed rape on minor victim­girl aged below 7 years and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 376(I) of IPC? 3 OF 7 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­007439­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 278/14 3] Does the prosecution prove that accused on the given date, time and ..In the negative. place procured minor girl aged below 18 years, by inducing her by any means to go from any place or to do any act with intent that said girl may be, or knowing that it is likely she will be forced or seduced to illicit intercourse with another person and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 366A of IPC? 4] Does the prosecution prove that accused on the given day, date, time ..In the negative. and place committed sexual penetrative assault on the minor victim­ girl and thereby committed an offence of aggravated penetrative sexual assault punishable under sections 4, 6, 8 and 10 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act? 5] Does the prosecution prove that accused on the given day, date, time ..In the negative. and place committed sexual harassment upon a child i.e. minor victim­girl by committing rape on her and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 12 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act? 6] What order ? Accused is acquitted as per final order. REASONS As to point nos. 1 to 6 :­ 5] In the instant case prosecution has made very serious allegations against accused of initially having kidnapped the victim from the custody of the natural guardian and after committing such kidnapping has confined the victim and her brother in his house and while they were confined has committed rape and penetrative sexual assault on the victim who was minor at the relevant time. Hence, prosecution was required to establish all said allegations by cogent and reliable evidence. However, except panch witness and medical officer prosecution could not procure the presence of any of the witness to record their substantive evidence. Hence, after having provided prosecution sufficient opportunities for procuring the 4 OF 7 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­007439­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 278/14 presence of the said material witnesses, the court was constrained to proceed on the next stage of hearing and was constrained to record statement of accused considering his detention in custody since the date of arrest. 6] Allegations of having committed rape and penetrative sexual assault has been made against accused in such matter opinion of medical officer plays an important role. No doubt opinion of medical officer is not binding on the court but same has to be consider as corroborative evidence for proving the allegations of such heinous offences. In the instant case if we perused the complaint of mother of the victim then it is apparent that allegation of having committed rape on the minor daughter of the complainant has been made. If either rape or penetrative sexual assault is committed then internal injuries are bound to occur though there are fewer chances of occurrence of external injuries in view of physical ability of the major person in comparison to minor victim. However, on perusal of the medical evidence in this matter it is apparent that medical officer has neither found any external injuries nor any internal injuries to the victim when he has examined the victim on the ground as a victim of such heinous offence. She has categorically made reference in his statement that hymen was also found to be intact during her examination. If the accused would have really inserted his penis then atleast there was every possibility of hymen being torn at the relevant time. In absence it is difficult to accept that there was either 5 OF 7 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­007439­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 278/14 insertion of penis as alleged or any penetrative sexual assault on the victim at the relevant time. Medical evidence is totally against case of the prosecution. Therefore, in absence of any other evidence court has to accept his defence being substantiated by medical evidence. Hence, if the said defence is accepted then court has to record the findings that evidence is inconsistent and is certainly not sufficient to prove the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt. Having said so, I therefore, do not hesitate to record my findings against point no.1 to 5 in the negative and proceed to pass following order. ORDER 1. Accused Ajit Eknath Khade is acquitted from the offence punishable under sections 342, 376(1), 366A of Indian Penal Code and under section Sec. 4, 6, 8, 10 and 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 2. He is in jail since the date of his arrest. He be set at liberty forthwith if not required in any other case. 3. Inform jailer accordingly. 4. Muddemal property i.e. clothes and carpet being worthless, be destroyed after appeal period. 6 OF 7 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­007439­2014 Special Case (POCSO) No. 278/14 5. Accused is directed to execute P.R. and S.B. of Rs.10,000/­ with a solvent surety in like amount under amended provisions of Section 437­A of Code of Criminal Procedure and the bond so executed shall remain in force for period of six months from the date of its execution. 6. Proceeding accordingly shall stand closed. Thane (Hemant M.Patwardhan) Date: 01.10.2018 D.J.­1 & Additional Sessions Judge, Thane. 7 OF 7

Sr.No. Points Findings 1] Whether prosecution proved that on In negative 04/03/2013 at 8.00 p.m. near the public toilet at Juinagar, accused insulted modesty of complainant by showing obscene video in his mobile intending that the same shall be seen by her and committed sexual harassment on her? 2] Whether prosecution proved that by In negative showing the obscene video to the minor victim­girl, the accused committed offence u/s. 67 of I.T. R E A SO N S As to Point Nos. 1 to 3 :­ 6] P.W.1­victim deposed that she was residing at her aunt Sunita Phale at Juinagar. Her date of birth is 26/03/1999. The accused is her cousin brother residing near her house. On the day of incident in the year 2013 she was at home. Accused came there and slapped on her thigh. Victim stated her that accused used to show obscene picture to her on mobile, and therefore, they went to Nerul police station and victim lodged complaint. The witness stated that she had not seen exactly what was in mobile. Police seized mobile of accused. 8] From accused side in cross­examination of complainant it was asked whether incident of beating and showing obscene picture was happened before one month of lodging complaint and witness answered in negative. She denied that no obscene photo was shown to her by the accused. She stated that presently she has no complaint against accused. She admitted that the accused being cousin brother used to come to her and she admitted that he being cousin brother used to tease her. Brother and sister used to beat each other in fun. 9] What appears from the evidence on record is that complainant stated about happening of incident with her one month prior to lodging of complaint when obscene photo was shown to her and when she refused to watch it accused slapped her. Another incident was happened on 04/03/2013 but that time again he shown the obscene film near the public toilet. However, in evidence, she stated that before two days of complaint she was called by accused near toilet and no film was shown at that time but one day before it, half naked picture was shown to her. So it appears that complainant is disclosing about different incidents as compared to complaint and she is not firm about dates. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 376 of I.P.C. and section 3, 4, 5(J)(2)(3)(L) Q and 6 of P.O.C.S.O. Act, from the allegations in the F.I.R. the applicant do not appear to be the main accused against whom the allegations of rape are there and as per F.I.R. the allegations of rape are against co­accused Vicky Bhoir and it is contended that the girl was having love affair with Vicky Bhoir and the allegations of molestation and rape are against him and only allegation made against the present applicant that the applicant frequently took Vicky Bhoir and the victim girl near river bank near the bushes in his rickshaw and there Vicky Bhoir committed forcible sexual intercourse with the victim girl. In such circumstance whether the allegations against the accused are true or not, would be the question to be decided on merits. Even nothing is stated to be recovered from the applicant/accused. 4] Then, it is well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be gone into detail and only prima facie material showing involvement of the accused is to be seen and the main criteria to be considered is whether the .. 3 .. bail 2669/2014 (Order below Exhibit 1) applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence. 5] In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 6] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 7] Then, it has also to be mentioned that the investigation in the matter though almost completed the charge sheet is yet to be submitted, it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 8] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is allowed. .. 4 .. bail 2669/2014 (Order below Exhibit 1) Applicant/accused Kailas alias Banti Dattu Nahire is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ He shall attend the concerned police station on every Saturday between 3.00 p.m. to 5.00 p.m. till filing of the charge sheet and shall co­operate with the investigation. He shall not threaten and pressurize the prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 22.01.2015. (Ms.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.

.. 1 .. Bail No. 2763/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) Criminal Bail Application No. 2763/2015. Smt. Hamida Mohammad Shaikh .. Applicant versus The State of Maharashtra Through Mumbra Police Station .. Non­applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 1] By this application the applicant is seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C., who was arrested on 18.10.2015 by Mumbra Police Station in connection with C.R.No.I­828/2015 registered for an offence punishable under section 370(2)(3) of I.P.C. and section 4, 8, 17 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Mrs. Reena Korade for the applicant/accused and learned A.P.P. Mr. B.D.Hinge for State. I.O. present. Case diary produced. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 17.10.2015 at the instance of the informant P.S.I. Sharad Panje attached to A.H.T.C. Crime Branch with an indictment that on secret information a trap was laid at the house of accused Hamida Shaikh who alongwith other accused used to procure victims for prostitution and from there two accused were arrested and one minor victim­girl was .. 2 .. Bail No. 2763/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) rescued. Therefore, the report came to be lodged. 4] The learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant­accused is falsely implicated. She submitted that the husband of present applicant­accused lodged report with Mumbra police station against two accused Sharifbhai and Jahidbhai who falsely implicated his wife i.e. present applicant­accused, in this false case. She further submitted that the matter was reported in various newspapers. Her further submission is that applicant­ accused is an innocent lady and permanent resident of Thane and she is having two small children. She is behind bars since one month. She is ready to abide by any conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing him on bail. 5] Per contra, the learned A.P.P. opposed the application on the ground that minor victim­girl aged about 15 years was procured for prostitution. The present applicant­accused accepted money for prostitution and she was caught red­handed when the trap was laid. The investigation is in progress. Prima facie there is strong case against the accused and there is possibility of accused repeating the offence if released on bail and prayed for rejection of application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of investigation papers it appears that trap was laid on receiving secret information that prostitution is carried out at the residential house of the present applicant­accused. When trap was laid at the house of present .. 3 .. Bail No. 2763/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) applicant­accused with the help of decoy customer, the victim­girl was found in the bedroom of present applicant­accused. Further, the amount of Rs.500/­ which was given to the decoy customer for purpose of trap was found with the present applicant­accused which clearly shows that the applicant­accused is having the knowledge and she is actively involved in the business of prostitution. The rescued is a minor girl aged about 15 years. Though the learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant is falsely implicated and the F.I.R. is registered against one Sharifbhai and Jahidbhai with Mumbra police station at the instance of applicant­accused, the fact that the minor victim­girl was rescued from the bedroom of applicant­accused cannot be overlooked. Prima facie the applicant­accused appears to be involved in serious offence. The investigation is still in progress. The apprehension of the learned A.P.P. about tampering of witnesses and fleeing away from justice are well founded. No case is made out against the applicant­accused to release her on bail. They came around 7.00 p.m. The victim girl (P.W.2) was playing with her friends. Victim girl P.W.2 deposed that when she found herself thirsty, she went to the house of grandmother to drink water. She took water. The accused come close to her and took her behind the building and moved hand over her body. Anand Tarte (P.W.1) saw that girl and the accused behind the building No. B­11. They caught the accused. P.W.1 deposed that boy was beaten and taken to the police station. 9] I have heard Ld. A.P.P. and Ld. Advocate for the accused. Ld. Advocate for the accused submitted that girl was not alone. Girl was playing with her friends. So, how accused could come to her and took her. It has come in evidence of victim girl that when she was coming from her grandmother's house, accused dragged her. Similarly, accused 5 Special Case ( POCSO ) No. 281/2016 CNR No.MHTH01­007535­2016 was seen by Anand Tarte (P.W.1) behind the back of building B­11. It is strongly contended that Sushama Bhadange (P.W.3) and her husband have come after the incident occurred. But, the fact remains that the victim girl has herself identified the accused. The girl remembers that it was a day of Ganpati emulsion. The accused also reside in the same locality. So, the plea of accused that they have falsely implicated him is out of question. It has come in evidence of Anand Tarte (P.W.1) and victim girl (P.W.2) that accused immediately dragged the girl and moved hand over her body. It is pertinent to note that the victim girl has not stated that the accused has either pressed, brushed her sensitive parts. So, the offence committed by accused is of using criminal force to outrage modesty of minor girl. In view of this, I hold accused guilty of offence u/sec. 354 of Indian Penal Code and not u/sec. 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act. Here, I take pause to hear the accused on the point of sentence. 10] I have heard accused on the point of sentence. Ld. Advocate Smt. Korde submitted that accused is 22 years old. He is in custody since 12.09.2016. He appeared for 12th, but failed. He was addicted to drug It is submitted that he was idle laying at home. He wants to improve himself. He shall be given lesser punishment. Ld. APP submitted that the offence is very serious and it is committed with the minor girl. It is submitted that no leniency will be shown otherwise wrong message will be sent in the Society. I have assessed all circumstances. Since the accused is below 20 years of age at the time of commission of offence and he was addicted to drug and has some psychological disorder symptoms and repents, so desires to go in society and improve himself. 6 Special Case ( POCSO ) No. 281/2016 CNR No.MHTH01­007535­2016 In view of this, I find it just and proper to release him under Probation of Offenders Act than to sentence him Hence, I answer point No.1 in affirmative and point No.2 in negative. In answer to point No.3 I pass following order : ORDER 1] The accused Rahul Ramesh Patekar is hereby convicted of offence u/s. 354 of Indian Penal Code and instead of sentencing him, he is released on probation of good conduct for five years and accused shall execute good behaviour bond of Rs. 15,000/­. 2] The accused Rahul Ramesh Patekar is hereby acquitted of offence u/s. 7,8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 3] The accused be released forthwith if not required in any other offence. Inform the jail superintendent accordingly. 4] Pronounced and dictated in open court. On 12.09.2016 she was on duty. She examined the victim. There was bruise on outer angle of both eyes and as per say of victim it was caused while playing. There was bite mark on the left cheek. P.W.8 Vasudev Bhimrao More is the API of Nerul, police station. He investigated CR No.I­367/2016. He arrested the accused on 12.09.2016. He prepared seizure panchanama of the clothes of the victim and accused. He deposited the clothes of victim in the police station on 12.09.2016 vide receipt Exh.27 and clothes of the accused deposited vide receipt Exh.31. He obtained the birth certificate of the victim. As per that birth certificate the victim's birth date is 04.08.2010. He sent the victim and accused for medical examination vide his letter Exh.28 and 29. He prepared panchanama of the spot of incident i.e. room of the accused at Exh.30. That panchanama was prepared at about 4.00 a.m. to 5.30 a.m. on 12.09.2016 in the Kamlesh Thakur Chawl, last room that room was shown by the informant. Rajesh, Ramkaran, Jitu and Dharmendra were residing there. That room was 10 X 12 ft. 17. He sent clothes of the victim, clothes of accused, samples of victim and accused to FSL Kalina, Santacruz on 17.09.2016 by his letter Exh.33. There is no admission in his cross­examination. There is no contradiction or omission pointed out in his cross­examination. 18. C.A report of pubic hair , nail clipping, blood sample, semen of accused is marked Exh.7 vide MLC No.B­5750/2016. It is reported that neither blood nor tissue on Exh.2 (nail ), no semen on pubic hair. The blood group is of 'O'. The C.A report of vaginal swab, blood of the victim is at Exh.10 vide MLC NO.B­5749/16. It is reported that the blood is of 'B' group and vaginal swab is referred to DNA. DNA report is not received in the court. 19. Considering the evidence on record prosecution has proved that victim was residing at Sector­20,Nerul, Navi Mumbai accused was also residing in Kamlesh Thakur Chawl in one room, Sector­20, Nerul, Navi Mumbai. On the day of incident there was Ganpati Festival. The victim was playing there. It is proved by the prosecution that accused gave temptation of biscuit to the victim and taken her to his room and done penetrative sexual assault upon her with ejaculation. The victim immediately narrated the incident to her mother, the accused was also searched immediately at night with the help of witnesses. FIR was lodged immediately. The Medical examination was done on the next day morning. The panchanama of the spot was also prepared at early in the morning on 12.09.2016. The clothes of the victim and accused were seized immediately. In the medical examination it is reported that there is evidence of sexual assault or intercourse cannot be ruled out. 20. It is proved by the prosecution that accused was arrested immediately and he was identified by the victim and witnesses at the time of arrest as well as before the court. There is no contradiction or omission in the evidence of any of the witnesses. The evidence of P.W.1,2 4 and 5 are corroborated on the material points and particulars. The history given before the Medical Offier is corroborated the evidence of victim. The clothes of the victim and accused were seized and sealed in presence of panchas and they were sent for chemical examination. The sample of the victim and accused were taken and sent to FSL Kalina. It is proved that victim was 6 years old on the day of incident. 21. All these incriminating circumstances are put to the accused in his statement under section 313 of Cr. P.C. at Exh.35. He admitted in question No.6 that he was caught by Rajesh Kevat and parents of victim and taken him to the police station. In question No.18 he admitted that he was residing in the room of Rajesh Kevat and Ramkaran was also residing in that room. He admitted at question No.21 that Rajesh and Ramakaran after having dinner they had gone to see Ganpati. At that time he came at the room. In question No.27 he admitted that he was taken by Kamlesh and Rajesh to the police station. He also admitted that he was sent for medical examination in question No.51. In last question he stated that there was one major girl residing infront of his room and he was seeing at her. So that girl had threatened to beat him with chapple because of that incident this false case is filed against him. However, the accused has not examined any witness in support of his defence. 22. There are presumptions under section 29 and 30 in the POCSO Act, 2012. It is provided that, “where a person is prosecuted for committing or abetting or attempting to commit any offence under sections 3,5,7 and 9 of this Act, the Special Court shall presume, that such person has committed or abetted or attempted to commit the offence, as the case may be unless the contrary is proved. It is also provided that in any prosecution for any offence under this Act which requires a culpable mental state on the part of the accused, the Special Court shall presume the existence of such mental state but it shall be a defence for the accused to prove the fact that he had no such mental state with respect to the act charged as an offence in that prosecution. 23. In this case prosecution has proved beyond all reasonable doubt all the incriminating circumstances. There is no reason to lodge false complaint against the accused. Therefore burden shifts upon the accused to rebut the presumptions under section 29 and 30. The accused has not rebutted the presumptions. 24. The Ld. Counsel on behalf of the accused argued that there are many people used red shirt, therefore, the evidence of the victim in respect of the uncle had wearing red shirt cannot be believed. In this respect the court is of the view that the victim has not only stated the uncle was wearing red shirt, but also stated the description that he had beard, he was slim, heighted and taken to his room. The victim also shown the room of the accused. It is also proved by the prosecution that in the same room the accused was residing along with Rajesh and Ramkaran. Therefore, the evidence of the victim is trustworthy and reliable. It is further argued by the Ld. Counsel on behalf of the accused that there was CCTV camera in the society, but it is not checked. In this respect the Investigating Officer has examined. He has not stated that there was CCTV Camera in the society where the victim had gone in Ganpati Pendol. Therefore, this submission is not tenable. The Counsel further submitted that, if the victim is of 6 years old, if raped her hymen should have been ruptured, but in this case there was no bleeding, no injury on private part and her hymen was not ruptured. In this respect the court is of the view that to prove offence under section 5(m) and Section 3 of POCSO Act the rupture of hymen is not essential requirement. It is provided under section 3 of the POCSO Act 2012 that penetrative sexual assault means­ A person is said to commit “penetrative sexual assault” if­ (a) he penetrates his penis, to any extent, into the vagina, mouth, urethra or anus of a child or makes the child to do so with him or any other person; or (b) he inserts, to any extent, any object or a part of the body, not being the penis, into the vagina, the urethra or anus of the child or makes the child to do so with him or any other person; or (c) he manipulates any part of the body of the child so as to cause penetration into the vagina, urethra, anus or any part of body of the child or makes the child to do so with him or any other person; or (d) he applies his mouth to the penis, vagina, anus, urethra of the child or makes the child to do so to such person or any other person. Section 5(m) is aggravated penetrative sexual assault it means whoever commits penetrative sexual assault on a child below 12 years or is said to have been committed aggravated penetrative sexual assault. 25. In this case as per the medical examination report hymen of the victim is not ruptured. It is not torn and there was no bleeding. It does not essential to prove the offences under section 3 and section 5(m) of the POCSO Act 2012. Penetration may be to any extent it means even the penetration on the outer part of the vagina is sufficient which should not be required to be ruptured of hymen. It is no where provided under section 3 and section 5(m) of the Act. The evidence of the victim in his case is totally trustworthy, believable. Her mother has also found sticky substance on her thighs, private part and on her pant and victim has narrated the incident in her word to her mother which amongst to penetrative sexual assault upon her. Therefore, the submission of Ld. Counsel is not tenable. 26. The Ld. Counsel submitted that no prompt FIR has given. In this respect, if we perused the FIR it was lodged at 3.03 a.m., in the night. Incident took place in the evening after that victim narrated the incident to her mother and thereafter her parents had searched the accused and he was taken to police station immediately at night. The search of the accused was taken at about 10.00 p.m and thereafter the accused was taken to the police station and then FIR came to be lodged. There is no delay in lodging FIR considering all the aspects of the case. It is further argued on behalf of the accused that the accused had sexually harassed one girl and in that incident there was quarrel between them and therefore, the accused presumed to be of a bad character and falsely implicated. In this respect the court is of the view that there is no evidence and details are brought by the accused to believe upon the defence who was that girl and what was the incident and what was the relation of that girl with the informant and victim is not brought by the accused on record and therefore this submission is also not tenable. 27. It is further submitted on behalf of the accused that other boys were also coming to the room of accused, but their statements are not recorded. However, this submission is not tenable because it is not proved in the evidence that other children would also come to the room of the accused. On the contrary, it is proved that the accused has lifted the victim from the pendol of Ganpati and she was alone taken to the room of the accused and accused closed the door of his room. So there is no access to other children in the room. So this submission is not tenable. 28. Ld.APP Smt. Hiwrale given the written notes of arguments. It is submitted that the prosecution has proved the case beyond doubt. The APP submitted relied upon the decision in case of Nim Tshering Lepcha V/s. State of Sikkim 2017 ALL MR (Cri) Journal 630. It was the case of section 3 and 4 of POCSO Act, 2012. The victim was 7 years old allegedly raped by 60 years old man. Her medical examination was done after 7 days. The doctor found redness in vaginal area, but no injury on genital. It was held that mere absence of spermatozoa in her inner garments and absence of injury cannot negate prosecution case. It was also observed that there was no reason for victim to concoct a lurid incident. Court shall presume that the incident shall occur. There was also delay in lodging the FIR of six days. Held, the delay was not fatal to the prosecution case. 29. Considering the evidence on record and the submissions made by Ld. APP and the observations in above reported case the court is of the view that evidence laid by the prosecution is reliable, acceptable and trustworthy and admissible. There is no reason to disbelieve any of the witness. The prosecution has therefore proved the ingredients of the offences under section 3 and section 5(m) of the POCSO Act, 2012. Therefore, accused is liable to be convicted. Date­15/02/2018. (S.C. Khalipe) Thane. Additional Sessions Judge, Thane. 30. Today the accused is produced before the court from jail authority. His Advocate Smt. Sarita Gaikwad and Ld. APP are present. 31. Heard accused on point of sentence. He has submitted that he did not do anything. His Advocate Smt. Sarita Gaikwad submitted that the accused has not done anything. He is young. It is his first offence, therefore, lenient view may be taken. 32. Ld. A.P.P. Smt.Hiwrale submitted that the offences are proved beyond doubt, therefore, accused may be convicted with maximum punishment. 33. I did not find any mitigating circumstance for taking lenient view in this case. The age of the accused is not a mitigating factor. 34. I found the following aggravated circumstances:­ That the victim is six years old. While she was playing the accused gave temptation of biscuit and taken her to his home and committed the heinous crime. The victim has identified the accused. The victim is six years old. Accused is 20 years old. 35. Considering the nature of offence I am of the view that accused is liable to be punished with maximum sentence and with fine and the fine amount is liable to be paid to the victim's mother as compensation and I found that the fine amount is not an adequate compensation, therefore, the District Legal Services Authority is requested to give adequate compensation to the victim's mother as per rules. I pass following order of sentence which is sufficient for ends of justice. ORDER 1. The accused Dharmendra Harishankar Saket is convicted under section 235(2) of Criminal Procedure Code for the offences under section 3 punishable under section 4 of POCSO Act 2012 and section 5(m) punishable under section 6 of POCSO Act, 2012. 2. The accused is sentenced to suffer imprisonment for period of ten years and to pay fine of Rs.50,000/­ (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) for offence under section 5(m) punishable under section 6 of POCSO Act 2012, in default of payment of fine he shall suffer simple imprisonment for the period of one year. No separate sentence is awarded for the offence under section 3 punishable under section 4 of POCSO Act, 2012. 3 After realization of fine amount it shall be given to the victim's mother as compensation after appeal period is over. 4 The accused is in jail from 12.09.2016 the set off be given from 12.09.2016 till today under the provisions of section 428 of Cr. P.C. 5 The muddemal clothes of victim and accused being worthless be destroyed after appeal period and if the appeal is preferred it shall be destroyed after the decision of the appeal as per the order of Honourable Apex Court. 6 The District Legal Services of Thane is requested to award compensation to victim's mother as per rules within one month from the date of this order. 7 The Judgment is dictated and declared in open court. 8. The copy of Judgment shall be given to the accused free of costs. Thane. (S.C. Khalipe) Date:15.02.2018 Additional Sessions Judge,Thane.

.. 1 .. bail 2698/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) Order below Exh.1 in Criminal Bail Application No. 2698 of 2014 This application is filed by applicant Abdul Mobin Kararhussain Khan for his release on bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with crime no. I­604/2014 registered at Mira Road police station on the basis of the complaint for offence punishable under section 354(d)of I.P.C. and section 7 and 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012. It was contended and argued that the applicant is arrested in connection with this crime on the complaint filed with the allegation that the applicant outraged modesty of the complainant victim girl. It is further contended and argued that no such incident has happened and the applicant is falsely implicated in this crime. It is further submitted that the applicant is permanent resident of the address given and that if the present applicant/accused is released on bail, he will co­operate with the investigation and will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not abscond and therefore the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. 2] The application is objected to on behalf of prosecution by filing reply and it was contended and argued that at the time of incident the accused followed the victim when she was going home after attending tuition class and also asked her as to whether she is annoyed with the accused and thereby he outraged her modesty. It is further submitted that in such circumstance if the applicant/accused is released on bail, there is possibility of the applicant threatening the victim girl and the prosecution witnesses. It is also contended that if the applicant is released on bail he may abscond and will not be available for trial. It was therefore contended that the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail. .. 2 .. bail 2698/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) 3] As is clear, though the offences charged against the applicant/accused is of serious nature under section 354(d) of I.P.C. and section 7 and 8 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and the girl is stated to be 15 years old, it appears that the accused had been arrested 19.12.2014. Then it is contended on behalf of the applicant/accused that he is falsely implicated in the crime. In such circumstance whether the allegations against the accused are true or not, would be the question to be decided on merits. Even nothing is stated to be recovered from the applicant/ accused. 4] Then it is well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence. 5] In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 6] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. .. 3 .. bail 2698/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) 7] Then, it has also to be mentioned that the investigation in the matter though almost completed the charge sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 8] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is allowed. Applicant/accused Abdul Mobin Kararhussain Khan is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ He shall attend the concerned police station on every Saturday between 3.00 p.m. to 5.00 p.m. till filing of the charge sheet and shall co­operate with the investigation. He shall not threaten and pressurize the prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence. He shall not leave India without permission of this court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 08.01.2015. (Mrs.V.V.Virkar) Special Judge (Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act) Thane.

1 Order Exh.1 Anti. Bail Appln. No. 2842/2016 ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN ANTICIPATORY BAIL APPN.NO.2842/2016 Heard Ld. Adv. Mrs. Sandhya Sawant for the applicant. Ld. A.P.P. Mrs. Kamthe for the State. I.O. present. 1] The applicant has approached this court apprehending his arrest by Rabale police station, in Crime No. I­358/2016 for offence U/s. 354(B) of the I.P.C. and Sec. 8 of the POCSO Act, 2012. 2] It is the prosecution case that on 16/10/2016 at about 10.30 a.m while the complainant and her daughter were passing through Airoli Sector­ 06, Jain Mandir and going towards Bhimnagar, accused/applicant met them and threatened the complainant that “Tune Jo mere Khilaf Gunha Dakhal kiya Hai vo vapis le nahi to tujhe jaanse maar dunga” and also pushed her. The applicant fondled the breast of the complainant's minor daughter (aged 11 years) and told her that “Tum Bahut Kamjor Ho” and thus, molested her. 3] Ld. Adv. Mrs. Sawant has submitted that the applicant has been falsely implicated in this case. There was a dispute between the parties and civil suit is pending between them. The applicant did nothing with the complainant. 4] Per contra, Ld. A.P.P. Mrs. Kamthe has vehemently opposed the bail application on the ground that the applicant has committed the offence with a minor girl, who is only 11 years old, on a public road and also threatened and pushed the complainant. The investigation is still in 2 Order Exh.1 Anti. Bail Appln. No. 2842/2016 progress. Custodial interrogation is required to ascertain the correct facts from the accused. The age of the victim is only 11 years. Ld. A.P.P. and I.O. have submitted that custodial interrogation may be required for at­least a day or two to interrogate the accused. Initially, when the A.B.A. was filed, the offence was not registered. The applicant was only apprehending that an offence U/s. 354 of IPC may be registered against him. However, it is pertinent to note that if the applicant had not committed the offence of outraging modesty, how would he have anticipated that an offence U/s. 354 IPC (and no other offence) would be registered against him ! Therefore, there is no substance in the submission of the Ld. Advocate for the applicant that no such offence was committed by him. The applicant may even get emboldened to commit such offences further. 6] The age of the victim is only 11 years. Custodial interrogation is required for at­least a day or two to interrogate the accused. An accused armed with an order of Anticipatory bail is differently placed from an accused who is interrogated otherwise. In view thereof, I am inclined to reject the bail application. ORDER Anticipatory Bail Application (Exh.1) is hereby rejected. Thane. ( Mridula V.K.Bhatia ) Dt:­16/11/2016. Dist. Judge – 08 and Special Judge (POCSO A), Thane.

Even nothing is to be recovered from the applicant/accused. 4] Then, it is also well settled that at this stage of deciding bail application the evidence on record need not be scrutinized in detail and the main criteria to be considered is whether the .. 3 .. bail 2706/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) applicant would be available for trial and whether there is any possibility of the applicant tampering with prosecution evidence if he is released on bail. 5] In that respect it is contended by the applicant that he is permanent resident of the address given and he will not abscond if released on bail and that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed. 6] Then, though it is submitted on behalf of the prosecution that the offence is of serious nature and the possibility of the applicant/accused being absconded or tampering with prosecution evidence is there, that aspect can be taken care of by saddling certain conditions and on that ground the application cannot be rejected. 7] Then, it has also to be mentioned that the investigation in the matter though almost completed the charge sheet is yet to be submitted and it would take time to complete the investigation and submit the charge sheet and then to conclude the trial in the matter and looking to the fact that the matter is comparatively new one, it would take longer time to dispose of the matter and there is no point in keeping the applicant/accused in jail for uncertain period. 8] In all such circumstance I am of the view that this is a fit case wherein the applicant can be released on bail. I therefore pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is allowed. .. 4 .. bail 2706/2014 (Ord.Exh.1) Applicant/accused Dinesh Sunil Rathod alias Akki D'Souza is released on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one surety in the like amount, subject to following conditions ­ He shall attend the concerned police station on every Tuesday between 6.00 p.m. to 8.00 p.m. and shall co­operate in investigation. He shall not leave India without permission of this court. He shall furnish proof of his residence. Date : 30.01.2015. O.B. Exh.1 Cri. Bail Appln.No.2834/17 ORDER BELOW EXH.1 IN CRI. BAIL APPLN. NO.2834/17 1] Applicant has preferred this application for grant of bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. on the ground that applicant has been falsely implicated in the present crime and he has not committed any offence as alleged. According to the applicant he is well known businessman and has no criminal antecedents to his discredit. According to applicant, police machinery failed to produce details regarding financial gain alleged to be received by the applicant. According to him if he is released on bail he is ready to abide by any terms and conditions imposed by the court. Hence, he has requested to release him on bail. 2] Say of I.O. was called for. I.O. has categorically objected the application on the ground that applicant­accused was found in possession of Gateway, SIM box etc. and thus their involvement is clear on record. According to I.O. in the offence total 12 accused are arrested who were conducting illegal business of telephone exchange by using those SIM box and with the help of 448 SIM cards. According to I.O. investigation in the matter is still in progress as it is of technical nature and vast. According to I.O. the applicant is not likely to make his appearance before the court if released on bail. According to I.O. revenue of the government itself in crores of rupees is involved in the matter and correspondence has already been made to concern department to know exact figure of the revenue. Hence, I.O. has requested to reject the O.B. Exh.1 Cri. Bail Appln.No.2834/17 application. 3] Heard rival advocates. They have submitted in terms of grounds of application and say. It was categorically pointed out that besides the allegation of SIM cards being recovered from the accused nothing else has been brought on record which categorically shows that accused has ever induced any person to cheat him and hence learned advocate has attempted to submit that when the main ingredient to constitute the offence is missing accused cannot be detained in the custody. On the other hand learned P.P. has objected the application on the ground put forth by the I.O. and has categorically pointed out that though charge­sheet is filed investigation is still in progress and much more needs to be come out of the said investigation. Hence, he has requested to reject the application. 4] After having heard rival advocates, I have gone through the copy of charge­sheet produced. On its perusal it is apparent that the concern I.O. has seized either SIM box or SIM cards at the instance of accused or from their possession itself. Allegations of having conducted business of illegal telephone exchange has been made against accused and I.O. has also alleged that by the said act the accused have deprived the government of revenue in crores of rupees. Though applicant's advocate has pointed out that there is nothing in the charge­ sheet as well which goes to show that accused themselves have induced anybody to either deliver certain property or to convert O.B. Exh.1 Cri. Bail Appln.No.2834/17 it in valuable security for their use. Further, though said ingredient is not categorically mentioned in the statement of witnesses, the court has to read it between the line. As per the admitted position as many as 448 SIM cards were seized from various accused referred in the charge­sheet and thus, from the particular act of seizure the applicant­accused is apparently involved in the matter. Allegations of prosecution itself goes to show that in the present matter revenue in crores of rupees of government is involved. Therefore, unless a proper opportunity is granted to prosecution to complete investigation in the matter though initially charge­sheet is produced before the concern court in itself in my opinion is not sufficient to enlarge accused on bail particularly considering serious allegation of cheating and depriving government itself from its revenue. As apprehended by I.O. considering the fact that further investigation is still in progress releasing the accused at this stage as well will certainly hamper the investigation and will certainly allow the applicant­accused to help other accused to abscond. No doubt for conviction of particular applicant­ accused necessary ingredients of offence are require to be established but this is certainly not a stage wherein prosecution has to establish minute details of the allegation. Prima facie seizure of SIM card, Gateway etc. and allegations of prosecution are certainly sufficient to establish the nexus between the accused and the crime and considering the fact that department of telecommunication of Government of India are yet to report the exact figure of the amount cheated or amount deprived by the act by the accused, releasing the accused will certainly give O.B. Exh.1 Cri. Bail Appln.No.2834/17 a wrong signal in the society. Having regards to all these facts though rule is of bail and not jail, this case is exception to the said rule. Having said so, I am not inclined to release the accused on bail. Accordingly, the order. ORDER Application is rejected. Thane (Hemant M. Patwardhan) Date: 02.01.2018 D.J.­4 & Addl. Sessions Judge, Thane

1 Bail No. 2878/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) Criminal Bail Application No.2878/2015 Laxman Ravji Chavan .. Applicant versus The State of Maharashtra Through Rabale Police Station .. Non­applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 By this application the applicant is seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. who was arrested 28.10.2015 by Vartaknagar Police Station in connection with C.R.No.I­ 367/2015 registered for an offence punishable under section 363, 376 of I.P.C. and section 3, 4, 5(l), 6 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as P.O.C.S.O. Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Mrs. Korade for the applicant/accused and learned A.P.P. Mrs. Deshmukh for State. I.O. present. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 27.10.2015 at the instance of the informant/victim­girl aged about 19 years with an indictment that before 8 to 9 months accused took her 2 Bail No. 2878/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) to Borivali and from there to Gorai and established physical relations with her on the pretext of marriage and he repeated the act on same pretext and thereafter refused to marry. Therefore, the report was lodged. 4] The learned Counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant­accused is falsely implicated. She submitted that it is the case of love affair and the victim­girl was having consent for the said act. She submitted that vague and general allegations are made without stating the date or time. She submitted that the victim­girl roamed with the accused and had been to various lodges with him and thus her consent is clear. The accused is behind bars since one month and ten days. He is permanent resident of Thane. He is ready to abide any conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing him on bail. 5] Per contra, the learned A.P.P. opposed the application submitting that during the investigation the girl was found minor and therefore, the provisions of P.O.C.S.O. Act were applied. She submitted that as the girl is minor, there is no question of her consent. The accused is involved in serious offence. The investigation is in progress. There are chances of tampering with witnesses and prayed for rejection of application. 3 Bail No. 2878/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R., it appears that the F.I.R. is lodged by the victim­girl herself stating her age as 19 years. Further, from the contents of F.I.R. it is clear that the victim­girl was knowing the accused. Earlier they were having friendship and later on they developed love affair. She was roaming with the accused and had talked about marriage. Further, from the F.I.R. it appears that the accused established physical relationship with the informant on the pretext of marriage and the act was not forceful and even the act is stated to have occurred before 8 to 9 months at lodge at Gorai and thereafter at different lodges for 3 to 4 times they were having physical contact. There is clear mention in the F.I.R. itself that as accused refused to marry her, she lodged the complaint. Though during the investigation the victim­girl was found minor, her date of birth is 18.12.1997 and is about to attain majority and having understanding of her own act. From the F.I.R. itself it appears that the victim­girl is consenting party. The accused is behind bars since 28.10.2015. The material part of investigation appears to have been completed. No fruitful purpose would be served by further incarceration of accused. The object of bail is neither punitive nor preventive but to secure the present of the accused at the time of trial. He is ready to abide by the conditions imposed by the Court. In such circumstances the apprehension of learned A.P.P. about 4 Bail No. 2878/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) tampering of witnesses can be addressed by imposing suitable conditions. Hence, I pass the following order ­ ORDER 1) The application is allowed. 2) Applicant namely Laxman Ravji Chavan be released on bail on his executing P.R. Bond of ₹ 15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one local solvent surety in the like amount on the following conditions ­ A] Applicant shall attend the concerned police station on every Sunday between 10.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon till filing the charge­sheet. B] Applicant shall co­operate in investigation and shall not tamper with prosecution witnesses. C] Applicant shall furnish his and his two blood relatives' address proofs and contact numbers and he is duty bound to inform I.O. and Court about the change of address, if any. D] Applicant shall not contact victim­girl or any other witnesses in any manner. Thane. Date : 08.12.2015. (Ms. U.M. Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act), Thane.

1 Bail No. 2879/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) Criminal Bail Application No. 2879/2015. Ibarat Hussain alias Bablu Kaisar Hussain Shaikh .. Applicant versus The State of Maharashtra Through Bhayander Police Station .. Non­applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 1] By this application the applicant is seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C., who was arrested on 09.09.2015 by Bhayander Police Station in connection with C.R.No.I­ 182/2015 registered for an offence punishable under section 376(2)(i) of I.P.C. and section 4, 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Mrs. Reena Korade for the applicant/accused and learned A.P.P. Mrs. H.A.Deshmukh for State. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 25.08.2015 at the instance of the informant/mother of victim­girl in respect of kidnapping of her daughter aged 15 years by one unknown person. Therefore, initially offence was registered under section 363 of I.P.C. During investigation the victim girl was found on railway station by some social worker and brought to the police station and after inquiry it was revealed that accused committed 2 Bail No. 2879/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) sexual assault on her. Therefore, the offence under section 376(2) (i) of I.P.C. and section4 and 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act were attracted. 4] The learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant­accused is falsely implicated. She submitted that there is delay of four days in lodging the F.I.R. No such incident as alleged in the F.I.R. was ever taken place. The accused is behind bars since two months and three weeks. The investigation is almost completed. The accused is permanent resident of the address given in the application and is ready to abide by any conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing him on bail. 5] Per contra, the learned A.P.P. opposed the application submitting that after the sexual assault the victim was very much frightened and therefore, instead going home, she had been to the railway station and there she was noticed by some social worker and brought to police station and then the offence revealed. She submitted that the accused is involved in serious offence. There are chances of tampering of the witnesses and prayed for rejection of application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R. it appears that initially offence of kidnapping minor daughter of informant was registered stating therein that on 22.08.2015 at about 3.00 p.m. the victim girl left the house as she had to attend tuition and since then she did not return. The perusal of police papers shows that the victim girl is of 15 years old and when she was going to attend 3 Bail No. 2879/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) her tuition, firstly she had been to the house of her friend Parveen. At that time accused who is brother of said Parveen, told her that Parveen is not at home and asked the victim to wait inside house and thereafter by closing the door, the accused firstly inappropriately touched the victim girl and then also touched her private part and then committed sexual assault on her and thereafter he threatened her not to disclose the incident to anybody. Within short time her friend Parveen returned. AT that time the victim was crying but due to threatening she could not disclose anything to her friend. The victim girl was frightened due to that incident and in confused state of mind she firstly had been to C.S.T. and then to Kalyan station and again went to C.S.T. At that time one social worker inquired with her and then she was brought to the police station. Thus, it clearly appears that the accused committed sexual assault on the victim girl. It is not a case of love affair. The accused is involved in a serious offence. The investigation is still in progress. The apprehension of the A.P.P. about tampering of witnesses is well founded. Looking to the serious nature of offence, there are chances of accused being fled away. Hence, accused is not entitled to be released on bail. I, therefore, pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is rejected. Thane. Date : 01.12.2015. (Ms. U.M. Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act), Thane.

According to her, on 30/10/2015 at about 1.00 p.m. when she was cooking, that time, the daughter of her sister Naina came there and she told that near one statue, some boys were outraging the modesty of victims i.e. her daughter and the daughter of her brother and that time, she was accompanied with them. When informant asked about the incident to victim­girls, then they narrated that prior to two days accused persons uttered obscene words on mobile and demanded for sex. On that day accused Nitin and one unknown person abused them, outraged their modesty, intent to insult their modesty, intentionally insulted by giving provocation and also committed sexual harassment. On the basis of report, PSO Vartak nagar police station registered C.R.No.I­599/2015 U/s. 354, 354 (A) & (D), 504, 509 r/w 34 of I.P. Code and U/s.12 of POCSO Act. Investigation was entrusted to probationary PSI Shri Kulkarni, who visited the spot and prepared spot panchanama, recorded the statement of victim and witnesses. The statement of victims are recorded u/s. 164 of Cr.P.C. and after completion of investigation he submitted the charge­sheet before the Special Judge (POCSO Act), Thane. ..3/- CNR NO.MHTH01-007764-2016 ..3.. Spl.C. No.290/2016 (Exh.No.22) 3] Charge Exh.5 was framed and explained to accused persons to which they pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. Their defence is that of total denial. 4] Considering the case of the prosecution following points arise for my determination and I have recorded my findings thereon for the reasons discussed below. POINTS FINDINGS 1 Does the prosecution prove that on 31/10/2015 at about 01.00 p.m. at Lokmanya nagar, accused persons in furtherance of their common intention, No. used criminal force to victim­girls intending to outrage their modesty thereby committed an offence punishable u/sec. 354 of I.P.C. ? 2 Does the prosecution further prove that on the aforesaid date, time and place accused persons in furtherance of their No. common intention made advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures demanded for sexual favours and made sexually coloured remarks i.e. said victim girl 'zavayla de' and thereby committed an offence U/s.354A of I.P. Code? 3 Does the prosecution further prove that on the aforesaid date, time and place accused persons in furtherance of their common intention attempted to contact victim­girls and contacted them No. repeatedly and also by calling on mobile despite clear indication of disinterest by victim and thereby committed an offence punishable U/s. 354(d) r/w 34 of I.P. Code? ..4/- CNR NO.MHTH01-007764-2016 ..4.. Spl.C. No.290/2016 (Exh.No.22) 4 Does the prosecution further prove that on the aforesaid date, time and place accused persons in furtherance of their common intention accused No.1 uttered words to victim ' thamb thamb, tuzya aichi gand, tuzya gandit dam nahi ka, tu katarian Kaif lagus chalalis ka and No. accused No.2 uttered words to victim on mobile that zavalya de and thereby committed an offence punishable U/s. 509 of I.P. Code? 5 Does the prosecution further prove that on the aforesaid date, time and place accused persons in furtherance of their common intention, intentionally insulted victim girls by abusing them and thereby No. gave provocation to them intending that such provocation will cause them to break public peace and thereby committed an offence Punishable U/s. 504 of I.P. Code? 6 Does the prosecution further prove that on the aforesaid date, time and place accused No.1 uttered the words to victim thamb thamb, tuzya aichi gand, tuzya gandit dam nahi ka, majha mobile number ghe, tu katarian Kaif lagun geli ka and accused No.2 uttered words to No. another victim that zavalya de with intention that such words shall be heard by victims and repeatedly followed them and contacted victim girls directly and through mobile phone and thereby committed an offence U/s. 11 for sexual harassment punishableU/s. 12 of POCSO Act? 7 What order ? As per final order. ..5/- CNR NO.MHTH01-007764-2016 ..5.. Spl.C. No.290/2016 (Exh.No.22) REASONS Points Nos. 1 to 6 : 5] These points are interlinked to each other, hence in order to avoid the repetition of evidence they are clubbed together. 6] At Exh.11 prosecution examined P.W.1 Sharda Parshuram Dhodade informant, who is mother of one victim­girl and aunt of another victim. Then prosecution examined victims P.W.2 and P.W.3 at Exh.14 & 16 respectively. Prosecution relied on FIR Exh.12, Printed FIR Exh.13, statement U/s. 164 of Cr.P.C. at Exh. 15 & 17. Ld. Defence Counsel admitted documents, spot panchanama Exh.18 and bonafide certificates Exh. 19 & 20. Then prosecution filed evidence close pursis Exh.21. As there is no incriminating evidence against the accused persons, therefore, their statement u/s 313 of Cr.P.C. is dispensed with. Heard Ld. A.P.P. and Adv. Smt. Sali for accused persons. 7] P.W.1 informant deposed that one victim­girl is her daughter and another victim­girl is daughter of her brother. On 30/10/2015 at 1.00 p.m. they both went to bring vegetables. At that time, boys outraged their modesty and victims told her about it. Thereafter, she went to police station and lodged complaint. She do not know the accused present before the Court. Though she admitted the signature on the complaint Exh.12, but she failed to state about the accused persons and as such, she declared hostile. Inspite, cross­ examination on behalf of prosecution, nothing brought on record against accused persons. The suggestion given to her that there was settlement out of Court and as such, she deposed falsely against accused persons only to save them. ..6/- CNR NO.MHTH01-007764-2016 ..6.. Spl.C. No.290/2016 (Exh.No.22) 8] P.W.2/victim deposed that in the year 2015 she was residing at Lokmanyanagar with her parents. On 30/10/2015 she and her sister were going for bringing vegetables. At that time, somebody outraged their modesty, but she cannot state who are those? At that time, those persons abused them and whistled. Thereafter, she told about it to her mother and she lodged complaint. If the evidence of this victim is tested with the FIR Exh.12, then it reveals that as per FIR the incident firstly narrated by niece of informant Naina and according to Naina she was also accompanied with them. Thus, testimony of victim­P.W.2 is otherwise as mentioned in FIR. That creates a doubt in the testimony of victim­P.W.2. 9] P.W.3/victim deposed that in the year 2015 she was residing at the house of complainant. On 30/10/2015 she and her sister were going for bringing vegetables. At that time, from back side, somebody outraged their modesty. Thereafter, she told about it to complainant and she lodged complaint. She do not know the names of persons, who outraged our modesty. She do not know the accused present before the Court. Thus, this victim is also reluctant to state against the accused persons and as such, inference can be drawn when complainant/informant, victims and accused persons are residing in the same vicinity and by the passage of time, there was settlement out of Court in between them, and as such, there is no incriminating evidence against the accused persons. 10] Thus, practically there is no evidence on the point of outrage of modesty, abuse, criminal intimidation and sexual harassment on victims at the hands of accused persons. Victim­ ..7/- CNR NO.MHTH01-007764-2016 ..7.. Spl.C. No.290/2016 (Exh.No.22) girls themselves have not supported the case of prosecution, then, examination of remaining witness is nothing but abuse of process of law by wasting precious time of Court. Therefore, I answer the point Nos. 1 to 6 in the negative and proceed to pass the following order. : ORDER : 1] Accused Manoj Manik Chaudhari and Nitin Sheshrao Vakte are hereby acquitted u/sec. 235(1) of Cr.P.C. of the offences punishable u/secs. 354, 354(A), 354(D), 504 & 509 of the Indian Penal Code and under Section­12 of POCSO Act. 2] Their bail bonds stand cancelled. 3] Accused shall comply forthwith the provision U/Sec.437­A Cr.P.C. by furnishing fresh P.R. and S.B. of Rs.10,000/­each. --1-- ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN CRIMINAL BAIL APPLICATION NO.2887/2017 The applicant Pravin Ashok Palve has applied for bail under section 439 of Cr. P.C. in C.R.No.I­111/2017 registered in Jawhar police station for the offence under section 354(B), 452 of Indian Penal Code and Section 8,12 of POCSO Act. 2. It is contended that the complainant and present applicant having love affair since long. The father of the informant pressurizing the applicant to perform marriage with his daughter, but the applicant is student and having no source of income. The complainant also not completed age of 18 years, therefore, he promise to marry with his daughter. The false case is filed only to pressurize the applicant. It is submitted that the offence is not punishable with death or imprisonment for life. Investigation is almost completed. It is the first bail application. The applicant is ready to co­operate for the trial. 3. The original complainant has given strong objection vide Exh.5. It is contended that since the date of arrest the family members of the applicant are continuously harassing and giving threats to the family of the complainant. The complainant has obtained transfer certificate and taken admission in another school. She has closed her tuition classes due to pressure and harassment of the applicant and his family members. The complainant and her family are suffering loss of her education. The complainant is minor, therefore, if released --2-- on bail he is likely to tamper the prosecution witnesses. The complainant has also filed N.C complaint and copy of FIR. 4. Investigation Officer has given say at Exh.4. It is contended that the incident took place on 11.11.2017. The informant is 17 years 11 months and 29 days old. The present applicant is 20 years old. On the day of incident at 11.30 p.m. the door of the informant was opened. The accused entered into their house and sexually assaulted the prosecutrix. So if he released on bail he is likely to repeat the offence and tamper the prosecution witnesses. 5. Considering the facts and circumstances of this case the court is of the view that the offence is not punishable with death or imprisonment for life. Investigation is almost completed. It is not just and proper to keep the applicant behind the bar till final disposal of the case. The applicant is young and student so if certain conditions are imposed to the applicant it will sufficient to the ends of justice. The court is also of the view that investigation is almost completed. The detention of the applicant behind the bar is not required. Therefore, on conditions the applicant is entitled for bail. Therefore, I proceed to pass following order. :ORDER: 1. Application is allowed. 2. The applicant Pravin Ashok Palve shall be released on P.B. and S.B. of Rs.15,000/­(Rupees Fifeen Thousand Only). 3. He shall co­operate for the investigation as and when --3-- necessary and shall attend the concerned police station. 4. He shall give undertaking that he shall not contact, tamper, harass, threaten the informant and any of her family members. 5. The applicant shall not enter into the premises where the informant resides. 6. He shall not enter into the school or tuition classes where the informant is learning. 7. He shall not repeat any of such kind of offence. Thane. ( S.C. Khalipe ) Date :06/12/2017. Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

Therefore, the report was lodged. 4] The learned Counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant­accused is falsely implicated. He further submitted that the sections of I.P.C. are triable by J.M.F.C. and the custodial interrogation of the applicant is not necessary. He is ready to co­operate in investigation and prayed for his release on anticipatory bail. 5] Per contra, the learned A.P.P. opposed the application on the ground that the offence is in respect of minor girl and the custodial interrogation of the applicant is necessary. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R. it appears that the allegations are only in respect of making indecent gestures and using obscene language intending to insult modesty of the victim­girl. Accused ­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­­ Appearances :­­ Smt.Chandane Ld. A.P.P. for the prosecution. She was also residing alongwith her family in the neighbourhood of “A”.
