She alongwith her another sister Shubhangi had been to Municipal Hospital at Karavegaon. At about 12.30 p.m. she received phone call of her husband who informed her that latch of his house was applied from the outside and the door was closed and there was noise of crying of “A” from her house and “A” was giving calls as “Mummy, Mummy”. Therefore, he asked Manda (P.W.2) to come back immediately. Immediately thereafter she came back and opened the door of her house. Thereafter, Manda (P.W.2) alongwith her husband went to the house of “A” where they found that she was frightened and crying. Manda (P.W.2) enquired with “A”. At that time “A” disclosed that Vijay uncle (accused) had been there in the house. He hugged her and kissed her on her lips. Thereafter he touched her body and removed her underwear and thereafter he touched her private part and 3 Special Case No. 291/2016(Jud.) CNR No.MHTH01-007803-2016 thereafter he inserted his private part in her private part. Therefore, she started crying. There was paining on her private part. Thereafter, Manda (P.W.2) called the parents of “A” . They all took “A” to the Municipal Hospital at Vashi for medical examination. However, doctor told them to Nerul Police Station to lodge report about the incident. Therefore, they came to Nerul Police Station where Manda (P.W.2) lodged F.I.R. [3] On the basis of the said information, crime vide C.R. No.I­335/2016 under Section 376,452 & 342 of IPC and U/sec.4 and 8 of the POSCO Act came to be registered and handed over to P.S.I. Nitin Shinde for investigation. On the same day, he arrested the accused and seized his wearing clothes in presence of panch witnesses and prepared panchanama to that effect. Thereafter, on the same day he forwarded the victim girl i.e. “A” to the Municipal Hospital, Navi Mumbai for medical examination. Accordingly her medical examination was done. Thereafter, the matter was handed over to A.P.I.Gaikwad for investigation. [4] On 23/8/2016 API Gaikwad (P.W.5) got recorded statement of “A”, the victim girl through woman police constable Smt.Patil. Thereafter, on the same day he forwarded the accused to the Municipal Hospital, Navi Mumbai for medical examination. Accordingly his medical examination was done. On the same day he visited to the spot of incident and prepared panchanama of the spot in presence of panch witnesses. 4 Special Case No. 291/2016(Jud.) CNR No.MHTH01-007803-2016 [5] Thereafter, he recorded statements of the witnesses. On 17/10/2016 he got recorded statement of the victim girl i.e. “A” before the Ld. Magistrate U/Sec.164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Thereafter, on 28/8/2016 he forwarded seized muddemal to F.S.L. Kalina for Chemical Analysis. On completion of the investigation, he submitted chargesheet against the accused under Section 376, 452 & 342 of the IPC and U/sec.4 and 8 of the POSCO Act, in the Court of J.M.F.C., Vashi. [6] Since the offence under Section 4 and 8 of the POCSO Act is triable exclusively by the Special Court , the Ld. J.M.F.C., Vashi committed the case to this Court. [7] My Ld. Predecessor framed Charge (Exh.4) against the accused under Sections 376(2)(i), 452 and 342 of the IPC and U/sec.4 and 8 of the POSCO Act. Particulars of the offence were read over and explained to the accused to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. [8] Statement of the accused U/Sec. 313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is recorded. He denied allegations made by the prosecution. His defence is that husband of Manda (P.W.2) borrowed money from him as hand loan. When he went to him to demand the said money, her husband under the influence of liquor raised quarrel with him and two days thereafter the present false case is lodged against him. He claimed himself to be innocent. [9] Following points arise for my determination. I have recorded my findings thereon for the reasons stated below : 5 Special Case No. 291/2016(Jud.) CNR No.MHTH01-007803-2016 SNO POINTS FINDINGS 1 Whether prosecution prove that the accused committed sexual assault on “A” a minor girl aged about 8 years, who was incapable of giving consent ? Yes. 2 Whether prosecution prove that the accused committed penetrative sexual assault on “A” a minor girl aged about 8 years ? Yes. 3 Whether prosecution prove that the accused committed sexual assault on “A” a minor girl aged about 8 years ? Yes. 4 Whether the prosecution prove that the accused committed trespass by entering into the room of “A” situated at Sharad Pail Chawl, Room No.4,Sector No.23, Darawegaon, Nerul, Navi Mumbai ? Yes. 5 Whether the prosecution prove that the accused wrongfully confined “A” in a room situated at Sharad Pail Chawl, Room No.4, Sector No.23, Darawegaon, Nerul, Navi Mumbai ? Yes. 6 What order ? The accused is acquitted of the offence U/S.342 of I.P.C. and convicted U/S.376(2)(i) & 452 of I.P.C. and U/S.4 & 8 of POCSO Act. 6 Special Case No. 291/2016(Jud.) CNR No.MHTH01-007803-2016 REASONS AS TO POINTS NO. 1 to 3 :­ [10] To attract offence U/Sec.376 (2)(i) of the I.P.C. and U/Sec. 4 and 8 of the POCSO Act against the accused, prosecution must prove that at the time of the incident the victim girl was minor or under 16 years of age. As per Sec.2 (d) of the POCSO Act, “child” means any person below the age of 18 years. [11] According to the prosecution the incident took place on 22/8/2016 and birth date of “A” ­the victim girl is 1/3/2009. Therefore, at the time of the incident she was about 7 years old minor girl. However, from the defence taken by the accused it appears that, he has not admitted that, the victim girl was 8 years old. Ld. Advocate for the accused submitted that, though the prosecution is claiming that the victim girl was born on 1/3/2009 and she was child, no reliable evidence has been produced on the record. Hence, it cannot be held that, at that time of the incident the victim girl was child. [12] In this connection, on perusal of the evidence of the prosecution, it appears that, birth certificate of the victim girl issued by Municipal Corporation of Navi Mumbai has been produced on record and it is marked at Exh.33. [13] Ld.Advocate for the accused further submitted that the said copy of the birth certificate came to be produced on record at 7 Special Case No. 291/2016(Jud.) CNR No.MHTH01-007803-2016 belated stage. Therefore, the accused could not get opportunity to challenge its veracity. It is the duty of the prosecution to prove the said birth certificate by adducing evidence of its author. Mere tendering such certificate and marking it as exhibit cannot be said that the prosecution has proved birth date of the victim girl. In support of his argument he relied upon the case law Ravi Anandrao Gurpude V/s. State of Maharashtra 2017 ALL MR (Cri) 1509, wherein it is held by the Hon'ble Division Bench of Bombay High Court that from the aforesaid provisions it is crystal clear that the prosecution is under bounden duty to prove that the victim is a child. Unless the prosecution successfully establishes that the victim is a child within the clause (d) of Sec.2 of the POCSO Act, a person cannot be convicted for the offence punishable under the provisions of the POCSO Act. [14] Ld.Advocate for the accused further relied upon the case law, Sujit Bhurandas Borkar V/s. The State of Maharashtra 2016 ALL MR (Cri) 2029, wherein it is held that 8. The next question is about the offences for which the appellant was convicted by the Trial Judge. In this connection, the utmost important factor, that was required to be satisfactorily proved by the prosecution, was the age of 'P' (PW 2). In a most casual manner, the prosecution placed on record the certified copy of a Bonafide Certificate from the school showing the date of birth, and was readily accepted by the learned Trial Judge without insisting for the legal proof thereof. By merely tendering or by merely exhibiting a Certificate, the date of birth cannot be said to have been proved according to Evidence Act. It was incumbent on the part of the prosecution to prove the entry from the Register of Date of Birth or in respect of Bonafide 8 Special Case No. 291/2016(Jud.) CNR No.MHTH01-007803-2016 Certificate through the concerned Headmaster or the school authorities by summoning the concerned person in the Court. But that was not done. The only inference, therefore, that will have to be drawn, is that the date of birth has not been proved from the documentary evidence. [15] On the other hand Ld. A.P.P. Smt.Chandane submitted that no procedure is prescribed under POCSO Act for determining age of the victim child. Therefore, court can follow the procedure contemplated in Juvenile Justice Rules, 2007 for the said purpose. In support of her argument she relied upon the case law, Subramanaim V/s. The State of Tamilnadu, 2017 ALL MR (Cri) Journal 170. [16] Ld.A.P.P. further submitted that the I.O. has produced on record authenticated copy of the birth certificate of the victim girl. The entries in the said certificate were recorded on 12/3/2009. Therefore, it cannot be said that the birth certificate was manufactured for the purpose of the instant case. Hence, the said birth certificate is admissible in evidence. In support of her argument she relied upon the case law, Robin Gurung V/s. State of Sikkim, 2018 ALL MR (Cri) Journal 443. [17] In this regard, Ld. Advocate for the accused submitted that the above case laws i.e. Subramaniam V/s. State of Tamilnadu and Robin Gurug V/s. State of Sikkim (supra) are not from our own parent High Court i.e. High Court of Bombay. As against the said case laws, the case laws of the Hon'ble High Court of Bombay cited by the accused as above regarding the 9 Special Case No. 291/2016(Jud.) CNR No.MHTH01-007803-2016 admissibility of birth certificate are applicable to the case in hand and it is the duty of prosecution to prove the contents of said birth certificate by adducing by appropriate evidence. Since, the prosecution has merely produced on record copy of the birth certificate and has not adduced evidence of any witness to prove its contents it cannot be said that the prosecution has proved date of birth and age of the victim girl. [18] In response to the above argument, Ld.A.P.P. Smt. Chandane relied upon the case law of the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the matter of Sunita Sawhney V/s. Union of India and Ors., LEX (DLH) 2015 12 343, wherein the Hon'ble Single Bench after having legal research on this aspect concluded that since the entry in a birth and death register is made by concerned official in discharge of his official duties, it is admissible in evidence and it is not necessary to examine the author thereof. In para 13 of the said judgment His Lordship observed thus, 13. My legal research as to the status of the Register of Birth & Death maintained under the Act and the Certificates of Birth & Death issued of extracts thereof shows that : (A) A Division Bench of the High Court of Punjab & Haryana in Bansi Ram Naru Ram Vs.Jit Ram Gehru Ram held that as against the evidence as to age in birth registers, the entry in birth register was held to be much more contemporaneous than the entry in school register and therefore more reliable and inspiring greater confidence. (B) The High Court of Karnataka in Vanajakshamma Vs. P.Gopala Krishna, 1970 AIR(Mys) 305 held that the extract of a birth register maintained under the Act is a public document to be read in evidence. 10 Special Case No. 291/2016(Jud.) CNR No.MHTH01-007803-2016 (C) Supreme Court in Harpal Singh V/s. State of Mimachal Pradesh, 1981 1 SCC 560 held that since the entry in a birth and death register is made by concerned official in discharge of his official duties, it is admissible in evidence and it is necessary to examined the author thereof. (D) The High Court of Karnataka in Khatalsaheb Wd. Khadirsaheb Inamdar Vs. Ameersaheb, on consideration of a plethora of case law, concluded that an entry in a birth and death register is admissible in evidence to show that a particular person by that name mentioned in the certificate was born or dead on that particular day, though cannot be evidence of paternity of a person mentioned there, because it is not the duty of the Registrar under the said Act to make any enquiry with respect to the entry as to paternity. It was further held that the certificate under the Act cannot be used for any purpose other than to prove the date of birth or death. (E) A Division Bench of the High Court of Bombay in Shri.Joaquim Constantinho Carvalho Vs. State, held that for determination of the age of a prosecutrix in a case of rape, a birth certificate issued by the Municipal Council being a public record is to be presumed to be authentic and correct and is to prevail upon the birth certificate issued by the Church. (F) This Court in Km. Para Vs. Director, Central Board of Secondary Education, 2004 111 DLT 573 held that to resolve a conflict between the dates of birth, the document which has been issued under the Registration of Births and Deaths Act has to be given effect to. (G) Supreme Court in Ravinder Singh Gorkhi Vs. State of U.P.,2006 5 SCC 584 held that entries in births and deaths register made by a public servant in discharge of official duty are relevant and admissible in evidence. (H) The High Court of Orissa in Siba Prasad Jena Vs. Puspanjali Jena, held a birth certificate issued under the Act aforesaid to be a public document admissible in evidence, without requiring any further proof thereof. 11 Special Case No. 291/2016(Jud.) CNR No.MHTH01-007803-2016 (I) A Division Bench of the High Court of Punjab & Haryana in Resham Singh Vs. Union of India,held that a date of birth in the Passport entered on the basis of Matriculation Certificate is liable to be corrected on the basis of the date of birth in the birth certificate as primacy has to be accorded to date of birth reflected in birth certificate. It was further observed that the PIAs had misunderstood legal nature of a birth certificate issued under the aforesaid Act and had erred in rejecting the application for correction of the date of birth on the Passport. (J) The High of Bombay in Jayant Gopalrao Pachade Vs. Motilal Kuber Kanoje, relying on Gopi Chand Arya Vs. Sm.Bedamo Kuer, 1966 AIR(Pat) 231, held that a birth/ death certificate being an entry made by a public servant in the ordinary course of his public duty and which entry is a public document, must have a presumption of correctness attached to it. It was further held that an entry in a birth or death register is conclusive evidence, unless disproved. (K) The High Court of Gujarat in Arpanaben Krunal Shah Vs. Regional Passport Office, held that as per the scheme of the Act aforesaid, entries in the register of birth and death are to be considered as correct, unless any declaration is otherwise of a competent Civil Court. It was further held that the PIAs when approached for correction of date of birth on the Passport are to normally treat the entries in the birth register as valid for the purpose of correction in Passport already issued and particularly, as against evidence of School Leaving Certificate weightage deserves to be given to the certificate of birth. It was further held that the Passport Authority can make correction in the Passport already issued, if genuine an proper circumstances are placed before it. A direction was accordingly issued for correction of date of birth in the passport already issued to bring it in consonance of date of birth in the birth certificate. (L) Supreme Court in CIDCO Vs.Vasudha Gorakhnath Mandevelkar, 2009 7 SCC 283 held that entry in a birth register prevails over an entry in school register. It was 12 Special Case No. 291/2016(Jud.) CNR No.MHTH01-007803-2016 further held that entries in a birth and death register raise a presumption of correctness. (M) The High Court of Orissa in Bikram Ray Vs. Smt.Jema Hembram, held that a certificate of birth issued under the aforesaid Act is a public document admissible in evidence and it is not necessary to prove who made the entries and what was the source of information. It was held that the register maintained under the said Act being a public document, presumption of correctness attaches to it. (N) The High Court of Punjab & Haryana in Surender Vs. State of Haryana, held that the certified copy of birth certificate is admissible in evidence without any further proof. (O) This Court in Abbas Hussain @ Munim Vs. Govt. of NCT of Delhi, held that the object of introduction of registration of births and deaths vide the Act is to give legal status to the official machinery for registration of births and deaths. (P) The High Court of Punjab & Haryana again in Ms. Seerat Khara Vs. Central Board of Secondary Education, held that birth certificate being a public document is presumed to be genuine in terms of Sections 79 & 80 of the Evidence Act. (Q) Supreme Court recently in Iswarlal Mohanlal Thakkar Vs. Paschim Gujarat Vij Co.Ltd.,2014 6 SCC 434 held that the High Court had committed a grave miscarriage of justice by not accepting the birth certificate as conclusive proof of age, the same being an entry in the public record. (R) A Division Bench of the High Court of Punjab & Haryana recently in Ambika Kaul Vs. Central Board of Secondary Education, held that the Registration of Births and Deaths Act was enacted with an object to have adequate and accurate country wide data for registration of births and deaths in the country and the said Act gives statutory recognition to the birth certificates and carries a presumption of correction. 13 Special Case No. 291/2016(Jud.) CNR No.MHTH01-007803-2016 [19] Considering what is observed by His Lordship as above, it appears that the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Harpalsingh V/s. State of Himachal Pradesh, 1981 (1) SCC 560 held that since the entry in a birth and death register is made by concerned official in discharge of his official duties, it is admissible in evidence and it is not necessary to examine the author thereof. Therefore, the said birth certificate (Exh.33) is admissible in evidence and its contents can be read as evidence. [20] In view of the aforementioned circumstances the case law Ravi Anandrao Gurpude (supra) of the Hon'ble High Court of Bombay is not applicable to the case in hand. Moreover, it is necessary to mention that the Hon'ble Division Bench of the High Court of Bombay in Ravi Anandrao Gurpude (supra) has not placed reliance on the birth certificate of the victim girl only on the ground that its author has not been examined, but there were some other more reasons also for which reliance was not placed on the birth certificate of the victim girl. [21] From the birth certificate (Exh.33) produced on the record, it appears that birth date of the victim girl is 1/3/2009. According to the prosecution case the incident took place on 22/8/2016. Thus, at the time of the said incident the victim girl was about 8 years old. That is she was under the age of 16 years as mentioned sixthly in Section 375 of the I.P.C. and under the age of 18 years as required in Clause (d) of Sec.2 of th POCSO Act. Hence, I have no hesitation to hold that at the time of the incident the victim girl was “child”. 14 Special Case No. 291/2016(Jud.) CNR No.MHTH01-007803-2016 [22] Manda (P.W.2) is not definitely as an eye witness to the evidence. Her evidence shows that she alongwith her another sister Shubhangi had been to the Municipal Hospital at Karavegaon. At that time she received a phone call of her husband who informed her that door of their house was closed by applying latch from outside and he heard noise of crying of “A” from her house. Therefore, immediately she came back to the house, opened the door of her own house and thereafter she alongwith her husband went to the house of “A” where “A” was found crying and scared. On enquiry “A” disclosed her that Vijay Kaka (accused) had been in the house, he hugged her, kissed her on her lips, and also touched her private part. “A” also disclosed her that the accused then removed her underwear and inserted his private part in her private part. Therefore, she was crying. [23] So also it has come in the evidence of “A” , the victim girl that on that day she had been to her house alongwith her younger brother. Her parents had gone to their work. At about 12.00 of noon Vijay (accused) had been to their house. He removed her pant (underwear) and also removed his pant an attempted to insert his penis in her private part. Therefore there was paining. Hence, she shouted as “Mummy Mummy”. She was repeatedly telling the accused to leave her, but he was inserting his penis in her private part. When she shouted loudly he ran away. [24] Ld. A.P.P. Smt. Chandane submitted that no doubt evidence of Manda (P.W.2) is not direct evidence. However, 15 Special Case No. 291/2016(Jud.) CNR No.MHTH01-007803-2016 evidence of “A” (P.W.1) , the victim girl is direct evidence. She has deposed the entire incident as it had happened. Therefore, only because the victim girl is minor her evidence cannot be doubted. Moreover testimony of “A” (P.W.1) is corroborated by medical evidence. Hence, the prosecution has proved the guilt of accused beyond all reasonable grounds. [25] On the other hand Ld.Advocate for the accused submitted that it is the case of the accused that husband of Manda (P.W.2) borrowed money from him as hand loan. When the accused went to him and demanded the money back, he (husband of Manda) was under the influence of liquor. At that time he raised quarrel with the accused and two days therefore the present case has been lodged and the accused is falsely implicated. In the circumstances, the prosecution case which is mainly rests upon the evidence of child witness about 8 years cannot be relied upon in absence of corroboration. In support of his argument he relied upon the case laws, John @ Vivek Ramesh Jadhav v/s. State of Maharashtra 2015 ALL MR (Cri) 4053, wherein it is held that, 6. The trial Court believed the story as narrated by the child. Virtually all the contents of the FIR have been narrated by the child during her substantive evidence before the court. It is significant to note that the age of the prosecutrix girl PW No.2 is eight years. She was not administered oath considering her understanding capacity as to the sanctity of the oath. Also the substantive evidence of PW No.1 is in consonance with what is mentioned in th FIR. However, during the cross­examination of PW No.1, the strained relations between the parties were brought on record. It is admitted position that the present appellant­ accused is th landlord of the Chawl where in one of the 16 Special Case No. 291/2016(Jud.) CNR No.MHTH01-007803-2016 rooms the parents of the victim girl reside as tenants. It was suggested during the cross­examination of PW No.1 that there were arrears of rent and the landlord was demanding arrears of rent to the father of the girl and also the landlord had asked the father of the girl to vacate the premises. On this count, there was dispute. In the considered opinion of this Court, this was the probable defence raised on behalf of the accused and the prototype evidence of PW No.1 and 2 would have been critically examined by the trial Court in the light of the said defence. However, the trial Court has failed to appreciate the said evidence and believe the testimony of the child witness. Whatever is the evidence of PW No.1 complainant mother, is in fact hearsay evidence,as according to her, entire events were narrated by the child after the child was taken back to home by her mother PW No.1. As such in fact the entire case of the prosecution rests only on the substantive evidence of child witness PW No.2, then aged about 8 years. In the opinion of this Court, it will be definitely risky to rely upon the evidence of child when there is no other corroborative evidence, moreover, there could not have been any medical evidence in the case considering the allegations. [26] Ld.Advocate for the accused further submitted that, in the present matter as per the evidence of the victim girl itself her younger brother was present in the house. However, though he was eye witness to the incident he has not been examined by the prosecution. Therefore, it would not be just and proper to place reliance upon the uncorroborated testimony of the child witness i.e. the victim girl. In support of his argument he relied upon the decision of the Hon'ble High Court of Bombay (Nagpur Bench) in the matter of Navin Dhaniram Baraiye V/s. The State of Maharashtra (Cri. Appeal No.406/2017 decided on 25/6/2018), wherein His Lordship held that ; 17 Special Case No. 291/2016(Jud.) CNR No.MHTH01-007803-2016 25. The prosecution chose to examine only victim no.1 and victim no.2 was not examined, although his statement was recorded by the police. Therefore, it is only the evidence of PW 2 (victim no.1) , which could be said to be direct evidence in support of the prosecution case. It is undisputed that the victim no.1 (PW 2) was a boy of tender age when the alleged incidents took place and he was still of tender age when his evidence was recorded in Court. Being a child witness of tender age and the sole direct witness in support of the prosecution case, the evidence of the said PW 2 has to be evaluated with great care and circumspection. In this context, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Radhey Shyam Vs. State of Rajasthan (supra) has held as follows:­ “12. In Panchhi, (1998 SCC (Cri) 1561) after reiterating the same principles, this Court observed that the evidence of a child witness must be evaluated more carefully and with greater circumspection because a child is susceptible to be swayed by what others tell him and, thus, a child witness is an easy prey to tutoring. This Court further observed that the courts have held that the evidence of a child witness must find adequate corroboration before it is relied upon. But it is more a rule of practical wisdom than of law. It is not necessary to refer to other judgments cited by learned counsel because they reiterate the same principles. The conclusion which can be deduced from the relevant pronouncements of this Court is that the evidence of a child witness must be subjected to close scrutiny to rule out the possibility of tutoring. It can be relied upon if the court finds that the child witness has sufficient intelligence and understanding of the obligation of an oath. As a matter of caution, the court must find adequate corroboration to the child witness's evidence. If found, reliable and truthful and corroborated by other evidence on record, it can be accepted without hesitation. We will scrutinize PW­2 Banwari's evidence in light of the above principles.” 18 Special Case No. 291/2016(Jud.) CNR No.MHTH01-007803-2016 [27] It is well settled proposition of law that evidence is to be appreciated on the basis of quality and not on the quantity. Therefore, only because evidence of “A” is not corroborated by other evidence , the same cannot be relied upon. If the testimony of sole witness inspire the confidence the same can be relied upon and even on the basis of sole testimony accused can be convicted. By making reference of the case law John @ Vivek Ramesh Jadhav (Supra) the accused is trying to establish that due to transaction of hand loan there was quarrel between the husband of Manda (P.W.2) and the accused and therefore he has been falsely implicated. Therefore, possibility of giving false evidence on the part of the victim girl cannot be ruled out. Hence, sole testimony of the victim girl cannot be relied upon. However, upon going through the said case law John @ Vivek (supra) it appears that admittedly there was dispute between the parties regarding house property and there was dispute between landlord an tenant. Therefore, considering the established rivalry between the parties the Hon'ble Lordship held that in absence of any other corroborative evidence testimony of child witness is not reliable. However, in the present matter the accused put forth his defence that due to the dispute regarding hand loan he has been falsely implicated. However, the said defence regarding transaction of hand loan has not been established by the accused. Therefore, bare words of suggestion to the prosecution witnesses in cross­ examination would not take place of substantive evidence. Therefore, the case law­ John @ Vivek (supra) is also not applicable to this case on the facts. 19 Special Case No. 291/2016(Jud.) CNR No.MHTH01-007803-2016 [28] So far evidence of younger brother of the victim girl is concerned, it is necessary to note that at the time of the incident the victim girl was about 7 years. Old. Definitely her younger brother would have been about 3 to 4 years old, who had just started to speak. Therefore, it cannot be said that the said younger brother of the victim girl was the witness capable of giving evidence before the court. Hence, the objection raised by the defence side about non­examination of younger brother of the victim girl goes away and therefore the case law i.e. Navin Dhaniram Baraiye (Supra) is also not applicable to the case in hand. [29] On the costs of the repetition, it is necessary to mention that “A” (P.W.1) states that on that day she had been to her house alongwith her younger brother. Her parents had gone to their work. At about 12.00 of noon Vijay (accused) had been to their house. He removed her pant (underwear) and also removed his pant an attempted to insert his penis in her private part. Therefore there was paining. Hence, she shouted as “Mummy Mummy”. She was repeatedly telling the accused to leave her, but he was inserting his penis in her private part. When she shouted loudly he ran away. [30] The above evidence on the part of the victim girl is sufficient and cogent to prove ingredients of Sec.376(2)(i) of I.P.C. and Sec.4 & 8 of the POCSO Act. 20 Special Case No. 291/2016(Jud.) CNR No.MHTH01-007803-2016 [31] It cannot be said that testimony of the victim girl is not corroborated. As per the prosecution story on the day of the incident itself the victim girl was forwarded to Municipal Hospital, Navi Mumbai for medical examination. Accordingly the concerned doctor examined her. Dr.Meenakshi Sawant (PW.3) who medically examined the victim girl and issued medical certificate (Ex.20). It has come in her evidence and it is mentioned in the said certificate that, history of sexual assault was stated by the mother of the victim girl. On examination of the private part of the victim girl it was found that there was evidence of abrasion on left labia minora, which was fresh. Dr.Meenakshi Sawant (P.W.3) opined that there was forceful insertion in the private part of the victim girl and evidence of sexual intercourse by the accused cannot be ruled out. [32] During the cross­examination it was suggested to Dr.Meenakshi Sawant that apart from the discharge of Leucorrhoea it also causes intense itching on the private part of the female and due to vigorous itching and scratching such abrasion on labia minora is possible. It is also suggested that while scratching private part such abrasion on labia minora is possible. From the said cross­ examination it appears that the defence wans to suggest that due to scratching on the private part abrasion on labia minora has been caused to the victim girl. However, the defence has not asked any question about such abrasion or scratching to the victim girl nor brought any positive evidence to brush aside the evidence of Dr. Meenakshi Sawant (P.W.3) . Therefore, in my opinion evidence of the victim girl is fully corroborated by Dr.Meenakshi Sawant (P.W.3). 21 Special Case No. 291/2016(Jud.) CNR No.MHTH01-007803-2016 [33] As regards to the statements of the victim girl recorded before the police , the Ld. Magistrate U/Sec.164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and before the court, Ld.Adv. for the accused submitted that all these three statements are inconsistent . Hence, they cannot be relied upon. In the statement before the police officer the victim girl states that “Kaka” came to her house, kissed her lips, touched her body by hands and removed her pant and thereafter also touched her private part by hand and thereafter inserted his private part in her private part. However, in the statement recorded U/Sec.164 of Cr.P.C. she states “Vijay Kaka”a was watching T.V. in her house. At that time he took her in the corner of the cupboard and removed his own pant and her pant and thereafter inserted his private part in her private part. But, she states different story before this court. Therefore, such inconsistency in her statements is sufficient to raise doubt about the truthfulness of her testimony. Therefore, her testimony cannot be relied upon. [34] I have gone through all these three statements of the victim girl. It is well settle that no witness can depose before the court the case as it was stated by it before the police or any other authority. While deposing before the court some omissions, contradictions, inconsistencies and improvements are bound to be occurred. Such omissions, contradictions, inconsistencies or improvements are fatal only if they are in respect of the material particulars of the case and go to the very route of the case. However, considering these three statements of the victim girl and 22 Special Case No. 291/2016(Jud.) CNR No.MHTH01-007803-2016 inconsistencies between them, I am of the opinion that they are not fatal because they are not in respect of material particulars. If the victim girl at one place calls the accused as “Kaka” and on the another place calls him “Vijay Kaka” it would not make any difference because she knows the accused since long and therefore there is at all no possibility of misidentification of the accused. Hence, for this minor reason testimony of the victim girl cannot be doubted. [35] Moreover, in the present matter, the FIR regarding the incident was lodged immediately after the incident. It is well settled that, lodging of FIR immediately after the incident inspires the confidence. In the present matter Woman Police Constable Patil recorded statement of the victim girl. Her statement recorded before the court is consistent with the prosecution case as well as with the testimony of her maternal aunt i.e. Manda (PW.2). In the circumstances, only because there are some minor inconsistencies in her statement before police, statement U/Sec.164 of Cr.P.C. and the statement before the court does not make the said evidence of the victim girl worthless or unreliable. [36] It is well settled that, conviction of an accused can be based on the testimony of solitary witness. However, the testimony of the sole witness should be of sterling quality which should inspired the confidence of the court for its implicit acceptance. In the present case, on the basis of evidence adduced by the prosecution it appears that, testimony of “A”­the victim girl (PW.1) 23 Special Case No. 291/2016(Jud.) CNR No.MHTH01-007803-2016 is sufficient and cogent to prove the guilt of accused. Moreover, her testimony is corroborated by her aunt Manda (PW.2) and Dr.Meenakshi (P.W.3). Therefore, I found no reason to disbelieve their testimonies. [37] In my opinion defence taken by the accused also appears not probable because in an Indian society it is observed that modesty of a woman has much importance. If any woman faces sexual assault at the hands of any person , even then many time she keeps quite only because she is afraid of stigmas which will be attached to her character in such cases. Therefore, it is highly impossible and improbable that only because there was quarrel between the accused and the husband of Manda (P.W.2)on account of the payment of hand loan , the parents of the victim girl by putting future of their own daughter on the stake lodge false complaint and that too relating to sexual assault. Moreover the accused has not put forth any details regarding payment of said hand loan he was expected to give the details of the transaction that how much amount of money was given to the husband of Manda (P.W.2) and when the said amount was given. In the circumstances, defence taken by the accused appears not acceptable. [38] For the reasons stated above I hold that the prosecution has proved the guilt of accused U/Secs.376(2)(i) of I.P.C. and U/Secs.4 & 8 of POCSO Act. I, therefore, answer point Nos.1 to 3 in the affirmative. 24 Special Case No. 291/2016(Jud.) CNR No.MHTH01-007803-2016 AS TO POINT NO.4 : [39] To bring home the guilt of accused U/Sec. 452 of I.P.C. prosecution must prove that the accused committed house trespass and the same was committed after making preparation for causing hurt or for assaulting or for wrongfully restrain some person. From the above mentioned facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence adduced by the prosecution it is clear that at the time of the incident the accused by entering into the house of “A” the victim girl committed house trespass, he had gone there with preparation for assaulting the victim girl sexually. Thus, the ingredients of Sec.452 of I.P.C. are proved by the prosecution. I, therefore hold the accused guilty of the offence U/Sec.452 of I.P.C. Hence , I answer point No.4 in the affirmative. AS TO POINT NO.5 : [40] To establish offence U/Sec. 342 of I.P.C. prosecution must prove that the accused obstructed some person voluntarily and the effect of such obstruction was to restrain that person from proceeding beyond a certain limit and the said restrain was wrongful. In the present case it is alleged by the prosecution that the accused wrongfully confined the victim girl. However, on examination of evidence of the prosecution it appears that it is no where stated that the accused confined the victim girl. It has only come in the evidence of Manda (P.W.2) that after coming back to house she opened the door of her house and thereafter she alongwith her husband went to the house of the victim girl. However, it is nowhere stated by Manda (P.w.2) nor by “A” 25 Special Case No. 291/2016(Jud.) CNR No.MHTH01-007803-2016 (P.W.1) the victim girl that the accused closed the door of the house of the victim girl from outside and confined her wrongfully. Therefore, in my opinion evidence of the prosecution is not sufficient and cogent to prove the guilt of accused U/Sec. 342 of I.P.C. I , therefore answer point No.5 in the negative. AS TO POINT NO.6:­ [41] As mentioned above the prosecution has proved guilt of accused U/sec.376(2)(i) and 452 of the IPC and U/sec. 4 and 8 of the POCSO Act. Hence, the accused is liable to be convicted. [42] Before parting with the judgment, I would like to hear the accused on the point of sentence. Thane ( S. B. 1 Bail No. 2911/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) Criminal Bail Application No.2911/2015 Jaypal Govind Pardeshi .. Applicant versus The State of Maharashtra Through Thane Nagar Police Station .. Non­applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 By this application the applicant is seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. who was arrested on 26.10.2015 by Thane Nagar Police Station in connection with C.R.No.I­235/2015 registered for an offence punishable under section 376(2)(f)(i)(n), 506 of I.P.C. and section 4 and 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as P.O.C.S.O. Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Mr. R.S.Jagtap for the applicant/accused and learned A.P.P. Mrs. Navale for State. I.O. present. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 26.10.2015 at the instance of the informant/victim­girl aged about 14 years with an indictment that on 24.10.2015 and on 26.10.2015 accused committed unnatural sex against the order of nature 2 Bail No. 2911/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) and also sexual assault and threatened her not to disclose it to anybody. 4] The learned Counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant­accused is falsely implicated. He submitted that there is delay of two days in lodging the F.I.R. He further submitted that the victim­girl stated her age approximately 14 years and placed his reliance on the judgment of Hon'ble High Court in case of Satyam Fulore vs. State of Maharashtra – 2015 ALL MR (Cri) 2785. He submitted that the accused is behind bar since his arrest. He is permanent resident of address given and is ready to abide any conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing him on bail. 5] Per contra, the learned A.P.P. strongly opposed the application submitting that the offence is serious. The victim is only 14 years old and accused committed a heinous crime. The medical certificate also supports the version of victim. She further submitted that the accused is a security guard and his wife is also working in police department and thus there are chances of pressurizing the victim girl and tampering with witnesses. The investigation is in progress and prayed for rejection of application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of police papers and F.I.R. it appears that the victim is aged about 14 years. She was 3 Bail No. 2911/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) staying at the house of accused due to poor financial condition of her parents. On 24.10.2015 when the wife of accused was on duty, on that day accused committed unnatural sex against the order of nature with the victim­girl and on 26.10.2015 again he did the same thing and thereafter the victim­girl immediately disclosed the incident to one of her friends who met her in grocery shop and thereafter, she immediately rushed to police station and lodged the complaint. As per ossification test the age of victim is stated as 14 – 15 years. The medical certificate of the victim­girl also substantiates the allegations made in the F.I.R. The case law relied on the learned counsel for applicant­ accused is totally on different footing and not applicable in the facts of the case. The investigation is in progress and is at nascent stage. Considering submission about the position of the accused and his wife, the apprehension about pressurizing the victim and tampering with witnesses is well founded. Hence, no case is made out for releasing the accused on bail. I, therefore, pass the following order ­ ORDER The application stands rejected. Thane. Date : 16.12.2015 (Ms. U.M. Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act), Thane.

Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Mr. Naresh Pradhan for the applicant/accused and learned A.P.P. Mrs. Navale for State. I.O. absent. Case diary is not produced. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 15.11.2015 at the instance of the informant/father of victim­girl aged about 16 years with an indictment that the accused kidnapped his 2 Bail No. 2921/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) daughter with intent to compel her to marry with him and forced or seduced for illicit intercourse. 4] The learned Counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant­accused is falsely implicated. He submitted that it is a case of love affair. The victim­girl is in love with the accused and eloped with him on her own wish. He submitted that the statement of the victim­girl is recorded under section 164 of Cr.P.C. wherein she has stated that there was no sexual relationship between the accused and herself. He further submitted that the accused is behind bar since one month and the investigation is practically completed. The accused is not having any criminal antecedents. He is permanent resident of Navi Mumbai and is ready to abide any conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing him on bail. 5] Per contra, the learned A.P.P. opposed the application submitting that the offence is serious. The victim­ girl was minor and there is no question of her consent. She further submitted that in fact when the victim­girl was produced for recording under section 164 of Cr.P.C. at that time the brother of the accused was present in the Court premises and pressurized the victim­girl. Non­applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 1] By this application the applicant is seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C., who was arrested on 01.11.2015 by Shreenagar Police Station in connection with C.R.No.I­214/2015 registered for an offence punishable under section 363, 366A, 376(2) (i) of I.P.C. and section 4, 17 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Mr. Rajkumar Yadav for the applicant/accused and learned A.P.P. Mrs. Navale for State. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 29.09.2015 at the instance of the informant/paternal aunt of the victim­girl with an indictment that the accused took away her minor niece from her custody. Therefore, firstly the offence under section 363 of I.P.C. was registered. During investigation the victim girl was found in the custody of the accused and it was revealed that the victim girl was subjected to forceful sexual intercourse and therefore, offence under section 376 (2)(i) of I.P.C. and section 4, 17 of P.O.C.S.O. Act were added. 2 Bail No. 2924/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) 4] The learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant­accused is falsely implicated. He submitted that accused and victim­girl are in love since one year and victim­girl married with the accused. He further submitted that the victim­girl went with accused on her own will in presence of informant and no threats were extended to her. He further submitted that the parents of the girl have no grievance and they are today present in the Court and ready to file their affidavit. He further submitted that the victim­girl got married with the accused. The learned counsel also produced the victim­girl and her mother before the court and prayed that accused be released on bail. 5] Per contra, the learned A.P.P. opposed the application submitting that the victim­girl is minor aged about 13 years and therefore no question of consent arises. She submitted that the accused was continuously harassing the victim­girl since one year and therefore her parents kept her with informant and from there accused took her away to Delhi and committed sexual assault on her. The investigation is in progress and prayed for rejection of application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R. it appears that the victim­girl is minor aged about 13 years and as per her birth certificate, her date of birth is 01.06.2003. In F.I.R. it is stated that the accused and the victim were having love affair and therefore, her parents kept the victim­girl with her since two months. There also the accused was continuously following her. He called the victim­girl on the pretext of taking back his ATM card and from there, he took away 3 Bail No. 2924/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) the victim­girl to Delhi and stayed there for about one month and thereafter, they were traced by police. Further, the medical certificate of the victim­girl also supports the case of the prosecution about penetrative sexual assault on her. During this period the accused also established physical relations with her. Though it is submitted that the victim was having consent for it, looking to the age of the victim­girl her consent is of no consequences in the eyes of law. The accused is involved in a serious offence. The investigation is in progress and at nascent stage. Further, the clear effort for tampering of witness has been made on the side of accused by producing the victim­girl and her mother before the Court. It is clear evidence of tampering of witness and thus the apprehension of learned A.P.P. appears to be well founded. In such circumstances the accused is not entitled to be released on bail. Hence, I pass the following order ­ ORDER The application is rejected. Thane. Date : 01.12.2015. (Ms. U.M. Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act), Thane.

On the alleged day of incident accused slapped complainant/victim, touches her chest and threatened to commit rape on her and to kill her. 3] Accused has submitted that, he is innocent and has not committed any offence. Present case is concocted case. The FIR is lodged with intention to harass the applicant and coerce him in leaving Bhiwandi. He is reputed person in the society and is the only earning member of his family. There is no eye witness to the alleged incident. There are no criminal antecedents against him. Nothing is to be recovered at his instance. He has permanent place of residence. He is ready to abide by any terms and conditions imposed by the Court. He will not tamper the prosecution evidence and he will co­operate in investigation. ..2.. Cri. Bail Appln. No.2870/2018 (Rashid @ Faheem Ahmad Mushtaque Ahmad Ansari Vs. State of Maharashtra) C.R.No.I­197/2018 of Nizampura Police Stn. MHTH01­007912­2018 Therefore, he prays for bail. Hence this application. 4] Called say of Investigating Officer and Ld. A.P.P. Advocate for accused relied on the ruling reported in State through CBI Vs. Amaramani Tripathi in Appeal (Cri) 1248 of 2005 and Thulia Kali Vs. The State of Tamil Nadu reported in 1973 AIR 501. 6] I have gone through the papers. On perusal of Say it is seen that, the accused is arrested on 13.10.2018 and since then he is behind the bars. On perusal of FIR it is seen that the alleged offence took place on 11.10.2018 and the present FIR came to be lodged on 13.10.2018. Thus, there is delay of two days in lodging the FIR which is not explained. The offence is not punishable with imprisonment for life or death. Considering the nature of offence, ..3.. Cri. 1 Bail No. 2937/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) Criminal Bail Application No.2937/2015 Nitesh Bhimrao Kadam .. Applicant versus The State of Maharashtra Through Vartaknagar Police Station .. Non­applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 1] By this application the applicant is seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. who was arrested on 08.10.2015 by Vartaknagar Police Station in connection with C.R.No.I­553/2015 registered for an offence punishable under section 376, 323 and 506 of I.P.C. and section 4 and 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as P.O.C.S.O. Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Mr. L.R. Bandal for the applicant/accused and learned A.P.P. Mrs. R.A. Navale for State. I.O. present with case papers. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 08.10.2015 at the instance of the informant victim­girl aged about 17 years with an indictment that since June, 2013 to 05.10.2015 accused 2 Bail No. 2937/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) repeatedly committed sexual assault on her and threatened her that he will publish her nude clippings and also threatened to kill her and her parent and brother. 4] The learned Counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant­accused is falsely implicated. He submitted that accused and victim­girl are close relative. He further submitted that the father of accused and victim are working in a same school and though the father of accused is junior he superseded the father of victim girl and therefore this false complaint has been lodged. He submitted that there is gross delay in lodging FIR without any explanation. There is no medical record to support the contention of the victim. He submitted that accused is in jail since 74 days and the investigation is virtually completed. The accused is not having any criminal antecedent. He is permanent resident of Thane and is ready to abide any conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing him on bail. 5] Per contra, the learned A.P.P. opposed the application submitting that the offence is serious. The victim­girl was minor and there is no question of her consent. She further submitted that the accused overpowered and committed sexual assault on the victim­girl and even gave threats to her. He took the disadvantage of their friendship. She further submitted that the 3 Bail No. 2937/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) statement of victim­girl under the provisions of section 164 of Cr.P.C. is recorded and she give the same version as given in the FIR. The investigation is in progress and thus, there are chances of tampering with witnesses and prayed for rejection of application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of police papers and F.I.R. it appears that the victim­girl is of 17 years and thus attained the age of discretion and knowing the consequences of her own act. The accused and victim­girl are knowing each other as their father were working as a peon in a same school. From the FIR itself it is clear that the accused used to pick and drop the victim various times from her college to home. The first incident appears to be of June, 2013 and the last as such is of 05.10.2015 and the FIR was lodged on 08.10.2015. Thus there appears a reasonable delay. The accused is behind the bar since 75 days. The investigation is practically completed and only formality of filing charge­sheet appears to be remained. The accused has no criminal antecedents. No fruitful purpose would be served by further incarceration of accused. The object of bail is neither punitive nor preventive but to secure the presence of the accused at the time of trial. He is ready to abide by the conditions imposed by the Court. In such circumstances the apprehension of learned A.P.P. about tampering of witnesses can be addressed by imposing suitable conditions. Hence, I pass the 4 Bail No. 2937/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) following order ­ ORDER 1) The application is allowed. 2) Applicant namely Nitesh Bhimrao Kadam be released on bail on his executing P.R. Bond of ₹ 30,000/­ [rupees thirty thousand only] with one or two local solvent sureties in the like amount on the following conditions ­ A] Applicant shall attend the concerned police station on every Sunday between 10.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon till filing of the charge­sheet. B] Applicant shall co­operate in investigation and shall not tamper with prosecution witnesses. C] Applicant shall furnish his and his two blood relatives' address proofs and contact numbers and he is duty bound to inform I.O. and Court about the change of address, if any. Thane. Date : 23.12.2015 (Ms. U.M. Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act), Thane.

He submitted that applicants want that victim­girl should marry with Rashid. However, the victim­girl was not desired to marry with him and therefore she implicated them in false case. He submitted that the person Mohammad Ali with whom she had been to lodge report is having old rivalry with them and therefore with his help, a concocted story has been made out. He further submitted that applicant no.2 is having no role stated in F.I.R. The applicants are behind bar since their arrest. They are ready to abide any conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing them on bail. 5] Per contra, the learned A.P.P. opposed the application submitting that the offence is serious. She submitted that specific role of all accused is mentioned in F.I.R. Applicant no.1 locked the girl inside and then accused Rashid Ali committed sexual assault on her. She further submitted that the medical report also supports the version of the victim­girl. Accused even extended life threats to the victim­girl. The investigation is in progress. There are chances of tampering with witnesses and prayed for rejection of application. 3 Bail No. 2939/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R., it appears that the victim­girl is staying with her maternal aunt, applicant no.1, at her house since thirteen years. It is also evident that the present applicant no.1 wants to marry the victim­girl with her son Rashid Ali, however, victim­girl was opposing the marriage as she want to pursue her studies. The F.I.R. is also evident that on 12.11.2015 the present applicant no.1 locked her in room with accused Rashid and then alleged act of sexual assault took place. As far as role of applicant no.2 is concerned, it is stated that on second day she forced the victim­girl to submit herself for sexual relationship with her brother, however, victim­girl pretended that she want to attend nature's call and then with the help of her uncle, who is staying in the neighbourhood, lodged the report in the police station. From report it appears that the present applicants are stated as abettors and the main culprit is accused Rashid Ali. As far as the material part of investigation in respect of present applicants is concerned, it appears to be completed. Both the applicants are women. The object of bail is neither punitive or preventive but to secure the present of the accused at the time of trial. The applicants are readyto abide by the conditions imposed by the Court. In such circumstances the apprehension of learned A.P.P. about tampering of witnesses can be addressed by imposing stringent conditions. Hence, I pass the following order ­ ORDER 1) The application is allowed. 2) Applicants namely Mrs. Shakirabano A. Momin and Ms. Parvin A. Momin be released on bail on their executing P.R. 4 Bail No. 2939/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) Bond of ₹ 25,000/­ [rupees twenty five thousand only] each with one local solvent surety each in the like amount on the following conditions ­ A] Applicants shall attend the concerned police station on every Sunday between 10.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon till filing the charge­sheet. B] Applicants shall co­operate in investigation and shall not tamper with prosecution witnesses. C] Applicants shall furnish their and their two blood relatives' address proofs and contact numbers and they are duty bound to inform I.O. and Court about the change of address, if any. D] Applicants shall not contact victim­girl or any other witnesses in any manner. Thane. Date : 02.12.2015. (Ms. U.M. Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act), Thane.

Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Mr. Mukesh Dongarge for the applicant/accused and learned A.P.P. Mrs. Deshmukh for State. I.O. present. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 07.11.2015 at the instance of the informant one Mr. James Babu Vergese with 2 Bail No.2946/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) an indictment that he received secret information in respect of human trafficking and accordingly raid was conducted at Shubham Bar and Restaurant and from there three accused were arrested and three victims were rescued. Therefore, the report was lodged. 4] The learned counsel for the applicant­accused submitted that the applicant­accused is falsely implicated. He further submitted that the accused was arrested after raid. He further submitted that the place where the alleged raid was conducted is a restaurant and therefore it is not possible to carry out prostitution at that place. He further submitted that said place is not a brothel and no prostitution is carried out there. He further submitted that three girls were rescued, however, F.I.R.. is silent as to for which girl the amount was paid while trapping. In F.I.R. role of applicant­accused is not described. There is no direct involvement of the accused. It is not a case of penetrative sexual assault. The applicant has no criminal antecedents. His father attends fishery business and parents thereafter sell fish. She is learning in St. Joseph High School, Uttan in 9th standard and attends school at about 7.00 a.m. upto 1.00 p.m. There is holiday on Thursday and Sunday to the school. 3] It is alleged that on the days of holidays, she goes to the house of her uncle Franky Bhanga to watch the television. Swiden (accused) is employed by his Uncle and he visits his house. She came in acquaintance with him and became friends. They were talking with each other on telephone. The accused was having cell number 7045213837 and his brother was having cell number 9930704317. The accused told her, “Tula bhagitlyashivay mala chain padat nahi, tu bandaravan yet ja tula bandaravan bhagat jain”. She told him that she does not like. .....3/­ 3 Spl.POCSO Case 300/2016 4] It is alleged that on 22/09/2016 on Thursday at about 7.00 p.m. she went to the house of her Uncle Franky Bhanga to watch the T.V. The accused came asked for drinking water. She provided the water and she told that she does not like him. 5] It is alleged that on 23/09/2016 at about 1.15 p.m. she was proceeding to home accused met her on the way and told that he want to tell something. She went to the garden at about 7.00 p.m. near St. Joseph High School and the accused was already present there. The accused told that she likes him and “Tula baghitlyashivay mala chain padat nahi. Tu roj bandaravan yet ja”. Accused asked that if she informed this fact, he will took poison and threatened him. It is alleged that accused was always watching her when she was proceeding after school was over. 6] It is lastly alleged that on 26/09/2016 when the school was over, accused was watching her. She informed the incident to her parents and thereafter lodged complaint. 7] During investigation concerned police drawn the spot panchanama, memorandum and panchanama of spot, recorded statement of witnesses, accused was arrested and after completion of investigation and collection of call details submitted charge­sheet. 8] On hearing learned APP and defence counsel .....4/­ 4 Spl.POCSO Case 300/2016 charge below Exh.2 was framed under section 354(A)(D), 506 of I.P.C. and 7, 8, 11(iv) r.w. 12 of POCSO Act and same when read over and explained to the accused in vernacular, he has denied it vide his statement Exh.3. 9] Prosecution examined in all four witnesses. The accused also examined defence witness D.W. Franky Bhanga. 10] From the evidence and statement under section 313 of Cr.P.C. the defence of accused is of denial. 11] In the circumstances following points arise for my determination and I record my finding to them for the reasons mentioned hereinafter :­ Sr. POINTS FINDINGS No. 1] Whether prosecution proved that in In the August to 26/09/2016 near St. affirmative. Joseph High School, Mira Bhayandar, District Thane within the jurisdiction of Uttan Sagari Police Station accused committed the act of physical contact with victim Dolfina/made sexual coloured remarks and or attempted to contact victim repeatedly, despite her clear indication of disinterest ? 2] Whether it is proved that on the said date, time and place and In the during the course of same negative. .....5/­ 5 Spl.POCSO Case 300/2016 transaction accused threatened complainant victim Dolfina and thus committed offence of criminal intimidation? 3] Whether it is proved that on the In the said date time and place and affirmative. during the course of same transaction accused committed the act of sexual assault ? 4] Whether it is proved that on the In the said date, time and place and affirmative. during the course of same transaction accused repeatedly or constantly either followed, watch and tried to contact the victim ? 5] What order ? Accused is convicted. REASONS POINT NO. 2 : 12] Prosecution examined P.W. Dolfina, who is victim, P.W. Lavina, her mother, P.W. Rahul Jadhav, panch, P.W. Jagdish Bangar, who was Investigating Officer. 13] The complaint mentions that accused threatened that if she informed the incident, he will take poison and thus threatened. P.W. Dolfina stated that accused told her that if she tell anything to anybody, he will consume poison. Her complaint is at Exh.7. She is the only witness as mother was informed lateron. The I.O. only stated that as evidence was .....6/­ 6 Spl.POCSO Case 300/2016 found he submitted charge­sheet. The offence of criminal intimidation prescribed in section 503 of I.P.C., on the face of record is not found proved. With this brief reasoning I answer point in the negative. POINTS NO. 1, 3 & 4 : 14] For the sake of convenient discussion points are clubbed. 15] P.W.Dolfina stated that she is studying in 9th standard in St. Joseph High School, Uttan and attends school from 7.00 a.m. to 1.00 p.m. She is having holiday on Thursday and Sunday. Franky Bhanga is her Uncle and she occasionally visit to his house for watching T.V. accused Swiden was coming to his house and she came acquaintance with him. On 22/09/2016 being Thursday there was holiday. She went to her uncle's house to watch T.V. Accused Swiden came there and asked drinking water, she gave him drinking water. 16] Her evidence shows that on 23/09/2016 when she was retuning from school at about 1.15 p.m. Swiden met her on the way and called her in the garden near St. Joseph High School. She went there at about 7.00 p.m. and he told that he likes her and that “Tula baghitlya shivay mala chain padat nahi”. He told to come to port daily and in garden tried to take kiss. He had taken her forcibly near him. Her evidence .....7/­ 7 Spl.POCSO Case 300/2016 shows that on 26/09/2016 accused was seeing her. She informed the incident to her parents and complaint was lodged. She admitted that he her uncle employed accused on his boat. However, she denied that she was giving phone call to accused on the mobile of her brother. 17] The learned A.P.P. submitted that the evidence of victim Dolfina is sufficient to believe the act of sexual assault. On the other hand, learned defence sounsl submitted that the cell number does not belong to accused. She herself has come to the garden. He submitted that there was no force nor the act of sexual assault. He also submitted that the statement of Uncle who is examined as defence witness was not recorded and at the relevant time accused was on his boat. 18] It appears that the plea of alibi is taken. This aspect I am discussing after the evidence of P.W. Lavina. 19] P.W. Lavina stated that on 26/09/2016 when her daughter was coming from school accused was constantly seeing her. Her reported that one day accused asked for drinking water and that he told that he likes her. Her daughter also informed that accused called her near St. Joseph High School and tried to come near her and taken her kiss. The victim did not tell about the taking of kiss. 20] It may be noted that parents particularly mother of victim not only lodging the complaint but deposed before the .....8/­ 8 Spl.POCSO Case 300/2016 Court and normally this conduct requires consideration for the simple reason that the growing girl would not be exposed regarding the incident of chastity or modesty. 21] It may further be noted that mother was suggested that her daughter was liking accused. 22] So far as the spot is concerned, P.W.Rahul Jadhav proved spot panchanama Exh.10. He is also the witness on the point that on 29/09/2016 accused gave a memorandum that he will show the spot as per Exh.11 and shown spot for which the panchanama Exh.12 was drawn. This fact was not found much controverted. However, the learned defence counsel submitted that garden is a public place and there is always public visiting and there may be watchman also. The public garden or the municipal garden in the city of Thane suburb may be considered of a common knowledge for the reason that nobody generally would indulge, watching much less reporting to the police about any obscene act. 23] Now coming to the plea of alibi, the evidence of DP.W. Fanky Bhanga shows that he has employed the accused in his boat in August, 2016. Accused was attending regular on his boat. They attend sea at about 10.00 a.m. and returning at about 7.00 p.m. and accused was not on leave. He stated that on 3/11/2016 he has not gone to Uttan Sagari Police Station for recording statement. Assuming that he .....9/­ 9 Spl.POCSO Case 300/2016 employeed accused as labour on the boat, he has acquaintance with P.W. Dolfina. Even further assuming that he was attending boat from 10.00 a.m. to 7.00 p.m., but it is a private job and the evidence is not believable that on 22/09/2016 or 23/09/2016 or 26/09/2016 accused has had not seen the victim. The onus shifted on accused that he was not present either in garden, nor met victim Dolfina could not be found discharged. The defence found improbable. 24] The last witness is P.W. Jagdish Bangar, who being I.O. in crime No.I­72/2016 drawn the spot panchanama, recorded statement, memorandum and other panchanama and submitted charge­sheet. 25] I have discussed cell number mentioned in the complaint is not in the name of accused. That suggestion alone will not prove that he was not at all present in the garden, nor seen victim Dolfina or did not follow her. 26] Having considered the entire evidence on record, it appears that accused made sexual coloured remarks that “Tula Baghitlya shivay mala chain padat nahi”. It also appears that accused followed or tried to contact complainant despite her clear indication of disinterest. 27] The prosecution alleged that sexual assault prescribed in section 7 of the POCSO Act which requires that who ever intend touches vagina, penis, anus or breast of the .....10/­ 10 Spl.POCSO Case 300/2016 child or makes the child touch vagina, penis, anus or breast or thus any other act with sexual intend which involves physical contact, is said to have committed sexual assault. 28] The provisions of section 11 (iv) of POCSO Act prescribe the sexual harassment and in this case repeatedly or constantly or following, watching either directly or through electronic means. In the present case there is no believable evidence about cell phone, call details much less crtificate under section 65B of the Indian Evidence Act. At the same time, the evidence of complainant is believable that accused was following her when she was coming from school/watching her directly. Therefore offence under section 354(A)and (D) of I.P.C. and section 11(iv) of the POCSO Act are attracted in the present case and the offence under those section only in view of the evidence particularly of victim is found proved and not under section 7 of POCSO Act. 29] It is here I have heard the accused on the point of sentence. He submitted that his father is dead, mother is old and has to do labour work. He is unmarried. 30] Learned A.P.P. submitted that maximum punishment be imposed. The defence counsel also submitted that he was in jail for four months. In the circumstances, considering facts and request I am of the opinion following sentence will be just and proper :­ .....11/­ 11 Spl.POCSO Case 300/2016 ORDER 1] Accused Swiden Greshan Colaso is convicted for the offence punishable under section 354(A) (D) of I.P.C. as per sec. 235(2) of Cr.P.C. and sentence to suffer S.I. for one year. 2] Accused is also convicted for the offence punishable under section 11(iv) 12 of POCSO Act as per section 235(2) of Cr.P.C. and sentence to suffer S.I. for one year. 3] Substantial sentences to run concurrently. 4] Set off be given to him under section 428 of Cr.P.C. for the period he under gone in jail i.e. from 26/09/2016 to 12/01/2017. 5] Accused is acquitted for the offence punishable under section 7 and 8 of POCSO and under section 506 of I.P.C. as per section 235(1) of Cr.P.C. 6] Accused to surrender his bail bond. Thane. (M.M.Walimohammed) Dt. 16/03/2017. Additional Sessions Judge­6, And Spl. Judge, POCSO Thane. ...../­

Criminal Misc. Application No. 431of 2015 Sushant Vijay Gaikwad. .. Applicant versus The State of Maharashtra Through Kalwa P.S. .. Non-Applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 1] This is an application moved for relaxation of conditions imposed while allowing the Anticipatory Bail Application No. 719/2015. 2] Heard advocate Mrs. Rohini Gavande for applicant and A.P.P. Mrs. R.A. Navale for State. 3] Upon hearing and perusal of the documents filed with the application, it appears that the applicant/accused had moved anticipatory bail application No. 719/2015 being apprehending his arrest in connection with C.R.No.I-114/2015 registered with Kalwa Police Station for offence punishable under section 452, 342, 354, 376(c), 506 of I.P.C. and section 8 Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (In short P.O.C.S.O.) It is matter of record that the application filed by the applicant for anticipatory bail was allowed by order dt. 05.09.2015 and directed to furnish P.R.Bond of ₹ 15,000/- with one surety in the like amount in the event of his arrest and he was further directed to attend the concerned police station on evey Tuesday between 3.00 p.m. to 5.00 plm. and also directed to co-operate with the investigating machinery. 4] The Ld. Counsel for the applicant submitted that since the interim orders, the accused is regularly attending Kalwa Police Station and marking his presence and also maintained the diary in this respect. She further submitted that due to frequent attendance the applicant could not attend his office regularly and it is difficult to take leave from his office and therefore, he was compelled to resign from the office. She submitted that since about a year chargesheet is not submitted and prayed for relaxation of the condition to attend the concerned office in every week. 5] Per contra, Ld. A.P.P. opposed the application submitting that the investigation is still in progress and chargesheet will submit within few days and prayed for rejection of the application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of the say filed by the investigating officer below Exh.7, it clearly transpired that the chargesheet is not submitted till today. The F.I.R. is registered on 12.03.2015 and applicant is protected by the interim order dt. 20.0.3.2015 and since then he is attending the police station as per the direction of the Court and the said order is confirmed on 05.09.2015. Further the applicant produced on record the extract of diary showing his regular attendance at the Kalwa Police station. The say filed by the investigating officer did not disclose any convincing reason for delay in filing the chargesheet. Therefore, for the default of the investigating officer, the applicant can not be allowed to suffer and I found substance in the submissions of the Ld. Counsel of the applicant that due to regular attendance of the accused on the working day i.e. Tuesday, it affects his service. Therefore, in the peculiar facts of case, I do not find any impediment for modifying and relax the condition of the attendance. Hence, I pass following order ORDER 1] The application is allowed. 2] The condition imposed in A.B.A. No. 719/2015 about attendance of concerned police station on every Tuesday between 3.00 p.m. to 5.00 p.m. is hereby modified to the extent that the applicant shall attend the police station as and when called by the investigating officer. Thane. Date : 29.01.2016. (Ms.U.M.Nandeshwar) Additional Sessions Judge-1, Thane.

1 Bail No.2949/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) Criminal Bail Application No. 2949/2015 Nasreen Mohammed Mulla .. Applicant (Spelled as Nasreen Khatoon Abdul Sattar Sardar in Remand Report). versus The State of Maharashtra Through Narpoli Police Station .. Non-applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 1] By this application, applicant is seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C., who was arrested on 18.11.2015 by Narpoli Police Station in connection with C.R.No.I-519/2015 registered for an offence punishable under section 366A, 370A, 370(2)(3)(4) of I.P.C. and section 4, 8, 17 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act), and section 3, 4, 5, 7, 9 of Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act (hereinafter in short I.T.P.A.) 2] Heard learned advocate Mr. Swapnil Patil for the applicant/accused and learned A.P.P. Mrs.R.A. Navale for State assisted by the advocate for original complainant. I.O. present. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 18.11.2015 at the instance of the informant Vikas Suresh Gupta, social worker, with an indictment that he received secret 2 Bail No.2949/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) information about prostitution being carried out at Sun Lodging and Boarding, opposite to Rajlaxmi Complex, Old Agra road, Kalher, Bhiwandi. Therefore, in turn he conveyed the information to the police and accordingly the raid was conducted at Sun Lodging and Boarding where nine accused were found procuring victims for prostitution and from there seven accused were arrested and two victims were rescued. 4] The learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant/accused is falsely implicated. He submitted that only role assigned to the present applicant is that she is sister of one of the accused and sent her for prostitution by rickshaw. He further submitted that the applicant was not arrested from the spot. However, she was called in the police station and she was shown as arrested. He further submitted that the victim is of 18 years age and therefore, the provisions of P.O.C.S.O, Act are not applicable and provisions of PITA Act are also not applicable. He further submitted that other accused are released on bail and accused is entitled on parity. She is ready to abide by any conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing her on bail. 5] The learned A.P.P. opposed the application on the ground that the applicant is involved in serious offence. She submitted that the applicant herself was indulging her minor sister in prostitution and she was doing the work knowingly and keeping the earning with her. She submitted that the victim-girl clearly stated the name of the present applicant in her statement recorded under section 164 of Cr.P.C. She is the main accused and therefore, parity isnot applicable to her. The investigation is in progress. There are chances of 3 Bail No.2949/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) tampering the witnesses and there is possibility of accused repeating the offence if released on bail and prayed for rejection of application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R. it appears that seven accused were arrested during the raid which was conducted on information that prostitution is carried out at Sun Lodging and Boarding. The role of the present applicant appears from the F.I.R. that she is the sister of one of the victim-girl and pushed her in the prostitution. Even the statement of the victim-girl under provisions of section 164 of Cr.P.C. is recorded wherein also she clearly stated that her sister i.e. the present applicant forced her for prostitution and sent her there with one autorickshaw driver. Thus, there is prima facie against the accused. The parity is not applicable, as the role of the accused who are released on bail is different and the present applicant is the main accused. The investigation is still in progress. Two accused are still absconding. The apprehension of Ld. A.P.P. about tampering of witnesses is well founded. Hence, this is not an appropriate stage and no case is made out by the applicant to release the accused on bail. Hence, I pass the following order. ORDER The application stands rejected. There are chances of tampering the witnesses and there is possibility of accused repeating the offence if released on bail and prayed for rejection of application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R. it appears that seven accused were arrested during the raid which was conducted on information that prostitution is carried out at Sun Lodging and Boarding. Prima facie no direct link of the accused appears to connect him with the alleged offence and he was found outside the premises of lodge. The applicant is behind bars since one month. The material part of investigation in respect of present applicant appears to have completed. No purpose would be served by further incarceration of applicant-accused. The object of bail is neither preventive nor punitive but to secure the presence of accused at the time of trial. The apprehension of A.P.P. can be addressed by imposing stringent conditions. Hence, I pass the following order - ORDER 1) The application is allowed. 2) Applicant Manoj Pawan Gupta be released on bail on her executing P.R. Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act), Thane.
