There is no reason to tell lie and prosecution has proved the case. On the other hand, learned defence counsel submitted that there was dispute between family members, he is falsely involved. He submitted that CC TV footage is not collected, call details are not proved and finally submitted that independent witnesses are not examined. 12] In these circumstances following points arise for my determination and I record my finding to them for the reasons mentioned hereinafter :­ Sr. POINTS FINDINGS No. 1] Whether prosecution proved that in In the between November, 2014 to affirmative. 04/04/2016 within the house of complainant at Vartaknagar within the jurisdiction of Vartaknagar Police Station victim Swati tried to contact to foster personal interaction, despite clear indication of her disinterest ? 2] Whether prosecution proved that In the on the said date, time and place affirmative. and during the course of same transaction accused insulted the modesty of victim Swati Gaste aged 13 years by blowing whistle and .....5/­ 5 Spl.POCSO Case 297/2016 making some call ? 3] Whether prosecution proved that In the on the said date, time and place affirmative. and during the course of same transaction accused committed sexual assault ? 4] What order ? 1 Bail No. 3026/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) Criminal Bail Application No.3026/2015 Vajid Rahamad Ali alias Sheikh .. Applicant versus The State of Maharashtra Through Vartaknagar Police Station .. Non­applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 By this application the applicant is seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. who was arrested on 04.10.2015 by Naupada Police Station in connection with C.R.No.I­545/2015 registered for an offence punishable under section 363 of I.P.C. and section 4, 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as P.O.C.S.O. Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Mr. Kanhere for the applicant/ accused and learned A.P.P. Mrs. Navle for State. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 04.10.2015 at the instance of the informant/mother of the victim­girl with an indictment that her daughter/victim­girl aged 17 years was kidnapped by accused. Therefore, the report was lodged. 4] The learned Counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant­accused is falsely implicated. He submitted that the applicant and victim­girl were having love affair which was not liked by the mother of the victim­girl. Even in F.I.R. itself there is mention that informant found her daughter and accused together, she 2 Bail No. 3026/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) objected for that and thereafter settled the marriage of her daughter with another boy which was scheduled on 10.11.2015. The learned counsel further submitted that as the victim­girl was not willing to marry with another boy, she on her own left the house and accused did not kidnap her or induce her to leave the house. He submitted that the accused is behind bar since tow months. The investigation is almost completed. The accused is ready to abide any conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing him on bail. 5] Per contra, the learned A.P.P. opposed the application only on the application that the victim­girl is minor and the accused is involved in serious offence. There are chances of tampering with witnesses and prayed for rejection of application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R., it appears that the victim­girl is aged about 17 years and from F.I.R. itself it is clear that she was acquainted with accused and having friendship with him which was objected by the informant and therefore, her marriage was settled with another boy which was scheduled on 10.11.2015. Thereafter, on 03.10.2015 informant did not find her daughter in the house and therefore on suspicion she lodged complaint against the accused. The learned counsel for accused also made submission that now the victim­girl is already married. The accused is a young boy of 21 years and is behind bars since two months. Though statutory period for filing the charge­sheet is completed, till today the charge­sheet is not filed and thus the accused is otherwise also entitled for statutory bail under section 167(2) of Cr.P.C. The object of bail is neither punitive or preventive 3 Bail No. 3026/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) but to secure the present of the accused at the time of trial. The applicant is ready to abide by the conditions imposed by the Court. In such circumstances the apprehension of learned A.P.P. about tampering of witnesses can be addressed by imposing suitable conditions. Hence, I pass the following order ­ ORDER 1) The application is allowed. 2) Applicant namely Vajid Rahamad Ali alias Sheikh be released on bail on his executing P.R. Bond of ₹ 15,000/­ [rupees fifteen thousand only] with one local surety in the like amount on the following conditions ­ A] Applicant shall attend the concerned police station on every Sunday between 10.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon till filing the charge­sheet. B] Applicants shall co­operate in investigation and shall not tamper with prosecution witnesses. C] Applicant shall furnish his and his two blood relatives' address proofs and contact numbers and he is duty bound to inform I.O. and Court about the change of address, if any. D] Applicant shall not contact victim­girl or any other witnesses in any manner. Thane. Date : 07.12.2015. (Ms. U.M. Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act), Thane.

1 Bail No.3029/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) Criminal Bail Application No. 3029/2015 Jyoti Tripad Madhel .. Applicant versus The State of Maharashtra Through Narpoli Police Station .. Non-applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 1] By this application, applicant is seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C., who was arrested on 18.11.2015 by Narpoli Police Station in connection with C.R.No.I-519/2015 registered for an offence punishable under section 366A, 370A, 370(2)(3)(4) of I.P.C. and section 4, 8, 17 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act), and section 3, 4, 5, 7, 9 of Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act (hereinafter in short I.T.P.A.) 2] Heard learned advocate Mr. Eknath Phad for the applicant/accused and learned A.P.P. Mrs.R.A. Navale for State assisted by the advocate for original complainant. I.O. present. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 18.11.2015 at the instance of the informant Vikas Suresh Gupta, social worker, with an indictment that he received secret information about prostitution being carried out at Sun 2 Bail No.3029/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) Lodging and Boarding, opposite to Rajlaxmi Complex, Old Agra road, Kalher, Bhiwandi. Therefore, in turn he conveyed the information to the police and accordingly the raid was conducted at Sun Lodging and Boarding where nine accused were found procuring victims for prostitution and from there seven accused were arrested and two victims were rescued. 4] The learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant-accused is falsely implicated. He submitted that only role assigned to the present applicant is that she is mother of one of the victim-girl and it is alleged that the amount of ₹ 74,000/0 was found with her. He further submitted that infact, the victim is of 18 years age and therefore, the provisions of P.O.C.S.O, Act are not applicable and provisions of PITA Act are also not applicable. He further submitted that other accused are released on bail and accused is entitled for parity. She is ready to abide by any conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing her on bail. 5] The learned A.P.P. opposed the application on the ground that the applicant is involved in serious offence. She submitted that the applicant herself was indulging her minor daughter in prostitution and she was doing the work knowingly and keeping the earning with her. She submitted that the amount of ₹ 74,000/- and one Nokia mobile was seized from her during her personal search. She is the main accused and therefore, parity is not applicable to her. The investigation is in progress. There are chances of tampering the witnesses and there is possibility of accused repeating the offence if released on bail and prayed for rejection of 3 Bail No.3029/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R. it appears that seven accused were arrested during the raid which was conducted on information that prostitution is carried out at Sun Lodging and Boarding. The role of the present applicant appears from the F.I.R. that she is the mother of one of the minor victim-girl and pushed her in the prostitution. The applicant was arrested from the spot and the amount of ₹ 74,000/- and one Nokia Mobile was seized from her during her personal search when the trap was laid. Even the statement of the victim-girl under provisions of section 164 of Cr.P.C. is recorded wherein also she clearly stated that her mother i.e. the present applicant forced her for prostitution. Thus, there is prima facie against the accused. The investigation is still in progress. Two accused are still absconding. The parity is not applicable as the role of the accused who are released on bail is on different footing and they were not arrested from spot and the present applicant is the main accused. The apprehension of Ld. A.P.P. about tampering of witnesses is well founded. Hence, this is not an appropriate stage and no case is made out by the applicant to release the accused on bail. Hence, I pass the following order. ORDER The application stands rejected. Thane. Date : 29.01.2016. (Ms.U.M. Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act), Thane.

CNR NO.MHTH01­008102­2018 co­operate in investigation. Therefore, he prays for bail. Hence this application. 4] Called say of Investigating Officer and Ld. A.P.P. .. 1 .. Anticipatory Bail No.3067/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1.) Anticipatory Bail Appln No.3067/2015. Shankar Narsaya Gundala ... Applicant versus State of Maharashtra (Through Shantinagar Police Station) ... Non­applicant. ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 1] This is an application moved by applicant for his release on anticipatory bail under section 438 of Cr.P.C., being apprehending his arrest in C.R.No.I­194/2015 registered at Shantinagar Police Station for the offence punishable under section 376 read with section 34 of I.P.C. and section 3, 4 of Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act) and also under section 3, 4, 5 of Maharashtra Prevention and Eradication of Human Sacrifice and Other Inhuman, Evil and Aghori Practices and Black Magic Act, 2013 (hereinafter in short Black Magic Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Mr. G.B.Chavan for the applicant/accused and learned A.P.P. Mrs. Navale for State. I.O. present. Perused case papers. .. 2 .. Anticipatory Bail No.3067/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1.) 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 29.07.2015 at the instance of informant/victim­girl aged about 17 years 10 months with an indictment that since 05.07.2015 to 14.07.2015 her father Aklal Ansari with common intention with other accused persons including present applicant, married informant with one Baba Salim Ansari who assured them of causing rainfall of money ( iS'kkpk ikÅl ) and Baba Salim then committed sexual assault on her and other accused persons facilitated for marriage of minor girl and abetted black magic. 4] The learned Advocate for the applicant submitted that the applicant is falsely implicated. He submitted that the applicant is a senior citizen aged about 69 years and he was ex­councillor. He submitted that the father of victim was once working with the applicant and applicant attended the marriage of victim only on the invitation of his employee i.e. father of victim­girl. Except that he has no role in the present offence. He further submitted that after the marriage of victim with Baba Salim, the applicant immediately left for his native place and has no concern with the sexual assault on the victim­girl. The learned counsel for applicant also submitted that the applicant was at his native place and therefore, he was not knowing about involvement of his .. 3 .. Anticipatory Bail No.3067/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1.) name in the present offence and he was not absconding. After filing the charge­sheet against other accused, he came to know about his implication in the present crime. He further submitted that the supplementary statement of the victim­girl was recorded wherein she stated that the house where the marriage was performed was not of the present applicant and only role assigned to the present applicant in her statement recorded under section 164 of Cr.P.C. is that he was present for the marriage as a witness. He thus submitted that the arrest of the accused would cause loss to his reputation and malign his image in the society. He has no criminal antecedents. He is ready to co­operate in investigation. His custodial interrogation is not necessary and prayed for protection of applicant by grant of anticipatory bail. 5] The learned A.P.P. strongly opposed the application submitting that the F.I.R. speaks in volume. She submitted that name and role of present applicant is clearly mentioned in the F.I.R. It is the applicant who facilitated the marriage. She further brought to my notice that the statement of one witness Dattu Malaiyya Kassa recorded under section 164 of Cr.P.C. submitting that he has stated before the learned Magistrate that it is the applicant who facilitated this marriage by introducing the girl as per the .. 4 .. Anticipatory Bail No.3067/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1.) demand of Baba Salim and he even was present during the marriage which was performed at about 12.45 in the midnight by Kazi. He also stated that when Salim took the girl upstairs, at that time even the victim­girl's father questioned him and on that the present applicant threatened him to keep mum and even there was quarrel between applicant and father of the girl. After 20 to 25 minutes the applicant called Salim Baba and Baba informed him that there was no rainfall of money. She thus submitted that the applicant was all the time present during the marriage and even thereafter and he made available the girl for the marriage. She further submitted that the offence is very serious and the accused is equally responsible for the offence. All the accused conspired together for commission of said offence. Though charge­sheet in respect of other accused is submitted, the custodial interrogation of the present applicant is necessary and prayed for rejection of the application. 6] While considering the anticipatory bail application, I have to consider some important factors like seriousness of the offence, the manner of commission of offence, its impact on society, necessity of custodial interrogation, criminal antecedents of the applicants, the .. 5 .. Anticipatory Bail No.3067/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1.) possibility of tampering of witnesses and at the same time, I have to consider the possibility of false implication and personal liberty of the applicants. 7] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R. and case papers it appears that the victim­girl lodged the report on 29.07.2015 wherein she had stated that her father is loom worker and having poor financial condition. Once her father's friend had been to their house and informed that there is one Maharaj and Baba who cause rain shower of money. It was also informed to them that Baba Salim Ansari staying at Diwanshah Dargah road, Bhiwandi perform rituals for having rain shower of money and for that purpose he requires unmarried virgin girl with long hair. Informant's father forced for the marriage. On 07.07.2015 one Shankar i.e. present applicant, and one Arun had been to their house and told that the informant has to marry with Baba Salim and he would have the rain shower of money and thereafter she could obtain Talakh from him and for that purpose they have to go to Temghar for the performance of Nikah. When informant's father took her to Temghar, at that time present applicant Shankar alongwith 3 to 4 other persons were present. At about 11.00 p.m. Baba Salim came there and at about 1200 hours their marriage was performed by Moulana in presence .. 6 .. Anticipatory Bail No.3067/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1.) of Shankar i.e. present applicant and Arun and their 3 to 4 friends. Thereafter, Salim took the informant/victim in another block and then he pretended of playing magic and uttered chants and then he told her that the time has lapsed and therefore, now there would be no rain shower and established physical relationship with her by saying that she is his wife. At about 2.30 they went downstairs where her father was there and Salim told that there was no rain shower and therefore her father took her home. For about two days Salim did not come to take her. Therefore, the informant suspected foul play and by searching the address of accused Salim had been to 'Diwanshah Dargah' but Salim was not found there. On 14.07.2015 Salim's friend brought Talakhnama stating that Salim has pronounced Talakh to her and thereafter the victim lodged the report. 8] From bare perusal of F.I.R. it prima facie appears that it was the present applicant who introduced the victim as the girl as per the requirement of Baba Salim and he was present at the place where the marriage was performed by Moulana and applicant even signed the Nikahnama as a witness. It is also pertinent to note that said Nikah was performed at midnight at 1200 hours. Performing Nikah at such odd hours itself shows that the applicant was having .. 7 .. Anticipatory Bail No.3067/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1.) knowledge about the act and he conspired with the main accused and other accused. Thus, his intention is also transpired from his conduct. Further, though it was strongly urged by the counsel for the applicant that applicant was only present during the marriage and he immediately left the place for going to his native place, however, it is only the stage of investigation and the investigation in respect of present applicant is still underway as the applicant was not available for inquiry. Furthermore, the statement of the witness Dattu Malaiyya Kassa clearly transpires the role of the present applicant and he stated the role of the applicant in detail in respect of making available the girl, facilitating the girl, his presence during the marriage and even thereafter and he even threatened and quarreled with the father of the victim­girl when some queries were put to him. Though the charge­sheet in respect of other accused is submitted, however, the investigation in respect of present applicant is still going on. 9] The Black Magic Act enacted with an object act to bring social awakening and awareness in the society and to create a healthy and social environment with the view to protect the common people in the society against the evil and sinister practices thriving on ignorance, and to combat and .. 8 .. Anticipatory Bail No.3067/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1.) eradicate human sacrifice and other inhuman, evil, sinister and aghori practices propagated in the name of so called supernatural or magical powers or evil spirits commonly known as by conman with sinister motive of exploiting the common people in the society and thereby destroying very social fiber of the society; and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. The allegations are very serious and having grave impact and therefore, the thorough investigation with the custody of accused is very much necessary. Further, looking to the conduct of applicant of eluding himself from clutches of investigating machinery for about 4­5 months, he is not at all entitled for protection from this Court. Therefore, I pass following order ­ ORDER The application is rejected. Date : 16.12.2015. (Ms. U.M. Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act), Thane.

Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­008238­2016 Special Case (POCSO) No. 310/2016 Received on : 05.12.2016 Registered on : 05.12.2016 Decided on : 20.12.2018 Duration : 2Ys. 0Ms. 15 Ds. IN THE COURT OF D.J.­1 & ADDL. SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE. (Presided over by Hemant M. Patwardhan) Special Case (POCSO) No. 310/2016 Exh.No.42 State of Maharashtra, (Through Navghar Police station) ..Complainant V/s. Ganesh Vithal Vadule. Age: 21 years, R/at. Medatiya Raviraj Complex, A/1, Vimalraj (Work in progress of construction), Ground floor, Ideal park, Mira road (East) ..Accused Appearance:­ DGP Shri. Londhe for the State. Advocate Shri. A.A. Dhumal for accused JUDGMENT (Delivered on this 20th day of December 2018) Accused Ganesh Vithal Vadule was facing trial under sections 376(2) (i) of Penal Code with Sec. 4 and 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 on following facts. 1 to 18 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­008238­2016 Special Case (POCSO) No. 310/2016 1] That on 07.09.2016, at about 5.00 hours and three days prior to it, at Medatiya Raviraj Complex, A/1, Vimalraj (Work in progress of construction) Ground floor, Ideal park, Mira road (East) Dist. Thane within jurisdiction of Navghar police station, Dist. Thane accused has committed rape on victim minor girl of 13 years old, repeatedly and as the girl was minor said act of the accused was considered to be with sexual intent of committing aggravated penetrative sexual assault of the victim. Thus, on complaint lodged by victim's father an offence punishable under aforesaid sections came to be registered against accused. On completion of investigation he was charge­sheeted. 2] My learned Predecessor was pleased to frame charge below Exh.10 and has certified that contents of it was read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. Accused has pleaded not guilty and claim to be tried. His defence was that of total denial and that he has been falsely implicated in the matter due to some quarrel between the accused and father of victim. 3] As the accused has claim to be tried, prosecution has then proceeded to examine complainant and father of the victim as PW1, victim as PW2, medical officer Dr. Narendra Baluram Kumar as PW3 and finally I.O. API Mr Prashant Subhash Shirke as PW4 respectively. After the evidence of the prosecution, statement of accused was 2 to 18 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­008238­2016 Special Case (POCSO) No. 310/2016 recorded wherein accused has reiterated his defence of his false implication on the ground of quarrel. 4] Arguments of rival advocates were heard. As per learned prosecutor the victim has not only deposed as to how accused has committed repeated sexual assaults on her but said deposition of the victim has been categorically substantiated by medical officer's evidence. Thus, according to learned P.P. act of the accused of threatening victim before committing sexual assaults are itself sufficient to inferred his intention of committing that act with sexual intend. According to learned P.P. though during arguments, defence has put defence of his false implication on the ground of quarrel, said defence was never referred to witnesses during their cross­ examination. According to him cross­examination only contains suggestion and said suggestion cannot be evidence, which is sufficient to discard deposition of prosecution witnesses. According to him thus, deposition of the witnesses are sufficient to establish the guilt of accused beyond reasonable doubt. He has therefore, requested to consider all these facts and hold accused guilty of the offence under both the said section. 5] Per contra, learned defence advocate has categorically pointed out that evidence of the victim is not supported by medical officer. Thus said fact itself is sufficient to discard allegations of the 3 to 18 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­008238­2016 Special Case (POCSO) No. 310/2016 prosecution. According to him the victim was not able to narrate the incident properly and the said has not been properly corroborated by other witnesses. Thus, defence of false implication of the applicant­ accused due to quarrel took place between him and father of the victim can be considered to be more probable than that of prosecution's case. According to him medical officer was not able to note down injuries on genital parts of victim which itself is against settled proposition and thus, on the basis of medical evidence it cannot be said that rape has been committed either once or repeatedly by the accused. He has then relied upon Judgment of Hon'ble Delhi High Court wherein reliance is placed on Judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court to substantiate that when medical evidence did not support prosecution it is not sufficient to convict the accused under section 376 of IPC. Learned advocate has therefore, requested to discard all the aforesaid evidence and requested to acquit accused from all the charges. 6] After having heard the rival advocates, I have gone through citations relied upon by the defence. On the basis of aforesaid rival arguments, following points arise for my consideration and I record my findings against each of them for the reasons noted below:­ S.N Points Findings 1] Does the prosecution prove that accused on 07.09.2016 at about 5.00 ..In the hrs. and three days before it, at Medatiya Raviraj Complex, A/1, negative. Vimalraj (Work in progress of construction), Ground floor, Ideal park, 4 to 18 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­008238­2016 Special Case (POCSO) No. 310/2016 Mira road (East), within jurisdiction of Navghar police station, Dist. Thane committed rape on victim, a minor aged 13 years repeatedly and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 376 (2)(i) of IPC? 2] Does the prosecution prove that accused on aforesaid dates time and ..In the place, committed aggravated penetrative sexual assault on victim, a affirmative minor aged of 13 years and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 4 under Sec. 4, 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, of POCSO Act 2012? only. 3] What order ? Accused is convicted as per final order. REASONS As to point nos. 1 to 3 :­ 7] In the instant case prosecution has come forward with allegations of accused having committed rape on the victim and as at the time of offence, victim was minor the act of the accused was also termed as aggravated penetrative sexual assault. Thus, prosecution was launched against accused person under 376(2)(i) of IPC read with section 4 and 8 of POCSO Act. Prosecution was thus, require to prove necessary ingredients of the said sections. Prosecution in order to prove it has examined aforesaid witnesses. Prosecution witnesses have accordingly and categorically deposed in terms of allegations of prosecution. Hence, on the basis of the said substantive evidence learned P.P. has requested to convict the accused. Said evidence thus needs to be scrutinized on background of the defence of the accused. 5 to 18 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­008238­2016 Special Case (POCSO) No. 310/2016 8] Material evidence in the matter was that of the victim as she herself was subjected to sexual assault. Though complaint was lodged by her father, it was on first hand information from the victim. Therefore, the material evidence is that of victim herself. On plain perusal of her deposition, it is apparent that though she was minor at the relevant time of evidence, considering that she is aware of sanctity of oath and was able to give rational answers to preliminary questions put forth to her, her evidence was recorded on oath. Then she has categorically deposed before this court that the accused was residing adjacent to her house and on 06.09.2016 had been to her house and had asked her to visit her house else threatened her to kill her parents. According to her, accused had sexual intercourse with her on four occasions prior to 06.09.2016. Thus, when she was caught in the house of accused on 07.09.2016 at 5.00 a.m. by her parents she had disclosed those facts of previous sexual intercourse with accused on 3­4 occasions and on her disclosure statement, her father had lodged complaint. Having regards to said fact her cross­examination was of material importance to disprove her allegations. On perusal of record it is apparent that an attempt was made by the defence to bring it on record that victim was never alone in the house to give an opportunity to accused person to commit sexual assault on her. However, said questions were put forth was not in any direct form 6 to 18 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­008238­2016 Special Case (POCSO) No. 310/2016 but just in indirect form by bringing the age of the sister on record. However, even if we considered that that age of her sister was around two years at the time of incident it is hard to accept that said sister of the victim would really create any obstacle in the act of the accused. Therefore, said fact though considered as it is then also it is no way favourable to accused persons. As court time is over adjourn till tomorrow. Thane (Hemant M.Patwardhan) Date: 19.12.2018 D.J.­1 & Additional Sessions Judge, Thane. 9] In the instant case prosecution was launched about incident dated 07.09.2016 wherein it is alleged by the prosecution that parents of the victim did not find victim on the spot where she was sleeping therefore, started searching for her and they found victim in hut of accused persons sleeping on the bed with accused. Therefore, parents made inquiries with the victim and then she has disclosed to them that accused himself had called her under a threat to kill them and after sexually assaulting her had threatened her not to disclose that fact to anybody else. She also appears to have disclosed that accused has committed rape on her on 3­4 occasions prior to said incident therefore, prosecution was actually launched. 7 to 18 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­008238­2016 Special Case (POCSO) No. 310/2016 However, as a matter of fact if evidence of the victim is considered as it is then she in categorical words has stated that on 07.09.2016 there were no physical relations between her and accused person. Thus, so far as allegation of having committed any sexual assault on 07.09.2016 due to the evidence of the victim, the prosecution case or allegation can be easily discarded. However, allegations were not restricted to incident dated 07.09.2016. Thus, court has to consider whether the allegations made by the victim about having subjected to sexual assault by accused person, the evidence of prosecutrix along with surrounding circumstances are required to be consider. 10] In the instant case the victim has categorically made reference of she being subjected to sexual assault or sexual intercourse on four occasions prior to the incident. As referred to above besides the victim there was no direct eye witness to the said incident. Thus, court has to consider surrounding circumstances and medical evidence brought before the court to substantiate the facts. On perusal of the medical evidence it is apparent that medical officer PW3 Dr. Narendra Baluram Kumar has categorically deposed that during the local examination of the victim he has found that hymen was not intact and old hymeneal tear was present 2 O'clock and 6 O'clock position. In order to get clarification as to what said position of 2 O'clock and 6 O'clock indicates, specific question was put to him wherein he has categorically opined that position of hymeneal tear as 8 to 18 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­008238­2016 Special Case (POCSO) No. 310/2016 2 O'clock and 6 O'clock suggest repeated sexual intercourse. On the basis of said opinion, learned P.P. has requested court to hold accused guilty of commission of rape as well. It was also pointed out to him that only suggestions were put forth to said medical officer that due to some physical activities or unhygienic condition there is likelihood of hymen not remaining intact and said suggestions were categorically denied. Thus, fact remains on record as opined by the medical office that victim was subjected to repeated intercourse or that possibility of sexual assault cannot be ruled out remain unchallenged on record. Therefore, if the said testimony of medical officer is considered then it is apparently sufficient to come to the said conclusion. 11] However, as referred to above court has to consider prosecution's evidence in the light of defence of accused persons. In present matter learned defence advocate has relied upon Judgment of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in case of Atender Yadav V/s. State Govt. of NCT of Delhi wherein Hon'ble their Lordship were dealing with matter of rape allegedly committed by the father on his own daughter wherein medical officer before Hon'ble their Lordship have also opined that hymen was not intact and on that basis learned trial Judge has considered prosecution as probable and has convicted the father. Appeal before Hon'ble their Lordship was then filed wherein Hon'ble their Lordship have discussed various legal aspects on 9 to 18 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­008238­2016 Special Case (POCSO) No. 310/2016 Medico Legal Points on opinion of authors like Dr. Modi, Dr. K.S. Narayan Reddy, Dr. R.M. Zhala and Dr. B.B. Raju. The important observations of Hon'ble their Lordship are based upon Modi's Medical Jurisprudence. Therefore, this court has to consider it. Hon'ble their Lordship in paragraph No. 56 of their Judgment by referring page no. 475 of Modi's Medical Jurisprudence has quoted :­ “In nubile virgins, the hymen as a result of complete sexual intercourse, is usually ruptured, having one or move radiate tears “Frequent sexual intercourse and parturition completely destroy the hymen, which is represented by several small tags of tissue, which are called carunculae hymenealis or myrtiformes.” “In small children, the hymen is not usually ruptured, but may become red and congested with the inflammation and bruishing of the labia. If considerable force is used, there is often laceration of fourchette and perinaeum.” ­ In the present case, no injury either healed or having any old scar marks etc. was present either on fourchette or on perinaeum” "The reason is obvious, medical jurisprudence evidences that in adolescent girls the hymen is situated relatively more posteriorly and for said reason there is a possibility of rape being committed without the hymen being torn; the converse whereof would be that if the hymen of an adolescent girl is torn due to rape, the penetration has to be a deep penetration. The medical jurisprudence guides that the labia majora are the first to be encountered by the male organ and they are subjected to blunt forceful blows, depending on the vigour and the force used by the accused and counteracted by the victim. The narrowness of the vaginal canal makes it inevitable for the male organ to inflict blunt, forceful blows on the labia and such blows lead to contusion because of looseness and vascularity. The feature of such contusion is revealed against the pink background of the mucous membrane dark red contusion being evident to the naked eye." 10 to 18 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­008238­2016 Special Case (POCSO) No. 310/2016 12] Sum and substance of the observations after having discussed aforesaid opinion of said well known author on Medical Legal Cases it was observed by Hon'ble their Lordship that it is the duty of the medical officer who has locally examined the victim to categorically give opinion about hymen stood ruptured at earlier or carried an old tear. Doctor himself has given his clear opinion that it was untouched for the reasons that such condition obviously relate to hymen. In the instant case doctor has not given any such opinion and thus, merely because doctor has opined on the basis of old tear position of 2 O'clock and 6 O'clock, victim cannot be said to be subjected to forcible intercourse by accused person. Therefore, on the basis of aforesaid facts it is difficult to accept that opinion of the doctor is sufficient to corroborate the victim's deposition. There is no record before the court about victim's complaint about her suffering any injury in her private part, any kind of bleeding or any vaginal discharge or suffering any kind of pain which could have call for urgent medical attention or upsetting her normal routine. If at initial stage if intercourse could have been committed forcibly all the said sufferings and bleeding or paining is bound to occur and in absence of any such complaint on part of victim it is difficult to say that she was really subjected to rape as alleged by him on 07.09.2016. 13] In the instant case allegations are not restricted to commission of rape but also prosecution has alleged that accused has 11 to 18 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­008238­2016 Special Case (POCSO) No. 310/2016 committed penetrative sexual assaults punishable under section 4 and 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 Act. On perusal of section 3 of said Act it appears that said section lays down as to what penetrative sexual assaults means. Said definition covers if a person penetrates his penis, to any extent, into the vagina, mouth, urethra or anus of a child or insertion to any extent any object or a part of the body not being the penis, into the vagina, the urethra or anus of child. It also speaks about manipulating of any part or application of his mouth to vagina or penis as the case may be with sexual intent. Wherein section 7 defines what sexual assault means. In the instant case if we consider the allegation of the victim that accused has actually committed sexual intercourse with her then apparently those allegations if considered as it is then will certainly come within purview of section 7 of POCSO Act. Though my learned Predecessor has framed charge both under section 4 and 8 of POCSO Act I do not find substance so far as it relates to section 8 of the Act is concerned. Therefore, allegation against Section 4 of the Act can be considered. 14] Intention of a particular person while committing assault of sexual nature is of material importance. In the instant case accused was aware that victim is child within the meaning of Act as she was below age of 18 years on the day of commission of offence and in spite of being aware of that fact he has forced her to come to 12 to 18 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­008238­2016 Special Case (POCSO) No. 310/2016 his own house under a threat to killing her parents. Therefore, victim has no other alternative being of very tender age to obey direction of accused person. Therefore, intention of the accused can be gathered from his act of directing the victim to come to his house during night hours by threatening the parents he intents to commit sort of sexual assault on the victim within the meaning of section 4 of the Act. Therefore, court has to consider the deposition of the victim so far as sexual assaults are concerned. 15] Though there was no injury found on the private part of the victim and though in view of the opinion of expert in the field like Dr. Modi, Dr. K.S. Narayan Reddy, Dr. R.M. Zhala and Dr. B.B. Raju mere fact that hymen was torn is not sufficient to inferred that rape has been committed but said evidence is sufficient to inferred that penetration must have been given by the accused either by inserting penis or any other part of his body therefore, only position of hymen was found 2 O'clock and 6 O'clock by the medical officer who has locally examined the victim. To consider completion of offence, within the meaning of section 3 of the Act, any sexual assault referred in any of the Clauses of definition is sufficient. The victim has categorically made reference of assaults being committed on 3­4 occasions by the accused. Surrounding circumstances like the victim was found in the hut of the accused on 07.09.2016 corroborate the allegation that accused must have called her under 13 to 18 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­008238­2016 Special Case (POCSO) No. 310/2016 the said threat and further during cross­examination of material witnesses there is nothing on record to disbelieve the version of the victim so far as penetrative sexual assaults are concerned. The defence has only put forth suggestion that accused has never committed any sexual assault on her. However, prior to the said suggestion direct question was put forth whether victim had informed to her parents about initial sexual assault on her and she has replied in negative with addition that she did not inform as accused has threatened her to kill her parents. 16] Surprisingly, even if said direct question's answer was totally against accused, learned defence advocate has not put forth any further suggestion denying that accused have never committed sexual assault or has threatened the victim as alleged by her. Hence, in absence of any such suggestions initial fact which was brought during cross­examination about specific act of accused of committing sexual assault remain intact and unshaken on record. Thus, if the substantive evidence of victim in examination­in­chief is considered which is then corroborated in cross­examination then in my opinion that substantive evidence in itself is sufficient to make out case under section 4 of POCSO Act. In such cases evidence of the victim must be given pre­dominant consideration without even corroboration, testimony of victim can be accepted. In the instant case particular victim has not only categorically made reference of 14 to 18 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­008238­2016 Special Case (POCSO) No. 310/2016 sexual assaults committed by accused but same has been corroborated by the cross­examination of the victim and by the deposition of medical officer. Having regards to these facts in my opinion allegations by the victim atleast penetrative sexual assaults are concerned can be said to be properly established. 17] Once court has come to the conclusion that prosecution has succeeded in establishing its case on the basis of substantive evidence then the court has to presume that accused has committed offence unless contrary is proved by taking recourse of section 29 and 30 of POCSO Act. Once that presumption is raised it is for the defence to disprove the allegations. In the instant case it was the defence of accused that he has been falsely implicated in the matter only because there was quarrel between the accused and the father of the victim that too under the influence of liquor for some previous reason. However, though said defence was argued nothing to that sort was brought on record to discard allegations of prosecution. Except suggestion in the cross­examination of the father of the victim i.e. PW1 that out of the rivalry he has implicated accused in this false case. Defence has even failed to put forth as what was the ground for rivalry between victim's father and the accused person during cross­ examination of PW1. Therefore, if we consider these facts then it is difficult to accept that substance has been brought on record which is sufficient to disprove the prosecution's case. Defence was never put 15 to 18 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­008238­2016 Special Case (POCSO) No. 310/2016 forth to material eye witness i.e victim during cross examination was restricted to denials and tutored by the other witnesses. Thus, there is also no consistency in the defence to accept it and to say that by said evidence, he has rebutted presumption under section 29 of Act. 18] If the defence has failed to rebut that presumption, again another presumption under section 30 of POCSO Act has to be raised against accused and once that presumption is raised against accused court has to conclude that offence was committed having mental state of sexual intention while committing the sexual assault on the victim. Thus, there appears to be no ground to implicate the accused falsely in the matter. Having regards to these facts the court has to accept the consistent evidence of the prosecution so far as assault as defined under section 3 of POCSO Act is concerned. Therefore, I do not hesitate to record my findings so far as point no.2 is concerned in affirmative and no.1 in negative. As I recorded my findings so far as allegations of prosecution under POCSO Act are concerned in affirmative I am required to defer the Judgment for hearing accused on the point of sentence. Needless to mention that by recording my findings against point no.2 in affirmative, I hold that accused guilty for offence punishable under section 4 of the Act. 19] Heard accused on the point of sentence. Accused has submitted to take lenient view and impose minimum sentence as he 16 to 18 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­008238­2016 Special Case (POCSO) No. 310/2016 still maintains that he has not committed any offence. Also, heard learned advocate of the accused who has submitted that accused is only 21 years old therefore, leniency be shown to him and minimum punishment be awarded. Per contra, learned DGP has submitted that incidences of committing crime against child are increasing in the society therefore, in order to give proper message to the society in such matters, determent punishment for imprisonment for life be imposed. After having heard the rival advocates and having consider facts and circumstances in which offence has been committed in my opinion the submissions of the learned advocate for the accused particularly considering age of the accused to show leniency can be accepted. To my mind minimum prescribed punishment provided under said Act will suffice the purpose. Accordingly, the order. ORDER 1] Accused Ganesh Vithal Vadule is hereby convicted for the offence punishable under section 4 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act 2012 and he is sentenced to suffer R.I. for seven years and shall pay fine of Rs.2000/­ i/d. to suffer further R.I. for two months. 2] Accused is hereby acquitted from the offence punishable under section 376(2)(i) of Indian Penal Code. 17 to 18 Judgment CNR No. MHTH01­008238­2016 Special Case (POCSO) No. 310/2016 3] Accused is in jail since the date of his arrest therefore, by exercising powers under section 428 of Cr.P.C. set off is granted for period already undergone by him. 4] Muddemal property viz. clothes of victim and accused being worthless be destroyed after appeal period. 5] Copy of the Judgment be provided to the accused free of cost. Thane (Hemant M.Patwardhan) Date: 20.12.2018 D.J.­1 & Additional Sessions Judge, Thane. 18 to 18

Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Mr. Jitendra Aheir for accused and learned A.P.P. Mrs. Kapre for State. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 16.09.2015 at the instance of the informant/victim-girl aged about 15 years with an indictment that accused enticed away the victim-girl and on the pretext of marriage, committed sexual assault on her and when she carries pregnancy, refused to marry her. 2 Bail No.3122/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) 4] The learned advocate for accused submitted that accused is falsely implicated. He submitted that this is the case of love affair though the victim girl was mentioned as 15 years in the F.I.R., in fact she has completed 18 years. As per her birth certificate and therefore, the provisions of P.O.C.S.O. Act are not attracted. He further submitted that the allegations of rape are from 2012 to 2015 but no complaint was ever filed. He further submitted that in fact, the accused and victim had performed their marriage in the temple which was not liked by parents of the girl and therefore, false F.I.R. was lodged. He further submitted that the investigation is completed and chargesheet is filed and the accused is behind bars since 4-1/2 months. He is ready to abide by conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing him on bail. 5] Per contra, the learned A.P.P. opposed the application submitting that the offence is serious in respect of minor girl. She further submitted that the victim is carrying pregnancy of 4 months. The accused and victim are staying in the same area and there are chances of pressurizing the victim-girl and tampering the witnesses and prayed for rejection of application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of case papers, it appears that it appears that the F.I.R came to be lodged with the serious allegations that the minor girl aged about 15 years enticed by the accused on the pretext of marriage, subjected to sexual assault from time time and because of 3 Bail No.3122/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) which she carries pregnancy and thereafter accused refused to marry. The Ld. counsel for the applicant filed birth certificate of the victim-girl on record wherein her date of birth is mentioned as 31.8.1997. However, the said certificate is a zerox copy and hence, cannot be considered at this stage. No doubt, there are very serious allegations against the accused and there is prima facie case against the accused as medical certificate also supports the version of victim-girl and also reveals that victim-girl carrying pregnancy of 04 months. However, now the investigation has been completed and the chargesheet in respect of the case recently submitted in the Court and registered as Spl. Case No. 262/2015. Thus, looking to the pendency of matters in this Court, the trial of case would take some considerable time. The object of bail is neither punitive nor preventive but to secure the present of the accused at the time of trial. No purpose would be served by further incarceration of the accused. The accused is not having any criminal antecedents. He is ready to abide by the conditions imposed by the Court. In such circumstances the apprehension of learned A.P.P. about tampering of witnesses can be addressed by imposing suitable conditions. Hence, I pass the following order - ORDER 1) The application is allowed. 2) Applicant namely Sanjay Suresh Govind be released on bail on his executing P.R. .. 1 .. Anticipatory Bail Appln. 3141/2015 Order below Exhibit 1 Anticipatory Bail Appln No.3141/2015 Mayuresh Shamkant Patil ... Applicant versus State of Maharashtra (Through Wada Police Station) ... Non­applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 1] This is an application moved by the applicant under section 438 of Cr.P.C. for his release on anticipatory bail alongwith application for grant of interim protection, being apprehending his arrest in connection with C.R.No.I­302/2015 registered by Wada Police Station for the offence punishable under section 376, 420 of I.P. Code and section 4 and 8 of P.O.C.S.O. Act. 2] Heard learned advocate Mr. Dhanajay Patil for the applicant/accused and A.P.P. Mrs. Navale for the State. 3] F.I.R. came to be registered on 18/09/2015 at the instance of informant / victim­girl with an indictment that since four years accused on pretext of performing marriage established physical relationship with her and latter refused to marry. 4] The learned Advocate for the applicant submitted that this is second anticipatory bail application moved by the applicant in the changed circumstances that the informant / victim filed an application in the police station for withdrawing her complaint .. 2 .. Anticipatory Bail Appln. 3141/2015 Order below Exhibit 1 alongwith her affidavit wherein she has stated that there was no physical relationship with accused and she is withdrawing all allegations. He submitted that while rejecting the first bail application, the Hon'ble Additional Sessions Court clearly observed that the provisions of P.O.C.S.O. Act are not applicable as the application of Act is from date 14.11.2012 and the alleged incident stated in the F.I.R. is of August or September, 2012. He, thus, submitted that the offence is out of purview of provisions of P.O.C.S.O. Act and victim was consenting party and as victim­girl herself wants to withdraw the complaint, the custodial interrogation of applicant is not necessary and the accused requires protection from this Court and prayed for interim protection till filing of the reply. 5] While considering the anticipatory bail application, I have to consider some important factors like seriousness of the offence, the manner of commission of offence, its impact on society, necessity of custodial interrogation, criminal antecedents of the applicants, the possibility of tampering of witnesses and at the same time, I have to consider the possibility of false implication and personal liberty of the applicants. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of the documents annexed with the application, it is evident that this is second anticipatory bail application moved by the present applicant. On perusal of the F.I.R. dated 17/09/2015 it appears that the informant is aged about 19 years and since about four years accused on the pretext of marriage established physical relationship with her. Thus, it clearly appears that .. 3 .. Anticipatory Bail Appln. 3141/2015 Order below Exhibit 1 the informant was aged below 16 years when the first act of physical relationship was committed and therefore, the consent of the victim at that material time is immaterial. Further, while rejecting the first anticipatory bail application the erstwhile Additional Sessions Judge in very clear term held that the investigation is at very per­matured stage and unless fair opportunity is granted to the investigating machinery to investigate thoroughly the matter will not come to logical end. Further, Learned A.P.P. rightly submitted that placing on record the affidavit of the victim­girl clearly shows an attempt on the part of the applicant about the tampering of evidence. 7] It prima­facie appears that the first Anticipatory bail Application No.2916/2015 filed by applicant was rejected on merit on 01/12/2015. And the so called application of withdrawal of report/complaint and affidavit appears to be of dated 08/12/2015 today i.e. on 16/12/2015 the applicant is again before this court praying protection. Which compel to draw only one inference that serious attempt of tampering by pressurizing victim was made by the applicant/accused or on his behest after rejection of first anticipatory bail application. In such peculiar facts of the case and looking to seriousness of offence and serious attempt of tampering of evidence, the applicant is not at all entitled for interim protection at the hands of this Court. Granting protection in such peculiar facts of case would certainly convey very wrong massage in society to do any serious crime against the women and then by adopting tactics to file her affidavit before police and be scout free from the clutches of investigating agency. This would be sheer misuse of court proceedings .. 4 .. Anticipatory Bail Appln. 3141/2015 Order below Exhibit 1 and such practice is required to be deprecated. The main (second) application for anticipatory bail being devoid of merit also does not sustain and is liable to be rejected at threshold. Hence, I pass following order ­ ORDER The application stands rejected. Date : 16.12.2015. (Ms.U.M.Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act) Thane.

Non-applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 1] This is an application moved by the accused in person seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. who was arrested on 25.11.2015 by Mira Road Police Station in connection with C.R.No.I-387/2015 registered for an offence punishable under section 376, 323, 504, 506 read with section 34 of I.P.C. and section3, 4, 5(f)(l)(m) and 6 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as P.O.C.S.O. Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Mr. N.M.Mote for accused and learned A.P.P. Mrs. Kapre for State. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 23.11.2015 at the instance of the informant / mother of victim-girl who is aged about 9 years with an indictment that victim-girl is sexually assaulted by three teachers of her school since year 2014 by calling her in different classrooms and by .. 2 .. Bail No.3161/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) threatening to kill her and her parents if she disclose the incident to anybody. During investigation it was revealed that the present applicant-accused aided the principal accused in commission of crime. 4] The learned advocate for accused submitted that the accused is falsely implicated. He submitted that the applicant-accused is a lady attendant in school bus and she was not allowed to enter in school premises. He further submitted that she was purely appointed on temporary basis and since her appointment there is no complaint against her of whatever nature. He further submitted that the name of present applicant is included belatedly. Even in the first and second remand report there is no mention about the role of the present applicant. She has no personal contact with the victim. It is further submitted that the applicant was in police custody for five days and nothing incriminating was seized at her instance. She is no way connected with the crime. Investigation is practically completed. She is permanent resident of Dahisar, Mumbai and is ready to abide any conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing her on bail. 5] Per contra, the learned A.P.P. strongly opposed the application submitting that the offence is serious. The victim is of very tender age. She submitted that the applicant-accused is lady attendant in school bus and she used to take the victim to the room where the three .. 3 .. Bail No.3161/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) teachers of the school alterately sexually assaulted the victim-girl. The victim girl identified the applicant from among the other lady attendants as the lady who used to take her to the room. She submitted that girl student was sexually assaulted in school premises. The investigation is in progress. There are chances of tampering the witnesses and prayed for rejection of application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of case papers, it appears that the victim-girl is aged about 9 years and student of 4th Std. As victim-girl was avoiding to go to school and appeared to be frightened, therefore, her mother/informant inquired with her and on that, the victim-girl disclosed her ordeal that since she was in in 3rd Std. one lady attendant (Mavshi), whose name she was not knowing, used to take her to classroom, and there her P.T. , drawing and other teachers used to commit sexual assault on her and used to threaten her to kill her and her parents. Therefore, the report was lodged. Though name of present applicant-accused is not mentioned in the F.I.R., however, her role is clearly transpired in the F.I.R. The offence is very serious in nature as tender-age girl was sexually assaulted about a year in the school premises by three accused persons who are none else than teachers working in same school and the present applicant-accused who is lady attendant used to facilitate them for the said heinous crime. Even the victim-girl identified the present applicant- accused among the other lady attendants. Even in medical .. 4 .. Bail No.3161/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1) certificate the detail history about sexual assault by three teachers with the help of lady attendant is clearly mentioned. The investigation is in progress. Considering the seriousness of offence, the apprehension of learned A.P.P. about tampering of witnesses is well founded. Hence, no case is made out against the accused to release the applicant-accused on bail. I, therefore, pass the following order - ORDER The application is rejected. Thane. Date : 08.01.2016 (Ms. U.M. Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act) Thane.

It is contended that the applicant is falsely implicated. There was love affair between victim and the present applicant and victim herself has eloped away with the applicant. Previously also she has eloped away with the applicant. In 2016 FIR was lodged by the parents of the victim about kidnapping. After that victim came home on the same day. The prosecutrix had left her house as per own will and stayed with the applicant for about four months. 3. The prosecutrix is 17 years old and the applicant is 19 years old. The investigation is almost completed. There was love affair between applicant and the prosecutrix. The applicant is ready to abide by the conditions and face the trial. Therefore, he prayed for bail. 4. The applicant is produced copy of FIR and copy of letter given by the prosecutrix to Shree Nagar Police Station. In that she has mentioned that she is 18 years old and she has left the house by her own will because of harassment and beating of her parents and her parents had given false complaint against her. --2-- 5. Investigation Officer has given say at Exh.4. It is contended that the present applicant had kidnapped the minor victim aged 17 years old and took her at Shelu District Raigad and kept physical relation with her and made her pregnant for four months. Previously also the applicant had kidnapped the prosecutrix. Accordingly CR NO.515/2016 under section 363 of IPC and CR NO.I­72/2017 under section 363 of IPC was registered. Presented on : 16.12.2015 Registered on : 16.12.2015 Decided on : 27.10.2017 Duration : 01Y.10M.11D IN THE COURT OF SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE, AT : THANE. Presided over by S.C. Khalipe ­Additional Sessions Judge, Thane SPECIAL CASE NO.266/2015 Exh.No. The State of Maharashtra Through Rabale MIDC Police Station. ….. Prosecution V/s. 1. Sitaram Mallesh Kamble Age 27 years, Occ: Service. 2. Sahadev Anil Kadam Age 27 years, Occ: Service No.1 and2 residing at Room No.975, Diva Naka, Mahatma Gandhi Nagar, Rabale, Navi Mumbai. 3. Kusum Anil Kadam Adult, Occ:­Household R/at. Diva Naka, Mahatma Gandhi Nagar, Rabale, MIDC, Navi Mumbai. ...Accused. Offence punishable under Sections 509, 452, 294, 504, 506 read with 34 of Indian Penal Code and section 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act,2012. Appearance: A.P.P. Smt.Hiwrale for the prosecution. Advocate Shri. S. J. Patankar for accused. :J U D G M E N T: (Delivered on this 27th Day of October, 2017) The accused are charged for the offence punishable under sections 509, 452, 294, 504, 506 read with 34 of Indian Penal Code and section 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act,2012. 2. It is the case of prosecution that:­ On 19.09.2015 the victim aged 15 years was alone at home. At about 6.00 p.m. she was filling water from the tab connection outside of her house. At that time accused Nos.1 and 2 Sitaram Mallesh Kamble and Sahadev Anil Kadam entered into her house forcibly. The accused No.1 and 2 threatened the victim and accused No.1 Sitaram Kamble removed chain of his pant and shown his penis to the victim. The victim shouted, therefore, adjoining people gathered. The accused Nos.1 and 2 ran away from her house. The victim then narrated the incident to her neighbouring woman and also narrated to her mother. After that the victim, her mother and aunt were going to police station for lodging FIR. It is alleged that accused Nos.2 and 3 obstructed them on the road and threatened not to lodge FIR against them, otherwise they will kill them and they beat and assaulted them with fist blows. The victim thereafter went to Rabale MIDC police station and lodged FIR. 3. C.R.No.I­190/2015 was registered in Rabale MIDC police station and it is investigated by woman police officer Kunda N. Gawade. She prepared panchanama of the spot, recorded statement of witnesses, arrested three accused persons at different dates and collected bonafide certificate of the victim from her school and sent charge­sheet against three accused persons. 4. Charge was framed at Exh.17 against the accused persons under section 509, 452, 294, 504, 506 read with 34 of Indian Penal Code and section 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act,2012. They pleaded not guilty. 5. Considering the evidence on record following points arose for my determination. I have given its findings with reasons as under­ Sr.No Points Findings 1. Does prosecution prove that accused In Nos.1 and 2 on 19.09.2015 at about 6.00 Affirmative p.m., in furtherance of their common intention with intent to insult modesty of minor victim aged 15 years exhibited object i.e. penis with intent that the object shall be seen by the child and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 509 read with 34 of Indian Penal Code? 2. Does prosecution prove that accused In Nos.1 and 2 in furtherance of their Affirmative common intention committed house trespass by entering into the house of victim for committing any offence and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 452 read with 34 of Indian Penal Code? 3 Does prosecution prove that accused In Nos.1 and 2 in furtherance of their Negative common intention did any obscene act in public place and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 294 read with 34 of Indian Penal Code? 4 Does prosecution prove that accused In Nos.1 and 2 on the same date, time and Affirmative place, intentionally insulted the victim by abusing her in filthy language and gave her provocation to break public peace and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 504 read with 34 of Indian Penal Code? 5 Does prosecution prove that accused In Nos.2 and 3 on the same date, time and Affirmative place, committed criminal intimidation by threatening the victim and witnesses to kill them and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 506 read with 34 of Indian Penal Code? 6 Does prosecution prove that accused In Nos.1 and 2 on the same date, time and Affirmative place, with sexual intent committed sexual assault by showing part of the body i.e. penis of accused NO.1 with intent that such part of body shall be seen by the child and thereby committed an offence under section 11 punishable under section 12 of the POCSO Act,2012? 7 What offences are proved and what order? Offence under section 509, 452, 504, 506 r/w 34 of IPC and section 12 of POCSO Act, 2012 proved and order as per final order. REASONS AS TO POINT NOS.1 TO 7:­ 6. To prove the offences prosecution has examined victim at Exh.22, one independent witness Manisha Balu Sonawane at Exh24 and P.W.3 Investigating Officer Kunda Namdev Gawade at Exh.25. 7. From the evidence on record it has come on record that the victim was learning in 10th standard in the year 2015. Her birth date is 24.04.2000. The Investigating Officer has also stated that she has collected the bonafide certificate of the victim which is at Article­1. As per that certificate the victim's birth date is 24.04.2000. The accused has not specifically challenged the birth date of the victim. Merely suggestion was given in the cross examination of Investigating Officer that the victim was more than 18 years i.e. denied. Therefore, the evidence of the victim and Investigating Officer in respect of birth date of the victim is liable to be accepted. So the prosecution has proved beyond doubt that the victim was below 18 years i.e. 15 years old at the time of incident, therefore, provision of POCSO Act, 2012 are applicable. 8. It is evident that on 19.09.2015at 6.00 p.m., the victim alone at home. Her family members gone for work. At 6.00 p.m, water came to the tab connection outside the house of the victim. So she attached pipe to the tab and taking water in the house. At that time accused Nos.1 and 2 forcibly entered into her house and asked whether water is coming fast. The victim replied that water is coming fast, but you should go out of the house, but accused Nos.1 and 2 did not turn out of the house. The accused No.1 Sitaram Mallesh Kamble removed the chain of his pant and showed his penis to the victim against her wish and will. The accused No.2 was also inside her house. He did not resist the accused No.1 from doing so. He did not turn out at that time from the house. The victim, therefore, shouted, adjoining people also collected there while the accused Nos.1 and 2 ran away from her house. 9. It has come on record that the victim immediately narrated the incident to her neighbouring woman Jyoti Chavan and after her mother came home she narrated the incident to her mother. After that the victim, her mother and aunt Chhaya Rathod were going to police station. At that time accused No.2 Sahadev Anil Kadam, his mother Suman Anil Kadam obstructed them on the road and threatened that don't go to the police station otherwise they will kill her and they beat her and her mother and aunt and assaulted them. Thereafter the victim went to the police station and lodged FIR vide Exh.23. 10. P.W.2 Manisha Balu Sonawane was residing adjoining to the house of victim. She knows the victim and her family members. She was working as Aanganwadi Teacher and also maid servant. After her work was over at 6.00 p.m., she was coming from her work. In the area of her house she saw people were running and shouting. She realized that something was happened, so she asked people what happened. She came to know that two boys, i.e. Sitaram Kamble and Sahadev Kadam entered into the house of victim and they sexually harassed her. 11. It has come on record that the victim has lodged FIR immediately on the day of incident at evening against three accused persons. There is no delay in lodging FIR and investigation was done by woman police officer Kunda Gawade. Panchanama of the spot was prepared in midnight of 19.09.2015 and 20.09.2015 vide Exh.26. Three accused persons were arrested on three different dates. Bonafide certificate of the victim was collected by the Investigating Officer. She recorded statement of witnesses as per their say. 12. In the cross examination of the witnesses it was suggested that they had not stated the colour of the clothes of the accused to the police. The court is of the view that the victim has given names of the accused in her FIR, therefore, colour of the clothes of the accused is not material. 13. It is suggested in the cross examination of witnesses that Jyoti Chavan had dispute with the accused and therefore as per say of Jyoti Chavan is false FIR was lodged. This suggestion is denied by the witnesses. The accused has taken vague defence. The accused have not suggested specifically what was the relation between Jyoti Chavan and accused and what was the reason behind the quarrel. If, there was any quarrel or dispute Jyoti Chavan would have taken the steps against accused she would not take the help of prosecutrix for lodging such serious nature offence. Therefore, the defence raised in the cross examination of the witnesses is not at all probable and believable. 14. The accused Nos.1 to 3 have not stated in their statement under section 313 of Cr. P.C., about any dispute between Jyoti Chavan and them. Nobody have stated why the witnesses have deposed against them. They have denied incriminating circumstances put to them, but they have not stated any reason why the false case has been lodged against them. They have not stated whether there was any dispute and what was the reason behind that. So no explanation is at all given by the accused about the case. 15. The court has come to the conclusion that evidence of the victim and witnesses have corroborative and trustworthy. There is no reason to disbelieve the victim. It is evidence that the incident is not witnessed by any witness. There is no eye witness to the incident. Of course the incident took place in the house of the victim and therefore, it is not probable of having witnessed by anybody. So the case is based upon sole testimony of the victim. The court is of the view that the victim's statement inspire confidence and there is no reason to disbelieve her. 16. Ld. A.P.P. relied upon the decision in case of Vijay Alias Chinee V/s. State of Madhya Pradesh (2010) 98 Supreme Court Cases 191. It was held that, “in rape case sole testimony of prosecutrix, if found to be worthy of credence and reliable, requires no corroboration. The court may convict the accused on the sole testimony of the prosecutrix.” In the present case also there is sole testimony of the victim. Her evidence is trustworthy and believable there is presumption under section 29 and 30 of POCSO Act. The accused have not rebutted the presumption. There was no friendship or enmity between them, therefore, I am of the view that the evidence of the prosecution is reliable, trustworthy and sufficient to prove the guilt of the accused. 17. The prosecution has proved ingredients of Section 509 of Indian Penal Code. Accused Nos.1 and 2 entered into the house of victim and accused No.1 showed his penis to the victim with intent to insult the modesty of the victim. This offence is also similar with the offence under section 11(i) Of POCSO Act,2012 As per provisions of section 42 of POCSO Act, 2012 accused are liable to be convicted for the offence either under Indian Penal Code or POCSO Act, 2012 which provides punishment which is greater in degree. 18. The offence under section 11 of POCSO Act is punishable under section 12 of the said Act. The punishment is imprisonment either description of a term which may extent to three years and shall also liable to fine and punishment under section 509 of Indian Penal Code is with simple imprisonment for a term which may extent to three yeas and also with fine. The court is of the view that the punishment provides under section 12 of POCSO Act, 2012 is greater in decree. Therefore, I convict the accused under section 12 of POCSO Act, 2012. 19. The prosecution has proved the ingredients of section 452 read with 34 of Indian Penal Code against accused Nos.1 and 2 they in furtherance of their common intention committed criminal trespass into the house of victim with intent to commit offence. 20. The court is of the view that the prosecution could not prove offence under section 294 of Indian Penal Code because it require obscene act in a public place. House of the victim is not a public place. The incident took place inside the house and it is not witnessed by any other person so it is not took place in public place and therefore, ingredients of offence under section 294 of Indian Penal Code are not at all proved against accused Nos.1 and 2. 21. It is proved by the prosecution that accused Nos.1 and 2 threatened the victim 'don't shout we will not leave you' coupled with showing penis by the accused No.1 to the victim. So it is intentional insult and thereby gives her provocation intending or knowing that it is likely that such provocation will cause her to break public peace. So ingredients of offence under section 504 of Indian Penal Code also proved against accused No.1 and 2. 22. It is proved by the prosecution that while the victim and her aunt and mother were going to police station accused Nos.2 and 3 Sahadev Anil Kadam and Kusum Anil Kadam obstructed them and threatened don't go to the police station, otherwise they will kill her and they assaulted her and beat her. So the prosecution has proved ingredients of offence under section 506 read with section 34 of Indian Penal Code. 23. I therefore come to the conclusion that prosecution has proved the offences under section 12 of POCSO Act, 2012 read with Section 509 read with 34 of Indian Penal Code and Section 452, 504 read with 34 of Indian Penal Code against accused Nos.1 and 2 and offence under section 506 read with section 34 against accused Nos.2 and 3. Date:27.10.2017 (S. C. Khalipe) Thane. Additional Sessions Judge, Thane. 24. Before passing sentence I heard accused on the point of sentence. They submitted that they have not committed any offence. 25. In reply Ld. A.P.P. Smt.Hiwrale submitted that the offences are proved beyond doubt, therefore, accused may be convicted with maximum punishment. 26. Considering the facts and circumstance of this case I do not found any mitigating circumstance. I am also view that due to the incident the minor victim is molested and therefore some compensation is required to be given to her out of fine amount. Accordingly, I pass following order which is sufficient for the ends of justice. ORDER 1] The accused Nos. 1 Sitaram Mallesh Kamble and No. 2 Sahadev Anil Kadam are convicted under section 235(2) of Criminal Procedure Code for the offence punishable under section 11 of POCSO Act, 2012 read with section 509 of Indian Penal Code and Section 452 read with 34 of Indian Penal Code and section 504 read with 34 of Indian Penal Code and accused Nos.2 Sahadev Anil Kadam and accused No.3 Kusum Anil Kadam are convicted for the offence punishable under section 506 read with 34 of Indian Penal Code. 2 The accused Nos.1 and 2 are sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for the period six months each and to pay fine of Rs.5,000/­ (Rupees five thousand only) each for the offence punishable under Section 11 of POCSO Act, 2012. read with section 509 of IPC, in default of payment of fine they shall suffer S.I. for the period of one month. 3. The accused Nos.1 and 2 are sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for six months each and to pay fine of Rs.3,000/­ each for the offence punishable under section 452 read with 34 of Indian Penal Code. In default of payment of fine they shall suffer S.I. for the period of one month. 4. The accused Nos.1 and 2 are sentenced to pay fine of Rs.500/­ each for the offence punishable under section 504 read with 34 of Indian Penal Code. In default of payment of fine they shall suffer S.I. for the period of 15 days each. 5. Accused No.2 Sahadev Anil Kadam and accused No.3 Kusum Anil Kadam are sentenced to pay fine of Rs.3,000/­ each for the offence punishable under section 506 read with 34 of Indian Penal Code. In default of payment of fine they shall suffer S.I. for the period of 15 days each. 6. After realization of fine amount the amount of Rs.15,000/­ (Rupees Fifteen Thousand Only) shall be paid to the victim P.W.1 as compensation after the appeal period and rest of the fine amount shall be credited to the State. 7. The accused Nos.1 and 2 are acquitted under section 235(1) of Cr.P.C of the offence charged under section 294 read with 34 of Indian Penal Code. 8. The sentence of imprisonment of above offences shall run concurrently. 9. The accused No.1 and 2 were arrested on 20.09.2015 and accused No.3 was arrested on 29.11.2015 and accused No.1 was released on bail on 14.10.2015, accused No.2 released on bail on 23.10.2015 and accused No.3 was released on bail on 17.12.2015 therefore set off be given under section 428 of Cr. P.C. for this period. 10. The Judgment is dictated and declared in open court. 11 The copy of Judgment shall be given to the accused free of costs. Thane. (S.C. Khalipe) Date:27.10.2017. Additional Sessions Judge,Thane.
