He is permanent resident of Thane and ready to abide by conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing him on bail. 5] The learned A.P.P. strongly opposed the application submitting that the F.I.R. speaks in volume. She submitted that though the name of the accused is not mentioned in the F.I.R., however, F.I.R. is not encyclopedia and role of present applicant is clearly mentioned in the F.I.R. The applicant/accused was present during the marriage and his name wass revealed during the investigation. He is the conspirator and having knowledge about the act. The accused was absconding for four months and thereafter he was arrested. One of the witness whose statement is recorded under section 164 of Cr.P.C. clearly stated the specific name of the present applicant/accused and his role.The investigation is in progress. There are chances of tampering of the witnesses and prayed for rejection of the application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R. and case papers it appears that the victim­girl lodged the report on 29.07.2015 wherein she had stated that her father is loom .. 4 .. Anticipatory Bail No.3067/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1.) worker and having poor financial condition. Once her father's friend had been to their house and informed that there is one Maharaj and Baba who cause rain shower of money. It was also informed to them that Baba Salim Ansari staying at Diwanshah Dargah road, Bhiwandi perform rituals for having rain shower of money and for that purpose he requires unmarried virgin girl with long hair. Informant's father forced for the marriage. On 07.07.2015 one Shankar and one Arun had been to their house and told that the informant has to marry with Baba Salim and he would have the shower of money and thereafter she could obtain Talakh from him and for that purpose they have to go to Temghar for the performance of Nikah. When informant's father took her to Temghar, at that time accused Shankar alongwith 3 to 4 other persons were present. At about 11.00 p.m. Baba Salim came there and at about 1200 hours their marriage was performed by Moulana in presence of Shankar and Arun and their 3 to 4 friends. Thereafter, Salim took the informant/victim in another block and then he pretended of playing magic and uttered chants and then he told her that the time has lapsed and therefore, now there would be no rain shower and established physical relationship with her by saying that she is his wife. At about 2.30 they went downstairs where her father was there and Salim told that there was no rain .. 5 .. Bail 3168/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1.) shower and therefore her father took her home. For about two days Salim did not come to take her. Therefore, the informant suspected foul play and by searching the address of accused Salim had been to 'Diwanshah Dargah' but Salim was not found there. On 14.07.2015 Salim's friend brought Talakhnama stating that Salim has pronounced Talakh to her and thereafter the victim lodged the report. 7] From bare perusal of F.I.R. it prima facie appears that it was the present applicant who introduced the victim as the girl as per the requirement of Baba Salim and he was present at the place where the marriage was performed by Moulana and applicant even signed the Nikahnama as a witness. It is also pertinent to note that said Nikah was performed at midnight at 1200 hours. Performing Nikah at such odd hours itself shows that the applicant was having knowledge about the act and he conspired with the main accused and other accused. Thus, his intention is also transpired from his conduct. Further, though it was strongly urged by the counsel for the applicant that applicant was only present during the marriage, however, the investigation in respect of present applicant is still underway as the applicant was not available for inquiry and was absconding for about four months. Furthermore, the statement of the witness Dattu .. 6 .. Anticipatory Bail No.3067/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1.) Malaiyya Kassa clearly transpires the role of the present applicant and he stated the role of the applicant in detail in respect of making available the girl, facilitating the girl, his presence during the marriage and even thereafter. Though the charge­sheet in respect of other accused is submitted, however, the investigation in respect of present applicant is still going on. 8] The Black Magic Act enacted with an object act to bring social awakening and awareness in the society and to create a healthy and social environment with the view to protect the common people in the society against the evil and sinister practices thriving on ignorance, and to combat and eradicate human sacrifice and other inhuman, evil, sinister and aghori practices propagated in the name of so called supernatural or magical powers or evil spirits commonly known as by conman with sinister motive of exploiting the common people in the society and thereby destroying very social fiber of the society; and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. The allegations are very serious and having grave impact and therefore, the thorough investigation is necessary. The investigation is still in progess, therefore, at this stage, no case made out for releasing the accused on bail. Hence, I pass following order ­ .. 7 .. Bail 3168/2015 (Order below Exhibit 1.) Non-applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 By this application the applicant is seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. who was arrested 14.12.2015 by Shantinagar Police Station in connection with C.R.No.I-313/2015 registered for an offence punishable under section 354A of I.P.C. and section 11, 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as P.O.C.S.O. Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Mr. Nilesh Gaikwad for the applicant/accused and learned A.P.P. Mrs. Phad for State. I.O. present. Case diary produced. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 13.12.2015 at the instance of the informant/father of 2 Bail No. 3213/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) victim-girl aged about 11 years with an indictment that accused who is their neighbourer called the victim-girl in his house and shown pornography in his mobile and outraged her modesty. 4] The learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant-accused is falsely implicated. He submitted that there is delay of 8 hours in lodging of F.I.R. The accused is staying in neighbourhood of informant, however, there is no single N.C. case filed against him. He further submitted that mobile of accused is seized, however, there is no electronic evidence against him. He further submitted that the accused is behind bars since his arrest. He is permanent resident of address given. He is ready to abide any conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing him on bail. 5] Per contra, the learned A.P.P. opposed the application submitting that the accused is involved in serious offence which is in respect of minor girl of 11 years. The accused has shown pornography because of which the victim was frightened. The accused has thrown the memory card of the mobile in water and now the mobile has been sent to C.A. for retrieving the data. The investigation is in progress. The accused is residing in same vicinity and there are chances of tampering with witnesses and prayed for rejection of application. 3 Bail No. 3213/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R. and the case papers, it appears that the allegations are in respect of showing pornography to minor victim girl who is aged 11 years. The mobile of the accused is already seized and as submitted by the learned A.P.P. it is sent to C.A. for retrieving the data. The material part of investigation appears to have been completed. There are no criminal antecedents of the accused. No fruitful purpose would be served by further incarceration of accused. The object of bail is neither punitive nor preventive but to secure the present of the accused at the time of trial. He is ready to abide by the conditions imposed by the Court. Non-applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 By this application the applicants are seeking their release on anticipatory bail under section 438 of Cr.P.C. being apprehending their arrest at the hands of Bhiwandi City Police Station in connection with C.R.No.I- 352/2015 registered for an offence punishable under section 363, 366A, 376 of I.P.C. and section 3, 4, 6 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as P.O.C.S.O. Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Mr. Arakade for the applicant/accused and learned A.P.P. Mrs. R.A.Navale for State. I.O. present. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 16.12.2015 at the instance of the informant/victim-girl aged about 17 years with an indictment that since October, 2014 accused 2 Anticipatory Bail No. 3216/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) on the pretext of marriage did sexual relationship with her and kidnapped her and kept her at his house and the mother and sister of accused demanded money for her marriage with accused and abused and assaulted her. 4] The learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant-accused is falsely implicated. He further submitted that since ten months the victim-girl and accused Moharram Ali were staying separately from the present applicants at Uttar Pradesh. He submitted that in fact as the girl was minor, the applicants drove the victim and accused from the house. The main accused is already arrested and behind bar. There is nothing to recover from the present applicants and their custodial interrogation is not necessary. They are ready to co-operate in investigation and prayed for their release on anticipatory bail. 5] Per contra, the learned A.P.P. opposed the application submitting that the offence is in respect of minor girl. SPECIAL CASE (POCSO) NO. 272 OF 2015 CNR : MHTH01­008603­2015 Exh. No. The State (Through Kapurbavdi Police Station, Thane.) ..Prosecution V/s. 1] Akshay Sudhakar Khaware, Age 19 years, R/o. Shivshankar chawl, Manoramanagar, Thane, 2] Pradeep Pralhad Chavan, Age 21 years, R/o. Shivshankar chawl, Manoramanagar, Thane, 3] Abhimanyu Narsu Patil, Age 20 years, R/o. Shivshankar chawl, Manoramanagar, Thane, 4] Hemant Tanaji More, Age 20 years, R/o. Azad Nagar, Thane, 5] Chetan Hanumant Kamble, Age 20 years, R/o. Azad Nagar, Thane, 6] Bhausaheb Vishnu Khillare, Age 23 years, R/o. Azad Nagar, Thane. ..Accused. 2 POCSO Case. No. 272/2015. Appearance :­ ___________________________________________________________ For State : Special P.P. Shri. Londhe. For Accused : Adv. Shri. Phad. ___________________________________________________________ JUDGMENT (Delivered on 25.10.2018.) 1] The accused are facing trial for the offence punishable u/s. 147, 148, 307, 336, 354(1)(d), 323, 324, 504, 506 r/w. Sec. 149 of I.P.C. and section 11 and 12 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. The prosecution case in nut­shell is as follows : 2] Informant Gopal Ratan Teji is father of the minor girl and he was residing within the jurisdiction of Manoramanagar police chowky. His daughter was studying in 10th standard and was 15 years of age at the relevant time. Accused Akshay Sudhakar Khaware was following his daughter for one year prior to the incident. The daughter of informant had told about the same for eight months prior to the incident. Thereafter, the informant had gone to the house of accused Akshay and informed his parents about the same. He was advised by the informant and parents of Akshay. One month thereafter, again Akshay followed the daughter of informant (hereinafter referred as victim), when she was going to attend tuitions. When the victim informed about the same at home, wife of informant tried to convince Akshay. On that, Akshay said that “Jo Karana Hai, Kar Lo, Mai Guddi Ko le Jaunga.” 3] Thereafter, on 23.09.15 at about 6.00 p.m., the informant went 3 POCSO Case. No. 272/2015. along with his daughter, children, relatives and colleagues by name Sampat and Akash for immersion of Ganpati idol towards creek via Kolshet road. At that time, the victim informed that accused Akshay was hiding himself behind the bus and following her, so also, he was making gestures towards the victim. At that time, informant and other persons caught Akshay and tried to convince him. However, he got enraged and left the spot. At about 10.00 p.m., when they were returning after immersion of Ganpati idol, they reached near Biar India Company. At that time, accused Akshay came with his five­six friends on three motor­cycles and started throwing bricks towards informant and other persons. One of the bricks hit on right side of chest of Akash Teji. Akshay tried to kill Sampat Savariya by assaulting beer bottle on his head and left elbow. Thereafter, Akshay and his friends abused and assaulted the informant and his maternal cousin Kalu Dargaj by fist and kick blows. The passer­by persons rescued them. At that time, police from Kapurbavdi police station came there. Therefore, those persons ran away from the spot. However, police caught Akshay Khaware. One person fled away on red motor­cycle while other persons ran away by leaving motor­cycles on the spot. The numbers of said motor­cycles are MH04/GG/2835 Pulsar motor­cycle and MH04/GW/9642 Activa Scooter. Police sent Sampat and Akash to Civil hospital for treatment. Thereafter, informant lodged F.I.R. against the accused persons. 4] As per F.I.R., C.R. No. 403/15 came to be registered for commission of offence punishable u/s. 147, 148, 307, 336, 354(1)(d), 323, 324, 504, 506 r/w. Sec. 149 of I.P.C. and section 11 and 12 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. P.I. Abhijit Mohite conducted investigation of the crime. After preparation of spot panchanama, recording statements of witnesses and arresting the accused, 4 POCSO Case. No. 272/2015. he filed charge­sheet against the accused persons for the offence punishable u/s. 147, 148, 307, 336, 354(1)(d), 323, 324, 504, 506 r/w. Sec. 149 of I.P.C. and section 11 and 12 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 5] Charge came to be framed against accused persons vide Exh.11 for the offence punishable u/s. 147, 148, 307, 336, 354(1)(d), 323, 324, 504, 506 r/w. Sec. 149 of I.P.C. and section 11 and 12 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, by my learned predecessor. Contents of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular, to which they pleaded not guilty and claimed for trial. 6] In order to prove the guilt of the accused, the prosecution had examined in all four witnesses i.e. Gopal Ratan Teji informant as P.W.1 at Exh. 24, victim as P.W.2 at Exh. 26, P.S.I. Amruta Sahebrao Choure P.S.O. as P.W.3 at Exh. 30, P.I. Abhijit Mohite investigation officer as P.W.4 at Exh. 34. 7] Prosecution also relied upon the F.I.R. Exh. 31, arrest panchanama Exh. 32, seizure panchanama of clothes of informant Exh. 33, spot panchanama Exh. 35, arrest panchanama of rest of the accused i.e. accused Nos. 2 to 6 at Exh. 36, seizure panchanama of clothes of accused Nos. 1 to 6 Exh. 37, medico­legal certificate of Sampat Savariya Exh. 38, medico­legal certificate of Akash Teji Exh. 39, forwarding letter issued to Director of Forensic Laboratory, Kalina, Mumbai, for sending muddemal articles for chemical analysis Exh. 40. Thereafter, vide pursis Exh. 42, the prosecution closed its evidence. 8] Statements of accused persons came to be recorded u/s. 313 of 5 POCSO Case. No. 272/2015. Cr.P.C. for the purpose of confronting only incriminating material to the accused. The defence of the accused persons is of total denial and of false implication. 9] Heard learned P.P. Shri. Londhe for the State and learned counsel Shri. Phad, for the accused. 10] Following points emerged for my consideration and I have recorded my findings thereon for the reasons given below. Points Findings 1] Whether the prosecution has proved No. that on 23.09.2015 at about 8.00 p.m., accused no. 1 committed sexual harassment of minor victim by making gestures towards her, when she was going on Kolshet road for immersion of Ganpati idol and thereby, he committed an offence punishable u/s. 11 and 12 of the POCSO Act ? 2] Whether the prosecution has proved No. that on 23.09.2015 at 10.00 p.m, all the accused persons came on three motor­ cycles and assaulted the informant and the witnesses by throwing bricks at them and thereafter, abused and assaulted them by fist and kick blows, with an intention to kill them ? 3] What order ? As per final order. REASONS 11] Ld. Special P.P. Shri. Londhe submitted that though in the present case, the informant and the victim have not supported the prosecution case, however, the prosecution has examined P.S.O. who 6 POCSO Case. No. 272/2015. recorded the F.I.R. and said P.S.O. P.W.3 has proved the contents of F.I.R. as well as portion marked A and B thereof. The name of accused No. 1 has specifically mentioned in the F.I.R. The medico­legal certificates and the other documents clearly indicate towards the guilt of the accused. Hence, they may be held guilty of commission of the offence punishable u/s. 147, 148, 307, 336, 354(1)(d), 323, 324, 504, 506 r/w. Sec. 149 of I.P.C. and section 11 and 12 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, and be punished by imposing maximum sentence prescribed for the same. 12] On the other hand, Ld. Counsel Shri. Phad submitted that in the present case, informant as well as the victim who are the alleged eye­ witnesses of the incident, have specifically denied involvement of present accused persons. They have come with specific case that quarrel was going on amongst boys and in that quarrel, one of the family members of the victim sustained injury. That the informant had mentioned that he had lodged F.I.R., however, he had denied the contents of portion marked A and B which contains incriminating material against accused persons. The informant does not know Marathi as well as contents of the F.I.R. Therefore, there is strong doubt as to whether the F.I.R. came to be recorded as per narration of the informant himself. Moreover, the injured witnesses have not examined by the prosecution. The witnesses have admitted that there was dark and they could not see the assailants. Though names of accused Nos. 2 to 6 are not reflecting in F.I.R. and those accused persons are shown to be unknown, however, the investigating officer did not take steps to conduct test identification parade of accused persons. Therefore, there is no material as to how the names of accused Nos. 2 to 6 revealed. In such circumstances, there is no material against the accused persons. So also, there is no material to show that the incident as alleged 7 POCSO Case. No. 272/2015. by the prosecution has ever taken place. Hence, the accused may be honourably acquitted from the charges. 13] It has come in the evidence of P.W.1 Gopal Ratan Teji that victim is his daughter. At the time of incident, she was studying in 8 th standard in Gurukul high­school. He does not know the accused persons in the court. The victim informed him that some boys were teasing her. Therefore, he went to the school and informed the school authorities. On 23.09.15 at 6.00 p.m., he had gone for immersion of Ganpati idol. While returning back, quarrel was going on between some boys. In pelting of stones by those boys, friend of this witness sustained injury to his head. They took him to Kapurbavdi police station. Police sent them to Civil hospital. After primary treatment, they took him to private hospital. His daughter did not tell him name of any person who was teasing her. He denied the suggestion that when he went for immersion of Ganpati idol, somebody chased his daughter. They caught him on the spot. He further deposed that he had lodged F.i.R. with police. He had narrated about the incident while lodging F.I.R. and F.I.R. at Exh. 25 bears his signature. However, he deposed that the boys who were teasing his daughter were not present in the court. As the witness did not support the contents of F.I.R. and the prosecution version, the permission was granted to the learned A.P.P. to ask leading questions to the witness as per the provisions u/s. 154 of the Indian Evidence Act. However, the witness denied the suggestion that he narrated the contents of portion marked A and B out of the F.I.R. and expressed inability to explain as to how said portion is reflecting in the F.I.R. 14] During his cross­examination, he admitted that he cannot read or write Marathi and he does not know as to what is written in the F.I.R. 8 POCSO Case. No. 272/2015. He admitted that there was dark on the place of incident and so many people had gathered there. He also admitted that he did not see the persons who were quarreling. He admitted that the police did not call him for identification of accused. So also that the present accused are no way concerned with the incident. 15] It has come in the evidence of victim P.W.2 that her date of birth is 7th July, 1999. At the time of incident, she was studying in 10 th standard in Gurukul Vidyamandir, Thane. She does not know accused persons in the court. On 23.09.15, she had gone for immersion of Ganpati idol. While returning to home, the incident of pelting stones was going on. Due to dark, she could not see properly. However, one of her family members sustained injury. No incident occurred in respect of her. She denied that somebody was going on motor­cycle by making gestures towards her and therefore, her relative caught him or that said person went away and came with friends and assaulted all of them. Police did not make any enquiry with her. In spite of granting permission to ask leading questions to Ld. A.P.P., this witness denied every suggestion put by the prosecution, so also, denied the contents of portion marked A and B out of her so­called statement before police. 16] It has come in the evidence of P.W.3 P.S.I. Amruta Sahebrao Choure that in September, 2015, she was posted as P.S.I. in Kapurbavdi police station. On 24.09.15, she was P.S.O. of the police station. On that day, she recorded F.I.R. of Gopal Ratan Teji as per his narration. He narrated that, accused Akshay Khaware was chasing and teasing daughter of informant, therefore his family members had advised him not to do so. However, on the day of immersion of Ganesh idols, he again chased her and on stopping him, he along with co­accused assaulted them by bricks 9 POCSO Case. No. 272/2015. and glass bottles. The informant recorded his F.I.R. dated 24.09.15 at Exh.31. Accordingly, Crime No. I­ 403/15 came to be registered. At 3.00 a.m., she arrested accused Akshay Khaware in presence of panchas by arrest panchanama Exh. 32. It is admitted by defence. On the same day, she seized clothes on the person of informant Gopal Ratan Teji in presence of panchas by seizure panchanama Exh.33 dated 24.09.15. It is admitted by defence. Further investigation was entrusted to P.I. Mohite. The witness identified accused Akshay Khaware before the court. 17] During her cross­examination, she denied the suggestion that she did not record F.I.R. as per narration of informant or that contents of portion marked A and B out of the F.I.R. were not narrated by the informant. However, she admitted that she did not collect any documentary proof about age of the victim. However, she denied that at the relevant time of commission of offence, victim was above 18 years of age. 18] It has come in the evidence of P.W.4 P.I. Abhijit Mohite that in September, 2015, he was posted as P.I. at Kapurbavdi police station. Investigation of C.R. No. 403/15 was entrusted to him on 24.09.15. On the same day, he went to the spot along with panchas and prepared spot panchanama dated 24.09.15 at Exh. 35 as admitted by defence. On the same day, he arrested accused Abhimanyu Patil, Pradip Chavan, Hemant More, Chetan Kamble, and Bhausaheb Khillare in presence of panchas by arrest panchanama dated 24.09.15 at Exh. 36. On next day on 25.09.15, he seized clothes on the person of accused by seizure panchanama dated 24.09.15 at Exh. 37. He collected medico­legal certificates Exh. 38 and 39 dated 08.10.15 of Sampat Savariya and Akash Teji respectively. They are admitted by defence. The seized articles were sent to Forensic laboratory, 10 POCSO Case. No. 272/2015. Kalina, vide letter dated 01.10.15 Exh. 40. He also recorded statements of some witnesses including victim. As it revealed during investigation that accused had assaulted the informant and witnesses and teased the victim, therefore, he filed charge­sheet against them, accordingly. The witness identified the accused present in the court. 19] During his cross­examination, he admitted that he did not record supplementary statement of informant. So also, that he did not collect any document to ascertain age of the victim. He did not arrange for recording statement of victim u/s. 164 of Cr.P.C. He did not prepare for test identification parade of accused. However, he deposed that the accused were residing in same vicinity and were knowing each­other. He admitted that the other accused persons than Akshay were unknown as per F.I.R. Further, he denied other suggestions about lodging false charge­ sheet or recording incorrect statements of witnesses. 20] If the evidence on record would perused, though the informant has deposed that he had lodged F.I.R., however, he denied the contents of portion marked A and B out of the F.I.R. He has narrated totally different story than the F.I.R. He has specifically denied the involvement of accused No. 1 in the alleged incident of following his daughter as well as teasing her. He has also denied the alleged incident of assault by accused persons. He has come with the case that quarrel was going on amongst the boys and in said quarrel, the boys pelted stones and in the same, his colleague Sampat Sawariya sustained injury, while in the F.I.R., it is mentioned that Sampat sustained injury by beer bottle while Akash Teji sustained injury by brick. Therefore, this oral evidence is totally contrary to the F.I.R. The informant has also deposed that he does not know Marathi. So also, the contents of F.I.R. were not read over to him before obtaining his signature. 11 POCSO Case. No. 272/2015. P.W.2 has also denied involvement of accused persons in commission of the offence. In spite of granting permission to ask leading questions to the informant as well as the victim, the prosecution failed to bring out any incriminating material against the accused from their oral evidence. 21] It is also the matter of fact that though the names of other accused persons than accused No. 1 were not mentioned in the F.I.R. and it is just mentioned that they were colleagues of accused No. 1. The investigating officer did not arrange for test identification parade of those persons, which was very much necessary. The prosecution has also not examined said injured persons Sampat and Akash Teji. So also, the medico­legal certificate of Akash Teji shows no external injury which is contrary to the contents of F.I.R. In my view, the prosecution has failed to prove the allegations of making gestures towards the victim by accused No. 1 as well as assault by all accused persons with bricks as well as fist and kick blows. Therefore, the evidence of P.W.3 P.S.O. who recorded F.I.R., cannot be a sole basis for holding the accused guilty of commission of offence. 22] Except said F.I.R., there is no material on record indicating towards the guilt of accused persons. So also, even in the F.I.R., name of only accused No. 1 is mentioned. It shows that there is no material at all against accused No. 2 to 6. In such circumstances, when the eye­witnesses are denying involvement of accused persons including accused No. 1 in commission of offence, in my view, the prosecution has failed to prove the charges against the accused persons beyond reasonable doubt. It is settled position of law that benefit of such reasonable doubt always goes in favour of accused. Hence, it is necessary to answer point No. 1 and 2 in the negative by holding that the prosecution has failed to prove the charges 12 POCSO Case. No. 272/2015. against the accused persons beyond reasonable doubt. Consequentially, the accused persons are required to be acquitted from the charges. 23] So far as muddemal property is concerned, Bajaj Pulsar motor­ cycle bearing No. MH04/GG/2835 and Honda Activa Scooter bearing No. MH04/GW/9642 need to be given in possession of their registered owners and remaining muddemal i.e. clothes being worthless, need to be destroyed. 24] In the light of above observations about acquittal of accused and disposal of muddemal property, in answer to point No. 3, I pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused Nos. 1 to 6 are hereby, acquitted under sec. 235(1) of the Criminal Procedure Code, from the offence punishable u/s. 147, 148, 307, 336, 354(1)(d), 323, 324, 504, 506 r/w. Sec. 149 of I.P.C. and section 11 and 12 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 2] Their bail bonds stand cancelled and sureties stood discharged. 3] They are hereby directed to furnish bail bond of Rs.15,000/­ each with a surety of like amount, so as to appear before the higher Court in compliance with Sec. 437­ A of Code of Criminal Procedure. 4] Muddemal property Bajaj Pulsar motor­ cycle bearing No. MH04/GG/2835 and 13 POCSO Case. No. 272/2015. Honda Activa Scooter bearing No. MH04/GW/9642 be given in possession of their registered owners and remaining muddemal i.e. clothes be destroyed, after appeal period is over. 5] Pronounced in open court. Non­applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 1] By this application the applicant is seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C., who was arrested on 17.12.2015 by Mumbra Police Station in connection with C.R.No. I­950/2015 registered for an offence punishable under section 354 of I.P.C. and section 7 and 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Mr Quamruddin Ansari for the applicant/ accused and learned A.P.P. Mrs. R.A. Navale for State. I.O. present. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 15.12.2015 at the instance of the informant/mother of victim­girl aged about 9 years with an indictment that the accused outraged her modesty by confining her in the tuition class. 4] The learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant­accused is falsely implicated. He submitted that there is delay of 3 days in lodging FIR. He submitted that applicant is reputed 2 Bail No. 3192/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) man and trustee of Masjid­e­Fateh Welfare and Educational Trust Mumbra. He further submitted that one Mohammad Aslam Mohammad Mekrani illegally wants to take over the affairs of Mosque. He further submitted that therefore the applicant had issued him notice and said Mohammed Aslam threatened him to implicate him in the false case and the present FIR is the result of that threatening. He further submitted that accused is having clean past and he is taking the classes in the Mosque. He is permanent resident of the address given in the application and is ready to abide by any conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing him on bail. 5] Per contra, the learned A.P.P. strongly opposed the application submitting that the FIR was lodged by the grand mother of the victim and there is no reason to implicate the accused falsely. She further submitted that though applicant is teacher in the Mosque he outraged the modesty of student of 9 years. She also submitted that the investigation is in progress and there are chances of tampering of the witnesses. The accused is resident of U.P. and there are chances of his fleeing away and prayed for rejection of application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R. and case papers it appears that there are serious allegations about outraging modesty of victim girl aged 9 years who is student of the accused. The defence of accused about false implication at behest of one Mohd. Aslam cannot be considered at this stage. However, it is also clear that details scrutiny of the case is not permitted at the time of considering bail application. Though there is prima facie case against accused, however, it also appears that the material part of the investigation 3 Bail No. 3192/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) have been completed. The accused is behind bar since 15 days. He do not have any criminal antecedent. The object of bail is neither preventive nor punitive but to secure the presence of accused at the time of trial. No purpose would be served by further incarceration of applicant­accused. The accused is ready to abide by any conditions imposed by the Court. The apprehension of A.P.P. can be addressed by imposing stringent conditions as the accused is involved in serious offence. Hence, I pass the following order ­ ORDER 1) The application is allowed. 2) Applicant Nurulla Tafjullu Hussain Ansari be released on bail on his executing P.R. Bond of ₹ 20,000/­ [rupees twenty thousand only] with one local solvent surety in the like amount on the following conditions ­ A] Accused shall attend the concerned police station on every Monday in between 10.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon till further order. B] Applicant shall not tamper with prosecution witnesses. C] Applicant shall furnish his and his two blood relatives' address proofs and contact numbers and he is duty bound to inform I.O. and Court about the change of address, if any. D] Applicant shall not contact and pressurize victim­girl and any other witnesses in any manner and he shall maintain decency hereinafter. Thane. Date : 01.01.2016. (Ms. U.M. Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act), Thane.

Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­008634­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No.273/15 Received on : 22.12.2015 Registered on : 22.12.2015 Decided on : 07.01.2019 Duration : 3Ys. 0Ms. 26 Ds. IN THE COURT OF D.J.­1 & ADDL. SESSIONS JUDGE, THANE. (Presided over by Hemant M. Patwardhan) Special Case (POCSO) No. 273/15 Exh.No.42 State of Maharashtra. (Through Turbhe MIDC Police station) ..Complainant V/s. Kishan Baban Kshirsagar. Age­ 40 years, R/at. Near Medhekar House, Hanumannagar, Turbhe Naka, Navi Mumbai ..Accused Appearance:­ APP Smt. Moholkar for the State. Advocate Shri. Patankar for accused JUDGMENT (Delivered on this 7th day of January 2019) Accused Kishan Baban Kshirsagar was facing trial under sections 354 of Penal Code with Sec. 8, 10 and 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 on following facts. 1 to 12 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­008634­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No.273/15 1] That on 14.10.2015, at Hanumannagar, Turbhenaka, Navi Mumbai within the jurisdiction of Turbhe MIDC Police station accused used criminal force on minor victim girl aged about five years and at the same time with sexual intents had touched her private part and breast. Therefore, on the complaint lodged by the complainant, an offence punishable under aforesaid sections came to be registered against accused. On completion of investigation he was charge­sheeted. 2] My learned Predecessor was pleased to frame charge below Exh.5 and has certified that contents of it was read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. Accused has pleaded not guilty and claim to be tried. His defence was that of total denial and that he has been falsely implicated in the matter as he has taken over business place where the uncle of the victim was carrying laundry business. 3] As the accused has claim to be tried, prosecution has then proceeded to examine complainant, victim girl, panch witness and I.O. to bring home the guilt of the accused at home. Then arguments of the rival advocates were heard. Learned P.P. has categorically pointed out that complainant and victim had categorically deposed as to how incident had occurred. According to learned P.P. complainant has himself witnessed the incident and thus his deposition cannot be discarded when nothing fruitful was brought 2 to 12 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­008634­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No.273/15 during his cross­examination to implicate accused in this case. According to submissions victim girl has also categorically deposed as to how accused has committed sexual assault with her by using criminal force. Thus, according to learned P.P. incident deposed by the victim has not been denied at all the same is certainly sufficient to prove the guilt of the accused. She has therefore, requested the court to convict the accused as per the charges. 4] Per contra, learned defence advocate has categorically pointed out that there are contradictions in the deposition of the complainant and the victim therefore, those contradictory statements are in itself sufficient to discard the allegations. He has then pointed out that alleged spot of incident is situated in crowded place where traffic is moving round the O'clock and thus highly improbable that accused will commit any such offence in such area. He has then pointed out that complainant has admitted that unless entering in the particular shop, it is difficult to see anything going on in the shop therefore if said admission is consider then allegation of complainant that he had seen the legs of his niece from outside can be discarded. According to him accused has been falsely implicated in the matter as the complainant who has borrowed an amount of Rs.3000/­ from him was wanted to avoid return of that borrowed amount. Hence, he has requested to consider the defence of the accused as probable and acquit him from all the charges. 3 to 12 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­008634­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No.273/15 5] On the basis of aforesaid facts, following points arise for my consideration and I record my findings against each of them for the reasons noted below:­ S.N Points Findings 1] Does prosecution prove that accused on 14.10.2015 at Hanumannagar, ..In the Turbhenaka, Navi Mumbai within the jurisdiction of Turbhe MIDC affirmative. Police station, used criminal force to complainant's niece, (brother's daughter) minor victim aged about 5 years who was playing in front of the house and caught­hold her intending to outrage her modesty, took her to his laundry and by moving his hand on her breast, by touching her private part by inserting his another hand in her pant and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 354 of IPC? 2] Does prosecution prove that accused on aforesaid date, time and place, ..In the committed sexual assault on complainant's niece, (brother's daughter) affirmative. minor victim aged about 5 years, took her to his laundry and by moving his hand on her breast, by touching her private part by inserting his another hand in her pant and thereby committed an offence punishable under section 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012? 3] Does prosecution prove that accused on aforesaid date, time and place, ..In the committed aggravated sexual assault on complainant's niece, (brother's negative. daughter) minor victim aged about 5 years, by touching her private part by inserting his another hand in her pant and by kissing her and thereby committed an offence punishable under Sec.10 read with Section 9(m) of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012? 4] Does the prosecution prove that accused on aforesaid date, time and ..In the place, committed sexual harassment upon complainant's niece negative. (brother's daughter) minor victim aged about 5 years, took her to his laundry and by moving his hand on her breast, by touching her private part by inserting his another hand in her pant and thereby committed an offence punishable under Sec. 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012? 5] What order ? Accused is convicted as per final order. REASONS As to point nos. 1 to 5 :­ 6] All these points are interlined with each other and are considered at once. In the instant case prosecution has alleged that 4 to 12 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­008634­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No.273/15 accused has committed assault on victim with intent to outrage her modesty and as the victim was minor within the meaning of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 assault made by accused were treated as sexual assault with sexual intent and thus, he was prosecuted under section 354 of IPC read with section 8, 10 and 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. In order to substantiate the allegations and to bring the guilt of the accused at home aforesaid four witnesses were examined. Out of said four witnesses, witness no.1 is the complainant, witness no.2 is the victim herself and witness no.3 is the panch witness wherein witness no.4 was I.O. As per the allegation of prosecution when the mother of the victim could not trace her out she asked the complainant to help her to search victim and while the complainant was searching for her, he has found victim's leg from half open shutter of the shop of the accused person. Therefore, according to the allegations he himself has open shutter and has seen the accused moving his hand on the breast of the victim, kissing her wherein his other hand was under the nicker of the victim girl. Thus, he took the victim in the custody and called the police on the spot. He has then lodged complaint to set law in motion. Thus, from his deposition it is apparent that he himself is eye witness of incident. Accordingly, he has categorically deposed in terms of prosecution's case. Though he was cross­examined at length except the fact that area was crowded and traffic moves round O'clock there and fact 5 to 12 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­008634­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No.273/15 that inside of the shop cannot be seen from outside unless shop is entered into nothing else has been brought on record. Except a suggestion that false case is filed even his allegation of having witnessed the incident as above has not been even denied. Thus, it is apparent on record that said depositions so far as material allegations about occurrence of the incidents are concerned remain unchallenged on record. 7] Victim was then examined who has then categorically deposed in question put to her as to what actually had happened that the accused had dragged her in his shop and while she was weeping has pressed her breast and private part. Then, complainant came there, saw the incident and beat the accused. Thus, it is apparent from her deposition that victim has not only deposed categorically in terms of the prosecution's case but has corroborated facts narrated by the complainant. By her deposition presence of the complainant was also brought on the spot by the victim. Again at the cost of repetition I am constrained to say that itself suggestion that complainant has narrated the incident to police nothing else was even suggested to the said witness. Even though it is considered that scope of cross­ examination under the POCSO Act is very limited but still it was expected from the defence to at least put suggestion to the effect denying the prosecution's case. However, to the best knowledge of the learned advocate even the said suggestions were not put forth to discard allegations of the victim. If we consider the age of the victim 6 to 12 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­008634­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No.273/15 then as rule of prudence the court is require to look for corroboration of the facts narrated by her which corroboration is on record through the deposition of complainant. Therefore, if we consider deposition of both material witnesses it is apparent that material facts about occurrence of the incident have categorically brought on record. 8] On perusal of the authority it is apparent that accused was charged under section 354 of IPC read with section 8,10 and 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Section 354 of IPC deals with assault of criminal force to woman with intent to outrage her modesty wherein section 8,10 and 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 deals with sexual assault and punishment for aggravated sexual assault. Section 7 of POCSO defines what are the sexual assaults actually means and the said definition includes even touch by any person to vagina, penis or breast of a child with sexual intent is sufficient to bring the particular act within the purview of said section. The basic ingredients of section 354 of IPC is also an assault of criminal force either intending to outrage or knowingly that by his act he is likely to outrage the modesty of a woman. In the instant case when eye witnesses of the incident along with victim herself has categorically narrated the incident in which she has suffered. Said depositions are certainly sufficient to raise presumption under section 29 and 30 of section 8,10 and 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Section 29 deals with presumption as to the 7 to 12 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­008634­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No.273/15 commission of certain offences and section 30 deals with presumption of culpable mental state of the particular person. In the instant case when the accused at about 11.00 p.m. has initially dragged the victim in his shop, shut the shutter though partly and then committed act of kissing or moving his hand either on the breast or private part of the victim then his intention can be gathered from the particular act committed by him at the particular time. Accused thus can be said of having knowledge of the fact that his act of moving his hand on the private part of the victim or breast of the victim was certainly and likely to outrage modesty of the victim. So also his said act considering the aforesaid act committed at about 11.00 p.m. in his own shop is sufficient to attract his mental state of having sexual intends while committing said act. Presence of the accused on the spot was categorically brought by the deposition of both the said eye witnesses. Accused has not denied the fact that he was found on the spot along with victim. Therefore, if we consider all these facts then some minor discrepancies which were brought in the deposition of I.O. can be easily discarded. Though the I.O. has admitted that she did not refer exact residential address of accused either in the charge­sheet or panchanama in itself is not sufficient to accept that accused has been falsely implicated in the matter. It is apparent on record that his residential address is referred in the charge­sheet as well as in the charge and even if we consider that fact as it is then also as referred to above his presence on the spot 8 to 12 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­008634­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No.273/15 has been categorically brought by the deposition of eye witnesses as well as victim then such minor omissions and contradictions has to be discarded. Having regards to the said facts it is difficult to accept that said contradictions and omissions in the evidence of I.O. is sufficient to discard otherwise established facts on record. 9] In the instant case the accused in order to discard prosecution's case has attempted to put forth two different defences viz. that the complainant has borrowed amount of Rs.3000/­ from him which he did not want to repay and as the accused himself has taken over the laundry business of the victim's uncle i.e. complainant he has been implicated in this matter. However, both said defences of the accused nowhere prima facie appears to have been even established to discard allegations of the prosecution. The defence of accused having taken over the laundry business of the complainant has only been put forth in the statement under section 313 of Cr.P.C. without there being even suggestion to that effect during cross­ examination of the complainant. Though defence of having lend an amount of Rs.3000/­ was put forth in cross­examination in suggestion form, the accused has even failed to suggest period when particular amount was really borrowed. Thus, all that defences are apparently based on very vague contentions. Having regards to the specific denial of those defences, I do not find defence of the accused probable to consider the presumption under section 29 and 30 of POCSO Act really rebutted. Having regards to these facts to my 9 to 12 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­008634­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No.273/15 mind whatever material and substance is brought before the court is certainly sufficient to hold that allegations against accused are proved under Section 354 of IPC and section 8 of POCSO Act. Before parting with the findings I would like to add that though charge was also framed under section 10 and 12 of the Act defining section 9 of aggravated sexual assault deals with sexual assaults being committed either by the police officer, member of the armed forces or when a child is subjected to sexual assault by one or more persons of a group in furtherance of their common intention and section 11 of the Act defines sexual harassment with sexual intents wherein pre­requisite are uttering any word or making some sound or gesture or exhibits part of his own body while committing sexual assault. However, in the instant case there are no such allegations either of assault being committed by group of persons or by the accused himself by making any gestures, sound or uttering any words. Therefore, in my considered view charge under section 10 or 12 cannot be said to have been established even if the depositions of the aforesaid material witnesses are considered. Therefore, I do not hesitate to record my findings so far as point no.1 and 2 are concerned in affirmative and point no.3 and 4 are concerned in negative. As I record my findings against point no.1 and 2 in affirmative I do not hesitate to hold accused guilty of the offence punishable under section 354 of IPC read with section 8 of POCSO Act. As I hold accused guilty of the offence, Judgment is 10 to 12 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­008634­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No.273/15 deffered for hearing the accused on the point of sentence. 10] Heard accused on the point of sentence. He has submitted to take lenient view on the ground that he still maintain that he is not committed any such offence. Also, heard learned advocate of the accused who has submitted to take lenient view on the ground that since last more than three years he is in jail and is not able to pay any fine amount. Per contra, learned P.P. Smt. Moholkar has categorically pointed out that such offences are increasing in the society therefore, in order to give proper message in the society accused be severally punished. After having heard rival submissions I have gone through the provisions of law under which accused was convicted wherein under section 354 of IPC punishment prescribed is around two years wherein under section 8 of POCSO Act punishment prescribed is three years with fine. Therefore, considering said punishment in my view following order would suffice the purpose. Accordingly, the order. ORDER 1] Accused Kisan Baban Kshirsagar is hereby convicted for the offence punishable under section 354 of IPC read with section 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act 2012 and he is sentenced to suffer R.I. for two years under section 354 of IPC and three years under section 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act 2012 and shall also be liable to pay fine of Rs.2500/­ i/d. to suffer further S.I. for ten days. 11 to 12 Judgment CNR NO.MHTH01­008634­2015 Special (POCSO) Case No.273/15 2] Accused is hereby acquitted from the offence punishable under section 10 and 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act 2012. 3] Both the sentences shall run concurrently. 4] Accused is in jail since the date of his arrest therefore, by exercising powers under section 428 of Cr.P.C. set off is granted for period already undergone by him. 5] Muddemal property viz. two coins of Rs.2/­ be returned to the complainant after appeal period. 6] On payment of fine amount, said be paid to victim as compensation. 7] Copy of the Judgment be provided to the accused free of cost. Thane (Hemant M.Patwardhan) Date: 07.01.2019 D.J.­1 & Additional Sessions Judge, Thane. 12 to 12

--1-- ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN CRIMINAL BAIL APPLICATION NO.3198/2017 CNR NO.MHTH01­008649­2017 Applicant Mahesh Sanjay Jadhav has applied for bail under section 439 of Cr. P.C in C.R.No.I­212/2017 registered in Wagle Estate police station for the offence under section 376 of Indian Penal Code and section 4,6,8,12 of POCSO Act. 2. It is contended that the victim herself came with the applicant at Shirdi and resided with him and with her consent the alleged incident took place in July 2017. Thereafter in the Ganpati Festival the physical relation was committed. But till 11.11.2017 no FIR given by the victim. The accused has produced some documents i.e. photographs of victim and accused showing that the victim is wearing Mangalsutra and she has married and she has given smiling pose with the accused. It shows that alleged incident was consensual. Chargesheet is filed, but there is no documentary evidence i.e. birth certificate to show that the victim was minor. 3. Investigating Officer has given his say at Exh.4. It is contended that the victim was 16 years old at the time of incident, she has became pregnant. So, if the accused is released on bail he is likely to tamper. 4. I heard Ld. Counsel on behalf of the accused and Ld. APP. 5. The Counsel for the accused relied upon decision in case of Sunil Mahadev Patil V/s. The State of Maharashtra 2016 ALL MR (Cri) 1712. In that case the victim was 15 years old and accused was 20 years old. They eloped away and garlanded each other and performed sexual intercourse. On this mitigating circumstances the bail was granted. In case of Satyam Ramchandra Fulore 2015 ALL MR --2-- (Cri) 2785 in that case the victim was in love with the applicant. There was no history of sexual or physical assault. From the medical examination the victim, was 16 years old at the time of alleged incident, she has attained the age of understanding and on that ground the bail was granted. 6. In this case considering the photographs produced by the accused and the statement of the victim it appears that the victim had love affair with the present applicant. She has eloped away with the accused and at her house the alleged incident took place. It also appears that the victim has wearing Mangalsutra it prima facie shows that the victim and accused had performed marriage. So considering these mitigating factors and observations in above reported cases I am of the view that there is strong prima facie case made out to release the accused on bail. Hence, I pass following order. :ORDER: 1. Application is allowed. 2. Accused Mahesh Sanjay Jadhav shall be released on PB and SB of Rs.20,000/­ (Rupees Twenty Thousand Only) with one or two local solvent sureties in like amount. 3. Code and u/sec. 7 & 8 of POCSO Act. 2] In brief it is the case of prosecution that on 10.8.2016 at about 2.00 p.m. informant Riya went to market for purchasing household articles. Thereafter she went to house and narrated the incident to her mother. Then, they went to police station and she lodged report. 3] On the basis of complaint, offence came to be registered at Crime No. 383/2015 for the offence punishable u/s 354 of IPC and u/s 7 & 8 of POCSO Act. Investigation was entrusted to PSI Smt. Suryavanshi. She recorded the statement of complainant and witnesses. She prepared the spot panchanama in the presence of panchas. Accused was arrested on 11.8.2016. After completion of investigation she submitted the charge­sheet before the Special Judge (POCSO Act), Thane. 4] Charge Exh.3 was framed and explained to accused to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. His defence is that of total denial. 5] Considering the case of the prosecution following points arise for my determination and I have recorded my findings thereon for the reasons discussed below. POINTS FINDINGS 1 Does the prosecution prove that on 10.8.2016 at about 2.00 p.m. opposite Fakruddin Dargah, Amrutnagar Maarket, Mumbra accused used criminal force to Kum. Riya Shahid Shaikh aged 16 years with intend to outrage her modestyand thereby committed an offence punishable u/sec. 354 of I.P.C. ? .. REASONS Points Nos. 1 & 2 : 6] These points are interlinked to each other, hence in order to avoid the repetition of evidence they are clubbed together. 7] Prosecution examined in all two witnesses. P.W.1 Hafiza at Exh.9 who is mother of informant Riya and PW 2 Riya at Exh.10. Accused admitted spot panchanama Exh.8. Both the witnesses turned hostile and as there is no incriminating evidence against the accused, therefore, his statement u/s 313 of Cr.P.C. is dispensed with. 8] PW 1 Haifza deposed that on 10.8.2016 there was quarrel and as such in fit of anger, complaint came to be lodged against accused. She denied portion marked A from her police statement. On going through that portion marked A, it reveals that this witness is a hearsay witness as at the time of incident, she was not present on the spot and incident was narrated her by informant. Therefore, evidence of this witness is of no use. It is to be noted that she admitted in her cross examination by the Ld. APP that there is settlement out of Court between complainant and accused and both are going to marry. This clearly shows that due to settlement, witness is reluctant to depose about the incident. 9] PW 2 Riya is the informant and she deposed that on 10.8.2016 there was quarrel between her and accused and as such, ..4/- ..4.. Sandhya Jadhav for the accused. JUDGMENT (Delivered on this 6th day of July 2017) Accused was facing trial under sections 354, 323, 504 and 506 of IPC read with section 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 on following facts:­ 1 to 5 Judgment Special (POCSO) Case No. 275/2015 1] That on 28/02/2015 at about 20.45 hours in the Compound of Building in which victim was residing accused no.1 has demanded mobile number of the victim and on her refusal has molested her and also has abused her and assault her by means of slaps. According to prosecution at the same time accused no.2 has threatened her with dire consequences. Hence, on the complaint lodged by victim offences punishable under aforesaid sections came to be registered against accused. 2] During pendency of case accused no.2 Shahnavaj alias Shanu was expired. Hence, case stands abated against him. On appearance of accused no.1 charge was framed below Exh.4 and contents of said charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular. Accused pleaded not guilty and claim to be tried. His defence was of total denial. 3] On the basis of the aforesaid facts, in order to substantiate the allegations prosecution has examined victim as witness no.1. Victim has attained the age of majority on date of recording of her evidence. Hence, her deposition was recorded in regular fashion. After deposition she being adult member has passed pursis that she do not wish to examine any more witness. On the basis of the said evidence arguments of rival advocates were heard. Both rival advocates have submitted in terms of their respective claim and defence. 2 to 5 Judgment Special (POCSO) Case No. 275/2015 4] On the basis of aforesaid rival arguments, following points arose for my consideration and I record my findings against each of them for the reasons noted below :­ Sr.N. Points Findings 1] Does the prosecution prove that accused alongwith deceased ..Negative. accused Shahanavaj @ Shanu Jarulla Khan on 28/02/2015 at about 20.45 hours at Compound of Vimal Park Building, Darga Road, Amrutnagar, Mumbra, Dist. Thane, in the Jurisdiction of Mumbra Police Staton, Thane, used criminal force to complainant namely Kum. Afarin Kayamuddin Shaikh, a minor age – 16 years intending to outrage her modesty and thereby committed an offence punishable under Section 354 of Indian Penal Code ? 2] Does the prosecution prove that on the above date, time and ..Negative. place in voluntarily caused hurt to complainant namely Kum. Afarin Kayamuddin Shaikh, a minor age – 16 years and thereby committed an offence punishable under Section 323 of Indian Penal Code of IPC ? 3] Does the prosecution prove that on the above date, time and ..Negative. place named accused on aforesaid date, time and place, intentionally insulted the complainant namely Kum. Afarin Kayamuddin Shaikh, a minor age – 16 years by abusing her in filthy language and thereby gave provocation to her to break public peace and thereby committed an offence punishable under Section 504 of Indian Penal Code 4] Does the prosecution prove that on the above date, time and ..Negative. place accused committed criminal intimidation by threatening to complainant viz. Kum. Afarin Kayamuddin Shaikh, a minor age – 16 years and thereby committed an offence punishable under Section 506 of Indian Penal Code and within my cognizance. 5] Does the prosecution prove that on the above date, time and ..Negative. place, committed sexual assault on complainant viz. Kum. Afarin Kayamuddin Shaikh, a minor age – 16 years and thereby committed an offence punishable under Section 7, 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 6] What order? Accused is acquitted as per final order. 3 to 5 Judgment Special (POCSO) Case No. 275/2015 REASONS As to point no.1 to 6 :­ 5] All these points are interlinked with each other and therefore are considered at once. In the present matter victim has alleged that on the date of incident initially one person by name Javed with intend to outrage her modesty has used criminal force intending and knowingly that his act will outrage her modesty and accused no.2 has abused, threatened and also suspected her character. Besides, said allegations she did not utter any word about either she being assaulted by means of slaps or was threatened with dire consequences. Hence, so far as allegations under section 323 or 506 are concerned, as there are absolutely no allegations made against accused by the victim said needs no consideration and on that basis itself accused cannot be said to be guilty of the said offence. 6] Though, she has made allegations against accused Shanu as he has been already expired and case has been abated against him, the court again need not consider the said allegations. Hence, court has to consider only allegations against accused Javed. However, in view of the clear deposition of the victim that police has wrongly implicated the present accused and she has intimated police about wrong implication of the accused even at the stage of bail and as on date also and 4 to 5 Judgment Special (POCSO) Case No. 275/2015 has specifically further deposed that accused person before the court though is known as Javed he was not present at the time of incident. Hence, from the deposition of the victim it can be said that though the incident was occurred as alleged, present accused no.1 Javed is not real culprit. Hence, even if we consider the deposition of victim as it is than also there is nothing on record to implicate accused Javed before the court in the incident. The evidence cannot be said to be sufficient to convict him in the matter. Having regards to the said facts, I do not hesitate to record my findings against point no.1 to 5 in negative and proceed to pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused is acquitted from the offence punishable under sections 354, 323, 504 and 506 of IPC read with section 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 . 2] Bail bond of accused shall stands canceled. 3] Accused is directed to execute P.R. Bond of Rs.10,000/­ as per amended provisions of section 437(A) of Cr.P.C. and bonds so executed shall remain in force for the period of six months from the date of its execution. 4] Proceeding is accordingly closed. Hence point Nos.1 to 3 are answered in the affirmative. 17] As accused is held guilty for the offence punishable u/s.363, 376 of Indian Penal Code and section 4 and 12 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, he is liable to be convicted and sentenced for the sames. At this juncture I heard the accused on quantum of sentence. 18] Heard the accused on quantum of sentence. The accused submitted nothing on the point of sentence. A.P.P. Mr.Kadu submitted that offence being serious maximum punishment be inflicted upon the accused. 19] It is pertinent to note here that the birth date of the victim is 20.08.2002. At the time of sexual intercourse between the accused and the victim girl the victim was less than 14 years old. Considering said fact, the punishment is to J­Spl.Case POCSO ­ 335­16 ­ S­363,376, 4,12.doc .....9/­ ..9.. J­Spl.Case POCSO No.– 335/2016.. Exh.43. CNR No. MHTH01­008670­2016 be inflicted upon. Offence punishable u/s.363 of the Indian Penal Code is an independent offence. Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code and section of 4 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act is in respect of one and same act. Under such circumstances punishment u/s.4 of the Act alone is to be inflicted as it is special enactment. In view of stringent offence u/s.4 of the Act, it is not necessary to again punish for section 12 of the Act. With these observations following order is passed. ORDER 1. --1-- ORDER BELOW EXH. 1 IN CRIMINAL BAIL APPLICATION NO.3219/2017 CNR NO.MHTH 01­008694­2017 The applicant Sunil Shiva Rathod has applied for bail under section 439 of Cr. P.C. in C.R.No.I­298/2017 registered in Rabale MIDC Police Station for the offence under sections 376, 376(2)(n), 328, 323,506 of Indian Penal Code and Section 4,8,12 of POCSO Act. 2. It is contended that the applicant is falsely implicated. He was arrested on 30.10.2017 and since then he is in jail. Investigation is almost completed. His further custody behind bar is not necessary. There was friendship between victim and present accused. He has not induced or threatened the victim. The applicant is studying in 12th standard and his examination is in February 2018. The applicant is ready to abide by the conditions and face the trial. He has fixed residence place, therefore, he prayed for bail. 3. Investigation Officer has given say at Exh.5. It is contended the victim is 15 years 8 months old. Accused took the victim at Gorai Beach for moving and then gave some powder to smell and after victim became unconscious the accused committed sexual intercourse with her and he took video clip of it and therefore he took disadvantage and on threatening committed sexual intercourse with her for second time and also beat her with leather belt and committed sexual --2-- intercourse against her wish. If the applicant is released on bail he is likely to tamper the prosecution witnesses. 4. I heard Ld. Counsel on behalf of accused. He relied upon the decision in case of Sunil Mahadeb Patil V/s. The State of Maharashtra 2016 ALL MR (Cri) 1712. In which the girl was 15 years old and boy was 20 years old and they eloped away and garlanded each other and after that they performed sexual intercourse. On these mitigating circumstance the Honourable High Court grant bail to the applicant. In case of Mahesh Balkrishna Dandane V/s. The State of Maharashtra 2015 ALL MR (Cri) 2805. In that case it was held that, “whether relationship between parties were consensual or not, is to be tested independently, depending on the facts and circumstances of each case. No straight jacket formula or any kind of labelling can be adopted.” In case of Shiney Suraj Ahuja V/s. State of Maharashtra 2010 ALL MR (Cri) 92. In that case it was held that, “while considering the bail application, the court is not supposed to deal with the submissions in minute details and pronounce correctness or otherwise of the same. However, court is expected to broadly consider evidence, material and circumstances on record and then form an opinion as to whether the applicant is entitled to be released on bail or otherwise.” --3-- 5. The applicant has produced the copy of FIR. On perusal of FIR it appears that the victim was residing with her grand mother in February 2017. She acquainted with the present applicant. Thereafter they would contact with each other on mobile phone. They would move together. One day the accused took the victim at Gorai Beach for moving along with the other friends. After that accused took her in hotel and gave powder to smell. After that she became unconscious and when she became conscious she was infront of her house in a rickshaw. On next day she was paining in stomach and waist. After its 15 days accused called victim at highway and the took her to Gorai Beach along with friends. At that time the accused showed her video clip in which there were nude photos of the victim and accused gave powder to smell. At that time also she became unconscious. When she was became conscious she was infront of her house. Thereafter in April 2017 in summer days accused took the victim in Gorai Beach. At that time accused forced to have sexual intercourse with her. He beat her with leather belt and also assaulted her with blade and committed sexual intercourse with her, but the accused had threatened to kill her and her grand mother. Therefore she did not disclose this fact to anybody. Thereafter she stopped to contact the accused, but the accused was contacting the victim. On 06.10.2017 the accused had come to the house of victim and threatened her that if she did not continue relation he will circulate her photographs on facebook and therefore, the --4-- victim and her grand mother contacted the Child Line NGO and with their help lodged FIR. 6. Considering the facts mentioned in the FIR the court is of the view that there is strong prima facie case made out against this accused. There is no consent at all of the victim for having sexual intercourse, but her consent was taken by administering powder to smell and by making her unconscious. The accused had taken her nude video clips and for the second time he blackmailed her for having sexual relation. In third time the accused had beaten her with leather belt and forcibly took her consent for having sexual relation. 7. Considering the facts mentioned in the FIR there is no where made out that the victim herself has consented for having sexual relation. The victim is minor, therefore, her consent is not at all material. The accused threatened to kill her. The victim was minor and she was residing with her grand mother. Therefore, she could not dare to disclose the incident. 8. The court is of the view that offence is very serious and victim has not consented for having sexual relation. The victim had merely friendship with the accused and she would talk with him that does not mean that she had love affair with him and she had voluntarily gone with the accused. Therefore, there is strong prima facie case made out. --5-- 9. Accused is 21 years old. The offence is serious and heinous and therefore if he released on bail he is likely to repeat the offence and likely to tamper witnesses and victim and therefore he is not entitle for bail. 10. The facts and circumstances of the above reported cases are different than the present facts, therefore, I am of the view that in this case applicant is not entitled for bail. Hence, I proceed to pass following order. :ORDER: Application for bail is rejected. Thane. ( S.C. Khalipe ) Date :04/01/2018. Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

Thereafter, he came to her backside and moved his hand on her hairs. When she opposed, he moved his hand on her chest and on private part. 3] Accused has submitted that, he is innocent and is falsely implicated in present crime. The complainant is having previous enmity with his family and hence, he is falsely implicated. He is of young age of 23 years. He has permanent place of residence. Investigating Officer has filed his Say and taken strong objection to release him on bail by submitting that, accused has outraged the modesty of a small victim girl of aged about 10 years by showing her vulgar pictures from his mobile and by moving his hand on her chest and also on private part. 1 Bail No.3289/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) Criminal Bail Application No. 3289/2015 1) Shamsuddin Mohammed Kazi 2) Mansur Shamsuddin Kazi .. Applicants versus The State of Maharashtra Through Koparkhairane P.S. .. Non-applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 1] This is an application moved by the accused in person seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. who was arrested on 18.12.2015 by Kopar khairane Police Station in connection with C.R.No.I-417/2015 registered for an offence punishable under section 376, 506 of I.P.C. and section 4 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as P.O.C.S.O. Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Mr. P.R.Pendor for accused and learned A.P.P. Mrs. Kapre for State. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 18.12.2015 at the instance of the informant / mother of victim-girl who is aged about 6 years with an indictment that in July, 2015 accused no.1 Shamshuddin inserted finger in private part of victim-girl and on 16.12.2015 at about 1230 hours accused 2 Bail No.3289/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) no.2 Maksud Kazi inserted finger in private part of victim- girl. 4] The learned advocate for accused submitted that both accused are falsely implicated. He submitted that as far as allegation against accused no.1 is concerned, no specific date is being given in the F.I.R. and neither considerable reason is mentioned in the F.I.R. He further submitted that even there is delay in lodging the F.I.R. in respect of accused no.2 as the act is stated to be of 16.11.2015 and F.I.R. is lodged on 18.12.2015. He further submitted that the victim's family and accused are staying in same building and there were frequent petty dispute on account of throwing garbage etc. He submitted that the family of accused once complained against the informant in the society and thereafter, this false F.I.R. is deliberately lodged which is after thought. He further submitted that both accused are permanent residents of Thane and accused no.1 is 62 years old and they are ready to abide any conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing them on bail. 5] Per contra, the learned A.P.P. strongly opposed the application submitting that the offence is serious. The victim is of very tender age. The informant will not stake the character of a small child. Investigation is in progress. Statement of the victim girl under section 164 of Cr.P.C. is yet to be recorded. The accused are staying in same building and there are chances of tampering the witnesses 3 Bail No.3289/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) and prayed for rejection of application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of case papers, it appears that the F.I.R. came to be registered against two accused specifying their acts. Accused no.1 who is aged 65 years once in July, 2015 inserted finger in vagina of minor victim-girl aged about 5 years. At that time it was brought to the notice of accused no.1 and she assured that he will not repeat the same act and therefore at that particular time the informant did not lodge complaint to police. Thereafter, on 16.12.2015 around 1200 hours accused no.2 who is staying at third floor in the same building inserted finger in the rectum of victim-girl and therefore, she was crying. The victim-girl pointed out the accused and on asking by her mother/informant, accused avoided to answer and threatened her to kill if she lodge complaint with the police. Same history of sexual assault is given in medical certificate. The statement of the victim-girl as per provisions of section 164 of Cr.PC.. is yet to be recorded. The investigation is in progress. The accused are staying in same building where the informant stays. In such circumstances the apprehension of learned A.P.P. about tampering of witnesses is well founded. At this stage no case is made out against the accused to release them on bail. I, therefore, pass the following order - ORDER The application is rejected. Thane. Date : 08.01.2016 (Ms. U.M. Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act) Thane.

Non-applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 1] By this application the applicant is seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C., who was arrested on 25.11.2015 by Vashi Police Station in connection with C.R.No.I-556/2015 registered for an offence punishable under section 376(2) of I.P.C. and section 5(m), 6 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short P.O.C.S.O. Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Mr. A.S.Guru for the applicant/accused and learned A.P.P. Mrs. R.A.Navale for State. I.O. present with case papers. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 24.11.2015 at the instance of the informant/mother of the victim-girl aged 8 years with an indictment that on 21.11.2015 when her daughter/victim-girl had been to the house of her tuition teacher at that time when her teacher went 2 Bail No. 3290/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) outside, accused, who is son of her teacher, committed sexual assault on her in the kitchen. 4] The learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant-accused is falsely implicated. He submitted that there is unexplained delay in lodging the F.I.R. He further submitted that the victim had been to the tuition with her friend Hansika and therefore the allegation made in the F.I.R. does not appear to be truthful. He further submitted that before eight days of incident, there was quarrel between mother of accused and the informant for the reason of tuition fee and therefore, the false complaint has been registered. The applicant is young boy of 20 years and student of Engineering. He has no antecedents and ready to abide by any conditions imposed by the Court and prayed that accused be released on bail. 5] Per contra, the learned A.P.P. opposed the application submitting that the victim-girl is minor aged about 8 years and the statement of victim under section 164 of Cr.P.C. is recorded which is in the same line. The investigation is in progress. The first bail application of the accused is rejected on 21.12.2015. There are chances of tampering the witnesses and prayed for rejection of application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of F.I.R. it appears that this is second bail application moved by the 3 Bail No. 3290/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) applicant. His first bail application vide No.3061/2015 is recently decided and rejected on merit. Therefore, now the only question which is to be considered is the change of circumstances. The learned counsel for applicant submitted that the accused is an engineering student and his ife will be spoiled if he remains behind bar. Except that, he failed to point out any change of circumstances. It appears that since the rejection of first bail application on 21.12.2015, there is absolutely no change in circumstances. The investigation is still in progress. Hence, no case made out for reconsideration of the bail application. I, therefore, pass the following order - ORDER The application is rejected. Thane.
