1 Bail No. 3292/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) Criminal Bail Application No.3292/2015 Farhan Suleman Patel. .. Applicant versus The State of Maharashtra Through Nayanagar P.S. .. Non-applicant ORDER BELOW EXHIBIT 1 By this application the applicant is seeking regular bail under section 439 of Cr.P.C. who was arrested on 26.12.2015 by Nayanagar Police Station in connection with C.R.No.II-25/2015 registered for an offence punishable under section 509 of I.P.C. and section 12 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereinafter in short referred to as P.O.C.S.O. Act). 2] Heard learned advocate Mr. P.V. Kharge for the applicant/accused and learned A.P.P. Mrs. R.A. Nawale for State. I.O. present with case diary. 3] The F.I.R. came to be registered on 26.12.2015 at the instance of the informant/mother of the victim-girl aged about 11 years with an indictment that the accused with an intent to cause sexual harassment to the victim girl, exhibited his private part 2 Bail No. 3292/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) to the victim girl and by giving indecent gesture outraged her modesty. 4] The learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant-accused is falsely implicated. He submitted that the offence under Section 509 of I.P.C. is not applicable. He submitted that the allegations made that from the window the accused gave indecent gesture by exhibiting his private part . However, the said window is quite heighted and it is not quite possible. He further submitted that prior to two months some parts of the vehicle of the accused were stolen from the premises of the society. However, he did not lodge complaint at that time and members of society, were apprehending that their name may be implicated , therefore, at the instance of people of the society, the false F.IR. was registered against him. He is ready to abide any conditions imposed by the Court and prayed for releasing him on bail. 5] Per contra, the learned A.P.P. opposed the application submitting that the offence is serious. She submitted that F.I.R. discloses act of accused. There is no enmity between the informant and accused to implicate him falsely. The window is quite big and from there, accused did indecent act. The minor victim girl is very much scared. The investigation is in progress and there are chances of tampering of witnesses and prayed 3 Bail No. 3292/2015 (order below Exhibit 1) for rejection of the application. 6] Upon hearing and perusal of police papers and F.I.R. it appears that the allegations against the accused are that the accused with an intent to cause sexual harassment to the victim-girl aged 11 years only, exhibited his private part and gave indecent signals to the victim girl. The investigation is in progress and at nascent stage. The accused stated to be the resident of same vicinity. The victim is minor girl and therefore, looking to the facts of the case, the apprehension of Ld. A.P.P. about tampering of the witnesses is well founded. Hence, no case is made out for releasing the applicant/accused on bail. Hence, I pass the following order - ORDER The application stand rejected. Thane. Date : 18.01.2016. (Ms.U.M.Nandeshwar) Special Judge (P.O.C.S.O. Act), Thane.

Adsul. ___________________________________________________________ JUDGMENT (Delivered on 01.01.2019.) 1] Accused is facing trial for the offence punishable u/s. 354D and 504 of I.P.C. and section 8 and 12 of the POCSO Act. 2 POCSO Case. No. 341/2016. The prosecution case in nut­shell is as follows : 2] The informant herself is victim. She is residing with her parents at Kashimira. At the time of incident, she had appeared for examination of 10th standard and since 10.04.16, she was going to Kirti Classes at Dahisar station for MSCIT. Prior to that, she was daily leaving home at 9.00 a.m. and after school, she used to return at 6.30 p.m. 3] Since August, 2015, a boy was daily used to stop at Kashimira bus­stop at 9 a.m. He used to stare at the victim, however, she used to ignore. Thereafter, he started following her up to Kashimira bus­stop. Thereafter, sometimes, he used to follow her in bus up to Dahisar. Due to fear, she did not inform the same at home. One day, when she asked him as to why he was following her, at that time, he ran away. Thereafter, due to completion of examination, she was at home. 4] Thereafter, on 10.04.16, the victim came to Kashimira bus­ stop to attain the class at Dahisar. On that day, said person did not come. Two days thereafter, said person used to come at bus­stop and used to get­ in in the bus and sit where the victim used to sit and used to stare at her. Thereby, he was doing the act as to make her feel shy. As the person used to daily follow her silently, therefore, she informed the same to her mother. One day, her mother came with the victim and asked said person his name. He informed his name as Shivkumar Mourya, resident of Ghodbunder Shifting. When her mother again asked as to why he was again silently following her. On that, said person abused the victim and her mother and went away. 5] On 22.04.16 at about 9.00 a.m., again said person came on bus­stop when the informant was standing at bus­stop for going to class. 3 POCSO Case. No. 341/2016. When the informant stood apart, said person also came and stood beside the informant. Therefore, the informant narrated the incident to her mother and went to police station and lodged F.I.R. 6] As per F.I.R., C.R. No. 290/16 came to be registered against the accused for the offence punishable u/s. 354 D, 504 of I.P.C. and section 12 of the POCSO Act. A.P.I. Govind Borade conducted the investigation of the matter. He arrested the accused from his house, prepared spot panchanama, recorded statements of father and mother of victim, collected photo­copy of the birth certificate of the victim. However, due to his transfer, A.P.I. Kolhe submitted the charge­sheet against the accused for commission of offence punishable u/s. 354 D, 504 of I.P.C. and sec. 8, 12 of the POCSO Act. 7] My learned predecessor framed charge against the accused for the offence punishable u/s. 354 D, 504 of I.P.C. and u/s. 8, 12 of POCSO Act, vide Exh.3. The contents of charge were read over and explained to the accused by my learned predecessor in vernacular, to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed for trial. 8] Prosecution examined in all three witnesses, P.W.1 is mother of the victim at Exh.6, P.W.2 is the victim at Exh.7 and P.W.3 is the investigating officer Mr. Govind Baburao Borade at Exh.15. 9] Prosecution has relied upon the documents i.e. F.I.R. Exh.8, arrest form of accused Exh. 16, spot panchanama Exh. 12. Thereafter, by pursis Exh. 17, the prosecution has closed its evidence. 10] Statement of accused u/s. 313 of Cr.P.C. came to be recorded to the extent of only incriminating material against him. The defence of the accused is of total denial and false implication. 4 POCSO Case. No. 341/2016. 11] Heard learned A.P.P. Shri. Vinit Avinash Kulkarni for the State and learned counsel Shri. S.B. Adsul for the accused. 12] Following points emerged for my consideration and I have recorded my findings thereon for the reasons given below. Points Findings 1] Whether the prosecution has proved Yes. that in between August, 2015 till 22.04.16 from Kashimira bus­stop to Dahisar station, Mumbai, when complainant victim was stopping at Kashimira bus­stop for going to school and class, accused had repeatedly chased her and was staring at her ? 2] Whether the prosecution has proved No. that in the above period and place, accused had abused victim and her mother when her mother asked about the offence of stalking committed by him ? 3] Whether the accused is guilty of Yes. offence punishable u/s. 354 D of I.P.C. ? 4] Whether the accused is guilty of Yes. commission of offence u/s. 11(iv) punishable u/s. 12 of the POCSO Act ? 5] Whether the accused is guilty of No. commission of offence u/s. 8 of the POCSO Act ? 6] What order ? As per final order. REASONS 13] Ld. Special P.P. Shri. V.A. Kulkarni for the prosecution 5 POCSO Case. No. 341/2016. submitted that in the present case, P.W.2 the victim has deposed categorically about the occurrence of alleged incident. She was followed by the accused even since August, 2015. She tolerated the same for some days. However, ultimately informed her mother about the same. Her date of birth as 03.10.2000, has not challenged by the defence. There are allegations of staring at the victim as well as making gestures at her. He used to watch her by sitting on fronter seat of the victim in the bus. Mother of the victim also tried to convince the accused, however, he quarreled with her and ultimately on 22.04.16, F.I.R. came to be lodged against him. Both the witnesses i.e. mother of victim and victim have identified the accused in the court. Though the accused has taken defence that there was quarrel between mother of victim and accused, however, no evidence to that effect has produced on record, so also, reason of said quarrel has also not come on record. Therefore, said defence cannot be taken into consideration. 14] Even as per prosecution case, a quarrel had taken place between mother of victim and accused, but reason for the same was the illegal activities of accused of staring at her daughter and making gestures at her. Therefore, there is no reason to disbelieve the version of prosecution. Hence, by holding that accused has committed offence u/s. 354­D, 504 of I.P.C. and sec. 12 of the POCSO Act, the accused may be convicted and sentenced with maximum imprisonment prescribed for the offence. However, he candidly admitted that there are no ingredients of section 8 of the POCSO Act in the allegations against the accused. 15] On the other hand, Ld. Counsel Shri. S.B. Adsul for defence submitted that the birth certificate of the victim has not proved and therefore, not exhibited. The same cannot be read in evidence. Therefore, it cannot be held that the informant was minor at the relevant time and 6 POCSO Case. No. 341/2016. provisions of POCSO Act are not applicable to the case. That there is no independent witness to the incident though it has came on record that the bus­stop is crowded place, so also, the fly­over at Dahisar is also crowded place. The I.O. could not get CCTV footage of the incident, though now there are CCTV cameras installed in the buses. The statement of driver or conductor or even co­passengers has not recorded. The I.O. has not collected any evidence about the timings or attendance register of the tuition class allegedly attended by the informant. Therefore, there is no cogent evidence against the accused. 16] He submitted that even the I.O. has admitted that a quarrel had taken place between accused and mother of informant, which is a defence of the accused. Therefore, a separate evidence about said quarrel is not necessary. He submitted that there is no material to show that the accused has committed any offence. Moreover, in respect of the alleged offence u/s. 354­D of I.P.C., the intention or knowledge of the accused is required to be proved and the prosecution has failed to prove the same. In support of his case, he relied upon decision of Hon'ble Bombay High Court in the case of 'Bandu Vitthalrao Borwar Vs. State of Maharashtra, Criminal Appeal No. 50 of 2016 dated 17.10.2016', and submitted that as the prosecution failed to prove the allegations against accused beyond reasonable doubt, hence, he may be acquitted from the charges. 17] In the light of above submissions, it is required to scrutinize the material on record. As to Points No. 1 and 2:­ 18] It has come in the evidence of P.W.1 Khatija Nazir Mulani that she is residing at Janatanagar since 2007. Victim is her daughter. In the 7 POCSO Case. No. 341/2016. year 2016, she was 16 years old. Her date of birth is 03.10.2000. At that time, she was studying in 10th standard in Vidya­Mandir, Dahisar. She used to go to tuition at 9.00 a.m. and sometimes, used to return at 10.00 or 11.00 a.m. and when time does not permit, she used to return at 6.00 p.m. She informed her that one boy was chasing her. He used to get in, in same bus in which her daughter used to catch. He used to alight from bus on the spot where her daughter used to alight. Subsequently, he started coming with another boy. Whenever she used to climb on the stair­case, he used to stare at her. This incident was continued for many days. One day, she went to bus­stop with her daughter. Her daughter did not get in, in two consecutive buses. The boy also did not get in those buses. Thereafter, she told her daughter to get in the third bus. Immediately, after her daughter, said boy got into the third bus. Thereafter, she got inside the bus. After sensing the same, said boy alighted in between. After two days, she again went to the bus­stop and asked the boy as to why he was behaving so. He started giving evasive answers. She took him to police chowky and they lodged complaint. Her daughter lodged F.I.R. Name of said boy was Shivkumar Mourya. The witness identified the accused present in the court. On the same day, police recorded her statement. She had supplied her daughter's birth certificate to police. 19] During her cross­examination, she admitted that the bus­stop where her daughter used to go, was crowded one. That the starting time of class was fixed. However, her daughter used to return at 10 a.m. or 11 a.m., otherwise, even up to 6 p.m. She cannot tell the date on which her daughter informed her that some boy was chasing her. She did not narrate before the police that accused was also going with another boy. She admitted that on the date of incident, her daughter showed her said boy. 8 POCSO Case. No. 341/2016. She cannot tell the date on which she firstly went to the bus­stop. She admitted that on that day also, there was considerable crowd on the bus­ stop. It is the main bus­stop in the area and large number of people use the same. 20] That she did not narrate before police that on first day, her daughter skipped two buses and when she got in third bus, the boy also got inside behind her. She admitted that when after two days, she talked to the said boy, they had a quarrel. However, denied that the quarrel was so intensive that said boy used some bad words and left the spot. She admitted that when she went to police station, police informed her name of the boy as Shivkumar Mourya. She denied the suggestion that as she had quarrel with accused on 22.04.16, therefore, she lodged false F.I.R. against the accused. 21] It has come in the evidence of P.W.2 victim that, she had passed H.S.C. from Rawal College. Her birth date is 03.10.2000. In the year 2016, she was residing at Kashimira with her parents. At that time, she was studying in 10th standard in Vidya­Mandir, Dahisar. She was also pursuing M.S.C.I.T. from Kirti Classes. She used to go at 9.00 or 10.00 a.m. and used to return at 6.00 p.m. Since August, 2015, accused daily used to come at bus­stop and follow her. He used to stare at her badly and used to make gestures, due to which she used to feel ashamed. Once, he came with another boy and the accused was pointing at her and staring at her badly. He used to sit on the fronter seat than her and used to look at her. Once when she was going by sky­walk of Dahisar station, he went ahead of her and thereafter, he was staring her from the ground. Initially, she tolerated him. However, when it increased, she informed her mother. They decided to keep watch on him and handover him to police. On next 9 POCSO Case. No. 341/2016. day, he did not come. Thereafter, again he came there, at that time, her mother was with her. On first day, her mother tried to convince him. However, his action did not stop. On next day, i.e. 22.04.16, he was handed over in the custody of police. She lodged F.I.R. Exh.8 dated 22.04.16 against the accused. Her statement was also recorded before Magistrate u/s. 164 of Cr.P.C. Victim identified the accused before the court. 22] During her cross­examination, she admitted that she used to go to school at Dahisar from Kashimira. That the bus­stop was crowded place. Dahisar is also crowded place. She denied the suggestion that she used to travel with her friends. She noticed about the accused first time in August, 2015. She never tried to raise alarm or never informed public about the accused. Initially, she did not lodge complaint as she thought that she should inform her parents first. She further deposed that she had narrated in F.I.R. that the accused used to stare at her by sitting on fronter seat, than her. She had also narrated that he was staring at her with bad intention. She had also narrated that accused overtook her at Dahisar sky­ walk and was staring at her. However, she could not explain as to why above­said things have not mentioned in F.I.R. She cannot tell exact date when she went with her mother. However, it was in November. Further, she denied the suggestions put by the defence. 23] It has come in the evidence of P.W.3 A.P.I. Govind Borade, the investigating officer that from March, 2014 to May, 16, he was posted as A.P.I. with Kashimira police station. Investigation of C.R. No. 290/2016 was entrusted to him. He arrested the accused from his house in presence of panchas by arrest form at Exh. 16. He prepared spot panchanama at Exh. 12. He recorded statements of mother and father of 10 POCSO Case. No. 341/2016. informant. He collected copy of birth certificate of the informant and her date of birth is 03.10.2000. 24] During his cross­examination, he admitted that spot of incident is on high­way near bus­stop, having frequent traffic. There are various shops and houses near the bus­stop. The bus­stop is near Kashimira police station. He had searched for CCTV footage nearby bus­stop, however, could not get the same. He did not record statements of driver, conductor or passengers of the bus. He did not collect any evidence to show that the victim was going to tuition class. He admitted that he did not verify timing of tuition class from the institute. He did not collect attendance register of informant from the tuition class. He admitted that mother of victim is social worker in the area. He admitted that accused had abused mother of victim before the incident, however, denied the suggestion that mother of victim abused him. Further, he denied other suggestions put by the defence about recording false F.I.R. and incorrect statements and registration of crime due to pressure of the social worker, mother of the informant. 25] Hence, from above evidence of prosecution, it is necessary to ascertain as to whether, the accused has committed any offence, of which charge has framed against him. 26] If the above evidence of prosecution would perused, the evidence of P.W.1 and P.W.2 is corroborating to each­other on the point of the allegations of accused following the victim when she used to go to school from bus­stop to Dahisar. The victim has specifically deposed that since August, 2015, the accused daily used to come at bus­stop and follow her. Initially, she tolerated, however, subsequently, she informed her mother i.e. P.W.1. On the further point, there is some improvement and the narration about the mother coming with the informant/victim at bus­stop, 11 POCSO Case. No. 341/2016. so also asking her to skip two buses and getting into third one and the accused also doing the same thing, has not reflecting in the F.I.R. However, only on that ground, evidence of P.W.1 and P.W.2 cannot be discarded. The objection of defence on this evidence is the I.O. had not recorded statements of the co­passengers, driver and conductor of the bus, so also, the I.O. could not collect any CCTV footage of the bus­stop or even the bus. 27] On the point of independent witnesses and CCTV footage, it is necessary to consider that the allegations of accused are not of physical assault or even touch, but they are of silently following the victim. In such cases, it is possible that the co­passenger may not have noticed it. The victim has specifically deposed that she did not inform to her parents also. Therefore, informing any passenger or even driver or conductor of the bus is out of question. So also, now­a­days, it is very difficult to get an independent witness. However, there is no reason to disbelieve the P.W.1 and P.W.2, only because they are interested witnesses. 28] Though the defence has tried to make out the case that due to quarrel with the mother of the victim, the accused has falsely implicated, however, no suggestion has put to either of the witnesses as to on what issue the quarrel was taken place and at which place. No doubt, the prosecution witnesses have admitted that quarrel had taken place, but as per prosecution version, said quarrel was due to accosting the accused by mother of victim and accused was following the victim. Therefore, merely asking question that quarrel had taken place between accused and mother of the victim by itself, would not be sufficient to create the suspicion about the prosecution version. As per prosecution also, quarrel had taken place and reason for the same was illegal deeds of the accused. The accused has 12 POCSO Case. No. 341/2016. not come with a different reason of quarrel. Therefore, such suggestion of mere quarrel would not absolve the accused from explaining the incriminating material against him. Except above­said defence, the accused has not explained the things. 29] From the entire evidence of prosecution, especially the oral testimony of P.W.1 and P.W.2, it has clearly came on record that from August, 2015 till 22.04.16, the accused Shivkumar Mourya was following the victim from bus­stop of Kashimira till the bus­stop at Dahisar. However, at the same time, there are allegations that when the mother of the victim accosted the accused, at that time, the accused started giving arrogant answers. Therefore, he was taken to police station. 30] Admittedly, there are no allegations of commission of any offence u/s. 8 of the POCSO Act, however, there are specific allegations of commission of offence u/s. 11(iv) of the POCSO Act, which had caused sexual harassment to the victim. Following minor victim for nearabout 7­8 months constantly, staring at her by sitting in fronter seat in the bus, would certainly fall in clause (iv) of section 11 of the POCSO Act. It has also came in the evidence of P.W.2 that once she was going on sky­walk of Dahisar station, the accused went ahead of her and thereafter, he was staring at her from the ground. Therefore, in my view, the prosecution has succeeded in proving the factum that accused used to follow her daily from Kashimira bus­stop till Dahisar. 31] In present case, though charge has also framed against accused for commission of offence punishable u/s. 504 of I.P.C., however, nowhere in the entire evidence of any of the prosecution witnesses, the exact words used by the accused about the quarrel have mentioned. So also, none of the witnesses have deposed in their examination­in­chief about any quarrel. 13 POCSO Case. No. 341/2016. There is only reference of giving arrogant answers. Merely on that ground, it cannot be said that the accused is guilty of commission of any offence punishable u/s. 504 of I.P.C. and evidence of prosecution in that regard is not sufficient. Moreover, mother of the victim herself has denied in her cross­examination the suggestion that accused used some bad words to her. Hence, at the most, it can be said that the prosecution has succeeded in proving that the accused was following the victim from August, 2015 to April, 2016. Hence, point No. 1 is hereby, answered in the affirmative and point No. 2 is answered in the negative. As to Point No. 3­ 32] Now, in order to bring the act of the accused under the provisions of POCSO Act, it is necessary for the prosecution to show that the victim was minor at the relevant time. On this point, the prosecution has examined only two witnesses i.e. P.W.1 and P.W.2. Both have categorically deposed that the date of birth of victim is 03.10.2000. However, the original birth certificate of the victim has not produced on record. Though the photo­copy of birth certificate is forming part of charge­sheet, the prosecution has not taken efforts to get it proved. Therefore, it is the contention of the defence that when the prosecution has failed to prove the birth certificate, it cannot be held that the victim was minor at the relevant time of incident. 33] However, on this point, the prosecution has submitted that as the defence has not taken pains to even deny the date of birth of the victim in the cross­examination of the victim herself or that of her mother, the said date is required to be treated as admitted and the prosecution did not thought it necessary to examine any other witness on this point and therefore, the said date of birth of the victim which remained unchallenged, 14 POCSO Case. No. 341/2016. is required to be accepted. As per said date of birth, the victim was just 16 years and 6 months old at the time of incident in question. It is matter of fact that defence has not put any suggestion to either of the prosecution witnesses, so as to deny the alleged date of birth of the victim. P.W.1 is mother of the victim who has given birth to the victim. She being mother, is the most natural and reliable witness on the point of age of the victim. On this point, reliance can be placed on the observations of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of 'Fateh Chand Vs. State of Haryana: 2009 Cr.L.J., 2942'. Considering the observations of Apex Court in the above­ said case, it can be held that mother of victim i.e. P.W.1 is competent to prove the date of birth of the victim, especially when no suggestions were put to her denying the same. Hence, in my view, the prosecution has succeeded in proving that at the time of incident, the victim was minor and date of her birth was 03.10.2000. 34] Once, it is held that the victim was minor at the relevant time of incident, so also that the accused was continuously following her from August, 2015 till 22.04.2016, it is necessary to consider as to whether the act of accused constitutes offence punishable u/s. 354 D of I.P.C. and section8 and 12 of the POCSO Act. 35] So far as section 354 D of I.P.C. is concerned, it is slightly different than section 11 of the POCSO Act. In section 11 of the POCSO Act, an indication of disinterest by the victim is not necessary. Obviously, the POCSO Act deals with children and therefore, interest and disinterest of minor is immaterial. Therefore, though it was argued by the defence that section 354 D of I.P.C. may not be applicable to present case, as there are no allegations that the accused was following the victim though she gave clear indication of disinterest. The defence would be there is no material 15 POCSO Case. No. 341/2016. on record to show that the victim had expressed her disinterest in the accused. So also, to constitute an offence of stalking, mere following woman is not sufficient and in addition to following, the accused must contact her or attempt to contact her. However, it is the case of the prosecution that the accused was silently following her and there are no allegations of any attempt of accused to contact her. However, if the evidence of prosecution would perused, it is clear that both P.W.1 and P.W.2 have deposed that the mother of the victim had accosted the accused, however, his behaviour did not change and he again followed the victim. The incident of accosting the accused is clear indication of disinterest. Moreover, the victim being child, the question of her interest or disinterest cannot be raised. Hence, when the prosecution has succeeded in proving that the accused was following the victim for nearabout eight months, he was following her with foster personal interaction and there was clear indication by the victim about her disinterest and in spite of the same, she was being followed. Hence, it is necessary to held that the accused is guilty of commission of the offence u/s. 354 D(i) of I.P.C. Hence, point No. 3 is answered in the affirmative. As to Point No. 4­ 36] While considering the act of the accused under the provisions of the POCSO Act, it is necessary to consider the word 'sexual intent'. On the point of the wording 'sexual intent' in section 11 of the POCSO Act, the learned counsel for defence has relied upon the observations of Hon'ble Bombay High Court in the case of 'Bandu Vitthal Borwar Vs. State of Maharashtra in Cri. Appeal No. 50/2016', in which it is observed that­ '11. It is obvious that the intent, which is nothing but a state of mind, must be to establish some 16 POCSO Case. No. 341/2016. sort of physical contact or must be related to or associated with sex or indicative of involvement of sex in the relationship, if it is to be considered as sexual. I have already stated that the utterance indicating an expectation of a person that the other person should love him would not by itself amount to sexual intent as contemplated by the legislature. There should be something more which must suggest that the real intention is to drag in the angle of sex, if the words uttered are to be taken as conveying sexual intent. If we consider the other evidence of the prosecution in order to ascertain the state of mind of the appellant, we would find that there is not a single circumstance, which would indicate that the appellant's real intention was to establish a sexual contact with the appellant then or in near future. No evidence has been brought on record throwing any light upon the eye expressions, voice modulations, body language etc. of the appellant. Besides, the utterances in question have not been made repeatedly but only singularly. Such being the nature of evidence, I do not think that the utterances made by the appellant, in the presence of the victim girl and that were heard by her as well as her friend P.W.6 Manisha in this case, indicated any sexual intent on the part of the appellant. If this is so, it would have to be said that even the offence punishable under section 12 of the POCSO Act, which is an offence of sexual harassment, has not been proved by the prosecution beyond reasonable doubt. The learned Additional Sessions Judge has committed an illegality in not considering the true import of the offence of sexual harassment, as denied in section 11 of the POCSO Act.' 37] I have gone through the entire Judgment of the case. In the said case, there were allegations against the accused therein that on the particular day, the appellant accosted the victim by stopping her and further putting question as to why she did not love appellant. On negative reply by victim, the appellant got angry and slapped on her face. In said case, obviously said touch of accused was out of anger. The same is not the case 17 POCSO Case. No. 341/2016. in present situation. The accused was repeatedly following the victim for nearabout eight months continuously. It has also came on record that when the victim skipped two buses as per directions of her mother, accused also skipped those two buses and got into third bus after the victim. This conduct of accused clarifies his intention. Hence, the observations in the case of 'Bandu Vitthal Borwar' (supra) are not helpful to the accused. 38] In the present case, there are allegations that accused was following repeatedly the victim. It has also come on record that the mother of the victim accosted the accused one day before lodging F.I.R. However, the behaviour of accused did not change and again he followed the victim. Therefore, the victim lodged complaint by going to police station along with her mother. Admittedly, there are no allegations of any other kind like uttering any words or making any gestures or showing any other objectionable things to the victim. There are no allegations of threat to the victim. However, there are only allegations of repeatedly following the victim. Therefore, act of the accused squarely falls in section 11(iv) of the POCSO Act. Hence, the accused is required to held guilty of commission of offence u/s. 11(iv) punishable u/s. 12 of the POCSO Act. Hence, point No. 4 is answered in affirmative. As to Point No. 5­ 39] Though my learned predecessor has framed charge against the accused for commission of offence punishable u/s. 8 of the POCSO Act by alleging that he had outraged the modesty and committed sexual assault on the victim, however, if the entire case of prosecution would perused, there are neither allegations of any such nature in F.I.R., nor there is any evidence to that effect. Learned Special P.P. has also candidly admitted 18 POCSO Case. No. 341/2016. that there are no such allegations against the accused. Considering the same, Point No. 5 is required to be answered in the negative by holding the accused not guilty of commission of any offence punishable u/s. 8 of the POCSO Act. 40] As the accused is held guilty of commission of offence punishable u/s. 354 D of I.P.C. and section 11(iv) punishable u/s. 12 of the POCSO Act, it is necessary to hear the accused on the point of sentence. Hence, I take a pause to hear the accused on the point of sentence. Thane, (V.Y. Jadhav) Date­ 01.01.2019. Additional Sessions Judge, Thane. 41] The accused apprised that he is held guilty for commission of offence punishable u/s. 354 D of the Indian Penal Code and section 12 of the POCSO Act. The prescribed punishment for each of the offence is up to three years and also with fine. 42] Heard the accused himself, Ld. Counsel for accused and Ld. P.P. Shri. Londhe on the point of sentence. 43] Ld. P.P. Shri. Londhe submitted that considering the nature of crime that though the accused had never threatened the victim, however, for eight months, he was continuously following the victim, it has caused a trauma to the victim. Hence, maximum sentence may be awarded. 44] On the other hand, Ld. Counsel for defence on instructions from accused submitted that the accused is just 26 years old youth and sole bread­winner of the family. He was not even knowing the victim. There are no criminal antecedents against him. He had already undergone some 19 POCSO Case. No. 341/2016. days in prison. Considering the age and absence of any criminal antecedents, so also, considering that even the allegations are of following the victim and there are no allegations of even bodily touch or attempt to contact her, the alleged act of the accused is much lighter than the other set of crimes mentioned in the respective sections. Hence, he may be sentenced with minimum punishment and may be sentenced for imprisonment for the period which he had already undergone in custody. 45] Considering the material on record, it is clear that the alleged act of the accused of following the victim silently, though constitutes the offence u/s. 354 D of I.P.C. and section 11(iv) of the POCSO Act. Maximum punishment for commission of each of the said offence is imprisonment for three years with fine. However, if the alleged act of the accused would be compared with other acts mentioned in those respective sections, then certainly the role of accused is much lighter. There are no allegations of any attempt to contact the victim. So also, there are no allegations that at any point of time, he had touched the victim. So also, considering the age of the accused as well as lack of any criminal antecedents, in my view, directing the accused to suffer imprisonment of lesser period like one month along with fine would suffice the purpose. Considering that as per record, the accused was in custody since 22.04.2016 till 16.05.2016 i.e. for a period of 24 days, therefore, he can be also sentenced to imprisonment for the period which he has already undergone. At the same time, it is also necessary to impose fine on the accused. Considering the nature of the offence and earning capacity of the accused, in my view, fine of Rs.10,000/­for each of the offence punishable u/s. 354 D of I.P.C. and sec. 11(iv) of the POCSO Act, would suffice the purpose. 20 POCSO Case. No. 341/2016. 46] So far as disposal of muddemal property is concerned, as the charge­sheet does not reflect any muddemal articles, an order for disposal of the same is not warranted. As to Point No. 6­ 47] In the above observations, the accused is held guilty for commission of offence punishable u/s. 354 D of I.P.C. and sec. 11(iv) of the POCSO Act. So also, he is held not guilty and acquitted from the charges of commission of offence under sec. 504 of I.P.C. and section 8 of the POCSO Act. So also, as he is directed to suffer imprisonment of the sentence undergone by him during trial and as he is directed to pay fine of Rs.10,000/­ for commission of each of the offence punishable u/s. 354 D of I.P.C. and sec. 11(iv) of the POCSO Act, hence, in answer to point No. 5, I pass following order. ORDER 1] Accused Shivkumar Ramaas Mourya, is hereby, convicted under sec. 235(2) of the Criminal Procedure Code, of the offence punishable u/s. 354D of I.P.C. and he is sentenced to suffer simple imprisonment for the period which he has already undergone in jail and to pay fine of Rs.10,000/­ (Rupees Ten Thousand Only) in default of payment of fine, he shall further suffer simple imprisonment for seven days. 2] Accused Shivkumar Ramaas Mourya, is hereby, convicted under sec. 235(2) of the 21 POCSO Case. No. 341/2016. Criminal Procedure Code, of the offence u/s. sec. 11(iv) of the POCSO Act, and he is sentenced to suffer simple imprisonment for the period which he has already undergone in jail and to pay fine of Rs.10,000/­ (Rupees Ten Thousand Only) in default of payment of fine, he shall further suffer simple imprisonment for seven days. 3] Both the substantive sentences shall run concurrently. 4] He is in custody from 22.04.2016 till 16.05.2016. Hence, he is entitled for set­off for the said period u/s. 428 of Cr.P.C. 5] Accused Shivkumar Ramaas Mourya is hereby, acquitted u/s. 235(1) of Cr.P.C. of an offence punishable u/s. 504 of I.P.C. and section 8 of the POCSO Act. 6] The accused is hereby, apprised of his right to prefer appeal against the order. 7] Copy of this Judgment and order be given to the accused in gratis. 8] Pronounced in open court. Thane, (V.Y. Jadhav) Date­ 01.01.2019. Additional Sessions Judge, Thane.

Agra, State U.P. ..Accused. ___________________________________________________________ Appearances­ Learned Special P.P. Smt. Phad, for the State. Learned Advocate Shri. Rathod, for the accused. ___________________________________________________________ JUDGMENT (Delivered on 23.05.2018.) 1] Accused Rajesh Hariprasad Singh is facing trial for the 2 POCSO Case. No. 342/2016. offences punishable u/s. 354 of I.P.C. and u/s. 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 2] It is the case of prosecution that on 31.10.16 at evening time, accused ordered the victim aged about 14 years to prepare tea. She had prepared tea in kitchen room. Accused went to her and put his hand in her top and tried to kiss her. By these allegations, Smt. Babali Dipak Singh had lodged her report Exh.13 against accused which is registered vide C.R. no. 437/16 u/s. 354 of I.P.C. and u/s. 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. Police had carried out investigation. He has recorded spot panchanama in presence of panchas and statements of witnesses. After investigation, charge­sheet was submitted. 3] Heard both sides. I framed the charge against the accused for the offences punishable under section 354 of I.P.C. and u/s. 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act on 05/12/2017. Details of the charge were read over and explained to the accused in vernacular, to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. His defence is of total denial. It is the defence of accused that the maternal uncle of victim had demanded one flat, shop and Rs. Forty Lakhs to the accused. As he had not paid the same, false complaint is lodged through victim. 4] During trial, defence has admitted no documents. 5] To bring home the guilt of the accused for the charges leveled against him, the prosecution has examined as many as three witnesses i.e. P.W. Name of witness Exh. Description No. No. 1] Smt. Babali Dipak Singh 12 Sister of Sudha Rahul Singh and Anita Suresh Singh. 2] Ruby Rajesh Singh 14 Wife of accused. 3 POCSO Case. No. 342/2016. 3] Victim 16 Victim. 6] Accused did not enter into witness box. He has not examined defence witness. 7] Heard learned A.P.P. Shri. Kadu for the State and learned counsel Shri. Rathod for the accused. 8] Following points arise for my determination, which are being answered for the reasons given herein­below. POINTS FINDINGS 1] Whether prosecution proved that on No. 31.10.16 at 18.30 hours in the house of accused, he used criminal force on minor victim aged about 13 years by pulling her near him, kissed her, pressed her chest and thereby, committed offence u/s. 354 of I.P.C. and u/s. 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act ? 2] What order ? As per final order. REASONS POINT NO. 1 9] Relations between accused, Sudha Rahul Singh, Shubhangi, Sakshi, Anita Suresh Singh, Ruby and victim is not in dispute. Sudha Rahul Singh is sister of Babali. Shubhangi and Sakshi are daughters of Sudha Rahul Singh. Ruby is daughter of Anita Suresh Singh who died in the year 2008. P.W.2 Ruby is wife of accused. Their marriage was taken 4 POCSO Case. No. 342/2016. place in the year 2009. She blessed a daughter. However, dispute was taken place between them and they are residing separately. 10] P.W.3 victim is sole witness of the incident. The incident took place in the house of accused when none person were present. Accused happens to be brother­in­law of victim aged about 13­14 years. Her date of birth rather her age on the date of incident is not seriously challenged by the accused. The evidence of P.W.3 is only material one. It is to be scrutinized carefully. 11] P.W.3 victim deposed in her evidence that in the year 2016 during Diwali, accused ordered to prepare tea. She had prepared tea in kitchen. Accused came to her and put his hand in her top and tried to kiss her. She pushed him and came out. Thereafter, her mother and others came there. She had narrated the incident to them. 12] It has come in the cross­examination of P.W.3 victim that on the occasion of Diwali, she along with her mother, her aunt Sudha, Sudha's two daughters Shubhangi and Sakshi, her cousin sister Ruby, Ruby's three children, accused, Shravan and Krishna were residing in the house of aunt Sudha. In summer season and Diwali season, school used to remain closed. She along with her mother came to the house of Sudha to spent their Diwali vacation. There was Diwali vacation to her brothers Shravan and Krishna. Prior to one or two days of the day of alleged incident, accused had fired Shubhangi, alleging that she had committed theft of Mangalsutra of Ruby. 13] Victim P.W.3 further deposed in her cross­examination that on occasion of delivery of Ruby Rajesh Singh, she had been at Ruby's house for about one month, happily. Her mother had filed criminal case against accused Rajesh Singh in Agra Court, for committing rape on her. Her top 5 POCSO Case. No. 342/2016. was not torn. Her three maternal uncles, maternal aunt Sudha, Jyoti; her mother, her sister Shubhangi and Ruby and herself had been to police station. She did not know about report of her mother Babali. 14] P.W.1 Babali and P.W.2 Ruby Singh are not eye­witnesses to the incident. Their cross­examination is material one in order to appreciate the story of prosecution whether it is reliable or not. 15] P.W.1 Babali deposed in her cross­examination that victim had stayed for about one to one and half months at the house of accused at Samshabad for taking care of Ruby. It was happened in the year 2016. Prior to that, victim was residing along with her at Fatyabad. During Navratra, 2016, they came to Mumbai as tourist. After their tour, they were going to Fatyabad. Her parents are maintaining her and she is jobless. Since last four­five years, they are maintaining her. Her sister Sudha Rahul Singh is working in Ladies Bar as a waiter. 16] She further deposed in her cross­examination that accused is having two sons and one daughter. Ruby had lost her Mangalsutra. Accused was alleging against Shubhangi daughter of Sudha Rahul Singh. Due to that, there was hot talk. Ruby had filed application for maintenance against accused Rajesh in Agra Court. Accused Rajesh has lodged his report against me, Ruby, Sudha, Jyoti, Jayram, Mohini, Rita, Omvati and Kanhayya. Her brothers are residing in the vicinity of her sister Sudha Rahul Singh. Prior to one day of this F.I.R., quarrel between accused and his wife Ruby was taken place. She herself, her sister and her brother had given understanding to the accused. Due to said quarrel, accused was taken by police to police station. Prior to her report, there was no report or N.C. against accused by her or any of their family members. There was no quarrel with accused. 6 POCSO Case. No. 342/2016. 17] She further deposed in her cross­examination that in Agra court, she filed case no. 267/2017 against accused Rajesh. The said report is in respect of rape by the accused on her daughter i.e. victim during the period when she was residing at the house of accused for taking care of Ruby during her delivery. Her statement is recorded in Agra court. She cannot read Hindi. She had stated before the said court that the said incident was taken place on 31.10.16 at 04.30 a.m. Allahabad High Court had quashed her F.I.R. Economic condition of accused is sound. She along with her sister Sudha are leading their lives on their hands. Her brother Bhagirath is servant in one cloth shop, whereas her another brother Jayram is rickshaw­puller. Her brothers are also poor. 18] It has come in the cross­examination of Ruby Singh that she studied up to 5th standard in Hindi medium. She along with her husband had been to Mumbai as tourist. On 12.10.16, they reached to Thane. There was theft of her Mangalsutra. Accused had suspected upon Shubhangi. Since 01.11.16, she is residing separately from her husband. 19] She further deposed in his cross­examination that she had filed application for maintenance against accused in Agra court Exh.15. Accused had filed case against them in Agra court. However, she had been to the bank and had opened the locker. She voluntarily stated that nothing was found in it. Babali had filed rape case against accused in Agra court. 20] It further seems from the evidence on record that the accused had put up his defence to all three witnesses in their cross­examination. The dispute between prosecution witnesses and accused can be gathered. Mother of victim had also filed case before Agra court alleging that the accused had committed rape on present victim. The story of prosecution does not inspire confidence in toto and there might be some fishy. If really 7 POCSO Case. No. 342/2016. accused had raped at Agra on victim, then certainly Babali along with victim would not have come to the house of accused at Thane. The relations between accused and his wife are also strained. She had also filed her case against accused and in order to support the prosecution, she had deposed before this court against her husband i.e. accused. 21] Having considered the nature of offence, evidence on record and discussed reasons, it is difficult to hold that the accused had committed the offence and prosecution proved the case beyond all reasonable doubts. The testimony of P.W.3 victim does not inspire confidence, having considered the previous circumstances brought by accused on record. Consequently, I have no other option, than to record my findings to the points in the negative. In the result, I proceed to pass the following order. ORDER 1] Accused Rajesh Hariprasad Singh is hereby, acquitted under sec. 235(1) of the Criminal Procedure Code, of the offences punishable u/s. 354 of I.P.C. and u/s. 8 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act. 2] Accused Rajesh Hariprasad Singh be enlarged on P.R. bond of Rs.15,000/­ with surety of like amount. The effect of this bail order will remain in force for the period of six months from today, as per section 8 POCSO Case. No. 342/2016. 437­(A) of Cr.P.C. 3] Muddemal, if any, being worthless, be destroyed after appeal period is over. Thane, (A.S. Bhaisare) Date­ 23.05.2018. P.C. in C.R.No.I­514/2017 registered in Bhayander police station for the offence under section 354­A, 354D of Indian Penal Code and Section 4, 8, 12 of POCSO Act. 2. Advocate for accused relied on following rulings : [i] Naresh @ Nana Baliram Sonawane & … Vs. State of Maharashtra, 2000 (5) Bom.C.R. 382; [ii] Sanjay Baban Bhujbal Vs. The State of Maharashtra, 1998 (2) ALT Cri.13; [iii] Akhtar Ansari Vs. The State of Jharkhand in Cr.M.P. No.144 of 2017; [iv] Bhujangrao s/o Pratiba Jadhav Vs. The State of Maharashtra, 1992 (2) Bom.C.R. 198; [v] Periyasamy Vs. State in Crl.O.P.No.28108 of 2009 (Madras High Court); [vi] Raghubir Singh & Others Vs. State of Bihar, 1987 AIR 149); [vii] Hari Singh Vs. State of Rajasthan, LEX (RAJ) 1998 7 13; [viii] Chaganti Satyanarayana & Ors. Vs. State of Andhra Pradesh, ..2.. Cri. Bail Appln. No.3311/2018 (Lalbabu Laxmanlal Shrivastav V/s State of Maharashtra) C.R.No.I­317/2018 of Bhiwandi Shahar Police Stn. CNR NO.MHTH01­009157­2018 Volume I, Recent Criminal Report, Page 40); [ix] Rakesh Kumar Paul Vs. The State of Assam in Special Leave to Appeal (Cri.) No.2009 of 2017; [x] Union of India through CBI Vs. Nirala Yadav @ Raja Ram Yadav @ Deepak Yadav, 2014 ALL SCR 3451; [xi] Basram Vs. State of Rajasthan in S.B. Criminal Miscellaneous Bail No.2326/2018. 4] The offences which are registered against the accused are under sections 354 of IPC and under sections 7, 8, 9(d), 10 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. After perusing the offence punishable under section 354 of IPC it is seen that, the punishment prescribed is imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than one year but which may extend to five years. The punishment prescribed for offence under section 7 punishable under section 8 of POCSO Act is imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than three years but which may extend to five years. So also, the punishment prescribed for offence under section 9(d) punishable under section 10 of POCSO Act is imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than five years but which may extend to seven years. Therefore, the detention of the accused in this crime can be only for 60 days and not more than that in view of provision of sub­section (2) of Section 167 of Cr.P.C. In such situation police ought to have file charge­sheet on or before 01.12.2018, however, they failed to file charge­sheet within said stipulated period and have filed charge­sheet on 05.12.2018 i.e. on 64 th day. ..3.. Cri. Bail Appln. No.3311/2018 (Lalbabu Laxmanlal Shrivastav V/s State of Maharashtra) C.R.No.I­317/2018 of Bhiwandi Shahar Police Stn. CNR NO.MHTH01­009157­2018 4] The accused came to be arrested on 02.10.2018 as same is very much clear from the remand papers. He was produced for the first time for remand on 02.10.2018. Therefore, the period of 60 days will have to be calculated from 02.10.2018. After said calculation, the day on which applicant has filed present application i.e. 02.12.2018 is the 61st day as the 60 days are already over on 01.12.2018. Considering said fact, the accused is certainly entitled for the statutory bail as he has filed the bail application after completion of 60 days and he has shown his willingness to furnish surety.
